title: The Gandhiji University (Amendment) Act, 1987
purpose: To further amend the Gandhiji University Act, 1985, for certain matters incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the Gandhiji University.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Gandhiji University (Amendment) Act, 1987 and that it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of June, 1987.

Amends section 10 of the Gandhiji University Act, 1985 (referred to as the Principal Act). It modifies sub-sections (1) and (4) regarding the period of appointment of committee members and the words and figures to be substituted in sub-sections (5) and (6) concerning specified sections and sub-sections.

main_sections.section_title: Revival of the committee and validation
main_sections.description: Provides for the revival of the committee and validation of actions taken. Notwithstanding anything contained in the Principal Act or any other law, the term of office of the members of the committee appointed by the Chancellor under section 10 of the Principal Act, notification No. 9838/B5/C1, dated the 3rd March, 1987, which expired on the 2nd day of June, 1987, shall with effect from the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette revive and accordingly anything done or to be done or any action taken or to be taken by the Chancellor or the said committee or any other person or authority in the purported exercise of the powers and functions conferred by or under the Principal Act shall not be deemed to be invalid or ever to have been invalid merely on the ground that it at the term of office of the members of the committee aforesaid had expired on the said date.

important_rules: The Act shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of June, 1987.
The term of office of committee members appointed by the Chancellor is revived and actions taken are validated.
key_procedures: The Act is published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary for general information.
The Bill was passed by the Legislative Assembly and received the assent of the Governor on the 7th day of July, 1987.
administration: Law (Legislation-C) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The notification concerning committee members was dated 3rd March, 1987.
The revival of the committee and validation of actions applies to actions taken or to be taken by the Chancellor or the committee.

key_definitions.Senate: The Senate of the Gandhiji University

title: THE GENERAL SALES TAX (AMENDMENT AND VALIDATION) ACT, 1962
purpose: To amend the General Sales Tax Act, 1125, and to validate the levy, assessment and collection of tax on certain sales.
scope: Applies to sales of goods within the State of Kerala. It also covers proceedings and actions taken under the principal Act.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the General Sales Tax (Amendment and Validation) Act, 1962.

Amends section 26 of the General Sales Tax Act, 1125 (Act XI of 1125). It substitutes clauses (b) and (2A) of sub-section (1) of section 26. Clause (b) now refers to figures and words '6th day of March 1951' and '6th day of September 1955'. New sub-section (2A) states that anything contained in sub-section (1) or section 26 of the principal Act, any sale or purchase which took place on or before the 6th day of September 1955, shall be deemed to have taken place inside the State. It also states that the goods had actually been delivered as a direct result of sale or purchase for the purpose of consumption in the State, though the property in the goods by reason of such sale or purchase passed in another State under the general law relating to sale of goods, and be subject to tax under this Act accordingly.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of the levy, collection, etc., of taxes.
main_sections.description: Notwithstanding any judgment, decree, order of any court, authority or tribunal, or any notification under section 6 of the principal Act, or any press note issued by the Government, all taxes levied, assessed or collected on sales or purchases falling within the purview of sub-section (2A) of section 26 of the principal Act as amended by this Act shall for all purposes be deemed to be, and to have always been, validly levied, assessed or collected. Further, all proceedings taken, orders passed and acts done by any officer, authority or tribunal for the levy, assessment or collection of tax on such sales or purchases shall for all purposes be deemed to be and to have always been, taken, passed and done in accordance with law. All such proceedings, orders and acts may be continued if taken, passed and done under the principal Act as amended by this Act. Provided that nothing in this Act shall render any person liable to be convicted of an offence in respect of anything done or omitted to be done by him before the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette, if such act or omission was not an offence under the principal Act before the aforesaid date, but for the provisions of this Act.

penalties: No specific penalties are detailed in the provided sections, but the validation section clarifies that acts done before the publication of this Act will not be an offence if they were not offences under the principal Act prior to this amendment.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Tax authorities as per the General Sales Tax Act, 1125.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through levy, assessment, and collection of taxes as per the principal Act and its amendments.

duties: Duty to pay sales tax on goods sold or purchased within the State, subject to the provisions of the Act.

key_procedures: Levy, assessment, and collection of sales tax on goods.
Validation of past tax levies, assessments, and collections.
administration: Tax administration under the Kerala Sales Tax Act.
important_notes: The amendments made by sub-section (1) shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1951.
The Act retrospectively validates tax levies, assessments, and collections.
Acts done before the publication of this Act are not an offence if they were not offences under the principal Act before the date of publication.

title: THE GENERAL SALES TAX (AMENDMENT AND VALIDATION) ACT, 1963
purpose: To further amend the General Sales Tax Act, 1125, and to provide for certain other connected matters.
scope: Applies to the General Sales Tax Act, 1125, and matters connected therewith.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the General Sales Tax (Amendment and Validation) Act, 1963. This section and section 3 shall come into force at once and section 2 shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st November, 1957.

Amends section 11 of the General Sales Tax Act, 1125 (Act XI of 1125). In sub-section (1), the proviso shall be omitted, and for sub-section (2), the following sub-section shall be substituted, namely:--(2) Every person who has collected or collects any amount purporting to be by way of tax under this Act on or after the 1st November, 1957, whether or not tax is due from him under this Act in respect of the transaction in which he has collected or collects such amount, shall pay over to Government within such time and in such manner as may be prescribed all amounts so collected by him, if they are in excess of the tax, if any, paid by him for the period during which the collections were made; and, in default of such payments, the amounts may be recovered as if they were arrears of land revenue.

Notwithstanding anything contained in any judgment, decree or order of any court,--(a) all amounts falling within the purview of sub-section (2) of section 11 of the General Sales Tax Act, 1125, as amended by this Act, and paid by, or collected or recovered from, a dealer on or after the 1st November, 1957, shall, for all purposes, be deemed to be, and to have always been, validly paid, collected or recovered; and (b) all proceedings taken, orders passed and acts done by any officer or authority for the collection or recovery of any amount under sub-section (2) of section 11 shall, for all purposes, be deemed to be, and to have always been, taken, passed and done in accordance with law, and such proceedings, orders and acts may be continued as if taken, passed and done under the General Sales Tax Act, 1125, as amended by this Act. Provided that nothing in this Act shall render any person liable to be convicted of any offence in respect of anything done or omitted to be done by him before the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette if such act or omission was not an offence under the General Sales Tax Act, 1125, before the aforesaid date, but the provisions of this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Officer or authority under the General Sales Tax Act, 1125
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Recovery of amounts as arrears of land revenue; continuation of existing proceedings.

rights: Right to have collected amounts deemed validly paid, collected or recovered.
Right to have proceedings, orders, and acts deemed validly taken, passed, and done.
duties: Duty to pay over to Government excess collected amounts.
obligations: Obligation to pay over excess collected amounts to the Government within the prescribed time and manner.

key_procedures: Collection and payment of sales tax as per the General Sales Tax Act, 1125.
Payment of excess collected amounts to the Government.
Continuation of legal proceedings related to collection and recovery of tax.
administration: General Sales Tax Department (inferred)
important_notes: The Act has retrospective effect from 1st November, 1957 for certain provisions.
Validation of past collections and proceedings.

No person shall be convicted for acts or omissions that were not offences prior to the Act's publication, if such acts or omissions were in compliance with the General Sales Tax Act, 1125, before the publication date.

title: THE GENERAL SALES TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1958
purpose: To amend the General Sales Tax Act, 1125.
scope: Applies to the General Sales Tax Act, 1125.

main_sections.description: Names the act as the General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 1958. States that sections 2 and 3 shall come into force on the 1st day of April, 1957, and sections 4 and 5 shall come into force on such date or dates as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint. However, later amendments suggest the commencement for sections 2 and 3 is April 1st, 1957, but for sections 4 and 5 it is the date of notification in the Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 2-A, Act XI of 1125.
main_sections.description: Amends section 2-A of the General Sales Tax Act, 1125. It renames "judicial officer" to "Magistrate" in sub-section (1) of section 2-A, where the words 'judicial officer not below the rank of District Judge' appeared.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 5-A, Act XI of 1125.
main_sections.description: Amends section 5-A of the principal Act by inserting a new sub-section (1-A). This new sub-section states that a dealer shall be liable to pay tax on the turnover of the stock of goods mentioned in sub-section (1) which were in his possession, custody or control immediately before the 14th day of December, 1957, at the point or points and at the rate applicable immediately before the said date.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new sections for section 16.
main_sections.description: Replaces section 16 of the principal Act with new sections. The new section 16 mandates that every person licensed or registered under this Act, and every dealer who is required to do so by the prescribed authority, must maintain true and correct accounts and records. These records should be in Malayalam, Tamil, Kannada, Gujarati or English, relating to their business and showing particulars as prescribed. The Act also mentions that "the prescribed manner" can be specified.

To maintain records in Malayalam, Tamil, Kannada, Gujarati or English.

title: THE GENERAL SALES TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1960
purpose: To amend the General Sales Tax Act, 1125, and to validate certain notifications, orders and proceedings under the Act.
scope: The Act applies to the state of Kerala, as it amends the General Sales Tax Act, 1125, which is applicable in that state.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 1960.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 5, Act XI of 1125.
main_sections.description: Amends section 5 of the principal Act by inserting a new clause (vii) regarding the point of sale for tax purposes. The sale of goods in column (2) of Schedule 1 shall be liable to tax under section 3, sub-section (1), only at such single point in the series of sales by successive dealers as may be specified by the Government by notification in the Gazette; and where the taxable point is specified as a point of sale, the seller shall be liable for the tax on the turnover for which the goods are sold by him at such point and where the taxable point is specified as a point of purchase, the buyer shall be liable for the tax on the turnover for which the goods are bought by him at such point.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of certain notifications, orders, etc.
main_sections.description: Provides for the validation of all notifications issued on or after the 28th day of September, 1957, by the Government in exercise of the powers conferred on them by sub-section (vii) of section 5 of the principal Act. Also validates all taxes levied, assessed or collected in pursuance of the notifications issued under clause (vii) of section 5 of the principal Act. Further validates proceedings taken and done and orders and actions taken and done and all such proceedings, orders and actions and all such notifications in pursuance of which they were taken, passed and done were issued under clause (vii) of section 5 of the principal Act as amended by this Act.
The General Sales Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 1960 (Ordinance No. 1 of 1960), is hereby repealed.

important_rules: Rule: The sale of goods in column (2) of Schedule 1 shall be liable to tax under section 3, sub-section (1), only at such single point in the series of sales by successive dealers as may be specified by the Government by notification in the Gazette.
Rule: Where the taxable point is specified as a point of sale, the seller shall be liable for the tax on the turnover for which the goods are sold by him at such point.
Rule: Where the taxable point is specified as a point of purchase, the buyer shall be liable for the tax on the turnover for which the goods are bought by him at such point.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government (by notification in the Gazette)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By specifying the point of sale or purchase for tax liability.

duties: Duty: Seller is liable for tax on turnover when the taxable point is a point of sale.
Duty: Buyer is liable for tax on turnover when the taxable point is a point of purchase.

key_procedures: Procedure: The Government may specify, by notification in the Gazette, the single point in the series of sales by successive dealers where the sale of goods in column (2) of Schedule 1 shall be liable to tax under section 3, sub-section (1).
Procedure: The Act validates notifications issued and taxes levied or collected under the previous provisions, ensuring continuity and legal standing of past actions.
administration: Government of Kerala
important_notes: The amendment comes into force with effect from the first day of October, 1957.

Notifications issued and taxes levied or collected in pursuance of the notifications issued under clause (vii) of section 5 of the principal Act before the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette are deemed to have been issued, taken, passed and done.

title: The General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 1961
purpose: To amend the General Sales Tax Act, 1125, for the purposes hereinafter appearing, specifically concerning the sale of rice issued from Central or State Government depots, and to insert a new section regarding payment of tax by dealers on the basis of total turnover.
scope: This Act applies to the General Sales Tax Act, 1125. It covers the sale of rice issued from Central or State Government depots and payment of tax based on turnover. It also specifies exemptions and conditions for dealers.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 1961. It shall come into force with effect on and from the 1st day of April, 1961.

In section 4 of the General Sales Tax Act, 1125 (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), for the words "foreign liquor", the words "foreign liquor including Indian made foreign liquor" shall be substituted.

In section 5 of the principal Act, for clause (vi) of sub-section (1), the following clause shall be substituted: "(vi) the sale of rice issued from Central or State Government depots for sale through fair price shops declared as such by the Government by notification in the Gazette, shall be exempt from taxation under section 3, sub-section (1)."

After section 6 of the principal Act, the following section shall be inserted, namely: "6A. Payment of tax at compounded rates:-(1) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1) of section 3, every dealer whose total turnover in the year commencing on the 1st day of April, 1961, or any subsequent year, is not more than twenty-five thousand rupees may at his option, instead of paying the tax in accordance with the provisions of that sub-section, pay tax for that year at the following rates, namely :-
(i) Where the total turnover does not exceed fifteen thousand rupees - One hundred and fifty rupees per annum.
(ii) Where the total turnover exceeds fifteen thousand rupees but does not exceed twenty-five thousand rupees - Three hundred rupees per annum.
Provided that, -
(i) if the total turnover of a dealer relates only to the goods specified in Schedule I, he shall not be entitled to exercise the option under this sub-section ;
(ii) where the total turnover of a dealer relates both to the goods specified in Schedule I and to goods other than those specified in that Schedule, the dealer shall be entitled to exercise the option under this sub-section only in respect of the turnover relating to such other goods, and in respect of the turnover relating to the goods specified in Schedule I he shall be liable to pay the tax under sub-section (1) of section 3.
(2) Any dealer whose estimated total turnover for a year does not exceed twenty-five thousand rupees may apply to the assessing authority to be permitted to pay tax under this section, and, on being so permitted, he shall pay the tax due in advance during the year in monthly or other prescribed installments, and tax for that purpose shall submit such returns in such manner as may be prescribed.
(3) The tax paid under sub-section (2) shall be subject to such adjustment as may be prescribed on the completion of the final assessment in the manner prescribed."

In Schedule I of the principal Act, for item 1, the following items shall be substituted, namely :-
1. Foreign liquor including Indian made foreign liquor
2. Country liquor other than toddy
2A. Food grains

important_rules: Dealers whose total turnover does not exceed fifteen thousand rupees per annum can pay a compounded tax of one hundred and fifty rupees per annum.
Dealers whose total turnover exceeds fifteen thousand rupees but does not exceed twenty-five thousand rupees per annum can pay a compounded tax of three hundred rupees per annum.
Dealers whose turnover relates only to goods specified in Schedule I are not entitled to exercise the option for compounded tax.
Dealers with mixed turnover (Schedule I goods and other goods) can only exercise the option for compounded tax on turnover relating to non-Schedule I goods.
Dealers paying tax under sub-section (1) of section 3 will be liable for tax on Schedule I goods.
Dealers can apply to be permitted to pay tax in advance during the year in monthly or other prescribed installments if their estimated total turnover does not exceed twenty-five thousand rupees.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Assessing authority
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through prescribed assessment and return submission processes.

rights: Right to pay tax at compounded rates for eligible dealers (turnover not exceeding twenty-five thousand rupees).
duties: Dealers must pay tax in accordance with the provisions of the Act.
Dealers opting for compounded tax must pay it in advance.
Dealers must submit such returns in such manner as may be prescribed.
obligations: Dealers are obligated to pay tax on their sales as per the specified rates and procedures.

key_procedures: Application for permission to pay tax at compounded rates for dealers with estimated total turnover not exceeding twenty-five thousand rupees.
Payment of compounded tax in advance, in monthly or other prescribed installments.
Submission of returns in the prescribed manner.
Final assessment to adjust the tax paid.
Substitution of specific items in Schedule I.
administration: Department/agency that administers this
important_notes: The Act is published in the Gazette Extra-ordinary dated 30th March 1961.
The sale of rice issued from Central or State Government depots for sale through fair price shops is exempt from taxation.
The compounded tax rates apply to eligible dealers who opt for it.
The provisions for compounded tax are subject to conditions and may require application and permission from the assessing authority.

title: The General Sales Tax (Second Amendment and Validation) Act, 1962
purpose: To further amend the General Sales Tax Act, 1125, and to provide for certain other connected matters, including validation of actions taken under the principal Act.
scope: Applies to the matters connected with the General Sales Tax Act, 1125, and actions taken under its provisions.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the General Sales Tax (Second Amendment and Validation) Act, 1962. Section 2 shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of October, 1957.

Amends sub-section (2) of section 27 of the General Sales Tax Act, 1125 (Act XI of 1125), to provide that the powers and authorities appointed under the principal Act, and actions taken or notices issued by them, shall be deemed to be valid, even if questioned. The Government has the power to exercise these powers and issue such notices and orders.

Notwithstanding anything contained in any judgment, decree or order of any court, all actions done, notices issued, proceedings taken or orders passed under the provisions of any of the Acts repealed by sub-section (2) of section 27 of the principal Act, by the Government or by any officer or authority appointed under the principal Act, shall be deemed to be, and to have always been, validly done, issued, taken or passed as if such acts were done, notices were issued, proceedings were taken or orders were passed by the Government or by the corresponding officer or authority, as the case may be, under the aforesaid repealed Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government or any officer or authority appointed under the principal Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By issuing notices, taking proceedings, and passing orders, all of which are deemed valid.

key_procedures: Section 2 and 3 of this Act came into force on October 1, 1957, and are to be read as part of the General Sales Tax Act, 1125.
administration: The General Sales Tax Act, 1125, administered by the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act is a second amendment and validation act.
Published in the Gazette Extraordinary, dated the 19th April 1962.

Amends section 15 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 (Central Act 30 of 1956) by inserting a new clause (c) in sub-section (2). The new clause states that any property inherited by a female Hindu from her pre-deceased son shall not devolve, not upon the other heirs referred to in sub-section (1) in the order specified therein, but upon the heirs of the pre-deceased son from whom she inherited the property.

important_rules: Property inherited by a female Hindu from her pre-deceased son shall devolve upon the heirs of the pre-deceased son, not upon other heirs.

title: THE INDIAN REGISTRATION (KERALA AMENDMENT) ACT, 1968
purpose: To further amend the Indian Registration Act, 1908, in its application to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Indian Registration (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1968. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.
In sub-section (2) of section 17 of the Indian Registration Act, 1908 (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), clauses (ix) and (x) shall be omitted.
In section 19 of the principal Act, the words "and also by a true copy" shall be omitted.

After section 19 of the principal Act, the following section shall be inserted, namely:— “19A. Documents presented for registration to be accompanied by true copies thereof.—(1) No document shall be accepted for registration unless it is accompanied by a true copy thereof. (2) The true copy referred to in sub-section (1) shall be neatly handwritten, printed, typewritten, lithographed or otherwise prepared in accordance with such rules as may be made in this behalf.”

In section 45 of the principal Act, — (a) in sub-section (1), for the words, letters and figure "cause the contents thereof to be entered into his Book No. 3", the words, letters and figure "cause the contents thereof to be made and filed in his Book No. 3" shall be substituted; (b) in sub-section (2), for the words "copy has been made", the words "true copy has been filed" shall be substituted.

In sub-section (2) of section 46 of the principal Act,— (a) for the words "unless the will has been already copied", the words "unless a true copy of the will has already been filed" shall be substituted; (b) for the words, letters and figure "cause the will to be copied into his Book No. 3", the words, letters and figure "cause a true copy of the will to be made and filed in his Book No. 3" shall be substituted.

In section 51 of the principal Act,— (a) for sub-section (2) the following sub-section shall be substituted, namely:— “(2) In Book I all files be filed— (i) true copies of all documents; and (ii) all memoranda, registered under sections 17, 18 and 89 which relate to immovable property, and are not wills;”

important_rules: Rule: Documents presented for registration must be accompanied by a true copy thereof.
Rule: The true copy must be neatly handwritten, printed, typewritten, lithographed or otherwise prepared according to rules.
Rule: For Section 45, instead of entering contents into Book No. 3, the contents must be made and filed in Book No. 3.
Rule: For Section 46, a true copy of the will must be made and filed in Book No. 3, not just copied.
Rule: Book I shall contain true copies of all documents and all memoranda related to immovable property (excluding wills).

duties: Duty to provide a true copy of the document for registration.
obligations: Obligation to ensure the true copy is prepared according to specified methods.

key_procedures: Procedure: When presenting a document for registration, a true copy of the document must also be submitted.
Procedure: The true copy must be prepared in a neat and legible manner, either handwritten, printed, typewritten, lithographed, or otherwise as per prescribed rules.

Inserts a new section 10B titled 'Power to issue orders regarding terms and conditions of service pending settlement of disputes' into the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (Central Act 14 of 1947), as amended for the State of Kerala. This section empowers the State Government to issue orders concerning terms and conditions of employment or industrial peace, which are necessary or expedient for securing public safety, convenience, or the maintenance of public order or supplies and services essential to the life of the community.
This section is listed in the contents but not detailed in the provided text.
This section is listed in the contents but not detailed in the provided text.

important_rules: Section 10B(1): Where an industrial dispute has been referred by the State Government to a Labour Court or Tribunal, and in the opinion of that Government, it is necessary or expedient to do so for securing the public safety or convenience or the maintenance of public order or supplies and services essential to the life of the community, or for maintaining employment or industrial peace in the establishment concerning which such reference has been made, it may, by general or special order, make provision regarding terms and conditions of employment or work.
Section 10B(2)(a): Orders may be issued requiring employers to observe certain terms and conditions as may be specified.
Section 10B(2)(b): Orders may be issued for requiring any public utility service not to close or remain closed and to work or continue to work on such terms and conditions as may be specified.
Section 10B(2)(c): Orders may be issued for any incidental or supplementary matters which appear to be necessary or expedient for the purposes of the order.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through general or special orders issued under section 10B.

duties: Employers are obligated to observe specified terms and conditions of employment or work when ordered by the State Government.
Public utility services are obligated not to close or remain closed and to continue working under specified terms and conditions when ordered by the State Government.

key_procedures: When an industrial dispute is referred to a Labour Court or Tribunal, the State Government can issue orders under section 10B if it deems it necessary for specific reasons (public safety, convenience, etc.).
These orders can specify terms and conditions of employment or work for employers.
Specific provisions can be made for public utility services to remain operational.
Incidental and supplementary provisions can be included as needed.
administration: State Government (specifically powers vested under Section 10B)
important_notes: The amendment is in the application of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, to the State of Kerala.

purpose: To amend the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 in its application to the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.industrial_dispute: Refers to any dispute or difference between employers and workmen, or between workmen and workmen, which is connected with the employment or non-employment or the terms of employment or with the conditions of labour, of any person.
key_definitions.workman: Means any person who is employed in any industry to do any manual, unskilled, skilled, technical, operational, clerical or any other kind of work, for hire or reward, whether the terms of employment be expressed or implied, and includes for the purposes of any proceedings under this Act in relation to a dispute, a person who has been dismissed, discharged or retrenched, or otherwise terminated from employment.

important_rules: Disputes relating to termination of service of individual workmen are to be treated as industrial disputes.
The Act shall be deemed to have come into force on September 27, 2017.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly detailed in the provided text, but typically the Labour Department or relevant industrial tribunals/courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings, tribunals, and courts.

rights: Right of individual workmen to have their disputes regarding termination, dismissal, discharge, or retrenchment treated as industrial disputes.

key_procedures: If an individual workman's dispute regarding termination, dismissal, discharge, or retrenchment is not settled by mutual negotiation, it is to be treated as an industrial dispute under the Act.
administration: Labour Department, Government of Kerala (inferred from the nature of the act and the Gazette notification).
important_notes: This is an amendment to the existing Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.
The amendment aims to provide a more robust mechanism for resolving individual disputes.
The notification is from the Kerala Gazette, Part I.

purpose: To regulate the manufacture, storage, sale, and distribution of livestock feed, poultry feed, and mineral mixtures in Kerala to ensure quality, safety, and prevent adulteration and harmful practices.
scope: This Act applies to all livestock feed, poultry feed, and mineral mixtures manufactured, stored, transported, sold, offered for sale, or held within the State of Kerala. It applies to all persons, companies, institutions, establishments, and societies involved in these activities.

key_definitions.poultry feed: Includes feed for chickens, ducks, turkeys, and other domestic birds.
key_definitions.mineral mixture: Includes supplements containing essential minerals for livestock and poultry.
key_definitions.adulterated: Means any feed which is mixed or diluted with any substance whether wholly or in part so as to reduce or injuriously affect its quality, strength or purity.
key_definitions.substandard: Means any feed which is not in conformity with the prescribed standards.
key_definitions.misbranded: Means any feed which is incorrectly labelled as to the name, or which bears a label or other information concerning such article which is false or misleading in any material respect.

main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to notify laboratories as primary analytical laboratories and referral laboratories for analyzing samples of livestock feed, poultry feed, or mineral mixture.

Details the process for collecting samples of feed for analysis, including dividing samples into parts, sealing, marking, and obtaining signatures of relevant parties and witnesses. It also outlines the powers of entry and inspection for Feed Safety Assurance Officers.

Specifies the duties of the Feed Safety Assurance Officer regarding the handling and submission of collected samples for analysis, including delivering sealed samples to relevant parties and submitting samples to analytical laboratories.
Mandates that analysis reports from approved laboratories be delivered within a maximum period of twenty-one days and prohibits the display or use of these reports for advertisement.

main_sections.section_title: Confiscation and disposal by Feed Safety Assurance Officer
main_sections.description: Grants the Feed Safety Assurance Officer or authorized officers the power to seize and dispose of livestock feed, poultry feed, or mineral mixture that is unlicensed, adulterated, substandard, or misbranded.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure for Inquiry by Licensing Authority
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for the Licensing Authority to conduct inquiries into contraventions of the Act, requiring a reasonable opportunity of being heard for the accused.
Defines penalties for violations, including suspension or cancellation of licenses and fines, with escalating penalties for subsequent violations or when severe harm is caused.
Provides for the right to appeal against orders imposing penalties to the State Feed Quality Consultative Committee.

main_sections.section_title: Offences to be tried by the Court
main_sections.description: Specifies offenses that are punishable by a Court, including imprisonment and fines, particularly for third and subsequent violations, or when severe harm to livestock/poultry occurs. It also allows for forfeiture of seized feed and compensation to affected owners.

States that no Court shall take cognizance of an offense under the Act except on a written complaint by the Feed Safety Enforcement Officer and that such offenses are triable by a Judicial Magistrate of the First Class.

main_sections.section_title: Offences by Companies, Institutions, Establishments or Societies
main_sections.description: Makes provisions for offenses committed by corporate entities, holding individuals in charge responsible, with provisions for proving lack of knowledge or due diligence.

important_rules: Samples collected for analysis must be divided into five parts, marked, sealed, and fastened in an air-tight container in the presence of two witnesses.
No person shall obstruct a Feed Safety Assurance Officer from collecting samples.
When a sample is taken from an authorized agent, dealer, or transporter, they must furnish the name and details of the person on whose behalf the stock is held.
Persons who have purchased feed for their own use and possess a voucher may apply to have their samples analyzed at their own expense.
Analysis reports cannot be displayed on premises or used for advertisement.

penalties: First violation: Suspension of license (60 days to 6 months) or fine (₹25,000 to ₹50,000) or both.
Second violation: Suspension of license (6 months to 1 year) or fine (₹50,000 to ₹2 lakh) or both.
Third violation or severe injury/harm/death to livestock/poultry: Cancellation of license (up to 5 years) by Licensing Authority.

For third or continuing offenses, or severe violations recommended by the State Feed Quality Consultative Committee and proved by two labs, or causing death/serious injury/harm to livestock/poultry: Imprisonment (6 months to 1 year) and fine (up to ₹10 lakh) by Court.
Compensation to the owner of livestock/poultry for death or severe injury/harm, recoverable as arrears of land revenue if not paid.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Feed Safety Assurance Officer, Feed Safety Enforcement Officer, Licensing Authority, State Feed Quality Consultative Committee, and Courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, sampling, analysis of feed, inquiries by Licensing Authority, imposition of penalties, appeals, and prosecution in courts. Seizure and disposal of non-compliant feed are also key enforcement mechanisms.

rights: Right to a reasonable opportunity of being heard before an inquiry or penalty.
Right to appeal against orders imposing penalties.
Right to obtain compensation for livestock/poultry affected by violations.
duties: Manufacturers, storers, sellers, and distributors must adhere to quality and safety standards.
Persons from whom samples are taken must cooperate with Feed Safety Assurance Officers.
Companies and institutions have a duty to ensure their operations comply with the Act.
Licensed entities have a duty to operate within the terms and conditions of their license.
obligations: To ensure that livestock feed, poultry feed, and mineral mixtures are not adulterated, substandard, or misbranded.
To obtain and maintain necessary licenses for manufacture, storage, sale, and distribution.
To allow authorized officers to enter establishments, inspect premises, and collect samples.
To cooperate with inquiries and provide necessary documents and information.

key_procedures: Sample collection and analysis: A Feed Safety Assurance Officer collects samples, divides them, seals them, and sends them to an approved laboratory for analysis. The report is then used to determine further action.
Inquiry and penalty imposition: If a contravention is suspected, the Licensing Authority conducts an inquiry, affords a hearing, and if a violation is found, imposes penalties as prescribed.
Appeal process: An aggrieved person can appeal a penalty order to the State Feed Quality Consultative Committee within thirty days.

Court proceedings: Serious offenses are tried by a Court of Judicial Magistrate of the First Class, based on a complaint from the Feed Safety Enforcement Officer and recommendation from the State Feed Quality Consultative Committee.
administration: The administration and enforcement of this Act involve multiple authorities, including the Licensing Authority, Feed Safety Assurance Officers, Feed Safety Enforcement Officers, and the State Feed Quality Consultative Committee.
important_notes: If a sample is found to cause immediate health hazards, the expenses for analysis shall be borne by the licensee.
In case of a contradiction in analysis reports from two labs, the sample will be sent to a referral lab.
Offenses by companies can lead to prosecution of individuals in charge, unless they prove the offense was without their knowledge or they exercised due diligence.

title: The Kerala Abkari Workers’ Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2022
purpose: To amend the Kerala Abkari Workers’ Welfare Fund Act, 1989, to include new categories of workers in the definition of 'Abkari Worker' and to modify contribution rates and procedures related to the welfare fund.
scope: This Act applies to abkari workers in Kerala and their welfare fund, as established by the Kerala Abkari Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 1989. It amends specific sections of the principal Act.

key_definitions.Abkari Worker: The amendment expands the scope of 'Abkari Worker' to include individuals involved in 'labelling, transport to warehouses or wholesale shops or bars or clubs,' in addition to existing definitions.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Kerala Abkari Workers' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2022, and states that it shall come into force immediately.
Amends clause (a) of section 2 of the principal Act by replacing 'transport' with 'labelling, transport to warehouses or wholesale shops or bars or clubs'.

Inserts a new section 3A titled 'Publication of list of Abkari Workers as members'. This section details the process for maintaining a register of abkari workers, publishing an annual list of members and those removed, handling objections, and decision-making by the Chairman of the Board.
Amends section 4 of the principal Act by substituting sub-section (1) with new contribution rates and also amends sub-section (2).

important_rules: Rule 1 (from Section 3A(1)): The Chief Welfare Fund Inspector must maintain a register of workers enrolled in the Abkari Workers' Welfare Fund, including the employer's name.
Rule 2 (from Section 3A(2)): An annual list of members and those removed from membership must be published by the Chief Welfare Fund Inspector before March 31st for public notice and objections.
Rule 3 (from Section 3A(3)): Objections to the published list must be submitted to the Chief Welfare Fund Inspector within 30 days of publication.
Rule 4 (from Section 3A(5)): The Chairman of the Board must consider objections, provide a hearing opportunity, and make decisions and consequential changes to the list.

Rule 5 (from Section 4(1)): Employer contribution to the fund shall be ten percent of the wages payable to each abkari worker. Abkari worker's contribution shall be eleven and a half percent of their monthly wage.
Rule 6 (from Section 4(2)): The percentage in sub-section (2) of section 4 is changed from 'five per cent' to 'seven per cent'.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Chief Welfare Fund Inspector and the Chairman of the Board.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the processes outlined in the Act, including maintaining registers, publishing lists, handling objections, and making decisions. Enforcement of contribution rules is implied but not explicitly detailed in the provided text.

rights: Right to be heard before any decision is made regarding objections to the membership list (Section 3A(5)).
duties: Duty of the Chief Welfare Fund Inspector to maintain registers and publish lists (Section 3A(1) & (2)).
Duty of abkari workers and employers to contribute to the fund as per the specified percentages (Section 4).
obligations: Obligation for the Chief Welfare Fund Inspector to submit objections to the Chairman (Section 3A(4)).
Obligation for the Chairman to consider objections and take decisions (Section 3A(5)).

key_procedures: Publication of Abkari Workers' Membership List: The Chief Welfare Fund Inspector maintains a register, publishes an annual list of members and those removed, receives objections within 30 days, submits objections to the Chairman, who then hears aggrieved parties and makes a decision and updates the list accordingly.

Contribution Calculation and Payment: Employers must contribute 10% of abkari worker wages, and abkari workers must contribute 11.5% of their monthly wages. (Note: Specific procedures for payment and collection are not detailed in this amendment).
administration: Law (Legislation-C) Department, Government of Kerala. The operational administration of the fund appears to involve the Chief Welfare Fund Inspector and the Board.
important_notes: The amendment significantly alters the scope of 'Abkari Worker' to be more inclusive of activities related to distribution and sale.
The contribution rates for both employers and workers have been revised.
A new procedural mechanism for maintaining transparency and addressing grievances regarding the membership list has been introduced.

title: THE KERALA AGRICULTURAL INCOME TAX (REPEAL) ACT, 2021
purpose: To repeal the Kerala Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1991.
scope: This act applies to the State of Kerala and its jurisdiction. It repeals the previous Agricultural Income Tax Act of 1991.

main_sections.description: This section names the act as the Kerala Agricultural Income Tax (Repeal) Act, 2021, and states that it comes into force at once.

This section repeals the Kerala Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1991 (15 of 1991). It includes provisions that ensure that the repeal does not affect actions, offenses, penalties, proceedings, rights, obligations, or liabilities incurred under the repealed Act. It also specifies how pending matters, appeals, and revisions under the repealed Act should be handled.

important_rules: Rule: The repeal of the Kerala Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1991, shall not affect anything done or any offense committed, or any fine or penalty incurred, or any proceedings initiated before the commencement of this Act.
Rule: The repeal shall not revive anything not in force or existing at the time the repeal takes effect.
Rule: The repeal shall not affect the previous operation of the repealed Act or anything duly done or suffered thereunder.
Rule: The repeal shall not affect any right, privilege, obligation, or liability acquired, accrued, or incurred under the repealed Act.
Rule: The repeal shall not affect any fine, penalty, forfeiture, or punishment incurred in respect of any offense committed against the repealed Act.

Rule: The repeal shall not affect any investigation, legal proceedings, or remedy in respect of any such right, privilege, obligation, liability, fines, penalty, forfeiture, or punishment, and such matters may be instituted, continued, or enforced as if the Act had not been passed.
Rule: Pending applications, appeals, or revisions before any authority or officer appointed under the repealed Act shall be heard and disposed of as if the Act had not been passed.
Rule: Pending appeals before the appellate authority appointed under the repealed Act shall be heard and disposed of as if the Act had not been passed.

Rule: Nothing in the repeal section shall affect the right to continue and complete proceedings related to tax assessment, imposition, collection, and levying under the repealed Act, including the liability to pay amounts due and the right to refunds.

penalties: Any fine, penalty, forfeiture, or punishment incurred in respect of any offense committed against the repealed Act shall still be imposed as if the repealing Act had not been passed.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Authorities and officers appointed under the repealed Act, and appellate authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Investigations, legal proceedings, and remedies may be instituted, continued, or enforced as if the repealing Act had not been passed. Pending matters will be heard and disposed of by existing authorities.

rights: Right to refunds under the repealed Act.
Rights acquired, accrued, or incurred under the repealed Act continue to be protected.
duties: Liability to pay the amount due from any person under the repealed Act continues.
obligations: Obligations acquired, accrued, or incurred under the repealed Act continue to be protected.

key_procedures: Procedure for handling pending applications, appeals, and revisions under the repealed Act: These will be heard and disposed of by the relevant authorities as if the repealing Act had not been passed.
Procedure for continuing and completing tax assessment, imposition, collection, and levying under the repealed Act: These proceedings remain unaffected and can be continued and completed.
administration: Law (Legislation-A) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The act is a repeal act, meaning its primary function is to nullify a previous act.
The savings clause is extensive, ensuring that past actions and liabilities under the repealed Act are not extinguished.

title: THE KERALA AGRICULTURAL WORKERS’ (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2021
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Agricultural Workers’ Act, 1974, for the purposes specified therein.
scope: This act applies to agricultural land and agricultural workers within the state of Kerala. It amends the provisions related to contributions to the Agricultural Workers' Welfare Fund.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Agricultural Workers’ (Amendment) Act, 2021, and that it shall be deemed to have come into force on January 16, 2020.

This section amends Section 9 of the Kerala Agricultural Workers’ Act, 1974. It modifies sub-sections (1), (2), and (4) concerning contributions to the Agricultural Workers' Welfare Fund. Specifically, it revises the rates of contribution for landowners based on the extent of land held, increases the penalty amount, and alters the government's contribution to the Fund.

This section repeals the Kerala Agricultural Workers’ (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021 (133 of 2021) and clarifies that any actions taken under the Ordinance are deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Landowners holding between twenty Ares and forty Ares of agricultural land shall pay fifty paise per Are per annum as contribution to the Fund.
Landowners holding more than forty Ares of agricultural land shall contribute one rupee per Are per annum to the Fund.
The penalty for certain offenses under sub-section (2) of section 9 has been increased from five rupees to twenty rupees.

The Government shall contribute to the Fund an amount equal to twenty-five percent of the contribution paid by registered agricultural workers annually, with a maximum limit of five rupees per capita.

penalties: The penalty under sub-section (2) of section 9 has been increased from five rupees to twenty rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but implied to be the relevant government department overseeing agricultural workers and land ownership in Kerala.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not explicitly detailed in the provided text, but likely involves the collection of contributions and enforcement of payment obligations by the designated authority.

duties: Landowners have a duty to contribute to the Agricultural Workers' Welfare Fund based on the extent of agricultural land they hold.
Agricultural workers are expected to contribute to the Fund, upon which the government's contribution is based.
obligations: Obligation for landowners to pay specified contributions to the Fund.
Obligation for the Government to contribute to the Fund as specified.

key_procedures: Contribution calculation and payment by landowners based on land extent.
Government's contribution to the Fund based on registered agricultural workers' contributions.
administration: The Law (Legislation-C) Department, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on January 16, 2020.
The amendments are made to the Kerala Agricultural Workers’ Act, 1974.

title: THE KERALA BUILDING TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2023
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Building Tax Act, 1975, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to buildings within Kerala and the assessment and taxation of building tax and additional tax.

key_definitions.principal Act: The Kerala Building Tax Act, 1975 (7 of 1975)

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Government by notification in the Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of certain expression by certain other expression
main_sections.description: Substitutes the expression 'luxury tax' with 'additional tax' wherever it occurs in the principal Act.

Substitutes Explanation 2 to clause (e) of section 2 of the principal Act. This amendment clarifies the assessment of buildings with multiple apartments or flats, especially concerning ownership, plinth area, and scenarios involving builders retaining parts of the building or purchasers owning interconnected units.

Amends section 5A of the principal Act by substituting the marginal heading and sub-section (1). It introduces or clarifies the charging of an annual additional tax on residential buildings with a plinth area of 278.7 square metres and above, completed on or after April 1, 1999.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 6
main_sections.description: Replaces section 6 of the principal Act. The new section clarifies that the plinth area for the purpose of assessment of building tax or additional tax shall be as specified in the software/occupancy certificate/tax assessment details approved by Local Self Government Institutions.
Substitutes sub-section (2) of section 13 of the principal Act. This amendment restricts the District Collector from suo motu revising an order if it was passed more than one year previously.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 21
main_sections.description: Replaces section 21 of the principal Act. The new section provides that if on further verification, information provided in a return under section 7 or an amended return under section 8 is found to be false, fifty per cent of the building tax shall be levied as a fine.

important_rules: Rule 1: For buildings with multiple apartments/flats owned by different persons, each apartment/flat is deemed a separate building, assessed based on ownership and plinth area specified in approved documentation. (Section 3(i))

Rule 2: If a builder retains ownership of part or whole of a building, they are liable for building and additional tax on the retained plinth area. If the owner sells parts after assessment, each part is assessed separately for additional tax only. (Section 3(ii))

Rule 3: If a person buys interconnected flats/apartments, it's treated as a single unit for tax assessment based on aggregate plinth area. Non-interconnected units are assessed separately. (Section 3(iii))
Rule 4: An additional tax is levied annually on residential buildings with a plinth area of 278.7 sq metres or more, completed on or after April 1, 1999. (Section 4(ii))
Rule 5: The plinth area for tax assessment is determined by the software/occupancy certificate/tax assessment details approved by Local Self Government Institutions. (Section 5)
Rule 6: The District Collector cannot suo motu revise an order if it was passed more than one year ago. (Section 6)
Rule 7: Providing false statements in returns for assessment will result in a fine of fifty percent of the building tax. (Section 7)

penalties: Fifty per cent of the building tax shall be levied as a fine if false statements are furnished for assessment.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Implied to be the assessing authority and District Collector, as per sections 13 and 21 of the principal Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment of building tax and additional tax based on plinth area and ownership, with provisions for revision by authorities and penalties for false information.

rights: Right to have building tax and additional tax assessed based on specified plinth area documentation.
duties: Duty to pay building tax and additional tax.
Duty to furnish true and correct information in returns for assessment.
obligations: Obligation to pay additional tax on residential buildings above a certain plinth area and completion date.
Obligation for builders to pay tax on retained plinth area.
Obligation for owners of interconnected flats/apartments to pay tax on aggregate plinth area.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Amendment of Section 3 - Assessment of buildings with multiple apartments/flats involves determining ownership, plinth area from approved documents, and separate assessment for units or interconnected units as specified.
Procedure 2: Amendment of Section 4 - Levy of additional tax on residential buildings meeting specific plinth area and completion date criteria.
Procedure 3: Amendment of Section 5 - Determination of plinth area for tax assessment relies on documentation approved by Local Self Government Institutions.
Procedure 4: Amendment of Section 7 - Filing of returns (original and amended) and the consequence of providing false information, leading to a fine of 50% of building tax.
administration: Law (Legislation-B) Department, Government of Kerala, and Local Self Government Institutions for approving documentation.
important_notes: The Act comes into force on a date to be notified by the Government.
The term 'luxury tax' has been replaced by 'additional tax'.

important_rules: Rule 1 (Section 16A): Before imposing a penalty under section 16, the Government will designate an officer (Joint Director equivalent) who must provide the dealer with written directions and a time period (not exceeding ninety days) to comply with the provisions. If the dealer complies within this period, no proceedings will be initiated.

Rule 2 (Section 16B(1)): Failure to pay the penalty imposed under section 16 within ninety days of receiving the order copy will result in punishment of imprisonment up to six months and a fine double the penalty amount.
Rule 3 (Section 16C(1)): An officer designated under section 16A, after conducting an inquiry, shall impose the penalty as provided under the Act.
Rule 4 (Section 16D(1)): Offences under section 16B can be compounded by the Compounding Officer upon payment of seventy-five percent of the penalty amount, either before or after prosecution starts.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months and with fine of double the amount imposed as penalty for default in payment of penalty (Section 16B(1)).
Penalty of twenty-five thousand rupees for offences under sections 16(1), 16(2), and 16(3) of the principal Act (as amended by this Act).
Penalty to be imposed by the designated officer after an enquiry (Section 16C(1)).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Designated officers by the Government, including an officer equivalent to the rank of Joint Director in the Industries/Coir Department (Section 16A) and the Appellate Authority (Section 16C(3)). penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through designated officers conducting inquiries, imposing penalties, and offering opportunities for compliance or compounding of offences. Appeals can be filed against orders of the designated officer.

rights: Right to be given an opportunity to comply before penalty imposition (Section 16A).

Right to have an appeal heard by the Appellate Authority (Section 16C(4)).

duties: Duty to pay penalty within ninety days of receipt of order (Section 16B(1)).
Duty to comply with directions and time limits set by the designated officer (Section 16A).
Duty to appear and provide evidence or documents when summoned by the inquiry officer (Section 16C(2)).
obligations: Obligation of the Government to designate officers for penalty imposition and compounding (Sections 16A, 16D).
Obligation of the officer to conduct inquiries and impose penalties (Section 16C(1)).
Obligation of the Appellate Authority to hear appeals and pass orders (Section 16C(4)).

key_procedures: Procedure for imposing penalty: Government designates an officer, who provides a dealer with a written direction and a time limit (up to 90 days) for compliance. If complied, no proceedings. If not, inquiry and penalty imposition by the officer (Sections 16A, 16C).

Procedure for appeal: A person aggrieved by an officer's order can file an appeal with the Appellate Authority within 30 days. The Appellate Authority can entertain late appeals if sufficient cause is shown and must pass an order within 60 days after hearing parties (Section 16C(3), 16C(4)).
Procedure for compounding offences: An accused can apply to the Compounding Officer before or after prosecution to compound the offence by paying 75% of the penalty (Section 16D).
administration: Law (Legislation-C) Department, Government of Kerala is responsible for the notification and publication. The administration of the act involves designated officers from Industries/Coir Department and the Appellate Authority.
important_notes: The penalty for offences under section 16 has been significantly increased from potential imprisonment and fines to a fixed penalty of twenty-five thousand rupees.
Sub-section (4) of section 16 of the principal Act has been omitted.
Penalties collected are to be credited to the Consolidated Fund of the State (Section 16C(5)).
No court inferior to a Judicial Magistrate of the First Class can try offences under section 16B(1).
No court can take cognizance of an offence under section 16B(1) without the previous sanction of the officer authorized to impose penalty and his written report.

Obligation to follow the legislative process for amending contribution and grant rates through notifications.

important_rules: Rule 1: Prior to imposing a penalty under section 17, an opportunity must be given to the person concerned to comply with relevant provisions within a time period not exceeding ninety days. If compliance is achieved, no proceedings shall be initiated.

penalties: Liability to a penalty of double the amount due by him under this Act (for offenses under section 17(1)).
Liability to a penalty of twenty-five thousand rupees (for offenses under section 17(2)).
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months and with a fine of double the amount imposed as penalty for non-payment of penalty under section 17B(1).
Compounding of offences under section 17B on payment of seventy-five percent of the fine provided.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Officers designated by the Government, including an officer equivalent to the rank of Coir Project Officer in the Industries/Coir Department (for imposing penalties), and an officer equivalent to the rank of Joint Director in the Industries/Coir Department (for compounding offenses).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Penalties are imposed after an enquiry. Recovery of dues is done as per the Kerala Revenue Recovery Act, 1968. Offences under section 17B are tried by a Judicial Magistrate of the First Class.

rights: Right to an opportunity to comply with provisions before penalty imposition (Section 17A).

Right to have an appeal entertained after expiry of the period if prevented by sufficient cause (Section 17C(3)).

obligations: Obligation to pay penalties as determined by the authorities.

Obligation to cooperate with inquiries conducted by officers.

administration: The Industries/Coir Department of the Government of Kerala appears to be the administering department, as officers from this department are designated for imposing penalties and compounding offenses.

title: THE KERALA DAIRY FARMERS WELFARE FUND (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2023
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Dairy Farmers’ Welfare Fund Act, 2007, to provide for the constitution of a Fund to grant relief to dairy farmers engaged in cattle rearing in Kerala, ensure their welfare, pay pensions, implement insurance schemes for them and their families, and provide other financial assistance, including schemes for the distribution of feed and medicine for their cattle.
scope: The Act applies to dairy farmers engaged in cattle rearing in the State of Kerala. It also amends definitions and provisions related to co-operative societies and the administration of the Fund within the state.

key_definitions.Anand Pattern Milk Producers Co -operati: Milk Producers Co-operative Societies registered and functioning in Kerala after January 1, 1980, under the administrative control of the Dairy Development Department, as per the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969 and its rules.
key_definitions.Traditional Primary Milk Co-operative So: Primary Milk Co-operative Societies (Dairy Co-operative Societies, Milk Producers Co-operative Societies) registered and functioning prior to the commencement of the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969, under erstwhile laws in Travancore, Kochi, Travancore-Kochi, and Malabar areas, and those registered before January 1, 1980, and functioning under the 1969 Act and its rules, all under the administrative control of the Dairy Development Department.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Kerala Dairy Farmers’ Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2023, and that it shall come into force at once.

Substitutes the long title of the principal Act (Kerala Dairy Farmers’ Welfare Fund Act, 2007) with a revised title reflecting the expanded purpose of the Act regarding welfare, pension, insurance, and financial assistance for dairy farmers and their families.
Substitutes the preamble of the principal Act with a revised preamble mirroring the expanded purpose mentioned in the amended long title.

Amends section 2 of the principal Act by inserting a new definition for 'Anand Pattern Milk Producers Co-operative Society' and 'Traditional Primary Milk Co-operative Society', and modifying the definition in clause (d) related to milk marketing.

Amends section 3 of the principal Act by substituting item (iv) of sub-section (2) to include receipts from various entities like cattle feed manufacturing establishments and veterinary medicine distributors, and by inserting a new clause (e) in sub-section (4) related to schemes for the distribution of medicines and equipment for cattle.

Amends section 4 of the principal Act by substituting sub-section (2) regarding the application process for membership (online or offline submission and verification) and substituting sub-section (4) detailing the procedure for rejection of applications and the requirement to provide an opportunity for being heard.

Replaces section 6 of the principal Act with a new section requiring societies to maintain registers detailing milk quantity, dates, member information, pensioner details, contribution details, and details of contributions collected from dairy farmers, and to submit these registers for inspection by the Chief Executive Officer or authorized officers.

Amends section 8 of the principal Act by substituting sub-section (3) to specify the composition of the Board of Directors, which will consist of sixteen directors, including representatives from milk co-operative unions, traditional primary milk co-operative societies, Anand Pattern milk producer co-operative societies, the Chief Executive Officer, and government-nominated officials from various departments.

Amends section 11 of the principal Act by substituting sub-section (2) to define the Chief Executive Officer as a whole-time officer of the Dairy Development Department, who will participate in Board meetings and maintain records.

Amends section 13 of the principal Act by inserting sub-section (4) which empowers the Board to collect contributions from dairy farmers and remit them to the Fund monthly, or recover them from the concerned society secretary along with arrears if not remitted.

important_rules: Societies must maintain detailed registers regarding milk collection, member contributions, and pensioner information.
Applications for membership must be submitted in a prescribed format, either offline or online, and are subject to verification and approval by the Chief Executive Officer.
Dairy farmers' contributions must be remitted to the Fund by the society monthly, failing which the Board has the power to recover the amount with arrears.
The Board of Directors will consist of sixteen members with specific representation from various co-operative bodies and government officials.

rights: Dairy farmers have the right to relief, welfare, pension, and insurance schemes.
Dairy farmers have the right to be heard before their membership application is rejected.
Dairy farmers have the right to receive financial assistance, including schemes for feed and medicine.
duties: Societies have a duty to maintain proper registers and submit them for inspection.
Societies have a duty to remit contributions to the Fund monthly.
Dairy farmers have a duty to make contributions to the Fund as prescribed.
obligations: Societies are obligated to facilitate the collection and remittance of contributions from dairy farmers.
Dairy farmers are obligated to comply with the provisions of the Act and the rules made thereunder.

key_procedures: Membership Application Procedure: An application for membership must be submitted in the prescribed format (offline or online). The concerned milk society will review the application and forward it to the Chief Executive Officer. The empowered Dairy Development Department Officer will verify the application at the applicant's residence and submit it to the Board. If the Board decides to reject the application, the applicant must be notified in writing or online within fifteen days of the decision, along with the reasons for rejection. An opportunity to be heard must be given before rejecting an application.

Contribution Remittance Procedure: Dairy farmers' contributions must be remitted to the Fund by the society by the end of the month. If not remitted, the Board has the power to recover the amount from the concerned society secretary along with arrears, with the arrears charged at the monthly rate.
