The amendments focus on membership revival for members in arrears and introduce a provision for a onetime settlement scheme.

title: THE KERALA EMPLOYMENT GUARANTEE WORKERS WELFARE FUND ACT, 2021
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a Fund to grant relief to, to ensure the welfare of, to pay pension and other benefits to the workers who come under the purview of Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme and Ayyankali Urban Employment Guarantee Scheme in the State of Kerala, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala and covers workers registered under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme and the Ayyankali Urban Employment Guarantee Scheme. It also applies to matters connected with or incidental to the welfare fund for these workers.

key_definitions.Board: The Kerala Employment Guarantee Workers’ Welfare Fund Board constituted under sub-section (1) of section 8.
key_definitions.Chief Executive Officer: The Chief Executive Officer appointed under sub-section (1) of section 13.
key_definitions.contribution: The sum of money payable to the Fund under sub-section (1) of section 4.
key_definitions.District Welfare Officer: The District Welfare Officer appointed under sub-section (1) of section 13.
key_definitions.Employment Guarantee Worker: A worker who has received an employment guarantee card by registering in grama panchayats or Municipal Council/Corporation in the State, based on the provisions of the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005 or the Ayyankali Urban Employment Guarantee Scheme.
key_definitions.family: Wife or husband, their minor children and unmarried daughters, and includes father, mother or mentally or physically disabled children or widowed daughters who are solely dependent on the worker.
key_definitions.Fund: The Kerala Employment Guarantee Workers' Fund constituted under sub-section (1) of section 3.
key_definitions.identity card: An identity card issued by the Board to the employment guarantee worker.
key_definitions.member: A member of the Fund.
key_definitions.Mission Director: The Kerala State Mission Director for the implementation of Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme or Director of Urban Affairs, having State level charge of Ayyankali Urban Employment Guarantee Mission.
key_definitions.Notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette of the Government of Kerala.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Scheme: The Kerala Employment Guarantee Workers’ Welfare Fund Scheme framed under sub-section (1) of section 3.
key_definitions.year: A financial year which commences from 1st April.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act as the Kerala Employment Guarantee Workers’ Welfare Fund Act, 2021, and states that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Government by notification in the Gazette.

This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including Board, Chief Executive Officer, contribution, District Welfare Officer, Employment Guarantee Worker, family, Fund, Government, identity card, member, Mission Director, Notification, prescribed, Schedule, Scheme, and year.

main_sections.section_title: Kerala Employment Guarantee Workers’ Welfare Fund
main_sections.description: This section provides for the framing of the Kerala Employment Guarantee Workers’ Welfare Fund Scheme by the Government and the constitution of a Fund. It details what shall be credited to the Fund, how it will be administered, and the purposes for which the Fund may be utilized. It also outlines the process for laying the Scheme before the Legislative Assembly.

This section specifies the contribution payable by every worker who joins the Fund, the modes of remittance, and the contributions to be made by the Government and the State Government. It also allows for modification of the contribution rate by the Government.
This section defines the eligibility criteria for membership in the Fund, specifying age limits and the requirement of having received an employment guarantee card.

This section empowers the Government to remove any difficulties in the operation of the Act by issuing an order in the Gazette, provided such order is not inconsistent with the Act and is issued within two years of the Act's commencement. Such orders must be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

This section grants the Government the power to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act. It also details the procedure for laying these rules before the Legislative Assembly for approval or amendment.

This section repeals the Kerala Employment Guarantee Workers’ Welfare Fund Ordinance, 2021 (Ordinance No. 125 of 2021) and states that anything done or omitted to be done under the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or omitted to be done under this Act.

important_rules: Every worker joining the Fund shall contribute Rs. 50 per month.
Contributions can be remitted monthly, half-yearly, or yearly in approved banks.
The Government and the State Government shall also contribute to the Fund.
The Government can modify the contribution rate every three years by notification.
Membership in the Fund is for employment guarantee workers aged between 18 and 55 years who have an employment guarantee card.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala and the Board established under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through rules and schemes framed under the Act, and by the Board which administers the Fund.

rights: Right to receive relief and welfare benefits as prescribed.
Right to pension and other benefits upon meeting eligibility criteria.
Right to access financial assistance for specific purposes (treatment, marriage, education).
duties: Duty of every worker to contribute to the Fund.
Duty to register and obtain an employment guarantee card to be eligible for membership.
obligations: Obligation of the Government to frame the Scheme and constitute the Fund.
Obligation of the Board to administer the Fund and disburse benefits.
Obligation to comply with the rules and provisions of the Act and the Scheme.

key_procedures: Framing of the Kerala Employment Guarantee Workers’ Welfare Fund Scheme by the Government.
Constitution of the Kerala Employment Guarantee Workers’ Welfare Fund.
Contribution by workers and the Government to the Fund.
Application for and disbursement of benefits (pension, family pension, financial assistance) from the Fund.
Issuance and renewal of identity cards to members.
Procedure for laying the Scheme and rules before the Legislative Assembly.
Procedure for removing grievances of members.
administration: The Fund is vested in and administered by the Kerala Employment Guarantee Workers’ Welfare Fund Board, under the overall purview of the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act repeals the Kerala Employment Guarantee Workers’ Welfare Fund Ordinance, 2021.
Orders issued by the Government to remove difficulties are subject to approval by the Legislative Assembly and have a time limit of two years from the commencement of the Act.
The Scheme and rules made under the Act are subject to scrutiny and amendment by the Legislative Assembly.

title: THE KERALA EPIDEMIC DISEASES ACT, 2021
purpose: To unify and consolidate the laws relating to the regulation and prevention of epidemic diseases and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala. It governs the regulation and prevention of epidemic diseases and related matters.

key_definitions.epidemic disease: Any disease declared as epidemic disease by notification published in the official gazette, by the Government.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules or regulations made under this Act.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its commencement. Section 8 came into force on July 4, 2020, and other sections on March 27, 2020.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Epidemic Disease', 'Government', 'prescribed', 'regulation', and 'State'.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to notify epidemic disease
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to notify any disease as an epidemic disease by notification in the official gazette, either for the entire State or specific parts thereof.

main_sections.section_title: Power to take special measures and specify Regulations as to epidemic disease
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to take necessary measures and specify temporary regulations or orders to prevent the outbreak or spread of epidemic diseases. This includes powers to prohibit certain activities, inspect arriving persons, seal borders, impose transport restrictions, prescribe social distancing norms, restrict congregations, regulate offices and institutions, and control the functioning of shops, commercial establishments, and factories.

Prescribes penalties for contravention of regulations or orders made under the Act, or for obstructing empowered officers. Penalties include imprisonment up to two years or a fine up to ten thousand rupees, or both.
Specifies penalties for any person who resists or obstructs the execution of any duty under the Act. Penalties include imprisonment up to two years or a fine up to ten thousand rupees, or both.

main_sections.section_title: Offences under this Act to be cognizable and non-bailable
main_sections.description: Declares all offences under this Act to be cognizable and non-bailable, notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
Allows for the compounding of offences punishable under the Act by authorized officers before or after the commencement of proceedings, with the permission of the court.

main_sections.section_title: Saving as to certain other laws
main_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act are in addition to and not in derogation of any other law for the time being in force.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection against legal proceedings for any act done or intended to be done in good faith in pursuance of this Act or any rule or regulation made thereunder.
Empowers the Government to remove any difficulties in the operation of the Act by order published in the Gazette, for a period not exceeding two years from the commencement of the Act.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of the Act. These rules are subject to laying before the State Legislature for modification or annulment.

Repeals the Epidemic Diseases Act (1072 M.E.), the Travancore Epidemic Diseases Act (1073 M.E.), and the Kerala Epidemic Diseases Ordinance, 2021. It also saves anything done or deemed to have been done under these repealed enactments.

important_rules: Rule: Persons arriving in the State by air, rail, road, sea or any other means are subject to inspection and quarantine or isolation if suspected of being infected with an epidemic disease.
Rule: Restrictions may be imposed on public and private transport operations.
Rule: Social distancing norms must be prescribed and followed.
Rule: Congregations of people in public places and religious institutions may be restricted or prohibited.
Rule: Functioning of Government and private offices, and educational institutions may be regulated or restricted.
Rule: Operation of shops, commercial establishments, factories, workshops, and warehouses may be prohibited or restricted.

penalties: Imprisonment up to two years or a fine up to ten thousand rupees, or both, for contravening regulations or orders, or obstructing empowered officers.
Imprisonment up to two years or a fine up to ten thousand rupees, or both, for resisting or obstructing the execution of any duty under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Empowered officers as specified by the Government. District Collectors are also empowered to exercise powers and duties specified in regulations or orders.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications, regulations, and orders issued by the Government, and by the actions of empowered officers and District Collectors. Offences are cognizable and non-bailable.

rights: Right to protection of action taken in good faith.
duties: Duty to observe regulations and orders made under the Act.
Duty not to resist or obstruct empowered officers.
obligations: Obligation to undergo inspection and quarantine/isolation if suspected of an epidemic disease.
Obligation to comply with social distancing norms.
Obligation to comply with restrictions on gatherings and movement.

key_procedures: Procedure: Government notifies a disease as an epidemic disease by notification in the Official Gazette.
Procedure: Government takes special measures and specifies regulations to prevent the outbreak or spread of the epidemic disease.
Procedure: Empowered officers enforce these regulations and orders, which may include inspection, quarantine, and imposing restrictions.
Procedure: Offences under the Act can lead to penalties including imprisonment and fines.
Procedure: Offences can be compounded by authorized officers.
Procedure: Rules are made by the Government and laid before the State Legislature.
administration: Law (Legislation-H) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: Section 8 of the Act came into force retrospectively on July 4, 2020, and other sections on March 27, 2020.
The Act repeals earlier state-specific epidemic disease enactments.
Actions taken in good faith by individuals or authorities under the Act are protected from legal proceedings.
The Government has the power to remove difficulties for a period of two years from the commencement of the Act.

title: THE KERALA FARMERS' WELFARE FUND ACT, 2019
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a Welfare Fund for the welfare of farmers engaged in agriculture in the State of Kerala, to pay pension and other allowances to them, and to attract the younger generation into agriculture, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to farmers engaged in agriculture in the State of Kerala. It defines 'agriculture' broadly to include horticulture, farming of medicinal plants, planting of crops, fruit trees, vegetables, grass, fodder grass, trees, any kind of cultivation in soil, conducting nursery, breeding and keeping of livestock (including fish, ornamental fish, mussel, oyster, bees, silk worm, poultry, duck, quail, goat, rabbit, cattle, pig), and the use of land for agriculture-allied activities or any other agricultural purposes. Specific exclusions are made for plantation crops like rubber, coffee, tea, and cardamom farmers exceeding seven and a half acres.

key_definitions.agriculture: Includes horticulture, farming of medicinal plants, planting of crops and intercrops, fruit trees, vegetables, grass, fodder grass and trees or any kind of cultivation in soil, conducting nursery, breeding and keeping of livestock including fish, ornamental fish, mussel, oyster, bees, silk worm, poultry, duck, quail, goat, rabbit, cattle, pig and the use of land for agriculture allied activities or any other agricultural purposes.
key_definitions.board: The Kerala Farmers' Welfare Fund Board constituted as per section 11.
key_definitions.chief_executive_officer: The Chief Executive Officer appointed as per sub-section (1) of section 15.
key_definitions.contribution: The amount payable to the Fund as per section 8.
key_definitions.family: Includes wife or husband of the farmer, their minor or differently abled children, adopted children, unmarried or widowed or divorced daughters and widows and minor children of deceased sons of farmer; and parents of the farmer who are dependent on him.
key_definitions.farmer: A person who holds, whether as owner or licensee or mortgagee in possession or oral lessee or Government land lessee or kuthakapattakaran or partly in one capacity and partly in another, possession of land having an extent of not less than five cents and not exceeding fifteen acres and annual income does not exceed Rupees five lakhs and whose principal means of livelihood is agriculture for a period of not less than three years. Exceptions exist for plantation crops.
key_definitions.fund: The Kerala Farmers' Welfare Fund constituted as per section 3.
key_definitions.kissan_abhiman_scheme: A scheme introduced for providing benefits to paddy cultivators and pension to them on completion of sixty years of age, subsequently extended to small scale and nominal farmers.
key_definitions.member: A member of the Fund.
key_definitions.notification: Notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules under this Act.
key_definitions.scheme: The Kerala Farmers' Welfare Fund Scheme framed under this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Farmers' Welfare Fund Act, 2019, and it shall come into force at once.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'agriculture', 'Board', 'Chief Executive Officer', 'contribution', 'family', 'farmer', 'Fund', 'Government', 'Kissan Abhiman Scheme', 'member', 'Notification', 'prescribed', 'Schedule', and 'Scheme'.

Details the framing of the Kerala Farmers' Welfare Fund Scheme by the Government, constitution of the Fund, what shall be credited to the Fund (contributions, grants, loans, advances, amounts from Kissan Abhiman Scheme, etc.), the vesting and administration of the Fund by the Board, and the utilization of the Fund for various welfare purposes (pension, family pension, death benefits, financial assistance for disability, treatment, maternity, marriage, education, compensation for accidents, etc.). It also covers investment of the Fund, amendments to the Scheme, and laying of the Scheme before the Legislative Assembly.

Outlines the eligibility for membership (farmers aged 18 years or above), automatic membership for members of Kissan Abhiman Scheme upon fund transfer, eligibility for farmers aged 56 on commencement of the Act, the application process through Krishibhavan, certification by Agricultural Officer, registration or rejection of applications with reasons, appeal process to the Chief Executive Officer or other designated authority, and provision of membership certificates, identity cards, and pass books.

main_sections.section_title: Cancellation of membership in the Fund
main_sections.description: Covers conditions under which membership can be cancelled, such as manipulation or false information provided by a member.

important_rules: Rule 1: Farmers must be at least 18 years old to register as a member of the Fund, with special provisions for those already under the Kissan Abhiman Scheme and those aged 56 or above at the commencement of the Act.

Rule 2: Applications for membership must be submitted to Krishibhavan, either directly or online, along with required documents and registration fee, and certified by the relevant Agricultural Officer.

Rule 3: The Fund shall be credited with contributions, grants, loans, advances, amounts from the Kissan Abhiman Scheme, government grants equivalent to Kissan Abhiman Scheme implementation funds, fee levies, sale proceeds of welfare fund stamps, amounts sanctioned for farmer welfare or environmental protection, agricultural incentives, and any other amounts specified by the Scheme.

Rule 4: The Fund can be utilized for pensions (including for those who completed 56 years at Act commencement), benefits for small scale marginal farmers under Kissan Abhiman Scheme, financial assistance for disability, treatment, maternity, marriage, education, compensation for accidents and deaths, and refund of contributions for ineligible members.
Rule 5: The Scheme, once framed, shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly for a period of fourteen days, and any amendments or annulments made by the Assembly will affect the Scheme's validity.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Act implies enforcement by the Kerala Farmers' Welfare Fund Board and designated authorities like the Chief Executive Officer and Agricultural Officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the registration and cancellation of membership process, appeals, and administration of the Fund and Scheme by the Board and its officers.

rights: Right to receive pension and other allowances upon meeting the eligibility criteria.
Right to receive financial assistance for disability, treatment, maternity, marriage, and education.
Right to receive compensation for accidents, deaths, and natural calamities.
Right to appeal against decisions regarding membership cancellation or rejection.
Right to receive a membership certificate, identity card, and pass book.
duties: Duty to remit contributions to the Fund as per the Act and Scheme.
Duty to provide accurate information for membership registration and continuation.
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act and the Scheme.
obligations: Farmers have an obligation to contribute to the Fund to avail its benefits.
The Government has an obligation to frame the Scheme and ensure the proper functioning of the Fund and the Board.

key_procedures: Membership Registration: Application to Krishibhavan (direct or online), certification by Agricultural Officer, registration or rejection within 30 days, and appeal process to Chief Executive Officer.

Fund Utilization: The Board, with government sanction, can invest the Fund and frame new schemes. The Fund is utilized for pensions, financial assistance, compensation, and administrative expenses as per the Scheme.
Scheme Laying Before Assembly: The framed Scheme is laid before the Legislative Assembly for a specified period, allowing for amendments or annulment.
administration: The Kerala Farmers' Welfare Fund Board, constituted as per section 11, administers the Fund. The Chief Executive Officer appointed under section 15 is also a key administrative figure.
important_notes: The definition of 'farmer' has specific landholding and income limits, with exclusions for certain plantation crops.
The Act provides for retrospective or prospective amendments to the Scheme by the Government.
The Scheme becomes effective only after being laid before the Legislative Assembly and subject to its approval or amendment.

title: THE KERALA FINANCE (No. 2) ACT, 2018
purpose: To give effect to certain financial proposals of the Government of Kerala for the Financial Year 2018-2019, and to amend the Kerala Ceiling on Government Guarantees Act, 2003.
scope: This act applies to the state of Kerala. It specifically amends the Kerala Ceiling on Government Guarantees Act, 2003, relating to financial proposals for the financial year 2018-2019.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act as 'The Kerala Finance (No. 2) Act, 2018' and states that it comes into force on the 1st day of April, 2018.

Amends Section 3 of the Kerala Ceiling on Government Guarantees Act, 2003 (30 of 2003). It substitutes the words 'rupees twenty one thousand crores' with 'five per cent of the Gross State Domestic Product of the State as, calculated by the Department of Economics and Statistics, for the respective financial year'.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Act shall commence on the 1st day of April, 2018.

Rule 2: Section 3 of the Kerala Ceiling on Government Guarantees Act, 2003 is amended to replace a fixed monetary limit with a percentage of the Gross State Domestic Product for government guarantees.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Department of Economics and Statistics is involved in calculating the Gross State Domestic Product which is referenced in the amendment.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement would likely be through the provisions of the amended Kerala Ceiling on Government Guarantees Act, 2003.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Calculation of Gross State Domestic Product by the Department of Economics and Statistics for the respective financial year.
Procedure 2: Application of the 5% limit of the calculated GSDP for government guarantees, as per the amended Act.
administration: Law (Legislation-A) Department, Government of Kerala is responsible for the publication of the Act. The Department of Economics and Statistics is involved in the calculation of GSDP.
important_notes: Note 1: The amendment changes the ceiling on government guarantees from a fixed amount to a variable percentage of the GSDP.
Note 2: The act specifically targets the financial year 2018-2019 for its financial proposals.

title: THE KERALA FINANCE (No. 2) ACT, 2022
purpose: To give effect to certain financial proposals of the Government of Kerala for the Financial Year 2022-2023.
scope: This act amends the Kerala Ceiling on Government Guarantees Act, 2003. It applies to the financial proposals of the Government of Kerala for the financial year 2022-2023 and sets a ceiling on government guarantees.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Kerala Finance (No. 2) Act, 2022' and states that it is deemed to have come into force on April 1, 2022.
Substitutes section 3 of the Kerala Ceiling on Government Guarantees Act, 2003, with a new section that defines the ceiling on government guarantees.

important_rules: Rule 1: The total outstanding Government Guarantees as on the first day of April of any year shall not exceed 100% of the total revenue receipts as per the annual financial statement of the State in the preceding year or 10% of the Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP), whichever is lower.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government of Kerala (implied through the enactment of the Finance Act and amendment of the Guarantee Act)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By setting a statutory limit on government guarantees, ensuring adherence to financial prudence.

duties: Duty to adhere to the prescribed ceiling on government guarantees.
obligations: Obligation for the Government of Kerala to ensure that total outstanding government guarantees do not exceed the specified limits.

key_procedures: The procedure for setting the ceiling on government guarantees is established by amending the existing Act. The calculation involves comparing total revenue receipts of the preceding year with 10% of the GSDP, and whichever is lower becomes the maximum limit for outstanding guarantees.
administration: Law (Legislation-A) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force retrospectively from April 1, 2022.
The amendment specifically targets the financial year 2022-2023 and aims to control the extent of government financial commitments through guarantees.

title: THE KERALA FINANCE (No. 2) ACT, 2023
purpose: To provide for amendments to the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 and the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994, for the purpose of giving effect to the financial proposals of the Government of Kerala for the financial year 2023-2024.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Kerala and amends existing legislation concerning local self-government bodies (Panchayats and Municipalities) related to financial matters and taxation.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act as 'The Kerala Finance (No. 2) Act, 2023' and states that it comes into force on April 1, 2023.

Details the amendments made to the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 (Act 13 of 1994). This includes inserting new sub-sections regarding the imposition of fees for licenses and permissions, changes to the calculation and revision of property tax rates, and provisions for the collection of arrears.

Details the amendments made to the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994 (Act 20 of 1994). Similar to the amendments to the Panchayat Raj Act, this section introduces changes related to fees for licenses and permissions, property tax rate adjustments, and provisions for collecting arrears, but specifically for municipalities.

important_rules: Panchayats and Municipalities can levy fees for the grant of any license, permit, permission, registration, or service, as provided for in this Act or any other law or rules framed by the Government.
Property tax rates for various categories of buildings will be revised every five years. The revised rates shall not be less than five percent higher than the rates of the preceding year.
The Government or the Municipality/Corporation can revise property tax rates every five years. The increase in tax rates should not be less than five percent of the previous year's rate.
The basis for property tax calculation includes floor area, land value, and construction features. The government can notify different rates based on usage.
New, renovated, or altered buildings will have their property tax determined by the Secretary, with an annual increase of five percent on the determined tax.
Existing buildings with a determined annual property tax will see a five percent annual increase on the previous year's tax.
Certain exemptions or reductions from property tax are specified, including for educational institutions and owner-occupied houses up to sixty square meters of floor area.
The penalty for delayed payment of taxes, fees, or rent will be at a rate of two percent per month.

Arrears of taxes, surcharge, fees, rent, etc., shall be recovered as public revenue arrears under the relevant laws. The Secretary can enforce recovery through distress warrants and sale of movable property, or by directing a Magistrate to take appropriate action.

penalties: Penalty for delayed payment of taxes, fees, or rent is two percent per month.
Provisions for recovery of arrears through distress warrants, sale of movable property, or by directing a Magistrate.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Secretary (for Panchayats) and Secretary/Municipality/Corporation (for Municipalities). The Magistrate can be involved in recovery proceedings.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Recovery of arrears through distress warrants, sale of movable property, or by directing a Magistrate. Imposition of property tax and collection of fees and other charges.

rights: Right to receive services for which fees are charged.
Right to object to property tax determinations (implied through the process of tax determination).
duties: Duty to pay property tax and other levied taxes and fees.
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act regarding property tax calculation and payment.
Duty to pay delayed payment penalties.
Duty of Panchayats and Municipalities to collect fees and taxes as prescribed.
obligations: Obligation to pay property tax based on the determined rates and annual increments.
Obligation to pay fees for licenses, permits, and services.
Obligation to pay penalties for late payments.

key_procedures: Procedure for determining property tax for new, renovated, or altered buildings, including annual increments.
Procedure for determining property tax for existing buildings with annual increments.
Procedure for recovering arrears of taxes, fees, and rent through distress warrants and sale of property.
Procedure for a Municipality to collect fees and service charges from beneficiaries of municipal services and institutions.
Procedure for the Government or Local Bodies to notify and revise property tax rates every five years.
administration: Local Self-Government bodies (Panchayats and Municipalities) under the overall purview of the State Government.
important_notes: Exemptions from property tax include educational institutions funded or aided by the government, and hostels for students of such institutions. Owner-occupied houses up to sixty square meters of floor area are also exempted.
The Act specifies that the revised property tax rates should not be less than five percent higher than the rates of the preceding year, and this increase applies annually.
The Act allows for the rounding of the calculated tax to the nearest whole number.
Specific provisions are made for the recovery of dues, including the possibility of movable property seizure and, in certain circumstances, imprisonment of defaulters.
The Act clarifies that the provisions regarding exemptions and enhancements under sub-section (7) are not applicable when property tax is revised.

title: THE KERALA FINANCE ACT, 2020
purpose: This Act makes amendments to various existing Kerala Acts to facilitate fiscal reforms and revenue generation for the State of Kerala. It primarily focuses on amending the Kerala Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1991 and the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, and also includes provisions related to motor vehicle taxes.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala. Its provisions cover individuals and entities liable under the Kerala Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1991, the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, and motor vehicle taxation within the state. Specific amendments also impact the Union Territories of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, and Ladakh in the context of GST.

main_sections.description: Substitutes section 37C of the Kerala Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1991, to introduce a scheme for the reduction of arrears in certain cases, allowing assessees to settle outstanding tax and other amounts up to March 31, 2017, by paying a reduced percentage of the principal amount.

Amends various sections of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, including definitions, provisions related to composition levy, input tax credit, registration cancellation, and penalties. It also makes consequential amendments to reflect changes in the territorial jurisdiction of Union Territories.

Substitutes section 12 of the Kerala Finance Act, 2019, to provide a scheme for the reduction of arrears in certain cases, similar to the one introduced for the Agricultural Income Tax Act, but related to arrears of tax or other amounts due under that Act up to June 30, 2017.

important_rules: Rule 1: Under Section 37C(1) of the Kerala Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1991, assessees can opt to settle arrears up to March 31, 2017, by paying 50% of the principal tax arrears, or 40% if paid in lump sum within 30 days of intimation.

Rule 2: Under Section 9(1) of the Kerala Finance Act, 2019, assessees can opt to settle arrears up to June 30, 2017, by paying 50% of the principal tax arrears, or 40% if paid in lump sum within 30 days of intimation.
Rule 3: Under Section 8(2) of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, the words 'or services' are inserted after 'of goods' in sub-section (2) of section 10.

Rule 4: Under Section 8(8) of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, a new sub-section (1A) is inserted into section 122, making persons who retain the benefit of a transaction liable to a penalty equivalent to the tax evaded or input tax credit availed.
Rule 5: Under Section 8(9) of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, the wording related to offenses and input tax credit availment in section 132 is amended.

penalties: Penalty equivalent to the tax evaded or input tax credit availed of or passed on, for persons retaining the benefit of certain transactions under Section 122(1A) of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.
Penalties for various offenses related to GST, as amended in Section 132 of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, including fraudulently availing input tax credit.

As per Section 37C(2) of the Kerala Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1991, and Section 9(2) of the Kerala Finance Act, 2019, upon settlement of arrears under the respective schemes, revenue recovery proceedings initiated shall be withdrawn and the assessee shall not be liable for collection charges.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Assessing authorities and other relevant tax authorities under the respective Acts (Kerala Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1991, Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, Kerala Finance Act, 2019).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment, demand notices, settlement schemes, and where necessary, revenue recovery proceedings.

rights: Right to opt for settlement of arrears under the schemes provided in Section 37C of the Kerala Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1991, and Section 12 of the Kerala Finance Act, 2019.
Right to have revenue recovery proceedings withdrawn upon successful settlement of arrears.
Right to have any amount paid towards tax after service of demand notice, credited as tax before reckoning arrears for settlement, under specific conditions.
Right to extension of time for certain actions under the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, on sufficient cause.
duties: Duty to withdraw all cases pending before any appellate or revisional authority, tribunal, or courts when opting for settlement of arrears.
Duty to file a declaration along with the option to settle arrears.
Duty to pay the settled amount of arrears within the prescribed timelines (on or before March 31, 2021, for the 2020 schemes).
Duty to furnish proof of payments made towards arrears.
Duty to adhere to the form and manner of submission of options, intimations, and payments as specified by the Commissioner.
Duty to register under GST when liable.
Duty to issue tax invoices as prescribed.
obligations: Obligation to pay tax and other amounts due under the respective Acts.
Obligation to comply with the terms and conditions of the settlement schemes.
Obligation to desist from seeking refunds or adjustments for amounts settled under the schemes.
Obligation to adhere to registration requirements and cancellation procedures under GST.

key_procedures: Procedure for Settlement of Arrears (Agricultural Income Tax): An assessee in arrears up to March 31, 2017, submits an option to the assessing authority on or before November 30, 2020. The assessing authority determines the amount and intimates the assessee. Payment must be remitted on or before March 31, 2021, with options for lump sum or installments. Assessee must withdraw pending cases.

Procedure for Settlement of Arrears (Finance Act, 2019): An assessee in arrears up to June 30, 2017, submits an option to the assessing authority on or before November 30, 2020. The assessing authority determines the amount and intimates the assessee. Payment must be remitted on or before March 31, 2021, with options for lump sum or installments. Assessee must withdraw pending cases.

Procedure for GST Registration Cancellation: A taxable person may apply for cancellation of registration under Section 29(1)(c) of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, if no longer liable or opting out voluntarily. The application process and conditions are detailed within the Act.
administration: The administration of this Act is primarily carried out by the respective departments responsible for implementing the Kerala Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1991, and the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, which would include the Commissioner of Commercial Taxes, Kerala.
important_notes: The settlement schemes for arrears are time-bound, with specific deadlines for opting in and making payments.
Amounts settled under the arrears reduction schemes are final and no refunds or adjustments will be allowed subsequently.
Payments made towards penalty or its interest will not be credited for settlement under the arrears reduction schemes.
Amendments to the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, have retrospective effect from July 1, 2017, in certain cases.
The Act specifies that it is a digitally signed Gazette and authenticity can be verified through a specific web link.

title: THE KERALA FINANCE ACT, 2018
purpose: This Act amends various Kerala state tax laws to implement financial proposals, adjust tax rates, extend deadlines, introduce new provisions, and streamline tax administration. The primary objective is to augment state revenue and facilitate smoother tax compliance.
scope: The act applies to the State of Kerala and amends specific sections of several existing Kerala tax acts including the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, the Kerala Agricultural Income Tax Act, the Kerala Value Added Tax Act, and the Kerala Finance Act, 2008. It also affects provisions related to the Kerala Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 and the Kerala Tax on Luxuries Act, 1976.

key_definitions.Joint Commissioner (Appeals): A newly defined role within the Kerala Value Added Tax Act, 2003, appointed under sub-section (3) of section 3, to handle appeals.
key_definitions.repealed Act: Refers to the Kerala Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 and the Kerala Tax on Luxuries Act, 1976 for the purpose of settling arrears under section 12.

main_sections.description: Amends the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1973, by substituting specific words and figures in various sub-sections and the Schedule. It also introduces new sub-items to serial number 7(i) of the Schedule and adds Annexure IV for Short Term Tax on motor vehicles.
Amends the Kerala Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1991, by substituting specific dates in sub-sections (5) and (7) of section 37C, likely extending the compliance or reporting deadlines.

Significantly amends the Kerala Value Added Tax Act, 2003. It introduces the definition of 'Joint Commissioner (Appeals)', amends sections related to tax payment deadlines, introduces a new proviso for settlement of tax arrears, and makes various changes to appeal provisions and the powers of appellate authorities. It also introduces a waiver of certain arrears and penalty provisions for inter-state sales of arecanut.
Amends the Kerala Finance Act, 2008, by modifying provisions related to foreign liquor, omitting sub-section (2A), and substituting sub-section (3) concerning the utilization of Social Security Cess.

main_sections.section_title: Reduction of arrears in certain cases
main_sections.description: Provides a scheme for assessees to settle arrears of tax or other amounts due under the Kerala Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, and the Kerala Tax on Luxuries Act, 1976, for periods up to March 31, 2011, by paying the principal tax amount and a percentage of the penalty.

important_rules: Rule related to tax payment for motor vehicles where the annual tax does not exceed rupees one thousand five hundred: tax shall be paid yearly on an annual licence.

Specific tax rates and calculations for different types of vehicles are substituted and introduced in the Schedule of the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1973, including for autorickshaws and e-rickshaws.
Provisions for short-term tax (Annexure IV) are introduced for motor vehicles brought to the State for temporary use.
Dealers opting for waiver of arrears and penalty for inter-state sale of arecanut must pay the assessed tax in lumpsum or installments and withdraw pending court cases.
Assessees can opt to settle arrears under the Kerala Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 and Kerala Tax on Luxuries Act, 1976, by paying the principal tax and thirty percent of the penalty.

penalties: Penalty provisions are mentioned in the context of settling arrears and waivers, for instance, in section 10(8) related to waiver of penalty under sections 67 and 68 of the Kerala Value Added Tax Act, 2003.

Section 10(6)(a)(ii) of the Kerala Value Added Tax Act, 2003, allows dealers who failed to take registration to settle cases on payment of registration fee and an amount equal to the registration fee as penalty.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Likely the respective tax authorities under each amended Act, such as assessing authorities, Commissioners, Joint Commissioners (Appeals), Deputy Commissioners (Appeals), and Assistant Commissioners (Appeals).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment orders, appeal mechanisms, penalty imposition for non-compliance, and settlement schemes for arrears.

rights: Right to appeal orders to designated appellate authorities (Joint Commissioner (Appeals), Deputy Commissioner (Appeals), Assistant Commissioner (Appeals)).
Right to opt for settlement of arrears under specific schemes.
Right to revise returns for technical or clerical defects under certain conditions.
duties: Duty to pay motor vehicle tax as specified.
Duty to pay tax as per the Kerala Value Added Tax Act, 2003, including revised deadlines and provisions for arrears.
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Kerala Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1991.
Duty to file options for waiver of arrears and penalty within specified timelines.
Duty to withdraw pending court cases as a condition for waiver.
obligations: Obligation to pay tax on time.
Obligation to adhere to revised dates for tax filings and payments.
Obligation to pay assessed tax and penalty as per settlement schemes.

key_procedures: Procedure for amending the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1973, by substituting specific words, figures, and inserting new sub-items and annexures.

Procedure for assessees to opt for settlement of arrears under the Kerala Value Added Tax Act, 2003, Kerala Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, and Kerala Tax on Luxuries Act, 1976, by submitting an option to the assessing authority and making payments.
Procedure for dealers to apply for revision of returns due to technical or clerical defects, subject to conditions.
Procedure for dealers to file options for waiver of certain arrears and penalty under the Kerala Value Added Tax Act, 2003, for inter-state sale of arecanut.
Procedure for appointing and empowering Joint Commissioner (Appeals) within the Kerala Value Added Tax Act, 2003.
administration: Various departments and authorities under the Kerala State Government, including the Commercial Taxes Department and Motor Vehicles Department, are responsible for the administration of the amended acts.
important_notes: Certain amendments, like the one relating to the FIRST SCHEDULE of the Kerala Value Added Tax Act, 2003 (item 17B), are deemed to have come into force on a specific past date (July 19, 2011).
The Act introduces provisions for settlement of arrears and waiver of penalties, indicating a focus on resolving long-standing tax issues.
There are specific conditions and deadlines for opting into settlement and waiver schemes, with provisions for extension by the Commissioner in certain cases.
The Act consolidates and streamlines appeal processes within the Kerala Value Added Tax Act, 2003, by redefining the roles and jurisdiction of appellate authorities.

title: THE KERALA FINANCE ACT, 2020
purpose: This Act amends various existing Kerala state tax laws to introduce financial provisions, update tax structures, and provide relief measures. It aims to streamline tax administration, offer settlement schemes for tax arrears, and align state tax laws with national guidelines where applicable. The purpose is to generate revenue for the state while offering opportunities for taxpayers to regularize their compliance.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala. It amends several specific Acts, including the Kerala Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1991, the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, and the Kerala Finance Act, 2019. It covers various tax-related matters, including agricultural income tax, goods and services tax, and luxury tax, as well as provisions for settlement of tax arrears.

key_definitions.assessee: A person who is in arrears of tax or any other amount due under the respective Acts.
key_definitions.arrears: Tax or any other amount due under the Act relating to a specific period, for which the assessee is in default.
key_definitions.principal amount of tax in arrears: The original tax amount due, excluding any interest or penalty.

main_sections.description: Substitutes Section 37C of the Kerala Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1991, to introduce a scheme for reduction of arrears in certain cases, allowing assessees to settle arrears by paying a percentage of the principal tax amount.

Amends various sections of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017. These amendments include changes to definitions of Union Territories, inclusion of 'services' in certain clauses, omission of certain words, substitution of clauses related to registration cancellation, extension of time limits for certain actions, and insertion of a penalty provision for retaining benefits of certain transactions.

Substitutes Section 12 of the Kerala Finance Act, 2019, to introduce a scheme for reduction of arrears in certain cases related to the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, and the Kerala Tax on Luxuries Act, 1976. This scheme allows settlement of arrears on payment of a percentage of the principal tax amount.

important_rules: Rule 1: Assessees can opt to settle arrears of tax up to March 31, 2017 (for Agricultural Income Tax) or June 30, 2017 (for GST/Luxury Tax) by paying 50% of the principal tax arrears, or 40% if paid in lump sum within 30 days of intimation.
Rule 2: Settlement of arrears under these schemes requires the assessee to withdraw all pending cases before any appellate or revisional authority, tribunal, or courts.
Rule 3: All arrears, including tax, interest, and penalties, pertaining to an assessee must be settled together under the scheme.
Rule 4: The option to settle arrears must be submitted by a specified date (e.g., November 30, 2020), with provisions for delayed submission in certain cases.
Rule 5: Payments for settled arrears can be made in installments, with a minimum first installment requirement and a maximum number of installments.
Rule 6: Amounts paid towards penalty or its interest will not be credited or refunded under these settlement schemes.

Rule 7: Amendments to the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, include clarifications on Union Territories, inclusion of services in certain provisions, and adjustments to time limits and penalty provisions.

penalties: Any person who retains the benefit of a transaction covered under specific clauses of Section 122 of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, and at whose instance such transaction is conducted, shall be liable to a penalty equivalent to the tax evaded or input tax credit availed or passed on.

Offences related to tax evasion, fraudulent input tax credit claims, and retention of benefits arising from such offences are punishable as per the provisions of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Assessing authorities and other designated officers under the respective tax laws.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment, demand and collection of tax, initiation of revenue recovery proceedings, and prosecution for offences. Enforcement also involves verifying compliance with settlement schemes and imposing penalties for violations.

rights: Right to opt for settling tax arrears under the specified schemes.
Right to withdraw revenue recovery proceedings upon settlement of arrears.
Right to have payments made towards arrears credited as tax before reckoning settlement amounts.
duties: Duty to withdraw all pending appellate, revisional, or court cases to opt for the settlement scheme.
Duty to pay the settled amount of arrears within the prescribed timelines and in the prescribed manner.
Duty to furnish proof of payments made towards arrears.
obligations: Obligation to settle all arrears, including tax, interest, and penalties, together under the scheme.
Obligation not to seek any refund or adjustment for amounts settled under the scheme.
Obligation to comply with the timelines and conditions stipulated in the settlement schemes.

key_procedures: Procedure for Settlement of Arrears (Agricultural Income Tax and GST/Luxury Tax):
1. Assessee submits an option to the assessing authority to settle arrears by paying a specified percentage of the principal tax amount.
2. Assessee withdraws all pending appeals/revisions and files a declaration.
3. Assessing authority determines the settlement amount and intimates the assessee.
4. Assessee remits the amount in lump sum or installments by a specified date (e.g., March 31, 2021).
5. Upon settlement, revenue recovery proceedings are withdrawn, and no further claims for refund or adjustment are allowed.
administration: The administration of the Act involves various departments and authorities responsible for tax collection and enforcement, including the Commissioner of Commercial Taxes, assessing authorities, and other officers empowered under the respective Acts.
important_notes: No refund or adjustment will be allowed for amounts settled under these schemes under any circumstances.
Amounts paid towards penalty or its interest will not be credited or considered for settlement.
The provisions related to the settlement of arrears have specific deadlines for opting and making payments.
Amendments to the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, aim to align with national GST law changes and address specific compliance issues.

title: THE KERALA FINANCE ACT, 2021
purpose: To give effect to certain financial proposals of the Government of Kerala for the Financial Year 2021-2022.
scope: This act applies to the state of Kerala and concerns financial proposals related to various state tax laws for the financial year 2021-2022. It amends several existing Kerala Acts related to finance and taxation.

key_definitions.earliest arrear: For the purpose of the amended sections in the Kerala Surcharge on Taxes Act, 1957, the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, and the Kerala Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1991, 'earliest arrear' means the outstanding dues related to the oldest year among the arrears pending against an assessee.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Kerala Finance Act, 2021, and specifies the commencement dates for different sub-sections and remaining sections of the Act. Sub-sections (3) and (4) of section 8 are deemed to have come into force on August 1, 2021; sub-section (5) of section 8 is deemed to have come into force on June 1, 2021; other provisions of section 8 come into force on a date appointed by the Government; and the remaining sections are deemed to have come into force on June 10, 2021.

Amends the Kerala Surcharge on Taxes Act, 1957 (Act 11 of 1957). It revises percentages for surcharge, changes the definition of 'assessee' to 'a year' in certain contexts, extends deadlines for payment and financial year ends, and inserts a new sub-section (12A) regarding appropriation of part payments towards arrears.

Amends the Kerala Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1959 (Act 10 of 1960). It inserts a proviso to sub-section (1) of section 76, limiting the maximum additional court fee leviable in appeals under the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, to rupees twenty thousand.

Amends the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963 (Act 15 of 1963). It makes insertions for financial years 2015-16, modifies deadlines for tax settlement, revises percentages for certain clauses, changes 'assessee' to 'a year' in some contexts, extends financial year ends, and inserts sub-section (11A) for appropriation of part payments towards arrears.

Amends the Kerala Building Tax Act, 1975 (Act 7 of 1975). It inserts sub-section (1A) in section 5, stating that for green buildings, the building tax shall be levied at fifty percent of the rate specified in Schedule 1.

Amends the Kerala Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1991 (Act 15 of 1991). It revises percentages for certain clauses, changes 'assessee' to 'a year' in some contexts, extends deadlines for payment and financial year ends, and inserts sub-section (12A) for appropriation of part payments towards arrears.
Amends the Kerala Value Added Tax Act, 2003 (Act 30 of 2004). It inserts new serial numbers 98B and 98C in the third Schedule for Liquified Natural Gas and Natural Gas in gaseous state, respectively.

Amends the Kerala State Goods And Services Tax Act, 2017 (Act 20 of 2017). It inserts a new clause (aa) in section 7 regarding activities/transactions between a person and its members, inserts clause (aa) in section 16 regarding supplier's outward supplies, omits sub-section (5) of section 35, substitutes section 44 regarding annual returns, revises the proviso to sub-section (1) of section 50 concerning interest on tax, makes substitutions in section 74 and 75, substitutes sub-section (1) of section 83 regarding provisional attachment of property, inserts a proviso in sub-section (6) of section 107 regarding appeal conditions, and substitutes clauses (a) and (b) in sub-section (1) of section 129 concerning penalties for goods.

important_rules: Rule 1: Amendments to Kerala Surcharge on Taxes Act, 1957, revise surcharge percentages to seventy percent and sixty percent in certain clauses.

Rule 2: Amendments to Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, and Kerala Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1991, introduce sub-sections (11A) and (12A) respectively, for the appropriation of part payments towards arrears.
Rule 3: Amendments to Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, clarify that activities/transactions between a person and its members are treated as separate persons for GST purposes.

Rule 4: Amendments to Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, require the supplier to furnish details of outward supplies in a statement and communicate them to the recipient for input tax credit.
Rule 5: Amendments to Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, modify the conditions for paying interest on delayed tax payments, linking it to the electronic cash ledger.
Rule 6: Amendments to Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, adjust penalties related to tax evasion and goods in transit.

penalties: For goods in transit under the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, a penalty equal to two hundred percent of the tax payable on such goods, or in case of exempted goods, an amount equal to two percent of the value of the goods or rupees twenty-five thousand, whichever is lower, shall be levied.
In the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, amendments in section 74 suggest reduced scope for certain penalties related to tax evasion.
In the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, an appeal against an order under sub-section (3) of section 129 is permitted only after paying twenty-five percent of the penalty.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala and its designated tax authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amendments to existing tax laws, including changes in tax rates, deadlines, penalties, and procedures for assessment, recovery, and appeals.

rights: Right to appeal against certain orders related to tax and penalties, subject to conditions like payment of a percentage of the penalty.
Right to avail input tax credit under GST, subject to supplier furnishing outward supply details.
Right to have part payments appropriated towards the earliest arrears.
duties: Duty to pay taxes as per the provisions of the amended Acts.
Duty to furnish annual returns and reconciliation statements as prescribed under the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.
Duty to comply with the financial proposals implemented through this Act.
obligations: Obligation to pay increased surcharge on taxes in certain cases.
Obligation to adhere to revised deadlines for tax payments and financial year ends.
Obligation to meet new conditions for filing appeals against penalty orders.
Obligation for suppliers to furnish outward supply details for GST purposes.

key_procedures: Procedure for appropriation of part payments towards arrears: Amounts paid in part are appropriated towards the earliest arrear, and the balance towards subsequent years. For tax settlements, credit is given as surcharge before reckoning arrears.
Procedure for appeals under the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017: An appeal under section 129(3) can only be filed after paying twenty-five percent of the penalty.

Procedure for annual returns under the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017: Registered persons (with exceptions) must furnish an annual return, possibly with a self-certified reconciliation statement, in a prescribed manner and time.

Procedure for provisional attachment of property: The Commissioner may, for protecting revenue, provisionally attach property, including bank accounts, after initiating proceedings under specified chapters.
administration: Law (Legislation-A) Department, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act gives effect to financial proposals for the Financial Year 2021-2022.
Several amendments are retrospective, with specific commencement dates mentioned for different provisions.
Exemptions from filing annual returns under the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, may be granted by the Commissioner.
The Act clarifies that for GST purposes, a person and its members or constituents are deemed to be two separate persons for supply of activities or transactions.

title: THE KERALA FINANCE ACT, 2022
purpose: To give effect to certain financial proposals of the Government of Kerala for the Financial Year 2022-2023.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala. It amends various existing acts related to finance, taxation, and motor vehicles. The scope includes financial proposals, surcharges, land tax, sales tax, motor vehicles taxation, agricultural income tax, and the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act.

main_sections.description: Names the act as the Kerala Finance Act, 2022, and specifies its commencement dates. Certain provisions are deemed to have come into force on March 18, 2022, others on April 1, 2022, and some on a date appointed by the Government.
Amends the Kerala Surcharge on Taxes Act, 1957, by modifying the dates for which surcharges apply.
Amends the Kerala Land Tax Act, 1961, by substituting provisions for basic tax rates based on area and type of local body (Panchayat, Municipal Council, Municipal Corporation).
Amends the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, by modifying dates related to tax provisions and extending the applicability of certain sections.

Amends the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976. This section introduces a new table for Green Tax rates for various vehicle classes and ages, and also includes a provision for reduced trimonthly tax for specific rental Caravans. It also amends tax rates for certain vehicle classes.
Amends the Kerala Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1991, by modifying the dates for which certain provisions related to agricultural income tax apply.

Amends the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017. This is a substantial amendment covering various sections related to input tax credit, furnishing of returns, cancellation of registration, and communication of supply details.

important_rules: Rule 1: Amendment of The Kerala Surcharge on Taxes Act, 1957, to extend the period for surcharges (e.g., from 30th November, 2021, to 31st August, 2022, and from 31st March, 2022, to 31st December, 2022).
Rule 2: Revision of basic tax rates under The Kerala Land Tax Act, 1961, based on area extent and the type of local authority (Panchayat, Municipal Council, Municipal Corporation).
Rule 3: Changes in Green Tax rates and incidence of levy for various categories of vehicles under The Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976.

Rule 4: Amendments to The Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, including modifications to the conditions for availing input tax credit, timelines for furnishing returns, and grounds for cancellation of registration.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Various authorities as per the respective amended Acts (e.g., Tax authorities for finance and GST related acts, Motor Vehicles Department for Motor Vehicles Taxation Act).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the mechanisms established by the respective amended Acts, including assessment, collection of taxes, and penalties for non-compliance.

rights: Right to avail input tax credit under specified conditions (amended GST Act).
Right to receive communicated details of inward supplies under GST.
duties: Duty to pay basic tax at prescribed rates under The Kerala Land Tax Act.
Duty to pay Green Tax for motor vehicles.
Duty to furnish returns and pay taxes under the GST Act.
Duty to comply with various financial and tax regulations introduced or amended by the Act.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to extended financial periods for surcharges.
Obligation to meet new conditions and restrictions for furnishing GST returns and availing input tax credit.
Obligation for registered persons to furnish outward supply details under GST.

key_procedures: Procedure for availing input tax credit under the amended GST Act, subject to conditions and restrictions.
Procedure for furnishing outward supply details under the GST Act, including conditions and timelines.
Procedure for communicating details of inward supplies and input tax credit electronically to registered persons under the GST Act.
Procedure for renewal of registration and fitness certificates for vehicles, with implications for Green Tax payment.
Procedure for paying basic tax at different rates based on land area and local body type.
administration: Law (Legislation-A) Department, Government of Kerala (for enactment); Various departments related to finance, taxes, and transport for administration and enforcement of amended acts.
important_notes: The Act gives effect to financial proposals for the Financial Year 2022-2023.
Certain provisions have retrospective effect, deemed to have come into force on specific dates in 2022.
The Act introduces significant changes to the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, impacting input tax credit, return filing, and registration cancellations.

title: THE KERALA FINANCE ACT, 2023
purpose: This Act makes amendments to various sections of existing laws, primarily related to tax administration and revenue collection in Kerala. The amendments aim to redefine roles, designations, and powers of tax officials, streamline appeal processes, and update references to specific tax departments.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala and governs the administration and enforcement of tax laws within the state. It specifically impacts the functioning and designations of various tax officers and authorities, including those dealing with State Tax, Commercial Tax, and Goods and Services Tax. It also affects the procedures for appeals and the pre-deposit requirements for tax disputes.

key_definitions.assistant_commissioner_of_state_tax: Any person appointed to be an Assistant Commissioner of State Tax under sub-section (3) of section 3.
key_definitions.commissioner_of_state_tax: The Commissioner of State Tax appointed as such by the Government.
key_definitions.deputy_commissioner_of_state_tax: Any person appointed to be a Deputy Commissioner of State Tax under sub-section (3) of section 3.
key_definitions.joint_commissioner_of_state_tax: Any person appointed to be a Joint Commissioner of State Tax under sub-section (3) of section 3.
key_definitions.joint_commissioner_of_state_tax_appeals: Any person appointed to be a Joint Commissioner of State Tax (Appeals) under sub-section (3) of section 3.
key_definitions.special_commissioner_of_state_tax: Any person appointed to be a Special Commissioner of State Tax under sub-section (3) of section 3 of this Act.
key_definitions.state_tax_officer: Any person appointed to be a State Tax Officer under sub-section (3) of section 3 of this Act.
key_definitions.appellate_authority: Replaces references to Joint Commissioner (Appeals), Deputy Commissioner (Appeals), and Assistant Commissioner (Appeals) in certain contexts related to appeals.

main_sections.description: This section details changes to Section 3 of an unspecified Act. It includes substitutions for the word 'Commissioner' with 'Commissioner of State Tax', and significant changes to the designations of appointed tax officials, replacing terms like 'Commercial Tax Officers' with 'Special Commissioners of State Tax, Additional Commissioners of State Tax, Additional Commissioners of State Tax (Appeals), Joint Commissioners of State Tax, Joint Commissioner of State Tax (Appeals), Deputy Commissioners of State Tax, Assistant Commissioners of State Tax, State Tax Officers'. It also modifies how these appointments are made and how powers are assigned.
This section amends Section 4 of an unspecified Act, specifically in sub-section (4), clause (iv), by substituting 'Commercial Tax Officer' with 'Assistant Commissioner of State Tax'.
This section states that Section 8 of an unspecified Act shall be omitted.
This section amends Section 18, sub-section (1), of an unspecified Act, by substituting 'Deputy Commissioner' with 'Joint Commissioner of State Tax'.
This section states that Section 18C of an unspecified Act shall be omitted.
This section amends Section 20 of an unspecified Act by substituting 'Commissioner' with 'Commissioner of State Tax' in sub-sections (2A) (proviso), (3), and (4).
This section amends Section 20A, sub-section (1), of an unspecified Act, by substituting 'Deputy Commissioners' with 'Joint Commissioners of State Tax'.
This section amends Section 23, sub-section (1), of an unspecified Act, by substituting 'Deputy Commissioners' with 'Joint Commissioners of State Tax'.
This section amends Section 25B of an unspecified Act by substituting 'Deputy Commissioner' with 'Joint Commissioners of State Tax'.

This section amends Section 33 of an unspecified Act. The marginal heading and sub-section (1) are changed by substituting 'Assistant Commissioners'/'Assistant Commissioner' with 'Deputy Commissioners of State Tax'.
This section amends Section 42, sub-section (2), fourth proviso, of an unspecified Act, by substituting 'Commissioner' with 'Commissioner of State Tax'.
This section amends the proviso to Section 43 of an unspecified Act, by substituting 'Commissioner' with 'Commissioner of State Tax'.
This section amends Section 44 of an unspecified Act. Sub-section (3) proviso and sub-section (7) clauses (b) and (f) are amended by substituting 'Commissioner' with 'Commissioner of State Tax'.

This section amends Section 47 of an unspecified Act. Sub-section (3) replaces 'Commercial Tax Department' with 'State Goods and Services Tax Department'. Sub-section (5) substitutes 'Commercial Tax Officer' with 'State Tax Officer'. Sub-section (16A) substitutes 'Commissioner' with 'Commissioner of State Tax'.
This section states that Section 48 of an unspecified Act shall be omitted.

This section makes several amendments to Section 49 of an unspecified Act: (a) 'Commercial Tax Officer' to 'State Tax Officer'; (b) 'Assistant Commissioner' to 'Deputy Commissioner of State Tax'; (c) 'Deputy Commissioner' to 'Joint Commissioner of State Tax'; (d) and (e) 'Commissioner' to 'Commissioner of State Tax'.
This section amends the proviso to Section 54 of an unspecified Act, by substituting 'Deputy Commissioner' with 'Joint Commissioner of State Tax'.

This section significantly amends Section 55 of an unspecified Act, primarily concerning appeals. It replaces references to 'Joint Commissioner (Appeals), Deputy Commissioner (Appeals) and Assistant Commissioner (Appeals)' with 'Appellate Authority'. It clarifies appeal hierarchy, introduces a new deadline for presenting appeals (September 30, 2023), and mandates the transfer of pending appeals as of April 1, 2023, to the appropriate authority. It also specifies a pre-deposit amount for appeals: 'a pre-deposit amount of 10 per cent of the disputed amount of tax, subject to a maximum of ₹ 5 Crores'.

This section amends Section 56 of an unspecified Act. It replaces 'Deputy Commissioner' with 'Joint Commissioner of State Tax' in the marginal heading and sub-sections (1), (2), and (3). Sub-section (2)(b) also replaces 'Deputy Commissioner (Appeals) or the Assistant Commissioner (Appeals)' with 'Appellate Authority'.

This section amends Section 57 of an unspecified Act. It replaces 'Deputy Commissioner' with 'Joint Commissioner of State Tax' in the marginal heading and sub-section (1). Sub-section (1) proviso (second) and sub-section (3) proviso replace 'Deputy Commissioner (Appeals)' or 'Deputy Commissioner (Appeals) or Assistant Commissioner (Appeals)' with 'Appellate Authority'. Sub-section (3)(i) replaces 'the Deputy Commissioner may' with 'the Joint Commissioner of State Tax may'. Sub-section (4) proviso replaces 'the Deputy Commissioner' with 'Joint Commissioner of State Tax'.

This section amends Section 58 of an unspecified Act. It replaces 'Commissioner' with 'Commissioner of State Tax' in the marginal heading and sub-sections (1), (2), and (3). Sub-sections (1)(b) and (2)(b) replace 'Joint Commissioner (Appeals), Deputy Commissioner (Appeals) or Assistant Commissioner (Appeals)' with 'Appellate Authority'.

This section amends Section 58A of an unspecified Act.
