title: THE KERALA FISCAL RESPONSIBILITY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2018
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2003, for purposes specified within the act, primarily focusing on fiscal management, deficit reduction, and debt management.
scope: This act applies to the State of Kerala and its fiscal management as governed by the Kerala Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2003. It specifically addresses the period from 2017-2018 to 2019-2020.

main_sections.description: This section names the act as the Kerala Fiscal Responsibility (Amendment) Act, 2018, and states that it is deemed to have come into force on April 1, 2017.

This section substitutes sub-section (2) of Section 4 of the principal Act (The Kerala Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2003). The amended sub-section details specific fiscal targets for the Government of Kerala for the period 2017-2018 to 2019-2020, including eliminating revenue deficit, building revenue surplus, maintaining fiscal deficit at 3% of GSDP, and reducing total debt liabilities.

important_rules: The Government shall eliminate the revenue deficit completely during the period from 2017-2018 to 2019-2020.
The Government shall build up surplus amount of revenue and utilize such amount for discharging liabilities in excess of assets.
The Government shall maintain the fiscal deficit to 3 per cent of the Gross State Domestic Product during the period from 2017-2018 to 2019-2020.
The State shall reduce the total debt liabilities in the years 2017-2018, 2018-2019, and 2019-2020 in the order of 30.40%, 30.01%, and 29.67% respectively of the Gross State Domestic Product.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala (implied through the legislative authority)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legislative amendment and subsequent fiscal policy implementation and monitoring by the State Government.

rights: Eligibility for additional reduction of 0.25% borrowing limit if GSDP to debt ratio is <= 25% in the preceding year.
Eligibility for additional borrowing limit of 0.25% of GSDP if interest payments are <= 10% of revenue receipts in the preceding year.
Option to utilize concessions separately or together if both criteria for additional fiscal space are met, with a maximum fiscal deficit to GSDP ratio of 3.5%.
duties: Eliminate revenue deficit completely.
Build up revenue surplus and utilize for liabilities.
Maintain fiscal deficit at 3% of GSDP.
Reduce total debt liabilities as specified.
obligations: The State must not have a revenue deficit in the year borrowing limits are fixed and the immediately preceding year to avail additional fiscal space concessions.

key_procedures: Amendment of Section 4 of the principal Act to introduce new fiscal targets.
The Government shall eliminate revenue deficit, build revenue surplus, maintain fiscal deficit at 3% of GSDP, and reduce total debt liabilities within the specified period and percentages.
administration: Law (Legislation-A) Department, Government of Kerala (for publication); The fiscal management is administered by the Finance Department of the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: Additional fiscal space for borrowing is available under specific conditions related to debt-to-GSDP ratio and interest payments. The total fiscal deficit to GSDP ratio can reach up to 3.5% if certain criteria are met.
The concessions for additional fiscal space are conditional on the absence of a revenue deficit in the current and preceding year.
The 'additional fiscal space' availed shall be utilized for the State's share of Centrally Sponsored Schemes.

title: THE KERALA FISCAL RESPONSIBILITY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2021
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2003.
scope: This act applies to the State of Kerala. It amends the principal Act concerning fiscal responsibility and borrowing limits of the State.

main_sections.description: This section names the act as the Kerala Fiscal Responsibility (Amendment) Act, 2021. It also specifies that clause (a) of section 2 is deemed to have come into force on February 26, 2020, and clause (b) on May 17, 2020.

This section amends Section 4 of the Kerala Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2003. It includes provisions for additional borrowing for the financial years 2019-2020 and 2020-21, with specific conditions and criteria related to fiscal deficit and state-level reforms.

This section repeals the Kerala Fiscal Responsibility (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021 (102 of 2021). It also clarifies that any actions taken or deemed to have been taken under the repealed Ordinance shall be considered as done under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: For the financial year 2019-2020, the State is eligible for an additional one-time special dispensation borrowing of Rs. 1471 crore beyond the fiscal deficit of 3% of the Gross State Domestic Product. This amount must be utilized within the financial year 2019-2020.
For the financial year 2020-21, the State shall maintain its fiscal deficit at 3% of the Gross State Domestic Product.
For the financial year 2020-21, the State is eligible for additional borrowing of 2% of the Gross State Domestic Product, in addition to the 3% fiscal deficit.

The eligibility for the 2% additional borrowing in 2020-21 is subject to the implementation of four specific state-level reforms: One Nation One Ration Card System, Ease of doing business reforms, Urban Local body/Utility reforms, and Power sector reforms.
Each state-level reform carries a weightage of 0.25% of the Gross State Domestic Product, totaling 1% for additional borrowing.

The remaining 1% of additional borrowing will be available in two installments of 0.50% each. The first installment is untied, while the second requires the implementation of at least three out of the four specified state-level reforms.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but implied to be under the purview of the State Government and its financial departments.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legislative amendment and adherence to the fiscal responsibility norms and borrowing limits set by the Act.

rights: Right to additional borrowing under specific conditions and for designated financial years.
duties: Duty to maintain fiscal deficit within stipulated percentages.
Duty to utilize additional borrowing within the financial year it is sanctioned.
Duty to implement state-level reforms to be eligible for full additional borrowing.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the provisions of the Kerala Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2003, as amended.
Obligation to report on fiscal performance as per the principal Act.

administration: Law (Legislation-A) Department, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The amendments made by this Act are to be read in conjunction with the principal Kerala Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2003.
The retrospective application of certain sections as indicated in Section 1(2) is a key aspect.

title: THE KERALA FISH PROCUREMENT, MARKETING AND MAINTENANCE OF QUALITY ACT, 2021
purpose: To provide for regulating of fish procurement, auctioning and marketing, to promote systematic, hygienic and efficient auctioning and marketing, to maintain quality and for other matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to fish procurement, auctioning, and marketing within the state of Kerala. It covers all aquatic animals that are edible and have economic and commercial value. It also applies to various entities involved in the fish trade, including fishermen, auctioneers, societies managing landing centers and markets, and government authorities.

key_definitions.Adjudicating Officer: An officer authorized by the Government under sub-section (1) of section 26 of this Act.
key_definitions.Appellate Authority: The District Collector having jurisdiction over the district concerned.
key_definitions.auction commission: The amount or fish realized from fish sellers as a service charge for the auction conducted or for providing facilities for conducting auction.
key_definitions.auctioneer: The person who has obtained a valid license for fish auctioning under section 5.
key_definitions.Authorised Officer: An officer of the rank of Assistant Director in the Fisheries Department having jurisdiction over that area, authorized by the Government by notification, for exercising the powers and for performing the duties assigned under this Act.
key_definitions.fish: All aquatic animals which are edible and having economic and commercial value.
key_definitions.landing centre: The place notified under section 3 of this Act, where fish can be brought directly from the sea to the shore.
key_definitions.market: The place notified under section 3 of this Act where marketing or transferring of fish is carried out for domestic consumption or exporting other than landing centre, harbour, shop room, booth and fish farm.

main_sections.description: Specifies the name of the Act and its deemed commencement date, which is the 24th day of September, 2021.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as 'Adjudicating Officer', 'Appellate Authority', 'auctioneer', 'fish', 'landing centre', 'market', and others.

main_sections.section_title: Power to declare landing centre, harbour and market
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to declare landing centers, harbours, and markets by notification, and to specify their physical infrastructure standards.
Regulates fish auctioning, prohibiting it outside notified areas unless licensed and specifying the procedure and commission for auctioning.

Grants powers to the Adjudicating Officer and Appellate Authority to conduct inquiries similar to a civil court, including summoning witnesses, requiring production of documents, and examining evidence.
Defines penalties for contravention of specific sections of the Act, including fines for selling contaminated or substandard fish and provides for the suspension or cancellation of licenses.

Specifies that offences under certain sections of the Act shall be tried by a Judicial First Class Magistrate court and outlines the penalties, including imprisonment and fines, for various degrees of offences.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection against legal proceedings for any action taken or intended to be taken in good faith under the Act or rules made thereunder.
Grants the Government power to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act by issuing orders, within a specified period.
Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, and mandates that such rules be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

Repeals the Kerala Fish Procurement, Marketing and Maintenance of Quality Ordinance, 2021, and provides that anything done or omitted to be done under the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or omitted to be done under this Act.

important_rules: Fish auctioning must only be conducted in notified landing centers, harbours, and markets, and only by persons holding a valid license.
An auction commission not exceeding five percent of the auction amount can be realized and apportioned as prescribed.
Selling fish that is unfit for human consumption, contaminated, or of substandard quality is a punishable offence.
Actions taken in good faith by officers or authorities under the Act are protected from legal proceedings.
The Government can make rules for the implementation of the Act, which will be subject to modification or annulment by the Legislative Assembly.

penalties: For contravening sections 13, 18, and 22 (selling contaminated or substandard fish): First offence - fine up to ten thousand rupees; Second offence - fine up to twenty-five thousand rupees; Third and subsequent offences - fine up to one lakh rupees.

For contravening sections 4, 6, and 15: First offence - imprisonment up to two months or a fine up to one lakh rupees or both; Second offence - imprisonment up to one year or a fine up to three lakh rupees or both; Third and subsequent offences - imprisonment up to one year or a fine up to five lakh rupees or both.
In addition to monetary penalties, licenses can be suspended or cancelled.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Adjudicating Officer, Appellate Authority, Authorised Officer, and Judicial First Class Magistrate court.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inquiries, trials for offences, imposition of fines, suspension or cancellation of licenses, and by issuing orders to remove difficulties.

rights: Fishermen have the right to directly market fish without auction.
Persons acting in good faith under the Act have protection from legal proceedings.
duties: To conduct fish auctioning only in notified places and with a valid license.
To maintain the quality of fish.
To comply with rules and regulations made under the Act.
To cooperate with inquiries conducted by authorities.
obligations: To ensure fish sold is fit for human consumption and free from contamination.
To adhere to the prescribed procedures for auctioning and marketing.
Organizations found guilty of offences will have their directors, managers, or officers held responsible.

key_procedures: Declaration of landing centres, harbours, and markets by the Government through notification.
Licensing of auctioneers for conducting fish auctioning.
Conducting inquiries by Adjudicating Officers and Appellate Authorities with powers similar to civil courts.
Trial of offences by Judicial First Class Magistrate courts.
Procedure for making and laying of rules before the Legislative Assembly.
administration: Government of Kerala, specifically the Law (Legislation-I) Department for notifications and the Fisheries Department for enforcement through authorized officers.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on 24th September, 2021.
The Kerala Fish Procurement, Marketing and Maintenance of Quality Ordinance, 2021, has been repealed by this Act.
Any difficulties in giving effect to the Act can be removed by the Government through orders, but such orders cannot be issued after two years from the commencement date of the Act.
Rules made under the Act are subject to modification or annulment by the Kerala Legislative Assembly.

title: THE KERALA FISH PROCUREMENT, MARKETING AND MAINTENANCE OF QUALITY ACT, 2021
purpose: To provide for regulating of fish procurement, auctioning and marketing, to promote systematic, hygienic and efficient auctioning and marketing, to maintain quality and for other matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the procurement, auctioning, marketing, and maintenance of quality of fish within the State of Kerala. It covers various entities involved in the fish trade, including fishermen, auctioneers, societies managing landing centers, harbors, and markets, and individuals or organizations involved in processing and storage.

key_definitions.Adjudicating Officer: An officer authorised by the Government under sub-section (1) of section 26 of this Act.
key_definitions.Appellate Authority: The District Collector having jurisdiction over the district concerned.
key_definitions.auction commission: The amount or fish realised from fish sellers as a service charge for the auction conducted or for providing facilities for conducting auction.
key_definitions.auctioneer: The person who has obtained a valid licence for fish auctioning under section 5.
key_definitions.Authorised Officer: An officer of the rank of Assistant Director in the Fisheries Department having jurisdiction over that area, authorised by the Government by notification, for exercising the powers and for performing the duties assigned under this Act.
key_definitions.chilled storage: The facility to store fish chilled at low temperature on a commercial basis.
key_definitions.transportation facility: Mechanised vehicle used for the distribution of fish through road, on commercial basis.
key_definitions.fish: All aquatic animals which are edible and having economic and commercial value.
key_definitions.fishing: Catching, collecting, attracting or chasing fish by adopting any means.
key_definitions.Fish Landing Centre Management Society: The society constituted under section 7 of this Act for the management and maintenance of a landing centre.
key_definitions.Fish Market Management Society: The society constituted under section 11 of this Act for the management and maintenance of a market.
key_definitions.fisherman: A person engaged mainly in fishing for livelihood.
key_definitions.harbour: The place with necessary infrastructure for landing fishing vessels and for unloading and handling fish safely and hygienically.
key_definitions.Harbour Management Society: The society constituted under section 9 of this Act for the management and maintenance of a fishing harbour.
key_definitions.ice plant: The establishment producing ice industrially/commercially for keeping fish without being spoiled.
key_definitions.landing centre: The place notified under section 3 of this Act, where fish can be brought directly from the sea to the shore.
key_definitions.market: The place notified under section 3 of this Act where marketing or transferring of fish is carried out for domestic consumption or exporting other than landing centre, harbour, shop room, booth and fish farm.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the official gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.pre-processing: Beheading, separation of meat, removal of gills, removal of entrails, removal of scales etc. of fish.
key_definitions.pre-processing centre: An establishment, place or premise set up for doing pre-processing of fish industrially / commercially.
key_definitions.processing: Canning, pickling, cooking, drying, marinading, freezing, drying by smoking or preparing fish for marketing in similar manner.
key_definitions.processing centre: An establishment, place or premise set up for processing fish commercially.
key_definitions.State Level Fish Quality Maintenance Com: The Committee constituted as per section 16.
key_definitions.user fee: The fees realised from persons, institutions and vehicles towards the utilization or use of infrastructure arranged by the Government or Local Self Government Institutions in the landing centre, harbour or market.
key_definitions.vessel: A vehicle used for fishing or transporting fish by water.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act as 'The Kerala Fish Procurement, Marketing and Maintenance of Quality Act, 2021' and specifies that it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 24th day of September, 2021.

This section provides definitions for various terms used throughout the Act, such as Adjudicating Officer, Appellate Authority, auction commission, auctioneer, Authorised Officer, chilled storage, transportation facility, fish, fishing, various societies (Fish Landing Centre Management Society, Fish Market Management Society, Harbour Management Society), fisherman, Government, harbour, ice plant, landing centre, market, notification, prescribed, pre-processing, pre-processing centre, processing, processing centre, State Level Fish Quality Maintenance Committee, user fee, and vessel.

main_sections.section_title: Power to declare landing centre, harbour and market
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to declare landing centres, harbours, and markets by notification for the purposes of the Act and to specify their physical infrastructure standards.

Prohibits fish auctioning outside notified landing centres, harbours, and markets, requires a licence for auctioning, and prescribes the manner of conducting auctions and the auction commission which can be up to five percent of the auction amount.
Requires auctioneers to obtain a licence from the Authorised Officer and outlines the conditions and fees for such licences, including the power to suspend or cancel licences.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of Adjudicating Officer and Appellate Authority
main_sections.description: Grants the Adjudicating Officer and Appellate Authority powers similar to a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, for conducting inquiries and appeals, including summoning witnesses, requiring production of documents, and receiving evidence.

main_sections.section_title: Power to inquire by Adjudicating Officer and Appellate Authority
main_sections.description: Confers powers on the Adjudicating Officer and Appellate Authority to inquire into matters under the Act, akin to a civil court, including summoning individuals, examining them under oath, requiring the production of documents, and issuing commissions for examining witnesses or documents.

Prescribes penalties for contravention of certain sections (13, 18, 22) and conditions of a licence, including engaging in sale of substandard or adulterated fish. Penalties increase with subsequent offences, ranging from ₹10,000 for the first offence to ₹1,00,000 for the third and subsequent offences. The Adjudicating Officer can also suspend or cancel the licence.

Specifies that contravention of sections 4, 6, and 15 shall be tried by a Judicial First Class Magistrate. It also details penalties for such offences, which include imprisonment and fines, with increasing severity for repeat offenders. The Act also covers offences by companies and cooperative societies.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection against legal proceedings for any act done or intended to be done in good faith in pursuance of the Act or rules made thereunder.

Grants the Government the power to remove any difficulties in the implementation of the Act by issuing orders, provided such orders are made within two years from the commencement of the Act. Such orders must be laid before the Legislative Assembly.
Authorises the Government to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of the Act. Such rules, once made, are to be laid before the Legislative Assembly for approval or amendment.

Repeals the Kerala Fish Procurement, Marketing and Maintenance of Quality Ordinance, 2021 (Ordinance No. 112 of 2021) and saves actions taken or things done under the Ordinance as if they were done under this Act.

important_rules: No person shall conduct fish auctioning through places other than notified landing centres, harbours, and markets (Section 4(1)).
A licence under Section 5 is mandatory for conducting fish auctioning (Section 4(2)).
The manner of conducting fish auctioning and allied activities shall be in the prescribed manner (Section 4(3)).
An auction commission not exceeding five percent of the auction amount can be realised (Section 4(4)).
Auctioneers must obtain a valid licence from the Authorised Officer (Section 5(1)).
The Government may, by notification, declare landing centres, harbours, and markets (Section 3(1)).
The Government may specify standards for the physical infrastructure of landing centres, harbours, and markets (Section 3(2)).

penalties: For contravention of Sections 13, 18, 22 or licence conditions, involving sale of substandard or adulterated fish: First offence - ₹10,000; Second offence - ₹25,000; Third and subsequent offences - ₹1,00,000. The Adjudicating Officer can also suspend or cancel the licence (Section 29(1) & (2)).

For contravention of Sections 4, 6, 15 or rules made thereunder: First offence - imprisonment for up to two months or a fine up to ₹1,00,000, or both; Second offence - imprisonment for up to one year or a fine up to ₹3,00,000, or both; Third and subsequent offences - imprisonment for up to one year or a fine up to ₹5,00,000, or both (Section 30(2)).
Offences by companies and cooperative societies are also punishable (Section 30(4)).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Adjudicating Officer, Appellate Authority (District Collector), Authorised Officer, and Judicial First Class Magistrate.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inquiries and adjudication by the Adjudicating Officer, appeals to the Appellate Authority, trials by Judicial First Class Magistrate, imposition of fines, suspension or cancellation of licences, and imprisonment.

rights: Fishermen have the right to directly market their fish without auction (Section 4(1) Proviso).
Persons acting in good faith under the Act are protected from legal proceedings (Section 31).
The Government has the power to remove difficulties and make rules (Sections 32 & 33).
duties: To obtain a licence for fish auctioning (Section 4(2)).
To conduct fish auctioning in a prescribed manner (Section 4(3)).
To ensure the quality of fish procured and marketed.
To comply with rules and regulations made under the Act.
obligations: Obligation to obtain a licence for auctioning.
Obligation to adhere to the prescribed procedures for auctioning and marketing.
Obligation to maintain the quality of fish.
Obligation to pay auction commission and user fees as prescribed.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining a licence for fish auctioning (Section 5).
Procedure for conducting fish auctioning (Section 4(3) and prescribed manner).
Procedure for appeals against decisions of the Adjudicating Officer (Section 28(1) refers to civil procedure for appeal, Section 27 likely details this).
Procedure for inquiries and investigations by Adjudicating Officer and Appellate Authority (Section 28).
administration: The Act is administered by the Government of Kerala. Specific officers like the Adjudicating Officer, Appellate Authority, and Authorised Officers are appointed for its implementation. The Law (Legislation-I) Department is involved in the publication of the Act.
important_notes: Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are saved (Section 34(2)).
The Act provides for the removal of difficulties within two years of its commencement (Section 32(1)).
Rules made under the Act must be laid before the Legislative Assembly (Section 33(2)).
The Act came into force retrospectively from 24th September, 2021 (Section 1(2)).

title: THE KERALA FISHERMEN DEBT RELIEF COMMISSION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2018
purpose: To amend THE KERALA FISHERMEN DEBT RELIEF COMMISSION ACT, 2008.
scope: Applies to fishermen in Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Fishermen Debt Relief Commission (Amendment) Act, 2018. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 27th day of December, 2018.

In the Kerala Fishermen Debt Relief Commission Act, 2008 (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), in Section 2, after clause (k), the following clauses shall be inserted, namely:— '(l) "financial year" means the period commencing on the 1st day of April and ending on the 31st day of March of the succeeding year; (m) "fishermen" means and includes traditional fishermen, whose livelihood is dependent on fishing and who own and operate fishing gear or small fishing boats, individually or collectively, for their livelihood.' And in clause (l) of Section 2 of the principal Act, for the words 'financial year', the words 'financial year' shall be substituted.

important_rules: The Act is deemed to have come into force on December 27, 2018.
The definition of 'fishermen' is expanded to include traditional fishermen dependent on fishing and owning fishing gear or small fishing boats.
administration: The Kerala State Fisheries Department is likely to administer this act.
important_notes: The amendment is effective retrospectively from December 27, 2018.
The term 'financial year' is defined.

title: THE KERALA GENERAL SALES TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2025
purpose: To further amend the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, and by extension to sales tax matters within Kerala. Specifically amends provisions related to the definition of 'Horti-wine' and its inclusion in certain contexts.

key_definitions.Horti-wine: Shall have the same meaning as assigned to it in clause (g) of rule 2 of the Kerala Small Scale Winery (for production of horti-wine from tropical fruits and agricultural products of Kerala) Rules, 2022.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 2025 and that it shall come into force at once.
Amends section 5 by adding a new sub-section (1), where the words and symbol "means and includes wine," are replaced by "Horti-wine,".

Amends the schedule by inserting after the heading "Foreign Liquor", in item (iv), after the word "Wine", the words and symbol "including horti-wine" shall be inserted. It also inserts a new clause (ia) under explanation (i) defining 'Horti-wine'.

administration: Law (Legislation-A) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.
The amendment specifically addresses the definition and scope of 'Horti-wine'.

title: THE KERALA GOVERNMENT LAND ASSIGNMENT (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2023
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Government Land Assignment Act, 1960, to provide for the regularization of contraventions of conditions of patta and rules, and to permit the use of assigned land for purposes other than originally assigned.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Kerala and concerns the assignment of Government land, specifically amendments to the Kerala Government Land Assignment Act, 1960.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Government Land Assignment (Amendment) Act, 2023, and that it shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new section 4A after section 4
main_sections.description: Inserts a new section 4A, titled 'Usage of assigned land for any other purposes'. This section allows the Government to regularize contraventions of patta conditions and rules in force on the commencement date of the amendment act. It also empowers the Government to permit assignees to use the assigned land for purposes other than the original assignment, subject to prescribed terms and conditions.

Amends section 7 of the principal Act by inserting new items (oa) and (ob) after item (o) in sub-section (1). These amendments empower the Government to prescribe procedures for regularizing contraventions of patta conditions and rules, and for permitting the use of assigned land for purposes other than the original assignment.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Government is competent to regularize any contraventions of the conditions attached to the patta and of the rules made under this Act, which were in force on the date of commencement of the Kerala Government Land Assignment (Amendment) Act, 2023, in the manner prescribed.

Rule 2: The Government is competent to permit an assignee, who holds the assigned land as on the commencement date of the amendment Act, to use the land for purposes other than the original assignment, on such terms and conditions as may be prescribed, if the Government is satisfied and records the reasons in writing.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through prescribed procedures for regularization and permission for land use changes.

rights: Right of the Government to regularize contraventions of land assignment conditions.
Right of the Government to permit change of land use for assigned land.
Right of assignees to seek regularization of contraventions and permission for change of land use, subject to prescribed conditions.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Regularizing contraventions of patta conditions and rules. The specific procedure is to be prescribed by the Government.
Procedure 2: Permitting the use of assigned land for purposes other than originally assigned. The specific procedure is to be prescribed by the Government.
administration: Law (Legislation-B) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The amendment act is intended to provide flexibility in land use and address existing contraventions of land assignment conditions.
The effective date of commencement is 'at once'.

title: THE KERALA HEADLOAD WORKERS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2021
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Headload Workers Act, 1978.
scope: This Act applies to headload workers in Kerala and amends the existing Kerala Headload Workers Act, 1978.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Kerala Headload Workers (Amendment) Act, 2021, and specifies that it is deemed to have come into force on October 27, 2020.

Amends Section 7 of the principal Act by reducing the maximum weight a headload worker can carry from seventy-five kilograms to fifty-five kilograms, and inserts a new sub-section (1A) stating that no woman and adolescent headload worker shall be required to carry more than thirty-five kilograms.

Amends Section 43 of the principal Act. Sub-section (1) allows rules to be inserted either prospectively or retrospectively. Sub-section (2) inserts a new clause (d) concerning the terms and conditions of service of officers and employees of the Board, including their retirement benefits.

Repeals the Kerala Headload Workers (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021 (127 of 2021). Anything done or taken under the repealed Ordinance is deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Maximum weight for general headload workers reduced to 55 kilograms.
Maximum weight for women and adolescent headload workers limited to 35 kilograms.
Rules can be applied prospectively or retrospectively.
Terms and conditions of service, including retirement benefits for Board officers and employees, are to be addressed.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but implied to be the authorities responsible for enforcing the principal Act and its amendments.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the rules and regulations made under the Act.

rights: Right for women and adolescent headload workers to not carry more than 35 kilograms.
duties: Duty of employers/principals to adhere to the revised weight limits.
Duty of the Board to address terms and conditions of service for its officers and employees.

administration: Law (Legislation-C) Department, Government of Kerala, and the Board established under the principal Act.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force retrospectively from October 27, 2020.
The amendments are made to further the objectives of the Kerala Headload Workers Act, 1978.

title: The Kerala Healthcare Service Persons and Healthcare Service Institutions (Prevention of Violence and Damage to Property) Amendment Act, 2023
purpose: To amend the Kerala Healthcare Service Persons and Healthcare Service Institutions (Prevention of Violence and Damage to Property) Act, 2012, to further prevent violence against healthcare service persons and damage to property in healthcare service institutions.
scope: This Act applies to healthcare service persons and healthcare service institutions within the state of Kerala. It amends the principal Act of 2012.

key_definitions.healthcare service person: As defined in the principal Act, expanded by this amendment to include nursing students, para-medical students, para-medical workers, security guards, managerial staff, ministerial staff, ambulance drivers and helpers, and any other person notified by the Government.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Healthcare Service Persons and Healthcare Service Institutions (Prevention of Violence and Damage to Property) Amendment Act, 2023, and it is deemed to have come into force on May 24, 2023.

Amends Section 2 of the principal Act (Act 14 of 2012) to expand the definition of 'healthcare service persons' to include more categories of personnel and students, and to add a definition for 'prescribed'.

Amends Section 4 of the principal Act by revising penalties for acts of violence and damage to property. It specifies imprisonment terms and fine amounts for different degrees of offenses, and declares these offenses as cognizable and non-bailable.

Inserts a new section 4A which mandates the expeditious completion of investigations and trials for cases registered under this Act. It sets time limits for investigation (60 days from FIR) and trial (1 year, extendable by 6 months). It also provides for the designation of Special Courts and Special Public Prosecutors for speedy trial.

Amends Section 7 of the principal Act by inserting a new sub-section (2) that outlines measures for ensuring the security and safety of healthcare service institutions and persons, including the appointment of security personnel, installation of CCTV cameras, establishment of control rooms, display of important information, and preparation of protocols.

Repeals the Kerala Healthcare Service Persons and Healthcare Service Institutions (Prevention of Violence and Damage to Property) Amendment Ordinance, 2023 (Ordinance No. 1 of 2023), while saving any actions taken or proceedings initiated under the said Ordinance as if they were taken or initiated under this Act.

important_rules: Any person committing or abetting an act of violence as defined in the Act shall be punished with imprisonment from six months to five years and a fine of ₹50,000 to ₹2,00,000.
If an act of violence results in grievous hurt to a healthcare service person, the punishment shall be imprisonment from one year to seven years and a fine of ₹1,00,000 to ₹5,00,000.
Offenses under Section 4(1) are cognizable and non-bailable.
Investigation of cases registered under this Act must be completed within 60 days from the date of FIR by an officer not below the rank of Inspector.
Trials should be concluded within one year, with provisions for extension, and Special Courts are to be designated for speedy trial.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term not less than six months and not exceeding five years, and a fine not less than fifty thousand rupees and not exceeding two lakh rupees for committing or abetting an act of violence.

Imprisonment for a term not less than one year and not exceeding seven years, and a fine not less than one lakh rupees and not exceeding five lakh rupees, if the act of violence causes grievous hurt as defined in the Indian Penal Code.
Offences under sub-section (1) of section 4 are cognizable and non-bailable.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Police officers (investigation by Inspector rank and above), Courts (Sessions Courts designated as Special Courts for speedy trial).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through criminal proceedings, investigation by police, and trial by designated courts with provisions for expeditious disposal of cases.

rights: Right of healthcare service persons to be protected from violence and damage to property.
Right to a speedy trial for offenses under the Act.
duties: Duty of all persons to refrain from committing acts of violence or causing damage to property in healthcare institutions.
Duty of the State Government to take measures for security, including appointment of security personnel, installation of CCTV, and preparation of protocols.
Duty of police officers to investigate cases expeditiously.
Duty of courts to conduct trials expeditiously.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the prescribed timelines for investigation and trial.
Obligation to ensure that healthcare service persons are protected and treated with respect.

key_procedures: Registration of a case under the Act.
Investigation of the case by a police officer not below the rank of Inspector within 60 days.
Trial of the case by a designated Special Court, with an endeavour to conclude within one year.
Designation of Special Courts and Special Public Prosecutors by the State Government in concurrence with the High Court.
administration: Law (Legislation) Department, Government of Kerala (responsible for notification and publication); State Government (for designating Special Courts and Prosecutors); Police Department (for investigation); Judiciary (for trial).
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the principal Act of 2012.
The amendment is deemed to have come into force on May 24, 2023.
The definition of 'healthcare service persons' has been significantly broadened.
Provisions for speedy trial are a key feature of the amendment.

title: THE KERALA HIGH COURT SERVICES (DETERMINATION OF RETIREMENT AGE) AMENDMENT ACT, 2022
purpose: To amend the Kerala High Court Services (Determination of Retirement Age) Act, 2008, specifically to modify the provisions related to the determination of retirement age for employees of the Kerala High Court.
scope: This act applies to employees of the Kerala High Court. It specifically addresses the retirement age based on the date of appointment and whether the employee is a member of the National Pension System.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala High Court Services (Determination of Retirement Age) Amendment Act, 2022, and that it shall be deemed to have come into force on April 24, 2009.

This section amends Section 2 of the principal Act (The Kerala High Court Services (Determination of Retirement Age) Act, 2008). It substitutes the existing provision regarding retirement age with a new provision that differentiates retirement age based on the date of appointment (before or on/after April 1, 2013) and membership in the National Pension System.

important_rules: Employees appointed before April 1, 2013, shall retire from service on the afternoon of the last day of the month in which they attain the age of 56 years.

Employees appointed on or after April 1, 2013, and who are members of the National Pension System, shall retire from service on the afternoon of the last day of the month in which they attain the age of 60 years, or as decided by the Government from time to time.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated in the provided text, but implied to be the administrative bodies overseeing the Kerala High Court services.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application and enforcement of the amended provisions of the Act.

key_procedures: Determination of retirement age based on the employee's date of appointment and National Pension System membership.
administration: Law (Legislation-E) Department, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on April 24, 2009.
The amendment introduces a distinction in retirement age based on the date of appointment and National Pension System membership.

title: THE KERALA HIGH COURT(AMENDMENT) ACT, 2018
purpose: To further amend the Kerala High Court Act, 1958.
scope: Applies to proceedings and awards related to the Kerala High Court, specifically amending provisions concerning monetary amounts and the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal.

main_sections.description: Names the act as the Kerala High Court (Amendment) Act, 2018, and states that it shall come into force on the 15th day of December, 2017.

Amends section 3 of the Kerala High Court Act, 1958. Specifically, it substitutes "forty lakh rupees" for "one lakh rupees" in clause (13)(b) and inserts a new sub-clause (h) concerning awards from the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal after sub-clause (g).

main_sections.section_title: Special provision in respect of pending appeals, suits and other proceedings
main_sections.description: States that notwithstanding anything contained in the principal Act or any other law, the provisions of sub-clauses (b) and (h) of section 3, as amended by this Act, will apply to any judgment, decree, or order of any court. This implies that the amendments regarding monetary limits and the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal awards are retrospective or apply to existing cases.

important_rules: In clause (13) of section 3 of the principal Act, for the words "one lakh rupees", the words "forty lakh rupees" shall be substituted.
After sub-clause (g) of clause (13) of section 3, a new sub-clause (h) shall be inserted: "(h) from an award passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal."
administration: Law (Legislation-E) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Kerala High Court Act, 1958.
The amendment concerning monetary limits is a significant increase from one lakh rupees to forty lakh rupees.
The amendment specifically addresses awards from the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal.

title: THE KERALA INDUSTRIAL INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2025
purpose: To amend the Kerala Industrial Infrastructure Development Act, 1993.
scope: Applies to industrial units established by an entrepreneur or allottee under an agreement with the Kerala Industrial Infrastructure Development Corporation on land owned by the Corporation within Kerala.

key_definitions.industrial unit: Any industrial unit established by an entrepreneur or allottee under an agreement with the Corporation in the land owned by the Corporation.
key_definitions.undertaking: Any building, plant and machinery or any other assets of the industrial unit established by an entrepreneur or allottee under an agreement with the Corporation in the land owned by the Corporation.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Industrial Infrastructure Development (Amendment) Act, 2025 and it shall come into force at once.

Inserts a new sub-section (7) to section 22 of the principal Act, detailing the procedure for dealing with outstanding payments by an industrial unit after the competent authority has taken possession of the premises. This includes issuing a notice for payment and, in case of failure, transferring the undertaking along with assets to another willing purchaser after valuation.
Amends sub-sections (1) and (2) of section 30 of the principal Act to revise the penalties for offenses, increasing the minimum fine and extending the maximum fine.
Omitted section 42 of the principal Act.
Omitted section 43 of the principal Act.

Amends section 45 of the principal Act, replacing imprisonment and fine provisions with a liability to a fine not less than ten thousand rupees but not exceeding fifty thousand rupees, subject to prescribed conditions.

Amends section 46 of the principal Act, replacing imprisonment and fine provisions with a liability to a fine not less than ten thousand rupees but not exceeding fifty thousand rupees, subject to prescribed conditions.

Amends section 47 of the principal Act, replacing imprisonment and fine provisions with a liability to a fine not less than ten thousand rupees but not exceeding fifty thousand rupees, subject to prescribed conditions.

Amends section 48 of the principal Act, replacing a fine provision with a liability to a fine not less than ten thousand rupees but not exceeding fifty thousand rupees, subject to prescribed conditions.

Inserts a new section 48A which empowers the Government to designate an officer (not below the rank of General Manager of the Corporation) to impose fines for offenses under sections 30, 45, 46, 47, and 48 after an inquiry. It also outlines the powers of the inquiring officer and the appeal process to the Managing Director of the Corporation.

important_rules: If an industrial unit fails to make outstanding payments after the competent authority has taken possession of the premises, the Corporation shall take necessary action, including transferring the undertaking and selling assets to recover dues.
Penalties for offenses under sections 30, 45, 46, 47, and 48 are revised to a minimum of ten thousand rupees and a maximum of fifty thousand rupees, subject to prescribed conditions.
An officer not below the rank of General Manager of the Corporation may be designated to impose fines after an inquiry.
Appeals against orders made by the designated officer shall be preferred to the Managing Director of the Corporation within thirty days.

penalties: For offenses under section 30(1) and 30(2): A fine not less than ten thousand rupees but not exceeding fifty thousand rupees.
For offenses under section 45: A fine not less than ten thousand rupees but not exceeding fifty thousand rupees.
For offenses under section 46: A fine not less than ten thousand rupees but not exceeding fifty thousand rupees.
For offenses under section 47: A fine not less than ten thousand rupees but not exceeding fifty thousand rupees.
For offenses under section 48: A fine not less than ten thousand rupees but not exceeding fifty thousand rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The competent authority, the designated officer (not below the rank of General Manager of the Corporation) for imposing fines, and the appellate authority (Managing Director of the Corporation).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through issuance of notices, taking possession of premises, transferring undertakings and selling assets, imposing fines after inquiry, and hearing appeals.

rights: Right of the Kerala Industrial Infrastructure Development Corporation to recover outstanding dues by transferring undertakings and selling assets.
Right of an aggrieved person to prefer an appeal against an order imposing a fine.
Right of the appellate authority to entertain appeals after the expiry of the period if sufficient cause is shown.
duties: Duty of the competent authority to issue a notice for outstanding payments.
Duty of the designated officer to hold an inquiry before imposing a fine.
Duty of the appellate authority to give parties an opportunity of being heard.
Duty of the appellate authority to pass an order within sixty days of receiving an appeal.
obligations: Obligation of the person to make outstanding payments to the Corporation.
Obligation of the person to appear before the inquiring officer to give evidence or produce documents.
Obligation to file an appeal within the prescribed time and manner.

key_procedures: Procedure for recovery of outstanding payments: Competent authority takes possession, issues notice for payment. If payment is not made, the Corporation may transfer the undertaking and sell assets after valuation by an independent valuer.
Procedure for imposing fines: Government designates an officer of appropriate rank. The officer holds an inquiry, can summon persons and documents, and imposes a fine if an offense is proved.

Procedure for appeal against fine orders: An aggrieved person can appeal to the Managing Director of the Corporation within thirty days, with provisions for condonation of delay. The appellate authority hears parties and passes an order within sixty days.
administration: Law (Legislation-C) Department, Government of Kerala; Kerala Industrial Infrastructure Development Corporation.
important_notes: The Act comes into force at once.
Specific definitions are provided for 'industrial unit' and 'undertaking' in relation to Section 22.

purpose: The purpose of the act is to provide for the establishment of Industrial Single Window Clearance Boards and Industrial Township Area Development in the State of Kerala, aiming to streamline and expedite the process of industrial clearances and development.

key_definitions.Industrial Township: Refers to a specifically developed area designated for industrial activities.

title: THE KERALA INDUSTRIAL SINGLE WINDOW CLEARANCE BOARDS AND INDUSTRIAL TOWNSHIP AREA DEVELOPMENT (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2025
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Industrial Single Window Clearance Boards and Industrial Township Area Development Act, 1999, specifically to promote investment.
scope: This act applies to the State of Kerala and amends the principal Act related to industrial clearances and township development, with a focus on promoting investment.

key_definitions.Kerala Investment Promotion and Facilita: Refers to the cell established under section 6C of the Kerala Micro Small Medium Enterprises and Other Enterprises Facilitation Act, 2019.
key_definitions.Kerala State Investment Promotion Board: A board constituted under section 13 G of the principal Act.
key_definitions.Kerala State Investment Promotion Monito: A committee constituted under section 13 I of the principal Act.
key_definitions.Industrial Policy: Means the industrial policy declared by the Government and in force at the relevant time.
key_definitions.Mega Investments: Means investments of more than one hundred crore rupees.
key_definitions.New Generation Enterprises: Means such new generation enterprises as may be specified in the industrial policy.
key_definitions.Special Packages: Means such special packages as may be specified in the industrial policy.
key_definitions.Exceptional Requirements: Means requirements for relaxations beyond those specified in the industrial policy.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Kerala Industrial Single Window Clearance Boards and Industrial Township Area Development (Amendment) Act, 2025, and states that it comes into force at once.
Amends the long title of the principal Act by inserting the words "and to promote investment" after "modernisation of enterprises".
Amends the preamble of the principal Act by inserting the words "and to promote investment" after "licenses for enterprises".

Inserts new clauses (ia), (ib), and (ic) into section 2 of the principal Act, defining 'Kerala Investment Promotion and Facilitation Cell', 'Kerala State Investment Promotion Board', and 'Kerala State Investment Promotion Monitoring Committee'.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new Chapter II B
main_sections.description: Inserts a new Chapter II B into the principal Act, detailing the constitution, powers, and functions of the Kerala State Investment Promotion Board and the Kerala State Investment Promotion Monitoring Committee.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of Kerala State Investment Promotion Board
main_sections.description: Details the constitution of the Kerala State Investment Promotion Board, specifying its Chairperson, Co-Chairperson, Vice Chairpersons, Member Secretary, Members, and Convenor. It also states that the Government shall constitute the Board by notification in the Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of the Kerala State Investment Promotion Board
main_sections.description: Outlines the powers and functions of the Kerala State Investment Promotion Board, including convening meetings, resolving difficulties in implementing industrial policy, making coordinated decisions for relaxations, deciding on special packages, considering relaxations for large investments, reviving sick industries, facilitating coordination between departments, providing guidance to investors, and attracting domestic and foreign investors.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of Kerala State Investment Promotion Monitoring Committee
main_sections.description: Details the constitution of the Kerala State Investment Promotion Monitoring Committee, specifying its Chairperson, Vice Chairperson, Members, and Member-Convenor. It also states that the Government shall constitute the Committee by notification in the Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of the Kerala State Investment Promotion Monitoring Committee
main_sections.description: Outlines the powers and functions of the Kerala State Investment Promotion Monitoring Committee, including convening meetings and transacting business, implementing decisions of the Board, issuing necessary procedures and regulations, facilitating coordination and monitoring of project implementation, and recommending measures to overcome obstacles to investment.

States that officers and employees of the Kerala Investment Promotion and Facilitation Cell shall render necessary assistance for the performance of the functions of the Board and the Committee. It also allows for the utilization of services of such experts and others as may be determined.

important_rules: The principal Act is further amended to include provisions for promoting investment.
The Kerala State Investment Promotion Board is constituted with the Chief Minister as Chairperson and various Ministers and officials as members.
The Kerala State Investment Promotion Monitoring Committee is constituted with the Chief Secretary as Chairperson and various Principal Secretaries as members.
The Board has powers to resolve industrial policy implementation issues and grant relaxations.
The Committee is responsible for implementing the Board's decisions and monitoring project implementation.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Act implies enforcement through the powers vested in the constituted Board and Committee, and by the Government through notifications.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the executive actions and decisions of the Kerala State Investment Promotion Board and the Kerala State Investment Promotion Monitoring Committee, as well as through government notifications and the implementation of industrial policy.

rights: Investors have the right to approach the Kerala State Investment Promotion Board for guidance and proposals.
Industries have the right to expect steps to resolve difficulties arising during the implementation of industrial policy.
duties: The Kerala Investment Promotion and Facilitation Cell has a duty to render necessary assistance to the Board and Committee.
The Board has a duty to take steps to resolve difficulties and make coordinated decisions for relaxations.
The Committee has a duty to implement the decisions of the Board and monitor projects.
obligations: The Government has an obligation to constitute the Board and Committee by notification.
The Board and Committee have an obligation to perform their specified functions and powers.

key_procedures: Constitution of the Kerala State Investment Promotion Board by Government notification.
Constitution of the Kerala State Investment Promotion Monitoring Committee by Government notification.
Convening of meetings by the Chairperson of the Board.
Taking coordinated decisions for allowing relaxations in industrial policy.
Implementing decisions of the Board by the Committee.
Monitoring of project implementation by the Committee.
administration: Industries Department, Government of Kerala, and specifically the Kerala State Investment Promotion Board and Kerala State Investment Promotion Monitoring Committee.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Principal Act of 1999 (Act 5 of 2000).
The amendment specifically aims to promote investment and facilitate large investments.
Definitions of 'Mega Investments', 'New Generation Enterprises', 'Special Packages', and 'Exceptional Requirements' are provided within the context of the industrial policy.

title: THE KERALA INVESTMENT PROMOTION AND FACILITATION (No. 2) ACT, 2018
purpose: To give effect to certain proposals of the Government of Kerala to avoid delay in granting various licenses, permissions, approvals, and clearances required under various enactments, and to provide for other matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act primarily amends existing acts, specifically the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 and the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994, to streamline and expedite the process of obtaining various licenses and permissions for industries, factories, trades, entrepreneurship activities, and other services within the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: Names the act as the Kerala Investment Promotion and Facilitation (No. 2) Act, 2018, and states that it shall be deemed to have come into force on October 20, 2017.
Details amendments to the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, 1994, including changes to headings and procedures related to granting licenses and permissions for industries and trades.
Details amendments to the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994, including changes to headings and procedures related to granting licenses and permissions for industries and trades.

important_rules: Rule: Applications for licenses/permissions must be acknowledged upon receipt.
Rule: Applications and supporting documents should be verified immediately.
Rule: If supporting documents are missing, the applicant must be informed in writing and given up to five days to submit them.

Rule: For the Kerala Municipality Act, licenses shall remain in force for five years and be renewed for another five years without application upon payment of the prescribed fee, thirty days before expiry.

Rule: In cases where an order on an application is not communicated within thirty days of receipt, the application shall be deemed to have been allowed, subject to the Act, rules, bye-laws, and imposed conditions. The Secretary has the power to cancel such a license after issuing a show-cause notice.
Rule: The Secretary may obtain expert opinion for nuisance determination at the cost of the owner or person in charge, with reports due within fifteen days.

penalties: Penalty: For cancellation of a license due to violation, the Secretary may impose a penalty not exceeding rupees five lakhs.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Secretary of the concerned Panchayat or Municipality, or an officer authorized by the Secretary.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the process of application verification, granting or refusal of licenses/permissions, and the imposition of penalties for violations.

rights: Right to receive an acknowledgement for the application.
Right to be informed of missing documents and a reasonable period to submit them.
Right to have an application deemed allowed if no order is communicated within the specified period (under certain conditions).
Right to have licenses renewed for a further period under the Kerala Municipality Act.
duties: Duty to issue an acknowledgement to the applicant.
Duty to verify applications and supporting documents.
Duty to inform applicants of missing documents.
Duty to inquire and report on whether an establishment is objectionable due to density of population, nuisance, or pollution.
Duty to grant permission or license as expeditiously as possible, subject to conditions.
Duty of the Secretary to obtain expert opinion at the cost of the owner when determining nuisance.
obligations: Obligation to submit all required supporting documents.
Obligation to adhere to imposed conditions on licenses/permissions.
Obligation to pay the prescribed fee for license renewal.
Obligation to comply with show-cause notices and provide submissions if a license is to be cancelled.

key_procedures: Procedure: Applicant submits an application along with supporting documents.
Procedure: Secretary or authorized officer issues an acknowledgement and verifies the application and documents on the spot.
Procedure: If documents are missing, the applicant is notified and given up to five days to submit them.
Procedure: The Secretary inquires and reports to the Panchayat/Council regarding the objectionability of the establishment.
Procedure: The Panchayat/Council, after considering reports, grants permission within thirty days, absolutely or subject to conditions.
Procedure: If no order is communicated within thirty days, the application is deemed allowed.
Procedure: For renewals under the Municipality Act, payment of fees thirty days before expiry leads to automatic renewal for five years.
administration: The Act amends existing legislation administered by local self-government bodies (Panchayats and Municipalities) in Kerala, with the Secretary playing a key role in the application and licensing process.
important_notes: Note: The Act is a 'No. 2' Act for 2018, implying there might be other related acts.
Note: The Act is deemed to have come into force retrospectively from October 20, 2017.
Note: Amendments are made to specific sections of the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 and the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994.

title: THE KERALA INVESTMENT PROMOTION AND FACILITATION ACT, 2018
purpose: To give effect to certain proposals of the Government of Kerala to avoid delay in granting various licenses, permissions, approvals, and clearances required under various enactments and to provide for other matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala. It aims to streamline and expedite the process of obtaining licenses, permissions, approvals, and clearances for investments within the State. It amends existing acts related to commercial establishments and headload workers.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act as the 'Kerala Investment Promotion and Facilitation Act, 2018'. It also states that the Act is deemed to have come into force on October 20, 2017.

This section amends Section 5A of the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1960. It inserts the words 'on the same day of the receipt of application' after 'in the prescribed form' in sub-section (4), implying a faster processing of applications.

This section inserts a new section, '9A. Engaging the services of headload workers', after Section 9 of the Kerala Headload Workers Act, 1978. This new section outlines the conditions under which employers shall engage registered headload workers and specifies that headload workers are entitled to wages only if their services have been engaged by the employer or owner.

This section grants the Government the power to make rules, either prospectively or retrospectively, for carrying into effect the provisions of this Act. It also outlines the procedure for laying these rules before the Legislative Assembly.

This section repeals the Kerala Investment Promotion and Facilitation Ordinance, 2018. It also includes a saving clause stating that anything done or any action taken under the amended Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1960, and the Kerala Headload Workers Act, 1978, by the said Ordinance, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the said Acts as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Rule under Section 4: The Government may make rules for the purpose of carrying into effect the provisions of the Act. These rules can be made prospectively or retrospectively and are subject to modification or annulment by the Legislative Assembly.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala, likely through the departments responsible for implementing the amended acts (e.g., Labour Department, Industries Department).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By ensuring compliance with the amended provisions of the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1960, and the Kerala Headload Workers Act, 1978, which are facilitated by this Act.

rights: Right for employers to expect expedited processing of licenses, permissions, approvals, and clearances.
Right for registered headload workers to be engaged for work in their establishment, subject to provisions.
duties: Duty of employers to engage registered headload workers.
Duty of the Government to make rules for the effective implementation of the Act.
obligations: Obligation for employers to engage headload workers under certain conditions.
Obligation for headload workers to be registered to be entitled to wages.

key_procedures: Procedure for applications under the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1960: Applications for licenses, permissions, approvals, or clearances are to be processed and issued on the same day of receipt, as amended by this Act.
Procedure for engaging headload workers: Employers must engage registered headload workers, with exceptions for skilled work requiring machinery or specialized skills.
administration: The Act's administration would involve various departments of the Government of Kerala, particularly those dealing with investment, industries, and labour regulations, as it amends existing legislation.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force retrospectively from October 20, 2017.
Amendments are made to the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1960, and the Kerala Headload Workers Act, 1978, to facilitate faster investment processes.

title: THE KERALA IRRIGATION AND WATER CONSERVATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2018
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Irrigation and Water Conservation Act, 2003, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Irrigation and Water Conservation Act, 2003.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Irrigation and Water Conservation (Amendment) Act, 2018, and it is deemed to have come into force on the 8th day of December, 2017.

Inserts a new sub-section (4) in section 37 of the principal Act, prohibiting the deposit of rubbish, filth, or excreta or other waste materials into any distributary system or water course, or allowing waste water into it or polluting the water in any other way.
Inserts a clause (k) in sub-section (1) of section 58 of the principal Act, stating that a police officer not below the rank of an Inspector General of Police shall be nominated by the Government.

important_rules: No person shall deposit or cause to deposit rubbish or filth or excreta or any other waste materials in any distributary system or water course or allow to flow waste water into it or pollute the water in any other way.
A police officer not below the rank of an Inspector General of Police shall be nominated by the Government.
administration: Law (Legislation-F) Department, Government of Kerala

title: THE KERALA LABOUR WELFARE FUND (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2021
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1975.
scope: This act applies to the State of Kerala and amends the provisions of the Kerala Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1975, specifically concerning contributions and related matters for the welfare of labour.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Labour Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2021, and it shall be deemed to have come into force on January 16, 2020.

This section amends sub-section (1) of section 15 of the principal Act (Kerala Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1975). It substitutes the words 'four rupees' with 'forty five rupees' and 'eight rupees' with 'forty five rupees'.

This section repeals the Kerala Labour Welfare Fund (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021 (120 of 2021). It also provides a saving clause, stating that anything done or actions taken under the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: For the words 'four rupees' in sub-section (1) of section 15 of the principal Act, the words 'forty five rupees' shall be substituted.
Rule 2: For the words 'eight rupees' in sub-section (1) of section 15 of the principal Act, the words 'forty five rupees' shall be substituted.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but implied to be the authorities responsible for administering the Kerala Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1975.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not explicitly detailed in the provided text.

obligations: Obligation to comply with the amended contribution rates as per section 15 of the principal Act, as modified by this amendment.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Amendment of Section 15 of the principal Act: The process involves substituting specific monetary values in sub-section (1) of section 15. The old amounts of 'four rupees' and 'eight rupees' are replaced by 'forty five rupees'.
administration: The administration of the Kerala Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1975, and its amendments, would typically fall under the Labour Department of the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: Note 1: The Act is deemed to have come into force retrospectively from January 16, 2020.
Note 2: The amendment replaces the previous Ordinance (120 of 2021) with this Act, ensuring continuity of actions taken under the Ordinance.

title: THE KERALA LAND REFORMS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2021
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963.
scope: This act applies to the state of Kerala and specifically amends provisions related to land reforms as outlined in the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 2021, and it shall come into force at once.

This section amends sub-section (1) of section 102 of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963. It substitutes the existing words, figures, and letter 'Section 106 or Section 106A' with 'Section 106, Section 106A or Section 106B'.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not specified in the provided text.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not specified in the provided text.

administration: Law (Legislation-B) Department, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 5th day of January, 2023.
The notification was published on the 6th January, 2023.

title: THE KERALA LIVESTOCK FEED, POULTRY FEED AND MINERAL MIXTURE (REGULATION OF MANUFACTURE, STORAGE, DIS.) ACT
purpose: To regulate the manufacture, storage, distribution, and sale of livestock feed, poultry feed, and mineral mixture to ensure quality and safety, preventing adulteration, sub-standard products, and misbranding, thereby safeguarding animal health and productivity.
scope: This Act applies to livestock feed, poultry feed, and mineral mixture manufactured, stored, transported, sold, offered for sale, or held within the state of Kerala. It covers all persons involved in these activities, including manufacturers, storers, distributors, sellers, authorized agents, and dealers.

main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to notify laboratories as primary analytical and referral laboratories for analyzing samples of livestock feed, poultry feed, or mineral mixture, provided they are established by government or accredited by NAB. Such notification will be published in the Official Gazette.

Outlines the procedure for collecting samples of livestock feed, poultry feed, or mineral mixture by a Feed Safety Assurance Officer. It details the process of dividing samples, sealing, witnessing, and obtaining signatures. It also covers entry into establishments and vehicles for verification, seizure procedures, and the obligation of agents to provide details of the person on whose behalf stock is held. Additionally, it allows consumers to get their purchased samples analyzed at their own expense.

Details the responsibilities of the Feed Safety Assurance Officer regarding the analysis of collected samples, including delivering sealed samples to the concerned person and the Feed Safety Enforcement Officer, and submitting samples to authorized laboratories for testing within a specified timeframe. It also specifies that expenses for analysis will be borne by the responsible parties if the sample is found to be not up to standard.

Mandates that approved primary analytical laboratories analyze received samples and provide a report to the Feed Safety Assurance Officer within a maximum period of twenty-one days. It also prohibits the display or use of analysis reports for advertisement.

main_sections.section_title: Confiscation and disposal by Feed Safety Assurance Officer
main_sections.description: Authorizes the Feed Safety Assurance Officer or authorized officer to immediately seize and dispose of livestock feed, poultry feed, or mineral mixture that are manufactured, stored, distributed, or sold without a license, or are adulterated, substandard, or misbranded. Expenses incurred during seizure and disposal will be recovered from the responsible party or licensee.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure for Inquiry by Licensing Authority
main_sections.description: Details the process of inquiry by the Licensing Authority when a person contravenes any provision of the Act or rules. It requires the authority to provide a reasonable opportunity of being heard before imposing penalties as per section 20. The Licensing Authority is vested with powers of a Civil Court for summoning witnesses, requiring production of documents, and receiving evidence on affidavit.

Specifies penalties for violations of the Act. For a first violation, it includes license suspension (60 days to 6 months) or fine (₹25,000 to ₹50,000) or both. For a second violation, license suspension (6 months to 1 year) or fine (₹50,000 to ₹2 lakh) or both. For a third violation or if severe injury, harm on productivity, or death to livestock/poultry occurs, the license can be cancelled up to five years.

Provides for an appeal process. Any person aggrieved by an order imposing a penalty under section 20 can prefer an appeal to the State Feed Quality Consultative Committee within thirty days of the order. Appeals must be disposed of within sixty days after a hearing.

main_sections.section_title: Offences to be tried by the Court
main_sections.description: Deals with offenses triable by a court. Third or continuing offenses, severe violations recommended by the State Feed Quality Consultative Committee and confirmed by two labs, or offenses causing death/serious injury to livestock/poultry are punishable by imprisonment (6 months to 1 year) and fine (up to ₹10 lakh). It also allows for forfeiture and disposal of seized products and mandates compensation to owners for death or injury to livestock/poultry.

States that no court shall take cognizance of an offense under this Act except on a written complaint filed by the Feed Safety Enforcement Officer, based on a recommendation from the State Feed Quality Consultative Committee. Offenses are triable by a Judicial Magistrate of the First Class.

main_sections.section_title: Offences by Companies, Institutions, Establishments or Societies
main_sections.description: Addresses offenses committed by corporate entities. It holds persons in charge and responsible for the business liable. It also provides for the liability of directors, managers, or other employees if the offense is committed with their consent, connivance, or neglect.

important_rules: Samples collected for analysis must be divided into five parts, marked, sealed, and fastened in an airtight container in the presence of two witnesses.

A Feed Safety Assurance Officer may enter any establishment or vehicle involved in the manufacture, storage, sale, or transport of livestock feed, poultry feed, or mineral mixture to verify compliance with the Act.
Any person from whom a sample is taken must provide their signature or thumb impression, or in their refusal, two witnesses' signatures/thumb impressions will be taken.
Analysis reports from laboratories cannot be displayed on premises or used for advertisement purposes.
Seized livestock feed, poultry feed, or mineral mixture that is adulterated, substandard, or misbranded must be immediately seized and disposed of.
Penalties for violations are tiered based on the number of offenses, with increasing severity including license suspension, fines, and potential cancellation of the license.
Appeals against penalty orders must be filed within thirty days before the State Feed Quality Consultative Committee and disposed of within sixty days.
Offenses causing death or severe injury to livestock/poultry will be tried by a court and may result in imprisonment and fines, along with compensation to the owner.
