Companies, institutions, or societies committing offenses under the Act are liable, with individuals in charge and responsible for the business being held accountable.

penalties: First violation: Suspension of license (60 days to 6 months) or fine (₹25,000 to ₹50,000) or both.
Second violation: Suspension of license (6 months to 1 year) or fine (₹50,000 to ₹2 lakh) or both.
Third violation or severe injury/harm/death to livestock/poultry: Cancellation of license up to five years.
Offenses tried by court (third/continuing/severe violations): Imprisonment (6 months to 1 year) and fine (up to ₹10 lakh).
Compensation to owner of livestock/poultry for death, severe injury, or harm on productivity.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Feed Safety Assurance Officer, authorized officers, Licensing Authority, State Feed Quality Consultative Committee, and Courts of Judicial Magistrate of the First Class.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through sampling, analysis, seizure, confiscation, disposal of products, inquiries, imposition of penalties, appeals, and prosecution in courts. Enforcement also involves verification of compliance at manufacturing, storage, and sales premises and during transportation.

rights: Right to a reasonable opportunity of being heard before an inquiry and penalty.
Right to prefer an appeal against an order imposing penalty.
Right to compensation for death or severe injury to livestock/poultry caused by an offense.
Consumers have the right to get their purchased feed analyzed at their own expense.
duties: Manufacturers, storers, distributors, and sellers must adhere to the quality standards and regulations prescribed by the Act.
Persons from whom samples are taken must cooperate and provide necessary signatures/thumb impressions.
Agents, dealers, and transporters must furnish required details of stock holders.
Licensees must comply with the terms and conditions under which their license is granted.
Companies and institutions have a duty to ensure their directors, managers, and employees comply with the Act.
obligations: Obligation to obtain a license for manufacture, storage, distribution, or sale of livestock feed, poultry feed, and mineral mixture.
Obligation to ensure products are not adulterated, substandard, or misbranded.
Obligation to cooperate with Feed Safety Assurance Officers and other enforcement authorities.
Obligation to pay expenses for analysis if the product is found to be substandard.
Obligation to pay penalties and compensation as determined by the authorities or courts.

key_procedures: Sampling: Collection of samples by Feed Safety Assurance Officer, division into five parts, sealing, witnessing, and obtaining signatures.
Analysis: Submission of sealed samples to approved laboratories for testing within specified timelines, with expense recovery if found substandard.
Inquiry: Conducting an inquiry by the Licensing Authority with an opportunity for the person to be heard, before imposing penalties.
Appeal: Filing an appeal to the State Feed Quality Consultative Committee within thirty days of penalty order.
Prosecution: Initiation of prosecution based on complaint by Feed Safety Enforcement Officer and recommendation by State Feed Quality Consultative Committee, for offenses triable by court.
Confiscation and Disposal: Immediate seizure and disposal of sub-standard, adulterated, or misbranded products.
administration: The Act is administered through various authorities including the Licensing Authority, Feed Safety Assurance Officer, Feed Safety Enforcement Officer, and the State Feed Quality Consultative Committee. The Government also plays a role in notifying laboratories and approving rates for analysis.
important_notes: Expenses for analysis of samples will be borne by the licensee if the sample may cause immediate health hazards.
If a sample is subject to speedy and natural decay, the Feed Safety Assurance Officer shall apply to the Licensing Authority for permission to dispose of it.
The Act provides for distinct procedures and penalties for offenses tried by the Licensing Authority and offenses tried by a Court.
In case of contradiction in analysis reports from two labs, the State Feed Quality Consultative Committee can send the sample to a referral lab.

title: THE KERALA LOCAL SELF GOVERNMENT COMMON SERVICE ACT 2022
purpose: To provide for the common service of the local self-governments in the State of Kerala, to regulate the recruitment and conditions of service of persons appointed to the common service and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the local self-governments in the State of Kerala. This includes Corporations, Municipalities, Town Panchayats, and Grama Panchayats.

key_definitions.Local Self-Government: Includes Corporations, Municipalities, Town Panchayats and Grama Panchayats.
key_definitions.Common Service: Means the common service constituted for the local self-governments in the State for the purpose of this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Kerala Local Self Government Common Service Act, 2022'. It also outlines the extent of its application and when it comes into force.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'Local Self-Government', 'Common Service', 'Government', etc.

important_rules: The Act establishes a Common Service for local self-governments.
It aims to regulate recruitment and conditions of service for persons appointed to this Common Service.
The Act likely details procedures for appointment, promotion, disciplinary actions, and other service-related matters for employees within the local self-government Common Service.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through rules and regulations made under the Act, and potentially through designated authorities within the local self-government structures.

rights: Employees in the Common Service have rights pertaining to their recruitment, service conditions, and career progression as defined by the Act and rules.
duties: Employees are expected to perform their duties diligently and in accordance with the rules and regulations.
Local Self-Governments have a duty to implement the provisions of the Act and establish and manage the Common Service.
obligations: The Government has an obligation to frame the necessary rules and oversee the implementation of the Act.

key_procedures: Establishment of the Common Service for local self-governments.
Recruitment procedures for various posts within the Common Service.
Procedures for appointment, promotion, transfer, and disciplinary actions.
Mechanisms for addressing grievances of employees in the Common Service.
administration: Department of Local Self-Government, Government of Kerala
important_notes: This Act consolidates and standardizes the service conditions across different local self-governing bodies in Kerala.
The Act appears to supersede or amend existing provisions related to the services of local self-government employees.
The gazette notification indicates the date of publication and the registration number of the act.

title: THE KERALA LOK AYUKTA (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2022
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Lok Ayukta Act, 1999.
scope: This Act amends the Kerala Lok Ayukta Act, 1999, and applies to matters concerning the Lok Ayukta and Upa-Lok Ayuktas in Kerala.

key_definitions.principal Act: The Kerala Lok Ayukta Act, 1999 (8 of 1999).
key_definitions.public servant: Defined in clause (o) of section 2 of the principal Act.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Kerala Lok Ayukta (Amendment) Act, 2022, and specifies the commencement dates for its various sections. Sections 2, 3(iii), 5, 6(i), 6(ii), and 7 come into force at once, while the remaining sections are deemed to have come into force on February 7, 2022.

Amends clause (d) of section 2 of the principal Act to specify that in the case of the Chief Minister, the State Legislative Assembly is the relevant body, and inserts a new item for Members of the State Legislative Assembly, referring to the Speaker of the State Legislative Assembly.

Makes several amendments to section 3 of the principal Act, including inserting 'or that of a Judge of a High Court' in sub-section (2), omitting 'holds or' in sub-section (3), and omitting the proviso to sub-section (3).

Amends sub-section (1) of section 5 of the principal Act to include 'or till he completes the age of seventy years, whichever is earlier' as a condition for appointment, and inserts a proviso stating that Lok Ayukta and Upa-Lok Ayukta appointed before this amendment remain governed by the original provisions.
Omit sub-section (3) of section 6 of the principal Act.

Omit item (v) of sub-section (1) and the words 'or an office bearer of a political party at the State level' from sub-section (2) of section 7 of the principal Act. Inserts new sub-sections (5A) and (5B) regarding the discharge of functions by a Upa-Lok Ayukta in case of vacancy or absence of the Lok Ayukta.

Substitutes section 14 of the principal Act. The amended section details the process for recommendations made by the Lok Ayukta or Upa-Lok Ayukta after investigation, requiring the competent authority to examine the recommendation and communicate action taken or reasons for inaction within ninety days. Special provisions are made for the State Legislative Assembly and for public servants falling under specific categories.
Omit the words, figures, and symbol 'Notwithstanding anything contained in section 14,' from section 15 of the principal Act.
Provides for the validation of actions taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the Kerala Lok Ayukta (Amendment) Ordinance, 2022, ensuring continuity of legal effect.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Competent authorities as defined in the principal Act and this amendment, including the State Legislative Assembly, Speaker of the State Legislative Assembly, and appointing authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through examination of recommendations, communication of action taken or proposed, and initiation of appropriate action by competent and appointing authorities as detailed in Section 14.

rights: Right of the Lok Ayukta and Upa-Lok Ayukta to make recommendations regarding public servants found unfit to hold their posts.
Right of the competent authority to examine recommendations and decide on action or reasons for inaction.
duties: Duty of the competent authority to examine recommendations and communicate action within ninety days.
Duty of appointing authorities to initiate appropriate action for certain public servants.
Duty of the Government to take appropriate action for All India Service members.
obligations: Obligation of the Lok Ayukta or Upa-Lok Ayukta to make recommendations when a complaint is substantiated and the public servant is unfit.
Obligation to adhere to time limits for action by competent authorities.

key_procedures: Procedure for amendment of the Kerala Lok Ayukta Act, 1999, involving legislative enactment.

Procedure for handling recommendations of the Lok Ayukta or Upa-Lok Ayukta: Investigation, satisfaction of substantiation, recommendation to competent authority, examination of recommendation by competent authority, communication of action or reasons for inaction within 90 days (with exclusions for Legislative Assembly sessions).
Procedure for vacancy or absence of Lok Ayukta: Governor may authorize the senior-most Upa-Lok Ayukta to discharge functions.
administration: Law (Legislation-E) Department, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act is published by authority and received the assent of the President on February 9, 2024.
The commencement dates for different sections vary, with some coming into force immediately and others deemed to have come into force on February 7, 2022.
A proviso ensures that Lok Ayukta and Upa-Lok Ayukta appointed before this amendment continue to be governed by the old provisions.
The validation section ensures that actions taken under the previous ordinance are considered valid under the amended Act.

title: THE KERALA MARINE FISHING REGULATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2021
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Marine Fishing Regulation Act, 1980, for purposes including the regulation of fishermen in fishing vessels and restricting the use of fishing vessels for purposes other than fishing.
scope: The Act applies to marine fishing activities and fishing vessels within the State of Kerala. It regulates owners and users of fishing vessels and fishermen on board.

key_definitions.principal Act: The Kerala Marine Fishing Regulation Act, 1980 (10 of 1981).
key_definitions.Authorised Officer: An officer designated to grant permission for using fishing vessels for purposes other than fishing.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Kerala Marine Fishing Regulation (Amendment) Act, 2021, and states that it is deemed to have come into force on October 5, 2020.
Amends the preamble of the principal Act to include 'as well as the fishermen in the fishing vessels' after 'fishing vessels in the sea'.

Renumber section 5 to 4A and insert new sections 5 and 5A. Section 5 empowers restriction and regulation of fishermen in fishing vessels, requiring Aadhar possession. Section 5A prohibits the use of fishing vessels for purposes other than fishing without prior permission from the Authorised Officer.

Amends section 17 of the principal Act, primarily concerning penalties. It revises the penalty structure for contraventions of sections 4A, 7, or 9 based on the horsepower of the fishing vessel and introduces penalties for contravening sections 5 and 5A. It also includes provisions for cancellation of registration and license, and forfeiture of vessels for repeated offenses under section 5A.

Repeals the Kerala Marine Fishing Regulation (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021, and provides that anything done or actions taken under the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the Act.

important_rules: Rule: No owner of a fishing vessel shall allow any person in the fishing vessel unless they possess Aadhar (Section 5).
Rule: No owner of a fishing vessel shall use it for any purpose other than fishing without prior permission from the Authorised Officer (Section 5A).

penalties: For contravention of sections 4A, 7, or 9 (by owner/master of a fishing vessel), penalties are graded based on the horsepower of the vessel, ranging from five thousand rupees (up to 10 hp) to two lakh fifty thousand rupees (above 280 hp).
For contravention of sections 4A, 5A, or 9 by any person using a non-motorised fishing vessel, a penalty of five thousand rupees applies.
For contravention of section 5 (regarding Aadhar possession), penalty may extend to one thousand rupees, two thousand rupees for a second offense, and five thousand rupees for subsequent offenses.

For contravention of section 5A (using vessel for non-fishing purposes), penalties are as specified in section 17(1)(a) and (b). For second or subsequent offenses, registration and license shall be cancelled, and the fishing vessel shall be forfeited.
For contravening any provision of the Act or rules where no specific penalty is provided, a fine may extend to five thousand rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Adjudicating Officer is mentioned in relation to inquiries and imposing penalties.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inquiries conducted by the Adjudicating Officer, leading to the imposition of fines, cancellation of registration/licenses, and forfeiture of vessels.

rights: Right to use fishing vessels for fishing, subject to compliance with the Act and regulations.
Right to obtain permission from the Authorised Officer to use a fishing vessel for non-fishing purposes.
duties: Duty of fishing vessel owners to ensure persons on board possess Aadhar.
Duty of fishing vessel owners to use vessels only for fishing or obtain prior permission for other uses.
Duty to comply with all provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder.
obligations: Obligation to pay prescribed penalties for contraventions.
Obligation to have fishing vessels registered and licensed.

key_procedures: Procedure for inquiry by the Adjudicating Officer to determine contravention of provisions like sections 4A, 7, or 9.
Procedure for obtaining prior permission from the Authorised Officer to use a fishing vessel for purposes other than fishing.
administration: Law (Legislation-I) Department of the Government of Kerala is involved in the notification and publication of the Act. The Adjudicating Officer and Authorised Officer are key administrative roles for enforcement.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force retrospectively from October 5, 2020.
Penalties for contravening section 5A include cancellation of registration and license and forfeiture of the vessel for repeat offenses.

title: THE KERALA MARINE FISHING REGULATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2021
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Marine Fishing Regulation Act, 1980, for the purposes of regulating fishing vessels and fishermen within the sea.
scope: Applies to fishing vessels and fishermen operating in the sea within the geographical jurisdiction of Kerala. It amends the principal Act (The Kerala Marine Fishing Regulation Act, 1980).

key_definitions.fishing vessel: Not explicitly defined in the amendment, but implied to be a vessel used for fishing.
key_definitions.fishermen: Refers to persons in fishing vessels.
key_definitions.Authorised Officer: An officer designated to grant permission for uses other than fishing.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Kerala Marine Fishing Regulation (Amendment) Act, 2021, and states that it is deemed to have come into force on October 5, 2020.
Amends the preamble of the principal Act to include 'as well as the fishermen in the fishing vessels' after 'fishing vessels in the sea'.

Renumbering section '5' to '4A' and inserting new sections '5' and '5A'. Section '5' empowers the restriction and regulation of fishermen in fishing vessels, requiring Aadhar possession. Section '5A' prohibits the use of fishing vessels for purposes other than fishing without prior permission from the Authorised Officer.

Substitutes sub-section (1) and its clauses to detail penalties for contravention of sections 4A, 7, 9, 5A, and rules made thereunder. It introduces a tiered penalty system based on the horsepower of the fishing vessel and a fixed penalty for non-motorised vessels. It also inserts sub-sections (4a), (4b), and (4c) to define penalties for contravening section 5, section 5A, and general contraventions of the Act or rules, respectively. This includes provisions for cancellation of registration and license, and forfeiture of the vessel for repeated offenses under section 5A.

Repeals the Kerala Marine Fishing Regulation (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021 (110 of 2021) and saves all actions taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance.

important_rules: No owner of a fishing vessel shall allow any person in the fishing vessel unless he possesses Aadhar (Section 5).
No owner of a fishing vessel shall use, or cause or allow to be used, the fishing vessel for any purpose other than fishing without the prior permission of the Authorised Officer (Section 5A).
Penalties are prescribed based on the horsepower of the fishing vessel for contravening provisions like sections 4A, 7, or 9 (Section 17(1)(a)).
A penalty of five thousand rupees is prescribed for using non-motorised fishing vessels in contravention of sections 4A, 5A, or 9, or any rules made thereunder (Section 17(1)(b)).

penalties: For contravening Section 5: Penalty up to one thousand rupees for the first offense, up to two thousand rupees for the second offense, and up to five thousand rupees for subsequent offenses.

For contravening Section 5A: Penalties as mentioned in Section 17(1)(a) and (b). For second or subsequent offenses, the registration and license of the vessel shall be cancelled and the fishing vessel shall be forfeited.

For contravening sections 4A, 7, or 9 based on vessel horsepower (Section 17(1)(a)): Tiered penalties ranging from five thousand rupees (for vessels up to 10 hp) to two lakh fifty thousand rupees (for vessels above 280 hp).
For contravening sections 4A, 5A, or 9 with non-motorised vessels: A penalty of five thousand rupees (Section 17(1)(b)).
For contravening any provision of the Act or rules where no specific penalty is provided: Fine up to five thousand rupees (Section 17(4c)).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Adjudicating Officer is mentioned in relation to conducting inquiries and imposing penalties.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inquiries conducted by the Adjudicating Officer, imposition of fines, cancellation of registration and licenses, and forfeiture of fishing vessels.

rights: Right to use fishing vessels for fishing, subject to compliance with the Act.
Right to obtain permission from the Authorised Officer to use fishing vessels for purposes other than fishing.
duties: Duty of fishing vessel owners to ensure all persons on board possess Aadhar.
Duty of fishing vessel owners to obtain prior permission for uses other than fishing.
Duty to comply with provisions of sections 4A, 7, 9, and 5A of the principal Act and rules made thereunder.
obligations: Obligation to pay penalties as prescribed for contraventions.
Obligation to surrender registration and license and face forfeiture of the vessel for repeated offenses under Section 5A.

key_procedures: Inquiry by the Adjudicating Officer under Section 16 to determine contraventions of specified sections of the Act.
Application of tiered penalties based on horsepower of fishing vessels for contraventions.
Procedure for obtaining prior permission from the Authorised Officer for using fishing vessels for non-fishing purposes.
Procedure for cancellation of registration and license, and forfeiture of vessels for repeated offenses related to Section 5A.
administration: The Law (Legislation-I) Department of the Government of Kerala is indicated as the department responsible for publishing the Act. The Adjudicating Officer and Authorised Officer are appointed for enforcement and permission granting.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force retrospectively from October 5, 2020.
The amendment introduces mandatory Aadhar possession for persons in fishing vessels.
Stricter penalties, including vessel forfeiture, are introduced for using fishing vessels for unauthorized purposes.
Penalties are scaled based on the horsepower of the fishing vessel.

title: THE KERALA MARITIME BOARD (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2022
purpose: To amend the Kerala Maritime Board Act, 2017 for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: This act applies to the State of Kerala and amends the Kerala Maritime Board Act, 2017. It concerns the functioning, administration, and personnel of the Kerala Maritime Board.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Maritime Board (Amendment) Act, 2022, and it is deemed to have come into force on January 19, 2022.

Amends Section 3 of the principal Act regarding the Board's headquarters, regional office, nomination of the Chairman, eligibility criteria for the Chairman, and the role of the Chief Executive Officer.
Amends Section 8 of the principal Act to allow the Government to act on its own motion or the Board to act with the Government's previous approval.

Adds a sentence to Section 9(2) of the principal Act, requiring the responsible person to ensure the Board functions in the Government's interests and adheres to laws, rules, and procedures, including financial provisions.
Amends Section 13(1) of the principal Act, substituting the word 'notification' with 'order'.
Inserts a new sub-section (1a) into Section 14 of the principal Act, making the Controller of Finance and Accounts responsible for ensuring financial discipline in Board transactions.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 17
main_sections.description: Substitutes a new Section 17 concerning special provisions for employees of the Port Directorate and offices of the Ports. It addresses their continuation as Government employees, option to become Board employees, utilization of services, and disciplinary actions.
Omit section 18 of the principal Act.
Amends Section 90 of the principal Act regarding emergency situations, including changing the reason for intervention and the process for appointing an administrator.
Amends Section 91 of the principal Act, changing references from 'policy directions' to 'directions regarding priority matters'.
Amends Section 92 of the principal Act to include the State Government along with the Ministry of Shipping, Government of India.

Validates actions taken under the Kerala Maritime Board (Amendment) Ordinance, 2022 (9 of 2022) and prior to the commencement of this Act, ensuring they are considered as if done under the principal Act as amended.

important_rules: The headquarters of the Board shall be at Thiruvananthapuram and shall have a regional office at Kochi.
The Chairman shall be nominated by the State Government and must be an officer of All India Service or have administrative experience in government or public sector ports/Maritime Boards.
The Chief Executive Officer is designated as the Member Secretary.
The number of members in sub-section (5) of section 3 is reduced from five to three.
The Board must function according to government interests and strictly adhere to laws, rules, and procedures.
It is the duty of the Controller of Finance and Accounts to ensure financial discipline.
Employees of the Port Directorate and Port offices on the appointed day continue as Government employees with certain options and provisions for disciplinary action by the Board.
In emergency situations, intervention can be based on 'reasons mentioned in the order' instead of 'grave emergency'.
An administrator can be appointed to manage the Board's affairs for a period specified in the notification.
The Board's directions are related to 'priority matters' rather than 'policy directions'.

penalties: Disciplinary actions can be taken against employees continuing as Government employees (Section 17(3)).
The Board has powers of disciplinary action against any employee (Section 17(3)).
An administrator can be appointed if the Board fails to perform its duties within the prescribed period (Section 90(1)(b)).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Kerala Maritime Board, and the Government of Kerala.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amendments to existing sections, insertion of new sections, and provisions for appointment of administrators and disciplinary actions.

rights: Employees continuing as Government employees have rights that would have been available had the Board not been constituted (Section 17(1)).
Employees continuing as Government employees can choose to become Board employees (Section 17(2)).
Government employees continuing as such have the right to appeal to the Government against disciplinary action taken by the Board (Section 17(3)).
duties: The Board must function according to the interests of the Government and strictly adhere to all laws, rules, and procedures (Section 9(2)).
It shall be the duty of the Controller of Finance and Accounts to ensure financial discipline in all transactions of the Board (Section 14(1a)).
The Government has the right to utilize the services of employees who continue as Government employees, ensuring their rights are not infringed (Section 17(3)).
obligations: Strict adherence to all laws, rules, and procedures, including financial provisions, by the Board (Section 9(2)).
Ensuring financial discipline in all Board transactions (Section 14(1a)).
Employees have the obligation to comply with the utilization of their services by the Government (Section 17(3)).

key_procedures: Nomination of the Chairman by the State Government.
Process for employees of Port Directorate and Port offices to continue as Government employees or opt to become Board employees.
Process for disciplinary action against employees by the Board, with appeal to the Government.
Appointment of an administrator in case of Board's failure to perform duties.
Amendments to existing sections of the principal Act, involving substitution, insertion, or omission of specific provisions.
administration: Law (Legislation-I) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on January 19, 2022.
Section 17 provides for special provisions for employees transitioning from the Port Directorate and Port offices to the Board, ensuring continuity of service and rights.
Section 12 (Validation) confirms that actions taken under the Ordinance and prior to the Act's publication are legally valid as if done under the amended principal Act.

title: THE KERALA MEDICAL EDUCATION (REGULATION AND CONTROL OF ADMISSION TO PRIVATE MEDICAL EDUCATIONAL INST.) ACT
purpose: To regulate and control admission to private medical educational institutions in Kerala.
scope: Applies to private medical educational institutions in Kerala and the admission process therein.

key_definitions.private_medical_educational_institution: Includes colleges for degree courses in medicine, dentistry, homeopathy, Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani and other systems of Indian Medicine, as well as colleges for nursing, pharmacy and paramedical courses.
key_definitions.admission_process: Includes the process of selection and admission of students to any private medical educational institution.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and the date from which it comes into force.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'private medical educational institution', 'admission process', etc.
Outlines the principles and procedures for regulating admission to private medical educational institutions, emphasizing merit and transparency.
Establishes an Admission Supervisory Board responsible for overseeing the admission process and ensuring its fairness.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of the Board
main_sections.description: Details the powers and functions of the Admission Supervisory Board, including framing admission guidelines, hearing grievances, and taking corrective actions.
Addresses the regulation of fees that can be charged by private medical educational institutions.
Specifies penalties for any contravention of the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Admission to private medical educational institutions shall be based on merit as determined by entrance examinations and other prescribed criteria.
No capitation fees or donation shall be collected by any private medical educational institution.
The Admission Supervisory Board shall ensure transparency in the admission process and hear all grievances.
Institutions must adhere to the fee structure prescribed by the government.

penalties: Imprisonment and/or fine for contravention of the Act's provisions.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Admission Supervisory Board and other authorities designated by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, audits, investigations, and legal proceedings.

rights: Students have the right to a fair and transparent admission process based on merit.
Institutions have the right to charge prescribed fees.
duties: Institutions have the duty to comply with the admission regulations and guidelines.
Institutions have the duty to maintain transparency in admissions and fee collection.
Institutions have the duty not to collect capitation fees or donations.
obligations: To conduct admissions strictly on merit.
To submit admission details to the Supervisory Board.

key_procedures: Conducting entrance examinations for selection of students.
Publication of admission merit lists.
Handling of student grievances related to admission.
Reporting admission details to the Admission Supervisory Board.
administration: The Health and Family Welfare Department, Government of Kerala, likely oversees the implementation of this Act.
important_notes: The Act aims to prevent malpractice and irregularities in the admission of students to private medical colleges.
It seeks to ensure that admission is based solely on merit, thus benefiting deserving candidates.
The establishment of an independent Admission Supervisory Board is a key mechanism for effective regulation.

title: THE KERALA METROPOLITAN TRANSPORT AUTHORITY ACT, 2019
purpose: To provide for the establishment of Metropolitan Transport Authorities in the metropolitan areas of the State and for the co-ordination and integration of transport services and facilities therein and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to metropolitan areas in Kerala.

key_definitions.metropolitan area: An area declared as such by the Government by notification in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.transport authority: Refers to the Metropolitan Transport Authority established under the Act.
key_definitions.transport service: Includes any service or facility for the carriage of passengers or goods by road, rail, air or water.

main_sections.description: This section likely details the short title of the Act, its geographical extent of application, and the date from which it comes into force.
This section provides definitions for various terms used throughout the Act, ensuring clarity and consistent interpretation.

main_sections.section_title: Functions of the Metropolitan Transport Authority
main_sections.description: Outlines the various responsibilities and duties of the Metropolitan Transport Authority, including planning, coordination, and development of transport services and facilities.
Grants the Government or the Authority the power to frame rules and regulations to carry out the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: The Act likely establishes a Metropolitan Transport Authority for each metropolitan area.
The Authority will be responsible for planning and coordinating transport services.
Rules may be framed to govern the operation of transport services within metropolitan areas.

penalties: Specific penalties for contravention of provisions or rules made under the Act are likely detailed in later sections not fully visible.
Fines or other punishments may be prescribed.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Likely the Metropolitan Transport Authority and other relevant authorities as specified in the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the Authority and other enforcement agencies to ensure compliance with the Act's provisions and regulations.

rights: Citizens have the right to efficient and coordinated transport services within metropolitan areas.
The public has a right to be informed about transport plans and policies.
duties: The Metropolitan Transport Authority has the duty to plan, coordinate, and integrate transport services.
Transport operators have a duty to comply with the regulations and directives issued under the Act.
The Government has a duty to facilitate the establishment and functioning of the Authorities.
obligations: Operators of transport services must adhere to standards and regulations set by the Authority.

key_procedures: Establishment of Metropolitan Transport Authorities.
Development of integrated transport plans for metropolitan areas.
Coordination of various modes of transport (road, rail, etc.).
Regulation of transport services and facilities.
Framing of rules and bye-laws by the Authority.
administration: Likely the Transport Department of the Government of Kerala, and the Metropolitan Transport Authorities themselves.
important_notes: The Act aims to address the challenges of urban transport in metropolitan areas of Kerala.
The "digitally signed Gazette" note indicates the authenticity of the document.
The Act may contain provisions for penalties and enforcement mechanisms for non-compliance.

title: THE KERALA MICRO SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES FACILITATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2021
purpose: To amend the Kerala Micro Small and Medium Enterprises Facilitation Act, 2019 (Act 16 of 2019) to further facilitate the timely approval of other business enterprises.
scope: This act applies to the state of Kerala and amends the existing Act which deals with the facilitation of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and now extends its provisions to 'other business enterprises'.

key_definitions.Bureau: Refers to the 'Investment Facilitation Bureau' constituted under section 6A.
key_definitions.Scrutiny list: Means the list of fees payable along with the application by other business enterprises.
key_definitions.Other business enterprise: Means a business enterprise as defined in clause (dA) of Section 2 of the Kerala Industrial Single Window Clearance Boards and Industrial Township Development Act, 1999 (Act 5 of 2000), but does not include Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Kerala Micro Small and Medium Enterprises Facilitation (Amendment) Act, 2021' and states that it shall be deemed to have come into force on October 5, 2020.
Amends the long title of the principal Act (Kerala Micro Small and Medium Enterprises Facilitation Act, 2019) by inserting words to facilitate timely approval for other business enterprises.
Amends the preamble of the principal Act by inserting words to facilitate timely approval for other business enterprises.
Amends Section 1(1) of the principal Act by substituting 'Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises' with 'Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and Other Business Enterprises'.

Amends Section 2 of the principal Act. It substitutes 'Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises' with 'Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and Other Business Enterprises' in clause (c). It also inserts new clauses defining 'Bureau' and 'Scrutiny list', and inserts clause (dAj) defining 'Other business enterprise'.
Inserts new sections dealing with the formation, powers, and functions of the Investment Facilitation Bureau for facilitating other business enterprises.
Amends Section 12 of the principal Act to include the Bureau in relation to nodal agencies.
Repeals the Kerala Micro Small and Medium Enterprises Facilitation (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021 and provides for savings regarding actions taken under the said Ordinance.

important_rules: Rule: The Investment Facilitation Bureau shall be constituted by the Government through notification, comprising specified members to expedite approvals for other business enterprises.

Rule: The Bureau shall have the power to grant or reject applications for setting up other business enterprises within a specified period (two working days) after scrutinizing the application and scrutiny list.
Rule: An approval granted by the Bureau shall be valid for five years from the date of grant. Every other business enterprise shall submit a certificate of compliance within one year.

Rule: The Bureau may recommend to the competent authority for revocation of approval if an other business enterprise violates the provisions of the Act or rules, or if the information provided in the application is found to be false.

penalties: Revocation of approval by the Bureau upon recommendation to the competent authority, if the enterprise violates provisions or provides false information.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Bureau and competent authorities designated under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application process, scrutiny of applications and documents, issuance of approvals, and potential revocation of approvals.

rights: Right of 'other business enterprises' to receive timely approvals.
Right to apply for approval for establishing an 'other business enterprise'.
duties: Duty of the Bureau to facilitate timely approvals.
Duty of 'other business enterprises' to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules.
Duty of 'other business enterprises' to submit a certificate of compliance within one year of receiving approval.
Duty to submit application and pay fees in the prescribed manner.
obligations: Obligation to submit a joint application with a scrutiny list.
Obligation to comply with the terms and conditions of the approval.

key_procedures: Procedure: An 'other business enterprise' shall submit a joint application in the prescribed form, along with a scrutiny list and prescribed fees, to the Chief Executive Officer of the Bureau through the online portal.
Procedure: The Bureau shall, after scrutinizing the application and the scrutiny list, either grant approval with or without conditions, or require further details within two working days.

Procedure: Upon receiving approval, the 'other business enterprise' must submit a certificate of compliance within one year, and apply for renewal at least three months before the expiry of the approval.
administration: The Act is administered through the 'Investment Facilitation Bureau', constituted under the Act. The Kerala State Industrial Development Corporation and its associated entities like the Kerala Investment Promotion and Facilitation Cell play a role.
important_notes: Note: The Act explicitly states that an approval granted does not entitle any person to use land in contravention of the Kerala Paddy Land and Wet Land Conservation Act, 2008 or the Master Plan notified under the Kerala Town and Country Planning Act, 2016.
Note: The approval granted by the Bureau can be used as a valid document for any requirement, including financial assistance from banks or financial institutions.

title: THE KERALA MINERALS (VESTING OF RIGHTS) ACT, 2021
purpose: To vest in the Government the rights of the minerals in the soil and subsoil of the land in the State, excluding land that comes under the purview of the Travancore Proclamation dated 14th day of June, 1881 and Cochin Proclamation of 1905.
scope: The Act applies to all lands within the State of Kerala. Its subject matter scope is the rights to minerals in the soil and subsoil. It excludes lands covered by the Travancore Proclamation of 1881 and the Cochin Proclamation of 1905.

key_definitions.minerals: Minerals and minor-minerals as defined in clause (ad) and clause (e) respectively, of section 3 of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957 (Central Act 67 of 1957).
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Sub-section (1) states the short title of the Act as the Kerala Minerals (Vesting of Rights) Act, 2021. Sub-section (2) deems the Act to have come into force on December 30, 2019.
Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'Government', 'minerals', 'prescribed', and 'State'.

Declares that all rights in minerals in the soil and subsoil of all lands, irrespective of ownership or tenure, shall stand vested in and be subject to the control of the Government from the commencement date of the Act. This vests these rights despite any other law, court judgment, decree, order, or proclamation.
Specifies that the manner of vesting of mineral rights in the State (excluding areas under the specified proclamations) shall be the same as in the Travancore and Cochin areas previously mentioned.

Grants the Government the power to make rules by notification in the Gazette to carry out the provisions of the Act. It also mandates that these rules must be laid before the Legislative Assembly for a specific period, allowing for modifications or annulment by the Assembly.

Empowers the Government to issue orders published in the Gazette to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act's provisions, provided such orders are not inconsistent with the Act and are made within two years of the commencement date. Such orders also need to be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

Repeals the Kerala Minerals (Vesting of Rights) Ordinance, 2021 (Ordinance 124 of 2021). It also provides a saving clause, stating that anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act can be made by the Government through a Gazette notification.
Any rule made must be laid before the Legislative Assembly and is subject to its modification or annulment.
The Government can issue orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act, with certain limitations on time and consistency with the Act.

rights: All rights in minerals in the soil and subsoil of lands in the State (excluding specified areas) are vested in the Government.
duties: The Government has control over the vested mineral rights.

key_procedures: Vesting of mineral rights in the Government from the commencement date of the Act.
Making and laying of rules before the Legislative Assembly for approval or modification.
Removal of difficulties by the Government through Gazette notification, subject to legislative review.
administration: The Government of Kerala (specifically, the Law (Legislation-C) Department is mentioned in the notification for publication).
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force retrospectively from December 30, 2019.
The power to remove difficulties exists for a period of two years from the commencement of the Act.
The Act repeals the Kerala Minerals (Vesting of Rights) Ordinance, 2021, but actions taken under the Ordinance are saved.

title: THE KERALA MOTOR TRANSPORT WORKERS’ PAYMENT OF FAIR WAGES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2023
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Motor Transport Workers’ Payment of Fair Wages Act, 1971, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: This Act applies to motor transport workers employed or paid in specified areas within the state of Kerala. It amends the Kerala Motor Transport Workers’ Payment of Fair Wages Act, 1971.

key_definitions.authority: The authority appointed under section 3A of the Act.
key_definitions.Deputy Labour Commissioner: The Deputy Labour Commissioner of the State having jurisdiction in the respective areas.
key_definitions.Inspector: The Chief Inspector or any Inspector appointed under sub-section (1) of section 4 of the Motor Transport Workers Act, 1961 (Central Act 27 of 1961).
key_definitions.Labour Commissioner: The Labour Commissioner of the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Kerala Motor Transport Workers’ Payment of Fair Wages (Amendment) Act, 2023, and states that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Government by notification in the Gazette.

Amends Section 2 of the principal Act by re-lettering existing clause (a) to (ab) and inserting new clauses (a), (aa), (ac), (ad), and (e) to define 'authority', 'Deputy Labour Commissioner', 'Inspector', 'Labour Commissioner', and 'Government'.

Inserts a new section 3A titled 'Claims arising out of non-payment of fair wages and penalty thereof'. This section empowers the Government to appoint an authority to hear and decide claims related to underpayment of fair wages, outlines the application process, the authority's powers to direct payment and compensation, and the appeal process to the Labour Commissioner.
Amends Section 4 of the principal Act by substituting the words 'five hundred rupees' with 'two thousand rupees'.
Amends sub-section (1) of Section 6 of the principal Act by substituting the word 'authority' with the word 'Inspector'.

important_rules: Rule: Applications for claims regarding underpayment of fair wages must be presented within six months from the date fair wages become payable, with provisions for condoning delay for sufficient cause.
Rule: An appeal against an order of the authority must be filed within sixty days of receiving the order.
Rule: No appeal shall be admitted unless the appellant deposits the amount required to be paid or provides a certificate of deposit.

penalties: Penalty: Employers found to be paying less than fair wages may be directed to pay the deficit amount along with compensation not exceeding ten times the deficit amount.
Penalty: Failure to pay the amount directed by the authority can lead to recovery as arrears of public revenue due on land.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The 'authority' appointed under section 3A (not below the rank of Deputy Labour Commissioner), and the Collector for recovery purposes.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the process of hearing claims, issuing directions for payment and compensation, and recovery by the Collector if payments are not made.

rights: Right of motor transport workers to receive fair wages.
Right of motor transport workers to apply for redressal of claims regarding underpayment of fair wages.
Right to appeal against the order of the authority to the Labour Commissioner.
duties: Duty of employers to pay fair wages to motor transport workers.
Duty of employers to comply with directions issued by the authority regarding payment of fair wages and compensation.
obligations: Obligation of the employer to pay the directed amount and compensation within the time limit fixed by the authority.
Obligation of the appellant to deposit the required amount or produce a certificate of deposit to prefer an appeal.

key_procedures: Procedure for filing a claim: A motor transport worker, or their representative, can apply to the appointed authority within six months (with possibility of condonation) for a direction regarding underpayment of fair wages.
Procedure for hearing a claim: The authority shall hear the applicant and the employer, conduct further enquiry if necessary, and then direct payment of the deficit and compensation.
Procedure for appeal: A person aggrieved by an order can appeal to the Labour Commissioner within sixty days, subject to depositing the due amount.
administration: Law (Legislation-C) Department of the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: Note: The Act specifies that the 'authority' appointed under section 3A will be an officer not below the rank of Deputy Labour Commissioner.
Note: The maximum compensation for deficit in fair wages can be ten times the amount of the deficit.
Note: The fine under Section 4 has been increased from five hundred rupees to two thousand rupees.

title: THE KERALA MOTOR VEHICLES TAXATION (VALIDATION) ACT, 2017
purpose: To validate all acts, proceedings, or things done or taken by the Government, its officers, or any subordinate authority in connection with the levy and collection of motor vehicles tax during the period from April 1, 2007, to July 23, 2014.
scope: This Act applies to acts, proceedings, and things related to the levy and collection of motor vehicles tax in Kerala. It specifically covers the period from April 1, 2007, to July 23, 2014. The validation extends to actions taken by the Government, any officer of the Government, or any authority under the Government.

main_sections.description: (1) States the short title of the Act as the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation (Validation) Act, 2017. (2) Declares that the Act shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of levy, collection, etc. of taxes on motor vehicles
main_sections.description: This is the main operative section. It stipulates that notwithstanding any provision in the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976, or any other law or court order, all motor vehicle taxes assessed, levied, or collected between April 1, 2007, and July 23, 2014, are deemed valid. It further states that all related actions taken by the Government or its authorities during this period are also deemed lawful, as if the tax was levied under the amended Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act. It also bars suits for refunds and prevents courts from enforcing orders for refunds of such taxes.

important_rules: All motor vehicle taxes assessed, levied, or collected from April 1, 2007, to July 23, 2014, are deemed to have always been validly assessed, levied, or collected.

All acts, proceedings, or things done or taken by the Government or its officers/authorities in connection with the assessment, levy, or collection of these taxes are deemed to have always been done or taken in accordance with the law.
No suit or other proceeding shall be instituted, maintained, or continued in any court against the Government or any person/authority for the refund of any tax paid under this validation.
No court shall enforce any decree or order directing the refund of any tax paid under this validation.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government or any officer of the Government or any authority under the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the validation of past actions and the prohibition of legal challenges seeking refunds.

rights: The right of the Government and its authorities to have their past actions regarding motor vehicle tax levy and collection (between April 1, 2007, and July 23, 2014) deemed lawful.
obligations: Taxpayers are obligated to accept the validated levy and collection of taxes without recourse to legal action for refunds.
Courts are obligated not to enforce decrees or orders for the refund of such validated taxes.

administration: Law (Legislation-D) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The validation specifically covers the period from April 1, 2007, to July 23, 2014.
The validation is effective irrespective of any contrary provisions in other laws or court judgments.
The validation is in pursuance of clause (3) of Article 348 of the Constitution of India.

title: THE KERALA MUNICIPALITY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2020
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994 (20 of 1994).
scope: This act applies to municipalities in the state of Kerala and amends specific provisions within the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994.

main_sections.description: (1) This Act may be called the Kerala Municipality (Amendment) Act, 2020. (2) It shall come into force at once.

This section details the amendments to sub-section (3) of section 6 of the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994. Specifically, it modifies clause (a) and clause (b) of the said sub-section by substituting certain numerical values.  

In clause (a):
- Sub-clause (i): 'twenty five' is replaced with 'twenty six'.
- Sub-clause (ii): 'twenty five' is replaced with 'twenty six', and 'fifty two' is replaced with 'fifty three'.

In clause (b):
- Sub-clause (i): 'fifty five' is replaced with 'fifty six'.
- Sub-clause (ii): 'fifty five' is replaced with 'fifty six', and 'one hundred' is replaced with 'one hundred and one'.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but implied to be the authorities responsible for implementing the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text.

administration: Law (Legislation-C) Department, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The act comes into force immediately upon enactment.
The amendments are specific numerical changes to section 6(3) of the principal Act.

title: THE KERALA MUNICIPALITY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2023
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994. Specifically amends section 407 of the principal act. Geographical scope is the state of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the act as 'The Kerala Municipality (Amendment) Act, 2023' and specifies that it shall come into force immediately.
This section amends sub-section (1) of section 407 of the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994. It substitutes the date '31st July, 2017' with '7th November, 2019'.

important_rules: Substitution of date in Section 407(1) of the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994: The figures, words, and symbol '31st July, 2017' are replaced with '7th November, 2019'.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but implied to be within the purview of the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994 and its administrative bodies.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application and enforcement of the amended provisions of the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994.

administration: Law (Legislation-C) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act was passed by the Kerala Legislative Assembly and received the assent of the Governor on April 11, 2023.
The Act is a translation in English of the Malayalam version.

title: THE KERALA MUNICIPALITY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2024
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994, primarily to introduce provisions related to waste management and its associated regulations.
scope: This act applies to municipalities within the state of Kerala. It amends the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994, specifically focusing on waste management, collection, processing, disposal, and related user fees and penalties.

key_definitions.waste management: The segregation, collection, transportation, storage, processing, or disposal of waste, including solid waste.

main_sections.description: Names the act as the Kerala Municipality (Amendment) Act, 2024, and specifies its commencement date. Items (i) and (vi) of section 25 come into force immediately, while other sections are deemed to have come into force on December 9, 2023.
Inserts the term 'waste management' into sub-section (1) of section 58 of the principal Act, following 'welfare programmes'.
Inserts a new Chapter XVIA, titled 'Management of waste', after section 325 of the principal Act.
Defines 'waste management' for the purposes of Chapter XVIA and section 58. It also states that undefined terms will derive their meaning from the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.

Substitutes sub-section (1a) to clarify the municipality's duties in waste management vesting with the council and discharged through the Secretary. Inserts sub-section (1aa) making the Secretary responsible for discharging these duties and empowering delegation. Substitutes sub-section (3) to allow the municipality to make arrangements for waste management activities directly or through other entities.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new sections after section 326
main_sections.description: Inserts new sections 326A, 326B, 326C, and 326D. These sections deal with the Council carrying out Government directions on solid waste management, responsibilities of the Secretary on waste management (including legal actions and fund expenditure), the responsibility of waste generators to hand over segregated waste and pay user fees, and provisions relating to user fees.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 327
main_sections.description: Replaces section 327 with a new section detailing the duties of waste generators for storage and deposit of solid waste, including the provision and maintenance of bins and proper segregation and deposit of waste. It also empowers the Secretary to impose fines for contravention.
Amends the marginal heading of section 328 to 'Contract with waste generator or owner or occupier for the removal of waste' and modifies the existing provision to refer to 'waste generator'.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 329
main_sections.description: Replaces section 329 of the principal Act with a new section (details not fully provided in the excerpt).

Makes several amendments to the Fourth Schedule, including changes to penalties for failure to submit licenses, relating to maintaining cleanliness of premises, and other specified violations. It also adjusts penalty amounts.
Repeals the Kerala Municipality (Amendment) Ordinance, 2023 (Ordinance 3 of 2023) and saves any actions taken or things done under the repealed Ordinance.

important_rules: Every household, owner, occupier of any premises, hotel, restaurant, industry, hospital or any other establishment must hand over or deposit segregated waste in the designated location and pay the user fee to the municipality or authorised agency as directed by the Secretary through public notice.

Each waste generator must provide separate bins or receptacles for the storage of biodegradable, non-biodegradable, and domestic hazardous waste, kept in good condition and at designated places as directed by the Secretary.
Waste generators must segregate and deposit waste as specified for easy collection and disposal.
Municipalities shall fix a user fee for services related to waste management for every waste generator.
If the Government fixes a user fee rate, the Council shall not fix a rate lower than that.
Waste generators must pay the user fee before the last date of every month or as decided by the Municipality.
Failure to pay user fee will result in recovery with a fine of fifty percent per month, only if the fee remains unpaid for ninety days past the due date.

penalties: Fines for contravention of provisions related to handing over segregated waste and paying user fees: not less than one thousand rupees but not exceeding ten thousand rupees.
Fines for contravention of provisions related to waste storage and deposit: not less than one thousand rupees but not exceeding ten thousand rupees.
Fine at the rate of fifty percent per month on unpaid user fees, recoverable only after ninety days of default.
Disciplinary action by the Government against the Secretary or responsible officers for failure or default in implementing decisions related to waste management.
Imposition of fine on the Council by the Government if it fails to comply with Government directions on solid waste management, after providing an opportunity to be heard.
Various penalties for offences under the Fourth Schedule, with amounts adjusted to reflect increased fines (e.g., from five hundred rupees to ten thousand rupees).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Secretary of the Municipality, the Council, the Government of Kerala, and authorized agencies.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through imposition of fines, legal actions, recovery of fees and fines as arrears of public revenue, disciplinary action against officials, and refusal of services to defaulters.

rights: Right to be heard before a fine is imposed on the Council for non-compliance with Government directions.
Right to exemption from user fee payment in whole or in part for certain waste generators or vacant buildings, as determined by the Government or Municipality.
Right to receive services in connection with waste management upon payment of user fees.
duties: Duty of the Council to carry out waste management duties and responsibilities through the Secretary.
Duty of the Secretary to discharge municipality's duties in waste management, delegate tasks, initiate legal actions, compound offences, and ensure effective waste management.
Duty of every household, owner, occupier, and establishment to hand over segregated waste and pay user fees.
Duty of waste generators to provide and maintain appropriate bins, segregate and deposit waste correctly.
Duty of each Municipality to fix and collect user fees for waste management services.
Duty of the Chairperson to ensure agendas related to Government directions are placed before the Council for decision.
obligations: Obligation of the Council to comply with Government directions on solid waste management.
Obligation of the Secretary to implement decisions regarding waste management, including those with deemed approval.
Obligation of waste generators to pay user fees by the specified dates.
Obligation of the Municipality to provide waste management services.
Obligation to comply with the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, and rules made thereunder in relation to waste management.

key_procedures: The Council shall discharge its duties and responsibilities regarding waste management through the Secretary.
The Secretary may delegate waste management duties to specific officers or employees based on streets, areas, or work nature.
The Council must take decisions on Government directions for solid waste management within one month; failure to do so results in deemed approval.
The Secretary must implement decisions, including deemed approvals, and face disciplinary action for failure.
Government may impose fines on the Council for non-compliance with directions, after giving a reasonable opportunity to be heard.
The Secretary may initiate legal action or compound offences related to waste management.

The Secretary may refuse services to user fee defaulters until payment is made.

administration: The Law (Legislation-C) Department of the Government of Kerala oversees the publication and notification of this Act. The day-to-day administration of waste management and related matters under this Act falls under the purview of the Municipalities, their Councils, and Secretaries.
important_notes: The Act aims to align waste management practices with the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
Words and expressions not defined in this Act but defined in the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, and its rules, shall have the same meanings as per that Act.
A deemed approval mechanism exists for Government directions on solid waste management if the Council fails to decide within one month.
The Government can impose fines on Municipal Councils for non-compliance with directions, but an opportunity to be heard must be given.

title: THE KERALA CO-OPERATIVE SOCIETIES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2021
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969, for the purposes specified in the Act.
scope: This Act applies to co-operative societies in the state of Kerala. It specifically introduces amendments related to Anand Pattern Milk Co-operative Societies, Regional Co-operative Milk Producers' Unions, District Co-operative Banks, and recruitment processes within Regional Co-operative Milk Producers' Unions.

key_definitions.anand_pattern_milk_co_operative_society: A Primary Dairy Co-operative Society, also known as 'Ksheerolpadaka Sahakarana Sangam', registered on or after January 1, 1980, functioning as per Anand Pattern model bye-laws. Its main objectives are procuring and marketing milk and milk products, supplying surplus milk to Regional Co-operative Milk Producers' Unions, and providing inputs to dairy farmers within its area of operation.
key_definitions.district_co_operative_bank: A central society with jurisdiction over one revenue district, having Primary Agricultural Credit Societies and Urban Co-operative Banks as members. Its principal object is to raise funds for lending to its members. This definition includes banks that existed before Registrar's orders under section 74H and ceased to exist due to them, with a proviso for continuation under certain conditions.
key_definitions.recruitment_committees: Committees constituted under section 80BB of the Act, responsible for the selection and recruitment of all permanent employees of Regional Co-operative Milk Producers' Unions.
key_definitions.regional_co_operative_milk_producers_uni: A central society whose members are Anand Pattern Primary Dairy Co-operative Societies. Its principal objective is to procure, process, and market milk and milk products, and to provide technical, financial, and production input assistance to its member societies and dairy farmers within an area covering two or more revenue districts.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Kerala Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2021, and specifies the dates from which various provisions come into force. Notably, some clauses are deemed to have come into force retrospectively.

Amends Section 2 of the principal Act by inserting new definitions for 'Anand Pattern Milk Co-operative Society', and substituting the definition of 'District Co-operative Bank'. It also inserts definitions for 'Recruitment Committees' and 'Regional Co-operative Milk Producers' Union'.

Adds a sub-section to Section 8A, mandating the admission of Anand Pattern Milk Co-operative Societies with a regular elected Managing Committee and engaged in milk procurement and sales, as members of the Regional Co-operative Milk Producers' Union, irrespective of other provisions.

Adds a proviso to Section 16(1) detailing specific membership eligibility criteria for Anand Pattern Milk Co-operative Societies, requiring members to own milch animals and pour a minimum quantity of milk.

Inserts a new section 16B that specifies eligibility conditions for continuing as an active member of Anand Pattern Milk Co-operative Societies, focusing on milk pouring quantity and animal ownership. It also states that only active members are eligible for committee membership.

Adds sub-sections to Section 28 introducing term limits (more than three terms or fifteen years, whichever is higher) for Presidents of Anand Pattern Milk Co-operative Societies holding office in the committee of a Regional Co-operative Milk Producers' Union. It also outlines conditions for eligibility to contest and hold office, including audit classification and milk supply, and specifies that the delegate to general body meetings and elections must be the President of the member society.

Adds sub-sections to Section 28AB, imposing term limits (two consecutive terms) for Presidents of Anand Pattern Milk Co-operative Societies holding office as President or Chairman of a Regional Co-operative Milk Producers' Union. It also mandates that either the President or Vice-President of Anand Pattern Milk Co-operative Societies must be a woman.

Adds a sub-section to Section 64 mandating an Annual Performance Audit for Regional Co-operative Milk Producers' Unions and their apex societies every financial year, to be conducted by individuals from a panel approved by the Functional Registrar of Dairy Co-operatives.

Amends Section 74H by adding clauses to sub-section (1) empowering the Registrar to order the merger of District Co-operative Banks with Kerala State Co-operative Bank under specific conditions, including consultation with the RBI and a public interest clause. It outlines the procedure for objections and suggestions. It also adds sub-section (1A) detailing the transfer of assets and liabilities upon merger.

Inserts a new section 80BB providing for the constitution of Recruitment Committees by the Government for the selection and recruitment process of all permanent employees of Regional Co-operative Milk Producers' Unions.

important_rules: Rule related to Anand Pattern Milk Co-operative Societies: Members must own milch animals, reside within the area of operation, and pour milk for a specified number of days and quantity to be admitted or continue as members.

Rule related to Anand Pattern Milk Co-operative Societies: To continue as an active member, one must pour at least five hundred litres of milk for 180 days in the preceding twelve months and own at least one milch cow or buffalo, reared in a shed or farm within the society's area of operation.

Rule related to committee membership in Anand Pattern Milk Co-operative Societies: Only active members (as defined by the pouring and ownership criteria) are eligible to become or continue as members of the society's committee.

Rule related to Regional Co-operative Milk Producers' Union committee membership: Presidents of Anand Pattern Milk Co-operative Societies can hold office on the Regional Co-operative Milk Producers' Union committee for a maximum of three terms or fifteen years.

Rule related to eligibility for Regional Co-operative Milk Producers' Union committee elections: Presidents of Anand Pattern Milk Co-operative Societies can contest elections only if their society has an audit classification of A or B and supplies a minimum quantity of milk to the Union.

Rule for Regional Co-operative Milk Producers' Union committee delegates: The delegate representing a member Anand Pattern Milk Co-operative Society at general body meetings and elections must be the President of that member society.

Rule for Regional Co-operative Milk Producers' Union President/Chairman: Presidents of Anand Pattern Milk Co-operative Societies can hold office as President or Chairman of a Regional Co-operative Milk Producers' Union for no more than two consecutive terms.
Rule for Anand Pattern Milk Co-operative Societies leadership: Either the President or the Vice-President of an Anand Pattern Milk Co-operative Society must be a woman.

Rule for Regional Co-operative Milk Producers' Union and Apex Society Audits: Annual Performance Audits must be conducted every financial year by engaging persons from a panel recommended by the apex society and approved by the Functional Registrar of Dairy Co-operatives.

Rule for District Co-operative Bank Mergers: If a District Co-operative Bank's general body does not pass a resolution under section 14A, the Registrar can order its merger with the Kerala State Co-operative Bank after consulting the RBI and following a defined procedure for objections and suggestions.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Registrar of Co-operative Societies, the Governor of Kerala (for assent), and potentially other designated authorities as implied by the enforcement of various provisions.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amendments to the principal Act, specific directives from the Registrar (e.g., for mergers), and the application of defined eligibility criteria and term limits for various positions within co-operative societies and unions. Enforcement also includes audit processes and potential legal challenges.

rights: Right of Anand Pattern Milk Co-operative Societies to be admitted as members of Regional Co-operative Milk Producers' Unions.
Right of members of District Co-operative Banks to object to proposed merger orders and withdraw shares/deposits/loans.
Right of Anand Pattern Milk Co-operative Societies to have either their President or Vice-President be a woman.
Right of societies to have their delegates to Regional Co-operative Milk Producers' Union meetings be their President.
duties: Duty of Anand Pattern Milk Co-operative Societies to procure and market milk, and provide inputs to dairy farmers.
Duty of Anand Pattern Milk Co-operative Societies to meet specific milk pouring and animal ownership criteria to remain active members and eligible for committee positions.
Duty of Regional Co-operative Milk Producers' Unions to provide technical, financial, and production input assistance to member societies and dairy farmers.
Duty of Regional Co-operative Milk Producers' Unions and their apex societies to undergo annual performance audits.
Duty of District Co-operative Banks to follow procedures for resolutions under section 14A and to comply with merger orders if issued.
obligations: Obligation for certain office bearers in Regional Co-operative Milk Producers' Unions to adhere to term limits.
Obligation for Presidents of Anand Pattern Milk Co-operative Societies to meet audit and milk supply criteria to contest elections for Regional Co-operative Milk Producers' Union committees.
Obligation to constitute and utilize Recruitment Committees for appointments in Regional Co-operative Milk Producers' Unions.

key_procedures: Procedure for admitting Anand Pattern Milk Co-operative Societies as members of Regional Co-operative Milk Producers' Unions: Societies with elected committees and active milk business must be admitted.

Procedure for eligibility to continue as an active member of Anand Pattern Milk Co-operative Societies: Members must meet specific milk pouring and animal ownership criteria within defined periods and areas of operation.

Procedure for holding office in Regional Co-operative Milk Producers' Union committees by Presidents of Anand Pattern Milk Co-operative Societies: Adherence to term limits and eligibility conditions (audit classification, milk supply) is required.

Procedure for contesting elections to Regional Co-operative Milk Producers' Union committees by Presidents of Anand Pattern Milk Co-operative Societies: The member society must meet audit classification and milk supply minimums. Special provisions exist for revived or newly Anand Pattern-model societies.

Procedure for merger of District Co-operative Banks: The Registrar, after consulting RBI, can order a merger if the general body doesn't pass a resolution under section 14A. This involves sending proposed orders, publishing notices, considering objections within a specified period, and making modifications if necessary. Members/creditors objecting have the option to withdraw their stake.

Procedure for conducting Annual Performance Audits: Audits of Regional Co-operative Milk Producers' Unions and their apex societies are to be conducted annually by engaging personnel from an approved panel.
administration: The Law Department (Legislation-H) of the Government of Kerala publishes the Act. The Registrar of Co-operative Societies plays a significant role in enforcement and decision-making, particularly concerning mergers. The Functional Registrar of Dairy Co-operatives is involved in approving panels for audits.
important_notes: Some provisions of the Act have retrospective effect, coming into force on dates in 2020 and early 2021.
The definition of 'District Co-operative Bank' includes those that have ceased to exist due to Registrar's orders, with specific conditions for their continuation.

Exceptions and provisos exist for term limits and eligibility criteria in various sections, particularly for existing office bearers, revived societies, or those newly adopting Anand Pattern bye-laws.
The appointment of employees in Regional Co-operative Milk Producers' Unions is exclusively managed by newly constituted Recruitment Committees.

purpose: To further amend the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, 1994.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and amends provisions of the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, 1994.

key_definitions.empaneled_licensee: A person registered with the Regional Joint Director of Urban Affairs or registered under the Kerala Panchayat Raj Building Permit Rules, 2019, who is qualified to issue self-certification and is empanelled by the local self-government or competent authority as an institution, architect, engineer, building designer, supervisor or town planner.
key_definitions.buildings_of_low_occupancy_risk: Includes residential buildings with an area of less than 100 square meters and up to two floors, hostels, orphanages, dormitories, old age homes, seminaries with a built-up area of less than 200 square meters, educational institutions with a built-up area of less than 200 square meters, buildings for public congregation for religious and charitable purposes with a built-up area of less than 200 square meters, buildings with a built-up area of less than 100 square meters and falling under G1 category, and buildings with a built-up area of less than 100 square meters that are non-hazardous and low-risk.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Kerala Panchayat Raj (Amendment) Act, 2021'. It also specifies the commencement dates for various sections, with some sections deemed to have come into force retrospectively.

Amends Section 70 of the principal Act, modifying the timings for certain provisions and inserting a new sub-section related to postal voting for specific categories of people.
