Amends Section 235A of the principal Act by including 'or buildings of low occupancy risk' and modifying the descriptions of 'any inspection' to include 'any inspection with online mode'.
Amends Section 235H of the principal Act by inserting the phrase 'including buildings of low occupancy risk'.
Amends Section 235I of the principal Act by reducing the time period from 'thirty days' to 'fifteen days'.
Amends Section 235J of the principal Act by reducing the time period from 'thirty days' to 'fifteen days'.

Inserts a new Section 235TE in the principal Act, providing for the application for construction or reconstruction of buildings of low occupancy risk. It outlines the process of submitting self-certified applications and obtaining a license certificate.

Amends Section 235Z of the principal Act by adding new sub-sections detailing penalties for violations related to self-certification of buildings of low occupancy risk. It specifies suspension periods for empanelled licensees and imposes fines on owners and licensees for deviations from approved plans.

Repeals the Kerala Panchayat Raj (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021 (Ordinance 134 of 2021). It also includes a saving clause stating that anything done or deemed to have been done under the repealed Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done under this Act.

important_rules: Self-certification for low occupancy risk buildings: The owner and the empanelled licensee jointly provide a self-certification stating that the building plan, layout plan, etc., comply with the provisions of the Act, rules, and any directives issued.
Postal voting provisions: Specified categories of voters, including those affected by an epidemic or in quarantine, are eligible for postal voting.

License suspension and penalties: Empanelled licensees can have their licenses suspended for up to five years for violations related to self-certification. Fines are imposed on owners and licensees for constructing buildings in violation of self-certified plans.
Time limits for appeals: Appeals against orders from the registering authority can be filed with the Government within thirty days of receiving the order.

penalties: Suspension of empanelled licensee's practice for up to five years.

Fines for owners and empanelled licensees for violations of self-certified plans: Rs. 2 lakhs for buildings up to 100 sq. m., Rs. 4 lakhs for buildings up to 200 sq. m., and Rs. 6 lakhs for buildings up to 300 sq. m.

penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspection, issuance of notices, imposition of penalties, suspension of licenses, and appeals.

duties: Duty of owner and empanelled licensee to provide self-certification.
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act, rules, and directives.
obligations: Obligation to obtain a license certificate for construction or reconstruction of low occupancy risk buildings.
Obligation to adhere to the timings specified for postal voting and direct voting.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining a license certificate for low occupancy risk buildings: Submit a self-certified application with relevant documents to the Secretary.
Procedure for postal voting: Eligible voters can cast their votes by post or in person at the polling station during the specified time.
Procedure for appeal against orders: File an appeal with the Government within thirty days of receiving the order.

The Act repeals the Kerala Panchayat Raj (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021, but actions taken under the Ordinance are validated.

title: THE KERALA PAYMENT OF PENSION TO MEMBERS OF LEGISLATURE (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2018
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature Act, 1976, to revise the pension rates for former members of the Kerala Legislature.

important_rules: For any period below two years of service, the pension rate is Rs. 8,000 per mensem.
For two years in the aggregate, the pension rate is Rs. 8,000 per mensem.
For three years in the aggregate, the pension rate is Rs. 12,000 per mensem.
For four years in the aggregate, the pension rate is Rs. 16,000 per mensem.
For five years in the aggregate, the pension rate is Rs. 20,000 per mensem.
An additional pension of Rs. 1,000 per mensem is payable for every year in excess of five years of service.
Fractions of a half year and above in calculating the net qualifying period for pension shall be rounded to the next completed year.
An additional pension of Rs. 3,000 per mensem is payable on completion of seventy years of age.
An additional pension of Rs. 3,500 per mensem is payable on completion of eighty years of age.
The maximum pension eligible under this Act shall not exceed Rs. 50,000 per mensem in aggregate.

title: The Kerala Plantation Tax (Repeal) Act, 2021
purpose: To repeal the Kerala Plantation Tax Act, 1960 (Act 17 of 1960).
scope: This Act applies to the State of Kerala and pertains to the repeal of the previously existing Kerala Plantation Tax Act, 1960. It primarily deals with the legal framework surrounding plantation tax collection and its cessation.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Plantation Tax (Repeal) Act, 2021, and that it shall come into force immediately.

This section formally repeals the Kerala Plantation Tax Act, 1960 (Act 17 of 1960). It also includes saving provisions to ensure that actions taken, offences committed, penalties incurred, and proceedings initiated under the repealed Act before the commencement of this Act are not affected. It clarifies that the repeal will not revive anything not in force, affect previous operations, or alter any rights, privileges, obligations, or liabilities acquired or incurred under the repealed Act. Furthermore, it ensures that any investigation, legal proceeding, or remedy in respect of such matters can be instituted, continued, or enforced as if the repealing Act had not been passed. Subsection (2) specifies that appeals pending before the Appellate Authority appointed under the repealed Act will be heard and disposed of as if the repealing Act had not been passed. It also states that nothing in subsection (1) affects the right to continue and complete proceedings related to tax assessment, imposition, collection, and levies under the repealed Act, or the liability to pay amounts due or the right to refunds.

penalties: Any fine, penalty, forfeiture, or punishment incurred in respect of any offence committed against the repealed Act shall not be affected by this repeal.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned as an enforcement authority for this repeal act itself, but the saving clauses refer to 'Appellate Authority' appointed under the repealed Act and the continuation of 'legal proceeding or remedy'.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The Act itself comes into force 'at once'. The saving provisions ensure that matters related to the repealed Act continue to be handled as if the repeal had not occurred, implying the continuation of existing legal processes for those specific matters.

rights: Any right acquired, accrued, or incurred under the repealed Act shall not be affected.
Any right to get a refund of the amount due under the repealed Act shall not be affected.
duties: Any obligation acquired, accrued, or incurred under the repealed Act shall not be affected.
The liability to pay the amount due from any person under the repealed Act shall not be affected.
obligations: Any obligation acquired, accrued, or incurred under the repealed Act shall not be affected.

key_procedures: Repeal of the Kerala Plantation Tax Act, 1960.
Continuation and disposal of appeals pending before the Appellate Authority appointed under the repealed Act.
Continuation and completion of proceedings related to tax assessment, imposition, collection, and levies under the repealed Act.
Handling of any fine, penalty, forfeiture, or punishment incurred in respect of offences under the repealed Act.

Institution, continuation, or enforcement of any investigation, legal proceeding, or remedy in respect of rights, privileges, obligations, liabilities, fines, penalties, forfeitures, or punishments as per the repealed Act.
administration: Law (Legislation-B) Department, Government of Kerala, as indicated by the notification and the presence of the Law Secretary.
important_notes: The Act comes into force immediately upon its enactment.
The repeal of the Kerala Plantation Tax Act, 1960, does not affect past actions, penalties, or ongoing legal proceedings related to that Act.

purpose: This amendment act aims to amend the Kerala Private Forests (Vesting and Assignment) Act, 1971. It introduces specific provisions and clarifications regarding the assessment of compensation for private forests vested with the government.
scope: The act applies to private forests in Kerala that have vested with the government under the Kerala Private Forests (Vesting and Assignment) Act, 1971. It specifically addresses the procedures for determining the value and compensation for these forests.

Rule 3: Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1) of Section 3 of the principal Act, the compensation for private forests shall be deemed to be the value of the forest produce, or an amount equivalent to the average yield of five per cent of the forest produce obtained from a forest with an extent of 30 acres, as may be prescribed.

obligations: Obligation to correctly assess the value of vested private forests.
Obligation to follow prescribed procedures for compensation assessment.

Procedure for using other evidence to establish the special nature of the property if not cultivated.
Procedure for determining the value of forest produce or an equivalent amount based on prescribed yields.

title: THE KERALA PUBLIC RECORDS ACT, 2025
purpose: To regulate the appraisal, collection, classification, preservation, administration of public records of the Government Departments, Local Self Government Institutions, State Public Sector Undertakings, Commissions, Boards and Committees constituted by the Government and accepting records from private sources and matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to public records of Government Departments, Local Self Government Institutions, State Public Sector Undertakings, Commissions, Boards and Committees constituted by the Government, and also includes records accepted from private sources within the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.appraisal: The evaluation of historical value of public records.
key_definitions.public_records: Includes any manuscript, copper plates, copper rolls, bamboo splints, palm leaves, ancient texts, leaves, case files, diagram, maps, photos, charts, documents, paper records, files, canvas records, plans, audio clippings and other various media records; any microfilm, microfiche and facsimile copy of records; any reproduction of image or images in its real size or not, embodied in such microfilm; any other records produced by computer or any other device, of any records creating agency.
key_definitions.archival_value: Records having historical, national or administrative importance which is recommended by the board to be acquired by the State Archives Department.
key_definitions.permanent_value: Records which are identified as not destructible after appraisal under various office manuals prevailing in the State which provides for the administration, preservation, appraisal, disposal etc., of public records.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and that it shall come into force at once.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'appraisal', 'Board', 'defunct institutions', 'Director', 'file', 'Government', 'Head of the Department', 'periodical review', 'prescribed', 'public records', 'public records of archival value', 'public records of permanent value', 'Purchase Committee', 'records creating agency', 'records from private sources', 'records officer', 'reference media', 'retension schedule', 'rules', and 'State'.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the Government to co-ordinate, regulate and supervise operations connected with administration, maintenance and appraisal of public records
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to co-ordinate, regulate and supervise all operations related to public records, and to authorize the Director or other officers to carry out specific functions such as supervision, acceptance of records, custody, arrangement, protection, exhibition, preparation of inventories, analysis of records management systems, ensuring security, promoting space utilization, providing advice, survey and inspection, organizing training, accepting records of archival value from private sources, regulating access, receiving records from defunct institutions, providing certified copies, destruction and disposal, accepting records of historical/national/administrative importance, and providing guidelines for preservation of records destroyed in disasters.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition against taking of originals of public records of permanent value out of the State
main_sections.description: Prohibits the removal of original public records of permanent value from the State without prior government approval, unless for official purposes.
Mandates every records creating agency to authorize one of its officers as a records officer and to set up record rooms and authorize a records officer for each.

Outlines the responsibilities of the records officer, including arrangement, maintenance, preservation, periodical review and weeding, appraisal, destruction, preparation of retention schedules, recommendations for declassification, adoption of standards, compilation of annual indices, and other record management functions.

main_sections.section_title: Power to determine norms and standards for training in archival science
main_sections.description: Grants the Director, with the Board's approval, the power to determine norms and standards for training in archival science and related subjects, including syllabus, evaluation, and examinations.

main_sections.section_title: Protection for acts done in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection against legal proceedings for acts done or intended to be done in good faith in pursuance of the Act or rules made thereunder.
States that the provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith in any other law for the time being in force.

Empowers the Government to make provisions to remove any difficulty in the implementation of the Act, not inconsistent with its provisions, within two years of its commencement. Such orders must be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act. These rules can cover various aspects of record management, including deposit of permanent records, disposal, appraisal, classification, destruction, submission of reports, and acceptance of records. Rules made must be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

Repeals a specific Government Order (G.O.(MS) No. 157/76/H.Edn. dated October 11, 1976) and states that anything done or any action taken under the repealed order shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Rules can be made by the Government to prescribe various aspects of record management, including the period for deposit of permanent records, the process for appraisal and destruction of records, the method of classification, the reporting procedures for records officers, and the manner of accepting records from private and defunct sources.
Any rule made under the Act must be laid before the Legislative Assembly and is subject to amendment or annulment by the Assembly.

penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the Government to co-ordinate, regulate and supervise operations, and through the responsibilities assigned to the Director and Records Officers.

obligations: Obligation not to take original public records of permanent value out of the State without prior approval.

Collection, classification, preservation, and administration of public records.

important_notes: The Act is a legislative amendment to a previous Act (2015 Act 18) and an Ordinance (2025 Ordinance 1).
The amendment is deemed to have come into force retrospectively from August 14, 2025.
A specific university, the National University of Advanced Legal Studies, is a focal point for the new provisions.

title: The Kerala Public Service Commission (Additional Functions as respects the services under the Waqf Board) Repealing Act, 2022
purpose: To repeal the Kerala Public Service Commission (Additional Functions as respects the services under the Waqf Board) Act, 2021.
scope: This act applies to the services under the Waqf Board in Kerala and concerns the additional functions of the Kerala Public Service Commission in relation to these services. The primary scope of this specific act is to repeal a previous act.

key_definitions.repealed Act: The Kerala Public Service Commission (Additional Functions as respects the services under the Waqf Board) Act, 2021 (Act 15 of 2021).

main_sections.description: (1) States that the Act may be called the Kerala Public Service Commission (Additional Functions as respects the services under the Waqf Board) Repealing Act, 2022. (2) States that the Act shall come into force at once.
This section formally repeals the Kerala Public Service Commission (Additional Functions as respects the services under the Waqf Board) Act, 2021 (Act 15 of 2021).

Notwithstanding the repeal of the 2021 Act, this section clarifies that the repeal will not affect the validity, invalidity, effect, or consequence of anything done or suffered, or any right, title, obligation, or liability acquired, accrued, or incurred under the repealed Act from its commencement date up to the commencement date of the current repealing Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not specified in the provided text, as the act is a repealing act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not specified in the provided text.

rights: Any rights acquired under the repealed Act are preserved.
duties: Any duties incurred under the repealed Act are preserved.
obligations: Any obligations acquired under the repealed Act are preserved.

administration: Law (Legislation-B) Department, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act repeals the Kerala Public Service Commission (Additional Functions as respects the services under the Waqf Board) Act, 2021 (Act 15 of 2021).
The 'Saving' clause (Section 3) is crucial for ensuring continuity and protection of actions and liabilities incurred under the now-repealed Act.

title: THE KERALA REPEALING AND SAVING ACT, 2022
purpose: To repeal certain enactments which are obsolete or no longer needed.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala and concerns the repeal of specific previously enacted laws that are no longer considered necessary or are outdated. The scope of repeal is defined by the Schedule attached to the Act.

main_sections.description: (1) This Act may be called the Kerala Repealing and Saving Act, 2022. (2) It shall come into force at once.
The enactments specified in the Schedule to this Act are hereby repealed.

This section details what is NOT affected by the repeal of enactments. It clarifies that the repeal does not affect: 
(1) Any other enactment where the repealed enactment has been applied, incorporated, or referred to. 
(2) The validity, invalidity, effect, or consequences of anything already done or suffered. 
(3) Any right, title, obligation, or liability already acquired, accrued, or incurred, or any remedy or proceeding in respect thereof. 
(4) Any release or discharge of any debt, penalty, obligation, liability, claim, or demand, or any indemnity already granted. 
(5) The proof of any past act or thing. 
(6) Any principle or rule of law, or established jurisdiction, form or course of pleading, practice or procedure, or existing usage, custom, privilege, restriction, exemption, office or appointment that may have been affirmed, recognized, or derived from the repealed enactments. 
(7) The repeal will not revive or restore any jurisdiction, office, custom, liability, right, title, privilege, restriction, exemption, usage, practice, procedure, or other matter or thing that is not currently existing or in force. 
(2) The provisions of section 4 of the Kerala Interpretation and General Clauses Act, 1125 (VII of 1125) shall be applicable with respect to the repeal of any enactment under this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Enactments listed in the Schedule to this Act are repealed.
Rule 2: The repeal of any enactment in the Schedule does not affect other laws that have applied, incorporated, or referred to the repealed enactment.
Rule 3: The repeal does not affect any actions taken, rights acquired, or obligations incurred before the repeal.
Rule 4: The repeal does not revive any repealed jurisdiction, office, or custom.
Rule 5: Section 4 of the Kerala Interpretation and General Clauses Act, 1125 (VII of 1125) applies to the repeals made by this Act.
administration: Law (Legislation-D) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act came into force immediately upon enactment.
A comprehensive schedule of repealed enactments is provided, categorised by their origin (Travancore, Cochin, Travancore-Cochin, Malabar, Kerala Acts).

title: THE KERALA REVENUE RECOVERY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2024
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Revenue Recovery Act, 1968.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and pertains to the recovery of revenue and other dues under the Kerala Revenue Recovery Act, 1968.

key_definitions.bought-in-land: Any immovable property purchased on behalf of the Government or an institution under sub-section (2) of section 50 of the principal Act.
key_definitions.collection_charges: Any amount payable by the defaulter to the Government for the realisation of amounts due under the Act, at a rate prescribed by the Government.
key_definitions.e-auction: An auction conducted through online mode.
key_definitions.processing_charge: The amount payable to the Government by an institution notified under section 71 of the Act, in cases of realisation of arrears directly by the requisition authority after the initiation of revenue recovery proceedings, at a rate prescribed by the Government.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Kerala Revenue Recovery (Amendment) Act, 2024, and that it comes into force at once.

Amends section 2 of the principal Act by inserting definitions for 'bought-in-land', 'collection charges', 'e-auction', and 'processing charge', and also modifies an existing clause related to attached property.

Amends section 6 of the principal Act by substituting the interest rate from 'twelve per cent' to 'nine per cent', with a proviso that the interest rate shall not exceed the contractual rate in certain cases.

Amends sub-section (1) of section 12 of the principal Act to include 'e-auction' as a mode of public auction and mandates publication of notice in a newspaper and on the website of the District Administration.

Adds a new sub-section (3) to section 36 of the principal Act, allowing a defaulter to request the Collector to limit attachment to a portion of immovable property if its value exceeds the arrear amount.

Inserts a new sub-section (4) into section 44 of the principal Act, permitting the defaulter to agree for sale of attached immovable property with the Collector's permission, provided revenue recovery dues are paid from sale consideration.
Amends section 49 of the principal Act to include 'e-auction' in public auction and mandates publication of notice in a newspaper and on the website of the District Administration.

Substitutes the marginal heading of section 50 and amends sub-sections to allow bidding on behalf of institutions notified under section 71, modifies the bidding amount, and includes provisions for handling bought-in-land and calculating property value for institutions.

Inserts a new section 50A dealing with the reconveyance of bought-in-land, allowing defaulters (including legal heirs) to apply for reconveyance within 5 years of confirmation of sale upon payment of dues and charges. It also restricts transfer or setting apart of such land by the Government or institution during this period.
Amends the proviso to section 54 of the principal Act to include giving parties concerned a reasonable opportunity of being heard.
Substitutes sub-section (2) of section 57 of the principal Act to mandate registration of the certificate of sale under the Indian Registration Act, 1908.
Amends sub-section (2) of section 69 of the principal Act to include a condition that the debt must not be barred by limitation under the Limitation Act, 1963.
Amends section 74 of the principal Act by omitting the word 'male' from item (a) and allowing service of notice 'by e-mail' in item (b).

Inserts new sections: 83A granting the Government special power to issue stay and allow instalments; 83B empowering the Government to issue moratorium; 83C enabling settlement schemes for bought-in-land; and 83D detailing intimation of settlement schemes.

important_rules: Interest rate on arrears shall not exceed twelve per cent (amended to nine per cent), but shall not exceed the contractual rate if applicable.
Notice of attachment or sale must be published in a newspaper with circulation in the area and on the District Administration's website.
A defaulter can request to limit attachment to a portion of immovable property if its value exceeds the arrear amount.
Defaulters may be permitted to enter into an agreement for sale of attached property with Collector's permission, provided dues are paid from sale consideration.
Reconveyance of bought-in-land is possible within 5 years of sale confirmation upon full payment of dues, charges, and interest.
The Government or institution cannot transfer or set apart bought-in-land for 5 years from confirmation of sale.
The Government has the power to postpone proceedings, allow instalments, or issue moratorium on revenue recovery.
Settlement schemes for recovery of arrears for bought-in-land can be introduced.
Any settlement entered into after initiation of revenue recovery proceedings requires prior intimation to the Collector.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Collector, and other officers as notified by the Government. The Government also has overarching powers regarding stays, instalments, and moratoriums.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through revenue recovery proceedings, attachment and sale of property, e-auctions, and by enforcing payment of dues, interest, collection charges, and processing charges.

rights: Right of the defaulter to request limitation of attachment of property.
Right of the defaulter to apply for reconveyance of bought-in-land within 5 years.
Right of the defaulter to seek stay or instalments from the Government.
Right of the purchaser to make an agreement for sale of attached property with Collector's permission.
Right to be heard before certain decisions are made (amendment to section 54).
duties: Duty of the defaulter to pay revenue recovery dues, interest, collection charges, and processing charges.
Duty to remit revenue recovery dues and other charges before executing a sale deed.
Duty to provide intimation of settlement schemes to the Collector.
obligations: Institutions notified under section 71 have obligations related to bidding and purchase of property.
The Government or institution acquiring bought-in-land has obligations regarding revenue records, intimation to sub-registry, and valuation of property.
Requisition authorities are liable to remit expenses and charges in case of settlement under a scheme.

key_procedures: Procedure for amending definitions in Section 2 of the principal Act.
Procedure for modification of interest rates and adding provisos in Section 6.
Procedure for inclusion of e-auction and newspaper/website publication in auction notices (Sections 4 and 7).
Procedure for defaulting parties to request limitation of attachment (Section 5).
Procedure for a defaulter and purchaser to seek permission for sale agreement from the Collector (Section 6).
Procedure for Government or institution bidding on behalf of Government (Section 8).
Procedure for reconveyance of bought-in-land within 5 years (Section 9).
Procedure for registration of sale certificate under Indian Registration Act (Section 11).
Procedure for Government to exercise special powers of stay, instalments, and moratorium (Sections 83A, 83B).
Procedure for introducing and intimating settlement schemes (Sections 83C, 83D).
administration: The Kerala Revenue Recovery Act, 1968, administered by the Revenue Department of the Government of Kerala. Specific amendments involve the Collector and other notified officers.
important_notes: The Act aims to streamline revenue recovery processes and introduce modern methods like e-auctions.
Specific provisions are made for institutions notified under Section 71, enabling them to participate more actively in recovery proceedings.
The time limit for reconveyance of bought-in-land is strictly set at 5 years.
The amendment emphasizes the need for transparency by mandating publication of notices on websites.
Exceptions are made for certain dues (e.g., compensation under Employee's Compensation Act, gratuity benefits) from the Government's power to grant stays and instalments.

title: THE KERALA RIGHT TO BURIAL OF CORPSE IN CHRISTIAN (MALANKARA ORTHODOX-JACOBITE) CEMETERIES ACT, 2020
purpose: To provide for the burial of corpse and funeral services of Christians belonging to Malankara Orthodox-Jacobite denominations and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to Christians belonging to the Malankara Orthodox-Jacobite denominations within Kerala. It specifically addresses the right to burial in cemeteries designated for these denominations.

key_definitions.cemetery: A place set apart for burial of the corpses of parishioners in a concrete cell or pit made in the ground.
key_definitions.christian: Any person belonging to the Orthodox-Jacobite denominations of Malankara Christian Church who believes in the Bible, accepts Jesus Christ as the only begotten Son of God, and has been baptized.
key_definitions.parish: A group of Christian families having a church or prayer hall for its members to offer worship.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called The Kerala Right to Burial of Corpse in Christian (Malankara Orthodox-Jacobite) Cemeteries Act, 2020, and that it is deemed to have come into force on January 7, 2020.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'cemetery', 'Christian', 'Government', 'parish', and 'prescribed'.

Establishes the right of all members of families belonging to a parish to be buried in the cemetery where their ancestors were buried. It also clarifies that relatives of a deceased member may opt for funeral services at another location or with a priest of their choice.

Specifies penalties for anyone who prevents or attempts to prevent the burial of a corpse in violation of Section 3. Penalties include imprisonment up to one year, a fine up to ten thousand rupees, or both.

main_sections.section_title: Offences shall be cognizable, bailable and compoundable
main_sections.description: Declares that offences under this Act are cognizable, bailable, and can be compounded by the family members of the deceased.

Mandates the Vicar of the parish to maintain a separate register for burials conducted under Section 3. This register is to be a permanent record, and certificates can be issued upon application and payment of prescribed fees.
Empowers the Government to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act by notification in the Gazette. These rules must be laid before the Legislative Assembly for modification or annulment.

Repeals The Kerala Christian Cemeteries (Right to burial of corpse) Ordinance, 2020 (1 of 2020). It also states that anything done or action taken under the repealed Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: All members of families belonging to a parish have the right to be buried in the cemetery where their ancestors were buried.
Relatives of a deceased member of a parish can choose to forego funeral services in the church or its cemetery and opt for services elsewhere or with a priest of their choice.
The Vicar of a parish must maintain a separate register for all burials.
Offences under the Act are cognizable, bailable, and compoundable by the deceased's family members.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year.
Fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees.
Both imprisonment and fine.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Implied to be the authorities responsible for enforcing criminal law in Kerala, likely including the police and the courts, as offenses are cognizable and subject to conviction.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings, including investigation of complaints, prosecution, and sentencing by courts. The Act also specifies that offenses are cognizable, bailable, and compoundable.

rights: Right of all members of families belonging to a parish to be buried in their ancestral cemetery.
Right of relatives of a deceased member to choose funeral services at an alternative location or with a priest of their choice.
Right to obtain certificates regarding burials from the Vicar.
Right to have offences under the Act compounded by family members.
duties: Duty of the Vicar to maintain a separate register for burials.
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act regarding burial and funeral services.
Duty to lay rules before the Legislative Assembly for scrutiny.
obligations: Obligation to avoid preventing burials in violation of Section 3.
Obligation to adhere to prescribed procedures for maintaining registers and issuing certificates.

key_procedures: Burial of a corpse in the ancestral cemetery for members of families belonging to a parish.
Arrangement of funeral services, either in the church/cemetery or at an alternative location.
Maintenance of a burial register by the Vicar.
Issuance of burial certificates upon application and payment of fees.
Making and laying of rules by the Government before the Legislative Assembly.
administration: Law (Legislation-E) Department, Government of Kerala. The Vicar of the parish is responsible for maintaining registers.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on January 7, 2020.
The explanation to Section 3 clarifies that 'member of a family' includes descendants but excludes those who have left the Orthodox-Jacobite faith.
The repeal of the Ordinance includes a saving clause, meaning anything done under the Ordinance is considered valid under the new Act.

title: THE KERALA RIGHT TO PUBLIC SERVICE ACT, 2025
purpose: To provide for the delivery of public services to eligible persons within the stipulated time limit, including to make accountable the public servants in case of default and for matters connected therewith and incidental thereto.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Kerala and governs the delivery of public services by public authorities and public servants to eligible persons.

key_definitions.Commission: The Commission constituted under section 10 of the Act.
key_definitions.days: Working days of the public authority concerned.
key_definitions.designated officer: An officer designated as per section 4 of the Act.
key_definitions.electronic mode: Any method, process or application to deliver any service electronically, including but not limited to Government to Government, Government to citizen or Government to business transactions, data interchange and other digital supply transactions whether conducted through e-mail, mobile services, cloud computing, document management, voice or data transmission or otherwise.
key_definitions.eligible person: A person who is eligible to obtain services notified under this Act and includes a person duly authorized in writing by such eligible person.
key_definitions.first appellate authority: An officer notified as per section 4 of the Act.
key_definitions.public authority: An authority or body or Local Self Government Institution established or constituted by or under the Constitution, by any other law made by Parliament or State Legislature, or by notification issued or order made by the Government. It also includes bodies owned, controlled or substantially financed by the Government, or other bodies required to render public service as notified by the Government.
key_definitions.public service: Public services rendered by the Government, electronically or otherwise, and includes services notified by the department concerned as per section 4 of this Act.
key_definitions.second appellate authority: An officer not below the rank of a Joint Secretary notified by the Administrative Department concerned for the purposes of section 8 of the Act.
key_definitions.stipulated time limit: The time limit specified under section 4 of this Act for rendering service by the designated officer.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Right to Public Service Act, 2025, and it shall come into force at once.

This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as 'Commission', 'days', 'designated officer', 'electronic mode', 'eligible person', 'first appellate authority', 'public authority', 'public service', 'second appellate authority', and 'stipulated time limit'.
This section establishes the right of every eligible person to obtain notified public services within the stipulated time limit, subject to the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power to notify public services, special public services, stipulated time limit, designated officers etc.
main_sections.description: This section empowers the head of a department to notify public services, special public services, stipulated time limits, designated officers, and first appellate authorities. It also allows the Government to designate different officers for different services at various levels.

main_sections.section_title: Rendering of public service within stipulated time limit.
main_sections.description: This section outlines the process for rendering public services, including the commencement of the stipulated time limit, maintenance of applications, acknowledgement of applications, and the procedure for rendering or rejecting services with reasons in case of rejection.

This section mandates public authorities to deliver all public services through electronic mode, subject to feasibility, within the notified time limit, with exceptions for services that cannot be delivered electronically or are declared exempt by the Government. It also requires the publication and annual review of schedules for electronic service delivery.

This section provides for the right of any person whose application has been rejected, who has not received a service within the stipulated time limit, or who has received a deficient service, to prefer an appeal to the first appellate authority within thirty days. The first appellate authority may condone delays if sufficient cause is shown.

This section details the recovery of penalties imposed under the Act from the salary, pension, or assets of the designated or other officer. It also allows the appellate authority or commission to grant compensation from recovered penalties to the eligible person.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: This section protects any government officer or employee from any suit, prosecution, or other legal proceeding for anything done or intended to be done in good faith in pursuance of the provisions of this Act, without prior sanction of the Government.

This section states that the provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any other law for the time being in force or in any decree, order or decision of any court or other authority.

main_sections.section_title: Exclusion of jurisdiction of civil courts
main_sections.description: This section excludes the jurisdiction of civil courts to entertain any suit or proceeding in respect of any action taken or order passed by the Government or any authority or officer in pursuance of the powers conferred by this Act.

This section empowers the Government to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act by an order, provided such order is not made after the expiry of two years from the commencement of the Act. Such orders are to be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

This section empowers the Government to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act, with or without retrospective effect. Such rules are to be laid before the Legislative Assembly and are subject to modification or annulment by the Assembly.

This section repeals the Kerala State Service Delivery Act, 2012 (18 of 2012). It also provides that anything done or any action taken or any proceeding commenced under the repealed Act shall be deemed to have been done, taken or commenced under this Act, unless inconsistent with its provisions.

penalties: Imposition of penalties on designated officers or other officers for failure to render public service or for contravening provisions of the Act, as per service rules.
Recovery of penalties from salary, pension, or other assets.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Designated officers, first appellate authority, second appellate authority, and the Commission.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the process of receiving applications, rendering services, appeals, and penalties as laid out in the Act.

rights: Right of every eligible person to obtain notified public services within the stipulated time limit.
Right to appeal to the first appellate authority if service is rejected, delayed, or deficient.
Right to seek further appeal to the second appellate authority.
duties: Duty of heads of departments to notify public services, time limits, designated officers, and appellate authorities.
Duty of designated officers to render public service within the stipulated time limit or reject applications with reasons.
Duty of public authorities to deliver services electronically where feasible.
Duty of the Government to frame rules and notify standards.
obligations: Obligation of public authorities to make public services accessible.
Obligation of public servants to act in good faith and within the scope of the Act.
Obligation to comply with orders of appellate authorities and the Commission.

key_procedures: Application for public service -> Receipt and acknowledgement by designated officer -> Rendering of service or rejection with reasons within the stipulated time limit.
If service rejected, delayed, or deficient: Filing of first appeal to the first appellate authority within 30 days. Hearing and decision by the first appellate authority.
If dissatisfied with the first appellate authority's decision: Filing of second appeal to the second appellate authority.
Further appeal to the Commission if dissatisfied with the second appellate authority's decision.
administration: Government of Kerala, Law (Legislation-B) Department (for notification and publication). The Act's implementation involves various departments and public authorities within the Kerala Government.
important_notes: The Act can be amended or repealed by the Legislative Assembly.
Rules made under the Act are subject to scrutiny by the Legislative Assembly.
The Government has the power to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act, but not after two years of its commencement.

title: THE KERALA SHOPS AND COMMERCIAL ESTABLISHMENTS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2021
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1960, for the purposes hereinafter appearing, specifically by introducing provisions related to automation systems and defining new roles.
scope: This act amends the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1960. It applies to shops and commercial establishments within the state of Kerala. The amendments primarily concern the procedures for registration, renewal, and administrative roles within the framework of the principal Act.

key_definitions.Labour Administrator: An officer of the Labour department of the State who is notified as an Inspector under this Act.
key_definitions.Labour Commissionerate Automation System: A software owned and operated by the Labour department to provide end-to-end solutions for employers, employees, and Labour Administrators.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act as the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments (Amendment) Act, 2021, and states that it shall be deemed to have come into force on November 9, 2020.
Inserts new clauses (9A) and (9B) into Section 2 of the principal Act, defining 'Labour Administrator' and 'Labour Commissionerate Automation System'.
Amends Section 5A of the principal Act by incorporating the 'Labour Commissionerate Automation System' into the application process for registration and renewal, and also omits sub-section (7).

Repeals the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021 (123 of 2021) and provides a saving clause, ensuring that actions taken under the Ordinance are deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Applications for registration and renewal must be made through the Labour Commissionerate Automation System.
Applications for renewal of registration certificates must be made at least thirty days before the expiry of the current period.

Registration certificates shall be renewed automatically upon payment of prescribed fees through the Labour Commissionerate Automation System, provided the renewal application is submitted within the stipulated time.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Labour department and notified Labour Administrators (Inspectors).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is through the administrative procedures established by the principal Act and its amendments, including the use of the Labour Commissionerate Automation System for applications and renewals.

rights: Right to have registration certificates renewed automatically under specified conditions.
Right to access services through the Labour Commissionerate Automation System for employers, employees, and Labour Administrators.
duties: Duty to make applications for registration and renewal through the Labour Commissionerate Automation System.
Duty to apply for renewal at least thirty days before the expiry of the registration certificate.
obligations: Obligation to pay prescribed fees for renewal of registration.
Obligation for the Labour department to operate and maintain the Labour Commissionerate Automation System.

key_procedures: Procedure for making an application for registration: Application to be made through the Labour Commissionerate Automation System.
Procedure for renewal of registration: Application to be made at least thirty days before expiry, payment of fees, and automatic renewal through the Labour Commissionerate Automation System.
administration: Labour department of the State Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force retrospectively from November 9, 2020.
Sub-section (7) of Section 5A of the principal Act has been omitted.

title: THE KERALA SHOPS AND COMMERCIAL ESTABLISHMENTS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2018
purpose: To amend the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1960, to provide for certain changes related to shops and commercial establishments in Kerala.
scope: Applies to shops and commercial establishments in Kerala.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title as the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments (Amendment) Act, 2018, and states that it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 10th day of August, 1940. However, it also clarifies that the provisions of the amending act will have effect from the date of publication in the Gazette, as applicable.

This section details the amendments made to the principal Act (Act 19 of 1960). It specifically amends Section 2 of the principal Act, relating to definitions. The amendment includes the deletion of sub-clause (i) of clause (6) and the insertion of a new sub-clause (i). It also amends sub-clause (ii) of clause (6) and clause (11).

This section is titled 'Validation'. It states that notwithstanding anything contained in any judgment, decree, or order of any court, all actions taken or things done or purporting to have been taken or done under the principal Act or any notification or order issued thereunder shall be deemed to have been validly taken or done.

important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force retrospectively from August 10, 1940.
The amendments are intended to validate actions taken under the principal Act, even if they were subject to legal challenges.
The validation clause ensures that past actions are considered lawful, preventing future disputes based on previous interpretations.

title: The Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Workers' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2021
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 2006, to address matters that have arisen since its enactment.
scope: This Act applies to the state of Kerala and specifically amends the 'Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 2006'. It concerns workers in shops and commercial establishments within Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Workers' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2021, and that it is deemed to have come into force on February 24, 2021.
Amends sub-section (6) of section 4 of the principal Act (Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 2006) by substituting '(1) and (2)' with '(1), (2) and (3)'.

Repeals the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Workers' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021 (121 of 2021). It also provides that anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The act itself does not specify enforcement authorities or penalties, as it is an amendment act. Enforcement would be governed by the principal Act (The Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 2006) and its subsequent rules.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: As an amendment, the enforcement mechanisms are those established by the principal Act.

administration: The Law (Legislation-C) Department of the Government of Kerala is responsible for the notification and publication of the Act. The administration of the principal Act would be under the relevant department overseeing labour welfare in Kerala.
important_notes: The Act is a further amendment to the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 2006.
The amendment is deemed to have come into force retrospectively from February 24, 2021.
The amendment specifically modifies Section 4 of the principal Act, implying changes related to the functioning or provisions governed by that section.
The repeal of the Ordinance and the saving clause ensure continuity and validity of actions taken under the Ordinance.

title: THE KERALA SINGLE DWELLING PLACE PROTECTION ACT, 2025
purpose: To provide for preventing families from losing their single dwelling place through eviction due to non-repayment of loans raised from financial institutions by mortgaging such dwelling places, and for taking measures including protection of such dwelling places.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Kerala and concerns the protection of single dwelling places mortgaged to financial institutions functioning within the State for loans raised by debtors.

key_definitions.appeal: An appeal to be filed under section 21 of the Act.
key_definitions.debtor: A person or persons who raised a loan by mortgaging a single dwelling place belonging to himself or a surety from a financial institution functioning in the State.
key_definitions.District Level Dwelling Place Protection: The committee to be constituted under section 6 of the Act.
key_definitions.family: The wife or husband, children, father or mother of the debtor.
key_definitions.financial institution: A bank functioning in the State and included in the Second Schedule to the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, or a non-banking financial company as defined in the said Act, or a society registered under the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969, and includes other institutions notified by the Government.
key_definitions.fund: A fund to be constituted under section 25 of the Act.
key_definitions.gazette: The official gazette of the State.
key_definitions.notification: A notification published in the gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.State Level Dwelling Place Protection Co: The committee to be constituted under section 13 of the Act.

main_sections.description: (1) This Act may be called the Kerala Single Dwelling Place Protection Act, 2025. (2) It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification, appoint.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'appeal', 'debtor', 'District Level Dwelling Place Protection Committee', 'family', 'financial institution', 'fund', 'gazette', 'Government', 'notification', 'prescribed', 'State', and 'State Level Dwelling Place Protection Committee'.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration as to giving effect to the directive principle
main_sections.description: Declares that the Act is for giving effect to the directive principle laid down in clause (b) of article 39 of the Constitution of India concerning securing the welfare of the people.

Provides that families who lose their dwelling place due to attachment or recovery proceedings initiated by financial institutions for non-repayment of mortgaged loans are eligible for protection under the Act.

Outlines the criteria for eligibility for protection, including loan and repayment limits, absence of other properties or repayment means, land extent, annual income, non-transfer of properties after loan date, Aadhaar holder status, and specified loan purposes (education, treatment, marriage, house building/renovation, agriculture, livelihood creation).

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of the District Level Dwelling Place Protection Committee
main_sections.description: States that the Government shall, by notification, constitute a District Level Dwelling Place Protection Committee in each district.

main_sections.section_title: Composition of the District Level Dwelling Place Protection Committee
main_sections.description: Specifies the members of the District Level Dwelling Place Protection Committee, including the District Development Commissioner (Chairperson), Principal Agriculture Officer, Deputy Director of Panchayat, a representative of the District Disaster Management Authority, Deputy Collector (Disaster Management) (Member Secretary), representatives from co-operative and banking sectors, and the Lead District Manager. It also allows for the constitution of sub-committees.
Requires any person seeking benefits under the Act to submit a prescribed application with allied documents to the District Level Dwelling Place Protection Committee.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of the District Level Dwelling Place Protection Committee
main_sections.description: Details the powers and functions of the committee, including conducting preliminary inquiries, conciliation measures, rearranging repayment terms, submitting recommendations to the State Level Committee for Government taking over repayment liability, conducting inquiries, and submitting detailed reports with asset valuation, Tahasildar certificates, recommendations on repayment advantage, reports on alternative dwelling places, assessment of repayment obstacles, probability of subjecting remaining properties to proceedings, and other required documents. It also specifies a time limit for action on applications.

main_sections.section_title: The headquarters of the District Level Dwelling Place Protection Committee
main_sections.description: States that the headquarters of the District Level Dwelling Place Protection Committee shall be at the District Collectorate.

main_sections.section_title: Protection for acts done in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection from any legal proceedings or prosecution to the Government, its officers, or members/officers/employees of the Dwelling Place Protection Committees for any act done or intended to be done in good faith in pursuance of the Act or rules made thereunder.

(1) If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of the Act, the Government may, by general or special order published in the Gazette, make provisions not inconsistent with the Act for removing the difficulty. (2) Such orders must be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

(1) The Government may, by notification, make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of the Act, with retrospective or prospective effect. (2) Such rules must be laid before the Legislative Assembly for a period of fourteen days and are subject to modifications or annulment by the Assembly.

important_rules: Eligibility for protection is subject to specific criteria including loan amounts, repayment limits, debtor's financial status, land extent, annual income, and the purpose of the loan.
The Government has the power to amend eligibility criteria by notification.
A family can only receive Government support for repayment liability once.
The District Level Dwelling Place Protection Committee has powers of inquiry and conciliation to resolve repayment issues.
If conciliation fails or repayment is impossible, the District Level Committee recommends to the State Level Committee for Government intervention.
Rules made under the Act must be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: District Level Dwelling Place Protection Committee, State Level Dwelling Place Protection Committee, Government of Kerala.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inquiries, conciliation, recommendations for government intervention, and by making rules and issuing notifications.

rights: Right of eligible families to protection of their single dwelling place.
Right to apply for benefits under the Act.
duties: Duty of the Government to constitute protection committees and make rules.
Duty of the District Level Dwelling Place Protection Committee to conduct inquiries and make recommendations.
Duty to lay rules and orders before the Legislative Assembly.
obligations: Debtors have an obligation to repay loans.
Financial institutions are subject to the provisions of the Act regarding recovery proceedings.

key_procedures: Application Submission: Eligible persons submit a prescribed application with documents to the District Level Dwelling Place Protection Committee.
Inquiry and Conciliation: The District Level Committee conducts preliminary inquiry and conciliation measures to resolve repayment issues.

Recommendation to State Level Committee: If conciliation fails or repayment is impossible, the District Level Committee submits recommendations to the State Level Committee, including potential Government takeover of repayment.
Government Intervention: Based on recommendations, the Government may take over repayment liability.
Rule Making and Laying: The Government makes rules, and these rules (along with orders for removing difficulties) are laid before the Legislative Assembly.
administration: Law (Legislation-I) Department, Government of Kerala, and the District Level and State Level Dwelling Place Protection Committees.
important_notes: The Act aims to protect families from losing their only home due to loan defaults.
Loans raised for specific purposes (education, treatment, etc.) are prioritized for protection.
Protection is not available if the debtor or family has other means of repayment or owns substantial other properties.
The Act also provides for protection of actions taken in good faith by government officials and committee members.

title: The Kerala Small Plantation Workers’ Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2021
purpose: To amend the Kerala Small Plantation Workers’ Welfare Fund Act, 2008, for the purposes hereinafter appearing, specifically to increase certain contribution amounts.
scope: This act applies to the State of Kerala and specifically amends the provisions related to contributions under the Kerala Small Plantation Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 2008.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act as the Kerala Small Plantation Workers’ Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2021, and states that it shall be deemed to have come into force on July 30, 2020.
Amends Section 5 of the principal Act (Kerala Small Plantation Workers’ Welfare Fund Act, 2008) by substituting increased monetary values for contributions in sub-sections (1), (2), and (3).

Repeals the Kerala Small Plantation Workers’ Welfare Fund (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021 (130 of 2021). It also provides a saving clause, ensuring that anything done or deemed to have been done under the repealed Ordinance shall be considered as done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Increase the contribution amount in sub-section (1) of Section 5 from 'one hundred and twenty rupees' to 'one hundred and eighty rupees'.
Rule 2: Increase the contribution amount in sub-section (2) of Section 5 from 'one hundred and twenty rupees' to 'one hundred and eighty rupees'.
Rule 3: Increase the contribution amount in sub-section (3) of Section 5 from 'two hundred and forty rupees' to 'three hundred and sixty rupees'.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but implied to be the authority administering the principal Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not explicitly detailed in the provided text.

administration: The Act is administered by the Government of Kerala, likely through its Law Department and the department responsible for implementing the Kerala Small Plantation Workers' Welfare Fund.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force retrospectively from July 30, 2020.
The Kerala Small Plantation Workers’ Welfare Fund (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021, which was previously in effect, has been repealed.

title: THE KERALA SOCIETIES REGISTRATION ACT, 2025
purpose: To co-ordinate the laws relating to the registration of artistic, literary, scientific, education, charitable and sports societies and to register societies for the promotion of artistic, literary, scientific, education, charitable and sports activities, the dissemination of useful knowledge and for the promotion of natural resources and infrastructure in the State of Kerala and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to societies registered or deemed to be registered under this Act in the State of Kerala. It covers societies for the promotion of charity, education, culture, science, literature, arts, sports, commerce and industry, dissemination of useful knowledge, and promotion and conservation of natural resources and infrastructure.

key_definitions.administrator: Administrator appointed as per section 39 of the Act.
key_definitions.day: A working day of the competent authority concerned.
key_definitions.governing body: The committee or the administrators, directors or any other body entrusted with the management of the society under its rules and regulations.
key_definitions.inspector general of registration: An officer appointed as per section 3 of the Registration Act, 1908 (Central Act 16 of 1908).
key_definitions.inspector of society: An officer appointed by the Government to perform the duties of an Inspector of societies. If no such officer is appointed, the Registrar shall be the Inspector of society.
key_definitions.member: A person admitted to the membership of a society according to its rules, regulations, and bye-laws, who has signed the roll for subscription payment and has not resigned or been removed. Members with subscriptions in arrears for over three months are not entitled to vote and are not considered members.
key_definitions.memorandum of association: Memorandum of association of the societies as per section 6 of this Act.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.registrar: An officer appointed by the Government to perform the duties of a Registrar under this Act. If no such officer is appointed, the Inspector General of Registration shall perform the duties of the Registrar.
key_definitions.society: A society registered or deemed to be registered under this Act.
key_definitions.year: The year beginning on January 1st and ending on December 31st, or another date with the Registrar's permission for specific societies.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Kerala Societies Registration Act, 2025, and specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Government through a Gazette notification.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including administrator, day, governing body, Government, Inspector General of Registration, Inspector of society, member, memorandum of association, prescribed, Registrar, society, and year.

main_sections.section_title: Societies to which the Act applies.
main_sections.description: Specifies the types of societies that can be registered under the Act, including those for charity, education, culture, science, literature, arts, sports, commerce, industry, dissemination of useful knowledge, and promotion/conservation of natural resources and infrastructure, provided they do not distribute profits among members.
States that a society must have at least seven members who are Indian citizens and have completed the age of eighteen years for registration.
Outlines that members associating for purposes specified in section 3 can form a society by including their names in the memorandum of association and undertaking the registration process.

Details the particulars required in the memorandum of association (name, objects, area of operation, governing body details, registered office location) and states that rules and regulations (covering membership, meetings, governing body proceedings) must be registered along with it. It also specifies formatting and signatory requirements for the memorandum and rules.

Details the powers and duties of an administrator appointed to manage a society, including conducting elections, and the government's authority to extend the administrator's term or dissolve the society under certain circumstances. It also mentions the formation of an advisory committee.

Defines offences related to non-compliance with the Act's provisions, including contravening Section 15, making false declarations, or failing to comply with lawful orders or provide required information. Penalties include a fine up to one thousand rupees, without prejudice to other legal penalties.

main_sections.section_title: Trial of offences under this Act.
main_sections.description: Specifies that offences under this Act can only be tried upon a report from the Registrar, with his written permission, or with the permission of an officer subordinate to him authorized by the Registrar. It also grants the Registrar the power to compound offences upon payment of a compounding fee.

main_sections.section_title: Trial of offences under this Act.
main_sections.description: States that offences under this Act shall be tried by a Judicial First Class Magistrate Court.
Empowers the Government to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act, which must be laid before the Legislative Assembly for approval or amendment.

Grants the Government the power to issue orders to remove any difficulties in enforcing the Act, provided such orders are not inconsistent with the Act and are issued within two years of the Act's commencement. These orders must also be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

Repeals the Societies Registration Act, 1860 (Central Act 21 of 1860) in the Malabar district and the Travancore-Cochin Literary, Scientific and Charitable Societies Registration Act, 1955 (Act 12 of 1955). It also includes savings provisions for actions taken under the repealed Acts.

important_rules: Rule: Memorandum of association must include name, objects, area of operation, details of the governing body, and registered office location of the society.
Rule: Rules and regulations covering membership, general meetings, voting, and governing body proceedings must be registered along with the memorandum of association.

Rule: Members of the memorandum must include their address, description, government-approved identity card number, age, and occupation, and sign in the presence of a witness who also attests the signature and provides their details.
Rule: Societies must have at least seven members who are Indian citizens and have completed 18 years of age.
Rule: No person with subscription arrears exceeding three months is considered a member or is entitled to vote.

penalties: Fine up to one thousand rupees for offences like contravening Section 15, making false declarations, or failing to comply with lawful orders or provide information.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Registrar, Inspector of Society, and Judicial First Class Magistrate Court for trial of offences.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Offences are tried by a Judicial First Class Magistrate Court. Offences can be compounded by the Registrar upon payment of a fee. Actions taken under the Act are subject to rules made by the Government and laid before the Legislative Assembly.

rights: Right to form a society for specific purposes.
Right to vote in society proceedings (for eligible members).
duties: Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder.
Duty to provide required information.
Duty to pay subscription dues to remain a member in good standing.
obligations: Obligation to register the society and its memorandum of association and rules.
Obligation for members to sign the memorandum of association.
Obligation for the society to maintain its registered office and records.

key_procedures: Procedure: Formation and Registration of a Society: Members associate for a purpose specified in section 3, form a society with a memorandum of association, and register it according to the Act's provisions and rules.

Procedure: Registration of Memorandum and Rules: The memorandum of association must contain specific particulars. Rules and regulations regarding membership, meetings, and the governing body must be registered along with it. Both documents need to be printed/typed, divided into paragraphs, numbered, and signed by members and witnesses.
Procedure: Handling Offences: Offences are tried by a Judicial First Class Magistrate Court. The Registrar can compound offences upon payment of a fee.
Procedure: Making Rules: The Government can make rules to carry out the Act's provisions, which are then laid before the Legislative Assembly.
Procedure: Removing Difficulties: The Government can issue orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act, subject to conditions and legislative scrutiny.
administration: Government of Kerala (Law (Legislation-A) Department)
important_notes: Note: The Act repeals the Societies Registration Act, 1860 (Central Act 21 of 1860) in the Malabar district and the Travancore-Cochin Literary, Scientific and Charitable Societies Registration Act, 1955 (Act 12 of 1955).
Note: Actions taken under the repealed Acts are deemed valid.
Note: Any difficulties in enforcing the Act can be removed by government orders, but not later than two years from the commencement of the Act.
Note: Rules made by the Government and orders issued to remove difficulties must be laid before the Kerala Legislative Assembly.

title: THE KERALA SPORTS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2018
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Sports Act, 2000.
scope: The Act applies to sports in Kerala, amending the existing Kerala Sports Act, 2000.

key_definitions.Standing Committee: means the Standing Committee of the State Sports Council.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Sports (Amendment) Act, 2018 and it shall come into force on the 20th day of August, 2018.
Amends Section 2 of the principal Act by omitting certain clauses and substituting a new clause defining 'Standing Committee'.

Amends Section 3 of the principal Act concerning the composition of the State Sports Council, including provisions for elected members from District Sports Councils, Universities, Legislative Assembly, Municipal Corporations, Panchayats, and nominated members.
Amends Section 4 of the principal Act by substituting certain words and phrases related to the Executive Committee and the role of members.
Amends Section 5 of the principal Act by omitting certain words and symbols.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 6
main_sections.description: Substitutes a new section 6 which details the composition of the Standing Committee of the State Sports Council, including its members and their election/nomination processes, and outlines the functions and meeting requirements of the Standing Committee.

Amends Section 9 of the principal Act, concerning 'Ex-officio Members', by inserting new clauses for District Medical Officers and provisions for elected members from various levels of Panchayats, with specific mention of representation for women and Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes.
Amends Section 10 of the principal Act by omitting certain words.
Amends Section 11 of the principal Act by substituting provisions for the Executive Committee of the District Sports Council, detailing its composition and the roles of its members.
Amends Section 12 of the principal Act by substituting the word 'Chairman' with 'President'.
Amends Section 13 of the principal Act by substituting certain words related to the powers and duties of the Chairman.

important_rules: No person shall hold office of President or Vice-President of the State Sports Council for a total period exceeding ten years.
The quorum for meeting of the Standing Committee shall be one-third of its total membership including an ex-officio member.
The Standing Committee shall supervise the general functioning of the State Sports Council.
key_procedures: Election of members to the Standing Committee of the State Sports Council from members of the Sports Sports Council.
Election of members from District Sports Councils, Universities, Legislative Assembly, Municipal Corporations, and Panchayats to the State Sports Council.
Meeting procedures for the Standing Committee, including quorum and scheduling.
administration: Law (Legislation-D) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act further amends the Kerala Sports Act, 2000.
Specific clauses and subsections of the principal Act are omitted or substituted.
There are provisions for representation of women and Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes in elected bodies.
A member of the State Sports Council shall not cease to be a member solely on the ground that he has ceased to be the captain of a university team within one year of his election.

title: THE KERALA STATE ELDERLY COMMISSION ACT, 2025
purpose: To constitute an Elderly Commission for giving guidelines in matters related to the welfare and protection of the elderly, to enable their rehabilitation, to undertake and carry out schemes and activities necessary for making use of their skills and experience for the general public, and to ensure the protection of rights and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala and concerns the welfare, protection, and rehabilitation of elderly persons, defined as individuals who have completed sixty years of age.

key_definitions.Care Centre: Government old age homes or old age homes recognized by the Orphanage Control Board for protecting the elderly.
key_definitions.Commission: The Kerala State Elderly Commission constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.Elderly: A person who has completed sixty years of age.
key_definitions.Notification: A notification published in the Gazette.
key_definitions.Old Age Home: Any institution where elders are accommodated or protected.
key_definitions.Prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act as the Kerala State Elderly Commission Act, 2025, and states that it shall be deemed to have come into force on December 21, 2024.

This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Care Centre', 'Chairperson', 'Commission', 'Elderly', 'Government', 'Member', 'Notification', 'Old Age Home', and 'Prescribed'.

This section details the constitution of the Kerala State Elderly Commission, including its establishment by the Government, composition (Chairperson and up to four members), appointment of the Chairperson and members (who must be elderly with relevant experience, including representation from Scheduled Castes/Tribes and women), appointment of a Secretary, Registrar, and Finance Officer, and its headquarters in Thiruvananthapuram.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office and conditions of service of Chairperson and members
main_sections.description: This section outlines the term of office (three years), resignation, filling of casual vacancies, grounds for removal from office (insolvency, conviction, unsound mind, absence from meetings, abuse of position, abstaining from functions, incapacity), prohibition of other employment for the Chairperson, eligibility for re-appointment (maximum two terms), superintendence and administration vested in the Chairperson, and conditions of service including salary and allowances.

main_sections.section_title: Officers and Staff of the Commission
main_sections.description: This section states that the Government shall appoint officers and staff to the Commission for its functions, and their appointment method, salaries, and service conditions will be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Salaries, allowances and the administrative expenses to be allotted from grants
main_sections.description: This section specifies that salaries, allowances, honorarium, sitting fees for members, and administrative expenses for officers and staff will be drawn from the grants referred to in sub-section (1) of section 12.

main_sections.section_title: Vacancies etc. not to invalidate the proceedings of the Commission
