main_sections.description: This section clarifies that any vacancy in the Commission or defect in its constitution will not invalidate its acts or proceedings.

This section details the conduct of meetings of the Commission, including timing and place as determined by the Chairperson, authentication of orders and decisions, and the provision for inviting special invitees with knowledge in the subject matter but without voting rights.

This section elaborates on the functions of the Commission, including issuing guidelines for the welfare and protection of the elderly, providing assistance and rehabilitation, undertaking schemes for utilizing their skills for public benefit, conducting inspections and inquiries, coordinating government departments, advising the government on welfare schemes, investigating complaints of denial or violation of rights, conducting inquiries in detention facilities, preparing and publishing status statements of the elderly, and advising on other referred matters.

This section outlines the powers of the Commission to utilize the services of government officers and officers of government-owned corporations or local authorities for carrying out its functions. It also states that the Commission shall have all the powers of a civil court in matters it deals with.

important_rules: The Act, and any rules made thereunder, must be laid before the State Legislature.
The Chairperson and members of the Commission shall be elderly individuals with experience in elderly welfare.
The Chairperson shall be a full-time officer with the rank of Secretary to Government.
The Chairperson shall not engage in any other paid employment or work.
The Commission's acts or proceedings are not invalid due to vacancies or defects in its constitution.
Special invitees to Commission meetings can participate but do not have voting rights.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Kerala State Elderly Commission and potentially other relevant authorities as indicated by the Commission's recommendations.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, inquiries, recommendations for remedial measures, coordination of government departments, and bringing violations to the notice of concerned authorities. The Act also grants the Commission powers of a civil court.

rights: Right to welfare and protection for the elderly.
Right to rehabilitation for the elderly.
Right to have their skills and experience utilized for the general public.
Protection of rights of the elderly.
Right to legal aid when needed.
Elderly persons detained in prisons or lock-ups have a right to inquiry into their conditions.
duties: Duty of the Government to constitute the Commission.
Duty of the Commission to provide guidelines, assistance, and rehabilitation for the elderly.
Duty of the Commission to undertake schemes for utilizing the skills and experience of the elderly.
Duty of the Commission to coordinate government efforts for elderly welfare.
Duty of the Commission to investigate complaints and report to authorities.
Duty of the Commission to prepare and publish status statements of the elderly.
obligations: Obligations of the Government to appoint officers and staff to the Commission.
Obligations related to the prescribed manner of appointment, salaries, and conditions of service for Commission staff.
Obligations for ensuring the welfare and protection of the elderly as per the Constitution and other laws.

key_procedures: Constitution of the Commission by Government notification.
Appointment of Chairperson and members with specific qualifications and representation.
Appointment of Secretary, Registrar, and Finance Officer.
Conduct of meetings as per prescribed procedures.
Commission's process for handling complaints: preliminary inquiry, report preparation, notification to authorities, and recommendation for action, including providing legal aid.
Commission's process for inquiries in detention facilities and submission of reports.
Laying of rules before the State Legislature.
administration: The Law (Legislation-H) Department of the Government of Kerala is involved in the notification process. The day-to-day administration of the Commission is vested in the Chairperson.
important_notes: The Act retroactively came into force on December 21, 2024.
The Act repeals the Kerala State Elderly Commission Ordinance, 2024 (3 of 2024), and validates actions taken under it.
The Chairperson is a full-time officer with the rank of Secretary to Government.
Members of the Commission shall be elderly and have experience in elderly welfare, with specific representation requirements.
The Commission's headquarters are in Thiruvananthapuram.

title: THE KERALA GENERAL SALES TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2021
purpose: Further to amend the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963 for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and pertains to amendments to the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.

key_definitions.principal Act: The Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963 (15 of 1963).

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 2021 and states that it is deemed to have come into force on the 16th day of May, 2020.
Amends the SCHEDULE of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963 by substituting specific entries under the heading 'Foreign Liquor' in serial number 2.

Repeals the Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021 (105 of 2021) and provides that anything done or deemed to have been done under the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Rule: The Act is deemed to have come into force on 16th May, 2020.
Rule: Specific serial numbers and entries related to 'Foreign Liquor' in the SCHEDULE of the principal Act are substituted.
Rule: Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are saved and deemed to be taken under the amended Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but implied to be the authorities under the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text.

key_procedures: Procedure: Substitution of entries in the SCHEDULE of the principal Act.
administration: Law (Legislation-A) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: Note: This amendment is retrospective, with effect from 16th May, 2020.
Note: The amendment specifically targets entries under 'Foreign Liquor' in the Schedule.

title: THE KERALA STATE GOODS AND SERVICES TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2024
purpose: To further amend the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, primarily to incorporate provisions related to online gaming, online money gaming, and specified actionable claims.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and is an amendment to the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017. It affects persons engaged in the supply of specified actionable claims, including those related to online money gaming, and persons supplying online money gaming from outside India to India.

key_definitions.online_gaming: Offering of a game on the internet or an electronic network, including online money gaming.
key_definitions.online_money_gaming: Online gaming where players pay or deposit money or money's worth (including virtual digital assets) in expectation of winning money or money's worth, regardless of skill or chance.
key_definitions.specified_actionable_claim: Actionable claims involved in or by way of betting, casinos, gambling, horse racing, lottery, or online money gaming.
key_definitions.virtual_digital_asset: Has the same meaning as assigned in clause (47A) of section 2 of the Income-tax Act, 1961.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax (Amendment) Act, 2024 and states that it is deemed to have come into force on October 1, 2023.

Inserts new definitions for 'online gaming', 'online money gaming', 'specified actionable claim', and 'virtual digital asset'. It also clarifies that a person organizing or managing the supply of specified actionable claims is deemed to be a supplier.
Amends section 24 of the principal Act to include every person supplying online money gaming from outside India to a person in India for mandatory registration.
Substitutes 'specified actionable claims' for 'lottery, betting and gambling' in paragraph 6 of Schedule III.
States that the amendments are without prejudice to other laws prohibiting, restricting, or regulating betting, casino, gambling, horse racing, lottery, or online gaming.
Repeals the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2023 (1 of 2024) and provides for continuity of actions taken under the Ordinance.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly detailed in the provided text, but implied to be the authorities under the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, as amended.

duties: Persons organizing or managing the supply of specified actionable claims are deemed suppliers and are liable to pay tax.
Every person supplying online money gaming from outside India to a person in India is required to register.

administration: Law (Legislation-A) Department, Government of Kerala, and by extension, the GST administration in Kerala.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on October 1, 2023.
The amendments are without prejudice to other laws regulating betting, casino, gambling, horse racing, lottery, or online gaming.
The repeal of the Ordinance does not affect actions taken under it.

title: THE KERALA STATE GOODS AND SERVICES TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2018
purpose: An Act to amend the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017. To expedite the amendment of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 (20 of 2017) for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.

key_definitions.services: For the removal of doubts, it is hereby clarified that the expression "services" includes facilitating or arranging transactions in securities.

main_sections.description: Provides that the Act may be called the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax (Amendment) Act, 2018. The provisions of this Act shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint. Different dates may be appointed for different provisions and any reference in any such provision to the commencement of this Act shall be construed as a reference to the coming into force of that provision.

Amends section 2 of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act). Specifically amends sub-clause (4) regarding the Appellate Authority and Appellate Tribunal, and sub-clause (16) regarding the Central Board of Excise and Customs.

Amends section 7 of the principal Act, with effect from the 1st day of July, 2017. It modifies sub-section (1) by adding 'and' after 'business' and 'a consideration', and omitting certain clauses. It also inserts a new sub-section (1A) and amends sub-section (3).

Substitutes sub-section (4) of section 9 of the principal Act. The substituted sub-section states that the Government may, on the recommendations of the Council, specify a class of registered persons who shall, in respect of supply of specified categories of goods or services or both received from an unregistered supplier, pay the tax on reverse charge basis as the recipient of such supply. All the provisions of this Act shall apply to such recipient as if he is the person liable for paying the tax in relation to such supply of goods or services or both.
Amends section 10 of the principal Act. Amends sub-section (1) concerning the tax payable and the proivso. Inserts a new proviso after the existing proviso.
Amends section 12 of the principal Act by omitting the words, brackets and figure "sub-section (1)" in clause (a), sub-section (2).
Amends section 13 of the principal Act by omitting the words, brackets and figure "sub-section (2)" occurring at both the places.
Amends section 16 of the principal Act by substituting the Explanation in sub-section (2), clause (b).
Amends section 17 of the principal Act. Inserts an Explanation in sub-section (3) and substitutes clauses (a) and (b) in sub-section (5).
Amends section 20 of the principal Act by substituting the words and figures "under entry 84.", the words, figures and letter "under entries 84 and 92A" in clause (c) of the Explanation.
Amends section 22 of the principal Act. Inserts a proviso in sub-section (1) and amends the Explanation in clause (iii) of sub-section (1).
Amends section 24 of the principal Act by substituting the words "commerce operator" and the words and figures "who is required to collect tax at source under section 52" in clause (x).
Amends section 25 of the principal Act by inserting a proviso in sub-section (1), after the proviso and before the Explanation.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By notification in the Official Gazette.

key_procedures: Notification of commencement date by the Government in the Official Gazette.
Government may specify different dates for different provisions.
Government may, on recommendations of the Council, specify registered persons liable for reverse charge tax on certain supplies.
Input tax credit for certain services and goods may be available under specific conditions.
administration: Law (Legislation-A) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act aims to amend the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.
Some amendments are effective from July 1, 2017.
The Act includes clarifications on the definition of 'services' and the scope of input tax credit for certain categories.

title: THE KERALA STATE HIGHER EDUCATION COUNCIL (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2018
purpose: To amend the Kerala State Higher Education Council Act, 2007.
scope: Applies to the Kerala State Higher Education Council and related matters within the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.RUSA: Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan, a centrally sponsored scheme for higher education.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala State Higher Education Council (Amendment) Act, 2018. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 5th day of July, 2017.

In the Kerala State Higher Education Council Act, 2007 (22 of 2007) (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), in the preamble, in the first paragraph, for the word "experts", the words "experts, teachers, students" shall be substituted.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of certain expressions by certain other expressions
main_sections.description: In the principal Act, for the words "Advisory Council", "Executive Council" and "Governing Council", wherever they occur, the words "Advisory Body", "Executive Body" and "Governing Body" shall, respectively, be substituted.

In section 2 of the principal Act, after clause (s), the following clause shall be inserted, namely: "(sa) "RUSA" means the Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan, a centrally sponsored scheme for higher education;".

In section 4 of the principal Act, - (i) in sub-section (1), for clause (a), the following clause shall be substituted, namely: "(a) to render advice to the Government, Universities, colleges and other institutions of higher education in the State in matters of access, equity and excellence in higher education;" (ii) in sub-section (2), after clause (y), the following clauses shall be inserted, namely:- "(z) conduct longitudinal studies to understand the impact of student learning; (za) promote and integrate scientifically proven indigenous knowledge systems in the State higher education system; (zb) evolve programmes to improve access to higher education for differently abled students; (zc) collaborate with the Government in the implementation of RUSA and other similar centrally sponsored schemes and other central sector schemes within the State; (zd) evolve common academic guidelines for Universities in the State for mutual recognition, approval or equalization of academic programmes or areas of studies and nomenclature thereof; (ze) evolve common academic guidelines for Universities in the State for recognition, approval or equalization of academic programmes or areas of studies and nomenclature thereof of various programmes conducted or co-ordinated by Universities or higher education institutions outside the State and outside the country; (zf) facilitate the dissemination of knowledge of higher education to target audience through electronic and print media.".

In section 5 of the principal Act, after sub-section (3), the following sub-section shall be inserted, namely: "(4) The Patron may refer any matter relating to higher education and higher education institutions, as he deems fit, for the expert opinion of the Council.".

In section 6 of the principal Act, after sub-section (3), the following sub-section shall be inserted, namely: "(4) The Visitor may refer any matter relating to higher education and higher education institutions, as he deems fit, for the expert opinion of the Council.".
In section 9 of the principal Act, in sub-section (3), the words "as may be prescribed", the words "or delegated by the Vice-Chairman from time to time" shall be inserted.
In section 10 of the principal Act, in sub-section (4), the words "as may be prescribed", the words "or delegated by the Vice-Chairman from time to time" shall be inserted.

In section 11 of the principal Act, in sub-section (2),— (i) after the words "shall be reconstituted", the word "simultaneously" shall be inserted; (ii) in the proviso, for the words "shall continue to be in office for a further period of six months or till their reconstitution, whichever is earlier", the words "shall continue to hold office till their reconstitution" shall be substituted.

In section 12 of the principal Act,— (i) for item (k), the following item shall be substituted, namely:- "(k) one Vice-Chancellor of a University outside the State of Kerala established by an Act of another State, nominated by the Government;" (ii) after item (ab), the following items shall be inserted, namely: — "(ac) one Chairman or Vice-Chairman of a State Higher Education Council outside the State of Kerala, nominated by the Government; (ad) one Vice-Chancellor of a Central University outside the State, nominated by the Government."

In section 14 of the principal Act, after item (r), the following items shall be inserted, namely:— "(s) one nominee of the Ministry of Human Resources Development, Government of India, not below the rank of a Joint Secretary; (t) State Project Director, RUSA; (u) one Principal of an affiliated college, nominated by the Government; (v) one non-teaching staff member of a University or College, nominated by the Government."

In section 15 of the principal Act, in clause (k),— (i) after the words "it shall meet", the words "at least twice a year" shall be inserted; (ii) the words "provided that it shall meet at least twice a year" shall be omitted.
In section 17 of the principal Act, for clause (c), the following clause shall be substituted, namely:— "(c) it shall nominate one of its members to the Academic Council of each University.".
In section 20 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), in the first proviso, the words "for a further period of six months or" and the words "whichever is earlier" shall be omitted.
In section 25 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), after the words "the University Grants Commission", the symbol and word ".RUSA" shall be inserted.

main_sections.section_title: Special provision relating to existing Governing Council
main_sections.description: Notwithstanding anything contained in the principal Act, on and from the date of commencement of the Kerala State Higher Education Council (Amendment) Ordinance, 2017 (13 of 2017), the existing Governing Council shall stand dissolved and all the members of the said Governing Council shall be deemed to have vacated their offices as such on such dissolution.

(1) The Kerala State Higher Education Council (Amendment) Ordinance, 2018 (26 of 2018) is hereby repealed. (2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

administration: Government of Kerala, Law (Legislation-G) Department
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on the 5th day of July, 2017.
The Kerala State Higher Education Council (Amendment) Ordinance, 2018 is repealed and replaced by this Act.
Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are deemed to have been taken under this Act.

title: THE KERALA TAILORING WORKERS’ WELFARE FUND (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2021
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Tailoring Workers’ Welfare Fund Act, 1994, to update contribution amounts and related provisions.
scope: This Act applies to tailoring workers and employers engaged in tailoring work within the state of Kerala. It amends the principal Act of 1994.

key_definitions.tailoring worker: An individual engaged in tailoring work.
key_definitions.self employed person: A person engaged in tailoring work on their own behalf.
key_definitions.employer: A person or entity that engages tailoring workers.
key_definitions.Fund: Refers to the Kerala Tailoring Workers' Welfare Fund.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act as 'The Kerala Tailoring Workers’ Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2021' and states that it shall be deemed to have come into force on April 21, 2020.

This section details the amendments to section 7 of the principal Act. It substitutes sub-section (1) and sub-section (2) of section 7, altering the contribution amounts and responsibilities for tailoring workers and employers.

This section repeals the Kerala Tailoring Workers’ Welfare Fund (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021. It also includes a saving clause, ensuring that anything done or deemed to have been done under the repealed Ordinance is considered to have been done under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Every tailoring worker and self-employed person shall contribute fifty rupees per month to the Fund.
Rule 2: Every employer shall contribute twenty-five rupees per month for each tailoring worker engaged by them.

Rule 3: Every employer shall pay seventy-five rupees to the Fund per month for each tailoring worker, which includes the worker's contribution. However, workers can remit their own contribution if they are prepared to do so, in which case the employer only needs to pay their own contribution.
Rule 4: The Kerala Tailoring Workers’ Welfare Fund (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021 is repealed.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Implicitly, the authorities responsible for administering the Kerala Tailoring Workers' Welfare Fund under the principal Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the mechanisms established by the principal Act for collection of contributions and administration of the Fund.

rights: Tailoring workers have the right to have their contributions remitted by their employer, or to remit it themselves if they choose.
Workers who remit their own contributions are covered under the Fund.
duties: Every tailoring worker and self-employed person has a duty to contribute fifty rupees per month to the Fund.
Every employer has a duty to contribute twenty-five rupees per month for each tailoring worker engaged by them.

Every employer has a duty to pay seventy-five rupees to the Fund per month for each tailoring worker, which includes the worker's contribution, unless the worker chooses to remit their own contribution.
obligations: The obligation to contribute to the Fund rests on both individual workers (or self-employed persons) and employers.
Employers are obligated to ensure the correct amount of contribution is paid to the Fund, considering whether the worker remits their own share or if the employer facilitates the entire payment.

key_procedures: Amendment of Section 7 of the principal Act: This involves substituting the existing sub-sections (1) and (2) with new provisions that specify the monthly contribution amounts for tailoring workers and employers.
Deemed commencement: The Act is deemed to have come into force on April 21, 2020, meaning actions taken or contributions made from that date are validated by this amendment.
Repeal of Ordinance: The Kerala Tailoring Workers’ Welfare Fund (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021 is officially repealed.
administration: The Kerala Tailoring Workers' Welfare Fund, as governed by the principal Act and this amendment.
important_notes: The Act is considered to have come into force retroactively from April 21, 2020.
The repeal of the Ordinance does not invalidate actions taken under it; such actions are deemed to have been taken under the amended principal Act.

title: THE KERALA TAXATION LAWS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2023
purpose: To further amend the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 and the Kerala Finance Act, 2023.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Kerala. It amends specific provisions of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, and the Kerala Finance Act, 2023, impacting taxation laws within the state.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Kerala Taxation Laws (Amendment) Act, 2023, and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Government via official gazette notification.

Details amendments to the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 (Act 20 of 2017). This includes changes to sections related to the manner and time for appealing cancellation orders, extending the time for furnishing valid returns in case of assessment orders, substituting the constitution of the Appellate Tribunal, omitting certain sections, and modifying references to Benches of the Appellate Tribunal.
Amends section 11, sub-section (4) of the Kerala Finance Act, 2023 (Act 17 of 2023), by changing 'section 22 and section 24' to 'section 22 or section 24'.

Repeals the Kerala Taxation Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 2023 (Ordinance 2 of 2023). It also provides that anything done or actions taken under the Acts as amended by the Ordinance are deemed to have been done or taken under the Acts as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Rule under Section 2(1)(a): A cancellation order can be appealed in a prescribed manner, within a prescribed time, and subject to prescribed conditions and restrictions.

Rule under Section 2(2)(b): A registered person who fails to furnish a valid return within sixty days of the assessment order can furnish it within a further period of sixty days by paying an additional late fee of one hundred rupees per day of delay. If a valid return is furnished within this extended period, the assessment order is deemed withdrawn, but liability for interest and late fees continues.

penalties: Late fee of one hundred rupees for each day of delay beyond sixty days for furnishing a valid return after an assessment order, if an extension is granted.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala, through its tax departments and authorities responsible for the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, and the Kerala Finance Act, 2023.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the mechanisms and authorities established under the amended Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, and the Kerala Finance Act, 2023, including assessment, appeals, and enforcement of late fees and other statutory liabilities.

rights: Right to appeal against assessment orders within an extended period under specific conditions and payment of late fees.
Right to have an assessment order deemed withdrawn if a valid return is filed within the extended period.
duties: Duty to furnish valid returns within the prescribed timeframes.
Duty to comply with assessment orders.
Duty to pay applicable late fees and interest.
obligations: Obligation to appeal cancellation orders in the prescribed manner, time, and subject to conditions.
Obligation to pay late fees for delayed return filing after assessment orders, even if an extension is granted.
Obligation to pay interest under section 50 and late fee under section 47 of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.

key_procedures: Appeals against cancellation orders: To be filed in the prescribed manner, within the prescribed time, and subject to prescribed conditions and restrictions.

Filing of valid return after assessment order: A registered person has 60 days to furnish a valid return. If not, they can furnish it within a further 60 days by paying a daily late fee. This action can lead to the assessment order being deemed withdrawn.
administration: Law (Legislation-A) Department, Government of Kerala, and the tax administration bodies responsible for implementing the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, and the Kerala Finance Act, 2023.
important_notes: The Act aims to streamline and clarify certain aspects of the taxation laws in Kerala.
The amendments regarding the Appellate Tribunal benches align with the structure established by the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.
The repeal and saving clause ensures continuity and validity of actions taken under the previous Ordinance.

title: THE KERALA TAXATION LAWS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2024
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Finance Act, 2008, the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 and the Kerala Finance Act, 2024.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala. It amends specific provisions of three existing Kerala tax laws, primarily concerning the Kerala Finance Act, 2008, the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, and the Kerala Finance Act, 2024.

key_definitions.input_service_distributor: An office of the supplier of goods or services or both which receives tax invoices towards the receipt of input services, including invoices in respect of services liable to tax under sub-section (3) or sub-section (4) of section 9, for or on behalf of distinct persons referred to in section 25, and liable to distribute the input tax credit in respect of such invoices in the manner provided in section 20.
key_definitions.arrears_of_tax_or_surcharge: Has the same meaning as assigned in the Kerala Finance Act, 2024 (18 of 2024).
key_definitions.certificate_of_settlement: Has the same meaning as assigned in the Kerala Finance Act, 2024 (18 of 2024).
key_definitions.specified_order: Has the same meaning as assigned in the Kerala Finance Act, 2024 (18 of 2024).

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and outlines the commencement dates for its various provisions, with some provisions deemed to have come into force on specific dates in August, October, and April, while others will come into force on a date appointed by the Government.

Inserts a new sub-section (6) into Section 6 of the Kerala Finance Act, 2008. This new sub-section deals with the settlement of cess payable on arrears of tax under Chapter III of the Kerala Finance Act, 2024, and discharges the dealer from liability for such cess, with no provision for refund if already paid.

Introduces several amendments to the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017. These include substitutions and insertions in various sections, covering definitions, levy of tax, time of supply, input tax credit availability, distribution of credit by Input Service Distributors, and procedures for determination of tax.

important_rules: Rule 1: Specific provisions of the Act come into force on different dates, with some having retrospective effect.
Rule 2: Cess payable on arrears of tax settled under Chapter III of the Kerala Finance Act, 2024, is deemed settled, and the dealer is discharged from liability, with no refund for already paid cess.

Rule 3: Amendments to the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, include changes to the definition of 'Input Service Distributor', clarification on the levy of tax on extra neutral alcohol, insertion of a new section for non-recovery of GST due to general practice, and modifications to input tax credit rules.
Rule 4: The time limit for availing input tax credit for specific financial years (2017-18 to 2020-21) is extended up to November 30, 2021.
Rule 5: Procedures for availing input tax credit after revocation of registration cancellation are detailed.
Rule 6: Section 17(5)(i) of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, is amended to limit the application of Section 74 to periods up to the Financial Year 2023-24.
Rule 7: Section 20 of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, is substituted to detail the manner of distribution of credit by Input Service Distributors.
Rule 8: Section 39(3) is amended to require registered persons to electronically furnish a return for every calendar month, irrespective of whether deductions were made.
Rule 9: A new sub-section (15) is inserted into Section 54, disallowing refund of unutilised input tax credit on zero-rated supply of goods if subjected to export duty.

Rule 10: Section 73 and Section 74 of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, are amended to specify their applicability for determination of tax pertaining to periods up to the Financial Year 2023-24.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government of Kerala (specifically, the Law Department is involved in publishing the Act, and the relevant tax authorities under the GST and Finance Acts would be responsible for enforcement).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amendments to existing tax laws, enforcement will be carried out by the respective tax departments responsible for administering the Kerala Finance Act, 2008, the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, and the Kerala Finance Act, 2024.

rights: Right to discharge from liability for cess on arrears of tax settled under Chapter III of the Kerala Finance Act, 2024, where applicable.
Right to avail input tax credit under certain conditions and within specified timelines, even after registration cancellation revocation.
Right to claim input tax credit for specific financial years under certain conditions.
duties: Duty to comply with the amended provisions of the Kerala Finance Act, 2008, the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, and the Kerala Finance Act, 2024.
Duty for registered persons to electronically furnish monthly returns under Section 39.
Duty to attend and provide information or documents when summoned by an officer.
Duty to distribute input tax credit by Input Service Distributors as prescribed.
obligations: Obligation to pay tax and other charges as per the amended laws.
Obligation for Input Service Distributors to register and distribute input tax credit.
Obligation to adhere to the timelines for filing returns and availing input tax credit.

key_procedures: Procedure for settlement of cess on arrears of tax under the Kerala Finance Act, 2024.
Procedure for distribution of input tax credit by Input Service Distributors.
Procedure for availing input tax credit in specific scenarios related to financial years and registration cancellation.
Procedure for determination of tax under Section 73 and Section 74 for periods up to FY 2023-24.
Procedure for summoning persons and requiring them to state the truth, make statements, or produce documents during examination.
administration: The administration of this Act will be through the respective departments responsible for the enforcement of the Kerala Finance Act, 2008, the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, and the Kerala Finance Act, 2024. The Law Department of the Government of Kerala is responsible for the publication of the Act.
important_notes: No refund of cess is available if it has already been paid and is deemed settled under the provisions of this Act.
The Act makes provisions for situations where Goods and Services Tax was not levied or was short-levied due to a general practice.
Specific time limits are prescribed for availing input tax credit in various circumstances.
Refund of unutilised input tax credit on zero-rated supply of goods is not allowed if such supply is subjected to export duty.
Amendments to Section 73 and Section 74 limit their application to tax determination pertaining to periods up to the Financial Year 2023-24.

title: THE KERALA TODDY INDUSTRY DEVELOPMENT BOARD ACT, 2021
purpose: To provide for the constitution of the Toddy Industry Development Board to promote and develop the traditional toddy industry in the State of Kerala and matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: This act applies to the State of Kerala and concerns the promotion and development of the traditional toddy industry. It establishes the Kerala Toddy Industry Development Board.

key_definitions.Board: The Kerala Toddy Industry Development Board constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.Chief Executive Officer: The Chief Executive Officer of the Board appointed under section 13.
key_definitions.Excise Commissioner: An officer appointed by the Government under clause (a) of section 4 of the Abkari Act, 1077 (1 of 1077).
key_definitions.member: Member of the Board.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.regulation: Regulations made by the Board under this Act.
key_definitions.toddy: Toddy as defined under clause (n) of rule 2 of the Kerala Abkari Shops Disposal Rules, 2002.
key_definitions.toddy shop: Toddy shop as defined under clause (c) of rule 2 of the Kerala Abkari Shops Disposal Rules, 2002.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Toddy Industry Development Board Act, 2021 and it is deemed to have come into force on February 25, 2021.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'Chairperson', 'Chief Executive Officer', 'Excise Commissioner', 'Government', 'member', 'prescribed', 'regulation', 'State', 'toddy', and 'toddy shop'.

Details the constitution of the Kerala Toddy Industry Development Board, its corporate status, perpetual succession, common seal, and powers. It also specifies the composition of the Board, including the Chairperson and various members representing government departments, academic institutions, trade unions, licensees associations, and coconut farmers.

main_sections.section_title: Service conditions and term of office of the Chairperson and members
main_sections.description: Specifies that the Chairperson and non-official members may hold office for five years and that their salary and allowances will be as prescribed.
Empowers the Government to reconstitute the Board by notification and specifies that members of the previously constituted Board will vacate their offices upon reconstitution unless re-appointed.

main_sections.section_title: Disqualification for being appointed, or for continuing as, a member of the Board
main_sections.description: Lists grounds for disqualification from appointment or continuation as a Board member, including unsound mind, undischarged insolvency, conviction for certain offenses, and holding interest in Board contracts.

main_sections.section_title: Removal or suspension of members from their office
main_sections.description: Outlines the conditions under which the Government may remove a Chairperson or member, such as refusal to work, conviction, absence from meetings, abuse of official position, or unsuitability. It also allows for suspension during proceedings and prohibits re-appointment after removal.

main_sections.section_title: Resignation of office by a member
main_sections.description: Allows any member to resign by giving written notice to the Government, with the resignation becoming effective upon acceptance.

main_sections.section_title: Vacancy to be filled in as early as possible
main_sections.description: Mandates that vacancies arising from disqualification, removal, or resignation be filled by the Government as early as possible, with the new member serving the remainder of the original term.

main_sections.section_title: Vacancies etc. not to invalidate proceedings of the Board
main_sections.description: Ensures that the Board's proceedings are not invalidated due to vacancies or defects in its constitution.

main_sections.section_title: Temporary association of persons with the Board for particular purposes
main_sections.description: Allows the Board to associate individuals for specific purposes, granting them the right to participate in discussions but not to vote.

Specifies that the Board shall meet at prescribed times and places, follow procedural rules, and meet at least once every three months. It also details the presiding officer, quorum, decision-making process (majority vote, casting vote for the Chairperson), and the forwarding of minutes to the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Chief Executive Officer and other staff of the Board
main_sections.description: Covers the appointment of the Chief Executive Officer (on deputation) and other necessary officers and staff, along with their powers, duties, conditions of service, salary, and allowances as may be prescribed.

Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, with retrospective or prospective effect. It lists specific matters for which rules can be made, including salaries and allowances for the Chairperson and members, powers and duties of the Chief Executive Officer, appointment of staff, contract procedures, annual and supplementary plans, budget preparation, accounting, and annual reports.

Empowers the Board, with the prior approval of the Government, to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules. It specifies areas for which regulations can be made, such as temporary association of persons, meeting times and procedures, and financial standing committee powers.

Repeals the Kerala Toddy Industry Development Board Ordinance, 2021 (Ordinance 103 of 2021) and provides that anything done or deemed to have been done under the Ordinance shall be considered as done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Rules can be made by the Government to implement the Act, with retrospective or prospective effect (Section 34(1)).

Specific matters for which rules can be made include salaries and allowances for the Chairperson and members, powers and duties of the Chief Executive Officer, appointment and service conditions of staff, contract procedures, annual and supplementary plans, budget preparation, accounting, and annual reports (Section 34(2)).
Regulations can be made by the Board, with prior Government approval, for specific purposes like temporary association of individuals, meeting procedures, and financial committee powers (Section 35).
The Board shall meet at least once in every three months (Section 12(1)).
A person disqualified under Section 6, removed under Section 7, or resigned under Section 8 ceases to be a member of the Board (Section 9(1)).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala and the Kerala Toddy Industry Development Board.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the promulgation of rules and regulations, and by the actions of the Board and its officers.

rights: The Board has the right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property.
The Board has the power to enter into contracts.
The Board can sue and be sued in its name.
Persons associated with the Board for specific purposes have the right to participate in discussions (but not to vote).
The Chairperson or presiding member has a casting vote in case of equality of votes.
duties: The Government shall constitute the Board.
The Board shall promote and develop the traditional toddy industry.
The Board shall exercise powers and perform functions conferred by the Act.
The Board shall ensure its proceedings are not invalidated by vacancies or defects.
Minutes of every Board meeting shall be forwarded to the Government within fifteen days.
obligations: The Board must operate subject to the provisions of the Act.
Members removed from the Board are not eligible for re-appointment.
The Government must provide a reasonable opportunity of being heard before removing a member.
Any member removed or disqualified shall cease to be a member of the Board.

key_procedures: Constitution of the Board: Government notification to constitute the Board comprising a Chairperson and specified members (Section 3).
Appointment of Chairperson and Members: By notification in the Official Gazette (Section 3(5)).
Reconstitution of the Board: By Government notification specifying reasons (Section 5).
Removal of Members: Government order after providing an opportunity to be heard (Section 7).
Resignation of Members: Written notice to the Government and acceptance (Section 8).
Filling of Vacancies: By the Government as early as possible (Section 9).
Board Meetings: Held at prescribed times and places, at least once every three months, with a quorum of one-third of members (Section 12).
Appointment of Chief Executive Officer: By the Government on deputation (Section 13(1)).
Making of Rules: By the Government through gazette notification (Section 34).
Making of Regulations: By the Board with prior Government approval through gazette notification (Section 35).
administration: The Government of Kerala (Law (Legislation-A) Department is indicated in the notification). The Board itself is also responsible for administration of its functions.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on February 25, 2021 (Section 1(2)).
The repeal of the Ordinance does not affect anything done or deemed to have been done under it (Section 36(2)).
A person removed from the Board under Section 7 cannot be reappointed or appointed in any other capacity under the Board (Section 7(3)).

title: THE KERALA UNIVERSITY (ALTERNATE ARRANGEMENT TEMPORARILY OF THE SENATE AND SYNDICATE) ACT, 2018
purpose: To make provisions for the alternate arrangement temporarily of the Senate and Syndicate of the Kerala University.
scope: Applies to the Kerala University.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala University (Alternate Arrangement Temporarily of the Senate and Syndicate) Act, 2018, and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 17th day of May, 2018.

main_sections.section_title: Special provision for temporary alternate arrangement for exercising the powers and performing the functions of the Senate and Syndicate of the Kerala University
main_sections.description: Notwithstanding anything contained in the Kerala University Act, 1974 or any statute, regulation, ordinance or rules made thereunder, the functions of the Senate and Syndicate of the University shall be exercised by an interim body nominated by the Government. This interim body will function for a period of six months or till the reconstitution of the Senate and Syndicate in accordance with the provisions of the Kerala University Act, 1974, whichever is earlier. The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, nominate an interim body consisting of ex-officio members of the Syndicate, nominated members (teachers, principals, teacher representatives, students, and eminent persons from education sector belonging to Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes).

Repeals the Kerala University (Alternate Arrangement Temporarily of the Senate and Syndicate) Ordinance, 2018. It also saves anything done or any action taken under the said Ordinance from being affected.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through gazette notification for nominating the interim body and by the provisions of the Act.

key_procedures: Nomination of an interim body by the Government via gazette notification to exercise powers and perform functions of the Senate and Syndicate.

purpose: To amend the Kerala University of Fisheries and Ocean Studies Act, 2010 (Act 5 of 2011) for the purposes specified in the Act.

key_definitions.Extension Council: The Extension Council constituted under section 19A of this Act.
key_definitions.Faculty Board of Studies: The Faculty Board of Studies constituted in each Faculty under sub-section (4) of section 25.

key_definitions.Librarian: The librarian of the university appointed under section 40.
key_definitions.Pro-Vice-Chancellor: The Pro-Vice-Chancellor of the University appointed under section 35.
key_definitions.University Engineer: The University Engineer appointed under section 39.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Kerala University of Fisheries And Ocean Studies (Amendment) Act, 2021' and deems it to have come into force on February 26, 2021.

Inserts 'fisheries, aquaculture, control of fish diseases, fish processing and fish marketing' after 'environmental science,' in the preamble of the principal Act.
Substitutes 'Fisheries And Ocean Studies' with 'Fi sheries And Ocean Studies' in sub-section (1) of section 1 of the principal Act.

Introduces several amendments to section 2 of the principal Act, including omitting certain clauses, inserting new definitions (e.g., Controller of Examinations, Extension Council, Faculty Board of Studies, Librarian, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, University Engineer), and substituting existing clauses.

Substitutes 'Fisheries and Ocean studies' with 'Fisheries and Ocean Studies' in sub-section (1) and replaces 'School Governing Council, Departmental Governing Councils' with 'Extension Council, Faculty Board of studies' in sub-section (2) of section 3 of the principal Act.
Inserts 'on the basis of detailed study' after 'in respective fields' in item (iv) of section 5 of the principal Act.

Amends section 8 of the principal Act to omit 'school', insert 'including digitally stored' for documents, and substitutes sub-section (2) regarding government inspection and inquiry notice periods. Substitutes 'School Governing Councils; Departmental Governing Councils; faculties;' with 'Extension Council; Faculty Board of Studies;' in section 9 of the principal Act.

Amends sub-section (1) of section 10 of the principal Act by modifying ex-officio member descriptions, substituting nominated members, omitting certain elected members, and adding 'Dean of all Faculties of the University' and 'the Registrar' as ex-officio members. Substitutes 'schools' with 'Faculty Boards of Studies' in sub-section (3) of section 49 of the principal Act.
Omit 'School Directors' and their punctuation from sub-section (6) of section 50 and substitutes 'eighty-five' with 'eighty-six' in sub-section (7) of section 50 of the principal Act.
Omit the second proviso to sub-section (1) of section 52 of the principal Act.

Substitutes section 60 of the principal Act with a new section establishing a 'University Ombudsman' responsible for inquiring into public grievances and allegations regarding maladministration, corruption, or favoritism, and recommending prosecution if necessary. The Ombudsman must be a retired High Court judge and have a term of one year.

Substitutes sub-section (1) of section 64 of the principal Act to redefine the composition of the Finance Committee, including the Vice-Chancellor as Chairperson, Secretaries from Finance and Fisheries Departments, Director of Fisheries, two members nominated by the University Governing Council, the Finance Officer, and the Registrar as Member Secretary. It also inserts a new sub-section (3) stating that the interval between two meetings of the Finance Committee shall not exceed three months and the quorum is half the total number of members.

Substitutes 'section 42' with 'section 68' in item (i) of section 69 of the principal Act.
Substitutes 'schools' with 'Faculties' in sub-section (1) of section 71 of the principal Act.

important_rules: Teachers in the University shall be categorized as Professor, Associate Professor, and Assistant Professor. However, a teacher can be deputed for teaching in another Faculty if necessary.
Faculty of Fisheries Engineering, Management, and Fishery Geography departments in the University are to be retained in the Faculty of Fisheries.

Appointment, powers, and duties of teachers shall be as prescribed by the Statutes. However, for teachers continuing in the Faculty of Fisheries on the commencement date of this Act, a B.F.Sc. degree is not mandatory.
Heads of Departments are responsible for the implementation of teaching, research, and extension activities assigned to teachers.

penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, inquiries, investigations by the Ombudsman, and implementation of recommendations by the University authorities and the State Government.

Right to create teaching/non-teaching posts for administration with government permission.
Right to manage university funds and finances.

Duty to prescribe qualifications for teachers and staff.
Duty to maintain academic standards.
Duty to cooperate with government inspections and inquiries.
Duty to implement directions from the Government and authorities.
Duty to ensure timely furnishing of information to the Government by the Registrar.

University authorities are obligated to implement directions from the Government.
The University must create posts with the permission of the State Government.

Conduct of Finance Committee meetings with a defined quorum and frequency.
Appointment of a University Ombudsman through government notification.
Government-initiated inspections or inquiries of the University with prior notice.
Procedure for creating teaching, research, and administrative posts with State Government permission.

This section details amendments to section 20 of the principal Act. It substitutes the rank of 'Labour Commissioner' with 'Deputy Labour Commissioner' for certain officers, increases the fine from 'fifty rupees' to 'one hundred rupees' in sub-section (4), and modifies clause (b) of sub-section (5) regarding recovery of dues.
This section amends section 22 of the principal Act, substituting the fine from 'five hundred rupees' to 'one lakh rupees'.

This new section outlines penalties for contraventions of the Act or rules made thereunder, including fines up to two lakh rupees and additional daily fines for continuing contraventions, with specific provisions for subsequent convictions and the Magistrate's power to impose fines exceeding ten thousand rupees.

penalties: Contravention of the Act or rules: fine up to two lakh rupees and an additional fine of up to two thousand rupees per day for continuing contravention. The total fine shall not exceed two thousand rupees per worker employed.

Magistrate can impose a fine exceeding ten thousand rupees, notwithstanding section 29(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

title: The Non-Resident Indians’ (Keralites) Commission Amendment Act, 2022
purpose: To amend the Non-Resident Indians’ (Keralites) Commission Act, 2015, for purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: This act applies to the Non-Resident Indians’ (Keralites) Commission Act, 2015, and specifically amends sections 3 and 4 of the principal Act. It is enacted in the Seventy-third Year of the Republic of India.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Non-Resident Indians’ (Keralites) Commission Amendment Act, 2022, and that it shall come into force at once.
Amends item (v) of sub-section (2) of section 3 of the principal Act by substituting the figures '65' with the words 'sixty eight'.

Amends section 4 of the principal Act. Sub-section (1) substitutes 're-appointment' with 're-nomination'. The proviso to sub-section (2) substitutes 'nominated' with 'nominated' (this appears to be a typo in the original document, likely intended to be a different word or phrase, but as per the text, it's a substitution of the same word).

important_rules: Rule 1: Substitution of age limit in Section 3(2)(v) from 65 to 68 years.
Rule 2: Substitution of 're-appointment' with 're-nomination' in Section 4(1).
Rule 3: Substitution of 'nominated' with 'nominated' in the proviso to Section 4(2).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not specified in the provided text.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not specified in the provided text.

administration: Law (Legislation-H) Department, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The act is a translation in English of the original Malayalam act.
The Governor of Kerala has authorized the publication of this English translation.
The principal act being amended is the Non-Resident Indians’ (Keralites) Commission Act, 2015 (Act 3 of 2016).

title: THE NON-RESIDENT KERALITES WELFARE (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2019
purpose: To further amend the Non-Resident Keralites Welfare Act, 2008, specifically to introduce provisions for a 'Non-Resident Keralites' Dividend Scheme' and to expand the types of societies that can be set up under the Act.
scope: This act applies to Non-Resident Keralites and their welfare, and concerns the framework established by the Non-Resident Keralites Welfare Act, 2008. It also impacts institutions and societies that can be set up for the welfare of non-resident Keralites.

key_definitions.dividend: Share of profit on the invested amount, given to the investor by the agency that receives investments as per the Non-Resident Keralites' Dividend Scheme.
key_definitions.non_resident_keralites_dividend_scheme: A dividend scheme for non-resident Keralites framed as per section 8A of the Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Non-Resident Keralites' Welfare (Amendment) Act, 2019, and that it is deemed to have come into force on October 22, 2018.
Amends Section 2 of the principal Act (Non-Resident Keralites Welfare Act, 2008) by inserting new clauses to define 'Dividend' and 'Non-Resident Keralites' Dividend Scheme'.

Inserts a new section 8A into the principal Act, which empowers the Government to frame a scheme for deposits from non-resident Keralites and for giving monthly dividends. It also allows the Board, with Government approval, to set up institutions for the implementation of this scheme and other welfare activities.

Amends Section 14 of the principal Act to include societies registered under the Travancore-Cochin Literary, Scientific and Charitable Societies Registration Act, 1955, in addition to existing provisions.

Repeals the Non-Resident Keralites' Welfare (Amendment) Ordinance, 2019 (25 of 2019) and provides that anything done or taken under the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: A Non-Resident Keralites' Dividend Scheme can be framed by the Government for deposits received from non-resident Keralites.
This scheme includes providing a monthly dividend to depositors, based on the utilization of their deposits.
The Board may set up institutions for the scheme's implementation and other welfare activities with prior Government approval, as per Section 14.
Societies registered under the Travancore-Cochin Literary, Scientific and Charitable Societies Registration Act, 1955, can be established under Section 14.

rights: Right of non-resident Keralites to receive monthly dividends from their deposits under the dividend scheme.
Right of the Government to frame schemes for the welfare of non-resident Keralites.
duties: Duty of the Government to frame schemes for deposits and dividends for non-resident Keralites.
Duty of the Board to implement the scheme and welfare activities.
Duty of the Board to seek Government approval for setting up institutions.
obligations: Obligation of the agency receiving investments to give a share of profit (dividend) to the investor.
Obligation for any actions taken under the repealed Ordinance to be deemed valid under the new Act.

key_procedures: Framing of a Non-Resident Keralites' Dividend Scheme by the Government.
Utilizing deposits received from non-resident Keralites.
Providing monthly dividends to depositors.
Setting up of institutions by the Board with Government approval for scheme implementation and welfare activities.
administration: The Government (specifically the Law Department is mentioned in the notification for publication) and the Board established under the principal Act.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force retrospectively from October 22, 2018.
The Non-Resident Keralites' Welfare (Amendment) Ordinance, 2019, has been repealed.

title: THE NON-RESIDENT KERALITES’ WELFARE (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2024
purpose: To further amend the Non-Resident Keralites’ Welfare Act, 2008.
scope: This act applies to the Non-Resident Keralites' Welfare Act, 2008, and its provisions. It aims to amend specific sections of the principal act to improve the welfare mechanisms for Non-Resident Keralites.

key_definitions.dividend: The sum allotted to the Board on the deposit transferred to the agencies specified by the Government as per the Non-Resident Keralites’ Dividend Scheme for providing an assured sum to the members or beneficiaries of the said Scheme which the said agencies shall give to the Board together with the Government share.

main_sections.description: (1) This Act may be called the Non-Resident Keralites’ Welfare (Amendment) Act, 2024. (2) It shall come into force at once.
Substitutes clause (ga) in section 2 of the principal Act with a new definition for 'Dividend'.

Inserts a new sub-section (2) to section 8A of the principal Act, empowering the Government to make additions, amendments, omissions, or variations in the Scheme by notification in the Gazette, prospectively or retrospectively.

Amends sub-sections (3) and (4) of section 9 of the principal Act, and omits sub-section (5). It revises the composition of the Board, specifying the number and representation of directors, and designates the Chairman.

Amends sub-section (1) of section 10 of the principal Act by adding specific wording regarding the commencement of the term. It also inserts a new sub-section (4) to address the filling of casual vacancies for nominated directors.

important_rules: The Board shall consist of fifteen Directors nominated by the Government.
Five Directors will represent Non-Resident Keralites (abroad).
Two Directors will represent Non-Resident Keralites (India).
Four officers will represent the Government (ex-officio).
One Director will represent the Overseas Development and Employment Promotion Consultants Limited (ex-officio).
The Chief Executive Officer of the Board will be an ex-officio Director.
One representative from NORKA-ROOTS will be an ex-officio Director.
One Director will be nominated by the Government.
The Chairman of the Board shall be appointed from among the Directors representing Non-Resident Keralites (abroad).
A casual vacancy for a nominated Director shall be filled as soon as possible, and the new nominee will hold office for the remaining term.
The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, modify the Scheme framed under sub-section (1) of section 8A, either prospectively or retrospectively.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala and the Board established under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications in the Gazette for scheme modifications and appointment of directors, and by filling casual vacancies.

rights: Members or beneficiaries of the Non-Resident Keralites’ Dividend Scheme have the right to receive an assured sum as per the scheme.
Nominated Directors have the right to hold office for their specified term, with provisions for filling casual vacancies.
duties: Agencies specified by the Government are obligated to provide the Government share and other sums to the Board for the Dividend Scheme.
The Government has a duty to ensure the effective implementation and administration of the Non-Resident Keralites’ Welfare Act.
obligations: Agencies receiving deposits for the Dividend Scheme have an obligation to provide the allotted sum to the Board.
The Government has an obligation to fill casual vacancies for nominated directors promptly.
The Board has an obligation to ensure the provision of assured sums to members or beneficiaries of the Dividend Scheme.

key_procedures: Government notification in the Gazette for any addition, amendment, omission, or variation in the Scheme framed under section 8A.
Nomination of fifteen Directors to the Board by the Government through a Gazette notification.
Appointment of one of the Directors representing Non-Resident Keralites (abroad) as the Chairman of the Board by the Government.
Filling of casual vacancies for nominated Directors by the Government as soon as possible.
administration: The Law (Legislation-H) Department, Government of Kerala, is responsible for the notification and translation of the Act. The Board established under the principal Act is responsible for the overall administration of the welfare schemes.
important_notes: The amendment comes into force immediately upon enactment.
The Act explicitly states that the Government can make changes to the Scheme prospectively or retrospectively.
The composition of the Board has been significantly revised in terms of the number and representation of directors.

title: THE PAYMENT OF SALARIES AND ALLOWANCES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2018
purpose: To further amend the Payment of Salaries and Allowances Act, 1951, for the purposes hereinafter appearing, specifically by revising salary and allowance rates for certain legislative positions and members.
scope: This act applies to the State of Kerala and amends the provisions of the principal Act (Payment of Salaries and Allowances Act, 1951) concerning the salaries and allowances of members of the Legislative Assembly, Chief Whip, and Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly, as well as travel allowances for air journeys.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Payment of Salaries and Allowances (Amendment) Act, 2018, and it comes into force on April 1, 2018.

Amends Section 3 of the principal Act to increase the salary of the Chief Whip from one thousand rupees to two thousand rupees and a certain other amount from twelve thousand rupees to forty thousand rupees.

Amends Section 4 of the principal Act to increase the salary of the Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly from one thousand rupees to two thousand rupees and a certain other amount from twelve thousand rupees to forty thousand rupees.
Amends Section 5C of the principal Act to substitute 'five lakh rupees' with 'twenty lakh rupees'.

Inserts a new Section 5D, which states that every member of the Legislative Assembly shall be entitled to be reimbursed for air journey charges inside and outside the State for attending meetings, subject to a maximum of fifty thousand rupees per annum.
Amends sub-section (2) of Section 6 of the principal Act to substitute 'ten thousand and five hundred rupees' with 'seventeen thousand rupees'.
Amends Section 8, sub-section (1) of the principal Act, by substituting specific rupee amounts in clauses (a), (aa), and the proviso to clause (b).
Amends Section 8A of the principal Act by substituting specific rupee amounts in sub-sections (5) and (5A).
Amends Section 8B of the principal Act by substituting 'other than' with 'of the Legislative Assembly including'.

Amends the Schedule to the principal Act, specifically item I and item II, by revising rates for kilometers, incidental expenses, and daily allowances for various modes of travel including air journeys, and introducing new provisions for air travel reimbursement.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Act shall come into force on the 1st day of April, 2018.
Rule 2: The salary of the Chief Whip is increased to two thousand rupees.
Rule 3: The salary of the Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly is increased to two thousand rupees.
Rule 4: Members of the Legislative Assembly are entitled to reimbursement for air journeys within and outside the State for attending meetings, up to a maximum of fifty thousand rupees per annum.
Rule 5: Various rates for kilometers, incidental expenses, and daily allowances for different modes of travel (e.g., car, air) for members of the Legislative Assembly have been revised.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Act is administered by the Government of Kerala, likely through the Law (Legislation-I) Department and relevant finance/assembly secretariats. Enforcement would be through the provisions of the principal Act and its amendments.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Payment of Salaries and Allowances Act, 1951, as amended by this Act, which governs the disbursement of salaries and allowances to legislative members. Non-compliance would be handled according to existing legal frameworks for public officials.

rights: Right to receive enhanced salaries as per amended provisions.
Right to reimbursement for air journeys for attending meetings, subject to prescribed limits.
Right to receive allowances for travel as stipulated in the amended schedule.
duties: Duty to adhere to the specified limits for air journey reimbursements.
Duty to utilize allowances as per the provisions of the Act.
obligations: Obligation to perform duties of office as a member of the Legislative Assembly.
Obligation to ensure that claims for salaries and allowances are in accordance with the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Amendments to salaries and allowances are effective from April 1, 2018.
Procedure 2: Claims for air journey reimbursement are to be made subject to the maximum limit of fifty thousand rupees per annum.
Procedure 3: Revisions to per kilometer rates and daily allowances in the Schedule are to be applied by the relevant disbursing authorities.
administration: Law (Legislation-I) Department, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act specifically amends existing provisions of the Payment of Salaries and Allowances Act, 1951, by increasing monetary figures for salaries and allowances.
Certain allowances related to incidental expenses for travel have been omitted or modified.
New provisions regarding air travel reimbursement for members of the Legislative Assembly have been introduced.
The Act is a consolidated amendment to the principal Act, indicating that the principal Act remains in force with these modifications.

title: THE SREE PANDARAVAKA LANDS (VESTING AND ENFRANCHISEMENT) AMENDMENT ACT, 2023
purpose: To further amend the Sree Pandaravaka Lands (Vesting and Enfranchisement) Act, 1971, specifically to revise the annuity payable under section 6 of the principal Act.
scope: This act applies to the Sree Pandaravaka lands in Kerala and amends the principal Act of 1971. It specifically pertains to the revision of annuities for these lands.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Sree Pandaravaka Lands (Vesting and Enfranchisement) Amendment Act, 2023, and that it shall come into force at once.
This section inserts a new section, 6A, into the principal Act of 1971. This new section deals with the revision of annuity.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Government, in consultation with the Commissioner of Land Revenue and in the prescribed manner, shall revise the annuity payable under section 6 of the principal Act.
Rule 2: The revised annuity shall be thrice the amount of the existing annuity, which is specified as ₹1,75,500.
Rule 3: After the initial revision, the annuity shall be enhanced by twenty-five percent at the expiration of every five years.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government and the Commissioner of Land Revenue are involved in the process of revising the annuity.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The revised annuity is to be paid as per the provisions of the Act and in the manner prescribed.

rights: The right to receive a revised annuity based on the amendment.
duties: The Government has a duty to revise the annuity in consultation with the Commissioner of Land Revenue and in the prescribed manner.
The Government has a duty to enhance the annuity every five years.
obligations: The obligation to pay the revised annuity as determined by the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Consultation between the Government and the Commissioner of Land Revenue for annuity revision.
Procedure 2: Revision of annuity to thrice the original amount (₹1,75,500) from the commencement date of the Amendment Act.
Procedure 3: Enhancement of the revised annuity by twenty-five percent every five years thereafter.
administration: Law (Legislation-B) Department, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act came into force on the date of its enactment, September 27, 2023.
The revised annuity amount is specifically set at ₹1,75,500 and is subject to periodic enhancements.

title: THE SREE SANKARACHARYA UNIVERSITY OF SANSKRIT (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2018
purpose: To further amend the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit Act, 1994.
scope: Applies to the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as 'The Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (Amendment) Act, 2018' and states it came into force on 1st day of November, 2017.

Amends section 31 of the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit Act, 1994. It specifically addresses the retirement age of teachers. For teachers qualified as per UGC Regulations, retirement is at the end of the academic year in which they attain sixty years. Service benefits are governed by sub-rule (c) of rule 60 of Part I of the Kerala Service Rules. For non-teaching staff, officers, and other employees, the retirement age is the same as applicable to Government Service employees.

Repeals The Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (Amendment) Ordinance, 2018 (24 of 2018). It also states that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken or deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Teachers qualifying under UGC Regulations must retire at the end of the academic year in which they turn sixty.
Retirement age for non-teaching staff and officers is the same as for Government Service employees.
key_procedures: The Act came into force retrospectively from November 1, 2017.
The repeal of the Ordinance ensures continuity of actions taken under it.
administration: Law (Legislation-G) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: Short-term contract appointments are subject to the approval of the Selection Committee constituted in the manner prescribed in the Statutes.
The age limit for short-term contract appointments for a period not exceeding three years shall not apply.

title: THE TRAVANCORE-COCHIN HINDU RELIGIOUS INSTITUTIONS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2018
purpose: To further amend the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950 for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to Hindu Religious Institutions in the erstwhile Travancore-Cochin area, as amended by this Act.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions (Amendment) Act, 2018. Sections 2, 3 and 7 shall be deemed to have come into force on the 14th day of November, 2017 and the remaining provisions of this Act shall come into force at once.

In the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950 (Act XV of 1950) (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), in section 10, in sub-section (1), for the words "three years", the words "two years" shall be substituted.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 12.
main_sections.description: For section 12 of the principal Act, the following section shall be substituted, namely:- "12. Honoraria for President and members.—The President and members of the Board shall be entitled to receive per mensem, such honoraria and sitting fees, as may be fixed by the Government from time to time, by notification published in the Official Gazette."

After section 13A of the principal Act, the following section shall be inserted, namely:- "13B. Appointment of Devaswom Commissioner.—The Board shall appoint an officer not below the rank of a Deputy Commissioner who is eligible to be promoted as Devaswom Commissioner, and in the absence of such officer, an officer not below the rank of a Joint Secretary to Government, on deputation, as Devaswom Commissioner."
In sub-section (2) of section 29 of the principal Act, the words "who shall be appointed by the Board. He shall be a Hindu." shall be omitted.
In sub-section (1) of section 70 of the principal Act, for the words "three years", the words "two years" shall be substituted.

For sub-section (2) of section 71 of the principal Act, the following sub-section shall be substituted, namely:- "(2) The President and members of the Board shall be entitled to receive per mensem, such honoraria and sitting fees, as may be fixed by the Government from time to time, by notification published in the Official Gazette."

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 74A.
main_sections.description: For section 74A of the principal Act, the following section shall be substituted, namely:- "74A. Appointment of Devaswom Commissioner.—The Board shall appoint an officer not below the rank of a Deputy Commissioner who is eligible to be promoted as Devaswom Commissioner, and in the absence of such officer, an officer not below the rank of a Joint Secretary to Government, on deputation, as Devaswom Commissioner."

(1) The Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions (Amendment) Ordinance, 2018 (28 of 2018) is hereby repealed. (2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Sections 2, 3 and 7 of this Act are deemed to have come into force on 14th November 2017.
The President and members of the Board shall be entitled to receive honoraria and sitting fees as fixed by the Government.
The Board shall appoint a Devaswom Commissioner who is not below the rank of a Deputy Commissioner, or in their absence, a Joint Secretary on deputation.
The words "three years" in Section 10 and Section 70 of the principal Act are substituted with "two years".

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By notification published in the Official Gazette, and through actions taken under the Act.

rights: President and members of the Board are entitled to receive honoraria and sitting fees.
obligations: The Board shall appoint a Devaswom Commissioner of a certain rank or eligibility.

key_procedures: Amendment of specific sections of the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950.
Fixing of honoraria and sitting fees for the President and members of the Board by the Government.
Appointment of a Devaswom Commissioner by the Board.
Repeal and saving of previous ordinances related to the amendment.
administration: Law (Legislation-B) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The amendment aims to update provisions related to the term of office (reduced from three to two years in certain sections) and honoraria/sitting fees for Board members.
