The amendment clarifies the appointment process for the Devaswom Commissioner.
Provisions related to the Hindu faith of the appointing authority for the Board have been omitted.
The Act repeals the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions (Amendment) Ordinance, 2018, while saving actions taken under it.

title: THE KERALA APPROPRIATION ACT, 2020
purpose: To authorise payment and appropriation of certain further sums from and out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala for the services of the financial year 2019-2020.
scope: This act applies to the State of Kerala and governs the appropriation of funds from the Consolidated Fund of the State for the financial year 2019-2020. It covers various services and purposes as detailed in the Schedule.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Appropriation Act, 2020.

main_sections.section_title: Issue of ₹ 33038,87,61,000 from and out of the consolidated fund of the State of Kerala for the services of the financial year 2019-2020
main_sections.description: Authorizes the payment and application of sums not exceeding ₹ 33,038,87,61,000 from the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala for defraying charges for the services and purposes specified in the Schedule during the Financial Year 2019-2020.
States that the sums authorized to be paid and applied under this Act shall be appropriated for the services and purposes specified in the Schedule in relation to the Financial Year 2019-2020.

important_rules: Sums not exceeding those specified in column (3) of the Schedule, amounting in aggregate to ₹33,038,87,61,000, may be paid and applied from the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala.
These funds are for defraying several charges that will come in the course of payment during the Financial Year 2019-2020, in respect of services and purposes specified in column (2) of the Schedule.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be the State Government of Kerala through its financial and legislative processes.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the legislative process of passing the Appropriation Act and subsequent financial management by the State Government.

duties: The State Government has a duty to manage the Consolidated Fund of Kerala and to appropriate funds as authorized by this Act.
The Legislative Assembly has the role of voting on demands for grants, which are then appropriated by this Act.
obligations: To ensure that funds are disbursed and utilized for the specified services and purposes.
To adhere to the limits and allocations set forth in the Schedule.

key_procedures: The Governor of Kerala is pleased to authorize the publication of the Act's English translation.
The Act authorizes payment and appropriation of funds from the Consolidated Fund of the State.
The Schedule details the specific services and purposes for which funds are appropriated, including 'Voted by the Legislative Assembly' and 'Charged on the Consolidated Fund' amounts.
administration: The Law (Legislation-A) Department of the Government of Kerala is responsible for the notification and publication of this act.
important_notes: The Act specifies a total sum of ₹33,038,87,61,000 to be paid and applied from the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala.
The Schedule provides a detailed breakdown of the amounts appropriated for various services and purposes, categorized into 'Voted by the Legislative Assembly' and 'Charged on the Consolidated Fund'.

title: The Code Of Criminal Procedure (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1987
purpose: To amend the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, in its application to the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Code of Criminal Procedure (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1987. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 2nd day of December, 1974.

Amends section 11 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Central Act 2 of 1974). Inserts a new sub-section (1A) which empowers the State Government to establish special courts of Judicial Magistrates of First Class in specific areas or for specific classes of cases. Also amends sub-section (2) regarding the period of commencement.

Validates any notification issued by the State Government before the commencement of this Act, and before the commencement of the Code of Criminal Procedure (Amendment) Act, 1978, for establishing any special court of the Judicial Magistrate of the First Class having jurisdiction over more than one district, provided such notification is issued under section 11 of the said Code as amended by this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through establishment of special courts and notifications.

key_procedures: Establishment of special courts of Judicial Magistrates of First Class by the State Government for specific cases or areas.
Validation of previously issued notifications for establishing such courts.
administration: Law (Legislation-B) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The amendment is deemed to have come into force on December 2, 1974.
The Act is published by the authority of the Kerala Government.
The Act was passed by the Legislative Assembly and received the assent of the President on October 12, 1987.

title: THE ENGINEERING TECHNICIANS' CO-OPERATIVE SOCIETIES (ACQUISITION AND TRANSFER OF UNDERTAKINGS) ACT, 1977
purpose: To provide for the acquisition and transfer of the undertakings of the Kerala State Engineering Technicians (Workshop) Industrial Co-operative Society Limited, S. Ind (ST) No. 1 and the societies promoted by it and for matters connected thereto or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the undertakings of the Kerala State Engineering Technicians (Workshop) Industrial Co-operative Society Ltd., S. Ind (ST) No. 1 and societies promoted by it. The Act also applies to the Government of Kerala and the Planning Commission, as well as existing employees of the societies.

key_definitions.appointed day: The date on which this Act comes into force.
key_definitions.Director of Industries and Commerce: Means the Director of Industries and Commerce of the State of Kerala and includes any officer authorised by the Government to perform the functions of the Director of Industries and Commerce under this Act.
key_definitions.Engineering Technicians' Co-operative So: Means the ENCOS or any of the promoted societies.
key_definitions.member-employee: Means an employee of a society who has taken shares in the society for the purpose of securing employment in the service of the society.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.share: Means a share in the capital of the society.
key_definitions.company: Means any body and includes a firm or other association of individuals.
key_definitions.director: In relation to a firm, means a partner in the firm.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Engineering Technicians' Co-operative Societies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1977. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 17th day of March, 1977.

Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Director of Industries and Commerce', 'Engineering Technicians' Co-operative Society or 'society'', 'member-employee', 'prescribed', and 'share'.

main_sections.section_title: Undertakings of Engineering Technicians' Co-operative Societies to vest in the Government.
main_sections.description: Upon the 'appointed day', the undertakings of the Engineering Technicians' Co-operative Societies shall stand transferred to and vest in the Government. All rights, interests, and liabilities will also vest in the Government.

The vesting of undertakings includes all assets, rights, powers, authorities, and privileges, including lands, buildings, workshops, stores, instruments, machinery and equipment, cash balances, cash on hand, reserve fund, investments, and book debts. All contracts, agreements, and liabilities related to the undertakings also transfer. Any pending legal proceedings will continue against the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Duty to deliver possession of property acquired, and documents relating thereto.
main_sections.description: Every person in possession or custody of any property or document belonging to the vested undertakings must deliver it to the Government or any person authorised by the Government.

The Managing Director or any officer employed in connection with the undertakings must furnish a complete inventory of all properties and assets of the societies immediately after the appointed day. They must also furnish particulars of all liabilities and obligations.

main_sections.section_title: Termination of service of existing employees.
main_sections.description: The services of every officer or employee employed immediately before the appointed day in connection with the affairs of the societies shall stand terminated. However, they will be entitled to certain compensation or payment as prescribed.
Details the payment to be made to the shareholders of the societies and the interest payable on such amounts. It also covers the payment of loans obtained by member-employees.

Specifies penalties for contravention of the Act, including having possession, custody or control of property of the undertaking, or obtaining possession of property belonging to the undertaking. Penalties can also apply to companies for offences under this section.

States that if an offence under the Act is committed by a company, every person who was in charge of the company's affairs at the time shall be deemed guilty and liable for the offence, unless they can prove due diligence.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
main_sections.description: No suit, prosecution or other legal proceedings shall lie against the Government or any officer or other person for anything done or intended to be done under this Act.
The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make rules to carry out the provisions of this Act. Every rule made shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

The Engineering Technicians' Co-operative Societies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Ordinance, 1977 (12 of 1977), is hereby repealed. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been taken or done under this Act.

important_rules: All assets, rights, powers, authorities and privileges of the vested undertakings shall stand transferred to and vest in the Government.

All contracts and working arrangements subsisting immediately before the appointed day and affecting any of the societies shall, in so far as they relate to the undertaking of that society, cease to have effect or be enforceable against the society or any officer thereof, and shall be of as full force and effect against or in favour of the Government.
Every person in possession or custody of any property or document belonging to the vested undertakings must deliver it to the Government or its authorised representative.
The Managing Director or any officer employed in connection with the undertakings must furnish a complete inventory of properties and assets, and particulars of liabilities and obligations.
Employees' services are terminated, but they are entitled to compensation or payment.
Rules made by the Government under this Act must be laid before the Legislative Assembly.
Any action taken in good faith under this Act is protected from legal proceedings.

penalties: Punishable with imprisonment which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
In the case of a company, deemed guilty of the offence and liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly.
If proves that the offence was committed without his knowledge or that he had exercised all due diligence to prevent the commission of such offence.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through penalties for contravention of the Act, including imprisonment and fines. Enforcement is also implied through the vesting of undertakings in the Government and the powers granted to the Government to make rules.

rights: Shareholders are entitled to receive an amount equal to the value of their shares.
Member-employees who have obtained a loan from any bank for purchase of shares are entitled to receive balance payment.
Employees whose services are terminated are entitled to compensation or payment.
Protection from legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith.
duties: Duty to deliver possession of acquired property and documents to the Government.
Duty to furnish particulars of properties, assets, liabilities, and obligations of the societies.
Duty to comply with rules made by the Government.
obligations: Obligation to transfer undertakings to the Government.
Obligation to hand over all documents and records related to the undertakings.
Obligation for companies to ensure officers and employees comply with the Act.

key_procedures: Upon the appointed day, the undertakings of the societies vest in the Government.
All assets, liabilities, and contracts transfer to the Government.
Persons in possession of property or documents must deliver them to the Government.
The Managing Director must provide an inventory of assets and liabilities.
Employee services are terminated, with provisions for compensation.
Payment of an amount to shareholders and loan repayment for member-employees.
Penalties are prescribed for offences under the Act.
The Government can make rules, which must be laid before the Legislative Assembly.
administration: The Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on March 17, 1977.
The Ordinance of 1977 is repealed, but actions taken under it are saved.
The Government has the power to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act.
No suit, prosecution, or legal proceedings lie against the Government or its officers for acts done in good faith under the Act.

title: THE GURUVAYOOR DEVASWOM (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2001
purpose: An Act further to amend the Guruvayoor Devaswom Act, 1978. The preamble states it is expedient to amend the Guruvayoor Devaswom Act, 1978, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: The Act applies to the Guruvayoor Devaswom and related matters as amended by this Act.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Guruvayoor Devaswom (Amendment) Act, 2001, and it shall come into force at once.
Amends Section 5 of the Guruvayoor Devaswom Act, 1978, by substituting the words 'two years' with 'four years'.

Inserts a new Section 6A after Section 6 of the principal Act. This new section details the role and powers of the Commissioner. The Commissioner will be in charge of the Committee, and their term will be subject to the provisions related to clause (d) or clause (e) of sub-section (1) of Section 4 or by resignation or otherwise. If the vacancy in the Committee is filled, the remaining members cannot constitute a quorum for a meeting of the Committee. The Commissioner shall hold charge and exercise the powers and perform the functions of the Committee until the vacancy is filled as provided in this Act to constitute the quorum.
Amends Section 7 of the principal Act, substituting the words 'three members' with 'four members'.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided sections, but the Commissioner seems to be the primary enforcement/administrative figure for the Committee.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions outlined in the amended Act, particularly regarding the functions and powers of the Commissioner and the Committee.

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act: The Act comes into force immediately upon enactment.
Amendment of existing sections: Specific sections of the Guruvayoor Devaswom Act, 1978, are amended by substituting or inserting new text.
Appointment and role of Commissioner: The process and implications of appointing a Commissioner and managing Committee vacancies are outlined.
Constitution of the Committee: Rules regarding the quorum and the effect of vacancies on the Committee's ability to meet.
administration: Guruvayoor Devaswom
important_notes: The amendment regarding the Commissioner's tenure and role is a significant addition.
The increase in the number of members required for the Committee from 'three' to 'four' is another key change.
A footnote clarifies that the assent of the Governor was received on the 29th December 2001, and the Act was published in the Extraordinary Gazette No. 2092 dated 31-12-2001.

title: THE KERALA ELECTRICITY DUTY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1989
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Electricity Duty Act, 1963.
scope: Applies to electricity consumed in Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Electricity Duty (Amendment) Act, 1989 and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of August, 1988.
Specifies an amendment to the Schedule of the Kerala Electricity Duty Act, 1963 (23 of 1963), by substituting an entry in column (3) against item 4(b) to '10 paise per unit of energy consumed'.

Repeals the Kerala Electricity Duty (Amendment) Ordinance, 1988 (17 of 1988) and provides that nothing done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Electricity duty is to be charged at 10 paise per unit of energy consumed.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 31st day of January 1989 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 109 dated the 31st January 1989.
The Act is deemed to have come into force on 1st August 1988.

title: THE KERALA APPROPRIATION (No. 3) ACT, 1976
purpose: To provide for the authorisation of appropriation of moneys out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala to meet the amounts spent on certain services during the financial year ended on the 31st day of March, 1968, in excess of the amounts granted for those services and for that year.
scope: The act applies to the State of Kerala and concerns the appropriation of funds from its Consolidated Fund for specific services during the financial year ending March 31, 1968.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Appropriation (No. 3) Act, 1976.

main_sections.section_title: Issue of Rs 43,00,171 out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala to meet certain excess expenditure for the year ended on the 31st March, 1968
main_sections.description: Authorises the issue of Rs. 43,00,171 from the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala to meet excess expenditure for the year ended March 31, 1968. This amount is specified in column (3) of the Schedule, amounting to forty-three lakhs, one hundred and seventy-one rupees.

States that the sums deemed to have been authorised to be paid and applied from and out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala under this Act shall be deemed to have been appropriated for the services and purposes expressed in the Schedule in relation to the financial year ended on the 31st day of March, 1968.

important_notes: *Received the assent of the Governor on the 22nd day of May, 1976 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No 314, dated 24th May, 1976.

title: The Kerala Appropriation (No. 6) Act, 1970
purpose: To provide for the authorisation of appropriation of moneys out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala to meet the amounts spent or to be spent on certain services during the financial year ended on the 31st day of March, 1968, in excess of the amounts granted for those services and for that year.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and the expenditure incurred during the financial year ending March 31, 1968.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Appropriation (No. 6) Act, 1970.

main_sections.section_title: Issue of Rs 51,66,982 out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala to meet certain excess expenditure for the year ended on the 31st March, 1968.
main_sections.description: Authorises the issue of Rs 51,66,982 from the Consolidated Fund of Kerala to cover excess expenditure for the financial year ending March 31, 1968.
This section, indicated by a dash, likely signifies the formal appropriation of the amounts mentioned in Section 2.

important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 326, dated 30th November 1970.

title: The Kerala Decentralisation of Powers Act, 2000
purpose: The act aims to decentralize powers to local authorities and bodies in Kerala. It details the composition, functions, and powers of various authorities and committees involved in this decentralization process, particularly focusing on education and local governance.
scope: The act applies to the state of Kerala and concerns the decentralization of powers related to local self-government and educational administration.

key_definitions.local authority: Means any person legally entitled to the control or management of any local fund or legally entitled to impose any cess, rate, duty, fee or tax and includes the Panchayat or the Council of the Municipality, as the case may be, and also includes the Secretary of such local authority if he has been specifically authorised by the local authority for discharging the duties and functions under this Act.
key_definitions.Explanation (Local authority): A person means and includes any authority or body corporate.

main_sections.description: This section outlines the composition of the District Educational Authority, specifying the roles of the District Panchayat President, Chairperson of the standing committee for Health and Education, nominated members from various bodies and agencies, and the Deputy Director of Education.

main_sections.section_title: Functions of the District Educational Authority
main_sections.description: Details the functions of the District Educational Authority, including assessing educational needs, supervising schemes related to health and school children, and promoting educational activities.

This section establishes the Educational Development Committee, defining its role in considering and making proposals for the welfare needs of each school. It also specifies substitutions for terms like 'Government' and 'Education Department'.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment to Kerala Government Land Assignment Act, 1960
main_sections.description: This section amends the Kerala Government Land Assignment Act, 1960, by inserting provisions regarding the assignment of Government land for public purpose without consulting the local authority in certain cases.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment to Kerala Survey and Boundaries Act, 1961
main_sections.description: This section amends the Kerala Survey and Boundaries Act, 1961, regarding the survey and demarcation of lands belonging to the local authority and the procedure for notification to the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment to Kerala Cattle Trespass Act, 1961
main_sections.description: This section amends the Kerala Cattle Trespass Act, 1961, by making substitutions for the term 'local authority'.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment to Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1961
main_sections.description: This section amends the Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1961, by introducing provisions related to entertainment tax, including rates and the definition of 'local authority'.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment to Kerala Places of Public Resort Act, 1963
main_sections.description: This section amends the Kerala Places of Public Resort Act, 1963, making substitutions in provisions related to authority for application and appeal.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment to Kerala Local Authorities Loans Act, 1963
main_sections.description: This section amends the Kerala Local Authorities Loans Act, 1963, by making substitutions for the term 'local authority'.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment to Kerala Land Development Act, 1964
main_sections.description: This section amends the Kerala Land Development Act, 1964, by inserting definitions for 'Board', 'Collector', and 'District Committee'.

important_rules: The term of office of members of the District Educational Authority other than the functional members of local authorities and ex-officio members shall be five years from the date of the first meeting of the District Educational Authority.
An outgoing member shall continue in office until the election or nomination, as the case may be, of his successor.
The election of the members of the District Educational Authority shall be conducted in such manner as may be prescribed.

The term of office of a member elected or nominated to fill a casual vacancy shall be for so long only as the member whose place has been filled would have been entitled to hold office if the vacancy had not occurred.
It shall be lawful for the District Educational Authority to exercise its powers under this Act notwithstanding any vacancy in the Authority.

Government land assignable for public purpose may be assigned under section (1) without consulting the local authority as defined in the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 (13 of 1994) or the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994 (20 of 1994) as the case may be, and if such local authority requires such land, for carrying out any of the functions assigned to it, Government may set apart such land for that purpose.

Whenever a local authority as defined in the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 (13 of 1994) or the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994 (20 of 1994) requests the Government for surveying and demarcating the boundaries of any land vested or owned by it, the Government or any officer or authority authorised by the Government in this behalf, by notification in the Gazette shall get the land surveyed and demarcated.
Pounds may be established at such places in each village Panchayat or municipality if the local authority so decides.
Any pound established in one local authority may be used by the adjacent local authority subject to the conditions as may be mutually agreed by the local authorities concerned.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Local authorities, District Educational Authority, Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the respective authorities, prescribed procedures, notifications, and potential legal actions as implied by the amendments to various acts.

rights: Right to request survey and demarcation of land from the Government.
Right to establish pounds.
Right to manage educational development and welfare needs of schools.
duties: Duty to assess educational needs of the district.
Duty to supervise schemes related to health and school children.
Duty to promote educational activities.
Duty to arrange adequate toilet and drinking water facilities in schools.
Duty to ensure the proper functioning and management of local authorities and educational bodies.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to prescribed procedures for elections and nominations to authorities.
Obligation to comply with the conditions of land assignment and survey notifications.

key_procedures: Election and nomination of members to the District Educational Authority in a prescribed manner.
Procedure for surveying and demarcating lands belonging to local authorities upon request.
Procedure for assigning Government land for public purposes.
Procedure for establishing and using pounds by local authorities.
administration: Various local authorities, District Educational Authority, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: Certain sections make substitutions in existing acts, indicating a need to refer to the original acts for complete context.
The act is amended by subsequent legislation, as indicated by references to specific amendment acts and years.
Explanations are provided for key terms like 'local authority' and 'escaped tax' within the amending sections.

title: The Kerala Electricity Duty (Amendment) Act, 1969
purpose: To amend the Kerala Electricity Duty Act, 1963, for the purposes therein appearing.
scope: Applies to persons consuming energy and licensees in Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Electricity Duty (Amendment) Act, 1969, and shall come into force on such date as the Government may by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

Inserts a new section 5A concerning persons consuming energy generated by themselves to install a meter at such point and in such manner as may be prescribed and shall maintain it at all times in proper order.

Amends section 8 of the principal Act by omitting the word "and" in clause (i) at the end, and in clause (ii) at the end, and inserting a new clause (iii) stating "If the sum was payable by a person who consumed energy generated by himself, from such person."

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 9
main_sections.description: Substitutes section 9 of the principal Act. New section 9 covers penalties: (1) If any licensee fails to keep books of accounts or to submit returns as required by section 6, he shall be punishable with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees. (2) If any licensee or other person intentionally obstructs an Inspecting Officer appointed under section 7 in the performance of his duties or in the exercise of his powers under this Act or the rules made thereunder, he shall be punishable with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees.

Amends section 11 of the principal Act by renumbering sub-section (1) as sub-section (2), and inserting a new sub-section (2) stating that the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, exempt any consumer from the payment of the whole or any portion of the electricity duty payable on energy generated and consumed by him during periods when there is failure of supply of energy by the licensee or there is only a restricted supply of energy by the licensee, as the case may be.

In section 13 of the principal Act, in sub-section (2), after clause (a), the following clause shall be inserted, namely – "(aa) the point at which, and the manner in which, a meter shall be installed as required by section 5A";

Amends the Schedule to the principal Act, after item 4, the following item shall be inserted, namely – "5 Consumers who generate energy for their own consumption 12 paise per unit of energy generated and consumed."

important_rules: Rule 1: Consumers generating their own energy must install and maintain a meter as prescribed.
Rule 2: Licensees failing to keep accounts or submit returns are punishable with fine.
Rule 3: Obstructing an Inspecting Officer is punishable with fine.

penalties: Fine up to one thousand rupees for failure to keep books of accounts or submit returns.
Fine up to one thousand rupees for obstructing an Inspecting Officer.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Inspecting Officer appointed under section 7 of the principal Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through penalties (fines) and other powers vested in the Inspecting Officer.

rights: Right for the Government to exempt consumers from electricity duty under specific conditions (e.g., energy supply failure).
duties: Duty for consumers generating their own energy to install and maintain a meter.
Duty for licensees to keep books of accounts and submit returns.
Duty for licensees and other persons not to obstruct Inspecting Officers.
obligations: Obligation for licensees to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Insertion of new section 5A requires consumers generating their own energy to install and maintain a meter.
Procedure 2: Substitution of section 9 outlines penalties for non-compliance by licensees and obstruction of Inspecting Officers.
Procedure 3: Amendment of section 11 allows the Government to exempt consumers from duty payments via notification.
Procedure 4: Amendment of the Schedule introduces a duty rate for consumers generating their own energy.
administration: The Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to The Kerala Electricity Duty Act, 1963.
The Act came into force on a date appointed by the Government by notification in the Gazette.
A new duty of 12 paise per unit of energy generated and consumed is introduced for consumers who generate their own energy.
The Government has the power to exempt consumers from duty under certain circumstances.

title: THE KERALA GENERAL SALES TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1983
purpose: To further amend the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala, amending the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.

main_sections.description: Provides that this Act may be called the Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 1983, and that clauses (a) and (b) of section 2 and sections 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1982, and the remaining provisions of this Act shall be deemed to have come into force on the 14th day of October, 1982.

Amends section 5 of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963 (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act). It substitutes certain phrases and inserts a new sub-section (3A) regarding tax liability of a dealer for sale of goods. It also provides for exceptions to this sub-section.
Amends section 5A of the principal Act by substituting specific monetary figures in sub-section (2) and sub-section (3).
Amends section 7 of the principal Act by substituting specific monetary figures.
Amends section 13 of the principal Act by substituting specific monetary figures in sub-section (1) and sub-section (2).
Amends section 17 of the principal Act by substituting specific monetary figures in sub-sections (4) and (5).
Omit section 18 of the principal Act.
Amends section 34 of the principal Act by omitting certain words, brackets, figures and sub-sections.

Amends the First Schedule to the principal Act by substituting serial numbers, figures, and descriptions of goods and their tax liability at the point of first sale. It includes various categories of goods like synthetic rubber, plastics, artificial silk yarn, staple fibre yarn, paints, colours, varnishes, pigments, polishes, indigo, enamel, putty, balc oil, white oil, turpentine oil, thinners, emers, paint brushes, Dicalcium Phosphate, Grinders, mixers, hot plates, water heaters, washing machines, cooking ranges, domestic electric appliances, plastics and articles made of plastics, synthetic materials other than plastics, and plastic pipes.

Amends the Third Schedule to the principal Act by omitting serial number 11A and the entry relating thereto, and by inserting a new entry relating to 'Slates and slate pencils' and 'Tapioca and its products' at the end.

Repeals the Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 1982 (3 of 1982) and provides that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be the sales tax authorities responsible for administering the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amendments to existing sections and schedules of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, which includes assessment, collection, and penalties for non-compliance.

duties: Dealers are liable to tax at a rate higher than four per cent, for sale of goods mentioned in the First Schedule.
Dealers are required to declare goods filled in and signed by them to the assessing authority.
obligations: To comply with the provisions of the amended Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.

key_procedures: Dealers selling goods specified in the First Schedule are liable to tax at a specified rate. If the goods are not component parts, the tax is at the rate of only four per cent on the taxable turnover relating to such industrial raw materials or packing materials.

The provisions of this sub-section shall not apply to any sale unless the dealer selling the goods furnishes to the assessing authority in the prescribed manner a declaration duly filled in and signed by the dealer to whom the goods are sold containing the prescribed particulars in the prescribed form.
administration: Sales Tax Department of the Kerala Government.
important_notes: The Act came into force on different dates for different provisions.
Received the assent of the Governor on the 6th day of April, 1983 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No 407 dated the 7th April, 1983.

title: THE KERALA LAND DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION LIMITED (SPECIAL POWERS) AMENDMENT ACT, 1977
purpose: To amend The Kerala Land Development Corporation Limited (Special Powers) Act, 1974.
scope: Applies to The Kerala Land Development Corporation Limited.

key_definitions.appellate authority: an officer not below the rank of Deputy Collector, appointed by the Government to be an appellate authority for the purposes of this Act.
key_definitions.Inquiring Officer: an officer appointed as such by the Corporation or by the Government or by an officer authorised by the Government in this behalf.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Land Development Corporation Limited (Special Powers) Amendment Act, 1977.
Amends section 2 of the Kerala Land Development Corporation Limited (Special Powers) Act, 1974, by re-lettering clause (a) to (aa) and inserting a new clause (aa) which defines 'appellate authority'.

Amends section 3 of the principal Act by omitting sub-section (1), clause (c) shall be omitted. In sub-section (2), for the words "the Corporation shall appoint an Officer called the Inquiring Officer", the words "the Corporation or the Government or an Officer authorised by the Government in this behalf shall appoint an Inquiring Officer" shall be substituted.

Amends section 5 of the principal Act, in sub-section (2), the words "in a newspaper which, in the opinion of the Corporation, has the widest circulation in the locality", the words "in two or more newspapers having wide circulation in the locality as may be determined by the Corporation" shall be substituted.

Amends section 14 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), clause (e) is substituted with "the principles of apportionment of the cost of such works", and clause (h) is substituted with restrictions on owners regarding use of land.
Inserts new sections 14A and 14B after section 14 of the principal Act. Section 14A deals with interim payment of cost and Section 14B deals with additional liability to be apportioned among owners.

Amends section 16 of the principal Act. In section 16, in sub-section (1), the following sub-sections shall be substituted: (a) any owner or person liable under section 10 to pay cost or part of cost of any work or to pay any amount by way of contribution, who objects to such liability, or any owner or other person who is aggrieved by any decision of the Corporation under sub-section (4) of section 14 or under sub-section (3) of section 15, may, within such time as may be prescribed, appeal to the appellate authority. (1a) On receipt of an appeal under sub-section (1), the appellate authority shall, after giving the appellant and the Corporation a reasonable opportunity of being heard either in person or by a representative pass such order on the appeal as it deems fit.

Inserts new sections 21A and 21B after section 21 of the principal Act. Section 21A relates to delegation of powers and functions of the Corporation. Section 21B relates to execution of agreement for certain purposes.

The Kerala Land Development Corporation Limited (Special Powers) Amendment Ordinance, 1977, is repealed. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act, as if this Act had come into force on the 21st day of February, 1977.

important_rules: The following sub-sections shall be substituted: '(a) any owner or person liable under section 10 to pay the cost or part of the cost of any work or to pay any amount by way of contribution, who objects to such liability, or any owner or other person who is aggrieved by any decision of the Corporation under sub-section (4) of section 14 or under sub-section (3) of section 15, may, within such time as may be prescribed, appeal to the appellate authority.'

On receipt of an appeal under sub-section (1), the appellate authority shall, after giving the appellant and the Corporation a reasonable opportunity of being heard either in person or by a representative pass such order on the appeal as it deems fit.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Appellate Authority (appointed by the Government)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Appeals process for decisions related to cost apportionment and land use.

rights: Right to appeal against decisions of the Corporation regarding liability or cost apportionment.
duties: Owners benefited by any work under section 14A shall pay the cost of such work.
Any amount paid under sub-section (1) of section 14 shall be adjusted towards the cost payable by him under section 10.
obligations: Every owner benefited by any work shall pay the cost of such work.

key_procedures: Appeal process: An owner or person liable for cost, or aggrieved by a decision, can appeal to the appellate authority within a prescribed time.
Hearing of appeals: The appellate authority must give the appellant and the Corporation a reasonable opportunity of being heard before passing an order.
administration: The Kerala Land Development Corporation Limited
important_notes: The Amendment Act is to be read with The Kerala Land Development Corporation Limited (Special Powers) Act, 1974.
The repeal and saving clause indicates that actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are valid as if taken under the amended Act.
The Amendment Act came into force on the 21st day of February, 1977.

title: The Kerala Municipalities (Second Amendment) Act, 1987
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960, for the purposes hereafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Municipalities in Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Municipalities (Second Amendment) Act, 1987. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 26th day of September, 1987.

In the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960 (14 of 1961), in section 7, for sub-section (6), the following sub-section shall be substituted, namely: "(6) Three seats shall be reserved for women in the Council."
In amendment of section 54A of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), for the words "two years", the words "thirty months" shall be substituted.

In section 67 of the principal Act, the marginal heading shall be substituted with "Prohibition of public meetings on the day preceding the election day and on the election day.". For sub-section (1), the following sub-section shall be substituted, namely: "(1) No person shall convene, hold or attend any public meeting within the municipal area in connection with an election to the Corporation during the period of forty-eight hours ending with the hour fixed for the conclusion of the poll in that area."
In section 344 of the principal Act, in sub-section (2), the proviso to clause (b) shall be omitted.
In section 412 of the principal Act, in sub-section (2), for the words "one hundred and fourteen months", the words "one hundred and twenty months" shall be substituted.

Section 4 of the Local Authorities Laws (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1987 (5 of 1987), is hereby repealed. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said section shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Rule: Three seats shall be reserved for women in the Council.
Rule: The period of "two years" in section 54A(1) is substituted with "thirty months".

Rule: Prohibition of public meetings on the day preceding the election day and on the election day. No person shall convene, hold or attend any public meeting within the municipal area in connection with an election to the Corporation during the period of forty-eight hours ending with the hour fixed for the conclusion of the poll in that area.
administration: Law (Legislation-C) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on 26th September, 1987.
The Act amends The Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960.
Section 4 of the Local Authorities Laws (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1987 is repealed and saved.
Any action taken under the repealed section is deemed to have been taken under this Act.

title: THE KERALA PANCHAYATS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1967
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Panchayats (Amendment) Act, 1967. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint; and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Act.
In section 5 of the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960 (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), the proviso to sub-section (3) shall be omitted.

For section 8 of the principal Act, the following section shall be substituted: "8. Reservation of seats for women. (1) In every Panchayat there shall be reserved one seat for women in such ward as has the largest number of women electors among the wards in the Panchayat. (2) The Government or any officer authorised by the Government in this behalf shall specify the ward for the purposes of sub-section (1) : Provided that before specifying such ward, the Government or such officer, as the case may be, shall publish, in such manner as may be prescribed by notice in the prescribed form, inviting objections and suggestions in the matter and consider the objections and suggestions, if any, so received. (3) Nothing contained in sub-section (1) shall be deemed to prevent women from standing for election to the non-reserved seats in the Panchayat."

In section 10 of the principal Act, (1) for sub-section (3), the following sub-section shall be substituted, namely :-" (3) The ward in which a seat is reserved under section 7 or section 8, shall in addition to a member for the non-reserved seat, elect a member for the reserved seat. Explanation. --Where the seat reserved under section 7 is in the ward in which a seat is reserved under section 8, that ward shall elect members for both the reserved seats in addition to a member for the non-reserved seat. " ; (2) in sub-section (5), after the word and figure "section 7", the words and figure "or for women under section 8" shall be inserted; (3) in sub-section (6), for the words "the other vote", the words "the other vote or votes, as the case may be," shall be substituted.

In section 54 of the principal Act, (a) in sub-section (3), after the words "Any officer of the Government", the words "not below the rank of District Panchayat Officer" shall be inserted; (b) for sub-sections (4), (5) and (6), the following sub-sections shall be substituted, namely :- " (4) The officer authorised under sub-section (3) shall preside at the meeting convened under this section : Provided that, if such officer is unable to preside at the meeting on medical grounds, an officer not below the rank of Tahsildar authorised by the District Panchayat Officer in this behalf shall preside at the meeting.

In sub-section (1) of section 57 of the principal Act, — (a) in clause (a), for the words, "the roads of the Malabar District Board", the words "or district roads" shall be substituted; (b) after clause (l), the following clause shall be inserted, namely :- " (m) maintenance of the Village Court established for the Panchayat area, by providing accommodation, necessary staff and funds for meeting contingent expenditure."

In section 62 of the principal Act, — (a) in sub-section (1), — (i) for the words "and the roads of the Malabar District Board", the words "or district roads" shall be substituted; (ii) for the words "shall vest in the Panchayat", the words "shall stand transferred to, and vest in, the Panchayat" shall be substituted; (b) after sub-section (1), the following sub-section shall be inserted, namely :- " (1A) Subject to the provisions of this Act, all rights and liabilities of the Government in relation to the public roads and other properties, materials and things vested in the Panchayat under sub-section (1) or sub-section (3), shall, from the date of such vesting, be the rights and liabilities of the Panchayat."; (c) in sub-section (2), — (i) for the words "The Government may", the words, brackets, figures and letter "Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1A), the Government may" shall be substituted; (ii) the following proviso shall be inserted at the end, namely :- " Provided that, before issuing such a notification, the Government shall consult the Panchayat concerned and give due regard to its objections, if any."

In section 82 of the principal Act, — (a) in sub-section (1), for the words "shall vest in the Panchayat and be subject to its control", the words "shall stand transferred to, and vest in, the Panchayat" shall be substituted; (b) after sub-section (1), the following sub-section shall be inserted, namely :- " (1) Subject to the provisions of this Act, all rights and liabilities of the Government in relation to the watercourses, springs, reservoirs, tanks, cisterns, fountains, wells, standpipes and other water works vested in the Panchayat under sub-section (1) shall, from the date of such vesting, be the rights and liabilities of the Panchayat."; (c) for sub-section (2), the following sub-section shall be substituted, namely :- " (2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1A), the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, assume the administration of any public source of water supply and public land adjacent and appertaining thereto after consulting the Panchayat and giving due regard to its objections, if any."
The word "nominated" shall be omitted.

key_procedures: Specifying wards for reservation of seats for women by the Government or authorized officer, involving publication of notice, inviting objections, and consideration of suggestions.
Election of members for reserved and non-reserved seats in wards where reservations apply.
Procedures for presiding over meetings by authorized officers or their substitutes in case of inability to attend.
Substitution of specific wording in various sections regarding roads, transfer of property, and government rights and liabilities.
Government assumption of administration of public water sources after consulting the Panchayat and considering objections.
important_notes: Published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 178, dated 5th September, 1967.

title: THE KERALA PANCHAYATS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1987
purpose: To amend the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960 for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960.

main_sections.description:
(1) This Act may be called the Kerala Panchayats (Amendment) Act, 1987.
(2) It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 26th day of September, 1987.

In the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960 (32 of 1960) (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), in section 8: 
(i) for sub-section (1), the following sub-section shall be substituted, namely:--
"(1) In every Panchayat there shall be reserved two seats for women.";
(ii) in sub-section (2) and in the proviso thereto, for the word "ward", the word, "wards" shall be substituted.

In section 99 of the principal Act:--
(i) for the marginal heading, the following marginal heading shall be substituted, namely:--
"Prohibition of public meetings on the preceding election day and on the election day.";
(ii) for sub-section (1), the following sub-section shall be substituted, namely:--
"(1) No person shall convene, hold or attend any public meeting within the Panchayat area in connection with an election to that Panchayat during the period of forty-eight hours ending with the hour fixed for the conclusion of the poll."

(1) Section 3 of the Local Authorities Laws (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1987 (5 of 1987), is hereby repealed.
(2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said section shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Two seats shall be reserved for women in every Panchayat.

No person shall convene, hold or attend any public meeting within the Panchayat area in connection with an election to that Panchayat during the period of forty-eight hours ending with the hour fixed for the conclusion of the poll.

obligations: To comply with the prohibition of public meetings before and on election day.

administration: Law (Legislation-C) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on the 26th day of September, 1987.
Anything done or action taken under the principal Act as amended by the repealed Ordinance is deemed valid under this Act.

title: The Kerala Public Libraries (Kerala Granthasala Sanghom) Amendment Act, 1991
purpose: To amend the Kerala Public Libraries (Kerala Granthasala Sanghom) Act, 1989.
scope: Applies to Kerala Public Libraries and the Kerala Granthasala Sanghom.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Public Libraries (Kerala Granthasala Sanghom) Amendment Act, 1991, and shall come into force at once.

Substitutes Section 39 of the principal Act (Kerala Public Libraries (Kerala Granthasala Sanghom) Act, 1989). The substituted section deals with the Board of Control, its remaining in office for a certain period, its dissolution upon notification, and the management of properties vested in the Board. It also details the procedure for conducting the first election to the Councils and Unions referred to in sub-section (1) of the substituted section, and the terms of office, salaries, allowances, and other conditions of service of the members of the Committee.

Amends Section 50 of the principal Act by substituting sub-section (2). The substituted sub-section states that notwithstanding any repeal, the Board of Control appointed by order made under the Kerala Granthasala Sanghom (Taking over of Management) Act, 1977, shall remain in office till a Committee under sub-section (1) of section 39 of this Act is appointed.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government, Board of Control, Committee, Councils, Unions
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through orders issued by the Government and the Committee, and elections.

rights: Right to conduct elections to Councils and Unions.
Right to manage properties vested in the Board of Control.
duties: Duty to comply with directions issued by the Government.
obligations: Members of the Committee are subject to conditions prescribed by the Government regarding their functions, salaries, allowances, and other conditions of service.

key_procedures: Procedure for conducting the first election to the Councils and Unions referred to in sub-section (1) of the substituted Section 39.
Procedure for the dissolution of the Board of Control upon notification.
Procedure for the administration of properties vested in the Board of Control.
administration: Government, Board of Control, Committee
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 12th day of November, 1991 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 1368 dated the 13th November 1991.
The provisions regarding the Board of Control and its dissolution are dependent on Government notification.

title: THE KERALA LAND DEVELOPMENT (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1976
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala Land Development Act, 1964, for the purposes herein-after appearing.
scope: The Act applies to the Kerala Land Development Act, 1964 and its amendments.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Land Development (Amendment) Act, 1976, and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint. It also notes that it received the assent of the Governor on the 28th day of November, 1976 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 701, dated 9th December, 1976.

This section amends section 3 of the Kerala Land Development Act, 1964. It specifies that in sub-section (2), after item (aa), a new item '(aaa) the Secretary to Government, Agriculture Department, ex officio,;' shall be inserted, and item (e) shall be substituted with 'the Director of Agriculture (Soil Conservation Unit), ex officio,;'. It also states that in sub-section (3), the words 'Director of Soil Conservation' shall be substituted with 'Director of Agriculture (Soil Conservation Unit)'.

This section amends section 6 of the principal Act. It states that in sub-section (1), in item (b), the words 'District Agricultural Officer' shall be substituted with 'District Soil Conservation Officer'.
This section amends section 13 of the principal Act, substituting the words 'a District Agricultural Officer' with 'District Soil Conservation Officer'.

This section amends section 20 of the principal Act. For sub-section (1), the following sub-sections shall be substituted: '(1) The Executing Officer or the Padasekharam Committee, as the case may be, executing the work, shall, as soon as may be after the completion of the work in any land included in a scheme, prepare a statement setting out— (a) the name of the owner of such land, (b) the nature and extent of the work carried out in such land, (c) the total amount to be recovered from the owner, (d) the period within which such amount is to be recovered; (e) the person or persons liable to maintain and repair the work; and (f) the rights, if any, of the owner as regards the use of the work; and (g) such other matters as may be prescribed. (1A) The amount specified in the statement prepared under sub-section (1) as the total amount to be recovered from the owner shall be liable to be enhanced or reduced if on the apportionment of the total cost of the scheme among the beneficiaries it is found that such amount is less or more than the amount due from such owner. (1B) The statement prepared under sub-section (1) shall be communicated by the Executing Officer or the Padasekharam Committee, as the case may be, to the owner of the land in which the work has been carried out.'.

rights: Rights of the owner as regards the use of the work (as may be prescribed).
duties: Duty to maintain and repair the work (by the person or persons liable).
obligations: Obligation to pay the total amount to be recovered from the owner for work done in their land, within a specified period.

key_procedures: Preparation of a statement by the Executing Officer or Padasekharam Committee after completion of work, detailing owner's name, work nature and extent, recovery amount, payment period, maintenance liability, and owner's rights.
Communication of the prepared statement to the land owner.
Potential enhancement or reduction of the recovered amount based on apportionment of scheme costs among beneficiaries.
administration: Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on 28th November 1976 and was published on 9th December 1976.
Amendments are made to The Kerala Land Development Act, 1964.
Certain officials' designations and departments are amended or substituted.

title: The Madras Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (Amendment) Act, 1967
purpose: To further amend The Madras Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Act, 1951.
scope: Applies to Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments in the Malabar District as referred to in sub-section (2) of section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (Central Act 37 of 1956).

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Madras Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (Amendment) Act, 1967.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Madras Act XIX of 1951
main_sections.description: Amends section 29 of the Madras Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Act, 1951. Specifically, it modifies the proviso concerning the term of exceeding five years. It allows the Commissioner, under certain emergency or justifiable circumstances, to dispense with the prescribed procedure for sanction.

important_rules: Rule: The words "for a term exceeding five years" shall be omitted from sub-section (1) of section 29 of the principal Act.

Rule: After the omitted proviso, a new further proviso shall be inserted, stating that the Commissioner, if satisfied due to emergency or other reasons, may dispense with the procedure prescribed in the foregoing proviso, with the previous sanction of the Government.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Commissioner and Government (for sanction to dispense with procedure)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amendments to existing legislation and the exercise of powers by the Commissioner.

rights: Right of the Commissioner to dispense with procedure under specific conditions.
obligations: Obligation for the Commissioner to obtain previous sanction of the Government to dispense with procedure under emergency/special circumstances.

key_procedures: Procedure: Omission of specified words from section 29(1) of the principal Act.
Procedure: Insertion of a new proviso allowing the Commissioner to dispense with procedure under emergency/special circumstances with Government sanction.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be under the purview of the Commissioner and the Government concerning Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments.
important_notes: This Act is published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 151, dated 7th August, 1967.

title: THE PRE-DEGREE COURSE (ABOLITION) ACT, 1997
purpose: To abolish Pre-Degree Course in the State of Kerala in a phased manner commencing from the academic year 1997-98 and to provide for matters incidental or ancillary thereto.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala. Aims to abolish the Pre-Degree Course in Universities and other state governments in India have abolished Pre-Degree Course by accepting 10+2 system of school education. Aims to improve standards of higher education.

key_definitions.academic_year: A period of twelve months commencing from the first day of June and ending with the thirty first day of May of the following year.
key_definitions.Committee: The Empowered Committee constituted by sub-section (2) of section 3.
key_definitions.University_laws: Means the Kerala University Act, 1974 (17 of 1974), the Calicut University Act, 1975 (5 of 1975), the Mahatma Gandhi University Act, 1985 (12 of 1985) and the Kannur University Act, 1996 (22 of 1996) and the Statutes, Ordinances, Regulations, the rules and the byelaws made under the said Acts.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Pre-Degree Course (Abolition) Act, 1997. Clauses (c) and (d) of sub-section (2) of section 3 shall come into force at once and the remaining provisions of this Act shall be deemed to have come into force on the 3rd day of June, 1997.
Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, unless the context otherwise requires.

Notwithstanding anything contained in the University laws, or in any agreement or contract, with effect on and from the date of commencement of the Act, the Government reserve to themselves the right, by order, published in the Gazette, to prohibit the conduct of Pre-Degree Course or such number of batches of the said course in an academic year in such colleges, may be specified, the end. Students in such colleges may be specified. No college shall grant affiliation to the said course in such colleges and shall not affiliate the college which violates the prohibition contained in the said order. No college shall be specified in the order under sub-section (1) unless it is recommended by an Empowered Committee consisting of the Principal Secretary to Government, Higher Education Department – Chairman; the Vice-Chancellor of one of the Universities in the State nominated by the Government – Member; the Secretary to Government, General Education Department – Member; the Director of Collegiate Education–Member-Secretary; the Director of Public Instruction–Member; and the Director of Higher Secondary Education–Member.

The Committee shall meet at such time and place as may be determined by the Chairman. Meetings of the Committee shall be presided over by the Chairman and in his absence, by a Member chosen by the Members present from among themselves. The quorum for a meeting of the Committee shall be three. Decision of the Committee shall be taken by the majority of Members present at a meeting and where the Members divide equally, the decision of the Chairman shall prevail. Minutes of the meeting of the Committee shall be approved by the Chairman and all proceedings, orders and other instruments of the Committee, based on the minutes, shall be authenticated by the signature of the Member-Secretary. The procedure to be followed in a meeting shall be such, as may be determined by the Chairman.

Notwithstanding anything contained in the University laws or in any agreement or contract, no appointment of non-teaching staff in any University and no appointment of teaching and non-teaching staff in any college shall be made for a period of three years from the date of commencement of this Act. Provided that, in the exigencies of service, such appointment may be made, with the previous approval of the Committee.

The Pre-Degree Course (Abolition) Ordinance, 1997 (10 of 1997), is hereby repealed. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: No college shall grant affiliation to the Pre-Degree Course or such number of batches of the said course in an academic year in such colleges, may be specified.
No college shall be specified in the order under sub-section (1) unless it is recommended by an Empowered Committee.

No appointment of non-teaching staff in any University and no appointment of teaching and non-teaching staff in any college shall be made for a period of three years from the date of commencement of this Act, unless approved by the Committee.
Repealed the Pre-Degree Course (Abolition) Ordinance, 1997.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Empowered Committee
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Recommendation by the Empowered Committee for specifying colleges, and approval for appointments in exigencies.

obligations: Colleges must comply with the prohibition of conducting Pre-Degree Courses.
Colleges must not seek affiliation for the Pre-Degree Course.
Universities must adhere to the ban on appointing new staff for a period of three years.

key_procedures: Process for abolishing Pre-Degree Course: Government issues order prohibiting conduct, based on recommendation from Empowered Committee. Students in specified colleges may be specified.

Procedure for Committee meetings: Determined by the Chairman. Presided by Chairman or nominated Member. Quorum is three. Decisions by majority, Chairman decides ties. Minutes approved by Chairman and authenticated by Member-Secretary.
administration: Higher Education Department (implied by Principal Secretary to Government, Higher Education Department as Chairman of the Committee).
important_notes: The Act aims to align with the national policy of accepting 10+2 system of school education.
The Act is enacted in the Forty-eight year of the Republic of India.
The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 7th day of January 1998 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 52 dated 9th January 1998.

title: The Sree Pandaravaka Lands (Vesting and Enfranchisement) Amendment Act, 1977
purpose: To further amend the Sree Pandaravaka Lands (Vesting and Enfranchisement) Act, 1971.
scope: Applies to the Sree Pandaravaka Lands within the state of Kerala, amending provisions related to vesting and enfranchisement of these lands. Specifically, it amends Section 13 of the principal Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it is deemed to have come into force on August 1, 1975.
Amends the proviso to sub-section (1) of Section 13 of the principal Act (Act 20 of 1971) by substituting the words "four years" with "six years".

Repeals the Sree Pandaravaka Lands (Vesting and Enfranchisement) Amendment Ordinance, 1977 (10 of 1977). It also includes a saving clause stating that anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: The time period mentioned in the proviso to sub-section (1) of Section 13 of the principal Act is extended from four years to six years.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated in the provided text, but implied to be the authorities responsible for administering land laws in Kerala.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application of the amended provisions of the principal Act.

administration: Not explicitly stated in the provided text, but likely related to the land revenue or land reforms departments of the Kerala Government.
important_notes: The Act was received the assent of the President on the 12th day of August, 1977.
The Act was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary dated 12th August, 1977.
The Act is an amendment to the Sree Pandaravaka Lands (Vesting and Enfranchisement) Act, 1971 (Act 20 of 1971).

title: THE UNIVERSITY LAWS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2007 (ACT 24 OF 2007)
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala University Act, 1974, the Calicut University Act, 1975, the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit Act, 1994 and the Kannur University Act, 1996.
scope: Applies to the Kerala University Act, 1974, the Calicut University Act, 1975, the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit Act, 1994, and the Kannur University Act, 1996.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the University Laws (Amendment) Act, 2007, and it came into force on the 5th day of February, 2005.
Amends the Kerala University Act, 1974, by inserting a provision to nominate a member to the State Higher Education Council.
Amends the Calicut University Act, 1975, by inserting a provision to nominate a member to the State Higher Education Council.
Amends the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit Act, 1994, by inserting a provision to nominate a member to the State Higher Education Council.
Amends the Kannur University Act, 1996, by inserting a provision to nominate a member to the State Higher Education Council.

Repeals the University Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 2007 (46 of 2007), except for Section 5. It also states that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the respective University Acts prior to this Act shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_notes: Received the assent of Governor on the 13th October, 2007 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No 1858 dated 15th October, 2007.
Section 6(2) clarifies that notwithstanding the repeal of the Ordinance, actions taken under the previous Acts are considered valid.

title: The Abkari (Amendment) Act, 1997
purpose: To further amend the Abkari Act 1 of 1077 for the purposes specified within the Act, primarily focusing on changes to definitions, offences, penalties, and procedural aspects related to abkari (liquor) regulation and enforcement.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Kerala and amends the Abkari Act 1 of 1077. It governs the regulation of abkari (liquor) and related activities within the state. The scope extends to the definition of 'transit', procedures for arrest and seizure, offences, and penalties associated with abkari violations.

key_definitions.transit: The movement of goods from one place within a state to another place within that state or to any other state through the territory of the State of Kerala. 'State' in this definition refers to any state other than Kerala, including a Union Territory.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as 'The Abkari (Amendment) Act, 1997' and states that it is deemed to have come into force on June 3, 1997.
Substitutes clause (17A) in section 3 of the principal Act to redefine 'transit' and clarify the meaning of 'State' in that context.

Renumber s section 8 as sub-section (1) and inserts a new sub-section (2). It replaces the word 'transit' with 'without permit transit' in sub-section (1) and specifies penalties for contravening sub-section (1), including imprisonment up to ten years and a fine of at least one lakh rupees.
Omit s clause (o) of sub-section (2) of section 29 of the principal Act.
Omit s the words and figures 'section 55 or section 57 or section 58 of' from section 30 of the principal Act.
Omit s specific sections (including 8, 15C, 55, 55B, 56A, 57, 58, 58A, 58B) from section 31 of the principal Act and also omits the proviso.

In sub-section (1), substitutes 'Abkari Officer' for 'officer of the Excise Department or the Police Department' and 'this Act' for references to specific sections. It also substitutes sub-sections (2) and (3) with a new sub-section (2) stating that the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 applies to arrests, searches, and seizures under this Act, where not inconsistent.
Substitutes 'Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Central Act 2 of 1974)' for 'Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898' in section 36.

Replaces section 40 of the principal Act with new provisions regarding procedure on arrest and seizure, including informing the arrested person of grounds for arrest, entitlement to bail, and production of arrested persons and seized articles before the appropriate authority or officer.

Replaces section 41 and inserts a new section 41A. Section 41 deals with the disposal of arrested persons, including release on bail. Section 41A declares offences under this Act as cognizable and non-bailable, with specific limitations on granting bail for offences punishable with imprisonment of three years or more.
Substitutes 'Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Central Act 2 of 1974)' for 'Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898' in section 43.
Substitutes 'under this Act' for 'in the manner provided in section 40' in section 44.

Replaces section 50 and inserts section 50A. Section 50 mandates timely completion of investigations and forwarding of reports to the Magistrate. Section 50A outlines the procedure to be adopted by the Magistrate upon receipt of the report.

Amends section 55 by omitting certain phrases, changing 'shall on conviction before a Magistrate be punished' to 'shall be punishable', and increasing penalties for offences under clause (1) to ten years imprisonment and a fine of at least one lakh rupees.
Omit s section 55A of the principal Act.
Amends section 55B to increase the punishment to imprisonment up to five years and a fine of at least twenty-five thousand rupees.
Omit s clause (c) of section 56 of the principal Act.
Amends sub-section (1) of section 56A to increase punishment to five years imprisonment and a fine of at least fifty thousand rupees. Amends sub-section (2) to increase fine to five thousand rupees.
Amends section 57 to increase punishment to five years imprisonment or a fine of up to fifty thousand rupees or both.
Amends section 58 to increase punishment to ten years imprisonment and a fine of at least one lakh rupees.
Amends section 58A to increase punishment to five years imprisonment or a fine of up to fifty thousand rupees or both.
Amends section 58B to provide for imprisonment up to three years and a fine of up to twenty-five thousand rupees.
Amends section 59 to provide for imprisonment up to three years or a fine of up to twenty-five thousand rupees or both.
Amends section 60 to provide for a fine of up to ten thousand rupees or imprisonment for up to one year or both.
Amends section 61 to provide for a fine of up to twenty-five thousand rupees or imprisonment for up to three years or both.
Amends section 63 to provide for a fine of up to five thousand rupees or imprisonment for up to two years or both.
Amends section 64 by replacing references to section 55 with references to sections 55, 55B, 56A, 57, 58, 58A, and 58B.

important_rules: Rule: Any person contravening sub-section (1) of section 8 (regarding transit without permit) shall be punishable with imprisonment up to ten years and a fine of at least one lakh rupees.

Rule: Offences under this Act are declared cognizable and non-bailable. For offences punishable with imprisonment of three years or more, bail can only be granted if the Public Prosecutor has had an opportunity to oppose the application and the court is satisfied there are reasonable grounds to believe the accused is not guilty and will not commit offences while on bail.
Rule: Investigations into offences under this Act must be completed without unnecessary delay.
Rule: Abkari Officers must inform arrested persons of the grounds for arrest and their entitlement to bail if applicable.
Rule: Arrested persons and seized articles must be produced before the appropriate Magistrate or officer without unnecessary delay.

penalties: Contravention of transit without permit (Section 8(2)): Imprisonment up to ten years and a fine not less than one lakh rupees.

Offences under amended sections (e.g., 55, 55B, 56A, 57, 58, 58A, 58B, 59, 60, 61, 63, 64): Penalties vary, with increased terms of imprisonment (up to 3, 5, or 10 years) and significantly higher fines (ranging from ten thousand to one lakh rupees or more), often with imprisonment and fine as alternatives or in addition.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Abkari Officers, officers of the Excise Department or the Police Department, and competent courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through arrest, search, and seizure procedures as provided under the Act and the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. Investigations are conducted by Abkari Officers, and cases are prosecuted in competent courts.

rights: Right to be informed of grounds for arrest.
Right to be released on bail (subject to conditions and offence severity).
duties: Duty to obtain permits for transit.
Duty to cooperate with investigations and legal proceedings.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Abkari Act and its amendments.
Obligation for authorities to follow prescribed procedures for arrest, seizure, and production of accused persons.
