key_procedures: Procedure for arrest and seizure (Section 40): Includes informing the arrested person of grounds, entitlement to bail, and production before the appropriate authority without unnecessary delay.
Procedure for disposal of arrested persons (Section 41): Dictates release on bail or production before a Magistrate depending on the severity of the offence.
Procedure on receipt of report (Section 50A): Outlines how a Magistrate should inquire into an offence and proceed with the trial upon receiving a final report from an Abkari Officer.
administration: The Act is administered by the Excise Department of the Government of Kerala, with Abkari Officers playing a key role in enforcement.
important_notes: The Act is a retrospective amendment, deemed to have come into force on June 3, 1997.
The amendments significantly enhance penalties for abkari-related offences, reflecting a stricter stance on the regulation of liquor.
The Act extensively modifies the application of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, to align with abkari offences, particularly concerning arrest, search, seizure, and bail provisions.

title: THE ABKARI (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1973
purpose: To further amend the Abkari Act, I of 1077.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Abkari (Amendment) Act, 1973. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

In the Abkari Act, I of 1077, section 55A shall be re-lettered as section 55B and before that section, the following section shall be inserted, namely: "55A Magistrates of second class to have power to impose minimum penalties for certain first offences.—Notwithstanding anything contained in section 32 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (Central Act 5 of 1898), it shall be lawful for a Magistrate of the second class to pass the minimum sentence mentioned in paragraph (i) of the proviso to clause (1) of section 55, for a first offence referred to in that paragraph, in excess of his powers under section 32 of the said Code."

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By notification in the Gazette.

rights: Magistrates of second class have the power to impose minimum penalties for certain first offences, even in excess of their powers under section 32 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.

key_procedures: The Government is empowered to notify the date of commencement of this Act in the Gazette.
administration: Abkari Department
important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 350 dated 23rd April 1973.

title: THE ABKARI (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1984
purpose: To further amend the Abkari Act, 1 of 1077, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to acts related to liquor and intoxicating drugs within the jurisdiction of Kerala.

key_definitions.grievous hurt: The explanation for 'grievous hurt' in section 57B states it shall have the same meaning as in section 320 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (Central Act 45 of 1860).

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Abkari (Amendment) Act, 1984 and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 3rd day of November, 1983.
Amends section 57 of the Abkari Act, 1 of 1077 by inserting new clauses to define 'any noxious drug' and 'any article prohibited'. It also replaces certain wording within the existing section.

Inserts new sections 57A and 57B into the principal Act. Section 57A deals with the adulteration of liquor or intoxicating drugs, and the penalties associated with causing grievous hurt or death as a result. Section 57B deals with compensation orders for offences under section 57A.

Repeals the Abkari (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984 (61 of 1984). It also states that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Penalties for adulteration of liquor or intoxicating drugs leading to grievous hurt can range from imprisonment for a term not less than two years (extendable to life with fine up to fifty thousand rupees) to imprisonment for a term not less than three years (extendable to life with fine up to fifty thousand rupees) if death results.
Rule 2: In any other case, imprisonment for a term not less than one year (extendable to ten years with fine up to twenty-five thousand rupees) applies.
Rule 3: Whoever omits to take reasonable precautions to prevent the mixing of any noxious substance with liquor or intoxicating drug is punishable.
Rule 4: Whoever possesses any liquor or intoxicating drug which is mixed with any noxious substance shall be punishable.

Rule 5: Notwithstanding anything in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, no person prosecuted or convicted under sub-section (1) or sub-section (2) of section 57A, shall be kept in custody, released on bail or on his own bond, unless there is an opportunity to oppose such release or the court is satisfied that there are reasonable grounds for believing that he is not guilty of such offence.

penalties: For adulteration causing grievous hurt: Imprisonment for a term not less than two years (extendable to life with fine up to fifty thousand rupees).
For adulteration causing death: Imprisonment for a term not less than three years (extendable to life with fine up to fifty thousand rupees).
In any other case of adulteration: Imprisonment for a term not less than one year (extendable to ten years with fine up to twenty-five thousand rupees).
For omission to take precautions: Same penalties as for adulteration causing grievous hurt or death depending on the result.
For possession of mixed liquor/drug: Imprisonment for a term not less than one year (extendable to ten years with fine up to twenty-five thousand rupees).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Implied to be the Abkari Department and the courts. The Code of Criminal Procedure is referenced for procedural aspects.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through prosecution and court proceedings. Bail is restricted in certain cases under section 57A. Compensation can be ordered under section 57B for offences causing grievous hurt or death.

rights: Right to appeal to the High Court within ninety days from the date of order under sub-section (1) of section 57B, or with leave of the High Court, even after the expiry of the said period.
duties: Duty to take reasonable precautions to prevent the mixing of any noxious substance with liquor or intoxicating drug.
Duty not to adulterate liquor or intoxicating drug.
obligations: Obligation to pay compensation as ordered by the court under section 57B.

key_procedures: Procedure for prosecution and punishment for adulteration of liquor or intoxicating drugs under section 57A.
Procedure for ordering compensation for offences causing grievous hurt or death under section 57B.
Procedure for appeals against orders under section 57B, including time limits and conditions for appeal.
administration: The Abkari Department (implied, as it deals with Abkari matters).
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on November 3, 1983.
The Abkari (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984 is repealed.
Anything done under the Ordinance is deemed to have been done under this Act.
The definition of 'grievous hurt' refers to the Indian Penal Code.
The High Court has discretion to entertain appeals even after the ninety-day period for compensation orders under section 57B, if sufficient cause is shown.

title: The Abkari (Amendment) Act, 2010 (2010-ലെ 3-ാം ആക്ട്)
purpose: To amend the Abkari Act, 1077 (1 of 1077) and to include the provisions for licensing and control of the sale of Indian Made Foreign Liquor and IMFL products and to provide for better regulation of abkari revenue.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Kerala and all abkari revenue generated within the State.

key_definitions.abhkari: Refers to intoxicating liquors, including arrack and toddy.
key_definitions.liquor: Includes all liquors, and includes spirits of wine, spirit, wine, beer, toddy and intoxicating drugs.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force from the date specified by the Government.
Amends Section 1 of the Principal Act relating to the short title and commencement of the Act.
Amends Section 12 of the Principal Act regarding the licensing of the sale of intoxicating liquors.
Amends Section 15 of the Principal Act concerning the duties of officers appointed under the Act.
Amends Section 30 of the Principal Act which deals with penalties for illicit manufacture, sale, etc., of abkari.
Amends Section 53 of the Principal Act relating to the powers of the Collector to issue licenses.
Amends Section 55 of the Principal Act concerning the penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act or rules made thereunder.
Amends Section 56 of the Principal Act dealing with compounding of offences.
Amends Section 57 of the Principal Act relating to the powers of revision by the Government.
Amends Section 62 of the Principal Act concerning the powers of arrest and seizure.
Amends Section 67 of the Principal Act regarding the prohibition of certain acts.
Inserts new sections after Section 67 of the Principal Act to provide for licensing of the sale of Indian Made Foreign Liquor and IMFL products and for other related matters.

important_rules: Rules regarding the licensing of the sale of Indian Made Foreign Liquor and IMFL products.
Provisions for the enhancement of abkari revenue through licensing and regulation.
Penalties for various offences related to abkari, including illicit trade and contravention of license conditions.

penalties: Imprisonment and/or fine for illicit manufacture, sale, etc.
Confiscation of liquor and tools used in illicit trade.
Fines for contravention of license conditions or provisions of the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Abkari Officers, Police Officers, and other officers authorized by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspection, search, seizure, arrest, and prosecution of offenders.

rights: Right to apply for and obtain licenses for the sale of liquor under prescribed conditions.
Right to conduct abkari business in accordance with the provisions of the Act and rules.
duties: Duty to comply with the provisions of the Abkari Act and the rules made thereunder.
Duty to obtain necessary licenses for the manufacture, sale, or possession of liquor.
Duty to pay abkari duties and taxes as prescribed.
obligations: Obligation to maintain records and submit reports as required by the authorities.

key_procedures: Procedure for application and grant of licenses for abkari trade.
Procedure for inspection, search, seizure, and arrest by abkari officers.
Procedure for compounding of offences.
administration: Excise Department, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act aims to provide a more comprehensive framework for the regulation of the abkari trade in Kerala.
Specific details on licensing fees, conditions, and procedures are likely to be covered in the rules framed under the Act.
The amendments reflect an effort to increase state revenue from the abkari sector and to ensure better control over the sale of alcoholic beverages.

title: THE ABKARI (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2010
purpose: To amend the Abkari Act 1 of 1077 for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala, amending specific sections of the Abkari Act 1 of 1077.

key_definitions.counterfeit: For the purpose of the section, the expression "counterfeit" shall have the same meaning as in section 28 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (Central Act 45 of 1860).
key_definitions.document: In this section, the word "document", unless anything contrary is specified in any other section in this Act shall have the same meaning as in section 3 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872. (Central Act 1 of 1872)

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Abkari (Amendment) Act 2010 and that Section 2 shall come into force on the 30th day of March, 1996, and the remaining provisions on the 7th day of December, 2009.

Inserts a provision that notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, no import fee shall be levied on rectified spirit or Extra Neutral Alcohol including absolute alcohol intended to be used for the manufacture of liquor meant for human consumption.

Introduces Section 12C, which deals with the "Prohibition of counterfeiting, selling, buying, receiving, possessing, etc. of any forged or counterfeit label or security sticker". It prohibits individuals from engaging in such activities and also from performing any part of the process of counterfeiting or selling liquor with counterfeit labels. It also prohibits the sale of liquor if the label or sticker is forged or counterfeit. It further states that no person shall make or sell or dispose of any machinery, printing press, computer, printer or scanner or any similar material for the purpose of being used or knowing or having reason to believe that it is intended to be used for forging or counterfeiting any label or security sticker for the sale of liquor.
Amends section 15C of the principal Act by substituting certain words and adding an Explanation to define "public passenger or goods vehicle".

Introduces Section 30A, granting "Abkari Officers" powers similar to those of police officers for the purpose of investigation of offences under this Act, including the power of investigation under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

Inserts Section 53B, which deals with the "Jurisdiction of courts on articles seized". It states that whenever any vehicle or other conveyance used for committing any offence is seized or detained under this Act, and if any court finds that it shall be released temporarily, it shall do so with direction to execute a sufficient bond by way of cash security equivalent to the market value of such vehicle or conveyance. Such release will be subject to verification by the Mechanical Engineer of the Excise Department or any Mechanical Engineer or above the rank of an Assistant Executive Engineer of the State Public Works Department, for production of such vehicle or conveyance on demand before the court or the authorized officer and such order shall not prevent the authorized officer from taking or continuing action under section 67B of this Act.

Inserts several new sections: 55C (Penalty for counterfeiting, selling, etc. of label or security sticker), 55D (Penalty for criminal conspiracy), 55E (Penalty for false marking of property or use of false property mark), 55F (Penalty for possession of things described in section 55E), and 55G (Penalty for making or using of false document), and 55H (Penalty for unlawful advertisement).
Amends section 56 of the principal Act by substituting the words "two thousand rupees" with "twenty five thousand rupees".
Amends section 57 in clause (a), by omitting the word "foreign".

Inserts Section 62, titled "Offence committed by several persons in furtherance of common intention". It states that when an offence under this Act is committed by several persons in furtherance of a common intention, each of such persons shall be guilty of that offence as if it was committed by him alone.

Amends section 67 of the principal Act by substituting the title and sub-section (1). The new title is "Power to impose fine", and the new sub-section (1) states that the Commissioner shall be competent to impose such fine as may be prescribed in the rules, on any person holding a licence or permit issued under this Act, for contravention of any rule made under this Act. It also includes a proviso that no order imposing any fine under this section shall be made without giving the person an opportunity of being heard.

Inserts Section 67A, titled "Power to compound offences". It states that the Commissioner of Excise or the Deputy Commissioner of Excise of the District concerned or any Abkari Officer specially empowered by the Government in this behalf by notification in the Gazette, may accept, from any person reasonably suspected of having committed any of the offences specified in column (1) of the Table below, a sum of money as composition as specified in column (3) of the said Table, by way of composition for the offence which may have been committed and where any property has been seized, the same shall be confiscated to Government or disposed of in such manner as may be prescribed.

Repeals The Abkari (Amendment) Ordinance, 2010 (6 of 2010). Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: No import fee shall be levied on rectified spirit or Extra Neutral Alcohol including absolute alcohol intended to be used for the manufacture of liquor meant for human consumption.
No person shall counterfeit, sell, buy, receive, possess, etc. any forged or counterfeit label or security sticker.
No person shall perform any part of the process of counterfeiting, label or security sticker sale of liquor.

No person shall make or sell or dispose of any machinery, printing press, computer, printer or scanner or any similar material for the purpose of being used or knowing or having reason to believe that it is intended to be used for forging or counterfeiting any label or security sticker for the sale of liquor.

Whoever contravenes the provisions of section 12C of this Act, shall, on conviction before a competent court, be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years or with a fine which may extend to rupees one lakh or with both.

When two or more persons agree to do or cause to be done an act which is illegal under this Act and does such an illegal act in pursuance of such agreement by any one or more of the parties to that agreement, each and every person who is a party to the criminal conspiracy shall, on conviction, be punished with the same punishment provided for the offence committed.

Whoever prints, publishes or gives any advertisement soliciting use of or offering any liquor or intoxicating drug shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to twenty-five thousand rupees or with both. This shall not apply to price list for display at the points of sale for consumer information.
Offences committed by several persons in furtherance of common intention shall make each person guilty as if committed by him alone.

The Commissioner shall be competent to impose such fine as may be prescribed in the rules, on any person holding a licence or permit issued under this Act, for contravention of any rule made under this Act, provided that no order imposing any fine shall be made without giving the person an opportunity of being heard.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years or with a fine which may extend to rupees one lakh or with both (for counterfeiting, selling, etc. of label or security sticker and criminal conspiracy).
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine which may extend to one lakh rupees or with both (for false marking of property or use of false property mark).
Same punishment as provided for the offence under section 55E, for possession of things described in section 55E.
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine which may extend to one lakh rupees or with both (for making or using of false document).
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to twenty-five thousand rupees or with both (for unlawful advertisement).
Punishment with imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years in furtherance of common intention.
Fine as prescribed in rules for contravention of any rule made under this Act.

Compounding fees as specified in the Table (e.g., 5,000 rupees for transporting liquor or intoxicating drug in excess of the quantity prescribed, 10,000 rupees for taps or causes to be tapped any toddy producing tree in contravention of the Act, Rules or any order made under the Act, 25,000 rupees for misconduct by licensee etc.).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Abkari Officers, Commissioner of Excise, Deputy Commissioner of Excise of the District concerned or any Abkari Officer specially empowered by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Investigation of offences, seizure of vehicles and conveyances, confiscation of property, imposition of fines, and compounding of offences.

rights: Right to an opportunity of being heard before any order imposing a fine is made.
Right to have a vehicle or other conveyance released temporarily by executing a bond by way of cash security, if the court finds it appropriate.
duties: Persons are duty-bound not to engage in counterfeiting, selling, buying, receiving, or possessing forged or counterfeit labels or security stickers.
Individuals must not sell liquor with counterfeit labels or stickers.
Individuals must not perform any part of the counterfeiting process.
Advertisers must not solicit the use of or offer any liquor or intoxicating drug.
Those found guilty of criminal conspiracy must face punishment.
Individuals must not make or use false documents.
Licensees must avoid misconduct.
Individuals must adhere to rules and regulations concerning liquor and intoxicating drugs.
obligations: Persons suspected of offences may have their property confiscated or disposed of.
Suspected offenders may be required to pay a sum of money as composition for the offence.

key_procedures: Investigation of offences by Abkari Officers with powers similar to police officers.
Seizure and temporary release of vehicles/conveyances used in offences, with conditions for bond and cash security.
Compounding of offences by the Commissioner of Excise or empowered officers, involving payment of a sum of money.
Confiscation or disposal of seized property.
Imposition of fines by the Commissioner of Excise with prior opportunity for the person to be heard.
Repeal and saving clause to ensure continuity of actions taken under previous ordinances.
administration: The Abkari Department of the Government of Kerala (inferred from the context of the Abkari Act).
important_notes: The amendment comes into force on specific dates for different sections (March 30, 1996, and December 7, 2009).
No import fee is levied on rectified spirit or Extra Neutral Alcohol for human consumption liquor manufacturing.
The definition of "counterfeit" refers to the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
The definition of "document" refers to the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.
The amendment specifies penalties for various offences including counterfeiting, criminal conspiracy, false marking, and unlawful advertising.
A Table is provided listing specific offences and their corresponding compounding fees.
The Abkari (Amendment) Ordinance, 2010, has been repealed and saving provisions are in place.
Price list displays for liquor at points of sale are exempt from the penalty for unlawful advertisement.

title: The Abkari (Amendment) Act, 1969
purpose: To further amend the Abkari Act, I of 1077.
scope: Applies to the Abkari Act, I of 1077, and concerns the sale of liquor, duty of excise, and luxury tax.

Amends section 18 of the Abkari Act, I of 1077, by substituting clauses and figures related to duty of excise and luxury tax on liquor.

important_rules: Amendment to section 18(2) regarding the sale of liquor and the form of a gallonage fee or vending fee.
Substitution of figures related to duty of excise and luxury tax on liquor, with specific effective dates.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not specified in the provided text.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not specified in the provided text.

title: THE ABKARI (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1975
purpose: To further amend the Abkari Act I of 1077 for the purposes therein appearing.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Kerala and makes amendments to the Abkari Act I of 1077.

key_definitions.Transit: Means to move from one place in a State to another place in that State through the territory of the State of Kerala.
key_definitions.State: In this clause, "State" means the State of Karnataka or the State of Tamil Nadu or the Union territory of Pondicherry.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Abkari (Amendment) Act, 1975, and it shall come into force at once.
Amends section 3 of the Abkari Act I of 1077 by inserting a new clause (17A) defining 'Transit' and an explanation for 'State'.
Amends sub-section (2) of section 29 of the principal Act, in clause (j), by substituting the words 'possession or transport' with 'possession, transit or transport'.
Amends section 55 of the principal Act, in clause (a), by substituting the words 'transports or possesses' with 'transports, transits or possesses'.

important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 11th day of April, 1975 and published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 189 dated 11th April, 1975.

title: The Abkari (Amendment) Act, 1995 (Act 12 of 1995)
purpose: To further amend the Abkari Act, 1077 (1 of 1077).
scope: Applies to offenses related to the Abkari Act in Kerala.

key_definitions.intoxicating drug: Means any intoxicating substance, other than a narcotic drug or psychotropic substance regulated by the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 (Central Act 61 of 1985), which the Government may by notification declare to be an intoxicating drug.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Abkari (Amendment) Act, 1995 and shall come into force at once.

Amends section 26 of the Abkari Act, 1077 by replacing the clause "(bb) if the holder thereof or his servant, or any one acting with his express or implied permission on his behalf, sells or stores for sale liquor in any place other than the licensed premises; or" with new wording regarding offences.

Amends section 55 of the principal Act. It replaces "sells liquor" with "sells or stores for sale liquor" and specifies that for offences falling under clause (d) or clause (e), with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years and with fine which shall not be less than twenty-five thousand rupees, and for an offence falling under clause (d) or clause (e), with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees or with both.
Omission of section 55A of the principal Act.

Amends section 58 of the principal Act. It allows for imprisonment for a term which may extend to three thousand rupees, or with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with both. It also introduces a fine of fifteen thousand rupees for a term which shall not be less than rupees fifteen thousand and with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year.

Inserts a new section 64A regarding penalty for allowing any land, building, room, space or enclosure, or any part thereof, to be used for the manufacture, sale or storing for sale of liquor or intoxicating drug without a license or permit. Penalties include fines not less than twenty-five thousand rupees, unless the court is satisfied that all due and reasonable precautions were taken.

Amends section 67 of the principal Act. It provides powers to the Abkari Officer to cancel or suspend licenses or permits for offences committed under specific sections and to levy a sum of money not less than ten thousand rupees and not exceeding twenty-five thousand rupees, or by way of compensation, as the case may be.

Amends section 67A of the principal Act. It substitutes "not exceeding two thousand rupees" with "rupees five thousand" and adds a proviso stating that if the holder of such licence or permit sells or stores for sale liquor in any premises, other than the licensed premises; such penalty shall not be less than twenty-five thousand rupees.

Repeals The Abkari (Amendment) Ordinance, 1995 (13 of 1995). It also states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act, as amended by the said Ordinance, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Sale or storage of liquor or intoxicating drug without a license or permit is penalized.
Penalties for offenses under sections 26, 55, 58, 64A, 67, and 67A are specified, including fines and imprisonment.
Abkari Officers have the power to compound offenses by accepting sums of money.
Licenses or permits can be cancelled or suspended for certain offenses.

penalties: Fines not less than twenty-five thousand rupees for offences under section 64A.
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years and fine not less than twenty-five thousand rupees for offences under section 55.
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or fine up to ten thousand rupees for offences under section 55.
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three thousand rupees or imprisonment up to six months or both under section 58.
Fine of not less than fifteen thousand rupees and imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year under section 58.
Sum of money not less than ten thousand rupees and not exceeding twenty-five thousand rupees under section 67.
Fine of five thousand rupees for words "not exceeding two thousand rupees" under section 67A.
Penalty not less than twenty-five thousand rupees for selling or storing liquor in premises other than licensed premises under section 67A.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Abkari Officers
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through imposition of fines, imprisonment, cancellation or suspension of licenses/permits, and compounding of offenses.

rights: Right to hold a licence or permit for sale or storage of liquor or intoxicating drug (subject to conditions).
duties: Duty to obtain a license or permit for the sale or storage of liquor or intoxicating drug.
Duty to comply with the conditions of the license or permit.
Duty to ensure that no liquor or intoxicating drug is sold or stored in premises other than licensed premises.
Duty to take due and reasonable precautions to prevent the use of premises for illegal activities related to liquor or intoxicating drugs.
obligations: Obligation to pay penalties and fines as prescribed by the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure for amendment of existing sections of the Abkari Act, 1077.
Procedure for insertion of new sections into the Abkari Act, 1077.
Procedure for omission of sections from the Abkari Act, 1077.
Procedure for compounding offenses by Abkari Officers.
Procedure for cancellation or suspension of licenses/permits.
Procedure for taking action against individuals who sell or store liquor or intoxicating drugs without a valid license or permit.
administration: The Abkari Department of the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 5th day of August 1995 and was published in the Gazette extraordinary No. 789 dated 5th August 1995.
The Abkari (Amendment) Ordinance, 1995 (13 of 1995) is hereby repealed.
Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

title: The Abkari (Amendment) Act, 2003
purpose: To further amend the Abkari Act, 1 of 1077 for the purposes appearing hereinafter.
scope: Applies to the Abkari Act, 1 of 1077 and amendments made by this Act.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Abkari (Amendment) Act, 2003. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 3rd day of September, 2002.

Inserts a new section 53A titled 'Disposal of seized liquor, intoxicating drugs or articles' into the Abkari Act, 1 of 1077. This section outlines procedures for the disposal of seized liquor, intoxicating drugs, or articles, including inventory, notification, and application to a Magistrate for disposal. It also addresses where liquor or intoxicating drug or article has been kept under custody of any court. An explanation clarifies that 'article' for the purpose of this section includes jaggery and other like substances, the value of which depreciates in passage of time.

Repeals the Abkari (Amendment) Ordinance, 2002. Notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance is deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, the State Government may, having regard to the nature of the liquor, intoxicating drug or article, its vulnerability to theft, substitution, constraints of proper storage space or any other relevant consideration, by notification in the official Gazette, specify such liquor, intoxicating drug or article which shall, as soon as may be after its seizure, be disposed of by the authorised officer referred to in section 67B, in such manner as the Government may, from time to time determine after following the procedure hereinafter specified.

Rule 2: Where any such notified liquor, intoxicating drug or article has been seized under this Act, the authorised officer shall prepare an inventory of such liquor, intoxicating drug or article containing such details relating to their description, quality, quantity, mode of packing, marks, numbers of such other identifying particulars of the liquor, intoxicating drug or article or the packing containers in which they are kept, place of origin and other particulars, as the authorised officer may consider relevant to identify the liquor, intoxicating drug or article in any proceedings under this Act and make an application to any Magistrate having jurisdiction over the area where the seized liquor, intoxicating drug or articles are stored for the purpose of— (a) certifying the correctness of the inventory so prepared, or (b) taking, in the presence of such Magistrate, photographs of such liquor, intoxicating drug or article and certifying such photographs as true; or (c) allowing to draw representative samples of such liquor, intoxicating drug or article in the presence of such Magistrate and certifying the correctness of any list of samples so drawn.

Rule 3: Where an application is made under sub-section (2) the Magistrate shall, as soon as may be, visit the place where such liquor, intoxicating drug or articles are stored and take appropriate steps as specified in clauses (a), (b) and (c) of sub-section (2), and allow the application.

Rule 4: Where any liquor or intoxicating drug or article under this Act has been kept under the custody of any court in connection with any offence committed under this Act, before the commencement of the Abkari (Amendment) Act, 2003 or has been brought before a Magistrate without complying the procedure laid down in sub-section (2), the authorised officer shall obtain prior permission of the Court or Magistrate before initiating proceedings under sub-section (2).

Rule 5: Notwithstanding anything contained in the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 (Central Act 1 of 1872) or the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Central Act 2 of 1974), any Court trying an offence under this Act, shall treat the inventory, the photographs of liquor, intoxicating drug or article and any list of samples drawn under sub-sections (2) and (4) certified by the Magistrate, as primary evidence in respect of such offence.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Authorised officer, Magistrate, Court
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Seizure, inventory, photography, sample drawing, court proceedings, disposal of seized items.

rights: Right to specify liquor, intoxicating drug or article for immediate disposal by notification.
Right to prepare inventory of seized items.
Right to apply to Magistrate for certification of inventory and photographs.
Right to draw representative samples in presence of Magistrate.
Right to obtain prior permission from Court or Magistrate for proceedings concerning items in custody.
Right to have inventory and photographs treated as primary evidence.
duties: Duty to specify liquor, intoxicating drug or article for immediate disposal by notification (State Government).
Duty to prepare an inventory of seized liquor, intoxicating drug or article.
Duty to apply to Magistrate for certification and photographic evidence.
Duty to draw representative samples in presence of Magistrate.
Duty to obtain prior permission from Court or Magistrate before initiating proceedings.
Duty to treat inventory and photographs as primary evidence.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: If liquor, intoxicating drug or article is seized, the authorised officer shall prepare an inventory. Then, an application is made to a Magistrate to certify the correctness of the inventory and to take photographs of the seized items. Representative samples can also be drawn in the presence of the Magistrate. The Magistrate shall visit the place, verify the inventory, take photographs, and allow samples to be drawn.
Procedure 2: For items seized under the Act but kept in court custody, prior permission from the court or Magistrate is required before initiating proceedings under sub-section (2) of section 53A.
Procedure 3: Inventory and photographs certified by the Magistrate are considered primary evidence in court proceedings.
administration: State Government
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on September 3, 2002.
Article includes jaggery and other like substances whose value depreciates over time.
The Abkari (Amendment) Ordinance, 2002 is repealed, but actions taken under it are saved.
The provisions regarding evidence in court proceedings are modified by this Act.

title: The Abkari (Second Amendment) Act, 1975
purpose: To further amend the Abkari Act of 1977 for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to actions related to liquor and intoxicating drugs within Kerala, affecting individuals, property, and enforcement authorities.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Abkari (Second Amendment) Act, 1975, and shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 34
main_sections.description: Substitutes the existing section 34 of the Abkari Act of 1077. The new section grants powers to officers of the Excise Department or Police Department to seize and detain contraband liquor, vehicles, or other conveyances without warrant, and to arrest persons suspected of committing offenses under the Act. It also details procedures for search and confiscation.
Amends section 67 of the principal Act by substituting 'two thousand rupees' with 'five thousand rupees' and modifying the portion regarding the value of goods to be omitted.

Inserts new sections dealing with: 67B: Confiscation of property by Abkari Officers. 67C: Issue of show cause notice before confiscation. 67D: Property not liable to be returned to owner. 67E: Appeal. 67F: Revision. 67G: Award of confiscation not to interfere with other punishments. 67H: Property confiscated when to vest in Government.

Provides that notwithstanding anything contained in any law, any judgment, decree or order of any court, all animals, carts, vessels and other conveyances used in carrying any receptacle, package or covering containing any liquor, intoxicating drug, material, still, utensil, implement or apparatus in respect of, or by means of, which an offence under the principal Act is believed to have been committed and seized and detained before the commencement of this Act may be disposed of under the provisions of the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Officers can seize and detain contraband liquor, vehicles, and other conveyances without a warrant.
Officers can arrest persons suspected of offenses under the Act without a warrant.
The value of goods estimated for confiscation is to be mentioned.
Confiscated property generally vests in the Government.
An order of confiscation does not prevent prosecution for any offense.

penalties: Fines mentioned in amended section 67 (formerly 'two thousand rupees', now 'five thousand rupees'). Specific penalties for offenses under sections 15C or 55 or section 57 or section 58 are referred to, implying existing penalties still apply.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Excise Department and Police Department officers, Assistant Excise Commissioner, Appellate authority, Commissioner.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Seizure and detention of contraband and conveyances, arrest of offenders, confiscation of property, issue of show cause notices, appeals, and revisions.

rights: Right to make representations against confiscation.
Right to appeal against orders of confiscation.
Right to seek revision of orders.
Opportunity of being heard before an order prejudicial to a person is passed under certain sections.
duties: Duty of the officer making an arrest to ensure bail if sufficient bail is tendered.
Duty to issue show cause notice before confiscation.
Duty to give an opportunity of being heard before an order is passed.
obligations: Obligation to produce before an officer empowered to admit to bail.
Obligation to present seized property for confiscation.
Obligation to ensure property is fit for human consumption before disposal.

key_procedures: Seizure and detention of liquor, vehicles, and other conveyances.
Arrest of persons suspected of committing offenses.
Issuing a show cause notice before confiscation of property.
Appealing against confiscation orders to a higher authority.
Seeking revision of appellate authority orders by the Government.
Disposal of seized property, including potential destruction if unfit for human consumption.
administration: Excise Department, Police Department, Assistant Excise Commissioner, Government.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Abkari Act, 1077.
The Act received the assent of the Governor on 1st August 1975 and was published on 1st August 1975.
The Act is deemed to have been in force at the time of seizure and detention of offences committed under the principal Act.
Confiscation procedures require a show cause notice and an opportunity to be heard.

title: The Abkari (Amendment) Act, 2014
purpose: To amend the Abkari Act, 1077 ME (corresponding to 1935 AD) for the purpose of introducing amendments to various sections.
scope: This act applies to the state of Kerala and amends specific sections of the existing Abkari Act, 1077 ME.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Abkari (Amendment) Act, 2014' and clarifies that Sections 6(F) and 6(G) are deemed to have come into force on 26th February 2013 and 27th September 2013, respectively.
Amends Section 15F of the Abkari Act, 1077 ME. It replaces the age '18' with '21' in two instances within this section.
Amends Section 15G of the Abkari Act, 1077 ME. It replaces the age '18' with '21' and the word 'three' with 'twenty-two' in this section.

Amends Section 18 of the Abkari Act, 1077 ME. It introduces a new subsection (4)(B) specifying a penalty of 30 rupees (Indian Rupees) per litre for foreign liquor. This amount is fixed and subject to review.

Inserts a new Section 55F into the Abkari Act, 1077 ME. This section deals with penalties for not displaying health warnings on advertisements related to alcoholic beverages. It mandates that advertisements must clearly display 'Consumption of Alcohol is Injurious to Health/Alcoholic beverages are injurious to health' in a visual format, covering at least 1/10th of the advertisement's area. Failure to comply can result in a fine of three to six months imprisonment or a fine of Rs. 5,000 to Rs. 10,000, or both.

Amends Section 67 of the Abkari Act, 1077 ME. It increases the penalty from Rs. 25,000 to Rs. 3,00,000. It also inserts a new subsection (3) detailing penalties for possessing or altering certain types of liquor containers or bottles without proper authorization, including forfeiture of the liquor and potential prosecution under other provisions of the Act.
Amends Section 67F of the Abkari Act, 1077 ME. It replaces the age '18' with '21' in the first Proviso to subsection (1) of the said section.

Repeals the Abkari (Amendment) Ordinance, 2013 (Ordinance No. 40 of 2013) and states that any action taken or anything done or omitted to be done under the repealed Ordinance shall be deemed to have been taken or done or omitted to be done under the corresponding provisions of this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Advertisements for alcoholic beverages must display health warnings ('Consumption of Alcohol is Injurious to Health/Alcoholic beverages are injurious to health') prominently. (Section 55F)
Rule 2: Unauthorized alteration, removal, or falsification of seals or labels on liquor containers is subject to severe penalties. (Section 67(3))
Rule 3: The minimum age for consuming or dealing with certain alcoholic beverages has been raised to 21 years. (Sections 15F, 15G, 67F)

penalties: Section 4: Penalty of Rs. 30 per litre for foreign liquor.
Section 55F: Imprisonment of three to six months or a fine of Rs. 5,000 to Rs. 10,000, or both, for non-compliance with advertisement display rules.
Section 67: Increased penalty to Rs. 3,00,000 for offences under Section 67.
Section 67(3): Forfeiture of liquor and potential penalties as prescribed under the Act for unauthorized liquor containers.
Section 15F, 15G, 67F: Violations related to age restrictions may incur penalties as per the general provisions of the Abkari Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Abkari Department and relevant law enforcement agencies in Kerala.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, raids, prosecution, and imposition of fines and imprisonment as stipulated in the Act.

rights: Right to be informed about the health risks of alcohol consumption through mandatory advertisements.
duties: Duty of manufacturers and advertisers to comply with health warning display requirements.
Duty of individuals to adhere to age restrictions for alcohol consumption.
Duty of all individuals and entities to comply with the provisions of the Abkari Act.
obligations: Obligation to pay prescribed penalties for violations.
Obligation to obtain necessary licenses and permissions for dealing with alcoholic substances.

key_procedures: Procedure for displaying health warnings on alcoholic beverage advertisements: Advertisers must ensure that warnings occupy at least 1/10th of the advertisement area and are clearly visible. (Section 55F)
Procedure for dealing with unauthorized liquor containers: Authorities can seize liquor from such containers and take further action as per Section 67(3).
Procedure for amendment of the Abkari Act: The Act outlines specific sections to be amended by replacing or inserting new clauses and subsections.
administration: The Abkari Department of the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The amendment raises the age limit related to alcohol from 18 to 21 in several sections.
The Act repeals the Abkari (Amendment) Ordinance, 2013, ensuring continuity of legal provisions.

title: THE AGRICULTURAL INCOME TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1983
purpose: To further amend the Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1950 for the purpose hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to agricultural income tax in Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that the Act can be called the Agricultural Income Tax (Amendment) Act, 1983 and it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1983.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Schedule.-In the Schedule to the Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1950 (XXII of 1950)
main_sections.description: This section details amendments to the Schedule of the principal Act. It specifies the tax rates for different slabs of total agricultural income. For instance, it outlines that for income not exceeding Rs. 20,000, no tax is levied. For income exceeding Rs. 20,000 but not exceeding Rs. 23,000, the tax is 30 per cent of the amount. Different rates are specified for higher income brackets, up to Rs. 70,000 and above. The rates are also presented in terms of percentage of the amount by which the total agricultural income exceeds certain thresholds.

This section repeals the Agricultural Income Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 1982 (4 of 1982). It also states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text.

administration: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text. Likely the State Tax Department of Kerala.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 6th day of April, 1983 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 408 dated the 8th April, 1983.

title: THE AGRICULTURAL INCOME-TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1971
purpose: To further amend the Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950 for the purpose herein-after appearing.
scope: Applies to agricultural income. The provisions of this Act shall be deemed to have come into force on the 8th day of March, 1971. Section 2 of the principal Act is amended. Section 3 relates to validation of any assessment of agricultural income made before the date of publication of this Act. Section 4 deals with repeal and saving.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Agricultural Income-tax (Amendment) Act, 1971 and that Section 2 shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1962, and the remaining provisions of this Act shall be deemed to have come into force on the 8th day of March, 1971.

Amends Section 2 of the Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950 (XXII of 1950). Specifically, it amends sub-clause (1) for sub-clause (1) to include a proviso defining 'agricultural purposes' and a new sub-clause (3) for the proviso. It also clarifies 'rent or revenue derived from land which is used for agricultural purposes'.

Provides for the validation of anything contained in any law or in any judgment, decree or order of any court, tribunal or other authority to the contrary, any assessment of agricultural income made or purporting to have been made under the principal Act before the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette, in respect of any land not assessed to land revenue in the State or subject to a local rate and collected by officers of the Government as such, shall be deemed to be as valid and effective as if such assessment had been made under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

Repeals the Agricultural Income-tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 1971 (11 of 1971) and states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the said Ordinance or the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act or the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Land revenue or local rate assessment is considered for agricultural purposes.
Certain definitions regarding rent and revenue derived from land are specified.
Validation of past assessments made under the principal Act before the amendment.
key_procedures: Amendment of Section 2 of the principal Act.
Validation of assessments made prior to the Act's publication.
Repeal of the Agricultural Income-tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 1971.
administration: Government (implied by reference to officers of the Government, Gazette)
important_notes: The definition of 'agricultural purposes' is clarified to include land within the municipality, municipal corporation, notified area committee, town area committee, town committee or any other name) or a cantonment board and which has a population of not less than ten thousand according to the last preceding census of which the relevant figures have been published before the first day of the previous year, or in any area within such distance, not being more than eight kilometres, from the local limits of any municipality or cantonment board referred to in item (A), as may be specified by the Central Government under the proviso to sub-clause (3) of clause (1) of section 2 of the Income-tax Act, 1961

All acts, proceedings or things done or taken or purporting to have been done or taken by any officer or authority in connection with such assessment shall, for all purposes, be deemed to be, and to have always been, done or taken in accordance with law.

All taxes on agricultural income charged or collected or purporting to have been charged or collected in consequence of such assessment shall, for all purposes, be deemed to be, and to have always been, charged or collected in accordance with law.
No suit or other proceeding shall be maintained or continued in any court, tribunal or other authority for the refund of any such tax so collected.
No court shall enforce any decree or order directing the refund of any such tax so collected.

Any such tax charged in consequence of such assessment before the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette, but not collected before that date, may be recovered in the manner provided under the principal Act as amended by this Act, and the rules made thereunder.

Where no such tax was charged, before the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette, in consequence of such assessment, such tax may be charged and collected under the principal Act as amended by this Act and the rules made thereunder.

title: The Agricultural Income-Tax (Amendment) Act, 1974
purpose: To further amend the Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: This Act applies to agricultural income derived from lands situated within the State and received by him within or without the State but does not include: (a) any agricultural income derived from land situated without the State. (b) any agricultural income derived from properties held under trust wholly for charitable or religious purposes to the extent to which such income is applied to such purposes in the State. (c) any agricultural income derived from property held under trust in part only for such purposes, to the extent to which such income is applied to such purposes in the State.

key_definitions.total agricultural income: Subject to the provisions of this Act, the total agricultural income of any previous year of any person comprised all agricultural income derived from land situated within the State and received by him within or without the State but does not include-
key_definitions.trust: "trust" includes any other legal obligation and "relative" in relation to an individual, means— (i) spouse of the individual, (ii) brother or sister of the individual, (iii) brother or sister of the spouse of the individual; (iv) any lineal ascendant or descendant of the individual (v) any lineal ascendant or descendant of the spouse of the individual; (vi) spouse of a person referred to in sub-clause (ii), sub-clause (iii), sub-clause (iv) or sub-clause (v); (vii) any lineal descendant of a brother or sister of either the individual or of the spouse of the individual.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Agricultural Income-tax (Amendment) Act, 1974. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette appoint.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 4
main_sections.description: Substitution of new section for section 4 of the Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950. The following section shall be substituted, namely: "4. Total agricultural income (1) Subject to the provisions of this Act, the total agricultural income of any previous year of any person comprised all agricultural income derived from land situated within the State and received by him within or without the State but does not include- (a) any agricultural income derived from land situated without the State. (b) any agricultural income derived from properties held under trust wholly for charitable or religious purposes to the extent to which such income is applied to such purposes in the State. (c) any agricultural income derived from property held under trust in part only for such purposes, to the extent to which such income is applied to such purposes in the State. (2) For the purposes of sub-section (1) agricultural income derived from any land situated within the State, which is in the possession of the mortgagor thereof shall, notwithstanding anything contained in section 23 be deemed to be agricultural income received by the mortgagor: Provided that where the agricultural income-tax charged on such agricultural income cannot be recovered from the mortgagor, such tax shall be payable by and recoverable from the mortgagee, and the mortgagor shall be entitled to recover the same from the mortgagee for the amount of the tax so paid. (3) Nothing contained in clause (b) or clause (c) of sub-section (1) shall operate so as to exclude from the total agricultural income of the person in receipt thereof— (a) any part of the agricultural income from the property held under trust for private religious purposes which does not ensure for the benefit of the public (b) in the case of a trust for charitable purposes or a charitable institution any agricultural income thereof, if the trust or institution is created or established for the benefit of any particular religious community or caste; (c) in the case of a trust for charitable or religious purposes or a charitable or religious institution, any agricultural income thereof— (i) if under the terms of the trust or the rules governing the institution any part of such income ensures, or (ii) if any part of such income or any property of the trust or institution is diverted during the previous year used or applied for any purpose during the previous year. (4) Without prejudice to the generality of the provisions of clause (c) of sub-section (3) the income or the property of the trust or institution or any part of such income or property shall, for the purposes of that clause, be deemed to have been used or applied for a person referred to in sub-section (3)— (a) if any part of the income or property of the trust or institution continues to be lent to any person referred to in sub-section (5) for any period during the previous year without either adequate security or interest; (b) if any amount is paid by way of salary, allowance or otherwise during the previous year to any person referred to in sub-section (5) out of the resources of the trust or institution for services rendered by that person to such trust or institution and the amount so paid is in excess of what may be reasonably paid for such services; (c) if a substantial portion of the income or property of the trust or institution is diverted during the previous year in favour of any person referred to in sub-section (5). (d) if any funds of the trust or institution are or continue to be remain invested for any period during the previous years in any concern in which any person referred to in sub-section (5) has a substantial interest (5) The persons referred to in clause (c) of sub-section (3) are the following, namely— (a) the author of the trust or the founder of the institution: (b) any person who has made a substantial contribution to the trust or institution. (c) where such author, founder or person is a Hindu undivided family, a member of the family; (d) any trustee of the trust or manager (by whatever name called) of the institution; (e) any relative of any such author, founder, person or member as aforesaid. (f) any concern in which any of the persons referred to in clauses (a) (b) and (c) and has a substantial interest (6) For the purposes of this section— (a) "trust" includes any other legal obligation and "relative" in relation to an individual, means— (i) spouse of the individual, (ii) brother or sister of the individual, (iii) brother or sister of the spouse of the individual; (iv) any lineal ascendant or descendant of the individual (v) any lineal ascendant or descendant of the spouse of the individual; (vi) spouse of a person referred to in sub-clause (ii), sub-clause (iii), sub-clause (iv) or sub-clause (v); (vii) any lineal descendant of a brother or sister of either the individual or of the spouse of the individual. (b) a trust or institution created or established for the benefit of Scheduled Castes, Backward Classes, Scheduled Tribes or women and children shall not be deemed to be a trust or institution created or established for the benefit of a religious community or caste within the meaning of clause (b) of sub-section (3). (c) "charitable purposes" includes relief of the poor, education medical relief and the advancement of any other object of public utility (7) a person shall be deemed to have a substantial interest in a concern— (i) in a case where the concern is a company if its shares (not being shares entitled to a fixed rate of dividend whether with or without a further right to participate in profits) carrying not less than twenty per cent of the voting power are, at any time during the previous year, owned beneficially by such person or partly by such person and partly by one or more of the other persons referred to in sub-section (7). (ii) in the case of any other concern, if such person is entitled to and one or more of the other persons referred to in sub-section (5) are entitled in the aggregate, at any time during the previous year, to not less than twenty per cent of the profits of such concern."

In section 5 of the principal Act, for clause (a), the following shall be substituted, namely:— "(a) any sums paid in the previous year on account of— (i) land revenue or any tax in lieu thereof due to the Government the Sheendipadaravagi or the Shecpadam, (ii) Tinuruppuvaram, and (iii) local rates and cesses and municipal taxes, in respect of the land from which the agricultural income is derived."

Amendment of section 10—Section 40 of the principal Act shall be re-numbered as sub-section (1) of that section and after sub-section (1) so re-numbered the following sub-sections shall be inserted, namely:— "(2) If default is made in paying any amount referred to in sub-section (1) or any instalment thereof the whole of the amount outstanding on the date of default shall become immediately due and shall, subject to the charge of the Government in respect of basic tax payable under the provisions of the Kerala Land Tax Act, 1961 (13 of 1961), be a first charge on the properties of the assessee liable to pay such amount and where such amount or part thereof relates to the agricultural income from properties transferred by the assessee which is included in his total agricultural income in pursuance of sub-section (2), also on such properties (3) Where, during the pendency of any proceeding under this Act any assessee creates a charge on, or alienates, by way of sale, mortgage, exchange or any other mode of transfer, the property in respect of which agricultural income-tax is payable with intent to defraud the Government or such alienation shall be void as against any claim in respect of any amount that may be found payable by the assessee on completion of the said proceeding Provided that nothing in this sub section shall impair the rights of a transferee in good faith and for consideration."
In section 41 of the principal Act, in sub-section (4), for the words, brackets and figures "section 10" the words, brackets and figures "sub-section (1) of section 10" shall be substituted.
Chapter IX of the principal Act shall be omitted.
In the Schedule to the principal Act— (a) in Part I in sub-paragraph (1) of paragraph 11, for items 1 to 5 (both inclusive) the following items shall be substituted namely—

important_rules: Agricultural income derived from properties held under trust wholly for charitable or religious purposes is excluded if the income is applied to such purposes in the State.
Agricultural income derived from property held under trust in part only for charitable or religious purposes is excluded to the extent it is applied to such purposes in the State.
Tax on agricultural income from mortgaged land is payable by the mortgagee if it cannot be recovered from the mortgagor.

Certain income is not excluded from total agricultural income even if it's from a trust for private religious purposes, or for the benefit of a specific religious community or caste, or if diverted for certain purposes.
A person is deemed to have a substantial interest in a concern if they own 20% or more of its shares or profits.
Amendments to Section 5 regarding allowable deductions for land revenue, tax in lieu thereof, etc.
Amendment to Section 10 regarding default in payment and creation of charges on property.
Omission of Chapter IX of the principal Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, including charges on properties and potential recovery from mortgagees.

rights: Right to recover tax from mortgagee if not recovered from mortgagor.
Right to transfer property subject to tax.
duties: Duty to pay agricultural income-tax.
Duty to include certain income in total agricultural income as per the Act.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the amended Act.
Obligation to ensure that property is not alienated to defraud government claims.

key_procedures: Notification in the Gazette to bring the Act into force.
Substitution of sections and re-numbering of existing sections.
Imposition of first charge on properties for tax dues.
Declaration of alienation of property as void if made to defraud the government.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be the relevant tax administration authority in Kerala.
important_notes: The Act came into force on a date appointed by the Government via notification in the Gazette.
Received the assent of the Governor on the 19th day of March, 1974 and published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 306 dated 20th March 1974.
The definition of 'trust' is expanded to include legal obligations and 'relative' has a specific definition.
The definition of 'charitable purposes' is clarified.
Provisions for substantial interest in a concern are detailed.
The amendment regarding tax on agricultural income derived from mortgaged land is significant.

title: THE AGRICULTURAL INCOME TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1959.
purpose: To further amend the Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: The act applies to agricultural income tax in Kerala. Specifically, it addresses provisions for the financial year 1958-59 in respect of agricultural income derived from lands in the Malabar district and the remaining part of the State.

key_definitions.previous year: In clause (2) of section 2, for the purpose of assessment for the financial year 1958-59 in respect of agricultural income derived from lands in the Malabar district and the remaining part of the State, 'previous year' for the assessment for the financial year commencing from the 1st day of April, 1958 and so far as such assessment relates to the agricultural income derived from lands situated in the Malabar district referred to in sub-section (2) of section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (Central Act 37 of 1956), shall be the period commencing on the 1st day of November, 1956 and ending on the 31st day of March, 1958, or, if the accounts of the assessee have been made up to a date within the financial year ending on the 31st day of March, 1958, then, at the option of the assessee, the period commencing on the 1st day of November, 1956 and ending on the aforesaid date to which, the accounts have been so made up.
key_definitions.average annual income: Shall be an amount bearing to the aforesaid total agricultural income the same proportion as the period of twelve months bears to the period of previous year as defined in this section.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Agricultural Income-tax (Amendment) Act, 1959. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1957.

After section 2 of the Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950 (Act XXII of 1950), the following sections shall be added, namely: '2A. Special definition of 'previous year' for the purpose of assessment for the financial year 1958-59 in respect of agricultural income derived from lands in the Malabar district—Notwithstanding anything contained in clause (2) of section 2, 'previous year' for the assessment for the financial year commencing from the 1st day of April, 1958 and so far as such assessment relates to the agricultural income derived from lands situated in the Malabar district referred to in sub-section (2) of section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (Central Act 37 of 1956), shall be the period commencing on the 1st day of November, 1956 and ending on the 31st day of March, 1958, or, if the accounts of the assessee have been made up to a date within the financial year ending on the 31st day of March, 1958, then, at the option of the assessee, the period commencing on the 1st day of November, 1956 and ending on the aforesaid date to which, the accounts have been so made up. Provided that (i) notwithstanding anything contained in sections 3 and 5B, the agricultural income-tax and super-tax chargeable on the total agricultural income of the previous year as reckoned in this section shall be at the rates applicable to the 'average annual income' according to the Schedule, such 'average annual income' shall be an amount bearing to the aforesaid total agricultural income the same proportion as the period of twelve months bears to the period of the previous year as defined in this section; and (ii) the limit for exemption from chargeability to tax shall be determined with reference to the 'average annual income'. 2B. Special provision for the computation of total agricultural income for the assessment year 1958-59 of persons holding lands both in the Malabar district and the remaining part of the State—Notwithstanding anything contained in section 2A and section 4, the total agricultural income for the assessment year 1958-59 of any person holding lands situated both in the Malabar district referred to in sub-section (2) of section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (Central Act 37 of 1958), and in the remaining part of the State shall be the aggregate of the income derived from lands situated in the said Malabar district during the previous year as defined in section 2A chargeable to tax and the income derived from the lands situated in the remaining part of the State during the previous year as defined in clause (o) of section 2, chargeable to tax: Provided that the tax chargeable on the total agricultural income shall be at the rate applicable to an amount made up of the "average annual income" as determined in clause (i) of the proviso to section 2A and the agricultural income derived from the lands situated in the State excluding the said Malabar district during the previous year as defined in clause (o) of section 2 and the limit for exemption from chargeability to tax shall be determined with reference to the amount so made up.'

(1) The Agricultural Income-tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 1959 (2 of 1959), is hereby repealed. (2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken in the exercise of any powers conferred by or under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken in the exercise of the powers conferred by or under this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: The act is deemed to have come into force on April 1, 1957.
Rule 2: Special definition of 'previous year' for assessment year 1958-59 concerning agricultural income from lands in the Malabar district.
Rule 3: The limit for exemption from tax is determined with reference to the 'average annual income'.

rights: Assessee has the option to determine the 'previous year' based on their accounts for income derived from lands in the Malabar district for the assessment year 1958-59.
duties: Assessee must comply with the provisions for agricultural income tax and super-tax.
Assessee must adhere to the rates applicable to 'average annual income'.
obligations: Obligation to pay agricultural income tax and super-tax based on the total agricultural income and relevant definitions.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Defining the 'previous year' for the assessment year 1958-59 for agricultural income from lands in the Malabar district, considering income from both Malabar and other parts of the State. This involves calculating the aggregate income and determining tax rates based on 'average annual income'.
Procedure 2: Repeal of the Agricultural Income-tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 1959, with a saving clause to ensure validity of actions taken under the Ordinance.
administration: Likely the State Government of Kerala or its relevant finance/revenue department, based on the context of agricultural income tax.
important_notes: The act contains a special definition of 'previous year' for a specific assessment period (1958-59) and geographic region (Malabar district).
The calculation of tax and exemption limits are tied to the 'average annual income'.
Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance of 1959 are considered valid under this Act.

title: The Agricultural Income Tax (Amendment) Act, 1961
purpose: To further amend the Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1950, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala, specifically referencing the 'Kerala Municipal Laws'.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Agricultural Income Tax (Amendment) Act, 1961, and it shall be deemed to have come into force with effect on and from the 1st day of April, 1951.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 5 of Act XXII of 1950
main_sections.description: Amends section 5 of the Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1950. The amendment refers to 'Explanation 1' and 'Explanation 2' and appears to modify how agricultural income is defined and assessed, particularly concerning deductions for cultivation, upkeep, or maintenance of plantations.

Provides that notwithstanding anything contained in any judgment, decree, or order of any court, all taxes levied, assessed, or collected under the principal Act shall for all purposes be deemed to be and to have always been levied, assessed, or collected under that Act as amended by this Act. It also validates all proceedings taken, orders passed, and acts done by any officer, authority, or tribunal under the principal Act. However, it states that this validation does not affect the publication of the Act in the Gazette or provisions of this Act.
Repeals The Kerala Agricultural Income Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 1961 (Ordinance No. 3 of 1961).

important_rules: Agricultural income is to be computed after allowing deductions for cultivation, upkeep, or maintenance of plantations and expenses of like nature.
The Act is deemed to have come into force on April 1, 1951.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned but implied to be tax authorities under the Agricultural Income Tax Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the assessment and collection of taxes as per the Act and its amendments.

duties: Duty to pay agricultural income tax as per the provisions of the Act.

key_procedures: Assessment and collection of agricultural income tax.
Deduction of expenses related to cultivation, upkeep, and maintenance of plantations.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be the tax administration of the Kerala Government.
important_notes: This Act amends the Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1950 (Act XXII of 1950).
Proceedings taken under the principal Act are validated.
The Act had retrospective effect from April 1, 1951.
The Kerala Agricultural Income Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 1961 (Ordinance No. 3 of 1961) is repealed.

title: THE AGRICULTURAL INCOME TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1964
purpose: To further amend the Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950.
scope: Applies to agricultural income, as amended by this Act, for the purposes hereinafter appearing. The Act appears to be enacted in the Fifteenth Year of the Republic of India.

key_definitions.Hindu undivided family: Includes an undivided Marumakkathayam tarwad or tharavadh, an undivided Aliyasanthana family or branch or Marumakkathayam tarwad or tharavadh, and an undivided Mitakshara family.
key_definitions.cultivator or receiver of rent: Includes a person whose business consists in the ordinary and usual course of its day-to-day transactions of acquiring or disposing of crops or of receiving or transmitting the same for consideration.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Agricultural Income Tax (Amendment) Act, 1964' and specifies its commencement date. It also states that the Act shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1951, and that the remaining provisions shall come into force on such date as the Government may notify in the Gazette.

Amends Section 2 of the Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950 (Act XXVI of 1950). It introduces amendments to clause (a) and clause (u) of sub-section (2) of Section 2, which relate to definitions. For instance, it clarifies the definition of 'Hindu undivided family' and 'cultivator or receiver of rent'.

Amends Section 3 of the principal Act. It substitutes words in sub-section (1) of section 3 of the principal Act, which appears to relate to the application of the Act to Hindu undivided families and other governed by law like Nambudiris.
Omits Section 3A of the principal Act.

Amends Section 10 of the principal Act. It substitutes provisions within sub-section (1) of section 10, specifically relating to the treatment of partitions in Hindu undivided families and the conditions for such treatment. It also introduces a new clause (e) to sub-section (1).

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 16
main_sections.description: Substitutes a new section for Section 16 of the principal Act. The new section pertains to the Appellate Tribunal, outlining its constitution (Chairman and two other members), the qualifications of the Chairman, and the process of appointment and filling vacancies. It also details how the Tribunal will function, including decisions made by a Bench and the referral of matters to a Bench consisting of all members.

Amends Section 18 of the principal Act. It deals with the assessment of Hindu undivided families and provides details on how partitions will be assessed, especially when an order is made after the commencement of the Act.
Amends Section 21 of the principal Act. It substitutes the expression 'Agricultural Income-tax Officer' with 'the Income-tax Officer' in sub-section (1) of section 21.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 29
main_sections.description: Substitutes a new section for Section 29 of the principal Act. The new section appears to relate to the assessment and reassessment of agricultural income, setting time limits for such actions, especially in cases where a notice has been issued or an order made.
