It also provides for exceptions to these time limits.

Amends Section 31 of the principal Act. It adds a further proviso to sub-section (1) of section 31, concerning the powers of the Agricultural Income-tax Officer to inspect records and the conditions under which this can be done.

Amends Section 33 of the principal Act. It renumbers sub-section (1) of section 33 and also renumbers the following sub-section. It also introduces a new sub-section (2) concerning the insertion of new text related to the time limits for making orders of assessment or reassessment.
Omits Section 37 of the principal Act.
Amends Section 42 of the principal Act. It omits the words 'or tarwad' and 'a Hindu undivided family' in sub-section (1) of section 42.
Amends Section 56 of the principal Act. It substitutes the words 'Hindu undivided family' and 'Marumakkathayam tarwad' with 'Hindu undivided family' and 'Marumakkathayam tarwad' respectively.
Amends Section 57 of the principal Act. It substitutes the words 'Hindu undivided family' and 'Marumakkathayam tarwad' with 'Hindu undivided family' and 'Marumakkathayam tarwad' respectively.

Amends Section 58 of the principal Act. It substitutes the words 'Hindu undivided family' and 'Marumakkathayam tarwad' with 'Hindu undivided family' and 'Marumakkathayam tarwad' respectively. It also substitutes other words in clause (e) and sub-section (1) of section 10.

Amends Section 64 of the principal Act. It substitutes the words 'Hindu undivided family' or 'Aliyasanthana family or branch or Marumakkathayam tarwad' with 'Hindu undivided family' or 'Marumakkathayam tarwad'. It also substitutes the words 'or to the Manager or Karanavan or any adult member of the family or tarwad' with 'or to the Manager or Karanavan or any adult member of the family'.
Amends Section 67 of the principal Act. It concerns the substitution of words in clause (e) of sub-section (2) of section 67.
Amends the Schedule to the principal Act. In Part I, it amends the rates of agricultural income tax. In Part II, it makes substitutions concerning Hindu undivided families and their partitions.

important_rules: Rule regarding the computation of period of limitation for purposes of proceedings stayed by an order of injunction.
Rules regarding the insertion of new text into section 31 and section 33 of the principal Act.
Rules regarding the amendment of the Schedule, specifically the rates of agricultural income tax and provisions related to Hindu undivided families and partitions.

rights: Right to claim a share on partition in a Hindu undivided family under certain conditions.
Right to appeal to the Appellate Tribunal.
Right to receive rent as a cultivator.
duties: Duty to pay agricultural income tax.
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act and its amendments.
obligations: Obligation for Hindu undivided families to have their partitions assessed according to the Act.
Obligation for members and groups of members of Hindu undivided families to be jointly and severally liable for the total agricultural income received by or on behalf of the family.

key_procedures: Procedure for amendment of various sections of the principal Act, including substitution of clauses, omission of sections, and renumbering of sub-sections.
Procedure for the constitution and functioning of the Appellate Tribunal.
Procedure for assessment and reassessment of agricultural income, including time limits and exceptions.
Procedure for the application of the Act to Hindu undivided families and the assessment of their partitions.
Procedure for publishing regulations made under sub-section (4) of the substituted section 16 in the Gazette.
administration: The Agricultural Income-tax Officer is mentioned as an authority responsible for certain actions under the Act. The Appellate Tribunal is established for appeals.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1951, with remaining provisions to be notified.
Clarifications on 'Hindu undivided family' definition, including provisions for partitions and implications for members.
Provisions regarding the Appellate Tribunal's composition and decision-making process.
Specific rates of agricultural income tax are detailed in the Schedule for different income brackets.
The Act also addresses specific provisions for tarwads, tharavadhs, and Aliyasanthana families.

title: THE AGRICULTURAL INCOME TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1976
purpose: To further amend the Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1950, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to agricultural income as computed by the Agricultural Income Tax Officer in Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Agricultural Income Tax (Amendment) Act, 1976.

Amends section 16 of the principal Act (The Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1950) concerning the provisions related to the Appellate Tribunal, including its composition, powers, and the procedure for deciding cases where members differ in opinion.
Amends section 35 of the principal Act by substituting 'five years' for 'three years' wherever they occur.

Amends section 64 of the principal Act by substituting a new sub-section (1) regarding required notice to be served or given for the purpose of this Act and its rules. It details how the notice should be served or given, including to persons or their representatives, and what to do if the person cannot be found.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 66
main_sections.description: Substitutes section 66 of the principal Act with a new section titled 'Power to order production of accounts and powers of entry, inspection, etc.'. This new section grants powers to Agricultural Income Tax Officers to order production of accounts and documents, conduct searches, seize documents, and enter premises.

Repeals The Agricultural Income Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 1975 (13 of 1975). It also states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act if this Act had come into force on the 27th day of October, 1975.

important_rules: Rule: Sub-section (1) of Section 64 of the principal Act is substituted with new provisions regarding notice service.
Rule: Section 66 is substituted with new provisions detailing the powers of an Agricultural Income Tax Officer regarding production of accounts, inspection, and seizure of documents.

Rule: The powers conferred by sub-sections (3) and (5) of the new section 66 shall include the power to break open any box or receptacle/place and to seal any box or receptacle/building, and then to break open such box, receptacle, godown or building on the authority of an authorisation in writing by the Board of Revenue.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Agricultural Income Tax Officer, and potentially other officers authorized by the Board of Revenue.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through powers of inspection, search, seizure of documents and accounts, and entry into premises.

rights: Right of an assessee or any other person to be served with due notice under Section 64.
Right to have seized accounts, registers, records or other documents returned beyond a specified period, unless required for prosecution.
duties: Duty of any assessee or any other person to produce accounts and documents when required by an Agricultural Income Tax Officer.
Duty to comply with requisition made by an Agricultural Income Tax Officer.
Duty of any person to allow entry and inspection of vessels, vehicles, or premises by an Agricultural Income Tax Officer.
obligations: Obligation to allow inspection and seizure of documents deemed relevant for proceedings under the Act.
Obligation to make residential accommodation available for search or inspection under certain conditions.

key_procedures: Procedure for service of notice under Section 64, including substitute service and service on persons not found.
Procedure for ordering production of accounts and documents, including their nature and relevance.
Procedure for inspection and search of premises, vessels, and vehicles.
Procedure for seizure of accounts, registers, records, or other documents.
Procedure for the return of seized documents after a specified period.
Procedure for breaking open and sealing premises or receptacles, and subsequent entry.
Procedure for the constitution and functioning of the Appellate Tribunal, including quorum and decision-making when members differ.
administration: Agricultural Income Tax Department (implied)
important_notes: Section 16(3)(a) lists three ways the functions of the Appellate Tribunal may be performed: by a Bench consisting of the Chairman and any other member, by a Bench consisting of the Chairman and two other members, or by a Bench consisting of two or more members other than the Chairman.

The Chairman or any other member of the Appellate Tribunal may, if sitting singly, dispose of any case which pertains to an assessee whose total agricultural income does not exceed fifteen thousand rupees.
If the Chairman is not a member of a Bench, the decision of the majority of the members of the Tribunal who have heard the case shall be deemed to be the decision of the Bench.

If any officer below the rank of an Agricultural Income Tax Officer has reason to believe that an assessee is trying to evade tax, he may, for reasons to be recorded, search and search any place where the assessee or such other person is keeping or is reasonably believed to be keeping any accounts, registers, records or other documents relating to his agricultural income.
For the purposes of Section 66, 'place' includes any godown, building, vessel, vehicle, box or receptacle.
All searches under Section 66 shall, so far as may be, be made in accordance with the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Central Act 2 of 1974).

Seized accounts, registers, records or other documents shall not be retained by the officer seizing them beyond a period of thirty days from the date of the seizure, except with the permission of the next higher authority, unless they are required for any prosecution under this Act.

The power to break open any box or receptacle or the door of any premises shall be exercised only after the owner or any other person in occupation of the premises fails or refuses to open the door on being called upon to do so.
The Agricultural Income Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 1975 (13 of 1975), is hereby repealed.

Anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act if this Act had come into force on the 27th day of October, 1975.

title: The Agricultural Income-tax (Amendment) Act, 1970
purpose: To amend the Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950, for the purposes therein appearing.
scope: Applies to the agricultural income-tax in Kerala.

key_definitions.company: In section 56 of the principal Act, the word "company" shall be omitted. In the second proviso, the words "not being a company" shall be omitted. The following Explanation shall be inserted at the end, namely: – "Explanation.—For the removal of doubts it is hereby declared that no super-tax shall be chargeable in respect of the total agricultural income of a company."

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Agricultural Income-tax (Amendment) Act, 1970. Sections 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7 are deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1970. Section 4 shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1958 and the remaining provisions of this Act shall come into force at once.

Amends section 2 of the Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950 (XXII of 1950). It re-letters clause (h) and defines 'company' and 'domestic company'. It also re-letters clause (kk) and defines 'foreign company'.
Amends section 3 of the principal Act, in sub-section (3), for the words "six thousand rupees", in both the places where they occur, the words "seven thousand rupees" shall be substituted.

Amends section 35 of the principal Act, in sub-section (2), the following proviso is substituted, namely: – "Provided further that nothing contained in this section limiting the time within which any action may be taken or any order, assessment or re-assessment may be made shall apply to— (a) a re-assessment made under section 19; or (b) an assessment or re-assessment made in consequence of, or to give effect to, (i) any finding or direction contained, in, an order under section 31 or section 32 or section 34 or section 60; or (ii) an order or decision of any court."

Amends section 56 of the principal Act. In the opening paragraph, the word "company," shall be omitted. In the second proviso, the words "not being a company" shall be omitted. The following Explanation shall be inserted at the end, namely:— "Explanation.—For the removal of doubts it is hereby declared that no super-tax shall be chargeable in respect of the total agricultural income of a company."
Amends section 57 of the principal Act.

Amends the Schedule to the principal Act. For Part I, the following shall be substituted, namely:— "PART I (See section 3) (Rates of Agricultural Income-tax) (1) In the case of a person other than a company— A. Where the total agricultural income does not exceed ten thousand rupees— Rate 1. Where the total agricultural income does not exceed Rs. 7,500 Rs. 175. 2. Where the total agricultural income exceeds Rs. 7,500 but does not exceed Rs. 10,000 Rs. 400. B. Where the total agricultural income exceeds ten thousand rupees— 1. On the first Rs. 2,000 of the total agricultural income Nil. 2. On the next Rs. 2,500 of the total agricultural income Five paise in the rupee. 3. On the next Rs. 5,000 of the total agricultural income Eleven paise in the rupee. 4. On the next Rs. 5,000 of the total agricultural income Eighteen paise in the rupee. 5. On the balance of the total agricultural income Twenty-five paise in the rupee. Provided that no agricultural income-tax shall be payable on a total agricultural income which is less than five thousand rupees. The limit referred to in the above proviso shall be seven thousand rupees in the case of every Hindu undivided family which satisfies as at the end of the previous year the condition that it consists of at least five members entitled to claim a share on partition. Provided further that the agricultural income-tax payable shall in no case exceed one-half of the amount by which the total agricultural income exceeds five thousand rupees or seven thousand rupees, as the case may be. (2) In the case of a domestic company— A. Where the total agricultural income does not exceed Rs 25,000 45 per cent of the total agricultural income B. Where the total agricultural income exceeds Rs. 25,000 but does not exceed Rs. 1 lakh 50 per cent of the total agricultural income. Provided that the agricultural income-tax payable shall not exceed the aggregate of— (a) the agricultural income-tax which would have been payable by the company if its total agricultural income had been Rs. 1 lakh; and (b) 80 per cent of the amount by which the total agricultural income exceeds Rs 1 lakh. C Where the total agricultural income exceeds Rs 1 lakh but does not exceed Rs. 3 lakhs 55 per cent of the total agricultural income. Provided that the agricultural income-tax payable shall not exceed the aggregate of— (a) the agricultural income-tax which would have been payable by the company if its total agricultural income had been Rs. 3 lakhs; and (b) 80 per cent of the amount by which the total agricultural income exceeds Rs. 3 lakhs. D. Where the total agricultural income exceeds Rs. 3 lakhs but does not exceed Rs. 10 lakhs 60 per cent of the total agricultural income. Provided that the agricultural income-tax payable shall not exceed the aggregate of— (a) the agricultural income-tax which would have been payable by the company if its total agricultural income had been Rs. 3 lakhs; and (b) 80 per cent of the amount by which the total agricultural income exceeds Rs. 3 lakhs. E. Where the total agricultural income exceeds Rs 10 lakhs 65 per cent of the total agricultural income: Provided that the agricultural income-tax payable shall not exceed the aggregate of— (a) the agricultural income-tax which would have been payable by the company if its total agricultural income had been Rs. 10 lakhs; and (b) 80 per cent of the amount by which the total agricultural income exceeds Rs. 10 lakhs. (3) In the case of a foreign company, 75 per cent of the total agricultural income " (ii) In Part II, — (a) in paragraph A, the words, "not being a case to which paragraph B applies" shall be omitted, (b) paragraph B shall be omitted

Notwithstanding any judgment, decree or order of any court, tribunal or other authority to the contrary, any assessment or re-assessment of agricultural income made or purporting to have been made under section 35 of the principal Act before the 27th day of April, 1970, shall be deemed to be valid and effective as if such assessment or re-assessment had been made under the said section as amended by this Act, and accordingly— (a) all acts, proceedings or things done or taken by any officer or authority in connection with such assessment or re-assessment shall, for all purposes, be deemed to be, and to have always been, done or taken in accordance with law; (b) all taxes on agricultural income charged or collected or purporting to have been charged or collected in consequence of such assessment or re-assessment shall, for all purposes, be deemed to be, and to have always been, charged or collected in accordance with law; (c) no suit or other proceeding shall be maintained or continued in any court, tribunal or other authority for the refund of any such tax so collected; (d) no court shall enforce any decree or order directing the refund of any such tax so collected; (e) any such tax charged in consequence of such assessment or re-assessment before the 27th day of April, 1970, but not collected before that date, may be recovered in the manner provided under the principal Act as amended by this Act and the rules made thereunder; and (f) where no such tax was charged before the 27th day of April, 1970, in consequence of such assessment or re-assessment, such tax may be charged and collected under the principal Act as amended by this Act and the rules made thereunder: Provided that nothing contained in this section shall render any person liable to be convicted of an offence in respect of anything done or omitted to be done by him before the 27th day of April, 1970, If such act or omission would not be an offence under the principal Act but for the provisions of this Act. (2) For the removal of doubts, it is hereby declared that nothing in sub-section (1) shall be construed as preventing any person from claiming refund of any tax paid by him in excess of the amount due from him under the principal Act as amended by this Act.
This section is not detailed in the provided pages but is listed in the contents.

important_rules: Sections 2, 3, 5, 6, and 7 are deemed to have come into force on 1st April 1970.
Section 4 is deemed to have come into force on 1st April 1958.
Remaining provisions come into force at once.
No super-tax is chargeable on the total agricultural income of a company.
The tax rates for agricultural income are specified in the Schedule.
For a domestic company, the agricultural income-tax payable shall not exceed a certain aggregate amount based on income thresholds.
For a foreign company, the rate is 75% of the total agricultural income.

penalties: No penalty explicitly mentioned for the amendments themselves in the provided text.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Implied to be the tax authorities responsible for agricultural income tax in Kerala.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment and collection of agricultural income tax as per the Act and its amendments.

rights: Right to claim refund of tax paid in excess of the amount due under the amended Act, for actions taken before 27th April 1970.
duties: Duty to pay agricultural income tax as per the Act.
Duty to comply with assessments and re-assessments.
obligations: Obligation to pay tax correctly based on the amended rates and provisions.

key_procedures: Amendment of sections of the principal Act to modify definitions, tax rates, and assessment provisions.
Validation of past assessments and re-assessments made under section 35 before 27th April 1970.
Procedural steps for charging and collecting tax, including provisions for recovery of tax not collected before a certain date.
administration: The administration of this Act would fall under the purview of the State Government of Kerala, likely through its revenue or finance department and associated tax collection agencies.
important_notes: The Act is a further amendment to the Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950.
Specific dates for commencement of different sections are provided.
Validation of past assessments and re-assessments are included.
No person shall be liable for an offence for acts or omissions before 27th April 1970, if they were not offences under the original Act.
The Schedule provides the rates of agricultural income-tax for individuals and companies.

title: THE AGRICULTURAL INCOME-TAX (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 1971
purpose: To amend the Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Kerala, and it amends the Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950.

key_definitions.Judicial Officer: The words 'who is or has been a Judicial Officer, the words "who is, or has been, or is qualified to be appointed as, a Judicial Officer" shall be substituted.
key_definitions.salestax practitioner: means any person possessing the qualifications prescribed for a salestax practitioner under the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963 (15 of 1963).

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Agricultural Income-tax (Second Amendment) Act, 1971.

Amends section 16 of the Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950 (XXII of 1950). It modifies the wording related to Judicial Officers and introduces provisions for disqualification and appointment of additional members to the Appellate Tribunal.
Amends section 61 of the principal Act. It introduces the definition of 'salestax practitioner' and provides for its insertion in the relevant clause.

important_rules: Any member who has previously dealt with any case coming up before the Appellate Tribunal in any other capacity or is personally interested in any case coming up before the Appellate Tribunal, shall be disqualified to hear that case.

Where any member of the Appellate Tribunal is disqualified under sub-section (3A) to hear any case coming up before the Tribunal and the remaining members are divided in their opinion on any point connected with that case, the Government may appoint a person qualified to be appointed as a member of the Appellate Tribunal as an additional member of the Tribunal and, thereupon, that point shall be referred to a Bench consisting of the members who are not disqualified and such additional member.

If two members of the Appellate Tribunal are disqualified under sub-section (3A) to hear any case coming up before the Tribunal, the Government may appoint a person qualified to be appointed as a member of the Appellate Tribunal as an additional member of the Tribunal and, thereupon, a Bench consisting of the members who is not disqualified and such additional member may dispose of that case.

Where any case is heard by a Bench referred to in sub-section (3C) and the members are divided in their opinion on any point, the Government may appoint a person qualified to be appointed as a member of the Appellate Tribunal as a second additional member of the Tribunal and, thereupon, that point shall be referred for decision to a Bench consisting of the member who is not disqualified under sub-section (3A), the additional member appointed under sub-section (3C) and the second additional member appointed under this sub-section.

An additional member appointed under sub-section (3B) or sub-section (3C) or a second additional member appointed under sub-section (3D) shall cease to hold office on the disposal of the case for which he was appointed.

rights: Right to have a case heard by a tribunal where a member is not disqualified.
Right to have a case heard by a Bench including an additional or second additional member when there is a division of opinion.

key_procedures: Disqualification of Appellate Tribunal members if they have prior involvement or personal interest in a case.
Appointment of additional members to the Appellate Tribunal in cases of disqualification or divided opinions among existing members.
Referral of points of decision to a Bench including the appointed additional member(s) in specific circumstances.
administration: The administration of this act would fall under the purview of the State Government of Kerala, likely through its Finance or Revenue department, responsible for taxation laws.
important_notes: The Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 337, dated 31st July, 1971.
This is the second amendment to The Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1971, implying previous amendments.

title: The Agricultural Income Tax (Second Amendment) Act, 1961
purpose: To further amend the Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1950.

key_definitions.agricultural income: Income derived from any agricultural land by any tenant, lessee, holder or owner thereof for the cultivation of plants, which no agricultural income has been derived during the previous year.
key_definitions.assessee: Person or entity liable to pay tax.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Agricultural Income Tax (Second Amendment) Act, 1961. It shall come into force with effect from and on the 1st day of April, 1961.

Amends the Schedule to the Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950, in Part II of the Schedule. It substitutes specific items related to 'On the balance of the total agricultural income' with revised rates ('Thirty-four naye paise' and 'Thirty-one naye paise').

important_rules: The amendments made by this Act shall come into force with effect from and on the 1st day of April, 1961.
Specific items in Part II of the Schedule of the Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950, are to be substituted with new rates for 'On the balance of the total agricultural income'.
key_procedures: Commencement of the Act: 1st day of April, 1961.
Substitution of rates in the Schedule: Specific items in Part II of the Schedule are to be replaced with updated figures for agricultural income tax calculation.
important_notes: The Act is published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 30th March 1961.
The Agricultural Income Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 1961 (Ordinance 1 of 1961), is hereby repealed.

title: THE AGRICULTURAL INCOME TAX (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 1976
purpose: To further amend the Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1950, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to agricultural income tax in Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Agricultural Income Tax (Second Amendment) Act, 1976, and specifies its commencement date as the 1st day of April, 1976.

Amends section 3 of the Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1950 (XXII of 1950), specifically sub-section (3), by substituting the words 'and whose agricultural income exceeds seven thousand rupees' with 'or to seven thousand rupees whichever is higher'.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new section after section 18
main_sections.description: Inserts a new section, '18A. Agricultural income for purposes of assessment of certain assessees to remain uncharged for three years', which details conditions under which agricultural income will not be changed for assessment purposes for three years, particularly when it does not exceed twenty-five thousand rupees in the two financial years immediately preceding the financial year of assessment. It also outlines specific tax rates for different income brackets.

Amends the Schedule to the principal Act. It omits the word and figure 'Part I' and substitutes a paragraph relating to the total agricultural income not exceeding Rs. 8,000, and then provides a graduated scale of tax rates for income exceeding Rs. 8,000 up to Rs. 70,000, and a further rate for income exceeding Rs. 70,000. It also makes a substitution for figures '75' to '75' in paragraph (c) of sub-section (3).
Repeals the Agricultural Income Tax (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1976 (7 of 1976), and saves anything done or action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance.

important_rules: Rule 1: Agricultural income for assessment of certain assessees will remain unchanged for three years if certain conditions regarding income levels in preceding financial years are met.
Rule 2: Tax on agricultural income is levied at progressive rates based on income brackets specified in the Schedule.
key_procedures: Procedure 1: Assessment of agricultural income for certain assessees will remain uncharged for three years under specific income thresholds in preceding financial years.
Procedure 2: Calculation of tax on agricultural income follows a graduated scale based on the total agricultural income.
Procedure 3: The Ordinance of 1976 is repealed, and actions taken under the principal Act are saved.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 19th day of November, 1976, and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 683, dated 20th November, 1976.
The commencement date of the Act is April 1, 1976.
Section 2(3) of the principal Act is amended regarding the threshold for agricultural income to be considered higher.

title: THE AGRICULTURAL INCOME-TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1981
purpose: To further amend the Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to agricultural income derived from the cultivation of paddy, tapioca, plantain, ginger, ragi, pulses, sesamum, vegetables, sweet potato and tubers, and agricultural income derived from property held under trust wholly for charitable or religious purposes in the State.

key_definitions.agricultural income: Any agricultural income derived by cultivation of paddy, tapioca, plantain, ginger, ragi, pulses, sesamum, vegetables, sweet potato and tubers; any agricultural income derived from property held under trust wholly for charitable or religious purposes in the State.
key_definitions.scheduled bank: Means the State Bank of India constituted under the State Bank of India Act, 1955, a subsidiary bank as defined in the State Bank of India (Subsidiary Banks) Act, 1959, a corresponding new bank constituted under section 3 of the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1970, or any other bank, being a bank included in the second schedule to the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called The Agricultural Income-tax (Amendment) Act, 1981 and that Section 4 shall come into force on the 1st day of April, 1982 and the remaining provisions of this Act shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1981.

Amends section 4 of the Principal Act by inserting new clauses (aa), (b), (c), and (d) and an Explanation, which deal with how agricultural income is applied to charitable or religious purposes and the calculation of such income when it falls short of seventy-five per cent of the agricultural income.
Inserts a new section 61A titled 'Rounding off of agricultural income, etc.' which provides rules for rounding off the amount of total agricultural income and the amount of tax.
Amends the Schedule to the Principal Act by substituting paragraph (1) with new provisions related to tax rates based on total agricultural income.

important_rules: Any agricultural income derived from property held under trust wholly for charitable or religious purposes in the State shall not be applied to such purposes to the extent that the income so accumulated or set apart is not in excess of twenty-five per cent of the agricultural income from such property.
Agricultural income deemed to be the income of the person in receipt of the income, subject to certain conditions regarding its application or deposit.

Rules for rounding off agricultural income, where if the last figure in the amount is five or more, the amount shall be increased to the next higher amount, and if it is less than five, it shall be rounded off to the nearest lower amount.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Agricultural Income-tax Officer
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment and imposition of tax based on the provisions of the Act and its amendments.

rights: Right to apply agricultural income derived from property held under trust wholly for charitable or religious purposes, up to seventy-five percent of the income.
duties: Duty to apply agricultural income derived from property held under trust wholly for charitable or religious purposes in the State.
obligations: Obligation to have agricultural income to be deemed as the income of the person in receipt of the income when certain conditions are met regarding its application or deposit.

key_procedures: Calculation of agricultural income derived from property held under trust for charitable or religious purposes, with a provision for accumulation or setting apart up to twenty-five percent of the income.
Procedure for rounding off agricultural income and tax amounts to the nearest multiple of ten rupees.
Procedure for assessing tax based on different slabs of total agricultural income as defined in the amended Schedule.
administration: Kerala State Government (implied through the Act title and gazette notification reference)
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 23rd day of September, 1981 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 745 dated the 24th September, 1981.
The provisions of Section 4 come into force on 1st April 1982, while other provisions are deemed to have come into force on 1st April 1981.

title: THE AGRICULTURAL INCOME-TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1980
purpose: To further amend the Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to agricultural income tax in Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Agricultural Income-tax (Amendment) Act, 1980. It shall have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1980.
In section 2 of the Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950 (XXII of 1950) (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), in clause (a), the Explanation shall be omitted.

Inserts a new section 17A regarding self-assessment. This section details how to furnish returns, accompany them with proof of payment, and what happens if a person fails to pay tax or any part thereof. It also covers recovery of tax and penalties.

In subsection (1) of section 31 of the principal Act, after the proviso, the following proviso shall be inserted: "Provided further that no appeal shall be entertained under this section unless it is accompanied by satisfactory proof of the payment of the tax admitted by the appellant to be due."

In subsection (1) of section 34 of the principal Act, the following proviso shall be inserted at the end: "Provided also that no application for revision shall be entertained under this section unless it is accompanied by satisfactory proof of the payment of the tax admitted by the petitioner to be due."
Amends the Schedule regarding the tax rate for agricultural income. It provides a tiered system based on the total agricultural income for companies and other individuals.

important_rules: Rule: Returns must be accompanied by proof of payment of tax.
Rule: Appeals and revisions are not entertained without satisfactory proof of payment of admitted tax.
Rule: Specific tax rates apply based on the total agricultural income, with different rates for individuals and companies.

penalties: Penalty equal to two per cent of such tax or part thereof, or as the case may be, recovered from him by way of penalty for every month during which the default continues.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Assessing authority
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By way of penalty; assessment of tax due; notice of demand.

rights: Right to furnish a return of total agricultural income.
duties: Duty to furnish a return of total agricultural income.
Duty to pay tax on agricultural income.
obligations: Obligation to provide satisfactory proof of tax payment for appeals and revisions.

key_procedures: Procedure: Filing self-assessment returns accompanied by proof of payment.
Procedure: Recovery of tax and penalties by the assessing authority.
Procedure: Appeal and revision processes requiring payment of admitted tax.
administration: Agricultural Income-tax Department (implied from the Act's focus)
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 19th day of August, 1980 and was published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 392 dated 20th August, 1980.
The commencement date for the Act is April 1, 1980.
Explanations in clause (a) of section 2 of the principal Act are omitted.

title: The Agricultural Income-Tax (Amendment) Act, 1967
purpose: To further amend the Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950.
scope: Applies to agricultural income, specifically amending the rates of tax for certain income slabs and modifying provisions related to expenditure incurred by individuals out of their income.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Agricultural Income-tax (Amendment) Act, 1967, and it shall come into force on a date notified by the Government in the Gazette.
Amends section 17 of the Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950, regarding the insertion of words and the expenditure incurred by individuals out of their income at the end of the section.
Amends the Schedule to the principal Act by substituting "naye paise" with "paise" wherever they occur.

important_rules: The Act comes into force on a date specified by the Government via notification in the Gazette.
Rates for agricultural income tax are amended as specified in the Schedule, affecting slabs of Rs. 15,000 and the balance of total agricultural income.
The term "naye paise" is replaced with "paise" throughout the Schedule.
key_procedures: Government notification in the Gazette to bring the Act into force.
Amendment of Section 17 of the principal Act concerning expenditure.
Substitution of currency terms in the Schedule.
administration: The Kerala State Government (implied by reference to Kerala Gazette).
important_notes: Published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 164, dated 28th August, 1967.

title: The Arthapalisa, Jenmibhogam and Karathilchilavu (Abolition) Act, 2007
purpose: To abolish the Arthapalisa, Jenmibhogam and Karathilchilavu payments and to provide for compensation thereof.
scope: Applies to the territory of the State of Kerala. Covers Arthapalisa, Jenmibhogam and Karathilchilavu payments related to land tenure in Travancore.

key_definitions.appointed day: The date on which this Act comes into force.
key_definitions.Arthapalisa: Allowance payable by the Government either in paddy or in money to the option of the Jenmi, prior to the Proclamation, excluding political or family pension.
key_definitions.Jenmi: A person entitled to receive Arthapalisa, Jenmibhogam or Karathilchilavu from the Government.
key_definitions.Jenmibhogam: A portion of paddy assessed as tax on some of the lands classified in the Revenue Settlement of 1061 M.E. as Pandarapattom and paid to the Jenmies in recognition of their claims.
key_definitions.Karathilchilavu: A pension or allowance payable by the Government to the holders of certain lands who were entitled to pensions or allowances from the Government, and were allowed to set off such dues from the land tax payable by them for those lands.
key_definitions.Proclamation: The Proclamation issued by His Highness the Maharaja of Travancore on the 27th day of August, 1917.
key_definitions.TahSildar: The Tahsildar of the taluk in which the Government Treasury from which the Arthapalisa or Jenmibhogam is payable is situated, or any other officer empowered by the Government to exercise the powers of a Tahsildar.

main_sections.description: Names the Act, specifies its territorial extent (State of Kerala), and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Government via notification.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Arthapalisa', 'Jenmi', 'Jenmibhogam', 'Karathilchilavu', 'Proclamation', and 'TahSildar'.

main_sections.section_title: Abolition of Arthapalisa, Jenmibhogam and Karathilchilavu
main_sections.description: Declares the abolition of Arthapalisa, Jenmibhogam, and Karathilchilavu from the appointed day. Specifies that the Government will not be liable to pay these to the Jenmi, and the Jenmi's right to receive them will stand extinguished.

main_sections.section_title: Amount of compensation to be paid
main_sections.description: Specifies that compensation is to be paid in cash and outlines the calculation method: twelve times the money value of the Arthapalisa or Jenmibhogam, or the commutation rate specified in sub-section (2). It also states that the commutation rate of paddy in respect of Arthapalisa, Jenmibhogam and Karathilchilavu shall be ninety rupees per standard para.

main_sections.section_title: Compensation to be paid in cash
main_sections.description: Reiterates that the compensation payable under this Act shall be paid in cash.

main_sections.section_title: Proceedings relating to payment of compensation to lie before Tahsildar
main_sections.description: States that all proceedings related to the assessment of compensation payable to a Jenmi under this Act, and the payment of the same, will be handled by the Tahsildar.

main_sections.section_title: Compensation rolls to be prepared by the Tahsildar
main_sections.description: Mandates the Tahsildar to prepare a draft compensation roll for every Jenmi, detailing the Arthapalisa, Jenmibhogam or Karathilchilavu, the amount payable annually, and other prescribed particulars.

Requires the draft compensation roll to be published in the Gazette and in other prescribed ways, with a notice inviting objections from interested persons. It also outlines the process for serving notice on family members of the Jenmi and for filing objections.

main_sections.section_title: Order of Tahsildar to be deemed to be decree of Civil Court
main_sections.description: States that the order of the Tahsildar in deciding a claim or objection under section 8 will be deemed to be a decree of a Civil Court and will contain a concise statement of the case, points for determination, the decision, and reasons. It also allows for appeals against the Tahsildar's order to the Sub-Court within thirty days of communication.

main_sections.section_title: Corrections to the final compensation rolls
main_sections.description: Except as provided, no correction shall be made to the compensation roll after it has become final, unless the Tahsildar makes it to correct an accidental slip or omission or on his own motion or on application filed by a person interested.

Details the payment of compensation to persons whose names are entered in the compensation roll, and to their legal representatives if they die before payment. It also covers situations where the person entitled to receive compensation is a trust or a minor, or is suffering from legal disability or is a limited owner, and specifies how the compensation shall be deposited or paid. Further, it addresses scenarios where a suit or proceeding is pending, requiring the Tahsildar to place the amount at the disposal of the court or authority.

main_sections.section_title: Payment of compensation to be full discharge of the liability to pay Arthapalisa, Jenmibhogam or Karathilchilavu
main_sections.description: Declares that the payment of compensation under this Act shall be a full discharge of the Government's liability to pay Arthapalisa, Jenmibhogam or Karathilchilavu.

States that any arrears of Arthapalisa, Jenmibhogam or Karathilchilavu due to a Jenmi, before the appointed day and remaining unpaid after that day, shall be paid to the Jenmi in the same manner as before the commencement of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: No action to lie against Government or any officer or person authorized under the Act
main_sections.description: Provides that no suit, prosecution or other legal proceedings shall lie against the Government or any officer or person authorized under the Act for any act done or purported to be done under this Act or for any act done in good faith in respect of its provisions.

Empowers the Government to make rules, by notification in the Gazette, for carrying into effect the provisions of this Act. Specific matters that may be covered by these rules include the preparation of the draft compensation roll, the time for preferring objections, fees for appeals, and the authority or bank for deposits.

Repeals the Arthapalisa, Jenmibhogam and Karathilchilavu (Abolition) Ordinance, 2007. It also states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Compensation shall be paid in cash.
The commutation rate of paddy in respect of Arthapalisa, Jenmibhogam and Karathilchilavu shall be ninety rupees per standard para.
Rules made by the Government can cover the manner of preparing compensation rolls, time for objections, appeal fees, and deposit procedures.
Every rule made under this Act shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly for a total period of fourteen days which may be comprised in one session or in two successive sessions.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: TahSildar, Government, Civil Court (in appeals)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment and payment of compensation rolls prepared by the Tahsildar, and legal proceedings as per Civil Court procedures for objections and appeals.

rights: Right of Jenmi to receive compensation.
Right to appeal against Tahsildar's order to the Sub-Court.
Right to receive arrears of Arthapalisa, Jenmibhogam or Karathilchilavu due before the appointed day.
duties: Duty of the Government to pay compensation.
Duty of the Tahsildar to prepare compensation rolls and process claims.
Duty of Jenmis to submit claims and objections as per prescribed procedures.
obligations: The Jenmi's right to receive Arthapalisa, Jenmibhogam or Karathilchilavu is extinguished upon the Act's commencement.

key_procedures: Preparation of draft compensation rolls by the Tahsildar.
Publication of the draft roll and invitation of objections.
Hearing and decision of claims/objections by the Tahsildar.
Appeal against Tahsildar's order to the Sub-Court.
Payment of compensation to eligible persons.
Making rules by the Government for the Act's implementation.
administration: Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act provides for the abolition of certain traditional payments related to land tenure in Kerala.
Compensation is paid in cash, replacing the previous forms of payment.
The Act repeals the Arthapalisa, Jenmibhogam and Karathilchilavu (Abolition) Ordinance, 2007, with savings for actions taken under the Ordinance.
No legal action can be taken against the Government or its officers for acts done in good faith under this Act.

title: The Assumption Of Management Of Estates Proclamations (Repeal) Act, 1963
purpose: To repeal the Proclamations assuming the management of certain estates in Cochin.
scope: This Act applies to Proclamations assuming the management of certain estates in the former State of Cochin.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Assumption of Management of Estates Proclamations (Repeal) Act, 1963 and shall come into force at once.
Repeals the Proclamations mentioned in the Schedule.

States that no action shall lie against the Government or any person for acts done or ordered to be done during the period of management under or in pursuance of the Proclamations or rules framed thereunder.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of surrenders made before the Act
main_sections.description: Validates surrenders made before the Act, deeming them to have always been valid, provided they were made before the commencement of this Act. Any execution and registration of receipts in favour of the Governor of Kerala or the Cochin Dewan Board are also deemed valid. The validity of such surrenders shall be maintained in any court.

important_rules: Proclamations mentioned in the Schedule are hereby repealed.

No action shall lie against the Government or any person for acts done or ordered to be done during the period of management under or in pursuance of the repealed Proclamations or rules framed thereunder.
Surrenders made before the Act are deemed valid.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal provisions and validation of past actions.

rights: Individuals whose estates were managed under the Proclamations have their surrenders validated.

key_procedures: The repeal of specific Proclamations is enacted by Section 2 of the Act.
Validation of surrenders made prior to the Act's commencement.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 19th day of November, 1963 and was published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 19th November, 1963.
The Schedule lists the specific Proclamations being repealed, including their numbers, dates, and the estates they concerned.

title: THE BONDED LABOUR SYSTEM (ABOLITION) ACT, 1975
purpose: An Act to provide for the abolition of the bonded labour system prevalent in the districts of Kozhikode, Malappuram and Cannanore in the State of Kerala.
scope: The Act applies to the whole of the districts of Kozhikode, Malappuram and Cannanore in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.bonded_labour_system: Bonded labour system consists in the payment of cash called vallurukavu panam or nulpuponam or by whatever name it may locally be known or the payment in kind, by one person (hereinafter called the creditor) to a person belonging to a Scheduled Tribe (hereinafter called the debtor), whether evidenced by writing or otherwise, on any one or both of the following terms, namely: (a) that in consideration of the payment of cash or the payment in kind made by the creditor to the debtor, the debtor shall, by himself or through members of his family, render labour or personal service to the creditor for a specified period, either without wages or on payment of nominal wages; (b) that on failure to render the labour or personal service referred to in clause (a), the debtor shall be bound to repay the cash or the value of the thing received by him and vacate the hut, if any, occupied by him and situated in the land belonging to the creditor.
key_definitions.scheduled_tribe: The expression "Scheduled Tribe" shall have the meaning assigned to it in the Constitution of India.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1975, and that it extends to the whole of the districts of Kozhikode, Malappuram and Cannanore in the State of Kerala.

Defines the term 'bonded labour system' including its various forms of payment (cash or kind) and the obligations of the debtor to render labour or personal service. It also defines the consequences of failure to render service, including repayment and vacating of accommodation.
Declares that from the date of commencement of this Act, the bonded labour system shall stand abolished. It also prohibits any payment of cash or in kind under the bonded labour system.

main_sections.section_title: Obligation to perform labour or personal service to be deemed extinguished
main_sections.description: States that all obligations of the debtor to perform labour or personal service arising from any payment of cash or any payment in kind under the bonded labour system, made before the commencement of this Act, shall be deemed extinguished. It also clarifies that this does not affect the liability to repay the whole or part of the cash or value of the thing received.

Outlines the procedure for determining past debts. If cash or the value of things given under the bonded labour system before commencement has not been repaid, the creditor must report claims to the Government. The debtor can file objections. The Revenue Divisional Officer, after considering claims and objections, will determine the amount due and the terms of repayment.
Provides for an appeal against an order under sub-section (4) of section 5 to the District Collector within sixty days. The District Collector's decision on appeal is final.

main_sections.section_title: Legal practitioner not to appear before Revenue Divisional Officer and District Collector
main_sections.description: Prohibits legal practitioners from appearing before the Revenue Divisional Officer or the District Collector in any proceeding under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Revenue Divisional Officer and District Collector to have certain powers of civil court
main_sections.description: Grants the Revenue Divisional Officer and the District Collector all the powers of a civil court while trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, in respect of summoning and enforcing attendance, requiring discovery and production of documents, receiving evidence on affidavit, and examining witnesses or for local investigation.

main_sections.section_title: Orders under sections 5 and 6 to be deemed decrees of civil courts
main_sections.description: States that orders passed under sections 5 and 6 shall be deemed to be decrees of a civil court and shall be executed as such. Every order referred to in sub-section (1) shall contain a concise statement of the case, the points for determination, the decision and the reasons for such decision. An order passed by a civil court in execution of an order under section 5 or section 6 shall not be subject to revision by the court to which appeals ordinarily lie against decisions of the said court.

main_sections.section_title: Government to assist debtor in repayment of debt
main_sections.description: The Government may, by such rules as may be made in this behalf, pay to a debtor, by way of grant, the amount of the debt due from him to the creditor and the interest, if any, thereon as determined under section 5, for the purpose of repayment to the creditor.

main_sections.section_title: Bar of jurisdiction of civil courts
main_sections.description: No civil court shall have jurisdiction to entertain any suit or proceeding in respect of any matter which the Revenue Divisional Officer or the District Collector is empowered by this Act to decide, and no injunction shall be granted by any court in respect of any action taken or to be taken by them in pursuance of any power conferred by this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of certain suits to the Revenue Divisional Officer
main_sections.description: All suits relating to the recovery of the cash paid or the value of the thing given under the bonded labour system, pending before any court at the commencement of this Act, shall be transferred to the Revenue Divisional Officer within whose jurisdiction the debtor ordinarily resides, to be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of this Act.

Whoever (a) pays any cash or makes any payment in kind or abets any person to pay any cash or make any payment in kind under the bonded labour system; or (b) compels the debtor or abets any person to compel the debtor to render labour or personal service by reason of any payment of cash or any payment in kind under the bonded labour system, shall be punishable for every such payment, abetment or compulsion with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than one month but which may extend to one year, or with fine which shall not be less than one hundred rupees but which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.

main_sections.section_title: Offences under the Act to be cognizable
main_sections.description: Not withstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Central Act 2 of 1974), every offence under this Act shall be cognizable.
No court inferior to that of a magistrate of the first class shall try any offence punishable under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Creditor not to accept any payment against discharged debt
main_sections.description: No creditor shall accept any payment against any claim for a debt which has been discharged or deemed to have been discharged under this Act. Whoever contravenes this provision shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than one month but which may extend to one year, or with fine which shall not be less than one hundred rupees but which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both. The court convicting any person under this section may, in addition to the fine, direct such person to deposit the amount so accepted in the court within a period to be specified in the order, for being refunded to the debtor.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make rules for the purpose of carrying into effect the provisions of this Act. Every rule made under this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before the Legislative Assembly while it is in session for a total period of fourteen days which may be comprised in one session or in two successive sessions and, if before the expiry of the session in which it is so laid or the session immediately following, the Legislative Assembly makes any modification in the rule or decides that the rule should not be made, the rule shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect, as the case may be, so however that any such modification or annulment shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that rule.

important_rules: All obligations of the debtor to perform labour or personal service arising from any payment of cash or any payment in kind under the bonded labour system, made before the commencement of this Act, shall be deemed extinguished (Section 4(1)).
No creditor shall accept any payment against any claim for a debt which has been discharged or deemed to have been discharged under this Act (Section 16(1)).

Rules made under this Act must be laid before the Legislative Assembly for a total period of fourteen days. Modifications or annulments by the Assembly shall affect the rule's future effect without prejudice to past validity (Section 17(2)).

penalties: Imprisonment for a term not less than one month but extending to one year, or fine not less than one hundred rupees but extending to five hundred rupees, or both, for contravening Section 13 (compelling labour or making/abetting payments).

Imprisonment for a term not less than one month but extending to one year, or fine not less than one hundred rupees but extending to five hundred rupees, or both, for contravening Section 16(1) (creditor accepting payment against discharged debt).
Deposit of wrongfully accepted payment by the court for refund to the debtor (Section 16(3)).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Revenue Divisional Officer, District Collector, and Magistrate of the first class.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Offences are cognizable (Section 14). Civil courts' jurisdiction is barred in matters the Revenue Divisional Officer or District Collector is empowered to decide (Section 11). Orders of the Revenue Divisional Officer and District Collector are deemed decrees of civil courts and shall be executed as such (Section 9).

rights: Debtors have the right to be free from obligations to perform labour or personal service arising from past debts (Section 4(1)).
Debtors have the right to not have creditors accept payment against a discharged debt (Section 16(1)).
Aggrieved persons have the right to appeal against orders under Section 5 (Section 6(1)).
duties: Creditors have the duty to report claims for past debts to the Government (Section 5(1)(a)).
Debtors have the duty to file objections to claims (Section 5(1)(b)).
Creditors have the duty not to accept payment against a discharged debt (Section 16(1)).
obligations: Debtors were previously obligated to render labour or personal service for specified periods without wages or on nominal wages in consideration of cash or kind payments (defined in Section 2). These obligations are now extinguished (Section 4).

key_procedures: Determination of past debts: Creditor reports claims, debtor files objections. Revenue Divisional Officer determines the amount due and repayment terms (Section 5).
Appeal against debt determination: Aggrieved party can appeal to the District Collector within sixty days (Section 6).
Transfer of suits: Suits relating to recovery of cash or value of things under bonded labour system pending at commencement are transferred to the Revenue Divisional Officer (Section 12).
administration: The Government makes rules for the Act's implementation. Revenue Divisional Officers and District Collectors are key administrative authorities with civil court powers for certain matters.
important_notes: The Act specifically applies to the districts of Kozhikode, Malappuram, and Cannanore in Kerala.
Legal practitioners are not allowed to appear before the Revenue Divisional Officer or District Collector in proceedings under this Act.
The Act aims to abolish the system, not necessarily to forgive all prior monetary obligations if they are separate from the bonded labour itself and can be repaid.

key_definitions.Syndicate: Means the Syndicate of the University.
