main_sections.description: Outlines the extensive powers of the Syndicate, including affiliating colleges, making and amending Ordinances, holding and administering University properties, directing the form, custody and use of the common seal, constituting Boards of Inspection, prescribing qualifications of teachers, appointing and suspending/dismissing teachers and employees, fixing emoluments, charging fees, awarding fellowships and scholarships, exercising supervision and control over residence and discipline of students, and framing financial estimates.

main_sections.section_title: Election of members to the Senate and the Syndicate
main_sections.description: Specifies that the election of members to the Senate and Syndicate shall be conducted on the principle of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote in accordance with the Statutes.

Defines the composition of the Academic Council, listing its members as the Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, Director of Public Instruction, Director of Collegiate Education, Director of Education, Deans of Faculties, Heads of University Departments of Study, Fifteen Principals other than Deans of Faculties of Colleges nominated by the Vice-Chancellor, and Ten members co-opted by the Academic Council.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and duties of the Academic Council
main_sections.description: Details the powers and duties of the Academic Council, including control and general regulation of standards, instruction, education and examinations, making and amending regulations, advising the Senate and Syndicate, making proposals for the Senate and Syndicate, making regulations for special courses of study, encouragement of co-operation, making regulations regarding courses of study, constituting Faculties, and making proposals to the Syndicate for the framing of Ordinances.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office of Academic Council
main_sections.description: States that members of the Academic Council nominated or co-opted shall hold office for a period of three years from the date of nomination or co-option, or in the case of members elected, for a period of three years from the date of election, and may be eligible for re-nomination or re-election.

Lists the faculties within the University, including Arts, Science, Engineering, Oriental Studies, Fine Arts, Commerce, Technology, Medicine, Forestry, Fisheries, Mining, Education, Veterinary Science, Philosophy, Adult Education and Extension Service, and other such faculties as may be prescribed.
Provides for a Dean for each Faculty, who shall be nominated by the Vice-Chancellor and shall hold office as a Dean for such term as may be prescribed by the Statutes.
States that there shall be Boards of Studies attached to each department of study in the University, and their constitution and powers shall be prescribed by the Ordinances.

Declares that all colleges existing within the jurisdiction of the University at the commencement of the Act shall stand affiliated to the University, and the Government may transfer any institution to the University subject to terms and conditions.

Covers various matters related to the Statutes, including powers and duties of officers, constitution and powers of Senate and Syndicate, election of members, degrees, diplomas, titles, certificates, withdrawal or cancellation of degrees, maintenance of registers, holding of convocations, conferment of honorary degrees, maintenance of accounts, fixation of scales of pay, and other matters required or authorized by the Act.

Details the process for making Statutes, involving the Senate's consideration of draft Statutes, placement before the Senate, passing by the Senate with or without amendment, and submission to the Government.

Covers matters that may be provided for in the Ordinances, including courses of study, conduct of examinations, admission of students, levy of fees, residence and discipline of students, qualifications of teachers, appointment and prescription of terms of office of members of Boards of Studies and Examiners, scales of pay, and other matters prescribed by Ordinances.

Outlines the procedure for making Ordinances, requiring submission by the Syndicate to the Senate for approval, and specifying the powers of the Senate to amend or cancel them. The Chancellor may direct the operation of any Ordinance to be suspended.

States that the Academic Council may make Regulations consistent with the Act, Statutes, and Ordinances. All Regulations require submission to the Senate for consideration. The Senate has power to amend or cancel any such Regulation.
Grants the Syndicate power to make Rules and Bye-laws consistent with the provisions of the Act, Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations.
Establishes the 'University Fund' which shall be applied to the purposes of the University, and states that the University Fund shall be kept in the Government Treasury.

Specifies that the University shall receive grants as may be fixed by the Government each year, and the Government may pay such grants for the purpose of expansion of academic and research functions and for assisting affiliated colleges.

Requires annual accounts of the University to be prepared under the directions of the Syndicate and submitted to the Government for audit. Audited accounts are to be published in the Gazette and copies thereof submitted to the Senate and Government. The Syndicate shall also prepare financial estimates for the ensuing year.
States that the annual report of the University shall be prepared by the Syndicate and submitted to the Senate.

Details the Government's powers regarding the University, including appointing auditors, requiring auditors to maintain continuous audit, specifying the cost of audit, requiring auditors to report on transactions and forward copies to the Government, specifying what auditors shall report, and granting the Government the right to cause an inspection of the University and its institutions. The Government must give notice before inspection and the University is entitled to represent itself.

important_rules: Members of the Syndicate cannot hold office for a longer period than three months after ceasing to be such a member unless they become a member of the electorate.
The Syndicate shall have the power to punish employees who are suspended and dismissed.
The election of members to the Senate and Syndicate must be conducted using the single transferable vote.
All Statutes passed by the Senate shall be submitted to the Chancellor, and the Chancellor may sanction, disallow or remit the same for further consideration.
No statute, amendment or repeal shall have effect until it has been assented to by the Chancellor.
The Senate shall have power, by a resolution passed by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present at such meeting, to cancel or modify any such Ordinance or Regulation.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government and the Syndicate are implied authorities for enforcement through their powers of appointment, dismissal, inspection, and making rules and regulations.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is through the powers vested in the University's bodies (Syndicate, Senate, Academic Council) through Statutes, Ordinances, Regulations, and Bye-laws, as well as Government oversight and inspection.

rights: Right of appeal to a tribunal appointed by the Chancellor for employees punished by the Syndicate.
Right to frame financial estimates of the University and submit them to the Senate.
Right to receive grants from the Government.
Right to have accounts audited by Government appointed auditors.
Right to have annual reports prepared and submitted.
Government's right to cause inspection of the University and its institutions.
Government's right to inquire into the affairs of the University.
duties: Duty to affiliate colleges in accordance with prescribed conditions.
Duty to prepare financial estimates.
Duty to maintain a register of registered graduates.
Duty to prepare and submit annual accounts and reports.
Duty to ensure continuous audit of University accounts.
Duty to make University provisions for the purpose of expansion of academic and research functions.
Duty to submit for consideration by the Senate, any draft Statute or amendment.
Duty to submit all Statutes to the Chancellor for assent.
Duty to submit all Ordinances and Regulations to the Senate for consideration.
obligations: Obligation to frame financial estimates of the University and submit them to the Senate.
Obligation to conduct examinations and approve and publish the results thereof.
Obligation to ensure proper conduct and conditions of employment for staff.
Obligation to bear the cost of the audit as fixed by the Government.
Obligation to provide notice to the University in case of inspection and to represent itself.
Obligation to provide to the Government information regarding the University.

key_procedures: Procedure for making Statutes: Senate may take into consideration draft Statutes, place them before the Senate, pass them with or without amendment, and submit them to the Government. Any Statute passed affecting powers, duties or authority of the University, the Syndicate, or the opinion of the Officer concerned, requires prior consideration by the Syndicate and the opinion of the Officer concerned must be taken into account. All Statutes require the Chancellor's assent.

Procedure for making Ordinances: Syndicate submits Ordinances to the Senate for approval. The Senate may amend or cancel Ordinances. The Chancellor may direct the operation of any Ordinance to be suspended.
Procedure for making Regulations: Academic Council makes Regulations, which must be submitted to the Senate for consideration. The Senate has the power to amend or cancel them.
Audit and reporting: Annual accounts are prepared by the Syndicate, submitted for audit by Government auditors, and published. Annual reports are also prepared and submitted to the Senate.
Inspection by Government: Government has the right to inspect University institutions and conduct inquiries. Notice must be given to the University.
administration: The administration of the University is vested in the Syndicate, Senate, and Academic Council, with oversight from the Chancellor and the Government.
important_notes: The Syndicate's power to suspend and dismiss teachers and employees is subject to a right of appeal to a tribunal appointed by the Chancellor, whose decision is final and binding.
The Government has the right to cause an inspection of the University and its institutions and to inquire into its affairs, with a provision for notice and representation by the University.
The University Fund is to be kept in the Government Treasury.
The University shall receive grants from the Government each year, which may be used for expansion of academic and research functions and for assisting affiliated colleges.

title: The Chalakudy and Malappuram Municipal Councils (Extension of Term of Office of Councillors) Act, 1976
purpose: To provide for the further extension of the term of office of the councillors of the Chalakudy and Malappuram Municipalities.
scope: The act applies to the Chalakudy and Malappuram Municipal Councils.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Chalakudy and Malappuram Municipal Councils (Extension of Term of Office of Councillors) Act, 1976. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 30th day of November, 1976.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of term of office of municipal councillors
main_sections.description: The term of office of the councillors of the Chalakudy and Malappuram Municipalities constituted under the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960 (14 of 1961), which expires on the 30th day of November, 1976, shall, except up to the 1st day of November, 1977, be extended.

Repeals the Chalakudy and Malappuram Municipal Councils (Extension of Term of Office of Councillors) Ordinance, 1976 (13 of 1976). Nothing done or any action taken under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: The Act came into force on November 30, 1976.
The term of office of councillors of Chalakudy and Malappuram Municipalities is extended up to November 1, 1977.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 15th day of January, 1977.
Published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 36 dated 18th January, 1977.

title: THE COCHIN UNIVERSITY OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2007
purpose: To further amend the Cochin University of Science and Technology Act, 1986 for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Cochin University of Science and Technology Act, 1986.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title as 'The Cochin University of Science and Technology (Amendment) Act, 2007' and specifies that Clause (d) of sub-section (1) of section 2 of the principal Act shall be deemed to have come into force on the 5th day of February, 2007 and the remaining provisions shall come into force at once.
Amends section 17 of the Cochin University of Science and Technology Act, 1986 (the principal Act) by inserting new items and making substitutions in sub-section (1) and sub-section (2).
Amends section 19 of the principal Act by inserting 'v) a woman nominated by the Government' in the heading 'other members', after item (iv).

Repeals section 5 of the University Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 2007 (46 of 2007) and states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Clause (d) of sub-section (1) of section 2 of the principal Act to come into force on 5th February, 2007.
Other provisions of this Act to come into force at once.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be the University administration and government bodies responsible for higher education in Kerala.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the implementation of the amended provisions of the Cochin University of Science and Technology Act, 1986.

key_procedures: Insertion of specific roles and nominations into the University structure, particularly concerning the Syndicate and representation.
Replacement and addition of text in specific sections of the principal Act as detailed in section 2 and 3.
administration: Cochin University of Science and Technology and relevant Government departments in Kerala.
important_notes: The Act is a translation from Malayalam.
Received the assent of the Governor on 13th October, 2007 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 1859 dated 15th October, 2007.

title: THE COCHIN UNIVERSITY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1975
purpose: To further amend the Cochin University Act, 1971.
scope: Applies to the Cochin University Act, 1971.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Cochin University (Amendment) Act, 1975.

Amends section 10 of the Cochin University Act, 1971, by inserting a new sub-section (15A) concerning the exercise of powers and performance of duties of the Vice-Chancellor by the Chancellor in the event of a permanent vacancy in the office of the Vice-Chancellor.
Amends section 56 of the principal Act, specifically the proviso to sub-section (2), by replacing the words "one year" with "one year and six months".

Repeals the Cochin University (Third Amendment) Ordinance, 1974 (18 of 1974) and saves any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance if such Act had come into force on the 16th day of December, 1974.

administration: Cochin University
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 2nd day of April, 1975 and published in the Gazette Extraordinary No.170 dated 2nd April, 1975.

title: The Cochin University (Second Amendment) Act, 1975
purpose: To further amend the Cochin University Act, 1971.
scope: Applies to the Cochin University Act, 1971. Specifically amends section 56 of the principal Act regarding time periods.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Cochin University (Second Amendment) Act, 1975.

Amends section 56 of the Cochin University Act, 1971. It substitutes the words "two years and six months" for "one year and six months" in the proviso to sub-section (2) of section 56 of the principal Act.

Repeals the Cochin University (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1975 (4 of 1975). It also provides that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act, and this Act shall come into force on the 19th day of June, 1975.

administration: The Cochin University.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 7th day of September, 1975 and published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 527 dated 8th September, 1975.

title: The Cochin Abkari (Extension and Amendment) Act, 1967
purpose: To extend the Cochin Abkari Act, I of 1077 and the rules, orders, and notifications made or issued thereunder to the areas of the State of Kerala where the said Act is not in force, and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act extends the Cochin Abkari Act, 1 of 1077, and its associated rules, orders, and notifications to the entire State of Kerala. This includes all areas within the State of Kerala where the principal Act was not in force prior to the commencement of this amending Act.

key_definitions.Collector: Means the Collector of a district and includes any other officer appointed by the Government to exercise the powers and perform the duties of a Collector under this Act.
key_definitions.Import: Means to bring into the State.
key_definitions.Export: Means to take out of the State.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies the commencement dates for its various provisions. Some provisions came into force on a date appointed by the Government through notification, while others were deemed to have come into force on May 11, 1967.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of Cochin Act, I of 1077 and the rules, orders and notifications thereunder to the whole of the State of Kerala
main_sections.description: This section formally extends the Cochin Abkari Act, 1 of 1077, and all its associated rules, orders, and notifications to all areas of the State of Kerala where it was not previously in force.
Amends the preamble of the principal Act by substituting 'State of Kerala' for 'Cochin State'.
Throughout the principal Act, the word 'Diwan' is substituted with 'Government'.
Amends section 1 of the principal Act by substituting 'Abkari Act' for 'Cochin Abkari Act', 'State of Kerala' for 'Cochin State', and omitting the paragraph relating to commencement.
Amends section 2 of the principal Act by omitting certain phrases and substituting 'licenses and privileges' for 'licenses'.

Amends section 3 of the principal Act by substituting clauses related to 'Collector', omitting clause (5), substituting 'Indian Penal Code' for 'Cochin Penal Code', omitting 'Madras' from an explanation, omitting 'Cochin' and 'by sea' from clause (12), substituting 'Dangerous Drugs Act, 1930' for 'Cochin Dangerous Drugs Act', substituting 'including' for 'otherwise than by way of', substituting new clauses for (16) and (17) defining 'Import' and 'Export', omitting 'Cochin' from clause (18), and substituting 'tent, booth, raft, vehicle and vessel' for 'tent and vessel' in clause (21). It also inserts a new clause (24) defining 'State'.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new sections for sections 6 and 7
main_sections.description: Replaces sections 6 and 7 of the principal Act. New Section 6 deals with the import of liquor or intoxicating drugs, requiring permission and payment of duties. New Section 7 regulates the export of liquor or intoxicating drugs, also requiring permission and either payment of duties or execution of a bond.
Amends section 12 of the principal Act to include 'winery or other manufactory in which liquor is manufactured' in the prohibition of construction or working.

Inserts new sections. Section 12-A prohibits the manufacture of preparations containing liquor or intoxicating drugs in excess of specified quantities. Section 12-B regulates the utilization of liquor or intoxicating drugs in manufacture and limits the possession of certain preparations, with exceptions for medicinal preparations.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 14
main_sections.description: Replaces section 14 of the principal Act with provisions empowering the Commissioner, with Government approval, to establish and control distilleries, breweries, wineries, and warehouses, prescribe supervision modes, establishment costs, and wastage allowances for alcohol.

Inserts new sections. Section 15A prohibits consumption or use of liquor by persons under 18. Section 15B prohibits the sale or delivery of liquor to persons under 18. Section 15C prohibits consumption of liquor in public places unless permitted by a license, defining 'public place'.

Amends section 26 of the principal Act by substituting clause (c) to include conviction for offenses under the Dangerous Drugs Act, 1930, or the Trade and Merchandise Marks Act, 1958, or sections 478 to 489 of the Indian Penal Code as grounds for license cancellation.

Amends section 29 of the principal Act by substituting various terms related to distilleries, breweries, wineries, manufactories, and warehouses, and replacing 'Cochin Contract Act, XXIII of 1112' with 'Indian Contract Act, 1872'.

important_rules: No liquor or intoxicating drug shall be imported without the permission of the Government or an authorized officer and without payment of due duties, taxes, and fees.
Permission for import of liquor or intoxicating drugs is subject to conditions and restrictions specified by the Government.
No liquor or intoxicating drug shall be exported without permission and either payment of duties or execution of a bond for payment.
Permission for export of liquor or intoxicating drugs is subject to conditions and restrictions specified by the Government.
No preparation containing liquor or intoxicating drug shall be manufactured in excess of the quantity specified by the Commissioner.
No person shall utilize liquor or intoxicating drug in the manufacture of any preparation in excess of the quantity specified by the Commissioner and except under a license.
No person shall possess any preparation containing liquor or intoxicating drug (other than a medicinal preparation for bona fide treatment) in excess of the quantity specified by the Commissioner.
No person under the age of 18 years shall consume or use any liquor.
No person licensed to sell liquor, or their employee, shall sell or deliver liquor to any person under the age of 18 years.

No person shall consume liquor in any public place unless permitted by a license from the Commissioner. 'Public place' is defined to include streets, courts, public offices, places of amusement, passenger boats, public passenger vehicles, and dining/refreshment rooms in certain establishments, but excludes private residential rooms.

penalties: Conviction of any offence against this Act or of any cognizable and non-bailable offence or of any offence under the Dangerous Drugs Act, 1930, or under the Trade and Merchandise Marks Act, 1958, or under sections 478 to 489 of the Indian Penal Code can lead to the cancellation of a license.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government, and officers appointed by the Government, including the Commissioner and Collectors.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through licensing, prohibition of certain activities without permission or license, imposition of duties and taxes, and provisions for license cancellation upon conviction of specified offenses.

rights: Right to obtain licenses for activities related to liquor manufacturing and warehousing (subject to conditions and approval).
Right to use liquor or intoxicating drugs in manufacture under a license.
Right to possess medicinal preparations containing liquor or intoxicating drugs for bona fide treatment, subject to specified limits.
duties: Duty to obtain permission for import and export of liquor or intoxicating drugs.
Duty to pay duties, taxes, and fees on imported liquor or intoxicating drugs.
Duty to comply with conditions and restrictions specified by the Government for import and export.
Duty to obtain a license for manufacturing preparations containing liquor or intoxicating drugs.
Duty to adhere to specified quantities for manufacture and possession of preparations containing liquor or intoxicating drugs.
Duty for licensed sellers to not sell liquor to persons under 18 years of age.
Duty to not consume liquor in public places without a license.
obligations: Obligation to execute a bond for payment of duties on exported liquor or intoxicating drugs if immediate payment is not made.
Obligation to ensure proper collection of duties, taxes, and other dues payable under the Act through prescribed supervision modes.
Obligation to bear the cost of supervision establishment and incidental charges for licensed manufactories and warehouses.

key_procedures: Application for and grant of licenses for establishing distilleries, breweries, wineries, or warehouses.
Obtaining Government or authorized officer's permission for the import or export of liquor or intoxicating drugs, subject to conditions and payment of duties or bond execution.
Specification of quantities for manufacture and possession of preparations containing liquor or intoxicating drugs by the Commissioner.
Procedure for cancellation of a license upon conviction of specified offenses.
administration: The Government of Kerala, and officers appointed by the Government, including the Commissioner and Collectors.
important_notes: The commencement of certain provisions of the Act was staggered, with different dates appointed by the Government via notification.

The Act extensively amends the principal Cochin Abkari Act, 1 of 1077, by substituting definitions, inserting new sections, and modifying existing ones to align with the expanded territorial scope and updated legal framework.

title: The Cochin Proclamation III of 1123 (Repealing) Act, 1951
purpose: To repeal the Cochin Proclamation, III of 1123, and the Cochin Proclamation, III of 1123 (Repealing) Ordinance, 1951 (Ordinance V of 1951).
scope: Applies to the repeal of the specified Proclamation and Ordinance.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Cochin Proclamation, III of 1123 (Repealing) Act, 1951, and that it shall come into force at once.
Repeals the Cochin Proclamation, III of 1123, and the Cochin Proclamation, III of 1123 (Repealing) Ordinance, 1951 (Ordinance V of 1951).

important_notes: Published in Gazette Extraordinary dated 11th October 1951.

title: The Cochin University (Amendment) Act, 1974
purpose: To amend The Cochin University Act, 1971.
scope: Applies to The Cochin University, Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Cochin University (Amendment) Act, 1974.

Amends section 56 of the Cochin University Act, 1971. The amendment states that the following provisions shall be inserted at the end of the said section: 'Provided that if, for any reason the constitution of any of the authorities of the University in accordance with the provisions in Chapter IV of this Act cannot be done before the expiry of the period for which that authority is nominated under sub-section (2), the Chancellor may, by notification to the Gazette, extend the period of that authority for a further period not exceeding one year.'

(1) The Cochin University (Amendment) Ordinance, 1973 (19 of 1973) is hereby repealed. (2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

administration: The Cochin University
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 12th day of March, 1974 and published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 272 dated 12th March 1974.

title: The Cochin University (Second Amendment) Act, 1974
purpose: To further amend the Cochin University Act, 1971, for the purpose hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Cochin University.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Cochin University (Second Amendment) Act, 1974, and it shall come into force at once.

Amends section 15 of the Cochin University Act, 1971. Specifically, in item (4) under the heading "ELECTED MEMBERS", the words "elected by the Legislative Assembly" are substituted with "elected by the Members of the Legislative Assembly".

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Governor of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Assent and publication in the Gazette Extraordinary.

key_procedures: Receiving the assent of the Governor on the 12th day of November 1974.
Publication in the Gazette Extraordinary No 780 dated 15th November 1974.
administration: Cochin University
important_notes: Repeal and saving of The Kerala Municipal Councils (Extension of Term of Office of Councillors) Ordinance, 1974 (4 of 1974).

title: The Cochin University Act, 1971
purpose: To provide for the establishment and incorporation of a University at Cochin and to enable it to make provision for the instruction and training in such branches of learning as it may think fit, for the furtherance of research and advancement and dissemination of knowledge and for collaboration with industries for the same, and for the establishment of campuses and for the constitution of authorities for the University and for the regulation of its affairs and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to the establishment, incorporation, regulation, and administration of the Cochin University. It covers faculties, deans, boards of studies, finance committee, boards of appointments, statutes, ordinances, regulations, and rules. The scope extends to students, staff, and the overall functioning of the university.

main_sections.description: This section details the powers of the University to have faculties, the charge of teaching and research within faculties, the composition of faculties, and the departments that may be comprised within a faculty.
This section outlines the appointment of Deans of Faculties, their responsibilities concerning the observance of statutes, ordinances, and regulations, and the term of office for a Dean.

This section states that there shall be a Board of Studies attached to each Department of Study in the University, and that the constitution and powers of these Boards shall be prescribed by the Statutes.

This section establishes a Finance Committee with the Vice-Chancellor as Chairman to advise the University on any question affecting its finances. It also specifies that the constitution, powers, and functions of the Finance Committee, and its procedure in financial matters, including the delegation of its powers, shall be prescribed by the Statutes.

This section deals with the constitution of Boards of Appointments for making selections for various positions within the University, including Professors, Readers, and Lecturers. It outlines the composition of these boards and the process for selection.

This section indicates that the Statutes may provide for matters such as the constitution, functions, and powers of the authorities of the University, election and continuance in office of members of authorities, powers and duties of officers, teachers, and employees, conferment of Honorary Degrees, holding of convocations, award and withdrawal of degrees, establishment, maintenance and abolition of Faculties, Departments, hostels, colleges and institutions, conditions under which colleges may be admitted to the University, institution of Fellowships, Scholarships, etc., procedure of election to authorities, classification of teachers, institution of Pension, Provident Fund, acceptance and management of bequests, donations and endowments, and registration of Registered Graduates.

This section details the process by which Statutes are made, amended, or repealed by the Senate, including proposals by the Syndicate and the role of the Senate in approving or rejecting draft Statutes.

This section outlines the matters for which Ordinances may be made by the Syndicate, including admission of students, courses of study, award of degrees and diplomas, conditions relating to award of fellowships, scholarships, etc., conduct of examinations, conditions of residence of students, special arrangements for women students, emoluments, terms and conditions of service of employees, management of colleges and other institutions, supervision of constituent colleges and special studies in recognised institutions, and fees.

This section describes the procedure for making Ordinances, including consultation with the Academic Council and the Board or Boards of Studies concerned, submission of Ordinances to the Chancellor and Senate, and the process for amendment or cancellation.

This section specifies that the Academic Council may, subject to the approval of the Syndicate, make regulations consistent with the Act and the Statutes and Ordinances. It lists various matters for which regulations may be made, including admission of students, recognition of examinations, decision of University Courses and Examinations, and conditions for award of degrees, diplomas, and certificates. It also includes conditions for recognition of hostels and discipline of students.

key_procedures: Procedure for making Statutes: Statutes are made by the Senate, and the process involves proposals from the Syndicate, draft approval, and Senate review. Statutes can be amended or repealed.

Procedure for making Ordinances: Ordinances are made by the Syndicate, with consultation from the Academic Council and relevant Boards of Studies. They are submitted to the Chancellor and Senate for approval, cancellation, or amendment.
Procedure for making Regulations: Regulations are made by the Academic Council, subject to the approval of the Syndicate, and must be consistent with the Act, Statutes, and Ordinances.
administration: The Cochin University
important_notes: Statutes can provide for a wide range of matters concerning the University's constitution, functions, and administration.
Ordinances cover more detailed operational aspects of the University, such as admissions, courses, examinations, and student affairs.
Regulations provide specific rules within the framework of Statutes and Ordinances, issued by the Academic Council.
The Vice-Chancellor plays a key role in the Finance Committee and in the approval of Statutes and Ordinances.
The Senate and Syndicate are key authorities in the making and approval of Statutes and Ordinances.

title: The Cochin University of Science and Technology (Amendment) Act, 1990
purpose: To amend the Cochin University of Science and Technology Act, 1986.
scope: Applies to the Cochin University of Science and Technology.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and its commencement date. The Act is called the Cochin University of Science and Technology (Amendment) Act, 1990. Section 1(2) states that this Act shall be deemed to have come into force on the 26th day of September, 1986. Section 1(3) states that the amendments made by this Act shall be in addition to and not in derogation of any other law for the time being in force.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 2 of Act 23 of 1986
main_sections.description: This section amends Section 2 of the Cochin University of Science and Technology Act, 1986. It inserts clauses relating to the definitions of 'Vice-Chancellor', 'Pro-Vice-Chancellor', and 'Statutes'.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 11 of Act 23 of 1986
main_sections.description: This section amends Section 11 of the Cochin University of Science and Technology Act, 1986. It concerns the powers and functions of the Syndicate. The amendment appears to be related to the Syndicate's approval of statutes and ordinances. The section specifies that the Syndicate may approve statutes and ordinances subject to such conditions as it may deem fit. It also clarifies that the Syndicate can delegate certain powers to the Vice-Chancellor or Pro-Vice-Chancellor.
This section makes an amendment to Section 22 of the Principal Act. The amendment likely pertains to the composition or powers of a specific body within the University.
This section makes an amendment to Section 23 of the Principal Act. The amendment likely relates to the procedures or functions of a specific body or aspect of the University's governance.

important_rules: Section 1(2): The Act is deemed to have come into force on September 26, 1986.
Section 1(3): Amendments are in addition to other laws.
administration: Cochin University of Science and Technology
important_notes: The Act amends the Cochin University of Science and Technology Act, 1986 (Act 23 of 1986).
Specific amendments are made to sections 2, 11, 22, and 23 of the Principal Act.

title: The Cochin University of Science and Technology (Amendment) Act, 2012
purpose: To further amend the Cochin University of Science and Technology Act, 1986.
scope: Applies to The Cochin University of Science and Technology.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Cochin University of Science and Technology (Amendment) Act, 2012. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of December, 2011.

Amends section 17 of the Cochin University of Science and Technology Act, 1986 regarding the composition of the Senate. Specifically, it changes references to 'one a University Professor' to 'one a University Professor elected to the Senate as per item (v) under the heading 'Elected Members' in section 19' and replaces 'Mayor of Cochin' and 'Chairperson of Kalamassery Municipality' with 'Mayor of Cochin and the Chairperson of Kalamassery Municipality'.

Amends section 19 of the principal Act. It replaces 'Mayor of Cochin' and 'Chairperson of Kalamassery Municipality' with 'Mayor of Cochin and the Chairperson of Kalamassery Municipality' under the heading 'Ex-Officio Members'. It also introduces a sub-clause (iv) regarding six experts nominated by the Government from the field of Higher Education, one of whom shall be from Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes and one shall be a woman.

Notwithstanding anything contained in the principal Act, on the date of commencement of this Act, the existing members in office nominated under items (viii) and (xiv) of sub-section (1) of section 17 and under items (iv) and (v) under the heading 'Other Members' in section 19 of the principal Act, shall cease to hold their office by virtue of the provisions of this Act.

The Cochin University of Science and Technology (Amendment) Ordinance, 2012 (24 of 2012) is hereby repealed. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act, as amended by this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Governor of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Publication in the Gazette of Kerala.

administration: Law (Legislation-G) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act is a translation in English language of the notification published under the authority of the Governor.
The Act is enacted in the Sixty-third Year of the Republic of India.
The Act is deemed to have come into force on 1st December, 2011.

title: The Cochin University of Science and Technology Act, 1986
purpose: The Act aims to establish and incorporate a University at Cochin by the name 'The Cochin University of Science and Technology' for the advancement of University education and to facilitate the ideal to be achieved by such University.
scope: The Act applies to the establishment and functioning of the Cochin University of Science and Technology.

key_definitions.University: The Cochin University of Science and Technology established under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including University, State Government, Senate, Syndicate, Academic Council, etc.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment and incorporation of the University
main_sections.description: Establishes the Cochin University of Science and Technology with perpetual succession and a common seal, and powers to acquire and hold property and to sue and be sued.

Outlines the objectives of the University, including promoting higher education and research in technology, science, and other branches of learning, providing instruction and training, and promoting interdisciplinary studies.
Details the powers of the University, such as establishing departments, colleges, research institutions, conducting examinations, conferring degrees, and entering into collaborations.
Describes the constitution, powers, and functions of the Senate, which is the principal academic body of the University.
Details the constitution, powers, and functions of the Syndicate, which is the executive body of the University.
Explains the constitution, powers, and functions of the Academic Council, which is responsible for academic affairs of the University.
Outlines the establishment of various faculties within the University and their respective functions.
Defines the appointment, powers, and duties of the Pro-Vice-Chancellor.
Details the appointment, powers, and duties of the Registrar.
Specifies the appointment, powers, and duties of the Finance Officer.
Outlines the appointment, powers, and duties of the Controller of Examinations.
Provides for the appointment of other officers as may be deemed necessary by the University.
Details the process for making, amending, and repealing Statutes of the University.
Explains the process for making, amending, and repealing Ordinances of the University.

important_rules: Statutes of the University shall provide for the constitution, powers and duties of the bodies of the University.
Ordinances of the University shall provide for the conduct of academic and other activities of the University.
The University shall have power to confer degrees, diplomas, certificates and other academic distinctions.

rights: Right to establish departments, colleges and institutions.
Right to conduct examinations and confer degrees.
Right to enter into collaborations with other institutions.
Right to receive grants and donations.
duties: Duty to promote higher education and research.
Duty to provide instruction and training.
Duty to maintain academic standards.
obligations: The University shall be open to all persons of any caste, creed, race or sex.
The University shall strive to promote the advancement and dissemination of knowledge.

key_procedures: Procedure for making and amending Statutes.
Procedure for making and amending Ordinances.
Procedure for the admission of students.
Procedure for conducting examinations and awarding degrees.
administration: The administration of the University is vested in the Senate, Syndicate and the Vice-Chancellor and Pro-Vice-Chancellor.
important_notes: The University shall be open to all persons of any caste, creed, race or sex and no person shall be debarred from any department or course of study on any of these grounds.
The University shall be residential and its students shall be required to reside in the hostels provided by the University or in such other places as may be approved by the University.

title: THE CODE OF CIVIL PROCEDURE (KERALA AMENDMENT) ACT, 1957
purpose: To amend the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, in its application to the State of Kerala.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala. It amends the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Code of Civil Procedure (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1957. It also specifies that it extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

This section repeals two previous acts: the Code of Civil Procedure (Madras Amendment) Act, 1950 (XXXIV of 1950) and the Code of Civil Procedure (Travancore-Cochin Amendment) Act, 1951 (XVII of 1951). It specifies that any references to these repealed acts in other enactments will be considered references to the corresponding provisions of the principal Act as amended by this Act.

This section amends section 60 of the principal Act. Specifically, it modifies clause (g) of the proviso to sub-section (1). The words "stipends and gratuities granted to pensioners of the Government" are to be replaced with "the words 'or of a local authority' shall be inserted."

This section amends section 100 of the principal Act. It states that in sub-section (1) of section 100, after clause (c), a new clause (d) shall be added. This new clause (d) concerns the finding of the lower appellate court on any question of fact raised to the right decision of the case on the merits, being in conflict with the finding of the Court of first instance on such question.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By notification in the Gazette.

administration: Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
The amendment is specific to its application within the State of Kerala.
The Act repeals previous amendments from Madras and Travancore-Cochin.

title: The Code of Civil Procedure (Travancore Cochin) Amendment Act, 1951
purpose: To amend the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Central Act V of 1908) in its application to the State of Travancore-Cochin.
scope: Applies to the State of Travancore-Cochin.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called The Code of Civil Procedure (Travancore Cochin Amendment) Act, 1951, that it extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin, and that it shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 100, Act V of 1908
main_sections.description: Amends Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Central Act V of 1908) by adding a new clause (d) to sub-section (1). The new clause pertains to the finding of the lower appellate court on any question of fact material to the right decision of the case on the merits, when being in conflict with the finding of the court of first instance on such question.
States that The Code of Civil Procedure (Travancore-Cochin Amendment) Ordinance, 1951 (II of 1951) is hereby repealed.

important_notes: The Act was published in the Gazette Extra-Ordinary dated 27th October 1951.

title: The Code of Civil Procedure (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1987
purpose: To further amend the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, in its application to the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Code of Civil Procedure (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1987, extends to the whole of the State of Kerala, and shall come into force at once.

Amends Section 60 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Central Act 5 of 1908) by inserting a new clause (gg) to the proviso, which states that all moneys payable to the beneficiaries under the Family Benefit Scheme for the employees of the Government of Kerala shall be exempted from attachment.

important_rules: Moneys payable to beneficiaries under the Family Benefit Scheme for the employees of the Government of Kerala are exempt from attachment.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned, but likely implied to be the courts administering the Code of Civil Procedure.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application and enforcement of the amended Code of Civil Procedure.

rights: Beneficiaries of the Family Benefit Scheme have a right to receive their payments free from attachment.

administration: Law (Legislation-B) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the President on the 23rd day of December, 1987.
Published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary on 5th January 1988.

title: THE CODE OF CRIMINAL PROCEDURE (KERALA AMENDMENT) ACT, 1957
purpose: To further amend the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, in its application to the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Code of Criminal Procedure (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1957. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.

After section 406A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, a new section 407A is inserted concerning the appeal from sentence of Magistrate of the second or third class, and its transfer to the District Magistrate or any other Magistrate.

In section 408 of the principal Act, the words "any other Magistrate", the words "either Magistrate of the first class", and for the words "any Magistrate", the words "a Magistrate of the first class" are substituted.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 409
main_sections.description: Section 409 of the principal Act is substituted with a new section concerning appeals to the Court of Session or Sessions Judge, which can be heard by the Sessions Judge or by an Additional Sessions Judge.

important_rules: Any person convicted on a trial held by any Magistrate of the second or third class, or any person sentenced under section 349 or in respect of whom an order has been made or a sentence has been passed under section 380 by a subordinate Magistrate of the second class, may appeal to the District Magistrate.
The District Magistrate may direct that any appeal under the section, or any class of such appeals, shall be heard by any Magistrate of the first class subordinate to the District Magistrate.

rights: Right to appeal from sentence of Magistrate of the second or third class.

key_procedures: Appeals from sentences of Magistrates of the second or third class are to be presented to the District Magistrate.
The District Magistrate can transfer appeals to a subordinate Magistrate of the first class.
Appeals to the Court of Session or Sessions Judge shall be heard by the Sessions Judge or by an Additional Sessions Judge.
important_notes: The Act is enacted by the President in the Eighth Year of the Republic of India.
The Act is published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary dated 27th March 1957.

title: THE CODE OF CRIMINAL PROCEDURE (KERALA AMENDMENT) ACT, 1963
purpose: To further amend the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, in its application to the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Code of Criminal Procedure (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1963. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

In clause (m) of sub-section (1) of section 260 of the principal Act, for the words and figures 'section 20 of the Cattle Trespass Act, 1871' the words and figures 'section 19 of the Kerala Cattle Trespass Act, 1961' shall be substituted.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By notification in the Gazette.

administration: Not specified in the provided text, but likely the Home Department or Law Department of the Kerala Government.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the President on 12th February 1963 and was published in the Gazette Extraordinary, dated 18th February 1963.

title: THE EDAVAGAI RIGHTS ACQUISITION ACT, 1955
purpose: An Act to provide for the acquisition or extinguishment of Edavagai rights.
scope: It extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin.

key_definitions.Edavagai of Edapally: Means the Edavagai Estate of Edapally Swaroopam comprising the freehold lands in the Edavagai villages of (a) Edapally North in Parur Taluk, (b) Edapally South in Parur Taluk, (c) Thrikunnapuzha in Karthigapally Taluk, (d) Kalloppara in Thiruvalla Taluk and (e) Pazhayalam in Kunnathnad Taluk, recognised as such in the Revenue accounts and not owned by Government.
key_definitions.Edavagai of Kilimanoor: Means the Edavagai Estate of Kilimanoor Kottaram comprising the freehold lands in the Edavagai villages of (a) Pazhayakunnumpel in Chirayinkil Taluk and (b) Kilimanoor in Chirayinkil Taluk, recognised as such in the Revenue accounts and not owned by Government.
key_definitions.Edavagai of Poonjar: Means the freehold lands of Poonjar Koickal in the Edavagai village of Poonjar in Meenachil Taluk, recognised as such in the Revenue accounts and not owned by Government.
key_definitions.Edavagai of Vanjipuzha: Means the freehold lands of the Vanjipuzha Matom comprised in the Edavagai villages of (a) Cheruvully in Changanacherry Taluk, (b) Chirakadavu in Changanacherry Taluk, and (c) Peruvanthanam in Peermade Taluk, recognised as such in the Revenue accounts and not owned by Government.
key_definitions.Edavagai rights: Means all the rights and privileges vested in the Edapally Swaroopam, the Kilimanoor Kottaram, the Poonjar Koickal and the Vanjipuzha Matom relating to their respective Edavagais and includes the case of the Poonjar Koickal the right to receive Melvaram in respect of lands situate within the Edavagais of Poonjar.
key_definitions.Chief: In relation to the Edapally Swaroopam or the Kilimanoor Kottaram, or the Poonjar Koickal, or the Vanjipuzha Matom means the senior male member or other members of the respective families in whom the management of the family is vested for the time being.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Edavagai Rights Acquisition Act, 1955. It extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin. It shall come into force on the 1st day of January 1956.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Edavagai of Edapally', 'Edavagai of Kilimanoor', 'Edavagai of Poonjar', 'Edavagai of Vanjipuzha', 'Edavagai rights', and 'Chief'.

main_sections.section_title: Acquisition or extinguishment of Edavagai rights.
main_sections.description: Provides for the extinguishment of Edavagai rights of the Edapally Swaroopam and the Poonjar Koickal relating to Excise Revenues of the Edavagais of Edapally and Poonjar. Also extinguishes Edavagai rights of the Edapally Swaroopam and the Poonjar Koickal relating to other rights than Excise Revenues. Similar provisions apply to the Kilimanoor Kottaram and the Vanjipuzha Matom.

Details the compensation payable by the Government for the extinguishment of privileges and acquisition of rights. Specifies amounts and modes of payment, including annual income, interest, and annuities.

main_sections.section_title: Compensation payable for the extinguishment of privileges
main_sections.description: Details the compensation payable by the Government for the extinguishment of privileges, including a period of twenty years' interest and annual payments. Also specifies how such compensation is to be determined and paid to the private family deity or the Chief.

main_sections.section_title: Compensation payable for the acquisition of Edavagai rights etc.
main_sections.description: Details the compensation payable for the acquisition of Edavagai rights. Specifies amounts to be retained by Government, paid to the Chief, and other members of the family, including annuities for life-time members and their children.

States that arrears of rent and other debts payable to Edavagais at the commencement of the Act are deemed to be public revenue and shall be recoverable by the Government under the provisions of the Act. Specifies how collected amounts are to be distributed.

main_sections.section_title: Rights of registered land holders and other tenants.
main_sections.description: On and from the first day of April 1956, every registered landholder thereof shall be deemed to be a registered holder and pattadar under Government, and the holding shall be liable to land tax imposed by Government.

main_sections.section_title: Power to notify names of members and amount of Annuity.
main_sections.description: The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, specify the names of the Kilimanoor Kottaram and Poonjar Koickal who are entitled to life annuities under Section 6 and the annuity which each of them is entitled to receive.

main_sections.section_title: Expenditure to be charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State.
main_sections.description: Any expenditure incurred by the Government under this Act shall be expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State of Travancore-Cochin.

Specifies that the provisions of the Act shall not apply to lands owned by Devaswoms, lands held by Chiefs or their families or members, or lands in the direct possession of the Chiefs of the Edavagais or the Edapally Swaroopam, the Kilimanoor Kottaram, the Poonjar Koickal, or the Vanjipuzha Matom, or any of the members thereof, if such lands are situated within the respective Edavagais. Also states that lands falling under sub-section (1) shall be liable to basic tax imposed by Government from time to time.

The Government may make rules for prescribing the form of certificate to be issued to annuity holders, for enabling the Government to grant annuities, and for such other matters as may be necessary for giving effect to the provisions of this Act.

Repeals the Travancore Edavagai Act, III of 1908, and the Travancore Edavagai Act, III of 1109. Also states that the repeal shall not affect the revival, force or existing effect of any law, legal proceeding, remedy, investigation, or substitution.

important_rules: Edavagai rights are to be extinguished or acquired by the Government.
Compensation is payable by the Government for the extinguishment of privileges and acquisition of rights.
Arrears of rent and other debts payable to Edavagais are to be collected as public revenue.
Registered landholders are liable to land tax.
The Government has the power to make rules for the implementation of the Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, including recovery of public revenue and imposition of land tax.

rights: Right to receive compensation for extinguishment of privileges and acquisition of rights.
duties: Duty to pay land tax by registered landholders.
Duty to recognize the Government's acquisition of Edavagai rights.
obligations: Obligation of the Government to pay compensation.
Obligation of the Government to manage Edavagai lands if not owned by Government.

key_procedures: Procedure for acquisition of Edavagai rights and extinguishment of privileges.
Procedure for calculating and paying compensation.
Procedure for collecting arrears of rent and other debts.
Procedure for the Government to make rules for the Act's implementation.
administration: Government
important_notes: The Act repeals the Travancore Edavagai Act, III of 1908, and the Travancore Edavagai Act, III of 1109.
The repeal does not affect the revival, force, or existing effect of any law, legal proceeding, remedy, investigation, or substitution.
The expenditure incurred under the Act is charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State.
The provisions of this Act do not apply to certain categories of lands owned by Devaswoms, Chiefs, or their families.

title: THE EDAVAGAI RIGHTS ACQUISITION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2007
purpose: To amend the Edavagai Rights Acquisition Act, 1955, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: This Act applies to amendments to the Edavagai Rights Acquisition Act, 1955.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Edavagai Rights Acquisition (Amendment) Act, 2007. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 3rd day of December, 2005.
Amends section 6 of the Edavagai Rights Acquisition Act, 1955 (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act) by substituting specific phrases related to interest rates and cash annuities.

Repeals the Edavagai Rights Acquisition (Amendment) Ordinance, 2007 (52 of 2007). It also states that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act, as amended by the said Ordinance, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act, as amended by this Act.

important_notes: Received the assent of Governor on the 13th October, 2007 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No 1866 dated 15th October, 2007.

title: THE ELECTRICITY (SUPPLY) KERALA AMENDMENT ACT, 1983
purpose: To amend the Electricity (Supply) Act, 1948, in its application to the State of Kerala. The preamble states that it is expedient to amend the Electricity (Supply) Act, 1948, in its application to the State of Kerala, for the purpose hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and amends the Electricity (Supply) Act, 1948.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act as the Electricity (Supply) Kerala Amendment Act, 1983, states its extent of application (the State of Kerala), and specifies its commencement date as the date it came into force on the 21st day of February, 1983.

This section amends section 49 of the Electricity (Supply) Act, 1948. It introduces sub-section (5) to section 49, which details provisions regarding payment for electricity supplied by the Board. It specifies that payment should be made in respect of electricity supplied after commencement at such price, calculated in accordance with the uniform tariff framed or modified from time to time, and applicable to the category of the party to whom such supply belongs. It also states that the Board is not entitled to reimbursement from the price of any amount on account of increase in price of electricity supplied to it by the Board or on account of any tax, duty, surcharge, levy, cess or any other imposition or charges payable by such party in respect of the electricity supplied to it by the Board.

This section repeals the Electricity (Supply) Kerala Amendment Ordinance, 1983 (Ordinance 6 of 1983). It also includes a saving provision stating that nothing done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Payment for electricity supplied by the Board after commencement must be at the price calculated according to the uniform tariff.
The Board is not entitled to reimbursement for increased electricity prices or taxes/duties/cess/levies paid by the Board for supplying electricity.
The Electricity (Supply) Kerala Amendment Ordinance, 1983 is repealed.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated in the provided text, but likely the Electricity Board or relevant government authorities under the Electricity (Supply) Act, 1948.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Electricity (Supply) Act, 1948, as amended.

rights: The Board has the right to receive payment for electricity supplied according to the uniform tariff.
duties: The Board has the duty to supply electricity according to the uniform tariff.
obligations: Parties receiving electricity supply have an obligation to make payments as per the specified tariff.

key_procedures: Procedure for payment of electricity supplied: Payment is to be made at the price calculated in accordance with the uniform tariff applicable to the category of the party receiving the supply.
Procedure for amendment: Section 49 of the principal Act is amended by inserting a new sub-section (5).
Procedure for repeal: The Electricity (Supply) Kerala Amendment Ordinance, 1983, is repealed.
administration: Likely the Electricity Department or Board in Kerala, operating under the framework of the Electricity (Supply) Act, 1948.
important_notes: The Act came into force on the 21st day of February, 1983.
The Electricity (Supply) Kerala Amendment Ordinance, 1983 (Ordinance 6 of 1983) has been repealed.
Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are considered valid under the amended Act.

title: The Electricity Duty (Amendment) Act, 1958
purpose: To amend the Travancore-Cochin Electricity Duty Act, 1950 and the Madras Electricity Duty Act, 1939.
scope: Applies to consumers of electricity, with specific provisions for bulk consumers and licensees, within the geographical scope of the erstwhile Travancore-Cochin and Madras regions as applicable to Kerala.

key_definitions.bulk consumer: Means a consumer other than a licensee taking supply at 11 Kilo Volt or more.
key_definitions.licensee: Refers to entities involved in the supply of electricity, with specific amendments to related terms like 'licensees' and 'bulk consumers' in various sections.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Electricity Duty (Amendment) Act, 1958 and shall come into force on such date as the Government may notify.

main_sections.section_title: Amendments to the Travancore-Cochin Electricity Duty Act, 1950.
main_sections.description: This section details the specific amendments made to the Travancore-Cochin Electricity Duty Act, 1950. It includes changes to definitions, insertion of new sections related to duty on bulk consumers, and amendments to the schedule concerning rates of duty.

main_sections.section_title: Amendments to the Madras Electricity Duty Act, 1939.
main_sections.description: This section details amendments made to the Madras Electricity Duty Act, 1939, concerning its application to the Malabar District. It involves substitutions for terms like 'by licensees' and 'by licensees and bulk consumers', and the insertion of a new section regarding levy of duty on bulk consumers and a revised schedule.

important_rules: Levy of duty on bulk consumers: Every bulk consumer belonging to any class specified in column (1) of the Schedule shall pay every month to the Government in the prescribed manner a duty calculated at the rates specified against that class in column (2) thereof.

Provided that in cases where the supply of energy to a bulk consumer is regulated by an agreement entered into between the Government or the Kerala Electricity Board and the bulk consumer, it shall be competent for the Government either to reduce the rate at which duty is leviable on such consumer or to exempt such consumer from payment of duty under this section.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government of Kerala (implied by notification power and administration)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the levy and collection of electricity duty as prescribed in the Act and its schedules.

rights: Consumers have the right to have duty rates applied as per the schedule, with provisions for reduction or exemption for bulk consumers under specific agreements.
duties: Duty of bulk consumers to pay monthly electricity duty as calculated.
Duty of licensees to comply with the provisions of the Act and related regulations.
obligations: Obligation of the Government to notify the commencement date of the Act.

key_procedures: Notification of commencement date by the Government.
Calculation and monthly payment of electricity duty by bulk consumers as per the schedule.
Application for reduction or exemption of duty for bulk consumers based on agreements with the Government or Kerala Electricity Board.
administration: Government of Kerala (implied)
important_notes: The Act amends two pre-existing acts: the Travancore-Cochin Electricity Duty Act, 1950, and the Madras Electricity Duty Act, 1939.
Specific rates of duty are detailed in the Schedule, with variations based on the class of consumer and voltage of supply.
The Act makes specific provisions for the Malabar District concerning the application of the Madras Electricity Duty Act, 1939.

scope: Applies to the Travancore-Cochin Electricity Duty Act, 1950 and the Madras Electricity Duty Act, 1939.

main_sections.description: Amends the Schedule to the Madras Electricity Duty Act, 1939 (Act V of 1939) by substituting '0.25 Naya Paisa' and '0.2 Naya Paisa' for the existing entries '25 Naye Paise' and '2 Naye Paise'.

administration: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided pages.

title: The Essential Articles Control and Requisitioning (Temporary Powers) Amendment Act, 1958
purpose: To amend the Essential Articles Control and Requisitioning (Temporary Powers) Act, 1949.
scope: The Act applies to the amendment of the Essential Articles Control and Requisitioning (Temporary Powers) Act, 1949. Specific applicability details are not fully provided in the scanned pages.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Essential Articles Control and Requisitioning (Temporary Powers) Amendment Act, 1958, and that it shall come into force at once.

title: The Evacuee Interest (Separation) Travancore-Cochin Supplementary Act, 1954
purpose: To supplement certain provisions of the Evacuee Interest (Separation) Act, 1951 (Central Act LXIV of 1951).
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Evacuee Interest (Separation) Travancore-Cochin Supplementary Act, 1954. It extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 15th day of December 1952.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of certain provisions of Central Act LXIV of 1951
main_sections.description: The Evacuee Interest (Separation) Act, 1951 (Central Act LXIV of 1951), shall, so far as it relates to any matter enumerated in List II in the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India, stand validated and binding as if it had been passed by the Legislature of the State of Travancore-Cochin.
The Evacuee Interest (Separation) Travancore-Cochin Supplementary Ordinance, 1953 (Ordinance IV of 1953) is hereby repealed.

important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on the 15th day of December 1952.
Certain provisions of the Central Act LXIV of 1951 are validated and considered binding as if passed by the Travancore-Cochin Legislature.
The Travancore-Cochin Supplementary Ordinance, 1953 (Ordinance IV of 1953) is repealed by this Act.

title: The Evacuee Interest (Separation) Kerala Supplementary Act, 1960
purpose: To further supplement the Evacuee Interest (Separation) Act, 1951, by providing for the separation of evacuee interest, especially in cases where such interest is less than a certain proportion, and to make other incidental provisions.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Kerala. It came into force on a date to be appointed by the Central Government.

key_definitions.evacuee_interest: Interest which has vested in the Custodian of Enemy Property for India, or which is treated as evacuee interest under the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950, and includes the interest of an evacuee in property where such interest is less than one-fourth of the total interest in the property.
key_definitions.evacuee_interest_in_property: Includes the interest of an evacuee in property where such interest is less than one-fourth of the total interest in the property.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act, its extent (State of Kerala), and states that it shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may appoint.

main_sections.section_title: Application of Evacuee Interest (Separation) Amendment Act, 1960, to the State.
main_sections.description: This section clarifies that the amendments made to the Evacuee Interest (Separation) Act, 1951 by the Evacuee Interest (Separation) Amendment Act, 1960 (Central Act 64 of 1951), are to be treated as valid in the State of Kerala, to the extent that they are not inconsistent with the provisions contained in the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Central Government (for appointing commencement date), Legislature of the State of Kerala (for enacting the supplementary provisions).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application of the Evacuee Interest (Separation) Act, 1951 and its amendments as made applicable to the State.

key_procedures: The Act establishes the framework for the separation of evacuee interests, implying procedures for identification, valuation, and transfer of such interests.
The application of the Central Act's amendments suggests adherence to existing procedures for evacuee property management and separation.
administration: The administration would likely fall under the purview of authorities dealing with evacuee property, possibly under the Custodian of Enemy Property for India or designated state authorities.
important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 30th September, 1960.

title: THE GANDHIJI UNIVERSITY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1986
purpose: To amend The Gandhiji University Act, 1985.
scope: Applies to the Gandhiji University and its assets, liabilities, staff, and students.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Gandhiji University (Amendment) Act, 1986. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 15th day of October, 1985.
Inserts section 96A into the Gandhiji University Act, 1985, concerning the transfer of certain persons and assets from the University of Cochin to the Gandhiji University.

Repeals the Gandhiji University (Amendment) Ordinance, 1986 (46 of 1986). Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the Principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the Principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Transfer of certain persons from the University of Cochin to the Gandhiji University.
Transfer of assets, whether movable or immovable, including lands and buildings of the University of Cochin to the Gandhiji University.

All suits and other legal proceedings instituted or defended or which might be for the vesting and transfer under sub-section (1) have been instituted or defended by or against the University of Cochin may be continued or instituted or defended by or against the Gandhiji University.

Any person on the non-teaching staff of the University of Cochin may, subject to such conditions and restriction as may be specified by the Government in this behalf, opt to serve in connection with the affairs of the Gandhiji University.
The Vice-Chancellors of the University of Cochin and the Gandhiji University, by general or special order, shall stand allotted to serve in connection with the affairs of the Gandhiji University.
Provided that the number of non-teaching staff so allotted shall not exceed the sanctioned strength of non-teaching staff for the departments mentioned in sub-section (1).

Every person who becomes an employee of the Gandhiji University under sub-sections (4) and (8) shall, hold office under that University by the same tenure, at the same remuneration and upon the same terms and conditions with the same rights and privileges as to pension, gratuity, if any, and other matters, as he would have held the same on the date of commencement of the Gandhiji University (Amendment) Act, 1986, or on the date specified in the order under sub-section (6), as the case may be, as if the Gandhiji University (Amendment) Act, 1986, had not been passed.

The sums to the credit of the provident fund accounts of the persons referred to in sub-sections (4) and (8) as on the date of commencement of the Gandhiji University (Amendment) Act, 1986, or as on the date specified in the general or special order mentioned in sub-section (6) as the case may be, shall be transferred to the Gandhiji University and the liability in respect of the said provident fund accounts shall be the liability of the Gandhiji University.

There shall be paid to the Gandhiji University out of the accumulation in the superannuation fund and other like funds, if any, of the University of Cochin such amounts as have been credited to the superannuation fund and other like funds, if any, on behalf of the persons referred to in sub-sections (4) and (8).
The amounts paid under sub-section (11) shall form part of the superannuation fund or other like funds, if any, established by the Gandhiji University for the benefit of its employees.

Any student who, immediately before the commencement of the Gandhiji University (Amendment) Act, 1986, was undergoing any course in the Departments of Hindi or Law of the University of Cochin shall be permitted to complete his course under the University of Cochin and the Gandhiji University shall provide for the instructions of such students in accordance with the course of study in the University of Cochin and shall comply with such directions as may be given to it by the University of Cochin in respect of those students.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through orders issued by the Government and powers vested under the Act.

rights: Employees transferred have rights regarding tenure, remuneration, and privileges.
Students enrolled before the amendment can complete their courses.
duties: Gandhiji University shall provide instructions for students completing their courses.
Gandhiji University shall comply with directions from the University of Cochin regarding student instructions.
obligations: Transfer of liabilities and obligations of the University of Cochin regarding staff and assets to the Gandhiji University.

key_procedures: Transfer of staff and assets from University of Cochin to Gandhiji University as per Government orders.
Students to complete courses under the new arrangement.
Repeal of the Amendment Ordinance and saving of actions taken under it.
administration: The Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on 15th October, 1985.
Received the assent of the Governor on 30th November, 1986 and published in the Kerala Gazette, Extraordinary No. 1070 dated 30th November, 1986.
The amendment involves transferring assets, liabilities, and staff from the University of Cochin to the Gandhiji University.

title: The Gandhiji University (Second Amendment) Act, 1986
purpose: To further amend the Gandhiji University Act, 1985.
scope: Applies to the Gandhiji University.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Gandhiji University (Second Amendment) Act, 1986 and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 13th day of June, 1986.
Amends section 94 of the Gandhiji University Act, 1985, substituting the words "forty eight months" for the words "two years".

Repeals the Gandhiji University (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1986 (47 of 1986) and saves any action taken or deemed to have been taken or done under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance.

important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 30th day of November, 1986 and published in the Kerala Gazette, Extraordinary No. 1071 dated 30th November, 1986.

title: THE GANDHIJI UNIVERSITY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1987
