purpose: To further amend the Gandhiji University Act, 1985, for certain matters incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to matters concerning the Gandhiji University Act, 1985.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Gandhiji University (Amendment) Act, 1987. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of June, 1987.
Amends section 10 of the Gandhiji University Act, 1985. Specifically, it modifies sub-sections (4) and (6) regarding the period of office for members of the committee and their appointments.

main_sections.section_title: Revival of the committee and validation
main_sections.description: States that notwithstanding anything contained in the principal Act or in any other law, the term of office of members of the committee appointed by the Chancellor under section 10 of the principal Act, notification No. S3-5385/85/D2 dated the 3rd March, 1987 which expired on the 2nd day of June, 1987, shall with effect from the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette revive and accordingly anything done or to be done or any action taken or to be taken by the Chancellor or the said committee or any other person or authority in the purported exercise of the powers and functions conferred by or under the principal Act shall not be deemed to be invalid or ever to have been invalid merely on the ground that it at the term of office of the members of the committee aforesaid had expired on the said date.

important_rules: The Act is deemed to have come into force on June 1, 1987.
Modifications to the term of office of committee members appointed by the Chancellor under section 10 of the principal Act.
Validation of actions taken by the Chancellor or committee prior to the revival of the committee, even if their terms had expired.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Chancellor or other authorized persons/authorities related to the University.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the principal Act and this amendment.

key_procedures: Amendment of specific sections of the principal Act through legislative process.
Publication in the Gazette for general information and commencement of the Act.
Revival and validation of actions related to committee appointments.
administration: Law (Legislation-C) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Gandhiji University Act, 1985.
Specific notification number (No. S3-5385/85/D2) is referenced for committee appointments.
The amendment aims to rectify potential invalidity of actions due to expired terms of committee members.

title: The Gandhiji University (Dissolution of the Senate and the Syndicate) Act, 1988
purpose: To provide for the dissolution of the Senate and the Syndicate of the Gandhiji University and to entrust the powers and functions of the Senate and the Syndicate temporarily to the Vice-Chancellor of the Gandhiji University.
scope: Applies to the Gandhiji University, its Senate and Syndicate.

key_definitions.Gandhiji University: Gandhiji University constituted under the Gandhiji University Act, 1955 (12 of 1955).
key_definitions.Senate and Syndicate: The Senate and the Syndicate of the Gandhiji University.
key_definitions.Vice-Chancellor: The Vice-Chancellor of the Gandhiji University.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Gandhiji University (Dissolution of the Senate and the Syndicate) Act, 1988. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 24th day of December, 1957.
Defines terms used in the Act: Gandhiji University, Senate and Syndicate, and Vice-Chancellor.

main_sections.section_title: Dissolution of the Senate and the Syndicate
main_sections.description: Provides for the dissolution of the Senate and the Syndicate of the Gandhiji University from the date of commencement of this Act. The Senate and Syndicate shall stand dissolved.
Upon the dissolution of the Senate and the Syndicate under Section 3, all members of the Senate and the Syndicate shall be deemed to have vacated their offices.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of the Senate and the Syndicate
main_sections.description: Specifies that the powers and functions of the Senate and the Syndicate shall be exercised by the Vice-Chancellor. It also states that the powers and functions of the Senate and Syndicate as provided in sub-section (1) of section 12 of the Gandhiji University Act, 1955, during the interval between the dissolution and re-constitution of the Senate and the Syndicate, shall be exercised and performed by the Vice-Chancellor to such extent as the Government may determine.

main_sections.section_title: Reconstitution of the Senate and Syndicate
main_sections.description: States that the Senate and the Syndicate shall be reconstituted in accordance with the provisions of the Gandhiji University Act, 1955, within one year from the date of commencement of this Act.

Empowers the Government to make provisions for removing difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, with the caveat that such provisions should not be inconsistent with the provisions of this Act. Any such order shall be published in the Gazette and laid before the State Legislature.

Repeals the Gandhiji University (Dissolution of the Senate and the Syndicate) Ordinance, 1987. It also states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: The Senate and Syndicate of the Gandhiji University are dissolved.
Members of the Senate and Syndicate vacate their offices upon dissolution.
The Vice-Chancellor shall exercise the powers and functions of the dissolved Senate and Syndicate.
The Senate and Syndicate must be reconstituted within one year of the Act's commencement.
The Gandhiji University (Dissolution of the Senate and the Syndicate) Ordinance, 1987 is repealed, but actions taken under it remain valid.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through orders issued under Section 7 to remove difficulties. Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are saved.

rights: The Vice-Chancellor has the right to exercise the powers and functions of the Senate and Syndicate.
The Government has the power to issue orders to remove difficulties.
duties: The Government has the duty to ensure the reconstitution of the Senate and Syndicate within one year.
Any order issued by the Government for removing difficulties must be published in the Gazette and laid before the State Legislature.
obligations: The Vice-Chancellor is obligated to exercise the powers and functions of the Senate and Syndicate.

key_procedures: Dissolution of the Senate and Syndicate.
Vacating of offices by members.
Assumption of powers and functions by the Vice-Chancellor.
Reconstitution of the Senate and Syndicate within one year.
Government's procedure for removing difficulties via orders published in the Gazette and laid before the State Legislature.
Repeal of the 1987 Ordinance and saving of actions taken under it.
administration: Government of Kerala, Law (Legislation-C) Department
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on December 24, 1957.
The Act repeals the Gandhiji University (Dissolution of the Senate and the Syndicate) Ordinance, 1987 (7 of 1987).
Any difficulties in implementing the Act can be addressed by Government orders, subject to certain conditions.

title: The General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 1958
purpose: To amend the General Sales Tax Act, 1125 (Act XI of 1125) for purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and its transactions related to sales tax as per the General Sales Tax Act, 1125.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 1958. Specifies the commencement dates for different sections. Sections 1, 2, and 3 shall come into force on the 1st day of April, 1957. Sections 4 and 5 shall come into force on such date or dates as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint. Section 6 comes into force on the same date as section 4. Section 7 is the repeal section.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 2-A, Act XI of 1125
main_sections.description: Amends section 2-A of the Principal Act. It replaces the phrase "a judicial officer not below the rank of Additional District Judge" with "a judicial officer not below the rank of District Judge".

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 5-A, Act XI of 1125
main_sections.description: Amends section 5-A of the Principal Act. Introduces a new sub-section (1-A) which states that a dealer shall be liable to pay tax on the turnover of the stock of goods mentioned in sub-section (1) which were in his possession, custody or control immediately before the 14th day of December, 1957, at the point or points and at the rate applicable immediately before the said date.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new sections for section 16
main_sections.description: Substitutes new sections for section 16 of the Principal Act. The new section 16 deals with the maintenance of true and correct accounts and records by dealers. It mandates every dealer to keep registered under the Act to maintain such accounts and records as may be prescribed. The new section 16-A provides for the establishment of check posts or barriers and inspection of goods while in transit. It empowers the Government to establish such check posts or barriers and notify them. It also outlines the procedures for inspection of goods, vehicle records, and the issuance of sale or delivery notes. It grants powers to officers to seize and confiscate goods in specific circumstances, with provisions for informing the owner and the manner of inquiry.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 24, Act XI of 1125
main_sections.description: Amends section 24 of the Principal Act by inserting new clauses (b-i) to (b-v) after clause (b) in sub-section (2). These new clauses relate to the administration of check posts and barriers, the registration and work therein, the disposal of confiscated goods, the issue of bills or cash memoranda, the maintenance of counterfoils, the maintenance of purchase bills or accounts of purchases and sales, and the issue of delivery notes in respect of goods delivered to retail dealers.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Schedule 1, Act XI of 1125
main_sections.description: Amends Schedule 1 of the Principal Act. It substitutes items 6, 7 and 8 with new descriptions and corresponding rates. This includes motor vehicles, motor cycles, refrigerators, air conditioning plants, gramophones, time-pieces, watches, wireless reception instruments, cinematographic equipment, photographic equipment, binoculars, telescopes, opera glasses, iron and steel safes, arms, cigarettes, and dictaphones.
Repeals The General Sales Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 1958 (No. 1 of 1958).

important_rules: Dealers registered under the Act must maintain true and correct accounts and records as prescribed.
Goods carried in a vehicle or boat are subject to inspection at check posts or barriers.
The owner or person in charge of a vehicle or boat carrying goods must maintain a vehicle record, trip sheet, or a bill of sale or delivery note.
Confiscated goods must be handled and accounted for according to prescribed procedures.
The issue of bills or cash memoranda and the maintenance of counterfoils is mandatory.
Purchase bills or accounts of purchases and sales by dealers must be maintained.
Delivery notes are required in respect of goods delivered to retail dealers.

penalties: The act provides for confiscation of goods if a declaration made under sub-section (2) of section 16-A is false. The officer adjudging confiscation may give an option to pay in lieu of confiscation an amount not exceeding four times the tax recoverable where the goods are taxable.
For items that are taxable under the Act, the penalty for goods confiscated under section 16-A may be up to four times the tax recoverable.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government (through officers empowered under the Act)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Establishment of check posts and barriers for inspection of goods in transit. Seizure and confiscation of goods found to be in contravention of the Act. Inquiry into confiscated goods. Granting option to pay fine in lieu of confiscation.

rights: Dealers have the right to be informed of the grounds for confiscation of goods.
Dealers have the right to an inquiry when goods are confiscated.
Dealers have the option to pay a fine in lieu of confiscation of goods.
duties: Dealers have a duty to maintain true and correct accounts and records.
Dealers have a duty to produce vehicle records, trip sheets, or bills of sale/delivery notes when required.
Dealers have a duty to submit goods for inspection at check posts or barriers.
Dealers have a duty to issue bills or cash memoranda and maintain counterfoils.
Dealers have a duty to maintain purchase bills or accounts of purchases and sales.
Dealers have a duty to issue delivery notes for goods sold to retail dealers.
obligations: Dealers are obligated to pay tax on the turnover of goods in their possession, custody, or control as specified in section 3.

key_procedures: Procedure for establishment and operation of check posts or barriers for inspection of goods in transit, including notification, inspection of vehicle records, and issuance of sale/delivery notes.
Procedure for seizure and confiscation of goods found to be in contravention of the Act, including informing the owner, conducting an inquiry, and allowing payment of a fine in lieu of confiscation.
Procedure for amendment of the Principal Act by substituting or inserting new sections and clauses.
Procedure for substitution of items in Schedule 1 of the Principal Act.
administration: Government of Kerala (implied by the context of Kerala Sales Tax Act)
important_notes: The amendments are effective from various dates, some retrospective.
The Act repeals The General Sales Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 1958.
Specific items and their corresponding rates are amended in Schedule 1.

title: THE GENERAL SALES TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1961
purpose: To further amend the General Sales Tax Act, 1950, for the purposes hereinafter appearing. The amendments seem to relate to the sale of rice issued from Central or State Government depots, notification of goods exempt from taxation, and payment of tax on turnover.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala and deals with the General Sales Tax. It specifically mentions the application to goods issued from Central or State Government depots and goods specified in Schedule I and other goods. It also mentions a turnover threshold for dealers.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 1961, and it shall come into force with effect from and on the 1st day of April, 1961.

This section amends Section 4 of the principal Act (Act XI of 1950) by adding a sub-section (4) concerning the sale of rice issued from Central or State Government depots for public distribution. It specifies conditions for exemption from taxation for such sales and the requirement for notification in the Gazette.

This section amends Section 5 of the principal Act, clause (vi), by substituting the clause related to the sale of rice issued from Central or State Government depots. It also mentions inserting a new section 6A concerning the payment of tax by dealers.

This section inserts a new section 6A after section 6 of the principal Act. This new section deals with the payment of tax by dealers whose total turnover in any year does not exceed fifteen thousand rupees or twenty-five thousand rupees. It outlines the rates of tax applicable based on turnover and provides for exemptions under certain conditions.
This section amends Schedule I of the principal Act by substituting the items related to 'Foreign liquor including Indian made foreign liquor', 'Country liquor other than toddy', and 'Food grains'.

important_rules: Rule 1: Sales of rice issued from Central or State Government depots for public distribution are exempt from taxation upon notification in the Gazette.
Rule 2: Dealers with a total turnover not exceeding fifteen thousand rupees per annum pay a rate of tax of one hundred and fifty rupees per annum.
Rule 3: Dealers with a total turnover exceeding fifteen thousand rupees but not exceeding twenty-five thousand rupees pay a rate of tax of three hundred rupees per annum.
Rule 4: Dealers with a total turnover exceeding twenty-five thousand rupees may be permitted to pay tax under the assessing authority's direction, subject to prescribed conditions.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Assessing authority
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Assessing authority may permit dealers to pay tax under prescribed conditions.

rights: Dealers with total turnover below certain thresholds have specific tax payment provisions.
Dealers may be entitled to exercise options related to goods specified in Schedule I and other goods.
duties: Dealers are subject to the provisions of the General Sales Tax Act and its amendments.
Dealers may have to pay tax based on their turnover.
obligations: Dealers must comply with the payment of tax as prescribed by the Act.
Dealers must obtain permission from the assessing authority to pay tax under certain circumstances.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: For sales of rice from government depots, the procedure involves notification in the Gazette for exemption from taxation.

Procedure 2: For dealers with turnover above certain thresholds, the procedure involves assessing their turnover and determining tax liability, with provisions for paying tax under the direction of the assessing authority.
Procedure 3: Amendment of Schedule I involves substituting specific items related to liquor and food grains.
administration: Law Department, Secretariat, Kerala
important_notes: The Act came into force from the 1st day of April, 1961.
Published in the Gazette Extra-ordinary dated 30th March 1961, 34/4095.
The provisions regarding turnover thresholds and tax payment are specifically outlined.
The exemption for rice sales is contingent on a Gazette notification.
The amendment to Schedule I affects the classification and taxation of liquor and food grains.

title: THE GENERAL SALES TAX (SECOND AMENDMENT AND VALIDATION) ACT, 1962
purpose: To amend the General Sales Tax Act, 1125, and to provide for certain other connected matters.
scope: Applies to the entire Republic of India, specifically concerning the General Sales Tax Act, 1125.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the General Sales Tax (Second Amendment and Validation) Act, 1962. It also states that section 2 shall come into force at once, and section 3 shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of October, 1957.

This section amends sub-section (2) of section 27 of the General Sales Tax Act, 1125 (Act XI of 1125), stating that provided the powers and authorities appointed under this Act shall be competent to exercise on and after the 1st day of October, 1957, the same powers were exercisable before the said date by the corresponding officers and authorities appointed under the aforesaid Acts, in respect of all matters arising under the aforesaid Acts; and, if any question arises as to who such corresponding officers and authorities are, the decision of the Government, therefore shall be final.

This section provides that notwithstanding anything contained in any judgment, decree or order of any court, all actions done, notices issued, proceedings taken or orders passed under the provisions of any of the Acts repealed by sub-section (2) of section 27 of the principal Act, by the Government or by any officer or authority appointed under the principal Act, shall be deemed to be, and to have always been, validly done, issued, taken or passed as if such acts, were done, notices were issued, proceedings were taken or orders were passed by the Government or by the corresponding officer or authority, as the case may be, under the aforesaid repealed Act.

administration: Government of Kerala (inferred from the context of a State Act)
important_notes: This Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary, dated the 19th April 1962.

title: The General Sales Tax (Second Amendment) Act, 1960
purpose: To further amend the General Sales Tax Act, 1950 (Act XI of 1950) for the purposes mentioned.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the General Sales Tax (Second Amendment) Act, 1960. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

In section 5 of the General Sales Tax Act, 1950 (Act XI of 1950), after clause (vii), the following proviso shall be added: "Provided that the sale effected after the commencement of the General Sales Tax (Second Amendment) Act, 1960, of goods of the description specified in column (2) of items 46 to 49 (both inclusive) of Schedule I, which were in the stock of any dealer in the State at the commencement of the said Act, shall be liable to tax at single point in accordance with the provisions of this clause notwithstanding the fact that tax has been levied under this Act on the sale of such goods effected before such commencement."

In Schedule I to the principal Act, after item 45, the following items shall be inserted, namely: 46. Bicycles, tandem cycles and cycle combinations and tyres, tubes and accessories and parts thereof 47. Paints, colours, lacquers and varnishes 48. Scents and perfumes, powders, snows, scented hair oils, scented sticks, cosmetics and toilet requisites except soaps 49. Lubricating oils and greases

important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 30th July, 1963.

title: THE GURUVAYUR TOWNSHIP ACT, 1961
purpose: To constitute a Township for Guruvayur in the Trichur District and to provide for its administration.
scope: Applies to the Guruvayur Township area as defined in the schedule, which includes portions of Guruvayur, Iringaprom, Thaikkad, Chowghat, and Kuttanpadi Panchayats and Malabar District Board.

key_definitions.township: An area declared as a township for the purpose of the Act.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and that it comes into force on the date of appointment by the Government through notification in the Gazette. Also states that the Constitution and composition of the committee for administration of Guruvayur Township is detailed in the following sections.

Declares Guruvayur to be a township and that the area specified in the Schedule shall be a township. The Government can alter the limits of the area by notification in the Gazette, and such alteration will have effect from the date specified.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution and composition of committee for administration of Guruvayur Township.
main_sections.description: Details the formation of a committee for administering the municipal affairs of the Guruvayur Township. The Government shall, by notification, constitute a committee of seven members, to be elected by the Guruvayur Township Committee. The committee will consist of seven members, of whom at least four shall be non-officials. The Government shall appoint the Chairman and the Executive Officer.

main_sections.section_title: Application of Kerala Act of 1961 and other enactments to Guruvayur Township subject to specified modifications, additions and restrictions.
main_sections.description: Specifies that the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960 and other enactments will apply to the Guruvayur Township with modifications and restrictions as specified by the Government through notification. This includes provisions regarding the application of the Act, exercise of powers, and duties of local authorities.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of property rights and liabilities of Chowghat and Kottapadi Panchayats and of Malabar District Board.
main_sections.description: Details the transfer of property, rights, and liabilities of the specified Panchayats and the Malabar District Board to the Guruvayur Township Committee. This includes all lands, buildings, works, and other property, vested in or held by them, and all their rights, liabilities, and obligations.

Grants the Government the power to remove any difficulties that may arise in giving effect to the provisions of the Act, by order, which may be in the form of a modification of the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: The Government shall, by notification in the Gazette, constitute a committee for the administration of the municipal affairs of the Guruvayur Township.
The committee shall consist of seven members, of whom at least four shall be non-officials.
The Government shall appoint the Chairman and the Executive Officer of the Township Committee.
The Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960, shall apply to the Guruvayur Township with specified modifications and restrictions.
Property, rights, and liabilities of certain Panchayats and the Malabar District Board shall be transferred to the Guruvayur Township Committee.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government, through notifications and the constituted Township Committee.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By applying provisions of the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960, with modifications, and through the powers vested in the Township Committee and the Government's power to remove difficulties.

rights: Right to administer municipal affairs of Guruvayur Township.
Right to own and manage transferred properties and liabilities.
duties: Duty to administer municipal affairs of Guruvayur Township.
Duty to comply with provisions of the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960, as modified.
Duty to manage transferred properties and liabilities.
obligations: Obligation to carry out the functions and duties as specified by the Act and relevant enactments.

key_procedures: Constitution of the Township Committee by Government notification.
Appointment of Chairman and Executive Officer.
Application of Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960, with modifications.
Transfer of properties and liabilities.
Removal of difficulties by Government order.
administration: The Guruvayur Township Committee, constituted by the Government, administers the township. The Government retains oversight and power to issue notifications and orders.
important_notes: The Act is subject to modifications and restrictions specified by the Government.
The Government has the power to alter the limits of the township area by notification.
The Government has the power to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.

title: THE HINDU SUCCESSION (KERALA AMENDMENT) ACT, 2015
purpose: To further amend the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, in its application to the State of Kerala.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala and amends the Hindu Succession Act, 1956.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Hindu Succession (Kerala Amendment) Act, 2015, it extends to the whole of the State of Kerala, and it shall come into force at once.

Amends section 15 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 (Central Act 30 of 1956) by inserting a new clause (c) in sub-section (2). This amendment concerns the devolution of property inherited by a female Hindu from her pre-deceased son, specifying that such property shall devolve upon the heirs of the pre-deceased son.

important_rules: Property inherited by a female Hindu from her pre-deceased son shall devolve upon the heirs of the pre-deceased son.

rights: Right to property inherited by a female Hindu from her pre-deceased son.

administration: Law (Legislation F) Department, Government of Kerala

title: THE HOLDINGS (STAY OF EXECUTION PROCEEDINGS) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1952
purpose: To further amend the Holdings (Stay of Execution Proceedings) Act, 1950 (Act VIII of 1950) as amended by Act I of 1951. The amendment involves changing the duration mentioned in the original Act.
scope: Applies to the Holdings (Stay of Execution Proceedings) Act, 1950 and its amendments.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Holdings (Stay of Execution Proceedings) (Amendment) Act, 1952, and it shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 4, Act VIII of 1950
main_sections.description: This section amends Section 4 of the Holdings (Stay of Execution Proceedings) Act, 1950. It substitutes the words "two years" with "three years" in the said section.
This section repeals the Holdings (Stay of Execution Proceedings) (Amendment, Ordinance, 1952, (II of 1952).

important_rules: Substitution of 'two years' with 'three years' in Section 4 of the Holdings (Stay of Execution Proceedings) Act, 1950.
The Holdings (Stay of Execution Proceedings) (Amendment) Act, 1952 comes into force immediately upon enactment.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Holdings (Stay of Execution Proceedings) Act, 1950.
The amendment changes the duration from two years to three years.
An Ordinance related to this amendment (Ordinance, 1952, (II of 1952)) is repealed.

title: The Holdings (Stay of Execution Proceedings) Amendment Act, 1955.
purpose: To further amend The Holdings (Stay of Execution Proceedings) Act, 1950.
scope: Applies to The Holdings (Stay of Execution Proceedings) Act, 1950, as amended by various subsequent acts and ordinances.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as 'The Holdings (Stay of Execution Proceedings) Amendment Act, 1955' and states that it shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 4, Act VIII of 1950
main_sections.description: Amends Section 4 of the principal Act of 1950. Specifically, it substitutes the words 'five years and two months' with 'five years and six months' in relation to certain provisions.
Repeals The Holdings (Stay of Execution Proceedings) Amendment Ordinance, 1955 (Ordinance I of 1955).

important_notes: The Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary, dated 28th April 1955.
The principal Act being amended is The Holdings (Stay of Execution Proceedings) Act, 1950.
The amendment is made in the Sixth Year of the Republic of India.

title: THE INDIAN EASEMENTS (EXTENSION) ACT, 1961
purpose: To extend the Indian Easements Act, 1882, to the whole of the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Kerala. It extends the provisions of the Indian Easements Act, 1882 to Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Indian Easements (Extension) Act, 1961 and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of the Indian Easements Act, 1882
main_sections.description: Declares that the Indian Easements Act, 1882, as in force in the Malabar district, is extended to the whole of the State of Kerala. Any reference to the Malabar district in the said Act is to be read as a reference to the whole of the State of Kerala.

Repeals the Travancore-Cochin Easements Act, 1951. Savings clause: Provided that the repeal shall not affect any previous operation of the said Act or anything duly done or suffered thereunder, any right, privilege, obligation or liability acquired, accrued or incurred, any penalty, forfeiture or punishment incurred, or any investigation, legal proceeding or remedy in respect of any such right, privilege, obligation, liability, penalty, forfeiture or punishment. It also states that any such investigation, legal proceeding or remedy may be continued, enforced and any such penalty, forfeiture or punishment may be imposed, as if the Act had not been passed.

Grants the Government the power, by order notified in the Gazette, to make such provisions as appear to them necessary for the removal of difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Indian Easements Act extended by this Act to the whole of the State of Kerala.

important_rules: The Indian Easements Act, 1882, is extended to the whole of the State of Kerala.
References to the Malabar district in the Indian Easements Act, 1882, shall be construed as references to the whole of the State of Kerala.
The Travancore-Cochin Easements Act, 1951, is repealed.

penalties: Any penalty, forfeiture or punishment incurred in respect of any offence committed against the said Act, or any such right, privilege, obligation or liability acquired, accrued or incurred.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala (implied by the power to remove difficulties and notification in the Gazette)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Investigations, legal proceedings, or remedies may be continued or enforced as if the Act had not been passed.

rights: Any right acquired under the previous Act.
duties: Any duty acquired under the previous Act.
obligations: Any obligation acquired under the previous Act.

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act: Upon such date as the Government may appoint by notification in the Gazette.
Removal of difficulties: The Government may issue orders to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Act.
administration: The Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary, dated the 21st day of February 1962.
The repeal of the Travancore-Cochin Easements Act, 1951, does not affect past operations, liabilities, penalties, or ongoing legal proceedings.

title: The Indian Partnership (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1973
purpose: To amend the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, in its application to the State of Kerala.
scope: This Act applies to the whole of the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Indian Partnership (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1973. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new Schedule for Schedule I
main_sections.description: Schedule I to the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 (Central Act 9 of 1932) shall be substituted with a new Schedule, namely the one provided in this Act, which details maximum fees for various services related to the Act.

important_rules: Rule: Government may exempt any element of skill, by notification in the Gazette, from all or any provisions of this Act, subject to restrictions and conditions.
Rule: Police officers below the rank of a Sub Inspector of Police are exempted from certain provisions.
Rule: Police officers not below the rank of a Sub Inspector of Police are exempted from certain provisions.

penalties: Fifteen rupees for statement under section 58.
Five rupees for statement under section 60.
Five rupees for intimation under section 61.
Five rupees for intimation under section 62.
Five rupees for notice under section 63.
Five rupees for application under section 64.
Two rupees for inspecting one volume of the Register.
Two rupees for the inspection of all documents relating to one firm.
Fifty paise for each hundred words or part thereof for copies from the Register of Firms.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned for the amendment itself, but likely the Registrar of Firms or other designated authorities under the Indian Partnership Act, 1932.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the collection of prescribed fees for various services as detailed in the substituted Schedule I.

rights: Right to obtain statements under section 58.
Right to obtain statements under section 60.
Right to obtain intimations under sections 61 and 62.
Right to receive notices under section 63.
Right to apply under section 64.
Right to inspect the Register of Firms.
Right to inspect documents relating to a firm.
Right to obtain copies from the Register of Firms.
duties: Duty to pay prescribed fees for various services as detailed in Schedule I.

key_procedures: Procedure: To obtain various documents, intimations, notices, or copies from the Register of Firms, the prescribed fees must be paid.
Procedure: Inspection of the Register of Firms or documents relating to a firm requires payment of a fee.
administration: Not explicitly stated in the provided excerpt, but likely falls under the purview of the State Government of Kerala and its relevant departments dealing with company law and registration.
important_notes: Exemptions may be granted by the Government to any element of skill, by notification in the Gazette, subject to restrictions and conditions.
Police officers below the rank of a Sub Inspector of Police are exempted from certain provisions.
Police officers not below the rank of a Sub Inspector of Police are exempted from certain provisions.
The Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 810 dated 24th August, 1973.

title: The Indian Registration (Travancore-Cochin Amendment) Act, 1952
purpose: To amend the Indian Registration Act, 1908 (Central Act XVI of 1908) as applicable to the State of Travancore-Cochin.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Indian Registration (Travancore-Cochin Amendment) Act, 1952. It extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin. It shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 69, Central Act XVI of 1908.
main_sections.description: After clause (b) of sub-section (1) of Section 69 of the Indian Registration Act, 1908, the following clause shall be inserted, namely: "(bb) providing for the grant of licences to document writers, the revocation of such licences, the terms and conditions subject to which and the authority by whom such licences shall be granted and generally for all purposes connected with the writing of documents to be presented for registration".

key_procedures: Amendment of Section 69 of the Indian Registration Act, 1908 by inserting a new clause (bb) to provide for the grant and revocation of licences for document writers, their terms and conditions, and the authority for granting them.
important_notes: Published in the Gazette dated 23 rd December 1952 in Part I, Section iii.

title: The Indian Registration (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1968
purpose: To further amend the Indian Registration Act, 1908, in its application to the State of Kerala.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Indian Registration (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1968, and it extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.
Amends section 17 of the Indian Registration Act, 1908 (Central Act XVI of 1908) by inserting specific clauses related to documents presented for registration.
Amends section 19 of the principal Act.
Inserts a new section 19A regarding documents presented for registration to be accompanied by true copies thereof, and acceptance of true copies.
Amends section 45 of the principal Act by substituting words and figures in sub-section (1) and sub-section (2).
Amends section 46 of the principal Act by substituting words in sub-section (2) regarding true copies of documents.
Amends section 51 of the principal Act by substituting clauses in sub-section (2) concerning the contents of Book I.
Amends section 52 of the principal Act by substituting a clause in sub-section (1) regarding the true copy of the document.
Amends section 54 of the principal Act by substituting words related to filing a memorandum.
Amends section 55 of the principal Act by substituting words in sub-section (2), (4), and (5) regarding true copies.
Amends section 60 of the principal Act by substituting words in sub-section (1) regarding the true copy of the document.
Amends section 61 of the principal Act by substituting sub-section (1) regarding endorsements and certificates related to true copies of documents, maps, or plans.
Amends section 62 of the principal Act by substituting sub-section (1) regarding the translation of documents.
Amends section 78 of the principal Act by renumbering sub-section (1) and inserting a new sub-section (2) concerning the government's power to make rules.
Amends section 81 of the principal Act by substituting words related to registering or filing a true copy of a document.
Amends section 82 of the principal Act by substituting words in clause (b) regarding the Act or rules made thereunder.
Amends section 89 of the principal Act by omitting sub-sections (1) and (4) and inserting new sub-sections (5) and (6) concerning decrees, orders, and the attachment of immovable property.
Inserts a new section 89A giving the State Government power to make rules for filing true copies of documents and the generality of the foregoing power.

Repeals the Indian Registration (Kerala Amendment) Ordinance, 1967 (3 of 1967) and saves anything done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act if it had come into force on the 1st day of January, 1968.

important_rules: Documents presented for registration must be accompanied by their true copies.
True copies can be handwritten, printed, typewritten, lithographed, or otherwise prepared in accordance with specific rules.
Rules made by the State Government regarding true copies and filing of such copies are effective.
All rules made under this section shall be published in the Official Gazette and come into force on the day they are so published.
Rules made by the Legislative Assembly shall be laid before it, and if modified, the rule continues to have effect.
Subsequent modifications or annulments of rules do not prejudice their validity.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government (for making rules)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Rules made by the State Government are enforced upon publication in the Official Gazette.

rights: Right to present documents for registration with true copies.
duties: Duty to provide true copies of documents for registration.
obligations: Obligation to comply with rules regarding true copies and their preparation.
Obligation to file true copies of documents along with the originals.

key_procedures: Presenting documents for registration accompanied by true copies.
Preparation of true copies in handwritten, printed, typewritten, lithographed, or otherwise specified formats.
Filing of true copies along with the original document.
The State Government making rules for the filing of true copies, which are to be published in the Official Gazette.
In cases of decrees, orders, or attachment of property, sending a copy of the decree or order with a memorandum to the registering officer.
Issuing a written demand before the recovery of the property defaulting under the Revenue Recovery Act.
administration: State Government (for making rules)
important_notes: This is an amendment act to the Indian Registration Act, 1908.
The amendments are specific to the State of Kerala.
The Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 49, dated 22nd February, 1968.
The Ordinance of 1967 is repealed, and anything done under it is saved.

title: THE INDUSTRIAL DISPUTES (KERALA AMENDMENT) ACT, 1979
purpose: To further amend the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, in its application to the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala, further amending the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Industrial Disputes (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1979 and that it extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.

Inserts a new section 10B into the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947. This new section deals with the power to issue orders regarding terms and conditions of service pending settlement of disputes, specifically concerning public utility services. It allows the State Government to issue orders requiring employers to observe terms and conditions, or to prohibit certain actions, and outlines consequences for non-compliance. It also defines 'public utility service'.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new section 29A. Penalty for failure to comply with an order issued under section 10B.
main_sections.description: Inserts a new section 29A which provides for a penalty for any employer who fails to comply with any order issued under section 10B. The penalty is imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than six months but which may extend to one year, along with a fine.

Repeals the Industrial Disputes (Kerala Amendment) Ordinance, 1979. It also includes a saving clause stating that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act, if this Act had come into force on the 30th day of July, 1979.

important_rules: Employers in public utility services must adhere to the terms and conditions of service pending settlement of disputes as ordered by the State Government. (Section 10B(1))
Employers must not vary, to the prejudice of workmen, the conditions of service applicable to them immediately before the order was made, for three months. (Section 10B(1))
Employers are prohibited from discontinuing the employment of workmen or increasing their workload without due cause during the period of the order. (Section 10B(1))
Employers must provide payment of money to employees as may be determined by the order. (Section 10B(1)(a))
Employers in public utility services are prohibited from closing down or working on terms and conditions that are not close to or remaining in existence. (Section 10B(1)(b))
Any incidental or supplementary matters necessary for the purpose of the order must be attended to. (Section 10B(1)(c))

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than six months but which may extend to one year, and also with fine, for failure to comply with an order issued under section 10B. (Section 29A)
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government is empowered to issue orders under section 10B and enforce compliance.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through penalties of imprisonment and fines as stipulated in Section 29A for non-compliance with orders issued under Section 10B.

rights: Workmen have the right to have their terms and conditions of service observed by employers pending settlement of disputes in public utility services, as per orders issued by the State Government. (Section 10B)
duties: Employers in public utility services have a duty to comply with orders issued by the State Government regarding terms and conditions of service pending dispute settlement. (Section 10B)
obligations: Employers are obligated to observe specific terms and conditions and refrain from certain actions as directed by the State Government under Section 10B of the Act.

key_procedures: Issuance of orders by the State Government under Section 10B to regulate terms and conditions of service in public utility services during dispute settlement.
Enforcement of these orders through penalties for non-compliance, as outlined in Section 29A.
administration: The State Government of Kerala appears to be the primary administrator and enforcer of this amendment.
important_notes: The amendment inserts new sections 10B and 29A into the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.
The provisions of this Act are deemed to have come into force on the 30th day of July, 1979, due to the repeal and saving clause related to the Ordinance.

title: THE IRRIGATION LAWS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1978
purpose: An Act further to amend the Malabar Irrigation Works (Construction and Levy of Cess) Act, 1947 and the Travancore-Cochin Irrigation Act, 1956.
scope: Applies to irrigation works and their maintenance, specifically amending existing Acts related to irrigation works in Kerala.

key_definitions.lift irrigation work: means an irrigation work by which water for irrigation purposes is supplied with the aid of pumping sets or other mechanical devices.
key_definitions.co-operative society: means a co-operative society registered or deemed to be registered under the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969 (21 of 1969).

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Irrigation Laws (Amendment) Act, 1978. It also specifies that Clause (a) of section 3 shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of July, 1974 and the remaining provisions of this Act shall be deemed to have come into force on the 17th day of October, 1977.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Madras Act VII of 1947.
main_sections.description: Amends the Malabar Irrigation Works (Construction and Levy of Cess) Act, 1947 (Madras Act VII of 1947) by inserting clauses related to 'lift irrigation work' and 'Entrustment of lift irrigation works to co-operative societies'.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Travancore-Cochin Act VII of 1956.
main_sections.description: Amends the Travancore-Cochin Irrigation Act, 1956 (Act VII of 1956) by inserting provisions for construction of new irrigation works by Government and entrusting maintenance of lift irrigation works to co-operative societies.
Repeals the Irrigation Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1977 (19 of 1977) and provides savings for actions taken or to be taken under the repealed Ordinance and the amended Acts.

important_rules: Any lift irrigation work constructed by Government may be entrusted to a co-operative society.
The State Government may authorise the collection by such society of the water cess levied under section 12 or section 15 in relation to such irrigation work.

The State Government may, if they consider it necessary in the public interest so to do, construct a minor irrigation work on any land belonging to or vested in a local authority or acquired by them for the purpose, without following the procedure specified in the said sections.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amendments to existing irrigation laws and their respective enforcement mechanisms.

rights: The right of the State Government to construct minor irrigation works on local authority land.
The right of the State Government to authorise co-operative societies to collect water cess.
duties: The duty of the State Government to consider public interest when constructing minor irrigation works.
obligations: Co-operative societies entrusted with lift irrigation works must maintain them subject to terms and conditions prescribed.

key_procedures: Procedure for entrusting the maintenance of lift irrigation works to co-operative societies.
Procedure for authorising co-operative societies to collect water cess.
Procedure for the State Government to construct minor irrigation works on local authority land without following standard procedures if deemed necessary in public interest.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but likely the Department of Irrigation or a related ministry within the Kerala State Government.
important_notes: The Act came into force on different dates for different provisions.
The Act amends the Malabar Irrigation Works (Construction and Levy of Cess) Act, 1947 and the Travancore-Cochin Irrigation Act, 1956.
The definition of 'co-operative society' refers to the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969.
The Ordinance repealing the Irrigation Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1977 had specific saving provisions.

title: The Judicial Proceedings (Validation) Act, 1971
purpose: To validate certain proceedings, decrees, orders and acts of the Courts of District Judges invested with the jurisdiction of a Land Acquisition Court under the Kerala Land Acquisition Act, 1961, which might otherwise be invalid due to jurisdictional doubts.
scope: The Act applies to proceedings, decrees, orders and acts of the Courts of District Judges and Subordinate Judges invested with the jurisdiction of a Land Acquisition Court under the Kerala Land Acquisition Act, 1961, in references under that Act, where such appeals were instituted in the High Court.

main_sections.description: (1) This Act may be called the Judicial Proceedings (Validation) Act, 1971. (2) It shall come into force at once.

Notwithstanding any judgment, decree or order of any court, all proceedings taken, all decrees and orders passed and all other acts and things done by Courts of District Judges on appeals from the decisions of the Courts of Subordinate Judges invested with the jurisdiction of a Land Acquisition Court under the Kerala Land Acquisition Act, 1961 (21 of 1962), in references under that Act, instituted in the High Court, shall be deemed to have been taken, passed or done in accordance with law and shall not be deemed to be invalid or ever to have been invalid merely on the ground that the said Courts had no jurisdiction to entertain such appeals.

important_rules: All proceedings, decrees, orders, and acts done by Courts of District Judges on appeals from subordinate judges, under the Kerala Land Acquisition Act, 1961, shall be deemed valid.
These acts, decrees, and orders shall not be considered invalid due to lack of jurisdiction in the said courts to entertain the appeals.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not specified, implied to be through judicial interpretation and application of the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By deeming certain past actions as valid and lawful, preventing them from being challenged on grounds of jurisdiction.

administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but likely falls under the purview of the Kerala State Judiciary and relevant administrative departments overseeing land acquisition and judicial processes.
important_notes: The Act is retrospective, validating actions taken in the past.

The validation is specific to appeals from decisions of Subordinate Judges invested with jurisdiction under the Kerala Land Acquisition Act, 1961, and heard by District Judges and then referred to the High Court.
Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 345, dated 5th August, 1971.

title: The Judicial Proceedings (Validation) Act, 1958
purpose: To validate the proceedings and acts of certain Courts, particularly those that were made void due to notifications abolishing them with effect from the first day of November 1956.
scope: Applies to all decrees, orders passed, all plaints, written statements, memoranda of appeals, applications, petitions and other documents received, all proceedings taken and all acts and things done, by or before the Courts specified in the Schedule or any Judge or Officer thereof, during the period from the first day of November, 1956, to the 6th day of November, 1956.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Judicial Proceedings (Validation) Act, 1958, and it shall come into force at once.

This section validates all decrees and orders passed, all plaints, written statements, memoranda of appeals, applications, petitions and other documents received, all proceedings taken and all acts and things done, by or before the Courts specified in the Schedule or any Judge or Officer thereof, during the period from the first day of November, 1956, to the 6th day of November, 1956, both days inclusive, deemed to have been validly passed, received, taken or done, notwithstanding that the said Courts were abolished with effect from the first day of November, 1956, by Government Notifications No. C4-30275/56/JD (1) and (2) dated the 1st day of November, 1956.

important_rules: All decrees and orders passed, plaints, written statements, memoranda of appeals, applications, petitions and other documents received, all proceedings taken and all acts and things done by or before the specified Courts between November 1, 1956 and November 6, 1956, are deemed valid.
This validation is effective despite the abolition of these Courts by Government Notifications on November 1, 1956.
important_notes: The Act is published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 17th July, 1958.

title: The Kerala Bovine Breeding Act, 2024
purpose: To provide for regulating breeding activities such as the production of semen from bovine bulls used for breeding, processing, storage, sale and distribution of semendoses including artificial insemination and bovine breeding and allied activities with the object of increasing the best variety of bovines in the State of Kerala and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala. It covers all activities related to bovine breeding, including semen production, processing, storage, sale, distribution, and artificial insemination, as well as allied activities.

key_definitions.artificial_insemination_a_i: The act of artificially depositing breeding bulls’ semen into the matured cattle's reproductive tract by means of technology. Cattle include cow, cow-heifer, buffalo, and buffalo heifer.
key_definitions.authority: The Bovine Breeding Regulatory Authority constituted under section 3 of the Act.
key_definitions.bovine: Cow, cow-bull, cow-heifer, buffalo, buffalo-bull, and buffalo heifer.
key_definitions.semendose: A dose of semen kept in semen straw.
key_definitions.recognised_laboratory: The Institute for Animal Diseases/Regional Diseases Diagnostic Laboratory or any other Laboratory duly authorised by the Authority.

main_sections.description: This section names the Act as the Kerala Bovine Breeding Act, 2024, and states that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Government.
This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as Artificial Insemination (A.I.), Authority, Bovine, Semen, Recognised Laboratory, etc.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of the Bovine Breeding Regulatory Authority
main_sections.description: This section outlines the constitution of the Bovine Breeding Regulatory Authority, its members (including Chairperson, Secretary, and other officials), and the role of the Registrar.

This section details the various functions of the Bovine Breeding Regulatory Authority, including implementing breeding policy, regulating storage and sale of semendoses, certifying bulls, registering semen stations and banks, certifying AI technicians, and organizing awareness programs.

This section states that no premises can be searched for an offence under this Act without a written order from the Authority or an authorized officer. Offences are triable by a Judicial First Class Magistrate.
This section clarifies that any document purporting to be a report from a recognised laboratory is admissible as evidence in any proceedings under the Act.
All experts and officers of the Authority are deemed to be public servants under the Bharatiya Nyaya Samhita, 2023.
No civil court has jurisdiction to set aside any order or interfere with any proceedings of the Authority or its officers regarding matters concerning this Act.

Protection of action taken in good faith. No suit, prosecution or other legal proceedings shall lie against the Authority or any of its members, officers, or experts for anything done or intended to be done in good faith under this Act or rules made thereunder.
The Government has the power to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act. These rules must be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

The Government can issue orders to remove any difficulties in the implementation of the Act, but not after two years from the commencement of the Act. These orders must be laid before the Legislative Assembly.
The Kerala Livestock Improvement Act, 1961, is repealed. However, anything done or any action taken under the repealed Act is considered to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Artificial insemination involves artificially depositing semen into the reproductive tract of cattle.
Premises used for semen storage, distribution, trade, or utilization are covered under the Act.
Misbranded semen is defined as semen where the DNA profile does not match the recorded DNA profile.
Sub-standard semen lacks specified standards.
Unauthorised semen doses are those without approval from the Authority.

penalties: The text provided does not explicitly detail specific monetary penalties or imprisonment terms for violations. It mentions that offences are punishable and triable by a Judicial First Class Magistrate (Section 24(2)). Further details on penalties would likely be found in other sections or rules not included in the provided text.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Bovine Breeding Regulatory Authority and officers authorized by it.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through searches of premises with prior authorization, examination of reports from recognized laboratories, and prosecution of offenders by Judicial First Class Magistrate Courts.

rights: Right to have actions taken in good faith protected from legal proceedings.
Right to seek clarification/orders to remove difficulties in Act implementation from the Government.
duties: Duty of the Authority to implement bovine breeding policy and allied services.
Duty of related authorities to provide necessary assistance and information to the Authority (Section 26).
Duty of the Government to provide funds for the Authority's functioning (Section 33).
obligations: Obligation to comply with the regulations on semen production, processing, storage, sale, and distribution.
Obligation for AI technicians to be certified by the Authority.
Obligation for semen stations, banks, and AI centres to be registered.
Obligation for bulls and buffalo-bulls to be certified by the Authority for semen production.

key_procedures: Constitution of the Bovine Breeding Regulatory Authority: The Government constitutes the Authority through a Gazette notification.
Certification of bulls and AI technicians: The Authority certifies breeding bulls and AI technicians based on prescribed criteria and procedures.
Registration of semen stations, banks, and AI centres: These entities must be registered with the Authority as per the Act and rules.
Rule making: The Government can make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act, which are then laid before the Legislative Assembly.
Removal of difficulties: The Government can issue orders to remove difficulties, subject to laying them before the Legislative Assembly.
administration: The Bovine Breeding Regulatory Authority, with its headquarters in the office of the Directorate of Animal Husbandry Department of the State. The Government of Kerala is responsible for making rules and issuing notifications.
important_notes: The Act repeals The Kerala Livestock Improvement Act, 1961.
Actions taken under the repealed Act are deemed valid under this new Act.
The Government has the power to remove difficulties in implementing the Act for a period of two years from its commencement.

title: The Kanam Tenancy Abolition (Amendment) Act, 1979
purpose: To amend the Kanam Tenancy Abolition Act, 1976, for the purpose hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to amendments to the Kanam Tenancy Abolition Act, 1976.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kanam Tenancy Abolition (Amendment) Act, 1979, and that it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of January, 1970.

Amends section 15 of the Kanam Tenancy Abolition Act, 1976, by substituting words and figures within one year from the date of publication of the Kanam Tenancy Abolition Ordinance, 1975, in the Gazette.

Repeals the Kanam Tenancy Abolition (Amendment) Ordinance, 1973 (5 of 1973). It also provides that nothing done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_notes: The Act received the assent of the President on the 2nd November, 1979, and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 785, dated 3rd November, 1979.

title: THE KANAM TENANCY ABOLITION (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 1979
purpose: To further amend the Kanam Tenancy Abolition Act, 1976, for the purposes hereinafter appearing. Specifically, this amendment concerns the restoration of possession of certain holdings sold for arrears of jenmikaram.
scope: Applies to the Kanam Tenancy Abolition Act, 1976, and its provisions related to holdings sold for arrears of jenmikaram.

key_definitions.kanam tenancy: A form of land tenure in Kerala.
key_definitions.jenmikaram: A payment or share due to the jenmi (landlord) from the tenant.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kanam Tenancy Abolition (Second Amendment) Act, 1979, and shall come into force on the 1st day of January, 1970.

Inserts a new section, 15A, into the Kanam Tenancy Abolition Act, 1976, concerning the restoration of possession of certain holdings sold for arrears of jenmikaram. This section details conditions under which possession can be restored, including deposit of amounts and court orders.

Repeals the Kanam Tenancy Abolition (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1979 (12 of 1979). It also includes a saving clause stating that anything done or any action taken under the repealed Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Holdings sold for arrears of jenmikaram can be restored to the Kanam tenant if certain conditions are met.

Rule 2: The Kanam tenant is entitled to restoration of possession of a holding if they deposit an amount equal to the arrears of jenmikaram for the one year immediately preceding the appointed day, within six months from the date of publication of the Kanam Tenancy Abolition (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1979.
Rule 3: If a holding has been sold to a purchaser other than the decree-holder, the amount to be deposited shall be equal to the purchase money plus interest at the rate of six per cent per annum.
Rule 4: If the deposited amount is found insufficient, the court shall not pass an order unless the deficit is deposited within a specified period.

Rule 5: The court may order the applicant to deposit the purchase money with any further amount as it may specify, towards the cost of the auction purchaser and the value of improvements, if any, effected after the sale.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through court orders for restoration of possession and deposit of amounts.

rights: Right of the Kanam tenant to seek restoration of possession of holdings sold for arrears of jenmikaram.
Right to have the sale set aside upon fulfillment of deposit conditions.
duties: Duty of the Kanam tenant to deposit specified amounts within prescribed time limits.
Duty of the court to inquire and pass orders on applications for restoration.
obligations: Obligation to deposit purchase money and interest if applicable.
Obligation to deposit any deficit amount required by the court.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: A Kanam tenant whose holding was sold for arrears of jenmikaram can apply for restoration of possession.

Procedure 2: The tenant must deposit the arrears of jenmikaram for the preceding year (or purchase money plus interest if sold to a third party) within six months from the publication of the relevant ordinance.
Procedure 3: The court will conduct a summary inquiry and, if satisfied, set aside the sale and restore possession to the applicant, provided any deficit amount is also deposited.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but likely administered by the State Government of Kerala, specifically the departments dealing with land revenue and tenancy matters.
important_notes: The Act has retrospective effect from January 1, 1970.
The inserted section 15A applies to holdings sold for arrears of jenmikaram.
The Kanam Tenancy Abolition (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1979, has been repealed but actions taken under it are saved.

title: THE KANAM TENANCY ACT, 1955 (XXIV OF 1955)
purpose: To confer full proprietary rights on kanam tenants in the Cochin area subject only to the payment of jennikaram and to provide for the settlement, collection and payment of jennikaram and for matters incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of Cochin and also to the enclaves which formed part of the Malabar District and which have been absorbed in the State of Travancore-Cochin under the Provinces and States (Absorption of Enclaves) Order, 1950. It applies to kanam tenants and jennikaram tenants in the specified areas.

key_definitions.fractional fee: The fee fixed as claimable in substitution of the renewal fees in annual instalments at the rate of seven per cent. of the aggregate value or amount of one year's michavaram or of the renewal fees payable under the Cochin Tenancy Act, XV of 1911, whether it is less or in annual instalments, proportionally lower in percentage when renewal on the expiry of any longer period is provided for by the Kanam.
key_definitions.Holding: parcels of land held under a single arrangement by a tenant from a jemmi and shall include any portion of a holding if above defined which the jemmi and kanam-tenant have agreed to treat as a separate holding.
key_definitions.Jenmi: A person immediately under whom a kanam-tenant holds.
key_definitions.Kanam: A Kanam means a demised land with the following incidents: (i) an initial lump sum consideration in money or in kind or both given or deemed to be given by the kanam-tenant to the jenmi which is mentioned as such in the demise and bears a specified interest; (ii) the payment of michavaram, if any, by the kanam-tenant to the jenmi; (iii) the right of the tenant to occupy the property demised for 12 years or for any other longer period which is specified; (iv) in respect of a demise created prior to the commencement of this Act the liability to pay a renewal fee on renewal of the demise.
key_definitions.Kanam amount: The amount specified in sub-clause (i) of Clause (4) of this section in respect of a kanam.
key_definitions.Michavaram: The balance of money or produce payable periodically under the contract of tenancy to the jenmi after deducting from the pattom the interest due on the kanam amount and puramkadam, if any.
key_definitions.Pattom: The jenmi's share as fixed by the contract of tenancy of the produce of the holding whether in money or in kind or both, but does not include renewal fee.
key_definitions.Puravaka dues: Whatever is payable in money or in kind or both by the terms of a demise other than pattom or michavaram and renewal fee.
key_definitions.Puramkadam: A further sum of consideration received by the jenmi subsequently to the kanam amount from a kanam tenant in respect of the holding.
key_definitions.Renewal fee: Fees payable by a kanam-tenant to his jenmi under the contract of tenancy for the renewal of the kanam which the kanam-tenant has been holding any land.
key_definitions.Kanam-tenant: A person who holds land on Kanam tenure.
key_definitions.Jennikaram: In respect of a holding or any land comprised in a holding means the amount payable in respect of that holding or land under the provisions of this Act by the Kanam-tenant to the jenmi, every year in lieu of all claims of the jenmi in respect of the holding or land and shall be the sum total of the michavaram and the fractional fee.
key_definitions.Prescribed: Prescribed by Rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kanam Tenancy Act, 1955. It extends to the whole of Cochin and also to the enclaves which formed part of the Malabar District and which have been absorbed in the State of Travancore-Cochin under the Provinces and States (Absorption of Enclaves) Order, 1950. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'fractional fee', 'Holding', 'Jenmi', 'Kanam', 'Kanam amount', 'Michavaram', 'Pattom', 'Pay', 'Puravaka dues', 'Puramkadam', 'Renewal fee', 'Kanam-tenant', 'Jennikaram', and 'Prescribed'.

main_sections.section_title: Kanam-tenant owner of land subject only to payment of jennikaram
main_sections.description: States that a Kanam-tenant is the owner of the land subject only to the payment of jennikaram. It clarifies that the jenmi shall not have any right, claim or interest in any land in a holding except the right to receive the jennikaram and the kanam-tenant shall be deemed to be the owner of the land subject only to the payment of the jennikaram. It also clarifies that notwithstanding any usage or contract to the contrary, no kanam-tenant has the right to relinquish his holding or any portion thereof and no jenmi has the right to evict a kanam-tenant from his holding or any portion thereof. Similarly, notwithstanding any usage or contract to the contrary, every kanam-tenant has the right to make any improvement in respect of his holding without reference to, or interference from the jenmi. The jenmi's right as well as the kanam-tenant's right is heritable as well as transferable by sale, gift or otherwise. The jenmi's right to the jennikaram shall be deemed to be immovable property.

main_sections.section_title: Jennikaram how fixed on land being divided
main_sections.description: If any land is divided for any reason, the jennikaram on each portion of the land shall be fixed in the proportion of the Government tax that will be fixed on such portion of land and the jennikaram so fixed shall be the jennikaram due thereon.

The jennikaram of a holding together with the interest, if any, due thereon, when it becomes an arrear, shall be claimable by the jenmi and shall, subject to the priority of the rights of the Government, for arrears of tax be a first charge on the holding.

main_sections.section_title: Kanam-tenant's liability on jenmi's right being transferred
main_sections.description: When the jenmi's right in any land comprised in a holding is transferred by sale, gift or otherwise, he shall be liable to the transferee for the jennikaram which became due after the transfer and was paid to the jenmi whose right so transferred, unless a transferor or transferee has, before the payment, given notice of the transfer to the kanam-tenant by registered post.

main_sections.section_title: Kanam-tenant's liability on holding being transferred
main_sections.description: When any land comprised in a holding or any holding is divided or is transferred by sale, gift or otherwise by the kanam-tenant without the consent of the jenmi, the kanam-tenant shall continue liable for the jennikaram accruing due after such division or transfer, unless and until notice by registered post of such division or transfer is given to the jenmi by any sharer or transferor or transferee, as the case may be, and until the transfer of registry is effected in the Land Revenue records in accordance with the division or transfer.

main_sections.section_title: Kanam tenant's liability on land being divided
main_sections.description: This provision does not affect any liability of any sharer or transferee as between such person and other sharers or the transferor, as the case may be, to pay the jennikaram.
Notwithstanding any usage or contract to the contrary, it shall not be obligatory on the jenmi to renew, or on the kanam-tenant to accept the renewal of a contract of kanam.
Notwithstanding any usage or contract to the contrary, the jennikaram of any land shall not be liable to alteration or revision at any time.
No kanam can be created after this Act comes into force except by a registered instrument.

main_sections.section_title: Particulars which kanam instrument should contain
main_sections.description: No instrument by which a kanam is created or its counterpart shall be registered unless it contains: (a) the name, if any, and description and extent of the holding; (b) the Government revenue and local taxes, if any, payable in respect of the holding; (c) the kanam amount and puramkadam, if any; (d) the rate or the amount of interest payable in respect of the kanam amount and puramkadam, if any; and (e) the michavaram, fractional fee and the jennikaram payable in respect of the holding.

main_sections.section_title: Appeal from the order of the Registrar
main_sections.description: An order of the Registrar refusing registration on the ground of the absence of any of the particulars specified in Section 12 shall be subject to appeal in accordance with the provisions of the Indian Registration Act, 1908.

main_sections.section_title: Stamp and registration charges for kanam instruments
main_sections.description: The stamp and registration charges for kanam instruments and for its counterpart shall be borne by the kanam-tenant and the jenmi respectively.

main_sections.section_title: When summary suit will not lie
main_sections.description: No summary suit or claim for enforcing payment of any jennikaram shall be enter-tained by the Courts under this Act unless either the jennikaram or michavaram and the renewal fees with reference to which the jennikaram has to be ascertained, are specified in the kanam document or its counterpart duly registered or in a decree of a Civil Court obtained in a regular suit between the jenmi and the kanam-tenant.

main_sections.section_title: Jennikaram alone payable to jemmi with interest if in arrears
main_sections.description: Jennikaram shall be entitled to receive and every Kanam-tenant shall be bound to pay in respect of all land in the latter's holding the jennikaram due thereon, and notwithstanding any contract or usage to the contrary the jenmi shall not be entitled to receive from the kanam-tenant and the kanam-tenant shall be bound to pay to the jenmi anything else in respect of the land. The jennikaram shall be payable in such instalments and on such dates as the Government may, by rules made under this Act, determine, or in the absence of such rules, at or before the close of each Financial year. An arrear of jennikaram shall bear simple interest at the rate of six per cent. per annum. Notwithstanding any usage or contract to the contrary, the kanam-tenant shall be liable to pay all Government and local taxes in respect of the land comprised in his holding whether existing at the time of the demise or imposed afterwards. Where according to the terms of contract of kanam, renewal fees are payable at the expiry of a specified period and one or more such periods have expired at the commencement of this Act, and no renewal fees have been paid, the aggregate amount of the renewal fees payable under the contract of kanam in respect of such period or periods shall, subject to the provisions of sub-section (2), be payable by the kanam-tenant to the jenmi.

main_sections.section_title: Kanam-tenant may pay jennikaram in money
main_sections.description: The Jiemmi shall not be entitled to receive from the Kanam-tenant and the Kanam-tenant shall be bound to pay to the Jemmi anything else in respect of the land.
