important_rules: A Kanam can only be created by a registered instrument after the Act comes into force.

The jennikaram accrues due after a division or transfer of land is payable by the kanam-tenant, unless notice of such division or transfer is given to the jenmi by registered post and the transfer of registry is effected.
Jennikaram shall be paid in such instalments and on such dates as the Government may determine, or at or before the close of each Financial year.
An arrear of jennikaram shall bear simple interest at the rate of six per cent. per annum.
Kanam-tenants are liable to pay all Government and local taxes in respect of the land comprised in their holding.

No summary suit or claim for jennikaram shall be entertained unless the jennikaram or michavaram and renewal fees are specified in the kanam document or its counterpart or a court decree.
Jennikaram may be deposited by the Kanam-tenant with the Tahsildar.
Suits against the Government concerning jennikaram collection are subject to specific conditions.
The Kanam Tenancy Act, 1955 repeals previous legislation.

Explanation I: Kanam transactions executed before the Act are subject to specific provisions regarding renewal fees.

title: THE KANAM TENANCY ABOLITION ACT, 1976
purpose: An Act to provide for the abolition of the intermediary rights of jenmies in lands held by kanam tenants in the Cochin area of the State.
scope: Applies to the whole of the Cochin area of the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Cochin area: The area comprising— (i) the portion of the State of Kerala which before the 1st day of July, 1949, formed the State of Cochin excluding the enclaves absorbed in the Malabar district under the Provinces and States (Absorption of Enclaves) Order, 1950 : and (ii) the enclaves which formed part of the Malabar district absorbed in the State of Travancore-Cochin under the said Order.
key_definitions.cultivating tenant: The holder of a kudiyiruppu and "wakf" shall have the meanings respectively assigned to them in the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 (1 of 1964).
key_definitions.holding: The right, title and interest of such person have vested under the provisions of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 (1 of 1964).
key_definitions.kanam tenant: Means a person who holds land on kanam tenure and includes— (i) the heir, assignee or legal representative of such person ; or (ii) a cultivating tenant or holder of a kudiyiruppu in whom the right, title and interest of such person have vested under the provisions of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 (1 of 1964).
key_definitions.institution of a public nature: Shall include a public trust and a wakf.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Settlement Officer: Means the Settlement Officer appointed under section 23.

main_sections.description: States the short title as the Kanam Tenancy Abolition Act, 1976. Specifies that it extends to the whole of the Cochin area of the State of Kerala. States that it is deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of January, 1970.

Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Cochin area', 'cultivating tenant', 'holding', 'kanam tenant', 'institution of a public nature', 'prescribed', and 'Settlement Officer'.

States that notwithstanding anything in any law or contract, the jenmi shall not have the right to receive payment of jenmikaram and the kanam tenant shall have no liability to pay jenmikaram to the jenmi, and the right to receive payment of, and the liability to pay, jenmikaram shall stand extinguished.

main_sections.section_title: Amount payable for extinguishment of right to receive jenmikaram.
main_sections.description: Specifies the amount payable by the Government to every jenmi for the extinguishment of their right to receive jenmikaram, which is an amount equal to eight and one-third times the aggregate of the annual amount of jenmikaram payable to him immediately before the appointed day, after deducting a sum equal to five per centum of the said aggregate on account of collection charges. Also details how this amount is to be paid (in cash or in Government bonds) and when it becomes due.

main_sections.section_title: Mode of payment of amount due under section 4(1).
main_sections.description: Details the mode of payment of the amount due under section 4(1), which may be paid either in cash or in Government bonds carrying interest at the rate of four and a half per centum per annum, redeemable at the expiration of six years from the date of issue of the bonds, or partly in cash and partly in such bonds, as may be prescribed.

Deals with interim payments where there is delay in the assessment or payment of the amount payable under section 4(1) or the annuity payable under sub-section (3) of that section. The Government may direct direct payment of such amount as may be prescribed, by way of interim relief. Provides for the case where the amount payable has not been determined in accordance with the provisions of this Act before the expiry of one year from the date of publication of the Kanam Tenancy Abolition Ordinance, 1975, in the Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Proceedings relating to assessment and payment of amounts to lie before the Settlement Officer.
main_sections.description: States that all proceedings relating to assessment of the amount payable under sub-section (1) of section 4 or the annuity payable under sub-section (3) of that section and to the payment of the same to the persons entitled thereto shall lie before the Settlement Officer within whose jurisdiction the holding is situate.

main_sections.section_title: Jenmikaram register presumed to describe correctly the right, title and interest of the jenmi and kanam tenant.
main_sections.description: States that every entry in the Register of Jenmikaram prepared under the Kanam Tenancy Act, 1955, and which is valid and effective immediately before the appointed day, shall, for the purpose of assessment and payment of the amount or annuity under section 4, be deemed to describe correctly the right, title and interest of every jenmi and kanam tenant in respect of the holding or part thereof to which it relates. Also provides for modifications or corrections to the register.

main_sections.section_title: Rolls to be prepared by the Settlement Officer.
main_sections.description: Mandates the Settlement Officer to prepare, in the manner prescribed, a draft roll of every jenmi in respect of the holding or part thereof, showing (a) the jenmikaram in respect of the holding or part thereof; (b) the names of persons entitled to receive the jenmikaram; (c) the kanam tenants liable to pay the jenmikaram in respect of the holding or part thereof; (d) the amount or annuity, as the case may be, payable under this Act, and (e) such other particulars as may be prescribed.

Details the procedure for publication of the draft roll, including publishing a notice, serving or causing to be served on the jenmi and kanam tenant concerned, and calling upon all persons interested, including members of the family of the jenmi, claiming any portion of the amount payable under sub-section (1) of section 4, whether by way of a share or by way of maintenance or otherwise to appear and file objections and claims. Also outlines the process for hearing objections and claims.

main_sections.section_title: Orders of Settlement Officer to be deemed to be decrees of civil court.
main_sections.description: States that the order of the Settlement Officer in deciding an objection or claim under section 10 or apportioning the amount payable under sub-section (1) of section 4 among the persons entitled thereto shall be deemed to be a decree of a civil court and shall contain a concise statement of the case, the points for determination, the decision thereon and the reasons for such decision.

important_rules: Jenmikaram is abolished. Jenmis are not entitled to receive it, and kanam tenants are not liable to pay it.
The Government shall pay compensation to every jenmi for the extinguishment of their right to receive jenmikaram.
The compensation amount is calculated based on a multiple of the annual jenmikaram amount, after a deduction for collection charges.
The compensation amount is to be paid in cash or Government bonds.
Proceedings related to the assessment and payment of jenmikaram amounts must be conducted before the Settlement Officer.
Entries in the Jenmikaram register prior to the appointed day are presumed to be correct regarding the rights and interests of jenmis and kanam tenants.

rights: Jenmis have a right to receive compensation from the Government for the abolition of their jenmikaram.
Kanam tenants have the right to have their liability to pay jenmikaram extinguished.
duties: The Government has a duty to pay compensation to jenmis.
The Settlement Officer has a duty to prepare draft rolls and conduct proceedings for assessment and payment.
Transferors and transferees have an obligation to give notice of transfer (as per section 20, though content not extracted).
obligations: Kanam tenants are liable to pay compensation under certain circumstances (e.g., division of holding, as per section 21, though content not extracted).

key_procedures: Assessment and payment of jenmikaram extinguishment compensation: This involves proceedings before the Settlement Officer.
Preparation and publication of jenmikaram rolls: The Settlement Officer prepares draft rolls, which are then published for objections.
Hearing of objections and claims: The Settlement Officer hears and decides any objections or claims filed concerning the draft rolls.
Issuance of orders by Settlement Officer: Orders of the Settlement Officer in these matters are deemed to be decrees of a civil court.
administration: Settlement Officers are appointed and are central to the administration of this Act, particularly in assessing and managing compensation and rolls. The Government is responsible for making compensation payments.
important_notes: The Act commenced on the 1st day of January, 1970.
The Act specifically applies to the Cochin area of the State of Kerala.
The Act received the assent of the President on the 25th day of March, 1976, and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 193, dated 25th March 1976.

title: The Kannan Devan Hills (Resumption of Lands) Act, 1971
purpose: An Act to provide for the resumption of lands other than plantations in the Kannan Devan Hills village in the Devicolam taluk of the Kottayam district and for the distribution of such lands for cultivation and purposes ancillary thereto.
scope: Applies to lands comprising the revenue village of Kannan Devan Hills in the Devicolam taluk of the Kottayam district, excluding plantations.

key_definitions.building: Shall not include a temporary shed
key_definitions.Collector: Means the District Collector Kottayam, or any other officer not below the rank of a District Collector appointed by the Government, by notification in the Gazette, to exercise the powers and perform the functions of the Collector under this Act
key_definitions.Land Board: Means the Land Board constituted under section 100 of the Kerala Land Reform Act, 1963 (1 of 1964)
key_definitions.lessee: Means a person in possession of any land situate in the Kannan Devan Hills village in the Devicolam taluk of the Kottayam district, who has derived the right to such possession by means of a document executed by late Mr. John Daniel Munroe of London and Peermade on the 11th day of July, 1877, for coffee cultivation, or any person claiming through him or any person claiming under or through any of the successors-in-interest of the said Mr. John Daniel Munroe
key_definitions.plantation: Means any land used by a person principally for the cultivation of tea, coffee, cocoa, rubber, cardamom or cinnamon (hereinafter referred to as 'plantation crops')
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act

main_sections.description: States the short title as The Kannan Devan Hills (Resumption of Lands) Act, 1971, that it came into force on January 21, 1971, and applies to lands comprising the revenue village of Kannan Devan Hills in the Devicolam taluk of the Kottayam district.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'building', 'Collector', 'Land Board', 'lessee', 'plantation', and 'prescribed'.

main_sections.section_title: Vesting of possession of certain lands
main_sections.description: States that notwithstanding any contract or document, possession of certain lands shall be transferred to and vested in the Government free from encumbrances. It also specifies exceptions for trespassers and certain buildings and play-grounds. It also covers personal cultivation and lands where the lessee has not exercised rights.

main_sections.section_title: Restoration of possession of lands in certain cases
main_sections.description: Details the circumstances under which possession of resumed lands can be restored, including for purposes ancillary to cultivation, for the preparation of the same for the market, or for the preservation of an existing plantation. It outlines the procedure for application and inquiry by the Land Board.
Covers temporary arrangements for the restoration of possession of land under section 4.
Details the process for the Collector to demarcate the boundaries of resumed lands and publish notifications.
Outlines the procedure for the Land Board to decide disputes regarding the vesting of lands.

main_sections.section_title: No compensation to be payable for vesting
main_sections.description: States that no compensation shall be payable for the extinguishment of rights under section 3.
Describes how the Government shall assign possession of lands vested in the Government to agriculturists and agricultural labourers.

main_sections.section_title: Eviction of persons in occupation on the appointed day
main_sections.description: Empowers the Collector or any officer authorised by him to summarily evict any person in occupation of land vested in the Government.
Prohibits trespass on resumed lands and outlines penalties for contravention.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of Land Board and Collector
main_sections.description: Confers powers on the Land Board and the Collector to exercise powers conferred by the Act, including summoning persons, requiring production of documents, receiving affidavits, and issuing commissions.
Specifies the rights of the Government or any officer to use private way in any land, and the rights of any member of the public to use private way in lands not vested in the Government.
Provides indemnity to the Government and the Land Board for acts done in good faith.
States that no Court shall take cognizance of offences except on a complaint by the Collector or an officer authorised by the Government.
States that the Act does not affect any rights of mortgagees or holders of encumbrances.
Empowers the Government to make such orders as may be necessary to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Repeals certain previous enactments and provides for savings.

important_rules: Possession of certain lands (other than plantations) vests in the Government from the appointed day.
No compensation is payable for the vesting of lands.
The Collector has the power to summarily evict persons in occupation of vested lands.
Trespassing on resumed lands after the appointed day is prohibited.
The Government can make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both (for contravening provisions related to private way or trespass).
Confiscation of building, shed or other structures put up on land that is trespassed upon.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Collector or any officer authorised by him, and the Land Board.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Eviction, demarcation of boundaries, decision of disputes, prosecution for trespass.

rights: Right of the Government to resume possession of lands.
Right to use private way in Government-vested lands (for Government), and in non-vested lands (for public).
Right of persons to apply for restoration of resumed lands under certain conditions.
Rights of mortgagees and holders of encumbrances are saved (section 16).
duties: Duty of the Government to distribute resumed lands for cultivation.
Duty of the Collector to demarcate boundaries and publish notifications.
Duty of the Land Board to decide disputes regarding vesting.
obligations: Obligation not to trespass on resumed lands after the appointed day.
Obligation to comply with any orders made by the Government to remove difficulties.

key_procedures: Procedure for vesting of possession of lands by the Government (Section 3).
Procedure for restoration of possession of lands by the Land Board upon application (Section 4).
Procedure for demarcation of boundaries of resumed lands by the Collector (Section 6).
Procedure for the decision of disputes regarding vesting by the Land Board (Section 7).
Procedure for eviction of persons in occupation of vested lands by the Collector (Section 10).
administration: The Government of Kerala and the Land Board.
important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary, No. 219, dated 22nd April, 1971.
The Act aims to provide for resumption of lands other than plantations.
No compensation is payable for the vesting of lands.
The Act provides for the distribution of resumed lands for cultivation.
Powers are conferred on the Collector and the Land Board for the implementation of the Act.

title: The Kannur University (Amendment) Act, 1998
purpose: To amend The Kannur University Act, 1996.
scope: This Act applies to The Kannur University and its jurisdiction.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title as 'The Kannur University (Amendment) Act, 1998' and states that it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 29th day of September, 1998.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 96 of Act 22 of 1996
main_sections.description: Amends Section 96 of the Kannur University Act, 1996, concerning the constitution of the Senate. It clarifies that the Senate shall consist of the Pro-Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, and members of the Executive Council and Academic Council who are ex-officio members.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 1 of Act 22 of 1996
main_sections.description: Amends Section 1 of the Kannur University Act, 1996. It clarifies that the University shall be known as the 'Kannur University' and will have its headquarters at Kannur. It also states that the University shall have jurisdiction over the districts of Kannur, Kasaragod, Wayanad, and Kozhikode.

important_rules: The Kannur University (Amendment) Act, 1998, is deemed to have come into force on September 29, 1998.
The amendment to Section 96 of Act 22 of 1996 clarifies the ex-officio members of the Senate.
The amendment to Section 1 of Act 22 of 1996 confirms the name and jurisdiction of the Kannur University.
important_notes: The Act references 'The Kannur University Act, 1996 (Act 22 of 1996)' as the principal Act being amended.
The amendments are presented as insertions and substitutions within the original Act.

title: THE KANNUR UNIVERSITY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1998
purpose: An Act to amend the Kannur University Act, 1996.
scope: The Act applies to the Kannur University and any other provisions of this Act or in the Calicut University Act, 1975. It also affects pre-degree courses in colleges within the areas referred to in sub-section (1) of section 96. It provides for instruction of students of such courses in accordance with the course of study in the Calicut University.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kannur University (Amendment) Act, 1998. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 9th day of November, 1995.

A new section 96A is inserted into the Kannur University Act, 1996, the following section shall be inserted, namely:— '96A. Pre-degree course to continue to be affiliated to the Calicut University.—Notwithstanding anything contained in any other provisions of this Act or in the Calicut University Act, 1975 (5 of 1975), Pre-degree courses in the colleges within the areas referred to in sub-section (1) of section 96 shall continue to be affiliated to the Calicut University and the University constituted under this Act shall provide for instruction of students of such courses in accordance with the course of study in the Calicut University and comply with such directions as may be given to it by the Calicut University in respect of that course of study.'

The Kannur University (Amendment) Ordinance, 1998 (1 of 1998), is hereby repealed. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the Kannur University Act, 1996 (22 of 1996), as amended by the said Ordinance, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the said Act, as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Pre-degree courses affiliated to Calicut University shall continue to be so affiliated.
The Kannur University shall provide for instruction of students in these courses according to the Calicut University's course of study and comply with Calicut University's directions.
Anything done or actions taken under the Kannur University Act, 1996 (as amended by the Ordinance) are deemed to have been done or taken under the said Act as amended by this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Kannur University and the Calicut University
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Compliance with directions and provision of instruction as per the course of study.

rights: Students have the right to instruction in pre-degree courses according to the course of study in the Calicut University.
duties: The Kannur University has a duty to provide for instruction of students in pre-degree courses.
obligations: The Kannur University must comply with directions given by the Calicut University regarding pre-degree courses.

administration: Kannur University
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 23rd day of April, 1998 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 638 dated 24th April, 1998.
The Kannur University (Amendment) Ordinance, 1998 is repealed.

title: The Kannur University (Amendment) Act, 2001
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kannur University Act, 1996.
scope: Applies to the Kannur University Act, 1996. Specific amendments relate to various sections of the principal Act concerning the Senate, Syndicate, their powers, composition, and procedures.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kannur University (Amendment) Act, 2001, and that sections 2 and 17 shall come into force with effect from the 28th day of August, 2001, and the remaining provisions shall come into force at once.

Amends section 2 of the Kannur University Act, 1996, by inserting a definition for 'Un-aided college' which means a private college not entitled to financial assistance from the Government or the University.
Amends section 19 of the principal Act, by modifying clauses relating to 'Ex-officio Members' of the Syndicate.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 21
main_sections.description: Substitutes section 21 of the principal Act with new provisions detailing the 'Powers and functions of the Senate' which include reviewing policies, suggesting improvements, considering annual reports, and advising the Chancellor.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 23
main_sections.description: Substitutes section 23 of the principal Act, detailing the composition of the Syndicate, including 'Ex-officio members' and 'Other members'.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 24
main_sections.description: Substitutes section 24 of the principal Act concerning the term of office for members of the Syndicate. It specifies conditions for holding office and eligibility for re-election.

Amends section 25 of the principal Act, substituting words and clauses related to 'Statutes and Ordinances' and introducing new clauses for determining degrees, diplomas, academic distinctions, canceling or amending Regulations, and preparing the budget.
Amends section 37 of the principal Act by omitting the word 'Syndicate' in clause (c).

Amends section 38 of the principal Act. It substitutes 'Senate' with 'Syndicate' in sub-section (1) and modifies the existing proviso. It also makes changes in sub-sections (2) and (3) regarding 'Senate' and 'Syndicate'.
Amends section 40 of the principal Act by omitting sub-section (4) and sub-section (5).

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 42
main_sections.description: Substitutes section 42 of the principal Act with new provisions regarding 'Procedure for making Regulations'. It clarifies that Regulations under this Act shall have effect from their date of being laid before the Syndicate, unless otherwise provided. It also specifies conditions for the lapse or revival of Regulations.
Amends section 43 of the principal Act by adding a proviso to sub-section (1) regarding the submission of Rules, Bye-laws or Orders to the Senate. It also omits sub-section (3).

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the heading in Chapter VI
main_sections.description: Amends the heading in Chapter VI of the principal Act by omitting the words 'THE SYNDICATE'.
Amends section 45 of the principal Act by omitting the words 'the Syndicate' occurring in the marginal heading and the section.
Amends section 47 of the principal Act by substituting 'Senate' with 'Vice-Chancellor' in sub-section (2), and modifying sub-sections relating to the recommendation of the Syndicate.
Amends section 51 of the principal Act by substituting 'Senate' with 'Chancellor' in sub-section (1) and substituting sub-section (2) regarding the Chancellor's approval of financial estimates.

Substitutes section 97 of the principal Act with new 'Special provisions in respect of un-aided colleges'. This section covers scales of pay, conditions of service, admission and selection of students, and fees payable. It also outlines the recommendations of a Committee constituted by the Government for these matters.

main_sections.section_title: Dissolution of the Senate and Syndicate
main_sections.description: This section pertains to the dissolution of the Senate and Syndicate, and matters Pertaining to the act. (This appears to be a title for a section not fully elaborated in the provided snippets).
This section likely deals with the repeal of existing provisions and savings clauses related to the Act. (This appears to be a title for a section not fully elaborated in the provided snippets).

key_procedures: Procedure for making Regulations: All Regulations shall take effect from the date they are laid before the Syndicate, unless otherwise specified.

Conditions for lapse or revival of Regulations: If a Regulation is not laid before the Syndicate as required, it shall lapse. If a laid Regulation is repealed by the Syndicate, the repeal shall revive from the next meeting of the Syndicate.
administration: Kannur University
important_notes: Sections 2 and 17 of the Act came into force on August 28, 2001.
The Act refers to the Kannur University Act, 1996 as the principal Act.
Specific amendments are made to sections concerning 'Ex-officio Members' of the Syndicate, including the Secretary to Government, Education Department.
The Act clarifies the powers and functions of the Senate.
Provisions are made for the composition of the Syndicate, including 'Other members' nominated by the Government.
The Act defines 'Un-aided college' as a private college not receiving financial aid from the Government or University.
The Act specifies that no Regulation can be cancelled or amended without the approval of the Academic Council.
The Act outlines the process for appointing committees and delegating functions.
The Act provides for recommendations from a Committee constituted by the Government regarding un-aided colleges.

title: The Kerala Co-operative Land Mortgage Banks (Amendment) Act, 1983
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Co-operative Land Mortgage Banks Act, 1960, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Co-operative Land Mortgage Banks Act, 1960.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Co-operative Land Mortgage Banks (Amendment) Act, 1983, and shall come into force at once.

Inserts a new section 4B into the Kerala Co-operative Land Mortgage Banks Act, 1960, which deals with 'Issue of debentures by Board to other bodies approved by Government'. This section outlines conditions under which the Government may permit the Board to issue debentures, including restrictions on terms and conditions for repayment.
Amends section 7 of the principal Act by adding the words, figure and letter 'section 4 A' or 'section 4B' after 'section 4'.

important_rules: Debentures issued under subsection (1) of the new section 4B may contain a term fixing a period not exceeding twenty years from the date of issue, during which they shall be irredeemable, or reserving to the Board the right to call for redemption at any time, if the debentures in advance of the date fixed for redemption after giving to the debenture-holder concerned not less than three months' notice in writing.
key_procedures: Insertion of new section 4B to allow the Board to issue debentures to other bodies approved by the Government, subject to specific conditions.
Amendment of section 7 to include references to the newly inserted section 4B.
administration: The Kerala Co-operative Land Mortgage Banks.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 22nd day of April, 1983, and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 458 dated the 25th April, 1983.

title: THE KERALA AGRARIAN RELATIONS (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 1962 (Act 26 of 1962)
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Agrarian Relations Act, 1960, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to agrarian relations in Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Agrarian Relations (Second Amendment) Act, 1962.

Amends section 2 of the Kerala Agrarian Relations Act, 1960 (Act 26 of 1961), hereafter referred to as the principal Act, sub-clause (i) of clause (50), after item (i), the following item shall be inserted, namely: -- "(ii) a mortgagee who is referred to in section 4-A or section 4-B; ".

Inserts new sections 4-A and 4-B after section 4 of the principal Act. Section 4-A deals with certain mortgages with possession to be deemed tenants, and section 4-B deals with the interest on the mortgage amount and the option of the mortgagor to treat the mortgage as security for rent.

The Kerala Agrarian Relations (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1962 (Ordinance No. 6 of 1962), is hereby repealed. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act, as if this Act had commenced on the 6th day of September, 1962.

important_rules: A mortgagee with possession of immovable property in Cochin shall be deemed to be a tenant for the purposes of this Act, if the property comprised in the mortgage consists of agricultural land.
The interest on the mortgage amount is less than forty per cent of the total rent fixed in the mortgage document and there is a stipulation for the payment of customary dues.

The mortgagor shall return the mortgage money or the portion thereof, which he does not elect to treat as security for rent to the tenant within six months from the commencement of the Kerala Agrarian Relations (Second Amendment) Act, 1962.

Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in any law or contract, or in any judgment, decree or order of Court, a mortgage with possession of immovable property situate in Cochin shall be deemed to be a tenant for the purposes of this Act, if -- (a) the property comprised in the mortgage consists of agricultural land; and (b) he was by himself or through any member of his family or tarwad holding the property comprised in the mortgage as a verumpattamdar on, or after the first day of Chingam, 1111.

rights: Right of a mortgagee with possession to be deemed a tenant under certain conditions.
Option of the mortgagor to treat the mortgage money or any portion thereof as security for rent.
duties: Duty of the mortgagor to return mortgage money or portion thereof within six months if not elected as security for rent.

key_procedures: Insertion of new sections 4-A and 4-B into the principal Act to define mortgagees with possession as tenants and to regulate the treatment of mortgage amounts as security for rent.
Repeal of the Kerala Agrarian Relations (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1962, with a saving clause that actions taken under the Ordinance are valid under this Act.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 6th day of November, 1962 and published in the Gazette Extraordinary, dated the 7th November 1962.

The verumpattamdar was terminated after the first day of Chingam, 1111 and before the commencement of the Kerala Agrarian Relations (Second Amendment) Act, 1961, but is continued in possession of the property, without interruption, by himself or through any member of his family or tarwad, as a mortgagee with possession from the date of such termination, till the commencement of the Kerala Agrarian Relations (Second Amendment) Act, 1962.
The saving clause in section 4 ensures that any actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are legally recognized under this new Act.

title: THE KERALA AGRICULTURAL UNIVERSITY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1986
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala Agricultural University Act, 1971.
scope: The Act applies to the Kerala Agricultural University and its provisions.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Agricultural University (Amendment) Act, 1986, and that it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 6th day of August, 1984.

This section amends section 42 of the Kerala Agricultural University Act, 1971. It revises the normal retirement age for Deans of Faculties, Director of Research, Director of Extension, Director of Veterinary Research and Education, and Director of Post Graduate Studies to sixty years. It also specifies the normal retirement age for Officers of the University other than the Chancellor, Pro-Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor and Pro-Chancellor to be fifty-five years.

This section repeals the Kerala Agricultural University (Amendment) Ordinance, 1986. It also includes a saving clause stating that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or taken or any action deemed to have been taken or deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

administration: Kerala Agricultural University
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 30th day of November, 1986 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 1075 dated 30th November, 1986.

title: The Kerala Co-Operative Societies (Amendment) Act, 1986
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969, and its amendments.

key_definitions.primary credit society: means a society other than an apex or central society which has as its principal object the raising of funds to be lent to its members.
key_definitions.Scheduled Castes: means the Scheduled Castes in relation to the State of Kerala as specified in the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950.
key_definitions.Scheduled Tribes: means the Scheduled Tribes in relation to the State of Kerala as specified in the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Act, 1986, and specifies the dates for commencement of its various sections.
Amends section 2 of the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969, by inserting new clauses related to 'primary credit society', 'Scheduled Castes', and 'Scheduled Tribes'.

Inserts a new section 28A which provides for reservation for women members and members belonging to Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes in committees, with provisions to prevent the exclusion of women or Scheduled Castes/Tribes from committees.

Amends section 69 of the principal Act by adding an Explanation. The term "Registrar" means the Registrar of Co-operative Societies appointed under section 3 of the principal Act, and includes any person on whom the powers of the Registrar under this section and section 70 are conferred.

Amends section 70 of the principal Act by adding a proviso stating that provided a transfer under clause (b) or a reference under clause (c) shall not be made to a person equal or superior to him in rank.

Amends section 80 of the principal Act by adding a sub-section stating that notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1) or sub-section (2), ten per cent of the posts of employees of every society shall be reserved for appointment from persons belonging to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes where the method of appointment to such posts is by direct recruitment.
Amends section 88 of the principal Act by substituting the words "three years", the words "five years" shall be substituted.
Amends section 89 of the principal Act by substituting the words "three years", the words "five years" shall be substituted.

Validates anything contained in any law for the time being in force, or in any judgment, decree, order of any court or other authority, any transfer or reference of a dispute under clause (b) or clause (c), as the case may be, of sub-section (1) of section 70 of the principal Act, made before the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette by any person on whom the powers of the Registrar under sections 69 and 70 of the said Act have been conferred shall be, and shall be deemed always to have been valid and in accordance with law, and accordingly, any decision or award passed by any person in pursuance of any such transfer or reference, as the case may be, shall not be deemed to be invalid or ever to have been invalid merely on the ground that such transfer or reference was made by any person other than the Registrar appointed under sub-section (1) of section 3 of the principal Act and any such decision or award shall not be called in question in any court on the said ground.

Repeals the Kerala Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Ordinance, 1986 (55 of 1986) and the Kerala Co-operative Societies (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1986 (59 of 1986), and saves anything done or taken action or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinances.

important_rules: Reservation for women members and members belonging to Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes in committees, with specific provisions for their inclusion.
Any transfer under clause (b) or reference under clause (c) of section 70 of the principal Act shall not be made to a person equal or superior to him in rank.
Ten percent of employee posts in every society are to be reserved for appointment from Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes where direct recruitment is the method of appointment.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Registrar of Co-operative Societies (as defined in section 69)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the Registrar and the legal framework of the Co-operative Societies Act.

rights: Right to have reservation in committees for women, Scheduled Castes, and Scheduled Tribes.
Right to valid decisions and awards made under specific provisions of the Act.
duties: Duty to comply with the provisions of the amended Act.
Duty of the Registrar and appointed authorities to act within their conferred powers.
obligations: Obligation to reserve 10% of employee posts for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes where direct recruitment is applicable.

key_procedures: Procedure for commencement of the Act's sections on specified dates.
Procedure for insertion of new clauses and sections into the principal Act.
Procedure for appointment of employees from Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Procedure for validation of past actions and decisions made under the Act.
administration: Co-operative Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act has retrospective effect for certain provisions as indicated by the commencement dates.
The term 'Registrar' can include persons to whom powers are delegated.
The validation section ensures the legality of past actions taken under specific circumstances.
Repeal and saving clause addresses the transition from ordinances to the Act.

title: THE KERALA CO-OPERATIVE SOCIETIES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1995
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969.
scope: The Act applies to the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969, and its amendments.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Act, 1995, and it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 25th day of April, 1995.

This section describes the amendments made to section 80 of the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969, specifically regarding sub-sections (3) and (3B) concerning recruitment rules and appointments.
This section states that the following Schedule shall be inserted at the end of the principal Act.
This section repeals the Kerala Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Ordinance, 1995 (10 of 1995) and saves anything done or any action taken under the principal Act, as amended by the said Ordinance.

important_rules: Rule: Notwithstanding anything contained in the principal Act or the rules made or orders issued thereunder or in the bye-laws of any society relating to the recruitment and conditions of service of officers and servants of societies, all appointments of officers and servants of the societies mentioned in the Schedule shall be made from a select list of candidates furnished by the Kerala Public Service Commission.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Kerala Public Service Commission (for appointment of officers and servants of societies in the Schedule)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the amended provisions of the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969.

key_procedures: Procedure: All appointments to the societies listed in the inserted Schedule are to be made by direct recruitment from a select list of candidates furnished by the Kerala Public Service Commission.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be under the purview of the Kerala Government concerning Co-operative Societies.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on April 25, 1995.
Sub-section (3) of Section 80 is amended to include the conditions regarding recruitment and service of officers and servants.

Sub-section (3B) states that all appointments made by direct recruitment to societies in the Schedule after April 25, 1995, and before the date of publication of this Act, shall be invalid unless made from a select list provided by the Kerala Public Service Commission.
The Schedule lists various Co-operative Societies and Federations in Kerala.

title: The Kerala Contingency Fund (Amendment) Act, 1963

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Contingency Fund (Amendment) Act, 1963.

In sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Kerala Contingency Fund Act, 1957 (Act 6 of 1957), the words 'a sum of fifty lakhs of rupees' shall be substituted by the words 'a sum of one hundred and fifty lakhs of rupees'.

important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on 9th January 1963.

title: The Kerala Contingency Fund (Amendment) Act, 2005
purpose: This act amends The Kerala Contingency Fund Act, 1957 to clarify certain provisions related to the Contingency Fund.
scope: Applies to the Contingency Fund of the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This section likely states the short title of the Act as 'The Kerala Contingency Fund (Amendment) Act, 2005' and specifies its commencement date. It also refers to the principal Act of 1957.
This section details the amendments made to the Kerala Contingency Fund Act, 1957. It specifically amends section 6 of the principal Act concerning the Contingency Fund.

This section introduces a new section into the principal Act of 1957. The new section clarifies that the Contingency Fund, as per section 6 of the principal Act and amended by this Act, shall be applied and expended for such purposes as the Government may deem necessary to meet unforeseen expenditure. It also states that the amount expended shall be repaid into the Fund from the Consolidated Fund of the State.

important_rules: The Contingency Fund of the State shall be applied and expended for such purposes as the Government may deem necessary to meet unforeseen expenditure.
Any amount expended from the Contingency Fund shall be repaid into the Fund from the Consolidated Fund of the State.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through financial management and appropriation from the Consolidated Fund of the State.

duties: The Government has the duty to manage the Contingency Fund for unforeseen expenditures.
The Government has the duty to ensure that any amount expended from the Fund is repaid into it.

key_procedures: When unforeseen expenditure is required, the Government may utilize the Contingency Fund.
After expenditure from the Contingency Fund, the amount must be reimbursed from the Consolidated Fund of the State.
administration: The Finance Department, Government of Kerala (inferred)
important_notes: The amendment clarifies the purpose and usage of the Contingency Fund for unforeseen expenditures.
The fund is replenished from the Consolidated Fund of the State.

title: THE KERALA CONTINGENCY FUND (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1994
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala Contingency Fund Act, 1957. WHEREAS it is expedient further to amend the Kerala Contingency Fund Act, 1957, for the purpose hereinafter appearing; BE IT enacted in the Forty-fifth Year of the Republic of India as follows:
scope: Applies to the Kerala Contingency Fund Act, 1957.

title: THE KERALA CRIMINAL LAW AMENDMENT ACT, 1962
purpose: To amend the Indian Penal Code and the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, and in their application to the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.public servant: For the purposes of sections 162, 163, 164, 165 and 165A of the Indian Penal Code, the words 'public servant' shall denote persons who are public servants within the meaning of section 21 or who are deemed to be 'public servants' within the meaning of that section under any law for the time being in force, persons falling under any of the descriptions hereinafter following, namely: (i) Every officer in the service or pay of the Travancore Devaswom Board or the Cochin Devaswom Board; (ii) Every officer in the service or pay and every member of the Wakf's Board constituted under the Wakf's Act, 1954 (Central Act 29 of 1954); (iii) A President and every member of a Village Court or Village Panchayat Court; (iv) Every member of the Board of Directors or of the executive or managing committee and every officer or servant of a co-operative society registered or deemed to be registered under the law relating to co-operative societies for the time being in force; (v) Every member of the governing body and every officer or servant in the service or pay of a society registered under the Travancore-Cochin Literary, Scientific and Charitable Societies Registration Act, 1955 or the Societies Registration Act, 1860, and receiving aid or grant from the Government; (vi) Every teacher or other officer or servant of the University of Kerala; (vii) Every examiner of a University Examination or a Government Examination; (viii) Every Manager, or teacher or servant of an educational institution which receives or has received aid or grant from the Government or the University of Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1962, it extends to the whole of the State of Kerala, and it shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 161, Central Act 45 of 1860
main_sections.description: Amends section 161 of the Indian Penal Code (Central Act 45 of 1860) by inserting a clause that the words, figures and letter 'public servant' shall denote persons who are public servants within the meaning of section 21 or who are deemed to be 'public servants' within the meaning of that section under any law for the time being in force, persons falling under any of the descriptions hereinafter following, namely: (i) to (viii) as detailed in key_definitions.

Amends the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 (Central Act 2 of 1947). In section 2, the following section shall be substituted, namely: '2. Interpretation.—For the purposes of this Act, “public servant” shall have the meaning assigned to it under the explanation to section 161 of the Indian Penal Code as amended by the Kerala Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1962; (a) in section 2A, for the words, figures and letter “section 161, section 165 or section 165A”, the words, figures and letter “section 161, 162, 163, 164, 165 or 165A” shall be substituted; (b) in sub-section (1) of section 6, after clause (b), the following clause shall be inserted, namely: — “(c) in the case of a person falling under any of the descriptions mentioned in items (i) to (viii) in the explanation to ‘Public servant’ in section 161 of the Indian Penal Code as amended by the Kerala Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1962, save by or with the sanction of the State Government.”'

important_rules: Public servants are defined broadly to include various officials and members of boards and societies, not just government employees.

The definition of 'public servant' is extended to include individuals serving in specific bodies like the Travancore Devaswom Board, Wakf's Board, Village Courts, cooperative societies, educational institutions receiving aid, and universities.
Sanction of the State Government is required for prosecution in certain cases involving public servants as defined by this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings and prosecution, requiring sanction of the State Government for certain offenses.

duties: Public servants have a duty to act within the scope of their authority and the law.
Individuals falling under the expanded definition of 'public servant' are subject to the provisions of the Indian Penal Code and the Prevention of Corruption Act.
obligations: Sanction of the State Government is an obligation for prosecution under certain circumstances.

key_procedures: Bringing the act into force via a notification by the Government.
Prosecution of public servants, which requires sanction from the State Government in specific cases outlined in the act.
administration: The State Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the President on the 25th day of December 1962 and was published in the Gazette Extraordinary, dated the 31st December 1962.
The amendments primarily focus on expanding the definition of 'public servant' to ensure broader application of anti-corruption laws.

title: The Kerala Debtors (Temporary Relief) Act, 1975
purpose: An Act to provide temporary relief to certain debtors in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.agricultural land: Land used for agriculture or horticulture, not being land appurtenant to a residential building.
key_definitions.artisan: A person who does not hold any agricultural land and whose principal means of livelihood is production or repair of traditional tools, implements and other articles or things used for agriculture or purposes ancillary thereto and includes a person who normally earns his livelihood by practising craft either by his own labour or by the labour of the members of his family.
key_definitions.creditor: Shall include the heirs, legal representatives and assigns of the creditor.
key_definitions.debt: Means any liability in cash or kind, whether secured or unsecured, due from or incurred by a debtor on or before the commencement of this Act, whether payable under a contract, or under a decree or order of any court, or otherwise, but does not include- (a) any sum payable to- (i) the Government of Kerala or the Government of India or the Government of any other State or Union territory in India or any local authority, or (ii) the Reserve Bank of India or the State Bank of India or any subsidiary bank within the meaning of clause (k) of section 2 of the State Bank of India (Subsidiary Banks) Act, 1959 or the Travancore Credit Bank (in liquidation) constituted under the Travancore Credit Bank Act, IV of 1113; or (iii) a corporation owned or controlled by the Government of Kerala or the Government of any other State or Union territory in India or the Government of India or a Government company as defined in the Companies Act, 1956, or (iv) the Tea Board constituted under the Tea Act, 1953, or the Coffee Board constituted under the Coffee Act, 1942, or the Rubber Board constituted under the Rubber Act, 1947, or the Cardamom Board constituted under the Cardamom Act, 1965; or (v) any co-operative society, including a Land Mortgage Bank, registered or deemed to be registered under the Co-operative Societies Act for the time being in force, or (b) any sum payable to any corresponding new bank specified in column (2) of the First Schedule to the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1970; or (c) any liability arising out of a breach of trust or any tortious liability, or (d) any liability in respect of maintenance, whether under a decree or court or otherwise; or (e) any liability in respect of wages or remuneration due as salary or otherwise for services rendered; or (f) any debt which represents the price of goods purchased for the purpose of trade, or (g) any liability for which a charge is provided under sub-clause (b) of clause (4) of section 55 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, or (h) any rent payable in respect of any building; or (i) any rent or michavaram payable in respect of any land; or (j) any debt or debts due to a widow at the commencement of this Act, provided that the value of the property owned by her at such commencement, including the principal amount of the debt or debts so due, does not exceed ten thousand rupees. Explanation. For the purposes of this sub-clause, the house in which the widow lives, her wearing apparel or similar personal belongings shall not be regarded as property, or (k) any liability incurred or arising under a chitty or kuri which is registered or licensed under the Travancore Chitties Act, 1120, or the Cochin Kuries Act, VII of 1107, or conducted under any chit fund scheme, and which has not terminated one year before the commencement of this Act: Provided that nothing in this sub-clause shall apply to the liability of a foreman incurred or arising under any such chitty or kuri, where the foreman is a co-operative society registered or deemed to be registered under the Co-operative Societies Act for the time being in force. Explanation. For the purposes of this sub-clause, a chitty or kuri shall be deemed to have terminated- (i) when the period fixed in the variola or vaimbu or kuripattika or the period as altered by a subsequent special resolution for the duration of the chitty or kuri, has expired; or (ii) when the legal representative of a deceased foreman or the guardian of a foreman of unsound mind or the subscriber or the subscribers selected therefor fails or fail to conduct the chitty or kuri or to make suitable arrangements for the further conduct of the chitty or kuri, or (iii) on the failure of the foreman to pay the prize amount to the subscriber within one month from the due date thereof; or (iv) on the failure of the foreman or foramen to conduct the chitty or kuri at any instalment or on any other date before the next instalment as may be agreed upon in writing by a majority of the non-prized subscribers. Provided that if there are more foremen than one and one or more of such foremen are living and is or are not disqualified to conduct the chitty or kuri, the chitty or kuri shall not be deemed to have terminated if there is provision in the variola or vaimbu or kuripattika enabling the remaining foreman or foremen to conduct the chitty or kuri or if the non-prized subscribers agree by a special resolution to conduct of the chitty or kuri by the remaining foreman or foremen ; or (l) any debt exceeding three thousand rupees borrowed under a single transaction and due before the commencement of this Act to any banking company as defined in the Banking Regulation Act, 1949; or (m) any amount due on account of any goods to a financier who financed the purchase of such goods and whose principal business is to finance the purchase of goods, or (n) any sum advanced for the purposes of agriculture by an institution receiving financial assistance from the Agricultural Refinance Corporation established under the Agricultural Refinance Corporation Act, 1963. Explanation 1. For the purposes of this clause, - (i) the liability of a surety who is a debtor shall be deemed to be a debt within the meaning of this Act notwithstanding that the principal debtor is not a debtor for the purposes of this Act. (ii) where a debt has been split up in any manner whatsoever, whether before or after the commencement of this Act, and fresh documents have been executed in respect of different portions of the debt, each such different portion shall be a debt. Explanation II. Where the debt is a liability in kind, the value of the commodity shall be commuted at the market rate prevailing on the date on which the debt was incurred. (5) "debtor" means any person who has an interest, other than as a simple mortgagee, in any agricultural land in the State of Kerala, from whom any debt is due and includes- (a) a landless labourer, (b) an artisan; and (c) a kudikidappukaran but does not include- (i) any person assessed to salestax on a turnover which in the aggregate is not less than twenty thousand rupees in any two years within the three years immediately preceding the commencement of this Act, under the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, or the law of any other State relating to salestax, (ii) any person assessed to income-tax under the Income-tax Act, 1961, in any two years within the three years immediately preceding the commencement of this Act and whose total income for the purposes of the said Act exceeded eight thousand rupees per annum; (iii) any person assessed to agricultural income-tax in any two years within the three years immediately preceding the commencement of this Act, under the Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950, or under any other law relating to agricultural income-tax, on an income exceeding eight thousand rupees per annum. Explanation. Notwithstanding anything contained in the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, where a creditor proves that his debtor is a person assessed to income-tax in sub-clause (i) or sub-clause (ii) or sub-clause (iii) for the period referred to in that sub-clause, the burden of proving that such debtor does not fall under the category specified in that sub-clause shall lie on the debtor. (iv) a firm registered under the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, or a company as defined in the Companies Act, 1956, or a corporation formed in pursuance of an Act of Parliament of the United Kingdom or of any special Indian Law. Explanation. For the purposes of this clause, the term "person" shall include a family, provided that sub-clauses (i) to (iii), in their application to a family consisting of not less than five members, shall have effect as if for the turnover, total income or income specified therein, twice such turnover, total income or income, as the case may be, were substituted: (6) "family" means a Hindu undivided family or a Marumakkathayam tarwad or thavazhi or an Aliyasanthana kudumba or kavaru or a Nambudiri illom; (7) "interest" means any amount or other thing paid or payable in excess of the principal amount borrowed or pecuniary obligation incurred, or where anything has been borrowed in kind in excess of what has been so borrowed, by whatsoever name such amount or thing may be called, and whether the same is paid or payable entirely in cash or entirely in kind or partly in cash and partly in kind and whether the same is expressly mentioned or not in the document or contract, if any, (8) "kudikidappukaran" shall have the same meaning as in clause (25) of section 2 of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963; (9) "landless labourer" means a person who does not hold any agricultural land and whose principal means of livelihood is manual labour; (10) "pay" with its grammatical variations, includes deliver; (11) "principal amount" means the amount originally advanced, together with such sum, if any, as has been subsequently allowed, notwithstanding any stipulation to treat any interest as principal and notwithstanding that the debt has been renewed or included in a fresh document, whether by the same creditor or his heirs, legal representatives or assigns or by any other person acting on his behalf or in his interest, and whether in favour of the same creditor or his heirs, legal representatives or assigns or of any other person acting on his behalf or in his interest.
key_definitions.foreman: Shall have the same meaning as in clause (25) of section 2 of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963.
key_definitions.kudikidappukaran: Shall have the same meaning as in clause (25) of section 2 of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963.
key_definitions.landless labourer: Means a person who does not hold any agricultural land and whose principal means of livelihood is manual labour.
key_definitions.pay: With its grammatical variations, includes deliver.
key_definitions.principal amount: Means the amount originally advanced, together with such sum, if any, as has been subsequently allowed, notwithstanding any stipulation to treat any interest as principal and notwithstanding that the debt has been renewed or included in a fresh document, whether by the same creditor or his heirs, legal representatives or assigns or by any other person acting on his behalf or in his interest, and whether in favour of the same creditor or his heirs, legal representatives or assigns or of any other person acting on his behalf or in his interest.
key_definitions.suit: Shall not include a claim to a set-off made in a suit instituted by a debtor.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Debtors (Temporary Relief) Act, 1975, that it extends to the whole of the State of Kerala, and that it shall come into force at once.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including "agricultural land", "artisan", "creditor", "debt", "debtor", "family", "interest", "kudikidappukaran", "landless labourer", "pay", and "principal amount".

main_sections.section_title: Bar of suits and applications and other proceedings
main_sections.description: No recovery of a debt shall be instituted, no application for execution of a decree in respect of a debt shall be made, and no appeal, revision petition or application for review against any decree or order in any such suit or application shall be presented or made in any civil or revenue court before the expiry of one year from the commencement of this Act or such longer period as may be specified by the Government by notification in the Gazette, and all such suits, applications, appeals and petitions instituted, made or presented before such commencement and pending at such commencement shall stand stayed for the said period.

main_sections.section_title: Presumption as to transfer of immovable property of debtor
main_sections.description: (1) Every transfer of immovable property made by a debtor entitled to the benefits of section 3, made during the period mentioned in that section shall, in any suit or other proceedings with respect to such transfer, be presumed, until the contrary is proved, to have been made with intent to defeat or delay the creditors of the transferor. (2) Where a debtor entitled to the benefits of section 3 has in collusion with another allowed his immovable property to be sold during the period mentioned in that section through court or otherwise, with a view to defeat or delay his creditors, the sale shall be voidable at the option of any creditor so defeated or delayed.

Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, where a debtor entitled to the benefits of section 3, with intent to defeat or delay his creditor or creditors, has made any voluntary transfer of any interest in immovable property during the period mentioned in the said section, such debtor shall not be entitled to the benefits of that section

In computing the period of limitation for a suit for recovery of a debt or an application for the execution of a decree in respect of a debt or an appeal, revision petition or application for review against any decree or order in any such suit or application, the time during which the institution of the suit or the making of the application or the presentation of the appeal or petition was barred under section 3 shall be excluded.

main_sections.section_title: Interest not to accrue in respect of debts
main_sections.description: Interest shall not accrue in respect of debts during the period mentioned in section 3.

main_sections.section_title: Act to override other laws, contracts, etc.
main_sections.description: The provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any other law for the time being in force or in any contract or agreement.
The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make rules to carry out all or any of the purposes of this Act.

important_rules: No recovery of debt shall be instituted during the period specified.
No application for execution of a decree in respect of a debt shall be made during the period specified.
No appeal, revision petition or application for review against any decree or order in any suit or application shall be presented or made during the period specified.
All such suits, applications, appeals and petitions instituted, made or presented before the commencement and pending at such commencement shall stand stayed for the said period.
Transfer of immovable property by a debtor during the specified period is presumed to be with intent to defeat or delay creditors, unless proved otherwise.
Sales of immovable property by a debtor in collusion with another, during the specified period, are voidable at the creditor's option.
Debtors who made voluntary transfers of interest in immovable property with intent to defeat or delay creditors during the specified period are excluded from the benefits of the Act.
Interest shall not accrue in respect of debts during the period mentioned in section 3.

penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the stay of legal proceedings as stipulated in Section 3, and presumptions regarding property transfers as per Section 4.

rights: Debtors entitled to the benefits of section 3 have the right to temporary relief from debt recovery.
Creditors have the right to void sales of debtor's property made in collusion, as per Section 4(2).
duties: Debtors must not attempt to defeat or delay creditors through property transfers during the specified period.

key_procedures: Section 3 outlines the procedure of staying all suits, applications, and proceedings related to debt recovery for a specified period.
Section 4 outlines the procedure for presuming intent to defeat or delay creditors in cases of property transfer by debtors.
Section 6 outlines the procedure for computing the period of limitation by excluding the period during which proceedings were barred by Section 3.

title: THE KERALA FOREST (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1975
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala Forest Act, 1961, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Forest Act, 1961. The amendments pertain to confiscation of timber, charcoal, firewood, ivory, tools, ropes, chains, boats, vehicles and cattle used in committing forest offences.

key_definitions.authorised officer: An officer authorised by the Government for the purpose of the Act, not being below the rank of an Assistant Conservator of Forests.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Forest (Amendment) Act, 1975.

In section 52 of the principal Act, in the Explanation to sub-section (1), for the words and figures "section 53 and section 55", the words, figures and letters "section 53, section 55, section 61A and section 61B", shall be substituted.

After section 61 of the principal Act, the following sections shall be inserted, namely: "61A. Confiscation by Forest Officers in certain cases. (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in the foregoing provisions of this Chapter, where a forest offence is believed to have been committed in respect of timber, charcoal, firewood or ivory which is the property of the Government, the officer seizing the property under sub-section (1) of section 52 shall, without any unreasonable delay, produce it, together with all tools, ropes, chains, boats, vehicles and cattle used in committing such offence, before an officer authorised by the Government in this behalf by notification in the Gazette, not being below the rank of an Assistant Conservator of Forests (hereinafter referred to as the authorised officer). (2) Where an authorised officer seizes under sub-section (1) of section 52 any timber, charcoal, firewood or ivory which is the property of the Government, or where any such property is produced before an authorised officer under sub-section (1) of this section and he is satisfied that a forest offence has been committed in respect of such property, such authorised officer may, whether or not a prosecution is instituted for the commission of such forest offence, order confiscation of the property so seized together with all tools, ropes, chains, boats, vehicles and cattle used in committing such offence."

(1) The Kerala Forest (Amendment) Ordinance, 1975 (5 of 1975) is hereby repealed. (2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act or if this Act had come into force on the 21st day of June, 1975.

important_rules: Rule 61A(1): Where a forest offence is believed to have been committed in respect of timber, charcoal, firewood or ivory which is the property of the Government, the seizing officer shall produce it, along with associated tools, vehicles, and cattle, before an authorised officer.
Rule 61A(2): An authorised officer, satisfied that a forest offence has occurred, may order confiscation of the seized property, tools, vehicles, and cattle, even if no prosecution is instituted.

Rule 61A: No order of confiscating any timber, charcoal, firewood, ivory, tools, ropes, chains, boats, vehicles or cattle shall be made under section 61A unless the person from whom the same is seized is given a reasonable opportunity of being heard.

Rule 61B: Any person aggrieved by an order passed under section 61A or section 61C may, within thirty days from the date of communication of such order, appeal to the District Judge having jurisdiction over the area in which the property to which the order relates has been seized.
Rule 61E: The award of confiscation shall not prevent the infliction of any punishment to which the person affected thereby is liable under this Act.

penalties: Confiscation of property seized (timber, charcoal, firewood, ivory, tools, ropes, chains, boats, vehicles, cattle).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Authorised officers (not below the rank of Assistant Conservator of Forests), and District Judges for appeals.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through orders of confiscation by authorised officers, and appeals to the District Judge.

rights: Right to be given an opportunity of being heard before confiscation.
Right to appeal to the District Judge against a confiscation order.

key_procedures: Procedure for confiscation of forest produce and associated items: When a forest offence is suspected concerning government property (timber, charcoal, firewood, ivory), the seized items and related tools/vehicles/cattle must be produced before an authorised officer. The authorised officer, after being satisfied that an offence has occurred, can order confiscation after providing the concerned person an opportunity to be heard.

Procedure for appeal against confiscation: A person aggrieved by a confiscation order can appeal to the District Judge within 30 days of receiving the order. The District Judge's order on appeal is final.
administration: Forest Department (implied, as it deals with forest offences and conservators).
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 7th day of September, 1975 and published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 328 dated 8th September, 1975.

key_definitions.hotel: Means any premises or part of premises including a house-boat, restaurant, bar or a tent where lodging with or without board or any kind of eatables or beverages is provided for a monetary consideration.
key_definitions.hotel-keeper: Means any person who owns or operates a hotel as proprietor and includes a person managing or operating the affairs of a hotel for and on behalf of 'the proprietor'.
key_definitions.malpractice: Includes dishonesty, cheating, touting, impersonation, obstruction in allowing free choice for shopping or stay or travel arrangements, charging a price higher than that listed under this Act, failure to display price label at the article, failure to give cash memos and wilful failure to execute an order within the stipulated time or according to the terms agreed.
key_definitions.notified article: Means any article notified by the Government in the Gazette, or in any publication prescribed in this behalf for purposes of this Act.
key_definitions.part: Means a part of this Act.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed, by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.prescribed authority: Means the authority notified as such by the Government, provided that, different authorities may be notified for different provisions of this Act.
key_definitions.tourist area: Means any area notified by the Government in the Gazette or any publication prescribed in this behalf, to be a tourist area for purposes of this Act.
key_definitions.tourist: Means a person or group of persons including pilgrims visiting the State from any part of India or outside India and includes a traveller or a group of persons visiting a particular area from any other part of the State.
key_definitions.travel agent: Means a person engaged in the business of making travel, trekking, camping, tour operating, or other travel arrangements for tourists for a monetary consideration and includes a tourist guide, excursion agent, tent and camping agent or cargo agent.
key_definitions.person: Includes a firm, company, corporation and association of persons.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Registration of Tourist Trade Act, 1991. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and comes into force on such date as the Government may by notification in the Gazette appoint.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'black-list', 'certificate of registration', 'dealer', 'hotel', 'hotel-keeper', 'malpractice', 'notified article', 'part', 'prescribed', 'prescribed authority', 'tourist area', 'tourist', 'travel agent', and 'person'.

Requires every person intending to carry on business as a dealer under this Act to apply for registration to the prescribed authority in the prescribed manner. It also specifies that anyone already carrying on such business in a tourist area must apply for registration within three months of the article's notification. Additionally, it states that every application made under sub-section (1) shall be disposed of within three months from the date of receipt of the application, failing which the application is deemed to have been accepted for registration.

States that the prescribed authority shall, unless registration is refused under section 5, direct that the name and particulars of the dealer be entered in the register maintained for the purpose and shall issue a certificate of registration to the dealer in the prescribed form.

Outlines the grounds on which the prescribed authority may refuse registration, including conviction of any offence under Chapters XIV and XVI of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, or under any of the provisions of this Act or any offence punishable under any law providing for the prevention of hoarding, smuggling or profiteering or adulteration of food, violation of foreign exchange regulations or foreign contribution regulations or the possession or sale of any narcotic drugs or psychotropic substances or corruption, and having not been declared an insolvent by a court of competent jurisdiction, or having his name removed from the register under clause (b) or clause (c) of section 6 and six months have not elapsed since the date of removal. It also states that no application for registration shall be refused unless the person applying for registration has been afforded a reasonable opportunity of being heard.

main_sections.section_title: Removal of the name from the register.
main_sections.description: Details the circumstances under which the prescribed authority may, by an order in writing, remove the name of a dealer from the register and cancel his certificate of registration. These include the dealer ceasing to be a dealer, being convicted of any offence, being declared an insolvent, having a complaint of malpractice received and proved against him, or if he is black-listed by the prescribed authority under section 7. It also states that any dealer whose name is removed from the register under this section shall forthwith cease to be a dealer.

Allows the prescribed authority to, on a complaint of malpractice having been proved or for any other offence committed under the Act, after inquiry, order the black-listing of a dealer. Particulars of a dealer black-listed shall be exhibited at conspicuous places in all tourist areas and notified to all travel, trade and other concerned organisations. The action taken under this sub-section shall not protect such dealer from being prosecuted under the provisions of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Notice of removal and black-listing of dealer.
