main_sections.description: Requires the prescribed authority, before removing the name of a dealer from the register under section 6 or black-listing him under section 7, to give notice to the dealer of the grounds on which it is proposed to take action, and hold an inquiry in the presence of the dealer giving him a reasonable opportunity of showing cause against it.

Mandates every person intending to operate a hotel in a tourist area to apply for registration to the prescribed authority. It also stipulates that any person already operating a hotel in a tourist area must apply for registration within three months of the notification. All applications are to be disposed of within three months from the date of receipt, and if not, they are deemed accepted.

States that the prescribed authority shall, unless registration is refused under section 11, direct that the name and particulars of the hotel and hotel-keeper be entered in the register and issue a certificate of registration.

Lists the grounds for refusing hotel registration, including if the hotel-keeper has been convicted of any offence under Chapters XIV and XVI of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, or under any of the provisions of this Act or any offence punishable under any law providing for the prevention of hoarding, smuggling or profiteering or adulteration of food, violation of foreign exchange regulations or foreign contribution regulations or the possession or sale of any narcotic drugs or psychotropic substances or corruption, and two years have not elapsed since the termination of the sentence imposed upon him.

main_sections.section_title: Removal of the name from the register.
main_sections.description: Details the grounds for removing a hotel's name from the register, similar to dealer removal, including cessation of business, conviction of offences, insolvency, complaints of malpractice, or black-listing.
Allows for the black-listing of hotels for malpractice or other offences, with particulars to be exhibited and notified. Action under this section does not preclude prosecution.

main_sections.section_title: Notice of removal and black-listing of hotel.
main_sections.description: Requires the prescribed authority to give notice and hold an inquiry before removing a hotel from the register or black-listing it.
Empowers the prescribed authority to fix the rates for hotels.
Obligates hotel-keepers to display prescribed information.
Requires hotel-keepers to present detailed bills to customers.
Mandates registration for travel agents.
Deals with the issuance of certificates of registration for travel agents.
Specifies grounds for refusal to register travel agents.

main_sections.section_title: Removal of the name from the register.
main_sections.description: Details the process for removing a travel agent's name from the register.
Outlines the provisions for black-listing travel agents.

main_sections.section_title: Notice of removal and black-listing of travel agent.
main_sections.description: Requires notice and inquiry before removal or black-listing of travel agents.
Allows for the fixation of rates for services provided by travel agents.

main_sections.section_title: Travel agent not to receive or demand tips.
main_sections.description: Prohibits travel agents from receiving or demanding tips.
Provides for appeals against orders passed under the Act.
Deals with the power of revision of orders.
Imposes penalties for failure to register.
Penalizes the making of false statements.

main_sections.section_title: Certificate and documents to be shown to persons on demand.
main_sections.description: Requires registered persons to show certificates and documents when demanded.
Prohibits the assignment of registration certificates.
Specifies penalties for engaging in malpractice.
Penalizes obstruction of lawful authorities.
Deals with the summary trial of offences.
Introduces a special rule of evidence for certain offences.
Governs the institution of proceedings under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the prescribed authority to summon and enforce attendance of witnesses and other persons.
main_sections.description: Grants the prescribed authority power to summon witnesses and enforce attendance.
Provides for the composition of certain offences.
Requires notification of changes to details submitted for registration.

main_sections.section_title: Return of the certificate of registration.
main_sections.description: Deals with the return of registration certificates.
Provides for the issuance of duplicate certificates.

main_sections.section_title: Certificate of registration to be kept exhibited.
main_sections.description: Mandates that the certificate of registration be kept exhibited.

main_sections.section_title: Publication of list of person removed from the register.
main_sections.description: Requires the publication of lists of persons removed from the register.
Grants power to inspect premises and records.

main_sections.section_title: Fixation of rates for other services.
main_sections.description: Allows for the fixation of rates for other services.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the Government to apply the Act to other persons.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to extend the Act's application to other persons.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and duties of Police in respect of offences and assistance to the prescribed authority.
main_sections.description: Defines the powers and duties of the Police regarding offences and assistance to the prescribed authority.
Provides indemnity to persons acting in good faith under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Reservation of powers of local authority.
main_sections.description: Deals with the reservation of powers for local authorities.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the Government to regulate the courses of instruction or training in Tourism.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to regulate courses of instruction or training in Tourism.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Every person intending to carry on business as a dealer or operate a hotel must apply for registration to the prescribed authority.
Existing dealers and hotel operators must apply for registration within three months of the relevant notification.
Applications for registration must be disposed of within three months, failing which they are deemed accepted.
Dealers and hotel keepers must display their registration certificates.
Travel agents are prohibited from receiving or demanding tips.

penalties: Penalty for default in registration (Section 28)
Penalty for false statement (Section 29)
Penalty for malpractice (Section 32)
Penalty for obstructing lawful authorities (Section 33)
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The prescribed authority, Government, and Police.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through registration, inspection, imposition of penalties, black-listing, and prosecution for offences.

rights: Right to apply for registration.
Right to receive a certificate of registration.
Right to appeal against orders.
Right to be heard before refusal of registration or removal from register.
Right to receive detailed bills from hotel-keepers.
Right to approach lawful authorities.
duties: Duty to apply for registration as a dealer or hotel-keeper.
Duty to display registration certificate.
Duty to provide services as per prescribed standards.
Duty to display information in hotels.
Duty to present detailed bills.
Duty to not obstruct lawful authorities.
Duty to comply with provisions of the Act and rules.
Duty to not receive or demand tips as a travel agent.
obligations: Obligation to maintain prescribed records.
Obligation to notify any changes in registration details.
Obligation to surrender certificate of registration upon removal from the register.

key_procedures: Application for registration as a dealer or hotel-keeper.
Issuance and display of certificate of registration.
Procedures for refusal of registration, removal from register, and black-listing.
Procedures for appeals and revisions.
Procedures for inspecting premises and records.
Procedures for notifying changes and obtaining duplicate certificates.
Procedures for prosecuting offenders.
administration: The Government of Kerala and the 'Prescribed Authority' appointed under the Act.
important_notes: The Act aims to promote tourism development in Kerala.
Specific penalties are prescribed for various offences and contraventions.
The Government has the power to make rules to carry out the Act's provisions.

title: THE KERALA STATE HIGHER EDUCATION COUNCIL ACT, 2007
purpose: To provide for the setting up of the Kerala State Higher Education Council, to forge a synergistic relationship among them by occupying an operational space in between the Government and Universities and between Universities and apex level regulatory bodies, with the objects of (i) ensuring the autonomy and accountability of all institutions of higher education in the State, (ii) promoting academic excellence and social justice by providing academic input to the State Government for policy formulation and perspective planning, and (iii) guiding the growth of higher education in accordance with the socio-economic requirements of the State. Also to co-ordinate the implementation of policies in all higher education institutions in the State, network various programmes in higher education undertaken and promoted by the Central and State Governments and by national level regulatory bodies, provide common facilities for all Universities, research institutions, colleges and other centres of higher education, and promote the objectives of social justice and excellence in education.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. It applies to all institutions of higher education in the State.

key_definitions.Advisory Council: The Advisory Council of the Council.
key_definitions.All India Council for Technical Educatio: The All India Council for Technical Education Act, 1987 (Central Act 52 of 1987).
key_definitions.Bar Council of India: The Bar Council constituted under the Advocates Act, 1961 (Central Act 25 of 1961).
key_definitions.college: Any Higher Education Institution affiliated to a University.
key_definitions.Council: The Kerala State Higher Education Council constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.Executive Council: The Executive Council of the Council.
key_definitions.Governing Council: The Governing Council of the Council.
key_definitions.higher education: The education and research studies leading to the award of a degree or diploma or certificate by a University or an Institution approved by a University.
key_definitions.institution: An academic institution of higher education and research, not being a college, associated with and admitted to the privileges of a University or maintained by a University.
key_definitions.Medical Council of India: The Council constituted under the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956 (Central Act 102 of 1956).
key_definitions.member: A member of the Advisory Council, the Governing Council or the Executive Council.
key_definitions.National Council for Teacher Education: The Council constituted under the National Council for Teacher Education Act, 1993 (Central Act 73 of 1993).
key_definitions.Notification: The notification published in the official Gazette.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.regular student: A regular student of a University or a college affiliated to a University.
key_definitions.regulations: The regulations made by the Governing Council under this Act.
key_definitions.Statutes, Ordinances and Regulations: The Statutes, Ordinances and Regulations of a University means respectively, the Statutes, the Ordinances and the Regulations issued under the respective Acts of a University.
key_definitions.teacher: Any regular teacher working in a University, Government College or Government Aided College or Institution whose appointment has been made by a University or Government or approved by a University.
key_definitions.University: Any University in the State established by an Act of the State Legislature.
key_definitions.University Grants Commission: The Commission constituted under the University Grants Commission Act, 1956 (Central Act 3 of 1956).

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala State Higher Education Council Act, 2007, and it extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. It also states that it shall be deemed to have come into force on 25th January, 2007.

This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Advisory Council', 'College', 'Council', 'Executive Council', 'Government', 'Higher Education', 'Institution', 'Notification', 'Patron', 'Prescribed', 'Regular Student', 'Regulations', 'State', 'Statutes, Ordinances and Regulations', 'Teacher', 'University', 'University Grants Commission', and 'Vice-Chairman'.

This section outlines the constitution of the Kerala State Higher Education Council. It states that the Government may, by notification, constitute the Council with effect from such date as may be specified therein. The Council shall be a body corporate by the name aforesaid, having perpetual succession and a common seal and shall by the said name sue and be sued. The headquarters of the Council shall be at Thiruvananthapuram.

main_sections.section_title: Responsibilities and functions of the Council
main_sections.description: This section details the responsibilities and functions of the Council. These include rendering general advice to the Government, Universities and other institutions of higher education; co-ordinating the roles of the Government, Universities and apex regulatory agencies in higher education within the State; evolving new concepts and programmes in higher education; providing common facilities in higher education without impinging upon the autonomy of other institutions of higher education; providing academic input to the Government and Universities; undertaking independent research for the generation of new ideas; promoting social justice and academic excellence; developing human resources planning; evolving guidelines for linkages of academic nature; promoting relevance of higher education for economic, social and cultural development; reviewing existing guidelines and furnishing recommendations for regulating admissions; suggesting improvements in curriculum and syllabi; organising short-term courses; advising the Government on the starting of new courses; making proposals for generation and utilisation of funds; evolving general guidelines for the release of grants; evolving schemes for providing equitable opportunities for higher education; reviewing periodically the Statutes, Ordinances and Regulations of the Universities; and providing common facilities for the entire State by establishing centres.

The Governor of Kerala shall be the Patron of the Council. The Patron shall have the right to call for report on any matter pertaining to the affairs of the Council and offer suggestions for the improvement of the functioning of the Council. The Patron shall have the right to address any meeting of the Council, if he so desires.

rights: The Patron has the right to call for report on any matter pertaining to the affairs of the Council and offer suggestions for the improvement of the functioning of the Council.
The Patron has the right to address any meeting of the Council, if he so desires.
duties: The Council shall have the following general responsibilities and functions: (a) to render general advice to the Government, Universities and other institutions of higher education in the State.
(b) to co-ordinate the roles of the Government, Universities and apex regulatory agencies in higher education within the State.
(c) to evolve new concepts and programmes in higher education.
(d) to provide common facilities in higher education without impinging upon the autonomy of other institutions of higher education.

administration: The Government of Kerala
important_notes: Received the assent of Governor on the 13th October, 2007 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No 1856 dated 15th October, 2007.

title: THE KERALA SURVEY AND BOUNDARIES ACT, 1961
purpose: To consolidate, amend and unify the law relating to the survey of lands and settlement of boundary disputes in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint. The Act applies to any land and any boundaries thereof within the state. Registered holders of land have specific responsibilities and rights under the act.

key_definitions.Collector: Means the Collector of the district, having jurisdiction over the area.
key_definitions.Government land: Means any land the proprietary right in which vests in the Government.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made by the Government under this Act.
key_definitions.registered holder of any land: Means the person in whose name the land in question is registered in the Government accounts of the village.
key_definitions.Explanation (1) to registered holder: When any person other than the registered holder is in lawful management of a land, or otherwise than as agent or servant of the registered holder, has mortgage, such person shall be deemed to be the registered holder in respect of such land.
key_definitions.Explanation (2) to registered holder: When a land is so registered in the names of two or more persons jointly, the registered holder shall for the purposes of this Act, be the person who is recognised by the other joint holder or joint holders as the manager of the land or who, in the case of dispute, is recognised by the Collector as the principal joint holder.
key_definitions.registered land: Means any land the proprietary right in which does not vest in the Government.
key_definitions.survey: Includes all operations incidental to the determination, measurement and record of a boundary or boundaries or any part of a boundary and includes a resurvey.
key_definitions.survey mark: Means any mark or object, erected, made, employed or specified by a Survey Officer to indicate or determine or assist in determining the position or level of any point or power.
key_definitions.Survey Officer: Means any officer appointed by the Government as a Survey Officer under section 3.
key_definitions.Village Official: Includes Village Officer, Village Assistant Adhikari, Menon, Potail and Shambog.

main_sections.description: States the short title as "The Kerala Survey and Boundaries Act, 1961", its extent to the whole of the State of Kerala, and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Government via notification.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including Collector, Government land, prescribed, registered holder of any land, survey, survey mark, Survey Officer, and Village Official, along with explanations for specific terms.

Empowers the Government to appoint Survey Officers by name or by virtue of their office. It also specifies that Survey Officers are subject to the control of the Government and other authorities appointed by the Government. Survey Officers shall exercise powers and perform duties within their local limits as prescribed by the Government, and the Government may specify conditions under which powers may be exercised by others.

main_sections.section_title: Government may direct the survey of any land or any boundary of any land.
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to direct the survey of any land or any boundary within the State, or any boundary of the land in the State of Kerala.

main_sections.section_title: Survey of lands hit by sea erosion or action of river.
main_sections.description: Deals with the survey of lands affected by sea erosion or river action, requiring it to be done by a Survey Officer or other authorised official.

main_sections.section_title: Notification to be published by Survey Officers.
main_sections.description: Requires Survey Officers to publish a notification in the Gazette, specifying the date, time, and place for conducting a survey. The notification must also be affixed at a conspicuous place and time at the survey location. A copy of the notification must be sent to the registered holder and served if necessary.

main_sections.section_title: Cost of survey operations may be defrayed in the first instance by Government in certain cases.
main_sections.description: Allows the Government to initially bear the cost of survey operations in specific cases, which may then be recovered from persons concerned.

main_sections.section_title: Survey to be carried out in the prescribed manner.
main_sections.description: Mandates that surveys are to be conducted in the manner prescribed by rules made under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power to record boundary as undisputed.
main_sections.description: Grants Survey Officers the power to record a boundary as undisputed after making inquiries and if no dispute is brought to their notice.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Survey Officers to determine and record a disputed boundary with reasons.
main_sections.description: Empowers Survey Officers to determine and record disputed boundaries, providing their decisions with reasons. Every decision given by a Survey Officer under this section is to be notified to the registered holders of the land, and shall be final, subject to appeal.

main_sections.section_title: Appeal against orders of Survey Officer.
main_sections.description: Establishes the right to appeal against orders of a Survey Officer. Appeals are to be preferred to the Collector, and then to the appellate authority specified by the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Period within which appeal may be preferred.
main_sections.description: Specifies the time limits for preferring appeals against orders under sections 6, section 9 or section 10, generally three months from the date of service of notice or from the date of the decision.

main_sections.section_title: Completion of demarcation to be notified.
main_sections.description: Requires the Survey Officer to notify the completion of demarcation. If the land is not demarcated within a certain period, the Survey Officer shall notify its completion to the village office and any relevant co-owners of the land.

main_sections.section_title: Right to institute a suit in respect of boundary of the property surveyed.
main_sections.description: Grants any person aggrieved by a boundary determination the right to institute a suit to set aside or alter the determination within one year from the date of notification. However, this right is subject to the provisions of the law of limitation and the survey shall be held to be correct unless altered.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of registered holders for maintenance of survey marks.
main_sections.description: Makes registered holders of land liable for the maintenance, repair, and replacement of survey marks. Failure to do so can result in the Government or its officers carrying out the work and recovering the cost from the registered holder. This also applies to registered holders in possession of land through lease or mortgage.

Allows Survey Officers or Collectors to impose charges for work done under section 15. Appeals against these charges can be preferred to the appellate authority. Any person aggrieved by an order of the appellate authority may also appeal to the Government.

Outlines the duties of Village Officials, including to prevent destruction, injury, removal or alteration of survey marks within their jurisdiction. They must also report such occurrences to the Survey Officer.

main_sections.section_title: Power to enter upon, examine and clear obstruction on lands.
main_sections.description: Grants Survey Officers the power to enter upon, examine, and clear any obstructions on lands for the purpose of surveying. This includes cutting down trees, clearing fences, and removing other obstacles necessary for the survey.

main_sections.section_title: Power to summon witnesses and require production of documents.
main_sections.description: Empowers Survey Officers to summon witnesses and require the production of documents related to land surveys. They can also request assistance from any person for survey purposes.
Allows the Collector or Survey Officer, with the consent of all parties concerned, to refer any dispute to arbitration.

main_sections.section_title: Registered holder may recover expenses paid by him from owner.
main_sections.description: States that if a registered holder pays expenses incurred by the Government for a survey, they can recover these expenses from the owner of the land, along with interest at a specified rate.

Grants the Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act. These rules can cover various aspects, including prescribing survey procedures, defining classes of officers, regulating the conduct of officers, and specifying fees.

main_sections.section_title: Immunity for acts done or purporting to be done in good faith.
main_sections.description: Provides immunity from prosecution or legal proceedings for acts done or intended to be done in good faith under the Act or rules made thereunder.
Repeals previous legislation and provides for savings, referencing The Madras Survey and Boundaries Act, 1923, and section 5 of the State Reorganisation Act, 1956.

important_rules: Surveys are to be carried out in the prescribed manner.
Registered holders of land are liable for the maintenance, repair, and replacement of survey marks.
Village Officials must prevent the destruction, injury, removal, or alteration of survey marks within their jurisdiction and report such incidents.
Survey Officers have the power to enter upon lands, examine, and clear obstructions for survey purposes.
Survey Officers can summon witnesses and require the production of documents related to land surveys.
Rules may be made by the Government to prescribe different procedures for different survey operations, define classes of officers, and regulate their conduct.

penalties: Recovery of costs for maintenance, renewal, or repair of survey marks from registered holders.
Potential recovery of expenses for survey operations from applicants if land is found not to be subject to survey.
Penalties for obstruction or interference with survey marks or operations as prescribed by rules.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Survey Officers, Collectors, Government, and other authorities appointed by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through orders and decisions of Survey Officers and Collectors, appeal processes, and the power to recover costs. Government can make rules to prescribe penalties.

rights: Right to appeal against orders of Survey Officers.
Right to institute a suit in respect of boundary determinations.
Right for registered holders to recover expenses paid from the owner.
Right to be notified about survey operations and decisions.
duties: Duty of Survey Officers to conduct surveys, determine boundaries, and record decisions.
Duty of registered holders to maintain survey marks.
Duty of Village Officials to prevent damage to survey marks and report incidents.
Duty to attend inquiries and provide documents when summoned by Survey Officers.
obligations: Obligation for registered holders to bear the cost of survey operations related to their land, unless otherwise prescribed.
Obligation to provide labour and assistance for survey operations when required.

key_procedures: Procedure for conducting surveys: Notification by Survey Officer, affixing notice at the site, serving notice to registered holders, carrying out the survey in the prescribed manner.
Procedure for determining disputed boundaries: Survey Officer to make inquiries, record the boundary with reasons, and notify registered holders.
Procedure for appeals: Appeals against Survey Officer's orders to the Collector, then to the appellate authority, within prescribed time limits.
Procedure for maintenance of survey marks: Registered holders are responsible for maintenance, repair, and renewal. Costs can be recovered if neglected.
Procedure for instituting a suit: For aggrieved persons challenging boundary determinations within a specified period.
administration: The Government of Kerala, through its appointed Survey Officers and Collectors, administers this Act. The Government also has the power to make rules for its implementation.
important_notes: The Act aims to consolidate and unify the law on survey and boundaries in Kerala.
Registered holders of land have significant responsibilities regarding survey marks.
Decisions of Survey Officers on disputed boundaries are final, subject to appeal.
The Act includes provisions for recovery of costs associated with surveys and maintenance of survey marks.
Immunity is provided for acts done in good faith under the Act.

title: The Kerala Tailoring Workers Welfare Fund Act, 1994
purpose: The purpose of the act is to provide for the establishment and administration of a welfare fund for tailoring workers in Kerala.
scope: The Act applies to tailoring workers in the state of Kerala.

key_definitions.tailoring_worker: Any person who is engaged in tailoring work and is covered by this Act.
key_definitions.welfare_fund: The fund established under this Act for the welfare of tailoring workers.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and its commencement date.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'tailoring worker', 'employer', 'fund', etc.
Deals with the establishment of the Tailoring Workers Welfare Fund.
Outlines the provisions related to contributions made to the Welfare Fund by employers and workers.
Specifies the objects for which the fund can be utilized, such as providing benefits to tailoring workers.
Describes how the Welfare Fund is to be administered, including the formation of a Welfare Fund Board.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and duties of the Board
main_sections.description: Details the powers and responsibilities of the Tailoring Workers Welfare Fund Board.
Covers the appointment of officers and other staff required for the administration of the Act.

important_rules: Contributions to the Welfare Fund must be made by employers and workers as prescribed.
The fund shall be used for the welfare of tailoring workers, including but not limited to, medical aid, educational assistance, and financial assistance.
The Board is responsible for the proper management and utilization of the fund.

penalties: Penalty for non-payment of contributions (details of amount/duration not specified in these pages).
Penalty for obstruction of officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Tailoring Workers Welfare Fund Board and authorized officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, demand of contributions, and legal proceedings in case of non-compliance.

rights: Right of tailoring workers to receive benefits from the Welfare Fund.
Right to be informed about the management of the fund.
duties: Duty of employers to deduct and pay contributions.
Duty of workers to contribute to the fund.
Duty of the Board to administer the fund efficiently.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder.

key_procedures: Procedure for the registration of tailoring workers and employers.
Procedure for the collection and remittance of contributions.
Procedure for the disbursement of benefits to tailoring workers.
administration: The Kerala Tailoring Workers Welfare Fund Board.
important_notes: The Act was amended in 1994.
The Act supersedes any prior law, custom or usage inconsistent with its provisions.

title: THE KERALA TAX ON ENTRY OF MOTOR VEHICLES INTO LOCAL AREAS ACT, 1994
purpose: To provide for the levy of tax on the entry of motor vehicles into local areas for use or sale therein.
scope: The Act applies to the whole of the State of Kerala. It covers the entry of motor vehicles into local areas for use or sale therein.

key_definitions.accessories: Means car air conditioner, music system or any other article fitted to a motor vehicle which is not included in the original invoice.
key_definitions.appellate authority: Means an appellate authority appointed under section 6.
key_definitions.assessing authority: Means an assessing authority appointed under section 5.
key_definitions.entry of motor vehicle into a local area: Means with all its grammatical variations and cognate expressions, means entry of motor vehicle into a local area from any place outside the State for use or sale therein.
key_definitions.General Sales Tax Act: Means the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963 (13 of 1963).
key_definitions.importer: Means a person who brings a motor vehicle into a local area from any place outside the State for use or sale therein or who owns the vehicle at the time of its entry into the local area.
key_definitions.local area: Means the area of jurisdiction of a local authority.
key_definitions.local authority: Means a Municipal Corporation constituted under the Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, 1961 (30 of 1961) or a Municipality constituted under the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960 (14 of 1961) or a Municipality constituted under the law relating to Municipalities, made in accordance with the provisions in Part IXA of the Constitution of India or the Township specified in section 2 of the Guruvayoor Township Act, 1961 (43 of 1961) or a Panchayat constituted or declared to have been constituted for the local administration of a Panchayat area under the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960 (32 of 1960) or a Panchayat constituted under the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 (13 of 1994) or a Cantonment declared under the Cantonments Act, 1924 (Central Act 2 of 1924);
key_definitions.motor vehicle: Means a motor vehicle as defined in clause (28) of section 2 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (Central Act 59 of 1988).
key_definitions.notification: Means a notification published in the Gazette;
key_definitions.person: Includes any company or association or body of individuals whether incorporated or not, a firm, a local authority, the Government of any other State or Union Territory;
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act;
key_definitions.purchase value: Means the value of a motor vehicle, as ascertained from the original invoice and includes the value of accessories fitted in the vehicle, insurance, excise duties, trailer duties, sales tax, transport fee, freight charges and all other charges incidentally levied on the purchase of a motor vehicle:
key_definitions.tax: Means tax payable under this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Tax on Entry of Motor Vehicles into Local Areas Act, 1994. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force at once. It also includes definitions for various terms used in the Act.

Provides definitions for terms such as 'accessories', 'appellate authority', 'assessing authority', 'entry of motor vehicle into a local area', 'General Sales Tax Act', 'Government', 'importer', 'local area', 'local authority', 'motor vehicle', 'notification', 'person', 'prescribed', 'purchase value', and 'tax'.

Specifies that tax shall be levied and collected on the entry of any motor vehicle into any local area for use or sale therein. The rate of tax will be as may be fixed by the Government by notification, but not exceeding the rates specified for motor vehicles in the First Schedule to the Kerala General Sales Tax Act. It also provides exceptions for certain vehicles registered in any Union Territory or other State, and vehicles owned by the property of the Central Government or used exclusively for defence purposes.

Deals with the reduction of tax liability for importers who are dealers in motor vehicles and have paid tax under the General Sales Tax Act. It also covers reduction of tax for importers who are not dealers in motor vehicles but have purchased a motor vehicle for their own use in any Union Territory or other State.

Empowers the Government to appoint officers of the Agricultural Income Tax and Sales Tax Department as assessing authorities for the purposes of this Act, and to assign them such local area or local areas as may be specified.

Empowers the Government to appoint officers of the Agricultural Income Tax and Sales Tax Department as appellate authorities for the purposes of this Act, and to assign them such local area or local areas as may be specified.

Mandates every person liable to pay tax under this Act to furnish returns in such form, for such period, by such dates and to such authority, as may be prescribed. It also outlines the process for furnishing revised returns.

Details the process of assessment, including when an assessing authority is satisfied that a return furnished is correct and complete, and when it is of the opinion that a return is not correct and complete. It also outlines the procedure for issuing a notice and the requirement to produce evidence.

Provides for reassessment if an assessing authority has reason to believe that any purchase value or part thereof has escaped assessment or has been assessed at a lower rate. The reassessment can be done for any period within five years from the date of order of assessment or the date of service of notice.
Specifies that tax shall be paid in the manner hereinafter provided. It outlines the procedure for paying the tax, including the submission of returns and the payment of the difference in tax.
Details the procedure for the refund of tax by the assessing authority when any amount of tax and the penalty, if any, paid by a person exceeds the amount due for any period.

States that the Government may, by notification, exempt any specified class of importers from payment of the whole or part of the tax payable under this Act, subject to such conditions as they may impose.

Lays down the procedure for appeals against any original order under this Act to the appellate authority. It also specifies conditions under which appeals can be entertained and the powers of the appellate authority.

Allows the Board of Revenue, suo motu or on an application made in that behalf, to call for and examine the records of any proceedings or order made by an assessing authority or appellate authority and pass such order as it thinks just and proper.

Implies that penalties are prescribed for violations of the Act, though the specific details of penalties are not fully detailed in the provided table of contents. Section 10(4)(iii) mentions a penalty levied under section 15.

main_sections.section_title: Officers and employees to be public servants
main_sections.description: Declares that officers and employees acting under this Act are considered public servants.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection to persons acting in good faith in pursuance of the provisions of this Act or any rule or order made thereunder.
Indicates a restriction related to the registration of motor vehicles, likely in relation to tax compliance, though details are not in the table of contents.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Every person liable to pay tax under this Act shall furnish returns in such form, for such period, by such dates and to such authority, as may be prescribed.

Rule 2: If any person liable to pay tax under this Act, having furnished a return under sub-section (1), discovers any omission or incorrect statement therein, he may furnish a revised return before the expiry of three months from the last date prescribed for furnishing the return under that sub-section.
Rule 3: The tax shall be paid in the manner hereinafter provided.

Rule 4: Subject to such conditions as they may impose, the Government may, by notification, exempt any specified class of importers from payment of the whole or part of the tax payable under this Act.

penalties: Penalty levied under section 15 (details not fully available in provided content).
Penalty for any tax or penalty remaining unpaid after the date specified in the notice for payment, which shall be recoverable as if it were an arrear of public revenue due on land.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Assessing authorities and Appellate authorities appointed under the Act, and officers of the Agricultural Income Tax and Sales Tax Department.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment, reassessment, collection of tax and penalties, and appeals and revisions.

rights: Right to appeal against original orders.
Right to revision of orders.
Right to refund of excess tax paid.
duties: Duty to pay tax on the entry of motor vehicles into local areas.
Duty to furnish returns.
Duty to pay tax within the prescribed period.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder.
Obligation to provide correct and complete information in returns and assessments.

key_procedures: Procedure for Levy of Tax: Tax is levied on the entry of motor vehicles into local areas for use or sale therein, at rates notified by the Government, not exceeding specified limits.

Procedure for Assessment: Persons liable to pay tax must furnish returns. The assessing authority assesses the tax based on the returns or after inquiry. This includes processes for original assessment and reassessment.
Procedure for Payment of Tax: Tax is to be paid in the prescribed manner, usually to the Government Treasury.
Procedure for Refund: If tax paid exceeds the amount due, a refund can be claimed.
Procedure for Appeals: An aggrieved person can appeal to the appellate authority against an original order. Further appeals or revisions are also outlined.
Procedure for Exemptions: The Government can grant exemptions through notification under specified conditions.
administration: The Act is administered by the Government of Kerala, likely through its Sales Tax Department or equivalent bodies responsible for taxation and revenue collection.
important_notes: The Act was enacted on the 9th day of June 1994 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extra Ordinary No. 550, dated the 10th June 1994.
The tax rates are subject to notification by the Government, not exceeding specified limits under the Kerala General Sales Tax Act.
Specific exemptions can be granted by the Government.
Protection is provided for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

title: THE KERALA (SCHEDULED CASTES AND SCHEDULED TRIBES) REGULATION OF ISSUE OF COMMUNITY CERTIFICATES ACT, 1996
purpose: To provide for and to regulate the issue of community certificates to members of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the State of Kerala and to prevent malpractices in securing such certificates.
scope: The Act applies to the entire State of Kerala and concerns the issue of community certificates to members of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

key_definitions.appointment in public service: means appointment to a service for post under the State or Central Government and includes appointment to any post of the State or Central Government undertakings.
key_definitions.appointing authority: in relation to a service or post means the authority empowered to make appointment to such service or post, and includes appointing authorities in respect of the services and posts in connection with the affairs of the Central Government and the State and Central Government undertakings.
key_definitions.Community Certificate: means the certificate issued by the competent authority in the prescribed form indicating therein the Scheduled Caste or the Scheduled Tribe, as the case may be, to which a person belongs.
key_definitions.Competent Authority: means any officer or authority authorised by the Government by notification to perform the functions of the competent authority under this Act, for such areas or for such purposes as may be specified in the notification.
key_definitions.Co-operative Institution: means a Co-operative Society of Society registered or deemed to be registered under the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969 (21 of 1969).
key_definitions.Educational Institution: means any School, College, Polytechnic, Industrial Training Centre, Industrial Training Institute, College of Fine Arts, College of Music, Engineering College, Medical College, Ayurveda College, Homoeopathy College, Dental College, College of Nursing, Nurses Training School, Health Visons Training School, Colleges under the control of the Kerala Agricultural University and various Colleges or Institutions under the control of any University established by an Act of the State Legislature and any other institution imparting education as may be specified by the Government by notification in the Gazette, from time to time.
key_definitions.Expert Agency: means an officer, or team of officers belonging to the Anthropological Wing of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Development Department of the State Government, entrusted with the research, training and developmental studies of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes and also includes the Director of that Department, if he belongs to the Anthropology Wing of the Department or is an Anthropologist or Sociologist.
key_definitions.Local authority: means a local authority as defined in the Kerala Panchayati Raj Act, 1994 (13 of 1994) or the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1994 (20 of 1994) as the case may be.
key_definitions.Notification: means a notification published in the Gazette and the word 'notified' shall be construed accordingly.
key_definitions.Prescribed: means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes: shall have the meanings respectively assigned to them in clause (24) and clause (25) of Article 366 of the Constitution of India.
key_definitions.Screening Committee: means a committee mentioned in section 6.
key_definitions.Scrutiny Committee: means the committee constituted by the Government by notification under section 8 to perform the functions of the Scrutiny Committee under this Act for such areas or for such purposes as may be specified in the notification.
key_definitions.Special Court: means a Court of Session specified as a special court under section 21.
key_definitions.Special Public Prosecutor: means a Public Prosecutor specified by the Government as a Special Public Prosecutor or an advocate, by notification under section 22.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala (Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes) Regulation of Issue of Community Certificates Act, 1996. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and comes into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'appointment in public service', 'appointing authority', 'Community Certificate', 'Competent Authority', 'Co-operative Institution', 'Educational Institution', 'Expert Agency', 'Government', 'Local authority', 'Notification', 'Prescribed', 'Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes', 'Screening Committee', 'Scrutiny Committee', 'Special Court', and 'Special Public Prosecutor'.

main_sections.section_title: Proof of the Scheduled Caste or the Scheduled Tribe Status.
main_sections.description: States that notwithstanding anything contained in the Act, any person belonging to any of the Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes claiming any benefit, concession, protection, exemption or reservation provided to such Castes or Tribes either for any appointment in public services or for admission into educational institutions, exclusively intended for members of the Scheduled Castes or the Scheduled Tribes, or for contesting for the seats reserved for them in any educational institution in the State or outside the State, for the students of the State or local authority or co-operative institution, shall prove his claim by a Certificate issued for the purpose under this Act, by the competent authority, in the prescribed manner.

Any person belonging to any of the Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes, in order to prove his claim that he belongs to the Scheduled Caste or the Scheduled Tribe, as the case may be, for any purpose, shall make an application in such form and in such manner, as may be prescribed, to the competent authority for the issue of a Community Certificate.

main_sections.section_title: Community Certificate to be issued only by the Competent Authority.
main_sections.description: The Competent Authority may on an application made to it under section 4, by following the prescribed procedure, satisfy itself about the genuineness or otherwise of the claim made therein and the same shall issue a community certificate within such period and in such form as may be prescribed or reject the application for reasons to be recorded in writing.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of Screening Committee for verification of Community Certificate.
main_sections.description: Details the constitution of a Screening Committee by the Government for verification of community certificates of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in educational institutions. The committee is to ensure the genuineness of the claim and can conduct enquiries.

Production of a community certificate issued by the Competent Authority shall not preclude the appointing authority, or head of the educational institution or any other office or authority superior to the appointing authority or head of the educational institution including the State Government, from verifying or causing to be verified the claim of an individual that he belongs to the Scheduled Caste or the Scheduled Tribe, as the case may be, at the time of initial appointment, selection or admission or at any stage thereafter.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of Scrutiny Committee for verification of community certificates.
main_sections.description: The Government shall constitute a Scrutiny Committee for verification of community certificates. Any person belonging to Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes or any appointing authority or local body or heads of educational institutions may make an application in such form and in such manner as may be prescribed by the scrutiny committee for verification of community certificates.

The expert agency may conduct enquiries as it may deem fit into the claim of an individual or group of individuals that he or they belong to the Scheduled Caste or the Scheduled Tribe in the following circumstances: studies on basis of field studies, on petitions and complaints received, and on references, requisitions, directions or proposals received from the State and Central Governments, the competent authorities or the screening committee or the scrutiny committee.

Where an application is made to the competent authority under section 4 for the issue of a community certificate in respect of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe or in any enquiry conducted by the Competent Authority, the Expert Agency, or the Scrutiny Committee or in any trial or offence under this Act, the burden of proving that he belongs to such Caste or Tribe shall be on the claimant.

Where, before or after the commencement of this Act, a person not belonging to any of the Scheduled Castes or the Scheduled Tribes has obtained a false community certificate to the effect that either hisself or his children belongs or belong to such Caste or Tribe, the Scrutiny Committee may either suo motu or on a written complaint or report by any person or authority, call for the records and enquire into the genuineness of such certificate and if it is of the opinion that the certificate was obtained fraudulently, it shall, by order, cancel the certificate after giving the person concerned an opportunity of making a representation, if any.

Any person aggrieved by an order passed by the Competent Authority, District Collector, Government, High Court, or any other authority may prefer an appeal or review within specified time limits and to the respective higher authorities.

main_sections.section_title: Power of stay and revision by the Government.
main_sections.description: The Government, by itself or through its officer or authority subordinate to it, can stay, revise, or modify any order passed by any authority under this Act, except in cases of decisions of the Scrutiny Committee on revision or application made to them within the prescribed period.

main_sections.section_title: Competent Authority, the Expert Agency and Scrutiny Committee to exercise powers of the Civil Court
main_sections.description: The Competent Authority, the Expert Agency, and the Scrutiny Committee shall, while holding an enquiry under this Act, have all the powers of a Civil Court trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 in respect of the following matters: summoning and enforcing attendance, requiring discovery and production of documents, receiving evidence on affidavits, requisitioning public records, issuing commissions, and any other matter specified by the Government.

Outlines penalties for whoever obtains a community certificate by furnishing false information or by filing a false statement, or by making a false representation. It also includes penalties for making false reports, and for obtaining benefits based on false certificates.
Provides for the appointment of Special Public Prosecutors for conducting cases under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Offence under the Act cognizable and non-bailable.
main_sections.description: Declares offences under this Act as cognizable and non-bailable.

main_sections.section_title: Bar of jurisdiction of civil courts
main_sections.description: States that no civil court shall have jurisdiction to entertain or decide any suit or proceeding in respect of any matter which the Government or the Competent Authority or the Scrutiny Committee or the Screening Committee or the Expert Agency is empowered or required to decide or determine under this Act. Any order passed by the Government or any officer or authority or tribunal under this Act shall be final and shall not be liable to be questioned in any civil court.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of acts done in good faith
main_sections.description: No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against any person for anything which is in good faith done or intended to be done in pursuance of this Act or any rule or notification or order made thereunder.
The provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any other law for the time being in force.
Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Departmental proceedings not barred by prosecution
main_sections.description: States that nothing in this Act shall prevent the institution of departmental proceedings against any person for any offence committed under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Cancellation of Community Certificate issued to a person to be proof against the relatives of the same blood.
main_sections.description: If a community certificate is cancelled by the Scrutiny Committee, it shall be proof against the relatives of the same blood of the person concerned.
Deals with transitional provisions related to the Act.

important_rules: Community Certificates must be issued only by the Competent Authority.
The Competent Authority must satisfy itself about the genuineness of the claim before issuing a certificate.
Any person claiming benefits as a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe must prove their claim with a Certificate issued under this Act.
The Screening Committee is to verify community certificates of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in educational institutions.
The Scrutiny Committee is to verify community certificates upon application or suo motu.
Expert Agencies can conduct field studies, inquire into petitions and complaints, and process references for verification.
The burden of proof for belonging to a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe lies with the claimant.
False community certificates can be cancelled, and penalties will apply.
Appeals and reviews against orders are allowed to higher authorities.
The Government has the power of stay and revision over orders.
Offences under the Act are cognizable and non-bailable.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both (for obtaining a false certificate or making a false report).
For obtaining benefits through false certificates, imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees, or with both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Competent Authority, Expert Agency, Scrutiny Committee, Government, Special Public Prosecutor.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inquiries, verification processes, cancellation of certificates, prosecution of offenders, imposition of fines and imprisonment, and the appellate and review procedures.

rights: Right to apply for a Community Certificate if belonging to Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes.
Right to appeal or seek review against orders passed under the Act.
duties: Duty to prove claim of belonging to Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes through a valid certificate.
Duty to comply with the procedures laid down in the Act for obtaining certificates.
obligations: Obligation to not obtain or attempt to obtain a community certificate by false means.
Obligation to provide truthful information when making an application or during an inquiry.

key_procedures: Application for Community Certificate: A person belonging to Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes must apply to the competent authority in the prescribed form and manner.

Issuance of Community Certificate: The Competent Authority, after satisfying itself about the genuineness of the claim through prescribed procedure, shall issue the certificate or reject the application with reasons.
Verification of Certificates: The Screening Committee and Scrutiny Committee conduct verification of community certificates.
Enquiry by Expert Agency: The expert agency may conduct enquiries to verify claims.
Cancellation of False Certificates: The Scrutiny Committee can cancel false certificates after due inquiry and opportunity for representation.
Appeal Process: Aggrieved persons can appeal to higher authorities against orders passed under the Act.
administration: The Government of Kerala, through various authorities and committees constituted under the Act.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the President on the 24th day of September, 1996 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 1151 dated 1st October, 1996.
The Act is designed to prevent malpractices and ensure that benefits are availed by genuine members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
The burden of proof for community status lies with the claimant.
Even after issuance, community certificates can be verified and cancelled if found fraudulent.

title: THE KERALA ABKARI LAWS (AMENDMENT AND VALIDATION) ACT, 1964
purpose: To further amend the Cochin Abkari Act I of 1077, and the Abkari Act (Travancore Act IV of 1073), and to validate the levy and collection of duty on liquor and intoxicating drugs made under the said Acts.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala. It amends existing Abkari Acts of Cochin and Travancore, affecting the levy and collection of duties on liquor and intoxicating drugs.

key_definitions.rental: Means the rental payable under section 18A in consideration of the grant of an exclusive or other privilege of manufacturing, supplying or selling any liquor or intoxicating drugs.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Abkari Laws (Amendment and Validation) Act, 1964. Sub-sections (2) and (3) specify the commencement dates for different sections.
Amends Section 3 of the Cochin Abkari Act, I of 1077, by amending the definition of 'intoxicating drugs'.
Omits Section 16 of the Cochin Act.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new heading for heading 'V. Duties' in Cochin Act.
main_sections.description: Substitutes the heading 'V. DUTIES, TAXES AND RENTALS' for the heading 'V. Duties' in the Cochin Act.
Amends Section 17 of the Cochin Act, by substituting 'V. DUTIES, TAXES AND RENTALS' for 'V. DUTIES' and providing for the levy of a duty of amount and ending with 'intoxicating drugs'.
Amends Section 18 of the Cochin Act, by inserting provisions for the levy of duty of excise and luxury tax on liquor and intoxicating drugs.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new section 18A in Cochin Act.
main_sections.description: Inserts a new Section 18A into the Cochin Act, dealing with the grant of exclusive or other privilege of manufacturing, supplying or selling by retail, and the rental payable.
Amends Section 19 of the Cochin Act, by substituting 'duty, tax and rental' for 'duty'.
Amends Section 20 of the Cochin Act, by substituting 'All or any of the duties, tax and rentals' for 'All or any of the duties'.
Amends Section 21 of the Cochin Act, by substituting 'farmer' for 'farmer under section 20'.
Amends Section 26 of the Cochin Act, by substituting 'any fee, duty, tax or rental' for 'any fee or duty'.
Amends Section 58 of the Cochin Act, by substituting 'duty, tax and rental' for 'duty'.
Amends Section 3 of the Abkari Act (Travancore Act IV of 1073), by substituting 'means' for 'includes'.
Omits Section 14 of the Travancore Act.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new heading for heading 'V. Duties' in Travancore Act.
main_sections.description: Substitutes 'V. DUTIES, TAXES AND RENTALS' for 'V. DUTIES' in the Travancore Act.
Amends Section 15 of the Travancore Act, by substituting 'be levied on all liquor and intoxicating drugs' and adding an explanation for the levy of duty of excise or luxury tax.
Amends Section 16 of the Travancore Act, by renumbering sub-section (1) and substituting 'duty of excise or luxury tax' and adding provisions for its levy.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new section 16 A in Travancore Act.
main_sections.description: Inserts Section 16 A in the Travancore Act, dealing with the grant of exclusive or other privilege and rental payable to the Government.
Amends Section 17 of the Travancore Act, by substituting 'All or any of the duties, tax and rentals' for 'All or any of the duties'.
Amends Section 18 of the Travancore Act, by substituting 'section 14', 'figure and letter 'section 16A'' for 'section 14'.
Amends Section 22 of the Travancore Act, by substituting 'any fee, duty, tax or rental' for 'any fee or duty'.
Amends Section 54 of the Travancore Act, by substituting 'duty, tax and rental payable' for 'prescribed duty'.

main_sections.section_title: Revival and amendment of Cochin and Travancore Acts in certain areas.
main_sections.description: Revives and amends the Cochin and Travancore Abkari Acts in the areas where they had ceased to be in force, and provides for their re-enforcement.
Validates any judgment or order of any court, and any levy or collection of duties, taxes, or fees made under the existing Acts, as if they had been in force.
Repeals the Kerala Abkari Laws (Amendment and Validation) Ordinance, 1964.

important_rules: Duty of excise on liquors (Indian made) is Rs. 20 per proof litre or Rs. 90-92 per proof gallon.
Duty of excise on intoxicating drugs is Rs. 1 per gram or Rs. 933.10 per seer.
Duty of excise in the form of tax on trees tapped for toddy is Rs. 25 per tree per half-year or part thereof.
Luxury tax for sale of foreign liquor in wholesale is Rs. 5,000 for a year or part thereof.
Luxury tax for sale of foreign liquor in hotels or restaurants is Rs. 4,000 for a year or part thereof.
Luxury tax for sale of medicated wines is Rs. 1,000 for a year or part thereof.
Luxury tax for sale of foreign liquor in non-proprietary clubs to members is Rs. 500 for a year or part thereof.
Luxury tax for special licence for sale of foreign liquor is Rs. 500 for a year or part thereof.
Levy of gallonage fee on fermented spirit is Rs. 10 per bulk litre or Rs. 45-46 per bulk gallon.
Levy of gallonage fee on denatured spirit including methylated spirit is Rs. 1 per bulk litre or Rs. 4-54 per bulk gallon.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government is empowered to make rules, and the District Collector is involved in the grant of privilege and collection of rental.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the levy and collection of duties, taxes, and rentals as specified in the Act, and through the enforcement of rules made by the Government.

rights: Right to the exclusive or other privilege of manufacturing, supplying or selling by retail any liquor or intoxicating drugs within any local area on his or their payment of rental to the Government.
duties: Duty to pay excise or luxury tax on liquor and intoxicating drugs.
Duty to pay rental for the exclusive or other privilege of dealing in liquor and intoxicating drugs.

key_procedures: Grant of exclusive or other privilege of manufacturing, supplying or selling by retail any liquor or intoxicating drugs.
Collection of rental for such privileges through auction, negotiation or other methods as determined by the Government.
Levy and collection of duty of excise and luxury tax on liquor and intoxicating drugs.
administration: The Government of Kerala (implied by the context of Kerala Abkari Laws).
important_notes: The Act validates past actions of levy and collection of duties, taxes, and fees.
The Act addresses the dual legislative jurisdiction of Cochin and Travancore and consolidates them under Kerala.

title: The Kerala Abkari Workers Welfare Fund Act, 1989
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a Welfare Fund for Abkari workers in the State of Kerala, and for matters connected therewith.
scope: This Act applies to Abkari workers in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Abkari worker: A person employed or engaged in connection with the production, manufacture, distillation, sale, or transport of intoxicating drinks and substances in the State.
key_definitions.Fund: The Abkari Workers Welfare Fund constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.Board: The Abkari Workers Welfare Fund Board constituted under section 4.
key_definitions.Prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Intoxicating drink or substance: Any liquor or intoxicating substance as defined in the Abkari Act.
key_definitions.Casual worker: A worker engaged on a daily basis or for a short term.
key_definitions.Permanent worker: A worker engaged on a regular basis for a longer term.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and its commencement.
Defines various terms used in the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of the Abkari Workers Welfare Fund
main_sections.description: Establishes the Abkari Workers Welfare Fund.
Provides for the constitution of the Abkari Workers Welfare Fund Board.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of the Board
main_sections.description: Outlines the powers and functions of the Board.
Details how contributions are made to the Fund.
Specifies how the Fund can be utilised.

important_rules: Contributions to the Fund shall be made by employers and such other sources as may be prescribed.
The Fund shall be used for the welfare of Abkari workers, including financial assistance, medical facilities, education, and other benefits.
The Board shall manage the Fund and invest it in such securities as the Government may approve.
The Board shall maintain proper accounts and get them audited annually.

penalties: Penalty for failure to contribute to the Fund: Imprisonment which may extend to six months or fine or both.
Penalty for false statements: Imprisonment which may extend to three months or fine or both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Abkari Workers Welfare Fund Board and other authorities appointed by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, inquiries, and legal proceedings.

rights: Right of Abkari workers to receive benefits from the Fund.
Right of Abkari workers to have their grievances redressed by the Board.
duties: Duty of employers to contribute to the Fund.
Duty of the Board to manage the Fund efficiently and for the benefit of the workers.
Duty of individuals to provide true and correct information when required.
obligations: Obligation of the Government to make rules and regulations for the effective implementation of the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure for claiming benefits from the Fund: Application to the Board with necessary documents.
Procedure for management and investment of the Fund: As determined by the Board and approved by the Government.
Procedure for audit of accounts: Annual audit by auditors appointed by the Government.
administration: The Abkari Workers Welfare Fund Board, under the overall supervision of the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act aims to provide social security and welfare measures for Abkari workers.
The Government has the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.

title: THE KERALA ADDITIONAL SALES TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1979
purpose: To amend the Kerala Additional Sales Tax Act, 1978.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Additional Sales Tax Act, 1978.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Additional Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 1979, and that it shall come into force at once.
Specifies that in the long title to the Kerala Additional Sales Tax Act, 1978, the words and figures "for the financial year 1978-79" shall be omitted.
States that in the preamble to the Principal Act, the words and figures "for the financial year 1978-79" shall be omitted.
Amends section 2 of the Principal Act by substituting words and figures related to the financial year for the year 1978-79.

important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 30th March, 1979 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 247, 31st March, 1979.

title: THE KERALA ADDITIONAL SALES TAX ACT, 1978
purpose: To provide for the levy of additional sales tax for the financial year 1978-79.
scope: Applies to sales and purchase taxes during 1978-79 in Kerala.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Kerala Additional Sales Tax Act, 1978, and states that it came into force on the 1st day of April, 1978.

main_sections.section_title: Levy of additional tax on sales and purchase taxes during 1978-79.
main_sections.description: Details the levy of additional tax. The tax payable under the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, for the financial year commencing on the first day of April, 1978, shall be increased by ten per cent of such tax. It specifies that the additional tax is payable at a reduced rate by virtue of a notification under section 10, and if the dealer opted for the tax payable at the compounded rate, the additional tax is payable at a reduced or compounded rate. It also states that notwithstanding anything contained in subsection (1), the tax shall not be increased under subsection (1), if the tax together with surcharge, if any, payable thereon under the Kerala Surcharge on Taxes Act, 1957, is equal to four per cent of the taxable turnover of such goods. Further, if the tax together with surcharge is less than four per cent of the taxable turnover of such goods, the amount by which the tax is increased under subsection (1) shall not exceed the difference between four per cent of the taxable turnover of such goods and the aggregate amount of the tax and such surcharge, if any, payable on such taxable turnover.

Repeals The Kerala Additional Sales Tax Ordinance, 1978. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: The additional tax payable under subsection (1) of section 2 shall be in addition to the surcharge payable under the Kerala Surcharge on Taxes Act, 1957.
Rule 2: The provisions of the Sales Tax Act shall apply in relation to the additional tax payable under subsection (1) of section 2 as they apply in relation to the tax payable under that Act.

obligations: Obligation: Dealers are obligated to pay the additional sales tax as specified in the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure: Levy of additional tax by increasing the tax payable under the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, by ten per cent for the financial year 1978-79.
important_notes: Note: The Act was received the assent of the Governor on the 1st day of August, 1978 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 507 dated 2nd August, 1978.

title: The Kerala Additional Tax On Entertainments And Surcharge On Show Tax (Amendment) Act, 1975
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Additional Tax on Entertainments and Surcharge on Show Tax Act, 1963.
scope: Applies to entertainments and surcharge on show tax within Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Additional Tax on Entertainments and Surcharge on Show Tax (Amendment) Act, 1975. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 2.
main_sections.description: This section substitutes the existing section 2 of the principal Act with a new section concerning the levy of additional tax on entertainments. It specifies that an additional tax will be levied on each price for admission to any entertainment subject to the levy of entertainment tax under section 3 of the Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1961, at the rate of sixty per cent of the entertainments tax. It also addresses the scenario where entertainments tax is compounded, stating the additional tax on entertainments will be sixty per cent of the compounded amount.
In section 4 of the principal Act, the last sentence shall be omitted.

important_rules: An additional tax is levied on entertainments at a rate of sixty per cent of the entertainments tax.
If the entertainments tax is compounded, the additional tax on entertainments is sixty per cent of the compounded amount.
The last sentence of section 4 of the principal Act is omitted.
key_procedures: The Government may appoint a date for the commencement of the Act through a notification in the Gazette.
administration: The Government of Kerala.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 1st day of June 1975 and published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 280, dated 3rd June 1975.

title: The Kerala Additional Tax on Entertainments and Surcharge on Show Tax (Amendment) Act, 1972
purpose: To amend the Kerala Additional Tax on Entertainments and Surcharge on Show Tax Act, 1963.
scope: Applies to entertainments and surcharge on show tax within the state of Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Additional Tax on Entertainments and Surcharge on Show Tax (Amendment) Act, 1972.

Inserts a new section 2A into the Principal Act concerning the levy of surcharge on entertainments. It outlines that anything contained in the Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1961, and the Kerala Additional Tax on Entertainments and Surcharge on Show Tax (Amendment) Act, 1972, will have effect from the commencement of the latter Act. It also details that on each payment of admission subject to entertainment tax, a surcharge will be levied. The section specifies rates of surcharge based on the amount of entertainment tax levied, with an additional tax levied under section 2 of the Act.

Repeals the Kerala Additional Tax on Entertainments and Surcharge on Show Tax Ordinance, 1971. It also states that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act. It further clarifies that for the removal of doubts, nothing contained in sub-section (2) shall be deemed to affect the levy and collection of surcharge on entertainments under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance.

important_rules: Any payment of admission to an entertainment subject to entertainment tax shall be levied a surcharge on entertainments.
The surcharge shall be calculated at specified rates based on the amount of entertainment tax levied.
The surcharge on entertainments shall be collected in the manner laid down in section 4 and the entire proceeds shall be made over by the local authority to the Government.
The local authority shall not be entitled to any collection charges for collecting the said surcharge.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Local authority and the Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Collection of surcharge on entertainments and making over proceeds to the Government.

duties: Duty to pay surcharge on entertainments.
Duty of local authority to collect surcharge and make over proceeds to the Government.

key_procedures: Levy of surcharge on entertainments on each payment of admission.
Collection of surcharge by the local authority.
Remittance of collected surcharge proceeds to the Government.
administration: Local Authorities and the Government
important_notes: The Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 189, dated 28th March, 1972.
Anything done or action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance (Ordinance, 1971) shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.
This Act came into force on the 1st day of January, 1972 (as per section 3(2) which refers to the Ordinance coming into force on that date, implying the amended Act also takes effect from then).

title: The Kerala Additional Tax on Entertainments and Surcharge on Show Tax (Amendment) Act, 1973
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Additional Tax on Entertainments and Surcharge on Show Tax Act, 1963.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala, amending the provisions related to entertainments and surcharge on show tax.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Additional Tax on Entertainments and Surcharge on Show Tax (Amendment) Act, 1973. It came into force on the 1st day of April, 1973.
Section 2A of the Kerala Additional Tax on Entertainments and Surcharge on Show Tax Act, 1963 (22 of 1963), shall be omitted.
The Kerala Additional Tax on Entertainments and Surcharge on Show Tax (Amendment) Act, 1972 (7 of 1972), is hereby repealed.

important_notes: This Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 301 dated 1st April, 1973.

title: THE KERALA ADDITIONAL TAX ON ENTERTAINMENTS AND SURCHARGE ON SHOW TAX ACT, 1963
purpose: To provide for the levy of additional tax on entertainments and a surcharge on show tax in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to entertainments and shows in the State of Kerala.
