main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Additional Tax on Entertainments and Surcharge on Show Tax Act, 1963, and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

main_sections.section_title: Levy of additional tax on entertainments.
main_sections.description: Levies an additional tax on entertainments, notwithstanding anything contained in the Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1961 (Act 20 of 1961), with effect from the commencement of this Act on each payment of admission to any entertainment, which is subject to the levy of entertainments tax under section 3 of the said Act.

main_sections.section_title: Levy of surcharge on show tax.
main_sections.description: States that a surcharge shall be levied on every show tax which is subject to a show tax under section 125 of the Calicut City Municipal Act, 1961 (Act 14 of 1961), section 68 of the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960 (Act 14 of 1961), or subsection (5) of section 66 of the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960 (Act 32 of 1960) at the rate of twenty-five per cent of the said show tax.

main_sections.section_title: Collection and payment of additional tax and surcharge by Local Authorities.
main_sections.description: Details the collection and payment of additional tax and surcharge by Local Authorities, stating that the provisions of the Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1961, and the rules, orders, bye-laws and notifications made or issued thereunder for the time being in force, and the provisions of the Calicut City Municipal Act, 1960, the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960, and the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960, shall apply to the levy, assessment and recovery of the additional tax or show tax, and the case may be, along with such tax. It also specifies that the entire proceeds of the additional tax or surcharge collected shall be made over by the local authority to the Government after deducting two per cent of the amount collected towards collection charges.

main_sections.section_title: Surcharge to be collected to the nearest naya paisa.
main_sections.description: Specifies that the amount of surcharge payable under this Act shall be determined to the nearest naya paisa, and any fraction of a naya paisa equal to or exceeding half shall be regarded as one naya paisa, and any fraction less than half shall be disregarded.

Grants the Government the power to remove any difficulties that may arise in giving effect to the provisions of this Act by notification in the Gazette, and such orders are to appear to them to be necessary or expedient for removing the difficulty.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government, through Local Authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the levy, assessment, and recovery mechanisms established by the relevant Local Authority Acts and this Act.

duties: Local Authorities have the duty to collect and pay the additional tax and surcharge to the Government.
obligations: Operators of entertainments and shows are obligated to pay the additional tax and surcharge.

key_procedures: Levy of additional tax on all payments of admission to any entertainment, subject to the existing entertainments tax.
Levy of surcharge on show tax at 25% of the existing show tax.
Collection, assessment, and recovery of the additional tax and surcharge by Local Authorities, following their existing procedures.
Remittance of collected amounts to the Government by Local Authorities, deducting 2% for collection charges.
Rounding off surcharge amounts to the nearest naya paisa.
administration: Government of Kerala, likely through its Finance Department or a designated tax authority, and Local Authorities.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on 30th March 1963 and was published in the Gazette Extraordinary, dated 1st April 1963.

The rates of additional tax on entertainments are specified: (i) fifty naye paise, (ii) fifty naye paise, but does not exceed one rupee, and (iii) five naye paise, twenty naye paise, respectively. (Note: The document is not entirely clear on the exact breakdown of these rates as presented, but they are linked to specific conditions.)
The surcharge is levied at the rate of twenty-five per cent of the said show tax.
The Government has the power to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act by notification.

title: The Kerala Additional Tax on Lands (Repeal) Act, 1967
purpose: To repeal the Kerala Additional Tax on Lands Act, 1961.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala. The act being repealed pertains to additional tax on lands.

main_sections.description: (1) This Act may be called the Kerala Additional Tax on Lands (Repeal) Act, 1967. (2) It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 11th day of October, 1962.
The Kerala Additional Tax on Lands Act, 1961 (25 of 1961), is hereby repealed.

important_notes: Published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 114, dated 12th July, 1967.

title: THE KERALA ADVOCATES' WELFARE FUND ACT, 1980
purpose: An Act to provide for the constitution of a welfare fund for the payment of retirement benefits to advocates in the State of Kerala and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to advocates in the State of Kerala. It also concerns matters connected with the welfare fund for advocates.

key_definitions.advocate: A person whose name has been entered in the State roll of advocates prepared and maintained by the Bar Council of Kerala under section 17 of the Advocates' Act, 1961 (Central Act 25 of 1961) and who is a member of a Bar Association.
key_definitions.bar association: An association of advocates recognised and registered by the Bar Council under section 13.
key_definitions.bar council: The Bar Council of Kerala constituted under section 3 of the Advocates' Act, 1961 (Central Act 25 of 1961).
key_definitions.cessation of practice: Removal of the name of an advocate from the State roll maintained by the Bar Council on account of his retirement or death.
key_definitions.dependents: Means wife, husband, father, mother and unmarried minor children of such of them as exist.
key_definitions.fund: Means the Advocates' Welfare Fund constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.member of the fund: Means an advocate admitted to the benefit of the Fund and continuing to be a member thereof under the provisions of this Act.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by the Bar Council by rule made under this Act.
key_definitions.retirement: Means stoppage of practice as an advocate communicated to and recorded by the Bar Council.
key_definitions.stamp: Means the stamp printed and distributed under section 22.
key_definitions.suspension of practice: Means voluntary suspension of practice as an advocate or suspension by the Bar Council for misconduct.
key_definitions.trustee committee: Means the committee established under section 4.

main_sections.description: (1) This Act may be called the Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund Act, 1980. (2) It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. (3) It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Advocate', 'Bar Association', 'Bar Council', 'Cessation of Practice', 'Dependents', 'Fund', 'Member of the Fund', 'Prescribed', 'Retirement', 'Stamp', 'State', 'Suspension of Practice', and 'Trustee Committee'.

(1) The Government shall constitute a fund called the Advocates' Welfare Fund. (2) There shall be credited to the Fund: (a) all amounts paid by the Bar Council under section 12; (b) any other contribution made by the Bar Council; (c) any voluntary donation or contribution made to the Fund by the Bar Council of India, any Bar Association, any other association or institution, any advocate or any other person; (d) any grant made by the State Government to the Fund; (e) the amount set apart from the Legal Benefit Fund constituted under sub-section (2) of section 76 of the Kerala Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1959 (10 of 1960); (f) any sum borrowed from the Life Insurance Corporation of India on the death of an advocate under the Group Insurance Policy; (g) any profit or dividend received from the Life Insurance Corporation of India in respect of Policies of Group Insurance of the members of the Fund; (h) any interest or dividend or other return on any investment made of any part of the Fund; (i) all sums collected by way of sale of stamps under section 22; (j) all sums collected under section 15 by way of application fees and annual subscriptions and interest thereon.

(1) The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, establish, with effect from such date as may be specified therein, a Committee to be called the Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund Trustee Committee. (2) The Trustee Committee shall be a body corporate having perpetual succession and a common seal with power to acquire and hold property and shall, by the said name, sue and be sued. (3) The Trustee Committee shall consist of: (a) the Advocate General of Kerala, who shall be the Chairman of the Trustee Committee, ex-officio; (b) the Law Secretary to Government, ex-officio; (c) two members nominated by the Government; (d) two members of the Bar Council, nominated by it; (e) the treasurer of the Bar Council, who shall be the treasurer of the Trustee Committee, ex-officio; (f) the Secretary of the Bar Council, who shall be the Secretary of the Trustee Committee, ex-officio. (4) A member nominated by the Government under clause (c) of sub-section (3) shall hold office for a term of four years. (5) A member nominated by the Bar Council under clause (d) of sub-section (3) shall hold office for a term of four years or for the duration of his membership in the Bar Council, whichever is less.

main_sections.section_title: Disqualifications and removal of nominated members of Trustee Committee.
main_sections.description: (1) A member nominated under clause (c) or clause (d) of sub-section (4) of section 4 shall be disqualified to be a member of the Trustee Committee, if he-- (a) becomes of unsound mind; or (b) is adjudged insolvent; or (c) is absent without leave of the Trustee Committee for more than three consecutive meetings of the committee; or (d) is a defaulter to the Fund (in case he is a member of the fund) or has committed breach of trust; or (e) is convicted by a criminal court for an offence involving moral turpitude, unless such conviction has been set aside. (2) The Government may remove any member who is or has become disqualified under sub-section (1) from membership of the Trustee Committee: Provided that no order removing any member shall be passed unless that member and the Bar Council in the case of a member nominated by it have been given an opportunity of being heard.

main_sections.section_title: Resignation by nominated members of Trustee Committee and filling up of casual vacancies.
main_sections.description: (1) Any nominated member may, after giving three months' notice in writing to the Government or the Bar Council, as the case may be, and on such resignation having been accepted by the Government or the Bar Council, shall be deemed to have vacated his office. Provided that the Bar Council shall consult the Government before accepting the resignation. (2) A casual vacancy in the office of a member referred to in sub-section (1) may be filled up, as soon as may be, by the Government or the Bar Council, as the case may be, and a member so nominated to fill such vacancy shall hold office for the unexpired portion of the term of office of the member whose place he fills.

main_sections.section_title: Act of Trustee Committee not to be invalidated by vacancy, defect, etc.
main_sections.description: No act done or proceeding taken under this Act or the rules made thereunder by the Trustee Committee shall be invalidated merely by reason of-- (a) any vacancy or defect in the constitution of the committee; or (b) any defect or irregularity in the nomination of any person as a member thereof; or (c) any defect or irregularity in such act or proceeding not affecting the merits of the case.
The Fund shall vest in, and be held and applied by, the Trustee Committee subject to the provisions, and for the purposes of this Act.

(1) The Trustee Committee shall administer the Fund. (2) In the administration of the Fund, the Trustee Committee shall, subject to the provisions of this Act and the Rules made thereunder, -- (a) hold the amounts and assets belonging to the Fund in trust; (b) receive applications for admission or readmission to the Fund and dispose of such applications within ninety days from the date of receipt thereof; (c) receive applications from the members of the Fund, their nominees or legal representatives, as the case may be, for payment out of the Fund, conduct such enquiry as it deems necessary for the disposal of such applications and dispose of the applications within five months from the date of receipt thereof; (d) record in the minutes book of the Trustee Committee its decisions on the applications; (e) pay to the applicants amounts at the rates specified in the Schedule; (f) send such periodical and annual reports as may be prescribed, to the Government and the Bar Council; (g) communicate to the applicants by registered post with acknowledgement due the decisions of the Trustee Committee in respect of applications for admission or readmission to the Fund or claims to the benefit of the Fund; (h) do such other acts or are, or may be, required to be done under this Act and the rules made thereunder.

(1) The Trustee Committee may, with the prior approval of the Government and the Bar Council, borrow, from time to time, any sum required for carrying out the purposes of this Act. (2) The Trustee Committee shall deposit all moneys and receipts forming part of the Fund in any scheduled bank or invest the same in loans to any corporation owned or controlled by the Central Government or the State Government or in loans floated by the Central Government or the State Government or in any other manner as the Bar Council may, from time to time, direct with the prior approval of the Government. (3) All amounts due and payable under this Act and all expenditure relating to the management and administration of the Fund shall be paid out of the Fund. (4) The accounts of the Trustee Committee shall be audited annually by a Chartered Accountant appointed by the Bar Council. (5) The accounts of the Trustee Committee, as certified by the auditor, together with the audit report thereon, shall be forwarded to the Bar Council by the Trustee Committee and the Bar Council may issue such directions as it deems fit to the Trustee Committee in respect thereof. (6) The Trustee Committee shall comply with the directions issued by the Bar Council under sub-section (5).

main_sections.section_title: Powers and duties of Secretary -- The Secretary of the Trustee Committee shall--
main_sections.description: (a) be the chief executive authority of the Trustee Committee and responsible for carrying out its decisions; (b) represent the Trustee Committee in all suits and proceedings for and against the committee; (c) authenticate by his signature all decisions and instructions of the Trustee Committee; (d) operate the bank accounts of the Trustee Committee jointly with the Treasurer; (e) convene meetings of the Trustee Committee and prepare its minutes; (f) attend the meetings of the Trustee Committee with all the necessary records and information; (g) maintain such forms, registers and other records as may be prescribed from time to time and do all correspondence relating to the Trustee Committee; (h) inspect and verify periodically the accounts and registers of the Bar Associations regarding stamps; (i) prepare an annual statement of business transacted by the Trustee Committee during each financial year; and (j) do such other acts as may be directed by the Trustee Committee and the Bar Council.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of certain monies to the Fund.
main_sections.description: The Bar Council shall pay to the Fund annually an amount equal to twenty per cent. of the enrolment fees realised by it.

main_sections.section_title: Recognition and registration of Bar Association.
main_sections.description: (1) All associations of advocates known by any name functioning in any court centre may, before a date to be notified by the Bar Council in this behalf, apply to the Bar Council in such form as may be prescribed for recognition and registration. (2) Every application for recognition and registration shall be accompanied by the rules or bye-laws of the association, names and addresses of the office-bearers of the association and an up-to-date list of the members of the association showing the name, address, age, date of enrolment and the ordinary place of practice of each member. (3) The Bar Council may, after such enquiry as it deems necessary, recognise the association and issue a certificate of registration in such form as may be prescribed. (4) The decision of the Bar Council regarding the recognition and registration of a Bar Association shall be final.

main_sections.section_title: Duties of Bar Association.—(1) Every Bar Association shall, on or before the 15th April every year, intimate to the Bar Council a list of its members as on the 31st March of that year. (2) Every Bar Association shall intimate to the Bar Council— (a) any change of the office bearers of the association with fifteen days from such change; (b) any change in the membership including admissions and readmissions within thirty days of such change; (c) the death, retirement or voluntary suspension of practice of any of its members within thirty days from the date of occurrence thereof; and (d) such other matters as may be required by the Bar Council from time to time.

main_sections.description: (1) Every advocate practising in any court in the State and being a member of a Bar Association recognised by the Bar Council, in such form as may be prescribed, may apply to the Trustee Committee for admission as a member of the Fund, in such form as may be prescribed. (2) On receipt of an application under sub-section (1), the Trustee Committee shall make such enquiry as it deems fit and either admit the applicant to the Fund or for reasons to be recorded in writing reject the application: Provided that no order rejecting an application shall be passed unless the applicant has been given an opportunity of being heard. (3) Every applicant shall pay an application fee of two hundred rupees in the course of one year equal instalments, in such manner as may be prescribed, the first instalment being payable along with the application, to the account of the Trustee Committee. (4) In the event of rejection of the application, the first instalment of the admission fee paid along with the application shall be refunded to the applicant. (5) Every member shall pay an annual subscription to the Fund on or before the 30th June of every year at the following rates, namely:— When the standing of the Advocate at the Bar is five years or more, but less than fifteen years,— rupees fifty. Where the standing of the Advocate at the Bar is fifteen years or more— one hundred rupees. (6) A member shall be entitled to pay the subscription under sub-section (5) in two equal half yearly instalments at his option. (7) Any member who fails to remit the annual subscription for an year before the 30th June of that year shall be liable to be removed from the membership of the Fund (8) A person removed from the membership of the Fund under sub-section (7) shall be readmitted to the Fund on payment of the arrears with interest at twelve per cent per annum within six months from the date of removal. (9) Every member shall, at the time of admission to the membership of the Fund make a nomination conferring on one or more persons the right to receive the amount which may be due to him from the Fund in the event of his death before the amount has been paid to him. (10) If a member nominates more than one person under sub-section (9) he shall specify in the nomination the amount or share payable to each of the nominees in such manner as to cover the whole of the amount that may be due to him.

important_rules: Every advocate practising in any court in the State and being a member of a Bar Association recognised by the Bar Council may apply to the Trustee Committee for admission as a member of the Fund.
Every applicant shall pay an application fee of two hundred rupees in equal instalments.
Every member shall pay an annual subscription to the Fund on or before the 30th June of every year.
The annual subscription rates vary based on the standing of the Advocate at the Bar (five years or more, but less than fifteen years: fifty rupees; fifteen years or more: one hundred rupees).
A member can pay the subscription in two equal half-yearly instalments.
Members who fail to remit the annual subscription by the due date are liable to be removed from membership.
Readmission to the Fund is possible upon payment of arrears with interest within six months of removal.
Members must make a nomination conferring the right to receive amounts due in case of death.

penalties: Removal from membership of the Fund for failure to remit annual subscription by the due date.
Interest at twelve per cent per annum on arrears for readmission.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Trustee Committee, Bar Council, Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through administrative actions like removal from membership, acceptance of applications for admission/readmission, collection of fees and subscriptions, and the power of the Bar Council to issue directions to the Trustee Committee.

rights: Right to apply for admission to the Fund.
Right to receive retirement benefits from the Fund.
Right to nominate persons to receive amounts due in case of death.
Right to be readmitted to the Fund upon payment of arrears and interest if removed.
duties: Duty to pay application fee.
Duty to pay annual subscription.
Duty to inform the Bar Council of changes in membership (for Bar Associations).
Duty of the Trustee Committee to administer the Fund, receive and dispose of applications, and manage funds.
Duty of the Secretary of the Trustee Committee to act as chief executive authority, represent the committee, and operate bank accounts.
Duty of the Bar Council to recognize and register Bar Associations and issue directions to the Trustee Committee.
obligations: Nomination of beneficiaries for amounts due upon death.

key_procedures: Application for admission to the Fund: An advocate submits an application to the Trustee Committee, pays an application fee in instalments, and the committee may admit or reject the application after inquiry.
Payment of annual subscription: Members pay annual subscriptions by June 30th each year. Failure to do so can lead to removal.
Nomination for death benefits: Members make nominations for beneficiaries to receive amounts due upon their death.
Recognition and registration of Bar Associations: Associations apply to the Bar Council with required documents, and the Council conducts an inquiry before granting recognition.
Reporting by Bar Associations: Associations must annually intimate membership lists and report changes in office bearers and membership to the Bar Council.
administration: The Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund Trustee Committee administers the Fund. The Advocate General of Kerala is the ex-officio Chairman of the Trustee Committee. The Secretary of the Trustee Committee is the chief executive authority.
important_notes: The Act distinguishes between 'retirement' and 'suspension of practice'.
The Trustee Committee is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
The Bar Council has oversight and can issue directions to the Trustee Committee.
The Act outlines specific criteria for disqualification and removal of nominated members of the Trustee Committee.
There are specific timelines for the Trustee Committee to process applications (ninety days for admission/readmission, five months for payment out of the Fund).

title: The Kerala Advocates Clerks Welfare Fund Act, 2003
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a Welfare Fund for the benefit of Advocates' Clerks in the State of Kerala.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala and to all Advocates' Clerks within the State.

key_definitions.Advocates' Clerks: A person employed by an advocate as a clerk, typist, driver, or any other capacity in connection with his professional work. It includes persons who were formerly employed as Advocates' Clerks.
key_definitions.Welfare Fund: The Kerala Advocates' Clerks Welfare Fund constituted under the Act.
key_definitions.Prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and its commencement.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Advocates' Clerks', 'Welfare Fund', and 'Prescribed'.
Establishes the Kerala Advocates' Clerks Welfare Fund and specifies its sources of income, including contributions from advocates and clerks, grants, and donations.
Deals with the management and administration of the Welfare Fund by a Board of Trustees.
Specifies how the moneys in the Welfare Fund shall be invested.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and duties of the Board of Trustees
main_sections.description: Outlines the powers and duties of the Board of Trustees in managing and operating the Welfare Fund.

main_sections.section_title: Schemes for the benefit of Advocates' Clerks
main_sections.description: Empowers the Board of Trustees to frame schemes for the welfare of Advocates' Clerks, such as financial assistance, medical aid, and other benefits.
Details the mandatory contributions to the Welfare Fund by advocates and clerks.
Grants the government the power to exempt certain persons or classes of persons from the provisions of the Act or the contributions to the Fund.
Provides for the imposition of penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Every advocate shall, on or before such date as may be prescribed, contribute to the Welfare Fund a sum of money at such rate as may be prescribed.
Every Advocates' Clerk shall, on or before such date as may be prescribed, contribute to the Welfare Fund a sum of money at such rate as may be prescribed.
The Board of Trustees shall meet at least once in every quarter to consider the accounts of the Fund and the schemes for the benefit of Advocates' Clerks.

penalties: Failure to make contributions may result in penalties as prescribed.
Contravention of other provisions of the Act may lead to penalties.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Board of Trustees and the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the imposition of penalties, collection of contributions, and implementation of welfare schemes.

rights: Advocates' Clerks have the right to benefit from the welfare schemes formulated by the Board of Trustees.
duties: Advocates have the duty to contribute to the Welfare Fund.
Advocates' Clerks have the duty to contribute to the Welfare Fund.
The Board of Trustees has the duty to manage and administer the Welfare Fund efficiently and to frame welfare schemes.
obligations: Obligation of advocates to ensure their clerks are covered under the welfare scheme.

key_procedures: Procedure for contribution to the Welfare Fund by advocates and clerks.
Procedure for framing and implementing welfare schemes for Advocates' Clerks by the Board of Trustees.
Procedure for the management and investment of the Welfare Fund.
administration: The Kerala Advocates' Clerks Welfare Fund Board of Trustees.
important_notes: The Act aims to ensure the social and economic security of Advocates' Clerks.
The Act empowers the State Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

title: THE KERALA ADVOCATES' CLERKS WELFARE FUND ACT, 2003
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a Welfare Fund for the benefit of Advocates' Clerks in the State of Kerala and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Advocates' Clerks in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Advocate: A person whose name has been entered in the State Roll of Advocates, prepared and maintained by the Bar Council of Kerala under section 17 of the Advocates Act, 1961 (Central Act 25 of 1961) and practising as an Advocate, whether he is a Member of a Bar Association or not.
key_definitions.Advocates' Clerk: A Clerk employed by an Advocate and recognised as such by such Authority and in such manner as may be prescribed and who is a member of an Advocates' Clerks Association.
key_definitions.Advocates' Clerks Association: An association of Advocates' Clerks recognised and registered under section 15.
key_definitions.Member of the Fund: An Advocate's Clerk admitted to the fund and continuing to be a member thereof by paying the subscriptions under the provisions of this Act.
key_definitions.Notification: A notification published in the Kerala Gazette and the word "Notified" shall be construed accordingly.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.retirement: Stoppage of employment as Advocate Clerk for reasons other than for joining service or for carrying on any other gainful occupation communicated to and recorded in the manner prescribed.
key_definitions.stamp: Kerala Advocates' Clerks Welfare Fund Stamp printed and distributed under section 14.
key_definitions.vakalathnama: A vakalathnama, memorandum of appearance or any other document by which an advocate is empowered to appear and plead before any court, tribunal or authority.

main_sections.description:
(1) This Act may be called the Kerala Advocates' Clerks Welfare Fund Act, 2003.
(2) It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires, definitions for "Advocate", "Advocates' Clerk", "Advocates' Clerks Association", "Government", "Member of the Fund", "Notification", "prescribed", "retirement", "Secretary", "stamp", and "vakalathnama" are provided.

main_sections.section_title: Disqualification and removal of nominated members of the Committee
main_sections.description:
A member nominated under clause (e) of sub-section (3) of section 4 shall be disqualified to be a member of the Committee and shall cease to be such member, if he, —
(a) becomes of unsound mind, or
(b) is adjudged as insolvent, or
(c) is absent without leave of the Committee for more than three consecutive meetings of the Committee.
Provided that the member ceasing to hold office under this clause may be restored by the Committee, if such member makes an application for the condonation of his absence and the Committee is satisfied that there was sufficient cause for such absence, or
(d) is a perpetual defaulter to the Fund (in case he is a member of the Fund) or has committed breach of trust, or
(e) is convicted by a criminal court for an offence involving moral turpitude, unless such conviction has been set aside on appeal.

main_sections.section_title: Resignation by nominated member of the Committee and filling up of casual vacancies.
main_sections.description:
(1) Any member nominated under clause (e) of sub-section (3) of section 4 may resign his office by giving one month notice in writing to the Chairman of the Committee and from the date of acceptance of resignation by the Chairman, he shall be deemed to have vacated his office 34/2258/04/DTP.
(2) Any casual vacancy in the office of a member referred to in sub-section (1) shall be filled up, as soon as may be and a member so nominated to fill such vacancy shall hold office only for the remaining portion of the term of his predecessor.

(1) The Committee shall meet at least once in three months or more often, if found necessary, to transact its business.
(2) Four members of the Committee shall form the quorum for a meeting of the Committee.
(3) The Chairman or in his absence, a member elected by the Members present at the meeting, shall preside over a meeting of the Committee.
(4) Any matter coming up before a meeting of the Committee shall be decided by a majority of the members present and voting at the meeting and, in the case of any equality of votes, the Chairman or the member presiding over the meeting shall have and exercise a casting vote.

main_sections.section_title: Travelling and daily allowance to members of Committee.
main_sections.description: The members of the Committee shall be eligible to get such travelling allowance and daily allowance as may be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Act of Committee not to be invalidated by defect etc
main_sections.description:
No act done or proceedings taken under this Act or the rules made thereunder by the Committee shall be invalidated merely by reason of, —
(a) any vacancy or defect in the constitution of the Committee; or
(b) any defect or irregularity in the election of any person as a member thereof; or
(c) any defect or irregularity in such act or proceedings not affecting the merits of the case.

The Fund shall vest in and be held by the Committee in such manner as may be prescribed and used, subject to the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder, only for the purposes of granting pension benefits and other benefits.

(1) The Committee, may, with the prior approval of the Government, borrow from time to time any sum required for carrying out the purposes of this Act.
(2) The Committee shall deposit all moneys and receipts forming part of the Fund in the Treasury Accounts or in any Scheduled Banks as defined in the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (Central Act 2 of 1934) or invest the same in loans to any corporation owned or controlled by the Central Government or the State Government or in loans floated by the Central Government or State Government, with the approval of the Government or in any other manner as may be prescribed.
(3) All amounts due and payable under this Act and all expenditure relating to the management and administration of the Fund shall be paid out of the Fund.
(4) The accounts of the Committee shall be audited annually by a Chartered Accountant appointed by the Committee, with the prior approval of the Government.
(5) The accounts as certified by the auditor together with the audit report thereon shall be forwarded to the Government by the Committee and the Government may issue such directions as it deems fit to the Committee in respect thereof and shall place such accounts and the audit report thereon before the Legislative Assembly.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment, powers and duties of Secretary.
Kerala Advocates' Clerks Welfare Fund Stamp.
main_sections.description:
(1) There shall be printed at the Government Press by the Committee in such form and in such manner as may be prescribed stamps of the value of two rupees inscribed as "the Kerala Advocates' Clerks Welfare Fund Stamp".
(2) Every Vakalath filed before any court, authority or tribunal shall be affixed with a stamp as specified in sub-section (1), in addition to the court fee stamps, if any, and the stamps to be affixed under any other Act and no Vakalath shall be valid unless it is so stamped.
Provided that this sub-section shall not apply to any Vakalath filed on behalf of the Central or State Government.
(3) Every stamp affixed in Vakalaths filed before any court, tribunal or other authority shall be cancelled in the manner provided in the Kerala Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1959 (10 of 1960).
(4) The custody of the stamps printed under this section shall be with the Committee and, the supply and sale of stamps shall be in such manner as may be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Recognition and Registration of Advocates' Clerks Association
main_sections.description:
(1) All association of Advocates' Clerks functioning on the date of commencement of this Act, in any court headquarters may, before a date to be notified by Committee in this behalf apply to the Committee in such form and in such manner as may be prescribed, for recognition and registration as an Advocates' Clerk Association under this Act and any association of Advocates' Clerks constituted after the commencement of this Act may apply for such registration within three months from the date of its constitution.
(2) Every application for recognition and registration shall be accompanied by the rules or bye laws of the association, name and address of the office bearers of the association, and an up-to-date list of the members of the association with name, address and the ordinary place of employment of such member.
(3) The Committee may, after such inquiry as it deems necessary recognise the Association as an Advocates' Clerks Association and issue a certificate of recognition and registration in such form as may be prescribed.
(4) The decision of the Committee regarding the recognition and registration of an Association shall be final.

(1) Every Advocates' Clerks Association shall, on or before 15th April of every year, intimate to the Committee a list of the members as on 31st March of that year.
(2) Every Advocates' Clerks Association shall intimate in writing to the Committee of,—
(a) any change of the office bearers of the Advocates' Clerks Association within fifteen days from such change,
(b) any change in number of members including admission and re-admission within thirty days of such changes,
(c) the death or retirement of any of its members within thirty days from the date of occurrence thereof, and

important_rules: Advocates' Clerks must pay subscriptions to be a member of the Fund.
Vakalath filed before any court, authority or tribunal must have a stamp of the value of two rupees inscribed as "the Kerala Advocates' Clerks Welfare Fund Stamp".
Advocates' Clerks Associations must intimate the list of members annually to the Committee.
Advocates' Clerks Associations must intimate changes in office bearers, membership, death or retirement of members to the Committee.
The Committee shall meet at least once in three months or more often, if found necessary, to transact its business.
Four members of the Committee shall form the quorum for a meeting.
The Committee shall deposit all moneys and receipts forming part of the Fund in Treasury Accounts or in Scheduled Banks or invest in loans to corporations or government, as may be prescribed.
The Committee may borrow from time to time any sum required for carrying out the purposes of this Act, with the prior approval of the Government.
The Committee may delegate any of its functions to the Secretary or any other officer appointed by the Government.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Committee (implied from sections on functions and administration).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the functions of the Committee as outlined in Section 11, including receiving applications, paying benefits, controlling and supervising the scheme, and maintaining accounts and reports. Enforcement of stamp usage is also implied.

rights: Right to receive pension benefits and other benefits from the Fund (implied from Section 10).
duties: Duty to pay subscriptions to be a member of the Fund.
Duty to affix the Kerala Advocates' Clerks Welfare Fund Stamp on Vakalaths.
Duty of Advocates' Clerks Associations to intimate member lists and changes to the Committee.
Duty of the Committee to administer the Fund, process applications, pay benefits, and maintain accounts.
Duty of the Government to establish the Fund and the Committee, and to oversee the administration.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder.

key_procedures: Application for recognition and registration of Advocates' Clerks Associations: Associations must apply in the prescribed form with rules, bye-laws, office bearer details, and member lists. The Committee will inquire and issue a certificate.

Intimation of changes by Advocates' Clerks Associations: Associations must notify the Committee of changes in office bearers, membership numbers, or member deaths/retirements within specified timeframes.
Meeting procedures of the Committee: Meetings require a quorum of four members, chaired by the Chairman or an elected member, with decisions made by majority vote.
Application for Fund benefits: Members (or their nominees/representatives) can apply for benefits, and the Committee will conduct an inquiry and dispose of applications.
Annual audit of accounts: The Committee's accounts are audited annually by a Chartered Accountant, with reports forwarded to the Government.
Printing and sale of stamps: Stamps of a specified value are printed by the Government Press and sold by the Committee.
administration: The Government of Kerala (for establishment of the Fund and Committee) and the Kerala Advocates' Clerks Welfare Fund Committee (for administration of the Fund and Scheme).
important_notes: The Act is a translation from Malayalam and was published under the authority of the Governor.
The Act came into force on a date appointed by the Government by notification in the Gazette.
The Act does not apply to Vakalaths filed on behalf of the Central or State Government regarding stamp duty.
Stamp affixed in Vakalaths must be cancelled as provided in the Kerala Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1959.
The Committee has the power to borrow funds with the prior approval of the Government.
The Government may issue directions to the Committee regarding the accounts and audit report.

title: The Kerala Advocates Clerks Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2013
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Advocates' Clerks Welfare Fund Act, 2003.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Advocates' Clerks Welfare Fund Act, 2003.

key_definitions.principal Act: The Kerala Advocates' Clerks Welfare Fund Act, 2003 (27 of 2003).

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Advocates' Clerks Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2013. Section 2 of this Act shall be deemed to have come into force on the 15th day of January, 2013, Section 3 shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 2004, Section 4 shall be deemed to have come into force on the 26th day of November, 2010, Section 5 shall be deemed to have come into force on the 18th day of November, 2011, Section 6 shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 2012 and the remaining provisions shall be deemed to have come into force on the 13th day of August, 2012.
In the Kerala Advocates' Clerks Welfare Fund Act, 2003 (27 of 2003), in sub-section (1) of section 14 for the words "value of six rupees" the words "value of twelve rupees" shall be substituted.

In section 17 of the principal Act, in sub-section (5), the following sub-sections shall be substituted, namely:-
(5) Every member of the Fund shall pay to the Fund an annual subscription of one thousand two hundred rupees and if it is paid in lump sum, shall be paid on or before 30th June of every year and, if not, shall be paid in three equal instalments on or before 30th June, 30th September and 31st December respectively: Provided that the members who fail to remit the annual subscription in lump sum or in instalments within the specified time limit as aforesaid, shall remit such arrears with interest at twelve per cent to aforestated 31st December.
(5A) Every existing member shall remit the arrears of the annual subscription due for the period from the 1st day of April, 2004 to the 26th day of November, 2010, the date on which the Kerala Advocates' Clerks Welfare Fund (Amendment) Ordinance, 2010 (57 of 2010), was published in the gazette in three equal instalments, before 31st December, 2010, 30th June, 2011 and 31st December, 2011, respectively: Provided that those who fail to remit any instalment on 31st December, 2011 shall remit such arrears with twelve per cent interest in equal instalments not exceeding six before 30th September, 2012.
(ii) in sub-section (6) for the words and figures "before 30th June" the words and figures "before 31st December" shall be substituted.

In section 18 of the principal Act, after sub-section (6), the following sub-section shall be inserted, namely:-
"(7) A member whose membership has ceased and received pension and other benefits shall not be eligible for re-admission in the Fund."

In section 26 of the principal Act, the existing section shall be numbered as sub-section (1) of that section and after sub-section (1) so numbered, the following sub-section shall be inserted, namely:-
"(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in the Kerala Advocates' Clerks Welfare Fund Scheme, 1985, all kinds of assets and liabilities of the said scheme shall be transferred to the Committee constituted under section 4 of this Act."
In section 27 of the principal Act, for the words "twenty per cent" the words "thirty per cent" shall be substituted.

(1) The Kerala Advocates' Clerks Welfare Fund (Amendment) Ordinance, 2013 (15 of 2013) is hereby repealed.
(2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Every member of the Fund shall pay an annual subscription of one thousand two hundred rupees.
Annual subscription can be paid in a lump sum or in three equal installments.
Members failing to remit dues must pay arrears with interest at twelve per cent.
Existing members must remit arrears of annual subscription due for the period from April 1, 2004, to November 26, 2010, in three equal installments before December 31, 2011.
Those failing to remit any installment on December 31, 2011, shall remit arrears with twelve per cent interest in equal installments not exceeding six before September 30, 2012.
Members whose membership has ceased and received pension and other benefits are not eligible for re-admission in the Fund.
All assets and liabilities of the Kerala Advocates' Clerks Welfare Fund Scheme, 1985, shall be transferred to the Committee constituted under section 4 of this Act.
The Kerala Advocates' Clerks Welfare Fund (Amendment) Ordinance, 2013 (15 of 2013) is repealed.

penalties: Interest at twelve per cent on delayed payments of annual subscription.
Interest at twelve per cent on arrears of annual subscription for the period April 1, 2004, to November 26, 2010.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Committee constituted under section 4 of the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions and procedures outlined in the Act and its amendments.

rights: Right to pension and other benefits for eligible members.
duties: Duty to pay annual subscription to the Fund.
Duty to pay arrears of subscription with interest if payment is delayed.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the rules regarding payment of subscriptions and arrears.

key_procedures: Payment of annual subscription: Either in a lump sum or in three equal installments on or before June 30, September 30, and December 31.

Remittance of arrears: For the period April 1, 2004, to November 26, 2010, in three equal installments before December 31, 2011. For delayed installments on December 31, 2011, with 12% interest in equal installments not exceeding six before September 30, 2012.
Transfer of assets and liabilities: All assets and liabilities of the 1985 Scheme are transferred to the Committee.
administration: The Committee constituted under section 4 of the Act.
important_notes: The Act further amends the Kerala Advocates' Clerks Welfare Fund Act, 2003.
Different sections of the Act came into force on different dates.
Substitution of monetary values in Section 14.
Specific provisions for the payment of annual subscription and arrears with interest.
Certain members are ineligible for re-admission.
Repeal of the Kerala Advocates' Clerks Welfare Fund (Amendment) Ordinance, 2013, with savings clause.

title: The Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 1993
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund Act, 1980, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to advocates practicing in Kerala. The amendments pertain to contributions to the Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund and the schedule of contributions based on years of practice.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 1993. It shall come into force at once.

Amends section 15 of the Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund Act, 1980, by substituting the amounts for 'rupees two hundred' and 'rupees three hundred' with 'rupees fifty rupees' and 'one hundred rupees' and 'two hundred rupees' respectively.

Amends section 16 of the principal Act. It substitutes the words 'every four years of practice at the Bar' with 'every two years of practice at the Bar' and further substitutes the words 'two thousand rupees per year of practice' with 'three thousand one hundred and twenty-five rupees per year of practice'. It also updates the figures relating to contributions based on practice years from May 6, 1989, and the date of commencement of this Act.

Substitutes the existing Schedule to the principal Act with a new Schedule. This new Schedule details the contribution amounts for advocates based on their years of practice, ranging from 5 years to 32 years.

important_rules: Rule 1: Contributions to the Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund have been revised based on the years of practice.
Rule 2: The schedule of contributions is updated as per the new schedule introduced by this amendment.
Rule 3: The revised contribution amounts are effective from May 6, 1989, and also from the date of commencement of this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but likely the Bar Council or a designated authority under the principal Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text.

duties: Advocates have a duty to contribute to the Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund as per the revised schedule.

key_procedures: The primary procedure affected is the calculation and payment of contributions to the Advocates' Welfare Fund by advocates based on their years of practice, as outlined in the substituted Schedule.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but likely the Kerala Bar Council or a related governmental body.
important_notes: The Governor of Kerala received the assent to this Act on the 3rd day of March, 1993.
The Act was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 233 dated the 3rd March, 1993.
The amendments to section 16 regarding contributions are effective from May 6, 1989, and also from the date of commencement of this Act for contributions made thereafter.

title: The Kerala Advocates Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 1986
purpose: To amend the Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund Act, 1980.
scope: Applies to advocates in Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 1986. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 5th day of April, 1981.

To sub-section (1) of section 23 of the Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund Act, 1980 (21 of 1980) (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), the following proviso shall be added, namely: 'Provided that nothing contained in this sub-section shall apply in respect of any memorandum of appearance filed by an advocate appearing on behalf of the Government.'

(1) The Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Ordinance, 1986 (61 of 1986), is hereby repealed.
(2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 30th day of November, 1986 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 1081 dated 30th November, 1986.

title: The Kerala Advocates Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2010
purpose: This act amends the Kerala Advocates Welfare Fund Act, 1980, to bring about changes and updates to the existing provisions regarding the Advocates Welfare Fund.
scope: The Act applies to advocates in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.advocate: Carries on the profession of an Advocate and filing of at least 5 vakalath per year in cases of Advocates other than Senior Advocates, under the Advocates Act, 1961 (Central Act 25 of 1961).
key_definitions.permanent disablement: Means such physical or mental disablement which totally incapacitates an Advocate to continue his professional practice for ever.
key_definitions.bar association: Shall have such certificate of recommendations as mentioned in sub-section (5) of section 15 to its members on request made to that effect.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2010, and it would come into force on the date of its publication.
This section amends section 2 of the principal Act by inserting new clauses and modifying existing ones, particularly concerning the definitions of 'actual practice' and 'permanent disablement'.
This section amends section 3 of the principal Act, likely related to the constitution or management of the Fund, by inserting new sub-sections.
This section amends section 9 of the principal Act, regarding the subscription to the Fund. It specifies annual subscription rates based on the standing of the Advocate at the Bar.
This section amends section 11 of the principal Act, regarding applications for membership in the Fund.
This section amends section 14 of the principal Act, regarding the benefits from the Fund.
This section amends section 15 of the principal Act, concerning the issuance of certificates of recommendations.
This section amends section 16 of the principal Act, relating to cessation of practice and entitlement to benefits from the Fund.
This section amends section 18 of the principal Act, likely pertaining to the 'Bar Council' and 'Trustee Committee'.
This section amends section 22 of the principal Act, concerning 'Bar Associations' and their 'outlets'.
This section amends section 23 of the principal Act, likely concerning who is a member of the Fund and provisions related to fees.

This section repeals the Kerala Advocates Welfare Fund (Amendment) Ordinance, 2010, and states that anything done or any action taken under the Ordinance would be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Advocates engaged in full-time employment in the Central or State Government or any Public or Private Sector Undertaking are not admitted as members of the Fund or permitted to resume membership in the Fund.

An Advocate whose membership has ceased due to resignation from practice or cessation of practice before attaining the age of sixty years, shall be eligible for refund of the annual subscription paid.
Payment of refund of the annual amount of rupees one lakh in aggregate or at the rate specified in sub-section (1) whichever is higher, is applicable in certain cases.
In the event of death of a member while in actual practice, his nominee or heir is entitled to receive from and out of the Fund an amount of five lakh rupees.

Every member shall pay an annual subscription to the Fund on or before the 30th June of every year at the following rates: Three hundred rupees (if Bar is less than five years), Seven hundred rupees (if Bar is between five and ten years), One thousand rupees (if Bar is between ten and fifteen years), Two thousand rupees (if Bar is between fifteen and twenty years), Two thousand five hundred rupees (if Bar is between twenty and twenty-five years), Three thousand rupees (if Bar is above twenty-five years).

penalties: No specific penalties are detailed in the provided text for violations, but clause (iv) of Section 12 mentions that any person found responsible for causing loss to the Fund may be held liable for making good such loss.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Act implies enforcement by the Bar Council and the Trustee Committee, and potentially the government. Section 12 also mentions "Court, Tribunal or other Authority".
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Actions related to membership, subscriptions, benefits, and recovery of losses to the Fund are implied as methods of enforcement.

rights: Right to receive welfare benefits from the Fund upon fulfilling the conditions.
Right to be issued certificates of recommendations by the Bar Association.
Right to claim refund of subscriptions under specific circumstances.
Right for nominees/heirs to receive death benefits.
duties: Duty to pay annual subscription to the Fund.
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules.
Duty of the Bar Association to provide recommendations and process applications.
obligations: Obligation to continue professional practice for a certain period to be eligible for certain benefits.
Obligation to not claim benefits if not a member in good standing.

key_procedures: Application for membership in the Fund by an advocate, including submission of required documents and recommendations.
Payment of annual subscription to the Fund by the due date.
Application for benefits from the Fund, including retirement and disability benefits.
Procedure for refund of subscriptions under specific conditions.
Procedure for obtaining certificates of recommendations from the Bar Association.
Procedure for claiming death benefits by nominees or heirs.
administration: The Act implies administration by the Kerala State Legislature, with involvement of the Bar Council, Trustee Committee, and Bar Associations. The Law (Legislation F) Department of the Government of Kerala is indicated as the issuing authority for notifications.
important_notes: The amendment comes into force upon publication in the Gazette.
Advocates in full-time employment with Government or Public/Private Sector Undertakings are not eligible for membership.
Specific rates of annual subscription are prescribed based on the number of years of standing at the Bar.
The Kerala Advocates Welfare Fund (Amendment) Ordinance, 2010, is repealed and replaced by this Act.
Actions taken under the Ordinance are deemed valid under the Act.

title: THE KERALA ADVOCATES' WELFARE FUND (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1995
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund Act, 1980.
scope: Applies to advocates in Kerala.

key_definitions.cessation of practice: means removal of the name of an advocate from the State roll maintained by the Bar Council on account of his retirement or death and includes any disqualification of a member to practise in the State under article 220 of the Constitution of India or any other law for the time being in force.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 1995. Clause (ii) of section 5 shall be deemed to have come into force on the 20th day of April, 1981 and the remaining provisions of this Act shall come into force at once.

Amends section 2 of the Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund Act, 1980. It substitutes the words "and who is a member of a Bar Association" for "and who is a member of a Bar Association" and also substitutes clause (d) with a definition of 'cessation of practice'.

In sub-section (2) of section 9 of the principal Act, after sub-clause (b), a new sub-clause (bb) is inserted to remove a member from the fund for contravention of any of the provisions of this Act or the rules framed thereunder after giving the member concerned an opportunity of being heard.

In section 15 of the Principal Act, in sub-section (5), "one hundred rupees" and "two hundred rupees" are substituted with "one hundred rupees" and "two hundred rupees" respectively. Also, in sub-section (5), the following proviso is added: "Provided that an advocate designed as senior Advocate an annual subscription to the fund at the rate of one thousand and five hundred rupees before the 30th June of every year" and sub-section (6) shall be omitted. Sub-sections (7) and (8) are also substituted, namely: "(7) A member who fails to remit the annual subscription for a year on or before the 30th June of that year may, within a period of six months from the said date, remit the amount in arrears together with fine at the rate of five rupees per month or part thereof. (8) Where a member fails to remit the annual subscription together with fine within the period specified in sub-section (7), the Trustee Committee shall issue a notice to such member by registered post in the address as entered in the register of members of the Fund directing him to show cause, if any, why he should not be removed from the membership of the Fund for non-payment of the subscription. Where the defaulter, within one month from the date of such notice, furnishes sufficient cause to the satisfaction of the Trustee Committee for the non-payment and also remits the entire arrears of subscription together with fine till the date of payment and notice charge, the Trustee Committee may abstain from taking or proceeding with any action against him in respect of such non-payment and in other cases, the Trustee Committee shall remove the defaulter from the membership of the Fund. (8A) Notwithstanding anything contained in the foregoing provisions of this section, where, on receipt of a complaint or otherwise, the Trustee Committee is satisfied after such enquiry as they may think fit, that a member has voluntarily suspended practice or ceased to practice without intimation to the Trustee Committee, or has become disqualifi ed to practice under any law for the time being in force, they may, after giving such member a reasonable opportunity of showing cause against the proposed action and after considering the cause, if any, shown, remove him from the membership of the Fund."

In the principal Act, in section 16, namely:- "Provided that a member removed under sub-section (8) or sub-section (8A) of section 15 or a member who has not continued his membership of the Fund at least for five years shall be entitled, on cessation of practice:- (a) after the commencement of Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 1995, to fifty percentage of the amount at the rate of three thousand and one hundred and twenty-five rupees calculated for every completed year of practice; and (b) before the commencement of the said Act, to fifty percentage of the amount at the rate specified in sub-section (1A) calculated for every completed year of practice." Also, sub-section (1) is inserted: "(1A) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1) or in any judgment, decree or order of any court, tribunal or other authority, a member on cessation of his practice on or before the 2nd day of March, 1993 shall be entitled to receive from out of the Fund an amount calculated at the rate of one thousand rupees for every completed year of practice for the period up to 5th May, 1989 and at the rate of two thousand rupees for every completed year of practice for the remaining period." Sub-section (4) is substituted: "(4) For calculating the period of completed year of practice for the purpose of payment:- (i) under sub-section (1), every two years of practice at the bar, and (ii) under sub-section (1A), every four years of practice at the bar before the admission of a member to the Fund shall be computed as one year of practice and added on to the number of years of practice after such admission: Provided that in computing the period of practice, the period of suspension of practice, either voluntary or otherwise, shall be excluded." Further it is provided that in the case of a person who resumes practice after being in government service or in any other employment, the period of practice counted for retirement benefit or other service benefits therein, if any, shall not be taken into account. Also, it is provided that in the case of a person who does not apply to become a member of the Fund within six months from the commencement of the Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 1995 or within six months of his enrolment as Advocate, as the case may be, the period of practice, if any, before admission of such person to the Fund shall not be taken into account.
In the principal Act, for the words "Three members", the words "Five members" are substituted.

In sub-section (1) of section 22, the words "two rupees", the words "five rupees and ten rupees" shall be substituted. In sub-section (2), the following sub-section shall be substituted, namely:- "(2) The stamps shall be of such size and colour as may be decided by the Bar Council from time to time".

In section 23 of the Principal Act, for sub-section (1), the following sub-section shall be substituted, namely:- "(1) Every vakalath filed by an advocate shall, in addition to the court fee stamps affixed there on, be stamped with the welfare fund stamp of value of ten rupees in the case of vakalath filed before High Court and of the value of five rupees in the case of vakalath filed before subordinate courts, tribunals or other authorities, and no vakalath shall be valid unless it is so stamped": Provided that nothing contained in this sub-section shall apply in respect of any memorandum of appearance filed by an advocate appearing on behalf of the Government. Explanation.—If three or more advocates jointly appear by a single vakalath, the maximum number of stamps that may be affixed thereon shall be three".

important_rules: Advocates must pay an annual subscription to the fund.
Members who fail to remit the annual subscription within the specified period will be subject to fine and potential removal from the fund.
The Trustee Committee is empowered to issue notices and take action against members for non-payment of subscriptions.
Members who voluntarily suspend practice or are disqualified may be removed from the fund.
Specific provisions exist for calculating completed years of practice for payment purposes.
Vakalath filed by an advocate must be stamped with welfare fund stamps of a specified value.

penalties: Fine for delayed subscription remittance at the rate of five rupees per month or part thereof.
Removal from membership of the Fund for non-payment of subscription after due notice and opportunity to show cause.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Trustee Committee
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Issuance of notices, conducting enquiries, and removal from membership.

rights: Right to receive benefits from the fund upon cessation of practice, subject to eligibility criteria and calculated based on years of practice.
Right to an opportunity of being heard before removal from the fund.
Right to have a vakalath considered valid only if stamped with the welfare fund stamp.
duties: Duty to pay annual subscription to the fund.
Duty to remit subscription arrears with fine within the stipulated period.
Duty to inform the Trustee Committee about voluntary suspension of practice or disqualification.
Duty to ensure vakalath filings are properly stamped.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act and the rules framed thereunder.

key_procedures: Remittance of annual subscription by members of the fund by 30th June each year.
Procedure for members who fail to remit subscription: remittance of amount in arrears with fine within six months of the due date.
Procedure for the Trustee Committee to issue notices to defaulters and take action for non-payment.
Procedure for applying for benefits from the fund upon cessation of practice.
Procedure for stamping vakalath filings with welfare fund stamps.
administration: The Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund Act, 1980 (as amended) is administered by the relevant authorities under the Act, likely involving the Bar Council and a Trustee Committee.
important_notes: Certain provisions of this Act came into force on the 20th day of April, 1981.
The Act specifies different rates for annual subscription and benefits based on the period of practice and commencement of the Amendment Act.
Special provisions exist for calculating the period of practice, excluding periods of suspension.
The Act clarifies circumstances under which persons resuming practice or those who do not apply for membership within a certain period are treated.
An explanation is provided regarding the maximum number of stamps for joint vakalath appearances.

title: The Kerala Advocates Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2001
purpose: An Act to further amend the Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund Act, 1980.
scope: Applies to advocates in Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2001. It came into force at once and the remaining provisions of this Act shall be deemed to have come into force on the 22nd day of November, 2000.

Amends section 15 of the Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund Act, 1980 (21 of 1980) regarding annual subscription to the Fund. It specifies the subscription rates based on the standing of the advocate at the Bar, ranging from less than five years to fifteen years and more. It also includes a provision for advocates designated as Senior Advocates.

Inserts a new sub-section (2A) in Section 16 of the principal Act. This sub-section addresses the event of death of a member while in active practice and before attaining the age of fifty-five years, where there is no surviving legal heir. In such cases, the nominee is entitled to receive from the Fund an amount at the rate specified in the Schedule or an amount of two lakh rupees, whichever is higher.

Amends Section 23 of the principal Act by replacing the words "an advocate" with "who is a member of the Fund" and the words "ten rupees" and "five rupees" with "fifteen rupees" and "ten rupees", respectively.
Substitutes the existing Schedule to the principal Act with a new schedule detailing annual subscription amounts for advocates based on years of practice, ranging from 5 years of practice upwards.

Repeals the Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Ordinance, 2001 (33 of 2001). It also states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the said Ordinance or under the principal Act as amended by that Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Every member shall pay an annual subscription to the Fund on or before 30th June of every year at the following rates: two hundred rupees (less than five years standing at the Bar), five hundred rupees (five years and more but less than ten years), one thousand rupees (ten years and more but less than fifteen years), and one thousand and five hundred rupees (fifteen years and more).
An advocate designated as Senior Advocate under the Advocates' Act, 1961 shall pay an annual subscription at the rate of three thousand rupees.

In case of death of a member while in active practice and before attaining the age of fifty-five years, where there is no surviving legal heir, the nominee is entitled to receive from the Fund an amount at the rate specified in the Schedule or an amount of two lakh rupees, whichever is higher.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned, but likely the Bar Council or designated authorities under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund Act, 1980 and its amendments.

rights: Right to receive benefits from the Fund upon fulfilling the conditions.
Right of nominee to receive amounts in case of the member's death under specific circumstances.
duties: Duty to pay annual subscription to the Fund.
Duty to adhere to the provisions of the Act and the principal Act.
obligations: Obligation to pay subscription on or before June 30th every year.
Obligation to comply with the subscription rates based on years of practice and designation.

key_procedures: Procedure for payment of annual subscription: Members must pay the specified amount on or before June 30th each year, with rates varying based on years of practice and designation as Senior Advocate.

Procedure for claims in case of death: In the event of a member's death before 55 years of age and without legal heirs, the nominee is entitled to benefits as per the Schedule or a fixed amount of two lakh rupees, whichever is higher.
administration: The Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund Board (implied from the principal Act and the nature of the fund).
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 23rd November, 2001 and was published in the Kerala Extraordinary Gazette No. 1852 dated 23rd November, 2001.
The commencement of the Act was with immediate effect, while certain provisions were deemed to have come into force on November 22, 2000.
The Repeal and Saving clause ensures continuity of actions taken under the repealed Ordinance.

title: THE KERALA ADVOCATES WELFARE FUND (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2016
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund Act, 1980.
scope: Applies to Advocates and the Kerala Advocates Welfare Fund.

key_definitions.actual practice: Means carrying on the profession of an Advocate other than senior Advocate and filing of at least five vakalaths per year by an Advocate whose name is included in the list of practising Advocates published and maintained by the Bar Council in accordance with the rules made by it under section 27.
key_definitions.Advocates Academy: Means the academy constituted by the Bar Council for providing training to Advocates to enable them to give efficient legal service to the people.
key_definitions.non-practising Advocate: Means an Advocate who is not in actual practice.
key_definitions.practising Advocate: Means an Advocate in actual practice.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2016' and states that it comes into force at once.

Amends section 2 of the principal Act (The Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund Act, 1980) by substituting and inserting new clauses related to definitions such as 'actual practice', 'Advocates Academy', 'non-practising Advocate', and 'practising Advocate'.

Amends section 9 of the principal Act by inserting new clauses related to providing assistance to Advocates and stipends to Advocates who have less than three years standing at the bar and meet certain income criteria. It also substitutes sub-sections concerning admission of practising Advocates to the Trustee Committee and new members enrolled after retirement.

Amends section 15 of the principal Act by substituting provisions related to the subscription payable by members of the Fund, including new classifications for subscription amounts based on years of standing at the Bar. It also introduces provisions for members who voluntarily suspend their membership and the conditions for resumption.
Amends section 16 of the principal Act by substituting specific monetary figures related to the fund.

Amends section 18 of the principal Act by inserting a provision regarding a period of three years during which members of the Fund in case of hospitalized treatment involving major surgical operation or for cancer treatment and other critical illness are covered.

Amends section 23 of the principal Act by substituting a provision regarding vakalaths filed by an Advocate and the welfare fund stamp of fifty rupees on the vakalath filed before the High Court and the value of twenty-five rupees in the case of vakalath filed before subordinate courts, tribunals and other authorities.

important_rules: An Advocate who is a member of the Fund and is removed from the list of practising Advocates published and maintained by the Bar Council shall not be entitled to continue as a member of the Fund and during such period, such Advocate whose name is included in the list of non-practising Advocates maintained by the Bar Council shall be deemed to have been suspended from the Fund.
An Advocate who has not joined the Fund may apply to the Trustee Committee for admission as a member of the Fund on payment of annual subscription.
Every member of the Fund shall pay an annual subscription to the Fund on or before the 30th June of every year at the rates specified.

Every vakalath filed by an Advocate shall, in addition to the court fee stamp affixed thereon, be affixed with the welfare fund stamp of fifty rupees in the case of vakalath filed before the High Court and of twenty-five rupees in the case of vakalath filed before subordinate courts, tribunals and other authorities.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Bar Council
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through maintenance of lists of practising and non-practising Advocates and by prescribing rules for the functioning of the Advocates Welfare Fund.

rights: Practising Advocates in any court in the State may apply to the Trustee Committee for admission as a member of the Fund.
An Advocate enrolled after retirement from an employment shall be admitted as a member of the Fund if eligible.
duties: Advocates must pay annual subscriptions to the Fund.
Vakalaths filed by Advocates must have the specified welfare fund stamp affixed.
obligations: Members of the Fund who voluntarily suspend their membership may resume it on payment of two thousand rupees as resumption charges.

key_procedures: Admission of members to the Fund: Practising Advocates can apply to the Trustee Committee. Enrolled Advocates after retirement from employment are eligible if they meet criteria.
Subscription payment: Annual subscriptions are to be paid by members by June 30th of each year.
Resumption of suspended membership: Members who voluntarily suspend membership can resume by paying resumption charges and having their resumption recorded.
administration: Government of Kerala, Law (Legislation-C) Department
important_notes: The provision regarding the eligibility of a person for admission as a member after retirement is subject to a proviso that such sub-section shall not be applicable to a person who was in employment for a period not exceeding five years or if the pension does not exceed five thousand rupees per month.
Members of the Fund are eligible to claim benefits only up to ten years of their previous actual practice.
The Act is an amendment to the Kerala Advocates Welfare Fund Act, 1980.

title: THE KERALA ADVOCATES' WELFARE FUND (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1989
purpose: To amend the Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund Act, 1980, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: The Act applies to advocates in Kerala and relates to the Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 1989. It also specifies the commencement date as the 5th day of April, 1981, with certain provisions to come into force on the 6th day of May, 1989.
Amends section 2 of the Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund Act, 1980, by substituting the words 'unmarried minor children' with 'sons and daughters'.
