Amends section 4 of the principal Act by substituting 'two members' with 'three members' and inserting a clause regarding the President of the Kerala Bar Federation, ex-officio.

Amends section 13 of the principal Act by omitting a date to be notified by the Bar Council and adding a provision regarding reasons to be recorded in writing to recognise only one association for the Centre.
Inserts a new section 13A, titled 'Cancellation of recognition and registration of Bar Association', which deals with the grounds and procedure for cancelling recognition or registration.

Amends section 15 of the principal Act by adding provisos to sub-section (4) regarding the refund of admission fee in case of rejection of an application. It also clarifies the admission fee for membership as two hundred rupees.

Amends section 16 of the principal Act by adding provisos to sub-section (4) regarding the exclusion of certain periods from the computation of the period of practice for retirement or other benefit, and for individuals who do not apply to become members of the Fund.
Amends section 21 of the principal Act by inserting a new clause (b) regarding the subscription for membership in the Fund from other banks.

Amends section 23 of the principal Act by substituting sub-section (1) to state that every vakalath filed by an Advocate shall be affixed with a stamp in addition to court fee stamps, and such vakalath shall be valid unless so stamped. It also includes an explanation that two or more Advocates jointly appearing by a single vakalath separate stamps affixed by each.
Substitutes the Schedule to the principal Act with a new Schedule, likely containing updated amounts or criteria.

Repeals The Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Ordinance, 1989 (4 of 1989), and states that anything done or action taken under the principal Act as amended by the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Advocates applying for membership to the Fund shall pay a sum of rupees two hundred towards admission fee along with the application, as prescribed by the committee of the Trustee Committee.
In the event of rejection of an application, the admission fee paid shall be refunded to the applicant.
In computing the period of practice, the period of suspension, practice, either voluntary or otherwise, shall be excluded.
Every vakalath filed by an Advocate shall be affixed with a stamp in addition to the court fee stamps affixed thereon, and no vakalath shall be valid unless so stamped.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Bar Council, Kerala Bar Federation
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Cancellation of recognition and registration of Bar Associations, scrutiny of applications for membership, and enforcement of rules related to vakalath stamping.

rights: Right to apply for membership to the Fund.
Right to refund of admission fee if application is rejected.
duties: Duty to pay admission fee.
Duty to affix stamp on vakalath in addition to court fee stamps.
obligations: Advocates are obliged to comply with the provisions of the Act and its amendments regarding welfare fund contributions and membership.

key_procedures: Procedure for applying for membership to the Fund, including payment of admission fee.
Procedure for cancellation of recognition and registration of a Bar Association.
Procedure for stamping vakalaths filed by Advocates.
administration: The Kerala Bar Council and the Advocate's Welfare Fund Committee (implied).
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 15th day of July 1989 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 659 dt. the 15th July 1989.
Certain provisions came into force on April 5, 1981, and others on May 6, 1989.
The substitution of the Schedule provides updated financial contributions based on years of standing.
The Act repeals the Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Ordinance, 1989.

title: THE KERALA AGRARIAN RELATIONS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1962
purpose: To amend the Kerala Agrarian Relations Act, 1960, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Agrarian Relations (Amendment) Act, 1962.

In section 34 of the Kerala Agrarian Relations Act, 1960 (Act 4 of 1961):
(i) in sub-section (1),—
(a) for the words "one year of the commencement of this Act", the words "two years of the commencement of this Act" shall be substituted;
(b) for the last proviso, the following proviso shall be substituted, namely:—
"Provided further that in the case of such arrears of rent due to a small holder within the meaning of section 18,—
(a) from a tenant who has in his possession land in excess of 15 acres of double-crop land, or its equivalent, the provisions of this sub-section shall not apply ; and
(b) the amount payable under sub-section (5) shall be paid,—
(i) where arrears of rent on or before the 15th August, 1962; for not more than one year are outstanding,
(ii) where arrears of rent in two equal instalments, the due dates being the 15th August, for more than one year, but not 1962 and the 15th February, more than two years, are outstanding,
1963;
(iii) where arrears of rent in three equal instalments, the due for more than two years are out-standing,
dates being the 15th August, 1962, the 15th February, 1963 and the 15th August, 1963;
Provided that a tenant holding under a small holder shall pay the entire amount on or before the 15th August, 1962.
(7) If a tenant to whom sub-section (5) applies fails to make any of the payments which he has to make under sub-section (6) on or before the date fixed thereof, he shall not be entitled to the benefits conferred by sub-section (5), and shall be liable to pay the entire arrears of rent for the period specified in that sub-section which he would have been liable to pay if sub-sections (5) and (6) had not been enacted; but credit shall be given to any amount paid by him under sub-section (6) towards such arrears of rent.
(8) In computing the period of limitation for the institution of suits or proceedings for recovery of arrears of rent accrued due after the 11th April, 1957, and outstanding on the 15th February, 1961, the time allowed under sub-sections (5) and (6) for the payment of the arrears of rent shall be excluded."

(1) The Kerala Agrarian Relations (Amendment) Ordinance, 1962 (Ordinance No. 2 of 1962), is hereby repealed.
(2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act, as if this Act had commenced on the 6th day of February, 1962.

important_rules: Arrears of rent accrued due after 11th April, 1957, and outstanding on 15th February, 1961, shall be dealt with as specified.
Provisions regarding payment of arrears of rent by tenants of small holders are detailed.

Time allowed for payment of arrears of rent under sub-sections (5) and (6) shall be excluded for computing the period of limitation for suits or proceedings for recovery of rent accrued due after 11th April, 1957, and outstanding on 15th February, 1961.

penalties: If a tenant fails to make payments as per sub-section (6), they are liable to pay entire arrears of rent and will not be entitled to benefits of sub-section (5).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned, likely implied to be relevant authorities under the parent Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings for recovery of arrears of rent.

rights: Tenants have the right to pay arrears of rent in instalments as specified.
Tenants of small holders have the right to pay entire amount on or before 15th August, 1962.
duties: Tenants are obligated to pay arrears of rent within the stipulated time frames.
obligations: Obligation to pay arrears of rent on or before specified dates.

key_procedures: Procedure for payment of arrears of rent by tenants based on the amount and duration of outstanding rent.
Procedure for calculating the period of limitation for suits or proceedings for recovery of rent arrears.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned, likely administered by the relevant departments of the Kerala State Government responsible for agrarian relations.
important_notes: The Act specifically addresses arrears of rent accrued due after April 11, 1957, and outstanding on February 15, 1961.
Exceptions are made for tenants of small holders and for tenants possessing land exceeding 15 acres of double-crop land.
The Act repeals the Kerala Agrarian Relations (Amendment) Ordinance, 1962, but validates actions taken under it.

title: The Kerala Agricultural Debtors (Temporary Relief) Act, 2001
purpose: To provide temporary relief to agricultural debtors in Kerala.
scope: The Act applies to agricultural debtors within the state of Kerala. It specifies various conditions and definitions related to agricultural debtors and their debts.

key_definitions.agricultural debtor: Includes persons who are or have been engaged in agricultural operations and have incurred debts related to such operations.
key_definitions.debt: Refers to various types of financial obligations, including loans, mortgages, and other liabilities incurred for agricultural purposes.
key_definitions.secured debt: A debt for which security is provided, typically immovable property.
key_definitions.unsecured debt: A debt for which no specific security is provided.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (Kerala), and the date of commencement.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'agricultural debtor', 'debt', 'secured debt', 'unsecured debt', and 'prescribed'.
Deals with the stay of legal proceedings against agricultural debtors, including eviction, sale of property, and execution of decrees.
Outlines the powers of the court to grant relief to agricultural debtors, including postponement of sale, stay of execution, and modification of decrees.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Specifies that the Act does not affect the rights of bona fide purchasers for value without notice of the provisions of the Act.
Details the temporary relief that may be granted to agricultural debtors, such as suspension of payment of debts and moratoriums.

important_rules: Proceedings for eviction of agricultural debtors from their land or homestead shall be stayed.
Sale of immovable property of an agricultural debtor to satisfy a debt shall be postponed.
Execution of decrees and orders against agricultural debtors shall be stayed under certain conditions.
Debts incurred by agricultural debtors may be subject to a moratorium or reduction.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts, as specified in the Act, and potentially other authorities designated by the Government through rules.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through stay of proceedings, postponement of sales, and modification of decrees by the courts.

rights: Right to stay of proceedings related to debt recovery and eviction.
Right to have sale of property postponed.
Right to claim temporary relief from debt obligations.

key_procedures: An agricultural debtor can apply to the appropriate court for relief under the Act.
The court, upon application and satisfaction of the conditions, can grant a stay of proceedings, postpone sales, or modify decrees.
The Act provides for temporary relief measures like moratoriums on debt payments.
administration: The Government of Kerala, likely through the Revenue Department or Agriculture Department, with powers to make rules.
important_notes: The Act provides temporary relief and is not a permanent solution to debt issues.
The definitions of 'agricultural debtor' and 'debt' are crucial for determining the applicability of the Act.
The Act aims to prevent distress sales and protect agricultural livelihoods during a specific period.

title: The Kerala Agricultural Income Tax (Amendment Act), 2005
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1991.
scope: The Act applies to agricultural income tax in Kerala.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Agricultural Income Tax (Amendment) Act, 2005, and it came into force on the 1st day of April, 2005.

This section provides for the substitution of clause (5) of section 2 of the principal Act. The substituted clause defines 'Deputy Commissioner (Appeals)' as a person appointed to be a Deputy Commissioner (Appeals) of Agricultural Income Tax under section 24.
This section amends clause (d) of section 24 in the principal Act, substituting the words 'Appellate Assistant Commissioner' with 'Deputy Commissioner (Appeals)'.
This section amends the proviso to sub-section (1) of section 25 in the principal Act, substituting the words 'Appellate Assistant Commissioner' with 'Deputy Commissioner (Appeals)'.
This section amends sub-section (27) in the principal Act, substituting the words 'Appellate Assistant Commissioner' with 'Deputy Commissioner (Appeals)'.
This section amends section 29 in the principal Act, substituting the words 'Appellate Assistant Commissioner' with 'Deputy Commissioner (Appeals)'.
This section amends sub-section (7) of section 43 in the principal Act, substituting the words 'Appellate Assistant Commissioner' and 'Deputy Commissioner' with 'Deputy Commissioner (Appeals)'.
This section amends sub-section (1) of section 72 in the principal Act, substituting the words 'Appellate Assistant Commissioner' with 'Deputy Commissioner (Appeals)'.

This section amends clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 74 in the principal Act, substituting the words 'Appellate Assistant Commissioner' and 'Deputy Commissioner' with 'Deputy Commissioner (Appeals)'.
This section amends the principal Act by substituting 'Appellate Assistant Commissioner' with 'Deputy Commissioner (Appeals)' in sub-section (1) and in sub-section (2) (a).

This section amends the principal Act by substituting 'an Appellate Assistant Commissioner or the Deputy Commissioner' with 'the Deputy Commissioner (Appeals)' in sub-section (1) and sub-clause (b) of sub-section (2).
This section amends clause (a) of section 78A in the principal Act, substituting the words 'Appellate Assistant Commissioner' with 'Deputy Commissioner (Appeals)'.
This section amends the principal Act by substituting 'the Appellate Assistant Commissioner' with 'the Deputy Commissioner (Appeals)' in sub-section (1) and sub-section (5).
This section amends section 96 in the principal Act by substituting 'to another Appellate Assistant Commissioner or a Deputy Commissioner' with 'to the Deputy Commissioner (Appeals)'.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Deputy Commissioner (Appeals)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Amendments to existing sections of the principal Act, indicating procedural and administrative changes related to appeals.

key_procedures: Appeals to the Deputy Commissioner (Appeals) as per amended sections.
administration: The Kerala State Government (implied by the nature of the act)
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 1st day of September, 2005 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 2030 dated 2nd September, 2005.

title: The Agricultural Income-tax (Amendment) Act, 1960
purpose: To further amend the Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950.
scope: Applies to the agricultural income-tax in Kerala, specifically amending provisions related to composition and payment, insertion of new sections, and amendments to existing sections and the Schedule.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called The Agricultural Income-tax (Amendment) Act, 1960, and it shall be deemed to have come into force on the first day of April, 1960.

Inserts a new section 3A concerning the composition and consolidated payment of agricultural income-tax. Any assessee, other than a company, may apply to the Agricultural Income-tax Officer to compound their tax liability for the financial year commencing on April 1, 1960, or any subsequent financial year, provided their total agricultural income for the previous year does not exceed five thousand rupees. The application must be made within such time and in such manner as prescribed. The Agricultural Income-tax Officer, after satisfying themselves, will correctly assess the total agricultural income of the assessee. Provisions regarding collection and recovery of the consolidated amount are also specified. The payment of seventy-five rupees is mentioned for this consolidated payment. The provisions of this Act relating to collection and recovery of agricultural income-tax shall apply to the collection and recovery of the consolidated amount payable under sub-section (3) of the new section 3A.
Amends section 31 of the principal Act by substituting the words and figures 'sections 19, 20, 21, 23, 29 and 41' with 'sections 3A, 19, 20, 21, 23, 29 and 41'.

Amends section 67 of the principal Act. In sub-section (2) of section 67, after the clause (c), a new clause (cc) is to be inserted, which states that the Act will apply in relation to the manner and time within which applications under section 3A shall be made and the form of, and the particulars to be contained in, such applications.

Amends the Schedule in Part I of the Schedule to the principal Act. In the first proviso, the words 'three thousand rupees' are substituted with 'three thousand and six hundred rupees'. In the second proviso, in clause (1), for the words 'three thousand rupees', the words 'three thousand and six hundred rupees' shall be substituted.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Agricultural Income-tax Officer
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Collection and recovery of consolidated tax amounts as per general provisions.

rights: Right to apply for composition and consolidated payment of agricultural income-tax (for assessees other than companies, under certain conditions).
duties: Duty to make applications for composition within prescribed time and manner.
Duty to provide particulars in applications as prescribed.
obligations: Obligation to pay the consolidated agricultural income-tax as determined.

key_procedures: Procedure for applying for composition and consolidated payment of agricultural income-tax: Assessees (other than companies) with total agricultural income not exceeding five thousand rupees for the previous year can apply to the Agricultural Income-tax Officer. The application must be made in the prescribed form, within the prescribed time, and contain the prescribed particulars. The Officer will then assess the total agricultural income and the consolidated amount payable. The provisions for collection and recovery of agricultural income-tax apply to this consolidated payment.
administration: Agricultural Income-tax Officer
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on the first day of April, 1960.
The provisions for composition and consolidated payment under section 3A apply to assessees other than companies.
The total agricultural income for the previous year must not exceed five thousand rupees to be eligible for composition under section 3A.
The consolidated payment is set at seventy-five rupees.
Published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 2nd August, 1960.

title: THE KERALA AGRICULTURAL PESTS AND DISEASES ACT, 1958
purpose: To make provision for preventing the spread of insect pests, plant diseases and noxious weeds within the State of Kerala. WHEREAS it is expedient to take measures to prevent the spread of insect pests, plant diseases and noxious weeds injurious to health or to crops, plants, trees or water-supply or obstructive to water-ways within the State of Kerala.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala and covers insect pests, plant diseases, and noxious weeds that are injurious to health or to crops, plants, trees or water-supply, or are obstructive to water-ways.

key_definitions.insect pest: any insect or other invertebrate animal which has been declared by notification under section 3 or section 9 of this Act to be an insect pest.
key_definitions.plant disease: any fungoid, bacterial, parasitic or other disease which has been declared by notification under section 3 or section 9 of this Act to be a plant disease;
key_definitions.noxious weed: any weed which has been declared by notification under section 3 of this Act to be a noxious weed.
key_definitions.plant: includes the fruit, leaves, bark, cuttings or any living portion of a plant but does not include the seed unless the seed has been specially included in the definition of plant by the Government by notification;
key_definitions.occupier: means the person having for the time being the right of occupation of any land, premises, or water or his authorised agent or any person in actual occupation of the land, premises or water, and includes a local authority and a company having such right of occupation or in such actual occupation;
key_definitions.notified area: means the area covered by a notification published under section 3 or section 9;
key_definitions.Director of Agriculture: means an officer appointed by the Government to be the Director of Agriculture and includes every person who for the time being performs the duties of the office;
key_definitions.prescribed: means prescribed by notification or rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Agricultural Pests and Diseases Act, 1958, that it extends to the whole of the State of Kerala, and that it shall come into force at once.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'insect pest', 'plant disease', 'noxious weed', 'plant', 'occupier', 'notified area', 'Director of Agriculture', and 'prescribed'.

main_sections.section_title: Notification by the Government of areas affected by insect pests, plant diseases or noxious weeds.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to notify areas affected by insect pests, plant diseases or noxious weeds. Such notification can declare a pest or disease, prohibit or restrict the removal of plants, define local areas, and prescribe remedial or preventive measures.

Makes the occupier liable to carry out remedial and preventive measures prescribed in a notification under section 3. The explanation clarifies that the occupier is deemed to be the occupier of all lands within the meaning of section 3(1) of the Kerala Land Conservancy Act, 1957.
Grants any officer appointed under section 21 the right of entry on any land or water within a notified area to take necessary action.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure where measures prescribed to eradicate insect pests include removal or destruction of plants.
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for eradicating insect pests, which may include the removal or destruction of plants. If an occupier fails to comply, the inspecting officer or officer under his supervision may carry out the removal or destruction, and the occupier shall be deemed to have committed an offence.

main_sections.section_title: Inspecting officer may serve a notice on occupier to take remedial or preventive action.
main_sections.description: Allows an inspecting officer to serve a notice on an occupier to take specified remedial or preventive action. If the occupier fails to comply, they may prefer an appeal to the prescribed officer. The decision of the appeal is final.

main_sections.section_title: Occupier failing to comply with the notice served on him commits an offence.
main_sections.description: States that an occupier failing to comply with a notice served by an inspecting officer commits an offence. The government can then take remedial or preventive measures, and the occupier will be deemed to have committed an offence and liable for compensation.

main_sections.section_title: Preventive or remedial measures in emergent cases.
main_sections.description: Allows the Government to take preventive or remedial measures without prior notice if it is satisfied that any pest or disease is injurious. These measures may be taken by notification in the Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Recovery from the occupier of the cost of preventive or remedial measures carried out by the inspecting officer.
main_sections.description: Deals with the recovery of costs for preventive or remedial measures carried out by the inspecting officer. The cost is recoverable as an arrear of land revenue. It also specifies how the cost is calculated and mentions that any occupier aggrieved by an order can apply to the Government for revision.

main_sections.section_title: Destruction of trees or plants in execution of remedial or preventive measures and compensation therefor.
main_sections.description: Addresses the destruction of trees or plants as part of remedial or preventive measures. Compensation may be payable for such destruction under certain conditions, but not for cotton plants destroyed under specific clauses. The value of the tree or plant is determined at the time of its destruction.

main_sections.section_title: Claims for compensation how and when to be made.
main_sections.description: Specifies the procedure for making claims for compensation, including the timeframe and the authority to whom the claim should be submitted. The valuing officer will investigate and assess the claim, and the award of compensation cannot exceed the rates prescribed. An appeal against the award can be preferred.

Details the process of awarding compensation, including the inquiry and assessment by the valuing officer. The award cannot exceed prescribed rates, and an appeal against it can be made to the prescribed officer.

Allows either the occupier or the inspecting officer to prefer an appeal against an award within thirty days of the date of receipt of the award. The appeal is to be preferred to the prescribed officer.

main_sections.section_title: Obligation of village officers to report on insect pests, plant diseases or noxious weeds.
main_sections.description: Mandates village officers and other officers to report on insect pests, plant diseases or noxious weeds in their respective areas to the notified authority. Areas where such pests are prevalent appear to be reported the same to the Collector.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for offence under section 6 or section 8.
main_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for offences under section 6 or section 8, which includes a fine not exceeding fifty rupees or default imprisonment for a period not exceeding ten days.

main_sections.section_title: Contravention notification under section 3 (1) (b) to be an offence and punishment therefor.
main_sections.description: Deals with contravention of notifications issued under section 3(1)(b), which prohibits or restricts the removal of plants. Such contravention is an offence punishable with a fine not exceeding fifty rupees or simple imprisonment for a period not exceeding ten days.

main_sections.section_title: Compensation for trees and plants destroyed by occupier.
main_sections.description: Addresses compensation for trees and plants destroyed by an occupier in obedience to a notice issued under section 7. The occupier is entitled to compensation under certain conditions, provided the destruction was in obedience to the notice and the tree or plant was destroyed as aforesaid.

main_sections.section_title: Compensation not payable for noxious weeds destroyed.
main_sections.description: States that no compensation is payable for noxious weeds destroyed.

main_sections.section_title: Institution of prosecutions or other legal proceedings under the Act.
main_sections.description: Specifies that no suit, prosecution, or other legal proceedings shall lie against any officer for anything done in good faith in carrying out the provisions of the Act. It also states that no prosecution shall be commenced without the previous sanction of the Collector, and no prosecution shall be commenced six months after the date of the alleged offence.
Empowers the Government to appoint inspecting officers from time to time, prescribing their powers in sections 5, 6 and 7.

Allows the Government to delegate its powers under the Act to the Director of Agriculture or any other officer, or to any local authority, or to the president or chairman of any local authority, except for powers to make rules.

Grants the Government the power to make rules by notification in the Gazette, consistent with the provisions of the Act. These rules can prescribe methods for publication of descriptions of insect pests, plant diseases, and noxious weeds, and treatment to be followed.

main_sections.section_title: Rules to be laid before the Legislative Assembly.
main_sections.description: States that rules made under the Act shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly.
Repeals any existing provisions.

important_rules: Occupiers are liable to carry out remedial and preventive measures prescribed by the Government in notified areas.
Inspecting officers can serve notices on occupiers for remedial or preventive action.
The Government can take immediate preventive or remedial measures in emergent cases.
Costs of preventive or remedial measures carried out by the inspecting officer are recoverable from the occupier.
Destruction of trees or plants as part of remedial measures may be compensated, but not for noxious weeds.
Village officers have an obligation to report on insect pests, plant diseases, or noxious weeds.
Contravention of notifications prohibiting the removal of plants is an offence.

penalties: Fine not exceeding fifty rupees or simple imprisonment for a period not exceeding ten days for offences under section 6 or section 8.
Fine not exceeding fifty rupees or simple imprisonment for a period not exceeding ten days for contravening notifications under section 3 (1) (b).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Inspecting officers appointed by the Government, and village officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notification of affected areas, service of notices on occupiers, carrying out remedial and preventive measures, recovery of costs, and prosecution for non-compliance.

rights: Right of entry for inspecting officers on any land or water within a notified area.
Right to appeal against awards of compensation.
Right to prefer an appeal against an award of compensation.
duties: Duty of occupiers to comply with notices and prescribed measures.
Duty of village officers to report on insect pests, plant diseases or noxious weeds.
Duty of the Government to notify affected areas and prescribe measures.
obligations: Obligation of occupiers to carry out remedial and preventive measures.
Obligation for village officers and other officers to report on pests, diseases, and weeds.

key_procedures: Notification of affected areas by the Government, including declaration of pests, diseases, or weeds, and prescription of measures.
Service of notice by inspecting officers on occupiers requiring remedial or preventive action.
Appeals against decisions of inspecting officers or awards of compensation.
Recovery of costs of remedial or preventive measures from occupiers.
Claims for compensation for destroyed trees or plants.
administration: The Act is administered by the Government of Kerala, with powers delegated to the Director of Agriculture and other officers. Inspecting officers are appointed for enforcement.
important_notes: The Act aims to prevent the spread of agricultural pests, diseases, and noxious weeds within Kerala.
The definition of 'plant' includes fruit, leaves, bark, and cuttings, but not seeds unless specifically included.
Compensation is not payable for the destruction of noxious weeds.
Prosecutions require previous sanction from the Collector and have a time limit for commencement.
Rules made under the Act must be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

title: The Kerala Agricultural University (Amendment) Act, 1995
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Agricultural University Act, 1971.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Agricultural University.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Agricultural University (Amendment) Act, 1995, and it shall come into force at once.
This section amends sub-section (4) of section 42 of the Kerala Agricultural University Act, 1971. It substitutes specific terms within that sub-section.

purpose: To amend The Kerala Agricultural University Act, 1971.
scope: Applies to The Kerala Agricultural University and its affairs.

key_definitions.university: Refers to The Kerala Agricultural University established under the Kerala Agricultural University Act, 1971.
key_definitions.state_government: Refers to the Government of Kerala.
key_definitions.ordinance: Refers to the Kerala Agricultural University (Amendment) Ordinance, 1997.
key_definitions.act: Refers to The Kerala Agricultural University Act, 1971.

main_sections.description: Amends Section 14 of the Principal Act, which likely pertains to the composition or powers of a governing body of the university.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 15 of the Principal Act
main_sections.description: Amends Section 15 of the Principal Act, which might relate to the powers and functions of the university's authorities.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 27 of the Principal Act
main_sections.description: Amends Section 27 of the Principal Act, potentially dealing with the financial matters or audit of the university.

The amendments in this Act are made to The Kerala Agricultural University Act, 1971.
Specific sections of the Principal Act (Sections 2, 14, 15, and 27) are being amended.
The Act clarifies that the provisions of the Kerala Agricultural University (Amendment) Ordinance, 1997 shall have effect notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force.
key_procedures: Amendments are made to specific sections of the principal Act, implying procedural changes or clarifications within the university's framework.

important_notes: The Act supersedes any contrary provisions in existing laws.

title: The Kerala Agricultural University (Amendment) Act, 1972
purpose: To amend the Kerala Agricultural University Act, 1971.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Agricultural University and its employees.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Agricultural University (Amendment) Act, 1972.

Amends section 58 of the Kerala Agricultural University Act, 1971, concerning the transfer of employees. It clarifies provisions regarding employees of the Government who become employees of the University, ensuring their continuity of service and rights. It also addresses the transfer of any employee of the Government to the University on notification, and the eligibility of employees to become employees of the University and their claim.

Amends section 60 of the principal Act by adding a proviso regarding examinations for students of the Agricultural College and Research Institute, Vellayani and students of the Kerala Veterinary College and Research Institute, Mannuthy. It states that examinations conducted during the year 1972 shall be conducted, and degrees, diplomas, and certificates granted on successful completion shall be by the Kerala University or the Calicut University, as the case may be, if requested by the University established under this Act, as if the College had been affiliated to the Kerala University or the Calicut University, as the case may be.

(1) The Kerala Agricultural University (Amendment) Ordinance, 1972 (1 of 1972), is hereby repealed. (2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act as if this Act had come into force on the 29th day of January, 1972.

important_rules: Employees of the Government who have become employees of the University shall cease to be employees of the Government and shall become employees of the University. Their continuity of service will be maintained. The University will have the effect of depriving any other person who has superior claim and is willing to be appointed under the University. (Section 58(1)(a))

Any employee of the Government who, on the date specified in the notification under sub-section (1) or in the order under sub-section (3), was eligible to become an employee of the University and who has superior claim than any person who has become an employee of the University on that date, may be transferred to the University. (Section 58(1)(b))

Examinations conducted in 1972 for students of the Agricultural College and Research Institute, Vellayani and Kerala Veterinary College and Research Institute, Mannuthy shall be conducted, and degrees/diplomas/certificates granted by the Kerala or Calicut University if requested, as if the College was affiliated. (Section 60(1))

rights: Employees transferred from the Government to the University retain their service continuity and rights.
Employees eligible and with superior claim have the right to be appointed to the University.
obligations: The University has an obligation to ensure the smooth transfer and continuity of service for its employees.

key_procedures: Procedure for amendment of Section 58: The amendment specifies how employees of the Government transition to being employees of the University, detailing continuity of service and eligibility based on claims.

Procedure for amendment of Section 60: The amendment outlines the process for conducting examinations and granting degrees/diplomas for specific colleges in 1972, involving the Kerala or Calicut University.
Procedure for repeal and saving: The Ordinance is repealed, but actions taken under it are considered valid as if done under the Act.
administration: The Kerala Agricultural University
important_notes: The Kerala Agricultural University (Amendment) Ordinance, 1972 (1 of 1972) is repealed.
Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are deemed to have been taken under this Act.
The Act came into force on the 29th day of January, 1972.

title: The Kerala Agricultural University (Amendment) Act, 1973
purpose: To amend the Kerala Agricultural University Act, 1971.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Agricultural University.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Kerala Agricultural University (Amendment) Act, 1973 and states it shall come into force on the 21st day of April, 1973.

Amends section 27 of the Kerala Agricultural University Act, 1971 (33 of 1971) by adding a proviso. The proviso states that a Vice-Chancellor appointed before the expiry of the period for which he has been appointed, either by resignation or otherwise, shall continue until the expiry of that period or until the Chancellor determines.

Repeals the Kerala Agricultural University (Amendment) Ordinance, 1973 (4 of 1973). It also provides that anything done or any action taken under the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

administration: Kerala Agricultural University
important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 638 dated 18th July, 1973.

title: The Kerala Agricultural University (Amendment) Act, 1974

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Agricultural University (Amendment) Act, 1974. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 27th day of November, 1973.

title: The Kerala Agricultural University (Amendment) Act, 1980
purpose: To amend the Kerala Agricultural University Act, 1971, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Agricultural University and its activities.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Agricultural University (Amendment) Act, 1980. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 7th day of June, 1980.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 15
main_sections.description: Substitutes the existing section 15 of the Kerala Agricultural University Act, 1971, regarding the term of office of members of the Executive Committee and their holding office.
Amends section 29 of the principal Act by inserting a new subsection (1-A) regarding the appointment of Pro-Vice-Chancellor.
Repeals the Kerala Agricultural University (Amendment) Ordinance, 1980, and provides for saving any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance.

important_rules: Members of the Executive Committee shall cease to hold office on the day immediately preceding the date of reconstitution of the General Council.

Members of the Executive Committee who have ceased to hold office by virtue of the provisions of subsection (1) shall be competent to exercise the powers and perform the functions of the Executive Committee under this Act and the Statutes, Ordinances and Regulations.
No person other than an ex-officio member or the member representing the Indian Council of Agricultural Research shall be eligible to hold office for more than two terms in succession.
The Chancellor, if he considers it necessary, appoint a Pro-Vice-Chancellor in consultation with the Vice-Chancellor.
key_procedures: Reconstitution of the General Council.
Appointment of Pro-Vice-Chancellor by the Chancellor in consultation with the Vice-Chancellor.
administration: Kerala Agricultural University

The following subsection shall be substituted for subsection (4) for section 29: "Subject to the proviso to this Act and the Statutes, Ordinances and Regulations, the powers and functions of the Pro-Vice-Chancellor shall be determined by the Chancellor in consultation with the Vice-Chancellor."

title: The Kerala Agricultural University Act 1971
purpose: To provide for the establishment and incorporation of an Agricultural University in the State of Kerala and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to the establishment, incorporation, functions, administration, and officers of the Kerala Agricultural University.

key_definitions.Authority: Includes the General Council, the Executive Committee, and any other Authority constituted under the Act.
key_definitions.University: Refers to the Kerala Agricultural University.
key_definitions.Statutes: Means the Statutes of the University made under the Act.
key_definitions.Ordinances: Means the Ordinances of the University made under the Act.
key_definitions.Regulations: Means the Regulations of the University made under the Act.

main_sections.description: Ensures that the validity of any act or proceeding of any Authority of the University is not affected by reason of any defect in its constitution or any vacancy among its members or by reason of some person having taken part in proceedings who was subsequently found not to have been entitled to do so. Also states that no suit, prosecution, or other proceedings shall lie against any officer or employee of the University for any act done or purported to be done in good faith in pursuance of the Act, Statutes, Ordinances, or Regulations. It also clarifies that no officer or employee shall be liable in respect of any act done in good faith in the course of executing duties or discharging functions under the Act.

Lists the Officers of the University, which include the Chancellor, Pro-Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor (if any), Registrar, Comptroller, Director of Physical Plant, Librarian, Deans of Faculties, Director of Student Welfare, Director of Research, and Director of Extension, and other persons as may be declared by Statutes to be Officers of the University.

States that the Governor of Kerala shall be the Chancellor of the University. The Chancellor shall be the Head of the University and preside at meetings of the General Council and at any convocation of the University. The Chancellor shall also confer honorary degrees and exercise such other powers as may be conferred or imposed by the Statutes.

States that the Minister in charge of Agricultural Development of the State shall be the Pro-Chancellor. The Pro-Chancellor shall exercise all powers and perform all functions of the Chancellor during the Chancellor's absence or inability to act. The Pro-Chancellor shall also exercise such other powers and perform such other functions as may be delegated by the Chancellor.

Details the appointment of the Vice-Chancellor, who shall be a full-time officer. The Vice-Chancellor is appointed by the Chancellor on the recommendation of a selection committee. The section also outlines the term of office and eligibility for re-appointment for the Vice-Chancellor and provisions for emoluments and conditions of service.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and duties of the Vice-Chancellor.
main_sections.description: Outlines the Vice-Chancellor's role as the principal executive and academic officer. The Vice-Chancellor exercises general control over the affairs of the University, presides over meetings of the Executive Committee and Academic Council, and ensures the faithful observance of the provisions of the Act, Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations. The Vice-Chancellor is also responsible for the presentation of budget estimates and statements of accounts and may take immediate action in emergencies. The Vice-Chancellor oversees the appointment, suspension, and dismissal of officers, teachers, and employees and is responsible for the proper administration, coordination, and integration of teaching, research, and extension education.

Specifies that the Pro-Vice-Chancellor shall be a whole-time salaried officer assisting the Vice-Chancellor in discharging duties. The Pro-Vice-Chancellor's salary and other conditions of service are prescribed by Statutes. The Pro-Vice-Chancellor may be delegated powers and functions by the Vice-Chancellor.

Defines the Registrar as a whole-time officer appointed by the Executive Committee. The Registrar is responsible for the custody of records, the common seal, and serves as the ex-officio Secretary to the General Council, Executive Committee, and Academic Council. The Registrar manages applications for entrance, keeps records of courses, curricula, and other information. The Registrar is also responsible for maintaining academic performance records of students, including courses taken, grades obtained, degrees awarded, and other items pertinent to student academic performance. Other duties may be assigned by the Executive Committee or Vice-Chancellor.

States that the Comptroller is a whole-time officer appointed by the Government on terms and conditions they deem fit. The Comptroller manages the funds and investments of the University and advises on its financial policy. The Comptroller is responsible for the preparation of the budget and statements of accounts. The Comptroller also ensures that no expenditure is incurred without authorization and that expenditures do not contravene statutory provisions. Additionally, the Comptroller is responsible for the revision of the budget when required and for expediting the approval of the budget.

Specifies that the Director of Physical Plant is appointed by the Executive Committee and is responsible for the general custodian of all properties of the University. Duties include making arrangements for construction and maintenance of buildings and other structures, making arrangements for the purchase and maintenance of machinery and equipment, and maintaining lawns, grounds, and gardens of the University campus. Other duties may be assigned by the Vice-Chancellor, and the Director is responsible to the Executive Committee for discharging their duties.

States that the Librarian is appointed by the Executive Committee and is responsible for the committee that purchases, catalogues, maintains, issues, and receives books and journals for the library. The Librarian's salary and other conditions of service are prescribed by Statutes.

Mandates that there shall be a Dean for each Faculty, appointed in such manner as prescribed. The General Council may direct that a Dean shall be in charge of more than one Faculty. Deans shall be full-time salaried officers and shall hold office for a period as may be prescribed. They shall be paid such salary and allowances and be subject to such conditions of service as may be prescribed. The Dean shall be the Chairman of the Board of Studies of the Faculty and shall be responsible to the Vice-Chancellor for the observance of Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations, and for the organization and conduct of those functions. They shall work in close liaison with other officers and Heads of Departments and discharge other duties as may be necessary for the proper functioning of their respective Faculties.

States that there shall be a Director of Research who is a whole-time salaried Officer of the University, appointed by the Executive Committee in accordance with the Statutes. The Director's salary and allowances and other conditions of service are prescribed. The Director is responsible for the direction and co-ordination of research programmes and for efficient working of research stations. The Director may exercise such powers and perform such duties as may be conferred or imposed by the Statutes.

States that there shall be a Director of Extension who is a whole-time salaried Officer of the University, appointed by the Executive Committee in accordance with the Statutes. The Director's salary and allowances and other conditions of service are prescribed. The Director of Extension is appointed by the Executive Committee in accordance with the Statutes.

important_rules: No order for removal of any person from the ground that such person has been convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude shall be passed against any person without giving them an opportunity of being heard.
If any question arises as to whether any person has been duly nominated or elected as a member of any Authority, the question shall be referred to the Chancellor whose decision shall be final.

No act or proceeding of any Authority or other body of the University shall be invalid merely by reason of any defect in its constitution or any vacancy among its members or by reason of some person having taken part in the proceedings who was subsequently found not to have been entitled to do so.

No suit, prosecution, or other proceedings shall lie against any officer or other employee of the University for any act done or purported to be done in good faith in pursuance of this Act, the Statutes, the Ordinances and the Regulations thereunder.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Executive Committee, and other Authorities of the University as established by the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers and duties vested in various officers and authorities of the University as defined in the Act, Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations.

rights: Any person convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude has the right to be heard before an order for removal is passed.
Members of any Authority have the right to participate in proceedings, even if their entitlement is later questioned, without invalidating the proceedings.
Officers and employees of the University have the right to be protected from legal proceedings for acts done in good faith in pursuance of the Act.
duties: Officers and employees must act in good faith in the course of executing duties and discharging functions under the Act.
The Vice-Chancellor has a duty to exercise general control over the affairs of the University and ensure the faithful observance of the Act, Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations.
The Registrar has duties related to record keeping, common seal management, and administration of academic affairs.
The Comptroller has duties related to financial management, budgeting, and expenditure control.
The Director of Physical Plant is responsible for the maintenance and management of University properties.
The Librarian is responsible for the management of the University library's collection and services.
Deans of Faculties are responsible for the organization and conduct of faculty functions and the observance of University rules.
obligations: Officers and employees are obligated to perform their duties and discharge functions under the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure for removal of a person convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude: An opportunity of being heard must be provided.
Procedure for resolving questions of nomination or election to Authorities: Referral to the Chancellor for a final decision.
Procedure for appointment of the Vice-Chancellor: Involves a selection committee and recommendation to the Chancellor.
Procedure for appointments of other officers (Registrar, Comptroller, Directors, Librarian, Deans): Generally made by the Executive Committee or Government, in accordance with the Statutes.
Procedure for the selection of candidates for positions: The selection committee establishes its own procedure for inviting nominations, considering candidates, and providing recommendations.
administration: The Kerala Agricultural University, as established by the Act, with its various authorities and officers.
important_notes: Section 23(1) provides for the 'Savings of validity' of University proceedings despite defects in constitution or participation by ineligible persons.
Section 23(2) and (3) provide for the protection of officers and employees from legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith.
The tenure of the Vice-Chancellor is generally for five years, with eligibility for re-appointment for another five years.
The resignation of the Vice-Chancellor takes effect from the date of relief.
The Pro-Vice-Chancellor acts for the Vice-Chancellor in case of absence or inability to act.

title: The Kerala Agricultural University (Amendment) Act, 2001
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Agricultural University Act, 1971, for the purposes therein appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Agricultural University.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Agricultural University (Amendment) Act, 2001 and it shall come into force at once.
Amends Section 2 of the Kerala Agricultural University Act, 1971 (33 of 1971). Clause (18) of the principal Act is omitted.
Amends Section 3 of the principal Act. The words "Pro-Vice-Chancellor" are omitted.
Amends Section 10 of the principal Act. Substitutes provisions related to 'Ex-officio Members' and 'Elected Members'.
Amends Section 14 of the principal Act. Substitutes provisions related to 'Ex-officio Members' and omits provisions related to 'Other Members'.
Amends Section 17 of the principal Act. Clause (b) of sub-section (1) shall be omitted.
Amends Section 24 of the principal Act. Item (4) shall be omitted.

Amends Section 27 of the principal Act. In sub-section (11), the words "the Pro-Vice-Chancellor shall exercise the powers and perform the duties of the Vice-Chancellor and in his absence" shall be omitted.
Section 29 of the principal Act shall be omitted.
Amends Section 47 of the principal Act. Substitutes sub-section (2) and omits sub-section (4) related to the submission of accounts and audit report to the Government.
Amends Section 57 of the principal Act. Substitutes sub-section (2) concerning the General Council's role in forwarding comments on the table of the Legislative Assembly.

Provides for the dissolution of the General Council. Notwithstanding anything contained in the principal Act, the General Council shall stand dissolved. Members are deemed to have vacated their offices. The General Council shall be reconstituted within six months. The Chancellor shall nominate members to exercise powers and perform functions until reconstitution.

key_procedures: Procedure for reconstitution of the General Council after dissolution, including nomination by the Chancellor and a six-month timeline.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 26th December, 2001 and was published in Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 2062 dated 26-12-2001.

title: The Kerala Agricultural Workers' (Amendment) Act, 2010
purpose: To amend the Kerala Agricultural Workers' Act, 1974, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to agricultural workers in Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Agricultural Workers' (Amendment) Act, 2010. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 5th day of January, 2010.

Amends section 9 of the Kerala Agricultural Workers' Act, 1974. It substitutes sub-section (1) with provisions regarding land ownership and contributions to a Fund. It also inserts a new sub-section (4) stating the Government's annual contribution to the Fund from grants, equal to the contribution paid by registered agricultural workers.

Repeals the Kerala Agricultural Workers' (Amendment) Ordinance, 2010. Notwithstanding the repeal, any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Every land owner holding more than forty ares in extent of agricultural land shall pay contribution to the Fund at the rate of twenty-five paise per are per annum for the land held by him in excess of forty ares or part thereof in the manner prescribed.
administration: Law (Legislation-C) Department, Government of Kerala

title: The Kerala Agricultural Workers' (Amendment) Act, 2003
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Agricultural Workers' Act, 1974.
scope: Applies to agricultural workers in Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Agricultural Workers' (Amendment) Act, 2003, and it shall come into force at once.
Amends sub-section (2) of section 9 of the Kerala Agricultural Workers' Act, 1974 (Act 18 of 1974) by substituting the words "two rupees" for the words "five rupees".

important_rules: Substitution of "two rupees" for "five rupees" in section 9(2) of the principal Act.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on 16th August, 2003 and published as Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No 1551 dated 20th August, 2003.

title: The Kerala Agricultural Workers Act 1974
purpose: The Act aims to regulate the employment conditions, wages, and welfare of agricultural workers in Kerala, and to provide for the settlement of disputes related to their employment.
scope: The Act applies to agricultural workers and landowners in the state of Kerala. It covers matters related to wages, over-time work, disputes, and the maintenance of registers and records.

key_definitions.agricultural worker: A person who is employed for wages by a landowner for any agricultural operations.
key_definitions.landowner: A person who owns land and employs agricultural workers for agricultural operations.
key_definitions.Collector: Means the District Collector or any other officer appointed by the Government to exercise the powers and perform the functions of a Collector under the Kerala Revenue Recovery Act, 1968.

main_sections.section_title: Enforcement of payment of prescribed wages.
main_sections.description: Deals with the enforcement of payment of prescribed wages to agricultural workers. It outlines the process for conciliation officers to direct landowners to pay unpaid wages and the procedures for recovering such payments, including the possibility of recovery as arrears of public revenue.
Specifies the entitlement of agricultural workers to wages for over-time work and the rate at which such wages are to be calculated.

Details the procedure for the settlement of agricultural disputes through conciliation, with provisions for bringing parties to the dispute together and making efforts for an amicable settlement. It also outlines the process for referring disputes to the Labour Officer and the subsequent steps if settlement is not reached.
Provides for an appeal against any order passed by a Conciliation Officer or the Agricultural Tribunal.

main_sections.section_title: Decision in appeal in respect of prescribed wages
main_sections.description: Deals with decisions in appeals concerning prescribed wages, including the recovery of excess payments made by landowners.

main_sections.section_title: Reference or decision of disputes by Government
main_sections.description: Outlines the process by which the Government can refer or decide agricultural disputes, including those related to the area of land or the award of compensation.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government as respects awards
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to modify or withdraw awards made under the Act if it is considered inexpedient in the public interest.
Specifies penalties for obstructing Inspectors or Conciliation Officers in the discharge of their duties, or for refusing to afford them reasonable facilities.
Imposes penalties for making false statements or representations to avoid payments or for enabling any person to evade any provision of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for breach of settlement or award
main_sections.description: Details penalties for breaches of settlement or awards made under the Act.
Covers penalties for contraventions of the Act or its rules, where no other penalty is specifically provided.
Provides for enhanced penalties in cases of previous convictions under the Act.
Addresses offences committed by companies, making them liable for punishment.
Specifies that no court shall take cognizance of an offence punishable under the Act except on a complaint made by the Government or an authorized officer.
Sets a time limit for prosecutions under the Act.
Mandates the preparation and maintenance of a register of agricultural workers by the executive authority.

main_sections.section_title: Maintenance of registers and records by landowners
main_sections.description: Requires landowners to maintain certain registers and records as may be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Bar of jurisdiction of civil courts
main_sections.description: Stipulates that civil courts shall have no jurisdiction to entertain proceedings related to this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power to take evidence on oath, etc.
main_sections.description: Confers powers on authorities and officers to take evidence on oath and conduct investigations similar to those in civil courts.

main_sections.section_title: Recovery of money due from landowners
main_sections.description: Provides for the recovery of money due to agricultural workers from landowners, including through the Collector and as arrears of public revenue.

important_rules: Landowners must pay prescribed wages to agricultural workers.
Wages for over-time work are to be paid at a specified rate.
Disputes are to be settled through conciliation proceedings.
Inspectors and Conciliation Officers have the power to conduct inquiries and demand facilities.

penalties: Obstruction of Inspectors/Conciliation Officers: Imprisonment up to six months or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both.
False statements: Imprisonment up to six months or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both.
Breach of settlement/award: Imprisonment up to one year or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both, with additional penalties for subsequent breaches.
Other contraventions: Imprisonment up to six months or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both, with enhanced penalties for subsequent contraventions.
Enhanced penalty for previous conviction: Imprisonment up to six months but not less than one month, or fine up to two thousand rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Conciliation Officers, Labour Officers, Inspectors, Agricultural Tribunals, and the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through conciliation proceedings, appeals to tribunals, government orders, recovery of dues as public revenue, and prosecution for offences.

rights: Right to receive prescribed wages for agricultural work.
Right to receive wages for over-time work.
Right to have disputes settled through conciliation.
Right to appeal against orders.
duties: Duty of landowners to pay prescribed wages.
Duty of landowners to maintain registers and records.
Duty of all persons to cooperate with Inspectors and Conciliation Officers.
obligations: Landowners have an obligation to ensure proper payment of wages and to comply with awards and settlements.

key_procedures: Dispute settlement: Parties involved in an agricultural dispute should approach the Conciliation Officer for amicable settlement. If settlement is not reached, the dispute may be referred to the Labour Officer and subsequently to the Agricultural Tribunal.
Recovery of wages: If a landowner fails to pay prescribed wages, a Conciliation Officer can direct payment. If payment is not made, the amount can be recovered as arrears of public revenue.
Appeals: Appeals against orders of the Conciliation Officer lie with the Agricultural Tribunal. Further appeals can be made to the Government.
Maintenance of registers: Agricultural workers' registers are to be maintained by the executive authority, and landowners must maintain specified registers and records.
administration: The Act is administered by various authorities including the Labour Department, Conciliation Officers, Labour Officers, and the Agricultural Tribunal, with the Government having overarching powers.
important_notes: The Act aims to protect the interests of agricultural workers.
Provisions exist for the recovery of dues as arrears of public revenue, highlighting the seriousness of wage payment obligations.
There are specific limitations on the jurisdiction of civil courts regarding matters covered by this Act.

title: THE KERALA AGRICULTURAL WORKERS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1990
purpose: To amend the Kerala Agricultural Workers Act, 1974 for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to agricultural workers in Kerala and their dependents.

key_definitions.Board: Means the Agricultural Workers' Welfare Fund Board constituted under section 11.
key_definitions.Provident Fund: Means the Provident Fund constituted under section 8.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Agricultural Workers (Amendment) Act, 1990 and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of September, 1989.
Amends section 2 of the principal Act by substituting clauses (g) and (p) in the definition of 'Board' and 'Scheme' respectively.
Amends section 7 of the principal Act by substituting sub-section (5), item (b), the following item shall be substituted.
Amends section 8 of the principal Act by substituting 'Provident Fund' for 'Welfare Fund' in sub-section (1) and in sub-section (2) the words 'Welfare Fund' are substituted for 'Fund'.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 9.
main_sections.description: Replaces section 9 of the principal Act with new provisions regarding 'Contributions to the Fund'. It specifies contribution rates for land owners based on land extent and for registered agricultural workers. It also states that any loan, grant or advance made by Government of India, State Government, a local body, or any other institution shall be credited to the Fund, and loan grant or advance made by any authority or institution shall be utilised for no other purpose than the purpose for which it was given.
Amends section 11 of the principal Act by substituting 'Provident Fund' for 'Welfare Fund'.

Amends section 14 of the principal Act by substituting sub-section (3) to clarify that any amount standing to the credit of a member in the Fund at the time of his ceasing to be an agricultural worker, whether on the ground that he is over sixty years of age or that he is incapacitated and is unable to work or on the ground of cessation of his membership due to default in payment of contribution to the Fund or on any other ground, shall, subject to any deduction authorised by the Scheme, be paid to him and shall be free from any debt or other liability incurred by that member before his ceasing to be an agricultural worker.
Amends section 42 of the principal Act by substituting words, figures and brackets in sections 18, 20, 23, 24 clause (b) of sub-section (1) and sub-sections (3) and (4) of section 25.

Amends the schedule to the principal Act by substituting words, making changes to the manner of registration of agricultural workers and their contribution to the Fund, substituting expressions related to the Fund, and deleting and renumbering items.

Repeals the Kerala Agricultural Workers (Amendment) Ordinance, 1989 (9 of 1989) and states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Land owners contributing to the Fund are required to pay at the rate of ten rupees per annum per hectare of land.
Registered agricultural workers shall pay contribution to the Fund at the rate of two rupees per mensem.
Any loan, grant or advance made by the Government of India, the State Government, a local body, or any other institution shall be credited to the Fund.
The manner in which agricultural workers and the manner in which the agricultural workers shall pay contribution to the Fund is specified.

The manner in which accounts shall be kept, the investment of money belonging to the Fund in accordance with any direction issued or conditions specified by the Government, the preparation of the Budget, the audit of accounts and the submission of reports to Government are detailed.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated in the provided text, but implied to be government authorities and the Welfare Fund Board.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not explicitly detailed in the provided text.

rights: Agricultural workers and their dependents are eligible for benefits like superannuation, maternity benefit, medical assistance, educational assistance, dependent children's housing construction advance, advance for renovation and expansion of house or for maintenance or repair to house, advance for purchase of agricultural land, advance for marriage expenses of a member or his daughter/daughters, payment of insurance premium for the members, payment of old age pension, etc.
duties: Land owners have a duty to contribute to the Fund based on land extent.
Registered agricultural workers have a duty to contribute to the Fund on a monthly basis.
obligations: Land owners holding more than half a hectare but less than one hectare in extent of agricultural land shall pay contribution to the Fund at the rate of ten rupees per annum per hectare of land.
Registered agricultural workers shall pay contribution to the Fund at the rate of two rupees per mensem.
Any loan, grant or advance made by the Government of India, the State Government, a local body, or any other institution shall be credited to the Fund.

key_procedures: Contribution to the Fund by land owners and agricultural workers as specified.
Crediting of loans, grants, or advances to the Fund.
Registration of agricultural workers and their contribution to the Fund.
Management of Fund accounts, investment of funds, preparation of budget, audit of accounts, and submission of reports to the Government.
Payment of amounts standing to the credit of a member in the Fund upon cessation of being an agricultural worker, subject to deductions authorized by the Scheme.
administration: The Kerala Agricultural Workers Welfare Fund Board.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on September 1, 1989.
The Act repeals the Kerala Agricultural Workers (Amendment) Ordinance, 1989 (9 of 1989).

Any amount standing to the credit of a member in the Fund at the time of ceasing to be an agricultural worker shall be paid to him and shall be free from any debt or other liability incurred by that member.

The Fund is utilized for the welfare of agricultural workers or their dependents, including benefits such as superannuation, maternity benefit, medical assistance, educational assistance, housing advances, and old age pension.
The fee to be levied for any of the purposes specified in the schedule.

title: THE KERALA AGRICULTURISTS' DEBT RELIEF (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1973
purpose: An Act to amend the Kerala Agriculturists' Debt Relief Act, 1970, for the purpose hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to agriculturists in Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Agriculturists' Debt Relief (Amendment) Act, 1973 and it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 14th day of July, 1970.

Amends clause (4) of section 2 of the Kerala Agriculturists' Debt Relief Act, 1970 (11 of 1970) by substituting a new proviso regarding the right of the bank to recover the sum did not arise by reason of any assignment made or any transfer effected by operation of law, subsequent to the 1st day of July, 1957.

Repeals the Kerala Agriculturists' Debt Relief (Amendment) Ordinance, 1973 (1 of 1973) and provides that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: The Act came into force on the 14th day of July, 1970.
Specific amendments are made to Section 2 of the principal Act concerning the recovery of sums by banks.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided pages.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided pages.

rights: Right of a bank to recover a sum if it did not arise by reason of assignment or transfer by operation of law after July 1, 1957.

administration: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided pages.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Kerala Agriculturists' Debt Relief Act, 1970.
The Kerala Agriculturists' Debt Relief (Amendment) Ordinance, 1973 (1 of 1973) has been repealed.
Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

title: The Kerala Agriculturists Debt Relief (Amendment) Act, 1962
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Agriculturists Debt Relief Act, 1958.
scope: The Act applies to agriculturists in Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Agriculturists Debt Relief (Amendment) Act, 1962.

Amends section 18 of the Kerala Agriculturists Debt Relief Act, 1958 by re-numbering sub-section (1) and making specific substitutions within it concerning the amount of excess, value of homestead, and deposit of sums in court. It also introduces new provisions regarding charges and the first installment of excess sums.

important_rules: If the amount of excess, or where the value of the homestead exceeds both one-fourth of the entire assets and Rs. 6,500, the excess value of the homestead, whichever is smaller, shall be deposited by the debtor in court in fifteen half-yearly installments together with interest accrued.

There shall be a first charge on the homestead subject only to the charge for public revenue due on land as defined in the Revenue Recovery Act for the time being in force for any tax, cess, fee or such other dues chargeable by virtue of any enactment for the time being in force in respect of the land on which the homestead is situated.
The first installment of such excess amount shall be payable before the expiry of a period of six months from the date of allotment of the homestead.
key_procedures: Deposit of excess amounts in court through installments.
Payment of the first installment of excess sums within a specified timeframe.
important_notes: The amendment is made to the Kerala Agriculturists Debt Relief Act, 1958.
The Act received the assent of the President on 27th April, 1963.
The Act was published in the Gazette Extra ordinary, dated 29th April, 1963.

title: THE KERALA AGRICULTURISTS DEBT RELIEF ACT, 1958
purpose: To give relief to indebted agriculturists in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the whole of the Kerala State. The Act is intended to provide relief for the relief of indebted agriculturists in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.agriculturist: Means a person who has an interest, other than as a simple mortgage, in any agricultural or horticultural land, and shall include a varamdär, kudikidappukāran, kanikkāran, sām-belāldār, sambalādār, licensee, and tharikulakkāran, but shall not include: (i) any person assessed to sales-tax on a turnover which in the aggregate is not less than thirty thousand rupees in any two years within the three years immediately preceding the commencement of this Act, under the Madras General Sales-tax Act, 1939 or the General Sales-tax Act, 1125 or the Central Sales-tax Act, 1956 or the law of any other State relating to sales-tax. (ii) any person assessed to income-tax under the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922 in any two years within the three years immediately preceding the commencement of this Act. (iii) any person assessed to agricultural income-tax in any two years within the three years immediately preceding the commencement of this Act under the Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950 or under any other law relating to agricultural income-tax on an income exceeding five thousand rupees per annum, or any person liable to pay basic tax exceeding one hundred and fifty rupees per annum in any three years after 1950-51 and before the commencement of this Act.
key_definitions.court: Means any civil court having jurisdiction to entertain a suit for the recovery or discharge of a debt.
key_definitions.debt: Means any liability in cash or kind, whether secured or unsecured, due from or incurred by an agriculturist on or before the commencement of this Act, whether payable under a contract or under a decree or order of any Court, or otherwise, and includes any debt or balance of debt due at the commencement of this Act under the Madras Indebted Agriculturists (Re-payment of Debts) Act, 1955, or the Travancore-Cochin Indebted Agriculturists Relief Act, 1956, but does not include- (i) any sum payable to the State or the Central Government or to any local authority. (ii) any sum payable to the State Bank of India or the Reserve Bank of India or to any co-operative society including a land mortgage bank registered or deemed to be registered under the Travancore-Cochin Co-operative Societies Act, 1951 or the Madras Co-operative Societies Act, 1932, provided that the right of the bank or the society to recover the sum did not arise by reason of an assignment made subsequent to the last day of July, 1957. (iii) any liability arising out of a breach of trust; (iv) any liability in respect of maintenance; (v) any liability in respect of wages or remuneration due as salary or otherwise for services rendered; (vi) any debt which represents the price of goods purchased for purpose of trade; (vii) any liability for which a charge is provided under sub-clause (b) of clause (4) of section 55 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882; (viii) any debt or debts due to a widow at the commencement of this Act, provided that the value of the property owned by her at the commencement of this Act, including the principal amount of debt or debts so due does not exceed six thousand rupees. (ix) any rent payable in respect of any land or building.
