(x) any liability incurred or arising out of a chitty or kuri which is registered or licensed under the Travancore Chitties Act, 1107, or conducted under any chit fund scheme, and which had not terminated one year before the commencement of this Act.
key_definitions.foreman: Means when the legal representative of a deceased foreman or guardian of a foreman of unsound mind and the conditions imposed were being done. (b) when the legal representative of a deceased foreman or guardian of a foreman of unsound mind and the subscriber selected thereafter fail to conduct the chitty or kuri or to make suitable arrangements for the further conduct of the chitty or kuri or (c) on the failure of the foreman to pay the prize amount to the subscriber within one month from the date thereof. or (d) on the failure of the foreman to conduct the chitty or kuri at any instalment or on any other date before the next instalment as may be agreed upon in writing by a majority of the non-prized subscribers.
key_definitions.kudlikidappukāran: means a person who has no homestead or land of his own to erect a homestead and- (i) who has been permitted with or without an obligation to pay rent by an owner of land or any other person in lawful possession, to have the use and occupation of a portion of the land in his possession for the purpose of erecting a homestead. or (ii) who is in occupation of a hut situated in a portion of the land with the permission of the person entitled to possession of such land, but otherwise has no interest in the land.
key_definitions.malabar: means the area comprising the Malabar district referred to in sub-section (2) of section 2 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.
key_definitions.principal: means the amount originally advanced together with such sum, if any, as has been subsequently advanced, notwithstanding any stipulation to treat any interest as principal and notwithstand-ing that the debt has been renewed or included in a fresh document whether by the same debtor or by his heirs, legal representatives, or assigns or by any other person acting on his behalf or in his interest and whether in favour of the same creditor or his heirs, legal representatives or assigns or of any other person acting on his behalf or in his interest.
key_definitions.varam: means a joint Hindu family or a marumakkāthāyam tarwad or tavazhi, or a kudumba, or kavaru or an illom.
key_definitions.varamdär: means a person who under the system known as varam, pathivaram, pankuvāram or pankupattam or by any other name, has agreed, whether in writing or not, with the owner or other person in lawful possession of any land, to cultivate the land and share with him the produce of the land.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called The Kerala Agriculturists Debt Relief Act, 1958. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force at once.
Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'agriculturist', 'court', and 'debt'. It also includes explanations for these definitions, clarifying their scope and application.

Specifies that no application for execution of a decree in respect of a debt shall be made against any agriculturist in any court before the expiry of six months from the commencement of this Act. It also clarifies when a decree for possession of land shall not be deemed to be a decree in respect of a debt.

Deals with the payment of debt in instalments. Subject to the provisions of sub-section (3) notwithstanding anything contained in any law or contract or in any decree or order of Court, any debt may be discharged in the manner specified in sub-section (2). It also specifies the rate of payment of each instalment.

main_sections.section_title: Calculation of interest in the case of debt.
main_sections.description: Provides for the calculation of interest in the case of debt for the purposes of payment under this Act, stating that no interest shall be deemed to be payable towards the debt than one half of the principal shall be deemed payable towards which accrued due till the commencement of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Application of payment towards debt under Section 4 and limit of time for execution of decree.
main_sections.description: When any amount has been paid or recovered towards any debt referred to in section 4, the Court shall apply it in the order of costs due under the decree (where the debt has ripened into a decree), then, interest as re-calculated under section 4 and next towards principal. It also specifies that the provisions of section 4 shall, for purposes of execution, be deemed to be a subsequent order of Court within the meaning of clause (b) of sub-section (1) of section 45 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

Where, before the commencement of this Act, a Court has passed a decree for repayment of a debt, it shall, on the application of any judgment-debtor who is an agriculturist or on the application of the decree-holder, apply the provisions of this Act to such decree and shall, notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, amend the decree accordingly or enter satisfaction, as the case may be. The provisions of sub-section (1) shall also apply to cases where, after the commencement of this Act, a Court has passed a decree for the repayment of any debt.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Court to decide doubts and disputes regarding amount payable under Section 4.
main_sections.description: Any debtor or creditor may apply to the Court for an order fixing the amount payable under section 4 and in that application he shall state what is the correct amount payable according to him. If the debt is covered by a decree, the application shall be made to the Court which passed the decree. If the debt is not covered by a decree, the application shall be made to the Court competent to pass a decree for the recovery of the debt. An application made by a debtor under sub-section (1) shall be dismissed if the debtor fails to deposit with the Court. before which such application is pending, the amount of any instalment which on his admission is payable by him under the provisions of this Act and has accrued due and no second application for the same purpose shall be entertained. Provided that the Court may extend the time for making the deposit for any just and sufficient cause. A proceeding under this section shall, for purposes of inquiry and disposal, be deemed to be a proceeding to which section 141 of the Civil Procedure Code, 1908, applies. The Court shall by its order determine the amount which the debtor has to pay under the provisions of section 4 and the time.
Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Repeals any existing law, custom or usage in force in the State of Kerala, in so far as it is inconsistent with the provisions of this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: No application for execution of a decree in respect of a debt shall be made against any agriculturist in any court before the expiry of six months from the commencement of this Act.
Rule 2: Any debt may be discharged in instalments, subject to specific provisions regarding payment schedules.
Rule 3: The interest payable on debt shall not exceed one half of the principal amount that accrued due till the commencement of the Act.
Rule 4: Payments made towards debt shall be applied in order of costs, then interest, and finally principal.
Rule 5: Courts have the power to decide doubts and disputes regarding the amount payable under Section 4.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts in the State of Kerala.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through applications to the court for execution of decrees, or for determination of amounts payable. The Act also provides for amendment of existing decrees.

rights: Right to have debts discharged in instalments.
Right to have interest calculation capped at half the principal accrued due.
Right to have disputes regarding debt amounts resolved by the Court.
duties: Duty to pay debts as per the provisions of the Act, including instalments where applicable.
Duty to comply with court orders regarding debt settlement.
obligations: Agriculturists have an obligation to settle their debts according to the relief provided by the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: To seek relief under the Act, a debtor or creditor can apply to the court to fix the amount payable under Section 4. If the debt is covered by a decree, the application goes to the court that passed the decree. If not, it goes to the competent court.

Procedure 2: If a debtor fails to deposit any admitted instalment amount with the court while an application is pending, the application can be dismissed. However, the court may extend the time for deposit for just and sufficient cause.
Procedure 3: Courts can amend certain decrees to align with the provisions of this Act, or enter satisfaction if the decree is satisfied according to the Act's terms.
administration: The State Government has the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, indicating administrative oversight.
important_notes: The Act provides relief to 'agriculturists' as defined within the Act, with specific exclusions.
The definition of 'debt' is broad but excludes certain types of liabilities like taxes, maintenance, wages, and trade debts.
Explanations are provided for various definitions to clarify their meaning and application.
The Act overrides conflicting provisions in any existing law, custom, or usage in force in the State of Kerala.
A decree for possession of land shall not be deemed to be a decree in respect of a debt by reason merely of means profits being also included in such decree.

title: The Kerala Agriculturists Debt Relief Act, 1970
purpose: To provide for the relief of agriculturists from their debts and to regulate certain transactions relating to agricultural land.
scope: The Act applies to agriculturists in the State of Kerala. It covers transactions entered into before the commencement of the Act and certain types of mortgages and melpattoms granted by agriculturists.

key_definitions.agriculturist: A person who cultivates land personally or for whose personal cultivation land is used, and who derives his principal income from agriculture.
key_definitions.debt: Any liability, whether secured or unsecured, whether payable immediately or at a future date, whether certain or contingent, arising out of a loan or advance or otherwise, but does not include liability for maintenance.

main_sections.section_title: Certain transactions to be deemed mortgages
main_sections.description: Deals with transactions entered into by agriculturists on or after July 14, 1958, which are disguised as sales or leases but are in reality related to debts. It also allows persons described as agents or servants in cultivation contracts to prove they are tenants.
Specifies how decrees and orders for debt recovery should be made against agriculturists, including provisions for instalments and joint liabilities with non-agriculturists.

main_sections.section_title: Special provision in respect of certain mortgages by agriculturists
main_sections.description: Provides special provisions for subsisting mortgages executed by agriculturists, allowing them to recover mortgaged property by depositing a portion of the mortgage amount, arrears of interest, and the value of improvements. It also details the process for recovering the balance amount and termination of leases.

main_sections.section_title: Sales with condition to repurchase, to be deemed mortgages
main_sections.description: Declares sales with a condition to repurchase within a stipulated period, where the period has not expired at the commencement of the Act, to be deemed as mortgages, and applies the provisions of Section 11.

Provides for the termination of melpattoms granted by agriculturists for periods of two years or more, allowing the agriculturist to terminate the melpattom on application to the court and depositing a portion of the advance outstanding. It outlines the process for final determination of amounts and recovery of balances.
Allows an agriculturist to deposit instalments of a debt in court and apply for recording part satisfaction. It also provides for extension of time for such deposits.

main_sections.section_title: Application to court by persons unable to pay their debts
main_sections.description: Enables an agriculturist unable to pay their debts to apply to the court for a full settlement of such debts. It outlines the particulars to be included in the application and the court's power to stay proceedings during the pendency of such an application.

important_rules: Transactions disguised as sales or leases of immovable property by agriculturists since July 14, 1958, can be proven to be related to debts. The income or usufructs are appropriated towards interest and then principal.

Mortgaged property can be recovered by an agriculturist mortgagor by depositing one-third of the mortgage amount, arrears of interest, and the value of improvements. The balance is to be paid in instalments.
Melpattoms granted by agriculturists for two years or more can be terminated by the agriculturist by depositing one-third of the advance outstanding.
An agriculturist unable to pay debts can apply for a full settlement of debts, leading to a stay of suits or execution of decrees against them.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts in Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through court orders, decrees, and execution proceedings as laid out in the Act and the Code of Civil Procedure.

rights: Right of an agriculturist to prove that a transaction is a debt.
Right of an agriculturist mortgagor to recover mortgaged property.
Right of an agriculturist to terminate a melpattom.
Right of an agriculturist to apply for a full settlement of debts.
Right to have debts restructured into instalments.
duties: Duty to pay debts as per the Act's provisions or court orders.
Duty to deposit specified amounts for debt relief or recovery of property/termination of melpattom.
Duty to provide necessary particulars in applications to the court.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to instalment payment schedules.
Obligation to pay interest at the rate specified in Section 5 or 6 percent per annum as applicable.
Obligation to deposit court-fees as prescribed.

key_procedures: Procedure for proving a transaction as a debt: An agriculturist may apply to the court to plead and adduce evidence that a transaction is really in respect of a debt.

Procedure for recovery of mortgaged property: An agriculturist mortgagor applies to the court, deposits specified amounts, and the court orders possession. The mortgagee recovers the balance by sale in instalments.
Procedure for termination of melpattom: An agriculturist applies to the court, deposits a portion of the advance outstanding, and the court determines the balance and orders payment in instalments.

Procedure for settlement of debts: An agriculturist unable to pay debts applies to the court with full details of claims and property. The court fixes a hearing date, issues notices, and may stay proceedings.
administration: The administration of the Act is primarily through the judicial system (Courts) in Kerala, with procedural aspects likely overseen by the Revenue Department or a designated authority for agricultural matters.
important_notes: Sub-section (3) of Section 9 does not affect the rights of bona fide alienees of the creditor who derived rights before July 25, 1968.
Section 11 (8) provides special provisions for mortgages where the property is leased back to the mortgagor.
Section 11 (10) clarifies that the section does not affect the rights of mortgagees conferred with the rights of a tenant under any law.
The Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, applies to applications made under Section 14.
Applications under Section 15 require specific particulars to be included and verified in the manner prescribed by the Code of Civil Procedure.

title: THE KERALA AGRICULTURISTS DEBT RELIEF (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1960
purpose: To amend The Kerala Agriculturists Debt Relief Act, 1958.
scope: Applies to agriculturists in Kerala, specifically concerning debt relief.

key_definitions.melpattam: Any transaction relating to the usufructs of trees for a specific period in recoupment of an advance made or promised.
key_definitions.melpattamdhar: Mortgagor, debtor and creditor, including their heirs, legal representatives and assigns.

main_sections.description: Names the act as The Kerala Agriculturists Debt Relief (Amendment) Act, 1960 and states when it comes into force. It also provides a historical note about its enactment and publication.

Amends Section 2 of the principal Act (The Kerala Agriculturists Debt Relief Act, 1958). It makes several substitutions and additions to the definitions and provisions within this section, including those related to 'horticultural land', 'varomdar', and 'in the State of Kerala'. It also clarifies the meaning of terms and provides specific stipulations for sub-clauses.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 4, Act 31 of 1958
main_sections.description: Substitutes the entire Section 4 of the principal Act. The new Section 4 deals with 'Payment of debt in instalments', specifying conditions and rules regarding the repayment of debts, including those to banking companies and the total amount payable by instalments.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 5, Act 31 of 1958
main_sections.description: Substitutes the entire Section 5 of the principal Act. The new Section 5 addresses 'Interest payable on debt and rents.', detailing how interest is calculated, including specific rates and conditions for debts incurred under various circumstances. It also includes provisions for the determination of interest and related charges.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new section 11A, Act 31 of 1958
main_sections.description: Inserts a new Section 11A into the principal Act, titled 'Special provisions regarding certain melpattoms'. This section provides specific rules and explanations regarding the 'advance amount' that bears to the total amount of the melpattam as the unexpired term of the melpattam bears to its full term, particularly in cases of dispute.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new section 23A, Act 31 of 1958
main_sections.description: Inserts a new Section 23A into the principal Act, titled 'Appeals'. This section outlines the procedure for appeals against orders passed under various sections of the principal Act, specifying that appeals shall lie to the District Court and must be filed within sixty days of the date of the order appealed against.

Amends Section 26 of the principal Act. It clarifies that the Travancore Debt Relief Act, 1115, shall be renumbered as sub-section (1) of that section, and a new sub-section (2) is added concerning the applicability of provisions of repeated repeal under court law or an order passed for payment in instalments to the option of the debtor to be discharged in accordance with the provisions of those enactments.

important_rules: Rule 1: Debts are to be paid in instalments, with specific conditions on the number of instalments and their timing.
Rule 2: Interest calculations on debts are subject to specific rates and conditions, particularly for banking companies.
Rule 3: Provisions are made for the calculation and payment of advance amounts concerning melpattoms.
Rule 4: Appeals against orders passed under certain sections of the Act must be filed within sixty days.
Rule 5: The provisions of the Indian Limitation Act, 1908, are applicable to appeals and applications filed under this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly detailed in the provided excerpt, but implied to be judicial and administrative authorities responsible for debt relief and related legal matters.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through court proceedings, appeals, and adherence to the rules and procedures outlined in the Act.

rights: Right of agriculturists to have their debts relieved under specific conditions.
Right to appeal against certain orders passed under the Act.
duties: Duty to repay debts in accordance with the instalment provisions.
Duty to comply with the interest calculation and payment rules.
obligations: Obligation to pay debts before the commencement of the Act in certain cases.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Determining the amount of a debt and its repayment schedule, including interest.
Procedure 2: Appealing against orders related to debt relief or instalment payments.
Procedure 3: Calculation of advance amounts and their relation to melpattam terms.
Procedure 4: Application of provisions of the Indian Limitation Act for filing appeals and applications.
administration: The administration likely falls under the purview of the Kerala State Government's legal and revenue departments, responsible for implementing debt relief measures.
important_notes: Received the assent of the President on 21st January 1961 and published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 30th January 1961.
The Act makes extensive amendments to the principal Act of 1958, substituting entire sections and inserting new ones.
The provisions concerning the recovery of debt due to a banking company in liquidation are specifically addressed.
Clarifications are provided for the interpretation of terms like 'melpattam' and 'melpattamdhar'.
The Act aims to provide relief to agriculturists by restructuring their debt obligations.

title: THE KERALA AGRICULTURISTS' LOANS ACT, 1961
purpose: To consolidate and amend the laws relating to loans of money by the Government for land and agricultural improvements in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and its agriculturists.

key_definitions.Collector: The Collector of the district or any officer empowered by the Government to discharge the functions of a Collector under this Act.
key_definitions.improvement: Means any work which adds to the value of the land, and includes the following, namely: the construction of wells, tanks, sluice bund and other works for the storage, supply or distribution of water for the purposes of agriculture or for the use of men and cattle employed in agriculture; the preparation of land for irrigation; the drainage, reclamation, from rivers or other waters, or protection from floods or from erosion or other damage by water, of land used for agricultural purposes or land which is vulnerable; the construction of permanent bunds around Punja or Kayal fields used for agricultural purposes; the reclamation, clearance, enclosure of permanent improvement of land for agricultural purposes; the construction of walls, boundary walls (Kaviyalas), store houses, farm houses and cattle sheds; the renewal or reconstruction of any of the foregoing works, or alterations therein or additions thereto; the planting or rearing of such kinds of plants and crops as may be notified by the Government; such other works as the Government may, from time to time, by notification declare to be improvements for the purposes of this Act.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (the whole of the State of Kerala), and that it shall come into force at once.
This section defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Collector', 'improvement', and 'prescribed'.

main_sections.section_title: Purpose for which loans may be granted under this Part
main_sections.description: Loans under this Part can be granted by the Government or any officer or authority empowered by the Government for making improvements to land. These improvements are to be notified in the Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Mode of dealing with application for loans
main_sections.description: Applications for loans are to be dealt with by the authority to whom the application is made. This authority must publish a notice in the Gazette and fix a place and time for hearing objections before deciding.
Loans are repayable in such manner and at such time as may be prescribed by rules. If not paid, the loan becomes recoverable as if it were arrears of land revenue.
Any encumbrance created on the land offered as security for a loan is void against the Government after the order granting the loan.

Details the conditions under which loans are recoverable, including arrears of land revenue, and the consequences for the borrower and surety. It also states that encumbrances on land are free after the loan is granted and recovered.

main_sections.section_title: Order granting loan conclusive on certain points
main_sections.description: An order granting a loan is conclusive evidence that the work described is an improvement and that the person mentioned had the right to a such improvement.

The Government may make rules for carrying out the purposes of Part II, including rules for applications, manner of conducting inquiries, security for loans, interest rates, inspection of works, and the manner of keeping and auditing accounts.
The Government may make rules for carrying out the purposes of Part III, which deals with loans for distress, purchase of seed, cattle, etc.
Loans granted under Part III are recoverable in the same manner as loans under Part II, including if the borrower has become surety for the repayment.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of joint borrowers as among themselves
main_sections.description: When a loan is made under Part II or Part III to members of a village community, they are jointly and severally bound to the Government for repayment. The statement showing the portion of the amount each person is bound to contribute is entered upon the order granting the loan and is conclusive evidence.
This section repeals The Land Improvement Loans Act, 1883, and The Kerala Agriculturists Loans Act, 1884, and any corresponding provisions in other Acts, subject to certain savings.

important_rules: Rules made under Section 9 and 10 must be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

Rules made under Section 9 for carrying out the purposes of Part II are to be laid before the Legislative Assembly as soon as possible after they are made and are subject to such modifications as the Assembly may make during the session in which they are so laid or the session immediately following.

Rules made under Section 10 for carrying out the purposes of Part III are to be laid before the Legislative Assembly as soon as possible after they are made and are subject to such modifications as the Assembly may make during the session in which they are so laid or the session immediately following.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Collector, and other officers empowered by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Loans are recoverable as arrears of land revenue. Encumbrances on land are void against the Government. Liability of joint borrowers is joint and several.

rights: Agriculturists have the right to apply for loans for land and agricultural improvements.
Borrowers have the right to have their loan applications considered and heard.
duties: Borrowers have the duty to repay loans as per the prescribed manner and time.
Joint borrowers have the duty to be jointly and severally liable for the loan.
obligations: Obligation to create encumbrances on land offered as security only after the loan is granted and in accordance with the law.

key_procedures: Application for loans is made to the designated authority.
The authority publishes a notice for objections.
The authority hears objections and passes an order.
Loans are repayable in a prescribed manner.
Recovery of loans is done as arrears of land revenue if not paid.
Rules may prescribe procedures for various aspects of loan management.
administration: The Government of Kerala and officers empowered by the Government.
important_notes: The Act consolidates and amends laws relating to agricultural loans.
Certain previous Acts are repealed, but this does not affect advances made before the commencement of this Act.
The rate of interest shall not be less than three per cent nor more than five per cent per annum.
The Government may, from time to time, by notification, declare to be improvements for the purposes of this Act, such other works as they deem fit.

title: THE KERALA ANATOMY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1964
purpose: To amend the Kerala Anatomy Act, 1957.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala and concerns the lawful possession and handling of dead bodies for anatomical examination and dissection.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Anatomy (Amendment) Act, 1964 and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification, appoint.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the Long Title and Preamble, Act 17 of 1957.
main_sections.description: This section omits the 'unclained' from the Long Title and Preamble of the principal Act (The Kerala Anatomy Act, 1957).

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new section 4A in Act 17 of 1957.
main_sections.description: Inserts a new section (4A) into the principal Act. This section deals with the taking possession of dead bodies for anatomical examination and dissection.

important_rules: Taking possession of dead bodies: A party lawfully in possession of a dead person's body may permit an authorised officer to take possession for anatomical examination or dissection, provided the officer has a reason to believe that the deceased had expressed an objection to their body being so dealt with after death, or that the surviving spouse or any near relative of the deceased objected to the body being so dealt with.

Circumstances for permitting possession: The party lawfully in possession of a dead person's body may permit the authorised officer to take possession for anatomical examination or dissection under specific conditions, including doubt regarding the cause of death or when it is expedient to do so, and after informing the police officer as per the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.

No permission for specific bodies: Permission to take possession of a dead body under this section is not required to be obtained from the party who was lawfully in possession of the body after death in cases where the body is of a deceased person who has been entrusted with the body solely for the purpose of its interment, burial, cremation or disposal otherwise.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government (by notification)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By bringing the Act into force on a specified date.

rights: The right of an authorised officer to take possession of a dead body for anatomical examination or dissection under specific conditions.
The right of the surviving spouse or near relative of the deceased to object to the body being dealt with.
duties: Duty of the party lawfully in possession to permit authorised officer to take possession of a dead body under specified circumstances.
Duty to inform the police officer regarding the taking of a dead body under certain conditions.

key_procedures: Bringing the Act into force: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Government through notification.

Taking possession of dead bodies: An authorised officer can take possession of a dead body for anatomical examination or dissection if the party in lawful possession permits them, and there is no objection from the surviving spouse or near relative, and the deceased had not objected. Exceptions apply to bodies held solely for interment, burial, cremation, or disposal.
administration: Government of Kerala
important_notes: The amendment specifically addresses the omission of the word 'unclaimed' from the principal Act.
The new section 4A provides detailed provisions regarding the taking possession of dead bodies for anatomical purposes, including conditions and exceptions.

title: THE KERALA ANATOMY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1988
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala Anatomy Act, 1957.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Anatomy Act, 1957.

main_sections.description: (1) This Act may be called the Kerala Anatomy (Amendment) Act, 1988. (2) It shall come into force at once.

In section 10 of the Kerala Anatomy Act, 1957 (17 of 1957), after sub-section (2), the following sub-section shall be inserted, namely: "(3) Every rule made under this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before the Legislative Assembly while it is in session for a total period of fourteen days which may be comprised in one session or in two successive sessions, and if, before the expiry of the session in which it is so laid or the session immediately following, the Legislative Assembly makes any modification in the rule or decides that the rule should not be made, the rule shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect, as the case may be; so however that any such modification or annulment shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that rule."

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Legislative Assembly (for laying and modifying rules)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the process of laying rules before the Legislative Assembly and potential modification or annulment.

key_procedures: Rules made under the Act must be laid before the Legislative Assembly for a total period of fourteen days (in one or two successive sessions).
The Legislative Assembly can modify or annul the rule during this period.
Modifications or annulments are without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under the rule.
administration: Law (Legislation-C) Department, Government of Kerala

title: The Kerala Anatomy Act, 1957
purpose: To provide for the supply of bodies of deceased persons to teaching medical institutions for the purpose of anatomical examination and dissection.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. It applies to unclaimed dead bodies in hospitals, prisons, and public places, and their use for anatomical examination and dissection by teaching medical institutions. It also covers the consent for using deceased persons' bodies for anatomical purposes.

key_definitions.authorized_officer: An officer authorized by the Government under Section 3 of the Act.
key_definitions.hospital: Any hospital established or maintained by the Government, any municipal council, or other local authority, and any other hospital declared by the Government for the purposes of this Act.
key_definitions.near_relative: Includes a wife, husband, parent, son, daughter, brother, or sister. It also includes any other person related by lineal consanguinity within three degrees or collateral consanguinity within six degrees, or by marriage with any of the aforesaid relatives, as defined in the Indian Succession Act, 1925.
key_definitions.teaching_medical_institution: Institutions specified in the Schedule to the Act, and any other institution declared by the Government for the purposes of this Act.
key_definitions.unclaimed_body: The body of a person who dies in a hospital, prison, or public place, which has not been claimed by any of his near relatives or by any recognised religious or public institution belonging to the religion of the deceased within a prescribed time.

main_sections.description: Defines the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of the State of Kerala), and commencement dates for different provisions.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'authorized officer', 'hospital', 'near relative', 'prescribed', 'teaching medical institution', and 'unclaimed body'.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to authorize officers to act under section 4
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to authorize officers, by notification, to act under Section 4 of the Act within a specified area.

main_sections.section_title: Unclaimed dead bodies in hospitals, prisons and public places how to be dealt with
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for dealing with unclaimed dead bodies found in hospitals, prisons, and public places, including reporting to the authorized officer and handing over to teaching medical institutions, with provisions for religious institutions and exceptions.

main_sections.section_title: Taking possession of dead bodies with the prior consent of deceased persons
main_sections.description: Introduces provisions for taking possession of dead bodies based on the prior written or oral consent of the deceased person, with safeguards and exceptions.

main_sections.section_title: Doubt or dispute as to near relative to be referred to Magistrate of the First Class
main_sections.description: Specifies that any doubt or dispute regarding whether a person is a near relative will be referred to a Magistrate of the First Class, whose decision will be final.
Prescribes penalties for disposing of or abetting the disposal of unclaimed bodies contrary to the Act, or obstructing authorized officers or institutions.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of Police and other officers to assist in obtaining possession of unclaimed bodies
main_sections.description: Mandates police, medical, public health, local authority officers, and village officers to assist authorized officers in their duties.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of persons acting under this Act
main_sections.description: Provides protection from legal proceedings for anything done or intended to be done in good faith in pursuance of the Act.
Declares officers appointed or authorized under the Act as public servants under the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, with specific areas for rule-making detailed, and a provision for laying rules before the Legislative Assembly.

important_rules: Rule relating to the period within which a near relative may claim a deceased person's body (as per Section 10(2)(a)).
Rule relating to the procedure for the disposal of an unclaimed body (as per Section 10(2)(b)).
Rule relating to the conditions under which institutions may be recognised for the purpose of Section 4(3) (as per Section 10(2)(c)).
Rule relating to the manner in which a body may be preserved from decay (as per Section 10(2)(d)).
Rule relating to the procedure for proceedings under Section 5(1) (as per Section 10(2)(e)).
Rules may also cover other prescribed matters (as per Section 10(2)(f)).

penalties: Fine which may extend to five hundred rupees for disposing of, abetting the disposal of, or obstructing the taking possession of, removing, or using of an unclaimed body in a manner not provided by the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Authorized officers, authorities in charge of teaching medical institutions, police officers (in certain circumstances), and other officers as mandated by the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings for violations of the Act's provisions, including obstruction and improper disposal of bodies. Police and other designated officers are bound to assist in the enforcement.

rights: Right of near relatives or religious/public institutions to claim bodies.
Right of teaching medical institutions to receive bodies for anatomical examination, if required.
Right of persons acting in good faith under the Act to protection from legal proceedings.
duties: Duty of authorities in charge of hospitals/prisons to report unclaimed bodies.
Duty of authorized officers to take possession of unclaimed bodies and hand them over appropriately.
Duty of police and other specified officers to assist authorized officers.
Duty of institutions to adhere to prescribed conditions for recognition if dealing with bodies under Section 4(3).
obligations: Obligation to claim bodies within prescribed times.
Obligation to follow the procedures outlined in the Act for the handling and disposal of bodies.
Obligation to obtain prior consent for using a deceased person's body for anatomical examination if such consent was expressed.
Obligation for authorities to preserve bodies from decay as prescribed.

key_procedures: Reporting of unclaimed bodies by hospital/prison authorities to the authorized officer, with intimation to religious/public institutions (Section 4(1)).

Authorized officer taking possession of unclaimed bodies and handing them over to teaching medical institutions, with exceptions for religious claims or deceased's prior declarations (Section 4(1), 4(2), 4(3)).
Referral of disputes regarding near relatives to a Magistrate of the First Class (Section 5).
Procedure for taking possession of bodies with the deceased's prior consent (Section 4A).

Forwarding of bodies to police officers under Section 174 of the Code of Criminal Procedure in cases of doubt regarding cause of death or as deemed expedient by the authorized officer (Section 4(4), 4A(3)).
Disposal of unclaimed bodies not required by teaching medical institutions as prescribed (Section 4(5)).
Preservation of bodies from decay pending decisions (Section 5(2)).
administration: The Government of Kerala is responsible for authorizing officers, making notifications, and making rules under the Act. The Act also involves the administration of teaching medical institutions, hospitals, prisons, and local authorities.
important_notes: Omitted text indicated by [*********] suggests that certain parts of the original Act might have been modified or removed by subsequent amendments (e.g., Act 3 of 1964).
The Act was amended in 1964 (Act 3 of 1964) and 1984 (Act 30 of 1984) and 1988 (Act 23 of 1988), indicating potential changes to its provisions.

Bodies can be handed over to religious or public institutions under specific conditions, especially if a near relative cannot claim it due to reasons beyond their control or if the deceased expressed an objection to dissection (Section 4(3)).
The Act provides for consent-based use of bodies for anatomical examination (Section 4A).
Rules made under the Act must be laid before the Legislative Assembly, and can be modified or annulled by the Assembly (Section 10(3)).

title: The Kerala Ancient Monuments And Archaeological Sites And Remains Act, 1969
purpose: To provide for the preservation of ancient monuments and archaeological sites and remains, other than those of national importance, for the regulation of archaeological excavations and for the protection of sculptures, carvings and other like objects.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.ancient monument: Means any structure, erection or monument, or any tumulus or place of internment, or any cave, rock-sculpture, inscription or monolith, which is of historical, archaeological or artistic interest and which has been in existence for not less than one hundred years and includes the remains of an ancient monument, the site of an ancient monument, and such portion of land adjoining the site of an ancient monument as may be required for fencing or covering in or otherwise preserving such monument, and the means of access to, and convenient inspection of, an ancient monument.
key_definitions.antiquity: Includes (i) any coin, sculpture, manuscript, epigraph or other work of art or craftsmanship, (ii) any article, object or thing detached from a building or cave, (iii) any article, object or thing illustrative of science, art, crafts, literature, religion, customs, morals or politics in bygone ages, (iv) any article object or thing of historical interest, and (v) any article, object or thing declared by the Government, by notification, to be an antiquity for the purposes of this Act, which has been in existence for not less than one hundred years.
key_definitions.archaeological officer: Means an officer of the Department of Archaeology of the Government not lower in rank than an epigraphic assistant.
key_definitions.archaeological sites and remains: Means any area which contains or is reasonably believed to contain ruins or relics of historical or archaeological importance which have been in existence for not less than one hundred years, and includes such portion of land adjoining the area as may be required for fencing or covering in or otherwise preserving it, and the means of access to, and convenient inspection of, the area, but does not include any archaeological site or remains declared by or under any law made by Parliament to be of national importance.
key_definitions.director: Means the Director of Archaeology and includes any officer authorised by the Government to exercise the powers and perform the duties of the Director under this Act.
key_definitions.maintain: Includes its grammatical variations and cognate expressions, includes the fencing, covering in, repair, restoring and cleansing of a protected monument, and the doing of any act which may be necessary for the purpose of preserving a protected monument or of securing convenient access thereto;
key_definitions.notification: Means a notification published in the Gazette;
key_definitions.owner: Includes (i) a joint owner invested with powers of management on behalf of himself and other joint owners and the successor-in-title of any such owner; and (ii) any manager or trustee exercising powers of management and the successor-in-office of any such manager or trustee; (iii) 'prescribed' means prescribed by rules made under this Act; (j) 'protected area' means any archaeological site and remains which is declared to be a protected area or under this Act; (k) 'protected monument' means an ancient monument which is declared to be a protected monument or by the Government, by notification, gives two months' notice of their intention to declare such ancient monument or archaeological site and remains to be a protected monument or a protected area, as the case may be, and a copy of every such notification shall be affixed in a conspicuous place near the monument or site and remains, as the case may be.
key_definitions.protected monument: Means an ancient monument which is declared to be a protected monument by the Government, by notification.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1968, extends to the whole of the State of Kerala, and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'ancient monument', 'antiquity', 'archaeological officer', 'archaeological sites and remains', 'director', 'maintain', 'notification', 'owner', 'prescribed', 'protected area', and 'protected monument'.

main_sections.section_title: Certain ancient monuments, etc., deemed to be protected monuments or areas
main_sections.description: Declares that all ancient monuments and historical monuments which have been declared under the Ancient Monuments Preservation Act, 1904, or the Travancore Ancient Monuments Preservation Act, IX of 1110 (Cochin Act) to be protected monuments, and any area which has been declared under any of the said Acts to be a protected area, but which has not been declared by or under any law made by Parliament to be of national importance, shall be deemed to be protected monuments for the purposes of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to declare ancient monuments etc., to be protected monuments and areas
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to declare any ancient monument or archaeological site and remains to be a protected monument or a protected area, after giving two months' notice of their intention and affixing a copy of the notification in a conspicuous place. It also details the process for persons interested in such monuments or sites to raise objections.

main_sections.section_title: Acquisition of rights in a protected monument
main_sections.description: Grants the Director, with the sanction of the Government, the power to purchase or take a lease of, or accept a gift or bequest of, any protected monument. It also specifies procedures for protected monuments without an owner and the owner's rights and responsibilities.

main_sections.section_title: Preservation of protected monument by agreement
main_sections.description: Allows the Director, with the sanction of the Government, to propose an agreement with the owner of a protected monument for its maintenance. The agreement can include provisions for maintenance, custody, and duties of persons employed, restriction of owner's rights, payment of expenses, and termination of the agreement.

main_sections.section_title: Relinquishment of Government rights in a monument
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to relinquish its rights in a monument.

main_sections.section_title: Right of access to protected monuments
main_sections.description: Grants the public the right of access to protected monuments.

main_sections.section_title: Restrictions of enjoyment of property rights in protected areas
main_sections.description: Allows for restrictions on the enjoyment of property rights in protected areas.

main_sections.section_title: Power to acquire a protected area
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to acquire a protected area.
Deals with excavations within protected areas.

main_sections.section_title: Excavation in areas other than protected areas
main_sections.description: Deals with excavations in areas other than protected areas.

main_sections.section_title: Compulsory_purchase of antiquities, etc., discovered during excavation operations
main_sections.description: Allows for the compulsory purchase of antiquities discovered during excavation operations.
Covers excavation and related activities for archaeological purposes.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to control moving of antiquities
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to control the movement of antiquities.
Allows for the purchase of antiquities by the Government.
Deals with compensation for loss or damage.

main_sections.section_title: Assessment of market value or compensation
main_sections.description: Outlines the process for assessing market value or compensation.
Allows for the delegation of powers.
Specifies penalties for contravention of the Act.
Defines the jurisdiction for trying offences under the Act.
Declares certain offences under the Act to be cognizable.
Contains a special provision regarding fines.

main_sections.section_title: Recovery of amounts due to the Government
main_sections.description: Provides for the recovery of amounts due to the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Ancient monuments, etc., no longer requiring protection
main_sections.description: Addresses ancient monuments, etc., that no longer require protection.
Grants the power to correct mistakes.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken under the Act
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith under the Act.
Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Repeals existing laws on the subject.

penalties: Penalties for contravening provisions of the Act (detailed in Section 30, though specific amounts/durations are not fully visible in the provided pages).
A special provision regarding fines (Section 33).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Director (of Archaeology) and the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notification, agreements, acquisition of rights, compulsory purchase of antiquities, and imposition of penalties for offences.

rights: Right of access to protected monuments for the public (Section 18).
Owner's right to use the monument for any purpose and to charge any fee for entry or inspection, subject to agreement terms (Section 6).
duties: Duty of any person employed to watch over a monument as per an agreement (Section 6).
obligations: Owners have obligations regarding the maintenance and preservation of their protected monuments, as may be stipulated in agreements.

key_procedures: Declaring a monument or site as protected: The Government issues a notification after a notice period, with objections considered.
Acquiring rights in a protected monument: Purchase, lease, gift, or bequest by the Director with Government sanction.
Preservation by agreement: Proposing an agreement between the Director and the owner for maintenance.
Excavation procedures: Regulations for excavation in protected and other areas.
Rule-making procedure: The Government makes rules to carry out the Act's purposes.
administration: The Department of Archaeology of the Government, likely headed by the Director of Archaeology.
important_notes: The Act applies to monuments and sites of historical, archaeological, or artistic interest that have been in existence for at least one hundred years.
Monuments of national importance declared by Parliament are excluded from this Act.
The Act distinguishes between 'protected monuments' (ancient monuments declared so) and 'protected areas' (archaeological sites and remains declared so).
Agreements for the maintenance of protected monuments can be terminated after three years with six months' notice.
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected.

title: The Kerala Anganawadi Workers' and Anganawadi Helpers' Welfare Fund Act, 2016
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a Welfare Fund for the welfare of Anganawadi workers and Anganawadi helpers in the Anganawadis which were introduced in the State under Integrated Child Development Services Programme and are functioning in the State of Kerala and to provide pension and other benefits to them and for other matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to Anganawadi workers and Anganawadi helpers introduced in the State under the Integrated Child Development Services Programme in Kerala.

key_definitions.Board: The Anganawadi Workers and Anganawadi Helpers Welfare Fund Board constituted under section 10.
key_definitions.contribution: The amount payable to the Welfare Fund by the members of the Welfare Fund under sub-sections (1) and (2) of section 4 and by the Government under section 17.
key_definitions.Anganawadi Worker: A person who has been selected by a selection committee or promoted from Anganawadi helper or has been appointed by transfer from Balawadi or such other institutions and is working in the Anganawadi on Honorarium basis or has been appointed permanently as worker as per the guidelines approved by the Government from time to time.
key_definitions.Anganawadi Helper: A person who has been selected by a selection committee or has been appointed by transfer from Balawadi or such other institution and is working in the Anganawadi on Honorarium basis or has been appointed permanently as a helper as per the guidelines approved by the Government from time to time.
key_definitions.Fund: The Kerala Anganawadi Workers' and Anganawadi Helpers' Welfare Fund constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.Member: An Anganawadi worker or Anganawadi helper who has enrolled as a member in the Welfare Fund or continuing as a member of the Workers Welfare Fund under the provisions of this Act.
key_definitions.Dependents: Husband, minor children, unmarried or widowed or divorced daughters, mentally or physically disabled children or father or mother who are solely dependent on the member.
key_definitions.Scheme: The Kerala Anganawadi Workers' and Anganawadi Helpers' Welfare Fund Scheme framed under this Act.
key_definitions.Workers' Welfare Fund: Means the Kerala Anganawadi Workers' Welfare Fund framed as per the Government Order issued under G. O. (P) No. 12/92/SWD, dated 10th April, 1992 of the Social Welfare Department.
key_definitions.Notification: A notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.Prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Chief Executive Officer: The Chief Executive Officer, appointed under section 15.
key_definitions.Integrated Child Development Service Sch: A social security scheme implemented by the Central Government on 2nd October, 1975 for the health care and service of the children below the age of six years, pregnant women and breast feeding mothers.
key_definitions.Selection Committee: A selection committee constituted by the Government for the selection of Anganawadi worker and Anganawadi helper.

main_sections.description:
(1) This Act may be called the Kerala Anganawadi Workers' and Anganawadi Helpers' Welfare Fund Act, 2016.
(2) It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 12th day of November, 2015.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including Board, contribution, Anganawadi Worker, Anganawadi Helper, Fund, Government, Member, Dependents, Scheme, Workers' Welfare Fund, Notification, Prescribed, Chief Executive Officer, Integrated Child Development Service Scheme, Schedule, and Selection Committee.

main_sections.section_title: Kerala Anganawadi Workers' and Anganawadi Helpers' Welfare Fund

main_sections.description:
(1) Each Anganawadi Worker shall pay two hundred rupees per month as contribution to the Fund.
(2) Each Anganawadi Helper who is a member of the Welfare Fund shall pay one hundred rupees per month as contribution to the Fund.
(3) The Government may, by notification, from time to time revise the rate of contribution referred in sub-sections (1) and (2) up to a limit of five hundred rupees for the management of the Scheme.
(4) The contribution shall be paid in the name of the Chief Executive Officer or an officer authorised in this behalf as specified in the Scheme.

(1) Any person who has got permanent appointment as Anganawadi Worker or Anganawadi Helper in the Anganawadis of Kerala may apply to the Board for a membership in the Fund in such form and manner as may be specified in the Scheme.
(2) On an application under sub-section (1), the Board may make such enquiry as it deems fit and either admit the applicant to the Fund or for reasons to be recorded in writing, reject the application:
Provided that no order rejecting an application shall be passed without giving the applicant an opportunity of being heard:
Provided further that any person aggrieved by an order rejecting any application for membership may prefer an appeal to the Government within such period as may be specified in the Scheme.
(3) Every applicant shall pay such an amount as application fee along with the application in such manner as may be specified in the Scheme.
(4) Every member who has been enrolled as member in the Fund shall be issued a certificate of membership, identity card and a pass book recording the details as may be prescribed and a register shall be kept in this regard.
(5) A member of the Fund, on completion of service or on resignation or on termination from service shall cease to be a member of the Fund.

(1) The membership of a member shall be cancelled by the Board or the officer authorised in this behalf, if it is found that a member has made manipulation of any kind or has given false information at any time in connection with the conditions for the membership or to obtain benefits as per the Scheme:
Provided that no order of cancellation of membership shall be passed unless the applicant has been given an opportunity of being heard.
(2) Membership in the Fund shall automatically cease if a member commits default in making payment of contribution, continuously, for a period of six months.
(3) Appeal against the orders under sub-section (1) shall be filed before the Government within such period as may be specified in the Scheme.

The membership of a member which has been ceased under sub-section (2) of section 6 may be revived on payment of arrears along with interest at the rate of twelve per cent per annum within six months from the date of cessation of such membership.
Every member of the Welfare Fund shall join the insurance scheme made applicable to them, each year.
The accounts of the Fund shall be audited annually by such auditor or auditors as may be appointed by the Government.
Provides for the constitution of the Anganawadi Workers and Anganawadi Helpers Welfare Fund Board.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of the Board
main_sections.description: Details the powers and functions of the Board for the administration of the Fund.
The Government shall have the power to frame a Scheme to provide for pension and other benefits to Anganawadi Workers and Helpers.
The Board may delegate its powers and functions to the Chief Executive Officer or any other officer.
Empowers officers to enter and inspect premises for the purpose of the Act.
Provides for the appointment of a Chief Executive Officer and defines his powers and duties.
Outlines the responsibilities of the Board for the effective administration of the Fund.
Specifies the contribution to be made by the Government to the Fund.
Grants the Board the power to borrow money for the purposes of the Fund.

important_rules: Anganawadi Workers must pay Rs. 200 per month as contribution to the Fund.
Anganawadi Helpers must pay Rs. 100 per month as contribution to the Fund.
The Government may revise contribution rates up to Rs. 500 per month.
Contribution shall be paid in the name of the Chief Executive Officer.
Members who default in contribution payments for six consecutive months will have their membership automatically cease.
Every member must join an applicable insurance scheme each year.

penalties: Manipulation of any kind or false information to obtain benefits may lead to cancellation of membership (Section 6(1)).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Board and the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the framing of a Scheme, the administration by the Board, and the enforcement of rules by the Government and authorised officers.

rights: Right to apply for membership in the Welfare Fund.
Right to appeal to the Government against rejection of membership application.
Right to receive pension and other benefits as per the Scheme.
Right to revive membership under certain conditions.
duties: Duty to pay prescribed contributions to the Fund.
Duty to join the applicable insurance scheme annually.
obligations: Obligation to provide correct information for membership.
Obligation for members whose membership ceases to cease to be a member of the Fund.

key_procedures: Application for membership: A person with permanent appointment as Anganawadi Worker or Helper can apply in the prescribed form. The Board may conduct an enquiry before admission or rejection. An appeal against rejection lies with the Government.
Payment of contribution: Contributions must be paid monthly in the name of the Chief Executive Officer.

Cancellation of membership: Membership can be cancelled by the Board for manipulation or false information, or automatically ceases due to continuous default in payment for six months. An appeal against cancellation lies with the Government.
Revival of membership: Ceased membership can be revived within six months of cessation by paying arrears with interest.
administration: The Kerala Anganawadi Workers' and Anganawadi Helpers' Welfare Fund Board, under the overall supervision of the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on November 12, 2015.
The Scheme framed under the Act can cover matters specified in the Schedule.
The Fund shall vest in and be administered by the Board.
The Government has the power to revise contribution rates.
The Board has the power to delegate powers to the Chief Executive Officer or other officers.
The Board has the power to borrow money for the Fund.
The Government's contribution to the Fund is specified.

title: The Kerala Animals and Birds Sacrifices Prohibition Act, 1968
purpose: To consolidate and amend the laws relating to prohibition of the sacrifice of animals and birds in or in the precincts of Hindu temples in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.precincts: In relation to a temple, includes all lands and buildings near a temple, whether belonging to the temple or not, which are ordinarily used for purposes connected with the worship conducted inside the temple or outside, and in particular the mandapams, prakarams, back-yards, front-yards and foot-yards of the temple, by whatever name called, and also the ground on which the temple car ordinarily stands.
key_definitions.sacrifice: Means the killing or maiming of any animal or bird for the purpose, or with the intention, of propitiating any deity.
key_definitions.temple: Means a place by whatever designation known, used as a place of public religious worship, and dedicated to, or for the benefit of, or used as of right by, the Hindu community or any section thereof, as a place of public religious worship.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Animals and Birds Sacrifices Prohibition Act, 1968 and that it extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.
Defines terms such as 'precincts', 'sacrifice', and 'temple' as used in the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Sacrifice of animals and birds in temples or its precincts prohibited.
main_sections.description: Prohibits any person from sacrificing any animal or bird in a temple or its precincts.
Prohibits any person from officiating or offering to officiate, performing or offering to perform, or serving, assisting, or participating, in any sacrifice in a temple or its precincts.

main_sections.section_title: Temple or its precincts not to be allowed to be used for sacrifice.
main_sections.description: Prohibits any person from knowingly allowing any temple or its precincts to be used for sacrifice.
Specifies penalties for contravening the provisions of sections 3, 4, and 5.
States that no offence punishable under this Act shall be inquired into or tried by a court inferior to that of a Magistrate of the first or second class.

Repeals The Madras Animals and Birds Sacrifices Prohibition Act, 1950, as in force in the Malabar district, and sub-section (2) of section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (Central Act 37 of 1956), and the Travancore-Cochin Animals and Birds Sacrifices Prohibition Act, 1953 (VII of 1953).

important_rules: No person shall sacrifice any animal or bird in a temple or its precincts.
No person shall officiate or offer to officiate, perform or offer to perform, or serve, assist, or participate, in any sacrifice in a temple or its precincts.
No person shall knowingly allow any temple or its precincts to be used for sacrifice.

penalties: Whoever contravenes the provisions of section 3 shall be punishable with fine which may extend to three hundred rupees.
Whoever contravenes the provisions of section 4 shall be punishable with fine which may extend to three hundred rupees.

Provided that if the offender is an officer, servant, authority, trustee or priest of the temple or the holder of any office in receipt of emoluments or perquisites for the performance of any service in the temple, he shall be punishable with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to three hundred rupees, or with both.

Whoever contravenes the provisions of section 5 shall be punishable with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to three hundred rupees, or with both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Magistrate of the first or second class.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Offences are inquired into and tried by Magistrates of the first or second class.

duties: Duty to not sacrifice animals or birds in temples or precincts.
Duty to not officiate or participate in sacrifices.
Duty not to allow temples or precincts to be used for sacrifice.
obligations: Religious institutions and their staff have an obligation to ensure that sacrifices are not performed on their premises and to prevent such activities.

key_procedures: Inquiry and trial of offences under this Act are conducted by Magistrates of the first or second class.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but likely the Home Department of the Government of Kerala or a relevant department dealing with religious affairs and public order.
important_notes: The Act repeals previous acts concerning animal and bird sacrifices in the specified regions of Kerala.
Penalties for contravention can include fines and, in certain cases for specific roles, imprisonment.

title: The Kerala Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act, 2007
purpose: To provide for the effective prevention and control of certain kind of anti-social activities in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and concerns anti-social activities within the state.

key_definitions.anti-social activity: Means acting in such manner as to cause or likely to cause directly or indirectly, the feeling of insecurity, danger or fear among the general public or any section thereof or any danger to the safety of individuals, safety of public health or the ecological system or any loss or damage to public exchequer or to any public or private property or indulges in any activities referred in clauses (c), (e), (g), (h), (i), (j), (m), (q), (r), and (s) of this section.
key_definitions.advisory board: Means an advisory board constituted under section 8 by the Government.
key_definitions.authorised officer: Means any officer authorised by the Government under sub-section (2) of section 3.
key_definitions.bootlegger: Means a person who distills, manufactures, stores, transports or takes away, imports, exports, sells or distributes any liquor, intoxicating drug or other intoxicating substance in contravention of the Teri Act (1 of 1077) and the Rules and Orders issued thereunder or any of the provisions contained in any other law for the time being in force, knowingly them or aided, abetted or is accessory to or does any of the matters mentioned above, by any person or through any person by providing any amount, vehicle, vessel, other conveyance or any tank or other articles whatever it may be, or the person who abets to do any such matter in any manner.
key_definitions.close relative: Means spouse, parent, children or sibling and first degree blood-relatives of such spouse, parent, children or sibling and includes the children or spouses of such persons.
key_definitions.counterfeiter: Means any person who knowingly and wilfully makes, stocks or distributes counterfeit coins or currency or valuable security defined in section 30 of the Indian Penal Code (Central Act 45 of 1860) and includes a person who knowingly abets any such activities.
key_definitions.detention order: Means an order made under section 3.
key_definitions.depredator of environment: Means a person who, by any direct act by which he derives pecuniary or commercial benefit, commits an offence under any law relating to protection of environment or rivers or under any law relating to sand mining or under any law relating to quarrying or mining, or who commits or abets the commission of offences punishable under any law relating to conservation of forests or wildlife.
key_definitions.digital data and copyright pirate: Means any person who knowingly and deliberately creates, for commercial purposes, any copyright law in relation to any book, music, film software, artistic scientific work and includes any person who illegally enters through the identity of the user and illegally uses any computer or digital network for any illegal profit by deceiving any person or any computer system.
key_definitions.drug offender: Means a person who illegally cultivates, manufactures, stocks, transports, sells or distributes any drug in contravention of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 (Central Act 61 of 1985) or in contravention of any other law for the time being in force, or who knowingly does anything befitting or facilitating such activity.
key_definitions.goonda: Means a person who indulges in any anti-social activity or promotes or abets any illegal activity which are harmful for the maintenance of the public order directly or indirectly and includes a bootlegger, a counterfeiter, a depredator of environment, a digital data and copyright pirate, a drug offender, a hawala racketeer, a hired ruffian, a money framer, a loan shark and a known rowdy.
key_definitions.hawala racketeer: Means a person who, on his own motion or as a member of any organized group which illegally buys, sells or deals with Indian currency or foreign exchanges, engages in such illegal activity.
key_definitions.hired ruffian: Means any person who receives pecuniary consideration in cash or kind for use of unlawful force either by himself or through police officers or any person or for criminally intimidating any person or for damaging any property belonging to any other person or for illegally dispossessing any person from any movable or immovable property in his possession.
key_definitions.immoral traffic offender: Means a person who commits or abets the commission of any offence under the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956 (Central Act 104 of 1956).
key_definitions.known goonda: Means a goonda that had been, for acts done within the previous seven years as calculated from the date of the order imposing any restriction or detention under this Act.— (i) found guilty, by a competent court or authority at least once for an offence within the meaning of the term 'goonda' as defined in clause (j) of section 2; or (ii) found in any investigation or enquiry by a competent police officer, authority or competent court on complaints initiated by persons other than police officers, in two separate instances not forming part of the same transaction, the offence committed any act within the meaning of the term 'goonda' as defined in clause (j) of section 2.
key_definitions.known rowdy: Means any person, who had been, by reason of acts done within the previous seven years as calculated from the date of the order imposing any restriction or detention under this Act.— (i) made guilty, by a competent court at least twice for an offence of the nature under item (i) of clause (I) of section 2 or any notice as such under the said clause; or

main_sections.description: This section identifies the Act as 'The Kerala Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act, 2007' and states that it shall come into force on the 13th day of December 2006.

This section provides definitions for various terms used throughout the Act, including 'anti-social activity', 'advisory board', 'authorised officer', 'bootlegger', 'close relative', 'counterfeiter', 'detention order', 'depredator of environment', 'digital data and copyright pirate', 'drug offender', 'goonda', 'government', 'hawala racketeer', 'hired ruffian', 'immoral traffic offender', 'known goonda', and 'known rowdy'.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make orders for detaining known Goondas and known Rowdies

purpose: To amend The Kerala Anti-social Activities (Prevention) Act, 2014.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.anti_social_activity: Refers to specific acts listed in the Principal Act, including those that endanger public order or are committed with the intention of acquiring unlawful pecuniary or other advantages.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and its commencement date. It states that this Act may be called the Kerala Anti-social Activities (Prevention) Amendment Act, 2014. It also states that the provisions of this Act shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of October, 2014.

Amends Section 2 of the Principal Act. It inserts a new clause (ii-a) which defines 'controlled body' as a group of two or more individuals, or a society or association of persons, whether registered or not, which is engaged in anti-social activities.
Inserts new sections 3A and 3B into the Principal Act. Section 3A deals with the powers of the District Magistrate and Section 3B deals with the procedure for issuing orders for detention.
Amends Section 4 of the Principal Act, which deals with the prohibition of anti-social activities. It clarifies the types of activities that are considered anti-social.
Amends Section 17 of the Principal Act. This section deals with the detention orders. The amendment specifies the requirements for issuing a detention order and the procedure for its review.
Amends Section 18 of the Principal Act, concerning the powers of the Government to amend the schedules. It clarifies the process for amending the schedules to the Act.
Amends Section 22 of the Principal Act, which deals with the powers of the State Government to make rules. It allows for the Government to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.

Repeals the Kerala Anti-social Activities (Prevention) Ordinance, 2014. It also includes savings provisions, meaning that anything done or any action taken under the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the corresponding provisions of this Act.

title: The Kerala Automobiles Limited (Validation Of Appointment Of Personnel) Act, 2004
purpose: To validate the appointment of personnel made in the Kerala Automobiles Limited in the vacancies which arose during the period from the 1st day of July, 1978 to 28th day of March, 1984.
scope: The Act applies to the Kerala Automobiles Limited and the appointment of personnel made in the company during the specified period.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act and its commencement. It is deemed to have come into force on the 15th day of September, 2003.

This section validates all appointments of personnel made in the Kerala Automobiles Limited in the vacancies that arose between July 1, 1978, and March 28, 1984, notwithstanding anything contained in certain guidelines issued by the Government or any court order, decree, or judgment. Such appointments are deemed to have been validly done and the validity of such acts is not to be questioned in any court of law on the ground that they have not been done in pursuance of the guidelines issued by the Government.

This section repeals the Kerala Automobiles Limited (Validation of Appointment of Personnel) Ordinance, 2003. Notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the Ordinance is deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.
