title: THE KERALA AYURVEDA HEALTH CENTRES (ISSUE OF LICENCE AND CONTROL) ACT, 2007
purpose: To provide for the issue of licence to Ayurveda Health Centres in the State and to control their function.
scope: Applies to Ayurveda Health Centres in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Ayurveda Health Centre: An establishment or premises by whatever name known to provide Ayurveda treatment but does not include the establishments under the direct ownership or management of the Government and the dispensaries conducted by the Ayurveda Medical Practitioner only for the mere diagnosis and distribution of medicines or the agencies selling the medicine.
key_definitions.Director: Director of Department of Indian System of Medicine under the Government of Kerala.
key_definitions.Local Self Government Institution: A Village Panchayat constituted under the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 (13 of 1994), or a Municipality constituted under the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994 (20 of 1994).
key_definitions.Manager: The owner or the person responsible for the administration and management of an Ayurveda Health Centre.
key_definitions.Masseur/Therapist: A person employed for the treatment as directed by a registered Medical Practitioner in an Ayurveda Health Centre and having recognised qualifications as prescribed.
key_definitions.Nurse: A person employed for nursing duty in an Ayurveda Health Centre and having equivalent qualification, as prescribed.
key_definitions.Prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Licence: Licence issued by the Director after conducting necessary inspections as specified in this Act.
key_definitions.Medical Practitioner: An Ayurveda Medical Practitioner registered under the Travancore-Cochin Medical Practitioners Act, 1953 (9 of 1953) or Indian Medicine Central Council Act, 1970 (Central Act 48 of 1970).
key_definitions.Treatment: All types of treatments provided as per Ayurveda system of treatment, for the cure of any particular disease or improving the health of any person.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act as The Kerala Ayurveda Health Centres (Issue of Licence and Control) Act, 2007, its extent to the whole of the State of Kerala, and that it shall come into force from such date as the Government may by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Ayurveda Health Centre', 'Director', 'Government', 'Local Self Government Institution', 'Manager', 'Masseur/Therapist', 'Nurse', 'Prescribed', 'Licence', 'Medical Practitioner', 'State', and 'Treatment'.

main_sections.section_title: Issue of Licence to Ayurveda Health Centres
main_sections.description: States that no person shall run an Ayurveda Health Centre without a licence issued under this Act, and such licence must be obtained from the Local Self Government Institution. It also specifies that centres functioning prior to the commencement of the Act must obtain a licence within six months of the Act's commencement, and if they fail to obtain it, they cannot continue to function after six months from the date of application.

main_sections.section_title: Conditions for the issue of Licence
main_sections.description: Details the conditions for issuing a licence based on the facilities of treatment in the Ayurveda Health Centres, categorizing them into Category (A), (B), and (C) with specific requirements for each regarding accommodation, treatment rooms, drinking water, light, hygienic equipment, medical practitioner consultation, instruments, therapists/masseurs, nurses, and necessary employees. It also outlines conditions for inpatient treatment and general conditions applicable to all categories.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and duties of the Director
main_sections.description: Outlines the powers of the Director to issue or renew licences, to enter any Ayurveda Health Centre, to complain or suo motu inspect, and to enquire into conditions. It also details the Director's duty and responsibility to conduct inspections and searches.

Specifies that every application for licence or renewal of an Ayurveda Health Centre shall be submitted to the Director in the prescribed form, along with the fees as prescribed. The Director shall take decision on the application within the prescribed time.

If, upon inspection, it is found that an Ayurveda Health Centre is not complying with or violating the conditions, the Director or the Medical Officer authorised by him shall issue a notice specifying such default or defects. If the Manager of such a centre fails to rectify the same within the time limit, the Director shall cancel the licence.

Any person who establishes or conducts any Ayurveda Health Centre without licence, in contravention of the provisions of this Act, shall be punished with imprisonment not less than six months and with fine which may extend to one lakh rupees. Any person who commits an offence under this Act, except those mentioned in sub-section (1), shall, on conviction, be punished with fine, which may extend to fifty thousand rupees.

If an offence committed under this Act is by a company, the person at the time of commission of the offence was in charge of, and was responsible to the company for the conduct of its business, shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence. Provided that nothing contained in this sub-section shall render any such person liable to any punishment if he proves that the offence was committed without his knowledge, or that he had exercised all due diligence to prevent the commission of such offence. Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), where any offence under this Act has been committed by a company and it is proved that the offence has been committed with the connivance or neglect on the part of any Director or Manager or Secretary or any other officer of the company, such Director or Manager or Secretary or any other officer of the company also shall be deemed to be guilty of that offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly.
This section likely details how offences under the act are brought to the attention of the authorities, though the content is not fully visible in the provided images.
This section likely provides a mechanism for appealing decisions made under the Act, though the content is not fully visible in the provided images.
The Government shall have power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act.

If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, the Government may, by order published in the Gazette, make such provisions, not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act, as appear to them to be necessary or expedient for removing the difficulty.
This section likely deals with the repeal of any previous enactments and provisions for saving existing actions or licences, though the specific content is not fully visible.

important_rules: No person shall run an Ayurveda Health Centre without a licence issued under this Act.
Licences must be obtained from the Local Self Government Institution.
Ayurveda Health Centres must meet specific facility requirements based on their category (A, B, or C).
Treatment of male patients who come to a centre for treatment shall be done only by male therapist/masseur and the treatment of female patient shall be done only by female therapist/masseurs.
Only quality medicines shall be used in an Ayurveda Health Centre for treatment and the components of the medicines shall be convinced to the examiner.
Medicines and oils used for one patient shall not be used for another patient.
Every Ayurveda Health Centre shall be established in healthy surroundings only and shall be free from sound pollution, as far as possible.

The name, licence number, details of the licence and working hours of each Ayurveda Health Centre shall be exhibited in the building or premises where it is established in a manner clearly visible from outside.
Registers and case sheet as prescribed shall be kept for recording details of the persons coming for treatment in an Ayurveda Health Centre.
No Ayurveda Health Centre shall function in the vehicles used on land or in water.

penalties: Imprisonment not less than six months and fine which may extend to one lakh rupees for establishing or conducting an Ayurveda Health Centre without a licence.
Fine which may extend to fifty thousand rupees for other offences under this Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Director, Medical Officer authorised by the Director, and Local Self Government Institutions.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, imposition of penalties (imprisonment and fines), and cancellation of licences for non-compliance.

rights: Right to apply for a licence to run an Ayurveda Health Centre.
Right to appeal against decisions made under the Act (implied by Section 11).
duties: Duty to obtain a licence before running an Ayurveda Health Centre.
Duty to comply with the conditions specified for the issue of licence.
Duty to display licence details and working hours.
Duty to maintain registers and case sheets.
Duty to use only quality medicines and not reuse medicines.
Duty to maintain healthy and pollution-free surroundings.
Duty to ensure that treatment is provided by qualified personnel.
obligations: Obligation for the Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Obligation for the Government to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act through orders.

key_procedures: Application for Licence: Submit application to the Director in the prescribed form with fees.
Inspection and Verification: Director or authorized officers conduct inspections and verify compliance with conditions.
Issue/Renewal of Licence: Based on inspection report and certification, licence is issued or renewed.
Cancellation of Licence: If non-compliance is found, a notice is issued, and if not rectified, the licence can be cancelled.
Penalty Imposition: For contravention of provisions, penalties are imposed as per the Act.
administration: The Government of Kerala, and the Department of Indian System of Medicine (headed by the Director).
important_notes: The Act came into force on the 15th October, 2007, as per Gazette Extraordinary No. 1862 dated 15th October, 2007.
Inpatient treatment in category (B) and (C) health centres cannot include complicated treatments like 'Vamanami', 'Virechanami', 'Vasthi' and 'Panchakarma' treatments, and 'Udavarthanam'.
Health Centres functioning along with other establishments may be included in category (C) but independent Health Centres shall not include in category (C).

key_definitions.Fund: Refers to the Welfare Fund constituted under this Act.
key_definitions.Employer: Includes any person who employs a worker, or who has control over the business of an employer.

Empowers the Government to frame schemes for the implementation of the Act.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

Penalties are prescribed for non-compliance with the provisions of the Act, ensuring its enforceability.

title: THE KERALA BAMBOO, KATTUVALLI AND PANDANUS LEAF WORKERS WELFARE FUND ACT, 1998
purpose: An Act to provide for the constitution of a Fund to grant relief to, to promote the welfare of, and to pay pension to, bamboo, kattuvalli and pandanus leaf workers and self-employed persons in bamboo, kattuvalli and pandanus leaf industries in the State of Kerala.
scope: The Act applies to bamboo, kattuvalli and pandanus leaf workers and self-employed persons in bamboo, kattuvalli and pandanus leaf industries in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.bamboo industry: means an industry to which bamboo, reeds or cane is used as raw material for making bamboo products and includes collecting, storing or distributing bamboo, reeds or cane for the purpose of making bamboo products or doing any work in connection with or incidental thereto.
key_definitions.bamboo product: means any article which is made out of bamboo, reeds or cane.
key_definitions.bamboo worker or kattuvalli or pandanus: means any person who is employed for wages to do any work in connection with or incidental to the bamboo industry or kattuvalli industry or pandanus leaf industry, as the case may be, and who gets his wages, directly or indirectly from the employer, dealer or producer of bamboo products or kattuvalli products or pandanus leaf products or means any person employed by, or through a contractor or through an agent and depends mainly on bamboo industry or kattuvalli or pandanus leaf industry for his livelihood and also a person whom the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, from time to time, declare to be a bamboo, kattuvalli or pandanus leaf worker for the purpose of this Act, but does not include a person engaged in collecting bamboo, reed or cane for the purpose of making pulp, paper and artificial threads with mechanical aid.
key_definitions.Board: means the Kerala Bamboo, Kattuvalli and Pandanus Leaf Workers' Welfare Fund Board constituted under section 6.
key_definitions.Chief Executive Officer: means the Chief Executive Officer appointed under sub-section (1) of section 9.
key_definitions.contribution: means the money payable to the Fund under section 4.
key_definitions.dealer: means any person who is engaged in the business of purchase, sale or storage for sale of bamboo or kattuvalli or pandanus leaf products.
key_definitions.employer: means any person who employs, whether directly or indirectly, or whether on behalf of himself or for any other person, one or more bamboo or kattuvalli or pandanus leaf workers to do any work in connection with the various process in bamboo or kattuvalli or pandanus leaf industry.
key_definitions.family: means husband, wife and their minor sons, unmarried daughters and mentally retarded children.
key_definitions.Fund: means the Bamboo, Kattuvalli and Pandanus Leaf Workers' Welfare Fund established under section 3.
key_definitions.kattuvalli industry: means an industry in which kattuvalli is used as a raw material for making kattuvalli products and includes collecting, storing or distributing kattuvalli for the purpose of making kattuvalli products or doing any work in connection with or incidental thereto.
key_definitions.kattuvalli products: means anything made out of raw or processed kattuvalli.
key_definitions.member: means a member of the Fund.
key_definitions.pandanus leaf industry: means an industry in which pandanus leaf is used as raw materials for making products out of it and includes collecting, storing or distributing pandanus leaf for the purpose of making pandanus leaf products or doing any work in connection with or incidental thereto.
key_definitions.pandanus leaf product: means mats, basket toys, handicraft items, fancy things, furniture, thazhapaya, vattu and such other things made out of raw or processed pandanus leaf.
key_definitions.person: includes a company, a firm, an association of individuals or a co-operative society registered or deemed to be registered under the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969 (21 of 1969).
key_definitions.prescribed: means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.producer of bamboo or kattuvalli or pand: means a person who carries on the business of making bamboo or kattuvalli or pandanus leaf products for export or for internal use.
key_definitions.Schedule: means the Schedule to this Act.
key_definitions.Scheme: means the Scheme framed under this Act.
key_definitions.self-employed person: means a person other than a bamboo or kattuvalli or pandanus leaf worker who is engaged in the making of bamboo, reeds, cane, kattuvalli or pandanus leaf or engaged in the making of bamboo products or kattuvalli products or pandanus leaf products and depends mainly on bamboo industry or kattuvalli industry or pandanus leaf industry for his livelihood.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act, its extent of application, and the date of commencement.
This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as 'bamboo industry', 'bamboo worker', 'Board', 'Fund', etc.

main_sections.section_title: Bamboo, Kattuvalli and Pandanus Leaf Workers' Welfare Fund
main_sections.description: This section describes the constitution of the Welfare Fund and how it is to be established. It also details the sources from which the Fund will receive money, including contributions, grants, loans, donations, amounts raised by the Board, and fees levied under the Scheme. The section also outlines the purposes for which the Fund can be utilized, such as payment of pension, financial assistance, maternity benefits, medical expenses, educational facilities, and gratuity.

This section specifies the contributions to be made to the Fund by employers, producers, and self-employed persons engaged in the bamboo, kattuvalli, and pandanus leaf industries. It details the per-month contribution amounts and how the Government can contribute to the Fund.

This section grants the Government the power to add to, amend, or vary the Scheme by notification in the Gazette. It also states that such modifications, if not made in the same session of the Legislative Assembly, shall have effect only after it is modified in the Legislative Assembly, without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under the Scheme.

This section outlines the constitution of the 'Kerala Bamboo, Kattuvalli and Pandanus Leaf Workers' Welfare Fund Board'. It describes the Board as a body corporate, its composition (not exceeding fifteen Directors, including representatives of government, employers, dealers, producers, and workers), the appointment of Directors, and the functions of the Chairman and the Board.

This section defines the term of office for Directors appointed under sub-section (1) of section 6, which is for a period of three years. It also provides conditions under which a Director may be removed from office and the option for a Director to resign.

important_rules: Contributions to the Fund are mandatory for employers, producers, and self-employed persons in the relevant industries.
The Fund shall be used for specific welfare purposes including pensions, financial assistance, maternity benefits, medical expenses, and educational facilities.
The Government has the power to modify the Scheme through notifications.
Directors of the Board have a term of office of three years.
Any modifications to the Scheme by the Government must be placed before the Legislative Assembly.

penalties: Penalty for offences by companies.
Penalty for power to recover damages.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Board, and potentially other authorities as designated by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through provisions for recovery of damages, penalties for offences, and the general administrative powers of the Board.

rights: Right to receive welfare benefits such as pension, financial assistance, maternity benefits, medical expenses, and educational facilities from the Fund.
Right for members who have completed sixty years of age to receive pension.
Right for members who were bamboo or kattuvalli or pandanus leaf workers before the commencement of the Act to receive pension under certain conditions.
duties: Duty of employers, producers, and self-employed persons to contribute to the Fund.
Duty of the Board to administer the Fund and implement the Scheme.
Duty of the Government to establish the Fund and the Board.
obligations: Obligation for employers and every producer of bamboo products or kattuvalli products or pandanus leaf products to contribute to the Fund.
Obligation for every self-employed person to contribute to the Fund.

key_procedures: Establishment of the Welfare Fund and the Board.
Collection of contributions from various stakeholders.
Utilization of the Fund for specified welfare purposes.
Modification of the Scheme by the Government.
Appointment and term of office of Directors of the Board.
administration: The Kerala Bamboo, Kattuvalli and Pandanus Leaf Workers' Welfare Fund Board.
important_notes: The Act extends to the whole of Kerala.
The Act came into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, frame a Scheme for the establishment of a Fund under this Act for the welfare of bamboo, kattuvalli and pandanus leaf workers and self-employed persons.
Any modification of the Scheme shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

title: THE KERALA BEEDI AND CIGAR WORKERS' WELFARE FUND ACT, 1995
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a fund to grant relief to, promote the welfare of, and to pay pension to beedi and cigar workers and self-employed persons in beedi and cigar industries in the State of Kerala and matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to beedi and cigar workers and self-employed persons in beedi and cigar industries in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Board: The Kerala Beedi and Cigar Workers' Welfare Fund Board constituted under section 7.
key_definitions.Chief Welfare Fund Inspector: The Chief Welfare Fund Inspector appointed under sub-section (1) of section 10.
key_definitions.contribution: The sum of money payable to the Fund under section 5.
key_definitions.employee: A person employed directly or through any agency, whether for wages or not, in any beedi or cigar establishment to do any work, skilled, unskilled, manual or clerical and includes any person who is given raw materials by an employer or a contractor for converting them into beedi or cigar at home; and any person not employed by an employer or contractor, but under agreement with the employer or contractor.
key_definitions.employer: In relation to contract labour, the principal employer; and in relation to any other labour, the person who has the ultimate control over the affairs of any establishment or who has, by reason of his advancing money, supplying goods or otherwise, a substantial interest in it, the control of the affairs of any establishment and includes any other person to whom the affairs of the establishment are entrusted, whether called the manager, superintendent or by any other name.
key_definitions.family: means wife, minor sons, unmarried daughters; and father and mother who are solely dependent on the beedi or cigar worker or the self-employed person.
key_definitions.Fund: means the Kerala Beedi and Cigar Workers' Welfare Fund established under section 3 and the Scheme.
key_definitions.member: means an employee or self-employed person registered in the Scheme under section 4.
key_definitions.prescribed: means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Scheme: means the Scheme framed under this Act.
key_definitions.wages: means all emoluments which are earned by an employee while on duty or on leave with wages in accordance with the terms of the contract of employment and which are paid or payable in cash to him, but does not include the cash value of any food concession; overtime allowance, bonus and commission.
key_definitions.Welfare Fund Inspector: means a Welfare Fund Inspector appointed under sub-section (1) of section 10.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Beedi and Cigar Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 1995. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'Chief Welfare Fund Inspector', 'contribution', 'employee', 'employer', 'family', 'Fund', 'member', 'prescribed', 'Scheme', 'wages', 'Welfare Fund Inspector', and 'year'.

main_sections.section_title: Beedi and Cigar Workers' Welfare Fund
main_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of the Kerala Beedi and Cigar Workers' Welfare Fund for the benefit of employees in the beedi and cigar industries and matters connected therewith. The Fund shall be established by the Government by notification in the Gazette. The Fund shall be a body corporate. The Fund shall be applied for the purposes specified in the Scheme, including grants or loans for education, medical benefits, and other welfare measures. The Fund shall be administered by the Board and audited by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India or any other person appointed by the State Government.

main_sections.section_title: Registration of beedi and cigar workers
main_sections.description: Every employee or self-employed person is to be a member upon registering his name in the manner specified in the Scheme as a beneficiary of the Fund. The registration is to be done by the Chief Welfare Fund Inspector or other officers authorized by him.

Specifies that every employer shall be paid to the Fund at the rate of six rupees per mensem in respect of each employee. Every self-employed person shall contribute to the Fund two rupees per mensem. Every employer shall, along with his contribution, pay to the Fund the contribution in respect of the employees engaged by him. The Government shall contribute to the Fund every year by way of grant or on a matching basis an amount equal to the contribution paid by the employees under sub-section (1). Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, the employer shall be entitled to recover from the employee his contribution by deduction from his wages or in such manner as may be prescribed, and such deduction shall be deemed to be a deduction authorized by or under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 (Central Act 4 of 1936).

main_sections.section_title: Scheme for Welfare of Beedi and Cigar Workers
main_sections.description: The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, frame a Scheme to be called the Beedi and Cigar Workers' Welfare Fund Scheme for the establishment of a Fund under this Act for employees and self-employed persons in beedi and cigar industries. The Scheme may provide for the constitution of a Board, the benefits to be provided, the manner of administration of the Fund, the recovery of contributions, and other incidental matters. The Scheme shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, constitute a Board to be called the Kerala Beedi and Cigar Workers' Welfare Fund Board. The Board shall be a body corporate. The Board shall consist of an equal number of Directors representing the Government, the employers and the employees. The Government shall publish the names of the Chairman and Directors in the Gazette. The Board shall administer the Fund in such manner as may be specified in the Scheme. The Government may, with the previous approval of the Government, delegate to the Chairman or to the Chief Welfare Fund Inspector or to any Welfare Fund Inspector such of its powers and functions under this Act or the Scheme as it may consider necessary for the efficient administration of the Fund, subject to such restrictions and conditions, if any, as it may specify.
A Director shall hold office for a period of three years.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, remove any non-official Director for reasons to be recorded in writing. The Government may remove a Director if he is considered unsuitable or incapable of acting as a Director or has abused his position as a Director to render his continuance as such undesirable in the public interest.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Chief Welfare Fund Inspector and Welfare Fund Inspectors
main_sections.description: The Government may appoint a Chief Welfare Fund Inspector and such other staff as they consider necessary to assist the Chief Welfare Fund Inspector in the discharge of his duties under this Act. The Chief Welfare Fund Inspector shall be the Chief Executive Officer of the Board. The method of appointment, salary and allowances, discipline and other conditions of service of the Chief Welfare Fund Inspector and Welfare Fund Inspectors and other staff shall be such as may be prescribed by the Government. Duty of employer to file return - Every employer shall, before the fifth day of every month, file a return showing the details of contributions paid into the Fund, in such manner as may be specified in the Scheme.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Chief Welfare Fund Inspector and Welfare Fund Inspectors
main_sections.description: The Government may appoint a Chief Welfare Fund Inspector and such other staff as they consider necessary to assist the Chief Welfare Fund Inspector in the discharge of his duties under this Act. The Chief Welfare Fund Inspector shall be the Chief Executive Officer of the Board. The method of appointment, salary and allowances, discipline and other conditions of service of the Chief Welfare Fund Inspector and Welfare Fund Inspectors and other staff shall be such as may be prescribed by the Government. Duty of employer to file return - Every employer shall, before the fifth day of every month, file a return showing the details of contributions paid into the Fund, in such manner as may be specified in the Scheme.

main_sections.section_title: Determination of amount due from employers
main_sections.description: The Chief Welfare Fund Inspector or any other Welfare Fund Inspector authorised by him in this behalf may, by order, determine the amount due from any employer under the provisions of this Act or the Scheme and for this purpose, may conduct such inquiry as he may deem necessary. Any officer conducting the inquiry under sub-section (1) shall have the powers of a civil court trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Central Act 5 of 1908), in respect of the following matters, namely: enforcing the attendance of any person and examining him on oath; requiring the discovery and production of documents; issuing commissions for the examination of witnesses. Any inquiry under this section shall be deemed to be a judicial proceeding within the meaning of section 193 and section 228 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (Central Act 45 of 1860) and for the purposes of section 196 of that Code. No order determining the amount due from any employer shall be made under sub-section (1) unless the employer has been given a reasonable opportunity of being heard.

main_sections.section_title: Recovery of amount due from employers
main_sections.description: Any amount due from an employer may be recovered from him by the Chief Welfare Fund Inspector or any other Welfare Fund Inspector authorised by him in this behalf, as an arrear of land revenue. The amount due from any employer shall be recovered from him by the Chief Welfare Fund Inspector or any other Welfare Fund Inspector authorised by him in this behalf, as an arrear of land revenue.

main_sections.section_title: Recovery of money due from employer
main_sections.description: Any amount due from an employer in pursuance of the provisions of this Act or the Scheme, other than an amount in arrear under sub-section (1) of section 13, may, if it is in arrear, be recovered together with interest thereon at the rate of sixteen per cent per annum in the same manner as an arrear of public revenue due on land.

The amount standing to the credit of any member in the Fund shall not be liable to attachment under any decree or order of any court in respect of any debt or liability incurred by the member, and neither the said amount nor any part thereof shall be a subject of sale in execution of a decree or order of any court. Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, the employer shall be entitled to recover from the employee his contribution by deduction from his wages or in such manner as may be prescribed, and such deduction shall be deemed to be a deduction authorized by or under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 (Central Act 4 of 1936).

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make rules for the purpose of carrying into effect the provisions of this Act. Every rule made under this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before the Legislative Assembly, which, when in session or within a total period of fourteen days which comprises in its one session or in two successive sessions immediately following the session or, if the Legislative Assembly is not in session, within the said period of fourteen days, whichever is earlier, either generally or in such modified form as it likes, and shall, unless the Assembly earlier decides otherwise, be valid only at the expiry of the said period of fourteen days. But without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under the rule.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make rules for the purpose of carrying into effect the provisions of this Act. Every rule made under this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before the Legislative Assembly, which, when in session or within a total period of fourteen days which comprises in its one session or in two successive sessions immediately following the session or, if the Legislative Assembly is not in session, within the said period of fourteen days, whichever is earlier, either generally or in such modified form as it likes, and shall, unless the Assembly earlier decides otherwise, be valid only at the expiry of the said period of fourteen days. But without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under the rule.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make rules for the purpose of carrying into effect the provisions of this Act. Every rule made under this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before the Legislative Assembly, which, when in session or within a total period of fourteen days which comprises in its one session or in two successive sessions immediately following the session or, if the Legislative Assembly is not in session, within the said period of fourteen days, whichever is earlier, either generally or in such modified form as it likes, and shall, unless the Assembly earlier decides otherwise, be valid only at the expiry of the said period of fourteen days. But without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under the rule.

If an offence under this Act is committed by a company, every person who, at the time the offence was committed, was in charge of, and was responsible to the company for the conduct of the business of the company, as well as the company, shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly. Provided that nothing contained in this sub-section shall render any such person liable to any punishment provided in this Act if he proves that the offence was committed without his knowledge or that he exercised all due diligence to prevent the commission of such offence.

No court shall take cognizance of any offence punishable under this Act except on a report in writing of the facts constituting such offence made by a person authorised by the Government in this behalf. Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Central Act 2 of 1974), an offence under sub-section (1) shall be cognizable.

main_sections.section_title: Enhanced punishment for second or subsequent offence
main_sections.description: Whoever commits an offence punishable under this Act shall, for the first offence, be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, but which shall not be less than three months, and with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees. Provided that the court may, for any adequate and special reasons to be mentioned in the judgment, impose a sentence of imprisonment for a term of less than three months.

If an offence under this Act is committed by a company, every person who, at the time the offence was committed, was in charge of, and was responsible to the company for the conduct of the business of the company, as well as the company, shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly. Provided that nothing contained in this sub-section shall render any such person liable to any punishment provided in this Act if he proves that the offence was committed without his knowledge or that he exercised all due diligence to prevent the commission of such offence.

The amount standing to the credit of any member in the Fund shall not be liable to attachment under any decree or order of any court in respect of any debt or liability incurred by the member, and neither the said amount nor any part thereof shall be a subject of sale in execution of a decree or order of any court. Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, the employer shall be entitled to recover from the employee his contribution by deduction from his wages or in such manner as may be prescribed, and such deduction shall be deemed to be a deduction authorized by or under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 (Central Act 4 of 1936).

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make rules for the purpose of carrying into effect the provisions of this Act. Every rule made under this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before the Legislative Assembly, which, when in session or within a total period of fourteen days which comprises in its one session or in two successive sessions immediately following the session or, if the Legislative Assembly is not in session, within the said period of fourteen days, whichever is earlier, either generally or in such modified form as it likes, and shall, unless the Assembly earlier decides otherwise, be valid only at the expiry of the said period of fourteen days. But without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under the rule.

If, on inspection of the accounts of the Board or otherwise, the Government is satisfied that the Board has made default in the performance of the duties imposed on it by or under this Act or the Scheme, or has persistently failed to comply with any directions issued by the Government or the Chief Welfare Fund Inspector under this Act or the Scheme, or has become incapable of performing its duties, or has contravened any provisions of this Act or the Scheme, the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, supersede the Board for such period as may be specified in the notification. The Government may, at any time, cancel or amend the notification issued under sub-section (1). During the period of supersession, the Board shall not function and the members thereof shall vacate their offices. The Government may, after it has satisfied itself that the Board has been reconstituted or the causes for supersession have been removed, by notification in the Gazette, revoke the supersession. The Government may, at any time, appoint a person or persons to manage the affairs of the Board during the period of supersession.

The Kerala Beedi and Cigar Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Ordinance, 1995 (Ordinance No. 5 of 1995) is hereby repealed. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken or any right accrued or liabilities incurred or any penalty or punishment incurred or any proceeding initiated or any appointment made or any notification issued or any order passed or any rule made or any Scheme framed or any notice served or any licence granted or any fine imposed or any contract entered into or any agreement executed under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken or accrued or incurred or initiated or made or passed or framed or served or granted or imposed or entered into or executed under the corresponding provisions of this Act and accordingly shall have effect for all the purposes of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Bar of jurisdiction of civil courts
main_sections.description: No civil court shall have jurisdiction to settle, decide or deal with any question or to determine any matter which is by or under this Act or the Scheme required to be settled, decided or dealt with or determined by the Government or Chief Welfare Fund Inspector or any other officer appointed under section 10.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make rules for the purpose of carrying into effect the provisions of this Act. Every rule made under this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before the Legislative Assembly, which, when in session or within a total period of fourteen days which comprises in its one session or in two successive sessions immediately following the session or, if the Legislative Assembly is not in session, within the said period of fourteen days, whichever is earlier, either generally or in such modified form as it likes, and shall, unless the Assembly earlier decides otherwise, be valid only at the expiry of the said period of fourteen days. But without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under the rule.

important_rules: Every employer shall, before the fifth day of every month, file a return showing the details of contributions paid into the Fund, in such manner as may be specified in the Scheme.
The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, frame a Scheme to be called the Beedi and Cigar Workers' Welfare Fund Scheme for the establishment of a Fund under this Act.
The Fund shall be applied for the purposes specified in the Scheme, including grants or loans for education, medical benefits, and other welfare measures.
The Board shall be administered by the Fund and audited by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India or any other person appointed by the State Government.
The contributions shall be at the rate of six rupees per mensem for each employee and two rupees per mensem for each self-employed person.
The Government shall contribute to the Fund every year by way of grant or on a matching basis an amount equal to the contribution paid by the employees.
The employer shall be entitled to recover from the employee his contribution by deduction from his wages or in such manner as may be prescribed.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, but which shall not be less than three months, and with fine which may extend to four thousand rupees for a first offence.
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, and with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees for a second or subsequent offence.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Chief Welfare Fund Inspector, Welfare Fund Inspectors, and officers authorized by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By taking cognizance of offences by courts, recovery of amounts due as arrears of land revenue, and other legal proceedings as per the Act and Scheme.

rights: Right to receive welfare measures and pension as per the Scheme.
Right to have contribution credited to the Fund.
Right to have the amount standing to the credit in the Fund protected from attachment.
duties: Duty of employer to pay contributions to the Fund.
Duty of employer to file monthly returns.
Duty of employee/self-employed person to be registered as a member.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act and the Scheme.

key_procedures: Registration of employees and self-employed persons as members of the Scheme.
Collection of contributions from employers and self-employed persons.
Administration of the Fund by the Board.
Application of the Fund for welfare measures as specified in the Scheme.
Filing of monthly returns by employers.
Determination of amounts due from employers by the Chief Welfare Fund Inspector.
Recovery of amounts due from employers.
administration: The Kerala Beedi and Cigar Workers' Welfare Fund Board.
important_notes: Received the assent of the President on the 21st day of November 1995 and Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 1271 dated 16th December 1995.
The Scheme shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly.
The Fund shall be audited by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India or any other person appointed by the State Government.
The provisions of the Act and the Scheme shall be in addition to and not in derogation of any other law for the time being in force.

title: The Kerala Beedi and Cigar Industrial Premises (Regulation of Conditions of Work) Act, 1961
purpose: To regulate the conditions of work in beedi and cigar industrial premises in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to all beedi and cigar industrial premises in the State of Kerala.  The Act regulates the conditions of work for employees in these premises.

key_definitions.adult: A person who has completed his eighteenth year of age.
key_definitions.beedi and cigar industrial premises: Any place or premises (including the precincts thereof) in any part of which any manufacturing process connected with the production of beddies or cigar, or both is being carried on with or without the aid of power.
key_definitions.child: A person who has not completed his fourteenth year of age.
key_definitions.competent authority: Any officer authorised by the Government by notification to perform the functions of the competent authority under the Act for such areas as may be specified in the notification.
key_definitions.day: Means the period of twenty-four hours beginning at mid-night.
key_definitions.employee: Means a person employed directly or through any agency, whether for wages or not, in any beedi and cigar industry, to do any work, skilled, manual or clerical, and includes any person who is employed in such industry and declared by the Government by notification to be an employee for the purpose of this Act.
key_definitions.manufacturing process: Means any process, for, or incidental to, making, finishing, packing, labelling or otherwise treating any article or substance with a view to its use, sale, transport, delivery or disposal as beddies or cigars or both.
key_definitions.notification: Means a notification published in the Gazette.
key_definitions.opened: Means opened for carrying out any of the processes connected with the manufacture of beedi or cigar.
key_definitions.period of work: Means the time during which an employee is at the disposal of the employer.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.wages: Means all remuneration (whether by way of salary, allowances or otherwise) expressed in terms of money or capable of being so expressed, which would, if the terms of employment, express or implied, were fulfilled, be payable to a person employed in respect of his employment or work done in such employment, and includes - (i) any remuneration payable under any award or settlement between the parties or order of a court, (ii) any remuneration to which the person employed is entitled in respect of over-time work or holidays or any leave period, (iii) any additional remuneration payable under the terms of employment (whether called a bonus or by any other name), (iv) any sum which by reason of the termination of employment or the sum which is paid under any law, contract or instrument which provides for the payment of such sum, whether with or without deductions, but does not provide for the time within which the payment is to be made, (v) any sum to which the person employed is entitled under any scheme framed under any law for the time being in force, but does not include- (a) any bonus (whether under a scheme of profit sharing or otherwise) which does not form part of the remuneration payable under the terms of employment or which is not payable under any award or settlement between the parties or order of a court, (b) the value of any house-accommodation, or of the supply of light, water, medical attendance or other amenity or of any service excluded from the computation of wages by a general or special order of the Government, (c) any contribution paid by the employer to any pension or provident fund, and the interest which may have accrued thereon, (d) any travelling allowance or the value of any travelling concession, (e) any sum paid to the employed person to defray special expenses entailed on him by the nature of his employment, or (g) any gratuity payable on the termination of employment in cases other than those specified in sub-clause (iv) ;
key_definitions.week: Means a period of seven days beginning at midnight of Saturday ;
key_definitions.young person: Means a person who has completed his fourteenth year but has not completed his eighteenth year of age.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Beedi and Cigar Industrial Premises (Regulation of Conditions of Work) Act, 1961, extends to the whole of the State of Kerala, and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different areas and for different provisions of the Act.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'adult', 'beedi and cigar industrial premises', 'child', 'competent authority', 'day', 'employee', 'manufacturing process', 'notification', 'opened', 'period of work', 'prescribed', 'wages', 'week', and 'young person'.

main_sections.section_title: Beedi and cigar industrial premises to be licensed
main_sections.description: Mandates that no beedi and cigar industrial premises can be operated without a license from the competent authority. Specifies conditions for obtaining a license, including the suitability of the place, manufacturer's experience, financial capacity, and adherence to labor laws. Also outlines grounds for refusal or cancellation of a license.

Details the process for applying for a license for beedi and cigar industrial premises. Includes requirements for the application form, prescribed fees, and the information that the competent authority shall consider before granting or refusing a license. It also covers the renewal, cancellation, and suspension of licenses, as well as appeal procedures.

Provides for appeals against decisions of the competent authority regarding the grant or refusal of a license or the cancellation or suspension thereof. Appeals are to be made to such authority as the Government may specify.

main_sections.section_title: Opening and closing of beedi and cigar industrial premises
main_sections.description: Specifies that no beedi and cigar industrial premises shall be opened on any day earlier than 7 a.m. or closed later than 7 p.m.

main_sections.section_title: Daily and weekly hours of work in beedi and cigar industrial premises
main_sections.description: Regulates the daily and weekly hours of work for employees.  No employee can be allowed to work in beedi and cigar industrial premises for more than nine hours in a day or more than forty-eight hours in a week.  Exceptions are made for certain workers with specific conditions regarding overtime pay and aggregate work hours.

main_sections.section_title: Spread over of periods of work
main_sections.description: Addresses the 'spread over' of work periods, stating that periods of work of an employee in beedi and cigar industrial premises shall be so arranged that they do not exceed twelve hours in a day and one and a half hours in the intervening period.
Stipulates that where an employee employed in any beedi and cigar industrial premises works overtime, they shall be entitled to wages at twice the ordinary rate of wages for that day.
Requires that every employee in a beedi and cigar industrial premises shall be allowed in each week a holiday of one whole day.  It also details conditions under which wages are payable on a holiday.

Requires that notice of periods of work shall be displayed and correctly maintained in every beedi and cigar industrial premises.  The notice should specify for every day the periods during which employees may be required to work.
States that the wage period for beedi and cigar industrial premises shall not exceed one month.

Grants every employee in a beedi and cigar industrial premises annual leave with wages. The calculation of leave is based on days worked and is at the rate of one day for every twenty days of work.  It also clarifies that this leave is exclusive of holidays occurring during or at the beginning or end of the leave period.

Specifies that for the period of leave, employees are entitled to wages at the rate equal to the daily average of their total full-time earnings in the preceding months.  It also addresses the situation where an employee has not worked for the minimum qualifying period for leave.

Mandates that no employee shall be dismissed without a minimum of one month's notice or wages in lieu thereof.  Provides exceptions for misconduct.  It also requires that when services of employees are dispensed with, a charge of misconduct supported by satisfactory evidence needs to be provided.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of employment of children and women
main_sections.description: Prohibits the employment of children and women in any beedi and cigar industrial premises except between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m.

Empowers the Government to make rules requiring the provision of canteens in beedi and cigar industrial premises employing one hundred and fifty or more employees.  Also, one or more canteens can be provided and maintained by the employer for the use of the employees.

Requires every beedi and cigar industrial premises to provide sufficient latrine and urinal accommodation of prescribed types for the use of employees.  It specifies requirements for separate facilities for male and female employees and proper maintenance, including connection to a waterborne sewage system.
Requires the provision of adequate washing facilities for employees in beedi and cigar industrial premises.
Mandates that every beedi and cigar industrial premises shall be kept clean and free from effluvia arising from any drain, sanitary convenience or nuisance.
Requires that effective and suitable provision shall be made for ventilation in every beedi and cigar industrial premises.
Requires measures for protection against fire in beedi and cigar industrial premises.

main_sections.section_title: Central Act 20 of 1946 to apply to beedi and cigar industrial premises
main_sections.description: States that the Employment of Children Act, 1938 (Central Act XX of 1938), shall apply to beedi and cigar industrial premises.

main_sections.section_title: Application of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, to beedi and cigar industrial premises
main_sections.description: Extends the provisions of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, to beedi and cigar industrial premises.

main_sections.section_title: Factories Act not to apply to beedi and cigar industrial premises
main_sections.description: Exempts beedi and cigar industrial premises from the provisions of the Factories Act, 1948.

main_sections.section_title: Rights and privileges under other laws, etc., not affected
main_sections.description: Clarifies that the Act does not affect any rights or privileges that employees may have under other existing laws.
Grants the Government the power to exempt any beedi or cigar industrial premises from all or any of the provisions of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment, powers and duties of Inspectors
main_sections.description: Details the appointment, powers, and duties of Inspectors appointed under the Act. Inspectors have the power to enter premises, inspect records, and take measures to ensure compliance with the Act.
Outlines the specific powers granted to Inspectors, including the power to enter, inspect, take evidence, and seize documents if necessary for the enforcement of the Act.
Prescribes penalties for obstructing an Inspector in the performance of their duties under the Act.
Provides for a general penalty for contravention of any provision of the Act or rules made thereunder, for which no specific penalty is provided.
Provides indemnity to government servants acting in good faith in pursuance of the provisions of the Act or rules made thereunder.
Specifies that no court shall take cognizance of any offence punishable under this Act except on complaint made by, or with the previous sanction of, the Inspector.
Grants the Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: No beedi and cigar industrial premises shall be opened on any day earlier than 7 a.m. or closed later than 7 p.m. (Section 6).
Employees cannot work more than nine hours a day or forty-eight hours a week, with exceptions for overtime pay (Section 7).
Overtime work must be compensated at twice the ordinary rate of wages (Section 9).
Every employee is entitled to one whole day holiday per week (Section 10).
Notice of periods of work must be displayed (Section 11).
No employee shall be dismissed without at least one month's notice or wages in lieu thereof, except for misconduct (Section 15).
Employment of children and women is restricted to specific hours (Section 16).
Adequate latrine and urinal facilities must be provided for employees (Section 18).
Premises must be kept clean and well-ventilated (Sections 20 & 21).
Measures must be taken for protection against fire (Section 22).

penalties: Penalty for obstructing Inspector (Section 30)
General penalty for offences (Section 31)
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Inspectors appointed under the Act, and the Competent Authority.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections by appointed Inspectors, who have powers to enter premises, examine records, and take evidence. Penalties are prescribed for non-compliance.  The Act also relies on court action for cognizance of offenses based on complaints by Inspectors.

rights: Right to annual leave with wages (Section 13)
Right to wages for overtime work at twice the ordinary rate (Section 9)
Right to a weekly holiday (Section 10)
Right to receive at least one month's notice or wages in lieu of notice before dismissal (Section 15)
Right to adequate latrine and urinal facilities (Section 18)
Right to adequate washing facilities (Section 19)
duties: Duty to obtain a license to operate beedi and cigar industrial premises (Section 3)
Duty to maintain cleanliness and ventilation in premises (Sections 20 & 21)
Duty to display notice of periods of work (Section 11)
Duty to pay wages for overtime work at the prescribed rate (Section 9)
Duty to provide a weekly holiday (Section 10)
Duty to provide notice before dismissal or pay wages in lieu thereof (Section 15)
obligations: Obligation to comply with the regulations concerning working hours, spread over, holidays, and leave.
Obligation to provide and maintain sanitary facilities and ensure cleanliness and ventilation.
Obligation to provide adequate facilities for protection against fire.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining a license for beedi and cigar industrial premises, including application submission, consideration by the competent authority, and issuance or refusal of the license (Section 4).
Procedure for renewal, cancellation, or suspension of licenses, with provisions for appeals (Sections 4 & 5).
Procedure for Inspectors to enforce the Act, including inspection of premises and records (Sections 28 & 29).
Procedure for filing complaints in court for offenses under the Act, requiring Inspector's complaint or sanction (Section 33).
administration: The Government of Kerala and the Competent Authority appointed by the Government.
important_notes: The Act aims to regulate the conditions of work, not the industry itself, distinguishing it from the Factories Act.
The Act was enacted in 1961 and came into force in 1962.
The Act provides for specific exemptions from its provisions by the Government.
The Act clarifies that it does not affect rights or privileges employees may have under other laws.
The definition of 'wages' is comprehensive and includes various forms of remuneration.

title: THE KERALA BOARD OF REVENUE ABOLITION ACT, 1996
purpose: To abolish the Board of Revenue in Kerala and transfer its functions and powers to other authorities.
scope: Applies to the entire State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Board of Revenue: Refers to the Board of Revenue constituted under the Board of Revenue Act, 1981.
key_definitions.State Government: Refers to the Government of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act and its commencement date.
This section defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'Board of Revenue', 'State Government', and 'Prescribed'.

main_sections.section_title: Abolition of the Board of Revenue
main_sections.description: This section formally abolishes the Board of Revenue of Kerala.
This section details the transfer of powers, functions, and proceedings of the Board of Revenue to the State Government or such other authorities as may be specified.
This section repeals the relevant existing laws and includes provisions for savings, ensuring continuity and validity of actions taken prior to the abolition.

important_rules: The Board of Revenue shall stand abolished from such date as the Government may by notification appoint.
All powers, functions, and proceedings of the Board of Revenue shall be transferred to the State Government or such other authority as may be specified by the State Government.

Any appointment, order, rule, or notification made or issued by the Board of Revenue before its abolition shall continue to be in force until superseded by an order or notification by the State Government.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government of Kerala.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the transfer of powers and functions to designated authorities and the continuation of existing legal frameworks where applicable.

rights: Right to have the functions and powers of the abolished Board of Revenue exercised by the designated authorities.
duties: Duty of the State Government to ensure the smooth transfer of functions and proceedings.
Duty of the designated authorities to exercise the transferred powers and functions diligently.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the provisions of the Act regarding the abolition and transfer of functions.

key_procedures: Notification by the State Government to appoint the date of abolition.
Transfer of all pending proceedings and records from the Board of Revenue to the successor authorities.
Issuance of necessary orders and notifications by the State Government to delegate or assign the functions of the Board of Revenue.
administration: The Law Department, Government of Kerala, and other designated departments/authorities.
important_notes: The Act aims to streamline administrative structures in Kerala by abolishing the Board of Revenue.
The provisions of the Act are designed to ensure that the abolition does not disrupt governance or affect pending legal matters.
The State Government has the authority to specify which authorities will take over the functions of the Board of Revenue.

title: The Kerala Board of Revenue Act, 1957
purpose: To constitute a Board of Revenue for the State of Kerala and to define its powers and functions.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Board: Means the Board of Revenue constituted under this Act.
key_definitions.member: Means a member of the Board.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Board of Revenue Act, 1957. (2) It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. (3) It shall come into force at once.
Defines 'Board' and 'member'.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of the Board of Revenue
main_sections.description: There shall be constituted for the State of Kerala a Board of Revenue consisting of one or more members as the Government may from time to time think fit to appoint.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of control and supervision of the Board
main_sections.description: The Board shall be the administrative head of the departments mentioned in the First Schedule and shall exercise general supervision over all authorities in the State in so far as such authorities deal with matters mentioned in the First Schedule. The Board shall exercise such other powers as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, confer on it.

main_sections.section_title: Exercise of jurisdiction by one or more members of the Board
main_sections.description: The Board, with the previous sanction of the Government, may make rules for the exercise by one or more members of the Board of the powers and functions of the Board and all decisions made pursuant to such exercise shall be deemed to be the decisions of the Board.

main_sections.section_title: Decision on matters before the Board
main_sections.description: The decision in any case before the full Board or before two or more members thereof shall be in accordance with the opinion of the majority of the members. Where there is no such majority concurring in the same decision in a case before two or more members not constituting the full Board, the entire case shall be referred to the full Board for its decision. When there is no majority concurring in the same decision in a case before the full Board, the matter on which there is disagreement shall be referred to the Government and such matter shall be decided according to the opinion of the Government.

The Board may, either of its own motion or on the application of any party, review any order passed by itself on the ground of mistake, misrepresentation, fraud or error of procedure or any other sufficient reason and pass such orders in reference thereto as it thinks fit. Provided that an order shall be varied or reversed to the disadvantage of any party unless notice has been given to such party.
Every application under section 7 for a review of an order must be made within a period of three months from the date of the order.

The Board may, from time to time with the previous sanction of the Government, make rules for regulating generally the practice and procedure of the Board including rules as to the persons practising before the Board, as to the time within which, in the absence of any express provision in the relevant enactment, appeals or applications for revision to the Board may be filed, and as to the cost and incidental to any proceedings before the Board.

The Board shall, in respect of all matters subject to its appellate or revisional jurisdiction, have superintendence over all authorities. In so far as such authorities deal with matters subject to the superintendence of the Board, the following things, that is to say:

main_sections.section_title: Power to amend the First and Second Schedules
main_sections.description: The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, amend, alter or add to the First or Second Schedule.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to make rules
main_sections.description: The Government may make rules to carry out all or any of the purposes of this Act.
All rules made under this Act shall be published in the Gazette.
The enactments mentioned in the Third Schedule, in so far as they are applicable to any part of the State of Kerala, are hereby repealed.

important_rules: Rules regarding the practice and procedure of the Board (Section 9).
Rules for regulating the practice and proceedings in respect of accounts (Section 10(b)).
Rules regarding prescription of forms in which books, entries and accounts shall be kept by such authorities (Section 10(c)).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Board of Revenue.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through its administrative functions, control, supervision, and the power to make rules.

rights: Right to apply for review of an order (Section 7).
duties: Duty to exercise general supervision over all authorities (Section 4).
obligations: Obligation to provide notice to a party before varying or reversing an order to their disadvantage (Section 7).

key_procedures: Procedure for review of orders (Section 7) - Board can review its own motion or upon application, on grounds of mistake, misrepresentation, fraud, or error of procedure, provided notice is given if the order is varied to a party's disadvantage.
Procedure for application for review - Must be made within three months from the date of the order (Section 8).
administration: The Board of Revenue.
important_notes: The First Schedule lists departments over which the Board shall have administrative control, including Land revenue, Records and land acquisition, Excise and prohibition, Court of Wards, Sales-tax, Mines and minerals, Tamine relief, Civil supplies, and Housing.
The Third Schedule contains enactments that are repealed.
The Act was enacted by the President in the Eighth Year of the Republic of India.

title: THE KERALA BORSTAL SCHOOLS ACT, 1961 (ACT 31 OF 1961)
purpose: To make provision for the establishment and regulation of borstal schools for the detention and training of adolescent offenders.
scope: The Act applies to adolescent offenders in the State of Kerala. Specific provisions are made for their detention, training, and the management of borstal schools. It also applies to the transfer of incorrigibles, etc., to prisons and provides for appeal and revision.

key_definitions.adolescent offender: Means any person who has been convicted of any offence punishable with imprisonment or who has been ordered to give security under section 118 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (Central Act 5 of 1898), has failed to do so and who at the time of such conviction or failure to give security is not less than 16 years of age but not more than 21 years of age.
key_definitions.borstal school: Means a corrective institution wherein adolescent offenders, while detained in pursuance of this Act, are given such industrial or agricultural training and other instruction and are subject to such disciplinary and moral influences as will conduce to their reformation and the prevention of crime.
key_definitions.Inspector-General: Means the Inspector-General of Prisons and includes any officer appointed by the Government to exercise or perform all or any of the powers or duties of the Inspector-General under this Act.
key_definitions.probation officer: Means an officer appointed to be a probation officer or recognised as such under section 13 of the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958 (Central Act 20 of 1958).

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Borstal Schools Act, 1961 and outlines its application. It can be applied by notification in the Gazette to adolescent offenders in any local area in the State. The Government can modify or cancel such notification.
This section provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'adolescent offender', 'borstal school', 'Inspector-General', 'probation officer', and 'State'.
This section empowers the Government to establish borstal schools and specifies that every borstal school shall be visited by a Superintendent appointed by the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Application of the Prisons Acts and the Prisoners Acts.
main_sections.description: This section states that the Prisons Acts and the Prisoners Acts, as applicable to the State, will apply to borstal schools and prisoners detained therein, with certain adaptations and exceptions.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Court to pass order of detention in borstal school.
main_sections.description: This section outlines the power of a court to order the detention of an adolescent offender in a borstal school, subject to the offender's character, habits, or residence, and if it appears to the court that the offender's detention in a borstal school would be conducive to his reformation and the prevention of crime. It also specifies conditions regarding the term of detention, which should not be less than two years and not exceed seven years, and not extend beyond the age of twenty-one years.

main_sections.section_title: Preliminary inquiry and finding as to age of adolescent offender.
main_sections.description: This section mandates a preliminary inquiry before passing an order under section 5, to determine the age of the adolescent offender.

main_sections.section_title: Limitation on powers conferred by section 5.
main_sections.description: This section clarifies that the power to order detention in a borstal school is subject to the provisions of section 5.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Inspector-General to transfer persons to borstal school.
main_sections.description: This section grants the Inspector-General the power to transfer adolescent offenders who have been sentenced to imprisonment to a borstal school, subject to certain conditions and Government approval. It also clarifies that such transfer is not to be considered a punishment.

main_sections.section_title: Government to determine the borstal school to which adolescent offender shall be sent.
main_sections.description: This section empowers the Government to decide which borstal school an adolescent offender will be sent to.

main_sections.section_title: Removal from one borstal school to another.
main_sections.description: This section allows the Inspector-General to remove an inmate from one borstal school to another.

main_sections.section_title: Reception of offenders from and transfer of offenders to other States in India.
main_sections.description: This section deals with the reception of offenders from other States and the transfer of offenders to other States in India, with Government approval.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of incorrigibles, etc., to prisons.
main_sections.description: This section allows for the transfer of inmates who are incorrigible or who pose a bad influence to prisons. It specifies that the remaining term of imprisonment shall be computed in the manner prescribed and that the maximum period of imprisonment in a prison shall not exceed seven years.

This section gives the Inspector-General the power to release inmates on licence, after considering the report of the probation officer, if satisfied that there is a reasonable probability that the inmate will abstain from crime and lead a useful and industrious life. The licence may contain conditions, including abstention from the vicinity of the borstal school or from association with criminals. The licence holder must report to the officer in charge of the police station and to the probation officer. The licence can be revoked.
This section states that every licence granted under section 13 shall be in such form and shall contain such conditions as the Government may by rules prescribe.

This section details the process of revoking a licence. The Inspector-General can revoke a licence if the inmate absconds from a borstal school or fails to return to the borstal school upon revocation of the licence. The inmate may be arrested without warrant and taken back to the borstal school. The licence can also be revoked if the inmate violates any condition of the licence.

This section states that if an inmate escapes from a borstal school, his licence shall be forfeited. If he absconds from a borstal school or fails to return to it when his licence is revoked, he shall be liable to be arrested without warrant and taken back to the borstal school. The period of absence from the borstal school shall be treated as part of the term of his detention. Any inmate failing to return to the borstal school after his licence has expired or has been revoked shall be excluded in computing the time during which he is to be detained in the borstal school.

This section allows the Inspector-General to release an inmate on parole for such period or periods and subject to such conditions as may be determined by him. This can be for the purpose of enabling the inmate to take up employment or to receive instructions or training.

main_sections.section_title: Absence under licence or on parole to be counted towards period of detention.
main_sections.description: This section specifies that absence under licence or on parole shall be counted towards the period of detention.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Inspector-General to allow inmates to receive instruction or training.
main_sections.description: This section empowers the Inspector-General to allow inmates to receive instructions or training. The Government may also allow inmates to receive instruction or training in any other institution without being released from the borstal school.

This section details the management of borstal schools, including the constitution, powers, and duties of visiting committees. It states that the visiting committee shall consist of the Sessions Judge, the District Magistrate, and the District Educational Officer of the district in which the school is situated, along with non-official members appointed by the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution, powers and duties of visiting committees.
main_sections.description: This section elaborates on the constitution, powers, and duties of visiting committees. It mentions that non-official members shall hold office for two years and can be re-appointed. The committee's duties include visiting the school, advising on improvements, reporting to the Inspector-General, interviewing inmates, and considering cases of release on licence. The Government shall be entitled to all information from the Superintendent regarding the records of the school and can take action as deemed necessary.
This section states that inmates of a borstal school shall be divided by the Superintendent according to their industry and good conduct into three grades: ordinary, star, and special.

This section lists the punishments that may be inflicted on an inmate for offences. These include formal warning, extra drill, deprivation of privileges, and reduction in grade. No punishment shall be awarded to an inmate by any official except the Superintendent or in his absence, the exercising officer. It also mentions that the punishments shall be in the forms and no other, i.e. formal warning, extra drill, deprivation of the privileges of the grade, and reduction in grade.

This section states that no inmate of a borstal school shall be made to work for more than six hours a day. Provided that extra drill awarded as a punishment under sub-section (1) of section 23 shall not be deemed for the purposes of this section to be work.

This section pertains to the appeal and revision processes under the Act. Any person affected by an order of the Inspector-General under this Act may appeal to the Government whose orders shall be final. This is in accordance with the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (Central Act 5 of 1898).

main_sections.section_title: Minimum age-limit of adolescents in areas to which the Children Acts have not been extended.
main_sections.description: This section specifies the minimum age-limit of adolescents in areas where the Children Acts have not been extended. It refers to the provisions of the Madras Children Act, 1920 (Act IV of 1920), the Cochin Children Act, XXXVI of 1111, and the Travancore Children Act, 1120 (Act XXIX of 1120). It notes that figures '16' appearing in section 2(i) of this Act shall be read as '15'.

important_rules: Inmates can be released on licence if there is a reasonable probability they will abstain from crime and lead an industrious life. The licence may stipulate conditions like abstaining from the vicinity of the borstal school or from associating with criminals.
