The licence holder must report to the officer in charge of the police station and the probation officer.
The Inspector-General has the power to revoke a licence if the inmate escapes or fails to return to the borstal school.
Absence under licence or on parole counts towards the period of detention.
Visiting committees have duties including visiting schools, advising on improvements, interviewing inmates, and considering release cases.
Inmates are classified into three grades: ordinary, star, and special, based on industry and conduct.
Punishments for offences include formal warning, extra drill, deprivation of privileges, and reduction in grade.
Inmates cannot be made to work for more than six hours a day.

penalties: Formal warning
Extra drill
Deprivation of the privileges of the grade
Reduction in grade
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Inspector-General, Government, Courts, Probation Officers, Superintendent of Borstal Schools, Visiting Committees.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through orders of detention in borstal schools, transfer to prisons, revocation of licences, arrests for escape or failure to return, and adherence to prescribed rules and procedures.

rights: Right to have age determined before passing an order of detention.
Right to appeal and revision against orders.
Right to be informed of the terms of licence and conditions.
Right to be considered for release on licence or parole.
Right to receive instruction or training.
duties: Duty of the court to conduct preliminary inquiry regarding age.
Duty of the Inspector-General to consider probation officer's report before release on licence.
Duty of the Superintendent to classify inmates into grades.
Duty of the Superintendent to maintain records and submit reports.
Duty of the visiting committee to visit schools and advise on improvements.
obligations: Adherence to the conditions of licence or parole.
Abstention from crime and leading an industrious life.
Reporting to designated authorities as per licence conditions.
Compliance with disciplinary and moral influences in the borstal school.
Compliance with rules regarding hours of work and punishment.

key_procedures: Committal to Borstal School: Court passes an order of detention after preliminary inquiry into age and suitability for reformation. The Government determines the specific borstal school.
Release on Licence: Inspector-General can grant licence based on probation officer's report, subject to conditions. Licence can be revoked for escape, failure to return, or violation of conditions.
Transfer of Inmates: Inmates can be transferred between borstal schools, to other States, or to prisons if incorrigible, with Government approval.
Management and Visiting Committees: Borstal schools are managed by Superintendents, with oversight from visiting committees and the Inspector-General.
Classification and Punishment: Inmates are graded, and punishments are prescribed for offences.
Appeal and Revision: Procedures exist for appeal and revision against orders passed under the Act.
administration: The Act is administered by the Government of Kerala, with the Inspector-General of Prisons and the Superintendent of Borstal Schools playing key roles. The Department of Home or equivalent is likely responsible for the implementation.
important_notes: The Act's applicability can be extended by notification in the Gazette.
The age limit for an adolescent offender is between 16 and 21 years, but can be read as 15 in certain areas.
The term of detention in a borstal school generally does not exceed seven years and shall not extend beyond the age of twenty-one years.
Transfers to prisons are for incorrigible inmates.
The Government has broad powers to make rules and issue notifications to further the provisions of the Act.

title: THE KERALA BUILDING TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1990 (Act 1 of 1991)
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala Building Tax Act, 1975, for the purpose hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala. The amendments are to the Kerala Building Tax Act, 1975.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Building Tax (Amendment) Act, 1990. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 6th day of November, 1990.

Inserts a new section 3A titled 'Power to make exemption'. This section empowers the Government to make exemptions from payment of building tax for the promotion of tourism or for buildings constructed during a specific period or in specific areas, as may be prescribed by rules.
Repeals the Kerala Building Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 1990 (8 of 1990) and saves any action taken or done under the said Ordinance as amended by this Act.

important_rules: The Government may grant exemption from the payment of building tax for the promotion of tourism.
Exemptions can be granted for buildings constructed during a specific period or in specific areas.
Specifics of exemptions are to be prescribed in the rules.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government (for granting exemptions)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through rules and by virtue of the principal Act.

rights: Right of the Government to make exemptions for tourism promotion or specific building construction.

key_procedures: Procedure for seeking exemption from building tax by the Government.
administration: The Government of Kerala
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 3rd day of January, 1991 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 24 dated the 4th January, 1991.

title: The Kerala Building Tax (Amendment) Act, 1992
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Building Tax Act, 1975.
scope: Applies to buildings in Kerala. The amendments pertain to the calculation of building tax, exemptions, and related procedures.

key_definitions.appointed day: Date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
key_definitions.plinth area: Means the area included in the floor of a building and where a building has more than one-floor the aggregate area included in all the floors together.
key_definitions.major repair or improvement: Means a repair or improvement in respect of a building the result of which the plinth area of the building is increased.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Building Tax (Amendment) Act, 1992. It will come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette appoint, and the remaining provisions will come into force on the 10th day of February, 1992.
Amends section 2 of the Kerala Building Tax Act, 1975 by substituting clauses related to definitions of 'appointed day', 'major repair or improvement', and adding clauses for 'plinth area'.
Amends section 3 of the principal Act by substituting words, figures and bracket in sub-section (1) or under section 3A.
Amends section 3A of the principal Act by substituting sub-section (1) and adding a new sub-section (1A) regarding the Government's power to exempt payment of building tax.

Inserts a new section 3B titled 'Misuse of exemption by the assessee'. It states that if a building for which exemption was granted is used for a purpose other than that for which exemption was given, the owner shall be liable to pay building tax along with a penalty.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 5
main_sections.description: Substitutes section 5 of the principal Act with a new section detailing 'Charge of building tax' based on plinth area and other provisions.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 6
main_sections.description: Substitutes section 6 of the principal Act with a new section regarding 'Determination of plinth area' for the purposes of the Act.
Amends section 7 of the principal Act. Sub-section (1) is substituted, and sub-section (2) is omitted.

Amends section 13 of the principal Act by adding sub-section (4) stating no application for revision under sub-section (1) by an aggrieved party shall lie if fifty percent of the building tax has been paid.
Section 16 of the principal Act is omitted.

Amends section 18 of the principal Act by renumbering sub-section (1) and substituting the subsequent sub-section, detailing the issuance of completion certificate or assignment of building number or door number.
Amends section 23 of the principal Act by substituting the words 'in this behalf' with 'either suo motu or on application by the assessee'.
Amends section 26 of the principal Act by substituting clause (a) of sub-section (2) regarding the determination of plinth area of buildings and the plinth area of major repairs and improvements.

Substitutes the Schedule in the principal Act with a new Schedule titled 'Rate of Building Tax' which specifies rates for residential and other buildings based on plinth area and type of local authority.

Repeals the Kerala Building Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 1992 (2 of 1992) and provides that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Buildings are classified for tax purposes based on their plinth area and type (residential vs. other).
The tax rate increases with the plinth area of the building.
Exemptions granted for building tax can be revoked if the building is misused, leading to liability for tax and penalty.
The plinth area of associated structures like out-houses, garages, etc., is added to the main building's plinth area for tax calculation.
The building tax is payable by the owner of the building.

penalties: Penalty at the rate of 12% per annum on the date of completion of construction of the building for misuse of exemption.

If the building tax is not paid or paid short, the owner shall be liable to pay the building tax along with penalty at the rate of 12% per annum from the date of completion of construction of the building.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Assessing authority appointed under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment of building tax, imposition of penalties for misuse of exemptions or non-payment/short payment of tax, and by requiring submission of relevant information and certificates.

rights: Right to exemption from building tax under specific conditions (e.g., for certain types of buildings or if the building tax paid is less than twenty-five per cent of the total cost of construction).
Right to be heard before an assessment is made or revised.
Right to revision of assessment.
duties: Duty to pay building tax as per the provisions of the Act.
Duty to comply with notification requirements by the Government regarding commencement of the Act and its provisions.
Duty to provide information and certificates as required by the assessing authority.
obligations: Obligation to pay building tax with penalty if exemption is misused.
Obligation to pay the building tax on the plinth area of the building.
Obligation to pay the building tax on major repairs or improvements that increase the plinth area.

key_procedures: Obtaining exemption from building tax requires meeting specific criteria and may involve an application to the assessing authority.
Determination of plinth area for tax assessment involves measurement and verification, possibly by the local authority or other specified bodies.
Revision of assessment is a process available to aggrieved parties, with a condition of paying a portion of the tax.
Issuance of completion certificates and assignment of building numbers/door numbers are linked to tax assessment.
administration: Law (Legislation-A) Department, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act provides for the substitution of the Schedule with rates of Building Tax for different categories of buildings.
In the case of buildings certified by a competent authority (like Nirmitthi Kendras) as low-cost residential buildings, the rate of building tax shall be reduced by 25%.
The Act repeals the Kerala Building Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 1992, but ensures continuity of actions taken under the Ordinance.

title: THE KERALA BUILDINGS (LEASE AND RENT CONTROL) AMENDMENT ACT, 1966
purpose: To amend the Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1965.
scope: The Act applies to buildings within the State of Kerala and governs lease and rent control matters.

key_definitions.tenant: Means any person by whom or on whose account rent is payable for a building and includes (i) the heir or heirs of a deceased tenant, and (ii) a person continuing in possession after the termination of the tenancy of his favour, but does not include a Kudikidappukaran as defined in the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 (Kerala Act 1 of 1964) or a person placed in occupation of the building by its tenant or a person to whom the collection of rents or fees in a public market, cart-stand or slaughter-house or of rents for shops has been farmed out or leased by a Municipal Council, Municipal Corporation or Township Committee or Panchayat.
key_definitions.fair rent: Refers to the fair rent fixed by the Rent Control Court, and if not so fixed, it means the fair rent as determined by the Controller. The amendment specifies criteria for determining fair rent in certain cases, including based on property tax or house tax.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Amendment Act, 1966. Clause (a) of section 2 shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1965, and the remaining provisions of this Act shall come into force at once.
Amends section 2 of the principal Act by inserting certain clauses and substituting words, specifically regarding the definition of 'tenant' and 'fair rent'.
Amends section 5 of the principal Act, particularly in the proviso to sub-section (2), concerning the determination of 'fair rent'.

Amends section 11 of the principal Act, for clause (c) of sub-section (2), the following clause shall be substituted: '(c) the order of the Rent Control Court directing the tenant to put the landlord in possession of the building shall not be executed before the expiry of one month from the date of such order or such further period as the Rent Control Court may, in its discretion allow; and if the tenant deposits the arrears of rent with interest and cost of proceedings within the said period of one month or such further period, as the case may be, it shall vacate that order.'

Amends section 13 of the principal Act, inserting new provisions regarding 'Accommodation Controller' and substituting words. It also specifies that any application pending before the Rent Control Court immediately before the commencement of this Act shall stand transferred to the Accommodation Controller.
Amends section 14 of the principal Act, by adding new words and figures to section 12.
Inserts a new section 20A titled 'Power to revise' which allows the appellate authority or the revising authority, as the case may be, to revise any order for good cause shown.
Amends section 26 of the principal Act, substituting words 'Municipal Council', 'Municipal Corporation or Township Committee' where they occur.

Amends the Schedule to the principal Act, by making references to Municipality, Corporation or Township as constricting references to the area for the time being within the jurisdiction of the Municipal Council, Municipal Corporation or Township Committee, as the case may be.

main_sections.section_title: Re-opening of orders for eviction in certain cases
main_sections.description: This section deals with the re-opening of orders for eviction. Notwithstanding any decree or order of court, where after the 2nd day of April, 1959, and before the 31st day of August, 1961, an order has been made by the Rent Control Court under sub-section (3) of section 12 of the Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1959, directing the tenant to put the landlord in possession of a building, on the ground that the tenant has failed to pay or deposit the arrears of rent under subsections (1) and (2) of that section, without giving the tenant the time specified in the proviso to the said sub-section (2), the tenant shall, on deposit of all arrears of rent admitted by him to be due in respect of the building up to the date of deposit, be entitled to make an application within thirty days from the date of publication of this Act for re-opening the order, and on such application the Rent Control Court shall re-open the order and dispose of it afresh in accordance with the provisions of the said Act as if it had not expired: Provided that no tenant shall be entitled to make an application under this section if the landlord had obtained possession of the building before the date of the publication of this Act.

important_rules: Rule regarding the execution of eviction orders, allowing for vacation if rent arrears are deposited.
Rules for determining 'fair rent' based on property tax or house tax.
Tenant's entitlement to apply for re-opening of eviction orders under specific conditions related to rent deposit and timing.

penalties: Specific penalties are not detailed in the provided sections, but the Act enables enforcement through Rent Control Courts and Accommodation Controllers.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Rent Control Courts and Accommodation Controllers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through court orders, eviction proceedings, and revision powers of authorities.

rights: Right of a tenant to apply for re-opening of an eviction order under certain circumstances.
Right of a tenant to have an eviction order vacated upon depositing rent arrears.
Right to have pending applications transferred to the Accommodation Controller.
duties: Duty of a tenant to pay or deposit rent as stipulated by the Act.
obligations: Obligation of the landlord to follow the prescribed procedure for eviction.

key_procedures: Procedure for determining 'fair rent' based on property tax or house tax.
Procedure for re-opening eviction orders by tenants who deposit rent arrears.
Procedure for transferring pending applications to the Accommodation Controller.
administration: The Act is administered through Rent Control Courts and Accommodation Controllers, likely under the purview of a State Government department related to housing or revenue.
important_notes: The Act came into force with retrospective effect from April 1, 1965, for certain provisions.
References to 'Municipality', 'Municipal Corporation' or 'Township Committee' in the Schedule are construed as references to the area within the jurisdiction of these bodies.
An order of eviction can be vacated if the tenant deposits all arrears of rent, including interest and costs, within a specified period.

title: THE KERALA BUILDING TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1980
purpose: An Act to amend the Kerala Building Tax Act, 1975.
scope: Applies to buildings in Kerala, specifically amending the Kerala Building Tax Act, 1975.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Building Tax (Amendment) Act, 1980, and it came into force on the 1st day of April, 1973.
Amends section 2 of the Kerala Building Tax Act, 1975 (7 of 1975) by substituting "sixteen" with "ten" in clause (f) and "seventy-five thousand rupees" for "twenty thousand rupees" in clause (h).

Amends section 5 of the principal Act by substituting "seventy-five thousand rupees" for "twenty thousand rupees" in sub-section (1), and in sub-section (3), and "twenty-five thousand rupees" for "ten thousand rupees" in sub-section (4).

Amends section 7 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1) by substituting "seventy-five thousand rupees" for "twenty thousand rupees" in clause (a) and "twenty-five thousand rupees" for "ten thousand rupees" in clause (d).

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new Schedule for existing Schedule.
main_sections.description: Substitutes a new Schedule for the existing Schedule in the principal Act, detailing the rates of building tax based on capital value.

important_rules: The rate of tax is Nil where the capital value of a building is Rs. 75,000 or less.
For buildings where the capital value exceeds Rs. 75,000, the tax rate increases incrementally with the capital value.
The tax rates are specified for different slabs of capital value, including the first Rs. 25,000 of such excess, and subsequent increments of Rs. 25,000, Rs. 50,000, and the balance.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided sections.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided sections.

key_procedures: Amendment of specific sections of the Kerala Building Tax Act, 1975 by substitution of monetary values and schedules.
Substitution of the Schedule to define new rates of building tax based on capital value.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided sections, but implied to be the authority responsible for the Kerala Building Tax Act, 1975.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 15th day of January 1981.
Published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 47 dated the 16th January, 1981.

title: THE KERALA BUILDING TAX ACT, 1975
purpose: An Act to provide for the levy of a tax on buildings.
scope: It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1975.

key_definitions.annual value of a building: The gross annual rent which the building may at the time of completion be expected to let from month to month or from year to year.
key_definitions.appellate authority: An appellate authority appointed under section 4.
key_definitions.assessee: A person by whom building tax or any other sum of money is payable under this Act and includes every person in respect of whom any proceeding under this Act has been taken for the assessment of the building tax payable by him.
key_definitions.assessing authority: An assessing authority appointed under section 4.
key_definitions.building: A house, out-house, garage, or any other structure, or part thereof, whether of masonry, bricks, wood, metal or other material, but does not include any portable shelter or any shed constructed principally of mud, bamboos, leaves, grass or thatch or a latrine which is not attached to the main structure.
key_definitions.capital value of a building: The value arrived at by multiplying the annual value of a building by sixteen.
key_definitions.local authority: A municipal corporation or a municipal council or a township committee or a panchayat or a cantonment board.
key_definitions.major repair or improvement: In respect of a building, means a repair or improvement as a result of which the capital value of the building is increased by more than twenty thousand rupees.
key_definitions.owner: Includes a person who for the time being is receiving, or is entitled to receive, the rent of any building, whether on his own account or on account of himself and others or as an agent, trustee, guardian or receiver for any other person or who should so received the rent or be entitled to receive it if the building or part thereof were let to a tenant.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Building Tax Act, 1975, extends to the whole of Kerala, and came into force on April 1, 1975.

Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'annual value', 'appellate authority', 'assessee', 'assessing authority', 'building', 'capital value', 'local authority', 'major repair or improvement', 'owner', and 'prescribed'.

Lists exemptions from the Act, including buildings owned by the Government of Kerala or the Government of India, and buildings used principally for religious, charitable or educational purposes or as factories or workshops. An explanation clarifies 'charitable purpose' to include relief of the poor and free medical relief. It also outlines the procedure for resolving questions of whether a building falls under exemption.

Empowers the Government to appoint assessing authorities and appellate authorities for the purposes of the Act. It also states that all officers and persons employed in the execution of the Act shall observe and follow the orders, instructions, and directions of the Board of Revenue.

States that a tax (building tax) shall be charged at the rate specified in the Schedule in respect of every building, the construction of which is completed on or after April 1, 1973, and the capital value of which exceeds twenty thousand rupees. It also addresses tax on major repairs or improvements and on new constructions or additions.

Lays out the process for determining the capital value for the purposes of the Act, which is the annual value fixed for a building in the assessment books of the local authority. It includes provisions for cases where the annual value is too low or not fixed, and specifies factors the assessing authority shall have regard to, such as location, nature and quality of the structure, capability for profitable use, amenities, access to roads, land value, estimated construction cost, and other prescribed factors.

main_sections.section_title: Return of completion, etc., of building
main_sections.description: Requires the owner of every building to furnish a return within two months from the date of completion of construction, or major repairs or improvements, or new constructions or additions or combinations. It also stipulates the content of such returns and the circumstances under which the assessing authority may issue a notice to furnish a return.

main_sections.section_title: Return after due date and amendment of return
main_sections.description: Deals with the situation where a person has not furnished a return within the allowed time or has furnished an incorrect or wrong statement, allowing for a revised return.

Outlines the process of assessment by the assessing authority, including serving notice to the assessee to produce or cause to be produced evidence of their return. It also covers the authority's power to conduct inquiries or inspections and to make an assessment based on available evidence or after hearing the assessee.
Covers the issuance of a notice of demand for the tax assessed.
Deals with appeals against assessment orders.
Allows for reference to the District Court on questions of law.

main_sections.section_title: Power of revision of the District Collector
main_sections.description: Grants the District Collector power to revise orders.

main_sections.section_title: Power of revision of the Government
main_sections.description: Grants the Government power to revise orders.
Allows for the rectification of mistakes in orders.

main_sections.section_title: Revision of building tax when annual value is revised by local authority
main_sections.description: Deals with the revision of building tax when the annual value of the building is revised by the local authority.

main_sections.section_title: Power to take evidence on oath, etc.
main_sections.description: Grants the assessing or appellate authority power to take evidence on oath.
Specifies the manner and time of payment of building tax.
Outlines the modes and times for recovery of building tax.
Covers provisions for refunds of building tax.
Addresses the consequences of making false statements in declarations.
Deals with penalties for failure to furnish a return.
Grants the assessing authority power to inspect buildings.
Covers provisions related to prosecutions under the Act.
Specifies the manner in which notices are to be served.
Grants the Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.
Restricts suits against Government or any officer for acts done in good faith under the Act.
Deals with the computation of the period of limitation for actions under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Building tax not to be taken into account in fixing fair rent
main_sections.description: States that building tax should not be considered when fixing fair rent.
Empowers the Government to remove difficulties in the application of the Act.
Repeals previous legislation and provides savings.

important_rules: Rule: Owners of buildings must furnish returns upon completion of construction, major repairs, improvements, new constructions, or additions within two months of the completion date.
Rule: Building tax is charged on buildings with a capital value exceeding twenty thousand rupees.
Rule: False statements in declarations can lead to penalties.

penalties: Penalties for failure to furnish return.
Penalties for making false statements in declarations.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Assessing authorities appointed by the Government, and appellate authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment of tax, issuance of notices of demand, recovery procedures, and potentially prosecutions.

rights: Right to appeal against assessment orders.
Right to seek revision of orders from the District Collector and the Government.
Right to rectification of mistakes in orders.
Right to receive refunds where applicable.
duties: Duty to furnish returns of completion, major repairs, improvements, new constructions, or additions.
Duty to pay building tax.
Duty to comply with notices and orders issued under the Act.
obligations: Obligation to allow inspection of buildings by the assessing authority.

key_procedures: Procedure for assessment of building tax, including furnishing of returns, inquiry, inspection, and determination of tax liability.
Procedure for appeal against assessment orders, including reference to the District Court and powers of revision for the District Collector and the Government.
Procedure for recovery of building tax.
Procedure for rectification of mistakes in orders.
Procedure for serving notices.
administration: The Government of Kerala and the Board of Revenue are involved in the administration, with powers to appoint authorities and issue directions.
important_notes: Buildings used principally for religious, charitable or educational purposes or as factories or workshops are exempt.
The Act applies to buildings constructed on or after April 1, 1973, with a capital value exceeding twenty thousand rupees.
The Act aims to levy tax on buildings, and its provisions extend to the entire state of Kerala.

title: The Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1959
purpose: To control the lease and rent of buildings in Kerala.
scope: Applies to buildings in Kerala.

main_sections.description: Payment or deposit of rent during the pendency of proceedings for eviction. (1) No tenant against whom an application for eviction has been made by a landlord under section 11, shall be entitled to contest the application before the Rent Control Court under that section, or to prefer any appeal under section 18 against any order made by the Rent Control Court on the application, unless he has paid or deposits to the landlord or deposits with the Rent Control Court or the appellate authority, as the case may be, all arrears of rent admitted by the tenant to be due in respect of the building up to the date of payment or deposit and continues to pay or to deposit any rent which may subsequently become due in respect of the building, until the termination of the proceedings before the Rent Control Court or the appellate authority, as the case may be.

The deposit of rent under sub-section (1) shall be made within the time and in the manner prescribed and shall be accompanied by the fee prescribed for the service of the notice referred to in sub-section (4). If any tenant fails to pay or to deposit the rent as aforesaid, the Rent Control Court or the appellate authority, as the case may be, shall, unless the tenant shows sufficient cause to the contrary, stop all further proceedings and make an order directing the tenant to put the landlord in possession of the building.

Landlord not to interfere with amenities enjoyed by the tenant. (1) No landlord shall, without just or sufficient cause, cut off or withhold or with hold any of the amenities enjoyed by the tenant. (2) A tenant in occupation of a building may, if the landlord has contravened the provisions of this section, make an application to the Rent Control Court complaining of such contravention. (3) If the tenant satisfies the Rent Control Court that the amenities were cut off or withheld with a view to compel him to vacate the building or to pay an enhanced rent, the Rent Control Court may pass an interim order, directing the landlord to restore the amenities immediately, pending the enquiry referred to in sub-section (4).

Every order made under section 11 or section 13 or section 19 and every order passed on appeal under section 18 or on revision under section 20, after the expiry of the time allowed therein be executed by the Munsiff or if there are more than one Munsiff, by the Principal Munsiff having original jurisdiction over the area in which the building is situated as if it were a decree passed by him.

main_sections.section_title: Decisions which have become final not to be re-opened
main_sections.description: The Rent Control Court shall summarily reject any application under sub-section (2), (3), (4), (5), (7) or (8) of section 11 which raises substantially the same issues as have been finally decided or as purport to have been finally decided or as purporting to have been finally decided in a former proceeding under this Act or under the corresponding provisions of any law in force prior to the commencement of this Act or the corresponding provisions of any law repealed or superseded by such law.

main_sections.section_title: Orders of Rent Control Court to be pronounced in open Court
main_sections.description: Every order passed by a Rent Control Court under this Act shall be pronounced in open Court on the day on which the case is finally heard, or on some future day of which due notice shall be given to the parties.

main_sections.section_title: Conversion of buildings and failure by landlord to make necessary repair
main_sections.description: (1) No residential building shall be converted into a non-residential building or vice versa and no such building shall be divided into separate portions for letting on rent or for other purposes except with the permission in writing of the Accommodation Controller. Provided that where such conversion involves structural alteration of the building, the consent of the landlord shall also be necessary. (2) Notwithstanding any law, custom, usage or contract to the contrary, the landlord shall be bound to attend to the periodical maintenance and necessary repairs of the building. If a landlord fails to attend to such maintenance or repairs to the building and amenities thereto within a reasonable time after notice is given by the tenant, it shall be competent for the Accommodation Controller to direct on application by the tenant that such maintenance and repairs may be attended to by the tenant and that the charges and cost thereof may be deducted with interest at 6% per annum from the rent which is payable by him.

(1) (a) The Government may, by general or special order notified in the Gazette, confer on such officers and authorities not below the rank of a Subordinate Judge the powers of appellate authority for the purposes of this Act in such areas or in such classes of cases as may be specified in the order. (b) Any person aggrieved by an order passed by the Rent Control Court may, within thirty days from the date of such order, prefer an appeal in writing to the appellate authority having jurisdiction. In computing to the thirty days aforesaid, the time taken to obtain a certified copy of the order appealed against shall be excluded. (2) On such appeal being preferred, the appellate authority may order of stay of further proceedings in the matter pending decision on the appeal. (3) The appellate authority shall send for the records of the case from the Rent Control Court and after giving the parties an opportunity of being heard and, if necessary, after making such further enquiry as it thinks fit either directly or through the Rent Control Court, shall decide the appeal. Explanation. The appellate authority may, while confirming the order of eviction passed by the Rent Control Court, grant an extension of time to the tenant for putting the landlord in possession of the building. (4) The appellate authority shall have all the powers of the Rent Control Court including the fixing of arrears of rent. (5) The decision of the appellate authority, and subject to such decision, an order of the Rent Control Court shall be final and shall not be liable to be called in question in any Court of law, except as provided in section 20.

Subject to such conditions and limitations, if any, as may be prescribed, the costs of and incident to all proceedings before the Rent Control Court or the appellate authority referred to in section 18 shall be in the discretion of the Rent Control Court or the appellate authority which shall have full power to determine by whom or what of what property and to what extent such costs are to be paid and to give all necessary directions for the purpose.

(1) In cases where the appellate authority empowered under section 18 is a Subordinate Judge, the District Court, and in other cases the High Court may, at any time, on the application of any aggrieved party, call for and examine the records relating to any order passed or proceedings taken under this Act by such authority for the purposes of satisfying itself as to the legality, regularity or propriety of such order or proceedings, and may pass such order in reference thereto as it thinks fit. (2) The costs of and incident to all proceedings before the High Court or District Court under sub-section (1) shall be in its discretion.

important_rules: Landlords cannot cut off or withhold amenities without just or sufficient cause.
Tenants can apply to the Rent Control Court if amenities are withheld with the intention to compel them to vacate or pay enhanced rent.
The landlord is bound to attend to periodical maintenance and necessary repairs of the building.
If a landlord fails to carry out maintenance or repairs within a reasonable time after notice, the tenant can get it done and deduct the cost from the rent.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Rent Control Court, Appellate Authority, Accommodation Controller
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Court orders, appeals, summary rejection of applications, deductions from rent.

rights: Tenant's right to amenities and maintenance.
Right to appeal against Rent Control Court orders.
Right to apply for revision of orders.
Tenant's right to challenge eviction if rent is paid/deposited.
duties: Tenant's duty to pay or deposit rent.
Landlord's duty to provide and maintain amenities.
Landlord's duty to carry out repairs.
obligations: Landlord's obligation to obtain permission for conversion of buildings.
Tenant's obligation to obtain permission for sub-letting or transferring rights.

key_procedures: Procedure for eviction and tenant's right to contest by paying/depositing rent.
Procedure for landlord's application for eviction.
Procedure for tenant's complaint regarding withheld amenities.
Procedure for appeals and revisions of orders.
important_notes: Explanation for computing the period of continuous occupation from 1st April 1940.
Explanation of interim orders passed by the Rent Control Court.
Explanation of the appellate authority's powers.

title: The Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1965
purpose: To provide, in the interests of the general public, for the control of the lease and rent of buildings in the State of Kerala and to prevent speculative and disruptive trading in the matter of such lease and rent, and to safeguard the interests of tenants.
scope: Applies to buildings, including residential buildings or parts of buildings, in the State of Kerala. Certain provisions may not apply to buildings owned by local authorities, government, or for specific educational institutions.  The Act applies to tenants receiving rent in respect of the landlord's property.

key_definitions.building: Includes a house, or part of a house, and, if it is part of a building, also includes the land or other premises appurtenant thereto and includes the furniture, if any, let along with such building.
key_definitions.landlord: A person who is entitled to receive rent in respect of any building or part of a building.
key_definitions.tenant: A person who is entitled to the benefits of this Act and includes any person who continues to remain in possession of the building after the expiry of the period of tenancy, whether before or after the commencement of this Act, but does not include a person against whom a decree or order for eviction has been made by a Court of Law.
key_definitions.Rent Control Court: Shall mean the Court of the Munsiff concerned.

main_sections.description: Details grounds on which a landlord can seek eviction of a tenant, including non-payment of rent, subletting without consent, damage to the building, nuisance, and requirement for landlord's own use or for an educational institution. It also outlines conditions for applying for eviction and procedures related to eviction orders.

Specifies the process for tenants to pay or deposit rent when the landlord refuses to accept it or when there are doubts about who is entitled to receive the rent. This includes depositing rent with the Rent Control Court.

main_sections.section_title: Landlord not to interfere with amenities enjoyed by the tenant
main_sections.description: Prohibits landlords from interfering with amenities provided to a tenant, and outlines the procedure for tenants to complain to the Rent Control Court if such interference occurs.
Deals with the execution of orders passed by the Rent Control Court or other authorities under the Act, including orders for eviction and restoration of amenities, and provides for appeals.

main_sections.section_title: Decisions which have become final not to be reopened
main_sections.description: Stipulates that decisions of the Rent Control Court and appellate authorities become final and cannot be reopened, subject to specific conditions regarding review of applications.

main_sections.section_title: Orders of Rent Control Court to be pronounced in open Court
main_sections.description: Mandates that orders of the Rent Control Court must be pronounced in an open Court.

main_sections.section_title: Conversion of buildings and failure to landlord to make necessary repairs
main_sections.description: Addresses conversion of residential buildings into non-residential ones and the landlord's responsibility for repairs. It also outlines the tenant's recourse if the landlord fails to undertake necessary maintenance.
Details the appellate authority for orders passed under the Act, the procedure for filing appeals, and the powers of the appellate authority.
Covers the provision for costs in proceedings before the Rent Control Court and the appellate authority.
Outlines how rent is determined, including the method for fixing fair rent in certain circumstances and how rent is to be paid or deposited.

main_sections.section_title: Order under the Act to be binding on sub-tenants
main_sections.description: States that orders for the eviction of a tenant passed under the Act are binding on sub-tenants.

main_sections.section_title: Proceedings by or against legal representative
main_sections.description: Refers to the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure for proceedings by or against legal representatives.
Confers powers upon the Accommodation Controller, Rent Control Court, and appellate authority regarding summoning witnesses, examining documents, and other procedural matters.

main_sections.section_title: Time within which proceedings have to be disposed of
main_sections.description: Specifies that the Rent Control Court shall, as far as practicable, pass final orders within four months from the date of appearance of the parties.
Allows the Government to exempt any building or class of buildings from the provisions of the Act by notification in the Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Executive authorities of local bodies to furnish certified extracts from property-tax or house-assessment books
main_sections.description: Requires executive authorities of local bodies to provide certified extracts from property-tax or house-assessment books upon application and payment of a fee.

main_sections.section_title: Landlord and tenant to furnish particulars
main_sections.description: Mandates that landlords and tenants furnish particulars to the Accommodation Controller or Rent Control Court as required.
Empowers the Government to appoint Inspectors to inspect buildings and assist the Rent Control Court.
Outlines penalties for contravening certain provisions of the Act, including fines and imprisonment.

main_sections.section_title: Fixation of fair rent suo motu by Court
main_sections.description: Allows the Rent Control Court to fix fair rent suo motu in certain circumstances.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including prescribing procedures, manner of serving orders, and applications.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

important_rules: A landlord cannot seek eviction solely for the purpose of re-letting the premises to a new tenant, unless there are specific grounds for eviction.
Tenants who continue to occupy a building after the expiry of their tenancy are still protected under certain conditions.
Rent paid or deposited by a tenant shall not be less than two weeks from the date on which it becomes due.
Any order passed by the Rent Control Court or appellate authority for eviction of a tenant shall be binding on sub-tenants, even if they were not parties to the original proceedings.

Sub-section (6) of Section 11 states that a landlord may apply for eviction if the building is required for his own use or for the use of any member of his family, and he is not occupying a building of his own in the locality.
If a tenant has contravened any of the provisions of this section, the landlord can make an application to the Rent Control Court complaining of such contravention.
If a landlord fails to undertake necessary maintenance or repairs to the building within a reasonable time after notice, the tenant can apply to the Accommodation Controller for the repairs.
Any order made under this Act and not previously published in the Gazette shall not be invalid merely on the ground of non-publication.
The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, exempt any building or class of buildings from all or any of the provisions of this Act.

Sub-section (1) of Section 29 states that if any person contravenes any of the provisions of sub-sections (1), (2), (4), (5), and (6) of section 11, clause (a) of sub-section (1) and clause (b) of sub-section (2) of section 12, sub-section (1) of section 13, sub-section (1) of section 14 and section 17, he shall be punishable with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees and in default of simple imprisonment which may extend to two weeks.

penalties: Contravention of provisions related to eviction (Sec. 11), payment/deposit of rent (Sec. 12), landlord's interference with amenities (Sec. 13), and repairs (Sec. 17): Fine up to two thousand rupees and/or simple imprisonment up to two weeks.
Landlord receiving unreasonable rent in respect of any building: Fine up to two thousand rupees or with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two months, or with both.
Contravention of provisions under Section 29: Fine up to two thousand rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Rent Control Court, Accommodation Controller, Appellate Authority, and Inspectors appointed by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through court proceedings, eviction orders, imposition of fines, imprisonment, and special orders related to rent fixation and repairs.

rights: Tenant's right to continue in possession under certain conditions, even after tenancy expiry.
Tenant's right to have amenities provided by the landlord.
Tenant's right to get repairs done if the landlord fails.
Landlord's right to seek eviction on specified grounds.
Right to appeal against orders of the Rent Control Court.
Right to receive fair rent as determined by the Act.
duties: Tenant's duty to pay rent on time.
Tenant's duty not to sublet without consent.
Tenant's duty not to damage the building.
Landlord's duty to provide and maintain amenities.
Landlord's duty to carry out necessary repairs.
Landlord's duty to provide particulars when required.
Tenant's duty to vacate the building when an eviction order is passed.
obligations: Obligation for landlords and tenants to furnish particulars when requested by the Accommodation Controller or Rent Control Court.
Obligation for parties to adhere to orders passed by the Rent Control Court and appellate authorities.

key_procedures: Eviction: Landlord files an application with the Rent Control Court on specified grounds. Tenant is given notice and an opportunity to be heard. Court passes an eviction order if grounds are met.
Rent Deposit: If a landlord refuses rent or there's doubt about entitlement, the tenant can deposit rent with the Rent Control Court. This deposit protects the tenant from eviction for non-payment.

Repair of Buildings: Tenant can notify the landlord about necessary repairs. If the landlord fails to act, the tenant can apply to the Accommodation Controller, who may authorize the tenant to carry out repairs and deduct costs from rent.
Appeals: Orders of the Rent Control Court can be appealed to the appellate authority within a specified period.
Fixation of Fair Rent: In certain cases, the Rent Control Court can fix the fair rent of a building.
administration: The Act is administered by the Rent Control Court, Accommodation Controller, and the appellate authority established under the Act. The Government also plays a role in making rules and providing exemptions.
important_notes: Sub-section (10) of Section 11 states that no order for eviction shall be passed if the landlord has already obtained an order for eviction in respect of the same building under sub-section (1) to (9).

Sub-section (12) of Section 11 clarifies that where a landlord has obtained possession of a building by obtaining an order under sub-section (3), he is not permitted to occupy it and vacate it without reasonable cause within one month of the date of obtaining possession.

Sub-section (14) of Section 11 states that a tenant shall not be entitled to apply for eviction if the building is in a friolous or vexatious situation, and the Rent Control Court may direct that compensation not exceeding fifty rupees be paid by such tenant to the landlord.
The Act aims to prevent speculative and disruptive trading in the lease and rent of buildings.
The provisions of Sections 146 and Order XXVII of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 shall apply to proceedings under this Act.

Sub-section (2) of Section 31 allows the Government to make rules without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing powers, and such rules may provide for all matters expressly required or allowed by the Act to be prescribed.

An Explanation under Section 13 states that an interim order may be passed by the Rent Control Court or the appellate authority by which the landlord is given temporary possession of the building, and such order can be modified or cancelled.

title: The Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Amendment Act, 1972
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1965.
scope: Applies to buildings in Kerala that are subject to the Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1965.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Amendment Act, 1972.

Inserts a new provision into section 11 of the principal Act regarding applications under this clause. It states that an application under this clause shall not be made for the first time in respect of one and the same tenancy unless the landlord has sent a registered notice to the tenant intimating the contravention of the said condition of the lease and the tenant has failed to terminate the transfer or the sub-lease, as the case may be, within thirty days of the receipt of the notice or the refusal thereof.

Inserts a new sub-section (6) after sub-section (5) of section 13. This sub-section deals with appeals against orders passed by the Accommodation Controller. It specifies that a tenant or landlord aggrieved by an order may prefer an appeal to the District Collector within thirty days from the date of receipt of the order. The District Collector can then pass such orders on appeal as they deem fit. It also clarifies that the District Collector shall have the powers vested in a Civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, when trying a suit in respect of matters specified in clauses (a) to (k) of sub-section (1) of section 23 for the purpose of disposing of an appeal.

important_rules: An application under section 11, clause (i) of the principal Act cannot be made for the first time for the same tenancy unless a registered notice is sent to the tenant about the contravention and they fail to rectify it within 30 days.
Appeals against orders of the Accommodation Controller must be filed with the District Collector within thirty days of receiving the order.
The District Collector has the powers of a Civil Court when hearing appeals under this section.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Accommodation Controller, District Collector
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through orders issued by the Accommodation Controller and appeals heard by the District Collector.

rights: Right to appeal against an order passed by the Accommodation Controller.
The District Collector has the power to dispose of appeals.
duties: Landlord's duty to send a registered notice to the tenant regarding contravention of lease conditions before making a first-time application under section 11.
Tenant's duty to rectify lease contraventions within 30 days of receiving notice.

key_procedures: Procedure for applying to amend section 11 of the principal Act concerning tenancy conditions.
Procedure for filing an appeal to the District Collector against an order by the Accommodation Controller, including the timeframe and the powers of the District Collector.
important_notes: This Act is an amendment to the Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1965.
The Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 161, dated 27th February, 1973.

title: The Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Amendment Act, 1973
purpose: To further amend The Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1965, for the purpose hereinafter appearing. This amendment also inserts a new section 11A regarding special provisions for members of the Armed Forces.
scope: The Act applies to buildings and tenancies within Kerala, with specific provisions relating to members of the Armed Forces and their families. It covers suits, applications, appeals, and proceedings related to leases and rent control.

key_definitions.family: For the purpose of section 11A, 'family' shall mean such relations of the landlord as ordinarily live with him and are depended on him.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Amendment Act, 1973.

Introduces a new section 11A into the principal Act. This section provides special provisions for members of the Armed Forces, allowing them certain exemptions and procedures for recovery of possession of a residential building occupied by them or their families.

main_sections.section_title: Stay of suits, applications, etc., for arrears of Jhennikaram
main_sections.description: Stipulates that notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in the Kanan Tenancy Act, 1955 (XXIV of 1955) or any other law, no suit, application, decree, or order, or any proceeding, for the recovery of arrears of Jhennikaram shall lie or have effect if it was pending before the commencement of this Act.

Specifies that in computing the period of limitation for suits, applications, appeals, or revisions concerning the institution or making of applications or the filing of appeals and revisions prohibited under this Act, the time during which such suits or other proceedings or applications or appeals or revisions were prohibited under this Act shall be excluded.

important_rules: No suit or application or other proceeding for the recovery of arrears of Jhennikaram accrued due before the commencement of this Act shall be instituted.
No application, or proceedings in execution of a decree or order for the recovery of such arrears of Jhennikaram or other application or proceedings incidental thereto shall stand stayed.

All appeals against decrees or orders relating to arrears of Jhennikaram accrued due before the commencement of this Act and all revisions relating to such arrears shall stand stayed, and no court or other authority or officer shall proceed with any such appeal or revision filed after such commencement.
Special provisions apply for members of the Armed Forces regarding the recovery of possession of a residential building.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts, Rent Control Court, and prescribed authority
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through suits, applications, decrees, orders, appeals, and revisions, with specific stay provisions and limitations on their effectiveness.

rights: Right to seek recovery of possession of a residential building by members of the Armed Forces under specific conditions.
Right to apply for eviction of a tenant by members of the Armed Forces.
obligations: Landlords serving under special conditions are required to provide service to their families.
Landlords cannot recover possession of a building from a tenant except under specific circumstances as outlined in section 11A.

key_procedures: Procedure for seeking recovery of possession by members of the Armed Forces: An application must be made to the Rent Control Court. The Court may direct the landlord or member of his family to put the landlord in possession. Such possession shall not be later than fifteen days from the date of the order.

Procedure for recovery of possession where landlord is serving under special conditions: Application under this section shall not be entertained by the Rent Control Court unless the same is accompanied by a certificate of the prescribed authority.
administration: Likely administered by the Government of Kerala, specifically departments dealing with housing, revenue, and law. The Rent Control Court and prescribed authorities are the enforcing bodies at the ground level.
important_notes: The provisions related to the stay of suits and proceedings for arrears of Jhennikaram are critical.
Section 11A provides a specific carve-out for members of the Armed Forces.
The definition of 'family' in relation to landlords is clarified for the purpose of section 11A.
The Act specifies that certain recovery actions are not to be entertained by the Rent Control Court unless specific documents are provided.

title: THE KERALA BUILDINGS (LEASE AND RENT CONTROL) AMENDMENT ACT, 1961
purpose: To amend the Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1959, for the purposes herein-after appearing.
scope: Applies to buildings (residential and non-residential) in Kerala. The Act governs lease and rent control of these buildings.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Amendment Act, 1961. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 3rd day of April, 1959.
Amends section 2 of the principal Act by substituting words and phrases related to 'any furniture affixed' and 'any fittings affixed'.

Substitutes the proviso to sub-section (2) of section 5 of the principal Act with a new proviso that includes conditions for increased rent in certain cases, specifically regarding residential or non-residential buildings where fittings have been affixed and excluded from valuation for the purpose of fixing property tax or house tax.

Amends section 8 of the principal Act by relettering existing clauses and substituting words to reflect amendments related to rent payable for buildings in case of a falling under clause (ii) of the proviso to sub-section (2) of section 5.

Amends section 11 of the principal Act by substituting words in the first proviso to sub-section (3) and adding a new proviso concerning the landlord's right to recover possession and provisions for tenant's livelihood, trade or business.

Amends section 12 of the principal Act. Substitutes sub-section (1) and specifies that the deposit made shall be made within such time as the Court may fix and in such manner as may be prescribed, and shall be accompanied by a fee prescribed for the service of notice referred to in sub-section (4). Also provides for time fixed by the Court for the deposit of arrears of rent not to be less than four weeks from the date of the order, and the time fixed for the deposit of rent which subsequently accrues due shall not be less than two weeks from the date on which the rent becomes due.
Amends section 29 of the principal Act by substituting words, figures, letter and words in sub-section (1) and sub-section (2) of section 8.
Amends section 36 of the principal Act. The following shall be added namely: 'unless and until they are superseded by appointment or constitution, as the case may be, under this Act.'

Amends the Schedule to the principal Act by substituting items for items 60, 62, 63 and 64. Mentions 'Kuthuparamba Panchayat including Pattiam and Mananderi', 'Kasargod Panchayat', 'Kanhangad Panchayat', 'Paiyannur Panchayat'.

title: The Kerala Buildings Tax Act, 1961
purpose: An Act to provide for the levy of a tax on buildings.
scope: Extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. It came into force with effect on and from the 2nd day of March, 1961.

key_definitions.appellate authority: The appellate authority means the appellate authority appointed by the Government.
key_definitions.assessee: Assessee means a person by whom buildings tax or any other sum of money is payable under this Act, and includes every person in respect of whom any proceeding under this Act has been taken for the assessment of buildings tax payable by him.
key_definitions.assessing authority: Assessing authority means the assessing authority appointed by the Government.
key_definitions.building: Building means a house, out-house, garage, or any other structure, or part thereof, whether of masonry, bricks, wood, metal, or other material, but does not include any portable shelter or any shed constructed principally of mud, bamboo, leaves, grass or thatch or a latrine which is not attached to the main structure.
key_definitions.floorage: Floorage means the area included in the floor of a building, and where a building has more than one floor, the aggregate area included in the floors thereof.
key_definitions.owner: Owner includes a person who for the time being is receiving or is entitled to receive, the rent of any building whether on his own account or on account of himself or others or has agent, trustee, guardian or receiver for any other person who should so receive the rent or be entitled to receive it if the building or part thereof were let to a tenant.

Obligation to provide information to the assessing authority.

title: THE KERALA CASHEW FACTORIES (ACQUISITION) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2009
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Cashew Factories (Acquisition) Act, 1974, for the purposes hereinafter appearing. Specifically, to amend provisions related to the acquisition of cashew factories, especially those in possession of the Kerala State Cashew Development Corporation, and to address unemployment issues in the cashew sector.
scope: Applies to cashew factories in Kerala, with specific reference to those in the possession of the Kerala State Cashew Development Corporation (KSDC).

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Cashew Factories (Acquisition) Amendment Act, 2009. It came into force on the 1st day of August, 2009.

Amends Section 2 of the principal Act (Kerala Cashew Factories (Acquisition) Act, 1974) by adding new clauses. These clauses address the acquisition of cashew factories in possession of KSDC, regardless of the nature of their tenure (lease, requisition, etc.) and the government's opinion on the necessity of such acquisition to prevent lay off or retrenchment of workers.

Amends Section 3 of the principal Act. It inserts new clauses (c) and (d) to the proviso of sub-section (1) of section 3. These new clauses clarify that acquisition can occur if there has been large-scale unemployment or if cashew factories possessed by KSDC, under lease or requisition, are not being utilized to prevent unemployment.

Inserts a new Section 3B after Section 3A of the principal Act. This new section deals with the acquisition of cashew factories in the possession of KSDC, irrespective of lease status, and empowers the government to acquire them if it is of the opinion that it is necessary to prevent unemployment. It also states that such factories shall be transferred to and vest in the Government.

Amends Section 5 of the principal Act by inserting a new sub-section (4). This new sub-section deals with the inventory of cashew factories originally leased or requisitioned and now under the possession of KSDC. The inventory prepared originally shall be the inventory for all purposes.

Amends the Schedule of the principal Act. The existing Schedule shall be numbered as 'Schedule I' and after it, a new 'Schedule II' shall be added, detailing specific cashew factories with their registration numbers, description, and owner's name and address.

important_rules: Cashew factories in the possession of the Kerala State Cashew Development Corporation (KSDC) can be acquired by the Government.
Acquisition is permissible if there has been large-scale unemployment or if KSDC-possessed factories are not utilized to prevent employee/worker retrenchment.
The inventory prepared for factories originally leased or requisitioned by KSDC shall serve as the official inventory.
The Act specifies the details of cashew factories to be included in Schedule II, including their registration, description, and owner information.

penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through provisions of the principal Act and this amendment act, including powers of acquisition and vesting of factories in the Government.

rights: Right of the Government to acquire cashew factories under specified conditions.
Right of the Government to declare acquired factories as vested in itself.
duties: Duty to ensure employment for workers in cashew factories.
Duty to manage acquired cashew factories for public interest.
obligations: Obligation to prevent lay off or retrenchment of workers in the cashew sector.
Obligation to transfer acquired cashew factories to the Government.

key_procedures: Amendment of existing sections of the Principal Act (Kerala Cashew Factories (Acquisition) Act, 1974).
Insertion of new sections (e.g., Section 3B) and sub-sections.
Addition of a new Schedule (Schedule II) to the Principal Act, detailing specific cashew factories.
administration: Kerala Government
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the President on 17th August, 2010.
It was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No 2026 dated 3rd September, 2010.
The Amendment Act of 2009 came into force on 1st August 2009.

title: THE KERALA CASHEW FACTORIES (ACQUISITION) ACT, 1974
purpose: An Act to provide for the acquisition, in the public interest, of certain cashew factories.
scope: The Act applies to cashew factories in Kerala. It aims to prevent large-scale unemployment among workers in the cashew industry and to provide employment to workers who have been rendered unemployed.

key_definitions.appointed day: the date of publication of the declaration under sub-section (1) of section 3 or under sub-section (2) of section 4.
key_definitions.Cashew factory: means a factory, wherein processing of cashewnuts is being carried on and includes the factory building, the site thereof, and the buildings and lands appurtenant thereto used or necessary for, or in connection with, the working of the factory.
key_definitions.Corporation: means the Kerala State Cashew Development Corporation Limited, incorporated under the Companies Act, 1956 (Central Act 1 of 1956).
key_definitions.Factories Act: means the Factories Act, 1948 (Central Act 63 of 1948).
key_definitions.Federation: means the Kerala State Co-operative Marketing Federation.
key_definitions.processing: with reference to cashewnuts, includes extraction of cashewnut oil and roasting, shelling, peeling, grading and treating of cashewnuts, add cloves.

key_definitions.prescribed: means prescribed by rules made under this Act.

title: The Kerala Cashew Factories (Acquisition) Amendment Act, 1985
purpose: To amend The Kerala Cashew Factories (Acquisition) Act, 1974.
scope: Applies to the amendment of The Kerala Cashew Factories Acquisition Act, 1974.

key_definitions.Federation: Means the Kerala State Co-operative Marketing Federation.
key_definitions.workers' co-operative society or society: Means a co-operative society registered under the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969 (21 of 1969) and formed with the object of managing a cashew factory which has been closed down or vested under the Act in the Government and of which at least ninety per cent of the members are workmen within the meaning of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (Central Act 14 of 1947), who have been immediately before the appointed day, in the employment of the cashew factory.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Cashew Factories (Acquisition) Amendment Act, 1985. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 28th day of February, 1984.
Amends section 2 of the principal Act by inserting a definition for 'Federation' and a definition for 'workers' co-operative society or society'.

Substitutes sub-section (1) of section 8 of the principal Act. It provides for entrusting a cashew factory to the Government, the Federation or a workers' co-operative society, and for management thereof. It also clarifies that notwithstanding anything contained in section 3, the Government may, by order, entrust a cashew factory vested in them to the Federation or a workers' co-operative society or to any other institution approved by the Government for such period and on such terms and conditions as may be specified.

Inserts a new section 10A concerning the continuance of employees of cashew factories vested in the Government or entrusted to the Federation or to a workers' co-operative society or to any other institution approved by the Government. It also addresses the continuity of service and employment of workmen and clarifies their rights and conditions of employment.

Amends section 11 of the principal Act to substitute the words 'the Government or the Corporation' with 'the Government or the Corporation or the Federation or a workers' co-operative society or an institution'.
Amends section 12 of the principal Act by inserting 'or the Corporation or the Federation or a workers' co-operative society or an institution' after 'the Corporation'.

Amends section 15 of the principal Act by substituting in sub-section (1) and sub-section (2) the words 'the Government or the Corporation' with 'the Government or the Corporation or the Federation or a workers' co-operative society or an institution'.

Repeals The Kerala Cashew Factories (Acquisition) Ordinance, 1985 (69 of 1985). Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: The Act is deemed to have come into force on February 28, 1984.
Cashew factories vested in the Government can be entrusted to the Federation or a workers' co-operative society or any other approved institution for management.

Employees of vested cashew factories are to continue in employment with the same terms and conditions, and are entitled to pension, gratuity, and other benefits as if they had continued in the employment of the cashew factory.
The continuity of service and employment of workmen shall not be interrupted.
The provisions of section 10 of the principal Act shall apply to any person employed in a cashew factory entrusted to the Federation or a workers' co-operative society or any other institution.

rights: Workers employed in cashew factories vested in the Government or entrusted to the Federation or a workers' co-operative society are entitled to continue in employment.
Workers are entitled to the same terms and conditions of service, including pension, gratuity, and other retirement benefits, as if they had continued in the employment of the cashew factory.
Employees shall not be entitled to any payment by way of gratuity or retirement benefits for any leave not availed of, or for any other benefits, prior to the appointed day.

No claim for compensation shall be maintainable against the Government or the Federation or the society or the institution for any loss or damage suffered by the occupant of the cashew factory immediately before the appointed day.
duties: The Government may entrust a cashew factory vested in them to the Federation or a workers' co-operative society or any other institution approved by the Government for management.
obligations: The Federation or a workers' co-operative society or any institution to which a cashew factory is entrusted shall, for management, become and from the date on which the cashew factory is so entrusted, be an employee of the Federation or the society or the institution.

key_procedures: Entrustment of a cashew factory vested in the Government to the Federation or a workers' co-operative society or any other approved institution by Government order.
Continuance of employment for workmen of such cashew factories under the new management with existing terms and conditions.
Application of Section 10 of the principal Act to persons employed in cashew factories entrusted to the Federation or a workers' co-operative society or institution.
administration: The Kerala State Government (implied through the Act's context and amendment)
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Kerala Cashew Factories (Acquisition) Act, 1974.
The amendments are retrospective, deemed to have come into force on February 28, 1984.

title: The Kerala Cashew Factories (Acquisition) Amendment Act, 1995
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Cashew Factories (Acquisition) Act, 1974.
scope: The Act applies to the acquisition of cashew factories in Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Cashew Factories (Acquisition) Amendment Act, 1995, and it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of May, 1984.
Amends section 2 of the Kerala Cashew Factories (Acquisition) Act, 1974, by inserting words, figures, and brackets or under sub-section (1) as shall be added at the end.

Inserts a new section 3A into the principal Act concerning the power to acquire cashew factories in public interest. It specifies conditions for acquisition, including the satisfaction of the Government, closure of factories, and re-starting necessity. It also states that no order under this sub-section shall be published unless approved by a resolution of the Legislative Assembly. Furthermore, it clarifies that provisions of section 3 and section 4 may apply to a declaration made under sub-section (1) as they apply to a declaration made under sub-section (1) of section 3.

Amends section 5 of the principal Act. It states that words, figures, and brackets in section 5 or the publication of notice under sub-section (1) of section 5, or after a resolution passed by the Legislative Assembly under sub-section (1) of section 5, shall be substituted.

Amends section 6 of the principal Act. Similar to section 4, it addresses the substitution of words, figures, and brackets in section 6 or the publication of notice under sub-section (1) of section 6, or after a resolution passed by the Legislative Assembly under sub-section (1) of section 6.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration as to acquisition of certain cashew factories
main_sections.description: This section states that it is expedient in the public interest that the cashew factories specified in the Schedule to this Act shall, notwithstanding anything contained in any judgment, decree or order of any court, tribunal or other authority, or notwithstanding anything contained in any other law, agreement or other instrument for the time being in force, stand transferred to, and vest in, the Government with effect from the date noted against each. It also clarifies that provisions of section 4, sections 7 to 16 (both inclusive) of the principal Act shall, as far as may be, apply to, or in relation to, the cashew factories in respect of which a declaration has been made under sub-section (1) of section 3A. It further declares that for removal of doubt, the dates mentioned in the Schedule against each factory shall be the 'appointed day' in respect of that factory for the purposes of the principal Act. Finally, it states that all acts, proceedings or things done or taken by the Government or any officer or authority in respect of cashew factories mentioned in the Schedule, including all orders issued under sub-section (1) of section 6 during the period commencing on or from the dates noted against each and ending with the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette, shall, for all purposes, be, and shall be deemed always to have been, valid and effective as if the amendments made to the principal Act by this Act had been in force at all material times.

important_rules: Rule 1: If the Government is satisfied that a cashew factory is closed and re-starting it is necessary in the public interest, it can acquire the factory.
Rule 2: No order for acquisition of a cashew factory can be published unless it is supported by a resolution of the Legislative Assembly.
Rule 3: The provisions of section 3 and section 4 of the principal Act apply to a declaration made under sub-section (1) of section 3 of this Act.
Rule 4: The Act and its amendments are deemed to have come into force from May 1, 1984.
Rule 5: For the factories listed in the Schedule, they stand transferred to and vest in the Government from the date specified against each, irrespective of any court orders or other laws.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through acquisition of factories and vesting of management with the Government.

rights: Right of the Government to acquire cashew factories in public interest.
Right of the Government to take over management of acquired cashew factories.
