obligations: Obligation of the Government to seek Legislative Assembly resolution for acquisition orders.
Obligation to follow the procedures laid out in the Act for acquisition.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Declaration of expediency to acquire a cashew factory in public interest by the Government.
Procedure 2: Obtaining a resolution from the Legislative Assembly to publish the acquisition order.
Procedure 3: Transfer of ownership and vesting of the factory with the Government on the specified date.
Procedure 4: Application of relevant sections of the principal Act for acquisition and post-acquisition matters.
administration: Department of Industries and Commerce, Government of Kerala (inferred).
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 16th day of August 1995 and published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 828 dated 16th August 1995.
The Act has retrospective effect from May 1, 1984.
All past actions and proceedings related to the acquisition of cashew factories, prior to the commencement of this Act, are deemed valid and effective.

title: THE KERALA CASHEW FACTORIES (REQUISITIONING) AMENDMENT ACT, 1985
purpose: To amend the Kerala Cashew Factories (Requisitioning) Act, 1979, for purposes appearing in the Preamble.
scope: Applies to cashew factories within Kerala. The amendments relate to the requisitioning of cashew factories.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Cashew Factories (Requisitioning) Amendment Act, 1985. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 26th day of February, 1982.

Amends section 3 of the Kerala Cashew Factories (Requisitioning) Act, 1979 (6 of 1979). In sub-section (1), for the words "by order published in the Gazette, requisition that cashew factory for such period not exceeding five years as may be specified in the order and may make such further orders as appear to them to be necessary or expedient in connection with the requisition,", the following shall be substituted: "by order published in the Gazette—(a) requisition that cashew factory for such period not exceeding five years as may be specified in the order; (b) extend the period of requisition by five years at a time; (c) make such further orders as appear to them to be necessary or expedient in connection with the requisition;".

Notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force, or in any judgment, decree or order of any court, or in any contract, agreement or other arrangement, where any cashew factory had been requisitioned under sub-section (1) of section 3 of the principal Act and vested in the Kerala State Cashew Development Corporation Limited under sub-section (3) of that section, before the commencement of this Act and the period of such requisition and vesting had expired before the date of publication of the Kerala Cashew Factories (Requisitioning) Amendment Ordinance, 1984 (40 of 1984), in the Gazette, but such cashew factory continued in the possession of the said Corporation until that date, such requisitioning and vesting shall be deemed to have been continued by orders under sub-section (1) and sub-section (3) of section 3 of the principal Act as amended by this Act, and accordingly any action taken by the Government or the said Corporation in respect of such cashew factory shall be, and shall be deemed always to have been valid and in accordance with law.

(1) The Kerala Cashew Factories (Requisitioning) Amendment Ordinance, 1985 (70 of 1985), is hereby repealed. (2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

key_procedures: Amendment of Section 3: The process involves substituting specific wording within sub-section (1) of section 3 of the principal Act to allow for requisitioning of cashew factories for periods not exceeding five years, with options to extend by five years at a time, and to make further necessary orders related to the requisition.

Validation of actions: Actions taken under the principal Act, particularly regarding requisitioning and vesting of cashew factories, are validated even if the requisition period expired before the amendment, provided the factory remained in possession of the Corporation. Such actions are deemed valid under the amended Act.

Repeal and Saving: The Kerala Cashew Factories (Requisitioning) Amendment Ordinance, 1985, is repealed. Actions taken under this Ordinance are saved and deemed to have been taken under the amended Act.
important_notes: The commencement date of the Act is retrospectively fixed to February 26, 1982.
The amendments are intended to validate past actions and streamline the process of requisitioning cashew factories.
Received the assent of the President on the 14th day of October, 1985 and published in the Kerala Gazette, Extraordinary No. 829 dated the 15th October, 1985.

title: The Kerala Cashew Workers' Relief and Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2003
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Cashew Workers' Relief and Welfare Fund Act, 1979, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to Kerala and concerns the Kerala Cashew Workers' Relief and Welfare Fund.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Cashew Workers' Relief and Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2003, and shall come into force at once.
Amends section 5 of the Kerala Cashew Workers' Relief and Welfare Fund Act, 1979 (19 of 1979) by substituting words and inserting a new sub-section (3A).

important_rules: Substitution of words in sub-section (2) of section 5 of the principal Act: 'fifty paise' shall be substituted by 'one rupee'.

Insertion of a new sub-section (3A) in section 5 of the principal Act: 'The Government shall contribute to the Fund every year by way of grant an amount equal to the amount of contribution paid by employees under sub-section (2)'.'

obligations: The Government has an obligation to contribute to the Fund annually an amount equal to the employee contributions.

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act: The Act comes into force immediately upon its enactment.
Amendment process: Specific sections of the principal Act are amended by substitution and insertion of new provisions.
administration: The Government of Kerala (as indicated by the reference to Kerala Gazette).
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on 9th August, 2003.
Published in Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No 1509 dated 12th August, 2003.

title: THE KERALA CASHEW WORKERS RELIEF AND WELFARE FUND (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1987
purpose: An Act to amend the Kerala Cashew Workers Relief and Welfare Fund Act, 1979.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Cashew Workers Relief and Welfare Fund Act, 1979.

key_definitions.employee: Refers to 'employer or employee' as defined in the principal Act, with 'or the Government' inserted.
key_definitions.family: For the purpose of clause (aaa) of sub-section (4) of section 4, means wife in case of male employee; husband in case of female employee; minor sons; minor daughters; father and mother who are solely dependent upon the employee.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Cashew Workers Relief and Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 1987, and shall come into force at once.
Amends section 2 of the Kerala Cashew Workers Relief and Welfare Fund Act, 1979, by inserting the words "or the Government" after 'employer or employee'.
Amends section 3 of the principal Act, in clause (a) of sub-section (2), by substituting the words "employers and employees" with "employer and employees".

Inserts new clauses after clause (a) of sub-section (4) of section 4 of the principal Act. These include provisions for payment of pension, family pension, financial assistance to employees suffering from permanent disablement or temporary disablement, and loans or grants for marriage of children, expenses in connection with death of dependent, or expenses for construction or maintenance of house. It also introduces provisions for maternity benefits, medical facilities, and educational facilities for employees and their families.

Inserts a new sub-section (3A) in section 5 of the principal Act, stating that the Government shall contribute to the fund every year by way of grant on a matching basis an amount equal to the contribution paid by employees under sub-section (2).
Omits sub-section (6) and the words "the Vice-Chairman" in sub-section (7) of section 7 of the principal Act.

Inserts new items 5A and 5B in the schedule to the principal Act. Item 5A deals with the amount and conditions for payment of pension, family pension, grant, and advances from the fund. Item 5B specifies the purposes for which the fund may be utilized for the welfare of employees or their dependents.

important_rules: The Act shall come into force at once (Section 1).
The Government shall contribute to the fund annually on a matching basis to the employees' contribution (Section 5).
Specific provisions for payment of pension, family pension, financial assistance, and loans/grants for various purposes are detailed (Section 4).

rights: Right to receive pension and family pension.
Right to receive financial assistance for permanent disablement or temporary disablement.
Right to receive loans or grants for marriage of children, expenses related to death of a dependent, or for house construction/maintenance.
Right to maternity benefits, medical facilities, and educational facilities for employees and their families.

key_procedures: Amendment of various sections of the principal Act, 1979.
Insertion of new clauses and sub-sections to define benefits, contributions, and purposes of the fund.
Procedures for the payment of pension, family pension, grants, and advances from the fund are to be defined in the schedule (Section 7).
administration: Law (Legislation-C) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The principal Act being amended is The Kerala Cashew Workers Relief and Welfare Fund Act, 1979.
The amendment was passed by the Legislative Assembly and received the assent of the Governor on the 22nd day of January, 1988.

title: THE KERALA CASHEW WORKERS RELIEF AND WELFARE FUND ACT, 1979
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a fund to grant relief to, and promote the welfare of, employees in cashew factories in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to all cashew factories registered and licensed in the State of Kerala under the Factories Act, 1948 (Central Act 63 of 1948) and to employees in such factories.

key_definitions.Board: Kerala Cashew Workers Relief and Welfare Fund Board constituted under section 7.
key_definitions.contribution: The contribution payable by an employer or employee under the scheme.
key_definitions.cashew factory: A factory wherein processing of cashewnuts is being carried on and which is registered and licensed under the Factories Act, 1948 (Central Act 63 of 1948).
key_definitions.employer: Any person who employs, whether directly or through another person or whether on behalf of himself or any other person, one or more employee or employees and includes any person who has a licence for the construction of extension of a cashew factory under the Factories Act, 1948 (Central Act 63 of 1948).
key_definitions.employee: Any person who is employed in any cashew factory for wages for processing cashewnuts and who gets his wages directly or indirectly from the employer and includes (i) any person employed by or through a contractor or through an agent or in connection with the processing of cashewnuts; and (ii) clerical and other staff employed in connection with the processing of cashewnuts.
key_definitions.Fund: Kerala Cashew Workers Relief and Welfare Fund established under the scheme.
key_definitions.member: Any employee who contributes to the Fund.
key_definitions.processing: With reference to cashewnuts, means loading, unloading, transporting, stacking, unstucking, soaking, roasting, shelling, frying, peeling, grading, filling, packing or otherwise treating or adapting cashewnuts with a view to their use, delivery, sale or other disposal, and includes work connected with the maintenance of processed cashewnuts.
key_definitions.scheme: The scheme framed under this Act.
key_definitions.wages: All remuneration received or payable to an employee for work done or services rendered by him and includes leave and holiday wages paid or payable to him under any law or agreement for the time being in force, but does not include overtime allowance, bonus and commission.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, commencement and application.
main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Kerala Cashew Workers Relief and Welfare Fund Act, 1979. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint. It applies to all cashew factories registered and licensed in the State of Kerala under the Factories Act, 1948.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'contribution', 'cashew factory', 'employer', 'employee', 'Fund', 'member', 'processing', 'scheme', 'State', and 'wages'.

main_sections.section_title: Kerala Cashew Workers Relief and Welfare Fund.
main_sections.description: States that the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, frame a scheme for the establishment of a Fund under this Act. The Fund shall be constituted as soon as may be after the framing of the scheme and shall be credited to the Kerala Cashew Workers Relief and Welfare Fund and, in accordance with the provisions of this Act and the scheme. Contributions shall be paid by employers and employees, by any voluntary donations, and by grants or advances made by the Central Government or the Government of Kerala or any local authority, and any other amount which, under the provisions of the scheme, shall be credited to the Fund. The Fund shall vest in and be administered by the Board.

main_sections.section_title: Purposes for which Fund may be expended.
main_sections.description: Specifies that the Fund shall be expended for the following purposes: (a) payment of relief wages to employees in cashew factories when there is no work in those factories, and (b) payment of such other amount as may be specified in the scheme.

main_sections.section_title: Contribution and matters which may be provided for in the scheme.
main_sections.description: Details the contribution to the Fund: (1) The contribution which shall be paid by an employer to the Fund shall be at the rate of twenty rupees for every twenty-five kilograms of cashewnut kernels processed within the State. (2) The contribution which shall be paid by an employee shall be at the rate of one rupee for every day of work done by him in the cashew factory. (3) The employees' contribution shall be deducted by the employer from the wages payable and remitted to the Fund along with the employer's share before the date specified in section 9. (4) Where the amount of contribution payable under this Act involves a fraction of a rupee, the scheme may provide for rounding off to the nearest rupee, half-a-rupee or quarter of a rupee.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, add to, amend or vary the scheme either prospectively or retrospectively. Every notification under sub-section (1) shall be laid, as soon as may be, after it is issued, before the Legislative Assembly while it is in session for a total period of fourteen days which may be comprised in one session or in two successive sessions and if before the expiry of the session in which it is so laid or the session immediately following, the Legislative Assembly makes any modification in the scheme or decides that the notification should not be issued, the notification shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form, or be of no effect, as the case may be, so however that any such modification or annulment shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that notification.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, constitute, with effect from such date as may be specified therein, a Board to be called the Kerala Cashew Workers Relief and Welfare Fund Board for the administration of the Fund and to supervise or carry out the activities financed from the Fund. The Board shall be a body corporate by the name aforesaid having perpetual succession and a common seal and shall by the said name sue and be sued. The Board shall consist of such number of Directors as may be appointed by the Government and they shall be chosen in such manner as may be provided for in the scheme. Provided that the Board shall include an equal number of Directors representing the Government, the employers and the employees. One of the Directors of the Board shall be appointed by the Government as its Chairman. The Board shall elect from among its members a Vice-Chairman who shall exercise such powers and perform such functions of the Chairman as may be specified in the scheme. The Government shall publish in the Gazette the names of the Chairman, the Vice-Chairman and the other Directors of the Board. The Board shall administer the Fund vested in it in such manner as may be specified in the scheme.

The Government may appoint a Chief Executive Officer and such Inspectors as they consider necessary to assist the Chief Executive Officer in the exercise of his powers and the discharge of his duties. The Board may, with the previous approval of the Government, appoint such officers and other employees as it may consider necessary for assisting it in the administration of the Fund. The method of recruitment, salary and allowances, discipline and other conditions of service of the Chief Executive Officer and the Inspectors shall be such as may be specified by the Government, and the method of recruitment, salary and allowances, discipline and other conditions of service of the officers and other employees appointed by the Board shall be such as may be specified by the Board with the previous approval of the Government. In making appointments to the posts of officers and other employees to be appointed by the Board, the provisions of clauses (a), (b) and (c) of rule 14 and the provisions of rules 15, 16 and 17 of the Kerala State and Subordinate Services Rules, 1958, as amended from time to time, shall, mutatis mutandis, be observed.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of employer to file return.
main_sections.description: Every employer shall, before the 10th of every month, file a return showing the details of contributions paid into the Fund, in such manner as may be specified in the scheme.

main_sections.section_title: Determination of amounts due from employers.
main_sections.description: The Chief Executive Officer or any Inspector authorised by him in this behalf may, by order, determine the amounts due from any employer under the provisions of this Act or of the scheme and for this purpose may conduct such enquiry as he may deem necessary. The officer conducting the enquiry under sub-section (1) shall, for the purposes of such enquiry, have the same powers as are vested in a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Central Act 5 of 1908), when trying a suit, in respect of the following matters, namely: (a) enforcing the attendance of any person and examining him on oath; (b) requiring the discovery and production of documents; (c) receiving evidence on affidavit. Any enquiry under this section shall be deemed to be a judicial proceeding within the meaning of sections 193 and 228, and for the purposes of section 196, of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (Central Act 45 of 1860). No order determining the amount due from any employer shall be made under sub-section (1) unless the employer has been given a reasonable opportunity of being heard. Any person aggrieved by an order under sub-section (1) may prefer an appeal to the Government or such other authority as may be specified by the Government in this behalf, within sixty days from the date of the receipt of the order and the decision of the Government or such other authority on such appeal shall be final.

main_sections.section_title: Provisional assessment where return is not filed.
main_sections.description: If any employer fails to submit the return as required by section 9, the Chief Executive Officer or the Inspector authorised by him in this behalf may provisionally determine the amount due from that employer to the Fund. Provided that no provisional assessment shall be made final till the party is given an opportunity of being heard.

main_sections.section_title: Mode of recovery of money due from employers.
main_sections.description: Any amount due from an employer in pursuance of the provisions of this Act or the scheme, if any amount is in arrears, shall be recovered in the same manner as an arrear of land revenue.

(1) Whoever, for the purpose of avoiding any payment to be made by himself under this Act or under the scheme or of enabling any other person to avoid such payment, knowingly makes or causes to be made any false statement or false representation, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both. (2) Whoever contravenes or makes default in complying with any of the provisions of this Act or of the scheme shall, if no other penalty is elsewhere provided by or under this Act for such contravention or non-compliance, be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

main_sections.section_title: Enhanced punishment for default in payment of employees' contributions already deducted.
main_sections.description: (1) Whoever makes default in the payment of the contribution to the Fund after having deducted it from the wages of the employees in accordance with the provisions of this Act or the scheme, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, but which shall not be less than three months, and with fine which may extend to four thousand rupees. (2) Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Central Act 2 of 1974), an offence under sub-section (1) shall be cognizable.

main_sections.section_title: Enhanced punishment for second or subsequent offence.
main_sections.description: Whoever, having been convicted by a court of an offence punishable under this Act, commits the same offence again, shall be punishable for every such subsequent offence with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, but which shall not be less than three months, and with fine which may extend to four thousand rupees.

Where an offence under this Act has been committed by a company, every person who, at the time the offence was committed, was in charge of, and was responsible to the company for the conduct of the business of the company, as well as the company, shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly: Provided that nothing contained in this sub-section shall render any such person liable to any punishment if he proves that the offence was committed without his knowledge or that he exercised all due diligence to prevent the commission of such offence. (2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), where an offence under this Act has been committed by a company, and it can be proved that the offence has been committed with the consent or connivance of, or is attributable to any neglect on the part of, any Director, Manager, Secretary or other officer of the company, such Director, Manager, Secretary or other officer shall also be deemed to be guilty of that offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly.

No court shall take cognizance of an offence punishable under this Act or any scheme framed thereunder, except on a complaint in writing made by the Board or by an officer authorised in this behalf by the Board or by the Government.
The Government or the Board may, by order, direct an inquiry to be made into the affairs of the Fund or the scheme or into the conduct of the members of the Board or any employee of the Fund.

If the Board makes default in the performance of any duty imposed on it by or under this Act or the scheme, or does anything which is likely to be prejudicial to the interests of the employees, the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, supersede the Board for such period as may be specified in the notification.
The Government or the Board may, by order, recover from any person who has been found to be responsible for any loss or damage caused to the Fund or the scheme, the amount of such loss or damage.

main_sections.section_title: Bar of benefits under Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.
main_sections.description: Notwithstanding anything contained in the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, no employee shall be entitled to any benefit under this Act or the scheme if he is already in receipt of any similar benefit under any other law or agreement.

main_sections.section_title: Bar of jurisdiction of civil courts.
main_sections.description: Save as expressly provided in this Act, no civil court shall have jurisdiction to entertain any suit or proceeding in respect of any matter which the Government or the Board or any officer or other person is empowered by this Act to dispose of or decide.

main_sections.section_title: Directors of the Board etc., to be public servants.
main_sections.description: The Chairman and other Directors of the Board and the officers and employees of the Board shall be deemed to be public servants within the meaning of section 21 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (45 of 1860).

main_sections.section_title: Protection of actions taken in good faith.
main_sections.description: No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against the Government or the Board or any officer or other employee of the Government or the Board for anything which is in good faith done or intended to be done in pursuance of this Act or the scheme.

If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act or the scheme, the Government may, by order published in the Gazette, make such provisions as appear to them to be necessary or expedient for removing the difficulty.

important_rules: Employers must deduct employees' contributions and remit them to the Fund along with their own share before the date specified in section 9.
The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, add to, amend or vary the scheme either prospectively or retrospectively.
The Board shall be administered in such manner as may be specified in the scheme.
Any amount due from an employer if in arrears, shall be recovered in the same manner as an arrear of land revenue.
Offences under the Act can be cognizable.
The Chairman and other Directors of the Board and the officers and employees of the Board shall be deemed to be public servants.
No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against the Government or the Board or any officer or other employee for anything done in good faith in pursuance of this Act or the scheme.

penalties: Avoidance of payment: Imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both.
Contravention or default: Imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both.
Default in payment of deducted contributions: Imprisonment up to one year (minimum three months), and fine up to four thousand rupees.
Second or subsequent offence: Imprisonment up to one year (minimum three months), and fine up to four thousand rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government, the Board, and officers authorized by them.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings, recovery of arrears as land revenue, and imposition of penalties as defined in the Act. Cognizance of offences can be taken by courts upon complaint by the Board or authorized officers.

rights: Employees are entitled to relief wages when there is no work in cashew factories, as specified in the scheme.
Employees are entitled to other benefits as may be specified in the scheme.
Any person aggrieved by an order under section 10 (determination of amounts due) may prefer an appeal to the Government or other specified authority.
No provisional assessment shall be made final without giving the party an opportunity of being heard.
duties: Employers have a duty to pay contributions to the Fund.
Employers have a duty to deduct employees' contributions from wages and remit them to the Fund.
Employers have a duty to file a monthly return showing contribution details.
The Board has a duty to administer the Fund and supervise activities financed by it.
Officers conducting inquiries have powers vested in civil courts for summoning witnesses and examining documents.
obligations: Employers must comply with the provisions of the Act and the scheme.
Employees must contribute to the Fund as per the scheme.

key_procedures: Establishment of the Fund and Scheme: The Government frames a scheme for the Fund, which is then constituted.
Contribution Payment: Employers deduct employee contributions and pay their own contributions to the Fund.
Return Filing: Employers file monthly returns detailing contributions.
Determination of Amounts Due: Chief Executive Officer or Inspector can determine amounts due from employers after inquiry.
Appeals: Aggrieved parties can appeal against determination orders.
Recovery of Arrears: Amounts due from employers are recovered as land revenue arrears.
Offence Cognizance: Courts take cognizance of offences based on complaints by the Board or authorized officers.
Scheme Modification: Government can modify the scheme through notification.
Board Supersession: Government can supersede the Board in case of default or prejudicial actions.
administration: The Kerala Cashew Workers Relief and Welfare Fund Board administers the Fund, overseen by the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act was enacted in 1979 but its Act number is 19 of 1984, suggesting a delay in its official promulgation or amendment.
Received the assent of the President on the 30th day of July, 1984 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 742 dated the 22nd August, 1984.
The definition of 'processing' is quite extensive, covering various stages of cashew handling.
Offences under the Act can be cognizable.
The jurisdiction of civil courts is barred except as expressly provided in the Act.
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected from legal proceedings.

title: THE KERALA CASUAL, TEMPORARY AND BADLI WORKERS (WAGES) ACT, 1989
purpose: To provide for the fixation of wages payable to casual, temporary and badli workers in certain establishments and employments and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to every factory, plantation and motor transport undertaking; every establishment to which any of the provisions of the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1960 applies, and which is specified by the Government by notification in the Gazette and which is situate in such area or areas as may be specified in the notification; and such other establishment or undertaking as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, specify.

key_definitions.badli worker: A worker who is appointed in the place of a permanent worker who is temporarily absent.
key_definitions.casual worker: A worker whose employment is of a casual nature.
key_definitions.employer: Means, in relation to any establishment, factory, plantation, motor transport undertaking or other undertaking, the person who, or the authority which, has the ultimate control over the affairs of the establishment, factory, plantation, motor transport undertaking or other undertaking, and where the said affairs are entrusted to a managing agent, director or by any other name, such person, the managing director or by any other name, such person.
key_definitions.factory: Has the meaning assigned to it in clause (m) of section 2 of the Factories Act, 1948 (Central Act 63 of 1948).
key_definitions.permanent worker: Means a worker who is employed on a permanent basis.
key_definitions.plantation: Has the meaning assigned to it in clause (f) of section 2 of the Plantations Labour Act, 1951 (Central Act 69 of 1951).
key_definitions.temporary worker: Means a worker who has been engaged for work which is of an essentially temporary nature likely to be finished within a limited period.
key_definitions.wages: Has the meaning assigned to it in clause (vi) of section 2 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 (Central Act 4 of 1936).
key_definitions.worker: Means any person who is employed for hire or reward to do any work, skilled or unskilled, manual or clerical, in any establishment or employment to which this Act applies and includes an out worker to whom any articles or materials are given out by another person to be made up, cleaned, washed, altered, ornamented, furnished, prepared, adopted or otherwise processed.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, commencement and application
main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Kerala Casual, Temporary and Badli Workers (Wages) Act, 1989. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala, comes into force on such date as the Government may appoint, and applies to specific categories of establishments and undertakings as outlined in the scope.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'badli worker', 'casual worker', 'employer', 'factory', 'permanent worker', 'plantation', 'state', 'temporary worker', 'wages', and 'worker'.

main_sections.section_title: Wages payable to casual, temporary or badli workers.
main_sections.description: States that nothing contained in any law or for the time being in force, or in any judgment, decree or order of any court or other authority, or in any contract or other agreement, shall employer shall pay to any casual, temporary or badli worker employed by him in an establishment, factory, plantation, motor transport undertaking or other undertaking, rates less than the minimum wages payable in cash or in kind to a permanent worker for performing the same work or work of a similar nature.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to appoint authorities for hearing and deciding claims and complaints.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to appoint such officers, not below the rank of a District Labour Officer, as authorities for hearing and deciding claims arising out of non-payment of wages and complaints regarding contravention of section 3. It also outlines the procedure for making claims and complaints, including the powers of the appointed authorities.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of employers to maintain registers.
main_sections.description: Mandates employers to maintain such registers and other documents in relation to casual, temporary and badli workers as may be prescribed.

Provides for the appointment of Inspectors by the Government to inspect establishments and check compliance with the Act. It also defines an Inspector as a public servant and outlines their powers, including entering and inspecting premises, examining witnesses, and taking extracts from registers and other documents.

Specifies penalties for contravening the provisions of the Act, including penalties for employers who contravene section 3, obstruct an Inspector, or refuse to provide information. Penalties also apply to companies where an offence is committed.

Deals with offences committed by companies, stating that when an offence under the Act has been committed by a company, the company and every person in charge of and responsible to the company for the conduct of its business, as well as the company itself, shall be deemed guilty of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly. It also defines 'company' and 'director' for the purposes of this section.

Stipulates that no court inferior to that of a Judicial Magistrate of the first class shall try any offence punishable under this Act. It also specifies that no court shall take cognizance of an offence punishable under this Act except upon a complaint made with the sanction of the Government or an officer authorised by them.

States that notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force, in any proceeding under this Act, the burden of proving that a work performed by a casual, temporary or badli worker is not the same work or work of a similar nature as that performed by a permanent worker shall be on the employer.

Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act. These rules may prescribe the manner in which claims referred to in section 4 shall be made, registers and other documents which an employer is required to maintain, and any other matter which is required to be, or may be, prescribed. It also outlines the procedure for laying rules before the Legislative Assembly.

important_rules: Employers must pay casual, temporary, or badli workers wages not less than the minimum wages paid to permanent workers for similar work.
Employers must maintain registers and documents related to casual, temporary, and badli workers.
Rules made under the Act must be laid before the Legislative Assembly and are subject to modification by the Assembly.

penalties: Contravention of section 3: fine up to five thousand rupees.
Refusal or obstruction to an Inspector: fine up to two thousand rupees.
Employer contravening provisions: fine up to five thousand rupees.
Refusal or wilful neglect to afford an Inspector reasonable facilities for making an inspection: fine up to two thousand rupees.
Employer refusing to give evidence or produce documents to an Inspector: fine up to one thousand rupees.
Person making default in complying with provisions of any rule or order: fine up to five thousand rupees.
Offences by Companies: Guilty of the offence and liable to be proceeded against and punished.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government, Inspectors appointed by the Government, and authorities appointed by the Government for hearing and deciding claims and complaints.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections by appointed Inspectors, hearing and deciding of claims and complaints by appointed authorities, and prosecution for offences by courts.

rights: Right to receive wages not less than the minimum wages paid to permanent workers for similar work.
Right to have claims and complaints regarding wages heard and decided by appointed authorities.
Right to have offences tried by a Judicial Magistrate of the first class.
Right to natural justice in inquiries and proceedings.
duties: Duty of employers to pay minimum wages to casual, temporary, and badli workers.
Duty of employers to maintain registers and documents.
Duty of employers to cooperate with Inspectors and provide necessary facilities and information.
Duty of every person to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder.
obligations: Employers have an obligation to ensure that casual, temporary, and badli workers receive fair wages.
Companies have an obligation to ensure their directors and officers comply with the Act.

key_procedures: Claim or Complaint Procedure: An aggrieved worker can file a claim or complaint with an authority appointed by the Government. The authority will hear the case and make an order. Appeals against these orders can be made to higher authorities.
Inspection Procedure: Inspectors can enter any establishment, inspect premises, examine registers and other documents, and question persons to ensure compliance with the Act.
Rule Making Procedure: The Government makes rules, which are then laid before the Legislative Assembly for potential modification.
administration: The Government of Kerala (presumably through its Labour Department)
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the President on the 14th day of January, 1990, and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 57 dated the 22nd January, 1990.
The burden of proof that the work performed by a casual, temporary or badli worker is not the same work or work of a similar nature as that performed by a permanent worker shall be on the employer.
Rules made under the Act can be modified by the Legislative Assembly and will only have effect after being laid before the Assembly.

title: The Kerala Cattle Trespass (Amendment) Act, 1975
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Cattle Trespass Act, 1961.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala. Concerns cattle trespass.

key_definitions.aerodromes: For the purposes of section 11A, 'aerodrome' shall have the same meaning assigned to it under the Aircraft Act, 1934 (Central Act 22 of 1934).

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Cattle Trespass (Amendment) Act, 1975. It shall come into force at once.

Amends section 11 of the Kerala Cattle Trespass Act, 1961. In sub-section (1), for the last sentence, the following is substituted: 'Different scales may be prescribed for different local areas or for different localities within the same local area and for different kinds of cattle'.
Inserts a new section 11A after section 11 of the principal Act. This section deals with special provisions for cattle straying in aerodromes.

important_rules: Cattle straying in aerodromes are habitually allowed to trespass and cause nuisance. This will be dealt with by notification in the Gazette.
For every head of cattle of any kind found in an aerodrome, it may be seized and impounded.
The amount of fine shall not exceed four times the fine prescribed under sub-section (1) of section 11.

penalties: Fine not exceeding four times the fine prescribed under sub-section (1) of section 11 for cattle found in aerodromes.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Director (implied, for notification and seizure)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Seizure and impounding of cattle found in aerodromes after notification in the Gazette.

rights: Right to prescribe different scales of fines for different local areas or localities and for different kinds of cattle.
duties: Duty to issue notification in the Gazette regarding cattle straying in aerodromes.

key_procedures: For cattle straying in aerodromes: Notification in the Gazette by the Director regarding the allowance of trespass and nuisance. Seizure and impounding of cattle. Levying of fine not exceeding four times the prescribed fine under section 11(1).
administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but likely related to the Department responsible for Animal Husbandry or Revenue.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 1st day of June 1975 and published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 278, dated 3rd June 1975.

title: THE KERALA CATTLE TRESPASS ACT, 1961 (Act 26 of 1961)
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to trespass by cattle on lands and causing damage to crops and other produce therein, in the State of Kerala.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. It applies to cattle trespassing on land or crops or public roads, canals and embankments, and causing damage. The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, exclude any area from the operation of this Act.

key_definitions.cattle: Means cows, oxen and bulls and includes elephants, camels, buffaloes, horses, mares, paddings, ponies, colts, fillies, mules, asses, pigs, rams, ewes, sheep, lambs, goats, kids and fowls and such other kinds of animals as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, specify.
key_definitions.director: Means the Director of Local Bodies appointed by the Government.
key_definitions.local_authority: Means any Municipal Corporation, Municipal Council or Panchayat, or, in area where there is no Municipal Corporation, Municipal Council or Panchayat, such authority as the Government may appoint in this behalf.

main_sections.description: States the title of the Act as 'The Kerala Cattle Trespass Act, 1961', its extent to the whole of Kerala, and its commencement.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'cattle', 'Director', and 'local authority'.
Authorizes the establishment of pounds for impounding cattle and specifies that the area for which a pound is established shall be determined by the Director.

main_sections.section_title: Control of pounds and rates of charge for feeding impounded cattle
main_sections.description: States that pounds are under the control of the local authority, which fixes rates for feeding and watering impounded cattle. These rates shall be exhibited conspicuously.
Requires every pound to be in charge of a pound-keeper appointed by the local authority. Pound-keepers are deemed public servants and their appointment may be suspended or removed by the authority.

main_sections.section_title: To keep registers and furnish returns
main_sections.description: Pound-keepers must keep registers and furnish returns.
Details the information pound-keepers must record when registering cattle seizures, including descriptions of the cattle and the owner's residence.

main_sections.section_title: To take charge of and feed cattle
main_sections.description: Pound-keepers are responsible for taking charge of and feeding impounded cattle.

main_sections.section_title: Cattle damaging land may be seized and police to aid such seizures
main_sections.description: Empowers the cultivator, occupier, or owner of land, or police officers, to seize cattle that damage land, crops, or public roads, canals, and embankments. Police are required to assist in such seizures.

main_sections.section_title: Cattle damaging public roads, canals and embankments
main_sections.description: Specifies that police officers employed by local authorities can seize cattle damaging public roads, canals, and embankments.
Specifies fines for impounded cattle, which vary based on the area and type of cattle. Fines can be doubled in certain circumstances and are credited to the local authority.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure when owner claims the cattle and pays fines and charges
main_sections.description: Outlines the process for owners claiming impounded cattle, requiring payment of fines and charges. If cattle are not claimed within seven days, they can be sold.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure if cattle be not claimed within a week
main_sections.description: If cattle are not claimed within seven days of notice, they can be sold by public auction.

main_sections.section_title: Delivery to owner disputing legality of seizure, but making deposit
main_sections.description: Allows for the delivery of cattle to an owner disputing the seizure, provided they pay the fines and expenses.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure when owner refuses or omits to pay the fines and expenses
main_sections.description: Details the process if the owner refuses or omits to pay fines and expenses, leading to the sale of the cattle and disposal of proceeds.

main_sections.section_title: Disposal of fines, expenses and surplus proceeds of sale
main_sections.description: Specifies how fines, expenses, and surplus proceeds from the sale of cattle are to be disposed of.

main_sections.section_title: Application of fines and unclaimed proceeds of sale
main_sections.description: States that fines and unclaimed proceeds from sales are credited to the fund of the local authority.

main_sections.section_title: Officers and pound-keepers not to purchase cattle at sales under this Act
main_sections.description: Prohibits officers and pound-keepers from purchasing cattle at sales conducted under the Act.
Allows any person whose cattle have been seized or detained under the Act to make a complaint to the District Magistrate.
Details the procedure for the Magistrate to examine complaints regarding illegal seizure or detention of cattle.

main_sections.section_title: Compensation for illegal seizure or detention of cattle
main_sections.description: Provides for compensation to the complainant if the seizure or detention is judged illegal.
Specifies how compensation awarded under Section 21 is to be recovered, similar to the recovery of fines under the Code of Criminal Procedure.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for forcibly opposing the seizure of cattle or rescuing the same
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for forcibly opposing the seizure of cattle or rescuing them.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for damage caused to land or crops or public road by cattle
main_sections.description: Defines penalties for damage caused by cattle to land, crops, or public roads, including fines and imprisonment.

main_sections.section_title: Recovery of penalty for mischief committed by causing cattle trespass
main_sections.description: Deals with the recovery of penalties for mischief caused by cattle trespass, including the recovery of the value of damage and expenses.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of police to investigate offences under section 24
main_sections.description: Grants police officers the power to investigate offences under Section 24.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty on pound-keeper failing to perform duties
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for pound-keepers who fail to perform their duties related to impounded cattle.

main_sections.section_title: Application of fines recovered under sections 24, 25 and 27
main_sections.description: Explains how fines recovered under specific sections are to be applied.

main_sections.section_title: Saving of right to sue for compensation
main_sections.description: Preserves the right of individuals to sue for compensation in cases not covered by the Act.
Allows for set-off in certain compensation claims.
Empowers the Government to delegate its powers under the Act.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Repeals previous laws and provides for savings.

important_rules: Cattle damaging land, crops, or public roads, canals, and embankments may be seized.
Police officers have powers to seize cattle causing damage to public roads, canals, and embankments.
Pound-keepers must maintain registers of seized cattle and furnish returns.
Fines collected under the Act are credited to the local authority.
Officers and pound-keepers are prohibited from purchasing cattle at sales conducted under this Act.
Cattle not claimed within seven days from the date of notice can be sold by public auction.

penalties: Penalty for forcibly opposing seizure or rescuing cattle: Imprisonment not exceeding six months or fine not exceeding five hundred rupees, or both.

Penalty for damage caused to land or crops or public road by cattle: Fine not exceeding twenty-five rupees, and for a second or subsequent offence, not exceeding two hundred and fifty rupees or imprisonment for a term not exceeding three months, or both.
Penalty for mischief by causing cattle trespass: Fines and expenses recovered from the sale of cattle.
Penalty on pound-keeper failing to perform duties: Imprisonment not exceeding six months or fine not exceeding five hundred rupees, or both.
Compensation for illegal seizure or detention: Amount to be determined by the Magistrate, not exceeding one hundred rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Police officers, cultivators, occupiers of land, pound-keepers, and the District Magistrate.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Seizure of cattle, imposition of fines, imprisonment, and recovery of compensation through judicial processes.

rights: Right of cultivators, occupiers, or owners of land to seize cattle damaging their property.
Right of police to seize cattle causing damage to public roads, canals, and embankments.
Right of owners to claim impounded cattle upon payment of fines and charges.
Right to sue for compensation for illegal seizure or detention.
duties: Duty of pound-keepers to maintain registers, keep records, and take charge of impounded cattle.
Duty of pound-keepers to feed and water impounded cattle.
Duty of police to aid in the seizure of cattle damaging public property.
Duty of owners to pay fines and charges for impounded cattle.
Duty of the Government to notify the commencement of the Act and any exclusions of areas.
obligations: Obligation to prevent cattle from trespassing and causing damage.
Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act regarding seizure, impounding, and sale of cattle.

key_procedures: Seizure of cattle: When cattle cause damage to land, crops, or public property, they can be seized by concerned individuals or police.
Impounding of cattle: Seized cattle are to be taken to a pound for detention.
Claiming and release of cattle: Owners can claim impounded cattle by paying fines and charges. If not claimed within a specified period, they are sold.
Sale of cattle: Unclaimed cattle or cattle for which fines are not paid are sold by public auction.
Complaint to Magistrate: Persons aggrieved by illegal seizure or detention can file a complaint with the District Magistrate.
administration: The Government of Kerala, through the Director of Local Bodies and local authorities.
important_notes: The Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 15th July 1961.
The Government has the power to exclude any area from the operation of the Act.
Fines recovered under Sections 24, 25, and 27 are to be used for specific purposes related to the Act.
The Act consolidates and amends existing laws on cattle trespass.
The Director of Local Bodies plays a significant role in determining pound areas and other administrative aspects.

title: The Kerala Ceiling on Government Guarantees Act, 2003
purpose: To provide for the ceiling on Government guarantees and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and its Government.

key_definitions.guarantee: Means any promise, undertaking or assurance made by the Government to pay to a third party any sum of money, or to fulfil any obligation of a third party, in the event of the default of such third party in the payment of such money or in the fulfilment of such obligation.
key_definitions.financial institution: Means a bank, insurance company, co-operative society, statutory corporation or any other institution notified by the Government in this behalf.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and its commencement date.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as Government, guarantee, financial institution, etc.
Specifies the maximum limit or ceiling on the total amount of guarantees that the Government can issue.
Outlines the powers vested in the Government regarding the issuance and management of guarantees.
Grants the Government the power to demand information from any person or institution regarding guarantees.
Empowers the Government to frame rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of any previous enactment on the subject and savings provisions.

important_rules: The total amount of guarantees issued by the Government shall not exceed the ceiling specified.
Guarantees shall be issued only for specific purposes and in accordance with prescribed procedures.
The Government shall periodically review the outstanding guarantees and their impact.

penalties: Penalty for contravention of the Act or rules may include fines or other penalties as prescribed.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala and such authorities as may be authorized by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through imposition of penalties, recovery of dues, and other legal measures as provided in the Act and rules.

rights: Right of the Government to issue guarantees within the prescribed ceiling.
Right of the Government to call for information and take necessary action to safeguard its interests.
duties: Duty of the Government to ensure that guarantees are issued prudently and within the specified limits.
Duty of beneficiaries of guarantees to comply with the terms and conditions.
Duty of the Government to publish relevant information regarding guarantees.
obligations: Obligation of the Government to meet its guarantee commitments in case of default by the principal debtor.

key_procedures: Procedure for application and approval of Government guarantees.
Procedure for monitoring and reviewing existing guarantees.
Procedure for enforcement of guarantees in case of default.
administration: The Finance Department or any other department/agency designated by the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act aims to prevent excessive financial commitment by the Government through guarantees.
The ceiling on guarantees can be revised by the Government through notification.
Specific exclusions or conditions might apply to certain types of guarantees as detailed in the Act or rules.

title: THE KERALA CEILING ON GOVERNMENT GUARANTEES ACT, 2003
purpose: An Act to provide for ceiling on Government guarantees and other matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. It is expedient to provide for ceiling on Government guarantees issued on behalf of the Government departments, public sector undertakings, local authorities, statutory boards, corporations and co-operative institutions and for promoting fiscal discipline of the State.
scope: The Act applies to Government departments, public sector undertakings, local authorities, statutory boards, corporations and co-operative institutions of the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Government guarantee: includes the guarantee given by the State Government on behalf of the Government departments, public sector undertakings, local authorities, statutory boards, corporations and co-operative institutions
key_definitions.prescribed: means prescribed by rules made under the Act

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Ceiling on Government Guarantees Act, 2002. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
The total outstanding Government guarantees as on the first day of April of any year shall not exceed rupees fourteen thousand crores.
Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, no Government guarantee shall be given in respect of a loan of any private individual, Institution or Company.

The Government shall charge a minimum of 0.75 per cent per annum as guarantee commission, which shall not be waived under any circumstances. Depending on the default risk of any project, the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, specify commission at an enhanced rate. The guarantee given shall not be extended on the expiry of the guarantee period unless the borrower had paid in full the guarantee commission due to the government.

The Government shall, by notification in the Gazette, constitute a fund called the Guarantee Redemption Fund. The Guarantee commission charged under section 5 shall form the corpus of the Guarantee Redemption Fund and it shall be remitted in the Public Accounts of the State. The administration of Guarantee Redemption Fund shall be in such manner as may be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to make rules
main_sections.description: The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make rules for the purpose of carrying into effect the provisions of this Act. Every rule made under this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before the Legislative Assembly while it is in session for a total period of fourteen days, which may be comprised in one session or in two successive sessions, and, if, before the expiry of the session in which it is so laid or the session immediately following, the Legislative Assembly makes any modification in the rule, or decides that the rule should not be made, the rule shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect, as the case may be, so, however, that any such modification or annulment shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that rule.

important_rules: Government guarantees shall not exceed a total outstanding amount of rupees fourteen thousand crores as on the first day of April of any year.
No Government guarantee shall be given for loans of private individuals, institutions, or companies.
A minimum of 0.75% per annum as guarantee commission shall be charged on all guarantees, which cannot be waived.
The Government may specify an enhanced guarantee commission rate based on the default risk of a project.
Guarantees cannot be extended beyond their expiry period if the full guarantee commission due has not been paid by the borrower.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through rules made under the Act and by ensuring compliance with the provisions related to guarantee limits and commission charges.

duties: The Government has a duty to not exceed the ceiling on Government guarantees.
The Government has a duty to charge guarantee commission and maintain a Guarantee Redemption Fund.
obligations: Borrowers have an obligation to pay the full guarantee commission due to the government.

key_procedures: The Government, by notification in the Gazette, may specify an enhanced guarantee commission at an enhanced rate, depending on the default risk of any project.
The Government shall constitute a Guarantee Redemption Fund by notification in the Gazette.
Rules made under the Act shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly for approval or modification.
administration: The Government of Kerala, and its departments responsible for finance and guarantees. The Guarantee Redemption Fund is administered as prescribed by the Government.
important_notes: The preamble mentions the year 2002 for the Act title, but the document and filename refer to 2003. This seems to be a discrepancy.
The Act is enacted in the Fifty-fourth Year of the Republic of India.
The rules made under this Act are subject to modification or annulment by the Legislative Assembly.

title: THE KERALA CEILING ON GOVERNMENT GUARANTEES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2015
purpose: To amend the Kerala Ceiling on Government Guarantees Act, 2003.
scope: This act applies to the State of Kerala and deals with government guarantees.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Ceiling on Government Guarantees (Amendment) Act, 2015, and that it shall come into force at once.

This section amends Section 3 of the Kerala Ceiling on Government Guarantees Act, 2003. It substitutes the words 'fourteen thousand crores' with 'twenty one thousand crores' in relation to the ceiling on government guarantees.

important_rules: The ceiling on government guarantees, as previously set at fourteen thousand crores, is now increased to twenty one thousand crores.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The enforcement authority is not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but it would typically be the relevant government departments in Kerala responsible for financial matters and guarantees.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The act is enforced through legislative amendment, changing the financial limits for government guarantees.

obligations: The government of Kerala is obligated to adhere to the revised ceiling on government guarantees.

administration: The Law (Legislation-A) Department of the Government of Kerala is involved in the notification and publication of this Act.
important_notes: The amendment is effective immediately upon its enactment.
The increase in the ceiling signifies a change in the financial limits within which the Kerala government can provide guarantees.

title: The Kerala Children Act 1972
purpose: The purpose of this act is to provide for the care, protection, and rehabilitation of children in need, and to deal with offenses committed by and against children. It aims to establish a framework for the administration of juvenile justice in Kerala.
scope: The Act applies to all children within the State of Kerala. It covers various aspects of a child's life, including their involvement in legal proceedings, protection from exploitation, and provision of care and rehabilitation services.

key_definitions.child: A person who has not completed the age of eighteen years.
key_definitions.competent authority: The authority designated by the Government to exercise powers and discharge duties conferred by this Act.
key_definitions.juvenile: A child who has committed an offense.
key_definitions.neglected child: A child who is found begging, destitute, or living in circumstances of moral danger, or whose parents are unable to provide for their care and protection.

main_sections.section_title: Proceeding under Chapter VIII of the Criminal Procedure Code not competent against child.—Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (Central Act 5 of 1898), no proceeding shall be instituted and no order shall be passed against a child under Chapter VIII of the said Code
main_sections.description: Prohibits proceedings against a child under Chapter VIII of the Criminal Procedure Code, 1898, and bars the institution of such proceedings or passing of orders against a child under that chapter.

main_sections.section_title: No joint trial of child and person not a child— (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in section 239 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (Central Act 5 of 1898) or any other law for the time being in force, no child shall be charged with or tried for any offence together with a person who is not a child.
main_sections.description: Prohibits the joint trial of a child with a person who is not a child, even if they are accused of the same offense. If a child is accused of an offense, and the child would not be considered an adult under sub-section (1), the court shall direct separate trials.

main_sections.section_title: Power of police officers to administer warning.—Any police officer not below the rank of a Sub Inspector, if he is of opinion that any offence reported or suspected to have been committed by a child is not of a serious nature or that it is not a repetition of a previous offence already committed by the child, may, notwithstanding anything contained in any other provision of this Act or in any other law for the time being in force and subject to such restrictions and limitations as may be prescribed, let such child off after administering suitable warning to such child
main_sections.description: Empowers police officers, not below the rank of Sub Inspector, to administer a warning to a child if an offense is not serious or a repetition of a previous one. Such children may be let off with a warning, subject to prescribed restrictions and limitations.

main_sections.section_title: Removal of disqualification attaching to conviction.—Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law, a child who has committed an offence and has been dealt with under the provisions of this Act shall not suffer disqualification, if any, attaching to a conviction of an offence under such law.
main_sections.description: States that a child dealt with under this Act for an offense shall not suffer any disqualification that might normally attach to a conviction under other laws.

main_sections.section_title: Special provision in respect of pending cases.—Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, all proceedings in respect of a child pending in any court in any area on the date on which this Act comes into force in that area, shall be continued in that court as if this Act had not been passed and if the court finds that the child has committed an offence, it shall record such finding and instead of passing any sentence in respect of the child, forward the child to the competent authority which shall pass orders in respect of that child in accordance with the provisions of this Act as if it had been satisfied on inquiry under this Act that the child has committed the offence
main_sections.description: Provides special provisions for cases pending before the Act comes into force. Proceedings will continue under the old law, but if a child is found guilty, they will be forwarded to the competent authority for orders under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Sittings etc, of children's courts.—(1) A children's court shall hold its sittings at such place, on such day and in such manner, as may be prescribed.
main_sections.description: Specifies that children's courts will hold their sittings at prescribed places, on prescribed days, and in the prescribed manner.

main_sections.section_title: Persons who may be present before competent authority.—(1) Save as provided in this Act, no person shall be present at any sitting of a competent authority, except—
main_sections.description: Details who is permitted to be present at a sitting of a competent authority, excluding the officer of the competent authority and other specified individuals like parents, guardians, or legal practitioners.

main_sections.section_title: Attendance of parent or guardian of child.—Any competent authority before which a child is brought under any of the provisions of this Act may, whenever it so thinks fit, require any parent or guardian having the actual charge of, or control over, the child to be present at any proceeding in respect of the child
main_sections.description: Grants the competent authority the power to require the presence of a child's parent or guardian at any proceeding concerning the child.

main_sections.section_title: Dispensing with attendance of child.—If, at any stage during the course of an inquiry, a competent authority is satisfied that the attendance of the child is not essential for the purpose of the inquiry, the competent authority may dispense with his attendance and proceed with the inquiry in the absence of the child
main_sections.description: Allows a competent authority to dispense with a child's attendance during an inquiry if it is deemed not essential for the purpose of the inquiry.

main_sections.section_title: Committal to approved place of child suffering from dangerous disease and its future disposal.—(1) When a child who has been brought before a competent authority under this Act is found to be suffering from a disease requiring prolonged medical treatment or physical or mental complaint that will respond to treatment, the competent authority may send the child to any place recognised to be an approved place in accordance with the rules made under this Act for such period as it may think necessary for the required treatment
main_sections.description: Enables the competent authority to send a child suffering from a disease or mental complaint requiring prolonged treatment to an approved place for a necessary period.

main_sections.section_title: Presumption and determination of age.—(1) Where it appears to a competent authority that a person brought before it under any of the provisions of this Act (otherwise than for the purpose of giving evidence) is a child, the competent authority shall make due inquiry as to the age of that person and for that purpose shall take such evidence as may be necessary and shall record a finding whether the person is a child or not, stating his age as nearly as may be
main_sections.description: Requires a competent authority to inquire into the age of a person brought before it if there is doubt, and to record a finding on their age. No order of a competent authority shall be deemed invalid merely by any subsequent proof that the person in respect of whom the order was made was not a child.

main_sections.section_title: Circumstances to be taken into consideration in making orders under the Act.—In making any order in respect of a child, under this Act, a competent authority shall take into consideration the following circumstances, namely—
main_sections.description: Lists circumstances to be considered by a competent authority when making orders regarding a child, including the child's age, circumstances, reports, religious persuasion, and opinions of the competent authority.

main_sections.section_title: Sending a child outside jurisdiction.—In the case of a neglected or delinquent child whose ordinary place of residence lies outside the jurisdiction of the competent authority before which he is brought, the competent authority may, if satisfied after due inquiry that it is expedient so to do, send the child back to a relative or other person who is fit and willing to receive him at his ordinary place of residence and exercise care and control over him, notwithstanding that such place of residence is outside the jurisdiction of the competent authority, and the competent authority exercising jurisdiction over the place to which the child is sent shall in respect of any matter arising subsequently have the same powers in relation to the child as if the original order had been passed by itself
main_sections.description: Allows a competent authority to send a neglected or delinquent child back to their place of residence outside its jurisdiction if a suitable relative or person is willing to receive and care for them. The competent authority in the destination jurisdiction will then have similar powers.

main_sections.section_title: Reports to be treated as confidential.—The report of the probation officer or any circumstance considered by the competent authority under section 33 shall be treated as confidential
main_sections.description: Mandates that reports from probation officers and circumstances considered by the competent authority under section 33 must be treated as confidential.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of publication of names, etc, of children involved in any proceeding under the Act.—(1) No report in any newspaper, magazine or news sheet of any inquiry regard- ing a child under this Act shall disclose the name, address or school or any other particulars calculated to lead to the identification of the child, nor shall any picture of such child be published
main_sections.description: Prohibits the publication of names, addresses, schools, or any other identifying particulars of children involved in proceedings under this Act in newspapers or other media. Pictures of such children are also prohibited from publication.

main_sections.section_title: Appeals.—(1) Subject to the provisions of this section, any person aggrieved by an order made by a competent authority may, either on its own motion or on an application received in that behalf, amend any order as to the institution to which a child is to be sent or as to the person under whose care or supervision a child is to be placed under this Act.
main_sections.description: Allows appeals against orders made by a competent authority. A court of session may entertain an appeal within thirty days if satisfied that the appellant was prevented by sufficient cause from preferring the appeal in time. No appeal lies against certain orders.

main_sections.section_title: Revision.—The High Court may, at any time, either of its own motion or on an application received in this behalf, call for the record of any proceeding in which any competent authority or court of session has passed an order, for the purpose of satisfying itself as to the legality or propriety of such order and may pass such order in relation thereto as thinks fit.
main_sections.description: Grants the High Court the power of revision over proceedings and orders of competent authorities and courts of session under this Act, allowing it to examine legality and propriety and pass appropriate orders.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure in inquiries, appeals and revision proceedings.—(1) Save as otherwise expressly provided by this Act, a competent authority while holding any inquiry under any of the provisions of this Act, shall follow such procedure as may be prescribed and subject thereto, shall follow, as far as may be, the procedure laid down in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (Central Act 5 of 1898), for trials in summons cases
main_sections.description: Specifies that for inquiries, appeals, and revision proceedings, a competent authority shall follow prescribed procedures, and where not prescribed, the procedure laid down in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, for summons cases.

main_sections.section_title: Power to amend orders.—(1) Without prejudice to the provisions for appeal and revision under this Act, any competent authority may, either on its own motion or on an application received in this behalf, amend any order as to the institution to which a child is to be sent or as to the person under whose care or supervision a child is to be placed under this Act.
main_sections.description: Empowers competent authorities to amend their own orders regarding the institution to which a child is sent or the person under whose care they are placed, either on their own motion or upon application.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for cruelty to child.—(1) Whoever, having the actual charge of, or control over, a child, assaults, abandons, exposes or wilfully neglects the child or causes or procures him to be assaulted, abandoned, exposed or neglected in a manner likely to cause such child unnecessary mental and physical suffering, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.
main_sections.description: Punishes individuals who have charge or control of a child and assault, abandon, expose, or neglect them in a manner causing unnecessary suffering. Penalties include imprisonment up to six months, fine, or both.

main_sections.section_title: Employment of children for begging.—(1) Whoever employs or uses any child for the purposes of begging or causes any child to beg shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.
main_sections.description: Punishes those who employ or use a child for begging or cause a child to beg. Penalties include imprisonment up to one year, fine, or both.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for giving intoxicating liquor or dangerous drug to a child.—Whoever gives, or causes to be given, to any child any intoxicating liquor or any dangerous drug, except upon the order of a duly qualified medical practitioner or in case of sickness or other urgent cause, shall be punishable with fine which may extend to two hundred rupees.
main_sections.description: Penalizes the giving of intoxicating liquor or dangerous drugs to a child, except under medical order or for urgent causes. The penalty is a fine up to two hundred rupees.

main_sections.section_title: Exploitation of child employees.—Whoever ostensibly procures a child for the purpose of any employment and withholds the earning of the child or uses such earning for his own purposes shall be punishable with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees.
main_sections.description: Punishes those who procure a child for employment and withhold their earnings or use them for their own purposes. The penalty is a fine up to one thousand rupees.
