main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to discharge and transfer children.—(1) The Government may, at any time, order a neglected or delinquent child to be discharged from the children's home or special school either absolutely or on such conditions as the Government may think fit to impose
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to order the discharge of a neglected or delinquent child from a children's home or special school, either absolutely or with conditions.

important_rules: No child can be tried jointly with a person who is not a child.
Police officers can issue warnings to children for minor offenses.
Orders of competent authorities regarding children are subject to appeal and revision.
Proceedings in inquiries, appeals, and revisions should generally follow the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.
Publication of a child's identity in newspaper reports of inquiries under this Act is prohibited.
Competent authorities must consider specific circumstances when making orders about children.

penalties: Cruelty to child: Imprisonment up to six months, or fine, or both.
Employment for begging: Imprisonment up to one year, or fine, or both.
Giving intoxicating liquor/dangerous drug to a child: Fine up to two hundred rupees.
Exploitation of child employees: Fine up to one thousand rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Competent authorities, police officers, and courts of session, with overall oversight by the Government and High Court.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inquiries, proceedings in children's courts, appeals, revisions, and imposition of penalties as prescribed in the Act.

rights: Right to not be tried jointly with adults.
Right to receive appropriate treatment if suffering from a disease.
Right to have parent or guardian present at proceedings (unless dispensed with).
Right to have one's identity protected in newspaper reports.
duties: Duty of police officers to administer warnings where appropriate.
Duty of competent authorities to conduct inquiries and consider circumstances.
Duty of all persons to treat reports and considered circumstances as confidential.
Duty of the Government to provide for discharge and transfer of children.
obligations: Obligation on those in charge of children to not assault, abandon, expose, or neglect them.
Obligation not to employ children for begging or cause them to beg.
Obligation not to give intoxicating liquor or dangerous drugs to children except as prescribed.
Obligation not to withhold earnings of child employees or use them for own purposes.

key_procedures: Inquiry by competent authority: Follows prescribed procedures, and where not prescribed, the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.
Appeal: Against orders of competent authority to the court of session within thirty days.
Revision: By the High Court at any time on its own motion or application.
Dispensing with child's attendance: If the competent authority is satisfied it's not essential for the inquiry.
Committal for treatment: Sending a child with a disease to an approved place for medical treatment.
Determination of age: Competent authority conducts an inquiry to ascertain a person's age if in doubt.
administration: Competent authorities designated by the Government, with judicial oversight by courts of session and the High Court.
important_notes: Proceedings pending before the Act's commencement will continue under the old law, but sentences will be passed by the competent authority under this Act.
A child dealt with under this Act does not suffer disqualification normally attached to a conviction.
The High Court has broad powers of revision over orders made under the Act.
Reports from probation officers and circumstances considered by competent authorities are confidential.
The Government has the power to discharge or transfer children from children's homes or special schools.

title: The Kerala Chitties Act, 1975
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to chitties in the State of Kerala, and to provide for the regulation of chitties and the conduct of chitty business, to protect the interests of subscribers, and to provide for the efficient administration and supervision of chitties. The Act aims to provide for the orderly conduct of chitty schemes, the rights and liabilities of foremen and subscribers, and the settlement of disputes.
scope: This Act applies to all chitties conducted in the State of Kerala. It governs the conduct of chitty business, the rights and duties of foremen and subscribers, and the registration and supervision of chitties.

key_definitions.chitty: A transaction which is entered into by two or more persons who agree to contribute monthly to a fund which is offered to one of them in succession according to the highest bid or the lowest bid or by auction or by tender or in any other prescribed manner, and includes a kuri.
key_definitions.foreman: The person who conducts a chitty or an auction or a tender or any other mode of drawing of lots in the chitty and includes his legal representatives, heirs or assigns.
key_definitions.subscriber: A person who holds a ticket in a chitty and includes his legal representatives, heirs or assigns.
key_definitions.non-prized subscriber: A subscriber who has not received the prize amount in a chitty.
key_definitions.prized subscriber: A subscriber who has received the prize amount in a chitty.

main_sections.description: Specifies that every foreman shall be liable to the subscribers for the amounts due to them, and that where there are more foremen than one in a chitty, each of them shall be jointly and severally liable for the subscribers' obligations.

Deals with situations where a foreman withdraws from a chitty. It states that such withdrawal is not valid unless consented to in writing by all non-prized and unpaid prized subscribers, with a copy of such assent filed with the Registrar. It also clarifies that the withdrawal of a foreman does not affect the security given under section 15.

main_sections.section_title: Non-prized subscribers to pay subscriptions and get receipts
main_sections.description: States that every non-prized subscriber shall pay his subscription at the time and place mentioned in the variola and shall on such payment be entitled to get a receipt from the foreman. In default of any payment, the non-prized subscriber shall be liable to such consequences as provided for in the variola.

Provides for the removal of defaulting subscribers. If a non-prized subscriber defaults in payment, the foreman may, after intimating him by written notice, remove his name from the list of subscribers and substitute another person. Provided that if the defaulter pays up the defaulted instalment with interest at the rate of nine per cent per annum within one week of receipt of such notice, his name shall not be liable to be removed.

main_sections.section_title: Amount due to defaulting subscriber how dealt with
main_sections.description: Covers how amounts due to defaulting subscribers are handled. When a substituted subscriber draws the prize amount, the defaulting subscriber shall be entitled to recover from the foreman his subscriptions subject to such deductions as may be provided for in the variola. The foreman shall on demand made by the defaulting subscriber and on his executing acknowledgment in writing be bound to pay the amount due to him before the date of the next succeeding instalment. If the defaulting subscriber fails to furnish the acknowledgment, the foreman shall, before the date of the next succeeding instalment, deposit in an approved bank the amount due. The amount deposited shall not be withdrawn for any purpose other than for payment to the defaulting subscriber. Any foreman who contravenes these provisions shall be punishable with fine.

main_sections.section_title: Prized subscriber to sign minutes of proceedings
main_sections.description: Requires that in cases where the prize amount is determined by auction, every prized subscriber or a person authorized by him in writing shall sign the minutes of the proceedings relating to the drawing at which he obtains his prize.

Mandates that before drawing the prize amount, every prized subscriber shall furnish, and before making payment of the prize amount, the foreman shall take, reasonable security for the due payment of future subscriptions. If the foreman is the prized subscriber, he shall give security for the due payment of future subscriptions. If any foreman makes default in complying with these provisions, he shall be punishable with fine.

main_sections.section_title: Consequences of prized subscriber defaulting to pay subscriptions
main_sections.description: Outlines the consequences when a prized subscriber defaults in paying subscriptions. Every prized subscriber shall pay his subscriptions regularly, and on such payment shall be entitled to get a receipt. He shall be liable to such consequences as may be provided for in the variola and subject to the provisions of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Foreman to give notice in writing before demanding payment of all future subscriptions
main_sections.description: States that a foreman shall not be entitled to claim consolidated payment of all future subscriptions from a defaulting prized subscriber unless he has demanded the same in writing. If, in a suit instituted by a foreman, the defendant pays into court or before the date of the next succeeding instalment, the amount due, with interest and costs, the court shall pass a decree directing the defendant to deposit in court the amount due to the plaintiff. This section also addresses the handling of future subscriptions when they fall due and the liabilities arising from such non-payment.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of rights of foreman when voidable
main_sections.description: No transfer of the rights of a foreman to receive subscriptions from prized subscribers shall be made without the previous sanction in writing of the Registrar. Any transfer of the rights of a foreman to receive subscriptions from prized subscribers shall, if it defeats or delays a non-prized subscriber, be voidable at the instance of such subscriber. When under sub-section (2) a transfer is disputed by a subscriber, the burden of proving that the foreman was in solvent circumstances at the time of the transfer and that the transfer does not defeat or delay such subscriber is upon the transferee.
Every transfer by a non-prized subscriber of his rights in the chitty shall be in writing and shall be filed with the foreman.
Every transfer under section 31 shall be recognised by the foreman unless (a) the transferee is not solvent; or (b) the transfer was effected with a view to defeat the provisions of any law.

main_sections.section_title: Entry of transferee's name in the books
main_sections.description: Every transfer made under section 30 or section 31 shall be entered by the foreman in the books of the chitty. A true copy of every entry made under sub-section (1) shall be filed by the foreman with the Registrar within fourteen days from the date of such entry, in default of which the foreman shall be punishable with fine.

The foreman may, on his own initiative, convene a special meeting of the general body of subscribers for considering any proposal to pass a special resolution. The foreman shall convene such a meeting on the requisition in writing of not less than twenty-five per cent of the number of non-prized and unpaid prized subscribers, and the meeting so convened shall be held within thirty days of the date of receipt of the requisition. If the foreman refuses or fails to call the meeting within fourteen days of the receipt of such requisition, not less than twenty-five per cent of the number of non-prized and unpaid prized subscribers may give notice of the fact to the Registrar. The Registrar shall, within twenty-one days of the receipt of a notice under sub-section (2), convene a special meeting. The Registrar shall be present at every special meeting convened. The meeting shall elect its own chairman.

main_sections.section_title: Provision for continuation of chitties in certain cases
main_sections.description: Deals with the continuation of chitties in cases of foreman's death or insolvency. If a foreman dies or becomes of unsound mind, his legal representative or guardian may, in the absence of any provision in the variola to the contrary, take the place of the foreman and continue the chitty. If the legal representative or guardian fails to make any arrangement, any one or more of the non-prized or prized subscribers may, with the Registrar's permission, continue the chitty. When a foreman is adjudicated an insolvent, his legal representative or guardian, or a subscriber authorized by the Registrar, may continue the chitty. Provided that if there are more foremen than one and one or more of them are living, the chitty shall not be deemed to have terminated under this clause. If there is provision in the variola enabling the remaining foreman or foremen to conduct the chitty, they shall do so.

A chitty shall be deemed to have terminated only (a) when the period fixed in the variola has expired or has been altered by a special resolution for the duration of the chitty; or (b) when all the non-prized and unpaid prized subscribers consent in writing to the termination and a copy of such consent is filed with the Registrar within fourteen days of such consent; or (c) when the legal representative of a deceased foreman or the guardian of a foreman of unsound mind or subscribers selected therefor fail or fail to continue the chitty or make suitable arrangements for its further conduct as provided in section 35.

main_sections.section_title: Copy of resolution, etc., to be filed with the Registrar
main_sections.description: A true copy of every assent mentioned in sub-section (1) of section 22 and of every consent and resolution mentioned in section 36, with the date of such assent, consent or resolution, shall be filed by the foreman or by the remaining foreman or foremen, as the case may be, with the Registrar within fourteen days from the date of such assent, consent or resolution. Any foreman who contravenes these provisions shall be punishable with fine.

Except in the case of termination of a chitty under clause (a) or clause (b) of section 36, every non-prized subscriber shall, unless otherwise provided for in the variola, be entitled to get back his subscription at the termination of the chitty without any deduction for veethapalis (if any received by him). Except in the case of termination of a chitty under clause (a) or clause (b) of section 36, if a chitty terminates on a date earlier than the date originally fixed in the variola, the non-prized subscribers' claim shall be deemed to have arisen on the date on which he has notice thereof.

main_sections.section_title: Preference of subscribers over chitty assets
main_sections.description: Where there are debts due from the foreman of a chitty in relation thereto and also other debts due from such foreman, the chitty assets shall be a first charge for payment of the chitty debts due to the subscribers.

main_sections.section_title: Foreman to allow subscriber to examine chitty records
main_sections.description: Every foreman shall allow the non-prized and unpaid prized subscribers all reasonable facilities on all chitty days and on such other days as may be specified in the variola within such hours as may be provided therefor in the variola, for the inspection of security bonds and documents, receipts and other records, taken from prized subscribers or furnished by the foreman himself in his capacity as a subscriber, and all chitty records including account books and pass books, balance sheets and profit and loss accounts and such other records as may show the actual financial position of the chitty scheme. Any foreman who contravenes the provisions of this section shall be punishable with fine.

main_sections.section_title: Preservation of chitty records by foreman
main_sections.description: All the records pertaining to a chitty shall be preserved intact by the foreman and kept for a period of twelve years from the date of termination of the chitty and if he fails to do so, he shall be punishable with fine.

important_rules: Foremen must be liable to subscribers for amounts due.
Withdrawal of a foreman requires written consent from all non-prized and unpaid prized subscribers, with a copy filed with the Registrar.
Non-prized subscribers must pay their subscriptions on time and are entitled to receipts.
Defaulting subscribers can be removed after notice, but can be reinstated if they pay the defaulted amount with interest within a week.
Prized subscribers must furnish security before drawing the prize amount.
Foremen must demand consolidated payment of future subscriptions in writing before claiming it.
Transfers of foreman rights require the Registrar's sanction.
Meetings of the general body of subscribers can be convened by the foreman or by a requisition from at least 25% of non-prized and unpaid prized subscribers.
Foremen must allow subscribers to inspect chitty records.

penalties: Fine which may extend to one hundred rupees for contravening provisions related to default of payment by foremen (Section 25)
Fine which may extend to one hundred rupees for foreman making default in complying with provisions regarding security by prized subscribers (Section 27)
Fine which may extend to one hundred rupees for foreman contravening provisions related to demanding consolidated payment of future subscriptions (Section 29)
Fine which may extend to one hundred rupees for foreman contravening provisions regarding the entry of transferee's name in books (Section 33)
Fine which may extend to one hundred rupees for foreman contravening provisions related to calling meetings (Section 34)
Fine which may extend to one hundred rupees for foreman contravening provisions regarding the inspection of chitty records (Section 40)
Fine which may extend to three hundred rupees for any foreman who contravenes the provisions of section 25 and section 40
Fine which may extend to three hundred rupees for any foreman who contravenes the provisions of sub-section (4) or sub-section (5) or sub-section (6) of section 34
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Registrar of Chits
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through fines imposed on foremen and subscribers for non-compliance with provisions. The Registrar has the authority to convene meetings and ensure compliance with the Act's regulations.

rights: Subscribers have the right to receive prize amounts and subscriptions.
Subscribers have the right to inspect chitty records.
Non-prized subscribers have the right to receive back their subscriptions upon termination of a chitty (with certain conditions).
Subscribers have the right to have their foreman's liabilities enforced.
Subscribers have the right to have chitty meetings convened for discussions.
Subscribers have the right to dispute transfers of foreman rights.
duties: Foremen have the duty to conduct chitties according to the Act and variola.
Foremen have the duty to maintain accurate records and allow inspection.
Foremen have the duty to provide receipts for subscriptions.
Foremen have the duty to furnish security when required.
Subscribers have the duty to pay subscriptions on time.
Subscribers have the duty to furnish security when required.
obligations: Foremen are obligated to act in the best interest of subscribers and ensure the proper functioning of the chitty.
Foremen are obligated to ensure the security of chitty assets.
Subscribers are obligated to comply with the terms of the variola and the Act.

key_procedures: Conducting chitty meetings: Foreman convenes meetings on his initiative or on requisition from 25% of subscribers. Meetings are held within 30 days of requisition, and the Registrar can convene one if the foreman fails to do so. The Registrar attends, and the meeting elects a chairman.
Transfer of foreman rights: Requires prior sanction in writing from the Registrar. If contested, the burden of proof is on the transferee.
Filing of resolutions and consents: Copies of assents, consents, and resolutions regarding foreman withdrawal or chitty termination must be filed with the Registrar within 14 days.
Preservation of records: Foremen must preserve chitty records for 12 years after termination.
administration: The Registrar of Chits is the primary administrative authority responsible for the oversight and regulation of chitties under this Act.
important_notes: The Act specifies penalties for various contraventions by foremen, typically involving fines.
The variola, which is a document specific to each chitty, contains detailed rules and procedures that supplement the Act.
The Act provides for the resolution of disputes and liabilities arising from chitty transactions.
Section 35 and 36 deal with important provisions for the continuation or termination of chitties in cases of foreman's death, insolvency, or unsoundness of mind.
The Act emphasizes the importance of transparency by requiring foremen to allow subscribers to examine chitty records.

title: The Kerala Chitties (Amendment) Act, 1978
purpose: To amend the Kerala Chitties Act, 1975, for the purpose hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Chitties Act, 1975, and subsequent amendments.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Chitties (Amendment) Act, 1978. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 3rd day of May, 1978.

Inserts a new section 70A in the Kerala Chitties Act, 1975 (43 of 1975), after section 70. The new section 70A grants power to the Government, by notification in the Gazette, to exempt any company owned by the Government of Kerala or any co-operative society registered or deemed to be registered under the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969 (21 of 1969), from all or any of the provisions of the principal Act.

Repeals the Kerala Chitties (Amendment) Ordinance, 1978 (13 of 1978). Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: The Government may, by notification in the Gazette and for reasons to be specified in such notification, exempt any company owned by the Government of Kerala or any co-operative society registered or deemed to be registered under the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969 (21 of 1969), from all or any of the provisions of this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notification in the Gazette to grant exemptions.

rights: Right of the Government to exempt certain entities from the provisions of the Act.

key_procedures: Notification in the Gazette by the Government to grant exemptions to specified entities.
The Act is deemed to have come into force on May 3, 1978.
administration: Implied to be the relevant department of the Government of Kerala that oversees co-operative societies and financial regulations.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 1st day of August, 1978 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 506 dated 2nd August, 1978.
The amendment ordinance of 1978 is repealed but actions taken under it are saved.

title: The Kerala Cinemas (Regulation) Amendment Act, 1975
purpose: To amend The Kerala Cinemas (Regulation) Act, 1958, for the purposes herein appearing.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala, concerning the regulation of cinemas.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Cinemas (Regulation) Amendment Act, 1975, and shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 4
main_sections.description: Substitutes section 4 of the principal Act. The new section deals with the licensing authority, defining it as the executive authority of a local authority or such executive authority as may be specified by the Government. It also outlines the conditions for granting a license, including the prerequisite of the previous concurrence of the local authority and allows the Government to constitute licensing authorities for specific areas or parts of the State.

Amends section 5 of the principal Act. Specifically, it modifies clause (i) of sub-section (7) by substituting the existing text with provisions regarding the licensing authority and executive authority. It also inserts a new sub-section (8) detailing the process for appointing officers or authorities by the Government to call for records of any case under appeal and pass orders thereon.

Amends section 6 of the principal Act. It substitutes the words 'and with the previous concurrence of the local authority concerned' with new wording. It also inserts a proviso stating that the previous concurrence of the local authority shall not be necessary for the renewal of a permit under sub-section (1).

Amends section 11 of the principal Act. The amendment pertains to substituting certain words and figures related to the Travancore-Cochin Places of Public Resort Act, 1951, and the Madras Entertainments Tax Act, 1939, and the Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1961.

Substitutes the Schedule to the principal Act with a new schedule listing the following Acts: The Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960; The Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960; and The Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, 1961.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The licensing authority, which can be the executive authority of a local authority or a specified authority by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the granting, renewal, and potential appeal processes related to cinema licenses.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining a cinema license, involving application to the licensing authority.
Process for appeal against orders passed by the licensing authority.
Procedure for renewal of cinema permits.
Process for substitution of Acts in the Schedule.
administration: The State Government and its designated authorities are responsible for administering this Act.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 4th day of July, 1975, and was published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 339 dated 5th July, 1975.
The amendment to section 4 clarifies the role and powers of the licensing authority.
The amendment to section 5 provides for governmental oversight and record-keeping in appeal cases.
The amendment to section 6 exempts renewals from requiring previous local authority concurrence under certain conditions.

title: The Kerala Cinemas (Regulation) Amendment Act, 1960
purpose: To amend the Kerala Cinemas (Regulation) Act, 1958, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala and pertains to the regulation of cinemas.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Cinemas (Regulation) Amendment Act, 1960. It shall come into force at once.

Inserts a new section 8A into the Kerala Cinemas (Regulation) Act, 1958, granting power to the licensing authority to enter any place of cinematograph exhibition, inspect licenses, and prevent exhibition without a license or in violation of provisions. It also allows the authority to impose conditions or restrictions if it deems necessary. A proviso clarifies that before preventing further exhibition, the licensee or other person exhibiting such films shall be given a reasonable opportunity to show cause against the proposed action.

Inserts a new section 12A into the principal Act, stating that no suit, prosecution, or other legal proceedings shall lie against any person for anything done or intended to be done in good faith under this Act.

important_rules: Rule: The licensing authority has the power to enter any place of cinematograph exhibition.
Rule: The licensing authority can inspect licenses and prevent exhibitions without a license or in violation of the Act's provisions.
Rule: The licensing authority can impose conditions or restrictions as necessary.
Rule: No suit, prosecution, or other legal proceedings shall lie against any person for anything done or intended to be done in good faith under this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Licensing authority
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspection, prevention of exhibition, and imposition of conditions/restrictions. Also by protection from legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith.

rights: Right of the licensing authority to enter and inspect places of exhibition.
Right of the licensee or exhibitor to be given an opportunity to show cause before exhibition is prevented.
duties: Duty to obtain a license for cinematograph exhibition.
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules issued thereunder.
obligations: Obligation of the licensing authority to act in good faith when taking action.
Obligation of persons to comply with the provisions of the Act and the terms of their license.

key_procedures: Procedure: If a cinematograph exhibition is found to be in violation of provisions, the licensing authority can prevent further exhibition after giving the concerned party a chance to explain.
Procedure: Actions taken in good faith by any person under the Act are protected from legal proceedings.
administration: The document mentions the "licensing authority", implying an administrative body responsible for granting and overseeing cinema licenses.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Kerala Cinemas (Regulation) Act, 1958.
The insertion of new sections aims to enhance regulatory powers and provide legal protection for good faith actions.

title: The Kerala Civil Courts (Amendment) Act, 1958
purpose: To amend the Kerala Civil Courts Act, 1957, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Civil Courts Act, 1957.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Civil Courts (Amendment) Act, 1951, and that it shall come into force at once.

Substitutes a new sub-section for sub-section (1) of section 7 of the Kerala Civil Courts Act, 1957. The new sub-section deals with the places or seats at which civil courts may be held and how these may be fixed or altered by the Government in consultation with the High Court.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 10
main_sections.description: Substitutes a new section for section 10 of the principal Act. The new section 10 concerns the local limits of jurisdiction of Munsiffs' Courts, stating that these limits shall be fixed and may be varied by the Government in consultation with the High Court.

Amends section 13 of the principal Act by renumbering sub-section (1) as sub-section (1) of that section and making consequential changes to monetary amounts. It also introduces provisions for the application of decrees and orders of Subordinate Judge's Courts passed after the commencement of the Kerala Civil Courts (Amendment) Act, 1958, notwithstanding anything contained in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 26th March, 1959.

Inserts new sections 20A and 20B after section 20 of the principal Act. Section 20A deals with the maintenance of forms, books, and registers by civil courts and the subordination of civil courts to the High Court. Section 20B concerns the constitution and functions of Committees, which may be formed by the High Court for civil courts to include matters such as dissemination of legal knowledge, making recommendations for improvements, bringing the notice of the High Court specific cases of corruption, and providing facilities for closer association between the Bar and the Bench.

important_rules: The place or places at which any court referred to in section 2 shall be held, may be fixed, and from time to time, be altered by the Government in consultation with the High Court.
The local limits of jurisdiction of Munsiffs' Courts shall be fixed and may, from time to time, vary, by the Government in consultation with the High Court.

The Government, for discharging their functions and responsibilities, require through the High Court, the civil courts subordinate to the High Court to furnish to the Government such particulars and information relating to the working of Courts and other matters as they may call for from them from time to time.
The rules regulating the constitution of Committees shall be such as may be prescribed by the Government in consultation with the High Court.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government and High Court
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Alteration of court locations, fixing/varying jurisdiction, requiring information from courts.

rights: Right to have court locations fixed and altered by the Government in consultation with the High Court.
Right to have local limits of jurisdiction of Munsiffs' Courts fixed and varied by the Government in consultation with the High Court.
duties: Duty of civil courts to furnish particulars and information to the Government through the High Court.
Duty of the High Court to constitute committees for civil courts and delegate functions.
Duty of the committee to disseminate legal knowledge, make recommendations, report cases of corruption, and facilitate liaison between Bar and Bench.
obligations: Obligation of civil courts to conform to the orders of Subordinate Judge's Courts passed after the commencement of the Kerala Civil Courts (Amendment) Act, 1958.

key_procedures: Procedure for fixing and altering court locations: Government in consultation with the High Court.
Procedure for fixing and varying local limits of jurisdiction of Munsiffs' Courts: Government in consultation with the High Court.
Procedure for obtaining information on court working: Government requires it through the High Court.

Procedure for forming and functioning of Committees: Constitution by High Court, functions including dissemination of legal knowledge, recommendations, reporting corruption, and liaison between Bar and Bench, with rules prescribed by the Government in consultation with the High Court.
administration: High Court of Kerala, and the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Kerala Civil Courts Act, 1957.
Amendments pertain to court locations, jurisdiction, and the establishment of committees.
The Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 26th March, 1959.

title: The Kerala Civil Courts (Amendment) Act, 1973
purpose: To amend the Kerala Civil Courts Act, 1957.
scope: Applies to the civil courts in Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Civil Courts (Amendment) Act, 1973. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 15th day of February, 1957.

Amends section 13 of the Kerala Civil Courts Act, 1957, by substituting the first proviso. The substituted proviso states that whenever a Subordinate Judge's Court is established in any district at a place other than the place where the District Court is stationed, appeals from the decrees or orders of the Munsiff's Courts within the local limits of the jurisdiction of such Subordinate Judge's Court may be preferred in such Subordinate Judge's Court.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not specified in the provided text.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not specified in the provided text.

key_procedures: Appeals from decrees or orders of Munsiff's Courts within the local limits of a Subordinate Judge's Court's jurisdiction can be preferred to that Subordinate Judge's Court, provided the Subordinate Judge's Court is established at a different location than the District Court.
administration: Not specified in the provided text.
important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 677 dated 26th July, 1973.

title: THE KERALA CIVIL COURTS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1996
purpose: To amend the Kerala Civil Courts Act, 1957, for purposes hereafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and concerns the Civil Courts.

main_sections.description: This section names the Act as the Kerala Civil Courts (Amendment) Act 1996 and states that it shall come into force at once.
This section amends sub-section (2) of section 11 of the Kerala Civil Courts Act, 1957. It substitutes the words "fifteen thousand rupees" with "one lakh rupees".
This section amends sub-section (1) of section 13 of the principal Act. It substitutes the words "twenty-five thousand rupees" with "two lakhs rupees".

important_notes: Received the Assent of the Governor on the 26th day of March, 1996 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 476 dated 27 th March 1996.

title: THE KERALA CIVIL COURTS ACT, 1957
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to civil courts in the State of Kerala, subordinate to the High Court of Kerala.
scope: Applies to civil courts in the State of Kerala, subordinate to the High Court.

key_definitions.court: Means the District Court unless the Government have appointed (as they are hereby empowered to do) a special judicial officer within any specified local limits to perform the functions of the Court under this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Civil Courts Act, 1957, extends to the whole of the State of Kerala, and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Defines the classes of civil courts subordinate to the High Court, namely: the court of a District Judge, the court of a Subordinate Judge, and the court of a Munsiff.

Empowers the Government to establish District Courts by notification, specifying their limits and altering them as needed. The Government shall establish a District Court for each district and a Judge shall be appointed to it.

Allows the Government to appoint Additional District Judges when business of a District Court requires. An Additional District Judge shall discharge all or any of the functions of the District Judge assigned to him.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of Subordinate Judge's Courts and Munsiff's Courts
main_sections.description: Provides for the establishment of Subordinate Judge's Courts and Munsiff's Courts in each district in consultation with the High Court. The Government may, by notification, fix the number of Subordinate Judges and Munsiffs.

main_sections.section_title: Principal and Additional Subordinate Judge and Munsiff
main_sections.description: Deals with the appointment of Principal and Additional Subordinate Judges and Munsiffs. It also specifies that Judges or Munsiffs may exercise powers conferred by the Act. The Government may make arrangements for the distribution of business among the various Judges or Munsiffs.

Specifies that courts shall be held at fixed places, which can be altered by the Government. District Courts and Subordinate Judge's Courts are to be in the district headquarters or a place determined by the Government, while Munsiff's Courts are to be in the Munsiff's Court's jurisdiction or a place approved by the Government.
States that every court under this Act shall use a seal of such form and dimensions as prescribed by the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Local limits of jurisdiction of Subordinate Judge's Courts
main_sections.description: Allows the Government to fix and alter the local limits of jurisdiction of Subordinate Judge's Courts.

main_sections.section_title: Local limits of jurisdiction of Munsiff's Courts
main_sections.description: Allows the High Court to fix and alter the local limits of jurisdiction of Munsiff's Courts.

main_sections.section_title: Jurisdiction of District Court and Subordinate Judge's Court in original suits
main_sections.description: Defines the jurisdiction of District Courts and Subordinate Judge's Courts in original suits, extending to all suits and proceedings of a civil nature except those of which cognizance is barred. It also specifies that the jurisdiction of a District Court or Subordinate Judge's Court extends subject to the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. The jurisdiction of the District Court extends to suits where the subject-matter does not exceed five thousand rupees.

main_sections.section_title: Appeals from decrees and orders of District Court or Subordinate Judge's Court
main_sections.description: States that appeals from decrees and orders of District Courts or Subordinate Judge's Courts shall be as provided in section 13, and special appeals shall lie when allowed by law.

main_sections.section_title: Appellate jurisdiction of District Court and Subordinate Judge's Court
main_sections.description: Defines the appellate jurisdiction of District Courts and Subordinate Judge's Courts. Appeals from decrees and orders of a Munsiff's Court where the amount or value of the subject-matter of the suit does not exceed seven thousand and five hundred rupees, and from the original decrees and orders of a Subordinate Judge's Court, shall lie to the District Court. Appeals from the decrees and orders of a District Court or a Subordinate Judge's Court in original suits where the amount or value of the subject-matter exceeds seven thousand and five hundred rupees shall lie to the High Court. Provided that a Subordinate Judge's Court may hear appeals from decrees and orders of Munsiff's Courts within its appellate jurisdiction. Provided further that the District Court may remove to itself or to the High Court any appeal from the decrees and orders of Munsiff's Courts preferred in the District Court.

main_sections.section_title: Power to require witness or party to make oath or affirmation
main_sections.description: Grants the power to require a witness or party to take an oath or affirmation.

main_sections.section_title: Judges not to try suits in which they are interested
main_sections.description: Prohibits District Judges or Subordinate Judges from trying suits in which they are personally interested. It also states that no District Judge or Subordinate Judge shall hear any appeal in which he is personally interested.

main_sections.section_title: Temporary discharge of duties of District Judge
main_sections.description: Deals with the temporary discharge of duties of a District Judge due to illness or otherwise. The senior Additional District Judge or the senior Subordinate Judge or Munsiff shall assume charge, and if the office is vacant, the senior most officer shall discharge the duties until a successor is appointed.

main_sections.section_title: District Judge to control civil courts of District
main_sections.description: States that the District Judge shall, subject to other provisions of the Act and rules, have general control over all civil courts in the district, with the High Court having general control over all civil courts in the State.

main_sections.section_title: Investiture of District or Subordinate Judge or Munsiff with small cause jurisdiction
main_sections.description: Allows the High Court to invest a District Judge, Subordinate Judge, or Munsiff with small cause jurisdiction up to a certain pecuniary limit.
Grants the High Court power to permit civil courts to adjourn from time to time, not exceeding sixty days in aggregate each year.
States that ministerial officers shall perform duties imposed upon them by the presiding officer of the court.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Acts XI of 1989 and XV of 1950
main_sections.description: Amends The Land Acquisition Act, (XI of 1089) by substituting 'Court' for 'District Court' and The Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950 (XV of 1950) by renumbering and amending certain sections.

Repeals the Madras Civil Courts Act, 1873 and the Kerala Civil Courts Act, 1957, and also The Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950 and the Travancore-Cochin Civil Courts Act, 1951. It also includes provisions for savings, ensuring that anything done or any appointment made under the repealed Acts shall be deemed to have been done or made under this Act.

important_rules: Judges shall not try suits in which they are personally interested.
District Judges and Subordinate Judges shall not hear appeals in which they are personally interested.
Ministerial officers shall perform duties assigned to them by the presiding officer.
Civil courts may adjourn sittings for a period not exceeding sixty days in the aggregate in each year, as permitted by the High Court.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government and the High Court
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the establishment and regulation of civil courts, appointment of judges, and the High Court's general control over all civil courts.

rights: Right to appeal from decrees and orders of subordinate courts.
Right to have a District Court or Subordinate Judge's Court established for each district.
duties: Duty of District Judge to control civil courts in the district.
Duty of ministerial officers to perform assigned tasks.
Duty of Judges not to try suits in which they are interested.

key_procedures: Establishment of District Courts, Subordinate Judge's Courts, and Munsiff's Courts by notification.
Appointment of Judges and Munsiffs.
Determination and alteration of local limits of jurisdiction.
Appeals process from decrees and orders of subordinate courts to District Courts and High Courts.
Procedure for temporary discharge of duties of a District Judge.
Investiture of small cause jurisdiction.
administration: The High Court and the State Government.
important_notes: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.
The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Government.
The Act consolidates and amends existing laws relating to civil courts.
Provisions for savings ensure continuity of actions taken under repealed Acts.

title: THE KERALA CIVIL COURTS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1986
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala Civil Courts Act, 1957, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: The Act amends the Kerala Civil Courts Act, 1957.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Civil Courts (Amendment) Act, 1986.

In sub-section (1) of section 11 of the Kerala Civil Courts Act, 1957 (1 of 1957) (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), for the words "five thousand rupees", the words "fifteen thousand rupees" shall be, and shall be deemed to have been, substituted with effect from the 6th day of September, 1983.

In sub-section (1) of section 13 of the principal Act, for the words "ten thousand rupees", the words "twenty-five thousand rupees" shall be, and shall be deemed to have been, substituted with effect from the 6th day of January, 1984.

In section 18 of the principal Act, for the words "one thousand rupees" and "five hundred rupees" (the words "one thousand and five hundred rupees" and "one thousand rupees" shall be, and shall be deemed to have been, respectively substituted with effect from the 17th day of April, 1985.

In section 19 of the principal Act, for sub-section (2), the following sub-section shall be, and shall be deemed to have been, substituted with effect from the 5th day of April, 1986, namely: - "(2) During the adjournment of a civil court, the High Court shall nominate a District Judge for each District, who shall have the power to make provisional orders on all urgent matters and for such purpose, appeals, plaints and petitions and other matters which would ordinarily be presented to such civil court shall have been received in the District Court and any such order shall, except on matters to be presented in the District Court itself, remain in force until such matter has been heard and decided by the court having jurisdiction and in the case of orders passed on matters to be presented in the District Court itself, such order shall be an order passed by a court having jurisdiction."

(1) The Kerala Civil Courts (Amendment) Ordinance, 1986 (56 of 1986), is hereby repealed.
(2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 30th day of November, 1986 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No 1082 dated 30th November, 1986.

title: The Kerala Civil Courts (Amendment) Act, 2013
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Civil Courts Act, 1957, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Civil Courts Act, 1957.

main_sections.description:
(1) This Act may be called the Kerala Civil Courts (Amendment) Act, 2013.
(2) It shall come into force at once.

In sub-section (2) of section 11 of the Kerala Civil Courts Act, 1957 (1 of 1957) (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), for the words "one lakh rupees", the words "ten lakh rupees" shall be substituted.
In sub-section (1) of section 13 of the principal Act, for the words "two lakh rupees", the words "twenty lakh rupees" shall be substituted.

administration: Law (Legislation-E) Department, Government of Kerala

title: The Kerala Civil Courts (Amendment) Act, 1990
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala Civil Courts Act, 1957.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Civil Courts Act, 1957.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Civil Courts (Amendment) Act, 1990.

In the Kerala Civil Courts Act, 1957 (1 of 1957), after section 20B, the following section shall be inserted, namely:— "20C. Rules to be laid before the Legislative Assembly.—Every rule made under this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before the Legislative Assembly while it is in session for a total period of fourteen days which may be comprised in one session or in two successive sessions, and if, before the expiry of the session in which it is so laid or the session immediately following, the Legislative Assembly makes any modification in the rule or decides that the rule should not be made, the rule shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect, as the case may be; so, however, that any such modification or annulment shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that rule."

important_rules: Every rule made under this Act shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly as soon as may be after it is made.
The rule shall be laid for a total period of fourteen days which may be comprised in one session or in two successive sessions.
If the Legislative Assembly makes any modification in the rule or decides that the rule should not be made, the rule shall have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect.
Any modification or annulment shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that rule.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Legislative Assembly
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By making modifications or deciding not to make the rule.

key_procedures: Rules made under the Act must be laid before the Legislative Assembly.
The Legislative Assembly has the power to modify or annul these rules.
administration: Kerala Civil Courts
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 28th day of February 1990 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 192 dated the 1st March 1990.

title: The Kerala Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2017
purpose: To amend the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969.
scope: Applies to all co-operative societies registered or deemed to be registered under the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969.

key_definitions.co-operative society: An autonomous body formed voluntarily by people for their mutual benefit.
key_definitions.amendment: Changes or modifications made to the existing Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Amends Section 2 of the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969, by adding a new clause defining 'expert' and 'management committee'.
Amends Section 16 of the Act related to the disqualification for being a member of a committee.
Amends Section 18 of the Act concerning the constitution of committees.
Amends Section 19 of the Act relating to the election of members of committees.
Amends Section 28 of the Act regarding the powers of the Registrar.
Amends Section 32 of the Act concerning the convening of meetings of the committee.
Inserts a new section 42A related to the appointment of managing directors and chief executive officers in co-operative societies.
Substitutes Section 101 of the Act, which deals with the power to make rules.

important_rules: Societies must ensure that elections to committees are conducted according to the amended provisions.
The Registrar's powers regarding the control and supervision of co-operative societies are clarified.
Specific provisions are made for the appointment and qualifications of managing directors and chief executive officers.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Registrar of Co-operative Societies and other authorities appointed by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, audits, inquiries, and legal proceedings as prescribed by the Act and rules.

rights: Members have the right to participate in the democratic management of the society.
Members have the right to elect and be elected to the committee.
duties: Societies have a duty to function in accordance with the provisions of the Act and the rules.
Members have a duty to contribute to the society's success and uphold its principles.
obligations: Co-operative societies are obligated to maintain proper accounts and submit them for audit.

key_procedures: Procedure for the election of committee members as per the amended provisions.
Procedure for the appointment of managing directors and chief executive officers.
Procedure for the Registrar to exercise powers related to inquiry and audit.
administration: Department of Co-operation, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The amendment aims to strengthen the governance and management of co-operative societies in Kerala.
The Act emphasizes transparency and accountability in the functioning of co-operative societies.

title: THE KERALA CO-OPERATIVE LAND MORTGAGE BANKS ACT, 1960
purpose: To facilitate the working of co-operative land mortgage banks in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala. It concerns co-operative land mortgage banks and their operations, including debentures, mortgages, and sale of mortgaged property.

key_definitions.Board: Board of Directors of the Central Land Mortgage Bank
key_definitions.Central Mortgage Bank: The Kerala Co-operative Central Land Mortgage Bank, Limited
key_definitions.Committee: In relation to a primary mortgage bank, means the Board of Directors or Board of Management or the Panchayat or the Committee of management or the governing body to whom the management of its affairs is entrusted
key_definitions.Co-operative society: A co-operative society registered or deemed to be registered under the Travancore-Cochin Co-operative Societies Act, 1952, and the Madras Co-operative Societies Act, 1932
key_definitions.Malabar: The Malabar district referred to in sub-section (2) of section 3 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (37 of 1956)
key_definitions.notified order: An order notified in the Gazette
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made by the Government under this Act
key_definitions.primary mortgage bank: A co-operative land mortgage bank registered or deemed to be registered under the Travancore-Cochin Co-operative Societies Act, 1952, and admitted as a member of the Central Mortgage Bank
key_definitions.Registrar: Means the person appointed by the Government to be the Registrar of Co-operative Societies for the State
key_definitions.Trustee: Means the Trustee referred to in section 5

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Co-operative Land Mortgage Banks Act, 1960. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'Central Mortgage Bank', 'Committee', 'Co-operative society', 'Malabar', 'notified order', 'prescribed', 'primary mortgage bank', 'Registrar', 'State', and 'Trustee'.

main_sections.section_title: Admission of land mortgage banks registered under the Madras Co-operative Societies Act, 1932, as members of the Central Mortgage Bank.
main_sections.description: Allows land mortgage banks registered under the Madras Co-operative Societies Act, 1932, to be admitted as members of the Central Mortgage Bank, provided they are admitted before the commencement of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Issue of debentures by the Board.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Board to issue debentures to raise funds. It specifies conditions regarding the term, amount, and security of these debentures.
Deals with the distraint (seizure) and sale of produce when an instalment of mortgage money is unpaid. It outlines the process and conditions for distraint and sale.

main_sections.section_title: Power of sale when to be exercised.
main_sections.description: Grants the power of sale to the Central Mortgage Bank or a primary mortgage bank under certain conditions, such as default in payment of mortgage money or where the property is likely to sell to better advantage.

important_rules: Debentures issued by the Board may contain a term fixing a period not exceeding twenty years from the date of issue during which they shall be irredeemable (Section 4(1)(b)).

The total amount due on debentures issued by the Board and outstanding, at any time, shall not exceed the aggregate of the amounts due on the mortgages and other assets referred to in clause (a) or sub-section (1) and the amounts paid thereunder and remaining in the hands of the Board or of the Trustee at such time (Section 4(2)).
Distraint shall be made after the expiry of twelve months from the date on which the instalment fell due (Section 9(1)).

No power of sale shall be exercised unless the mortgagor or any person who has any interest in or upon the property is given notice in writing requiring payment of the mortgage money or part thereof (Section 12(2)(b)).
Application for sale may be made by the Board or Committee, and the sale may be by public auction (Section 13(1) & (2)).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Board, Committee, Registrar, and Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through distraint and sale of produce or mortgaged property, by making rules, issuing notifications, and appointing trustees.

rights: Right of mortgage bank to recover money and grant valid discharge (Section 32)
Right of mortgage bank to apply for sale and manner of sale (Section 13)
Right of Central Mortgage Bank or primary mortgage bank to purchase the mortgaged property at sale (Section 18)
Right of mortgage bank to claim prior debts of mortgagor (Section 29)
duties: Duty of the Board to issue debentures (Section 4)
Duty of the Trustee to manage affairs and execute mortgages (Section 5)
Duty to repay debenture holders with interest (Section 4)
Duty to register documents executed on behalf of the Central Mortgage Bank or a primary mortgage bank (Section 31)
obligations: Obligation to give notice in writing requiring payment of mortgage money before sale (Section 12(2)(b))

key_procedures: Issuance of debentures by the Board, including terms and conditions (Section 4).
Appointment of Trustee and their powers and functions (Section 5).
Distraint of produce upon default of payment, including when it can be made, how to be effected, and the process of sale (Sections 8, 9, 10).
Exercise of power of sale by the bank, including conditions, notice requirements, and process of sale (Sections 12, 13, 14).
Registration of documents executed by the mortgage bank or Trustee (Section 31).
Application to Court for winding up of a primary mortgage bank (not explicitly detailed in the provided content but implied by the existence of such provisions in similar acts).
administration: The Government, Board of Directors of the Central Mortgage Bank, and Committees of primary mortgage banks.
important_notes: The Act was enacted by the President in the Tenth Year of the Republic of India (Page 3).
The Act was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary dated 29th January, 1960 (Page 2, footnote).
Certain rights and liabilities of the Cochin Co-operative Land Mortgage Bank to continue (Section 44).
Powers of Government to make rules are vested in various sections for different purposes (e.g., Section 11, Section 22).

title: The Kerala Co-Operative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2002
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969.
scope: Applies to societies within the state of Kerala.

key_definitions.Central Society: A society which has as its object to raise funds to be lent to its members, with jurisdiction over one revenue district and having as its members any type of primary societies and Federal and Central Societies having headquarters in such district.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Co-Operative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2002. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 4th day of May, 2002.

Amends Section 2 of the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969. It substitutes the following clause for clause (ia): "(ia) 'District Co-operative Bank' means a Central Society, the principal object of which is to raise funds to be lent to its members, with jurisdiction over one revenue district and having as its members any type of primary societies and Federal and Central Societies having headquarters in such district."
In Section 18 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), the first and second provisos shall be omitted, and in the third proviso, the word "also" shall be omitted.

In Section 20 of the principal Act, in the opening paragraph, for the words "every active member", the words "every member" shall be substituted, and the second proviso shall be omitted. The Explanation shall be omitted.

Inserts a new Section 28AA after Section 28A in the principal Act. This new section deals with the Election and Removal of President, Vice-President, etc. It states that a committee constituted under sub-section (1) of section 28 shall elect from themselves a President, a Vice-President, a Treasurer or any other officer, by whatever name he is designated, in the manner as may be prescribed. A committee shall remove from office the President, Vice-President or the Treasurer or any other officer if a motion expressing want of confidence in any or all of them is carried with the support of the majority of the members of such committee in accordance with the procedure as may be prescribed.

In Section 80A of the principal Act, after sub-section (1), the following sub-section shall be inserted, namely: "(1A) The Self Financing Pension Scheme framed under sub-section (1) may also provide for payment of pension from the pension fund, at such rates and subject to such conditions and restrictions as may be specified therein, to persons retired from service of any society during the period between 1st January, 1974 and 3rd June, 1993 and are alive."

main_sections.section_title: Special provision in respect of the existing District Co-operative Banks
main_sections.description: Provides for certain provisions regarding existing District Co-operative Banks. (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in the principal Act or in any judgment, decree or order of any court, tribunal or other authority, on the commencement of this Act, (a) any primary society which had ceased to be a member of any District Co-operative Bank on the commencement of the Kerala Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Act, 1997 (15 of 1997), shall be deemed to have become a member of such District Co-operative Bank and the share amount, if any, of such society transferred to suspense account shall be deemed to be the share amount in respect of the said society. (b) any primary society enrolled as a nominal or associate member of the District Co-operative Bank after the commencement of the Kerala Co-operative Societies (Second Amendment) Act, 1997 (15 of 1997), shall cease to be such nominal or associate member and such society may apply for membership in the District Co-operative Bank afresh. (c) the Committee in office of a District Co-operative Bank at such commencement shall cease to exist and the Registrar shall be competent to appoint a new committee or one or more administrator or administrators, who need not be members of the society, to manage the affairs of the society for a period not exceeding six months, as may be specified in the order, which period may, at the discretion of the Registrar, be extended from time to time, so however that the aggregate period does not exceed one year. (2) The committee or administrator or administrators appointed under sub-section (1) shall, subject to the control of the Registrar and to such instructions as he may from time to time give, have power to exercise the powers and perform the functions of the committee or of any officer of the society and take such action as may be required in the interests of the society. (3) The committee or administrator or administrators shall, before the expiry of its or his or their term of office, arrange for the constitution of a new committee in accordance with the provisions contained in the principal Act and the bye-laws of the society.

(1) The Kerala Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Ordinance, 2002 (6 of 2002), is hereby repealed. (2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Registrar is the primary enforcement authority.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The Registrar has control and can issue instructions to committees and administrators. Enforcement includes appointing administrators and ensuring new committees are formed.

rights: Right to form or join cooperative societies.
Right to pension for retired employees under specific conditions.
duties: Societies must adhere to the provisions of the principal Act and this Amendment Act.
Committees and administrators have duties to manage society affairs and arrange for new committees.
obligations: District Co-operative Banks must ensure proper management and constitution of new committees.

key_procedures: Election of President, Vice-President, and Treasurer by a committee.
Procedure for removal of President, Vice-President, or Treasurer by a vote of no confidence.
Appointment of administrators by the Registrar to manage society affairs if a committee ceases to exist.
Arrangement for the constitution of a new committee before the expiry of the term of the current committee or administrator.
administration: The Registrar of Co-operative Societies, Kerala.
important_notes: The Act was necessitated by the repeal of the Kerala Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Ordinance, 2002.
The Act has retrospective effect from May 4, 2002.
Certain provisions regarding District Co-operative Banks have special conditions and retrospective application.
Received the assent of the Governor on 4th July, 2002 and published in Kerala Extraordinary Gazette No 967 dated 5th July, 2002.

title: THE KERALA CO-OPERATIVE SOCIETIES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1971
purpose: To amend the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969 for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: The Act applies to the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Act, 1971. It shall come into force at once.
Amends section 33 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), by substituting figures '82' and '83' for '82' and '83' respectively.
Amends section 72 of the principal Act, in sub-section (3), by substituting figures '82' and '83' for '82' and '83' respectively.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new sections for section 81
main_sections.description: Substitutes new sections for section 81 of the principal Act. This includes provisions for the constitution of a single member Tribunal, qualifications for appointment, and the term, salary and allowances for members. It also empowers the Government to make rules for regulating the procedure and disposal of business of the Tribunal. A new section 81A is introduced regarding provisions as to certain pending proceedings.

Amends section 82 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), by omitting clauses (b) and (c) of sub-section (1) and omitting clauses (a) for the words 'nine members one from each Revenue District in the State', the words 'one member from each Revenue District in the State' shall be substituted.

Amends section 89 of the principal Act, in sub-section (4), in clause (a) for the words 'nine members one from each Revenue District in the State', the words 'one member from each Revenue District in the State' shall be substituted.

Repeals The Kerala Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Ordinance, 1971 (19 of 1971). It also states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Regarding quorum of the committee and resignation of members.
Provisions for the constitution and functioning of a Tribunal.

title: The Kerala Co-Operative Societies (Amendment) Act, 1974
purpose: To amend the Kerala Co-Operative Societies Act, 1969, for the purpose hereinafter appearing. Specifically, to insert Chapter X-A relating to insured co-operative banks.
scope: Applies to insured co-operative banks and related matters as defined within the act. It amends the Kerala Co-Operative Societies Act, 1969.

key_definitions.co-operative bank: Means a bank as has been defined in the Deposit Insurance Corporation Act, 1961.
key_definitions.insured co-operative bank: Means a society which is an insured bank under the provisions of the Deposit Insurance Corporation Act, 1961.
key_definitions.transferee bank: In relation to an insured co-operative bank, means a co-operative bank— (a) with which such insured co-operative bank is amalgamated, or (b) to which the assets and liabilities of such insured co-operative bank are transferred, or (c) into which such insured co-operative bank is divided or converted under the provisions of section 12 or section 14 of the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969 (21 of 1969).

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Act, 1974.
In the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969 (21 of 1969) (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), after Chapter X, the following Chapter shall be inserted, namely:—
Deals with matters concerning insured co-operative banks, including orders for winding up, amalgamation, reconstruction, and the powers of the Reserve Bank of India in relation to such banks.

Repeals the Kerala Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Ordinance, 1973 (13 of 1973), and provides that anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act shall come into force on the 20th day of November, 1973.

Empowers the Government, if any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, to order anything not inconsistent with such provisions which appears to them necessary for the purpose of removing the difficulty.

Repeals The Kerala Restriction on Cutting and Destruction of Valuable Trees Ordinance, 1974 (1 of 1974), and states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government, Reserve Bank of India, Registrar.

key_definitions.primary agricultural credit society: Means a Service Co-operative Society, a Service Co-operative Bank, a Farmers Service Co-operative Bank, a Financial Co-operative Bank and a Rural Bank the principal object of which is to undertake agricultural credit activities and to provide loans and advances for agricultural purposes, the rate of interest on such loans and advances shall be the rate fixed by the Registrar and having its area of operation confined to a Village, Panchayath or a Municipality.
key_definitions.urban co-operative society: Means a co-operative society the principal object of which is to undertake non-agricultural credit activities and to raise funds to be lent to its members with its area of operation confined to a municipality or a corporation.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Act, 2010, and it shall come into force at once.

It modifies the phrasing regarding the purpose of organising co-operative societies to emphasize 'self governing' and 'self governance'. It also adds a clause about promoting scientific and technological development, health care, market intervention and management excellence in the co-operative sector.

Introduces amendments to section 2 of the principal Act, specifically in relation to insertion of definitions for 'Co-operative Ombudsman' and 'Director of Co-operative Audit', and substitution of definitions for 'Miscellaneous Societies' and 'Primary Agricultural Credit Society', and insertion of definition for 'Urban Co-operative Society'.
Amends section 6 of the principal Act by modifying the wording related to individuals who can be considered as 'who is an individual'.

Adds a proviso to section 9 of the principal Act, stating that the Government and the Registrar shall have power to regulate and control the working of a society for the economic and social betterment of its members and the general public.

Amends section 28 of the principal Act. It substitutes sub-section (1A) to specify the maximum number of members in the committee of a Primary Co-operative Society and in the case of other types of co-operative societies. It also inserts a proviso to sub-section (1A) concerning the maximum number of members in committees of Primary Co-operative Societies prior to the commencement of the Amendment Act, 2010. It further inserts a new sub-section (1C) to section 1B regarding reservation for members of a Primary Credit Society or an Urban Co-operative Bank in the committee.

Amends section 28A of the principal Act. It substitutes sub-section (1) to specify the number of seats for women members and substitutes sub-section (3) to clarify the representation of women and persons belonging to Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes in the committee of a society, including the nomination of persons by the Government or Registrar.

Inserts a new section 28AA in the principal Act, which provides for reservation for persons with banking experience or professional qualification in the committees of Urban Co-operative Banks. It specifies that not less than two seats shall be reserved in such committees.
Amends section 28B of the principal Act by adding the words 'and Representative General Body' after certain phrases related to the conduct of elections to the committees.

Amends section 32 of the principal Act by substituting clause (d) of sub-section (1). This amendment relates to the powers of the committee regarding misappropriation or destruction of records, and the procedure for removing a committee and appointing an administrator. It specifies that the aggregate period of administrator's charge shall not exceed one year.

Amends section 33 of the principal Act by substituting clause (b) of sub-section (1). This amendment deals with the situation where a new committee is prevented from entering office or fails to enter upon office, and the Registrar's power to appoint an administrator. It clarifies the conditions and duration for the administrator's appointment.

Amends section 36A of the principal Act by inserting certain words related to 'State Co-operative Bank or a District Co-operative Bank or a Primary Agricultural Credit Society or a Primary Housing Society' or 'Urban Co-operative Bank or any Primary Co-operative Societies dealing with credit activities'.

key_procedures: The appointment of an administrator for a society when a new committee is prevented from entering office or fails to enter upon office, and the conditions and duration for such appointment.
administration: Co-operative Department, Government of Kerala (inferred from the context of Kerala Co-operative Societies Act)
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on 26th April, 2010 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 1033 dated 28th April, 2010.

Provided further that if the above principal object is not fulfilled, such societies shall lose all characteristics of a Primary Agricultural Credit Society as specified in the Act, Rules and Bye-laws except the existing staff strength.
Provided that the restriction regarding the area of operation shall not be applicable to the existing urban co-operative societies.

The Kerala Co-operative Employees' Welfare Scheme.-(1) The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, frame a Scheme to be called the Kerala Co-operative Employees' Welfare Scheme for the establishment and management of a Fund by name "the Kerala Co-operative Employees' Welfare Fund" and there shall be established, as soon as may be, after framing of the Scheme, a Fund in accordance with the provisions of this Act and the Scheme. (2) The Welfare Fund established under the Scheme shall vest in the Kerala State Co-operative Employees' Welfare Board and be administered by such body or authority as may be specified in the Scheme. (3) Subject to the provisions of this Act, the Scheme may provide for the following matters, namely:- (i) the management and administration of the Kerala State Co-operative Employees' Welfare Fund; (ii) powers and functions of the authority or body to be constituted thereunder; and (iii) the composition and pattern of the establishment set up of the Kerala State Co-operative Employees' Welfare Board constituted under the Scheme. 80D. Kerala State Co-operative Employees' Welfare Board.-(1) The Government shall, by notification in the Gazette, constitute a Board to be called "the Kerala State Co-operative Employees' Welfare Board" for implementing the welfare schemes for the regular employees, commission agents and the persons working in the capacity of any other name on commission basis in a Co-operative society registered or deemed to be registered under this Act and coming under the administrative control of the Registrar of Co-operative Societies as well as other departments of the State Government in accordance with the provisions of this Act and the Scheme.
