(3) The Board may provide money and other aids to the employees in their indigent conditions and for the following purposes, namely:- (i) for the payment of financial assistance to the family of the deceased employees; (ii) for the payment of medical assistance to the employees who have undergone treatment for diseases to be specified therein; (iii) for refund of the contributions made by the employees on their retirement or relief on other grounds; (iv) for the grant of advances to the employees for meeting their medical expenses; (v) for awarding cash prizes to the children of employees at such rates and subject to such conditions as may be specified therein; and (vi) for any other purposes provided for in the Scheme or which may be found necessary or proper for the implementation of the Scheme. (4) The Government may make rules with regard to the terms and conditions of the services of the Kerala State Co-operative Employees' Welfare Fund. 80E. Transfer of assets and control of the existing Kerala State Co-operative Employees' Welfare Board.-(1) Notwithstanding contained in the rules for the constitution and administration of the Kerala State Co-operative Employees' Welfare Board issued in G. O. (Rt.) No.383/86/Co-op. dated 30th September, 1986 and from the date of constitution of the Kerala State Co-operative Employees' Welfare Board under sub-section (1) of section 80D, all assets and liabilities of the existing Kerala State Co-operative Employees' Welfare Board shall be transferred to the Kerala State Co-operative Employees' Welfare Board constituted under the said sub-section. (2) On and from the date of constitution of the Kerala State Co-operative Employees' Welfare Board under sub-section (1) of section 80D, the existing Kerala State Co-operative Employees' Welfare Fund constituted under G. O. (Rt.) No.383/86/Co-op. dated 30th September, 1986 shall vest in the Kerala State Co-operative Employees' Welfare Board constituted under the said sub-section and the control and supervision of the existing fund shall be with the said Board."

(1) The Kerala Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Ordinance, 2013 (25 of 2013) is hereby repealed. main_sections.description: This section details amendments to the Travancore-Cochin Co-operative Societies Act, 1951. It includes provisions for inserting new sub-sections related to amalgamating societies, appeals against refusal, and the process of amalgamation initiated by the Registrar. It also covers the rights of creditors and members during amalgamation and the registration of new societies.

main_sections.section_title: Amendments to the Madras Co-operative Societies Act, 1932
main_sections.description: This section details amendments to the Madras Co-operative Societies Act, 1932. It involves renumbering of sections and insertion of new sub-sections concerning the amalgamation of societies. Similar to the amendments in Section 2, it addresses appeals, the Registrar's powers in amalgamation, and the rights of members and creditors. It also outlines the process for the registration of new societies and the cancellation of old ones.

important_rules: Any person aggrieved by the refusal of a co-operative society to be admitted as a member, or by the Registrar's decision on appeal, must accept the Registrar's decision.
Before arriving at a decision, the Registrar must give parties concerned a reasonable opportunity to be heard and take into consideration the interest of the society or any ulterior motive.

The Registrar can direct the amalgamation of societies where it is necessary or desirable for increasing their strength or usefulness. This must be done within a specified time and in accordance with prescribed procedures.

If societies fail to amalgamate within the specified time, the Registrar can give an opportunity to the committee of each society to state its objections, and if none are raised, direct the amalgamation.
Every registered society directed to amalgamate must give notice of the direction to all its members and creditors within one month of the receipt of the Registrar's direction.

Any member or creditor of a society can withdraw their shares, deposits, or loans, or demand a return of their amount within one month of the service of notice, notwithstanding any agreement to the contrary.
Any member or creditor who does not exercise their option within the specified period is deemed to have assented to the amalgamation.

After the repayment of share capital and claims of creditors, if any, by societies directed to amalgamate or after a majority of members and creditors have assented, the Registrar may register the new society.
Upon registration of a new society, the registration of the old societies is deemed cancelled, and the new society inherits the assets and liabilities of the original societies.
Directions from the Registrar under specific clauses and any other order passed by him under these sub-sections shall be final and not subject to challenge in any civil court.

penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through directives, notifications, registration, cancellation, and ensuring adherence to procedures.

Right to object to amalgamation.
duties: Societies must provide notice of amalgamation directions to members and creditors.
Societies must comply with the Registrar's directions regarding amalgamation.
Societies must facilitate the transfer of assets and liabilities to the new society upon registration.
obligations: Members and creditors have an obligation to exercise their rights within the stipulated timeframes during amalgamation.

Cancellation of Old Societies: Upon registration of a new society formed by amalgamation, the registration of the constituent old societies is deemed cancelled.
Receiving and Processing Applications: The act implies procedures for admitting members and processing appeals and objections related to societies.

Amends Section 2 of the Principal Act by inserting a new clause (1-ca) which defines 'disqualified' to mean disqualified under section 28B or section 28C.

Inserts a new Section 28B titled 'Disqualification of members of committee for other disqualifications' which outlines various grounds for disqualification of members of the committee of a co-operative society, including conviction of certain offences, insolvency, unsound mind, and holding office of profit. It also states that a disqualified person shall not be eligible to be a member of the committee for a period of six years from the date of disqualification.

Inserts a new Section 28C titled 'Disqualification of members of committee for being an office bearer or member of committee in more than two societies' which disqualifies a person from being an office bearer or member of the committee of more than two co-operative societies.

Amends Section 69 of the Principal Act by substituting the existing sub-section (2) with new provisions related to the audit of accounts of co-operative societies. It specifies the authority responsible for auditing and the timeframe for completing the audit.

important_rules: Members of a co-operative society's committee are disqualified if they are convicted of certain offences, are insolvent, or are of unsound mind.
A person cannot be an office bearer or committee member in more than two co-operative societies.
The accounts of co-operative societies must be audited annually by the Registrar or any person authorized by him.
The audit report must be submitted to the committee and the general body of the society.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Registrar of Co-operative Societies
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through disqualification of committee members, audit of accounts, and other powers vested in the Registrar.

rights: Members have the right to have the accounts of the society audited.
duties: Co-operative societies have a duty to get their accounts audited annually.
Members of the committee have a duty to act in the best interests of the society and its members.

key_procedures: Procedure for disqualification of committee members: If a member falls under any of the disqualifying conditions, they shall be deemed to be disqualified and shall not be eligible to be a member for six years.

Procedure for audit: The accounts of a co-operative society shall be audited annually by the Registrar or a person authorized by him. The audit report is then submitted to the committee and the general body.
administration: Co-operation Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act aims to improve the governance and financial health of co-operative societies in Kerala.
The disqualification provisions are intended to ensure that only fit and proper persons manage the affairs of co-operative societies.
The amendment regarding audit procedures is to ensure timely and efficient auditing of co-operative societies' accounts.

title: The Kerala Coir Workers Welfare Cess Act, 2008
purpose: To provide for the levy and collection of a cess on coir workers to fund welfare measures for them.
scope: The Act applies to coir workers in the State of Kerala. It aims to establish a welfare fund for the benefit of these workers.

key_definitions.coir worker: Any person employed or engaged in the production, processing, or sale of coir products.
key_definitions.cess: A tax or levy imposed for a specific purpose, in this case, for the welfare of coir workers.
key_definitions.welfare fund: A fund established under the Act to provide benefits and amenities to coir workers.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies when it comes into force.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'coir worker', 'cess', 'welfare fund', etc.
Details the provisions for levying and collecting the welfare cess on coir workers. This includes specifying the rate of cess and the manner of its collection.
Provides for the establishment of a Coir Workers Welfare Fund and its management.
Outlines the purposes for which the Welfare Fund can be utilized, such as providing pensions, medical aid, educational assistance, etc., to coir workers.
Grants powers to the Government to make rules and issue directions for the effective implementation of the Act.
Allows for the appointment of officers to administer the provisions of the Act and manage the Welfare Fund.
Empowers the Government to frame rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Grants the Government the power to remove any difficulties that may arise in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of any existing laws on the subject and provides for savings.

important_rules: A welfare cess is to be levied and collected on coir workers.
The collected cess shall be credited to a Welfare Fund established for the benefit of coir workers.
The Welfare Fund shall be utilized for specified welfare measures for coir workers.
The Government has the power to frame rules for the implementation of the Act.

penalties: Penalties for non-compliance with the provisions of the Act, including fines and imprisonment.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government and officers appointed under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the collection of cess, management of the Welfare Fund, and imposition of penalties for violations.

rights: Coir workers have the right to benefit from the Welfare Fund for specified purposes.
Coir workers have the right to receive benefits such as pensions, medical aid, and educational assistance.
duties: Coir workers have a duty to contribute to the Welfare Fund through the cess.
Employers and others responsible for the coir industry have a duty to facilitate the collection of cess.
obligations: The Government has an obligation to establish and manage the Welfare Fund effectively.
The Government has an obligation to ensure that the benefits reach the intended coir workers.

key_procedures: Procedure for levy and collection of the welfare cess.
Procedure for the establishment and management of the Coir Workers Welfare Fund.
Procedure for claiming benefits from the Welfare Fund.
Procedure for enforcing penalties for non-compliance.
administration: The State Government of Kerala, likely through its Labour Department or a designated authority.
important_notes: The Act aims to improve the socio-economic conditions of coir workers.
The Act has provisions for removing difficulties in its implementation.
The Act may have repealed or amended earlier legislation on the subject.

title: The Kerala Coir Workers' Welfare Cess Act, 2008
purpose: To provide for the levy and collection of cess on the sale proceeds of coconut husk, coconut husk fibre, coir and coir products with a view to augmenting the resources of the Kerala Coir Workers' Welfare Fund Board constituted under section 6 of the Kerala Coir Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 1987.
scope: Applies to the levy and collection of cess on the sale proceeds of coconut husk, coconut husk fibre, coir and coir products within the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Assessing Officer: An officer appointed by the Government under section 4.
key_definitions.Board: The Kerala Coir Workers' Welfare Fund Board constituted under section 6 of the Kerala Coir Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 1987.
key_definitions.Coir: The coir obtained by the spinning of coconut husk fibre separated from the husk of the coconut.
key_definitions.Coir products: means mats and mattings, rugs and carpets, coconut husk fibre, other rubberized coir products manufactured by using coconut husk fibre, coir or pith wholly or partly and it includes products manufactured in traditional looms and mechanised looms; other products and other allied products with the backing of PVC, rubber or any similar backing materials.
key_definitions.Dealer: means any person engaged in the business of buying, selling or storing for sale of coconut husk, coconut husk fibre, coir or any coir products, within the State of Kerala, but it does not include a cultivator who stores his own coconut husk, for sale;
key_definitions.Fund: means Kerala Coir Workers' Welfare Fund established under section 3, of the Kerala Coir Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 1987,.
key_definitions.prescribed: prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.sale proceeds: the value of buying and selling of coconut husk, coconut husk fibre, coir or coir products made in the State of Kerala for sale or to process otherwise

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its commencement.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act.
Details the levy and collection of cess on coconut husk, coconut husk fibre, coir or coir products. The cess is not to exceed one percent of the total sale proceeds.
Empowers the Government to appoint an Assessing Officer.
Requires every dealer to maintain registers and records as prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Furnishing of Returns by the dealer
main_sections.description: Mandates dealers to furnish returns showing sale proceeds of the previous financial year.
Outlines the procedure for assessment of cess by the Assessing Officer.
Allows for provisional collection of cess if the amount payable is not determined.

main_sections.section_title: Interest payable on delay in payment of Cess
main_sections.description: Specifies the interest rate for delayed payment of cess.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for non-payment of Cess within the specified time
main_sections.description: Imposes a penalty for non-payment of cess within the specified time.

main_sections.section_title: Recovery of amount due under this Act
main_sections.description: Details the recovery of any amount due under the Act.
Provides for the right to appeal against an order of assessment.
Allows for revision of orders by the Government or Appellate Authority.
Grants Assessing Officers or other authorized officers the power to enter premises and inspect records.
Requires the Board to furnish returns of collected cess.
Specifies penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions.
Deals with offences committed by companies.

main_sections.section_title: Bar of jurisdiction of Civil Courts
main_sections.description: Bars civil courts from entertaining suits or proceedings concerning matters under this Act.
Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Cess levied shall not exceed one percent of the total sale proceeds.
Dealers must furnish returns showing sale proceeds of the previous financial year.
Dealers have the right to appeal against orders of assessment.
Assessing Officers have the power to enter premises and inspect records.
Penalties are prescribed for non-payment of cess and contravention of Act provisions.

penalties: Penalty for non-payment of cess: Imprisonment which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees or with both.
Penalty for contravention of provisions: Imprisonment which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees or with both.
Penalty for contravention of provisions (if no other penalty provided): Imprisonment which may extend to three months or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees or with both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Assessing Officer, Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment, recovery proceedings, penalties, and legal action for offences.

rights: Right to appeal against orders of assessment.
Right to be heard before penalties are imposed.
duties: Duty of dealers to pay cess.
Duty of dealers to furnish returns.
Duty of dealers to maintain registers and records.
Duty to cooperate with Assessing Officer during inquiry.
obligations: Obligation to pay cess at the prescribed rate.
Obligation to pay interest on delayed payment of cess.
Obligation for companies to ensure compliance with the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure for assessment of cess involves inquiry, collection of information, and passing of assessment orders.
Procedure for appeal involves preferring an appeal to the Director of Coir Development within sixty days of the order.
Procedure for revision involves application by the aggrieved person or suo motu by the Government.
Procedure for power to entry involves authorized officers entering premises and inspecting records.
Procedure for recovery of amount due involves recovery as an arrear of land revenue.
administration: Department of Coir Development, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act is an augmentation of the resources of the Kerala Coir Workers' Welfare Fund Board.
The cess is levied on the sale proceeds of coconut husk, coconut husk fibre, coir and coir products.
Civil Courts are barred from jurisdiction in matters dealt with by this Act.
The Government has the power to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act.

title: The Kerala Coir Workers Welfare Fund Act, 1987
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a fund to grant relief to, to promote the welfare of, and to pay pension to coir workers and self-employed persons in coir industry in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala. Covers coir workers, self-employed persons in the coir industry, coir co-operative societies, employers, producers, and dealers of coir products.

key_definitions.board: The Kerala Coir Workers' Welfare Fund Board.
key_definitions.chief_executive_officer: The Chief Executive Officer appointed under section 9.
key_definitions.coir_products: Mats and mattings, rugs and carpets, ropes and other articles manufactured wholly or partly from coir and coir yarn.
key_definitions.coir_worker: Any person who is employed for wages to do any work in connection with the various processes in coir industry and who gets his wages directly or indirectly from the employer, dealer or producer of coir products, and includes any person employed by or through a contractor or through an agent and depends mainly on coir industry for his livelihood, and includes any other person employed in coir industry, whom the Government may by notification in the Gazette from time to time declare to be a coir worker for the purposes of this Act.
key_definitions.fund: The Coir Workers' Welfare Fund established under section 4 and the scheme.
key_definitions.scheme: A scheme framed under this Act.
key_definitions.self_employed_person: A person other than a coir worker, who is engaged in the extraction of coir fibre, spinning yarn and manufacture of coir products for other persons and depends mainly on coir industry for his livelihood.
key_definitions.yarn: The coir yarn obtained by the spinning of fibre.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Coir Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 1987, extends to the whole of the State of Kerala, and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'Chief Executive Officer', 'coir products', 'coir worker', 'contribution', 'dealer', 'Director of Coir Development', 'employer', 'family', 'fibre', 'fund', 'husk', 'member', 'person', 'prescribed', 'processes in coir industry', 'producer of coir products', 'scheme', 'self-employed person', 'yarn', and 'year'.

Empowers the Government to frame a scheme for the establishment of a fund for the welfare of coir workers and self-employed persons in the coir industry. The scheme shall be called the Kerala Coir Workers' Welfare Fund Scheme. The scheme shall come into force as soon as may be after its framing and shall be published in the Gazette. The fund shall consist of contributions, amount borrowed, damages recovered, grants or loans, donations, amounts raised by the Board, and fee levied under the scheme. The fund shall vest in, and be administered by the Board. The fund may be utilised for payment of pension to members, payment to families of deceased members, financial assistance to members, payment of loans or grants to members to meet expenses, maternity benefits, distress relief, and for any other purpose specified in the scheme. The scheme shall be laid, as soon as may be, before the Legislative Assembly.

Specifies the contributions to the fund by coir workers, coir co-operative societies, employers, producers, and dealers of coir products. It also states the contribution from the Government. An explanation clarifies that a coir co-operative society means a society registered or deemed to be registered under the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969.
Allows the Government to amend or add to the scheme by notification in the Gazette. Any such modification shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

Provides for the constitution of the 'Kerala Coir Workers' Welfare Fund Board' for the administration of the fund. The Board shall be a body corporate. It shall consist of a Chairman and such number of Directors as may be prescribed, not exceeding fifteen. Not less than fifty per cent of the Directors shall be from coir workers and self-employed persons, and the remaining shall represent the Government, employers, producers and/or dealers.
Specifies the term of office of Directors, who shall hold office for a period of three years. It also outlines conditions for removal and resignation of Directors.

Details the circumstances under which non-official Directors may be removed from office, including absence from meetings and inability to discharge duties. A Director must be given an opportunity to show cause before removal.

important_rules: Every coir worker and every self-employed person shall contribute to the fund one rupee each per month.
Every employer other than a coir co-operative society shall contribute to the fund two rupees per month in respect of each coir worker.
Every coir co-operative society which employs a coir worker shall contribute to the fund one rupee per month in respect of each such coir worker.

penalties: Section 17: Penalty for contravention of the provisions of the Act or rules, regulations or schemes framed thereunder.
Section 17: Penalty for offences by Companies.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Board and the Chief Executive Officer are responsible for the administration and enforcement of the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, rules, regulations, and schemes framed thereunder. Penalties are prescribed for contraventions.

rights: Right to pension for members unable to work due to old age or infirmity who have completed the age of sixty years.

Right to pension for persons who before the commencement of the Act was a coir worker or a self-employed person and completed the age of sixty years or who suffers from permanent disablement and is out of employment.
Right to payment of family pension to the spouse of a deceased member.
Right to payment of financial assistance to a member who suffers from permanent or temporary disability.

Right to payment of loans or grants to a member to meet the day to day expenses during off season or to meet expenses for the marriage of children or for expenses in connection with disease or death of dependants or for expenses in connection with the education of children or for expenses for construction or maintenance of houses.
Right to provide maternity benefits to women workers engaged in coir industry who are not eligible for such benefits under any other law for the time being in force.
Right to provide for distress relief to the family of a member affected by natural calamities and epidemics.

Right to provide for the coir workers, self-employed persons and members of their families medical facilities, nurseries and creches, and education, vocational training and facilities for part-time employment.
Right to implementation of any other purpose specified in the scheme.
duties: Duty to contribute to the fund (coir workers, self-employed persons, employers, co-operative societies, producers, dealers).
Duty of the Board to administer the fund vested in it.
Duty of the Board to supervise the activities financed from the fund.
obligations: Every coir worker and every self-employed person shall contribute to the fund.
Every employer other than a coir co-operative society shall contribute to the fund.
Every coir co-operative society which employs a coir worker shall contribute to the fund.

key_procedures: Framing of the Kerala Coir Workers' Welfare Fund Scheme by the Government.
Collection of contributions to the fund from various stakeholders.
Administration of the fund by the Board.
Utilization of the fund for specified welfare purposes.
Appointment of officers and staff for the Board.
Conduct of meetings of the Board.
Audit of accounts of the Board and remuneration of auditors.
Submission of annual report and audited statement of accounts to the Government.
administration: The Act is administered by the 'Kerala Coir Workers' Welfare Fund Board', constituted under the Act. The Government of Kerala is also involved in framing the scheme and making notifications.
important_notes: The scheme shall be laid, as soon as may be, after it is framed, before the Legislative Assembly while it is in session for a total period of fourteen days which may be comprised in one session or in two successive sessions, and if, before the expiry of the session in which it is so laid or the sessions immediately following, the Legislative Assembly makes any modification in the scheme, the scheme shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form, however that any such modification shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under the scheme.
The Board shall be a 'body corporate' by the name aforesaid, having perpetual succession and a common seal and shall by the said name sue and be sued.
The Board shall consist of such number of Directors not exceeding fifteen in number, as may be supported by the Government and they shall be chosen in such manner as may be prescribed.

Provided that fifty per cent of the number of Directors shall be from among coir workers and self-employed persons and the remaining shall represent the Government, employers, producers and/or dealers.

title: The Kerala Command Area Development (Amendment) Act, 2000
purpose: The purpose of this amendment act is to amend the Kerala Command Area Development Act, 1986, for specific reasons outlined in the act itself. The preamble suggests it is to make further provisions regarding the development of command areas and to amend certain sections of the Principal Act. Specific amendments seem to relate to the definition and functioning of 'Command Area Development Authority' and 'Command Area'.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala and concerns the development of command areas. The specific areas covered by the amendments are detailed within the sections.

key_definitions.command_area: This seems to be a key term, with specific definitions or amendments related to it appearing in the text. For instance, Section 2(1) refers to 'command area' as defined in Section 2(1) of the Principal Act. Section 4(1) further elaborates on the 'command area' in relation to the Command Area Development Authority.
key_definitions.command_area_development_authority: This entity is central to the act. Section 2(1) of the amendment act seems to be replacing or amending the definition of this authority from the Principal Act, possibly to clarify its role and functions in relation to the command area.
key_definitions.principal_act: Refers to the Kerala Command Area Development Act, 1986, which is being amended by this Act.

main_sections.description: This section likely states the short title of the Act and when it comes into effect. Based on the text, the short title appears to be 'The Kerala Command Area Development (Amendment) Act, 2000'. The text also mentions 'commencement' which suggests the date of its enforcement.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 2 of Act 26 of 1986
main_sections.description: This section amends Section 2 of the Principal Act (Act 26 of 1986). It appears to be introducing or modifying definitions within the Principal Act, specifically concerning the 'Command Area Development Authority' and 'Command Area'. It may be replacing or adding sub-clauses to the original definitions.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 12 of Act 26 of 1986
main_sections.description: This section amends Section 12 of the Principal Act. It specifies that sub-clause (3) of Section 12 is being omitted and replaced, likely dealing with the powers, functions, or constitution of the Command Area Development Authority.

This section inserts a new section, 19A, into the Principal Act. This new section seems to address 'Functions of the Authority'. It details the responsibilities and duties of the Command Area Development Authority in relation to the command area. The text lists specific functions, including planning, implementation, supervision, coordination, and monitoring of development works.

important_rules: The Command Area Development Authority is responsible for planning, implementing, supervising, coordinating, and monitoring development works within the command area.
The Authority may perform such other functions as are entrusted to it by the Government or as may be prescribed.
The amendment likely clarifies or expands the scope of activities undertaken by the Command Area Development Authority.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Command Area Development Authority
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the planning, implementation, supervision, coordination, and monitoring of development works as detailed in the new Section 19A.

duties: The Command Area Development Authority has the duty to plan development works.
The Authority has the duty to implement development works.
The Authority has the duty to supervise development works.
The Authority has the duty to coordinate development works.
The Authority has the duty to monitor development works.
obligations: The Authority must perform functions entrusted by the Government or prescribed by rules.

key_procedures: Procedure for planning, implementing, supervising, coordinating, and monitoring development works within the command area by the Command Area Development Authority.
administration: The Act is administered by the authorities established under the Kerala Command Area Development Act, 1986, specifically the Command Area Development Authority.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Kerala Command Area Development Act, 1986 (Act 26 of 1986).
The Act introduces a new section (19A) to the Principal Act, detailing the functions of the Authority.
The amendment involves the omission and replacement of sub-clause (3) of Section 12 of the Principal Act.

title: THE KERALA COMMAND AREAS DEVELOPMENT ACT, 1986
purpose: To provide for the development of command areas for irrigation projects in the State of Kerala and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to command areas identified for irrigation projects in the State of Kerala. It outlines the powers and functions of the Command Area Development Authority and other related bodies.

key_definitions.command_area: The area under command of a project in which irrigation is provided.
key_definitions.authority: The Command Area Development Authority constituted under the Act.
key_definitions.project: An irrigation project including its components like reservoirs, canals, and other structures.
key_definitions.developer: Any person who undertakes any development activity within the command area.

main_sections.description: Describes the formation of the Command Area Development Authority, its composition, appointment of members, and its powers and functions.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of the Authority
main_sections.description: Details the various powers and functions of the Authority, including planning, execution, supervision, and coordination of command area development activities, and making recommendations to the Government.
Grants the Government the power to issue directions to the Authority regarding the implementation of the Act and policies.
Empowers the Authority to acquire land for the purpose of carrying out its functions and development activities.
Outlines the Authority's power to prepare and implement schemes for the development of the command area, including infrastructure development and land use planning.
Allows the Authority to levy betterment charges on lands that have benefited from the development activities undertaken.
Provides for the constitution of Advisory Committees to assist the Authority in its functions.
Confers upon the Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.
Grants the Authority the power to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules.
Allows the Authority to delegate its powers and functions to any officer or committee.
Grants officers authorized by the Authority the power to enter and inspect any land or premises for the purpose of the Act.

important_rules: Beneficiaries must pay betterment charges as levied by the Authority.
Development activities within command areas must be in accordance with approved schemes.
All irrigation infrastructure within command areas is subject to the control and management of the Authority.

penalties: Penalties for contravention of the Act or rules, which may include fines.
Specific penalties for obstruction or refusal to comply with directions or inspections.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Command Area Development Authority and officers authorized by it.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, imposition of penalties, and legal proceedings as prescribed by the Act and rules.

rights: Right to receive irrigation benefits as per project design.
Right to information regarding schemes and development plans.
duties: Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules.
Duty to pay betterment charges and other fees as levied.
Duty to maintain farm level irrigation infrastructure.
Duty to cooperate with the Authority in its development activities.
obligations: Landowners in command areas have an obligation to facilitate the development and maintenance of irrigation facilities.

key_procedures: Preparation and approval of command area development schemes.
Levy and collection of betterment charges.
Inspection and monitoring of development activities.
Enforcement of provisions through penalties and legal actions.
administration: The Department of Irrigation, Government of Kerala, is generally responsible for the oversight and implementation of such acts, with the Command Area Development Authority acting as the primary administrative body for specific command areas.
important_notes: The Act aims to ensure efficient and equitable distribution of water resources.
Development activities are focused on maximizing agricultural productivity and improving the socio-economic conditions of the farming community.
The Act provides for the establishment of a decentralized administrative structure for command area development.

title: THE KERALA COMPENSATION FOR TENANTS IMPROVEMENTS ACT, 1958
purpose: To make provision for payment of compensation for improvements made by tenants in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force at once.

key_definitions.eviction: means the recovery of possession of land from a tenant.
key_definitions.improvement: means any work or product of a work which adds to the value of the holding, is suitable to it and consistent with the purpose for which the holding is let, mortgaged or occupied, but does not include such clearances, embankments, levellings, enclosures, temporary wells and water-channels as are made by the tenant in the ordinary course of cultivation and without any special expenditure or any other benefit accruing to land from the ordinary operations of husbandry.
key_definitions.tenant: with its grammatical variations and cognate expressions includes- (i) a person who, as lessee, sub-lessee, mortgagee or sub-mortgagee or in good faith believing himself to be lessee, sub-lessee, mortgagee of land, is in possession thereof; (ii) a person who with the bona fide intention of attorning and paying a reasonable rent to the person entitled to cultivate or let waste land, but without the permission of such person, brings such land, under cultivation and is in occupation thereof as cultivator; and (iii) a person who comes into possession of land belonging to another person and makes improvement thereon in the bona fide belief that he is entitled to make such improvements.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Kerala Compensation for Tenants Improvements Act, 1958', its extent to the whole of the State of Kerala, and that it shall come into force at once.
Provides definitions for terms like 'eviction', 'improvement', 'State', and 'tenant'.

main_sections.section_title: What are presumed to be improvements.
main_sections.description: Lists specific works and products of works that are presumed to be improvements for the purposes of the Act, including erection of dwelling houses, construction of tanks, wells, channels, drainage, reclamation, planting of trees and maintenance of fruit trees.

main_sections.section_title: Tenant entitled to compensation for improvements.
main_sections.description: Entitles a tenant, on eviction, to compensation for improvements made by him or by any person from whom he derived title, provided the compensation was not already paid and every tenant to whom compensation is due shall, notwithstanding the determination of the tenancy, be entitled to possession of the land until eviction in execution of a decree or order of court. It also states that this section shall not apply to tenants holding lands under the Government. It further clarifies that a tenant continuing in possession shall be subject to the terms of his lease or mortgage, if any.

main_sections.section_title: Decree in eviction to be conditional on payment of compensation.
main_sections.description: Stipulates that a decree for eviction against a tenant will be conditional on the payment of compensation as assessed by the court under sections 7 to 16, unless the tenant has caused substantial injury to the land.

main_sections.section_title: Tenant's right to remove buildings, works or trees deemed not improvements.
main_sections.description: Grants a tenant the right to remove buildings, works, or trees that are not deemed improvements, provided they have erected them without a decree or order for eviction and the court finds no improvement that can be claimed. The tenant must fix a time for removal. If the tenant does not remove them within the fixed time, they become the property of the landlord.

main_sections.section_title: Improvement producing an increase in the value of the annual net produce.
main_sections.description: Deals with improvements that increase the value of the annual net produce, stating that the compensation will be based on the increase in the value of the annual net produce of the holding and will be awarded as the average net money value of such increase at 20 times the amount.

Addresses compensation for trees or plants that have spontaneously grown, stating that compensation will be three-fourths of the sum which the trees or plants might reasonably be expected to realise if sold by public auction.

Deals with other types of improvements not covered by section 7 or 8, stating that compensation will be awarded based on the cost of labour, including supervision, and materials, together with expenditure, if any, which would at the time of valuation, be requisite to make the improvement, less a reasonable deduction for deterioration.

main_sections.section_title: Value of improvement to be ascertained in the way most favourable to the tenant.
main_sections.description: Mandates that the value of any improvement should be ascertained in the manner most favourable to the tenant, with specific examples provided for compensation for jack trees, coconut trees, and cardamom plantations.

main_sections.section_title: Improvement consisting in protection and maintenance of trees and plants.
main_sections.description: States that the compensation for improvements related to the protection and maintenance of trees and plants shall be the proper cost of such protection and maintenance, as ascertained in section 9.

main_sections.section_title: Power to frame tables of maximum and minimum rates of compensation.
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to frame tables of maximum and minimum rates of compensation for the whole or any part of the State, showing the maximum and minimum rates applicable to various classes of improvements.

main_sections.section_title: Power to prepare tables of prices of produce, etc.

title: The Kerala Conservation Of Paddy Land And Wetland (Act 28 OF 2008) Act, 2008
purpose: To conserve paddy land and wetland in the State of Kerala, to prevent their conversion into other lands, and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: This Act applies to all paddy lands and wetlands in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.paddy_land: Means all the land being cultivated with paddy and includes all types of paddy lands whether reclaimed or not, and also includes rivers, streams and canals passing through paddy land.
key_definitions.wetland: Means all lands in the State of Kerala which are sources of water and includes tanks, ponds, lakes, rivers, streams, canals, ponds, channels, and reservoirs and includes the land within its banks or boundaries.
key_definitions.conversion: Means the act of changing the nature of paddy land or wetland into any other land for the purpose of any development or infrastructure project, and includes filling up of paddy land or wetland with any material, leveling of paddy land or wetland, destruction of bunds or embankments of paddy land or wetland or any act which alters the original character of the paddy land or wetland.
key_definitions.collector: Means the Collector of a revenue district and includes any officer not below the rank of Tahsildar authorised by the Government to perform the functions of a Collector under this Act.
key_definitions.local_authority: Means a Municipal Corporation, Municipal Council, City Corporation, Town Council or Village Panchayat constituted under the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1994 or the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, 1994.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and its commencement.

Details the powers of the Government under this Act, including making rules, issuing directions, etc.
Provides for the constitution of a District Level Committee and a Local Level Committee to oversee the implementation of the Act.
Empowers various officers to take measures for the conservation of paddy land and wetland, including inspection, search, and seizure.

important_rules: No person shall convert paddy land or wetland into any other land without the prior permission of the empowered authority.

The empowered authority shall not grant permission for conversion of paddy land or wetland unless it is satisfied that such conversion is necessary for a public purpose or for a project of public importance.
Local authorities shall take measures for the conservation of paddy land and wetland within their jurisdiction.
The Government may take such measures as it deems fit for the conservation of paddy land and wetland.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or with fine which may extend to fifty thousand rupees or with both, for contravention of the provisions of the Act.
For subsequent contravention, imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years and with fine which may extend to one lakh rupees.

penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By issuing orders, directions, and taking appropriate measures for the restoration of paddy land and wetland.

Right to information regarding actions taken under the Act.
duties: Duty to conserve paddy land and wetland.
Duty to obtain necessary permissions before conversion.
Duty of local authorities to protect paddy land and wetland within their jurisdiction.
obligations: Obligation to restore converted paddy land or wetland to its original character.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining permission for conversion of paddy land or wetland.
Procedure for appealing against orders passed by authorities.
Procedure for restoration of converted paddy land or wetland.
administration: Department of Revenue, Government of Kerala.

key_definitions.wetland: Land lying between terrestrial and aquatic systems, where the water table is usually at or near the surface or which is covered by shallow water or characterized by the presence of sluggishly moving or standing water, saturating the soil with water and includes backwaters, estuary, fens, lagoon, mangroves, marshes, salt marsh and swamp forests but does not include paddy lands and rivers;

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Conservation of Paddy Land and Wetland Act, 2008. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force at once.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including Collector, Committee, conversion, district, drainage channel, Government, holder of paddy land, intermediary crop, Kudumbasree units, Local Self Government Institution, paddy land, Padasekhara Samithi, public purpose, reclamation, State, State Level Committee, wetland, and year.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition on conversion or reclamation of paddy land
main_sections.description: On and from the date of commencement of this Act, no owner, occupier or the person in custody of any paddy land shall undertake any activity for the conversion or reclamation of such paddy land except in accordance with the provisions of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power to regularise the conversion or reclamation of Paddy land made before the commencement of the Act
main_sections.description: Empowers the Collector to regularise the conversion or reclamation of paddy land under certain conditions, subject to the payment of a fee and with the satisfaction that the conversion or reclamation has been done for a public purpose.
The Government shall take suitable measures, from time to time, in order to assist the farmers to augment the production of paddy in the State.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of Local Level Monitoring Committee
main_sections.description: There shall be a Local Level Monitoring Committee in each Panchayat or Municipality, consisting of members specified in sub-section (2), for the purpose of monitoring the implementation of the provisions of this Act. The composition includes the President/Chairperson/Mayor, Agricultural Officer/Officers, Village Officer/Officers, and three representatives of farmers.

main_sections.section_title: The term of the Local Level Monitoring Committee and other related matters
main_sections.description: Details the term of office and other related matters concerning the Local Level Monitoring Committee.
Designates officers responsible for reporting on matters related to the Act.
Provides for the constitution of a State Level Committee.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of District Level Authorised Committee
main_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of a District Level Authorised Committee.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to grant exemption
main_sections.description: The Government may grant exemption from the provisions of this Act under certain circumstances.
Prohibits the reclamation of wetland.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Authorised Officers and their Powers
main_sections.description: Deals with the appointment of Authorized Officers and the powers conferred upon them.
Specifies the powers of the District Collector under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Refusal of licence by the Local Authority
main_sections.description: Details the circumstances under which a Local Authority may refuse a licence.

main_sections.section_title: Direction to cultivate paddy land left fallow
main_sections.description: Empowers authorities to direct cultivation of paddy land that has been left fallow.

main_sections.section_title: Fallow paddy land to be got cultivated
main_sections.description: Ensures that fallow paddy land is brought under cultivation.

main_sections.section_title: Eviction of person to whom the right has been entrusted in certain cases
main_sections.description: Provides for the eviction of persons in certain cases where rights have been entrusted to them.
Grants special powers to the Collector.
Confers powers of entry and seizure upon authorized officers.
Allows for the confiscation of vessels, vehicles, etc., used in contravention of the Act.
Provides for an appeal against confiscation orders.

main_sections.section_title: Award of confiscation not to interfere with other punishment
main_sections.description: Clarifies that confiscation awards do not prevent other punishments.
Specifies penalties for contravention of the Act.
Deals with offences committed by companies.
Describes how offences under the Act are to be taken cognizance of.

main_sections.section_title: Grant of injunction etc., by Civil Courts
main_sections.description: Concerns the grant of injunctions by Civil Courts.

main_sections.section_title: Sums due recoverable as arrears of land revenue to Government
main_sections.description: Specifies that sums due under the Act are recoverable as arrears of land revenue.
Provides for the revision of orders passed under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Protects actions taken in good faith under the Act.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: No owner, occupier, or person in custody of paddy land shall undertake any activity for its conversion or reclamation except in accordance with the Act's provisions.
The Government shall take measures to assist farmers in augmenting paddy production.
Fallow paddy land must be brought under cultivation.
Reclamation of wetlands is prohibited.
The Government can grant exemptions from the Act's provisions.
Sums due under the Act are recoverable as arrears of land revenue.

penalties: Penalties are specified under Section 23. Specific amounts or durations are not detailed in the provided excerpts but imply a range of punishments.
Offences by companies are also addressed, suggesting penalties applicable to corporate entities.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Collector, Authorised Officers, Local Level Monitoring Committee, State Level Committee, District Level Authorised Committee, Government of Kerala.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the appointment of authorized officers, powers of entry and seizure, confiscation of vessels and vehicles, and penalties for contravention. Sums due are recoverable as arrears of land revenue. Civil courts can grant injunctions.

rights: Right to appeal against confiscation.
Right to seek regularisation of conversion/reclamation done before the Act's commencement (under specific conditions).
duties: Duty of owners, occupiers, and persons in custody of paddy land to comply with the prohibition on conversion or reclamation.
Duty to assist farmers in augmenting paddy production (Government).
obligations: Obligation to bring fallow paddy land under cultivation.
Obligation to adhere to the prohibition on reclamation of wetlands.

key_procedures: Procedure for regularisation of conversion or reclamation of paddy land made before the commencement of the Act, involving application to the Collector and payment of a fee.
Procedure for the constitution and functioning of the Local Level Monitoring Committee, State Level Committee, and District Level Authorised Committee.
Procedure for applying for and obtaining licenses or permissions related to land use.
Procedure for appeal against confiscation orders.
Procedure for taking cognizance of offences.
administration: Government of Kerala, Collector, Authorised Officers, Local Level Monitoring Committee, State Level Committee, District Level Authorised Committee.
important_notes: Section 3A, inserted by Act 12 of 2015, provides for the regularization of paddy land conversion/reclamation made before the commencement of the Act.
Received the assent of the Governor on the 11th August, 2008 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 1790 dated 12th August, 2008.
The Act aims to sustain the ecological system in the State of Kerala.
In case of intermediary crops, the cultivation must be in an interchangeable manner according to the ecological nature of the paddy land.
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected.

title: The Kerala Conservation of Paddy Land and Wetland (Amendment) Act, 2011
purpose: To amend the Kerala Conservation of Paddy Land and Wetland Act, 2008.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala. It amends the Principal Act of 2008.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Conservation of Paddy Land and Wetland (Amendment) Act, 2011, and it shall come into force on the 12th day of August, 2008.

Amends section 12 of the Kerala Conservation of Paddy Land and Wetland Act, 2008. It substitutes specific phrases in sub-section (1) and (5) of section 12. Specifically, in sub-section (1), it replaces 'not below the rank of Revenue Divisional Officer' with 'not below the rank of Village Officer'. In sub-section (5), it deals with the consequences of an officer authorised under sub-section (1) failing to take action on a report received by him regarding a violation of the Act.
Amends section 13 of the principal Act by substituting phrases related to 'any paddy land' and 'the said paddy land' with 'any paddy land' and 'the said paddy land or wetland' respectively.
Amends section 19 in sub-section (1) of the principal Act, by substituting the words 'of a Revenue Divisional Officer' with 'of Village Officer'.

Deals with the validation of anything done or omitted to be done under the Kerala Conservation of Paddy Land and Wetland (Amendment) Ordinance, 2011, notwithstanding the cessation of its operation. It clarifies that actions taken under the Ordinance are deemed to have been done or taken under the provisions of the principal Act as amended by this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly detailed in this amendment, but likely relates to authorities established under the principal Act of 2008.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Implied through the amendments to sections regarding officer responsibilities and the application of the Act.

administration: Law (Legislation-B) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The amendment is in pursuance of clause (3) of Article 348 of the Constitution of India.
The English translation of the Act is published in the Gazette.
The Act refers to 'The Kerala Conservation of Paddy Land and Wetland Act, 2008' as the 'principal Act'.

title: The Kerala Construction Workers Welfare Fund Act, 1989
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a welfare fund for the construction workers in the State of Kerala and for the regulation and utilization of such fund for the benefit of construction workers.
scope: This Act applies to construction workers in the State of Kerala. The definition of 'construction worker' is elaborated in Section 2.

key_definitions.construction worker: A person who is employed directly or indirectly, through a contractor or otherwise, in connection with any construction work, and includes any such person who is in casual employment, but does not include an officer or employee of the Central Government or the State Government or any local authority or a person employed in clerical or supervisory capacity.
key_definitions.construction work: Includes any work relating to the construction, alteration, repair, maintenance or demolition of any building, bridge, road, railway, dam, canal, power project, or any other construction project.
key_definitions.fund: The Kerala Construction Workers Welfare Fund constituted under this Act.
key_definitions.employer: Any person who employs construction workers.

main_sections.description: Establishes the Kerala Construction Workers Welfare Fund.
Outlines the purposes for which the fund can be utilized, including providing financial assistance, education, medical facilities, housing, and other welfare measures to construction workers.
Specifies the sources of contributions to the fund, which include contributions from employers, government grants, and other sources.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and Duties of the Board
main_sections.description: Details the responsibilities of the Board constituted to administer the fund, including managing the fund, investing it, and implementing welfare schemes.
Empowers the Board to make regulations consistent with the Act for the administration of the fund and the welfare of construction workers.
Specifies the penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act.
Deals with the procedure for taking cognizance of offences under the Act.
Grants the Government the power to exempt any person or class of persons from the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the Government to remove any difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the Government to make orders for carrying into effect the provisions of the Act.
Repeals previous enactments and provides for savings.

important_rules: Employers are required to contribute to the fund.
The fund is to be utilized for the welfare of construction workers.
The Board is responsible for the proper management and utilization of the fund.

penalties: Imprisonment which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both, for contravention of certain provisions (Section 20).
Fine for failure to comply with directions from the Board.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Board constituted under the Act, and the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through penalties, prosecution for offences, and government oversight and rule-making powers.

rights: Construction workers have the right to receive benefits from the welfare fund.
Construction workers have the right to access medical, educational, and housing facilities provided by the fund.
duties: Employers have the duty to contribute to the welfare fund.
Employers have the duty to comply with the provisions of the Act and the rules made thereunder.
obligations: The Board has the obligation to manage the fund efficiently and utilize it for the welfare of construction workers.

key_procedures: Collection of contributions from employers.
Disbursement of benefits to construction workers as per schemes framed by the Board.
Investment of surplus funds.
Maintenance of accounts and audit.
administration: The Act is administered by the Board constituted under Section 15 and overseen by the State Government.
important_notes: The definition of 'construction worker' and 'construction work' are crucial for determining applicability.
The Act empowers the government to make rules and the Board to make regulations to further the objectives of the Act.
The Act provides for the removal of difficulties in its implementation.

title: The Kerala Contingency Fund (Amendment) Act, 1972
purpose: To amend the Kerala Contingency Fund Act, 1957.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Contingency Fund Act, 1957.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Contingency Fund (Amendment) Act, 1972. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 28th day of August, 1972.

In sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Kerala Contingency Fund Act, 1957 (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), for the words "one hundred and fifty lakhs of rupees", the words "three hundred lakhs of rupees" shall be substituted.

The Kerala General Sales-tax (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1972 (3 of 1972) is hereby repealed. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Substitution of "three hundred lakhs of rupees" for "one hundred and fifty lakhs of rupees" in Section 2(1) of the principal Act.
The Kerala General Sales-tax (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1972 is repealed.
Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are deemed to have been taken under the amended principal Act.
key_procedures: The Act comes into force on August 28, 1972.
Amendment of Section 2 of the principal Act involves substituting financial figures.
administration: The Kerala Contingency Fund Act, 1957 is being amended, suggesting administration by the Finance Department or equivalent in the Kerala Government.
important_notes: The amendment comes into force retrospectively from August 28, 1972.
The Kerala General Sales-tax (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1972 is being repealed.
Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are protected.

title: The Kerala Contingency Fund (Amendment) Act, 1978
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Contingency Fund Act, 1957, for the purpose hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Contingency Fund (Amendment) Act, 1978, and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 9th day of January, 1978.
Amends sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Kerala Contingency Fund Act, 1957. It substitutes the words "three hundred lakhs of rupees" with "five hundred lakhs of rupees".

Repeals the Kerala Contingency Fund Ordinance, 1978 (2 of 1978). It also states that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 1st day of March, 1978, and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 148 dated 3rd March, 1978.

title: The Kerala Contingency Fund (Amendment) Act, 1979
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Contingency Fund Act, 1957.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala. The amendments pertain to the Kerala Contingency Fund.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Contingency Fund (Amendment) Act, 1979, and it came into force on the 17th day of November 1978.
This section amends sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Kerala Contingency Fund Act, 1957 (6 of 1957). The words 'eight hundred lakhs of rupees' are substituted with 'five hundred lakhs of rupees'.

This section repeals the Kerala Contingency Fund (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1978 (28 of 1978). It also includes a saving clause stating that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_notes: The Act was received the assent of the Governor on the 21st March, 1979 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 212, dated 28th March, 1979.
