title: THE KERALA CONTINGENCY FUND (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1983
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Contingency Fund Act, 1957, for the purpose hereinafter appearing.
scope: The Act applies to Kerala and amends the Kerala Contingency Fund Act, 1957.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Contingency Fund (Amendment) Act, 1983, and it shall come into force at once.
Amends sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Kerala Contingency Fund Act, 1957, by substituting the words "fifteen crores of rupees" for the words "eight hundred lakhs of rupees".

administration: Likely the Finance Department of the Kerala State Government, based on the nature of the Act.
important_notes: The Act was received the assent of the Governor on the 12th day of August, 1983, and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 893 dated the 17th August, 1983.

title: The Kerala Contingency Fund Act, 1957
purpose: To provide for the establishment and maintenance of a Contingency Fund for the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala. The act establishes a fund to meet unforeseen expenditure pending authorization by the State Legislature.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Contingency Fund Act, 1957. It shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of the Contingency Fund of Kerala
main_sections.description: Establishes a Contingency Fund in the nature of an imprest, entitled "The Contingency Fund of Kerala", consisting of a sum of fifty lakhs of rupees withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala. This fund shall be held on behalf of the Governor of Kerala by the Secretary to the Government of Kerala in the Department of Finance. The Governor shall have authority to make advances therefrom for the purpose of meeting any unforeseen expenditure pending authorization by the State Legislature by law under Article 205 or Article 206 of the Constitution. As often as any such expenditure is authorised by law as aforesaid, the Government shall recoup to the Contingency Fund an amount equal to the advance taken from such Fund to meet the expenditure.

For the purpose of carrying out the object of this Act, the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make rules regulating all matters connected with or ancillary to the custody of, the payment of moneys into and the withdrawal of moneys from, the contingency Fund of the State of Kerala.
The Contingency Fund Act, 1950 (Act XXXII of 1950), is hereby repealed.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through rules made by the Government under Section 3.

rights: The Governor has the authority to make advances from the Contingency Fund for unforeseen expenditure pending legislative authorization.
duties: The Government shall recoup the Contingency Fund for advances made.

key_procedures: Expenditure from the Contingency Fund for unforeseen purposes requires an advance by the Governor (through the Secretary, Finance Department).
Subsequent authorization by the State Legislature is required for such expenditure.
The Contingency Fund must be recouped with the amount advanced once the expenditure is authorized.
administration: Department of Finance, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The initial corpus of the fund is fifty lakhs of rupees.
The act repeals the Contingency Fund Act, 1950.

title: THE KERALA CONTROL OF POISON CONTAMINATED ARTICLES (VALIDATION) ACT, 1958
purpose: To validate orders issued and action taken to prevent danger to life and health by consumption of articles contaminated with poisonous substances and to provide for certain matters connected therewith.
scope: Extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. Applies to the validation of orders, directions and actions for preventing danger to life and health by consumption of articles contaminated with poisonous substances.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as 'The Kerala Control of Poison Contaminated Articles (Validation) Act, 1958' and states its extent and commencement.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of orders, directions and actions for preventing danger to life and health by consumption of articles contaminated with poisonous substances.
main_sections.description: This section deals with the validation of orders, directions, and actions taken by the Government, including authorising officers of the Government to: (i) inspect shops, godowns, hotels, restaurants and other places where articles of food and cattle fodder are stored; (ii) take samples of food and cattle fodder; (iii) analyse and test samples; (iv) freeze and prohibit movement, sale and disposal of contaminated articles; (v) direct the surrender of said articles. It also validates orders issued by the District Collectors and other officers, and actions taken in pursuance of these orders and directions.

main_sections.section_title: Compensation for articles taken over or surrendered.
main_sections.description: Provides for compensation for articles of food or cattle fodder surrendered to the Government, especially those taken over on or before May 22, 1958, or transported along with or stored in contact with such articles. Compensation is to be paid based on the price paid for the article, including insurance and transport charges. It also addresses situations where articles were destroyed, and outlines how payment should be determined by the Revenue Divisional Officer or Inspecting Assistant Commissioner.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
main_sections.description: No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against any person for anything done or intended to be done in pursuance of any order or direction referred to in section 2.
Repeals the Kerala Control of Poison Contaminated Articles (Validation) Ordinance, 1958. Saves anything done or any liability incurred under the said Ordinance.

important_rules: Orders, directions, and actions taken to prevent danger from poisonous contaminated articles are validated.
Government or its authorised officers can inspect, sample, test, freeze, prohibit, and direct surrender of contaminated articles.
Compensation is payable for articles taken over or surrendered, based on purchase price and related charges.
No legal action can be taken against individuals acting in good faith under the provisions of section 2.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government, Authorising officers of the Government, District Collectors and other officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspection, sampling, testing, freezing, prohibition of movement/sale/disposal, directing surrender of articles, and by issuing orders and directions.

rights: Right to compensation for articles taken over or surrendered.
Right to have compensation amount determined by Revenue Divisional Officer or Inspecting Assistant Commissioner.
duties: Duty to surrender contaminated articles when directed.
Duty to comply with orders and directions issued under the Act.
obligations: Obligation to pay compensation for articles taken over or surrendered.

key_procedures: Validation of orders, directions, and actions taken by the Government and its officers for public health and safety concerning poisonous contaminated articles.
Process for inspecting, sampling, testing, and controlling contaminated articles.
Procedure for determining and paying compensation for surrendered or taken-over articles.
administration: The Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act serves to validate actions already taken, indicating a retroactive effect for specific purposes.
Compensation is to be paid to the person who surrendered or from whom the article was taken, at the price at which it was purchased.
Any payment made before the commencement of the Act towards compensation shall be taken into account.

title: THE KERALA CORNEAL GRAFTING ACT, 1963
purpose: To make provision with respect to the use of the eyes of deceased persons for therapeutic purposes in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala. The act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and may, by notification in the Gazette, be brought into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

key_definitions.approved institution: means an institution specified in the Schedule and includes any other institution declared by the Government by notification in the Gazette, to be an approved institution for the purposes of this Act.
key_definitions.near relative: means any of the following relatives of the deceased, namely, a wife, husband, parent, son, daughter, brother or sister and includes any other person who is related to the deceased (i) by lineal consanguinity within three degrees or by collateral consanguinity within six degrees or (ii) by marriage with any of the relatives aforesaid.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Corneal Grafting Act, 1963. (1) It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. (3) It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Defines terms used in the Act, including 'approved institution' and 'near relative'.

main_sections.section_title: Removal of the eyes of deceased persons.
main_sections.description: Outlines the conditions and procedures for the removal of eyes from deceased persons for therapeutic purposes. This includes specifying who can authorize the removal, the requirement of a request, and the conditions under which a request can be made or withdrawn. It also states that no authority shall be given for the removal of eyes from a deceased person by any person who has been entrusted with the body solely for the purpose of its interment, cremation or disposal.

The Government may, by notification in the gazette, make such rules as may be necessary for carrying out the purposes of this Act. Every rule made under this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before the Legislative Assembly while it is in session for a total period of fourteen days which may be comprised in one session or in two successive sessions, and if, before the expiry of the sessions in which it is so laid, or the session immediately following, the Legislative Assembly makes any modification in the rule or decides that the rule should not be made, the rule shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect, as the case may be; so however that any such modification or annulment shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that rule.

important_rules: Rule: Any person, if either in writing at any time or orally in the presence of two or more persons during his last illness, has expressed an unequivocal request that his eye or eyes be used for therapeutic purposes after his death, the party lawfully in possession of his body after his death may, unless the said party has reason to believe that the request was subsequently withdrawn, authorise the removal of the eye or eyes from the body for use for those purposes.

Rule: Without prejudice to sub-section (1), the party lawfully in possession of the body of a deceased person may authorise the removal of the eye or eyes from the body for the purposes aforesaid unless that party has reason to believe :- (a) that the deceased had expressed an objection to his eye or eyes being so dealt with after his death, and had not withdrawn it; or (b) that the surviving spouse or any near relative of the deceased objects to the eye or eyes of the deceased being so dealt with.

Rule: An authority given under this Act in respect of any deceased person shall be sufficient warrant for the removal of the eye or eyes from the body and its or their use for the purposes aforesaid ; but no such removal shall be effected except by a medical officer possessing the prescribed qualifications and attached to, or employed in, an approved institution, who must have satisfied himself by a personal examination of the body that life is extinct and the eye or eyes shall after such removal be handed over by such medical officer to the nearest approved institution.

Rule: No authority for the removal of the eye or eyes under this Act shall be given by the party empowered to give such authority, he having reason to believe that an inquest may be required to be held on the body.

Rule: Any person who, knowing or having reason to believe that an inquest may be required to be held over a dead body, gives, or allows the giving of any authority under this Act, shall on conviction before a Magistrate be liable to fine which may extend to two hundred rupees.

Rule: No authority shall be given under this Act in respect of the body of a deceased person by any person who has been entrusted with the body solely for the purpose of its interment, burial, cremation or disposal otherwise.

penalties: Fine up to two hundred rupees for giving authority for removal of eyes when an inquest may be required on the dead body.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Magistrate
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Conviction before a Magistrate.

rights: Right of a deceased person to request the use of his eyes for therapeutic purposes.
Right of the party lawfully in possession of a deceased person's body to authorize eye removal based on the deceased's request.
Right of an authority given under this Act to be a sufficient warrant for the removal and use of eyes for therapeutic purposes.
duties: Duty of the medical officer to satisfy himself by personal examination that life is extinct before removal of eyes.
Duty of the medical officer to hand over removed eyes to the nearest approved institution.
obligations: Obligation to not authorize eye removal if there is reason to believe an inquest may be required.

key_procedures: Procedure for authorization of eye removal from a deceased person based on their prior request, with conditions and exceptions.
Procedure for medical examination and handover of removed eyes to an approved institution.
Procedure for making rules and their laying before the Legislative Assembly for modification or annulment.
administration: The Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act came into force on the 15th March 1963 as per notification in the Gazette Extraordinary, dated 16th March, 1963.
The rules made under this Act are subject to modification or annulment by the Legislative Assembly.
The Act does not apply to the removal of eyes from a body entrusted solely for interment, burial, cremation, or disposal.

title: The Kerala Corneal Grafting (Amendment) Act, 1988
purpose: To amend the Kerala Corneal Grafting Act, 1963, for the purpose hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Corneal Grafting (Amendment) Act, 1988, and it shall come into force at once.

Inserts a new sub-section (6A) to section 3 of the Kerala Corneal Grafting Act, 1963. This new sub-section deals with the authority to remove eyes from a dead body for medico-legal or pathological purposes, under specific conditions and with regard to the deceased's expressed wishes or lack thereof.

important_rules: The cornea may be removed from a dead body for medico-legal purposes if the death was not caused by accident or any other unnatural cause.
The cornea may be removed from a dead body for pathological purposes.

Authority for removal of eyes from a dead body requires satisfaction that the deceased had not expressed any objection to his eyes being used for therapeutic purposes after his death, or where he had granted authority for the use of his eyes for therapeutic purposes before his death, and this authority had not been revoked.
The authority for removal of eyes can be granted by the competent authority under the Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Competent authority under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions and procedures outlined in the Act.

key_procedures: To obtain authority for the removal of eyes from a dead body for medico-legal or pathological purposes, the competent authority must be satisfied regarding the deceased's wishes and the circumstances of death.
administration: Law (Legislation-C) Department, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Preamble indicates the Act is intended to amend the Kerala Corneal Grafting Act, 1963.
The amendment comes into force immediately upon enactment.
The insertion of sub-section (6A) to section 3 provides specific conditions for eye removal from deceased persons.

title: THE KERALA COURT-FEES AND SUITS VALUATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1969
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Court-Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1959.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala, specifically amending the Court-Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1959.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Court-Fees and Suits Valuation (Amendment) Act, 1969. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

Amends Schedule II to the Kerala Court-Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1959. Specifically, in entries relating to Article 11, under item (v), after the words "Corporation of Trivandrum", the words "or the Corporation of Calicut" shall be inserted. Also, after sub-item (iv), a new sub-item (v) is inserted regarding election petitions presented to the High Court under section 80A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, with a court fee of two hundred and fifty rupees.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala (through notification in the Gazette)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By notification in the Gazette to appoint the commencement date.

key_procedures: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Government through a Gazette notification.
Specific amendments are made to Schedule II of the Principal Act concerning court fees for election petitions.
administration: Implied to be the relevant department or authority responsible for court fees and valuation in the State of Kerala.
important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 75, dated 26th March, 1969.

title: The Kerala Court Fees and Suits Valuation (Amendment) Act, 2003
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1959.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala, amending provisions related to court fees and suits valuation as specified in the original Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Court Fees and Suits Valuation (Amendment) Act, 2003 and shall come into force on the 26th day of October, 2002.

Inserts a new section 52A to the principal Act, which deals with the fee payable on a Memorandum of Appeal filed before the High Court against the order of Income Tax Appellate Tribunal or the Wealth Tax Appellate Tribunal, under the Income Tax Act, 1961, or the Central Act of 1961 or the Wealth Tax Act, 1957.
Amends section 72 of the principal Act, with the entries relating thereto to be omitted.
Inserts a new section 73A to the principal Act, detailing special provisions regarding charges, appeals, revision, etc., before any Court.
Amends section 81 of the principal Act, concerning deductions to be made when allowance is made in the Act for damaged or spoiled stamps, and where Court orders refund of fees to any person.
Amends section 83 of the principal Act, specifically in relation to the words 'High Court' and 'appellate jurisdiction'.

Amends Schedule I of the principal Act by substituting 'Four rupees' for 'Two rupees' in various places within the Schedule, and also making other specific textual substitutions for different fee amounts.

Amends Schedule II of the principal Act by making extensive substitutions of monetary values and phrases throughout the schedule, including specific amendments to Article 3 and other sub-items and clauses.
Repeals the Kerala Court Fees and Suits Valuation (Amendment) Ordinance, 2003.

administration: Not explicitly stated, but likely the Revenue Department or the Judiciary of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on 6th March, 2003 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 386 dated 6th March, 2003.

title: THE KERALA COURT-FEES AND SUITS VALUATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1972
purpose: To amend the Kerala Court-Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1959, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala. It concerns the court fees and valuation of suits and appeals within the jurisdiction of the Kerala courts.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Court-Fees and Suits Valuation (Amendment) Act, 1972. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Inserts a new section 74A into the Kerala Court-Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1959, dealing with special provisions regarding certain appeals.
Amends Schedule I of the principal Act by substituting 'forty paise' for 'Thirty-seven paise' and 'eighty paise' for 'seventy-five paise'.
Amends Schedule II of the principal Act, including changes to currency amounts and the designation of civic authorities.

important_rules: Rule 1: Court fees for appeals in specific circumstances (e.g., against a decree in a suit referred to in section 74, or for decrees in suits instituted by members of Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes with limited income) are subject to special provisions.

Rule 2: The court shall not admit a memorandum of appeal if the court fee payable under the Act is not paid, except under specific conditions related to the Collector of the district or the suit being dismissed.
Rule 3: The Government may recover court fees from the party that caused the appeal.
Rule 4: When an order is made under section 74A, a copy shall be forwarded to the Collector of the district who may recover the court-fees specified therein.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Collector of the district, and the Government are involved in the enforcement and recovery of court fees.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By requiring payment of court fees, admitting or not admitting appeals based on fee payment, and recovering fees through the Collector.

rights: The Government has the right to apply to the court to make an order for the payment of court fees.
The appellant has the right to appeal, subject to payment of court fees or specific exemptions.
duties: The appellant has a duty to pay the court fees required for an appeal.
obligations: Obligation to pay court fees as prescribed by the Act and its schedules.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Filing an appeal requires payment of court fees. If court fees are not paid, the memorandum of appeal may not be admitted, unless exceptions apply and the Collector is required to pay the fee.
Procedure 2: The Government can direct the Collector to recover unpaid court fees.
administration: The Government of Kerala (through notifications and potential directions to the Collector).
important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No 179, dated 20th March, 1972.
Section 74A provides special provisions for certain appeals, particularly concerning the financial limitations of appellants.
Amendments to Schedules I and II adjust the monetary values of court fees.

title: THE KERALA COURT-FEES AND SUITS VALUATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1966
purpose: To amend the Kerala Court-Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1959, and to make further provisions related to court fees and suits valuation in Kerala.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and governs court fees and valuation of suits within its jurisdiction.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act as the Kerala Court-Fees and Suits Valuation (Amendment) Act, 1966, and specifies its commencement date as the date of its publication in the Gazette.
This section amends Section 81 of the principal Act (Kerala Court-Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1959). It replaces the words "seven paise" with "naye paise" and "seven rupees" with "naye rupees".

This section amends Schedule I of the principal Act. It modifies the wording related to court fees for amounts exceeding a certain value, specifying fees in "naye paise" and "rupees" instead of the older currency terms.

This section amends Schedule II of the principal Act. It makes changes to the entries relating to court fees, substituting "naye paise" and "rupees" for the older denominations. It also makes specific substitutions for entries related to "One rupee and fifty naye paise", "Two rupees", "Three rupees", and "Five rupees".
This section amends Schedule III of the principal Act by substituting the word "paise" with "nP" wherever it occurs.

important_rules: Rule: Court fees and suit valuations shall be calculated in "naye paise" and "rupees" as specified in the amended schedules.
Rule: The Act shall come into force on such date as the Government may notify in the Gazette.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala (implied through notification power)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application of the amended court fees and valuation rules in legal proceedings.

duties: Duty: Litigants have a duty to pay the court fees and follow the valuation rules as amended by this Act.

key_procedures: Procedure: To ascertain the correct court fee payable for a suit or application based on the valuation, as detailed in the amended Schedules I, II, and III.
Procedure: For the Government to bring the Act into force by publishing a notification in the Gazette.
administration: The judiciary and administrative bodies responsible for the collection of court fees in Kerala.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the principal Act of 1959.
The amendments introduced by this Act are to be read in conjunction with the principal Act.
Specific currency conversions and substitutions are detailed in the amendments to Schedules I and II.
Published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 84, dated 12th September, 1966.

title: The Kerala Court Of Wards Act, 1967
purpose: To provide for the superintendence and management of the property of disqualified proprietors, and for matters connected therewith. The Act aims to protect the interests of the ward and his family, and also creditors and the public revenue, by ensuring proper management of estates and preventing their deterioration.
scope: The Act applies to the superintendence and management of the property of disqualified proprietors in the State of Kerala. It covers the management of estates, collection of rents, liquidation of debts, and the release of property from superintendence.

key_definitions.ward: A disqualified proprietor whose property is under the superintendence of the Court of Wards.
key_definitions.property: Includes immoveable property, stock or shares, debentures, and other moveable property belonging to the ward.

main_sections.section_title: Surplus how to be dealt with
main_sections.description: Deals with the disposal of surplus income from the ward's property, including investments in securities guaranteed by the Government of India or local authorities, or in immoveable property.
Outlines the restrictions on a ward's ability to transfer or create any charge or interest in his property, subject to superintendence of the court.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of court as to property under its superintendence
main_sections.description: Grants the Court of Wards extensive powers to manage the ward's property, including the power to mortgage or sell the whole or any part of the property, and to lease it out.
Empowers the court to establish necessary establishments and incur charges for the management of persons and properties under its superintendence, to be borne by the properties.
Lays down the procedure for notifying claims against the ward and the process of their ascertainment and settlement by the Collector.

main_sections.section_title: Claimants to furnish full particulars and documents
main_sections.description: Requires claimants to furnish full particulars and documents to the Collector within a prescribed period for the verification of their claims.

main_sections.section_title: Pecuniary claim of Government, etc., not affected
main_sections.description: Clarifies that pecuniary claims of the Government or local authorities are not affected by certain provisions of the Act.
Details the Collector's role in admitting or disallowing claims and the process of informing the claimants.

main_sections.section_title: Claims not notified cease to carry interest, etc.
main_sections.description: Stipulates that claims not notified within the prescribed period or not admitted by the Collector will cease to carry interest and cannot be enforced against the ward's property.

main_sections.section_title: Inadmissibility in evidence of documents not produced
main_sections.description: States that documents not produced before the Collector under the control of the ward's property cannot be admitted as evidence.

main_sections.section_title: When mortgage in possession of a mortgagee.
main_sections.description: Governs the situation when a mortgaged property is in the possession of a mortgagee, and the Government's rights in such property.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
main_sections.description: Protects suits brought in good faith against the Government, the Court of Wards, or any public servant or person duly appointed or authorised under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Suit not to be instituted until after notice to Collector.
main_sections.description: Prohibits the institution of suits relating to the property of a ward without first giving notice to the Collector.

main_sections.section_title: Suit or proceeding by or against ward.
main_sections.description: Details the procedure for suits and proceedings by or against a ward, including the requirement of appointing a manager or next friend.
Addresses the payment of costs incurred in suits or proceedings against a manager or other officer competent to act as manager under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Suits must be authorised by court.
main_sections.description: Requires suits to be brought only with the authorization of the Court of Wards, unless by the manager or other officer competent to act as manager.

main_sections.section_title: Adjudication of civil disputes between two or more wards.
main_sections.description: Provides for the adjudication of civil disputes between two or more wards by the civil court, with the Collector's involvement.
Outlines the circumstances under which the Government may release persons and property from superintendence, including when the ward is no longer disqualified.

main_sections.section_title: Release of estate under section 17 when debts cannot be liquidated within reasonable time.
main_sections.description: Deals with the release of an estate from superintendence under section 17 if debts cannot be liquidated within a reasonable time, with provisions for notification and government sanction.

main_sections.section_title: When estate taken under management section 17 may be over to proprietor.
main_sections.description: Specifies the conditions under which an estate taken under management may be returned to the proprietor, if debts have been discharged and liabilities are met.

important_rules: A ward cannot transfer or create any charge or interest in his property without the consent of the Court of Wards (Section 33).
Claims against the ward's property must be notified to the Collector within a specified period (Section 36).
Documents not produced before the Collector cannot be used as evidence (Section 41).
Suits relating to the ward's property require prior notice to the Collector (Section 44).
Encumbrances on the ward's property are subject to the terms of the instrument and may be affected by superintendence (Section 42, 50).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Court of Wards, the Collector, and civil courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings, sale or mortgage of property, appointment of managers, and adjudication of disputes.

rights: Right of the ward to have his property managed for his benefit.
Right of creditors to have their claims considered and settled.
Right of the Government to recover revenue and taxes.
duties: Duty of the Court of Wards to manage the property judiciously.
Duty of the Collector to ascertain and settle debts.
Duty of claimants to provide necessary documentation.
obligations: Obligation of the ward to comply with the orders of the Court of Wards regarding his property.
Obligation to notify claims within the prescribed period.

key_procedures: Procedure for ascertainment and settlement of debts (Section 36-41).
Procedure for release of property from superintendence (Section 49-51).
Procedure for adjudication of civil disputes involving wards (Section 48).
administration: The Court of Wards and the Collector.
important_notes: The Act aims to protect the ward's property from mismanagement and dissipation.
The Government has significant powers under the Act to manage estates and recover dues.
Provisions exist for the release of property once the ward is no longer disqualified or debts are settled.

title: THE KERALA COURT-FEES AND SUITS VALUATION (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 1976
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Court-fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1959.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala and relates to court fees and suits valuation.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Court-fees and Suits Valuation (Second Amendment) Act, 1976. It also specifies that it shall come into force on such date as the Government may by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

Inserts a new section, 78A, titled 'Writing name or initials on or across the stamp'. This section specifies that whoever affixes any adhesive stamp under this Act shall, at the time of affixing such stamp, write on or across the stamp his name or initials or the name or initials of his firm with the true date of his so writing so that it cannot be used again. It also states that any document bearing an adhesive stamp which does not bear the name or initials of the person who affixes the stamp or of his firm, as required by sub-section (1), so that it cannot be used again, shall, so far as such stamp is concerned, be deemed to be unstamped.

Amends section 80 of the principal Act by adding a proviso. The proviso states that in the case of an adhesive stamp, no such cancellation shall have effect unless it bears the name or initials of the person who affixes the stamp or of his firm, as required by sub-section (1) of section 78A.

important_rules: Rule 1: Any adhesive stamp affixed under this Act must have the name or initials of the user and the date written on or across it, making it impossible to reuse.
Rule 2: Documents with adhesive stamps lacking the required name, initials, or date will be considered unstamped.
Rule 3: The cancellation of an adhesive stamp is only valid if it includes the name, initials, and date as required by section 78A(1).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications in the Gazette and amendment of existing acts.

duties: Duty to write name or initials and date on adhesive stamps affixed under the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Government notification in the Gazette to bring the Act into force.
Procedure 2: Affixing adhesive stamps and writing name/initials and date on them.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but likely the Kerala State Government or its relevant departments dealing with finance and legal matters.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 19th day of November, 1976 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 657, dated 30th November, 1976.

title: The Kerala Court-Fees And Suits Valuation (Amendment) Act, 1991
purpose: To amend the Kerala Court-Fees And Suits Valuation Act, 1959, for the purposes appearing therein.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Court-Fees and Suits Valuation (Amendment) Act, 1991. It came into force on the 5th day of December, 1990.

Inserts section 4A titled 'Levy of fee at the time of institution of suit'. It stipulates that the amount of fee to be paid on plaint at the time of institution of suit shall be one-tenth of the amount of fee chargeable under this Act. It also provides for extensions of time for payment of fees under certain conditions.
Amends section 7 by substituting 'market value of land' with 'market value of agricultural land'.
Amends section 25 by substituting monetary values (rupees three hundred, rupees one thousand, rupees four hundred) with new values.
Amends section 26 regarding fees in Munsiff's Court and Sub-Court or District Court based on market value of property and relief.
Amends section 27 by substituting monetary values (rupees one hundred and fifty, rupees two hundred) with new values.
Amends section 30 by substituting monetary values (rupees three hundred) with 'rupees one thousand'.
Amends section 31 by substituting monetary values (rupees three hundred) with 'rupees one thousand'.
Amends section 35 by substituting monetary values (rupees three hundred) with 'rupees one thousand'.
Amends section 37 by substituting monetary values (Rupees twenty) with 'Rupees fifty' and adding specific provisions for Sub-Court or District Court.
Amends section 45 by substituting monetary values (rupees three hundred) with 'rupees one thousand'.
Amends section 50 regarding fees in Revenue Court, Munsiff's Court, and Sub-Court or District Court based on monetary value and subject matter.
Amends section 52 by adding a proviso regarding the payment of fees in appeals and extension of time for such payment.
Amends section 69 by adding a proviso regarding the refund of fees.

Amends section 72 by inserting new items related to petitions under specific acts (Native Converts Marriage Dissolution Act, Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, Indian Divorce Act, Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act, Hindu Marriage Act, Indian Divorce Act, Constitution).

Amends section 74 by substituting clauses related to suits instituted by members of Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe and income thresholds. Also amends clauses related to monthly income and annual income thresholds.

Amends Schedule I with new fee structures based on monetary value and specific provisions for articles and entries related to probate and letters of administration, and certificates under the Indian Succession Act.
This section is mentioned in the contents but not fully detailed in the provided images.
This section is mentioned in the contents but not detailed in the provided images.

important_rules: Rule: Fee at the time of institution of suit is one-tenth of the chargeable fee.
Rule: Extensions for fee payment may be granted for up to thirty days.
Rule: Fees for certain suits are specified based on market value and relief sought.
Rule: Specific monetary thresholds are defined for various types of suits and petitions.
Rule: Fees are prescribed for probate and letters of administration based on the value of the estate.
Rule: Fees are prescribed for certificates under the Indian Succession Act based on the value of debt or security.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts in Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the levying and payment of court fees as prescribed by the Act.

rights: Right to claim extensions for fee payment under certain circumstances.
duties: Duty to pay court fees at the time of institution of suits.
Duty to comply with the fee structures prescribed in Schedule I and II.
Duty to adhere to the monetary limits and conditions specified for different types of suits.
obligations: Obligation to pay the correct court fee for initiating legal proceedings.

key_procedures: Procedure: Determine the appropriate court fee based on the nature of the suit, relief sought, and value of the subject matter as per the Act and its Schedules.
Procedure: Pay the prescribed court fee at the time of filing the plaint or petition.
Procedure: In case of difficulty or specific circumstances, apply for an extension of time for payment of fees, not exceeding fifteen days initially, and possibly extendable by the court.
Procedure: For appeals and other proceedings, follow the fee payment rules outlined in the Act and Schedules.
administration: Not explicitly stated in the provided sections, but likely the Revenue Department and the Judiciary of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act came into force retrospectively from December 5, 1990.
Specific monetary values in existing sections have been amended.
New categories of suits and petitions have been included for fee calculation.
The 'Explanation' under clause (vi) of section 74 has been omitted.
The Act specifies fee structures for various types of suits, including those involving recovery of compensation, suits by associations, and suits by persons serving in armed forces.

title: The Kerala Court-Fees and Suits Valuation (Amendment) Act, 2016
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Court-Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1959.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Court-Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1959.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Court-Fees and Suits Valuation (Amendment) Act, 2016. It shall come into force at once.

Amends sub-section (3) of section 76 of the Kerala Court-Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1959. It specifies the amounts to be set apart every year towards the Legal Benefit Fund constituted under section 3 of the Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund Act, 1980 and towards the Legal Benefit Fund collected under section 3 of the Kerala Advocates' Clerks Welfare Fund Act, 2003. It also specifies that any remaining amount after retaining an amount equal to ten percent for providing infrastructure to the litigants shall be transferred to such Funds.

important_rules: Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, an amount equal to seventy percent of the Legal Benefit Fund collected under sub-section (2) shall be set apart every year towards the Fund constituted under section 3 of the Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund Act, 1980.
An amount equal to thirty percent of the Legal Benefit Fund collected shall be set apart towards the Fund constituted under section 3 of the Kerala Advocates' Clerks Welfare Fund Act, 2003.
Provided that the amount so set apart shall be transferred to such Funds after retaining an amount equal to ten percent for providing infrastructure to the litigants.
key_procedures: Set apart seventy percent of the collected Legal Benefit Fund towards the Kerala Advocates' Welfare Fund Act, 1980.
Set apart thirty percent of the collected Legal Benefit Fund towards the Kerala Advocates' Clerks Welfare Fund Act, 2003.
Transfer remaining funds after retaining ten percent for infrastructure.
administration: Law (Legislation-C) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: This amendment is expedient for further amending the Kerala Court-Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1959.

title: The Kerala Court-fees and Suits Valuation (Amendment) Act, 1976
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Court-fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1959.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Court-fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1959.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Court-fees and Suits Valuation (Amendment) Act, 1976.

In Schedule II to the Kerala Court-fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1959 (10 of 1960), in article 10, after clause (j), the following clause shall be inserted, namely:- '(jj) (i) Application under section 8 (1) of the Kerala Private Forests (Vesting and Assignment) Act, 1971, to the Tribunal constituted under that Act Ten rupees (ii) Application to such Tribunal for an interlocutory order Three rupees'.

(1) The Kerala Court-fees and Suits Valuation (Amendment) Ordinance, 1976 (8 of 1976), is hereby repealed. (2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act, as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act as if this Act had come into force on the 23rd day of July, 1976.

key_procedures: Amendment of Schedule II of the principal Act by inserting new clauses related to applications under the Kerala Private Forests (Vesting and Assignment) Act, 1971.
Repeal of the Kerala Court-fees and Suits Valuation (Amendment) Ordinance, 1976, with a saving clause for actions taken under the Ordinance.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 19th day of November, 1976 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 659, dated 20th November, 1976.
The Act came into force on the 23rd day of July, 1976.

title: The Kerala Cultivators and Tenants (Temporary Protection) Act, 1970
purpose: To provide for the stay of suits and other proceedings for the determination of rights in respect of lands occupied by certain classes of persons, for the temporary protection of tenants against proceedings for the recovery of arrears of rent, and for matters incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. It applies to suits, proceedings, applications, and appeals related to land occupied by certain classes of persons and arrears of rent.

key_definitions.interpretation: Words and expressions used in this Act shall have the meanings respectively assigned to them in the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 (1 of 1964).

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, commencement and duration
main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, commencement date, and duration. The Act came into force at once and ceased to have effect on April 16, 1972.
Defines the interpretation of words and expressions used in the Act by referring to the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963.

main_sections.section_title: Stay of suits and other proceedings for determination of rights in respect of lands occupied by certain classes of persons
main_sections.description: Provides for the stay of suits and other proceedings concerning the determination of rights in lands occupied by certain individuals. It outlines conditions based on occupation periods and specific circumstances, such as honest belief of tenancy or occupation under a registered deed.

main_sections.section_title: Stay of suits, applications, etc., for arrears of rent
main_sections.description: Stipulates that no suit, application, or proceedings for the recovery of arrears of rent accrued before May 1, 1968, or for the execution of decrees for such arrears, shall lie. It also mandates the stay of all pending proceedings related to such arrears.
Provides for the stay of proceedings in respect of applications filed or purported to have been filed under Section 13C and sub-section (2) of Section 45A of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963.

States that the period during which suits, applications, or other proceedings were prohibited under this Act and the Kerala Stay of Recovery of Arrears of Rent Ordinance, 1970, shall be excluded in computing the period of limitation.
Exempts leases or tenancies that are already exempted from the provisions of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963, by Section 3 thereof from the purview of this Act.

Repeals the Kerala Stay of Recovery of Arrears of Rent Ordinance, 1970. It also provides that anything done or action taken under the repealed Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Rule: Suits and proceedings for determination of rights in certain occupied lands shall be stayed if a written statement is filed by the party claiming occupation under specific conditions related to the Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 1969, and dates like April 11, 1967, and April 11, 1957.

Rule: No suit, application, or proceedings for recovery of arrears of rent accrued before May 1, 1968, or for execution of decrees for such arrears, shall lie. All such pending proceedings shall be stayed.
Rule: Proceedings related to applications filed under Section 13C and sub-section (2) of Section 45A of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963, pending at the commencement of this Act, shall be stayed.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts, Land Tribunals, appellate authorities, and other designated officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the stay of suits, applications, and other proceedings as mandated by the Act.

rights: Right of tenants to temporary protection against proceedings for recovery of arrears of rent.
Right of persons occupying land under certain conditions to have suits and proceedings for determination of rights stayed.

key_procedures: Procedure: Filing of a written statement in a suit or proceeding to claim a stay based on occupation of land under specific conditions (Section 3).
Procedure: Automatic stay of suits, applications, and proceedings related to arrears of rent accrued before May 1, 1968 (Section 4).
Procedure: Stay of certain applications filed under the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 (Section 5).
administration: The Act is administered through the judicial and quasi-judicial mechanisms of the State, including courts and Land Tribunals, as guided by the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963.
important_notes: The Act is a temporary measure, with a specified duration of effect.
The Act includes provisions for computing limitation periods by excluding the time during which proceedings were prohibited.
The Act does not apply to leases or tenancies exempted under Section 3 of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963.
The repeal of the Kerala Stay of Recovery of Arrears of Rent Ordinance, 1970, is accompanied by a saving clause that validates actions taken under it.

title: The Kerala Cultivators and Tenants (Temporary Protection) Amendment Act, 1971
purpose: To amend the Kerala Cultivators and Tenants (Temporary Protection) Act, 1970. The preamble explicitly states that it is expedient to amend the Kerala Cultivators and Tenants (Temporary Protection) Act, 1970.
scope: The act applies to Kerala and concerns cultivators and tenants. Specifically, it amends section 75A of the Kerala University Act, 1969, and inserts a new section 2A into the principal Act (The Kerala Cultivators and Tenants (Temporary Protection) Act, 1970). The new section 2A addresses the stay of suits and other proceedings for redemption of certain mortgages, focusing on land in Kerala.

key_definitions.mortgagee: Shall include a predecessor-in-interest of the mortgagee or lessee, as the case may be.
key_definitions.lessee: Shall include a predecessor-in-interest of the mortgagee or lessee, as the case may be.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Cultivators and Tenants (Temporary Protection) Amendment Act, 1971.

In the Kerala Cultivators and Tenants (Temporary Protection) Act, 1970 (20 of 1970), in section 1, in sub-section (3), for the words, figures and letters 'the 16th day of October, 1971', the words, figures and letters 'the 16th day of April, 1972' shall be substituted.

Inserts a new section 2A into the principal Act, dealing with the stay of suits and other proceedings for redemption of certain mortgages. This section outlines conditions under which such proceedings will be stayed, particularly concerning land, including land held under mortgage.

Repeals the Kerala University (Amendment) Ordinance, 1971 (21 of 1971). It also contains a saving clause stating that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

Repeals the Kerala Cultivators and Tenants (Temporary Protection) Amendment Ordinance, 1971 (20 of 1971). Similar to section 3, it has a saving clause that actions taken under the Ordinance are deemed to have been taken under this Act, which commenced on the 15th day of October, 1971.

important_rules: Proceedings for redemption of certain mortgages on land (including land under mortgage) shall be stayed under specific conditions related to continuous possession of land by the cultivator or tenant, or building of a residential house on the land.
The stay of proceedings applies notwithstanding any decree or order of any court or authority.

The conditions for staying proceedings include continuous possession of land for at least fifty years immediately preceding January 1, 1970, or building a residential house on the land and occupying it for at least twenty years immediately preceding January 1, 1970.
The provisions related to the stay of proceedings do not apply if the party who has filed or files a statement admitting the tenant's right to the land.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Land Tribunals, courts, and appellate authorities are mentioned in relation to the stay of suits and proceedings.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the stay of suits and other proceedings for redemption of certain mortgages, as outlined in the newly inserted section 2A.

rights: Right to have suits and proceedings for redemption of certain mortgages stayed under specified conditions.

key_procedures: Filing a statement admitting the tenant's right to the land, which can prevent the application of the stay of proceedings.
The process of computing the period of fifty years and twenty years for possession and building respectively, as described in the Explanations I and II.
Application to court or Land Tribunal for stay of proceedings related to mortgage redemption under the conditions specified in section 2A.
administration: The act implies administration by the revenue and land reform departments of the Kerala Government, as it deals with land, cultivators, tenants, and mortgages.
important_notes: The Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 10, dated 4th January, 1972.
Explanation I provides rules for computing the period of continuous possession or occupation by a lessee.
Explanation II provides rules for computing the period of fifty years where the predecessor-in-interest or predecessors-in-interest of the mortgagee or lessee was or were in possession of the land.

Explanation III provides rules for computing the period of twenty years referred to in clause (b) for occupation of a building by any member of the family of the mortgagee or lessee for residential purpose.
Explanation IV clarifies that 'mortgagee' or 'lessee' shall include a predecessor-in-interest, and 'building' includes a hut.
The amendment to section 1 of the principal Act alters the date from October 16, 1971, to April 16, 1972.

title: THE KERALA CULTURAL ACTIVISTS WELFARE FUND ACT, 2010
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a Fund to grant relief to the cultural activists, to promote their welfare and to pay pension to those who engaged in various forms of art, literature and cultural activities in the State of Kerala and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to cultural activists engaged in various forms of art, literature and cultural activities in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Academy: means the Kerala State Chalachithra Academy, the Kerala Sahithya Academy, the Kerala Sangeetha Nadaka Academy, the Kerala Lalithakala Academy, the Folklore Academy and the Kerala Kalamandalam Deemed University established by the Government of Kerala
key_definitions.Board: means the Kerala Cultural Activists' Welfare Fund Board constituted under section 8
key_definitions.Contribution: means the amount payable to the Fund under section 6
key_definitions.Cultural activist: means any person engaged in any of the activities relating to the field of cinema, electronic media, cable and Direct to Home network, drama, music, kathakali, gamela, mimics, literature, painting, sculpture, folklore, ritual arts, semi classical arts, folk songs, make up, percussion arts, magic, circus, margamkali, chavittu nadakam, cartoon, poetic story presentation, recitation of Holy Books, Bible recitation, Koran recitation, Mappilakalakal, stage decoration, light and sound, costume design, art of advertising, painting, compering, photography or any person working as librarian in libraries approved by the State Library Council or any person working in connection with any such other form of art, literature, culture, cultural speech or any such other activities for their livelihood or any person who was engaged or is being engaged in such other activities as declared by Government, by notification in the Gazette, for the purposes of this Act.
key_definitions.Cultural activity: means an activity performed by a cultural activist and recognized as such by the respective Academy or Organisations or Trade or such other Body or Association approved by Government for the purposes of this Act, in which the activist is a member
key_definitions.Chalachithra Academy: means the Kerala State Chalachithra Academy established by the Government of Kerala
key_definitions.family: means wife or husband, minor sons and unmarried daughters of a cultural activist and includes in it his father mother and mentally retarded or physically handicapped or widowed daughters who are solely dependent upon him
key_definitions.Folklore Academy: means the Kerala State Folklore Academy established by the Government of Kerala
key_definitions.Fund: means the Kerala Cultural Activists' Welfare Fund constituted under the scheme as provided in section 3 of the Act
key_definitions.Kalamandalam: means the Kerala Kalamandalam Deemed University established by the Government of Kerala and approved by the University Grants Commission
key_definitions.Lalithakala Academy: means the Kerala Lalithakala Academy established by the Government of Kerala
key_definitions.member: means a member of the Fund
key_definitions.Nadaka Academy: means the Kerala Sangeetha Nadaka Academy established by the Government of Kerala
key_definitions.notification: means a notification published in the Kerala Official Gazette
key_definitions.prescribed: means prescribed by rules made under this Act
key_definitions.Sahithya Academy: means the Kerala Sahithya Academy established by the Government of Kerala
key_definitions.Scheme: means the Kerala Cultural Activists' Welfare Fund Scheme framed under section 3 of this Act
key_definitions.Schedule: means the Schedule appended to this Act
key_definitions.Secretary: means the Secretary appointed under sub-section (1) of section 13 of this Act
key_definitions.Trade body: means an Association registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 (Central Act XXI of 1860) or the Travancore-Cochin Literary, Scientific and Charitable Societies Registration Act, 1955 (12 of 1955)

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Cultural Activists' Welfare Fund Act, 2010. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including Academy, Board, Contribution, Cultural activist, Cultural activity, and others.

main_sections.description: Establishes the Kerala Cultural Activists' Welfare Fund, details its constitution, and specifies the sources of credit to the Fund.
Allows the Government to frame separate welfare schemes for different classes of cultural activists and specifies how such schemes shall be constituted and operate.
Empowers the Government to modify, add to, or omit from or vary any Scheme framed under section 3.
Specifies the contributions to be made to the Fund by various individuals and entities, including monthly contributions from cultural activists and grants from the Government.
Outlines the eligibility criteria for becoming a member of the Fund, including age requirements and contribution stipulations.
Details the constitution of the Board, its composition, appointment of Directors, and its functions to manage the Fund.

important_rules: Cultural activists engaged in specific artistic and cultural activities are eligible for benefits.
Contributions to the Fund are mandatory for certain categories of individuals and entities.
The Government has the power to frame, modify, or amend schemes related to the Fund.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government and the Board
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications in the Gazette, framing of schemes, and constitution of a Board.

rights: Cultural activists have the right to receive relief, promote their welfare, and receive pension.
Eligible cultural activists have the right to register as members.
duties: Members have a duty to contribute to the Fund as prescribed.

key_procedures: Notification by the Government to bring the Act into force.
Framing of schemes by the Government for the constitution and management of the Fund.
Constitution of the Kerala Cultural Activists' Welfare Fund Board.
Registration of cultural activists as members of the Fund.
Payment of contributions to the Fund.
Application for and disbursement of benefits (pension, financial assistance etc.).
administration: Government of Kerala (Legislation D) Department
important_notes: The Act is an English translation of the Malayalam original published under the authority of the Governor.
The Fund shall be utilized for specific purposes outlined in the Act, including pension payments, financial assistance for medical treatment, marriage, and educational purposes.
The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, revise the rate of contribution specified in sub-sections (1) and (2) once in three years.

title: The Kerala Cultural Activists Welfare Fund Act, 2010
purpose: The purpose of the Act is to provide for the establishment of a Welfare Fund for cultural activists and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. It aims to ensure the welfare of cultural activists by providing financial assistance and other benefits.
scope: The Act applies to cultural activists in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.cultural_activist: An artist, writer, journalist, folk artist, theater artist, film artist, literary critic, musician, dancer, sculptor, photographer, cartoonist, folklorist, orator, and other persons engaged in the promotion and development of culture in the State.
key_definitions.welfare_fund: The fund established under this Act for the welfare of cultural activists.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act and states that it shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint. It also specifies that the Act is applicable to the entire State of Kerala.
This section defines various terms used in the Act, including 'cultural activist', 'State Government', 'Fund', 'prescribed', 'Scheme', and 'Welfare Fund'.

This section establishes the Kerala Cultural Activists Welfare Fund and states that it shall be credited with grants from the Central Government, State Government, donations, and other sources. It also outlines the objectives for which the Fund can be utilized, such as providing financial assistance, medical aid, and pension to cultural activists.

This section deals with the management of the Welfare Fund. It states that the Fund shall be managed by a Board constituted by the Government. The Board shall consist of a Chairman and such other members as may be prescribed. It also specifies the powers and functions of the Board, including framing schemes for the utilization of the Fund.

main_sections.section_title: Schemes for the welfare of cultural activists
main_sections.description: This section empowers the Government to frame schemes for the welfare of cultural activists, including schemes for financial assistance, scholarships, medical aid, and pension. It also specifies the procedure for framing and implementing these schemes.

This section grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act. It also specifies the matters for which rules may be made, including the constitution of the Board, the terms and conditions of service of its members, and the manner in which the Fund shall be administered.

important_rules: Cultural activists must be registered with the Welfare Fund to be eligible for benefits.
The Welfare Fund shall be utilized for providing financial assistance, medical aid, pension, and other benefits to registered cultural activists.
The Board shall frame schemes for the disbursement of benefits from the Welfare Fund.
The Government shall have the power to make rules for the effective implementation of the Act.

penalties: Penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act or rules made thereunder may be imposed as prescribed.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government and the Board constituted under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the framing of schemes, rules, and by ensuring compliance with the provisions of the Act.

rights: Right to receive benefits from the Welfare Fund if registered and eligible.
Right to access healthcare and financial assistance as per the schemes.
duties: Duty to adhere to the provisions of the Act and rules.
Duty to provide accurate information for registration and availing benefits.
obligations: Cultural activists have an obligation to contribute to the cultural landscape of the state.

key_procedures: Registration of cultural activists with the Welfare Fund.
Application for benefits from the Welfare Fund.
Consideration of applications and disbursement of benefits by the Board.
administration: The Act is administered by the State Government, with the operational management of the Welfare Fund vested in a Board constituted by the Government.
important_notes: The Act aims to provide a safety net for cultural activists who may face financial hardship.
The Welfare Fund is intended to support the livelihood and well-being of those contributing to Kerala's cultural heritage.
The Act emphasizes the importance of cultural preservation and promotion through dedicated welfare measures.

title: The Kerala Dairy Farmers' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2007
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a Fund to grant relief to, to ensure the welfare of, and to pay pension to the Farmers engaged in cattle rearing in the State of Kerala.
scope: The Act applies to farmers engaged in cattle rearing in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Board: means the Kerala Dairy Farmers' Welfare Fund Board constituted under section 8.
key_definitions.Chief Executive Officer: means the Chief Executive Officer appointed under sub-section (1) of section 11.
key_definitions.contribution: means the sum of money payable to the Fund under section 7.
key_definitions.Dairy Farmer: means a person who owns or rear one or more cows or she buffaloes and milks at least 500 litres of milk per year in the State in a milk co-operative society functioning in his dwelling place or in a milk society nearby the area of his dwelling place, due to the reason that no milk Co-operative society is functioning in such place;
key_definitions.family: means (i) wife or husband of the dairy farmer, their minor or mentally retarded or physically challenged children and unmarried daughters; (ii) father and mother who are dependent upon the Dairy farmer,
key_definitions.Fund: means the Dairy Farmers' Welfare Fund established under section 3;
key_definitions.Member: means a member of the Fund,
key_definitions.Milma: means the Kerala Co-operative Milk Marketing Federation,
key_definitions.prescribed: means prescribed by rules made under this Act;
key_definitions.Regional Union: means the apex society functioning in the milk co-operative sector,
key_definitions.Schedule: means the Schedule to this Act,
key_definitions.Scheme: means the Kerala Dairy Farmers' Welfare Fund Scheme framed under this Act,
key_definitions.Society: means Primary Milk Co-operative Society registered or deemed to be registered under the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969 (21 of 1969) and functioning under the Dairy Development Department.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Dairy Farmers' Welfare Fund Act, 2007. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 24th day of August, 2005.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'Chief Executive Officer', 'contribution', 'Dairy Farmer', 'family', 'Fund', 'Member', 'Milma', 'prescribed', 'Regional Union', 'Schedule', 'Scheme', 'Society', and 'year'.

States that the Government shall, by notification in the Gazette, frame a scheme to be called the 'Kerala Dairy Farmers' Welfare Fund Scheme' for the establishment of a Fund and there shall be established a fund as soon as possible, in accordance with the provisions of this Act and the Scheme. The Fund shall be credited to the Fund, and shall include contribution specified under section 7, receipts from the interest of the Reserve Fund, grants and loans or advances made by the Government of India, State Government or any Institutions, donations received from cattle feed manufacturing establishments, milk product manufactures, private dairy owners, veterinary medicine manufactures and distributors and cattle semen producers and distributors and donations or receipts received from any other source, amount under any item raised by the decision of the Board from other sources to augment the resources of the Board, fees or fine levied under the scheme, and any other amount which, under the provisions of the scheme shall be credited to the Fund.

Every Dairy Farmer who has completed 18 years of age shall be eligible for registration as member of the Fund under the provision of this Act and Scheme. In case of death of any member within the minimum period for eligibility for the benefit, his successor shall be deemed to be continuing as a member in case he measures milk continuously thereafter.

main_sections.section_title: Cessation of membership in the Fund
main_sections.description: If a member commits an offence under section 17 or any other provision of this Act his membership in the fund shall be ceased.

Every society shall maintain a register in the prescribed form showing the details of the quantity of milk collected by the society, the date on which milk was supplied, etc. which are necessary for the implementation of the scheme and it shall be submitted for inspection, whenever required by the Chief Executive Officer or the Officer authorised by him.

The contribution to the Fund shall be in the following rates, namely: (a) each dairy farmer twenty rupees per month, (ii) each society shall, (a) twelve paise for each litre of milk to be collected and sold by the society locally, (b) five paise for each litre of milk to be given by the society to the Milma or to the Regional Union (iii) twelve paise per each litre of milk to be sold by Milma or the Regional Union.

The Board shall be called the Kerala Dairy Farmers' Welfare Fund Board, and shall be a body corporate. The Board shall consist of twelve Directors, including one member each elected from the Governing bodies of the three Regional Milk Co-operative Unions representing the Dairy farmers, three persons nominated by the Government from among the Presidents of traditional Primary Milk Co-operative Societies, Director of Dairy Development Department or representative, three persons nominated by the Government, representing the Government, Chief Executive Officer (Ex-officio), and Milma Chairman. One of the Directors shall be appointed by the Government to be its Chairman. The Government shall publish in the Gazette the names of the Chairman and the Directors of the Board. The Board shall administer the Fund vested in it.

main_sections.section_title: Term of Office of the Directors
main_sections.description: A Director appointed under sub-section (3) of section 8 shall hold office for a period of three years from the date he assume the charge in office. Notwithstanding anything contained in section 10, the Government may, at any time, for reasons to be recorded in writing, remove from office, any Director of the Board, after giving him a reasonable opportunity to show cause, against the proposed removal.

The membership of non-official Directors, who, without the previous permission of the Board, has been absent from three consecutive meetings of the Board, shall be removed. A non-official Director of the Board removed under sub-section (1) shall be disqualified for reappointment as a Director for a period of one year from the date of his removal.

The Government may appoint a Chief Executive Officer and such number of other officers and staff as they consider necessary to assist the Board in the discharge of its functions and duties under this Act. The Chief Executive Officer shall be an officer of the Dairy Development Department not below the post of Deputy Director working in the Dairy Development Department. Subject to the provisions of sub-section (4), the method of appointment, salary and allowances and other conditions of service of the Chief Executive Officer and the other officers and staff appointed under sub-section (1), shall be fixed by the Board with the approval of the Government. In the case of posts in the service under the Board to which appointments are made by direct recruitment the provisions in clauses (a), (b) and (c) of rule 14 and also the provisions contained in rules 15, 16, 17 and 17(a) of the Kerala State and Subordinate Service Rules, 1958 as amended from time to time shall be followed, 'mutatis mutandis'

The Chief Executive Officer or any other officer authorised by the Board in this behalf shall, after making such enquiry as may be necessary and after giving the society liable to pay the contribution under section 7, an opportunity to be heard, by order, determine the amount of contribution due under the provisions of this Act and the Scheme. The officer conducting the enquiry under sub-section (1) shall, for the purposes of such enquiry, have the same powers as are vested in a Civil Court while trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Central Act 5 of 1908), in respect of the following matters, namely – (a) enforce the attendance of any person and examining him on oath, (b) requiring the discovery and production of documents; (c) receiving evidence on affidavits, (d) issuing commissions for the examination of witnesses.

It shall be the duty of the Secretary of the Society/Chief Executive to pay in time the amount due to the Fund by each society, Milma and the Regional Union liable to pay the contribution under section 7. Where the contribution is not paid on or before the due date, the Board shall have the power to recover with interest from the officer authorised under sub-section (1). Each dairy farmer shall pay the contribution to be paid to the Fund under section 7 to the respective societies and it shall be the duty of the Secretary of the Society to remit such amount to the Fund in the manner as may be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Action against Secretary of the Society/Chief Executive
main_sections.description: Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, the Board may take action against the Secretary of the Society/Chief Executive concerned, if the contribution of the society, Milma and the Regional Union under section 7 has not been paid to the Fund.

main_sections.section_title: Priority of Payment of contribution over other debts
main_sections.description: Where any order has been made liquidating the society liable to pay contribution under section 7, the contribution due under this Act, while liquidating, shall be deemed to be included among the debts, which are to be paid in priority to all other debts.
