key_definitions.appellate authority: Means an appellate authority appointed under section 6.
key_definitions.creditor: Shall include the heirs, legal representatives and assigns of the creditor.
key_definitions.debt: Means any liability in cash or kind, whether secured or unsecured, due from or incurred by a debtor on or before the date of commencement of this Act, whether payable under a contract, or under a decree or order of any court, or otherwise, and subsisting on that date but does not include-(a) any sum payable to-(i) the Government of Kerala or the Government of India or the Government of any other State or Union Territory in India or any local authority, or (ii) the Reserve Bank of India or the State Bank of India or any subsidiary bank with the meaning of clause (k) of section 2 of the State Bank of India (Subsidiary Banks) Act, 1959 or the Travancore Credit Bank Act (in liquidation) constituted under the Travancore Credit Bank Act, 1947; or (iii) a corporation owned or controlled by the Government of Kerala or the Government of any other State or Union Territory in India or the Government of India or a Government Company as defined in the Companies Act, 1956; or (iv) the Tea Board constituted under the Tea Act, 1953, or the Coffee Board constituted under the Coffee Act, 1942, or the Rubber Board constituted under the Rubber Act, 1947, or the Cardamom Board constituted under the Cardamom Act, 1965; or (v) any co-operative society, including a Land Mortgage Bank, registered or deemed to be registered under the Co-operative Societies Act for the time being in force; or (b) any sum payable to any corresponding new bank specified in column (2) of the First Schedule to the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1970; or (c) any liability arising out of a breach of trust or any tortious liability; or (d) any liability in respect of maintenance, whether under a decree of court or otherwise; or (e) any liability in respect of wages or remuneration due as salary or otherwise for services rendered; or (f) any debt which represents the price of goods purchased; or (g) any liability for which a charge is provided under sub-clause (b) of clause (4) of section 55 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882; or (h) any rent payable in respect of any building; or (i) any rent or michavaram payable in respect of any land; or (j) any debt or debts due to a widow at the commencement of this Act, provided that the value of the property owned by her at such commencement, including the principal amount of the debt or debts so due, does not exceed ten thousand rupees.
key_definitions.Explanation for sub-clause (j) of 'debt': For the purposes of this sub-clause, the house in which the widow lives, her wearing apparel or similar personal belongings shall not be regarded as property; or (k) any liability incurred or arising out of a chitty or kuri which is registered or licensed under the Travancore Chitty Act, 1120, or the Cochin Chitty Act VII of 1107, or the Kerala Chitty Act, 1975, or continued under any chitty fund scheme, and which has not terminated two years before the commencement of this Act: Provided that nothing in this sub-clause shall apply to the liability of a foreman incurred or arising under any such chitty or kuri where the foreman is a co-operative society registered or deemed to be registered under the Co-operative Societies Act for the time being in force.
key_definitions.debtor: Means any person whose annual income does not exceed three thousand rupees, and from whom any debt is due, but does not include-(i) any person from whom debt or debts exceeding three thousand rupees (excluding interest) is or are due; (ii) a firm registered under the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, or a company as defined in the Companies Act, 1956, or a corporation formed in pursuance of an Act of Parliament of the United Kingdom or of any special Indian Law.
key_definitions.Explanation for 'debtor': For the purposes of this clause, the term 'person' shall include a family.
key_definitions.family: Means a Hindu undivided family or a Marumakka-thayam tarwad or tavazhu or an Aliyasanthana kutumba or kavaru or a Nambudiri illom;
key_definitions.interest: Means any amount or other things paid or payable in excess of the principal amount borrowed or payable or obligation incurred, or, if any, obligation has been borrowed in kind, in excess of what has been borrowed, by whomever, namely, such amount or thing may be called, and whether the same is paid or payable entirely in cash or entirely in kind or partly in cash and partly in kind and whether the same is expressly mentioned or not in the document or contract, if any;
key_definitions.pay: With its grammatical variations, includes deliver;
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act;
key_definitions.principal amount: Means the amount originally advanced together with such sum, if any, as has been subsequently advanced, notwithstanding any stipulation to treat any interest as principal and notwithstanding that the debt has been entered or included in a fresh document, whether by the same debtor or by his heirs, legal representatives or assigns or by any other person acting on his behalf or in his interest, and whether in favour of the same creditor or his heirs, legal representatives or assigns or of any other person acting on his behalf or in his interest;
key_definitions.Tribunal: Means a Tribunal constituted under section 5.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Debt Relief Act, 1977, it extends to the whole of the State of Kerala, and it came into force on the 13th day of January, 1977.
Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'appellate authority', 'creditor', 'debt', 'debtor', 'family', 'interest', 'pay', 'prescribed', 'principal amount', and 'Tribunal'.

Specifies that any decree and the interest thereon payable by a debtor to a creditor shall be deemed to be wholly discharged, and no civil court shall entertain any suit or other proceeding against a debtor for the recovery of any debt or part of a debt or any interest thereon. It also covers suits and other proceedings pending at the commencement of this Act and provides exceptions for the sale of movable or immovable property.

Deals with the reconveyance of property by a debtor or any other person on behalf of such debtor to the Tribunal within three months from the commencement of this Act or within such further period as may be notified by the Government. The Tribunal shall make necessary inquiries and, if satisfied, direct the person in possession of the property to deliver possession to the applicant or the person on whose behalf the application has been made.
Empowers the Government to constitute Tribunals and specifies that a Tribunal shall consist of a sole member who shall be an officer not below the rank of Tahsildar appointed by the Government.
Empowers the Government to notify an appellate authority for the purposes of this Act and states that an appellate authority shall be an officer not below the rank of Revenue Divisional Officer.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of Tribunal and appellate authority
main_sections.description: Grants Tribunals and appellate authorities the powers of a civil court while trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, including summoning and enforcing attendance, examining on oath, requiring discovery and production of documents, and any other matter which may be prescribed. The decisions of Tribunals and appellate authorities shall have the force of a decree of a civil court.

main_sections.section_title: Legal practitioners not to appear before Tribunals and appellate authorities
main_sections.description: Prohibits legal practitioners from appearing before Tribunals and appellate authorities in any law for the time being in force, unless specifically allowed in any proceedings before a Tribunal or an appellate authority under this Act.

States that notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force, in any suit or other proceeding, the burden of proving that a debtor is not entitled to protection under the provisions of this Act shall be on the creditor.

main_sections.section_title: Bar of jurisdiction of civil courts
main_sections.description: Ousts the jurisdiction of civil courts to decide or deal with any question or to determine any matter which is, or by this Act, required to be decided or dealt with, or to be determined, by the Tribunal or the appellate authority.

main_sections.section_title: Acts to over-ride other laws, contracts, etc.
main_sections.description: Declares that the provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, or in any other law for the time being in force, or in any custom, usage or contract, or in any decree or order of a court or other authority.
Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act. Such rules, as soon as may be after it is made, shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

Repeals the Kerala Debtors (Temporary Relief) Act, 1975 and the Kerala Debt Relief Ordinance, 1977. It also provides that nothing done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the repealed Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Debts and interest payable by a debtor to a creditor are deemed to be wholly discharged.
No civil court can entertain suits or proceedings for debt recovery after the commencement of the Act.
The Act overrides other laws, contracts, and court orders.
Legal practitioners are generally prohibited from appearing before Tribunals and appellate authorities.
The burden of proof that a debtor is not entitled to protection lies with the creditor.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Tribunals and appellate authorities
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Decisions of Tribunals and appellate authorities have the force of a decree of a civil court.

rights: Right of debtors to debt relief.
Right to have debts discharged.
obligations: Obligation of creditors to accept discharge of debt.
Obligation of persons in possession of reconveyed property to deliver possession.

key_procedures: Application to the Tribunal for relief.
Tribunal's inquiry and decision.
Appeal to the appellate authority.
Reconveyance of property process.
administration: The Government of Kerala (implied by the context of the Act being specific to Kerala and the power to make rules and appoint authorities).
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the President on the 12th day of August, 1977 and was published in the Kerala Gazette No. 474 dated 12th August, 1977.
The Act has overriding effect over other laws, contracts, and court orders.
Specific exclusions exist for certain types of payables from being considered 'debt'.
Limitations apply to liabilities incurred from certain chitty or kuri schemes.
Annual income limit for a debtor is specified as not exceeding three thousand rupees.

title: The Kerala Devaswom Recruitment Board (Amendment) Act, 2016
purpose: To amend the Kerala Devaswom Recruitment Board Act, 2015.
scope: Applies to the Devaswom Recruitment Board and its functioning.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Devaswom Recruitment Board (Amendment) Act, 2016. It shall come into force at once.

Amends Section 3 of the Kerala Devaswom Recruitment Board Act, 2015, by substituting a new sub-section regarding the composition of the Board. The Board shall consist of a Chairperson and two members nominated by the Government, who belong to Hindu religion and having faith in God and temple worship. A person who is or has been a District Judge or qualified to be appointed as a District Judge shall be appointed as Chairperson of the Board. Among the members one shall be a woman and one shall be a person belonging to Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe. Members shall have experience in handling labour, service or administrative matters.

Amends Section 5 of the principal Act. For sub-section (1) of Section 5, the following sub-section shall be substituted: "(1) The Chairperson and other members may continue in office till the completion of a Period of three years from the date on which they assume office."
Amends Section 8 of the principal Act. In section 8, in sub-section (4), for the word "four" the word "two" shall be substituted.

main_sections.section_title: Special provision relating to the existing Chairperson and Members of the Board
main_sections.description: Notwithstanding anything contrary contained in the principal Act, the existing Chairperson and members of the Board shall cease to hold office as such from the date of commencement of the Kerala Devaswom Recruitment Board (Amendment) Act, 2016.

administration: Law (Legislation-B) Department, Government of Kerala

title: The Kerala Devaswom Recruitment Board Act, 2015
purpose: To provide for the constitution of an autonomous Devaswom Recruitment Board for preparing select lists of candidates for appointments in various posts (other than hereditary posts and posts in aided educational institutions) in Devaswom Boards of the State of Kerala and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the Devaswom Boards of the State of Kerala, specifically for recruitment to various posts except for hereditary posts and posts in aided educational institutions. The Act is enacted in India and concerns the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Board: The Kerala Devaswom Recruitment Board constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.Devaswom Board: Means the Travancore Devaswom Board or Cochin Devaswom Board or Malabar Devaswom Board or Guruvayoor Devaswom Managing Committee or Koodalmanickam Devaswom Managing Committee.
key_definitions.Hindu Scheduled Tribe: Means a person belonging to the Scheduled Tribe-Hindu Community.
key_definitions.hereditary posts: Means such posts as may be prescribed by the rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Member: Means a member of the Board and includes the Chairperson.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules or regulations made under this Act.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Kerala Devaswom Recruitment Board Act, 2015' and that it is deemed to have come into force on March 1, 2014.
Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'Devaswom Board', 'Government', 'Hindu Scheduled Tribe', 'hereditary posts', 'Member', and 'prescribed'.

Details the establishment of the Kerala Devaswom Recruitment Board as an independent and autonomous corporate body. It outlines the composition of the Board (six members nominated by the Government, belonging to Hindu religion, having faith in God and temple rituals; one Chairperson not below the rank of Secretary to Government; one woman; and one member from Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe), the appointment of a Secretary, and the headquarters of the Board.

Lists the grounds on which a person is disqualified from being a member of the Board, including unsound mind, undischarged insolvent, office-bearer/employee of Local Self Government Institution or Devaswom Board, interest in contracts with the Board, conviction for moral turpitude offenses, removal from office by court order, or engagement in liquor production/sale.

main_sections.section_title: Term of Office and conditions of service of the Chairperson and Members
main_sections.description: Specifies the term of office for the Chairperson and members (five years or until age 65, whichever is earlier). It also covers resignation, filling temporary vacancies, grounds for removal from office by the Government (with an opportunity to be heard), eligibility for re-appointment (not eligible), and that they shall be full-time officers with prescribed salary and allowances.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of officers and employees of the Board
main_sections.description: Describes the appointment of officers and employees by the Government for the Board's management, including a Law Officer, Finance Officer, and other prescribed officers. It states that these officers and employees must belong to the Hindu religion and have faith in God and temple rituals. It also covers initial appointments through deputation and subsequent appointments by the Board directly or on deputation, as prescribed by regulations. The terms and conditions of service are to be as prescribed and generally align with Government employee rules.

main_sections.section_title: Vacancies etc. not to invalidate proceedings of the Board
main_sections.description: Stipulates that the Board's proceedings are not invalidated due to vacancies or defects in its constitution.

Outlines the procedures for Board meetings, including when and where they are held, convened by the Secretary on the Chairperson's recommendation, presided over by the Chairperson (or a member in their absence), quorum (four members including the Chairperson), decision-making by majority vote with a casting vote for the presiding officer, and the maintenance of minutes signed by attendees.

Details the primary functions of the Board, including preparing select lists for appointments (other than hereditary and aided educational institution posts) in Devaswom Boards, inviting applications, conducting written examinations and interviews, making arrangements for examinations (question papers, supervision, valuation), conducting other entrusted examinations, and obtaining examination details from Devaswom Boards. It also emphasizes the Board's responsibility for the proper conduct and secrecy of examinations, maintaining records, and furnishing select lists to Devaswom Boards.
States that the expenditure of the Board, including salaries, allowances, and pensions, is to be met from the Consolidated Fund of the State.
Specifies that the Government shall grant necessary amounts to the Board for its purposes after due appropriation by law in the State Legislative Assembly.

Requires the Board to prepare an annual budget of anticipated income and expenditure for the next financial year and submit it to the Government within two months of each financial year's commencement.

Mandates the Board to maintain proper accounts, prepare annual statements of accounts in a prescribed form in consultation with the Accountant General, and have its accounts audited annually by the Accountant General. The Board must pay for the audit. The Accountant General has rights similar to auditing Government accounts, including inspecting records. The Board must forward the certified accounts and audit report to the Government, which then lays it before the Legislative Assembly.
Requires the Board to prepare an annual report detailing its activities for the previous financial year in a prescribed form and time, and forward a copy to the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Chairperson, Members and Employees of the Board to be public servants
main_sections.description: Declares that the Chairperson, Members, and Employees of the Board are deemed to be public servants within the meaning of Section 21 of the Indian Penal Code.

important_rules: Members of the Board must belong to the Hindu religion and have faith in God and temple rituals.
The Chairperson of the Board shall be a person who is or has been holding a post not below the rank of Secretary to Government.
Among other members of the Board, one shall be a woman and one shall be a member belonging to Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe.
Officers and employees of the Board shall belong to the Hindu religion and have faith in God and temple rituals.
The Board shall prepare select lists for appointment to various posts other than hereditary posts and posts in aided educational institutions.
The Board's expenditure, including salaries, allowances, and pensions, shall be met from the Consolidated Fund of the State.
The Board shall prepare and submit an annual budget to the Government.
The Board's accounts shall be audited annually by the Accountant General.
The Chairperson, Members, and Employees of the Board are considered public servants.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala, the Board itself, and potentially the Accountant General for audit matters.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, including the constitution of the Board, its powers and functions, the audit of its accounts, and the declaration of its members and employees as public servants.

rights: Candidates applying for more than one post or to more than one Devaswom Board shall not be denied the right to appear in more than one examination (subject to certain conditions regarding examinations on the same day).
The Government has the right to appoint officers and employees to the Board and to remove members under specific conditions.
The Accountant General has the right to demand production of documents and inspect offices during audits.
duties: The Board has the duty to prepare select lists for appointments.
The Board has the duty to invite applications, conduct examinations/interviews, and prepare select lists.
The Board has the duty to make arrangements for examinations (question papers, supervision, valuation).
The Board has the duty to furnish select lists to Devaswom Boards and advise candidates.
The Board has the duty to maintain proper accounts and prepare annual statements of accounts.
The Board has the duty to prepare and submit an annual budget.
The Board has the duty to prepare and submit an annual report.
The Government has the duty to appropriate funds to the Board.
The Board has the duty to ensure the proper conduct and secrecy of examinations.
obligations: Devaswom Boards are implicitly obliged to request recruitments from the Board when needed and to act upon the select lists provided.
The Board is obligated to function as an independent and autonomous body.
The Board is obligated to provide a reasonable opportunity of being heard to any person facing removal from office.
The Board is obligated to maintain the secrecy of examination materials and results.

key_procedures: Constitution of the Board: The Government notifies the constitution of the Kerala Devaswom Recruitment Board.
Nomination of Members: The Government nominates six members, including a Chairperson, a woman, and a member from Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe, adhering to specific criteria.

Recruitment Process: The Board invites applications, conducts written examinations and/or interviews, and prepares select lists for posts in Devaswom Boards (excluding hereditary and aided educational institution posts).
Budget Preparation and Submission: The Board prepares an annual budget and submits it to the Government.

Audit and Reporting: The Board maintains accounts, which are audited annually by the Accountant General. The Board submits certified accounts and audit reports to the Government, which are then laid before the Legislative Assembly.
Annual Report Preparation: The Board prepares and submits an annual report on its activities to the Government.
administration: The Government of Kerala, specifically the Law (Legislation-B) Department, is involved in the notification and oversight of the Act. The Kerala Devaswom Recruitment Board is the primary administrative body for its functions.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on March 1, 2014.
The Act excludes hereditary posts and posts in aided educational institutions from its purview for recruitment by the Board.
The Act emphasizes the independent and autonomous nature of the Devaswom Recruitment Board.
The Act requires members and employees to profess the Hindu religion and have faith in God and temple rituals.
A person once appointed as Chairperson or Member is not eligible for re-appointment.

title: The Kerala Dairy Farmers Welfare Fund Act, 2007
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a Fund to grant relief to, to ensure the welfare of and to pay pension to the Farmers engaged in cattle rearing in the State of Kerala and for matters incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to Farmers engaged in cattle rearing in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Board: means the Kerala Dairy Farmers' Welfare Fund Board constituted under section 8.
key_definitions.Chief Executive Officer: means the Chief Executive Officer appointed under sub-section (1) of section 11.
key_definitions.contribution: means the sum of money payable to the Fund under section 7.
key_definitions.Dairy Farmer: means a person who owns or rear one or more cows or she buffaloes and markets atleast 500 litres of milk per year in the State in a milk co-operative society functioning in his dwelling place or in a milk society nearby the area of his dwelling place, due to the reason that no milk co-operative society is functioning in such place.
key_definitions.family: means (i) wife or husband of the Dairy Farmer, their minor or mentally retarded or physically challenged children and unmarried daughters; (ii) father and mother who are dependent upon the Dairy Farmer;
key_definitions.Fund: means the Dairy Farmers' Welfare Fund established under section 3.
key_definitions.Member: means a member of the Fund.
key_definitions.Milma: means the Kerala Co-operative Milk Marketing Federation.
key_definitions.prescribed: means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Regional Union: means the apex society functioning in the milk co-operative sector.
key_definitions.Scheme: means the Kerala Dairy Farmers' Welfare Fund Scheme framed under this Act.
key_definitions.society: means Primary Milk Co-operative Society registered or deemed to be registered under the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969 (21 of 1969) and functioning under the Dairy Development Department.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Dairy Farmers' Welfare Fund Act, 2007 and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 24th day of August, 2005.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including Board, Chief Executive Officer, contribution, Dairy Farmer, family, Fund, Member, Milma, prescribed, Regional Union, Scheme, society, and year.

States that the Government shall, by notification in the Gazette, frame a Scheme to be called the 'Kerala Dairy Farmers' Welfare Fund Scheme' for the establishment of a Fund under this Act for the welfare of the Dairy Farmers in the State and there shall be established a fund as soon as possible, in accordance with the provisions of this Act and the Scheme. It also details the sources of the Fund, including contribution, receipts from the reserve Fund, contributions or grants or loans or advances made by the Government, donations, amounts raised by the Board, fees or fines, and any other amount. The Fund shall be vested in the Board, constituted under section 8 and administered as provided in sub-section (1) of section 11.

Every Dairy Farmer who has completed 18 years of age shall be eligible for registration as member of the Fund under the provision of this Act and Scheme. Application for registration shall be made in such forms as may be prescribed, to the Officer of the Dairy Development Department authorised by the Chief Executive Officer or on his behalf in whose jurisdiction the applicant resides. Every application shall be accompanied by such documents together with the fee for registration as may be specified in the Scheme.

main_sections.section_title: Cessation of membership in the Fund
main_sections.description: A member shall commit an offence under section 17 or any other provision of this Act his membership in the fund shall be ceased.

Every society shall maintain a register in the prescribed form showing the details of the quantity of milk collected by the society, the date on which milk was supplied etc. which are necessary for the implementation of the scheme and it shall be submitted for inspection, whenever required by the Chief Executive Officer or the Officer authorised by him.

Details the rates of contribution to the Fund: (i) each dairy farmer twenty rupees per month; (ii) each society shall pay (a) *0.1 percent of the sale price for each litre of milk to be collected and sold by the society locally. (b) *0.3 percent of the sale price for each litre of milk to be given by the society to the Milma or to the Regional Union. (iii) *0.75 percent of the sale price per each litre of milk to be sold by Milma or the Regional Union.

Constitutes the Kerala Dairy Farmers' Welfare Fund Board. The Board shall be a body corporate by the name aforesaid, having perpetual succession and common seal and shall by the said name sue and be sued. The Board shall consist of twelve Directors as follows: one member each, elected from the Governing bodies of the three Regional Milk Co-operative Unions representing the Dairy farmers; three persons nominated by the Government from among the Presidents of traditional Primary Milk Co-operative Societies; Director of Dairy Development Department or representative; three persons nominated by the Government, representing the Government; Chief Executive Officer (Ex-officio); Milma Chairman. One of the Directors of the Board shall be appointed by the Government to be its Chairman. The Government shall publish in the Gazette the names of the Chairman and the Directors of the Board. The Board shall administer the Fund vested in it in such manner as may be specified in the scheme.

main_sections.section_title: Term of Office of the Directors
main_sections.description: A Director appointed under sub-section (3) of section 8 shall hold office for a period of three years from the date he assumes or charge in office. Notwithstanding anything contained in section 10, the Government may, at any time, for reasons to be recorded in writing, remove from office, any Director of the Board. After giving him a reasonable opportunity to show-cause, against the proposed removal. Provided that it shall not be necessary to record in writing, the reason for removal or to give an opportunity to show cause against the proposed removal, if the Government or the nominee that it is not expedient in the public interest to record its reasons in writing or to give such opportunity. Any Director may resign his membership by giving notice in writing to the Government and his resignation shall come into force on the date of receipt of the letter of resignation by the Government.
A non-official Director of the Board removed under sub-section (1) shall be debarred for reappointment as a Director for a period of one year from the date of his removal.

The Government may appoint a Chief Executive Officer and such number of other officers and staff as they consider necessary to assist the Board in the discharge of its functions and duties under this Act. The Chief Executive Officer shall be an officer of the Dairy Development Department not below the post of Deputy Director working in the Dairy Development Department. Subject to the provisions of this Act, the scheme framed under sub-section (1) may provide for the matters specified in sub-section (4) and in the scheme.

important_rules: Every Dairy Farmer who has completed 18 years of age shall be eligible for registration as member of the Fund.

Application for registration shall be made in such forms as may be prescribed, to the Officer of the Dairy Development Department authorised by the Chief Executive Officer or on his behalf in whose jurisdiction the applicant resides.
Every application shall be accompanied by such documents together with the fee for registration as may be specified in the Scheme.

Contribution to the Fund shall be: each dairy farmer twenty rupees per month; each society shall pay 0.1 percent of the sale price for each litre of milk to be collected and sold by the society locally; 0.3 percent of the sale price for each litre of milk to be given by the society to the Milma or to the Regional Union; 0.75 percent of the sale price per each litre of milk to be sold by Milma or the Regional Union.

penalties: Section 17: Penalty for offences.
Enhanced punishment for the second or subsequent offence.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Chief Executive Officer or Officer authorised by him.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through penalties for offences and potentially through the Scheme.

rights: Right to pension (for eligible dairy farmers).
Right to financial assistance for permanent disability.
Right to financial assistance for other specified purposes in the scheme.
duties: Dairy farmers have a duty to contribute to the Fund.
Societies have a duty to maintain registers and submit them for inspection.
Members have a duty to comply with the provisions of this Act and the Scheme.
obligations: Members have an obligation to register as members of the Fund if eligible.
Societies have an obligation to collect and remit contributions.

key_procedures: Application for registration as a member of the Fund in the prescribed form, accompanied by necessary documents and fee.
Submission of applications to the authorised officer of the Dairy Development Department.
Maintenance of registers by societies showing milk collection details and submission for inspection.
Processes for removal of Directors from the Board.
Procedures for appointment of Chief Executive Officer, officers and staff.
Appeals process for decisions made by the Chief Executive Officer or other authority.
administration: Dairy Development Department (for appointment of officers and staff), The Board (for administration of the Fund).
important_notes: The Act was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 703 dated 13th April, 2007.
The Act shall be deemed to have come into force on the 24th day of August, 2005.
The Scheme is to be framed by the Government by notification in the Gazette.
Section 17 deals with penalties for offences.
Section 18: Enhanced punishment for the second or subsequent offence.
Section 19: Offence by Societies.
Section 20: Protection of Acts done in good faith.
Section 21: Directions by the Government.
Section 22: Power to supersede the Board.
Section 23: Audit of the Accounts of the Board.
Section 24: Annual Report and Audited Statement of Accounts.
Section 25: Bar of jurisdiction of Civil Courts.
Section 26: Power to make rules.
Section 27: Repeal and saving.
Section 28: Schedule.

title: The Kerala District Administration (Amendment) Act, 1991
purpose: To further amend the Kerala District Administration Act, 1979.
scope: Applies to the Kerala District Administration, specifically concerning district councils and their administration.

key_definitions.collector: Means the Collector of the district concerned.
key_definitions.returned candidate: Means a candidate who has been declared duly elected.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala District Administration (Amendment) Act, 1991 and specifies provisions for commencement and commencement dates for various sections and clauses.
Amends Section 2 of the Kerala District Administration Act, 1979 by substituting existing clauses and adding new ones, including definitions related to 'Collector' and 'member'.
Amends Section 5 of the principal Act by substituting words and figures related to 'fixed under section 4' and amending sub-sections.
Amends Section 6 of the principal Act by substituting words and figures in sub-section (1) and in the first proviso to sub-section (1).
Amends Section 9 of the principal Act by substituting the opening sentence in sub-section (1) and amending sub-section (2) and its clauses.
Amends Section 16 of the principal Act by substituting sub-section (1) and adding a new sub-section (4) regarding casual vacancies.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new sections for section 21
main_sections.description: Substitutes new sections for Section 21, introducing Section 21A (District Court to try election petitions) and Section 21B (Presentation of petitions), along with grounds for declaring an election void.

main_sections.section_title: Special provision to validate certain act etc.
main_sections.description: Contains provisions to validate certain acts and to give effect to the Act.
Repeals the Kerala District Administration (Amendment) Ordinance, 1991 and provides for savings.

important_rules: A person shall not be qualified to be elected or nominated as a member of the district council unless they have any division in the district and the words 'any division in the district and in case of election,' are substituted.

Provided that where a Member of the House of the People (Lok Sabha) or a Member of the Legislative Assembly of the State is chosen as Speaker, as the case may be, of the House of the People (Lok Sabha) or of the Legislative Assembly of the State, he shall cease to be an ex-officio member.

The term of office of members of the district council shall, save as otherwise expressly provided in this Act, be as follows: (a) in the case of an elected member five years from the date of constitution or re-constitution of that district council; (b) in the case of an ex-officio member for such period until he ceases to hold the office by virtue of which he has become an ex-officio member, and (c) in the case of a nominated member for such period during which the person by whom he was nominated holds the office by virtue of which the nomination was made or on the expiry of the term of the district council in which he was nominated, whichever is earlier.
No person shall be entitled to stand for election for more than one seat in the district council.
Subject to the provisions of section 21H where a member other than an ex-officio member shall cease to hold office as such if he

In arrears of any pecuniary nature due by him to the district council in respect of which a bill or a notice has been duly served upon him and the time, if any, specified therein to clear the arrears has expired; or

Every election petition shall be presented by the district council having jurisdiction over the area in which the office of the district council concerned is situated.

penalties: Grounds for declaring an election to be void include the date of the election, corrupt practice by a returned candidate or his agent, or nomination improperly rejected.

title: The Kerala District Administration (Amendment) Act, 1989
purpose: To amend the Kerala District Administration Act, 1979, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala District Administration Act, 1979, and its subsequent amendments.

key_definitions.taluk samithi: means a taluk samithi constituted under section 128 of the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960 (32 of 1960), inserted in that Act by the Fourth Schedule of this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called The Kerala District Administration (Amendment) Act, 1989, and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Amends section 2 of the principal Act, substituting various clauses including those for 'district' and 'taluk samithi'.

important_rules: The number of members in every district council shall not be less than twenty or more than forty.

The district council shall consist of such number of members as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, fix in accordance with the scale of one member for every fifty thousand or part thereof of the population of the district, elected in the manner prescribed.

Persons convicted of an offence punishable under Chapter IXA of the Indian Penal Code or under any law for the time being in force relating to the infringement of the secrecy of an election shall be disqualified from being elected or from holding the office of member for a period of five years from the date of his conviction or for such shorter period as the court may by order determine.
A person who is subject to any disqualification, other than that relating to age, for being chosen as a member of the Legislative Assembly shall also be disqualified for being elected as a member.

penalties: Disqualification from being elected or holding office for a period of five years from the date of conviction for an offence under Chapter IXA of the Indian Penal Code or election laws.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government, Court
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By notification in the Gazette, by court order, by court determination.

rights: Right to be elected as a member of a district council (subject to eligibility criteria).
Right to vote at elections of members of district councils.
Right to receive monthly allowances and house rent allowance as prescribed.
duties: To attend meetings of the district council and the General Standing Committee and Finance Standing Committee.
To carry into effect the resolutions of the district council.
To control officers and employees working under the district council subject to general superintendence and control of the President and such rules as may be made by the Government.
To discharge all the duties and exercise all the powers specifically imposed or conferred on the Secretary by or under this Act.
obligations: Members of the district council must be elected.

Elections to district councils are to be held.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, fix the scale of members for district councils based on population.
Members of the district council shall be elected.
The Secretary shall attend meetings of the district council and committees, carry into effect resolutions, control officers and employees, and discharge duties and exercise powers.

title: THE KERALA DISTRICT ADMINISTRATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1990
purpose: To further amend the Kerala District Administration Act, 1979 (7 of 1980). The preamble states that it is expedient to further amend the Kerala District Administration Act, 1979, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: The Act applies to the Kerala District Administration and its related provisions. It amends the principal Act of 1979.

key_definitions.district: means a revenue district, excluding the area within the limits of a cantonment declared under the Cantonments Act, 1924 (Central Act 2 of 1924).
key_definitions.vehicle or vessel: means any vehicle or vessel or capable of being used for the purpose of road or water transport, whether propelled by mechanical power or otherwise and whether used for drawing other vehicles or vessels or otherwise.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala District Administration (Amendment) Act, 1990. Section 2 shall be deemed to have come into force on the 12th day of December, 1989. Sections 3, 4, 5 and 6 shall be deemed to have come into force on the 3rd day of May, 1990. The remaining provisions shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint and different dates may be appointed for different areas and for different provisions of this Act.

Amends section 2 of the Kerala District Administration Act, 1979. Clause (c) of sub-section (1) is substituted to define 'district' as a revenue district, excluding cantonment areas. Clause (pp) is substituted with new wording concerning 'section 128' and 'section 128A'.

Amends section 10 of the principal Act. A new sub-section (1A) is inserted. This new sub-section (1A) clarifies provisions regarding the electoral roll and its preparation, specifically noting that it is not the one prepared or revised in the year in which the notice of election to the district council is to be published, or where the said electoral roll is the one revised without conducting an intensive revision subsequently, there shall be prepared by the authority prescribed under sub-section (2), an electoral roll for each district council under the superintendence, direction and control of the Director of Elections.

Amends section 47 of the principal Act, substituting words and brackets referring to 'The Kerala Land Acquisition Act, 1961 (21 of 1962)' with 'the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (Central Act 1 of 1894)'.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new Chapter VI A
main_sections.description: Inserts a new Chapter VI A after Chapter VI of the principal Act. This new chapter is titled 'ELECTORAL OFFENCES'.
Inserts a new section 101A into the principal Act, titled 'Removal of difficulties'.
This section likely deals with the repeal of any conflicting previous provisions and saving clauses for existing matters.

important_rules: Prohibition of public meeting on the day preceding the election day and on the election day (74A(1)).

No person shall convene, hold or attend any public meeting within the district in connection with an election to the district council of that district during the period of forty-eight hours ending with the hour fixed for the conclusion of the poll (74A(1)).

Any person who contravenes the provisions of sub-section (1) shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees (74A(2)).
Disturbances at election meetings are prohibited (74B).
Penalty for disorderly conduct in or near polling stations (74C).
Prohibition of canvassing in or near polling stations (74D).
Removal of ballot papers or ballot boxes from polling station to be an offence (74E).
Infringement of secrecy of elections is prohibited (74G).

No person who is a returning officer, or an assistant returning officer, or a presiding officer or an election or an official clerk appointed by the returning officer or the presiding officer to perform any duty in connection with an election shall, in the conduct or the management of the election do any act (other than the giving of vote) for the furtherance of the prospects of the election of a candidate (74H(1)).
Penalty for illegal hiring or procuring of conveyances at elections (741).
Breaches of official duty in connection with elections are punishable (74K).
Requisition of premises etc., for election purposes are governed by specific rules (74L).
Promoting enmity between classes in connection with elections is prohibited (74M).
Restriction on the printing of pamphlets, posters, etc. is imposed (74N).

Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees (for contravention of 74B).
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees (for contravention of 74C(1)).

Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees (for contravention of 74E(3)).

Imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both (for contravention of 74E(2) if the person is a returning officer or a presiding officer or an election or an official clerk).
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both (for contravention of 74E(2) if the person is any other officer).
Punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both (for contravention of 74F).
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both (for contravention of 74G).
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both (for contravention of 74H(1)).
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees (for contravention of 74H(3)).

Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to three months (for contravention of 74L(4)).

Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both (for contravention of 74N).

title: The Kerala Document Writers', Scribes' and Stamp Vendors' Welfare Fund Act, 2012
purpose: An Act to provide for the constitution of a Welfare Fund for the welfare of the document writers, scribes and stamp vendors in the State of Kerala, to pay pension and other benefits to them and for other matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to document writers, scribes and stamp vendors in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Board: means the Kerala Document Writers', Scribes' and Stamp Vendors' Welfare Fund Board constituted under section 9.
key_definitions.cessation of employment: means ceasing of employment of a licensee consequent to the cancellation or surrender of the licence obtained for doing the employment;
key_definitions.contribution: means the amount payable to the Welfare Fund by the members under sub-section (1) of section 4 and by the Government under sub-section (1) of section 26;
key_definitions.dependent: means wife or husband, minor sons, unmarried or widowed or divorced daughters, mentally or physically disabled children, father, mother who are solely dependent upon the member;
key_definitions.Document Writer: means a person having a licence who is engaged in the profession of preparing documents including 'enquiry as to title, preparation of draft deeds and engrossing the deed on stamp paper for registration as per the Kerala Document Writers' Licence Rules, 1960;
key_definitions.Fund: means the Kerala Document Writers', Scribes' and Stamp Vendors' Welfare Fund constituted under sub-section (1) of section 3;
key_definitions.Inspector General of Registration: means the Inspector General of Registration of the Government of Kerala;
key_definitions.member: means a Document Writer or a Scribe or a Stamp Vendor, who has been admitted as a member of the Welfare Fund under the provisions of this Act or who is continuing as a member of the Kerala Document Writers', Scribes' and Stamp Vendors' Welfare Fund Scheme, 1991;
key_definitions.notification: means a notification published in the Kerala Gazette;
key_definitions.prescribed: means prescribed by rules made under this Act;
key_definitions.Registering Authority: means the District Registrar (General) of the district concerned;
key_definitions.Scheme: means the Kerala Document Writers', Scribes' and Stamp Vendors' Welfare Fund Scheme framed under this Act;
key_definitions.Scribe: means a person who assists a Document Writer in the preparation of documents and who possesses a valid scribe licence to transcribe the documents to be presented for registration as defined in sub-rule (5) of rule 3 of the Kerala Document Writers' Licence Rules, 1960 ;
key_definitions.Secretary: means the Secretary of the Board constituted as per this Act;
key_definitions.stamp: means the Kerala Document Writers', Scribes' and Stamp Vendors' Welfare Fund Stamp printed and distributed under section 24;
key_definitions.Stamp Vendor: means a person who has acquired a licence as per rule 35 of the Kerala Manufacture and Sale of Stamp Rules, 1960 and acted in the profession of selling non-judicial stamps and stamp papers.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Document Writers', Scribes' and Stamp Vendors' Welfare Fund Act, 2012 and it came into force on the 31st day of January, 2012.

This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as Board, cessation of employment, contribution, dependent, Document Writer, Fund, Government, Inspector General of Registration, member, notification, prescribed, Registering Authority, Scheme, Scribe, Secretary, stamp, and Stamp Vendor.

main_sections.section_title: Kerala Document Writers', Scribes' and Stamp Vendors' Welfare Fund
main_sections.description: This section deals with the constitution of the Welfare Fund. It states that the Government shall, as soon as may be, after the commencement of this Act, by notification, frame a Scheme to be called the "Kerala Document Writers', Scribes' and Stamp Vendors' Welfare Fund Scheme" and after the framing of the Scheme, constitute a Fund to be called "the Kerala Document Writers', Scribes' and Stamp Vendors' Welfare Fund" in accordance with the provisions of this Act and the Scheme. The Fund shall consist of various credits including contributions, application fees, borrowed amounts, amounts from sale of stamp paper, voluntary donations, profits from investments, grants, loans, advances, and other amounts raised by the Board. The Fund shall vest in the Board and be administered by the Board. The Fund may be utilized for payment of fixed amount and pension to members, family pension, financial assistance on death, illness or accident, repayment of contribution, financial assistance to meet marriage expenses, expenses related to livelihood, purchase of land and building, education, special relief, and day-to-day administrative expenses of the Board.

This section outlines the contribution to the Fund. Every Document Writer, Scribe and Stamp Vendor eligible to become a member shall pay a prescribed contribution per month. The Government may, by notification, revise the rate of contribution. The contribution shall be paid in the name of the Secretary or officer authorised in this behalf.

This section details the membership in the Fund. Any person holding a valid licence of document writer or scribe under the Kerala Document Writers' Licence Rules, 1960 or a valid licence of a Stamp Vendor under the Kerala Manufacture and Sale of Stamp Rules, 1960, and is below the age of 65 years on the date of application, may apply to the Board for admission as a member. Provided that where the Fund, under the Kerala Document Writers, Scribes and Stamp Vendors Welfare Fund Scheme, 1991, is transferred to this Act, those who are members of the said Scheme shall be deemed to be members of the Fund. Provided further that no person employed as a Document Writer, Scribe or Stamp Vendor after retiring from the service of the Central Government or any State Government or any public sector undertaking or local Authority with retirement benefits, shall be eligible for membership. On an application under sub-section (1), the Board may make such enquiry as it deems fit and further admit the applicant to the Fund or for reasons to be recorded in writing reject the application. Provided that no order rejecting an application shall be passed unless the applicant has been given an opportunity of being heard. Provided further that any person aggrieved by an order rejecting any application for membership may prefer an appeal to the Government within such period as may be specified in the Scheme. Every applicant shall pay an application fee of one hundred rupees along with the application in such manner as may be specified in the Scheme. A member of the Fund, on completion of 65 years of age or on voluntarily applying for pension by surrendering his licence after 25 years of membership, shall cease to be a member of the Fund. Every person who has been enrolled as member in the Fund shall be given certificate of membership and pass book recording the rate of contribution, details of enrolment in the register, date of birth, due date for payment of contribution etc., by the Registering Authority. The Registering Authority shall keep a register of members coming under its jurisdiction and at the State level, the Secretary of Board shall keep a register of members enrolled in the Fund, showing the district-wise details of members.

This section states that the membership of a member shall be cancelled by the Registering Authority if it is found that a member has made manipulation of any kind or has given false information at any time in connection with the conditions for the membership or to obtain benefits as per the Scheme.

important_rules: Every Document Writer, Scribe and Stamp Vendor eligible to become a member shall pay a prescribed contribution per month to the Fund.

The Government may, by notification, from time to time, revise the rate of contribution referred to in sub-section (1) up to a maximum limit of five hundred rupees, taking into account the amount required for the management of the Scheme.

Any person holding a valid licence of document writer or scribe under the Kerala Document Writers' Licence Rules, 1960 or a valid licence of a Stamp Vendor under the Kerala Manufacture and Sale of Stamp Rules, 1960, and is below the age of 65 years on the date of application, may apply to the Board for admission as a member.
Every applicant shall pay an application fee of one hundred rupees along with the application in such manner as may be specified in the Scheme.
A member of the Fund, on completion of 65 years of age or on voluntarily applying for pension by surrendering his licence after 25 years of membership, shall cease to be a member of the Fund.

Every person who has been enrolled as member in the Fund shall be given certificate of membership and pass book recording the rate of contribution, details of enrolment in the register, date of birth, due date for payment of contribution etc., by the Registering Authority.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Registering Authority, Government, Board
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Cancellation of membership for manipulation or false information; appeals to the Government for rejected applications.

rights: Right to pension and other benefits from the Welfare Fund.
Right to appeal to the Government against rejection of membership application.
duties: Duty to pay monthly contributions to the Fund.
Duty to provide accurate information for membership and benefits.
Duty to adhere to the provisions of the Scheme.
obligations: Obligation to pay application fee for membership.

key_procedures: Framing of a Scheme by the Government for the Welfare Fund.
Constitution of the Welfare Fund Board.
Application for membership by eligible persons.
Enquiry by the Board before admitting an applicant.
Issuance of certificate of membership and pass book.
Payment of contributions by members.
Cessation of membership under certain conditions.
Cancellation of membership for manipulation or false information.
administration: The Board (Kerala Document Writers', Scribes' and Stamp Vendors' Welfare Fund Board) administers the Fund, and the Government has overall regulatory authority.
important_notes: The Act is a translation in English of '2012-ലെ കേരള ഡോക്യുമെന്റ് എഴുത്തുകാരുടേയും കൈയെഴുത്ത് പ്രതി എഴുത്തുകാരുടേയും സ്റ്റാമ്പ് വില്പനക്കാരുടേയും ക്ഷേമനിധി നിയമം' published under the authority of the Governor.
Explanation 1 under Section 3: The Board has the power to take decision regarding the eligibility of pensionary benefits payable to a member who could not continue his employment due to ill health.

Explanation 2 under Section 3: A person who had completed sixty-five years of age and who had been a Document Writer, Scribe or Stamp Vendor for twenty five years before the commencement of this Act shall become eligible for special pension if he becomes a member and remits contribution for a period of one year under the provisions of this Act.

title: THE KERALA DRAMATIC PERFORMANCES ACT, 1961
purpose: To provide for better control of public dramatic performances in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to public dramatic performances in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.objectionable_performance: Any play, pantomime or other drama which is grossly indecent, scurrilous or obscene; or is likely to seduce any member of any of the armed forces of the Union of India or of any police force from his allegiance or his duty, or prejudice the recruiting of persons to serve in any such force; or is deliberately intended to outrage the religious feelings of any class of the citizens of India by insulting or blaspheming or profaning the religion or the religious beliefs of that class.
key_definitions.public_place: Includes any building or enclosure or any place in the open air and any pandal where the sides are not enclosed to which the public are admitted to witness a performance.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Dramatic Performances Act, 1961. It shall come into force at once.
Defines 'objectionable performance' and 'public place'.

The Government is satisfied that any play, pantomime or other drama performed or about to be performed in a public place is an objectionable performance, they may, by order stating the grounds on which they consider the performance objectionable, prohibit the performance.
The District Collector can prohibit temporarily performances if there is a reasonable opportunity of such performance being objectionable.
Details how orders of prohibition are served.
Penalties for disobeying an order of prohibition.
Penalties for persons who disobey orders of prohibition, including imprisonment and fines.
The Government or District Collector can call for information regarding intended performances.

main_sections.section_title: Power to call for copy of purport of drama, etc.
main_sections.description: Power to require copies of plays or pantomimes for examination.
Provides for appeals to the High Court against orders of prohibition.

main_sections.section_title: Saving of prosecutions under other laws.
main_sections.description: This Act does not prevent prosecution under other laws.

main_sections.section_title: Protection for acts done in good faith.
main_sections.description: No suit, prosecution or other legal proceedings shall be instituted against any authority or officer for anything done in good faith under this Act.
The Government may make rules to carry out the purposes of this Act.
Repeals certain previous acts related to dramatic performances.

important_rules: Rule 1: No order under sub-section (1) shall be made without giving a reasonable opportunity to the organizer or other principal persons responsible for the conduct of the performance or the owner or occupier of the public place in which such performance is intended to take place to show cause why the performance should not be prohibited.
Rule 2: Every order made under sub-section (1) shall be published in the Gazette.

Rule 3: All rules made under sub-section (1) shall, as soon as possible after they are made, be laid on the table of the Legislative Assembly for a period of fourteen days and shall be subject to such modification by way of repeal or amendment as the Legislative Assembly may make during the session in which they are so laid or the Session immediately following.

penalties: Penalty for disobeying order: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or both.
Penalty for disobeying prohibition: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: District Collector and Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By issuing orders of prohibition, calling for information, and imposing penalties including fines and imprisonment.

rights: Right to appeal to the High Court against an order of prohibition.
duties: Duty to comply with orders of prohibition.
Duty to provide information when called for.
obligations: Obligation for organizers, performers, owners, and occupiers of public places to ensure performances are not objectionable.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Prohibition of objectionable performances involves the Government being satisfied that a performance is objectionable, issuing an order stating the grounds, and publishing it in the Gazette. The concerned parties must be given an opportunity to show cause before the order is made.

Procedure 2: Temporary prohibition can be ordered by the District Collector if there is a reasonable opportunity of an immediate objectionable performance, without prior notice in certain circumstances. However, the order must be served and published in the Gazette.
Procedure 3: Appeal against an order of prohibition can be filed with the High Court within a specified period.
administration: The Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act was enacted in the Twelfth Year of the Republic of India.
The publication of the Act was in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 26th December 1961.

The Travancore Dramatic Performances Act, 1115, the Cochin Dramatic Performances Act, LX of 1112, and the Madras Dramatic Performances Act, 1954 (XXIII of 1954) are repealed as far as they apply to the Malabar district referred to in sub-section (2) of section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.

title: THE KERALA EDUCATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1985
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Education Act, 1958.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Education Act, 1958 and any actions taken or deemed to have been taken or done or any action amended by this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Education (Amendment) Act, 1985 and that it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 13th day of October, 1982.
Amends sub-section (1) of section 36 of the Kerala Education Act, 1958 (6 of 1959) by inserting the words "either prospectively or retrospectively" after the words "The Government may make rules".

Repeals the Kerala Education (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984 (91 of 1984). It also provides that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken or done under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

administration: The Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 11th day of April, 1985.
Published in the Kerala Gazette, Extraordinary No. 307 dated the 12th April, 1985.

title: The Kerala Education (Amendment) Act, 2021
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Education Act, 1958 for purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Kerala and amends the Kerala Education Act, 1958, specifically concerning the administration and definitions related to education within the state.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as 'The Kerala Education (Amendment) Act, 2021' and states that it is deemed to have come into force on May 31, 2019.
Amends section 4 of the principal Act by substituting 'Department of Education' with 'Department of General Education' and 'Director of Public Instruction' with 'Director of General Education'.
Amends sub-section (1) of section 9 of the principal Act by replacing 'Headmaster' with 'Headmaster or Headmistress or Principal or Vice-Principal, as the case may be'.
Amends sub-section (2) of section 17 of the principal Act by substituting 'Headmasters' with 'Headmasters or Headmistresses or Principals, as the case may be' in clauses (g) and (h).
Amends clause (iv) of section 22 of the principal Act by substituting 'Education Department' with 'Department of General Education'.
Amends section 34 of the principal Act by substituting 'Education Department' with 'Department of General Education'.

Repeals The Kerala Education (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021 (101 of 2021) and provides that anything done or deemed to have been done under the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done under this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated in the provided text, but implied to be governmental education authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amendments to the principal Act, implying enforcement through existing legal and administrative channels.

administration: Department of General Education (implied by amendments).
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on May 31, 2019.
The Act repeals The Kerala Education (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021.

title: The Kerala Education (Amendment) Act, 1969
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala Education Act, 1958.
scope: The act applies to the Kerala Education Act, 1958, and any educational institutions covered by it.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Education (Amendment) Act, 1969.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new section after section 12.
main_sections.description: Inserts a new section 12A, granting disciplinary powers to the Government or authorized officers over teachers of aided schools. It outlines procedures for disciplinary action, including suspension and taking action against the teacher concerned.
Repeals the Kerala Education (Amendment) Ordinance, 1969 (3 of 1969) and saves any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Government or an authorized officer can impose disciplinary powers over teachers of aided schools.
Rule 2: Notwithstanding anything contained in section 11 or section 12, the Government or authorized officer can take disciplinary proceedings and suspend teachers.

Rule 3: Before exercising powers of suspension, the Government or authorized officer must inform the manager regarding circumstances requiring disciplinary action and give the manager a reasonable opportunity to take action.
Rule 4: If the manager fails to take appropriate action, the Government or authorized officer can take disciplinary action against the teacher.

penalties: Penalties specified in the rules made under this Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government or the authorized officer.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through disciplinary proceedings, including suspension and imposition of penalties as specified in the rules.

rights: Right to impose disciplinary powers over teachers of aided schools.
Right to suspend teachers pending disciplinary proceedings.
Right to take disciplinary action if the manager fails to act.
duties: Duty to give the manager a reasonable opportunity to take disciplinary action before the Government or authorized officer intervenes.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: The Government or authorized officer can take disciplinary proceedings against teachers of aided schools, including suspension.
Procedure 2: Before suspending a teacher, the Government or authorized officer must inform the manager and provide an opportunity for the manager to take action.
Procedure 3: If the manager does not take appropriate action, the Government or authorized officer can proceed with disciplinary action.
administration: The Department responsible for education in Kerala.
important_notes: The Act amends the Kerala Education Act, 1958.
The Act is published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 209 dated 11th September, 1969.
The Act is referred to as Act 31 of 1969.

title: THE KERALA EDUCATION (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 1960
purpose: To amend the Kerala Education Act, 1958, for the purposes herein after appearing.
scope: The Act applies to the whole of the State of Kerala and comes into force at once.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Education (Second Amendment) Act, 1960. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. It shall come into force at once.

For section 11 of the Kerala Education Act, 1958 (6 of 1959), the following section shall be substituted: "11. Appointment of teachers in aided schools. Subject to the rules and conditions laid down by the Government, teachers of aided schools shall be appointed by the managers of such schools from among persons who possess the qualifications prescribed under section 10."

For section 12 of the principal Act, the following section shall be substituted, namely: "12. Conditions of service of aided school teachers.— (1) The conditions of service of teachers in aided schools, including conditions relating to pay, pension, provident fund, insurance and age of retirement, shall be such as may be prescribed by the Government. (2) A teacher in an aided school shall be dismissed, removed or reduced in rank by the manager without the previous sanction of the officer authorised by the Government in this behalf or placed under suspension by the manager for a continuous period exceeding fifteen days without previous sanction."

In section 13 of the principal Act, the words and figures "notwithstanding the fact that they are not included in the list of candidates selected by the Public Service Commission under section 11" shall be omitted.

In section 36, sub-section (2) of the principal Act, after clause (e), the following shall be inserted as clause (ee) regulating admissions to schools maintained by the Government or receiving aid out of State funds, by making special provisions for the advancement of socially and Educationally backward classes of citizens and the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes:.
The Kerala Education (Amendment) Act, 1963 (8 of 1960), is hereby repealed.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Officer authorised by the Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Sanction from the authorised officer is required for dismissal, removal, or reduction in rank of teachers in aided schools.

obligations: Managers of aided schools must appoint teachers possessing prescribed qualifications.
Conditions of service for aided school teachers are subject to government prescription.

key_procedures: Appointment of teachers in aided schools is done by managers, subject to rules and qualifications.
Dismissal, removal, or reduction in rank of aided school teachers requires prior sanction from a government-authorised officer.
Suspension of aided school teachers for more than fifteen days requires prior sanction from a government-authorised officer.
administration: Law Department, Secretariat, Kerala State
important_notes: The amendment is to the Kerala Education Act, 1958.
Section 13 amendment removes a condition regarding the Public Service Commission list.
Section 36 amendment allows for special provisions for socially and educationally backward classes, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in admissions.
The Kerala Education (Amendment) Act, 1963, is repealed.

title: The Kerala Education Act, 1958
purpose: To provide for the better organisation and development of educational institutions in the State.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. It applies to all schools within the state. It also outlines provisions for Government and private schools, aided schools, and educational agencies.

key_definitions.aided school: means a private school which is recognised by and is receiving aid from the Government, but shall not include educational institutions entitled to receive grants under article 337 of the Constitution of India, except in so far as they are receiving aid in excess of the grants to which they are so entitled.
key_definitions.educational agency: means any person or body of persons permitted to establish and maintain any private school under this Act.
key_definitions.existing school: means any aided, recognised or Government school established before the commencement of this Act and continuing as such at such commencement;
key_definitions.Local Educational Authority: means the authority constituted by the Government under section 17;
key_definitions.minority schools: means schools of their choice established and administered, or administered, by such minorities as have the right to do so under clause (1) of article 30 of the Constitution;
key_definitions.prescribed: means prescribed by rules made under this Act;
key_definitions.private school: means an aided or recognised school;
key_definitions.recognised school: means a private school recognised by the Government under this Act;
key_definitions.school: includes the land, buildings, playgrounds and hostels of the school and the movable properties such as furniture, books, apparatus, maps and equipments pertaining to the school;

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its applicability to the whole of the State of Kerala, and that it shall come into force on such date as the Government may appoint.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'aided school', 'educational agency', 'existing school', 'Local Educational Authority', 'minority schools', 'prescribed', 'private school', 'recognised school', 'school', and 'State'.

Outlines the Government's role in regulating the establishment and recognition of schools, including primary and other stages of education and teacher training. It also empowers the Government to establish and maintain schools or permit persons to do so, and to recognise any school.
Establishes the State Education Advisory Board to advise the Government on educational policy and administration. It details the composition of the Board, including the Chairman and other members.

main_sections.section_title: Manager to send list of properties.
main_sections.description: Requires the manager of every aided school to furnish a statement of all movable and immovable properties of the school to the Government by the first day of April each year.

main_sections.section_title: Restriction on alienation of property of aided school.
main_sections.description: Prohibits the sale, mortgage, lease, pledge, charge, or transfer of possession of any property of an aided school without the previous permission in writing of the District Educational Officer.

Specifies that any educational agency may appoint a manager of an aided school, subject to approval by the Government. It also outlines the responsibilities of the manager, including the conduct of the school, the possession and control of school properties, and maintaining records and accounts.

main_sections.section_title: Recovery of amounts due from the manager.
main_sections.description: Details the process for the recovery of any amount due from the manager of an aided school to the Government, including through agreement, scheme, or as arrears of salary. It also outlines the procedure for inquiry and recovery of amounts due to teachers.

main_sections.section_title: Salary of teachers, etc., and grants to aided schools.
main_sections.description: States that the manager of an aided school shall pay the salary of all teachers. It also outlines the Government's role in paying the salary of non-teaching staff and making grants to aided schools for purposes like maintenance, improvement, and repairs.
Empowers the Government to prescribe the qualifications for appointment of teachers in Government and private schools.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of teachers in Government and aided schools.
main_sections.description: Requires the Public Service Commission to select candidates for appointment as teachers in Government and aided schools, with due regard to the number of vacancies and the courses of the year.

penalties: Conviction for contravening provisions of sub-section (8) of section 7 may lead to a fine extending to two hundred rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: District Educational Officer, Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Permission for alienation of property, inquiry into amounts due from managers, recovery of amounts, and appointment of teachers are subject to prescribed procedures and approval from the relevant authorities.

rights: Minority communities have the right to establish and administer schools of their choice under article 30 of the Constitution.
duties: Managers of schools are responsible for the conduct of the school and the properties thereof.
Managers are responsible for maintaining school properties in proper and good condition.
