Managers are responsible for maintaining records and accounts of the school.
Guardians have an obligation to send their children to school.
obligations: Obligation on guardian to send children to school.

key_procedures: Procedure for appointment of teachers in Government and aided schools involves selection by the Public Service Commission.
Procedure for recovery of amounts due from the manager of an aided school to the Government.
Procedure for recovery of amounts due to teachers from the manager.
Procedure for obtaining permission for alienation of property of an aided school.
administration: The Department of Education and the State Education Advisory Board are involved in the administration of the Act.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the President on 19th February, 1959 and was published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 24th February, 1959.

The establishment of new schools or the opening of a higher class in any private school is subject to the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder, unless otherwise notified by the Government.
No court shall take cognizance of an offence punishable under sub-section (8) except with the previous sanction of the Government.

title: THE KERALA EDUCATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1960
purpose: To suspend temporarily the operation of section 11 of the Kerala Education Act, 1958.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and relates to educational matters covered by the Kerala Education Act, 1958.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called, the Kerala Education (Amendment) Act, 1960.

main_sections.section_title: Suspension of operation of section 11 of Act 6 of 1959 and the rules thereunder
main_sections.description: Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (3) of section 1 of the Kerala Education Act, 1958 (6 of 1959), and in Notification No. Ed. (C. Spl.) 21564/59/EHD, dated 27th May, 1959, bringing into force section 11 and certain other sections of the said Act with effect from the first day of June 1959, nothing in the said section 11 or in the Kerala Education Rules 1959, in so far as such rules relate to matters provided for in that section, shall come into operation or shall be deemed ever to have come into operation until the first day of January, 1961.
The Kerala Education (Amendment) Ordinance, 1960 (No. 2 of 1960), is hereby repealed.

important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 8th July 1960.

title: The Kerala Electricity Duty (Amendment) Act, 1972
purpose: To amend The Kerala Electricity Duty Act, 1963. The preamble indicates it is expedient to amend the Act for the purpose appearing.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala. It specifically relates to the Electricity Duty.

key_definitions.Explanation (to section 2): Where any licensee consumes energy generated by himself or supplied to him by the Kerala State Electricity Board, he shall be deemed to be a consumer in respect of the energy so consumed except in respect of the energy consumed by him for purpose connected with the construction, maintenance and operation for his generating, transmitting and distributing systems.

main_sections.description: (1) This Act may be called the Kerala Electricity Duty (Amendment) Act, 1972. (2) It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 15th day of April, 1963.
For the Explanation to sub-section (a) of section 2 of the Kerala Electricity Duty Act, 1963 (23 of 1963), the following shall be substituted, namely:—

important_rules: Consumption of energy by a licensee, generated by himself or supplied by the Kerala State Electricity Board, is deemed to be consumption by a consumer. This exception does not apply to energy consumed for construction, maintenance, and operation of his generating, transmitting, and distributing systems.
administration: The Kerala State Electricity Board is mentioned in relation to energy supply and consumption.
important_notes: The Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 740, dated 11th December, 1972.
The commencement date is retrospective, April 15, 1963.

title: The Kerala Electricity Duty (Amendment) Act, 1977
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Electricity Duty Act, 1963, for the purpose hereinafter appearing.
scope: This Act applies to Kerala and amends the Kerala Electricity Duty Act, 1963.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Electricity Duty (Amendment) Act, 1977.
In section 8 of the Kerala Electricity Duty Act, 1963 (23 of 1963), for the words "twelve per cent", the words "eighteen per cent" shall be substituted.

important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 23rd day of August, 1977 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 498 dated 25th August 1977.

title: THE KERALA ELECTRICITY DUTY (VALIDATION) ACT, 1965
purpose: To validate the levy and collection of duty on sales of electrical energy under the Travancore-Cochin Electricity Duty Act, 1950.
scope: Applies to sales of electrical energy where duty was levied or collected under the Travancore-Cochin Electricity Duty Act, 1950.

key_definitions.duty: Means the duty on sale of electrical energy.
key_definitions.repeated Act: Means the Travancore-Cochin Electricity Duty Act, 1950 (Travancore-Cochin Electricity Duty Act IV of 1950), repealed by section 18 of the Kerala Electricity Duty Act, 1965 (Kerala Act 23 of 1963).

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Electricity Duty (Validation) Act, 1965, and shall come into force at once.
Defines 'duty' and 'repeated Act'.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of levy and collection of duty on sales of electrical energy.—
main_sections.description: Sub-section (1) states that notwithstanding any judgment, decree, or order of any court, all duties levied or collected or purporting to have been levied or collected under the repealed Act and the rules made thereunder before the 15th day of April, 1963, are deemed to have been validly levied or collected in accordance with law. It also states that provisions relating to the levy and collection of such duty had been in force and had been included in, and formed part of, this section and this section had been in force at all material times when such duty was levied or collected. Sub-section (1) also clarifies that no suit or other proceeding shall be maintained or continued for the refund of any duty paid under the repealed Act and the rules made thereunder. Further, it clarifies that no court shall enforce a decree or order directing the refund of any duty paid under the repealed Act and the rules made thereunder. Sub-section (2) states that for the removal of doubts, it is hereby declared that nothing in sub-section (1) shall be construed as preventing any person from claiming refund of any duty paid by him in excess of the amount due from him under the repealed Act and the rules made thereunder.

important_notes: The Act was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 61, dated the 14th July, 1965.
The validation applies to the levy and collection of duty on sales of electrical energy under the Travancore-Cochin Electricity Duty Act, 1950.
The validation is retroactive, covering duties levied or collected before April 15, 1963.

title: The Kerala Electricity Surcharge (levy and collection) Act, 1989
purpose: To provide for the levy and collection of a surcharge on electricity consumed in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to all electricity consumed in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.consumer: Includes any person or entity who consumes electricity.
key_definitions.electricity: Includes electrical energy supplied or generated.
key_definitions.surcharge: The additional amount levied on electricity consumption.
key_definitions.State Government: Refers to the Government of Kerala.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the date from which it comes into force.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'consumer', 'electricity', 'surcharge', and 'State Government'.
Specifies the rate at which the surcharge is to be levied on electricity consumed and outlines any exemptions or conditions.
Details the procedure for collecting the surcharge by the electricity supply undertaking and remitting it to the State Government.
Grants the State Government the power to exempt certain categories of consumers or areas from the levy of surcharge under specific circumstances.
Empowers the State Government to frame rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Certain provisions to override other laws
main_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent contained in any other law for the time being in force.
Specifies penalties for contravening the provisions of the Act or rules made thereunder.
Provides the State Government with the power to make orders to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of any previous enactments on the subject and savings of certain actions taken thereunder.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the Kerala State Electricity Board (Additional Surcharge) Act, 1984
main_sections.description: Amends the Kerala State Electricity Board (Additional Surcharge) Act, 1984.
Empowers the Government to remove difficulties in the application of the Act.

important_rules: Electricity supply undertakings are responsible for levying and collecting the surcharge.
The collected surcharge must be remitted to the State Government within the prescribed period.
Certain consumers or areas may be exempted from the surcharge as per government orders.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
Failure to comply with provisions can lead to penalties.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government and designated authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through prescribed procedures for levy, collection, and remittance of the surcharge, and by imposing penalties for non-compliance.

rights: Consumers have the right to be informed about the surcharge and its application.
The State Government has the right to levy and collect the surcharge for public purposes.
duties: Electricity supply undertakings have the duty to correctly levy, collect, and remit the surcharge.
Consumers have the duty to pay the surcharge as applicable.
obligations: To comply with the provisions of the Act and the rules framed thereunder.

key_procedures: Levy of surcharge on electricity consumption.
Collection of surcharge by electricity supply undertakings.
Remittance of collected surcharge to the State Government.
Application for exemption from surcharge (if applicable).
Enforcement of penalties for non-compliance.
administration: The State Government, likely through its Electricity Department or designated agencies.
important_notes: The Act aims to generate additional revenue for the State by imposing a surcharge on electricity.
Specific rates of surcharge and exemption categories are detailed in the Act and its subsequent rules.
The Act amends the Kerala State Electricity Board (Additional Surcharge) Act, 1984.

title: The Kerala Enquiries and Summonses (Amendment) Act, 1962
purpose: To amend the Kerala Enquiries and Summonses Act, 1960.
scope: Applies to enquiries and summonses in Kerala. It specifically amends Section 9 of the principal Act and its sub-sections regarding the powers of a government officer to conduct enquiries.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Enquiries and Summonses (Amendment) Act, 1962.

This section details the amendments to Section 9 of the Kerala Enquiries and Summonses Act, 1960. It clarifies that 'conduct of any public servant' includes their conduct as a public servant. It also expands the powers of a Government officer in conducting enquiries to include summoning and enforcing attendance, requiring discovery and production of documents, receiving affidavits, requisitioning records, issuing commissions for examining witnesses, and any other matter specified in the notification.

Repeals the Kerala Enquiries and Summonses (Amendment) Ordinance, 1962. It also includes a saving clause stating that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken in the exercise of powers conferred by or under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken in the exercise of the powers conferred by or under this Act if such thing was done or action was taken.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, invest any officer deputed by them to make an enquiry into the conduct of any public servant with the powers of a civil court while trying a subject under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, in respect of the following matters.

Rule 2: Powers conferred on officers include summoning and enforcing attendance, requiring discovery and production of documents, receiving affidavits, requisitioning public records, and issuing commissions for examination of witnesses.
Rule 3: Anything done or any action taken under the repealed Ordinance is deemed valid if it aligns with the provisions of this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government (by notification)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By investing specified officers with powers of a civil court for conducting enquiries into the conduct of public servants.

rights: Right of the Government to invest officers with civil court powers for enquiries.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Government issues a notification to invest an officer with civil court powers for enquiries.
Procedure 2: The invested officer conducts enquiries by summoning witnesses, requiring documents, etc., as if they were a civil court.
administration: Likely administered by the General Administration Department or a relevant department dealing with public service conduct and enquiries in the Kerala Government.
important_notes: The Amendment Act effectively brings the provisions of the repealed Ordinance into permanent statute.
The powers conferred are specifically for enquiries into the conduct of public servants.

title: The Kerala Enquiries and Summonses Act, 1960
purpose: To make provision for facilitating enquiries into certain matters and to empower certain officers to issue summonses for the attendance of persons or the production of documents in enquiries.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Kerala Enquiries and Summonses Act, 1960', its extent to the whole of the State of Kerala, and its commencement date as published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 25th October, 1960.

main_sections.section_title: Revenue Officers empowered to summon persons to appear or to produce any document before them
main_sections.description: Empowers Revenue Officers, Collectors, Deputy Collectors, Revenue Divisional Officers, Tahsildars and Deputy Tahsildars to summon any person to appear, to produce any document or to answer any question necessary for the investigation of any matter.

States that summonses are issued by virtue of the powers conferred by Section 2, shall be in writing, authenticated by signature and seal of the officer, specifying the purpose, the place and time of appearance, and that the person summoned shall appear and produce documents.

Details the process of serving summonses by delivering a copy to the summoned person or to an adult male member of his family. If the person cannot be found, the summons can be affixed to the outer door of his house. If a written acknowledgement is obtained, it suffices as service.

main_sections.section_title: Persons summoned to produce documents may send them by third party
main_sections.description: Allows persons summoned to produce documents to send them by a third party if they are unable to appear in person due to sickness, infirmity, or other sufficient cause. Such persons are required to attend the inquiry if their attendance is necessary and they are summoned for the purpose of giving evidence.

main_sections.section_title: When personal attendance of witnesses may be dispensed with and procedure in such cases
main_sections.description: Allows for personal attendance to be dispensed with if the person is suffering from sickness, infirmity, or other sufficient cause preventing attendance, and they are summoned to give evidence. They may send a representative if necessary. However, if the officer deems their personal attendance essential for examination or disposition, they must appear.

main_sections.section_title: Travelling and other expenses of persons summoned
main_sections.description: States that rules for travelling and other expenses of summoned persons are to be made by the Government and published in the Gazette.

Requires persons summoned for examination to answer truly all questions relating to the matter, failing which they may be liable to criminal charge or penalty/forfeiture. Statements made are not to be used as evidence against them in judicial proceedings, unless they are taken in evidence.

main_sections.section_title: Investment of powers on other officers
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to invest powers by notification in the Gazette upon any officer of public interest to summon any person to appear before them for enquiry, to produce documents or for inquiry, provided such powers are necessary for the conduct of such enquiry. The provisions of sections 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 shall apply to such enquiry.
Repeals the Acts mentioned in the Schedule as in force in the State of Kerala.

important_rules: Revenue Officers are empowered to summon persons to appear or to produce documents.
Summonses must be in writing, authenticated, and specify the purpose and place/time of appearance.
Persons summoned to produce documents may send them by a third party if unable to attend in person due to valid reasons.
Personal attendance of witnesses may be dispensed with under certain circumstances, but officers can still require it if deemed essential.
Summoned persons must answer all questions truthfully.
The Government can empower other officers to issue summonses for public interest enquiries.

penalties: Liability to a criminal charge or to a penalty or forfeiture for failing to answer questions truthfully or for other contraventions (as implied in section 8).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Revenue Officers (as defined in Section 2) and other officers empowered by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the issuance of summonses for appearance, production of documents, and truthful answers. Non-compliance can lead to criminal charges or penalties.

rights: Right to send a representative if personal attendance is dispensed with due to sickness, infirmity, or other sufficient cause (Section 5 & 6).
Statements made during examination are generally not to be used as evidence against the person in judicial proceedings (Section 8).
duties: Duty to appear in person or by authorized representative when summoned (Section 3, 5, 6).
Duty to produce documents when summoned (Section 3).
Duty to answer all questions truly relating to the matter under enquiry (Section 8).
obligations: Obligation to comply with the summons issued under the Act.

key_procedures: Issuance of summons by authorized officers.
Service of summons by delivery or affixation.
Appearance in person or by representative.
Production of documents.
Examination of witnesses and answering questions.
Dispensing with personal attendance under specific conditions.
administration: The Act is administered by the Government of Kerala, which has the power to make rules and empower officers.
important_notes: The Act is a repeal of earlier enactments mentioned in the Schedule.
The powers under the Act are exercisable by Revenue Officers and those empowered by the Government.
Provisions exist for sending documents by third party if personal attendance is not possible for producing documents.
The application of the Act is limited to the State of Kerala.

title: THE KERALA ESCHEATS AND FORFEITURES ACT, 1964
purpose: To provide for the administration, supervision, custody and disposal of escheats and unclaimed property in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to escheats and unclaimed property in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Board: Means the Board of Revenue for the State of Kerala constituted under the Kerala Board of Revenue Act, 1957.
key_definitions.Collector: Means the Collector of a district and includes any other officer empowered by the Government to exercise all or any of the powers of a Collector under this Act.
key_definitions.court: Means any civil court of competent jurisdiction.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Escheats and Forfeitures Act, 1964, and extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Defines 'Board', 'Collector', and 'court'.
Where a person dies intestate and without leaving legal heirs, all his property shall be escheat and shall belong to the Government.

Whenever the Collector receives information from any source that any person in possession of any movable or immovable property lying within his jurisdiction has died intestate and without legal heirs, he shall cause an inquiry to be made as to whether the deceased has died intestate and whether he has left any legal heirs.
After an inquiry, the Collector is satisfied that the deceased has died intestate, the inquiry report is to be published in the Gazette.
If any claim is preferred within the period fixed under section 5, the Collector shall investigate the claim and make his decision, which shall be final.
An appeal against the Collector's decision shall lie to the Board within three months from the date of the decision. Further appeal lies to the Government.
The decision of the Collector shall not give effect until the time for institution of a suit under section 11 is over or until the suit, if any instituted, is finally disposed of.

In the case of escheats which are movable property, the Collector shall take steps for the sale of the property by public auction in the manner prescribed, the sale proceeds being credited to the Government.

The Collector may take possession of escheat property, or property of a person dying intestate without heirs. If there is opposition or risk of damage, the Collector may file a suit to establish the right of the Government.

Nothing in this Chapter shall be held to prevent parties deeming themselves aggrieved by any decision or order passed or proceedings taken or purporting to be passed or taken from suing the Government in the civil courts.

main_sections.section_title: Police to take charge of unclaimed properties found on public places.
main_sections.description: Any article found in a public place, the owner of which is not known, shall be taken charge of by any police officer who shall send them for disposal to the Collector.
The Collector shall publish a notice in the Gazette inviting claims to prefer articles sent to him by the police under section 12 within three months from the date of publication of the notice.

If no claim is preferred within the period specified in sub-section (1) of section 13, the Collector shall pass an order for the forfeiture of the articles, and the articles shall thereupon be sold in public auction.
If a claim is preferred within the time allowed and it is not contested, the article shall be handed over to the claimant.
In the case of a contested claim, the Collector shall refer the matter to the court and shall be guided by the decision of the court.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to make rules.
main_sections.description: The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make rules for the purpose of carrying into effect the provisions of this Act. Such rules may provide for the superintendence and disposal of escheats and unclaimed articles; the manner in which property shall be managed by the Government; the procedure to be observed in public auctions under this Act; and any other matter which has to be, or may be, prescribed.

Repeals the Madras Escheats and Escheats Regulation, 1811 (VII of 1817) in so far as it relates to escheats in the Malabar District and section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (Central Act 37 of 1956).

important_rules: Property of a person dying intestate and without heirs escheats to the Government.
The Collector is responsible for investigating claims to escheat property.
Unclaimed articles found in public places are to be taken charge of by the police and sent to the Collector.
Published notice in the Gazette is required for unclaimed articles to allow claimants to come forward.
Articles not claimed within three months after publication of notice will be forfeited and sold.
Contested claims regarding escheat property or unclaimed articles must be referred to the court.
The Government has the power to make rules for the administration and disposal of escheats and unclaimed property.
Rules made by the Government shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly and shall have effect after fourteen days of being so laid, unless approved by the Assembly earlier.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Collector, Government, Civil Courts
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Investigation, decision by Collector, appeals to Board and Government, suits in civil courts, public auction of property.

rights: Right to appeal against the Collector's decision.
Right to sue in civil courts if aggrieved by a decision or order.
Right to claim unclaimed articles within the prescribed period.
duties: Duty of the Collector to investigate claims and manage escheat property.
Duty of police officers to take charge of unclaimed articles and send them to the Collector.
Duty to adhere to rules and procedures laid down in the Act and by the Government.
obligations: Obligation to follow the procedure for claiming property or articles.

key_procedures: For Escheats: Inquiry by Collector -> Publication in Gazette -> Investigation of claims -> Decision by Collector -> Appeal to Board/Government -> Disposal of property (sale).
For Unclaimed Property: Police take charge -> Send to Collector -> Publication in Gazette -> Claim period -> Forfeiture and sale if unclaimed, or return to claimant if claimed.
For Contested Claims: Reference to court and decision by court.
Making Rules: Government notification -> Laying before Legislative Assembly -> Effect after 14 days or earlier approval.
administration: Board of Revenue, Collector, Government
important_notes: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.
The Act came into force on a date notified by the Government.
The repeal of the Madras Escheats and Escheats Regulation, 1811, is specific to the Malabar District and section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.
Rules made under the Act can be modified or annulled by the Legislative Assembly.

title: THE KERALA ESCHEATS AND FORFEITURES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1976
purpose: To amend The Kerala Escheats and Forfeitures Act, 1964, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to abandoned property within Kerala.

key_definitions.abandoned_property: Any immovable property abandoned by the rightful owner thereof shall be abandoned property and shall belong to the Government.
key_definitions.preliminary_inquiry: Whenever the Collector receives information from any source that any immovable property situate within his jurisdiction has been abandoned by the rightful owner thereof, he shall cause an inquiry to be made as to which there is any legal claimant to such property.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Escheats and Forfeitures (Amendment) Act, 1976. It came into force on the date of receipt of the Governor's assent, which was on the 11th day of November, 1976 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 648, dated 13th November, 1976.

Inserts a new Chapter IIA titled "Abandoned Property" into The Kerala Escheats and Forfeitures Act, 1964. This chapter deals with the procedures for handling abandoned property, including preliminary inquiry, publication of notice, investigation and decision, appeal, taking possession by the Collector, saving of right to sue, and disposal of abandoned property.

Amends section 17 of the principal Act by replacing the words "escheats" with "escheats", and "abandoned property" with "abandoned property" in clause (a) of sub-section (2). It also inserts the words, figures and letter "or section 11F" at the end of clause (n) in sub-section (2).

important_rules: If any claim is preferred within six months from the date of publication of the notice, the Collector shall investigate the claim and decide the case.
No order under sub-section (1) or sub-section (2) shall be passed without giving all persons interested an opportunity of being heard.

If there is opposition in the taking possession of any property by the Collector under sub-section (1), the person in possession of the property may be left in possession thereof until the claim is finally settled.
The property taken possession of under sub-section (1), shall be managed by the Government in the manner prescribed.
Abandoned property shall not be sold until it has been in the possession of the Government for not less than twelve years.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Collector
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inquiries, notices, decisions, appeals, and taking possession of abandoned property.

rights: Right of rightful owners to claim abandoned property within a specified period.
Right of interested persons to be heard before any order is passed regarding abandoned property.
duties: Duty of the Collector to conduct preliminary inquiry upon receiving information about abandoned property.
Duty of the Collector to publish a notice regarding abandoned property.
Duty of the Collector to investigate claims and issue decisions.
Duty of the Government to manage the property taken possession of.
obligations: Obligation to provide information during preliminary inquiry.
Obligation to file claims within the stipulated time.

key_procedures: Preliminary Inquiry: Collector receives information, investigates if there's a legal claimant.
Publication of Notice: Collector publishes notice if satisfied about abandonment, inviting claims.
Investigation and Decision: Collector investigates claims and makes a decision.
Appeal: Aggrieved persons can appeal the Collector's decision to the Board and then to the Government.
Taking Possession: Collector can take possession of abandoned property.

Disposal of Property: Abandoned property can be disposed of according to the provisions of the Kerala Government Land Assignment Act, 1960, after being in government possession for at least twelve years.
administration: The Government, through the Collector and the Board.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 11th day of November, 1976.
Published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 648, dated 13th November, 1976.
The new Chapter IIA deals with abandoned property.
No order regarding abandoned property shall be passed without giving interested persons an opportunity of being heard.

title: The Kerala Essential Articles Control (Temporary Powers) Act, 1961
purpose: An Act to provide, in the interest of the general public, for the control of the production, supply and distribution of, and trade and commerce in, certain articles.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Kerala. It shall come into force at once and shall remain in force for a period of five years from the date of the commencement of this Act.

key_definitions.essential article: means any article (not being an essential commodity as defined in the Essential Commodities Act, 1955) which may be declared by the Government by notification ordered to be an essential article
key_definitions.Notified order: means an order notified in the Gazette
key_definitions.Undertaking: means any undertaking by way of trade or business and includes the occupation of handling, loading or unloading goods in the course of transport

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, commencement and duration
main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its extent (whole of Kerala), commencement, and duration (five years from commencement).
Defines 'essential article', 'Notified order', and 'Undertaking'.

main_sections.section_title: Powers to control production, supply, distribution, etc., of essential articles
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to make orders to secure the maintenance or increase of supplies of essential articles, for equitable distribution and availability at fair prices. This includes powers to regulate production, supply, distribution, trade, transport, storage, sale, acquisition, and dealing in essential articles, as well as to compel manufacturers and dealers to sell specific quantities to the Government or its agents. It also includes provisions for fixing prices and preventing hoarding.
Allows the Government to delegate its powers under this Act to any officer or authority subordinate to it, subject to specified conditions.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of orders inconsistent with other enactments
main_sections.description: Specifies that any order made under this Act, even if inconsistent with other enactments, shall have effect unless such other enactment has been repealed by this Act.

Outlines penalties for contravening orders made under Section 3, including imprisonment and fines. Penalties vary based on the specific contravention, with more severe penalties for repeated offenses or for acting with knowledge of falsity in false statements.
States that attempting to contravene or abetting the contravention of any order made under Section 3 shall be deemed to have contravened that order.

Makes it an offense to make or furnish any false information, statement, or document when required to do so under an order made under Section 3, if the person knows or has reasonable cause to believe the information to be false or does not believe it to be true.

Deals with offenses committed by companies, stating that if a company contravenes an order, every person in charge of the company's business at the time, as well as the company itself, shall be deemed guilty. It also holds directors, managers, secretaries, and other officers of the company liable if they were knowingly involved in the contravention or if the offense was committed with their connivance.

States that no court shall take cognizance of any offense made punishable by this Act except upon a report in writing of the facts constituting such offense made by a person who is a public servant as defined in section 21 of the Indian Penal Code.
Where an order purports to have been made and signed by an authority in exercise of any power conferred by or under this Act, a court shall presume that such order was so made by that authority.

When a person is prosecuted for contravening an order prohibiting the doing of a thing without a lawful authority or permit, the burden of proving that he has such authority or permit shall lie on him.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken under Act
main_sections.description: No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against any person for anything done or intended to be done in good faith in pursuance of any order made under section 3.

important_rules: Government can issue orders to control production, supply, distribution, trade, and commerce of essential articles.
Orders can regulate the production, supply, distribution, transport, storage, and sale of essential articles.
Orders can fix prices of essential articles.
Orders can compel the sale of essential articles to the Government or its agents.
Orders can prevent hoarding and ensure equitable distribution.
False statements made under orders are punishable.
Companies can be held liable for contraventions of orders, with officers also facing penalties.
Cognizance of offenses requires a report from a public servant.

penalties: Imprisonment which may extend to one year and shall also be liable to fine (for contravening orders under Section 3(g) or clause (e) of sub-section (2) of that section, with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year and also be liable to fine)

Imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years and shall also be liable to fine, or with both (for contravening any other order made under Section 3, with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years and also be liable to fine, or with both)
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both (for false statements)
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through orders issued under Section 3, with penalties for contravention. Enforcement also involves presumption of orders made and signed by authority, and burden of proof lying on the accused for certain violations. Protection is provided for actions taken in good faith.

rights: Right to assume that orders made and signed by authority are valid (Section 11).
duties: Duty to comply with orders made under Section 3 regarding essential articles.
Duty to not make false statements when required by an order.
Duty of companies and their officers to ensure compliance with orders.
obligations: Obligation to provide essential articles at fair prices.
Obligation to cooperate with government control measures for essential articles.

key_procedures: Government issues 'Notified orders' under Section 3 to control essential articles.
Individuals or companies contravening these orders face penalties.
Offenses are taken cognizance of upon a report from a public servant.
Burden of proof may shift to the accused to prove lawful authority or permit for certain contraventions.
administration: The Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act was enacted in the Twelfth Year of the Republic of India and came into force on 17th January 1962.
The Act is temporary and had an initial duration of five years.
Orders made under this Act have effect even if inconsistent with other enactments, unless the other enactment is repealed by this Act.
Protection is afforded to persons acting in good faith under this Act.

title: The Kerala Essential Articles Control (Temporary Powers) Continuance Act, 1979
purpose: To continue the Kerala Essential Articles Control (Temporary Powers) Act, 1961, for a further period.
scope: Applies to Kerala and continues the provisions of the Kerala Essential Articles Control (Temporary Powers) Act, 1961.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Essential Articles Control (Temporary Powers) Continuance Act, 1979.
Amends sub-section (3) of section 1 of the Kerala Essential Articles Control (Temporary Powers) Act, 1961 (3 of 1962) by substituting the words "seventeen years" with "twenty years".

(1) The Kerala Essential Articles Control (Temporary Powers) Continuance Ordinance, 1979 (1 of 1979), is hereby repealed. (2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act as if this Act had come into force on the 16th day of January, 1979.

important_notes: The Act continues the Kerala Essential Articles Control (Temporary Powers) Act, 1961.
The principal Act's duration was extended from seventeen years to twenty years.
The Kerala Essential Articles Control (Temporary Powers) Continuance Ordinance, 1979, is repealed.
Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.
The Act came into force on the 16th day of January, 1979.

title: THE KERALA ESSENTIAL ARTICLES CONTROL (TEMPORARY POWERS) CONTINUANCE ACT, 1969
purpose: To further continue the Kerala Essential Articles Control (Temporary Powers) Act, 1961.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala and concerns the control of essential articles through temporary powers.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Essential Articles Control (Temporary Powers) Continuance Act, 1969.
This section amends sub-section (3) of section 1 of the Kerala Essential Articles Control (Temporary Powers) Act, 1961, by substituting the words 'seven years' with 'nine years'.

important_notes: The Act is a continuance of the Kerala Essential Articles Control (Temporary Powers) Act, 1961.
The amendment changes the duration from seven years to nine years in the principal Act.
Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 14, dated 16th January 1969.

title: THE KERALA ESSENTIAL ARTICLES CONTROL (TEMPORARY POWERS) CONTINUANCE ACT, 1976
purpose: An Act further to continue the Kerala Essential Articles Control (Temporary Powers) Act, 1961, for a further period.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Essential Articles Control (Temporary Powers) Continuance Act, 1976.

In sub-section (3) of section 1 of the Kerala Essential Articles Control (Temporary Powers) Act, 1961 (3 of 1962) (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), for the words "fourteen years", the words "seventeen years" shall be substituted.

(1) The Kerala Essential Articles Control (Temporary Powers) Continuance Ordinance, 1976 (1 of 1976) is hereby repealed. (2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act as if this Act had come into force on the 15th day of January, 1976.

important_notes: Received the assent of the President on the 25th day of March, 1976 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 194, dated 25th March 1976.

title: The Kerala Essential Articles Control Act, 1986
purpose: To provide for the control, in the public interest, of the production, supply and distribution of essential articles and of the price at which they may be bought or sold, and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and to essential articles as defined in the Act.

key_definitions.essential_article: Any article or class of articles declared by the State Government by notification in the Gazette to be essential for the life of the community, having regard to the production, supply or distribution thereof and all or any of the following classes of articles, namely: food-stuffs, including edible oils and fats; cloths and textile piece-goods; fuel, including charcoal, firewood and kerosene; medicines and medical preparations; disinfectants; cattle fodder and concentrated feeding stuffs; and such other articles as the State Government may, by notification, specify.
key_definitions.dealer: A person carrying on the business of buying, selling or distributing any essential article, whether wholesale or retail, and includes a manufacturer, an importer and an exporter of any such article.
key_definitions.control_order: An order made under this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Essential Articles Control Act, 1986, and extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'essential article', 'dealer', and 'control order'.

main_sections.section_title: Power to control production, supply, distribution and price of essential articles
main_sections.description: Empowers the State Government to make orders to regulate or prohibit the production, supply, distribution, and price of essential articles. This includes requirements for licenses, permits, and the holding of stocks.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of entry, inspection, search and seizure
main_sections.description: Grants authorized officers the power to enter, inspect, search, and seize any place, vehicle, or article if they have reason to believe that any provision of the Act or any control order has been contravened.
Provides for an appeal against any order made by an authority under the Act or any control order.
Defines what constitutes an offence under the Act, including contravention of any provision of the Act or any control order, or failure to comply with any lawful order issued by an authority.
Prescribes penalties for offences under the Act, including imprisonment and fines. The penalties vary based on the gravity of the offence.

Specifies that no court shall take cognizance of any offence punishable under this Act except upon a report in writing of the facts constituting such offence made by a person authorized in this behalf by the State Government or the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection to government servants and other persons acting in good faith in pursuance of the provisions of this Act or any control order.
Empowers the State Government to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Dealers may be required to obtain licenses or permits to buy, sell, or distribute essential articles.
Dealers must maintain records of all transactions involving essential articles.
The State Government may fix the maximum price at which essential articles can be sold.
Movement of essential articles into or out of the State may be regulated or prohibited.
Stocks of essential articles must be reported and may be subject to limits.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
For contravention of any order regarding the refusal to sell an essential article, imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government, and officers authorized by the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspection, search, seizure, and prosecution of offenders.

rights: Consumers have the right to access essential articles at fair prices.
Dealers have the right to appeal against orders passed under the Act.
duties: Dealers have a duty to comply with the provisions of the Act and any control orders.
Dealers have a duty to maintain accurate records of transactions.
Dealers have a duty to sell essential articles at the prescribed prices.
obligations: Obligation to obtain necessary licenses or permits for dealing in essential articles.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining a license or permit for dealing in essential articles.
Procedure for reporting stocks of essential articles.
Procedure for appeal against orders passed under the Act.
Procedure for inspection, search, and seizure of essential articles and related documents.
administration: The Department of Food and Civil Supplies, Government of Kerala, is generally responsible for the administration of such acts.
important_notes: The Act aims to ensure the availability of essential articles at fair prices to the public.
The State Government has wide powers to control the production, supply, distribution, and price of essential articles.
Penalties for contravention of the Act can be severe, including imprisonment and fines.

title: The Kerala Essential Articles Control (Temporary Powers) Continuance Act, 1967
purpose: To continue the Kerala Essential Articles Control (Temporary Powers) Act, 1961, for a further period.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala, regarding the control of essential articles under temporary powers.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Essential Articles Control (Temporary Powers) Continuance Act, 1967.
Amends sub-section (3) of section 1 of the Kerala Essential Articles Control (Temporary Powers) Act, 1961 (Kerala Act 3 of 1962) by substituting the words "five years" with "seven years".

administration: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be administered under the framework of the original Act.
important_notes: Published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 13, dated 16th January, 1967.

title: The Kerala Essential Services Maintenance Act, 1994
purpose: To provide for the maintenance of certain essential services and the prohibition of strikes, lock-outs, and other disturbances in such services. This act aims to ensure the continuous supply and service of certain essential commodities and services to the public.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala and to such essential services as may be specified by the Government by notification. The Act primarily concerns employment in essential services.

key_definitions.essential_service: Includes services specified in the Schedule or declared as such by the Government, such as public transport, supply of electricity, water, and medical services.
key_definitions.strike: A cessation of work by a body of persons employed in any essential service acting in combination or a refusal under a common understanding of any number of persons who are, or have been, employed in any essential service to continue to work or accept employment.
key_definitions.lock-out: The closing of a place of employment or the suspension of work, or the refusal by an employer to continue to employ any persons employed by him.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act and its commencement date. The Act is called The Kerala Essential Services Maintenance Act, 1994.
This section defines various terms used in the Act, including 'essential service', 'strike', 'lock-out', 'employer', 'employee', etc.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of strikes and lock-outs in certain essential services
main_sections.description: This section prohibits strikes and lock-outs in specified essential services. It empowers the Government to declare any service as an essential service and prohibit strikes or lock-outs therein.
This section provides the Government with the power to prohibit sympathetic strikes in essential services.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make orders in respect of employees in essential services
main_sections.description: This section grants the Government the power to make orders regarding the employment of persons in essential services, including their transfer or posting.

main_sections.section_title: General prohibition of strikes and lock-outs
main_sections.description: This section broadly prohibits strikes and lock-outs in essential services.
This section deals with the power of the Government to issue orders related to the maintenance of essential services. It mentions the repeal and saving of certain provisions of prior acts.
This section outlines the penalties for contravening the provisions of the Act, including imprisonment and fines.

important_rules: Employees in essential services are prohibited from participating in strikes.
Employers are prohibited from declaring lock-outs in essential services.
Sympathetic strikes in essential services are prohibited.
The Government can issue orders to ensure the continuous functioning of essential services.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both (for contravention of certain provisions).
Fine for continuing strike/lock-out.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government of Kerala and its appointed authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings, imposition of penalties (fines and imprisonment), and government orders to ensure compliance.

duties: Duty of employees to not participate in strikes in essential services.
Duty of employers to not declare lock-outs in essential services.
Duty to comply with orders issued by the Government under the Act.
obligations: Obligation to maintain the continuous supply and service of essential commodities and services.

key_procedures: Declaration of essential services by the Government through notification.
Issuance of orders by the Government to prohibit strikes/lock-outs or to regulate employment.
Legal proceedings and penalties for violations of the Act.
administration: The Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act repeals and saves certain provisions of the Essential Services Maintenance Act, 1968, as amended by the Kerala Essential Services Maintenance Ordinance, 1993.
The Act aims to prevent disruption of services that are vital for the public.

title: The Kerala Farmers' Debt Relief Commission Act, 2006
purpose: To provide relief to farmers who are in distress due to indebtedness, by constituting a Commission with power to pass awards after adjudication and to recommend appropriate measures for the redressal of the grievances of such farmers through conciliation and negotiation and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to farmers who are in distress due to indebtedness. The benefits conferred by the Act are available only in respect of debts incurred by farmers before the 29th December, 2001. The scope also covers "agriculture" which includes horticulture, farming and growing of medicinal plants, crops and intercrops, fruits, vegetables, flowers, grass, fodder grass and trees or any kind of cultivation of soil, conducting nursery, breeding and keeping of livestock including fish, mussel, bees, silkworm, poultry, duck, cattle or pig and the use of land for agriculture allied activities or any other agricultural purposes.

key_definitions.agriculture: Includes horticulture, farming and growing of medicinal plants, crops and intercrops, fruits, vegetables, flowers, grass, fodder grass and trees or any kind of cultivation of soil, conducting nursery, breeding and keeping of livestock including fish, mussel, bees, silkworm, poultry, duck, cattle or pig and the use of land for agriculture allied activities or any other agricultural purposes.
key_definitions.agricultural labourer: Means a person who, in consideration of the wages payable to him by a landowner, works on the agricultural land of such landowner or does any other agricultural operation.
key_definitions.appropriate level of debt: Means the amount determined by the Commission as repayable by the debtor under clause (b) of sub-section (1) of section 5.
key_definitions.commission: Means the Kerala State Farmers' Debt Relief Commission constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.co-operative society: Means a society registered or deemed to have been registered under the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969 (21 of 1969).
key_definitions.creditor: Means any person engaged in money lending, whether under a licence or not and includes his heirs, legal representatives, assignees, co-operative society and any other person as may be notified by the Government.
key_definitions.debt: Means any liability, whether secured or unsecured, due from a farmer on or before the commencement of this Act, whether payable under a contract, or under a decree or order of any Court or Tribunal, or otherwise, and includes: (a) any sum payable to,-- (i) an institutional creditor, (ii) a co-operative society, (b) any sum borrowed by a farmer from the creditor.
key_definitions.farmer: Means a person who holds as owner, licensee, mortgagee in possession, oral lease, Government land lease "Kuthakapatnam" or partly in one capacity and partly in another with possession of an extent of land not exceeding four hectares and whose principal means of livelihood is agriculture and whose annual income does not exceed two lakhs rupees and includes an agricultural labourer, Kudumbasree and self help group units doing cultivation by taking over agricultural land on lease agreement condition.
key_definitions.financial institution: Means any financial institution constituted by or under any Central Act, State Act for the time being in force and owned and controlled by the Government.
key_definitions.institutional creditor: Means the State Bank of India or any Subsidiary Bank within the meaning of clause (k) of section 2 of the State Bank of India (Subsidiary Banks) Act, 1959 or any Scheduled Bank.
key_definitions.interest: Means any amount payable in excess of the principal amount borrowed or pecuniary obligation incurred, by whatsoever name such amount may be called, whether the same is expressly mentioned or not in the document or contract, if any.
key_definitions.member: Means a member of the Commission and includes the Chairman;
key_definitions.penal interest: Means any amount payable in excess of interest on a debt;
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules under this Act.
key_definitions.principal amount: Means the amount originally advanced together with the amount, if any, as has been subsequently advanced, notwithstanding any stipulation to treat any interest as capital and notwithstanding that the debt has been renewed, whether by the same farmer or by his heirs, assignees, or legal representatives or by any other person acting on his behalf or on his interest, and whether in favour of the same creditor or his heirs, assignees or legal representatives or of any other person acting on his behalf or on his interest.
key_definitions.secretary: Means the Secretary to the Commission appointed under sub-section (4) of Section 3.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Farmers' Debt Relief Commission Act, 2006 and shall come into force at once.

Details the establishment of the Kerala Farmers' Debt Relief Commission. It states the Government shall, as soon as may be after the commencement of this Act, by notification in the Gazette, constitute a Commission by the name 'The Kerala Farmers' Debt Relief Commission' for the purpose of exercising the powers and performing the functions under this Act. The Commission shall consist of five members: a retired High Court Judge (Chairman), an agricultural expert, two representatives of farmers, and a person working in economic/co-operative sector (Members). The Chairman and Members shall be nominated by the Government. The Government may appoint a Secretary and other staff as may be necessary, to assist the Commission. The Secretary shall be subject to the administrative control of the Chairman.

main_sections.section_title: Term of the Commission and conditions of service of the members
main_sections.description: Specifies that the term of the commission shall be 3 years, which the Government may extend. It also outlines conditions for resignation of a member, vacancy arising by resignation or otherwise, and grounds on which the Government may remove a member (declared as undischarged insolvent, becomes incapable of continuing, unsound mind, convicted for an offence involving moral turpitude or financial irregularities, or abused his official position). It also states the Commission shall regulate its own procedure and the salary and allowances of the Chairman and members shall be as prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and Functions of the Commission
main_sections.description: Outlines the powers and functions of the Commission. These include: (a) recommending to the Government suitable guidelines for declaring distress affected area or distress affected farmer; (b) fixing the rate of interest and appropriate level of debt payable by the farmer; (c) undertaking conciliation for settlement of disputes between indebted farmers and creditors; (d) adjudicating disputes between farmers and creditors and passing awards; (e) entering into negotiations for loan waiver, interest rate relief, loan rescheduling or loan moratorium; (f) recommending to the Government regarding the extent and manner of debt relief; (g) recommending to the Government to take over debt and exonerate farmers; (h) recommending to the Government to take such acts as may be necessary to ensure that future credit requirements of farmers are met; (i) making periodical reports to the Government on farmer indebtedness and performing other functions as prescribed. Additionally, the Commission has powers to issue orders in abeyance of repayment of all debts of farmers, considering crop loss, for a period not less than one year but not more than 3 years, subject to awards and directions under sub-section (1). Any debt relief granted by the waiver of principal, interest and penal interest shall not exceed seventy-five per cent of the debt if such debt is fifty thousand rupees or less and fifty per cent if such debt exceeds fifty thousand rupees, arrived at after settlement or rupees one lakh whichever is less. Awards passed by the Commission are final and shall not be called in question in any court. The Commission has powers to summon and enforce attendance, requiring discovery and production of documents, receiving evidence on affidavit, issuing commissions for examination of witnesses, inspecting property, and requisitioning public records. The Commission shall have the purpose of exercising the powers conferred by or under this Act, have all the powers of a Civil Court while trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

title: The Kerala Finance Act, 2003
purpose: To give effect to certain financial proposals of the Government of Kerala for the financial year 2003-2004.
scope: Applies to the financial year 2003-2004 in Kerala. It amends various existing acts and introduces duties and taxes on specific items like liquor and intoxicating drugs.

key_definitions.blending: The mixing of two different spirits of the same or different strength.
key_definitions.bonded_warehouse: Means a warehouse where liquor is stored in bond.
key_definitions.compounding: Means the preparation of foreign liquor by the addition of flavouring or colouring matter or both, to imported or Indian made spirits.
key_definitions.importer: Means a person who brings or causes to be brought any goods whether for himself or on behalf of his principal or any other person, into a local area, from any place outside the State for use, consumption or sales therein or who owns the goods at the time of entry into the local area.
key_definitions.foreign_liquor: Means any liquor produced, manufactured or blended and compounded abroad and imported into India by land, air or sea.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Kerala Finance Act, 2003 and specifies its commencement dates for different sub-sections.

Amends the Abkari Act, 1077 by inserting definitions for 'Blending', 'Bonded Warehouse', 'Compounding' and 'Foreign Liquor', and also introduces duty on liquor or intoxicating drugs and luxury tax on liquor.
Amends the Kerala Tax on Luxuries Act, 1976, by substituting certain words and phrases.
Amends the Kerala Tax on Entry of Goods into Local Areas Act, 1994, by substituting certain words, phrases and clauses. It also introduces a new section regarding 'Power to amend the Schedule'.

important_rules: No liquor or intoxicating drug shall be permitted to be exported unless the duties, taxes, fees and such other sums as are due to the Government under this Act in respect of such liquor or intoxicating drug have been paid or a bond for such payment on its exportation or re-exportation has been executed.
Duty on liquor or intoxicating drugs may be levied, in such manner as may be prescribed, on liquors or intoxicating drugs.
Luxury tax shall be levied at such rates as may be fixed by the Government, from time to time, by notification in the Gazette, not exceeding the rates specified below.

penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amendments to existing acts, levy of duties, taxes, fees, and luxury tax. Power to amend schedules and make rules is also granted.

Luxury tax on liquor to be levied and collected.
obligations: Payment of duties, taxes, fees and other sums due to the Government in respect of liquor or intoxicating drugs.

administration: Department of Finance, Government of Kerala

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Finance Act, 1985 and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1985.

Amends the Kerala Stamp Act, 1959. It specifies changes in rates and amounts for various entries in Schedule 4, including 'Five rupees', 'Ten rupees', 'Three rupees', 'Fifty rupees', 'Two hundred rupees', 'One thousand rupees', 'Seventy-five rupees', and 'fifty rupees'.

Amends the Kerala Plantation Tax Act, 1960. It substitutes Schedule I (Rates of Plantation Tax) with new rates based on the aggregate extent of plantations held by a person, differentiating between holdings not exceeding four hectares, not exceeding eight hectares, not exceeding twenty hectares, and exceeding twenty hectares.

Amends the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963. It details substitutions in the First Schedule regarding upholstered furniture and sofa sets, dressing tables, and other types of wood, rattan, or bamboo. It also specifies changes for hosiery goods made of cotton and other than those made of cotton. It further details amendments for 'Class of vehicle' under quarterly tax, including weights for unloaded bicycles and other vehicles.

Amends the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976. It specifies amendments for Motor Cycles (including Motor Scooters and Vehicles with attachment for propelling the same by mechanical power), differentiating between bicycles not exceeding 100 kg, not exceeding 200 kg, and exceeding 200 kg in unladen weight, as well as bicycles with side car or drawing a trailer. It also details amendments for vehicles not exceeding 750 kg, not exceeding 1500 kg, and not more than 2250 kg in unladen weight.

Amends the Kerala Tax on Luxuries in Hotels and Lodging Houses Act, 1976. It introduces a provision requiring proprietors to submit returns within a specified time and allows the assessing authority to proceed with the assessment even if the return is incorrect or incomplete, after giving the proprietor an opportunity to be heard and to produce relevant materials.
Amends the Kerala Additional Sales Tax Act, 1978. It states that the words 'fifteen per cent' shall be substituted with 'twenty per cent' in section 2, sub-section (1).

purpose: The act appears to be an amendment to various existing acts, primarily related to taxation and finance within the state of Kerala. title: The Kerala Finance Act, 2008
purpose: This Act amends various provisions of Kerala tax laws, including the Kerala Finance Act, 2005, to introduce changes in tax collection, assessment, and penalties, primarily related to sales tax and other levies. The objective is to enhance revenue collection and streamline tax administration.
scope: The Act applies to the state of Kerala and covers various categories of dealers, businesses, and specific goods and services as detailed within its sections. It impacts transactions, assessments, and compliance requirements within Kerala.

key_definitions.bar_attached_hotel: A hotel or restaurant or club or any other place, which is licensed under the Foreign Liquor Rules to serve foreign liquor falling under Serial Number 2 of the Fourth Schedule, but shall not include any hotel or restaurant, not being a star hotel, which is licensed to serve only beer.
key_definitions.sister_concern: Means a business run by a proprietorship or partnership, association of persons, or a company which is controlled by the dealer, or by a person whom the dealer controls, or by a person who is controlled by the same person who controls the dealer.

main_sections.description: Provides detailed explanations and clarifications for various clauses, including those related to 'bar attached hotel' and tax payment options for dealers of gold, silver, platinum group metals. It also covers scenarios like new branches, compounded tax, and tax on sales exceeding certain limits.

Deals with the tax payment options for dealers in ornaments or wares or articles of gold, silver or platinum group metals. It specifies tax at one hundred and fifty per cent of the highest tax payable by him as conceded in the return or accounts, or tax paid by him under this Act, whichever is higher, for a year during any of the three consecutive years preceding that to which such option relates.
Empowers the assessing authority to refuse permission to pay tax under this section if relevant information is not supplied, or if there is a failure to supply sufficient information.
States that notwithstanding anything contained in sections 55 or 60 of this Act, orders under sub-clause (ii) shall be appealable to the Appellate Tribunals.
Specifies that if permission has been cancelled, the amount, if any paid based on the permission, shall be apportioned against the output tax due of the dealer.

Deals with dealers who had tax paid for the succeeding year under this clause and states that one hundred and fifteen per cent of such tax paid during the previous year and in case of dealers covered under Explanation 6 of this clause, one hundred and fifteen per cent of the tax so re-determined.

Provides that the contractor may produce a liability certificate in relation to such works contracts from the assessing authority showing the tax liability or tax remittance, as the case may be, of the contractor in relation to the work.

Specifies that where a liability certificate has been produced as per sub-section (2), payment shall be effected to a work contractor, on the basis of the said certificate, and in case of work awarded by Government of Kerala, Kerala Water Authority or Local Authorities, after deducting four per cent of the amount paid as per the works contract, and in other cases, after deducting eight per cent of the amount paid as per the works contract in the case of contractors registered under this Act.

Provides that the awarder shall not insist from the contractor, not being a dealer registered under the provisions of the Central Sales Tax Act, 1956 (Central Act 74 of 1956) any certificate issued by the assessing authority showing the tax liability or tax remittances, as the case may be, of the contractor in relation to the work.
Amends the third proviso of section 8 of the Central Sales Tax Act, 1956, by substituting 'in excess of four per cent' for 'in excess of four per cent'.

Allows for input tax credit if the amount covered under credit notes issued by a supplier does not affect the input tax credit already availed of or on account of reimbursement of any expenses incurred by the dealer. It also allows for input tax credit on purchases made from a sister concern of the dealer where no input tax credit was availed and actual physical transfer of goods is involved.
Defines 'sister concern' for the purpose of the preceding provisos.
Amends the third proviso of section 8 of the Central Sales Tax Act, 1956, by substituting 'in excess of four per cent' for 'in excess of four per cent'.
Amends the second proviso of section 8 of the Central Sales Tax Act, 1956, by substituting 'in excess of four per cent' for 'in excess of four per cent'.

Introduces a new section, '15B Special drive for registration', requiring dealers who voluntarily applied for registration under the Act for the period from 15th December, 2007 to 31st March, 2008, to get registered. This includes obtaining registration with effect from the date of commencement of business irrespective of the date of application, claiming input tax credit on their purchases covered under bills/invoices of registered dealers within the State from the date of commencement of business, and paying tax under sub-section (5) of section 6, subject to eligibility and filing application for compounding upon registration.

States that any person who intends to establish an industrial unit may get himself registered under this section. Every application for registration of an Industrial Unit shall be supported by a certificate in the prescribed form issued by the Director of Industries and Commerce, the Kerala State Industrial Development Corporation or the Kerala Financial Corporation. A provisional registration certificate shall be issued to the applicant within seven days from the date of application. The form of application, fee for registration, the conditions and the authority empowered to issue such certificates shall be as may be certificate. The provisional registration certificate shall be issued under this section to facilitate the holder for procurement of all materials for construction and establishment of the Industrial Unit, including raw materials for trial production in such quantity as may be specified in such certificate. Every holder of a provisional registration certificate shall, before starting commercial production in the Industrial Unit, get himself registered under section 15.

Empowers the Deputy Commissioners having jurisdiction over the area to condone delay in filing any refund under this Act and Rules made thereunder, and in filing options under section 8 of this Act upto 31st December, 2008 for the years 2005-06, 2006-07 and 2007-08. It also extends the time limit for completion of any assessment under this Act by a further period of three years from the date of condoning such delay.

States that where on scrutiny of returns or verification of accounts in any proceedings under this Act, in respect of dealers paying tax under sub-section (3) of section 6, it is found that the amount of tax if any, paid by such dealer is less than the amount of tax he is liable to pay on finalising such proceedings, the assessing authority shall direct the dealer to pay difference of tax between the amount of tax already paid and that fixed in such proceedings, together with thrice the amount of such difference as penalty.
Stipulates that no proceeding made under sub-section (7) shall be completed without affording the dealer an opportunity of being heard.

Amends the words, brackets, figures and letters 'compounded tax under clause (a) to clause (d) of section 8', and 'tax under clause (a) of section 8 by those undertaking works of Government of Kerala, Kerala Water Authority and Local Authorities, and under clause (b), clause (c)(ii) and clause (d) of section 8' shall be substituted.

Introduces a proviso allowing dealers to use electronic billing and accounting subject to such restrictions and conditions as may be prescribed. It also introduces a clause in sub-section (9) that 'opportunity of being heard' and 'confiscate such goods' shall be inserted. It further adds a provision that if any officer, in the course of any inspection or search of any business place, building or any another place finds that goods are stored in undeclared godown, such stock shall be treated as stock outside the regular books of accounts of the dealer. It also specifies that godowns in respect of which prior written intimation had been given to the registering authority by the dealer shall not be treated as undeclared godowns.

Amends the sub-section to allow the Government to notify areas where tax evasion has taken place and direct the dealer to pay the difference of tax. It also allows for checking evasion of tax in any place or prices in the State. Notification in the Gazette shall specify such areas, hereinafter referred to as the notified area, and direct setting up to check posts at such place or places, and define the boundaries of such notified area and may demarcate such boundaries by means of barriers or otherwise for the purpose of regulating the passage of goods across the notified area.

Specifies that where goods are imported into the State through coastal cargo, through air and through the Railways, the importer or clearing agents, by whatever name called, shall, on arrival of such goods, furnish a declaration before the Commercial Tax Officer having jurisdiction over the place of import as may be prescribed. While transporting such goods within the State or across the State, the transporter/person in charge of the vehicle/vessel shall keep a copy of such declaration duly acknowledged by the concerned authority and shall be produced for verification by any authority under this Act.
Amends the sub-section to replace 'seize' with 'words 'seize' the words 'words 'and confiscate' and 'words 'and confiscate''.
Introduces a proviso that the maximum compounding fee collectible as a single offence spread over several return periods in a financial year shall be two lakh rupees.

States that notwithstanding anything contained elsewhere in this Act, where a case of tax evasion has been detected and proceedings have been initiated against such evasion, the dealer shall not be permitted to revise the returns in respect of the return period covered in the penal proceedings until such proceedings are finalised.
Amends the Explanation to insert the words 'or part-time employee holding Diploma in Sales Taxation issued by the Centre for Taxation Studies'.
Amends the words 'Schedule to this Act' to 'either prospectively or retrospectively'.
Omitted.
