main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Finance Act, 1983 and specifies its commencement date as the 1st day of April, 1983, with remaining provisions coming into force on the 13th day of June, 1983.

Amends the Kerala Money Lenders Act, 1958 (35 of 1958). It includes specific modifications to section 2, section 4, clause (1) of section 5, and section 6, as well as the insertion of new sub-sections concerning licence granting, conditions, and fees. It also deals with the removal of doubts regarding the liability of money lenders with branches in the State.

Amends the Kerala Stamp Act, 1959 (17 of 1959). It substitutes a new section ('48. Release') that defines release as any instrument where a person renounces a claim upon another person or against any specified property, and specifies the duty payable based on whether the release operates in favour of the spouse or children or in any other case, referencing the duty rates for conveyances.

Amends the Kerala Land Tax Act, 1961 (13 of 1961). It adds provisos to sub-section (1) and sub-section (2) of section 6, dealing with the rate of basic tax for every financial year commencing with 1983-84, and the aggregate extent of land held by a landholder in the State. It also specifies amendments to words and figures in the opening paragraph and the first and second provisos.

Amends the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963 (15 of 1963). It makes amendments to section 14, including substituting 'ten rupees' with 'ten rupees' and 'fifty rupees' with 'fifty rupees' in sub-section (1), and 'five rupees' with 'five rupees' and 'twenty-five rupees' with 'twenty-five rupees' in sub-section (3). It also includes amendments to the First Schedule, and provides for the substitution of specific entries and figures, including those related to 'French Coffee' and its taxation.

Amends the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976 (19 of 1976). It substitutes section 25, relating to the amount of tax leviable under sub-section (1) of section 3. This section deals with increased tax amounts in cases of motor vehicle increase or when the registered owner is a fleet owner, and provisions related to tax leviable under sub-section (1) of section 3.
Amends the Kerala Additional Sales Tax Act, 1978 (20 of 1978). It substitutes section 2, concerning the words 'ten per cent', with 'fifteen per cent'.

Amends the Kerala Forest Produce (Fixation of Selling Price) Act, 1978 (29 of 1978). It inserts a new section '5A' which deals with additional price to be paid by industrial establishments for purchasing bamboos, reeds, or eucalyptus. It specifies that the additional price is at the rate of twenty-five rupees per tonne of bamboos, reeds or eucalyptus, and that the amount obtained shall be set apart for regeneration of bamboos, reeds, and eucalyptus.

Repeals the Kerala Finance Ordinance, 1983 (20 of 1983). It also states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the Acts specified in sections 3 to 9 of the said Ordinance, as amended by this Act, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act as amended by this Act.

key_definitions.Foreign Liquor (Foreign made): Means any liquor produced, manufactured, or blended and compounded abroad and imported into India by land, air or sea.

Amends the Abkari Act, 1077 (1 of 1077). Amends the Kerala Tax on Luxuries Act, 1976, by making omissions and substitutions in items (a), (b), (c) and (d) of sub-section (2) of section 4.
Amends the Kerala Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1991, in section 41, by substituting the words 'five years' for 'six years'.

Amends the Kerala Tax on Entry of Goods into Local Areas Act, 1994. It inserts new sections, specifically '9B Disposal of detained goods', detailing procedures for the owner or representative of detained goods to stop the vehicle or vessel, allow inspection, and the consequences of not remitting entry tax. important_rules: Rule 1: Item (2) of sub-section (2), item (b) of sub-section (6) and sub-section (7) of section 3 of this Act shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 2002, and shall be in force till the 2nd day of April, 2002. Rule 2: (1) after item (b) under the heading "(2) Luxury Tax" the following items and entries shall respectively be inserted, namely — "(c) When levied in the form of a fee for licence for the sale of Foreign Liquor (Foreign made) (i) in wholesale Rs 25,000.00 (Rupees Twenty-five lakhs) for a year or part thereof (ii) in retail Rs 10,000.00 (Rupees Ten lakhs) for a year or part thereof (iii) in hotels or restaurants Rs 25,000.00 (Rupees Twenty-five lakhs) for a year or part thereof (iv) in non-proprietory clubs to its members Rs 10,000.00 (Rupees Ten lakhs) for a year or part thereof (v) in Seamen's and Marine officer's clubs to its members Rs 10,000.00 (Rupees Ten lakhs) for a year or part thereof.

Rule 3: (d) when levied in the form of gallonage fee (1) Foreign Liquor (Foreign made) other than beer and wine Rs 200 (Rupees Two hundred) per bulk litre (2) For Foreign made beer and wine Rs 25 (Rupees Twenty-five) per bulk litre.

penalties: Penalty of Rs. 10,000 (Rupees Ten thousand only) for certain offences under the Act relating to foreign liquor.

Penalty of Rs. 25,000 (Rupees Twenty-five thousand only) for certain offences under the Act relating to foreign liquor, particularly involving re-constitution, alteration or modification of any license.

For offences under Section 7 of the Kerala Tax on Entry of Goods into Local Areas Act, 1994, where goods are detained, the owner or representative may face consequences related to the stopping of the vehicle and non-remittal of entry tax.

penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Seizure and sale of goods by public auction; imposition of penalties; requiring entry tax remittance; directions from the Sales Tax Officer.

duties: Duty to remit entry tax liable under this Act.

Duty of the owner of the goods or his representative or other person in charge of the vehicle or vessel to not remit the required amount of tax within 14 days from the date of stopping the vehicle or vessel, the officer not below the rank of Sales Tax Officer may, by order, seize the goods and forward the records to the Officer superior to him to pass order assessing the tax liable under this Act.
Duty of the officer to whom the records were transferred to pass appropriate orders and direct the owner of the goods to remit the tax assessed if any, within 30 days.

If the tax assessed is not remitted within the period mentioned in the order, the goods seized under sub-section (2) shall be sold by the officer who assessed the tax by public auction to the highest bidder and the sale proceeds shall be remitted in the Government Treasury.

If the goods seized are of a perishable nature or subject to speedy and natural decay or when the expenses of keeping them in custody are likely to exceed their value, the officer in charge of the notified area shall immediately sell such goods or otherwise dispose of them and remit the sale proceeds of such goods or the amount obtained by the disposal of such goods otherwise than by sale in the Government Treasury.
obligations: Obligation to pay taxes and fees as prescribed by the Act.
Obligation to comply with the directions issued by the Sales Tax Officer/Assistant Sales Tax Officer regarding tax remittance.

Ready-made garments, hosiery goods, bed sheets, towels, pillow covers, napkins and baby diapers are subject to tax.
Spare parts and accessories of motor vehicles and motor vessels are taxed if the bore diameter is below 5 centimeters.
Squashes, sauces, fruit juices, fruit pulp, soda, mineral water, Horlicks, Boost, Bournvita, Complan, Glucose D, Glucovita and similar other items are subject to tax.
Shampoo, Talcum Powder including medicated talcum powder, sandal wood oil, ramachom oil, Cinnamon oil, other perfumeries and cosmetics not falling under any other entry in this Schedule are taxed.
Suitcases and brief cases of all kinds made of plastics, nylon, leather or moulded material are taxed.

Tabulating machines, calculating machines, duplicating machines, parts and accessories thereof are taxed.
Water supply and sanitary equipments and fittings, water meter, its spare parts and accessories are taxed.

Rubber, whether in natural or semi processed form not coming under items (b) and (c) below, or brought from outside the State, or reclaimed rubber or synthetic rubber, are subject to tax at the point first sale in the State by a dealer.
Soaps other than handmade are taxed.
Galvanised Iron Pipes (G I Pipe) are taxed.
Handmade paper, handmade soap and handmade agarbathi shall be substituted.

main_sections.description: Dealers are required to register with the registering authority. Failure to register may result in the dealer not being entitled to any benefits accruing from such registration.

main_sections.section_title: Issuance of sale bill by dealers
main_sections.description: Every dealer registered or liable to get himself registered shall compulsorily issue a bill or an invoice or cash memorandum in respect of every sale of goods liable to tax under this Act involving transaction amounting to not less than one hundred rupees.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for non-issuance of sale bill

important_rules: Goods on purchase of Duty Entitlement Pass Book or any similar license for import of any goods and goods so imported are used, consumed or disposed of in the manner specified in this sub-section, the input tax paid on the purchase of such Duty Entitlement Pass Book or any similar license shall for the purpose of this section and section 11, be deemed to be the input tax paid on the goods imported.
Consignments of goods shall be accompanied by delivery notes when it is dealer to dealer transaction and sale bill in case the transport is between a dealer to the consumer.
Goods shall be accompanied by delivery notes when it is dealer to dealer transaction and sale bill in case the transport is between a dealer to the consumer.

All vehicles carrying goods, other than those specifically notified by the Commissioner shall be subjected to scanning and weighing by the scanning and weighing agency at such check post, where such facilities are available whether controlled by the Government, or any other agency approved by the Government, and the driver or the person incharge of the vehicle shall be liable to pay the weighing and scanning charges at rates notified by the Commissioner.
The dealer shall have an option to get the offence compounded, on the spot, on the payment of fifty per cent of penalty payable under sub-section (1).

penalties: Amount not exceeding twice the amount of tax evaded or sought to be evaded or one thousand rupees for the first offence, whichever is higher.

Compounding of offence: fifty per cent of penalty payable under sub-section (1).
Cancellation of registration for committing the offence in sub-section (1) for more than ten occasions.

title: The Kerala Finance Act, 2007
purpose: This act appears to be an amendment or supplement to existing legislation, focusing on tax rates, amendments to previous acts, and provisions for revenue collection. Specifically, it details rates for 'ONE TIME TAX' on vehicles and amends provisions related to luxury tax and value-added tax.
scope: The act applies to vehicles registered in Kerala, luxury services provided in convention centers, hotels, clubs, and similar establishments, and sales of goods under the Kerala Value Added Tax Act, 2003. It also amends existing acts like the Kerala Tax on Luxuries Act, 1976, and the Kerala Value Added Tax Act, 2003, thereby extending its scope to those provisions as well.

key_definitions.one time tax: A tax levied at a specific rate based on the class of vehicle and its age.
key_definitions.luxury tax: Tax applied to charges received in respect of service rendered outside of hotel premises, such as vehicle hire, boat hire, and trekking. Also applies to charges for accommodation and amenities in specific establishments.
key_definitions.value added tax (VAT): Tax applied to goods specified in the Second and Third Schedules, and on aerated branded soft drinks.

main_sections.description: This section details the rates of one-time tax for various classes of vehicles, including motor cycles, three wheelers, omni buses, and motor cars. The tax rate is calculated as a percentage of the purchase value of the vehicle, with adjustments based on the age of the vehicle.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Act 32 of 1976.—In the Kerala Tax on Luxuries Act, 1976 (32 of 1976), in sub-section (2) of Section 4,—
main_sections.description: This section amends the Kerala Tax on Luxuries Act, 1976. It modifies the wording related to 'per room' charges and introduces provisions for luxury tax on convention centers, clubs, and other establishments. It also makes changes to how charges for accommodation and amenities are taxed, with specific thresholds and rates.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Act 30 of 2004.—In the Kerala Value Added Tax Act, 2003 (30 of 2004),—
main_sections.description: This section amends the Kerala Value Added Tax Act, 2003. It introduces changes to the rate of tax on specific goods, including those in the Second and Third Schedules and aerated branded soft drinks. It also modifies provisions related to the eligibility of dealers for tax payments and how taxes are collected, including debits and credits for differential tax.

important_rules: Rule 1: Motor Cycles (including Motor Scooters and Cycles with attachment for propelling the same by mechanical power) and bicycles of all category with or without side car or drawing a trailer are subject to 6% of the purchase value.

Rule 2: Three Wheelers (including tricycle and cycle rickshaws with attachment for propelling the same by mechanical power) not used for transport of goods or passengers are subject to 6% of the purchase value.
Rule 3: Omni bus for private use (Private Service Vehicle-NTV) and Motor Cars are subject to 6% of the purchase value.

Rule 4: The percentage of the one time tax leviable under 'A' is dependent on the age of the vehicle. For example, a vehicle not more than one year old has 100% tax, while a vehicle more than 14 years old but not more than 15 years old has 7% tax.

Rule 5: Luxury tax on convention centres, halls, kalyanamandapam, auditorium and similar establishments will be levied at the rate of fifteen per cent where gross charges of accommodation and other amenities are above rupees twenty thousand per day.

Rule 6: Dealers whose output tax liability per annum is twenty five lakhs or more on account of taxable sale in the State and every wholesale dealer, distributor and dealers holding van sale permit, shall file their returns as well as purchase and sale lists electronically.

Rule 7: Provided that where a dealer effects taxable sale, he shall furnish the name and address of the purchaser in the sale bill/invoices, and where the sale is to a dealer, the address shall include TIN or PIN, as the case may be.

penalties: Any amount recoverable under this Act and remaining unpaid shall be a charge on the properties of the defaulter and may be recovered as an arrear of public revenue due on land.
For cone crushers, a tax of Rs 7,50,000 per annum is levied.

penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement includes the charge on properties of defaulters for unpaid amounts, recovery as arrears of public revenue, and specific tax collection mechanisms outlined in the amended acts.

rights: Right to claim input tax credit for eligible dealers.
Right to receive payment even without taking registration under the Act for certain categories.
Right to claim tax paid by him on the purchase value of such goods at the time of purchase for dealers paying tax under sub-section (5) of section 6.

Duty to pay luxury tax on specified services.
Duty to pay value added tax on specified goods.
Duty to file returns and maintain purchase and sale lists electronically for certain dealers.
Duty to furnish purchaser's name and address in sale bills/invoices.
Duty to ensure payments are made even without registration under the Act for certain beneficiaries.
obligations: Obligation to comply with tax rates and payment schedules as per the Act and amended provisions.
Obligation for dealers to provide accurate address information including TIN or PIN.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Calculation and payment of one time tax for vehicles based on their class and age, as a percentage of the purchase value.
Procedure 2: Levy and payment of luxury tax on charges for accommodation, amenities, and services provided in specified establishments, with different rates based on the value of charges.
Procedure 3: Application of value added tax on specified goods, with amendments detailing rates and provisions for tax collection.
Procedure 4: Dealers to file returns and maintain electronic records of purchases and sales.
Procedure 5: Issuance of debit notes for differential tax and claiming input tax credit.
Procedure 6: Registration and payment procedures for dealers under different tax regimes as outlined in the amended Acts.
administration: Various tax departments within the Kerala Government, implied to administer the Kerala Tax on Luxuries Act and the Kerala Value Added Tax Act.
important_notes: The rates for one time tax on vehicles are tiered based on the age of the vehicle.
The luxury tax provisions have specific thresholds for charges and exceptions like vehicle hire, boat hire, and trekking.
Amendments to the Kerala Value Added Tax Act include provisions for differential tax and eligibility for tax payments.
The act clarifies provisions for dealers, including those who opt to pay compounded tax and those who have started business during specific periods.

A proviso states that the rate of tax in the case of casual traders shall be two thousand five hundred rupees per month and the maximum period of validity of registration certificate shall be three months from the date of issue of certificate.

It is provided that dealers whose output tax liability per annum is twenty five lakhs or more, shall file their returns as well as purchase and sale lists electronically in addition to the hard copy to be filed along with the returns.

main_sections.description: This section amends the Kerala Tax on Luxuries Act, 1976, specifically concerning the imposition of tax on hostels and the liability of directors of private companies.
This section amends the Kerala Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1991, by omitting certain words and substituting others in item (3) and (4) of the schedule.

This section amends the Kerala Value Added Tax Act, 2004. It modifies provisions related to plastic carry bags, disposable plates, and specifies the tax rate on certain goods. It also includes amendments to the explanation of 'building materials' and introduces a new provision regarding tax on cooked food, sweets, beverages, and fruit juices manufactured by prisoners and sold by the Kerala Prison and Correctional Services Department.

important_rules: Motor vehicles other than those liable to tax under the foregoing provisions of this Schedule for every square meter or part thereof of the floor area are taxed at Rs. 150/-.
Goods carriages with GVW up to 3000 Kg are taxed at Rs. 3000/-.

Goods carriages with GVW exceeding 1500 Kg but not exceeding 2000 Kg are taxed at Rs. 12200/-.

Certain types of plastic carry bags, including non-woven poly propylene bags, have been substituted in the schedule.
The rate of tax on the sale of disposable plates and cups made of styrofoam for the financial years 2013-14 and 2014-15 shall be at five percent.

Tax shall not be levied on hostels run directly by educational institutions and working women's hostels run by religious or charitable institutions registered under the Travancore-Cochin Literary, Scientific and Charitable Societies Registration Act, 1955.

Tax on rooms where gross charges of accommodation for residence and other amenities and services provided is above Rupees four hundred and up to one thousand rupees per day is at the rate of six percent.

penalties: Liability of Directors of a Private company: where any tax or other amount recoverable under this Act from any proprietor being a private company, whether existing or wound up or under liquidation, cannot be recovered, every person who was a director of such company at any time during the period for which the tax or other amount is due under this Act shall be jointly and severally liable for the payment of such tax or other amount unless he proves that the non-recovery cannot be attributed to any negligence, misfeasance or breach of duty on his part in relation to the affairs of the company.

duties: Duty to pay tax on various goods and services as specified in the act.
Duty to comply with the amended provisions of the Kerala Tax on Luxuries Act, 1976, Kerala Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1991, and Kerala Value Added Tax Act, 2004.
obligations: Directors of private companies have a joint and several liability for unpaid taxes if the company defaults, unless they can prove no negligence.

title: The Kerala Finance (No. 2) Act, 2015
purpose: An Act to give effect to certain financial proposals of the Government of Kerala for the Financial Year 2015-2016.

main_sections.description: (1) This Act may be called the Kerala Finance (No. 2) Act, 2015. (2) It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 2015.

In the Kerala Conservation of Paddy Land and Wet land Act, 2008 (28 of 2008), after section 3, the following section shall be inserted, namely:-"3A. Power to regularise the conversion or reclamation of paddy land made before the commencement of the Act.- Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or any other Act, rules or orders for the time being in force or in any judgement, decree or order of any court, tribunal or other authority, where before the commencement of this Act, any owner, occupier or the person in custody of any paddy land had undertaken conversion or reclamation of the said paddy land otherwise than in accordance with the provisions of any other Act existing at that time, the Collector may, regularise such conversion or reclamation, by recovering a fee equal to 25 percent of the fair value of the said land notified under section 28A of the Kerala Stamp Act, 1959 (17 of 1959) or the fair value of adjacent land of similar nature, if the fair value of said land is not notified."

important_rules: Rule 1: The Act is to give effect to financial proposals for the Financial Year 2015-2016.
Rule 2: The Act came into force on April 1, 2015.
Rule 3: Amendments are made to the Kerala Conservation of Paddy Land and Wet land Act, 2008.
Rule 4: Conversion or reclamation of paddy land before the commencement of the Act can be regularized by the Collector.
Rule 5: A fee equal to 25 percent of the fair value of the land (or adjacent land if not notified) is to be recovered for regularization.

penalties: Fee equal to 25 percent of the fair value of the said land notified under section 28A of the Kerala Stamp Act, 1959 (17 of 1959) or the fair value of adjacent land of similar nature, if the fair value of said land is not notified.

penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By recovering a fee for the regularization of unauthorized conversion or reclamation of paddy land.

rights: Right of the Collector to regularize conversion/reclamation of paddy land.

duties: Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act regarding regularization.
obligations: Obligation to pay the prescribed fee for regularization.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Owners/occupiers who have converted/reclaimed paddy land before the commencement of the Act can apply to the Collector for regularization.
