title: THE KERALA FIRE FORCE ACT, 1962
purpose: To provide for the establishment and maintenance of a Fire Force for the State of Kerala.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and can be brought into force in any area on such date as the Government may appoint.

key_definitions.Collector: The Chief Officer in charge of the revenue administration of the district and includes an acting or officiating Collector. Also any officer appointed by the Government to exercise the functions of the Collector.
key_definitions.Director: The Director of the Fire Force for the State of Kerala.
key_definitions.fire-fighting property: Lands and buildings used as fire stations, engines, equipment, tools, implements and things whatsoever used for fire-fighting; motor vehicles and other means of transport used in connection with fire-fighting; and fire-fighting means.
key_definitions.fire-station: Any post or place declared generally or specially, by the Government to be a fire-station.
key_definitions.Force: The Kerala Fire Force maintained under this Act.
key_definitions.officer-in-charge of a fire-station: Includes when the officer-in-charge of the fire-station is absent from the station or unable from illness or other cause to perform his duties, the fire officer present at the station who is next in rank to such officer.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act is the Kerala Fire Force Act, 1962, extends to the whole of Kerala, and will commence on such date as the Government may appoint.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including Collector, Director, fire-fighting property, fire-station, Force, officer-in-charge of a fire-station, and prescribed.
States that the Fire Force shall be maintained by the Government and shall be called the Kerala Fire Force, for services in the local areas in which the Act is in force.

main_sections.section_title: Superintendence and control of the Force
main_sections.description: Vests the superintendence and control of the Force in the Director and mandates that the Director shall be carried on by him in accordance with the provisions of the Act and any rules made thereunder. It also states that the Government may appoint such officers as it may deem fit to assist the Director.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of members of the Force
main_sections.description: The Director, or such other officers of the Force as the Government may authorize, shall appoint members of the Force in accordance with the rules made under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Issue of certificate to members of Force
main_sections.description: Every person appointed to the Force shall, on appointment, receive a certificate in the prescribed form.
Empowers the Government to raise an Auxiliary Force by the enrolment of volunteers for such areas and on such terms and conditions as it may deem fit.
The entire expenditure in connection with the Force shall be met out of the Consolidated Fund of the State.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to make orders
main_sections.description: The Government may, from time to time, make such general or special orders as it thinks fit for the efficient functioning of the Force, including orders for providing adequate supply of water and for securing that it shall be available for use, for constructing or providing stations or hiring places for accommodating the members of the Force, for giving rewards to persons who have given notice of fires, for giving compensation to persons who have rendered effective service, and for the training, discipline and good conduct of members of the Force, and for the speedy attendance of members of the Force with necessary appliances and equipment.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of members of the Force on occasion of fire
main_sections.description: On the occasion of a fire in any area, any member of the Force who is in charge of fire-fighting operations may, remove or order any other member of the Force to remove, any person who is present and interferes with or impedes the operation, close any street or passage, break into or through or pull down any premises for the passage of hose or appliances, or cause them to be broken into or through, and require the authority to regulate the water supply at a specified pressure.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Director to make arrangements for supply of water
main_sections.description: The Director, with the previous sanction of the Government, may enter into an agreement with the authority in charge of water-supply for securing an adequate supply of water in case of fire.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Director to enter into arrangements for assistance
main_sections.description: The Director may enter into arrangements with any person who employs and maintains personnel or keeps equipment for fire-fighting purposes, to secure, on such terms as to payment or otherwise, the assistance of such personnel or equipment.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, require owners or occupants of premises in any area to take such preventive measures as are necessary to cause risk of fire. It also outlines the powers of the Director or any officer authorized by the Government in relation to the removal of objects likely to cause risk of fire and the seizure and sale of such objects.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition against transfer of fire fighting property
main_sections.description: No local authority shall transfer or otherwise part with any fire fighting property without the previous sanction of the Government.
The Director or any member of the Force may, if in his opinion it is necessary, requisition fire fighting property. The Government shall pay compensation for such requisition.

The Government may, after making such inquiry and investigation as it deems necessary, acquire fire fighting property. The Government shall pay compensation for such acquisition, based on market value.

main_sections.section_title: Principles and method of determining compensation
main_sections.description: Outlines the principles and methods for determining compensation for the requisition or acquisition of fire fighting property, primarily based on market value.
If the local authority does not agree with the compensation amount, it can be referred to the Munsiff’s Court for determination.
Provides for an appeal to the High Court against decisions of the Court regarding compensation.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for violation of duty, etc.
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for members of the Force who are found guilty of violation of duty, wilful breach of any provision of the Act, cowardice, withdrawal from duties, or absence from leave without reasonable cause.

Penalizes whoever fails without reasonable cause to comply with any of the requirements specified in a notification issued under sub-section (1) of section 13 or of a direction issued under sub-section (2) of that section.
Penalizes any person who wilfully obstructs or interferes with any member of the Force engaged in fire-fighting operations.
The Government may establish and maintain training centres for the prevention and extinguishment of fire.
A member of the Force shall not engage in any employment or other business other than his duties under the Act unless expressly permitted by the Director.

The Director or any officer authorized by the Government may order the dispatch of members of the Force, with necessary appliances and equipment, to assist in fire-fighting operations in any neighbouring area.
Members of the Force can be employed on other duties as directed by the Director.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of owner of property to pay compensation
main_sections.description: Owners of property may be liable to pay compensation for damages caused by fire fighting operations.

main_sections.section_title: Inquiry into origin of fire and report to Government
main_sections.description: The Director or any officer authorized can inquire into the origin of fires and report to the Government.
Power to obtain information related to fire hazards.
Power of entry for the purpose of fire fighting.
Rules regarding the consumption of water by the Fire Force.

main_sections.section_title: No compensation for interruption of water supply
main_sections.description: No compensation shall be paid for interruption of water supply caused by the Fire Force.
Police Officers shall aid the Fire Force.
Indemnity for actions taken in good faith under the Act.
The Government has the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

penalties: Imprisonment which may extend to three months or with fine which may extend to two hundred rupees (for violation of duty, etc.)
Imprisonment which may extend to three months or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees (for failure to take precautions)
Imprisonment which may extend to three months or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees (for wilfully obstructing fire fighting operations)
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Members of the Force, Director, Collector, Government, Police Officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through penalties as prescribed in the Act for violations, and by the powers vested in the Director and members of the Force for fire fighting operations and preventive measures.

rights: Right to receive a certificate upon appointment to the Force.
Members of the Force have powers to remove persons impeding operations, close streets, break into premises, and require authorities to regulate water supply.
Right to compensation for requisitioned or acquired fire fighting property.
Right to appeal to the High Court regarding compensation disputes.
duties: Members of the Force have a duty to perform their duties diligently and in accordance with the Act and rules.
Members of the Force are subject to the superintendence and control of the Director.
Owners or occupants of premises have a duty to take preventive measures against fire as notified by the Government.
obligations: Obligation to not transfer fire fighting property without Government sanction.
Obligation to comply with requirements for preventive measures.
Obligation to assist the Fire Force by Police Officers.

key_procedures: Appointment of members to the Force and issuance of certificates.
Requisitioning of fire fighting property, including the process of determining and paying compensation.
Acquisition of fire fighting property, including inquiry, determination of compensation, and notification.
Procedure for appealing compensation decisions to the Court and then to the High Court.
Process for obtaining an adequate supply of water for fire fighting through agreements.
Procedure for taking preventive measures against fire as notified by the Government.
administration: The Kerala Fire Force, under the superintendence and control of the Director, with overall administration by the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act was enacted in the Thirteenth Year of the Republic of India.
The Act received the assent of the President on the 16th day of June 1962 and was published in the Gazette Extraordinary on the 21st day of June 1962.

title: The Kerala Fiscal Responsibility (Amendment) Act, 2011
purpose: The purpose of this Act is to amend the Kerala Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2003, to incorporate fiscal responsibility measures and targets, particularly concerning revenue deficit, fiscal deficit, and public debt.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Kerala and its financial management.

main_sections.description: This section likely provides the short title of the Act and specifies when it comes into force.

This section introduces amendments to the Kerala Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2003. It details the specific changes being made to the original Act, likely related to fiscal targets and responsibilities.

important_rules: The Act amends Section 4 of the Kerala Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2003, to introduce new fiscal targets.
It specifies targets for revenue deficit, fiscal deficit, and public debt for the financial years 2011-12 to 2014-15.

For example, it mandates a revenue deficit of not more than 3.5 per cent of the Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) by the end of 2013-14, and a fiscal deficit of not more than 3 per cent of GSDP by the end of 2014-15.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Act implies that the State Government, through its finance department, would be responsible for enforcement.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement would likely involve monitoring compliance with the fiscal targets and taking corrective measures if deviations occur.

duties: The State Government has a duty to adhere to the fiscal targets set by the Act.
The State Government has a duty to present a strategy to bring the fiscal deficit to below 3 per cent of GSDP by the end of 2014-15.
obligations: The State Government is obligated to manage its finances in a fiscally responsible manner as outlined in the Act.

administration: The Finance Department of the Kerala State Government.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Kerala Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2003.
The amendment focuses on setting specific fiscal targets for several financial years.
It provides updated targets for revenue deficit, fiscal deficit, and public debt, replacing or modifying the targets in the original Act.

title: The Kerala Fiscal Responsibility (Amendment) Act, 2022
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2003, to set new targets for revenue surplus, fiscal deficit, and debt liabilities of the State.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and its financial management, specifically amending provisions related to fiscal targets for the period 2021-2022 to 2025-2026.

main_sections.description: (1) States that the Act may be called the Kerala Fiscal Responsibility (Amendment) Act, 2022. (2) Deems the Act to have come into force on April 1, 2021.

Substitutes sub-section (2) of section 4 of the Kerala Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2003, with new provisions regarding the elimination of revenue deficit and reduction of fiscal deficit and debt liabilities.

important_rules: Eliminate revenue deficit completely during the period from 2021-2022 to 2025-2026.
Achieve revenue surplus as a percentage of Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) in specified amounts for the years 2021-2022 to 2025-2026 (0.5%, 0.8%, 1.2%, 1.7%, 2.5% respectively).
Ensure that the targeted loan amount within the fiscal deficit limit is completely spent for asset development.

Reduce the fiscal deficit to 3% of estimated GSDP within five years from April 1, 2021, to March 31, 2026, by maintaining it at specific percentages of GSDP in preceding years (4.5%, 4%, 3.5%, 3.5% for 2021-2022 to 2024-2025, and then reducing to 3% in 2025-2026).
Reduce total debt liabilities of the State as a percentage of GSDP in specified amounts for the years 2021-2022 to 2025-2026 (34.7%, 34.5%, 33.7%, 32.8%, 32% respectively).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but implied to be the State Government and its financial departments.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through adherence to the fiscal targets and reporting mechanisms outlined in the Act and its predecessor.

rights: The State shall be eligible for capital expenditure linked borrowing if it achieves the targeted capital expenditure.
The State shall be eligible for additional borrowing linked to power sector performance if it fulfills entry-level conditions and performance evaluation criteria.

The State may have the option to utilize unutilized borrowing amounts in subsequent years within the Finance Commission award period if unable to fully utilize sanctioned borrowing in a particular year.
duties: Governments' duty to eliminate revenue deficit.
Governments' duty to increase revenue surplus.
Governments' duty to reduce fiscal deficit.
Governments' duty to reduce total debt liabilities.
States' duty to fulfill entry-level conditions and performance evaluation criteria for power sector borrowing.
obligations: Obligation to eliminate revenue deficit by 2025-2026.
Obligation to reduce fiscal deficit to 3% of GSDP by 2025-2026.
Obligation to reduce debt liabilities to specific percentages of GSDP by 2025-2026.

key_procedures: Amendment Procedure: The Act amends the existing Kerala Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2003, by substituting a specific sub-section.
Commencement: The Act is deemed to have come into force retrospectively from April 1, 2021.
administration: Law (Legislation-A) Department, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: Note (i): The upper limit of fiscal deficit includes 0.5% capital expenditure linked borrowing and an additional 0.5% borrowing linked to power sector performance during 2021-2022 to 2024-2025.

Note (ii): Eligibility for capital expenditure linked borrowing depends on achieving targets. Eligibility for power sector linked borrowing requires meeting specific conditions and evaluation criteria.

Note (iii): If the State cannot fully utilize its sanctioned borrowing (excluding power sector) in any of the first four years of the Finance Commission award period (2021-2022 to 2024-2025), it can use the unutilized amount in subsequent years within that period.

title: THE KERALA FISCAL RESPONSIBILITY ACT, 2003
purpose: An Act to provide for the responsibility of the Government to ensure prudence in fiscal management and fiscal stability by progressive elimination of revenue deficit and sustainable debt management consistent with fiscal stability, greater transparency in fiscal operations of the Government and conduct of fiscal policy in a medium term fiscal frame work and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the Government of Kerala and concerns its fiscal management, stability, and policy.

key_definitions.annual budget: the annual financial statement laid before the Legislative Assembly under article 202 of the Constitution of India
key_definitions.committee: means public expenditure review committee constituted under sub-section (1) of section 6
key_definitions.current year: means the year preceding the year for which the budget and medium term fiscal policy are being presented
key_definitions.fiscal deficit: means the excess of total expenditure of the Government over the total receipts and represents the borrowing requirements, and net of repayment of debt of the Government during the year, calculated as prescribed by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
key_definitions.fiscal indicators: means measures such as numerical ceilings and proportions to gross state domestic products as may be prescribed for evaluation of the fiscal position of the State Government
key_definitions.medium term fiscal framework: means the frame work drawn up by the Government for a five year period from the financial year on which this Act shall come into force with the objective of progressively eliminating the Revenue Deficit
key_definitions.prescribed: means prescribed by rules under this Act
key_definitions.previous year: means the year preceding the current year
key_definitions.revenue deficit: means the difference between revenue expenditure and revenue receipts and implies increase in the liabilities of the State without corresponding increase in the assets of the State calculated as prescribed by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
key_definitions.total liabilities: means liabilities upon the Consolidated Fund and public account of the State
key_definitions.triggers: means the intra year bench marks on deficit

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2003 and it shall come into force, on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including fiscal deficit, revenue deficit, fiscal indicators, and Government.

main_sections.section_title: Fiscal Policy Statement to be laid before the Legislative Assembly
main_sections.description: Mandates the Government to lay before the Legislative Assembly, along with the annual budget, a medium term fiscal policy statement and a fiscal policy strategy statement. The medium term fiscal policy statement shall set forth a three year rolling target for fiscal indicators with specification of underlying assumptions.

important_rules: The Government must progressively eliminate the revenue deficit.
The Government must ensure that the fiscal deficit does not exceed a prescribed percentage of the State Gross Domestic Product (SGDP).
The Government must not incur any new loans that would increase the total liabilities beyond a prescribed percentage of SGDP.
The Government must present a medium-term fiscal policy statement along with the annual budget.
The medium-term fiscal policy statement must include specific targets for fiscal indicators and underlying assumptions.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala, through its relevant departments and potentially the Comptroller and Auditor General of India for calculations.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legislative oversight, reporting requirements, and adherence to the fiscal targets and principles outlined in the Act.

duties: Duty of the Government to ensure prudence in fiscal management.
Duty of the Government to ensure fiscal stability.
Duty of the Government to progressively eliminate revenue deficit.
Duty of the Government to ensure sustainable debt management.
Duty of the Government to ensure greater transparency in fiscal operations.
Duty of the Government to present fiscal policy statements to the Legislative Assembly.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the targets and principles set forth in the Act regarding fiscal deficit, revenue deficit, and debt management.

key_procedures: Presentation of the Fiscal Policy Statement to the Legislative Assembly annually.
Setting of three-year rolling targets for fiscal indicators.
Specification of underlying assumptions for the fiscal policy statement.
Calculation of fiscal deficit and revenue deficit as prescribed by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
administration: The Finance Department of the Government of Kerala is likely the primary administrator of this Act.
important_notes: The Act provides for flexibility, allowing the Government to notify the commencement date.
The definitions are crucial for understanding the application and targets of the Act.
The Act aims for a medium-term approach to fiscal management, not just annual budgeting.

title: The Kerala Fish Seed Act, 2014
purpose: To provide for the regulation of the quality in production, marketing and stocking of fish seed and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the regulation of quality in production, marketing and stocking of fish seed within the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.fish_seed: means larval stages or juveniles or any other classes of seeds of aquatic life, including plant, plant origin, used for stocking in confined or open waters, such as ponds, tanks, lakes, reservoirs, rivers, pools, check dams and pens or cages or any other structures erected in water and includes- (i) seeds of aquatic animals including ornamental fish reared in fresh water, brackish water and marine water and in aquaria; (ii) seeds of shell fish, such as prawns, shrimps, lobsters, crab, gastropods, bivalves and such other crustaceans and molluscs; (iii) early stages of fish and larval stages of prawn, shrimp, lobsters, crabs, post larvae, zoea, mysis, megalopa and larval stages of molluscs, veliger and spat;
key_definitions.fish_seed_analysis: means the procedures of Fish Seed Analysis to verify that the seeds are free from pathogen and diseases and meet the required standards of quality and size
key_definitions.fish_seed_farm: means a place with water body or structures used for fish seed culture
key_definitions.fish_seed_inspector: means a Fish Seed Inspector appointed under section 18
key_definitions.fish_seed_laboratory: means the Fish Seed Laboratory established under section 11
key_definitions.fish_seed_rearing: means rearing of seeds of fin fishes or shell fishes or any other aquatic animals and aquatic plants in fresh waters or brackish waters or marine waters
key_definitions.hatchery: means a place where brooders are maintained and used for production of fish seed and includes a place where rearing of the seed for supply to fish farmer and this includes backyard hatchery or part of the farm including rearing in nurseries
key_definitions.import: means bringing fish seed into Kerala from other States or from outside India
key_definitions.kind: means one or more related species or such species of aquatic animals or aquatic plants each individually or collectively are known by one common name such as carps, shrimps, prawns, crabs, mussels, lobsters, sea weeds, aquarium plants
key_definitions.marketing: means the business of selling, offering to sell, bartering or otherwise supply or keeping for sale of any fish seed
key_definitions.notification: means a notification published in the official Gazette
key_definitions.notified_kind_or_variety: in relation to any fish seed means any kind or variety thereof notified under section 12
key_definitions.prescribed: means prescribed by rules made under this Act
key_definitions.quarantine: means a place of isolation for the purpose of observing animals and plants suspected of harbouring a pathogen prior to the introduction of such species to the new environment or state
key_definitions.regional_fish_seed_centre: means the Regional Fish Seed Centres established under section 7
key_definitions.state_fish_seed_centre: means the State Fish Seed Centre established under section 3
key_definitions.sub_centres: means the sub-centres established under sub-section (1) of section 10
key_definitions.variety: means a sub division of a kind identifiable by morphology, growth, yield, seed, re-production or other characteristics

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Fish Seed Act, 2014. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 13th day of February, 2014.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'fish seed', 'fish seed analysis', 'fish seed farm', 'fish seed inspector', 'fish seed laboratory', 'fish seed rearing', 'Government', 'hatchery', 'import', 'kind', 'marketing', 'notification', 'notified kind or variety', 'prescribed', 'quarantine', 'regional fish seed centre', 'state fish seed centre', 'sub-centres', and 'variety'.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of State Fish Seed Centre
main_sections.description: The Government may, as soon as may be after the commencement of this Act, by notification establish a centre called the State Fish Seed Centre.

main_sections.section_title: Duties of the State Fish Seed Centre
main_sections.description: The State Fish Seed Centre shall have the following duties, namely: (a) to make suggestions to the Government on all matters relating to production, rearing, stocking, marketing, transport, import and export of fish seed and its monitoring throughout the State; (b) to carry out such duties as to the registration of the fish seed farms and hatcheries and fish seed certification.

important_rules: No specific rules are detailed in the provided excerpts, but section 2(w) mentions 'prescribed' means prescribed by rules made under this Act, indicating that rules will govern specific aspects.
Section 38 outlines conditions for prohibiting import or export of fish seed, requiring prescribed standards.
Section 39 discusses restrictions on certain types of fish seed for aquaculture and propagation purposes, with specific criteria for prohibition.
Section 40 prohibits certain activities related to fish seed production and marketing without proper certification.

penalties: Penalties for contravention of provisions of the Act are indicated but specific amounts/durations are not detailed in these excerpts.
Section 36 mentions fines and imprisonment for violations.
Section 37 details penalties for contravening rules related to import or export of fish seed.
Section 38 outlines penalties for contravening restrictions on certain fish seeds.
Section 40 specifies penalties for prohibited activities without certification.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Fish Seed Inspectors and other authorised officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspection, prohibition of certain activities, and imposition of penalties including fines and imprisonment.

rights: Right to engage in legitimate fish seed production, marketing, etc., as per the Act.
Right to obtain certification for fish seed.
duties: Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder.
Duty to ensure the quality of fish seed.
Duty to obtain necessary certifications and approvals.
Duty to adhere to prescribed standards for production, stocking, marketing, transport, import, and export of fish seed.
obligations: Obligation to obtain licenses or registrations where prescribed.
Obligation to cooperate with Fish Seed Inspectors and authorised officers.

key_procedures: Establishment of State Fish Seed Centres.
Registration of fish seed farms and hatcheries.
Fish seed certification.
Procedure for obtaining approvals for import and export of fish seed, subject to prescribed standards and quarantine measures.
Procedures for inspection and enforcement by authorised officers.
administration: Law (Legislation-1) Department, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act was enacted in the Sixty-fifth year of the Republic of India.
The English language translation of the Act is authorised for publication.
Quarantine measures are required for the purpose of observing animals and plants suspected of harbouring a pathogen prior to introduction to a new environment or state.
Specific standards are to be prescribed for fish seed quality and other related matters.

title: THE KERALA FISHERMEN DEBT RELIEF COMMISSION ACT, 2008
purpose: To provide for 'urgent relief' to the fishermen who are in distress due to indebtedness, by constituting a Commission for recommending appropriate relief measures to such fishermen and for solving their problems through conciliation negotiation and adjudication and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to fishermen in Kerala who are in distress due to indebtedness, and their debts, including loans obtained from financial institutions.

key_definitions.debt: means any liability, in money, whether secured or unsecured, due from a fisherman, whether payable under a contract or under a decree or any order of any Court or Tribunal or otherwise and includes- (a) any sum payable to- (i) an institutional creditor; (ii) a co-operative society; (iii) a fishermen society; (b) any sum received from a creditor by a fisherman; (c) any type of loan taken by a fisherman from financial institutions and specified by the Government by notification.
key_definitions.creditor: means any person engaged in money lending, whether under a licence or not, his heirs, legal representatives, assignees, middle men and includes any other person or body benefited by the Government.
key_definitions.commission: means the Kerala State Fishermen Debt Relief Commission constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.fisherman: means a person who secures livelihood from the foremost means of livelihood and whose annual income does not exceed the annual income limit fixed by the Government from time to time and it includes the widow of a fisherman.
key_definitions.disaster affected area: means districts/district or fishermen zones forming part thereof in the State, declared by the Government under section 6, for the purpose of this Act, on the recommendations of the Commission;

main_sections.description: States that this may be called the Kerala Fishermen Debt Relief Commission Act, 2008, and it shall come into force at once.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'debt', 'creditor', 'fisherman', 'commission', 'disaster affected area', 'co-operative society', 'financial institution', 'fisherman society', and 'fishing'.

Details the composition of the Commission, which shall consist of five members, namely: a retired High Court Judge (Chairperson), an expert in fisheries, social, technical and financial administration, and three representatives of fishermen. The Chairperson and members are nominated by the Government. The Government shall appoint a Secretary and other employees as may be necessary to assist the Commission.

administration: The Government of Kerala

title: The Kerala Fishermen Debit Relief Commission Act, 2008
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a Commission for the relief of fishermen and to make provisions incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to fishermen in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.fishermen: Individuals engaged in fishing as a primary occupation.
key_definitions.debt: Any sum of money owed by a fisherman.
key_definitions.Commission: The Kerala Fishermen Debit Relief Commission constituted under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the date of commencement.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'Commission', 'fisherman', 'debt', etc.
Details the establishment, composition, and powers of the Kerala Fishermen Debit Relief Commission.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of the Commission
main_sections.description: Outlines the powers and functions of the Commission, including its authority to grant relief to fishermen regarding their debts.
Describes the schemes that the Commission may frame and implement for the relief of fishermen from debt.

important_rules: Fishermen facing debt issues can approach the Commission for relief.
The Commission has the power to investigate debt cases and grant appropriate relief.
Schemes for debt relief will be formulated and implemented by the Commission.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Kerala Fishermen Debit Relief Commission
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the Commission under the Act, including the power to investigate and grant relief.

rights: Fishermen have the right to seek relief from debt through the Commission.
The right to fair hearing and consideration of their cases by the Commission.
duties: The Commission has a duty to administer the Act and provide relief to eligible fishermen.
Fishermen have a duty to cooperate with the Commission in its proceedings.

key_procedures: Submission of applications for debt relief to the Commission.
Investigation and verification of debt claims by the Commission.
Granting of relief by the Commission based on its findings and the established schemes.
administration: The Kerala Fishermen Debit Relief Commission
important_notes: The Act aims to alleviate the financial burden on fishermen.
Specific details regarding eligibility criteria and types of relief may be found within the Act's provisions and subsequent schemes.

title: THE KERALA FISHERMEN WELFARE SOCIETIES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1985
purpose: To amend The Kerala Fishermen Welfare Societies Act, 1980.
scope: Applies to The Kerala Fishermen Welfare Societies and their committees.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Fishermen Welfare Societies (Amendment) Act, 1985. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 4th day of June, 1985.

Amends section 9 of the Kerala Fishermen Welfare Societies Act, 1980 (7 of 1981). It adds a proviso to sub-section (1) and a new sub-section (ii) to sub-section (4). The proviso to sub-section (1) states that every society shall consist of not less than six and not more than ten members nominated by the Government. The added sub-section (ii) to sub-section (4) states that provided that a member of the first committee after the commencement of this Act shall hold office for a period of three years from the date of his nomination.

Amends section 10 of the principal Act. It adds a new sub-section (3) stating that the Government may remove from office any member of the first committee after the commencement of this Act, who is absent without leave of the committee for more than three consecutive meetings of the committee, or has become subject to any of the disqualifications mentioned in sub-section (1), or, provided that no such member shall be removed on the ground mentioned in clause (a) without giving him an opportunity of being heard.

Repeals The Kerala Fishermen Welfare Societies (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984 (76 of 1984). Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Rule: Every society shall consist of not less than six and not more than ten members nominated by the Government.
Rule: A member of the first committee after the commencement of this Act shall hold office for a period of three years from the date of his nomination.

Rule: The Government may remove from office any member of the first committee after the commencement of this Act, who is absent without leave of the committee for more than three consecutive meetings of the committee, or has become subject to any of the disqualifications mentioned in sub-section (1).
Rule: No such member shall be removed on the ground of absence without leave without giving him an opportunity of being heard.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Removal from office for absence or disqualification.

rights: Right to be heard before removal from office on grounds of absence.
duties: Duty to attend committee meetings.
obligations: Obligation to avoid disqualifications.

key_procedures: Procedure: Nomination of committee members by the Government (6-10 members).
Procedure: Holding office for three years by members of the first committee.

Procedure: Removal of a committee member by the Government if absent for more than three consecutive meetings without leave, or subject to disqualification, after providing an opportunity to be heard.
administration: The Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act commenced on the 4th day of June, 1985.
The Kerala Fishermen Welfare Societies (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984 is repealed.
Actions taken under the Ordinance are saved.

title: THE KERALA FISHERMEN WELFARE SOCIETIES ACT, 1980
purpose: To provide for the organisation of fisheries villages and to constitute fishermen welfare societies for such villages with a view to develop the economic, social and cultural life of the fishermen community in the State of Kerala.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and applies to fishermen welfare societies formed under this Act.

key_definitions.committee: means the committee of a society
key_definitions.Director: means the Director of Fisheries for the State of Kerala and includes any other officer appointed by the Government to exercise the powers and perform the functions of the Director under this Act
key_definitions.Fisheries Officer: means an officer appointed as such by the Government for the exercise of the powers and performance of the functions of the Fisheries Officer under this Act
key_definitions.fisherman: means any person engaged mainly in fishing operations for his livelihood
key_definitions.fishermen's welfare society: or 'society' means a society constituted by the Government under section 4
key_definitions.fisheries village: means an area declared by the Government under section 3 to be a fisheries village
key_definitions.fishing operations: includes: (i) fishing by any means, mechanical or otherwise; and (ii) the sale of marine products, by members of families of fishermen, by transporting them to different places by headload or cycle load; (i) 'marine products' includes fish and shell-fish grown or cultured and caught from any inland waters.
key_definitions.Explanation for inland waters: For the purposes of this clause, 'inland waters' includes ponds, tanks and reservoirs;
key_definitions.member: means a member of a society
key_definitions.prescribed: means prescribed by rules made under this Act
key_definitions.president: means the president of the committee of a society
key_definitions.secretary: means the secretary of the committee of a society

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Fishermen Welfare Societies Act, 1980. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 21st day of November, 1980.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'committee', 'Director', 'fish', 'Fisheries Officer', 'fisherman', 'fishermen's welfare society', 'fisheries village', 'fishing operations', 'inland waters', 'member', 'prescribed', 'president', 'secretary', and 'State'.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, declare, by such name as may be specified in the notification, the areas to be fisheries villages for the purposes of this Act and define the local limits of each such village.

The Government shall, by notification in the Gazette, constitute a fishermen's welfare society for each fisheries village by such name as may be specified in the notification. Every society shall be a body corporate by the name under which it is constituted, having perpetual succession and a common seal, with power to acquire, hold and dispose of property, both movable and immovable, enter into contracts, institute and defend suits and other legal proceedings and to do all things necessary for the purposes for which it is constituted.

Every fisherman who permanently resides in a fisheries village or carries on fishing operations from or within a fisheries village and who has attained the age of eighteen years, and is not of unsound mind, shall be deemed to be a member of the society constituted for that fisheries village.

Any member of a society who has acted adversely to the interests of the society may be expelled upon a resolution of the general body passed at a special meeting convened for the purpose by the votes of not less than two-thirds of the total number of members present and voting at the meeting. No member shall be expelled under subsection (1) without giving him an opportunity to make representations.
Every member of a society shall have one vote in the affairs of the society. Provided that in the case of an equality of votes, the president shall have and exercise a second or casting vote.
Subject to the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder, the final authority of a society shall vest in the general body of its members.

For every society, there shall be a committee consisting of the following persons, namely: (a) such number of members, being not less than four and not more than eight, as may be determined in such manner as may be prescribed, to be elected by the members of the society in the prescribed manner from among themselves; (b) not more than two members to be nominated by the Government. The members of the committee shall elect one among themselves to be its president. An elected member of the committee shall hold office for a period of three years from the date of his election. A nominated member of the committee shall hold office for such term as the Government may determine. Any member of a committee may resign his office by giving notice thereof in writing to the Director and, on such resignation being accepted, shall be deemed to have vacated his office. A casual vacancy in the office of a member of a committee may be filled up, as soon as may be, by election or nomination, as the case may be, and a member elected or nominated to fill such vacancy shall hold office for the unexpired portion of the term of office of the member whose place he fills.

main_sections.section_title: Disqualifications and removal of members of committee.
main_sections.description: No person shall be elected or nominated as, or continue to be, a member of the committee if he: (a) is an officer or servant under the committee; or (b) is an undischarged insolvent; or (c) is of unsound mind; or (d) has been convicted by a criminal court for an offence involving moral turpitude, unless such conviction has been set aside. The Government may remove from office any elected member of a committee who: (a) is or has become subject to any of the disqualifications mentioned in subsection (1); or (b) has ceased to be a fisherman; or (c) is absent without leave of the committee for more than three consecutive meetings of the committee.

main_sections.section_title: Acts of committee not to be invalidated by informality, vacancy, etc.
main_sections.description: No act or proceeding taken under this Act by a committee shall be invalid merely on the ground of: (a) any vacancy or defect in the constitution of the committee; or (b) any defect or irregularity in the election or nomination of a person acting as a member thereof; or (c) any defect or irregularity in such act or proceeding not affecting the merits of the case.

A general body meeting of a society shall be held once in a year for the purpose of: (a) approval of the budget with reference to the duties and functions of the society prepared by the committee for the ensuing year; (b) election, if any, in the prescribed manner, of the members of the committee other than nominated members; (c) consideration of the audit report and the annual report; (d) disposal of the net profit; and (e) consideration of any other matter which may be brought forward in accordance with the bye-laws.

The committee of a society may, at any time, call a special general body meeting of the society and shall call such meeting within one month after receipt of a requisition in writing from the Director or from such number of members or a proportion of the total number of members, as may be prescribed. If a special general body meeting of a society is not called in accordance with the requisition referred to in subsection (1), the Director or any person authorised by him in this behalf shall have power to call such meeting and that meeting shall be deemed to be a meeting called by the committee. Notwithstanding anything contained in subsection (1) or subsection (2), the Director or any person authorised by him in this behalf may, at any time, call a special general body meeting of the society in such manner and at such time and place within the area of its operation as he may direct and such meeting shall be deemed to be a meeting called by the committee. Notwithstanding anything contained in the bye-laws of a society, the Director or any person authorised by him in this behalf, may, at any time summon a meeting of the committee of the society and that meeting shall be deemed to be a meeting called in accordance with the bye-laws of the society and shall have power to transact all business which can be transacted at a meeting of the committee under the bye-laws of the society and such other business as is specially mentioned in the requisition made by the Director or the person authorised. The Director or any other person deputed by him shall have the right to attend the committee or general body meeting of any society convened in accordance with the provisions of this section.
The management of the affairs of a society shall be vested in the committee of that society. The committee shall exercise such other powers and perform such other functions as may be prescribed.

The Fisheries Officer shall be the secretary of the committee. Provided that the secretary shall, in cases where he is satisfied that any decision made by the committee is ultra vires the provisions of this Act or any other law for the time being in force or is against the objects of the Act, report the matter to the Director within such time as may be prescribed and carry the decision into effect if it is not suspended or cancelled by the Director.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of Director to cancel decision of committee.
main_sections.description: If on receipt of a report under the proviso to subsection (2) of section 15 or otherwise, the Director is satisfied that any decision of a committee is ultra vires the provisions of this Act or any other law for the time being in force or is against the objects of this Act, he may, by order in writing, cancel the decision: Provided that no decision shall be cancelled under this section unless the committee has been given a reasonable opportunity of showing cause against the proposed action.

Subject to such rules as may be made in this behalf, a society may - (a) take measures to make available fishing implements to its members at reasonable cost; (b) advance loans to the members for the purchase of fishing implements and effect recovery of such loans in easy instalments; (c) provide facilities for storage, processing and marketing of marine products; (d) provide facilities to the members for the repair and maintenance of fishing implements; (e) evolve and implement schemes for the welfare of the residents of fisheries villages; (f) provide for the payment of accident relief to members and their families; (g) provide for the payment of incapacity or disability or old age benefits to members; (h) provide for such other welfare schemes as would improve the standard of living and ameliorate the social conditions of the members; (i) provide for matters ancillary or incidental to any of the functions aforesaid; and (j) perform such other functions as may be prescribed.

A society may appoint such officers and other employees as may be necessary for carrying out its functions under this Act. The conditions of appointment and service and scales of pay of the officers and servants referred to in subsection (1) shall be such as may be prescribed.
The Government may, after due appropriation made by the Legislative Assembly in this behalf, pay to the societies by way of grants or loans such amounts as they consider necessary.
A society may, from time to time, subject to the provisions of this Act and to such conditions as may be prescribed in this behalf, borrow any sum required for the purposes of this Act.

A society may invest or deposit its funds - (a) in Government Savings Bank; or (b) in any of the securities specified in section 20 of the Indian Trusts Act, 1882 (Central Act 2 of 1882); or (c) in any other approved for the purpose by the Director; or (d) in any other prescribed manner.
A society shall receive deposits and loans only to such extent and under such conditions as may be prescribed or as may be specified in the bye-laws.
A society shall not make a loan to any person other than a member: Provided that, with the general or special sanction of the Director, a society may make loans to another society.

main_sections.section_title: First charge of society on certain assets.
main_sections.description: Notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force, but subject to any prior claim of the Government in respect of land revenue or any money recoverable as land revenue, any debt or outstanding demand owing to a society by any member or past member or deceased member shall be a first charge - (a) upon the fishing implements of such member for the purchase of which the loan was taken from the society by such member; and (b) upon any other property purchased in whole or in part out of any loan given by the society. No person shall transfer any property which is subject to a charge under sub-section (1) except with the previous permission in writing of the society which holds the charge. Notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force, any transfer of property made in contravention of the provisions of sub-section (2) shall be void. The charge created under sub-section (1) shall be available as against any claim of the Government arising from any loan granted by them after the grant of the loan by the society.

rights: Members have the right to vote in society affairs.
Members have the right to an opportunity to make representations before expulsion.
Members have the right to receive loans from the society (subject to restrictions).
duties: Members are responsible for the repayment of loans.
Members must act in the interests of the society.
obligations: Fishermen residing in a fisheries village are obligated to be members of the society if they meet the age and mental soundness criteria.

key_procedures: Constitution of a committee: Election of members by society members and nomination by the Government.
Calling of special general body meetings: Can be called by the committee or the Director, or by a specified proportion of members.
Cancellation of committee decisions: The Director can cancel decisions that are ultra vires or against the objects of the Act after providing an opportunity to be heard.
administration: Director of Fisheries for the State of Kerala
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on the 21st day of November, 1980.
A casual vacancy in the committee can be filled by election or nomination.
No act or proceeding of the committee is invalidated by informality, vacancy, or defect in constitution.
The Director has the power to cancel a committee's decision if it is ultra vires or against the Act's objects.

title: THE KERALA FISHERMEN AND ALLIED WORKERS WELFARE CESS ACT, 2007
purpose: To provide for the levy and collection of cess on the sale proceeds of fish, fish products, allied objects and equipments within the State with a view to augmenting the resources of the Kerala Fishermen's Welfare Fund constituted under section 3 of the Kerala Fishermen's Welfare Fund Act, 1985 (30 of 1985) for the purpose of achieving the object to safeguard the interest of fishermen and allied workers in the State.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and is deemed to have come into force on 18th day of February, 2006. It applies to the sale of fish, fish products, allied objects and equipments within the State.

key_definitions.allied worker: Any person who is engaged mainly in fishery related activities for his livelihood and who does not come under the definition of the term 'fisherman' in clause (c) of section 2 of the Kerala Fishermen's Welfare Societies Act, 1980 (7 of 1981) and includes beach workers, fish distributors, fish curers, peeling workers and processing plant workers who are not members or not eligible to get membership, in any other statutory welfare scheme.
key_definitions.assessing officer: Means an officer appointed by the Government under section 5.
key_definitions.board: Means the Kerala Fishermen's Welfare Fund Board constituted under section 7 of the Kerala Fishermen's Welfare Fund Act, 1985 (30 of 1985).
key_definitions.dealer: Means any person who engages in the business of buying and selling of fish or processing fish or bringing into the State or sending outside the State-the fish (raw or processed) or fish product or allied objects or equipments, and includes- (i) a commission agent, a broker, auctioneer or any other mercantile agent by whatever name called, and (ii) a non-resident dealer or an agent of a non-resident dealer or a branch of a firm or company or association situated outside the State Provided that, fishermen and allied worker as defined in the Kerala Fishermen's Welfare Fund Act, 1985 (30 of 1985), shall not be included in this
key_definitions.fish: means shrimp, prawn, mussel, clam, cuttlefish, squids, crab including all varieties of fish or any other aquatic organisms and aquatic plants and ornamental fishes exploited commercially for edible or medicinal purposes or for manure or feed,
key_definitions.fisherman: means a fisherman as defined in clause (e) of section 2 of the Kerala Fishermen's Welfare Societies Act, 1980 (7 of 1981).
key_definitions.fishing vessel: means a ship or boat, whether or not fitted with mechanical means of propulsion, which is engaged in fishing for profit and includes, a catamaran, vanchi or vallam or by any craft known by local variations thereof,
key_definitions.fund: means the Kerala Fishermen's Welfare Fund established under section 3 of the Kerala Fishermen's Welfare Fund Act, 1985,
key_definitions.prescribed: means prescribed by rules made under this Act,
key_definitions.sale proceeds: means the sale value of all transactions carried out in the State including buying or selling, bringing in or sending outside the State, fish or fish products or allied objects or equipments for use or for processing otherwise

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Fishermen's and Allied Workers' Welfare Cess Act, 2007. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and is deemed to have come into force on 18th day of February, 2006.

Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'allied worker', 'assessing officer', 'Board', 'dealer', 'fish', 'fisherman', 'fishing vessel', 'fund', 'Government', 'prescribed', and 'sale proceeds'. Words and expressions used but not defined have the same meaning as in the Kerala Fishermen's Welfare Fund Act, 1985.

States that a cess shall be levied and collected for the purpose of the Kerala Fishermen Welfare Fund Act, 1985, and the scheme thereunder, at one percent of the total sale proceeds of a dealer in a financial year. The cess is to be collected from every dealer in such manner and at such time as prescribed. The cess levied is in addition to any cess, duty or tax leviable under any law. The proceeds are to be credited to the Fund of the Board, and the amount collected must be paid to the Fund before 30th June of every year.

The Director of Fisheries shall be the authority to administer, supervise and to enforce the Act. The Government shall appoint, by notification in the Gazette, such officers of the Fisheries Department not below the rank of Fisheries Extension Officer/Matsya Bhavan Officer as Assessing Officer for the purposes of the Act.

The Government shall appoint, by notification in the Gazette, such officers of the Fisheries Department not below the rank of Fisheries Extension Officer/Matsya Bhavan Officer as Assessing Officer for the purposes of the Act.

Every dealer shall maintain such registers and records as may be prescribed. The registers and records shall be kept in the establishment of the dealer and shall be produced on demand by any officer or authority under this Act for verification.

main_sections.section_title: Furnishing of Return by the dealer
main_sections.description: Every dealer shall furnish to the Assessing Officer of the area a return showing the sale proceeds of the previous financial year in the manner as may be prescribed. If any dealer fails to furnish the return, the Assessing Officer shall give notice requiring the dealer to furnish such return before the specified date.

On receipt of the return, the Assessing Officer shall, after making or causing to be made inquiry, assess the amount of cess payable by the dealer. If the dealer has not furnished the return, the Assessing Officer shall proceed to assess the amount of cess payable by the dealer after making inquiry. The order of assessment shall be made under sub-section (1) or sub-section (2) and the date within which the cess shall be paid by the dealer. The Assessing Officer conducting the inquiry shall have the same powers as are vested in a civil court while trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

Every dealer who is liable to pay cess under section 3 shall pay before fifteenth day of succeeding month, until assessing the amount payable by him under section 8 an amount equal to one-fourth of the cess payable by him annually in accordance with the assessment under section 8. Where the amount is not paid, the Assessing Officer shall issue notice to the defaulter showing the amount in arrears directing to pay the said amount within such period as may be shown in the notice. The amount paid under this section shall be adjusted against the assessment under section 8 for that year.

main_sections.section_title: Interest payable on delayed payment of Cess
main_sections.description: If any dealer fails to pay any amount of cess payable under section 3 within the time specified in the order of assessment, such dealer shall be liable to pay interest on the amount to be paid at the rate of two percent for every month or part of a month comprised in the period from the date on which such payment is due till such amount is actually paid.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for non-payment of Cess within the specified time
main_sections.description: If any amount of cess payable by any dealer under section 3 is not paid within the date specified in the order of assessment, it shall be deemed to be in arrears and the Assessing Officer may, after making such enquiry and after giving him a reasonable opportunity of being heard, impose on such dealer an amount as penalty not exceeding the amount of cess.

main_sections.section_title: Recovery of amount due under this Act
main_sections.description: Any amount due under this Act, including any interest or penalty, from a dealer may be recovered in the same manner as an arrear of public revenue due on land.

A dealer aggrieved by an order of assessment made under section 8, or by an order imposing penalty under section 11, may, within sixty days of receipt of order, prefer an appeal to the Director of Fisheries in such form and in such manner as may be prescribed. Provided that the Director of Fisheries may condone the delay in filing the appeal, if it is satisfied that the delay was on reasonable ground. On receipt of the appeal, the Director of Fisheries shall, after giving the appellant an opportunity of being heard in the matter, dispose of the appeal within one month. Every order passed shall be final and shall not be called in question in any court of law.

The Government may, either suo motu or on an application of the aggrieved person, call for the records of any proceedings taken by the Appellate Authority under sub-section (2) of section 13 and make such enquiry and pass such orders, as they deem fit. Provided that an application for revision under this section shall be made within thirty days from the date on which the order was communicated to the applicant and no order shall be passed under this section without giving the person an opportunity of being heard.

Any Assessing Officer or any other officer specially empowered in this behalf by the Government, may- (a) with such assistance, as he thinks fit, enter at any reasonable time, any establishment or place where he considers it necessary to enter for the purpose of this Act, including verification of the correctness of the particulars furnished by any dealer under section 7, (b) require the production of any register and any other document relating to the sale of fish, fish products, allied objects or equipments, and (c) exercise such other powers as may be prescribed.

Every Assessing Officer shall furnish to the Director of Fisheries every month a return showing the amount collected by him as cess, fine or interest during the previous month, in such form and within such period as may be prescribed. The Director of Fisheries shall furnish to the Government every year a return showing the total amount collected in the State as cess, fine or interest during the previous financial year, within such period and in such form as may be prescribed.

Any dealer, who fails to furnish a return under this Act, or has furnished incorrect particulars shall be punishable with imprisonment which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees or with both. Whoever, wilfully or intentionally evades or attempts to evade the payment of such cess, shall be punishable with imprisonment which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees or with both. Whoever, contravenes any of the provisions of this Act or the rules made thereunder shall, if no other penalty is elsewhere provided under this Act for such contravention, be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees or with both. No court shall take cognizance of an offence punishable under this section save on a complaint made by or under the authority of the Director of Fisheries.

Where an offence under this Act has been committed by a company, every person who, at the time of commission of offence, was in charge of and was responsible to the company for the conduct of the business of the company, as well as the company, shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly. Provided that nothing contained in this sub-section shall render any such person liable to any punishment if he proves that the offence was committed without his knowledge or that he had exercised all due diligence to prevent the commission of such offence. Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), where an offence under this Act has been committed with the consent or connivance of, or is attributable to any negligence on the part of any Director, Manager, Secretary or other officer bearer of the company, such director, manager, secretary or other office bearer shall also be deemed to be guilty of that offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly.

main_sections.section_title: Bar of jurisdiction of Civil Courts
main_sections.description: No Civil Court shall have jurisdiction to settle, decide or deal with any question or to determine any matter which is by or under this Act or the rules made thereunder required to be settled, decided or dealt with or to be determined by the Government or any authority or officer appointed under this Act.

The Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act. Without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing power, such rules may provide for all or any of the following matters, namely: (a) the manner in which and the time which the cess shall be levied and collected; (b) the manner in which the transfer of money to the Board shall be made; (c) the form and manner of maintaining the registers and records to be maintained by the dealer; (d) particulars of the return to be furnished by the dealer; (e) the manner in which an appeal may be filed; (f) the powers which may be exercised by the officers under clause (c) of section 15.

important_rules: Every dealer shall maintain such registers and records as may be prescribed.

penalties: Imprisonment up to six months or fine up to one thousand rupees or both for failure to furnish a return or for furnishing incorrect particulars.
Imprisonment up to six months or fine up to one thousand rupees or both for wilfully or intentionally evading or attempting to evade cess payment.

Amount of penalty not exceeding the amount of cess for non-payment of cess within the specified time.

title: The Kerala Fishermen's Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 1999
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Fishermen's Welfare Fund Act, 1985.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Fishermen's Welfare Fund.

key_definitions.allied worker: Means any person who is engaged in fishing harbours or fish landing centres or fish landing sites to carry out activities such as, unloading of fish from fishug crafts to fish baskets, transportation of fish baskets to auction site or icing site, transportation of trash fish or small fish to curing site, sorting of fish at the landing site, unloading and crushing of ice, packing fish with ice in boxes and loading of packed boxes into vehicles used for transportation, loading of fish directly from boats to lories, sale of ice in the fishing harbours or fish landing centres, cleaning auction hall, fishing crafts and supplying water for fishing boat, and mending and repair of fishing nets.
key_definitions.dealer: Means any person who carries on, within the State of Kerala, the business of buying or selling or processing fish or exporting fish (in raw or in processed form) or fish products and includes: a commission agent, a broker or any other mercantile agent; by whatever name called; and a non-resident dealer or an agent of a non-resident dealer or a local branch of a firm or company or association situated outside the State of Kerala.
key_definitions.fish: Means fish of all varieties including prawn, lobster, shellfish, clam, squids or any other aquatic organism exploited commercially for edible purposes or for manure;
key_definitions.fish curer: Means a worker who is engaged in the activities connected with drying, salted dry curing and salted wet curing;
key_definitions.fish products: Means fish in raw or in processed form;
key_definitions.peeling worker: Means a worker who is engaged in peeling prawn, lobster clam, cleaning squids and cuttle fishes in huts, peeling sheds and fish processing plants;
key_definitions.processing: Means any means of preservation of fish or fish products effected with or without physical or chemical changes by mechanical means, or otherwise, intended to facilitate increase in the shelf life of fish or fish products or to avoid loss during transit or value addition;
key_definitions.processing worker: Means a worker who is engaged in cleaning, grading processing and packing of fish or fish products;
key_definitions.sale proceeds: Means the amount realised or is likely to be realised by sale of fish or fish products;
key_definitions.Scheme: Means the Kerala Fishermen's Welfare Fund Scheme, framed under this Act;
key_definitions.small scale distributors: Means those persons engaged in distribution of fish from fish landing centres or fish harbours or fish curing yards or markets through retail outlets or by house delivery and includes: auto-carrier distributors, cycle load vendors, drivers and cleaners engaged in fish transporting on a permanent basis; head load vendors, including vendors, who sell fish in temporary camps; mini lorry distributors; and moped load distributors.
key_definitions.prawn filtration area: Means any water logged area where prawn filtration is carried on.
key_definitions.Prawn Culture Farm: Means a farm where prawn, including scampi, are cultured.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Fishermen's Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 1999. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 11th day of November, 1998.

Amends section 2 of the Kerala Fishermen's Welfare Fund Act, 1985 by relettering clauses and inserting new definitions for 'allied worker', 'dealer', 'fish', 'fish curer', 'fish products', 'peeling worker', 'processing', 'processing worker', 'sale proceeds', 'Scheme', and 'small scale distributors'.

Amends section 3 of the principal Act by inserting a new sub-section (1A) stating that notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, frame a scheme, exclusively for allied workers, to be called the 'Allied Workers' Welfare Scheme' under the said Fund and the provisions of sections 5, 16, 17, 18, 19, 21 and the schedule to this Act shall, mutatis mutandis in respect of the said scheme.

Amends section 4 of the principal Act by substituting sub-sections (1), (2), (3), (4) and (5). These amendments relate to contributions to the Fund by every fisherman, allied worker, dealer, owner of a fishing vessel, owner of a prawn filtration area or a prawn culture farm, and owners of fish markets or lessees or licensees. It also provides explanations for 'prawn filtration area' and 'Prawn Culture Farm'.

In sub-section (3), for clause (f), the following clause shall be substituted, namely: -- '(f) five representatives of the fishermen to be nominated by the Government, of whom two shall be from the allied workers;' and in sub-section (6), the word 'or to the Managing Director of the Kerala State Co-operative Federation for Fisheries Development' shall be omitted.
In section 13 of the principal Act, the proviso to sub-section (1) shall be omitted.

The Kerala Fishermen's Welfare Fund (Amendment) Ordinance, 1999 (2 of 1999) is hereby repealed. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken, under the principal Act, as amended by the said Ordinance, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

obligations: Every fisherman shall contribute to the Fund every year at such rate, as may be fixed by the Government from time to time on the recommendation of the Board.
Every allied worker shall contribute to the Fund, every year at such rate, as may be fixed by the Government, from time to time, on the recommendation of the Board.
A dealer shall contribute to the Fund, every year, one per cent of his sale proceeds in the year.

The owner of a fishing vessel of any category, shall contribute to the Fund, every month, an amount, at such rate, as may be fixed by the Government, from time to time, on the recommendation of the Board, to that category of fishing vessel.
The owner of a takenet or chinanet shall contribute to the Fund, at such rate, as may be fixed by the Government, from time to time, on the recommendation of the Board, for nine months every year.

The owner of a prawn filtration area or a prawn culture farm or a fish farm shall contribute to the fund every year, at such rate, per hectare, as may be fixed by the Government, from time to time, on the recommendation of the Board.

The owners of fish markets or lessees or licensees or any person claiming any right or interest, through such owners, or the owners of the ice plants supplying ice, mainly for the processing of fish and the vehicles engaged, mainly for the transportation of fish, shall contribute to the fund, every year, at such rate as may be fixed by the Government, from time to time, on the recommendation of the Board.

administration: Not explicitly stated, but likely related to fisheries or welfare departments of the Kerala Government.

The Allied Workers' Welfare Scheme is to be framed under the main Fund.

title: The Kerala Forest (Amendment) Act, 1989
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Forest Act, 1961 for the purpose hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Forest Act, 1961, specifically regarding the amendment of section 75A and the repeal and saving provisions related to the Kerala Forest Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1988.

title: THE KERALA FOREST (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1973
purpose: An Act to amend the Kerala Forest Act, 1961.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Forest (Amendment) Act, 1973. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 17th day of September, 1973.

Section 43 of the Kerala Forest Act, 1961 is renumbered as sub-section (1) of that section. New sub-sections (2) and (3) are inserted to provide for the collection and verification of timber, including provisions for the owner's claim and statements. A new sub-section (4) requires copies of notices to be affixed in Divisional Forest Offices and concerned Forest Range Offices.

The Kerala Forest (Amendment) Ordinance, 1973 is repealed. However, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Rule: Unmarked timber collected from any area referred to in section 42 shall be collected by the Divisional Forest Officer.

Rule: A notice under sub-section (2) shall contain a description of the timber and the place from which it was collected and the station where it is stored.

penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Issuing notices, collecting timber, requiring written statements.

rights: Right of the owner to claim timber if they can prove ownership.
duties: Duty to provide a written statement to the Divisional Forest Officer within a period of fourteen days from the date of service of notice.
obligations: Obligation for the Divisional Forest Officer to collect unmarked timber.

key_procedures: Procedure: If unmarked timber is collected from any area, the Divisional Forest Officer shall collect it. If the owner is not ascertainable, the officer shall require them to prove ownership.

Procedure: The Divisional Forest Officer shall issue a notice containing a description of the timber and its place of collection. The owner has fourteen days to submit a written statement to prove their claim.
Procedure: Copies of the notice must be affixed in the Divisional Forest Office and the concerned Forest Range Office.

scope: Applies to forest produce, sandalwood, sandalwood oil, and related activities within Kerala. It also pertains to the enforcement and penalties related to these forest produce.

key_definitions.sandalwood: means any portion of timber of sandal (santalum album) tree and includes bark, leaves and roots thereof, whether containing heartwood or not and whether in the form of roots, billets, pieces (sawn or otherwise), chips (whether coloured or not and whether mixed with other ingredients or not), sawdust, spent wood, flakes, pulp or derivatives of sandalwood such as sandalwood oil
key_definitions.authorised officer: means the Principal Chief Conservator of Forests or any other officer not below the rank of Divisional Forest Officer authorised by the Government for the purpose of this Chapter

main_sections.description: Prohibits the possession or transport of sandalwood in excess of one kilogram or sandalwood oil in excess of one hundred millilitre without permission. main_sections.description: Requires every person possessing sandalwood or sandalwood oil in excess of specified quantities to declare and surrender such quantity to the authorised officer within ninety days from the commencement of the Act.

main_sections.description: Specifies that the authorised officer shall pay the price fixed by the Government from time to time for sandalwood or sandalwood oil surrendered under section 47B or section 47C.

main_sections.section_title: Restriction on purchase, sale etc of sandalwood and sandalwood oil
main_sections.description: Prohibits the purchase, receive or acquire sandalwood or sandalwood oil otherwise than from the Government or the authorised officer or public sector undertakings owned by Government or any other agency authorised by Government. No licensee under this Chapter shall keep in his control, custody or possession or acquire, receive, sell or offer for sale or process or transport sandalwood or sandalwood oil except in accordance with the conditions of the licence granted.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for offences in regard to sandalwood
main_sections.description: Outlines penalties for offences related to forest offence having reference to cutting, uprooting or removal of a sandalwood tree or any part thereof. Specifies imprisonment terms and fines for first and subsequent offences. Also details penalties for contravening provisions of sections 47C and 47D.

main_sections.section_title: Seizure of sandalwood, sandalwood oil etc and confiscation thereon
