main_sections.description: Empowers the authorised officer to seize sandalwood, sandalwood oil, or any other contrivance used in the process of sale or transport. It states that seized items shall be liable to be seized under section 52 and the provisions contained in sections 61A, 61B, 61C, 61D, 61E and 61F shall mutatis mutandis apply to the seizure and confiscation thereof.

important_rules: Cutting and sale of sandalwood trees require prior permission from an authorised officer.
Possession or transport of sandalwood and sandalwood oil is restricted to specified quantities without permission.
Anyone possessing sandalwood or sandalwood oil above a certain stock limit must declare it within ninety days of the Act's commencement.
Sandalwood and sandalwood oil can only be purchased, sold, or acquired from the Government or authorised entities.
No person shall engage in the purchase, sale, or transport of sandalwood or sandalwood oil without a valid licence.

Licensed individuals must adhere to the conditions of their licence regarding control, custody, possession, acquisition, sale, offering for sale, processing, or transport of sandalwood or sandalwood oil.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than three years but may extend to seven years and with fine which shall not be less than ten thousand rupees but may extend to twenty-five thousand rupees (for first offence of cutting/uprooting/removal of sandalwood tree).
Imprisonment shall not be less than five years and the amount of fine shall not be less than twenty thousand rupees (for second or subsequent offence).

Imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than three years but may extend to seven years and with fine which shall not be less than twenty-five thousand rupees but may extend to rupees one lakh (for contravening provisions of section 47C).
Imprisonment shall not be less than five years and the amount of fine shall not be less than fifty thousand rupees (for second or subsequent offence under section 47C).

Imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than three years but may extend to seven years and with fine which shall not be less than twenty-five thousand rupees but may extend to rupees one lakh (for contravening provisions of section 47D and 47F).
Imprisonment shall not be less than five years and the amount of fine shall not be less than fifty thousand rupees (for second or subsequent offence under section 47D and 47F).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Authorised officer (Principal Chief Conservator of Forests or any other officer not below the rank of Divisional Forest Officer authorised by the Government)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through seizure of sandalwood, sandalwood oil etc., confiscation of seized items, prosecution and imposition of penalties including imprisonment and fines. Seized items are liable to be seized under section 52, and relevant provisions of sections 61A, 61B, 61C, 61D, 61E and 61F apply to seizure and confiscation.

rights: Right to obtain permission for cutting/sale of sandalwood trees for personal use under specific conditions.
Right to obtain a licence for possession or transport of sandalwood and sandalwood oil for specified purposes.
Right to receive payment for surrendered sandalwood or sandalwood oil at rates fixed by the Government.
Right to appeal decisions regarding licences or permissions to the Government.
duties: Duty to obtain permission before cutting or selling sandalwood trees.
Duty to obtain a licence for possession or transport of sandalwood and sandalwood oil above prescribed limits.
Duty to declare stock of sandalwood and sandalwood oil if exceeding prescribed limits.
Duty to purchase, sell, or acquire sandalwood or sandalwood oil only from authorised sources.
Duty to comply with the conditions of any licence granted.
Duty to surrender excess stock of sandalwood or sandalwood oil to the authorised officer.
obligations: Obligation to report to the Government when a decision is made regarding permission for cutting sandalwood trees.
Obligation to follow the rules and procedures prescribed under this Act and the principal Act.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining permission to cut or sell sandalwood trees: The owner must apply to the authorised officer. The officer may grant or refuse permission based on specific criteria, potentially requiring a written report to the Government for certain decisions.
Procedure for obtaining a licence for possession or transport of sandalwood/oil: An application is made to the authorised officer, who may issue a licence subject to restrictions and conditions.
Procedure for declaring stock: Persons exceeding stock limits must declare and surrender the excess quantity to the authorised officer within ninety days.
Procedure for seizure and confiscation: Seized sandalwood, sandalwood oil, or related items are subject to section 52 and other relevant sections of the principal Act.
administration: The Principal Chief Conservator of Forests or an authorised Divisional Forest Officer, under the authority of the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act further amends the Kerala Forest Act, 1961.
The Act inserts a new Chapter VI A concerning provisions relating to sandalwood.
Permission to cut or sell sandalwood trees can be refused if the tree is dead or wind fallen and its cutting would endanger life or property, or enable use of the cleared area for building purposes.
The authorised officer has the power to cancel or suspend licences.

The authorised officer may issue licences for possession or transport of sandalwood oil to religious institutions, artisans, licensed manufacturers, and registered practitioners of indigenous medicines or any corporation or society owned by the Government for their bona fide purposes, subject to restrictions and conditions.

title: THE KERALA FOREST (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1980
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Forest Act, 1961.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Forest Act, 1961. Amendments introduced by this Act apply to matters specified within the Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Forest (Amendment) Act, 1980, and it came into force on the 1st day of June, 1980.

Inserts a new section 12A concerning appeals to the High Court. This section details the conditions under which an appeal can be made, the timeframe for filing, and the powers of the High Court and District Court regarding such appeals. It also specifies the fees for appeals.

Amends section 14 of the principal Act. It modifies the provisions related to appeals to the High Court against orders of the District Court, particularly concerning the period for filing appeals and the grounds for dismissal.

Provides for situations where any appeal, if deemed to have been done or taken under section 11, has been disposed of by the District Court, or any judgment, decree, or order of the Government or any person objecting to any order of the District Court in an appeal under section 11, made before the specified date of publication of this Ordinance and before the date of publication of the Kerala Forest (Amendment) Ordinance, 1980 (8 of 1980) in the Gazette, within a period of ninety days from the date of such publication, appeal to the High Court against such order, and the provisions of subsections (2) to (5) (both inclusive) of section 12A of the principal Act as amended by this Act shall apply in respect of such appeal.

Repeals the Kerala Forest (Amendment) Ordinance, 1980 (8 of 1980), and states that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the said Ordinance or the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act, or, as the case may be, under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided sections. Likely forest authorities or judicial bodies as per the principal Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the judicial process, including appeals to the High Court and District Court as detailed in the amended sections.

rights: Right to appeal to the High Court against certain orders of the District Court.

key_procedures: Filing an appeal to the High Court against orders of the District Court within a specified period (90 days).
The process for appealing involves presenting the appeal in the prescribed manner and form, accompanied by a fee of one hundred rupees.
The District Court may confirm, cancel, or pass such other orders as it thinks fit on an appeal.
The High Court can set aside, remand, or pass other orders on appeals from the District Court.
administration: The administration of the Forest Act would typically fall under the Forest Department of the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act commenced on June 1, 1980.
The Act refers to and amends the Kerala Forest Act, 1961.
The Act also repeals the Kerala Forest (Amendment) Ordinance, 1980 (8 of 1980).

title: THE KERALA FOREST (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1993
purpose: To amend the Kerala Forest Act, 1961, for the purposes appearing.
scope: Applies to forest-related activities and land within Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Forest (Amendment) Act, 1993, and it shall come into force on the 12th day of November, 1992.
Amends Section 7 of the principal Act by substituting specific words and figures related to 'proclamation' and 'notification'.

Amends Section 27 of the principal Act by substituting sub-section (1) with provisions that define prohibited actions in forests, including setting fires, clearing land, and causing damage to forests or forest produce. It also specifies penalties for these offenses.
States that the Schedule to the principal Act shall be omitted.

Repeals the Kerala Forest (Amendment) Ordinance, 1992 (9 of 1992). It also provides a saving clause stating that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Do not set fire to a Reserved Forest or kindles or leaves burning any fire in such manner as to endanger the same.

Do not set fire to jungles or forests other than Reserved Forest and a land proposed to be constituted a Reserved Forest, without taking precautionary measures to prevent the spread of fire into Reserved Forest and land proposed to be constituted a Reserved Forest.

Do not cultivate or clears or breaks up any land for cultivation or for any other purpose or puts up any shed or other structures or plants trees on any land in a Reserved Forest or a land proposed to be constituted a Reserved Forest.
Do not damage, alter or removes any wall, ditch, embankment, fence hedge or railing in a Reserved Forest.

Do not cut or fell any trees or girdles, marks, lops, taps, uproots, burns, saws, converts or removes any tree including fallen or felled, or strips off the bark or leaves from or otherwise damages the same.
Do not trespass or causes cattle or permits or causes cattle to trespass on any land in a Reserved Forest.
Do not quarry stones, burns lime or charcoal or collects or subjects to any manufacturing process or removes any forest produce, or
Do not causes any damage by negligence in felling any tree, reed or cutting or dragging any timber in a Reserved Forest.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than one year but may extend to five years and with fine which shall not be less than one thousand rupees but may extend to five thousand rupees for causing damage by negligence in felling any tree, reed or cutting or dragging any timber in a Reserved Forest.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be forest authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings and penalties as described in Section 3 of the Act.

duties: Duty to prevent the spread of fire into Reserved Forests.
Duty to refrain from cultivating, clearing, building, planting, damaging, altering, removing, cutting, quarrying, collecting, or causing damage within Reserved Forests without authorization.

key_procedures: Omission of the Schedule to the principal Act.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but likely falls under the purview of the Forest Department of the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 26th day of February, 1993 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 214 dated the 27th February 1993.
The Act comes into force on the 12th day of November, 1992.

title: THE KERALA FOREST (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1986
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Forest Act, 1961, by introducing a new Chapter XA regarding Forest Development Tax.
scope: Applies to all forest produce disposed of by the Government for sale, and to members of Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes for personal use of their traditional crafts or to co-operative societies of Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes.

key_definitions.sale: In relation to the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963 (15 of 1963), the tax payable under sub-section (1) in respect of any forest produce shall be collected along with the consideration paid therefor.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Forest (Amendment) Act, 1986, and it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of September, 1984.
Inserts a new Chapter XA, titled 'FOREST DEVELOPMENT TAX', into the Kerala Forest Act, 1961.

Imposes a tax on forest produce disposed of by the Government for sale at the rate of five per cent of the amount of consideration paid. Provides exemption for tax on any forest produce, except timber, charcoal, cane, bamboo and firewood, sold to members of Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes for personal use or for use in traditional crafts, or to co-operative societies of Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of Kerala Forest Development Fund
main_sections.description: Establishes a Kerala Forest Development Fund for the purpose of the Development Fund. Details the crediting of proceeds, deduction of expenses, and the remaining amount being entered into and transferred to the Development Fund. Specifies that no sum shall be paid or applied from and out of the Development Fund except as provided in sub-section (5), and the standing amount shall be expended in such manner and subject to such conditions as prescribed by rules made under this Act. The Government may hold and administer the fund, or delegate this to the Chief Conservator of Forests, subject to special directions. The fund is for specified purposes like sixty per cent for planting and maintenance of soft-wood trees and other species of trees, and forty per cent for forest research.

Repeals the Kerala Forest (Amendment) Ordinance, 1986. States that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken or deemed to have been done or taken under the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Forest development tax shall be levied and collected at the rate of five per cent of the amount of consideration paid on forest produce disposed of by the Government for sale.

No tax shall be levied or collected on any forest produce, except timber, charcoal, cane, bamboo and firewood, sold to members of Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes for personal use or for use in their traditional crafts, or to Co-operative Societies of Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes.
The tax payable under sub-section (1) shall be collected along with the consideration paid therefor.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government, through the Chief Conservator of Forests, or as directed by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the levy and collection of tax on forest produce and the administration of the Forest Development Fund.

rights: Right of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes to purchase certain forest produce without tax for personal use or traditional crafts.
duties: Duty to pay forest development tax at the prescribed rate.
Duty to collect tax along with the consideration paid for forest produce.
obligations: The Government is obligated to establish and administer the Kerala Forest Development Fund for specified purposes.

key_procedures: Procedure for levy and collection of forest development tax on forest produce disposed of by the Government for sale.
Procedure for the establishment and administration of the Kerala Forest Development Fund, including crediting proceeds and deducting expenses.
Procedure for the repeal of the Kerala Forest (Amendment) Ordinance, 1986, and saving of actions taken under it.
administration: The Government, potentially through the Chief Conservator of Forests, administers the Forest Development Fund.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of September, 1984.
The assent of the Governor was received on the 28th day of November, 1986, and it was published in the Kerala Gazette, Extraordinary No. 1067 dated 29th November, 1986.
The Kerala Forest (Amendment) Ordinance, 1986, is repealed.

title: The Kerala Forest (Vesting And Management Of Ecologically Fragile Lands) Act, 2003
purpose: To provide for the vesting in the Government and the management of ecologically fragile lands in the State of Kerala and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to ecologically fragile lands in the State of Kerala. The definition of 'ecologically fragile land' is provided in the Act, referring to forest land and other lands with rich biodiversity that require special protection.

key_definitions.ecologically_fragile_lands: Includes forest land and other lands within the State possessing rich biodiversity and requiring special protection due to their ecological importance, biological diversity, geomorphological characteristics, proximity to ecologically sensitive areas, etc.
key_definitions.forest_land: Includes all lands classified as forest under the Indian Forest Act, 1927 or any other law in force in the State, and also includes land notified by the Government as forest land.
key_definitions.management: Includes conservation, protection, regeneration, sustainable utilization, and research of ecologically fragile lands.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its extent to the whole of the State of Kerala, and the date of commencement.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'ecologically fragile lands', 'Government', 'forest land', 'management', etc.

main_sections.section_title: Vesting of ecologically fragile lands in Government
main_sections.description: Declares that all ecologically fragile lands shall vest in the Government and that the Government shall have the power to manage them.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of the Government to protect and manage ecologically fragile lands
main_sections.description: Outlines the powers of the Government to protect and manage ecologically fragile lands, including measures for conservation, regeneration, and prevention of activities detrimental to these lands.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of Ecological Fragile Lands Protection Authority
main_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of an authority to advise the Government on matters relating to the protection and management of ecologically fragile lands.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of certain activities in ecologically fragile lands
main_sections.description: Prohibits certain activities such as clearing of forests, quarrying, industrial activities, and the establishment of permanent structures in ecologically fragile lands.

main_sections.section_title: Power to declare areas as ecologically fragile lands
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to declare any area as ecologically fragile land.
Provides for the constitution of a Forest Advisory Committee to advise the Government on forest conservation and management matters.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Specifies the penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act and the rules made thereunder.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides for the protection of any action taken in good faith in pursuance of the provisions of the Act.
Grants the Government the power to remove any difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
Repeals certain previous enactments and provides for savings.

important_rules: Prohibition of clearing of forests, quarrying, industrial activities, and establishment of permanent structures in ecologically fragile lands (Section 6).
Regulations on grazing and collection of forest produce in ecologically fragile lands.
Rules regarding the constitution and functions of the Ecological Fragile Lands Protection Authority and the Forest Advisory Committee.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine which may extend to one lakh rupees or with both (Section 10(1)).
For subsequent offences, imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and with fine which may extend to two lakh rupees (Section 10(1)).
Penalties for contravention of specific rules, such as those related to grazing or collection of forest produce, may vary.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Forest Department and other authorities designated by the Government of Kerala.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, monitoring, and legal proceedings against offenders.

rights: The right of the Government to vest and manage ecologically fragile lands.
The right of the public to information regarding the protection and management of these lands.
duties: The duty of the Government to protect and manage ecologically fragile lands.
The duty of individuals and organizations to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules.
The duty to prevent activities detrimental to ecologically fragile lands.
obligations: Obligation to obtain prior approval for any activity that might affect ecologically fragile lands.
Obligation to report any illegal activities in these areas.

key_procedures: Procedure for the Government to declare areas as ecologically fragile lands (Section 7).
Procedure for the constitution and functioning of the Ecological Fragile Lands Protection Authority and the Forest Advisory Committee.
Procedure for seeking permission for any activity within or affecting ecologically fragile lands.
Procedure for prosecution and imposition of penalties for contravention of the Act.
administration: The Forest Department, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act aims to preserve unique ecosystems and biodiversity hotspots in Kerala.
It emphasizes the importance of scientific management and conservation of these sensitive areas.
The Act provides for citizen participation and awareness regarding the protection of ecologically fragile lands.

title: THE KERALA FOREST (VESTING AND MANAGEMENT OF ECOLOGICALLY FRAGILE LANDS) ACT, 2003
purpose: To provide for the vesting in the Government of ecologically fragile lands in the State of Kerala and for the management of such lands with a view to maintaining ecological balance and conserving the bio-diversity.
scope: Applies to ecologically fragile lands in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.custodian: The Principal Chief Conservator of Forests of the State or any other officer not below the rank of a Conservator of Forests appointed by the Government, by notification in the Gazette, to exercise the powers and perform the functions of the custodian under this Act.
key_definitions.ecologically fragile lands: Any forest land or any portion thereof held by any person and lying contiguous to or encircled by a reserved forest or a vested forest or any other forest land owned by the Government and predominantly supporting natural vegetation, and (ii) any land declared to be an ecologically fragile land by the Government by notification in the Gazette under section 4;
key_definitions.forest: Means any land principally covered with naturally grown trees and undergrowth and includes any forest statutorily recognised and declared reserved forest, protected forest or otherwise, but does not include any land which is used principally for the cultivation of crops of long duration such as tea, coffee, rubber, pepper, cardamom, coconut, arecanut or cashew or any other sites of residential buildings and surroundings essential for the convenient use of such buildings;
key_definitions.land: Includes rivers, streams and its origin and other water bodies,
key_definitions.natural vegetation: Means a growing stock predominantly of a plant species or of a number of plant species occurring naturally on the land,
key_definitions.owner: In relation to an ecologically fragile land includes a mortgagee, lessee or any other person having the right of possession and enjoyment of the ecologically fragile land,
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act,
key_definitions.reserved forests: Means the forests reserved under section 19 of the Kerala Forest Act, 1961 (4 of 1962) and includes forests notified under section 4 of the said Act,
key_definitions.tribunal: Means a tribunal constituted under section 9 of this Act,

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its commencement date, which is the 2nd day of June, 2000.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'custodian', 'ecologically fragile lands', 'forest', 'land', 'natural vegetation', 'owner', 'prescribed', 'reserved forests', and 'tribunal'.

main_sections.section_title: Ecologically fragile lands to vest in Government
main_sections.description: Declares that ecologically fragile lands vest in the Government, and the owner or other person thereon shall stand extinguished from the said date. It also mandates notification and placement before the Advisory Committee for perusal.

main_sections.section_title: Power to declare ecologically fragile land
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to declare land as ecologically fragile, with prior notification and opportunity for the owner to be heard. It also states that no person shall change the legal status or ownership of land proposed to be declared.

main_sections.section_title: Ecologically fragile land to be deemed to be reserved forests
main_sections.description: Subject to provisions of section 16, all ecologically fragile lands vested in Government under section 3 and section 4 shall be deemed to be reserved forests constituted under the Kerala Forest Act, 1961 and the provisions of that Act shall, so far as may be, apply to such lands.
Requires the custodian to demarcate the boundaries of ecologically fragile lands vested in the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Eviction of persons in unauthorized occupation
main_sections.description: Empowers the custodian or forest officer to evict any person in unauthorized occupation of an ecologically fragile land vested in the Government after giving thirty days' notice.

Entitles the owner of land vested in the Government to compensation for improvements, but no compensation for the vesting or extinguishment of rights. The compensation payable and its mode of payment shall be prescribed.

Provides for the constitution of one or more Tribunals by notification in the Gazette for the purpose of the Act. The Tribunal shall be a Judicial Officer not below the rank of a District Judge, and the Government shall define the areas within which each Tribunal shall exercise jurisdiction.

main_sections.section_title: Settlement of disputes by the Tribunal
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for the Tribunal to settle disputes regarding whether any land is an ecologically fragile land or not, or whether it has vested in the Government or not. It also addresses compensation determined under section 8.

Provides for appeals against decisions of the Tribunal to the High Court within a period of sixty days. The High Court may admit an appeal if satisfied about sufficient cause. The appeal shall be in the prescribed form and verified by a fee of five hundred rupees. The High Court may confirm, cancel, or remand the decision, or pass orders as it may think fit.

Grants the Tribunal powers to exercise any power conferred by or under this Act, including summoning witnesses, requiring discovery of documents, receiving evidence on affidavit, issuing commissions, inspecting property, and requisitioning public records.

main_sections.section_title: Bar of jurisdiction of Civil Court
main_sections.description: Excludes Civil Courts from jurisdiction to deal with any question or to determine any matter which is by or under this Act, required to be decided or dealt with by the Tribunal, the custodian or any other officer.

States that no suit, prosecution or legal proceedings shall lie against the Government or the Tribunal or the custodian or any other officer for anything done in good faith or ordered to be done under this Act or any rule or order made thereunder.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution and functions of the Advisory Committee
main_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of an Advisory Committee by the Government to advise on identifying lands which are ecologically fragile and recommending them to the Government. The Committee shall consist of the Principal Chief Conservator of Forests and two Members of the Legislative Assembly nominated by the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Ecologically fragile lands to be managed by Forest Department as per Management Plans
main_sections.description: Deals with the management of ecologically fragile lands by the Forest Department according to Management Plans.
Grants the Government the power to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Deals with validation and transitory provisions related to the Act.

important_rules: Lands declared ecologically fragile are vested in the Government.
Owners of vested lands are eligible for compensation for improvements.
Eviction of unauthorized occupants is permitted after notice.
Management of ecologically fragile lands is to be done by the Forest Department as per Management Plans.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Custodian and Forest Department
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through eviction of unauthorized occupants, management of lands, and resolution of disputes by the Tribunal.

rights: Owners of vested lands are eligible for compensation for improvements.
duties: Owners shall not change the legal status or ownership of land proposed to be declared ecologically fragile.
The custodian shall demarcate boundaries of ecologically fragile lands.
The Forest Department shall manage ecologically fragile lands as per Management Plans.

key_procedures: Declaration of ecologically fragile land by the Government after notification and hearing the owner.
Vesting of ecologically fragile lands in the Government.
Demarcation of boundaries of vested lands.
Eviction of unauthorized occupants.
Settlement of disputes by the Tribunal.
Appeal against Tribunal decisions to the High Court.
administration: Forest Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act aims to maintain ecological balance and conserve bio-diversity.
Ecologically fragile lands are deemed to be reserved forests.
Civil Court jurisdiction is barred for matters covered by the Tribunal.
The Act includes provisions for indemnity for actions taken in good faith.

title: THE KERALA FOREST (VESTING AND MANAGEMENT OF ECOLOGICALLY FRAGILE LANDS) AMENDMENT ACT, 2009
purpose: To amend the Kerala Forest (Vesting and Management of Ecologically Fragile Lands) Act, 2003 for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to lands in Kerala, specifically concerning ecologically fragile lands as defined or managed under the Principal Act.

main_sections.description: Names the act as the Kerala Forest (Vesting and Management of Ecologically Fragile Lands) Amendment Act, 2009 and states that it shall come into force on the 20th day of August, 2009.

Amends the Kerala Forest (Vesting and Management of Ecologically Fragile Lands) Act, 2003 by inserting two new sections. Section 10A deals with Dispute Redressal in respect of lands having an extent of not more than two hectares. Section 10B outlines the Constitution of the Ecologically Fragile Land Claim Dispute Redressal Committee.

Repeals the Kerala Forest (Vesting and Management of Ecologically Fragile Lands) Amendment Ordinance, 2009. States that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Lands with an extent of not more than two hectares are subject to specific dispute redressal procedures. (Section 10A(1))

If any owner of land notified under section 3 has an extent of not more than two hectares and has any dispute as to whether such land is an ecologically fragile land or not, they may file an application before the Principal Chief Conservator of Forests for settlement of such dispute. (Section 10A(1))
The Principal Chief Conservator of Forests shall refer the dispute to the Ecologically Fragile Land Claim Dispute Redressal Committee constituted under section 10B. (Section 10A(2))

The Ecologically Fragile Land Claim Dispute Redressal Committee shall consist of members from various departments and institutions, including Local Divisional Forest Officer/Wildlife Warden, Working Plan Officer, representatives from Research Institutes, Member of Legislative Assembly, President of the Village Panchayat, Agriculture Officer, and Revenue Officer. (Section 10B(2))
The Committee shall hear the dispute in the manner and for preferring an application under sub-section (1) shall be such as may be prescribed. (Section 10A(5) & 10B(3))

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Principal Chief Conservator of Forests, Ecologically Fragile Land Claim Dispute Redressal Committee.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Dispute resolution through application to the Principal Chief Conservator of Forests and referral to the Committee. The Committee will detail a report to the Principal Chief Conservator of Forests. Proceedings may be suspended by the Tribunal. (Sections 10A(1-7))

rights: Right to seek dispute redressal for lands not exceeding two hectares, if disputed as ecologically fragile. (Section 10A(1))
Right to have disputes heard by the Ecologically Fragile Land Claim Dispute Redressal Committee. (Section 10A(2))
obligations: Landowners with disputed ecologically fragile lands not exceeding two hectares must file an application for settlement. (Section 10A(1))
The Principal Chief Conservator of Forests has a duty to refer disputes to the Committee and forward detailed reports with recommendations. (Section 10A(2), 10A(3))
The Committee has a duty to investigate, detail a report, and forward it with recommendations to the Government. (Section 10A(3))

key_procedures: Dispute Resolution for small landholdings: 1. File an application to the Principal Chief Conservator of Forests if land (<= 2 hectares) is disputed as ecologically fragile. 2. The Principal Chief Conservator of Forests refers the dispute to the Ecologically Fragile Land Claim Dispute Redressal Committee. 3. The Committee inspects the land, details a report, and forwards it with recommendations to the Government. 4. The Government makes a decision. 5. If the decision is to continue proceedings, they will be done within such time as prescribed. 6. If the land is determined to be ecologically fragile, possession may be returned to the Government and proceedings suspended by the Tribunal. 7. No application for settlement of dispute shall be filed after expiry of six months from the publication date of this Act. (Section 10A)

Constitution of the Committee: The Committee is constituted by the Government by notification, with specific members from forest, planning, research, legislative, local governance, agriculture, and revenue sectors. (Section 10B)
administration: The Act is administered by the Forest Department, Kerala, with the Principal Chief Conservator of Forests playing a key role in dispute resolution.
important_notes: The amendment ordinance of 2009 is repealed and saved by this Act. (Section 3(1))
Any action taken under the repealed Ordinance is considered valid under the amended Act. (Section 3(2))
The Act came into force on August 20, 2009. (Section 1(2))
Dispute applications must be filed within six months of the Act's publication. (Section 10A(7))

title: The Kerala Forest (Vesting and Management of Ecologically Fragile Lands) Act, 2003
purpose: To provide for the vesting in the Government of ecologically fragile lands in the State of Kerala and for the management of such lands with a view to maintaining ecological balance and conserving the bio-diversity.
scope: The Act applies to ecologically fragile lands in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.custodian: Means the Principal Chief Conservator of Forests of the State or any other officer not below the rank of a Conservator of Forests appointed by the Government, by notification in the Gazette, to exercise the powers and perform the functions of the custodian under this Act.
key_definitions.ecologically fragile lands: means (i) any forest land or any portion thereof held by any person and lying contiguous to or enclosed in a reserved forest or a vested forest or any other forest land owned by the Government and predominantly supporting natural vegetation; and (ii) any land declared to be an ecologically fragile land by the Government by notification in the Gazette under section 4.
key_definitions.forest: means any land principally covered with grown trees and undergrowth and includes any forest statutorily recognised and declared as reserved forest, protected forest or otherwise, but does not include any land which is used primarily for the cultivation of crops or for duration of long duration such as tea, coffee, rubber, cardamom, coconut, arecanut, cashew, or any other sites of residential buildings and surroundings essential for the convenient use of such buildings;
key_definitions.land: includes rivers, streams and its origin and other water bodies;
key_definitions.natural vegetation: means a growing stock predominantly of a plant species or of a number of plant species occurring naturally on the land;
key_definitions.owner: in relation to an ecologically fragile land includes a mortgagee, lessee or any other person having the right of possession and enjoyment of the ecologically fragile land;
key_definitions.prescribed: means prescribed by rules made under this Act;
key_definitions.reserved forests: means the forests reserved under section 19 of the Kerala Forest Act, 1961 (4 of 1962) and includes forests notified under section 4 of the said Act;
key_definitions.tribunal: means a tribunal constituted under section 9 of this Act;
key_definitions.vested forests: means any forest vested in Government under section 3 of the Kerala Private Forests (Vesting and Assignment) Act, 1971 (26 of 1971).

main_sections.description: States that the Act can be called The Kerala Forest (Vesting and Management of Ecologically Fragile Lands) Act, 2003 and it came into force on the 2nd day of June, 2000.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'custodian', 'ecologically fragile lands', 'forest', 'land', 'natural vegetation', 'owner', 'prescribed', 'reserved forests', 'tribunal', and 'vested forests'.

main_sections.section_title: Ecologically fragile lands to vest in Government
main_sections.description: States that notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, or in any judgment, decree or order of any court or tribunal or in any contract, contract or other documents, with effect from the date of commencement of this Act, the ownership and possession of all ecologically fragile lands shall be held by any person or any other form of right on them shall stand transferred to and vested in the Government free from all encumbrances and the right, title and interest of the owner or any other person thereon shall stand extinguished from the said date.

main_sections.section_title: Power to declare ecologically fragile land
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to declare any land to be an ecologically fragile land by notification in the Gazette, after an accommodation of the Advisory Committee appointed for the purpose under section 15 of this Act. It also specifies that no declaration can be made without giving the owner a thirty-day notice. Additionally, no person shall change the legal status or ownership of land proposed to be declared as ecologically fragile after the notice is issued. Any land declared ecologically fragile is subject to the provisions of section 3, meaning its ownership and possession vest in the Government, free from encumbrances.

main_sections.section_title: Ecologically fragile lands to be deemed to be reserved forests
main_sections.description: States that all ecologically fragile lands vested in the Government under section 3 and section 4 shall be deemed to be reserved forests constituted under the Kerala Forest Act, 1961 (4 of 1962), and the provisions of that Act shall as far as may be, apply to such lands.

Requires the custodian to demarcate the boundaries of ecologically fragile lands under section 3 or section 4 within such time as may be prescribed, after the commencement of the Act or the notification under sub-section (1) of section 4, as the case may be.

main_sections.section_title: Eviction of persons in unauthorised occupation
main_sections.description: Empowers the custodian or an officer not below the rank of Divisional Forest Officer to evict any person in unauthorised occupation of any ecologically fragile land vested in the Government under section 3 or section 4, after giving such person thirty days notice. It also specifies that any thing contained in any other law shall not prevent the custodian or officer from taking necessary steps to evict such persons or to remove them from the land.

Specifies that in respect of land vested in the Government under sub-section (1) of section 4, the owner shall be eligible for compensation for the said land, including the permanent improvements thereon. However, no compensation shall be payable for the vesting of any ecologically fragile land or for its extinguishment. The compensation payable shall be determined in such manner as may be prescribed.

Provides for the Government to constitute one or more Tribunals, by notification in the Gazette, for the purpose of this Act. The Tribunal shall be a judicial Officer not below the rank of a District Judge. The Tribunal shall decide all matters within its competence and may review any of its decisions. The Tribunal, in exercising its powers, shall follow such procedure as may be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Settlement of disputes by the Tribunal
main_sections.description: Deals with the settlement of disputes by the Tribunal, including disputes arising from claims of ownership of ecologically fragile land or portions thereof that have vested in the Government. It outlines the process for compensation determination and appeals to the High Court.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Custodian or officers authorized by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Eviction of persons in unauthorized occupation, demarcation of boundaries, and settlement of disputes through a Tribunal.

rights: Right to compensation for land vested in the Government under section 4 (for owners).
duties: Duty of the custodian to demarcate boundaries of ecologically fragile lands.
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act regarding vesting and management of ecologically fragile lands.

key_procedures: Declaration of ecologically fragile land: Government notifies in the Gazette after consulting the Advisory Committee.
Eviction process: Custodian or authorized officer gives 30 days' notice to occupants.
Compensation determination: As prescribed by rules.
Dispute settlement: Through the constituted Tribunal, with appeal to the High Court.
administration: Forest Department (inferred from the mention of Conservator of Forests and Forest Department as managing ecologically fragile lands).
important_notes: The Act came into force on June 2, 2000, but is enacted as Act 21 of 2005.
Ecologically fragile lands declared under this Act are deemed to be reserved forests under the Kerala Forest Act, 1961.
A dispute redressal mechanism through a Tribunal and appeals to the High Court is established.

title: The Kerala Forest Produce (Fixation of Selling Price) Amendment Act, 1989
purpose: To amend The Kerala Forest Produce (Fixation of Selling Price) Act, 1977.
scope: Applies to the fixation of selling prices for forest produce in Kerala.

main_sections.description: This section likely provides the short title of the act and its commencement date. It refers to the amendment of the Kerala Forest Produce (Fixation of Selling Price) Act, 1977.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 2 of Act 22 of 1977
main_sections.description: This section introduces amendments to Section 2 of the Principal Act (Act 22 of 1977). It seems to modify definitions or add new ones relevant to the act. Specifically, it mentions amendment of "clause (1)" of section 2 and insertion of "clause (2A)" in relation to "timber". It also amends the "Explanation" to section 2.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 5 of Act 22 of 1977
main_sections.description: This section amends Section 5 of the Principal Act (Act 22 of 1977). It appears to relate to the powers of the Government or authorities regarding the fixation of selling prices or related matters. It specifically mentions "sub-section (1)" of section 5 and the insertion of "sub-section (1A)".

important_rules: Rule 1: The act amends the Kerala Forest Produce (Fixation of Selling Price) Act, 1977.
Rule 2: It modifies the definitions and provisions related to the fixation of selling prices for forest produce.
Rule 3: Specific amendments are made to sections 2 and 5 of the Principal Act.

penalties: The scanned document doesn't explicitly detail penalties for violations of this amendment act. Penalties would likely be found in the principal Act of 1977 or subsequent amendments.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Likely the Forest Department or designated authorities under the Kerala Forest Produce (Fixation of Selling Price) Act, 1977.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The document does not specify the methods of enforcement for this amendment.

rights: Right to have selling prices of forest produce fixed in accordance with the provisions of the Act.
duties: Duty to comply with the fixed selling prices for forest produce.
Duty to adhere to the provisions of the amended Act.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: The process for fixing selling prices would be governed by the principal Act and any procedures introduced or modified by this amendment.
Procedure 2: Amendments to section 2 and 5 suggest changes in how definitions are interpreted or how the price fixation process is carried out.
administration: Likely the Forest Department of the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The act is an amendment to the Kerala Forest Produce (Fixation of Selling Price) Act, 1977.
Specific amendments are made to Section 2 and Section 5 of the Principal Act.
The amendment seems to update or clarify definitions and provisions related to price fixation.
Mentions of 'timber' in amendments suggest a focus on this specific forest produce.
References to '1988-ലെ ചട്ടം 24', '1978-ലെ ചട്ടം 29', '1988-ലെ 18', and '1989-ലെ 31-ാം നമ്പർ' indicate that this amendment integrates or supersedes previous regulations and notifications.

title: THE KERALA FOREST PRODUCE (FIXATION OF SELLING PRICE) ACT, 1978
purpose: To provide for the fixation of the selling price of certain important forest produce, for the prohibition of the sale of such forest produce at less than the price so fixed and for matters incidental or ancillary thereto, and to safeguard the forest wealth of the State.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala, concerning the sale of forest produce and its price fixation.

key_definitions.committee: The expert committee constituted under section 4.
key_definitions.forest: Means any reserved forest within the meaning of the Kerala Forest Act, 1961 (4 of 1961) and includes any forest vested in the Government under section 3 of the Kerala Private Forests (Vesting and Assignment) Act, 1971 (26 of 1971).
key_definitions.forest_produce: Means bamboos, reeds, eucalyptus, vateria indica (Vellapine), dipterocarpus species (kalpine), calophyllum species (punna), cedrelatoo (chandana vembu), palaquin elipticum (pali), ailanthus malabaricum (matti), bombox malabaricum (clavu), evodia roxburghiana (kambil), dysoxylum malabaricum (vellakil), adina cordifolia (kadambu), anogeissus latifolia (vekkalec), kydia calycina (tanda), macaranaga peltata (upasthy or vatta), alstonia scholaris (pala) and terminalia bellirica (thanali).
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.selling_price: Means the price of that forest produce fixed by the Government under section 3.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Forest Produce (Fixation of Selling Price) Act, 1978. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force at once.
Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'committee', 'forest', 'forest produce', 'prescribed', 'selling price', and 'State'.

main_sections.section_title: Government to notify selling price of forest produce.
main_sections.description: Requires the Government to notify the selling price of every forest produce for the financial year before its commencement, through publication in the Gazette. Amendments to this price can be made during the financial year after consultation with the expert committee.

Mandates the Government to constitute an expert committee for recommending a fair and reasonable selling price for each forest produce. The committee will consist of members including representatives from agricultural production, forests, government finance, statistics, and forest research, along with a joint secretary from the Government of Forests who will be the Secretary.

main_sections.section_title: Forest produce to be sold at price not less than the selling price.
main_sections.description: Prohibits the sale of forest produce by the Government or any forest officer at a price less than the selling price notified under sub-section (2) of section 3. It also states that the sale of any forest produce in contravention of sub-section (1) shall be null and void and not enforceable in a court of law.

Allows the Government, in public interest, to notify in the Gazette, exemption from the section 5 provisions to any forest produce. This exemption can be for any company owned by the Central Government or the Government of Kerala, or for not exceeding ten cubic meters of any co-operative society registered or deemed to be registered under the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969.

main_sections.section_title: Ten percent of selling price to be utilised for forest development.
main_sections.description: Mandates that ten percent of the amount obtained by the sale of forest produce, after the commencement of this Act, shall be utilized for the development of forests, subject to rules made under this Act.

Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of this Act. These rules may provide for all matters expressly required or allowed to be prescribed, or any other matter that is to be or may be prescribed.

important_rules: Selling price of forest produce must be notified by the Government before the commencement of each financial year and published in the Gazette.
Forest produce cannot be sold by the Government or forest officers at a price less than the notified selling price.
Sale of forest produce in contravention of the above rule is void and unenforceable.
Ten percent of the sale proceeds of forest produce must be utilized for forest development.
Rules made under the Act may provide for all matters required or allowed to be prescribed.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government (implied through the Act's provisions for notification, rule-making, and exemptions).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the notification of selling prices, prohibition of sales below the fixed price, and by making rules and providing exemptions as deemed necessary.

rights: The right of the Government to fix and notify the selling price of forest produce.
The right of the Government to exempt certain forest produce from the provisions of section 5.
The right of the Government to make rules for the effective implementation of the Act.
duties: The duty of the Government to notify the selling price of forest produce.
The duty of the Government to constitute an expert committee for price recommendations.
The duty to utilize ten percent of the selling price for forest development.
obligations: The obligation not to sell forest produce at a price less than the notified selling price.
The obligation to comply with the rules made under the Act.

key_procedures: Government notifies the selling price of forest produce annually through the Gazette.
Government constitutes an expert committee to recommend selling prices.
Government may fix exemptions from the selling price provisions.
Ten percent of sale proceeds are allocated for forest development.
Government makes rules to facilitate the Act's implementation.
administration: The Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act aims to safeguard the forest wealth of the State.
Sales of forest produce in contravention of the price fixation are void.
Exemptions can be granted to specific entities or quantities of forest produce.
A portion of the sale proceeds is mandated for forest development.
The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 19th day of September, 1978 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 606 dated 27th September, 1978.

title: The Kerala Forests Act, 1961
purpose: To provide for the control over forests and lands not at the disposal of Government or in which Government have limited interest, to regulate the management and control of forest lands and waste lands, and to provide for the control over forest produce and other related matters.
scope: The Act applies to forests and lands within the State of Kerala. It covers the control of forests, forest lands, waste lands, forest produce, and the regulation of activities related to these, including grazing, cultivation, timber trade, and the preservation of wild elephants.

key_definitions.forest-produce: Includes timber and fuel-wood, and also includes [among other things] trees, leaves, fruits, seeds, roots, bark, and all other parts or produce of trees, and all other produce of forest land, whether specifically mentioned or not.
key_definitions.timber: Includes wood of any kind, and also includes fuel-wood, charcoal, stumps, logs, planks, beams, rafters, posts, bamboos, and all other forms and derivatives of timber.
key_definitions.forest-land: Includes any land which is the property of Government or which Government may, by notification in the Gazette, declare to be forest land, and all lands on which the Government have any rights or interests.

main_sections.section_title: Power to regulate or prohibit certain acts
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to regulate or prohibit acts such as grazing, cultivation, hunting, shooting, fishing, and the collection of forest produce in reserved forests and other specified lands.

main_sections.section_title: Power to regulate or prohibit the cutting of grass and pasturing of cattle and regulate the payments, if any, to be made for such cutting or pasturing
main_sections.description: Details the Government's authority to regulate or prohibit grass cutting and cattle grazing, including the power to set payments for such activities. It also covers regulations related to protection against storms, winds, stones, floods, and the preservation of soil on ridges and slopes, and the prevention of land erosion.

main_sections.section_title: Power to close land against pasture
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to close land against pasture, with penalties for violations. The section also clarifies that land left open for a period might imply rights for persons to have pasture.
Specifies penalties, including imprisonment and fines, for violations of rules under Section 30, such as pasturing cattle or causing them to trespass in closed land.

main_sections.section_title: Of the control over Forests and Lands not at the disposal of Government or in which Government have limited interest
main_sections.description: Deals with the Government's control over forests and lands not fully at its disposal or where its interest is limited. It outlines the Government's power to regulate or prohibit breaking up land, clearing it, or pasturing cattle.

Describes the procedure for the acquisition of forest land by the Government for public purposes, including compensation and resolution of disputes. It also allows the Government to retain land if the owner is unwilling to sell.

main_sections.section_title: Acquisition of forest or land under the rules
main_sections.description: Further elaborates on the acquisition of forest or land for public purposes, stating that the same principles apply as in Section 34.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of forests at request of owners
main_sections.description: Allows the Government to protect forests at the request of owners, including managing them on behalf of the owner and making rules for their management.

main_sections.section_title: Management of forests, the joint property of Government and other persons
main_sections.description: Addresses the management of forests that are jointly owned by the Government and other persons, allowing for joint management or the Government undertaking management.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make rules to regulate trade and transit of timber and other forest produce
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to make rules to regulate the trade and transit of timber and other forest produce, including prohibitions, inspections, and fees.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for breach of rules made under Section 39
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for violating rules made under Section 39, including imprisonment and fines.

main_sections.section_title: Holder of passes to produce the same for inspection
main_sections.description: Requires holders of passes for timber or forest produce to produce them for inspection.

main_sections.section_title: Collection of drift and stranded timber
main_sections.description: Deals with the collection of drift and stranded timber, including its property rights and how it is to be handled by Forest Officers.

main_sections.section_title: Notice to claimants of drift timber
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for giving notice to claimants of drift timber, including publication in the Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure on claim preferred to fit timber
main_sections.description: Describes the procedure when a claim is preferred for timber, including the process of accepting or rejecting the claim and dealing with the sale proceeds.
Covers the disposal of timber for which no claim is preferred.

main_sections.section_title: Payment to be made by claimant before timber is delivered to him
main_sections.description: Specifies that claimants must make payments before timber is delivered to them.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make rules and prescribe penalties
main_sections.description: Grants the Government power to make rules and prescribe penalties related to salvaging, collection, and registration of timber and other forest produce.

main_sections.section_title: Killing, etc., of wild elephants prohibited
main_sections.description: Prohibits the killing, wounding, or capturing of wild elephants except as provided by the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Punishments for killing, etc., wild elephants without authorization
main_sections.description: Specifies punishments for unauthorized killing or wounding of wild elephants, including imprisonment and fines.

main_sections.section_title: Captured wild elephants and tusks and teeth of elephants killed, the property of Government
main_sections.description: Declares that captured wild elephants and their tusks and teeth are the property of the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Grant of permits for shooting or capturing of wild elephants
main_sections.description: Allows the Government to grant permits for shooting or capturing wild elephants, subject to rules.

main_sections.section_title: Seizure of property liable to confiscation
main_sections.description: Empowers officers to seize property liable to confiscation for offenses under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Powers to seize timber and forest produce
main_sections.description: Grants Forest Officers the power to seize timber and forest produce involved in offenses.
Outlines the procedure to be followed after the seizure of property.
States that timber found in contravention of the Act is liable to confiscation by the Government.

important_rules: No person shall without authorization, hunt, shoot, kill, wound, or capture any wild elephant (Section 48).
Holders of passes for timber or forest produce must produce them for inspection (Section 41).
Timber or forest produce found in contravention of the Act is liable to confiscation (Section 55).
The Government may prescribe penalties for contraventions of rules related to timber and forest produce (Section 40).
The Government may regulate or prohibit the cutting of grass and pasturing of cattle (Section 30).
Land can be closed against pasture by the Government (Section 31).

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or fine which may extend to one hundred rupees, or both (for contravention of certain rules under Section 29).
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or fine which may extend to one hundred rupees, or both (for trespassing cattle into closed lands under Section 32).
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or both (for contravention of rules under Section 47).

Imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or fine which may extend to three thousand rupees, or both (for killing, wounding, or capturing wild elephants without authorization under Section 49).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Forest Officers, Magistrates, Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Seizure of property, imposition of fines, imprisonment, confiscation of timber and forest produce, prosecution of offenders.

rights: Right of persons to have pasture in land left open for a period, if not explicitly prohibited (implied in Section 31).
Right of owners to request protection of their forests (Section 36).
duties: Duty to comply with regulations regarding grazing, cultivation, hunting, and forest produce (various sections).
Duty to produce passes for timber or forest produce for inspection (Section 41).
Duty to comply with rules regarding the transit of timber and forest produce (Section 39).
Duty to not kill, wound, or capture wild elephants without authorization (Section 48).
obligations: Obligation to pay amounts for cattle trespass into closed lands (Section 32).
Obligation to make payments before timber is delivered (Section 46).

key_procedures: Procedure for acquiring forest land for public purposes, involving notification, negotiation, and potential dispute resolution (Section 34).
Procedure for the collection and disposal of drift and stranded timber, including notice to claimants and sale of unclaimed timber (Sections 42, 43, 44, 45).
Procedure for seizure of property liable to confiscation, including reporting to the Magistrate (Section 52, 54).
administration: The Government of Kerala, likely through its Forest Department.
important_notes: The Government may exempt any person or class of persons from the operation of any of the rules (regarding land closure for pasture) (Section 31).
Notifications issued by the Government under this Act can be altered or cancelled by the Government (Section 33, 37, 39).
The Act provides for the protection of wild elephants (Chapter VII).
The Act deals with offenses, penalties, and procedure for their enforcement (Chapter VIII).

title: THE KERALA GAMING (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1973
purpose: To amend the Kerala Gaming Act, 1960, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This section names the Act as the Kerala Gaming (Amendment) Act, 1973, and states it shall come into force at once.

Amends section 8 of the principal Act. The words 'be liable to fine not exceeding two hundred rupees or to imprisonment which may extend to one month or to fine which may extend to five hundred rupees or to both' have been substituted.

A new section 14A, titled 'Exemptions', is inserted. This section allows the Government to exempt from any of the provisions of this Act, with such restrictions and conditions as may be specified, any game where the element of skill is predominantly more significant than the element of chance.
Amends section 15 of the principal Act. In sub-section (2), the words 'Any police officer' are replaced with 'Any police officer not below the rank of a Sub Inspector of Police'.
Amends section 19 of the principal Act. In sub-section (1), the words 'Any police officer' are replaced with 'Any police officer not below the rank of a Sub Inspector of Police'.

important_rules: Any game where the element of skill is predominantly more significant than the element of chance may be exempted by the Government, subject to specified restrictions and conditions.

penalties: Fine not exceeding two hundred rupees or imprisonment which may extend to one month, OR fine which may extend to five hundred rupees or both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Police officers (specifically, those not below the rank of Sub Inspector for certain provisions)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is through the actions of police officers and potential penalties as outlined in the Act.

key_procedures: Insertion of new sections and substitution of existing wording in various sections of the principal Act.
Exemption procedure for certain games by the Government.
administration: Implied to be administered by the relevant authorities in Kerala responsible for gaming laws.
important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 800 dated 22nd August, 1973.
The amendment is effective from the date of publication.

title: The Kerala Gaming (Amendment) Act, 2005
purpose: To amend The Kerala Gaming Act, 1960 for the purposes mentioned in the act.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala. It amends specific sections of The Kerala Gaming Act, 1960.

key_definitions.gaming: Any game of mere skill or chance, or any game which involves the element of chance or skill, or both.
key_definitions.keeper of a common gaming-house: Any person who, on any premises kept or used for gambling, opens, keeps, or uses the same for the purpose of gambling, or permits or manages gambling therein, or assists or knowingly acts or aids in the management or opening or keeping of such premises, or negotiates any insurance or stake therein or who has the immediate care or control of any such premises.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1960.
Amends Section 1 of the principal Act (The Kerala Gaming Act, 1960) by adding a new sub-section (3) to clarify that the Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.
Amends Section 2 of the principal Act by inserting new definitions or modifying existing ones, particularly concerning 'gaming' and 'keeper of a common gaming-house'.

important_rules: Gaming is prohibited in common gaming-houses.
Keeping or using premises as a common gaming-house is an offense.
Assisting in the management of a common gaming-house is an offense.

penalties: For first offense under certain sections: imprisonment which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees or with both.
For subsequent offense under certain sections: imprisonment which may extend to one year and with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Police officers, as empowered by the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Search of suspected premises, arrest of offenders, and prosecution.

rights: Right to be informed of the grounds for arrest.
duties: Duty of keepers of common gaming-houses to allow lawful search.
Duty of police to search suspected premises and seize gambling instruments.
obligations: Obligation to refrain from gaming in common gaming-houses.
Obligation to refrain from keeping or managing common gaming-houses.

key_procedures: Procedure for search of suspected premises by a police officer.
Procedure for arrest of persons found gambling.
Procedure for seizure of gaming instruments.
administration: The Police Department is responsible for the enforcement of this Act.
important_notes: The Act is a retrospective amendment, deemed to have come into force on 1st April 1960.
The Act repeals certain provisions of other acts related to gaming in specific areas of Kerala.
The amendment aims to consolidate and clarify the laws related to gaming in the state.

title: THE KERALA GAMING (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2005
purpose: To amend the Kerala Gaming Act, 1960 for the purposes hereinafter appearing. The preamble highlights the concerns regarding the organization and conduct of games of chances, fortunes, and guesses, particularly on-line lotteries, which are deemed to attract a substantial population and lead to penury and desperation. It also emphasizes the need to protect the social and economic interests of the State and prevent such social evils.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala and amends the Kerala Gaming Act, 1960. It specifically addresses on-line lotteries, paper lotteries, and related activities within the state. The amendments also refer to the Lotteries (Regulation) Act, 1998.

key_definitions.central computer server: Means a server class computer installed at a central location which accepts, processes, stores and validates the on-line lottery transactions and otherwise manages, monitors and controls the entire on-line lottery system.
key_definitions.gaming: Means wagering, betting or gambling, which includes the organizing, conducting, promoting, marketing or selling of on-line lotteries, but does not include paper lotteries organized, conducted or promoted by any State Government or the Central Government.
key_definitions.on-line lottery: Means a system of gambling organized, conducted, promoted, marketed or sold through electronic devices including computers, computer peripherals and other equipments for operating on-line lottery systems, lottery terminals, etc., where the information about the player's choice of any particular number or combination of numbers etc. is simultaneously registered with the central computer server which assigns a unique number to verify the validity.
key_definitions.on-line lottery terminal: Means a terminal connected to the Central Computer Server where on-line lottery tickets are marketed or sold in retail in common gaming houses.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Gaming (Amendment) Act, 2005 and that it shall come into force at once. It also mentions that the Act received the assent of the Governor on 6th day of April, 2005 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 750, dated 8th April, 2005.

Amends Section 2 of the principal Act by inserting new definitions and substituting existing ones, including definitions for 'central computer server', 'gaming', 'on-line lottery', and 'on-line lottery terminal'.
Amends Section 3 of the principal Act by adding words and a proviso related to offences under the Act.
Amends Section 4 of the principal Act by adding a new sub-section concerning whoever commits any offence relating to gambling by means of on-line lotteries.
Amends Section 7 of the principal Act by renumbering existing sub-sections and adding a new sub-section related to gambling by means of on-line lotteries.
Amends Section 8 of the principal Act by renumbering existing sub-sections and adding a new sub-section concerning offences relating to gambling by means of on-line lotteries.
Amends Section 9 of the principal Act by renumbering existing sub-sections and adding a new sub-section regarding offences relating to gambling by means of on-line lotteries.

Inserts a new section 9A, titled 'Penalty for attempt to open a common gaming house for gaming in on-line lottery', which penalizes whoever attempts or assists to open such a house or makes any preparation for the same.

Amends Section 10 of the principal Act by inserting a proviso stating that all instruments of gaming relating to on-line lottery shall be sold and converted into money as per the order of the Magistrate.

Inserts a new section 10A, titled 'Interim custody of articles seized relating to on-line lottery', which deals with the release of seized instruments of gaming by the Magistrate upon furnishing security.
Amends Section 19 of the principal Act by inserting a proviso regarding the cognizability and bailability of offences relating to gambling in on-line lottery.

Inserts a new section 19A, titled 'Offences to be tried summarily', stating that all offences under this Act shall be tried summarily by the Judicial Magistrate of the First Class specially empowered by the Government, with reference to specific sections of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

important_rules: Whoever commits any offence relating to gambling by means of on-line lotteries shall be liable on conviction to a fine of rupees ten thousand or with imprisonment which may extend to three years or with both.

Whoever commits any offence relating to gambling by means of on-line lotteries shall be liable on conviction to a fine of rupees twenty thousand or with imprisonment which may extend to one year or with both.

Whoever commits any offence relating to gambling by means of on-line lotteries shall be liable on conviction to a fine of rupees twenty thousand or with imprisonment which may extend to two years or with both.

Whoever commits any offence relating to gambling by means of on-line lotteries shall be liable on conviction to a fine of rupees ten thousand or with imprisonment which may extend to one year or with both.
All instruments of gaming relating to on-line lottery shall be sold and converted into money as per the order of the Magistrate.
Offences relating to gambling in on-line lottery shall not only be cognizable but also non-bailable.

penalties: Fine of rupees ten thousand or imprisonment up to three years or both for offences relating to gambling by means of on-line lotteries.
Fine of rupees twenty thousand or imprisonment up to one year or both for offences relating to gambling by means of on-line lotteries.
Fine of rupees twenty thousand or imprisonment up to two years or both for offences relating to gambling by means of on-line lotteries.
Fine of rupees ten thousand or imprisonment up to one year or both for attempting to open a common gaming house for gaming in on-line lottery.
All instruments of gaming relating to on-line lottery shall be sold and converted into money.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Judicial Magistrate of the First Class specially empowered by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Offences are to be tried summarily by the Judicial Magistrate of the First Class. Seized instruments of gaming relating to on-line lottery can be released by the Magistrate upon furnishing security. Offences are cognizable and non-bailable.

rights: Right to have interim custody of seized articles relating to on-line lottery released by the Magistrate upon furnishing security.
obligations: Obligation not to organize, conduct, promote, market or sell on-line lotteries or to attempt to open a common gaming house for such purpose.
Obligation to comply with provisions related to the seizure and interim custody of gaming instruments.

key_procedures: Summary trial of offences under the Act by the Judicial Magistrate of the First Class.
Procedure for interim custody and release of seized articles relating to on-line lottery by the Magistrate upon furnishing security.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be handled by the State Government and its judicial machinery.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on 6th day of April, 2005 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 750, dated 8th April, 2005.
The amendments are in relation to 'on-line lotteries' and 'paper lotteries'.
Offences under this Act are to be tried summarily by the Judicial Magistrate of the First Class.
Offences relating to gambling in on-line lottery are cognizable and non-bailable.

title: The Kerala Gaming Act, 1960
purpose: To make better provision for the punishment of gaming and the keeping of common gaming houses in the State of Kerala.
scope: This Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and applies to gaming and keeping of common gaming houses.

key_definitions.common gaming house: Any house, room, tent, enclosure, vehicle, vessel or any place whatsoever in which cards, dice, tables or other instruments of gaming are kept or used for the profit or gain of the person owning, occupying, using or keeping such place. It also includes any place opened, kept or used or permitted to be opened, kept or used for the purpose of gaming.
key_definitions.gaming: Does not include a lottery but includes wagering or betting. This comprises the collection or soliciting of bets, the receipt or distribution of winnings or prizes, in money or otherwise, in respect of any wager or bet, or any act which is intended to aid or facilitate wagering or betting.
key_definitions.instruments of gaming: Includes any article used or intended to be used as a subject or means of, or for the purpose of carrying on or facilitating or in connection with gaming. It also includes books, lists, tickets, forms or other documents used or intended to be used as a register or recorded or evidence of gaming, and any winnings or prizes in money or otherwise, distributed or intended to be distributed in respect of any gaming.
