main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (whole of Kerala), and that it comes into force at once.
Provides definitions for 'common gaming house', 'gaming', and 'instruments of gaming'.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for opening, etc., any enclosure, etc., for certain forms of gaming
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for opening, keeping, using, permitting to be used, or assisting in the business of gaming in specified places for specific types of gaming, including horse-races, commodity/stock prices, motor vehicle registration numbers, and chance-dependent wagering/betting schemes.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for being found in a gaming house
main_sections.description: Penalizes persons found gaming or present for the purpose of gaming in a place referred to in Section 3. It also establishes a presumption that a person found in such a place during gaming was there for that purpose.
Empowers a Magistrate or Police Officer (not below Sub-Inspector) to enter, search, and seize instruments of gaming and persons found in suspected common gaming houses.

main_sections.section_title: Cards, dice, etc., found in search under Section 5 to be evidence that the place is a common gaming house
main_sections.description: States that instruments of gaming found during a search are evidence that the place is a common gaming house and that persons found there were present for gaming, even if no play was actually witnessed.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for opening, etc., a common gaming house
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for opening, keeping, using, permitting to be used, conducting, assisting in conducting, or advancing money for gaming in a common gaming house.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for being found gaming in a common gaming house
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for persons found gaming or present for the purpose of gaming in a common gaming house. It also establishes a presumption that persons found therein during gaming were there for that purpose.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for refusing to give name and address and for giving false name and address
main_sections.description: Penalizes persons found in a common gaming house who refuse to give their name and address or give a false one.

main_sections.section_title: Instruments of gaming may be ordered to be destroyed on conviction
main_sections.description: Allows the convicting Magistrate to order destruction of instruments of gaming, forfeiture of moneys and securities seized, or their return to rightful owners.

main_sections.section_title: Proof of playing for stakes unnecessary
main_sections.description: Clarifies that it is not necessary to prove that persons were playing for money, wager, bet, or stake to convict for keeping or managing a common gaming house.

main_sections.section_title: Magistrate may require any person apprehended to be sworn and give evidence
main_sections.description: Empowers Magistrates to require persons found in entered premises to give evidence on oath regarding unlawful gaming or obstruction of entry, without being excused on the ground of self-incrimination.
Indemnifies witnesses who make a true and faithful discovery of all things concerning gaming from prosecutions under the Act for prior offenses.

main_sections.section_title: Act not to apply to certain games
main_sections.description: Exempts games of mere skill from the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the Government to exempt certain games from the Act if the element of skill is predominant over chance, through notification.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for gaming and setting birds and animals to fight in public places
main_sections.description: Penalizes gaming with instruments in public places and setting birds/animals to fight in public places, or aiding/abetting such fights.
Specifies who can try the offences under this Act (details not fully provided in excerpt).
Prescribes penalties for repeat offenders (details not fully provided in excerpt).

main_sections.section_title: Payment of portion of fine to informer
main_sections.description: Allows for payment of a portion of the fine to informers.

main_sections.section_title: Police may arrest without warrant on view of offence
main_sections.description: Authorizes police officers to arrest without a warrant upon witnessing an offence under the Act.
Indicates that this section deals with the repeal of any previous enactments (details not fully provided in excerpt).

important_rules: Any place where instruments of gaming are kept or used for the profit of the keeper is considered a common gaming house.
Wagering or betting is considered gaming, but lotteries are not.
Instruments of gaming found in a searched place are considered evidence of it being a common gaming house.
Persons found in a common gaming house during gaming are presumed to be there for the purpose of gaming.
It is not necessary to prove that people were playing for stakes to secure a conviction related to common gaming houses.
Games of mere skill are exempt from the provisions of this Act.

penalties: Imprisonment up to one year or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both, for opening, keeping, or using places for certain forms of gaming (Section 3). Minimum punishment prescribed in absence of special reasons.
Imprisonment up to one month or fine up to five hundred rupees, or both, for being found in a gaming house for the purpose of gaming (Section 4).
Fine not exceeding five hundred rupees, or imprisonment not exceeding three months, or both, for opening, keeping, or conducting a common gaming house (Section 7).
Imprisonment up to one month or fine up to five hundred rupees, or both, for being found gaming in a common gaming house (Section 8).
Penalty not exceeding five hundred rupees and costs, or imprisonment not exceeding one month for refusing to give name/address or giving a false one (Section 9).
Imprisonment not exceeding one month or fine not exceeding two hundred rupees, or both, for gaming in public places or setting birds/animals to fight in public places (Section 15).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Magistrates and Police Officers (not below the rank of Sub-Inspector for search powers).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Entry and search powers for police and magistrates, arrest without warrant for offenses viewed by police, requirement for apprehended persons to give evidence.

rights: Right to be indemnified from prosecution if examined as a witness and make a true discovery of gaming activities (Section 13).
Right to have instruments of gaming, seized money, or articles returned if deemed entitled by the Magistrate (Section 10).
duties: Duty to provide correct name and address when required by an officer or Magistrate (Section 9).
Duty to give evidence on oath when required by a Magistrate regarding unlawful gaming, even if it tends to criminate oneself (Section 12).
obligations: Obligation not to open, keep, use, or permit to be used any common gaming house.
Obligation not to participate in or facilitate gaming in prohibited places or for prohibited activities.
Obligation not to engage in gaming or setting birds/animals to fight in public places.

key_procedures: Upon credible information, a Magistrate or Police Officer (not below SI) can record reasons, enter any suspected common gaming house by force if necessary, arrest persons found therein, seize instruments of gaming, money, and articles, and search all parts of the place and persons in custody (Section 5).

If a person is found in a common gaming house and is required by an officer or Magistrate to give their name and address, they must comply. Refusal or false information can lead to penalties (Section 9).

A Magistrate can require a person apprehended to be sworn and give evidence about unlawful gaming or obstruction. Refusal to be sworn or answer questions can lead to charges under the Indian Penal Code (Section 12).
Witnesses who make a true discovery of gaming activities can receive a certificate of indemnity from the Magistrate (Section 13).
administration: The Act is administered by the State Government and its agencies, including Magistrates and the Police Department.
important_notes: The Act specifically lists several types of gaming that are penalized, including those related to horse-races, commodity/stock market prices, and specific types of wagering/betting.
The Act provides a presumption of guilt for persons found in gaming houses.
The definition of gaming explicitly includes wagering and betting but excludes lotteries.
Games of mere skill are explicitly exempted from the Act.
The Government has the power to exempt certain games if skill is predominant over chance.

title: THE KERALA GENERAL SALES TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1995 (ACT 11 OF 1995)
purpose: To amend the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963 for purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: The act applies to the State of Kerala and deals with the taxation of turnover of dealers in respect of transfer of property involved in the execution of works contracts.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 1995. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1984.

Amends Section 2 of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963 by inserting a new clause regarding the purpose of the Act, transfer of property in goods, and the definition of works contract. It also adds a proviso to clause (xxv) concerning the taxable turnover of a dealer in respect of transfer of property involved in the execution of works contract, and a new note to Explanation IA concerning the substitution of a sub-clause.

Inserts a new section 5C into the principal Act, titled 'Deduction of certain amounts in arriving at the taxable turnover of a dealer in respect of transfer of property in the execution of works contract.' This section specifies amounts that are not to be deducted and provides conditions for deductions, including proof of sub-contractor's tax payment and specific charges like labour, planning, designing, and consumables.

Validates any judgment, decree, order, assessment, levy, or collection of any tax on the turnover of a dealer in respect of property transfer in works contracts made or purporting to have been made between May 1, 1993, and December 31, 1991, or ending March 31, 1991. It also specifies that no suit or proceedings shall be maintained for refund of tax collected under these circumstances, and no court shall enforce any decree for refund. Furthermore, it validates tax assessed under the principal Act before May 18, 1995, if not collected before that date.

Repeals The Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 1995. It also states that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

key_procedures: Procedure for calculating taxable turnover in works contracts by allowing deductions for specific expenses, provided certain conditions are met (e.g., proof of sub-contractor tax payment).
Procedure for validation of past tax assessments, levies, and collections related to works contracts, even if made under specific circumstances or dated periods.
important_notes: The amendment regarding works contracts is deemed to have come into force from April 1, 1984.
Received the assent of the Governor on 5th day of August 1995 and published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 790, dated 5th August 1995.
The validation section covers acts done or purporting to have been done between May 1, 1993 and March 31, 1991.

title: THE KERALA GENERAL SALES TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1986
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 1986, and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1984.

Amends section 39 of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963. It includes a sub-section (3) stating that notwithstanding anything contained in the Act, where the point of levy of tax in respect of any goods is changed from the point of first sale to the point of first purchase in the State, the value of such goods held in stock by any person on the date of such change of the point of levy of tax and for which tax at the point of first sale in the State has not been levied, shall be deemed to be the taxable turnover in respect of such goods at the point of first purchase under this Act.

States that the Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 1986 is hereby repealed, and notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 28th day of November, 1986 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No 1068 dated 29th November, 1986.

title: THE KERALA GENERAL SALES TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1999
purpose: To amend the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, for purposes stated within the act.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and its laws concerning general sales tax.

main_sections.description: This section likely provides the short title of the act and specifies when it comes into force. It mentions "The Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 1999" and refers to the "Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963".

This section deals with the amendment of Section 2 of the Principal Act (The Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963). It introduces new sub-sections and clauses, specifically relating to 'dealer' and 'taxable turnover'.

This section concerns the amendment of Section 17 of the Principal Act. It clarifies provisions related to appeals, particularly concerning the time limits and procedures for filing appeals to higher authorities.

This section involves the amendment of Section 21 of the Principal Act. It seems to address the revision of orders, potentially by the Commissioner or other designated authorities, and the conditions under which such revisions can be made.

key_procedures: Filing appeals to appellate authorities with specified time limits and conditions.
Revision of orders by the Commissioner or designated authorities under defined circumstances.
administration: Likely administered by the Commercial Taxes Department of the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The amendment specifically refers to the "Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963" as the Principal Act.
New definitions and clarifications are introduced, particularly regarding 'dealer' and 'taxable turnover'.

title: THE KERALA GENERAL SALES TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2002
purpose: To further amend the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and concerns amendments to the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.

key_definitions.Oil Company: Means the Cochin Refineries Ltd., Indian Oil Corporation Ltd., Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd., Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd., Indo-Burma Petroleum Company Ltd., and includes such other company as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette specify in this behalf.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 2002. It also specifies that certain clauses (a), (b), (c) and (c) of section 3 and section 4 of this Act shall be deemed to have come into force on the 31st day of December, 2001 and section 2, clause (d) of section 3 and section 5 of this Act shall be deemed to have come into force on the 3rd day of April, 2002.
Amends section 5D in the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963 (15 of 1963) by substituting figures and words in the First Schedule.

Amends the First Schedule to the principal Act by inserting new serial numbers and entries, specifically for 'Cutlery' and 'Computer Software', and also for various petroleum products and lubricating oils, specifying their tax liability under section 5.
Amends the Third Schedule to the principal Act by substituting serial number 12A and the entry against it.
Amends the Fifth Schedule to the Principal Act by substituting serial number 12 and the entries against it, and the Explanation thereunder shall be omitted.

Repeals (1) The Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2002 (2 of 2002) and the Kerala General Sales Tax (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 2002 (4 of 2002). It also states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the Principal Act as amended by the said Ordinances shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the Principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_notes: The amendments regarding the commencement of certain sections are effective retrospectively from December 31, 2001 and April 3, 2002.

The amendments to the First Schedule include changes to tax liability under section 5 for specific goods like Cutlery, Computer Software, various petroleum products (including High Speed Diesel Oil, Kerosene, Motor spirit, Naphtha, Other Petroleum Products, Aviation Turbine Fuel, Liquified Petroleum Gas), and lubricating oils.
The amendments to the First Schedule also include entries for 'Stainless steel sheets not falling under the Second Schedule' and 'Articles of stainless steel not falling under the Second Schedule'.

title: THE KERALA GENERAL SALES TAX (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 2003
purpose: Further to amend the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963 for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963. Amendments relate to 'notified goods', 'smuggling', and procedures for confiscation and release of goods and vehicles.

key_definitions.notified goods: means coffee, rubber, cardamom, ginger, pepper, arecanut, cashew nut, iron and steel and any other goods notified by the Government.
key_definitions.smuggling: means transportation of goods without proper documents as specified in sub-section (1) of section 30E of the Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala General Sales Tax (Second Amendment) Act, 2003. It also specifies the dates from which various sections and provisions of this Act shall be deemed to have come into force.
Inserts new clauses (xVB) and (xxiiB) into section 2 of the principal Act, defining 'notified goods' and 'smuggling' respectively.

Inserts new sub-section (7C) into section 7 of the principal Act, detailing the requirements for a certificate to be obtained by an awarder from the contractor or assessee liable to tax under clause (iv) of sub-section (1) of section 5 and opted for payment of tax under sub-section (7) or (7A) of section 7. It also specifies the procedure for assessing authority and the consequence of non-compliance.
Amends section 22 of the principal Act by inserting the words "pay over the same" before the word "Government" in sub-section (1).

Inserts new sections 30E and 30F. Section 30E deals with the confiscation of notified goods, vehicles or vessels involved in smuggling and the procedure for seizure and detention. Section 30F outlines the procedure as to perishable goods seized under section 30E.

Amends section 31 of the principal Act by inserting a new clause (iii) in sub-section (1) regarding persons who undertake to transport or deliver any consignment of notified goods in any vehicle or vessel or any other conveyance exceeding a specified value, and the requirement of a permit obtained from the authority.

Repeals the Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2003 (4 of 2003). It also states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Confiscation of notified goods and vehicles involved in smuggling requires the owner or person in charge of the vehicle/vessel to carry with him, in addition to documents prescribed, a permit obtained from the prescribed authority.

If the authorised officer has reason to suspect that notified goods are being transported in contravention of sub-section (1) of section 30E, they may, without any unreasonable delay, produce the goods and the vehicle before the Assessing Officer.
Notified goods seized under sub-section (1) of section 30E are not accompanied by the required documents, they shall be deemed to be smuggled goods for the purposes of the Act.

The authorised officer shall give the person in charge of the notified goods and the vehicle a notice in writing informing them of the reason for seizure and detention and an opportunity of being heard.

Provided that the authorised officer may release the notified goods and the vehicle seized and detained, if the owner or person in charge files an option to pay in lieu of seizure and detention, a penalty equal to thrice the amount of tax due at the rate applicable to the goods.

If the owner or the vehicle or vessel produces the permit prescribed in sub-section (1) and the owner of the notified goods proves the bonafides of the transport of goods within seven days of the seizure and detention, the authorised officer shall release the goods and the vehicle.

No order confiscating any vehicle or vessel shall be made under sub-section (5), if the owner or the person in charge proves to the satisfaction of the authorised officer that the notified goods were carried without his knowledge or connivance.

The authorised officer shall also afford an opportunity to pay a penalty equal to thrice the amount of tax attempted to be evaded by the owner of the goods and rupees one lakh or twice the amount of tax due or an amount of rupees fifty thousand whichever is higher for the release of the vehicle or vessel in lieu of detention.

penalties: Penalty equal to thrice the amount of tax due at the rate applicable to the goods for release of notified goods in lieu of seizure and detention.

Penalty equal to thrice the amount of tax attempted to be evaded by the owner of the goods and rupees one lakh or twice the amount of tax due or an amount of rupees fifty thousand whichever is higher for the release of the vehicle or vessel in lieu of detention.
Penalty for carrying notified goods in contravention of sub-section (1) of section 30E: to be levied as specified in sub-section (4) of section 30E.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Authorised Officer (which may include the Assessing Officer, Inspecting Assistant Commissioner, or any other officer as may be empowered by the Government).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Seizure and detention of notified goods and vehicles; confiscation of goods and vehicles; imposition of penalties. Provisions for appeal against orders of confiscation and revision are also included.

rights: Right to obtain a certificate from the contractor or assessee regarding tax liability.
Right to be heard before seizure and detention of goods and vehicles.
Right to release of goods and vehicles upon payment of penalty in lieu of seizure and detention.
Right to prove bonafides of transport of goods within seven days to secure release of goods and vehicle.
Right to appeal against an order of confiscation.
Right to apply for revision against an order of the Deputy Commissioner.
Right to apply for revision against an order of the Commissioner.
duties: Duty to carry goods with proper documents.
Duty to obtain a permit for transport of notified goods exceeding a specified value.
Duty to comply with requirements of section 30E regarding transport of notified goods.
Duty to produce goods and vehicle before the Assessing Officer if there is suspicion of contravention.
obligations: Obligation to pay tax as per the Act.
Obligation to obtain necessary permits and documents for transporting notified goods.
Obligation to cooperate with authorised officers during inspection and enforcement.

key_procedures: Seizure and detention of notified goods and vehicles: If an authorised officer has reason to suspect contravention of sub-section (1) of section 30E, they shall seize and detain the goods and vehicle. The officer shall give the person in charge a notice and an opportunity of being heard.
Release of goods and vehicles: Goods and vehicles may be released upon payment of penalty in lieu of seizure and detention, or upon proving bonafides of transport within seven days.
Procedure for perishable goods: Perishable goods seized under section 30E may be sold by the authorised officer, with the sale proceeds to be remitted to the Government Treasury.

Appeal against confiscation: Any person aggrieved by an order of confiscation under sub-section (6) of section 30E may, within thirty days from the date of communication of such order, file an appeal to the Deputy Commissioner.

Revision against Deputy Commissioner's order: Any person aggrieved by an order passed by the Deputy Commissioner may, within thirty days from the date of communication of such order, file a revision to the Commissioner.

Revision against Commissioner's order: Any person aggrieved by an order passed by the Commissioner may, within ninety days from the date of communication of such order, file a revision to the Government.
administration: Kerala State Government (through its tax administration departments and officers).
important_notes: The amendments made by this Act are effective retrospectively for certain sections.
The awarder obtaining a certificate from the contractor or assessee is subject to specific conditions regarding tax liability.
The Act clarifies that if a vehicle or vessel is involved in smuggling, and the owner proves lack of knowledge or connivance, no confiscation order shall be made.
The awarder is eligible to get a certificate from the contractor or assessee if the latter has opted for payment of tax under sub-section (7) or (7A) of section 7.
The power to issue a certificate to the awarder is vested with the assessing authority or any other officer empowered by the Government.
The provision for appeal and revision applies to orders made under sub-section (6) of section 30E and orders passed by the Deputy Commissioner and Commissioner.
The award of confiscation under section 30E shall not prevent any punishment to which the person affected thereby is liable under the Act.

title: The Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 2021
purpose: To further amend the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.
scope: This Act amends the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963. It applies to the State of Kerala. Specifically, it amends the Schedule of the Act relating to 'Foreign Liquor' and substitutes certain serial numbers.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 2021' and specifies that it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 16th day of May, 2020.

Amends the SCHEDULE of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963. In the serial number 2, under the heading 'Foreign Liquor', it substitutes existing serial numbers (27, 80, 102, 72, 212, 202) with new ones (37, 115, 112, 82, 247, 237).

Repeals the Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021 (105 of 2021). It also provides a saving clause, stating that anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but implied to be the authorities responsible for administering the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not explicitly detailed in the provided text.

administration: Law (Legislation-A) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on May 16, 2020.
The Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2021 is repealed.

title: THE PROHIBITION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1967
purpose: To further amend the Prohibition Act, 1950.

title: THE KERALA GENERAL SALES TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1968
purpose: To further amend the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala. Specifically deals with the validation of levy and collection of taxes on certain sales made by the Central Government or State Government, or for commission, remuneration or other valuable consideration. It also applies to sales made by the Central Government or a State Government on or after the 1st day of April, 1963 and before the 29th day of November, 1967.

key_definitions.Explanation (1): Used to define the words 'the Central Government or a State Government, a local authority, a company' and to deem them always to have been used.
key_definitions.Explanation (2): Defines what constitutes a dealer for the purposes of the Act, including entities that buy, sell, supply, or distribute goods, directly or otherwise, for cash or for deferred payment, or for commission, remuneration or other valuable consideration.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala General Sales-tax Act, 1963 (15 of 1963).

Amends section 2 of the Kerala General Sales-tax Act, 1963. It makes amendments in clause (viii) and in sub-clause (a), and also includes a new Explanation (1A) regarding the transfer of property in goods by the Central Government or a State Government.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of levy and collection of taxes on certain sales made by Central Government or State Government.
main_sections.description: This section validates the levy and collection of taxes on certain sales made by the Central Government or a State Government on or after April 1, 1963, and before November 29, 1967, provided such sales were not made in the course of business for all purposes.

Repeals the Kerala General Sales Tax (Third Amendment) Ordinance, 1967 (8 of 1967) and provides a saving clause that anything done or action taken under the repealed Ordinance before the commencement of this Act is deemed to have been done or taken under this Act if it commenced on or after November 29, 1967.

key_procedures: The Act amends existing definitions within the Principal Act to clarify the scope of 'dealer' and the application of the Act to sales made by government entities. It also provides for the validation of past tax levies and collections under specific circumstances.
Section 4 outlines the procedure for repealing an ordinance and ensuring continuity of actions taken under it.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be the relevant tax administration authority in Kerala.
important_notes: The Explanations added to section 2 are deemed to have always been inserted.
Sales made by the Central Government or a State Government before November 29, 1967, were validated if not made in the course of business.
Section 4 states that notwithstanding the repeal of the Ordinance, anything done or action taken under the Ordinance before the commencement of this Act is valid if done or taken under this Act.

title: THE KERALA GENERAL SALES TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1972
purpose: To amend the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: This Act applies to transactions covered by the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963. It specifically details procedures for the inspection of goods in transit and related enforcement measures.

key_definitions.goods: Implied to be items subject to sales tax and transport regulations.
key_definitions.officer: An officer empowered by the Government for enforcement purposes.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 1972.
Inserts a new section 29A into the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, detailing procedures for the inspection of goods in transit.
Amends sub-section (1) of section 34 of the principal Act by inserting the word, figures and letter 'section 29A'.

Repeals the Kerala General Sales Tax (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1971 (24 of 1971). It also states that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: The driver or other person in charge of a vehicle or vessel shall stop the vehicle or vessel at any notified area when so required by the officer in charge.
Rule 2: An officer can detain goods and shall be empowered to record statements if there are reasons to believe the tax due is evaded.
Rule 3: If goods are seized, the officer shall issue a receipt specifying the description and quantity of the goods.

Rule 4: Goods seized may be sold by public auction to the highest bidder if they are perishable nature or subject to speedy and natural decay, or when the expenses of keeping them in custody are likely to exceed their value.

penalties: Penalty not exceeding twice the amount of tax attempted to be evaded.
Goods seized shall be liable to be sold for the realisation of the penalty.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Officer empowered by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Inspection of goods in transit, detention of goods, seizure of goods, recording of statements, conducting inquiries, imposing penalties, and selling seized goods.

rights: Right to be heard by the owner of the goods before an inquiry.
Right to receive a receipt for seized goods.
Right to receive notice regarding the seizure of goods.
duties: Duty of the driver or person in charge of a vehicle to stop at a notified area when required.
Duty to produce proper and genuine documents.
Duty to furnish security for the amount of tax likely to be evaded.
obligations: Obligation to pay expenses and incidental charges for keeping seized goods.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: When an officer suspects tax evasion, they can stop a vehicle, inspect documents, and detain goods. They must record statements and allow the owner to present their case.
Procedure 2: If tax evasion is confirmed, a penalty can be imposed. Seized goods can be sold to recover the penalty. If goods are perishable, they can be sold immediately.
Procedure 3: Notice of seizure must be given to the owner of the goods, and the approximate value of the vehicle and goods, along with the provisions of the Act violated, must be indicated.
administration: The Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963 as amended.
important_notes: The Act clarifies that anything done under the Kerala General Sales Tax (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1971, is considered valid under this amended Act.
The Act specifies how seized goods that are perishable should be handled.
The sale proceeds of seized goods are to be remitted to the Government treasury.

title: THE KERALA GENERAL SALES TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1970
purpose: To amend the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.
scope: Applies to dealers in Kerala engaged in business of selling goods, and to the purchase of goods by dealers.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 1970, and that it shall come into force at once, with remaining provisions deemed to come into force on April 1, 1970.

Amends section 5 of the Principal Act by replacing words, brackets, figures and letter 'sub-section (1)' or 'sub-section (2)' with 'sub-section (1) or sub-section (2) of this section or under section 5A'.

Inserts a new section 5A titled 'Levy of purchase tax'. This section states that every dealer who purchases taxable goods from a registered dealer or any other person, and is liable to tax under this Act, must pay purchase tax. It outlines conditions under which purchase tax is payable, including when goods are consumed in manufacture or other goods for sale, disposed of, or despatched outside the State. It also specifies rates for turnover relating to purchase tax.
Amends section 13 of the Principal Act by inserting a clause '(ii-a)' stating that every dealer liable to pay tax under section 5A shall be inserted.
Amends the First Schedule of the Principal Act by substituting figures in column (4) and column (2) against specific Serial Numbers relating to various goods.

Repeals the Kerala General Sales Tax (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1970. It also provides a saving clause stating that anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the repealed Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Dealers are liable to pay purchase tax on taxable goods purchased from registered dealers or other persons, under specified conditions related to consumption, disposal, or despatch.
Rule 2: Purchase tax is payable at the rates mentioned in section 5.
Rule 3: Specific amendments are made to the First Schedule concerning the classification and taxation of various goods.
Rule 4: Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are considered valid under this Act.

Dealers are subject to the amendments made to section 5, section 13, and the First Schedule of the Principal Act.
obligations: Dealers must comply with the levy of purchase tax as outlined in the newly inserted section 5A.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Calculation and payment of purchase tax by dealers as per section 5A.
Procedure 2: Amendments to existing sections and the First Schedule of the Principal Act are now in effect.
administration: The administration of the Act would fall under the purview of the Sales Tax Department of the Kerala Government.
important_notes: The Act came into force immediately, with some provisions retroactively applied from April 1, 1970.
The insertion of section 5A introduces a new levy of purchase tax, significantly impacting dealers.
The amendments to the First Schedule detail specific changes in the taxation of various goods.

title: The Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 1978
purpose: To further amend the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and its jurisdiction.

key_definitions.component part: A 'component part' means an article which forms an identifiable constituent of any finished product, which along with others goes to make up the finished product and which is identifiable visually and is separable by a mechanical process and not by a chemical process, provided the identity of such article is not lost by separation.
key_definitions.person: Includes an individual, a joint family, a company, a firm, an association of persons or a body of individuals, whether incorporated or not, the Central Government or the Government of Kerala or the Government of any other State or Union Territory in India; and a local authority.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 1978, and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1978.

Amends section 2 of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963 (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act) by substituting clauses (viii), (xvi), and (xxvi) and inserting Explanations (1B) and inserting an Explanation after clause (xxvi).
Amends section 3 of the principal Act by inserting sub-sections (3) and (4).
Amends section 5 of the principal Act by substituting the words 'two thousand five hundred rupees' with 'ten thousand rupees'.
Amends section 5A of the principal Act by substituting the words 'two thousand five hundred rupees' with 'ten thousand rupees'.
Amends section 13 of the principal Act by substituting the words 'ten thousand rupees' with 'ten thousand rupees'.
Amends section 14 of the principal Act by inserting a new sub-section (2A) and also amending sub-section (4).

Amends section 17 of the principal Act by substituting clause (4) and inserting new clauses (6) and (8), and clarifying that certain provisions do not apply to evasion or removal of goods from the State.

Inserts a new section 19A titled 'Assessment in cases of price variation' which deals with circumstances under which a dealer receives any amount due to price variations and is required to submit a return.

Amends section 23 of the principal Act by substituting the words 'revising authority' with 'the words "or with n time specified therefor in this Act or in any rule made thereunder" shall be inserted'.
Amends section 25 of the principal Act by substituting certain words and phrases, including in sub-section (1) and sub-section (4).
Amends section 28 of the principal Act by substituting the words 'forty-five days' with the words 'sixty days'.
Inserts a new section 33A titled 'Warehousemen to submit returns' requiring warehousemen to furnish returns in respect of goods deposited in their warehouse.
Amends section 34 of the principal Act by substituting certain words and figures.

Amends section 35 of the principal Act by substituting certain wording and providing for appeals against orders of the Inspecting Assistant Commissioner or any officer or authority subordinate to them.
Amends section 37 of the principal Act by substituting certain wording in sub-sections (1) and (2).
Omits section 45 of the principal Act.
Amends section 45A of the principal Act by substituting certain words and phrases in sub-sections (1) and (3), and providing for a proviso in sub-section (5).
