important_rules: Dealers must register if their turnover exceeds a specified limit.
Returns must be submitted by dealers within a specified period.
Warehousemen must submit returns regarding deposited goods.
Assessment may be made by the assessing authority if returns appear incorrect or incomplete.
Penalties can be imposed for tax evasion or failure to comply with provisions.

penalties: Penalties for evasion of tax for the year for which the return has been submitted.
Penalties for non-compliance with orders or provisions of the Act.
Fine for making false statements or furnishing false returns.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Assessing Authority, Deputy Commissioner, Board of Revenue, Central Government, Government of Kerala, State or Union Territory Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment of tax, imposition of penalties, orders for compliance, inquiries, and appeals.

rights: Right to be given a reasonable opportunity to prove the correctness and completeness of a return before action is taken.
Right to appeal against certain orders.
duties: Duty to submit returns within the specified time.
Duty to pay tax as assessed.
Duty of warehousemen to furnish returns.
Duty to make correct and complete disclosure in returns.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder.

key_procedures: Procedure for assessment of tax in cases of price variation, including submission of returns and inquiry by the assessing authority.
Procedure for amendment of sections of the principal Act, involving substitution of words, phrases, or insertion of new sub-sections.
Procedure for imposing penalties and for reconsideration of such penalties by the Deputy Commissioner.
Procedure for appeals against orders passed by authorities.
administration: Department of Revenue (Kerala)
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 1st day of August, 1978, and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 508 dated 2nd August, 1978.
Provisions regarding turnover thresholds and tax rates are amended.
Specific definitions are provided for 'component part' and 'person'.
The Act clarifies provisions related to the assessment of tax in cases of price variation and evasion of tax.
Certain sections of the principal Act are amended or omitted.

title: The Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 1976
purpose: To further amend the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to registered dealers and non-registered dealers within Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 1976.

Amends section 4 of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, concerning the functions of the Appellate Tribunal and its composition into Benches, including provisions for the Chairman and other members, and how cases are disposed of when there are disagreements or when a member has previously dealt with a case.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 22.
main_sections.description: Substitutes section 22 of the principal Act, dealing with the 'Collection of tax by dealers'. It outlines provisions for registered dealers collecting tax and for non-registered dealers, with specific conditions on tax rates and collection.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 28.
main_sections.description: Substitutes section 28 of the principal Act, concerning 'Power to order production of accounts and powers of entry, inspection, etc.'. It grants powers to officers to require production of accounts, registers, records, or other documents, and to enter and search business premises. It also clarifies the definition of 'place' for search purposes and outlines procedures for seizure and retention of documents.
Amends section 46 of the principal Act. (Details not fully visible in the provided image).

Inserts a new section 46A, titled 'Penalty for illegal collection of tax, etc.'. This section penalizes persons who collect tax illegally. It specifies penalties for contravention of sub-section (2) or sub-section (3) of section 22, with imprisonment and fines.
Amends the First Schedule of the principal Act by inserting new entries for 'Hosiery goods' and 'Liquified petroleum gas' with their respective tax liabilities.
Amends the Second Schedule to the principal Act by substituting specific figures in column (4).

Repeals the Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 1975. It includes a saving clause stating that anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance is deemed to have been done or taken under this Act, provided the principal Act as amended came into force on 30th August, 1975.

important_rules: Registered dealers must collect tax payable by them on the sale of any goods.
Non-registered dealers shall not collect any sum purporting to be by way of tax.
No person other than a registered dealer shall collect any sum by way of, or purporting to be by way of, tax.

Officers below the rank of assessing authority may, at any reasonable time, enter any place of business or vessel or vehicle of any dealer and inspect accounts, registers, records, or other documents.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, and with fine which shall not be less than five thousand rupees but which may extend to twenty-five thousand rupees for illegal collection of tax.
A penalty not exceeding fifty per cent of the value of the goods not accounted for.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Officers not below the rank of assessing authority, and Magistrates of the first class.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By ordering production of accounts, inspection of business premises, search of business premises, seizure of documents, and imposition of penalties.

rights: Right to have a case heard by a Bench consisting of two or more members if the case involves a question of law.
Right to have a case heard by a Bench consisting of the Chairman and two other members, or by a Bench consisting of two or more members other than the Chairman.
Right to seek assistance from a Magistrate for search warrants.
Right for the owner or any other person to open any box or receptacle when being called upon to do so during an inspection or search.
duties: Registered dealers are to collect tax payable by them on the sale of goods.
Dealers are to produce accounts, registers, records, or other documents relating to their business when required.
Dealers are to furnish any other information relating to their business when required.
The owner or any other person in occupation of the premises must open the door or receptacle when called upon to do so during an inspection or search.
obligations: Dealers have an obligation to comply with the requirements of the Act regarding tax collection and record-keeping.

key_procedures: Appellate Tribunal Benches: Cases are heard by Benches, with specific compositions. If the members of a Bench differ in opinion, the point is decided according to the opinion of the majority. If the members are equally divided, the point or points are heard by the Chairman or other members as the Chairman may direct.

Search and Seizure: Officers can enter and search business premises if they have reason to believe a dealer is trying to evade tax. This may involve issuing a search warrant. Seized accounts, registers, records, or other documents can be retained for a specified period, subject to permission from higher authority.
Penalty for Illegal Collection: A Magistrate of the first class can impose penalties for illegal collection of tax. The penalty can include imprisonment and fines.
administration: The Central Government and the Government of Kerala (through designated authorities).
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on 22nd day of March, 1976 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 178, dated 22nd March 1976.
For the purposes of clause (b) of sub-section (2) of section 28, 'place' includes any godown, building, vessel, vehicle, box or receptacle.

Residential accommodation (not being a shop-cum-residence) cannot be entered into or searched except on the authority of a search warrant issued by a Magistrate of the first class having jurisdiction over the area.
Seized documents can be retained for a period of thirty days from the date of seizure, unless the next higher authority requires them for prosecution.
The power to break open any door or receptacle can be exercised only after the owner or any other person in occupation of the premises fails or refuses to open the door on being called upon to do so.
The Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 1975 (6 of 1975) is hereby repealed.

title: The Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 2005
purpose: To amend the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963 and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Kerala and deals with general sales tax.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as The Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 2005, and states that it shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint. It also specifies that the amendments made by this Act shall be in addition to and not in derogation of the provisions of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.

This section details the amendments made to the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963 (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act). It inserts new sub-sections and modifies existing ones. Key amendments include: - Insertion of a new section 4A regarding the charging of purchase tax. - Modification of section 5, relating to tax on sale or purchase of goods. - Amendments to section 18, concerning appeals to the Appellate Tribunal. - Amendments to section 18A, regarding revision by the Commissioner. - Amendments to section 21, concerning the imposition of penalty for offences. - Insertion of new sections 34A and 34B dealing with the power to call for records and power to compound offences respectively. - Amendment to section 63, regarding the power to make rules.

important_rules: Rule 1: Insertion of a new section 4A to the principal Act, which deals with the charging of purchase tax on certain goods.
Rule 2: Amendment to section 5 of the principal Act, to clarify the provisions related to tax on sale or purchase of goods.
Rule 3: Amendments to section 18 and 18A of the principal Act, concerning appeals and revision proceedings.
Rule 4: Insertion of new sections 34A and 34B to the principal Act, granting powers to the Commissioner to call for records and compound offences.
Rule 5: Amendment to section 21 of the principal Act, regarding penalties for offences.
Rule 6: Amendment to section 63 of the principal Act, relating to the power to make rules.

penalties: Penalty for offences under section 21 of the principal Act (as amended by this Act).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Commissioner of Sales Tax and other authorities appointed under the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment, appeals, revisions, and prosecution for offences as prescribed under the principal Act and its amendments.

rights: Right to appeal to the Appellate Tribunal against orders passed by the Deputy Commissioner.
Right to seek revision of orders by the Commissioner.
duties: Duty to pay sales tax and purchase tax as per the provisions of the Act.
Duty to maintain proper records and furnish returns.
Duty to comply with notices and orders issued by the authorities.
obligations: Obligation to pay purchase tax on specified goods.

key_procedures: Procedure for charging purchase tax under the newly inserted section 4A.
Procedure for filing appeals and revisions as per sections 18 and 18A.
Procedure for compounding of offences under section 34B.
Procedure for enforcement of penalties under section 21.
administration: The Department of Commercial Taxes, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act aims to streamline the sales tax administration and enhance revenue collection.
The amendments are intended to address specific issues identified in the implementation of the principal Act.
The commencement date of the Act is to be notified by the Government.

title: The Kerala General Sales Tax (Second Amendment) Act, 1972
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.
scope: Applies to Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala General Sales Tax (Second Amendment) Act, 1972, and that it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1972.
Amends section 5 of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963 (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), in clause (ii) of sub-section (1) and in sub-section (4).

Repeals the Kerala General Sales Tax (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1972 (3 of 1972), and provides that anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

administration: Kerala General Sales Tax Department
important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 581, dated 21st October, 1972.

title: THE KERALA GENERAL SALES TAX (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 1974 (ACT 19 OF 1974)
purpose: To further amend the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, and transactions within the purview of that Act in Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala General Sales Tax (Second Amendment) Act, 1974, and that it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 15th day of May, 1974.
Amends section 5 of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963 (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act) by substituting "three and a half per cent" for "four per cent" in two instances.

Repeals the Kerala General Sales Tax (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1974 (2 of 1974). It also states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

administration: Kerala State Government
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 31st day of October, 1974 and published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 754 dated 1st November, 1974.

title: The Kerala General Sales Tax (Second Amendment) Act, 1967
purpose: To amend the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala. It amends the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.

key_definitions.container: Includes gunny bags, tins, bottles or any other containers.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala General Sales Tax (Second Amendment) Act, 1967. Clause (a) of section 2 shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1963, and the remaining provisions of this Act shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

In section 5 of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963 (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), in sub-section (1), in clause (ii), the words "at all points of sale" shall be inserted at the end. Nothingwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1) or sub-section (2), but subject to sub-section (6), where goods sold are contained in containers or are packed in any packing materials, the rate of tax and the point of levy applicable to such containers or packing materials, as the case may be, shall, whether the price of the goods contained or the packing materials is charged separately or not, be the same as those applicable to goods contained or packed, and in determining the turnover of the goods, the turnover in respect of the containers or packing materials shall be included therein. Where the sale or purchase of goods contained in any containers or packed in any packing materials is exempt from tax, then, the sale or purchase of such containers or packing materials shall also be exempt from tax.

Amends the First Schedule to the principal Act. It details amendments for specific serial numbers and their descriptions, including "All varieties of tractors and bulldozers and spare parts thereof" and various motor vehicles and parts. It also lists amendments for items like "Asbestos sheets and products", "Mosaic tiles and marble chips", "Water supply and sanitary fittings", "Lubricating oils, greases, brake fluid, transformer oil and other quenching oils", "Sewing machines and spare parts and accessories thereof", "Copper, bronze and brass utensils", "Green and dried ginger", and "Sugar cane".

Amends the Second Schedule to the principal Act, by altering figures in specific columns for items like "Cotton fabrics, woollen fabrics and rayon or artificial silk fabrics as defined in items Nos. 19, 20 and 22 respectively of the First Schedule to the Central Excises and Salt Act, 1944."

Amends the Third Schedule to the principal Act. For item 7, the following item shall be substituted: "7. Cotton fabrics, woollen fabrics and rayon or artificial silk fabrics as defined in items Nos. 19, 20 and 22 respectively of the First Schedule to the Central Excises and Salt Act, 1944.". For item 15, the following item shall be inserted: "16. Dried fish."

important_rules: If goods are sold in containers or packed, the tax rate and point of levy for the containers/packing materials are the same as for the goods themselves.
If the sale of goods within containers is exempt from tax, the sale of the containers themselves is also exempt.
key_procedures: The Act comes into force on the 1st day of April, 1963, for certain provisions (amendment of section 2), and other provisions come into force on a date appointed by the Government via notification.
Amendments to the First, Second, and Third Schedules of the principal Act are detailed within the respective sections.
administration: Kerala State Government (implied, as it amends a Kerala State Act and mentions Government notifications)
important_notes: Published in the Kerala Gazette Extra-ordinary No. 162, dated 28th August, 1967.

title: THE KERALA GENERAL SALES TAX (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 1976
purpose: To further amend the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to dealers registered under the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963. It amends various sections of the principal Act concerning the levy and assessment of sales tax.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala General Sales Tax (Second Amendment) Act, 1976.

Amends section 3 of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, by inserting a new sub-section (1A) empowering the Board of Revenue to have superintendence over officers and persons employed in the execution of the Act, to call for returns, and to issue general rules and prescribe forms.

Amends section 18 of the principal Act. It substitutes sub-sections regarding the tax payable under any of the provisions of this Act, which may be assessed and levied in advance during the year and for that purpose a dealer may be required to furnish within the prescribed period either an advance estimate of his turnover for the year or such periodical returns of the actual turnover as may be prescribed. It also empowers the assessing authority to determine the amount of tax payable in respect of any period under sub-section (1) and on assessment the dealer shall pay the sum demanded in monthly or other prescribed instalments within such time as may be fixed by such authority.

Amends sub-section (2) of section 19 of the principal Act. It substitutes the words 'a penalty as provided in section 45A' for 'a penalty not exceeding one and a half times the tax so assessed', the words, figures and letter 'a penalty as provided in section 45 A' shall be substituted.
Amends sub-section (3) of section 23 of the principal Act. It substitutes 'one per cent' for 'half per cent' in clause (a) and 'two per cent' for 'one per cent' in clause (b).

Amends section 28 of the principal Act. It inserts a proviso to sub-section (3) and a new clause (c) to sub-section (9) of section 28 regarding searches. The proviso to sub-section (3) states that no residential accommodation shall be entered or searched unless the officer is specially authorised in writing by the Board of Revenue to search that accommodation. New clause (c) to sub-section (9) empowers the officer to search any person who has got out of, or is about to get into, or is in, any place referred to in clause (a) or clause (b) of sub-section (3) or any vessel or vehicle of any dealer, if the officer has reasons to suspect that such person has secreted about his person any goods or any accounts, registers, records or other documents.

Inserts a new section 45A in Chapter VIII of the Principal Act, titled 'Imposition of penalty by officers and authorities.' This section outlines penalties for various offenses: (1)(a) failing to register as a dealer; (1)(b) failing to keep true and complete accounts; (1)(c) failing to submit returns as required; (1)(d) submitting an untrue or incorrect return; (1)(e) failing to comply with notices or summons; (1)(f) failing to make a declaration or make use of goods for the declared purpose after purchasing goods in respect of which a declaration was made; (1)(g) acting in contravention of any provision of the Act or rules made thereunder, for which no express provision for payment of penalty or punishment is made by this Act. Penalties can be up to fifty rupees or twice the amount of sales tax or other amount evaded or sought to be evaded. The burden of proving that any person is not liable to the penalty under this section shall be on such person. Sub-sections (2) to (5) further detail procedures for imposing, reducing, or waiving penalties, including opportunities for the person to be heard.
Amends section 47 of the principal Act.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new sections 55 A and 55 B.
main_sections.description: Inserts two new sections: 55A, titled 'Rounding off of turnover, tax, etc.', which specifies rules for rounding off taxable turnover and tax amounts to the nearest rupee. 55B, titled 'Service of notice', provides guidelines for serving notices when the person to whom it is addressed cannot be found, or if the place of residence or business is absent, or if it is sent by registered post to the last known place of residence or business.

Amends the First Schedule of the principal Act by inserting new serial numbers and descriptions for 'Upholstered furniture supported on steel frames' and 'Hydrogenated oil, refined oil and margarine'.
Amends the Third Schedule of the principal Act by substituting 'Fresh fruits' for 'item 9' and inserting 'Bread' as item 14.

Repeals the Kerala General Sales Tax (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1975 (12 of 1975) and provides that anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act, if this Act had come into force on the 27th day of October, 1975.

important_rules: Rounding off of taxable turnover to the nearest multiple of ten rupees. If a part of a rupee consists of paise amounting to ten or more, it shall be rounded to the next higher amount which is a multiple of ten. If it is less than five, it shall be reduced to the next lower amount which is a multiple of ten.

Rounding off of tax or other amount due to the nearest rupee. If a part of a rupee consists of paise amounting to fifty or more, it shall be rounded to the next rupee. If it is less than fifty paise, it shall be ignored.
Rules for service of notice when the addressee is not found or is absent from residence/business, or notice is sent by registered post.

penalties: Up to fifty rupees or twice the amount of sales tax or other amount evaded or sought to be evaded.
Failure to register as a dealer.
Failure to keep true and complete accounts.
Failure to submit returns as required by the Act or rules.
Submitting an untrue or incorrect return.
Failure to comply with any notice or summons issued.
Failure to make a declaration or use goods for declared purpose after purchase.
Contravention of any provision of the Act or rules for which no express penalty is provided.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Assessing authority, Deputy Commissioner, Board of Revenue, officers authorized by the Board of Revenue.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment of tax, imposition of penalties, searches of persons and premises, and issuance of notices. The burden of proof for exemption from penalty lies with the person accused.

rights: Right to be heard before penalty is imposed or cancelled.
Right to have penalties reduced or waived under certain circumstances.
duties: Duty to register as a dealer.
Duty to keep true and complete accounts.
Duty to submit returns as required.
Duty to comply with notices and summons.
Duty to make declarations and use goods for declared purposes.
Duty to pay sales tax and other amounts due under the Act.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act and the rules made thereunder.

key_procedures: Procedure for imposition of penalties, including providing an opportunity for the person to be heard.
Procedure for rounding off turnover and tax amounts.
Procedure for service of notices.
Procedure for search of persons and premises.
administration: The Board of Revenue is responsible for superintendence and issuing rules and directions.
important_notes: Explanation regarding 'Notwithstanding anything contained in the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, the burden of proving that the escape from assessment was not due to wilful nondisclosure of assessable turnover by the dealer shall be on the dealer.'
Any residential accommodation can only be searched if the officer has specific written authorisation from the Board of Revenue.
The Kerala General Sales Tax (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1975, is repealed and savings are provided.

title: The Kerala General Sales Tax (Third Amendment) Act, 2003
purpose: To further amend the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.
scope: Applies to registered dealers who have collected any sum purporting to be additional sales tax under section 5D during the period from the 1st day of April, 2003 to the date of coming into force of this Act.

main_sections.description: Specifies that this Act may be called the Kerala General Sales Tax (Third Amendment) Act, 2003, and it shall come into force on the 1st day of July, 2003.
Amends section 5D of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, with a second proviso.

Provides that notwithstanding anything in the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, if any registered dealer collected sum as additional sales tax under section 5D during the period from April 1, 2003, to the date of this Act's commencement, the collected amount shall be deemed to have been validly collected under the provisions of the said Act. Dealers shall have the right to remit the amount to the Government before or on July 31, 2003, after which penal provisions of the Act will apply.

penalties: Penal provisions of the Act shall apply if amounts collected as additional sales tax are not remitted to the Government by July 31, 2003.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be the authorities responsible for enforcing the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the existing provisions and penal clauses of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.

rights: Registered dealers have the right to remit collected additional sales tax amounts to the Government by July 31, 2003.
duties: Registered dealers are duty-bound to remit collected additional sales tax amounts to the Government by July 31, 2003, to avoid penal provisions.

key_procedures: Collection of sums purporting to be additional sales tax under section 5D between April 1, 2003, and the commencement date of this Act.
Remittance of such collected amounts to the Government by the registered dealer on or before July 31, 2003.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but would fall under the purview of the Kerala State Government's tax administration departments.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on 30th June, 2003, and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 1145 dated 30th June, 2003.

title: THE KERALA GENERAL SALES TAX (THIRD AMENDMENT) ACT, 1974
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963. It amends the Act for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: The Act applies to businesses and transactions related to sales tax in Kerala. Specific amendments relate to the definition of 'business', taxation of certain food items, and items listed in the First and Second Schedules of the principal Act.

key_definitions.business: Includes any trade, commerce or manufacture, whether or not such trade, commerce, manufacture, adventure or concern is carried on with a motive to make gain or profit and whether or not any profit accrues from such trade, commerce, manufacture, adventure or concern.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala General Sales Tax (Third Amendment) Act, 1974.
Amends section 2 of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963 by substituting a new clause (vi) under 'business' to clarify its scope.

Amends section 5 of the principal Act by adding a proviso to sub-section (1) regarding the turnover of dealers in cooked food served in hotels, restaurants, etc., where total turnover in respect of such food is not less than two lakhs rupees.

Amends the First Schedule of the principal Act by substituting various figures against serial numbers for different items, including television sets, welding rods, pressure cookers, oil engine pumpsets, and various food items and other goods. It also introduces new entries like 'Television sets and parts and accessories thereof'.

Amends the Second Schedule of the principal Act by omitting certain entries and inserting new ones. It clarifies 'Oil seeds' and adds specific categories of 'iron and steel' and 'jute' and other fibres.
Amends the Third Schedule of the principal Act regarding the item 'tapioca'.

Repeals the Kerala General Sales Tax (Third Amendment) Ordinance, 1974. It states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act, with effect from the 1st day of July, 1974.

important_rules: Rule regarding turnover tax on cooked food in hotels/restaurants.
Specific tax rates and classifications for various goods in the First and Second Schedules.
Clarification on the scope of 'business' to include activities without profit motive.

duties: Dealers in cooked food served in hotels, restaurants, etc., with a turnover exceeding a certain limit are liable to pay tax.

key_procedures: Procedure for amending the First and Second Schedules by substituting figures and entries.
Procedure for repeal and saving of previous ordinances and actions taken under them.
administration: The administration of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act and its amendments would typically fall under the Department of Commercial Taxes, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 9th day of November, 1974 and published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 759 dated 12th November, 1974.
The amendments in Section 7 are effective from July 1, 1974.

title: The Kerala General Sales Tax (Third Amendment) Act, 1976
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala. The amendments relate to specific sections and schedules of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, impacting dealers, turnover thresholds, and specific goods.

key_definitions.rice products: means parched, puffed, or beaten rice and "wheat products" means maida, atta, suji, rava, resultant atta and bran.
key_definitions.pulses: whether whole or separated and whether with or without husk shall be treated as a single commodity for the purposes of levy of tax.
key_definitions.cereals: that is to say, paddy, rice, wheat, Jowar or Milo, Bajra, Maize, Ragi, Kodon, Kutki and Barley

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala General Sales Tax (Third Amendment) Act, 1976. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1976.
Amends section 5 of the principal Act by substituting "twenty thousand rupees" with "twenty-five thousand rupees" for certain phrases.
Amends section 5A of the principal Act, substituting "twenty thousand rupees" with "twenty-five thousand rupees" and "thirty thousand rupees" in specific contexts.

Amends section 7 of the principal Act. It introduces a sub-section allowing a dealer whose total turnover in a year is not less than twenty-five thousand rupees but not more than thirty thousand rupees, at their option, to pay tax at the rate of two percent on his taxable turnover, instead of other provisions. It also makes amendments to sub-sections (2) and (4) regarding omission of clauses and applicability of assessment.
Amends section 13 of the principal Act by substituting "twelve thousand rupees" with "twenty-five thousand rupees".

Inserts new sub-sections into section 17 of the principal Act. These sub-sections deal with acceptance of returns, exemption from tax for certain turnover amounts, provisions for refund or rebate, and penalties for evasion of tax.

Inserts new sub-sections (3A) and (3B) into section 18 of the principal Act, relating to the assessment of tax payable by a dealer for any quarter exceeding a certain amount, and the procedure for estimate and verification.

Amends the First Schedule of the principal Act by inserting serial number 56A regarding 'Rice products and wheat products' and their explanation. It also amends other serial numbers concerning the effect and insertion of provisions.
Amends the Second Schedule by inserting serial number '8' related to 'Crude oil' and its explanation, and also regarding 'Pulses'.
Amends the Third Schedule by omitting a provision related to dealers whose total turnover in a year is less than thirty-five thousand rupees.
Repeals The Kerala General Sales Tax (Third Amendment) Ordinance, 1976, and provides for saving provisions regarding anything done or action taken under the Ordinance.

penalties: Penalty for evasion of tax for which the return has been submitted or against whom proceedings for evasion of such tax are pending before any authority.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Assessing authority under the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment, imposition of penalties, and legal proceedings for evasion of tax.

rights: Right to option to pay tax at 2% on taxable turnover for dealers with turnover between twenty-five and thirty thousand rupees.
Right to refund or rebate of tax under certain conditions.
duties: Duty to submit return.
Duty to pay tax as per assessment.
obligations: Dealers with total turnover not exceeding one lakh rupees for the year not exceeding such year, shall accept the return for the year or any subsequent year submitted by them, unless the return is not accompanied by prescribed documents.

key_procedures: Procedure for assessment of tax, rebate, or refund under section 17.
Procedure for estimating tax payable by a dealer under section 18.
administration: Sales Tax Department of Kerala
important_notes: The amendment is effective from April 1, 1976.
The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 20th day of November 1976 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 873, dated 20th November 1976.
Provisions related to specific goods like rice products, wheat products, and crude oil have been amended in the Schedules.

Authorised retail distributor appointed under the Kerala Rationing Order, 1966, shall not be liable to pay tax under this Act in respect of tapioca sold to ration card holders, whatever be his turnover.

title: The Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963
purpose: The purpose of the act is to consolidate and amend the law relating to the levy of sales tax in the state of Kerala.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala and governs the taxation of sales of goods within the state.

key_definitions.goods: Goods include all materials, articles, and commodities, whether specified in any of the schedules or not, and includes also all materials, articles and commodities, the value of which is taken into account in the calculation of the turnover of a dealer, but does not include actionable claims, actionable securities, stocks, shares or other securities.
key_definitions.dealer: Dealer means any person who carries on the business of buying, selling, or distributing goods, or any other person who or any society, club or association which sells any goods to a member or other person.
key_definitions.turnover: Turnover means the aggregate amount of the purchase or sale prices received or receivable by a dealer in respect of any sale or purchase by him of any goods or goods specified in the scheduled of goods, as the case may be, either of the goods or in addition to the goods of his business, and includes the amount of purchase or sale price received or receivable by him in respect of any sale or purchase of any goods or goods specified in the scheduled of goods which is in addition to the goods of his business.

main_sections.section_title: Power to confiscate goods and to impose penalty.
main_sections.description: This section outlines the authority's power to confiscate goods and impose penalties when an officer adjuges that goods are liable to confiscation. It specifies conditions under which goods may be released on payment of tax and penalty, and the procedure for submitting goods and documents for examination.

This chapter details the procedures for appeals, revisions, and refunds under the Act. It covers appeals to the Appellate Assistant Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, Appellate Tribunal, and the High Court.

main_sections.section_title: Appeals to the Appellate Assistant Commissioner.
main_sections.description: Any person objecting to an order affecting him passed by an assessing authority under sub-section (6) or sub-section (7) of section 14, may prefer an appeal to the Appellate Assistant Commissioner.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of revision of the Deputy Commissioner suo motu.
main_sections.description: The Deputy Commissioner has the power to call for and examine the record of any proceeding under this Act or any order passed by an Inspecting Assistant Commissioner or any officer or authority of rank below that of an Inspecting Assistant Commissioner and may make such enquiry or cause such enquiry to be made and subject to the provisions of this Act pass such order thereon as he thinks fit.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of revision of Deputy Commissioner on application.
main_sections.description: Any person objecting to an order passed or proceeding recorded under section 34 or section 35, may within a period of thirty days from the date on which a copy of the order or proceeding was served on him in the manner prescribed, file an application for revision of such order or proceeding to the Deputy Commissioner.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of revision of the Board of Revenue suo motu.
main_sections.description: The Board of Revenue has the power to suo motu call for and examine the record of any proceeding or order passed by the Deputy Commissioner, Inspecting Assistant Commissioner or any officer or authority of rank below that of an Inspecting Assistant Commissioner and may make such enquiry or cause such enquiry to be made and subject to the provisions of this Act pass such order thereon as he thinks fit.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of revision of Board of Revenue on application.
main_sections.description: Any person objecting to an order passed by the Deputy Commissioner under sub-section (1) of section 35 or sub-section (3) of section 36, may within a period of thirty days from the date on which a copy of the order was served on him in the manner prescribed, file an application for revision of such order or proceeding to the Board of Revenue.

Any person empowered by the Government in this behalf or any officer objecting to an order passed by the Appellate Tribunal under sub-section (3) or sub-section (4) of section 35 and any person objecting to an order passed by the Inspecting Assistant Commissioner under clause (c) of sub-section (4) of section 28 may, within a period of sixty days from the date on which the order was served on him in the manner prescribed, appeal against such order to the Appellate Tribunal.

Any person objecting to an order passed by the Board of Revenue under section 37 may, within a period of ninety days from the date on which a copy of the order was served on him in the manner prescribed, appeal against such order to the High Court.

Any officer empowered by the Government in this behalf or any other person who objects to an order passed by the Appellate Tribunal under sub-section (4) or sub-section (7) of section 39, may within ninety days from the date on which a copy of such order is served on him in the manner prescribed, prefer a petition to the High Court on the ground that the Appellate Tribunal has either decided erroneously or failed to decide any question of law.

important_rules: Goods may be released on payment of tax and penalty calculated at the rates applicable to the goods liable to confiscation.

Provided that the officer may release the goods on cash security if he is of the opinion that further time is required to arrive at a correct finding as to whether a penalty is to be imposed or not and that the security so furnished shall be adjusted towards the penalty if it is payable or returned to the party, if otherwise.

Nothing contained in sub-section (2) or sub-section (3) shall apply in the case of goods transported which are exempted from tax under any of the provisions of this Act without any condition or restriction.

Forwarding agency, etc., to submit returns - Every clearing or forwarding house or agency, transporting agency, shipping agency, shipping out-agency or steamer agency in the State shall submit to the assessing authority of the area such returns as may be prescribed of all goods cleared, forwarded, transported or shipped by it.

Bank to submit returns - Every bank, including any branch of a bank or any banking institution in the State, shall every month to the assessing authority of the area a return in the prescribed form of all bills relating to goods discounted, cleared or negotiated by or through it during the preceding month, in such manner as may be prescribed.

penalties: Penalty for incorrect returns, incorrect payment of tax, etc.
Penalty for failure to submit returns.
Penalty for illegal transport of goods.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Assessing Authority, Appellate Assistant Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, Appellate Tribunal, High Court, Board of Revenue.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment of tax, imposition of penalties, confiscation of goods, and appeals/revisions at various levels of judicial and administrative bodies.

rights: Right to appeal against orders passed by authorities.
Right to seek revision of orders.
Right to receive refunds where applicable.
Right to be heard before an order adversely affecting a person is passed.
duties: Duty of dealers to submit returns.
Duty to pay tax and penalty.
Duty to present goods and documents for examination.
Duty to comply with prescribed procedures for appeals and revisions.
obligations: Obligation to pay tax on the sale of goods within the state.
Obligation to furnish correct and complete information to the authorities.

key_procedures: Procedure for filing appeals to the Appellate Assistant Commissioner, including the form and time limit for filing.
Procedure for revision of orders by the Deputy Commissioner and the Board of Revenue, both suo motu and on application.
Procedure for preferring appeals to the Appellate Tribunal and the High Court.
Procedure for submitting goods and documents for examination and potential confiscation.
Procedure for submitting returns by various agencies and banks.
administration: The administration of the Act involves various levels of tax authorities including the Assessing Authority, Appellate Assistant Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, Board of Revenue, and the High Court.
important_notes: Goods may be released on payment of tax and penalty.
Exempted goods are not subject to certain provisions related to confiscation.
Appeals and revisions have specific time limits for filing.
The Appellate Tribunal can, in certain cases, be accompanied by an officer not exceeding one hundred rupees.

title: The Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 1988
purpose: To further amend the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, for purposes appearing hereafter.
scope: Applies to the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963 and amendments made to it.

key_definitions.Liquor: Means any liquor manufactured in any country other than India and brought to India, and includes toddy, wine, brandy, champagne, sherry, rum, gin, whisky, beer, cider, cocoa, brandy, arrack and all other distilled or spirituous or fermented beverages brought into or produced or manufactured in the State.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 1988. Sub-clause (ii) of section 3 of the principal Act is deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of July, 1987 and the remaining provisions of the Act are deemed to have come into force on the 19th day of February, 1988.

Amends section 2 of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963 (15 of 1963). In Explanation to clause (xxvi), after the words "Notwithstanding anything contained in any other provision of this Act", the words "but subject to the provisions of section 8" shall be inserted.

Amends section 5 of the principal Act. (a) For the proviso to clause (v) of sub-section (1) of section 5, a new proviso is substituted regarding points of sale for goods. (b) After sub-section (2A), a new clause is inserted regarding tax levy on certain dealers.
Amends sub-section (2) of section 13 of the principal Act. The words "the First and Second Schedules" are replaced with "the First, Second, Fourth and Fifth Schedules".

Amends the opening paragraph in sub-section (3) of section 23 of the principal Act. Allows for tax or other amount assessed or due to be paid by instalments, with interest, if permitted by authorities.

Amends sub-section (1) of section 47 of the principal Act. (a) Specifies the penalty for evasion of tax. (b) Adds a proviso empowering the Board of Revenue to compound the offence on payment of a reduced amount.
Replaces the entire "FIFTH SCHEDULE" to the principal Act with a new schedule.

Repeals The Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 1988 (10 of 1988). Anything done or any action taken under the said Ordinance as amended by this Act is deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Tax on goods is levied at the point of first sale in the State by a dealer who is liable to tax under section 5.
Specific tax rates are prescribed for various goods in the Fifth Schedule.
Penalties apply for evasion of tax, with the possibility of compounding the offence.
Tax assessed or due can be paid by instalments with interest.

penalties: Penalty for evasion of tax: sum of money equal to the amount of tax so payable, subject to a minimum of rupees one hundred and maximum of rupees one lakh.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Board of Revenue (for compounding offences)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through tax assessment and penalty imposition as per the Act, and compounding of offences.

rights: Right to pay assessed tax by instalments (with interest).
duties: Duty to pay tax on goods sold.
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, as amended.
obligations: Obligation to pay tax on turnover as prescribed.
Obligation to be subject to penalties for tax evasion.

key_procedures: Procedure for amendment of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.
Procedure for levy of tax at different points of sale based on the schedule.
Procedure for compounding of offences by the Board of Revenue.
administration: Law (Legislation-A) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: Certain provisions are deemed to have come into force retrospectively.
The Act specifically addresses the taxation of various goods listed in the Fifth Schedule.
The repeal of the Ordinance of 1988 is accompanied by a saving clause to validate actions taken under it.

title: The Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 1990
purpose: To further amend the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and concerns the imposition and levy of sales tax.

key_definitions.protective_assessment: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in any judgment, decree, order, direction or decision of any Court, Tribunal or other Authority, where the assessing authority has reason to believe that any person is, or was carrying on business in the name of, or in association with any other person, either directly or indirectly, such person or any other capacity, such person or the person in whose name the registration certificate, if any, is taken, shall jointly and severally, be liable for the payment of the taxes, penalty or other amount due under this Act which shall be assessed, levied and recovered from all or any of such person or persons as if such person or persons are dealers.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 1990, and specifies its commencement dates for various clauses.
Amends section 5A of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, by modifying the wording in subsections (1) and (2).
Inserts a new section, 19C, dealing with Protective Assessment.

Amends section 29A of the principal Act by inserting new subsections (2A) and (2B) which deal with the detention of vehicles and goods in cases of failure to furnish security or in cases of non-payment of tax, and the consequences of such detention.

Amends the First Schedule to the principal Act by substituting serial numbers and entries. It specifically amends entries related to 'Copper Sulphate' and adds an explanation regarding Oil Company sales.
Amends the Second Schedule to the principal Act by substituting serial numbers and entries. It deals with 'Hides and skins whether in a raw or dressed state' and 'Groundnuts and ground seeds'.
Repeals the Kerala General Sales Tax (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1989, and provides for saving provisions for actions taken or things done under the repealed Ordinance.

penalties: Penalty for offenses related to vehicle detention under section 29A will be liable for payment of taxes, penalty or other amount due under this Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Assessing authority, Court, Tribunal, or other Authority as per the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment, levy, recovery of taxes and penalties, and potentially through detention of vehicles and goods.

duties: Persons carrying on business are liable for payment of taxes, penalty or other amount due under this Act.
Dealers are responsible for tax on the first point of sale.
obligations: Dealers are liable to pay tax under section 5.

key_procedures: Protective Assessment: If the assessing authority believes a person is liable, they can be jointly and severally liable for taxes, penalties, and other amounts due. Provided that before taking action, the persons concerned should be given a reasonable opportunity of being heard.

Vehicle/Goods Detention: In case of failure to furnish security or non-payment of tax, the vehicle or vessel may be detained for a period not exceeding 30 days from the date of furnishing security or the relevant date. If the dealer fails to pay tax after the seizure of goods, they can be detained.
administration: Assessing authority under the Kerala General Sales Tax Act.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 21st day of February 1990 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No 164 dated the 22nd February 1990.
Explanations have been added to certain entries in the First and Second Schedules.
The repeal of the Ordinance does not affect any action taken or thing done under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance.

title: The Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 2003
purpose: To amend the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.
scope: Applies to dealers in Kerala and deals with amendments to Section 17 of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 2003 and it came into force on the 26th day of October, 2002.

This section amends Section 17 of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963. It introduces changes to sub-section (4) and related provisos. The amendment clarifies the conditions under which the assessing authority may accept the return for any year, the assessment of total turnover, and the tax payable by a dealer. It also includes provisions for re-opened and escaped turnover assessments. The amendment further details how assessments will be conducted for returns filed by dealers under specific categories, disallowing claims for exemption or reduction if not proved.

Repeals the Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2002 (9 of 2002). States that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the provisions of the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Dealers' returns will be subject to scrutiny by the Deputy Commissioner, who may select twenty per cent by following such procedure as may be specified by the Commissioner. Records and other relevant documents will be examined.
Assessments of dealers found to have not accounted for purchases or sales, or who have attempted to evade payment of tax, will be conducted.
Re-opened and escaped turnover cases will be assessed as per the Act.
Claims for exemption or reduction in tax rate will only be allowed if supported by the statement required by the Act and the rules, and if proved to the satisfaction of the assessing authority.
Assessments for subsequent periods will cease to be eligible for dealers who have had any evasion of tax detected under this sub-section.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Assessing Authority, Deputy Commissioner, Commissioner
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment of returns, scrutiny of records, re-opening of assessments, and enforcement of provisions related to escaped turnover and evasion of tax.

rights: Right to have returns accepted by the assessing authority under certain conditions.
Right to claim exemptions or reductions in tax if supported by documentation and proven.
duties: Duty to file correct and complete returns.
Duty to account for all purchases and sales.
Duty to pay tax due.
Duty to provide supporting documents for claims of exemption or reduction.
obligations: Obligation to cooperate with the assessing authority during scrutiny and assessment.

key_procedures: Procedure for assessment of returns, including scrutiny and selection of cases by the Deputy Commissioner.
Procedure for handling cases of escaped turnover and evasion of tax.
Procedure for dealers to substantiate claims for exemption or reduction in tax.
administration: State Tax Department of Kerala
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on 6th March, 2003, and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No 387 dated 6th March, 2003.
The amendments made by this Act are retrospective to October 26th, 2002.

title: The Kerala General Salestax (Amendment) Act, 1971
purpose: To further amend the Kerala General Salestax Act, 1963, for the purposes hereinabove appearing.
scope: Applies to dealers in cooked food, including coffee, tea and like articles served in a hotel, restaurant, or any other place. The scope is further defined by turnover thresholds for taxable rates.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala General Salestax (Amendment) Act, 1971, and shall come into force on the 1st day of April, 1971.

Amends Section 5 of the Kerala General Salestax Act, 1963 (Act 15 of 1963) by substituting 'ten thousand rupees' with 'twenty thousand rupees' in sub-section (1) and in sub-section (2) and also for 'twenty thousand rupees' with 'twenty thousand rupees' and 'at the rates' with 'at the rates'.

Amends Section 5A of the Principal Act. This section introduces specific tax rates based on turnover thresholds for dealers of cooked food. It replaces 'ten thousand rupees' with 'twenty thousand rupees' in sub-section (2) and in sub-section (3). It also amends the tax rate for dealers with turnover not less than thirty-five thousand rupees but not more than seventy-five thousand rupees.

Amends Section 7 of the Principal Act. It introduces clauses (i) and (ii) to the principal Act, detailing tax rates for every dealer in cooked food. The amendment specifies that if the total turnover is not less than twenty-five thousand rupees but is not more than thirty-five thousand rupees, the dealer may opt for a tax rate of one percent on his taxable turnover. It also provides for specific tax rates based on different turnover slabs, ranging from thirty-five thousand rupees up to one lakh rupees.
Amends the third Schedule to the principal Act. In item 12, the words 'twenty thousand rupees' are substituted with 'thirty-five thousand rupees'.

important_rules: Dealers of cooked food with a total turnover of not less than twenty-five thousand rupees but not more than thirty-five thousand rupees may opt to pay tax at the rate of one percent on their taxable turnover.
Specific turnover thresholds are defined for different tax rates for dealers of cooked food.
The words 'ten thousand rupees' and 'twenty thousand rupees' have been replaced with 'twenty thousand rupees' and 'thirty-five thousand rupees' in various sections and schedules.

rights: Dealers of cooked food have the option to pay tax at a specific rate if their turnover falls within certain thresholds.
duties: Dealers must comply with the tax rates and turnover provisions stipulated by the Act.

key_procedures: Dealers must ensure their tax payments and reporting align with the amended turnover thresholds and rates.
The Act requires substitution of specific monetary amounts in existing sections and schedules.
important_notes: The Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 366, dated 23rd August, 1971.

title: The Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 1969
purpose: To amend the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, for purposes hereafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963. It addresses the sale of goods within Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 1969, and that Sections 3, 4, 5, 6, and the remaining provisions of the Act shall come into force at once, while Section 2 is deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1963.

Amends Section 4 of the principal Act (Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963), by substituting 'referred to as the principal Act' for 'whose who is, or has been, or is qualified to be appointed as, a Judicial Officer'.

Inserts a new section 21A, titled 'Firm dissolved or business discontinued', which deals with the assessment of tax liability when a business ceases to operate or a firm is dissolved. It clarifies that the assessing authority shall make an assessment of the taxable turnover of the firm or business, and the tax payable, and all provisions relating to levy of penalty or other amount under the Act shall apply.
Amends the First Schedule to the principal Act, by substituting entries for Serial Numbers 40 and 47, and an entry for Serial Number 71.
Amends the Second Schedule to the principal Act, by substituting an entry for Serial Number 71.
Amends the Third Schedule to the principal Act, by omitting item 14.

Validates any judgment, decree, or order of any court, tribunal, or other authority, or any assessment, levy, or collection of tax on the turnover of a firm which has been dissolved or the business carried on by which has been discontinued, made or purporting to have been made under the principal Act before the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette. It also validates all such assessment, levy, or collection of tax deemed to be valid and effective as if such assessment, levy or collection had been made under the principal Act as amended by this Act. It further specifies that no suit or other proceeding shall be maintained or continued in any court, tribunal or other authority for the refund of any such tax so collected, and no court shall enforce any decree or order directing the refund of any such tax so collected.

important_rules: Rule for assessment of tax when a firm is dissolved or business discontinued.
Provisions for continuing proceedings against a firm or business that has been dissolved or discontinued.
Rules regarding the validation of past assessments, levies, and collections of tax.

penalties: Penalty for levy or other amount under the Act may apply in cases of dissolution or discontinuance of business.
No penalty or other amount shall be refunded under certain circumstances as per section 7(2).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Assessing authority, judicial officers, courts, tribunals, other authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessments, levies, collections, and judicial or other proceedings.

rights: Right to have tax assessed and collected even after dissolution or discontinuance of business.
Right to recover tax in the manner provided under the principal Act if it was collected prior to the publication of this Act and is found to be erroneous.
duties: Duty to pay tax on the taxable turnover.
Duty to cooperate with the assessing authority in cases of dissolution or discontinuance.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, as amended.

key_procedures: Procedure for assessment of tax on dissolved firms or discontinued businesses.
Procedure for continuing proceedings against dissolved firms or discontinued businesses.
Procedure for validation of past tax assessments, levies, and collections.
Procedure for recovery of erroneously collected tax.
administration: Assessing Authority under the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.
important_notes: Section 21A applies to firms dissolved or businesses discontinued.
Section 7 validates past acts and proceedings, preventing refunds of tax collected, unless specific conditions are met.
The Act makes amendments to the First, Second, and Third Schedules of the principal Act.

Section 7(2) clarifies that no doubt shall be construed in preventing any person from claiming refund of any tax paid by him in excess of the amount due from him under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

title: THE KERALA GIFT GOODS (UNLAWFUL POSSESSION) ACT, 1963
purpose: To provide for the punishment of the offence of unlawful possession of gift goods supplied by certain relief organisations.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force at once.

key_definitions.gift goods: means any of the following goods, namely: (a) corn-meal; (b) milk powder; (c) vegetable oil (soya bean oil or sunflower seed oil) supplied, by way of gift, by any relief organisation to any State Government or to the Central Government or to any other person on behalf of such Government.
key_definitions.relief organisation: means any organisation specified in the Schedule.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called The Kerala Gift Goods (Unlawful Possession) Act, 1963, extends to the whole of the State of Kerala, and shall come into force at once.
Defines "gift goods" and "relief organisation" as specified in the JSON structure.

Declares that unlawful possession of gift goods is an offence and prescribes penalties for persons found or proved to have been in possession of such goods, with potential imprisonment for up to two years or fine, or both.

main_sections.section_title: Offences under the Act to be cognizable.
main_sections.description: States that notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (Central Act V of 1898), any offence under this Act shall be deemed to be a cognizable offence within the meaning of that Code. It also states that no court below that of a Magistrate of the First Class shall try any offence under this Act.

Grants the Government the power to notify or omit any organisation from the Schedule, and such notification or omission, if published in the Gazette, shall be deemed to be included in, or as the case may be, omitted from the Schedule.

main_sections.section_title: Notification to be placed before the Legislative Assembly.
main_sections.description: Requires every notification issued under this Act to be laid before the Legislative Assembly as soon as may be after it is issued, for a total period of fourteen days which may comprise one session or two successive sessions. It further specifies that the Assembly may make modifications or annulments, but without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that notification.

important_rules: Unlawful possession of gift goods is an offence.
Possession of gift goods may result in imprisonment and/or a fine.
Offences under this Act are cognizable.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts of Magistrate of the First Class
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Prosecution for unlawful possession of gift goods.

duties: To refrain from unlawfully possessing gift goods.
obligations: Notification of the Act must be placed before the Legislative Assembly for potential modifications.

key_procedures: Offences are tried by a Magistrate of the First Class.
Notifications amending the Schedule are published in the Gazette.
Notifications are laid before the Legislative Assembly for a specified period.
administration: The Government (presumably the State Government of Kerala)
important_notes: The Act was enacted in the Thirteenth Year of the Republic of India.
The Act received the assent of the Governor on 30th January 1963 and was published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 31st January 1963.
The list of 'relief organisations' is provided in The Schedule and can be amended by the Government.

title: THE KERALA GIFT GOODS (UNLAWFUL POSSESSION) AMENDMENT ACT, 1967
purpose: To amend The Kerala Gift Goods (Unlawful Possession) Act, 1963.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala, amending the provisions of The Kerala Gift Goods (Unlawful Possession) Act, 1963.

key_definitions.gift goods: Any of the goods specified in Schedule I, supplied by way of gift, by any relief organisation to any State Government or to the Central Government or to any other person on behalf of such Government.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Gift Goods (Unlawful Possession) Amendment Act, 1967.

Amends section 2 of The Kerala Gift Goods (Unlawful Possession) Act, 1963 (6 of 1963). It redefines 'gift goods' by referencing Schedule I and specifies that the word and figure 'Schedule II' shall be substituted for 'the Schedule' in clause (2).

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 5.
main_sections.description: Substitutes section 5 of the principal Act. The new section 5 grants the Government the power, by notification in the Gazette, to amend Schedule I by adding, omitting, or altering the name of any organisation, or adding, omitting, or altering the name of any goods from the said Schedule and thereupon that Schedule shall be deemed to be amended accordingly.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of existing Schedule and insertion of new Schedule.
main_sections.description: Amends the existing Schedule and inserts a new Schedule. The principal Act's Schedule is renumbered as Schedule II, and before Schedule II, a new Schedule is inserted, named Schedule I.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Government can amend Schedule I by notification in the Gazette, adding or omitting organisations or goods.
Rule 2: Schedule I will list goods supplied by way of gift from relief organisations to government entities or individuals on behalf of the government.
Rule 3: The original 'Schedule' in the principal Act is now referred to as 'Schedule II'.
key_procedures: Procedure 1: The Government can amend Schedule I by publishing a notification in the Gazette.
Procedure 2: Additions or deletions to the list of 'gift goods' and the organisations involved will be effective upon notification.
administration: Government of Kerala (implied from the title and context)
important_notes: Published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 107, dated 6th July, 1967.
The Act specifically amends The Kerala Gift Goods (Unlawful Possession) Act, 1963.

title: THE KERALA GOVERNMENT LAND ASSIGNMENT (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2012
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Government Land Assignment Act, 1960.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Government Land Assignment Act, 1960, and its subsequent amendments and ordinances.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Government Land Assignment (Amendment) Act, 2012. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 19th day of March, 1993.

Amends section 7 of the Kerala Government Land Assignment Act, 1960 (30 of 1960). It substitutes the words 'The Government may make rules, either prospectively or retrospectively,' for the opening words 'The Government may make rules,' in sub-section (1).

This section validates anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance, or under the provisions of the principal Act as amended by this Act. It also validates anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken after the cessation of operation of the said Ordinance and before the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette, which could have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance, if the said Ordinance had not ceased to operate, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not specified in the provided sections.
