title: THE KERALA GOVERNMENT LAND ASSIGNMENT ACT, 1960
purpose: To provide for the assignment of Government lands, regulating the assignment, and to remove doubts as to the validity of limitations and restrictions imposed in assignments of land by the Government or under their authority.
scope: The Act applies to the whole of the State of Kerala. It covers the assignment of Government lands.

key_definitions.Government lands: Includes all public roads, streets, lanes and paths, the bridges, ditches, dykes and fences on or beside the same; the bed of the sea and of harbours and creeks below high water-mark; the beds and banks of rivers, streams, irrigation and drainage channels. It also includes lands registered in the name of a person but subsequently abandoned or relinquished and all lands held by right of escheat, purchase, resumption, reversion or acquisition under the Land Acquisition Act for the time being in force.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act
key_definitions.assignment: Includes a transfer of land by way of lease and a grant of licence for the use of land

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Government Land Assignment Act, 1960, and it extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. It shall come into force at once.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Government lands', 'assignee', 'prescribed', and 'assignment'.

States that Government land may be assigned by the Government or by any prescribed authority, either absolutely or subject to such restrictions, limitations and conditions as may be prescribed. It also clarifies that any restriction to alienation, whether voluntary or otherwise, of the right of the assignee, shall be a restriction within the meaning of this section.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure to be followed before Government lands are assigned
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for assigning Government lands, which involves notification, consideration of objections, and inquiry by the Tahsildar or such other officer. It specifies that the Collector or Tahsildar shall have all the powers conferred by the law for the time being in force regarding summoning persons and for disposal of matters connected with revenue administration.

Details the process for issuing an order of assignment, including timelines for objections and appeals. It also states that the land may, subject to such rules as may be made by the Government, be assigned by the Government.

Prohibits any suit against the Government in respect of any order passed under this Act, except on the ground that the order is in breach of any completed agreement to assign, or that the land in respect of which such order has been passed is not Government land. It also establishes a two-year period for instituting proceedings related to the notice of such order.

Grants the Government the power to make rules regarding the assignment of land, including conditions of assignment, qualifications of persons, priority of assignment, and the procedure to be followed in assigning land. Rules can also cover publication of notifications, enquiry procedures, recovery of amounts due, protection of royalties, restrictions and limitations, appeals, revision, and the issue of Pattiah or other title-deed evidencing the assignment.

main_sections.section_title: Assignment to take effect with restrictions, conditions, etc., according to their tenor
main_sections.description: States that all provisions, restrictions, conditions and limitations contained in any assignment of Government land, or in any document evidencing the assignment, shall be valid and take effect according to their tenor, notwithstanding any law or custom to the contrary. The expression 'Government land' in this section includes land under the control or management of the Government at the time of assignment.

Repeals The Travancore-Cochin Government Land Assignment Act, 1950. It also states that the Government Grants Act, 1895 (Central Act 15 of 1895), in so far as it relates to any grant or other transfer of land or of an interest therein by or on behalf of the Government of Kerala, shall cease to apply to the Malabar District referred to in sub-clause (2) of section 5 of the State Reorganisation Act, 1956 (Central Act 37 of 1956). Furthermore, all rules and orders made or deemed to have been made under the Travancore-Cochin Government Land Assignment Act, 1950, are hereby repealed, and all rules and orders in force immediately before the commencement of this Act relating to the assignment of Government lands in the Malabar District are to cease to apply as far as they are inconsistent with this Act, while being deemed to have been made under this Act and continuing in force.

important_rules: Assignments of Government land may be absolute or subject to restrictions, limitations, and conditions.
Assignments must follow a prescribed procedure, including notification and consideration of objections.
Orders of assignment are subject to appeal within a specified time.
No suit can be filed against the Government regarding an order of assignment, unless it breaches a completed agreement or the land is not Government land.
The Government has the power to make detailed rules for the assignment of land.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government or prescribed authority, Collectors, and Tahsildars are involved in the enforcement and inquiry process.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the prescribed procedures for assignment, inquiry by officials, and the bar of suits which prevents legal challenges except under specific circumstances.

rights: Right to apply for assignment of Government land (subject to prescribed procedures and conditions).
duties: Applicants for land assignment must follow the prescribed procedures.
Assignees must adhere to the conditions of their assignment.
Government officials must follow the prescribed procedure for considering objections and issuing orders.

key_procedures: Procedure for Assignment of Government Land: 1. Government land is proposed to be assigned by the prescribed authority. 2. The Tahsildar or such other officer will conduct an inquiry. 3. Objections to the assignment can be preferred in writing. 4. The Tahsildar shall inquire into the objections and submit his report to the Collector. 5. The Collector shall, after considering the report, pass an order. 6. An appeal against the order may be preferred within a specified time.
Procedure for Rule Making: The Government can make rules to govern the assignment of land, including notification procedures, inquiry processes, and conditions of assignment.
administration: The Government of Kerala and prescribed authorities.
important_notes: Explanation 1 to Section 2 clarifies that 'lands registered in the name of a person but subsequently abandoned or relinquished and all lands held by right of escheat, purchase, resumption, reversion or acquisition under the Land Acquisition Act for the time being in force are Government lands within the meaning of this sub-section'.
Explanation II to Section 2 defines 'high water mark' as the highest point reached by the ordinary spring-tide at any season of the year.
Section 8 clarifies that the expression 'Government land' under that section includes land under the control or management of the Government at the time of assignment.

Section 9 repeals the Travancore-Cochin Government Land Assignment Act, 1950, and clarifies the applicability of the Government Grants Act, 1895, and previous rules and orders in the Malabar District.

title: THE KERALA GRANDHASALA SANGHAM (TAKING OVER OF MANAGEMENT) ACT, 1977
purpose: To provide for the taking over, in the public interest, of the management of the undertaking of the Kerala Grandhasala Sangham, with a view to ensuring the proper working of that Sangham and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the management of the undertaking of the Kerala Grandhasala Sangham.

key_definitions.association of articles: articles of association of the Grandhasala Sangham
key_definitions.district committee: a district committee constituted under article 24(a) of the articles of association
key_definitions.executive committee: the executive committee of the Grandhasala Sangham referred to in article 24 of the articles of association
key_definitions.governing council: the governing council of the Grandhasala Sangham constituted under article 24 of the articles of association
key_definitions.Grandhasala Sangham: the Kerala Grandhasala Sangham registered under the Travancore Companies Act, 1114 (TX of 1114)
key_definitions.notified order: an order notified in the Gazette
key_definitions.prescribed: prescribed by rules made under this Act
key_definitions.taluk union committee: a taluk union committee referred to in clause (3) of article 38 of the articles of association
key_definitions.undertaking: includes all assets, rights, leaseholds, powers, authorities and privileges and all property, movable and immovable, including lands, buildings, stores, equipments, automobiles and other vehicles, cash balances, reserve fund, investments and book debts and all other rights and interest arising out of such property as were immediately before the date of the notified order under sub-section (1) of section 3, in the ownership, possession, power or control of the Grandhasala Sangham, and all books of account, registers and all other documents of whatever nature relating thereto.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Grandhasala Sangham (Taking Over of Management) Act, 1977 and it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 16th day of March, 1977.
Defines terms used in the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Board to take over management of the undertaking of the Grandhasala Sangham
main_sections.description: The Government may, by notified order, appoint a body of persons (hereinafter referred to as the 'Board of Control') to take over the management of the undertaking. The Board of Control shall consist of a Chairman and such number of other members not exceeding ten as the Government may think fit, to be appointed by the Government. The Government may, either in the notified order issued under sub-section (1) or in a subsequent order, specify that one or more of the members of the Board of Control shall be full-time member or full time members thereof. The term of office of, the procedure to be followed in the discharge of their functions by, and the manner of filling vacancies among, the members of the Board of Control shall be such as may be prescribed. The salaries, allowances and other remuneration and the conditions of service of the members of the Board of Control shall be such as may be determined by the Government. Any notified order issued under sub-section (1) shall remain in force for such period not exceeding two years as may be specified in the order: Provided that if the Government are of opinion that in order to secure the proper management of the undertaking, it is expedient that any such notified order should continue in force after the expiry of the period specified in that order, they may, from time to time, by notification in the Gazette, extend such period by not more than six months at a time, but no such notified order shall in any case remain in force for more than five years.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of notified order issued under section 3
main_sections.description: Upon the issue of a notified order appointing a Board of Control to take over the management of the undertaking, all persons in charge of the management of the Grandhasala Sangham, including the President, Vice-President, General Secretary, Joint Secretaries and Treasurer and other members of the governing council, members of the executive committee and members of the district committees, and taluk union committees shall be deemed to have vacated their offices, as such. The Board of Control shall alone be entitled, notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force, to exercise all the powers of the governing council, executive committee, district committees and taluk union committees. As from the date of the notified order, the undertaking of the Grandhasala Sangham shall be deemed to be in the custody of the Board of Control who shall, as soon as may be after such date, take such steps as may be necessary to take into its possession, or under its control all properties, assets and effects and all actionable claims comprised in the undertaking. Subject to the other provisions contained in this Act and to the control of the Government, the Board of Control shall take such steps as may be necessary for the purpose of efficiently managing the affairs of the Grandhasala Sangham and shall exercise such other powers and have such other duties as may be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Contracts in bad faith, etc., may be cancelled or varied
main_sections.description: Without prejudice to the provisions contained in section 4, the Board of Control may, with the previous approval of the Government, make an application to any court having jurisdiction in this behalf for the purpose of cancelling or varying any contract or agreement entered into at any time before the issue of the notified order under sub-section (1) of section 3, between the Grandhasala Sangham and any other person, and the court may, if satisfied after due enquiry that such contract or agreement had been entered into in bad faith and is detrimental to the interest of the Grandhasala Sangham, make an order cancelling or varying (either unconditionally or subject to such conditions as it may think fit to impose) that contract or agreement, and the contract or agreement shall cease to have effect or, as the case may be, have effect subject to such variations.

main_sections.section_title: No right to compensation for termination of office
main_sections.description: Notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force, no person who ceases to hold any office by reason of the provisions contained in clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 4 shall be entitled to any compensation for the loss of office: Provided that nothing contained in this section shall affect the right of any such person to recover from the Grandhasala Sangham moneys receivable otherwise than by way of such compensation.

main_sections.section_title: Applicability of Kerala Non-trading Companies Act and Articles of Association
main_sections.description: Notwithstanding anything contained in the Kerala Non-Trading Companies Act, 1961 (42 of 1961), the Articles of Association of the Grandhasala Sangham shall stand suspended for the period during which the notified order under sub-section (1) of section 3 is in force. Subject to the provisions contained in sub-section (1) and to the other provisions contained in this Act and subject to such exceptions, restrictions and limitations, if any, as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, specify in this behalf, the Kerala Non-trading Companies Act, 1961 (42 of 1961) shall continue to apply to the Grandhasala Sangham in the same manner as it applied thereto before the issue of the notified order under sub-section (1) of section 3.

main_sections.section_title: Conditions of service, etc. of existing employees
main_sections.description: Every officer or employee employed, immediately before the date of the notified order under sub-section (1) of section 3, in connection with the affairs of the undertaking, shall, during the period in which such notified order is in force, hold his office by the same tenure at the same remuneration and upon the same terms and conditions and with the same rights and privileges as to gratuity and other matters as he would have held under the Grandhasala Sangham if such notified order had not been issued. Where the Grandhasala Sangham has established a provident, superannuation, welfare or any other fund for the benefit of its officers and other employees, such fund shall, with effect on and from the date of the notified order under sub-section (1) of section 3, stand transferred to, and vested in, the Board of Control.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to cancel notified order under section 3
main_sections.description: If at any time it appears to the Government on the application of any member of the Grandhasala Sangham or otherwise that the purpose of the notified order under sub-section (1) of section 3 has been fulfilled or that for any other reason it is not necessary that the order should remain in force, the Government may, by notified order, cancel such order.

main_sections.section_title: Duty to deliver possession of property and documents relating thereto
main_sections.description: As soon as may be after the issue of the notified order under sub-section (1) of section 3, every person having possession, custody or control of any property of the Grandhasala Sangham shall deliver the property to the Board of Control or to any such person as may be authorised by the Board in this behalf. Any person who, on the commencement of this Act, has in his possession or under his control any books, documents or other papers relating to the undertaking, including any letters or other communications to the Board of Control and shall deliver them up to the Board or to any such person as may be authorised by the Board in this behalf.
The Government may take all necessary steps for securing possession of all properties of the Grandhasala Sangham.

The Grandhasala Sangham shall, within ten days from the date of the notified order under sub-section (1) of section 3 or within such further period as the Government may allow in this behalf, furnish to the Board of Control a complete inventory of all the properties and assets (including particulars of, and investments and belongings) of the Sangham at the commencement of this Act, and of all the liabilities and obligations of the Sangham subsisting at such commencement and also of all agreements entered into by the Sangham in force at such commencement.

For the purpose of ascertaining whether any property is the property of the Grandhasala Sangham or for any other purpose mentioned in this Act or the rules made thereunder, any person authorised by the Government in this behalf shall have the right -- (a) to enter and inspect any premises; (b) to require any person having the possession, custody or control of any register or record of the Grandhasala Sangham to produce such register or record; (c) to require the owner of any property belonging to, or claimed to be the property of, the Grandhasala Sangham, to submit to the person so authorised such accounts, books or other documents or to furnish to him such information as he may reasonably think necessary; and (d) to examine any person having the control of, or employed in connection with, the Grandhasala Sangham and to require him to make any statement touching the affairs of the Sangham.
Any person authorised by the Government under sub-section (1) shall be a public servant within the meaning of section 21 of the Indian Penal Code (Central Act 45 of 1860).

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken under the Act
main_sections.description: If any person,-- (a) when required by this Act or by any order made under this Act to make any statement or furnish any information, makes any statement or furnishes any information which is false in any particular and which he knows or believes to be false or does not believe to be true; or (b) makes any such statement as aforesaid in any book, account, record, return or other document which he is required by any order made under this Act to submit, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees, or with both.

Any person who-- (a) having in his possession custody or control any property forming part of the assets of the Grandhasala Sangham, wrongly withholds such property from the Board of Control; or (b) wrongfully obtains possession of any property forming part of the assets of the Grandhasala Sangham, or (c) wilfully withholds or fails to produce to any person authorised under this Act, any register, record or other document which may be in his possession, custody or control; or (d) fails without any reasonable excuse to submit any accounts, books or other documents when required to do so, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees, or with both.

main_sections.section_title: Payment of remuneration and expenses out of the funds of Grandhasala Sangham
main_sections.description: No court shall take cognizance of an offence punishable under this Act except with the previous sanction of the Government or of an officer authorised by the Government in this behalf.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to give directions
main_sections.description: No suit, prosecution or other legal proceedings shall lie against the Government or the Board of Control or any member thereof or any other person for anything which is done in good faith or intended to be done under this Act.

The provisions of this Act or any rule or order made thereunder shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any law other than this Act or any instrument having effect by virtue of any law other than this Act.

All salaries, allowances and other remuneration paid to the Chairman and other members of the Board of Control or any other person who may be appointed or employed in connection with the affairs of the management of the Grandhasala Sangham and all other expenses duly incurred in connection with such management shall be paid out of the funds of the Grandhasala Sangham.

Notwithstanding anything contained in the foregoing provisions of this Act, the Government may give such directions to the Board of Control, as the Government may deem fit, for the proper management of the undertaking of the Grandhasala Sangham and the Board of Control shall comply with such directions.

important_rules: The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make rules to carry out the purposes of this Act.

Every rule made under this Act, shall, as soon as may be after it is made, before the Legislative Assembly while it is in session for a total period of fourteen days which may be comprised in one session or in two successive sessions, and if, before the expiry of the session in which it is so laid, or the session immediately following, the Legislative Assembly makes any modification in the rule or decides that the rule should not be made, the rule shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect, as the case may be, so, however, that any such modification or annulment shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that rule.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or fine which may extend to two thousand rupees, or both for making false statements or furnishing false information.

Imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or fine which may extend to two thousand rupees, or with both for wrongfully withholding or obtaining possession of assets, or failing to produce records, or failing to submit accounts.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government or an officer authorised by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through criminal prosecution for false statements or withholding of property/documents, and through court action for cancellation or variation of contracts. The Board of Control exercises powers granted by the Act.

rights: The Board of Control is entitled to exercise all powers of the governing council, executive committee, district committees, and taluk union committees.
The Board of Control has the right to enter and inspect premises, require production of registers/records, require submission of accounts/books/documents, and examine persons.
duties: Persons in possession of property of the Grandhasala Sangham must deliver it to the Board of Control.
Persons in control of books, documents, or papers must deliver them to the Board of Control.
The Grandhasala Sangham must furnish a complete inventory of properties, assets, liabilities, and agreements.
obligations: Officers and employees of the Sangham continue to hold their office under the same terms and conditions.
Provident, superannuation, and welfare funds of the Sangham are vested in the Board of Control.

key_procedures: Government issues a notified order appointing a Board of Control to take over the management of the Grandhasala Sangham's undertaking.
Upon the notified order, existing management vacates office, and the Board of Control assumes management.
The Board of Control takes possession of all properties and assets.
The Board of Control manages the affairs of the Sangham and exercises powers as prescribed.
The Board of Control can apply to a court to cancel or vary contracts made in bad faith.
The Government can cancel the notified order if the purpose is fulfilled or no longer necessary.
The Government may make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.
administration: The Government of Kerala, through the Board of Control appointed by it.
important_notes: The Act has an overriding effect on any inconsistent provisions in other laws or instruments.
No suit, prosecution, or legal proceedings shall lie against the Government or Board of Control for good faith actions.
Prosecution for offences under the Act requires prior sanction from the Government.
The Act repeals and saves the provisions of The Kerala Grandhasala Sangham (Taking Over of Management) Ordinance, 1977.

title: THE KERALA GRANDHASALA SANGHAM (TAKING OVER OF MANAGEMENT) AMENDMENT ACT, 1986
purpose: To amend The Kerala Grandhasala Sangham (Taking Over of Management) Act, 1977.
scope: Applies to The Kerala Grandhasala Sangham (Taking Over of Management) Act, 1977.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Grandhasala Sangham (Taking Over of Management) Amendment Act, 1986, and it came into force on April 2, 1982.
Amends section 3 of the principal Act by replacing the words 'five years' with 'eleven years' in relation to the principal Act.

Validates anything done or any action taken under the principal Act, or by the Board of Control, or by any other person or authority, as if such powers and functions had been validly exercised and conferred.

Repeals The Kerala Grandhasala Sangham (Taking Over of Management) Amendment Ordinance, 1986. It also saves anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken under the said Ordinance as amended by this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Board of Control (implied)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the principal Act and this Amendment Act.

administration: Not explicitly stated, but likely related to the Board of Control of The Kerala Grandhasala Sangham.
important_notes: The Act was deemed to have come into force on April 2, 1982.
The amendments are retrospective in nature concerning the commencement date.
Section 3, concerning validation, aims to ensure that actions taken under the principal Act or subsequent ordinances are legally sound.

title: The Kerala Grandsala Sangham (Taking Over Of Management) Amendment Act, 1988
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Grandsala Sangham (Taking Over of Management) Act, 1977, for purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Grandsala Sangham (Taking Over of Management) Act, 1977.

main_sections.description:
(1) This Act may be called the Kerala Grandsala Sangham (Taking Over of Management) Amendment Act, 1988.
(2) It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 20th day of May 1988.

In section 3 of the Kerala Grandsala Sangham (Taking Over of Management) Act, 1977 (19 of 1977), (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), in the proviso to sub-section (6), for the words "eleven years", the words "twelve years" shall be substituted.

(1) The Kerala Grandsala Sangham (Taking Over of Management) Amendment Ordinance, 1988 (12 of 1988), is hereby repealed.
(2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

administration: Government of Kerala, Law (Legislation-C) Department
important_notes: The Act is published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary, dated 1st August 1988.

title: THE KERALA GRANTS AND LEASES (MODIFICATION OF RIGHTS) ACT, 1980
purpose: To provide for the modification of rights under grants and leases of lands made or granted by or on behalf of the former States of Travancore and Cochin for cultivation.
scope: Applies to all grants and leases of lands made or granted by or on behalf of the former State of Travancore or Cochin for cultivation.

key_definitions.Collector: The Collector of the district.
key_definitions.grant: Any grant to which this Act applies.
key_definitions.grantee: Means the person in whose favour a grant has been made and includes his heirs, successors and assigns.
key_definitions.lease: Means any lease to which this Act applies.
key_definitions.lessee: Means the persons in who favour a lease deed has been executed and includes his heirs, successors and assigns.
key_definitions.lease deed: Means the document evidencing a lease.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.

Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'Collector', 'grant', 'grantee', 'lease', 'lessee', 'lease deed', and 'prescribed'.

No civil court shall have jurisdiction to decide or deal with any question or to determine any matter which is, by or under this Act, required to be decided or dealt with or to be determined by the Government or the Collector or any other officer.

No suit, prosecution or other legal proceedings shall lie against the Government or the Collector or any other person for anything which is in good faith done or intended to be done under this Act or any rule made thereunder.

If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, the Government may, by order, do anything not inconsistent with such provisions which appears to them necessary for the purpose of removing the difficulty.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make rules to carry out the purposes of this Act. Such rules may provide for the principles to be followed for the revision of assessment or rent, the form and particulars to be contained in any appeal, and any other matter.

Repeals the Kerala Grants and Leases (Modification of Rights) Ordinance, 1980. It also includes a saving clause stating that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Grantees or lessees may appropriate for their own use all trees standing on the land except teak, blackwood, ebony, karumthali and sandalwood at any two or more of those categories, subject to payment of scigniorage at the rates specified.
No timber rights are reserved for the Government and the grantees or lessees can appropriate the timber standing on the land without any restriction or limitation.
The principles to be followed for the revision of assessment or rent stipulated in any grant or lease deed.
The form of and the particulars to be contained in, any appeal under section (1) of section 6 and the fee for such appeal.
Any other matter which has to be, or may be, prescribed.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government, Collector
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through revision of assessment or rent, appeals, and removal of difficulties by government order.

rights: Grantees or lessees have the right to appropriate all trees standing on the land (except specific types) for their own use.
Grantees or lessees have the right to appropriate timber standing on the land without restriction or limitation.
obligations: Grantees and lessees are obligated to pay current scigniorage rates for trees.
Grantees and lessees are obligated to pay assessment or rent.
Grantees and lessees are obligated to comply with rules made under the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure for revision of assessment or rent by the Collector.
Procedure for appeal against decisions.
Procedure for removing difficulties by Government order.
Procedure for making rules by the Government.
administration: Government
important_notes: This Act is deemed to have come into force on the 25th day of June, 1980.
Received the assent of the President on the 7th day of August 1980 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 565 dated 7th August 1980.
The Kerala Grants and Leases (Modification of Rights) Ordinance, 1980 (4 of 1980) is hereby repealed.

title: THE KERALA GROUND WATER (CONTROL AND REGULATION) AMENDMENT ACT, 2005
purpose: To amend the Kerala Ground Water (Control and Regulation) Act, 2002, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to every user of ground water in the State.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Ground Water (Control and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2005. It shall come into force at once.

Amends section 9 of the Kerala Ground Water (Control and Regulation) Act, 2002. Specifically, sub-section (1) of section 9 is substituted to state that every user of ground water in the State shall, within such time as may be notified by the Government, apply to the Authority for registration as a user of ground water and for the grant of a certificate of registration.

important_rules: Every user of ground water in the State shall apply to the Authority for registration and for a certificate of registration within the time notified by the Government.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Authority (as established by the principal Act)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through registration and grant of certificates of registration for ground water users.

rights: Right to apply for registration as a user of ground water.
Right to obtain a certificate of registration.
duties: Duty to apply for registration as a user of ground water.
Duty to obtain a certificate of registration.
obligations: Obligation to comply with registration requirements as notified by the Government.

key_procedures: Application for registration as a user of ground water and for a certificate of registration must be made to the Authority within the time specified by the Government.
administration: The Authority (established under the principal Act)
important_notes: The principal Act is The Kerala Ground Water (Control and Regulation) Act, 2002.
This amendment was enacted in the Fifty-Sixth Year of the Republic of India.
Received the assent of the Governor on the 12th August 2005 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No 1839 dated 12th August, 2005.

title: THE KERALA HABITUAL OFFENDERS ACT, 1960 (ACT 28 OF 1960)
purpose: An Act to provide for the treatment and training of habitual offenders.
scope: Extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.code: means the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, or 'certified as a corrective settlement' means any place established, approved or certified as a corrective settlement under section 13.
key_definitions.district Magistrate: means the Collector of the district.
key_definitions.habitual offender: means a person who, during any continuous period of five years, whether before or after the commencement of this Act or partly before and partly after such commencement, has been convicted on conviction of not less than three occasions since he attained the age of eighteen years to a substantive term of imprisonment for any one or more of the specified offences committed on different occasions and not so convicted together as to form parts of the same transaction, such sentence not having been reversed in appeal or on revision:
key_definitions.prescribed: means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.registered offender: means a habitual offender registered or re-registered under this Act.
key_definitions.scheduled offence: means an offence specified in the Schedule or an offence analogous thereto.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Kerala Habitual Offenders Act, 1960', its extent to the whole of Kerala, and commencement upon notification.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Code', 'District Magistrate', 'habitual offender', 'prescribed', 'registered offender', 'scheduled offence', and 'State'.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to direct registration of habitual offenders.
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to direct the District Magistrate to make a register of habitual offenders within their district and inscribe therein names and other prescribed particulars.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure for preparing register and alterations therein.
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for preparing the register of habitual offenders, including notifying individuals, requiring them to furnish information, allowing them to appear at a time and place specified, and allowing them to furnish information as may be necessary to enable entry into the register.

main_sections.section_title: Charge of register and alterations therein.
main_sections.description: Specifies that the register shall be in the custody of the Superintendent of Police, who shall report to the District Magistrate any alterations made in his opinion.

main_sections.section_title: Power to take finger and palm impressions, foot-prints and photographs at any time.
main_sections.description: Grants power to take finger and palm impressions, foot-prints, and photographs of registered offenders at any time.

main_sections.section_title: Registered offenders to notify change of residence and to report themselves.
main_sections.description: Requires registered offenders to notify any change of residence and to report themselves to the authorities.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure by District Magistrate on change of residence of habitual offender to another district.
main_sections.description: Details the procedure for the District Magistrate when a habitual offender changes residence to another district, including informing the Magistrate of the new district and cancelling the registration in the old district.

main_sections.section_title: Duration of registration and re-registration of habitual offenders.
main_sections.description: Specifies the duration of registration and conditions for re-registration of habitual offenders, noting that registration ceases to be in force five years after its date or after cancellation unless re-registered.

main_sections.section_title: Right to make representations against registration, etc.
main_sections.description: Grants any person aggrieved by registration the right to make representations against it, and the Government shall consider such representations.

main_sections.section_title: Power to restrict movements of registered offenders.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to order restrictions on the movements of registered offenders, specifying the area and duration of such restrictions, not exceeding three years.

main_sections.section_title: Power to cancel or alter restrictions of movements.
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to cancel or alter any order made under section 11.
Empowers the Government to notify any place as a corrective settlement for the treatment and training of habitual offenders.

main_sections.section_title: Power to direct habitual offenders to receive corrective training.
main_sections.description: Grants the Government or District Magistrate power to direct habitual offenders to receive corrective training in a corrective settlement.

main_sections.section_title: Power to transfer from corrective settlement.
main_sections.description: Allows for the transfer of habitual offenders from one corrective settlement to another.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for failure to comply with certain provisions of the Act.
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for failure to comply with provisions of the Act, including imprisonment and fines.

main_sections.section_title: Arrest of persons found outside restriction area or corrective settlement.
main_sections.description: Authorizes the arrest of persons found outside their restricted area or who escape from a corrective settlement.
Bars courts from questioning the validity of any direction or order issued under the Act.
Prohibits legal proceedings against any person for anything done in good faith in pursuance of the Act.
Grants the Government the power to delegate its powers under the Act.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Repeals previous enactments and provides that anything done under those enactments shall be deemed to have been done under this Act.

important_rules: Registered offenders must notify change of residence and report themselves to the authorities.
Habitual offenders changing residence to another district must inform the District Magistrate of the new district.
Restrictions on movements of registered offenders cannot exceed three years.
Habitual offenders may be directed to receive corrective training in a corrective settlement.
Arrest is authorized for persons found outside their restricted area or who escape from a corrective settlement.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to two hundred rupees or both.
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees or both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: District Magistrate, Superintendent of Police, Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Registration, notification of changes, reporting, restrictions on movement, corrective training, arrest, legal proceedings.

rights: Right to make representations against registration, restriction of movement, or cancellation of registration.
Opportunity of being heard before registration, restriction, or cancellation.
Right to furnish information against registration.
duties: Habitual offenders must furnish information for registration.
Registered offenders must notify change of residence and report themselves.
Persons convicted of scheduled offences are subject to the Act.
obligations: Obligation to comply with directions for registration and training.
Obligation to abide by restrictions on movement.

key_procedures: Procedure for preparing a register of habitual offenders, including notification and opportunity to be heard.
Procedure for notifying change of residence to another district.
Procedure for directing habitual offenders to receive corrective training.
Procedure for arrest of persons found outside restriction areas or who escape from corrective settlements.
administration: Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act defines 'habitual offender' based on a pattern of convictions for specified offences over a five-year period.
The validity of directions or orders made under the Act cannot be questioned in any court.
No legal proceedings can be initiated against persons acting in good faith under the Act.
The Government has the power to delegate its functions and make rules.

title: The Kerala Hackney Carriage Act, 1963
purpose: To unify and amend the law relating to the regulation of Hackney Carriages in the State of Kerala.
scope: This Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force in the whole of the State of Kerala at once. However, certain sections come into force in specific areas and at different dates as may be notified by the Government.

key_definitions.Director: Means in relation to any area within the jurisdiction of a Municipal Corporation or any area comprised in a Municipality or Township, the Director appointed under clause (13) of section 3 of the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960 (Act 14 of 1960) and in relation to any Panchayat area the Director appointed under clause (7) of section 2 of the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960 (Act 32 of 1960).
key_definitions.driving: Includes drawing, pushing or propelling, and driver includes any person who drives, draws, pushes or propels any hackney carriage.
key_definitions.executive authority: Means, in the case of a Municipal Corporation or Municipal Council, the Commissioner of the Corporation or Council, as the case may be; in the case of a Panchayat, the executive authority of the Panchayat; and in the case of a Township, the executive officer of the Township Committee.
key_definitions.hackerney carriage: Means any wheeled vehicle drawn, pushed or propelled by a man, or drawn by horse, bullock or other animal and used for the conveyance of any person or goods and which stands or plies for hire by the hour or day or according to distance, and includes a rickshaw.
key_definitions.local authority: Means (a) in any City, the Corporation of that City; (b) in any Municipal area, the Municipal council concerned; (c) in any Panchayat area, the Panchayat concerned; and (d) in any Township, the Township Committee concerned.
key_definitions.Magistrate: Means any magistrate having local jurisdiction in any area to which this Act extends.
key_definitions.minor: Means any person who has not completed the age of eighteen years.
key_definitions.registering authority: Means the executive authority of the local authority concerned or any other person appointed by name or by virtue of his office by the Government for registering hackney carriages within a particular area.
key_definitions.rickshaw: Means a two-wheeled vehicle or a tri-cycle of special type drawn or propelled by a person and includes a cycle-rickshaw.
key_definitions.year of registration: Means the year ending with the 31st day of March.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Kerala Hackney Carriage Act, 1963'. It states that the Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force at once, with provisions for different sections to come into force in different areas and at different times.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Director', 'driving', 'executive authority', 'hackney carriage', 'horse', 'local authority', 'Magistrate', 'minor', 'registering authority', 'rickshaw', and 'year of registration'.
States that nothing in this Act shall apply to a hackney carriage owned by the Government or a local authority.
Mandates annual registration for all hackney carriages.
Details the process for applying for registration of a hackney carriage, including submitting the vehicle for inspection.
Describes the process by which the registering authority shall grant a carriage licence upon payment of the prescribed fee.
Specifies the fees for various types of hackney carriages and other related services.

main_sections.section_title: Fee for certified copy of register or licence.
main_sections.description: Specifies the fee for obtaining a certified copy of the registration or licence.

main_sections.section_title: Suspension of licence by Registering Authority.
main_sections.description: Empowers the registering authority to suspend a licence if they deem it fit, under certain conditions.
Details the procedure for transferring the registry of a hackney carriage.

main_sections.section_title: Notice of change of residence, etc., to be given by licensee.
main_sections.description: Obliges licensees to provide notice of any change of residence to the registering authority.

main_sections.section_title: Transfers and change of residence to be registered.
main_sections.description: Mandates registration of transfers and changes of residence with the registering authority.
Provides for an appeal against any order of the registering authority under this Act.
Requires hackney carriages to be numbered conspicuously. It also outlines penalties for tampering with or losing the number plate.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for plying for hire without plate or inscription.
main_sections.description: Imposes a penalty on hackney carriages operating without a valid plate or inscription.
Details the process and requirements for obtaining a driver's licence.

main_sections.section_title: Particulars of licence to be registered.
main_sections.description: Specifies that particulars of driver's licences shall be entered in a register.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for driving without licence or lending licence.
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for driving without a licence or lending a licence.

main_sections.section_title: Suspension of licence by registering authority.
main_sections.description: Allows the registering authority to suspend a driver's licence under certain circumstances.
Provides for an appeal against the suspension or cancellation of a driver's licence.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for suffering unlicensed person to drive.
main_sections.description: Penalizes owners who allow unlicensed individuals to drive their hackney carriages.
Requires drivers to be furnished with a badge upon the grant of a licence.

main_sections.section_title: Return of expired licence and badge.
main_sections.description: Mandates the return of expired licences and badges.
Imposes penalties for the use of counterfeit badges.

main_sections.section_title: Seizure of expired or counterfeit badge.
main_sections.description: Empowers authorities to seize expired or counterfeit badges.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for failure to produce licence before Magistrate.
main_sections.description: Penalizes drivers who fail to produce their licence before a Magistrate when required.

main_sections.section_title: Convictions under Act to be endorsed on licence.
main_sections.description: Requires convictions under the Act to be endorsed on the driver's licence.

main_sections.section_title: Cancellation or suspension of licence on conviction.
main_sections.description: Allows for cancellation or suspension of a licence upon conviction.

main_sections.section_title: Maximum fares for use of hackney carriages.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to fix maximum fares for hackney carriages.
Declares contracts for fares higher than the maximum prescribed to be invalid.

main_sections.section_title: Publication of authorised fares and distances.
main_sections.description: Requires authorized fares and distances to be published.

main_sections.section_title: The maximum distance to which the driver is bound to drive.
main_sections.description: Defines the maximum distance a driver is obliged to travel.

main_sections.section_title: Quantity of luggage to be carried.
main_sections.description: Regulates the quantity of luggage that can be carried.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for refusing to let hackney carriage for hire.
main_sections.description: Penalizes drivers for refusing to let their hackney carriage for hire.

main_sections.section_title: Penalties for various offences by driver.
main_sections.description: Outlines penalties for various offenses committed by drivers.

main_sections.section_title: Requisition to owner to furnish address of absent driver.
main_sections.description: Requires owners to provide the address of absent drivers.
Contains special provisions pertaining to rickshaws.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure in case of disputes between hirer and driver.
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure to be followed in case of disputes between the hirer and the driver.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure in case of refusal to pay fare.
main_sections.description: Details the procedure to be followed when a passenger refuses to pay the fare.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for defacing or destroying plate, badge, or table of fares.
main_sections.description: Imposes penalties for defacing or destroying the carriage plate, badge, or fare table.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for wilful damage to hackney carriage.
main_sections.description: Penalizes wilful damage to a hackney carriage.
Provides for the establishment and regulation of hackney carriage stands.

main_sections.section_title: Deposit with registering authority or Police Officer of property left in hackney carriage.
main_sections.description: Requires lost property found in hackney carriages to be deposited with the registering authority or a police officer.

main_sections.section_title: The registering authority or Police Officer to register particulars of property deposited and grant receipt.
main_sections.description: Details the procedure for registering lost property and issuing receipts.
Deals with the exparte disposal of criminal charges.
Imposes limitations on criminal proceedings.
Provides for compensation in cases of frivolous prosecution.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to make special rules.
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to make special rules.
Empowers local authorities to make bye-laws.
Prescribes penalties for the breach of bye-laws.
Allows for the delegation of the registering authority's functions.
Contains provisions for the repeal of previous laws and saving clauses.

important_rules: Annual registration of every hackney carriage is compulsory.
Hackney carriages must be registered with the registering authority.
Drivers must obtain a licence to drive a hackney carriage.
Drivers must wear their badge when driving.
Fares must not exceed the maximum prescribed by the Government.
Lost property found in hackney carriages must be deposited with the registering authority or police.
Local authorities have the power to make bye-laws for the regulation of hackney carriages.

penalties: Penalty for plying for hire without plate or inscription: liable to a fine not exceeding twenty rupees.
Penalty for wilful damage to hackney carriage: liable to a fine not exceeding twenty rupees.
Penalty for defacing or destroying plate, badge, or table of fares: liable to a fine not exceeding fifty rupees.
Penalty for driving without licence or lending licence: liable to a fine not exceeding twenty rupees.
Penalty for suffering unlicensed person to drive: liable to a fine not exceeding fifty rupees.
Penalty for using counterfeit badge: liable to a fine not exceeding ten rupees.
Penalty for failure to produce licence before Magistrate: liable to a fine not exceeding twenty rupees.
Penalty for various offences by driver: liable to a fine not exceeding fifty rupees.
Penalty for breach of bye-laws: as may be prescribed by the bye-laws.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Registering authority, Police officers, and Magistrates.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through imposition of fines, suspension or cancellation of licences, seizure of badges, and prosecution for various offences.

rights: Right to obtain a licence if the applicant is not a minor and is fit for public use (for hackney carriages).
Right to appeal against orders of the registering authority.
Right to receive a receipt for lost property deposited.
duties: Duty to get hackney carriages registered annually.
Duty to obtain a driver's licence.
Duty to wear the driver's badge.
Duty to inform the registering authority of change of residence.
Duty to produce licence upon demand by the registering authority or police.
Duty to deposit lost property with the registering authority or police.
Duty of owners to furnish address of absent drivers.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act and any rules or bye-laws made thereunder.
Obligation not to charge fares exceeding the prescribed maximum.
Obligation to display number plates and inscriptions on hackney carriages.

key_procedures: Application for registration of a hackney carriage and the subsequent inspection and grant of licence.
Application for a driver's licence, including requirements and the grant of the licence and badge.
Procedure for appeal against orders of the registering authority.
Procedure for depositing and claiming lost property found in hackney carriages.
Procedure for handling disputes between hirers and drivers.
Procedure for dealing with refusal to pay fares.
administration: The administration of this Act appears to be primarily vested in the 'Registering Authority' which is defined in relation to local authorities (Municipal Corporations, Municipalities, Panchayats, Townships) and potentially a state-level 'Director'. The Government also has powers to make special rules.
important_notes: This Act does not apply to hackney carriages owned by the Government or local authorities.
The Act came into force on different dates for different sections and areas within the State of Kerala.
The definition of 'hackney carriage' is broad and includes rickshaws.
Convictions under the Act are endorsed on the driver's licence, which can lead to cancellation or suspension.
The Government has the power to make special rules and fix maximum fares.

title: The Kerala Handloom Workers Welfare Cess Act, 2007
purpose: To provide for the levy and collection of cess on the sale proceeds of yarn, textile or textile products with a view to augmenting the resources of the Kerala Handloom Workers' Welfare Fund Board constituted under the Kerala Handloom Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 1989.
scope: Applies to dealers in yarn, textile, or textile products within the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Assessing Officer: An Officer appointed by the Government under section 4.
key_definitions.Board: The Kerala Handloom Workers' Welfare Fund Board constituted under section 6 of the Kerala Handloom Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 1989.
key_definitions.dealer: Any person who carries on the business of manufacturing, selling, processing, supplying, purchasing or storing for sale of yarn, textile or textile products.
key_definitions.fund: Kerala Handloom Workers' Welfare Fund.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.sale proceeds: The value of buying and selling of yarn, textile or textile products in the State of Kerala, for sale or to process otherwise.
key_definitions.textile: Means any cloth-woven in handloom or powerloom (including textile mills) or any other looms out of cotton yarn, polyester yarn, silk yarn or any other yarn (blended or otherwise), but does not include khadi products.
key_definitions.textile products: Means any garment or other articles manufactured by using cloth as basic component.
key_definitions.yarn: Means cotton yarn, polyester fibre, silk yarn or any other blended fibre which can be used for weaving cloth.

main_sections.description: Names the act as the Kerala Handloom Workers' Welfare Cess Act, 2007, and states its commencement on a date notified by the Government.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including Assessing Officer, Board, dealer, fund, Government, prescribed, sale proceeds, textile, textile products, and yarn.

Specifies that cess shall be levied and collected at the rate of a quarter per cent of the total sale proceeds of yarn, textile or textile products, with provisions for exemption for dealers whose sale proceeds are less than five lakh rupees for a year.
Empowers the Government to appoint Assessing Officers, not below the rank of Assistant Labour Officer or Officers of equal status, to determine the jurisdiction of their assessments.

Mandates every dealer to maintain such registers and records in their commercial establishment as may be prescribed, and these must be produced for verification upon demand by any Officer or authority.

main_sections.section_title: Furnishing of Returns by the Dealer
main_sections.description: Requires every dealer to furnish a return showing the sale proceeds of the previous financial year to the Assessing Officer in such manner and at such time as may be prescribed. It also outlines the procedure if a dealer fails to furnish the return.
Details the process for the Assessing Officer to assess the cess payable by the dealer based on the return furnished or after making an enquiry.

Allows for the provisional collection of cess by way of advance cess on or before the 10th of every month, equivalent to one-twelfth of the amount annually payable according to the latest assessment under section 7. It also outlines procedures for issuing notices for default.

main_sections.section_title: Interest payable on delay in payment of Cess
main_sections.description: Specifies that if a dealer fails to pay any amount of cess payable within the time specified, interest at the rate of one per cent per month or part thereof, comprising the period from the date on which such payment is due till such amount is actually paid, will be payable.

main_sections.section_title: Fine for Non-payment of cess within the specified time
main_sections.description: States that if any amount of cess payable by any dealer under section 3 is not paid within the specified time, the dealer shall be deemed to be in arrears and the Assessing Officer may, after making such enquiry as deemed fit, impose a fine not exceeding the amount of cess.

main_sections.section_title: Recovery of amount due under this Act
main_sections.description: Empowers the recovery of any amount due under the Act, including any interest or penalty, in the same manner as an arrear of land revenue.

Allows for appeals against an order of assessment or an order imposing a fine under section 10. It outlines the procedure for appeals, including the authority to whom the appeal is preferred and the process for hearing the appeal.

Grants any Assessing Officer or other officer empowered by the Government the authority to enter any establishment, with or without assistance, to inspect and verify the correctness of particulars furnished by any dealer, require the production of any register or document, and exercise other powers as may be prescribed.

Requires every Assessing Officer to furnish, every month, a return showing the amount of cess collected by him to the Board or other authority as directed. The Chief Executive Officer of the Board or the specified authority shall also furnish a return to the Government.
Specifies penalties for dealers who fail to furnish a return, or wilfully evade or attempt to evade the payment of cess. Penalties can include imprisonment and fines.

Deals with offences committed by companies, making every person responsible for the conduct of the business of the company liable to be proceeded against and punished. It also defines 'company' and 'director' for the purposes of this section.

main_sections.section_title: Bar of Jurisdiction of Civil Courts
main_sections.description: Prohibits Civil Courts from having jurisdiction to settle, decide or deal with any question or to determine any matter which is by or under this Act or the rules required to be settled, decided or dealt with by the Government or any authority or Officer appointed under this Act.

Empowers the Government to make rules by notification in the Gazette for carrying out the provisions of the Act. These rules can cover various aspects including the manner and time of levying and collecting cess, maintenance of registers, furnishing of returns, appeals, and other matters.

Repeals the Kerala Handloom Workers' Welfare Cess Ordinance, 2007, and states that anything done or any action taken under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Dealers must furnish returns showing sale proceeds to the Assessing Officer as prescribed.
Assessing Officers have the power to assess cess payable by dealers.
Interest is payable on delayed payment of cess.
The Government can make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act.

penalties: Failure to furnish return: Punishable with imprisonment up to six months or with fine up to five thousand rupees or both.
Wilful evasion or attempt to evade cess payment: Punishable with imprisonment up to six months or with fine up to five thousand rupees or both.
Contravention of provisions: Punishable with imprisonment for a term up to three months or with fine up to two thousand five hundred rupees or both.
Offences by companies: Liable for punishment as per section 16.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Assessing Officers, Government, and other officers empowered by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment of cess, recovery of amounts due, imposition of penalties and fines, and legal proceedings for offences. Civil Courts are barred from jurisdiction.

rights: Dealers have the right to appeal against orders of assessment or penalty.
Dealers have the right to be given a reasonable opportunity of being heard before penalties are imposed.
duties: Dealers have the duty to furnish returns.
Dealers have the duty to pay cess and interest on delayed payments.
Dealers have the duty to maintain registers and records.
Dealers have the duty to produce registers and records for verification.
obligations: Obligation to pay cess on sale proceeds of yarn, textile, or textile products.

key_procedures: Furnishing of returns by dealers: Dealers must submit returns detailing sale proceeds within a prescribed time.
Assessment of cess: The Assessing Officer assesses the cess payable based on the furnished return or after an enquiry.
Provisional collection of cess: Advance cess can be collected monthly.
Appeal process: Dealers can appeal against assessment or penalty orders to prescribed authorities.
Power of entry and inspection: Authorized officers can enter premises to inspect records and verify compliance.
administration: The Kerala Handloom Workers' Welfare Fund Board and officers appointed by the Government (e.g., Assessing Officers).
important_notes: Cess is not levied on sale proceeds of less than five lakh rupees for a year.
The Act repeals the Kerala Handloom Workers' Welfare Cess Ordinance, 2007.

title: The Kerala Handloom Workers Welfare Fund Amendment Act, 2008
purpose: To amend The Kerala Handloom Workers Welfare Fund Act, 1987.
scope: Applicable to handloom workers in Kerala.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it comes into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 2 of Act 14 of 1987
main_sections.description: Amends Section 2 of the principal Act (The Kerala Handloom Workers Welfare Fund Act, 1987) by inserting a new clause (ii-a) to define "Fund" as the Kerala Handloom Workers Welfare Fund established under Section 3.
Inserts a new Section 2-A titled 'Power to make rules'. It states that the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.

Amends Section 58 of the principal Act by substituting certain phrases relating to the administration and management of the Fund. It clarifies that the Fund shall be administered and managed by the Board constituted under the Act.

Inserts a new Section 62-A titled 'Power to remove difficulties'. It empowers the Government to make provisions not inconsistent with the Act, for the purpose of removing any difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act, for a period of two years from the commencement of this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through rules made by the Government and by the provisions for removing difficulties.

key_procedures: The Government may make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act by notification in the Gazette.
The Government has the power to remove difficulties in implementing the Act for a period of two years.
administration: The Board constituted under the Act
important_notes: The Act specifies that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Government via notification.
The power to remove difficulties is limited to a period of two years from the commencement of the Act.

title: THE KERALA HANDLOOM WORKERS' WELFARE FUND (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2008
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Handloom Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 1989, for the purposes hereinafter appearing. Specifically, to provide for a special provision for giving pension to handloom workers who happened to be retired at the age of 58 years.
scope: Applies to handloom workers in Kerala who are eligible for pension and were retired at the age of 58 years.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Handloom Workers' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2008 and it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 16th day of January, 2008.

Amends Section 3 of the Kerala Handloom Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 1989 by substituting 'sixty years' with 'fifty-eight years' in two instances within the section, effectively lowering the age limit for a particular provision.

Amends Section 5 of the principal Act, after the word "scheme", the words "either prospectively or retrospectively" shall be inserted. This likely allows for amendments to be applied either from the date of the amendment or from an earlier date.

main_sections.section_title: Special provision for giving pension to the handloom workers who happened to be retired at the age of 58 years
main_sections.description: Notwithstanding anything contained in the principal Act, handloom workers who were retired at the age of 58 years by any reasons, shall have eligibility for pension but they have no eligibility for pension arrears.

Repeals The Kerala Handloom Workers' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Ordinance, 2008 (24 of 2008). It also states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the said Ordinance, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Handloom workers who retired at the age of 58 years are eligible for pension.
Eligibility for pension for those retired at 58 years is to be applied from January 16, 2008.
No pension arrears are payable to those retired at 58 years.
Amendments related to the 'scheme' can be applied prospectively or retrospectively.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided sections, but likely the relevant government department or authority responsible for the Handloom Workers' Welfare Fund.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided sections.

rights: Right to pension for handloom workers retired at the age of 58 years.

key_procedures: To amend the Kerala Handloom Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 1989.
To provide for pension eligibility for handloom workers retired at 58 years.
To repeal the Amendment Ordinance and ensure continuity of actions taken under it.
administration: The administration of the Handloom Workers' Welfare Fund would likely fall under a government department related to industries or handlooms in Kerala.
important_notes: The Act is retrospective in its commencement, coming into force on January 16, 2008.
Received the assent of Governor on 26th December 2008 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No 2745 dated 29th December 2008.
Pension eligibility for those retired at 58 is a special provision and does not include pension arrears.

title: THE KERALA HEADLOAD WORKERS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2013
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Headload Workers' Act, 1978.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Headload Workers' Act, 1978.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Headload Workers' (Amendment) Act, 2013. Sections 3 and 4 of this Act shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of January, 2009 and the remaining sections shall be deemed to have come into force on the 14th day of June, 2010.

In section 2 of the principal Act, for clause (k), the following clause shall be substituted: "(k) "family" means,-- (i) husband; (ii) wife; (iii) minor children; including legally adopted children; (iv) mentally challenged children; (v) dependent parents; (vi) unmarried or widowed daughters who are dependent; (vii) physically challenged children who are dependent; and (viii) wholly dependent unmarried sisters."

In section 13 of the principal Act, after clause (b) of sub-section (2), the following clause shall be inserted, namely: -- "(bb) for providing benefits under the Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948 (Central Act 34 of 1948) to headload workers."

In section 24 of the principal Act, -- (a) for the words "Workmen's Compensation" occurring in the marginal heading and in the opening sentence, the words "Employees Compensation" shall be substituted; (b) for the word "workmen", the word "employees" shall be substituted; (c) to the existing provision, the following proviso shall be added, namely: -- "Provided that the Employees Compensation Act, 1923 (Central Act 8 of 1923) shall not apply to the headload workers insured under the Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948 (Central Act 34 of 1948)."
In section 37 of the principal Act, for the word "Government", the word "Board" shall be substituted.

The Kerala Headload Workers' (Amendment) Ordinance, 2013 (12 of 2013) is hereby repealed. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

scope: This Act applies to the State of Kerala and concerns headload workers, Advisory Committees, and the revenue districts within the state.

key_definitions.Convenor: In sub-sections (5) and (6), 'Convenor' refers to the 'District Secretary' or the 'Special Area Secretary' as the case may be.
key_definitions.District Secretary: Referred to as 'Convenor' in certain contexts.
key_definitions.Special Area Secretary: Referred to as 'Convenor' in certain contexts.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Headload Workers' (Second Amendment) Act, 2008, and it came into force on the 18th day of April, 2008.

Substitutes sub-section (1) of Section 18 of the principal Act, empowering the Government to appoint Special Committees for every revenue district, and provides for the cessation of jurisdiction of committees upon the appointment of a new committee.

Inserts a new section 19A, titled 'Appointment of Advisory Committees'. This section outlines the composition and functions of Advisory Committees, including the number of members, representation of employers and headload workers, and the role of the Board and its officers.

main_sections.section_title: Special provision for dissolving the existing Committee
main_sections.description: Provides for the reconstitution of Committees by the Government, in accordance with section 18 of the principal Act, as amended by this Ordinance. It states that upon the commencement of this Act, all existing Committees constituted prior to its date of commencement shall be dissolved, and their powers and functions transferred to the reconstituted Committees.

Repeals the Kerala Headload Workers' (Amendment) Ordinance, 2008 (26 of 2008). It also includes a saving clause stating that the repeal shall not affect any action taken or deemed to have been taken or any right or liability accrued under the principal Act, as amended by the said Ordinance.

important_rules: The Government, by notification in the Gazette, shall appoint a Committee for every revenue district and on the recommendation of the Board, shall appoint as many Special Committees as they deem fit in any area falling within any industrial township or other special areas of importance in the State, to be known by such name as may be specified in the notification for the purpose of exercising the powers and performing the function of the Committee under the Act and the Scheme in relation to that area.
The term of office of the members of the Advisory Committee and the conduct of business of the Advisory Committee shall be such as may be decided by the Board from time to time.
All existing Committees constituted prior to the date of commencement of this Act shall be dissolved.

title: The Kerala Headload Workers Act, 1978
purpose: To regulate the employment of headload workers in the State of Kerala and to make provision for their welfare, for the settlement of disputes in respect of their employment or non-employment and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to the employment of headload workers in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.adolescent: A person who has completed his fifteenth year of age but has not completed his eighteenth year of age.
key_definitions.adult: A person who has completed his eighteenth year of age.
key_definitions.appellate authority: In relation to any area, means the appellate authority under section 4.
key_definitions.conciliation officer: In relation to any area, means the Conciliation Officer appointed under section 3.
key_definitions.contractor: In relation to an establishment, means a person who undertakes any work for such establishment by engaging headload workers on hire or otherwise, or who supplies headload workers as individuals or in groups for the purpose of engaging them in such establishment and includes a sub-contractor and a broker.
key_definitions.dispute: Any dispute or difference between employers and employees or between employers and headload workers, or between headload workers and headload workers, which is connected with the employment or non-employment or the terms of employment or the conditions of employment, of any headload workers.
key_definitions.employer: In relation to a headload worker engaged by or through a contractor, the principal employer; in relation to a headload worker who is not employed by any employer or contractor, the committee constituted under section 18; and in relation to any other headload worker, the person who has ultimate control over the affairs of the establishment in or for which the headload worker is employed and includes any other person to whom the affairs of such establishment are entrusted, whether such person is called an agent, manager or by any other name prevailing in such establishment.
key_definitions.establishment: Means an establishment specified in the Schedule and includes the precincts thereof.
key_definitions.family: Means husband, wife, dependent parents, minor children and unmarried or widowed daughters.
key_definitions.fund: Means a fund constituted under a scheme.
key_definitions.headload worker: Means a person engaged directly or through a contractor in or for an establishment, whether for wages or not, for loading or unloading or carrying on head or person or in a trolly any article or articles in or from or to a vehicle or any place in such establishment, and includes any person not employed by any employer or contractor but engaged in the loading or unloading or carrying on head or person or in a trolly any article or articles for wages, but does not include a person engaged by an individual for domestic purposes.
key_definitions.minor: Means a person who has not completed his fifteen year of age or who has not completed his fifteen year of age.
