key_definitions.principal employer: Means an employer who engages a headload worker by or through a contractor in an establishment.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.scheme: A scheme made under this Act.
key_definitions.wages: Means all remuneration, whether payable in cash or in kind, which would, the terms of employment express or implied, were fulfilled, be payable to a headload worker employed in an establishment or for work done in such establishment, but does not include— (i) the value of— (A) any house accommodation, supply of light, water or medical attendance or; (B) any other amenity or service excluded by general or special order of the Government; or (ii) any contribution paid by the employer to any pension fund or any scheme of social insurance and the interest which may have accrued thereon; or (iii) any travelling allowance or value af any travelling concession. or (iv) any sum paid to a headload worker to defray special expenses entailed on him by the nature of his employment; (v) any gratuity payable on discharge; (vi) any bonus.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Headload Workers Act, 1978. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different areas and for different provisions of this Act and for different establishments.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'adolescent', 'adult', 'appellate authority', 'board', 'committee', 'conciliation officer', 'contractor', 'dispute', 'employer', 'establishment', 'family', 'fund', 'headload worker', 'inspector', 'minor', 'principal employer', 'prescribed', 'scheme', and 'wages'.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Conciliation Officers, Appellate authorities.
main_sections.description: The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint, for any area specified therein any officer of the Labour Department not below the rank of Deputy Labour Officer to be a Conciliation Officer for the purpose of performing the functions entrusted to the Conciliation Officer by or under this Act.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint for any area specified therein an officer of the Labour Department not below the rank of District Labour Officer to be an appellate authority for the purpose of performing the functions of the appellate authority under this Act.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint, such officers, or such persons as possess the prescribed qualifications, as they think fit, to be Inspectors for the purposes of this Act and define the local limits within which they shall exercise their powers. Subject to any rules made in this behalf, an Inspector may, within the local limits for which he is appointed: (a) enter, with such assistance, if any, as he thinks fit, any establishment or place, or public authority, as he thinks fit, any establishment wherein headload workers are employed or wherefrom work is given out to headload workers, for the purpose of examining any register, record of wages or notices required to be kept or exhibited under any scheme or rule made under this Act and require the production thereof either on the spot or in the office of the Inspector. Provided that the Inspector shall not enter any establishment at any time between 7 p. m. and 7 a. m. except when work is being carried on in such establishment; (b) examine any person found in any such establishment, if he has reasonable cause to believe that such person is a headload worker employed therein or to whom work is given from; (c) require any person giving any work to a headload worker or a group of headload workers to give any information, which is in his power to give, in respect of the name and address of the persons to whom the work is given and in respect of payments made or to be made for the said work; (d) seize or take copies of such registers, records of wages or notices or portions thereof, as he may consider relevant in respect of an offence under this Act or any scheme or rule made thereunder which he has reason to believe has been committed by an employer; and (e) exercise such other powers as may be prescribed. Every employer shall afford all reasonable facilities for making an entry, inspection, examination or inquiry under this Act.

No adult headload worker shall be required to work for more than eight hours in any day and no adolescent or minor headload worker shall be required to work for more than six hours in any day. Provided that nothing contained in this section shall be deemed to prohibit an agreement between the employer and the headload workers for working for less than eight hours or six hours, as the case may be, on any particular day or days on all days of employment or to affect any custom or practice prevailing in the locality under which the headload worker is required to work for less than eight hours or six hours, as the case may be.
No headload worker shall be required to carry on his head or person at any time any article or articles weighing more than seventy-five kilograms.

The period of work on each day shall be so fixed that no period shall exceed three hours of continuous work and no headload worker shall work for more than three hours continuously before he has had an interval for rest of at least half an hour.
Every employer shall pay to any headload workers employed by him such wages as may be prescribed; and different wages may be prescribed for different establishments and for different kinds of work.

main_sections.section_title: Wages for work between 7 p. m. and 7 a. m.
main_sections.description: Where a headload worker is required by an employer to work at any time between 7 p. m. and 7 a. m. he shall be paid for such work one and a half times the wages payable to him under section 9.

If any employer pays less than the wages due to a headload worker or refuses to pay such wages, the headload worker or an official of the union of which he is a member may make an application to the Conciliation Officer for a direction under subsection (2). On receipt of an application under subsection (1), the Conciliation Officer shall, after giving the applicant and the employer an opportunity of being heard and after such inquiry, if any, which he may consider necessary, direct— (a) in the case of a claim arising out of the payment of less than the wages, the payment to the headload worker of the amount by which the wages payable to him exceeds the amount actually paid by the employer; (b) in the case of a claim arising out of non-payment of wages, the payment of wages due to the headload worker. If, as a result of a direction under subsection (2), any amount of the wages becomes payable to a headload worker, the Conciliation Officer shall, if the amount is not paid in accordance with such direction, make a report to the Collector specifying the full particulars regarding the amount of wages due to the headload worker, and on receipt of such report the Collector shall proceed to recover the same from the employer as if it were an arrear of public revenue due on land. Explanation.—In this section and section 36, “Collector” means the District Collector or any other officer appointed by the Government to exercise the powers and perform the functions of a Collector under the Kerala Revenue Recovery Act, 1968 (15 of 1968).

Against any order passed by a Conciliation Officer under section 11, an appeal shall lie to the appellate authority within a period of thirty days from the date of the order appealed against, and the decision of the appellate authority on such appeal shall be final. Provided that the appellate authority may admit an appeal presented after the expiration of the said period of thirty days if it is satisfied that the appellant had sufficient cause for not presenting the appeal within that period. The appellate authority shall have no power to stay the operation of the order of the Conciliation Officer pending disposal of the appeal, except for good and sufficient reasons to be recorded in writing.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make one or more scheme or schemes for any employment or group of employments in one or more area specified therein. Provided that no such notification shall come into force, unless a draft thereof has been published in the Gazette and unless it is finalised after considering objections or suggestions received within one month of the publication of such draft in the Gazette. The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, add to the Schedule any establishment in respect of the headload workers whereof the opinion of the Government that the establishment should be made under this Act, and thereupon the establishment so added shall be deemed to be an establishment specified in the Schedule for the purposes of this Act. Every notification under subsection (1) shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is issued, before the Legislative Assembly, while it is in session for a total period of fourteen days which may be comprised in one session or in two successive sessions, and if, before the expiry of the session in which it is so laid or the session immediately following, the Legislative Assembly makes any modification in the notification or decides that the notification should not be issued, the notification shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect, as the case may be; so however that any such modification or annulment shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that notification.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, by notification in the Gazette, by name as specified in the notification for the purpose of exercising the powers and performing the functions of the Board under this Act and the schemes. The Board shall be a body corporate by the name specified, having perpetual succession and a common seal, with power to acquire, hold and dispose of property and to contract and may, by that name, sue and be sued. The Board shall consist of members nominated from time to time by the Government representing the employers, the headload workers and the Government.

important_rules: Adult headload workers shall not be required to work for more than eight hours in any day.
Adolescent or minor headload workers shall not be required to work for more than six hours in any day.
No headload worker shall be required to carry on his head or person at any time any article or articles weighing more than seventy-five kilograms.

The period of work on each day shall be fixed so that no period shall exceed three hours of continuous work, and no headload worker shall work for more than three hours continuously before having an interval for rest of at least half an hour.
Wages for work between 7 p.m. and 7 a.m. shall be one and a half times the wages payable for work during normal hours.

penalties: Penalty for making false statements, etc.
Other penalties
Enhanced penalty after previous conviction.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Conciliation Officers, Appellate Authorities, Inspectors, Collector.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inquiries, directions for payment of wages, appeals, seizures of records, and recovery of dues as public revenue.

rights: Right to prescribed wages.
Right to intervals for rest.
Right to challenge incorrect wage payments or non-payment of wages.
Right to appeal against orders of Conciliation Officers.
duties: Employers must pay prescribed wages.
Employers must provide intervals for rest.
Employers must maintain registers and records.
Employers must afford reasonable facilities to Inspectors.
obligations: Obligation to follow scheme provisions.
Obligation to cooperate with Inspectors.

key_procedures: Application to Conciliation Officer for enforcement of wages: If an employer pays less than the wages due or refuses to pay, the headload worker or union official can apply to the Conciliation Officer.
Conciliation Officer's inquiry and direction: The Conciliation Officer hears both parties and may direct the employer to pay the correct wages.
Appeal against Conciliation Officer's order: An appeal can be filed with the appellate authority within thirty days.
Role of Collector in wage recovery: If wages are not paid as directed, the Collector can recover the amount as public revenue.
Establishment of schemes: The Government can make schemes for employment or group of employments in specified areas.
Appointment of Board members: The Government may constitute a Board with representatives of employers, headload workers, and the Government.
administration: Labour Department, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.
Different dates for commencement can be appointed for different areas and provisions.
The Act may be amended or substituted by schemes made under it.
The Government may add to the Schedule any establishment.
The validity of anything previously done under a notification shall not be prejudiced by its modification or annulment.

title: The Kerala Healthcare Service Persons and Healthcare Service Institutions (Prevention of Violence and Damage to Property) Act, 2012
purpose: To prohibit violence against healthcare service persons and to prevent damage and loss to property in healthcare service institutions and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to all healthcare service persons and healthcare service institutions in Kerala.

key_definitions.healthcare service institutions: Means all institutions providing healthcare to people which are under the control of the State or the Central Government or Local Bodies etc; including any private hospital having facilities for treatment of the sick and used for their reception or stay; any private maternity home where women are usually received and accommodated for the purpose of confinement and ante-natal and post-natal care in connection with child birth or anything connected therewith; and any private nursing home used or intended to be used for the reception and accommodation of persons suffering from any sickness, injury or infirmity whether of body or mind and, providing treatment or nursing or both of them and include a maternity home, convalescent home, clinic, residence and consulting rooms of healthcare service persons;
key_definitions.healthcare service persons: Includes Registered Medical Practitioners, working in healthcare service institutions, including those having provisional registration; registered nurses; medical students; nursing students; para medical workers employed and working in medical service institutions; 'offender' means any person who, either by himself or as a member of a group of persons or organisations, commits or attempts to commit or abets or incites the commission of violence under this Act;
key_definitions.property: Means any property, movable or immovable or medical equipment owned by or in possession of or under the control of any healthcare service person or owned by or in possession of or under the control of any healthcare service institution;
key_definitions.violence: Means activities causing any harm, injury or endangering the life, intimidation, obstruction or hindrance, to any healthcare service person in discharge of duty in any healthcare service institution or damage or loss to property in healthcare service institutions.

main_sections.description: States the short title as The Kerala Healthcare Service Persons and Healthcare Service Institutions (Prevention of Violence and Damage to Property) Act, 2012 and that it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 26th day of August, 2010.
Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'healthcare service institutions', 'healthcare service persons', 'property', and 'violence'.
Prohibits acts of violence against healthcare service persons or damage or loss to property in a healthcare service institution.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty and other consequence for violation of section 3
main_sections.description: Outlines penalties for offenders, including imprisonment and fines. Also specifies compensation to the healthcare service institution for damaged property.

main_sections.section_title: Act to be in addition to and not in derogation of any other law
main_sections.description: Clarifies that the provisions of this Act are in addition to and not in derogation of other existing laws.

main_sections.section_title: Responsibility of healthcare service institutions to give complete information of medical treatment
main_sections.description: Requires healthcare service institutions to furnish complete information about medical treatment provided by them to their relatives.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act, which will be published in the Official Gazette.

Repeals The Kerala Healthcare Service Persons and Healthcare Service Institutions (Prevention of Violence and Damage to Property) Ordinance, 2012 (27 of 2012) and provides savings for actions taken under the Ordinance.

important_rules: Rule 1: Violence against healthcare service persons or damage to property in a healthcare service institution is prohibited.
Rule 2: Offenders committing violence or damage are liable to imprisonment and fines.
Rule 3: Healthcare service institutions must provide complete medical treatment information to relatives.
Rule 4: Government has the power to make rules to implement the Act.

penalties: Imprisonment for a period which may extend to three years and with fine which may extend to fifty thousand rupees (for contravention of section 3).
Liability to pay twice the amount of purchase price of medical equipment damaged (for contravention of section 3(2)).
Recovery of such amount as arrears of land revenue (if not paid as compensation).
Any offender committed during the period from 13th July, 2011 to 11th day of February, 2011, is liable to be convicted under this Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings as per the penalties outlined in the Act. Rules made by the Government under the Act will also guide enforcement.

rights: Right to be free from violence while discharging duties in a healthcare service institution.
Right to have property in healthcare service institutions protected from damage or loss.
duties: Duty of healthcare service persons to perform their duties without hindrance.
Duty of healthcare service institutions to provide complete medical information to relatives.
Duty of healthcare service institutions to ensure safety and security of their persons and property.
obligations: Obligation of offenders to face penalties as prescribed by the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Reporting acts of violence or damage to property to the authorities.
Procedure 2: Prosecution and conviction of offenders as per the Act's provisions.
Procedure 3: Compensation to healthcare service institutions for damaged property.
administration: Government of Kerala, Law (Legislation-II) Department
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force retrospectively from August 26, 2010.
The Act also covers actions taken under The Kerala Healthcare Service Persons and Healthcare Service Institutions (Prevention of Violence and Damage to Property) Ordinance, 2012.
The definition of 'violence' is broad and includes activities causing harm, injury, endangering life, intimidation, obstruction, or hindrance.

title: The Kerala Hereditary Village Offices (Abolition) Act, 1961
purpose: To abolish hereditary village offices and the emoluments appertaining thereto in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to hereditary village offices and holders of such offices in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.emoluments: Means money salaries and all other kinds of remuneration granted or continued in respect of, or annexed to, any hereditary village office.
key_definitions.existing law relating to a hereditary vi: Includes any enactment, rule, bye-law, regulation, order, notification, standing order or any other instrument or custom, usage or practice relating to a hereditary village office, which is in force immediately before the appointed date.
key_definitions.hereditary village office: Means a village office to which emoluments have been attached and which is held under any existing law relating to a hereditary village office or for the performance of duties connected with the administration or collection of the revenue or with the maintenance of order or with the settlement of boundaries or other matter of civil administration of a village, whether the services originally appertaining to the office continue, or have ceased, to be performed, and by whatsoever designation the office may be locally known.
key_definitions.holder of a hereditary village office: Means a person holding a hereditary village office permanently or officiating in a permanent vacancy after selection in accordance with the procedure in force immediately before the appointed date.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Hereditary Village Offices (Abolition) Act, 1961, and extends to the whole of the Malabar district referred to in sub-section (2) of section 3 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (Central Act 37 of 1956).

Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'appointed date', 'emoluments', 'existing law relating to a hereditary village office', 'hereditary village office', 'holder of a hereditary village office', and 'prescribed'.

main_sections.section_title: Abolition of hereditary village offices together with emoluments thereof.
main_sections.description: Declares that hereditary village offices and their emoluments shall cease to exist from the appointed date. It also states that the provisions of this section do not affect any obligation or liability already incurred or any proceeding or remedy in respect of such obligation or liability before the appointed date.

main_sections.section_title: Power of District Collector to decide whether a person was the holder of a hereditary village office and appeal therefrom.
main_sections.description: Grants the District Collector the power to decide whether a person was a holder of a hereditary village office before the appointed date. Appeals against such decisions can be made to the Board of Revenue.

main_sections.section_title: Relief to holders of village offices abolished under the Act.
main_sections.description: Provides relief to holders of village offices abolished under the Act, including the right to hold and receive emoluments, or any right to customary fees or perquisites. It also allows for the possibility of tendering service.

main_sections.section_title: Power to take evidence on oath, etc.
main_sections.description: Empowers the District Collector and the Board of Revenue to take evidence on oath, summon persons, require production of documents, and receive evidence on affidavit for the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Enquiries and proceedings to be judicial proceedings.
main_sections.description: States that all inquiries and proceedings before the District Collector or the Board of Revenue under the Act shall be deemed to be judicial proceedings within the meaning of sections 193, 219 and 228 of the Indian Penal Code.

Grants the Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, including rules for determining questions as to whether a person was a holder of a hereditary village office, procedure for appeals, qualifications and conditions for appointment, and principles for determining the gratuity payable. It also states that all rules made under this section shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly for a period not less than fourteen days.

Allows the Government to issue directions to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act. Such directions, if they appear to be inconsistent with the provisions, will be deemed to be part of the Act.

Repeals any existing law relating to hereditary village offices in force in the Malabar district. It also states that the repeal does not affect any obligation or liability already incurred or any proceeding or remedy in respect of such obligation or liability before the appointed date. It also repeals the Kerala Hereditary Village Offices (Abolition) Ordinance, 1961.

important_rules: Hereditary village offices and their emoluments are abolished from the appointed date (September 1, 1961).
Holders of abolished hereditary village offices are entitled to relief, which may include the right to hold and receive emoluments, customary fees, or perquisites.
Rules made under the Act must be laid before the Legislative Assembly for a period of not less than fourteen days and are subject to modification by the Assembly.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: District Collector and Board of Revenue
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inquiries, judicial proceedings, and the power to make rules.

rights: Holders of abolished hereditary village offices have a right to relief.
Persons aggrieved by the decision of the District Collector can appeal to the Board of Revenue.
obligations: Holders of hereditary village offices before the appointed date had certain obligations related to their office and the collection of revenue or maintenance of order.

key_procedures: Determination of holder status: District Collector decides if a person was a holder of a hereditary village office, with appeal to the Board of Revenue.
Relief application: Holders of abolished offices can seek relief based on prescribed rules.
Rule-making: Government makes rules for the Act's implementation, subject to legislative scrutiny.
Dispute resolution: Inquiries and proceedings are judicial proceedings.
administration: The Act is administered through the District Collector and the Board of Revenue, with powers vested in the Government to make rules and issue directions.
important_notes: The Act extends to the Malabar district.
The abolition of hereditary village offices does not affect obligations or liabilities incurred before the appointed date.
The Act repeals the Kerala Hereditary Village Offices (Abolition) Ordinance, 1961.

title: The Kerala High Court (Amendment) Act, 1987
purpose: To further amend the Kerala High Court Act, 1958, for the purpose hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala High Court Act, 1958. The scope of the amendment itself is limited to specific sections within the principal act.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala High Court (Amendment) Act, 1987, and it shall come into force at once.
Amends section 5 of the Kerala High Court Act, 1958 (5 of 1959) by omitting the word "or" at the end of clause (ii) and by omitting clause (iii).

administration: Law (Legislation-B) Department, Government of Kerala

title: The Kerala High Court (Amendment) Act, 1989
purpose: To further amend the Kerala High Court Act, 1958.
scope: Applies to the Kerala High Court.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala High Court (Amendment) Act, 1989 and it shall come into force at once.
Amends section 3 of the Kerala High Court Act, 1958 (5 of 1959). Specifically, in sub-clause (b) of clause (13), the words "ten thousand rupees" shall be substituted with "one lakh rupees".

important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 28th day of August 1989 and published in the Kerala Gazette extraordinary No. 811 dated the 29th August 1989.

title: THE KERALA HIGH COURT (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1966
purpose: An Act to amend the Kerala High Court Act, 1958.
scope: Applies to the High Court of Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala High Court (Amendment) Act, 1966, and it shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Amends section 3 of the Kerala High Court Act, 1958 (Kerala Act 5 of 1959). It substitutes a new clause for clause (13), which is related to the principal Act for sub-clause (i).

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 5
main_sections.description: Substitutes a new section for section 5 of the principal Act. This new section deals with appeals from judgments or orders of a Single Judge.

important_rules: Appeals lie to a Bench of two Judges from a judgment or order of a Single Judge in the exercise of original jurisdiction.

Appeals lie to a Bench of two Judges from a judgment of a Single Judge in the exercise of appellate jurisdiction in respect of a decree or order made in the exercise of original jurisdiction by a subordinate court.

Appeals lie to a Bench of two Judges from a judgment of a Single Judge in the exercise of appellate jurisdiction in respect of a decree or order made in the exercise of appellate jurisdiction by a subordinate court, if the Judge who passed such judgment certifies that the case is a fit one for appeal.

rights: Right to appeal from a judgment or order of a Single Judge to a Bench of two Judges under certain conditions.

key_procedures: Appeals from a Single Judge's judgment or order to a Bench of two Judges are outlined, specifying the types of judgments/orders eligible for appeal and the conditions under which appeals are permitted.
important_notes: The amendments are made in the exercise of powers conferred by section 3 of the Kerala State Legislature (Delegation of Powers) Act, 1965.
The Act was enacted by the President in the seventeenth year of the Republic of India.
Published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 68, dated 16th July, 1966.

title: The Kerala High Court Services (Determination of Retirement Age) Act, 2008
purpose: To determine the retirement age of certain High Court service personnel in Kerala.
scope: Applies to the Kerala High Court service, specifically regarding the determination of retirement age.

main_sections.description: This section likely states the short title of the Act and when it comes into effect.
This section would define what constitutes the retirement age for the purpose of this Act.
This section establishes the rules and procedures for determining the retirement age.
This section likely details the implications of the determined retirement age, such as the effective date of retirement and any related procedures.

important_rules: The retirement age for certain High Court service personnel is to be determined as per this Act.
Specific rules will govern the process of determining the retirement age.
The Act specifies provisions that come into effect upon retirement.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Likely the Kerala High Court administration or a designated authority.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application of the provisions of the Act in determining and implementing retirement.

rights: Right to have retirement age determined as per the Act.
Right to retire at the determined age.
duties: Duty of the administration to implement the provisions of the Act.
Duty to adhere to the determined retirement age.

key_procedures: Procedure for determining the retirement age based on the Act's provisions.
Procedures related to the effective date of retirement.
administration: Kerala High Court Administration.
important_notes: The Act amends existing provisions related to retirement age for High Court service.
The retirement age is determined for officers and employees of the High Court.
The retirement age for officers and employees of the High Court is fixed at 55 years.

title: THE KERALA HIGH COURT SERVICES (DETERMINATION OF RETIREMENT AGE) ACT, 2008
purpose: To determine the retirement age of the officers and servants of the High Court of Kerala.
scope: Applies to officers and servants of the High Court of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act and states that it may be called the Kerala High Court Services (Determination of Retirement Age) Act, 2008. It also specifies that the Act shall come into force on the 1st day of January, 2007.

main_sections.section_title: Determination of Retirement Age in High Court Services
main_sections.description: This section determines the retirement age for officers and servants of the High Court of Kerala. Notwithstanding anything in any other law, rule, or order, the compulsory retirement of an officer or servant of the High Court of Kerala shall take effect from the afternoon of the last day of the month in which they attain the age of 55 years.

main_sections.section_title: Special Provision for Payment of Salary
main_sections.description: This section outlines a special provision for the payment of salary. Notwithstanding anything contained in the Act, officers or servants of the High Court of Kerala, if continued in service beyond the age of 55 years, will be eligible for salary and allowances for the period during which they actually worked until the 22nd day of October, 2007. Their service during this period will not be counted for any other service benefits or pensionary benefits.

This section deals with the repeal of the Kerala High Court Services (Determination of Retirement Age) Ordinance, 2007. It also states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or action taken under the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: The retirement age for officers and servants of the High Court of Kerala is 55 years.
Compulsory retirement takes effect from the afternoon of the last day of the month in which the age of 55 years is attained.
Service beyond 55 years until October 22, 2007, is eligible for salary and allowances for actual work performed, but not for other benefits or pensionary benefits.

rights: Right to receive salary and allowances for service rendered beyond the age of 55 until October 22, 2007, for officers and servants of the High Court of Kerala.
duties: Duty to comply with the retirement age as determined by the Act.
Duty to ensure that service beyond retirement age is only compensated for salary and allowances for the specified period.

key_procedures: Compulsory retirement is to be effected on the last day of the month in which the individual attains the age of 55 years.
administration: Kerala High Court
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 26th December 2008.
The Act was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 2746 dated 27th December 2008.

title: The Kerala Highway Protection Act, 1999
purpose: To provide for the protection of highways in Kerala and to prevent obstruction, encroachment, damage, and misuse of highways. The act aims to ensure the smooth flow of traffic and the safety of highway users.
scope: The Act applies to all highways in the State of Kerala. It covers individuals, authorities, agencies, and companies involved in activities that may affect highways.

key_definitions.highway: Includes the carriage way, the adjoining shoulders, roadside land, and any structure or device belonging to the highway.
key_definitions.highway authority: The Government, or any officer or authority authorized by the Government, responsible for the maintenance and protection of highways.

main_sections.section_title: Restriction of traffic where high-way is temporarily closed
main_sections.description: Details provisions for restricting traffic when a highway is temporarily closed for reasons such as maintenance, repair, or emergencies. It outlines the authority's power to issue notices and enforce regulations during such closures.

main_sections.section_title: Consent of highway authority required to do certain acts on highway
main_sections.description: Requires consent from the highway authority for any person or agency to construct, place, maintain, or carry any cable, wire, pipe, drain, sewer, or channel along, under, or over any highway. It also specifies conditions for granting consent and imposition of charges.

main_sections.section_title: Prevention of damage to and repair of highway
main_sections.description: Prohibits anyone from willfully or negligently causing damage to a highway or allowing any vehicle or animal to cause damage. It also addresses the repair of damaged highways.
Deals with the acquisition of land for highway purposes by the highway authority, including procedures for negotiation and purchase or requisition of land.

main_sections.section_title: Application of certain provisions to lands adjacent to the national highways
main_sections.description: Specifies that certain provisions of the Act shall be lawful for competent authorities to determine building lines and control lines for national highways, with reference to specific sections of the Act and the Constitution of India.

main_sections.section_title: General provision for punishment of offences
main_sections.description: Outlines the general penalty for offenses under the Act, where no specific penalty is provided. It specifies the punishment for conviction, including fines.

main_sections.section_title: Disobedience of orders, obstruction and refusal of information
main_sections.description: Addresses offenses related to disobedience of lawful directions, obstruction of authorized persons, and refusal to provide information to the highway authority. It specifies penalties for such offenses.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty on contravention of restriction relating to laying of means of access or erecting any building etc.
main_sections.description: Imposes penalties for contravening restrictions related to laying access means or erecting buildings near highways. It includes fines for continuing offenses.
Specifies penalties for encroaching on highway land, including fines for the first offense and daily levies for continuing offenses.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for causing damage to highway
main_sections.description: Imposes penalties for willfully causing damage to a highway by a vehicle or animal, including fines.
Grants the highway authority the power to compound offenses, meaning to settle them by agreement with the offender, subject to certain conditions.

Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including matters related to the preparation of schemes, standards for highways, application of land for use, and maintenance of highways.
Provides for the constitution of appellate authorities by the Government to hear appeals against orders passed under the Act. It also specifies the powers of these authorities.
Details the procedures for serving notices under the Act, including methods of delivery and deemed service.
Allows the highway authority to delegate its powers and functions under the Act to officers or authorities subordinate to it.

main_sections.section_title: Persons deemed to be public servants
main_sections.description: Declares persons acting under the authority of the Government or highway authority in the execution of their duties and functions under the Act to be public servants.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection from legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith under the Act by the Government, any authority, or any person.
Addresses offenses committed by companies, making them liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly, even if the individual person committing the offense is not identifiable.
Specifies that no court shall take cognizance of any offense punishable under the Act except on a report in writing from the highway authority or any other officer authorized by the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Police officers to assist highway authorities
main_sections.description: Requires police officers to assist highway authorities in the execution of their duties and functions under the Act, including taking measures to prevent obstruction or damage to highways.

main_sections.section_title: Duties of Village Officials to report to highway authority
main_sections.description: Imposes duties on Village officials, Village Assistants, or other village officials to report to the nearest police station or highway authority any damage to the highway or encroachment on highway land.

main_sections.section_title: Power to utilise highway land for purposes other than road purposes
main_sections.description: Grants the highway authority the power to utilize highway land temporarily for purposes other than road purposes, such as forming part of a highway which is not immediately required for traffic, subject to prescribed conditions.

main_sections.section_title: Saving as regards land under the control of Central Government
main_sections.description: States that nothing in the Act shall apply to lands vested in or under the control of the Central Government or any area falling within the limits of a Cantonment Board, Major Port Trust, or other authority under the administrative control of the Central Government.

main_sections.section_title: Removal of structure which obstructs the view or distraction of persons using highway
main_sections.description: Empowers the highway authority to order the removal of structures that obstruct the view or distract persons using a highway, especially at bends or corners.

main_sections.section_title: Regulation of traffic when highway is deemed unsafe
main_sections.description: Allows the highway authority to regulate traffic when a highway is deemed unsafe for vehicles or persons, including prohibiting certain types of traffic or vehicles.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of heavy vehicles on certain highways
main_sections.description: Empowers the highway authority to prohibit the plying of heavy vehicles on certain highways if the road is not designed for such vehicles or if the weight exceeds a certain limit. It also allows for restrictions on bridge construction or causeways.

important_rules: No person shall construct, place, maintain, or carry any cable, wire, pipe, drain, sewer, or channel along, under, or over any highway without the consent of the highway authority. (Section 26(1))
No person shall willfully or negligently cause damage to a highway or allow any vehicle or animal to cause damage. (Section 27(1))
No person shall construct or alter any building or structure or do any other work in contravention of the provisions of Section 19 or sub-section (1) of Section 20. (Section 32(1))
No person shall encroach on any highway land. (Section 33)
No person shall willfully cause any damage to a highway by a vehicle or animal. (Section 34)
Police officers shall assist highway authorities in the execution of their duties. (Section 44)
Village officials must report damage to or encroachment on highway land to the police or highway authority. (Section 45)

penalties: Fine up to one hundred rupees for offenses where no specific penalty is provided (Section 30(1)).

Fine which may extend to five hundred rupees for a first conviction, and which may extend to two thousand rupees for a second conviction for disobedience of orders, obstruction, or refusal of information (Section 31(1)).
Fine which may extend to five thousand rupees for contravention of restrictions relating to laying of means of access or erecting any building (Section 32(1)).
Fine up to one thousand rupees per day in case of a continuing offense (Section 32(2)).

Fine which may extend to two thousand rupees for the first offense and further fine which may extend to a lumpsum levy not exceeding five hundred rupees for each day for a continuing encroachment (Section 33).
Fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees for causing damage to a highway by a vehicle or animal (Section 34).

Fine which may extend to two thousand rupees for a first conviction, and which may extend to two thousand rupees for repeated offenses related to prohibition of heavy vehicles on certain highways (Section 24).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Highway authority, Police officers, and other competent authorities as designated by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through imposition of fines, requiring removal of obstructions, and legal proceedings by courts.

rights: Right to apply for permission to construct or do certain acts on the highway, subject to consent and conditions. (Section 26)
Right to appeal against orders of the highway authority to an appellate authority. (Section 37)
duties: Duty to obtain consent of the highway authority before undertaking any construction or activity on the highway. (Section 26)
Duty to not cause damage to the highway. (Section 27)
Duty of village officials to report damage or encroachment. (Section 45)
Duty of police officers to assist highway authorities. (Section 44)
obligations: Obligation to comply with restrictions on traffic during temporary highway closures. (Section 25)
Obligation to adhere to building lines and control lines for national highways. (Section 29)
Obligation to not disobey lawful orders or obstruct authorized persons. (Section 31)

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining consent from the highway authority for any work on the highway, including application, examination, and potential imposition of conditions and charges. (Section 26)
Procedure for acquisition of land for highway purposes, involving negotiation and purchase or requisition. (Section 28)
Procedure for compounding of offenses by the highway authority. (Section 35)
Procedure for serving notices under the Act, including methods of delivery and deemed service. (Section 38)
Procedure for appealing against orders of the highway authority, including deadlines for filing appeals and communication of decisions. (Section 37(7) & (8))
Procedure for courts to take cognizance of offenses, requiring a written report from the highway authority. (Section 43)
administration: The State Government and the Highway Authority (which can be the Government or an authorized officer/authority).
important_notes: The Act does not apply to lands under the control of the Central Government. (Section 47)
Actions taken in good faith by the Government or authorities under the Act are protected from legal proceedings. (Section 41)
Companies can be held liable for offenses committed under the Act. (Section 42)
Rules made by the Government under the Act are to be laid before the Legislative Assembly. (Section 36(3))

title: The Kerala Homeguards Act, 1960
purpose: To provide for the constitution of Home Guards in the State of Kerala, for their employment in emergencies and for other purposes.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala. The act concerns the constitution, appointment, functions, duties, powers, control, and penalties related to Home Guards.

key_definitions.Home Guards: Means a person who is appointed as a Home Guard under this Act.
key_definitions.prescribed: means prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as The Kerala Home Guards Act, 1960, that it extends to the whole of Kerala, and it came into force at once.
Defines 'Home Guards' and 'prescribed'.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of Home Guards and appointment of Commandant-General and Commandant.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to constitute volunteer bodies called 'Home Guards' and to appoint a Commandant-General and Commandants. Outlines their functions and duties in relation to protection of persons, security of property, and public safety.

Subject to the approval of the Commandant-General, the Commandant may appoint Home Guards. Specifies the criteria for appointment based on fitness and willingness to serve, and the requirement to be detailed to any office of command in the Home Guards. Also states that notwithstanding anything contained in the Act, the Commandant-General may appoint any member to any post under his control.

The Commandant-General may call out Home Guards for training or to discharge functions or duties assigned to them under Section 3. The Government may also call out members for any purpose under this Act.

Members of the Home Guards called out under Section 5 have the same powers, privileges, and protection as an officer of police acting for the time being in force. However, no prosecution can be instituted against a member except with the previous sanction of the Commandant-General.

main_sections.section_title: Control by Officers of Police Force.
main_sections.description: Members of the Home Guards, when called out under Section 5, shall be under the control of the officers of the police force in such manner and to such extent as may be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Home Guards not to resign without notice.
main_sections.description: A member of the Home Guards shall not resign without giving at least one month's notice to the Commandant.

main_sections.section_title: Certificate, arms, etc., to be delivered up by person ceasing to be member.
main_sections.description: Upon ceasing to be a member, a Home Guard must deliver up their certificate of appointment and any arms, accoutrements, clothing, or other necessary items. Warrants for these items may be issued by police officers.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment of members for neglect of duty, etc.
main_sections.description: Details punishments for members who suspend, reduce, neglect or dismiss duties, or disobey lawful orders. Also covers penalties for discharging duties in a manner that causes breach of discipline or misconduct. The Commandant-General has the authority to discharge any member under his control. Includes provisions for appeals against orders and penalties. Penalties can include imprisonment and fines.

Specifies penalties for Home Guards who refuse to obey orders or discharge duties under Section 5, including imprisonment and fines. Also covers penalties for wilful refusal to deliver up certificates or other articles.

main_sections.section_title: Disciplinary action against commandant or the Commandant-General.
main_sections.description: Outlines disciplinary actions that can be taken against Commandants and the Commandant-General, including suspension, dismissal, removal, and reduction in rank. These actions are subject to prescribed rules and can involve inquiry into misconduct. Police officers may also be involved in enforcing penalties.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to make rules.
main_sections.description: The Government has the power to make rules, notified in the Gazette, to carry out the purposes of the Act. These rules can cover various aspects including the exercise of control by police officers, organization, appointment, functions, discipline, and disciplinary action for Home Guards, and general provisions.

main_sections.section_title: Officers and members of Home Guards to be public servants.
main_sections.description: Declares that officers and members of Home Guards are deemed to be public servants within the meaning of the Indian Penal Code.

main_sections.section_title: Officers and members of Home Guards not disqualified from elections to Legislature or to Local Authorities.
main_sections.description: States that being an officer or member of the Home Guards does not disqualify a person from being elected to the Legislature or Local Authorities, provided they are not an officer or member of the Home Guards.
Repeals The Madras Home Guards Act, 1948, as in force in Malabar district and Section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.

important_rules: Members must not resign without giving one month's notice.
Home Guards must deliver up their certificates of appointment, arms, accoutrements, clothing, and other necessary items upon ceasing to be a member.
Members called out under Section 5 are under the control of police officers as prescribed.
Rules made by the Government can regulate the exercise of control by police officers over Home Guards, their organization, appointment, functions, discipline, and other matters.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months or with fine which may extend to two hundred and fifty rupees (Section 11).
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month or with fine which may extend to one hundred rupees (Section 11).
Fines (Section 10 and 11).
Imprisonment, removal, suspension, reduction to a lower rank (Section 12).
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months or fine (Section 10).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Commandant-General, Commandants, Officers of Police Force, and the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through disciplinary actions like suspension, dismissal, removal, reduction in rank; imposition of fines and imprisonment; and through rules prescribed by the Government. Prosecutions require sanction from the Commandant-General.

rights: Home Guards called out under Section 5 have the same powers, privileges, and protection as police officers.
Members have the right to appeal against certain orders.
duties: To protect persons, secure property, and maintain public safety.
To obey lawful orders of the Commandant-General and Commandants.
To discharge functions and duties assigned to them.
To deliver up certificates and equipment upon ceasing to be a member.
Not to resign without notice.
obligations: To serve as a Home Guard as appointed.
To adhere to discipline and rules governing Home Guards.

key_procedures: Appointment of Home Guards by Commandants, subject to Commandant-General's approval.
Calling out Home Guards for training or duty by the Commandant-General or the Government.
Disciplinary action procedures against Commandants and Commandant-General, involving inquiry and prescribed rules.
Appeals against orders passed by the Commandant-General or Government.
Making of rules by the Government through notification in the Gazette.
administration: The Government of Kerala (implied, as it's a State Act and powers are vested in the Government).
important_notes: The Act is a repeal of previous legislation related to Home Guards in the region.
Members of Home Guards are considered public servants.
Membership in Home Guards does not disqualify individuals from elections to legislative bodies or local authorities.

title: The Kerala Identification Of Prisoners Act, 1963
purpose: To unify and amend the laws authorising the taking of measurements and photographs of convicts and others in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and authorizes the taking of measurements and photographs of convicts and others in the State.

key_definitions.measurements: Includes finger impressions and foot-print impressions.
key_definitions.police officer: Means an officer in charge of a police station, a police officer making an investigation under Chapter XIV of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (Central Act 5 of 1898), or any other police officer not below the rank of a Sub-Inspector.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Identification of Prisoners Act, 1963, its extent is the whole of the State of Kerala, and it shall come into force at once.
Provides definitions for terms used in the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Taking of measurements, etc., of convicted persons.
main_sections.description: Empowers the taking of measurements and photographs of convicted persons.

main_sections.section_title: Taking of measurements, etc., of non-convicted persons.
main_sections.description: Empowers the taking of measurements and photographs of non-convicted persons.

main_sections.section_title: Taking of measurements, etc., of habitual offenders against whom conviction made.
main_sections.description: Authorizes the taking of measurements and photographs of habitual offenders against whom a conviction has been made.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Magistrate to order a person to be measured or photographed.
main_sections.description: Grants Magistrates the power to order persons to be measured or photographed.

main_sections.section_title: Resistance to the taking of measurements, etc.
main_sections.description: Deals with resistance to the taking of measurements or photographs.

main_sections.section_title: Destruction of photographs and records of measurements, etc., on acquisition.
main_sections.description: Covers the destruction of photographs and records of measurements.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of the Act.
States that no suit or other proceeding shall lie against any person for anything done or intended to be done in good faith under the Act or any rule made thereunder.

Repeals the Identification of Prisoners Act, 1920 (Central Act 33 of 1920) and the Travancore-Cochin Identification of Prisoners Act, 1950 (Act 19 of 1950) in so far as they apply to the Malabar district.

important_rules: Measurements and photographs may be taken of convicted persons who have been previously convicted of an offence punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term of one year or upwards, or of any offence which would render him liable to enhanced punishment on a subsequent conviction.
Measurements and photographs of non-convicted persons can be taken if they have been arrested in connection with an offence punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term of one year or upwards.
Habitual offenders against whom a conviction has been made can have their measurements and photographs taken.
Magistrates can order persons to be measured or photographed if satisfied of the purposes of investigation or proceeding under the Code of Criminal Procedure.
The Government may make rules for the purpose of carrying into effect the provisions of the Act.

Rules may include restrictions on taking photographs, places where measurements and photographs may be taken, the nature of measurements, the method of taking measurements, dress to be worn, and the preservation, safe custody, destruction, and disposal of records.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Police officers, Magistrates, and the Government (for making rules).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the taking of measurements and photographs as authorized by the Act, and through the powers granted to Magistrates. Resistance to these actions is addressed.

rights: Right to resist taking of measurements or photographs if not lawfully required.
duties: Duty to submit to the taking of measurements and photographs when lawfully required.

key_procedures: If a person is convicted of an offence punishable with rigorous imprisonment for one year or upwards, their measurements and photographs can be taken. If they are convicted of an offence which would render them liable to enhanced punishment on a subsequent conviction, their measurements and photographs can also be taken.
If a non-convicted person is arrested in connection with an offence punishable with rigorous imprisonment for one year or upwards, their measurements and photographs can be taken.
If a habitual offender has been convicted, their measurements and photographs can be taken.

A Magistrate, if satisfied that it is necessary for the purposes of investigation or proceeding under the Code of Criminal Procedure, can order a person to be measured or photographed. If the person to whom the order relates is produced before the Magistrate and placed in the case, the Magistrate may, by a police officer, allow his measurements or photograph to be taken.
No order for taking photographs shall be directed to any person at some time been arrested in connection with such investigation or proceeding.
administration: The Government (for making rules).
important_notes: Resistance to the taking of measurements or photographs is deemed to be an offence under section 186 of the Indian Penal Code.

Photographs and records of measurements of convicted persons who have not been previously convicted of an offence punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term of one year or upwards, or of any offence for which his measurements taken have been photographed or acquired by any court, all measurements and all photographs (both negatives and copies) taken shall unless the Court or (in a case where such person is released without trial) the District Magistrate for reasons to be recorded in writing otherwise directs, be destroyed or made over to him.

Rules made under this section shall not have effect in so far as any modification or annulment thereof may be in the rule or decided that the rule should not be made. The rule shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect, as the case may be; so however that any such modification or annulment shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that rule.

title: The Kerala Industrial Employees' Payment of Gratuity Act, 1970
purpose: To provide for the payment of gratuity to employees in factories, plantations, and other establishments in the State of Kerala.

scope.geographical: The whole of the State of Kerala.
scope.subject_matter: Applies to factories, plantations (admeasuring 10.125 hectares or more or employing ten or more persons), establishments defined under the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1960, establishments defined under the Beedi and Cigar Workers (Conditions of Employment) Act, 1966 (employing ten or more persons), and motor transport undertakings. The Government can also extend its provisions to other entities via notification.
scope.employee_criteria: Employees whose monthly wages do not exceed seven hundred and fifty rupees and who are not subject to the Army Act, Air Force Act, Navy Act, Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund Act, or employed in the police service or prisons.

key_definitions.completed_year_of_service: Uninterrupted service for one year, including service interrupted by sickness, accident, leave, strike, lock-out, or cessation of work not due to the employee's fault.
key_definitions.continuous_service: Uninterrupted service, including service interrupted by sickness, accident, leave, strike, lock-out, or cessation of work not due to the employee's fault.
key_definitions.controlling_authority: The authority appointed by the Government under Section 3 responsible for the administration of the Act.
key_definitions.employee: Any person employed in a covered establishment for skilled or unskilled, manual, clerical, or supervisory work for hire or reward, provided their monthly wages do not exceed Rs. 750 and they are not in certain specific services (military, police, prison).
key_definitions.employer: The person or authority in ultimate control of the affairs of the establishment, including government appointees, local authority appointees, or managers/managing directors in other cases.
key_definitions.family: Includes spouse, children (married or unmarried), dependent parents, and the widow and children of a deceased son for male employees. For female employees, it includes husband, children, dependent parents (of employee or husband), and widow and children of a deceased son. A female employee can exclude her husband by written notice.
key_definitions.wages: All remuneration, including dearness allowance, value of house accommodation, light, water, medical attendance, or other amenities/services, and travelling concessions. Excludes bonus, commission, overtime wages, and night allowance.

main_sections.description: Names the Act, specifies its geographical reach (entire State of Kerala), and outlines its initial application to various types of establishments.

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'completed year of service', 'continuous service', 'controlling authority', 'employee', 'employer', 'family', 'prescribed', 'retirement', 'superannuation', and 'wages'.
Empowers the Government to appoint a Controlling Authority by notification for the administration of the Act.

Specifies the conditions under which gratuity is payable to an employee (superannuation, retirement, resignation, retrenchment, discharge, dismissal after 5 years of continuous service, death, or total disablement). It also details the calculation of gratuity, maximum payable amount, and conditions for voluntary retirement/resignation.
Grants the Government the power to exempt any establishment from the Act's provisions if employees receive benefits superior to those provided by the Act.

Outlines the process for employees to make nominations for the receipt of gratuity in case of their death, including rules for nominations in favour of family members and modification/revocation of nominations.

main_sections.section_title: Application for gratuity and procedure for payment
main_sections.description: Details the procedure for employees to apply for gratuity and the employer's responsibility to pay the amount, including notification to the employee and controlling authority.

Describes the procedure for the recovery of unpaid gratuity amounts by the Controlling Authority, including the power to conduct inquiries, issue certificates to the Collector, and provisions for appeal.
Specifies penalties for making false statements or representations to avoid payment, and for contravening the provisions of the Act or rules.

main_sections.section_title: Protection for acts done in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection from suits or legal proceedings against the controlling authority or other authorities for actions taken in good faith under the Act.
Allows the Government to delegate its powers under the Act.
Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of any previous laws and savings provisions.

important_rules: Gratuity is payable on superannuation, retirement, resignation, retrenchment, discharge, or dismissal after a minimum of five years of continuous service, or in case of death or total disablement.
Gratuity is calculated at the rate of fifteen days' wages for every completed year of service (or part thereof exceeding six months), based on the last drawn wages.
The maximum gratuity payable shall not exceed fifteen months' wages.
Employees voluntarily retiring or resigning must give one month's written notice to the employer.
Employees with one year of service must make a nomination in the prescribed form to receive gratuity in case of death before payment.
Nominations made by employees with a family must be in favour of one or more family members.
The employer must pay gratuity to an employee as soon as it becomes payable, and within a prescribed time.
If gratuity is not paid within the prescribed time, the Controlling Authority can determine the amount and recover it as arrears of land revenue.

penalties: Imprisonment up to six months or a fine up to one thousand rupees, or both, for knowingly making false statements or representations to avoid payment.
Imprisonment up to three months or a fine up to one thousand rupees, or both, for contravening or defaulting in complying with the Act or rules.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Controlling Authority appointed by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inquiries conducted by the Controlling Authority with powers similar to a civil court, and recovery of unpaid gratuity as arrears of land revenue. Penalties are imposed for violations of the Act or rules.

rights: Right to receive gratuity upon superannuation, retirement, resignation, retrenchment, discharge, dismissal (after 5 years continuous service), death, or total disablement.
Right to nominate a person to receive gratuity in case of death.
Right to receive gratuity even if better terms are available under an award, agreement, or contract.
Right to appeal against an order of the Controlling Authority regarding gratuity amount.
duties: Duty of the employer to pay gratuity as per the Act.
Duty of the employer to inform the employee and Controlling Authority when gratuity becomes payable.
Duty of the employee to make a nomination for gratuity if they have completed one year of service.
Duty of the employee to give one month's written notice for voluntary retirement or resignation.
Duty of the employer to provide a reasonable opportunity of being heard before an order determining gratuity amount is made.
obligations: Obligation of the employer to ensure compliance with the payment of gratuity provisions.
Obligation of the employee to adhere to nomination procedures and notice periods for resignation/retirement.

key_procedures: Employee completes one year of service and makes a nomination.
Employee applies for gratuity upon eligibility (superannuation, retirement, etc.) within the prescribed time and form.
Employer determines gratuity amount and pays it to the employee within the prescribed time.
If gratuity is unpaid, the Controlling Authority conducts an inquiry, determines the amount, and issues a recovery certificate to the Collector.
Appeals against the Controlling Authority's order can be preferred to the Government or a specified authority within sixty days.
administration: The Controlling Authority, appointed by the Government, is responsible for the administration of this Act.
important_notes: The Government can extend the Act's application to other establishments via notification.
The Act does not affect the right to better terms of gratuity or retirement benefits available under any award or agreement.
Voluntary retirement or resignation for gratuity payment is limited to 5% of total employees in a year, with eligibility determined by service length if the limit is exceeded.
Protection is provided for acts done in good faith by the controlling authority or other officers under the Act.

title: THE KERALA INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS (NATIONAL AND FESTIVAL HOLIDAYS) AMENDMENT ACT, 1969
purpose: An Act to amend the Kerala Industrial Establishments (National and Festival Holidays) Act, 1958, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to Industrial Establishments in Kerala. The amendments concern the calculation of holidays and the power of employers to require employees to work on holidays.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act as 'The Kerala Industrial Establishments (National and Festival Holidays) Amendment Act, 1969' and states that it shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Amends section 2 of the principal Act by substituting the word 'fifty' with 'twenty' in sub-clause (i) of clause (e), and the word 'twenty' with 'fifty' in clause (g).

Amends section 3 of the principal Act. This section deals with the circumstances under which an industrial establishment commences work for the first time, after the commencement of a calendar year, the number of holidays for festivals allowable to an employee under this section during the remainder of that calendar year shall not be less than the number calculated at the rate of one day for every three months or part thereof of the remainder of such calendar year.

Inserts a new section 4-A titled 'Power of employer to require employee to work on holidays'. This section allows an employer, notwithstanding anything contained in section 3, to require any employee to work on any holiday allowed under that section. The notice must be served in the prescribed manner, and a copy of the notice must be displayed in the premises of the industrial establishment, not less than twenty-four hours before such holiday.

Amends section 5 of the principal Act. It allows an employee to be entitled to twice the wages and to avail himself of a substituted holiday on any other day when working on a holiday allowed under section 3. It also provides that no such employee shall be entitled to be paid any wages for any of the holidays allowed under section 3, other than the wages for the period of thirty days within a continuous period of ninety days immediately preceding such holiday, on the 26th January, the 15th August and the 1st May, unless he has been in the service under the employer for a total period of thirty days within a continuous period of ninety days immediately preceding such holiday.

Amends sub-section (3) of section 12 of the principal Act. It states that every rule made under this Act shall be laid as soon as may be after it is made before the Legislative Assembly while it is in session for a total period of fourteen days which may be comprised in one session or in two successive sessions, and if, before the expiry of the sessions in which it is so laid or the session immediately following, the Legislative Assembly agrees in making any modification in the rule or the Legislative Assembly agrees that the rule should not be made, the rule shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect, as the case may be; so however that any such modification or annulment shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that rule.

important_rules: An employer can require an employee to work on a holiday, provided a notice is served in the prescribed manner at least twenty-four hours before the holiday.
Employees working on a holiday are entitled to twice their wages and a substituted holiday on another day.

Wages for specific national holidays (Jan 26, Aug 15, May 1) are only payable if the employee has served for 30 days in the 90 days preceding the holiday, or for the thirty days within a continuous period of ninety days immediately preceding such holiday.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government of Kerala (implied through notification and appointment)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications and appointments by the Government.

rights: Right to national and festival holidays.
Right to receive wages for holidays, under certain conditions.
Right to be paid twice the wages for working on a holiday.
Right to an alternative holiday if required to work on a holiday.
duties: Duty of employer to grant holidays.
Duty of employer to issue notice for working on holidays.
Duty to adhere to rules laid by the Legislative Assembly.
obligations: Obligation to serve for a minimum period to be eligible for wages on certain national holidays.

key_procedures: Procedure for serving notice to employees about working on a holiday (at least 24 hours prior).
Procedure for laying rules before the Legislative Assembly for modification or annulment.
administration: Government of Kerala
important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 50, dated 24th February, 1969.
A weekly or other holiday or authorised leave availed of by an employee shall be included in computing the period of thirty days mentioned in the preceding proviso (referring to Section 5 amendment).

title: The Kerala Industrial Establishments (National and Festival Holidays) Amendment Act, 1979
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Industrial Establishments (National and Festival Holidays) Act, 1958, for the purpose hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to Industrial Establishments in Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Industrial Establishments (National and Festival Holidays) Amendment Act, 1979.

In sub-section (3) of section 5 of the Kerala Industrial Establishments (National and Festival Holidays) Act, 1958 (47 of 1958), in clause (i), for the words 'the Month', the words 'the thirty working days' shall be substituted.

important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 5th November, 1979 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 806, dated 8th November, 1979.

title: The Kerala Industrial Establishments (National and Festival Holidays) Amendment Act, 1990
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Industrial Establishments (National and Festival Holidays) Act, 1958.
scope: Applies to industrial establishments in Kerala.

key_definitions.strike: For the purpose of this sub-section, the expression "strike" shall have the meaning assigned to them in the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (Central Act 14 of 1947).
key_definitions.lock-out: For the purpose of this sub-section, the expression "lock-out" shall have the meaning assigned to them in the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (Central Act 14 of 1947).
key_definitions.lay-off: For the purpose of this sub-section, the expression "lay-off" shall have the meaning assigned to them in the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (Central Act 14 of 1947).

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Industrial Establishments (National and Festival Holidays) Amendment Act, 1990, and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Amends section 3 of the Principal Act (Kerala Industrial Establishments (National and Festival Holidays) Act, 1958) by substituting specific words and figures related to holidays.

Amends section 5 of the Principal Act by substituting a new sub-section (1) and amending the proviso to sub-section (3). The amendment clarifies conditions under which employees shall not be paid wages for holidays, particularly during strikes, lock-outs, or illegal lay-offs, and specifies a penalty for employees participating in illegal strikes.

important_rules: Notwithstanding any contract to the contrary, every employee shall be paid wages for each of the holidays allowed to him under section 3, whether or not the employer has acquired, or could not require, him under sub-section (1) of section 4A to work on that holiday, or whether that holiday falls or does not fall during the period of a strike or illegal lock-out.

Provided that if such holiday falls during the period of a strike or lock-out, the employee shall be paid fifty per cent of the total of the basic wages and dearness allowance that he would have been entitled to, had he not been so laid off.
An employee participating in an illegal strike shall not be entitled to wages for any holiday falling during the period of such strike.

penalties: 50% of basic wages and dearness allowance for holidays falling during a strike or lock-out (if not illegal).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government (through notification in the Gazette for commencement, and likely through labor authorities for enforcement of the Act's provisions).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through Government notification for commencement, and enforcement of amended sections pertaining to holidays and wages during industrial disputes.

rights: Right to receive wages for national and festival holidays allowed under section 3.
Right to receive 50% of wages for holidays falling during a strike or lock-out (if not illegal).
obligations: Employers must pay wages for national and festival holidays.
Employees must not participate in illegal strikes to receive holiday wages.

key_procedures: The Government appoints the date of commencement by notification in the Gazette.
Amendments to sections 3 and 5 of the Principal Act are made, impacting the payment of wages for holidays under specific circumstances.
administration: The Labour Department or equivalent government department in Kerala is likely responsible for the administration of this Act.
