important_notes: The Act received the assent of the President on the 24th day of July, 1990 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 779 dated the 6th August, 1990.
The meaning of 'strike', 'lock-out', and 'lay-off' are specifically tied to the definitions provided in the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (Central Act 14 of 1947).

title: The Kerala Industrial Revitalisation Fund Act, 1999
purpose: To provide for the establishment of a Fund for the revitalization of sick industrial units in the State of Kerala and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to sick industrial units in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.sick_industrial_unit: An industrial unit which has been registered for not less than five years and which has been closed down or has been in operation for the previous five consecutive financial years with cash losses in each of those years or cumulative cash losses which have resulted in the erosion of fifty per cent. or more of its net worth.
key_definitions.fund: The Kerala Industrial Revitalisation Fund established under this Act.
key_definitions.revitalisation: The process of bringing a sick industrial unit back to financial health and operational efficiency.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and its commencement date.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'Fund', 'sick industrial unit', 'revitalisation', etc.
Establishes the Kerala Industrial Revitalisation Fund and outlines its objectives and sources of fund.
Grants powers to the Government to make rules and regulations for the implementation of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Scheme for revitalisation of sick industrial units
main_sections.description: Provides for the framing of schemes for the revitalisation of sick industrial units.
Empowers the Government to issue directions to the agencies involved in the revitalisation process.
Grants power to the Government to exempt any industrial unit or class of industrial units from the provisions of the Act.
Confers power on the Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Laying of rules and notifications before the Legislative Assembly
main_sections.description: Specifies the procedure for laying of rules and notifications before the Kerala Legislative Assembly.
Repeals any existing law on the subject and provides for savings.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Fund shall be utilised for providing financial assistance, rehabilitation packages, and other support measures for the revitalisation of sick industrial units.
Rule 2: The Government shall frame schemes for the identification and revitalisation of sick industrial units.
Rule 3: The agencies involved in the revitalisation process shall adhere to the directions issued by the Government.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala and agencies designated by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the implementation of revitalisation schemes, provision of financial assistance, and enforcement of directions.

rights: Sick industrial units have the right to receive assistance from the Fund for their revitalisation.
Stakeholders of sick industrial units have the right to be heard during the formulation of revitalisation schemes.
duties: Industrial units seeking assistance must comply with the conditions prescribed in the revitalisation schemes.
Agencies involved must perform their duties efficiently and effectively to achieve the objectives of the Act.
obligations: The Government has the obligation to establish and manage the Fund effectively.
The Government has the obligation to frame appropriate schemes for the revitalisation of sick industrial units.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Identification of sick industrial units based on defined criteria.
Procedure 2: Formulation of a revitalisation scheme for the identified unit.
Procedure 3: Approval and implementation of the scheme, including financial assistance and other support measures.
Procedure 4: Monitoring and evaluation of the progress of revitalisation.
administration: Industries Department, Government of Kerala (inferred).
important_notes: The Act aims to address the issue of industrial sickness in Kerala and promote industrial growth.
The effective functioning of the Fund and the successful implementation of revitalisation schemes are crucial for the achievement of the Act's objectives.

title: THE KERALA INDUSTRIAL SINGLE WINDOW CLEARANCE BOARDS AND INDUSTRIAL TOWNSHIP AREA DEVELOPMENT ACT, 1999
purpose: To provide special provision for speedy issue of various licences, clearances and certificates required for setting up of industrial undertakings in the State of Kerala and for the Constitution of Industrial Township Area Development Authorities and for matter connected therewith. To promote and assist the orderly establishment, and rapid growth and development of industries in the State.
scope: The Act applies to industrial undertakings in the State of Kerala and deals with the establishment of Single Window Clearance Boards at the State, District and Industrial Area levels. It also covers the constitution of Industrial Township Authorities.

key_definitions.authority: Any Department of Government or Government agencies or Grama Panchayat or Municipality which are required to issue clearances or licences or certificates or permits for setting up an industrial undertaking in the State.
key_definitions.bye-laws: Bye-laws made by the State Board under this Act.
key_definitions.district board: The District Single Window Clearance Board constituted under sub-section (1) of section 4 of this Act.
key_definitions.designated authority of industrial area: The Managing Director or any other Officer appointed by the Government for purposes of promoting and maintaining the industrial area concerned.
key_definitions.industrial area: Any area in the State declared to be an industrial area by the Government by notification in the Gazette from time to time and includes industrial estates, development areas, development plots, mini industrial estates, industrial parks and growth centres.
key_definitions.industrial area board: The Kerala State Single Window Clearance Board constituted under sub-section (1) of section 5 of the Act.
key_definitions.industrial township area: An industrial area referred to in section 14 of this Act.
key_definitions.industrial township authority: An Industrial Township Authority constituted for an industrial township area under section 15 and the Scheme.
key_definitions.industrial undertaking: A factory, workshop or work-place where steam power, water power, mechanical power or electrical power is used to any premises where any machinery or manufacturing plant driven by any power as aforesaid is installed or any industrial undertaking where ten or more workers are employed with or without the aid of power.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.scheme: The Scheme framed under this Act.
key_definitions.small scale industrial undertaking: An industrial undertaking which in accordance with the requirements specified under section 11 B of Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951 is entitled to be regarded as a Small Scale Industrial undertaking for the purpose of that Act.
key_definitions.state board: The Kerala State Single Window Clearance Board constituted under sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Act.
key_definitions.state enactment: A Proclamation or Act of Travancore or Cochin, an Act or Ordinance of Travancore-Cochin, an Act passed by the Legislature of the State of Kerala, or an Ordinance promulgated by the Governor and in force in the State and includes a rule, order, bye-law or regulation made in exercise of a power conferred by any such Act or Ordinance by the Government or an authority subordinate to Government.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Industrial Single Window Clearance Boards and Industrial Township Area Development Act, 1999. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including Authority, Bye-laws, District Board, Designated Authority of Industrial Area, Government, Industrial Area, Industrial Area Board, Industrial Township Area, Industrial Township Authority, Industrial Undertaking, Prescribed, Scheme, Small Scale Industrial Undertaking, State Board, and State Enactment.

For the purpose of speedy issue of various licences, clearances or certificates required under various State enactments for setting up of industrial undertakings in the State, the Government may, by notification, constitute State Single Window Clearance Board for the State to be called the Kerala State Single Window Clearance Board. The Board shall be a body corporate by the name aforesaid having perpetual succession and a common seal. The State Board shall consist of the following members: Chief Secretary to Government, The Secretaries to Government in charge of Industries, Finance, Labour, Local Administration, Revenue, Taxes, Irrigation, Power and Forests departments, Executive Director, Bureau of Industrial Promotion, Kerala, Managing Director, Kerala State Industrial Development Corporation, Director of Industries and Commerce, Managing Director, Kerala State Industrial Infrastructure Development Corporation, Chairman, Kerala State Electricity Board, Managing Director, Kerala Financial Corporation, Chief Town Planner, Chairman, Kerala State Pollution Control Board, Chief Electrical Inspector, Director of Factories and Boilers, Director of Mining and Geology, Director of Health Services. The Chief Secretary to Government shall be the Chairman and the Managing Director, Kerala State Industrial Development Corporation shall be the Convenor of the State Board. The State Board may associate itself, in such manner and for such purposes as may be prescribed by any person whose assistance or advice it may desire to have in the performance of any of its functions under the Act, and the person so associated shall have the right to take part in the meetings of the State Board relating to that purpose as a special invitee and shall not be considered as a member of the State Board.

For the purpose of speedy issue of various licences, clearances or certificates required under the various State enactments for setting up of small scale industrial undertakings having capital investment of not more than two lakhs rupees in each district of the State, the Government may, by notification, constitute a District Single Window Clearance Board for each district in the State. Every District Single Window Clearance Board shall be a body corporate by the name of the District for which it is constituted, having perpetual succession and a common seal. Every District Single Window Clearance Board shall consist of the following members, namely:- Collector of the District, General Manager, District Industries Centre of the district concerned, The President of the Grama Panchayat concerned or Chairperson of the Municipality concerned in cases where licence is required from the local bodies; The District Officer of the Kerala Pollution Control Board or any other officer of the Board nominated by the Chairman, Kerala State Pollution Control Board; The District Officer of the Electrical Inspectorate or any other officer nominated by the Chief Town Planner; The District Officer of the Town Planning Department o. any other officer nominated by the Chief Town Planner; District Medical Officer; An Officer of the Kerala State Electricity Board not below the rank of Executive Engineer nominated by the Chairman, Kerala State Electricity Board; District Officer, Factories and Boilers Inspectorate; Divisional Forest Officer; District Labour Officer; Secretary, Urban Development Authority or Secretary, District Panchayat, Deputy Commissioner, Sales Tax and Agricultural Income Tax; An Officer of the Kerala Water Authority not below the rank of Executive Engineer nominated by the Managing Director, Kerala Water Authority. The Collector of the District shall be the Chairman and the General Manager, District Industries Centre shall be the Convenor of the District Board. The District Board shall meet at such time and place to be fixed by the Chairman of the District Board and shall observe such procedure in regard to its transaction of business as may be made in the bye-laws.

For the purpose of speedy issue of various licences, clearances or certificates required under the various State enactments for setting up of small scale industrial undertakings in the various industrial areas of the State, the Government may, by notification constitute Single Window Clearance Boards for every industrial areas in the State to be called Industrial Area Single Window Clearance Board. Every Industrial Area Single Window Clearance Board shall be a body corporate by the name of the Industrial Area for which it is constituted, having perpetual succession and a common seal. Every Industrial Area Single Window Clearance Board shall consist of the following members, namely:— Principal Secretary to Government, Industries Department or his nominee, Collector of the District; Chief Executive of the Agency owning or managing the industrial area; Designated Authority of industrial area concerned; District Officer of the State Pollution Control Board, District Officer of the Electrical Inspectorate, District Officer of the Town Planning Department, District Medical Officer, Executive Engineer of the Kerala State Electricity Board, District Officer, Factories and Boilers Inspectorate.

key_procedures: The establishment and functioning of State, District, and Industrial Area Single Window Clearance Boards for the speedy issue of industrial clearances and licences.
The process of constituting these Boards, including the appointment of members and the roles of the Chairman and Convenor.
The requirement for Boards to be body corporates with perpetual succession and a common seal.
The conduct of meetings and transaction of business by the Boards, to be governed by bye-laws.
administration: Government of Kerala

title: The Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund (Amendment) Act, 2002
purpose: To amend The Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Act, 1999.
scope: Applies to The Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Act, 1999.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund (Amendment) Act, 2002' and states that it comes into force from the date of commencement of The Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Act, 1999.

Amends section 18 of The Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Act, 1999, regarding the powers of the Government to issue directions. It also inserts a new sub-section (2) in section 18, clarifying that the Government's directions to the Fund shall be binding and the Government may issue such directions as it deems fit.

Inserts a new section 18A into the Principal Act. This new section deals with the powers of the Government to issue directions and the duty of the Fund to comply. It states that the Government may, from time to time, issue such directions as it may deem fit to the Fund in regard to the affairs of the Fund, and the Fund shall comply with such directions. It also specifies that if any doubt arises in the interpretation of any direction, the Government shall have the power to decide it.

important_rules: The commencement of this Act is deemed to have taken place on the 24th day of November 1999.
The Government may issue directions to the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund.
The Fund shall comply with the directions issued by the Government.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through directions issued to the Fund and by the Fund's compliance with these directions.

rights: The Government has the right to issue directions to the Fund.
The Government has the right to decide on interpretations of its directions.
duties: The Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund has the duty to comply with the directions issued by the Government.

key_procedures: Procedure for amendment of the Act: The Act was passed by the Legislative Assembly and assented to by the Governor.
Procedure for issuing directions: The Government issues written directions to the Fund.
Procedure for compliance: The Fund is obligated to follow the issued directions.
Procedure for clarification: If there's ambiguity in a direction, the Government provides the final interpretation.
administration: The Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund
important_notes: The amendment is retrospective, effective from November 24, 1999.
The purpose of the amendment is to strengthen the Government's oversight and control over the Fund's operations.

title: THE KERALA INFRASTRUCTURE INVESTMENT FUND ACT, 1999
purpose: To provide for the establishment of the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Board: means the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.Fund: means the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund established under section 4.
key_definitions.Infrastructure: means projects or undertakings that promote the economic development of the State, and includes projects in the sectors of power, roads, ports, airports, water supply and sanitation, telecommunications, education, health, tourism, etc.
key_definitions.Member: means a Member of the Board and includes the Chairman.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act, its extent of application, and when it comes into force.
This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act.
This section deals with the establishment and composition of the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board.
This section describes the establishment of the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund.

main_sections.section_title: Objects and Purposes of the Fund
main_sections.description: This section outlines the main objectives and purposes for which the Fund is established.
This section details how the Fund can be invested and the types of projects it can finance.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of the Board
main_sections.description: This section enumerates the powers and functions of the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board.
This section pertains to the borrowing powers of the Board.
This section deals with the accounts to be maintained by the Fund and their audit.
This section grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
This section allows the Board to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules.
This section provides for savings and clarifies that the Act does not affect certain existing laws or powers.
This section likely repeals any previous enactments on the subject and provides for savings.

important_rules: Investments made by the Fund shall be for the purpose of promoting economic development of the State.
The Board shall have the power to borrow money from such sources and on such terms and conditions as may be specified.
The Government may, by notification, make rules to carry out the purposes of this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board and the Government of Kerala.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, rules, and regulations made thereunder. Enforcement would involve financial oversight, investment approvals, and potentially legal remedies for non-compliance.

rights: Right to establish and manage the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund.
Right to invest in projects promoting economic development.
Right to borrow funds for the Fund's operations.
duties: Duty to manage the Fund prudently and in the best interests of the State.
Duty to maintain proper accounts and undergo audit.
Duty to ensure that investments align with the Act's objectives.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the provisions of the Act, rules, and regulations.

key_procedures: Procedure for the constitution and functioning of the Board.
Procedure for the establishment and management of the Fund.
Procedures for making investments and for borrowing funds.
administration: The Government of Kerala, and the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board.
important_notes: The Act consolidates and regulates infrastructure investment in the State.
It aims to facilitate the development of critical infrastructure projects.

title: The Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Act, 1999
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a fund for investments in the infrastructure projects in the State and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the whole of the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Board: means the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board constituted under section 4
key_definitions.Financial assistance: means the types of assistance specified in the Scheme
key_definitions.Fund: means the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund established under section 3 and the scheme
key_definitions.Fund Manager: means the Fund Manager of the Board
key_definitions.Infrastructure projects: includes projects in the sectors of electricity, power, roads, irrigation, ports, airports, water supply, inland navigation, solid waste management and drainage or a multipurpose project in any one or more of these areas
key_definitions.Local Self Government Institution: means a Panchayat under the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 (13 of 1994) or a Municipality constituted under the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994 (20 of 1994)
key_definitions.Other undertakings: means Public Companies established in the State under the Companies Act, 1956 (Central Act 1 of 1956) in joint sector, where the investment of the Government is not less than forty per cent of the total paid up share capital, or societies established under the Travancore-Cochin Literary, Scientific and Charitable Societies Registration Act, 1955 (XII of 1955) or the Societies Registration Act, 1860 (Central Act 21 of 1860) and where Government, Local Self Government Institutions or any Public Sector Undertaking, as the case may be, have not less than fifty per cent of interest in its assets, ownership and management
key_definitions.Public Sector Undertaking: means any Government Company established in the State under the Companies Act, 1956 (Central Act 1 of 1956) or a Co-operative Society registered or deemed to have been registered under the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969 (21 of 1969) where the Government holds not less than fifty per cent of the share capital and substantial control over its management and includes public undertakings established under a statute
key_definitions.Schedule: means the Schedule to this Act
key_definitions.Scheme: means the scheme framed under this Act
key_definitions.Undertakings: means public sector undertakings or other undertakings

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Act, 1999. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 11th day of November, 1999.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'Financial assistance', 'Fund', 'Fund Manager', 'Government', 'Infrastructure projects', 'Local Self Government Institution', 'Other undertakings', 'Public Sector Undertaking', 'Schedule', 'Scheme', 'State', 'Undertakings', and 'Year'.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, frame a Scheme to be called the 'Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Scheme' for the establishment of a fund under this Act for investments in the infrastructure projects of the State. The Scheme shall be established as soon as may be after the framing of the Scheme, a fund in accordance with the provisions of this Act and the scheme.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, constitute a Board to be called 'the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board' for the administration of the fund and to supervise or carry out the activities financed from the fund. The Board shall be a body corporate by the name aforesaid, having perpetual succession and a common seal and shall by the said name sue or be sued. The Board shall consist of the Chief Secretary to Government of Kerala; the Principal Secretary (Finance); the Secretary (Public Works); the Secretary (Irrigation); the Secretary (Planning); the Secretary (Revenue); the Secretary (Finance Resources); and two persons who have proven experience in development banking nominated by the Government. The Chief Secretary shall be the Chairman of the Board. The Secretary (Finance Resources) shall be the Fund Manager of the Board. The Board shall administer the fund vested in it in such manner as may be specified in the scheme.

A member appointed under clause (h) of sub-section (3) of section 4 shall hold office during the pleasure of the Government. Any member appointed under clause (h) of sub-section (3) of section 4 may resign his membership by giving notice in writing to the Government but shall continue in office until his resignation is accepted by the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and Functions of the Board
main_sections.description: Subject to the provisions of this Act, the Board shall have the following powers and functions, namely: (a) to mobilise resources for the utilisation of the fund; (b) to sanction financial assistance to the undertakings per the scheme; (c) to recover the amounts due to the Board from the assisted undertakings as per the recovery schedule; (d) to modify, revise or reschedule the recoveries from any of the assisted undertakings as may be considered appropriate; (e) to opt for revenue recovery procedures, if found necessary and appropriate, against any of the assisted undertakings in the interest of the Board; (f) to disburse all expenses relating to the administration of the fund including travel, interest on borrowings, fees, professional charges and other expenses; (g) to invest any surplus fund of the Board, as may be available from time to time, in such manner as may be specified in the scheme and also to utilise such investments; (h) to review the performance of any undertaking receiving any assistance or loan from the fund on a periodic basis; (i) to enter into memorandum of undertakings or performance contract with any undertaking under the purview of this Act on behalf of the Government; (j) to enter into contracts on behalf of the Board; (k) to exercise such of the powers and functions as may be specified in the scheme; (l) to exercise such other powers and perform such other functions as may be conferred on or entrusted to it by the Government for carrying out the purposes of this Act, and incidental to it, (m) to do all acts necessary for, and incidental to, the carrying out of the functions entrusted or delegated to it.

The Government may, after due appropriation by law by the State Legislature, from time to time make such grants, advances and loans to the fund for the purposes of this Act on such terms and conditions as the Government may determine.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the Board to borrow and lend
main_sections.description: The Board may, from time to time, with the previous sanction of the Government and subject to such conditions as the Government may, by general or special order determine, borrow any sum required for the purposes of this Act. Whether by the issue of bonds or debentures or otherwise or by making arrangements with Banks or Institutions approved by the Government in that behalf. Bonds or debentures issued by the Board under this section shall be issued, transferred, dealt with or redeemed in such manner as the Government may, by general or special order, direct. Subject to the provisions of this Act and such conditions and limitations as may be specified in the scheme, the Board may, out of its funds, grant loans and advances to any public sector undertakings or other undertakings for the time being in force in the State.

The Government may, in such manner as they think fit, the payment of principal and interest of any loan proposed to be raised by the Board under section 8. Provided that the total guarantee issued by the Government under this Act shall not exceed a sum of rupees one thousand crores. The Government shall, so long as any such guarantee is in force, lay before the State Legislature in every year during the budget session, a statement of the guarantee, if any, given during the current financial year and up to date account of the total sums, if any, which have been paid out of the Consolidated Fund of the State by reason of such guarantee or paid into the said fund towards repayment of any monies so paid out.

The Government may appoint such number of officers and staff as they consider necessary to assist the Board in the discharge of its functions and duties under this Act or on deputation through the Public Service Commission. The method of appointment, salary and allowances, discipline and other conditions of service of the staff appointed under sub-section (1) shall be such as may be specified in the scheme.

main_sections.section_title: Mode of recovery of money due to Board
main_sections.description: All sums payable by any person to the Board or recoverable by it under this Act, the scheme and all charges or expenses incurred in connection therewith shall, without prejudice to any other mode of recovery, be recoverable as arrears of public revenue due on land under the provisions of the Revenue Recovery Act for the time being in force.

main_sections.section_title: Members of Board etc. to be public servants
main_sections.description: Every member of the Board, the Fund Manager and staff of the Board appointed under sub-section (1) of section 10 shall be deemed to be public servants within the meaning of section 21 of the Indian Penal Code (Central Act 45 of 1860).

main_sections.section_title: Protection for acts done in good faith
main_sections.description: No suit or other legal proceeding shall lie against any member of the Board or any other person in respect of anything which is done in good faith or intended to be done in good faith under this Act or under the scheme.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to issue directions
main_sections.description: Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act it shall be lawful for the Government to issue directions to the Board in matters relating to State and National Policies and such directions shall be binding on the Board. The Government may, after consultation with the Board, give to the Board general directions to be followed by the Board. In the exercise of the powers and performance of its duties under this Act, the Board shall not depart from any general direction issued under sub-section (2) except with the previous permission of Government.

The Board shall cause to be maintained such books of accounts and other books in relation to its accounts and prepare an annual statement of accounts and balance sheet in such form and in such manner as may be specified in the scheme. The accounts of the Board shall be audited by such auditor in such manner and at such time as the Government may, by general or special order, direct and the auditor so appointed shall have such powers of requiring the production of documents and the furnishing of information in respect of such matters. The accounts of the Board as certified by the auditor together with the audit report thereon shall be forwarded annually to the Government who may cause such directions to be made them fit and the Board shall comply with such directions.

main_sections.section_title: Annual report and audited statement of accounts
main_sections.description: The annual report of the Board shall be prepared under the direction of the Board and after approval by the Board, a copy of the report shall be submitted to Government before the end of July every year. The Government shall, as soon as the annual report is received, cause the same together with the audited statement of accounts to be laid on the table of the Legislative Assembly.

important_rules: All moneys specified in sub-section (2) shall be deposited into the public account of the Government or with the approval of the Government in any Nationalised Bank and the said account shall be operated by the Fund Manager.
Subject to the provisions of this Act, the scheme framed under sub-section (1) may provide for all or any of the matters specified in sub-section (4) and in the Schedule.

The scheme shall be laid, as soon as may be, after it is framed, before the Legislative Assembly while it is in session for a total period of fourteen days which may be in one session or in two successive sessions, and if, before the expiry of the session in which it is so laid or the session immediately following, the Legislative Assembly makes any modification in the scheme, the scheme shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form so, however, that any such modification shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under the scheme.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Board, the Government, and potentially public revenue recovery mechanisms.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Revenue Recovery Act for recovery of sums due, and through directions issued by the Government to the Board.

rights: Right to borrow sums required for the purposes of the Act.
Right to grant loans and advances to public sector undertakings or other undertakings.
Right to issue directions to the Board (Government).
duties: Duty to maintain books of accounts and prepare an annual statement of accounts and balance sheet.
Duty to submit the annual report and audited statement of accounts to the Government.
Duty to comply with general directions issued by the Government.
obligations: Obligation to deposit moneys into the public account of the Government or a Nationalised Bank.
Obligation to operate the said account by the Fund Manager.
Obligation to lay the annual report and audited statement of accounts before the Legislative Assembly.

key_procedures: Framing of the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Scheme by the Government.
Constitution of the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board by the Government.
Appointment of officers and staff for the Board.
Sanctioning of financial assistance to undertakings by the Board.
Recovery of amounts due to the Board from assisted undertakings.
Auditing of the Board's accounts by an auditor appointed by the Government.
Submission of annual reports and audited statements of accounts to the Government.
Laying of annual reports and audited statements of accounts before the Legislative Assembly.
administration: The Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board, with the Chief Secretary to Government of Kerala as Chairman and the Secretary (Finance Resources) as Fund Manager.
important_notes: The Act was enacted in the Fiftieth Year of the Republic of India.
The Act came into force on the 11th day of November, 1999.
The total guarantee issued by the Government under this Act shall not exceed a sum of rupees one thousand crores.
Members of the Board, the Fund Manager, and staff are deemed public servants.
Protection is provided for acts done in good faith by members or persons acting under the Act or scheme.
The scheme framed under the Act shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly and can be modified.

title: The Kerala Irrigation And Water Conservation Act, 2003
purpose: The Act aims to provide for the better conservation, management, and utilization of irrigation water in the State of Kerala, and to promote efficient irrigation practices and water resource management.
scope: The Act applies to all irrigation works, water resources, and related matters within the State of Kerala. It covers owners of land, water users' associations, and government authorities involved in irrigation and water conservation.

key_definitions.padasekharam: means collection of paddy fields contiguously situated, whether owned by one or more than one person.
key_definitions.irrigation land: means any land owned, controlled or maintained by Government for the purposes of an irrigation work but shall not include a poramboke.

main_sections.section_title: Collector, Punja Special Officer or authorized officer's powers
main_sections.description: Grants the Collector, Punja Special Officer or authorized officer the power to arrange dewatering of any padasekharam, undertake dewatering work, and install machinery for the purpose of such dewatering and to execute any temporary work incidental thereto.

States that where cultivation in any padasekharam is likely to be affected by want of proper irrigation or drainage facilities, the Collector, Punja Special Officer or officer authorized by the Government shall have the power to arrange for the execution of any temporary work as is necessary to irrigate or drain the padasekharam, and the cost shall be realised from the owners.

Deals with the construction or repair of bunds or portions of bunds by joint labour or at the cost of owners of a padasekharam, where the bund has not been constructed or repaired by the owners. The Collector or authorized officer shall carry out the work and recover the cost.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and duties of Collector, Punja Special Officer and authorised officer
main_sections.description: Confers powers and duties on the Collector, Punja Special Officer or authorized officer under sub-section (1) of section 31 to exercise such powers and perform such duties as may be prescribed, for the collective benefit of the owners of a padasekharam.

Any person aggrieved by an order under this Chapter, of the Collector, Punja Special Officer or authorized officer, may, within ten days from the date of receipt of such order, file an appeal to the Government. The Government may, by notification, specially empower an officer to hear such appeals. The order of the officer shall be final.
The Government, on their own motion or on application, may revise any order of the Collector or Punja Special Officer or authorized officer, after giving the person an opportunity of being heard.

Prohibits encroachment on irrigation land. The Government may declare any project area or irrigation land as protected area and take steps to remove encroachment. No person shall let out any industrial effluent or domestic effluent to any water course without proper treatment.

main_sections.section_title: Interference with functioning of cross drainage works
main_sections.description: No person, except with written permission of the Irrigation Officer, shall obstruct the proper functioning of cross drainage works, such as culverts, aqueducts, super passages, siphons, weirs, and allied works, which are constructed with the aid of the Government for the safety of canals or channels.

main_sections.section_title: Obligation of owners in respect of works affecting safety of canals
main_sections.description: Every owner of land whose tank, well, pond or other reservoir is situated above the level of any irrigation work, shall maintain the bunds and structures in safe and efficient condition. If the owner fails to comply, the Irrigation Officer may carry out repairs and recover the cost.

main_sections.section_title: Mining or quarrying near certain works
main_sections.description: Prohibits mining or quarrying within a radius of one kilometre of any bridge, dam, check dam or any other work, structure or construction owned, controlled or maintained by the Government, a local authority or any other authority, without permission. Appeals against refusal are provided.

No person other than the Irrigation Officer, regulator or flood gate of a reservoir, canal or water course of an irrigation work owned, controlled or maintained by the Government shall operate such gates.

No person shall fish in any reservoir without the permission of the Irrigation Officer and except in accordance with terms and conditions and subject to payment of such fees as may be prescribed. Explosives or poisonous substances are prohibited for fishing.
The Government may, by notification, prohibit or regulate by licence or otherwise, navigation for commercial purpose in an irrigation work.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of letting out water from irrigation work
main_sections.description: No person, other than an Irrigation Officer or an officer duly empowered by him, shall let out water from an irrigation work owned, controlled or maintained by the Government by cutting any bund or constructing a sluice or outlet or by any other similar contrivance.

Where the Government is of opinion that it is necessary to levy a betterment contribution, they may levy it from the owner of any land benefited by any major irrigation work constructed or completed after the commencement of this Act. The contribution is levied based on the increase in the gross produce.

Specifies the method for estimating the annual increase in gross produce and calculating the betterment contribution. It is twenty times the annual increase in gross produce, or one-fourth of the sum by which the said increase exceeds the cost estimated in the manner prescribed for making such class of land fit for advantageous irrigation.
States that the betterment contribution payable under section 46 shall be paid by the owner of the land in twenty equal annual instalments, on a notice of demand issued by the authority.

main_sections.section_title: Postponement of payment of betterment contribution
main_sections.description: Allows for postponement of payment of betterment contribution in case of failure of crops in any area, as per rules made thereunder.

Empowers the Government to authorize officers or local authorities to form water users' associations by farmers in areas of every forty hectares. Details the composition, election, and roles of such associations.

Outlines the objectives of the Farmers' Association to promote and secure distribution of water, ensure adequate maintenance of irrigation system, optimize agricultural production, protect the environment, and encourage ecological balance and water budget management.

Lists the functions of the Association, including preparing water schedules, planning irrigation system operation, regulating water use, promoting economy in water use, assisting in demand and contribution collection, maintaining registers, conducting audits, and resolving disputes.

main_sections.section_title: Power to levy and collect fees
main_sections.description: Grants associations the power to levy and collect fees and such other fees as may be prescribed for carrying out their functions.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of competent authority and his functions
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to appoint a competent authority and defines their functions related to the implementation and execution of decisions taken by the association.

important_rules: No person shall occupy any irrigation land for cultivation or any other purpose and the irrigation officer shall take all necessary steps to remove encroachment on such lands.
No person shall let out any industrial effluent or domestic effluent to any water course without proper treatment.
No person, except with the written permission of the Irrigation Officer, shall obstruct the proper functioning of cross drainage works.
Every owner of land whose tank, well, pond or other reservoir is situated above the level of any irrigation work, shall maintain the bunds and structures in the safe and efficient condition.

No person shall, without the written permission of the Irrigation Officer, conduct mining or quarrying operations within a radius of one kilometre of any bridge, dam, check dam or any other work, structure or construction owned, controlled or maintained by the Government, a local authority or any other authority.

No person other than the Irrigation Officer, regulator or flood gate of a reservoir, canal or water course of an irrigation work owned, controlled or maintained by the Government shall operate such gates.

No person shall fish in any reservoir without the permission of the Irrigation Officer and except in accordance with such terms and conditions and subject to the payment of such fees as may be prescribed.
No person shall let out water from an irrigation work owned, controlled or maintained by the Government by cutting any bund or constructing a sluice or outlet or by any other similar contrivance.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Collector, Punja Special Officer, Irrigation Officer, and Government-appointed authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through orders, notices, execution of works at the cost of owners, imposition of betterment contributions, and potential legal action for non-compliance.

rights: Right to appeal against orders passed by authorities.
Right to obtain permission for certain activities like mining or fishing.
Right to a rebate of 40% on betterment contribution if paid within one year.
duties: Duty of owners to maintain bunds and structures of irrigation works.
Duty to pay betterment contribution levied by the Government.
Duty of farmers to form and participate in water users' associations.
Duty to obtain permission before undertaking activities that may affect irrigation works.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the orders issued by the competent authorities.
Obligation to ensure safe and efficient condition of irrigation related structures owned by them.
Obligation to get registered as per the rules of the farmers' association.

key_procedures: Procedure for arranging dewatering or irrigation works by the Collector/authorized officer and recovery of costs.
Procedure for appeals against orders of the Collector or Punja Special Officer.
Procedure for revision of orders by the Government.
Procedure for forming and registering farmers' associations.
Procedure for levy and collection of betterment contribution and fees.
administration: Water Resources Department, Government of Kerala, and Agriculture Department.
important_notes: Explanation to Section 2(2) clarifies that the section applies to Section 33 and 34.
Explanation to Section 37 defines 'irrigation land'.
Explanation to Section 43 clarifies the scope of 'navigation for commercial purpose'.
The Act provides for a betterment contribution to be levied on lands benefited by major irrigation works.
Farmers' associations are to be registered in such manner as may be prescribed.

title: THE KERALA IRRIGATION WORKS (EXECUTION BY JOINT LABOUR) ACT, 1967
purpose: To provide for facilitating the execution of certain works connected with irrigation, flood-control or drainage for purposes of agriculture, to be done by the joint labour of cultivators, in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the entire State of Kerala. It concerns the execution of irrigation, flood-control, or drainage works by joint labour of cultivators.

key_definitions.majority of proprietors: Means the proprietors of more than one-half of a padasekharam.
key_definitions.padasekharam: Means collection of paddy fields contiguously situated, whether owned by one person or two or more persons.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.proprietor: Means the owner of any paddy field in a padasekharam and includes the cultivator or person in actual possession of such field.
key_definitions.Punja Special Officer: Means an officer appointed by the Government to exercise the powers and discharge the duties of a Punja Special Officer under this Act.
key_definitions.work: Includes the putting up of ring bunds and drainage of water.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Irrigation Works (Execution by Joint Labour) Act, 1967. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'majority of proprietors', 'padasekharam', 'prescribed', 'proprietor', 'Punja Special Officer', and 'work'.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure on failure to contribute cost or labour for work to be done by joint labour.
main_sections.description: Outlines the process when a proprietor fails to contribute cost or labour. It details how local committees, the District Collector, Punja Special Officer, or other authorized officers can ensure the work is done, recover costs from defaulting proprietors, and address refusal or failure to execute work.

Empowers the District Collector, Punja Special Officer, or other authorized officers to arrange for the dewatering of a padasekharam if proprietors fail to do so. It also covers temporary works for removal of obstruction and the recovery of costs from proprietors.

main_sections.section_title: Work not to be executed if majority of proprietors do not want the work to be executed.
main_sections.description: States that work will not be executed if the majority of proprietors do not want it, notwithstanding anything contained in sections 3 and 4, unless authorized by the Government or the District Collector, Punja Special Officer, or other authorized officer.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of District Collector, Punja Special Officer and officers authorised under section 3 or 4.
main_sections.description: Details the powers of the District Collector, Punja Special Officer, and other authorized officers regarding the exercise of functions under sections 3 and 4, including entering land, exercising powers, and performing duties related to irrigation.

Allows any person aggrieved by an order of the District Collector, Punja Special Officer, or any officer authorised under section 3 or 4 to appeal to the Government or any specified officer within a stipulated time.
Confers power upon the Government to revise any order of the District Collector, Punja Special Officer, or any officer authorised under section 3 or 4.
States that any sum of money payable under the provisions of this Act may be recovered as arrears of public revenue due on land under the provisions of the Revenue Recovery Act.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
main_sections.description: Protects the Government, officers, and persons performing functions under the Act from suits, prosecutions, or other legal proceedings for anything done or intended to be done in good faith in pursuance of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Officers and persons performing functions under the Act to be public servants.
main_sections.description: Declares that officers and persons performing functions under this Act shall be deemed to be public servants within the meaning of section 21 of the Indian Penal Code.
Grants the Government the power to make rules by notification in the Gazette to carry out the purposes of the Act. It also specifies that such rules will be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Travancore-Cochin Act VII of 1956.
main_sections.description: States that section 40A of the Travancore-Cochin Irrigation Act, 1956 (VII of 1956) shall be omitted.

important_rules: Any proprietor failing to contribute cost or labour for work connected with irrigation, flood-control, or drainage shall be liable for the cost of the work.

If a proprietor fails or neglects to do their share of work, it shall be lawful for the District Collector, the Punja Special Officer or any other officer authorized by the Government to arrange for the work to be done and recover the cost from the defaulting proprietor.

When any portion of a ring bund in a padasekharam has not been constructed or repaired properly, it shall be lawful for the District Collector, the Punja Special Officer or any other officer authorized by the Government to carry out the construction or repair and recover the cost from the proprietors liable to carry out such construction or repair.

When any cultivation in any padasekharam or in any field is likely to be affected due to want of proper irrigation or drainage facilities, the District Collector, the Punja Special Officer or any other officer authorised by the Government shall have power to arrange for temporary works for removal of obstruction to existing vachals, provision for new vachals or such other temporary works as are necessary to irrigate or drain the padasekharam or the field.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: District Collector, Punja Special Officer, and other officers authorized by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through direct execution of work, recovery of costs as arrears of public revenue, and other measures as prescribed by the Act and rules.

rights: Right to appeal against orders of the District Collector or Punja Special Officer.
Right to have irrigation, flood-control, or drainage works executed for their benefit.
duties: Duty to contribute cost or labour for the execution of works connected with irrigation, flood-control, or drainage.
Duty to participate in joint labour for the execution of such works.
obligations: Obligation to bear the cost of work if defaulting in contribution.

key_procedures: Procedure for executing works when a proprietor fails to contribute cost or labour: The District Collector, Punja Special Officer, or authorized officer can arrange for the work to be done and recover costs.
Procedure for appealing orders: Aggrieved persons can appeal to the Government or a specified officer.
Procedure for rule making: The Government can make rules by notification in the Gazette.
administration: The Government of Kerala (implied, as it is a State Act and powers are vested in Government appointed officers).
important_notes: The Act was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 174, dated 4th September, 1967.
Officers and persons performing functions under the Act are deemed public servants.
Section 40A of the Travancore-Cochin Irrigation Act, 1956 (VII of 1956) has been omitted by this Act.

title: THE KERALA IRRIGATION WORKS (EXECUTION BY JOINT LABOUR) AMENDMENT ACT, 1969
purpose: To amend the Kerala Irrigation Works (Execution by Joint Labour) Act, 1967, for the purpose hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Irrigation Works (Execution by Joint Labour) Act, 1967.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Irrigation Works (Execution by Joint Labour) Amendment Act, 1969.

After section 10 of the Kerala Irrigation Works (Execution by Joint Labour) Act, 1967 (20 of 1967), the following section shall be inserted, namely:
"10A. Suit or application for the issue of an injunction.—Save as otherwise provided in section 10, all claims in respect of anything done under this Act may be tried by the civil court, but no such court shall entertain a suit or application for the issue of an injunction to restrain the exercise of any powers or the performance of any duties conferred or imposed by this Act upon the Government, the District Collector, the Punja Special Officer or any other officer or person authorised under section 3 or section 4, except where the result of the exercise of such power or the performance of such duties is solely to adjudicate the rights between private parties".

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government, District Collector, Punja Special Officer or any other authorised officer or person.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Exercise of powers and performance of duties conferred or imposed by the Act.

rights: Right to have claims in respect of anything done under the Act tried by the civil court, subject to exceptions.
duties: To perform duties conferred or imposed by the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure for adjudication of rights between private parties by civil court is excluded from the scope of injunctions, except in specific circumstances where the exercise of powers or performance of duties solely adjudicates private rights.
important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 112 dated 28th April, 1969.

title: THE KERALA IRRIGATION AND WATER CONSERVATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2006
purpose: To amend the Kerala Irrigation and Water Conservation Act, 2003 for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and concerns irrigation and water conservation.

key_definitions.custodian: Means any State Government, or any local authority, body corporate, association of persons or an individual, who under any law, contract, treaty, agreement, order, judgement or decree has been granted the right to establish, or has established or is running or otherwise operating any dam within the State of Kerala.
key_definitions.scheduled_dam: Means any dam included in the SECOND SCHEDULE or any dam which may be notified by the Government from time to time as a scheduled dam.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Irrigation and Water Conservation (Amendment) Act, 2006. It shall come into force at once.
Inserts new clauses (1) after clause (j) and (2) after clause (al) in section 2 of the principal Act, defining 'custodian' and 'scheduled dam'.

Amends sub-section (1) and (2) of section 57 of the principal Act by deleting certain words and inserting new sub-section (3). It states that provisions in this Chapter are in addition to and not in derogation of any other laws.

Amends section 59 by renumbering sub-section (1) and deleting certain words. It also adds a new sub-section (2) stating that the quorum at the meeting of the Authority shall not be less than fifty per cent of the total number of members of the Authority.

Substitutes section 62 of the principal Act with new provisions detailing the functions of the Authority, including evaluating safety and security of dams, conducting periodical inspections, advising on security measures against terrorism, sabotage, and directing custodians to carry out necessary alterations or suspensions of dam functions. It also includes provisions for directing government or any other agency to take possession and control of a dam and for the authority to issue directions. It also gives the Authority powers regarding advice or recommendation received.

Inserts new sections 62A and 62B. Section 62A defines 'Scheduled dams' and states that the provisions of this Act related to Scheduled dams and their impediments shall not be altered except in accordance with the provisions of this Act. Section 62B outlines the 'Powers of the Authority' concerning applications for consent in writing for increasing, augmenting, adding to or expanding storage capacity or water spread area of Maximum Water Level or Full Reservoir Level of Civil Courts.

Inserts new section 68A titled 'Protection of action and immunities from challenge etc.'. It states that no suit, prosecution or other legal proceedings shall lie against the Authority or any officer or employee in respect of anything done in good faith or intended to be done in the discharge of official duties under this Act. It also states that no civil court shall have jurisdiction to settle, decide, or deal with any question of fact or to determine any matter which is by or under this Act required to be settled, decided or dealt with or to be determined by the Authority under this Act.
Inserts the Second Schedule, which lists 'Scheduled dams' with details like SI No., Name of Dam, Year of Completion, and Full Reservoir Level Fixed.

important_rules: The quorum at the meeting of the Authority shall not be less than fifty per cent of the total number of members of the Authority.

No suit, prosecution or other legal proceedings shall lie against the Authority or any officer or employee in respect of anything done in good faith or intended to be done in the discharge of official duties under this Act.

Any act or work or preparation by any custodian or any other agency in progress on the date of commencement of the Kerala Irrigation and Water Conservation (Amendment) Act, 2006 shall immediately be stopped and the Government, custodian, or any other agency shall submit an application to obtain prior consent of the Authority for such intended increase, augmentation, addition or expansion of the storage capacity or for increase of Full Reservoir Level of Scheduled dam.

rights: Right to establish, or has established or is running or otherwise operating any dam within the State of Kerala (for custodians).
duties: Official duties of officers and employees of the Authority.
Duties of custodians to obtain prior consent of the Authority for certain actions related to dams.
obligations: Obligation of the Government, custodian, or any other agency to submit an application to the Authority for intended increase, augmentation, addition or expansion of storage capacity or Full Reservoir Level of Scheduled dam.

key_procedures: Application for consent for dam modifications: Custodians must submit an application to the Authority for obtaining prior consent for any intended increase, augmentation, addition or expansion of storage capacity or Full Reservoir Level of Scheduled dam.

Issuance of directions by the Authority: Where a direction is issued by the Authority under sub-section (1) to the custodian or any other agency, it shall take immediate measures within the time frame stipulated by the Authority or do or refrain from doing such things within such time frame as may be stipulated, to comply with the directions of the Authority.
Judicial proceedings regarding dams: Proceedings before the Authority shall be deemed to be a judicial proceeding within the meaning of section 193 and 228 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
administration: The Authority established under the Act.
important_notes: The provisions of this Act are in addition to and not in derogation of any other provisions contained in any other law.

No civil court shall have jurisdiction to settle, decide, or deal with any question of fact or to determine any matter which is by or under this Act required to be settled, decided or dealt with or to be determined by the Authority under this Act.
The Second Schedule, containing a list of 'Scheduled dams', is an integral part of the Act.

title: The Kerala Jewellery Workers Welfare Fund Act, 2009
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a Fund to grant relief to, to ensure the welfare of and to pay pension to the workers and self employed persons engaged in the processing of gold, silver, platinum, copper, brass, bronze, bullion, gem, pearl (except artificial pearl) and manufacturing jewellery or figures or other products by using it or its alloy and product and doing other connected works in the State of Kerala and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to workers and self-employed persons engaged in the processing of gold, silver, platinum, copper, brass, bronze, bullion, gem, pearl (except artificial pearl) and manufacturing jewellery or figures or other products by using it or its alloy and product and doing other connected works in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.board: Kerala Jewellery Workers' Welfare Fund Board
key_definitions.chief_executive_officer: Chief Executive Officer appointed under sub-section (1) of section 21
key_definitions.contribution: Sum of money payable to the Fund under section 4
key_definitions.dealer: Establishment or person or an agent engaged in the processing of gold, silver, platinum, copper, brass, bronze, bullion, gem, pearl (except artificial pearl) or buys or sells jewellery or figures or other products made by using its alloy or product
key_definitions.employer: Person who makes use of the service of one or more workers either directly or through another person, in his own establishment or in other places for manufacturing jewellery or figures or any other product by using gold, silver, platinum, copper, brass, bronze, bullion, gem, pearl (except artificial pearl) or its alloy or of modifications or other products and manufacturing or moulding any form of jewellery or figures or other products by using it and does not include a person who is working under any employer
key_definitions.family: Husband or wife, their minor children, major mentally retarded children, unmarried daughters including adopted children, father, mother and widowed daughters who are solely dependent upon the worker or self-employed person
key_definitions.fund: Kerala Jewellery Workers' Welfare Fund to be constituted under section 3
key_definitions.jewellery: Ornaments, figures, articles and other forms and of modifications, products, which are made after mixing/processing for putting on or for decorating or for any other use which are made mainly by using gold, silver, platinum, copper, brass, bronze, bullion, gem, pearl (except artificial pearl) etc or its alloy
key_definitions.member: Member of the Fund
key_definitions.nominated_person: Person nominated and includes a person who comes under the definition of family
key_definitions.person: Includes a company or an establishment or an association of individuals or a co-operative society registered or to be registered under the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969 (21 of 1969) or an association which is legal or not or trust or firm or establishment which is either religious or social
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules or schemes made under this Act
key_definitions.scheme: Kerala Jewellery Workers' Welfare Scheme framed under section 3
key_definitions.self_employed_person: Person who is really engaged himself for his livelihood mainly in the works and connected works of processing gold, silver, platinum, copper, brass, bronze, bullion, gem, pearl (except artificial pearl) or its alloy or of modifications or other products and manufacturing or moulding any form of jewellery or figures or other products by using it and does not include a person who is working under any employer
key_definitions.worker: Person who is engaged under an employer either directly or otherwise or through an agent or on contract basis, or otherwise mainly in the works and connected works of processing gold, silver, platinum, copper, brass, bronze, bullion, gem, pearl (except artificial pearl) or its alloy or modifications or other products and manufacturing or modifying any form of jewellery or figure or other products by using it
key_definitions.year: Financial year from 1st April to 31st March of the next year
key_definitions.sale_proceeds: Value of buying and selling of gold, silver, platinum, copper, brass, bronze, bullion, gem, pearl (except artificial pearl) and jewellery or figures or other products made by using that obtained after processing or its alloy or products in the State of Kerala

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Jewellery Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 2009. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'Chief Executive Officer', 'contribution', 'dealer', 'employer', 'family', 'Fund', 'jewellery', 'member', 'nominated person', 'person', 'prescribed', 'Schedule', 'Scheme', 'self employed person', 'worker', 'year', and 'sale proceeds'.

main_sections.section_title: Kerala Jewellery Workers' Welfare Fund Scheme
main_sections.description: The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, frame a scheme to be called the Kerala Jewellery Workers' Welfare Scheme for the welfare of the workers and self employed persons coming under this Act and thereafter as soon as may be possible constitute a Fund in accordance with the provisions of this Act and the Scheme. The Scheme framed under sub-section (1) may provide for all or any of the matters specified in sub-section (5) and in the Schedule. The following shall be credited to the Fund, namely— (a) the contributions specified under section 4, (b) the cess amounts received under section 5, (c) amounts borrowed by the Board under section 22, (d) compensation realised under section 29, (e) any other amount to be credited to the Fund under the provisions of the Rules and the Scheme, (f) any donation from any other source. The Fund shall vest in the Board and be administered by the Board constituted under section 19. The Fund may be utilised for all or any of the following purposes and for the partial or full implementation of that, namely— (a) for payment of pension to the following persons,— (i) to a member who had completed sixty years of age and had remitted contribution for a period not less than five years, (ii) to a person who had completed sixty years of age before the commencement of the Scheme or not eligible for membership in the Scheme but had been a worker or self employed person, for a period of ten years, subject to the provisions of the Scheme, (iii) to a member who had remitted contribution to the Fund for at least ten years continuously and is unable to do any work, for a period of two years due to permanent physical infirmity, (iv) to a person of the member’s family, on the event of the death of a member who had remitted contribution to the Fund continuously for at least ten years, in the order of preference, as may be prescribed, (b) for the payment of maternity benefits, as may be prescribed, to the woman member who had remitted contribution to the Fund continuously at least for a period of two years and not coming within the purview of the Employees State Insurance Scheme, (c) for the payment of financial assistance to the marriage of the daughters of the members and woman members who had remitted contribution to the Fund continuously at least for a period of three years, (d) for providing educational benefits or grant to the children of members who had remitted contribution to the Fund continuously at least for a period of two years, (e) for providing medical assistance, as may be prescribed, to the members and family members of the members who had remitted contribution to the Fund continuously, at least for a period of one year, for diseases like Cancer, Tuberculosis, Heart Disease, AIDS, Kidney Disease, Cerebral Hemorrhage, (f) for providing financial assistance to the family on the death of a member, as may be prescribed in the Scheme, if a member died during the tenure of his membership or within two years on the event of permanent physical infirmity, (g) for providing financial assistance, as may be prescribed, to the family of the person who died within three years after becoming a member as per the Scheme and entitled for pension, (h) for providing loan to a member for constructing house or for the repair and maintenance of the house who had remitted contribution to the Fund at least for a period of five years, (i) for providing a consolidated amount to a member, in the event of becoming unable to continue the employment, who had remitted contribution to the Fund at least for a period of five years, at such rates as may be prescribed on the basis of the number of years he had worked, (j) for implementing any other purposes as may be provided in the Scheme.

Every worker and self employed person shall pay to the Fund the sum of Rs. twenty per month as contribution. The Government shall pay to the Fund every year an amount equal to five percentage of the amount remitted by every member under sub-section (1) as contribution. The amount of contribution to be remitted as such, shall be remitted to the Fund in the manner as may be prescribed in the Scheme.

For the purpose of collecting amount to the fund, for the welfare of the jewellery workers and self employed persons, every dealer shall be liable to pay a sum amounting to 0.25% of his jewellery sale proceeds of a year to the Consolidated Fund of the Government as cess in the manner as may be prescribed. Provided that this is not applicable to dealers whose sale proceeds are less than ten lakh rupees for a year. The cess levied under sub-section (1) shall be collected from every dealer, in the manner and time as may be prescribed. The cess levied under sub-section (1) shall be in addition to any cess, duty or tax as may be levied under any other law for the time being in force. The amount collected as cess under sub-section (2) shall be credited to the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala, in the manner as may be prescribed. The amount of cess collected by the Government shall be paid to the Fund of the Board after deducting the cost of collection of such cess not exceeding one per cent of the amount collected every year, before 30th June, in such manner as may be prescribed.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint officers of the Labour Department, not below the rank of Assistant Labour Officer Grade I or other officers not below the same rank of the Government as Assessing Officers for the purposes of this Act and may fix the local limits of their jurisdiction.

Every dealer shall maintain such registers and records in the manner prescribed. The registers and records shall be maintained in the commercial establishment of the dealer and they shall be produced for verification on demand by any officer or Authority authorised by this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Furnishing of returns by the dealer
main_sections.description: Every dealer shall furnish returns showing the sale proceeds of the previous financial year to the Assessing Officer in the manner and time as may be prescribed. If any dealer liable to pay the cess under section 5 fails to furnish the return under sub-section (1), the Assessing Officer shall give a notice demanding such dealer to furnish such return before the date as may be specified in the notice.

An Assessing Officer who is in receipt of a return under section 8 shall, after making or cause to make an enquiry in such manner as he may think fit, by order, assess the amount of cess payable by the dealer.

important_rules: Every worker and self-employed person must pay Rs. 20 per month as contribution to the Fund.
The Government shall contribute annually an amount equal to five percent of the amount remitted by every member.
Dealers are liable to pay a cess amounting to 0.25% of their jewellery sale proceeds annually to the Consolidated Fund of the Government.
Dealers whose sale proceeds are less than ten lakh rupees per year are exempt from this cess.
The cess levied shall be collected from every dealer in the prescribed manner and time.
Every dealer shall maintain registers and records and produce them for verification on demand.
Dealers must furnish returns showing sale proceeds of the previous financial year to the Assessing Officer.

penalties: Enhanced punishment for second or subsequent offence (Section 27)
Offences by company (Section 28)
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Assessing Officer and other Authorities authorised by this Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment of cess, demands for returns, verification of records, and potential legal action for offences.

rights: Right to pension upon completion of sixty years of age and remitting contribution for at least five years (or ten years for those who did not have eligible membership)
Right to maternity benefits for women members
Right to financial assistance for marriage of daughters
Right to educational benefits for children
Right to medical assistance for specified diseases
Right to financial assistance for family on death of member
Right to loan for house construction/repair
Right to a consolidated amount upon becoming unable to continue employment
duties: Duty to pay monthly contribution (workers and self-employed)
Duty to furnish returns by dealers
Duty to maintain registers and records by dealers
obligations: Obligation for dealers to pay cess.
Obligation for workers and self-employed persons to contribute to the fund.

key_procedures: Scheme formulation and notification by the Government.
Constitution of the Fund and Board.
Collection of contributions and cess.
Appointment of Assessing Officers.
Maintenance of registers and furnishing of returns by dealers.
Assessment of cess payable by dealers.
Application for benefits from the Fund (e.g., pension, maternity benefits, financial assistance, loans) as per Scheme provisions.
Appeal process for decisions made under the Act.
administration: The Board constituted under section 19 administers the Fund. The Government has powers to notify schemes, appoint officers, and make rules.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 1st day of August, 2009 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 1413, dated 1st August, 2009.

The Scheme framed under sub-section (1) of Section 3 shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is framed, before the Legislative Assembly while it is in session for a total period of fourteen days which may be comprised in one session or in two successive sessions and, if before the expiry of the session in which it is so laid or the session immediately following, the Legislative Assembly makes any amendment in the Scheme, the Scheme shall thereafter have effect only in such amended form.
Any amendment to the Scheme shall not prejudice the validity of anything previously done under the Scheme.
The cess levied is not applicable to dealers with sale proceeds less than ten lakh rupees per year.
The cost of collection of cess by the Government shall not exceed one per cent of the amount collected every year.

title: THE KERALA JOINT HINDU FAMILY SYSTEM (ABOLITION) ACT, 1975
purpose: To abolish the joint family system among Hindus in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Joint Hindu Family: Any Hindu family with community of property and includes— (1) a tarwad or thavazhi governed by the Madras Marumakkathayam Act, 1932, the Travancore Nayar Act, II of 1100, the Travancore Ezhava Act, III of 1100, the Nanjinad Vellala Act of 1101, the Travancore Kshatriya Act of 1108, the Travancore Krishnavaka Marumakkathayee Act, VII of 1115, the Cochin Nayar Act, XXIX of 1113, or the Cochin Marumakkathayam Act, XXXIII of 1113, (2) a kutumba or kavaru governed by the Madras Ahyasanthana Act, 1949, (3) an illom governed by the Kerala Nambudiri Act, 1958, and (4) an undivided Hindu family governed by the Mitakshara law.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Joint Hindu Family System (Abolition) Act, 1975, extends to the whole of the State of Kerala, and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint. (Received the assent of the President on the 10th August 1976 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 484, dated 17th August, 1976).
Defines "Joint Hindu Family" as described in the key definitions.

main_sections.section_title: Birth in family not to give rise to rights in property.
main_sections.description: States that after the commencement of this Act, no right to claim any interest in any property of an ancestor, during his or her lifetime, which is founded on the mere fact that the claimant was born in the family of the ancestor, shall be recognised in any court.

main_sections.section_title: Joint tenancy to be replaced by tenancy in common.
