main_sections.description: Declares that all members of an Undivided Hindu Family governed by the Mitakshara law holding any coparcenary property on the day the Act comes into force shall, with effect from that day, be deemed to hold it as tenants-in-common as if a partition had taken place among all the members that they would hold their respective property and if each one of them is holding his or her share separately as full owner thereof. Provided that nothing in this sub-section shall affect the right to maintenance or the right to marriage or funeral expenses out of the coparcenary property or the right to residence, if any, of the members of an undivided Hindu family, other than persons who have been entitled to hold their shares separately, and any such right can be enforced as if this Act had not been passed.

main_sections.section_title: Rule of pious obligation of Hindu son abrogated.
main_sections.description: States that after the commencement of this Act, no court shall, save as provided in sub-section (2), recognise any right to proceed against a son, grandson or great-grandson for the recovery of any debt due from his father, grandfather or great-grandfather or any alienation of property in respect of or in satisfaction of any such debt on the ground of the pious obligation under the Hindu law, of the son, grandson or great-grandson to discharge any such debt. (2) In the case of any debt contracted before the commencement of this Act, nothing contained in sub-section (1) shall affect (a) the right of any creditor to proceed against the son, grandson or great-grandson, as the case may be, or (b) any alienation made in respect of, or in satisfaction of, any such debt, and any such right or alienation shall be enforceable to the same extent as it would have been enforceable if this Act had not been passed. Explanation: For the purposes of sub-section (2), the expression "son", "grandson" or "great-grandson" shall be deemed to refer to the son, grandson or great-grandson, as the case may be, who was born or adopted prior to the commencement of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of members of Joint Hindu Family for debts contracted before Act not affected.
main_sections.description: States that where a debt binding on a Joint Hindu Family has been contracted before the commencement of this Act by the Kartha, Yejman, Manager or Kartha, as the case may be, of the family, nothing herein contained shall effect the liability of any member of the family to discharge any such debt, and any such liability may be enforced against all or any of the members liable therefor in the same manner and to the same extent as it would have been enforceable if this Act had not been passed.

States that (1) Save as otherwise expressly provided in this Act, any text, rule or interpretation of Hindu Law or any custom or usage as part of that law in force immediately before the commencement of this Act shall cease to have effect with respect to any matter for which provision is made in this Act. (2) The Acts mentioned in the Schedule, in so far as they apply to the whole or any part of the State of Kerala, are hereby repealed.

important_rules: No new right to claim interest in ancestral property based solely on birth in the family shall be recognised after the Act commences.
Joint tenancy in coparcenary property will be treated as tenancy in common from the commencement of the Act.
The pious obligation of a Hindu son to discharge his father's, grandfather's, or great-grandfather's debt is abrogated for debts contracted after the commencement of the Act.

rights: Right to hold shares separately as full owner (subject to certain provisos)
Right to maintenance or marriage or funeral expenses out of coparcenary property (for members other than those holding separate shares)
Right to residence (for members other than those holding separate shares)
obligations: Members of an undivided Hindu family are deemed to hold property as tenants-in-common.

important_notes: The Act received the assent of the President on the 10th August 1976 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 484, dated 17th August, 1976.
The definition of "Joint Hindu Family" includes various customary laws specific to different communities in Kerala.
Provisions regarding debts contracted before the commencement of the Act are preserved.
The repeal of certain Acts is listed in the Schedule.
The commencement date of the Act is to be notified by the Government.

title: The Kerala Public Service Commission (Additional Functions) Act, 1964
purpose: To provide for the exercise of certain additional functions by the Kerala Public Service Commission in respect of appointment of officers and servants of the Kerala State Electricity Board and their conditions of service.
scope: The Act applies to the Kerala Public Service Commission, the Kerala State Electricity Board, its officers, and servants, and matters related to their recruitment, conditions of service, and disciplinary proceedings. It also covers rules made by the Government under the Act.

key_definitions.Electricity Board: Means the Kerala State Electricity Board constituted under section 5 of the Electricity (Supply) Act, 1948.
key_definitions.Public Service Commission: Means the Kerala Public Service Commission.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Public Service Commission (Additional Functions) Act, 1963, and it shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Defines terms such as 'Electricity Board' and 'Public Service Commission' in the context of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Functions of the Public Service Commission in respect of services under the Electricity Board
main_sections.description: Outlines the functions of the Public Service Commission concerning recruitment, conditions of service, and disciplinary matters for officers and servants of the Electricity Board. It includes provisions for advising on matters referred to them, and the Government's power to make rules.

Grants the Government the power to make rules in consultation with the Public Service Commission for carrying out the purposes of the Act. These rules can cover procedures for consultation and any other incidental matters.

important_rules: Rules made under this Act by the Legislative Assembly shall be laid before it as soon as may be after it is made, and shall have effect subject to modifications if any, made by the Assembly.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through rules made by the Government and laying of such rules before the Legislative Assembly.

rights: Right of the Public Service Commission to be consulted on matters relating to recruitment, conditions of service, and disciplinary proceedings of Electricity Board employees.
Right of the Public Service Commission to advise on any matter referred to them by the Government.
Right of individuals to claim compensation for injuries sustained while serving the Electricity Board, with such costs being paid out of the Electricity Board's funds.
duties: Duty of the Public Service Commission to advise on any matter referred to them by the Government.

key_procedures: Consultation between the Government and the Public Service Commission for making rules under the Act.
Laying of rules made by the Legislative Assembly before the Assembly for a period of fourteen days in successive sessions for potential modification.
The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint the date of commencement of the Act.
administration: Government of Kerala (implied, as the Act is a Kerala State Act)
important_notes: The Act came into effect on a date appointed by the Government by notification.
Rules made under the Act are subject to modification by the Legislative Assembly.
Any modification or annulment of a rule made by the Legislative Assembly shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that rule.

title: The Kerala Khadi and Village Industries Board (Amendment) Act, 1967
purpose: To amend the Kerala Khadi and Village Industries Board Act, 1957.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Khadi and Village Industries Board and its operations.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Khadi and Village Industries Board (Amendment) Act, 1967.

Inserts a new section 4A to the Kerala Khadi and Village Industries Board Act, 1957. This new section deals with the reconstitution of the Board. It states that the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, and for reasons to be specified in the notification, reconstitute the Board in accordance with the provisions of sub-section (2) of section 4. It also specifies that when the Board is reconstituted under the provisions of sub-section (2), all members of the Board (including the Chairman and Vice-Chairman) holding office immediately before such reconstitution shall, from the date of reconstitution, vacate their offices as such members, notwithstanding that their term of office has not expired, unless they are appointed as members of the Board as so reconstituted.

important_rules: Any notification issued under sub-section (1) of section 4A shall be laid as soon as may be after it is issued before the Legislative Assembly while it is in session for a total period of fourteen days which may be comprised in one session or in two successive sessions, and if, before the expiry of the session in which it is so laid, or the session immediately following, the Legislative Assembly makes any modification in the notification or decides that the notification should not be issued, the notification shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect, as the case may be; so however that any such modification or annulment shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that notification.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications in the Gazette.

key_procedures: Reconstitution of the Board: The Government can reconstitute the Board by issuing a notification in the Gazette, provided valid reasons are specified. Upon reconstitution, existing members vacate their offices, even if their term isn't over, unless reappointed.
administration: The Kerala Khadi and Village Industries Board.
important_notes: Published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 175, dated 4th September, 1967.
The provisions of the inserted section 4A are subject to laying before and potential modification/annulment by the Legislative Assembly.

title: The Kerala Khadi And Village Industries Board (Amendment) Act, 1975
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Khadi and Village Industries Board Act, 1957, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: The Act applies to the Kerala Khadi and Village Industries Board.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Khadi and Village Industries Board (Amendment) Act, 1975. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

Amends section 4 of the Kerala Khadi and Village Industries Board Act, 1957. It adds a proviso to sub-section (2) requiring that at least one of the non-official members so appointed shall be a person belonging to a Scheduled Caste or a Scheduled Tribe.

Amends section 16 of the principal Act. It inserts clauses (iii), (iv), and (v) which relate to the Board's power to require any person granted loan or financial assistance to maintain accounts and records, to inspect accounts and records, and to supervise activities carried on by any person utilising loan or financial assistance.

Amends section 29 of the principal Act. It re-numbers sub-section (1) as sub-section (1) and inserts a new sub-section (2) requiring the Board to forward a copy of the audited annual statement of accounts referred to in sub-section (1) within two months from the end of the financial year to which such statement relates, and to lay such statement before the Legislative Assembly as soon as may be after it is received by the Government.

Inserts new sections 30A and 30B. Section 30A deals with circumstances in which the Board may be dissolved, including if the Board has made default in discharging its duties, is influenced or entrused by the Act or exceeded its powers, has disregarded Government directions, or if circumstances have arisen that render the Board unable to perform its functions. Section 30B deals with vesting of rights, liabilities, etc., of the Board on dissolution.

important_rules: Rule: At least one non-official member appointed to the Board shall belong to a Scheduled Caste or a Scheduled Tribe.
Rule: The Board has the power to require recipients of loans or financial assistance to maintain accounts and records and to allow inspection of these.
Rule: The Board may supervise activities funded by its loans or financial assistance and issue directions.
Rule: The Board must forward its audited annual statement of accounts to the Government within two months of the financial year end.
Rule: The audited annual statement of accounts must be laid before the Legislative Assembly.
Rule: The Government can dissolve the Board under specific circumstances outlined in section 30A.
Rule: Upon dissolution, all rights, obligations, liabilities, properties, and functions of the Board shall vest in the Government.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government, Board, or its officers/authorities as specified.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notification in the Gazette, inspections, directions, and by vesting of assets upon dissolution.

rights: Right of the Government to dissolve the Board under certain conditions.
Right of the Government to take over the rights, liabilities, properties, and functions of the Board upon dissolution.
duties: Duty of the Board to require proper maintenance and inspection of accounts related to loans and financial assistance.
Duty of the Board to forward its audited annual statement of accounts to the Government.
Duty of the Board to lay the audited annual statement of accounts before the Legislative Assembly.

key_procedures: Procedure: Notification by the Government for commencement of the Act.
Procedure: Appointment of Board members with at least one from Scheduled Caste/Tribe.
Procedure: Inspection of accounts and records related to loans/assistance.
Procedure: Submission and laying of audited annual financial statements before the Legislative Assembly.
Procedure: Dissolution of the Board by Government notification.
Procedure: Vesting of Board's assets and liabilities in the Government upon dissolution.
administration: The Kerala Khadi and Village Industries Board, under the purview of the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The amendment received the assent of the Governor on the 20th day of May, 1975, and was published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 258, dated 21st May 1975.
The expressions "Scheduled Caste" and "Scheduled Tribe" have the same meaning as in the Constitution of India.

title: THE KERALA KHADI AND VILLAGE INDUSTRIES BOARD (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1960
purpose: To amend the Kerala Khadi and Village Industries Board Act, 1957.
scope: The Act applies to the Kerala Khadi and Village Industries Board and its functions.

key_definitions.Board: The Kerala Khadi and Village Industries Board.
key_definitions.secretary: Means the secretary to the Board appointed under sub-section (1) of section 10.
key_definitions.official non-officials: Non-officials who have shown an active interest in the production and development of khadi or in the development of village industries, and officials.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Khadi and Village Industries Board (Amendment) Act, 1960, and provides for its commencement.
Amends section 2 of the principal Act by inserting new clauses, including definitions for 'Khadi and Village Industries Commission' and 'secretary', and specifying the composition of the Board.
Amends section 4 of the principal Act, modifying provisions related to the appointment and roles of the Chairman and Vice-chairman, and the composition of the Board.
Amends section 6 of the principal Act, concerning the powers and duties of the Board.
Amends section 9 of the principal Act, dealing with how the Chairman and other members shall be omitted.

Inserts a new section 9A, titled 'Temporary association of persons with the Board for particular purposes', which allows the Board to associate persons for specific functions without giving them voting rights.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 10.
main_sections.description: Substitutes section 10, dealing with the Secretary and other members of staff of the Board, including their appointment, remuneration, and duties.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 11.
main_sections.description: Substitutes section 11, concerning Standing Finance Committees and other committees, and the Board's power to appoint committees for specific purposes.
Amends section 12 of the principal Act, relating to the powers and functions of the Board.
Amends section 14 of the principal Act, concerning the Chairman and other members.

Amends section 15 of the principal Act, relating to the powers of the Board to grant loans and give other assistance for the development of Khadi and Village Industries, and to arrange for the supply of raw materials and tools.

Amends section 16 of the principal Act, by inserting a proviso to clause (i) of sub-section (1) that the previous sanction of the Government is not necessary for any lease, sale or transfer of immovable property to the Khadi and Village Industries Commission.
Inserts a new section 19A, titled 'Power of Board to alter scheme', allowing the Board to alter schemes with previous approval, provided aggregate amounts sanctioned do not exceed specified limits.

Amends section 23 of the principal Act by adding a proviso, stating that the previous sanction of the Government shall not be necessary to borrow any sum from the Khadi and Village Industries Commission.

Amends section 25 of the principal Act, re-numbering sub-section (1) and adding a new sub-section (2) that no sum shall be expended by or on behalf of the Board unless expenditure is covered by a specific provision in the budget approved by the Government.
Inserts new sections 29A and 29B. Section 29A deals with the recovery of arrears, and section 29B empowers the Board to write off irrecoverable amounts up to two thousand rupees.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 30.
main_sections.description: Substitutes section 30, concerning the power of the Government to give directions to the Board.
Amends section 33 of the principal Act by inserting new clauses related to remuneration, allowances, and other conditions of service, and powers to be exercised by the secretary.

Amends section 34 of the principal Act, relating to the Standing Finance Committee, its appointment, and the procedure to be followed by committees in discharging their functions, including maintenance of minutes of meetings and transmission of copies to the Government.

important_rules: No sum shall be expended by or on behalf of the Board unless such expenditure is covered by a specific provision in the budget approved by the Government under sub-section (1) of section 25.
The Board may, within the limits of the budget, sanction any reappropriation from one head of expenditure to another or from a provision made for one scheme to that in respect of another.
The previous sanction of the Government is not necessary for any lease, sale or other transfer of immovable property to the Khadi and Village Industries Commission.

The Board may, by order, depute one or more officers of the Government to attend any meetings of the Board and to take part in the discussions of the Board, but such officers or officials shall not have the right to vote.

penalties: Recovery of arrears (Section 29A)
Write off irrecoverable amounts up to two thousand rupees in each case (Section 29B)
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Kerala Khadi and Village Industries Board, and the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through provisions for recovery of arrears and by the Government's power to give directions.

rights: Right to borrow sums from the Khadi and Village Industries Commission without Government sanction (Section 23).
Right to alter schemes with previous approval (Section 19A).
Right to write off irrecoverable amounts up to two thousand rupees per case (Section 29B).
duties: Duty to manage and discharge functions related to Khadi and Village Industries.
Duty of the Standing Finance Committee to perform functions relating to finances of the Board.
Duty to arrange for supply of raw materials, tools and implements for Khadi and Village Industries.
Duty to provide deserving persons with gainful employment through organisation of Khadi and Village Industries.
obligations: Expenditure must be covered by the budget approved by the Government.
The Board is bound by directions given by the Government.

key_procedures: Procedure for the Board to sanction reappropriation of funds within the budget.
Procedure for the Board to appoint committees for specific purposes.
Procedure for the Standing Finance Committee to perform its functions.
Procedure for the appointment and discharge of duties of the Secretary.
Procedure for the Board to alter schemes with previous approval.
Procedure for recovery of arrears.
administration: The Kerala Khadi and Village Industries Board, with oversight from the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act commenced on the date of its publication in the Gazette Extraordinary, August 20, 1960.
The Board shall consist of official and non-official members.
The Government may depute officers to attend Board meetings but they shall not have voting rights.
Expenditure must be within the budget and sanctioned by the appropriate authority.

title: The Kerala Khadi and Village Industries Board (Amendment) Act, 1965
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Khadi and Village Industries Board Act, 1957.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Khadi and Village Industries Board, established under the Kerala State Legislature (Delegation of Powers) Act, 1957.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act and states that it shall come into force at once.

This section amends section 4 of the Kerala Khadi and Village Industries Board Act, 1957. It likely relates to the composition of the Board, specifically mentioning the substitution of 'The Chairman, Vice-Chairman and other members' with 'the Chairman, Vice-Chairman and other members' in sub-section (2) and potentially other parts of section 4. It also states that the Board shall consist of not less than five and not more than fifteen members appointed by the Government, and provides for the nomination of a Chairman and another member from among non-official members. It further clarifies that the Vice-Chairman shall be nominated from among the non-official members.

This section amends section 14 of the principal Act (The Kerala Khadi and Village Industries Board Act, 1957) by substituting certain words. The exact substitution is not fully visible, but it involves 'the Chairman, Vice-Chairman and other members'.

This section amends section 33 of the principal Act (The Kerala Khadi and Village Industries Board Act, 1957) by substituting certain words. The exact substitution is not fully visible, but it involves 'the Chairman, Vice-Chairman and other members'.

administration: The Kerala Khadi and Village Industries Board
important_notes: Published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 113, dated the 19th October, 1965.

title: The Kerala Khadi workers welfare fund Act, 1989
purpose: To provide for the establishment and administration of a fund for the welfare of Khadi workers in the State of Kerala.
scope: This Act applies to Khadi workers in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.khadi_worker: Means a person engaged in the production of Khadi.
key_definitions.fund: Means the Kerala Khadi Workers Welfare Fund established under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and its commencement date.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'Fund', 'Khadi Worker', 'Board', etc.
Establishes the Kerala Khadi Workers Welfare Fund and outlines its sources of income.
Specifies the purposes for which the Fund can be utilized, including medical aid, education, marriage, and retirement benefits for Khadi workers.
Provides for the constitution of a Board to administer the Fund.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of the Board
main_sections.description: Details the powers and functions of the Board in managing and administering the Fund.

important_rules: Contributions to the Fund shall be made by the Government, employers, and Khadi workers.
The Board shall frame regulations for the administration of the Fund.
The accounts of the Fund shall be audited annually.

penalties: Penalty for contravention of the provisions of the Act or rules.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Board constituted under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through regulations framed by the Board and penalties prescribed for non-compliance.

rights: Right of Khadi workers to receive benefits from the Fund.
duties: Duty of employers to contribute to the Fund.
Duty of Khadi workers to adhere to the rules for claiming benefits.

key_procedures: Procedure for applying for benefits from the Fund.
Procedure for contribution to the Fund by employers and workers.
Procedure for auditing the accounts of the Fund.
administration: The Kerala Khadi Workers Welfare Fund Board.
important_notes: The Act may be amended by the State Legislature.
The Government may frame rules to carry out the provisions of the Act.

title: The Kerala Kissan Pass Book Act, 2005
purpose: To provide for the issue of Pass Books to agriculturists and to make provision for certain matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to agriculturists in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Agriculturist: A person who cultivates land in the State either as owner, tenant or otherwise.
key_definitions.Pass Book: A book issued under this Act to an agriculturist containing particulars of his land, cultivation, etc.

main_sections.description: This section provides for the short title of the Act and its commencement.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'agriculturist', 'land', 'pass book', etc.
Lays down the procedure for the issue of Pass Books to agriculturists.
Specifies the details that should be included in the Pass Book.

main_sections.section_title: Correction and updating of Pass Book
main_sections.description: Deals with the process of correcting and updating the information in the Pass Book.
Obligates agriculturists to produce their Pass Book when required by competent authority.
Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: An agriculturist shall apply for a Pass Book within such period and in such manner as may be prescribed.
The Pass Book shall contain particulars of the land held by the agriculturist, crops cultivated, etc.
The Pass Book shall be updated whenever there is any change in the particulars contained therein.

penalties: Penalty for failure to produce Pass Book or for furnishing false information.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Competent authority appointed by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the requirement of producing the Pass Book and imposing penalties for non-compliance or false information.

rights: Right to obtain a Pass Book.
Right to have the Pass Book corrected and updated.
duties: Duty to apply for a Pass Book.
Duty to produce the Pass Book when required.
Duty to keep the Pass Book updated.
obligations: Obligation to furnish correct information for the Pass Book.

key_procedures: Procedure for application for a Pass Book.
Procedure for correction and updating of a Pass Book.
administration: Department of Agriculture, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act aims to provide a reliable record of an agriculturist's land and activities, which can be useful for various agricultural schemes and subsidies.
The Pass Book serves as proof of identity and entitlement for agriculturists.

title: The Kerala Labour Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 1994
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1975, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1975.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title as "The Kerala Labour Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 1994" and states that it shall come into force at once.

Amends section 2 of the Kerala Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1975. It substitutes 'two thousand and five hundred rupees' for 'seventy-five rupees' in sub-clause (d) of clause (1) and substitutes 'five' with 'two' for the word 'five' in sub-clause (iv) of clause (f).

Amends section 15 of the principal Act. It substitutes 'four rupee' and 'eight rupees' with 'two rupees' and 'seven rupees' respectively in sub-section (1), item (i), for the words "one rupee" and "two rupees".

Amends section 20 of the principal Act. It inserts the words "invest the same", the words "deposit the same in Government Treasuries or in nationalised banks or in scheduled banks or in district co-operative bank or" before the words "invest the same".

important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 24th day of March 1994 and published in the Kerala Gazette extraordinary No. 264, dated the 25th March, 1994.

title: THE KERALA LABOUR WELFARE FUND ACT, 1975 (Act II of 1977)
purpose: An Act to provide for the constitution of a fund for promoting the welfare of labour and for certain other matters connected therewith in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala. The Act's scope primarily concerns the welfare of labour, including provisions for a fund, contributions, and related matters.

key_definitions.board: Means the Kerala Labour Welfare Fund Board established under section 4.
key_definitions.commissioner: Means the Labour Welfare Fund Commissioner appointed under section 22.
key_definitions.contribution: Means the sum of money payable to the Board in accordance with the provisions of section 15.
key_definitions.employee: Means (i) any person who is employed for hire or reward to do any work skilled or unskilled, manual, supervisory, clerical or technical in an establishment for a period of one hundred and fifty days in a year, whether the terms of employment be express or implied, but does not include any person - (A) who is employed mainly in a managerial capacity; or (B) who draws wages exceeding seven hundred and fifty rupee per mensem or exercises either by the nature of the duties attached to the office or by reason of the powers vested in him, functions mainly of a managerial nature; or (C) who is employed as an apprentice or on part-time basis. Explanation.-An apprentice means a person who, according to the certified standing orders applicable to the establishment, is an apprentice or who is declared to be an apprentice by the authority specified in this behalf by the Government; and (ii) any other person employed in any establishment, whom the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, declare to be an employee for the purposes of this Act.
key_definitions.employer: Means a person who employs either directly or through another person, either on behalf of himself or any other person, one or more employees or in an establishment and includes - (i) in a factory, any person named under clause (f) of sub-section (1) of section 7 of the Factories Act, 1948 (Central Act 63 of 1948), as the manager; (ii) in any establishment, any person responsible to the owner for the supervision and control of the employees or for the payment of wages; (f) "establishment" includes - (i) a factory as defined in clause (m) of section 2 of the Factories Act, 1948 (Central Act 63 of 1948) or any place which is deemed to be a factory under sub-section (2) of section 83 of that Act; (ii) a motor transport undertaking as defined in clause (g) of section 2 of the Motor Transport Workers Act, 1961 (Central Act 27 of 1961); (iii) a plantation as defined in clause (f) of section 2 of the Plantations Labour Act, 1951 (Central Act 64 of 1951); (iv) any commercial establishment within the meaning of clause (4) of section 2 of the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1960 (34 of 1960), which employs, or on any working day during the preceding twelve months employed, five or more persons : Provided that any such commercial establishment shall continue to be an establishment for the purposes of this Act notwithstanding that there was a reduction in the number of persons to less than five at any subsequent time : Provided further that where for a continuous period of not less than six months the number of persons employed therein has been less than five, such commercial establishment shall cease to be an establishment for the purposes of this Act with effect from the beginning of the month following the expiry of the said period of six months, but employer shall, within one month from the date of such cessation, intimate by registered post the fact thereof to such authority as the Government may specify in this behalf; (v) an establishment, including a society registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 (Central Act 21 of 1860) or the Travancore-Cochin Literary, Scientific and Charitable Societies Registration Act, 1955 (XII of 1955), which carries on any business or trade or any work, in connection therewith or an cillary thereto and which employs, or on any working day during the preceding twelve months employed, more than twenty persons, but does not include an establishment (not being a factory) of the Central or any State Government; (vi) any other establishment which the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, declare to be an establishment for the purposes of this Act; (g) "Fund" means the Labour Welfare Fund constituted under section 3; (h) "Inspector" means an Inspector appointed under section 24; (i) "prescribed" means prescribed by rules made under this Act; (j) "State" means the State of Kerala; (k) "unpaid accumulation" means all payments other than gratuity due to an employee but not paid to him within a period of three years from the date on which the payments became due, whether before or after the commencement of this Act, and the gratuity accrued to an employee after the commencement of this Act but not paid within a period of three years from the date of such accrual, but does not include the amount of contribution, if any, paid by an employer to a provident fund established under the Employees' Provident Funds Act, 1952 (Central Act 19 of 1952) or any other provident fund established by the Government; (1) "wages" means wages as defined in clause (vi) of section 2 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 (Central Act 4 of 1936).

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1975. It also specifies that it extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different areas of the State.

This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'Commissioner', 'contribution', 'employee', 'employer', 'establishment', 'Fund', 'Inspector', 'prescribed', 'State', 'unpaid accumulation', and 'wages'.

This section outlines the constitution of a Fund called the Labour Welfare Fund. It specifies that the Government shall constitute such a Fund and that nothing contained in any other law for the time being in force or in any contract or instrument shall affect any unpaid accumulations, which shall be paid to the Board. It also details what shall be credited to the Fund.

This section deals with the establishment of the Labour Welfare Fund Board. It states that the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint a Board by the name 'Kerala Labour Welfare Fund Board' and that the Board shall be a body corporate having perpetual succession and a common seal, and shall, by the said name, sue and be sued.

This section describes the composition of the Board. It states that the Board shall consist of the Government servants appointed by the Government, namely (a) such number of representatives of employers and employees as may be prescribed, provided that both employers and employees shall have equal representation on the Board; and (b) such number of officials and non-officials as may be prescribed. It also mentions that the Government shall appoint one of the members of the Board to be its Chairman.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Chairman, and other members to be notified
main_sections.description: This section states that the appointment of the Chairman and other members of the Board shall be notified in the Gazette.

This section defines the term of office for members of the Board. The term of office for members of the Board other than the official members shall be three years from the date of their appointment and they shall be eligible for reappointment. Provided that a member may continue as such member until the appointment of his successor.

This section outlines the conditions under which a person shall not be chosen as, or continue to be, a member of the Board. These include being an insolvent or serving under the Government, being undischarged unsound mind, having been convicted by a criminal court for an offence involving moral turpitude unless such conviction has been set aside, or being in arrears of any sum due to the Board. It also states that the Government may remove any member who is or has become subject to any of the disqualifications mentioned in sub-section (1) or is absent without leave of the Board for more than three consecutive meetings.

main_sections.section_title: Resignation of office by member and filling up casual vacancies
main_sections.description: This section covers the resignation of members and the filling of casual vacancies. Any member other than an official member may resign his office by giving notice thereof in writing to the Government, and on such resignation being accepted, shall be deemed to have vacated his office. A casual vacancy in the office of a member may be filled up, as soon as may be, by the Government and a member so appointed to fill such vacancy shall hold office for the unexpired portion of the term of office of the member whose place he fills.

This section grants the Board the power to appoint committees for the purpose of advising it and for carrying into effect any of the matters specified in sub-section (3) of section 17, the Board may constitute one or more committees. Each committee constituted under sub-section (1) shall consist of atleast one member of the Board.

main_sections.section_title: Acts of Board or committee not to be invalidated by informality, vacancy, etc.
main_sections.description: This section clarifies that no act done or proceeding taken under this Act by the Board or any committee shall be invalid merely on the ground of any defect or irregularity in the appointment of a person acting as a member thereof; or of any defect or irregularity in such act or proceeding not affecting the merits of the case.
This section details the functions of the Board, which are to administer the Fund and such other functions as may be assigned to it by or under this Act.

This section addresses unpaid accumulations. It states that all unpaid accumulations shall be paid to the Board. Any unpaid accumulation paid to the Board in accordance with the provisions of section 3 shall, on such payment, discharge an employer of his liability to make payment to an employee in respect thereof, but to the extent only of the amount paid to the Board, and the liability to make payment to the employee to the extent aforesaid shall, subject to the succeeding provisions of this section, be deemed to be transferred to the Board. It also outlines the procedure for dealing with unpaid accumulations after two years from the date of becoming due, including notice and claim processes.

main_sections.section_title: Interest on unpaid accumulations or fines after notice of demand
main_sections.description: This section specifies that if any unpaid accumulation is not paid to the Board within one month from the date of the notice of demand, the employer shall be liable to pay interest on such amount at such rate as may be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Contribution to the Fund by employees and employers
main_sections.description: This section covers the contributions to the Fund. It states that the Government shall, by notification in the Gazette, specify the employer and the employees to whom the provisions of this Act shall apply. It also details the nature of contributions, which may include unpaid accumulations, fines, employer contributions, interest on unpaid accumulations, etc.
This section allows the Government to make grants and advances to the Fund.

This section states that the Fund shall vest in the Board and shall be applied by the Board to meet the expenses in connection with measures for the promotion of the welfare of labour, including the provision of facilities for the treatment of diseases, grant of scholarships to the children of labour, training of labour, and such other matters as may be prescribed.
This section empowers the Board to borrow money for the purposes of the Act, subject to such conditions as may be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Deposit of Fund and placing of accounts and audit report before State Legislature
main_sections.description: This section deals with the deposit and audit of the Fund's accounts. The accounts of the Fund shall be kept in such manner and audited by such authority as may be prescribed. The audited accounts together with the audit report shall be placed before the State Legislature.
This section allows the Board to invest the Fund in such securities as may be approved by the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to give directions to Board
main_sections.description: This section grants the Government the power to give directions to the Board generally or specifically in matters of policy and administration, and the Board shall be bound to follow such directions.
This section provides for the appointment of a Commissioner and specifies their powers and functions.
This section relates to the appointment and functions of a Finance Officer.
This section deals with the appointment and powers of Inspectors.
This section allows the Board to appoint such staff as it may deem necessary for the efficient performance of its functions.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government and authorised officers to call for records etc
main_sections.description: This section grants the Government and authorized officers the power to call for records and other information.

main_sections.section_title: Mode of recovery of sums payable to Board
main_sections.description: This section outlines the methods by which sums payable to the Board can be recovered.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for obstructing Inspector or for failure to produce documents, etc.
main_sections.description: This section prescribes penalties for obstructing an Inspector or failing to produce documents.
This section specifies how offences under the Act are to be taken cognizance of.
This section addresses how offences committed by companies are to be handled.
This section sets the time limit for prosecuting offences under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power to supervise welfare activities of establishment
main_sections.description: This section grants the Government or its authorized officers the power to supervise welfare activities in establishments.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for non-compliance with the direction of the Board
main_sections.description: This section specifies penalties for failing to comply with the directions issued by the Board.
This section requires the Board to prepare an annual report of its activities.
This section outlines the circumstances and procedure for superseding the Board.
This section allows the Board to delegate its powers to certain officers.

main_sections.section_title: Members of Board, Commissioner, Inspectors, etc. to be public servants
main_sections.description: This section declares that members of the Board, Commissioner, Inspectors, and other officers appointed under the Act shall be deemed to be public servants within the meaning of the Indian Penal Code.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: This section provides protection from legal proceedings for any action taken in good faith in pursuance of the provisions of this Act or rules or regulations made thereunder.
This section allows the Government to grant exemption from the provisions of the Act to certain establishments or classes of employees.
This section empowers the Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Rules and notifications to be laid before the Legislative Assembly
main_sections.description: This section mandates that rules and notifications made under the Act shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly of the State.
This section allows the Board to make regulations for the efficient functioning of the Board.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 8, Central Act 4 of 1936
main_sections.description: This section pertains to the amendment of section 8 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936.

important_rules: Contributions to the Fund shall be paid by employers and employees as specified by the Government.
Unpaid accumulations shall be paid to the Board.
The Board shall apply the Fund for measures promoting the welfare of labour.
Actions taken in good faith in pursuance of the Act are protected.
Rules and notifications made under the Act must be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

penalties: Penalty for obstructing Inspector or for failure to produce documents, etc.
Penalty for non-compliance with the direction of the Board.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Act implies enforcement by the Commissioner, Inspectors, and other authorized officers appointed by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspection, calling for records, issuing directions, and imposing penalties for non-compliance or obstruction.

rights: Employees have a right to benefit from welfare measures funded by the Act.
Employers have a duty to contribute to the Fund and comply with the Act's provisions.
duties: Employers must pay contributions to the Fund.
Employers must comply with directions from the Board and Inspectors.
The Board has a duty to administer the Fund and implement welfare measures.
obligations: Obligation to pay unpaid accumulations to the Board.

key_procedures: Procedure for the constitution and functioning of the Labour Welfare Fund Board.
Procedure for the collection and application of the Labour Welfare Fund.
Procedure for the handling of unpaid accumulations and claims related to them.
Procedure for the appointment and powers of the Commissioner and Inspectors.
Procedure for making rules and regulations.
administration: The Act is administered by the Government of Kerala, with the Labour Welfare Fund Board playing a key role in managing the Fund and implementing welfare measures.
important_notes: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.
Different dates may be appointed for commencement in different areas.
The definition of 'employee' is detailed and includes specific exclusions.
The definition of 'establishment' is comprehensive and includes various types of entities.
The Act aims to provide for the constitution of a fund for promoting the welfare of labour.

title: The Kerala Labour Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 1986
purpose: To amend the Kerala Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1975.
scope: Applies to employers and employees covered under the Kerala Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1975.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Labour Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 1986. Section 5 shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of January, 1983 and the remaining provisions of this Act shall be deemed to have come into force on the 25th day of February, 1984.
Amends section 2 of the Kerala Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1975 (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act).
Amends sub-section (2) of section 3 of the principal Act.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 14
main_sections.description: Substitutes a new section for section 14 of the principal Act, concerning "Interest on the employers' and employees' contributions, unpaid accumulations or fines after notice of demand."
Amends section 15 of the principal Act by substituting words and figures.
Inserts a new section 28A after section 28 of the principal Act, dealing with "Penalties for other offences."
Amends section 29 of the principal Act concerning complaints by or with the previous sanction in writing of the Commissioner.
Amends section 31 of the principal Act by substituting words and a proviso.
Repeals the Kerala Labour Welfare Fund (Amendment) Ordinance, 1986 (71 of 1986) and provides for savings.

important_rules: An employer who fails to pay amounts due to the Fund after receiving notice of demand from the Commissioner must pay within thirty days of such notice.
Employers failing to pay without reasonable cause are liable to pay simple interest at the rate of nine per cent per annum on the amount due.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both, for contravening or making default in complying with the provisions of the Act or rules.
Recovery of any amount due to the Fund or the Board, as if it were a fine imposed by a court, for making default in payment.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Commissioner (implied by section 29 and section 14)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notices of demand, imposition of penalties, and recovery of dues.

rights: Employers' and employees' contributions to the Fund.
Right to receive notice of demand before payment is enforced.
duties: Employers' duty to pay contributions.
Employees' duty to pay contributions (implied).
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules.
obligations: Obligation to pay dues within specified timeframes.
Obligation to pay interest on delayed payments.

key_procedures: Procedure for employers to pay contributions due to the Fund.
Procedure for the Commissioner to issue notices of demand for unpaid amounts.
Procedure for recovery of amounts due as if they were fines imposed by a court.
administration: Law (Legislation-C) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: Section 5 of the Act commenced on 1st January 1983.
Remaining provisions of the Act commenced on 25th February 1984.
The Kerala Labour Welfare Fund (Amendment) Ordinance, 1986 is repealed.
The Government may, subject to conditions, remit the whole or any part of the penalty imposed.
No court shall take cognizance of an offence after the expiry of three years from the date on which the offence is alleged to have been committed.

title: The Kerala Land Acquisition (Amendment) Act, 1966
purpose: To amend the Kerala Land Acquisition Act, 1961, by introducing new sections and substituting existing ones to facilitate land acquisition for specific purposes, including public purpose and projects by private companies, with provisions for compensation and notification.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala. It concerns the acquisition of land for public purposes and for certain companies as defined in the Act.

key_definitions.private company: Has the same meaning as in clause (4) of section 2 of the principal Act.
key_definitions.project purpose: Means the purpose of execution, expansion or development of a project.
key_definitions.project area: Means the area covered by one or more revenue villages or survey numbers, the whole or any portion of which is needed or is likely to be needed for a project purpose.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Land Acquisition (Amendment) Act, 1966 and that it shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

This section deals with the amendment of section 6 of the Kerala Land Acquisition Act, 1961. It specifies how the principal Act is to be read and interpreted, particularly concerning sub-section (1) and the declaration of a land being needed for a public purpose.

This section amends section 43 of the principal Act, making specific provisions for land acquisition for the construction of some building or work for a company which is engaged, or is taking steps for engaging itself, in any industry or work which is for a public purpose and that the building or work which such company is intending to construct is meant to subserve the public purpose of the industry or work for which it is being constructed.

This section amends section 44 of the Principal Act. It pertains to the purpose of proposed acquisition for obtaining land for the creation of dwelling houses for persons employed by the company or for the provision of amenities directly connected therewith. It also clarifies that such acquisition is for the construction of a work, that such work is likely to prove useful to the public, or that the proposed acquisition is for a purpose calculated to promote and develop agriculture, industry or co-operation. The section includes provisions for land acquisition for private companies under certain conditions.

This section inserts new sections 45A and 45B in Part VII of the Principal Act. Section 45A deals with 'Restoration or transfer etc.' and states that no company can acquire land under this Part, which is to be transferred by sale, mortgage, gift, lease or otherwise, except with the previous sanction of the Government. Section 45B states that land will not be acquired under this Part except for certain purposes, namely for private companies other than Government companies, and not outstanding anything contained in this Act, no land shall be acquired under this Part, except for the purpose mentioned in clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 43.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new sections for sections 46 to 48.
main_sections.description: This section substitutes new sections for sections 46 to 48 of the principal Act. These substituted sections relate to the acquisition of land in project areas and are to be specified by the Government by notification. They cover provisions for the application of these sections to land acquisition and define 'project area' and 'project purpose'.

This section provides for the validation of certain acquisitions made under the principal Act, or under the corresponding provisions of any of the Acts repealed by the Principal Act, before the date of the commencement of this Act. It specifies that these acquisitions are not to be questioned on the ground that they were not for a public purpose, as mentioned in clause (a) or clause (b) of section 43 or clause (c) of sub-section (1) of section 47A, or the corresponding provision of any of the Acts repealed by the Principal Act. Such acquisitions are deemed to have been made for the purpose mentioned in clause (aa) of the said sub-section.

important_rules: Rule 1: Land acquisition for private companies is permitted only for specific purposes related to public interest and development, and with government sanction.
Rule 2: Acquisitions made prior to the Act's commencement are validated if they were for purposes outlined in the Act, even if not explicitly stated as such at the time.
Rule 3: The Act provides for the substitution of new sections that govern the acquisition of land in project areas and defines terms like 'project area' and 'project purpose'.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government (State Government of Kerala) and Collector.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications, inquiries, and the process of land acquisition as outlined in the principal Act and its amendments.

rights: Right of landowners to compensation for acquired land.
Right to question acquisitions on specific grounds, as per the validation section.
duties: Duty to notify the acquisition of land.
Duty of the Collector to conduct inquiries and make awards.
obligations: Obligation of companies to obtain government sanction for land transfer.
Obligation to ensure that land acquisition serves a public purpose or specified company purposes.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Notification of land acquisition by the Government. Appointment of a date for inquiry by the Collector. Inquiry by the Collector into the land acquisition, including objections, measurement, and value of the land. Making an award by the Collector.

Procedure 2: Substitution of sections in the principal Act to incorporate new provisions for land acquisition, particularly for companies and project areas, requiring adherence to specific clauses and conditions.
administration: The Government of Kerala (specifically, the department concerned with land revenue and land acquisition).
important_notes: The Act is a President's Act, indicating it was enacted during a period of President's rule.
The commencement date of the Act is to be notified by the Government.
The definition of 'company' in section 2 is to be read in conjunction with the principal Act.
The Act makes specific provisions for acquisitions made by private companies engaged in industries or works for public purposes.
The validation section is crucial for regularizing past acquisitions that might have procedural or definitional inconsistencies under the original Act.

title: THE KERALA LAND ACQUISITION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1980
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala Land Acquisition Act, 1961, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Land Acquisition (Amendment) Act, 1980. Section 2 shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of May, 1977 and the remaining provisions of this Act shall be deemed to have come into force on the 4th day of November, 1980.

In section 3 of the Kerala Land Acquisition Act, 1961 (21 of 1962) (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), in subsection (1), after the words "in the Gazette", the words "or at two daily newspapers having wide circulation in that locality" shall be inserted.
In section 5 of the principal Act, in subsection (1), for the words "issue of the notification", the words "publication of the notification" shall be substituted.

In section 6 of the principal Act,-(a) in subsection (1), for the words "two years", the words "three years" shall be substituted; (b) in subsection (2), after the words "in the Gazette", the words "or in two daily newspapers having wide circulation in the locality in which the land to which the declaration relates is situate" shall be inserted.

In section 9 of the principal Act, in subsection (5), after the words "in the Gazette", the words "or in two daily newspapers having wide circulation in the locality in which such land is situate" shall be inserted.

In section 16 of the principal Act,-(a) in subsection (1),-(i) for the words "agree as to the amount of compensation", the words, brackets and figures "agree, whether before or after the date of publication of the notification under subsection (1) of section 3, as to the amount of compensation" shall be substituted; (ii) the following proviso shall be inserted at the end, namely:- "Provided that an agreement executed before the date of publication of the notification under sub-section (1) of section 3 shall not be binding on the persons interested after the expiry of four years from such date."; (b) in subsection (2), for the words "shall be conclusive evidence", the words, brackets and figure "shall, subject to the proviso to subsection(1), be conclusive evidence" shall be substituted.

Notwithstanding anything contained in any judgment decree or order of any court, any agreement as to the amount of compensation to be allowed for any land to be acquired under the principal Act executed after the 1st day of May, 1977 and before the date of commencement of this section shall not be deemed to be invalid or ever to have been invalid merely by reason of the fact that such agreement was executed before the date of publication of the notification under sub-section (1) of section 3 of the principal Act in respect of such land.

(1) The Kerala Land Acquisition (Amendment) Ordinance, 1980 (5 of 1980), is hereby repealed. (2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the Principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Publication of land acquisition notifications must be in the Gazette and two daily newspapers with wide circulation in the locality.
An agreement on compensation reached before the date of notification is only binding for four years from that date.
Agreements on compensation executed between May 1, 1977, and the date of commencement of this section are deemed valid, even if executed before notification publication.

rights: Right to compensation for land acquired.
Right to have agreements on compensation considered valid if executed within a specific timeframe.
duties: Duty to publish land acquisition notifications.
Duty to adhere to the time limits for compensation agreements.

key_procedures: Publishing land acquisition notifications in the Gazette and local newspapers.
Executing agreements for compensation amounts.
The process of land acquisition as governed by the principal Act and its amendments.
administration: Department of Revenue, Government of Kerala (inferred)
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 15th day of January, 1981 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 44 dated the 16th January, 1981.
The amendments are retrospective in some aspects, particularly regarding the commencement date of certain sections.

title: The Kerala Land Acquisition Act, 1962
purpose: To provide for the acquisition of land for public purposes and for the payment of compensation to persons interested in such land.
scope: This Act applies to the acquisition of land for public purposes in the State of Kerala. It applies to all persons interested in the land, including owners, cultivators, and other persons affected by the acquisition.

key_definitions.Collector: The officer appointed by the Government to perform the functions of the Collector under this Act.
key_definitions.interested person: Includes all persons, whether in possession of the land or not, who are legally entitled to or have a claim to any compensation on account of the acquisition of the land.
key_definitions.land: Includes benefits to arise out of land and things attached to the earth or permanently fastened to anything attached to the earth.

main_sections.description: Describes the procedure for serving notices to persons interested in the land, ensuring they are aware of the acquisition proceedings and can appear before the Court.
Specifies that the scope of inquiry for acquisition proceedings is restricted to the objections raised by the persons interested in the land.

main_sections.section_title: Proceedings to be in open Court
main_sections.description: States that all proceedings in relation to land acquisition must take place in open Court, allowing for public scrutiny and participation.

main_sections.section_title: Matters to be considered in determining compensation
main_sections.description: Details the factors to be taken into account when determining the amount of compensation for acquired land, including market value, damage from loss of standing crops, damage from severing land, damage from the acquisition affecting other property, and the compulsion to change residence or business.

main_sections.section_title: Matters to be neglected in determining compensation
main_sections.description: Outlines factors that should NOT be considered when determining compensation, such as the degree of urgency, any disinclination of the person interested to part with the land, damage not rendering the land unsuitable for a suit, or any increase in value due to the purpose of acquisition or subsequent improvements without sanction.

main_sections.section_title: Rules as to amount of compensation
main_sections.description: Sets out rules regarding the amount of compensation awarded, stating that it should not exceed the amount awarded by the Collector unless there are sufficient reasons, and the Court can make a claim if the applicant has refused to make such a claim.
Specifies that every award under this Part shall be in writing, signed by the Judge, and shall specify the amount awarded.
States that every award shall also state the amount of costs incurred in the proceedings under this Part and by what persons and in what proportions they are to be paid.

main_sections.section_title: Collector may be directed to pay interest on excess compensation
main_sections.description: Allows the Collector to be directed to pay interest on excess compensation if the amount awarded is higher than what the Collector had awarded.

main_sections.section_title: Particulars of apportionment or special cases
main_sections.description: Deals with the particulars of the apportionment of compensation among interested persons and special circumstances.
Addresses disputes arising from the apportionment of compensation, allowing for such disputes to be referred to the Court.

main_sections.section_title: Payment of compensation or deposit of the same in Court
main_sections.description: Details the process of payment or deposit of compensation money in Court, including conditions for making payments and the obligation of persons to receive compensation.

main_sections.section_title: Investment of money deposited in respect of lands belonging to persons interested in them
main_sections.description: Covers the investment of money deposited in Court for lands belonging to interested persons, including conditions for purchasing other lands or investing in Government securities.

main_sections.section_title: Investment of money deposited in other cases
main_sections.description: Specifies how money deposited in Court in other cases (not belonging to interested persons) should be invested.
Outlines the payment of interest on compensation amounts not paid or deposited before possession is taken.
Addresses the temporary occupation of land, including provisions for compensation and use of the land.

main_sections.section_title: Power to enter and take possession and compensation or restoration
main_sections.description: Grants the Collector the power to enter and take possession of land, and specifies conditions for compensation and restoration.

main_sections.section_title: Difference as to condition of land
main_sections.description: Deals with differences of opinion regarding the condition of land at the expiration of the term of acquisition or when agreements are made.

main_sections.section_title: Company may be authorised to enter and survey
main_sections.description: Authorizes companies to enter and survey land for the purpose of acquisition.

main_sections.section_title: Industrial concern, ordinarily employing not less than one hundred workmen, owned by an individual or by an association of individuals and not being a company
main_sections.description: Defines circumstances under which industrial concerns employing a significant number of workmen may be treated as companies for the purpose of acquisition.

main_sections.section_title: Previous consent of Government and execution of agreement necessary
main_sections.description: States that prior Government consent and the execution of an agreement are necessary for companies to acquire land.
Details the requirement for a previous inquiry before acquisition of land by a company, including the purpose of the acquisition and the public interest.
Outlines the conditions and terms of agreements between companies and the Government for land acquisition.
Specifies the procedure for publishing agreements made under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions applicable in case of notified projects
main_sections.description: Indicates that specific provisions of this Act apply to projects notified by the Government.
Provides definitions for terms used in Part VIII, including 'project area' and 'project purpose'.
Details the process of land acquisition for project purposes, including modifications to existing sections of the Act.
Describes the procedure for serving notices under this miscellaneous section.

important_rules: When a person's objection to acquisition is not considered, the Court will determine the compensation.
All proceedings in relation to land acquisition must take place in open Court.
Compensation must consider market value, damages, and any compulsory change in residence or business.
Compensation must NOT consider the degree of urgency or any increase in value due to the acquisition's purpose.
Compensation money deposited in Court should be invested appropriately for the benefit of the interested persons.
If land is taken temporarily, compensation must be paid, and the land restored to its original condition.
Companies must obtain prior Government consent and enter into agreements for land acquisition.
A previous inquiry is mandatory before a company acquires land to ascertain the public purpose and interest.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Collector and the Court.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings, including inquiries, hearings, and the issuance of awards and orders by the Court.

rights: Right to receive fair compensation for acquired land.
Right to object to the acquisition and present one's case.
Right to have proceedings conducted in open Court.
Right to have compensation determined considering market value and other damages.
duties: Duty to cooperate with the acquisition process.
Duty to provide information as required by the Collector.
obligations: Obligation to surrender possession of the land upon payment or deposit of compensation.
Obligation to allow entry and survey for acquisition purposes.

key_procedures: Notification of intention to acquire land.
Inquiry into objections raised by interested persons.
Hearing of claims for compensation.
Determination of compensation by the Collector or Court.
Payment or deposit of compensation.
Taking possession of the land.
administration: The Collector, appointed by the Government, is primarily responsible for administering this Act, with oversight and adjudication by the Court.
important_notes: The Act distinguishes between acquisition for public purposes and acquisition by companies.
The principles of compensation are detailed and aim to provide fair value to landowners.
Disputes regarding compensation and apportionment are to be resolved by the Court.
Temporary occupation of land is addressed with provisions for compensation and restoration.

title: THE KERALA LAND CONSERVANCY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1971
purpose: To amend the Kerala Land Conservancy Act, 1957, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the land in Kerala and individuals who occupy land, remove earth, or build structures on land, particularly government property.

key_definitions.agricultural labourer: means a person whose principal means of livelihood is the income he gets as wages in connection with the agricultural operations he performs
key_definitions.Explanation for Section 5: For the purposes of this section, occupation of any land shall be deemed to be occupation of such land.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Land Conservancy (Amendment) Act, 1971. It shall be deemed to have come into force on 5th day of January, 1971.

Substitutes 'Jenmes, Wargdars' for 'holders' and 'persons registered in the revenue records' for 'holders' in sub-section (1) (i) and (ii) of Section 3. Also substitutes 'licence' for 'lease or licence' in sub-section (1) (iv). Inserts Explanations A and IV regarding ownership and possession of land and land belonging to the Government respectively.

Amends section 5 by re-numbering sub-section (1) as sub-section (1) as so re-numbered. Adds an Explanation that for the removal of doubts, erection of any wall, fence or building or putting up any overhanging structure or projection (whether on a temporary or permanent basis) on or over any land shall be deemed to be occupation of such land.

Amends section 6 by inserting 'earth' for 'sand' in sub-section (1) and (2). Inserts sub-section (3A) regarding punishment for unauthorizedly destroying, removing or appropriating earth or sand from any land which is the property of Government. Also inserts sub-section (3B) regarding abetting such commission. Substitutes 'compensation or damages' for 'fine or damages' in sub-section (4) and inserts a new Explanation defining 'agricultural labourer'.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 7.
main_sections.description: Substitutes a new section 7 concerning punishment for unauthorisedly occupying land which is the property of Government. It specifies fines for such occupation and for continuing contravention. It also states that such persons shall not be liable to pay fine if they are eligible under the rules made under the Act for assignment of such land without auction, or if they apply under those rules for registry or lease of such land.

Amends section 8 by changing 'and the liability to pay such assessment shall cease from the date on which the land concerned is relinquished' to 'and the liability to pay such assessment shall cease from the date on which the land concerned is relinquished' shall be omitted. Inserts an Explanation that for the purposes of this section, occupation for any period during a financial year shall be deemed to be occupation for the whole of the financial year.

Amends section 11 by inserting a new sub-section (3) which states that notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (2), it is expedient in the public interest to take urgent action without following the procedure laid down in sub-section (2), without prejudice to the person's right to be heard, and that the Collector may enter upon the land and take possession thereof.

Amends section 12 by adding a proviso to the first paragraph regarding notice. It specifies conditions under which such notice is not necessary. Also substitutes a new paragraph for the second paragraph regarding the Collector's power to require any subordinate officer to hold an enquiry and submit a report.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new sections for sections 16, 17 and 18.
main_sections.description: Substitutes new sections 16, 17 and 18. Section 16 deals with Appeal and Revision. Section 17 deals with Limitation for appeal and revision. Section 18 deals with Petition of appeal or application for revision to be accompanied by the decision or order appealed against or sought to be revised.

Inserts new section 20A, which bars the jurisdiction of civil courts concerning any suit or proceeding for the eviction of any person from unauthorised occupation of land, or recovery of any fine, assessment, or compensation for damage to trees. It also states that no suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against the Government or any officer for anything done in pursuance of this Act.

important_rules: No person shall be liable for any punishment under section 6 for erecting any wall, fence or building or cause to erect any wall, fence or building or put up or cause to put up any overhanging structure or projection (whether on a temporary or permanent basis) on or over any land referred to in sub-section (1) except under and in accordance with the terms and conditions of a licence issued by the Government or such officer.
Whoever unauthorisedly destroys, removes or appropriates for himself earth or sand from any land which is the property of Government, whether a poramboke or not, shall be liable to pay such fine.

Whoever occupies land which is the property of Government, whether a poramboke or not, or not, or the recovery of any fine, assessment, or prohibitory assessment or the value of any trees destroyed or appropriated or any compensation or damages, payable under this Act or cost of eviction or removal of encroachments, or any portion of such fine, assessment, prohibitory assessment, value of trees compensation damages or cost.

penalties: For unauthorised destruction, removal or appropriation of earth or sand: not exceeding one hundred rupees in case of a first offence; not exceeding two hundred rupees in case of a second or subsequent offence.

For unauthorised occupying land which is the property of Government: not exceeding two hundred rupees; and in case of a continuing contravention, such additional fine not exceeding two hundred rupees for every day during which such contravention continues after fine has been imposed for the first such contravention, as may be imposed by the Collector.

For erecting wall, fence or building or putting up overhanging structure or projection without licence: not exceeding two hundred rupees and, in the case of a continuing contravention, an additional fine which may extend to two hundred rupees for every day during which such contravention continues after conviction for the first such contravention.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Collector, Revenue Divisional Officer, or other officer authorised by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through imposition of fines, eviction from land, and legal proceedings. Civil courts' jurisdiction is barred in certain matters.

rights: Right to apply for licence to erect structures on government land.
Right to appeal or seek revision against orders of the Collector or Revenue Divisional Officer.
duties: Duty to obtain a licence before erecting any wall, fence or building or structure on government land.
Duty to pay fines and compensation as prescribed by the Act for unauthorized occupation or damage to government land.
Duty to comply with orders of the Collector or other authorities.
obligations: To vacate government land upon receiving a notice for eviction.

key_procedures: Application for licence to erect structures: Persons desirous of obtaining a licence must apply to the Government in the prescribed form, accompanied by such fees as may be prescribed by rules.
