Appeal and Revision: Any person aggrieved by a decision or order of any officer authorised under section 15 may prefer an appeal or revision. The procedure for appeal and revision is outlined, including limitations and the authorities to whom appeals/revisions can be preferred.
Eviction from unauthorised occupation: The Collector may issue a notice to vacate the land. If the land is not vacated, the officer may enter upon the land and take possession.
administration: The Collector, Revenue Divisional Officer, and other officers authorised by the Government.
important_notes: Explanations are inserted to clarify the meaning of terms and provisions within the Act.
The Act provides for penalties for unauthorized occupation of government land and for destruction of earth or sand.
Civil court's jurisdiction is barred in matters related to eviction from unauthorised occupation and recovery of certain amounts.
The Act aims to protect government land and regulate its use and occupation.

title: The Kerala Land Conservancy (Amendment) Act, 2009
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala Land Conservancy Act, 1957.
scope: Applies to land conservancy within the state of Kerala.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Kerala Land Conservancy (Amendment) Act, 2009, and states that it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 8th day of November, 2008.
Amends the long title of the Kerala Land Conservancy Act, 1957, by adding words relating to matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
Amends the Preamble of the principal Act.
Substitutes section 7 of the principal Act concerning punishment for unauthorizedly occupying land. Punishments include imprisonment and fines.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new sections for sections 8 and 9
main_sections.description: Substitutes new sections 8 and 9 for sections 8 and 9 of the principal Act. This includes 'Abetment of offences' and 'Cognizance of offence'.
Amends section 11 of the principal Act, regarding 'pay a fine under section 7 and an assessment or prohibitory assessment under section 8', and substitutes words.
Amends section 13 of the principal Act.
Amends section 14 of the principal Act by omitting certain words from the marginal heading and sub-sections.
Amends section 16 of the principal Act by substituting 'the Board of Revenue' with 'the Commissioner of Land Revenue'.
Amends section 17 of the principal Act by substituting 'the Board of Revenue' with 'the Commissioner of Land Revenue'.

Amends section 19 of the principal Act. The existing proviso is substituted, stating that if any punishment has been imposed under section 7, no further punishment shall be imposed under any other law for the same offence.

Amends section 20A of the principal Act. Sub-section (1) states that no civil court shall have jurisdiction to entertain any suit or other legal proceedings against the Government in respect of any action taken by it for the eviction of any person, who is in unauthorized occupation of any land which is the property of Government, whether poramboke or not, or for the recovery of any fine or any other sum due to the Government under this Act. Sub-section (2) substitutes 'Board of Revenue' with 'Commissioner of Land Revenue'.

Repeals the Kerala Land Conservancy (Amendment) Ordinance, 2009. It also states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act, as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Punishment for unauthorizedly occupying land includes imprisonment and fines (Section 7).
Prohibition of civil court jurisdiction for suits against Government actions regarding eviction or recovery of dues related to unauthorized occupation (Section 20A(1)).
No further punishment for the same offence if punishment has already been imposed under section 7 (Section 19 proviso).

penalties: Imprisonment for unauthorized occupation of land: not less than three years but may extend to five years, and fine not less than fifty thousand rupees but may extend to two lakhs rupees.

Imprisonment for committing cheating or dishonestly creating documents related to land transfer: not less than seven years and fine not less than fifty thousand rupees but may extend to two lakhs rupees.

Imprisonment for unauthorized occupation entrusted to responsible persons: not less than three years but may extend to five years and fine not less than fifty thousand rupees but may extend to two lakhs rupees.

Imprisonment for erecting walls, fences, buildings, etc., without permission: not less than one year but may extend to two years and fine not less than ten thousand rupees but may extend to twenty five thousand rupees.
Imprisonment for abetment of offences: punishable with the same punishment as provided for the offence.
Fine for continuing contravention: may extend to five hundred rupees for each day during which the contravention continues.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government, competent authorities of the Government, Local Self Government Institutions, respective statutory bodies, and Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings, imposition of imprisonment and fines, and cognizance of offences by the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate.

rights: Right to occupy government land if lawfully permitted.
Right to have legal proceedings heard in civil court unless specifically excluded by law.
duties: Duty to not occupy government land without authorization.
Duty to not commit cheating or create false documents related to land.
Duty to not erect unauthorized structures on government land.
Duty to abide by the provisions of the Kerala Land Conservancy Act, 1957, as amended.
obligations: Obligation to pay fines and other sums due to the Government as per the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure for dealing with unauthorized occupation of government land, including penalties and enforcement.
Procedure for cognizance of offences by the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate.
Procedure for substitution of sections and amendments to existing sections of the principal Act.
Procedure for repeal and saving of prior ordinances.
administration: Commissioner of Land Revenue (substituted for Board of Revenue).
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on November 8, 2008.
No civil court has jurisdiction in cases of eviction or recovery of dues related to unauthorized occupation of government land.
No further punishment for the same offence if already punished under section 7.

title: The Kerala Land Development Corporation Limited (Special Powers) Act, 1974
purpose: To invest the Kerala Land Development Corporation Limited with certain powers to facilitate the execution of land development schemes in the State of Kerala.
scope: The Act applies to the whole of the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Corporation: Means the Kerala Land Development Corporation Limited registered under the Companies Act, 1956 (Central Act 1 of 1956).
key_definitions.cost of works: Includes charges for establishment and supervision.
key_definitions.Inquiring Officer: Means the officer appointed as such by the Corporation.
key_definitions.owner: Means any person for the time being receiving or entitled to receive, whether on his own account, or as agent, trustee, guardian, manager or receiver for another person, rent or profit derivable from land and includes a tenant, an occupant or mortgagee in possession of land.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.record of rights: Means the record of rights and liabilities prepared under section 11.
key_definitions.scheme: Means any land development scheme prepared or to be prepared under this Act.
key_definitions.work: Means any work of public utility constructed or carried out or to be constructed or carried out under any scheme under this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Land Development Corporation Limited (Special Powers) Act, 1974, extends to the whole of Kerala, and came into force on the 21st day of November, 1973.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including Corporation, cost of works, Inquiring Officer, owner, prescribed, record of rights, scheme, and work.
Empowers the Corporation to prepare a draft scheme for any area, specifying its object, boundaries, persons affected, and other relevant particulars.

main_sections.section_title: Matters for which a scheme may provide
main_sections.description: Details the various matters that a land development scheme may provide for, including control and prevention of soil erosion, preservation and improvement of soil, reclamation of waste, construction of earth and masonry works, consolidation of holdings, drainage of canals, construction of pumpsets, and provision of channels.

main_sections.section_title: Publication of scheme and inviting objections
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for publishing a draft scheme, including making copies available for inspection, publishing general notices, and serving separate notices on owners of lands affected by the scheme. It also details how objections can be submitted.
Requires the Inquiring Officer to inquire into objections received, record them, and submit a report with recommendations to the Corporation for modification or abandonment of the scheme.

main_sections.section_title: Decision to execute or abandon scheme or reference to Government for sanction
main_sections.description: States that after considering objections and the Inquiring Officer's report, the Corporation may decide to execute the scheme with or without modifications, or abandon it. The decision to execute may require Government sanction if specific conditions regarding land ownership are met.
Describes the process of publishing the sanctioned scheme, including public notification and making copies available for inspection.
Grants the Corporation the power to take up any work as per the scheme, and states that it shall be lawful for the Corporation to take up any work which is to be executed under the scheme.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of certain persons to pay cost or to contribute
main_sections.description: Specifies that every owner of land included in the scheme shall be liable to pay the cost or part of the cost of the work. It also details how such contributions are to be determined and collected.
Obligates persons liable to pay cost under section 10 to pay interest on such cost at a prescribed rate.

Grants Directors or other servants of the Corporation the right to enter upon, survey, and mark any land and do all such other acts as may be necessary for the purpose of preparing, inquiring into, or executing any scheme.
Requires the Corporation, after the execution of works under a scheme, to publish a declaration of completion. This declaration serves as conclusive evidence of completion.

Directs the Corporation to prepare a statement setting out the names of owners, maps and plans, and the cost of works. It also details amounts to be recovered from owners and the periods for such recovery.

main_sections.section_title: Obligation of owners of lands to maintain and repair works
main_sections.description: States that every owner of land included in a scheme is liable to maintain and repair works on their land as shown in the statement. If an owner fails to do so, the Corporation can carry out the maintenance and repair and recover the expenses.
Provides for appeals against decisions of the Corporation regarding cost or contribution to the Subordinate Judge, and subsequently to the District Court.
Allows the Corporation to rectify any mistake apparent from the record within one year from the date of an order or a mistake passed by it.

important_rules: Owners of land included in a scheme are liable to pay the cost or part of the cost of the work.
Persons liable to pay cost must also pay interest on such cost at a prescribed rate.
Owners of land are obligated to maintain and repair works on their land as specified.
The Corporation has the power to carry out maintenance and repairs if owners fail to do so and recover the expenses.

penalties: Expenses incurred by the Corporation for maintenance and repair if an owner fails to do so are recoverable.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Kerala Land Development Corporation Limited.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, including the power to enforce schemes, recover costs and expenses, and through the appellate procedures.

rights: Right of entry for Corporation officials to survey and mark land for scheme purposes.
Right to appeal against decisions regarding cost or contribution.
duties: Duty to prepare land development schemes.
Duty to publish schemes and invite objections.
Duty to maintain and repair works on land.
Duty to pay cost and interest as determined.
obligations: Obligation of owners to maintain and repair works.
Obligation to pay costs and interest.

key_procedures: Preparation of a draft scheme detailing its objects, boundaries, and affected persons.
Publication of the draft scheme and inviting objections from affected individuals.
Inquiry into objections by an Inquiring Officer and submission of a report to the Corporation.
Corporation's decision to execute, modify, or abandon the scheme, potentially requiring Government sanction.
Publication of the sanctioned scheme.
Execution of works as per the scheme.
Declaration of completion of works.
Preparation of a record of rights and liabilities, including costs to be recovered.
Obligation of owners to pay costs and maintain works.
Procedure for appeals against decisions related to cost or contribution.
administration: The Kerala Land Development Corporation Limited.
important_notes: The Act was preceded by an Ordinance in 1973, which was repealed and saved by this Act.
The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 12th day of March, 1974, and was published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 275 dated 12th March 1974.
Provisions regarding appeal are to the Subordinate Judge, and thereafter to the District Court.

title: The Kerala Land Development (Amendment) Act, 1973
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Land Development Act, 1964.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala, particularly concerning land development, and includes special provisions for linguistic minorities.

key_definitions.Padasekharam: means a collection of fields or other areas of lands, with or without a common outer bund, which is suitable for the adoption of a common cultivation programme or common agricultural operations including dewatering and irrigation.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act as the Kerala Land Development (Amendment) Act, 1973, and specifies that it shall come into force at once.
This section amends clause (ff) of section 2 of the Kerala Land Development Act, 1964, by substituting the definition of 'Padasekharam'.

This section inserts a new section, referred to as section 3, after section 2. This new section contains special provisions in respect of linguistic minorities, stating that notwithstanding anything contained in the Act, special provisions shall apply in respect of linguistic minorities in the State. It further details these provisions for Tamil and Kannada minority people regarding their correspondence with the State Government, its Secretariat, Heads of Departments, and local offices, and the use of English language.

important_rules: Special provisions in respect of linguistic minorities are applicable.

Tamil and Kannada minority people in the State may use their respective languages for correspondence with the State Government, its Secretariat, and Heads of Departments, and also with local offices of the State Government situated in those areas declared by the Government to be linguistic minority areas.
The replies sent to them in such cases shall also be in their respective minority languages.

rights: Linguistic minorities have the right to correspond with the State Government and its departments in their respective languages.
Linguistic minorities have the right to receive replies in their respective languages.

key_procedures: Amendment of existing sections of the Principal Act.
Insertion of new sections with specific provisions.
Declaration of areas as linguistic minority areas by the Government.
administration: State Government (specifically mentioning its Secretariat and Heads of Departments in relation to linguistic minorities).
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Kerala Land Development Act, 1964.
Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 595 dated 7th July, 1973.

title: THE KERALA LAND DEVELOPMENT ACT, 1964
purpose: To unify and amend the law relating to the preparation and execution of Land Development Schemes including Schemes for the conservation and development of soil resources, the control and prevention of soil erosion and the reclamation of waste lands, in the State of Kerala.
scope: Extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Board: Means the Kerala Land Development Board constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.Collector: Means the Collector of the district and includes any Officer not below the rank of a Tahsildar of the Government appointed by the Government to perform all or any of the functions of a Collector under this Act.
key_definitions.District Committee: Means the District Land Development Committee constituted under section 6.
key_definitions.Executing Officer: Means an Officer appointed under section 13 to execute a scheme.
key_definitions.Inquiring Officer: Means an Officer appointed as such by the District Committee.
key_definitions.owner: Means any person for the time being receiving or entitled to receive, whether on his own account, or as agent, trustee, guardian, manager or receiver for another person, the rent or profit derivable from land and includes a tenant, an occupant or mortgagee in possession of land.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.record of rights: Means the record of rights and liabilities prepared under section 20.
key_definitions.scheme: Means any Land Development Scheme prepared or to be prepared under this Act.
key_definitions.work: Means any work of public utility constructed, erected or carried out or to be constructed, erected or carried out under any scheme under this Act.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its extent to the whole of Kerala, and that it comes into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'Collector', 'District Committee', 'Executing Officer', 'Inquiring Officer', 'owner', 'prescribed', 'record of rights', 'scheme', and 'work'.
Establishes the Kerala Land Development Board, specifying its composition (Chairman, Members, Secretary) and the term of office for members.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of Government to direct preparation of schemes.
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to direct the Board to prepare plans and estimates for a scheme in any area within a district.

Outlines the functions of the Board, including directing the preparation of schemes, considering draft schemes, devising ways for speedy execution, fixing physical and financial targets, and performing other specified functions.

Mandates the Government to constitute a District Land Development Committee for each district, specifying its composition (Collector as Chairman, officers from relevant departments, and non-officials).

Details the functions of the District Committee, including making recommendations to the Board, preparing schemes, performing other functions pertaining to land development, executing sanctioned schemes, and carrying out instructions from the Board.

main_sections.section_title: Matters for which a scheme may provide.
main_sections.description: Lists the various matters that a scheme may cover, including soil conservation, erosion control, reclamation of waste lands, methods of cultivation and extension, construction of works, regulation of activities, and improvement of water supply.

Describes the process of preparing schemes, involving the Government or Board instructing the District Committee, and the District Committee preparing a draft scheme including its objects, boundaries, persons affected, work to be carried out, and agencies involved.

main_sections.section_title: Publication of scheme and inviting objections.
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for publishing a scheme, including notifying the draft scheme, inviting objections from affected persons, and publishing notices.
Requires the Inquiring Officer to submit a report to the District Committee after hearing objections and inquiries, with recommendations for modification.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the Board and the Government to sanction scheme with or without modifications.
main_sections.description: Grants the Board and the Government the power to sanction a scheme with or without modifications, after considering the report and recommendations.
Allows for the appointment of an Executing Officer by the District Committee to execute the scheme.

Empowers the Executing Officer to enforce the scheme, including carrying out the work at the cost of the owner if they default, and recovering expenses. It also covers situations where the owner is entitled to compensation.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to carry out works under a scheme.
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to carry out works under a scheme if it deems necessary, and to recover the costs from the owners of the lands included in the scheme.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of persons whose lands are not included in the scheme to contribute.
main_sections.description: Addresses the liability of persons whose lands are not included in a scheme but are benefited by it to contribute to the cost of the work.
Allows for reference to the Court for determining liabilities or contributions under the Act, with provisions for court procedures and objections.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make, grant or advance loan.
main_sections.description: Grants the power to make, grant, or advance loans for the purpose of carrying out works under a scheme.
Confers the right of entry upon any land for the purposes of the Act.
Requires the preparation and maintenance of records of rights and liabilities of persons affected by the scheme.

main_sections.section_title: Obligation of owners of lands to maintain and repair the works.
main_sections.description: Places an obligation on owners of lands to maintain and repair works constructed under a scheme.

main_sections.section_title: Notification of areas and control over them.
main_sections.description: Deals with the notification of areas and the control to be exercised over them under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power to regulate, restrict or prohibit certain matters within the notified area.
main_sections.description: Grants power to regulate, restrict, or prohibit certain activities within the notified area.

main_sections.section_title: Proclamation of order under section 23 and admission of claims for compensation.
main_sections.description: Concerns the proclamation of orders issued under section 23 and the admission of claims for compensation.

main_sections.section_title: Inquiries into claims and award of compensation.
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for inquiries into claims and the awarding of compensation.
Specifies the method by which compensation is to be awarded.

main_sections.section_title: Amount to be recoverable as arrears of land revenue.
main_sections.description: States that amounts recoverable under the Act shall be recoverable as arrears of land revenue.

main_sections.section_title: Permission to owners to increase rent on account of improvements effected.
main_sections.description: Deals with the permission to owners to increase rent due to improvements effected by a scheme.

main_sections.section_title: Certain Officers to be public servants.
main_sections.description: Declares certain officers appointed under the Act to be public servants.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of persons acting in good faith, limitation of suits and prosecutions.
main_sections.description: Provides protection to persons acting in good faith and limits suits and prosecutions.

main_sections.section_title: Vacancies amongst members or defect in the constitution not to invalidate proceedings of the Board or Committee.
main_sections.description: Ensures that vacancies or defects in the constitution of the Board or Committee do not invalidate their proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Schemes relating to areas lying in more than one district.
main_sections.description: Addresses the preparation of schemes that may involve areas in more than one district.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Repeals previous legislation, specifically The Travancore-Cochin Land Development Act, 1950.

main_sections.section_title: Certain schemes, etc., deemed to have been prepared under this Act and saving of work carried out under the Travancore-Cochin Land Development Act, 1950.
main_sections.description: Provides that certain existing schemes are deemed to have been prepared under this Act and saves work carried out under the repealed Act.

important_rules: Owners of land are obligated to maintain and repair works constructed under a scheme (Section 21).
Any amount recoverable under the Act is to be recovered as arrears of land revenue (Section 27).
The Government has the power to make rules for carrying out the Act's purposes (Section 33).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Executing Officer, District Committee, Board, Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By carrying out works at the cost of the owner if they default (Section 14), recovery of expenses, and through Court references for disputes (Section 17).

rights: Right of entry upon any land for the purposes of the Act (Section 19).
Owners may be entitled to compensation under certain circumstances (Section 14).
Owners may be permitted to increase rent on account of improvements effected (Section 28).
duties: Obligation of owners of lands to maintain and repair the works (Section 21).
obligations: Owners of lands included in a scheme are obligated to maintain and repair the works (Section 21).

key_procedures: Preparation of schemes involves Government/Board instruction, draft scheme preparation by the District Committee, and inclusion of specific details like objects, boundaries, persons affected, and work plans.
Publication of schemes requires notifying the draft, inviting objections from affected persons within thirty days, and publishing notices in newspapers and in the locality.

The process for sanctioning a scheme involves the Inquiring Officer's report, recommendations from the District Committee, and final sanction by the Board or Government, potentially with modifications.

Enforcement of schemes includes the Executing Officer carrying out works if owners default, recovering costs, and provisions for reference to Court for disputes concerning liabilities and contributions.
administration: The Kerala Land Development Board and District Land Development Committees, under the overall direction of the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act repeals The Travancore-Cochin Land Development Act, 1950, but saves work carried out under it.
Certain schemes and works from the previous Act are deemed to have been prepared or carried out under this Act.
Vacancies or defects in the constitution of the Board or Committees do not invalidate their proceedings.
Officers acting in good faith are protected from suits and prosecutions.
Schemes covering areas in more than one district are specifically addressed.

title: THE KERALA LAND REFORMS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2005
purpose: To amend The Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963, for the purposes hereinafter appearing, by making provisions related to land ceiling, acquisition of land, and insertion of new sections concerning deemed tenants and special provisions for certificates of title.
scope: Applies to lands in Kerala and to persons who are deemed tenants or who have acquired lands in excess of the ceiling area.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called The Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 2005, and shall come into force at once.
This section amends section 2 of the principal Act by substituting the word, figure, and letter "section 7D" with "section 7E".

This section inserts a new section 7E, which pertains to 'Certain persons who acquired lands to be deemed tenants'. It outlines conditions under which persons in possession of land not exceeding four hectares, acquired by themselves or their predecessors, shall be deemed tenants. It also covers situations where such land was surrendered or acquired under specific provisions.

This section amends section 84 of the principal Act by adding a new sub-section (4). This new sub-section clarifies that notwithstanding anything contained in sub-sections (1), (1A) or (2), or in any judgment, decree, or order of any court, tribunal or other authority, no acquisition of land referred to in section 7E shall be deemed to be invalid, or ever to have been invalid, by reason only of the fact that the land so acquired was found as, or forming part of, the land liable to be surrendered by the transferor as excess land under the provisions of this Act.

This section inserts a new section 106 B, which provides 'Special provision for issue of certificate of title'. It details how persons claiming to be deemed tenants under section 7E may apply to the Land Tribunal for a certificate of title. It specifies the procedure for application, verification of records, and the issuance of the certificate.

important_rules: Rule 1: Persons who acquired lands to be deemed tenants under specific conditions outlined in new section 7E.
Rule 2: Acquisition of land shall not be deemed invalid due to it being part of excess land liable for surrender, as per amended section 84.
Rule 3: A procedure is established for issuing certificates of title to deemed tenants under section 7E, as detailed in new section 106 B.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Land Tribunal
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through application and adjudication processes for deemed tenancy and certificates of title.

rights: Right to be deemed a tenant under certain conditions of land acquisition.
Right to apply for and obtain a certificate of title as a deemed tenant.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the conditions for being deemed a tenant.
Obligation to follow the prescribed procedure for obtaining a certificate of title.

key_procedures: Procedure for deeming a person as a tenant based on land acquisition circumstances (Section 7E).
Procedure for applying for and obtaining a certificate of title for deemed tenants, including application, verification, and issuance by the Land Tribunal (Section 106 B).
administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but likely relates to the revenue or land reform department of the Kerala Government, with the Land Tribunal as an adjudicatory body.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to The Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963.
The amendments came into effect immediately upon enactment.
The definition of deemed tenant is elaborated upon in the new section 7E.
A clarification is made regarding the validity of land acquisition in relation to excess land surrender in section 84.
A specific provision for issuing certificates of title to deemed tenants is introduced in section 106 B.

scope: The Act applies to the state of Kerala and concerns land reforms within the state. It specifically amends various sections of the principal Act of 1963.

key_definitions.land_holding: The extent of land held by a person.
key_definitions.revenue_village: The smallest administrative unit for land revenue purposes.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as the Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 2005, and specifies its commencement.
Amends section 2 of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963, likely related to definitions or preliminary provisions. It specifically refers to the definition of 'adult'.
Amends section 7 of the principal Act, which deals with the ceiling on land holdings.
Amends section 84 of the principal Act, which likely pertains to appeals or revision.
Amends section 106 of the principal Act, which may deal with rules or other miscellaneous provisions.

Specific amendments are made to sections defining 'adult' to clarify its application in the context of land reforms.
Changes are introduced to the appellate or revisionary procedures under the Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly detailed in the provided excerpts, but implied to be the authorities responsible for implementing the Kerala Land Reforms Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Implied through the legal framework of the Land Reforms Act and its amendments.

rights: The right to hold land up to the prescribed ceiling.
The right to appeal or seek revision against orders passed under the Act.
duties: Duty to comply with the provisions of the amended Act regarding land holdings.
Duty to provide accurate information to the authorities.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the land ceiling limits.

Procedures related to appeals and revisions to higher authorities.

The Act is presented as an amendment to existing legislation, indicating that it builds upon the framework of the 1963 Act.

title: The Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 1999
purpose: The act aims to amend the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963, to further regulate land holdings and transfers in Kerala.

key_definitions.land_reforms_act_1963: Refers to the principal legislation being amended.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 28B of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963

The act clarifies or modifies procedures related to land holdings and their management.

Steps involved in the enforcement of land reform measures.

title: The Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 2014
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963. WHEREAS, it is expedient further to amend the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 for the purposes hereinafter appearing; BE, it enacted in the Sixty-fifth Year of the Republic of India as follows:—
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala. Specifically mentions amendments to the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963. Deals with land holdings, including those for agricultural crops and dairy farms.

key_definitions.principal Act: The Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 (1 of 1964).

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 2014. Also mentions commencement dates for certain sections: Section 2 shall have come into force on the 18th day of October, 2006 and Section 3 shall be deemed to have come into force on the 19th day of June, 2012.

title: THE KERALA LAND REFORMS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1971
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963.
scope: Applies to Kerala. It amends the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963, by introducing new provisions, substituting existing sections, and modifying certain definitions and procedures related to land reforms.

key_definitions.kudikidappukaran: A person who cultivates or occupies land.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 1971, and specifies the commencement dates for its various provisions. Some provisions came into force on January 1, 1970, and others on the date of the Act's publication.

This explanation clarifies 'kudikidappukaran' in relation to dwelling houses on land owned by the Government or a corporation, and also clarifies 'but shall be deemed' and 'but shall be deemed', and 'in such a manner'.
Amends section 65 of the principal Act by inserting an Explanation. This explanation defines 'institution of a public trust or a public nature'.

Amends section 72F of the principal Act by substituting certain words and figures in sub-sections (1) and (5). It also inserts a new clause (hh) concerning the definition of 'landowner or intermediary' for annuity purposes.

Amends section 72N of the principal Act by inserting a new sub-section (1A) that deals with applications for annuity pending or deemed to be pending by the Government of India or the State Government.

Amends section 75 of the principal Act by substituting words in sub-section (3A) and inserting new sub-sections (3BB) and (3D) related to the requisition of land and the eviction of the kudikidappukaran. It also amends sub-section (3E) concerning compensation payable for land acquisition.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 77.

Amends section 80A by adding a further proviso to sub-section (4) regarding the purchase price of land and inserting a new sub-section (8A) clarifying that kudikidappukaran shall not be liable to pay the share of the purchase price in cases where the person in possession of land is holding such land under a landlord or more than one landlord.
Amends section 80B by adding a proviso to sub-section (3) regarding the Land Tribunal not passing any order under a sub-section until the disposal of the application.

Amends section 80C by substituting words in sub-section (1) and sub-section (2). It clarifies the process for depositing the first instalment of the purchase price and the issuance of a certificate of purchase by the Land Tribunal.

Amends section 81 by inserting a new Explanation II which includes 'a corporation owned or controlled by the Government of Kerala or the Government of any other State in India or the Government of India' within the definition of 'other authority'.

Amends section 82 by substituting sub-sections (3) and (4). It clarifies the calculation of the extent of land owned or held by a family or an unmarried person and introduces an Explanation regarding the share of land held by a member of a family or a co-operative society. It also specifies rules for land converted into any class of land specified in Schedule II.

Amends section 85 by substituting words in Explanation IV and inserting a new sub-section (6) and (9). It clarifies the definition of 'scheduled bank' and provides conditions under which the Land Board may not be bound to accept the choice of land surrender or to take possession of the land.

title: The Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 1972
purpose: The purpose of this act is to amend the Kerala Land Reforms Act to address issues related to land ownership, surrender, and compensation, particularly concerning land held by various individuals and families, including minors and those in absence. It also establishes and outlines the functions of Taluk Land Boards and Land Reforms Review Boards.
scope: The act applies to land holdings in Kerala, specifically addressing the ownership, possession, and surrender of lands, and the determination of extent and other particulars of such lands. It also defines the application of its provisions to different categories of persons and family structures.

key_definitions.bank: A scheduled bank as defined in the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, or a corresponding new bank constituted under the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1970, or the State Bank of India constituted under the State Bank of India Act, 1955, or a subsidiary bank as defined in the State Bank of India (Subsidiary Banks) Act, 1959.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new section 85A. - After section 85 of the principal Act, the following section shall be inserted, namely:—
main_sections.description: This section introduces a new section 85A, which mandates that certain persons (owning or holding more than twelve acres of land in extent, and every adult unmarried person and every family consisting of a sole surviving member owning or holding more than six acres of land, and every other person owning or holding more than twelve acres of land in extent of land) shall, within forty-five days from the commencement of the Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 1972, file a statement before the Land Board intimating the location, extent and such other particulars as may be prescribed, of all lands (including lands exempted under section 81) owned or held by such family or person.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 86. - In section 86 of the principal Act,—
main_sections.description: This section amends section 86 of the principal Act. It specifies that on the determination of the extent and other particulars of lands, the ownership or possession of both of which is or are to be surrendered under section 85, the ownership or possession of both shall, as the case may be, vest in the Government free from all encumbrances and the Taluk Land Board shall issue an order accordingly. It also introduces changes to sub-sections (2), (3), and (4) concerning the wording related to the Taluk Land Board and Taluk Land Board respectively.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 87. - In section 87 of the principal Act,—
main_sections.description: This section amends section 87 of the principal Act. It provides for the substitution of sub-section (2) of section 85, and related phrases, with new wording. It also amends sub-section (2) of section 86 and 85, ensuring that the provisions of sections 85 and 86 shall, so far as may be, apply to the vesting in the Government of the ownership or possession of both of the lands required to be surrendered under section (1).

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 88. - In section 88 of the principal Act,—
main_sections.description: This section amends section 88 of the principal Act. It clarifies that in sub-section (1), the words "is surrendered by, or assumed from, a person or" shall be omitted. It also introduces a new sub-section (1A) stating that notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), no person shall be entitled to any compensation in respect of any land owned by the Government of Kerala and held by him under lease or otherwise. It further makes substitutions for words like 'surrender' and 'assumption' in sub-sections (2) and (3), and amends the opening paragraph of sub-section (4) regarding the rights of a mortgagee in possession.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new sections 100A, 100B, 100C, 100D, and 100E. - After section 100 of the principal Act,—
main_sections.description: This section introduces several new sections: 100A (Constitution of Taluk Land Boards), 100B (Dissolution and reconstitution of Taluk Land Board), 100C (Powers of Taluk Land Board), 100D (Constitution of Land Reforms Review Board), and 100E (Powers of the Land Reforms Review Board). These sections establish and define the composition, functions, and powers of these boards.

important_rules: Any person owning or holding more than twelve acres of land, or an adult unmarried person and every family consisting of a sole surviving member owning or holding more than six acres, or any other person owning or holding more than twelve acres, must file a statement with the Land Board within forty-five days of the commencement of the Act.
On determination of land extent and particulars for surrender, ownership or possession vests in the Government, free from encumbrances.
Taluk Land Boards are constituted by the Government by notification in the Gazette for performing the functions of the Taluk Land Board under this Act.

A Taluk Land Board shall consist of an officer not below the rank of Deputy Collector appointed by the Government (who shall be the Chairman) and not more than six members nominated by the Government.

A person shall be disqualified for being nominated as, or for being, a member of the Taluk Land Board if he is or has been convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude and sentenced to imprisonment for not less than six months, if a period of five years has not elapsed from the date of expiry of the sentence.

The Government may, at any time, for reasons to be recorded in writing, remove from office any member of the Taluk Land Board after giving him a reasonable opportunity of showing cause against the proposed removal.
Land Reforms Review Boards are constituted by the Government by notification in the Gazette for the purpose of reviewing the progress of implementation of this Act.

penalties: Disqualification for membership of Taluk Land Board if convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude and sentenced to imprisonment for not less than six months, unless five years have elapsed since the sentence expiry.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Taluk Land Board and Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through determination of land ownership, surrender orders, and powers vested in the Taluk Land Board and Land Reforms Review Board to enforce the Act's provisions.

rights: Right to compensation for surrendered land (as per section 20 regarding growing crops and improvements).
Right to have a reasonable opportunity of showing cause against proposed removal from Taluk Land Board membership.
duties: Duty to file a statement with the Land Board regarding land holdings (as per section 85A).
Duty to surrender land ownership or possession as determined under section 85.
Duty to comply with orders issued by the Taluk Land Board.
Duty to assist the Taluk Land Board in performing its functions.
obligations: Obligation to provide necessary information to the Taluk Land Board.
Obligation for the Government to constitute and manage Taluk Land Boards and Land Reforms Review Boards.

key_procedures: Filing of statements by landowners regarding their holdings to the Land Board within a specified period (section 85A).
Determination of the extent and particulars of land ownership or possession for surrender under section 85.
Issuance of an order by the Taluk Land Board for the vesting of surrendered land in the Government.
Constitution and functioning of Taluk Land Boards for performing their duties.
Constitution and functioning of Land Reforms Review Boards for reviewing the progress of the Act's implementation.
Procedure for removal of a member of the Taluk Land Board.
Procedure for dissolution and reconstitution of a Taluk Land Board.
Powers of the Taluk Land Board including summoning, requiring discovery of documents, receiving evidence, and any other prescribed matters.
Powers of the Land Reforms Review Board including calling for returns, exercising powers, and laying down guide lines.
administration: Land Board, Taluk Land Board, Government of Kerala, and Land Reforms Review Board
important_notes: The Act refers to 'Taluk Land Board' and 'Taluk Land Board' in a way that suggests a distinction, though the context implies they refer to the same entity.
The term 'bank' is specifically defined in the context of this Act.

Section 85A specifically addresses the filing of statements for certain categories of landowners, including those owning more than twelve acres and adult unmarried persons or families with sole surviving members owning more than six acres.

Compensation payable under section 20 is for growing crops and improvements, if any, thereon, and no person shall be entitled to any amount other than the compensation payable under this section for the vesting in the Government or extinguishment of his rights (including his rights in respect of growing crops and improvements, if any) in respect of the land.

This section amends Section 103 of the principal Act, specifically substituting a new subsection (1A) that deals with the Government's powers to prescribe a petition for revision to the High Court.

title: The Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 1981
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963.
scope: Applies to land reforms in Kerala.

key_definitions.cultivating tenant: Not liable to pay rent if resumption application is rejected. Notwithstanding anything contained in any law in force, or in any contract, custom or usage, or in any judgment, decree or order of any court or Land Tribunal, in the case of a holding or part of a holding in respect of which an application for resumption under the provisions of this Act is rejected, the cultivating tenant shall not be liable to pay any rent for such holding or part of the holding, as the case may be, with effect on and from the date notified under subsection (1) of section 72.
key_definitions.Explanation (for section 84): For the purposes of clause (b), a land shall be deemed to have been assigned on registry if the purchase price payable for the assignment of that land or the first instalment thereof has been deposited as required by the rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 1981, and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of January, 1970, and the remaining provisions of this Act shall be deemed to have come into force on the 22nd day of June, 1981.
Inserts a new section 72QQ concerning the liability of cultivating tenants to pay rent after rejection of resumption applications.
Amends section 72S of the principal Act regarding resumption of holdings and liability to pay taxes and cesses.
Amends section 84 of the principal Act by inserting an Explanation regarding the assignment of land on registry.

Amends section 85 of the principal Act, specifically subsection (6), concerning proceedings for the determination of the extent and other particulars of any land, ownership or possession of which is to be surrendered by an adult unmarried person or family, and the procedure for surrender by such person or the remaining member of such family.

Amends section 109A of the principal Act by substituting 'five hundred rupees' with 'one thousand five hundred rupees' in the first proviso, and 'two thousand rupees' with 'five thousand rupees' in the second proviso.

Provides for transitory provisions where any judgment, decree, or order of any court or other authority, or any proceeding under the principal Act, has been determined, but prior to the principal Act as amended by this Act. It also addresses the restoration of proceedings for the representative of a deceased adult unmarried person or sole surviving member of a family.

(1) The Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Ordinance, 1981 (5 of 1981), is hereby repealed. The provisions of this Act shall be deemed to have come into force on different dates: sections 2 to 5 on January 1, 1970, and remaining provisions on June 22, 1981.
In cases of land surrender by an adult unmarried person or family, proceedings are deemed declared, and the family member who filed the statement can surrender the same extent of land.
Substitution of currency amounts in section 109A: 'five hundred rupees' becomes 'one thousand five hundred rupees', and 'two thousand rupees' becomes 'five thousand rupees'.

title: THE KERALA LAND REFORMS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1979 (Act 27 of 1979)

key_definitions.member of family: Means wife or husband, son or daughter.
key_definitions.land board: Refers to the Land Board or the Taluk Land Board.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 1979, and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 7th day of July, 1979.
Amends section 2 of the principal Act by substituting the words 'Land Board' or 'Taluk Land Board' in clause (44) of sub-clause (c).

Inserts a new section 6C concerning certain lessees who have made substantial improvements etc. to be deemed tenants. It outlines conditions under which such lessees are considered tenants and specifies how improvements are to be valued.
Amends section 19 of the principal Act by substituting the words 'Land Board' or 'Taluk Land Board'.

Substitutes sub-sections (2) and (3) of section 26. It mandates that a person liable to pay an amount determined under sub-section (2) shall deposit it with the Land Tribunal within six months. It also addresses the failure to deposit, requiring payment with interest to the District Collector and subsequent recovery by the Kerala Revenue Recovery Act, 1968.
Amends section 27 by renumbering Explanation II as Explanation III and inserting a new Explanation II concerning the calculation of interest on rent for the purpose of transfer of land.
Amends section 63 by adding a proviso and explanation to sub-section (7) concerning the payment of amounts to nominees.

Sub-section (11) outlines the procedure for an application under sub-section (10). Sub-section (12) describes the process for applications to the Land Board or Taluk Land Board regarding transfers of land.

Amends section 87 by renumbering Explanation I to Explanation II and inserting a new Explanation I concerning land converted into other classes of land under Schedule II and land under the purview of section 81.

Amends section 101 by inserting the words 'on its own motion or' at the beginning of clause (e) of sub-section (2).
Inserts a new section 108A concerning the Code of Civil Procedure to apply to proceedings before the Land Tribunal.

Application for restoration of ownership or possession of land to the Land Board or Taluk Land Board (Section 12).
Verification of applications by the Land Board or Taluk Land Board (Section 12).
Government decision on the public nature of institutions (Section 98A).
Land Tribunal proceedings governed by the Code of Civil Procedure (Section 108A).
Determination of purchase price and compensation, including rent and arrears of public revenue (Section 17).
administration: The administration of land reforms in Kerala is typically handled by the Revenue Department, with the Land Reforms Commissioner, Land Tribunals, Land Board, and Taluk Land Boards playing key roles.
important_notes: The Act is retrospective, deemed to have come into force on July 7, 1979.
Certain amendments are effective from January 1, 1970, or other specified dates.
The Act clarifies the definition of 'member of family' for specific purposes.
Provisions exist for land transfers to a son or daughter that may have been invalid under other laws.
The repeal of the 1979 Ordinance does not affect actions taken under it.

title: THE KERALA LAND REFORMS (AMENDMENT) AMENDING ACT, 1973
purpose: To amend the Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 1972, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Amending Act, 1973 and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 16th day of December, 1972.

Amends section 38 of the Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 1972. It specifies substitutions for certain words within the section, particularly concerning the 'Taluk Land Board' and provisions related to land surrender and objections.

Repeals the Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Ordinance, 1972 (11 of 1972). It also includes a saving clause stating that notwithstanding the repeal, any action taken under section 38 of the Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 1972 (17 of 1972) as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 341 dated 19th April, 1973.

title: THE KERALA LAND REFORMS (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 2005
purpose: An Act to further amend the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963.

key_definitions.cashew estate: For the purpose of this clause "cashew estate" shall mean any land principally cultivated with not less than 150 cashew trees per hectare.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Land Reforms (Second Amendment) Act, 2005, and it shall come into force at once.

Amends section 81 of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 (1 of 1964). It inserts a new clause (f) into sub-section (1), defining 'cashew estate'. It also inserts a new sub-section (4) which states that notwithstanding anything contained in the Act or any other law, for the time being in force or in any contract or other documents or in any judgement, decree or order of any Court or Tribunal or Taluk Land Board or Land Board or other authority, a person holding plantation and lands ancillary thereto or interspersed within such plantation, may use not exceeding five per centum of the extent of such holding for floriculture or for the cultivation of Vanilla or medicinal plants or other agricultural crops or for establishing hotels or resorts or other tourism projects and for purposes ancillary or connected therewith.
Inserts a proviso to sub-section (4) of section 82 of the principal Act, stating that nothing contained in this section shall apply to the conversion of any land into cashew estate.

important_rules: Lands principally cultivated with not less than 150 cashew trees per hectare are defined as 'cashew estates'.

Holdings that are plantations or ancillary to plantations can have up to 5% of their extent used for floriculture, cultivation of vanilla or medicinal plants, other agricultural crops, or for establishing hotels or resorts or other tourism projects, or for ancillary/connected purposes, notwithstanding other laws or contracts.
The provisions of section 82 (presumably relating to conversion of land) do not apply to the conversion of any land into cashew estate.
administration: Government of Kerala, Law (Legislation-B) Department
important_notes: The Act is a second amendment to the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963.
The amendment was passed by the Legislative Assembly and received the assent of the President on the 4th day of June, 2012.
The notification was published in the Kerala Gazette on 19th June 2012.
