title: THE KERALA LAND REFORMS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1989
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963.
scope: Applies to land within Kerala, specifically concerning tenancy, land holdings, and compensation related to land reforms.

key_definitions.Explanation in section 2: For the purpose of this clause, so much of the land appurtenant to the land under the Karaiama belonging to the landlord or any person claiming through him and in the possession and beneficial enjoyment of the Karaiama holder or his legal representative or any other person claiming through him as on the 24th day of January, 1989 shall, subject to a maximum of three cents in Corporation area, five cents in Municipal area and ten cents in Panchayats area, inclusive of the land under the Karaiama, be deemed to be Karaiama.
key_definitions.member of family: means wife or husband, son or daughter of such person.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 1989, and that it shall come into force at once.
Inserts an Explanation to clause (23A) of section 2 of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963, defining the extent of land appurtenant to Karaiama.
Substitutes the first proviso to clause (vi) of sub-section (1) of section 3 of the principal Act.

Inserts a new sub-section (3) to section 7 B of the principal Act, restricting anything contained in the Act or any contract, custom or usage from affecting the decree or order of any court, any person in occupation of land on the basis of an oral permission or a deed purporting to be lease deed.

Inserts sub-section (1A) to section 72D of the principal Act, stating that where the total extent of land held as tenant by a cultivating tenant is one hectare or below, he shall not be liable to pay purchase price under sub-section (1).
Substitutes sub-section (8) and the proviso thereunder in section 80 A of the principal Act, concerning purchase price payable by the Kudikidappukaran to the Kudikidappukkar's benefit Fund.
Amends sub-section (1) of section 80C of the principal Act, by omitting clauses (i), (5) and (6).
Omites section 80 D from the principal Act.
Omits the proviso to sub-section (1) of section 80 G of the principal Act.
Substitutes clauses (a) and (b) in the second proviso to sub-section (9) of section 85 of the principal Act, modifying the duration for 'expiry of three years' to 'expiry of seven years'.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 92
main_sections.description: Substitutes a new section 92 for section 92 of the principal Act, dealing with payment and compensation of encumbrance. It specifies conditions under which compensation is payable and when it is deposited with the Government. It also provides for the definition of 'member of family'.
Omits the words 'one half of' from clause (b) of sub-section (4) of section 109 of the principal Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Anything contained in this Act or in any other law or in any contract, custom or usage or in any judgement, decree or order of any court, any person in occupation of land on the basis of an oral permission or a deed purporting to be lease deed, granted by a tenant, if he or his predecessor-in-interest was in occupation of such land at the commencement of the Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 1969, shall not be affected.
Rule 2: A cultivating tenant holding land up to one hectare or below is not liable to pay purchase price.
Rule 3: Compensation or amount of encumbrance is payable to the person entitled to receive it, either in cash or in negotiable bonds redeemable after a specified period, with interest.

Rule 4: When a person entitled to compensation or amount of encumbrance is a minor or a person suffering from some legal disability, or a limited owner, the compensation or amount of encumbrance shall be deposited by the Government.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Taluk Land Board
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The Taluk Land Board may review its decision on ground that such decision has been made due to the failure to produce relevant data or other particulars relating to ownership or possession, or by collusion or fraud or any suppression of material facts. The Taluk Land Board shall not reopen any such case after the expiry of three years from the date of coming into force of the Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 1989.

rights: Right to receive compensation or amount of encumbrance under prescribed conditions.
Right of a Karaiama holder to beneficial enjoyment of the land appurtenant to Karaiama.
obligations: Obligation to pay purchase price for land under certain circumstances.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Amendment of sections of the principal Act to modify existing provisions and introduce new ones related to land reforms.
Procedure 2: The Taluk Land Board reviews decisions related to land ownership and possession under specific circumstances and within a defined time limit.
administration: The Act amends the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963, implying that the administration would likely fall under the Revenue Department or a specialized Land Reforms department in Kerala.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the President on the 26th day of May 1989 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 503 dated the 30th May 1989.
Section 4 states that the provisions related to oral permissions or lease deeds will not be affected if the occupation of land commenced before the Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 1969.
The Taluk Land Board has the power to review its decisions but cannot reopen cases after three years from the commencement of the Act.
The definition of 'member of family' includes wife or husband, son or daughter.

title: THE KERALA LAND RELINQUISHMENT (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1963
purpose: To amend The Kerala Land Relinquishment Act, 1958.
scope: Applies to land in Kerala, specifically concerning relinquishment by registered holders and cultivating tenants.

key_definitions.cultivating tenant: A person in possession of land for cultivation.
key_definitions.intermediary: A person between the registered holder and the cultivating tenant.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Land Relinquishment (Amendment) Act, 1963.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of long title and preamble
main_sections.description: Amends the long title and preamble of the Kerala Land Relinquishment Act, 1958.

Substitutes section 2 of the principal Act. 'Relinquishment' is defined to include, in the case of any land in possession of a registered holder, the unconditional surrender of all his rights over the land, and in the case of such land in the possession of a cultivating tenant, the unconditional surrender of their rights over the land by the registered holder, the cultivating tenant and the intermediaries, if any.

Amends section 3 of the principal Act. Where a registered holder or a registered holder, cultivating tenant and intermediaries, if any, jointly intend to relinquish any land under section 3, such registered holder, or as the case may be, such registered holder, cultivating tenant and intermediaries, if any, jointly may submit an application in the prescribed form to the Collector of the district in which the land is situated.

Amends section 4 of the principal Act. If in sub-section (2) for the words "the registered holder is competent to relinquish and has valid title in the land", the words "the registered holder, as the case may be, the registered holder, the cultivating tenant and the intermediaries, if any, of the land jointly is or are competent to relinquish and has or have valid title in the land" shall be substituted. For sub-section (6), the following sub-section shall be substituted, namely :- (6) The Collector may at any stage of the proceedings reject the application on any of the following grounds, namely :- (i) that the registered holder, or, as the case may be, the registered holder, the cultivating tenant and the intermediaries, if any, jointly is not, or are not, competent to relinquish the land; (ii) that the title of the registered holder, the tenant or the intermediaries, if any, is defective; (iv) that there are arrears of land revenue due on the land; (v) that the land is not accessible except through land not belonging to the Government; (vi) such other grounds as may be prescribed. For sub-section (8), for the words "of the registered holder", the words "of the registered holder, or, as the case may be, of the registered holder, the cultivating tenant and the intermediaries, if any, shall be substituted."

important_rules: Registered holders, cultivating tenants, and intermediaries may jointly intend to relinquish land.
An application for relinquishment must be submitted to the Collector in the prescribed form.
The Collector can reject an application if the applicants are not competent to relinquish, if the title is defective, if there are arrears of land revenue, or if the land is inaccessible.
The definition of relinquishment has been expanded to cover unconditional surrender of rights by various parties involved with the land.

rights: Right to relinquish land under certain conditions.
Rights of registered holders, cultivating tenants, and intermediaries regarding relinquishment.
duties: Duty to submit applications for relinquishment to the Collector.
Duty to ensure valid title and clear land revenue.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act and Rules regarding relinquishment.

key_procedures: Joint intent of registered holders, cultivating tenants, and intermediaries to relinquish land.
Submission of an application in the prescribed form to the Collector.
Collector's review and potential rejection of the application based on specified grounds.
Unconditional surrender of rights over the land.
administration: The Act is administered by the relevant authorities in the Kerala state government, likely within the land revenue or land reforms department.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on 17th February 1963.
Published in the Gazette Extraordinary, dated 18th February 1963.

title: THE KERALA LAND RELINQUISHMENT (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1966
purpose: To amend the Kerala Land Relinquishment Act, 1958.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Land Relinquishment (Amendment) Act, 1966. It shall come into force at once.

Amends section 2 of the Kerala Land Relinquishment Act, 1958, by substituting "the Revenue Divisional Officer of the division" for "the Collector of the district" and similarly for "Collector" where it occurs and for "Revenue Divisional Officer" where it occurs.
Amends section 4 of the principal Act. Sub-sections (2) to (6) are substituted for the word "Collector" and sub-sections (7) and (8) shall be omitted.
Inserts new sections 4A (Appeal), 4B (Revision), and 4C (Land relinquished to vest in Government).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Revenue Divisional Officer, Collector, Board of Revenue
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through appeal and revision processes as outlined in the new sections.

rights: Right to prefer an appeal to the Collector from an order of the Revenue Divisional Officer.
Right to apply to the Board of Revenue for revision of any order passed by the Collector.
duties: Land relinquished shall vest in the Government free of all encumbrances.

key_procedures: Appeal Process: Any person aggrieved by an order passed by the Revenue Divisional Officer can prefer an appeal to the Collector within such time as may be prescribed. The order of the Collector on such appeal shall be final.

Revision Process: The Board of Revenue may, either on its own motion or on an application made by any aggrieved person for revision, call for the record of any proceeding in which an order has been passed by the Collector under section 4A, and pass such order thereon as it thinks fit. Provided that the Board of Revenue shall not of its own motion call for the record of any such proceeding after the expiry of one year from the date of the order of the Collector. Every application for revision under sub-section (1) against an order of the Collector shall be made within one month from the date on which the order was communicated to the person aggrieved by the order.

Land Relinquishment Vesting: Where an application for relinquishment of any land is accepted in consequence of an order passed by the Revenue Divisional Officer under section 4 or the Collector under section 4A or the Board of Revenue under section 4B, such land together with all rights, title and interest of the registered holder or, as the case may be, of the registered holder, the cultivating tenant and the intermediaries, if any, in such land shall vest in the Government free of all encumbrances.
administration: Revenue Divisional Officer, Collector, Board of Revenue
important_notes: The amendments were made as further to the Kerala Land Relinquishment Act, 1958.
This Act was enacted by the President in the seventeenth year of the Republic of India.
Published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 95, dated 5th December, 1966.

title: THE KERALA LAND RELINQUISHMENT ACT, 1958
purpose: To make provision for the relinquishment of lands in the State of Kerala by registered holders in favour of Government.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force at once. It applies to registered holders of land in Kerala.

key_definitions.registered holder: In relation to any land means a person whose name is registered in the revenue records as the proprietor of the land.
key_definitions.relinquishment: Means unconditional surrender of all the rights of a registered holder over the land.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act is called the Kerala Land Relinquishment Act, 1958, extends to the whole of Kerala, and comes into force at once.
Defines 'registered holder', 'relinquishment', and 'prescribed'.

A registered holder may relinquish the whole or any portion of any land entered in his name in the revenue records, provided that such land or portion of land is in his possession and free of encumbrances.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure to be followed when lands are relinquished
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for relinquishment, including application to the Collector, inquiry, notice to interested persons, objections, and appeals to the Board of Revenue. It also specifies grounds on which the Collector can reject the application.

No land registered in the revenue records in the name of a person jointly with the name or names of one or more persons, shall be relinquished except with the consent of all the persons in whose names the land is registered in the revenue records.
Empowers the Government to make rules for the purpose of carrying out the provisions of this Act.

important_rules: A registered holder can relinquish land only if it is in their possession and free of encumbrances.
Relinquishment of jointly held land requires the consent of all registered holders.
The Collector must inquire into the application for relinquishment and consider objections.
Appeals against the Collector's decision can be made to the Board of Revenue.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Collector, and subsequently the Board of Revenue for appeals.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the procedures outlined in Section 4, including inquiry, issuing notices, accepting or rejecting applications, and hearing appeals.

rights: Right of a registered holder to relinquish land.
Right of interested persons to raise objections against relinquishment.
Right to appeal against the Collector's decision.
duties: Duty of the registered holder to follow the prescribed procedure for relinquishment.
Duty of the Collector to conduct proper inquiry and consider objections.
Duty to publish notice of relinquishment in the village where the land is situated.

key_procedures: Application for relinquishment by a registered holder to the Collector of the district.
Collector publishes a notice and inquires into the application.
Any interested person can object to the relinquishment.
Collector passes an order accepting or rejecting the application.
Appeal against the Collector's order to the Board of Revenue.
Relinquishment of jointly held land requires consent of all joint holders.
administration: The Government (through the Board of Revenue and Collectors).
important_notes: Relinquishment is only possible for land in possession and free of encumbrances.

Specific grounds exist for the Collector to reject a relinquishment application, including the registered holder not being competent to relinquish, defective revenue records, arrears of land revenue, or land not being accessible except through Government land.
The Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 8th August, 1958.

title: The Kerala Land Tax (Amendment) Act, 1972
purpose: To amend the Kerala Land Tax Act, 1961 for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: The Act applies to land within the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.landholder: In relation to any land held by a cultivating tenant, in possession of a kanam tenant, in relation to any land which has not been surveyed and is not held by a cultivating tenant, or in relation to any other land, the registered holder for the time being of such land, and includes his legal representatives and assigns, and any person who under any law for the time being in force is liable for the payment of public revenue due in respect of the land held by him.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Land Tax (Amendment) Act, 1972. It shall come into force at once. Certain clauses and sections are deemed to have come into force on specific dates in 1970, 1971, and 1956.
Amends section 3 of the principal Act by substituting clause (3) which defines 'landholder'.

Amends section 5 of the principal Act by omitting provisos and substituting a new proviso regarding situations where land is in possession of a tenant or other person not being the landholder, and the income obtained by the landholder from that land is less than the basic tax payable thereon.

Amends section 6 of the principal Act by adding a proviso to sub-section (3) and substituting sub-section (4) regarding the procedure for passing orders on an application and giving notice to the landholder concerned.

Inserts a new section 6A, titled 'Assessment of basic tax', which details the manner of assessment and the procedure for serving notices by the prescribed authority, including provisions for objections and inquiries.

Amends section 7 of the principal Act by substituting "section 6" with "sections 6 and 6A", omitting a proviso, and inserting a new sub-section (3A) regarding provisional assessment and notice. It also amends sub-section (6) to substitute dates and figure references.
Amends section 9 of the principal Act by substituting the words, brackets, figures and letter "or under sub-section (3) of section 6A".
Amends section 20 of the principal Act by omitting clause (a) and re-lettering clause (aa) as clause (a).

Repeals the Kerala Land Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 1972 (2 of 1972). Notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: The Act comes into force at once.
Certain provisions relating to commencement are deemed to have come into force on specific dates in the past.

The prescribed authority shall serve a provisional notice of demand in the prescribed form specifying the extent of the land, the rate and amount of basic tax payable, and requiring the landholder to prefer objections, if any.
The prescribed authority, after giving notice to the landholder concerned and any other person who it considers necessary, shall pass orders on an application or provisional assessment.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The prescribed authority
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through serving notices, conducting inquiries, and passing orders regarding land tax assessment and demand.

rights: Right to prefer objections in writing to the prescribed authority against a provisional notice of demand or rate or amount of basic tax.
duties: Duty of the landholder and any other person liable to pay the basic tax to comply with the notice served by the prescribed authority.
Duty to pay basic tax if liable.
obligations: Obligation to pay basic tax.

key_procedures: Serving of provisional notice of demand for basic tax by the prescribed authority.
Landholder's right to prefer objections in writing within a specified period.
Prescribed authority's duty to consider objections and pass orders.
Giving notice to the landholder concerned and any other person liable to pay the basic tax before passing final orders.
administration: The document does not explicitly state the administering department. However, it pertains to land tax, likely administered by a revenue or land revenue department of the Kerala State Government.
important_notes: The Act is published in the Gazette Extraordinary No 196, dated 30th March, 1972.
The amendment to section 3, related to the definition of 'landholder', makes specific provisions for different types of land tenure and possession.
Section 6A outlines a detailed procedure for the assessment of basic tax, emphasizing the need for notice and opportunity for objection.
The repeal of the 1972 Ordinance clarifies that actions taken under it are valid as if done under the amended principal Act.

title: THE KERALA LAND TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1968
purpose: To amend the Kerala Land Tax Act, 1961, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala. It amends the Kerala Land Tax Act, 1961.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Land Tax (Amendment) Act, 1968, and it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1968.

Amends section 5 of the Kerala Land Tax Act, 1961. It rephrases the basic tax to be charged and levied on any land, with a specific limit based on the aggregate extent of land held by the owner. It also specifies different rates for different types of crops or plants. For instance, for coconut, arecanut, pepper, tea, coffee, rubber, cardamom or cashew, a higher rate is applied. For any other special crop, plant or tree, a lower rate is applied. The section also details changes to the words regarding the rates of land tax, such as 'four rupees and ninety-four paise per hectare' and 'ten rupees per hectare'.
main_sections.details: Specifically, it amends the principal Act to substitute: "two rupees per acre" with "four rupees and ninety-four paise per hectare"; "ten rupees per acre" with "twenty-four rupees and seventy paise per hectare"; "two rupees per acre" with "four rupees and ninety-four paise per hectare". It also provides for a specific tax rate for land held by the owner, up to 0.810 hectare, and for land used for growing specific crops like coconut, arecanut, pepper, tea, coffee, rubber, cardamom or cashew, or any other special crop, plant or tree.

main_sections.description: Amends section 6 of the principal Act by substituting the words "four rupees and ninety-four paise per hectare" with "ten rupees per hectare" for certain cases, and similarly "two rupees per acre" with "four rupees and ninety-four paise per hectare" in a first proviso, and "two rupees per acre" with "four rupees and ninety-four paise per hectare" in a second proviso. It also provides for circumstances where the Government may notify the rate of land tax for specific crops.
main_sections.details: Modifies rates specified in sub-section (1) and pro-visos within sub-section (1) of section 6 of the principal Act. Also modifies the wording in sub-section (3) related to publication of notification.

main_sections.description: Amends section 7 of the principal Act. It modifies references to sub-sections and words within those sub-sections. It also changes the expiry period of a lease or license from "five years" to "the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette" for the purpose of replacement of "before the expiry of a period of five years from the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette, the words figures and letters 'before the 31st day of December, 1968' shall be substituted".
main_sections.details: Specifically deals with amendments to sub-section (4) and sub-section (6) of section 7 of the principal Act. The amendment in sub-section (6) concerns the period of validity for certain notices or licenses.

main_sections.description: Amends section 8 of the principal Act by substituting the existing monetary figures with new ones. Specifically, "Rs. 11-9-0 (one rupee and fifty-six naye paise per hectare)" is replaced by "Rs. 3 (three rupees and eighty-five paise per hectare)".
main_sections.details: Amends section 8 of the principal Act concerning the tax rates, replacing the old rate with a new one: "one rupee and fifty-six naye paise per hectare" with "three rupees and eighty-five paise per hectare".

main_sections.description: Repeals the Kerala Land Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 1968 (2 of 1968). It also states that the repeal shall not affect any right, duty, obligation, penalty, forfeiture or punishment acquired, accrued, or incurred, or any investigation, legal proceeding or remedy commenced or continued, or any order or action taken under the said Ordinance. Any such investigation, legal proceeding or remedy may be continued, and any such order or action may be continued, prosecuted, or enforced as if the Ordinance had not been repealed. Any appointment made, notification issued, rule or form made or issued, or any other thing done under the said Ordinance shall, in so far as it is consistent with the provisions of this Act, be deemed to have been made or done under this Act.

important_rules: Land tax rates for different extents of land and types of crops are revised.
Specific rates are provided for land used for growing coconut, arecanut, pepper, tea, coffee, rubber, cardamom or cashew, and for any other special crop, plant or tree.
The amendment clarifies the monetary values for land tax per hectare.
Amendments are made to the provisions regarding the expiry of leases or licenses under the principal Act.
key_procedures: The Act comes into force on April 1, 1968.
Any action taken under the repealed Ordinance continues to be valid under this Act.
important_notes: The Act is published in the Gazette Extraordinary, No. 229, dated 18th September, 1968.
The amendments made by this Act have retrospective effect from April 1, 1968.

title: THE KERALA LAND TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1969
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Land Tax Act, 1961.
scope: Applies to landholders in the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act is called the Kerala Land Tax (Amendment) Act, 1969 and that Section 2 of the Act is deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1968, with the remaining provisions of this Act to come into force at once.

This section amends Section 5 of the Kerala Land Tax Act, 1961. It introduces provisions regarding the aggregate extent of land held by a landholder in the State and the furnishing of returns for financial years. It also includes provisions for cases where a landholder makes a false statement or fails to produce documents, which may be treated as an offence under the Indian Penal Code.
This section amends Section 7 of the principal Act, specifically for the figures, letters and words '31st day of December, 1968', which are to be substituted with '31st day of December, 1970'.

This section amends Section 20 of the principal Act. It re-letters clause (a) of sub-section (2) to clause (aa) and inserts a new clause (a) to sub-section (2). The new clause (a) specifies that as to the time within which the return under sub-section (1A) of section 5 shall be furnished, the form of such return, the manner in which such return shall be verified and the particulars of such return shall contain.

important_rules: Landholders with an aggregate extent of land less than 0.5 hectare in the State shall furnish a return in that financial year within such time as may be prescribed.

The prescribed authority may serve on any landholder who has made a return under sub-section (1A), a notice requiring him to produce or cause to be produced, or before the date mentioned in any notice under sub-section (1B), such documents as are referred to in the notice.

If a landholder makes a statement in a verification mentioned in sub-section (1A) which is false and which he either knows or believes to be false or does not believe to be true, he shall be deemed to have committed the offence described in section 177 of the Indian Penal Code.

Notwithstanding anything contained in the proviso to sub-section (1), basic tax shall be charged and levied on the lands held by a landholder, if such landholder fails without reasonable cause or excuse - (a) to furnish in due time the return mentioned in sub-section (1A); or (b) to produce or cause to be produced on or before the date mentioned in any notice under sub-section (1B) such documents as are referred to in the notice.

penalties: False statements may be deemed an offence under section 177 of the Indian Penal Code.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Prescribed authority
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By serving notices requiring production of documents, and by levying basic tax in cases of failure to furnish returns or produce documents.

rights: Right to have an aggregate extent of land less than 0.5 hectare.
duties: Duty to furnish a return for the financial year within the prescribed time if the aggregate extent of land held is less than 0.5 hectare.
Duty to produce documents as required by the prescribed authority.

key_procedures: Furnishing of returns by landholders with less than 0.5 hectare of land.
Issuance of notices by the prescribed authority to landholders for production of documents.
Verification of returns and particulars of returns.
administration: The administration of this Act would likely fall under the revenue or land revenue department of the Kerala Government, based on the subject matter.
important_notes: Section 2 of the Act is deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1968.
Section 3 amends the date for figures, letters and words from '31st day of December, 1968' to '31st day of December, 1970'.

title: The Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 1976
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 for the purposes therein after appearing.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.kudikidappukaran: A person who has been issued a certificate of purchase under sub-section (2) of section 80C.
key_definitions.landless agricultural labourer: A labourer who does not possess any other land.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 1976.
Amends section 72H of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963, concerning the amendment of sub-sections (2), (3), (4) and (5) and substitution of sub-section (6).
Amends section 72I of the principal Act by substituting sub-section (4) or sub-section (5).
Amends section 75 of the principal Act by substituting clause (a) for clause (a).
Amends section 77 of the principal Act by adding a further proviso to sub-section (1).
Amends section 80C of the principal Act by substituting sub-section (2) and omitting sub-sections (3), (5) and (6).
Amends section 80D of the principal Act by substituting the words "the second or any subsequent instalment" for the words "any instalment".
Amends section 96 of the principal Act by substituting the Explanation.
Amends section 100A of the principal Act by substituting sub-section (2A) and inserting a new sub-section (6B).
Amends section 102 of the principal Act by inserting the words "sub-section (2) of section 77", shall be inserted.
Amends section 109 of the principal Act by substituting clause (c) for clause (c).
Amends section 123 of the principal Act by substituting words in sub-section (1) and sub-section (2).

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 123A.
main_sections.description: Substitutes a new section 123A concerning cognisance of offences under section 118A.
Repeals The Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Ordinance, 1975 and provides for saving of actions taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Rule regarding compensation payable under sub-section (1) in respect of a holding being paid in cash in lump within one year of the date of the Land Tribunal's order.

Rule regarding bearing of interest at the rate of four per cent per annum from the date of expiry of the said period of one year on such compensation if not paid on or before the expiry of the period.
Rules regarding the constitution of benches of the Taluk Land Board and the times and places of sitting.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Taluk Land Board, Judicial Magistrates
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Trial of offences punishable under section 118A by the Taluk Land Board of the taluk in which the person bound to file the statement under section 85A ordinarily resides. Trial of summons cases by Judicial Magistrates.

rights: Right of a cultivating tenant to opt to pay the purchase price payable by him under section 72L in a lump, or where the landowner or the intermediary is a small holder and the amount of compensation in respect of all holdings held by cultivating tenants under him does not exceed five thousand rupees, the amount of compensation determined under sub-section (3) shall be paid in cash in lump within one year from the date of such determination.

Provided that a person to whom a certificate of purchase has been issued under the said sub-section or his successor-in-interest shall not be entitled to any benefit under thus clause after the expiry of a period of twenty years from the date on which the right, title and interest in respect of the land allowed to be purchased by such person have vested in him under the said sub-section.
obligations: Person bound to file the statement under section 85A ordinarily resides, to appear before the Taluk Land Board of the taluk.

key_procedures: Procedure for substitution of sub-sections in section 72H, 72I, 75, 77, 80C, 80D, 96, 100A, 102, 109, 123 of the principal Act.
Procedure for substitution of section 123A defining cognisance of offences under section 118A.
Procedure for the trial of offences punishable under section 118A by the Taluk Land Board or by a Judicial Magistrate.
Procedure for the removal of doubts regarding the provisions of section 100A and section 118A.
administration: Taluk Land Board, Government
important_notes: Received the assent of the President on the 25th day of March, 1976 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 192, dated 25th March, 1976.

Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (4) or sub-section (5), where the cultivating tenant has opted to pay the purchase price payable by him under section 72L in a lump, or where the landowner or the intermediary is a small holder and the amount of compensation in respect of all holdings held by cultivating tenants under him does not exceed five thousand rupees, the amount of compensation determined under sub-section (3) shall be paid in cash in lump within one year from the date of such determination and if not so paid shall bear interest at the rate of four per cent per annum from the date of expiry of that period.

Provided further that the Land Tribunal shall not entertain any application under this sub-section in respect of a kudikidappu, if an order under sub-section (3) of section 80B allowing an application for the purchase of that kudikidappu has been passed and such order is in force.
The members of the Taluk Land Board shall be entitled to a sitting fee of ten rupees per day for attending the meetings of the Board.
Provided that the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, and for reasons to be stated in such notification, fix such other amount as they deem fit as sitting fee.

Provided that a person to whom a certificate of purchase has been issued under the said sub-section or his successor-in-interest shall not be entitled to any benefit under thus clause after the expiry of a period of twenty years from the date on which the right, title and interest in respect of the land allowed to be purchased by such person have vested in him under the said sub-section.

For the trial of offences punishable under section 118A by the Taluk Land Board, the Government may make rules in respect of the following matters, namely— (a) the constitution of benches consisting of two or more members of the Taluk Land Board; (b) the times and places of sitting, and (c) the mode of settling differences of opinion which may arise between the members of the bench so constituted.

For the removal of doubts it is hereby declared that, notwithstanding anything contained in section 100A, a Taluk Land Board or any member of a Taluk Land Board shall not take cognisance of, or try, any offence punishable under section 118A except in accordance with the provisions of this section and the rules made thereunder.

Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act as if this Act had come into force on the 11th day of December, 1975.

title: THE KERALA LIME SHELLS (CONTROL) ACT, 1957
purpose: To provide for the control of the acquisition, sale, supply and distribution of lime-shells in the State of Kerala.
scope: The entire State of Kerala.

key_definitions.dealer: A person carrying on, either personally or through any other person the business of selling lime shells, whether wholesale or retail.
key_definitions.Licensing Authority: An officer appointed by the Government to perform the functions of a Licensing Authority under this Act.
key_definitions.Lime-shell: Means the shells of all varieties of shellfish by whatever name called.
key_definitions.offer for sale: Includes an intimation by a dealer or producer of the price proposed by him for a sale of lime-shells made by the publication of a price list, by exposing his lime-shells for sale in association with a mark indicating price, by the furnishing of a quotation or otherwise howsoever.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.producer: Means a person carrying on the business of collecting lime-shells and stocking the same for sale.
key_definitions.dealer or producer licensed hereunder: Means a dealer or producer who is deemed to be in possession of lime-shells (a) when they are held on his behalf by another person; (b) notwithstanding that they are mortgaged to another person.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (the whole of Kerala), and that it shall come into force at once or by notification in the Gazette.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'dealer', 'Licensing Authority', 'lime-shell', 'offer for sale', 'prescribed', 'producer', and 'dealer or producer licensed hereunder'.

No person other than a dealer or producer licensed under this Act shall carry on the business of selling lime-shells or of collecting lime-shells and stocking the same for sale. The Licensing Authority may grant a license in such form and subject to such terms and conditions as may be prescribed, or may refuse to grant a licence, in which case he shall communicate his reasons for such refusal to the applicant. The Licensing Authority may, at any time during the currency of a licence, rescind the licence by order in writing to the licence holder, for a breach of any of the terms and conditions of the licence.

main_sections.section_title: Fixing of maximum prices and maximum quantities which may be held or sold.
main_sections.description: The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, fix in respect of lime-shells: (a) the maximum price or rate which may be charged by a dealer or producer. (b) the maximum quantity which may at any one time be possessed by a dealer or producer. (c) the maximum quantity which may in any one transaction be sold to any one person.

main_sections.section_title: Restrictions on sale, etc., where maximum is fixed under section 4.
main_sections.description: No dealer or producer licensed under this Act shall: (a) sell, agree to sell, offer for sale or otherwise dispose of lime-shells for a price or at a rate exceeding the maximum fixed by notification under clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 4. (b) have in his possession at any one time a quantity of lime-shells exceeding the maximum fixed by notification under clause (b) of sub-section (1) of section 4. (c) sell, agree to sell or offer for sale to any person in any one transaction a quantity of lime-shells exceeding the maximum fixed by notification under clause (c) of sub-section (1) of section 4.

main_sections.section_title: Duty to declare possession of excess stocks.
main_sections.description: Any dealer or producer licensed under this Act, having in his possession a quantity of lime-shells exceeding that permitted under this Act, shall forthwith report the fact to the Licensing Authority and shall take such action as to the storage, distribution or disposal of the excess quantity as the Licensing Authority may direct.

No dealer or producer licensed under this Act, unless previously authorised to do so by the Licensing Authority, refuse without sufficient cause, to sell to any person lime-shells within the limits as to quantity, if any, imposed under this Act. Explanation. - The possibility or expectation of obtaining a higher price for lime-shells at a later date shall not be deemed to be a sufficient cause for the purposes of this section.

(1) Every dealer or producer licensed under this Act, when selling lime-shells for cash shall, if the amount of the purchase is five rupees or more, in all cases, and if the amount of the purchase is less than five rupees, when so required by the purchaser, give to the purchaser a cash memorandum containing such particulars of the transaction as may be prescribed. (2) The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, exempt specified areas or classes of dealers or producers licensed under this Act from the operation of this section.

If in the opinion of the Government, it is necessary or expedient so to do, they may by order in writing- (a) prohibit the disposal of lime-shells except in such circumstances and under such conditions as may be specified in the order. (b) direct the sale of lime-shells to any such dealer or class of dealers licensed under this Act and in such quantities as may be specified in the order, and may make such further orders as appear to them to be necessary or expedient in connection with any order issued under this section.

(1) Whoever contravenes any of the provisions of this Act or any of the terms and conditions of a licence issued under this Act or any directions made under authority conferred by this Act, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term with may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both. (2) A court convicting any person of any offence punishable under this Act may order that the stock of lime-shells in respect of which the offence was committed and any property involved in or utilised for the commission of such offence shall be forfeited to the Government.

(1) If the person contravening the provisions of this Act is a company, every person, who at the time the contravention was committed was in charge of and was responsible to the company for the conduct of the business of the company as well as the company, shall be deemed to be guilty of the contravention and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly: Provided that nothing contained in this sub-section shall render any such person liable to any punishment if he proves that the contravention took place without his knowledge or that he exercised all due diligence to prevent such contravention. (2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), where an offence under this Act has been committed by a company and it is proved that the offence has been committed with the consent or connivance of, or is attributable to any neglect on the part of any director, manager, secretary or other officer of the company, such director, manager, secretary or other officer shall also be deemed to be guilty of that offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly. Explanation.—For the purposes of this section- (a) "company" means any body corporate, and includes a firm or other association of individuals, and (b) "director" in relation to a firm, means a partner in the firm.

main_sections.section_title: Offences under the Act to be cognizable.
main_sections.description: Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (Central Act V of 1898), all offences under this Act shall be cognizable.
No person other than a police officer of or above the rank of an Inspector of Police shall investigate any offence under this Act.

Any person competent to investigate any offence under this Act may search any place in which he has reason to believe that an offence under this Act has been, or is being, or is about to be, committed and the stock of lime-shells which is, or is about to be, committed and any property involved in or utilised for the commission of such offence.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
main_sections.description: No suit, prosecution or other legal proceedings shall lie against any person for anything which is in good faith done or intended to be done under this Act.

(1) The provisions of this Act shall not apply to the collection, stocking or selling of lime-shell by any person as curios or for making ornaments. (2) Subject to such conditions and restrictions as the Government may think fit to impose, they may, by general or special order notified in the Gazette, exempt from all or any of the provisions of this Act, any person or class of persons who— (i) collect lime-shell and stock them for conversion into lime for use as an ingredient in chewing material, or (ii) collect and sell lime-shells for the edible content thereof.

(1) The Government may make rules to carry out the purposes of this Act. (2) In particular and without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing power such rules may provide for all or any of the following matters, namely:— (a) all matters expressly required or allowed by this Act to be prescribed, (b) the charging of fees for licenses issued under this Act, (c) the maintenance by licensed dealers and producers generally or by any licensed dealer and producer in particular, of records of all sale and purchase transactions or disposals made by him, and the production of such records to the Licensing Authority. (d) the furnishing of such information as may be required by the Licensing Authority with respect to the business carried on by any dealer or producer, (e) the furnishing of returns to the Licensing Authority by licensed dealers and producers and the particulars which such returns shall contain. (3) All rules made under this Act shall be published in the Gazette.
The Travancore-Cochin Lime-shells (Control) Act, 1956. is hereby repealed.

important_rules: No person other than a licensed dealer or producer can sell or collect lime shells.
Dealers and producers must report excess stock of lime shells to the Licensing Authority.
Dealers and producers must provide cash memos for cash sales of Rs. 5 or more.
The Government can prohibit the disposal or direct the sale of lime shells under certain conditions.
No dealer or producer can refuse to sell lime shells without sufficient cause.
Rules made under the Act must be published in the Gazette.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.
Forfeiture of stock of lime-shells and any property involved in or utilised for the commission of the offence.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Licensing Authority and Police officers (Inspector of Police and above for investigation).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Investigation of offences by Police officers (Inspector rank and above), search and seizure of places and stocks, prosecution in courts.

rights: Right to obtain a license to deal or produce lime shells.
Right to receive a cash memorandum for cash sales.
Right to seek reasons for refusal of a license.
duties: Duty to obtain a license to deal or produce lime shells.
Duty to sell within prescribed prices and quantities.
Duty to report excess stocks.
Duty to provide cash memos.
Duty to comply with terms and conditions of the license and directions from the Licensing Authority.
obligations: Obligation to follow all provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining a license: Apply to the Licensing Authority in the prescribed form and subject to prescribed terms and conditions. The authority may grant or refuse the license, communicating reasons for refusal.
Procedure for reporting excess stocks: Dealer or producer must report immediately to the Licensing Authority.
Procedure for sale and purchase: Sale must be at a fixed price and quantity, and a cash memorandum must be provided if requested or for sales of Rs. 5 or more.
Procedure for investigation of offences: Conducted by Police officers of or above the rank of Inspector of Police.
Procedure for search and seizure: Carried out by any person competent to investigate an offence under the Act.
administration: Licensing Authority appointed by the Government, and the Government for making rules and notifications.
important_notes: The Act is repealed: The Travancore-Cochin Lime-shells (Control) Act, 1956.
Exemptions apply to collection, stocking, or selling lime-shells as curios or for making ornaments.
The Government may exempt certain persons or classes of persons from the Act's provisions by notification.
The Act extends to the whole of Kerala.

title: THE KERALA LIVE- STOCK IMPROVEMENT (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1968
purpose: To amend the Kerala Live-Stock Improvement Act, 1961, for the purpose hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Republic of India, specifically concerning the provisions of The Kerala Live-Stock Improvement Act, 1961.

key_definitions.principal Act: The Kerala Live-Stock Improvement Act, 1961 (17 of 1961)
key_definitions.religious institution: For the purposes of section 21, 'religious institution' means a math or temple.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Live-Stock Improvement (Amendment) Act, 1968.
In section 7 of the Kerala Live-Stock Improvement Act, 1961 (17 of 1961), the words "two miles" and the words "three kilometres" shall be substituted.

In section 8 of the principal Act, after sub-section (2), the following sub-section shall be inserted: "(3) A person keeping a bull, who has been required by an order under sub-section (1) to have it castrated, and the owner of the bull where such person is not the owner thereof, shall not part with possession or custody, or transfer the ownership, of the bull until it is castrated."

Section 11 of the principal Act shall be renumbered as sub-section (1) of that section and, after sub-section (1) so renumbered, the following sub-section shall be inserted, namely:- "(2) Whoever contravenes the provisions of sub-section (3) of section 8 shall be punishable with fine which may extend to one hundred rupees and, in the case of a second or subsequent offence, with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both."

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 21.
main_sections.description: For section 21 of the principal Act, the following section shall be substituted, namely:- "21. Saving.--Nothing contained in this Act shall apply to a bull dedicated to a religious institution in accordance with any religious usage or custom and directly maintained by that institution."

important_rules: Rule: A person keeping a bull, required to have it castrated, and the owner of the bull (if not the same person) shall not transfer possession, custody, or ownership of the bull until it is castrated.

Rule: Contravention of the provisions of sub-section (3) of section 8 is punishable with a fine up to one hundred rupees. For a second or subsequent offense, it can lead to imprisonment up to one month, or a fine up to five hundred rupees, or both.
Rule: The Act does not apply to bulls dedicated to religious institutions and maintained by them.

penalties: Fine up to one hundred rupees for contravening sub-section (3) of section 8.
For second or subsequent offense: Imprisonment up to one month, or fine up to five hundred rupees, or both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be the authorities responsible for the enforcement of the Kerala Live-Stock Improvement Act, 1961.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings and imposition of fines and imprisonment as specified for contraventions of the Act's provisions.

duties: Duty of a person keeping a bull to comply with an order for castration.
Duty of the owner of a bull (or the person in possession) not to transfer ownership or possession until castration is complete, if an order has been issued.
obligations: Obligation to be punishable for contravening certain provisions of section 8.

key_procedures: Procedure: If an order is issued for the castration of a bull, the person in possession and the owner must ensure the bull is not transferred in possession, custody, or ownership until the castration is completed.
Procedure: For violations of the above, penalties including fines and imprisonment can be imposed.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but likely falls under the purview of the relevant agricultural or animal husbandry department of the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: Section 21 provides a saving clause for bulls dedicated to religious institutions.
The amendment substitutes a new section 21.
The amendment is based on the Nineteenth Year of the Republic of India.

title: The Kerala Live-Stock Improvement Act, 1961
purpose: An Act to provide for the improvement of live-stock in the State of Kerala.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.bull: includes a buffalo-bull and a heifer
key_definitions.cow: includes a buffalo-cow and a heifer
key_definitions.Director: means the officer appointed by the Government as the Director of Animal Husbandry for the State of Kerala, and includes any other person on whom the powers or duties of the Director under this Act have been conferred or imposed under section 4
key_definitions.licence: means a licence granted under section 4
key_definitions.Licensing Officer: means the Director or any other officer person authorised to grant licences under section 4
key_definitions.prescribed: means prescribed by rules made under this Act
key_definitions.person: a person is said to "keep a bull" if he owns the bull or has the bull in his possession or custody; and a bull is said to be "castrated" if it is rendered incapable of propagating its species.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Live-Stock Improvement Act, 1961. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. This section shall come into force at once, and the Government may, from time to time by notification in the Gazette, apply all or any of the remaining provisions of this Act to the whole or any portion of the State of Kerala from such date and for such period, if any, as may be specified in the notification, and may cancel or modify any such notification.
Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'bull', 'cow', 'Director', 'licence', 'Licensing Officer', and 'prescribed'.
The Government may by general or special order confer on and impose upon any person all or any of the powers or duties of the Director under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Bulls which have attained a certain age to be licensed.
main_sections.description: No person shall keep a bull which has attained the prescribed age except under and in accordance with the terms, conditions and restrictions of a licence granted under this section, unless it is certified by the prescribed officer that the bull has been effectively castrated by a method and in a manner approved by the Director. This section also details when a licence can be refused or revoked, and conditions for surrender of licence.

Specifies grounds on which a licensing officer may refuse or revoke a licence, including defective or inferior conformation, suffering from incurable contagious or infectious disease, or being of a breed which is undesirable to propagate in the State of Kerala. It also covers instances where the licensing officer may hear a licencee and circumstances of licence revocation.
A licence granted in respect of a bull shall be surrendered without delay to the licensing officer, if the licence period expires or the licence is revoked under this Act, or the bull dies.

The licensing officer may by order require any person keeping a bull to submit it for inspection by himself or by any officer or person deputed by him for the purpose, at any reasonable time, either at the place where the bull is kept for the time being or at any other reasonable place specified in the order not being farther than two miles from the place where the bull ordinarily kept, and thereupon it shall be the duty of the person keeping the bull to submit it for inspection accordingly, and render all reasonable assistance in connection with such inspection to the officer concerned.

main_sections.section_title: Power to order castration of bulls.
main_sections.description: The licensing officer may by order require any person keeping a bull which in his opinion has attained the prescribed age, and in respect of which a licence is for the time being in force under this Act, to have it castrated within one month from the date of the service of the order by a method and in a manner approved by the Director and specified in the order. Such castrations shall be performed by a licensed veterinary surgeon or by any other person approved by the Director, free of charge, unless the owner or other person keeping the bull desires to make his own arrangements for complying with the order.

main_sections.section_title: Duty to inform owner of contents of notice or order of castration.
main_sections.description: If any notice or order served under section 4, section 5, or section 6 on any person who is not the owner of the bull, it shall be the duty of that person forthwith to take all reasonable steps to inform the owner of the contents of such notice or order, and if he fails to do so, he shall be liable to indemnify the owner against any loss the owner may sustain by reason thereof.

It shall be the duty of any person who for the time being keeps a bull in respect of which a licence has been obtained and is in force, to produce such licence (a) within a reasonable time, at any place where the bull is for the time being, on demand made by a licensing officer or an officer of the Animal Husbandry Department not below the rank of Veterinary Surgeon, or an officer of the Revenue Department not below the rank of Deputy Tahsildar or such other officer as may be authorised in this behalf by the Government by general or special order or (b) before a cow is served by the bull, on demand made by the person in charge of the cow.
Describes penalties for contravention of the Act's rules or terms, conditions, or restrictions of a licence, including fines and imprisonment.

main_sections.section_title: Power of licensing officer to castrate bulls.
main_sections.description: Details the powers of the licensing officer to castrate bulls if the owner fails to do so, including the process of seizure and sale of the bull if the owner cannot be traced or refuses to pay costs.

main_sections.section_title: Power of licensing officer etc. to inspect or mark bulls and enter premises.
main_sections.description: The licensing officer or any other officer authorised by him shall have power at all reasonable times to inspect any bull or to mark any bull with a prescribed mark in the prescribed manner, and to enter any premises for the purpose of inspection or marking.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of officer to report offences etc.
main_sections.description: It shall be the duty of all village officers and servants and all officers of the Animal Husbandry, Agricultural and Revenue Departments and officers and servants of Panchayats and Municipalities and other officers notified by the Government in this behalf to report the commission of any offence under this Act, to give immediate information to the nearest licensing officer of the commission of any offence, or of the intention or preparation to commit any offence, punishable under this Act, which may come to their knowledge, to take all reasonable measures in their power to prevent the commission of any such offence which they may know or have reason to believe is about or likely to be committed; and to assist any licensing officer in carrying out the provisions of this Act.
No Magistrate shall take cognizance of any offence under this Act except upon a complaint made by a licensing officer or any person authorised by such officer in this behalf.
All officers and servants specified in, or noticed under section 14 shall be deemed to be public servants within the meaning of section 21 of the Indian Penal Code.

No suit, prosecution or other proceedings shall lie against any officer or servant of the Government for any act done or purported to be done under this Act for the sanction of the Government for prosecution or defence in any suit, prosecution or other proceeding instituted within six months from the date of the act complained of.

main_sections.section_title: Limitation for certain suits and prosecutions.
main_sections.description: No suit, prosecution or other proceeding shall be instituted against any officer or servant of the Government in respect of any act done or purporting to be done under this Act, unless the suit, prosecution or other proceeding is instituted within six months from the date of the act complained of.

The Government may at any time either suo motu or on application, call for and examine the record of any order passed by, or any proceedings recorded by, any officer or person under this Act for the purpose of satisfying themselves as to the legality or propriety of such order or the regularity of such proceedings, and may pass such order or thereof as they think fit.

The Government may make rules to carry out the purposes of this Act. These rules can cover all matters expressed or required to be provided by this Act, circumstances under which licences may be granted, fees for licences, powers and duties of officers, and service of notices and orders. Rules made under this section shall, as soon as may be after they are made, be laid before the Legislative Assembly for a period of not less than fourteen days and shall be subject to such modifications, if any, as the Legislative Assembly may make during the session in which they are so laid or the session immediately following.

Nothing contained in this Act shall apply to a bull kept in good faith for a religious purpose in accordance with any religious usage or custom, provided that notice of the dedication is given in the prescribed manner to the licensing officer.

Repeals The Madras Live-stock Improvement Act, 1940 (Act XV of 1940) in its application to the Malabar District referred to in sub-section (2) of section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, and the Travancore-Cochin Live-Stock Improvement Act, 1954 (Act XII of 1954).

important_rules: No person shall keep a bull which has attained the prescribed age except under and in accordance with the terms, conditions and restrictions of a licence granted under this section, unless it is certified by the prescribed officer that the bull has been effectively castrated.
Licensing officers may refuse or revoke licences for defective or inferior conformation, incurable diseases, or undesirable breeds.
Owners must surrender licences upon expiry or revocation, or if the bull dies.
Licensing officers can order the castration of bulls not complying with licence requirements.
Offences under the Act are punishable with fine and/or imprisonment.
Government can make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, which are subject to modification by the Legislative Assembly.

penalties: Punishable with fine which may extend to twenty-five rupees and in the case of a second or any subsequent offence with fine which may extend to fifty rupees.
Punishable with fine which may extend to twenty-five rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Licensing Officer, Director, village officers, servants of Animal Husbandry, Agricultural and Revenue Departments, and officers of Panchayats and Municipalities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Inspection of bulls, ordering castration, licence issuance and revocation, prosecution of offences, and making rules.

rights: Right to obtain a licence for keeping a bull.
Right to receive notice of castration orders.
Right to have a licence considered.
duties: Duty to obtain a licence for keeping a bull.
Duty to submit bulls for inspection.
Duty to inform the owner of castration notices or orders.
Duty to produce licences upon demand.
Duty of officers to report offences and prevent their commission.
Duty to comply with rules and orders made under the Act.
obligations: Owners are obligated to have their bulls licensed and, if required, castrated.
Officers are obligated to enforce the provisions of the Act.

key_procedures: Application for and grant of licences for bulls.
Inspection of bulls by authorized officers.
Ordering and execution of castration of bulls.
Surrender of licences.
Reporting and cognizance of offences.
Rule-making procedure by the Government.
administration: The Director of Animal Husbandry (appointed by the Government) and other officers authorized under the Act.
important_notes: The Act can be applied to different parts of the State of Kerala by notification.
The Government can modify the application of provisions of the Act.
Bulls kept in good faith for religious purposes are exempt under certain conditions.
The Act repeals certain previous Live-Stock Improvement Acts applicable to specific regions of Kerala.

title: The Kerala Local Authorities (Constitution and Preparation of Electoral Rolls) Act, 1994
purpose: To provide for the constitution of Local Authorities in Kerala and the preparation of electoral rolls for such authorities.
scope: The Act applies to Local Authorities in the State of Kerala and the preparation of electoral rolls for them.

key_definitions.local authority: Includes the Corporation, Municipality, Town Planning Trust, Town Council, Town Planning Committee, Village Panchayat, etc. (as defined in various sections of the act).
key_definitions.electoral roll: Refers to the list of voters prepared for an election to a local authority.

main_sections.description: This section likely deals with preliminary matters such as short title, extent, commencement, and definitions.
This section likely covers the formation and structure of various local authorities in Kerala.
This section details the process of preparing electoral rolls for local authorities, including registration of voters, inclusion and deletion of names, and finalization of rolls.

important_rules: Voters must be citizens of India and ordinarily resident in the constituency.
Names of persons who are not qualified to be registered or who have died or permanently ceased to be ordinarily resident in the constituency shall be removed from the electoral roll.
The preparation of electoral rolls shall be subject to the superintendence, direction, and control of the State Election Commission.

penalties: Fines for obstruction or false information during the preparation of electoral rolls (specific amounts and durations are not detailed in the provided snippets).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Election Commission
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the appointment of Electoral Registration Officers and other officials, and by conducting inquiries and hearing objections.

rights: Right to be included in the electoral roll if eligible.
Right to object to the inclusion or exclusion of names.
duties: Duty of Electoral Registration Officers to prepare and revise electoral rolls.
Duty of citizens to provide correct information for the preparation of electoral rolls.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the procedures laid down for the preparation and revision of electoral rolls.

key_procedures: Procedure for the preparation of a draft electoral roll, inviting claims and objections.
Procedure for the hearing of claims and objections by the Electoral Registration Officer.
Procedure for the final publication of the electoral roll.
administration: State Election Commission, Kerala
important_notes: The Act has been amended over time, with references to subsequent amendments and ordinances.
Specific financial penalties are indicated in a table for different categories of offenses, e.g., a fine of 20,000 rupees for certain offenses.

title: The Kerala Local Authorities (Prohibition of Defection) Act, 1999
purpose: To prohibit defection from local authorities in Kerala.
scope: Applies to members of Local Authorities in Kerala.  The Act defines 'Local Authority' broadly to include Municipal Corporations, Municipal Councils, Panchayats, etc.

key_definitions.defector: A member of a local authority who voluntarily gives up his membership of such authority or votes or abstains from voting in any meeting of such authority contrary to any direction issued by the political party to which he belongs.
key_definitions.local_authority: Includes Municipal Corporation, Municipal Council, Grama Panchayat, Block Panchayat, District Panchayat, City Improvement Trust, Urban Development Authority, etc., as defined under various Kerala Acts.
key_definitions.political_party: A political party registered with the Election Commission of India, of which a member of a local authority is a member.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as The Kerala Local Authorities (Prohibition of Defection) Act, 1999, its extent to the whole of the State of Kerala, and its commencement.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'defector', 'local authority', 'political party', 'member', etc.

main_sections.section_title: Disqualification of members of local authorities on ground of defection
main_sections.description: Outlines the circumstances under which a member of a local authority shall be disqualified on the ground of defection. This includes voluntarily giving up membership of a political party, voting or abstaining from voting contrary to party directions, and expulsion from a political party.

main_sections.section_title: Decision on question as to disqualification
main_sections.description: Specifies that the decision on any question as to disqualification of a member shall be made by the presiding authority of the local authority.

States that no court shall have jurisdiction to entertain any suit, application or other proceedings in respect of any matter which the Presiding Authority is by, or under, this Act empowered to determine.
Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Repeals certain existing provisions and provides savings for actions taken under them.
Provides for the interpretation of any matter not specifically provided for in the Act.
Empowers the Government to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Provides for the validation of certain actions or proceedings.

important_rules: A member of a local authority is disqualified if they voluntarily give up their membership of the political party to which they belong.
A member is disqualified if they vote or abstain from voting in a meeting contrary to any direction issued by their political party.
A member is disqualified if they are expelled from their political party for defection.
Disqualification does not apply in cases of mergers of political parties, provided at least two-thirds of the members of the original party agree to the merger.

penalties: Disqualification from being a member of the local authority.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Presiding authority of the concerned local authority.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inquiries and decisions made by the presiding authority based on complaints or suo motu.

rights: Right to appeal to the High Court in certain cases of disqualification.
Right to be heard before a disqualification order is passed.
duties: Members have a duty to abide by the directions of their political party.
obligations: Members are obligated not to engage in defection as defined by the Act.

key_procedures: A complaint regarding defection can be made to the presiding authority.
The presiding authority shall make an inquiry into the complaint.
The member concerned shall be given an opportunity to be heard.
The presiding authority shall decide whether the member is disqualified or not.
Decisions of the presiding authority can be challenged in the High Court under certain conditions.
administration: The relevant department responsible for local self-government in Kerala, likely the Department of Local Self-Government Institutions.
important_notes: The Act aims to curb political horse-trading and ensure stability in local governance.
Mergers of political parties are permitted if two-thirds of the members agree.
The Act specifies exceptions, such as when a member votes against party directions with prior permission or abstains from voting for genuine reasons.

title: The Kerala Local Authorities (Prohibition of Defection Act), 1999
purpose: To prohibit defection among members of local authorities in the State of Kerala and to provide for disqualification of the defecting members for being members of the local authorities. It is expedient to bring out a comprehensive legislation for removing the ambiguity in the existing laws so as to relate to prohibition of defection among members of local authorities and disqualification of the defecting members for being members of the local authorities.
scope: This Act applies to members of local authorities in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.block_panchayat: A block panchayat constituted under the Kerala Panchayati Raj Act, 1994 (13 of 1994).
key_definitions.coalition: A coalition made between more than one political parties or between more than one political parties and one or more independent or between one political party and one or more than one independents or between more than one independents for the purpose of contesting any election of a local authority.
key_definitions.council: Means the Council of a Town Panchayat, a Municipal Council or a Municipal Corporation.
key_definitions.councillor: Means Councillor elected to the Council of any Municipality constituted under the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994 (20 of 1994).
key_definitions.district_panchayat: Means a district panchayat constituted under the Kerala Panchayati Raj Act, 1994 (13 of 1994).
key_definitions.independent: Means a person not belonging to any political party.
key_definitions.local_authority: Means a Panchayat at any level or a Municipality.
key_definitions.member: Means a Councillor or a member of a Panchayat at any level elected under the Kerala Panchayati Raj Act, 1994 (13 of 1994).
key_definitions.municipality: Means a Town Panchayat, a Municipal Council or a Municipal Corporation, constituted under the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994 (20 of 1994).
key_definitions.panchayat: Means a village panchayat, a block panchayat or a district panchayat.
key_definitions.political_party: Means a political party registered under section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 (Central Act 43 of 1951).
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by the rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.schedule: Means the schedule annexed to this Act.
key_definitions.state_election_commission: Means the State Election Commission appointed by the Governor under article 243K of the Constitution of India.
key_definitions.village_panchayat: Means the Village Panchayat constituted under the Kerala Panchayati Raj Act, 1994 (13 of 1994).

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Local Authorities (Prohibition of Defection) Act, 1999. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 2nd day of October, 1995.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'block panchayat', 'coalition', 'council', 'councillor', 'district panchayat', 'independent', 'local authority', 'member', 'municipality', 'panchayat', 'political party', 'prescribed', 'schedule', 'State', 'State Election Commission', and 'village panchayat'.

A member of a local authority belonging to any political party voluntarily gives up his membership of such political party, or if such member, contrary to any direction in writing issued by the political party to which he belongs or by a person or authority authorised by it in this behalf may file a petition before the State Election Commission for decision. Disqualification also applies to an independent member who joins any political party or coalition, or if a member of a coalition joins any political party or coalition. Explanation clarifies that a member who stood as a candidate in an election with the support of any one of the political parties or coalition shall be deemed to be a member included in that political party or coalition.

main_sections.section_title: Decision on question as to disqualification on ground of defection
main_sections.description: If any question arises as to whether a member of a local authority has become subject to disqualification under the provisions of this Act, the member of that local authority or the political party concerned or a person authorised by it may file a petition before the State Election Commission for decision. The State Election Commission, after making such enquiry as it deems necessary, decide whether such member has become subject to disqualification or not and its decision thereon shall be final. Where the State Election Commission decides that a member has become subject to disqualification under sub-section (2), he shall cease to be a member from the date of such decision and shall be disqualified for contesting as a candidate in an election to any local authority for six years from that date.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of the State Election Commission
