main_sections.description: Every petition under sub-section (1) of section 4 shall be disposed of by the State Election Commission in accordance with the procedure as applicable while trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Central Act 5 of 1908). The State Election Commission shall, while trying petition under sub-section (1), have the powers of a Civil Court while trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Central Act 5 of 1908), namely: (a) summoning and enforcing the attendance of any person and examining him on oath; (b) requiring the discovery and production of any document or other materials that may be produced as evidence; (c) receiving evidence on affidavit; (d) requisitioning any public record or copy thereof from any court or office; (e) issuing commission for taking from witness or document.

main_sections.section_title: Bar of jurisdiction of the Civil Courts
main_sections.description: No Civil Court shall have jurisdiction in respect of a matter in so far as it relates to disqualification of a member of a local authority under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the Government to make rules
main_sections.description: The Government may, by notification in the Gazette and in consultation with the State Election Commission, make rules, either prospectively or retrospectively, for carrying out all or any of the provisions of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of action taken by the State Election Commission in respect of defection
main_sections.description: Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law or in any judgment, decree or order of a Court, any petition relating to defection of a member of any local authority filed before the State Election Commission before the 2nd day of October, 1998 or any action or decision taken by the Commission thereon or any order disqualifying a member shall be deemed, as the case may be, to have been filed or taken or issued under the provisions of this Act.

The Kerala Panchayati Raj Act, 1994 (13 of 1994) and the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994 (20 of 1994) shall have effect, subject to the modifications specified in the First Schedule and Second Schedule respectively, from the 2nd day of October, 1998.

The Kerala Local Authorities (Prohibition of Defection) Ordinance, 1998 (14 of 1998) is hereby repealed. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: A member of a local authority belonging to any political party voluntarily gives up their membership of such political party.
A member of a local authority votes in an election contrary to any direction issued in writing by the political party to which he belongs or by a person or authority authorised by it.
An independent member joins any political party or coalition.
A member of a coalition joins any political party or coalition.

penalties: Disqualification from being a member of the local authority for six years from the date of decision.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Election Commission
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through petitions filed before the State Election Commission, which conducts inquiries and makes decisions.

rights: Right to file a petition before the State Election Commission for disqualification.
duties: Members of local authorities are expected to adhere to the directions of their political parties regarding voting.
obligations: Members elected with the support of a political party or coalition are obligated to remain with that party or coalition.

key_procedures: Filing a petition before the State Election Commission if a member of a local authority is suspected of defection.
The State Election Commission conducting an inquiry and making a final decision on disqualification.
The State Election Commission exercising powers similar to a Civil Court in trying a suit for summoning witnesses, production of documents, and receiving evidence.
administration: The Government of Kerala, through notification and consultation with the State Election Commission, makes rules for the implementation of the Act.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on October 2, 1995.
Actions taken by the State Election Commission regarding defection before October 2, 1998, are validated.
The Act includes amendments to the Kerala Panchayati Raj Act, 1994, and the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994.

title: The Kerala Local Authorities (Prohibition of Defection) Amendment Act, 2012
purpose: To further amend The Kerala Local Authorities (Prohibition of Defection) Act, 1999, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to Members of Local Authorities in Kerala.

key_definitions.direction in writing: Means a direction in writing signed with date, issued to a member belonging to, or having the support of a political party, by the person authorised by the political party from time to time to represent the symbol of the said political party for contesting in election, for exercising the vote favourably or unfavourably or to abstain from voting.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called The Kerala Local Authorities (Prohibition of Defection) Amendment Act, 2012, and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 17th day of January, 2012.

Amends Section 2 of the principal Act (The Kerala Local Authorities (Prohibition of Defection) Act, 1999) by inserting a new clause '(iv a)' relating to 'direction in writing' and amending the explanation for 'set up or given support'.

Repeals The Kerala Local Authorities (Prohibition of Defection) Amendment Ordinance, 2012 (50 of 2012) and provides that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: A 'direction in writing' issued by a political party to a member is a key element for disqualification under this act.
The direction must be signed with a date and issued by the authorized person of the political party.
The direction is for contesting in an election, for exercising the vote (favourably or unfavourably), or to abstain from voting.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The relevant authority under The Kerala Local Authorities (Prohibition of Defection) Act, 1999, likely the Presiding Officer of the Local Authority.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the process of disqualification of members of local authorities who defect or contravene the provisions of the Act.

duties: Members of local authorities have a duty to adhere to the directions issued by their political party regarding voting and contesting elections.
obligations: Members are obligated to follow the 'direction in writing' issued by their political party.

key_procedures: Issuance of a 'direction in writing' by a political party to a member.
Dispute arising regarding the direction, to be handled by the concerned political party and the member.

The direction in writing issued in this regard by the person authorised by the political party from time to time to recommend the symbol of the political party concerned for contesting in election shall be deemed to be valid.
administration: Department of Local Self Government, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act came into force retrospectively from January 17, 2012.
The Kerala Local Authorities (Prohibition of Defection) Amendment Ordinance, 2012, has been repealed.

title: The Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax (Amendment) Act, 2013
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1961.
scope: Applies to the Kerala State Legislature and concerns the entertainment tax levied and collected by local authorities.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax (Amendment) Act, 2013. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 25th day of November, 2012.

Inserts section 3C, 'Levy and collection of cess', into the principal Act. This section details the levy and collection of cess for the Kerala Cultural Activists' Welfare Fund from cinema admissions. It also outlines how the cess should be remitted to the Welfare Fund Board.
Amends section 5 of the principal Act by inserting new clauses related to tickets issued electronically and the provision of such tickets.
Amends section 6 of the principal Act by inserting new sub-section (4) concerning the renewal of licenses or permits for conducting cinema theatre and exhibition.

Amends section 11 of the principal Act by inserting a clause concerning the fixation of the rate of service charges and the manner in which it is to be collected and paid towards installation and maintenance of hardware and software applications for generating tickets in the electronic form.

Repeals The Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2013 (22 of 2013) and states that such repeal shall not affect any action taken or anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Cess levied for the Kerala Cultural Activists' Welfare Fund on cinema admissions shall be collected by the local authority.
The cess collected shall be remitted to the Kerala Cultural Activists' Welfare Fund Board.
Tickets in the electronic form must be issued with specific indications and may require specific officer authorization.
Licenses or permits for conducting cinema theatres and exhibitions need to be renewed after paying the entertainment tax.

penalties: Penalty at the rate of one and a half per cent per mensum on the amount not paid within the time limit specified.
Any amount paid by way of penalty shall be realised from the Secretary and President or Chairperson of the local authority.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Local authority
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Collection of cess, renewal of licenses/permits, and realization of penalties.

rights: Right to issue tickets in electronic form with necessary indications.
Right to collect cess for the Welfare Fund.
duties: Duty to levy and collect cess for the Kerala Cultural Activists' Welfare Fund.
Duty to remit the collected cess to the Welfare Fund Board.
Duty to obtain renewals for cinema theatre and exhibition permits.
Duty to install and maintain hardware and software for electronic ticketing.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act and the rules made thereunder.

key_procedures: Levy and collection of cess for the Kerala Cultural Activists' Welfare Fund on cinema admissions.
Remittance of collected cess to the Kerala Cultural Activists' Welfare Fund Board.
Issuance of tickets in electronic form, indicating relevant information.
Renewal of licenses or permits for conducting cinema theatres and exhibitions after payment of entertainment tax.
Fixation and collection of service charges for electronic ticketing systems.
administration: Law (Legislation-C) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act includes an amendment to levy a cess for the Kerala Cultural Activists' Welfare Fund.
The Act deals with electronic ticketing for entertainment events.
The provisions of sections 5, 6, 7, 7A and sections 8 to 10 shall apply in respect of cess on tickets for admission to cinema and the word 'tax' therein shall be construed as to include 'cess' also.
The amendment regarding the cess is deemed to have come into force on November 25, 2012.

title: The Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax (Amendment) Act, 2005
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1961, specifically for the purposes of amusement parks and the imposition of annual entertainment tax.
scope: Applies to amusement parks within the jurisdiction of local authorities in Kerala.

key_definitions.amusement park: A permanent outdoor door facility set up for entertainment which may include structures and buildings where admission is based on payment.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax (Amendment) Act, 2005, and it shall come into force on April 1, 1999.

Inserts a new section 3B into the Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1961. This section deals with the entertainment tax for amusement parks, specifying that proprietors will pay an annual tax based on the range of rates fixed by the local authority. It provides categories of amusement parks based on investment and area, with corresponding tax rates, and also details relaxation of rates during the initial years of operation. It also outlines the formation and functions of a committee to review the tax structure.
Repeals the Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2005 (7 of 2005) and saves anything done or taken under the Principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Proprietors of amusement parks shall pay an annual entertainment tax.
The tax is fixed by the local authority within specified ranges.
Tax rates for amusement parks are categorized based on investment and area.
Relaxation of entertainment tax is provided for the first four years of operation of an amusement park.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Local authorities
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the imposition of annual entertainment tax and regulations as per the Act.

duties: Proprietors of amusement parks have a duty to pay annual entertainment tax.

key_procedures: Categorization of amusement parks based on investment and area to determine tax rates.
Application of a tiered tax structure for amusement parks.
Procedure for the committee to review the tax structure every three years.
administration: Local Self Government Department (Urban and Rural), Finance (Expenditure) Department, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1961.
The commencement date of the Act is April 1, 1999.
A committee shall be constituted to review the tax structure every three years.
The Committee will consist of various government officials and the Chief Town Planner.

title: The Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax (Amendment) Act, 1975
purpose: To amend the Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1961, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: The Act applies to the Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1961, and the amendments pertain to the levy of entertainment tax by local authorities.

key_definitions.payment for admission: The price for admission and any payment for any purpose whatsoever connected with an entertainment (including any tax) which a person is required to make as a condition for attending or continuing to attend the entertainment in addition to the price for admission.
key_definitions.price for admission: The cost of a ticket (excluding any tax) for a seat or other accommodation in a place of entertainment and includes in respect of any person who, having been admitted to one part of a place of entertainment, is subsequently admitted to another part thereof for admission to which a higher payment is required.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax (Amendment) Act, 1975 and it shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
This section amends section 2 of the Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1961 (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act).

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 3
main_sections.description: This section substitutes a new section for section 3 of the principal Act. The new section provides general provision regarding the levy of tax and the rate of tax, stating that any local authority may levy a tax at a rate not less than fifteen per cent and not more than thirty per cent on each price for admission to any entertainment.

This section amends sub-section (1) of section 5 of the principal Act by substituting the words "where the payment is subject to entertainments tax", for the words "where the price for admission is subject to entertainments tax".
This section amends sub-section (3) of section 6 of the principal Act by substituting the words "payment for admission", for the words "payment of the price for admission".
This section amends sub-section (1) of section 7 of the principal Act by substituting the words "on the price for admission", for the words "on payments for admission".

important_rules: Local authorities may levy entertainment tax.
The rate of entertainment tax shall be not less than fifteen per cent and not more than thirty per cent on each price for admission to any entertainment.
The Act may be called the Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax (Amendment) Act, 1975.

rights: Local authorities have the right to levy entertainment tax within their jurisdiction.

key_procedures: Notification in the Gazette by the Government for the commencement of the Act.
Substitution of sections and wording within the principal Act as specified.
administration: The Government (presumably of Kerala) is involved in appointing the date of commencement and the local authorities are responsible for levying the tax.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 1st day of June 1975 and published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 279, dated 3rd June 1975.

title: The Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1961
purpose: To unify and amend the law relating to the imposition and collection of taxes on amusements and other entertainments in the State of Kerala.
scope: The Act applies to the entire State of Kerala and governs the imposition and collection of entertainment tax by local authorities on various forms of entertainment. It applies to persons admitted to entertainment and proprietors of entertainment.

key_definitions.admission to an entertainment: Includes admission to any place in which the entertainment is held.
key_definitions.agriculture: Includes horticulture and breeding of animals of every description.
key_definitions.entertainment: Includes any exhibition, performance, amusement, game, sport or race to which persons are admitted for payment.
key_definitions.institution: Includes a company, society club or other association of persons by whatever name called.
key_definitions.Local authority: Means (a) in any City, the Corporation of that City; (b) in any Municipal area, the Municipal Council concerned; and (c) in any area within the jurisdiction of a Panchayat, the Panchayat concerned.
key_definitions.payment for admission: Includes (a) any payment made by a person who, having been admitted to one part of a place of entertainment, is subsequently admitted to another part thereof, for admission to which a payment involving a tax or a higher rate of tax is required; (b) any payment for seats or other accommodation in a place of entertainment; and (c) any payment for any purpose, whatsoever connected with an entertainment which a person is required to make as a condition of attending or continuing to attend the entertainment in addition to the payment, if any, for admission to the entertainment.
key_definitions.proprietor: In relation to any entertainment includes any person responsible for the management thereof.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called The Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1961. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette appoint.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'admission to an entertainment', 'agriculture', 'entertainment', 'institution', 'Local authority', 'payment for admission', and 'proprietor'.

main_sections.section_title: General provisions regarding the levy of the tax and the rate of tax.
main_sections.description: States that every local authority may levy, and the entertainments tax shall be levied, at such rate not less than ten per cent and not more than twenty-five per cent on payment for admission to any entertainment.

main_sections.section_title: Composition and consolidated payment of tax.
main_sections.description: On the application of the proprietor of any entertainment in respect of which the entertainments tax is payable under section 3, the local authority may, subject to such rules as may be made by the Government in this behalf, compound the tax payable in respect of such entertainment for a consolidated payment.

main_sections.section_title: Admission of persons to entertainments subject to tax.
main_sections.description: No person shall be admitted for payment for any entertainment where the payment is subject to entertainment tax, except (a) with a ticket stamped with an impressed, embossed, engraved or adhesive stamp issued by the local authority indicating the proper tax for such ticket; or (b) in special cases, with the approval of the local authority, through a barrier which, or by means of a mechanical contrivance which, automatically registers the number of persons admitted, unless the proprietor of the entertainment has made arrangements approved by the local authority for furnishing returns of the payments for admission to the entertainment and has given security approved by the local authority for the payment of the entertainments tax. Nothing contained in sub-section (1) shall be deemed to preclude the local authority from requiring security from the proprietor of an entertainment for the payment of the entertainments tax in any other case.

The entertainments tax shall be paid by means of a ticket referred to in clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 5, and in the case of admission otherwise than by ticket, shall be calculated and paid on the number of admissions. The entertainments tax shall be recovered from the proprietor. Where the payment for admission to an entertainment is made wholly or partly by means of a lump sum paid as a subscription or contribution to any institution, or for a season ticket or for the right of admission to a series of entertainments or to any entertainment during a certain period of time, the entertainments tax shall be paid on the amount of such lump sum, but where the local authority is of the opinion that the payment of a lump sum or any payment for a ticket represents payment for other privileges or rights or proprietor besides the admission to an entertainment, it shall order tax to be levied only on that portion of the payment which is attributable to the admission to the entertainment. The local authority may also order the tax to be levied on such amount as appears to the local authority to represent the right of admission to entertainments in respect of which the entertainments tax is payable.

main_sections.section_title: Entertainment exempted from payment of tax.
main_sections.description: The entertainments tax shall not be levied on payments for admission to any entertainment (a) that is wholly of a religious educational character; or (b) that the entertainment is provided for purposes which are wholly or partly educational, cultural or scientific by an institution not conducted for profit and solely for those purposes; or (c) that the entertainment is provided by an institution not conducted for profit and solely for the purposes of promoting public health or the interests of agriculture or a manufacturing industry, and which consists solely of an exhibition of articles which are of material interest in connection with such questions relating to public health or agriculture, or of the products of the industry for promoting the interests of which the institution exists of the materials, machinery, appliances or food stuffs used in the production of those products; or (d) that the whole or the net proceeds of the entertainment is devoted to philanthropic, religious or charitable purposes. Any dispute as to whether an entertainment is of the character referred to in any of the clauses of sub-section (1) shall be referred to the District Collector, whose decision shall be final.

main_sections.section_title: Manner of recovery of tax and fines under the Act.
main_sections.description: Any amount due on account of the entertainments tax may be recovered by the local authority in the same manner as any tax payable to the local authority. Any fine imposed under this Act or rules or bye-laws made thereunder shall be recovered in the manner provided in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, and the recovery of fines shall be paid to the local authority concerned to be applied for the general purposes of such authority.

Any officer authorised by the local authority may (1) enter any place of entertainment while the entertainment is proceeding and any place ordinarily used as a place of entertainment at any reasonable time, with a view to securing whether the provisions of this Act or any rules made thereunder are being complied with. (2) If any person prevents or obstructs the entry of any officer so authorised, he shall, in addition to any other punishment to which he is liable under any law for the time being in force, be liable on conviction before a Magistrate to a fine not exceeding two hundred rupees. (3) Every officer authorised under this section shall be deemed to be a public servant within the meaning of section 21 of the Indian Penal Code.

If any person is admitted to payment for any place of entertainment and the provisions of section 5 are not complied with, the proprietor of the entertainment, to which such person is admitted shall, on conviction by a Magistrate, be liable in respect of each such offence to a fine not exceeding two hundred rupees and shall in addition be liable to pay any tax which should have been paid. Without prejudice to the provisions of sub-section (1) any officer authorised by the local authority in this behalf may enter any place of entertainment while the entertainment is proceeding, and any place ordinarily used as a place of entertainment at any reasonable time, if satisfied that the provisions of section 5 are not complied with, by order in writing prevent the further use of such place for the purposes of any entertainment: Provided that before preventing the further use of the place for the purpose of the entertainment the proprietor of the entertainment shall be given a reasonable opportunity to show cause against the proposed action. If the order under sub-section (2) is not complied with, the officer may require the officer in charge of the police station having jurisdiction over the place to prevent the further use of such place for the purpose of the entertainment and any officer in charge of the police station shall be bound to comply with the request.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the Government to make rules.
main_sections.description: The Government may make rules to carry out all or any of the purposes of this Act, not inconsistent therewith. In particular and without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing power they may make rules – (a) for the composition and consolidated payment of tax under section 4; and (b) for the presentation and disposal of applications for exemption from payment of the entertainments tax. In making any rules the Government may provide that a breach thereof shall be punishable with fine which may extend to one hundred rupees. All rules made under this Act shall be laid for not less than fourteen days before the Legislative Assembly, as soon as possible after they are made, and shall be subject to such modification, whether by way of repeal or amendment, as the Legislative Assembly may, during the session in which they are so laid or the session immediately following.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Local Authority to make bye-laws.
main_sections.description: Any local authority may make bye-laws not inconsistent with this Act or any rules made thereunder – (a) for the supply and use of labels or stamped or embossed tickets or for the stamping or embossing of tickets sent to be stamped or embossed and for securing the defacement of labels when used; (b) for the use of tickets covering the admission of more than one person or for the regulation of the time and place of holding any entertainment and on payment for seats or other accommodation; (c) for controlling the use of barriers or mechanical contrivances (including the prevention of the use of such barriers or mechanical contrivances for payments of a current amount) and for securing proper records of admission by means of barriers or mechanical contrivances; (d) for the checking of admissions, the keeping of accounts and furnishing of returns by the proprietors of entertainments to which the provisions of section 4 are applied or in respect of which the arrangements approved by the local authority for furnishing returns are made under section 5; (e) for the renewal of damaged or spoiled labels; (f) for the keeping of accounts of all labels used under this Act; (g) for the regulation of the time and place of holding an entertainment and supervision thereof; (h) for the regulation of the time and mode of collecting the tax under this Act, and (i) in general, for carrying out the purposes of this Act. In making a bye-law, the local authority may provide that a breach thereof shall be punishable with fine which may extend to fifty rupees and in case of a continuing breach with fine which may extend to fifteen rupees for every day during which the breach continues after conviction for the first breach. Such bye-laws shall have effect only when they have been approved by the Director of Local Bodies or such other officer not below the rank of a Deputy Director of Local Bodies as may be authorised by him in that behalf and published in the Gazette, provided that in the case of the bye-laws made by a Municipal Corporation, the approval shall be that of the Government.

The Travancore-Cochin Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1951 (Act VI of 1951) and the Madras Entertainments Tax Act, 1939 (Act X of 1939) in force in the Malabar District referred to in sub-section (2) of section 4 of the State Reorganisation Act, 1956 (Central Act 37 of 1956) are hereby repealed. Provided that any notification, order, rule or bye-law issued or made under the repealed Acts, shall, so far as it is not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act, continue in force, and be deemed to have been made or issued under the provisions of this Act, unless and until it is superseded by any notification, order, rule or bye-law made or issued under this Act.

important_rules: Admission to entertainment requires payment of tax unless exempted.
Tax is to be paid by means of stamped tickets or through approved mechanical registration.
Proprietors are responsible for collecting and paying the entertainment tax.
Certain educational, religious, charitable, and public health-promoting entertainments are exempt from tax.
Local authorities can compound tax for a consolidated payment under specified conditions.
Local authorities have the power to make bye-laws to regulate the collection of tax and related matters.
Government can make rules to implement the Act, including provisions for penalties for breach of rules.

penalties: Fine not exceeding two hundred rupees for obstructing authorized officers.
Fine not exceeding two hundred rupees for non-compliance with admission provisions, and liability to pay the tax due.
Fine up to fifty rupees for breach of bye-laws, and a continuing fine of fifteen rupees per day for continuing breach.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Local Authorities, Government, District Collector (for disputes on exemptions), Officers authorized by the Local Authority.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Inspection of entertainment places, requiring stamped tickets or mechanical registration for admission, ordering prevention of further use of premises for non-compliance, recovery of tax as arrears of tax payable to the local authority, imposition of fines.

rights: Right to exemption from tax for specified types of entertainments.
Right to appeal to the District Collector for disputes regarding exemption.
Right to show cause against an order preventing further use of the entertainment place.
duties: Duty to admit persons only with proper tax payment or exemption.
Duty to provide stamped tickets or use approved mechanical registration.
Duty to pay the levied entertainment tax.
Duty to comply with rules and bye-laws made under the Act.
Duty to allow inspection by authorized officers.
obligations: Obligation to furnish returns of payments for admission if required by the local authority.
Obligation to provide security if required by the local authority for tax payment.
Obligation to adhere to bye-laws regarding the use of tickets, barriers, and accounting.

key_procedures: Admission Procedure: Persons are admitted to entertainment only upon payment of the prescribed tax, typically through stamped tickets. In special cases, with local authority approval, mechanical registration can be used. Proprietors must ensure compliance.

Tax Collection and Payment: Entertainment tax is collected by the proprietor through the sale of tickets or as per consolidated payment agreements. Proprietors are responsible for remitting the collected tax to the local authority.

Exemption Application: Proprietors of entertainments seeking exemption must apply and prove that their entertainment fits the criteria outlined in Section 7. Disputes are resolved by the District Collector.

Rule Making Procedure: The Government can make rules, which are laid before the Legislative Assembly for modification. Local authorities can make bye-laws, subject to approval from designated authorities and publication.
administration: Local Authorities (Municipalities, Corporations, Panchayats), Kerala Government (for rule-making and oversight).
important_notes: The Act came into force on a date appointed by the Government through notification.
The Act repeals the Travancore-Cochin Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1951 and the Madras Entertainments Tax Act, 1939 (in force in the Malabar District).
Existing notifications, orders, rules, or bye-laws under the repealed Acts continue in force unless superseded by new provisions.
The Government has the power to grant exemption from tax.

title: The Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax (Amendment) Act, 1969
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1961, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1961.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax (Amendment) Act, 1969. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
In section 2 of the Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1961 (20 of 1961), the words "but does not include any magic performance" shall be inserted at the end.
In section 5 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), after the word and figure "section 4", the words, figure and letter "and section 6A" shall be inserted.

After section 6 of the principal Act, the following section shall be inserted, namely: "6A. Entertainments tax on dramatic and circus performances.—(1) Notwithstanding anything contained in sections 3 and 6, the entertainments tax leviable by a local authority— (a) on dramatic performances to which persons are admitted for payment shall be twenty-five rupees on each performance, and (b) on circus performances to which persons are admitted for payment shall be fifteen rupees on each performance. (2) The tax referred to in sub-section (1) shall be recoverable from the proprietor of the dramatic performance or circus performance, as the case may be. Explanation.—For the purposes of this section, the expression "dramatic performance" means any play, pantomime or other drama."

important_rules: The words "but does not include any magic performance" are inserted at the end of section 2 of the principal Act.
The words, figure and letter "and section 6A" are inserted after the word and figure "section 4" in sub-section (1) of section 5 of the principal Act.
A new section 6A is inserted concerning entertainments tax on dramatic and circus performances.
Tax on dramatic performances is twenty-five rupees per performance.
Tax on circus performances is fifteen rupees per performance.
Tax is recoverable from the proprietor of the performance.
Dramatic performance includes any play, pantomime or other drama.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Local authority
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Tax is recoverable from the proprietor of the dramatic performance or circus performance.

rights: Right to collect entertainments tax on dramatic and circus performances.
duties: Duty to collect tax as prescribed in section 6A.
obligations: Obligation for proprietors of dramatic and circus performances to pay the entertainments tax.

key_procedures: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Government through a Gazette notification.
Amendments are made to specific sections of the Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1961.
New section 6A specifies the tax rates for dramatic and circus performances.
The tax is recoverable from the proprietor.
administration: Local authorities in Kerala
important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 235 dated 25th September, 1969.

title: The Kerala Local Authorities Laws (Amendment) Act, 1959
purpose: To provide for the further extension of the term of office of the Mayor and other councillors and chairmen of standing committees of the Corporation of Trivandrum, and of the councillors of municipalities; and to provide for the recovery in certain cases of arrears of cesses, rates, taxes, fees or other sums due to Panchayats.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Local Authorities Laws, including municipal laws and Travancore-Cochin Panchayats Act, in Kerala.

key_definitions.Kerala municipal laws: Includes the Trivandrum City Municipal Act (Travancore Act 4 of 1916), the Travancore District Municipalities Act, 1116 (Travancore Act 23 of 1116), the Cochin Municipal Act XVIII of 1113 (Cochin Act XVIII of 1113), the Madras District Municipalities Act, 1920 (Madras Act 5 of 1920) as in force in Malabar, and the Municipal Laws (Amendment) Act, 1958 (Kerala Act 43 of 1958), and the Madras District Municipalities (Amendment) Act, 1958 (Kerala Act 44 of 1958).
key_definitions.Malabar: Means the Malabar district referred to in sub-section (2) of section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (37 of 1956).

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Local Authorities Laws (Amendment) Act, 1959.
Defines "Kerala municipal laws" and "Malabar".

main_sections.section_title: Extension of term of office of certain municipal functionaries.
main_sections.description: Extends the term of office of the Mayor and other councillors and chairmen of standing committees of the Corporation of Trivandrum, and of the councillors of any municipality constituted under the Madras District Municipalities Act, 1920 or the Travancore District Municipalities Act, 1116 or the Cochin Municipal Act XVIII of 1113, which expires at noon on the 1st day of September, 1959, up to such date not later than the 1st day of September, 1960, as may be specified in the notification.

main_sections.section_title: Election and term of office of new councillors in cases falling under section 3.
main_sections.description: Deals with the elections and term of office of new councillors when the term of office of the Mayor or of any chairman or councillor has been extended under section 3. It also specifies the conditions under which the Government shall cause elections and the term of office of the newly elected or appointed councillors.
Empowers the Government to remove any difficulties arising in giving effect to the provisions of this Act or of any of the Kerala municipal laws as modified by section 4, by order.

Inserts a new section 57A into the Travancore-Cochin Panchayats Act, 1950, concerning the recovery of arrears of cesses, etc., where Panchayats cease to exist or to exercise jurisdiction. This includes the recovery of arrears of land revenue under the Revenue Recovery Act for the time being in force.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal of Kerala Acts 43 and 44 of 1958.
main_sections.description: Repeals The Municipal Laws (Amendment) Act, 1958, and The Madras District Municipalities (Amendment) Act, 1958, with effect from the 1st day of September, 1959.

important_rules: The term of office for certain municipal functionaries can be extended up to a specified date in 1960.
Elections for new councillors must be held under specific conditions outlined in section 4.
Arrears of cesses, rates, taxes, fees or other sums due to Panchayats that have ceased to exist or exercise jurisdiction are recoverable under specific conditions and procedures.
The repeal of the Municipal Laws (Amendment) Act, 1958 and the Madras District Municipalities (Amendment) Act, 1958 is effective from September 1, 1959.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through specified procedures for elections, recovery of arrears, and removal of difficulties by government order.

duties: The Government shall cause elections to be held under specified conditions.
Newly elected or appointed councillors shall enter office on the date specified in the notification.
Panchayats that cease to exist or exercise jurisdiction shall have their arrears of cesses, etc., recovered by the Government.

key_procedures: Procedure for extension of term of office for municipal functionaries.
Procedure for conducting elections of new councillors.
Procedure for the recovery of arrears of cesses, rates, taxes, fees or other sums due to Panchayats.
Procedure for the Government to issue orders for removal of difficulties.
administration: The Government of Kerala (implied, as they have powers to issue notifications, orders, and cause elections).
important_notes: The Act was published in the Government of India Gazette Extraordinary dated 31st August 1959 and republished in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary dated 31st August 1959.
The Act is enacted by Parliament in the Tenth Year of the Republic of India.
The provisions regarding the extension of term of office do not affect anything in any of the Kerala municipal laws, but the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, extend the term of office.

title: The Kerala Local Authorities Laws (Amendment) Act, 1962
purpose: To amend the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960, the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960, the Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1961 and the Kerala Cattle Trespass Act, 1961.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala, amending the specified Acts concerning local authorities.

key_definitions.Deputy Director: Means the officer appointed by the Government by notification in the Gazette to perform the functions of a Deputy Director under this Act for the area specified in the notification.
key_definitions.Director: Means the officer appointed by the Government by notification in the Gazette to perform the functions of the Director under the Act.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Local Authorities Laws (Amendment) Act, 1962.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960 (Act 14 of 1961)
main_sections.description: Amends section 3, for clauses (12), (13) and (14), the following clauses shall be substituted, namely: -- '(12) 'Deputy Director' means the officer appointed by the Government by notification in the Gazette to perform the functions of a Deputy Director under this Act for the area specified in the notification ;', and '(14) 'election authority' means such authority, not being the chairman or vice-chairman or a councilor, as may be appointed by the Government by notification in the Gazette ;'. Amends section 81, in sub-section (2), for the words "Deputy Director", the word "Director" shall be substituted.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 2 of the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960 (Act 32 of 1960)
main_sections.description: In section 2 of the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960, for clauses (7) and (8), the following clauses shall be substituted, namely: -- '(7) 'Director' means the officer appointed by the Government by notification in the Gazette to perform the functions of the Director under this Act ;' and '(8) 'Deputy Director' means the officer appointed by the Government by notification in the Gazette to perform the functions of a Deputy Director under this Act for the area specified in the notification ;'.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 12 of the Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1961 (Act 20 of 1961)
main_sections.description: In section 12 of the Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1961, for the words "Director or such other officer not below the rank of Local Bodies" and "Director or such other officer not below the rank of a Deputy Director" shall be substituted. At the end of sub-section (3), the following explanation shall be inserted, namely: -- 'Explanation. --For the purposes of this sub-section the terms 'Director' and 'Deputy Director' shall -- (i) in their application to bye-laws made by a municipality, mean respectively the Director and the Deputy Director appointed by the Government to perform the functions of the Director and the Deputy Director under the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960 (Act 14 of 1961); and (ii) in their application to bye-laws made by a Panchayat, mean respectively the Director and the Deputy Director appointed by the Government to perform the functions of the Director and the Deputy Director under the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960 (Act 32 of 1960)'.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 2 of the Kerala Cattle Trespass Act, 1961 (Act 26 of 1961)
main_sections.description: In section 2 of the Kerala Cattle Trespass Act, 1961, for clause (2), the following clause shall be substituted, namely: -- '(2) 'Director' in relation to any area comprised in a municipality or a municipal corporation, shall mean the Director appointed under clause (13) of section 3 of the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960 (Act 14 of 1961), and, in relation to any area comprised in a Panchayat, shall mean the Director appointed under clause (7) of section 2 of Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960 (Act 32 of 1960) '.

(1) The Kerala Local Authorities Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1962 (Ordinance No. 3 of 1962) is hereby repealed. (2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken (including any appointment made) in the exercise of any powers conferred by or under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken in the exercise of the powers conferred by or under this Act as if this Act were in force on the day on which such thing was done or action was taken.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government (through appointed Directors and Deputy Directors)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By notification in the Gazette, appointment of authorities to perform functions under the amended acts.

key_procedures: Appointment of Director and Deputy Director: The Government may appoint officers as Director and Deputy Director to perform specific functions under the amended Acts by notification in the Gazette.
Substitution of Clauses: Specific clauses within the amended Acts are substituted by the definitions and roles of 'Director' and 'Deputy Director' as defined by this Act.
administration: The administration would likely fall under the department responsible for Local Self-Government in Kerala.
important_notes: The Act repeals the Kerala Local Authorities Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1962.
Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are deemed valid as if done under this Act.
The Act aims to standardize the definition and appointment of 'Director' and 'Deputy Director' across multiple local authority-related laws in Kerala.

title: THE KERALA LOCAL AUTHORITIES LOANS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2012
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Local Authorities Loans Act, 1963.
scope: Applies to Kerala Local Authorities.

key_definitions.accrual period: Means a financial year beginning on and from the 1st day of April and ending with the 31st day of March of the following year or part thereof ending with 31st March.
key_definitions.Board: Means the Board of Management appointed under sub-section (2) of section 3A.
key_definitions.Development Fund: Means the Kerala Local Government Development Fund constituted under sub-section (1) of section 3A and includes the aggregate of the contribution by the Government, investments, loans and all other properties.
key_definitions.Fund Manager: Means the asset management company to be constituted as specified in sub-section (4) of section 3A.
key_definitions.fund period: Means the period on and from the date of constitution of the Development Fund to the date of its revocation or transfer to the Consolidated Fund of the State under the provisions of section 3A.
key_definitions.Infrastructure Projects: Includes water supply, solid waste management, sanitation, storm water drains, roads, transportation systems, sites and services, area development and other remunerative and non-remunerative infrastructure projects for public use.
key_definitions.Investment: Means money lent or to be lent by the Development Fund only for infrastructure projects and includes money placed by the Development Fund in instruments such as Government promissory notes or other Government securities, stock or share in any banking company or other public company, or stocks, funds, shares, debenture, debenture stock, commercial papers, financial papers, short term or long term corporate deposits, securitised debt, mortgage, bonds, obligations and securities of any description whatsoever.
key_definitions.tender: Means any person who has given money to the Development Fund by way of loan.
key_definitions.management agreement: Means the management agreement between the Fund Manager and the Board.
key_definitions.net income: Means in relation to any accrual period, the net income earned by the Development Fund as shown in its audited statements of account for that accrual period, net of all costs, taxes and expenses, Fund Manager's remuneration and interest paid or payable on the borrowing by the Development Fund.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Local Authorities Loans (Amendment) Act, 2012. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 30th day of January, 2010.
Amends section 2 of the Kerala Local Authorities Loans Act, 1963 (30 of 1963).

Renumbering of clauses and insertion of new definitions, including "accrual period", "Board", "Development Fund", "Fund Manager", "fund period", "Government", "Infrastructure Projects", "Investment", "tender", "management agreement", "net income", and "State".

Inserts section 3A titled "Constitution of the Development Fund, financial management and services etc., by Government." This section outlines the objectives of the Development Fund, its establishment, and the powers and functions of the Board and Fund Manager.

important_rules: The Development Fund shall be constituted by the Government.

The Development Fund is for the purposes of establishing viable and sustainable financing arrangements, mobilising resources for infrastructure projects, borrowing or raising money, providing financial assistance for taking up and implementation of infrastructure projects, providing grants, enabling local authorities to access capital markets, guaranteeing performance of contracts, assisting local authorities in creating and maintenance of civic infrastructure, and subscribing to shares, stocks, debentures, bonds, etc., of any company or undertaking.
The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint a Board of Management to manage the Development Fund.
The Board shall have the power to do all things necessary and conducive to the attainment of the objectives of the Development Fund.
The Board shall have the power to make such reserves out of the income or capital as the Board deems proper for expenses, taxes and other liabilities of the Development Fund.
The Board shall maintain proper books of accounts, documents and other records with respect to the Development Fund.
The Board shall forward to the Government the following: unaudited financial statements of the Development Fund, annual reports including audited financial statements, and quarterly reports.
The accounts of the Development Fund shall be audited every year.
The Board shall not be liable on account of anything done in good faith, bona fide and with due diligence.

The Board shall only be chargeable for such money, stocks, funds and securities as the Board shall have actually received and shall not be liable or responsible for any banker, broker, custodian or other person in whose hands the same may be deposited or placed nor otherwise for any involuntary loss.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government and the Board.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers and functions vested in the Board and the Fund Manager, and through audits and reporting to the Government.

rights: The Board shall have the power at any time during the existence of the Development Fund to accept any property whether of an onerous nature or not from any person or persons from any other fund or otherwise with the intention of holding the same by or on behalf of the Board as an accretion to the Development Fund.
duties: The Board shall perform the following functions and duties: to provide financial assistance in relation to infrastructure projects, to enter into a management agreement, to supervise operations of the Fund Manager, to exercise due diligence in carrying out its duties for protecting the interests of the Development Fund, to hold the Development Fund on behalf of the Government, to accept additional contribution, to exercise power at any time by a resolution, to exercise the power, discretion, rights and immunities.

The Board shall not be liable for anything done or omitted to be done or suffered in reliance upon such advice or information nor be responsible for any loss occasioned by so acting nor for the consequences of any bona fide mistake, oversight or error of judgement on the part of such advisers.
The Board shall have the power to make such reserves out of the income or capital as the Board deems proper for expenses, taxes and other liabilities of the Development Fund.
The Board shall maintain proper books of accounts, documents and other records with respect to the Development Fund.
The Board shall forward to the Government the following: unaudited financial statements, annual reports including audited financial statements, and quarterly reports.
obligations: The Board shall not be liable on account of anything done in good faith, bona fide and with due diligence.

The Board shall only be chargeable for such money, stocks, funds and securities as the Board shall have actually received and shall not be liable or responsible for any banker, broker, custodian or other person in whose hands the same may be deposited or placed nor otherwise for any involuntary loss.

key_procedures: Amendment of section 2 of the Kerala Local Authorities Loans Act, 1963, involving renumbering of clauses and insertion of new definitions.
Insertion of new section 3A regarding the Constitution of the Development Fund, financial management, and services by the Government.
Appointment of a Board of Management by the Government to manage the Development Fund.
Submission of financial statements and reports by the Board to the Government.
Auditing of the Development Fund accounts every year.
administration: The Government of Kerala, through the Minister-in-charge of Urban Affairs and the Board of Management.
important_notes: The Act was deemed to have come into force on the 30th day of January, 2010.
The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 26th day of June 2012 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 1371 dated 27th June, 2012.

title: The Kerala Local Authorities Loans Act, 1963
purpose: To unify and amend the laws relating to the borrowing powers of local authorities in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to local authorities in the State of Kerala. It covers borrowing money, repayment of loans, and related procedures. It also clarifies the borrowing powers of local authorities.

key_definitions.local authority: Means any person legally entitled to control or management of any local fund or legally entitled to impose any cess, rate, duty, or tax and includes the Panchayat or the Council of the Municipality, as the case may be, and also includes officers of such local authority if he has been specifically authorised by the local authority for discharging the duties and functions under this Act.
key_definitions.funds: Means any measures which may be connected with or ancillary to any purpose specified in clauses (ii) and (iii) of section 3, and also includes the repayment of money previously borrowed in accordance with law.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act, its extent (State of Kerala), and commencement date.
This section defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'local authority', 'funds', and 'prescribed'.

This section outlines the conditions under which local authorities may borrow money, including the purpose for which the money may be borrowed, such as carrying out works, relief from famine, prevention of disease, and repayment of previous loans. It also specifies limitations on the amount and duration of such borrowings.

main_sections.section_title: Remedy by attachment if loan not repaid
main_sections.description: This section details the remedies available to lenders if a local authority fails to repay a loan, including attachment of the local authority's property and assets.

main_sections.section_title: Power of local authority to guarantee repayment of interest on, or to create a fund for repayment of capital expended on, any work to which the funds may be applied
main_sections.description: This section grants local authorities the power to guarantee the repayment of interest on loans or to create funds for repaying capital expended on specific works.

main_sections.section_title: Remedy by attachment if engagements not fulfilled
main_sections.description: This section provides a remedy by attachment if a local authority fails to fulfill its engagements.
This section deals with the issuance of short-term bills by local authorities.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to make rules
main_sections.description: This section empowers the Government to make rules regarding various aspects of the Act, including the nature of funds, applications for permission to borrow, inquiries, inspections, accounts, and the recording and enforcement of conditions on borrowing.

main_sections.section_title: Loans not to be effected except under this Act
main_sections.description: This section states that loans cannot be effected except in accordance with the provisions of this Act, with certain exceptions.

This section repeals previous legislation related to local authorities' loans, specifically mentioning the Madras Local Authorities Loans Act, 1914, and the Travancore-Cochin Local Authorities Loans Act, 1951.

important_rules: Local authorities may borrow money subject to prescribed conditions and the previous sanction of the Government for specific purposes listed in Section 3.
No portion of money borrowed shall be applied to any purpose other than that for which it was borrowed.
The time for repayment of any money borrowed shall not exceed sixty years.
The Government has the power to make rules regarding the borrowing powers of local authorities, including the nature of funds, applications, inquiries, inspections, accounts, and enforcement.

Loans shall not be effected except under this Act, with exceptions for precluding the exercise of borrowing powers by local authority or affecting the power conferred on any local authority to charge its funds by guaranteeing payment of interest.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government is involved in granting sanctions and making rules. The remedy by attachment implies enforcement by lenders or designated authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement includes the possibility of attachment of a local authority's property and assets if loans are not repaid or engagements are not fulfilled.

rights: Right of lenders to seek remedies by attachment if loans are not repaid.
Power of local authorities to borrow money for specified purposes.
Power of local authorities to guarantee repayment of interest or create funds.
Right to have rules made by the Government for the implementation of the Act.
duties: Duty of local authorities to repay borrowed money.
Duty to apply borrowed money only for the purpose for which it was borrowed.
Duty to adhere to conditions set by the Government for borrowing.
Duty to comply with rules made under the Act.
obligations: Obligation to repay loans with interest as per agreement.
Obligation to adhere to the terms and conditions specified in the borrowing arrangements.

key_procedures: Obtaining previous sanction from the Government before borrowing money.
Applying borrowed money strictly for the purpose for which it was sanctioned.
Repaying loans within the stipulated period.
Following the rules made by the Government for borrowing, including application, inquiry, and inspection processes.
Initiating attachment proceedings in case of non-repayment of loans.
administration: The Government of Kerala, specifically through departments responsible for local self-government and finance.
important_notes: The Act aims to consolidate and amend existing laws related to local authority loans in Kerala.
Specific exceptions exist to the rule that loans can only be effected under this Act.
Previous legislation such as the Madras Local Authorities Loans Act, 1914, and the Travancore-Cochin Local Authorities Loans Act, 1951, have been repealed by this Act.

title: THE KERALA LOCAL FUND AUDIT ACT, 1994
purpose: To provide for and to regulate the audit of the local funds under the management or control of certain local authorities in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to local funds under the management or control of certain local authorities in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.auditor: means the Director of Local Fund Audit and includes any other officer of the Local Fund Audit Department empowered by the Director to perform the functions of an auditor under this Act
key_definitions.concurrent audit: means continuous audit of accounts of a local authority by auditors specially appointed by the Government by virtue of the powers conferred on them by the relevant enactment
key_definitions.detailed audit: means an audit of accounts of the entire transactions for the whole year or for the period specified by the Director
key_definitions.Director: means the Director of Local Fund Audit and includes any person empowered by the Government to perform the functions of the Director of Local Fund Audit
key_definitions.Executive authority: means the principal executive officer of a local authority
key_definitions.local authority: means a Municipal Corporation constituted under the Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, 1961 (30 of 1961) or a Municipality constituted under the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960 (14 of 1961) or Township specified in section 2 of the Guruvayoor Township Act, 1961 (43 of 1961) or a Panchayat constituted or deemed to have been constituted for the local administration of a Panchayat area under the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960 (32 of 1960) or a Panchayats or a Municipality or a Metropolitan Planning Committee or a District Planning Committee constituted in the State in accordance with the provisions in Part IX and Part IXA respectively, of the Constitution of India
key_definitions.local fund: means (i) a fund administered by a local authority which, though not part of a Government Department, has been established by or under a law or orders of the Government, and (ii) any other fund which the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, declare to be a local fund for the purpose of this Act
key_definitions.prescribed: means prescribed by rules made under this Act
key_definitions.Schedule: means the Schedule appended to this Act
key_definitions.special audit: means an audit of accounts pertaining to a specified item or series of items requiring thorough examination, and includes re-audit of the accounts for a period already covered by audit as specified by the Director
key_definitions.surcharge: means an amount for which the auditor, in exercise of the powers vested in him under this Act, makes a person liable for loss, waste, misapplication or misappropriation of any money or other property belonging to any local authority.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Local Fund Audit Act, 1994, extends to the whole of the State of Kerala, and shall come into force on such date as the Government may by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'auditor', 'concurrent audit', 'detailed audit', 'Director', 'Executive authority', 'local authority', 'local fund', 'prescribed', 'Schedule', 'special audit', 'State', and 'surcharge'.

States that the Government shall, by notification in the Gazette, appoint a person having such qualifications as may be prescribed, to be the Director of Local Fund Audit in charge of the audit of accounts of a local authority or a local fund included in the Schedule. It also outlines the administrative role of the Director and the subordination of other officers to the Director.

Empowers the Director to conduct the audit of accounts of any local authority or a local fund. It specifies that the audit shall be conducted in the manner provided by or under this Act. It also states that the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, add any other authority, body, institution or local fund to the Schedule, referred to in sub-section (1), and on the publication of the notification, such authority, body, institution or local fund shall be deemed to be added to the Schedule. It also states that no authority, body, institution or local fund included in the Schedule referred to in sub-section (1) shall be omitted therefrom except by the authority of a law made by the State Legislature.

main_sections.section_title: Power of audit of accounts of certain authorities, bodies, institutions or funds
main_sections.description: Grants the Director the power to audit the accounts of certain authorities, bodies, institutions or funds, even if they are not included in the Schedule, provided the agreement between such authority, body, institution or fund and the Government allows for it.

main_sections.section_title: Audit of accounts of stock and stores and verification of cash balance
main_sections.description: Authorizes the auditor to have authority to audit and report on the accounts of stock and stores kept by a local authority specified in the Schedule. The Director, with the sanction of Government, may seek the services of any technical expert for the purpose referred to in sub-section (1), if in his opinion, it is necessary to do so.

main_sections.section_title: Manner in which audit is to be conducted
main_sections.description: Specifies that the auditor shall conduct the audit annually and at such intervals as may be decided by the Director or may conduct concurrent audit of such local authorities as are found necessary under the provisions of any law governing them or as may be decided by the Director in consultation with the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Auditor to be deemed to be public servant
main_sections.description: States that an auditor, for the purpose of powers and duties conferred and imposed on him by or under this Act, shall be deemed to be a public servant within the meaning of section 21 of the Indian Penal Code (Central Act 45 of 1860).

main_sections.section_title: Liability of local authorities to prepare and present accounts for audit
main_sections.description: Details the requirement for local authorities or local funds to prepare and present accounts for audit. It specifies that the accounts of a local authority or a local fund included in the Schedule, relating to a financial year, shall be prepared or caused to be prepared by the Executive authority, in such form and in such manner as may be prescribed, and presented for audit within four months of the close of that financial year. It also outlines penalties for failure to comply with these provisions and for making any false or incorrect statements.

States that the audit of accounts prepared and presented for audit under section 9 shall be completed by the auditor within six months of the date of its presentation for audit, failing which the officer responsible for the audit shall be liable to be proceeded against under the provisions of the Kerala Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1960.

main_sections.section_title: Power of auditor to require production of accounts and attendance of persons
main_sections.description: Grants the auditor the power to require the production of accounts, books, vouchers, and any other documents and also to require any person to attend before him and furnish information and explanations in connection with the audit.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for disobeying requisition under section 11
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for disobeying requisitions made by the auditor under section 11.

main_sections.section_title: Audit reports to be sent to certain officers and bodies as Government may direct
main_sections.description: States that audit reports shall be sent to such officers and bodies as the Government may direct.
Defines the contents of the audit report.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure to be followed after getting the report of the Director under section 13
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure to be followed after receiving the audit report.

main_sections.section_title: Auditor to surcharge illegal payments and loss caused by negligence or misconduct
main_sections.description: Empowers the auditor to surcharge illegal payments and losses caused by negligence or misconduct.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and duties of the Director
main_sections.description: Details the powers and duties of the Director.
Allows the Director to delegate his powers and functions.
Specifies the payment of charges for audit.

main_sections.section_title: Power to dispense with detailed audit
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to dispense with detailed audit in certain circumstances.

main_sections.section_title: Defalcation or loss in money or stores to be reported by the Executive authority
main_sections.description: Requires the Executive authority to report defalcation or loss in money or stores.
States that this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any other law for the time being in force.
Specifies the procedure for laying of audit reports.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith.

main_sections.section_title: Bar of jurisdiction of Civil courts
main_sections.description: Restricts the jurisdiction of Civil courts in certain matters.
Contains special provisions for pending audits.
Deals with the cognizance of offences under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Empowers the Government to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
Provides for savings related to the Act.

important_rules: Local authorities and local funds must prepare and present accounts for audit within four months of the close of the financial year.
Audit reports must be sent to officers and bodies as directed by the Government.
The Executive authority must report defalcations or losses in money or stores.
Auditors are deemed to be public servants.

penalties: Penalty for disobeying requisition under section 11 (details not provided in the Table of Contents).
Penalty for failure to prepare and present accounts for audit as per Section 9(2) can extend to three thousand rupees, but not less than one thousand rupees.
Penalties for false or incorrect statements in accounts as per Section 9(3).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Director of Local Fund Audit, Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through audit process, surcharges, and legal proceedings for non-compliance with provisions.

rights: Auditors have the right to require production of accounts and attendance of persons.
Auditors have the right to surcharge illegal payments and losses.
Protection for actions taken in good faith.
duties: Local authorities and their Executive authorities have a duty to prepare and present accounts for audit.
Executive authorities have a duty to report defalcations or losses.
Officers of the Local Fund Audit Department have a duty to conduct audits and perform their functions under the direction and control of the Director.
obligations: Obligation to comply with requisitions made by the auditor.
Obligation to provide truthful information and explanations during audit.

key_procedures: Annual audit of accounts of local authorities and local funds.
Preparation and presentation of accounts for audit by the Executive authority within four months of the close of the financial year.
Completion of audit by the auditor within six months of the date of presentation of accounts.
Reporting of audit findings to specified officers and bodies.
Process for surcharging illegal payments and losses.
Procedure for removal of difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
administration: Local Self-Government Department, Government of Kerala (inferred, as it deals with local authorities)
important_notes: The Act overrides other enactments in case of inconsistencies.
Civil courts' jurisdiction is barred in certain matters related to the Act.
The Government has the power to make rules and remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.

title: The Kerala Lok Ayukta Act, 1999
purpose: To make provisions for the appointment of Lok Ayukta and Upalokayuktas and for the investigation into complaints of corruption, injustice, or abuse of power by public servants.
scope: Applies to public servants as defined in the Act, including Ministers, Members of the Legislative Assembly, and certain other officers.

key_definitions.Public Servant: Includes Ministers, Members of the Legislative Assembly, and other persons specified in the Act.
key_definitions.Complaint: An allegation in writing by a person that a public servant has committed an offence or acted in a manner which is unjust, dishonest, or corrupt, or shows a want of integrity or is otherwise an abuse of power or a failure to act in accordance with the due process of law.
key_definitions.Lok Ayukta: The institution established under this Act to investigate complaints against public servants.
key_definitions.Upalokayukta: A subordinate body to the Lok Ayukta, also appointed to investigate complaints.

main_sections.section_title: Institutions of Lok Ayukta and Upalokayuktas
main_sections.description: Provides for the establishment and appointment of the Lok Ayukta and Upalokayuktas.

main_sections.section_title: Jurisdiction of Lok Ayukta and Upalokayuktas
main_sections.description: Defines the scope and limits of the investigative powers of the Lok Ayukta and Upalokayuktas.
Details the process for lodging a complaint and the subsequent investigation procedures.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of Lok Ayukta and Upalokayuktas
main_sections.description: Outlines the investigative powers, including summoning witnesses and examining documents.

main_sections.section_title: Reports of Lok Ayukta and Upalokayuktas
main_sections.description: Specifies the requirements for submitting investigation reports to the competent authority.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure when mal-administration is not established
main_sections.description: Covers the actions to be taken when a complaint is found to be unsubstantiated.
Deals with provisions related to defamation in the context of complaints.
Specifies the limitations on the jurisdiction of civil courts in matters covered by this Act.

important_rules: A complaint must be in writing and submitted to the Lok Ayukta or Upalokayukta.
The Lok Ayukta and Upalokayuktas shall conduct investigations in accordance with the principles of natural justice.
Public servants against whom a complaint is made shall be given an opportunity to be heard.

penalties: The Act does not specify direct monetary penalties for public servants for a finding of guilt. Instead, it focuses on recommendations for action by the competent authority.
Misconduct in relation to the performance of duties is addressed through recommendations for disciplinary action.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Lok Ayukta and Upalokayuktas are the primary enforcement authorities for investigations. The 'competent authority' (as defined in the Act, typically the government or other appointing authority) is responsible for taking action based on the Lok Ayukta's recommendations.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is primarily through investigation, reporting, and making recommendations to the competent authority for appropriate action, which may include disciplinary measures.

rights: Citizens have the right to file complaints against public servants for alleged mal-administration or corruption.
The right to a fair hearing and opportunity to respond for the accused public servant.
duties: Public servants have a duty to act with integrity, honesty, and in accordance with the law.
The Lok Ayukta and Upalokayuktas have a duty to conduct impartial and thorough investigations.
obligations: The competent authority has an obligation to consider the reports and recommendations of the Lok Ayukta and Upalokayukta and take appropriate action.

key_procedures: Lodging a complaint: A written complaint is submitted to the Lok Ayukta or Upalokayukta.
Preliminary scrutiny: The complaint is examined to determine if it requires investigation.
Investigation: If deemed necessary, the Lok Ayukta or Upalokayukta conducts an inquiry, which may involve summoning witnesses, gathering evidence, and examining documents.
Opportunity to be heard: The public servant accused is given a chance to present their case.
