Report and Recommendation: Upon completion of the investigation, a report is prepared and sent to the competent authority with recommendations for action.
Action by Competent Authority: The competent authority reviews the report and takes appropriate action.
administration: The administration of the Act involves the Kerala State Government, the Lok Ayukta, and the Upalokayuktas.
important_notes: The Act aims to provide a mechanism for redressal of grievances against public servants, complementing existing administrative and judicial remedies.
Certain categories of public servants and matters may be excluded from the jurisdiction of the Lok Ayukta and Upalokayuktas as specified in the Act.

title: The Kerala Lok Ayukta (Amendment) Act, 1999
purpose: To amend the Kerala Lok Ayukta Act, 1999.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and concerns amendments to the Kerala Lok Ayukta Act, 1999.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Kerala Lok Ayukta (Amendment) Act, 1999, and states that it is deemed to have come into force on November 15, 1998.
Amends sub-section (1) of section 22 of the principal Act by substituting the words 'six months' with 'one year and six months'.

Repeals the Kerala Lok Ayukta (Amendment) Ordinance, 1999 (3 of 1999), and provides that actions taken under the Ordinance are deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Kerala Lok Ayukta Act, 1999 (as amended).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions and procedures outlined in the principal Act and its amendments.

key_procedures: Amendment of Section 22: The time period in sub-section (1) of section 22 of the principal Act is extended from six months to one year and six months.
Repeal and Saving: The Kerala Lok Ayukta (Amendment) Ordinance, 1999, is repealed. Any action taken under the Ordinance is validated as if it were taken under the amended Act.
administration: The Kerala Lok Ayukta and associated bodies established under the Kerala Lok Ayukta Act, 1999.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on November 15, 1998.
The amendment specifically targets the time period mentioned in section 22(1) of the principal Act.

title: The Kerala Marine Fishing Regulation (Amendment) Act, 2017

key_definitions.fishing_gear: Refers to equipment used for fishing, including various types of nets and other devices.
key_definitions.fishing_vessel: Refers to any boat or vessel used for fishing purposes.
key_definitions.conservation_area: Designated areas for the conservation of marine resources.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 9A of the Act.
main_sections.description: This section appears to be an amendment to section 9A of the principal Act, likely pertaining to the regulation of fishing activities in specific areas or with certain gears.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 10 of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 12 of the Act.
main_sections.description: This section introduces amendments to section 12 of the principal Act, potentially related to the powers of authorities or procedures for enforcement.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 17 of the Act.
main_sections.description: This section modifies section 17 of the principal Act. The content suggests changes related to the designation of areas, types of fishing, and potentially the involvement of the FIRMA (Fisheries Resources Management Authority).

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 17A of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 18 of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 19 of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 20 of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 17 of the Act.
main_sections.description: This section amends section 17 of the principal Act. It specifically addresses changes to subsections (1) and (2) of section 17, which likely relate to the regulation of fishing vessels and gears.

important_rules: Prohibition of specific types of fishing gear and methods within designated areas to protect marine resources.
Regulations concerning the licensing and operation of fishing vessels.
Rules for fishing beyond a certain distance from the coast, potentially with specific restrictions.
Requirements for reporting and compliance with conservation measures.

penalties: Fines for contravening the provisions of the act.
Confiscation of fishing gear and vessels.
Imprisonment for repeat or serious offenses.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Likely the Kerala State Fisheries Department, Marine Enforcement Wing, and other authorized agencies.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, patrols, and legal proceedings.

rights: Right to engage in marine fishing activities within the prescribed regulations.
Right to obtain licenses and permits for fishing.
duties: Duty to comply with all regulations and restrictions imposed by the Act and Rules.
Duty to use only permitted fishing gears and methods.
Duty to report any violations or contraventions.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to conservation measures and protect marine biodiversity.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining fishing licenses and permits.
Procedure for reporting violations or contraventions.
Procedure for enforcement actions and adjudication of offenses.
administration: Kerala State Fisheries Department
important_notes: The Act aims to ensure sustainable marine fishing practices.
Specific amendments are made to enhance the regulatory framework for marine fishing.
The role of FIRMA (Fisheries Resources Management Authority) is significant in the implementation and management of these regulations.

title: The Kerala Marine Fishing Regulation (Amendment) Act, 1986
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Marine Fishing Regulation Act, 1980.
scope: Applies to marine fishing activities in Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Marine Fishing Regulation (Amendment) Act, 1986. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 15th day of October, 1985.

Amends section 17 of the Kerala Marine Fishing Regulation Act, 1980. It revises the penalty for using a fishing vessel in contravention of previous provisions, stating that a person found guilty by the adjudicating officer shall be liable to a penalty not less than twenty-five thousand rupees but which may extend to fifty thousand rupees, to be adjudged by the adjudicating officer. The proviso to sub-section (2) is substituted to specify that the penalty is imposed on a person for the second or subsequent time.

The Kerala Marine Fishing Regulation (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1986 (32 of 1986), is repealed. Notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Penalty for using a fishing vessel in contravention of the provisions of section 16 or section 7 is not less than twenty-five thousand rupees and may extend to fifty thousand rupees.
If a person is found guilty of using a fishing vessel in contravention for the second or subsequent time, the penalty shall be as specified in section 14.

penalties: Not less than twenty-five thousand rupees and may extend to fifty thousand rupees for using a fishing vessel in contravention of section 16 or section 7.
Penalty as specified in section 14 for second or subsequent contravention.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Adjudicating officer
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through adjudication by an adjudicating officer who determines guilt and imposes penalties.

duties: Compliance with the provisions of the Kerala Marine Fishing Regulation Act, 1980, as amended.

key_procedures: Adjudication process by an adjudicating officer to determine contravention and impose penalties.
The Act is deemed to have come into force on October 15, 1985, with saving provisions for actions taken under the repealed Ordinance.
administration: The document does not explicitly state the administering department or agency, but it falls under the purview of marine fishing regulations.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 4th day of August, 1986 and published in the Kerala Gazette, Extraordinary No. 701 dated 4th August, 1986.
The amendments are deemed to have come into force retrospectively from October 15, 1985.

title: The Kerala Marine Fishing Regulation (Second Amendment) Act, 1986
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Marine Fishing Regulation Act, 1980.
scope: Applies to marine fishing in Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Marine Fishing Regulation (Second Amendment) Act, 1986 and shall come into force on the 9th day of August, 1984.
Amends section 2 of the Kerala Marine Fishing Regulation Act, 1980.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 18.
main_sections.description: Substitutes a new section for section 18, which deals with appeals. It outlines the process for aggrieved persons to appeal to the District Collector and the conditions under which the Collector may entertain an appeal, including the possibility of an appeal after the expiry of sixty days if sufficient cause is shown. It also specifies conditions regarding the deposit of penalty amounts. The section clarifies that no appeal shall be entertained unless the appellate has deposited the amount of penalty payable under the order appealed against.
Amends section 19 of the principal Act by substituting specific words. For instance, 'Appellate Board' is replaced by 'District Collector' in certain contexts.
Amends section 20 of the principal Act. Similar to section 19, it involves substituting words like 'Appellate Board' and 'District Collector' in specific clauses and sub-sections.
Amends sub-section (2) of section 24 of the principal Act, specifically clause (k), concerning the procedure to be followed by the District Collector under section 18.

Deals with appeals pending before adjudicating officers under section 18 of the principal Act before the commencement of this Act. Such appeals are to be transferred to the District Collector having jurisdiction, who will dispose of them under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

Repeals the Kerala Marine Fishing Regulation (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1986. It also includes a saving clause stating that notwithstanding the repeal, any action taken or deemed to have been taken or any act done or deemed to have been done under the principal Act as amended by the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: District Collector
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the appellate process described in section 18.

rights: Right to appeal to the District Collector against orders of adjudicating officers.
obligations: Deposit of penalty amounts before an appeal can be entertained, with provisions for waiver under specific circumstances.

key_procedures: Appeals against orders of adjudicating officers: An aggrieved person can prefer an appeal to the District Collector within thirty days of the order. The District Collector may entertain appeals filed after thirty days but not after sixty days, provided sufficient cause is shown. Appeals will only be entertained if the appellant has deposited the amount of penalty payable.
Transfer of pending appeals: Appeals pending before adjudicating officers under section 18 of the principal Act are transferred to the District Collector.
administration: District Collector (in relation to appeals).
important_notes: The Act came into force on August 9, 1984.
The Act received the assent of the Governor on November 30, 1986.

title: THE KERALA MARINE FISHING REGULATION ACT, 1980
purpose: To provide for the regulation of fishing by fishing vessels in the sea along the coast line of the State.
scope: Applies to the regulation of fishing by fishing vessels in the sea along the coast line of the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.adjudicating officer: Any officer of the Fisheries Department, not below the rank of an Assistant Director of Fisheries, authorised by the Government, by notification in the Gazette, to exercise the powers conferred on, and discharge the duties imposed upon, the adjudicating officer by this Act for such area as may be specified in the notification.
key_definitions.authorised officer: The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, authorise in respect of the matter to which reference is made in the provision of this Act in which the expression occurs.
key_definitions.fishing vessel: A ship or boat, whether or not fitted with mechanical means of propulsion, which is engaged in sea-fishing for profit and includes a catamaran, a country craft, and a canoe, engaged in sea fishing.
key_definitions.port: Means the space within such limits as may from time to time be defined by the Government, by notification in the Gazette, for the purposes of this Act.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.registered fishing vessel: A fishing vessel registered under section 11 of the Marine Products Export Development Authority Act, 1972 (Central Act 13 of 1972).
key_definitions.specified area: Means such area in the sea along the entire coast line of the State, but not beyond territorial waters, as may be specified by the Government, by notification in the Gazette.
key_definitions.State: Means the State of Kerala and includes the territorial waters along the entire coast line of that State.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Marine Fishing Regulation Act, 1980, extends to the whole of the State of Kerala, and came into force on the 24th day of November, 1980.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'adjudicating officer', 'Appellate Board', 'authorised officer', 'fishing vessel', 'port', 'prescribed', 'registered fishing vessel', 'specified area', and 'State'.

main_sections.section_title: Authorisation of officers for the purposes of any provision of this Act
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to authorise any officer of the Government, by notification in the Gazette, to exercise the powers conferred on, and discharge the duties imposed upon, the adjudicating officer for such area as may be specified in the notification.

main_sections.section_title: Power to regulate, restrict or prohibit certain matters within specified area
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to regulate, restrict or prohibit, by order notified in the Gazette, matters such as the fishing in any specified area by class or classes of fishing vessels, the number of fishing vessels which may be used for fishing in any specified area, the catching in any specified area of such species of fish, and the use of such fishing gear in any specified area.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of use of fishing vessel in contravention of any order made under section 4.
main_sections.description: Prohibits the use of any fishing vessel in contravention of any order made under section 4. Such prohibition does not apply to fishing vessels constructed or operated in contravention of the order for the purpose of transit.

Requires a licence for the use of a fishing vessel for fishing in any specified area. The application for a licence shall be in such form, contain such particulars and be accompanied by such fees, as may be prescribed. The authorised officer may grant or refuse to grant the licence. The licence shall be in such form and subject to such conditions, including conditions as to payment of fees and furnishing of security, as may be prescribed. Licences granted under this section are valid for the period specified therein or for such extended period as the authorised officer may permit.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of fishing using fishing vessels which are not licenced
main_sections.description: Prohibits fishing using fishing vessels which are not licenced under section 6. This prohibition does not apply to fishing vessels used for fishing immediately before the commencement of this Act, for such period as may be specified by the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Cancellation, suspension and amendment of licenses.
main_sections.description: Deals with the cancellation, suspension, and amendment of licences. If a licensee has obtained a licence by misrepresentation or has contravened any provisions of the Act or any order or rule made thereunder, the authorised officer may, without prejudice to any penalty, cancel or suspend the licence or forfeit the whole or any part of the security. Subject to any rules made in this behalf, the authorised officer may also vary or amend a licence.

Requires every owner of a fishing vessel used or intended to be used for purposes of fishing and kept in the State, not being a fishing vessel registered under section 11 of the Marine Products Export Development Authority Act, 1972, to register such vessel under this Act. Applications for registration shall be made in the prescribed form and accompanied by prescribed fees. Registration once made continues in force until it is cancelled. Every registered vessel shall carry a registration mark, assigned to it by the authorised officer, displayed in the prescribed manner. No vessel, other than a registered fishing vessel, shall be entitled to a licence under section 6.

main_sections.section_title: Information to be given to authorized officer about movement of fishing vessels.
main_sections.description: Requires the owner of a registered fishing vessel moving from one port to another to give information to the authorised officer by whom the fishing vessel was registered and to the Port Officer having jurisdiction over the area where the fishing vessel has moved.

main_sections.section_title: Returns to be made by owners of registered fishing vessels
main_sections.description: Requires every owner of a registered fishing vessel to furnish to the authorised officer at the prescribed time and in the prescribed manner such returns as may be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Finality of orders under sections 6, 8, and 9.
main_sections.description: States that any order passed by the authorised officer under sections 6, 8 or 9, granting or refusing to grant a licence, or cancelling, suspending, varying or amending such licence, or refusing to register or cancelling the registration of a vessel, shall be final, subject to appeal under section 13.

main_sections.section_title: Appeals against orders refusing grant of licence, etc.
main_sections.description: Provides for appeals against orders refusing the grant of a licence, or cancelling, suspending, varying or amending such licence, or refusing to register or cancelling the registration of a vessel. Any person aggrieved by such an order may, within thirty days from the date on which the order is communicated to him, refer the appeal to such authority as may be prescribed (hereinafter in this section referred to as the appellate authority). The appellate authority may entertain the appeal after the expiry of the said period if satisfied that the appellant was prevented by sufficient cause from filing the appeal in time. On receipt of an appeal, the appellate authority shall give the appellant a reasonable opportunity of being heard and pass orders thereon as it deems fit. Every order passed by the appellate authority under this section shall be final.

main_sections.section_title: Power to enter and search fishing vessel
main_sections.description: Empowers the authorised officer to enter and search any fishing vessel if he has reasonable grounds to believe that any fishing vessel is being, or has been, used in contravention of any of the provisions of this Act or any order or rule made thereunder or any of the conditions of the licence. The authorised officer may enter and search such vessel and seize any fish found therein.

States that the authorised officer shall keep the fishing vessel impounded under section 14, in such place and in such manner as may be prescribed. In the absence of suitable facilities for the storage of the fish seized, the authorised officer may, if he is of the opinion that the disposal of such fish is necessary, dispose of such fish and deposit the proceeds thereof in the prescribed manner in the office of the adjudicating officer.

Deals with adjudication. Where any authorised officer referred to in section 14 has reason to believe that any fishing vessel is being, or has been, used in contravention of any of the provisions of this Act or any order or rule made thereunder or any of the conditions of the licence, he shall make inquiry into the matter. The adjudicating officer shall hold an inquiry into the matters mentioned in the report in the prescribed manner, after giving all the parties concerned a reasonable opportunity of being heard.

Specifies penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act, orders, rules, or licence conditions. Penalties include: (a) a fine not exceeding five thousand rupees if the value of the fish involved is one thousand rupees or less; (b) five times the value of the fish, if the value of the fish involved is more than one thousand rupees; or (c) a fine not exceeding five thousand rupees, in any other case, being a case not involving any fish, as may be adjudged by the adjudicating officer.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of Appellate Board and appeal to Appellate Board.
main_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of an Appellate Board and appeals to it. This section is likely to detail how the board is formed and the process for appeals, though details are not fully visible in the provided images.
Allows for revision of orders by the Appellate Board. This section is likely to outline the powers of the Appellate Board in revising decisions.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of adjudicating officer and Appellate Board in relation to holding enquiry and r this Act.
main_sections.description: Details the powers of the adjudicating officer and the Appellate Board concerning the holding of inquiries and other related matters under the Act.
Addresses how offences committed by companies are to be dealt with under the Act.
Allows for exemptions from certain provisions of the Act. This section likely outlines the conditions or circumstances under which exemptions may be granted.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
main_sections.description: Protects officers and other persons acting in good faith in pursuance of the provisions of this Act or any rule or order made thereunder from legal proceedings.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act.
Deals with the repeal of any existing law and savings, if any, relating to the provisions of this Act.

important_rules: No fishing vessel shall be used for fishing in any specified area except under and in accordance with a licence granted under section 6.

Every owner of a registered fishing vessel moving from one port to another shall inform the authorised officer by whom the fishing vessel was registered and the Port Officer having jurisdiction over the area where the fishing vessel has moved.
Returns as may be prescribed are to be furnished by owners of registered fishing vessels to the authorised officer at the prescribed time and in the prescribed manner.
No fishing vessel shall be used for fishing in contravention of any order made under section 4.
Every registered fishing vessel shall carry a registration mark, assigned to it by the authorised officer, displayed in the prescribed manner.

penalties: Fine not exceeding five thousand rupees if the value of the fish involved is one thousand rupees or less.
Five times the value of the fish, if the value of the fish involved is more than one thousand rupees.
Fine not exceeding five thousand rupees in any other case, being a case not involving any fish.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Authorised officers (as defined and appointed under the Act), Adjudicating Officers, and the Appellate Board.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through powers to regulate, restrict or prohibit fishing, licensing of vessels, registration of vessels, search and seizure of vessels and fish, adjudication of offences, imposition of penalties, and appeals.

rights: Right to appeal against orders refusing grant of licence, cancelling, suspending, varying or amending such licence, or refusing to register or cancelling the registration of a vessel.
duties: Duty to obtain a licence for fishing vessels.
Duty to register fishing vessels.
Duty to inform authorised officers about the movement of registered fishing vessels.
Duty to furnish returns as prescribed by owners of registered fishing vessels.
Duty to comply with orders made under section 4 regulating fishing.
obligations: Obligation to use fishing vessels only under a licence.
Obligation to comply with the conditions of a licence.
Obligation to display registration marks on registered fishing vessels.

key_procedures: Application for and grant/refusal of fishing vessel licences under section 6.
Registration of fishing vessels under section 9.
Procedure for appeals against orders of authorised officers under section 13.
Procedure for entry and search of fishing vessels by authorised officers under section 14.
Procedure for adjudication of offences and imposition of penalties by adjudicating officers under section 16 and 17.
administration: The Government of Kerala (likely through the Fisheries Department, as suggested by the definition of 'adjudicating officer').
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the President on the 17th day of January, 1981 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 54 dated the 20th January, 1981.
The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.
The Act came into force on the 24th day of November, 1980.
Exemptions from certain provisions may be granted under section 22.
Actions taken in good faith in pursuance of the Act are protected under section 23.

title: THE KERALA MATERNITY BENEFIT (REPEAL) ACT, 1970
purpose: To repeal the Kerala Maternity Benefit Act, 1957.
scope: This act applies to the state of Kerala and its legislative jurisdiction, with the specific subject matter being the repeal of the Kerala Maternity Benefit Act, 1957.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Maternity Benefit (Repeal) Act, 1970, and that it shall come into force on a date appointed by the Government through a notification in the Gazette.
This section explicitly repeals The Kerala Maternity Benefit Act, 1957 (Act 19 of 1957).

important_rules: Rule 1: The Act shall be called the Kerala Maternity Benefit (Repeal) Act, 1970.
Rule 2: The commencement date of this Act is to be determined by a government notification in the Gazette.
Rule 3: The Kerala Maternity Benefit Act, 1957 (Act 19 of 1957) is hereby repealed.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notification in the Gazette for commencement.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: The Government of Kerala shall, by notification in the Gazette, appoint the date on which this Act shall come into force.
administration: The Government of Kerala
important_notes: This Act repeals The Kerala Maternity Benefit Act, 1957 (Act 19 of 1957).

title: THE KERALA MATERNITY BENEFIT ACT, 1957
purpose: To prevent the employment of women in factories, plantations or other establishments some time before and some time after confinement and to provide for the payment of maternity benefit and medical benefit to them.
scope: Applies to factories, plantations, and other establishments where fifty or more persons are employed or were employed on any day of the preceding twelve months. The act also extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.employer: Includes the occupier and the manager of a plantation or a factory or an establishment.
key_definitions.establishment: Means an establishment to which the provisions of this Act have been extended under section 1, sub-section (2).
key_definitions.Certifying Surgeon: Means a qualified medical practitioner appointed as such for the purposes of this Act.
key_definitions.factory: Means a factory as defined in the Factories Act, 1948.
key_definitions.inspector: Means an Inspector appointed under section 14.
key_definitions.worker: In relation to a factory has the same meaning assigned to it by the Factories Act, 1948, and in relation to a plantation or establishment, means a person employed directly or through an agency, whether for hire or not, to do any work, skilled or unskilled, manual or clerical or any person so employed under a contractor engaged in the execution of the whole or any part of any work which is ordinarily part of the trade or business of the employer, but does not include a person whose total emoluments exceed three hundred rupees per mensem or any member of the managerial staff, that is to say a Manager, Assistant Manager, or other Agent of the employer.
key_definitions.plantation: Means any estate which is maintained for the purpose of growing cinchona, rubber, coffee, tea or cardamom and which is five acres or more in extent, or where fifty or more persons are employed or were employed on any day of the preceding twelve months for that purpose.
key_definitions.maternity benefit: Means the amount of money payable under the provisions of this Act to a woman employed in a plantation or a factory or an establishment.

main_sections.description: States the short title as The Kerala Maternity Benefit Act, 1957. Specifies its extent to the whole of the State of Kerala and that it shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint. It applies to all factories and plantations and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including employer, establishment, Certifying Surgeon, factory, inspector, worker, plantation, maternity benefit, and woman. It also states that unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context, the definitions shall apply.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of employment of women in certain period
main_sections.description: Prohibits the employment of women in any factory, plantation or other establishment during the six weeks immediately following the day of her confinement. Also prohibits employment during the period of pregnancy which is arduous or requires long hours of standing or which may in any way interfere with her pregnancy and is likely to cause miscarriage or adversely affect her health or interfere with the normal development of the fetus.

main_sections.section_title: Right to maternity benefit of women in factories, plantations and other establishments
main_sections.description: Entitles every woman in a factory, plantation or establishment, who has been employed therein for at least six months immediately preceding the date of her delivery, to maternity benefit at the rate of five rupees and twenty-five paise per week or calculated at the rate of 7/12 of the average daily wage. The benefit is payable for a maximum of twelve weeks, comprising six weeks immediately preceding and six weeks immediately following her confinement. Provides exceptions for women who have been employed for less than six months and for miscarriages.

main_sections.section_title: Notice of claim of maternity benefit and payment thereof
main_sections.description: Requires a woman claiming maternity benefit to give notice to her employer in writing stating that she may be absent from work for maternity benefit, her maternity benefit and medical benefit. Details the procedures for employers to make payments and for inspectors to direct payments. Also covers payment in case of death of the woman or if she is not named.

Grants a woman who has had a miscarriage a leave with wages at the rate of the average daily wage for a period of six weeks immediately following the date of miscarriage, provided she has been employed for at least six months immediately preceding the date of miscarriage. The leave is subject to production of a certificate signed by a Certifying Surgeon or other qualified medical practitioner.

main_sections.section_title: Leave for illness arising out of pregnancy or confinement
main_sections.description: Entitles a woman to leave with wages for a period not exceeding thirty days in addition to maternity leave, if she is unable to work by reason of illness arising out of pregnancy or confinement. This leave is in addition to the maternity leave and is subject to certain conditions and medical certification.

Every woman entitled to maternity benefit is also entitled to receive from her employer a medical bonus of ten rupees if no pre-natal confinement or post-natal care is provided by the employer free of charge.

main_sections.section_title: Payment of maternity benefit in case of claimant's death
main_sections.description: If a woman entitled to maternity benefit dies during the period for which she is entitled to maternity benefit, her employer shall pay the maternity benefit due to the person who undertakes the care of the child if the child is living, and if the child is not being to the nominee mentioned in the notice given under sub-section (1) of section 5, or to the heirs of the deceased woman.

Makes it unlawful for an employer to dismiss or discharge a woman on account of her absence from work due to pregnancy or confinement or on account of her absence on such a day that the notice will expire during such absence. Dismissal of a woman during pregnancy or for her absence during confinement shall not have the effect of depriving her of maternity benefit. However, if a woman is dismissed for misconduct, her maternity benefit may be forfeited.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Inspector to direct payments to be made
main_sections.description: Empowers the Inspector to direct the employer to make payments of maternity benefit if any woman entitled to it is withheld or denied. The Inspector can also inquire into complaints and make orders as deemed fit. Any person aggrieved by the order of the Inspector may appeal to the Labour Commissioner or such other officer as may be empowered by the Government.

States that if a woman works in a factory or plantation or an establishment after she has been permitted by her employer to absent herself under the provisions of section 5, she shall forfeit her claim to the payment of maternity benefit which she is entitled.

Every woman in a factory or plantation or an establishment who returns to duty after confinement shall be allowed to work, or rather be allowed two intervals of sufficient time to feed the child till the child attains the age of two years.

The Government may by notification in the Gazette appoint such officers of the Government as they think fit to be Inspectors for the purposes of this Act and assign them such local limits as they think fit.

Subject to any rules made by the Government, an Inspector may, within the local limits for which he is appointed, enter any place of use, or which he has reason to believe is used, as a factory or a plantation or an establishment. He can inspect any factory, plantation or establishment and the premises and such registers, records and notices as may be prescribed.
Declares Inspectors to be public servants within the meaning of section 21 of the Indian Penal Code.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for contravention of Act by Employer
main_sections.description: Imposes a penalty on any employer contravening any of the provisions of this Act. The penalty shall be a fine which may extend to two hundred and fifty rupees, and where the contravention is of the provision relating to the payment of maternity benefit and where the amount has not been already recovered, the court shall recover the amount due on account of maternity benefits if it were a fine and pay such amount to the person entitled thereto.
States that no Court inferior to that of a Magistrate of the First Class shall try any offence against this Act or any rules thereunder.

main_sections.section_title: Period of limitation for prosecution under Act
main_sections.description: Specifies that no prosecution for any offence against this Act or any rules thereunder shall be instituted except by or with the previous sanction of the Inspector. Further, no Court shall take cognizance of, or convict a person for, any offence against this Act or any rule thereunder unless complaint thereof has been made within six months from the date on which the offence was committed. It also provides for computing the period of six months to exclude the time taken for the purpose of obtaining the previous sanction of the Inspector.

Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of this Act. These rules can cover various aspects, including the preparation and maintenance of a muster roll, inspection of factories, plantations and other establishments, exercise of powers and performance of duties by Inspectors, and the method of payment of maternity benefit.

main_sections.section_title: A copy of Act and Rules to be exhibited in Factories, Plantations and other establishments employing women
main_sections.description: Requires that a copy of the Act and Rules be exhibited in a conspicuous place by the employer in every factory, plantation and establishment in which women are employed.

Repeals The Travancore-Cochin Maternity Benefit Act, 1952 (Act XX of 1952) and the Madras Maternity Benefit Act, 1934 (Act VI of 1934) in its application to the Malabar District referred to under sub-section (2) of section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956. They are hereby repealed.

important_rules: Every woman in a factory or plantation or an establishment who returns to duty after confinement shall be allowed to work, or rather be allowed two intervals of sufficient time to feed the child till the child attains the age of two years. (Section 13)
The Government may make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of this Act. (Section 20)
A copy of the Act and Rules shall be exhibited in a conspicuous place by the employer in every factory, plantation and establishment in which women are employed. (Section 21)

penalties: Contravention of the Act by an employer can result in a fine which may extend to two hundred and fifty rupees. (Section 17)
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Inspectors appointed under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspection of establishments, inquiry into complaints, and prosecution of offenders. The Inspector has the power to direct payments and take legal action.

rights: Right to maternity benefit for women employed in factories, plantations and other establishments.
Right to leave for miscarriage.
Right to leave for illness arising out of pregnancy or confinement.
Right to receive a medical bonus.
Right to claim maternity benefit in case of claimant's death.
Right to nursing breaks for feeding the child.
Right to be protected from dismissal during pregnancy or confinement.
duties: Duty of employer to provide maternity benefit and medical benefit.
Duty of employer to allow nursing breaks.
Duty of employer to exhibit a copy of the Act and Rules in the establishment.
obligations: Every woman claiming maternity benefit must give notice to her employer.
Employers have an obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder.

key_procedures: Claiming Maternity Benefit: A woman must give notice to her employer in writing of her claim for maternity benefit, stating the date from which she will be absent, and providing necessary documentation. (Section 5)
Payment of Maternity Benefit: The employer is liable to pay maternity benefit to the eligible woman. The Inspector can direct payment if it is withheld. (Section 5, 11)
Leave for Miscarriage: A woman who has had a miscarriage can claim leave with wages for six weeks following the miscarriage upon producing a certificate. (Section 6)
Leave for Illness related to Pregnancy/Confinement: A woman can claim additional leave up to thirty days for illness arising out of pregnancy or confinement, with medical certification. (Section 7)
administration: The Government of Kerala is responsible for the administration of the Act, including appointing Inspectors and making rules.
important_notes: The Act applies to establishments with fifty or more employees, or that have been specifically notified by the Government.
Maternity benefit is payable for a maximum of twelve weeks (six weeks before and six weeks after confinement).
Dismissal during pregnancy or confinement is generally unlawful and does not deprive a woman of maternity benefit, unless it's for misconduct.
The Act was enacted to replace previous legislation in the Travancore-Cochin and Madras regions.
Published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 9th November 1957.

title: The Kerala Medical Education (Regulation and Control of Admission to Private Medical Educational Institutions) Act, 2017
purpose: To provide for the regulation of admission and fixation of fee to private medical educational institutions in the State of Kerala and to provide for reservation of seats to students belonging to the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes in medical educational institutions.
scope: Applies to private medical educational institutions in the State of Kerala, including admission and fee fixation, and reservation of seats.

key_definitions.appropriate Authority: A Central or State authority established by the Central or the State Government for laying down norms and conditions for ensuring standards of medical education.
key_definitions.capitation fees: Any amount or thing, by whatever name called, whether in cash or in kind, paid or collected or received directly or indirectly in addition to the fees fixed under this Act.
key_definitions.centralized counselling: A common counselling and allotment of seats in colleges through a single window procedure by the Government or by any agency authorized by it for persons who have qualified in the common entrance test, for the purpose of merit based admission to medical colleges or institutions.
key_definitions.committee: The Admission and Fee Regulatory Committee constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.common entrance test: An entrance test conducted by the Central Board of Secondary Education, New Delhi or any agency authorized by the Government of India for determination of merit of the candidates.
key_definitions.fee: All fee including tuition fee and development charges.
key_definitions.management: Any person or body, by whatever name called, managing and controlling the private medical educational institutions.
key_definitions.medical course: A course of study notified as a medical or paramedical course by the appropriate authority, such as a degree, diploma or certificate, by whatever name called.
key_definitions.medical educational: Education in medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, ayurveda, homeopathy, siddha, unani, naturopathy, nursing and other medical courses.
key_definitions.minority: A community defined as minority under clause (f) of section 2 of the National Commission for Minority Educational Institutions Act, 2004 (Central Act 2 of 2005).
key_definitions.minority institution: An institution imparting medical education, established and administered by a minority.
key_definitions.non-resident Indian: Shall have the same meaning as assigned to it in clause (e) of section 114C of the Income Tax Act, 1961 (Central Act 43 of 1961).
key_definitions.other Backward Classes: Means the Other Backward Classes notified as such by the State Government as amended from time to time.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.private medical educational institution: A private aided or private unaided educational institution which is a college, a school, a department or an institution, by whatever name called, imparting medical education, other than those promoted and maintained by the Central Government or State Government, approved or recognized by an appropriate authority, which is affiliated to, or is a constituent unit of a university, established or incorporated by an Act of the State Legislature.
key_definitions.private unaided medical educational inst: A medical educational institution which is not receiving financial aid or grant-in-aid from any State or Central Government and which is not established or maintained by the Central Government, the State Government or any public body.
key_definitions.reserved seats: Seats reserved in favour of students belonging to the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes notified by the State Government.
key_definitions.sanctioned intake: The total number of seats sanctioned by an appropriate authority and notified by the State Government for admitting students in each course of study in a medical educational institution.
key_definitions.scheduled castes: Any caste, race or tribe or part of, or group within caste, race or tribe specified as Scheduled Castes with respect to the State of Kerala under Article 341 of the Constitution of India.
key_definitions.scheduled tribes: Any tribe or tribal community or part of, or group within such tribe or tribal community specified as Scheduled Tribes with respect to the State of Kerala under Article 342 of the Constitution of India.
key_definitions.university: A University established under any law made by the Legislature of the State.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Medical Education (Regulation and Control of Admission to Private Medical Educational Institutions) Act, 2017. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of June, 2017.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'appropriate authority', 'capitation fees', 'centralized counselling', 'committee', 'common entrance test', 'fee', 'government', 'management', 'medical course', 'medical educational', 'minority', 'minority institution', 'non-resident Indian', 'other backward classes', 'prescribed', 'private medical educational institution', 'private unaided medical educational institution', 'reserved seats', 'sanctioned intake', 'scheduled castes', 'scheduled tribes', 'state', and 'university'.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of the Admission and Fee Regulatory Committee
main_sections.description: Establishes the Admission and Fee Regulatory Committee by notification in the Gazette. The Committee is constituted for the purpose of supervision and guidance of admission process and for the fixation of fee that may be charged from students who get admission in medical courses in private medical educational institutions. The committee shall consist of a Chairperson and several members, including a retired judge of the Supreme Court or High Court, Secretary of Higher Education Department, Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department, Secretary, Law Department, Director, Directorate of Medical Education, Commissioner for Entrance Examinations, a representative from the Medical Council of India, an educational expert nominated by the Government, an educational expert belonging to the Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Scheduled Tribe community nominated by the Government, and one Chartered Accountant nominated by the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Term of the Committee and conditions of services of the members
main_sections.description: Specifies the term of office for members of the Committee, re-appointment eligibility, filling of casual vacancies, resignation of members, and that no act or proceedings of the Committee shall be invalid due to any defect or irregularity. The Committee shall regulate its own procedure for the conduct of its business. The salary and allowances and other conditions of service of the Chairperson and nominated members shall be as prescribed.
Details the procedure for meetings of the Committee, including when meetings shall be held, who shall preside in the absence of the Chairperson, and the quorum for meetings (four members).

Outlines the conditions under which a person is disqualified from being a member of the Committee. This includes being an undischarged insolvent, becoming incapable of continuing due to physical or mental disability, becoming unsound mind, conviction for an offence, or abuse of official position. Provided that the person shall be given a reasonable opportunity of being heard in the matter.

main_sections.section_title: Officers and other employees of the Committee
main_sections.description: States that the Government shall provide the Committee with such officers and employees as may be necessary for the efficient performance of its functions. The salaries and allowances and other conditions of service of these officers and employees shall be as prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of the Committee
main_sections.description: Details the powers and functions of the Committee, including the power to require a private medical educational institution to furnish, within a specified date, information, documents or records necessary for enabling the Committee to determine the fee that may be charged by the institution in respect of each medical course, and the fee so determined by the Committee shall be valid for such period as may be notified by the Government.

duties: Private medical educational institutions must provide information, documents or records as required by the Committee for fee determination.
Students admitted to medical courses are entitled to pay fees as determined by the Committee.

key_procedures: Establishment of the Admission and Fee Regulatory Committee through notification.
The Committee's role in supervising admission processes and fixing fees for private medical institutions.
Procedure for meetings of the Committee, including quorum and presiding officer.
Process for disqualifying members of the Committee, with an opportunity to be heard.
administration: Government of Kerala, Law (Legislation-H) Department
important_notes: The Act aims to regulate admissions and control fees in private medical educational institutions.
Reservations for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes are a key component.
The Admission and Fee Regulatory Committee plays a central role in the implementation of the Act.

title: THE KERALA MEDICAL OFFICERS' ADMISSION TO POST-GRADUATE COURSES UNDER SERVICE QUOTA ACT, 2008
purpose: To provide for quota of seats among Medical Officers of the State of Kerala and to have a selection procedure for admission to various Post-graduate Courses in the Medical Colleges under the service quota considering their service under the Government and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to Medical Officers of the State of Kerala seeking admission to Post-graduate Courses under the Service Quota.

key_definitions.difficult rural service area: The service rendered by a Medical Officer in a rural area declared as such by the Government.
key_definitions.Head of Department: The Head of Department means the Director of Medical Education or the Director of Health Services or the Director of Insurance Medical Services or the Director of Municipal Administration of the State of Kerala, as the case may be, under whose control a Medical Officer serves.
key_definitions.Medical Officer: A doctor with MBBS qualification who is in service under the control of a Head of Department and includes a lecturer or any other doctor with a different designation as the Government may specify.
key_definitions.Post-graduate Course: Any course of study after M.B.B.S. which may be a degree or diploma course declared as such in the prospectus.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.prospectus: The prospectus issued by the Director of Medical Education under the direction of the Government every year for admission to Post-graduate Course.
key_definitions.rural area service: The service rendered by a Medical Officer in an area declared by the Government as 'rural area'.
key_definitions.service: The service rendered by the Medical Officer under the Government for such period as may be prescribed.
key_definitions.service quota: The number of seats allotted for Medical Officers in the service of the State, from time to time, for admission to a Post-graduate Course of study, on such terms and conditions as may be prescribed.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Kerala Medical Officers' Admission to Post-graduate Courses Under Service Quota Act, 2008' and specifies that it shall come into force at once.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'difficult rural service area', 'Government', 'Head of Department', 'Medical Officer', 'Post-graduate Course', 'Post-graduate Course Selection Committee', 'prescribed', 'prospectus', 'rural area service', 'service', 'service quota', and 'State'.

main_sections.section_title: Selection of Medical Officers for admission to Post-graduate Course Under the Service Quota
main_sections.description: States that notwithstanding anything contained in the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956 (Central Act 102 of 1956) or any rule or regulation issued thereunder or in any judgment, decree or order of any court or authority, the selection of Medical Officers for admission to Post-graduate Course of study in the State under the service quota shall be made only under the provisions of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of Post-graduate Course Medical Selection Committee
main_sections.description: Details the composition of the Post-graduate Course Selection Committee, which shall consist of the Secretary to Government, Health and Family Welfare Department, Government of Kerala, the Director of Medical Education, the Director of Health Services, the Director of Insurance Medical Services, and the Joint Director of Medical Education (M) and the Joint Director of Medical Education (G). The Secretary to Government, Health and Family Welfare Department shall be the Chairman and the Director of Medical Education shall be the Convener of the Committee. The Committee shall discharge its functions in such manner as may be prescribed.

Outlines the procedure for selection, including that the Government may set apart seats not exceeding forty per cent of the total seats available to State quota in an academic year for the selection of Medical Officers under service quota. The academic qualification for admission to the Postgraduate Course shall be MBBS degree with minimum fifty per cent marks and other qualifications as prescribed. Details of eligibility, duration of courses, allotment, fee to be paid, reservations of seats and other details shall be published every year in the prospectus before the commencement of admission. The selection list finalized by the Committee shall be published by the Post-graduate Course Selection Committee for the information of the applicants.

States that every Medical Officer who has 'rural area service' or 'difficult rural area service', as the case may be, in the State shall be given weightage in selection in such manner as may be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides that no suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against the Government or any of its officers or employees for any act or omission which is done or omitted to be done in good faith or intended or omitted to be done under this Act.

Empowers the Government, if any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, to make any order, not inconsistent with the Act or rules, to remove the difficulty. Such orders shall not be made after the expiration of a period of two years from the commencement of this Act. Every order made under this section shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out all or any of the purposes of this Act, by notification in the Official Gazette. Every rule made shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly as soon as may be after it is made.

important_rules: Seats not exceeding forty per cent of the total seats available to State quota in an academic year can be set apart for the selection of Medical Officers under service quota.
Academic qualification for admission to Postgraduate Course is MBBS degree with minimum fifty per cent marks and other prescribed qualifications.
Details of eligibility, duration of courses, allotment, fee to be paid, and reservations of seats shall be published in the prospectus before the commencement of admission.
Weightage shall be given in selection to Medical Officers with 'rural area service' or 'difficult rural area service'.
Rules made under the Act must be laid before the Legislative Assembly.
key_procedures: Selection of Medical Officers for admission to Post-graduate Course under the service quota shall be made strictly according to the provisions of this Act.
The Post-graduate Course Selection Committee will finalize the selection list based on seniority and other prescribed criteria.
The finalized selection list will be published by the Committee for the information of applicants.
The Government may issue orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act, provided such orders are not inconsistent with the Act and are issued within two years of commencement.
The Government may make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
administration: The Government of Kerala, specifically the Health and Family Welfare Department, and the Department of Medical Education appear to be the primary administrative bodies.
important_notes: The Act overrides any provisions in the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956, or any other rules, regulations, judgments, decrees, or orders regarding the selection of Medical Officers for Post-graduate courses under the service quota.
No legal proceedings shall be initiated against the Government or its officers for actions taken in good faith under this Act.
Rules made by the Government under this Act are subject to modification or annulment by the Legislative Assembly.
Any order made by the Government to remove difficulties is valid only for two years from the commencement of the Act.

title: THE KERALA MONEY-LENDERS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1987
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Money-Lenders Act, 1958.
scope: Applies to persons engaged in money-lending in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.money-lender: A person whose main or subsidiary occupation is the business of advancing and realising loans or acceptance of deposits in the course of such business, and includes any person appointed by him to be in charge of a branch office or branch offices or a liaison office or any other office by whatever name called, of his principal place of business and a pawn-broker, but does not include—(a) a broker; and (b) a manufacturer;" (9A) "trader" means a person who in the regular course of business buys and sells goods or other property, whether movable or immovable, and includes— (a) a wholesale or retail merchant; (b) a commission agent;
key_definitions.trader: A person who in the regular course of business buys and sells goods or other property, whether movable or immovable, and includes— (a) a wholesale or retail merchant; (b) a commission agent; (c) a broker; and (d) a manufacturer.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Money-Lenders (Amendment) Act, 1987. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 12th day of May, 1987.
Amends section 2 of the principal Act (35 of 1958) (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act).

Amends sub-section (1) of section 3 of the principal Act, for the words "shall, except for one month or such longer period as the Government may specify", the words "for non-incorporated association of individuals shall commence or" shall be substituted.
Amends sub-section (2A) of section 4 of the principal Act, for the Explanation and the TABLE thereunder, the following Explanation and TABLE, shall be substituted, namely: -

Amends section 7 of the principal Act, after sub-section (2), the following sub-section shall be added, namely: - "(4) No money-lender shall give any presents, gifts, commission or any amount other than the interest provided in sub-section (2) of section 4 to any depositor in connection with the deposits received by such money-lender or receive any presents, gifts, commission or any amount other than the interest and other charges specified in this section from any person to whom money is advanced."

Amends section 9D of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), for clause (e), the following clause shall be substituted, namely:-""(e) submit to the Inspector concerned such returns relating to the deposits accepted and the loans advanced by him, in such form and at such times, as may be prescribed".

Amends section 9G of the principal Act, the existing provision shall be numbered as sub-section (1), and after sub-section (1) as so numbered, the following sub-section shall be added, namely:- "(2) Every pawn broker shall, on taking a pledge in pawn, insure the pledge with him any company or corporation which is authorised by law for such insurance, for an amount not less than the market value of such pledge."
In section 10 of the principal Act, sub-sections (3) and (4) shall be omitted.

After section 10 of the principal Act, the following sections shall be inserted, namely:- "10A. Power to order production of accounts and powers of entry and inspection.- (1) Any Inspector, Licensing Authority or Appellate Authority may, for the purpose of this Act, by notice, require any money-lender,- (a) to produce or cause to be produced before him any accounts, registers, records or other documents; or (b) to furnish or cause to be furnished any other information relating to his business and such money-lender shall comply with such requisition. (2) Any Inspector or Licensing Authority may, at any reasonable time, with or without the assistance of Police officers or other officers.— (a) enter any place of business or office of the money-lender; and (b) inspect any cash, accounts, registers, records, safes, vaults, pledges or other documents in such premises. (3) If any officer referred to in this section has reason to believe that the money-lender has violated any of the provisions of this Act or the rules made thereunder, he may, for reasons to be recorded in writing, enter and search the place of business of the money-lender or any other place which includes any godown, buildings, vessel, vehicle, box or receptacle where the money-lender keeps or is reasonably believed to be keeping any accounts, registers, other records, documents or pledges relating to his business: Provided that no residential building or premises shall be entered or searched unless such officer is specifically authorised in writing by the Member, Board of Revenue in charge of taxes to search that residential building or premises. (4) All searches under this section shall, so far as may be, made in accordance with the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Central Act 2 of 1974). (5) The officer making the inspection or search may seize necessary accounts, registers, records or other documents as he may seize and on such seizure shall, grant the money-lender a receipt of the things seized. (6) The registers, records or other documents seized under sub-section (5) shall not be retained by the officer seizing them beyond a period of thirty days from the date of the seizure, except with the permission of the next higher authority, unless they are required for any prosecution under this Act. (7) The powers conferred by sub-sections (3) and (5) shall include, — (a) the power to break-open any box or receptacle, safes, vaults or the door of any premises in which any accounts, registers, records or pledges of the money-lender are kept or reasonably suspected to be kept; (b) the power to break open the door shall be exercised only after the owner or any other person in occupation of the premises fails or refuses to open the same on being called upon to do so; (c) the power to search any person who has got out of or is about to get into or is in any place referred to in clause (a) or clause (b) of sub-section (2) of this section if the officer has reason to suspect that such person has secreted about his person any accounts, registers, records or other documents. 10B. Power to summon witnesses and cause production of documents.—(1) An Inspector, Licensing Authority or Appellate Authority shall for the purposes of this Act, have the same powers conferred on a Civil Court by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Central Act 5 of 1908), in respect of the following matters, namely:- (a) summoning and enforcing the attendance of any person and examining him on oath or affirmation; (b) compelling the production of any documents; (c) impounding of any documents, accounts or other records produced for reasons to be recorded in writing; and (d) any other matter which may be prescribed. (2) The officer who impounds the documents, accounts or registers of the money-lender shall grant a receipt of the things so impounded to the person who produced the same. 10C. Assistance of Police Officers.—Any officer authorised to inspect or search under section 10A may seek the assistance of the officer in charge of the Police Station having jurisdiction over the area to be inspected or searched and thereupon, such officer of the Police Station shall render all assistance necessary to the officer for the conduct of such inspection or search."
In section 11 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), for the opening words "who takes", the words "who pays interest", shall be substituted.

After section 11, the following section shall be inserted, namely:- "11A. Power to demand additional security.—(1) Notwithstanding anything contained in section 4, the Licensing Authority may demand from the money-lender additional security at any time, if in the opinion of such authority there is excess of liabilities over the assets of the money-lender: Provided that, while determining the excess of liabilities over assets, the security furnished by the money-lender under sub-section (2A) of section 4 of this Act shall be treated as assets of the money-lender: Provided further that in respect of the loans advanced by the money-lender against any security, in form, the Licensing Authority shall have power to revalue or determine the adequacy of the security or securities or revalue any assets for the purpose of determination of excess of liabilities over the assets. (2) The additional security to be furnished by the money-lender under sub-section (1) shall be equal to the amount of such excess of liabilities over the assets. (3) The additional security referred to in this section shall be furnished in any of the following forms:- (a) by deposit in the Government Treasury; or (b) by deposit with such authority, of Government Securities including National Savings Certificates; or (c) by deposit in Post Office Savings Bank or a Co-operative Bank and pledging of the pass book thereof, with such authority; or (d) by guarantee from a bank approved in this behalf by such authority agreeing to pay to the State Government on demand, the amount, of such additional security; or (e) by surety bonds from sureties acceptable to such authority, for the amount of such additional security. (4) The additional security furnished by the money-lender shall be retained till, in the opinion of the Licensing Authority, there exists excess of liabilities over the assets of the money-lender. (5) The additional security retained under sub-section (4) shall be utilised for the payment of the liabilities of the money-lender in connection with his business as money-lender, at the time of the winding up of the business or cancellation of the licence, as the case may be. (6) Any money-lender from whom additional security is demanded under this section and who carries on business without furnishing such security may extend his business for six months or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees or with both."

In section 14 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), after clause (c), the following clause shall be inserted, namely:- "(cc) if the licensee carries on business without furnishing the security or additional security as provided in this Act; or".
In section 16 of the principal Act, the words or for any compensation for such cancellation" shall be added at the end.

In section 16B of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), the following sub-section shall be substituted, namely:— "(1) Any person aggrieved by an order of the Licensing Authority under sub-section (3) of section 4 or sub-section (1) of section 14 or section 16A or by an order of the Inspector or the Licensing Authority under section 11A or section 18C or section 18D or section 18E, 18F, 18G and 18H—After section 18B of the principal Act, the following sections shall be inserted, namely:- "18C. Imposition of penalty by Officers and Authorities.—(1) If the Inspector or the Licensing Authority is satisfied that any person, — (a) being a person liable to take himself a licence under this Act, carries on the business of money-lending without taking such licence; or (b) has failed to keep true and complete accounts of the business; or (c) has failed to submit any return or statement as required by the provisions of this Act or the rules made thereunder; or (d) has submitted an untrue or incorrect return or statement; or (e) has acted in contravention of any of the provisions of this Act or the rules made thereunder, for the contravention of which, no express provision for payment of penalty or for punishment is made by this Act; Such Inspector or Authority may direct that such person shall pay, by way of penalty an amount not exceeding five thousand rupees. Explanation.—The burden of proving that any person is not liable to the penalty shall be on such person. (2) No order under sub-section (1) shall be passed unless the person on whom the penalty proposed to be imposed is given an opportunity of being heard in the matter. 18D. Penalty for collection of interest in excess of the rate prescribed under section 7.—(1) If the Inspector or the Licensing Authority is satisfied that any money-lender has received interest in excess of the rate of interest specified in section 7 or has carried on excess of the rate of interest fixed by the rules made under this Act, he may, direct that such money-lender shall pay by way of penalty an amount not exceeding thrice the amount of interest or other charges so received. Provided that in the case of interest or other charge collected at excess rate, no penalty shall be imposed if the Inspector or the Licensing Authority is satisfied that the sum so collected has been refunded to the person from whom it was collected. (2) No prosecution for an offence under this Act shall be instituted in respect of the same facts on which a penalty has been imposed under this section."

important_rules: Money-lenders must obtain a license.
Money-lenders must maintain true and complete accounts.
Money-lenders must submit returns as required by the Act.
Money-lenders cannot charge interest exceeding the prescribed rate.
Money-lenders must insure pledges with authorized companies for their market value.
Additional security may be demanded by the Licensing Authority if liabilities exceed assets.

penalties: Penalty not exceeding five thousand rupees for contravening provisions of the Act where no specific penalty is prescribed.
Penalty not exceeding thrice the amount of excess interest collected.
Fine which may extend to two thousand rupees for carrying on business without furnishing additional security.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Inspector, Licensing Authority, or Appellate Authority.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through imposition of penalties, demand for additional security, cancellation of licenses, and prosecution.

rights: Right to conduct searches under specific conditions.
Right to summon witnesses and compel production of documents.
Right to be heard before any penalty is imposed.
duties: Duty to take a license to carry on money-lending business.
Duty to keep true and complete accounts.
Duty to submit returns and statements as required.
Duty to comply with requisitions from the Inspector or Licensing Authority.
Duty to insure pledges.
Duty to furnish additional security when demanded.
obligations: Obligation to not charge interest exceeding the prescribed rate.
Obligation to not accept gifts or commissions from depositors.
Obligation to not fail to keep true and complete accounts.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining a money-lender's license (implied).
Procedure for inspection and search of money-lender's premises and documents by authorized officers.
Procedure for summoning witnesses and compelling production of documents.
Procedure for imposing penalties by the Inspector or Licensing Authority, including a hearing for the person concerned.
Procedure for demanding and furnishing additional security.
administration: GOVERNMENT OF KERALA, Law (Legislation-A) Department
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Kerala Money-Lenders Act, 1958.
The Act came into force retrospectively from May 12, 1987.
Searches of residential buildings require specific written authorization.
The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, applies to searches.
Seized documents cannot be retained beyond thirty days without higher authority permission.
Penalties are distinct from prosecution for offenses.

title: THE KERALA MONEY LENDERS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1986
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala Money Lenders Act, 1958.
scope: Applies to money lenders and their business in Kerala.

key_definitions.bank: Includes a banking company, the State Bank of India, a subsidiary bank, the Industrial Development Bank of India, a corresponding new bank, a Regional Rural Bank, and the Export Import Bank of India, the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development, and the Industrial Reconstruction Bank of India, and the Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India Limited.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Money Lenders (Amendment) Act, 1986 and it came into force on the 15th day of October, 1985.
Amends section 2 of the Kerala Money Lenders Act, 1958, by substituting a new definition for 'bank'.
Amends section 4 of the principal Act by inserting a new sub-clause (ii) regarding deposits.

Substitutes sub-section (1) of section 7 of the principal Act. It states that no money lender shall charge interest on any loan at a rate exceeding two per cent above the maximum rate of interest charged by commercial banks on loans granted by them.

Inserts a new section 9H which deals with the audit of accounts of money-lenders. It mandates that every money-lender shall get their accounts audited at least once every year by a person who is a chartered accountant. The audit report must be submitted to the officer or authority as specified by the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 12.
main_sections.description: Substitutes section 12 of the principal Act, which deals with cognizance of offences. It states that no court inferior to that of a Judicial Magistrate of the First Class shall try any offence punishable under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 17.
main_sections.description: Substitutes section 17 of the principal Act, titled 'Penalty for carrying on business without licence or in violation of the conditions of licence'. It specifies penalties for such violations.
Inserts a clause (6A) into section 18A of the principal Act, stating that the pawner may have the power of attorney or any other document related to his transactions.
Repeals the Kerala Money Lenders (Amendment) Ordinance, 1986, and provides for saving of anything done or deemed to have been done or taken under the Ordinance.

important_rules: Deposits shall only be accepted in accordance with the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and at rates of interest not exceeding the rates fixed by the Reserve Bank of India under the Non-banking Financial Companies (Reserve Bank) Directions, 1977.
No money lender shall charge interest on any loan at a rate exceeding two per cent above the maximum rate of interest charged by commercial banks on loans granted by them.
Every money-lender shall get their accounts audited at least once every year by a chartered accountant.
Money lenders must not carry on business without a licence or in violation of licence conditions.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and with fine which may extend to fifty thousand rupees for carrying on business without a licence or in violation of licence conditions.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Officer or authority specified by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through audit reports, court proceedings, and penalties as prescribed in the Act.

rights: Pawners have the right to possess power of attorney or other documents related to their transactions.
duties: Money lenders have the duty to get their accounts audited annually by a chartered accountant.
Money lenders have the duty to not charge interest above the prescribed limit.
Money lenders have the duty to obtain and comply with the conditions of a licence.
obligations: Money lenders have the obligation to comply with the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act and directions when accepting deposits.

key_procedures: Audit of accounts: Money lenders must have their accounts audited annually by a chartered accountant and submit the report to the specified authority.
Offences: Any offence punishable under this Act shall be tried by a Judicial Magistrate of the First Class.
Penalty for violation: Carrying on business without a licence or violating licence conditions can lead to imprisonment and fine.
administration: Government of Kerala (implied, as it is a State Act)
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 30th day of November, 1986, and was published in the Kerala Gazette, Extraordinary No. 1079 dated 30th November, 1986.
The Act repealed the Kerala Money Lenders (Amendment) Ordinance, 1986, but anything done or deemed to have been done under the Ordinance is saved.
The amendments pertain to definitions, audit requirements, interest rates, and penalties.

title: THE KERALA MONEY LENDERS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1963
purpose: To amend the Kerala Money Lenders Act, 1958.
scope: Applies to money lenders and pawnbrokers in Kerala.
