key_definitions.appellate authority: Any officer or authority appointed by the Government to exercise the powers of an appellate authority under this Act.
key_definitions.licensing authority: An officer or authority appointed by the Government to perform the functions of a licensing authority under this Act.
key_definitions.money lender: A person whose main or subsidiary occupation is the business of advancing and realising loans and includes a pawnbroker, but shall exclude a bank or a co-operative society or the Life Insurance Corporation of India established under section 3 of the Life Insurance Corporation Act, 1956 (Central Act 31 of 1956).
key_definitions.pawner: A person delivering an article for pawn to a pawnbroker.
key_definitions.pledge: An article received in pawn with a pawn-ticket.
key_definitions.pawnbroker: A person who keeps a shop for the purchase or sale of goods or chattels and who purchases goods or chattels and pays or advances thereon any sum of money, with or without any other business.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Money Lenders (Amendment) Act, 1963 and shall come into force at once.

Amends section 2 of the Kerala Money Lenders Act, 1958, by substituting new definitions for 'appellate authority' and 'licensing authority', and inserting definitions for 'money lender' and 'pawnbroker'.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 6.
main_sections.description: Substitutes the existing section 6 with a new section regarding money lenders' duty to exhibit their names over shops and use of specific terms like 'money lender' and 'pawnbroker'.
Amends section 9 of the principal Act, specifically subsection (1) regarding the rate of interest that money lenders can charge.
Inserts a new section 16A dealing with appeals to the appellate authority.
Inserts new sections 18A and 18B concerning certain acts of pawnbrokers and their books and accounts.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of owners and of pawners not having pawn-tickets.
main_sections.description: Outlines provisions related to the protection of owners and pawners who may have lost their pawn-tickets.

main_sections.section_title: Pawnbrokers to keep books, give receipts, etc.
main_sections.description: Mandates pawnbrokers to maintain records, issue receipts, and keep specific documents related to their transactions.
Specifies the period within which a pledge must be redeemed and the consequences of not redeeming it.

main_sections.section_title: Sale of pledge and inspection of sale book.
main_sections.description: Details the procedures for selling a pledge and the inspection of the sale book by the pawnbroker.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of pawnbroker in case of theft or fire.
main_sections.description: Defines the liability of a pawnbroker in situations of theft or fire affecting the pledged goods.
Provides for compensation for the depreciation of a pledge if the pawnbroker has acted wrongfully.

important_rules: Money lenders shall charge interest on any loan at a rate not exceeding twelve per cent per annum simple interest.
Every money lender shall exhibit his shop or place of business with the word "money lender" or "pawnbroker" and its equivalent in the regional language.
Pawnbrokers shall keep a regularly recorded and maintain a pledge book in the prescribed form.
Pawnbrokers shall issue a receipt for every sum paid by them.
A pawnbroker shall not sell any pledge unless three years from the date of the pledge have expired.
A pledge is redeemable within one year from the day of pawning, exclusive of the day of pawn; and there shall, for the purposes of this Act, be no redemption after the expiry of that year.

penalties: Punishment for making false declarations (imprisonment up to six months or fine up to one hundred rupees, or both).
Fine not exceeding two hundred and fifty rupees if any pawnbroker fails to give a receipt for a sum of money.
Fine not exceeding fifty rupees for contravening certain provisions related to the redemption of pledges.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Licensing authority, appellate authority, Magistrate or Judge.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through prosecution for offenses, appeals to appellate authority, and adherence to prescribed procedures for record-keeping and transactions.

rights: Right to redeem a pledge within the stipulated period.
Right to receive a proper receipt for payments made.
Right to appeal to the appellate authority against certain decisions.
duties: Duty of money lenders to not charge interest exceeding twelve per cent per annum simple interest.
Duty of money lenders to exhibit their names over their shops.
Duty of pawnbrokers to maintain pledge books and issue receipts.
Duty of pawnbrokers to protect pledged articles.
obligations: Obligation to redeem pledges within the prescribed time.
Obligation to comply with the record-keeping and reporting requirements for pawnbrokers.

key_procedures: Procedure for licensing of money lenders (implied by the existence of licensing authority).
Procedure for appeal against orders of the licensing authority.
Procedure for redemption of pledges.
Procedure for sale of pledges by pawnbrokers.
Procedure for keeping and maintaining pledge books and accounts by pawnbrokers.
administration: Implied to be administered by the relevant State Government departments overseeing financial institutions and trade.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 29th day of October, 1963 and was published in the Gazette Extraordinary, dated 4th November, 1963.
Explanations are provided for certain clauses and sections to clarify their meaning and application.

title: THE KERALA MONEY-LENDERS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1974
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Money-Lenders Act, 1958.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.money lender: means a person whose main or subsidiary occupation is the business of advancing and realising loans, and includes a pawn broker, but does not include- (a) a bank or a co-operative society, or (b) the Life Insurance Corporation of India established under section 3 of the Life Insurance Corporation Act, 1956 (Central Act 31 of 1956); or (c) the Industrial Finance Corporation established under section 3 of the Industrial Finance Corporation Act, 1948 (Central Act 15 of 1948); or (d) the Agricultural Refinance Corporation established under section 3 of the Agricultural Refinance Corporation Act, 1963 (Central Act 10 of 1963); or (e) the State Financial Corporation established under section 3 of the State Financial Corporation Act, 1951 (Central Act 63 of 1951); or (f) any institution established by or under an Act of Parliament of the Legislature of a State, which grants any loan or advance in pursuance of the provisions of that Act, or (g) any institution in the public sector, whether incorporated or not exempted by the Government by notification.
key_definitions.person: In the context of Explanation II, it includes "a firm or a joint family".

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Money-Lenders (Amendment) Act, 1974. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Amends section 2 of the principal Act (Kerala Money-Lenders Act, 1958) by substituting clause (7) to define "money lender" and provides further explanations for the purpose of this clause.
Inserts a new sub-section (4A) into section 4 of the principal Act regarding the licensing authority's discretion to refuse a license for reasons beyond a specified period.
Re-numbers sub-section (1) of section 12 of the principal Act and makes consequential changes.

Adds a proviso to section 22 of the principal Act stating that any licence issued before March 1, 1964, under the Madras Pawn Brokers Act, 1943, shall be deemed to be a licence validly issued under the provisions of this Act.

important_rules: Rule: The licensing authority may, if it is satisfied that an applicant could not apply for a licence under this Act for reasons beyond his control within the period referred to in sub-section (1) of section 4, grant a licence with retrospective effect on realising a penalty not exceeding the prescribed licence fee.
Rule: No court inferior to that of a Magistrate of the First Class shall try any offence punishable under this Act.

Rule: Licences issued before the 1st day of March, 1964, under the Madras Pawn Brokers Act, 1943 (Madras Act, XXIII of 1943), shall be deemed to be a licence validly issued under the provisions of this Act.

penalties: Offences punishable under this Act are triable by a Magistrate of the First Class.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government (through notification)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By notification and through the licensing authority.

rights: Right to obtain a licence (subject to conditions and potential retrospective grant).
duties: Duty to obtain a licence under the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure: Obtaining a licence under the Act.
Procedure: Applying for a licence retrospectively under specific circumstances, possibly involving a penalty.
Procedure: Prosecution of offences by a Magistrate of the First Class.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 23rd day of March 1974 and published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 318 dated 25th March 1974.
Section 2 of the principal Act is amended to substitute the definition of 'money lender'.

title: THE KERALA MONSOON FISHERY (PELAGIC) PROTECTION ACT, 2007
purpose: To provide for security of life and livelihood of the traditional fishermen and to ensure their subsistence by occupying pelagic fishery through tapping the unique pelagic fishery resources in the State like 'chakara' in monsoon season and to regulate them and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole State of Kerala and applies to pelagic fishery resources within the State during the monsoon season.

key_definitions.authorised officer: Means such officer as the Government may by notification in the Gazette authorise in respect of the matter in which reference is made in the provision of this Act in which the expression occurs.
key_definitions.fishing vessel: Means a vessel whether or not fitted with mechanical means of propulsion engaged in sea fishing and includes catamará, a country craft and a canoe.
key_definitions.traditional fisherman: Means any person engaged in fishing with or without traditional or modified traditional crafts and gears for his livelihood.
key_definitions.modified traditional crafts and gears: Means traditional crafts and gears, modified in their shape or form or size including means of propulsion by the usage of motors or engines for the exclusive purpose of propelling the crafts and vessels used by the Traditional Fisherman.
key_definitions.pelagic fishery: Means fishery or fishing activities relating to fishing of any species of fish resources distributed in the surface or sub-surface or column water areas of the specified area.
key_definitions.specified area: Means such area in the sea along the entire coast line of the state, but not beyond territorial waters, as may be specified by the Government by notification in the Gazette.
key_definitions.state: Means State of Kerala and includes the territorial waters along the entire coast line of the State.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Monsoon Fishery (pelagic) Protection Act, 2007, extends to the whole State of Kerala, and shall come into force at once.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'authorised officer', 'fishing vessel', 'traditional fisherman', 'modified traditional crafts and gears', 'pelagic fishery', 'specified area', and 'State'.

main_sections.section_title: Authorisation of Officers for the purpose of any provision of this Act
main_sections.description: Any officer of the Government authorised under section 3 of the Kerala Marine Fishing Regulation Act, 1980 (Act 10 of 1981) will be the Authorised Officers for the purpose of any of the provision of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Right of fishing during the Monsoon Season
main_sections.description: Notwithstanding anything contained in any law, judgement, decree or order of court, the traditional fishermen have the right to conduct pelagic fishery during monsoon season using traditional and modified traditional crafts and gears within the territorial waters. However, no fishing craft, gear or vessel which would harm the juvenile fish, egg of the fish and such other species which are necessary for the rejuvenation of the marine wealth found in the sea bed shall be used. Further, the Government may ban the right of fishing conferred under this section if they are convinced that any person misuses such fishery which is harmful to fish breeding and fish wealth in the sea bed.

main_sections.section_title: Power to enter and search fishing vessel
main_sections.description: An authorised officer may, if he has reason to believe that any fishing vessel or crafts and gears is being, or has been, used in contravention of any of the provisions of this Act or of any order or rule made thereunder, enter and search such vessel and impound and confiscate such vessel, fish and the implements thereto.

main_sections.section_title: Disposal of confiscated vessel, fish and implements
main_sections.description: The authorized officer shall keep the fishing vessels impounded under section 5 of the Act, in such place and in such manner as may be prescribed. The authorized officer shall dispose of the confiscated articles in such manner as may be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the Government to revoke or modify the orders
main_sections.description: The Government may, on report or complaint by the authorized officer or suo motu revoke, annul or modify any order issued by them under section 4 or 5 of the Act, as the case may be, if they are of the opinion that the circumstances render it necessary to do so.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act. Every rule made under this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before the Legislative Assembly, while it is in session, for a total period of fourteen days which may be comprised in one session or in two successive sessions, and if before the expiry of the session in which it is so laid or the session immediately following, the Legislative Assembly makes any modification in the rule or decides that the rule should not be made, the rule shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect, as the case may be; so, however, that any such modification or annulment shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that rule.

important_rules: Traditional fishermen have the right to conduct pelagic fishery during monsoon season using traditional and modified traditional crafts and gears within the territorial waters.
No fishing craft, gear or vessel that harms juvenile fish, eggs, or other species crucial for marine wealth rejuvenation can be used during the monsoon season.
The Government can ban the right of fishing if there is misuse that harms fish breeding and marine wealth.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Authorised officers appointed under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By entering and searching fishing vessels, impounding and confiscating vessels, fish, and implements used in contravention of the Act or its rules, and by potentially revoking or modifying orders.

rights: Traditional fishermen have the right to conduct pelagic fishery during monsoon season within territorial waters using traditional or modified traditional crafts and gears.
obligations: Users of fishing crafts and gears must not harm juvenile fish, fish eggs, or other species essential for marine wealth rejuvenation.

key_procedures: Authorisation of Officers: Officers under the Kerala Marine Fishing Regulation Act, 1980 are designated as Authorised Officers.
Conducting Pelagic Fishery: Traditional fishermen can fish during monsoon season, but must adhere to restrictions regarding crafts, gears, and impact on marine resources.
Search and Seizure: Authorised officers can enter, search, impound, and confiscate fishing vessels, fish, and implements found in contravention of the Act.
Disposal of Confiscated Items: Procedures for keeping and disposing of confiscated fishing vessels and articles are to be prescribed.
Revocation/Modification of Orders: The Government can revoke or modify orders issued under the Act based on reports or complaints.
Rule Making: The Government can make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act, which are subject to legislative scrutiny.
administration: The Government of Kerala (implied, as it's a Kerala State Act and the Government has powers under it).
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 21st June, 2007 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 1161 dated 21st June, 2007.
Rules made under the Act are subject to modification or annulment by the Legislative Assembly.

title: The Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2005
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 1985, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to motor transport undertakings and workers employed therein within the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.motor transport undertaking: Includes every registered owner or person having possession or control of a motor vehicle in respect of a motor transport undertaking.
key_definitions.self-employed person: Means a person other than an employee who is engaged in the profession of a motor transport undertaking by actually operating the vehicle and depending mainly on such a motor transport undertaking for his livelihood.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2005, and it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 7th day of June, 2005.
Amends section 2 of the principal Act by substituting clause (e) and inserting new clauses (ja) and (d) and omitting clause (k).
Substitutes section 4 of the principal Act, concerning Contribution to the Fund. It specifies the quantum of contribution payable by the employee, employer, and self-employed person.
Substitutes section 8 of the principal Act, dealing with the determination of amount due. It outlines the procedure for determining arrears and appeals.
Inserts a new section 8A concerning the production of receipt of remittance of welfare fund contribution.
Substitutes section 9 of the principal Act, related to the remittance of monthly contribution.
Substitutes section 10 of the principal Act, concerning the mode of recovery of moneys due from the employer, employee and self-employed person.
Inserts a new section 12A concerning registration and membership of the fund.
Amends section 15 of the principal Act by substituting the words 'one thousand rupees' and 'five thousand rupees'.
Amends section 25 of the principal Act by inserting words regarding notification in the Gazette.
Amends the Schedule to the principal Act by substituting the item relating to the rate of welfare fund payable to members and the conditions for such payment.
Repeals the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Ordinance, 2005, and saves anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance.

important_rules: Monthly contribution by employee, employer, and self-employed person is payable from every month as provided in the Scheme.
Monthly contribution becomes payable on or before the 7th day of the succeeding month.

Arrears of contribution due from the employer, employee, and self-employed person shall be recovered with interest thereon at the rate of 9 per cent per annum in the same manner as an arrear of public revenue due on land.

Every employer, every registered owner or person having possession or control of a motor vehicle in respect of a motor transport undertaking shall, when the vehicle is used for transport of passengers or goods for hire or reward, pay to the fund, the contribution due in respect of such motor vehicle.

penalties: Interest at the rate of 9 per cent per annum on delayed payments.
Penalties for contravention of provisions not specified with amounts/durations.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Chief Executive Officer or any other officer appointed by the Government, District Labour Officer.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Determination of arrears, review petitions, appeals to the Board, recovery as arrears of public revenue.

rights: Right to appeal against orders of determination of arrears.
Right to prefer an appeal before the District Labour Officer.
Right to prefer an appeal before the Board.
duties: Duty to pay contributions as specified.
Duty to remit monthly contributions on or before the 7th day of the succeeding month.
Duty to produce receipt of remittance of welfare fund contribution.
Duty to register and obtain identity card upon becoming a member of the fund.
obligations: Obligation to pay contribution payable by the employee, employer and self-employed person to the fund.

key_procedures: Procedure for determination of arrears by the Chief Executive Officer or appointed officer.
Procedure for filing a review petition before the authority who had determined the arrears.
Procedure for preferring an appeal to the District Labour Officer.
Procedure for preferring an appeal before the Board.
Procedure for recovery of arrears as arrears of public revenue.
administration: Not explicitly stated in the provided text, but likely falls under the purview of a government department related to labour or transport welfare.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 12th day of August, 2005, and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 1840 dated 12th August, 2005.
The amendment is retrospective from 7th June, 2005.
Any person aggrieved by an order under sub-section (2) of section 8 may prefer an appeal before the District Labour Officer.
Any person aggrieved by an order under sub-section (3) may prefer an appeal before the Labour Court.

title: THE KERALA MOTOR TRANSPORT WORKERS' PAYMENT OF FAIR WAGES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1988
purpose: To amend the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Payment of Fair Wages Act, 1971.
scope: Applies to motor transport workers in Kerala.

key_definitions.principal Act: The Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Payment of Fair Wages Act, 1971.
key_definitions.fair wages: Wages payable by an employer to the Kerala Motor Transport Workers.

main_sections.description: States that the Act can be called the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Payment of Fair Wages (Amendment) Act, 1988, and it comes into force on the 1st day of April, 1987.

Amends section 3 of the principal Act by inserting a proviso. This proviso mandates that arrears of fair wages payable by an employer should be paid before the expiry of three months from the date of publication of the Act, or not more than three monthly instalments.

Substitutes Schedule A in the principal Act with a new Schedule detailing wage scales for different categories of employees (Classes of Employers I and II, based on the number of vehicles owned) and their corresponding pay scales (I to VI).

Repeals the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Payment of Fair Wages (Amendment) Ordinance, 1988. It also saves any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance, to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Arrears of fair wages must be paid within three months of the Act's publication or in no more than three monthly instalments.
The Dearness Allowance is based on the average of the All India Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers for the year 1986.
For every point rise above 500 points in the Dearness Allowance index, wages will increase by Rs. 1.50 per mensem.
Dearness Allowance is subject to adjustments every six months based on the All India Average Consumer Price Index.
House Rent Allowance for workers is Rs. 20 per mensem.

Fitment Rules: The existing fair wages include basic pay, fixed Dearness Allowance of Rs. 88.20 (200 points), variable Dearness Allowance at the Cost of Living Number (300 points x 90 paise per point), and interim relief of Rs. 35.

Workers drawing fair wages at the existing rate will be brought onto the revised pay scale with effect from April 1, 1987, at the appropriate stage, either initial or higher stage, in the revised pay scale.

rights: Right to receive fair wages.
Right to receive Dearness Allowance.
Right to receive House Rent Allowance.
duties: Duty of employers to pay fair wages.
Duty of employers to pay arrears of fair wages within specified time limits.
Duty of employers to pay Dearness Allowance and House Rent Allowance as prescribed.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the revised pay scales.
Obligation to comply with the fitment rules.

key_procedures: Procedure for payment of arrears of fair wages: Within three months of publication or in three monthly instalments.
Procedure for calculating Dearness Allowance: Based on the All India Average Consumer Price Index, with adjustments every six months.
Procedure for fitment into revised pay scales: Workers are to be placed at the appropriate stage in the revised pay scale effective from April 1, 1987.
administration: Law (Legislation-C) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Dearness Allowance calculation is based on the average of the All India Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers for the year 1986 (base year).
The Act comes into force retrospectively from April 1, 1987, for certain provisions.
The repeal of the Ordinance does not affect any action taken under it, as those actions are deemed to have been taken under this Act.

title: THE KERALA MOTOR TRANSPORT WORKERS' PAYMENT OF FAIR WAGES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1997
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Payment of Fair Wages Act, 1971, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to motor transport workers in Kerala, as defined by the principal Act.

key_definitions.existing scale: The scale of wages mentioned in the Schedule immediately prior to 15th day of January, 1997.
key_definitions.revised scale: The scale substituted in the Schedule by the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Payment of Fair Wages (Amendment) Act, 1997.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Payment of Fair Wages (Amendment) Act, 1997. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 15th day of January, 1997.

Inserts a new section 6A in the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Payment of Fair Wages Act, 1971, regarding the power of the Government to amend the Schedule. Notifications are to be published in the Gazette and are subject to review by the Legislative Assembly. Modifications or annulments are effective without prejudice to prior actions.

Substitutes Schedule A of the principal Act with new pay scales for different categories of employees based on the number of vehicles owned by employers. It also provides rules for the fixation of pay, including Dearness Allowance, House Rent Allowance, and Grade increments.

Amends Schedule B of the principal Act by adding and modifying entries under various sub-headings such as 'Category I, Unskilled', 'Category III Skilled A', 'Category IV Skilled', and 'Category V Junior Supervising'.

Repeals the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Payment of Fair Wages (Amendment) Ordinance, 1996. Notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Rule for Dearness Allowance: Shall be paid on the basis of the All India Average Consumer Price Index Number published by Labour Bureau, Simla, for the half years January to June and July to December every year, at the rate of rupees 2 per mensem for every point above 1000 points. Amount of Dearness Allowance for January to June and July to December to be calculated and paid in September and March respectively.
Rule for House Rent Allowance: Every worker shall be paid House Rent Allowance, at the rate of rupees 30 per mensem.
Rule for Grade: Every worker who has ten years continuous service in a post shall be granted higher grade in the scale of pay of the immediate higher post.
Rule for Washing Allowance: Every worker shall be paid Washing Allowance at the rate of rupees 10 per mensem.

Rules for Fixation of Pay: (1) The initial pay of a motor transport worker shall be fixed in the existing scale by adding the following, namely: (a) the basic pay in the existing scale, (b) an amount of Rs. 750 equivalent to Dearness Allowance point between 500 and 1000, and (c) an amount equal to 10% of the total amount mentioned in items (a) and (b). (2) The pay shall be fixed in the revised scale on the basis of the amount computed under sub-rule (1) if the same is a stage in the revised scale and, if not, at the next stage above the amount so computed.

Every motor transport worker who has put in more than 5 years of service on January 1, 1997, shall be paid one increment in the revised scale as weightage on completion of every five years of service. The rate of such weightage shall be fixed in the revised scale after adding the weightage in the pay fixed under sub-rule (2).

rights: Right to fair wages as per the Act.
Right to Dearness Allowance.
Right to House Rent Allowance.
Right to Grade increment for continuous service.
Right to Washing Allowance.
duties: Motor transport workers are expected to adhere to the employment categories and service conditions outlined in the Act and its schedules.
obligations: Employers are obligated to pay fair wages, Dearness Allowance, House Rent Allowance, and Washing Allowance as stipulated.
Employers must adhere to the pay scales and increment rules.

key_procedures: Insertion of new sections and schedules into the principal Act through amendment.
Notification by the Government regarding amendments to the schedule, subject to publication in the Gazette and potential review by the Legislative Assembly.
Fixation of pay for motor transport workers based on existing scales, Dearness Allowance, and a percentage of the total.
Calculation and payment of Dearness Allowance based on the All India Average Consumer Price Index.
Granting of higher grade pay after ten years of continuous service.
administration: Kerala Government (implied by the Gazette notification and Legislative Assembly review)
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Payment of Fair Wages Act, 1971.
The commencement date of the Act is deemed to be January 15, 1997.
The Act repeals the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Payment of Fair Wages (Amendment) Ordinance, 1996, but savings are provided for actions taken under the Ordinance.
The Dearness Allowances shall be paid on the basis of the All India Average Consumer Price Index Number published by Labour Bureau, Simla.
The provisions regarding the fixation of pay and weightage are crucial for determining the salary of motor transport workers.

title: THE KERALA MOTOR TRANSPORT WORKERS' PAYMENT OF FAIR WAGES ACT, 1971
purpose: To provide for payment of fair rates of wages for motor transport workers in the State of Kerala and for matters incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to motor transport workers in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.employer: Means in relation to any motor transport undertaking, the person or the authority which has the ultimate control over the affairs of the motor transport undertaking, and where the said affairs are entrusted to any other person whether called a manager, managing director, managing agent or by any other name, such other person.
key_definitions.motor transport undertaking: Means a motor transport undertaking including a private carrier engaged in carrying passengers or goods or both by road for hire or reward.
key_definitions.motor transport worker: Means a person who is employed in a motor transport undertaking directly or through an agency, whether for wages or not, to work in a professional capacity on a transport vehicle or to attend to duties in connection with the arrival, departure, loading or unloading of such transport vehicle and includes a driver, conductor, cleaner, station staff, line checking staff, booking clerk, cash clerk, depot clerk, time keeper, watchman or attendant.
key_definitions.fair wages: Means the rate of wages payable to the motor transport workers specified in the Schedule to this Act or the agreed rate of wages whichever is higher.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Payment of Fair Wages Act, 1971 and extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. It also states that it shall be deemed to have come into force on the first day of April, 1969.
Provides definitions for 'employer', 'motor transport undertaking', 'motor transport worker', and 'fair wages'.

main_sections.section_title: Fair wages payable to motor transport workers
main_sections.description: States that notwithstanding anything contained in any other law, rule, order or notification, every employer shall pay to any motor transport worker under his employment fair wages in respect of his employment, or the work done in such employment.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for non-payment of fair wages
main_sections.description: Any employer who refuses to pay fair wages as provided in this Act to any motor transport worker without reasonable cause shall, on conviction, be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees or with both.

main_sections.section_title: Application by motor transport workers not included in the schedule
main_sections.description: Details the procedure for motor transport workers not included in the schedule to apply to the Labour Commissioner for their category to be included. It also outlines the appeal process against the orders of the Labour Commissioner.

No court shall take cognizance of an offence under this Act save on complaint made by such authority as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, specify. No court inferior to that of a Magistrate of the First Class shall try any offence under this Act.

The provisions contained in this Act shall be in addition to, and not in derogation of, the provisions contained in the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, the Minimum Wages Act, 1948, the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Conditions of Employment Rules, 1969, and the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.
Repeals the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Payment of Fair Wages Ordinance, 1971. Savings are made for any action taken or proceedings instituted under the said Ordinance.

important_rules: Employers must pay fair wages to motor transport workers.
Fair wages are defined as the rate of wages payable as per the Schedule or the agreed rate, whichever is higher.
Motor transport workers not included in the schedule can apply for inclusion through the Labour Commissioner.

penalties: Imprisonment for up to six months or a fine up to five hundred rupees or both for non-payment of fair wages without reasonable cause.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Labour Commissioner (for inclusion in schedule and appeals), Government (for specifying authorities to take cognizance of offences).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through court proceedings for penalties, and through administrative processes for inclusion and appeals related to fair wages.

rights: Right to receive fair wages as defined by the Act.
duties: Duty of employers to pay fair wages.
Duty of motor transport workers to report if they are not included in the schedule and wish to be.
Duty of the employer to comply with any order regarding inclusion of workers in the schedule.
obligations: Employers have an obligation to pay fair wages which is higher than the agreed rate if specified in the schedule.

key_procedures: Procedure for motor transport workers not included in the schedule to apply for inclusion to the Labour Commissioner.
Procedure for appealing against the orders of the Labour Commissioner to the Government.
Procedure for lodging a complaint for cognizance of an offence under the Act by a specified authority.
administration: The Kerala Government (indicated by 'Government' in various sections, and implied by the gazette notification requirement). The Labour Commissioner is also a key administrative figure.
important_notes: The Act commenced retrospectively from April 1, 1969.

The Act does not affect the provisions of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, the Minimum Wages Act, 1948, the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Conditions of Employment Rules, 1969, and the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.
Offences under the Act can only be taken cognizance of upon a complaint by an authority specified by the Government.
Schedule A provides details on Dearness allowance and House rent allowance for various categories of employees based on the number of vehicles in the employer's fleet.
Schedule B classifies workers into categories such as Unskilled, Semi-skilled, Skilled-A, Skilled-B, Junior Supervisory, and Senior Supervisory.

title: THE KERALA MOTOR TRANSPORT WORKERS' WELFARE FUND ACT, 1985
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a Fund to promote the welfare of motor transport workers in the State of Kerala.
scope: The Act applies to the entire State of Kerala and concerns motor transport workers and employers in that state.

key_definitions.Board: Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Welfare Fund Board constituted under section 6.
key_definitions.Chief Executive Officer: Chief Executive Officer appointed under sub-section (1) of section 7.
key_definitions.Contribution: Contribution payable in respect of a member of the Fund.
key_definitions.Employee: A person who is employed for wages in a motor transport undertaking directly or through an agency to work in a professional capacity on transport vehicle or to attend to duties in connection with the arrival, departure, loading or unloading of such transport vehicle and includes a driver, conductor, cleaner, station staff, line checking staff, booking clerk, cash clerk, depot clerk, time keeper, watchman or attendant.
key_definitions.Employer: In relation to any motor transport undertaking, the person who, or the authority which, has the ultimate control over the affairs of the motor transport undertaking, and where the said affairs are entrusted to any other person, whether called a manager, managing director, managing agent or by any other name, such person; other person.
key_definitions.Fund: The Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Welfare Fund established under the scheme.
key_definitions.Member: A member of the Fund and includes any person eligible to become a member of the Fund.
key_definitions.Motor transport undertaking: A motor transport undertaking engaged in carrying passengers or goods or both by road for hire or reward and includes a private carrier.
key_definitions.Prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Scheme: The scheme framed under this Act.
key_definitions.Wages: All emoluments which are earned by an employee while on duty or on leave with wages in accordance with the terms of the contract of employment and which are paid or payable in cash to him, but does not include- (i) the cash value of any food concession; (ii) overtime allowance, bonus and commission; (iii) all other words and expressions used but not defined in this Act and defined in the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939 (Central Act 4 of 1939), shall have the meanings respectively assigned to them in that Act.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 1985, its extent to the whole of the State of Kerala, and the date of its commencement, which is the 27th day of June, 1985.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including Board, Chief Executive Officer, Contribution, Employee, Employer, Fund, Member, Motor transport undertaking, Prescribed, Scheme, and Wages.
Establishes the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Welfare Fund and outlines its vesting and administration by the Board.

Specifies that the employer shall be paid eight per cent of the wages for the time being payable to each of the employees, and the employees' contribution shall be equal to the contribution payable by the employer in respect of him.

Allows the Government to add to, amend or vary the scheme either prospectively or retrospectively by notification in the Gazette. Provisions regarding notification and its effect if not issued are also mentioned.
Details the constitution of the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Welfare Fund Board, its corporate nature, the number and appointment of Directors, and their representation.
Empowers the Government to appoint a Chief Executive Officer and other officers and staff to assist the Board, and defines their powers and functions.

main_sections.section_title: Determination of amount due from employers
main_sections.description: Authorises the Chief Executive Officer or any other appointed officer to determine the amount due from any employer and conduct inquiries. It also outlines the procedure for appealing to the Government or any other authority.

Describes the process of provisional assessment of contributions by employers, with provision for annual adjustment and advance contributions. It also details the procedure for recovery of unpaid contributions.

main_sections.section_title: Mode of recovery of moneys due from employers
main_sections.description: Specifies that any amount due from an employer under the Act or scheme, if not paid, can be recovered as arrears of public revenue due on land.
States that the amount standing to the credit of any member in the Fund is not liable to attachment or to form part of the estate of a bankrupt or insolvent member.

main_sections.section_title: Priority of payment of contributions over other debts
main_sections.description: Establishes that the amount due from an employer for contributions to the Fund shall have priority over all other debts in case of insolvency or winding up of the company.

main_sections.section_title: Employer not to reduce wages etc.
main_sections.description: Prohibits employers from reducing wages or otherwise affecting the liability of the employee to the Fund, or reducing the quantum of benefits to which the employee is entitled.

main_sections.section_title: Directors of Board etc., to be public servants
main_sections.description: Declares that Directors of the Board and officers appointed under the Act are deemed to be public servants within the meaning of section 21 of the Indian Penal Code.
Outlines penalties for avoiding payment, making false statements, or contravening provisions of the Act or scheme, with imprisonment and fines.

main_sections.section_title: Enhanced punishment for default in payment of employees' contributions already deducted
main_sections.description: Provides for enhanced punishment for employers who default in paying employees' contributions already deducted, including imprisonment and fines.

main_sections.section_title: Enhanced punishment for second or subsequent offence
main_sections.description: Specifies enhanced punishment for second or subsequent offences under the Act.
Addresses offences committed by companies, stating that every person in charge of the company's affairs at the time of the offence is liable.
Empowers the Government to give directions to the Board.
Grants the Government the power to order an inquiry into the affairs of the Board.
Authorises the Government to supersede the Board in certain circumstances.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Bar of jurisdiction of civil courts
main_sections.description: Restricts the jurisdiction of civil courts to entertain any suit concerning any matter for which provision is made in the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Special provisions for transfer and vesting of welfare fund established by custom or agreement
main_sections.description: Makes special provisions for the transfer and vesting of any welfare fund established by custom or agreement into the Fund constituted under this Act.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Provides for the repeal of any existing law and savings for actions taken under such repealed law.

important_rules: Employers must contribute 8% of employee wages to the Fund. Employees' contribution is equal to the employer's contribution.
Employers cannot reduce wages or alter the terms of employment to the detriment of employees regarding Fund contributions or benefits.
Amounts standing to the credit of a member in the Fund are protected from attachment and insolvency proceedings.
Contributions due to the Fund have priority over other debts in case of company insolvency or winding up.
The Government can make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act.

penalties: For avoiding payment: Imprisonment up to six months or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both.
For contravening provisions: Imprisonment up to three months or fine up to five hundred rupees, or both.
Enhanced punishment for default in payment of employees' contributions already deducted: Imprisonment up to one year, not less than three months, and fine up to four thousand rupees.
Enhanced punishment for second or subsequent offence: Imprisonment up to one year, not less than three months, and fine up to four thousand rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Chief Executive Officer and other officers appointed under the Act are responsible for enforcing its provisions. The Government also has oversight powers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the determination of amounts due from employers, provisional assessments, recovery of arrears, penalties for contravention, and judicial proceedings.

rights: Members have a right to receive benefits from the Fund.
Members have the right to have their contributions credited to their account.
Members aggrieved by an order under sub-section (1) of section 8 have the right to appeal to the Government or any other authority.
duties: Employers have a duty to contribute to the Fund as specified.
Employers have a duty to deduct and pay employees' contributions.
Employers have a duty not to reduce wages or alter employment terms to the detriment of employees regarding the Fund.
obligations: Employers have an obligation to ensure that contributions are paid in accordance with the Act and scheme.

key_procedures: Determination of amount due from employers by the Chief Executive Officer.
Provisional assessment and payment of contributions by employers.
Recovery of arrears of contributions as public revenue due on land.
Appeal process for aggrieved employers.
Constitution and functioning of the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Welfare Fund Board.
Appointment and functions of the Chief Executive Officer and other officers.
Making of rules by the Government.
administration: The Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Welfare Fund Board and the Government of Kerala administer the Act. The Chief Executive Officer is responsible for day-to-day administration.
important_notes: The Act was received the assent of the President on the 12th day of August, 1985 and Published in the Kerala Gazette, Extraordinary No. 681 dated 16th August 1985.
The Act applies to motor transport undertakings within the State of Kerala.
The scheme framed under the Act is to be notified in the Gazette.
The Board is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
Penalties are prescribed for various offences under the Act.

title: THE KERALA MOTOR VEHICLES (TAXATION OF PASSENGERS AND GOODS) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1970
purpose: To amend The Kerala Motor Vehicles (Taxation of Passengers and Goods) Act, 1963, for purposes including the levy and collection of taxes on passengers and goods carried by motor vehicles.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and concerns motor vehicles carrying passengers and goods within the state.

main_sections.description: Specifies that this Act may be called the Kerala Motor Vehicles (Taxation of Passengers and Goods) (Amendment) Act, 1970, and outlines its commencement dates for different provisions. Sections 5 and 6 were deemed to have come into force from January 5, 1970, and other provisions from July 1st, 1965.

Amends Section 3 of the principal Act (1963). It clarifies that the words 'there shall be levied and paid to the Government a tax' replace 'there shall be levied a tax'. It also inserts new sub-sections to clarify the tax levy on passengers, luggage, and goods, stating that the operator is liable for the tax in the manner provided in the Act.

Amends Section 4 of the principal Act, replacing specific words and figures related to 'assessable on him under this Act' and 'payable by him under sub-section (3) of section 3' with bracketed and figured substitutions.

Amends Section 14 of the principal Act, changing the wording regarding 'fares and freights collected in respect of passengers travelling or luggage or goods transported therein' to 'fares, freights and taxes collected from passengers or consignors of goods transported'.
States that Section 18 of the principal Act shall be omitted.

Provides a validation clause, ensuring that any tax levied or collected under the principal Act, or actions taken in accordance with its provisions, will not be questioned due to any defect or omission. It also states that anything done or omitted before the commencement of this section, if it was lawful under the principal Act as amended, is deemed to have been done or omitted under the amended Act.

Repeals The Kerala Motor Vehicles (Taxation of Passengers and Goods) Amendment Ordinance, 1970. It also states that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance is deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Tax is to be levied and paid to the Government on passengers, luggage, and goods carried by motor vehicles.
The operator of the motor vehicle is liable to pay the tax.
Provisions related to the levy and collection of tax are specified in the principal Act and its amendments.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Implied to be the State Government or its authorized officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the principal Act and this Amendment Act, likely involving assessment, collection, and potential penalties for non-compliance.

duties: Duty of the operator to pay tax on passengers, luggage, and goods carried.
Duty of the Government to provide for the levy and collection of tax.

key_procedures: Levy and collection of tax on passengers, luggage, and goods.
Amendment and substitution of specific sections and words in the principal Act.
Commencement of various provisions on specified dates.
administration: The Kerala Motor Vehicles Department or a similar authority under the State Government.
important_notes: The amendment act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 263, dated 1st May, 1971.
Certain provisions have retrospective effect from January 5, 1970, and July 1st, 1965.

title: The Kerala Motor Vehicles (Taxation of Passengers and Goods) Amendment Act, 1972
purpose: To amend the Kerala Motor Vehicles (Taxation of Passengers and Goods) Act, 1963, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to amendments made to the Kerala Motor Vehicles (Taxation of Passengers and Goods) Act, 1963.

key_definitions.operator: Means the owner or the person having possession or control of the vehicle and includes any person whose name is entered in the permit as holder thereof.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Motor Vehicles (Taxation of Passengers and Goods) Amendment Act, 1972. It also specifies commencement dates for different sections: Section 2 shall be deemed to have come into force on July 1, 1967, Section 4 on July 1, 1963, and remaining provisions on the date of enforcement.
Amends section 2 of the Kerala Motor Vehicles (Taxation of Passengers and Goods) Act, 1963, by substituting the definition of 'operator'.
Amends section 3 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), by omitting the second proviso.

Amends section 8 of the principal Act by substituting 'three years' with 'ten years' for the words 'three years', and by inserting a new proviso regarding the exclusion of periods of stay under an injunction or order of any court from the period of limitation for tax assessment.

Inserts a new section 11A titled 'Transfers to defraud revenue', which deals with situations where an operator or other person liable to pay tax creates a charge on or parts with the possession of a vehicle by sale, mortgage, exchange, or any other mode of transfer, with the intention to defeat the recovery of tax. Such charge or transfer shall be void as against any claim in respect of the tax.

Validates any judgment, decree, or order of any court, all taxes levied, assessed, or collected, and purports that anything done or omitted to be done before the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette shall be deemed to have been levied, assessed, or collected in accordance with the provisions of the principal Act as amended by this Act. It also states that no suit or other proceeding shall be maintained or continued for the refund of any such tax paid under the principal Act. It further validates any tax assessed under the principal Act before the date of publication and not collected, and any tax due under the principal Act as amended but not assessed before the date of publication.

States that nothing contained in this Act shall render any person liable to be convicted of an offence in respect of anything done or omitted to be done by him before the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette, if such act or omission would not be an offence under the principal Act but for the provisions of this Act.

important_rules: Tax assessment period limitations can be extended due to injunctions or court orders.
Transfers of vehicles intended to defraud revenue are void against tax claims.
Acts done or omitted before the Act's publication are not offences if they were not offences under the original Act.

rights: Right of a charge-holder or transferee in good faith for consideration.
obligations: Obligation of operators to pay taxes.

key_procedures: Amendment of specific sections of the principal Act.
Insertion of a new section to address transfers to defraud revenue.
Validation of past assessments and collections.
Provisions for the commencement of different sections of the Act.
administration: The Kerala Motor Vehicles Department (implied, based on the Act's subject matter).
important_notes: The Act is published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 216, dated 12th March, 1973.

title: THE KERALA MOTOR VEHICLES (TAXATION OF PASSENGERS AND GOODS) AMENDMENT ACT, 1967
purpose: To amend the Kerala Motor Vehicles (Taxation of Passengers and Goods) Act, 1963, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: The Act applies to the Kerala Motor Vehicles (Taxation of Passengers and Goods) Act, 1963.

key_definitions.goods vehicle: Any motor vehicle constructed or adapted for use for the carriage of goods, or any motor vehicle not so constructed or adapted when used for the carriage of goods solely or in addition to passengers.
key_definitions.private carrier vehicle: Means a goods vehicle which is not a public carrier vehicle.
key_definitions.public carrier vehicle: Means a goods vehicle which is not a private carrier vehicle.

main_sections.description: (1) This Act may be called the Kerala Motor Vehicles (Taxation of Passengers and Goods) Amendment Act, 1967. (2) It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of July, 1967.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of long title and preamble.
main_sections.description: In the Kerala Motor Vehicles (Taxation of Passengers and Goods) Act, 1963 (125 of 1963) (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), in the long title and preamble, for the words "public carrier vehicles", the words "goods vehicles" shall be substituted.

In section 2 of the principal Act, (a) clause (aa) shall be re-lettered as clause (aa) and, before clause (aa) as so re-lettered, the following clause shall be inserted, namely:— "(a) 'goods vehicle' means any motor vehicle constructed or adapted for use for the carriage of goods, or any motor vehicle not so constructed or adapted when used for the carriage of goods solely or in addition to passengers;"; (b) after clause (d), the following clause shall be inserted, namely:— "(dd) 'private carrier vehicle' means a goods vehicle which is not a public carrier vehicle"; (c) in clause (i), for the words "public carrier vehicle", the words "goods vehicle" shall be substituted.

In section 3 of the Principal Act, (a) in the opening paragraph, for the portion beginning with the words "on all goods transported" and ending with the words "such public carrier vehicles", the following shall be substituted, namely:— "on all goods transported by goods vehicles, at the following rates, namely:— (a) in the case of stage carriages, 10 paise in the rupee on the fares and freights payable to the operators of such carriages; (b) in the case of public carrier vehicles, 5 paise in the rupee on the freights payable to the operators of such vehicles; (c) in the case of private carrier vehicles, 2 paise per tonne kilometre of the goods"; (b) in the first proviso, for the words "public carrier vehicles", the words "goods vehicles" shall be substituted.

In the Schedule to the principal Act, for clause (b) of sub-rule (1) of rule 2, the following clause shall be substituted, namely:— "(b) in the case of a goods vehicle— (i) not exceeding 9,500 kg, in RLW, of Rs. 112-50 (rupees one hundred and twelve and fifty paise) per quarter; (ii) exceeding 9,500 kg, but not exceeding 10,500 kg, in RLW, of Rs. 130 (rupees one hundred and thirty) per quarter; (iii) exceeding 10,500 kg, in RLW, of Rs. 180 (rupees one hundred and eighty) per quarter.".

important_rules: Substitution of 'public carrier vehicles' with 'goods vehicles' in the long title and preamble of the principal Act.
Substitution of specific rates for taxation based on vehicle type and weight, as detailed in Section 4 and Section 5.
Definition of 'goods vehicle' and 'private carrier vehicle' is provided in Section 3.
key_procedures: The Act commenced on July 1, 1967.
Amendments involve substituting specific terms and revising taxation rates for goods vehicles.
important_notes: Published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 218, dated 15th November, 1967.

title: The Kerala Motor Vehicles (Taxation of Passengers and Goods) Revival and Special Provisions Act, 1983
purpose: To revive and amend the Kerala Motor Vehicles (Taxation of Passengers and Goods) Act, 1963, and to make certain special provisions for the levy and collection of tax on goods carried or hauled by articulated vehicles, tractor-trailer combinations, tiller-trailer combinations, and trailers drawn by any other motor vehicle, for the period during which the said Act was in force.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala. It covers the levy and collection of tax on passengers and goods carried by articulated vehicles, tractor-trailer combinations, tiller-trailer combinations, and trailers drawn by any other motor vehicle within the state for a specific period.

key_definitions.articulated vehicle: A tractor which is attached to a trailer, where the trailer is superimposed on the tractor, and a part of the weight of the trailer is borne by the tractor.
key_definitions.carriage: Has its grammatical variations and cognate expressions, including 'haulage'.
key_definitions.goods vehicle: Any motor vehicle constructed, or adapted for use for the carriage of goods solely, or in addition to passengers, or any motor vehicle not so constructed or adapted when used for the carriage of goods solely, or in addition to passengers.
key_definitions.public carrier vehicle: Means a goods vehicle carrying goods for hire or reward.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called The Kerala Motor Vehicles (Taxation of Passengers and Goods) Revival and Special Provisions Act, 1983. It also specifies that it extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 22nd day of January, 1983.

All words and expressions used in this Act shall have the meanings respectively assigned to them in the Kerala Motor Vehicles (Taxation of Passengers and Goods) Act, 1963, as revived and amended by this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Revival of Kerala Act 25 of 1963 and rules made thereunder for certain purposes
main_sections.description: This section revives the Kerala Motor Vehicles (Taxation of Passengers and Goods) Act, 1963 (hereinafter referred to as the said Act) and the rules made thereunder. It states that they shall be deemed to have been in force, subject to the amendments and special provisions contained in this Act, for the purposes of levy and collection of tax on goods carried by articulated vehicles, tractor-trailer combinations, tiller-trailer combinations and trailers drawn by any other motor vehicle, for the period commencing on the 1st day of July, 1963 and ending with the 30th day of September, 1975.

This section makes amendments to the Kerala Motor Vehicles (Taxation of Passengers and Goods) Act, 1963. It substitutes certain clauses, including definitions for 'articulated vehicle' and 'goods vehicle', and makes provisions for 'composition of tax'.

main_sections.section_title: Special provisions in respect of tax on tractor-trailer combinations
main_sections.description: This section contains special provisions related to the tax on tractor-trailer combinations.

This section deals with the adjustment of tax that has already been collected on goods carried by articulated vehicles, tractor-trailer combinations, tiller-trailer combinations, and trailers drawn by any other motor vehicle for the period from July 1, 1963, to September 30, 1975. It specifies that if the tax collected is less than the amount due, the deficit will be recovered, and if it is in excess, the excess shall be refunded.

This section repeals the Kerala Motor Vehicles (Taxation of Passengers and Goods) Revival and Special Provisions Ordinance, 1983 (35 of 1983). It also includes savings provisions stating that nothing in the repeal shall render invalid any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the said Ordinance, and that nothing contained in this Act shall render any person liable to conviction for any offense committed before the commencement of this Act.

important_rules: The Kerala Motor Vehicles (Taxation of Passengers and Goods) Act, 1963, and its rules are revived and deemed to be in force subject to the amendments and special provisions of this Act for a specific period.

Tax on goods carried by specific types of vehicles for the period July 1, 1963, to September 30, 1975, shall be adjusted. Any deficit tax due will be recovered, and any excess tax collected will be refunded.
No person shall be liable to conviction for any offense committed before the commencement of this Act, despite the repeal of the Ordinance.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Commissioner is empowered to conduct investigations and take action.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The Commissioner has the power to regulate his own procedure, including summoning and enforcing attendance of witnesses, discovery and production of documents, receiving evidence on affidavits, and issuing commissions for examination of witnesses. Investigations can be treated as judicial proceedings.

rights: Right to claim a refund of excess tax collected.
Right to appeal to the principal civil court of original jurisdiction against a decision of the Commissioner within a specified period.
duties: Duty to pay the correct amount of tax.
Duty to provide proof of claim to the Commissioner within the time specified in the advertisement.
obligations: Obligation to cooperate with the Commissioner's investigation and follow prescribed procedures.

key_procedures: Procedure for the adjustment of tax already collected, involving recovery of deficits and refund of excesses.
Procedure for claimants to file proof of their claims with the Commissioner within a specified time.
Procedure for the Commissioner to investigate claims, which includes powers similar to those of a civil court.
administration: The Commissioner is the primary administrative authority responsible for enforcement and investigation.
important_notes: The Act has retrospective effect from January 22, 1983.
The Act revives and amends the Kerala Motor Vehicles (Taxation of Passengers and Goods) Act, 1963, for specific purposes and a defined period.
Special provisions are made for tax on tractor-trailer combinations and adjustment of tax already collected.
Appeals against the decision of the Commissioner can be made to the principal civil court of original jurisdiction.

title: The Kerala Motor Vehicles (Taxation) Amendment Act, 1967
purpose: To amend the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1963, for purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala. It amends the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1963.

key_definitions.fleet owner: means a person or an institution who, or which, is the registered owner of more than one hundred and fifty transport vehicles used or kept for use in the State.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Act, 1967, and it came into force on the 1st day of July, 1967.

In section 2 of the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1963, for clause (b), the following clause is substituted: "(b) 'laden weight', in respect of any motor vehicle, means the registered laden weight of that vehicle;".
Inserts a new section 24A titled 'Surcharge on tax'. This section outlines the amount of tax leviable in pursuance of sub-section (1) of section 3, in the case of any vehicle.
Amends Schedule I to the principal Act, specifically for sub-item (i) and sub-item (ii) of item 4. It details the surcharge on tax for vehicles based on laden weight.

important_rules: Surcharge on tax: The amount of tax leviable in pursuance of sub-section (1) of section 3 shall, in the case of any vehicle, be seventy-five per cent of the tax so leviable in respect of that vehicle.
The surcharge payable under sub-section (1) shall be paid in advance, in such manner and before such date as may be prescribed, for a quarter, half-year or year at the choice of the fleet owner.
The surcharge for a quarter shall not exceed one-fourth, and the surcharge for a half-year shall not exceed one-half, the surcharge for a year.

duties: Payment of surcharge on tax for motor vehicles.
obligations: Fleet owners are obligated to pay surcharge in advance for a quarter, half-year, or year.

key_procedures: Payment of surcharge: Surcharge is payable in advance in the prescribed manner and by the prescribed date for a quarter, half-year, or year at the choice of the fleet owner.
Amendment of Schedule I: The amendment details the new rates of surcharge based on vehicle laden weight for different categories of vehicles.
important_notes: Published in the Kerala Gazette Extra-ordinary No. 218, dated 15th November, 1967.
The surcharge is applicable in addition to the tax leviable in accordance with the provisions of the principal Act.
The provisions of this Act do not affect any penalty, forfeiture or punishment incurred or any legal proceeding commenced before the commencement of this Act.

title: THE KERALA MOTOR VEHICLES TAXATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1989
purpose: To amend the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976.
scope: Applies to motor vehicles and their owners/possessors within Kerala. The amendments pertain to the taxation and licensing of motor vehicles.

main_sections.description: Names the act as the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Act, 1989 and specifies commencement dates for different provisions.

Amends section 4 of the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976, specifically concerning the tax rates for different license periods and for specific types of vehicles like motor cycles and three wheelers. It also introduces provisions for rebates and a new Explanation for tax rates.
Amends section 6 of the principal Act, inserting a new sub-section (2) to address refunds for registered owners who have paid lump sum tax for a year or more.

Repeals the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Ordinance, 1988, and provides a saving clause stating that anything done or taken under the repealed Ordinance as amended by the principal Act shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Tax rates for motor cycles and three wheelers are specified for advance payment of tax.
Tax rates for annual, 5 years, 10 years, and 15 years licenses are defined.
Tax rates for quarterly licenses are also defined.
Rebates may be granted in respect of the tax for a year or more.
Registered owners who have paid lump sum tax for a year or more are entitled to a refund on cancellation of the registration of the vehicle.

rights: Right to receive a refund on cancellation of registration if lump sum tax for a year or more has been paid.
duties: Duty to pay motor vehicles tax as prescribed by the Act.

key_procedures: Process for determining tax rates based on license duration and vehicle type.
Procedure for claiming a refund of tax upon cancellation of registration.
important_notes: The Act commenced on the 1st day of July, 1987, with remaining provisions coming into force on the 22nd day of September, 1983.
The Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Ordinance, 1988 is repealed.
The Act is an amendment to the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976.

title: THE KERALA MOTOR VEHICLES TAXATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1993
purpose: To amend the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to motor vehicles and their owners/possessors within Kerala. It amends the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Act, 1993. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 3rd day of January, 1993.

Amends section 4 of the principal Act. It modifies the definition of 'motor vehicle' and provides for taxation for periods of two years, five years, or ten/fifteen years in lieu of annual license, particularly for motor scooters and cycles with attachment for propelling the same by mechanical power, and for three-wheelers or motor cars as specified in item 6A of the Schedule. It also amends the Explanation for words 'The tax for an annual licence' to not exceed four times, and 'The tax for two years' licence' to not exceed eight times.
Amends section 6 of the principal Act. It substitutes the words 'for any quarter or year' with 'for any period specified in section 4', and 'that quarter or year' with 'that period'.

Repeals the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Ordinance, 1993 (2 of 1993). Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Taxation for periods of two years, five years, or ten/fifteen years in lump sum upon a licence can be availed by a registered owner or person having possession or control of a motor scooter, cycle with attachment, or a three-wheeler or motor car as specified in item 6A of the Schedule.
Tax for an annual licence shall not exceed four times.
Tax for two years' licence shall not exceed eight times.

duties: Registered owner or person having possession or control of a motor scooter, cycle with attachment for propelling the same by mechanical power or a three wheeler or a motor car as specified in item 6A of the said Schedule shall pay the tax payable in respect of that vehicle in advance for a period of two years in lump sum upon a licence for such period.

key_procedures: Payment of tax in advance for two, five, or ten/fifteen years for specified vehicles in lump sum upon a licence.
administration: The Government of Kerala is responsible for the enactment and enforcement of this Act.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 2nd day of March 1993 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 234 dated the 3rd March 1993.
The amendment provisions are effective from 3rd January 1993.
Any action taken under the repealed Ordinance is considered valid under this Act.

title: The Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Act, 1972
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1963, for the purpose hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to motor vehicles in Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Act, 1972.
Inserts a new section 24B regarding surcharge on tax in respect of certain non-transport vehicles.
Deals with the cessation of operation of the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Ordinance, 1971, and its effect on actions taken, penalties incurred, investigations, etc.

important_rules: Surcharge of ten per cent on the rate of tax levied in pursuance of sub-section (1) of section 3 shall be levied in respect of certain non-transport vehicles.
The surcharge payable under sub-section (1) shall be paid along with the tax and notified by the Government.

penalties: Any penalty or punishment incurred in respect of any offence committed under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall not be affected.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be the relevant transport authorities under the principal Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By the relevant authorities under the principal Act.

rights: Any right, privilege, obligation or liability acquired, accrued or incurred under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall not be affected.

key_procedures: Payment of surcharge along with the tax as notified by the Government.
administration: Implied to be the transport department or relevant government authorities in Kerala.
important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 248, dated 5th May, 1972.
The cessation of operation of the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Ordinance, 1971, does not affect actions taken or penalties incurred under it.

No person shall be convicted of any offence under the principal Act as amended by this Act committed after the cessation of operation of the said Ordinance and before the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette.

title: The Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Act, 1973
purpose: To amend The Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1963.
scope: Applies to The Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1963.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Act, 1973, and it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1973.

Provides for the omission of section 24B from the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1963. It details the effects of such omission, including not reviving anything not in force or existing, not affecting previous operations or penalties, and not affecting investigations or proceedings already instituted.

Repeals The Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Ordinance, 1973 (6 of 1973). It also includes a saving clause stating that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act, as amended by the said Ordinance, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_notes: The Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 874 dated 13th September, 1973.
The amendment comes into force on the 1st day of April, 1973.

title: THE KERALA MOTOR VEHICLES TAXATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1986
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and motor vehicles plying therein, affecting taxation as per the principal Act.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Act, 1986. Section 2 shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1985 and the remaining provisions of this Act shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of January, 1985.

In section 4 of the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976 (19 of 1976), after the existing proviso and before the Explanation, the following further provisos shall be inserted: Provided further that where the tax payable in respect of a motor vehicle for a year does not exceed three hundred rupees, the tax shall be paid yearly upon an annual licence. Provided also that a registered owner or person having possession or control of the motor vehicle may, at his/her choice, pay the yearly tax payable under the second proviso in advance for any period up to 5 years, upon a licence for such period. Further, notwithstanding anything contained in any other provision of this Act, 'year', in relation to a motor vehicle in respect of which tax has to be paid yearly upon an annual licence in pursuance of the second proviso to sub-section (1), shall mean a period of twelve months commencing on the first day of the quarter in which the vehicle has been, or is, first registered in the State and annual tax licence in respect of such a vehicle shall be taken accordingly.

In the entries relating to Serial Number 4, for sub-class (i), under the heading "Rate of quarterly tax", the following sub-classes and entries shall be substituted: "(d) more than 6 passengers, but not more than 20 passengers, for every passenger 100.00 (e) more than 20 passengers, for every passenger 200.00"; In the proviso, after clause (4), the following clause shall be inserted: "(4A) the tax in respect of a motor vehicle which is registered in the State as new, or brought from outside the State, after the 1st day of April, 1985, and in respect of which tax has to be paid annually in pursuance of the second proviso to sub-section (1) of section 4, the annual tax payable for the first year shall be at the rate of 1/12th of the annual tax for each calendar month or part thereof from the date of such registration."

The Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Ordinance, 1986 (5 of 1986), is hereby repealed. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.
