important_rules: Motor vehicles will be taxed annually. The tax for a year does not exceed three hundred rupees.
Owners can choose to pay the annual tax for up to 5 years in advance.
The 'year' for calculating tax on an annual licence basis begins on the first day of the quarter in which the vehicle is first registered.
Quarterly tax rates for certain passenger vehicles are specified.
Annual tax for newly registered or out-of-state vehicles brought into Kerala after April 1, 1985, will be calculated pro-rata for the first year based on the date of registration.

rights: Right to pay annual tax for up to 5 years in advance.
duties: Duty to pay motor vehicles tax.
Duty to adhere to the commencement dates of the Act's provisions.
obligations: Obligation to pay tax as per the provisions of the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure for commencement: Section 2 (Short title and commencement) specifies the dates on which different parts of the Act come into force.

Procedure for amendment: Section 2 describes how section 4 of the principal Act is amended by inserting new provisos, and Section 3 details amendments to the Schedule regarding tax rates for passenger vehicles.
Procedure for repeal and saving: Section 4 repeals the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Ordinance, 1986, and ensures continuity of actions taken under the Ordinance.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 30th day of November, 1986 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 1073 dated 30th November, 1986.
The commencement date for Section 2 is April 1, 1985, and for the remaining provisions, January 1, 1985.
The amendment specifically addresses the taxation of motor vehicles registered in the State as new, or brought from outside the State after April 1, 1985.

title: THE KERALA MOTOR VEHICLES TAXATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1983
purpose: To amend the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976, for the purposes appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976 and motor vehicles in Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Act, 1983, and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of January, 1982.

Amends the Schedule to the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976, by substituting specific figures related to quarterly tax for vehicles. It also amends the heading and a sub-clause within the Schedule regarding the class of vehicles and the rate of quarterly tax. Specifically, it changes the figures '100.00' to '120.00' and modifies the wording for the rate of quarterly tax for certain vehicle classes.

Repeals the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Ordinance, 1983 (1 of 1983), and provides that anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: The Act is deemed to have come into force on January 1, 1982.
The figures "100.00" against sub-class (1) (d) under the heading "Class of vehicle" in the Schedule are substituted with "120.00".

The clause (a) of sub-class (iii) under the heading "Class of vehicle" and the entries against that clause under the heading "Rate of quarterly tax" are to be substituted to clarify the rates for specific vehicle classes.
The Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Ordinance, 1983 is repealed.
administration: Likely the Transport Department or a similar body responsible for motor vehicles in Kerala.
important_notes: The Act was received the assent of the Governor on the 6th day of April, 1983.
It was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 410, dated the 7th April, 1983.

title: The Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to the levy of taxes on motor vehicles in the State of Kerala.
scope: This Act applies to all motor vehicles within the State of Kerala. It covers the imposition, assessment, and collection of taxes on such vehicles.

key_definitions.motor_vehicle: Includes a motor car, motor cycle, omni bus, motor lorry, trailer and every description of vehicle, other than a vehicle of a special type adapted for use only under special conditions or for use by persons suffering from affliction or disability of mind or body, which is self-propelled and every kind of vehicle adapted for use upon roads, whether the power of propulsion is transmitted thereto from an external or internal source and includes a chassis, with or without engine, mounted on any means of transport, or a trailer.
key_definitions.owner: Includes the person whose name is entered in the Register of Motor Vehicles as the owner of the motor vehicle, and in case of a company, the manager or the person who is in charge of the affairs of the company, and in case of a motor vehicle on hire, the person who is in possession of the vehicle.
key_definitions.tax: Includes any tax, fee or other sum of money payable under this Act.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and its extent of application (State of Kerala).
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'motor vehicle', 'owner', 'tax', 'prescribed', etc.
Deals with the imposition of tax on motor vehicles at such rates as may be specified in the Schedule appended to the Act.
Specifies the basis and rates for taxing non-transport motor vehicles.
Specifies the basis and rates for taxing transport motor vehicles.
Empowers the Government to exempt certain classes of motor vehicles or uses from the payment of tax.
Lays down the procedure for payment of tax, including the period for which it is payable and the due dates.
Specifies who is liable for the payment of tax, generally the registered owner of the vehicle.
Provides for the refund of tax in certain circumstances, such as when a vehicle is kept off the road or exported.
Outlines the methods for collecting and recovering tax, including provisions for arrears.
Defines offenses related to non-payment of tax or evasion and prescribes penalties.
Grants power to compound certain offenses by payment of a sum of money.
Authorizes the State Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of any previous enactment and savings from such repeal.

important_rules: The tax on motor vehicles is to be paid annually or quarterly in advance.
The tax rates are specified in the Schedule appended to the Act and vary based on the type of vehicle, engine capacity, seating capacity, or unladen weight.
Vehicles used for specific purposes like police, fire brigade, or by disabled persons may be exempted from tax.
Provisions exist for temporary or permanent discontinuation of use of a vehicle, leading to potential tax refunds or adjustments.

penalties: Penalty for using a motor vehicle without paying the prescribed tax.
Penalty for failure to furnish information or producing documents.
Penalties for other contraventions of the Act or rules.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government and officers authorized by it, including the Transport Department officials.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through checks, inspections of vehicles, assessment of taxes, and legal proceedings for recovery of arrears or imposition of penalties.

rights: Right to claim refund of tax under prescribed conditions (e.g., keeping vehicle off road, export).
Right to appeal against assessment or demand of tax.
duties: Duty to pay the motor vehicle tax as prescribed by the Act.
Duty to display valid tax token/certificate.
Duty to inform authorities about changes in vehicle usage or ownership that may affect tax liability.
Duty to furnish information and documents as required by the authorities.
obligations: Obligation to ensure the vehicle is taxed before it is put on the road.
Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder.

key_procedures: Procedure for assessment and payment of tax: The owner is required to calculate the tax based on the vehicle's classification and pay it to the prescribed authority by the due date.
Procedure for claiming refund: An application for refund of tax needs to be submitted to the prescribed authority along with supporting documents, as per the rules.
Procedure for appealing against assessment: If an owner is aggrieved by an assessment or demand, they have the right to appeal to higher authorities as specified in the Act.
administration: The Transport Department of the Government of Kerala is responsible for the administration and enforcement of this Act.
important_notes: The Schedule appended to the Act contains the specific rates of tax for different categories of motor vehicles. These rates can be amended by the Government.
The Act is subject to amendments and updates by the State Legislature.
Specific exemptions are often notified by the Government through notifications in the official gazette.

title: THE KERALA MOTOR VEHICLES (TAXATION OF PASSENGERS AND GOODS) ACT, 1963
purpose: To provide for the levy of a tax on passengers and goods carried in stage carriages and public carrier vehicles in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to stage carriages and public carrier vehicles in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.notification: Means a notification published in the Gazette.
key_definitions.operator: Means any person whose name is entered in the permit as the holder thereof.
key_definitions.permit: Means a permit granted or countersigned under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939 (Central Act 4 of 1939), authorising the use of a vehicle as a stage carriage or as a public carrier vehicle in any part of the State.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.public_carrier_vehicle: Means a motor vehicle carrying or adapted to carry goods for hire or reward.
key_definitions.stage_carriage: Means a motor vehicle carrying or adapted to carry more than 25 persons, excluding the driver, which carries passengers for hire or reward, at separate fares paid by or for individual passengers, either the whole journey or for stages of the journey, and includes such a carriage when used as a contract carriage within the meaning of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939.
key_definitions.tax: Means the tax referred to in section 3,
key_definitions.taxable_vehicle: Means a stage carriage, or a public carrier vehicle, which is referred to in section 3.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Motor Vehicles (Taxation of Passengers and Goods) Act, 1963, it extends to the whole of the State of Kerala, and it shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification, appoint.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as 'notification', 'operator', 'permit', 'prescribed', 'public carrier vehicle', 'stage carriage', 'State', 'tax', and 'taxable vehicle'.

main_sections.section_title: Levy of tax on passengers and goods
main_sections.description: Specifies that from the date of commencement of the Act, a tax shall be levied and paid on the Government's tax on all passengers, luggage and goods carried by stage carriages and on all goods carried by public carrier vehicles. It details the rates of tax per rupee on fares and freights payable to operators of stage carriages and operators of public carrier vehicles.
Allows the prescribed operator to permit him in circumstances and under conditions specified in the Act, to compound the tax payable by him in lieu of the fixed manner specified in the Schedule.

Requires every taxable vehicle, upon delivery of return to the officer in charge of any police station which lies on or in the neighbourhood of the route on which such vehicle is used and which is specified by the prescribed officer, in consultation with the operator, a return in the prescribed form, either daily or at such other intervals as may be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Tax to be paid every month into Government Treasury
main_sections.description: Mandates that the tax collected shall be paid every month into the Government Treasury.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure where no payment is made, etc.
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure to be followed when tax is not paid or when there is a deficiency in payment, including imposition of penalty.
Deals with situations where fares and freights have escaped assessment and the procedure for assessment in such cases.
Specifies penalties for non-payment of tax, including fines and potential prosecution.
Details the methods for recovery of tax, including distraint of goods and sale of movable property.

main_sections.section_title: Liability to payment of tax by persons acceding to the ownership, possession or control of motor vehicles
main_sections.description: Establishes the liability of persons who become owners, possessors, or controllers of motor vehicles to pay the outstanding tax.

main_sections.section_title: Restrictions on the use of taxable vehicles in certain cases
main_sections.description: Imposes restrictions on the use of taxable vehicles in certain circumstances, potentially involving permits and compliance with the Act.
Provides for the right to appeal against any demand for tax made under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power to order production of accounts
main_sections.description: Grants the prescribed authority the power to order the production of accounts by operators.
Defines offences related to the Act and specifies the penalties that can be imposed.
Lays down provisions for offences committed by companies under the Act.
Allows for the composition of certain offences under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Reduction of tax in cases of certain motor vehicles
main_sections.description: Permits reduction of tax in specific cases concerning certain types of motor vehicles.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to notify exemptions and reductions
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to notify exemptions from or reductions in tax for certain vehicles or classes of vehicles.
Confers power on the Government to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of the Act.
Restricts certain legal proceedings against the Government or its officers for actions taken in good faith under the Act.
Specifies the limitation period for suits and prosecutions instituted under the Act.
Repeals any previous enactment on the subject.

important_rules: Tax is levied at specific rates on passengers, luggage, and goods carried by stage carriages and public carrier vehicles.
The tax on passengers and goods shall be levied and paid from the date of commencement of the Act.
Operators of taxable vehicles are required to submit returns in a prescribed form.
Tax collected must be paid into the Government Treasury monthly.
Penalties will be imposed for non-payment of tax, evasion, or other contraventions of the Act.

penalties: Penalty for non-payment of tax (Section 9): Fines, potentially including double the amount of tax due, and imprisonment.
General penalties for offences (Section 15): Fines, imprisonment, or both.
Penalties for offences by companies (Section 16): Fines applicable to the company and responsible individuals.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Prescribed officers, police station officers, and the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment of tax, recovery proceedings, imposition of penalties, and prosecution for offences. The Government also has the power to make rules for enforcement and notify exemptions.

rights: Right to appeal against any demand for tax (Section 13).
duties: Duty to pay tax on passengers and goods carried.
Duty to submit returns as prescribed (Section 5).
Duty to pay collected tax into the Government Treasury monthly (Section 6).
Duty to comply with restrictions on the use of taxable vehicles (Section 12).
obligations: Obligation for operators to compound tax if permitted.
Obligation for persons acceding to ownership, possession, or control of motor vehicles to pay outstanding tax.

key_procedures: Procedure for levy and payment of tax on passengers and goods.
Procedure for submission of returns and payment into the treasury.
Procedure for assessment of escaped fares and freights.
Procedure for recovery of tax.
Procedure for appealing against tax demands.
administration: The State Government of Kerala and its prescribed authorities administer the Act.
important_notes: The Act received the President's assent on 11th April, 1963, and was published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 15th April, 1963.

Explanation 1 under Section 3 clarifies that for the purposes of this provision, 'export' shall not include movements of goods from one port in the territory of India to another port in the said territory.

Provided further in Section 3 that no tax shall be levied on any passenger, luggage or goods carried in a stage carriage, if the total distance permitted to be covered by such stage carriage in a day, does not exceed eighty kilometers.
Provided that two or more vehicles shall not be chargeable under this clause in respect of the same trailer in Schedule 3.
Tax payable in respect of such vehicles used for carrying goods other than trailers falling under Clause 5 of this Schedule.

title: The Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Act, 2005 (Act 24 of 2005)
purpose: To amend The Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976.
scope: Applies to motor vehicles in the State of Kerala. Specifically addresses amendments to the taxation of motor vehicles.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called The Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Act, 2005 and it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1976.

This section details the specific amendments made to the principal Act (The Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976). It clarifies that the amendments are made to Section 4 of the principal Act, concerning the levy of tax on motor vehicles. It also references the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Rules, 1975 and specific amendments made in 2005.

This section validates certain actions and assessments made under the principal Act or any other law previously in force, ensuring that these actions are considered legal and effective despite any potential flaws or omissions in the prior legal framework.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Enforcement authority is implied to be the State Government or its designated agencies responsible for motor vehicle taxation.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement would be through the mechanisms provided in the principal Act, including assessment and collection of taxes.

duties: Duty to pay motor vehicle tax as per the amended provisions of the Act.

key_procedures: Amendment of existing tax structures for motor vehicles.
Validation of past tax assessments and actions.
administration: The administration of this Act would fall under the purview of the Transport Department or a similar authority within the Kerala State Government, responsible for motor vehicles and their taxation.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on April 1, 1976, indicating retrospective effect for some provisions.
The amendments are specifically made to Section 4 of the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976.
The Act includes a validation clause to regularize past actions and assessments.

title: THE KERALA MOTOR VEHICLES TAXATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2005
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976, for specific purposes, including amendments related to contributions to the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Welfare Fund.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976, and its provisions concerning motor vehicles and taxation within Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Act, 2005, and it shall come into force on the 7th day of June, 2005.

Amends Section 4 of the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976. It inserts new sub-sections (7) and (8). Sub-section (7) deals with the collection of contributions to the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Welfare Fund from every registered owner or person having possession or control of a motor vehicle, before effecting payment of tax. Sub-section (8) states that no tax under the Act shall be collected unless the remittance of contribution towards the welfare fund mentioned in sub-section (7) is produced.

Repeals the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Ordinance, 2005 (8 of 2005). It also states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the Principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the Principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Contributions to the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Welfare Fund must be collected from registered owners or persons in control of motor vehicles before the payment of tax.
Tax under the Act will only be collected if the remittance of contribution to the welfare fund is produced.

duties: Registered owners or persons in control of motor vehicles have a duty to contribute to the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Welfare Fund.
Taxpayers have a duty to produce proof of remittance of welfare fund contributions to pay motor vehicle tax.

key_procedures: Procedure to pay motor vehicle tax: A motor vehicle owner or person in control must first make the required contribution to the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Welfare Fund and then produce the remittance receipt when paying the motor vehicle tax.
administration: Likely the Transport Department of the Kerala Government, responsible for motor vehicles and their taxation.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 12th day of August, 2005 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 1841, dated 12th August, 2005.
The Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Ordinance, 2005 (8 of 2005) has been repealed.

title: The Requisitioning and Acquisition of Property (Amendment) Act, 1961
purpose: To further amend the Requisitioning and Acquisition of Property Act, 1955, for the purpose therein appearing.
scope: The act applies to the State of Kerala and concerns the requisitioning and acquisition of property.

main_sections.description: (1) This Act may be called the Requisitioning and Acquisition of Property (Amendment) Act, 1961. (2) It shall come into force at once.
In sub-section (3) of section 1 of the Requisitioning and Acquisition of Property Act, 1955 (Act I of 1956), for the words "six years", the words "twelve years" shall be substituted.

important_notes: Received the assent of the President on the 4th day of January 1962 and published in the Gazette Extraordinary, dated the 9th day of January 1962.

title: The Kerala Municipal Corporations (Amendment) Act, 1975
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, 1961.
scope: Applies to Municipal Corporations in Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Municipal Corporations (Amendment) Act, 1975, and it shall come into force at once.
Amends section 43A of the Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, 1961, by substituting the words "six months" with "one year" in the proviso to sub-section (1) of section 43A.

important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 7th day of May, 1975 and published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 229 dated 7th May 1975.

title: THE KERALA MUNICIPAL CORPORATIONS (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 1975
purpose: An Act to provide for the extension of the term of office of the Mayor, Deputy Mayor and other Councillors and Members and Chairmen of Standing Committees of the Corporation of the City of Cochin.
scope: Applies to the Corporation of the City of Cochin.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Municipal Corporations (Second Amendment) Act, 1975. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 31st day of May, 1975.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of the term of office of Mayor, Deputy Mayor, Councillors, etc., of the Corporation of the City of Cochin
main_sections.description: Extends the term of office of the Mayor, the Deputy Mayor and other Councillors and the Member and Chairmen of Standing Committees of the Corporation of the City of Cochin until the 2nd day of June, 1975, which expires on the 2nd day of December, 1975.

main_sections.section_title: Act 30 of 1961 to be modified temporarily
main_sections.description: The provisions of the said Act shall, in relation to the Corporation of the City of Cochin, have effect subject to modifications concerning the government causing elections, the term of office of newly elected councillors, and the election of the Mayor and Deputy Mayor.

Repeals the Kerala Municipal Corporation (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1975. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the said Ordinance or under the said Act as modified by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

key_procedures: Section 1: Commencement of the Act on May 31, 1975.
Section 3: Modifications related to elections and terms of office in the Corporation of the City of Cochin.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 16th day of August, 1975 and published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 468 dated 16th August, 1975.

title: The Kerala Municipal Corporations (Amendment) Act, 1986
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, 1961, and for certain matters incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to Municipal Corporations in Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Municipal Corporations (Amendment) Act, 1986, and specifies its commencement date and the commencement dates for certain sections of the principal Act.

Amends sub-section (1) of Section 5 of the Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, 1961 (30 of 1961) by substituting the clause related to the council's composition and the fixation of the number of councillors based on population.
Amends sub-section (1) of Section 67 of the principal Act by omitting a proviso.

main_sections.section_title: Special provision for vesting of the functions of the council and of the Mayor, the Deputy Mayor and of the standing committees and other committees of the municipal corporations of the cities of Trivandrum, Cochin and Calicut in Government for temporary period.
main_sections.description: Provides for the temporary vesting of functions of the council, Mayor, Deputy Mayor, standing committees, and other committees of the municipal corporations of Trivandrum, Cochin, and Calicut in the Government. This vesting is for a period of thirty months from the date immediately succeeding the said date, or until the expiry of the office of councillors on September 30, 1984, whichever is earlier. The Government may exercise these functions through designated officers.

Repeals Sections 4 and 6 of the Kerala Municipal Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1986 (72 of 1986). It also includes a saving clause stating that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the said section 4 or under section 6 of the said Ordinance, as amended by this Act, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the corresponding provision of this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act and rules framed thereunder.

key_procedures: Amendment of existing sections of the Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, 1961.
Vesting of municipal corporation functions in the Government under specific circumstances.
Repeal of certain ordinances and saving provisions for actions taken under them.
administration: Law (Legislation-C) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, 1961.
Certain provisions related to the number of councillors and their fixation are amended.
A special provision addresses the temporary vesting of powers in the Government during a transitional period.
The Act repeals specific parts of an Ordinance and saves actions taken under it.

title: The Kerala Municipal Corporations (Amendment) Act, 1976
purpose: To provide for the further extension of the term of office of the councillors of the Corporation of the City of Cochin.
scope: Applies to the Corporation of the City of Cochin.

key_definitions.said Act: The Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, 1961 (30 of 1961).

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Kerala Municipal Corporations (Amendment) Act, 1976 and specifies that it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of December, 1975.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of the term of office of councillors of the Corporation of the City of Cochin
main_sections.description: Extends the term of office of the councillors of the Corporation of the City of Cochin, which was constituted under the Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, 1961, until noon on the 2nd day of December, 1975. This extension is notwithstanding anything contained in the said Act.

main_sections.section_title: Act 30 of 1961 to be modified temporarily
main_sections.description: Modifies the provisions of the Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, 1961, temporarily with effect from the date of the Ordinance. It outlines conditions for elections to be held, the term of office of newly elected councillors, and the election of the Mayor and Deputy Mayor.

Repeals the Kerala Municipal Corporations (Fourth Amendment) Ordinance, 1975. It also includes a saving clause, stating that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the said Ordinance or under the said Act as modified by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: The Act is deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of December, 1975.
The term of office of councillors of the Corporation of the City of Cochin is extended until noon on the 2nd day of December, 1975.
Elections for the council are to be held in a manner that ensures newly elected councillors may enter office on the 2nd day of June, 1976.
The term of office of the newly elected councillors shall expire at noon on the 2nd day of June, 1981.
The election of the Mayor, Deputy Mayor, and members of the standing committee shall be held at the first meeting of the council after the 2nd day of December, 1975.
Each standing committee shall, at its first meeting after the election referred to in clause (c), elect one of its members (other than the Mayor) to be its chairman.
key_procedures: Extension of term of office of councillors: The Act explicitly extends the term of office for councillors of the Corporation of the City of Cochin.
Temporary modification of the 1961 Act: Section 3 details how the Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, 1961, is temporarily modified concerning elections and terms of office.
Repeal of Ordinance and saving provision: Section 4 repeals a specific ordinance and ensures that actions taken under the repealed ordinance are considered valid under the current act.
administration: Likely administered by the Department of Local Self-Government, Government of Kerala, given the subject matter.
important_notes: The Act was received the assent of the Governor on the 15th day of March, 1976 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No 165, dated 18th March 1976.
The extension of the term of office is specifically for the councillors of the Corporation of the City of Cochin.

title: THE KERALA MUNICIPAL CORPORATIONS (FOURTH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1976
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, 1961, for the purpose hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to municipal corporations in Kerala, specifically amending the Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, 1961.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Municipal Corporations (Fourth Amendment) Act, 1976.

Amends section 15 of the Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, 1961. It specifies that certain figures and words ('354, 406, 425 and rules') are to be substituted with figures and words ('354 and 406 and rules') and shall be deemed to have always been substituted.

Provides that notwithstanding any judgment, decree, or order of any court, all delegations purported to have been made by the Commissioner of a municipal corporation, concerning his powers, duties, or functions specified in section 425 of the principal Act, before the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette, shall be deemed to be, and to have always been, valid and in accordance with law, as if such delegations were made under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Commissioner of a municipal corporation (implied through section 425 of the principal Act)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Delegations of powers, duties, or functions under section 425 of the principal Act.

administration: Not explicitly mentioned in this amendment, but likely the Municipal Corporations themselves and relevant government departments in Kerala.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 19th day of November 1976 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 540, dated 20th November 1976.
The amendment concerning section 15 is retrospective, meaning it is deemed to have always been in effect.

title: The Kerala Municipal Councils (Extension Of Term Of Office Of Councillors )Act, 1975

title: THE KERALA MUNICIPAL COUNCILS (EXTENSION OF TERM OF OFFICE OF COUNCILLORS) ACT, 1979
purpose: To provide for the further extension of the term of office of the councillors of municipalities other than the Changanacherry and Tirur Municipalities.
scope: Applies to the councillors of municipalities in Kerala, specifically excluding the Changanacherry and Tirur Municipalities. It also applies to the Kerala Municipal Councils (Extension of Term of Office of Councillors) Ordinance, 1978.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Municipal Councils (Extension of Term of Office of Councillors) Act, 1979, and it came into force on the 31st day of October, 1978.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of term of office of municipal councillors
main_sections.description: Notwithstanding anything contained in the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960, the term of office of the councillors of all the municipalities constituted under that Act, other than the Changanacherry and Tirur Municipalities, which expires on the 1st day of November, 1978, shall extend up to noon on the 1st day of October, 1979.

The Kerala Municipal Councils (Extension of Term of Office of Councillors) Ordinance, 1978 (21 of 1978), is repealed. However, notwithstanding this repeal, anything done or any action taken under the said Ordinance is deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: The term of office of municipal councillors (excluding Changanacherry and Tirur Municipalities) expiring on November 1, 1978, is extended until noon on October 1, 1979.
administration: The document implies administration by the State Government of Kerala, as it pertains to municipal councils within the state.
important_notes: The Act was received the assent of the Governor on the 29th March, 1979 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 228, dated 29th March, 1979.
The extension of term of office is explicitly stated to be for municipalities *other than* Changanacherry and Tirur Municipalities.

title: THE KERALA MUNICIPAL LAWS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1961
purpose: To provide for the further extension of the term of office of the councillors of municipalities and for the postponement of the reconstitution of the Changanacherry Municipal Council.
scope: Applies to municipalities and specifically mentions the Changanacherry Municipal Council.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Municipal Laws (Amendment) Act, 1961.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of term of office of Municipal Councillors
main_sections.description: Extends the term of office of municipal councillors, notwithstanding anything contained in the Madras District Municipalities Act, 1920 (Madras Act V of 1920), as in force in the Malabar District referred to in sub-section (2) of section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, the Travancore-Cochin District Municipalities Act, 1911 (XXIII of 1911), or the Cochin Municipal Act, XVIII of 1911. The government may, by notification in the Gazette, extend the term of office of the councillors of any municipality constituted under any of the aforesaid Acts, which expires at noon on the 1st day of April, 1961, up to such date not later than the 1st day of September, 1961, as may be specified in the notification.

main_sections.section_title: Postponement of the reconstitution of the Changanacherry Municipal Council
main_sections.description: Postpones the reconstitution of the Changanacherry Municipal Council, notwithstanding anything contained in section 45 of the Travancore-Cochin District Municipalities Act, 1911 (XXIII of 1911), and the subsequent notification published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 27th March, 1961.
Sections 4 and 5 of the Kerala Municipal Laws (Amendment) Act, 1960 (Act 23 of 1960), shall be omitted.
Repeals The Kerala Municipal Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1961 (Ordinance No. 3 of 1961).

important_rules: Municipal councillors' term of office can be extended by notification in the Gazette.
The extension of term is limited, not later than September 1, 1961.
Reconstitution of the Changanacherry Municipal Council is postponed.
Sections 4 and 5 of Act 23 of 1960 are omitted.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government (through Gazette notification)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By issuing notifications in the Gazette.

key_procedures: Government can issue a notification in the Gazette to extend the term of office of municipal councillors.
The notification must specify the new date for the expiry of the term, which cannot be later than September 1, 1961.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be managed by the relevant state government department responsible for municipal affairs.
important_notes: The Act amends existing Kerala Municipal Laws.
It specifically addresses the term of office of councillors and the reconstitution of a particular council (Changanacherry).
It repeals a previous ordinance (Ordinance No. 3 of 1961).

title: The Kerala Municipalities (Amendment) Act, 1978
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960.
scope: Applies to municipalities in Kerala.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it shall come into force on the 31st day of October, 1977.
Inserts a new section 54A into the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960, which deals with the power of the Government to postpone elections and reconstitution of councils, and the consequences thereof.

Repeals the Kerala Municipalities (Amendment) Ordinance, 1977, and provides that anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Government has the power to postpone the election or reconstitution of a council if it is satisfied that it is not expedient to conduct elections due to the expiry of the term of councillors.
In case of postponement, the Government may by notification in the Gazette, direct the Commissioner to perform all or any of the powers and duties of the council, chairman, and standing committee.
The Government may determine the relationship of any person appointed under subsection (2) with the Government, Collector, and Director.
The Government may reconstitute the council on the date specified in the notification or before it expires.
Assets and liabilities of the postponed council shall be transferred to the reconstituted council.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government and Commissioner
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications and direct action by the Commissioner.

rights: Right of the Government to postpone elections and reconstitute councils.
duties: Duty of the Government to ensure continuity of municipal administration.

key_procedures: Government issues notification for postponement of election/reconstitution.
Government directs Commissioner to perform council's duties.
Government determines relationship of appointed persons.
Government issues notification for reconstitution of the council.
Assets and liabilities are transferred to the reconstituted council.
administration: Municipal Administration Department (inferred)
important_notes: The Act has retrospective effect from October 31, 1977.
The Act repeals the Kerala Municipalities (Amendment) Ordinance, 1977.

title: The Kerala Municipalities (Amendment) Act, 1972
purpose: An Act to further amend the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to municipalities in Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Municipalities (Amendment) Act, 1972, and shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 8.
main_sections.description: Substitutes a new section 8 in the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960, regarding the term of office of councillors, which shall save as otherwise expressly provided, be five years commencing from the date the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint. It also specifies provisions for extending the term by six months and the filling of casual vacancies, including those arising from the efflux of time or for casual elections. It also addresses the condition that a councillor elected at a casual election shall hold office only so long as the councillor whose place he is elected would have been entitled to hold office if the vacancy had not occurred.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new sections for section 58.
main_sections.description: Substitutes new sections for section 58 of the principal Act. These new sections include 'Revision of electoral roll', 'Correction of entries in electoral roll', 'Inclusion of names in electoral roll', and 'Appeals'.

Amends section 62 of the principal Act by substituting the word 'removed' for 'suspended' and inserting 'and five years have not elapsed from the date of such dismissal or removal' after 'by the Government'.

Amends section 86 by substituting 'two hundred and fifty' with 'one thousand' in sub-section (1), and 'two thousand' and 'one thousand' with 'ten thousand' and 'one thousand' respectively in sub-section (2). It also substitutes 'two thousand' and 'ten thousand' with 'fifty thousand' and 'ten thousand' respectively in sub-section (3), and 'fifty thousand' with 'ten thousand' in sub-section (4).
Amends section 92 of the principal Act, omitting sub-sections (4) and (5).

Amends section 93 of the principal Act. In sub-section (1), it inserts a proviso stating that certain functions of the health officer regarding disciplinary control over municipal staff shall be exercised by the commissioner. It also omits 'or disciplinary' after 'commissioner's'.
Amends section 100 of the principal Act by substituting 'ten per cent of that portion' with 'fifteen per cent of that portion'.

Amends section 110 of the principal Act by inserting a new clause '(a)' after clause (a) in sub-section (1), relating to transacting business outside the limits of the municipality. It also omits 'pension or' in clause (b).
Inserts new sections 123A and 123B concerning the numbering of vessels, vehicles, and animals, and the seizure of vessels, vehicles, and animals without municipal numbers.

important_rules: The term of office of councillors shall be five years, commencing from the date the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

Casual vacancies in the office of councillors shall be filled by ordinary elections, which shall be fixed by the election authority within a period of two months immediately preceding the date of expiry of the term of office.
A casual election of councillors shall be held at a casual election which shall be fixed by the election authority to take place as soon as may be after the occurrence of the vacancy.
No casual election shall be held to fill a vacancy occurring within three months before the ordinary date of retirement and that such vacancy shall be filled at the next ordinary election.

A councillor elected at a casual election shall enter upon office forthwith but shall hold office so long only as the councillor in whose place he is elected would have been entitled to hold office if the vacancy had not occurred.

The electoral roll for a municipality shall, unless otherwise directed by the Government for reasons to be recorded in writing, be revised by the election authority in the prescribed manner by reference to such date as may be specified by the Government before each ordinary election to the municipal council.

The election authority shall, if satisfied that the applicant is entitled to be registered in the electoral roll, direct his name to be included therein, provided that if the applicant is registered in the electoral roll of any other municipality, the applicant's name shall be struck off from the electoral roll of that other municipality.

No amendment, transposition or deletion of any entry shall be made under section 58A and no direction for the inclusion of a name in the electoral roll of a municipality shall be given under this section, after the last date for making nominations for an election to that municipality and before completion of that election.
An appeal shall lie to such authority, within such time and in such manner as may be prescribed from any order of the election authority under section 58A or 58B.

The Commissioner may direct that a municipal number shall be affixed to every vessel or vehicle for which a licence has been granted under section 123 and that a token bearing a municipal number shall be kept by the owner of every animal for which a licence has been granted under that section.
No municipal number shall be required in the case of a vehicle to which a number has to be affixed under the provisions of the Kerala Hackney Carriage Act, 18 of 1963.
All numbers affixed or tokens issued under this section shall be entered in a book to be kept for the purpose in the municipal office.
The book referred to in sub-section (2) shall be open to the inspection of any person who pays any tax to the municipality, at all reasonable times, without the payment of any fee.

If a municipal number is not affixed to a vessel or vehicle or a token bearing a municipal number is not obtained in respect of an animal, in pursuance of any direction under section 123A, the commissioner may at any time seize and detain such vessel, vehicle or animal.
Provided that no vehicle other than a bicycle or tricycle shall be seized or detained when actually employed in the conveyance of any passenger or goods.

If the vessel, vehicle or animal seized and the tax due thereon paid, and a municipal number affixed or token obtained, as the case may be, within ten days from the date of seizure, the commissioner may direct that the vessel, vehicle or animal, as the case may be, shall be sold in public auction and the proceeds of the sale applied to the payment of the tax, if any, due on the vessel, vehicle or animal sold.

penalties: Seizure and detention of vessel, vehicle, or animal if municipal number is not affixed or token is not obtained (Section 123B(1)).
Sale of seized vessel, vehicle, or animal in public auction to recover due taxes (Section 123B(2)).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Commissioner
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Issuing directions, seizing and detaining, ordering public auction.

rights: Right to appeal against orders of the election authority under section 58A or 58B.
Right to inspect the book of affixed numbers/tokens upon payment of a fee.
Right for the owner to recover seized vessel, vehicle, or animal upon payment of due taxes and obtaining municipal number/token within ten days of seizure.
duties: Duty to affix municipal numbers to vessels and vehicles for which a licence is granted.
Duty to keep a token bearing a municipal number for every animal for which a licence is granted.
Duty to pay any tax due on a vessel, vehicle, or animal to reclaim it after seizure.
obligations: To have a municipal number affixed to a vehicle if required by the Commissioner.
To obtain a municipal number or token if directed by the Commissioner.

key_procedures: Revision of electoral roll: To be revised by the election authority in the prescribed manner by reference to such date as may be specified by the Government before each ordinary election.
Inclusion of names in electoral roll: Application to the election authority, which, if satisfied, directs inclusion. Applicant's name shall be struck off from any other municipality's roll.
Appeals: Appeal against orders of the election authority under section 58A or 58B to a prescribed authority within a prescribed time and manner.
Numbering of vessels, vehicles, and animals: Commissioner may direct affixing of municipal numbers to licensed vessels/vehicles and issuing tokens for licensed animals.

Seizure and sale of vessels, vehicles, animals without municipal numbers: Commissioner may seize and detain, and if due taxes are paid and municipal number/token obtained within ten days, may direct sale in public auction to recover taxes.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but the Commissioner and Election Authority are involved in administration and enforcement.
important_notes: The Kerala Agricultural Pests and Diseases Act, 1958 (17 of 1958) is hereby repealed.
The Act is an amendment to the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960.
Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 742, dated 11th December, 1972.

title: THE KERALA MUNICIPALITIES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1973 (Act 9 of 1973)
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960.
scope: Applies to the Municipalities in Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Municipalities (Amendment) Act, 1973. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

Amends section 56 of the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960 (14 of 1961). Specifically, it modifies sub-sections (1) to (4) and inserts new provisions regarding the division of municipalities into wards, the election of councillors, and the determination of wards for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. It also outlines provisions for omitting certain sub-sections and altering ward definitions.

important_rules: One councillor shall be elected for each ward.
All the electors in a ward shall be entitled to vote at an election in that ward.
Sub-sections (5) and (6) shall be omitted.
When the number of councillors to be returned by a ward is altered or shall be omitted.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By notification in the Gazette.

rights: Right to vote for electors in a ward.

key_procedures: Division of a municipality into wards.
Election of councillors for each ward.
Determination of wards for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Appointment of commencement date by Government notification.
administration: Government of Kerala
important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 303, dated 2nd April, 1973.

title: The Kerala Municipalities (Amendment) Act, 1961
purpose: To provide for the further postponement of the constitution of the Badagara Municipal Council and the re-constitution of the Changanacherry Municipal Council.
scope: Applies to municipalities within Kerala, specifically concerning the Badagara Municipal Council and Changanacherry Municipal Council.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Municipalities (Amendment) Act, 1961.

main_sections.section_title: Postponement of the constitution of the Badagara Municipal Council
main_sections.description: Provides for the postponement of the constitution of the Badagara Municipal Council. The Government, by notification in the Gazette, can fix a day not later than the 1st day of June, 1962, for the constitution of the council and the commencement of its functions, notwithstanding anything in section 412 or any other provision of the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960 (Act 14 of 1961).

main_sections.section_title: Postponement of re-constitution of the Changanacherry Municipal Council
main_sections.description: Provides for the postponement of the re-constitution of the Changanacherry Municipal Council. The Government, by notification in the Gazette, for reasons to be stated, can postpone the re-constitution up to such date not later than the 1st day of June, 1962, as may be specified in the notification, notwithstanding anything contained in section 54 of the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960 (Act 14 of 1961).
Repeals The Kerala Municipal Laws (Amendment) Act, 1961 (Act 8 of 1961) and the Kerala Municipalities (Amendment) Ordinance, 1961 (Ordinance No. 6 of 1961).

important_rules: Rule 1: The Act is to be cited as the Kerala Municipalities (Amendment) Act, 1961.
Rule 2: The Government has the power to postpone the constitution of the Badagara Municipal Council until a specified date not later than June 1, 1962.
Rule 3: The Government has the power to postpone the re-constitution of the Changanacherry Municipal Council until a specified date not later than June 1, 1962.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications in the Gazette.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: The Government can postpone the constitution/re-constitution of specified municipal councils by issuing a notification in the Gazette.
Procedure 2: The notification must specify the date on which the council will be constituted or re-constituted, which cannot be later than June 1, 1962.
administration: Implied to be the Department responsible for Municipal Administration in the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: * Published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 23rd November, 1961.

purpose: An Act to provide for the further postponement of the constitution of the Badagara Municipal Council and the reconstitution of the Changanacherry Municipal Council.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government

key_procedures: The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, for reasons to be stated in the notification, fix any day not later than the 1st day of October, 1962, to be the day on which the newly elected councillors of the Badagara Municipality may come into office.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, for reasons to be stated in the notification, postpone the reconstitution of the Changanacherry Municipal Council up to such date, not later than the 1st day of October, 1962, as may be specified in the notification.

title: THE KERALA MUNICIPALITIES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1963
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to municipalities within Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Municipalities (Amendment) Act, 1963. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the first day of April, 1963.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 99 of Act 14 of 1961.
main_sections.description: Amends section 99 of the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960 (Act 14 of 1961) by substituting specific phrases related to the annual value of lands or buildings. It also includes provisions for how the substitution should be applied and defines 'tenant'.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 100 of Act 14 of 1961.
main_sections.description: Amends section 100 of the principal Act, in sub-section (2), by substituting phrases related to the annual value of lands and buildings.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 101 of Act 14 of 1961.
main_sections.description: Amends section 101 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), by substituting specific phrases related to buildings used for educational purposes, charitable purposes, and residential quarters.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 102 of Act 14 of 1961.
main_sections.description: Amends section 102 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), by inserting specific phrases into the words 'when levied on their annual value' and 'under section (2) of section 99'.

penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications and the application of amended sections of the principal Act.

key_procedures: The Act details the procedures for amending specific sections of the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960, by providing the exact wording to be substituted or inserted.
administration: Local Self-Government Department or equivalent, responsible for municipal administration in Kerala.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on 10th October, 1963, and was published in the Gazette Extraordinary, dated 11th October, 1963.

purpose: To amend the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960.
scope: Applies to municipalities in Kerala. Specifically amends section 7 of the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960, concerning the definition of 'population' for the purpose of the first election to Municipal Councils.

key_definitions.population: For the purpose of the first election to the Municipal Councils of the State of Kerala to be held after the commencement of this Act, 'population' shall mean the population as ascertained on the basis of the figures of the 1961 Census, whether provisional or final.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Municipalities (Second Amendment) Act, 1961 and that it shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment to section 7 of the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960
main_sections.description: This section amends section 7 of the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960, by adding a proviso to sub-section (5) which defines 'population' for the purpose of the first election to Municipal Councils of the State of Kerala.

key_procedures: The Act comes into force immediately upon its enactment.
important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 21st December 1961.

title: THE KERALA MUNICIPALITIES (THIRD AMENDMENT) ACT, 1979
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Municipalities (Third Amendment) Act, 1979, and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1978.

Amends section 104 of the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960, by adding a proviso. The proviso allows the municipal council, for special reasons and by resolution, to extend the time for specific purposes, not exceeding one year in the aggregate.

Amends Schedule II to the principal Act, specifically sub-rule (1) of rule 9, by adding a proviso. This proviso states that where the period of five years specified in section 104 has been extended by the municipal council, the revision of assessment books shall be made by the Commissioner within the extended period.

Repeals The Kerala Municipalities (Third Amendment) Ordinance, 1979 (13 of 1979). It also states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Commissioner (mentioned in relation to assessment books)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amendments to the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960 and the provisions of this Act.

key_procedures: Extending time for specific purposes by municipal council through resolution (not exceeding one year in aggregate).
Revision of assessment books by the Commissioner within the extended period when time for five years specified in section 104 has been extended.
administration: Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960
important_notes: The Act was received the assent of the Governor on the 4th November, 1979 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 791, dated 4th November, 1979.
The amendments are made retrospective to April 1, 1978.

title: THE KERALA MUNICIPALITIES (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 1986
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to municipalities in Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Municipalities (Second Amendment) Act, 1986. Section 2 of this Act shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of September, 1984 and the remaining provisions shall be deemed to have come into force on the 30th day of September, 1984.
In section 8 of the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960 (14 of 1961) (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), in sub-section (1), the proviso shall be omitted.

main_sections.section_title: Spatial provision for vesting of the functions of Council, Chairman, Standing Committee and other committees of certain Municipalities in the Government for temporary period.
main_sections.description: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in the principal Act or in any rule or bye-law made thereunder or in any judgment, decree or order of any court, in the case of every municipality the term of office of the councillors of which expires on the 30th day of September, 1986, the President of the Council and its Chairman and the Standing Committee and other committees which comes into existence on that date shall be vested in the Government for a period of thirty months from the date immediately succeeding the date on which the functions so vested shall be exercised by the Government in accordance with such rules as may be prescribed by them in that behalf.
(1) Clause (a) of section 3 and section 5 of the Kerala Municipal Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1986 (72 of 1986), are hereby repealed.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By exercising the functions of the Council, Chairman, Standing Committee and other committees during a temporary period.

administration: The Government of Kerala
important_notes: Section 2 of this Act is deemed to have come into force on September 1, 1984.
Remaining provisions of this Act are deemed to have come into force on September 30, 1984.
The vesting of functions in the Government for certain municipalities is for a temporary period of thirty months from the date immediately succeeding the expiry of the councillors' term.
The Kerala Municipal Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1986 is repealed.

Actions taken under the Kerala Municipality (Amendment) Ordinance, 2011, are validated, provided they are consistent with the provisions of the Principal Act as amended by this Act.

Validation clause ensures continuity and legality of past actions taken under a previous ordinance.

title: THE KERALA MUNICIPALITY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2000
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Municipality and its governance.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Municipality (Amendment) Act, 2000 and that it shall come into force with immediate effect.

Amends section 19 of the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994. It modifies the wording regarding the meeting convened by the State Election Commission and the substitution of certain words. It also omits sub-section (4A).
Amends section 38 of the Principal Act. It substitutes certain words concerning the period for which the Chairperson or the person presiding may decide and provides that the proviso shall be omitted.
Amends sub-section (1) of section 69 of the principal Act by substituting certain words.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new section after section 69
main_sections.description: Inserts a new section, '69A. Review of final orders by the State Election Commission.' This section details the process of applying for review of orders passed under section 69, including timelines for submission of applications, obtaining copies of orders, and requirements for publishing notice of orders.
Amends section 89 of the Principal Act by substituting certain words related to the expiry of the period of the elected council.
Amends section 383A of the Principal Act by substituting the existing proviso with a new one related to building construction and the three-meter limit.
Amends sub-section (1) of section 407 of the Principal Act by substituting words and figures relating to dates.

Repeals the Kerala Municipality (Amendment) Ordinance, 2000 (4 of 2000). It also states that nothing done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Section 7 of the Act shall come into force at once and the remaining sections shall be deemed to have come into force on the 18th day of January, 2000.
Sub-section (2) of section 19 is amended to change the wording for 'Government' and 'State Election Commission'.
Sub-section (4A) of section 19 is omitted.
Proviso in sub-section (3) of section 38 is omitted.
Section 69A requires that any order issued by the State Election Commission under sub-section (1) shall be published in the Gazette and in two local newspapers having wide circulation.

The substituted proviso in section 383A states that no application for construction of the first floor or second floor or both upon a building, existing as on the date of coming into force of this Act, shall be subject to the three-meter limit.

Provided that when the part of the existing building is demolished for the implementation of any town planning scheme, it shall be in such a way as not to adversely affect the remaining portion of the building or the new additions made, and the complete responsibility regarding the safety and stability of it shall be on the owner of the building.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Election Commission (for review of orders under section 69A)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amendments to existing sections of the Principal Act and insertion of new sections, with specific procedures outlined for certain actions.

duties: Owner of a building has the duty to ensure safety and stability during demolition of existing buildings for town planning schemes.
obligations: An application for review under sub-section (1) of section 69A shall be submitted within fifteen days from the date of passing of the final order on which the complaint is based.

Any order issued by the State Election Commission under sub-section (1) of section 69A shall be published in the Gazette and in two local newspapers having wide circulation in the concerned Municipal area.

key_procedures: Review of final orders by the State Election Commission: An aggrieved party can apply for a review of an order passed by the State Election Commission under section 69 within fifteen days of the order. The application must be in writing, accompanied by a copy of the order, and submitted to the Commission. The Commission may permit the applicant to obtain a copy of the order. The Commission shall publish the final order in the Gazette and local newspapers.

Building construction: Applications for construction of additional floors on existing buildings are subject to a three-meter limit. Demolition for town planning requires ensuring safety and stability of the remaining structure.
administration: Kerala Municipality
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994.
Certain sections of this Act came into force on January 18, 2000.
The Kerala Municipality (Amendment) Ordinance, 2000 is repealed, and actions taken under it are deemed to be taken under this Act.

title: The Kerala Municipality (Amendment) Act, 2012
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994, for purposes related to waste management and restriction on plastic carry bags.
scope: Applies to Municipalities within Kerala. Specifically addresses owners/managers of specified establishments regarding waste management, and restricts the sale and management of plastic carry bags and covers.

key_definitions.Municipality: Refers to the local governing body established under the Kerala Municipality Act.
key_definitions.Secretary: Refers to the Secretary of the Municipality.
key_definitions.bio-degradable waste: Waste that can be decomposed by biological processes.
key_definitions.non bio-degradable waste: Waste that cannot be decomposed by biological processes.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and specifies the commencement dates for its different sections. Section 2 is deemed to have come into force on November 1, 2010, while other sections came into force on November 25, 2011.
Amends sub-section (1) of section 143A of the principal Act by substituting 'three months' with 'fifteen months'.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new sections after section 334
main_sections.description: Inserts new sections 334A and 334B into the principal Act. Section 334A deals with management of waste at source, and section 334B deals with restriction on plastic carry bags and covers and management of plastic wastes.

important_rules: Rule 1: Owners/managers of specified establishments (trade centers, hospitals, markets, etc., and houses with plinth area > 400 sq. m) must segregate bio-degradable and non bio-degradable waste at source.
Rule 2: Bio-degradable waste must be processed at source or nearby with permission, without causing pollution.
Rule 3: Agreements must be made for non bio-degradable waste, with provision for take-back and fees to the Municipality.
Rule 4: Waste water must be processed scientifically at source or through recognized agencies, and not allowed to flow into water bodies or drains.
Rule 5: New establishments must have waste processing systems at the time of construction. Existing establishments may be given up to one year to comply.
Rule 6: No institution or person shall sell plastic carry bags/covers at a price lower than the minimum fixed by the Municipality or give them free of cost.
Rule 7: Applicants for licenses intending to sell plastic bags/covers may be charged an additional fee.
Rule 8: Consumers must keep waste plastic bags and covers segregated from other wastes.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term not less than six months but not exceeding one year, and a fine not less than ten thousand rupees but not exceeding fifty thousand rupees, or both, for violating sub-section (1) of section 334A.
A fine of not less than one thousand rupees for each day of continuing violation of sub-section (1) of section 334A.
Penalties for violations related to plastic carry bags and covers are not explicitly detailed in the provided text, but enforcement by the Secretary is mentioned.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Municipality and its Secretary are responsible for enforcing the provisions of the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications, fixing minimum prices, collecting fees, requiring agreements, issuing permits/licenses, and imposing penalties for violations. The Secretary is empowered to lodge complaints against violators.

rights: Owners/managers have the right to process bio-degradable waste at a neighbouring place with written permission of the Secretary.
Owners/managers have the right to enter into agreements for non bio-degradable waste management and waste water processing.
The Municipality has the right to fix minimum prices for plastic carry bags and collect additional fees.
Consumers have the right to manage waste plastic bags and covers as per bye-laws.
duties: Duty of owners/managers to segregate, process, and dispose of waste scientifically and without pollution.
Duty of owners/managers to enter into agreements for non bio-degradable waste and waste water management.
Duty of Municipalities to fix minimum prices for plastic bags and take steps to ensure compliance.
Duty of consumers to segregate waste plastic bags and covers.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the Environment Protection Act, 1986 and its rules.
Obligation to ensure no pollution to water, air, and sound.
Obligation to obtain working permits, licenses, or building numbers only if waste processing systems are in place.

key_procedures: Procedure for waste management at source: Segregation, processing of bio-degradable waste, agreements for non bio-degradable waste, and scientific processing of waste water.
Procedure for obtaining working permits/licenses: Municipalities shall not grant permits/licenses to establishments lacking waste processing systems.
Procedure for selling plastic carry bags/covers: Municipality shall fix minimum price; no sale below this price or free of cost; potential for additional license fees.
Procedure for consumer waste management: Segregation of waste plastic bags and covers.
administration: The Law (Legislation-C) Department of the Government of Kerala is involved in the publication and notification of the Act.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994.
Certain provisions have retrospective effect from November 1, 2010, and November 25, 2011.
Compliance with the Environment Protection Act, 1986 (Central Act 29 of 1986) and its rules is mandatory.
Municipalities may issue notifications and make bye-laws for specific aspects of the Act.

scope: Applies to the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994, and its amendments.

penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal amendments and the enforcement of the principal Act.

scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and specifically to municipalities within the state.

key_definitions.municipality: As defined in the principal Act (The Kerala Municipality Act, 1994).
key_definitions.electoral roll: Refers to the electoral roll of the concerned constituency.

Sections 3, 4 and 5 are deemed to have come into force on 13th day of November, 2014, and the remaining sections on the date of publication in the Gazette.

This section allows non-resident Indians to register as electors in their place of residence in India, provided their passport is located in India.

It includes provisions regarding the registration of non-resident individuals and specifies that the registration of an individual as an elector in a constituency where their passport is located is permissible. important_rules: Non-resident Indians can register in the electoral roll of their place of residence in India if their passport is located in India.
No place within a municipal area shall be used for certain purposes without proper authorization or compliance with the Act.
Specific conditions and procedures related to electoral roll registration and municipal area usage must be adhered to.

penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994 and this amendment act, including potential legal actions or penalties for non-compliance.

rights: Right for eligible non-resident Indians to register in the electoral roll.
Right to use municipal areas in accordance with the provisions of the Act.
duties: Duty of the government to ensure proper implementation of electoral processes.
Duty of individuals and entities to comply with the provisions of the Act regarding municipal areas and services.
obligations: Obligation to amend the principal Act to address specific issues related to electoral registration and municipal governance.

key_procedures: Procedure for registration of non-resident Indians in the electoral roll, as outlined in section 77A.
Procedure for amending sections of the principal Act, as detailed in sections 3, 4, and 5 of the Amendment Act.
