The amendment addresses specific provisions related to non-resident Indians and electoral rolls, as well as other aspects of municipal administration.

title: THE KERALA MUNICIPALITY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2014
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994 for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994. Specifically deals with amendments to sections related to property tax, educational institutions, and the establishment of Abkari shops.

key_definitions.Abkari shop: means a toddy shop or a foreign liquor shop or an establishment having FL-9 licence or a bar hotel, under the Abkari Act, 1077 and the rules made thereunder.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Municipality (Amendment) Act, 2014 and that it shall come into force on 25th day of November, 2012.

Amends section 233 of the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994 (20 of 1994) by substituting sub-section (4) to include limits of rates of basic property tax fixed by the Government under sub-section (2) and the rates of basic property tax once determined by the Council subject thereto under sub-section (3) shall be in force for five years from the date on which they come into force and thereafter on completion of every five years. The revised rate of tax shall be in force for the next five years. Special provisions are made for buildings which are new, reconstructed and altered in usage. The Council shall revise the rates of basic tax in such a manner as to have an enhancement of twenty five per cent on the existing limits and rates by the completion of the period of every five years. Also amends sub-section (4) of section 235 of the principal Act to include buildings exclusively used for educational purposes and upto the level of Higher Secondary under the ownership of educational institutions having recognition of the Government and hostel buildings in which the students of such institutions reside.

After clause (b) of section 235 of the principal Act, the following clause shall be inserted, namely:- "(ba) buildings exclusively used for educational purposes and upto the level of Higher Secondary under the ownership of educational institutions having recognition of the Government and hostel buildings in which the students of such institutions reside.".

In section 447 of the principal Act, after sub-section (6) the following sub-sections shall be inserted, namely:- "(7) Notwithstanding anything contained in the Abkari Act, 1077 (1 of 1077) or in any other law for the time being in force, no person shall, without previous permission in writing of the Municipality and otherwise than in accordance with the conditions specified in the permission, establish an Abkari shop within a municipal area: (8) While granting permission to establish an Abkari shop near an educational institution or place of worship, the distance limit prescribed in the Abkari Act for the time being in force or the rules framed thereunder shall be complied with and the Municipality shall not grant permission to establish an Abkari shop within the said distance limit. (9) A Municipality shall be competent, in consideration of public peace or morality or on the grounds of convenience or nuisance to order shifting from one place to another or closing of an Abkari shop within a period not exceeding fifteen days, as may be directed in this behalf. (10) Notwithstanding anything contained in this section, the provisions of sub-sections (7) to (9) shall not be applicable to any Abkari shop existing on the 25th day of November, 2012, the date of commencement of the Kerala Municipality (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 2012 (64 of 2012), or, subject to all existing legal provisions for re-establishing the toddy shops existing on the said date, in the area within the boundaries allotted for establishing them."

The Kerala Municipality (Amendment) Ordinance, 2013 (39 of 2013) is hereby repealed. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Permission is required from the Municipality to establish an Abkari shop within a municipal area.
When granting permission for an Abkari shop near an educational institution or place of worship, the distance limit prescribed in the Abkari Act must be complied with.
A Municipality can order the shifting or closing of an Abkari shop within 15 days for reasons of public peace, morality, convenience, or nuisance.
Sub-sections (7) to (9) do not apply to Abkari shops existing on November 25, 2012.
Basic property tax rates, once determined, are in force for five years.
The Council shall revise rates of basic tax to enhance by twenty-five percent every five years.

rights: Right to property tax revision every five years.
Right to establish Abkari shops under specific conditions and permissions.
duties: Duty to obtain prior written permission from the Municipality to establish an Abkari shop.
Duty to comply with distance limits for Abkari shops near educational institutions or places of worship.
Duty of the Municipality to revise property tax rates.
obligations: Obligation to ensure public peace, morality, convenience, or to prevent nuisance when regulating Abkari shops.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining permission to establish an Abkari shop: Apply to the Municipality for written permission and adhere to specified conditions, including distance limits from educational institutions and places of worship.
Procedure for Municipality to order shifting or closing of an Abkari shop: Municipality can direct shifting or closing within 15 days for public peace, morality, convenience, or nuisance.
Procedure for property tax revision: Council shall revise rates of basic tax to enhance by twenty-five percent every five years on existing limits and rates.
Procedure for amendment of sections: Specific sub-sections are substituted or inserted into sections 233, 235, and 447 of the principal Act.
administration: Law (Legislation-C) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act comes into force on November 25, 2012.
Existing Abkari shops as of November 25, 2012, are exempt from certain provisions.
The Act repeals The Kerala Municipality (Amendment) Ordinance, 2013 (39 of 2013).

title: THE KERALA NAMBUDIRI ACT, 1958
purpose: To provide for the family management and partition of illom properties among Nambudiris.
scope: Applies to Nambudiris and their illom properties in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.illom: All the members of a Nambudiri joint family with community of property and includes a 'mana'.
key_definitions.anandaravan: Any member of the illom other than the karanavan.
key_definitions.karanavan: The oldest major male member of an illom in whom the right to management of its properties vests.
key_definitions.major: A person who has attained eighteen years of age.
key_definitions.minor: A person who has not attained eighteen years of age.
key_definitions.Nambudiri: Means a member of the Nambudiri Brahmins community and includes the members of the following communities, namely, Pottus, Adigale, Elayads, Moosads, Pitarans, Namburs, Nambissans, Unnis and Embrandiris (including Sivolli, Haviek and other similar Brahmins known and recognised as Nambudiris) who follow customs, manners and usages similar to those of the Nambudiris and who are not marumakkattayees, and members of such other communities who follow customs, manners and usages similar to those of the Nambudiris and who are not marumakkattayees, as may be notified by the Government from time to time in the Gazette.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Nambudiri Act, 1958. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'illom', 'anandaravan', 'karanavan', 'major', 'minor', and 'Nambudiri'.

main_sections.section_title: Proprietary right of members in illom properties.
main_sections.description: Every member of an illom, whether male or female, shall have an equal proprietary interest in its properties.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of Karanavan to keep accounts.
main_sections.description: The karanavan shall keep true and correct accounts of the income and expenditure of the illom. These accounts shall be available for inspection at the illom house by the major anandaravans once in a year throughout the month of February following such year and any such anandaravan may take copies of or extracts from such accounts.

No sale or mortgage of any immovable property of an illom and no lease of any such property shall be valid, unless it is executed by the karanavan for consideration, for illom necessity or benefit and with the written consent of the majority of the major members of the illom.

Subject to the other provisions of this Act and to any arrangement that may be entered into between the major members of the illom or any order of a Court of competent jurisdiction, the karanavan has the right to be in possession and management of the properties of the illom including the exercise of 'uraima' or such other rights over Devaswoms and other institutions vested in the illom.

main_sections.section_title: Debt contracted or transaction entered into by Karanavan when binding on illom.
main_sections.description: It shall be lawful for the karanavan to contract, or enter into, debts or transactions other than those falling under section 5, without the written consent of the majority of the members of the illom: Provided that the debts or transactions so contracted or entered into are for illom necessity or benefit.

The burden of proving illom necessity or benefit shall be on the purchaser, mortgagee, pledgee, or other alienee, or creditor, as the case may be. But the court may presume such necessity where the majority of the major members of the illom are parties to or have given their written consent to the transaction.

Every member of an illom, whether living in the illom house or not, shall be entitled to maintenance consistent with the income and the circumstances of the illom. Any member of an illom shall be entitled to get a separate allotment of properties of the illom for his or her maintenance, as the case may be, provided there is just and sufficient cause for such allotment.
Any karanavan may by a registered document give up his rights as karanavan.

main_sections.section_title: Receiver to be appointed when illom consists of minors only.
main_sections.description: Where an illom consists only of minor members, the principal civil court of original jurisdiction within the local limits of which it is situated may, on the application of any one interested in it, appoint on such terms as the court deems fit a receiver to manage its affairs till any one of the minor members attains majority.

main_sections.section_title: Right of Nambudiri female to recover the marriage expenses and dowry.
main_sections.description: Any Nambudiri female of an illom who marries, or any unmarried female member of an illom who has completed the age of fifteen years at the time of marriage marries with the consent of her guardian in marriage, a male belonging to her community shall be entitled to recover from the illom properties the reasonable expenses of such marriage as well as her marriage settlement.

main_sections.section_title: Right of member to claim partition.
main_sections.description: Any member of an illom, male or female, may claim to take his or her share of all the properties of the illom over which it has power of disposal and separate from the illom. A member of an illom separating from it under sub-section (1) shall be entitled to such share of the illom properties as would fall to him or her if a division per capita were made among all the members of the illom then living. No claim to separate from an illom made on behalf of a minor member shall be allowed by any court unless it is satisfied that such separation would be to the benefit of such minor.

Any member of an illom who has changed his or her religion may claim, or be compelled by any other member of the illom, to take his or her share of the illom properties and separate from the illom. The member who claims or is compelled to divide from the illom under sub-section (1) shall be entitled to such share of the illom properties as would fall to him or her if a division per capita were made among all the members of the illom then living.

main_sections.section_title: Character of property taken on partition.
main_sections.description: The share obtained by any member separating from an illom under section 13 or under section 14 shall be the separate property of such member.

The Travancore Malayalam Brahuns Act of 1106 (III of 1106), the Cochin Nambudiri Act, XVII of 1114 and the Madras Nambudiri Act, 1932 (XXI of 1933), as in force in the Malabar District referred to in sub-section (2) of section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (Central Act 37 of 1956), are hereby repealed.

important_rules: Rule 1: Sales, mortgages, and leases of illom properties require the karanavan's execution, consideration, illom necessity/benefit, and written consent of the majority of major members.
Rule 2: The karanavan must maintain true and correct accounts of illom income and expenditure, which are available for inspection annually.
Rule 3: Every member of an illom has an equal proprietary interest in its properties.
Rule 4: Any member of an illom can claim partition of their share of properties and separate from the illom.
Rule 5: Property obtained on partition becomes the separate property of the member.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The courts of law are implied to enforce the provisions of the Act, particularly in cases of disputes related to partition or appointment of receivers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings and court orders, such as appointing a receiver for an illom with only minor members, or enforcing the validity of property transactions.

rights: Right of every member to an equal proprietary interest in illom properties.
Right of major anandaravans to inspect illom accounts.
Right of any member to claim partition and separate from the illom.
Right of Nambudiri females to recover marriage expenses and dowry.
Right of a karanavan to possession and management of illom properties.
Right of a karanavan to contract debts or enter into transactions for illom necessity or benefit without majority consent under specific conditions.
duties: Duty of the karanavan to keep true and correct accounts of the illom.
Duty to obtain written consent of the majority of major members for sales, mortgages, and leases of immovable illom property.
obligations: Obligation to ensure that sales, mortgages, and leases are for illom necessity or benefit.
Obligation for the karanavan to manage properties including exercise of 'uraima' or other rights over Devaswoms and institutions vested in the illom.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: For Sales, Mortgages, and Leases: The karanavan must execute the transaction, it must be for consideration, serve illom necessity or benefit, and have the written consent of the majority of major members.
Procedure 2: For Account Inspection: Major anandaravans can inspect the illom accounts at the illom house annually and take copies or extracts.
Procedure 3: For Partition: Any member can claim to take their share and separate. If separating due to change of religion, they are entitled to a per capita share.
Procedure 4: For Appointment of Receiver: If an illom has only minor members, any interested party can apply to the principal civil court to appoint a receiver.
administration: The administration and enforcement of the Act appear to fall under the purview of the civil courts and the government through its gazette notifications.
important_notes: The Act repeals the Travancore Malayalam Brahuns Act of 1106, the Cochin Nambudiri Act, XVII of 1114, and the Madras Nambudiri Act, 1932.
The definition of 'Nambudiri' includes specific communities mentioned and others notified by the Government.
The burden of proving illom necessity for debts or transactions lies with the claimant, but courts may presume it if the majority of major members consented.
Maintenance of illom members is to be consistent with the illom's income and circumstances.
Separation from an illom on change of religion can be compelled by other members.

title: THE KERALA NON-TRADING COMPANIES ACT, 1961
purpose: To provide for the incorporation, regulation and winding up of companies, other than trading corporations, with objects confined to the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to companies incorporated under this Act, and existing companies with objects confined to the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.company: Means a company, other than a trading corporation, with objects confined to the State of Kerala, formed and registered under the Companies Act, 1956 (Central Act I of 1956), as modified by this Act for any existing company as defined in clause (2).
key_definitions.existing company: Means a company other than a trading corporation, with objects confined to the State of Kerala, formed and registered under any of the companies laws specified below, namely:
key_definitions.Registrar: Means the Inspector-General of Registration for the State of Kerala or such other officer as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint to be the Registrar for the purposes of this Act.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala, Non-trading Companies Act, 1961. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
This section defines key terms used in the Act, including 'company', 'existing company', and 'Registrar'.

main_sections.section_title: Application of the Companies Act, 1956 (Central Act I of 1956) to non-trading companies with objects confined to the State of Kerala
main_sections.description: Specifies that the Companies Act, 1956, will apply to non-trading companies with objects confined to the State of Kerala, subject to modifications mentioned in the Schedule.

Every existing company with its registered office in the State of Kerala shall be deemed to have been validly and lawfully registered as if this Act and Rules had been in force at the time of its registration, and shall be governed by this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of registration of non-trading companies under Central Act I of 1956
main_sections.description: Validates the registration of non-trading companies under the Central Act I of 1956, ensuring that such registrations are deemed to have been done under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of records relating to existing companies to Registrar
main_sections.description: Requires the transfer of records relating to existing companies from the offices of Registrars appointed under the Companies Act, 1956, to the Registrar appointed under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Construction of Companies Act as applied to the State
main_sections.description: Any court may construe the provisions of the Companies Act, 1956, as applied by this Act, with such modifications as may be necessary to adapt them to the matters before the court.

Repeals the Travancore Companies Act, 1114 and the Indian Companies Act, 1882, and the Indian Companies Act, 1913, and the Registration of Transferred Companies Ordinance, 1942, as far as they relate to companies, other than trading corporations, with objects confined to one State.

important_rules: Non-trading companies with objects confined to the State of Kerala are regulated by this Act and the Companies Act, 1956, with modifications.
Existing companies with objects confined to Kerala are governed by this Act.
Registrations of non-trading companies under the Central Act of 1956 are validated.
Records of existing companies must be transferred to the Registrar appointed under this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala (implied through notification powers and appointment of Registrar)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application of the Companies Act, 1956, as modified by this Act, and by the Registrar's authority.

duties: Companies must have objects confined to the State of Kerala.
Existing companies must be governed by this Act.
obligations: Transfer of records relating to existing companies to the Registrar.

key_procedures: Incorporation, regulation, and winding up of non-trading companies.
Application of the Companies Act, 1956, with modifications.
Validation of existing registrations.
Transfer of company records.
administration: Inspector-General of Registration for the State of Kerala (as Registrar).
important_notes: References to 'the Central Government' and 'Government' in the Companies Act, 1956, shall be construed as references to the Government of Kerala.
References to 'Parliament' shall be construed as references to the Kerala Legislature.
References to 'the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India' shall be construed as references to the Accountant-General, Kerala.
Certain sections and clauses of the Companies Act, 1956, are omitted or modified in their application to this Act.

Rules made by the High Court as aforesaid all rules on the matters referred to in this section in force at the commencement of this Act shall continue to be in force in so far as they are not inconsistent with the provisions in this Act in the High Court and in courts subordinate thereto.

title: The Kerala Official Language (Legislation) Amendment Act, 1973
purpose: To amend the Kerala Official Language (Legislation) Act, 1969, for the purposes hereinafter appearing. Specifically, to provide for the adoption of Malayalam and English as the languages to be used for the official purposes of the State of Kerala.
scope: The act applies to the State of Kerala and concerns the adoption of languages for official purposes.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Official Language (Legislation) Amendment Act, 1973.

For the long title to the Kerala Official Language (Legislation) Act, 1969 (7 of 1969), the following shall be substituted, namely: 'An Act to provide for the adoption of Malayalam and English as the languages to be used for the official purposes of the State of Kerala.'

For the preamble to the principal Act, the following shall be substituted: 'WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for the adoption of Malayalam and English as the languages to be used for the official purposes of the State of Kerala and to provide for the adoption of Malayalam also as a language to be used in Bills introduced in, or Acts passed by, the Legislature of the State of Kerala or in Ordinances promulgated by the Governor or in subordinate legislation.'
For sub-section (1) of section 1 of the principal Act, the following sub-section shall be substituted: '(1) This Act may be called the Kerala Official Languages Act, 1969.'

After section 1 of the principal Act, the following sections shall be inserted: '1A. Malayalam and English to be the official languages of the State—Without prejudice to the provisions of articles 346 and 347 of the Constitution, Malayalam and English shall be the languages to be used for all or any of the official purposes of the State. 1B. Government's power to notify the official purposes for which Malayalam or English to be used—The Government may, by notification issued from time to time, direct that Malayalam or English shall be used in respect of such official purposes as may be specified in the notification. 1C. Notification issued under section 1B to be placed before the Legislative Assembly—Every notification issued under section 1B shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is issued, before the Legislative Assembly, while it is in session for a total period of fourteen days which may be comprised in one session, or in two successive sessions, and if, before the expiry of the session in which it is so laid or the session immediately following, the Legislative Assembly makes any modification in the notification or decides that the notification should not be issued, the notification shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect, as the case may be; so however, that any such modification or annulment shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that notification ".

After section 2 of the principal Act, the following section shall be inserted, namely: '3. Special provisions in respect of linguist's minorities—Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, the following special provisions shall apply in respect of linguistic minorities in the State, namely: (a) The Tamil and Kannada minority people in the State may use their respective languages for their correspondence with the State Government in the Secretariat and the Heads of Departments and also with all the local offices of the State Government situate in those areas which are declared by the Government to be linguistic minority areas for the purpose and the replies sent in such cases shall also be in their respective minority languages. (b) The linguistic minorities other than Tamil and Kannada in the State may use the English language for their correspondence with the State Government offices and in such cases the replies sent to them shall be in the English language ".

important_rules: Malayalam and English shall be the languages to be used for all or any of the official purposes of the State.
The Government may, by notification, specify the official purposes for which Malayalam or English shall be used.
Notifications regarding official purposes must be placed before the Legislative Assembly for potential modification or annulment.
Special provisions exist for linguistic minorities (Tamil, Kannada, and others) regarding their correspondence with the State Government.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications issued by the Government and subject to the approval or modification by the Legislative Assembly.

rights: Linguistic minorities (Tamil, Kannada) have the right to use their respective languages for correspondence with the State Government and receive replies in their languages.
Other linguistic minorities have the right to use English for correspondence with the State Government and receive replies in English.
obligations: The Government has the obligation to table notifications regarding the use of Malayalam or English for official purposes before the Legislative Assembly.
The Government has the obligation to ensure that replies to correspondence from linguistic minorities are provided in the language requested, as per the special provisions.

key_procedures: Government issues a notification specifying official purposes for Malayalam/English usage.
The notification is laid before the Legislative Assembly for a specified period (14 days across one or two sessions).
The Legislative Assembly can modify or annul the notification.
If no modification or annulment occurs, the notification takes effect.
administration: The Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Kerala Official Language (Legislation) Act, 1969.
The Preamble is amended to reflect the adoption of Malayalam and English as official languages.
The amendment includes provisions for the use of Malayalam and English for all official purposes.
Special provisions are made to accommodate the linguistic needs of minority communities within the State.

title: The Kerala Official Language (Legislation) Act, 1969
purpose: To adopt the regional language for use in Bills, Acts, Ordinances and Subordinate Legislation in pursuance of Article 345 of the Constitution. This act is to provide for the adoption of Malayalam as a language to be used in Bills introduced in, or Acts passed by the Legislature of the State of Kerala or in Ordinances promulgated by the Governor or in subordinate legislation.
scope: Applies to Bills, Acts, Ordinances, and Subordinate Legislation introduced in or passed by the Legislature of the State of Kerala, or promulgated by the Governor, and to orders, rules, regulations, and bye-laws issued by the Government under the Constitution or under any law made by Parliament or the Legislature of the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Official Language (Legislation) Act, 1969 and that it shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Language to be used in Bills, etc.
main_sections.description: Specifies the language to be used in Bills to be introduced or amended in the Legislative Assembly of the State of Kerala; Acts passed by the Legislature of the State of Kerala; Ordinances promulgated by the Governor under article 213 of the Constitution; and Orders, rules, regulations and bye-laws issued by the Government under the Constitution or under any law made by Parliament or the Legislature of the State of Kerala. The language shall be Malayalam or English.

important_rules: Bills introduced or amended in the Legislative Assembly of the State of Kerala shall use Malayalam or English.
Acts passed by the Legislature of the State of Kerala shall use Malayalam or English.
Ordinances promulgated by the Governor under article 213 of the Constitution shall use Malayalam or English.
Orders, rules, regulations and bye-laws issued by the Government under the Constitution or under any law made by Parliament or the Legislature of the State of Kerala shall use Malayalam or English.
important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 48, dated 19th February 1969.

title: THE KERALA PUBLIC BUILDINGS (EVICTION OF UNAUTHORISED OCCUPANTS) AMENDMENT ACT, 1975
purpose: To amend the Kerala Public Buildings (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1968.
scope: The Act applies to public buildings in Kerala and deals with the eviction of unauthorized occupants from such buildings. The amendment specifically modifies section 2 of the Principal Act of 1968.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Public Buildings (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Amendment Act, 1975.

This section details the specific amendments made to section 2 of the Kerala Public Buildings (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1968. It modifies clause (d) by omitting the word "and" in item (i) and inserting it at the end of item (ii). It also inserts a new item (iii) after the amended item (ii), which refers to "all buildings, whether residential or non-residential irrespective of categories or types, constructed by individuals or co-operative societies or other institutions with the aid of any loan from the Government."

important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 12th day of May, 1975 and published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 239 dated 13th May, 1975.

title: THE KERALA PANCHAYAT RAJ (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1996
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, 1994.
scope: Applies to Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Panchayat Raj (Amendment) Act, 1996. Sections 2, 5, 6 and 7 of this Act shall come into force at once and Section 3 shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of October, 1995 and the other Sections shall be deemed to have come into force on the 16th day of February 1996.
Sub-section (3) of Section 149 of the principal Act is amended by substituting 'within three months' for 'within six months'.
In Section 160 of the principal Act, the words 'pay and allowances' are substituted for 'monthly pay and allowance', and the words 'and honorarium' are substituted for 'honorarium'.

Section 283 of the principal Act is amended by inserting a new sub-section (1) empowering the Government to amend schedules by notification, and a new sub-section (2) stating that no entry in any Schedule, shall be omitted except under the authority of a law enacted by the State Legislature.

Amendments related to 'Public Health and Sanitation' in the Third Schedule. Specifically, 'of all types of Primary Health Centres' are substituted for 'of Community Health Centres' in item (a) under heading '12. Public Health Centres'. Also, 'Management of Balavadies, Nursery Schools, Seasonal Day Care Centres and Dormitories for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes' is inserted as item (j) under heading '14. Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes'.

Amendments related to 'Public Health' and 'Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes' in the Fourth Schedule. 'of Community Health Centres' is substituted for 'of Primary Health Centres' in item (a) under heading '4. Public Health'. Item (f) is omitted. 'control of Pre-matric Hostels.' is added as item (h) under heading '6. Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes'.
Amendments related to 'Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes' in the Fifth Schedule. Item (b) under heading '13. Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes' is amended.

The Kerala Panchayat Raj (Amendment) Ordinance, 1996 (3 of 1996) is repealed. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By notification in the Gazette.

key_procedures: Sections 2, 5, 6, and 7 of this Act come into force on specific dates, with Section 3 deemed to have come into force on October 1, 1995, and other sections on February 16, 1996.
The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make additions to the entries in a Schedule to this Act.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be under the purview of the State Legislature and the Kerala Government.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 26th day of March 1996 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 1054 dated 27th March, 1996.
The Kerala Panchayat Raj (Amendment) Ordinance, 1996 (3 of 1996) is repealed.
Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are deemed to have been taken under this Act.

title: The Kerala Panchayat Raj (Amendment) Act, 2009
purpose: An Act to further amend the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, 1994, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Panchayat Raj system, as amended by this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Panchayat Raj (Amendment) Act, 2009 and shall come into force at once.
Amends section 6 of the principal Act by substituting specific phrases related to numerical thresholds (e.g., 'less than twelve or more than twenty two').
Amends section 7 of the principal Act by substituting 'One-third' with 'fifty per cent' in specific clauses.
Amends section 8 of the principal Act by substituting 'One-third' with 'fifty per cent' in specific clauses.
Amends section 9 of the principal Act by substituting 'One-third' with 'fifty per cent' in specific clauses.

Inserts a new clause (aa) after clause (a) in sub-section (1) of section 34. This clause deals with community certificates produced before the Returning Officer or declaration submitted with the nomination paper for contesting seats reserved for Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes, and the time limit for such declarations. It also amends clause (g) by substituting 'the Panchayat concerned' with 'any Local Self Government Institution'.

Inserts a new clause (aa) after clause (a) in sub-section (1) of section 35, similar to the amendment in section 34 regarding community certificates. It also amends clause (f) and its explanation, and clause (i) concerning references to 'the Panchayat concerned' and 'any Local Self Government Institution'.
Amends section 49 of the principal Act by substituting 'the twentieth day' with 'the fourteenth day' in clause (d).
Amends sub-section (2) of section 52 by substituting specific wording related to nomination papers and community certificates for reserved seats.
Inserts new clauses into section 138 of the principal Act, relating to refusal to grant leave to a person entitled to leave and the consequences of non-compliance.

Inserts a new section 145A titled 'Grant of paid holiday to employees on the day of general election'. This section states that every person engaged in work in any trade establishment or industrial establishment or in any other establishment in the private sector who is eligible to vote in the Panchayat election shall be granted leave on the day of general election. It also specifies that wages of such persons shall not be reduced or disallowed on account of the leave granted, provided they are not ordinarily paid for such date. It also outlines a condition where if the absence of the voter may be injurious or causes substantial loss to the work, it can be engaged.

Amends section 153 of the principal Act by substituting 'One-third' with 'Fifty per cent' in specific clauses and inserting new clauses related to eligibility for election to the office of President or Vice-President based on community and the procedure for declaration of membership.

Amends Section 162 of the principal Act, concerning Standing Committees. It makes changes to the nomenclature of Standing Committees, reserves seats for women in every Standing Committee, and stipulates that elected members of the Panchayat, except the President and Vice-President, shall be elected members of any of the Standing Committees. It also omits sub-section (3) and inserts new sub-sections (4) and (5) concerning the election of members to each Standing Committee under the guidance of the State Election Commission and the designation of an officer or institution to be the Returning Officer. It further specifies provisions for the Vice-President being reserved for women.

penalties: Punishable with a fine up to five hundred rupees for contravening the provisions of the new section 145A.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Returning Officer, competent officer, State Election Commission, Government or Local Self Government Institution.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amendments to existing sections and insertion of new sections that define specific procedures, eligibility criteria, and penalties for non-compliance.

rights: Right to grant paid holiday for employees to vote in Panchayat elections.
Right to be elected as member of Standing Committee (with reservation for women).
duties: Duty of employers to grant paid holiday for employees to vote.
Duty to produce community certificates and declarations as per stipulated procedures.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the amended provisions of the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, 1994.
Obligation to follow procedures for contesting reserved seats and for the election of Standing Committee members.

key_procedures: Procedure for producing community certificates before the Returning Officer for contesting reserved seats.
Procedure for granting paid holiday to employees on the day of general election.
Procedure for election of members to Standing Committees under the guidance of the State Election Commission.
Procedure for declaration of membership of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
administration: Kerala Panchayat Raj Department, State Election Commission, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, 1994.
The amendments pertain to various sections, including those related to reservations, elections, and administrative procedures.
Specific time limits and conditions apply to community certificates and declarations.
Provisions are made for women's representation in Standing Committees and for the office of Vice-President.
Special provisions are made for granting paid holidays to employees to exercise their right to vote in Panchayat elections.

title: The Kerala Panchayat Raj (Amendment) Act, 2012
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, 1994.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, 1994, and its provisions.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Panchayat Raj (Amendment) Act, 2012, and it is deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of November, 2010.
Amends section 159 of the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, 1994, by substituting the words 'three months' with 'fifteen months'.

Repeals the Kerala Panchayat Raj (Amendment) Ordinance, 2012 (45 of 2012). It also states that any repeal or action taken under the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the Principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_notes: The Act was received the assent of the Governor on the 9th day of January 2013 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 92 dated 10th January, 2013.
The Act further amends the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, 1994.
The Preamble indicates that it is expedient to further amend the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, 1994.

title: The Kerala Panchayat Raj (Amendment) Act, 2013
act_number: Not explicitly visible as a single act number, but referenced by publication date and Gazette numbers.
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, 1994, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: The act applies to the Kerala Panchayat Raj system.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Panchayat Raj (Amendment) Act, 2013, and specifies its commencement dates.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 2 of Act 20 of 1994.
main_sections.description: Amends section 2 of the principal Act. It seems to replace the word "twice" with "thrice" in a sub-section related to the Act's enforcement or application.

title: THE KERALA PANCHAYATS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1969
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960.
scope: Applies to Kerala. Specifically addresses amendments to the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960. The amendments relate to land cess, land belonging to Panchayats, and recovery of excess land cess paid or collected.

main_sections.description: States that the Act is called The Kerala Panchayats (Amendment) Act, 1969, and that it will come into force on the 15th day of August, 1961. It also specifies that it relates to the insertion of new section 66A in the Travancore-Cochin Area of the State and on the 1st day of April, 1958 in the area comprised in the Malabar District, referred to in sub-section (2) of section 3 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (Central Act 37 of 1956). The remaining provisions of this Act shall come into force at once.
Refers to section 65 of the principal Act and states that in sub-section (2) thereof, for the words 'hereinafter referred to as the principal Act', the words 'shall be deemed to have been omitted'.

Inserts new sections 66A and 66B into the principal Act. Section 66A deals with 'Land Cess' and states that it shall be levied on every land in a Panchayat area, other than any land or class of lands which the Government may, in public interest, exempt by notification in the Gazette, at the rate of one sixteenth per centum of the capital value of the land and the cess so levied shall be payable by the owner of the land. It also states that nothing in this sub-section shall be deemed as authorising the levy of land cess in any Panchayat area in respect of any particular period during which such cess was not being levied in that Panchayat area prior to the 1st day of January, 1962. Furthermore, the Government may make rules providing for the manner of ascertaining the capital value of the lands for the purposes of sub-section (1).

Refers to section 117 of the principal Act and states that the following proviso shall be added, namely: 'Provided that, for the purposes of the recovery of the land cess levied under section 66A for the period before the date of commencement of such section, suit, set off, or prosecution may be instituted or commenced at any time before the expiration of a period of three years from that date.'

important_rules: Rule regarding the levy of land cess: It shall be levied on every land in a Panchayat area, other than exempted lands, at the rate of one sixteenth per centum of the capital value of the land and payable by the owner.
Rule on the period for which land cess can be levied: Nothing in section 66A authorizes the levy of land cess for any period prior to January 1, 1962, if it wasn't being levied then.

Rule on recovery of excess land cess: Land cess paid or collected in excess under sub-section (2) of section 66A can be recovered by the executive authority within ninety days from the date of communication of the order levying the land cess. This order must have been communicated to him for such refund.

Rule on recovery of land cess under section 66A: Recovery of land cess levied under section 66A for the period before the commencement of the Act can be initiated through suit, set off, or prosecution within three years from the date of commencement.

penalties: Recovery of excess land cess paid or collected (as per section 66B (2) and (3))
Provisions for suit, set off, or prosecution for recovery of land cess for the period before commencement of the Act (as per amended section 117)
