penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through recovery of excess land cess, or through suit, set off, or prosecution for recovery of past land cess.

rights: Right to have excess land cess paid or collected refunded (Section 66B (2) and (3))
duties: Duty to pay land cess levied under section 66A (Section 66A (1))
Duty to have capital value of land ascertained for land cess purposes (if rules are made by Government)
obligations: Obligation to pay land cess by the owner of the land.

key_procedures: Ascertaining capital value of land: The Government may make rules for the manner of ascertaining the capital value of lands for the purposes of levying land cess.

Recovery of excess land cess: If land cess is paid or collected in excess of the amount that would have been payable under sub-section (2) of section 66A, the excess amount shall be refunded to the person who paid such excess. This refund is to be made by the Executive Authority of the Panchayat within ninety days from the date on which the order levying the land cess payable under this Act was communicated to him, and no claim for such refund shall be entertained thereafter.

Recovery of past land cess: For the purposes of recovery of land cess levied under section 66A for the period before the date of commencement of this Act, suit, set off, or prosecution may be instituted or commenced at any time before the expiration of a period of three years from that date.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be the Panchayats and the State Government (for rule-making and notifications).
important_notes: The commencement date for certain provisions is August 15, 1961, for the Travancore-Cochin Area, and April 1, 1958, for the Malabar District.
Government has the power to exempt certain lands or classes of lands from land cess in public interest.
Rules for ascertaining capital value of lands can be made by the Government.
A time limit of three years from the commencement date of the Act is provided for initiating recovery proceedings for land cess levied before the commencement of the Act.

title: THE KERALA PANCHAYATS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1978
purpose: To amend the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960, and its provisions related to the election of members to wards.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Panchayats (Amendment) Act, 1978. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 31st day of August, 1977.

This section details amendments to Section 10 of the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960. It includes changes to the wording regarding reserved seats and the substitution of certain clauses. Specifically, it modifies the text related to "as many wards as there are non-reserved seats" and provides for substituting certain subsections and clauses. The amendments also include provisions for how electors of a ward shall be entitled to vote and what happens when the number of members to be returned by a ward is altered.

This section repeals the Kerala Panchayats (Amendment) Ordinance, 1977 (15 of 1977). It also states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the Principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the Principal Act as amended by this Act.

rights: Electors of a ward shall be entitled to vote at an election in that ward.

important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 16th day of March 1978 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 183 dated 17th March, 1978.

title: The Kerala Panchayats (Amendment) Act, 1971
purpose: To amend The Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960, for the purpose hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960 and related provisions.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called The Kerala Panchayats (Amendment) Act, 1971. It also specifies the commencement dates for different sections: section 3 of Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960 comes into force on August 15, 1958 in Travancore-Cochin area and April 1st, 1958 in Malabar area, and section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956. Sections 4 and 5 shall come into force on December 18, 1970, and remaining provisions come into force at once.

Replaces section 7 of The Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960. The new section mandates reservation of seats for members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in every panchayat. It also states that notwithstanding anything contained in the sub-section, provisions relating to reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in Panchayats shall cease to have effect upon the expiration of the period fixed in the Constitution of India for reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the State Legislative Assembly.
Inserts the word "annually" in section 66A of the principal Act, in the opening paragraph, after the words "there shall be levied".

Amends section 76 of the principal Act. In the opening paragraph, it makes substitutions regarding moneys received by the Panchayat, calls for a fund to be constituted under the Panchayat Act and applied for the purpose for which said fees are levied. It also makes substitutions for the words "with due regard to the expenditure to be incurred for rendering service to the trade" and "for the regulation of the trade, for which the licence or permission is granted" in sub-section (2)(i). Additionally, it inserts a new sub-section (3) regarding all fees for licences and permissions received by the panchayat under this Act or any other law shall be kept separate from the panchayat fund constituted under sub-section (1) and shall be utilised for the purpose for which the said fees are levied.

Amends section 109, in sub-section (2), by substituting the words "with the approval of the Director", the words "with due regard to the expenditure to be incurred for rendering service to the trade and for the regulation of the trade, for which the licence or permission is granted".

States that notwithstanding the expiry of The Kerala Panchayats (Amendment) Ordinance, 1970 (Ordinance No. 21 of 1970): (a) anything done or any action taken in exercise of any powers conferred by or under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken in exercise of the powers conferred by or under the corresponding provision of this Act; (b) anything done or any action taken after such expiry and before the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette which could have been done or taken under the said Ordinance if it had not expired, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act; (c) any investigation, legal proceedings or remedy which could have been instituted, continued or enforced under the said Ordinance if it had not expired, may be instituted, continued or enforced under the corresponding provision of this Act. It also states that the expiry of the Kerala Panchayats (Amendment) Ordinance, 1970, shall not affect: (a) any affect any right, privilege, obligation or liability acquired, accrued or incurred under the said Ordinance; (b) affect any penalty or punishment incurred in respect of any offence committed under the said Ordinance; or (c) affect any investigation, legal proceedings or remedy in respect of any such right, privilege, obligation, liability, penalty, or punishment and any such investigation, legal proceeding or remedy may be instituted, continued, or enforced under the provisions of this Act. It further states that notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, no person shall be convicted of any offence under this Act for having committed the same after the 22nd April, 1971, and before the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette.

penalties: Any penalty or punishment incurred in respect of any offence committed under the said Ordinance (Kerala Panchayats (Amendment) Ordinance, 1970) shall not be affected by the expiry of the Ordinance.

rights: Reservation of seats for members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in every panchayat.
duties: Fees collected for licences and permissions by the Panchayat under this Act or any other law for the time being in force, shall constitute a fund called the panchayat fund and shall be applied and disposed of in accordance with the provisions of this Act and such other law.

administration: The Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960, administered by the relevant department of the Kerala Government.
important_notes: Section 3 of The Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960 comes into force on August 15, 1958 in the Travancore-Cochin area of the State and on the 1st day of April, 1958 in the area comprised in the "Malabar District" referred to in sub-section (2) of section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (Central Act 37 of 1956).
Sections 4 and 5 of The Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960 shall come into force on the 18th day of December, 1970.
The remaining provisions of this Act shall come into force at once.
Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 257, dated 27th May, 1971.

title: THE KERALA PANCHAYATS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1962
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960, for the purposes hereinafter appearing and to provide for hearing of objections before division of panchayat areas into wards.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960 and its provisions regarding division of panchayat areas into wards and related matters.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Panchayats (Amendment) Act, 1962, and it shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 10 of Act 32 of 1960
main_sections.description: Amends section 10 of the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960 (Act 32 of 1960) regarding the division of panchayat areas into wards. It modifies the opening portion and allows for the Deputy Director to hear objections and make modifications.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 130 of Act 32 of 1960
main_sections.description: Amends section 130 of the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960 (Act 32 of 1960) by substituting the words "All notifications and rules" for "All rules".

main_sections.section_title: Revision of orders dividing panchayat areas into wards
main_sections.description: Provides for the revision of orders dividing panchayat areas into wards, including notification of such divisions, hearing of objections, and modification of proposals by the Deputy Director of Panchayats.

important_rules: The Deputy Director of Panchayats shall, as soon as may be, after the date specified in section 4(1), after hearing the objections and suggestions, if any, received by them, pass such orders thereon as they consider necessary and modify the division of panchayats accordingly.

The Deputy Directors of Panchayats shall publish in the prescribed manner the division of panchayat areas into wards as modified under section 4(2), or where there has been no modification, the division as originally published, and the division so published, shall, subject to the provisions of sub-section (4) be deemed to be division for the purpose of divisions of the Panchayats.

The Government may at any time call for the records connected with the division of a panchayat area into wards from the Deputy Director of Panchayats for the purpose of satisfying themselves of the legality, regularity or property of any order passed or proceedings taken in the said matter by the Deputy Director of Panchayats and pass such orders thereon as they may deem fit.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Deputy Director of Panchayats, Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the process of hearing objections, passing orders, publishing divisions, and the Government's power to call for records and pass orders.

rights: Right to raise objections and provide suggestions regarding the division of panchayat areas into wards.
duties: Duty of the Deputy Director of Panchayats to publish the division of panchayat areas into wards.
Duty of the Deputy Director of Panchayats to consider objections and suggestions.
obligations: Obligation of the Government to be satisfied with the legality, regularity, or property of orders passed by the Deputy Director of Panchayats.

key_procedures: Process for division of panchayat areas into wards involves publication, hearing of objections, passing of orders by the Deputy Director, and subsequent publication of the final division.
Procedure for revision of orders dividing panchayat areas into wards, including proposal of modification and approval by the Deputy Director.
Government's procedure to call for records from the Deputy Director of Panchayats to ensure legality and regularity of orders.
administration: Department of Panchayats, Government of Kerala
important_notes: This Act is an amendment to the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960 (Act 32 of 1960).
The Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary, dated the 2nd May 1962.

title: THE KERALA PANCHAYATS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1968
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960 and its provisions related to electoral rolls and nominations.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Panchayats (Amendment) Act, 1968.

Amends section 8 of the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960 (32 of 1960) by inserting a new sub-section (4) concerning the rights of a woman member nominated before the commencement of section 3 of the Kerala Panchayats (Amendment) Act, 1967 (22 of 1967) and holding office as such member immediately before such commencement.

Amends section 14 of the principal Act by substituting new words and figures for the words "Every person" in sub-section (1), specifically for provisions related to sections 15, 15A, 15B and 15C, where every person shall be substituted.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new sections for section 15.
main_sections.description: Substitutes new sections for section 15 of the principal Act. This includes provisions for revision of electoral rolls (section 15), correction of entries in electoral rolls (section 15A), inclusion of names in electoral rolls (section 15B), and appeals related to electoral rolls (section 15C).

Repeals the Kerala Panchayats (Amendment) Ordinance, 1968 (4 of 1968). It also includes a saving clause stating that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act, as if this Act had come into force on June 15, 1968.

important_rules: Rule: Nothing contained in section 3 of the Kerala Panchayats (Amendment) Act, 1967 shall be deemed to affect the rights of a woman member nominated before its commencement and holding office as such member immediately before the commencement of that Act. (Section 8(4))

Rule: Electoral roll for a Panchayat area shall, unless otherwise directed by the Government for reasons to be recorded in writing, be revised in the prescribed manner by reference to such date as may be specified by the Government, before each ordinary election to the Panchayat. (Section 15(1))

Rule: The electoral roll as revised under sub-section (1) shall be the electoral roll for the purposes of any ordinary or casual election to the Panchayat and shall be in force until the electoral roll for the Assembly Constituency as relates to the Panchayat area or any portion thereof is revised in pursuance of the provisions of the Representation of the People Act, 1950. (Section 15(2))

Rule: If the election authority, for a Panchayat area, on application made to it or on its own motion, is satisfied after such enquiry as it thinks fit, that any entry in the electoral roll of the Panchayat area is erroneous or defective in any particular, it should be transposed to another place in the roll or should be deleted from the ground that the person concerned has changed his place of ordinary residence within the Panchayat area, or is otherwise not entitled to be registered in that roll. (Section 15A(a), 15A(b), 15A(c))

Rule: Before taking any action under clause (a) or clause (b) or any action under clause (c) on the ground that the person concerned has ceased to be ordinarily resident in the Panchayat area or that he is otherwise not entitled to be registered in the electoral roll of that Panchayat area, the election authority shall give the person concerned a reasonable opportunity of being heard in respect of the action proposed to be taken in relation to him. (Section 15A proviso)
Rule: Any person whose name is not included in the electoral roll of a Panchayat area may apply to the election authority for the inclusion of his name in that roll. (Section 15B(1))
Rule: If the election authority, if satisfied that the applicant is entitled to be registered in the electoral roll, shall direct his name to be included therein. (Section 15B(2))

Rule: Provided that if the applicant is registered in the electoral roll of any other Panchayat area, the applicant's name shall be struck off from the electoral roll of that other Panchayat area. (Section 15B(2) proviso)

Rule: No amendment, transposition or deletion of any entry shall be made under section 15A and no direction for the inclusion of a name in the electoral roll of a Panchayat shall be given under this section, after the last date for making nominations for an election to that Panchayat and before the completion of that election. (Section 15B(3))
Rule: An appeal shall lie to such authority, within such time and in such manner as may be prescribed, from any order of the election authority under section 15A or section 15B. (Section 15C(1))

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Election authority, prescribed authority for appeals.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Revision, correction, transposition, deletion, and inclusion of entries in electoral rolls. Appeals against orders of the election authority.

rights: Right of a nominated woman member to hold office under certain conditions.
Right to have an entry in the electoral roll corrected, transposed, or deleted if erroneous or if no longer entitled.
Right to apply for inclusion of name in the electoral roll if entitled.
Right to appeal against orders of the election authority regarding electoral rolls.
obligations: Obligation to revise electoral rolls before each ordinary election.
Obligation for the election authority to provide an opportunity of being heard before making certain changes to electoral roll entries.

key_procedures: Procedure for revision of electoral rolls: Unless otherwise directed by the Government, electoral rolls for Panchayat areas are to be revised in a prescribed manner by reference to a specified date before each ordinary election.

Procedure for correction of entries in electoral rolls: If an election authority is satisfied that an entry is erroneous or defective, it can transpose or delete the entry after proper inquiry, provided the person concerned is given an opportunity to be heard.

Procedure for inclusion of names in electoral rolls: Any person not included in the electoral roll can apply to the election authority for inclusion, which shall be directed if the applicant is entitled. However, if the applicant is registered elsewhere, their name will be struck off from the other roll. No changes are permitted after the nomination deadline and before election completion.
Procedure for appeals: An appeal against an order of the election authority under sections 15A or 15B can be filed with a prescribed authority within a prescribed time and manner.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but implies administration by the Kerala government and its election authorities.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960.
The amendments relate to sections 8, 14, and 15 of the principal Act.
A specific provision addresses the rights of nominated women members.
The Act repeals the Kerala Panchayats (Amendment) Ordinance, 1968, with a saving clause.

title: THE KERALA PANCHAYATS (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 1978
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Panchayats (Second Amendment) Act, 1978.

This section deals with the amendment of section 66A of the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960 (32 of 1960). It adds a proviso to subsection (1) and omits subsection (1A). The proviso states that no such cess shall be leviable for any period in respect of which land cess has been levied under this section as originally enacted. Subsection (1A) shall be omitted.

important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 23rd day of March, 1978 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 219 dated 27th March, 1978.

title: THE KERALA PANCHAYATS (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 1976
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: (1) This Act may be called the Kerala Panchayats (Second Amendment) Act, 1976. (2) It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 6th day of October, 1975.

In section 66A of the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960 (32 of 1960), in sub-section (1B), the words 'or, where the land is in the possession of a mortgagee or lessee or other person having right to possession and enjoyment of the land, by such person' shall be inserted at the end.

(1) The Kerala Panchayats (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1976 (10 of 1976), is hereby repealed. (2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 20th day of November 1976 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 671, dated 20th November 1976.

title: THE KERALA PANCHAYATS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1976
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Panchayats (Amendment) Act, 1976.
In section 39 of the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960 (32 of 1960), in sub-section (2), the last sentence shall be omitted.

In section 66A of the principal Act, for sub-section (1), the following sub-sections shall be substituted, namely: -- "(1) If any panchayat by resolution determines that a land cess shall be levied, such cess shall, subject to the provisions of this Act be levied annually on every land in the panchayat area, other than any land or class of lands which the Government may, in public interest, exempt by notification in the Gazette, at the rate of one-sixteenth per cent of the capital value of the land (1A) The cess leviable under sub-section (1) may be levied with effect from the 1st day of April, 1973, or the 1st day of April, 1974, at the option of the panchayat Provided that no such cess shall be leviable for any period in respect of which such land cess has been levied under this section as originally enacted (1B) The cess levied under sub-section (1) shall be payable by the owner of the land "

After section 66B of the principal Act, the following section shall be inserted, namely: -- "66C Adjustment of cess collected on or after 26th March, 1969.--Notwithstanding anything contained in any judgment, decree or order of any court, the land cess levied and collected by a panchayat in respect of any land for the period commencing on the 26th day of March, 1969, and ending with the 31st day of March, 1973 under section 66A as originally enacted shall be adjusted -- (a) where the panchayat has levied the land cess for any period after the 31st day of March, 1973, towards such land cess, and (b) in other cases, towards any other dues payable by the owner of that land to the panchayat."

In section 82 of the principal Act, -- (a) in sub-section (1), for the words "All public water courses, springs, reservoirs, tanks, cisterns, fountains, wells, standpipes", the words and brackets "All public water courses (other than rivers passing through more areas than the panchayat area, which the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, specify), springs, reservoirs, tanks, cisterns, fountains, wells, kappus, chals, standpipes" shall be substituted, and (b) in sub-section (1A), after the word "wells," the words "kappus, chals, shall" be inserted.

(1) The Kerala Panchayats (Amendment) Ordinance, 1975 (11 of 1975), is hereby repealed (2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act as if this Act had come into force on the 6th day of October, 1975.

important_rules: Land cess shall be levied annually on every land in the panchayat area, at the rate of one-sixteenth per cent of the capital value of the land, unless exempted by the Government.
The land cess may be levied with effect from April 1, 1973, or April 1, 1974, at the option of the panchayat.
No cess shall be levied for any period for which it was already levied under the original enactment.
The cess levied under sub-section (1) shall be payable by the owner of the land.
Land cess collected on or after March 26, 1969, shall be adjusted towards such land cess or other dues payable to the panchayat.
The definition of "public water courses" is expanded to include "kappus, chals" and exclude "rivers passing through more areas than the panchayat area" unless specified by the Government.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Panchayat
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Collection of land cess, adjustment of collected cess towards dues.

rights: Right of panchayat to levy land cess.
Right of Government to exempt lands from land cess.
Right of landowner to have collected cess adjusted.
duties: Duty of panchayat to levy land cess.
Duty of owner to pay land cess.

key_procedures: Panchayat determines by resolution to levy land cess.
Government may, by notification, exempt certain lands.
Cess rate is one-sixteenth per cent of the capital value of the land.
Panchayat has the option to levy from April 1, 1973, or April 1, 1974.
Adjustment of previously collected cess.
administration: Local Self-Government Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 15th day of March 1976 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 164 dated 16th March 1976.
The Kerala Panchayats (Amendment) Ordinance, 1975 (11 of 1975) is repealed.
Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are deemed to be taken under this Act.

title: The Kerala Panchayats (Amendment) Act, 1991
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: This Act applies to the Kerala Panchayats and relevant government bodies within the state of Kerala.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies when it comes into force. Sections 2 and 3 were deemed to have come into force on February 3, 1987. Section 4 was deemed to have come into force on February 9, 1991, and the remaining provisions of this Act were deemed to have come into force on August 9, 1991.

Amends section 33 of the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960. It substitutes the words 'The Government shall regulate' with 'the rules made under the Kerala Public Services Act, 1968 (19 of 1968), regulate' and also substitutes 'and such regulations' with 'and such rules'.

Amends section 39 of the principal Act. It modifies sub-sections (1) and (2) by substituting existing text with new provisions regarding Officers and servants of the Panchayat and their remuneration. It also clarifies that the Government shall regulate classification, methods of recruitment, conditions of service, pay and allowances and discipline and conduct of officers and servants of Panchayats, other than contingent employees, through rules made under the Kerala Public Services Act, 1968.

Amends section 130 of the principal Act by inserting a new sub-section (4). This sub-section states that 'Nothing contained in this section shall apply to the making of rules under the Kerala Public Services Act, 1968 (19 of 1968), as provided in section 33 or section 39 and any such rules when made under the said Act shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly as provided in sub-section (2) of section 2 of that Act.'.

Repeals Section 4 of the Local Government Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1991 (7 of 1991). It also states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act, as amended by section 4 of the said Ordinance, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through rules made under the Kerala Public Services Act, 1968.

administration: Likely the Department of Local Self-Government, Government of Kerala, based on the subject matter.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 8th day of October 1991 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 1219 dated the 8th October 1991.

title: THE KERALA PANCHAYATS (THIRD AMENDMENT) ACT, 1976
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala, amending The Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called The Kerala Panchayats (Third Amendment) Act, 1976, and it shall come into force on such date as the Government may appoint by notification in the Gazette.
This section amends section 68 of the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960 (32 of 1960). Specifically, in sub-section (1), it substitutes the words "six per cent" for the words "four per cent".

important_rules: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Government via Gazette notification.
In section 68(1) of the principal Act, "four per cent" is replaced by "six per cent".

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notification in the Gazette.

key_procedures: The Act comes into force upon notification by the Government in the Gazette.
The amendment involves substituting specific words in a pre-existing section of the principal Act.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be under the purview of the Government of Kerala concerning Panchayats.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 14th day of November 1976 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 872 dated 20th November 1976.

title: THE KERALA PANCHAYATS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1979
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Panchayats and their administration.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Panchayats (Amendment) Act, 1979. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 6th day of March, 1979.

Amends section 55 of the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960. It substitutes provisions related to the duration of supersession of a panchayat, allowing for extensions and appointing Administrative Committees or Special Officers.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of period of supersession of Erattupetta Panchayat.
main_sections.description: Extends the period of supersession of the Erattupetta Panchayat in the Meenachil Taluk of the Kottayam District. It also specifies the appointment of a Special Officer to exercise the functions of the panchayat.
Repeals the Kerala Panchayats (Amendment) Ordinance, 1979 (7 of 1979). It also saves any action taken under the said Ordinance or the principal Act as amended by the Ordinance.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the appointment of Administrative Committees or Special Officers.

key_procedures: The process for superseding a panchayat and appointing an Administrative Committee or Special Officer is outlined in section 2.
administration: Kerala State Government
important_notes: The Act was received the assent of the Governor on the 4th November, 1979 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 792, dated 4th November, 1979.

title: The Kerala Parks, Play-Fields And Open Spaces (Preservation And Regulation) Act, 1969
purpose: To provide for the preservation and regulation of parks, play-fields and open spaces in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the entire State of Kerala and specifically to cities of Trivandrum, Cochin and Calicut, and to every municipality and township in the State of Kerala. It also applies to areas within the jurisdiction of a Panchayat, with effect from such date as may be specified by notification.

key_definitions.executive authority: Means in the case of a city or a municipality, the Commissioner of the Corporation, or of the municipality concerned, and in the case of a panchayat, the executive officer of the panchayat or of the township committee concerned.
key_definitions.open space: Means any land, whether enclosed or not, belonging to the Government or any local authority, on which there are no buildings, or of which no more than one-twentieth part is covered with buildings, and the whole or the remainder of which is used for purposes of recreation, air or light;
key_definitions.park: Means a piece of land on which there are no buildings or of which not more than one-twentieth part is covered with buildings, and the whole or the remainder of which is laid out as a garden with trees, plants or flower-beds or as a lawn or as a meadow and maintained as a place for the resort of the public for recreation, air or light;
key_definitions.play-field: Means a piece of land adapted for the purposes of play, game or sport and used by any school or college or club or other associations.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Parks, Play-fields and Open Spaces (Preservation and Regulation) Act, 1968. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Defines 'executive authority', 'open space', 'park', and 'play-field'.

main_sections.section_title: Preparation and submission of list of parks, play-fields and open spaces by executive authorities.
main_sections.description: Requires executive authorities to prepare and submit to the Government a list of parks, play-fields and open spaces within their jurisdiction, within six months from the date of commencement of the Act. The list should be accompanied by plans and maps. This list is subject to approval by the local authority and Government.

main_sections.section_title: Approval and publication of list by local authority and Government.
main_sections.description: Details the process for public objections and suggestions regarding the list, and the subsequent approval and publication of the list by the local authority and the Government.
Empowers the Government or any local authority to add to, vary or revoke a list published under Section 4, after following a prescribed procedure involving notice and consideration of objections.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of the use of parks, play-fields and open spaces in certain cases.
main_sections.description: Prohibits the use of listed parks, play-fields and open spaces for purposes other than those for which they were used prior to the Act, unless sanctioned by the executive authority. Temporary use for less than one month with permission is allowed. No sanction is necessary for park, play-field or open space belonging to the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Maintenance of parks, play-fields and open spaces.
main_sections.description: Mandates the maintenance of parks, play-fields and open spaces in a clean and proper condition.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of construction of buildings, etc.
main_sections.description: Prohibits the construction of buildings or any structure affecting the utility of any park, play-field or open space specified in the list, without previous sanction.

main_sections.section_title: Obligation of owners of parks and play-fields.
main_sections.description: Requires owners of parks and play-fields not vested in a local authority but included in the list, to maintain them in a clean and proper condition. Also requires them to execute necessary repairs and prohibits their removal or alteration without the executive authority’s approval. The executive authority can acquire such land if the owner fails to comply.
Requires executive authorities to submit an annual return to the Government regarding parks, play-fields and open spaces within their jurisdiction.
Empowers the removal of unauthorized persons from parks, play-fields, or open spaces without prejudice to other legal proceedings.
Prescribes penalties for offences under the Act, including throwing rubbish, or fencing off areas. Penalties include imprisonment up to one month or a fine up to two hundred rupees.

Gives the Government power to direct local authorities to take measures to enforce the provisions of the Act. Also grants the Government similar powers to those of the Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, the Kerala Panchayats Act, and the Kerala Land Acquisition Act for enforcing its orders.

Grants the Government the power to make rules for the purpose of carrying out the provisions of the Act. Rules may cover various aspects like control of persons, admission, restriction of animals, procedures, and submission of returns.

important_rules: Do not use parks, play-fields, and open spaces for purposes other than those specified in the list without executive authority sanction (Section 6).
Do not construct buildings or structures that affect the utility of listed parks, play-fields, or open spaces without prior sanction (Section 8).
Owners of listed parks and play-fields must maintain them in a clean and proper condition and carry out necessary repairs (Section 9).
Do not throw rubbish or fence off any park, play-field or open space (Section 12).
Do not enter or remain in any park, play-field or open space in contravention of any order or direction of the executive authority or any person authorized (Section 11).

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month or with fine which may extend to two hundred rupees for throwing rubbish or fencing off any park, play-field or open space (Section 12).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Executive Authority (e.g., Commissioner of Corporation, Executive Officer of Panchayat), Local Authority, and Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the preparation and publication of lists, issuance of sanctions, directions from the Government to local authorities, penalties for contravention, and the power of the executive authority to acquire land if obligations are not met.

rights: Right of the public to use parks, play-fields and open spaces for recreation (inferred).
Right to submit objections and suggestions regarding the list of parks, play-fields and open spaces (Section 4).
Right to appeal to the Government against any objection to the list approved by the local authority (Section 4).
duties: Duty of executive authorities to prepare and submit lists of parks, play-fields and open spaces (Section 3).
Duty of executive authorities to maintain the cleanliness and proper condition of parks, play-fields and open spaces (Section 7).
Duty of owners of parks and play-fields to maintain them in clean and proper condition and to carry out repairs (Section 9).
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder.
obligations: Obligation to maintain parks, play-fields and open spaces in a clean and proper condition (Section 7, Section 9).
Obligation of owners to get approval for removal or alteration of projections or obstructions or for repairs to buildings on parks/play-fields (Section 9).

key_procedures: Preparation and submission of a list of parks, play-fields and open spaces by executive authorities, including maps and plans (Section 3).
Publication of the list and inviting objections and suggestions from the public (Section 4).
Approval of the list by the local authority and the Government (Section 4).
Process for variation or revocation of the published list, including notice and consideration of objections (Section 5).
Procedure for seeking sanction for use of parks, play-fields, and open spaces for purposes other than specified, and for construction of buildings (Section 6, Section 8).
Submission of annual returns by executive authorities (Section 10).
administration: Executive Authorities (Commissioners of Corporations, Executive Officers of Panchayats), Local Authorities, and ultimately the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 17, dated 20th January, 1970. (Appears as a footnote on Page 2).

The Act is titled as 'The Kerala Parks, Play-Fields And Open Spaces (Preservation And Regulation) Act, 1968' in the preamble of the Act itself, though the cover page states 1969. This discrepancy should be noted.
The Act empowers the Government to make rules, which may provide for various aspects including controlling admission, restricting animals, and specifying procedures (Section 14).
The Government can direct the local authority to enforce the provisions effectively (Section 13).

title: The Kerala Payment Of Pension To Members Of Legislature (Amendment) Act, 2008

scope: Applies to members of the Kerala Legislature.

key_definitions.legislature: Means the Legislative Assembly of Kerala.
key_definitions.member: Means a member of the Legislative Assembly of Kerala.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and when it comes into force.
Amends the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature Act, 1976. This section details the specific changes being made to the principal Act.
Inserts a new section (2A) into the principal Act, likely related to the eligibility or calculation of pension.
Replaces the existing Schedule in the principal Act with a new one. The Schedule appears to detail pension amounts and related matters.

important_rules: Rule 1: Amendments to Section 2 of the Principal Act concerning definitions.
Rule 2: Provisions regarding the pension payable to members of the Legislature.
Rule 3: Details on the calculation and eligibility for pension, likely as per the substituted schedule.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Likely the State Government or a designated authority under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the amended Act and relevant rules.

rights: Right to receive pension as per the provisions of the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Application for pension (implied by the nature of the Act).
Procedure 2: Calculation and disbursement of pension as per the amended provisions and schedule.
administration: Likely the Department of Finance or a similar department of the Kerala State Government.
important_notes: The Act specifies pension amounts in Rupees, indicating financial benefits.

title: THE KERALA PAYMENT OF PENSION TO MEMBERS OF LEGISLATURE (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2008
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature Act, 1976, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to members of the Kerala Legislature and their pension entitlements.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature (Amendment) Act, 2008 and shall come into force at once.

Amends Section 2 of the principal Act by substituting words related to 'minor son or the unmarried daughter' and 'twenty five years' in clause (i) of sub-section (1E). It also inserts a new clause (11a) and a Note regarding the commencement of the sub-section.

Inserts a new Section 2B, 'Free Transit Coupons for Ex-Members of the Legislative Assembly', which outlines the provision of free transit coupons for ex-members subject to rules, with an aggregate value of twelve thousand rupees for a period of twelve calendar months, including rail travel coupons and fuel coupons.

Substitutes the existing Schedule with a new one, which details the 'Rate of Pension' based on the 'Period' of service, ranging from Rs. 4,000 per Mensa for periods below two years to Rs. 6,000 per Mensa for five years in the aggregate. It also includes provisions regarding additional pension for ex-members who served for five years and rules for calculating pension fractions and maximum pension.

important_rules: Ex-members are entitled to free transit coupons worth Rs. 12,000 per annum, including rail and fuel coupons.
The pension rate is determined by the period of service as a member.
An additional pension of Rs. 500 per year is provided for every year exceeding five years of service.
The maximum pension for an eligible member shall not exceed Rs. 20,000 per mensa in the aggregate.

rights: Right to receive pension as per the Act.
Right to receive free transit coupons for ex-members.

key_procedures: Calculation of pension based on years of service.
Application for and entitlement to free transit coupons for ex-members.
administration: Implied to be administered by the relevant department overseeing legislature affairs in Kerala.
important_notes: The sub-section regarding the insertion of new section 2B was deemed to have come into force on the 14th day of May, 1996.
Received the assent of Governor on the 1st August 2008 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No 1690 dated 2nd August, 2008.

title: The Kerala Payment Of Pension To Members Of Legislature (Amendment) Act, 2003
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature Act, 1976.
scope: Applies to members of the Legislature of Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature (Amendment) Act, 2003 and that it shall come into force on the 1st day of July, 2003.
Substitutes the existing Schedule in the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature Act, 1976 with a new schedule providing for 'Rate of Pension'.

important_rules: The new rates of pension are as follows: For any period below two years - Rs. 2,500; For two years in the aggregate - Rs. 3,000; For three years in the aggregate - Rs. 3,500; For four years in the aggregate - Rs. 4,000; For five years in the aggregate - Rs. 4,500.
A member who has served for a period exceeding five years shall be paid an additional pension of five hundred rupees per mensem for every year in excess of five years.
Fraction of half year and above in the qualifying period for pension shall be rounded to the next completed year.
The maximum pension to which a member is eligible shall not, in the aggregate, exceed twelve thousand and five hundred per mensem.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not specified
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not specified

rights: Right to receive pension based on years of service.
Right to receive additional pension for service exceeding five years.

key_procedures: Calculation of qualifying period for pension, rounding up fractions of half year or above.
Calculation of pension based on the substituted schedule and additional pension for service beyond five years.
administration: Not specified
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on 28th July, 2003.
Published as Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 1427 dated 30th July, 2003.

title: THE KERALA PAYMENT OF PENSION TO MEMBERS OF LEGISLATURE (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1994
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature Act, 1976 for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to members of the Kerala Legislature.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature (Amendment) Act, 1994, and it shall come into force at once.

Amends section 2 of the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature Act, 1976. It specifies that in sub-section (1), for the opening paragraph, new provisions are substituted regarding who can receive pension, including spouses. Also, in sub-section (1C), for the words, figures and brackets "Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature (Amendment) Act, 1982", the words, figures and brackets "Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature (Amendment) Act, 1994" shall be substituted. Further, after sub-section (1C), a new sub-section (1CC) is inserted concerning spouses referred to in sub-section (1A), (1B) and (1C) being eligible for enhanced rates of pension from time to time.

main_sections.section_title: In section 2A of the principal Act
main_sections.description: For the words, figures and brackets "of sub-section (1) of section 2", the words, figures and brackets "of sub-section (1) of section 2 and the spouse of such person" shall be substituted. In the Explanation, for the words "family of a person", the words "family of a person other than his or her spouse" shall be substituted.

main_sections.section_title: After section 3 of the principal Act, the following Schedule shall be added, namely:
main_sections.description: Adds a new Schedule titled "SCHEDULE" with "Rate of Pension" for "Any period below two years", "For two years in the aggregate", "For three years in the aggregate", "For four years in the aggregate", and "For five years in the aggregate", with corresponding monthly pension rates.

important_rules: Provided that where any person has served as member as stated in sub-section (1) of section 2 for a period exceeding five years there shall be paid to him an additional pension of two hundred and fifty rupees per mensem for every year or part thereof exceeding six months in excess of five years.

rights: Right to receive pension as per the Act and its amendments.
Spouses of members may be eligible for enhanced pension rates.

administration: The Legislature Secretariat is responsible for issuing instructions regarding pension payments.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 22nd day of April, 1994 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 546 dated the 22nd April, 1994.

title: THE KERALA PAYMENT OF PENSION TO MEMBERS OF LEGISLATURE (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 1986
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature Act, 1976, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to Members of the Legislature of Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature (Second Amendment) Act, 1986, and it shall come into force at once.
Amends Section 2 of the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature Act, 1976 (46 of 1976).

important_rules: In section 2, for the words "two hundred rupees", the words "three hundred rupees" shall be substituted.

In the proviso to section 2, after the words "in excess of two.", the word "years" shall be added and the words "so, however, that in no case the pension payable to such person shall exceed five-hundred rupees per mensem" shall be deleted.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not specified
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not specified
