title: The Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature (Amendment) Act, 1991
purpose: To amend the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature Act, 1976.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Legislature and provisions related to pension payment for its members.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature (Amendment) Act, 1991 and shall come into force on the 1st day of October, 1991.

This section amends section 2 of the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature Act, 1976. It involves substituting specific phrases like 'three hundred rupees' and 'four hundred rupees' with others. It also deals with amending provisions within sub-sections, including explanatory notes and the addition of new sub-sections concerning pension entitlement. Specifically, it allows for entitlement to pension under sub-section (1) to be received by any other person under law made by the State Government or any Corporation controlled by the State Government, or any authority, if such person is entitled to receive the pension under sub-section (1).

important_rules: Substitution of phrases within the original Act, e.g., 'three hundred rupees' and 'four hundred rupees'.
In the proviso to sub-section (1) of section 2, 'fifty rupees' and 'one hundred rupees' are to be substituted by 'one hundred rupees' and 'two hundred rupees' respectively.
The words 'every year' and 'six months' in the original Act are amended to 'every year' and 'six months' respectively.
An amendment to sub-section (3) of section 2 includes provisions for adding figures and brackets.
A new sub-section (4) is added to section 2, allowing for pension entitlement under sub-section (1) to be received by other entitled persons as specified.

rights: Members of the Legislature are entitled to receive pension under certain conditions.

key_procedures: The amendment process involves substituting specific text within the existing Act.
The Act comes into force on a specified date (1st October, 1991).
administration: The Act relates to the payment of pension to Members of Legislature, likely administered by the Kerala Legislature Secretariat or a related government department.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 31st day of October, 1991 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 1290 dated the 31st October, 1991.

title: The Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature (Amendment) Act, 2005
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature Act, 1976.
scope: Applies to the payment of pension to members of the Kerala Legislature.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature (Amendment) Act, 2005 and it shall come into force at once.

Amends section 2 of the Principal Act (Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature Act, 1976) by inserting provisions related to family pensions. It clarifies that if a spouse dies, the minor son or unmarried daughter is entitled to a family pension. If there are two persons entitled to family pension, the amount will be paid equally. It also adds a provision where any person entitled to pension under sub-section (1) is also entitled to any other pension from the Government of India or any Corporation, they can still receive the pension under this Act in addition to such other pension.
Amends the principal Act by substituting 'rupees seventeen thousand and five hundred' for 'rupees twelve thousand and five hundred' in the third proviso to the Schedule.

important_rules: Family pension is payable to the minor son or unmarried daughter of a deceased member.
If two persons are entitled to family pension, it shall be paid to them equally.
A person entitled to pension under this Act can also receive other pensions from the Government of India or any Corporation.
Specific monetary amounts in the Schedule have been updated.

rights: Right to receive pension as a member of the Kerala Legislature.
Right to family pension for minor son or unmarried daughter of a deceased member.
Right to receive pension under this Act in addition to other pensions.

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act upon enactment.
Insertion of new clauses into Section 2 of the principal Act regarding family pensions.
Substitution of specific monetary amounts in the Schedule.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 31st day of August, 2005 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No 2049 dated 2nd September, 2005.

title: THE KERALA PAYMENT OF ARREARS OF RENT IN INSTALMENTS ACT, 1979
purpose: To provide for installment facility for the payment of arrears of rent and for matters incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the entire State of Kerala. It concerns payment of arrears of rent and matters related to it.

key_definitions.court: Includes a Civil Court and a Land Tribunal.
key_definitions.rent: Shall have the same meaning as assigned to them in the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963.
key_definitions.tenant: Shall have the same meaning as assigned to them in the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Payment of Arrears of Rent in Instalments Act, 1979. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 19th day of July, 1979.
Defines terms used in the Act, including 'court', 'rent', and 'tenant'.

main_sections.section_title: Payment of arrears of rent in instalments.
main_sections.description: Allows tenants to pay arrears of rent in six equal half-yearly installments, provided they meet certain conditions and have not been evicted.

main_sections.section_title: Stay of suits, applications, etc., for arrears of rent.
main_sections.description: Provides for the stay of suits, applications, or other proceedings for recovery of arrears of rent or for eviction of tenants if the tenant makes the payment of arrears as stipulated.
Deals with the restoration of possession to tenants who were dispossessed before the commencement of the Act, under certain conditions.

main_sections.section_title: Tenants failing to pay instalments in time not entitled to benefits.
main_sections.description: Specifies that tenants who fail to pay installments on or before the due date are not entitled to the benefits conferred by the Act.
Deals with the computation of the period of limitation for the institution of suits, applications, or other proceedings prohibited or stayed under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Act not to apply to certain class of tenants.
main_sections.description: Exempts certain classes of tenants, specifically those defined in section 4(2) of the Kerala Debt Relief Act, 1977, from the purview of this Act.

Repeals the Kerala Payment of Arrears of Rent in Instalments Ordinance, 1979, and states that anything done or any action taken under the said Ordinance is deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Tenants may pay arrears of rent in six equal half-yearly installments.
The first installment must be paid on or before the 1st day of January, 1970, and the subsequent installments on or before the expiry of fifteen days from the due date.
Failure to pay installments on time disentitles tenants to the benefits of the Act.
Suits and proceedings for arrears of rent and eviction are stayed if the tenant complies with installment payments.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Court or Land Tribunal.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through stay of suits, applications, and proceedings related to rent arrears and eviction; also through restoration of possession.

rights: Right of a tenant to pay rent arrears in installments.
Right of a tenant to get possession restored under certain conditions.
duties: Duty of the tenant to pay installments on or before the due dates.
Duty of the court or Land Tribunal to grant stay of proceedings upon compliance with installment payments.

key_procedures: A tenant facing eviction or legal action for rent arrears can apply to pay the arrears in installments.
Upon the court or Land Tribunal being satisfied that the tenant's dispossession was prevented by sufficient cause, they can allow the tenant to deposit the installments.
The court or Land Tribunal shall stay suits, applications, and other proceedings once the tenant begins paying installments.
administration: Likely the Kerala State Government's Revenue Department or a similar body responsible for land and tenancy laws.
important_notes: The Act commenced on the 19th day of July, 1979.
The provisions regarding installment payments are to be treated as if they were in force from May 1, 1968, for the purpose of determining the amount of arrears.
The Act does not apply to tenants who are debtors as defined in clause (4) of section 2 of the Kerala Debt Relief Act, 1977.

title: THE KERALA PAYMENT OF PENSION TO MEMBERS OF LEGISLATURE (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1997
purpose: To further amend The Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature Act, 1976, for purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to members of the Kerala Legislature.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature (Amendment) Act, 1997. It shall come into force at once.
Amends section 2 of the principal Act by omitting sub-section (1) and the proviso to sub-section (2). It also substitutes certain words in the proviso to sub-section (2) and omits the Explanation.
Substitutes the existing Schedule in the principal Act with a new Schedule detailing the rate of pension per mensem based on the period served.

important_rules: The Act comes into force immediately upon enactment.
Pension rates are determined by the aggregate period of service as a member.
For periods exceeding five years of service, an additional pension of Rs. 250 per mensem for every year of service beyond five years is provided.
The maximum pension payable is Rs. 5000 per mensem in the aggregate.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be the relevant government authority administering pension benefits.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not explicitly stated.

rights: Right to receive pension based on years of service.
Right to an additional pension for service exceeding five years.

key_procedures: Calculating the qualifying period for pension: net qualifying period for pension is counted and rounded up to the next completed year.
Determining pension amount: Pension is calculated based on the aggregate period of service as per the provided schedule and additional provisions.
administration: The Government of Kerala (implied by the context of a Kerala State Act).
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 16th day of April, 1997 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No 495 dated 22nd April, 1997.
The rates of pension provided are subject to the conditions outlined in the schedule and the text of the Act.
The calculation of pension and the aggregate limit are important considerations.

title: THE KERALA PAYMENT OF PENSION TO MEMBERS OF LEGISLATURE (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2000
purpose: To amend the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature Act, 1976.
scope: Applies to Members of the Kerala Legislature.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature (Amendment) Act, 2000. It shall come into force at once.
Substitutes the Schedule in the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature Act, 1976 (46 of 1976) with a new Schedule detailing pension rates based on periods of service.

important_rules: For any period below two years in the aggregate, the pension is Rs. 2,000 per mensem.
For two years in the aggregate, the pension is Rs. 2,400 per mensem.
For three years in the aggregate, the pension is Rs. 2,800 per mensem.
For four years in the aggregate, the pension is Rs. 3,200 per mensem.
For five years in the aggregate, the pension is Rs. 3,600 per mensem.
Any person who has served as member for a period exceeding five years shall be paid an additional pension of four hundred rupees per mensem for every year in excess of five years.
Further, in calculating the net qualifying period for pension, a fraction of half year shall be rounded to the next completed year.
The maximum pension to which a member is eligible, in the aggregate, shall not exceed rupees seven thousand and five hundred per mensem.

rights: Right to receive pension as per the specified rates and conditions.
Right to receive additional pension for service exceeding five years.
Right for pension fraction of half year to be rounded to the next completed year.

key_procedures: Substitution of the existing Schedule with a new one detailing pension rates.
Calculation of pension based on periods of service, including rounding of fractions and additional pension for extended service.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on 25th day of April, 2000.
Published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 760 dated 26th April, 2000.
The maximum pension is capped at Rs. 7,500 per mensem.

title: THE KERALA PAYMENT OF PENSION TO MEMBERS OF LEGISLATURE (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1982
purpose: To amend the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature Act, 1976.
scope: Applies to Members of the Kerala Legislature.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature (Amendment) Act, 1982. It shall come into force at once.

Amends section 2 of the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature Act, 1976. It substitutes specific provisions regarding pension amounts, conditions for spouse's entitlement, and posthumous amendments. It also inserts an explanation regarding pension granted by the Government of India under specific schemes.

Inserts a new section 2A into the principal Act, which deals with medical facilities to ex-members. It specifies that ex-members and their families are entitled to medical treatment and other benefits to the same extent as members of the Kerala Legislative Assembly under the Kerala Legislative Assembly (Payment of Salaries and Allowances) Act, 1951.

important_rules: For ex-members who have served for two years, the pension is two hundred rupees per mensem.
For ex-members whose service was less than two years, the pension is one hundred and fifty rupees per mensem.

If a member dies or has died, his or her spouse shall, if such member would have been entitled to pension under sub-section (1), be entitled to the same pension as such member would have been entitled to if he or she had ceased to be a member on that date.
Where a person entitled to pension under sub-section (1) dies, his or her spouse shall be entitled to the same amount of pension as would have been payable to such person if he or she had not died.

For the purposes of the sub-section, pension granted by the Government of India under the Freedom Fighters Pension Scheme, 1972, or by the Government of Kerala under the Kerala Freedom Fighters, Pension Rules or by any other State Government under a scheme for payment of pension to freedom fighters shall not be deemed to be pension from the Government of India or, as the case may be, any State Government.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be through administrative channels related to pensions and legislative allowances.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Implied through the amendment of existing provisions and insertion of new ones related to pension and medical benefits.

rights: Members of the Legislature are entitled to pensions.
Spouses of deceased members are entitled to pensions under certain conditions.
Ex-members and their families are entitled to medical facilities and other benefits.

key_procedures: Amendment of Section 2: Involves substituting existing text with new provisions regarding pension amounts and conditions for entitlement.
Insertion of Section 2A: Involves adding a new section to the principal Act detailing the entitlement to medical facilities for ex-members.
administration: Implied to be managed by the department responsible for legislative affairs and pensions in Kerala.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 22nd day of October, 1982 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 743 dated the 23rd October, 1982.
The amendments are related to the payment of pension to members of the legislature.
The Act addresses conditions for pension entitlement for members, their spouses, and medical facilities for ex-members.

title: The Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature (Amendment) Act, 2012
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature Act, 1976, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to members of the Kerala Legislature.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature (Amendment) Act, 2012. It shall come into force at once.
In section 2B of the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature Act, 1976, in sub-section (1), the words "twelve thousand rupees" are substituted for "twenty four thousand rupees".
In the principal Act, for the Schedule, the following Schedule shall be substituted: "Schedule [See Section 2(1)] Rate of Pension" which lists pension rates based on years of service.

important_rules: The pension rates are as specified in the substituted Schedule.

Provided that where any person has served as a member as stated in sub-section (1) of section 2 for a period exceeding five years, there shall be paid to him an additional pension of seven hundred and fifty rupees per mensem for every year in excess of five years.
Provided further that in calculating the net qualifying period for pension, fraction of half year and above shall be rounded to the next completed year.

Provided also that the Ex-Members may be paid an additional pension of rupees two thousand and five hundred per mensem on completion of seventy years of age and rupees three thousand and five hundred per mensem on completion of eighty years of age and rupees three thousand and five hundred per mensem on completion of ninety years of age.
Provided also that the maximum pension to which a member is eligible under this Act shall not, in the aggregate, exceed rupees thirty five thousand per mensem.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government of Kerala, Law (Legislation-I) Department
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legislative action and administrative procedures.

rights: Right to receive pension based on years of service.
Right to receive additional pension for service exceeding five years.
Right to receive additional pension as an Ex-Member upon reaching specific age milestones.
obligations: Members are obligated to serve the legislature to be eligible for pension.

key_procedures: Application for pension likely involves submitting proof of service and meeting age criteria.
Calculation of pension includes qualifying period, additional pension for extended service, and special provisions for Ex-Members.
administration: Government of Kerala, Law (Legislation-I) Department
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature Act, 1976.
The amendment comes into force immediately.
The pension rates and additional pension provisions are detailed in the Schedule and subsequent provisos.

title: The Kerala Payment of Subsistence Allowance (Amendment) Act, 1979
purpose: To amend the Kerala Payment of Subsistence Allowance Act, 1972.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Payment of Subsistence Allowance Act, 1972, and specifically addresses amendments related to subsistence allowance during suspension periods and the application of the Act to certain establishments.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Payment of Subsistence Allowance (Amendment) Act, 1978, and shall come into force at once.

This section amends section 3 of the Kerala Payment of Subsistence Allowance Act, 1972. It modifies the provisions regarding the amount of subsistence allowance payable based on the period of suspension. For periods not exceeding ninety days of suspension, the allowance is seventy-five percent of the wages. For periods exceeding one hundred and eighty days, the allowance is equal to the wages the employee was drawing immediately before suspension.

This section inserts a new section 5A into the principal Act, titled 'Act not to apply to certain establishments'. It states that nothing contained in this Act shall apply to any public sector undertaking of the Central Government.

important_rules: Subsistence allowance during suspension: If the period of suspension exceeds ninety days, the amount of subsistence allowance shall be seventy-five percent of the wages.

Subsistence allowance during prolonged suspension: If the period of suspension exceeds one hundred and eighty days, the amount of subsistence allowance shall be equal to the wages the employee was drawing immediately before such suspension.
Exemption for certain establishments: The Act does not apply to any public sector undertaking of the Central Government.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated in the provided excerpt.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not explicitly stated in the provided excerpt.

rights: Right to subsistence allowance during suspension as per the specified rates.

administration: Not explicitly stated in the provided excerpt.
important_notes: The Act was received the assent of the President on the 13th February, 1979 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 137, dated 28th February, 1979.

title: THE KERALA PAYMENT OF SUBSISTENCE ALLOWANCE ACT, 1972
purpose: An Act to provide for the payment of subsistence allowance to the employees in certain establishments during the period of suspension.
scope: Applies to employees in certain establishments in Kerala during the period of suspension. The Act was enacted in the Twenty-third Year of the Republic of India.

key_definitions.employee: Any person employed in or in connection with the work of any establishment to do skilled, semi-skilled or unskilled manual, supervisory, technical, clerical or any other kind of work for hire or reward, whether the terms of employment be express or implied, but does not include such person who is employed mainly in a managerial or an administrative capacity or as an out-worker, that is to say, a person to whom any articles or materials are given out by or on behalf of the employer to be cleaned, washed, altered, ornamented or repaired by such out-worker in any place not under the control and management of the employer.
key_definitions.employer: The owner of an establishment and includes any person responsible to the owner for supervision and control of the establishment.
key_definitions.establishment: Any place where any industry, trade, business, undertaking, manufacture, occupation or service is carried on, but does not include any office or department of any Government or any establishment of any railway, major port, mine or oilfield.
key_definitions.period of suspension: In a case where express permission of the authority under sub-section (1) of section 32 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, is necessary before the employment of an employee can be validly terminated including the period until such permission is obtained and termination of service is effected
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act
key_definitions.suspension: An interim decision of an employer as a result of which an employee is debarred temporarily from attending his office and performing his functions in the establishment where he is employed, such restriction being imposed on the employee on the ground either that a disciplinary proceeding has already been, or is shortly to be instituted against him or that a criminal proceeding in respect of an offence alleged to have been committed by him is under investigation or trial.
key_definitions.wages: All remuneration capable of being expressed in terms of money, which would, if the terms of employment expressed or implied, were fulfilled, be payable to an employee in respect of his employment or of work done in such employment, and includes (i) such allowances (including dearness allowance) as the employee is for the time being entitled to; (ii) the value of any house accommodation or of supply of light, water, medical attendance or other amenity or of any service or of any concessional supply of food-grains or other articles; (iii) any travelling concession; but does not include— (i) any bonus; (ii) any contribution paid or payable by the employer to any pension fund or provident fund or for the benefit of the employer under any law for the time being in force; (iii) any gratuity payable on the termination of his service.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Payment of Subsistence Allowance Act, 1972. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Defines terms used in the Act, including 'employee', 'employer', 'establishment', 'period of suspension', 'prescribed', 'suspension', and 'wages'.

Specifies that whenever an employee is placed under suspension, he shall be paid by the employer for the period during which he is under suspension subsistence allowance of an amount equal to fifty per centum of the wages which the employee was drawing immediately before such suspension. It also provides for increased subsistence allowance in cases where the period of suspension exceeds ninety days, and conditions under which an employee is not entitled to subsistence allowance.

main_sections.section_title: Recovery of money due from an employer
main_sections.description: Outlines the process for recovering money due from an employer to an employee, including the application of such money to the recovery of money due to the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Saving of certain rights and privileges
main_sections.description: States that nothing in this Act shall affect any right or privilege to which any employee is entitled on the date of commencement of this Act under any law for the time being in force or under any contract, custom or usage, which is more favourable to him than any right or privilege conferred upon him by this Act.

Empowers the Government, by notification in the Gazette, to direct that any power exercisable by it under this Act or the rules made thereunder shall, in relation to such matters and subject to such conditions, if any, as may be specified in such notification, be exercisable also by such officer or authority subordinate to the Government as may be specified in the said notification.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken under the Act
main_sections.description: Provides that no suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against any person for anything which is in good faith done or intended to be done in pursuance of this Act or the rules made thereunder.

States that whoever contravenes any provision of this Act or any rule made thereunder shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months or with fine which shall be not less than one thousand rupees or with both.
Deals with offences committed by companies and other bodies corporate or associations of persons, where the offence was committed without their knowledge or consent.

main_sections.section_title: Presumption to be made in certain cases
main_sections.description: Specifies that in any proceedings under section 4 or in any prosecution under section 8, it shall be presumed, until the contrary is proved, the burden of proving which shall lie on the employer, that there has been an interim decision of the employer as a result of which the employee has been debarred temporarily from attending his office and performing his functions in the establishment where he is employed.

States that no court shall take cognizance of any offence punishable under this Act, save on complaint made by, or under the authority of, the Government. It also specifies that no court inferior to that of a Magistrate of the First Class shall try any offence punishable under this Act.

Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act. These rules can be made by notification in the Gazette. The section also outlines the procedure for laying such rules before the Legislative Assembly and their subsequent modification or annulment.

important_rules: An employee placed under suspension shall be paid by the employer subsistence allowance equal to fifty per centum of the wages drawn immediately before suspension.
If the period of suspension exceeds ninety days, the subsistence allowance shall be increased to seventy-five per centum of the wages drawn immediately before suspension.
An employee shall not be entitled to any subsistence allowance if he accepts employment in any establishment other than the establishment where he had been working immediately before his suspension.
Contravention of any provision of the Act or rules is punishable with imprisonment up to three months or a fine of not less than one thousand rupees or both.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months
Fine which shall be not less than one thousand rupees
Imprisonment and fine both
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings, including prosecution for contravention of the Act or rules, and through the recovery of money due from employers.

rights: Right to receive subsistence allowance during suspension.
Right to receive enhanced subsistence allowance if suspension exceeds ninety days.
Right to retain privileges and rights under other laws or contracts if more favourable.
duties: Duty of the employer to pay subsistence allowance to suspended employees.
Duty of companies and associations to ensure their officers act with knowledge and consent to avoid offences.
obligations: Obligation of the employer to pay fifty per centum of wages as subsistence allowance during suspension.

key_procedures: Payment of subsistence allowance by employer to suspended employee: 50% of previous wages.
Application for recovery of money due from employer: can be made by the employee, their representative, or the Government.
Rule making procedure: Government can make rules, which are then laid before the Legislative Assembly for approval and potential modification.
administration: The Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 881 dated 14th September, 1973.

Nothing in this Act affects any right or privilege to which any employee is entitled on the date of commencement of this Act under any law for the time being in force or under any contract, custom or usage, which is more favourable to him than any right or privilege conferred upon him by this Act.
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected from legal proceedings.

title: The Kerala Places Of Public Resort (Amendment) Act, 1975
purpose: To amend the Kerala Places of Public Resort Act, 1963.
scope: Applies to places licensed for purposes of cinematograph exhibition, temples, churches, mosques, or other places of public worship, or any building under the control of the State or Central Government.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Places of Public Resort (Amendment) Act, 1975, and shall come into force at once.
Substitutes sub-section (4) of section 1 of the Principal Act (Kerala Places of Public Resort Act, 1963) with new text regarding the application of the Act.

important_rules: Nothing in this Act shall apply to any place licensed for purposes of cinematograph exhibition under the Kerala Cinemas (Regulation) Act, 1958, or to any temple, church, mosque or other place of public worship or to any building belonging to or under the control of the State or Central Government.
administration: State Government of Kerala
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 4th day of July, 1975 and published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 338 dated 5th July, 1975.

title: THE KERALA PLACES OF PUBLIC RESORT (VALIDATION OF LEVY AND COLLECTION OF LICENCE FEE) ACT, 1971
purpose: To validate the levy and collection of certain licence fee under the Kerala Places of Public Resort Act, 1963 and the Rules issued thereunder.
scope: Applies to the levy and collection of licence fee by the licensing authority under the Kerala Places of Public Resort Act, 1963, and the rules made thereunder. It covers all acts, proceedings or things done or taken by the licensing authority in connection with such levy or collection, and validation of fees levied or collected. It also applies to any court, person or authority whatsoever.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Places of Public Resort (Validation of Levy and Collection of Licence Fee) Act, 1971.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of levy and collection of licence fee.
main_sections.description: This section validates the levy and collection of licence fee under the Kerala Places of Public Resort Act, 1963, and the rules made thereunder, notwithstanding any judgment, decree or order of any court to the contrary. It also deems all fees levied or collected or purported to have been levied or collected in pursuance of the said rule to have been validly levied, collected and, where applicable, credited and collected.

important_rules: The rate of fee directed by the Government by rule under the said Act with effect on and from the 1st day of August, 1965, and up to and inclusive of 10th day of February, 1969, shall be deemed to have been issued in accordance with law and the rates fixed under the said rule shall be deemed to be, and to have been, the rate of fee directed by the Government by rule under the said Act with effect on and from the 1st day of August, 1965, and up to and inclusive of 10th day of February, 1969.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Licensing authority, Government, and any court or person or authority whatsoever.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the levy and collection of licence fees, and by ensuring that no suit or other proceedings are maintained or continued against the Government, the local authority or any person or authority whatsoever for the refund of any fees paid.

rights: Right to levy and collect licence fee under the Act and rules.
Right to have fees levied or collected deemed valid.
obligations: Licensing authority has the obligation to levy and collect licence fees in accordance with the Act and rules.

key_procedures: The Act validates past actions related to the levy and collection of licence fees.
No legal challenges against the collected fees are permitted.
administration: Likely administered by the local authorities responsible for places of public resort in Kerala, under the oversight of the state government.
important_notes: This Act is a validation Act, specifically addressing potential legal challenges to the collection of licence fees that occurred between August 1, 1965, and February 10, 1969.
It clarifies that the fee rates fixed by the Government under the relevant rules during this period are considered lawful.
Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 365, dated 24th August, 1971.

title: The Kerala Places of Public Resort Act, 1963
purpose: To unify and amend the law relating to the licensing and inspection of places of public resort or entertainment in the State of Kerala.
scope: The Act applies to any place of public resort or entertainment in the State of Kerala, including buildings, enclosures, and areas of fifty square metres used for such purposes. It also covers temporary amusements, religious buildings, race-course circles, theatre, music hall, ballroom, gymnasium, and fencing school. The Act extends to the whole of Kerala.

key_definitions.place of public resort or entertainment: Shall mean any place, enclosure, building, tent, booth or other erection whether permanent or temporary, where music, singing, dancing or any diversion or game on the nature, carrying on the same is provided, and to which the public are admitted either on payment of money or with the intention that money may be collected from those admitted, otherwise than for charitable or religious purpose, and shall include a race-course circle, theatre, music hall, ballroom, bagatelle room, gymnasium and fencing school.
key_definitions.building: Includes any house, hut, shed or roofed enclosure.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, commencement, extent and application.
main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its commencement date, and its application to the State of Kerala.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'place of public resort or entertainment' and 'building'.

main_sections.section_title: No enclosed place or building with area of fifty square metres to be used for public resort or entertainment without a licence.
main_sections.description: Prohibits the use of enclosed places or buildings of fifty square metres or more for public resort or entertainment without a license.
Outlines the procedure for applying for a license to use an enclosed place or building for public resort or entertainment.

main_sections.section_title: Authority to whom application should be made.
main_sections.description: Specifies the authority to whom the application for a license should be submitted, depending on the location of the place or building.
Details the process followed by the authority upon receiving a license application, including inspection and potential alterations.
Describes the conditions under which a license may be granted, including satisfaction of safety and purpose requirements, and payment of fees.

main_sections.section_title: Licence to state period for which it is to be in force.
main_sections.description: Mandates that the license must specify the period for which it is valid and states that it remains in force until its expiration.
Explains the process for renewing a license, requiring an application before expiry and communication of rejection if not granted.
Lists the grounds upon which a license can be revoked or suspended, including misuse of the place, contravention of conditions, or if the place can no longer be safely used.
Establishes the right to appeal against orders of revocation or suspension of license and specifies the appellate authority and time limits for appeal.

main_sections.section_title: Power to enter place of public resort or entertainment to inspect licence or to prevent further use.
main_sections.description: Grants power to the licensing authority or any person authorised by them to enter and inspect places of public resort or entertainment.

main_sections.section_title: The Government may revise any proceedings under this Act.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to call for and examine records of proceedings and to revise them if necessary.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of smoking in certain places where entertainments are held.
main_sections.description: Prohibits smoking in enclosed places or buildings used for public resort or entertainment during permitted periods, except in designated areas like auditoriums.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken under the Act.
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith under the Act, preventing prosecution or legal proceedings against any person for anything done or intended to be done in pursuance of the Act.
Specifies penalties for contravening the Act, including fines imposed by a Magistrate and recovery procedures.
Outlines the duties of police officers, including communicating information received to licensing authorities and assisting them.

main_sections.section_title: Exercise of powers of police officers by municipal servant.
main_sections.description: Allows for the exercise of powers of police officers by municipal servants for the purposes of this Act.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, subject to legislative approval.
Repeals certain prior enactments relating to places of public resort in Malabar and Travancore-Cochin, with a saving clause for actions taken under those repealed laws.

Empowers the Government to issue orders to remove any difficulty in the transition from repealed enactments to this Act, provided such orders are made within two years of the commencement of this Act.

important_rules: No enclosed place or building with an area of fifty square metres or more can be used for public resort or entertainment without a valid license.
Licenses can be revoked or suspended if the place is used for illegal purposes, if conditions are violated, or if the place is no longer safe.
Smoking is prohibited in enclosed places or buildings used for public resort or entertainment during the prohibited period, except in designated areas.
Police officers have a duty to communicate relevant information to licensing authorities and assist them in their duties.
The Government can make rules for the effective implementation of the Act, subject to legislative review.

penalties: Fine not exceeding five hundred rupees for using a place of public resort or entertainment without a license or in contravention of licence conditions.
Penalties for contravening smoking prohibition: not exceeding fifty rupees, summarily punishable by police officers.
Penalties for exercising powers under Section 41 of the Kerala Police Act, 1960: fine not exceeding fifty rupees.
Recovery of fines may be paid over to the authority mentioned in Section 5.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Licensing authorities (e.g., Commissioner of Corporation, Commissioner of Municipality, Executive Officer of Township), Police Officers, Municipal Servants.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Inspection of licensed premises, revocation or suspension of licenses, imposition of fines, prosecution by police officers.

rights: Right to appeal against orders of revocation or suspension of license.
Right to apply for a license to use a place for public resort or entertainment.
duties: Duty of every police officer to communicate information received to the licensing authority and assist them.
Duty of persons operating places of public resort to obtain and adhere to licenses.
Duty to not smoke in prohibited areas during entertainment.
obligations: Obligation to obtain a license for operating a place of public resort or entertainment.
Obligation to comply with the terms and conditions of the license.
Obligation to allow inspection by authorities.
Obligation to pay fees for licenses.

key_procedures: Application for a license: Submission of application to the relevant authority, inspection of the premises, and decision by the authority.
Renewal of license: Application for renewal before expiry, and communication of the decision.
Appeals: Filing an appeal within thirty days of the order.
Revocation or suspension of license: Based on specified grounds, with provisions for appeal.
administration: The Government of Kerala is responsible for framing rules and making revisions. Specific licensing and enforcement are carried out by municipal and local authorities, and police officers.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on 21st November, 1963, and was published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 21st November, 1963.
The Act repeals The Madras Places of Public Resort Act, 1956 (Act II of 1956) and The Travancore-Cochin Places of Public Resort Act, 1951 (Act VIII of 1951).
Provisions of Section 5 of the Indian Limitation Act, 1908 apply to appeals under this section.
The appellate authority has the same powers as a Magistrate in inspecting places and requiring alterations.
The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, exempt any class of entertainments from certain provisions of this Act.

title: The Kerala Plant Diseases and Pests Act, 1972
purpose: To prevent the introduction, spread or re-appearance of plant diseases, pests, parasites and noxious weeds.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. It applies to any land, water or premises where plant diseases, pests, parasites and noxious weeds may be present or may spread, and to all occupiers of such areas.

key_definitions.affected area: Means any area declared as such under section 3.
key_definitions.District Collector: Means the Collector of the district and includes any officer authorised by the District Collector to perform all or any of the functions of the District Collector under this Act.
key_definitions.inspecting officer: Means an Inspecting Officer appointed under section 13.
key_definitions.noxious weed: Means any weed declared as such under section 3.
key_definitions.occupier: Means the person having for the time being the right of occupation of any land, water or premises, or his authorised agent or any person in actual occupation of the land, water or premises, and includes a local authority and a company having such right of occupation or in such actual occupation;
key_definitions.parasite: Means any plant or animal carrying on its existence wholly or in part on any agricultural crop, plant, tree, bush or herb and declared to be a parasite under section 3;
key_definitions.pest: Means any insect, invertebrate animal or vertebrate animal (including any other animal organism) and declared to be a pest under section 3;
key_definitions.plant: Includes all horticultural or agricultural crops, trees, bushes or herbs and also includes the seed, fruit, leaves, trunk, roots, bark or cutting or any part thereof;
key_definitions.plant disease: Means any fungoid, bacterial virus, vegetable organism, parasitical or other disease, declared to be a plant disease under section 3.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called The Kerala Plant Diseases and Pests Act, 1972, extends to the whole of Kerala, and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as affected area, District Collector, Inspecting Officer, noxious weed, occupier, parasite, pest, plant, plant disease, prescribed, and State.

main_sections.section_title: Power to declare plant diseases, pests, parasites and noxious weeds.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to declare any disease, pest, parasite or weed as injurious to plants or likely to contaminate water supply or be obstructive to waterways. It also allows the Government to declare any area as an affected area and to take measures to eradicate such diseases, pests, parasites, or weeds, and to prevent their introduction, spread or re-appearance.

Authorises the District Collector, after issuing a notification, to direct any occupier within the affected area to carry out preventive or remedial measures for the removal or destruction of plants infested or likely to be infested. It also allows for directions to prohibit or restrict movement of plants, soil, or manure, and to prohibit plantation or growth of certain plants.

main_sections.section_title: Duties of occupier on the issue of notice under section 4.
main_sections.description: Stipulates that on the issue of a notice under section 4, every occupier in the affected area must carry out the preventive or remedial measures specified in such notice.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Inspecting Officer to enter upon any land, water or premises.
main_sections.description: Grants Inspecting Officers the power to enter any land, water or premises in an affected area for the purpose of ascertaining whether there is any plant disease, pest, parasite or noxious weed, or whether any prohibition or restriction imposed under section 3 has been complied with, or whether preventive or remedial measures have been carried out.

Empowers the Inspecting Officer, if an inspection reveals non-compliance with measures or restrictions, to carry out preventive or remedial measures. The cost of such measures is payable by the occupier. The Inspecting Officer can assess and direct the occupier to pay the assessed amount.

main_sections.section_title: Power to carry out measures in emergent situations.
main_sections.description: Allows the Government, through the District Collector or Inspecting Officer, to take immediate preventive or remedial measures if plants are in danger of being damaged or destroyed by any plant disease, pest, parasite or noxious weed. The cost of these measures can be recovered from the occupier.

Provides for an appeal against an order passed under section 7 or section 8 to the District Collector or other authority as specified by the Government, if the assessment of the amount payable or charges are unreasonable.
Details the penalties for contravening the provisions of the Act or any order, rule, or direction issued thereunder. Penalties include imprisonment and/or fines.
Specifies that offences under this Act are cognizable and can be tried by a Magistrate.

main_sections.section_title: Obligation of Village Officers to report plant diseases, pests, etc.
main_sections.description: Places an obligation on Village Officers to report any occurrence of plant diseases, pests, parasites, or noxious weeds to the authorities.
Empowers the Government to appoint Inspecting Officers for the purposes of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Bar of suits or other legal proceedings.
main_sections.description: Provides that no suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against any person for anything done or intended to be done in good faith under the Act.
Allows the Government to delegate its powers under the Act to any officer or authority subordinate to it.
Confers power on the Government to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.
Provides for the repeal of any law in force in the State of Kerala which is inconsistent with the provisions of this Act.

important_rules: Occupiers in affected areas must comply with preventive or remedial measures notified by the District Collector.
Movement of plants, soil, or manure can be prohibited or restricted.
Plantation or growth of certain plants that are likely to be injurious to other plants is prohibited.
Costs incurred by the government for carrying out measures can be recovered from the occupier.
Village Officers must report occurrences of plant diseases, pests, etc.

penalties: Fine or imprisonment or both for contravention of the Act, orders, rules, or directions.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: District Collector, Inspecting Officers, and other officers appointed by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, issuance of notices and directions, carrying out of preventive and remedial measures, imposition of penalties, and legal proceedings.

rights: Right to appeal against certain orders passed under sections 7 and 8.
duties: Duty of occupier to carry out preventive or remedial measures specified in a notice.
Duty of Village Officers to report plant diseases, pests, etc.
obligations: Occupiers are obligated to facilitate inspections and comply with directions issued by authorities.

key_procedures: Declaration of affected areas and harmful organisms (Section 3).
Issuance of directions by the District Collector to occupiers (Section 4).
Implementation of preventive and remedial measures by occupiers (Section 5).
Inspection by Inspecting Officers (Section 6).
Carrying out of measures by authorities at the occupier's cost (Section 7).
Action in emergent situations (Section 8).
Process of appeal against certain orders (Section 9).
administration: The Act is administered by the Government of Kerala, likely through its agriculture or related departments, with powers delegated to the District Collector and Inspecting Officers.
important_notes: The Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary No 741, dated 11th December, 1972.
The Act aims to prevent the introduction, spread, or re-appearance of plant diseases, pests, parasites, and noxious weeds.
The Government has the power to declare specific areas as 'affected areas' and to specify organisms as pests, diseases, parasites, or noxious weeds.

title: The Kerala Plantation Tax (Amendment) Act, 1975
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala Plantation Tax Act, 1960.
scope: Applies to plantations in Kerala.

key_definitions.authorised_representative: A person authorised by the assessee in writing to appear on his behalf, being (a) a person related to the assessee in any manner or a person regularly employed by the assessee; or (b) any officer of a Scheduled Bank with which the assessee maintains a current account or has other regular dealings; or (c) any legal practitioner who is entitled to practise in any civil court in India; or (d) an accountant; or (e) an income-tax practitioner or a salestax practitioner.
key_definitions.scheduled_bank: Means a Bank included in the Second Schedule to the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
key_definitions.accountant: Has the same meaning as in section 61 of the Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950 (XXII of 1950).
key_definitions.income_tax_practitioner: Has the same meaning as in section 61 of the Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950 (XXII of 1950).
key_definitions.salestax_practitioner: Means a person possessing the qualifications prescribed for a salestax practitioner under the Kerala General Sales-tax Act, 1963 (15 of 1963).

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Plantation Tax (Amendment) Act, 1975.
Amends section 3 of the Kerala Plantation Tax Act, 1960 (17 of 1960). The amendment pertains to the assessing authority's power to revise the extent of plantations held by an assessee.
Inserts a new section 25A, titled "Appearance by authorised representative", which outlines the conditions under which an authorised representative can appear for an assessee.

important_rules: Rule: An assessing authority may, at any time, suo motu revise the extent of plantations held by an assessee determined under section 5, after affording him a reasonable opportunity of being heard.

Rule: An assessing authority shall, on application by an assessee, revise the extent of plantations held by him determined under section 5, if it is proved to the satisfaction of the assessing authority that circumstances exist for revising the extent of plantations held by that assessee.
Rule: An application under clause (b) shall be in the prescribed form and shall be verified in the prescribed manner.
Rule: Where the extent of plantations has been revised under clause (a) or clause (b), the plantation tax payable thereon shall be assessed on the basis of the revised extent.

rights: Right to be afforded a reasonable opportunity of being heard by the assessing authority when the extent of plantations is revised suo motu.
Right to apply to the assessing authority for revision of the extent of plantations held, if circumstances exist.

key_procedures: Procedure for revision of extent of plantations: The assessing authority can revise the extent of plantations suo motu or upon application by the assessee. If suo motu, the assessee must be given a reasonable opportunity of being heard. If by application, the assessee must prove circumstances justifying the revision. The application must be in the prescribed form and verified accordingly.
Procedure for assessment after revision: After revision of the extent of plantations, the plantation tax payable shall be assessed on the basis of the revised extent.
administration: Assessing authority (specific department not explicitly stated, but implied to be the authority responsible for plantation tax assessment).

purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala Plantation Tax Act, 1960.

In schedule I to the principal Act, for the words "two hectares" in both the places where they occur, the words "one hectare" shall be substituted.

In schedule II to the principal Act, (a) for the figures "200", "450" and "1000", the figures "150", "400" and "750" respectively shall be substituted; (b) for the figures "1500", in both the places where they occur the figures "1200" shall be substituted.

important_rules: The Act is deemed to have come into force on April 1, 1971.
Changes in the wording and figures related to hectares and monetary values in the Kerala Plantation Tax Act, 1960, are specified.
The term 'two hectares' is replaced by 'one hectare' in Schedule I.
Specific figures in Schedule II related to plantation sizes or values are replaced.

title: THE KERALA PLANTATION TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1981
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Plantation Tax Act, 1960, for purposes to be hereafter appearing.
scope: The Act applies to any category of plantation and the tax is levied on the extent of plantations held by a person.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Plantation Tax (Amendment) Act, 1981.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new Schedule for Schedule I.
main_sections.description: For Schedule I to the Kerala Plantation Tax Act, 1960 (17 of 1960), the following Schedule shall be, and shall be deemed to have been, substituted with effect on and from the 1st day of April, 1981.

Provides for the application of the substituted Schedule and empowers the Government to issue notifications for specified reasons, and specifies rules for laying such notifications before the Legislative Assembly.

important_rules: Plantation tax is Nil where the aggregate extent of plantations held by a person does not exceed four hectares.
Plantation tax of Fifty rupees per hectare is levied on the extent of plantations in excess of four hectares where the aggregate extent exceeds four hectares but does not exceed eight hectares.
Plantation tax of Sixty rupees per hectare is levied on the extent of plantations in excess of eight hectares where the aggregate extent does not exceed twenty hectares.
Plantation tax of Ninety rupees per hectare is levied on the extent of plantations in excess of twenty hectares where the aggregate extent exceeds twenty hectares.
For plantations not exceeding four hectares, the tax is Nil.
For the first four hectares where the aggregate extent exceeds four hectares, the tax is Nil.
For the next sixteen hectares where the aggregate extent exceeds four hectares, the tax is Fifty rupees per hectare.
For the remaining extent where the aggregate extent exceeds four hectares, the tax is Seventy rupees per hectare.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications issued by the Government and laying them before the Legislative Assembly.

key_procedures: Substitution of Schedule I with effect from April 1, 1981.
Government may notify specified reasons for applying the new Schedule.
Notifications issued under this section shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly.
administration: Government of Kerala

The provisions regarding the new Schedule apply with effect from April 1, 1981.

Notifications laid before the Legislative Assembly may be subject to modifications.
The application of the amended provisions is limited to the period commencing on and from April 1, 1981, and not exceeding one year, as may be specified in such notification.

title: The Kerala Plantations (Additional Tax) Act, 1960
purpose: To provide for the levy of an additional tax on plantations in the State of Kerala.
scope: Extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. Applies to the levy of an additional tax on plantations in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.assessee: Any person by whom plantation tax or any other sum of money is payable under this Act, and includes every person in respect of whom any proceeding under this Act has been taken for the assessment of plantation tax payable by him.
key_definitions.appellate authority: Means the appellate authority appointed by the Government.
key_definitions.assessing authority: Means the assessing authority appointed by the Government.
key_definitions.company: Means a company as defined in section 3 of the Companies Act, 1956 (Central Act 1 of 1956), and includes a foreign company within the meaning of section 591 of that Act.
key_definitions.person: Means any individual or association of individuals holding any plantation for himself or for any other, or partly for himself and partly for another, whether as owner, tenant, mortgagee in possession, trustee, receiver, common manager, administrator or executor, or for any capacity recognized by law and includes a Hindu undivided family, an Aliya-santhana family or branch, a Marumakkathayam tarwad or tavazhi, a Nambudiri family or other family to which the provisions of the Kerala Nambudiri Act, 1958, apply, a firm, a company or a co-operative society registered or deemed to be registered under the Travancore-Cochin Co-operative Societies Act, 1932, and any institution capable of holding property;
key_definitions.plantation: Means land used for growing one or more of the following: (i) coconnut trees; (ii) arecanut trees; (iii) rubber plants; (iv) coffee plants; (v) tea plants; (vi) cardamom plants; (vii) pepper vines; (7) "prescribed" means prescribed by rules made under this Act;
key_definitions.to hold: With reference to a plantation means to be in possession of the plantation as owner or as tenant or as mort-gagee in possession.
key_definitions.valuation date: In relation to the financial year commencing on the first day of April, 1960, means the first day of September, 1960, and in relation to any other financial year for which an assessment is to be made under this Act means the first day of April of that year.

main_sections.description: States that the Act is called the Kerala Plantations (Additional Tax) Act, 1960, extends to the whole of the State of Kerala, and came into force on the first day of April, 1960.
Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'assessee', 'appellate authority', 'assessing authority', 'company', 'person', 'plantation', 'prescribed', and 'to hold'.

Imposes a charge of additional plantation tax on plantations for every financial year commencing on or after April 1, 1960, to be levied on the basis of valuation date as specified in Schedule I. It also clarifies that the tax is payable irrespective of the extent of land comprised in the plantations.

Requires every person holding five acres or more in extent of plantations to furnish a return to the assessing authority by a specified date. It also details the process for furnishing returns for subsequent years and what happens if a person fails to furnish a return or if the return is incorrect.

main_sections.section_title: Determination of extent of plantation and the assessment of plantation tax.
main_sections.description: Deals with the process of determining the extent of a plantation and assessing the plantation tax. It outlines how the assessing authority can make a provisional assessment if a return is not furnished or is found to be incorrect, and how to revise assessments.

Details the procedure for making a provisional assessment by the assessing authority, at any time after the receipt of a return, or in cases where no return is filed. It also mentions that any amount paid towards a provisional assessment is adjustable against the regular assessment.

main_sections.section_title: Cancellation of assessment in certain cases.
main_sections.description: Provides for the cancellation of an assessment if a person proves to the satisfaction of the assessing authority that a notice of demand was issued without sufficient cause, or that he did not receive it, or was prevented from complying with it. The assessing authority shall cancel the assessment and proceed for a fresh assessment in accordance with the provisions of section 5.
States that when any plantation tax is due, the assessing authority shall issue a notice of demand in the prescribed form.

Outlines the right to appeal against an assessment or any order passed under the Act. It specifies the authorities to whom appeals can be made, the timelines for filing appeals, and the powers of the appellate authority, including the ability to confirm, reduce, enhance, or annul the assessment.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of revision of Board of Revenue.
main_sections.description: Grants the Board of Revenue the power to call for and examine the record of any proceeding, and to pass such orders as it thinks fit, for the purpose of satisfying itself as to the legality, correctness, or propriety of any assessment or other order.

Allows the appellate authority or assessing authority to rectify any mistake apparent from the record, either of their own motion or on an application by the assessee, within three years from the date of the order. This rectification can involve enhancing or reducing an assessment or refund. It also clarifies that such rectification shall not result in reducing or enhancing an assessment without giving the assessee a reasonable opportunity of being heard.

main_sections.section_title: Power to take evidence on oath, etc.
main_sections.description: Empowers the appellate authority and assessing authority to take evidence on oath, to enforce the attendance of any person, and to compel the production of documents and the issuing of commissions.
Specifies that any amount of plantation tax due shall be recoverable as an arrear of land revenue. It also mentions recovery through installments and by way of sale of immovable property.
States that unpaid plantation tax shall bear interest at the rate of nine percent per annum from the date of default.
Provides for the refund of any amount of plantation tax paid by an assessee which is found to be in excess of the amount properly assessable under the Act for that year.

main_sections.section_title: Power to set off amount of refund against tax remaining payable.
main_sections.description: Allows the assessing authority or the appellate authority to set off any amount due for refund against any tax remaining payable by the assessee.

No claim for refund of plantation tax shall be admitted unless it is made within one year from the date of the order of assessment or where an appeal or application for revision has been preferred, within one year from the date of the order in appeal or revision.

States that if any person makes a false statement in a verification mentioned in section 4 or section 9 which is false and which he either knows or believes to be false or does not believe to be true, he shall be deemed to have committed the offence described in section 177 of the Indian Penal Code.

main_sections.section_title: Failure to furnish return or document.
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for failure to furnish a return or document. This includes a penalty of fine for failure to furnish a return or document by the specified date, and a further daily fine if the default continues. It also states that a person who fails to produce or cause to be produced, as required by notice, any document or accounts shall be punishable with fine.
Grants the assessing authority the power to call for any information or produce any document as it may deem necessary for the purposes of the Act.
Deals with the prosecution of offences under the Act. It outlines the procedure for launching prosecutions and the authorities responsible for sanctioning them.

Specifies that no court shall take cognizance of an offence under the Act except upon a complaint in writing made by the assessing authority or any other officer empowered in this behalf by the State Government.
Deals with the territorial jurisdiction for the purpose of assessment.
Specifies the manner in which notices under the Act are to be served on assessees.

main_sections.section_title: Power to grant extension of time for returns, etc.
main_sections.description: Grants the assessing authority the power to extend the time for furnishing returns or documents.
Empowers the State Government to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of the Act.
Provides for the remission of plantation tax in certain cases as may be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Bar of suits in civil courts.
main_sections.description: Stipulates that no suit shall be brought in any civil court to set aside or modify any assessment or order made under the Act.
Details how periods of limitation are to be computed under the Act.
Allows the State Government to delegate its powers under the Act to any officer.
Empowers the State Government to remove any difficulties that may arise in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Details the rates at which plantation tax shall be levied and collected. (Content not fully visible in the provided images, but implied to contain tax rates).
Likely contains further details or tables related to the Act. (Content not fully visible in the provided images).

important_rules: Rule: Plantation tax is payable for every financial year commencing from April 1, 1960.
Rule: Returns must be furnished by individuals holding five acres or more in extent of plantations to the assessing authority by the prescribed date.
Rule: Failure to furnish a return or document can result in penalties, including a fine of not less than five rupees for every day during which the default continues.
Rule: False statements in declarations are considered an offence under the Indian Penal Code.
Rule: Plantation tax not paid on the due date shall bear interest at the rate of nine percent per annum from the date of default.

penalties: Fine for failure to furnish return or document, which may extend to five rupees for every day during which the default continues.
Fine for producing or causing to be produced, as required by notice, any document or accounts not produced, which may extend to five rupees for every day during which the default continues.
Offences related to false statements in declaration are treated as offences under section 177 of the Indian Penal Code.
Interest at the rate of nine percent per annum on delayed payment of plantation tax.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Assessing Authority, Appellate Authority, Board of Revenue, State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notices of demand, recovery proceedings as arrears of land revenue, prosecution for offences, imposition of fines and interest.

rights: Right to appeal against assessment orders.
Right to claim refund of excess tax paid.
Right to be heard before any reduction or enhancement of assessment in rectification proceedings.
duties: Duty to furnish returns related to plantations.
Duty to provide information and documents when called for by the assessing authority.
Duty to pay plantation tax on the due date.
obligations: Obligation to comply with notices of demand.
Obligation to pay plantation tax as determined by the assessing authority.

key_procedures: Procedure for furnishing returns: Individuals holding five acres or more must submit a return by the thirty-first day of December of every year. Subsequent years require returns by the first day of April.
Procedure for assessment: The assessing authority determines the extent of plantation and assesses the tax payable based on the valuation date and prescribed rates.
Procedure for appeal: An assessee aggrieved by an assessment order can appeal to the appellate authority within a specified period.
Procedure for rectification of mistakes: Assessees can apply for rectification of mistakes in assessment orders within three years.
Procedure for recovery of tax: Unpaid tax can be recovered as arrears of land revenue, with interest on defaults.
administration: The Act is administered by the assessing authorities appointed by the Government, with appellate authorities and the Board of Revenue having oversight and revisionary powers.
important_notes: The Act came into force on April 1, 1960.
Published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 24th August, 1960.
Limitation period for claims for refund is one year from the date of the order.
Civil courts are barred from setting aside or modifying any assessment or order made under the Act.
The State Government has the power to make rules and remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.

title: The Kerala Plantations (Additional Tax) Amendment Act, 1967
purpose: To amend the Kerala Plantations (Additional Tax) Act, 1960, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Plantations (Additional Tax) Act, 1960.

key_definitions.plantation: Not explicitly defined, but the act deals with land used for plantations.
key_definitions.tax: The act refers to 'additional tax' and 'plantation tax'.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Plantations (Additional Tax) Amendment Act, 1967. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Amends section 1 of the Kerala Plantations (Additional Tax) Act, 1960, by substituting the words 'Kerala Plantation Tax Act' for 'Kerala Plantations (Additional Tax) Act'.

Amends section 3 of the principal Act. In sub-section (1), for the words 'an additional tax', the words 'a tax' shall be substituted. For sub-section (5), the following sub-section shall be substituted: '(5) The tax charged on any land under this section shall be in addition to the land revenue or any tax in lieu thereof, if any, payable in respect of such land.'
Amends section 4 of the principal Act, by substituting the words 'two hectares' for 'five acres'.

Inserts a new section 6A titled 'Plantations escaping assessment'. This section deals with instances where the whole or any portion of a plantation chargeable to the plantation tax for any financial year has escaped assessment. It outlines the process for assessment and notice.

Amends section 9 of the principal Act. It introduces provisions for reference to the District Court regarding questions and limitations under sub-section (1) and how the District Court should handle such references and appeals.

Inserts a new section 9A titled 'Reference to District Court'. This section details the process of referring questions of law to the District Court, including conditions, time limits, and the procedure for the District Court to consider and decide upon such references.

Amends section 10 of the principal Act by inserting a proviso: 'Provided further that no order passed on the basis of the judgment passed on a reference under section 9A, shall, in so far as it relates to matters covered by the judgment, be subjected to revision by the Board of Revenue.'

Amends section 14 of the principal Act, by substituting the words 'land revenue or any tax in lieu thereof, if any, payable in respect of the land comprised in the plantation' for the words 'basic tax'.

Inserts a new section 31A titled 'Exemption'. This section empowers the Government, by notification in the Gazette, to exempt any plantation held by any public body or institution from the provisions of this Act, if the Government is satisfied that such exemption is necessary in the public interest. It also details the procedure for making such exemptions effective and subject to modification by the Legislative Assembly.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new Schedules for Schedules I and II
main_sections.description: Substitutes new Schedules I and II for the existing Schedules I and II of the principal Act. Schedule I specifies the rates of plantation tax based on the extent of plantations. Schedule II defines the 'extent of plantations' for the purposes of assessment, detailing how to calculate it based on different types of trees and crops.

important_rules: Tax charged on any land under section 3 is in addition to land revenue or any other tax payable on that land.
Exemptions from the Act can be granted by the Government by notification if deemed necessary in the public interest.
Any exemption granted by the Government is subject to modification by the Legislative Assembly.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government, Board of Revenue (for revisions), District Court (for references).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment, appeals to the District Court, and potential exemptions by Government notification.

rights: Right to appeal or refer questions of law to the District Court.
Right to receive notice in case of escaped assessment.
duties: Duty to pay plantation tax as per the provisions of the Act.
Duty to comply with notices issued under the Act.
obligations: Obligation to have plantations assessed for tax purposes.
Obligation to adhere to the defined methods for calculating the extent of plantations.

key_procedures: Procedure for assessment of plantations that have escaped assessment, including issuing notice and determining the extent.
Procedure for referring questions of law to the District Court, including conditions, time limits, and the District Court's role in hearing and deciding such references.
Procedure for the Government to grant exemptions, including notification and potential modification by the Legislative Assembly.
Procedure for calculating the extent of plantations for tax assessment purposes as defined in Schedule II.
administration: The Government (specifically mentioned in relation to notifications and exemptions), and the Board of Revenue (in relation to revisions).
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Kerala Plantations (Additional Tax) Act, 1960.
The commencement date of the Act is to be notified by the Government in the Gazette.
The rates of plantation tax are detailed in Schedule I.
The method of calculating the extent of plantations is detailed in Schedule II.
Any decision made on a reference to the District Court regarding section 9A is not subject to revision by the Board of Revenue concerning matters covered by that judgment.

title: THE KERALA POLICE (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1979
purpose: To amend the Kerala Police Act, 1960, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Police Act, 1960.

key_definitions.arms: For the purposes of section 21A, 'arms' means any type of offensive weapon and includes lathi, dand and stick.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Police (Amendment) Act, 1979. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Inserts a new section 21A into the Kerala Police Act, 1960. This new section relates to the power to prohibit mass drill, mass training, etc.
Amends section 25 of the principal Act by substituting 'order in writing' for 'order' and 'section 21A' for 'section 21' in specific clauses.
Inserts a new section 57A into the principal Act, concerning contravention of prohibition made under section 21A.
