important_rules: Rule 1: The District Magistrate may, whenever he considers it necessary so to do for the preservation of the public peace or public safety or for the maintenance of public order, by public notice or by order directed to individuals, prohibit, in any area within his jurisdiction, the holding of, or taking part in, any mass drill or mass training with arms or the carrying of arms in any procession.
Rule 2: No prohibition under section 21A shall remain in force for more than three months.

Rule 3: Whoever contravenes any prohibition made under section 21A shall, on conviction, be liable to imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, but which shall not be less than three months, and with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, but not less than three months.
Fine which may extend to two thousand rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: District Magistrate
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Issuing public notices or direct orders to individuals to prohibit mass drill, mass training, or carrying of arms. Enforcement also involves prosecution for contravention of prohibition orders.

obligations: Individuals must comply with prohibitions on holding or participating in mass drills or training, or carrying arms, when ordered by the District Magistrate for public peace, safety, or order.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: The District Magistrate may issue a public notice or a direct order to individuals to prohibit mass drills, mass training, or the carrying of arms in any area within their jurisdiction to preserve public peace, safety, or maintain public order.
Procedure 2: Any prohibition issued under section 21A is limited to a maximum duration of three months.
Procedure 3: Contravention of a prohibition order made under section 21A leads to liability for imprisonment and a fine.
administration: The Government (specifically mentioning the District Magistrate for issuing orders).
important_notes: Any prohibition under section 21A shall not remain in force for more than three months.
The act was received by the assent of the Governor on the 5th November, 1979 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 797, dated 6th November, 1979.

title: THE KERALA POLICE (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2000
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Police Act, 1960.
scope: Applies to actions related to physical training and permits issued under the Kerala Police Act, 1960.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Kerala Police (Amendment) Act, 2000, and states it came into force on the 18th day of January, 2000.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new sections after section 18
main_sections.description: Inserts new sections 18A and 18B into the Kerala Police Act, 1960, dealing with regulation of certain physical training and power to cancel permits.
Inserts new section 53B into the principal Act, dealing with penalties for contravention of section 18A.
Amends section 69 of the principal Act by inserting clauses regarding the grant of permits under section 18A and the procedure for appealing under sub-section (2) of section 18B.

Repeals the Kerala Police (Amendment) Ordinance, 2000 (1 of 2000) and states that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Regulation of certain physical training (Section 18A): Anything contained in any other law notwithstanding, a person can, by himself or by any person on his behalf, impart training to any member or members of the public in any physical activity involving methods of attack or self-defence unless he holds a permit issued by an authority as may be prescribed. Alternatively, the use of any premises, owned or possessed by him, for such training or organised participation in such training may be imparted by any person who does not hold a permit in that behalf. Such permits are for a period of three months, extendable by the Government by not exceeding six months, and shall not apply to educational institutions, clubs or gymnasiums recognised by the Kerala Sports council.
Permits are subject to conditions, restrictions, and fees as prescribed by rules. Police Officers below the rank of Sub-Inspector have free access to any place of training.
Contravention of provisions of section 18A is a cognizable and non-bailable offence. No prosecution without the sanction of the District Magistrate.

Power to cancel permits (Section 18B): The authority notified under sub-section (1) of section 18A may cancel or suspend a permit for reasons including non-payment of fees, breach of terms and conditions, or if the holder is convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude.
Appeals against permit cancellation/suspension orders lie with the Deputy Inspector General of Police.

penalties: Penalty for contravention of section 18A: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or fine which may extend to five thousand rupees or both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The authority notified under sub-section (1) of section 18A, and in case of appeals against permit cancellation/suspension, the Deputy Inspector General of Police.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through cancellation or suspension of permits, prosecution for contravention of section 18A, and appeals to higher authorities.

rights: Right to impart training in physical activity and self-defence under a permit (Section 18A).
Right to appeal against an order cancelling or suspending a permit (Section 18B).
duties: Duty to hold a permit for imparting training in physical activity and self-defence (Section 18A).
Duty to comply with the terms and conditions of the permit.
Duty to ensure that training is conducted in accordance with the Act and rules made thereunder.
Duty of Police Officers to have free access to training places.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining a permit for physical training (implied).
Procedure for appealing against the cancellation or suspension of a permit (Section 18B).
administration: Kerala Police
important_notes: The Act came into force on the 18th day of January, 2000.
A permit issued under section 18A is for a period of three months from the said date or within such period, as may be extended by the Government, which shall not exceed six months.

The provisions of sub-section (1) of section 18A shall not apply to an educational institution, owned or controlled by the Government or affiliated to any University in the State, as part of the curriculum or course of study; or a club or gymnasium recognised by the Kerala Sports council.
Contravention of section 18A is a cognizable and non-bailable offence.
No prosecution for contravention of section 18A without the previous sanction of the District Magistrate.
The Kerala Police (Amendment) Ordinance, 2000 (1 of 2000) is repealed.

title: THE KERALA POLICE (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2007
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Police Act, 1960 to make certain measures for improving the functioning of the Police in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Authority or Authorities: means the Police complaints Authority established at the State level and at the District level, respectively, under section 17E
key_definitions.Board: means the Police Establishment Board constituted under section 17 C
key_definitions.Commission: means the State Security Commission constituted under section 17 A

main_sections.description: States that this may be called the Kerala Police (Amendment) Act, 2007 and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 7th day of April, 2007.
Amends section 2 of the Kerala Police Act, 1960 by inserting new clauses relating to 'Authority' or 'Authorities', 'Board', and 'Commission'.

Inserts a new section 3A titled 'Separation of Investigation from Law and Order'. This section states that the Government may, having regard to the population in an area or the circumstances prevailing in such area, by order, separate the investigating police from the law and order police in such area as may be specified in order to speedier investigation, better expertise and improved rapport with people. It also states that the Superintendent of Police shall ensure the full co-ordination between the two wings of the police force separated under sub-section (1).

Substitutes section 4 of the principal Act. The administration of the police throughout the State shall, subject to the control of the Government, be vested in the Director General of Police. The Director General of Police shall be appointed by the Government from amongst those officers of the State cadre of the Indian Police Service who have either already been promoted to such rank or are eligible to be promoted to such rank, considering his overall record of service and experience for leading the police force of the State. It also states that provided that the officer selected as the Director General of Police must not have a charge pending against him in any Court or Tribunal or Departmental agency on a charge filed on behalf of the State.

The Government may ensure a minimum tenure or two years from the date of assuming charge of the post to the Director General of Police and to all Inspector Generals of Police in charge of Ranges, Superintendents of Police in charge of Districts and Station House Officers in charge of Police Stations. This provision does not apply in cases of superannuation, promotion, reversion, suspension and leave. The Government or the appointing authority may, without prejudice to any other legal or departmental action, transfer any police officer before completing the normal tenure of two years, on being satisfied prima facie that it is necessary to do so on any of the following grounds, namely: (a) if he is found incompetent and inefficient in the discharge of duties so as to affect the functioning of the police force, (b) if he is accused in a criminal case involving moral turpitude; (c) initiation of departmental proceedings against him; (d) if he exhibits a palpable bias in the discharge of duties; (e) misuse or abuse of powers vested in him; (f) incapacity in the discharge of official duties; (g) initiation of an enquiry against him by competent authority on a grave allegation of corruption or indifference in the discharge of duty; (h) if his conduct has been adversely commented upon by any judicial authority; (i) disorder or rampant crime on his area of jurisdiction; (j) public dissatisfaction with the effectiveness of policing in the jurisdiction, and (k) if he request to be transferred from the post.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new Chapter III A
main_sections.description: Inserts a new Chapter III A titled 'STATE SECURITY COMMISSION, POLICE ESTABLISHMENT BOARD AND POLICE COMPLAINTS AUTHORITY'.

Repeals The Kerala Police (Amendment) Ordinance, 2007 (45 of 2007) and states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act, as amended by this Act.

important_rules: The Superintendent of Police shall ensure the full co-ordination between the two wings of the police force separated under sub-section (1) of section 3A.

The Director General of Police shall be appointed by the Government from amongst those officers of the State cadre of the Indian Police Service who have either already been promoted to such rank or are eligible to be promoted to such rank, considering his overall record of service and experience for leading the police force of the State.
The Director General of Police must not have a charge pending against him in any Court or Tribunal or Departmental agency on a charge filed on behalf of the State.

duties: The Superintendent of Police shall ensure the full co-ordination between the two wings of the police force separated under sub-section (1) of section 3A.
obligations: The Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, constitute a State Security Commission for the purpose of exercising such functions and discharging such duties as may be assigned to the Commission under this Act.

The Government may constitute a Police Establishment Board which shall be departmental body consisting of the Director General of Police as Chairman and four other senior Police Officers of the Department of the rank of Additional Director General of Police as members.

The Government shall establish a Police Complaints Authority at the State level to look in to complaints of grave misconduct of all types against police officers and above the rank of Superintendent of Police.
The Government shall establish Police Complaints Authority at the district level to look into complaints against police officers of and up to the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police.

key_procedures: Separation of Investigation from Law and Order: The Government may, having regard to the population in an area or the circumstances prevailing in such area, by order, separate the investigating police from the law and order police in such area as may be specified in order to speedier investigation, better expertise and improved rapport with people.

Appointment of Director General of Police: The Government shall appoint the Director General of Police from officers of the State cadre of the Indian Police Service who have already been promoted or are eligible for promotion, considering their service record and experience.
Constitution of State Security Commission: The Government may constitute a State Security Commission by notification in the Official Gazette, to exercise assigned functions and duties.

Constitution of Police Establishment Board: The Government may constitute a Police Establishment Board, a departmental body, with the Director General of Police as Chairman and four senior Police Officers.

Establishment of State Police Complaints Authority: The Government shall establish a Police Complaints Authority at the State level to address complaints of grave misconduct against police officers of and above the rank of Superintendent.

Establishment of District Police Complaints Authority: The Government shall establish Police Complaints Authority at the district level to address complaints against police officers of and up to the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police.
administration: The Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Kerala Police (Amendment) Ordinance, 2007 (45 of 2007) is repealed, but actions taken under it are saved.
The minimum tenure of two years for Director General of Police, Inspector Generals of Police, and Station House Officers is applicable, with specific grounds for early transfer.

The State Security Commission consists of the Minister in-charge of Home Department as Chairman, Minister in-charge of Law, the Leader of Opposition, the Chief Secretary (ex-officio), the Secretary to Government, Home Department (ex-officio), the Director General of Police (ex-officio), and three non-official members.

title: THE KERALA POLICE (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 1979
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Police Act, 1960, for the purpose hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to acts related to police and possession of stolen property within Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Police (Second Amendment) Act, 1979.

After section 53 of the Police Act, 1960 (5 of 1961), the following section shall be inserted, namely:- '53 A. Penalty for possession of property believed to have been stolen.--Whoever is found in possession or is proved to have been in possession of anything which there is reason to believe to be stolen property or property fraudulently obtained and for the possession of which he fails satisfactorily to account, shall on conviction be liable to fine not exceeding one hundred rupees or to imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months or to both.'

important_rules: Rule 1: Whoever is found in possession or is proved to have been in possession of anything which there is reason to believe to be stolen property or property fraudulently obtained, and for the possession of which they fail to account satisfactorily, is subject to penalty.
Rule 2: The penalty for such possession is a fine not exceeding one hundred rupees or imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months or both.

penalties: Fine not exceeding one hundred rupees
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months
Or both
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be the police/judicial system responsible for enforcing the Police Act, 1960.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through conviction in a court of law upon being found in possession of suspected stolen property and failing to provide a satisfactory account.

duties: Duty to satisfactorily account for the possession of property believed to be stolen or fraudulently obtained.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: A person is found in possession of property, and there is reason to believe it is stolen or fraudulently obtained.
Procedure 2: The person must account satisfactorily for the possession of the property.
Procedure 3: If the account is not satisfactory, the person may be convicted and face penalties.
administration: Not explicitly stated in the provided text.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 5th December, 1979 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 874, dated 6th December, 1979.

title: The Kerala Police Act, 1960
purpose: To provide for the maintenance of public order and tranquility, the prevention and detection of crime, and the regulation of certain activities by the police.
scope: Applies to the entire state of Kerala and all persons within its jurisdiction, with specific provisions related to the duties and powers of police officers.

main_sections.section_title: Issue of orders for maintenance of order at religious ceremonials, etc.
main_sections.description: Empowers the District Magistrate to issue orders for the maintenance of order at religious ceremonies, public displays, or exhibitions, to prevent obstruction, annoyance, or danger to the public. Orders can be for prohibition, regulation, or attendance restrictions. Such orders must be published and conform to the law.

Outlines the comprehensive duties of every police officer, including serving summons, executing warrants, investigating cognizable offenses, preventing public nuisances, apprehending offenders, assisting in the maintenance of public peace, and performing other lawful duties.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of police on the occasion of fire
main_sections.description: Grants police officers the power to remove or order the removal of any person whose presence interferes with fire-fighting operations, and to take measures to extinguish fires or save life and property.

main_sections.section_title: Power to seize stolen property to be stolen.
main_sections.description: Details the authority of a police officer to seize suspected stolen property and the procedure for its examination and retention, including the role of the Magistrate.

main_sections.section_title: Powers to search for stolen property in certain cases without warrant.
main_sections.description: Allows police officers in certain areas to search for stolen property in dwelling-houses or other places without a warrant, if reasonable grounds exist, and to seize such property. This power is extended to places within the jurisdiction of the Magistrate. The search is to be conducted in accordance with the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.
Requires pawnbrokers and other dealers of certain articles to report stolen property and furnish information to the police. Failure to comply can lead to fines.

main_sections.section_title: Police officers above the rank of a constable may enter and inspect liquor shop, etc., without warrant.
main_sections.description: Empowers police officers above the rank of a constable to enter and inspect liquor shops and other establishments selling intoxicating drugs without a warrant.

main_sections.section_title: A superior police officer may himself perform duties imposed on his inferior, etc.
main_sections.description: Allows a superior police officer to perform duties assigned to a subordinate officer, and to delegate powers to a subordinate officer if deemed necessary. They can also suspend or prevent their subordinates from acting in certain situations.

main_sections.section_title: Police officer may lay information, etc.
main_sections.description: States that a police officer can lay information before a Magistrate and apply for summons, warrants, search-warrants, or other lawful process, acting in legal capacity.

main_sections.section_title: Persons bound to conform to reasonable directions of police
main_sections.description: Mandates that all persons must conform to reasonable directions issued by a police officer in the execution of their duty. Police officers can also arrest persons resisting or refusing to comply with such directions.

main_sections.section_title: Certificate, arms, etc., to be delivered up by person ceasing to be a police officer.--
main_sections.description: Requires every member of the police force, upon suspension or ceasing to be a police officer, to deliver up their certificate, arms, and accoutrements to their immediate superior. Failure to do so is an offense.

main_sections.section_title: Unlawful assumption of police functions, personation of police, etc.--
main_sections.description: Prohibits unlawful assumption of police functions or personation of a police officer, which is an offense.

main_sections.section_title: Penalties for neglect of duties, etc.--
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for police officers who contravene provisions of Section 15, are guilty of cowardice, or neglect their duties.

main_sections.section_title: Vexatious entry, search, arrest, etc., by police officers.--
main_sections.description: Penalizes police officers for vexatious entry, search, arrest, or seizure, and for unnecessary detention or delaying forwarding persons to a Magistrate, or for personal violence or holding threats without cause.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for exacting unauthorized fees, etc.--
main_sections.description: Imposes penalties on police officers for exacting unauthorized fees or receiving fees, gratuities, or allowances from people other than what is permitted by law.
Penalizes police officers who extort or attempt to extort property or valuable security through threat or by omitting or delaying to do an act which they are legally bound to do.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for false alarm of fire.--
main_sections.description: Punishes anyone who gives or causes to be given a false alarm of fire, which is an offense.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for certain offences on streets and open places.--
main_sections.description: Outlines punishments for various offenses committed on streets and open places, including slaughtering animals, damaging property, driving vehicles without care, obstructing traffic, violating traffic rules, and displaying offensive signs or markings.
Penalizes anyone who commits wilful trespass on any dwelling house or other building or on any land or ground attached thereto, without reasonable excuse and with intent to commit an offense.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for being found armed between sunset and sunrise
main_sections.description: Penalizes individuals found armed between sunset and sunrise with the intent to commit an offense or having their face covered or disguised.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for buying or taking pledge from a child.--
main_sections.description: Penalizes anyone who buys or takes a pledge from a child under a certain age.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for placing lights, etc., over or near any public place.--
main_sections.description: Penalizes placing lights, fire-balloons, fireworks, or sending up fire-balloons over or near any public place in a manner that may cause danger.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months, or fine which may extend to one hundred rupees, or both (Section 41)
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or fine which may extend to two hundred rupees, or both (Section 39, 41)
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or both (Section 42)
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to twelve months, or fine which may extend to one hundred rupees, or both (Section 44)
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to fifty rupees (Section 45)
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months and also fine (Section 46)
Imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months or fine not exceeding five hundred rupees or both (Section 47)
Imprisonment for a term not exceeding three months (Section 48, 49)
Fine which may extend to fifty rupees (Section 46)
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Police officers, District Magistrate, Magistrate.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through orders, summons, warrants, arrests, searches, and imposition of penalties as prescribed by the Act and the Code of Criminal Procedure.

rights: Right to search for stolen property in certain cases without warrant (Section 32)
Right to enter and inspect liquor shops without warrant (Section 34)
Right to perform duties imposed on inferiors and delegate powers (Section 36)
duties: To promptly serve every summons, obey and execute all orders and warrants lawfully issued (Section 29(a))
To collect and communicate information regarding cognizable offenses (Section 29(b))
To prevent the commission of cognizable offenses and their investigation (Section 29(b))
To preserve the peace and prevent public nuisances (Section 29(c))
To apprehend persons legally authorized to apprehend (Section 29(d))
To assist in maintaining public peace and order (Section 29(e))
To discharge such duties as are imposed by any law for the time being in force (Section 29(g))
To prevent injury attempted to be committed in view of public property or its removal (Section 29(h))
To afford every assistance within their power to disabled or helpless persons (Section 29(i))
To take prompt measures to procure necessary help for persons under arrest or in custody (Section 29(j))
To arrange for sustenance and shelter of every person under arrest or in custody (Section 29(k))
To use best endeavors to prevent loss or damage by fire (Section 29(l)(i))
To exert best endeavors to prevent accident or danger by fire (Section 29(l)(ii))
To prevent obstruction therein and traffic therein (Section 29(l)(iii))
To keep order in streets and public places (Section 29(m))
To regulate public bathing, washing, and landing places (Section 29(n))
To take charge of unclaimed property (Section 29(o))
To prevent entry into dwelling houses or other buildings without reasonable excuse (Section 29(p))
To perform all duties imposed by law in the manner and subject to conditions therein prescribed (Section 29(r))
To remove or order the removal of persons interfering with fire-fighting operations (Section 30(a))
To call on persons in charge of any fire-engine to render assistance (Section 30(c))
To take measures as may appear necessary for the preservation of life and property (Section 30(d))
To deliver up certificate, arms, etc., upon ceasing to be a police officer (Section 39(1))
To conform to reasonable directions of police officers (Section 38(1))
obligations: To execute all orders and warrants lawfully issued to them (Section 29(a))
To investigate cognizable offenses and take other steps consistent with law (Section 29(b))
To preserve the peace and prevent public nuisances (Section 29(c))
To apprehend persons whom they are legally authorized to apprehend (Section 29(d))
To assist in the maintenance of public peace and order (Section 29(e))
To provide necessary help for persons under arrest or in custody (Section 29(j))
To arrange for the proper sustenance and shelter of every person under arrest or in custody (Section 29(k))
To prevent obstruction and danger to the public from fire (Section 29(l)(iii))
To prevent obstruction therein and to the best of their ability prevent the infraction of any rule or order made under this Act or any other law (Section 29(l)(iii))
To regulate public bathing, washing, and landing places (Section 29(n))
To take charge of unclaimed property (Section 29(o))
To prevent entry into dwelling houses or other buildings without reasonable excuse (Section 29(p))
To take measures as may appear necessary for the preservation of life and property (Section 30(d))
To deliver up certificate, arms, etc., upon suspension or ceasing to be a police officer (Section 39(1))
To obey and execute lawful orders and warrants (Section 29(a))

key_procedures: Issuance of orders by District Magistrate for maintenance of order at religious ceremonies, public displays, or exhibitions, including prohibition, regulation, or attendance restrictions (Section 28).
Procedure for police officers to collect and communicate information regarding cognizable offenses, prevent their commission, and investigate them (Section 29(b)).
Procedure for apprehending offenders and persons legally authorized to be apprehended (Section 29(d)).
Procedure for police officers to seize suspected stolen property and the role of the Magistrate in examination and retention (Section 31).
Procedure for searching for stolen property in certain areas without a warrant and seizure of such property, conducted in accordance with the Code of Criminal Procedure (Section 32).
Procedure for pawnbrokers and dealers to report stolen property and furnish information to the police (Section 33).
Procedure for police officers to lay information before a Magistrate and apply for summons, warrants, or search-warrants (Section 37).
Procedure for police officers to deliver up their certificate, arms, and accoutrements upon suspension or ceasing to be a police officer (Section 39(1)).
Procedure for obtaining a warrant to search for and seize articles or documents by the Inspector-General or any Magistrate (Section 39(2)).
Procedure for applying for summons, warrants, search-warrants, or other lawful process before a Magistrate (Section 37).
Procedure for dealing with individuals found armed between sunset and sunrise with intent to commit an offense (Section 48).
administration: The Kerala Police Department, under the overall supervision of the Home Department of the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: Orders issued by the District Magistrate under Section 28 must be published and conform to the law.
Penalties for various offenses are specified, including imprisonment and fines.
The Act refers to the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, for certain procedures like searches.
Police officers above the rank of constable have specific powers to enter and inspect liquor shops without warrant (Section 34).
Superior police officers can perform duties of their subordinates and delegate powers (Section 36).
All persons are bound to conform to reasonable directions of police officers (Section 38).
Penalties for certain offenses on streets and open places are detailed in Section 46, covering a wide range of public order and traffic violations.

title: The Kerala Police Act, 2011 Erratum
purpose: To correct errors in the published translation in English of the Kerala Police Act, 2011 (Act 8 of 2011) and its corresponding errata notification.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Police Act, 2011, and specifically addresses errors in the published English translation and related notifications.
important_rules: The penalties stated in items (a) to (j) of sub-section (6) of section 101 shall not be treated as a bar for the promotion of a police officer.
The penalties stated in items (a) to (j) above shall not normally be treated as a bar for the promotion of a police officer.

rights: The right of police officers for promotion, which shall not be unduly barred by certain penalties.

administration: Law (Legislation-E) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: This is an erratum notification for the Kerala Police Act, 2011.
The correction pertains to the English translation and its interpretation regarding the impact of certain penalties on promotion.

title: THE KERALA PRESERVATION OF TREES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2003
purpose: To amend the Kerala Preservation of Trees Act, 1986.
scope: Applies to all land in Kerala. The act aims to prevent the cutting or causing to be cut any tree on any land without obtaining permission under this section.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Preservation of Trees (Amendment) Act, 2003 and that it shall come into force at once.

Amends section 4 of the Kerala Preservation of Trees Act, 1986, by inserting a new sub-section (6). This sub-section states that notwithstanding anything contained in the section or in any judgement, decree or order of any court, the owner of any land shall have the right to cut or cause to be cut any tree, other than a tree as defined in clause (e) of section 2, standing on such land, without obtaining a permission under this section.

important_rules: Owners of land have the right to cut or cause to be cut any tree on their land, except those defined in clause (e) of section 2, without requiring permission under this section.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not specified in the provided text.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not specified in the provided text.

rights: The right of a land owner to cut or cause to be cut any tree on their land, with the exception of certain trees, without requiring permission.

key_procedures: To cut or cause to be cut any tree on land, an owner generally needs permission. However, this amendment grants an exception for certain trees, allowing them to be cut without such permission.
administration: Not specified in the provided text.
important_notes: The amendment applies notwithstanding any existing judgement, decree or order of any court.
The exception for cutting trees does not apply to trees as defined in clause (e) of section 2 of the principal Act.

title: THE KERALA PRESERVATION OF PRIVATE FORESTS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1973
purpose: An Act to amend the Kerala Preservation of Private Forests Act, 1972.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala. Specifically, it deals with private forests, their preservation, and restrictions on their use, particularly concerning 'forest trees'.

key_definitions.forest tree: means a tree of any species other than the following, namely:— Erithrina Indica and Erithrina Lithosperma (Murukkų), Rubber (Havea Braziliensis), Jack (Artocarpus Integrifolia), Cashew (Anacardium Occidentale), Tamarind, Mango and Macaranga Pettata.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Preservation of Private Forests (Amendment) Act, 1973 and came into force on the 10th day of February, 1973.
Inserts a definition for 'forest tree' in section 2 of the Kerala Preservation of Private Forests Act, 1972.

Inserts a new section, 3A, into the principal Act, which deals with restrictions in respect of exempted lands. It states that no owner of any land which is not a private forest as defined in the Act, but to which the provisions of the Madras Preservation of Private Forests Act, 1949, applied immediately before the 10th day of May, 1971, and no person claiming under him, or any other person shall, without the previous permission of the District Collector, cut any forest tree from such land.
Amends section 4 of the principal Act by inserting the words 'or under section 3A' and substituting the word 'therem' with 'therein'.

Renumbers sub-section (1) of section 7 of the principal Act as sub-section (2) and inserts a new sub-section (1). The new sub-section (1) states that whoever contravenes the provisions of section 3A or any of the terms and conditions subject to which a permission has been granted under that section shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both.
Amends sub-section (2) of section 14 of the principal Act by making consequential changes related to section 3A.

Repeals the Kerala Preservation of Private Forests (Amendment) Ordinance, 1973 (3 of 1973). It also includes a saving provision stating that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Restriction on cutting forest trees from exempted lands without the permission of the District Collector, if the land was subject to the Madras Preservation of Private Forests Act, 1949.
Violation of section 3A provisions can lead to imprisonment up to two years or a fine up to five thousand rupees, or both.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years
Fine which may extend to five thousand rupees
Both imprisonment and fine
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: District Collector (for granting permission to cut forest trees)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Punishment by imprisonment and/or fine for contravention of section 3A provisions.

rights: Right to seek permission from the District Collector to cut forest trees from exempted lands under specific conditions.
duties: Duty not to cut forest trees from exempted lands without the prior permission of the District Collector, if the land is subject to the provisions mentioned in section 3A.
obligations: Owners of exempted lands (as defined in section 3A) have an obligation to obtain permission before cutting forest trees.

key_procedures: Procedure to obtain permission from the District Collector to cut forest trees from exempted lands.
Procedure for prosecution and punishment for violating section 3A.
administration: Likely administered by the Forest Department of the Government of Kerala, with the District Collector playing a key role in issuing permissions.
important_notes: The Act amends the Kerala Preservation of Private Forests Act, 1972.
The definition of 'forest tree' excludes certain common species like Rubber, Jack, Mango, etc.
The provisions of section 3A apply to lands that were not private forests but were subject to the Madras Preservation of Private Forests Act, 1949, prior to May 10, 1971.
The Act repeals the Kerala Preservation of Private Forests (Amendment) Ordinance, 1973.

title: The Kerala Preservation of Private Forests Act, 1972
purpose: An Act to prevent the indiscriminate destruction of private forests and to regulate the customary and prescriptive rights therein.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Kerala. The provisions of Chapter VIII of Act 4 of 1962, as modified, shall apply to offences punishable under this Act.

key_definitions.forest offence: Means an offence punishable under this Act.
key_definitions.owner: In relation to a private forest, includes a mortgagee, lessee or other person having right to possession and enjoyment of the private forest.
key_definitions.person: Includes a company, a religious or charitable institution of a public nature, a trust, a Hindu undivided family, a Marumakkathayam family or branch and a family governed by the Kerala Nambudiri Act, 1958 (27 of 1958).
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.private forest: In relation to the Malabar district referred to in sub-section (2) of section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (Central Act 37 of 1956)—(i) any land to which the Madras Preservation of Private Forests Act, 1949 (Madras Act XXVII of 1949), applied immediately before the 10th day of May, 1971, excluding—(A) lands which are gardens or nilams as defined in the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 (1 of 1964); (B) lands which are used principally for the cultivation of tea, coffee, cocoa, rubber, cardamom or cinnamon and lands used for any purpose ancillary to the cultivation of such crops or for the preparation of the same for the market. Explanation.—Lands used for the construction of office buildings, godowns, factories, quarters for workmen, hospitals, schools and playgrounds shall be deemed to be lands used for purposes ancillary to the cultivation of such crops; (C) lands which are principally cultivated with cashew or other fruit-bearing trees or are principally cultivated with any other agricultural crop; and (D) sites of buildings and lands appurtenant to, and necessary for, convenient enjoyment or use of, such buildings; (ii) any forest not owned by the Government, to which the Madras Preservation of Private Forests Act, 1949 (Madras Act XXVII of 1949), did not apply, including waste lands which are enclaves within wooded areas; (2) in relation to the remaining areas in the State of Kerala, any forest not owned by the Government, including waste lands which are enclaves within wooded areas. Explanation.—For the purposes of this clause, a land shall be deemed to be a waste land notwithstanding the existence thereon of scattered trees or shrubs.
key_definitions.forest officer: Shall have the meanings respectively assigned to them in section 2 of the Kerala Forest Act, 1961 (4 of 1962).
key_definitions.company: Means any body corporate and includes a firm, society or other association of individuals.
key_definitions.director: In relation to a firm, means a partner in the firm.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, commencement and duration
main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Preservation of Private Forests Act, 1972. It extends to the whole of Kerala and shall come into force at once and cease to have effect on the 31st day of December, 1973. Provisions of section 4 of the Interpretation and General Clauses Act, 1125 shall apply as if this Act had been repealed by an Act of the Kerala State Legislature.
Provides definitions for terms such as 'forest offence', 'owner', 'person', 'prescribed', 'private forest', 'forest officer', 'company', and 'director'.

Prohibits any owner of a private forest, without the previous sanction of the District Collector, from selling, mortgaging, leasing or otherwise alienating the whole or any portion of the private forest. Nothing in this sub-section shall be construed as preventing the owner from selling or otherwise dealing with the right to gather and remove forest produce other than trees, timber, reeds, charcoal, wild animals and skins, tusks, horns, bones, and other parts or produce of such animals, in the usual or customary manner, for a period not exceeding two years. Any alienation in contravention of sub-section (1) shall be null and void. No owner of any private forest and no person claiming under him, whether by virtue of a contract, licence or any other transaction entered into before or after the commencement of this Act or any other person shall, without the previous permission of the District Collector, cut trees from, or cultivate, the private forest or do any act likely to denude the private forest or alter the nature of the forest or diminish its utility as a forest. Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1) or sub-section (3), the Government may exempt any private forest or class of private forests or class of trees therein from all or any of the provisions of this section.

Any person aggrieved by an order under sub-section (1) of section 3 or under sub-section (3) of that section in regard to the sanction or permission referred to in that sub-section may, within two months of the receipt of that order, prefer an appeal in writing to the Government, and the Government shall pass such orders on the appeal as they may think fit.

main_sections.section_title: Power to prohibit or regulate certain acts
main_sections.description: If, in the opinion of the Government, it is necessary for the preservation of a private forest or private forests, they may, by notification in the Gazette, (a) prohibit or regulate the doing of any act likely to be detrimental to the preservation of such private forest or private forests; (b) regulate the exercise of customary or prescriptive rights in such private forest or private forests.

main_sections.section_title: Applicability of Chapter VIII of Act 4 of 1962
main_sections.description: The provisions of Chapter VIII of the Kerala Forest Act, 1961 (4 of 1962), shall apply to offences punishable under this Act, subject to the following modifications...

Whoever contravenes the provisions of sub-section (1) or sub-section (3) of section 3 or any of the terms and conditions subject to which a permission has been granted under sub-section (3) of section 3 or any of the terms of a notification under section 5 shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both.

Where an offence under this Act has been committed by a company, every person who, at the time the offence was committed, was in charge of, and was responsible to, the company for the conduct of its business, shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly. Provided that nothing contained in this sub-section shall render any person liable to punishment if he proves that the offence was committed without his knowledge, or that he had exercised all due diligence to prevent the commission of such offence. Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), where any offence under this Act has been committed by a company and it is proved that the offence has been committed with the consent or connivance of, or is attributable to any neglect on the part of, any director, manager, secretary or other officer of the company, such director, manager, secretary or other officer shall be deemed to be guilty of that offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly.

important_rules: No owner of a private forest can sell, mortgage, lease, or alienate any part of it without the District Collector's prior sanction.
Owners can still deal with rights to gather and remove forest produce (excluding trees, timber, etc.) for up to two years in the usual customary manner.
No person can cut trees from, cultivate, or do anything to denude or alter the nature of a private forest without the District Collector's prior permission.
The Government can exempt any private forest or class of private forests from the provisions of section 3.
The Government can, by notification, prohibit or regulate acts detrimental to private forests and regulate customary rights.
Penalties for contravening the Act include imprisonment up to two years and/or a fine up to five thousand rupees.
Companies committing offences are liable, with specific provisions for individuals within the company.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: District Collector (for permissions), Government (for appeals and notifications), Forest Officers (implied through application of Kerala Forest Act, 1961)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through penalties prescribed for contraventions, appeal process for aggrieved persons, and notifications issued by the Government.

rights: Right to appeal to the Government against orders of the District Collector regarding alienation or permission.
Right to exercise customary or prescriptive rights in private forests, subject to regulation by the Government.
duties: Duty to obtain sanction from the District Collector before selling, mortgaging, leasing, or alienating private forests.
Duty to obtain permission from the District Collector before cutting trees or undertaking activities that denude or alter the nature of private forests.
Duty of companies to ensure their business conduct does not result in offences under the Act.
obligations: Compliance with the terms and conditions of permissions granted under section 3(3).
Compliance with notifications issued by the Government under section 5.

key_procedures: Procedure for alienation of private forest: Owner must obtain sanction from the District Collector. If aggrieved by the order, an appeal can be preferred to the Government within two months.
Procedure for cutting trees or altering private forests: Owner or person must obtain permission from the District Collector. Appeals against orders follow the same process as above.
Procedure for enforcement of penalties: Contraventions of specific sections lead to penalties as defined in Section 7.
Procedure for companies committing offences: Designated individuals within the company are liable if they were in charge or responsible, unless they prove lack of knowledge or due diligence.
administration: The Government of Kerala (for overall administration, appeals, and notifications), District Collector (for sanctions and permissions).
important_notes: This Act was intended to prevent indiscriminate destruction of private forests and had a limited duration, ceasing to have effect on December 31, 1973.
The Act incorporates modifications to Chapter VIII of the Kerala Forest Act, 1961.
The Act was enacted following appeals filed before the Supreme Court against a decision of the Kerala High Court concerning the Kerala Private Forests (Vesting and Assignment) Act, 1971.

title: THE KERALA PRESERVATION OF TREES ACT, 1986
purpose: To provide for the preservation of trees in the State of Kerala, prevent soil erosion and destruction of trees, and loss of timber wealth.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala. It concerns the cutting of trees, particularly in notified areas, and the application for permission to cut trees. It also addresses the powers of authorised officers and appellate authorities, and the enforcement of its provisions.

key_definitions.appellate authority: An appellate authority appointed under sub-section (2) of section 3.
key_definitions.authorised officer: An officer appointed under sub-section (1) of section 3.
key_definitions.owner: In relation to any land, includes a mortgagee, lessee or other person having right to possession and enjoyment of that land.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Preservation of Trees Act, 1986. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 18th day of June, 1983.
Defines terms used in the Act, including 'appellate authority', 'authorised officer', 'owner', 'prescribed', and 'tree'.
Empowers the Government to appoint authorised officers and appellate authorities by notification in the Gazette for the purposes of the Act and to assign them local limits.

main_sections.section_title: Restriction regarding cutting, etc., of trees
main_sections.description: Prohibits the cutting of trees without the permission of the authorised officer, except in specific circumstances such as when a tree is dead, diseased, or windfall, or for the purpose of using the land for construction of a building, or for pruning as required by ordinary agricultural or horticultural practices.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of cutting of tree in notified areas
main_sections.description: Prohibits cutting of trees in notified areas without the Government's decree or order, or in agreement with other authorities. It also states that trees constituting a danger to life or property or dead, diseased or windfallen trees are exceptions.
Details the process for applying for permission to cut trees under sections 4 or 5, and the procedure for granting or refusing permission.
Provides for an appeal to the appellate authority against an order refusing permission under section 4 or 5 within a specified period.
Allows the Government or the appellate authority to revise orders passed under the Act.
Prescribes penalties for contravening the provisions of section 4 or section 5.
Deals with offences committed by companies and the liability of directors and other officers.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of authorised officers and appellate authorities
main_sections.description: Outlines the powers of authorised officers and appellate authorities, including summoning persons, requiring production of documents, and receiving evidence.
Grants authorised officers the power to enter and inspect any land for the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power to seize timber and other articles involved in commission of offence
main_sections.description: Empowers officers to seize timber and other articles involved in the commission of an offence under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power to release property seized under section 13
main_sections.description: Details the process for releasing property seized under section 13, which may involve furnishing a bond.

Specifies the procedure to be followed by a Magistrate upon receiving a report under section 13 or clause (a) or (b) of sub-section (4) of section 13 for the trial of the accused and disposal of seized property.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure as to perishable property seized under section 13
main_sections.description: Lays down the procedure for dealing with perishable property seized under section 13, including its sale if the authorised officer is satisfied it is expedient and in the public interest.

main_sections.section_title: Saving of power to release property seized
main_sections.description: Saves the power to release property seized under section 13.
Specifies that prosecution for offences under the Act shall be instituted by an authorised officer or other officer not below the rank of Forest Ranger.
States that no court shall take cognizance of any offence punishable under this Act except on a complaint made by an authorised officer or any other officer not below the rank of Forest Ranger.

main_sections.section_title: Bar of jurisdiction of civil courts
main_sections.description: Ousts the jurisdiction of civil courts in matters falling within the purview of this Act.
Provides indemnity to persons acting in good faith under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Restriction regarding cutting, etc., of trees in future assignment
main_sections.description: Imposes restrictions on cutting trees in future assignments of land.
Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Laying of notifications and rules before Legislative Assembly
main_sections.description: Requires notifications and rules made under the Act to be laid before the Legislative Assembly.
Grants the Government power to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
Repeals previous enactments and provides for savings.

important_rules: No person shall, without the previous permission in writing of the authorised officer, cut, uproot or burn, or cause to be cut, uprooted or burnt, any tree.
No person shall cut or otherwise damage, or cause to be cut or otherwise damaged, the branch of any tree.
No person shall, without the previous permission in writing of the authorised officer, destroy any plant of any tree or do any act which diminishes the value of any such plant.

No person shall, without the previous permission in writing of the authorised officer, cut, uproot, burn or otherwise destroy any tree in any area specified in the notification under sub-section (1) of section 5.

penalties: First offence: Imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than six months but which may extend to two years, and with fine which shall not be less than five hundred rupees but which may extend to two thousand rupees.

Second or subsequent offence: Imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to three years, and with fine which shall not be less than one thousand rupees but which may extend to five thousand rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Authorised officers and police officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through seizure of timber and other articles involved in the commission of an offence, prosecution of offenders, and application of penalties as prescribed.

rights: Right to appeal against an order refusing permission to cut a tree.
Right to be heard before an order is passed by the appellate authority or Government in revision.
duties: Duty to obtain permission before cutting, uprooting, or burning any tree.
Duty to comply with orders issued by authorised officers and appellate authorities.
Duty not to damage trees or diminish their value without permission.
obligations: Obligation to seek permission for cutting trees, except in specific cases.

key_procedures: Application for permission to cut trees under sections 4 or 5, followed by the procedure for granting or refusing permission.
Procedure for appeal to the appellate authority against refusal of permission.
Procedure for revision of orders by the Government or appellate authority.
Procedure for seizure of timber and other articles involved in an offence.
Procedure for trial of offences by Magistrates.
Procedure for dealing with perishable property seized under section 13.
administration: The Government of Kerala, through its authorised officers and appellate authorities.
important_notes: The term 'tree' includes any species of tree.
Explanation: 'Private forest' means any land which immediately before the 10th day of May, 1971, was a private forest as defined in the Kerala Private Forests (Vesting and Assignment) Act, 1971.

Provided that where permission to cut a tree is granted on the ground specified in clause (a) or clause (b), the authorised officer shall impose as a condition for the grant of such permission, the effective regeneration of an equal number of the same or other suitable species of trees.

Provided that where such compound exceeds one hectare in extent, the provisions of this sub-section shall apply only in respect of an extent of one hectare immediately surrounding the residential building.
The Act may be amended by the Legislative Assembly.

title: The Kerala Prevention and Control of Animal Diseases Act, 1967
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to the prevention and control of diseases affecting animals.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Kerala and may be appointed for different areas and for different provisions of this Act by notification.

key_definitions.animal: means any domestic animal or bird or any animal or bird kept in confinement;
key_definitions.disinfect: means to free from disease germs;
key_definitions.disinfest: means to free from vermins, lice, fleas, flies, mosquitoes and the like;
key_definitions.export: means taking out of the State to a place outside the State;
key_definitions.import: means bringing into the State from a place outside the State;
key_definitions.infected area: means any area declared as infected area by the Director of Animal Husbandry under section 17;
key_definitions.infected place: means any place declared as infected place under section 14 or section 15 or section 16;
key_definitions.infective animal: means any animal which is affected with a Scheduled disease or has recently been in contact with or in close proximity to an animal so affected;
key_definitions.Inspector: means an Inspector appointed under section 3;
key_definitions.prescribed: means prescribed by rules made under this Act;
key_definitions.Scheduled disease: means any disease specified in the Schedule;
key_definitions.Veterinary Surgeon: means a Veterinary Surgeon appointed under section 3.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Prevention and Control of Animal Diseases Act, 1967, that it extends to the whole of the State of Kerala, and that it shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'animal', 'disinfect', 'disinfest', 'export', 'import', 'infected area', 'infected place', 'infective animal', 'Inspector', 'prescribed', 'Scheduled disease', 'State', and 'Veterinary Surgeon'.
Empowers the Government to appoint Veterinary Surgeons and Inspectors and define their powers and duties, including the ability to enter premises and inspect animals and vehicles.

main_sections.section_title: Veterinary Surgeons and Inspectors to be public servants.
main_sections.description: Declares Veterinary Surgeons and Inspectors appointed under section 3 to be public servants within the meaning of the Indian Penal Code.

main_sections.section_title: Power to prohibit or regulate import, export or transport of animals and the holding of markets, fairs, etc.
main_sections.description: Grants the Government power to prohibit or regulate the import, export, or transport of animals and the holding of markets, fairs, etc., to prevent the outbreak or spread of Scheduled diseases. This includes regulating traffic and disinfection of animals and conveyances.

main_sections.section_title: Cleansing, disinfecting and disinfection of vessels and vehicles.
main_sections.description: Mandates the cleansing, disinfecting, and disinfection of vessels and vehicles used for transporting animals. The Government may appoint places for such disinfection.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of certain persons to report Scheduled diseases.
main_sections.description: Obligates every owner or person in charge of an animal, or veterinary practitioner, to report any suspicion of a Scheduled disease to the Inspector.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of Veterinary Surgeons to hold post-mortem examination.
main_sections.description: Empowers Veterinary Surgeons to hold post-mortem examinations of animals suspected to have died from a Scheduled disease.
Authorizes an Inspector, when of the opinion that an animal is infective, to order its isolation or segregation and seize the animal and remove it to a place of isolation or segregation.
Requires the Veterinary Surgeon, upon receipt of a report under sub-section (2) of section 9, to examine the animal and any other animals in contact or in close proximity to it.

main_sections.section_title: Action after examination by the Veterinary Surgeon.
main_sections.description: Outlines the actions a Veterinary Surgeon may take after examination, including ordering the return of an animal, or if the animal is infective, ordering its destruction. It also provides for compensation for animals destroyed.

Specifies that compensation shall be paid to the owner of an animal destroyed under section 11, determined in accordance with rules made by the Government. No compensation is payable for any offence punishable under the Act or for disease contracted through wilful neglect.

main_sections.section_title: Power to require disinfection of infected premises, vessels or vehicles.
main_sections.description: Grants the Government power to require the disinfection of infected premises, vessels, or vehicles.

Allows an Inspector to declare a private place as infected if there is reason to believe that animals within it are infective. The owner or person in charge must report this to the Veterinary Surgeon.

main_sections.section_title: Examination of infected place by Veterinary Surgeon.
main_sections.description: Directs the Veterinary Surgeon to examine an infected place reported under section 14 and take appropriate action.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of infected places of a public character.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to declare places of public character (e.g., local authority or railway administration managed places) as infected if infective animals are kept there. The Veterinary Surgeon shall cause a copy of such declaration to be published.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of infected areas by the Director of Animal Husbandry.
main_sections.description: Allows the Director of Animal Husbandry to declare any area as an infected area if there are infective animals within it. This declaration can be modified or cancelled.

main_sections.section_title: Removal of animals and things from infected areas or places.
main_sections.description: Prohibits the removal of animals and things from infected areas or places without permission.

main_sections.section_title: Power to require return of animals or things to infected area or place.
main_sections.description: Grants the Government power to require the return of animals or things to an infected area or place.

main_sections.section_title: Time for complying with notice, requisition or order.
main_sections.description: Deals with the timeframe for complying with notices, requisitions, or orders issued under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Recovery of expenses incurred under this Chapter.
main_sections.description: Provides for the recovery of expenses incurred under this Chapter.

main_sections.section_title: Penalties for contravention of provisions of the Act and Rules.
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for contravening provisions of the Act and Rules.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for keeping or grazing infective animal in unenclosed land.
main_sections.description: Imposes a penalty for keeping or grazing an infective animal in unenclosed land.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for bringing infective animals to the market.
main_sections.description: Imposes a penalty for bringing infective animals to a market.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for placing carcass of infective animal in liver, canal, etc.
main_sections.description: Imposes a penalty for improperly disposing of the carcass of an infective animal.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for disinterring carcass of diseased animal.
main_sections.description: Imposes a penalty for disinterring the carcass of a diseased animal.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for malicious and vexatious entry or seizure by Veterinary Surgeon or Inspector.
main_sections.description: Provides a penalty for malicious and vexatious actions by a Veterinary Surgeon or Inspector.
Deals with the power of arrest without order or warrant.
Covers the institution of proceedings under the Act.
Specifies the jurisdiction of Magistrates in relation to offences under the Act.
States that certain claims to compensation may be barred.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to make rules.
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Allows for the amendment of the Schedule to the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Rules and notifications issued under section 33 to be laid before the Legislative Assembly.
main_sections.description: Requires that rules and notifications issued under section 33 be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith under the Act.
Repeals any previous enactments inconsistent with this Act.

important_rules: All animals and things removed from infected areas or places must be returned if required.
The Government may make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act, including procedures for disinfection, quarantine, and compensation.
Rules and notifications issued by the Government must be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

penalties: Penalty for contravention of provisions of the Act and Rules.
Penalty for keeping or grazing infective animal in unenclosed land.
Penalty for bringing infective animals to the market.
Penalty for placing carcass of infective animal in liver, canal, etc.
Penalty for disinterring carcass of diseased animal.
Penalty for malicious and vexatious entry or seizure by Veterinary Surgeon or Inspector.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Veterinary Surgeons and Inspectors appointed under the Act, and the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, examinations, quarantining of animals, disinfection of premises and vehicles, and imposition of penalties. The Government can also make rules and issue notifications for enforcement.

rights: Right to compensation for animals destroyed, subject to rules.
duties: Duty of owners/caretakers to report Scheduled diseases.
Duty to comply with notices, requisitions, and orders issued under the Act.
Duty to ensure animals are not brought to market if infective.
Duty to properly dispose of carcasses of infective animals.
Duty to cooperate with Veterinary Surgeons and Inspectors.
obligations: Owners of animals have an obligation to report suspected Scheduled diseases.
Individuals are obligated to comply with any orders for disinfection or quarantine.

key_procedures: Declaration of infected places and areas by Inspectors and the Director of Animal Husbandry.
Examination of animals and places by Veterinary Surgeons.
Isolation and seizure of infective animals.
Disinfection of animals, premises, vessels, and vehicles.
Quarantine of animals at designated stations.
Post-mortem examination of deceased animals suspected of Scheduled diseases.
administration: The Government of Kerala (likely through the Department of Animal Husbandry or a related agency).
important_notes: Published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 24, dated 14th February, 1967.
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected.
The Act aims to consolidate and amend existing laws related to animal disease prevention and control.

title: The Kerala Prevention of Disturbances of Public Meetings Act, 1961
purpose: To provide for the prevention of disturbances of public meetings.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force at once.

key_definitions.public meeting: Means any meeting bona fide and lawfully held for a lawful purpose and for the furtherance or discussion of any matter of public concern to which the public or any particular section of the public is invited.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act, its extent of application to the State of Kerala, and states that it shall come into force immediately.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty on endeavour to break up public meetings
main_sections.description: This section outlines the penalty for anyone who endeavors to break up public meetings. It states that whoever, for the purpose of preventing the transaction of business for which the meeting was called, together with others, disturbs the meeting, shall be guilty of an offense. The penalty for this offense is imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one month or with fine which may extend to one hundred rupees or with both. It also states that any person who incites others to commit an offense under this section shall be guilty of a like offense. Furthermore, any Police Officer may arrest without warrant a person who commits an offense under this section.
This section repeals the Cochin Prevention of Disturbances of Public Meetings Act, XXVIII of 1124.

important_rules: It is unlawful to endeavor to break up public meetings.
Inciting others to disturb public meetings is an offense.
Police officers have the power to arrest without a warrant individuals committing offenses under this Act.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month
Fine which may extend to one hundred rupees
Imprisonment and/or fine (for disturbance of public meetings)
Like penalty (for inciting others to disturb public meetings)
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Police Officer
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Arrest without warrant by a Police Officer for offenses under this section.

rights: Right to hold public meetings for lawful purposes.
duties: Duty to not disturb public meetings.

key_procedures: Arrest: Police Officers may arrest without warrant any person committing an offense under Section 2.
Prosecution: Individuals found guilty of disturbing public meetings or inciting such disturbances are subject to penalties as prescribed.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, but likely a relevant department of the Kerala Government.
important_notes: The Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 6th December, 1961.
The Cochin Prevention of Disturbances of Public Meetings Act XXVIII of 1124 is repealed.

title: THE KERALA PREVENTION OF EVICTION ACT, 1966
purpose: To provide for the prevention of eviction of cultivating tenants, holders of Kudiyiruppu and Kudikidappukars from their holdings, Kudiyiruppu or Kudikidappu, as the case may be, in the State of Kerala and for the restoration in certain cases of the possession thereof and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act applies to the entire State of Kerala. It specifically addresses cultivating tenants, holders of Kudiyiruppu and Kudikidappukars.

key_definitions.cultivating tenant: A tenant cultivating land in the State of Kerala.
key_definitions.eviction: To quit or be removed from a holding.
key_definitions.holding: Land or buildings or both belonging to or vested in the Government of Kerala or any other State in India or a corporation owned or controlled by the Government of Kerala or the Government of any other State in India or the Government of India.
key_definitions.kudiyiruppu: A holding comprising a homestead with the land under it and any cultivable land attached to it.
key_definitions.kudikidappukaran: A person who, being an inhabitant of the State of Kerala, is in possession of any land belonging to any other person, not being a cultivating tenant or a permanent tenant, under a lease or licence or in any other capacity.
key_definitions.Scheduled Castes: The Scheduled Castes in relation to the State as specified in the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950.
key_definitions.Scheduled Tribes: The Scheduled Tribes in relation to the State as specified in the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act as 'The Kerala Prevention of Eviction Act, 1966'. It also states that it extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and came into force on the date of its first publication in the Kerala Gazette.

This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'cultivating tenant', 'eviction', 'holding', 'kudiyiruppu', 'kudikidappukaran', 'Scheduled Castes', and 'Scheduled Tribes'.

This section states that notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in any other law or in any contract, custom or usage, or in any judgment, decree or order of court, a person shall not be evicted from his holding except as provided by this section. It specifies that the provisions of this section shall not apply to (i) lands or buildings or both belonging to or vested in the Government of Kerala or the Government of any other State in India or a corporation owned or controlled by the Government of Kerala or the Government of any other State in India or the Government of India; (ii) any lease of land or building or both granted by the Administrator-General, Official Trustee or Receiver.

This section states that any person who contravenes the provisions of Section 3 shall be punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees, or with both.

main_sections.section_title: Cultivating tenants, etc., entitled to restoration of possession
main_sections.description: This section deals with the restoration of possession for cultivating tenants, holders of Kudiyiruppu and Kudikidappukars who have been evicted. It outlines the conditions and procedures for such restoration.

main_sections.section_title: Prevention of eviction of cultivating tenants, etc., who are not members of any Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe
main_sections.description: This section prevents the eviction of cultivating tenants, holders of Kudiyiruppu and Kudikidappukars who are not members of any Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe, except in accordance with the law in force for the time being.

main_sections.section_title: Cultivating tenants, etc., entitled to restoration of possession
main_sections.description: This section also deals with the restoration of possession for cultivating tenants, holders of Kudiyiruppu and Kudikidappukars who have been evicted.

main_sections.section_title: Stay of suits or other proceedings for eviction
main_sections.description: This section provides for the stay of suits or other proceedings for eviction pending before any court or authority when the Act comes into force.

This section clarifies the jurisdiction of courts regarding offenses under this Act. It states that no court inferior to that of a Magistrate of the First Class shall try an offence punishable under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Protection to persons acting in good faith under this Act
main_sections.description: This section protects persons acting in good faith under the provisions of this Act from any suit, prosecution, or other legal proceeding.
This section states that the provisions of this Act shall be in addition to, and not in derogation of, any other law for the time being in force regulating any of the matters dealt with in this Act.
This section grants the Government the power to make rules for the purpose of carrying into effect the provisions of this Act. It also details the procedure for making and laying down these rules.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963
main_sections.description: This section makes amendments to the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963.

This section outlines savings in relation to the expiry of the Kerala Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Prevention of Eviction Ordinance, 1966. It clarifies that the expiry of the Ordinance shall not affect any right, privilege, obligation or liability acquired, accrued or incurred under the said Ordinance. It also states that the expiry of the Ordinance shall not affect any investigation, legal proceeding or remedy in respect of any such right, privilege, obligation, liability, penalty or punishment, and any such investigation, legal proceeding or remedy may be instituted, continued or enforced, and any such penalty or punishment may be imposed as if this Act had commenced on the 5th day of July, 1966.

important_rules: No person shall be evicted from their holding except as provided by Section 3 of the Act.
Eviction contraventions are punishable with imprisonment and/or fine.
Cultivating tenants, holders of Kudiyiruppu and Kudikidappukars evicted are entitled to restoration of possession under certain conditions.
Rules made by the Government under Section 12 shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly.
The Act's provisions are in addition to, and not in derogation of, other laws.

penalties: Rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees, or with both, for contravention of Section 3.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Revenue Divisional Officer, Deputy Collector, and First Class Magistrate (for trying offenses).
