penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings, investigations, and imposition of penalties as prescribed by the Act. The Revenue Divisional Officer can take necessary inquiries and issue orders for restoration of possession. Magistrates of the First Class have jurisdiction to try offenses.

rights: Right to prevention of eviction from holdings (subject to exceptions).
Right to restoration of possession for evicted cultivating tenants, holders of Kudiyiruppu and Kudikidappukars.
Right to protection for persons acting in good faith under the Act.
duties: Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act regarding eviction.
Duty to restore possession to eligible persons.
obligations: Obligation to pay rent for land under lease.
Obligation to adhere to the terms of leases and licenses.

key_procedures: Procedure for restoration of possession: An application needs to be made to the Revenue Divisional Officer within thirty days from the date of service of the order, preference for the Collector of the district, and the decision of the Collector on such appeal shall be final. Appeals against orders made under sub-section (3) can be preferred within a specified time.

Procedure for dealing with evictions of tenants and holders of Kudiyiruppu/Kudikidappu not belonging to Scheduled Castes or Tribes: Any person who evicts such a tenant or holder shall be punishable with imprisonment or fine.

Procedure for instituting proceedings for offenses: No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against any person for anything which is in good faith done or intended to be done under this Act.
administration: The Kerala Government is empowered to make rules for the purpose of carrying into effect the provisions of this Act.
important_notes: The Act does not apply to lands or buildings belonging to or vested in the Government of Kerala or any other State in India or a corporation owned or controlled by the Government.
The Act does not apply to leases of land or building or both granted by the Administrator-General, Official Trustee or Receiver.
The Act commenced on the date of its first publication in the Kerala Gazette.
The expiry of the Kerala Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Prevention of Eviction Ordinance, 1966, does not affect any rights, privileges, or liabilities accrued under it.

title: The Kerala Prisons and Correctional Services (Management) Act 2010
purpose: To provide for the management of prisons and correctional services in Kerala, including the admission, treatment, employment, welfare, and release of prisoners, as well as the regulation of visitors and the redressal of grievances. The Act aims to ensure efficient and humane management of correctional facilities and promote the rehabilitation of prisoners.
scope: The Act applies to all prisons and correctional services within the State of Kerala. It covers the management of convicted prisoners, undertrial prisoners, civil prisoners, and foreign prisoners. It also outlines rules for visitors, employment of prisoners, and various welfare programs.

key_definitions.Prisoner: Includes convicted prisoners, undertrial prisoners, and civil prisoners.
key_definitions.Superintendent: The officer in charge of a prison.
key_definitions.Director General: The Director General of Prisons and Correctional Services.
key_definitions.Correctional Services: Services aimed at reforming and rehabilitating prisoners.

main_sections.description: This chapter details the rules and regulations concerning visitors to prisons. It specifies who can visit, the procedure for obtaining permission, and the powers of the Superintendent in regulating visits. It also covers provisions for foreign prisoners visiting their embassies.

This chapter outlines the provisions for employing prisoners in various capacities within and outside the prison. It covers the types of employment, facilities to be provided, wages, and special provisions for the employment of criminal and civil prisoners. It also includes provisions regarding the health of prisoners engaged in employment.

main_sections.section_title: HEALTH AND PERSONAL HYGIENE OF PRISONERS
main_sections.description: This chapter deals with the provision of medical aid and the maintenance of the health and personal hygiene of prisoners. It specifies the duties of the Prison Medical Officer, the criteria for general hygiene and sanitation, and the provision of specialized treatment.

This chapter describes various welfare programs to be implemented for prisoners, including educational facilities, vocational training, religious and moral instructions, and recreational activities. It also covers provisions for nursery schools and crèches for children of convicted female prisoners.

This chapter outlines the rules for granting remission, parole, and premature release to prisoners. It specifies the conditions and criteria for such grants, including behavior, sentence duration, and grounds for cancellation.

This chapter details the provisions for granting leave and escort visits to prisoners for specific purposes, such as visiting relatives or attending court. It specifies the conditions, duration, and procedures for such grants.

This chapter establishes a mechanism for the redressal of grievances of prisoners. It provides for the constitution of a Grievance Redressal Committee and outlines the procedure for receiving, investigating, and resolving complaints.

important_rules: Visitors may be searched by women warders or women staff with due regard to privacy and decency. Searching of women visitors shall be done in separate enclosures away from the view of male persons.
Foreign prisoners may be permitted to use internet facilities at their own cost for legal assistance and to contact their Embassies in India.

The Superintendent shall report the admission of any foreign national to the prison to the Director General immediately, stating full name, address, nationality, and sections under which the prisoner is detained.
Criminal prisoners sentenced to rigorous imprisonment shall be provided with facilities of appropriate labour.
Medical Officers shall assess the health of prisoners engaged in any kind of work and may recommend their removal from employment if it affects their health.
The Government shall prescribe the manner and quantum of utilisation of wages earned by prisoners.
Prisoners may be granted leave for good behaviour, eligibility, convicted prisoners with the objective of their better rehabilitation and re-socialisation.

The Grievance Redressal Committee shall meet once in three months or as may be necessary and shall follow such procedure as may be prescribed for the examination of petitions or representations received.

penalties: Penalty for failure to surrender on expiry of parole: Imprisonment with fine, which may extend to two years or with fine, or both.
Imprisonment awarded to the prisoner for the offence or offences for which he is undergoing the sentence.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Superintendent, Director General, Police Officers, and the Court.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through arrest, imprisonment, imposition of fines, and court proceedings. The Superintendent has powers to enforce rules within the prison, while police officers are involved in surrenders and arrests. Courts handle penal provisions.

rights: Right of foreign prisoners to use internet facilities at their own cost for legal assistance and to contact Embassies.
Right of prisoners to receive medical aid and to have their personal hygiene maintained.
Right of prisoners to be provided with adequate facilities for imparting education and vocational training.
Right of prisoners to have their grievances redressed.
Right of prisoners to be provided with full opportunity to make a complaint in writing and such complaints and grievances shall be redressed through the Grievance Redressal Committee.
duties: Duty of the Superintendent to ensure the orderly conduct of the prison and the welfare of prisoners.
Duty of the Prison Medical Officer to provide medical aid and attend to the health of prisoners.
Duty of the Government to provide adequate facilities for education, vocational training, and welfare programs.
Duty of prisoners to comply with the rules and regulations of the prison.
obligations: The Government shall establish a Fund called the 'Kerala Prisoners' Welfare Fund'.

key_procedures: Procedure for visiting a prisoner: Obtaining permission from the Superintendent, undergoing searches, and adhering to visiting hours and regulations.
Procedure for employment of prisoners: Determination of suitability for employment by the Medical Officer, assignment of tasks, and calculation of wages.
Procedure for redressal of grievances: Submitting a complaint to the Grievance Redressal Committee, examination of the complaint, and decision by the Committee.
Procedure for remission, parole, and premature release: Application as per rules, consideration by the Superintendent and other officers, and final decision.
administration: The Directorate of Prisons and Correctional Services, Kerala, under the general supervision of the Director General and the administrative control of the State Government.
important_notes: No prohibited articles shall be carried into the prison by visitors, and no visitor shall be allowed to meet the prisoner if any prohibited article is found.
The Superintendent shall forward a copy of the entries recorded by the visitor to the Director General, who may take appropriate further action.
The employment of criminal prisoners sentenced to rigorous imprisonment shall be with facilities of appropriate labour preferably based on their aptitude.

The Medical Officer's opinion on the health of any prisoner suffering from employment of any kind of class of labour shall be placed on such other record or class of labour as the Medical Officer may consider suitable for him.

title: THE KERALA PRIVATE FORESTS (VESTING AND ASSIGNMENT) AMENDMENT ACT, 1978
purpose: To amend the Kerala Private Forests (Vesting and Assignment) Act, 1971, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: The Act applies to the Kerala Private Forests (Vesting and Assignment) Act, 1971.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Private Forests (Vesting and Assignment) Amendment Act, 1978, and it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 25th day of August, 1977.

Amends section 7 of the Principal Act. It inserts new subsections (4A) and (4B) to provide that subject to the provisions of subsection (4) and section 8A, the decision of the Tribunal on any matter within its jurisdiction shall be final and conclusive.

Amends section 8 of the Principal Act. It inserts new subsections (3) and (4). Subsection (3) states that if the Tribunal decides that any land is not a private forest or that a private forest or portion thereof has not vested in the Government, and (a) no appeal has been preferred against the decision of the Tribunal within the period specified therefor, or (b) such appeal having been preferred has been dismissed by the High Court, the custodian shall, as soon as may be after the expiry of the period referred to in clause (a) or, as the case may be, after the date of the order of the High Court dismissing the appeal, restore possession of such land or private forest or portion, as the case may be, to the person in possession immediately before the appointed day.

Inserts a new section 8A, titled "Appeal to the High Court". This section outlines the conditions and procedures for appealing decisions of the Tribunal to the High Court. The Government or any person objecting to any decision of the Tribunal may, within a period of sixty days from the date of that decision, appeal against such decision to the High Court. The High Court may admit an appeal preferred after the expiration of the period of sixty days aforesaid if it is satisfied that the appellant had sufficient cause for not preferring the appeal within the said period. The appeal shall be in the prescribed form and shall be verified in the prescribed manner and shall be accompanied by a fee of one hundred rupees. On receipt of an appeal under subsection (1), the High Court may, after giving the parties a reasonable opportunity of being heard, either in person or by a representative, (a) confirm or cancel the decision of the Tribunal appealed against; or (b) set aside such decision and remand the case to the Tribunal for decision after further inquiry as may be directed; or (c) pass such other orders as it may think fit. If the High Court decides that any land is not a private forest or that a private forest or portion thereof has not vested in the Government, the custodian shall, as soon as may be, restore possession of such land or private forest or portion, as the case may be, to the person in possession thereof immediately before the appointed day.
Amends section 13 of the Principal Act. It states that "Except as otherwise provided in this Act" shall be, and shall be deemed always to have been, inserted in the beginning.

Provides that notwithstanding anything contained in any law or in any judgment, decree or order of any court, the Government or any person objecting to any decision of the Tribunal constituted under section 7 of the Principal Act, made at any time before the commencement of this Act, may, within a period of ninety days from such commencement, appeal to the High Court against such decision, and the provisions of subsections (2) to (5) (both inclusive) of section 8A of the Principal Act as amended by this Act shall apply in respect of such appeal.

Repeals the Kerala Private Forests (Vesting and Assignment) Ordinance, 1977 (Ordinance No. 14 of 1977). Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken or any such Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken or made under this Act.

important_rules: Appeals to the High Court against Tribunal decisions must be filed within sixty days of the decision.
The High Court can admit appeals filed after sixty days if sufficient cause is shown.
If the Tribunal decides land is not a private forest or hasn't vested, and no appeal is made or appeal is dismissed, possession is restored to the person in possession before the appointed day.
For appeals filed before the commencement of this Act, a ninety-day period from commencement is allowed for appeal to the High Court.
Anything done or action taken under the repealed Ordinance is deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The High Court and potentially the custodian (for restoration of possession).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Appeals to the High Court, restoration of possession.

rights: Right to appeal Tribunal decisions to the High Court.
Right to have possession restored if land is determined not to be a private forest or not vested.
Right to have prior actions under the repealed Ordinance recognized under this Act.
obligations: Compliance with the procedures for filing appeals to the High Court.

key_procedures: Filing an appeal to the High Court against a Tribunal decision within 60 days, in the prescribed form, with a fee of one hundred rupees.
The High Court's process for hearing appeals, which may include confirming, cancelling, remanding for further inquiry, or passing other orders.
Restoration of possession of land if it's determined not to be a private forest or not vested, following specific conditions regarding appeals.
administration: Implied to be administered by the relevant legal and land revenue departments of the Kerala Government.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on August 25, 1977.
Decisions of the Tribunal are final and conclusive, subject to the provisions of appeal.
The repeal of the Kerala Private Forests (Vesting and Assignment) Ordinance, 1977, does not affect actions taken under it.

title: THE KERALA PRIVATE FORESTS (VESTING AND ASSIGNMENT) ACT, 1971
purpose: An Act to provide for the vesting in the Government of private forests in the State of Kerala and for the assignment thereof to agriculturists and agricultural labourers for cultivation.
scope: The Act applies to the whole of the State of Kerala. It concerns private forests and their vesting in the Government and subsequent assignment to agriculturists and agricultural labourers.

key_definitions.custodian: Means the Chief Conservator of Forests of the State of Kerala or any other officer appointed by the Government, by notification in the Gazette, to exercise the powers and perform the functions of the custodian under this Act.
key_definitions.owner: In relation to a private forest, includes a mortgagee, lessee or other person having right to possession and enjoyment of the private forest.
key_definitions.person: Includes a company, a religious or charitable institution of a public nature, a trust, a Hindu undivided family, a Marumakkathayam tarwad or tavazhi, an Aliya-santhana family or branch and a family governed by the Kerala Nambudiri Act, 1958 (27 of 1958).
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.private_forest: In relation to the Malabar district referred to in sub-section (2) of section 5 of the States Re-organisation Act, 1956 (Central Act 37 of 1956),— (i) any land to which the Madras Preservation of Private Forests Act, 1949 (Madras Act XXVII of 1949), applied immediately before the appointed day excluding— (A) lands which are gardens or nilams as defined in the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 (1 of 1964); (B) lands which are used principally for the cultivation of tea, coffee, cocoa, rubber, cardamom or cinnamon and lands used for any purpose ancillary to the cultivation of such crops or for the preparation of the same for the market; (C) lands which are principally cultivated with cashew or other fruit-bearing trees or are principally cultivated with any other agricultural crop; and (D) sites of buildings and lands appurtenant to, and necessary for the convenient enjoyment or use of, such buildings; (ii) any forest not owned by the Government, to which the Madras Preservation of Private Forests Act, 1949, did not apply, including waste lands which are enclaves within wooded areas; (2) In relation to the remaining areas in the State of Kerala, any forest not owned by the Government, including waste lands which are enclaves within wooded areas.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Private Forests (Vesting and Assignment) Act, 1971, it extends to the whole of the State of Kerala, and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 10th day of May, 1971.
Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including "appointed day", "custodian", "owner", "person", "prescribed", and "private forest".

main_sections.section_title: Private forests to vest in Government
main_sections.description: Declares that notwithstanding anything contained in any other law, all private forests shall stand transferred to and vested in the Government on the appointed day, with their encumbrances, rights, title, and interest extinguished.

main_sections.section_title: Private forests to be deemed to be reserved forests
main_sections.description: States that private forests vested in the Government under section 3 shall be deemed to be reserved forests constituted under the Kerala Forest Act, 1961.

main_sections.section_title: Eviction of persons in unauthorised occupation
main_sections.description: Empowers the custodian to evict any person in unauthorized occupation of any private forest vested in the Government.
Mandates the custodian to demarcate the boundaries of private forests vested in the Government.

Provides for the constitution of one or more Tribunals for the purposes of the Act. The Tribunal shall consist of a single person who is, or has been, or is qualified to be appointed as, a District Judge.
Outlines the procedure for the Tribunal to settle disputes regarding whether any land is a private forest or not, or whether any private forest or portion thereof has vested in the Government or not.

main_sections.section_title: No compensation to be payable for vesting, etc.
main_sections.description: States that no compensation shall be payable for the vesting of any private forest or for the extinguishment of any right, title, and interest of the owner or any other person in any private forest under sub-section (1) of section 3.
Provides for the assignment of private forests to agriculturists and agricultural labourers. This section details the categories of persons eligible for assignment.

main_sections.section_title: Assignment to be made within two years
main_sections.description: Specifies that assignments of private forests under section 10 shall be completed within two years from the date of publication of the Act in the Gazette.

Grants the Tribunal and the custodian powers similar to those conferred by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, for summoning, examining, requiring discovery, issuing commissions, inspecting property, and requisitioning records.

main_sections.section_title: Bar of jurisdiction of civil courts
main_sections.description: Prohibits civil courts from deciding any question or determining any matter which is to be decided or determined by the Tribunal or the custodian under this Act.

States that no suit, prosecution, or other legal proceeding shall lie against the Government or the custodian or any other officer for anything done or intended to be done under this Act or any rule or order made thereunder.
Establishes a fund called the Agriculturists Welfare Fund, to be utilised for the settlement and welfare of persons to whom private forests or lands comprised in private forests have been assigned.
Empowers the Government to make orders as may be necessary for removing any difficulty in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including matters to be prescribed or allowed by the Act.
Repeals the Madras Private Forests (Vesting and Assignment) Act, 1964.

important_rules: Private forests shall vest in the Government on the appointed day (May 10, 1971).
No compensation shall be payable for the vesting of private forests.
Private forests vested in the Government shall be deemed to be reserved forests.
The Government may assign private forests to eligible agriculturists and agricultural labourers.
The assignment of private forests shall be completed within two years of the Act's publication.
Civil courts are barred from deciding matters that fall under the jurisdiction of the Tribunal or the custodian.
Rules made by the Government under this Act can cover all matters expressly required or allowed to be prescribed or any other matter which has to be, or may be, prescribed.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Custodian and the Tribunal, as appointed under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The custodian can evict persons in unauthorized occupation. The Tribunal has powers similar to civil courts for summoning, examining, and taking evidence. The Government can make rules for enforcement.

rights: Rights of eligible agriculturists and agricultural labourers to be assigned private forests.
Right to have disputes settled by the Tribunal.
duties: Duty of the custodian to demarcate boundaries.
Duty of persons in unauthorized occupation to vacate.
obligations: Owners' rights, title, and interest in private forests are extinguished upon vesting in the Government.

key_procedures: Vesting of private forests in the Government on the appointed day.
Eviction of unauthorized occupants by the custodian.
Demarcation of boundaries by the custodian.
Constitution and functioning of Tribunals for dispute settlement.
Procedure for assignment of private forests to eligible persons.
The Tribunal's procedure for hearing and deciding disputes.
Rules-making procedure by the Government.
administration: The Kerala State Government, specifically through the Chief Conservator of Forests as the Custodian, and the constituted Tribunals.
important_notes: The Act is retrospective in its commencement from May 10, 1971.
The Act clarifies what constitutes a 'private forest', excluding certain types of cultivated lands and areas.
No compensation is payable for the vesting of private forests.
The Act repeals the Madras Private Forests (Vesting and Assignment) Act, 1964.

title: THE KERALA PRIVATE FORESTS (VESTING AND ASSIGNMENT) AMENDMENT ACT, 1986
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Private Forests (Vesting and Assignment) Act, 1971, to address issues related to applications, appeals, and decisions concerning private forests, particularly those made before Tribunals or the Government, and to provide for the vesting and restoration of certain private forest lands.
scope: Applies to private forests in Kerala, and proceedings related to their vesting and assignment under the principal Act of 1971.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called The Kerala Private Forests (Vesting and Assignment) Amendment Act, 1986, and it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 19th day of November, 1983.

Inserts new sections 8B, 8C and 8D into the Kerala Private Forests (Vesting and Assignment) Act, 1971, to deal with power of Custodian to apply for review of decisions of Tribunal, power of Government to file appeal or application for review in certain cases, and decisions and orders liable to be reviewed or appealed against.

main_sections.section_title: Certain applications or appeals to be treated as validly made or filed.
main_sections.description: Declares that certain applications or appeals, notwithstanding anything contained in the Act or any other law, if made or filed within a specified period, shall be deemed to have been validly made or filed.

Repeals The Kerala Private Forests (Vesting and Assignment) Amendment Ordinance, 1986, and saves anything done or deemed to have been done or taken under the repealed Ordinance or the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Section 8B: The Custodian may apply for review of decisions of Tribunals under certain conditions.
Section 8C: The Government may file an appeal or application for review of decisions of Tribunals in certain cases.
Section 8D: Decisions and orders of Tribunals are subject to review or appeal under specific conditions.

Section 3: Applications and appeals made within six months from the commencement of the Kerala Private Forests (Vesting and Assignment) Amendment Act, 1986, and before the publication of the said Act in the Gazette, shall be deemed valid.
Section 4: The Kerala Private Forests (Vesting and Assignment) Amendment Ordinance, 1986, is repealed, but actions taken under it are saved.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Custodian and Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through review and appeal processes, and by deeming certain applications and appeals as valid.

rights: Right of the Custodian to apply for review of Tribunal decisions.
Right of the Government to file appeals or applications for review.
Right to have certain applications and appeals treated as valid.

key_procedures: Procedure for the Custodian to apply for review of Tribunal decisions (Section 8B).
Procedure for the Government to file appeals or applications for review (Section 8C).
Procedure for review and appeal against decisions and orders (Section 8D).
Procedure for verifying applications under sub-section (1) of section 8C and sub-section (2) or (3) of section 8C.
administration: Likely the Revenue Department or Forest Department of the Government of Kerala, as implied by the involvement of the Custodian and Government in the proceedings.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on November 19, 1983.
The Act aims to address delays in the disposal of cases related to private forests.
It clarifies the treatment of certain applications and appeals made prior to the Act's final publication.
The repealed Ordinance was largely consistent with the provisions of this Act.

title: THE KERALA PRIVATE FORESTS (VESTING AND ASSIGNMENT) AMENDMENT ACT, 1981.
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala Private Forests (Vesting and Assignment) Act, 1971.
scope: Applies to private forests in Kerala, as amended by this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Private Forests (Vesting and Assignment) Amendment Act, 1981, and it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 9th day of June, 1981.

Amends section 8 of the Kerala Private Forests (Vesting and Assignment) Act, 1971 (26 of 1971) by substituting the words "may apply to the Tribunal" for the words "may, within such period as may be prescribed, apply to the Tribunal".

Repeals the Kerala Private Forests (Vesting and Assignment) Amendment Ordinance, 1981 (4 of 1981). It also states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

key_procedures: Procedure to amend section 8 of the Principal Act: Substitute specific wording in section 8 regarding application to the Tribunal.
administration: Likely the Forest Department of the Government of Kerala, based on the subject matter.
important_notes: The Act was received the assent of the Governor on the 17th day of August 1981 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 656 dated the 17th August 1981.

title: The Kerala Professional Colleges or Institutions (Prohibition of Capitation Fee, Regulation of Admission, Fixation of Non-Exploitative Fee and Other Measures to Ensure Equity and Excellence in Professional Education) Amendment Act, 2007
purpose: To amend the Kerala Professional Colleges or Institutions (Prohibition of Capitation Fee, Regulation of Admission, Fixation of Non-exploitative Fee and Other Measures to Ensure Equity and Excellence in Professional Education) Act, 2006.
scope: Applies to professional colleges or institutions in Kerala.

main_sections.description: Names the Act and specifies the date of commencement. The Act may be called the Kerala Professional Colleges or Institutions (Prohibition of Capitation Fee, Regulation of Admission, Fixation of Non-exploitative Fee and Other Measures to Ensure Equity and Excellence in Professional Education) Amendment Act, 2007 and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of June, 2007.

Amends section 6 of the principal Act (Kerala Professional Colleges or Institutions (Prohibition of Capitation Fee, Regulation of Admission, Fixation of Non-exploitative Fee and Other Measures to Ensure Equity and Excellence in Professional Education) Act, 2006). Specifically, it amends sub-section (1) by replacing the words "for determination of the fee" with "from time to time" and omits the words "for a period of three years" from sub-section (5).

Repeals the Kerala Professional Colleges or Institutions (Prohibition of Capitation Fee, Regulation of Admission, Fixation of Non-exploitative Fee and Other Measures to Ensure Equity and Excellence in Professional Education) Ordinance, 2007 (58 of 2007). It also states that notwithstanding the repeal, any action taken or any thing done or taken under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act, as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Amendments are made to section 6 of the principal Act.
The phrase 'for determination of the fee' in sub-section (1) of section 6 is replaced.
The phrase 'for a period of three years' in sub-section (5) of section 6 is omitted.
key_procedures: The Act is enacted in the Fifty-eighth Year of the Republic of India.
The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 13th October, 2007 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 1867 dated 15th October, 2007.
important_notes: Received the assent of Governor on the 13th October, 2007 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No 1867 dated 15th October, 2007.

title: THE KERALA PROFESSIONAL COLLEGES OR INSTITUTIONS (PROHIBITION OF CAPITATION FEE, REGULATION OF ADMISSION AND FIXATION OF FEE) ACT, 2006
purpose: To prohibit the collection of capitation fee and to regulate the admission and fixation of fees in professional colleges or institutions in the State of Kerala.
scope: This Act applies to all professional colleges or institutions, whether existing or newly established, within the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.professional_college_or_institution: Means any college or institution imparting education or training in any of the professional courses and which is recognised by the Government or is affiliated to any university or board established by or under any law and includes any college or institution, whether or not affiliated to any university or board and whether or not recognised by the Government, where admission is made or any course is conducted on payment of any amount in excess of the fee prescribed by the Government, and the management of which is not vested in the Government.
key_definitions.capitation_fee: Means any amount collected by the management of a professional college or institution in excess of the fee prescribed by the Government by whatever name called, by whatever mode or system and whether paid by the student, his guardian or any person on his behalf.
key_definitions.management: Means the person or persons, whether natural or juristic, who manage or are responsible for the management of a professional college or institution.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and its commencement date.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'professional college or institution', 'capitation fee', and 'management'.
Prohibits the collection of capitation fees by any professional college or institution.

main_sections.section_title: Regulation of Admission and Fixation of Fee
main_sections.description: Lays down the rules for the regulation of admission and fixation of fees in professional colleges or institutions. It specifies the categories of seats, the authority for fixation of fees, and the procedure for admission.

important_rules: No professional college or institution shall collect capitation fee.
Admission to professional colleges or institutions shall be made on the basis of merit and according to the reservation policy of the Government.
The Government shall fix the fees for different courses in professional colleges or institutions.
The management of professional colleges or institutions shall maintain proper accounts and get them audited.
Appeals against the decisions of the Admission Supervisory Committee shall lie with the High Court.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees for contravention of the provisions of the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through provisions for penalties, fines, and the establishment of an Admission Supervisory Committee to oversee admissions and fee fixation.

rights: Right of students to admission based on merit and without paying capitation fees.
Right of the Government to regulate admissions and fix fees.
duties: Duty of management to comply with the provisions of the Act.
Duty of management to provide necessary facilities to students.
Duty of management to maintain accounts and get them audited.
obligations: Obligation to prohibit and not demand or accept capitation fee.

key_procedures: Procedure for admission to professional colleges or institutions based on merit and reservation.
Procedure for fixation of fees by the Government.
Procedure for auditing of accounts by the management.
administration: The Government of Kerala, likely through its Education Department or a designated authority.
important_notes: The Act aims to ensure transparency and fairness in the admission process and to prevent commercialization of professional education.
The Act empowers the Government to frame rules and issue orders for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

title: THE KERALA PROFESSIONAL COLLEGES OR INSTITUTIONS (PROHIBITION OF CAPITATION FEE, REGULATION OF ADMISSION, FIXATION OF NON-EXPLOITATIVE EQUITY AND EXCELLENCE IN PROFESSIONAL EDUCATION) ACT, 2006
purpose: To provide for prohibition of capitation fee, regulation of admission, fixation of non-exploitative fee, allottment of seats to Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and other socially and economically backward classes and other measures to ensure equity and excellence in professional education and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to professional colleges or institutions in the State of Kerala, including private educational institutions aiding or unaided, whether State or Central Government and minority and non-minority professional colleges or institutions.

key_definitions.Admission Supervisory Committee: The committee constituted under section 4 for regulating admission in unaided professional colleges or institutions.
key_definitions.Aided College: A professional college or an institution receiving recurring financial aid or grant-in-aid from any State or Central Government and includes minority and non-minority professional college or institution, as specified by the Government.
key_definitions.Capitation Fees: Any amount by whatever name called whether in cash or in kind paid or collected or received directly or indirectly in addition to the fees determined under this Act.
key_definitions.common entrance test: The entrance test conducted for determination of merit of the candidates followed by centralised counselling for the purpose of merit based admission to professional colleges or institutions through a single window system by the State Commissioner for Entrance Examinations.
key_definitions.fee: All fees including tuition fee, development fee and any other fee fixed by the Fee Regulatory Committee.
key_definitions.Fee Regulatory Committee: The Committee constituted under section 6 for determining the fee for admission to unaided professional colleges or institutions.
key_definitions.Freeship: Full or partial remission of tuition fee awarded to Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe and other socially, educationally and economically backward students on merit-cum-means basis by an unaided professional college or institution as may be prescribed.
key_definitions.general merit seats: Seats other than specified seats, minority seats and Non-Resident Indian seats and notified as such by Government or any agency authorised by it.
key_definitions.Higher Education Scholarship Fund: The fund for providing scholarship to socially and economically backward students on merit-cum-means basis.
key_definitions.management: Any person or body by whatever name called, under whose administration any unaided professional college or institution is functioning.
key_definitions.minority: A community belonging to a religious or linguistic minority for the purpose of this Act may be determined by Government taking the State as a unit.
key_definitions.minority professional college or institu: A professional college or institution established and maintained by a minority that fulfills the non-discriminatory criteria as laid down in this Act and determined as such by the Government.
key_definitions.minority seats: Seats reserved for students who belong to the community that runs the minority unaided professional college or institution and filled up on the basis of inter se merit in the manner as may be prescribed from the rank list prepared by the Commissioner for Entrance Examinations.
key_definitions.Non-Resident Indian seats: Seats reserved for children or wards of Non-Resident Indians to whom admission is given by the management in a fair, transparent and non-exploitative manner on the basis of fees as may be prescribed.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.privilege seats: Seats filled up through the single window system from the common merit list prepared by the Commissioner for Entrance Examinations from the common merit list prepared by the Commissioner for Entrance Examinations, on the basis of inter se merit from the applications submitted by the management of each unaided professional college or institution, as may be prescribed.
key_definitions.professional college or institution: A college or institution aided or unaided imparting professional courses in any of the following disciplines, namely— (a) Engineering and Technology, (b) Medicine, Dentistry, Pharmacy, Ayurveda, Homoeopathy, Siddha and Nursing; (c) Teacher education or any other discipline as may be declared by the Government by notification in the Gazette.
key_definitions.qualifying examination: The examination as may be prescribed as qualifying for the purpose of appearing for the Common Entrance Test.
key_definitions.single window system: The centralized system for admission administered by the State Commissioner for Entrance Examinations to professional courses in both aided and unaided, minority and non-minority colleges or institutions.
key_definitions.specified seats: Seats earmarked under sub-section (1) of section 10.
key_definitions.unaided professional college or institut: professional college or institution which is not receiving aid or grant-in-aid from any State or Central Government and includes minority and non-minority professional colleges or institutions.
key_definitions.University: A University established under any law made by the Legislature of the State.

main_sections.description: (1) This Act may be called the Kerala Professional Colleges or Institutions (Prohibition of Capitation Fee, Regulation of Admission, Fixation of Non-Exploitative Fee and Other Measures to Ensure Equity and Excellence in Professional Education) Act, 2006. (2) It shall come into force at once.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Admission Supervisory Committee', 'Aided College', 'Capitation Fees', 'common entrance test', 'fee', 'Fee Regulatory Committee', 'Freeship', 'general merit seats', 'Government', 'Higher Education Scholarship Fund', 'management', 'minority', 'minority professional college or institution', 'minority seats', 'Non-Resident Indian seats', 'prescribed', 'privilege seats', 'professional college or institution', 'qualifying examination', 'single window system', 'specified seats', 'State', 'unaided professional college or institution', and 'University'.

main_sections.section_title: Method of admission in Professional Colleges or Institutions
main_sections.description: Admission to any professional college or institution, or to any seat therein, shall not be made by any management, trustee or any person except in accordance with the provisions of any other law for the time being in force or in any judgment, decree or order of any Court or any other authority, admission of students in all professional colleges or institutions to all seats except Non-Resident Indian seats shall be made through Common Entrance Test conducted by the State followed by centralised counselling through a single window system in the order of merit by the State Commissioner for Entrance Examinations in accordance with such procedure as may be specified by the Government from time to time.

(1) The Government shall constitute an Admission Supervisory Committee to supervise and guide the process of admission of students to unaided professional colleges or institutions consisting of the following members, namely— (i) a retired judge of the Supreme Court or a High Court - Chairperson (ii) The Secretary to Government, Higher Education Department (ex-officio) - Member Secretary (iii) The Secretary to Government, Health and Family Welfare Department (ex-officio) - Member (iv) The Secretary to Government, Law Department (ex-officio) - Member (v) The Commissioner for Entrance Examinations, Kerala (ex-officio) - Member (vi) An Educational Expert belonging to the Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe Community - Member (2) The Admission Supervisory Committee may adopt its own procedure for the conduct of its business. (3) The terms and conditions of service of the Chairperson and the members of the Admission Supervisory Committee shall be as may be prescribed. (4) Non person who is associated with any unaided professional college or institution shall be eligible for being a member of the Admission Supervisory Committee. (5) A member of the Admission Supervisory Committee shall be removed if he or she does any act, which in the opinion of the Government, is unbecoming of a member of the Committee. The member so removed shall not be renominated to the Committee: Provided that no such member shall be removed from the committee without giving him or her an opportunity of being heard. (6) The Admission Supervisory Committee shall supervise and guide the entire process of admission of students to the unaided professional colleges or institutions with a view to ensure that the process is fair, transparent, merit-based and non-exploitative under the provisions of this Act. (7) The Admission Supervisory Committee may hear complaints with regard to admission in contravention of the provisions contained herein. If the Admission Supervisory Committee after enquiry finds that there has been any violation of the provisions of this Act, on the part of the unaided professional colleges or institutions, it shall make appropriate recommendation to the Government for imposing a fine upto rupees ten lakhs and the Government may on receipt of such recommendation, fix the fine and collect the same in the case of each such violation or any other course of action as it deems fit and the amount so fixed together with interest thereon shall be recovered as if it were an arrear of public revenue due on land. The Admission Supervisory Committee may also declare admission made in respect of any or all seats in a particular college or institution to be de-hors merit and therefore invalid and cancel the same to the concerned University. On the receipt of such communication, the University shall debar such candidates from appearing for any further examination and cancel the results of examinations already appeared for. (8) The Admission Supervisory Committee may if satisfied that any unaided professional college or institution has violated any of the provisions of this Act, recommend to the University or Statutory body for withdrawal of the affiliation or recognition of such college or institution or any other course of action it deems fit.

(1) No capitation fee shall be collected by or on behalf of an unaided professional college or institution or by any person who is in charge of or is responsible for the management of such college or institution or from in relation to any candidate in consideration of his or her admission to or continuance in any course of study or his or her promotion to a higher class in such college or institution under the management. (2) Where the Admission Supervisory Committee on receipt of any complaint or if otherwise satisfied that the management of an unaided professional college or institution or any person who is in charge of it or is responsible for the management of such college or institution has violated the provisions of sub-section (1), the admission supervisory Committee may after due enquiry recommend to the Government for taking penal action against the management. (3) The Admission Supervisory Committee shall have the power to regulate its own procedure in all matters arising out of the discharge of its functions, and shall, for the purpose of making any enquiry under this Act, have all the powers of a Civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Central Act 5 of 1908) while trying a suit in respect of the following matters, namely — (a) summoning and enforcing the attendance of any witness and examining him on oath; (b) requiring the discovery and production of any document, (c) receiving evidence on affidavit; (d) issuing commissions for the examinations of witnesses and for local inspections.

important_rules: No capitation fee shall be collected by or on behalf of an unaided professional college or institution or by any person who is in charge of or is responsible for the management of such college or institution or from in relation to any candidate in consideration of his or her admission to or continuance in any course of study or his or her promotion to a higher class in such college or institution under the management.

Admission to professional colleges or institutions, except for Non-Resident Indian seats, must be made through a Common Entrance Test followed by centralized counselling via a single window system, based on merit.
The Admission Supervisory Committee shall supervise and guide the entire admission process to ensure it is fair, transparent, merit-based, and non-exploitative.
The Admission Supervisory Committee can hear complaints regarding admission violations and recommend penal action to the Government.

penalties: Fine up to rupees ten lakhs and other courses of action deemed fit by the Government for violations of the Act.
Cancellation of admission made in respect of any or all seats in a particular college or institution if found de-hors merit.
Debarring candidates from further examinations and cancellation of results of already appeared examinations.
Withdrawal of affiliation or recognition of a college or institution or any other course of action deemed fit by the Admission Supervisory Committee.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Admission Supervisory Committee, Government of Kerala, Universities, and statutory bodies.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inquiries, recommendations for penal action, imposition of fines, cancellation of admissions, withdrawal of affiliations/recognitions, and debarment of candidates.

rights: Right to fair, transparent, and merit-based admission to professional colleges and institutions.
Right to equitable sharing of opportunities for education among different communities.
Right to protection and scholarship for economically weaker students.
duties: Duty of professional colleges and institutions to comply with the provisions of the Act regarding admission and fee fixation.
Duty of the Government to constitute and support the Admission Supervisory Committee.
Duty of the Commissioner for Entrance Examinations to conduct the Common Entrance Test and manage the single window system for admissions.
obligations: Obligation for professional colleges and institutions to ensure admission is based on merit through a centralized system.
Obligation to prohibit the collection of capitation fees.

key_procedures: Admission of students to professional colleges or institutions is to be made through a Common Entrance Test conducted by the State, followed by centralized counselling through a single window system based on merit.
The Admission Supervisory Committee may hear complaints and conduct inquiries into violations of the Act.
The Admission Supervisory Committee may recommend penal actions against erring managements to the Government.
administration: The Government of Kerala and the Admission Supervisory Committee.
important_notes: The Act aims to ensure equity and excellence in professional education in Kerala.
The provisions are in line with Supreme Court judgments regarding minority rights and the principle of equality.
The Act emphasizes a merit-based admission system and prohibits exploitative practices like capitation fees.

title: The Kerala Prohibition Of Ragging Act, 1998
purpose: To prohibit ragging in educational institutions in the state of Kerala.
scope: Applies to all educational institutions in Kerala, including colleges, universities, and other affiliated bodies.

key_definitions.ragging: Includes any act of teasing, abuse, tormenting, or causing physical or mental harm or discomfort to any student, or inciting or encouraging others to do so.
key_definitions.educational institution: Includes any college, university, or other institution where students are admitted for instruction or training.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Kerala Prohibition of Ragging Act, 1998' and states that it comes into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'ragging', 'educational institution', and 'student'.
Prohibits ragging in any form in educational institutions within the State.
Outlines the consequences for students found guilty of ragging, including disciplinary action and potential imprisonment.
Empowers the Government to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.
Specifies the jurisdiction of courts for trying offences under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection to persons acting in good faith in pursuance of the provisions of this Act or rules made thereunder.
Repeals any existing law or rule inconsistent with this Act, with savings for actions taken under the repealed provisions.
Grants the Government the power to make provisions for removing difficulties in the implementation of the Act.

important_rules: No student shall engage in or abet ragging in any educational institution.
Institutions must take steps to prevent ragging and to punish offenders.
Students have a right to be free from ragging.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both.
Suspension or expulsion from the educational institution.
Cancellation of admission.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Educational institutions, police, and the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through internal disciplinary committees of institutions, police investigation, and prosecution in courts.

rights: Right of every student to study in an environment free from fear and intimidation caused by ragging.
Right to be protected from acts of ragging.
duties: Duty of educational institutions to prevent and address ragging.
Duty of students to refrain from ragging and to report incidents of ragging.
obligations: Obligation of educational institutions to implement anti-ragging measures as prescribed by the Act and rules.

key_procedures: Reporting an incident of ragging to the institution's anti-ragging committee or the police.
Investigation of complaints by the institution's authorities.
Disciplinary proceedings against students found guilty of ragging.
Prosecution of offenders under the Act.
administration: The State Government of Kerala, through its education department and other relevant authorities.
important_notes: The Act aims to ensure a safe and conducive learning environment for all students.
Severe penalties are prescribed for those found guilty of ragging.

title: THE KERALA PROHIBITION OF RAGGING ACT, 1998
purpose: An Act to prohibit ragging in educational institutions in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to educational institutions in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.head of the educational institution: Means the Principal or the Head of the educational institution responsible for the management of that educational institution.
key_definitions.ragging: Means doing of any act, by disorderily conduct, to a student of an educational institution, which causes or is likely to cause physical or psychological harm or raising apprehension or fear or shame or embarrassment to that student and includes-(i) teasing, abusing or playing practical jokes on, or causing hurt to, such student, or (ii) asking a student to do any act or perform something which such student will not, in the ordinary course willingly, do.

main_sections.description: States the short title, extent, and commencement of the Act. The Act extends to the whole of Kerala and came into force on the 23rd day of October, 1997.
Defines terms used in the Act, including 'head of the educational institution' and 'ragging'.
Prohibits ragging within or without any educational institution.

Prescribes penalties for committing, participating in, abetting, or propagating ragging within or without an educational institution. Penalties include imprisonment for a term that may extend to two years and shall also be liable to a fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees.

States that any student convicted of an offence under section 4 shall be admitted from the educational institution and shall not be admitted in any other educational institution for a period of three years from the date of order of such dismissal.

Provides for the suspension of a student by the head of the educational institution, or by the parents or guardian, or a teacher if a complaint of ragging is received. The head of the institution must inquire into the complaint within seven days and, if a prima facie case is found, suspend the student and forward the complaint to the police.

If the head of the educational institution fails or neglects to take action as specified in section 6 when a complaint of ragging is made, such person shall be deemed to have abetted the offence of ragging and shall be punishable under section 4.

Empowers the Government, by notification in the Gazette, to make rules for carrying out all or any of the purposes of this Act. Any rule made under this section shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly.
Repeals the Kerala Prohibition of Ragging Ordinance, 1998, and states that anything done or action taken under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Ragging within or without any educational institution is prohibited.
Whoever commits, participates in, abets or propagates ragging shall be punished.
Students convicted of ragging offenses are subject to dismissal from the institution and a ban from re-admission to any other institution for three years.
Heads of educational institutions are required to take action upon receiving complaints of ragging.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years
Fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government (implied by power to make rules and notification in the Gazette).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through prohibition of ragging, penalties for offenders, dismissal/suspension of students, and inquiry procedures by educational institutions. The Government has the power to make rules for enforcement.

rights: Students have the right to be free from ragging.
Students have the right to have their complaints of ragging addressed.
duties: Students have the duty not to engage in ragging.
Heads of educational institutions have the duty to inquire into and act upon ragging complaints.
obligations: Educational institutions have an obligation to ensure their premises are free from ragging.

key_procedures: Receipt of a complaint of ragging.
Inquiry into the complaint by the head of the educational institution within seven days.
Suspension of the student if a prima facie case is found.
Forwarding the complaint to the police.
Dismissal of the student if convicted under section 4.
administration: The Government of Kerala (implied by the power to make rules and the title of the Act relating to the State of Kerala).
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on 23rd day of April 1998 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 1007 dated 24th June, 1998.
The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.
The Act came into force on the 23rd day of October, 1997.

title: The Kerala Prohibition of Charging Exorbitant Interest Act, 2012
purpose: To prohibit lending of money for exorbitant interest and to provide for stringent punishment for charging exorbitant interest in the money lending business in the State of Kerala and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala concerning money lending business and the charging of exorbitant interest.

key_definitions.daily_vatti: Interest on daily basis which will work out to an interest rate more than that specified under sub-section (1) of section 7 of the Kerala Money-Lenders Act, 1958 (35 of 1958).
key_definitions.debtor: A person who receives loan for exorbitant interest.
key_definitions.exorbitant_interest: Interest at the rate more than the rate specified in sub-section (1) of section 7 of the Kerala Money-Lenders Act, 1958 and includes daily vatti, hourly vatti, kandu vatti, meter vatti and thandal.
key_definitions.hourly_vatti: Interest on hourly basis which will work out to an interest rate more than that specified under sub-section (1) of section 7 of the Kerala Money-Lenders Act, 1958 (35 of 1958).
key_definitions.kandu_vatti: Interest which will work out to an interest rate more than that specified under sub-section (1) of section 7 of the Kerala Money-Lenders Act, 1958 (35 of 1958).
key_definitions.loan: Advance of money for daily vatti, hourly vatti, kandu vatti, meter vatti or thandal.
key_definitions.meter_vatti: Interest which will work out to an interest rate more than that specified under sub-section (1) of section 7 of the Kerala Money-Lenders Act, 1958 (35 of 1958) for every day on the loan amount not paid within the stipulated time.
key_definitions.thandal: Interest which will work out to an interest rate more than that specified under sub-section (1) of section 7 of the Kerala Money-Lenders Act, 1958 (35 of 1958) which is to be recovered daily along with the part of the loan amount.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Prohibition of Charging Exorbitant Interest Act, 2012 and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 27th day of August, 2012.

Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'daily vatti', 'debtor', 'exorbitant interest', 'hourly vatti', 'kandu vatti', 'loan', 'meter vatti', and 'thandal'. It also states that words and expressions not defined in this Act but defined in the Kerala Money-Lenders Act, 1958 (35 of 1958) shall have the meanings assigned to them in that Act.
No person shall charge exorbitant interest on any loan advanced by him.

main_sections.section_title: Offences to be cognizable and non-bailable
main_sections.description: Any offence under this Act shall be cognizable and non-bailable.

main_sections.section_title: Deposit of money and presentation of petition before the Court
main_sections.description: (1) A debtor may deposit the money due in respect of loan received by him from any person together with interest at the rate specified under sub-section (1) of section 7 of the Kerala Money-Lenders Act, 1958 (35 of 1958) into the Court, having jurisdiction, along with a petition to record that the amount deposited is in full or in part satisfaction of the loan including the interest thereon, as the case may be. (2) The Court shall, on receipt of a petition under sub-section (1), refer a copy of the petition to the person mentioned in the petition, directing him to give his version of the case within a period of fifteen days or within such other time as may be granted by the Court. The Court may, after due inquiry and after considering the versions of the parties, pass orders recording the satisfaction of the loan and interest thereon in full or in part, as the case may be.

important_rules: No person shall charge exorbitant interest on any loan advanced by him.

penalties: Offences are cognizable and non-bailable.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Courts (as implied by section 5 for deposit and petition)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through court procedures involving deposit of money and petition presentation by debtors.

rights: Right of a debtor to deposit the money due in court to satisfy the loan and interest.
obligations: Obligation for lenders not to charge exorbitant interest.

key_procedures: Procedure for debtors to deposit loan amounts with the court to claim satisfaction of the loan.
Court procedure to hear both debtor and lender and pass orders regarding loan satisfaction.
administration: Government of Kerala, Law (Legislation-A) Department
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on August 27, 2012.
Words and expressions not defined in this Act are to be interpreted as per the Kerala Money-Lenders Act, 1958.

title: The Kerala Promotion Of Tree Growth In Non-Forest Areas (Amendment) Act, 2007
purpose: To amend the Kerala Promotion of Tree Growth in Non-Forest Areas Act, 2005.
scope: Applies to tree growth in non-forest areas in Kerala.

key_definitions.specified tree: Includes Coconut, Rubber, Cashew, Tamarind, Mango, Jackfruit Tree, Kodampuli, Mattu, Aiecanut, Kounna, Seema, Konna, Nelli, Neem, Murukku, Jathi, Albezia, Silk cotton, Acacia, auraculi/ormis, Mangium, Anjili, Kuhmaram, Manchadu maram, Vatta, Palm tree, Aranama ram, Eucalyptus, Seemaplavu, Paala.
key_definitions.small holder: Means the owner of a non-forest land not exceeding one hectare in extent as on the date of coming into force of the Kerala Promotion of Tree Growth in Non-Forest Areas (Amendment) Act, 2007.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Promotion of Tree Growth in Non-Forest Areas (Amendment) Act, 2007. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 7th day of August, 2006.
Inserts new clauses in section 2 of the principal Act to define 'specified tree' and 'small holder'.

Substitutes section 6 of the principal Act. It states that owners of non-notified areas in non-forest land have the right to cut and transport any tree, standing on his land. It also outlines provisions for government notification for preservation of tree growth, and the role of authorized officers in preventing unlawful cutting or destruction of trees.

Substitutes section 7 of the principal Act, which deals with penalties. It prescribes punishments for whoever cuts, uproots, burns or otherwise destroys any tree other than sandalwood in violation of the provisions of this Act or transports any timber contravening the provisions of section 6 or files a false declaration. Penalties include imprisonment and fines.
Amends section 9 of the principal Act, substituting the words 'any timber has been transported' with 'any timber has been cut or any timber has been transported'.
Inserts a schedule listing trees for which no permission is necessary for cutting and removal.
Omits section 17 of the principal Act.
Repeals the Kerala Promotion of Tree Growth in Non-Forest Areas (Amendment) Ordinance, 2007 and provides for saving provisions.

important_rules: Owners of non-notified areas in non-forest land have the right to cut and transport any tree standing on their land.

Government may notify areas for preservation of tree growth, and direct that no tree standing in such notified areas shall be cut, uprooted, burnt or otherwise destroyed if it constitutes a danger to life or property or is windfallen.
No owner including a small holder shall cut or remove any sandalwood tree in any non-forest area without prior permission.
Specified trees can be cut or transported from non-forest land to any other place after obtaining permission and filing a declaration with the Authorized Officer.
Penalties are prescribed for violations, including cutting or uprooting trees, or transporting timber contravening the Act.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to twenty-five thousand rupees.

Imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than six months but which may extend to three years and with a fine which shall not be less than fifty thousand rupees, but which may extend to one lakh rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Authorised Officers (referred to as Authorised Officer in this Act) and Forest Officer, or such local limits as the Government thinks fit.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, including the requirement for permission, filing declarations, and imposition of penalties upon violation.

rights: Right of owners to cut and remove trees in non-notified areas in non-forest land, subject to other provisions.
Right to appeal against the order of refusal of permission by the Authorized Officer.
duties: Duty to obtain permission for cutting and transporting specified trees from non-forest land.
Duty to file a declaration with the Authorized Officer for cutting and transporting specified trees.
Duty to obtain prior permission in writing from the Authorised Officer and such prior permission shall not be required for the cutting and removal of trees except specified trees.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder.

key_procedures: For cutting or removing a specified tree from non-forest land: Obtain permission from the Authorised Officer. File a declaration with the Authorised Officer containing details of the land, tree species, quantity, and purpose of transport. Acknowledge receipt of the declaration within twenty days. Permission is granted if the trees are to be cut and removed from a non-notified area.
Appeal against refusal of permission: An appeal may be preferred before the concerned Divisional Forest Officer/Wildlife Warden within a specified time.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be handled by Forest Officers and Authorised Officers under the purview of the Kerala Government.
important_notes: The provisions for cutting and removing trees under section 3 of this Act shall not apply to trees, if any, reserved by the Government at the time of assignment of such land or trees standing on any land notified under section 5 of the Kerala Preservation of Trees Act, 1986 (35 of 1986) or the areas notified by the Custodian under the Kerala Forest (Vesting and Management of ecologically Fragile Lands) Act, 2003 (21 of 2005).
Note: For the purpose of this sub-section all the mangrove areas or Cardamom or coffee plantations shall be deemed to be notified areas.
The term 'timber' wherever used shall include firewood also.

title: The Kerala Promotion Of Tree Growth in Non-Forest Areas Act, 2005
purpose: To promote tree growth in non-forest areas of Kerala and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to all non-forest areas within the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.tree: Includes trees of any species, whether planted or self-grown, and also includes palms, bamboos, and ornamental plants.
key_definitions.non-forest area: Any land in the State of Kerala which is not a forest within the meaning of the Kerala Forest Act, 1961, or which has not been declared as a forest by the Government.
key_definitions.owner: Includes any person who is for the time being the owner of the land, or the person in possession or occupation of the land, or any other person having any right, title or interest in the land.

main_sections.description: Provides for the short title of the Act, its extent (State of Kerala), and its commencement.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'tree', 'non-forest area', 'owner', 'Government', etc.

main_sections.section_title: Power to prohibit or regulate cutting of trees
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to prohibit or regulate the cutting of trees in non-forest areas.
Specifies the procedure for obtaining permission to cut trees in non-forest areas.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for illegal cutting of trees
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for unauthorized cutting of trees.
Provides for the establishment of a Tree Authority for the implementation of the Act.
Outlines the functions and responsibilities of the Tree Authority.
Grants the Government the power to frame rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: No person shall cut any tree in a non-forest area without obtaining prior permission from the prescribed authority.
Permission for cutting trees will be granted based on specific criteria and for bonafide purposes.
The Tree Authority shall take steps to promote tree growth in non-forest areas.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees or with both for contravention of the provisions of the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Prescribed authority under the Act, and the Tree Authority.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, imposition of penalties, and legal proceedings.

rights: Right to obtain permission for cutting trees for bonafide purposes.
duties: Duty to obtain permission before cutting trees.
Duty to cooperate with the authorities in the promotion of tree growth.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act and the rules framed thereunder.

key_procedures: Application for permission to cut trees: Submission of an application to the prescribed authority with details of the tree and the purpose of cutting.
Inspection and decision: The prescribed authority will inspect the site and decide on the application.
Planting of compensatory trees: If permission is granted, the applicant may be required to plant a specified number of compensatory trees.
administration: The Act is administered by the Forest Department of the Government of Kerala, through the prescribed authorities and the Tree Authority.
important_notes: The Act aims to balance development needs with the necessity of preserving and promoting tree cover.
The rules made under the Act may prescribe the fees for obtaining permission for cutting trees.
Exceptions may be provided for specific categories of trees or for certain public utility purposes.

title: THE KERALA PROMOTION OF TREE GROWTH IN NON-FOREST AREAS ACT, 2005
purpose: To promote cultivation of trees in non-forest areas of the State, in order to increase green cover, preserve bio-diversity and arrest soil erosion and to increase availability of timber and bamboo for industry.
scope: Applies to all non-forest areas in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Local Self Government Institution: means a Panchayat at any level constituted under the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 (13 of 1994) or a Municipality constituted under the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994 (20 of 1994)
key_definitions.Non-Forest land: includes all private lands, lands vested in or transferred to or purchased by the Local Self Government Institutions, but does not include Cardamom Hill Reserve lands, lands declared or deemed to have been declared as reserve forest or any other forest land or land assigned to Scheduled Tribes under any law, for the time being in force and paddy fields;
key_definitions.prescribed tree: means prescribed by rules made under this Act
key_definitions.specified tree: means Teak (Tectona grandis), Rosewood (Dalbergia latifolia), Iruil (Xylia xylocarpa), Thempavu (Terminalia tomentosa), Kampalkom (Hopea parviflora), Vellakil (Dysoxylum malabaricum) or Ebony (Diospyrus sp )
key_definitions.tree: means any woody plant, whether fruit bearing or not, and includes bamboos

main_sections.section_title: Short title, commencement, extent and application
main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Promotion of Tree Growth in Non-Forest Areas Act, 2005. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. It shall come into force at once. It shall apply to all non-forest lands in the State.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Government', 'Local Self Government Institution', 'Non-Forest land', 'prescribed tree', 'specified tree', 'State', and 'tree'.

main_sections.section_title: Rights of owner of non-forest lands
main_sections.description: Every owner of non-forest land shall be free to plant trees in his land, as may be appropriate and generally contribute to the increase of tree cover in his land, in addition to any crop he may have grown over such land.

main_sections.section_title: Duties of Local Self Government Institutions
main_sections.description: Local Self Government Institutions shall promote tree growth in non-forest areas and be responsible for the cultivation of saplings in lands owned or transferred, carrying out census of existing trees, development and maintenance of nurseries, supply of seeds and saplings, getting trees planted or transplanted for construction of buildings, roads or for safeguarding life and property, organizing demonstrations and extension services, and undertaking or executing schemes for achieving the objects of this Act.

The Forest Department shall develop, maintain or approve private nurseries, supply seeds and saplings, to persons required to plant new trees or replace felled trees, execute social forestry schemes, give technical and other assistance in planting trees, and exercise powers and perform duties as laid down in the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Right of the owners to cut and remove trees
main_sections.description: Owners of non-forest land shall have the right to cut and transport any tree, other than sandalwood tree, standing on his land, provided that the tree is not a specified tree, or a tree standing on government notified land under section 5 of the Kerala Preservation of Trees Act, 1986. Timber transported from non-forest land to any other place requires declaration detailing number of trees, species, quantity of timber, and place of transport. Transported timber from reserve forest boundary within five kilometers requires inspection by Forest Range Officer. If no receipt is received within twenty days, it is deemed to have been received. Cutting and removal of trees standing on forest areas, owned, controlled or vested in a Local Self Government Institution and its disposal shall be governed by rules.

Whoever transports any timber contravening the provisions of section 6 or falsely declares any timber shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees.

If an offence under this Act is committed by a company, every person responsible for the conduct of its business shall be guilty and liable to punishment. Provided that nothing in this sub-section shall render any person liable if he proves that the offence was committed without his knowledge or that he exercised all due diligence to prevent the commission of such offence.

main_sections.section_title: Power to seize timber and other articles involved in the commission of the offence
main_sections.description: Any Officer of the Forest Department, below the rank of a Forester, may seize timber, tools, ropes, chains and other articles used in the commission of such offence, and also vehicles or boats used for carrying such timber.

main_sections.section_title: Power to release property seized under section 9
main_sections.description: The Divisional Forest Officer may release any seized tool, rope, chain or other article or any vehicle or boat, if it has been made to the Executive Court or the Judicial Magistrate of the First Class. Upon receiving a report under section 9(3), the Magistrate shall take measures as may be necessary for the trial of the accused and the disposal of the timber and tool, rope, chain or other article or any boat, vehicle or animal seized.
