Upon receipt of a report under section 9(3) of section 9, the Magistrate shall take measures as may be necessary for the trial of the accused and the disposal of the timber and tool, rope, chain or other article or any boat, vehicle or animal seized along with it, according to law.
No prosecution shall be instituted against any person without the sanction of the Divisional Forest Officer.
An offence punishable under this Act shall be tried before a Court of the Judicial Magistrate of the First Class having jurisdiction.

No suit, prosecution or other legal proceedings shall lie against the Government or any officer or authority or any other person for anything which is, in good faith done, or purporting to have been done under this Act or any rule or order made thereunder.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act. Every rule made under this section shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is issued or made, before the Legislative Assembly, while it is in session for a total period of fourteen days, which may be comprised in one session or in two successive sessions, and if, before the expiry of the session in which it is so laid or the session immediately following, the Legislative Assembly makes any modification in the rule or decides that the rule should not be issued, the rule shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect, as the case may be, so, however, that any such modification or annulment shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that notification or rule.

If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, the Government may, by order published in the Gazette, make such provisions, not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act, which appear to them necessary for the purpose of removing the difficulty. Every such order made under this section shall, as soon as may be after it is made, be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

Section 4 of the Kerala Preservation of Trees Act, 1986 (35 of 1986) is hereby repealed. Notwithstanding the repeal of section 4 of the Kerala Preservation of Trees Act, 1986 (35 of 1986), the provisions of section 4 to 23 of the Interpretation and General Clauses Act, 1125 (7 of 1125) shall apply upon the repeal of the said section.

important_rules: Owners of non-forest land are free to plant trees.
Local Self Government Institutions and the Forest Department have specific duties to promote tree growth and support cultivation.
Transportation of timber from non-forest land requires specific declarations.
Penalties are prescribed for contravening provisions related to timber transportation and false declarations.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees for contravening timber transportation rules or false declarations.
Offences by companies are punishable, with responsibility on persons in charge of business conduct.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Forest Department officials, including Divisional Forest Officers, and Judicial Magistrates of the First Class.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Seizure of timber and articles involved in offences, prosecution of offenders, and by laying down rules and procedures for the implementation of the Act.

rights: Owners of non-forest land have the right to plant trees.
Owners of non-forest land have the right to cut and transport trees (with exceptions for sandalwood and specified trees).
duties: Local Self Government Institutions have duties to promote tree growth, manage nurseries, supply seeds/saplings, conduct extension services, and ensure tree planting for infrastructure projects.
The Forest Department has duties to develop and manage nurseries, supply seeds/saplings, execute social forestry schemes, and provide technical assistance.
Individuals transporting timber must declare details of the timber and transport.
Companies are responsible for ensuring compliance with the Act by their personnel.
obligations: Individuals and companies must adhere to the provisions of the Act regarding tree growth and timber transport.

key_procedures: Procedure for reporting timber transport: Owner must declare the number of trees, species, quantity of timber, and place of transport.
Procedure for seizure of timber and articles: Forest Department officials can seize timber and associated items involved in offences.
Procedure for release of seized property: Divisional Forest Officer can release seized property.
Procedure for prosecution: Prosecution requires sanction from the Divisional Forest Officer and trial by the Judicial Magistrate of the First Class.
administration: Forest Department and Local Self Government Institutions are involved in administration and implementation. The Government has the power to make rules and remove difficulties.
important_notes: The Act aims to increase green cover, preserve bio-diversity, and arrest soil erosion.
The Act distinguishes between 'specified trees' and other trees.
The Government can make rules by notification in the Gazette, which are subject to modification or annulment by the Legislative Assembly.
The Act repeals Section 4 of the Kerala Preservation of Trees Act, 1986, but certain provisions of the Interpretation and General Clauses Act still apply.

title: The Kerala Protection Of River Banks and Regulation of Removal Of Sand Act, 2001
purpose: To provide for the protection of river banks and the regulation of the removal of sand in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the entire State of Kerala and concerns the protection of river banks and the regulation of sand removal.

key_definitions.river: Includes streams, canals, backwaters, and other bodies of water flowing in the river banks.
key_definitions.river bank: Means the land adjacent to a river up to a specified distance from the edge of the river.
key_definitions.sand: Includes sand, gravel, silt, and other materials removed from river beds and banks.
key_definitions.competent authority: Refers to the authority designated by the Government to implement this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and its commencement date.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'river', 'river bank', 'sand', and 'competent authority'.
Outlines the rules and restrictions regarding the removal of sand from rivers and their banks.
Details the powers vested in the competent authority for the implementation and enforcement of the Act, including inspection, seizure, and prohibition of sand removal.
Specifies the procedure for obtaining permits or licenses for the removal of sand and the conditions attached thereto.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of unauthorized removal of sand
main_sections.description: Prohibits the removal of sand without a valid permit or license and imposes penalties for violations.
Mandates measures for the protection of river banks from erosion and damage caused by sand removal or other activities.
Provides for the procedure to appeal against any order or decision passed by the competent authority.
Defines the offences under the Act and prescribes the penalties, including fines and imprisonment, for violations.

important_rules: Removal of sand from river banks is prohibited without a valid permit or license.
The competent authority has the power to inspect, seize, and confiscate materials and equipment used in unauthorized sand removal.
Measures must be taken to protect river banks from erosion and damage.
The Act specifies restrictions on the quantity and method of sand removal.
Penalties are prescribed for violations of the Act's provisions.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both.
Seizure of vehicles and equipment used for unauthorized sand removal.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Competent Authority appointed by the Government of Kerala.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspection, seizure of illegally extracted sand and vehicles, imposition of fines, and prosecution of offenders.

rights: Right to obtain a permit for sand removal under prescribed conditions.
Right to appeal against orders of the competent authority.
duties: Duty to protect river banks from degradation.
Duty to comply with the regulations for sand removal.
Duty to obtain necessary permits before undertaking sand removal activities.
obligations: Obligation to ensure that sand removal activities do not cause environmental damage or harm to river ecosystems.

key_procedures: Application for a permit to remove sand from a river bank.
Inspection and verification of applications by the competent authority.
Grant or refusal of permits with specific conditions.
Monitoring of sand removal activities to ensure compliance.
Action against unauthorized sand removal and violations of permit conditions.
Appellate procedure for challenging decisions of the competent authority.
administration: The Government of Kerala, through the departments responsible for Revenue, Water Resources, and Environment.
important_notes: The Act aims to balance the need for sand as a resource with the imperative of environmental protection.
Specific rules and guidelines for sand mining may be issued by the Government.
The Act emphasizes sustainable sand management practices.

title: The Kerala Protection of Interests of Depositors in Financial Establishments Act, 2013
purpose: To provide for the protection of interests of depositors in financial establishments in Kerala and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to financial establishments in Kerala and matters connected therewith. It also governs the attachment of property and conduct of criminal proceedings related to defaults in repayment of deposits.

key_definitions.competent authority: Means the authority appointed under section 4 of this Act.
key_definitions.deposit: Means the deposit of money either in lump sum or by instalments made in a financial establishment for a fixed period, for interest or for properties or for return in any kind or for any service.
key_definitions.financial establishment: Means a person, an association of persons, a partnership firm or a company registered under the Companies Act, 1956 (Central Act 1 of 1956) carrying on the business of receiving deposits under any scheme or arrangement or in any other manner but does not include a corporation or a co-operative society under the ownership or control of any State Government or of the Central Government or a banking company as defined in clause (c) of section 5 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
key_definitions.special court: Means a special court constituted under section 7 of this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Protection of Interests of Depositors in Financial Establishments Act, 2013 and shall come into force at once.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'competent authority', 'deposit', 'financial establishment', 'Government', 'property', and 'Special Court'.

main_sections.section_title: Attachment of property on default of return of deposits
main_sections.description: Outlines the process for attaching property of a financial establishment when it defaults in returning deposits or if the Government has reason to believe it is acting to defraud depositors. The Government can pass an ad-interim order of attachment.

Empowers the Government to appoint competent authorities by notification in the Gazette for exercising control over money and properties attached under section 3. It also details the powers of the competent authority, including making applications to the Special Court for attachment of property.

main_sections.section_title: Default in repayment of deposits and interests honouring the commitment
main_sections.description: Specifies that if a financial establishment defaults in repayment of deposits or interests, every person responsible for its management shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years and with fine which may extend to one lakh rupees. The financial establishment is also liable for fine which may extend to one lakh rupees.

Allows for the compounding of an offence punishable under section 5 before or after the institution of prosecution, by the competent authority with the permission of the Special Court, on payment of the entire amount due to the depositors.

Provides for the establishment of Special Courts by the Government for the purpose of the Act, with the concurrence of the Chief Justice of the High Court. These courts have jurisdiction to try cases arising under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of the Special Court regarding attachment, sale, realisation and distribution
main_sections.description: Details the powers of the Special Court in relation to attachment, sale, realization, and distribution of attached properties. This includes issuing notices, holding inquiries, ordering attachment or release of property, and directing the sale of attached properties.

main_sections.section_title: Attachment of property of mala fide transferees
main_sections.description: Deals with the attachment of property transferred with mala fide intention by a financial establishment or any person referred to in section 3, if the value of such property is found to be less than the amount due to depositors. The Special Court can order attachment of such property.
Allows for the release of attached property if the financial establishment or person provides adequate security to the satisfaction of the Special Court, in lieu of attachment.
Empowers the Special Court to provide from the attached property for the maintenance of the applicant and his family, and for expenses connected with criminal proceedings initiated against them.
Provides for any person aggrieved by an order of the Special Court to appeal before the High Court within thirty days from the date of the order.
Mandates the Government to appoint one or more advocates, not less than ten years standing, as Special Public Prosecutors for conducting cases in the Special Court.

important_rules: A financial establishment defaulting in returning deposits or interests is liable for punishment.
Persons responsible for the management of a defaulting financial establishment are subject to imprisonment and fine.
Property of financial establishments that default on deposits can be attached.
Transfers of property made with mala fide intention by a financial establishment or person referred to in section 3 can be attached.
The Special Court has the power to order the attachment, sale, realization, and distribution of attached properties.
Appeals against orders of the Special Court can be filed before the High Court.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years and with fine which may extend to one lakh rupees for default in repayment of deposits.
Fine which may extend to one lakh rupees for the financial establishment itself.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Competent Authority appointed by the Government, and the Special Court.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through attachment of property, sale of property, criminal prosecution, and imposition of fines and imprisonment.

rights: Depositors have the right to have their deposits and interests repaid.
Aggrieved persons have the right to appeal against orders of the Special Court to the High Court.
duties: Financial establishments have a duty to honour their commitments regarding the repayment of deposits and interests.
Persons responsible for the management of financial establishments have a duty to ensure timely repayment of deposits.
obligations: Financial establishments and their management have an obligation to comply with the provisions of this Act.

key_procedures: Upon default of return of deposits, the Government can pass an ad-interim order for attachment of property.
The competent authority can make an application to the Special Court for attachment of property.
The Special Court conducts proceedings for attachment, sale, realization, and distribution of attached properties.
Appeals against Special Court orders are filed before the High Court.
administration: Government of Kerala (Law (Legislation-A) Department)
important_notes: The Act is an English translation of the original Malayalam Act.
The Act came into force on the 14th December 2015.
The 'competent authority' is appointed by the Government and has significant powers in managing attached properties.
Special Courts are constituted to expedite cases under this Act.
The Act aims to protect the interests of depositors in financial establishments.

title: The Kerala Protection of River Banks and Regulation of Removal of Sand (Amendment) Act, 2013
purpose: To amend the Kerala Protection of River Banks and Regulation of Removal of Sand Act, 2001.
scope: The Act applies to the Kerala state and regulates the removal of sand from river banks.

key_definitions.authorised officer: The Commissioner of Land Revenue or any other officer entrusted by the Government under the said section to assist him.
key_definitions.vehicle: Includes country boat, raft and any other vessel.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Protection of River Banks and Regulation of Removal of Sand (Amendment) Act, 2013. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 25th day of November, 2012.
Amends section 2 of the principal Act by inserting new definitions for 'authorised officer' and 'State High Level Committee', and a new 'Special Protection Force'.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of State High Level Committee
main_sections.description: Details the constitution and functions of the State High Level Committee, including its meeting schedule, quorum, and powers.

Specifies that the Commissioner of Land Revenue shall be the authorised officer to exercise overall supervision of the implementation of the provisions of this Act, and all officers shall comply with his directions.
Introduces new sections 2A and 2B into the principal Act.

Amends section 3 of the principal Act, substituting 'two Environmentalists' with 'three Environmentalists' and adding new clauses for Revenue Divisional Officer and persons nominated by the Government.
Amends section 4 of the principal Act, similar to section 3, by substituting 'two Environmentalists' with 'three Environmentalists'.

Amends section 9 of the principal Act by replacing 'two Environmentalists' with 'three Environmentalists' and including 'expert agencies like the Centre for Earth Science Studies and Centre for Water Resources Development and Management'.
Amends section 12 of the principal Act by modifying time limits for sand removal operations and introducing a new explanation for 'water supply project'.
Amends section 15 of the principal Act, inserting new sub-sections regarding permitted areas for sand removal, demarcation of areas, and use of vehicles for sand collection and removal.

Amends section 17 of the principal Act, substituting 'the Secretary of the local authority concerned' with 'the Revenue Department' and adding provisions for nomination by the District Collector and Panchayat.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new sections for section 23
main_sections.description: Substitutes section 23 of the principal Act with new provisions regarding the seizure of sand, vehicles, tools, and implements used in its removal, and the role of the Village Officer or police officer.
Outlines the procedure for confiscation of sand and associated items, including the seizure process, report to Judicial Magistrate, and subsequent actions.
Provides for revision petitions to the District Collector against orders of confiscation within fifteen days.
Allows appeals to the District Court against orders of confiscation within thirty days.

main_sections.section_title: Return of the confiscated article or the amount paid in lieu of confiscation
main_sections.description: Details the process for returning confiscated articles or amounts paid in lieu of confiscation.

important_rules: Sand removal operations shall not be carried out within a distance of 500 meters from any bridge or any irrigation project or pumping station of water supply projects or check dams or from their retaining wall or the venue of any religious or cultural activities conducted on river bank or the sand bank in river or in part of the river.

No sand removal and transportation are permitted by putting up of chains and pillars so as to ensure that no vehicles are taken to river bank and no illegal sand removal and transportation are carried on.

penalties: The confiscation of sand, vehicles, tools, implements, loading equipment, vehicles and other articles used or intended to be used for such activities, including sand, shall be seized by an officer not below the rank of a Village Officer or a police officer not below the rank of a station house officer or a member of the Special Protection Force.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Commissioner of Land Revenue, District Collector, Judicial Magistrate, District Court, Revenue Divisional Officer, and officers of the Revenue Department.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through seizure and confiscation of sand and related materials, revision petitions, and appeals.

rights: Right to appeal against confiscation orders to the District Collector and District Court.
duties: All officers to comply with the directions given by the authorised officer.
Persons removing sand to do so only under the provisions of this Act and rules made thereunder.

key_procedures: Procedure for seizure and confiscation of sand, vehicles, tools, and implements used in illegal sand removal.
Procedure for filing revision petitions to the District Collector.
Procedure for filing appeals to the District Court.
Procedure for return of confiscated articles or amounts.
administration: Department of Law (Legislation-B) Department, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the principal Act of 2001.
Certain provisions are deemed to have come into force from November 25, 2012.
The State High Level Committee has powers to grant approval to any scheme.
The term 'vehicle' includes country boat, raft and any other vessel.

title: THE KERALA PROVISIONAL COLLECTION OF REVENUES ACT, 1985
purpose: To provide for the immediate effect for a limited period of provisions in Bills for giving effect to budget proposals.
scope: Applies to provisions in Bills relating to imposition or increase of taxes, duties, cesses, fees and other revenues introduced in the Legislative Assembly of Kerala, with effect from the commencement of the financial year to which the proposals relate.

key_definitions.declared provision: A provision in a Bill in respect of which a declaration has been made under section 3.
key_definitions.Legislative Assembly: The Legislative Assembly of the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as The Kerala Provisional Collection of Revenues Act, 1985, and specifies its commencement date as the 1st day of March 1984.
Defines 'declared provision' and 'Legislative Assembly'.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make declarations under this Act
main_sections.description: Grants the Legislative Assembly the power to declare a Bill imposing or increasing any tax, duty, cess, fee, or other revenue, to be expedient in the public interest, and to have effect from the date of introduction of the Bill.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of declarations under this Act and duration thereof
main_sections.description: States that a declared provision shall have the force of law from the 1st day of April following the date on which the Bill containing it is introduced in the Legislative Assembly, or on the date on which the Bill containing it is first published in the Kerala Gazette, whichever is later. The provision remains in force until the expiry of one hundred and twenty days from the date of its introduction.

main_sections.section_title: Certain refunds to be made when declaration ceases to have effect
main_sections.description: Specifies that where a declared provision ceases to have effect, any tax, duty, cess, fee, or other revenue collected under it, which would not have been collected if the provision had not been made, shall be refunded. The refund amount should not exceed the difference between the rate of such collection and the rate that would have been applicable without the declared provision.
Repeals The Kerala Provisional Collection of Revenues Ordinance, 1984, but saves any action taken or anything done or deemed to have been taken or done under the Ordinance.

important_rules: A declared provision in a Bill shall have the force of law on or after the 1st day of April following the introduction of the Bill, or the date of its first publication in the Kerala Gazette, whichever is later.
The declared provision shall remain in force for a maximum of one hundred and twenty days from the date of introduction of the Bill.
If a declared provision ceases to have effect, taxes, duties, etc., collected under it that would not have been collected otherwise must be refunded.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be the executive/revenue authorities responsible for collecting taxes and duties.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the collection of taxes, duties, cesses, fees, and other revenues as per the declared provisions in Bills.

rights: Right to receive refunds for taxes, duties, etc., collected under a declared provision that subsequently ceases to have effect, where such collection would not have occurred otherwise.
duties: Duty to collect taxes, duties, etc., as per declared provisions in Bills.
Duty to refund amounts collected under a declared provision that ceases to have effect, if those amounts would not have been collected otherwise.

key_procedures: Introduction of a Bill in the Legislative Assembly containing proposals for imposition or increase of taxes, duties, cesses, fees, or other revenues.
Declaration by the Legislative Assembly that the Bill is expedient in the public interest.
Collection of revenue based on the declared provision from the effective date until the expiry of 120 days from introduction.
Refund of collected revenue if the declared provision ceases to have effect and the collection would not have occurred otherwise.
administration: Implied to be the Finance Department and other relevant revenue departments of the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act provides for provisional collection of revenues, meaning it's a temporary measure.
The duration of the provisional collection is limited to 120 days.
The Act allows for the refund of revenues collected under provisional measures if the permanent legislation is not enacted or if the declared provision ceases to have effect.
The Kerala Provisional Collection of Revenues Ordinance, 1984, was repealed by this Act.

title: The Kerala Provisional Collection of Revenues (Amendment) Act, 1991
purpose: To amend the Kerala Provisional Collection of Revenues Act, 1985.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Provisional Collection of Revenues (Amendment) Act, 1991, and that it shall come into force at once.
Amends the preamble to the Kerala Provisional Collection of Revenues Act, 1985, by substituting specific words.
Amends section 3 of the principal Act by substituting specific words after the 'introduction of the Bill'.
Amends section 4 of the principal Act. This amendment involves substituting words in sub-section (1) and in clause (ii) of sub-section (2).
Amends section 5 of the principal Act. This amendment involves substituting words in the proviso to sub-section (1).

important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 31st day of July, 1991 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No 948 dated the 31st July 1991.

title: THE KERALA PUBLIC ACCOUNTANTS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2007
purpose: To amend the Kerala Public Accountants Act, 1963 for the purposes therein appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Public Accountants Act, 1963.

key_definitions.Government Law Officer: Any person appointed for a specified term or for any other specified purpose by the Government to conduct cases on behalf of the Government in any court, tribunal or other authority in the State of Kerala or any other State in India or in the Supreme Court.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Public Accountants (Amendment) Act, 2007, and it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 19th day of October, 2005.

In the Kerala Public Accountants Act, 1963 (37 of 1963) (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), in section 2, after clause (a), the following clause shall be inserted, namely:-
"(aa) "Government Law Officer" means any person appointed for a specified term or for any other specified purpose by the Government to conduct cases on behalf of the Government in any court, tribunal or other authority in the State of Kerala or any other State in India or in the Supreme Court,"
and in clause (b), the words "and includes a person who is, or has been, a Government Law Officer" shall be added at the end.

In Section 3 of the principal Act, to sub-section (1), the following Explanation shall be added, namely:-
"Explanation.—For the purposes of this sub-section,-
(i) a Government Law Officer appointed to conduct cases before any court (other than the High Court of Kerala or the Supreme Court), Tribunal or other authority shall be deemed to be a public accountant serving under the Collector, and
(ii) the Advocate General shall be deemed to be the Head of a Department of the Government, under whom a Government Law Officer appointed to conduct cases in the High Court of Kerala or the Supreme Court is or was serving."

The Kerala Public Accountants (Amendment) Ordinance, 2007 (8 of 2007) is hereby repealed. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_notes: Received the assent of Governor on the 13th April, 2007 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordnary No 704 dated 13th April, 2007.

title: The Kerala Public Accountants Act, 1963
purpose: To consolidate and amend the laws relating to the prevention of loss to the Government by the default or misconduct of public accountants in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Kerala. It covers 'public accountants' who are employed in the service of the Government or any other notified authority or institution and are entrusted with public funds or property.

key_definitions.Collector: The Collector of a district.
key_definitions.public_accountant: A person employed in the service of the Government or any other notified authority or institution, who is entrusted with the receipt, custody, possession or control of any moneys or securities for money, documents, or other property belonging to the Government or such authority/institution. This also includes persons entrusted with such property belonging to any person for and on behalf of the Government or any such authority or institution.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Public Accountants Act, 1963, and it extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.
Provides definitions for 'Collector' and 'public accountant'.

main_sections.section_title: Statements of particulars of claim to be drawn up by Collector or Head of Department
main_sections.description: Requires the Collector or Head of Department to draw up a statement of particulars of any claim against a public accountant. If the claimant is not a Collector, they may send the statement to the Collector of the jurisdiction where the accountant is or was employed. The Collector then issues a demand notice.

main_sections.section_title: Realisation of money and recovery of securities, etc., from public accountant
main_sections.description: Details the process for realizing money or recovering securities and property from a public accountant if they do not satisfy the demand or an adverse decision from the Collector. This can be done in the same manner as arrears of public revenue and involves powers similar to a Magistrate under the Code of Criminal Procedure for recovering property.

main_sections.section_title: Seizure and attachment of property of public accountant
main_sections.description: Empowers the Collector to issue a warrant for the immediate seizure of securities, documents, or property, or attachment of movable and immovable properties of a public accountant, if there is a belief that the accountant is attempting to conceal, destroy, or dispose of such assets to defeat proceedings under the Act. This is done pending the result of an enquiry.
Allows proceedings under the Act to be continued against the legal representative of a deceased public accountant, to the extent of the property of the deceased that has come into their hands.

Preserves the right of aggrieved parties to sue the Government or the concerned authority/institution in civil courts within one year from the cause of action, despite any proceedings taken under this Act.

Allows the Collector to delegate powers to subordinate officers not below the rank of Tahsildar, with certain restrictions. Orders passed by delegated officers are subject to confirmation by the Collector.
Repeals the Public Accountants Default Act, 1850, and other specified Acts and Regulations that were in force in any part of Kerala.

important_rules: Rule (Implied from Section 3): When a claim against a public accountant is identified, a detailed statement of particulars must be prepared by the Collector or Head of Department.
Rule (Implied from Section 3): A demand notice for money, securities, or property must be issued by the Collector, specifying delivery requirements and to whom it should be delivered.
Rule (Implied from Section 4): If a public accountant fails to satisfy a demand or an adverse decision, the Collector can recover dues as arrears of public revenue.

Rule (Implied from Section 5): Seizure or attachment of a public accountant's property requires the Collector to record reasons and can only happen if there's a belief of an attempt to conceal or dispose of assets.
Rule (Implied from Section 5 Proviso): Seizure or attachment will not take place or will be discontinued if the public accountant satisfies the claim or provides sufficient security.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Collector, and potentially other officers delegated powers by the Collector.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through drawing up statements of claims, issuing demand notices, recovery of dues as arrears of public revenue, seizure and attachment of property, and potentially through civil suits if remedies under the act are exhausted or deemed insufficient.

rights: Right of aggrieved parties to sue in civil courts (Section 7).
Right of a legal representative to be liable only to the extent of the deceased's property received and not disposed of (Section 6 Proviso).
duties: Duty of public accountants to satisfy claims for money, securities, documents, or property as demanded (Sections 3 & 4).
Duty of the Collector to draw up statements of claims and conduct enquiries (Section 3).
Duty of the Collector to issue demand notices and take recovery measures (Sections 3 & 4).
obligations: Public accountants have an obligation to be accountable for any loss to the Government due to their default or misconduct.
The Government or notified authorities/institutions have an obligation to prevent loss by taking action against defaulting public accountants.

key_procedures: Identification of a claim against a public accountant by the Collector or Head of Department.
Drawing up a statement of particulars of the claim.
Issuance of a demand notice by the Collector for delivery of money, securities, or property.
Enquiry by the Collector if the public accountant objects to the claim.
Recovery of money or property as arrears of public revenue if the demand is not satisfied or after a decision is made.
Seizure or attachment of property if there's an attempt to conceal or dispose of assets.
Continuance of proceedings against legal representatives upon the death of a public accountant.
administration: Public Works (Transport-A) Department (as per the Notification), with the Collector being the primary enforcer.
important_notes: The Act consolidates and amends existing laws related to public accountants.
The Act allows for delegation of powers by the Collector to subordinate officers, but with limitations.
The right to sue in civil courts is preserved, with a one-year limitation period for such suits.

title: The Kerala Public Buildings (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Amendment Act, 1986
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Public Buildings (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1968, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to public buildings in Kerala and deals with the eviction of unauthorized occupants from such buildings. The amendments are made to the principal Act of 1968.

key_definitions.company: A company in which not less than fifty-one per cent of the paid up share capital is held by the Government of Kerala or jointly by the Central Government and the Government of Kerala and includes a company which is a subsidiary of any such company.
key_definitions.corporation: A corporation established or constituted by or under any Central or State Act and owned or controlled by the Government of Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Public Buildings (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Amendment Act, 1986, and it shall come into force on the 7th day of February, 1983.

Amends Section 2 of the principal Act (Kerala Public Buildings (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1968) by re-lettering clause (aaa) and inserting new clauses defining 'company' and 'corporation'.
Amends Section 3 of the principal Act by substituting the proviso to clause (a).
Amends Section 6 of the principal Act by substituting certain words in the opening paragraph.
Amends Section 12 of the principal Act by substituting certain words in sub-section (2).
Amends Section 13 of the principal Act by substituting certain words.
Amends Section 14 of the principal Act by substituting certain words.
Amends Section 17 of the principal Act by substituting certain words.

Repeals the Kerala Public Buildings (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Ordinance, 1986 (54 of 1986). It also provides that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: The Act comes into force on the 7th day of February, 1983.
The definitions of 'company' and 'corporation' are amended in relation to the scope of the Act.
Amendments are made to various sections (3, 6, 12, 13, 14, 17) of the principal Act to modify its provisions.
key_procedures: The Act itself amends existing procedures for the eviction of unauthorized occupants from public buildings in Kerala. Specific procedural changes are detailed in the amendments to sections 2, 3, 6, 12, 13, 14, and 17 of the principal Act of 1968. These would involve how 'company' and 'corporation' are treated in eviction proceedings, and other related operational aspects.
Section 9 clarifies that actions taken under the repealed Ordinance remain valid under the amended Act.
administration: Likely administered by the relevant departments of the Kerala State Government dealing with public buildings and land management, as indicated by the definitions of 'company' and 'corporation' which involve the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Kerala Public Buildings (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1968.
The commencement date is retroactively set to February 7, 1983.
The Kerala Public Buildings (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Ordinance, 1986, has been repealed, with provisions to save actions taken under it.

scope: Applies to public libraries and the Kerala Grandhasala Sanghom in Kerala.

This section amends Section 12 of the principal Act. It details changes related to the Sanghom's board of directors and its powers. Specifically, it mentions the composition of the board, the appointment of the President, and the powers of the Sanghom regarding the management of its affairs. It also seems to introduce a new sub-section (2) to Section 12.
This section introduces a new section, 12A, into the principal Act. This new section likely deals with the election of members to the board of directors.
This section amends Section 20 of the principal Act. It pertains to the powers of the Sanghom regarding its property and affairs, likely including the management of funds and assets.

This section amends Section 26 of the principal Act, concerning the powers and functions of the Sanghom's executive committee and the General Council. It appears to clarify the roles and responsibilities of these bodies.

important_rules: The Sanghom shall have a Board of Directors consisting of a President and certain other members.
The President shall be appointed by the Government.
The Sanghom shall have the power to manage its affairs and property.
The executive committee and the General Council shall have specified powers and functions.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Likely the Government of Kerala and the Kerala Grandhasala Sanghom itself, through its administrative bodies.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions and powers granted by the Act to the Sanghom and its committees, and potentially through government oversight.

rights: Right of the Sanghom to manage its affairs and property.
duties: Duty to conduct elections for the board of directors.
obligations: Obligations related to the management of public libraries and the Sanghom's operations as defined in the amended sections.

The act amends The Kerala Public Libraries (Kerala Grandhasala Sanghom) Act, 1969.
Specific details regarding the number of members on the Board of Directors and their constituencies are provided in the amendments to Section 12 and the new Section 12A.

title: The Kerala Public Libraries (Kerala Grandhasala Sangham) Amendment Act, 1998
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Public Libraries (Kerala Grandhasala Sangham) Act, 1989.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Public Libraries (Kerala Grandhasala Sangham) Act, 1989. The amendments pertain to various sections of the principal Act, affecting definitions, constitution of committees, nominations, and references to other acts.

key_definitions.taluk_library_council: Means a Taluk Library Council constituted under section 13.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Public Libraries (Kerala Grandhasala Sangham) Amendment Act, 1998, and it came into force on the 20th day of April, 1998, with the remaining provisions coming into force on the 22nd day of May, 1998.
Amends section 2 of the Principal Act by substituting specific clauses related to the definition of 'Taluk Library Council'.

obligations: Obligation to substitute references to repealed Acts with current Acts as specified in Section 20.

Procedure for substitution of terms and references within the Act.
administration: Likely administered by the Department of Culture, Government of Kerala, or a similar department responsible for libraries and cultural affairs.

The Act makes significant amendments to the Kerala Public Libraries (Kerala Grandhasala Sangham) Act, 1989, updating definitions, committee compositions, and references to other legislation.
The Act repeals the Kerala Public Libraries (Kerala Grandhasala Sanghom) Amendment Ordinance, 1998, with a saving clause for actions taken under the Ordinance.

title: The Kerala Public Men Corruption (Investigations And Inquiries) Act, 1987
purpose: To provide for investigations and inquiries into allegations of corruption against public men in Kerala.
scope: Applies to public men in Kerala, including Chief Minister, Ministers, Members of the Legislative Assembly, and other persons specified in sub-clauses (iii) to (xii) of clause (j) of section 2.

key_definitions.public man: Includes Chief Minister, Minister, Member of the Legislative Assembly, and other specified persons holding public office.
key_definitions.appropriate authority: Means any authority which the Government may, by general or special order, in writing, determine to be appropriate authorities for the purposes of this Act.
key_definitions.corruption: Refers to acts of corruption by public men.

main_sections.description: Details the process for preliminary investigation by the Commission upon receipt of a complaint. It covers scrutiny, furnishing of copies to the public man, and making appropriate orders.

main_sections.section_title: Result of preliminary investigation and further action.
main_sections.description: Outlines the actions to be taken based on the preliminary investigation, including dismissing frivolous complaints or proceeding with further investigation, and the Commission's powers regarding the investigation and regulation of its proceedings.

Grants the Commission the power to issue search warrants to Police Officers or other authorities to search for and seize evidence related to investigations, including specific procedures for search and seizure.

Confers powers of a Civil Court on the Commission for the purpose of investigation, including summoning witnesses, examining on oath, requiring discovery and production of documents, receiving affidavits, and requisitioning public records.
Provides for prosecution for giving false evidence under section 183 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, in connection with proceedings before the Commission.

Details the process for the Commission to submit its report after an investigation, including communicating findings and recommendations to the competent authority and the Government, and annual reporting.

main_sections.section_title: Public man to vacate office if directed by Commission.
main_sections.description: Mandates that a public man shall make a declaration and intimate to the Commission the fact of such acceptance, and the Commission may direct a public man to vacate office under certain circumstances.
Empowers the Commission, after investigating a complaint of criminal offense, to direct prosecution of the public man concerned.
Stipulates that any information obtained by the Commission or its staff during an investigation shall be treated as confidential, with certain exceptions for purposes of proceedings or evidence.
Grants the Commission powers to punish for contempt of itself as the High Court, including reference to the High Court for certain matters.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken under the Act.
main_sections.description: Provides protection against suits, prosecutions, or other legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith under the Act. It also states that no proceedings of the Commission shall be invalid for want of form and, except on the ground of jurisdiction, no proceeding or decision shall be challenged in any court.

Allows the Commission to delegate its powers, by general or special order in writing, to the competent authority or other specified persons or authorities, except the power to make investigation under section 21.

main_sections.section_title: Conferment of additional function on Commission.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Governor to confer additional functions on the Commission by order, and for the Commission to exercise powers and discharge functions as if they were conferred by this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Public man to submit property statements.
main_sections.description: Requires public men to submit statements of their assets and liabilities within a specified period after the commencement of the Act and annually thereafter, and to disclose such statements to the competent authority.

States that no formal or open inquiry into any allegation against a public man shall be made except on the instance of the Government or by an order of the Government under the Commissions of Inquiry Act, 1952, or any other order of resolution of the Government.

Empowers the Commission to make allegations in the complaint as to be without substance or trivial in nature and not substantiated, and to pay such amount of costs as may be specified in the order to the public man referred to in sub-section (7) of section 13.

important_rules: The Commission shall have the powers of a Civil Court while trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
The Commission can order a public man to vacate office if it is satisfied that allegations against him are substantiated.
Information obtained by the Commission during an investigation shall be treated as confidential, with exceptions for proceedings or evidence.
The Commission has the power to punish for contempt of itself.

penalties: Prosecution for false evidence.
Public man may be compelled to give evidence or produce any document.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Commission, and the competent authority appointed by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through investigations, inquiries, issuance of search warrants, summoning of witnesses, production of documents, and prosecution.

rights: Right to be represented by counsel.
Right to be informed of allegations.
Right to have assistance of counsel in proceedings.
duties: Public men have a duty to cooperate with investigations.
Public men have a duty to submit property statements.
Public men have a duty to vacate office if directed by the Commission.
obligations: Obligation to ensure that investigations are conducted fairly.
Obligation to maintain secrecy of information obtained during investigation.

key_procedures: Receipt of complaint and preliminary investigation.
Issuance of search warrants and seizure of evidence.
Summoning witnesses and production of documents.
Submission of investigation reports to the Government.
Initiation of prosecution based on investigation findings.
administration: The Government of Kerala, through relevant departments and appointed authorities. The Commission itself also plays a significant administrative role.
important_notes: The Act draws powers and procedures from the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
The provisions of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, are applicable to investigations.
The Act aims to ensure that public men are held accountable for acts of corruption.

title: THE KERALA PUBLICMEN'S CORRUPTION (INVESTIGATIONS AND INQUIRIES) AMENDMENT ACT, 1989
purpose: To amend the Kerala Publicmen's Corruption (Investigations and Inquiries) Act, 1987, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.

title: THE KERALA PUBLIC SERVANTS (INQUIRIES) ACT, 1963
purpose: To amend and unify the law relating to public inquiries into the conduct of public servants in the service of the Government of Kerala.
scope: Applies to public servants in the service of the Government of Kerala.

key_definitions.public servant: Means a person appointed to any public service or post in connection with the affairs of the State of Kerala, but does not include a member of any Union Public Service or of any All India Service serving in connection with the affairs of the State of Kerala.
key_definitions.commissioner: References to commissioner shall, where more than one commissioner has been appointed, be construed as references to the commissioners.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Public Servants (Inquiries) Act, 1963 and that it shall come into force at once.
Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'public servant' and 'commissioner'.

main_sections.section_title: Articles of charge to be drawn up for public inquiry into the conduct of public servants.
main_sections.description: Government opinion on the nature of charges for public inquiry. When the Government is of opinion that a public servant has committed an act amounting to misconduct, it shall cause a charge to be drawn up and communicated to the public servant. The charge shall be stated in a way that the public servant can understand the substance of the allegations.

main_sections.section_title: Authority to whom inquiry may be committed. Notice to accused.
main_sections.description: The inquiry may be committed to the Court, Board or other authority to which the person accused is subordinate, or to the commissioner. Notice of the inquiry shall be given to the person accused at least fifteen days before the beginning of the inquiry.
Whenever the Government is of opinion that a prosecution shall be conducted, they shall nominate some person to conduct the same on their behalf.

main_sections.section_title: Charge by accuser to be written and verified. Institution of inquiry by Government.
main_sections.description: When a charge is brought by an accuser, the Government shall require the accusation to be written and verified on oath or solemn affirmation. The Government shall then decide whether to proceed with the inquiry.

main_sections.section_title: Security from accuser left by Government to prosecute.
main_sections.description: Where the Government is unable to prosecute, it may require the accuser to furnish security for the prosecution of the charges. The accuser will be responsible for the costs if the charges are malicious.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to abandon prosecution and to allow accuser to continue it.
main_sections.description: The Government has the power to abandon a prosecution and allow the accuser to continue it, provided that the accuser is able to show that they are doing so for malicious prosecution.

The commissioner shall have the same powers of punishing contempts and obstructions as are vested in Civil and Criminal Courts by the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898. They shall also have the same powers for the summoning of witnesses and for compelling the production of documents.

All persons disobeying any lawful process issued for the purposes of the commission shall be liable to the same penalties as if such process had been issued by the Court or other authority through whom it is executed.

main_sections.section_title: Copy of charge and list to be furnished to the accused.
main_sections.description: A copy of the articles of charges and the list of the documents and witnesses by which each charge is to be sustained, shall be delivered to the person accused at least seven days before the beginning of the inquiry, exclusive of the day of delivery and the first day of the inquiry.

main_sections.section_title: The accused to be permitted to inspect and take extracts from official records.
main_sections.description: The accused shall be permitted to inspect and take extracts from such official records, including documents produced by witnesses, as may specify their defence.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure at beginning of inquiry. Non-appearance of accused and admission of charge.
main_sections.description: Details the procedure at the beginning of an inquiry, including what happens if the accused does not appear or admits the charge.
Grants the prosecutor the right to address the commissioner.

main_sections.section_title: Evidence for prosecution and examination of witnesses.
main_sections.description: Outlines the process for presenting evidence for the prosecution and examining witnesses.

main_sections.section_title: Power to admit or call for new evidence for prosecution. Accused's right to adjournment.
main_sections.description: Details the power to admit new evidence and the accused's right to an adjournment.

main_sections.section_title: Defence of accused to be recorded only when written.
main_sections.description: Ensures that the defence of the accused is only recorded when it is presented in writing.

main_sections.section_title: Evidence for defence and examination of witnesses.
main_sections.description: Describes the procedure for presenting defence evidence and examining defence witnesses.

Specifies that notes of oral evidence shall be read to each witness by whom it was given and shall be signed by the witness in the presence of the Commissioner and shall be recorded with the proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Inquiry when closed with defence. Prosecution when entitled to reply and give evidence.
main_sections.description: Outlines the process when the inquiry is closed with the defence, and when the prosecution is entitled to reply or give evidence.

main_sections.section_title: Powers to require amendment of charge and to adjourn.
main_sections.description: Grants the Commissioner the power to amend charges and to adjourn the inquiry.
Requires the Commissioner to submit a report of the proceedings to the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to pass final orders.
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to pass final orders in inquiries, potentially after consulting the Public Service Commission.

main_sections.section_title: Saving of power of removal without inquiry under the Act.
main_sections.description: Saves the Government's power to remove a public servant without an inquiry under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to make rules.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.

Repeals The Public Servants (Inquiries) Act, 1850 (Central Act 37 of 1850) and the relevant section of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, as far as they relate to officers to whom the provisions of this Act apply.

important_rules: Rule: Charges for public inquiry into the conduct of public servants shall be drawn up and communicated to the public servant.
Rule: Notice of inquiry shall be given to the accused at least fifteen days before its commencement.
Rule: The accused shall be permitted to inspect and take extracts from official records relevant to their defence.
Rule: Oral evidence shall be read to the witness and signed in the presence of the Commissioner.
Rule: The Government may make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.

penalties: All persons disobeying any lawful process shall be liable to the same penalties as if such process had been issued by the Court or other authority through whom it is executed.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government and Commissioner
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inquiries, summoning of witnesses, production of documents, and issuance of lawful processes.

rights: Right of the accused to be informed of the charges.
Right of the accused to inspect and take extracts from official records for their defence.
Right of the accused to present their defence.
Right of the accused to an adjournment when new evidence is presented.
duties: Duty of the Government to draw up charges and conduct inquiries.
Duty of the Commissioner to conduct inquiries impartially.
Duty of witnesses to provide evidence when summoned.
obligations: Obligation of persons to obey lawful processes issued under the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure: Drawing up and serving of charges on the public servant.
Procedure: Conduct of inquiry by the Commissioner, including recording of evidence and examination of witnesses.
Procedure: Submission of a report by the Commissioner to the Government.
Procedure: Passing of final orders by the Government.
administration: The Government of Kerala (implied through the application of the Act to its public servants).
important_notes: The Act applies to public servants in the service of the Government of Kerala.
The Government has the power to abandon a prosecution.
The Government has the power to make rules.
The Act repeals previous legislation related to public servant inquiries.

title: The Kerala Public Services Act, 1968
purpose: To regulate the recruitment and conditions of service of persons appointed, to public services and posts in connection with the affairs of the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to persons appointed to public services and posts in connection with the affairs of the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Public Services Act, 1968.

main_sections.section_title: Regulation of recruitment and conditions of service
main_sections.description: The Government may make rules to regulate the recruitment, and conditions of service of persons appointed, to public services and posts in connection with the affairs of the State of Kerala. All rules made under this section shall be laid as soon as may be after it is made before the Legislative Assembly while it is in session for a total period of fourteen days which may be comprised in one session or in two successive sessions, and if before the expiry of the session in which it is so laid or the session immediately following, the Legislative Assembly agrees that the rule should be either modified or annulled, the rule shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect, as the case may be, so however that any such modification or annulment shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that rule.

All rules made under the proviso to Article 309 of the Constitution of India, regulating the recruitment and conditions of service of persons appointed, to public services and posts in connection with the affairs of the State of Kerala and in force immediately before the commencement of this Act, shall be deemed to have been made under this Act as if this Act had been in force on the date on which such rules were made and shall continue to be in force unless and until they are superseded by any rules made under this Act.

administration: State of Kerala
important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 225, dated 17th September, 1968.

title: The Kerala Public Service Commission (Additional Functions As Respects Certain Corporations And Companies) Act, 1970
purpose: To provide for the exercise of certain additional functions by the Kerala Public Service Commission as respects the services of certain Corporations and Companies.
scope: This Act applies to Corporations and Government Companies as defined in the Act, and the Kerala Public Service Commission, within the state of Kerala.

key_definitions.corporation: Includes the Kerala State Financial Corporation, the Kerala State Warehousing Corporation, the Kerala Khadi and Village Industries Board, the Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund Board, the Kerala Headload Workers' Welfare Board, the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Welfare Fund Board, and the Kerala Labour Welfare Fund Board.
key_definitions.government_company: A company where not less than fifty-one percent of paid-up share capital is held by the Government of Kerala, or partly by the Government of Kerala and partly by such a company, or a subsidiary of such a company.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act and states that it shall come into force at once.
This section defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Corporation', 'Government Company', and 'Public Service Commission'.

main_sections.section_title: Functions of the Public Service Commission in respect of services of certain Corporations and Companies
main_sections.description: This section outlines the additional functions of the Public Service Commission regarding the recruitment and appointment processes of specified Corporations and Government Companies. It details when these entities can consult the PSC and the PSC's duty to advise. It also provides for the resolution of differences of opinion.

This section grants the Government the power to make rules, in consultation with the PSC and the concerned entities, for carrying out the purposes of the Act. It specifies areas these rules may cover, including consultation procedures, and mandates laying rules before the Legislative Assembly for modification or annulment.

This section repeals the Kerala Public Service Commission (Additional Functions as respects certain Corporations and Companies) Ordinance, 1970, and saves anything done or deemed to have been done under the Ordinance as if it were done under this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala and the Kerala Public Service Commission are involved in the enforcement and administration of the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, including consultation mechanisms and the power to make rules.

rights: Corporations and Government Companies have the right to consult the Public Service Commission on recruitment and appointment matters.
duties: It is the duty of the Public Service Commission to advise Corporations and Government Companies when consulted.
obligations: Corporations and Government Companies are obliged to consult the PSC on specified recruitment matters.
The Government is obliged to consider the advice of the PSC when there is a difference of opinion, and refer matters back to the PSC before making a final decision against its advice.

key_procedures: Consultation Procedure: Corporations or Boards of Directors of Government Companies can consult the Public Service Commission on matters related to recruitment methods and appointment principles for direct recruitment. The PSC has a duty to advise on these matters.

Resolution of Differences: In case of disagreement between the PSC and a Corporation/Government Company, the matter is referred to the Government, whose decision is final. However, the Government must refer the matter back to the PSC if it intends to decide against the PSC's advice.

Rule Making Procedure: The Government, in consultation with the PSC and concerned entities, can make rules. These rules must be laid before the Legislative Assembly for a period of fourteen days in one or two successive sessions, during which the Assembly can modify or annul them.
administration: The Government of Kerala, in consultation with the Kerala Public Service Commission and the concerned Corporations/Boards of Directors.
important_notes: The definition of 'Corporation' has been expanded by subsequent amendments to include more welfare boards.
The definition of 'employee' in relation to Government Companies explicitly excludes directors and certain managerial positions.

title: THE KERALA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION (ADDITIONAL FUNCTIONS AS RESPECTS THE KERALA STATE ROAD TRANSPORT CORPORATION) ACT, 1970
purpose: To provide for the exercise of certain additional functions by the Kerala Public Service Commission as respects the services of the Kerala State Road Transport Corporation.
scope: Applies to the services of the Kerala State Road Transport Corporation.

key_definitions.Corporation: means the Kerala State Road Transport Corporation established under section 3 of the Road Transport Corporations Act, 1950 (Central Act 64 of 1950).
key_definitions.Public Service Commission: means the Kerala Public Service Commission.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Public Service Commission (Additional Functions as respects the Kerala State Road Transport Corporation) Act, 1970.
Defines 'Corporation' and 'Public Service Commission' in the context of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Functions of the Public Service Commission in respect of services under the Corporation.
main_sections.description: Outlines the Corporation's ability to consult the Public Service Commission on matters relating to recruitment of officers and servants, principles for appointments, and suitability of candidates. It also specifies that the Corporation must consult the Commission on matters under sub-section (1) and that any difference of opinion between the Commission and the Corporation must be referred to the Government for final decision. The Government's decision is final. The provided government is provided for, before taking a decision against the advice of the Public Service Commission, shall refer the matter to the Commission.

Grants the Government power to make rules, with prior consultation with the Public Service Commission, for carrying out the purposes of this Act. It also specifies that rules may provide for the procedure for consultation with the Public Service Commission and any matter incidental or necessary for the purpose of consultation.

Repeals the Kerala Public Service Commission (Additional Functions) Ordinance, 1969, and states that anything done or any action taken under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act, provided the Act has commenced on the 17th day of December, 1969.

important_rules: Rule: Every rule made under this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before the Legislative Assembly while it is in session for a total period of fourteen days which may be comprised in one session or in two successive sessions and, if before the expiry of the session in which it is so laid, or the session immediately following, the Legislative Assembly makes any modification in the rule or decides that the rule should not be made, the rule shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect, as the case may be; so however that any such modification or annulment shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that rule.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through rules made by the Government and decisions on differences of opinion between the Corporation and the Commission.

rights: The Corporation has the right to consult the Public Service Commission on recruitment and appointment matters.
duties: The Corporation has the duty to consult the Public Service Commission on matters related to recruitment and suitability of candidates for appointments.
obligations: The Corporation must refer any difference of opinion with the Public Service Commission to the Government for a final decision.

key_procedures: Consultation Procedure: When the Corporation needs to consult the Public Service Commission regarding recruitment, appointment principles, or suitability of candidates, it must follow the established procedures. Differences of opinion are resolved by referral to the Government.

Rule Making Procedure: The Government, after consulting the Public Service Commission, can make rules for the Act's implementation. These rules are subject to modification or annulment by the Legislative Assembly.
administration: The Government of Kerala is responsible for making rules under this Act and resolving disputes between the Corporation and the Public Service Commission.
important_notes: The Act was enacted in the Twentieth Year of the Republic of India.
The Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 37, dated 7th February, 1970.
The repeal of the Ordinance has a saving clause that actions taken under it are valid if the Act commenced on December 17, 1969.

title: THE KERALA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION (ADDITIONAL FUNCTIONS AS RESPECTS THE SERVICES UNDER LOCAL AUTHORITIES) AMENDMENT ACT, 1988
purpose: To amend the Kerala Public Service Commission (Additional Functions as Respects the Services under Local Authorities) Act, 1973.
scope: Applies to the services under Local Authorities in Kerala. Specifically amends Section 2 of Act, 1973.

key_definitions.local authorities: Includes the Kerala State Rural Development Board, the Trivandrum Town Planning Trust, the Calicut Town Planning Trust, and the Greater Cochin Development Authority, and any Town Planning Trust or development authority constituted under the Town Planning Act, 1920 (VII of 1920) or the Kerala State Rural Development Board Act, 1971 (15 of 1971).

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Public Service Commission (Additional Functions as Respects the Services under Local Authorities) Amendment Act, 1988. It shall come into force at once.

In clause (b) of section 2 of the Kerala Public Service Commission (Additional Functions as Respects the Services under Local Authorities) Act, 1973 (23 of 1973), for the words, figures and brackets, 'and includes the Kerala State Rural Development Board constituted under the Kerala State Rural Development Board Act, 1971, the Trivandrum Town Planning Trust constituted under the Trivandrum Town Planning Act, 1920 and the Greater Cochin Development Authority constituted under the Town Planning Act, 1920', the words, figures and brackets 'or a Town Planning Trust or a development authority constituted under the Town Planning Act (IV of 1910) or the Madras Town Planning Act, 1920 (VII of 1920) or under both and includes the Kerala State Rural Development Board constituted under the Kerala State Rural Development Board Act, 1971 (15 of 1971)' shall be substituted.

administration: Law (Legislation-C) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: This is an Amendment Act to the Kerala Public Service Commission (Additional Functions as Respects the Services under Local Authorities) Act, 1973.
The amendment specifically modifies the definition of 'local authorities' in Section 2 of the 1973 Act.

title: The Kerala Public Service Commission (Additional Functions as Respects the Kerala State Road Transport Corporation) Amendment Act, 1990
purpose: To amend the Kerala Public Service Commission (Additional Functions as respects the Kerala State Road Transport Corporation) Act, 1970, for purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: This Act applies to the Kerala Public Service Commission and the Kerala State Road Transport Corporation.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it shall come into force on the 9th day of February, 1970, and the remaining provisions of this Act shall come into force at once.
Inserts a new section 3A into the principal Act concerning the appointment of persons in Sports Quota.
Amends sub-section (2) of section 4 of the principal Act by inserting a new clause.

Provides for the validation of appointment by direct recruitment of persons proficient in sports and games made by the Corporation without consulting the Public Service Commission, subject to certain conditions.

important_rules: Appointments in Sports Quota shall not necessarily be subject to consultation with the Public Service Commission if certain conditions are met.

Appointments by direct recruitment of persons proficient in sports and games made by the Corporation, before the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette, shall be deemed to have been made in accordance with the provisions of section 3A of the principal Act and shall be valid for all purposes.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Kerala Public Service Commission and the Kerala State Road Transport Corporation
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the principal Act and this amending Act.

rights: The right to appoint persons in Sports Quota without necessarily consulting the Public Service Commission under specific circumstances.
duties: The duty to comply with the provisions of the amended Act.
The duty to ensure that appointments made are in accordance with the law.
obligations: Obligation to validate appointments made prior to the Act's enactment under specific conditions.

key_procedures: Procedure for appointing persons in Sports Quota as detailed in the inserted section 3A.
Procedure for validation of past appointments made by the Corporation.
administration: The Kerala Public Service Commission and the Kerala State Road Transport Corporation
important_notes: Appointments made under the new section 3A are notwithstanding anything contained in section 3.
The Act is deemed to have come into force on the 9th day of February, 1970, for certain provisions.
Appointments made under section 4 are validated even if made without consulting the Public Service Commission, provided they meet the criteria and are made before the publication of the Act.

title: THE KERALA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION (ADDITIONAL FUNCTIONS AS RESPECTS THE SERVICES UNDER THE KERALA ADMINISTRATIVE TRIBUNAL) ACT, 2017
purpose: To provide for the exercise of certain additional functions by the Kerala Public Service Commission as respects the services under the Kerala Administrative Tribunal.
scope: The act applies to the services under the Kerala Administrative Tribunal.

key_definitions.prescribed: means prescribed by rules made under this Act;
key_definitions.Public Service Commission: means the Kerala Public Service Commission;
key_definitions.services: means the services under the Kerala Administrative Tribunal;
key_definitions.Tribunal: means the Kerala Administrative Tribunal constituted under sub-section (2) of section 4 of the Administrative Tribunal Act, 1985 (Central Act 13 of 1985).

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Public Service Commission (Additional Functions as respects the services under the Kerala Administrative Tribunal) Act, 2017, and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Defines terms used in the Act, including 'prescribed', 'Public Service Commission', 'services', and 'Tribunal'.

main_sections.section_title: Functions of the Public Service Commission in respect of services under the Tribunal.
main_sections.description: Outlines the functions of the Public Service Commission regarding the recruitment and conditions of service of officers and employees of the Tribunal. It specifies the duty of the Public Service Commission to prepare a select list for appointment by direct recruitment and the requirement for the Tribunal to consult the Public Service Commission on matters relating to direct recruitment and making appointments. It also details the duty of the Public Service Commission to advise the Government on any matter as per sub-section (2), with provisions for consultation even when the Government makes rules.

Empowers the Government to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act, including rules for the preparation of select lists, consultation with the Public Service Commission, and other incidental matters.

Repeals the Kerala Public Service Commission (Additional Functions as respects the services under the Kerala Administrative Tribunal) Ordinance, 2017, and provides savings for actions taken under the repealed ordinance.
References the Ordinance that this Act supersedes.

important_rules: The Public Service Commission has the duty to prepare a select list for direct recruitment of officers and employees of the Tribunal.
The Tribunal must consult the Public Service Commission on matters relating to direct recruitment and appointment of its officers and employees.
The Public Service Commission shall advise the Government on any matter relating to the services under the Tribunal, as specified in sub-section (2) of section 3.
