rights: Right of the Government to authorize publication in the Gazette.
duties: Duty of the Public Service Commission to prepare select list for direct recruitment.
Duty of the Tribunal to consult the Public Service Commission.
obligations: Obligation of the Government to notify the commencement of the Act in the Gazette.

key_procedures: Preparation of a select list by the Public Service Commission for direct recruitment of officers and employees of the Tribunal.
Consultation process between the Tribunal and the Public Service Commission for recruitment and appointments.
Government making rules to carry out the provisions of the Act, which may include matters like preparation of select lists and consultation procedures.
administration: Government of Kerala, Law (Legislation-B) Department
important_notes: The Act is a translation in English language of the original Malayalam text.
The Act repeals the Kerala Public Service Commission (Additional Functions as respects the services under the Kerala Administrative Tribunal) Ordinance, 2017.
Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are saved.

title: The Kerala Public Service Commission (Additional Functions As Respects The Library Councils) Act, 2014
purpose: To provide for the exercise of certain additional functions by the Kerala Public Service Commission as respects the services under the Library Councils.
scope: Applies to services under the Library Councils in Kerala.

key_definitions.Library Councils: The Kerala State Library Council, the District Library Councils and the Taluk Library Councils constituted under section 3, section 10 and section 18, respectively, of the Kerala Public Libraries (Kerala Granthasala Sanghom) Act, 1989 (15 of 1989).
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act
key_definitions.services: The services under the Library Councils

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Public Service Commission (Additional Functions as Respects the Library Councils) Act, 2014. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 20th day of July, 2014.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including Government, Library Councils, prescribed, Public Service Commission, and services.

main_sections.section_title: Functions of the Public Service Commission
main_sections.description: Outlines the functions of the Public Service Commission concerning Library Councils, including consultation on recruitment matters and principles for appointments. It also details procedures for resolving differences of opinion between the Commission and the Library Councils, and the role of the Government in such cases.

Grants the Government the power to make rules, in consultation with the Public Service Commission and the Kerala State Library Council, for carrying out the purposes of the Act. These rules can include matters related to the procedure for the Kerala State Library Council's consultation with the Public Service Commission and any incidental or necessary matters.
Repeals the Kerala Public Service Commission (Additional Functions as Respects the Library Councils) Ordinance, 2014 (19 of 2014) and saves any act or action taken under that Ordinance.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Kerala State Library Council shall consult the Public Service Commission on all matters relating to the method of recruitment of officers and employees of the Library Councils.

Rule 2: The Kerala State Library Council shall consult the Public Service Commission on the principles to be followed in making appointments by direct recruitment to the posts under the Library Councils and the suitability of candidates for such appointments.

Rule 3: In case of any difference of opinion between the Public Service Commission and the Kerala State Library Council on a matter under sub-section (1), the Kerala State Library Council shall refer the matter to the Government and the decision of the Government thereon shall be final.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through rules made by the Government and decisions taken by the Government in case of disputes.

rights: Right of the Government to make rules.
duties: Duty of the Kerala State Library Council to consult the Public Service Commission on recruitment and appointment matters.
Duty of the Public Service Commission to provide advice on matters related to Library Councils.
obligations: Obligation to follow the decision of the Government in case of differences of opinion.

key_procedures: Consultation Procedure: The Kerala State Library Council must consult the Public Service Commission on recruitment methods and appointment principles.
Dispute Resolution Procedure: If there's a difference of opinion, the matter is referred to the Government, whose decision is final.
administration: Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on July 20, 2014.
The Kerala Public Service Commission (Additional Functions as Respects the Library Councils) Ordinance, 2014 is repealed.

title: The Kerala Public Service Commission(Additional Functions As Respects the Lok Ayukta) Act, 2014
purpose: An Act to provide for the exercise of certain additional functions by the Kerala Public Service Commission as respects the services of the Lok Ayukta.
scope: Applies to the exercise of functions by the Kerala Public Service Commission with respect to the services of the Lok Ayukta.

key_definitions.Lok Ayukta: means the Lok Ayukta appointed under section 3 of the Kerala Lok Ayukta Act, 1999 (8 of 1999) and includes the Upa-Lok Ayukta appointed under the said section.
key_definitions.Public Service Commission: means the Kerala Public Service Commission.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Public Service Commission (Additional Functions As Respects the Lok Ayukta) Act, 2014, and it shall come into force at once.
Defines 'Lok Ayukta' and 'Public Service Commission'.

main_sections.section_title: Functions of the Public Service Commission in respect of services under the Lok Ayukta
main_sections.description: Outlines the functions of the Public Service Commission regarding services under the Lok Ayukta, including consultation with the Lok Ayukta on matters relating to direct recruitment to posts and on principles for making appointments. It also states the duty of the Public Service Commission to prepare select lists, by appointment by direct recruitment, of officers and employees of the Lok Ayukta. It mandates the Lok Ayukta to consult the Public Service Commission on matters relating to direct recruitment and on appointment principles. It also specifies that if there is any difference of opinion between the Public Service Commission and the Lok Ayukta, the matter shall be referred to the Government whose decision shall be final. It also mentions the power of the Government to make rules specifying matters in which the Public Service Commission need not be consulted.

Grants the Government the power to make rules, in consultation with the Public Service Commission and the Lok Ayukta, by notification in the Gazette, for carrying out the purposes of the Act. Specifically, it allows for rules regarding the procedure to be followed by the Lok Ayukta for consultation with the Public Service Commission, and any matter incidental or necessary for the purpose of consultation. It also states that every rule made under this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before the Legislative Assembly, and any modification or annulment shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that rule.

duties: It shall be the duty of the Public Service Commission to prepare select list, for appointment by direct recruitment, of officers and employees of the Lok Ayukta.

key_procedures: When there is a difference of opinion between the Public Service Commission and the Lok Ayukta, the matter must be referred to the Government for a final decision.
Rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act can be made by the Government in consultation with the Public Service Commission and the Lok Ayukta.
Rules made under the Act must be laid before the Legislative Assembly for modification or annulment.
administration: Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act is an addition to the existing functions of the Kerala Public Service Commission concerning the Lok Ayukta.
The Government can make rules to specify circumstances where consultation with the Public Service Commission is not necessary.
Rules made under the Act are subject to the scrutiny of the Legislative Assembly.

title: THE KERALA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION (ADDITIONAL FUNCTIONS AS RESPECTS THE ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES UNDER DEVASWOM BOARDS) ACT, 2008
purpose: To provide for the exercise of certain additional functions by the Kerala Public Service Commission as respects the appointments of officers and servants in the Administrative Services under certain Devaswom Boards in the State of Kerala and their conditions of service.
scope: Applies to the Administrative Services under certain Devaswom Boards in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Devaswom Board: Means the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950 (XV of 1950) or the Cochin Devaswom Board referred to in clause (1) of section 61 of the said Act.
key_definitions.Public Service Commission: Means the Kerala Public Service Commission.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Public Service Commission (Additional Functions as Respects the Administrative Services under Devaswom Boards) Act, 2008. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Defines "Devaswom Board" and "Public Service Commission" for the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Functions of the Public Service Commission in respect of Administrative Services under Devaswom Boards
main_sections.description: Outlines the functions of the Public Service Commission regarding recruitment, preparation of select lists, and consultation for appointments to Administrative Services under Devaswom Boards. It also specifies that the Government may make rules for classifying matters for the purpose of consultation.

Empowers the Government, in consultation with the Public Service Commission and the Devaswom Boards, to make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act. These rules may include procedures for consultation and other incidental or necessary matters. Rules made under this Act must be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Government by notification in the Gazette.
Rule 2: Devaswom Boards shall consult the Public Service Commission regarding matters relating to direct recruitment to the posts under the Administrative Services of the Devaswom Board.

Rule 3: The Government may make rules specifying the matters in which, either generally, or in any particular case or class of cases or in any particular circumstances, it shall not be necessary for the Public Service Commission to be consulted.

duties: Duty of the Public Service Commission to prepare select list of candidates belonging to Hindu Religion for appointment by direct recruitment.
Duty of the Devaswom Board to consult the Public Service Commission regarding matters relating to direct recruitment to posts under the Administrative Services of the Devaswom Board.
Duty of the Public Service Commission to advise on any matter referred to them by the Government regarding administrative services of Devaswom Boards.

key_procedures: Procedure: The Government, in consultation with the Public Service Commission and the Devaswom Boards, may make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act. These rules shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly.
administration: Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 11th March 2008 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 1190 dated 12th March 2008.

Rules made under this Act shall have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect as the case may be, however, that any such modification or annulment shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that rule.

The Devaswom Board shall refer to the Government and the decision of the Government thereon shall be final in case of any difference of opinion between Public Service Commission and the Devaswom Board on any matter.

title: The Kerala Public Service Commission(Additional Functions as Respects the Services under the Universities) Act, 2015
purpose: To provide for the exercise of certain additional functions by the Kerala Public Service Commission as respects the services under the Universities.
scope: This Act applies to the services under the Universities in Kerala.

key_definitions.university: Refers to various Kerala Universities established under specific acts, including Kerala Agricultural University, University of Kerala, University of Calicut, Mahatma Gandhi University, Cochin University of Science and Technology, Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit, Kannur University, National University of Advanced Legal Studies, Kerala Veterinary and Animal Sciences University, Kerala University of Health Sciences, Kerala University of Fisheries and Ocean Studies, Thunchath Ezhuthachan Malayalam University, and A. P. J. Abdul Kalam Technological University.

main_sections.description: (1) This Act may be called the Kerala Public Service Commission (Additional Functions as Respects the Services under the Universities) Act, 2015. (2) It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 29th day of September, 2015.
Defines terms used in the Act, primarily 'University' referring to several specified universities in Kerala.

administration: Law (Legislation-G) Department, Government of Kerala

title: THE KERALA PUBLIC SERVICES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1983
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala Public Services Act, 1968.
scope: Applies to all public service matters covered by the Kerala Public Services Act, 1968.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Public Services (Amendment) Act, 1983. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of October, 1981.

Inserts a new section 4 into the Kerala Public Services Act, 1968, stating that notwithstanding anything contained in Chapter VI A or in any other law, nothing in the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, or in any other law for the time being in force, or in any judgment, decree or order of any court, the appointment of any person to any public service or post in connection with the affairs of the State of Kerala and the conditions of service (including termination of service) of any person appointed to any such service or post shall be governed by the provisions of this Act and the rules made or deemed to have been made thereunder.

Repeals the Kerala Public Services (Amendment) Ordinance, 1983 (36 of 1983). It also states that notwithstanding such repeal, any action taken or deemed to have been taken or done or deemed to have been done under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been taken or done under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned, likely through existing Public Service Commission and departmental authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through administrative actions and legal interpretation of the Act and associated rules.

administration: Likely administered by the General Administration Department of the Kerala State Government and overseen by the Kerala Public Service Commission.
important_notes: Received the assent of the President on the 5th day of January, 1984.
Published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 26 dated the 7th January 1984.

title: The Kerala Public Services (Amendment) Act, 1970
purpose: To amend the Kerala Public Services Act, 1968, specifically to allow for retrospective application of rules.
scope: This Act applies to the public services governed by the Kerala Public Services Act, 1968, within the state of Kerala. It specifically amends provisions related to rule-making powers concerning these services.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Kerala Public Services (Amendment) Act, 1970' and states that it is deemed to have come into force on September 17, 1968.

Amends sub-section (1) of section 2 of the principal Act (The Kerala Public Services Act, 1968) by inserting the words 'either prospectively or retrospectively' after 'The Government may make rules', thereby allowing rules to be made with retrospective effect.

Repeals the Kerala Public Services (Amendment) Ordinance, 1969 (6 of 1969). It also saves any rules made under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance, deeming them to have been issued under the Act as amended by this new Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Kerala State Government or its designated authorities under the principal Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application of rules made under the Kerala Public Services Act, 1968, as amended by this Act.

key_procedures: Amendment of Section 2(1) of the principal Act: Insertion of 'either prospectively or retrospectively' after 'The Government may make rules'.
administration: The Department of Personnel and Administrative Reforms, Government of Kerala, likely administers the principal Act and its amendments.
important_notes: The Act has retrospective effect from September 17, 1968.
The repeal of the Kerala Public Services (Amendment) Ordinance, 1969, does not invalidate rules made under it, as they are deemed to be issued under the amended principal Act.

title: THE KERALA PUBLIC SERVICES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1979
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Public Services Act, 1968.
scope: Applies to Kerala Public Services.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Public Services (Amendment) Act, 1979. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 3rd day of July, 1979.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 1.
main_sections.description: For section 1 of the Kerala Public Services Act, 1968 (19 of 1968) (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), the following section shall be, and shall be deemed always to have been, substituted, namely:— "(1) Short title and commencement.—(1) This Act may be called the Kerala Public Services Act, 1968. (2) Section 3 shall come into force on the 17th day of September, 1968 and the remaining provisions of this Act shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of November, 1956."

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 3.
main_sections.description: For section 3 of the principal Act, the following section shall be substituted, namely:— "(3) Continuance of existing rules.—All rules made under the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution of India, regulating the recruitment, and conditions of service of persons appointed, to public services and posts in connection with the affairs of the State of Kerala and in force immediately before the 17th September, 1968, shall be deemed to have been made under this Act and shall continue to be in force unless and until they are superseded by rules made under this Act."

(1) The Kerala Public Services (Amendment) Ordinance, 1979 (4 of 1979), is hereby repealed. (2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 13th October 1979 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 759, dated 23rd October, 1979.

title: THE KERALA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION (ADDITIONAL FUNCTIONS AS RESPECTS CERTAIN CORPORATIONS AND COMPANIES) AMENDMENT ACT, 1988
purpose: To amend the Kerala Public Service Commission (Additional Functions as Respects Certain Corporations and Companies) Act, 1970.
scope: The Act applies to the Kerala Public Service Commission and its functions concerning certain corporations and companies.

key_definitions.Government Company: means (i) a company in which not less than fifty-one per cent of the paid up share capital is held by the Government of Kerala; and (ii) a company so defined, in which not less than fifty-one per cent of the paid up share capital is held partly by the Government of Kerala and partly by a company mentioned in sub-clause (i); or (iii) a company which is a subsidiary within the meaning of section 4 of the said Act of a company mentioned in sub-clause (i).

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Public Service Commission (Additional Functions as Respects Certain Corporations and Companies) Amendment Act, 1988. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

Amends Section 2 of the Kerala Public Service Commission (Additional Functions as Respects Certain Corporations and Companies) Act, 1970. It substitutes figures and brackets 'or the 'Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund Board constituted under section 6 of the Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 1969 (20 of 1969), or the Kerala Headload Workers' Welfare Board established under section 4 of the Kerala Headload Workers' Act, 1978 (20 of 1980), or the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Welfare Fund Board constituted under section 6 of the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 1985 (21 of 1985) or the Kerala Labour Welfare Fund Board established under section 4 of the Kerala Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1975 (11 of 1977)' shall be inserted at the end. It also amends clause (b) to define 'Government Company'.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government of Kerala, Law (Legislation-A) Department
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legislative amendments and government notifications.

key_procedures: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Government through a Gazette notification.
administration: Government of Kerala, Law (Legislation-A) Department
important_notes: The notification pertains to the publication of the Bill passed by the Legislative Assembly and received the assent of the Governor.

title: The Kerala Public Ways (Restriction of Assemblies and Processions) Act, 2011
purpose: To provide for the protection of public ways for unobstructed movement by the public and for imposition of reasonable restrictions on the rights of any section of the public to assemble and collectively move thereon and to regulate procession through public ways and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the whole of the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.carriage way: the portion of the public way which is intended for the movement of vehicles or carriages of any type.
key_definitions.footpath: any area comprised in a public way carmarked for movement of pedestrian having a width of not less than one meter but not exceeding three meters on either side of the public way, after leaving sufficient space for the movement of vehicles.
key_definitions.public way: includes any highway, bridge, causeway, road, lane, footpath, square, courtyard, garden-path, channel or passage accessible to the public, which is not owned by a private person.
key_definitions.road-margin: the portion of the public way which extends outwards on each side from the footpath towards the outer edge of the public way.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Public Ways (Restriction of Assemblies and Processions) Act, 2011. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. It shall come into force at once.
Defines terms such as 'carriage way', 'footpath', 'licence', 'public way', and 'road-margin'.

main_sections.section_title: Rights of the public for movement on public ways
main_sections.description: States that all public ways shall have, subject to the laws governing the control of traffic and safety of public, the right to unobstructed movement by vehicles along carriageways and on foot along footpaths.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of obstruction on public ways
main_sections.description: No person shall cause any obstruction by conducting any business or meeting or assembly or procession or demonstration on any public way or part thereof. No meeting or assembly shall be conducted so as to obstruct any portion of the carriageway or footpath. No demonstration or procession shall be conducted in such a manner that the entire carriageway or free flow of traffic is fully obstructed.

main_sections.section_title: Regulation of conduct of festivals, assemblies, meetings etc.
main_sections.description: District Police Chief may impose reasonable restrictions on the right of unobstructed movement on public ways for a period not exceeding twenty-four hours in any particular area, in all or any of the following instances, namely (a) for the conduct of religious or national festivals, which are customary and have been established by tradition and for the conduct of such festivals of social, cultural or public importance which are declared to be so by the District Magistrate, (b) for security of the State or individuals which, in the opinion of the District Police Chief, necessitate such restrictions, (c) for the conduct of public assemblies or meetings, and (d) for the conduct of public demonstrations and processions. The District Police Chief shall issue a licence to the person, association, organization, trust or body which has applied for use of the public way, imposing such conditions in the licence, as he may deem just and reasonable. The District Police Chief shall not permit any erection of any structure either of a permanent or temporary nature on any public way unless it is allowed in writing by the appropriate authority of the department in charge of the upkeep and maintenance of the particular public way.

Any person who causes any obstruction on any public way otherwise than permitted under a licence issued under this Act or any person who abets or involves in such activity or any person who carries on any activity in violation of the conditions of a licence shall, on conviction, be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year and with fine proportionate to damage and inconvenience caused by such obstruction or with both. All offences under this Act shall be cognizable and bailable. An offence under this Act shall be compoundable by a Judicial Magistrate having jurisdiction to try the offence.

Nothing in this Act shall apply to a funeral procession or any action undertaken by the public or any member or group thereof in good faith to prevent danger arising from any natural or man-made calamity, disaster or accident.

The District Police Chief may, with the approval of the Government, delegate any of his powers under this Act to an officer not below the rank of Sub-Divisional Police Officer within his jurisdiction.

The Government may, by notification in the gazette make rules not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act to carry out the purposes of this Act. Every rule made under this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be, after it is made, before the Legislative Assembly while it is in session for a total period of fourteen days which may fall in one session or in two successive sessions and if before the expiry of the session in which it is so laid or the session immediately following, the Legislative Assembly makes any modification in the rule or decides that the rule should not be made, the rule shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect, as the case may be, so however, any such modification or annulment shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that rule.

If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, Government may by order do anything not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act which appears to them necessary for the purpose of removing the difficulty. Provided that no such order shall be made after the expiration of two years from the date of commencement of this Act. Every order made under sub-section (1) shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is issued, before the Legislative Assembly.

important_rules: No person shall cause any obstruction on any public way by conducting any business or meeting or assembly or procession or demonstration. (Section 4(1))
No meeting or assembly shall be conducted so as to obstruct any portion of the carriageway or footpath. (Section 4(2))
No demonstration or procession shall be conducted in such a manner that the entire carriageway or free flow of traffic is fully obstructed. (Section 4(3))

Restrictions on public ways for festivals, assemblies, meetings, security of the State, public assemblies or meetings, and public demonstrations and processions can be imposed by the District Police Chief. (Section 5(1))
Licences are required for the conduct of public assemblies or meetings and public demonstrations and processions. (Section 5(1)(d))
No structure shall be permitted on a public way unless allowed by the appropriate authority. (Section 5(5))
Obstruction on public ways is punishable with imprisonment up to one year and fine. (Section 6(1))
Offences under this Act are cognizable and bailable. (Section 6(2))
Offences under this Act are compoundable by a Judicial Magistrate. (Section 6(3))
The Act does not apply to funeral processions or actions taken in good faith to prevent danger from calamities. (Section 7)
Rules made under the Act must be laid before the Legislative Assembly. (Section 9(3))
Government can issue orders to remove difficulties within two years of commencement. (Section 10)

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year and fine proportionate to damage and inconvenience caused by such obstruction or with both. (Section 6(1))
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: District Police Chief, Judicial Magistrate.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Licensing, imposing restrictions, prosecution for offences, compounding of offences.

rights: Right to unobstructed movement by vehicles along carriageways and on foot along footpaths, subject to laws governing traffic and public safety. (Section 3)
duties: Duty to not cause obstruction on public ways by conducting business, meetings, assemblies, processions, or demonstrations. (Section 4(1))
Duty to not conduct meetings or assemblies in a manner that obstructs carriageways or footpaths. (Section 4(2))
Duty to not conduct demonstrations or processions in a manner that fully obstructs the carriageway or free flow of traffic. (Section 4(3))
Duty to obtain a licence for conducting public assemblies, meetings, demonstrations, or processions. (Section 5(1)(d))

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining a licence for public assemblies, meetings, demonstrations, or processions: Application to the District Police Chief, who may impose conditions. (Section 5(1)(d) and 5(5))
Procedure for imposing restrictions by the District Police Chief: Based on specific grounds like festivals, security, public assemblies, or processions. (Section 5(1))
Procedure for making rules by the Government: Notification in the gazette, subject to modification or annulment by the Legislative Assembly. (Section 9)
Procedure for removing difficulties: Government can issue orders within two years of commencement, subject to legislative approval. (Section 10)
administration: Government of Kerala, Law (Legislation-E) Department.
important_notes: The Act came into force on February 18, 2011. (Inferred from Gazette notification date)
The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.
The Act does not apply to funeral processions or actions taken in good faith to prevent danger from calamities. (Section 7)
The Legislative Assembly has the power to modify or annul rules made under the Act. (Section 9(3))
The Government has the power to remove difficulties within two years of the Act's commencement. (Section 10(1))

title: The Kerala Public Libraries (Kerala Grandhasala Sanghom) Act, 1989
purpose: To provide for the establishment and development of public libraries in the State of Kerala and for the constitution and functions of the Kerala Grandhasala Sanghom and its subordinate bodies for this purpose.
scope: The Act applies to public libraries in the State of Kerala and the organizations responsible for their management and development, including the Kerala Grandhasala Sanghom, District Library Councils, and Taluk Library Unions.

key_definitions.library: Any library established or maintained by the State Library Council or a District Library Council or a Taluk Library Union.
key_definitions.State Library Council: The body constituted under the Act for the overall supervision and development of library services in the State.
key_definitions.District Library Council: A council established for each district to oversee library services within that district.
key_definitions.Taluk Library Union: A union established for each taluk to manage library services within that taluk.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and duties of President and Vice-President of the Taluk Library Union
main_sections.description: Outlines the powers and duties of the President and Vice-President of a Taluk Library Union, including presiding over meetings and exercising powers as prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Secretary of the Taluk Library Union
main_sections.description: Defines the Secretary of the Taluk Library Union as the chief executive authority, detailing their duties to give effect to resolutions of the Union, exercise powers conferred by the President or Union, and manage the Union's affairs.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and Functions of Taluk Library Unions
main_sections.description: Specifies the powers and functions of Taluk Library Unions, including electing members to District Library Council, supervising and controlling library services, providing library service including mobile services, developing suitable lands and buildings, providing necessary equipment and conveniences, providing books, periodicals, films, etc., conducting lectures and seminars, accepting endowments, and appointing staff.
Addresses disqualification from being a member of a Council or Union and the process for affiliation of libraries.

main_sections.section_title: Disqualification of members of State Library Council, District Library Council and Taluk Library Union
main_sections.description: Details the conditions under which a person can be disqualified from being a member of these bodies, including absence from meetings, holding office by virtue of which they were elected, criminal convictions, unsound mind, and being declared so by a competent court.

Governs the affiliation of libraries to the State Library Council, District Library Council, or Taluk Library Union, requiring recommendation from the District Library Council and the State Library Council.

Mandates the preparation and implementation of a District Library Development Plan by the District Library Council to improve library services within the district. The Government may sanction or modify these plans.

main_sections.section_title: Government grant to the State Library Council
main_sections.description: States that the Government shall make every year a grant to the State Library Council, not less than one per cent of the total allocated for education in the State budget, for the purpose of programmes and projects of the Council.

Establishes the State Library Fund, to which all expenses of the State Library Council, District Library Councils and Taluk Library Unions shall be charged. The fund comprises grants from the Government or Central Government, contributions, gifts, Provident Fund, Superannuation Fund, and cess collected under section 48.

main_sections.section_title: Distribution of funds to the District Library Councils and Taluk Library Unions
main_sections.description: Outlines the distribution of funds by the State Library Council to District Library Councils and Taluk Library Unions, with amounts to be determined as may be required.

Requires the State Library Council and every District Library Council and Taluk Library Union to keep complete accounts of their financial transactions in the prescribed form. Accounts are subject to audit, disallowance, and surcharge.

Empowers the President of the State Library Council to inspect any library under its jurisdiction and delegate this power. Detailed reports of inspections are to be furnished to the concerned Council and District Library Council.

Provides for affiliated libraries to receive grants from the Taluk Library Union based on graduation lists, as may be prescribed. The State Library Council shall provide necessary funds to Taluk Library Unions for this purpose.

main_sections.section_title: District Library Councils and Taluk Library Unions to submit reports etc.
main_sections.description: Mandates District Library Councils and Taluk Library Unions to submit reports and furnish information to the State Library Council or any authorized person, as required.

Requires the President of the State Library Council to prepare an annual report on the working of the Council, including information and particulars as may be prescribed, and submit it to the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Merger of the Kerala Grandhasala Sanghom and transfer of its assets and liabilities
main_sections.description: Deals with the merger of the Kerala Grandhasala Sanghom and the transfer of its assets and liabilities to the State Library Council, with effect from a specified date. Provisions are made for the employment and terms of service of existing officers and employees.

main_sections.section_title: Board of control to remain in office for certain period
main_sections.description: States that the Board of Control of the Kerala Grandhasala Sanghom shall continue to function for a specified period until the constitution of the State Library Council, District Library Councils, and Taluk Library Unions.

Empowers the Government to make rules, either prospectively or retrospectively, for various matters including the constitution of members, administration, inspection, and maintenance of libraries, grading of libraries, grants, and standards.

important_rules: Taluk Library Unions shall transact business by resolutions passed in such manner and in accordance with such procedure as may be prescribed.
Copy of every resolution shall be forwarded to the District Library Council within fifteen days of its passing.
No person shall be a member of more than one Council or Union, with provisions for the expiration of membership upon election to a higher body or after the last election.

A person shall be disqualified from being chosen as a member of the State Library Council, District Library Council, or Taluk Library Union if they have been absent from meetings for three consecutive meetings without leave.
Affiliated libraries shall be entitled to receive grant from the Taluk Library Union based on the graduation list prepared under sub-section (5) of section 34, at such rates as may be prescribed.
The Government shall sanction or modify District Library Development Plans.
The Government shall make an annual grant to the State Library Council.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Library Council, District Library Councils, Taluk Library Unions, and the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, rules made thereunder, prescribed procedures, and inspection mechanisms. Penalties for specific contraventions are not detailed in the provided pages, but the Act generally provides for enforcement through its various sections.

rights: Right to receive library service including mobile library service for persons residing in the taluk.
Right to affiliation of libraries to the State Library Council, District Library Council, or Taluk Library Union.
Right to receive grants for affiliated libraries.
Right to have the State Library Council manage and develop library services.
duties: Duty of the Secretary of the Taluk Library Union to give effect to the resolutions of the said Union.
Duty of the Secretary of the Taluk Library Union to exercise other powers and perform such other duties as are, or may be, conferred or imposed by the President or the Taluk Library Union.
Duty to prepare and implement District Library Development Plans.
Duty to maintain accounts and submit them for audit.
Duty to submit reports and furnish information as required.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder.
Obligation to adhere to the terms and conditions of affiliation for libraries.
Obligation for the Government to make annual grants to the State Library Council.

key_procedures: Procedure for transaction of business by Taluk Library Unions through resolutions.
Procedure for forwarding resolutions to the District Library Council.
Procedure for affiliation of libraries, involving recommendations from the District Library Council and approval by the State Library Council.
Procedure for the preparation, submission, and sanction of District Library Development Plans.
Procedure for the preparation and audit of accounts by the State Library Council and its subordinate bodies.
Procedure for the inspection of libraries by the President of the State Library Council or their delegate.
Procedure for the distribution of funds to District Library Councils and Taluk Library Unions.
Procedure for the submission of annual reports by the State Library Council to the Government.
administration: The State Library Council is the primary administrative body, with District Library Councils and Taluk Library Unions functioning under its purview. The Government also plays a significant role in funding and rule-making.
important_notes: The provisions relating to the merger of the Kerala Grandhasala Sanghom are to be given effect to as if they were provisions of an Act for the time being in force.
The Government may, after previous publication, make rules either prospectively or retrospectively for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
The Government may, on application by the District Library Council, modify any District Library Development Plan sanctioned under sub-section (3) of section 29.

title: THE KERALA PUBLIC MEN (PREVENTION OF CORRUPTION) ACT, 1983
purpose: To provide for the establishment of an authority to investigate allegations of corruption against public men and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to public men in Kerala.

key_definitions.Chief Justice: Means the Chief Justice of the High Court of Kerala.
key_definitions.Commission: Means a Commission constituted under section 4.
key_definitions.Commissioner: Means a member of the Commission.
key_definitions.Legislative Assembly: Means the Legislative Assembly of the State of Kerala.
key_definitions.Local authority: Means a municipal corporation or a municipal council or a township committee or a panchayat.
key_definitions.political party: Means a political party or group which has representation in Parliament or in the Legislative Assembly, or a political party which is treated as a recognised political party in accordance with paragraph 6 of Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.public man: Means a person who holds or has held office in the State or the office of: (i) a Minister or the Chief Minister, or (ii) a member of the Legislative Assembly, or (iii) a member or the President of the Travancore Devaswom Board or the Cochin Devaswom Board or a member or the Chairman of the Guruvayoor Devaswom Managing Committee or a member or the Chairman of the Kerala Wakf Board, or (iv) the Chairman or the Vice-Chairman (by whatever name called) of: (A) a local authority, or (B) a Government Company as defined in section 617 of the Companies Act, 1956 (Central Act 1 of 1956), or (C) a statutory body or Corporation or Board established by or under a statute and owned or controlled by the Government of Kerala, including a co-operative society; or (D) any other Corporation or Board or Society owned or controlled by the Government of Kerala.
key_definitions.registered trade union: Means a trade union registered under the Trade Unions Act, 1926 (Central Act 16 of 1926).
key_definitions.public servant: Means public servant as defined in section 21 of the Indian Penal Code (Central Act 45 of 1860).
key_definitions.trade union: Means a trade union as defined in the Trade Unions Act, 1926 (Central Act 16 of 1926).

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Public Men (Prevention of Corruption) Act, 1983. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and comes into force on such date as the Government may by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Chief Justice', 'Commission', 'Commissioner', 'Governor', 'Legislative Assembly', 'Local authority', 'political party', 'prescribed', 'public man', 'registered trade union', 'public servant', 'State', and 'trade union'.

Defines corruption as accepting or obtaining any gratification for oneself or for any other person, any gratification whatsoever, other than legal remuneration, as a motive or reward for doing or forbearing to do any official act, or for showing or for bearing to show favour or disfavour to any person in the exercise of his official functions, or for corruptly or illegally abusing his position as a public man or for any other valuable thing of pecuniary advantage. It also includes abetting or otherwise abusing his position as a public man for personal gain or for the time being in force, said to commit corruption.

The Governor shall constitute a Commission consisting of three members to deal effectively with allegations of corruption against public men. The Governor shall, in consultation with the Chief Minister of the State and the Chief Justice, appoint the members. Two of the persons appointed shall be sitting or retired Judges of the Supreme Court or of the High Court, and the other member shall be a person who is not an officer below the rank of Secretary to Government. The Governor, in consultation with the Chief Justice, shall appoint one of the Judicial Members to be the Chairman of the Commission. Matters to be decided by the Commission shall be decided in accordance with the opinion of the majority of the Commissioners. No member of Parliament or of the Legislature of any State and shall not hold any office of trust or profit (other than the office as Commissioner), or be connected with any organisation the activities of which are likely to result in communal disharmony or hatred or carry on any business, or practice any profession and accordingly before entering upon his office, a person appointed as Commissioner shall resign such membership, if he holds any office of trust or profit, resign from such office; if he is carrying on any business, sever his connection with (short of divesting himself of ownership) with the conduct and management of such business; or if he is practising any profession, cease to practice such profession. A person who has been a member of a political party at any time during the period of five years immediately preceding his appointment shall not be eligible to be appointed as Commissioner. The conditions of service of a Commissioner shall be as prescribed by the Governor. A Commissioner shall not be removed from his office except by an order of the Governor passed after an address by the Legislative Assembly supported by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the total membership of the House and by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members of the Legislative Assembly present and voting has been presented to the Governor in the same session for such removal on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity. The procedure for the presentation of an address and for the investigation and proof of the misbehaviour or incapacity of a Commissioner shall be prescribed by the Governor by an order of the Governor and approved by the Legislative Assembly. A Commissioner shall have the like status, shall be entitled to the same salary, allowances and pension and shall be subject to the same conditions of service, as a Judge of the High Court of Kerala. Provided that the salary, allowances and pension and conditions of service of a sitting or a retired Judge or the Supreme Court appointed as Commissioner shall be such as may be specified by the Governor. Provided further that the salary, allowances and pension payable to, and other conditions of service of, a Commissioner shall not be varied to his disadvantage after his appointment.

Every person appointed as Commissioner shall, before he enters upon his office, make and subscribe before the Governor or some person appointed in that behalf by him, an oath or affirmation according to the form set out hereunder: 'I, A.B., having been appointed Commissioner do swear in the name of God/solemnly affirm that I will bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India as by law established and that I will faithfully and to the best of my ability, knowledge and judgement perform the duties of my office without fear or favour, affection or ill-will'.

The Commission shall have a Secretary and such other officers and employees as may be prescribed by the Governor in consultation with the Commission to assist the Commission in the exercise of its powers and the discharge of its functions under this Act. The conditions of service of the Secretary and other officers and employees shall be such as may be prescribed by the Governor in consultation with the Commission. Appointment of the Secretary and other officers and employees shall be made by the Commission. Provided that where such appointment is made by direct recruitment, the Kerala Public Service Commission shall be consulted. The rules for reservation of appointments and posts in Government service in favour of the Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes of citizens shall, mutatis mutandis, apply to appointments to be made by the Commission under sub-section (1).

Any person other than a public servant or a service association or a trade union may present a petition to the Commission with an additional copy for service on the opposite party requesting that an allegation of corruption against any public man specified in such petition may be investigated under this Act. Every petition under sub-section (1) shall be accompanied by an affidavit in support of the allegation contained therein and a Treasury receipt evidencing the deposit of a sum of five hundred rupees: Provided that no such treasury receipt shall be necessary where the petition is presented jointly by not less than ten members of the Legislative Assembly. Every petition under sub-section (1) as well as any schedule or annexure thereto shall be verified in the manner laid down in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Central Act 5 of 1908), for the verification of pleadings. Any person who presents a petition under sub-section (1) or any person shall not publish or cause to be published the contents of the petition in any manner whatsoever. Any person who contravenes the provisions of sub-section (4) shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

main_sections.section_title: Commission not to initiate proceedings in certain cases
main_sections.description: The Commission shall not conduct any investigation under this Act, if the allegation of corruption mentioned in the petition has been the subject matter of another investigation or inquiry.

important_rules: A person appointed as Commissioner shall, before he enters upon his office, make and subscribe before the Governor or some person appointed in that behalf by him, an oath or affirmation to bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India and to perform the duties of his office without fear or favour, affection or ill-will.
The Commission shall have a Secretary and such other officers and employees as may be prescribed by the Governor in consultation with the Commission.

Any person who contravenes the provisions of sub-section (4) of Section 8 (regarding publishing petition contents) shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both for contravening provisions regarding publishing petition contents.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Commission.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through investigation of allegations of corruption against public men based on petitions submitted to the Commission.

rights: Right of any person (other than a public servant or service association or trade union) to present a petition to the Commission requesting investigation of corruption allegations against public men.
duties: The Commissioner's duty to perform office functions without fear or favour, affection or ill-will.
Duty to accompany petition with affidavit and treasury receipt.
Duty to verify petitions as laid down in the Code of Civil Procedure.
Duty of any person not to publish petition contents.

key_procedures: Presentation of a petition to the Commission by any person (other than a public servant or service association or trade union) requesting investigation of corruption allegations against public men.

Accompanying the petition with an affidavit in support of the allegation and a Treasury receipt evidencing the deposit of a sum of five hundred rupees (with an exception for joint petitions by members of the Legislative Assembly).
Verification of every petition as laid down in the Code of Civil Procedure.
The Commission investigating allegations of corruption based on the petition.
administration: The Governor and the Commission.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the President on the 29th day of February, 1984 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 169 dated the 1st March, 1984.

The definition of 'public man' is extensive and includes ministers, members of the legislative assembly, chairmen/members of various boards and committees, and chairmen/vice-chairmen of local authorities and government companies.

title: THE KERALA RATION DEALERS WELFARE FUND ACT, 1998
purpose: To provide for the establishment of a Fund for the welfare of ration dealers in the State of Kerala and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to all ration dealers in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Fund: Means the Kerala Ration Dealers Welfare Fund.
key_definitions.Ration dealer: Means a person holding a license to distribute essential commodities under the Kerala Rationing Order, 1966 or any other order for the time being in force.
key_definitions.Welfare measures: Includes such measures as the Government may, by notification, specify for the benefit of ration dealers, their families and dependents.

main_sections.description: Provides for the short title of the Act and its commencement.
Defines various terms used in the Act.
Establishes the Kerala Ration Dealers Welfare Fund.
Outlines the objectives for which the Fund can be utilized, such as providing welfare measures, financial assistance, education, medical aid, etc., to ration dealers and their dependents.

main_sections.section_title: Moneys to be credited to the Fund
main_sections.description: Specifies the sources from which moneys are to be credited to the Fund, including contributions from the Government, contributions from ration dealers, grants, donations, etc.
Deals with the management of the Fund, including the appointment of a Board of Trustees and their powers and functions.
Empowers the Government to frame schemes for the administration of the Fund and the implementation of welfare measures.
Provides for the audit of the accounts of the Fund.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the Trustees to make regulations for the management of the Fund, subject to the rules made by the Government.

important_rules: Contributions to the Fund are mandatory for ration dealers.
The Government shall contribute to the Fund.
The Fund shall be used for the welfare of ration dealers and their dependents, including financial assistance, medical aid, and educational support.

penalties: Failure to comply with the provisions of the Act or rules may attract penalties, including fines.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government and the Board of Trustees are responsible for the enforcement of the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the framing of schemes, making rules and regulations, and imposing penalties for non-compliance.

rights: Ration dealers have the right to benefit from the welfare measures provided by the Fund.
Ration dealers have the right to receive financial assistance and other benefits as prescribed by the schemes.
duties: Ration dealers have a duty to contribute to the Fund.
Ration dealers have a duty to comply with the provisions of the Act and the rules and regulations framed thereunder.
obligations: The Government has an obligation to establish and manage the Fund for the welfare of ration dealers.

key_procedures: Application for benefits from the Fund must be made in the prescribed manner.
The Board of Trustees will scrutinize applications and sanction benefits based on the eligibility criteria and available funds.
administration: The administration of the Fund is vested in the Board of Trustees, appointed by the Government.
important_notes: The Act aims to provide a social security net for ration dealers in Kerala.
The Act was enacted to address the welfare needs of a significant section of the trading community.

title: The Kerala Ration Dealers Welfare Fund Act, 1998
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a Fund to grant relief to, and to promote the welfare of the ration dealers in the State of Kerala and for matters incidental or ancillary thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.contribution: The sum of money payable to the fund under section 6.
key_definitions.family: Means wife or husband, as the case may be, minor sons and unmarried daughters, dependent parents and mentally retarded sons.
key_definitions.fund: Means the Kerala Ration Dealers' Welfare Fund established under section 3.
key_definitions.managing_committee: Means the Kerala Ration Dealers' Welfare Fund Managing Committee constituted under sub-section (1) of section 9.
key_definitions.member: Means a member of the Fund.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.ration_dealer: Means a person appointed as an authorised retail distributor under sub-clause (1) of clause 45 of the Kerala Rationing Order, 1966 and includes a person deemed to be appointed as an authorised retail distributor under the said sub-clause.
key_definitions.scheme: Means the Kerala Ration Dealers' Welfare Fund Scheme framed under this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Ration Dealers' Welfare Fund Act, 1998, extends to the whole of the State of Kerala, and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'contribution', 'family', 'fund', 'managing committee', 'member', 'prescribed', 'ration dealer', 'scheme', and 'year'.

Empowers the Government to frame a Scheme for the establishment of a Fund for the welfare of ration dealers in the State. The Scheme is to be published in the Gazette. The Fund shall consist of contributions, grants, loans, donations, amounts raised by the Managing Committee, and any other amount levied or received.

States that every person who is a ration dealer shall register himself as a member of the Fund. A person who becomes a ration dealer after the commencement of the Act shall, within three months of his appointment, apply for membership. Application under sub-section (2) shall be in such form and contain such particulars as may be provided in the Scheme. Upon receipt of the application, the Managing Committee or authorised officer shall make inquiry and, if satisfied, admit the applicant as a member. Every application under sub-section (2) shall be accompanied by a fee, as may be fixed by the Managing Committee.

A person shall cease to be a member when he ceases to be a ration dealer or fails to contribute to the Fund continuously for a period of six months. Provided that the Managing Committee may restore membership if sufficient reason for default is satisfied.

Every member shall contribute to the Fund, per month, an amount as may be fixed by the Managing Committee. A ration dealer whose appointment is suspended pending inquiry shall contribute to the Fund on lump sum of such number of installments as may be fixed by the Managing Committee. The contributions, remittances and all other amounts due to the Fund shall be paid to the Chief Executive Officer or an officer authorised by the Managing Committee.

main_sections.section_title: Payment from Fund on cessation of membership
main_sections.description: On cessation of membership, a member shall be entitled to receive from out of the Fund, the amount specified in column (3) of the Second Schedule, subject to any deduction authorised by the Scheme. Provided that a ration dealer who ceases to be a member by reason of cancellation of his appointment shall be entitled only to an amount equal to the contribution made by him. In the event of death of a member, the amount specified in column (3) of the Second Schedule shall be paid to his nominee, or where there is no nominee, to his legal heirs. An application for payment from the Fund shall be made to the Managing Committee or any officer authorised by it. An application received under sub-section (4) shall be disposed of by the Managing Committee or the officer authorised by it.

The Government shall, by notification in the Gazette, constitute a Committee to be called the 'Kerala Ration Dealers' Welfare Fund Managing Committee' for the administration of the Fund. The Committee shall consist of the Commissioner of Civil Supplies (ex-officio) as Chairman, the Director of Civil Supplies (ex-officio) as Secretary and Chief Executive Officer, the Controller of Rationing (ex-officio), the Chief Accounts Officer, Civil Supplies Department (ex-officio), a representative of the Finance Department, a representative of the Law Department, and four representatives of the ration dealers nominated by the Government. The Managing Committee shall be a body corporate, have perpetual succession and a common seal, and shall have power to acquire, hold and dispose of property, both movable and immovable, and to enter into contracts. The Managing Committee shall administer the Fund in such manner as may be specified in the Scheme. The Chairman and the Chief Executive Officer shall exercise such powers and perform such functions as may be specified in the Scheme. The Managing Committee may, with previous approval of the Government, delegate to the Chairman or to any other member or to the Chief Executive Officer of the Managing Committee or to any other officer, such of its powers and functions under this Act or the Scheme, as it may consider necessary.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office of the members of the Managing Committee
main_sections.description: The members of the Managing Committee nominated under clause (g) of sub-section (1) of section 9 shall hold office during the pleasure of the Government but shall not exceed three years at a time. A non-official member may resign his membership by giving notice in writing to the Government, but shall continue to hold office until his resignation is accepted by the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Disqualification and removal of non-official members of the Managing Committee
main_sections.description: A person shall be disqualified to be nominated as a non-official member if he is of unsound mind, is an undischarged insolvent, or has been convicted by a criminal court for an offence involving moral turpitude. A non-official member shall be disqualified for being a member if he becomes subject to any of the disqualifications specified in sub-section (1); or absents himself, without permission of the Managing Committee, for three consecutive meetings. Provided that such absence may be condoned by the Managing Committee. The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, remove any non-official member if he is subject to any of the disqualifications referred to in sub-section (2); or if, in the opinion of the Government, he is incapable of acting as a member or has abused his position to render his continuance detrimental to public interest.

penalties: Enhanced punishment for second or subsequent offences.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Managing Committee, Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through provisions of the Act and Scheme, notifications in the Gazette, and inquiry processes.

rights: Right to receive benefits from the Fund on cessation of membership (Section 7)
Right to claim payment from Fund in event of death to nominee/legal heirs (Section 7)
duties: Ration dealers shall register themselves as members (Section 4)
Members shall contribute to the Fund (Section 6)
Members shall adhere to the Scheme framed under the Act
obligations: Payment of contributions by members.
Adherence to the rules and procedures laid down by the Managing Committee and the Scheme.

key_procedures: Membership registration process (Section 4)
Application and disposal of claims from the Fund (Section 7)
Constitution and functioning of the Managing Committee (Sections 9, 10, 11)
Government's power to frame Scheme and make modifications (Section 3, 8)
Process for disqualification and removal of members of the Managing Committee (Section 11)
administration: Kerala Ration Dealers' Welfare Fund Managing Committee, overseen by the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act can be modified by the Government by notification in the Gazette, provided such modification does not prejudice the validity of anything previously done. (Section 8)
The Managing Committee may delegate its powers and functions to the Chairman, other members, or the Chief Executive Officer. (Section 9)
The Government can remove non-official members of the Managing Committee under specific circumstances. (Section 11)

title: The Kerala Raw Cashew Nuts (Marketing and Transport and Fixation of Minimum Price) Amendment Act, 1988
purpose: To further amend The Kerala Raw Cashewnuts (Marketing and Transport and Fixation of Minimum Price) Act, 1981, with respect to the sale and purchase of raw cashewnuts within the State, to the exclusion of all others by the procurement and sale thereof at fair prices. It also aims to amend provisions related to agents, their duties, price fixation, processing, and sale of raw cashewnuts.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala, specifically concerning the marketing, transport, and fixation of minimum prices of raw cashew nuts. It affects the Government, agents, sub-agents, cashew factories, and cultivators.

key_definitions.agent: means the agent authorised by the Government under sub-section (1) of section 3.
key_definitions.notified price: means the price notified in relation to raw cashewnuts, used in section 5.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Raw Cashewnuts (Marketing and Transport and Fixation of Minimum Price) Amendment Act, 1988. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 5th day of February, 1988.

The long title of the principal Act, The Kerala Raw Cashewnuts (Marketing and Transport and Fixation of Minimum Price) Act, 1981 (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), is substituted to read as 'An Act to provide for the trade in raw cashew nuts by the State to the exclusion of all others by the procurement and sale thereof at fair prices'.

The Preamble to the principal Act is amended to insert a paragraph stating that it is necessary to provide that trade in raw cashewnuts within the State should be undertaken by the State to the exclusion of all others, by the procurement and sale thereof at fair prices.
In section 1 of the principal Act, for sub-section (1), the following sub-section is substituted: 'This Act may be called the Kerala Raw Cashewnuts (Procurement and Distribution) Act, 1981'.

Amendments are made to section 2 of the principal Act, including substitution of clause (a) ('agent'), omission of clause (dd), substitution of clause (e) ('notified price'), and omission of clause (m).
Sections 2A, 2B, and 2C of the principal Act are omitted.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 3
main_sections.description: A new section 3 is substituted, dealing with the 'Restriction on sale and purchase of raw cashew nuts'. It states that the Government may authorise any co-operative society as agent, and no person shall sell or purchase raw cashew nuts within the State except to or from an agent or sub-agent.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 4
main_sections.description: A new section 4 is substituted, titled 'Restriction on possession of raw cashew nuts'. It stipulates that no person, other than an agent or sub-agent, shall have in their possession raw cashew nuts in excess of fifty kilograms.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new sections for sections 5 and 6
main_sections.description: New sections 5 and 6 are substituted. Section 5 deals with 'Price to be paid by agent and sub-agents', outlining how prices are to be notified and paid. Section 6 pertains to 'Agent to furnish returns', requiring agents to furnish returns to the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 10
main_sections.description: A new section 10 is substituted, titled 'Prohibition of processing or conversion and restriction on sale etc.'. It prohibits processing or conversion, except in accordance with the provisions of section 11, or otherwise disposing of any raw cashew nuts purchased by him under this Act.

New sections 11, 12, and 13 are inserted. Section 11 pertains to 'Sale of raw cashew nuts to cashew factories'. Section 12 details the 'Duty of occupier to take delivery of raw cashew nuts'. Section 13 concerns 'Price to be paid by occupants of cashew factories'.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 14
main_sections.description: Section 14 is substituted and titled 'Processing of raw cashew nuts'. It states that processing shall be done only in a factory and at no other place.
In section 15 of the principal Act, the words 'a licensee or a sub-licensee or' are omitted.
In section 16 of the principal Act, the words 'two rupees' are substituted with 'ten rupees'.
In section 19 of the principal Act, the words 'the Co-operative Department', are substituted with 'the Industries Department'.
In section 20 of the principal Act, in sub-section (2), the words 'at the minimum price', are substituted with 'at the notified price'.

In section 22 of the principal Act, sub-section (2) is amended to substitute 'be paid the minimum price' with 'be paid the price' and 'and such price shall be determined in accordance with the provisions of section 5' shall be inserted at the end.

The Kerala Raw Cashewnuts (Marketing and Transport and Fixation of Minimum Price) Amendment Ordinance, 1988 (6 of 1988), is repealed. Notwithstanding the repeal, any action taken or anything done or omitted to be done or taken under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: No person shall sell any raw cashew nut within the State except to the agent or a sub-agent.
No person other than the agent or a sub-agent shall purchase any raw cashew nuts within the State.
No person other than the agent or a sub-agent shall have in possession, at any time, raw cashew nuts in excess of the quantity of fifty kilograms.

Raw cashew nuts sold to the cashew factories shall be purchased by the agent and sub-agents under this Act and sold to the cashew factories in the State which are registered in pursuance of the rules made under the Factories Act, 1948 (Central Act 63 of 1948), and which were eligible for imported cashewnuts under the Import Trade Control Policy of the Government of India, in accordance with the provisions of sub-section (2).

The agent shall furnish to the Government and to any officer specified by the Government in this behalf by notification in the Gazette on such day or days as may be prescribed, a return showing the place or places where raw cashew nuts have been stocked by him, the quantity thereof and the price paid by him therefor.

Prohibition of processing or conversion and restriction on sale etc.: The agent or a sub-agent shall not process or convert, or sell, except in accordance with the provisions of section 11, or otherwise dispose of, any raw cashew nuts purchased by him under this Act.

Processing of raw cashew nuts to be done in the concerned factory.—Roasting, shelling, peeling and grading of raw cashew nuts sold to a cashew factory shall be done only in that factory and at no other place.

penalties: Failure of an occupier of a cashew factory to take delivery of raw cashew nuts under sub-section (1) shall constitute a contravention of the provisions of this Act punishable under section 25.
Contravention of any of the provisions of this Act or any rule or order made thereunder shall be punishable under section 25.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government of Kerala, Law (Legislation-C) Department, Government, specified officers, agent, sub-agent.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications in the Gazette, orders issued by authorised officers, and penalties prescribed under section 25.

rights: Right to receive notified price for raw cashew nuts.
duties: Duty of an occupier of a cashew factory to take delivery of raw cashew nuts offered to be sold to his factory from the place and before the date referred to in sub-section (5) of section 11, after sale offer shall stand cancelled.
obligations: Obligation for agents to furnish returns to the Government.
Obligation for agents and sub-agents to sell raw cashew nuts to registered cashew factories.
Obligation to conduct processing of raw cashew nuts only in the concerned factory.

key_procedures: Procedure for authorizing co-operative societies as agents for procurement and sale of raw cashew nuts.
Procedure for agents to notify prices and pay the notified price to cultivators.
Procedure for agents to furnish returns to the Government.
Procedure for occupiers of cashew factories to take delivery of raw cashew nuts.
Procedure for setting the price of raw cashew nuts by the Government considering grade, quality, notified price, and incidental expenses.
administration: Government of Kerala, Law (Legislation-C) Department, Industries Department.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on the 5th day of February, 1988.
The Act effectively makes the State the sole authority for the trade in raw cashew nuts, excluding all others.
The Ordinance of 1988 is repealed and saved, meaning actions taken under it are valid.
Penalties for contravention of the Act are prescribed under section 25.

title: THE KERALA RAW CASHEW NUTS (PROCUREMENT AND DISTRIBUTION) AMENDMENT ACT, 1983
purpose: To amend the Kerala Raw Cashewnuts (Procurement and Distribution) Act, 1981.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and concerns the procurement and distribution of raw cashewnuts. It outlines provisions for licensing, maintenance of supplies, and related matters.

key_definitions.preamble: The introductory statement explaining the expediency for the amendment.
key_definitions.agent: Means the agent appointed under sub-section (2) of section 3.
key_definitions.licensee: Means a licensee or a sub-licensee.
key_definitions.processing: Means roasting, shelling, peeling or grading.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it shall come into force on the 22nd day of February, 1983.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new long title for existing long title
main_sections.description: Substitutes the long title of the principal Act with a new one to make provisions for facilitating the maintenance of supplies of raw cashewnuts produced within the State and for matters incidental thereto.
Amends the preamble of the principal Act by substituting the sixth paragraph.
Substitutes the sub-section (1) of section 1 of the principal Act.
Amends section 2 of the principal Act by substituting clause (a) and inserting a new clause (dd) and (m).
Inserts new sections concerning grant of license for purchase of raw cashewnuts, suspension of license, and appointment of sub-licenses.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 3
main_sections.description: Substitutes section 3 of the principal Act concerning who can sell raw cashewnuts.
Amends section 4 of the principal Act by modifying the opening paragraph and omitting the proviso.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new sections for sections 5 and 6
main_sections.description: Substitutes sections 5 and 6 of the principal Act concerning minimum price to be paid for raw cashewnuts and procurement of raw cashewnuts by the Government.
Amends section 10 of the principal Act by substituting the words 'provisions of section 11'
Omits sections 11, 12 and 13 of the principal Act.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 14
main_sections.description: Substitutes section 14 of the principal Act, defining 'processing'.
Amends section 15 of the principal Act by substituting the words 'licensee or a sub-licensee or the agent or a sub-agent'.
Amends section 20 of the principal Act by substituting the words 'at the minimum price'.
Amends section 22 of the principal Act by substituting the words 'be paid the minimum price'.
Repeals the Kerala Raw Cashewnuts (Procurement and Distribution) Amendment Ordinance, 1983 and saves actions taken under the Ordinance.

important_rules: A licensee may, within a period of thirty days from the commencement of the Act, or within such further period as may be specified by the Government, apply for a license to purchase raw cashewnuts.
An application for a license shall be accompanied by a court fee stamp of the value of two rupees.
The competent authority shall, after such inquiry as it considers necessary, grant the license.

No person shall sell any raw cashewnut within the State except to a licensee or a sub-licensee or the agent or a sub-agent and no person other than a licensee or a sub-licensee or the agent or a sub-agent shall purchase any raw cashewnut within the State.
