Minimum price to be paid for raw cashewnuts: A licensee or a sub-licensee or the agent or a sub-agent shall not purchase raw cashewnuts at a price which is less than the minimum price notified under sub-section (2).
Raw cashewnuts to be sold at not less than the minimum price.
Processing of raw cashewnuts to be done in registered factories within the State.

penalties: Any contravention of the provisions of this Act or any of the terms and conditions of a license may lead to suspension of license.
No license shall be suspended without giving the licensee an opportunity to state his case.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Competent authority appointed by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the grant, suspension, and cancellation of licenses, and through inquiries by the competent authority.

rights: Right to apply for a license to purchase raw cashewnuts.
Right of an applicant to be heard before rejection of an application.
duties: Licensees and sub-licensees must purchase raw cashewnuts at a price not less than the minimum price notified.

Agents and sub-licenses shall furnish to the Government and to any officer specified by the Government in this behalf by notification in the Gazette, on such day or days as may be prescribed, a return in the prescribed form showing the place or places where raw cashewnuts have been stocked by him, the quantity thereof and the price paid by him therefor.
obligations: To comply with the terms and conditions of the license.
To ensure that raw cashewnuts are processed in registered factories within the State.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining a license: Submit an application to the competent authority with a court fee stamp, and the authority will grant the license after inquiry if necessary.
Procedure for suspension of license: The competent authority may suspend a license for contravention of provisions, but only after giving the licensee an opportunity to be heard.
administration: The Government of Kerala, through competent authorities appointed by it.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 6th day of April, 1983 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No 409 dated the 7th - April, 1983.
The Act makes provisions for facilitating the maintenance of supplies of raw cashewnuts produced within the State.
The minimum price notified under sub-section (2) of section 2 is relevant for the purchase of raw cashewnuts.

title: THE KERALA RAW CASHEWNUTS (PROCUREMENT AND DISTRIBUTION) ACT, 1981
purpose: To provide for the trade in raw cashewnuts by the State to the exclusion of all others by the procurement and sale thereof at fair prices.
scope: Applies to the entire State of Kerala and all trade in raw cashewnuts within the State.

key_definitions.competent authority: The Government or an officer authorised by the Government to grant permits.
key_definitions.co-operative society: A society registered or deemed to be registered under the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969 (21 of 1969).
key_definitions.cultivator: A person who actually cultivates any land with cashew or who is entitled to take the usufructs from any land cultivated with cashew.
key_definitions.notified price: In relation to raw cashewnuts, the price notified under section (2) of section 5.
key_definitions.occupier: Means an occupier as defined in the Factories Act, 1948 (Central Act 63 of 1948).
key_definitions.per on: Includes a body corporate, a company, a firm, an association of individuals or a co-operative society.
key_definitions.permit: Means a permit referred to in section 15.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.sub-agent: Means a co-operative society appointed by the agent under section 9.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called The Kerala Raw Cashewnuts (Procurement and Distribution) Act, 1981. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 2nd day of February, 1981.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including agent, competent authority, co-operative society, cultivator, notified price, occupier, per on, permit, prescribed, raw cashew nut, State, and sub-agent.

main_sections.section_title: Restriction on sale and purchase of raw cashewnuts
main_sections.description: No person shall sell any raw cashew nut within the State except to the agent or sub-agent, with certain exceptions.

main_sections.section_title: Restriction on possession of raw cashewnuts
main_sections.description: No person other than the agent or sub-agent shall have in possession, at any time, raw cashew nuts in excess of fifty kilograms.

main_sections.section_title: Price to be paid by agent and sub-agents
main_sections.description: Specifies the price to be paid by occupiers of cashew factories for raw cashewnuts sold to them and the procedure for determining this price, considering factors like grade, quality, notified price, and incidental expenses.
Agents are required to furnish returns to the Government showing the place or places where raw cashewnuts have been stocked by them, along with the quantity and price paid.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to issue instructions to agent and sub-agents
main_sections.description: The Government has the power to issue general instructions to agents and sub-agents for efficiently carrying out their duties under the Act.
If an agent contravenes any provision of the Act or fails to comply with instructions, the Government may, after giving an opportunity for representation, remove the agent.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Co-operative Societies as sub-agents
main_sections.description: The Government may, by order, appoint any co-operative society as a sub-agent for the purposes of the Act and define the local area for which such appointment is made.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of processing or conversion and restriction on sale, etc.
main_sections.description: Prohibits processing or conversion of raw cashewnuts and restricts their sale except in accordance with the provisions of section 11 or otherwise disposed of.

main_sections.section_title: Sale of raw cashewnuts to cashew factories
main_sections.description: All raw cashewnuts purchased by the agent and sub-agents are to be sold to cashew factories in the State, subject to rules under the Factories Act and import trade control policy. The quantity to be sold is determined by the Government, considering the grade, quality, and license strength of the factory workers. Officers authorized by the Government can specify the quantity to be sold to each cashew factory.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of occupier to take delivery of raw cashewnuts
main_sections.description: Occupiers of cashew factories must take delivery of raw cashewnuts offered to them. If they fail to do so, the sale shall stand cancelled.

main_sections.section_title: Price to be paid by occupiers
main_sections.description: The price to be paid by occupiers of cashew factories for raw cashewnuts sold to them will be decided by the Government from time to time, taking into consideration the grade and quality of the cashewnuts, the notified price, and incidental expenses.

main_sections.section_title: Processing of raw cashewnuts to be done in the concerned factory
main_sections.description: Roasting, shelling, peeling and grading of raw cashewnuts sold to a cashew factory under section 11 shall be done only in that factory and at no other place.

main_sections.section_title: Restriction on transport of raw cashewnuts
main_sections.description: No person shall transport or attempt to transport raw cashewnuts from one place to another within the State except under a permit issued by the competent authority or any other officer authorised by the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Application form and form of permit
main_sections.description: An application for a permit must be in the prescribed form and verified in the prescribed manner, with a court-fee stamp of the value of two rupees.
The competent authority may refuse to grant a permit if it is satisfied that the applicant will defeat any of the provisions of this Act or rules made thereunder.

The competent authority may cancel a permit if an applicant has, after the issue of the permit, contravened any provision of the Act or rules, without prejudice to any other action against the holder.

Revenue Inspectors, Sales Tax Inspectors, officers of the Co-operative Department, Block Development Officers, and other specified officers are empowered to enter and search premises, inspect books, seize any animal, vessel, vehicle, or other conveyance used in carrying raw cashewnuts, and seize any raw cashewnuts suspected to be contravening the Act. Provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 apply to search and seizure.

Where raw cashewnuts are seized under this Act, and it is believed that they are in contravention of the Act, the Revenue Divisional Officer may order confiscation of the raw cashewnuts, their package, covering, receptacle, animal, vessel, vehicle or other conveyance used in carrying them. An owner of such conveyance may be given an option to pay a fine not less than one-half of the value of the seized items.

main_sections.section_title: Issue of show-cause notice before confiscation
main_sections.description: Before confiscating any raw cashewnuts, package, covering, receptacle, animal, vessel, vehicle or other conveyance, a notice must be issued to the owner informing them of the grounds for confiscation. The owner has an opportunity to make a representation and be heard in the matter. If the owner fails to comply, the confiscation order may be passed without prejudice to any other action.

Any person aggrieved by an order of confiscation under section 20 may, within one month from the date of communication of the order, appeal to the District Judge having jurisdiction over the area in which the raw cashewnuts subject to such order relate.

important_rules: No person shall sell any raw cashew nut within the State except to the agent or a sub-agent.
No person other than the agent or sub-agent shall have raw cashew nuts in possession exceeding fifty kilograms.
Raw cashewnuts purchased by the agent and sub-agents are to be sold to cashew factories in the State.
Processing of raw cashewnuts (roasting, shelling, peeling, grading) must be done in the concerned factory.
Transport of raw cashewnuts requires a permit from the competent authority.
Applications for permits must be in the prescribed form and accompanied by a court-fee stamp.

penalties: Liable to be punished with imprisonment which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees or with both for contravention of certain provisions.
Confiscation of raw cashewnuts and their associated conveyances.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Revenue Inspectors, Sales Tax Inspectors, officers of the Co-operative Department, Block Development Officers, and other officers authorised by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through powers of entry, seizure, confiscation, and imposition of penalties. Appeals against confiscation orders can be made to the District Judge.

rights: Right to obtain a permit for transport of raw cashewnuts.
Right to make a representation against confiscation orders.
Right to appeal against confiscation orders to the District Judge.
duties: Duty of agents to furnish returns.
Duty of occupiers to take delivery of raw cashewnuts.
Duty to comply with instructions issued by the Government.
Duty to adhere to the prescribed forms and procedures for permits and sales.
obligations: Obligation to sell raw cashewnuts only to authorised agents or sub-agents.
Obligation not to possess more than fifty kilograms of raw cashewnuts (unless an agent or sub-agent).

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining a transport permit: Submit an application in the prescribed form with a court-fee stamp to the competent authority.
Procedure for sale of raw cashewnuts to factories: Agents and sub-agents sell to cashew factories as per Government directives and quantities specified.
Procedure for confiscation: Issue of show-cause notice, opportunity for representation, and appeal to the District Judge.
Procedure for appeal: Appeal against confiscation order to the District Judge within one month of communication.
administration: The Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on February 2, 1981.

The Preamble indicates the rationale behind the Act, citing an essential article under the Essential Commodities Act and the Government's concern over unemployment and the state of the cashew industry.
Section 11 states that raw cashewnuts are to be sold to cashew factories in the State under the rules made under the Factories Act, 1948, and the Import Trade Control Policy.

title: THE KERALA RE-ENACTING ACT, 1958 (Act 23 of 1958)
purpose: To re-enact certain enactments, including those dealing with the consolidation and amendment of laws relating to civil courts in the State of Kerala, the removal of disqualifications, the interpretation and general clauses of Acts, the criminal procedure, road transport services, the board of revenue, small cause courts, and the Khadi and Village Industries Board.
scope: Applies to enactments as specified in the Schedule, which include various Acts of the State of Kerala and formerly of Travancore and Cochin.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Re-enacting Act, 1958, and shall come into force at once.
Specifies that the Acts mentioned in the Schedule are hereby re-enacted with the modifications provided in section 3 and the fourth column of the Schedule.

Details how the words 'Enacted by the President in the Ninth Year of the Republic of India' are to be replaced with 'Enacted by the President in the Seventh Year of the Republic of India' for Acts enacted before the long title of Acts Nos. 1 and 2 of 1957, and similarly for Acts enacted before the long title of Acts in the Eighth Year of the Republic of India. It also specifies that certain words in the Schedule are to be omitted.

key_procedures: To re-enact existing Acts with specified modifications.
To replace introductory phrases in certain Acts.
important_notes: The preamble indicates that the Act is based on the President's Proclamation under Article 356 of the Constitution.
The Act aims to consolidate and amend laws.
Modifications are applied to specific sections and the introductory phrases of the re-enacted Acts.

title: THE KERALA RE-ENACTING ACT, 1957
purpose: To re-enact certain President's Acts, as it was deemed necessary to replace an Act of the Legislature, the Kerala Re-enacting Ordinance, 1957 (Ordinance No. 6 of 1957), re-enacting certain President's Acts.
scope: Applies to the re-enactment of certain President's Acts and modifications to those Acts.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Re-enacting Act, 1957, and shall come into force at once.
The Acts specified in the Schedule are hereby re-enacted with the modifications specified in section 3 and in the fourth column of the Schedule.
Specifies modifications to the Acts, including omitting long titles and certain introductory phrases. It also details how to handle existing legislation and its validity.
The Kerala Re-enacting Ordinance, 1957 (No. 6 of 1957), is hereby repealed.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Kerala Re-enacting Act, 1957, shall come into force at once.
Rule 2: Acts specified in the Schedule are re-enacted with modifications.
Rule 3: Modifications to the Acts involve omitting specific phrases and clauses.
Rule 4: The Kerala Re-enacting Ordinance, 1957, is repealed.
key_procedures: Procedure 1: Identify the Acts listed in the Schedule for re-enactment.
Procedure 2: Apply the specified modifications from section 3 and the Schedule to the re-enacted Acts.
Procedure 3: Ensure that the commencement of the Act is immediate.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the President on 22nd January 1958 and was published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 23rd January 1958.
Modifications include details regarding the construction, repair and maintenance of irrigation works, conservation and distribution of water, and the levy of betterment contribution and water cess.
The validity of any cessation made under certain Acts is maintained.
The re-enacted Acts are explicitly stated to not affect the names of the irrigation works or their publication.
The re-enacted Acts do not cover arrears of land revenue under the Travancore-Cochin Revenue Recovery Act, 1941.

title: The Kerala Re-Enacting Act, 1968
purpose: To re-enact certain Acts enacted by the President for the State of Kerala, as it is expedient to re-enact certain Acts enacted by the President for the State of Kerala in exercise of the power of the Legislature of that State to make laws.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala. The Act re-enacts specific acts that were previously enacted by the President for the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Re-enacting Act, 1968.
The Acts mentioned in the First Schedule are hereby re-enacted with the modifications specified therein.
The Acts mentioned in the Second Schedule are hereby repealed.

important_notes: The Acts re-enacted are listed in the First Schedule.
The Acts repealed are listed in the Second Schedule.
Specific modifications to the re-enacted acts are provided.

The Act contains amendments to various Kerala Acts, including the Kerala Abkari Laws (Amendment and Validation) Act, 1964; Kerala Revenue Recovery Laws (Amendment) Act, 1964; Kerala State Legislature (Continuance of Use of English Language) Act, 1965; Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1965; Kerala Electricity Duty (Validation) Act, 1965; Kerala Salestax (Levy and Validation) Act, 1965; Kerala Khadi and Village Industries Board (Amendment) Act, 1965; Kerala Hindu Places of Public Worship (Authorisation of Entry) Act, 1965; Kerala Surcharge on Taxes (Amendment and Validation) Act, 1966; Kerala University (Amendment) Act, 1966; Kerala Land Acquisition (Amendment) Act, 1966; Pattazhi Devaswom Lands (Vesting and Enfranchisement) Amendment Act, 1966; Kerala High Court (Amendment) Act, 1966; Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Amendment Act, 1966; Kerala Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1966; Kerala Prevention of Eviction Act, 1966; Kerala Land Relinquishment (Amendment) Act, 1966; Kerala Essential Articles Control (Temporary Powers) Continuance Act, 1967; Kerala Court of Wards Act, 1967; Kerala Prevention and Control of Animal Diseases Act, 1967; Kerala General Salestax (Amendment) Act, 1967.

title: THE KERALA RE-ENACTING ACT, 1960
purpose: To re-enact certain Acts enacted by the Parliament for the State of Kerala, to provide for the recovery in certain cases of arrears of cesses, rates, taxes, fees or other sums due to panchayats, and to authorise payment and appropriation of certain further sums from and out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala for the services of the financial year 1959-60, and to provide for certain other connected matters.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala, re-enacting specific Acts and providing for financial matters related to the financial year 1959-60.

main_sections.description: (1) This Act may be called the Kerala Re-enacting Act, 1960. (2) It shall come into force at once. (3) Re-enactment of Acts: The Acts specified in the Schedule are hereby re-enacted with the modifications specified therein.
This section, along with the Schedule, details the specific Acts that are being re-enacted and modified by this Act.

Contains the list of Acts being re-enacted, with their respective amendments and substitution clauses. This includes the Kerala Local Authority Laws (Amendment) Act, 1959, the Kerala Appropriation Act, 1959, the Travancore-Cochin Vehicles Taxation (Amendment and Validation) Act, 1959, the Kerala Appropriation (No. 2) Act, 1959, the Kerala Co-operative Land Mortgage Banks Act, 1960, and the Kerala Warehouses Act, 1960. It also includes amendments to the Central Excises and Salt Act, 1944.

important_rules: The Acts specified in the Schedule are re-enacted with modifications.
Specific provisions for the recovery of arrears of cesses, rates, taxes, fees or other sums due to panchayats.
Authorization for payment and appropriation of further sums for the financial year 1959-60.
key_procedures: The Schedule outlines the specific procedures for re-enacting and modifying various existing laws.
Procedures are established for the recovery of certain arrears and for financial appropriations.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the President on 17th December 1960 and was published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 23rd December 1960.
The re-enacted Acts are effective from the date specified in the respective Acts or as modified.

title: The Kerala Re-enacting Act, 1966
purpose: To re-enact certain President's Acts, Kerala State Legislature (Delegation of Powers) Act, 1965 and other specified acts.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and re-enacts specified Acts.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Re-enacting Act, 1966, and it shall come into force at once.
Specifies that certain President's Acts, as listed in the Schedule, are hereby re-enacted.
Lists the specific President's Acts and Kerala State Legislature Acts that are being re-enacted.

important_rules: This Act may be called the Kerala Re-enacting Act, 1966.
The Act shall come into force at once.
The President's Acts specified in the Schedule are hereby re-enacted.
important_notes: Published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 28, dated 23rd March, 1966.

title: The Kerala Recognition of Trade Unions Act, 2010
purpose: To provide for the recognition of Trade Unions for facilitating collective bargaining and to check multiplicity of Trade Unions in industrial establishments and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to every industrial establishment situated in Kerala, except the industrial establishments for which Central Government is the appropriate Government under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947. It also applies to every registered trade union functioning in such industrial establishments.  The Act also defines 'local area' as such area comprising the whole or part of Kerala as the Government may specify by notification in the Official Gazette, in relation to any class of industry.

key_definitions.trade union: means a Trade Union registered under the Trade Unions Act, 1926 (Central Act 16 of 1926)
key_definitions.recognised trade union: means a Trade Union recognised under section 9 of this Act
key_definitions.industrial establishment: shall have the same meaning as in clause (ka) of section 2 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (Central Act 14 of 1947)
key_definitions.employer: shall have the same meaning as in clause (g) of section 2 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (Central Act 14 of 1947)
key_definitions.registrar: means the Registrar for recognition of Trade Unions under section 3 of this Act and includes any Additional or Deputy Registrar for recognition of Trade Unions

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Recognition of Trade Unions Act, 2010 and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint. It also details the application of the Act to industrial establishments in Kerala and registered trade unions functioning within them.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'trade union', 'recognised trade union', 'industrial establishment', 'employer', 'Government', 'local area', 'principal bargaining agent', 'recognised Trade Union', 'Registrar', 'sole bargaining agent', and 'workman'.

Empowers the Government to appoint a Registrar for the recognition of Trade Unions and the subordinate staff. It also specifies the powers and functions of the Registrar and any Additional or Deputy Registrar.

Outlines the procedure for any registered Trade Union to apply for a certificate of recognition. It specifies the conditions for such application, including the requirement to be functioning as a registered Trade Union in an industrial establishment or class of industry for a specified period.

Details the process for the Registrar to issue a certificate of recognition. This involves receiving an application, giving notice to other Trade Unions, holding an inquiry, and determining if the applicant Trade Union fulfills the conditions laid down.

main_sections.section_title: Withdrawal or cancellation of certificate for recognition
main_sections.description: States that a certificate for recognition can be withdrawn or cancelled by the Registrar if satisfied that it was obtained by fraud or misrepresentation or if the Trade Union has ceased to exist or has lost the requisite percentage of membership or has violated provisions of the Act. This requires a notice period before cancellation.

Provides for any Trade Union aggrieved by the refusal to issue, withdrawal, or cancellation of a certificate of recognition to appeal to the Government within a specified period. It also outlines the process for appeals, including the authority to confirm, modify, or reverse the Registrar's order.

Specifies that all workmen above the age of eighteen years and in service for a period of not less than one hundred and twenty days immediately before the date of announcement of an election to hold the purpose of section 5 are eligible for voting. It also addresses eligibility for voting in elections for an industrial establishment or class of industry.

Details the conditions under which the Registrar shall grant recognition to a Trade Union. This includes being the sole bargaining agent or principal bargaining agent or constituent of a joint bargaining council.

Lists the rights of a recognized Trade Union, including the right to bargain collectively, discuss and settle terms with employers, and participate in negotiations and proceedings concerning industrial relations.
Requires recognized Trade Unions to submit returns to the Registrar in the prescribed manner.
Outlines the consequences of a recognized Trade Union failing to submit the required returns.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for failure or refusal to grant recognition
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for failure or refusal to grant recognition as required by the Act.
Provides protection for lawful activities of trade unions.
Grants the Government the power to exempt any establishment or class of establishments from the provisions of this Act.
Empowers the Government to remove difficulties that may arise in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: A Trade Union applying for recognition must have been functioning as a registered Trade Union in an industrial establishment or class of industry for at least six months immediately preceding the date of filing the application.
The membership of the Trade Union must be open to all workmen employed in the industrial establishment or class of industry.
The Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, apply the provisions of this Act to any industrial establishment employing such number of persons less than fifty, as may be specified.
Recognized Trade Unions have the right to participate in negotiations, discussions, and settlement concerning terms of employment and industrial relations.
Recognized Trade Unions must submit returns to the Registrar in the prescribed manner.

penalties: Penalty for failure or refusal to grant recognition (details not specified in the provided pages).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Registrar for recognition of Trade Unions, and the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the appointment of a Registrar, the process of recognition, appeals, and the power to make rules.

rights: Rights of recognized Trade Unions to facilitate collective bargaining.
Right to participate in negotiations, discussion, and settlement of terms of employment.
Right to participate in proceedings relating to industrial relations.
Right to sign settlements which are binding.
duties: Duty to apply for recognition under prescribed conditions.
Duty to submit returns to the Registrar.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the provisions of the Trade Unions Act, 1926.
Obligation to ensure membership is open to all workmen in the relevant establishment or class of industry.
Obligation to comply with rules and orders made by the Registrar or Government under the Act.

key_procedures: Application for recognition of a Trade Union: A registered Trade Union must apply to the Registrar, fulfilling specified eligibility criteria and submitting prescribed fees.
Issuance of certificate of recognition: The Registrar will process the application, notify other Trade Unions, conduct inquiries, and if satisfied, issue a certificate.
Withdrawal or cancellation of recognition: The Registrar can withdraw or cancel a certificate if conditions are violated, after giving notice.
Appeals: Aggrieved parties can appeal to the Government against decisions of the Registrar.
Election of bargaining agent: If multiple unions apply, an election may be conducted by secret ballot.
administration: The Government of Kerala, through the Registrar for recognition of Trade Unions.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the President on 14th October, 2010 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 2397 dated 29th October, 2010.
The Act aims to check the multiplicity of Trade Unions.
The Government has the power to exempt certain establishments from the provisions of the Act.
The Act refers to the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (Central Act 14 of 1947) and the Trade Unions Act, 1926 (Central Act 16 of 1926) for definitions and context.

title: The Kerala Record of Rights Act, 1968
purpose: To provide for the preparation of record of rights in respect of lands in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to lands in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.kudikidappukaran: Shall have the meaning assigned to it in the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 (1 of 1964).
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by the rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.prescribed officer: Means an officer not below the rank of Deputy Tahsildar appointed by the Government to exercise the powers and discharge the duties of a prescribed officer under this Act.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Record of Rights Act, 1968. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Defines terms used in the Act, including 'kudikidappukaran', 'prescribed', and 'prescribed officer'.

Details the process for preparing a record of rights, including the information to be included and the role of the prescribed officer. It also outlines the procedure for the preparation and publication of draft records of rights and the consideration of objections.

Describes the process of publishing the draft record of rights, allowing for objections, and its consideration by the prescribed officer. The final record will be published after objections are considered and disposed of.

main_sections.section_title: Correction of clerical mistake in register.
main_sections.description: Empowers the prescribed officer to correct clerical mistakes in the record of rights on application or on their own motion.

Allows the prescribed officer to conduct inquiries or applications to revise the record of rights, provided that no order is passed without giving affected persons an opportunity to be heard. It also details conditions under which applications for revision can be made and the time limits for such applications.

main_sections.section_title: Acquisitions of rights to be reported.
main_sections.description: Requires any person acquiring rights by survivorship, succession, inheritance, partition, purchase, mortgage, gift, lease, or otherwise, or any person having charge of property, to report such acquisition to the officer as specified by the Government. It also outlines the procedure and penalties for failing to report.

Mandates that persons whose rights have been entered in the record of rights shall be bound to requisition of the officer engaged in preparation, maintenance, or revision of such rights to furnish information for inspection within thirty days.

main_sections.section_title: Record of rights to be admissible in evidence.
main_sections.description: States that the record of rights prepared under this Act shall be admissible in evidence before any court or tribunal. Certified copies of entries in the record of rights are also admissible.
Certified copies of entries in the record of rights may be granted by such officers and on payment of such fees as may be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Record of rights open to inspection.
main_sections.description: Subject to rules and payment of fees, the record of rights shall be open to inspection by the public during office hours.

Empowers any officer exercising powers under the Act to enter upon and take measurements of land for the purpose of preparing the record of rights, and to do all other acts necessary for that purpose.
Grants any officer exercising powers under the Act the powers of a civil court for summoning and enforcing attendance of persons, administering oaths, examining witnesses, and other related matters.

Prohibits suits against the Government or any officer for damage caused or injury suffered in good faith while carrying out the provisions of this Act. It also states that no prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against any officer for anything done in good faith under this Act or rules thereunder.

Allows the Government to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of the Act. Such rules shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly and shall have effect, subject to modifications agreed upon by the Assembly.

important_rules: Rules regarding the content and preparation of the record of rights.
Rules for the publication of draft records of rights and handling objections.
Rules for the inspection of the record of rights.
Rules regarding fees for certified copies and inspection.
Rules specifying the form and manner of reporting acquisitions of rights.

penalties: Penalty not exceeding two hundred rupees for failure to furnish information or produce documents when required.
Penalty of rupees two for failure to report acquisition of right within three months.
Penalty of rupees five for failure to report acquisition of right within one year.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Prescribed officers appointed by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inquiries, revision of records, summoning witnesses, and imposing penalties for non-compliance.

rights: Right to have one's rights in land recorded.
Right to inspect the record of rights.
Right to obtain certified copies of entries in the record of rights.
Right to be heard before any adverse order is passed under Section 6 (Revision).
duties: Duty to report acquisition of rights in land.
Duty to furnish information and produce documents as required by the prescribed officer.
Duty to present oneself for inquiry or examination when summoned.
obligations: Obligation to requisition of the officer engaged in preparation, maintenance or revision of record of rights to furnish information or documents for inspection within thirty days.

key_procedures: Preparation of draft record of rights by the prescribed officer.
Publication of the draft record and inviting objections.
Consideration and disposal of objections by the prescribed officer.
Publication of the final record of rights.
Correction of clerical mistakes in the record.
Revision of the record of rights upon application or on the officer's motion.
administration: The Revenue Divisional Officer is mentioned as an authority in Section 6 (Revision), implying overall administrative oversight.
important_notes: The Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 238 dated 4th October, 1968.
The Act was enacted in the Nineteenth Year of the Republic of India.
Any modification or annulment of rules made under Section 15 will not prejudice any validity of anything previously done under that rule.

title: THE KERALA RELIEF UNDERTAKINGS (SPECIAL PROVISIONS) AMENDMENT ACT, 1990
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Relief Undertakings (Special Provisions) Act, 1961.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Relief Undertakings (Special Provisions) Act, 1961.

key_definitions.national financial institution: Any financial institution with jurisdiction all over India, set up by enacting Special Acts in the Parliament with the objective of providing financial assistance to industrial units.
key_definitions.bank: Means a banking company as defined in clause (c) of section 5 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 (Central Act 10 of 1949).

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Relief Undertakings (Special Provisions) Amendment Act, 1990, and shall come into force at once.

Amends section 4 of the Kerala Relief Undertakings (Special Provisions) Act, 1961. It adds a proviso and Explanation to clause (b) of section 4. The proviso clarifies that the provisions of this clause shall not apply to the liabilities or obligations accrued or incurred in favour of national financial institutions and banks, and to any remedy for the enforcement thereof. The Explanation defines 'national financial institution' and 'bank'.

important_rules: Provisions of clause (b) of section 4 of the Principal Act shall not apply to liabilities or obligations accrued or incurred in favour of national financial institutions and banks.
No remedy shall be available for the enforcement of liabilities or obligations accrued or incurred in favour of national financial institutions and banks.

rights: Right of national financial institutions and banks to enforce liabilities and obligations incurred in their favour.

administration: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided excerpt, but likely falls under the purview of the relevant state government department dealing with industrial matters.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 20th day of August, 1990, and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 809 dated the 21st August, 1990.

title: THE KERALA RELIEF UNDERTAKINGS (SPECIAL PROVISIONS) AMENDMENT ACT, 1980
purpose: To amend The Kerala Relief Undertakings (Special Provisions) Act, 1961, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the state of Kerala and concerns relief undertakings within the state.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Relief Undertakings (Special Provisions) Amendment Act, 1980. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 21st day of November, 1980.
Amends section 3 of the Kerala Relief Undertakings (Special Provisions) Act, 1961, by substituting the words 'five years' with 'ten years'.

Amends section 4 of the principal Act. It specifies that after clause (a), the following clause shall be inserted: "(aa) after the period during which the relief undertaking continues, as such under sub-section (2) of section 3, any liability of the undertaking to pay tax under the Kerala General Sales-tax Act, 1963 (15 of 1963), incurred before the undertaking was declared a relief undertaking and any remedy for enforcing the payment thereof shall be suspended and all proceedings relating to the levy, assessment, collection and recovery of such tax pending before any court, tribunal, officer or authority shall be stayed.". Additionally, it states that in clause (b), for the words, brackets and letters "clause (b)", the words, brackets and letters "clause (aa) or clause (b)" shall be substituted.

The Kerala Relief Undertakings (Special Provisions) Amendment Ordinance, 1980 (10 of 1980) is hereby repealed. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: The Kerala Relief Undertakings (Special Provisions) Amendment Act, 1980, is deemed to have come into force on November 21, 1980.
The duration for which a relief undertaking continues, as per sub-section (2) of section 3, impacts liabilities to pay tax under the Kerala General Sales-tax Act, 1963, and related proceedings.
Repealed the Kerala Relief Undertakings (Special Provisions) Amendment Ordinance, 1980.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be authorities dealing with tax and legal proceedings related to relief undertakings.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through existing legal and tax collection mechanisms, including courts and tribunals.

rights: The right to suspend tax payment liabilities and related proceedings for a period specified under the Act.
duties: Undertakings have a duty to comply with tax regulations if not covered by the suspension provisions.
Authorities have a duty to enforce tax collection and legal proceedings when applicable.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the provisions of the amended Act, particularly concerning tax liabilities of relief undertakings.

key_procedures: Declaration of a relief undertaking and its continuation period as per section 3.
Suspension of tax payment and related legal proceedings for liabilities incurred before the declaration.
Continuation of actions taken under the repealed Ordinance under the new Act.
administration: Implied to be the departments/authorities responsible for industrial relief, tax collection, and legal matters in Kerala.
important_notes: The Act has retrospective effect from November 21, 1980.
The amendment specifically addresses the period of 'five years' being changed to 'ten years' in relation to relief undertakings.
The Act clarifies the treatment of tax liabilities incurred by undertakings before they are declared as relief undertakings.

title: The Kerala Repealing and Saving Act, 2022
purpose: To repeal certain enactments which are obsolete or no longer needed.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Kerala and repeals specific laws listed in its Schedule. It also contains saving provisions to ensure that the repeal does not affect ongoing matters, acquired rights, or existing legal principles.

main_sections.description: Sub-section (1) states that the Act may be called the Kerala Repealing and Saving Act, 2022. Sub-section (2) states that the Act shall come into force at once.
This section states that the enactments specified in the Schedule to this Act are hereby repealed.

Sub-section (1) outlines that the repeal of scheduled enactments will not affect other enactments that have applied, incorporated, or referred to the repealed enactment. It also clarifies that the repeal will not affect anything already done or suffered, acquired rights or liabilities, remedies, proceedings, discharges of debts or penalties, indemnities granted, or past acts. It further states that the repeal will not affect legal principles, jurisdiction, practices, customs, or appointments that may have been derived from the repealed enactments, nor will it revive any jurisdiction, office, custom, liability, right, title, privilege, restriction, exemption, usage, practice, procedure, or other matter or thing not currently existing or in force. Sub-section (2) states that the provisions of section 4 of the Kerala Interpretation and General Clauses Act, 1125 (VII of 1125) are applicable to the repeal of any enactment under this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not specified in the provided text, typical for a repealing act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not applicable as the act's primary function is repeal and saving.

rights: Preservation of rights already acquired, accrued, or incurred prior to the repeal of scheduled enactments.
duties: The saving clause implies a duty to respect existing legal frameworks and remedies not directly impacted by the repeal.
obligations: Preservation of obligations already acquired, accrued, or incurred prior to the repeal of scheduled enactments.

administration: Law (Legislation-D) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act comes into force immediately upon enactment.
The saving clause is extensive, aiming to prevent unintended consequences from the repeal of existing laws.
Section 3(2) explicitly invokes the Kerala Interpretation and General Clauses Act for interpreting the repeal provisions.

title: THE KERALA REQUISITIONING AND ACQUISITION OF PROPERTY ACT, 1981
purpose: An Act to provide for the requisitioning and acquisition of property for public purposes, not being purposes of the Union. It is expedient to provide for the requisitioning and acquisition of property for public purposes, not being purposes of the Union.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala and concerns the requisitioning and acquisition of property for public purposes.

key_definitions.award: Any award of the District Collector made under section 8.
key_definitions.landlord: Means any person who for the time being is receiving or is entitled to receive, the rent of any premises, whether on his own account, or on account or on behalf or for the benefit, of any other person or as a trustee, guardian or receiver for any other person, or who would so receive the rent or be entitled to receive the rent if the premises were let to a tenant.
key_definitions.person interested: In relation to any property, includes all persons claiming, or entitled to claim, an interest in the compensation payable on account of the requisitioning or acquisition of that property under this Act;
key_definitions.premises: Means any building or part of a building and includes— (i) the garden, grounds and out-houses, if any, appertaining to such building or part of a building; (ii) any fittings affixed to such building or part of a building for the more beneficial enjoyment thereof; (e) "prescribed" means prescribed by rules made under this Act; (f) "property" means movable or immovable property of every kind and includes any rights in or over such property;
key_definitions.tenant: Means any person by whom or on whose account rent is payable for any premises and includes such sub-tenants and other persons as have derived title under the tenant for the time being in force.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Requisitioning and Acquisition of Property Act, 1981. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. It shall come into force at once.
Defines terms used in the Act, including 'award', 'landlord', 'person interested', 'premises', 'property', 'State', and 'tenant'.

Grants the Government power to requisition property if it is needed for any public purpose, not being a purpose of the Union. This power can be exercised by the owner or any other person by way of notice in writing. It also outlines procedures for requisitioning immovable property and deals with circumstances where the property is owned by the tenant or exclusively used for religious worship.

main_sections.section_title: Power to take possession of requisitioned property.
main_sections.description: Allows the Government, after notice under sub-section (1), to order and direct any person in possession of the requisitioned property to surrender or deliver possession thereof to the Government or any person duly authorised by them.

States that all property requisitioned under section 3 shall be used for such purposes as mentioned in the notice of requisition. It also outlines the Government's power to repair and recover costs if the owner fails to do so.

Details the process of releasing requisitioned property, stating that the Government may, at any time, release property from requisition. It also covers situations where the property is released, including exceptions for acquired property.

Empowers the Government to acquire requisitioned property if it is of the opinion that it is necessary for a public purpose. This involves calling upon the owner to show cause why the property should not be acquired and considering any objections. It also states that no property shall be acquired under this section except in the following circumstances: (a) where any works have, during the period of requisition, been constructed on, in or over, the property wholly or partially at the expense of the Government and the Government decide that the value of, or the right to use, such works should be secured or preserved for the purposes of Government; or (b) where the cost of restoring the property to its condition at the time of requisition would, in the determination of the Government, be excessive and the owner declines to accept release from requisition of the property without payment of compensation for so restoring the property.

main_sections.section_title: Principles and method of determining compensation in cases where immovable property is requisitioned or acquired.
main_sections.description: Outlines the principles and methods for determining compensation for requisitioned or acquired immovable property. It includes provisions for agreement, payment within two months of taking possession, and recourse to the District Collector. It also specifies the amount of compensation payable for requisitioning of immovable property, including recurring payments, expenses of vacating, and damages.

main_sections.section_title: Payment of compensation relating to immovable property.
main_sections.description: Deals with the payment of compensation for immovable property, specifying that it shall be paid by the Government to the person or persons entitled thereto in such manner and within such time as may be specified in the award. The amount of compensation payable under an award shall carry interest at the rate of six per cent per annum from the date on which it is specified as payable in the award.

main_sections.section_title: Appeals from awards, in respect of compensation.
main_sections.description: Provides for appeals from awards made by the District Collector in respect of compensation. Any person aggrieved by an award may prefer an appeal to the District Court within sixty days from the date of such award. The District Court may entertain an appeal after the expiry of the said period of sixty days, if it is satisfied that the appellant was prevented by sufficient cause from filing the appeal in time.

main_sections.section_title: Government and officers and authorities to have certain powers of civil courts.
main_sections.description: Grants the Government or any officer or authority empowered by the Government the powers of civil courts, including summoning and enforcing attendance, requiring production of documents, receiving evidence on affidavits, requisitioning public records, and issuing commissions for examination of witnesses.

main_sections.section_title: Principles and method of determining compensation in cases where movable property is requisitioned or acquired.
main_sections.description: Similar to section 8, this section outlines the principles and methods for determining compensation for movable property requisitioned or acquired, which shall be determined in accordance with the rules to be made in this behalf by the Government.

Grants any officer empowered in this behalf by the Government the power to enter and inspect any property for the purpose of determining whether and if so, in what manner, an order under this Act shall be made in relation to such property or with a view to securing compliance with an order made under this Act.

Specifies the procedure for serving notices and orders issued under the Act. It includes service in the Gazette, on an individual, or by delivery or tendering to the person or affixing at the last known residence or business premises. It also covers cases where personal service is not possible.

States that no person interested in any immovable property requisitioned or acquired under this Act shall, without the previous written consent of the Government or except for the purposes of the Government, disturb any easement over the property.
Empowers the Government to delegate its powers under the Act to any officer or authority subordinate to it.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith in pursuance of the provisions of this Act or any rule or order made thereunder.

main_sections.section_title: Bar of jurisdiction of civil courts.
main_sections.description: Bars the jurisdiction of civil courts in matters relating to awards and compensation, except as provided in section 10.
Prescribes penalties for offences under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Certain persons to be public servants.
main_sections.description: Declares certain persons acting under the Act as public servants.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: Rule for determining compensation for requisitioned or acquired immovable property (Section 8).
Rule for determining compensation for requisitioned or acquired movable property (Section 12).
Rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act (Section 22).

penalties: Penalty for offences (Section 20). (Specific amounts/durations not detailed in the provided excerpt).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government and any officer or authority empowered by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through powers of civil courts (Section 11), orders, notices, and potential prosecution for offences.

rights: Right to receive compensation for requisitioned or acquired property.
Right to appeal against compensation awards (Section 10).
Right to show cause against acquisition of property (Section 7).
duties: Duty to surrender or deliver possession of requisitioned property upon order (Section 4).
Duty to not disturb easements without consent (Section 15).
Duty to comply with notices and orders issued under the Act (Section 13, 14).
obligations: Obligation of the Government to determine compensation and pay it within a specified time.
Obligation for persons to facilitate inspection and provide information as required.

key_procedures: Procedure for requisitioning property: Issuance of notice in writing, stating the purpose (Section 3).
Procedure for taking possession of requisitioned property: Issuance of an order to surrender possession (Section 4).
Procedure for acquiring requisitioned property: Issuance of notice, opportunity to show cause, and final decision by the Government (Section 7).
Procedure for determining compensation: Through agreement or by the District Collector, with provisions for appeals to the District Court (Sections 8, 9, 10).
Procedure for serving notices and orders: Through publication in the Gazette, personal service, or affixing (Section 14).
administration: The Government of Kerala, and officers or authorities empowered by the Government.
important_notes: The Act is for public purposes and does not apply to purposes of the Union (Preamble, Section 3).
The Government's opinion is crucial for requisitioning property (Section 3).
Compensation for immovable property acquired may include costs of works constructed by the Government or if restoration cost is excessive (Section 7).
Interest is payable on compensation awards from the date specified in the award (Section 9).
Civil court jurisdiction is barred in certain matters, with appeals to the District Court specified (Section 19).

title: The Kerala Restriction On Transfer by and Restoration Of Lands To Scheduled Tribes Act, 1999
purpose: To provide for the restriction on transfer of land by and restoration of lands to Scheduled Tribes in the State of Kerala and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act applies to lands belonging to Scheduled Tribes in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Scheduled Tribe: As defined in clause (24) of article 366 of the Constitution of India.
key_definitions.Land: Includes all lands whether wet or dry, with or without buildings, and includes incorporeal rights on land.
key_definitions.Tribal: Means a member of a Scheduled Tribe.
key_definitions.Transfer: Includes sale, gift, exchange, mortgage, lease, usufructuary mortgage or any other mode of transfer of possession, but does not include a lease for a period not exceeding thirty years or a mortgage in favour of Government or a financial institution or a co-operative society.
key_definitions.Restoration: Means re-delivery of possession of land to the tribal owner thereof.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the date of commencement.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'Scheduled Tribe', 'land', 'tribal', 'transfer', and 'restoration'.

main_sections.section_title: Restriction on transfer of land by a tribal
main_sections.description: States that no tribal shall transfer his land to any person other than a tribal. It also provides exceptions for transfers to the Government or certain institutions.

main_sections.section_title: Restoration of lands transferred in contravention of section 3
main_sections.description: Deals with the restoration of lands that have been transferred in contravention of Section 3. It outlines the procedure for such restoration.
Gives the Government the power to resume lands from non-tribals under certain circumstances.

main_sections.section_title: Special provisions for restoration of lands
main_sections.description: Contains specific provisions related to the restoration of lands, including time limits and procedures.

main_sections.section_title: Protection to persons acting in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection to persons who have acted in good faith in accordance with the provisions of the Act.
Specifies the appellate authority and the procedure for filing appeals against orders passed under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Bar of jurisdiction of Civil Courts
main_sections.description: Ousts the jurisdiction of Civil Courts in matters falling under the purview of the Act.
Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of any existing law and savings for actions taken under such law.

important_rules: A tribal cannot transfer their land to a non-tribal.
Lands transferred illegally to non-tribals are liable for restoration to the original tribal owner.
The Government has the power to resume certain lands.
Strict time limits are prescribed for restoration proceedings.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Tahsildar, the Collector, and other authorities as may be prescribed.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the procedures laid down in the Act, including orders for restoration and resumption of land.

rights: Tribals have the right to their ancestral lands.
Tribals have the right to have their illegally transferred lands restored.
duties: Tribals have a duty not to transfer their lands to non-tribals.
Authorities have a duty to implement the provisions of the Act.

key_procedures: Application for restoration of land can be made by the tribal owner or any interested party.
The authority concerned shall conduct an inquiry and pass an order for restoration if the conditions are met.
Appeals against orders can be filed within a specified period.
administration: The Revenue Department of the Government of Kerala is responsible for the administration of this Act.
important_notes: The Act aims to protect tribal lands from alienation and ensure their restoration.
Certain transfers are permitted under specific conditions, such as leases not exceeding thirty years or mortgages to specified institutions.
The Act seeks to prevent the exploitation of tribal communities and safeguard their socio-economic interests.

title: The Kerala Restriction on Transfer by and Restoration of Lands to Scheduled Tribes Act, 1999
purpose: To provide for restricting the transfer of lands by members of Scheduled Tribes in the State of Kerala and for the restoration of possession of lands alienated by such members and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to all lands belonging to members of Scheduled Tribes in the State of Kerala. It also concerns the restoration of alienated lands to Scheduled Tribes.

key_definitions.competent authority: Refers to any land means the District Collector of the district in which the land is situate or any other officer appointed by the Government to be the competent authority for the purpose of this Act, for the areas in which the land is situate.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Revenue Divisional Officer: With reference to any land means the Revenue Divisional Officer having jurisdiction over the area in which that land is situate or any other officer appointed by the Government to perform the functions of the Revenue Divisional Officer under this Act, in the area in which that land is situate.
key_definitions.Scheduled Tribe: Means any of the Scheduled Tribes in relation to the State as specified in the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950.
key_definitions.transfer: Means the transfer of land made by any person belonging to the Scheduled Tribe of lands in his ownership and possession to a person other than a member of the Scheduled Tribe by way of sale, mortgage, lease, gift and includes 'vilapanayam' and 'unduruthi'.
key_definitions.vilapanayam: Means hypothecation of crops on payment of consideration or otherwise.
key_definitions.unduruthi: Means an assignment of the right to collect the usufructs available or anticipated to be available to any land during a specified term for a specified price.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its extent (whole of the State of Kerala), and commencement date (24th day of January, 1986).

Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'competent authority', 'land', 'prescribed', 'Revenue Divisional Officer', 'Scheduled Tribe', 'State', 'transfer', 'vilapanayam', and 'unduruthi'.

Clarifies certain aspects of the definitions, particularly regarding leases of land granted by the Administrator General, Official Trustee or Official Receiver; mortgages, pledges or hypothecations to the Government or a member of a Scheduled Tribe in favour of a Co-operative Society registered or deemed to be registered under the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969 or a corporation or a nationalised bank or any other financing agency.
Prohibits any transfer of land of a Scheduled Tribe, notwithstanding anything to the contrary in any other law, contract, custom or usage, or any judgment, decree or order of any court.

Declares certain transfers of land possessed, enjoyed or owned by a member of a Scheduled Tribe, made without the previous consent in writing of the competent authority, to be invalid. It also specifies that transfers made prior to the commencement of the Act, with certain exceptions, are deemed to be invalid. Further clarifies that no invalid transfer shall render any transfer of land possessed, enjoyed or owned by a member of a Scheduled Tribe to a person other than a member of a Scheduled Tribe effected during the 'vilapanayam' and 'unduruthi' period, which does not exceed two hectares, invalid.

States that notwithstanding anything contained in section 5 or any judgment, decree or order of any court or other authority, a member of a Scheduled Tribe who had effected any transfer of land, possessed, enjoyed or owned by him, prior to the 1st day of January, 1960, and where an application for restoration of land under section 6 of the Kerala Restriction of Transfer of Lands and Restoration of Allocated Lands Act, 1975 (31 of 1975) has been filed before the publication of this Act, and the possession or enjoyment thereof has not been restored to him, such transfer shall be validated provided the transferee has made eligible for the retention of said land under sub-section (2) of section 5, to the extent of equal extent of land by way of allotment from the Government.

Deals with the restoration of possession or enjoyment of land to a Scheduled Tribe member if the land was transferred under section 4 or 5 and the Scheduled Tribe has ceased to be in possession or enjoyment. It outlines the procedure for eligible persons to apply for restoration, including within one year from the publication of the Act. It also specifies the process if the land is in possession of a person who has procured such transfer.

Addresses the liability to pay an amount equal to the aggregate of the actual amount of consideration received by the member of the Scheduled Tribe at the time of transfer and an amount determined by the competent authority for improvements, if any, made after the transfer and before the restoration. It also states that no amount shall be payable if the transfer was effected on or after the commencement of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Government to provide grants for the payment
main_sections.description: States that the Government shall, subject to prescribed conditions, provide grants to eligible members of Scheduled Tribes who are liable to pay amounts under section 8.

States that notwithstanding anything contained in section 6 or in the Kerala Government Land Assignment Act, 1960 (30 of 1960) and the rules issued thereunder, the Government shall assign land to the landless families of the Scheduled Tribes in the State, to an extent not exceeding forty Ares of land in the district they reside within a period of two years from the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette, or such further period as may be specified by Government by notification in the Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of Scheduled Tribe Rehabilitation and Welfare Fund
main_sections.description: Establishes a 'Scheduled Tribe Rehabilitation and Welfare Fund' to be constituted by the Government and administered in such manner as may be prescribed. The fund is to be used for the construction of houses for the Tribal families and for other welfare measures.

Specifies that any person who, on or after the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette procures transfer of any land in contravention of the provisions of section 4, shall be punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees.

States that no Magistrate of the First Class shall try any offence punishable under this Act. It also specifies that in a case where transfer of land in contravention of section 4 has been made on or after the publication of this Act in the Gazette, the Revenue Divisional Officer shall file a complaint to the Magistrate having jurisdiction to the Special Court, as the case may be, for the trial of the offences under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Bar on proceedings against Scheduled Tribes under Chapter X of the Code of Criminal Procedure
main_sections.description: Prohibits any person claiming to be a member of a Scheduled Tribe or any other person on his behalf from applying to the Revenue Divisional Officer for the restoration of possession or enjoyment of any land under the provisions of this Act, for the time being being in force, no Magistrate shall have jurisdiction under Chapter X of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Central Act 2 of 1974) in respect of any dispute between that person and any other person claiming to be in possession or enjoyment of the said land.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of competent authority and Revenue Divisional Officer
main_sections.description: Confers powers on the competent authority and Revenue Divisional Officer under this Act, including the powers of a Civil court while trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, for summoning and enforcing attendance, requiring discovery and production of documents, and any other matter which may be prescribed. It also states that the decisions of the competent authority and the Revenue Divisional Officer shall have the force of a decree of a Civil court and shall be executed through the Civil court having jurisdiction over the area.
States that the Government shall provide for legal assistance to the members of Scheduled Tribes for the execution of the orders of the Competent Authority or of the Revenue Divisional Officer.

Empowers the Government to remove any difficulties arising in giving effect to the provisions of the Act. Any order made by the Government under this section shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly. It also specifies that no order under this section shall be made after the expiration of a period of two years from the publication of this Act in the Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Protects any person acting in good faith in pursuance of the provisions of the Act from any suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding.
States that the provisions of this Act are in addition to and not in derogation of any other law for the time being in force.

main_sections.section_title: Bar of jurisdiction of Civil Courts
main_sections.description: Bars the jurisdiction of Civil Courts in respect of any matter which the Revenue Divisional Officer or the competent authority is empowered to determine under this Act.
Grants the Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of this Act.
Repeals the Kerala Restriction of Transfer of Lands and Restoration of Allocated Lands Act, 1975, and provides for savings.

important_rules: Transfers of land by members of Scheduled Tribes must not be made without the previous written consent of the competent authority.

Any land granted by the Administrator General, Official Trustee or Official Receiver to a member of a Scheduled Tribe is subject to certain restrictions regarding lease, mortgage, pledge or hypothecation.
The Government shall provide grants for the payment of amounts due under section 8.
Landless families of Scheduled Tribes are to be assigned land not exceeding forty Ares.
The Government shall have the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.

penalties: Rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or fine which may extend to two thousand rupees for procuring transfer of land in contravention of section 4.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Competent Authority and Revenue Divisional Officer, with appeals to the competent authority and then to the Revenue Divisional Officer or Civil court.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through complaint to the Magistrate by the Revenue Divisional Officer, execution of orders as decrees of a Civil Court, and through legal assistance provided by the Government.

rights: Right to have land restored if it was transferred in contravention of the Act.
Right to legal assistance from the Government for execution of orders.
Right to receive land not exceeding forty Ares for landless families of Scheduled Tribes.
duties: Duty to obtain prior consent of the competent authority for any transfer of land.
Duty to comply with rules and regulations prescribed under the Act.
obligations: Obligation to pay an amount equal to the consideration received plus improvements, if any, for restoration of land.
Obligation to abide by the decisions of the competent authority and Revenue Divisional Officer.

key_procedures: Application for restoration of possession or enjoyment of land: Eligible persons can apply orally or in writing to the Revenue Divisional Office within one year from the publication of the Act or as prescribed by Government notification.
Enforcement of orders: Decisions of the competent authority and Revenue Divisional Officer have the force of a Civil Court decree and are executed through the Civil Court.
Making of rules: The Government can make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.
administration: The Government of Kerala, and specifically the competent authority and Revenue Divisional Officer.
important_notes: The Act is in English and has a translated version in Malayalam.
The Act came into force from 24th January, 1986.
The Act overrides certain provisions of other laws in case of conflict.
The Government has the power to remove difficulties for a period of two years from the publication of the Act.

title: THE KERALA RESTRICTION ON CUTTING AND DESTRUCTION OF VALUABLE TREES ACT, 1974
purpose: To restrict the cutting and destruction of certain valuable trees in private lands in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to valuable trees in private lands in the State of Kerala. Specific valuable trees include sandalwood, rosewood, and teak. Also applies to cultivation of plants like tea, coffee, cocoa, rubber, cardamom, and cinnamon.

key_definitions.authorised officer: An officer appointed by the Government, by notification in the Gazette, for the purposes of this Act.
key_definitions.owner: In relation to any land, includes a mortgagee or other person having right to possession and enjoyment of that land.
key_definitions.plantation: Means any land used principally for the cultivation of tea, coffee, cocoa, rubber, cardamom or cinnamon and includes lands interspersed within the boundaries of the area principally cultivated with such crops.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.valuable tree: Means sandalwood tree, rosewood tree or teak tree.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Restriction on Cutting and Destruction of Valuable Trees Act, 1974. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 22nd day of January, 1974.
Defines terms used in the Act, including 'authorised officer', 'owner', 'plantation', 'prescribed', and 'valuable tree'.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint such officers as they think fit to be authorised officers for the purposes of this Act and assign to them such local limits as they think fit.

main_sections.section_title: Restriction regarding cutting of valuable trees
main_sections.description: No owner of any land (including a plantation), and no person claiming under him or any other person, shall without the previous permission of the authorised officer, cut any sandalwood tree or rosewood tree from that land.

main_sections.section_title: Restriction regarding destruction of valuable trees
main_sections.description: No person shall, without the previous permission of the authorised officer, destroy any sandalwood tree or rosewood tree or plant of any such tree or do any act which diminishes the value of any such tree or plant. No person shall, without the previous permission of the authorised officer, destroy any teak tree or plant of such tree standing in a plantation or do any act which diminishes the value of any such tree or plant.

The Government, either suo motu or on application by any person aggrieved, can call for and examine the record of any order passed by the authorised officer under section 4 or section 5. Such order can be modified or annulled if it is not in conformity with the legality, propriety, or regularity of such order.

Whoever contravenes the provisions of section 4 or section 5 shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both. In case of a second or subsequent offence, imprisonment shall not be less than one month but may extend to six months and fine not less than one thousand rupees but may extend to five thousand rupees.

If an offence under this Act is committed by a company, every person who, at the time the offence was committed, was in charge of, and was responsible to, the company for the conduct of its business, shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly.

Authorised officers have powers similar to a civil court trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, including summoning and enforcing attendance, requiring discovery and production of documents, and receiving evidence on affidavit.

Authorised officers or specially authorised officers by the Government can enter upon any land (including a plantation) at all reasonable times to ascertain terms and conditions subject to which any permission has been granted under this Act.
No prosecution shall be instituted against any person without the sanction of the authorised officer.
No order of the Government or the authorised officer under this Act shall be liable to be questioned in any court of law.

No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against the Government or the authorised officer or any other person for anything which is in good faith done or purported to have been done under this Act or any rule made thereunder.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act. Rules can prescribe the procedure to be followed by the authorised officer before granting permission and any other matter that may be prescribed. Rules made under this section shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly as soon as may be after they are made.

If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, the Government may, by order, do anything not inconsistent with such provisions, which appears to them necessary for the purpose of removing the difficulty.

The Kerala Restriction on Cutting and Destruction of Valuable Trees Ordinance, 1974, is hereby repealed. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Valuable trees like sandalwood, rosewood, and teak cannot be cut from private land without prior permission from an authorised officer.
Valuable trees or plants cannot be destroyed, or their value diminished, without prior permission.
Rules made by the Government under the Act must be laid before the Legislative Assembly.
The Government can make rules regarding procedures for granting permission for cutting or destroying trees.

penalties: First offence: Imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to five hundred rupees, or both.
Second or subsequent offence: Imprisonment not less than one month and up to six months, and fine not less than one thousand rupees and up to five thousand rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Authorised Officers appointed by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers granted to authorised officers for granting permissions, inspection, and instituting prosecutions upon sanction.

rights: Right to apply for permission to cut or destroy valuable trees (implied).
duties: Duty not to cut or destroy valuable trees without prior permission.
Duty not to diminish the value of valuable trees or plants without prior permission.
