obligations: Companies and their responsible officers have an obligation to ensure compliance with the Act.
Individuals and companies have an obligation to be aware of and comply with rules and regulations made under the Act.

key_procedures: Application for permission: Individuals must apply to the authorised officer for permission to cut or destroy valuable trees.
Government review: The Government can review orders of authorised officers (suo motu or on application) and revise them if necessary.
Rule making: Government can make rules for the purposes of the Act, which must be laid before the Legislative Assembly.
Prosecution: Prosecutions can only be instituted with the sanction of the authorised officer.
administration: The Government of Kerala and its appointed Authorised Officers.

title: THE KERALA REVENUE CARD ACT, 1999
purpose: An Act to provide for the issue of Revenue Cards to individual families to enable the members of such families to use the same as an authoritative document in lieu of various certificates issued by the Government departments, local bodies and other institutions of the Government and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for the issue of Revenue Cards to individual families to enable the members of such families to use the same for availing of various concessions, benefits or grants sanctioned by the Government departments from time to time and to use the same as an authoritative document in lieu of the various certificates issued by the Government departments, local bodies and other institutions of the Government;
scope: Applies to the whole of Kerala.  It comes into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the gazette, appoint. Provided that different dates may be appointed for different areas and for different provisions of this Act, and any reference in any such provision to the commencement of this Act shall be construed as a reference to the coming into force of that provision.

key_definitions.alienation: Includes transfer of property by way of sale, mortgage, gift, settlement, lease, hypothecation or partition of a request under a will;
key_definitions.basic tax: Means the tax imposed under the provisions of the Kerala Land Tax Act, 1961 (13 of 1951);
key_definitions.Collector: Means collector of the district having jurisdiction over the area;
key_definitions.family: Means husband and wife, their parents and children living with and dependent on them;
key_definitions.financial assistance: Means assistance by way of loans, advances, guarantees or otherwise for any purposes, as may be prescribed;
key_definitions.Government land: Means any land the proprietary right of which vests in the Government;
key_definitions.land: Means Government land or registered land;
key_definitions.land holder: In relation to any land held by a cultivating tenant as defined in the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 (1 of 1964) such cultivating tenant; In relation to any land which has not been surveyed and is not held by a cultivating tenant referred to in sub-clause (i), the proprietor of such land; In relation to any other land, the registered holder for the time being of such land, and includes his legal representatives and assigns and any person who under any law for the time being in force is liable for the payment of public revenue due in respect of the land held by him;
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act;
key_definitions.registered holder of any land: Means the person in whose name the land in question is registered in the Government accounts of the village.
key_definitions.registered land: Means any land the proprietary right of which does not vest in the Government or local bodies;
key_definitions.register of Revenue Cards: Means the register of Revenue Cards maintained under section 3;
key_definitions.registering authority: Means the registering officer appointed under the Indian Registration Act, 1908 (Central Act 16 of 1908);
key_definitions.Tahsildar: Means the Tahsildar of the taluk having jurisdiction over the area.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Revenue Card Act, 1999. It extends to the whole of Kerala and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the gazette, appoint.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including alienation, basic tax, Collector, family, financial assistance, Government, Government land, land, land holder, prescribed, registered holder of any land, registered land, register of Revenue Cards, registering authority, and Tahsildar.

Mandates that every Tahsildar shall maintain a Register of Revenue Cards in his office containing prescribed particulars, including details of the person whose Revenue Card is issued, full names, date of birth of each member, place of birth and information as to whether each member is married or not, widow or if the widow of a soldier died in the war or whether a divorcee or a person working abroad, or a soldier or an ex-serviceman or a freedom fighter, receiving pension from the Central/State Government etc., and the occupation and annual income of each member, annual income of the family, residential and professional address and the community, caste and religion of the members etc. It also includes details of persons in the family, if any, those who are in military service or handicapped or mentally retarded, date on which his name was entered in the Register, details of the land and building possessed or owned by each member, details of the land held by each member, details of financial assistance received, details of encumbrances made so far, details of benefits received under social security schemes or pension schemes, and any other particulars as may be prescribed. The register shall be a permanent register and entries therein shall be made, corrected, renewed or modified only in accordance with the provisions of this Act.

A Village shall be the unit for the issue of Revenue Cards. The Tahsildar shall publish a notice in each village, and in each corporation/municipality/village panchayat offices in such manner as may be prescribed, informing the residents and registered holders of the land in that area for the preparation or updating of the Revenue Card Register and for the issue of Revenue Cards to each family and to such person, if any, who does not belong to the family. The notice shall contain the details and other records to be furnished and also specify the date within which and the place where such details and records have to be furnished and the application for the issue of Revenue Cards shall be submitted. As soon as may be after the information are collected and after making necessary enquiries the Tahsildar shall cause to make necessary entries in the Revenue Card Register maintained in his office. The Revenue Card shall be issued under the seal and signature of the Tahsildar on realising the fees at the rate of rupees fifteen for each Revenue Card. Provided that no fees shall be realised for the Revenue Card issued to families below the poverty line.

When a Revenue Card is irrecoverably lost, destroyed, damaged, mutilated or rendered useless, the Tahsildar may, on application, issue a duplicate Revenue Card to the applicant after making necessary enquiries as he may deem fit.

If a member included in any Revenue Card makes a request in the form and the manner as may be prescribed, either by reason of partition of the family or by reason of his residing separately after marriage, new card shall be issued by observing the conditions for issuing Revenue Cards and consequential changes shall be made in the Revenue Card Register and in other related cards.

main_sections.section_title: Entering details relating to registration, transfer etc. of land in the Revenue Card
main_sections.description: When a sale is registered or any right over land, including those by way of sale, gift, mortgage, lease, exchange, partition or settlement is transferred, the registering authority shall demand to produce before him the Revenue Card also, if Revenue Card has been issued in respect of such land. The Tahsildar, on receipt of a copy of the entries in the Revenue Card made by the Registering Authority, shall make necessary changes in the Revenue Card Register for that purpose and issue a new Revenue Card after sub-division, if necessary, within such time and on collection of such fees as may be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Acquisition of rights to be reported
main_sections.description: Any person acquiring by succession, survivorship, inheritance, purchase or otherwise or by a decree or order of a court, or any order of the Government or other authority any right to or over any land as owner shall report in writing his acquisition of such right to the Village Officer. This shall be done within one month from the date of such acquisition or within such period as may be prescribed and the Village Officer shall give a written acknowledgement or receipt of the report to the person making the report and the matter shall be intimated to the Tahsildar within one week and on receipt of the information, the Tahsildar shall make necessary changes in the concerned Revenue Card Register within one month from the date of receipt of such information. Provided that where the person acquiring the right is a minor or otherwise disqualified, his guardian or any other person holding charge of his property shall report it to the Village Officer. Provided further that any person acquiring the right by virtue of a registered document shall be exempted from the obligation to report to the Village Officer. The Tahsildar shall cause necessary changes to be made in the Register of Revenue Cards kept by him and also, incorporate necessary changes in the Revenue Card issued under section 4 or issue a new Revenue Card after sub-division.

main_sections.section_title: Other rightful benefits to be incorporated
main_sections.description: Details of other rightful benefits to be incorporated, including natural calamities, relief, allowances, non-statutory pensions, benefits under social security schemes etc. in the Register of Revenue Cards and in the Revenue Card, properly to facilitate the various agencies to accept extract of the relevant page of the Revenue Card Register in lieu of various certificates.

Application for certified copies of entries in the Register of Revenue Cards may be made to the Tahsildar and such copies may be issued by the Tahsildar in such manner and on collection of such fees as may be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Modification of entries in Revenue Cards
main_sections.description: When any individual whose name is included in the Revenue Card claims that any modification was required in respect of any entry in the Revenue Card already issued under section 4 either by reason of the death of any person, or by the reason of transfer of interest in the land or by reason of any other subsequent changes in circumstances, he shall make an application to the Tahsildar for the modification of the relevant entries in the Revenue Card. An application under sub-section (1) shall contain such particulars as may be prescribed and shall be accompanied by documents and other supporting materials as evidence. Before passing an order on an application under sub-section (1), the Tahsildar shall follow such procedure as may be prescribed and shall also give a reasonable opportunity of being heard to the parties concerned. If the Tahsildar feels that a modification, as applied for is necessary he shall pass an order accordingly and cause changes to be made in the Revenue Cards. The Tahsildar shall reject the application if he feels that no changes are necessary after noting the reasons for rejection. An order under clause (a) or (b) of this sub-section shall contain the reasons for such order and shall be communicated to the concerned parties in such manner and within such period as may be prescribed. The entries regarding the annual income of each member and the annual income of the family included in each Revenue Card shall be renewed annually.

Any person whose rights or details are required to be entered in the Revenue Card under this Act shall be bound, on the requisition of the Tahsildar engaged in preparing or modifying the entries in the Revenue Cards to furnish or produce before him the relevant information or documents for inspection within such time as may be specified in such requisition or within such further time as the Tahsildar may in his discretion allow. All such information furnished or produced shall be within his knowledge or possession or under his authority. Where any information is furnished or any document is produced in accordance with the requisition under sub-section (1) the Tahsildar or the Officer authorised by him in this behalf shall give a written acknowledgement thereof to the person producing or furnishing the same and shall endorse on such document a note under his signature stating the fact of its production and the date thereof.

Any person aggrieved by an order of the Tahsildar under any of the provisions of this Act, may file an appeal before such authority and within such period as may be prescribed. The decision of such authority on such appeal under sub-section (1) shall be final.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for failure to furnish information
main_sections.description: Any person who wilfully defaults in producing any document required under section 4 or section 12 within the time specified in the notice or requisition under those sections or within such further time, if any, allowed by the Tahsildar under those sections shall be punishable with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees.

If any person who is required to furnish any information under this Act, furnishes any information which he knows or has reason to believe to be false, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months or with fine which may extend to three thousand rupees or with both.
No court shall take cognizance of any offence punishable under this Act except on a complaint made by an officer authorised in this behalf by the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: No suit or other proceedings shall lie against any officer or authority for anything which is done or purports to be done in good faith under this Act or the rules made thereunder.
Nothing contained in this Act shall apply to any land owned by the Central Government or the State Government or any local authority.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the State Government to direct that the Revenue Card may be accepted in lieu of various certificates issued by Government departments etc.
main_sections.description: The State Government may, by notification in the Gazette, direct that the entries in the Revenue Card issued under this Act may be used by the holder of such card as an authoritative document in lieu of the various certificates issued by the Government departments, local bodies and other institutions of the Government specified therein. When a notification under sub-section (1) is issued the officers of the Government department or the local bodies concerned shall accept the entries in the card as an authoritative document in lieu of the various certificates mentioned in such notification. A copy of the entries in the Revenue Card as certified in the manner prescribed shall be considered as a document in lieu of any certificate specified in sub-section (1).
The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make rules to carry out the purposes of this Act.

If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, the Government may, as occasion may require, by order published in the Gazette, do anything which appears to be necessary for removing the difficulty: Provided that no such order shall be made after the expiry of a period of two years from the commencement of this Act.
The provisions of this Act shall be in addition to, and not in derogation of, the provisions of any other law for the time being in force.

important_rules: Tahsildars shall maintain a Register of Revenue Cards containing prescribed particulars.
Revenue Cards shall be issued by the Tahsildar on payment of fees, except for families below the poverty line.
Persons acquiring rights in land must report such acquisition to the Village Officer.
Entries in Revenue Cards regarding annual income shall be renewed annually.
Any person whose rights or details are required for the Revenue Card must furnish information upon requisition by the Tahsildar.

penalties: Fine up to five hundred rupees for wilful default in producing documents required under sections 4 or 12.
Imprisonment up to three months or fine up to three thousand rupees, or both, for furnishing false information.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Tahsildar and officers authorised by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through court proceedings upon complaint made by an authorised officer.

rights: Right to use Revenue Card as an authoritative document in lieu of various certificates.
Right to appeal against orders of the Tahsildar.
duties: Duty to report acquisition of land rights.
Duty to furnish information or produce documents when required by the Tahsildar.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder.

key_procedures: Application for Revenue Card: Publish notice, collect details, make entries in the Register, issue card upon payment of fees.
Reporting land acquisition: Report to Village Officer within one month, Tahsildar makes necessary changes.
Modifying entries: Apply to Tahsildar, follow prescribed procedure, opportunity to be heard.
Appeals: File appeal to prescribed authority within a prescribed period.
administration: State Government
important_notes: The Act extends to the whole of Kerala.
Revenue Cards can be used as an authoritative document in lieu of various certificates issued by Government departments, local bodies, and other institutions.
No suit or proceedings shall lie against officers acting in good faith under the Act.
The Act does not apply to land owned by Central Government, State Government, or any local authority.
The Government has the power to remove difficulties in implementing the Act within two years of its commencement.

title: THE KERALA REVENUE RECOVERY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2007
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Revenue Recovery Act, 1968 for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: The act amends the Kerala Revenue Recovery Act, 1968. It applies to all matters governed by the principal Act, with specific provisions for class or classes of institutions of autonomous bodies and for aggrieved persons. The Repeal and Saving section also addresses previous enactments and actions taken under them.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Revenue Recovery (Amendment) Act, 2007. Section 3 of this Act shall be deemed to have come into force on the 27th day of February, 1980 and the remaining provisions shall be deemed to have come into force on the 12th day of December, 2005.

Amends section 69 of the Kerala Revenue Recovery Act, 1968. It substitutes specific phrases in sub-section (2) and (5) of section 69, particularly regarding 'the demand arose', 'the defaulter or his surety resides or holds property', and 'when a certificate is received under sub-section (1) or sub-section (4)' and 'a requisition under sub-section (2)' and 'the case may be, is received'. It also substitutes 'figure, brackets or sub-brackets' with 'words, figures and brackets'.

Amends section 71 of the principal Act. It provides that specified institution or classes of institutions of autonomous bodies, in case they are able to pay collection charges for the recovery of amounts, may do so at such rate and in such manner as prescribed by the Government.

Amends section 72 of the principle Act. It omits 'save where fraud alleged' in the marginal heading. The existing section 72 is re-numbered as sub-section (1) of that section. It introduces new provisions for re-numbering and substitution of words in clause (i) of sub-section (1) where 'Board of Revenue' is substituted with 'Commissioner of Land Revenue'. It also specifies that 'the proviso shall be omitted' and sub-section (2) is omitted. Further, it states that no civil court shall have jurisdiction to settle, decide or deal with any question or to determine any matter which is by or under this Act required to be settled or dealt with or to be determined by the Government, or the Commissioner of Land Revenue or the Collector or any officer of authority under this Act.

Amends section 81 of the principal Act. Sub-section (1) is substituted. It states that subject to the provisions contained in section 72, any person aggrieved by any decision or order passed or proceedings taken under this Act for arrears due or alleged to be due from him, may file a suit against the Government in a civil court of competent jurisdiction. It also clarifies that the person aggrieved has availed himself of the remedies for redressing his grievances provided in this Act. The proviso to sub-section (2) substitutes 'Board of Revenue' with 'Commissioner of Land Revenue'.
Amends section 83 of the principal Act. In the marginal heading and in sub-sections (1), (2) and (3), 'Board of Revenue' is substituted with 'Commissioner of Land Revenue'.

Repeals the Kerala Revenue Recovery (Amendment) Ordinance, 2007 (51 of 2007). Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act, as amended by the said Ordinance, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act, as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Institutions of autonomous bodies may pay collection charges for recovery of amounts at rates and in manners prescribed by the Government.
Persons aggrieved by decisions or orders under the Act, concerning arrears, may file a suit against the Government in a civil court, provided they have exhausted remedies under the Act.

No civil court has jurisdiction to decide matters required to be determined by the Government, Commissioner of Land Revenue, Collector, or other authority under the Act, except in cases not covered by section 72.
Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are deemed to have been taken under the amended Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government, Commissioner of Land Revenue, Collector, or any officer of authority under this Act
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings and civil court jurisdiction as prescribed by the Act.

rights: Right of aggrieved persons to seek remedies for grievances.
Right to file a suit in civil court for arrears due or alleged to be due, after exhausting remedies under the Act.
duties: Duty to pay collection charges for recovery of amounts by institutions of autonomous bodies.
Duty to comply with decisions and orders issued by the Government, Commissioner of Land Revenue, Collector, or other authorities under the Act.
obligations: Obligation for individuals or entities to adhere to the revenue recovery procedures as outlined in the principal Act and its amendments.

key_procedures: Amendment of specific sections (69, 71, 72, 81, 83) of the Kerala Revenue Recovery Act, 1968, to alter existing provisions.
Substitution of specific terms like 'Board of Revenue' with 'Commissioner of Land Revenue' in relevant sections.
Re-numbering of existing sections and sub-sections.
Omission of certain provisos and sub-sections.
Repeal of the Kerala Revenue Recovery (Amendment) Ordinance, 2007, with a saving clause for actions taken under it.
administration: The administration of the Act would involve the Board of Revenue (now Commissioner of Land Revenue), Collector, and other relevant government officials as per the principal Act and its amendments.
important_notes: Certain provisions of the Act are deemed to have come into force retrospectively (February 27, 1980, and December 12, 2005).
Specific substitutions of terms are made, changing the nomenclature of authorities involved.
The act clarifies the jurisdiction of civil courts in relation to matters determined by revenue authorities.
The Repeal and Saving clause ensures continuity of legal actions and decisions made under the previous Ordinance.

title: The Kerala Revenue Recovery Act, 1968
purpose: To consolidate and amend the laws relating to the recovery of arrears of public revenue in the State of Kerala.
scope: The Act applies to the entire State of Kerala and governs the recovery of arrears of public revenue, including land revenue. It also applies to certain other dues to the Government as may be specified by the Government.

key_definitions.arrear of public revenue due on land: Means the whole or any portion of any "kist" or "instalment" of such revenue not paid on the day on which it falls due according to the 'kistbandy' or any engagement or usage, and includes any "kist" or instalment of such revenue which has been forfeited or the payment of which has been postponed.
key_definitions.authorised officer: means the officer authorised to exercise the powers and perform the functions of the Collector under this Act.
key_definitions.Collector: means the District Collector or any other officer appointed by the Government by name or by virtue of his office to exercise the powers and perform the functions of a Collector under this Act.
key_definitions.land revenue: means the revenue charged on land and includes all other "taxes", "fees" and "cesses" on land, whether charged on land or not, and all "cesses" or other dues payable to the Government on account of water used for purposes of irrigation.
key_definitions.defaulter: means a person from whom an arrear of public revenue due on land is due, and includes a person who is responsible as surety for the payment of any such arrear.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as The Kerala Revenue Recovery Act, 1968, its extent to the whole of the State of Kerala, and its commencement by notification in the Gazette.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'arrear of public revenue due on land', 'authorised officer', 'Collector', 'land revenue', 'defaulter', and 'movable property'.

main_sections.section_title: Charge and security for public revenue
main_sections.description: Declares that the public revenue due on land is a charge on the land, and the buildings upon it, and the produce thereof.

main_sections.section_title: Revenue to be paid in time to the Collector or the Officer authorised
main_sections.description: Mandates that revenue is to be paid to the Collector or the authorised officer, with provisions for payment to land-holders in specific circumstances.

main_sections.section_title: Arrears of public revenue due on land how recovered
main_sections.description: Outlines the methods for recovering arrears of public revenue due on land, including attachment and sale of defaulter's property and arrest and detention.

main_sections.section_title: Interest on arrears of public revenue due on land
main_sections.description: Specifies that interest at the rate of six per cent per annum will be levied on arrears of public revenue due on land, as notified by the Government.
Requires the defaulter or the authorised officer to furnish the person employed to make the attachment with a demand in writing signed by him, specifying the amount due.

main_sections.section_title: Attachment of movable property (other than growing crops and ungathered products) in the possession of defaulter
main_sections.description: Details the procedure for attaching movable property, excluding growing crops and ungathered products, from the defaulter's possession. It includes steps like delivering a copy of the demand and an inventory to the defaulter, and proclaiming the attachment publicly.

main_sections.section_title: Attachment not to be excessive and certain articles not to be attached
main_sections.description: Prohibits excessive attachment and lists specific articles that cannot be attached, including wearing apparel, ornaments, minimum required for religious usage, implements of husbandry, tools of artisans, and certain notified items.
Stipulates that attachment by seizure must be made after sunrise and before sunset, and not otherwise.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure when defaulter neglects to pay after attachment
main_sections.description: Describes the procedure when the defaulter fails to pay after attachment, including the authorized officer's power to sell the attached property.

Specifies the provisions for the sale of attached property, including the sale of movable property as per subsections (2) and (3), and property attached as stock-in-trade. It also details the procedure for the sale of stock-in-trade.
States that the officer authorized to conduct the sale shall be the Collector or an authorized officer.
Details the process of conducting the sale of attached property, including public auction and adherence to specific rules.
Requires the purchase money to be paid at the time of sale or within a specified period.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure when the defaulter tenders payment of arrear after attachment but before sale of property
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure when the defaulter pays the arrears after attachment but before the sale of the property.

main_sections.section_title: Attachment and sale or disposal otherwise of growing crops or ungathered products
main_sections.description: Details the attachment, sale, or disposal of growing crops and ungathered products.

main_sections.section_title: Attached cattle or goods not to be used
main_sections.description: Prohibits the use of attached cattle or goods.
Covers the attachment of debts, shares, and other negotiable instruments.
Details the attachment of decrees.

main_sections.section_title: Attachment of share in movable property
main_sections.description: Covers the attachment of a share in movable property.
Details the attachment of negotiable instruments.

main_sections.section_title: Attachment of property in custody of court or public officer
main_sections.description: Deals with the attachment of property in the custody of a court or public officer.
Covers the attachment of partnership property.
Details the attachment of rents.

main_sections.section_title: Sale of negotiable instruments and shares in corporation
main_sections.description: Specifies the procedure for the sale of negotiable instruments and shares in a corporation.

main_sections.section_title: Order for payment of coin or currency notes
main_sections.description: Provides for orders for the payment of coin or currency notes.

main_sections.section_title: Restoration of property in cases of fraudulent conveyances
main_sections.description: Deals with the restoration of property in cases of fraudulent conveyances.

main_sections.section_title: Claims to property attached and sold
main_sections.description: Covers claims to property that has been attached and sold.

main_sections.section_title: Restoration of property forcibly or clandestinely taken away
main_sections.description: Deals with the restoration of property that has been forcibly or clandestinely taken away.

main_sections.section_title: Power to enter dwelling house, etc.
main_sections.description: Grants the power to enter dwelling houses for the purpose of attachment.

main_sections.section_title: Removal of property from apartments of women
main_sections.description: Specifies procedures for removing property from apartments of women, with protective measures.
Provides punishment for unlawful entry.

main_sections.section_title: Demand to be served prior to attachment of land
main_sections.description: Requires a demand notice to be served before the attachment of land.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure when defaulter neglects to pay
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure when the defaulter neglects to pay after the demand notice.
Describes the mode of attachment of land.
Covers the management of attached property.
Details the appointment of an agent for managing attached property.
Requires notice to be given upon the assumption of management of attached property.
Specifies the duties of the appointed agent.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of agent to suit or prosecution
main_sections.description: Makes the agent liable to suit or prosecution for misconduct.

main_sections.section_title: Surplus to go to the defaulter
main_sections.description: States that any surplus from the sale of attached property after satisfying the arrears will be returned to the defaulter.

main_sections.section_title: Attachment and assumption of management of business
main_sections.description: Deals with the attachment and assumption of management of a business.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of engagements and transfers by the defaulter
main_sections.description: Clarifies the effect of engagements and transfers made by the defaulter.
Outlines the procedure for tenants to make payments to the attaching officer.

main_sections.section_title: Claim for release of attachment by third parties
main_sections.description: Provides for claims for the release of attachment by third parties.

main_sections.section_title: Persons interested in land may obtain release from attachment
main_sections.description: Allows persons interested in the land to obtain release from attachment by paying the arrears.

main_sections.section_title: Judgment-creditor of the defaulter may pay arrears
main_sections.description: Permits a judgment-creditor of the defaulter to pay the arrears to prevent attachment.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure for sale of immovable property
main_sections.description: Details the procedure for the sale of immovable property.
Allows the Government to bid on its own behalf at sales.
Allows tender of arrears before the sale of property.

main_sections.section_title: Application to set aside sale on ground of material irregularity, mistake, etc.
main_sections.description: Provides for applications to set aside a sale due to material irregularity, mistake, or fraud.

main_sections.section_title: Application to set aside sale on ground of material irregularity, mistake, etc.
main_sections.description: Allows applications to set aside a sale on the ground of material irregularity, mistake, or fraud.

main_sections.section_title: Order confirming or setting aside sale
main_sections.description: Deals with the order confirming or setting aside the sale.

main_sections.section_title: Refund of deposit or purchase money when sale set aside
main_sections.description: Specifies refund procedures when a sale is set aside.

main_sections.section_title: On confirmation purchaser's name to be registered
main_sections.description: Requires the purchaser's name to be registered upon confirmation of sale.

main_sections.section_title: Name and title of such purchaser to be published
main_sections.description: Mandates the publication of the purchaser's name and title.
Outlines the process for delivering possession to the purchaser.

main_sections.section_title: Contracts and payments binding on purchaser
main_sections.description: Clarifies that existing contracts and payments are binding on the purchaser.

main_sections.section_title: Sale to be free of all encumbrances
main_sections.description: States that the sale of property is free from all encumbrances.

main_sections.section_title: Recovery of arrears due to defaulter on day of sale
main_sections.description: Deals with the recovery of arrears due to the defaulter on the day of sale.
Covers the sale of land for arrears.

main_sections.section_title: Sale may be postponed on tender of security
main_sections.description: Allows for postponement of sale upon tender of security.

main_sections.section_title: Apportionment of assessment when part only of a single property is sold
main_sections.description: Provides for the apportionment of assessment when only a part of a property is sold.

main_sections.section_title: Arrest in case of wilful and fraudulent non-payment of arrears
main_sections.description: Allows for the arrest of a defaulter in cases of wilful and fraudulent non-payment of arrears.
Details the procedure to be followed in case of arrest.

main_sections.section_title: Mode of enforcing payment by sureties
main_sections.description: Explains the mode of enforcing payment by sureties.

main_sections.section_title: Application of the Act for the recovery of certain other dues to Government
main_sections.description: Allows for the application of the Act for the recovery of other specified Government dues.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure for recovery of public revenue due on land when defaulter or surety resides outside the District and for the recovery of dues other than public revenue due on land
main_sections.description: Outlines procedures for recovery when defaulters/sureties are outside the district and for recovery of dues other than land revenue.
Allows for payment under protest.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to declare the Act applicable to any institution
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to declare the Act applicable to any institution.

main_sections.section_title: General bar to jurisdiction of Civil Courts save where fraud alleged
main_sections.description: Restricts the jurisdiction of Civil Courts, except in cases of alleged fraud.

main_sections.section_title: Delegation of powers of the Collector
main_sections.description: Allows the Collector to delegate powers.
Specifies rules for the service of notices.

main_sections.section_title: Mode of publication of notices, etc.
main_sections.description: Details the modes of publication of notices.

main_sections.section_title: Process servers to be paid batta
main_sections.description: Ensures process servers are paid their allowances (batta).

main_sections.section_title: Interest and charges recoverable as arrears
main_sections.description: States that interest and charges are recoverable as arrears.

main_sections.section_title: Liability for expenses of countermanded sale
main_sections.description: Fixes liability for expenses incurred due to a countermanded sale.

main_sections.section_title: Cognizance of questions relating to rate of public revenue
main_sections.description: Deals with cognizance of questions related to the rate of public revenue.

main_sections.section_title: Attachment of salaries and debts of defaulters
main_sections.description: Allows for the attachment of salaries and debts of defaulters.
Preserves the right to sue.

main_sections.section_title: Suits or prosecutions by persons aggrieved by proceedings
main_sections.description: Allows persons aggrieved by proceedings to file suits or prosecutions.

main_sections.section_title: Power of revision of Board of Revenue and Government
main_sections.description: Grants revisionary powers to the Board of Revenue and the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Who shall not bid at revenue sales
main_sections.description: Specifies persons who are prohibited from bidding at revenue sales.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for fraudulent conveyance of property to prevent attachment or for forcibly taking away property attached
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for fraudulent conveyance of property to avoid attachment or for forcibly taking away attached property.
Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Repeals previous laws on the subject.

important_rules: Public revenue due on land is a charge on the land and its produce.
Arrears of public revenue due on land shall bear interest at the rate of six per cent per annum.
Attachment by seizure must be made after sunrise and before sunset.
Attachment of property shall not be excessive, and certain articles are exempt from attachment.
Sales of attached property must be conducted publicly, and the defaulter has the right to pay arrears before the sale.
Persons aggrieved by proceedings may file suits or prosecutions, subject to certain limitations.

penalties: Penalty for fraudulent conveyance of property to prevent attachment or for forcibly taking away property attached (Section 85).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Collector, Authorized Officers, and the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through attachment and sale of movable and immovable property, arrest and detention of defaulters, assumption of management of property and businesses, and other coercive measures.

rights: Right of the defaulter to pay arrears before sale to prevent it.
Right of persons interested in land to obtain release from attachment.
Right to seek remedy in civil courts in cases of alleged fraud.
Right to sue for damages or prosecute those who commit illegal acts under the Act.
duties: Duty to pay public revenue on time.
Duty to comply with notices and orders issued under the Act.
Duty of the defaulter to provide a demand in writing signed by him to the person employed to make the attachment.
obligations: Obligation to pay arrears of revenue when demanded.
Obligation of the Government to notify applicable institutions under the Act.
Obligation of purchasers at revenue sales to register their names and have them published.

key_procedures: Demand Notice: Service of a written demand notice on the defaulter prior to attachment.
Attachment of Property: Seizure of movable or immovable property belonging to the defaulter.
Sale of Property: Public auction of attached property to recover arrears.
Arrest and Detention: In cases of wilful and fraudulent non-payment, the defaulter can be arrested and detained.
Recovery of Dues: Procedures for recovering arrears and other dues owed to the Government, including those from outside the district.
administration: The Act is administered by the Collector and other officers authorized by the Government, with oversight and rule-making powers vested in the Government and the Board of Revenue.
important_notes: The Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary, No. 111 dated 25th May, 1968.
Certain provisions were substituted by Act 13 of 1985.
The jurisdiction of Civil Courts is generally barred, except in cases involving allegations of fraud.
The Act allows for the recovery of certain other dues to the Government besides land revenue.

title: THE KERALA REVENUE RECOVERY LAWS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1964
purpose: To amend the Madras Revenue Recovery Act, 1864, as in force in the Malabar area of Kerala and the Travancore-Cochin Revenue Recovery Act, 1951.
scope: Applies to the Madras Revenue Recovery Act, 1864, as in force in the Malabar area of Kerala, and the Travancore-Cochin Revenue Recovery Act, 1951.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Revenue Recovery Laws (Amendment) Act, 1964, and that Sections 2 and 5 shall come into force at once; Section 3 shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of November, 1956; and Sections 3 and 4 shall be deemed to have come into force on the 22nd day of May, 1951.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 36A of Madras Act II of 1864
main_sections.description: Substitutes a new section 36A in the Madras Revenue Recovery Act, 1864, concerning postponement of sale and purchase by Government when property is put up for sale for arrears of public revenue. It details conditions under which a sale may be postponed and how the property may be purchased by the Government if no bid is received or if the highest bid is insufficient to cover the arrears. It also clarifies that the provisions of clauses (3), (4) and (5) of section 36 shall not apply to cases where immovable property is purchased on account of the Government under this section.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new section 36A in Travancore-Cochin Act VII of 1951
main_sections.description: Inserts a new section 36A into the Travancore-Cochin Revenue Recovery Act, 1951, which mirrors the provisions of the substituted section 36A of the Madras Revenue Recovery Act, 1864, regarding the postponement of sale and purchase by Government for arrears of public revenue.
Amends section 63 of the Travancore-Cochin Act, providing that nothing in that section shall be deemed to prohibit an officer of the Government from bidding on behalf of the Government.

Repeals the Revenue Recovery Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1964 (Kerala Ordinance No. 3 of 1964). It also states that notwithstanding such repeal, nothing done or any action taken under the Madras Revenue Recovery Act, 1864, as amended by this Act, shall be in force on the date on which such thing were done or action was taken.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Officer of the Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Sale and purchase of property for arrears of public revenue.

rights: Government's right to purchase property for arrears of public revenue.
obligations: Officers of the Government are prohibited from bidding on behalf of the Government under section 63 of the Travancore-Cochin Act, unless otherwise provided by this amendment.

key_procedures: Postponement of sale and purchase by Government for arrears of public revenue: If property is put up for sale and there is no bid or the highest bid is insufficient to cover the arrears, the sale shall be postponed, and the property may be purchased by the Government at the highest amount bid.
administration: Kerala State
important_notes: The amendment aims to address situations where immovable property is purchased on account of the Government under specific sections of the Acts.

title: THE KERALA REVOCATION OF ARBITRATION CLAUSES AND REOPENING OF AWARDS ACT, 1998
purpose: This act is enacted to provide for the revocation of arbitration clauses and the reopening of awards and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.arbitration clause: Any clause in an agreement providing for the reference of disputes to arbitration.
key_definitions.award: An award made by an arbitrator or arbitrators.

main_sections.description: This section provides for the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and the date of its commencement.
This section defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'arbitration clause', 'award', 'court', and 'prescribed'.
This section deals with the power of the court to revoke arbitration clauses in certain circumstances.
This section outlines the conditions under which an award can be reopened by the court.
This section grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
This section repeals the Arbitration Act, 1940, and other relevant laws, with savings for certain cases.
This section empowers the Government to remove any difficulties in the application of the provisions of this Act.
This section specifically repeals the Kerala Revocation of Arbitration Clauses and Reopening of Awards Ordinance, 1998.

important_rules: Rule: A court may revoke an arbitration clause if it finds that the clause is unreasonable or unjust.
Rule: An award can be reopened if it is found to be fraudulent, corrupt, or misconducted.
Rule: The court has the discretion to reopen an award in the interests of justice.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through judicial proceedings initiated under the Act.

rights: Right to have an arbitration clause revoked if it is found to be unreasonable or unjust.
Right to have an award reopened under specified conditions.

key_procedures: Procedure: To revoke an arbitration clause, an application must be filed in the appropriate court.
Procedure: To reopen an award, an application must be made to the court within the prescribed time limit, supported by relevant grounds.
administration: The State Government of Kerala likely oversees the administration of this Act, with courts being the primary enforcers.
important_notes: The Act aims to address situations where arbitration clauses or awards have led to unfair outcomes.
It provides a mechanism for judicial intervention in arbitration matters when necessary.
The Act repeals the previous Ordinance and brings into effect the provisions related to revocation and reopening.

title: The Kerala Road Fund Act, 2001
purpose: An Act to provide for the establishment of a Fund for investments in the transport facility projects in the State, to constitute a Board for the administration of the said Fund and to monitor and supervise the activities financed from the Fund.
scope: Applies to transport facility projects in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Board: Kerala Road Fund Board constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.bridge: Means a bridge with permanent structure, including approach and exit roads, guide funds and protective works thereto or a bridge with temporary structure of ferry services, as the case may be, and includes a bridge across railway lines, roads or waterways, underpass or overbridge.
key_definitions.collecting agent: Means any person entrusted with management and collection of user fee by any concessionaire, his agent, servant or sub-contractors entitled to collect user fees;
key_definitions.concession agreement: Means a tripartite agreement among the concessionaire, the Board and a Government agency or a statutory body specifically authorised by Government for the purpose whereby the concessionaire undertakes to finance, construct, maintain or operate a transport facility in accordance with the provisions of this Act
key_definitions.concessionaire: Means a party with which a concession agreement is entered into by the Board and a Government agency or a statutory body specifically authorised by Government for the purpose;
key_definitions.construction: Includes new construction, reconstruction, rehabilitation, repair and maintenance;
key_definitions.development cost: Means initial cost incurred on the development of any transport facility project before it is offered to a person for implementation and includes cost incurred on data collection, pre-feasibility studies or feasibility studies;
key_definitions.escrow account: Means a bank account in which cash is to be deposited or from which cash is to be withdrawn in the manner as may be specified in the concession agreement;
key_definitions.executive committee: Means the executive committee of the Board;
key_definitions.Fund: Means the Kerala Road Fund established under section 6;
key_definitions.government agency: Means a corporation owned or controlled by the Government or a company established by the Government for the purpose of construction or maintenance of roads or bridges or a highway authority;
key_definitions.highway authority: Means the highway authority appointed under section 4 of the Kerala Highway Protection Act, 1999 (6 of 2000);
key_definitions.Member Secretary of the Board: Means the Member Secretary of the Board;
key_definitions.motor vehicle: Means any mechanically propelled vehicle adapted for use upon roads, whether the power of propulsion is transmitted thereto from any external or internal source and includes a chassis to which the body has not been attached and a trailer;
key_definitions.owner: Includes, where the person in possession of a vehicle is a minor, the guardian of such minor and in relation to a vehicle which is the subject of a hire purchase agreement, the person in possession of the vehicle under that agreement;
key_definitions.person: Includes a body corporate, a company, a firm or an association of individuals whether incorporated or not;
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act;
key_definitions.project management agency: Means the Roads and Bridges Development Corporation of Kerala Ltd. established by the Government under the Companies Act, 1956 (Central Act 1 of 1956);
key_definitions.regulations: Means regulations made by the Board under this Act;
key_definitions.road: Means any road, way or land declared as a highway under section 3 of the Kerala Highway Protection Act, 1999 (6 of 2000), and includes any land acquired or demarcated for construction of a road;
key_definitions.rules: Means rules made by the Government under this Act;
key_definitions.section of road or bridge: Means a continuous length of road and or bridge as notified in the Government in the Gazette on which user fee shall be charged;
key_definitions.senior loan: Means a loan in respect of which a claim on assets is prior to the claim on assets in respect of other loan and which is specified as such in an agreement for providing finance;
key_definitions.subordinate loan: Means a loan in respect of which a claim on assets is subsequent to the claim on the assets in respect of another loan and which is specified as such in an agreement for providing finance;
key_definitions.subsidy: Means financial assistance in cash or kind provided by the Fund;
key_definitions.transport facility: Means, depending upon the case, a bridge or a tunnel including approach and exit roads thereto or a road or any section of bridge or tunnel or a specified combination of all or some of them;
key_definitions.using the transport facility: Means, depending upon the case, passing over a bridge or through a tunnel including approach and exit roads thereto or passing through a road or any section of bridge or tunnel or road or a specified combination of all or some of them;
key_definitions.user fee: Means the user fee collected in accordance with the provisions of this Act.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Road Fund Act, 2001, and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 7th day of September, 2001.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'bridge', 'collecting agent', 'concession agreement', 'concessionaire', 'construction', 'development cost', 'escrow account', 'executive committee', 'Fund', 'Government', 'government agency', 'highway authority', 'Member Secretary of the Board', 'motor vehicle', 'owner', 'person', 'prescribed', 'project management agency', 'regulations', 'road', 'rules', 'section of road or bridge', 'senior loan', 'State', 'subordinate loan', 'subsidy', 'transport facility', 'using the transport facility', and 'user fee'.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution and composition of Kerala Road Fund Board.
main_sections.description: Establishes the Kerala Road Fund Board and details its composition, including the Chairman, Vice-Chairman, and other members nominated from various government departments and financial institutions. It also outlines the rules for meetings and the quorum.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of the Board.
main_sections.description: Details the powers and functions of the Board, including formulating criteria for financing transport facility projects, raising funds, and performing other prescribed functions.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of the Executive Committee.
main_sections.description: Outlines the powers and functions of the Executive Committee, including approving concession agreements, sanctioning funds, and exercising other powers delegated by the Board.

Establishes the Kerala Road Fund and specifies the sources of its credit, including moneys from the Central Road Fund, contributions from the Government, user fees, grants, loans, and any other amount authorized for credit to the Fund.
Requires the Board to maintain books of accounts and prepare an annual statement of accounts and balance sheet, which are to be audited by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.

important_rules: The Act may be called the Kerala Road Fund Act, 2001.
The Act is deemed to have come into force on the 7th day of September, 2001.
Definitions provided for various terms are to be understood in the context of the Act unless otherwise required.

rights: Right to provide for establishment of a Fund for investments in transport facility projects.
Right to constitute a Board for administration of the Fund.
Right to monitor and supervise activities financed from the Fund.
duties: Duty to maintain books of accounts and prepare annual statements.
Duty to get accounts audited.

administration: The Kerala Road Fund Board and its Executive Committee administer the Act.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 23rd November, 2001 and published in Kerala Extraordinary Gazette No. 1853 dated 29th November, 2001.

The Government shall contribute to the Fund every year an amount equal to ten percent of the tax collected by them in the previous year under the provisions of the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1973 (19 of 1976), and the said amount shall be charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State.
The Board may invest any sum not required for immediate use in such securities or debentures as may be approved by the Board.

title: THE KERALA ROAD SAFETY AUTHORITY ACT, 2007
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a Road Safety Authority for the implementation of Road Safety programmes in the State, for the establishment of a Road Safety Fund and for matters connected therewith and incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and concerns road safety programmes, the establishment of a Road Safety Fund, and matters connected therewith. It also defines application to various authorities and individuals involved in road safety.

key_definitions.accident: means any incident, wherein, on account of the use of a motor vehicle on a public road, death, bodily injury or damage caused to any public properties, other vehicles, person, persons or property or to any public property or other vehicles, as the case may be;
key_definitions.Authority: means the 'Road Safety Authority' constituted under section 3;
key_definitions.cess: means the cess levied under section 10;
key_definitions.Chairman: means the Chairman of the Authority, Executive Committee or District Road Safety Council, as the case may be;
key_definitions.District Road Safety Council: means the District Road Safety Council constituted under section 19;
key_definitions.executive committee: means the executive committee of the Authority;
key_definitions.fund: means the Road Safety Fund constituted under section 11;
key_definitions.local authority: means a Panchayat constituted under the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 (13 of 1994) or a Municipality constituted under the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994 (20 of 1994);
key_definitions.public road: shall include, any private road to which public have access and also the traffic islands, medians and footpaths,
key_definitions.prescribed: means prescribed by rules made under this Act,
key_definitions.regulations: means the regulations made under section 39,
key_definitions.vehicle: includes any contraption or device used or capable of being used for the carriage or movement of human beings, animals or goods,

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Road Safety Authority Act, 2007 and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 7th day of January, 2006.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'accident', 'Authority', 'cess', 'Chairman', 'district', 'District Road Safety Council', 'executive committee', 'fund', 'local authority', 'public road', 'prescribed', 'regulations', and 'vehicle'.

Provides for the constitution of the Road Safety Authority by the Government through notification. It outlines the composition of the Authority, including the Chairman, members, and their roles and appointment procedures.

Details the various functions of the Authority, which include advising the Government on road safety policies, prescribing and enforcing road safety standards, formulating and implementing schemes, co-ordinating agencies, implementing awareness programmes, administering the Fund, and sanctioning expenditure for road safety projects and trauma-care programmes.
Establishes an Executive Committee for the Authority and outlines its composition and responsibilities, including the implementation of the decisions of the Authority.
Specifies the quorum and frequency of meetings for the Authority and the Executive Committee.
Deals with how matters are to be considered and disposed of at the meetings of the Authority or the Executive Committee.

main_sections.section_title: Vacancies etc not to invalidate proceedings of the Authority
main_sections.description: States that no act or proceedings of the Authority shall be invalid due to any vacancy or defect in its constitution.
Designates the Transport Commissioner as the ex-officio Road Safety Commissioner for the purpose of this Act.
Provides for the levy and collection of cess on every motor vehicle used or kept for use in the State for the purposes of this Act.
Provides for the establishment of the Kerala Road Safety Fund, to which amounts from various sources, including the cess, grants, and donations, shall be credited.

main_sections.section_title: Vesting and Administration of the Fund
main_sections.description: Specifies that the Fund shall vest in and be administered by the Authority.
Outlines how the Fund shall be utilized for the implementation of road safety programmes and schemes.

main_sections.section_title: Power to order removal of causes of accidents
main_sections.description: Grants the Authority the power to order the removal of causes of accidents.
Grants the Authority the power to order works to be carried out.
Empowers the Authority to recover costs incurred.

main_sections.section_title: Amounts recoverable as arrear of land revenue
main_sections.description: States that amounts recoverable under the Act shall be recovered as arrears of land revenue.
Allows for the delegation of powers by the Authority or the Government.
Provides for the constitution of District Road Safety Councils.
Deals with the staff of the Authority.
Covers the expenses of the Authority.
Relates to the keeping of accounts by the Authority.

main_sections.section_title: District Road Safety Council to submit reports etc.
main_sections.description: Requires the District Road Safety Council to submit reports to the Authority.
Mandates the Authority to submit an annual report.
Specifies the audit of the accounts of the Authority.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for failure to comply with the Authority's order
main_sections.description: Prescribes punishment for non-compliance with the Authority's orders.
Prescribes punishment for obstructing the Authority.
Allows for the compounding of offences.
Deals with offences committed by companies.
Provides for appeals against orders passed under the Act.
Allows for revision of orders.

main_sections.section_title: Members and Employees of the authority to be public servants
main_sections.description: Declares members and employees of the Authority as public servants.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith.
Specifies how offences are to be taken cognizance of and tried.

main_sections.section_title: Bar of jurisdiction of Civil Courts
main_sections.description: Excludes the jurisdiction of Civil Courts in certain matters.

main_sections.section_title: Act not in derogation of the Kerala Highway Protection Act, 1999
main_sections.description: Clarifies that this Act does not derogate from the Kerala Highway Protection Act, 1999.
Grants the Government the power to give directions to the Authority.
Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Allows the Authority to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules.
Provides for the removal of difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of any existing laws and savings provisions.

important_rules: Rule: Words and expressions not defined in this Act shall have the meanings respectively assigned to them in the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (Central Act 59 of 1988), Kerala Highway Protection Act, 1999 (6 of 2000) or the rules made thereunder.

Rule: The Authority shall be a body corporate by the name aforesaid, having perpetual succession and a common seal, with powers, subject to the provisions of this Act, to acquire, hold and dispose of property both movable and immovable and to contract and shall by the said name sue and be sued.

Rule: The Authority shall consist of the following members: Chairman, Minister for Transport (Vice-Chairman), Chief Secretary, Principal Secretary (Transport), Law Secretary, Principal Secretary (Home), Principal Secretary (Finance), Principal Secretary (Public Works), Principal Secretary (Health and Family Welfare), Principal Secretary (General Education), Principal Secretary (Local Self Government), Road Safety Commissioner (Chief Executive Officer), Director General of Police, Director, Health Services, Inspector General of Police (Traffic), Chief Engineer (Roads and Bridges), Chief Engineer (National Highways), Director, National Transportation, Planning and Research Centre, Secretary, State Transport Authority, and three persons who are experts in road safety nominated by the Government.
Rule: The nominated members of the Authority shall hold office for a period of five year from the date of appointment.
Rule: Any nominated member may at any time, resign his office by a letter addressed to the chairman of the Authority.

Rule: The Authority shall have the following functions, namely: - advising the Government on road safety policies; prescribing and enforcing road safety standards and procedures; formulate and implement schemes, projects and programmes, relating to road safety; co-ordinating the functions of all the agencies and Government Departments discharging duties related to road safety; Implementing road safety awareness programmes; administration of the Fund; sanctioning expenditure for the implementation of road safety Schemes and programmes; sanctioning expenditure for road safety projects and for purchase and installation of equipments and devices connected with road safety; sanctioning expenditure for the conduct of studies, projects and research on matters relating to road safety; sanctioning expenditure for trauma-care programmes or activities; sanctioning administrative expenditure of the authority; sanctioning expenditure on matters connected with road safety measures; formation of self help groups, under the leadership of the Authority for the rescue operation in the place of accident; discharging such other functions, as may be prescribed, having regard to the objects of this Act.

penalties: Punishment for failure to comply with the Authority's order (Section 26)
Punishment for obstructing the Authority (Section 27)
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Road Safety Authority and the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through orders issued by the Authority, imposition of punishments for non-compliance, and legal proceedings for obstruction.  Also through the levy and collection of cess, and the administration of the Road Safety Fund.

rights: Right to sue and be sued by the Authority in its corporate name.
Protection for actions taken in good faith by members and employees of the Authority.
duties: Duty to implement road safety programmes and schemes.
Duty to advise the Government on road safety policies.
Duty to co-ordinate activities of various agencies related to road safety.
Duty to form self-help groups for rescue operations.
Duty to submit annual reports and maintain accounts.
District Road Safety Councils must submit reports to the Authority.
obligations: Obligation to pay cess on motor vehicles.
Obligation to comply with the orders of the Authority.

key_procedures: Establishment of the Road Safety Authority and its Executive Committee, defining their composition and functions.
Levy and collection of cess on motor vehicles for the purpose of the Road Safety Fund.
Establishment and administration of the Kerala Road Safety Fund, outlining its sources and utilization.
Procedures for meetings, disposal of business, and decision-making by the Authority and Executive Committee.
Procedures for the constitution and reporting of District Road Safety Councils.
Procedures for dealing with accidents, including ordering removal of causes and works.
Procedures for appeals and revision of orders.
Procedures for compounding of offences.
administration: The Kerala Road Safety Authority, with the oversight and direction of the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act came into force on 7th January, 2006.
Words and expressions not defined in this Act shall have meanings as per the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Kerala Highway Protection Act, 1999, or their respective rules.
The Authority is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
Nominated members of the Authority hold office for five years.
The Transport Commissioner is the ex-officio Road Safety Commissioner.
Cess levied under the Act is collected as arrears of land revenue.
The Act is not in derogation of the Kerala Highway Protection Act, 1999.
Civil Courts' jurisdiction is barred in certain matters.

title: The Kerala Road Transport Services (Validation) Act, 1957
purpose: To validate the running and operation of certain road transport services by the Government, specifically addressing issues related to scheme preparation, permits, and compensation under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939.
scope: This Act applies to road transport services run and operated by the Government in Kerala at the commencement of the Act. Its subject matter scope is limited to the validation of these services concerning the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Road Transport Services (Validation) Act, 1957.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of the running and operation of certain road transport services by Government
main_sections.description: This section retroactively validates road transport services run and operated by the Government at the commencement of the Act. It deems these services to be run and operated under an approved scheme and in accordance with the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939. It explicitly states that the validity of such services cannot be questioned in any court on grounds of no scheme being prepared, approved, or published; no permit being obtained; or no compensation being paid or payable to permit holders due to cancellation or modification of permit terms.

important_rules: Rule: Any road transport service run and operated by the Government at the commencement of this Act shall be deemed to be a service run and operated under an approved scheme within the meaning of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, and in accordance with its provisions.

Rule: The validity of running and operating such government road transport services cannot be questioned in court based on the absence of a prepared, approved, or published scheme under the principal Act.

Rule: The validity of running and operating such government road transport services cannot be questioned in court based on the absence of a permit obtained under the principal Act for any motor vehicle used in connection with such service.

Rule: The validity of running and operating such government road transport services cannot be questioned in court based on the non-payment or non-liability to pay compensation as provided in section 68G of the principal Act to the permit holder due to cancellation or modification of permit terms.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The enforcement authority is implicitly the courts, which are barred from questioning the validity of services under specific grounds.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The Act's enforcement is primarily through the judicial system, by preventing challenges to the validity of services that meet the criteria of Section 2.

rights: Right of the Government to continue running and operating road transport services that are validated by this Act.

administration: The Act does not explicitly mention an administering department or agency, but the context suggests the Department of Transport or a related government body would oversee road transport services.
important_notes: This Act is a President's Act, re-enacted by Act 23 of 1958.
Published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary dated 27-03-1957.
The Act was enacted by the President in exercise of powers conferred by section 3 of the Kerala State Legislature (Delegation of powers) Act, 1956 (75 of 1956).

title: THE KERALA RYOTWARI TENANTS AND KUDIKIDAPPKARS PROTECTION ACT, 1962
purpose: An Act to provide for the temporary protection of tenants of ryotwari lands and kudikidappukars in the taluks of Hosdrug and Kasaragod in the Cannanore district.
scope: Applies to ryotwari lands and kudikidappukars in the taluks of Hosdrug and Kasaragod in the Cannanore district.

key_definitions.tenant: means a tenant as defined in the Kerala Agrarian Relations Act, 1960, and includes -- (a) the holder of a vaida gani lease. (b) a person holding under a transaction described in the document evidencing it as Bhoya, Ottu, Nanabatti, Ansar, Illidwar, or Krithasanna, Illidavar, but not being a usufructuary mortgage as defined in the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (Central Act 4 of 1882); (c) a cultivating tenant holding under a lease granted before the 15th day of February, 1961, by a usufructuary mortgagee as defined in the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (Central Act 4 of 1882); (d) a varomdar.
key_definitions.vaidagani lease: means a lease for a term of years
key_definitions.kudikidappukaran: means a Kudikidappukaran as defined in the Kerala Agrarian Relations Act, 1960, and includes a tenant who is not entitled to the benefits conferred by sub-section (3) and shall be liable to pay the future arrears of rent for the period specified in that sub-section which he would have been liable to pay but for sub-sections (3) and (4) had not been enacted, but credit shall be given for any amount paid by him under sub-section (4) towards such arrears of rent.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, application, commencement and duration.
main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, its application to certain taluks, and its commencement and duration.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, such as 'tenant', 'vaidagani lease', and 'kudikidappukaran'.

Specifies the leases or lands to which the Act does not apply, including leases of land belonging to or vested in the Government, leases of buildings, and leases of certain lands for industrial or commercial purposes.

main_sections.section_title: Stay of eviction of tenants and kudikidappukars.
main_sections.description: Provides for the stay of eviction of tenants and kudikidappukars except in certain circumstances such as non-payment of rent or contravention of lease terms. It also addresses the discharge of arrears of rent.

Details the provisions for the discharge of arrears of rent, outlining the amounts payable by different classes of tenants based on the extent of land held and the duration of arrears. It also specifies conditions under which future arrears are deemed to be discharged.

Deals with rent due after February 15, 1961, stating that certain tenants shall be recoverable only at the rate specified in the Schedule for the appropriate class of land or the contract rent, whichever is less. It also addresses rent due from intermediaries.

Provides for the remission of rent in cases where there has been damage to, or failure of, crops owing to causes beyond the control of the tenant. The extent of remission is proportionate to the extent of such damage or failure.

Specifies the period of limitation for recovery of arrears of rent, the time during which suits or proceedings for recovery of rent were stayed under the Kerala Stay of Eviction Proceedings Act, 1957, and the time allowed under Section 5 or sub-section (4), as the case may be, of Section 5, shall be excluded.
Grants the Government the power to make rules, by notification in the Gazette, to carry out the purposes of the Act. These rules must be laid before the Legislative Assembly.
Repeals the Kerala Ryotwari Tenants Protection Ordinance, 1962, and saves anything done or action taken under that Ordinance, provided it had commenced on or before January 11, 1962.

important_rules: Rules made under this Act shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly for a period of not less than fourteen days.

Such rules, as soon as possible after they are made, shall be subject to such modifications as the Legislative Assembly may make during the session in which they are so laid or the session immediately following.

rights: Right to protection from eviction except under specific conditions.
Right to remission of rent in cases of crop failure or damage.
duties: Duty to pay rent as stipulated.
Duty to comply with lease terms.
obligations: Obligation to pay future arrears of rent for a specified period if not relieved by sub-sections (3) and (4) of Section 2(d).

key_procedures: Procedure for discharge of arrears of rent based on land holding and duration of arrears.
Procedure for remission of rent due to crop failure or damage, determined by the extent of loss.
Procedure for applications for remission of rent to be filed within a specified time frame after the date of commencement of the Act.
administration: The Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act has provisions for the discharge of arrears of rent for different classes of tenants.
The remission of rent is proportionate to the extent of damage or failure of crops.
The Act specifies the period of limitation for recovery of rent arrears and allows for exclusion of certain periods.
Rules made under the Act are subject to modification by the Legislative Assembly.

title: The Kerala Sales Tax (Levy and Validation Amendment) Act, 1969
purpose: To amend the Kerala Sales Tax (Levy and Validation) Act, 1965, for the purpose hereinafter appearing.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala and concerns the levy and validation of sales tax.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Sales Tax (Levy and Validation) Amendment Act, 1969.

Amends section 4 of the Kerala Sales Tax (Levy and Validation) Act, 1965. It modifies the provisions concerning the sub-section (1) related to levying, assessing, or collecting taxes by any court, tribunal, or other authority. It also includes provisions regarding the non-maintenance of proceedings and the refund of tax paid under the General Sales Tax Act, as well as limitations on tax assessed and collected under the General Sales Tax Act before the 27th day of September, 1965.

important_rules: No court, tribunal, or other authority shall, notwithstanding any judgment, decree, or order, enforce any such tax paid under the General Sales Tax Act.
No court shall enforce a decree or order directing the refund of any such tax paid under the General Sales Tax Act.
Any such tax assessed under the General Sales Tax Act but not collected may be recovered in the manner provided by this Act and the rules made thereunder.
