Any such tax not assessed under the General Sales Tax Act before the 27th day of September, 1965, may be assessed within five years from the date of publication of this Act and recovered in the manner provided under the General Sales Tax Act and the rules made hereunder.
key_procedures: Assessment and recovery of sales tax that was not assessed or collected under the General Sales Tax Act before a specified date.
important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 90, dated 1st April, 1969.

title: THE KERALA SALES TAX (LEVY AND VALIDATION) ACT, 1965
purpose: To provide for the levy of a tax on the purchase of copra and cashew nut kernel and to validate the levy and collection of such tax.
scope: This Act applies to the whole of the State of Kerala. It covers the purchase of copra and cashew nut kernel.

key_definitions.Interpretation: References to the General Sales Tax Act shall be construed as reference to the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963 (Kerala Act XV of 1963), with its exceptions and definitions.
key_definitions.dealer: Means any dealer who has a turnover of copra or cashew nut kernel for the relevant periods.

main_sections.description: Names the act as The Kerala Sales Tax (Levy and Validation) Act, 1965, states its extent to the whole of the State of Kerala, and specifies the commencement dates for its provisions. Sections 2 and 3 came into force from April 1, 1958, and the remaining provisions from September 27, 1965.
Clarifies how references to the General Sales Tax Act should be interpreted in the context of this Act and defines terms used within the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of dealers for tax on the purchase of copra and cashew nut kernel.
main_sections.description: Establishes the liability of dealers to pay tax on their turnover of copra and cashew nut kernel for specific periods. It specifies the tax rates (four paise per rupee for turnover from March 1, 1963, to March 31, 1963; two paise per rupee for turnover from October 1, 1958, to March 31, 1963). It also states that no tax is levied on the purchase of copra or cashew nut kernel if tax has already been levied on its outward sale. No dealer whose total turnover in a year is less than ten thousand rupees is liable to pay tax for that year.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of levy and collection of tax under the General Sales Tax Act on copra and cashew nut kernel.
main_sections.description: Validates any levy, assessment, or collection of tax under the General Sales Tax Act on the purchase of copra and cashew nut kernel made during specified periods. It states that no suit or other proceeding shall be maintained for the refund of any such tax paid. It also allows for the assessment and recovery of any tax not collected, and for the refund of amounts wrongly collected.

States that nothing in the Act shall render any person liable to conviction for an offence in respect of anything done or omitted to be done before the date of publication of the Act, if such act or omission would not have been an offence under the General Sales Tax Act.

important_rules: Dealers are liable to pay tax on their turnover of copra and cashew nut kernel at specified rates for specified periods.
No tax is levied on the purchase of copra or cashew nut kernel if tax has already been levied on its outward sale.
Dealers with a total annual turnover below ten thousand rupees are exempt from paying tax under section 3(1).

penalties: Any person convicted for an offence under the General Sales Tax Act in respect of anything done or omitted before the date of publication of this Act.
No suit or other proceeding shall be maintained for the refund of any tax paid under the General Sales Tax Act for the specified periods.
No court shall enforce a decree or order directing the refund of any tax paid under the General Sales Tax Act before the 1st day of April, 1963, but not collected, may be recovered.
Any such tax not assessed under the General Sales Tax Act before the 1st day of April, 1963, may be assessed within three years from the date of publication of this Act and recovered.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be the authorities responsible for the administration of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment, collection, and legal proceedings as provided for under the General Sales Tax Act and this Act.

rights: Right to have wrongly collected tax refunded (Section 4(2)(ii)).
Right for tax to be recovered if not assessed or collected under the General Sales Tax Act (Section 4(1)).
duties: Duty of dealers to pay tax on their turnover of copra and cashew nut kernel.
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act regarding levy and collection of tax.
obligations: Obligation to pay tax as prescribed for the purchase of copra and cashew nut kernel.
Obligation to not seek refund of tax paid under the General Sales Tax Act for specified periods.

key_procedures: Levy and collection of tax on the purchase of copra and cashew nut kernel by dealers.
Validation of past levies and collections of tax under the General Sales Tax Act.
Assessment and recovery of tax where it was not assessed or collected.
Procedure for claiming refund of wrongly paid tax.
administration: Implied to be the Sales Tax department of the Kerala State Government.
important_notes: The Act is a validation Act, meaning it legalizes actions taken previously under a different law.
Specific tax rates and periods are detailed for the levy of tax on copra and cashew nut kernel.
The Act provides for the recovery of unassessed or uncollected tax, and for the refund of wrongly collected tax.
Section 5 ensures that actions taken in good faith before the Act's publication are not penalized if they were not offences under the previous Act.

title: The Kerala Sales-Tax Laws (Amendment) Act, 1957
purpose: To amend the laws relating to sales-tax in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to sales-tax laws in the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Sales-Tax Laws (Amendment) Act, 1957, and it shall come into force on the 1st day of April, 1957.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Travancore-Cochin Act XI of 1125.
main_sections.description: Amends section 3 of the Travancore-Cochin General Sales Tax Act, 1125 (XI of 1125) by substituting certain words related to currency denominations ('three pies', 'six pies', 'nine pies', 'one anna', 'three pies', 'two annas', 'three pies', 'four annas', 'naye paise', 'two naye paise', 'six naye paise', 'fifteen naye paise', 'five naye paise', 'eight naye paise') with their equivalent or altered denominations.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Madras Act IX of 1939.
main_sections.description: Amends section 5 of the Madras Sales Tax Act, 1939 (IX of 1939) in force in the Malabar district. It substitutes the phrase 'rate of eight annas naye paise per gallon' with 'rate of thirty-eight naye paise per gallon' for the tax on petrol. It also states that the State Government may, from time to time, notify any other rate at which the tax shall be payable, provided no such notification shall come into force until approved by the legislative assembly.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Madras Act VI of 1939.
main_sections.description: Amends section 3 of the Madras Sales of Motor Spirit Taxation Act, 1939 (VI of 1939) in force in the Malabar district. Similar to the amendment of Madras Act IX of 1939, it substitutes currency denominations in the context of sales of motor spirit.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Madras Act IV of 1953.
main_sections.description: Amends section 4 of the Madras Tobacco (Taxation of Sales and Registration) Act, 1953 (IV of 1953) in force in the Malabar district. It substitutes currency denominations ('three pies', 'six pies', 'nine pies', 'two annas', 'three pies', 'naye paise', 'two naye paise', 'five naye paise', 'six naye paise') related to tobacco sales.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Madras Act XI of 1954.
main_sections.description: Amends section 3 of the Madras Medium Cotton Cloth (Sales Tax) Act, 1954 (XLI of 1954) in force in the Malabar district. It substitutes currency denominations ('one anna', 'three pies', 'eight naye paise') concerning the sales of cotton cloth.

important_notes: The Act amends several existing sales tax laws in Kerala, primarily by updating currency denominations.
The amendments reflect a transition from older currency units (pies, annas) to the decimal system (naye paise) which was being introduced.
The State Government has the power to notify other rates for tax payable on petrol, subject to legislative assembly approval.
The Act came into force on 1st April, 1957.

title: The Kerala Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Regulation of Issue of Community Certificates (Amendment) Act
purpose: To amend the Kerala Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Regulation of Issue of Community Certificates Act, 1996, and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the regulation of the issue of community certificates to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes: The document refers to the categories of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes as defined in the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950 and the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950, and subsequent amendments.
key_definitions.Community Certificate: A certificate issued to identify individuals belonging to Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes.

main_sections.description: Refers to the Act as The Kerala Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Regulation of Issue of Community Certificates (Amendment) Act, 2008, and its commencement.
Details amendments made to the principal Act (Act 11 of 1996). This section is extensive and modifies various parts of the original Act, including definitions and procedural aspects.

important_rules: Rule: Any person claiming to be a member of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe shall, for the purpose of obtaining a Community Certificate, submit an application to the Tahsildar of the Taluk in which his permanent residence is situated.

Rule: The Tahsildar shall, after making such inquiry as he deems fit, and on being satisfied that the applicant is a member of the Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe, issue a Community Certificate in such form and containing such particulars as may be prescribed.
Rule: The Tahsildar shall maintain a register of all Community Certificates issued by him.

penalties: False information or declaration in application: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.
Obtaining certificate by false means: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
Contravention of provisions: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Tahsildar and other authorities empowered under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inquiry, investigation, and imposition of penalties as specified in the Act.

rights: Right to apply for and obtain a Community Certificate if belonging to a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe.
Right to appeal against decisions of the Tahsildar.
duties: Duty to provide true and correct information in the application.
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder.
obligations: Obligation of authorities to conduct fair and timely inquiries.
Obligation to maintain records of issued certificates.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining a Community Certificate: Application to Tahsildar -> Inquiry by Tahsildar -> Issuance of certificate if satisfied.
Procedure for appeal: Appeal against the decision of the Tahsildar to the Collector.
Procedure for correction of certificates: Application for correction to the Tahsildar.
Procedure for cancellation of certificates: Investigation and cancellation by the issuing authority or higher authority if found to be obtained fraudulently.
administration: Revenue Department, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The amendment specifies details regarding the scrutiny of applications, conditions for issuance of certificates, and the process for cancellation of certificates obtained fraudulently.
The Act emphasizes the importance of accurate documentation and proof of belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
The amendment clarifies the roles and responsibilities of the Tahsildar and other authorities in the process.
An asterisk (*) denotes an amendment made by Notification No. G.O.(Ms) No. 54/2007/SWD dated 26-06-2007 published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 1388 dated 26-06-2007.

title: THE KERALA SCHEDULED TRIBES (RESTRICTION ON TRANSFER OF LANDS AND RESTORATION OF ALIENATED LANDS) ACT, 1975
purpose: To provide for restricting the transfer of lands by members of Scheduled Tribes in the State of Kerala and for the restoration of possession of lands alienated by such members and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Kerala and its members of Scheduled Tribes.

key_definitions.competent authority: The District Collector of the district in which the land is situate or any other officer appointed by the Government for the purposes of this Act.
key_definitions.immovable property: Includes standing crops and trees but does not include growing grass.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Revenue Divisional Officer: With reference to any land, means the Revenue Divisional Officer having jurisdiction over the area in which that land is situate or any other officer appointed by the Government to perform the functions of the Revenue Divisional Officer under this Act, in the area in which that land is situate.
key_definitions.Scheduled Tribe: Means any of the Scheduled Tribes in relation to the State as specified in the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950.
key_definitions.transfer: In relation to immovable property is conveyed by any document or oral transaction, whether by way of mortgage with or without possession, lease, sale, gift or exchange, or in any other manner, not being a testamentary disposition; and includes a charge, ‘vilapanayam’, ‘unduruthi’, contract relating to immovable property, mortgage, pledge or hypothecation of crops or standing trees on payment of consideration or otherwise, voluntary surrender and abandonment.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Scheduled Tribes (Restriction on Transfer of Lands and Restoration of Alienated Lands) Act, 1975. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'competent authority', 'immovable property', 'prescribed', 'Revenue Divisional Officer', 'Scheduled Tribe', 'State', and 'transfer'.
Specifies transactions that are exempt from the provisions of this Act, including leases, mortgages, pledges, hypothecations, and voluntary surrenders under certain conditions.
Prohibits the transfer of immovable property of a Scheduled Tribe member to a non-Scheduled Tribe person without the previous consent of the competent authority.
Declares certain transfers of immovable property by a Scheduled Tribe member to a non-Scheduled Tribe person, made before or after the commencement of this Act, to be invalid.

Provides for the restoration of possession and enjoyment of immovable property to a member of a Scheduled Tribe where the transfer is invalid under section 4 or section 5. It outlines the procedure for application to the Revenue Divisional Officer.

Empowers the Government to take suo motu action for the restoration of possession or enjoyment of any immovable property of a Scheduled Tribe member if it is satisfied that such property has been deprived of by reason of a transfer which is invalid.

In any proceedings under this Act or in the trial of an offence punishable under section 13, the burden of proof of the validity of any transfer of immovable property shall lie on the person who claims such transfer to be valid.

main_sections.section_title: Inadmissibility of deeds for purposes of registration
main_sections.description: States that notwithstanding anything contained in the Registration Act, 1908, no deed of transfer of any immovable property executed in contravention of or contrary to the provisions of this Act shall be accepted for registration.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition to attachment of immovable properties
main_sections.description: Prohibits the attachment or sale of immovable property of a Scheduled Tribe member in execution of a money decree.

Specifies that when immovable property is restored to a member of a Scheduled Tribe, an amount equal to the aggregate of the actual amount of consideration received by such member at the time of the transfer and an amount determined by the competent authority for improvements, if any, made after the transfer and before such restoration shall be paid by him to the person from whom possession or enjoyment was restored.

main_sections.section_title: Government to advance loan for payment of amount
main_sections.description: Provides for the Government to advance loans to Scheduled Tribe members for the payment of amounts under section 11, and for the repayment of such loans.
Defines offences under the Act and prescribes penalties, including rigorous imprisonment and fines.

Specifies that no court inferior to that of a Magistrate of the First Class shall try any offence punishable under this Act. It also states that the Government may constitute one or more special courts exclusively for the trial of offences under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Bar on proceedings against Scheduled Tribes under Chapter X of the Code of Criminal Procedure
main_sections.description: Prohibits proceedings against a member of a Scheduled Tribe or any other person on his behalf under Chapter X of the Code of Criminal Procedure for the restoration of possession or enjoyment of any land under the provisions of this Act, or where the Government takes suo motu action, unless the Government has taken such action.

main_sections.section_title: Legal practitioner not to appear in proceedings under the Act
main_sections.description: Prohibits legal practitioners from appearing, pleading, or acting on behalf of any party in proceedings before the Revenue Divisional Officer or the competent authority or the Government, except with the written permission of such officer or authority or the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of competent authority and Revenue Divisional Officer
main_sections.description: Grants powers to the competent authority and Revenue Divisional Officer to make inquiries, pass orders for possession, and direct the delivery of property.
Empowers the Government to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection to persons acting in good faith in pursuance of the provisions of the Act.
States that the provisions of this Act are in addition to and not in derogation of any other law for the time being in force.

main_sections.section_title: Bar of jurisdiction of civil courts
main_sections.description: Bars the jurisdiction of civil courts to entertain any suit or proceeding in respect of any matter which the Government or the competent authority or the Revenue Divisional Officer is empowered by this Act to determine.
Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of this Act.

important_rules: No transfer of immovable property of a Scheduled Tribe member to a non-Scheduled Tribe person shall be made without the previous consent of the competent authority (Section 4).
Certain transfers made before or after the commencement of the Act are declared invalid (Section 5).
Immovable property of a Scheduled Tribe member is protected from attachment or sale in execution of a money decree (Section 10).
Legal practitioners are generally prohibited from appearing in proceedings before the Revenue Divisional Officer or competent authority without written permission (Section 16).

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees, or both (Section 13). This applies to any person who procures transfer of immovable property in contravention of the provisions of this Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Competent Authority, Revenue Divisional Officer, Government, Special Courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inquiries, orders for possession, restoration of property, prosecution for offences, and special court trials.

rights: Right to have transferred immovable property restored if the transfer is invalid (Section 6).
Right to be heard in matters of restoration of property (Section 6(3)).
Right to receive compensation for improvements made to restored property (Section 11).
duties: Duty to obtain prior consent before transferring immovable property to a non-Scheduled Tribe person (Section 4).
Duty to return possession of immovable property if the transfer is invalid (Section 6).
Duty to pay compensation for improvements if applicable (Section 11).
obligations: Obligation to comply with orders of the competent authority and Revenue Divisional Officer regarding restoration of property.

key_procedures: Application for Restoration of Property: A person entitled to restoration of possession or enjoyment of immovable property may make an application to the Revenue Divisional Officer within one year from the date of commencement of this Act or such further period as may be specified by the Government (Section 6(2)).

Inquiry by Revenue Divisional Officer: Upon receipt of an application, the Revenue Divisional Officer shall make or cause to be made necessary inquiries and if satisfied that the application is genuine, shall pass an order for the restoration of possession or enjoyment of the immovable property (Section 6(3)).

Service of Orders: Every order made under sub-section (3) shall be served on the person for whom it is intended, either by delivering it to that person or by delivering it to any officer of such person or by affixing a copy thereof to the outer-door or some conspicuous part of the premises (Section 6(4)).

Appeal: Any person aggrieved by an order under sub-section (3) may, within a period of thirty days from the date of service of the order, prefer an appeal to the competent authority, and the decision of the competent authority on such appeal shall be final and shall not be called in question in any court of law (Section 6(5)).
administration: Revenue Divisional Officer, Competent Authority, and the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act aims to protect the land rights of Scheduled Tribes in Kerala.
The burden of proof for the validity of a transfer lies with the claimant (Section 8).
Legal practitioners are generally excluded from appearing in proceedings under the Act to ensure a more direct and less technical process for the tribal beneficiaries (Section 16).

title: The Kerala Self Financing Professional Colleges (Prohibition Of Capitation Fees and Procedure for Admission) Act
purpose: To prohibit the collection of capitation fees and to regulate the admission procedure in self-financing professional colleges in Kerala.
scope: Applies to all self-financing professional colleges in the state of Kerala.

key_definitions.self_financing_professional_college: A college which is not under the management of the Government or a University and which is established and maintained for imparting professional education on payment of fees.
key_definitions.capitation_fee: Any amount collected from a student or his guardian by an institution or any person on behalf of the institution, other than the fee prescribed by the Government or the University, as a condition for admission to a course or for any other purpose.
key_definitions.professional_education: Education imparted in Colleges for courses leading to degrees or diplomas in Medicine, Engineering, Dental, Ayurveda, Homoeopathy, Indian Systems of Medicine, Law, Education, Agriculture, Veterinary Science and such other courses as may be notified by the Government from time to time.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies when it comes into force.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'self-financing professional college', 'capitation fee', 'professional education', etc.
Prohibits the collection of capitation fees by self-financing professional colleges.
Lays down the procedure for admission to self-financing professional colleges, including the constitution of admission committees and the method of selection.
Provides for the constitution of an Admission Supervisory Board to oversee the admission process.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of the Admission Supervisory Board
main_sections.description: Details the powers and functions of the Admission Supervisory Board, including receiving complaints and making recommendations.
Specifies the conditions for granting affiliation to self-financing professional colleges and the powers of the affiliating university.
Provides for the constitution of Admission Committees in each self-financing professional college.
Provides for the constitution of a Selection Committee for the purpose of admission.
Empowers the Government to fix the fees for courses in self-financing professional colleges.
Grants the Government the power to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of any existing laws and savings of certain actions.
Gives the Government the power to remove any difficulties that may arise in the implementation of the Act.

important_rules: No self-financing professional college shall collect capitation fee.
Admission to courses in self-financing professional colleges shall be made strictly on the basis of merit and in accordance with the procedure laid down in the Act and the rules made thereunder.
The Admission Committee of each college shall prepare a list of eligible candidates based on merit and forward it to the Selection Committee.
The Selection Committee shall, after verification of documents and eligibility, prepare the final list of candidates for admission.
The Government shall have the power to fix the fees for courses in self-financing professional colleges.
The Admission Supervisory Board shall monitor the admission process and ensure that it is conducted in a fair and transparent manner.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both, for contravention of the provisions relating to prohibition of capitation fee.
Cancellation of affiliation and recognition of the college for repeated violations.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala, the affiliating Universities, and the Admission Supervisory Board.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the Admission Supervisory Board, Admission Committees, Selection Committees, and by taking legal action against offenders. Affiliation and recognition can be cancelled.

rights: Right of students to be admitted on merit without paying capitation fees.
Right of colleges to receive prescribed fees.
Right of the Government to regulate admissions and fees.
duties: Duty of colleges not to collect capitation fees.
Duty of colleges to follow the prescribed admission procedure.
Duty of the Admission Supervisory Board to ensure fairness in admissions.
Duty of the Government to frame rules and regulations for effective implementation.
obligations: Obligation of colleges to maintain transparency in admissions.
Obligation of students to submit to the prescribed admission process.

key_procedures: Admission to professional courses in self-financing colleges will be based on merit, through a common entrance examination.
An Admission Supervisory Board will be constituted to oversee the entire admission process.
Each college will have an Admission Committee to prepare a list of eligible candidates.
A Selection Committee will be responsible for the final selection of candidates.
The Government will fix the fee structure for these colleges.
administration: Department of Higher Education, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act aims to ensure that admissions are based purely on merit and not on the ability to pay capitation fees.
The Act emphasizes transparency and fairness in the admission process.
The Government has the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.

title: The Kerala Service Inam Lands (Vesting and Enfranchisement) Act, 1981
purpose: To provide for the vesting and enfranchisement of Service Inam lands in the State of Kerala, by abolition of all services attached to such lands and for matters incidental or ancillary thereto.
scope: Applies to Service Inam lands in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.appointed day: The day on which the Act comes into force.
key_definitions.holding: Means any parcel or parcels of Service Inam land held by a single landholder.
key_definitions.landholder: Means a person holding Service Inam land.
key_definitions.land owner: Means the owner of Service Inam land.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Service Inam land: Means land held under a tenure to which some specific service or obligation in the shape of personal labour or supply of provisions is attached and includes land held under 'Viruthi', 'Gozhiyan', 'Karanma' or 'Erayili' tenure.
key_definitions.Settlement Officer: Means the Settlement Officer appointed under section 15.
key_definitions.to hold: Means to be in actual possession.
key_definitions.ceiling area: And 'family' shall have the meanings respectively assigned to them in the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 (1 of 1964).

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Service Inam Lands (Vesting and Enfranchisement) Act, 1981. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'holding', 'landholder', 'land owner', 'prescribed', 'Service Inam land', 'Settlement Officer', 'to hold', 'ceiling area', and 'family'.

main_sections.section_title: Vesting of the rights of landowners in Government and abolition of services
main_sections.description: Declares that notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force or in any contract, or in any judgment, decree or order of any court, with effect on and from the appointed day, all right, title and interest of the landowners in Service Inam lands held by landholders shall vest in the Government free from all encumbrances, and any service or obligation attached to Service Inam lands shall stand abolished, and the landholders shall have no liability or obligation to render any service attached to such lands.

main_sections.section_title: Amount to be paid by the Government
main_sections.description: Specifies the amount to be paid by the Government for the vesting of lands. The landowner shall be paid an amount calculated at the rate of one thousand two hundred rupees per acre of such lands. The amount shall be paid in cash in lump and shall bear interest at the rate of four and a half per cent per annum from the date on which the order of the Settlement Officer under section 7 has become final, till the date of payment.

States that the landholder of any holding or part of a holding, the right, title and interest in respect of which have vested in the Government under section 3, shall be entitled to assignment of such right, title and interest. This right is subject to certain conditions related to landholders who do not occupy the land and the ceiling area. A landholder entitled to assignment of the right, title and interest of a holding or part of a holding may, within such period as may be prescribed, apply to the Settlement Officer whose jurisdiction such holding or part is situate for assignment.

Lays down the purchase price for the assignment of land. The purchase price referred to shall be eight hundred and forty rupees per acre to be paid in sixteen equal annual instalments. Provided that if the amount is paid in one lump, the purchase price shall be seventy-five per cent of the said amount. The purchase price payable by the landholder shall be deposited with the Settlement Officer. It can be paid in a lump or in instalments.

main_sections.section_title: Settlement Officer to issue notices and determine the compensation and purchase price
main_sections.description: Mandates the Settlement Officer to issue notices and determine the compensation and purchase price. The Settlement Officer shall publish or cause to be published a public notice in such form and in such manner as may be prescribed, calling upon the landholders and the landowners to furnish claims and objections, and to prove their respective claims or in support of their objections. The Settlement Officer shall decide disputes as to whether land is Service Inam Land for the purposes of the Act and the decision of the Government thereon shall be final.

main_sections.section_title: Payment of amount to the landowner to be full discharge
main_sections.description: States that the payment of the amount specified in section 4 to a landowner and other persons entitled thereto in accordance with an order passed by the Settlement Officer under section 7 shall be a full discharge of the liability of the Government for payment of such amount and no further claims for payment of any amount shall lie against the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Issue of pattas and other documents to landholders
main_sections.description: Requires the Settlement Officer, after the order of the Settlement Officer under section 7 has become final, to issue pattas or other documents evidencing full proprietary rights of the landholders in their holdings.

main_sections.section_title: Amounts due to the Government to be recoverable under the Revenue Recovery Act
main_sections.description: Specifies that any amount due to the Government as arrears of purchase price or otherwise from any landholder under this Act shall be a first charge on his holding and the same shall be recoverable as arrears of public revenue due on land under the provisions of the Kerala Revenue Recovery Act, 1968.

main_sections.section_title: Orders of Settlement Officer to be deemed to be decrees of civil court
main_sections.description: Declares that orders of the Settlement Officer to be deemed to be decrees of civil court and shall contain a concise statement of the case, points for determination, the decision thereon and the reasons for such decision.

Allows any person aggrieved by an order of the Settlement Officer under section 7 to prefer an appeal within thirty days of the receipt of him of the order, to the District Collector having jurisdiction over the area in which the holding is situate. The District Collector, after giving the appellant a reasonable opportunity of being heard and after making such further enquiry as may be prescribed, pass such order on the appeal as he thinks fit.

Empowers the Board of Revenue, either on its own motion or on application by any person aggrieved by an order under section 12, to call for and examine the record of any proceeding in which such order has been passed for the purpose of satisfying itself as to the legality, regularity or propriety of such order or proceeding and pass such order thereon as it thinks fit. The Board of Revenue shall not of its own motion call for and examine the record of any proceeding unless the order to which the proceeding relates has been made not more than two years previously.

States that no correction shall be made in the order of the Settlement Officer after it has become final, provided that the Settlement Officer may, either of his own motion or on application filed by a person interested, correct any clerical or arithmetical mistake or any error arising therein from any accidental slip or omission. Provided that no such correction shall be made without giving an opportunity of being heard to the party who may be affected thereby.

States that the Government shall appoint as many Settlement Officers as may be necessary from among persons not below the rank of Tahsildar for the purpose of exercising the powers and performing the functions of a Settlement Officer under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of Settlement Officer, District Collector and Board of Revenue
main_sections.description: Grants Settlement Officers, District Collectors and the Board of Revenue all the powers of a civil court while trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, in respect of the following matters: summoning and enforcing the attendance of any person and examining him on oath; requiring the discovery and production of any document; receiving evidence on affidavit; issuing commissions for examination of witnesses or for local investigation; requisitioning any public record or copy thereof from any court or office; and any other matter which may be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Decision of disputes as to whether land is Service Inam Land
main_sections.description: Stipulates that any question arising as to whether any land is a Service Inam Land for the purposes of this Act or not, the question shall be referred to the Government for decision and the decision of the Government thereon shall be final.

main_sections.section_title: Bar of jurisdiction of civil courts
main_sections.description: Prohibits civil courts from deciding or dealing with any question or to determine any matter which is, by or under this Act, required to be decided or dealt with by any officer or authority under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides that no suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against the Government or any officer for any act, which in good faith done or intended to be done under this Act or the rules made thereunder.

Grants the Government the power, by order published in the Gazette, to make such provisions not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act which appear to them necessary for the purpose of removing any difficulty. Provided that no such order shall be made after the expiry of two years from the date on which this Act comes into force. Every order made under this section shall, as soon as may be after it is made, be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

Authorizes the Government, by notification in the Gazette, to make rules to carry out the purposes of this Act. These rules may provide for the following matters: the fees payable on applications, appeals and claims made under this Act and the persons by whom and the period within which such fees shall be paid; the procedure to be followed by the Settlement Officer; and any other matter which this Act is to be, or may be prescribed.

Repeals Proclamations dated the 16th May, 1886 and the 7th August, 1893, relating to Viruthi Services and the Proclamation dated the 13th May, 1893, relating to Service Inam Lands, issued by the Ruler of the former State of Travancore and Proclamation No. XII of 1122 dated the 21st December, 1946, promulgated by the Ruler of the former state of Cochin are hereby repealed.

important_rules: Landholders are entitled to assignment of Service Inam lands that have vested in the Government, subject to conditions regarding occupancy and ceiling area.
The purchase price for the assignment of land is eight hundred and forty rupees per acre, payable in sixteen annual instalments, or a lump sum representing seventy-five percent of the total amount.
The Settlement Officer is responsible for issuing notices, determining compensation and purchase prices, and resolving disputes related to Service Inam lands.
Any amount due to the Government as arrears of purchase price is a first charge on the holding and is recoverable as public revenue.
Civil courts are barred from deciding matters that are required to be decided by officers or authorities under this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Settlement Officer, District Collector, Board of Revenue, Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings, determination of claims and objections, issuance of orders and notices, and recovery of dues as public revenue.

rights: Landholders have the right to assignment of Service Inam lands.
Landowners have the right to receive compensation for vested lands.
Any person aggrieved by an order of the Settlement Officer has the right to appeal.
duties: Landholders have a duty to pay the purchase price for assigned lands.
Landholders have a duty to respond to notices and provide claims or objections.
obligations: Obligation to pay purchase price for assigned land.
Obligation to comply with orders of the Settlement Officer, District Collector, and Board of Revenue.

key_procedures: Determination of compensation and purchase price by the Settlement Officer.
Application by landholder for assignment of Service Inam land.
Process of appeal to the District Collector against orders of the Settlement Officer.
Process of revision by the Board of Revenue against orders under appeal.
Issuance of pattas and other documents by the Settlement Officer after the order becomes final.
administration: The Government and its designated officers, including Settlement Officers, District Collectors, and the Board of Revenue.
important_notes: The vesting of lands and abolition of services takes effect from the 'appointed day'.
The Act repeals certain prior Proclamations relating to Service Inam lands.
Rules made under the Act must be laid before the Legislative Assembly.
The Act provides protection for actions taken in good faith by the Government or its officers.

title: THE KERALA SHOPS AND COMMERCIAL ESTABLISHMENTS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1969
purpose: To amend The Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1960 for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to The Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1960.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called The Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments (Amendment) Act, 1969 and specifies commencement dates for its provisions.
Inserts a new Chapter 1A titled 'Registration' into the principal Act, dealing with registration of establishments, application procedures, and competent authority.
Inserts a new section 13A titled 'Special casual leave for sterilisation operation' which grants special casual leave for male and female employees who undergo sterilisation operations.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 14
main_sections.description: Substitutes section 14 with a new section concerning 'Wages during leave period', detailing how wages are calculated for employees on leave under section 13 or section 13A.
Amends section 29 of the principal Act to renumber existing sub-sections and insert references to the newly inserted sections and sub-sections.

important_rules: Rule: Employers must apply for registration of their establishment to the competent authority.
Rule: Applications for registration must be made within sixty days from the date of commencement of the establishment.
Rule: Employees undergoing sterilisation operation are entitled to special casual leave: six days for a male employee and fourteen days for a female employee.
Rule: Wages for leave under section 13 or 13A are to be paid at the rate equal to the daily average of his or her total full-time earnings.

penalties: Fine not exceeding two hundred and fifty rupees for breach of provisions of Sections 5A and 5C.
Fine not exceeding ten rupees for every day during which the breach continues after conviction for the first breach.
Fine not exceeding ten rupees for every day during which the breach continues after receipt of notice from the competent authority to discontinue such breach.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Competent authority
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Prosecution for breaches of the Act's provisions, issuance of notices to discontinue breaches.

rights: Right to registration certificate for establishments.
Right to special casual leave for employees undergoing sterilisation operation.
Right to receive wages during leave periods.
Right to appeal against the order of the competent authority refusing to grant or renew a registration certificate or cancelling or suspending it.
duties: Duty of employer to apply for registration.
Duty of employer to provide information in the application.
Duty of employer to give notice to the competent authority of closing an establishment.
Duty of employer to display registration certificate.
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules.
obligations: Obligation to pay wages during leave periods as prescribed.
Obligation for the employer to continue to pay the employee the amount payable under section 14 in respect of the period of special casual leave at the time of discharge.

key_procedures: Procedure for registration of an establishment: Employer applies to the competent authority, specifying details of the establishment, and pays prescribed fees. The competent authority registers the establishment and issues a certificate if satisfied.

Procedure for appealing a decision on registration: An aggrieved person can appeal to the competent authority within sixty days of the order, accompanied by the prescribed fee. The appeal may be decided by notification in the Gazette.

Procedure for giving notice of closing an establishment: Employer to give notice within ten days of closing to the competent authority, who shall remove the name of the establishment from the register and cancel the registration certificate.
Procedure for obtaining special casual leave: Employees undergoing sterilisation operation are eligible, with specific durations for male and female employees.
administration: Competent authority (as defined in the Act)
important_notes: Registration certificate granted under this Act is not valid beyond the year in which it is granted but may be renewed from year to year.
Application for renewal of a registration certificate must be made at least thirty days before the expiry of the period thereof.

The competent authority may, after giving the holder of a registration certificate granted or renewed under this Act, an opportunity of being heard, by order cancel or suspend the registration certificate if it appears to it that such registration certificate has been obtained by misrepresentation or fraud or that the employer has contravened or failed to comply with any of the provisions of this Act or the rules made thereunder.
The provisions of Chapter 1A shall come into force at once and section 2 shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

title: The Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishment Workers Welfare Fund Act, 2006
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a Welfare Fund for the workers employed in shops and commercial establishments in the State of Kerala and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to workers employed in shops and commercial establishments in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.establishment: Includes a shop or commercial establishment to which this Act applies.
key_definitions.fund: The Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishment Workers Welfare Fund constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.worker: Means a person employed in or in connection with the work of any establishment, and includes such other class of persons, as may, from time to time, be specified by the Government, by notification in the Gazette.
key_definitions.shop: Means any premises where any trade or business is carried on or where any services are rendered to customers, and includes an office, a store-room, godown, workplace or premises, adjoining to or connected with any shop, or where the business is carried on. Provided that no premises where the cinema trade is carried on shall be deemed to be a shop.
key_definitions.commercial_establishment: Means an establishment which is not a shop, but which carries on any trade or business or works for gain or profit and includes an establishment which is connected with the management of any such trade or business or establishment, or which provides any service to any other establishment, and includes a hotel, restaurant, boarding or lodging house, cafe, eatery, cinema or any place of public entertainment or amusement. Provided that any establishment, which is exclusively a manufacturing or industrial establishment, shall not be considered as a commercial establishment.
key_definitions.employer: Means a person who employs one or more persons in any establishment, and includes,- (i) any person who is managing the affairs of any establishment, whether directly or through any other person or agency; (ii) any person who is appointed as the manager, or is in charge of the management, of any establishment; (iii) any occupier of any establishment, within the meaning of the Factories Act, 1948 (Central Act 63 of 1948); (iv) any contractor who undertakes to do any work in, or in connection with, any establishment, for and on behalf of the employer.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act, its geographical extent (State of Kerala), and the date of commencement.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as 'establishment', 'fund', 'worker', 'shop', 'commercial establishment', and 'employer'.
Establishes the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishment Workers Welfare Fund and outlines its administration.
Details the purposes for which the Welfare Fund can be utilized, such as providing financial assistance, medical aid, educational facilities, etc., to the workers.
Specifies the sources from which money will be credited to the Fund, likely including contributions from employers and government grants.
Outlines how the Fund will be managed, typically by a Welfare Board or a similar body.

main_sections.section_title: Power to grant loans or advances
main_sections.description: Grants the managing authority the power to provide loans or advances from the Fund to workers under certain conditions.
Allows for the provision of grants from the Fund for various welfare activities.
Specifies the power of the managing authority to borrow funds if needed.
Details how the surplus funds of the Welfare Fund can be invested.
Requires the maintenance of proper accounts for the Fund and mandates an annual audit.
Empowers the Government to frame rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the Welfare Board or managing authority to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules.

main_sections.section_title: Laying of rules and regulations before the Legislative Assembly
main_sections.description: Specifies the procedure for placing the rules and regulations before the Kerala Legislative Assembly.
Grants the Government the power to issue orders to remove any difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Authorizes the Government to issue directions to the Welfare Board or other authorities for the proper administration of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of any existing laws on the subject and savings provisions.

important_rules: Contributions to the Fund by employers and potentially employees.
Eligibility criteria for workers to receive benefits from the Fund.
Procedures for application and disbursement of benefits.
Guidelines for the investment and management of the Fund.

penalties: Failure to comply with provisions relating to contributions or other requirements of the Act may lead to penalties, likely including fines or other disciplinary actions as specified in the rules.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government and authorities appointed by the Government, likely including the Welfare Board and inspectors.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, demands for contributions, imposition of penalties, and legal proceedings if necessary.

rights: Workers have the right to receive welfare benefits from the Fund as per the provisions of the Act and rules.
Workers have the right to be informed about their contributions and entitlements.
duties: Employers have a duty to contribute to the Welfare Fund as prescribed.
Employers have a duty to maintain records and provide information as required by the Act.
obligations: The Welfare Board has an obligation to manage the Fund efficiently and disburse benefits appropriately.

key_procedures: Establishment of the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishment Workers Welfare Fund.
Collection of contributions from employers.
Disbursement of welfare benefits to eligible workers.
Maintenance of accounts and audit of the Fund.
administration: The State Government of Kerala, likely through a designated department and a Welfare Board.
important_notes: The Act was enacted to provide a safety net and enhance the well-being of workers in the organized sector.
The specific benefits and contributions will be detailed in the rules and regulations framed under the Act.
The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 31st day of October, 2006 and was published in Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 1728 dated 31st October, 2006.

title: The Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 2006
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a Fund to grant relief to, to promote the welfare of and to pay pension to workers coming under the purview of the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1960 and self employed persons, and for other matters incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to workers and self-employed persons coming under the purview of the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1960, and to establishments as defined in that Act and other relevant legislation. Employees coming under the Factories Act, 1948 or the Plantation Labour Act, 1951 or other Welfare Funds are excluded.

key_definitions.Board: The Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Workers' Welfare Fund Board constituted under section 6.
key_definitions.Chief Executive Officer: The Chief Executive Officer appointed under sub-section (1) of section 9.
key_definitions.Contribution: The sum of money payable to the Fund under section 4.
key_definitions.Employer: A person who employs, directly or indirectly, whether on behalf of himself or for any other person, one or more workers to do any work in institutions including hospital, nursing home, ayurvedic pharmacy, dispensary, medical shop, paramedical institution, parcel service, petrol-diesel-autogas bunks, fish processing establishment, food processing establishment, textile manufacturing establishment, hotel, restaurant, meat shop, computer-carpet allied service establishment, printing press, telephone booth, courier service, cooking gas distribution agency, hostel, hill produce-procurement and marketing establishment, small scale copra processing unit, small scale oil mill, leather procurement establishment, small scale foot wear bag manufacturing establishment, cinema theatre, photo/video studio, bakery, automobile-engineering establishment, establishment providing sound, light and decoration or in trade/commercial establishments coming under the purview of the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1960, (34 of 1960).
key_definitions.family: Means (i) husband/wife, their minor children, unmarried daughters, and (ii) father, mother and widowed daughters who are dependent on the worker or self employed person, coming under the purview of the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1960.
key_definitions.Fund: The Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Workers' Welfare Fund established under section 3.
key_definitions.Worker: Means an employee coming under the purview of the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1960, (34 of 1960) and includes a person employed in Establishments including hospitals, nursing home, ayurvedic pharmacy, dispensary, medical shop, paramedical institution, parcel service, petrol-diesel-autogas bunks, fish processing establishment, food processing establishment, textile manufacturing establishment, hotel, restaurant, meat shop, computer-carpet allied service establishment, printing press, telephone booth, courier service, cooking gas distribution agency, hostel, hill produce-procurement and marketing establishment, small scale copra processing unit, small scale oil mill, leather procurement establishment, small scale foot wear bag manufacturing establishment, cinema theatre, photo/video studio, bakery, automobile-engineering establishment, establishment providing sound, light and decoration or in trade/commercial establishments and who receives wages from the employer directly or other wise or through contractor or agent or by agreement or otherwise or a self employed person and any other person, declared by the Government from time to time, by notification in the Gazette, for the purposes of this Act to be an employee coming under the purview of the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Act.
key_definitions.member: Means a member of the Fund.
key_definitions.person: Includes a company, a firm, an association of individuals or a co-operative society registered or deemed to have been registered under the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969 (21 of 1969).
key_definitions.schedule: Means the schedule to this Act.
key_definitions.scheme: Means a scheme framed under section 3.
key_definitions.self employed person: Means a person who actually engages himself mainly in a work coming under the purview of the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1960 for the livelihood, without employing any workers, and which does not include a person who is a member of Vyapari Vyavasayi Welfare Fund or Ration dealers Welfare Fund.
key_definitions.wages: Means the total amount received by an employee including dearness allowance and other allowances in a calendar month.
key_definitions.year: Means a financial year commencing on the 1st day of April.

main_sections.description: This act may be called the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 2006. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'Chief Executive Officer', 'Contribution', 'Employer', 'family', 'Fund', 'Worker', 'member', 'person', 'schedule', 'scheme', 'self employed person', 'wages', and 'year'.

main_sections.section_title: Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishment Worker's Welfare Fund
main_sections.description: Establishes the 'Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Workers' Welfare Fund Scheme'. The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, frame a scheme for the establishment of a Fund for the welfare of the workers coming under this Act. The scheme shall provide for the constitution of the Fund and its administration. The Fund shall vest in and be administered by the Board constituted under section 6. The Fund may be utilized for purposes such as payment of pension, maternity wages, financial assistance for marriage or connection with the death of dependants, and educational benefits. The scheme is subject to the provisions of this Act and the schedule.

Specifies the contributions to the fund. Every member shall contribute Rs. 20 per month. Every employer shall contribute Rs. 20 per month in respect of each worker employed by him. A self-employed person shall pay Rs. 20 every month in addition to the contribution as per sub-section (1). The Government may contribute by way of grant, an amount of Rs. 5 per month paid by each member under sub-section (1) or Rs. 25 per cent of the employee's contribution, whichever is higher. Contributions are to be deposited in a co-operative bank recognized by the Board or Nationalised Banks. The Government may, by notification, revise the rate of contribution and the rate of grant.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, modify or vary the scheme framed under this Act either prospectively or retrospectively. Every notification under this sub-section shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, constitute a Board by the name 'The Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Workers' Welfare Fund Board' for the administration of the Fund and to supervise and management the activities financed from the fund. The Board shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal. The Board shall consist of fifteen Directors nominated by Government: five representing workers and self-employed persons, five representing employees, and five representing the Government. One of the Directors shall be appointed by the Government to be its Chairman.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office of the Directors
main_sections.description: Details the term of office for Directors.
Outlines the process for removing non-official Directors.
Describes the appointment of officers and staff.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the Board to borrow
main_sections.description: Grants the Board the power to borrow funds.
Allows for the determination of amounts due under the Act.

Every employer shall contribute Rs. 20 per month in respect of each worker employed by him.
A self-employed person shall pay Rs. 20 every month in addition to their own contribution.
The Government may contribute Rs. 5 per month per member or 25% of the employee's contribution, whichever is higher.
Contributions shall be deposited in a co-operative bank or Nationalised Bank.
Employers are prohibited from reducing wages or benefits of employees due to this Act.
Directors of the Board and other officials are considered public servants.
The Board is responsible for the administration and supervision of the Fund.
The Fund can be used for pensions, maternity benefits, financial assistance for marriage/death of dependants, and educational benefits for members.
No one is eligible for maternity wages beyond a maximum of two times.

Enhanced punishment for second or subsequent offenses (details not specified).
Power to recover damages (details not specified).

Right to appeal against certain decisions.

Transfer of funds from existing Welfare Funds.
