Employees covered under the Factories Act, 1948, Plantation Labour Act, 1951, or other Welfare Funds are generally excluded.
The Government has the power to modify the scheme prospectively or retrospectively.
The Board is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
Directors of the Board are nominated by the Government, with specific representation for workers, self-employed persons, employees, and the Government.
The Act provides for the recovery of damages and imposes penalties for offenses.
Civil Court jurisdiction is barred in certain matters.
The Government has the power to remove difficulties and make rules to implement the Act.

title: THE KERALA SHOPS AND COMMERCIAL ESTABLISHMENTS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1979
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1960, for purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to shops and commercial establishments in Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments (Amendment) Act, 1979. It shall come into force at once.

Inserts a new sub-section (4A) in section 18 of the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1960. This sub-section deals with directing the payment of compensation under sub-section (3) or sub-section (4) of section 18, and includes the wages of the employee for the period kept out of employment as part of the compensation.

title: The Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1960
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to the regulation of conditions of work and employment in shops and commercial establishments in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Kerala, including the city of Trivandrum, all municipalities constituted under the Madras District Municipalities Act, 1920, all areas falling within the jurisdiction of Panchayats under the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960, and other areas as may be specified by the Government by notification.

key_definitions.apprentice: A person aged not less than twelve years whom an employer employs in his service for training by himself or by any other person for any trade or calling.
key_definitions.child: Means a person who has not completed his fourteenth year.
key_definitions.closed: Means not open for the service of any customer or open to any business connected with the establishment.
key_definitions.commercial establishment: Means a commercial or industrial or trading or banking or insurance establishment, or an administrative service in which persons employed are mainly engaged in office work; hotel, restaurant, boarding or eating house, cafe or any other refreshment house, a theatre or any other place of public amusement or entertainment and includes such other establishment as the Government may, by notification, declare to be a commercial establishment for the purposes of this Act, but does not include a factory.
key_definitions.day: The period of twenty-four hours beginning at mid-night.
key_definitions.employee: Means a person wholly or principally employed in, and in connection with, any establishment and includes an apprentice.
key_definitions.employer: Means a person owning, or having ultimate control over the affairs of, an establishment and includes the manager, agent or other person acting in the general management or control of an establishment.
key_definitions.establishment: Means a shop or a commercial establishment.
key_definitions.inspector: Means an Inspector appointed under this Act.
key_definitions.leave: Means leave provided for in Chapter III of this Act.
key_definitions.opened: Means opened for the service of any customer or to any business connected with the establishment.
key_definitions.period of work: Means the time during which an employee is at the disposal of the employer.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.shop: Means any premises where any trade or business is carried on or where services are rendered to customers, and includes offices, recreums, godowns or warehouses, whether in the same premises or otherwise, used in connection with the trade or business, but does not include a commercial establishment or a shop attached to a factory where the persons employed in the shop are allowed the benefits provided for workers under the Factories Act, 1948.
key_definitions.spread over: The period between the commencement and the termination of the work of an employee on any day.
key_definitions.work: The period of seven days beginning at mid-night of Saturday night or such other night as may be approved in writing for a particular area by the prescribed authority.
key_definitions.year: Means a year commencing on the first day of January.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its extent to the State of Kerala, and its commencement date.

Defines various terms used in the Act, such as apprentice, child, closed, commercial establishment, day, employee, employer, establishment, inspector, leave, opened, period of work, prescribed, shop, spread over, work, and year.

Details exemptions from the provisions of the Act for certain persons and establishments, including those in government employment, persons involved in travelling, caretakers, establishments under the Central or any State Government, local authorities, establishments in mines and oil fields, establishments in bazaars, and factories governed by the Factories Act, 1948. Also exempts hospitals and other institutions for treatment or care of the sick, infirm, the destitute or the mentally unfit, and such other establishments as the Government may specify.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to apply Act to exempted persons or establishments.
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to apply all or any of the provisions of the Act to any class of persons or establishments exempted under Section 3, either wholly or with modifications.
Empowers the Government to exempt any establishment or class of establishments from all or any of the provisions of the Act, if it is satisfied that it is in the public interest to do so.

Specifies the maximum number of hours of work in an establishment, which shall not exceed eight hours in any day and forty-eight hours in any week. It also includes provisions for overtime work and the total number of overtime hours.
Deals with the rate of wages for overtime work, stating that employees working overtime shall be entitled to wages at twice the ordinary rate of wages.
Mandates that employees working for more than four hours in an establishment shall be given an interval for rest of at least one hour.
Regulates the spread over of an employee's work in an establishment, which shall not spread over more than ten and a half hours in any day.

States that no establishment shall be opened earlier than and closed later than such hours as may be fixed by the Government. It also mentions that any customer being served at the time of closing shall be allowed to complete their service.

main_sections.section_title: Closing of shops and grant of weekly holidays.
main_sections.description: Specifies that every shop shall remain entirely closed on one day of the week, to be specified by the shopkeeper, and that every person employed in a shop or commercial establishment shall be allowed in each week a holiday of one whole day.

States that the provisions of Chapter III (Holidays and Leave) shall not operate to the prejudice of any rights to which an employee may be entitled under any other law or under the terms of any award, agreement or contract of service.

Outlines the entitlement to annual leave with wages for employees, based on their continuous service. It specifies conditions for earning leave, accumulation of leave, and payment of wages during leave.
Deals with the calculation and payment of wages during the leave period.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Inspectors to act for employees.
main_sections.description: Empowers Inspectors to take action on behalf of employees in certain situations.
Grants the Government the power to exempt establishments from certain provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Application and amendment of the Payment of Wages Act.
main_sections.description: Likely relates to the application or amendment of the Payment of Wages Act in relation to this Act.
Concerns the requirement of notice for dismissal of employees.
Prohibits the employment of children in shops and establishments.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of employment of women and persons below seventeen years during night.
main_sections.description: Prohibits the employment of women and persons below seventeen years of age during night hours.
Mandates cleanliness, adequate ventilation, and proper lighting in establishments.
Requires precautions to be taken against fire in establishments.
Provides for the mechanism of appeals against orders passed under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Apportionment of expenses under preceding sections.
main_sections.description: Deals with the apportionment of expenses related to provisions in preceding sections.
Grants the Government the power to appoint Inspectors to enforce the provisions of the Act.
Outlines the powers and duties of Inspectors appointed under the Act.
Declares Inspectors to be public servants for the purposes of the Indian Penal Code.

main_sections.section_title: Employer to produce registers, records, etc., for inspection.
main_sections.description: Obligates employers to produce registers, records, and other documents for inspection by Inspectors.
Specifies the penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Maintenance of registers and records and display of notices.
main_sections.description: Requires employers to maintain registers and records and display notices as prescribed by the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Saving of certain rights and privileges.
main_sections.description: Saves certain existing rights and privileges of employees.
Provides indemnity to persons acting in good faith in pursuance of the Act.
Allows the Government to delegate its powers under the Act to other authorities.
Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to suspend provisions of the Act during fairs and festivals.
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to suspend provisions of the Act during fairs and festivals.
Repeals certain previous enactments.

important_rules: No establishment shall be required or allowed to work for more than eight hours in any day and forty-eight hours in any week.
Employees working overtime shall be entitled to wages at twice the ordinary rate of wages.
Employees working for more than four hours shall be given an interval for rest of at least one hour.
The period of work of an employee shall not spread over more than ten and a half hours in any day.
Every shop shall remain entirely closed on one day of the week.
Every employee shall be allowed in each week a holiday of one whole day.
No establishment shall be opened earlier than and closed later than such hours as may be fixed by the Government.
Annual leave with wages shall be granted to employees based on continuous service.
Children and persons below seventeen years of age are prohibited from working during night hours.
Establishments must maintain cleanliness, ventilation, and lighting.

penalties: Penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions (details not specified in table of contents).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Inspectors appointed under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspection of registers, records, and premises, and by taking action against contraventions.

rights: Right to weekly holiday.
Right to annual leave with wages.
Right to intervals for rest.
Right to overtime wages.
Saving of certain rights and privileges.
duties: Duty to maintain registers and records.
Duty to display notices.
Duty to provide for cleanliness, ventilation, and lighting.
Duty to take precautions against fire.
obligations: Employers are obligated to comply with the hours of work, leave, and holiday provisions.
Employers must allow employees intervals for rest and weekly holidays.
Employers must produce registers and records for inspection.

key_procedures: Procedure for determining hours of work and weekly holidays.
Procedure for calculating and paying overtime wages.
Procedure for granting annual leave with wages.
Procedure for appeals against orders.
Procedure for maintaining registers and records and displaying notices.
administration: The Government of Kerala (through relevant departments responsible for labor and employment).
important_notes: The Act consolidates and amends existing laws on the subject.
The Government has the power to exempt certain establishments or classes of establishments from the provisions of the Act.
The Government can also extend the provisions of the Act to exempted establishments.
The Act provides for the appointment of Inspectors with specific powers and duties.
Certain rights and privileges of employees are saved.
The Government can suspend provisions during fairs and festivals.

title: THE KERALA SHOPS AND COMMERCIAL ESTABLISHMENTS WORKERS' WELFARE FUND (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2008
purpose: To amend the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 2006 for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: The Act applies to workers who are members of the Kerala Labour Welfare Fund and coming under the purview of the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1960, and specifically addresses the membership and cessation of membership in the Welfare Fund constituted under the Act.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Workers' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2008, and it came into force on the 10th day of June, 2008.

This section amends Section 2 of the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 2006. It makes provisions of the Factories Act, 1948, or the Plantation Labour Act, 1951, applicable if they are not included under the purview of this Act.

This section amends section 3 of the principal Act by adding a clause (f) for the refund of the amount of contribution remitted by members who are unable to work, for a period of more than two years due to permanent physical infirmity or had completed the age of sixty years.

This section inserts a new Section 3A into the principal Act. This new section defines a 'worker' who is a member of the Kerala Labour Welfare Fund and coming under the purview of the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1960. It also outlines the conditions under which a worker ceases to be a member of the Labour Welfare Fund.

This section repeals the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Workers' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Ordinance, 2008. It also includes a saving clause stating that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act, as amended by this Act.

rights: Right to refund of contributions under specific circumstances (Section 3).
duties: Workers who are members of the Kerala Labour Welfare Fund and under the purview of the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1960, are considered members of the Welfare Fund constituted under this Act.
obligations: Workers becoming members under sub-section (1) of Section 3A shall cease to be members of the Labour Welfare Fund under the Kerala Labour Welfare Fund Act, 1975.

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act on June 10, 2008.
Amending existing sections of the principal Act.
Insertion of a new section to define worker membership and cessation.
Repeal of a previous ordinance and saving of actions taken under it.
administration: The administration of the Act is implied to be under the relevant departments responsible for labor welfare and commercial establishments in Kerala.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 2006.
The amendment came into force retrospectively from June 10, 2008.
The Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Workers' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Ordinance, 2008 has been repealed.
Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are saved.

title: The Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Workers Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2017
purpose: To further amend The Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 2006, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to workers in Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments.

main_sections.description: (1) This Act may be called the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Workers' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2017. (2) It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 15th day of March, 2007.

In The Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 2006 (24 of 2006), in sub-section (4) of section 3, after clause (f), the following clauses shall be inserted, namely:-- "(g) for payment of the amount remitted as employees contribution by a member who has made contribution to the Fund continuously for at least for a period of two years, in the event of getting employment in Government or semi-Government Institutions, if such member has not availed any benefits from the Fund; (h) for payment of the amount remitted as contribution to the Fund to the dependants of a member who is not eligible for financial assistance on death."

important_rules: Rule 1: Payment of remitted employee contribution to members who have contributed for at least two years and get employment in Government or semi-Government Institutions, provided they haven't availed benefits.
Rule 2: Payment of remitted contribution to dependants of a member who is not eligible for financial assistance on death.

rights: Right to receive employee contribution under specific conditions.
Right for dependants to receive contribution on member's death under specific conditions.

key_procedures: Procedure for claiming employee contribution refund under sub-section (4) (g).
Procedure for claiming contribution payment by dependants under sub-section (4) (h).
administration: Law (Legislation-C) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The amendment is deemed to have come into force on March 15, 2007.
This amendment further amends The Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 2006.

title: THE KERALA SHOPS AND COMMERCIAL ESTABLISHMENTS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2014
purpose: This Act amends The Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1960.
scope: Applies to shops and commercial establishments in Kerala.

key_definitions.commercial establishment: Includes an establishment where business is carried on, but does not include a factory or a shop to which the provisions of the Factories Act, 1948, apply.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies when it comes into force. This amendment Act is referred to as the Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments (Amendment) Act, 2014.

Amends Section 1 of the Principal Act by substituting certain words and clauses, likely related to definitions or scope of application. It appears to be an amendment to the definition of 'establishment'.

Inserts new sections into the Principal Act. This section details specific amendments, including the insertion of new clauses related to the operation of shops and establishments, especially concerning opening and closing hours, and provisions for women employees.
Amends Section 21 of the Principal Act, likely related to the regulation of hours of work, rest intervals, and weekly holidays.
Amends Sections 29 and 30 of the Principal Act, possibly concerning registration, renewal of registration, and other administrative aspects.
Amends Sections 34 to 36 of the Principal Act, which typically deal with penalties, fines, and other enforcement provisions.

This section likely deals with the repeal of any existing provisions that are inconsistent with this Amendment Act and savings clauses to ensure continuity or validity of actions taken under the previous provisions.

important_rules: Shops and establishments may be permitted to remain open for longer hours, subject to prescribed conditions and payment of additional fees.
Specific provisions regarding the employment of women and their working hours are included.
The Act appears to introduce rules regarding overtime for employees.
There are provisions related to weekly holidays and rest intervals for employees.

penalties: Penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act, likely including fines.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala, through designated authorities (e.g., Labour Department officials).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, imposition of penalties, and prosecution for non-compliance.

rights: Right of employees to weekly holidays and rest intervals.
Rights related to working hours and conditions for women employees.
duties: Duty of employers to comply with the provisions of the Act regarding working hours, holidays, and conditions of employment.
Duty to obtain registration and renewal of registration.
Duty to maintain records and provide information to authorities.
obligations: Employers have an obligation to ensure the health, safety, and welfare of their employees as per the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure for applying for and obtaining registration/renewal of registration for shops and establishments.
Procedures for notifying authorities about changes in establishment details.
Procedures for enforcement actions, including inspections and penalties.
administration: Department of Labour, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act specifies that certain provisions come into effect from the date of publication in the Gazette.
The amendment introduces flexibility in the operating hours of shops and establishments, subject to regulatory oversight.
Special attention is given to the welfare and working conditions of women employees.

title: The Kerala Sick Textile Undertakings (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1985
purpose: To provide for the acquisition and transfer of certain sick textile undertakings to the Government and their management or re-opening for ensuring the production of essential textiles and employment of workers.
scope: This Act applies to sick textile undertakings in the State of Kerala that are specified in the Act or are notified by the Government.

key_definitions.sick_textile_undertaking: An industrial undertaking engaged in the manufacture of textiles, which is sick and requires acquisition and transfer for its effective management and revival.
key_definitions.undertaking: An industrial undertaking engaged in the manufacture of textiles, and includes all the assets and liabilities of such undertaking.
key_definitions.appropriate_government: Refers to the Government of Kerala.
key_definitions.person_interested: Includes owners, creditors, employees, and other stakeholders of the undertaking.

main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to acquire sick textile undertakings through notification if it is satisfied that such acquisition is necessary for the purpose of the Act.
Details the process and conditions under which the acquired undertakings are transferred to the Government or an authorized person/corporation.
Outlines the powers of the Government or the authorized person/corporation in managing the acquired undertakings, including the power to re-open, re-organize, or re-deploy assets.
Addresses the employment status, rights, and liabilities of the employees of the acquired undertakings.
Enumerates the broad powers of the Government in relation to the acquired undertakings, including making rules, appointing officers, and issuing directions.
Provides for the mechanism of appeal against certain orders passed under the Act.
Specifies the penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides for the protection of persons acting in good faith in pursuance of the provisions of the Act.
Grants the Government the power to remove any difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of any existing law and savings related to actions taken under such law.
Clarifies the applicability of other laws in conjunction with this Act.
Provides for the validation of certain actions taken prior to the commencement of the Act.
Grants the Government the power to issue directions to any person or authority for the proper implementation of the Act.
Deals with the transfer of all property, rights, liabilities, and obligations of the acquired undertaking to the Government or the transferee.

important_rules: Employees of the acquired undertaking are deemed to be in the service of the Government or the transferee.
The Government can appoint officers to manage the affairs of the acquired undertaking.
All contracts, deeds, and other instruments in relation to the undertaking are to have effect as if made by the Government or the transferee.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both, for contravention of provisions or rules.
Fine for contravention of directions issued by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government (Government of Kerala) and officers appointed by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications, orders, directions, appointment of officers, and legal proceedings for penalties.

rights: Right of employees to continue in service with continuity of service.
Right to compensation or benefits as may be determined by the Government.
duties: Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules.
Duty of the Government to manage or cause to manage the acquired undertaking for its revival.
obligations: Obligation to transfer all assets and liabilities of the sick textile undertaking to the Government.
Obligation of the transferee to manage the undertaking for the production of textiles and employment.

key_procedures: Notification by the Government of its intention to acquire a sick textile undertaking.
Acquisition of the undertaking upon service of notice.
Transfer of the undertaking to the Government or a designated authority.
Management and revival of the undertaking by the Government or its appointed agency.
Termination or alteration of employment contracts of employees if necessary for revival, with appropriate provisions for compensation.
administration: The Industries Department of the Government of Kerala, and any other department or agency specifically appointed by the Government for the management of the acquired undertakings.
important_notes: The Act aims to protect the interests of workers by ensuring employment and continuity of service.
The Government has extensive powers to ensure the revival and efficient operation of the acquired sick textile units.
The Act provides for the smooth transfer of ownership and liabilities to facilitate the revival process.

title: The Kerala Sick Textile Undertakings (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Amendment Act, 1990
purpose: To amend The Kerala Sick Textile Undertakings (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1974.
scope: Applies to sick textile undertakings in Kerala.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as The Kerala Sick Textile Undertakings (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Amendment Act, 1990 and its commencement.

Amends Section 1 of the Principal Act (The Kerala Sick Textile Undertakings (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1974) by inserting references to "or sick textile undertaking" after "textile undertaking".

Amends Section 2 of the Principal Act. It specifically addresses the definition of 'sick textile undertaking' by referencing the definition in Section 3(1)(o) of the Sick Textile Undertakings (Nationalisation) Act, 1974 and other related legislative provisions.

Amends Section 10-C of the Principal Act. It clarifies provisions related to the transfer of undertakings and liabilities, with a specific reference to the Sick Textile Undertakings (Nationalisation) Act, 1974.

important_rules: The Act amends specific sections of the original Act.
The definition of 'sick textile undertaking' is linked to national legislation.
important_notes: The amendment is based on existing national legislation regarding sick textile undertakings.
References are made to specific sections of the Principal Act of 1974 and the Sick Textile Undertakings (Nationalisation) Act, 1974.

title: The Kerala Slum Areas (Improvement and Clearance) Act, 1981
purpose: To provide for the improvement and clearance of slum areas in the State of Kerala and for the matters connected therewith. The act aims to make provisions for the improvement, development, clearance or re-development of land and the erection of buildings in slum areas and to deal with the eviction of persons from such areas.
scope: The Act applies to slum areas within the State of Kerala. It covers the improvement, development, clearance, and re-development of land and buildings within these areas. It also outlines procedures for the eviction of persons from slum areas.

key_definitions.slum area: As defined in the Act, areas considered to be slum areas for the purpose of this Act are those that are or may become sources of danger to health, safety or convenience of the public by reason of being unsanitary, dilapidated or overcrowded, or by the presence of buildings in any structures which are insanitary, dilapidated or which for any reason are not in a sanitary condition. Land referred to in this context includes sites of buildings, and land occupied by dwellings and people of such low income groups as may be prescribed.
key_definitions.competent authority: The competent authority refers to the authority designated to carry out the provisions of the Act, which can be the Corporation of Trivandrum, the Corporation of Calicut, or any municipal council or township committee or panchayat concerned, or the development authority or town planning trust having jurisdiction over the area in which the land is situated.

main_sections.description: Deals with the apportionment of amounts by the competent authority to persons entitled to receive it. It also provides for dispute resolution regarding apportionment, with appeals to the Collector and the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Payment of amount or deposit of the same in court.
main_sections.description: Specifies how payments or deposits are to be made to entitled persons, including provisions for deposit in court if persons are not found or refuse to receive payment.
Details the calculation and payment of interest on amounts due to persons entitled to receive payment for land acquired under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of competent authority in relation to determination of amount etc.
main_sections.description: Empowers the competent authority to determine amounts related to acquisition of land under Section 16, including requiring information from persons for determination. It also outlines inquiry powers, including summoning persons, examining evidence, and requisitioning public records.

Governs the use of land acquired under the Act. The Government can undertake measures for improvement, clearance, or re-development of land and erection of buildings. Land can also be leased or allotted for slum dwellers or persons of low income groups, subject to prescribed terms.

main_sections.section_title: Tenants from slum areas not to be evicted without permission of competent authority.
main_sections.description: Prohibits the eviction of tenants from slum areas without the prior written permission of the competent authority. It outlines the process for applying for and granting such permission, considering factors like alternative accommodation and the interest of improvement and clearance.

main_sections.section_title: Appeals against orders refusing to grant permission.
main_sections.description: Provides for appeals against orders of the competent authority refusing to grant permission for eviction. Such appeals are to be made to the Collector, and further appeals to the Government.

Allows the Government to revise orders passed by the Collector or the competent authority under specific sections of the Act, either suo motu or on application. The Government can also review orders made under sub-section (1) more than three months previously.

main_sections.section_title: Resumption of possession of premises vacated by a tenant.
main_sections.description: Deals with the resumption of possession of premises vacated by a tenant. The competent authority can order the resumption of possession for the purpose of improvement or re-erection of the building. It also outlines procedures for the owner to apply for and obtain possession.

main_sections.section_title: Rent of buildings in slum areas.
main_sections.description: Addresses the rent payable by tenants in slum areas, particularly concerning buildings acquired or improved under the Act. It differentiates rent payable by tenants occupying land acquired by the Government and those occupying buildings on land not acquired. It also specifies rent payable for buildings re-erected by the Government or local authority.

main_sections.section_title: Tenants not to sub-let or alienate.
main_sections.description: Prohibits tenants in slum areas from sub-letting or alienating their rights in a building without the permission of the competent authority. Such sub-leases or alienations are invalid and void.

main_sections.section_title: Application to Government or local authority.
main_sections.description: States that Sections 22 and 23 also apply to tenants of any building in a slum area belonging to the Government or any local authority.

Grants the competent authority the power to enter any building or land in a slum area or any area where the conditions necessitate action under the Act, for the purpose of inspection, measurement, valuation, survey, and to execute any work authorized by the Act.

Empowers the competent authority to inspect drains, latrines, urinals, cesspools, pipes, sewers, and channels, and to examine works under construction in slum areas. It also covers the inspection of land and buildings for the purpose of carrying out work.

main_sections.section_title: Power to enter land adjoining (and where work is in progress).
main_sections.description: Allows any officer authorized by the competent authority to enter any land adjoining a slum area where work is in progress, for the purpose of depositing or obtaining access to any site or materials required for the work.

Authorizes officers to break into buildings if necessary to carry out their duties under the Act, with provisions for opening doors, gates, or barriers, and dealing with occupants who may be absent or refuse entry.

main_sections.section_title: Entry to be made in day time.
main_sections.description: Specifies that entry into buildings under the Act is generally to be made during daylight hours, except in specific circumstances.

main_sections.section_title: Owner's consent ordinarily to be obtained.
main_sections.description: States that the owner's consent should ordinarily be obtained before entering or taking possession of a building or land. However, no such entry is required if there is no occupant and the owner is absent, provided notice of intention is given.

main_sections.section_title: Power of eviction to be exercised only by the competent authority.
main_sections.description: Confirms that the power of eviction can only be exercised by the competent authority, who may order the eviction of occupants from buildings if they have failed to vacate as required.

main_sections.section_title: Power to remove offensive or dangerous trades from slum areas.
main_sections.description: Grants the competent authority the power to order the removal of offensive or dangerous trades from slum areas to prevent nuisances.

Provides for appeals against orders or directions issued by the competent authority or the Collector. Appeals are to be made to the Collector within thirty days, and further appeals can be made to the Government within thirty days of the Collector's order.

important_rules: Tenants in slum areas cannot be evicted without the prior written permission of the competent authority (Section 22).
Sub-letting or alienation of rights by tenants in slum areas is prohibited without the competent authority's permission and is considered invalid (Section 27).
The competent authority has the power to order the removal of offensive or dangerous trades from slum areas (Section 36).
Entry into buildings for purposes of the Act is generally to be made during daylight hours (Section 33).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The competent authority (which can be a Corporation, Municipal Council, Township Committee, Panchayat, Development Authority, or Town Planning Trust, depending on the area). The Collector and the Government also have roles in appeal and revision processes.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement involves powers of entry, inspection, order issuance (e.g., for eviction, removal of trades), and the ability to take action where individuals fail to comply with the Act's provisions. Appeals and revisions provide mechanisms for challenging decisions.

rights: Persons entitled to receive compensation or payment for acquired land have the right to receive such amounts, including interest (Section 17, 18, 19).
Persons aggrieved by orders under the Act have the right to appeal (Section 23, 37).
Tenants have the right to not be evicted without due process and permission (Section 22).
The right to alternative accommodation is a consideration when evicting tenants (Section 22(3)).
duties: Persons whose land is acquired under the Act have a duty to cooperate in the determination of amounts (Section 17, 20).
Tenants have a duty to not sub-let or alienate their rights without permission (Section 27).
Occupants have a duty to vacate premises when ordered to do so (Section 25, 35).
obligations: The Government has an obligation to undertake measures for the improvement, clearance, or re-development of slum areas (Section 21).
The competent authority has obligations to conduct inquiries and ensure compliance with the Act.
Owners of land/buildings have obligations to comply with orders and directions issued under the Act, including vacating premises when required.

key_procedures: Procedure for apportionment of amounts: Disputes are referred to the Collector and then to the Government if necessary (Section 17).
Procedure for payment or deposit of amounts: Payments are made to entitled persons or deposited in court (Section 18).
Procedure for eviction of tenants: Application to the competent authority for permission, with specific factors to be considered. Appeals are provided (Section 22, 23).
Procedure for entry and inspection: Officers authorized by the competent authority can enter and inspect premises and land (Section 29, 30, 31, 32).
Procedure for appeals against orders: Appeals are made to the Collector, then to the Government (Section 37).
administration: The primary administrative body is the 'competent authority,' which varies by local jurisdiction (Corporation, Municipal Council, etc.). The Collector and the Government also play significant administrative and oversight roles.
important_notes: The Act provides for the Government to undertake measures for the improvement, clearance, or re-development of slum areas (Section 21(1)).
Land acquired under the Act can be allotted or leased for the accommodation of slum dwellers or persons of low income groups, subject to prescribed terms and conditions (Section 21(2)).
Appeals against orders of the competent authority regarding eviction permissions must be filed within thirty days (Section 23, 37).
The Government has the power to revise orders passed by subordinate authorities (Section 24).

title: THE KERALA SMALL CAUSE COURTS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1990
purpose: To amend the Kerala Small Cause Courts Act, 1957.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Small Cause Courts Act, 1957. The amendment concerns rules to be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Small Cause Courts (Amendment) Act, 1990.
Inserts a new section 32A into the Kerala Small Cause Courts Act, 1957, concerning rules to be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

important_rules: Rule 32A: Every rule made under this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before the Legislative Assembly while it is in session for a total period of fourteen days which may be comprised in one session or in two successive sessions, and if, before the expiry of the session in which it is so laid or the session immediately following, the Legislative Assembly makes any modification in the rule or decides that the rule should not be made, the rule shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect, as the case may be; so, however, that any such modification or annulment shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that rule.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Legislative Assembly
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Modification or annulment of rules laid before it.

rights: Right of the Legislative Assembly to modify or annul rules.
obligations: Government's obligation to lay rules before the Legislative Assembly.

key_procedures: Procedure for laying rules before the Legislative Assembly: Rules made under the Act must be presented to the Legislative Assembly for a total period of fourteen days, which can span one or two successive sessions. The Assembly has the power to modify or annul these rules.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be related to the courts and the Legislative Assembly of Kerala.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 28th day of February 1990 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 193 dated the 1st March 1990.

title: The Kerala Small Cause Courts Act, 1957
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to Courts of Small Causes in Kerala.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala.  It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.  The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.court_of_small_causes: Means a Court of Small Causes constituted under this Act, and includes any person exercising jurisdiction under this Act in any such Court.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (the whole of the State of Kerala), and that it will come into force on a date appointed by the Government.

Specifies that this Act does not affect certain existing jurisdictions of courts, including the Cochin Village Courts Act, 1888, and the Madras Village Courts Act, 1888, as in force in the Malabar district.
Defines 'Court of Small Causes' in the context of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of Courts of Small Causes
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to establish Courts of Small Causes by notification in the Gazette, and defines their local limits and where they may be held.
Details the appointment and qualifications of a Judge of a Court of Small Causes, including the appointment of times of sitting and the requirement of a qualified lawyer.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of times of sitting in certain circumstances
main_sections.description: Allows the appointment of specific sitting times for the Court.
Provides for the appointment of Additional Judges to assist the Judge.

main_sections.section_title: Power to require two Judges to sit as a Bench
main_sections.description: Grants the power to require two Judges to sit as a Bench, especially in cases where the decision of a single Judge might be questioned.

main_sections.section_title: Decision in case heard by a Bench
main_sections.description: Outlines how decisions are made when a case is heard by a Bench of two Judges, including provisions for differences of opinion and reference to the High Court.
Provides for the appointment of a Registrar for Courts of Small Causes.
Specifies the duties of ministerial officers and the High Court's power to impose further duties.

main_sections.section_title: Cognizance of suits by Courts of Small Causes
main_sections.description: States that Courts of Small Causes shall not take cognizance of suits except those specified in the Schedule.

main_sections.section_title: Exclusive jurisdiction of Courts of Small Causes
main_sections.description: Declares that the jurisdiction of Courts of Small Causes is exclusive, with exceptions as provided by the Act or other enactments.

main_sections.section_title: Application of the Code of Civil Procedure
main_sections.description: States that the procedure prescribed in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, shall be followed in all suits cognizable by these Courts, subject to specific provisions of this Act.
Allows the Registrar to try suits under certain conditions and to execute decrees.

main_sections.section_title: Admission, return and rejection of plaints by Registrar
main_sections.description: Defines the Registrar's powers regarding the admission, return, or rejection of plaints.

main_sections.section_title: Passing of decrees by Registrar on confession
main_sections.description: Outlines the Registrar's authority to pass decrees based on a confession.
Details the Registrar's role in the execution of decrees.

main_sections.section_title: Adjournment of cases by chief ministerial officer
main_sections.description: Allows the chief ministerial officer to adjourn cases when the Judge is absent.

main_sections.section_title: Return of plaints in suits involving questions of title
main_sections.description: Specifies when plaints should be returned if they involve questions of title.

main_sections.section_title: Appeal from certain orders of Court of Small Causes
main_sections.description: Provides for appeals from certain orders of the Court of Small Causes to the District Court.

main_sections.section_title: Revision of decrees and orders of Court of Small Causes
main_sections.description: Allows for revision of decrees and orders of the Court of Small Causes by the High Court.
States the finality of decrees and orders, subject to the provisions of the Act and the Code of Civil Procedure.

main_sections.section_title: Subordination of Courts of Small Causes
main_sections.description: Establishes the subordination of Courts of Small Causes to the District Court and the High Court.
Provides for the vacation period for Courts of Small Causes.
Mandates the use of a seal by Courts of Small Causes.

main_sections.section_title: Abolition of Courts of Small Causes
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to abolish Courts of Small Causes.

main_sections.section_title: Saving of power to appoint Judge of Courts of Small Causes to other office
main_sections.description: Reserves the Government's power to appoint a Judge of a Small Cause Court to another office.

main_sections.section_title: Application of Act to Courts invested with jurisdiction of Court of Small Causes
main_sections.description: Explains the application of the Act to courts invested with the jurisdiction of Courts of Small Causes.

important_rules: Rules regarding the appointment of Judges and Additional Judges.
Provisions for the constitution of Benches for hearing cases.
Procedures for the admission, return, and rejection of plaints.
Rules for the execution of decrees.
Procedures for appeals and revisions of orders.
Provisions related to the vacation of Courts.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: High Court, District Court, Registrar, Judges of Small Cause Courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through judicial proceedings, appeals, and revisions as prescribed by the Act and the Code of Civil Procedure.

rights: Right to appeal from certain orders of Courts of Small Causes.
Right to apply for revision of decrees and orders.
duties: Duty of Judges to discharge their functions.
Duty of ministerial officers to perform their duties.
Duty to comply with the Code of Civil Procedure.

key_procedures: Procedure for the establishment of Courts of Small Causes.
Procedure for the appointment of Judges and other officers.
Procedure for the trial of suits.
Procedure for the execution of decrees.
Procedure for appeals and revisions.
Procedure for the application of the Code of Civil Procedure.
administration: The Kerala State Legislature and the High Court of Kerala appear to be the primary administrative bodies, with the Government playing a role in establishment and appointments.
important_notes: The Act aims to consolidate and amend the law relating to Courts of Small Causes.
Savings clause preserves certain existing jurisdictions.
The Act specifies which suits are cognizable by Courts of Small Causes.

title: The Kerala Small Plantation Workers Welfare Fund Act, 2008
purpose: To provide for the establishment and administration of a welfare fund for small plantation workers in Kerala and to make better provision for the promotion of their welfare.
scope: Applies to small plantation workers in Kerala.  The Act defines 'small plantation' and 'plantation worker'.

key_definitions.small_plantation: As defined in the Act, likely referring to plantations below a certain size or acreage, differentiating from large-scale plantations.
key_definitions.plantation_worker: A person employed on a plantation for wages, including those engaged in cultivation, harvesting, processing, and other related activities on a plantation.
key_definitions.welfare_fund: The fund established under the Act for the welfare of plantation workers.
key_definitions.Board: Refers to the Board constituted under the Act for the administration of the Welfare Fund.

main_sections.description: Specifies the name of the Act, its geographical application within Kerala, and when it comes into force.
Provides definitions for various terms used throughout the Act, such as 'plantation', 'worker', 'employer', 'Board', 'Fund', etc.
Details the creation of the Small Plantation Workers' Welfare Fund.
Describes the formation, powers, and functions of the Board responsible for managing the Welfare Fund.
Outlines how contributions to the Welfare Fund are collected from employers and workers.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and Functions of the Board
main_sections.description: Specifies the responsibilities of the Board in administering the Fund, investing funds, and disbursing benefits.
Explains the purposes for which the Welfare Fund can be used, such as providing financial assistance, medical aid, education, etc., to workers.
Grants the Government the authority to frame rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Empowers the Board to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules for the efficient administration of the Fund.
Authorizes the Government to issue directions to remove any difficulties in the implementation of the Act.

important_rules: Employers are obligated to contribute to the Welfare Fund on behalf of their workers.
Contributions to the fund are to be made at prescribed rates.
The Board is responsible for the proper management and investment of the fund.
The fund can be utilized for various welfare measures for plantation workers, including financial assistance, medical aid, and educational support.

penalties: Penalties for failure to pay contributions.
Penalties for contravention of provisions of the Act or rules.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala, through designated authorities and the Board.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the imposition of fines and other legal actions as stipulated in the Act.

rights: Right of plantation workers to benefit from the Welfare Fund.
Right to receive various welfare schemes and assistance.
duties: Duty of employers to contribute to the Welfare Fund.
Duty of the Board to administer the fund efficiently and for the benefit of workers.
obligations: Obligation of employers to register with the Board and comply with contribution requirements.

key_procedures: Procedure for the establishment and functioning of the Board.
Procedure for collection and remittance of contributions.
Procedure for application and disbursement of benefits from the Welfare Fund.
Procedure for making rules and regulations under the Act.
administration: The Government of Kerala and the Board of Trustees established under the Act.
important_notes: The Act aims to address the welfare needs of workers in small plantations, which may have different characteristics from larger plantations.
The Act emphasizes the role of contributions from both employers and employees in funding the welfare measures.
The Board has the authority to invest the fund in safe and profitable ventures to ensure its growth.

title: THE KERALA SMALL PLANTATION WORKERS' WELFARE FUND ACT, 2008
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a Fund for promoting the welfare of, and to pay pension to, the workers in small plantations in the State of Kerala and for certain other matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to workers in small plantations in the State of Kerala and employers of such plantations.

key_definitions.Board: The Kerala Small Plantation Workers' Welfare Fund Board constituted under section 6.
key_definitions.Chief Executive Officer: The Chief Executive Officer appointed under sub-section (1) of section 9.
key_definitions.contribution: Means the sum of money payable to the Fund in accordance with the provisions of section 5.
key_definitions.employer: In relation to a plantation, means the person who has the ultimate control over the affairs of the plantation, and where the affairs of any plantation are entrusted to any other person (whether known as a managing agent or manager or superintendent or by any other name) such person shall be deemed as the employer in relation to that plantation.
key_definitions.family: Means wife or husband, minor sons and unmarried daughters of a plantation worker and includes his father, mother and mentally retarded or physically handicapped or widowed children who are solely dependent upon him.
key_definitions.Fund: Means the Small Plantation Worker's Welfare Fund established under section 3.
key_definitions.member: Means a member of the Fund.
key_definitions.plantation: Means any land used or intended to be used for cultivating one or more than one of rubber, tea, coffee, cardamom, coco, oil palm or cashew.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Schedule: Means the Schedule to this Act.
key_definitions.Scheme: Means a Scheme framed under sub section (1) of section 3.
key_definitions.small plantation: Means a plantation having an extent less than five hectares and where one or more small plantation workers are employed, but shall not include a plantation as defined in the Plantations Labour Act, 1951 (Central Act 69 of 1951).
key_definitions.small plantation worker: Means a person engaged for doing any work in a small plantation for not less than ninety days in the preceding twelve months for wages or reward, whether directly or through any contractor or agent, of the owner or company or family or Trust or Society and includes any self-employed person working in his own small plantation having an extent not more than half hectare.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Small Plantation Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 2008, it extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force at once.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including Board, Chief Executive Officer, contribution, employer, family, Fund, member, plantation, prescribed, Schedule, Scheme, small plantation, small plantation worker, and year.

main_sections.section_title: Small Plantation Workers' Welfare Fund Scheme
main_sections.description: The Government shall, by notification in the Gazette, frame a Scheme to be called the "Kerala Small Plantation Workers' Welfare Fund Scheme" and thereof after as soon as may constitute a Fund in accordance with the provisions of this Act and the Scheme. The Fund shall vest in the Board and be administered by the Board. Subject to the provisions of this Act, the Scheme may provide for all or any of the matters specified in the Schedule.

main_sections.section_title: Saving of certain rights and privileges
main_sections.description: On the date of commencement of this Act, any privileges which have been provided by the employer to the worker shall not be denied or reduced by the reason of payment of contribution.
Details the contribution amounts for every plantation worker, every employer, every self-employed person, and the Government to the Welfare Fund annually.

The Government shall, by notification in the Gazette, constitute a Board by the name "The Kerala Small Plantation Workers' Welfare Fund Board" for the administration of the Fund, to supervise and exercise the functions including the payment of financial assistance from the Fund. The Board shall be a body corporate by the name aforesaid, having perpetual succession and a common seal and shall, in the said name, sue and be sued. The Board shall consist of fifteen Directors as may be nominated by the Government as hereinafter provided, namely— (i) five members representing the plantation workers, (ii) five members representing the employers, (iii) five members representing the Government. The Government may appoint one of the Directors of the Board to be the Chairperson. The Government shall publish in the Gazette, the names of the Chairperson and the Directors of the Board. The Board shall administer the Fund vested in it, in such manner as specified in the Scheme. The Board may, with the previous approval of the Government, delegate the powers and functions under this Act or the Scheme as it may consider necessary for the efficient administration of the Fund to the Chief Executive Officer, subject to such condition and restrictions as may be specified.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office of the Directors
main_sections.description: A Director nominated under sub-section (3) of section 6 shall hold office for a period of three years from the date of such nomination, Provided that a Director may continue as Director till the appointment of his successor. Notwithstanding anything contained in section 8, the Government may, at any time for the reasons to be recorded in writing, remove any Director of the Board from his office, after giving him a reasonable opportunity of showing cause against the proposed removal. Provided that if the Government are of the opinion that it is not expedient in the public interest to record the reasons in writing or to give an opportunity, it shall not be necessary to record in writing the reasons for removal or to give an opportunity of showing cause against the proposed removal. Any Director may resign his office, by giving notice in writing to the Government, but shall continue in office until the resignation is accepted by the Government. A casual vacancy of the Director may be filled up by the Government and Director so appointed shall hold office for the unexpired term of office of the Director in whose vacancy he is appointed.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, remove any non-official Director of the Board from the said position on the following reasons - (a) If he absents himself for three consecutive meetings, without the permission of the Board. Provided that such absence may be condoned by the Board for sufficient reasons before the publication of the notification in the Gazette, (b) If the Government are of the opinion that he is ineligible to function as Director or has become incapable or the continuance of such Director by abusing his position is detrimental to the public interest Provided that before removing a Director under this sub-section, he shall be given a reasonable opportunity to show cause why he should not be removed. A non-official Director of the Board removed under clause (a) of sub-section (1) shall be disqualified for re-nomination as a Director of the Board for a period of three years from the date of his removal, unless otherwise ordered by the Government. A non-official Director of the Board removed under clause (b) of sub-section (1) shall not be eligible for re-nomination until he is declared by an order of the Government to be no longer ineligible.

The Government may appoint a Chief Executive Officer and such number of other officers and employees as may consider necessary for carrying out the functions of the Board under this Act. The conditions of appointment, service and the scales of pay of the officers and employees referred to in sub-section (1) shall be, as may be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the Board to borrow
main_sections.description: The Board may, from time to time with the previous approval of the Government and subject to such terms and conditions as may be specified by the Government, borrow the required amount for carrying out the purposes of this Act.

The Chief Executive Officer or any other officer authorised by him in this behalf may, after making such enquiry as he may consider necessary, from employer or plantation worker under the provisions of this Act and the Scheme made thereunder to ascertain the contribution to be received from the employer or the plantation worker as per the provision of this Act or the Scheme made thereunder.

main_sections.section_title: Provisional assessment and collection of contribution
main_sections.description: Every employer liable to pay contribution under section 5 shall, pending determination of the amount due from him under section 11, pay on every three months by way of an advance contribution and amount equal to one fourth of the amount payable annually by him according to the latest assessment under the said section, in the time and manner as specified in the Scheme. If the advance contribution of the employer is not paid on or before the due date, the officer authorised under section 11 or the Chief Executive Officer shall issue a notice to the defaulter showing the amount of arrears, and, if the contribution is not paid within fifteen days of the receipt of such notice, it may be recovered in the manner provided in section 13 of this Act.

important_rules: Every plantation worker shall contribute for every half year one hundred and twenty rupees each to the Fund.
Every employer shall contribute to the Fund every half year an amount of one hundred and twenty rupees equal to the contribution of the worker to the Fund.
Every self-employed member shall contribute for every half-year two hundred and forty rupees each to the Welfare Fund.
The Government shall contribute to the Fund at the rate of sixty rupees for half year for each worker/each self-employed person.
The contribution shall be paid to the Chief Executive Officer or to any officer authorised by the Board in this behalf.

penalties: Offences by companies - If any person contravenes any provision of this Act or any rule or scheme made thereunder, for which no penalty is provided for in this Act, he shall be punishable with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees and for the second or subsequent offence with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Chief Executive Officer and other authorised officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Recovery of contribution as arrears of land revenue, enforcement of attendance of persons, examination on oath, requiring discovery and production of documents, issuing commission for examination of witnesses. Proceedings in civil court for recovery.

rights: Workers are entitled to welfare benefits from the Fund.
Right to preference for certain benefits provided by the scheme.
duties: Employers have a duty to contribute to the Fund.
Workers have a duty to contribute to the Fund.
Self-employed members have a duty to contribute to the Fund.
The Government has a duty to contribute to the Fund.
obligations: Employers are obligated to pay contributions for their workers.
Workers are obligated to pay their own contributions if they are self-employed.

key_procedures: Framing of a Scheme by the Government for the constitution and administration of the Welfare Fund.
Collection of contributions from employers and workers.
Provisional assessment and collection of contributions.
Enquiry and determination of the amount due for contribution.
Recovery of unpaid contributions.
Application for benefits from the Fund as per the Scheme.
Resignation of Directors from the Board by giving notice in writing to the Government.
Removal of Directors by the Government under specific conditions.
Appointment of Chief Executive Officer and other staff.
Borrowing of funds by the Board with Government approval.
administration: The Kerala Small Plantation Workers' Welfare Fund Board
important_notes: The Act aims to promote the welfare and provide pension to workers in small plantations.
The Scheme may provide for various matters related to the Fund, including the constitution of the Fund, the terms and conditions for benefits, and the manner of administration.
The Government can amend or modify the Scheme by notification in the Gazette.
Penalties apply for contravention of the Act, rules, or schemes where no specific penalty is provided.

title: The Kerala Spinners Alappuzha (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertaking) Act, 2010
purpose: An Act to provide for the acquisition and transfer of the Kerala Spinners Ltd, Komalapuram, Alappuzha and for the acquisition and transfer of the right, title and interest of the owners in respect of the undertaking with a view to reorganizing and reviving the undertaking and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the acquisition and transfer of the Kerala Spinners Ltd, Komalapuram, Alappuzha and its undertaking, and the rights, title, and interest of its owners.

key_definitions.authorised person: The person or body of persons appointed under section 18AA of the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951 (Central Act 65 of 1951), to take over the management of the Sick Textile undertakings
key_definitions.bank: The Indian Overseas Bank, a Scheduled Bank as defined in clause (c) of section 2 of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (Central Act 2 of 1934)
key_definitions.Commissioner: The Commissioner of payments appointed under section 16
key_definitions.owner: When used in relation to the sick textile undertaking, means the person or firm or who or which was, immediately before the take-over of the management of the undertaking under section 18AA of the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951 (Central Act 65 of 1951), the immediate proprietor or lessee or occupier of the sick textile undertaking or any part thereof
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act
key_definitions.sick textile undertaking: The textile undertaking specified in the First Schedule and has been declared as sick company by the Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR)
key_definitions.specified date: Such date as the Government may, for the purpose of any provision of this Act, by notification in the Gazette, specify and different dates may be specified for different provisions of this Act
key_definitions.State Textile Corporation: The Kerala State Textile Corporation Limited formed and registered under the Companies Act, 1956 (Central Act 1 of 1956)
key_definitions.textile company: A company specified in column (2) of the First Schedule as owning the undertaking specified in the corresponding entry in column (1) of that Schedule
key_definitions.subsidiary textile corporation: A company formed by the State Textile Corporation as its subsidiary

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Spinners, Alappuzha (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertaking) Act, 2010, and it came into force on the 19th day of November, 2009.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'authorised person', 'bank', 'Commissioner', 'owner', 'prescribed', 'sick textile undertaking', 'specified date', 'State Textile Corporation', 'textile company', and 'subsidiary textile corporation'. It also specifies that words and expressions not defined in this Act but defined in the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951, and the Companies Act, 1956, shall have the meanings assigned to them in those Acts.

main_sections.section_title: Acquisition of rights of owners in respect of sick textile undertaking
main_sections.description: States that on the appointed day, the sick textile undertaking and the right, title and interest of the owner in relation to such sick textile undertaking shall, by virtue of this Act, stand transferred to, and shall vest absolutely in the State Government. It further details that the sick textile undertaking which stands vested in the State Government under sub-section (1) shall, immediately after it has so vested, stand transferred to, and vest in the State Textile Corporation. It also addresses the general effect of vesting, including all assets, rights, lease-hold powers, authorities and privileges, movable and immovable property, cash balances, reserve funds, investments and book debts, and all other rights and interests in, or arising out of, such property as were immediately before the appointed day in the possession, power or control of the authorized person and all books of account, registers and all other documents of whatever nature relating thereto. It also covers the transfer of all property vested in the State Government to the State Textile Corporation and the rights of mortgagees and other persons holding any charge, lien or other interest in relation to any such property.

Explains the consequences of the vesting of the sick textile undertaking in the State Government and then in the State Textile Corporation. This includes the transfer of all assets, rights, liabilities, and obligations.

main_sections.section_title: Owner to be liable for certain prior liabilities
main_sections.description: Specifies that every liability other than the liability specified in sub-section (2) of section 3, of the owner of the sick textile undertaking, in respect of any period prior to the appointed day shall not be a liability of such owner and shall be enforceable against him and not against the State Government or the State Textile Corporation. It also details liabilities arising in respect of loans advanced by the Central Government or the State Government to the sick textile undertaking and advance amounts to the sick textile undertaking.

important_rules: The sick textile undertaking and the owner's rights, title, and interest vest absolutely in the State Government on the appointed day.
The vested undertaking is then transferred to and vests in the State Textile Corporation.
All liabilities of the owner prior to the appointed day, except those specified, are not enforceable against the State Government or the State Textile Corporation.

rights: The State Government has the right to acquire the sick textile undertaking.
The State Textile Corporation has the right to manage the acquired undertaking.
duties: The owner has a duty to hand over the undertaking and all related assets and documents.
obligations: The State Textile Corporation has obligations related to the management of the undertaking.

key_procedures: Acquisition and transfer of the sick textile undertaking from the owner to the State Government, and then to the State Textile Corporation.
The appointed day is crucial for the transfer of rights, title, and interest.
Management and revival of the undertaking by the State Textile Corporation.
administration: The State Textile Corporation appears to be the primary administrative body for the acquired undertaking, with overall oversight likely by relevant government departments.
important_notes: The Act specifies an 'appointed day' which is critical for the transfer of ownership and rights.
The Act provides for the transfer of the undertaking to the State Textile Corporation.
Liabilities of the previous owner prior to the 'appointed day' are generally not the responsibility of the State Government or the State Textile Corporation.

title: THE KERALA SPORTS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2010

Amends Section 6-0 of the principal Act, concerning the appointment of the Selection Committee. It clarifies the composition and powers of the committee, including the replacement of certain clauses and the addition of a proviso.

Amends Section 9-0 of the principal Act. It modifies the provisions related to the 'Sports Fund' by replacing certain phrases and inserting new clauses regarding the management and utilization of the fund.

Amends Section 14-0 of the principal Act. It pertains to the 'Kerala State Sports Council' and introduces changes regarding its functions and operations, including the replacement of certain references.

Amends Section 17 of the principal Act. It deals with the 'Sports Development Authority' and modifies clauses related to its constitution and responsibilities, including the replacement of a phrase and the insertion of a new definition.

important_rules: The Selection Committee's composition and appointment process are modified.
The management and utilization of the Sports Fund are detailed.
Provisions related to the Kerala State Sports Council's functions are updated.
The powers and functions of the Sports Ombudsman are significantly revised.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Likely the Sports Ombudsman and relevant government departments, based on the Act's context.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act and any rules/regulations made thereunder.

rights: Right to benefit from the Sports Fund.
Right to appeal or seek redressal from the Sports Ombudsman.
duties: Duties related to the proper functioning of sports institutions and activities.
Duties of individuals and bodies involved in sports to adhere to the Act's provisions.
obligations: Obligations of sports organizations to comply with regulations.
Obligations of the government to promote sports.

key_procedures: Procedure for appointing the Selection Committee.
Procedure for managing and utilizing the Sports Fund.
Procedure for appointing and functioning of the Sports Ombudsman.
Procedure for amendments to sports-related laws and regulations.
administration: Likely the Department of Sports and Youth Affairs, Government of Kerala, or a similar designated body.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the existing Kerala Sports Act, 1974.
The Kerala Sports (Amendment) Ordinance, 2010, has been repealed.
The role and powers of the Sports Ombudsman have been significantly enhanced.

title: The Kerala Sports (Amendment) Act, 2010
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Sports Act, 2000 for purposes hereafter appearing.
scope: The Act applies to the Kerala Sports Act, 2000. It amends specific sections of the principal Act concerning sports and sports councils in Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called The Kerala Sports (Amendment) Act, 2010. It also specifies the commencement dates for certain sections, with Sections 6 and 7 deemed to have come into force on August 17, 2008, and the remaining provisions on January 5, 2009.
Amends Section 3 of the principal Act by substituting the words "international" and "national" with "international or national" in item (u) for the heading "Nominated Members".
Amends Section 6 of the principal Act by substituting words in sub-section (1) regarding elected members and making substitutions for "international" and "international or national".
Amends Section 9 of the principal Act by substituting words in clause (b) for the heading "Nominated Members".

Amends Section 14 of the principal Act by substituting the description of a "Deputy Collector in Government Service" to "officer of a Section Officer in the Kerala Secretariat Service or of similar rank in various Departments in Government Service".
Amends Section 47A of the principal Act by substituting the durations mentioned for "a period of two years" and "a period of three and a half years".
