Repeals The Kerala Sports (Amendment) Ordinance, 2010 (4 of 2010) and saves any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the said Ordinance, providing that such actions shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act, as amended by this Act.

important_notes: The translation is in English of "2010-ലെ കേരള കായിക സംബന്ധമായ (ഭേദഗതി)  öjå" published under the authority of the Governor.
Sections 6 and 7 of this Act are deemed to have come into force on August 17, 2008.
The remaining provisions of this Act came into force on January 5, 2009.

title: THE KERALA SPORTS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2007
purpose: To amend the Kerala Sports Act, 2000.
scope: The Act applies to the Kerala Sports Act, 2000 and its provisions.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Sports (Amendment) Act, 2007. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 18th day of August, 2006.

In the Kerala Sports Act, 2000, after section 47, the following sections shall be inserted, namely: '47A. Special provision for nomination of State Sports Council and District Sports Council.—Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or the rules made thereunder or in any judgment, decree or order of any Court, the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, constitute by nomination, the State Sports Council and the District Sports Council for a period of two years from the date of commencement of the Kerala Sports (Amendment) Act, 2007 or till the constitution of the said authorities in accordance with the provisions of this Act, whichever is earlier. 47B. Nomination to the First Corporation Sports Council, First Municipal Sports Council and First Village Sports Council.—Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, the First Corporation Sports Council, the First Municipal Sports Council and the First Village Sports Council shall be nominated by the Government and may continue for a period of two years from the date of such nomination or till the constitution of the said authorities in accordance with the provisions of this Act, whichever is earlier.'

(1) The Kerala Sports (Amendment) Ordinance, 2007 (30 of 2007) is hereby repealed. (2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Notification in the Gazette

key_procedures: Nomination of State Sports Council and District Sports Council by the Government.
Nomination of Corporation Sports Council, Municipal Sports Council, and Village Sports Council by the Government.
administration: Likely the Department of Sports and Youth Affairs, Government of Kerala, but not explicitly stated.
important_notes: The assent of the Governor was received on the 13th October, 2007 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 1860 dated 15th October, 2007.
The provisions regarding nomination are temporary and are in effect until the constitution of the respective authorities according to the main Act.

title: The Kerala Sports Act, 2000
purpose: To provide for the development, promotion and management of sports in the State of Kerala, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.

key_definitions.sports: Includes athletic sports, games, pastimes and all other forms of physical recreations or exercises.
key_definitions.sports organization: Includes any association, federation, society or body formed for the promotion and control of sports.
key_definitions.sports person: Means any person who has participated in any sports
key_definitions.Governing Body: Means the body established by the Government for the promotion and development of sports in the State.

main_sections.section_title: POWERS AND FUNCTIONS OF THE GOVERNMENT
main_sections.description: Outlines the powers and functions of the Government in relation to sports development and promotion.
Deals with the control and regulation of sports organizations in the state.
Specifies the functions that sports organizations are required to perform.
Details the duties and responsibilities of sports organizations.
Provides for the granting of financial assistance and grants to sports organizations and sports persons.
Establishes a Sports Development Fund for the promotion of sports.

main_sections.section_title: INQUIRY INTO THE AFFAIRS OF SPORTS ORGANISATIONS
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to inquire into the affairs of sports organizations.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Provides for the right of appeal against certain decisions.
Deals with the settlement of disputes and arbitration in matters related to sports.
Specifies the offences and penalties for violations of the Act.
Deals with the cognizance of offences under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: PROTECTION OF ACTION TAKEN IN GOOD FAITH
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith under the Act.
Ensures the continuation of existing laws until they are repealed or amended.

important_rules: Sports organizations must be registered and adhere to regulations.
Grants and financial assistance are subject to government approval and guidelines.
Disputes related to sports can be resolved through arbitration.
Offences under the Act are punishable by fines or imprisonment.

penalties: Fines as prescribed by the Act.
Imprisonment for certain offences.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government and authorities designated by it.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, inquiries, legal proceedings, and imposition of penalties.

rights: Right to participate in sports.
Right to receive support and assistance for sports development.
Right to appeal against certain decisions.
duties: Duty of sports organizations to promote and develop sports.
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder.
Duty to maintain transparency and accountability in financial matters.
obligations: Sports organizations have an obligation to ensure fair play and sportsmanship.

key_procedures: Procedure for registration of sports organizations.
Procedure for applying for grants and financial assistance.
Procedure for dispute resolution and arbitration.
Procedure for lodging complaints and taking action against offenders.
administration: Department of Sports and Youth Affairs, Government of Kerala (inferred).
important_notes: The Act aims to create a framework for the comprehensive development of sports in Kerala.
The Act emphasizes the role of sports organizations in achieving these objectives.
Provisions are made for the establishment of a Sports Development Fund to support sports initiatives.

title: THE KERALA STAMP (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1972
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Stamp Act, 1959.
scope: Applies to instruments chargeable with duty under the Kerala Stamp Act, 1959.

main_sections.description: Names the act as the Kerala Stamp (Amendment) Act, 1972.

Inserts a new section 3A concerning additional duty on instruments. It states that every instrument chargeable with duty under section 3 shall, in addition to such duty, be chargeable with a duty of twenty paise. It also mentions an additional duty with which an instrument is chargeable under sub-section (1) shall be paid and such payment shall be indicated on such instrument by means of adhesive stamps bearing the inscription 'refugee relief' whether with or without any other design, picture or inscription. Exceptions provided in sub-section (2) of the provisions of this Act shall apply in relation to the additional duty chargeable under sub-section (1) as they apply in relation to the duty chargeable under section 3.

Amends section 6 of the principal Act by inserting an Explanation after the proviso. The Explanation clarifies that in the proviso and in sub-section (1) of section 8, the term 'duty', wherever it occurs, means the duty chargeable under section 3.

Amends section 25 of the principal Act by inserting words in the proviso to the Explanation. It specifies that after the words 'duty already paid', the brackets, words, figures and letter '(other than the additional duty paid in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section 3A)' shall be inserted.

Amends article 30 of the Schedule to the principal Act, in item (i) of clause (b), in the entry in column (3), after the words 'duty already paid', the brackets, words, figures and letter '(other than the additional duty paid in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section 3A)' shall be inserted.

Repeals the Kerala Stamp Ordinance, 1971 (23 of 1971). Notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act if such Act had come into force on the 16th day of December, 1971.

important_rules: An additional duty of twenty paise is chargeable on instruments already subject to duty under section 3.
The additional duty shall be paid and indicated by means of adhesive stamps inscribed with 'refugee relief'.
Exceptions provided in sub-section (2) of the Act apply to the additional duty under sub-section (1) as they apply to duty under section 3.

duties: Instruments chargeable with duty under section 3 are also chargeable with an additional duty of twenty paise.
obligations: Payment of the additional duty by means of adhesive stamps bearing the inscription 'refugee relief'.

important_notes: The Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 181, dated 22nd March, 1972.
The amendment to section 6 clarifies that 'duty' refers to duty chargeable under section 3.
The amendment to section 25 and Schedule inserts specific wording related to additional duty paid in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section 3A.

title: The Kerala Stamp (Amendment) Act, 1973
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Stamp Act, 1959.

title: THE KERALA STAMP (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2013
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala Stamp Act, 1959.
scope: This Act applies to the Kerala Stamp Act, 1959.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Stamp (Amendment) Act, 2013 and it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 2010.

Amends section 28A of the Kerala Stamp Act, 1959 by substituting "one year" for "thirty days" and adding a proviso allowing the Collector to admit an appeal preferred after the said period of one year if he is satisfied that the appellant had sufficient cause for not preferring the appeal within the said period.
Repeals The Kerala Stamp (Amendment) Ordinance, 2013 (5 of 2013) and saves anything done or any action taken under the said Ordinance.

administration: Law (Legislation-A) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: This Act is an amendment to The Kerala Stamp Act, 1959.
The commencement date for the purpose of Section 1(2) is April 1, 2010.
The amendments made by Section 2 are retrospective to April 1, 2010.

title: THE KERALA STAMP (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1963
purpose: To amend the Kerala Stamp Act, 1959, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to instruments and transactions subject to stamp duty under The Kerala Stamp Act, 1959.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Stamp (Amendment) Act, 1963. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
In the Schedule to the Kerala Stamp Act, 1959, for entries 1 to 10 (both inclusive), the following entries shall be substituted.

important_rules: Rules regarding stamp duty on various instruments are specified in the Schedule, with rates varying based on the value or amount involved. For example, for an affidavit or declaration, the duty is three rupees seventy-five naye paise.

The duty for an agreement or bond depends on the amount secured. For example, for an agreement relating to deposit of title deeds or documents, if the amount secured exceeds Rs. 200 but does not exceed Rs. 400, the duty is Rs. 2.
Specific duties are prescribed for instruments like Bills of Exchange, Promissory Notes, and Agreements of Lease.

Exemptions are provided for certain instruments, such as affidavits or declarations made for immediate purpose of being filed or used in any Court, or for the purpose of enabling any person to receive any pension or charitable allowance.
Exemptions are also provided for agreements or memorandum of agreement not being a note or memorandum obligatory between parties other by agreement or operation of law.
Exemptions for Certificates of Sale of property put up as a separate lot and sold, provided the purchase money does not exceed Rs. 1,000.

duties: Duty to affix appropriate stamp duty on instruments as per the Schedule.
Obligation to pay stamp duty on instruments, including those related to the sale of property, agreements, and bonds.
obligations: Obligation to pay stamp duty on instruments, including those related to the sale of property, agreements, and bonds.

key_procedures: For instruments where the amount secured exceeds Rs. 200 but does not exceed Rs. 400, the duty is Rs. 2. For amounts exceeding Rs. 400 but not exceeding Rs. 600, the duty is Rs. 3.
For agreements or memorandum of agreement, the duty varies based on the amount secured. For example, if the amount secured exceeds Rs. 5,000 but does not exceed Rs. 7,500, the duty is Rs. 15.
For Bottomry Bonds, the duty is Rs. 1 for every Rs. 500 or part thereof, in excess of Rs. 1,000.
administration: The Government of Kerala, through relevant notifications and appointments.
important_notes: The Act was enacted in the Fourteenth Year of the Republic of India.
The Act received the assent of the Governor on 21st March, 1963 and was published in the Gazette Extraordinary, dated 22nd March, 1963.
The commencement date of the Act is to be appointed by the Government by notification in the Gazette.

Specific exemptions are detailed for various types of instruments, such as those related to the sale of goods or merchandise not being a note or memorandum obligatory between parties, or affidavits and declarations made for certain legal purposes.

title: The Kerala Stamp (Amendment) Act, 1988
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Stamp Act, 1959.
scope: Applies to instruments related to the Stamp Act in Kerala.

key_definitions.instrument: Includes all documents and writings by which any right or liability is or purports to be created, transferred, extended, extinguished or recorded.
key_definitions.land: Means land which is transferable under the law for the time being in force relating to land revenue, and includes benefits to arise out of land, and things attached to the earth or permanently fastened to anything attached to the earth.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Stamp (Amendment) Act, 1988. Sections 2 and 3 shall be deemed to have come into force on the 9th day of February, 1988, sections 4 and sub-sections (1) to (5), (7), (8), (11), (12), (13), (16), (17), (19), (20) and (21) of section 8 shall be deemed to have come into force on the 24th day of February, 1988 and the remaining provisions of this Act shall come into force on such date as the Government may by notification in the Gazette appoint and different dates may be appointed for such remaining provisions of this Act.

In the Kerala Stamp Act, 1959 (17 of 1959) (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), in section 2, after clause (m), the following clause shall be inserted, namely: – "(mm) 'minimum value of land' means the minimum value of land fixed by the Collector under section 28A by notification in the Gazette or the consideration paid for such land as set forth in the instrument, whichever is higher;"
In sub-section (1) of section 4 of the principal Act, for the words "two rupees", the words "fifteen rupees" shall be substituted.
In section 6 of the principal Act, for the words "five rupees", the words "fifteen rupees" shall be substituted.

After section 28 of the principal Act, the following section shall be inserted, namely: – "28A. Fixation of minimum value of land.—(1) The Collector shall, subject to such rules as may be prescribed by Government, fix the minimum value of lands situate within the area of his jurisdiction, for the purpose of determining the duty chargeable at the time of registration of instruments involving lands."

Section 45A is inserted which deals with instruments not bearing stamp of sufficient amount as per minimum value of land. It outlines procedures for the Registering Officer when registering such instruments, including verification, determination of value, and registration if conditions are met. It also includes provisions for appeals against the Registering Officer's decision.

Amends section 45 as renumbered. It clarifies that notwithstanding anything contained in this section, an instrument referred to in this section is an instrument involving transfer of land, the value or consideration thereof determined by the Collector under sub-section (2) or sub-section (3), as the case may be, shall be the basis for reckoning the proper amount of duty in respect of that instrument.

This section amends the Schedule of the principal Act by substituting specific entries related to various instruments like 'Agreement', 'Bond', 'Conveyance', 'Exchange of property', 'Gift', and 'Settlement' with revised duty rates and descriptions.

(1) The Kerala Stamp (Amendment) Ordinance, 1988 (2 of 1988), is hereby repealed. (2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Minimum value of land is determined by the Collector for duty assessment on instruments involving lands.
The Registering Officer must ensure that instruments related to land transfer are stamped according to the minimum value of land.
Provisions for appeals exist for persons aggrieved by the Registering Officer's decision regarding stamp duty on land instruments.

penalties: The Act details various stamp duties for different types of instruments. For instance, for Agreements, the duty is Rs. 5.00 for single draw, Rs. 2.50 in set of 2, and Rs. 1.25 in set of 3. For Conveyance, it's Rs. 100 or part thereof of the minimum value of land. Specific penalties for insufficient stamping are not explicitly detailed in the provided sections but are inherent to stamp acts.
Revised stamp duties are introduced for various instruments like Bonds, Conveyances, Gifts, and Settlements.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Collector and the Registering Officer are the primary authorities for enforcement.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the process of registration of instruments and assessment of stamp duty. Appeals against decisions can be made.

rights: Right to appeal against the decision of the Registering Officer regarding stamp duty assessment.
duties: Duty to pay the correct stamp duty as per the provisions of the Act.
Duty of the Collector to fix the minimum value of land.
Duty of the Registering Officer to verify and ensure correct stamping of instruments.
obligations: Obligation to register instruments involving transfer of land after proper stamping.

key_procedures: Fixation of minimum value of land by the Collector.
Procedure for the Registering Officer to assess and verify stamp duty on instruments, especially those involving land.
Process of appeal against the Registering Officer's decision.
administration: Law (Legislation-A) Department, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act is a further amendment to the Kerala Stamp Act, 1959.
Different sections of the Act have different commencement dates.
The Act provides for the repeal and re-enactment of the Kerala Stamp (Amendment) Ordinance, 1988.
Specific stamp duties are revised for a range of instruments, including agreements, bonds, conveyances, gifts, and settlements.

title: THE KERALA STAMP (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1991
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Stamp Act, 1959.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Stamp (Amendment) Act, 1991. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 11th day of January, 1991.
Amends section 2 of the Kerala Stamp Act, 1959.
Omits section 28A of the principal Act.
Omits section 45A of the principal Act.
Amends section 45B of the principal Act.

Amends the Schedule to the principal Act by modifying entries relating to various instruments and their respective stamp duties. This includes changes to conveyances, exchange of property, and release deeds, specifying stamp duties based on consideration value or fixed amounts for certain categories.
Repeals the Kerala Stamp (Amendment) Ordinance, 1991 (1 of 1991) and saves actions taken or rules made under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance.

important_rules: Stamp duty on conveyances is five rupees for every Rs. 100 or part thereof of the amount or value of the consideration.
Stamp duty on conveyances not being a transfer charged or exempted under section 55 is five rupees for every Rs. 100 or part thereof of the amount or value of the consideration.

Stamp duty on conveyances (as defined by section 2(d), not being a transfer charged or exempted under No. 21) where the property is situated within the Municipal Corporations or Municipalities is seven rupees fifty paise for every Rs. 100 or part thereof of the amount or value of the consideration.

Stamp duty on Exchange of property-instrument is the same duty as a conveyance (No. 21 or 22, as the case may be) for a consideration equal to the value of the property of greater value as set forth in such instrument.

Stamp duty on Partition-Instrument where the partition is among all or some of the family members is the same duty as a Bottomry Bond (No. 14) for the amount or value of the separated share or shares of the property.
Stamp duty on Partition-Instrument in any other case is two rupees or part thereof of every Rs. 100 or part thereof of the amount or value of the separated share or shares of the property.
Stamp duty on Release (not being a release in favour of his or her spouse or children) is the same duty as a Bottomry Bond (No. 14) for such amount or value as set forth in the release.
Stamp duty on Release in any other case is the same duty as a conveyance (No. 21 or 22, as the case may be) for such amount or value as set forth in the release.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided sections, but implied to be the relevant stamp duty authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the collection of stamp duties as prescribed by the Act.

duties: Duty to affix appropriate stamp duty on instruments as per the Act.
obligations: To comply with the provisions of the amended Act regarding stamp duties.

key_procedures: Payment of stamp duty for various instruments like conveyances, exchanges, partitions, and releases as specified in the Schedule.
Substitution of entries in the Schedule for specific instruments based on their nature and value.
administration: Department responsible for stamp duty administration in Kerala.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on January 11, 1991.
The amendments made by this Act are retrospective.
The explanation for 'Family' in the context of partition includes husband, wife, children and the legal heirs of the deceased children.

title: THE KERALA STAMP (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 1972
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Stamp Act, 1959.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala, amending the Kerala Stamp Act, 1959.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Stamp (Second Amendment) Act, 1972.
In sub-section (3) of section 45A of the Kerala Stamp Act, 1959 (17 of 1959), for the words "six months", the words "two years" shall be substituted.

important_rules: Substitution of the words "two years" for "six months" in sub-section (3) of section 45A of the Kerala Stamp Act, 1959.
important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 700, dated 27th November, 1972.

title: The Kerala Stamp (Amendment) Act, 2004
purpose: To amend the Kerala Stamp Act, 1959, concerning certain aspects of stamp duty and related provisions.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies when it comes into force. It refers to the Kerala Stamp (Amendment) Act, 2004 (Act 1 of 2004) and the Kerala Stamp Act, 1959.

Amends Section 2 of the Kerala Stamp Act, 1959, by inserting clauses regarding the definition of 'settlement' and 'transfer'. It defines 'settlement' to include any disposition of property, and clarifies that 'transfer' includes conveyance, mortgage, lease, exchange, or actionable claim.

Amends Section 21-A of the Kerala Stamp Act, 1959, by specifying that the duty on instruments relating to loans not exceeding one hundred rupees shall be as prescribed. It also makes a consequential amendment to Section 22-A.
Repeals the Kerala Stamp (Amendment) Ordinance, 2003 (Ordinance 6 of 2003), and provides savings for actions taken under the Ordinance.

important_rules: Instruments relating to loans not exceeding one hundred rupees shall be charged with stamp duty as prescribed.
The amendment concerning 'settlement' and 'transfer' clarifies the scope of these terms under the Act.
important_notes: The Act is a Tamil Nadu (Malabar) notification.
The Act introduces amendments to the existing Kerala Stamp Act, 1959.
The amendments are related to definitions and stamp duty on certain instruments.

title: THE KERALA STAMP (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2004
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Stamp Act, 1959.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Stamp (Amendment) Act, 2004 and it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 2nd day of December, 2003.

Inserts a new section 30A concerning 'Cealing on surcharge on stamp duty'. This section clarifies that notwithstanding anything contained in the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 or the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994, the rate of surcharge on stamp duty leviable on any instrument by a Grama Panchayat or a Municipality shall not exceed two per cent of the amount on which such stamp duty is payable.

Amends the Schedule to the Principal Act. Specifically, it amends serial number 21 (conveyance) by substituting the existing rates for 'Six rupees for every Rs 100 or part thereof, of the amount or value of the consideration for such conveyance' with 'Two rupees for every Rs 100 or part thereof, of the fair value of the property or the amount or value of the consideration for such conveyance, whichever is higher'. It also amends serial number 22 and the entries relating thereto.

Repeals The Kerala Stamp (Amendment) Ordinance, 2003 (6 of 2003). It also states that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: The surcharge on stamp duty leviable by a Grama Panchayat or a Municipality shall not exceed two per cent of the amount on which such stamp duty is payable.

The rate of stamp duty for conveyance will now be calculated based on the fair value of the property or the amount or value of the consideration, whichever is higher, at two rupees for every Rs 100 or part thereof.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be the relevant authorities under the Stamp Act and the Municipal Acts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Stamp Act, 1959 and the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, 1994, and the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994.

duties: Duty to pay stamp duty and surcharge as per the amended Act.
Duty of Grama Panchayats and Municipalities to levy surcharge not exceeding two per cent.

key_procedures: When registering a conveyance, the stamp duty and surcharge must be calculated based on the fair value of the property or the consideration amount, whichever is higher, subject to the surcharge not exceeding two percent.
The repeal of the Ordinance means that actions taken under it are now governed by this Act.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned, likely related to the Department of Revenue, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on December 2, 2003.
The Kerala Stamp (Amendment) Ordinance, 2003 is repealed.
Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are saved.

title: THE KERALA STATE AID TO INDUSTRIES ACT, 1963 (Act 34 of 1963)
purpose: To consolidate and amend the laws relating to the giving of State aid to industries in the State of Kerala.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala and concerns the giving of State aid to industries within the State.

key_definitions.Board: The State Aid to Industries Board constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.Company: Means a company as defined in section 3 of the Companies Act, 1956 (Central Act I of 1956) and includes a foreign company within the meaning of section 591 of that Act.
key_definitions.Director: Means the Director of Industries and Commerce and includes any person appointed by the Government either by name or by virtue of his office to perform all or any of the functions of the Director of Industries and Commerce under this Act.
key_definitions.Industry: Means any industrial business or enterprise conducted by the State by any individual, institution, company, association or body of individuals whether unincorporated or not and includes a cottage industry, a small scale industry, and a village industry; but shall not include an industry organised on co-operative basis which is eligible for financial assistance from the Kerala State Government or a Co-operative Bank under any specific development programme.
key_definitions.Cottage Industry: Means an industrial business or enterprise carried on in any premises to which the Factories Act, 1948 (Central Act 63 of 1948), does not apply, and includes dairy farming, bee-keeping and poultry farming.
key_definitions.Small Scale Industry: Means an industrial business or enterprise the capital invested in which does not exceed five lakhs of rupees.
key_definitions.Village Industry: Means any industry which forms the normal occupation, whether whole-time or part-time, of any class of the rural population of the State.
key_definitions.Machinery: Includes plant, apparatus, tools and other appliances required for the purpose of carrying on any industrial operation or process.
key_definitions.Owner: Means the person who owns any industrial undertaking and includes the successor-in-interest of such person in respect of such undertaking.
key_definitions.Prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.State aid: Means any aid given by or on behalf of the Government under the provisions of this Act and the rules, if any, made thereunder.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala State Aid to Industries Act, 1963. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'Company', 'Director', 'Industry', 'Cottage Industry', 'Small Scale Industry', 'Village Industry', 'Machinery', 'Owner', 'Prescribed', 'State', and 'State aid'.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of State Aid to Industries Board
main_sections.description: Provides for the constitution of the State Aid to Industries Board, specifying its members, including the Director of Industries and Commerce, officers from the Finance Department and Industries Department, members representing the Kerala Legislative Assembly, and representatives of industrial and commercial interests and organised trade unions. It also covers nominations, election or removal of members, and the Board's role in advising the Government on applications for State aid. Decisions of the Board require a majority vote, and members with a direct or indirect pecuniary interest must disclose it. Proceedings of the Board are generally valid despite any defect or irregularity in the constitution of the Board or any vacancy. Provisions are made for the term of office of members, resignation, removal of members, filling up of vacancies, presidency at meetings, dissolution of the Board, and industries to which aid may be given.

Specifies the types of industries that can be aided under this Act, including new or nascent industries, industries newly established in an area where such industries are underdeveloped or are likely to be successful, industries likely to become more profitable by an investment of more capital, small scale industries, cottage industries, village industries, and other such industrial concerns. It also states that no State aid shall be given to any joint stock company unless it is registered in India with a rupee capital and its members agree to prescribed propositions. Further, it outlines provisions for training of apprentices.

Details the various forms in which State aid can be granted, including by granting a loan, by guaranteeing of cash credit, overdraft or a fixed advance with a bank, by taking fully paid up shares or debentures, by guaranteeing interest on preference shares or debentures, by guaranteeing a minimum return on the whole or part of the capital of a joint stock company, by granting on favourable terms land, raw materials, firewood, water or any other property of the Government, and by purchasing machinery subject to such terms and conditions as may be prescribed, or by supplying machinery on hire purchase system.

main_sections.section_title: Conditions for the guarantee and grant under section 11 (c) and (f)
main_sections.description: Sets conditions for guarantees and grants for machinery on hire purchase systems. It states that the amount of the guarantee or grant shall not exceed the sum total of or exceed the value of the interest being guaranteed. The amount shall not exceed the value of the asset, and the terms and conditions for the loan or advance will be prescribed. The Government may guarantee loans or advances up to a certain percentage of the total investment or value of the asset.

Outlines conditions for granting loans. Loans shall not exceed the prescribed percentage of the value of the assets of the industry to which it is granted. Security may be required, and the value of the security will be ascertained by the sanctioning authority. Loans shall not be granted if encumbrances on the assets of the industry exceed a certain percentage of the value of such assets. The authority granting the loan may ask for collateral security up to a certain percentage of the loan amount.

Explains how loans are secured. Every loan granted shall be secured by a mortgage upon the whole or such portion of the assets of the business or enterprise as the sanctioning authority may consider sufficient and where the whole or any part of the assets are not in opinion of the sanctioning authority sufficient, by collateral security as may be required.

main_sections.section_title: Application for State aid and authorities by whom aid may be granted
main_sections.description: Details the application process for State aid and the authorities responsible for granting it. Applications are made to the District Industries Officer, who will make enquiries and forward them to the Regional Joint Director of Industries and Commerce or the Director. The Director will forward applications to the sanctioning authority. Where the sanctioning authority is the Director, applications are forwarded to the Regional Joint Director of Industries and Commerce. If the State aid applied for exceeds certain limits, a notice will be published in the Gazette. Every application for State aid exceeding a certain amount must be placed before the Board and will be granted only with its concurrence.
Empowers the Government to supervise assisted industries.
Allows for inspection of assisted industries and requires them to submit returns to the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Disposal of profits when condition of State aid is not fulfilled
main_sections.description: Deals with the disposal of profits when the conditions of State aid are not met.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to adjust security during currency of loans
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to adjust security during the currency of loans.

main_sections.section_title: Power of authority sanctioning the loan to terminate loan
main_sections.description: Authorizes the authority that sanctioned the loan to terminate it under certain circumstances.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken under the Act
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Persons acting under this Act to be deemed public servants
main_sections.description: Declares persons acting under this Act to be public servants.
Provides for penalties for contravention of the Act or rules made thereunder.

main_sections.section_title: Percentage of value to be deposited by hirer
main_sections.description: Specifies the percentage of the value to be deposited by a hirer under the hire purchase system.

main_sections.section_title: Particulars to be specified in the order when application is allowed
main_sections.description: Outlines particulars to be specified in an order when an application for hire purchase is allowed.

main_sections.section_title: Conditions of supply of machinery on hire purchase system
main_sections.description: Details the conditions for the supply of machinery on hire purchase.
Describes the consequences of default by the hirer.

main_sections.section_title: Option hire purchase machinery seized for default
main_sections.description: Covers the option for seizure of hire purchase machinery in case of default.
Details the process of termination of hiring by the hirer.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of hirer on termination of hiring under sections 27 and 29
main_sections.description: Specifies the liability of the hirer upon termination of hiring under specific sections.

main_sections.section_title: Termination of hiring on payment of cost of machinery, revision
main_sections.description: Deals with the termination of hiring upon payment of the cost of machinery and the provision for revision.
Provides for revision of orders under the Act.
Allows the Government to review orders passed under the Act.
Specifies fees to be levied under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Mode of recovery of money due
main_sections.description: Outlines the mode of recovery of money due to the Government.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Repeals previous legislation.

important_rules: Rule regarding the deposit of a percentage of the value by the hirer under a hire purchase system.
Rules regarding the conditions of supply of machinery on hire purchase.
Rules regarding the consequences of default by the hirer.
Rules regarding the termination of hiring.
Rules regarding the mode of recovery of money due.

penalties: Penalty for contravention of the Act or rules (Section 23).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government and authorities appointed under the Act (e.g., Director of Industries and Commerce, District Industries Officer).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through supervision of assisted industries, inspection, requiring returns, and imposition of penalties for contraventions.

rights: Industries have the right to apply for and receive State aid under the conditions specified.
The Government has the right to impose conditions on State aid.
duties: Industries receiving aid have a duty to comply with the terms and conditions of the aid.
The Board has a duty to advise the Government on applications for State aid.
Members of the Board have a duty to disclose any pecuniary interest.
obligations: Industries must provide security for loans as required.
Industries must submit to supervision and inspection.

key_procedures: Application for State aid: Applications are made to the District Industries Officer and forwarded through the hierarchy of authorities.
Grant of State aid: Aid can be granted in various forms (loans, guarantees, shares, etc.) subject to prescribed conditions.
Supervision and inspection of assisted industries: The Government can supervise and inspect industries receiving aid.
Termination of loans: Sanctioning authorities can terminate loans under certain circumstances.
Recovery of dues: Procedures for recovery of money due to the Government.
administration: The Act is administered by the Government of Kerala, with the Director of Industries and Commerce playing a significant role, and supported by the State Aid to Industries Board and District Industries Officers.
important_notes: The Act was received the assent of the Governor on the 29th day of October, 1963 and published in the Gazette Extra ordinary, dated 4th November, 1963.
The Board's advice is sought by the Government in dealing with applications for State aid.
Members of the Board with pecuniary interest must disclose it.
The Government may remove members of the Board for certain reasons.
The Act provides for the protection of actions taken in good faith.
Persons acting under the Act are deemed public servants.

title: THE KERALA STATE BACKWARD CLASSES (RESERVATION OF APPOINTMENTS OR POSTS IN THE SERVICES UNDER THE STATE) ACT, 1995
purpose: To provide for the continuance of the existing system of reservation of appointments or posts in the services under the State for the Backward Classes of citizens. This act addresses the policy decision to provide reservation for social and educational advancement of people belonging to Backward Classes of citizens. It also addresses the need to provide reservation based on the basis of their population and in proportion to their population in the State.
scope: The Act applies to the services under the State of Kerala and concerns the reservation of appointments or posts for Backward Classes of citizens in these services.

key_definitions.Commission: The Kerala State Commission for Backward Classes Act, 1993 (11 of 1993).
key_definitions.Backward Classes: Backward Classes of citizens other than Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, as specified by the Government from time to time, and included in List III of the Schedule to Part I of the Kerala State and Subordinate Services Rules, 1958, framed under Act 309 of the Constitution.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act as The Kerala State Backward Classes (Reservation of Appointments or Posts in the Services Under the State) Act, 1995. It also extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. Section 5 of this Act was deemed to have come into force on March 12, 1993, and the remaining provisions came into force on October 2, 1992.
This section provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'Commission', 'Backward Classes', 'Government', and 'State'.

It is hereby declared, having regard to known facts in existence in the State, that there are no socially advanced sections in any Backward Classes who have acquired capacity to compete with forward classes; and that the Backward Classes in the State are still not adequately represented in the services under the State and they continue to be entitled to reservation under clause (4) of Article 16 of the Constitution.

main_sections.section_title: Reservation of appointments or posts in the services under the State
main_sections.description: This section deals with the reservation of appointments or posts in the services under the State. Notwithstanding anything contained in any law or any judgment, decree or order of any court or other authority having regard to the social and educational backwardness of the Backward Classes of citizens, the system of reservations as in force on the date of commencement of this Act, as laid down in rules 14 to 17 of Part II of the Kerala State and Subordinate Services Rules, 1958, in appointments and posts in the services under the State for the Backward Classes of citizens, shall continue as such, for the present.

The Commission shall, in addition to the functions already conferred under the Kerala State Commission for Backward Classes Act, 1993, evaluate from time to time the degree of backwardness of the Backward Classes, and shall submit periodical reports to the Legislative Assembly of the State.

Notwithstanding anything contained in any judgment, decree or order of any court or other authority, the reservation of appointments or posts in the services under the State for the Backward Classes of citizens made, on the basis of the system of reservation as laid down in rules 14 to 17 of Part II of the Kerala State and Subordinate Services Rules, 1958, shall, for all purposes be deemed to be and to have always been validly made, in accordance with law, as if this Act had been in force at all material times when such reservations had been made.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Kerala State Commission for Backward Classes and the Government of Kerala.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, rules framed thereunder, and court judgments/orders. The Act also validates past reservations made under specific rules.

rights: Backward Classes of citizens are entitled to reservation in appointments or posts in the services under the State.
The existing system of reservation is continued for the present.
obligations: The Government has an obligation to ensure adequate representation of Backward Classes in the services.
The Commission has the duty to evaluate the backwardness of Backward Classes and submit reports.

key_procedures: The Act continues the existing system of reservation as laid down in rules 14 to 17 of Part II of the Kerala State and Subordinate Services Rules, 1958.
The Kerala State Commission for Backward Classes is tasked with evaluating the degree of backwardness of Backward Classes and submitting reports.
The Act provides for the validation of past reservations made under the specified rules.
administration: The Government of Kerala and the Kerala State Commission for Backward Classes.
important_notes: The Act acknowledges that there are no socially advanced sections within Backward Classes capable of competing with forward classes.
The Act aims to ensure adequate representation of Backward Classes in State services.
The Act validates past reservations made under specific rules, notwithstanding any court orders.
The continuation of reservation is stated to be 'for the present', implying it may be subject to review.

title: The Kerala State Co-Operative Agricultural Development Banks Act 1984
purpose: This act provides for the sale of property, including property charged by way of Gehan or mortgage or hypothecation, for the recovery of dues owed to Agricultural Development Banks and Primary Banks, without direct court intervention in certain circumstances. It also deals with the appointment of sale officers, distribution of sale proceeds, and other related matters.
scope: The act applies to Agricultural Development Banks and Primary Banks in Kerala, and to persons who have created a Gehan or mortgage or hypothecation on property in favour of these banks.

key_definitions.court: In this section, 'court' means the Civil court having jurisdiction to entertain a suit to enforce the Gehan or mortgage or hypothecation and within the limits of whose jurisdiction the property sold is situate.

main_sections.description: Details the process and conditions for selling property under distraint, including notice periods, deductions, and the application of sale proceeds. It outlines the rights of the defaulter and the bank concerning the sale and surplus funds.

main_sections.section_title: Power of sale of property charged without intervention of court
main_sections.description: Empowers Agricultural Development Banks and Primary Banks to sell property charged by Gehan or mortgage or hypothecation without court intervention, under specific conditions and with due notice. It also details the process of sale, including public auction and the roles of the Registrar and the Board.

main_sections.section_title: Application for sale and manner of sale
main_sections.description: Explains the process for applying for the sale of property charged under section 19 and the manner in which such sales should be conducted, including public auction and giving notice.

main_sections.section_title: Application to set aside sale or on dismissal of such application
main_sections.description: Deals with the application to set aside a sale and the conditions under which such an application can be made, including the time limits and the grounds for dismissal.

Outlines how the proceeds from a sale should be distributed, including the payment of all costs, charges, and expenses, followed by the satisfaction of the debt to the bank, and the balance to the person entitled. It also specifies how disputes regarding the distribution of residue should be handled.
Details the requirement for the sale officer to grant a certificate of sale to the purchaser upon full receipt of the sale price, and the effect of such a certificate in transferring title.

Describes the procedure for delivering possession of the property to the purchaser, including situations where the property is occupied by the person who created the mortgage or hypothecation, or by a third party.

main_sections.section_title: Right of Agricultural Development Bank or Primary Bank to purchase property at sale
main_sections.description: Grants the Agricultural Development Bank or a Primary Bank the right to purchase property at a sale conducted under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of receiver and his powers
main_sections.description: Empowers the Board to appoint a receiver to take possession of and manage the property charged, and outlines the powers of the receiver.

main_sections.section_title: Title of purchaser not to be impeached
main_sections.description: States that the title of a purchaser shall not be impeached on the ground of irregularity in the sale process, provided certain conditions are met.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of Agricultural Development Bank in case security property is insufficient
main_sections.description: Provides powers to the Agricultural Development Bank and Primary Bank to take action when the security property is insufficient to cover the loan, including seeking further security or recovery from other assets.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Board or Trustee to direct distraint and sale of produce and sale of mortgaged property
main_sections.description: Grants the Board or Trustee the power to direct distraint and sale of produce, and the sale of mortgaged property, in case of default.

main_sections.section_title: Bank's right to improvements effected after Gehan or mortgage or hypothecation
main_sections.description: Addresses the bank's right to improvements made to the property after the creation of the mortgage or hypothecation.

main_sections.section_title: Deduction from sale proceeds of agricultural produce in certain cases
main_sections.description: Specifies the deductions that can be made from the sale proceeds of agricultural produce under certain circumstances, particularly when dealing with co-operative societies and commodity boards.

main_sections.section_title: Gehan or mortgage or hypothecation not to be questioned in insolvency proceedings
main_sections.description: Prohibits questioning of a Gehan, mortgage, or hypothecation in insolvency proceedings if the charge was created in good faith for valuable consideration.

main_sections.section_title: Right of Agricultural Development Bank to pay prior debts
main_sections.description: Grants the Agricultural Development Bank or a Primary Bank the right to pay off prior debts on the secured property to protect its security interest.

important_rules: If property is sold under distraint, no amount is payable by the defaulter for the distraint if the sale proceeds are sufficient to cover the debt and expenses.
The Board or Committee has the power to order the sale of property charged without court intervention, subject to fulfilling certain conditions and giving notice.
Purchasers of property sold under this Act acquire a clear title, which cannot be impeached on grounds of irregularity in the sale process if certain conditions are met.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Agricultural Development Banks, Primary Banks, Registrar, Board, Committee, Trustee, Sale Officer
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Sale of property (including distraint), appointment of receivers, direct action for recovery of dues.

rights: Right of banks to sell charged property without court intervention.
Right of banks to purchase property at sales.
Right of purchasers to clear title upon sale.
Right of banks to pay prior debts on secured property.
Right to apply to set aside a sale under specific conditions.
duties: Duty to give notice to the defaulter and other relevant parties before sale.
Duty to distribute sale proceeds according to the Act.
Duty of the sale officer to issue a certificate of sale.
Duty to deliver possession of the property to the purchaser.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the procedures laid down for sale of property.
Obligation to give notice of sale as prescribed.

key_procedures: Procedure for sale of property under distraint (Section 18).
Procedure for sale of property without court intervention (Sections 19-21).
Procedure for distribution of sale proceeds (Section 22).
Procedure for obtaining a certificate of sale (Section 23).
Procedure for delivery of property to the purchaser (Section 24).
Procedure for appointment and powers of a receiver (Section 26).
Procedure for paying prior debts on secured property (Section 34).
administration: The Act appears to be administered by the relevant state authorities overseeing co-operative banks and agricultural finance in Kerala, with specific roles assigned to the Registrar, the Board, and Committees.
important_notes: The term 'court' in section 18 refers to the Civil court with jurisdiction over the property.
The Act allows for sales of property without court intervention to expedite recovery, provided procedures are followed.
The provisions of the Act are subject to other rules and regulations and may be applied with modifications by the Board or Trustee.
Explanation to section 32 clarifies the meaning of 'Commodity Boards'.

title: The Kerala State Co-operative Agricultural And Rural Development Banks (Amendment) Act, 1999
purpose: To amend the Kerala State Co-operative Agricultural and Rural Development Banks Act, 1960.
scope: Applies to the Kerala State Co-operative Agricultural and Rural Development Banks.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies when it comes into force.

Introduces amendments to the Kerala State Co-operative Agricultural and Rural Development Banks Act, 1960. Specifically, it mentions amendments to section 1, clause (i) of sub-section (1) of section 1999-1e, and section 2, sub-section (2).

important_rules: Amendments are made to the Principal Act (Act 20 of 1960).
Specific clauses and sub-sections of the Principal Act are being modified.
administration: Not explicitly stated in the provided text, but likely related to the Co-operative Department of the Kerala Government.
important_notes: The Act commenced on 18th October 1999.
The amendments are to the Kerala State Co-operative Agricultural and Rural Development Banks Act, 1960 (Act 20 of 1960).

title: THE KERALA STATE CO-OPERATIVE AGRICULTURAL AND RURAL DEVELOPMENT BANKS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1999
purpose: To further amend the Kerala State Co-operative Agricultural and Rural Development Banks Act, 1984, for the purpose hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala State Co-operative Agricultural and Rural Development Banks.

key_definitions.Registrar: Means the Registrar of Co-operative Societies appointed under sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969 (21 of 1969), and includes any officer of the Co-operative Department, not below the rank of Joint Registrar, on whom the powers and functions of the Registrar under this Act, except those under section 5 and section 44, are conferred, by general or special order, by the Government.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala State Co-operative Agricultural and Rural Development Banks (Amendment) Act, 1999, and that it shall come into force at once.
Amends section 2 of the Kerala State Co-operative Agricultural and Rural Development Banks Act, 1984, by substituting a new clause for clause (i) which defines 'Registrar'.

administration: Co-operative Department (implied by the definition of Registrar)
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 25th day of April 1999 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No.840 dated 27th April 1999.

title: The Kerala State Co-operative Agricultural Development Banks (Amendment) Act, 1990
purpose: To further amend the Kerala State Co-operative Agricultural Development Banks Act, 1984.
scope: Applies to The Kerala State Co-operative Agricultural Development Banks.

key_definitions.rural development: Any activity intended to promote the development in rural area and includes the following developmental activities: (1) development of handicrafts and other crafts, (2) small industries, (3) cottage and village industries, (4) industries in tiny and decentralised sector, (5) rural housing needs of the rural population.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala State Co-operative Agricultural Development Banks (Amendment) Act, 1990. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 11th day of May, 1990.

In the long title to the Kerala State Co-operative Agricultural Development Banks Act, 1984 (20 of 1984), for the words "Agricultural Development Banks", the words "Agricultural and Rural Development Banks" shall be substituted.
In the Preamble to the principal Act, for the words "Agricultural Development Banks", the words "Agricultural and Rural Development Banks" shall be substituted.
In section 1 of the principal Act, for the words "Agricultural Development Banks", the words "Agricultural and Rural Development Banks" shall be substituted.

Amendments to clause (a), clause (h), clause (i), clause (m), clause (iv), and insertion of a new clause (iiA) in section 2 of the principal Act, substituting "Agricultural Development Banks" with "Agricultural and Rural Development Banks" and defining "Rural Development" and its components.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of the words "Agricultural and Rural Development Bank"
main_sections.description: Throughout the principal Act, except in the Long title, Preamble sub-section (1) of section 1 and section 2, for the words "Agricultural Development Bank", wherever it occurs, the words "Agricultural and Rural Development Bank" shall be substituted.

main_sections.section_title: Construction of references to "Agricultural Development Bank" and "the Kerala State Co-operative Agricultural Development Banks Act"
main_sections.description: References to "Agricultural Development Bank" and "the Kerala State Co-operative Agricultural Development Banks Act" in any Act or in any rule, notification, proceeding, order, regulation, by-law, bond, debenture, agreement, guarantee or other instrument made, issued or continued in force under such Act or under the principal Act, shall be construed as reference to "Agricultural and Rural Development Bank" and the "Kerala State Co-operative Agricultural and Rural Development Banks Act" respectively.

Where immediately before the commencement of the Kerala State Co-operative Agricultural Development Banks (Amendment) Act, 1990, legal proceedings are pending in which the "Agricultural Development Bank" is a party, the "Agricultural and Rural Development Bank" shall be deemed to be substituted for the "Agricultural Development Bank" in those proceedings.
Amendments to section 8 of the principal Act, specifically in clause (h), insertion of new clauses like financing individual artisans, craftsmen, etc., and related activities.

In sub-section (1) of section 16 of the principal Act, after the words "produce of the land" and before the words "to which the Gehan", the words "raw materials work in process or finished goods" shall be inserted.

title: The Kerala State Commission For Backward Classes Act, 1993
purpose: To constitute a State Commission for Backward Classes other than the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala, concerning the identification and inclusion of Backward Classes.

key_definitions.backward classes: Such backward classes of citizens, other than the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes, as are specified by the Government as other backward classes in the list.
key_definitions.Commission: The Kerala State Commission for Backward Classes constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.List: Means the list of 'other backward classes' declared as such by the Government from time to time for the purpose of making provision for the reservation of appointments or posts in favour of backward classes of citizens which, in the opinion of the Government, are not adequately represented in the services under the Government and any local or other authority within the State or under the control of the Government.
key_definitions.Member: Means a Member of the Commission and includes the Chairperson.
key_definitions.Prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Specifies the Act as the Kerala State Commission for Backward Classes Act, 1993, its extension to the whole of the State of Kerala, and its commencement on the 10th day of March, 1993.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'backward classes', 'Commission', 'Government', 'List', 'Member', and 'prescribed'.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of the Kerala State Commission for Backward Classes
main_sections.description: Establishes the Kerala State Commission for Backward Classes, detailing its composition of a Chairperson and other members nominated by the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office and conditions of service of Chairperson and Members
main_sections.description: Outlines the term of office for the Chairperson and Members, which is three years, and the conditions for resignation, removal from office, and circumstances under which a person may be removed.

main_sections.section_title: Officers and other employees of the Commission
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to provide the Commission with such officers and employees as may be necessary for the efficient performance of its functions.

main_sections.section_title: Salaries, allowances and administrative expenses to be paid out of grants
main_sections.description: States that salaries, allowances, and administrative expenses of the Chairperson, Members, officers, and other employees will be paid out of grants, as prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Vacancies etc., not to invalidate the proceedings of the Commission
main_sections.description: Ensures that vacancies in the Commission or any defect in its constitution do not invalidate its proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure to be regulated by the Commission
main_sections.description: Grants the Commission the power to regulate its own procedure, including meeting schedules and quorum, with all orders authenticated by the Member-Secretary.

Details the functions of the Commission, including inquiring into requests for the inclusion of any class of citizens in the lists and hearing complaints of over-inclusion or under-inclusion of any backward class, and advising the Government.

Confers powers on the Commission, similar to those of a civil court, for summoning and enforcing attendance, discovering and production of evidence, receiving affidavits, requisitioning public records, and issuing commissions for examination of witnesses.

main_sections.section_title: Periodic revision of lists by Government
main_sections.description: Mandates the Government to periodically revise lists of backward classes, with the advice of the Commission.
States that the Government shall, after due appropriation by law, pay grants to the Commission for its purposes.

Requires the Commission to maintain proper accounts and other relevant records, which are to be audited by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, and the audit report to be submitted to the Government.
Mandates the Commission to prepare and submit an annual report to the Government for each financial year.

main_sections.section_title: Annual report and audit report to be laid before the Legislature
main_sections.description: Requires the Government to lay the annual report and the audit report before the Legislative Assembly.

main_sections.section_title: Chairperson, Members and employees of the Commission to be public servants
main_sections.description: Declares the Chairperson, Members, and employees of the Commission as public servants within the meaning of the Indian Penal Code.

Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including rules regarding salaries, allowances, and other administrative matters, as well as procedure for making rules.
Grants the Government the power to make provisions, by order published in the Gazette, to remove any difficulty in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Repeals the Kerala State Commission for Backward Classes Ordinance, 1993 (Ordinance No 5 of 1993) and saves anything done or any action taken under that Ordinance.

important_rules: Rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act can be made by the Government.
Rules may provide for salaries, allowances, and other terms and conditions of service of the Chairperson and Members, and officers and other employees.
The annual statement of accounts shall be maintained under sub-section (1) of section 13.
Every rule made under this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before the Legislative Assembly.
Rules can be modified or annulled by the Legislative Assembly.
Rules can be made to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Kerala State Commission for Backward Classes, and the Government of Kerala.

rights: Right of citizens to request inclusion in backward classes lists.
Right to be heard regarding inclusion/exclusion from backward classes lists.
Right to have proceedings of the Commission remain valid despite vacancies.
duties: Duty of the Government to constitute the Commission.
Duty of the Government to provide staff for the Commission.
Duty of the Commission to inquire into requests and complaints.
Duty of the Commission to advise the Government.
Duty of the Government to periodically revise lists of backward classes.
Duty of the Government to lay annual reports and audit reports before the Legislature.
obligations: Members and employees of the Commission are public servants.
Orders and decisions of the Commission must be authenticated by the Member-Secretary.

key_procedures: Procedure for inclusion of a class of citizens in the backward classes list involves the Commission inquiring into requests and complaints, and then advising the Government.
Procedure for regulating the Commission's meetings and business involves the Commission itself setting its meeting times and places and regulating its own procedure.
Procedure for financial matters includes the Government providing grants, and the Commission maintaining accounts which are audited by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
Procedure for rule-making involves the Government making rules and laying them before the Legislative Assembly.
Procedure for removing difficulties involves the Government issuing orders published in the Gazette.
administration: The Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 17th day of April, 1993 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 490 dated the 17th April, 1993.
The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.
The Act came into force on the 10th day of March, 1993.
The Kerala State Commission for Backward Classes Ordinance, 1993 (Ordinance No 5 of 1993) has been repealed.
Vacancies in the Commission do not invalidate its proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of the Kerala State Commission for economically backward classes among Forward Communities

main_sections.description: This section details the term of office for the Chairperson and members, their eligibility for re-appointment, resignation, and the grounds on which the Government can remove a person from office.

main_sections.section_title: Vacancies etc., not to invalidate proceedings of the Commission

main_sections.description: This section grants the Commission the power to regulate its own procedure, including how meetings are held and the authentication of its orders and decisions.

This section mandates that the Government shall cause the reports referred to in clause (e) of section 9 to be laid before the Legislative Assembly, along with the action taken or proposed.

important_rules: The Commission shall meet as and when necessary at such time and place as the Chairperson thinks fit. (Section 8(1))

rights: Right to identify forward communities in the State of Kerala. (Section 9(a))

title: The Kerala State Commission For The Scheduled Castes And The Scheduled Tribes Act, 2007
purpose: To constitute a Commission for the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes in the State of Kerala and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and concerns matters related to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

key_definitions.Commission: The Kerala State Commission for the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.Member: A member of the Commission and includes the Chairperson.

main_sections.description: States that the State Government shall constitute a body known as the 'Kerala State Commission for the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes' to exercise the powers conferred on it and to perform the functions assigned to it under the Act. It also covers filling of vacancies.

main_sections.section_title: Salary, allowances and administrative expenses to be paid out of grants
main_sections.description: Specifies that the salary, allowances, and administrative expenses of the Chairperson, Members, officers, and other employees shall be paid out of the grants referred to in section 12.

main_sections.section_title: Vacancies etc., not to invalidate proceedings of the Commission

Requires the State Government to cause reports referred to in clause (d) of section 9 to be laid before the Legislature Assembly, explaining the action taken or proposed to be taken and the reasons, if any, for non-acceptance of the recommendations.

title: THE KERALA STATE COMMISSION FOR BACKWARD CLASSES ACT, 1993
purpose: To constitute a State Commission for Backward Classes other than the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes and to provide for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and is deemed to have come into force on the 10th day of March, 1993. It applies to backward classes other than Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes as specified by the Government.

key_definitions.backward classes: means such backward classes of citizens, other than the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes, as are specified by the Government as 'other backward classes' in the list;
key_definitions.Commission: means the Kerala State Commission for Backward Classes constituted under section 3;
key_definitions.list: means the list of 'other backward classes' declared as such by the Government from time to time for the purpose of making provision for the reservation of appointments or posts in favour of backward classes of citizens, which, in the opinion of the Government, are not adequately represented in the services under the Government and any Local or other authority within the State or under the control of the Government;
key_definitions.Member: means a Member of the Commission and includes the Chairperson;
key_definitions.prescribed: means prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala State Commission for Backward Classes Act, 1993, extends to the whole of the State of Kerala, and came into force on the 10th day of March, 1993.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of the Kerala State Commission for Backward Classes
main_sections.description: Establishes the Kerala State Commission for Backward Classes, consisting of a Chairperson and Members appointed by the Government. The Commission will have a Chairperson who is or has been a Judge of the Supreme Court or a High Court, and two persons having special knowledge in matters relating to Backward Classes nominated by the Government. The Secretary to Government in charge of Backward Classes Welfare Department, ex-officio, will be the Member Secretary.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office and conditions of service of Chairperson and Members
main_sections.description: Specifies that the Chairperson and Members shall hold office for a term of three years from the date they assume office. A Member may resign by writing under his hand to the Government, or may be removed by the Government if they become an undischarged insolvent, convicted and sentenced to imprisonment for an offence, of unsound mind, refuse to act or incapable of acting, absent from three consecutive meetings without leave, or abuse position detrimental to public interest. Vacancies will be filled within three months. Salaries and allowances shall be as prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Officers and other employees of the Commission
main_sections.description: States that the Government shall provide the Commission with such officers and employees as may be necessary for the efficient functioning of the Commission. Their salaries and allowances shall be as prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Salaries, allowances and administrative expenses to be paid out of grants
main_sections.description: Specifies that salaries, allowances and administrative expenses of the Chairperson, Members, officers, and employees shall be paid out of grants referred to in section 12.

main_sections.section_title: Vacancies etc., not to invalidate the proceedings of the Commission
main_sections.description: No act or proceeding of the Commission shall be invalid on the ground of the existence of any vacancy or defect in the constitution of the Commission.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure to be regulated by the Commission
main_sections.description: The Commission shall meet as and when necessary at such time and place as the Chairperson may think fit, but at least once in three months. The Commission shall regulate its own procedure, and all orders and decisions shall be authenticated by the Member-Secretary or any other officer of the Commission duly authorised by the Member-Secretary.

The Commission shall examine requests for inclusion of any class of citizens as a backward class in lists and hear complaints of over inclusion or under inclusion of any backward class in such lists, and tender advice to the Government. The advice of the Commission shall ordinarily be binding upon the Government.

While performing its functions, the Commission shall have the powers of a civil court trying a suit and, in particular, the power to summon and enforce attendance of any person, requiring discovery and production of any document, receiving evidence on affidavits, requisitioning any public record or copy thereof from any court or office, and issuing commissions for examination of witnesses and documents, and any other matter which may be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Periodic revision of lists by Government
main_sections.description: The Government may, at any time, and shall at the expiration of ten years from the coming into force of this Act and every succeeding period of ten years thereafter, undertake revision of the lists with a view to excluding from such lists those classes who have ceased to be backward classes or for including in such lists new backward classes. The Government shall consult the Commission before undertaking any revision.

The Government shall, after due appropriation made by the State Legislature by law in this behalf, pay to the Commission by way of grants such sums of money as the Government may think fit for the purposes of this Act. Such sums shall be treated as expenditure payable out of the grants referred to in sub-section (1).

The Commission shall maintain proper accounts and other relevant records and prepare an annual statement of accounts as may be prescribed by the Government in consultation with the Comptroller and Auditor General of India. The accounts of the Commission shall be audited by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India. The Comptroller and Auditor General of India and any person appointed by him in connection with the audit of accounts of the Commission shall have the same rights and privileges and the authority in connection with the audit as the Comptroller and Auditor General of India generally has in connection with the audit of Government accounts and, in particular, shall have the right to demand the production of books, accounts, connected vouchers and other documents and papers and to inspect any of the offices of the Commission.

The Commission shall prepare, in such form and at such time, for each financial year, as may be prescribed its annual report, giving a full account of its activities during the previous financial year and forward a copy thereof to the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Annual report and audit report to be laid before the Legislature
main_sections.description: The Government shall cause the annual report together with a memorandum of action taken on the advice tendered by the Commission under section 9 and the reasons for the non-acceptance, if any, of such advice, and the audit report, to be laid as soon as may be after they are received before the Legislative Assembly.

main_sections.section_title: Chairperson, Members and employees of the Commission to be Public Servants
main_sections.description: The Chairperson, Members and employees of the Commission shall be deemed to be public servants within the meaning of Section 21 of the Indian Penal Code (Central Act 45 of 1860).
