The Government may by notification in the Gazette make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act either prospectively or retrospectively. Such rules may provide for all or any of the following matters.

If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, the Government may, by order published in the Gazette, make such provisions as appear to them to be necessary or expedient for removing the difficulty. Provided that no such order shall be made after the expiry of a period of two years from the commencement of this Act.
Repeals and saves provisions.

important_rules: The Commission shall meet at least once in three months.
All orders and decisions of the Commission shall be authenticated by the Member-Secretary or any other officer of the Commission duly authorised by the Member-Secretary.
The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act.

If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, the Government may, by order published in the Gazette, make such provisions as appear to them to be necessary or expedient for removing the difficulty, provided no such order shall be made after the expiry of two years from the commencement of this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through rules and orders made by the Government, and the powers vested in the Commission as a civil court.

rights: The Commission has the power to summon and enforce attendance of any person.
The Commission has the power to require the discovery and production of any document.
The Commission has the power to receive evidence on affidavits.
The Commission has the power to requisition any public record or copy thereof from any court or office.
The Commission has the power to issue commissions for the examination of witnesses and documents.
duties: The Commission shall examine requests for inclusion of any class of citizens as a backward class in lists.
The Commission shall hear complaints of over inclusion or under inclusion of any backward class in such lists.
The Commission shall tender advice to the Government.
The Commission shall prepare an annual report.
obligations: The advice of the Commission shall ordinarily be binding upon the Government.

key_procedures: Requests for inclusion of a class as a backward class are examined by the Commission, which then tenders advice to the Government.
Complaints of over or under inclusion in backward class lists are heard by the Commission, which advises the Government.
The Government undertakes periodic revision of backward class lists every ten years, after consulting the Commission.
The Commission's accounts are maintained, audited by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, and the audit report is laid before the Legislature.
The Commission prepares an annual report of its activities, which along with the Government's action on the Commission's advice and the audit report, is laid before the Legislative Assembly.
administration: Government of Kerala, specifically the Department dealing with Backward Classes Welfare.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 17th day of April, 1993 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 450 dated the 17th April, 1993.
Section 3(2) regarding the constitution of Chairperson and Members was substituted by Act 10 of 2000.

The Government can remove a Member if they are an undischarged insolvent, convicted and sentenced to imprisonment, of unsound mind, refuse to act, are absent from three consecutive meetings without leave, or abuse their position.
No person shall be removed under Section 4(3)(f) without being given a reasonable opportunity of being heard.
Any difficulty in giving effect to the Act can be removed by the Government through an order published in the Gazette, within two years of the Act's commencement.

title: The Kerala State Commission for Backward Classes (Amendment) Act, 2000
purpose: To amend the Kerala State Commission for Backward Classes Act, 1993.
scope: Applies to the Kerala State Commission for Backward Classes.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala State Commission for Backward Classes (Amendment) Act, 2000. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 18th day of January, 2000.

Amends section 3 of the Kerala State Commission for Backward Classes Act, 1993. Specifies the composition of the Commission, including a Chairman who is a Judge of the Supreme Court or a High Court, and two persons with special knowledge in matters relating to Backward Classes nominated by the Government. It also states that the Secretary to Government in charge of the Backward Classes Welfare Department of the Government, ex-officio, shall be the Member-Secretary of the Commission.

Repeals the Kerala State Commission for Backward Classes (Amendment) Ordinance, 2000 (2 of 2000). Notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act, as amended by the said Ordinance, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act, as amended by this Act.

administration: Government of Kerala, Department in charge of Backward Classes Welfare.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 30th day of March, 2000 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary, No. 594 dated 30th March, 2000.

title: The Kerala State Handloom Weavers Co-Operative Society (Special Provisions) Act, 1960
purpose: To make special provisions for the formation of the Kerala State Handloom Weavers' Co-operative Society.
scope: The Act applies to the entire State of Kerala. It also covers provisions related to the Madras Act and their application to certain societies within Kerala.

key_definitions.Madras Act: means the Madras Co-operative Societies Act, 1932, as in force in Malabar.
key_definitions.Malabar: means the Malabar district referred to in sub-section (2) of section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (Central Act 37 of 1955).
key_definitions.Travancore-Cochin Act: means the Travancore-Cochin Co-operative Societies Act, 1951.
key_definitions.Kozhikode Society: means the Kerala Handloom Weavers' Co-operative Society, Limited, No. 142, Kozhikode;
key_definitions.Trichur Society: means the Cochin Central Co-operative Industries Marketing Society, Limited, No. 401, Trichur;
key_definitions.Trivandrum Society: means the Travancore-Sreemoolam Handloom Weavers' Central Co-operative Society, Limited, No. 508, Trivandrum;
key_definitions.Registrar: means the Registrar of Co-operative Societies appointed under section 3 of the Travancore-Cochin Act;

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala State Handloom Weavers' Co-operative Society (Special Provisions) Act, 1960, extends to the whole of the State of Kerala, and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including "Madras Act", "Malabar", "Travancore-Cochin Act", "Kozhikode Society", "Trichur Society", "Trivandrum Society", "Registrar", and "State".

main_sections.section_title: Formation of the Kerala State Handloom Weavers' Co-operative Society
main_sections.description: Outlines the process for forming the Kerala State Handloom Weavers' Co-operative Society, including provisions for the amalgamation of existing societies and the transfer of their assets and liabilities. It specifies how certain societies are deemed to be formed or amalgamated under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions of the Madras Act to govern in certain matters
main_sections.description: States that provisions of the Madras Act, as otherwise provided in section 3, the rights and liabilities of a society registered or deemed to be registered under the Madras Act which has become a member of the Apex Society, shall continue to be governed by the provisions of the Madras Act, and the rules made thereunder, and the bye-laws of that society.

main_sections.section_title: Power to make rules for facilitating amalgamation
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to make rules, by notification in the Gazette, for such incidental, consequential or supplementary matters as are necessary for the purpose of this Act, and all such rules shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

Empowers the Government to remove any difficulty that may arise in giving effect to the provisions of the Act. The Government may do anything not inconsistent with the provisions of the Act that appears to them to be necessary for the purpose of removing the difficulty.

rights: Societies formed under the Act have the right to participate in the amalgamation process.
Societies have the right to have their assets and liabilities transferred upon amalgamation.
duties: Societies must comply with the provisions of the Act and any rules made thereunder.
Societies involved in amalgamation must follow the procedures outlined in the Act.
obligations: Societies that become members of the Apex Society are subject to the provisions of the Madras Act and the rules made thereunder, as well as the bye-laws of the Apex Society.

key_procedures: Amalgamation of handloom weavers' co-operative societies into the Kerala State Handloom Weavers' Co-operative Society, including provisions for transfer of assets, liabilities, and membership.
Government's power to make rules for facilitating amalgamation and to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
administration: The Government of Kerala, through relevant notifications and rule-making powers.
important_notes: The Act was enacted to make special provisions for the formation of the Kerala State Handloom Weavers' Co-operative Society.
Rules made under the Act are subject to modification or repeal by the Legislative Assembly.
The Government has the power to remove difficulties in the application of the Act.
Published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 17th April, 1960.

title: The Kerala State Higher Education Council (Amendment) Act, 2018
purpose: This act amends The Kerala State Higher Education Council Act, 2007.
scope: Applies to The Kerala State Higher Education Council Act, 2007.

key_definitions.Higher Education Council: Refers to The Kerala State Higher Education Council established under the principal Act.
key_definitions.Act: Refers to The Kerala State Higher Education Council Act, 2007.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Kerala State Higher Education Council (Amendment) Act, 2018' and states that it shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 5 of Act 6 of 2007
main_sections.description: Amends section 5 of the Principal Act, which deals with the constitution of the Council. This amendment likely pertains to the composition or powers related to the Council's formation.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 22 of Act 6 of 2007
main_sections.description: Amends section 22 of the Principal Act. This section, prior to amendment, likely dealt with the powers and functions of the Council, and the amendment introduces or modifies these.

Inserts new sections into the Principal Act. The specific content of these new sections is detailed through various sub-clauses, concerning amendments to existing sections or the introduction of new provisions related to the Council's operations, finances, and committees.
Inserts a new section 11A into the Principal Act, likely to provide for specific powers or procedures not covered in the original act.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 20 of Act 6 of 2007
main_sections.description: Amends section 20 of the Principal Act, possibly related to financial matters or powers of the Council.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 25 of Act 6 of 2007
main_sections.description: Amends section 25 of the Principal Act, which might concern the rule-making powers or specific operational aspects.
Provides for the repeal of any inconsistent provisions and saving of actions taken under the previous enactments.

important_rules: Amendments are made to sections concerning the constitution of the Council, its powers and functions, and financial provisions.
New sections are inserted to introduce additional provisions or clarify existing ones.
The Act ensures that actions taken under previous legislation remain valid unless inconsistent with the amendment.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala (implied through notification and rule-making powers)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications in the Gazette, and potentially through rules and regulations framed under the Act.

key_procedures: Government notification in the Gazette for commencement of the Act.
Amendment of specific sections of the Principal Act to alter its provisions.
Insertion of new sections to add or clarify functions and powers.
Saving of actions taken under the repealed or amended provisions.
administration: The Kerala State Higher Education Council
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the existing Kerala State Higher Education Council Act, 2007.
Specific sections of the 2007 Act are being amended.
New sections are being introduced to enhance or clarify the Council's functions and structure.
The Act specifies that the amendment comes into force on a date appointed by the Government.
It includes a repeal and saving clause to ensure legal continuity.

title: THE KERALA STATE HOUSING BOARD (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1990
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala State Housing Board Act, 1971.
scope: Applies to the Kerala State Housing Board and its operations.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala State Housing Board (Amendment) Act, 1990, and it came into force on the 27th day of May, 1989.

Amends section 19 of the Kerala State Housing Board Act, 1971, by substituting "receive pensions or gratuities" for "receive pensions or gratuities" and "such gratuities" for "such pensions, gratuities".
Amends section 162 of the principal Act by adding a proviso to sub-section (1) concerning regulations relating to pensions, which may be made either prospectively or retrospectively.
Repeals the Kerala State Housing Board (Amendment) Ordinance, 1990 (7 of 1990) and saves any repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the Ordinance.

administration: Kerala State Housing Board
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 20th day of January 1991 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 102 dated the 23rd January 1991.
The Act is an amendment to the Kerala State Housing Board Act, 1971.

title: THE KERALA STATE HOUSING BOARD (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1981
purpose: To amend the Kerala State Housing Board Act, 1971, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala State Housing Board Act, 1971.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala State Housing Board (Amendment) Act, 1981, and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 7th day of May, 1981.

Amends section 50 of the Kerala State Housing Board Act, 1971 (hereinafter referred to as the Principal Act), in subsection (2), for clause (a), the following clause shall be substituted: '(a) cause the said notice to be published in the Gazette or in two daily newspapers having wide circulation in the locality in which the area comprised in the scheme is situate, specifying the period upto which the objections will be received; and'.
Amends section 52 of the Principal Act, in subsection (1), for the words "first published", the word "published" shall be substituted.

The Kerala State Housing Board (Amendment) Ordinance, 1981 (2 of 1981), is hereby repealed. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_notes: Received the assent on the Governor on the 17th day of August, 1981 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 657 dated the 17th August, 1981.

title: The Kerala State Housing Board (Amendment) Act, 2012
purpose: To further amend The Kerala State Housing Board Act, 1971, for the purposes hereinafter appearing, specifically to insert a new section (36A) empowering the Board to undertake housing or improvement or development schemes through Joint Venture Project or Public-Private Partnership.
scope: Applies to The Kerala State Housing Board Act, 1971.

key_definitions.Joint Venture Project or Public-Private: means participation of the Board with private person or company selected through a transparent and open process for executing any housing or improvement or development scheme including commercial complexes, shopping malls etc.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called The Kerala State Housing Board (Amendment) Act, 2012 and shall come into force on the 16th day of February, 2012.

Inserts section 36A into The Kerala State Housing Board Act, 1971. This new section grants the Board power to undertake housing or improvement or development schemes through Joint Venture Project or Public-Private Partnership.

Repeals The Kerala State Housing Board (Amendment) Ordinance, 2012. Notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act, as amended by the said Ordinance is hereby kept valid.

important_rules: The Board is empowered to undertake housing or improvement or development schemes through Joint Venture Project or Public-Private Partnership.
Any scheme under Joint Venture Project or Public-Private Partnership requires selection of a private person or company through a transparent and open process.
The insertion of section 36A into the principal Act is effective from February 16, 2012.

rights: The Board has the right to undertake housing or development schemes through joint ventures or public-private partnerships.

key_procedures: Selection of private persons or companies for joint venture or public-private partnership schemes must be through a transparent and open process.
administration: Government of Kerala, Law (Legislation-ID) Department
important_notes: The Act is published by the authority of the Kerala Gazette.
The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 26th day of June, 2012.

title: THE KERALA STATE HOUSING BOARD (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1988
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala State Housing Board Act, 1971.
scope: Applies to the Kerala State Housing Board Act, 1971.

main_sections.description:
(1) The Act may be called the Kerala State Housing Board (Amendment) Act, 1988.
(2) It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 15th day of February, 1988.

In the Kerala State Housing Board Act, 1971 (19 of 1971) (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), in section 6 for sub-sections (1) and (2), the following sub-section shall be substituted, namely:-- 
"(1) The Chairman and the members of the Board shall hold office during the pleasure of the Government: 
Provided that the term of office of the Chairman appointed under section 4 or a member nominated under clause (c) of the said section shall not in any case exceed three years from the date of his appointment or nomination, as the case may be."
(2) Notwithstanding such repeal anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

administration: GOVERNMENT OF Kerala, Law (Legislation-C) Department
important_notes: The Act further amends the Kerala State Housing Board Act, 1971.
The amendment came into force on February 15, 1988.
Section 6 of the principal Act is amended regarding the term of office of the Chairman and members, stating they hold office during the pleasure of the Government, with a maximum term of three years.
Actions taken under the previous Ordinance are deemed valid under the amended Act.

title: The Kerala State Legislature (Continuance of the Use of English Language) Act, 1965
purpose: To provide for the continued use of English language for the transaction of business in the Legislature of the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the Legislature of the State of Kerala and the transaction of business therein.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called The Kerala State Legislature (Continuance of the Use of English Language) Act, 1965 and shall come into force on the 26th day of January, 1965.

main_sections.section_title: Continuance of English language for the transaction of business in the Legislature of the State.
main_sections.description: Notwithstanding the expiration of the period of fifteen years from the commencement of the Constitution, English language, as from the 26th day of January, 1965, shall continue to be used, in addition to the other languages referred to in clause (1) of article 210 thereof, for the transaction of business in the Legislature of the State of Kerala.

important_rules: English language shall continue to be used for the transaction of business in the Legislature of the State of Kerala, in addition to other languages referred to in clause (1) of article 210 of the Constitution.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be the Legislature itself and relevant authorities overseeing legislative proceedings.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the continued application of English in legislative proceedings as mandated by the Act.

duties: The duty to ensure the continued use of English language in the Legislature of Kerala for conducting business.

administration: The administration of this Act would fall under the purview of the Kerala State Legislature and its presiding officers.
important_notes: The Act was enacted in exercise of the powers conferred by section 3 of the Kerala State Legislature (Delegation of Powers) Act, 1964 (30 of 1964).
Published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 17, dated the 25th January, 1965.

title: The Kerala State Right to Service Act, 2012
purpose: To provide for the delivery of services to the general public within the stipulated time limit and for matters connected therewith and incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the delivery of services to the general public by the Government and its various departments, local self-government institutions, and statutory bodies in Kerala.

key_definitions.designated officer: An officer designated as such under section 3 for providing the services as per the provisions of this Act.
key_definitions.eligible person: A person who is eligible for the services notified under section 3.
key_definitions.first appellate authority: An officer notified as such under section 3.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.right to service: The right of an eligible person to obtain a service within the stipulated time limit.
key_definitions.service: Any service to be provided under the provisions of any law for the time being in force or as per Government orders issued from time to time, to the general public or by any Department of the Government or by a Local Self Government Institution or by a State Public Sector Undertaking or by a Statutory Body, as may be notified under section 3.
key_definitions.second appellate authority: An officer notified as such under section 3.
key_definitions.stipulated time limit: The maximum time limit notified under section 3 to provide the service by the designated officer or to dispose of an application for such service.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala State Right to Service Act, 2012, and it shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'designated officer', 'eligible person', 'first appellate authority', 'Government', 'prescribed', 'right to service', 'service', 'second appellate authority', and 'stipulated time limit'.

main_sections.section_title: Power to notify services, stipulated time limit, designated officer etc.
main_sections.description: This section empowers the Government to notify services, their stipulated time limits, and designated officers responsible for providing them. It also specifies that designated officers, first appellate authorities, and the second appellate authority shall be notified within six months of the commencement of the Act.
Every eligible person shall have the right to obtain the services notified under section 3 within the stipulated time limit.

The designated officer shall, on receipt of an application for service by an eligible person, without prejudice to the provisions of any law for the time being in force, provide the service or reject the application within the stipulated time limit. In case of rejection, reasons shall be stated in writing and intimated to the applicant.

Any person who does not receive the required service within the stipulated time or whose application is rejected under section 5 may file an appeal to the first appellate authority within thirty days from the date of rejection or expiry of the stipulated time limit. Further appeals can be made to the second appellate authority.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure to be followed in appeal
main_sections.description: The first appellate authority and the second appellate authority, while deciding an appeal, shall have the same powers as are vested in a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, including requiring the production and inspection of documents and issuing summons.

This section outlines penalties for the designated officer for failure to provide service within the stipulated time or for delay. Penalties can include fines. The second appellate authority may impose a fine on the designated officer, and the first appellate authority may impose a fine on the designated officer for unjustified rejection or delay.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against any person or officer for anything which is done or intended to be done in good faith under this Act or any rule made thereunder.

main_sections.section_title: Bar of jurisdiction of Civil Courts
main_sections.description: No civil court shall entertain any suit, application or other proceeding in respect of any order issued under this Act and no such order shall be called in question otherwise than by way of an appeal under this Act.
The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make rules to carry out the provisions of this Act. Every rule made under this Act shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

Where any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, the Government may, by order published in the Gazette, as occasion may require, do anything which is considered necessary for them and not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act or the rules made thereunder, for the purpose of removing such difficulty. Every order issued under this section shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

important_rules: Services, their stipulated time limits, and designated officers must be notified by the Government.
Designated officers, first appellate authorities, and second appellate authorities must be notified within six months of the Act's commencement.
Designated officers must provide service or reject applications with reasons within the stipulated time.
Appeals to the first appellate authority must be filed within thirty days of rejection or expiry of the stipulated time.
Penalties can be imposed on designated officers for failure to provide service or for delays.
No civil court can entertain suits or proceedings regarding orders issued under this Act, except through appeals.

penalties: Fine on designated officer for failure to provide service without sufficient and reasonable cause: not less than five hundred rupees and not more than five thousand rupees.
Fine on designated officer for delay in providing service: rate of two hundred and fifty rupees per day for each day's delay, sum of which shall not exceed five thousand rupees.
Fine on designated officer for unjustified rejection or delay in deciding appeal: not less than five hundred rupees and not more than five thousand rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Designated Officers, First Appellate Authority, Second Appellate Authority, and the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the process of application for services, appeals to appellate authorities, and imposition of penalties as prescribed in the Act.

rights: Right of an eligible person to obtain notified services within the stipulated time limit.
duties: Duty of the designated officer to provide service or reject the application with reasons within the stipulated time.
Duty of the appellate authorities to decide appeals within a stipulated time frame.
obligations: The Government has an obligation to notify services, stipulated time limits, and designated officers.
The Government has an obligation to make rules and issue orders to remove difficulties.

key_procedures: Obtaining a service: An eligible person applies to the designated officer.
If service is not provided or application rejected: Appeal to the first appellate authority within 30 days.
If unsatisfied with the first appellate authority's decision: Appeal to the second appellate authority within 60 days.
Disposal of appeals by appellate authorities following procedures similar to civil courts.
administration: Government of Kerala, Law (Legislation-B) Department.
important_notes: The Act came into force on a date to be notified in the Gazette.
Designated officers, first appellate authorities, and second appellate authorities must be notified within six months of commencement.
No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against any person or officer acting in good faith under the Act.

title: The Kerala State Road Transport Corporation (Passenger Group Personal Accident Insurance Scheme)
purpose: To implement a passenger group personal accident insurance scheme for the Kerala State Road Transport Corporation passengers.
scope: Applies to all passengers of the Kerala State Road Transport Corporation.

key_definitions.Corporation: Means the Kerala State Road Transport Corporation.
key_definitions.Scheme: Means the Passenger Group Personal Accident Insurance Scheme framed under this Act.
key_definitions.Passenger: Includes any person travelling in a Corporation bus.
key_definitions.Personal Accident Insurance: Insurance covering death or injury due to accident.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as Corporation, Scheme, Passenger, Personal Accident Insurance, etc.

main_sections.section_title: Framing of Passenger Group Personal Accident Insurance Scheme
main_sections.description: Empowers the Corporation to frame a Passenger Group Personal Accident Insurance Scheme, outlining its contents and the process for its framing.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Grants the Corporation the power to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules.
Provides for the supersession of the Corporation by the Government in certain circumstances.
Empowers the Government to remove any difficulties that may arise in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of any existing laws or provisions inconsistent with this Act and saves certain actions taken under the repealed provisions.
Specifies the applicability of the Act to the Corporation and its passengers.
Repeals the Kerala State Road Transport Corporation (Passenger Group Personal Accident Insurance Scheme) Ordinance, 2014, and provides for savings.

important_rules: Passengers travelling in Corporation buses are covered under the accident insurance scheme.
The scheme shall provide for compensation in case of death or injury to passengers due to accidents.
The Corporation shall be responsible for the implementation and management of the scheme.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Kerala State Road Transport Corporation and the Government of Kerala.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the framing of schemes, rules, and regulations, and by ensuring compliance with the provisions of the Act.

rights: Passengers have the right to compensation in case of death or injury due to an accident while travelling in a Corporation bus.
duties: The Corporation has a duty to implement and manage the accident insurance scheme effectively.
The Government has the duty to frame rules and regulations to ensure the smooth functioning of the Act.
obligations: The Corporation is obligated to ensure that passengers are adequately covered by the insurance scheme.

key_procedures: Framing of the Passenger Group Personal Accident Insurance Scheme by the Corporation.
Notification of the commencement date of the Act by the Government.
Application of the rules and regulations made under the Act for the implementation of the scheme.
administration: The Kerala State Road Transport Corporation and the Transport Department, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act aims to provide financial security to passengers in case of unforeseen accidents.
The scheme's details, including compensation amounts, are to be specified in the scheme framed by the Corporation.
The Act repeals the Ordinance of 2014, ensuring continuity and improvement of the insurance scheme.

title: THE KERALA STATE RURAL DEVELOPMENT BOARD (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1998
purpose: To amend The Kerala State Rural Development Board Act, 1971.
scope: Applies to The Kerala State Rural Development Board.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala State Rural Development Board (Amendment) Act, 1998. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 5th day of January, 1994.

Amends Section 6 of the Kerala State Rural Development Board Act, 1971 (15 of 1971). Inserts a sub-section (3) regarding the Board's power to make rules for pension, sanction towards pension, and other benefits for staff. It also states that retirement on superannuation or from the Fund shall be for the purpose of the Board and such amount and in such manner as prescribed by rules made by the Government.
To sub-section (1) of section 15 of the principal Act, the following proviso is added: "Provided that the rules relating to pension may be made, either prospectively or retrospectively."

The Kerala State Rural Development Board Ordinance, 1998 (12 of 1998) is hereby repealed. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act, as amended by the said Ordinance, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act, as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Rules regarding pension for the staff of the Board can be made, either prospectively or retrospectively.
Retirement on superannuation or from the Fund is for the purpose of the Board and such amount and in such manner as prescribed by rules made by the Government.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be the Board or relevant government bodies.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application of the Act and its amendments.

key_procedures: The process for making rules regarding pension for Board staff, which can be prospective or retrospective.
The procedure for repeal and saving of ordinances, ensuring continuity of actions taken under previous legislation.
administration: The Kerala State Rural Development Board.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 9th day of August 1998 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 1302 dated 10th August 1998.
The Act is deemed to have come into force on the 5th day of January, 1994.

title: THE KERALA STATE RURAL DEVELOPMENT BOARD ACT, 1971
purpose: An Act to provide for the establishment of a Kerala State Rural Development Board for arranging water supply and other development schemes in rural areas in the State of Kerala.
scope: The Act applies to all Panchayat areas in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Board: means the Kerala State Rural Development Board constituted under section 4.
key_definitions.Chairman: means the Chairman of the Board.
key_definitions.Member: means a member of the Board.
key_definitions.Panchayat: means a Panchayat as defined in clause (20) of section 2 of the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960 (32 of 1960).
key_definitions.Panchayat area: means the Panchayat area as defined in clause (21) of section 2 of the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960 (32 of 1960).

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala State Rural Development Board Act, 1971. (2) It extends to all the Panchayat areas in the State of Kerala. (3) It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including Board, Chairman, Member, Panchayat, and Panchayat area.

main_sections.section_title: Creation and incorporation of the Board
main_sections.description: The duty of carrying out the provisions of this Act shall, subject to the restrictions, conditions and limitations therein contained, be vested in a Board to be called 'the Kerala State Rural Development Board' and such Board shall be a body corporate and have perpetual succession and a common seal and shall, by the said name, sue and be sued.

The Board shall consist of a Chairman and such number of members not exceeding ten as may be fixed by the Government from time to time. (2) The members of the Board shall be nominated by the Government. Provided that a majority of the total number of members of the Board shall be non-officials who are members of the Panchayats in the State. (3) The Chairman and members of the Board shall hold office during the pleasure of the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Regulations for proceedings of the Board
main_sections.description: The Board may, by notification in the Gazette, make regulations not inconsistent with this Act and the rules made thereunder prescribing the procedure for holding its meetings, for transaction of business thereat and such other matters necessary for the purpose of giving effect to the provisions of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Officers and servants of the Board
main_sections.description: The Board may, with the prior approval of the Government, appoint such staff for the due performance of the functions vested in it under this Act. Provided that the Board may, with the prior approval of the Government, appoint officers in the service of the Government to attend to the functions of the Board in addition, to their duties under the Government. (2) The staff of the Board appointed under sub-section (1) shall be paid from the fund of the Board such remuneration as the Board may, with the prior approval of the Government, fix from time to time and they shall be under the administrative control of the Chairman. The Chairman shall be the authority competent to grant leave and to impose penalties on the members of the staff of the Board.

main_sections.section_title: Functions and duties of the Board
main_sections.description: It shall be lawful for the Board to arrange for the execution of any of the following types of schemes in a Panchayat area, namely - (a) water supply schemes, (b) sewerage schemes, (c) development schemes which shall include the construction of bus stands, cart stands, market buildings and the like: Provided that before arranging for the execution of any scheme within a Panchayat area, the Board shall consult the Panchayat concerned and obtain its concurrence to the scheme. (2) Any panchayat may request the Board to arrange for the execution of any of the types of schemes referred to in sub-section (1) within its area and the Board may, subject to availability of funds, make reasonable provision for executing the scheme.

main_sections.section_title: Execution of the schemes to be entrusted to Government Engineering Departments
main_sections.description: The execution of the schemes shall be arranged by the Board through the Engineering Departments of the Government.

The Board shall have its own fund. (2) The Board may accept grants, subventions, donations and gifts from the Central or State Government or a Panchayat or any individual or body, whether incorporate or not for all or any of the purposes of the Act. (3) All moneys received by or on behalf of the Board by virtue of this Act shall constitute the fund of the Board and shall be deposited into the public accounts of the Government under such detailed head of accounts as may be directed by the Government or in any nationalised bank. The said account shall be operated upon by the Chairman or such official members of the Board as may be authorised by the Government.

Subject to such conditions and limitations as may be laid down by the Government, and with their prior approval, the Board may, for the promotion and execution of any scheme under this Act, raise loans or borrow money from any bank or other financial institutions approved by the Government or from the Life Insurance Corporation of India established under section 3 of the Life Insurance Corporation Act, 1956 (Central Act 31 of 1956).

main_sections.section_title: Guarantee of loans by the Government
main_sections.description: The Government may guarantee in such manner as they think fit, the repayment of the principal and payment of interest of any loan proposed to be raised by the Board.

main_sections.section_title: Board to be a local authority under the Kerala Local Authorities Loans Act
main_sections.description: The Board shall be deemed to be a local authority for the purpose of the Kerala Local Authorities Loans Act, 1963 (30 of 1963).

main_sections.section_title: Board's power to recover the cost of the scheme from the beneficiary Panchayats
main_sections.description: (1) It shall be lawful for the Board to recover from a Panchayat in such annual instalments as may be decided upon in consultation with the Panchayat concerned, the whole or any portion of the expenditure incurred by the Board in the execution of any of the schemes under this Act within the Panchayat area. (2) If any Panchayat fails to pay the amount as decided upon, under sub-section (1), the Board, it shall be recoverable from the Panchayat in the manner laid down in the Kerala Local Authorities Loans Act, 1963 (30 of 1963).

If any dispute arises between the Board and any of the Panchayats in respect of the matters provided for in this Act, such dispute shall be referred to the Government whose decision thereon shall be final.

(1) The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make rules for the purpose of carrying into effect the provisions of this Act. (2) Every rule made under sub-section (1) shall be laid as soon as may be after it is made, before the Legislative Assembly while it is in session for a total period of fourteen days which may be comprised in one session or in two successive sessions, and, if, before the expiry of the session in which it is so laid or the session immediately following, the Legislative Assembly makes any modification in the rule or decides that the rule should not be issued, the rule shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect, as the case may be, so however that any such modification or annulment shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything done under that rule.

If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, the Government may, as occasion may require by order, do anything not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act which appears to them necessary or proper for the purpose of removing the difficulty.

important_rules: All moneys received by or on behalf of the Board shall constitute the fund of the Board and shall be deposited into the public accounts of the Government or in any nationalised bank.
The Board may raise loans or borrow money from any bank or other financial institutions approved by the Government or from the Life Insurance Corporation of India.
Any Panchayat may request the Board to arrange for the execution of types of schemes within its area.
The Board shall consult the Panchayat concerned and obtain its concurrence before arranging for the execution of any scheme.
The execution of schemes shall be arranged by the Board through the Engineering Departments of the Government.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through decisions on disputes (Section 14), and making rules (Section 15) and issuing orders to remove difficulties (Section 16).

rights: Right to sue and be sued in its corporate name (Section 3).
duties: To arrange for the execution of water supply, sewerage, and development schemes in Panchayat areas (Section 7).
obligations: To recover the cost of schemes from beneficiary Panchayats (Section 13).

key_procedures: The Board's proceedings are governed by regulations made by the Board itself (Section 5).
The Board appoints staff, who are under the administrative control of the Chairman (Section 6).
The Board consults Panchayats before executing schemes and can recover costs from them (Sections 7 & 13).
Disputes between the Board and Panchayats are referred to the Government for final decision (Section 14).
Government makes rules for implementing the Act, which are subject to modification by the Legislative Assembly (Section 15).
Government can issue orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act (Section 16).
administration: The Kerala State Rural Development Board.
important_notes: The Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 256, dated 27th May, 1971.
The Board is deemed to be a local authority for the purpose of the Kerala Local Authorities Loans Act, 1963.
Government has the power to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.

title: The Kerala State Rural Development Board (Amendment) Act, 1989
purpose: To amend the Kerala State Rural Development Board Act, 1971.
scope: Applies to the Kerala State Rural Development Board and its activities.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Kerala State Rural Development Board (Amendment) Act, 1989' and states that it shall come into force on the 26th day of May, 1989.

Amends section 7 of the Kerala State Rural Development Board Act, 1971. It modifies the wording related to the execution of schemes and advance loans by the Board. Specifically, it replaces certain phrases with others and allows the Board, subject to availability of funds, to arrange for the execution of schemes or advance loans.
Amends section 10 of the principal Act. It replaces the words 'other financial institutions' with 'or agencies'.

Amends section 13 of the principal Act. It states that it shall be lawful for the Board to recover from a Panchayat, in such annual installments as may be decided upon in consultation with the Panchayat concerned, the whole or any portion of the expenditure incurred or loans advanced by the Board for the execution of any of the schemes under this Act, together with interest, if any payable thereon.

Repeals The Kerala State Rural Development Board (Amendment) Ordinance, 1989 (6 of 1989). It also provides a saving clause, stating that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Kerala State Rural Development Board
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the recovery of expenditure or loans from Panchayats as specified in the amended Section 13.

obligations: Panchayats are obligated to repay expenditure or loans incurred by the Board for scheme execution, including interest, in annual installments.

key_procedures: Amendment of existing sections of the principal Act to clarify or modify the Board's powers and responsibilities.
Recovery of expenditure or loans from Panchayats by the Board.
administration: The Kerala State Rural Development Board
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 5th day of July 1989 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 630 dt. the 6th July 1989.
The commencement date of the Act is the 26th day of May, 1989.

title: THE KERALA STAY OF EVICTION PROCEEDINGS ACT, 1967
purpose: To provide for the stay of eviction to tenants and kudikidappukars and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act applies to the whole of the State of Kerala and comes into force on the 31st day of December, 1968. It applies to lands or buildings or both belonging to or vested in the Government of Kerala or the Government of any other State in India or the Government of India or a local authority or a corporation owned or controlled by the Government of Kerala or the Government of any other State in India or the Government of India. It also applies to any lease of land or building or both granted by the Administrator-General, Official Trustee or Official Receiver.

key_definitions.court: Includes context where otherwise requires, 'holding', 'improvement', 'kudikidappukaran', 'kudikidappukars', 'Land Tribunal', 'rent', 'resumption', and 'tenant'.
key_definitions.holding: Means a parcel or parcels of land held under a single transaction by a tenant from a landlord and shall include any portion of a holding as above defined which the landlord and tenant have agreed or are bound to treat as a separate holding.
key_definitions.kudikidappukaran: A person who has no homestead or any land exceeding three cents in extent, either as owner or as tenant in possession, on which he could erect a homestead.
key_definitions.rent: Includes arrear of rent payable by tenants.
key_definitions.restoration of possession: Relates to the holding of a tenant where the holding has been sold before the commencement of the Act and the tenant is entitled to restoration of possession.
key_definitions.cancellation of certain sales: Relates to sales of holding for arrears of rent or damages.
key_definitions.land tribunal: Includes civil courts and Land Tribunals.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, commencement and duration.
main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Stay of Eviction Proceedings Act, 1967. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. It shall come into force at once and shall cease to have effect on the 31st day of December, 1968. The provisions of section 4 of the Interpretation and General Clauses Act, 1125 (VII of 1125), shall apply as if this Act had been repealed by an Act of the Kerala State Legislature.

Defines 'court', 'eviction', 'holding', 'improvement', 'kudikidappukaran', 'kudikidappukars', 'Land Tribunal', 'rent', 'resumption' and 'tenant' with their respective meanings assigned to them in the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963.

Specifies the exemptions from the application of this Act, including lands or buildings vested in the Government of Kerala or India, or granted by Administrator-General, Official Trustee or Official Receiver. It also clarifies that a renewed tenancy or a lease granted by Administrator-General, Official Trustee or Official Receiver shall not be deemed to be a lease granted by the Administrator-General-General or the Official Trustee or the Official Receiver.

Provides for the stay of eviction proceedings in any court or Land Tribunal, notwithstanding anything contained in any other law, or in any contract, custom or usage, or in any judgment, decree or order of any court or Land Tribunal, with effect on and from the commencement of this Act, no suit or application or other proceedings for eviction or shifting of a kudikidappukaran from his holding or part thereof or for resumption of a holding or part thereof from a tenant, shall lie in any court or Land Tribunal, and all suits, applications, proceedings in execution of decrees or orders and other proceedings pending in courts or Land Tribunals at such commencement for such eviction, shifting or resumption shall be stayed.

main_sections.section_title: Arrears of rent payable by tenants.
main_sections.description: Stipulates that notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in any other law, or in any contract, custom or usage, or in any judgment, decree or order of any court or Land Tribunal, with effect on and from the commencement of this Act, no suit or application or other proceedings for the recovery of arrears of rent in respect of, or for damages for use and occupation of, a holding or a kudikidappu, accrued due before the 1st day of April, 1966, shall lie in any court or Land Tribunal, and all suits, applications, proceedings in execution of decrees or orders and other proceedings pending in courts or Land Tribunals at such commencement for recovery of arrears of rent or damages shall be stayed.

Provides for the restoration of possession of a holding to a tenant if the holding was sold in execution of a decree for arrears of rent and the tenant dispossessed of the holding after the first day of April, 1964 and before the commencement of the Act. The tenant is entitled to restoration of possession upon deposit of six per cent per annum of the sale consideration. The court may also order the deposit of suit amount towards costs of the decree-holder or auction-purchaser and value of improvements.

Deals with the cancellation of sales of holdings for arrears of rent. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, any holding sold before the commencement of the Act for arrears of rent, may, within three months from the commencement of this Act, upon deposit of the decree-amount with interest at the rate of six per cent per annum, be cancelled and the tenant restored to possession.

Specifies the period of limitation for suits, applications or other proceedings prohibited or stayed under this Act. The time during which such suits, applications or other proceedings were prohibited or stayed under the Kerala Stay of Eviction Proceedings Ordinance, 1967 (4 of 1967) and under this Act shall be excluded.
States that the provisions of this Act shall be in force in regulating any of the matters dealt with in this Act, notwithstanding anything in any other law for the time being in force.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963.
main_sections.description: Amends Section 2 and Section 29 of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963.

Repeals the Kerala Stay of Eviction Proceedings Ordinance, 1967 (4 of 1967) and provides that anything done or action taken under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Eviction proceedings are stayed from the commencement of the Act.
Suits or applications for recovery of arrears of rent accrued due before April 1, 1966, are stayed.
Tenants dispossessed of holdings after April 1, 1964, due to arrears of rent are entitled to restoration of possession upon deposit of sale consideration with interest.
Sales of holdings for arrears of rent can be cancelled within three months of the Act's commencement upon deposit of decree amount with interest.
Certain definitions from the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 are incorporated and amended.
Special provisions for mortgagees of waste lands are included.

penalties: Section 117-A: Penalty for disturbance of easements attached to kudikidappu – Any person who in any manner disturbs or interferes with the easements to which a kudikidappukaran is entitled shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees, or with both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts and Land Tribunals.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through stay of proceedings, restoration of possession, cancellation of sales, and imposition of penalties for disturbance of easements.

rights: Right of tenants to stay of eviction proceedings.
Right of tenants to restoration of possession of holdings sold for arrears of rent.
Right of kudikidappukars to protection from eviction and disturbance of easements.
duties: Duty of tenants to pay rent.
Duty of tenants to deposit sale consideration for restoration of possession.
Duty of persons to refrain from disturbing easements attached to kudikidappu.
obligations: Obligation to comply with orders of stay and restoration of possession.

key_procedures: Procedure for stay of eviction proceedings: Automatically applied from commencement of the Act.
Procedure for restoration of possession: Tenant to deposit sale consideration within a period specified by the court, along with interest and costs.
Procedure for cancellation of sales: Deposit of decree amount with interest within three months of Act commencement.
Procedure for amendment of Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963: Specific amendments to definitions and sections as detailed in Section 10.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but enforcement is through Courts and Land Tribunals.
important_notes: The Act has a limited duration and ceases to have effect on December 31, 1968.
The Act aims to provide relief to tenants and kudikidappukars from eviction and to regulate certain land dealings.
Specific definitions from the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 are incorporated, indicating a link between the two acts.
The Act contains provisions for the stay of proceedings and for the restoration of possession, reflecting its remedial nature.

title: The Kerala Stay Of Eviction Proceedings (Amendment) Act, 1969
purpose: To amend the Kerala Stay of Eviction Proceedings Act, 1967 for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Stay of Eviction Proceedings Act, 1967.

key_definitions.jenmi: Includes terms like 'jemmikararn' and 'kanam tenant' as they are respectively assigned in the Kanarn Tenancy Act, 1955.
key_definitions.kanam tenant: As defined in the Kanarn Tenancy Act, 1955.
key_definitions.holding: Means a parcel or parcels of land held under a single transaction by a tenant from a landlord and shall include any portion of a holding above defined which the landlord and tenant have agreed or are bound to treat as a separate holding.
key_definitions.intermediary: Means any person who, not being a landowner or mortgagee (other than a mortgagee deemed to be a tenant under section 4A, or section 5 of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 (1 of 1964) or under section 2A or section 2B of this Act), has an interest in the land and is entitled, by reason of such interest, to possession thereof, but has transferred such possession to any other person otherwise than by way of mortgage (other than a mortgage falling under any of the said sections).
key_definitions.kanam-kuzhikkanam: Means a transfer by a landlord to another person of garden lands or of other lands or of both— (a) with the fruit-bearing trees, if any, standing thereon at the time of the transfer; or (b) where the landlord reserves all or any one or more of such trees for his enjoyment or the enjoyment of any other person, with the remaining fruit-bearing trees, if any, standing thereon at the time of the transfer; for the enjoyment of those trees and for the purpose of planting such fruit-bearing trees thereon, the incidents of which transfer include— (i) a right in the transfer to hold the said lands liable for the consideration paid by him or due to him, which consideration is called "kanartham", and (ii) the liability of the transferor to pay to the transferee interest on the kanartham unless otherwise agreed to by the parties.
key_definitions.kudikidappukaran: Means a person who has neither a homestead nor any land exceeding five cents in extent, either as owner or as tenant in possession, on which he could erect a homestead;— (a) who has been permitted by or without an obligation to pay rent to a person in lawful possession of any land to have the use and occupation of a portion of such land for the purpose of erecting a homestead; or (b) who has been permitted by a person in lawful occupation of land to occupy, with or without an obligation to pay rent, a hut belonging to such person and situate in the said land, but otherwise has no interest in the land, and 'kudikidappu' means the land and the homestead or the hut so permitted to be erected or occupied together with the easements attached thereto : Provided that a person who, on the 1st day of April 1967, was in occupation of any land and the homestead thereon, or in occupation of a hut belonging to any other person, and who continued to be in such occupation on the date of publication of the Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Bill, 1968, in the Gazette shall be deemed to be in occupation of such land and homestead, or hut as the case may be, with permission as required under this clause.
key_definitions.kuzhichuvaim kudiyiruppum: means a transfer by a landlord to another person of garden lands or of other lands or of both situate in Malabar, reserving the right to enjoy the fruit-bearing trees standing thereon at the time of the transfer, for the purpose of making improvements thereon, and described as such in the contract of tenancy;
key_definitions.kuzhikkanam: means a transfer by a landlord to another person of garden lands or of other lands or of both— (a) with the fruit-bearing trees, if any, standing thereon at the time of the transfer; or (b) where the landlord reserves all or any one or more of such trees for his enjoyment or the enjoyment of any other person, with the remaining fruit-bearing trees, if any, standing thereon at the time of the transfer; for the enjoyment of those trees and for the purpose of planting such fruit-bearing trees thereon, and includes an ottikuzhikankam but shall not include a usufructuary mortgage as defined in the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (Central Act 4 of 1882).
key_definitions.possession: in relation to land includes occupation of land by a person deemed to be a tenant under section 4, section 4A, section 5, section 8 or section 9 of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 (1 of 1964) or under section 2A, section 2B, section 2C, section 2D, section 2E, or section 2F of this Act ;
key_definitions.tenant: means any person who has paid or has agreed to pay rent or other consideration, for his being allowed by another to possess and to enjoy the land of the latter and includes— (a) an intermediary, (b) a kanamdar, (c) a kanam-kuzhikamdamr, (d) a kuzhikánamdar, (e) a mulgenidar, (f) a verumpattamdar of any description (including a customary verumpattamdar), (g) the holder of a chalgeni lease, (h) the holder of a kudiyiruppu, (i) a person holding land under a kuzhichuvaim kudiyiruppum, (j) the holder of a karáima, (k) the holder of vaidageni lease, (l) a person who is deemed to be a tenant under section 4, section 4A, section 5, section 8, or section 9 of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 (1 of 1964), or section 2A, section 2B, section 2C, section 2D, section 2E, or section 2F of this Act;

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Stay of Eviction Proceedings (Amendment) Act, 1969. It shall come into force at once.

In sub-section (1) of section 1 of the Kerala Stay of Eviction Proceedings Act, 1967 (9 of 1967) (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), for the figures, letters and words "31st day of December, 1968", the figures, letters and words "31st day of December 1969" shall be substituted.

In sub-section (1) of section 1 of the Kerala Stay of Eviction Proceedings Act, 1967 (9 of 1967) (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), for the figures, letters and words "31st day of December, 1968", the figures, letters and words "31st day of December 1969" shall be substituted.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new sections for section 2.
main_sections.description: For section 2 of the principal Act, the following sections shall be substituted, namely : "2. Definition.—In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires,— (i) the terms 'jenmi', 'jemmikararn' and 'kanam tenant' shall have the meanings respectively assigned to them in the Kanarn Tenancy Act, 1955 (24 of 1955); (ii) the terms 'cochin', 'court', 'cultivate', 'cultivating tenant', 'customary verumpattamdar', 'eviction', 'holder of a chalgeni lease', 'kanamdar', 'kudiyiruppu', 'landlord', 'Land Tribunal', 'licensee', 'Malabar', 'mulgenidar', 'punam or kumri cultivator', 'rent', 'resumption', 'vaidageni lease', 'varamdar', 'vechukapukthidar' and 'verumpattamdar' shall have the meanings respectively assigned to them in the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 (1 of 1964); (iii) 'holding' means a parcel or parcels of land held under a single transaction by a tenant from a landlord and shall include any portion of a holding above defined which the landlord and tenant have agreed or are bound to treat as a separate holding. Explanation.—Where by act of parties or by operation of law, the interest of the tenant in his holding has been severed, splitting up the holding into two or more parts, or where a portion of the holding has been sub-leased, before the commencement of this Act, each such part or, as the case may be, each of the portions retained by the tenant and sub-leased, shall be deemed to be a separate holding. (iv) 'intermediary' means any person who, not being a landowner or mortgagee (other than a mortgagee deemed to be a tenant under section 4A, or section 5 of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 (1 of 1964) or under section 2A, section 2B, section 2C, section 2D, section 2E, or section 2F of this Act), has an interest in the land and is entitled, by reason of such interest, to possession thereof, but has transferred such possession to any other person otherwise than by way of mortgage (other than a mortgage falling under any of the said sections). Explanation.—Where such a person has transferred possession only of a portion of the land which he is so entitled to possess, he shall be deemed to be an intermediary in respect of that portion; (v) 'kanam-kuzhikamdamr' means a transfer by a landlord to another person of garden lands or of other lands or of both— (a) with the fruit-bearing trees, if any, standing thereon at the time of the transfer; or (b) where the landlord reserves all or any one or more of such trees for his enjoyment or the enjoyment of any other person, with the remaining fruit-bearing trees, if any, standing thereon at the time of the transfer; for the enjoyment of those trees and for the purpose of planting such fruit-bearing trees thereon, and includes an ottikuzhikankam but shall not include a usufructuary mortgage as defined in the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (Central Act 4 of 1882). (vi) 'karáima' means a transfer of land situate in the Kozhikode District in consideration of ground rent principally for the purpose of erecting a homestead and described as karáima in the document evidencing the transfer; (vii) 'kudikidappukaran' means a person who has neither a homestead nor any land exceeding five cents in extent, either as owner or as tenant in possession, on which he could erect a homestead;— (a) who has been permitted by or without an obligation to pay rent to a person in lawful possession of any land to have the use and occupation of a portion of such land for the purpose of erecting a homestead; or (b) who has been permitted by a person in lawful occupation of land to occupy, with or without an obligation to pay rent, a hut belonging to such person and situate in the said land, but otherwise has no interest in the land, and 'kudikidappu' means the land and the homestead or the hut so permitted to be erected or occupied together with the easements attached thereto : Provided that a person who, on the 1st day of April 1967, was in occupation of any land and the homestead thereon, or in occupation of a hut belonging to any other person, and who continued to be in such occupation on the date of publication of the Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Bill, 1968, in the Gazette shall be deemed to be in occupation of such land and homestead, or hut as the case may be, with permission as required under this clause. Explanation.—For the purposes of this clause, 'hut' means any dwelling house which was constructed at a cost not exceeding five hundred rupees, or could have, at the time of construction, yielded a monthly rent not exceeding five rupees. Explanation I.—Where any kudikidappukaran secures any mortgage with possession of the land in which the kudikidappu is situate, his kudikidappu right shall revive on the redemption of the mortgage, provided that he has at the time of the redemption no other homestead or as owner or as tenant in possession, on which he could erect a homestead. Explanation II.—Where a mortgage with possession erects his residence a homestead on land which he holds on mortgage, he shall be deemed to be a kudikidappukaran in respect of such homestead, provided that— (a) he has no other homestead or any land exceeding five cents in extent, either as owner or as tenant in possession, on which he could erect a homestead; and (b) his annual income does not exceed one thousand and five hundred rupees. Explanation IV.—Where a kudikidappukaran transfers his right in the kudikidappu to another person, such person shall be deemed to be a kudikidappukaran, if— (a) he has no other homestead or any land exceeding five cents in extent, either as owner or as tenant in possession, on which he could erect a homestead; and (b) his annual income does not exceed one thousand and five hundred rupees. Explanation V.—For the purposes of this clause, a person occupying the owner of a plantation and situate in the plantation shall not be deemed to be a tenant in connection with his employment in the plantation, unless— (i) he was, immediately before the commencement of this Act, entitled to the rights of a kudikidappukaran or the holder of a protected ulkudí or kudikidappukan under any law then in force, or (ii) he would have been entitled to the rights of a kudikidappukan if the area in which hut is situated had not been converted into a plantation subsequent to his occupation of that hut. (viii) 'kuzhichuvaim kudiyiruppum' means a transfer by a landlord to another person of garden lands or of other lands or of both situate in Malabar, reserving the right to enjoy the fruit-bearing trees standing thereon at the time of the transfer, for the purpose of making improvements thereon, and described as such in the contract of tenancy; (ix) 'kuzhikkanam' means a transfer by a landlord to another person of garden lands or of other lands or of both— (a) with the fruit-bearing trees, if any, standing thereon at the time of the transfer; or (b) where the landlord reserves all or any one or more of such trees for his enjoyment or the enjoyment of any other person, with the remaining fruit-bearing trees, if any, standing thereon at the time of the transfer; for the enjoyment of those trees and for the purpose of planting such fruit-bearing trees thereon, and includes an ottikuzhikankam but shall not include a usufructuary mortgage as defined in the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (Central Act 4 of 1882). (x) 'possession' in relation to land includes occupation of land by a person deemed to be a tenant under section 4, section 4A, section 5, section 8 or section 9 of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 (1 of 1964) or under section 2A, section 2B, section 2C, section 2D, section 2E, or section 2F of this Act ; (xi) 'tenant' means any person who has paid or has agreed to pay rent or other consideration, for his being allowed by another to possess and to enjoy the land of the latter and includes— (a) an intermediary, (b) a kanamdar, (c) a kanam-kuzhikamdamr, (d) a kuzhikánamdar, (e) a mulgenidar, (f) a verumpattamdar of any description (including a customary verumpattamdar), (g) the holder of a chalgeni lease, (h) the holder of a kudiyiruppu, (i) a person holding land under a kuzhichuvaim kudiyiruppum, (j) the holder of a karáima, (k) the holder of vaidageni lease, (l) a person who is deemed to be a tenant under section 4, section 4A, section 5, section 8, or section 9 of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 (1 of 1964), or section 2A, section 2B, section 2C, section 2D, section 2E, or section 2F of this Act ; 2A. Certain mortgagees holding land on verumpattam or after 1st Chingam, 1111, to be deemed tenants.—Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in any law, or in any contract, custom or usage, or in any judgment, decree or order of court a mortgage with possession of immoveable property situate in Cochin shall be deemed to be a tenant, if— (a) the property comprised in the mortgage consists of agricultural land; and (b) he was holding the property comprised in the mortgage as verumpattamdar on or after the first day of Chingam, 1111, and before the commencement of Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 (1 of 1964), but be continued in possession of the property, without interruption, as a mortgagee with possession from the date of such termination till the commencement of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 (1 of 1964). 2B. Certain persons who were holding land on or after 1st December, 1930, to be deemed tenants.—Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in any law, or in any contract, custom or usage, or in any judgment, decree or order of court, a person in possession of immoveable property in any area in the State to which the Malabar Tenancy Act, 1929, extended, whether as mortgagee or otherwise, shall be deemed to be a tenant, if— (a) the property in his possession consists of agricultural land; and (b) he or any of his predecessors-in-interest was holding the property as a tenant on or after the first day of December, 1930. Explanation.—For the purposes of this clause, 'tenant' means a tenant as defined in the Malabar Tenancy Act, 1929, as in force on the 1st day of November, 1956; and (c) the tenancy was terminated after the 1st day of December, 1930 and before the commencement of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 (1 of 1964), but his predecessors-in-interest or himself continued in possession of the property, without interruption, after the date of such termination till the commencement of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 (1 of 1964). 2C. Certain persons occupying land honestly believing to be tenants, to be deemed tenants.—Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in any law, or in any contract, custom or usage, or in any judgment, decree or order of court, any person who on the 11th day of April, 1957, was continuously in occupation of the land of another situated in Malabar, for not less than two years, honestly believing himself to be a tenant and continued to be in occupation of such land at the commencement of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 (1 of 1964), shall be deemed to be a tenant. Explanation.—Notwithstanding anything contained in the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, where a person has been continuously in occupation of any such land for the said period, it shall be presumed, until the contrary is proved, that he has been in such occupation honestly believing himself to be a tenant. 2D. Certain persons who were in occupation for not less than twenty years to be deemed tenants.—Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in any law, or in any contract, custom or usage or in any judgment, decree or order of court, any person who occupied any land believing it to be the property of Government, but which has subsequently been declared to be the property of the other person by any judgment, decree or order of court, and was continuously in occupation of the land for a period of not less than twenty years preceding the date of publication of the Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Bill, 1968, in the Gazette shall be deemed to be a tenant. 2E. Certain persons occupying lands believing to be tenants to be deemed tenants.—Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in any law, or in any judgment, decree or order of court, any person who on the 11th day of April 1957 was continuously in occupation of the land of another for not less than two years on the basis of a registered lease deed and continued to be in occupation of such land on the date of publication of the Kerala Land Reforms (Amendment) Act, 1968, in the Gazette shall be deemed to be a tenant, notwithstanding that the tenancy was created by a person not competent to do so. 2F. Certain other persons to be deemed tenants.—Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in any law, or in any contract, custom or usage, or in any judgment, decree or order of court, the following classes of persons shall be deemed to be tenants:— (i) a punam or kumri cultivator; (ii) a licensee, (iii) a varamdar, (iv) a vechukapukthidar, and (v) a person holding land situate in any part of the Taluk of Hosdurg in Kasaragod to which the Malabar Tenancy Act, 1882, did not extend, as a usufructuary mortgagee in the transfer of Property Act, 1882 (Central Act 4 of 1882), but not being a usufructuary mortgage as defined in the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (Central Act 4 of 1882). 2G. title: The Kerala Stay Of Eviction Proceedings Act, 1999
purpose: To stay eviction proceedings and to provide for the regulation of certain relationships between landlords and tenants.
scope: Applies to all eviction proceedings concerning land and buildings in the State of Kerala, and to landlords and tenants within the State.

key_definitions.landlord: Includes a person who, for the time being, is entitled to receive rent in respect of any land or building, whether on his own behalf or on behalf of any other person, or who would be so entitled if the land or building were let to a tenant.
key_definitions.tenant: Includes any person by whom or on whose behalf rent is or but for a special contract would be, payable for any land or building, and also includes the surviving spouse or any son or daughter of a deceased tenant who has not become a tenant by assignment.
key_definitions.eviction proceedings: Includes any suit or proceeding for the recovery of possession of any land or building from the tenant.
