(Note: The document shows the date of commencement as 26-06-1999).
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'landlord', 'tenant', and 'eviction proceedings'.

States that notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force, no eviction proceedings shall be instituted or continued against a tenant in respect of any land or building for a period of five years from the date of commencement of this Act or for such shorter period as the Government may, by notification, specify. It also outlines conditions under which eviction proceedings can be initiated, such as non-payment of rent, breach of lease terms, or bonafide need of the landlord.

important_rules: No eviction proceedings can be filed or continued for a period of five years from the commencement of the Act, with some exceptions.
Eviction is permitted if the tenant fails to pay rent within a specified period.
Eviction is permitted if the tenant has used the land or building for a purpose other than that for which it was let.
Eviction is permitted if the landlord requires the land or building for his own bonafide use or for the use of his family members.
Eviction is permitted if the tenant has sublet the land or building without the landlord's consent.

Tenant's defense against eviction proceedings based on the provisions of the Act.

title: THE KERALA STAY OF EVICTION PROCEEDINGS ACT, 1999
purpose: To provide for the stay of eviction of certain cultivating tenants and small holders from lands purchased by them and which are subsequently found as excess land to be surrendered under the provisions of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.interpretation: Unless the context otherwise requires, words and expressions used in this Act shall have the meanings, respectively, assigned to them in the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 (1 of 1964).

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, commencement and duration
main_sections.description: (1) This Act may be called the Kerala Stay of Eviction Proceedings Act, 1999. (2) It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. (3) It shall be deemed to have come into force with effect from the 31st March, 1999 and shall cease to have effect on the expiry of two years from the date of such commencement.
Defines terms based on the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963.

(1) Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 (1 of 1964), or in any other law for the time being in force or in any judgement, decree or order of any Court or in any proceedings of the Land Tribunal, the Taluk Land Board, the State Land Board or any other authority during the period of operation of this Act, 
(a) No cultivating tenant or small holder who holds or possesses any land by way of assignment or otherwise as purchaser for consideration evidenced by registered document or otherwise and which is subsequently found as excess land to be surrendered under the provisions of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 (1 of 1964), shall be evicted from, or dispossessed of, such land, and 
(b) all proceedings for such eviction or dispossession pending before any Court, Tribunal, Board or other authority referred to above, shall stand stayed. 
(2) Notwithstanding the expiry of the Kerala Stay of Eviction Proceedings Act, 1998 (5 of 1998) anything done or any action taken, after such expiry and before the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette by any Court or the Land Tribunal, the Taluk Land Board, the State Land Board or any other authority, to evict or dispossess such cultivating tenant or small holder from such land shall be invalid. 
(3) The expiry of the duration of the Kerala Stay of Eviction Proceedings Act, 1998 shall not adversely affect any right or privilege acquired or such cultivating tenant or small holder under the said Act.

important_rules: Eviction or dispossession of cultivating tenants or small holders of excess land is stayed.
Proceedings for eviction or dispossession are stayed.
Actions taken after the expiry of the 1998 Act but before the publication of this Act to evict or dispossess are invalid.

penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through stay of proceedings and invalidation of actions taken contrary to the act.

Omits section 9 of the principal Act.

important_rules: Rule regarding disputes on cultivation land: If any person claiming to be in possession and cultivating under section 4 or claiming to be entitled to cultivate any land under section 6 or section 7, and if prevented from cultivating, the Tahsildar shall pass an order to cultivate the land. If the applicant is entitled to cultivate, they will be restored to possession. If the land is prevented from cultivation due to the cultivation of land by a person causing such prevention or obstruction, they can be punished with imprisonment up to six months or with fine up to Rs. 500 or both.

Rule on interim order of injunction: Where any court has passed an interim order of injunction without giving notice to the opposite party, and the opposite party appears to dispute the injunction or right to cultivate the land, the injunction order shall stand vacated pending final orders.

penalties: Imprisonment up to six months or with fine up to Rs. 500 or both for preventing cultivation of land.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Tahsildar
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through orders regarding cultivation rights and potential penalties for obstruction.

rights: Right to cultivate land under certain circumstances.
Right to be restored to possession of land if entitled to cultivate.
obligations: Obligation to pay rent (in some cases of homestead occupation).

key_procedures: Procedure for disputes on cultivation: A person claiming to be in possession or entitled to cultivate land can approach the Tahsildar. The Tahsildar will inquire and pass an order regarding cultivation.
Procedure for interim injunctions: If an interim injunction is granted without notice and the opposite party appears, the injunction can be vacated pending final orders.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be handled by relevant authorities like the Tahsildar.
important_notes: The amendment extends the applicability of the principal Act until the 11th day of April 1959.
Certain provisions in section 4 are not to preclude recovery of rent or installment of rent if according to custom, usage, or agreement, rent is payable and accruing after the Act came into force.

title: The Kerala Stay of Eviction Proceedings (Amendment) Act, 1960
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Stay of Eviction Proceedings Act, 1957, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: This Act applies to any person evicted or whose eviction proceedings are pending, and relates to immovable property situated in any part of the State of Kerala. Specific provisions also refer to property in the Malabar Tenancy Act, 1929, and the Madras Cultivating Tenants Protection Act, 1955.

main_sections.description: This section names the Act as 'The Kerala Stay of Eviction Proceedings (Amendment) Act, 1960' and states that it shall come into force at once.

This section amends sub-section (3) of section 1 of the Kerala Stay of Eviction Proceedings Act, 1957. It modifies the dates and references to Acts related to eviction proceedings, specifically mentioning the '11th day of April, 1960' and the '22nd day of February, 1960'.

This section amends section 2 of the principal Act. It introduces a new clause (1) which defines 'holding' in relation to immovable property situated in any part of the State, including those under the Malabar Tenancy Act, 1929, or the Madras Cultivating Tenants Protection Act, 1955. It also addresses immovable property held under a single transaction or transferred by a leasehold right.

This section inserts a new section, 4A, into the principal Act, titled 'Restoration of certain persons to possession or occupation'. It outlines conditions under which persons evicted after a certain date (22nd day of February, 1960) would be restored to their possession or occupation, subject to court decrees and liabilities.

important_rules: Eviction proceedings and orders made under the Kerala Stay of Eviction Proceedings Act, 1957, are to be dealt with based on amendments specified in this Act.
The definition of 'holding' is broadened to include various types of immovable property and land tenure systems in Kerala.
Persons evicted under certain conditions after February 22, 1960, are entitled to restoration of possession or occupation.
Restoration is subject to the value of improvements, if any, effected by the person who obtained possession, and to the date of obtaining possession and the date of the decree.
The restoration of rights is contingent upon satisfaction of all liabilities and compliance with court orders.

rights: Right to restoration of possession or occupation for certain evicted persons.
Right to have liabilities restored to the person who evicted them.
duties: Duty to comply with court orders regarding eviction and restoration.
obligations: Obligation to pay the value of improvements if any, to the person who evicted them.
Obligation to satisfy all liabilities related to the property before restoration.

key_procedures: Amendment of Section 1 of the principal Act concerning the commencement and scope of the Act.
Amendment of Section 2 of the principal Act to redefine 'holding' and its applicability to various land types and tenures.

Insertion of Section 4A to provide for the restoration of possession or occupation to persons evicted after a specified date, outlining the conditions and procedures for such restoration, including the consideration of improvements and liabilities.

Process for restoration: A person evicted after February 22, 1960, would be entitled to be restored to possession or occupation if a decree or order had been passed. This restoration is subject to fulfilling certain conditions regarding improvements and liabilities.
important_notes: The Act was enacted by the Republic of India and is based on the Eleventh Year of the Republic of India.
The amendment received the assent of the President on 9th April, 1960, and was published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 11th April, 1960.
The Act addresses provisions related to the Malabar Tenancy Act, 1929, and the Madras Cultivating Tenants Protection Act, 1955.

title: The Kerala Stay of Eviction Proceedings (Amendment) Act, 1959
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Stay of Eviction Proceedings Act, 1957.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala. The amendment pertains to eviction proceedings.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Stay of Eviction Proceedings (Amendment) Act, 1959, and that it shall come into force at once.

This section amends sub-section (3) of section 1 of the Kerala Stay of Eviction Proceedings Act, 1957 (Act 1 of 1957). It substitutes the words, figures and letters 'the 11th day of April 1959' with 'the 11th day of April 1960'.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but likely the relevant authorities under the original Act of 1957.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings related to eviction.

key_procedures: Amendment of existing legislation: The Act amends a previous Act by substituting specific dates, likely extending the period for certain provisions related to eviction proceedings.
administration: Likely the Government of Kerala or its relevant departments responsible for land and legal matters.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the President on 9th April, 1959 and was published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 10th April 1959.

title: The Kerala Stay of Eviction Proceedings (Second Amendment) Act, 1960
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Stay of Eviction Proceedings Act, 1957.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: (1) This Act may be called the Kerala Stay of Eviction Proceedings (Second Amendment) Act, 1960. (2) This Act shall have effect on and from the 11th day of October, 1960.

In sub-section (3) of section 1 of the Kerala Stay of Eviction Proceedings Act, 1957 (Act 1 of 1957), for the words, figures and letters "the 11th day of October, 1960", the words, figures and letters "the 11th day of April, 1961" shall be substituted.

important_notes: Received the assent of the President on 12th October, 1960 and published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 12th October, 1960.

title: The Kerala Stay of Eviction Proceedings Act, 1957
purpose: To provide for the temporary protection of tenants, Kudikidappukars and certain other classes of persons cultivating land by staying eviction proceedings and to regulate certain other related matters.
scope: The Act applies to tenants, Kudikidappukars, and certain other classes of persons cultivating land in Kerala. It covers lands owned by the Government, lands granted by rights created by the Administrator General, Official Trustee or Receiver, buildings rented out including houses, shops or warehouses, and lands transferred for felling timber or for planting tea, coffee, rubber or any other special crop.

key_definitions.holding: means any immovable property held under a single transaction by which a leasehold right in the property is created and possession of the property is transferred by one person in favour of another and includes Kanapattam.
key_definitions.hut: means any building which is constructed principally of wood, mud, leaves, grass or thatch.
key_definitions.Kudikidappukaran: means a Kudikidappukaran as defined in the Travancore-Cochin Prevention of Eviction of Kudikidappukars Act, 1955, and includes any person in occupation of a hut (whether constructed by him or not) in any portion of a land belonging to and in the possession of another and who has been permitted by the latter to occupy that hut, but otherwise has no interest in the land.
key_definitions.Kudiyiruppu: means a Kudiyiruppu as defined in the Travancore-Cochin Prevention of Eviction of Kudikidappukars Act, 1955, and includes a hut occupied by the Kudikidappukaran.
key_definitions.Varomdar: means a person who under the system known as Varom, Pathivaram, Pankuvam or Pankupattam, or by any other name, has agreed, whether in writing or not, with the owner or other person in lawful possession of any land to cultivate the land and share with him the produce of the land.
key_definitions.Varom agreement: means an agreement, whether in writing or not, entered into between the Varomdar and the owner or other person in lawful possession of the land for the cultivation and sharing of the produce of the land.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Kerala Stay of Eviction Proceedings Act, 1957'. It also specifies that the Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force on the 11th day of October 1957.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'holding', 'hut', 'Kudikidappukaran', 'Kudiyiruppu', 'Varomdar', and 'Varom agreement'.

Specifies that the provisions of the Act do not apply to lands owned by the Government, lands granted by rights created by the Administrator General, Official Trustee or Receiver, buildings rented out including houses, shops or warehouses, lands transferred for felling timber or for planting tea, coffee, rubber or any other special crop, or for the preparation of the same for the market.

Stipulates that notwithstanding anything to the contrary in any other law, no suit or other proceedings for the recovery of arrears of rent or for damages for use and occupation of land, or for recovery of possession of land, shall be instituted or continued except with the previous sanction of the Government or such other officer as may be authorised by the Government in this behalf.

Provides that notwithstanding anything to the contrary in any other law, no suit or other proceedings for eviction of a Kudikidappukaran from his Kudiyiruppu or for the recovery of arrears of rent in respect of, or for damages for use and occupation of, the Kudiyiruppu shall lie in any Court and all such proceedings in execution of decrees or orders and all other proceedings pending in the Courts at such commencement for such eviction or recovery of arrears of such rent or damages shall be stayed.

main_sections.section_title: Varomdar's right to continue to cultivate lands
main_sections.description: Grants certain rights to Varomdars to continue cultivating lands under specific conditions, even if they do not have a formal agreement or if agricultural operations have not started yet.

main_sections.section_title: Continuance of Sambalapattam or Coolypattom arrangements
main_sections.description: Provides for the continuance of Sambalapattam or Coolypattom arrangements and states that notwithstanding anything to the contrary in any other law, no landlord shall be entitled to evict a tenant from any land under such arrangement or to terminate the same or to recover possession thereof or to sue for arrears of rent or damages in respect thereof, without the previous sanction of the Government.

States that the period of limitation prescribed for the institution of suits or proceedings prohibited or stayed under this Act, the time during which such suits or proceedings are prohibited or stayed shall be excluded.
Provides for the restoration of rights to persons who have been deprived of their rights as tenants or Kudiyiruppukars, subject to summary enquiry by the Court.
Repeals 'The Holdings (Stay of Execution Proceedings) Act, 1950' and 'The Kerala Stay of Eviction Proceedings Ordinance, 1957'.

important_rules: Eviction proceedings against tenants and Kudikidappukars are stayed.
Suits or proceedings for recovery of arrears of rent or damages for use and occupation of land cannot be instituted or continued without Government sanction.
Varomdars have the right to continue cultivating lands under certain conditions.
Sambalapattam and Coolypattom arrangements continue.
Periods of limitation are extended by the duration of the stay.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government or authorised officer
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through courts and by requiring sanction for institution or continuation of certain proceedings.

rights: Right of tenants and Kudikidappukars to stay of eviction.
Right of Varomdar to continue cultivation.
Right to restoration of rights previously deprived.

key_procedures: To obtain sanction from the Government or authorized officer before instituting or continuing eviction proceedings or recovery of arrears/damages.
Courts shall stay all proceedings in execution of decrees or orders and all other proceedings pending at the commencement of the Act for eviction or recovery of arrears/damages.
Summary enquiry by the Court for restoration of rights.
administration: The Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act does not apply to lands owned by the Government.
The Act does not apply to buildings rented out including houses, shops or warehouses.
The Act does not apply to lands transferred for felling timber or for planting tea, coffee, rubber or any other special crop, or for the preparation of the same for the market.

title: The Kerala Surcharge on Taxes (Amendment) Act, 1970
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Surcharge on Taxes Act, 1957.
scope: Applies to Kerala and individuals or companies subject to the Kerala Surcharge on Taxes Act, 1957.

key_definitions.company: Shall have the same meaning as in the Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Surcharge on Taxes (Amendment) Act, 1970, and that Section 2 shall come into force on April 1, 1970, and the remaining provisions of this Act shall come into force at once.
Amends Section 2 of the Kerala Surcharge on Taxes Act, 1957, by inserting the words "(other than a company)" after "any person" and adding an explanation for the term "company".

Repeals the Kerala Surcharge on Taxes (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1970 (16 of 1970). It also includes a saving clause stating that anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the Kerala Surcharge on Taxes Act, 1957, as amended by the said Ordinance, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act as amended by this Act.

important_notes: The Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 383, dated 30th November 1970.

title: THE KERALA SURCHARGE ON TAXES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2000
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Surcharge on Taxes Act, 1957, for the purpose hereinafter appearing. Specifically, to amend Section 3 of the Principal Act concerning the surcharge on tax payable under Section 5 of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, in relation to foreign liquor.
scope: Applies to taxes under Section 5 of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, specifically concerning surcharge on foreign liquor. The amendment impacts dealers in foreign liquor.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Surcharge on Taxes (Amendment) Act, 2000. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of January, 2000.

Amends Section 3 of the Kerala Surcharge on Taxes Act, 1957 (11 of 1957). It substitutes a sub-section stating that the tax payable under sub-section (1) of Section 5 of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, by a dealer in foreign liquor shall be increased by a surcharge at the rate of ten per cent, and the provisions of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, shall apply in relation to the said surcharge as they apply in relation to the tax payable under the said Act.

Repeals the Kerala Taxation Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1999 (7 of 1999), except section 4 thereof. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act, as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Rule: Dealers in foreign liquor shall pay a surcharge at the rate of ten per cent on the tax payable under sub-section (1) of section 5 of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.
Rule: Provisions of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, will apply to this surcharge as they apply to the tax.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be the authorities under the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application of the provisions of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.

duties: Duty: Dealers in foreign liquor have a duty to pay the increased surcharge on tax.
Duty: The provisions of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, will apply in relation to the surcharge.
obligations: Obligation: To comply with the surcharge provisions as amended by this Act.

key_procedures: Procedure: Dealers in foreign liquor must calculate and pay a surcharge of ten per cent on the tax levied under Section 5(1) of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.
Procedure: The surcharge payment is subject to the same rules and regulations as the tax itself, as per the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.
administration: The administration is implied to be under the purview of the tax authorities responsible for implementing the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on January 1, 2000.
The Kerala Taxation Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1999 (7 of 1999) is repealed, except for section 4.
Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are considered valid under the amended Act.

title: The Kerala Surcharge on Taxes (Amendment) Act, 1968
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Surcharge on Taxes Act, 1957, for the purpose indicated.
scope: The Act applies to the Kerala Surcharge on Taxes Act, 1957. Specifically, it amends section 3 of the principal Act.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Surcharge on Taxes (Amendment) Act, 1968, and it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of September, 1967.

This section amends section 3 of the Kerala Surcharge on Taxes Act, 1957 (11 of 1957). In the proviso to sub-section (1), the words 'two per centum' in both places where they occur, are to be substituted with the words 'three per centum'.

important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary, No. 64 dated 15th March, 1968.

title: The Kerala Surcharge on Taxes (Amendment and Validation) Act, 1966
purpose: To amend the Kerala Surcharge on Taxes Act, 1957 and to validate the levy and collection of surcharge on profession tax in certain cases.
scope: Applies to the levy and collection of surcharge on profession tax. The amendment pertains to the Kerala Surcharge on Taxes Act, 1957, and specifically addresses the application of surcharge, its limits, and validation of past levies.

main_sections.description: This section names the Act as 'The Kerala Surcharge on Taxes (Amendment and Validation) Act, 1966' and states that it came into force on September 1, 1957, along with the remaining provisions of the Kerala Surcharge on Taxes Act, 1957.

Amends section 2 of the Kerala Surcharge on Taxes Act, 1957, by inserting words to clarify that the surcharge applies to the levy and collection of profession tax. It also specifies that the words 'apply in relation to the levy and collection of the said surcharge' should be interpreted as 'apply in relation to the income-tax or super-tax payable under the said Act'.

Amends section 3 of the principal Act. It makes specific changes to sub-section (1) by replacing references to other taxation acts with 'the Travancore-Cochin General Sales Tax Act, 1125 or the Madras General Sales Tax Act, 1939'.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 4.
main_sections.description: Replaces section 4 of the principal Act. The new section deals with the levy of surcharge on profession tax. It specifies that the profession tax payable by a person or company whose half-yearly income is not less than one thousand and five hundred rupees, to respective local authorities, will be increased by a surcharge. This section also lists various municipal acts and district boards acts to which this provision applies. It further clarifies that no surcharge shall be levied under this section when profession tax payable by a person or company to any of the said local authorities is two hundred and fifty rupees or more per annum. It also covers cases where the profession tax payable by a person or company to any of the said local authorities is less than two hundred and fifty rupees per annum, with a surcharge limit. The section also validates the levy and collection of surcharge on profession tax under the purported exercise of the powers conferred by section 4 of the principal Act.

This section validates anything done or omitted to be done in any judgment, decree, or order by any court, where any surcharge has been levied or collected before the date of publication of this Act, or in any case where the aggregate amount of such surcharge and the profession tax referred to in section 4 is payable by a person or a company does not exceed the limit of two hundred and fifty rupees per annum, then such surcharge shall be deemed to have been validly levied or collected in accordance with law. It also specifies that in any case where the aggregate amount of such surcharge and profession tax exceeds the limit of two hundred and fifty rupees per annum, then that portion of the surcharge, if any, which together with such profession tax does not exceed the said limit, shall be deemed to have been validly levied or collected in accordance with law, as if such levy or collection had been made under section 4 of the principal Act as substituted by this Act. It further states that no suit or other proceeding shall be maintained or continued in any court for the refund of surcharge referred to in clause (i) or such portion of the surcharge as is referred to in clause (ii), as the case may be, which has already been paid. It also states that no court shall enforce any decree or order in so far as it relates to the refund of such surcharge or portion, as the case may be, which has already been paid. Finally, it clarifies that for the removal of doubts, it is declared that nothing in sub-section (1) shall be construed as preventing any person from claiming any refund of any surcharge paid by him in excess of the amount due from him under section 4 of the principal Act as substituted by this Act.

important_rules: Profession tax payable by a person or company to local authorities will be increased by a surcharge if their half-yearly income is not less than one thousand and five hundred rupees.

The surcharge limit for profession tax is two hundred and fifty rupees per annum. Any amount collected or levied in excess of this limit, if it does not exceed the total of the surcharge and the profession tax, is considered valid.
No refund of surcharge can be claimed or enforced by any court if it has already been paid, or if it relates to amounts deemed validly levied or collected under the Act.

penalties: Any dealer who collects the surcharge payable under sub-section (1) of section 4 shall be punishable with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees and no court below the rank of a Magistrate of the first class shall try any such offence.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Local authorities are empowered to collect surcharge on profession tax. The Act also implies enforcement by courts for matters related to levy, collection, and refunds.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through levy and collection of surcharge by local authorities, and through court proceedings for disputes or enforcement of the Act's provisions.

rights: The right to levy and collect surcharge on profession tax.
The right to claim refund of surcharge under specific conditions (though largely restricted by validation clauses).
duties: Duty to pay surcharge on profession tax as prescribed by the Act.
Duty of dealers to collect and remit the surcharge payable.
Duty to comply with court orders regarding surcharge.
obligations: Obligation to ensure that the levy and collection of surcharge are in accordance with the Act, even retrospectively.
Obligation for dealers to follow the specified penalty provisions if they contravene the surcharge collection rules.

key_procedures: Amendment of the Kerala Surcharge on Taxes Act, 1957, to include provisions for surcharge on profession tax.
Validation of past levies and collections of surcharge on profession tax, even if inconsistent with the original Act, provided they fall within specified limits.
Procedure for levying surcharge on profession tax by local authorities based on income thresholds.
Procedure for handling disputes and claims related to surcharge refunds, with limitations imposed by the validation section.
administration: The administration of this Act likely falls under the purview of the Kerala State Legislature (Delegation of Powers) Act, 1965, and the respective local authorities responsible for collecting profession tax.
important_notes: The Act specifically validates the levy and collection of surcharge on profession tax in certain cases, extending back to September 1, 1957.
The definition of 'surcharge' and its application are clarified to include profession tax.
A penalty is prescribed for dealers who collect surcharge under sub-section (1) of section 4, with limitations on court jurisdiction.
The validation section is extensive, aiming to regularize any past levies or collections that might have been questionable under the original Act, provided they met certain criteria.
A specific threshold for half-yearly income (Rs. 1,500) and an annual surcharge limit (Rs. 250) are mentioned in relation to profession tax.

title: The Kerala Surcharge on Taxes (Amendment) Act, 1976
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Surcharge on Taxes Act, 1957, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and the taxes governed by the Kerala Surcharge on Taxes Act, 1957.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Surcharge on Taxes (Amendment) Act, 1976. Clause (b) of section 3 shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of July 1975 and the remaining provisions of this Act shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1976.

In section 2 of the Kerala Surcharge on Taxes Act, 1957 (11 of 1957), the words 'income tax or super tax', in both the places where they occur, the words 'agricultural income tax' shall be substituted. Also, the words 'five per centum', the words 'ten per centum' shall be substituted.

Amends sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Principal Act. The 'tax payable under the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, shall, in the case of a dealer whose turnover-(a) is not less than one lakh rupees but does not exceed ten lakhs rupees in a year, be increased by a surcharge at the rate of five per centum, and (b) exceeds ten lakhs rupees in a year, be increased by a surcharge at the rate of eight per centum.' It also amends the proviso regarding 'three per centum' to 'four per centum'.
Sections 4 and 5 of the principal Act shall be omitted.

The Kerala Surcharge on Taxes (Amendment) Ordinance, 1976 (6 of 1976) is hereby repealed. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or action taken under the Principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: The surcharge on tax payable under the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, is increased for dealers based on their turnover.
For turnover not less than one lakh rupees but not exceeding ten lakhs rupees, the increase is five per centum.
For turnover exceeding ten lakhs rupees, the increase is eight per centum.
The provisions of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, shall apply in relation to the said surcharge.
The wording regarding 'three per centum' is substituted with 'four per centum' in the proviso.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text.

obligations: Dealers are obligated to pay the increased surcharge on their turnover as per the specified rates.

administration: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text, likely the State Tax Department of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 19th day of November, 1976 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 606, dated 20th November, 1976.
Certain provisions of the Act have retrospective effect.

title: THE KERALA SURCHARGE ON TAXES ACT, 1957
purpose: An Act to provide for levy of surcharges on certain taxes.
scope: Extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Surcharge on Taxes Act, 1957. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and comes into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

main_sections.section_title: Levy of surcharge on agricultural income-tax
main_sections.description: Specifies that the income-tax or super-tax payable by any person assessed to such tax under the Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950, shall be increased by a surcharge at the rate of five per centum of the tax payable each year, and these provisions shall apply to the levy and collection of the said surcharge.

main_sections.section_title: Levy of surcharge on sales and purchase taxes
main_sections.description: Details the levy of surcharge on sales and purchase taxes. For taxes payable under the Travancore-Cochin General Sales Tax Act, 1125, or the Madras General Sales Tax Act, 1939, by a dealer whose turnover exceeds thirty thousand rupees in a year, a surcharge at the rate of two and a half per centum of the tax payable shall be levied. This surcharge is to be levied, collected, and the provisions of the said Acts shall apply. It also specifies that where in respect of declared goods, the surcharge payable under the said Acts together with the surcharge payable under this Act exceeds two per centum of the sale or purchase price, the rate of surcharge on such goods shall be reduced to such an extent that the tax and the surcharge together shall not exceed two per centum of the sale or purchase price. This section also includes provisions for the levy of surcharge on profession tax.

main_sections.section_title: Levy of surcharge on profession tax
main_sections.description: States that the profession tax or tax on companies payable by a person or company whose half-yearly income is not less than one thousand and five hundred rupees to the respective local authorities under the Travancore-Cittium Municipal Act, the Travancore District Municipalities Act, 1116, the Cochin Municipal Act, XVIII of 1113, the Madras District Municipalities Act, 1920, the Travancore-Cochin Panchayats Act, 1950, or the Madras Village Panchayats Act, 1950, shall be increased by a surcharge for the purpose of the Government. The rate of five per centum of the profession tax or tax on companies payable and the local authorities concerned shall levy and collect the said surcharge along with the profession tax or the tax on companies in the same manner as if it were a profession tax or a tax on companies, and the provisions of law governing the levy and collection of such taxes shall in all respects apply therefor.

main_sections.section_title: Local authority to make over the surcharge collected to Government
main_sections.description: Mandates that the local authority concerned shall make over to the Government the surcharge so collected in such manner and subject to such deductions towards the cost of collections as the Government may, from time to time, by rules prescribe.
Grants the Government the power to do anything which appears to them necessary for the purpose of removing any difficulty in relation to the provisions of this Act.
Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act. These rules will be published in the Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment to the Madras Elementary Education Act, 1920
main_sections.description: Amends the Madras Elementary Education Act, 1920. Specifically, it states that sections 32 to 40 (both inclusive) of the Madras Elementary Education Act, 1920, as in force in the Malabar district, referred to in sub-section (2) of section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, shall be omitted. Furthermore, it clarifies that as soon as may be after the commencement of this Act, the elementary education fund constituted for such local authority under the said Act shall be transferred to the Government by such local authority and the same shall vest in the Government free of all trusts, liabilities and encumbrances. Thereupon, it shall be competent for the Government to utilize the said fund in such manner as they may deem fit.

duties: Local authorities must make over collected surcharge to the Government.

key_procedures: Levy and collection of surcharges on agricultural income-tax, sales and purchase taxes, and profession tax.
Transfer of elementary education fund to the Government.
administration: Government
important_notes: The surcharge on sales and purchase taxes shall not exceed two per centum of the sale or purchase price when combined with existing taxes.

title: THE KERALA SURVEY AND BOUNDARIES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2007
purpose: To amend the Kerala Survey and Boundaries Act, 1961, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Survey and Boundaries (Amendment) Act, 2007. Specifies that Sections 2 and 3 of this Act shall be deemed to have come into force on the 30th day of July, 2007, and the remaining sections shall be deemed to have come into force on the 6th day of January, 2006.

Amends section 8 of the Kerala Survey and Boundaries Act, 1961 (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act). It provides that for the purpose of speedy survey of vast areas of land, the Government may by notification in the official Gazette, authorise the concerned survey officer to conduct the survey through aerial survey or other suitable modern methods utilizing the services of such expert agencies, as may be specified by the Government in the said notification.
Amends section 12 of the principal Act, stating that for the words "three months" occurring in both the places, the words "one month" shall be substituted.

Amends section 13 of the principal Act, stating that for the words "is modified by a decree of a civil court", the words, figures and letter "is modified by an order of the Collector under section 13A or is modified by a decree of a civil court" shall be substituted.

Inserts a new section 13A titled "Power of revision by the Collector". This section grants the Collector the power to revise any order made by any person or authority concerning the determination of any boundary, provided they have received an application and examined the record. The Collector's revised order is final. It also states that any boundary modified or revised by the Collector under this section shall be published in the Gazette and on the notice board of the Village Office.

Amends section 14 of the principal Act. It specifies that after the words and figures "or section 11", the words, brackets, figures and letter "or aggrieved by an order passed by the Collector under sub-section (1) of section 13A" shall be inserted. It also states that after the words and figures "under section 13", the words, brackets, figures and letter "or sub-section (2) of section 13A, as the case may be," shall be inserted.

Repeals the Kerala Survey and Boundaries (Amendment) Ordinance, 2007. It includes a saving clause stating that the repeal shall not affect any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance.

The section also outlines procedures for notice of decisions regarding boundaries affecting land in villages and Taluks, and in offices of Panchayats or Municipal Councils.

In section 9 of the principal Act, the following sub-section shall be substituted: '(2) Notice of every decision of the Survey Officer under sub-section (1) shall be published— (a) in the Gazette or in two daily newspapers which, in the opinion of the Survey Officer, have wide circulation in the locality in which the lands, the boundaries of which may be affected by the decision, are situated; (b) in the offices of the Village and the Taluk in which such land are situated; and (c) in the office of the Panchayat or the Municipal Council or Municipal Corporation as the case may be, within whose jurisdiction such lands are situated.'

Amends section 6 of the Kerala Tax on Luxuries Act, 1976 by inserting new sub-sections (4), (5), and (6). These sub-sections deal with the completion of assessments, re-assessment of escaped assessment, and rectification of mistakes. They also specify procedures for giving notice and opportunities for being heard to the proprietor before enhancing an assessment or penalty.

important_rules: Any final assessment under section 6 shall be completed within a period of four years from the expiry of the year to which the assessment relates.

Where the whole or any part of the business of a hotel/house boat has escaped assessment to tax, the assessing authority may, within a period of five years from the expiry of the year to which the tax relates, determine the turnover and assess the tax payable after giving the proprietor a reasonable opportunity of being heard.
Where rectification has the effect of enhancing an assessment or penalty, the assessing authority shall make a refund to the person entitled thereto.

Where rectification has the effect of reducing an assessment or penalty, the assessing authority shall give the proprietor or other person a revised notice of assessment and thereupon the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder shall apply as if such notice had been given in the first instance.

Provided that before the proceedings against the promoter is so continued the previous proceedings or any part thereof be re-opened or that he may be heard before any order of assessment is passed against him.

(1) There shall be levied and collected a tax on paper lotteries at the following rates, namely:— (a) Ten lakh rupees for every bumper draw; and (b) Two lakh fifty thousand rupees in respect of any other draw; (2) Tax levied under sub-section (1) shall be paid by each promoter. (3) Where the Government of India or a Government of a State or Union Territory or a Country appoints more than one promoter in the State, one such promoter duly authorized by the respective Government or Country shall pay tax levied under sub-section (1).

(1) Every promoter selling lottery tickets shall get himself registered under this Act in such manner and on payment of such fees and security within such period as may be prescribed: Provided that a person ordinarily selling lottery tickets in retail shall not be liable to get himself registered. (2) The registration may be renewed from year to year on payment of the prescribed fees and security, until it is cancelled. (3) Unless the registration is cancelled or renewed, at the expiry of the period of registration, the security may be refunded or released to the promoter after adjusting any or all amount due from him, under this Act.

(1) Notwithstanding anything contained in section 10, every promoter liable to get himself registered under this Act shall submit a return to the Assistant Commissioner for such period, within such period and in such manner containing such particulars as may be prescribed. (2) Before any promoter submits tax in advance as provided under section 10, he shall furnish the full amount of tax payable by him under section 6 and shall furnish along with the return satisfactory proof of the payment of such tax, and after the final assessment is made, the amount of tax so paid shall be deemed to have been paid towards the tax finally assessed. (3) If the Assistant Commissioner is satisfied that any return submitted under sub-section (1) is correct and complete, he shall assess the promoter on the basis thereof. (4) If no return is submitted by the promoter under sub-section (1) before the period prescribed or if the Assistant Commissioner is satisfied that the return submitted to him is incorrect or incomplete, he shall assess the promoter to the best of his judgment recording the reasons for such assessment: Provided that before taking action under this sub-section the promoter shall be given reasonable opportunity of being heard. (5) While making any assessment under sub-section (4), the Assistant Commissioner may also direct the promoter to pay in addition to the tax assessed a penalty equal to two times of the amount of tax due that was not disclosed by the promoter in his return or in the case of failure to submit a return two times of the tax assessed.

(1) If the Assistant Commissioner has reasons to believe that any draw has escaped assessment to tax or has been assessed at a rate lower than the rate at which it is assessable under this Act, the Assistant Commissioner may, notwithstanding the fact that the assessment in respect of such draw was already before him at the time of assessment or re-assessment, but subject to the provisions of sub-section (3), at any time within a period of four years from the expiry of the period to which the tax relates, proceed to assess or re-assess to the best of his judgment the tax payable by the promoter in respect of such draw after issuing a notice to the promoter and after making such enquiry as he may consider necessary. (2) In making an assessment under sub-section (1) the Assistant Commissioner may, if he is satisfied that the escapement from assessment is due to willful non-disclosure of the draw by the promoter, direct him to pay in addition to the tax assessed under sub-section (1) a penalty equal to two times of the tax so assessed. Provided that no penalty under this sub-section shall be directed to be paid unless the promoter has been given a reasonable opportunity of being heard. Provided further that if the promoter, makes payment of the defaulted tax with interest the Assistant Commissioner, on application, may register the promoter or such person on payment of registration/renewal fees and security at the prescribed rate.

(1) Subject to such rules as may be prescribed, every promoter shall submit on the 1st day of every month, if the first day being a holiday, on the immediate next working day to the Assistant Commissioner a statement containing such particulars, as may be prescribed relating to the draws to be conducted during the month commencing from the next succeeding month and shall pay in advance the full amount of tax payable by him under this Act, in respect of the draws shown in the statement and the amount so payable shall for the purpose of section 12, be deemed to be an amount due under this Act from such promoter. (2) If default is committed in the payment of tax for any month, whether a statement as required under sub-section (1) is filed or not, or if the amount of tax paid is less than the amount of tax payable for any month, the promoter defaulting payment of tax or making short payment of tax shall, in addition to the tax, pay interest calculated at the rate of two per cent per month from the date of such default or short payment to the date of payment of such tax. (3) If no such statement is submitted by a promoter under sub-section (1) before the date specify or if the statement submitted by him appears to the Assistant Commissioner to be incorrect or incomplete, the Assistant Commissioner may assess the promoter provisionally for that month to the best of his judgment, recording the reasons for such assessment, and proceed to demand and collect the tax forthwith on the basis of such assessment, the above said tax shall immediately be adjusted towards the security amount paid under sub-section (1) of section 7. (4) Without prejudice to the actions contemplated under sub-sections (2) and (3) above, the Assistant Commissioner shall cancel the registration of the promoter granted under this Act and on such cancellation of registration, the promoter shall not be entitled to sell lottery tickets in the State.

(1) The tax or any other amount due under this Act shall be paid in specified manner and within the fixed time, as may be prescribed. (2) If default is made in making payment in accordance with sub-section (1),— (i) the whole of the amount outstanding on the date of default shall become immediately due and shall be a charge on the property of the promoter including any person appointed for selling lottery tickets jointly and severely, liable to pay tax under this Act, (ii) the promoter liable to pay the tax or any other amount due under this Act shall pay an interest equal to two per cent of the amount of tax or any other amount remaining unpaid for each month after the expiry of the time specified under sub-section (1). Explanation.—For the purposes of clause (ii), the interest payable for a part of a month shall be proportionately determined. (3) Any amount, which remains unpaid under this Act after the due date of payment, shall be recoverable from a promoter including any person appointed for selling lottery tickets jointly and severely in the manner specified under this Act. (4) Any tax due or assessed or any other amount due under this Act from a promoter or any other person, may without prejudice to any other mode of collection, be recovered, as if it were an arrear of land revenue.

main_sections.section_title: Recovery of tax, penalty or any other amount, from certain other persons
main_sections.description: (1) The Assistant Commissioner may at any time or from time to time, by notice in writing, a copy of which shall be forwarded to the promoter at his last address known to the Assistant Commissioner, require any person from whom money is due or may become due to the promoter or other person who holds or any subsequently hold money for or on account of the promoter or other person to pay to the Assistant Commissioner, either forthwith or within the time specified in the notice (but not later than the time when such money becomes due to the promoter or is tendered by him to the promoter or the person in default), all or any part of such money or all or any part of any debt owing to the promoter or the person in default which the Assistant Commissioner by notice demands. Provided that a notice shall not be deemed to be insufficient for the purposes of this sub-section by reason of any error or defect in it or in the service of it unless the Assistant Commissioner is satisfied that it is a material, and no person shall be deemed to be in default by reason of failure to comply with a notice under this sub-section unless it is proved that the notice was duly served on him and that the money specified in the notice was due to the promoter or the person in default at the time of the notice or thereafter. (2) Any person making any payment in compliance with a notice under sub-section (1) shall be deemed to have made the payment under the authority of the promoter or other person and the receipt of the Assistant Commissioner shall constitute a good and sufficient discharge of the liability of such person to the extent of the amount referred to in the receipt. (3) Any person discharging any liability to the promoter or other person after receipt of the notice referred to in this section shall be personally liable to the Assistant Commissioner to the extent of the liability of the promoter due under this Act, whichever is less. (4) Where any person to whom a notice under this section is sent, proves to the satisfaction of the Assistant Commissioner issuing such notice, that the sum demanded or any part thereof is not due and payable by him to the promoter or that he does not hold any money for or on account of the promoter, then nothing contained in this section shall be deemed to require such person to pay the sum demanded or any part thereof, to the Assistant Commissioner. (5) Any amount which a person is required to pay to the Assistant Commissioner or for which he is personally liable to the Assistant Commissioner under this section, if it remains unpaid, shall be a charge on the properties of the said promoter and may be recovered as if it were an arrear of land revenue. (6) For the purpose of this section, the amount due to a promoter or other person or any person shall be computed after taking into account such claims, if any, as may have fallen due for payment by such promoter or other person to such person and as may be lawfully subsisting.

main_sections.section_title: Tax payable on transfer of business, assessment of legal representatives, etc
main_sections.description: (1) When the ownership of the business of a promoter other than a Government is transferred, the transfer or and the transferee shall jointly and severally be liable to pay any tax or penalty or any other amount remaining unpaid at the date of transfer or that may become payable in respect of such business of transfer but relating to the periods up to the date of transfer and for the purpose of recovery of removal from the transferee, such transferee shall be deemed to be the promoter liable to pay the tax or penalty or other amount due under this Act.

important_rules: Promoters must submit a tax return to the Assistant Commissioner by the 1st of each month, or the next working day if the 1st is a holiday.
Promoters must pay the full amount of tax payable in advance for the draws scheduled for the following month.
If tax payment is defaulted or short-paid, interest at 2% per month will be charged from the date of default or short payment.
The State Government may issue orders, instructions, and directions for the administration of the Act.
Promoters selling lottery tickets must be registered under the Act, unless they are individuals selling retail.
Registration renewal is from year to year on payment of prescribed fees and security.

penalties: Penalty equal to two times the amount of tax due that was not disclosed in the return, or two times the assessed tax in case of failure to submit a return (Section 8(5)).
Penalty equal to two times the tax assessed if escapement from assessment is due to willful non-disclosure of the draw by the promoter (Section 9(2)).
Interest at 2% per month on defaulted or short-paid tax (Section 10(2)).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Assistant Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, and Commissioner of Commercial Taxes.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment and reassessment of tax, levying penalties and interest, recovery of unpaid tax as arrears of land revenue, and cancellation of promoter registration.

rights: Promoters have the right to be heard before action is taken under certain penalty provisions.
Promoters have the right to have their security refunded or released upon expiry of registration period, after adjustments.
A person receiving a notice to pay money due to a promoter can prove that the sum demanded is not due or they do not hold the money to be exempt from compliance.
duties: Promoters have a duty to register under the Act.
Promoters have a duty to submit returns and pay tax in advance.
Promoters have a duty to comply with orders, instructions, and directions issued by the authorities.
Officers and persons employed in the execution of the Act must observe and follow administrative instructions from the Commissioner.
obligations: Promoters have an obligation to pay the levied tax on paper lotteries.
Promoters are obligated to pay interest on defaulted or short-paid tax.

key_procedures: Registration of Promoters: Promoters must apply for registration, pay fees and security, and obtain registration.
Submission of Returns: Promoters must submit monthly returns detailing upcoming draws and pay advance tax.
Assessment: The Assistant Commissioner will assess tax based on submitted returns or by best judgment if returns are incorrect or missing.
Recovery of Tax: Unpaid tax can be recovered through various means, including as arrears of land revenue.
administration: Commercial Taxes Department, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act defines 'Paper Lottery' as any lottery other than an on-line lottery.
A person ordinarily selling lottery tickets in retail is not liable to get registered.
The State Government can issue orders and directions for the administration of the Act, but these cannot interfere with the discretion of Appellate Authorities.
The tax rates are specific amounts for 'bumper draws' and 'other draws'.
If a promoter's business is transferred, both the transferor and transferee are liable for unpaid tax and penalties.

title: The Kerala Tax on Employment (Amendment) Act, 1977
purpose: To amend The Kerala Tax on Employment Act, 1976, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to every employer and employee in Kerala, as governed by The Kerala Tax on Employment Act, 1976. Specifically addresses employment in any establishment.

key_definitions.employer: Means the person who is responsible for the disbursement of such salary or wages and includes the head of office of an establishment as well as the manager or agent of the employer.
key_definitions.employee: Impliedly, any person earning a salary or wages under an employer.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called The Kerala Tax on Employment (Amendment) Act, 1977, and it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 13th day of June, 1977.

Amends Section 2 of the principal Act by inserting a clause that defines 'employer' to include a person responsible for disbursement of salary or wages and the head of an establishment, manager, or agent. It also clarifies that the employer's liability to deduct and pay tax on employment applies to any person earning a salary or wages. Such tax shall be deducted by the employer from the employee's salary or wages if paid by the employer, and if the employer does not deduct it, they are liable to pay it. If the employer fails to deduct or pay the tax, they are directly liable to pay the tax on employment.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new sections for sections 5 to 12
main_sections.description: Substitutes new sections for sections 5 to 12 of the principal Act. This includes sections on employer's liability, registration and enrolment, payment of tax, assessment of employers, and penalties for non-payment of tax.
Amends section 13 of the Principal Act, likely relating to the notice of demand or service of notice.
Amends section 16 of the principal Act, specifically sub-section (3), concerning rectification of enhancing or reducing an assessment and its implications for the employer.

Amends section 20 of the principal Act. It specifies that an employer or other person who, without sufficient cause, fails to comply with any of the provisions of this Act, or rules framed thereunder, and is convicted before a Magistrate, shall be punishable with a fine not exceeding five thousand rupees, and with a continuing offense, a fine not exceeding fifty rupees per day during the period of the continuance of the offense.
Amends section 29 of the principal Act, likely concerning the procedure for deduction and remittance of tax and the form of certificates.

Repeals The Kerala Tax on Employment (Amendment) Ordinance, 1977 (13 of 1977). It also provides a saving clause, stating that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Employers are liable to deduct and pay tax on employment from the salary or wages of their employees.
Employers must obtain a certificate of registration or enrolment for any person liable to pay tax on employment under section 5.

Every employer must obtain a certificate of registration or enrolment within thirty days of the commencement of the Kerala Tax on Employment Act, 1977, or within thirty days from the date on which they become an employer or the case may be, from the date on which he engages in any profession, art, calling or business.
Employers are required to file returns and pay the tax due. Assessments will be made by the assessing authority.
Penalties apply for failure to deduct or pay tax, failure to register, or failure to file returns.

penalties: Penalty for non-payment of tax on employment: A fine not exceeding fifty per cent of the amount of tax due from him.
Penalty for failure to comply with provisions (conviction before a Magistrate): Fine not exceeding five thousand rupees, and a continuing fine not exceeding fifty rupees per day.
Penalty for failure to obtain registration or enrolment: A penalty not exceeding twenty rupees for each day of delay.
Penalty for failure to file return without sufficient cause: Fine not exceeding five hundred rupees and a continuing fine not exceeding fifty rupees per day.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The assessing authority.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment, demand notices, penalties, and prosecution before a Magistrate.

rights: Employees have the right to have tax deducted and paid by their employer.
Employers have the right to appeal or seek rectification of assessments.
duties: Duty of employer to deduct and pay tax on employment.
Duty of employer to obtain registration and enrolment.
Duty to apply for a certificate of registration or enrolment.
Duty to file returns and pay tax.
Duty to furnish information to the assessing authority.
obligations: Obligation to pay tax on employment.
Obligation to comply with notices and directions from the assessing authority.

key_procedures: Procedure for deduction and remittance of tax by employers.
Procedure for obtaining registration and enrolment.
Procedure for filing returns by employers.
Procedure for assessment of tax by the assessing authority.
Procedure for rectifying assessments.
Procedure for imposing penalties.
Procedure for recovery of tax.
administration: The assessing authority appointed under the Act.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on the 13th day of June, 1977.
The Kerala Tax on Employment (Amendment) Ordinance, 1977, is repealed.
Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are deemed to have been taken under this Act.

title: THE KERALA TAX ON EMPLOYMENT ACT, 1976
purpose: To provide for the levy of a tax on employment.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Kerala and comes into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

key_definitions.appellate authority: Means an appellate authority appointed under section 3.
key_definitions.company: Means a company as defined in section 3 of the Companies Act, 1956 (Central Act 1 of 1956), and includes a foreign company within the meaning of section 591 of that Act and a co-operative society registered or deemed to be registered under the law relating to co-operative societies for the time being in force, whether its principal place of business is situated in the State or not.
key_definitions.local authority: Means a municipal corporation or a municipal council or a township committee or a panchayat.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.transacts business: Shall be deemed to include the doing of acts of business of whatever nature, whether isolated or not, such as soliciting, obtaining or transmitting orders or buying, making, manufacturing, exporting, importing, recovering, transmitting or otherwise dealing with goods.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as The Kerala Tax on Employment Act, 1976, defines its extent to the whole of Kerala, and specifies that commencement will be by government notification in the Gazette.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'appellate authority', 'company', 'employment', 'local authority', 'prescribed', 'State', 'transacts business', and 'year'.

Empowers the Government to appoint such officers as they think fit to be assessing authorities for the purpose of this Act and assign them local limits. Also allows appointment of appellate authorities.

States that every person who exercises a profession, art or calling or transacts business or holds any appointment, public or private, within the State, shall be liable to tax on employment at the rate specified in the Schedule.

main_sections.section_title: Requisition on employers or their representatives to furnish list
main_sections.description: The assessing authority may require an employer or head of office or club or a firm or company to furnish a list of all persons employed by them, and particulars regarding employees.
Requires persons liable to tax on employment to file a return showing their income for the half-year. If the assessing authority is not satisfied, they can issue a notice to furnish particulars.

main_sections.section_title: Return after due date and amendment of return
main_sections.description: Deals with the submission of returns after the due date and the amendment of returns.
Outlines the process of assessment, including levying tax on the person liable based on the statement or return.

main_sections.section_title: Power to assess in case of escape from assessment
main_sections.description: Grants the assessing authority the power to assess any person who has escaped assessment in any half-year within three years from the date of such assessment.
Specifies the procedure for issuing a notice of demand when tax is due in consequence of any order passed under the Act.
Details how specified amounts payable as tax shall be paid and recovered, including provisions for delayed payment.
Establishes that arrears of tax on employment may be recovered under the provisions of the Revenue Recovery Act for the time being in force.
Provides for appeals against orders of assessment or other orders of the assessing authority to the appellate authority, and further to the District Court.
Allows the appellate authority, if satisfied that the decision on an appeal involves a question of law, to refer the case to the District Court.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of revision of the District Collector
main_sections.description: Grants the District Collector powers to revise orders passed by subordinate authorities.
Allows for the rectification of mistakes apparent from the record in any order passed under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power to take evidence on oath, etc.
main_sections.description: Empowers authorities under the Act to take evidence on oath, affirmation, or affidavit.
Deals with the provisions for refunds of tax paid in excess or erroneously.
Specifies the time limit for making claims for refund.
Covers offences and the prosecution of persons who contravene the provisions of the Act.
Addresses offences committed by companies and the liabilities of individuals within those companies.
Defines the manner in which notices under the Act are to be served.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of agents of companies, firms, associations, etc., to tax on employment
main_sections.description: Establishes the liability of agents of companies, firms, or associations for the tax on employment.

main_sections.section_title: Statements, returns, etc., to be confidential
main_sections.description: Stipulates that statements, returns, and other documents furnished under the Act shall be treated as confidential.
Provides rules for the computation of periods of limitation for various actions under the Act.
Ousts the jurisdiction of civil courts in certain matters related to the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of assessing authority, etc., to call for information from local authorities
main_sections.description: Grants assessing authorities the power to request information from local authorities.
Empowers the Government to remove any difficulties in the application of the Act.
Authorizes the Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of Housing Fund and its utilisation
main_sections.description: Provides for the establishment and utilization of a Housing Fund from the proceeds of the tax.
Repeals any previous legislation that is inconsistent with this Act.

important_rules: Persons exercising a profession, art, or calling, or transacting business, or holding any public or private appointment within the State are liable to tax on employment.
Returns showing income for the half-year must be filed by persons liable to tax.
Assessing authorities have the power to assess persons who have escaped assessment.
Arrears of tax can be recovered under the Revenue Recovery Act.
Statements, returns, and other documents furnished under the Act are to be kept confidential.

penalties: Penalties for non-compliance with provisions, failure to furnish returns, or providing false information (details not specified in the provided text but implied by the presence of 'Prosecutions' and 'Offences').
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Assessing Authorities, Government, District Collector
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Notices of demand, recovery proceedings under the Revenue Recovery Act, prosecutions for offences.

rights: Right to appeal against assessment orders.
Right to have evidence taken on oath.
Right to confidentiality of submitted documents.
duties: Duty to pay tax on employment.
Duty to file returns.
Duty to comply with notices and orders from assessing authorities.
Duty to assist in investigations.
obligations: Employers/representatives have an obligation to furnish lists of employees upon requisition.

key_procedures: Procedure for assessment of tax based on returns or escaped assessment.
Procedure for issuing notices of demand.
Procedure for recovery of tax.
Procedure for filing appeals against orders.
Procedure for rectification of mistakes.
Procedure for obtaining information from local authorities.
administration: Government of Kerala, Assessing Authorities appointed by the Government.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on 22nd day of March, 1976, and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No 181, dated 22nd March 1976.
The explanations to Section 4 clarify what constitutes 'aggregate income' for tax purposes.
The Act provides for a Housing Fund.
Civil court jurisdiction is barred in certain matters.

title: The Kerala Tax on Paper Lotteries (Amendment) Act, 2011
purpose: To amend the Kerala Tax on Paper Lotteries Act, 2005.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title as "The Kerala Tax on Paper Lotteries (Amendment) Act, 2011" and states that it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 2011.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 2 of Act 17 of 2005
main_sections.description: Amends Section 2 of the Kerala Tax on Paper Lotteries Act, 2005 (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act).

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 6 of Act 17 of 2005
main_sections.description: This section likely refers to an amendment within Section 2 that pertains to Section 6 of the principal Act. It appears to amend the definitions related to "lottery" and "lottery ticket" by adding a sub-clause (iii) to clause (i) and introducing a new clause (v) which deals with tickets of paper lotteries and other tickets declared as such by the Government.

Inserts a new Section 10A into the principal Act. This new section details the conditions and procedures for obtaining exemption from tax for paper lotteries. It specifies that the Government may, by notification, exempt any paper lottery from the tax levied under the Act, subject to certain conditions and if the net proceeds are utilised for specific purposes like education, health, disaster relief, etc. It also lists various categories of persons and bodies eligible for such exemptions. The sub-sections (i) to (xi) within this new section list specific entities or purposes for which exemptions can be granted.

This section likely deals with the repeal of any existing provisions that might be inconsistent with this amendment and also provides savings clauses to ensure that actions taken or rights acquired under the old provisions are not affected.

important_rules: Paper lotteries are subject to tax as per the Act.
Exemptions from tax for paper lotteries can be granted by the Government under specific conditions and for specified purposes.
The net proceeds from exempted lotteries must be used for purposes like education, health, disaster relief, poverty alleviation, and welfare of the poor and needy.
The Government may declare certain tickets as 'lottery tickets' for the purpose of the Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications and amendments to the principal Act.

rights: Right to claim exemption from tax under certain conditions.
Right to be notified by the Government regarding exemptions.
duties: Duty to pay tax on paper lotteries unless exempted.
Duty to utilize proceeds of exempted lotteries for specified welfare purposes.

key_procedures: Procedure for Government to issue notifications for exemption from tax.
Procedure for utilizing net proceeds of exempted lotteries for designated purposes.
administration: Government of Kerala
important_notes: This Act is an amendment to The Kerala Tax on Paper Lotteries Act, 2005.
The amendments are deemed to have come into force from 1st April, 2011.
The Act allows for exemptions for paper lotteries if their proceeds are used for social welfare and charitable purposes.

title: THE KERALA TAX ON LUXURIES IN HOTELS AND LODGING HOUSES ACT, 1976
purpose: To provide for the levy and collection of a tax on luxuries provided in hotels and lodging houses.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Kerala, specifically to luxuries provided in hotels and lodging houses.

key_definitions.appellate authority: Means an appellate authority appointed under sub-section (2) of section 3.
key_definitions.assessing authority: Means an assessing authority appointed under sub-section (1) of section 3.
key_definitions.Board of Revenue: Means the Board of Revenue constituted under the Kerala Board of Revenue Act, 1957.
key_definitions.company: Means a company as defined in section 3 of the Companies Act, 1956.
key_definitions.hotel: Means a building or part of a building where residential accommodation is by way of business provided for a monetary consideration and includes a lodging house.
key_definitions.luxury provided in a hotel: Means accommodation for residence and other amenities and services (exclusive of charges for food, drink and telephone calls) is fifteen rupees per day or more.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.proprietor: In relation to a hotel, includes the person who for the time being is in charge of the management of the hotel.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Tax on Luxuries in Hotels and Lodging Houses Act, 1976. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of July, 1976.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'appellate authority', 'assessing authority', 'Board of Revenue', 'company', 'hotel', 'luxury provided in a hotel', 'prescribed', and 'proprietor'.

Empowers the Government to appoint assessing and appellate authorities and specifies that all authorities and officers employed in the execution of this Act shall observe and follow the orders, instructions and directions of the Board of Revenue.

main_sections.section_title: Levy and collection of luxury tax
main_sections.description: Specifies that luxury tax shall be levied and collected at specified rates on luxury provided in a hotel. It also details how the tax is to be computed and collected, including provisions for rounding off the tax amount and payment into the Government treasury.

Requires every proprietor liable to pay luxury tax to submit a return within eight days after the end of the month to which the return relates. The return should show the number of rooms or other accommodation in the hotel, number of persons occupying such rooms, days of arrival and departure, and charges recovered.

Outlines the process of assessment and collection of tax. If a return is not submitted or the amount paid is incorrect, the assessing authority can issue a notice. If the proprietor fails to submit the return in time, the assessing authority shall assess the tax. If luxury tax is not paid within the prescribed period, a penalty may be levied.

Any person aggrieved by an order of assessment or penalty levied under section 6 may, within thirty days from the date of receipt of the order, appeal to the appellate authority. The appellate authority may confirm, annul or modify the assessment or penalty.
