The Board of Revenue may, either suo motu or on application, call for and examine the record and proceedings of any order made by the assessing authority and pass such order thereon as it thinks just and proper.

Specifies that nothing contained in the Kerala Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1959, or an appeal preferred under section 7 or an application for revision made under section 8 shall bear a court fee stamp of such value as may be prescribed.
Any luxury tax or penalty recoverable under this Act and remaining unpaid may be recovered as an arrear of public revenue due on land.
A notice under the provisions of this Act may be served by post or by delivering or tendering it to the person to whom it is addressed or to his agent or in such other manner as may be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Power to inspect and take copies of records and accounts
main_sections.description: The assessing authority shall have access at all reasonable times to a hotel or place of business of any person liable to collect or pay the luxury tax. The assessing authority may also examine working records and accounts, and take copies of them.

main_sections.section_title: Power to order production of accounts and powers of entry, inspection, etc.
main_sections.description: The assessing authority may require any proprietor to produce accounts, registers, records, or other documents. They may also enter any hotel or place of business, and inspect accounts, registers, records or other documents.

main_sections.section_title: Power to take evidence on oath, etc.
main_sections.description: The assessing authority, the appellate authority and the Board of Revenue shall, for the purposes of this Act, have the same powers as are vested in a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, when trying a suit, in respect of the following matters, namely: (a) summoning and enforcing the attendance of any person and examining him on oath; (b) requiring the discovery and production of any document; (c) receiving evidence on affidavits; (d) issuing commissions for the examination of witnesses or documents.
Provides for refunds in cases of overpayment or where tax is levied erroneously.
Sets the time limit for making claims for refund.
Provides for penalties for various offences under the Act.
Specifies offenses and penalties applicable to companies.

No civil court shall have jurisdiction to entertain any suit or proceeding in respect of any matter which an assessing authority or appellate authority or the Board of Revenue is empowered by or under this Act to determine.
Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of this Act.

If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, the Government may, by order, do anything not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act, which appears to be necessary or expedient for the purposes of removing the difficulty.
Repeals certain previous enactments and provides for savings.

important_rules: Luxury tax shall be levied and collected at specified rates on luxury provided in a hotel.
Returns must be submitted by proprietors within eight days after the end of each month.
The assessing authority can issue a notice for unpaid tax or incorrect payments.
Penalties may be levied for non-payment of luxury tax within the prescribed period.
Notice of assessment or penalty can be appealed within thirty days of receipt of the order.

penalties: Penalty for failure to pay luxury tax within the prescribed period (equal to a sum not exceeding the amount of luxury tax payable under this Act).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Assessing authority, Appellate authority, Board of Revenue.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment, imposition of penalties, recovery of unpaid tax as arrears of public revenue due on land, inspection of records, and powers of entry and seizure.

rights: Right to appeal against orders of assessment or penalty.
Right to be given a reasonable opportunity of being heard before certain orders are passed.
Right to claim refunds in cases of overpayment or erroneous levy.
duties: Duty to levy and collect luxury tax.
Duty to submit returns in the prescribed manner.
Duty to pay the collected luxury tax into the Government treasury.
Duty to allow inspection of records and accounts.
Duty to comply with requisitions for production of accounts and documents.
Duty to produce accounts, registers, records or other documents when required.
obligations: Obligation to pay luxury tax as per the provisions of the Act.

key_procedures: Submission of monthly returns by proprietors detailing occupancy and charges.
Assessment of tax by the assessing authority, including issuing notices and conducting hearings.
Payment of assessed tax to the Government treasury.
Appeal process for aggrieved persons to the appellate authority.
Revision process by the Board of Revenue.
Recovery of unpaid tax as arrears of public revenue.
Inspection and seizure of records and accounts by the assessing authority.
administration: Board of Revenue, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act came into force on the 1st day of July, 1976.

No residential accommodation (not being a hotel-cum-residence) shall be entered or searched, unless the assessing authority is specially authorised in writing by the Board of Revenue to search that accommodation.
Civil courts are barred from entertaining suits or proceedings concerning matters determined by assessing or appellate authorities or the Board of Revenue.

title: THE KERALA TAXATION LAWS (CONTINUATION AND VALIDATION OF RECOVERY PROCEEDINGS) ACT, 1967
purpose: To provide for the continuation and validation of recovery proceedings in relation to Government dues and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to Government dues, taxation authorities, and assesses in Kerala.

key_definitions.assessee: In relation to any scheduled Act, means an assessee as defined in that Act or a person who is liable to pay any Government dues under that Act.
key_definitions.Government dues: In relation to any scheduled Act, means any tax, penalty, fine, interest, or any other sum payable to the Government by an assessee under that Act, and shall include the surcharge on profession tax levied under section 4 of the Kerala Surcharge on Taxes Act, 1957 (11 of 1957).
key_definitions.scheduled Act: Means an Act specified in the Schedule.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Taxation Laws (Continuation and Validation of Recovery Proceedings) Act, 1967.
Defines terms used in the Act, including 'assessee', 'Government dues', and 'scheduled Act'.

main_sections.section_title: Continuation and validation of certain proceedings.
main_sections.description: Provides for the continuation and validation of recovery proceedings for Government dues, even if the demand was enhanced or a fresh notice of demand was not issued after the enhancement. It also covers situations where Government dues are reduced and the proceedings initiated on the basis of the original demand.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, add the name of any Act providing for the imposition or levy of any tax or duty in the Schedule, and on the issue of such notifications, the Act so added shall be deemed to be an Act specified in the Schedule within the meaning of clause (c) of section 2.

The provisions of this Act shall apply and shall be deemed always to have applied, in relation to every notice of demand served upon any assessee by any taxing authority under any scheduled Act, whether such notice was or is served before or after the commencement of this Act.

If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, the Government may, by order published in the Gazette, make such provisions not inconsistent with the purposes of this Act, as appear to them to be necessary or expedient for removing the difficulty.
The Government may make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act. Such rules shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly and may be amended or annulled by the Assembly.

important_rules: Recovery proceedings for Government dues can continue even if a fresh notice of demand was not issued after enhancement of the dues.
If Government dues are reduced, recovery proceedings initiated on the basis of the original demand can continue, but the amount recovered shall not exceed the reduced amount.
Any modification or annulment of rules made by the Government requires concurrence of the Legislative Assembly.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Taxing authority
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through recovery proceedings for Government dues.

rights: Assessee has the right to have Government dues reduced if they are found to be in excess of the actual liability.
duties: Assessee has the duty to pay Government dues as per the law.
Taxing authority has the duty to ensure proper recovery of Government dues.

key_procedures: Validation of ongoing recovery proceedings for Government dues.
Continuation of recovery proceedings even after enhancement of dues without a fresh demand notice.
Adjustment of recovery proceedings in case of reduction of Government dues.
Government can amend the Schedule to include new taxation Acts.
Government can make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, subject to Legislative Assembly approval.
administration: Government of Kerala
important_notes: This Act has retrospective effect.
The Schedule lists the taxation Acts to which this Act applies. The General Sales Tax Act, 1963 is listed.
Rules made under the Act are subject to modifications by the Legislative Assembly.

title: THE KERALA TEMPORARY STAY OF EVICTION PROCEEDINGS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2009
purpose: To amend the Kerala Temporary Stay of Eviction Proceedings Act, 2007, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Temporary Stay of Eviction Proceedings Act, 2007. Specifically deals with eviction proceedings under section 2 of the principal Act. It also covers cases of eviction proceedings before any Court or the Land Tribunal or the Taluk Land Board or the State Land Board or any other Authority for evicting the holders of the said land.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Temporary Stay of Eviction Proceedings (Amendment) Act, 2009 and it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 26th day of July, 2008.

In sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Kerala Temporary Stay of Eviction Proceedings Act, 2007 (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), for the words "stayed for a period of two years", the words "stayed for a period of four years" shall be substituted.

Notwithstanding the expiry of the period of the stay of eviction proceedings under section 2 of the principal Act, anything done or any action taken, after the expiry of such period and before the 8th day of April, 2009, the date of publication of the Kerala Temporary Stay of Eviction Proceedings (Amendment) Ordinance, 2009 (11 of 2009) by any Court or the Land Tribunal or the Taluk Land Board or the State Land Board or any other Authority, for evicting the holders of the said land shall be invalid.

This section states that the Kerala Temporary Stay of Eviction Proceedings (Amendment) Ordinance, 2009 (13 of 2009) is hereby repealed. It also provides that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: The period of stay of eviction proceedings under section 2(1) of the principal Act is extended from two years to four years.
Actions taken for eviction after the expiry of the original stay period and before April 8, 2009, by any relevant authority, are deemed invalid.
The Kerala Temporary Stay of Eviction Proceedings (Amendment) Ordinance, 2009 is repealed, but actions taken under it are considered valid under the new Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts, Land Tribunals, Taluk Land Boards, State Land Boards, and any other Authority responsible for eviction.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings related to eviction and the provisions of the Act.

rights: Right to a stay of eviction proceedings for a period of four years (as per the amendment).

key_procedures: Amendment of Section 2 of the principal Act to extend the duration of the stay of eviction proceedings.
Declaration of invalidity for eviction actions taken during a specific period (between expiry of original stay and April 8, 2009).
administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but likely falls under the purview of the Law Department or Revenue Department of the Kerala Government, given the nature of eviction and land-related matters.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on 26th July, 2008.
The amendment is retrospective.
Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are saved.
Received the assent of the Governor on the 11th day of September, 2009 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 1675 dated 11th September, 2009.

title: The Kerala Temporary Stay Of Eviction Proceedings Act, 2007
purpose: To provide for the stay of eviction of certain persons in occupation of the land vested in the Government, as surplus land under the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 (1 of 1964), situated in Raroth Village of Kozhikode Taluk of Kozhikode District, more particularly described in the Schedule for a temporary period, till final decisions on the pending applications for assignment of land under section 96 of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963, are taken.
scope: Applies to persons occupying surplus land under the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 in Raroth Village of Kozhikode Taluk, Kozhikode District, pending decisions on land assignment applications.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Temporary Stay of Eviction Proceedings Act, 2007, and it shall come into force on the 26th day of July, 2006.

Provides for the stay of eviction proceedings (including judgments, decrees, or orders of any court or other authority) for persons in occupation of land described in the Schedule, for a period of two years. It also directs the District Collector, Kozhikode to consider applications for assignment of such land and take final decisions. Nothing in this section shall be construed as preventing the District Collector from evicting any person within the period mentioned in sub-section (1) who is found to be ineligible for assignment of land under the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963.

Repeals the Kerala Temporary Stay of Eviction Proceedings Ordinance, 2007. It also states that nothing done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Eviction proceedings for persons occupying specified land are stayed for two years.
District Collector to consider and decide on land assignment applications within the stay period.
Ineligible persons can still be evicted.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: District Collector, Kozhikode
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Considering applications for land assignment and making final decisions; evicting ineligible persons.

rights: Right to stay of eviction for eligible persons.
Right to have land assignment applications considered.
duties: Duty of the District Collector to consider and decide on assignment applications.
Duty to ensure ineligible persons are not unfairly benefited.

key_procedures: Application for stay of eviction by eligible occupants.
Consideration of land assignment applications by the District Collector.
Final decision on land assignment.
Eviction of ineligible persons.
administration: District Collector, Kozhikode
important_notes: The stay period is two years from July 26, 2006.
The act specifically addresses land in Raroth Village, Kozhikode Taluk.
The act repeals the corresponding Ordinance.

title: THE KERALA TENANTS AND KUDIKIDAPPUKARS PROTECTION ACT, 1963
purpose: To provide for the temporary protection of tenants and kudikidappukars in the State of Kerala.
scope: The Act applies to tenants and kudikidappukars in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.tenant: Any person who has paid or has agreed to pay rent or other consideration, for his being allowed by another, to possess and to enjoy the land of the latter, and includes an intermediary, a kanam, a kanam-kuzhikkanam, a kuzhikkanam, a punam or kumri cultivator, a licensee in Kuttanad taluk, a varomdar, an odacharthudai or a person claiming under him, a mulgenidar, and a person holding land situated in any part of the taluk of Hosdurg or Kasargod to which the Malabar Tenancy Act, 1929 does not extend, but not being a benami or a tenant under a transaction known as vakbhayam.
key_definitions.kudikidappukaran: A person who has no home-stead or land, either as owner or as tenant in possession, to erect a homestead, and— (i) who has been permitted with or without an obligation to pay rent by a person in lawful possession of any land to have the use and occupation of a portion of such land for the purpose of erecting a homestead; or (ii) who has been permitted by a person in lawful possession of any land to occupy, with or without an obligation to pay rent, but belonging to such person and situate in the said land, but otherwise has no interest in the land; and "Kudikidappu" means the land and the homestead or the hut so permitted to be erected or occupied together with the easements attached thereto.
key_definitions.rent: means whatever is lawfully payable in money or in kind or in both by a person permitted to have the use and occupation of any land to the person so permitting, and includes michavaram, but does not include customary dues.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, commencement and duration
main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Tenants and Kudikidappukars Protection Act, 1963. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force at once and shall cease to have effect on the 31st day of December 1963. It also states that upon the expiry of this Act, the provisions of section 4 of the Interpretation and General Clauses Act, 1125 (Act VII of 1125) shall apply as if this Act had then been repealed by an Act of the Kerala State Legislature.

main_sections.section_title: Temporary stay of enforcement of rights, privileges, etc., under certain enactments.
main_sections.description: This section provides for the temporary stay of enforcement of rights, privileges, etc., under certain enactments. It specifies that during the period of operation of this Act, no suit or other proceedings— (i) for the recognition or enforcement of any right, privilege, obligation or liability acquired, accrued or incurred under the Kerala Agrarian Relations Act, 1960 (Act 4 of 1961), or the Kerala Ernakulam Tenants and Kudikidappukars Protection Act, 1962 (Act 18 of 1962), or the Madras Cultivating Tenants (Payment of Fair Rent) Act, 1956 (Act XXIV of 1956); or (ii) for the fixation of fair rent under the Malabar Tenancy Act, 1929 (Act XIV of 1930), shall be instituted in or before any court, tribunal or other authority, and all such suits and proceedings pending before any court, tribunal or other authority at the commencement of this Act shall be stayed.

This section provides definitions for various terms used in the Act. Key definitions include "Cochin", "enclaves", "customary dues", "eviction", "garden", "holding", "hut", "intermediary", "kanam", "kanam-kuzhikkanam", "Kuzhikkanam", "Licensee", "milam", "michavaram", "mulgeni", "odacharthu", "Paliyal", "Paramba", "private forests", "punam or kumri cultivator", "rent", "tenant", "vechupakuthidar", "varomdar", and "verumpattomdar".

This section states that nothing in this Act shall apply to— (i) leaves of land or of buildings or of both belonging to or vested in the Government of Kerala or the Government of any other State in India or the Government of India or a local authority or any other authority exempted from the provisions of this Act, in the public interest, by the Government by notification in the Gazette: Provided that, in respect of leases of kandukrishi lands, the provisions of section 5 shall apply to suits or other proceedings for eviction by any landlord other than the Government.

important_rules: No suit or other proceedings for the recognition or enforcement of any right, privilege, obligation or liability acquired, accrued or incurred under the Kerala Agrarian Relations Act, 1960, the Kerala Ernakulam Tenants and Kudikidappukars Protection Act, 1962, or the Madras Cultivating Tenants (Payment of Fair Rent) Act, 1956, or for the fixation of fair rent under the Malabar Tenancy Act, 1929, shall be instituted in or before any court, tribunal or other authority during the operation of this Act.
All suits and proceedings pending before any court, tribunal or other authority at the commencement of this Act shall be stayed.

rights: Temporary protection for tenants and kudikidappukars from eviction.

important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on 13th February 1963 and was published in the Gazette Extra-ordinary, dated 13th February 1963.

Explanation I under Section 3 clarifies that "Somalapattamdar", "Sambalachittudar" or "Coolipattomdar" in respect of any of the palaiat land situated in the Palghat district, shall be presumed to be a tenant, provided such presumption shall stand rebutted if it is proved that the "Somalapattamdar", "Sambalachittudar" or "Coolipattomdar" has not undertaken any risk of cultivation.

Explanation II under Section 3 clarifies that for the purposes of the sub-clause, any person who, on the 11th day of April, 1957, was continuously in occupation of the land of another situate in Malabar, for not less than two years, bonafide believing himself to be a tenant, shall be deemed to be a tenant, even if he did not belong to any of the categories mentioned.

Explanation III under Section 3 clarifies that for the purposes of this sub-clause, 'holder of a chalgeni lease' means a lessee or sub-lessee of specific immovable property situate in the taluk of Hosdurg or Kasargod in the district of Cannanore, who has contracted either express or impliedly, to hold the same under a lease, whether for a specified period or not.

Explanation IV under Section 3 clarifies that for the purposes of this sub-clause, any person who, by virtue of the provisions of section 6 of the Kerala Stay of Eviction Proceedings Act, 1957, was permitted to cultivate any nilam on the 11th day of April, 1957, and who continued to cultivate the nilam on the 10th day of December, 1962, shall be deemed to be a varamdar, notwithstanding the expiry of the term fixed under the varam arrangement.
Explanation V under Section 3 clarifies that 'cultivating tenant' means a tenant who actually cultivates the land comprised in his holding.

Explanation under Section 3 (26) clarifies that 'varom' means an arrangement between the varoundar and the owner or other person in lawful possession of any nilam for the cultivation of paddy and sharing of the paddy produce, and includes the arrangements known as pathivaram, pankuv varam, or pankupattom.

Explanation under Section 3 (31) clarifies that 'verumpattomdar' means a lessee or sub-lessee of immovable property, whether called verumpattomdar or venpattomdar, who has expressly or impliedly contracted to hold the same under a lease, with or without security, for rent, and includes a Thattukudiyen in the Palghat district, but does not include a kanamdar, kanam-kuzhikkanamdar, or kuzhikkanamdar.

Explanation under Section 3 (31) (h) clarifies that 'customary verumpattomdar' means any verumpattomdar who, before the commencement of the Malabar Tenancy (Amendment) Act, 1951, was entirely, by the custom of the locality in which the land is situated, to possession of the said land for a definite period of years, and for whose continuance therein after the termination of that period, for a further period a renewal of had to be paid to the landlord as an incident of the tenure.

Explanation I under Section 4 clarifies that 'lands belonging to or vested in the Government of Kerala shall for the purposes of this clause, have the same meaning as "Government Land" under sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Kerala Government Land Assignment Act, 1960, but leases done escheat to the Government shall not be deemed to be leases.

title: THE KERALA TENANTS AND KUDIKIDAPPUKARS PROTECTION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1964
purpose: To amend the Kerala Tenants and Kudikidappukars Protection Act, 1963.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Tenants and Kudikidappukars Protection (Amendment) Act, 1964.

Amends section 1 of the Kerala Tenants and Kudikidappukars Protection Act, 1963 (Act 7 of 1963), referring to the principal Act, in sub-section (3), for the words, figures and letters "the 31st day of December, 1963", the words, figures and letters "the 31st day of March, 1964" shall be substituted.

In section 6 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), for the words, figures and letters "the 31st day of December, 1963" the words, figures and letters "the 31st day of March, 1964" shall be substituted.

Repeals the Kerala Tenants and Kudikidappukars Protection (Amendment) Ordinance, 1963 (Ordinance No. 4 of 1963). Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken in the exercise of any power conferred by or under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken in the exercise of the powers conferred by or under this Act, as if this Act were in force on the date on which such thing was done or action was taken.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Act substitutes the date '31st day of December, 1963' with '31st day of March, 1964' in specific sections of the principal Act.
Rule 2: Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are considered valid under this Act.
important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 20th February, 1964.
Received the assent of the Governor on the 19th day of February, 1964.
For Statement of Objects and Reasons - see Gazette Extraordinary dated 27th January, 1964.
For report of the Select Committee - see Gazette Extraordinary dated 15th January, 1964.

title: THE KERALA TODDY WORKERS WELFARE FUND (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2009
purpose: To further amend The Kerala Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 1969.
scope: This Act applies to the Kerala Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund and its administration, as amended by this Act.

key_definitions.compensation: "Compensation" means an amount payable in lumpsum to a member for his treatment for injuries sustained during the course of his employment or to his legal heirs in the event of his death as a result of the injuries so sustained.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies that it shall come into force on the 19th day of January, 2009.
Amends Section 2 of the principal Act (The Kerala Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 1969) by inserting the definition of 'Compensation'.
Amends Section 4 of the principal Act by substituting 'eight per cent of the wages' with 'ten per cent of the wages' and adding a sub-section regarding employer contributions.
Amends the Schedule to the principal Act by inserting a new item, '16AAA Eligibility for and the manner of payment of compensation from the fund'.
Repeals The Kerala Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Ordinance, 2009 (17 of 2009) and provides for the saving of actions taken under the said Ordinance.

important_rules: Every employer shall pay to the fund ten rupees each for every half year in the case of every coconut tree and twenty rupees each for every year in the case of every palmirah tree tapped under his control to be utilized for the payment of compensation.

rights: Right to compensation for injuries sustained during employment or for legal heirs in case of death.
duties: Duty of employers to pay contributions to the fund.
obligations: Obligation for employers to contribute a specified amount per tree tapped.

key_procedures: Payment of compensation from the fund.
administration: The Kerala Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 27th day of September, 2009 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 787 dated 29th September, 2009.
The Act specifies the commencement date as January 19, 2009.

title: The Kerala Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 1969
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a fund to promote the welfare of toddy workers in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Kerala and to toddy workers as defined in the Act.

key_definitions.Board: The Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund Board constituted under section 6.
key_definitions.contribution: A contribution payable in respect of a member under a scheme.
key_definitions.employer: Any person who employs, whether directly or through another person, or whether on behalf of himself or any other person, one or more employees and includes any person who has a licence for the manufacture, distribution or sale of toddy under the Abkari Act for the time being in force.
key_definitions.employee: Any person who is employed for wages in connection with the tapping, manufacture, transport or sale of toddy and who gets his wages directly or indirectly from the employer and includes any person employed by or through a contractor or through an agent in or in connection with the tapping, manufacture, transport or sale of toddy.
key_definitions.fund: The Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund established under a scheme.
key_definitions.manufacture: Any process for the preparation of toddy and includes the preparation of a tree for tapping.
key_definitions.member: A member of the fund.
key_definitions.scheme: A scheme framed under this Act.
key_definitions.wages: All emoluments which are earned by an employee while on duty or on leave with wages in accordance with the terms of the contract of employment and which are paid or payable in cash to him, but does not include (i) the cash value of any food concession; (ii) overtime allowance, bonus, and commission.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as The Kerala Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 1969, states its extent to the whole of the State of Kerala, and its commencement upon notification in the Gazette.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'contribution', 'employer', 'employee', 'fund', 'manufacture', 'member', 'schedule', 'scheme', and 'wages'.

States that the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, frame a scheme for the establishment of a fund for employees and the framing of a fund in accordance with the provisions of this Act and the scheme. The fund shall vest in and be administered by the Board constituted under section 6.

main_sections.section_title: Contributions and matters which may be provided in the scheme
main_sections.description: Specifies that contributions to the fund shall be eight per cent of the wages payable to each of the employees, and the employer's contribution shall be equal to the employee's contribution. The scheme may provide for rounding off the contribution amount.

Allows the Government to add to, amend or vary the scheme framed under the Act by notification in the Gazette. Such modifications shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly and shall not take effect unless approved by the Assembly. However, prior modifications are effective until notification.

States that the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, constitute a Board to be called the Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund Board for the administration of the fund and to supervise its activities. The Board shall be a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal. It shall consist of a number of Directors as may be provided in the scheme, including an equal number of representatives of the Government, employers, and employees. The Government shall publish the names of all Directors and the Board shall administer the fund vested in it.

The Government may appoint a Chief Welfare Fund Inspector and Welfare Fund Inspectors. The Chief Welfare Fund Inspector shall be the Chief Executive Officer of the Board. The Board may appoint such staff as it considers necessary with the previous approval of the Government. Their recruitment, salary, allowances, discipline and other conditions of service shall be specified by the Government or the Board with the Government's approval.

main_sections.section_title: Determination of amounts due from employers
main_sections.description: The Chief Welfare Fund Inspector or any other Welfare Fund Inspector may, by order, determine the amount due from any employer under the provisions of this Act or the scheme. The officer conducting the inquiry shall have the powers of a court trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, including enforcing attendance, requiring discovery and production of documents, receiving evidence on affidavit, and issuing commissions. Any inquiry under this section shall be deemed a judicial proceeding. No order determining the amount shall be made unless the employer has been given a reasonable opportunity of being heard. Any person aggrieved by an order may prefer an appeal to the Government within sixty days of the receipt of the order.

main_sections.section_title: Mode of recovery of moneys due from employers
main_sections.description: Any amount due from an employer in pursuance of the provisions of this Act or the scheme may, if in arrear, be recovered in the same manner as an arrear of land revenue.

The amount standing to the credit of any member in the fund shall not be liable to attachment under any decree or order of any court in respect of any debt or liability incurred by the member, nor shall any receiver appointed under the Insolvency Act, 1955, be entitled to or have any claim on any such amount. Similarly, any amount standing to the credit of a member at the time of his death and payable to his nominee shall be free from any debt or liability incurred by the deceased or the nominee before the death of the member.

main_sections.section_title: Priority of payment of contributions over other debts
main_sections.description: Where any employer is adjudicated insolvent or is being wound up, any amount due from the employer under the scheme shall have priority over all other debts, including those due to the Government and employees, and shall be paid in priority to all other debts in the distribution of the property of the insolvent or the assets of the company being wound up.

main_sections.section_title: Employer not to reduce wages, etc.
main_sections.description: No employer shall, by reason only of his liability for the payment of any contribution to the fund, reduce the wages or indirectly reduce the total quantum of benefits to which an employee is entitled under the terms of his employment express or implied.

main_sections.section_title: Members of Board, etc., to be public servants
main_sections.description: Every Director of the Board, the Chief Welfare Fund Inspector and every Welfare Fund Inspector appointed under this Act shall be deemed to be a public servant within the meaning of section 21 of the Indian Penal Code.

Whoever for the purpose of avoiding any payment to be made by himself under this Act or the scheme or of enabling any other person to avoid such payment knowingly makes false statements or false representation shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both. Contravention or non-compliance with the provisions of this Act or the scheme, if no other penalty is provided, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both. Courts shall take cognizance of such offences only upon a report in writing from the Government or its authority.

If any company commits an offence under this Act, every officer of the company who is in default shall be deemed guilty of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly. For the purposes of this section, 'company' means any body corporate, and 'officer of the company' means any director, managing director, secretary, treasurer or manager and includes any person who is in default.

Where an employer makes default in the payment of any contribution to the fund, the Government may recover from the employer damages not exceeding twenty-five per cent of the amount of arrears as they may think fit to impose.

important_rules: Contributions to the fund by the employer shall be eight per cent of the wages payable to each employee.
The employer's contribution shall be equal to the employee's contribution.
Amounts standing to the credit of a member in the fund are protected from attachment for debts.
Contributions to the fund have priority over other debts when an employer is insolvent or being wound up.
Employers are prohibited from reducing wages or benefits solely due to their contribution liability.

penalties: Imprisonment for up to three months or fine up to five hundred rupees, or both, for making false statements to avoid payment.
Imprisonment for up to three months or fine up to five hundred rupees, or both, for contravention or non-compliance with the Act or scheme.
Damages not exceeding twenty-five per cent of arrears may be recovered from defaulting employers.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government and its appointed authorities (e.g., Chief Welfare Fund Inspector, Welfare Fund Inspectors).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Recovery of arrears as land revenue, judicial proceedings for offences, appeal to the Government for determination of amounts, and court cognizance of offences upon report.

rights: Right to appeal to the Government against orders determining amounts due from employers.
Right to protection of fund credit from attachment.
Right to priority of payment of contributions over other debts in case of insolvency or winding up of an employer.
duties: Duty of employer to contribute to the fund.
Duty of employers to not reduce wages or benefits due to fund contributions.
Duty of individuals making false statements to avoid payments under the Act or scheme to face penalties.
obligations: Employers are obligated to pay contributions as specified in the scheme.
Companies are obligated to ensure their officers comply with the Act.

key_procedures: Framing of the Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund Scheme by the Government.
Determination of amounts due from employers by Welfare Fund Inspectors, with powers similar to a civil court.
Recovery of outstanding amounts as arrears of land revenue.
Appeal process to the Government for aggrieved parties regarding amount determination.
Procedure for constitution of the Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund Board, including appointment of directors.
Procedure for modification of schemes through Government notification and Legislative Assembly approval.
Procedure for laying down conditions of service for appointed officers.
administration: The Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund Board, constituted by the Government, administers the fund.
important_notes: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.
The commencement date of the Act is to be notified in the Gazette.
Modifications to the scheme require notification in the Gazette and approval by the Legislative Assembly.
Directors of the Board, Chief Welfare Fund Inspector, and Welfare Fund Inspectors are considered public servants.

title: The Kerala Tolls (Amendment) Act, 2013
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Tolls Act, 1976.
scope: The Act applies within the state of Kerala.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as 'The Kerala Tolls (Amendment) Act, 2013' and states that its provisions shall come into force on the 28th day of November, 2011.
Amends section 2 of the Kerala Tolls Act, 1976. It substitutes 'one hundred lakhs rupees' for 'five hundred lakhs rupees' and 'or a three wheeler' for 'two wheeler'.

Repeals The Kerala Tolls (Amendment) Ordinance, 2013 (4 of 2013). It also states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act, as amended by the said Ordinance, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

administration: Law (Legislation-F) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act comes into force with retrospective effect from November 28, 2011.
Any action taken under the repealed Ordinance is considered valid under this Act.

title: THE KERALA TOLLS ACT, 1976
purpose: An Act to provide for the levy of tolls in respect of certain bridges in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to certain bridges in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.bridge: means any bridge on a highway, but does not include a bridge the cost of construction of which (including the cost of construction of the approach roads necessary for connecting the bridge to the highway) is less than fifteen lakhs rupees;
key_definitions.highway: means any road or way over which the public have a right of way, or are granted access, but does not include any highway declared to be a national highway under the National Highways Act, 1956 (Central Act 48 of 1956);
key_definitions.motor vehicle: means any mechanically propelled vehicle adapted for use upon roads, whether the power of propuls on is transmitted from an external or internal source, and includes a chassis to which a body has not been attached and a trailer;
key_definitions.owner: means, where the person in possession of a vehicle is a minor, the guardian of such minor and in relation to a vehicle which is the subject of a hire-purchase agreement, the person in possession of the vehicle under that agreement;
key_definitions.prescribed: means prescribed by rules made under this Act;

main_sections.description: The Act may be called the Kerala Tolls Act, 1976, and it extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Defines 'bridge', 'highway', 'motor vehicle', 'owner', and 'prescribed' in the context of the Act.

The Government may levy a toll on every motor vehicle entering a bridge constructed wholly or partly at the expense of the Government and declared upon for traffic after the 1st day of January, 1976. The toll shall be levied at such rate and for such period as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, declare to be necessary. The recovery of the amount expended upon such bridge by the Government, or such portion thereof as may be decided by the Government, together with interest at such rate as they may fix.

If any motor vehicle does not pay the toll, the officer appointed by the Government may seize the vehicle. The Government may also sell the property seized for discharge of the toll and expenses. Provided that if at any time before the sale the owner has actually begun, the person whose property has been seized tenders the amount of all the expenses incurred and double the toll payable by him, the property seized shall forthwith be released.
No toll shall be payable for the passage of any motor vehicle belonging to the Government of Kerala or the Government of India.

All police officers shall be bound to assist the toll collectors, when required, in the execution of this Act, and for that purpose shall have the same power which they have in the exercise of their ordinary police duties.

Any person entrusted with the management and collection of the toll may compound for any amount not exceeding one year with any person for a certain sum to be paid by such person for himself or for any motor vehicle kept by him, in lieu of the rates of toll authorised to be levied under this Act, subject to such conditions and restrictions as may be prescribed.

Penalties for evading tolls, obstructing officers, or not paying tolls. Penalties include fines and imprisonment. A Magistrate shall not take cognizance of any offence under this Act except on a complaint in writing made by an officer authorised by the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Exhibition of table of tolls and statement of penalties
main_sections.description: A table of the tolls authorised to be taken in respect of a bridge shall be put up in a conspicuous place near the entrance to such bridge legibly written or printed in English words and figures and also in those of the regional language.
No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against any officer or other person for anything which is in good faith done or intended to be done under this Act.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make rules for the purpose of carrying into effect the provisions of this Act. Such rules may provide for the determination of the rate of levy of the toll, method of collection of the toll, and any other matter prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment of Bridges and Roads Fund and its utilisation.
main_sections.description: Establishes a fund called the Kerala State Bridges and Roads Fund. Proceeds of toll, fines, and fees are credited to this fund. The fund is to be expended for the purpose of constructing bridges and roads. Any amount transferred to the fund shall be charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State. The fund shall be held and administered by the Government. Rules regarding expenditure from the fund may be prescribed.

If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, the Government may, by order, do anything not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act, which appears to them necessary for the purpose of removing the difficulty.

important_rules: Motor vehicles entering a bridge constructed or part-constructed at Government expense are subject to toll after January 1, 1976.
Tolls are to be levied at rates and for periods declared by the Government in the Gazette.
If toll is not paid, the vehicle may be seized, and the property sold to recover the toll and expenses.
Police officers must assist toll collectors.
The Government may make rules regarding toll rates, collection methods, and other matters.
Rules made by the Government under this Act shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

penalties: Fine which may extend to two hundred rupees, or with both, for any person entrusted with the management and collection of the toll who evades or demies any toll on any bridge.

Imprisonment which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to two hundred rupees, or with both, for any person who unlawfully demands or takes any other or higher toll than the lawful toll.

Fine which may extend to one hundred rupees on conviction by a Magistrate for attempting to cross any bridge without paying the toll payable by him under this Act or obstructing any officer or other person in the discharge of his duties imposed by or under this Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government appointed officers and police officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Seizure and sale of property for unpaid tolls, imposition of fines and imprisonment for violations.

rights: Right to exemption from toll for vehicles belonging to the Government of Kerala or the Government of India.
duties: Duty to pay toll for motor vehicles entering specified bridges.
Duty of police officers to assist toll collectors.
Duty to not obstruct officers in the discharge of their duties.
obligations: Obligation to comply with rules made under the Act.

key_procedures: Levy of toll by Government notification.
Seizure and sale of property for recovery of unpaid toll.
Making and laying of rules before the Legislative Assembly.
Removal of difficulties by Government order.
administration: The Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 23rd January, 1977 and was published in the Kerala Gazette No. 49 dated 25th January, 1977.
Basic tax, as defined in the Kerala Land Tax Act, 1961, is not subject to the toll levy.
Rules made by the Government have effect from the date they are made, but any modification or repeal of a rule shall not prejudice anything previously done under that rule.

title: THE KERALA TOLLS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1986
purpose: To amend the Kerala Tolls Act, 1976.
scope: The Act applies to the tolls collected under The Kerala Tolls Act, 1976.

key_definitions.company: A company in which not less than fifty-one per cent of the paid up share capital is held by the Government of Kerala or jointly by the Central Government and the Government of Kerala and includes a company which is a subsidiary of any such company.
key_definitions.corporation: A corporation established or constituted by or under a Central or State Act and owned or controlled by the Government of Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called The Kerala Tolls (Amendment) Act, 1986 and specifies the commencement dates for different clauses.
Amends section 2 of the principal Act by substituting "fifteen lakhs rupees" for "twenty-five lakhs rupees" and inserting new clauses defining 'company' and 'corporation'.
Amends section 3 of the principal Act by substituting specific figures, letters, and words for those appearing in sub-section (1) and adding a proviso to sub-section (3).

Inserts a new section regarding the levy of toll by company or corporation on every motor vehicle entering a bridge constructed by it, with provisions for toll rates, notification, and use of collected amounts.
Amends section 12 of the principal Act by substituting "Bridges and Roads Fund" for "Bridges Fund" and modifying the wording related to the proceeds of toll levied and collected.
Repeals The Kerala Tolls (Amendment) Ordinance, 1986 (52 of 1986) and provides a saving clause for actions taken under the repealed Ordinance.

important_rules: Tolls levied under section 3A are subject to notification in the Gazette and may be leviable at such rate and for such period as the Government may prescribe.
The toll levied shall be collected by the company or corporation, as the case may be, in such manner and in accordance with such rules as may be prescribed.
Any person employed in the management and collection of toll shall be liable to the same responsibilities as would belong to him if employed in the collection of basic tax.

The proceeds of the toll collected by a company or corporation shall be used for recouping amount spent, repayment of loan obtained from financial institution for construction, and for meeting expenses of collection and recovery of toll and other overhead charges.

rights: The Government has the right to specify the bridge in respect of which no toll shall be leviable under section 3A.
duties: Companies and corporations constructing bridges are responsible for levying and collecting tolls.
obligations: Companies and corporations must use the collected toll proceeds for specified purposes.
Employees involved in toll collection have responsibilities similar to those involved in basic tax collection.

key_procedures: Notification by the Government in the Gazette to levy toll under section 3A and to prescribe the rate and period.
Collection of toll by the company or corporation in the prescribed manner and according to rules.
Use of collected toll proceeds for specified purposes including recouping expenses and loan repayment.
administration: Government of Kerala
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 30th day of November, 1986 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 1083 dated 30th November, 1986.
The repeal of the Ordinance does not affect any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance.

title: The Kerala Tolls (Amendment) Act, 2004
purpose: To amend The Kerala Tolls Act, 1963, for reasons of public interest and to introduce specific changes regarding the collection of tolls.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala, specifically concerning the levying and collection of tolls on certain roads and bridges.

main_sections.description: This section likely specifies the short title of the Act and when it comes into force. Based on the document, it refers to 'The Kerala Tolls Act, 1963' as the principal Act being amended. It also mentions the commencement of this amending Act, potentially referencing '2004' year.
main_sections.details: Refers to Act No. 19 of 1963 and mentions the "Kerala Tolls (Amendment) Act, 2004."

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 2 of Act 19 of 1963
main_sections.description: This section amends Section 2 of the principal Act (The Kerala Tolls Act, 1963). Section 2 of the principal Act typically contains definitions. This amendment likely introduces or modifies definitions relevant to the Act.
main_sections.details: The amendment pertains to the definition of 'toll' and potentially other related terms. It states that Section 2 of the Kerala Tolls Act, 1963 (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act) shall be amended. The original definition of 'toll' is being replaced or modified.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 3 of Act 19 of 1963
main_sections.description: This section amends Section 3 of the principal Act. Section 3 of the principal Act likely deals with the power to levy tolls. This amendment would therefore modify how and where tolls can be levied.
main_sections.details: This section provides for the amendment of Section 3 of the principal Act. It implies changes to the authority or conditions under which tolls can be levied or collected.

important_rules: Rule 1: Tenders for collection of tolls may be invited by the Government, specifying conditions of tender, including the earnest money deposit, and the manner of acceptance of tender.
Rule 2: The Government may delegate the powers under this section to the District Collector.
Rule 3: The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make rules to carry out the provisions of this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala (likely through various departments and authorities designated by them).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder, including the collection of tolls and potential penalties for non-compliance.

rights: Right to levy and collect tolls as per the Act.
Right of the Government to frame rules and regulations.
duties: Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act regarding toll collection.
Duty to ensure fair and transparent tendering process for toll collection.
obligations: Obligation to deposit earnest money when submitting tenders for toll collection.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Tendering process for collection of tolls, including submission of tenders, earnest money deposit, and acceptance of tenders.
Procedure 2: Notification by the Government in the Gazette to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act.
administration: Likely the Department of Public Works or a similar government department responsible for roads and infrastructure in Kerala.
important_notes: The Act refers to an existing principal Act: The Kerala Tolls Act, 1963 (Act 19 of 1963).
The amendment specifically addresses the collection of tolls, suggesting a change in methodology or regulation around this aspect.
The Act allows for delegation of powers to the District Collector.
The Government has the power to make rules to facilitate the implementation of the Act.

title: THE KERALA TOLLS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1990
purpose: To amend the Kerala Tolls Act, 1976.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Tolls (Amendment) Act, 1990 and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 29th day of August, 1989.
Amends section 2 of the Kerala Tolls Act, 1976 (6 of 1977). Specifically, it substitutes the words 'twenty-five lakhs rupees' with 'thirty-five lakhs rupees'.

Inserts a new section 3B after section 3A of the principal Act. This new section relates to tolls for bridges. If there are more than one bridge within a radius of fifteen kilometers, then tolls will be levied only at the first of such bridges.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 5
main_sections.description: Substitutes section 5 of the principal Act. The substituted section provides exemptions from toll payment for any motor vehicle belonging to the Government of Kerala or the Government of India, and any stage carriage operated by the Kerala State Road Transport Corporation.

Repeals The Kerala Tolls (Amendment) Ordinance, 1989 (8 of 1989). It also includes a saving clause stating that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the Principal Act as amended by this Act. The assent of the Governor was received on February 21st, 1990, and it was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary on February 22nd, 1990.

important_rules: Tolls for bridges will be levied only at the first bridge if multiple bridges exist within a fifteen-kilometer radius.
Motor vehicles belonging to the Government of Kerala or the Government of India are exempt from toll payments.
Stage carriages operated by the Kerala State Road Transport Corporation are exempt from toll payments.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on August 29, 1989.
The Act amends the Kerala Tolls Act, 1976.
The amendment involves an increase in the monetary threshold from 'twenty-five lakhs rupees' to 'thirty-five lakhs rupees' in section 2 of the principal Act.

title: THE KERALA TORTS (MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS) ACT, 1976
purpose: To unify and amend the law relating to survival of causes of action, liability of joint tortfeasors and liability in cases of contributory negligence in respect of torts.
scope: The Act applies to the whole of the State of Kerala and comes into force at once. It covers causes of action arising from torts, including those where death results, and issues related to joint tortfeasors and contributory negligence.

key_definitions.tortfeasor: A person who commits a tort (a civil wrong).
key_definitions.contributory negligence: Where a person suffers damage partly from their own fault and partly from the fault of another person or persons, and in respect of the cause of action, the damage recoverable shall be reduced to a proportionate extent.
key_definitions.dependants: Includes the wife, husband, parent and child.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Torts (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1976, its extent to the whole of the State of Kerala, and that it shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of death on certain causes of action.
main_sections.description: Deals with the effect of death on causes of action in torts. It specifies that all causes of action subsisting against or vested in the deceased person shall survive for or against their estate, provided such action would have been maintainable by or against the deceased if living. It also outlines provisions for the recovery of damages in such cases and exclusions for exemplary damages.

Specifies how damages are recoverable in cases where a person's death results from a cause of action. Damages are to be calculated without reference to any loss or gain to the deceased's estate consequent to their death, except for a sum in respect of funeral expenses.

main_sections.section_title: Action in cases where death occurs before or at the same time the damage's suffered.
main_sections.description: Addresses situations where death occurs before or at the same time as the damage is suffered. If an action would have been maintainable by the deceased, it shall be maintainable by their personal representative against the person whose actionable wrong caused the death. Damages are to be calculated on the basis of loss or gain to the estate.

main_sections.section_title: Rights conferred by this Act to be in addition to rights conferred by the Fatal Accidents Act.
main_sections.description: Clarifies that the rights conferred by this Act are in addition to those already conferred by the Fatal Accidents Act, 1855, and it extends to causes of action not expressly excepted from section 2 of this Act.

States that in the event of insolvency, damages recoverable by virtue of this Act shall be provable in the administration of the insolvent's estate, notwithstanding that they arise from a liability that is unliquidated or arises otherwise than by contract, promise, or breach of trust.

main_sections.section_title: Proceedings against, and contribution between, joint and several tortfeasors.
main_sections.description: Deals with proceedings against and contribution between joint tortfeasors. It states that where damage is suffered by any person as a result of a tort, and one or more of the wrongdoers are joint tortfeasors, an action for damage may be brought against any of them. However, the total recovery shall not be a bar to an action against any other person who would if sued have been liable. It also outlines provisions for contribution between tortfeasors.

main_sections.section_title: Apportionment of liability in case of contributory negligence.
main_sections.description: Provides for the apportionment of liability in cases of contributory negligence. If a person suffers damage due partly to their own fault and partly to the fault of another, the damages recoverable shall be reduced to an extent that the court thinks just and equitable.

Repeals the Travancore Law Reforms (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1124 (Act XII of 1124), the Legal Representatives Suits Act, 1855 (Central Act XII of 1855), and certain provisions of the Indian Succession Act, 1925, as far as they relate to the revival of actions in torts.

important_rules: Causes of action subsisting against or vested in a deceased person survive for or against their estate.
Damages recoverable in cases of death from tortious acts are calculated without regard to gains or losses to the estate from the death, except for funeral expenses.
If damage is caused by joint tortfeasors, an action can be brought against any of them, and total recovery from one does not bar action against others.
In cases of contributory negligence, damages are reduced proportionally to the claimant's fault.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts of law
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings, including suits for damages and apportionment of liability.

rights: Right of a deceased person's estate to maintain causes of action.
Right of legal representatives to maintain causes of action on behalf of a deceased.
Right to recover damages for torts.
Right to contribution between joint tortfeasors.
Right to have liability apportioned in cases of contributory negligence.
duties: Duty to not commit tortious acts.
Duty to bear liability for one's tortious actions.
Duty to contribute to joint tortfeasors when applicable.
obligations: Obligation to compensate for damages caused by torts.
Obligation to contribute towards damages when acting as a joint tortfeasor.
Obligation to accept reduced damages in cases of contributory negligence.

key_procedures: Initiating legal action for tortious acts, including those where death has occurred.
Calculating damages in survival of action cases, excluding certain financial gains or losses to the estate.
Seeking contribution from joint tortfeasors.
Apportioning liability in instances of contributory negligence by the claimant.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be through the judicial system.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment and unification of existing laws related to torts.
Funeral expenses are considered in damage calculations.
The Act preserves rights conferred by the Fatal Accidents Act, 1855.

The term 'fault' includes negligence, breach of statutory duty, or other act or omission giving rise to liability for tort or would apart from this Act, give rise to defence of contributory negligence.
'Damage' includes loss of life and personal injury.

title: THE KERALA TOURISM (CONSERVATION AND PRESERVATION OF AREAS) ACT, 2005
purpose: To provide for the conservation and preservation of areas of tourist importance in the State of Kerala and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the entire State of Kerala, specifically to areas declared as tourist importance and the surrounding areas.

key_definitions.area: means any area of tourist importance declared as such by the Government under section 3.
key_definitions.development: means the construction, reconstruction, repair, alteration, addition or improvement of any building or other structure, or of any road, bridge, tunnel, canal, drainage, water supply, sewage or any other work or project for the benefit of the public, or of any amenity, facility or convenience for tourists, and includes the conservation, restoration or preservation of any heritage or monument of tourist importance.
key_definitions.preservation: means the conservation and protection of natural resources, ecological balance, landscape, heritage, culture, traditions and the general environment of any area of tourist importance from degradation or destruction.
key_definitions.tourism: means the activities associated with the recreation and leisure of persons traveling to and staying in places outside their usual environment for not more than one consecutive year for leisure, business and other purposes. It is the sum total of phenomena and relationships arising from the temporary and voluntary movement of people to and their stay in a given place.
key_definitions.tourist: means a person who travels to a place other than his usual environment for leisure, business or any other purpose, and stays there for at least twenty-four hours but not more than one year.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and mentions that it shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint. The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 9th day of March, 2005 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No 530 dated 9th day of March, 2005.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'area', 'development', 'Government', 'preservation', 'tourism', and 'tourist'.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration of areas of tourist importance
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to declare any area as an area of tourist importance by notification in the Gazette, considering factors like natural beauty, historical or cultural significance, and potential for tourism development. It also outlines the procedure for objections and passing of the declaration.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of Government to frame schemes for conservation and preservation of areas
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to frame schemes for the conservation and preservation of areas of tourist importance. Such schemes may include provisions for development, infrastructure, regulation of activities, and environmental protection. The Government also has the power to constitute a Board for implementation of the schemes.

Details the powers and functions of the Board constituted under the Act, which include advising the Government, preparing and implementing development schemes, coordinating with various agencies, and ensuring the conservation and preservation of designated areas.

main_sections.section_title: Regulation of activities in areas of tourist importance
main_sections.description: This section outlines various activities that may be regulated or prohibited within areas of tourist importance to ensure conservation and preservation. It covers aspects like construction, quarrying, felling of trees, pollution, and other activities detrimental to the environment or tourist appeal. It also addresses the issuance of permits and licenses for certain activities.
Specifies the penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Act or the rules and schemes made thereunder. Penalties may include fines and imprisonment.
Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: No person shall undertake any development or make any alteration in any building or structure within an area of tourist importance without the prior permission in writing of the Government or the Board.
No quarrying, mining, felling of trees, or any other activity that may cause pollution or damage to the environment shall be permitted within an area of tourist importance.
No person shall discharge or deposit any offensive matter or substance into any water body or public place within an area of tourist importance.
The Government or the Board may issue directions for the proper management and upkeep of amenities and facilities for tourists.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees or with both.
For subsequent contravention, imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months and also with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government and the Board constituted under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspection, issuing directions, imposing penalties, and taking legal action against offenders. The Act also provides for the establishment of a Board to oversee and implement conservation and preservation measures.

rights: The right to be informed about proposed schemes affecting areas of tourist importance.
The right to object to declarations of areas of tourist importance.
duties: Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act, rules, and schemes.
Duty to refrain from activities that harm the environment or degrade tourist areas.
Duty to obtain necessary permits and licenses for regulated activities.
obligations: Obligation to contribute to the conservation and preservation of tourist areas.

key_procedures: Declaration of an area as a tourist importance area: The Government may declare any area as a tourist importance area by notification, after considering objections.
Framing of schemes: The Government may frame schemes for the conservation and preservation of these areas.
Regulation of activities: Obtaining prior permission for development or alteration of buildings, and adhering to regulations on activities like quarrying, pollution, etc.
Enforcement and penalties: Action taken against those who contravene the Act's provisions.
administration: The Government of Kerala, likely through a designated department responsible for tourism and environmental conservation.
important_notes: The Act emphasizes the balance between tourism development and environmental conservation.
The Government has broad powers to protect and manage areas of tourist importance.
The Act empowers the Government to make rules, providing flexibility in implementation.

title: THE KERALA TREASURE TROVE ACT, 1968
purpose: To unify the laws relating to treasure trove in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala. It covers the finding, claiming, and distribution of treasure trove by finders, owners of the place, and the Government.

key_definitions.Collector: Means the Collector of a district or any other officer appointed by the Government to exercise the powers and perform the functions of a Collector under this Act.
key_definitions.owner: In relation to any land or thing, means any person who is entitled, under any reservation in an instrument of transfer of such land or thing affixed thereto, to treasure trove in such land or thing.
key_definitions.treasure trove: Means money, bullion or other valuables found hidden in the earth, the owner of which is unknown.

main_sections.description: States the short title as 'The Kerala Treasure Trove Act, 1968', its extent to the whole of the State of Kerala, and that it shall come into force at once.
Provides definitions for 'Collector', 'owner', and 'treasure trove'.

main_sections.section_title: Notice by finder of treasure trove
main_sections.description: Requires the finder of treasure trove to give notice to the Collector in writing, specifying the nature and approximate value of the treasure and the place where it was found. The notice should be given as soon as practicable.

Upon receiving a notice under section 3, the Collector shall publish a notification in the prescribed manner requiring persons claiming the treasure trove to appear before him within a specified period for making their claims.

main_sections.section_title: Forfeiture of right on failure to appear
main_sections.description: Any person who fails to appear or make a claim as required by the notification issued under section 4, or on subsequent day specified for that notification, shall forfeit their right to the treasure trove.

main_sections.section_title: Matters to be enquired into and determined by the Collector
main_sections.description: The Collector shall inquire into and determine matters related to ownership of the place where the treasure was found and the circumstances under which it was found or hidden.

main_sections.section_title: Time to be allowed for suit by person claiming the treasure trove
main_sections.description: If the Collector believes treasure trove was hidden more than one hundred years ago and a person claims ownership, the Collector may allow a period for the claimant to institute a suit in civil court to establish their right.

main_sections.section_title: When treasure trove may be declared ownerless
main_sections.description: If upon enquiry, the Collector has no reason to believe that the treasure trove was hidden within one hundred years before the date of the finding, or if a suit is instituted within the period and is rejected, the treasure trove may be declared ownerless.
When a declaration is made under sub-section (1) of section 8, the treasure trove shall be delivered to the finder or divided between the finder and the owner of the place as determined.

main_sections.section_title: When no other person claims as owner of the place, treasure trove to be given to the finder
main_sections.description: If no other person claims ownership of the place and the finder has complied with the notification requirements, the treasure trove will be given to the finder.

main_sections.section_title: When only one person claims and his claim is not disputed, treasure trove to be divided
main_sections.description: If only one person claims ownership and their claim is not disputed, the treasure trove is to be divided between the finder and that person.

main_sections.section_title: In case of dispute as to ownership of place, proceedings to be stayed
main_sections.description: If there is a dispute regarding the ownership of the place, proceedings will be stayed until the dispute is resolved by a civil court.
Deals with the settlement of disputes related to the ownership of the place where treasure trove is found.

main_sections.section_title: Division of treasure trove on the establishment of claim in court
main_sections.description: If a claim is established in court, the treasure trove will be divided between the finder and the claimant.

main_sections.section_title: Power to acquire treasure trove on behalf of the Government
main_sections.description: The Collector has the power to acquire treasure trove on behalf of the Government, either by paying its value or a portion thereof.

main_sections.section_title: Decision of Collector final and no suit to lie against him for acts done in good faith
main_sections.description: The Collector's decision is final, and no suit shall lie against him for actions taken in good faith under this Act, subject to civil procedure rules.

main_sections.section_title: Collector to exercise powers of civil court
main_sections.description: The Collector can exercise powers of a civil court for inquiries under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty on finder failing to give notice, etc.
main_sections.description: Penalizes finders who fail to give notice or do not make the deposit or alter or conceal the treasure, with imprisonment and fine.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty on owner abetting offence under section 18
main_sections.description: Penalizes owners who abet offenses under section 18, with imprisonment and fine.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty on owner or occupier for failure to give notice under section 3
main_sections.description: Penalizes owners or occupiers who fail to give notice under section 3, with imprisonment and fine.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for the purpose of carrying into effect the provisions of this Act.
Repeals the Travancore-Cochin Treasure Trove Act, 1951, and the Indian Treasure Trove Act, 1878, as in force in the Malabar district, and certain provisions of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.

important_rules: Finders must give notice of treasure trove to the Collector as soon as practicable.
Claimants must appear before the Collector within the specified period after notification to claim treasure trove.
If treasure trove is declared ownerless, it may be acquired by the Government.
The Collector has the power to acquire treasure trove on behalf of the Government.
The Government has the power to make rules for the implementation of the Act.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or fine with both (for finder failing to give notice, etc.)
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or fine with both (for owner abetting offense under section 18)
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or fine with both (for owner or occupier failing to give notice under section 3)
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Collector, and the Government (for making rules)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inquiries, notifications, declarations, court proceedings, and penalties including imprisonment and fines.

rights: Right of the finder to claim treasure trove if no other claimants appear or if their claim is not disputed.
Right of the owner of the place to claim a share of the treasure trove.
Right of the Government to acquire treasure trove.
Right of appeal for persons aggrieved by a declaration made under sub-section (1) of section 8 within two months from the date thereof to the Board of Revenue.
duties: Duty of the finder to give notice of treasure trove to the Collector.
Duty of claimants to appear before the Collector and establish their claims.
Duty to abide by rules made by the Government.
obligations: Obligation to deposit treasure trove with the Collector or Government treasury.
Obligation to follow the procedures laid out in the Act for claiming and distributing treasure trove.

key_procedures: Finder gives notice of treasure trove to the Collector.
Collector publishes a notification requiring claimants to appear.
Collector inquires into claims and determines ownership.
Treasure trove is divided between the finder and owner(s) or acquired by the Government.
