Disputes regarding ownership are settled through civil courts.
administration: Collector of the district and the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act defines 'treasure trove' as money, bullion, or other valuables found hidden in the earth, the owner of which is unknown.
A treasure trove found is presumed to have been hidden more than one hundred years ago, unless proven otherwise.
The Collector can exercise powers of a civil court.
Decisions of the Collector are final, unless appealed to the Board of Revenue within two months.
The Act repeals previous treasure trove acts in the state.

title: The Kerala University (Amendment) Act, 1966
purpose: To amend The Kerala University Act, 1957.
scope: The Act applies to The Kerala University.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala University (Amendment) Act, 1966.

In section 10 of the Kerala University Act, 1957 (Kerala Act XIV of 1957), (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), in sub-section (1), the following shall be added at the end, namely:— "and if the special committee fails to submit a panel of three names before the expiry of the term of office of the Vice-Chancellor, another special committee consisting of three new members, one elected by the Senate, one elected by the Syndicate and the third nominated by the Chancellor, shall within three months of its constitution make a unanimous recommendation of a person for appointment as Vice-Chancellor and the Chancellor shall appoint such person as Vice-Chancellor; and in case the committee is unable to recommend a name unanimously, it shall submit, within the said period of three months, a panel of three names to the Chancellor who shall appoint one from among the panel as Vice-Chancellor" ; and in sub-section (3), the following proviso shall be added at the end, namely:— "Provided that the Vice-Chancellor shall, notwithstanding the expiration of his term of office, continue to hold office until his successor is appointed by the Chancellor."

(1) The Kerala University (Amendment) Ordinance, 1966 (Kerala Ordinance I of 1966), is hereby repealed. (2) Notwithstanding such repeal, — (a) any appointment made under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been made in accordance with law and shall continue for the period for which it has been made, and (b) any other action or thing taken or done under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been validly taken or done under the principal Act as amended by this Act, if this Act had commenced on the 28th day of January, 1966.

important_rules: If the special committee fails to submit a panel of three names for Vice-Chancellor before the expiry of the term of office of the current Vice-Chancellor, a new special committee will be formed to recommend a candidate within three months.
If the new committee cannot unanimously recommend a person, they will submit a panel of three names to the Chancellor, who will appoint one from the panel.
A Vice-Chancellor will continue to hold office until their successor is appointed, even if their term has expired.
key_procedures: Process for appointing a Vice-Chancellor when the existing committee fails to submit a panel within the prescribed time.
Process for repealing and saving provisions from a previous Ordinance.
administration: The Kerala University
important_notes: Published in the Kerala Gazette Extra-ordinary No. 31, dated 26th March, 1966.

title: The Kerala University (Amendment) Act, 1971
purpose: To amend the Kerala University Act, 1969, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala University Act, 1969.

key_definitions.Appellate Tribunal: Means the Appellate Tribunal constituted under section 59A.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala University (Amendment) Act, 1971, and it came into force on the 10th day of December, 1970.
Amends section 2 of the Kerala University Act, 1969, by substituting "educational agency" or "corporate management" wherever they occur, with the words "educational agency" or "corporate management".
Amends section 50 of the Principal Act, by substituting "educational agency" or "corporate management" wherever they occur with the words "educational agency" or "corporate management".
Amends section 52 of the Principal Act, in sub-section (1), for the words "educational agency of that college", the words "educational agency or corporate management" shall be substituted.

Amends section 53 of the Principal Act. It details provisions related to principals of private colleges possessing qualifications, vacancies in the post of Principal, and advertisement of sub-section (2) of section 53. It also substitutes "governing body or managing council" with "educational agency or corporate management" in sub-section (5) and adds a clause at the end of sub-section (7).

Amends section 55 of the Principal Act. It substitutes "governing body" or "managing council" with "educational agency" or "corporate management" and clarifies provisions regarding teachers' probation.

Amends section 56 of the Principal Act. It substitutes sub-section (2) with provisions regarding teachers of private colleges being suspended and disciplinary proceedings initiated against them, and also includes provisions for appeal to the Vice Chancellor and the Appellate Tribunal.

Inserts a new section 59A, 'Constitution of Appellate Tribunal'. This section establishes an Appellate Tribunal, defines its composition (including a judicial officer, the Chancellor, and other members), its term of office, and vacancy filling. It also details the functioning of the Tribunal through Benches and decision-making by majority.
Amends section 61 of the Principal Act, substituting "and the governing body or managing council" with "and the governing body or managing council" in both places where they occur.
Repeals the Kerala University (Fourth Amendment) Ordinance, 1970, and saves anything done or any action taken under the Principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance.

important_rules: Principals of private colleges shall possess such qualifications as may be prescribed by the regulations.

Any teacher aggrieved by an appointment made under sub-section (2) or sub-section (7) may, within sixty days of the appointment or within sixty days of the date of commencement of this Act whichever is later, appeal to the Vice Chancellor, and the decision of the Vice Chancellor thereon shall be final.

Any teacher aggrieved by an order passed after the commencement of this Act in any disciplinary proceedings taken against him may, within sixty days from the date on which a copy of such order is served on him or within sixty days after the appellate tribunal under this Act has been constituted whichever period expires later, appeal to the Appellate Tribunal, and the Appellate Tribunal may, after giving the parties an opportunity of being heard, and after such further enquiry as may be necessary, pass such order thereon as it may deem fit, inclusive of the reinstatement of the teacher concerned.
No teacher of a private college shall be kept under suspension by the educational agency or the corporate management except when disciplinary proceedings are initiated against him.

penalties: A court fee of Rupees ten shall be leviable on petitions filed under sub-section (6).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Appellate Tribunal, Vice Chancellor, Educational agency, Corporate management.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Appeals to Vice Chancellor and Appellate Tribunal, disciplinary proceedings, substitution of terms in existing sections.

rights: Right to appeal to the Vice Chancellor against certain orders.
Right to appeal to the Appellate Tribunal against certain disciplinary proceedings.
Right to be heard before the Appellate Tribunal.
duties: Principals of private colleges shall possess prescribed qualifications.
Educational agencies and corporate managements are responsible for disciplinary proceedings.
obligations: Educational agencies and corporate managements must follow the Act and Regulations.

key_procedures: Appeals to the Vice Chancellor: Filed within 60 days of appointment or commencement of Act.
Appeals to the Appellate Tribunal: Filed within 60 days of receiving the order or constitution of the tribunal.
Constitution of Appellate Tribunal: Involves a judicial officer, Chancellor, and other members; decisions made by majority.
Proceedings before the Appellate Tribunal: Parties have an opportunity to be heard.
Order by the Appellate Tribunal: Can include reinstatement of the teacher.
Objection to an order by the Appellate Tribunal: Petition to the High Court within 60 days.
administration: The Government, Syndicate, Vice Chancellor, and the Appellate Tribunal are involved in the administration of this Act.
important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 253, dated 22nd May, 1971.
The Kerala University (Fourth Amendment) Ordinance, 1970 (20 of 1970) is hereby repealed.

All proceedings pending before the Syndicate under sub-section (9) of section 53 of the Act, immediately before the commencement of this Act shall stand transferred to the Vice Chancellor for disposal.

purpose: To validate certain acts done, orders passed and sanctions given by the Vice-Chancellor of the University of Kerala.

title: THE KERALA UNIVERSITY ACT, 1957
purpose: An Act to provide for the reorganisation of the University of Travancore.
scope: The Act applies to the entire State of Kerala.

key_definitions.College: A college maintained by, or affiliated to, the University.
key_definitions.Dean: The President of a Faculty of the University.
key_definitions.Board of Studies: A Board of Studies of the University.
key_definitions.Registered graduates: Means graduates registered under the provisions of this Act and the Statutes and includes graduates deemed to be registered graduates.
key_definitions.Teacher: A Professor, Assistant Professor, Reader, Lecturer, Instructor or such other person in-partaking instruction or supervising or controlling research in any of the colleges or other educational institutions of the University.
key_definitions.Student: Means a part-time or full-time student receiving instruction or carrying on research in any of the colleges or other educational institutions of the University.
key_definitions.Prescribed: Means prescribed by this Act, or the Statutes, or Ordinances framed thereunder.
key_definitions.University: Means the University of Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala University Act, 1957, and it shall come into force on such date or dates as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of the Act.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'College', 'Dean', 'Faculty', 'Board of Studies', 'Senate', 'Syndicate', 'State', 'Registered graduates', 'Teacher', 'Student', 'Prescribed', and 'University'.

Establishes the University of Kerala, stating that the Chancellor, the Pro-Chancellor, the Vice-Chancellor and the members of the Senate and of the Syndicate shall, as soon as may be, constitute a body corporate by the name of the University. It also states that the University shall have perpetual succession and a common seal, and may sue and be sued by the said name. It outlines the University's power to take, purchase, and hold property, mortgage, sell, dispose of, and otherwise alienate it, and to do all other acts incidental or appertaining to a body corporate.

Specifies that the jurisdiction of the University shall extend to the whole of the State and that no educational institution situate beyond the limits of the State shall, save with the sanction of the Chancellor, be affiliated to the University, and no educational institution within the State shall, save with the sanction of the Chancellor, continue affiliation to any other University established by law.

Details the extensive powers of the University, including providing for instruction, establishing colleges, holding examinations, conferring degrees, appointing examiners, fixing fees, regulating fees, holding and manage endowments, establishing and maintaining colleges and hostels, and exercising control over students.

main_sections.section_title: University open to all classes and creeds
main_sections.description: Declares that no person shall, on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth, residence, political opinion or any of them, be ineligible for or discriminated against in respect of any employment or office under the University, or admission to any degree or course of study in the University. It also provides conditions under which the Government may sanction recognition of any college or institution exclusively for women, or for education, instruction or residence, or reserve for women or members of socially and educationally Backward Classes or Scheduled Tribes, places for the purpose of admission as students.
Lists the officers of the University: the Chancellor, the Pro-Chancellor, the Vice-Chancellor, the Registrar, and such other Officers as may be provided for by the Statutes.

Defines the Chancellor as the Governor of the State, who shall be the head of the University and shall, while present, preside at meetings of the Senate and at any Convocation of the University. It also outlines the Chancellor's powers, which may be conferred upon him by the Act or the Statutes.

States that the Minister administering the subject of Education in the State for the time being shall be the Pro-Chancellor of the University and shall, in the absence of the Chancellor or during his inability to act, exercise all the functions of the Chancellor.

Details the appointment and powers of the Vice-Chancellor, including the Vice-Chancellor's role as the principal academic and executive officer, the Chairman of the Senate and the Syndicate, and the person responsible for the overall administration of the University. It also outlines the Vice-Chancellor's emergency powers and duties.

Describes the Registrar as a whole-time paid officer of the University appointed by the Syndicate for such period and on such terms as may be prescribed by the Statutes. The Registrar is responsible for exercising such powers and performing such duties as may be prescribed by the Statutes, or required by the Syndicate.
Lists the authorities of the University: the Senate, the Syndicate, the Faculties, and such other authorities as may be provided for in the Statutes.

Outlines the composition of the Senate, including Ex-Officio Members (Chancellor, Pro-Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Heads of University Departments of study and research, Director of Technical Education, Director of Public Instruction, Secretary to Government, Finance Department, Secretary to Government, Education Department, Director of recognised Research Institutions, Deans of Faculties, Principals of Colleges) and Elected Members (from registered graduates, members of the Legislative Assembly, teaching staff of affiliated colleges, Corporation of Trivandrum, Revenue District, Municipalities, Panchayats, heads of recognized trade unions, Heads of recognized High Schools).

rights: Right to confer degrees, certificates or other distinctions.
Right to withdraw or cancel degrees, titles, diplomas etc.
Right to grant fellowships, scholarships, studentships etc.
Right to affiliate to itself colleges within the State.
Right to withdraw affiliation from colleges.
Right to fix and receive fees payable to the University and to demand and receive such fees.
duties: Duty to provide for instruction in such branches of learning as the University may deem fit.
Duty to make provision for research and for the advancement and dissemination of knowledge.

Duty to institute and provide funds for the maintenance of students' advisory bureau, employment bureau, university athletic clubs, national cadet corps, university extension boards, university students' union, translation and publication bureau, and co-operative societies.
Duty to establish and maintain such other institutions as it may deem necessary.
Duty to exercise control over the students as will ensure their physical and moral well-being.

key_procedures: Appointment of Vice-Chancellor: In the absence of the Chancellor or during his inability to act, the Pro-Chancellor shall exercise all the functions of the Chancellor. The Vice-Chancellor shall be appointed by the Chancellor on the recommendation of a special committee consisting of three members, one elected by the Syndicate and the third nominated by the Chancellor.

Formation of Special Committee for Vice-Chancellor appointment: If in case the committee is unable to recommend a name unanimously, the Vice-Chancellor shall be appointed by the Chancellor for whom among a panel of three names submitted to him by the special committee.
Appointment of Registrar: The Registrar shall be a whole-time paid officer of the University appointed by the Syndicate for such period and on such terms as may be prescribed by the Statutes.
Procedure for making Statutes, Ordinances and Bye-laws: These are prescribed processes within the Act for the establishment and governance of the University.
administration: The Minister administering the subject of Education in the State is the Pro-Chancellor, indicating administrative oversight by the Education Department.
important_notes: The Act was enacted in the Eighth Year of the Republic of India.
The Act came into force on such date or dates as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Registered graduates of the University on the date of commencement of this Act shall be deemed to be registered graduates.

title: The Kerala University Act, 1972
purpose: To provide for the reorganisation of the University of Kerala with a view to establishing a teaching, residential and affiliating University for the southern districts of the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala, specifically the southern districts for the purpose of reorganizing the University of Kerala. The Act's provisions regarding affiliation, recognition, and establishment of colleges extend to private colleges and institutions within its territorial limits.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala University Act, 1974. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may by notification in the Gazette, appoint. Provided that different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Act and any reference in any such provision to the commencement of this Act shall be construed as a reference to the coming into force of that provision.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Academic Council', 'affiliated college', 'annual meeting', 'Appellate Tribunal', 'Board of Studies', 'Chancellor', 'college', 'department', 'educational agency', 'faculty', 'government college', 'hostel', 'non-teaching staff', 'principal', 'private college', 'Pro-Chancellor', 'Pro-Vice-Chancellor', 'recognised institution', 'registered graduates', 'Senate', 'State', 'Statutes, Ordinances, Regulations, bye-laws', 'student', 'Studies' Council', 'Syndicate', 'teacher', 'teacher of the University', 'University', 'University area', 'University Fund', and 'Vice-Chancellor'.

Establishes the University of Kerala, with the Chancellor, Pro-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, the Syndicate, and the Academic Council as its authorities. It states that the University shall be a body corporate by the name of the University of Kerala, with perpetual succession and a common seal, and shall sue and be sued by the said name.

Specifies the jurisdiction of the University to the revenue districts of Trivandrum, Quilon, Alleppey, Kottayam, Idukki and Ernakulam of the State. It also clarifies that no educational institution situated beyond these limits can be affiliated to the University without the sanction of the Chancellor and the Government, and no educational institution within these limits can seek affiliation to any other University established by law.

Outlines the extensive powers of the University, including providing instruction and training, establishing departments, conducting examinations, awarding degrees, holding honorary degrees, recognizing institutions, granting diplomas, transferring teachers, constituting appellate tribunals, dealing with hostels, promoting health and general welfare, exercising control over students, constituting boards, rectifying grievances, fixing fees, regulating fees, regulating emoluments and pattern of teachers, admitting students, holding endowments, establishing scholarships, awarding medals, establishing co-operative societies, and entering into associations with other Universities.

title: The Kerala University Act, 1969
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to the University of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the University of Kerala, its faculties, bodies, statutes, ordinances, regulations, rules, by-laws, and finances.

key_definitions.university: The University of Kerala established under this Act.
key_definitions.syndicate: The principal executive body of the University.
key_definitions.senate: The supreme governing body of the University.
key_definitions.statutes: The principal rules governing the University, as provided in section 30.
key_definitions.ordinances: Rules made by the Syndicate regarding the University's functioning, as provided in section 32.

main_sections.description: Governs the establishment, constitution, and control of Faculties within the University. It details the number of members and how they are to be appointed or elected. Each Faculty is subject to the control of the Academic Council.

Establishes the office of the Dean of each Faculty, who is elected in a manner prescribed by the Statutes. The Dean is responsible for the observance of Statutes, Ordinances, Regulations, and Bye-laws, and holds office for a term of four years.
States that there shall be a Board of Studies attached to each department of study in the University, and their constitution and powers are to be prescribed by the Statutes.
Provides for a Finance Committee with the Vice-Chancellor as Chairman to advise the University on financial matters. It also outlines the role of the Financial Officer.
States that the constitution, powers and duties of other authorities of the University shall be declared by the Statutes.
Specifies conditions under which a person is disqualified from being a member of any authority or body of the University, including age, unsound mind, insolvency, and conviction for certain offenses.

Details the scope of Statutes, which can provide for various matters including the appointment, powers, and duties of the Controller of Examinations, the powers and duties of the University, its constitution, the procedure for election of members to the Senate, and award of degrees, diplomas, titles, and other academic distinctions, as well as maintenance of registers and conferment of honorary degrees.
Outlines the process for making and amending Statutes, involving proposals from the Syndicate, consideration and approval by the Senate, and potential submission to the Chancellor.
Specifies the matters that can be covered by Ordinances, such as the levy of fees, residence and discipline of students, and work load and pattern of teaching staff.

Describes the procedure for making, amending, or repealing Ordinances, which requires the Syndicate to propose them, and they come into effect after being laid before the Senate, unless repealed or amended.
Defines the scope of Regulations, which can cover courses of study, examinations, admission of students, qualifications of teachers, and appointment and duties of examiners.
Details the procedure for making and amending Regulations, which are made by the Academic Council and take effect after being laid before the Senate.

Grants the Syndicate power to make rules, bye-laws, and orders consistent with the provisions of the Act, Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations for the guidance and working of Boards and Committees. It also allows for their cancellation or modification.
Mandates that all Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations shall be published in the Gazette.

main_sections.section_title: Resignation or removal of members of any authority or body
main_sections.description: Specifies how members of any authority or body of the University can resign or be removed from office, including grounds for removal like conviction for an offense or unsoundness of mind.

Establishes the University Fund, which receives all grants and loans from the State Government, University Grants Commission, and other sources, as well as income from fees, rents, and profits. This fund is to be employed for the purposes of the University.
States that the University shall receive grants for its maintenance from the Government, subject to such conditions as they think fit.

main_sections.section_title: Annual estimates of income and expenditure
main_sections.description: Requires the Syndicate to prepare annual financial estimates of income and expenditure, which are then to be submitted to the Senate for consideration and approval, with or without alterations.

Mandates the preparation of annual accounts of the University, which are to be submitted to the Government for audit. These accounts are then to be published in the Gazette and placed before the Senate and submitted to the Government.

Requires the Syndicate to prepare an annual report of the University's proceedings, which is to be submitted to the Senate. The Syndicate also informs the Senate of actions taken on the report, and a copy of the report with resolutions is to be submitted to the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Audit of accounts of the University
main_sections.description: States that the Government shall appoint auditors of the accounts of the University and the institution under its management.

important_rules: No person shall be qualified for election or nomination as a member of any authority or body of the University if they are below twenty-five years of age, of unsound mind, undischarged insolvent, or have been convicted by a court of law of an offence involving moral delinquency.

Statutes may provide for various matters including the appointment, powers, and duties of the Controller of Examinations, the constitution, powers and duties of the authorities of the University, the procedure for election of members to the Senate, and award of degrees, diplomas, titles, certificates and other academic distinctions.
Ordinances can be made for matters such as the levy of fees in colleges and other institutions, the residence and discipline of students, and the work load and pattern of teaching staff in colleges.
Regulations can be made for matters such as courses of study, admission of students, qualifications of teachers, and the appointment and prescription of duties of Boards of Studies and Examiners.
Rules, bye-laws, and orders made by the Syndicate must be consistent with the Act, Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations.

main_sections.description: Constitutes the Academic Council, which shall be in charge of the academic affairs of the University. It outlines its powers and responsibilities including academic standards, instruction, examinations, and conferring degrees and diplomas.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and Functions of the Academic Council.—
main_sections.description: Details the powers and functions of the Academic Council, including making regulations, supervising academic matters, advising the Vice-Chancellor, and regulating post-graduate research and extension education.
Establishes a Research Council with specified members and states its role in advising the University on research matters.
Constitutes the Finance Council, detailing its composition and powers related to preparing budgets, scrutinizing expenditures, and making recommendations on financial matters.
Establishes an Extension Council and outlines its composition and functions related to extension activities of the University.
Establishes a Board of Studies for every subject or group of subjects and specifies its composition and role.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of the Board of Studies.—
main_sections.description: Details the powers and functions of the Board of Studies, including recommending syllabi, books, and other materials for courses of study, and advising on matters related to examinations.
Establishes a Faculty Research Committee in each faculty.
Establishes a Project Co-ordination Committee in each faculty.
Establishes a Students Council in each faculty.
States that the University shall have the faculties of Veterinary and Animal Science and Dairy Science.
Refers to the constitution of other authorities of the University as may be prescribed in the Statutes.
Covers the financial aspects of the University, including funds, accounts, and audits.
Outlines the sources of income for the University's general fund.
Deals with the management of pension and provident funds of the University.
Covers other funds that the University may have.
Specifies the procedure for maintaining accounts and auditing the same.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the State Government to order Audit.—
main_sections.description: Grants the State Government the power to order an audit of the University's accounts.
Requires the University to prepare an annual report and submit it to the Government and the Legislature.
Establishes an Appellate Tribunal for the University.

main_sections.section_title: Bar of Jurisdiction of Civil Courts.—
main_sections.description: States that civil courts shall have no jurisdiction to decide or deal with any question relating to the Act or its rules, except as provided.
Deals with the making and amendment of Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations.
Outlines the provisions related to the Statutes of the University.
Details the procedure for making, amending, or repealing Statutes.
States that subject to the provisions of the Act and Statutes, the Board of Management shall have the power to make Ordinances.
Describes the procedure for making, amending, or repealing Ordinances.
States that the University may, by notification in the Official Gazette, make Regulations consistent with the Act and Statutes.
Grants the University the power to make bye-laws.

important_rules: The Academic Council shall consist of a specified list of members.
The Academic Council shall meet at least once in every four months.
The Finance Council shall consist of a specified list of members.
The Extension Council shall consist of a specified list of members.
The Board of Studies shall consist of a specified list of members.
The Faculty Research Committee shall be constituted in each faculty.
The Project Co-ordination Committee shall be constituted in each faculty.
The Students Council shall be constituted in each faculty.
The University shall have the faculties of Veterinary and Animal Science and Dairy Science.
The Management Council shall submit a copy of the accounts and the audit report to the State Government.
The State Government shall have the power to order an audit of the University's accounts.
The University shall prepare an annual report on its activities.
The Statutes shall be made, amended or repealed by the Management Council in the manner hereinafter provided.

The Board of Management shall have the power to make Ordinances, provided that no Ordinance concerning the matter connected with the standards of teaching and examination shall be made by the Board of Management unless a draft thereof has been considered by the Academic Council.
The University may, by notification in the Official Gazette, make Regulations consistent with this Act and Statutes and Ordinances.
Any Ordinance made by the Board of Management shall be submitted to the Chancellor who may assent thereto or withhold his assent.
The Board of Management shall have the power to make bye-laws.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The University authorities (e.g., Management Council, Academic Council, Vice-Chancellor), and the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the implementation of Statutes, Ordinances, Regulations, and by-laws made under the Act, and through audit and government oversight.

rights: Right to provide for the development of veterinary education, animal sciences education, and their associated fields of study and research.
Right to confer degrees and diplomas.
Right to make Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations.
Right to receive grants and donations.
duties: Duty to promote veterinary and animal sciences education and research.
Duty to maintain academic standards.
Duty to manage University funds and accounts properly.
Duty to prepare and submit annual reports.
Duty to conduct examinations and award degrees and diplomas.

key_procedures: Procedure for making Statutes: Draft by Management Council, consideration by Academic Council, submission to Chancellor, assent or refusal by Chancellor.
Procedure for making Ordinances: Draft by Board of Management, consideration by Academic Council for matters related to teaching and examination, submission to Chancellor.
Procedure for making Regulations: Made by the University by notification in the Official Gazette, consistent with Act and Statutes.
Procedure for making Bye-laws: By the University.
Audit procedure: Annual accounts and balance sheet prepared by Finance Officer, audited by the University's auditors, and submitted to the Vice-Chancellor, the Government, and the Legislature.
administration: The Kerala Veterinary and Animal Sciences University, with various councils and boards as its administrative bodies.
important_notes: The Act aims to establish a specialized university for veterinary and animal sciences.

Specific committees like Research Council, Finance Council, Extension Council, Board of Studies, Faculty Research Committee, Project Co-ordination Committee, and Students Council are established to manage different aspects of the University's functioning.
The Act also details the financial management, auditing, and reporting mechanisms of the University.

title: The Kerala Veterinary and Animal Sciences University (Amendment) Act, 2013
purpose: To amend the Kerala Veterinary and Animal Sciences University Act, 2010.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Veterinary and Animal Sciences University.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Veterinary and Animal Sciences University (Amendment) Act, 2013. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 26th day of March, 2012.

In the Kerala Veterinary and Animal Sciences University Act, 2010 (3 of 2011), (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), in sub-section (7) of section 57 for the words "fifty-five years", the words "fifty-six years" shall be substituted.

The Kerala Veterinary and Animal Sciences University (Amendment) Ordinance, 2013 (26 of 2013) is hereby repealed. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act, as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: The Act shall be deemed to have come into force on March 26, 2012.
Section 57(7) of the Principal Act is amended to change 'fifty-five years' to 'fifty-six years'.
administration: Law (Legislation-I) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Kerala Veterinary and Animal Sciences University (Amendment) Ordinance, 2013 is repealed.
Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are deemed to have been taken under this Act.

title: The Kerala Warehouses (Amendment) Act, 1963
purpose: To amend the Kerala Warehouses Act, 1960, for purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force at once.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Warehouses (Amendment) Act, 1963, extends to the whole of the State of Kerala, and shall come into force at once.

Amends section 19 of the Kerala Warehouses Act, 1960. Specifically, it adds a proviso to sub-section (1) and amends sub-section (2) concerning the warehousing corporation's liability for goods deposited in a warehouse established under the Agricultural Produce (Development and Warehousing) Corporations Act, 1956. The amendment clarifies that the corporation may agree to compensate the depositor for loss or damage arising from prescribed risks and can recover additional charges for insurance premia for such risks.

important_notes: Received the assent of the President on 27th February 1963. Published in the Gazette Extraordinary, dated 6th March 1963.

title: THE KERALA WAREHOUSES ACT, 1960
purpose: To provide for the regulation and licensing of warehouses in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Kerala and to all warehousing activities within its jurisdiction.

key_definitions.co-operative society: Means a society registered or deemed to be registered under the Travancore-Cochin Co-operative Societies Act, 1951, or the Madras Co-operative Societies Act, 1932, which engages in any of the activities specified in sub-section (1) of section 9 of the Agricultural Produce (Development and Warehousing) Corporations Act, 1956 (28 of 1956).
key_definitions.depositor: Means a person who tenders his goods to the warehouseman for storing in his warehouse, and includes any person who lawfully holds the receipt issued by the warehouseman in respect of such goods and derives title thereto by proper endorsement or transfer thereof to him by the depositor or the depositor's lawful transferee.
key_definitions.goods: Means any of the articles specified in the Schedule.
key_definitions.licensed warehouse: Means a warehouse licensed under this Act.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.prescribed authority: Means, in relation to any provision of this Act, the authority prescribed to carry out such provision.
key_definitions.receipt: Means a receipt in the prescribed form issued by a warehouseman for a person depositing goods in the warehouse.
key_definitions.rules: Means rules made by the Government under this Act.
key_definitions.warehouse: Means any building, structure or other protected enclosure which is or may be used for the purpose of storing goods on behalf of depositors, but does not include cloak rooms attached to hotels, railway stations, the premises of other public carriers, and the like.
key_definitions.warehouseman: Means a person who has obtained a licence under this Act in respect of his warehouse.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (State of Kerala), and the commencement date, which is upon notification in the Gazette.

This section defines various terms used in the Act, including 'co-operative society', 'depositor', 'goods', 'licensed warehouse', 'prescribed', 'prescribed authority', 'receipt', 'rules', 'warehouse', and 'warehouseman'.

This chapter covers the licensing of warehouses, including the procedure for obtaining a license, conditions for granting a license, term and renewal of licenses, suspension or cancellation of licenses, notice before suspension or cancellation, return of licence, and duplicate licence.

This chapter outlines the duties and responsibilities of a warehouseman, including the reasonable care of deposited goods, precautions against damage or injury, preservation of identity of goods, facilities for inspection, goods deteriorating in warehouse, delivery of goods, liability for shortage or excess, insurance of goods, prohibition of discrimination, and accounts.

This chapter deals with the inspection and grading of goods, including the powers of the prescribed authority to inspect or examine, licensing of weighers, samplers and graders, provisions regarding such licenses, and facilities for weighing, sampling and grading.
This chapter covers warehouse receipts, including the issuance of receipts for deposited goods and receipts for deposits in warehouses.

This chapter contains miscellaneous provisions such as appeals against orders, arbitration, compensation for suspension or cancellation of licence, government assistance for warehouses, inconsistent contracts, penalty and procedure, offences, power to amend the Schedule, rules, power to exempt, and repeals.

important_rules: Warehouseman shall not carry on the business of a warehouseman except under a licence granted under this Act.
Warehouseman must grant reasonable facilities for the depositor to inspect and satisfy himself that his goods are properly cared for.
Warehouseman must keep his warehouse clean and free from damp, and take all necessary precautions against rats and other pests.
Every warehouseman shall maintain accounts, books and records in such form and manner as may be prescribed.
The prescribed authority may at any time, suspend, cancel or suspend for contravention of the Act or rules.

penalties: Penalty for contravention of provisions of the Act or rules is to be determined by arbitration (Section 23(3) and Section 24(3)).
Offences by companies (Section 36).
Penalty and procedure (Section 35).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Prescribed authority.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspection, examination, licensing, suspension or cancellation of licenses, arbitration for disputes, and penalties for contraventions.

rights: Right of the depositor to have goods stored in a warehouse.
Right of the depositor to inspect his goods.
Right of the warehouseman to receive fees for services.
Right to appeal against orders of the prescribed authority.
Right to arbitration in certain disputes.
duties: Duty of the warehouseman to exercise reasonable care of deposited goods.
Duty of the warehouseman to preserve identity of goods.
Duty of the warehouseman to provide facilities for inspection.
Duty to maintain accounts and records.
Duty to issue receipts.
obligations: Obligation to obtain a licence to operate a warehouse.
Obligation to comply with terms and conditions of the licence.
Obligation to follow prescribed procedures for weighing, sampling and grading.
Obligation to maintain the warehouse in a clean and safe condition.

key_procedures: Application for a warehouse licence: Application to be made in the prescribed form to the prescribed authority.
Grant of licence: Prescribed authority shall grant a licence after satisfying that the warehouse is suitable for proper storage and the applicant is competent.
Renewal of licence: Every licence granted is valid for the prescribed period and may be renewed on application and payment of fees.
Suspension or cancellation of licence: May be suspended or cancelled for reasons specified in the Act.
Inspection and grading of goods: Prescribed authority may inspect or examine licensed warehouses and the accounts, books and records therein.
Issuance of warehouse receipts: Warehouseman shall issue a receipt for deposited goods in the prescribed form.
administration: Prescribed authority, likely under a relevant department of the Kerala State Government.
important_notes: The Act was enacted in the Tenth Year of the Republic of India, specifically by the President's Act 2 of 1960.
Published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary dated 29th January, 1960.
The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.
The Government may help to start warehouses, and contracts and agreements inconsistent with the Act to be void.
No compensation shall be payable for suspension or cancellation of a licence, unless the prescribed authority deems fit.
No warehouseman shall deny or lend against goods in warehouse, or lend on his own account or that of others, except in certain circumstances.
Insurance of goods in warehouses is mandated for warehousemen against risks and in such manner as may be prescribed, with provisions for recovery from depositors.
Discrimination prohibited: No warehouseman shall, in the conduct of his business, discriminate between persons desiring to avail themselves of the facilities of his warehouse.

title: The Kerala Water Supply and Sewerage Act, 1986
purpose: To provide for the control and regulation of water supply and sewerage, and for related matters.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and its inhabitants, concerning water supply and sewerage services.

key_definitions.Authority: Refers to the Kerala Water Authority.
key_definitions.owner: Includes any person who is for the time being entitled to receive or who would if the same were let out to rent be entitled to receive the rent of any premises or has the control over the premises.
key_definitions.premises: Includes any land, house, or building.
key_definitions.water supply: Means supply of water for any purpose except for any commercial or trade, manufacture or business, or gardens for purposes of irrigation, or for building purposes.
key_definitions.domestic purposes: Includes supply of water for residential purposes and for attached kitchens and domestic gardens, but not for building purposes or for gardens used for irrigation.

main_sections.section_title: Execution and registration of contracts etc.
main_sections.description: The Authority shall be in writing and executed by its officer and in such manner as may be provided by regulations.

The Authority shall have its own fund to be called the 'Kerala Water Authority Fund' which shall be deemed to be a local fund and to which shall be credited all moneys received otherwise than by way of loans by or on behalf of the Authority. The Authority shall also have another fund to be called the 'Kerala Water Authority's Loan Fund' which shall be also received by a local fund and to which shall be credited all moneys received by or on behalf of the Authority by way of loans.

The Authority shall, before the commencement of, and at any time during, a financial year prepare a statement or a supplementary statement, as the case may be, of the programme of its activities during the year as well as a financial estimate in respect thereof and the same shall be submitted in such manner, in such form, and by such dates as the Government may, by general or special order, direct, for the previous approval of the Government.

The Chairman or the Managing Director or any other member, officer or employee of the Authority shall be liable to surcharge for the loss, waste or mis-application of any money or property of the Authority if such loss, waste or misapplication is a direct consequence of his neglect or misconduct while acting as such Chairman or Managing Director or other member or officer or employee.
The Authority shall, by notification in the Gazette, fix the cost of water to be supplied by it according to volume and also the minimum cost to be charged in respect of each connection.

main_sections.section_title: Cost of collection and disposal of waste water
main_sections.description: The Authority shall, by notification in the Gazette, fix the cost of collection and disposal of waste water according to the basis referred to in section (1) except a fixed sum for a specified period on the basis of expected collection and disposal of waste water during that period.

main_sections.section_title: Definition of supply of water for domestic purposes
main_sections.description: The supply of water for domestic purposes under this Act means supply of water for any purpose except for any commerce or trade, manufacture or business; for gardens or for purposes of irrigation; for building purposes; for fountains, swimming bath public bath, or tanks or for any ornamental or mechanical purposes; for animals where they are kept for sale or hire, or for the sale of their produce or any preparation therefrom; for the consumption and use at restaurants, or by inmates of hotels, boarding houses, lodging-cum-boarding houses or residential clubs and for baths used by such inmates; for the consumption and use by persons resorting to theatres and cinemas; for making or watering streets; for washing vehicles where they are kept for sale or hire.

No owner or occupier of any premises to which water is supplied by the Authority shall cause or suffer any water to be wasted or cause or suffer the service pipe or any tap or other fitting or work connected therewith to remain out of repair so as to cause wastage of water.

main_sections.section_title: Power to cut off water supply
main_sections.description: The Authority may cut off the water supply from any premises under various conditions, including non-payment of dues, damage to meters, or contravention of provisions of the Act or rules/regulations.

important_rules: Employees' accounts with accumulated interest due till the said date and with the accounts relating to the said fund and the exclusion of the local body to be liable for payment of pension, provident fund, gratuity or other like sums as may be payable to such employees at the appropriate time in accordance with the conditions of their service.

Notwithstanding anything contained in the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, (Central Act 14 of 1947), or in any other law for the time being in force, the transfer of services of an employee to the Authority under sub-section (1) shall not entitle any such employee to any compensation that Act or such other law and no such claim shall be entertained by any court, tribunal or other authority.

Every permanent or temporary employee of a local body becoming an employee of the Authority under sub-section (1) shall, by and from the said date, be a permanent or temporary employee, as the case may be, of the Authority, against a permanent or temporary post which shall stand created in the establishment of the Authority with effect from the said date.
Nothing in any rule, regulations or order applicable to employees of the local bodies in relation to retrenchment or abolition of posts shall apply to any employee referred to in sub-section (1).

Notwithstanding anything contained in the foregoing sub-sections, the Authority shall be competent to take such disciplinary or other action as it thinks fit or to continue any such action already initiated against, or in respect of any employee who becomes an employee of the Authority under sub-section (1) in respect of any act or omission or conduct or record of such employee while he was in the service of the local body.

penalties: Any amount found due from any person as surcharge under sub-section (1) as a result of proceedings for surcharge shall be recoverable as arrears of land revenue.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Authority
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through surcharge proceedings and recovery as arrears of land revenue, and by cutting off water supply.

rights: Right to be supplied with water
Right to have meters installed and maintained
duties: Duty to pay for water supplied
Duty to maintain service pipes and fittings in good repair
Duty to prevent wastage of water
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act and regulations

key_procedures: Procedure for fixation of cost of water and waste water collection and disposal.
Procedure for sanctioning loans by the Government to the Authority.
Procedure for submitting estimates of income and expenditure for government approval.
Procedure for surcharge proceedings against members, officers, or employees of the Authority.
Procedure for dealing with wastage of water and cutting off supply.
administration: The Kerala Water Authority
important_notes: The Authority shall have its own fund.
The Authority may invest any sums not required for immediate use in such securities as may be approved by the Government.
The Government may guarantee the repayment of any loan and payment of interest on loans made or transferred to the Authority for the purposes of this Act.
The Authority may, subject to the approval of the Government, grant subsidies or contributions to the local authority.
The Authority may appropriate from its funds such sums as may be necessary for the efficient performance of its functions under this Act.
The Authority may, by notification, fix the charges for connection, dis-connection and re-connection of any water supply or sewer.
The Authority may provide water meters and charge rent for the meter.
The Authority may demand security sum from any consumer in connection with the supply of water or for sewer connection.
The Authority may cut off the water supply from any premises for various reasons including non-payment of dues, damage to meter, or contravention of the Act or rules.

No owner or occupier of any premises to which water is supplied by the Authority shall cause or suffer any water to be wasted or cause or suffer the service pipe or any tap or other fitting or work connected therewith to remain out of repair so as to cause wastage of water.

title: The Kerala Water Supply and Sewerage (Amendment) Act, 1993
purpose: To amend the Kerala Water Supply and Sewerage Act, 1986.
scope: Applies to Kerala Water Supply and Sewerage Act, 1986.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Water Supply and Sewerage (Amendment) Act, 1993. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 30th day of December, 1992.

Amends section 4 of the principal Act. It inserts a clause (h) and a clause (j) to the section. Clause (h) deals with two members appointed by the Government, one of whom shall be a member belonging to a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe. Clause (j) states that after clause (i), the following clause shall be inserted: 'An Accounts Member, who shall be a qualified Chartered Accountant having a minimum of fifteen years of experience in responsible position in a reputed commercial organisation or public sector undertaking or who shall be a member of the Accounts Service of the Central Government, appointed by the Government ".
Amends section 6 of the principal Act. It states that 'In section 6 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), for the words, letter and brackets "(i) or clause (i)" shall be substituted'.

Amends section 7 of the principal Act. It states that 'In section 7 of the principal Act, for the words "and the Technical Member" the words "the Technical Member and the Accounts Member" shall be substituted'.

Inserts a new section 18A titled "Power of Government to retransfer certain Water Supply and Sewerage Services". This section states that notwithstanding anything contained in the Act, the Government may, if they consider it necessary, by a resolution passed in this behalf by the local body which has its own electricity distribution system, direct that the water supply and sewerage services and other items mentioned in clauses (a) and (b) of sub-section (1) of section 18, which had been vested in the Authority under the said section, shall, on and from the date specified in the notification, revert in and stand retransferred to such local body, subject to such terms and conditions as may be mentioned therein and thereupon the local body shall exercise all powers and perform all functions relating thereto. It also states that all rights, liabilities and obligations relating to the water supply and sewerage services reverted under sub-section (1), including the right to recover arrears of water charges, meter hire and of any cost or fees, which were due to the Authority immediately before such retesting, shall vest in and stand transferred to the local body. Further, it states that where any doubt or dispute arises as to whether any property or asset revested in such local body under sub-section (1) or any right, liability or obligation has become the right, liability or obligation of the local body under this section, such doubt or dispute shall be referred to the Government whose decision thereon shall be final and binding on the Authority and the local body concerned. It also states that the Authority shall lend the services of such number of employees as may be necessary, to do the work in connection with the water supply or sewerage services or sewerage works revested in the local body under sub-section (1) and the salary, allowances, and contributions, if any, due to such employees shall be paid by the local body'.

Amends section 22 of the principal Act. It states that 'In the principal Act, in section 22, in clause (d) of sub-section (4), before the words "in any Nationalised Banks", the words "in any Scheduled Bank as defined in the Reserve Bank of India, Act, 1934 (Central Act 2 of 1934) or in any Co-operative Bank or" shall be inserted'.

The Kerala Water Supply and Sewerage (Amendment) Ordinance, 1992 (11 of 1992) is hereby repealed. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act, as amended by the said Ordinance, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act, as amended by this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through resolutions and notifications by the Government; decisions on disputes by the Government.

rights: Right to recover arrears of water charges, meter hire and any cost or fees from the local body.
duties: To exercise all powers and perform all functions relating to water supply and sewerage services retransferred to the local body.
obligations: To pay salary, allowances, and contributions for employees lent by the Authority.

key_procedures: Procedure for retransfer of Water Supply and Sewerage Services by the Government through a resolution.
Procedure for resolution of doubts or disputes regarding retransferred assets or liabilities.
administration: Kerala Water Supply and Sewerage Board
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on December 30, 1992.
Received the assent of the Governor on the 2nd day of March, 1993 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 227 dated the 2nd March 1993.

title: THE KERALA WATER SUPPLY AND SEWERAGE (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2008
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Water Supply and Sewerage Act, 1986.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Water Supply and Sewerage Act, 1986.

key_definitions.domestic sewage: waste water from any house or residence arising out of personal and normal human activities such as drinking, bathing, washing and cooking.
key_definitions.flat: buildings/independent villas having ten or more dwelling units or buildings having a total plinth area of one thousand square metres or more in a premise.
key_definitions.licensed plumber: a plumber who is provided with a license by the Authority to execute works relating to any water connection or domestic or non-domestic sewer connected to sewerage of the Authority, under sections 43 and 47B.
key_definitions.non-domestic sewage: sewage other than domestic sewage and includes industrial sewage.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Water Supply and Sewerage (Amendment) Act, 2008. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 29th day of January, 2008.

Amends Section 2 of the Kerala Water Supply and Sewerage Act, 1986 by substituting definitions for 'domestic sewage' and 'flat', and inserting definitions for 'licensed plumber' and 'non-domestic sewage'.
Amends Section 4 of the principal Act by substituting the clause related to the Secretary to Government in-charge of Water Resources Department.

Amends Section 14 of the principal Act by omitting certain words and inserting new clauses related to the manufacturing and marketing of packaged drinking water, mineral water, aerated water and other processed water, and any other matter consequential to the functions of the Authority.

Amends Section 15 of the principal Act by inserting a new sub-clause related to investment funds, with the previous approval of the Government, in any public sector undertakings or public sector companies involved in the production of goods or articles utilized for the functions of the Authority.

Inserts a new section 15A related to the manufacture and marketing of packaged drinking water, mineral water, aerated water and any other processed water or goods or articles necessary for water supply and sewerage, granting the Authority power to do so by regulations.
Amends Section 33 of the principal Act by substituting the clause related to the Authority charging meter rent for meters provided by the Authority at such rates as may be provided by regulations.

Amends Section 38 of the principal Act by substituting sub-sections (1), (2), and (3) to clarify the Authority's power to grant supply of water for domestic purposes on application made by the owner of any premises or by the occupier, subject to terms and conditions as may be provided by regulations. It also re-numbers sub-sections (4), (5) and (6) as sub-sections (2), (3) and (4) respectively, and inserts a new sub-section (5) regarding ownership and control of the pipe line up to the meter.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new sections 38 A and 38 B
main_sections.description: Inserts new sections 38A and 38B. Section 38A relates to water supply to flats and multi-storied buildings, stating the Authority may supply water through cisterns, tanks, sumps, and ground level reservoirs. Section 38B pertains to control over water supply connections, stating all water connections, irrespective of ownership, shall be under the control of the Authority and maintained properly and altered or repaired only in such manner as provided by regulations.

Amends Section 40 of the principal Act by inserting sub-sections (5) and (6). Sub-section (5) states that water from any public hydrant shall not be used for any non-domestic purpose. Sub-section (6) prohibits external instruments or pipes or hose or other devices connected to public hydrants for tapping water.

Inserts new section 40A, 'Punishment for illegal use of public hydrants'. Any person who unlawfully draws off or takes or use water from a public hydrant shall be punishable with fine not exceeding three thousand rupees and imprisonment for a term not exceeding one month or both.

Amends Section 42 of the principal Act by substituting clauses. Clause (1) states the consumer shall provide a water meter and attach it to the service pipes. Clause (2) states the consumer shall repair or replace water meters installed at his premises at his own cost. Clause (3) states notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), the Authority shall have the power to install its own water meters. Clause (4) states the provision of water meters and their transfer, use, maintenance, and testing, and the expense of installation and security shall be regulated by Regulations.

Amends Section 43 of the principal Act. It clarifies that works relating to water connection to be done by licensed plumbers and as per specifications. It specifies that no person other than a licensed plumber, duly authorized by the Authority, shall execute any work relating to water connection. It also states that a licensed plumber shall not contravene any of the specifications or standards relating to the execution of such works, and such works shall use sub-standard materials, appliances or fittings. It further states that where any such work is executed in contravention, connection shall be refused or disconnected. The Authority may, from time to time, fix charges to be paid to licensed plumbers for such work. No licensed plumber shall demand or receive charge for any such work in excess of the rate fixed by the Authority. If any licensed plumber executes any such works in contravention of the provisions, his license shall be suspended or cancelled. Complaints against licensed plumbers shall be filed before the Executive Engineer. The Executive Engineer, after making such inquiry, shall dispose of the complaint.

Inserts new section 43A, 'Offences by licensed Plumbers'. Whoever, being a licensed plumber, contravenes sub-sections (3) or sub-section (6) of section 43, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees or with both.

Inserts new section 45A, 'Non-liability of the Authority to pay penalty or damages'. The Authority shall not be liable in any way for any loss or damage or sufferings caused to any person by the cutting off the supply of water due to drought or accidents or works relating to re-laying or repairing of any water works or other unavoidable causes.
Amends Section 46 of the principal Act by inserting the words 'with or without any mechanical or other device' in clause (c) of sub-section (1).

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new sections 46 A, 46B, 46C, 46D and 46E
main_sections.description: Inserts new sections 46A to 46E. Section 46A prohibits construction of buildings etc., over land, pipes etc., without permission. If any private street is constructed or any building, wall, fence or other structure is erected on any land or pipes or mains belonging to the Authority, the Authority may remove or cause to remove the same. Expenses incurred by the Authority shall be recoverable as arrears of land revenue.

main_sections.description: No specific details are provided in the scanned document for the insertion of new sections 47A and 47B.

important_rules: Water from any public hydrant shall not be used for any non-domestic purpose.
No external instruments or pipes or hose or other devices shall be connected to any public hydrants for tapping water.
No cleaning or washing of any animal, vehicle, cloth, utensils or any other materials shall be done under or near any public hydrants.

penalties: Punishment for illegal use of public hydrants: fine not exceeding three thousand rupees and imprisonment for a term not exceeding one month or both.
Offences by licensed Plumbers: imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees or with both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Authority
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through regulations, by imposing penalties and imprisonment for specified offenses.

rights: Right to apply for supply of water for domestic purposes on the owner or occupier of premises.
Right of the Authority to install its own water meters.
duties: Duty of the consumer to provide and attach a water meter to the service pipes.
Duty of the consumer to repair or replace water meters installed at his premises at his own cost.
Duty of licensed plumbers to execute works relating to water connections as per specifications and standards.

obligations: Obligation to comply with terms and conditions for water supply as provided by regulations.
Obligation to pay meter rent.

Obligation to avoid any unlawful drawing off or taking or using water from a public hydrant.

Procedure for executing water connection works by licensed plumbers, requiring adherence to specifications and standards.

The Authority has the power to manufacture and market packaged drinking water, mineral water, aerated water and any other processed water or goods or articles necessary for water supply and sewerage, as may be provided by regulations.
The Authority shall not be liable for any loss or damage caused by cutting off water supply due to drought or accidents or repairs.
Expenses incurred by the Authority for removal of unauthorized constructions shall be recoverable as arrears of land revenue.

title: THE KERALA WATER SUPPLY AND SEWERAGE (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2005
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Water Supply and Sewerage Act, 1986.
scope: This act applies to Kerala and amends the Kerala Water Supply and Sewerage Act, 1986.

main_sections.description: This act may be called the Kerala Water Supply and Sewerage (Amendment) Act, 2005 and shall come into force at once.

Amends sub-section (2) of section 15 of the Kerala Water Supply and Sewerage Act, 1986. Specifically, it substitutes "rupees five crores" for "rupees one crore" in two instances within the proviso to clause (ii) and the proviso to clause (iv) of that sub-section.

important_rules: The short title of the act is 'The Kerala Water Supply and Sewerage (Amendment) Act, 2005'.
The act commenced immediately upon its enactment.
In section 15(2) of the principal Act, the financial limits have been increased from 'rupees one crore' to 'rupees five crores'.

title: The Kerala Water Supply and Sewerages (Amendment) Act, 2005
purpose: To amend The Kerala Water Supply and Sewerages Act, 1986.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala regarding water supply and sewerage services.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and the date of commencement. It states that the Act may be called the Kerala Water Supply and Sewerages (Amendment) Act, 2005 and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 17th day of June, 2005.

This section details the amendments made to The Kerala Water Supply and Sewerages Act, 1986. Specifically, it amends Section 15 of the Principal Act.  The amendment involves substituting or adding words to clarify definitions related to 'water supply' and 'sewerage'.

administration: Likely the Public Health Engineering Department or a similar body under the Kerala Government responsible for water supply and sewerage.

title: THE KERALA WEIGHTS AND MEASURES (ENFORCEMENT) ACT, 1958
purpose: To provide for the enforcement of standard weights and measures and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The whole of the State of Kerala. The Act may come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Act or for different areas or for different classes of undertakings or for different classes of goods.

key_definitions.commercial weight or measure: Means a weight or measure purporting to be a standard weight of measure used in any transaction for trade or commerce.
key_definitions.Controller: Means the Controller of Weights and Measures appointed under sub-section (1) of section 15 or any other officer empowered by the Government to exercise the powers and discharge the duties conferred or imposed on the Controller by or under this Act.
key_definitions.Inspector: Means an Inspector of Weights and Measures appointed under sub-section (1) of section 15 or any other officer empowered by the Government to exercise the powers and discharge the duties conferred or imposed on an Inspector by or under this Act.
key_definitions.measuring instrument: Means any instrument other than a weighing instrument and includes any instrument for measuring length, area, volume or capacity.
key_definitions.mint: Means the mint of the Central Government either in Bombay or in Calcutta.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.reference standards: Means the sets of standard weights and measures supplied to the Government by the Central Government in pursuance of sub-section (2) of section 15 of the Standards of Weights and Measures Act, 1956 (Central Act 89 of 1956).
key_definitions.stamping: Means marking in such manner as to be, so far as practicable, indelible and includes casting, engraving, etching and branding.
key_definitions.standard weight or measure: Means any unit of mass or measure referred to in sub-section (1) of section 13 of the Standards of Weights and Measures Act, 1956 (Central Act 89 of 1956) and includes any other weight or measure the continuance of the use of which is permitted by the Central Government under sub-section (1) of section 14 of the said Act.
key_definitions.verification: With its grammatical variations, used with reference to a weight or measure or measuring instrument includes the process of comparing, checking or testing such weight or measure of weighing or measuring instrument and also includes reverification.
key_definitions.weighing instrument: Means any instrument for weighing and includes scales with the weights belonging thereto, scale-beams, balances, spring balances, steel yards and other weighing machines.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Weights and Measures (Enforcement) Act, 1958. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Act or for different areas or for different classes of undertakings or for different classes of goods.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'commercial weight or measure', 'Controller', 'Inspector', 'measuring instrument', 'mint', 'prescribed', 'reference standards', 'stamping', 'standard weight or measure', 'verification', and 'weighing instrument'.

Details the purpose and preparation of working standards for verifying the correctness of commercial weights and measures and measuring instruments. It also specifies requirements for their making, keeping, and verification.

Outlines the purpose, preparation, and verification of secondary standards, which are to be made of such material and according to such designs and specifications as may be prescribed and stamped and authenticated by a person or authority as the Central Government may direct.
States that reference standards shall be kept at such places, in such custody and in such manner as the Government may direct.

For the purpose of verifying the correctness of commercial weights and measures and weighing and measuring instruments used in transactions for trade or commerce, the Government may prepare and keep many sets of authenticated standard weights and measures as they may deem necessary. Such instruments shall be of such kind, kept in such number and shall be verified and stamped in such manner as may be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of use of weights and measures other than standard weights and measures
main_sections.description: Prohibits the use of any weight or measure other than a standard weight or measure, or any custom, usage or practice, no unit of mass or measure, other than the standard weight or measure, shall be used in any transaction for trade or commerce, or in any dealing or contract, or for any work to be done, or goods to be sold or delivered in any area or class of goods or undertakings, in respect of which this section has come into force.

main_sections.section_title: Power to prescribe the use of weights only, or measures only, in certain cases
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power, by notification in the Gazette, to direct that in any specified trade or class of trades no transaction, dealing or contract shall be made or had except by weight only, or except by measure only. A notification issued under this section shall take effect in such area, with effect from such date, and subject to such conditions, if any, as may be specified therein.

main_sections.section_title: Marking of denominations on commercial weights and measures
main_sections.description: Every weight or measure manufactured for use as a commercial weight or measure shall bear the denomination of the weight or measure which it purports to be marked legibly on it in such manner as may be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of sale of unstamped commercial weights and measures
main_sections.description: No commercial weight or measure or weighing or measuring instrument shall be sold or delivered unless it has been verified and re-verified in accordance with the rules made under this Act and stamped in the prescribed manner by an Inspector with a stamp of verification.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of use of unstamped commercial weights and measures
main_sections.description: No weight or measure or weighing or measuring instrument shall be used in transactions for trade or commerce unless it has been verified and re-verified in accordance with the rules made under this Act and stamped in the prescribed manner by an Inspector with a stamp of verification.

Where the size of a commercial weight or measure renders it impracticable to have any denomination marked on it under the provisions of section 9 or to be stamped under the provisions of section 10 or section 11, the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, exempt such weight or measure from being so marked or stamped.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of manufacture, etc., of weights and measures without licence
main_sections.description: No person shall, in course of trade, manufacture, repair or sell any commercial weight or measure or any weighing or measuring instrument unless he has obtained in the prescribed manner a licence in this behalf from the Government or any officer authorised by the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Marking of weight or measure in sealed containers
main_sections.description: No person shall sell, offer for sale, expose for sale, or have in his possession for sale, any article contained in a sealed package or container unless such package or container bears thereon, or on a label securely attached thereto, a description of the net weight or measure of the article contained therein. Provided that the provisions of this section shall not apply to an article sold, offered for sale, exposed for sale, or in possession for sale, which is not ordinarily sold in transactions for trade or commerce by weight or measure.
The Government may appoint a Controller of Weights and Measures and as many Inspectors of Weights and Measures as may be prescribed.
Provides for the verification and stamping of weights, measures, and weighing or measuring instruments by Inspectors.
Grants Inspectors the power to inspect weights, measures, and weighing or measuring instruments.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Inspector to adjust weights or measures
main_sections.description: Empowers Inspectors to adjust weights or measures if they are found to be inaccurate.

main_sections.section_title: Manufactures, etc., to maintain records and accounts
main_sections.description: Requires manufacturers and dealers of weights and measures to maintain records and accounts.
Provides a mechanism for appeals against decisions made by Inspectors or the Controller.
Authorises the levy of fees for services related to weights and measures, such as verification and stamping.

main_sections.section_title: Validity of weights and measures duly stamped
main_sections.description: Specifies the validity period of stamped weights and measures.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for sale or delivery by weight or measure other than standard weight or measure
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for selling or delivering goods by weight or measure other than a standard weight or measure.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for sale of unstamped commercial weights and measures
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for the sale of unstamped commercial weights and measures.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for use of unstamped commercial weights or measures
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for the use of unstamped commercial weights or measures.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for manufacture of weights, etc., without licence
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for manufacturing weights, etc., without a valid licence.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for use of weight or measure in contravention of section 8
