main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for the use of weight or measure in contravention of section 8 (which relates to prescribing the use of weights only or measures only).

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for failure to mark weight or measure in sealed containers
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for failure to mark weight or measure in sealed containers as required by section 14.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for fraudulent use of weights, measures, etc.
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for fraudulent use of weights, measures, etc.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for being in possession of false weight or measure, etc.
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for being in possession of false weight or measure, etc.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for making or selling false weight or measure, etc.
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for making or selling false weight or measure, etc.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for giving short weight or measure
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for giving short weight or measure.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for forging, etc., of weight or measure
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for forging, etc., of weight or measure.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for neglect or refusal to produce weight or measure etc., for inspection
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for neglect or refusal to produce weight or measure etc., for inspection.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for breach of duty by Inspector
main_sections.description: Specifies penalties for breach of duty by an Inspector.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection from legal action for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Controller and Inspector to be public servants
main_sections.description: Declares the Controller and Inspectors as public servants for the purposes of certain sections of the Indian Penal Code.
Deals with the cognizance of offences under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Stamped weight, etc., to be presumed to be correct
main_sections.description: States that a stamped weight, etc., shall be presumed to be correct.
Provides for the punishment of companies for offences committed under the Act.
Empowers the Government to delegate its powers under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Limits of error to be tolerated in weights and measures
main_sections.description: Specifies the permissible limits of error in weights and measures.
Grants the Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.
Repeals previous laws and provides for savings.

important_rules: Weights and measures used in trade must be standard weights and measures.
Commercial weights and measures must bear their denominations.
Commercial weights and measures must be verified and stamped by an Inspector before sale or use.
Manufacture, repair, or sale of weights and measures requires a licence.
Articles sold in sealed containers must be marked with net weight or measure.
False weights and measures are prohibited.
Giving short weight or measure is an offence.
Forging or tampering with weights and measures is an offence.

penalties: Penalty for sale or delivery by weight or measure other than standard weight or measure.
Penalty for sale of unstamped commercial weights and measures.
Penalty for use of unstamped commercial weights or measures.
Penalty for manufacture of weights, etc., without licence.
Penalty for use of weight or measure in contravention of section 8.
Penalty for failure to mark weight or measure in sealed containers.
Penalty for fraudulent use of weights, measures, etc.
Penalty for being in possession of false weight or measure, etc.
Penalty for making or selling false weight or measure, etc.
Penalty for giving short weight or measure.
Penalty for forging, etc., of weight or measure.
Penalty for neglect or refusal to produce weight or measure etc., for inspection.
Penalty for breach of duty by Inspector.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Controller of Weights and Measures and Inspectors of Weights and Measures appointed by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Verification and stamping of weights and measures, inspection, imposition of penalties for contraventions.

rights: Right to use verified and stamped weights and measures.
Right to appeal against decisions of Inspectors.
duties: Duty to use standard weights and measures.
Duty to have commercial weights and measures verified and stamped.
Duty to obtain a licence for manufacturing, repairing, or selling weights and measures.
Duty to mark net weight or measure on articles in sealed containers.
Duty to maintain records and accounts (for manufacturers/dealers).
Duty of Inspectors to perform their duties diligently.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the Act and rules made thereunder.
Obligation not to use or sell false or fraudulent weights and measures.

key_procedures: Procedure for verification and stamping of weights and measures by Inspectors.
Procedure for obtaining a licence for manufacture, repair, or sale of weights and measures.
Procedure for appeal against orders of Inspectors or the Controller.
administration: The Government of Kerala, through its designated departments and appointed Controller and Inspectors of Weights and Measures.
important_notes: The Act may come into force on different dates for different provisions, areas, or classes of undertakings/goods.
Certain weights or measures may be exempted from denomination marking or stamping due to their size.
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected from legal action.
Stamped weights and measures are presumed to be correct.
The Government has the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.

title: THE KERALA WEIGHTS AND MEASURES (ENFORCEMENT) AMENDMENT ACT, 1964
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Weights and Measures (Enforcement) Act, 1958.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala. The Act amends the principal Act of 1958 which deals with weights and measures and their enforcement.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Weights and Measures (Enforcement) Amendment Act, 1964 and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

Amends section 2 of the Kerala Weights and Measures (Enforcement) Act, 1958 (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act) by inserting a new clause (ii) related to the use in transaction or trade or commerce for the purpose of determination or declaration of quantity of anything in terms of measurement of length, area, volume, capacity or weight in relation to: (i) any contract, whether by way of sale, exchange or otherwise; or (ii) any payments, whether by way of royalty, toll, duty or any other dues connected with or forming part of such transaction.
Amends section 3 of the principal Act by inserting in sub-section (1), the words "and special sets of working standards in relation to bullion and precious stones may also be prepared" to be omitted.

Amends section 7 of the principal Act. The sub-section (4) is to be substituted, namely: "(i) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law or any custom, usage or practice, no unit of mass or measure, other than the standard weights or measures shall be used in any transaction for trade or commerce in any area or class of goods or undertakings in respect of which this Act has come into force or be kept in any premises where such transactions are usually conducted." The proviso to sub-section (4) is to be further amended. It provides that the Government may, if they are satisfied that the use of such packages or containers renders it impracticable to comply with the provisions of this section, by notification in the Gazette, exempt such class of packages or containers from the operation of this section.
Amends section 14 of the principal Act. The words "Provided further that" shall be substituted. Also, the proviso is to be inserted.

Amends section 23 of the principal Act, after the commencement of the Kerala Weights and Measures (Enforcement) Amendment Act, 1964. It concerns the insertion of the words 'or whoever after the commencement of the Kerala Weights and Measures (Enforcement) Amendment Act, 1964, keeps any unit of mass or measure other than the standard weights or measures in any premises where such transactions are usually conducted, shall be inserted.'

Inserts a new section 37A titled 'Compounding of offences'. This section provides for the compounding of offences under sections 23, section 24, section 25, section 27, section 28, section 32 or section 34, other than a second or a subsequent offence under section 23 or section 25, may, either before or after the institution of the prosecution, be compounded by the Controller on payment of such sum as the Controller thinks fit. It also states that on payment by the offender of such sum, the offender, if in custody, shall be set at liberty and if any proceedings in any criminal court have been instituted against the offender in respect of the offence, the composition shall be deemed to amount to an acquittal, and no further criminal proceedings shall be taken against him in respect of such offence.

Inserts a new section 43A titled 'Exemption'. This section states that nothing in this Act shall apply to weights or measures or weighing or measuring instruments used by or in any unit or establishment of the Armed Forces of the Union.

important_rules: No unit of mass or measure, other than standard weights or measures, shall be used in any transaction for trade or commerce, except as prescribed.
Packages or containers may be exempted from certain provisions of section 37 by the Government via notification if their use makes compliance impracticable.
Offences under certain sections of the Act (23, 24, 25, 27, 28, 32, 34) can be compounded by the Controller.
The Act does not apply to weights or measures used by the Armed Forces of the Union.

penalties: Offences under sections 23, 24, 25, 27, 28, 32 or section 34 are compoundable.
If proceedings are instituted in court for an offence, compounding is deemed an acquittal.
Specific penalties for offences under sections 23, 24, 25, 27, 28, 32, 34 are detailed in the principal Act (not fully extracted here).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Controller
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through prosecution for offences, and compounding of offences by the Controller.

rights: Right to have transactions conducted using standard weights and measures.
Right to be set at liberty if in custody and the offence is compounded.
Right to not face further criminal proceedings if an offence is compounded.
duties: Duty to use only standard weights or measures in transactions.
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act regarding weights and measures.
Duty to refrain from committing offences related to weights and measures.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to declared quantities in trade and commerce.

key_procedures: Coming into force of the Act: As appointed by the Government by notification in the Gazette.

Compounding of offences: If an offence is compoundable, the offender can pay a sum determined by the Controller before or after prosecution. If in custody, they are released. If proceedings are ongoing, compounding acts as an acquittal.
Exemption process: The Government may notify exemptions for specific classes of packages or containers from certain provisions.
Application of the Act: For specific areas or goods, the Government may notify rules or standards.
administration: Government of Kerala (implied by the mention of 'Government' and 'Controller')
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Kerala Weights and Measures (Enforcement) Act, 1958.
The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 24th day of April, 1964.
Statement of Objects and Reasons was published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 5th March, 1964.

title: THE KERALA WEIGHTS AND MEASURES (ENFORCEMENT) AMENDMENT ACT, 1960
purpose: To amend the Kerala Weights and Measures (Enforcement) Act, 1958.
scope: Applies to persons, commodities, trades, and weighing or measuring instruments used or intended to be used for any purpose other than any trade or trades specified in the notification.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Weights and Measures (Enforcement) Amendment Act, 1960 and it shall come into force at once.

Inserts a new section, 40A, after section 40 of the Kerala Weights and Measures (Enforcement) Act, 1958. This new section grants the Government the power to exempt, by notification in the Gazette, persons, commodities, trades, or any class of weights, measures, or weighing or measuring instruments from the provisions of this Act, subject to such conditions and restrictions as they may think fit to impose.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notification in the Gazette.

rights: The Government has the power to exempt certain categories from the Act.

key_procedures: The Government can issue exemptions via a Gazette notification, specifying the persons, commodities, trades, or instruments, along with any conditions or restrictions.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned in this excerpt, but implied to be related to weights and measures regulation.
important_notes: The Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 8th July, 1960.

title: THE KERALA WOMEN'S COMMISSION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2007 (ACT 27 OF 2007)
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Women's Commission Act, 1991.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Women's Commission and its functioning as per the principal Act.

key_definitions.Secretary: means the Member Secretary of the Commission appointed under sub-section (1) of section 12

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Women's Commission (Amendment) Act, 2007. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 24th day of January, 2007.
Amends section 2 of the Kerala Women's Commission Act, 1991 (17 of 1995) by inserting a definition for 'Secretary'.

Substitutes sub-sections (1) and (2) of section 5 of the principal Act to redefine the composition of the Commission, including a Chairperson, other members, and members appointed by the Government under specific clauses.
Amends section 6 of the principal Act by substituting words in sub-section (1) concerning 'Every member' and 'the Secretary'.
Amends section 7 of the principal Act by substituting the word 'two' with 'four' in reference to a section.
Amends section 11 of the principal Act by renumbering an existing sub-section and inserting a new sub-section regarding the Secretary's tenure of office.
Substitutes section 12 of the principal Act, altering provisions related to the appointment of a Member Secretary and the Commission's role in making investigations.
Amends section 13 of the principal Act by substituting specific phrases related to the Director and the Secretary.
Amends section 21 of the principal Act by substituting the words 'signature of the Director' with 'signature of the Secretary'.
Amends section 28 of the principal Act by substituting phrases concerning 'conditions of service of the Director' with 'conditions of service of the Secretary, the Director'.

main_sections.section_title: Special provision relating to the existing Commission
main_sections.description: Provides special provisions regarding the existing Commission, its Chairperson and members upon the commencement of this Act, including their entitlements to honorarium and allowances.
Repeals the Kerala Women's Commission (Amendment) Ordinance, 2007 (42 of 2007) and provides for saving of anything done or any action taken under the Ordinance.

key_procedures: The Government may appoint a Member Secretary to the Commission, who shall be the Chief Executive Officer of the Commission. The Government may also appoint a Director, in consultation with the Commission, for making investigation for the purposes of this Act.
The Member Secretary and the Director shall carryout such directions issued by the Commission, besides exercising the functions conferred on them by this Act.
administration: The Government of Kerala
important_notes: Received the assent of Governor on the 13th October, 2007 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 1861 dated 15th October, 2007.

The Chairperson and members of the Commission who have ceased to hold office, by virtue of this Act, shall be entitled to honorarium and allowances only for the period for which they had held the office of the Chairperson or member of the Commission, as the case may be, and they shall not be entitled to honorarium and allowances or other benefits for the remaining period of their tenure, if any.

All investigations, inquiries or other proceedings pending before the Commission on the date of commencement of this Act and which have not been disposed of, shall stand transferred to, and be continued by the Commission constituted under the principal Act, as amended by this Act, as if they were commenced before it.

title: The Kerala Women's Commission (Amendment) Act, 2002
purpose: An Act to amend the Kerala Women's Commission Act, 1991 for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: The Act applies to Kerala and amends the Kerala Women's Commission Act, 1991.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Women's Commission (Amendment) Act, 2002 and that it shall come into force on the 20th day of April, 2002.

This section amends section 5 of the Kerala Women's Commission Act, 1991. It re-numbers sub-section (1) and re-numbers sub-sections (b) and (c) as sub-sections (2) and (3) respectively. It also substitutes the words 'Chairperson and not more than six other members to be appointed by the Government of whom one shall be a woman belonging to Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes' with 'Chairperson and not more than two other members to be appointed by the Government'.
This section amends section 6 of the Principal Act by substituting sub-section (4) regarding fixed honorarium and allowances.
This section amends section 7 of the Principal Act by substituting the word 'four' with 'two'.
This section amends section 13 of the Principal Act by substituting the words 'salaries and allowances payable to the members' with 'honorarium and allowances payable to the members'.

This section amends section 28 of the Principal Act by substituting clause (a) concerning honorarium, allowances and other conditions of service of the members, the salary, allowances and other conditions of service of the Director and other staff of the Commission.

main_sections.section_title: Special provision relating to the existing Commission
main_sections.description: This section provides that notwithstanding anything contained in the Principal Act or any other law, any judgment, decree or order of any court, on and from the date of commencement of this Act, the Chairperson and members of the existing Commission constituted under the provisions of the Principal Act shall be deemed to have vacated their offices. It also states that the Chairperson and members who cease to hold office by virtue of this Act shall be entitled to salary and allowances only for the period for which they had been Chairperson or members of the Commission, as the case may be. All investigations, inquiries or other proceedings pending before the Commission on the date of commencement of this Act and which have not been disposed of, shall stand transferred to, and be continued by, the Commission constituted under the Principal Act, as amended by this Act, if they were commenced before it.

This section repeals The Kerala Women's Commission (Amendment) Ordinance, 2002 (5 of 2002). It also provides that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the Principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the Principal Act as amended by this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Kerala Women's Commission and relevant authorities under the Principal Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Kerala Women's Commission Act, 1991 as amended.

rights: Members of the Commission are entitled to a fixed honorarium and other allowances.
Chairperson and members who cease to hold office are entitled to salary and allowances only for the period they served.

key_procedures: The Act comes into force on April 20, 2002.
Existing Commission members and Chairperson vacate office upon commencement of the Act.
Pending proceedings are transferred to the new Commission.
The Kerala Women's Commission (Amendment) Ordinance, 2002 is repealed.
administration: The Kerala Women's Commission
important_notes: The amendment is aimed at reforming the composition and administrative aspects of the Kerala Women's Commission.
Received the assent of the Governor on the 16th day of July, 2002 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 1049 dated 17th July, 2002.

title: THE KERALA WOMEN'S COMMISSION ACT, 1990
purpose: To provide for the Constitution of a Women's Commission to improve the status of women in the State of Kerala and to enquire into unfair practices affecting women and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.member: A member of the Commission and includes the Chairperson.
key_definitions.person: Includes a firm, company, corporation, or any public undertaking, association of persons, or the Government and its agencies including agencies receiving aid from the Government;
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act;
key_definitions.public servant: Any employee of the Government or a local body or any corporation owned or controlled by the Government or of any Government agency or any public undertakings;
key_definitions.registered: Registered with the commission under the Act;

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Women's Commission Act, 1991, extends to the whole of the State of Kerala, and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Defines terms used in the Act, including Commission, Director, Government, member, person, prescribed, public servant, registered, and unfair practice.

Provides for the constitution of the Kerala Women's Commission, to be known as the Kerala Women's Commission, comprising a Chairperson and not more than six other members to be appointed by the Government of whom one shall be a woman belonging to Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes. It also specifies that the Chairperson shall be an eminent woman committed to the cause of women with sufficient knowledge and experience in dealing with women's problems and that members of the Commission shall be persons of ability, integrity, intelligence and standing and having adequate knowledge and experience or have shown ability in dealing with problems relating to safeguarding and promoting the interests of women and protecting their rights.

main_sections.section_title: Application of other laws not barred.
main_sections.description: States that the provisions of this Act shall be in addition to and not in derogation of, any other law for the time being in force, except to the extent the provisions of the other law are inconsistent with the provisions of this Act.

Details the composition of the Commission, including the appointment of the Chairperson and members by the Government, with specific criteria for the Chairperson and members. It also states that the Government shall, by notification in the Gazette, constitute a Commission to be known as the Kerala Women's Commission which shall consist of a Chairperson and not more than six other members to be appointed by the Government of whom one shall be a woman belonging to Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes. It further states that the Chairperson shall be an eminent woman committed to the cause of women with sufficient knowledge and experience in dealing with women's problems. The members of the Commission shall be persons of ability, integrity, intelligence and standing and having adequate knowledge and experience or have shown ability in dealing with problems relating to safeguarding and promoting the interests of women and protecting their rights.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office and conditions of service of members.
main_sections.description: Specifies the term of office for members of the Commission as five years and outlines conditions of service, including resignation, removal from office for various reasons such as becoming an undischarged insolvent, conviction and sentence to imprisonment for an offence involving moral turpitude, refusal to act or becoming incapable of acting, absence from three consecutive meetings, or if the Government has so advised in the opinion of the Commission or the Government.

Details the grounds for removal of members from office, including bankruptcy, conviction for an offence involving moral turpitude, refusal to act, inability to perform duties, or habitual absence from meetings. It also covers removal for situations where the Government has advised so in the opinion of the Commission.

main_sections.section_title: Vacancies, etc., not to invalidate proceedings of the Commission.
main_sections.description: States that any vacancy in the Commission or defect in the constitution thereof shall not invalidate any proceedings or acts of the Commission.

Empowers the Government to make rules for the purpose of carrying into effect the provisions of this Act. This includes rules regarding the generality of the foregoing power, allowances to members, procedure for removal of members, procedure for registration, inquiry into matters, and investigation by the Director.

main_sections.section_title: Acts of the Commission not to be invalidated by informality or any vacancy, etc.
main_sections.description: Ensures that acts of the Commission are not invalidated due to informality or any vacancy.

Specifies conditions under which members can be removed from office, including becoming an undischarged insolvent, being convicted and sentenced to imprisonment for an offence involving moral turpitude, refusing to act or becoming incapable of acting, being absent from three consecutive meetings of the Commission, or if the Government has advised so in the opinion of the Chairperson or member.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Director and other staff of the Commission.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government, in consultation with the Commission, to appoint a Director for making investigations and to carry out such directives given by the Commission, besides other staff. The Government may appoint such other staff as may be necessary to assist the Commission by deputation or direct recruitment and prescribe their conditions of service.

Outlines the functions of the Commission, including inquiring into unfair practices, taking action thereon, inquiring into matters of importance concerning women, recommending measures to the Government on corrective measures, submitting annual reports to the Government, examining laws in force that affect women's constitutional equality and fair treatment, monitoring the working of laws enforcing women's rights, recommending protective measures for women, monitoring recruitment to public services and State Public Undertakings, recommending measures for ensuring equal opportunity for women, and inspecting or causing to be inspected by the Director or any officer of the Commission authorized by the Government, the offices or houses of such persons or agencies.

Details the procedure for the Commission to investigate complaints, including the timeframe for receiving recommendations and for the Government to take action. It also covers the Commission's power to direct the Government to take appropriate action and its right to proceed to ensure justice.

Grants the Commission powers similar to those of a civil court trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, including summoning and enforcing attendance of witnesses, examining them on oath, compelling production of documents, and receiving evidence on affidavits. It also includes powers to issue commissions for the examination of witnesses.

Further elaborates on the functions of the Commission, including inquiring into any unfair practice, taking action thereon, inquiring into matters of importance concerning women and issues concerning unfair practices, and reporting thereon to the Government on the corrective measures to be taken. It also includes functions related to examining laws, monitoring working of laws, recommending measures to the Government, monitoring recruitment, recommending protective measures, and inspecting offices.

Specifies the process for the Commission to inquire into unfair practices, including receiving written complaints, inquiring on its own knowledge or information, and making preliminary investigation when a complaint is made.

Allows the Commission, after investigation into any complaint, to satisfy itself that a person has committed any criminal offence and that he should be prosecuted in a court of law. If it finds so, it may pass an order to that effect.

main_sections.section_title: Annual report to be laid before the Legislative Assembly.
main_sections.description: Requires the Commission to submit an annual report to the Government, which shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly.
States that the Commission shall hold sittings at such places as it may deem fit and in the State of Kerala. It also requires the Commission to make regulations for its procedure.

main_sections.section_title: Authentication of orders, etc., of the Commission.
main_sections.description: Prescribes that all orders and decisions of the Commission shall be authenticated by the Chairperson or such other officer as may be authorised by the Commission.

main_sections.section_title: Donations, contributions, etc., to the Commission.
main_sections.description: Allows the Commission to accept donations and contributions from the Government, any person or any other source, and to receive money from the Government for its purposes.
Mandates that the Government shall consult the Commission on all major policy matters affecting women.

main_sections.section_title: Members, officers and employees of the Commission to be public servants.
main_sections.description: Declares that all members, officers, and employees of the Commission shall be deemed to be public servants within the meaning of Section 21 of the Indian Penal Code.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of acts done in good faith.
main_sections.description: Provides that no suit, prosecution or other legal proceedings shall lie against any member or officer of the Commission for anything done or intended to be done in good faith under the Act or the rules made thereunder.
Prohibits courts from granting injunctions in certain cases, particularly in relation to proceedings under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
Empowers the Government to remove any difficulty in giving effect to the provisions of the Act, including making any order not inconsistent with the provisions of the Act for this purpose.

Gives the Government the power to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of the Act, including rules regarding the generality of the foregoing power, allowances of members and other staff, procedure for removal of members, procedure for registration, procedure for inquiries, and investigation by the Director.

important_rules: All members, officers and employees of the Commission shall be deemed to be public servants within the meaning of Section 21 of the Indian Penal Code (Central Act 45 of 1860).

No suit, prosecution or other legal proceedings shall lie against any member or officer of the Commission for anything done or intended to be done in good faith under this Act or the rules made thereunder.

Courts shall not grant injunctions notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Central Act 5 of 1908), or any other law for the time being in force, or no court shall grant any injunction restraining any proceeding which is being or about to be taken under the provisions of this Act.
The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make rules for the purpose of carrying into effect the provisions of this Act.

In particular and without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing power, such rules may provide for: (i) the allowances payable to the members and the administrative expenses, including the salaries, allowances and pensions payable to, or in respect of, the Director and the other staff of the Commission, shall be charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State; (ii) the procedure for registration under section 14 of the Act; (iii) the procedure for inquiries under section 17 of the Act; (iv) investigations by the Director; (v) procedure for inspection of prisons, police stations, lock-ups, sub-jails, rescue homes or other places of custody where women are kept as prisoners or otherwise or shelters for women or other places run by the Government or by its agencies including agencies receiving aid from the Government for the purpose of ensuring secure equal opportunity to women or children or for the purpose of inquiring whether women or girls run by any person and or other places wherein unfair practice to women or girls is compli_d of or for holding of enquiries about the treatment that women or girls are subjected to at such places;

penalties: No specific monetary penalties are detailed in the provided sections. Enforcement relies on legal processes and official actions.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Commission and the Government of Kerala.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through investigations, inquiries, recommendations to the Government, initiation of prosecution for criminal offences, and use of powers similar to civil courts.

rights: Right to have status improved.
Right to have unfair practices affecting women inquired into.
Right to protection of interests.
Right to secure equal opportunity.
Right to be free from unfair practices.
duties: Duty of the Government to constitute and support the Commission.
Duty of the Commission to inquire into complaints and matters affecting women.
Duty of the Commission to recommend corrective measures.
Duty of the Commission to monitor laws affecting women.
Duty of the Commission to inspect relevant institutions.
Duty of the Commission to ensure equal opportunity for women.
obligations: Obligation of the Government to consult the Commission on major policy matters affecting women.

key_procedures: Complaint Submission: A woman can submit a complaint to the Commission regarding unfair practices or issues affecting her rights and interests.

Investigation: The Commission shall inquire into complaints and matters of importance concerning women. This can include written complaints, inquiries based on its own knowledge, and preliminary investigations.
Action on Investigation: Based on the investigation, the Commission may take action, recommend measures to the Government, or initiate prosecution if a criminal offence is suspected.
Reporting: The Commission shall submit annual reports to the Government, which are then laid before the Legislative Assembly.
Rule Making: The Government can make rules to implement the provisions of the Act, covering various aspects of the Commission's functioning and procedures.
administration: The Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act was received the assent of the President on the 22nd day of August 1995 and published in the Gazette extraordinary No. 920, dated 15th September 1995. (This note appears to refer to a later amendment or the actual gazette publication date, as the Act title is 1990).
The Act provides powers to the Commission similar to those of a civil court.
No court shall grant injunctions restraining proceedings under this Act.
The Government has the power to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act through appropriate orders.

title: THE KERALA APPROPRIATION (No. 6) ACT, 1976
purpose: To provide for the authorisation of appropriation of moneys out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala to meet the amounts spent on certain services during the financial year ended on the 31st day of March, 1971, in excess of the amounts granted for those services and for that year.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Appropriation (No. 6) Act, 1976.

main_sections.section_title: Issue of Rs 23,03,77,380 out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala to meet certain excess expenditure for the year ended on the 31st March, 1971
main_sections.description: Authorizes the issue of Rs 23,03,77,380 from the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala to meet excess expenditure for the financial year ended on 31st March, 1971, in excess of amounts granted for those services and for that year. The sums specified in column (3) of the Schedule aggregate to the sum of twenty-three crores, three lakhs, seventy-seven thousand, three hundred and eighty rupees shall be deemed to have been authorised to be paid and applied to meet the amounts spent for defraying the charges in respect of the services specified in column (2) of the Schedule during the financial year ended on the 31st day of March, 1971, in excess of the amounts granted for those services and for that year.

The sums deemed to have been authorised to be paid and applied from and out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala under this Act shall be deemed to have been appropriated for the services and purposes expressed in the Schedule in relation to the financial year ended on the 31st day of March, 1971.

important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 22nd day of May, 1976 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 316, dated 24th May 1976.

title: The Kerala Children (Amendment) Act, 1976
purpose: To amend The Kerala Children Act, 1972.
scope: This act applies to the state of Kerala and amends The Kerala Children Act, 1972.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Children (Amendment) Act, 1976.
In section 28 of the Kerala Children Act, 1972 (3 of 1973), sub-section (3) shall be omitted.

important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 14th day of November, 1976 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 661, dated 18th November, 1976.

title: THE KERALA ELECTRICITY DUTY ACT, 1963
purpose: To unify and amend the laws relating to the levy of duty on sale and consumption of electrical energy in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala. It concerns the levy of duty on the sale and consumption of electrical energy by licensees to consumers.

key_definitions.consumer: Includes a local authority, company or other person to whom energy is supplied by a licensee on payment of charges, or otherwise, and a licensee or other person who consumes energy generated by himself, but does not include a licensee to whom energy is supplied by the Kerala State Electricity Board for supply to others.
key_definitions.licensee: The Kerala State Electricity Board constituted under section 5 of the State Electricity (Supply) Act, 1948 (Central Act 54 of 1948), or any person licensed under Part II of the Indian Electricity Act, 1910 (Central Act 9 of 1910), to supply energy and includes any person who is deemed to have been so licensed, and any other person who has obtained the sanction of the Government under section 28 of the said Act.
key_definitions.electricity duty: Means electricity duty levied under section 3 of the Act.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala Electricity Duty Act, 1963, that it extends to the whole of the State of Kerala, and that it came into force on the date of notification by the Government, as it was enacted in the Fourteenth Year of the Republic of India.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'consumer', 'licensee', 'electricity duty', and 'prescribed'.

main_sections.section_title: Levy of Electricity Duty on certain sales of energy by licensees
main_sections.description: Specifies that every licensee shall, every month, pay a duty at the rate of 6 naye Paise per unit of energy sold at a price of more than 12 naye Paise per unit. The duty is payable by the licensee on energy sold to other licensees. If a licensee holds more than one licence, the duty shall be calculated and levied separately in respect of each licence. The duty on the sale of energy shall be borne by the licensee and not passed on to the consumer.

main_sections.section_title: Levy of Electricity Duty on consumers
main_sections.description: States that every consumer belonging to the classes specified in column (2) of the Schedule shall pay every month to the Government, in the prescribed manner, a duty calculated at the rate specified against such class in column (3) thereof. It also clarifies that if energy is supplied by an agreement entered into between the Government or the licensee and the consumer, the rate shall be competent for the Government to reduce it or exempt the consumer. Duty levied on consumers by the licensee is to be paid to the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Collection and payment of electricity duty levied on consumers
main_sections.description: Licensees shall collect and pay the electricity duty levied on consumers to the Government. For recovery of charges, the licensee shall follow the procedure in section 4 of the Indian Electricity Act, 1910. Any unpaid duty shall be recoverable as arrears of land revenue.

Every licensee shall keep books of account, in the prescribed form and to submit them to the Government at such times and in such forms as may be prescribed. Inspecting Officers are appointed to inspect these books.

The Government may appoint Inspecting Officers to inspect the books of account of licensees. These officers are empowered to perform duties and exercise such powers as may be prescribed for the purpose of carrying into effect the provisions of the Act.

Any sum due on account of electricity duty, if not paid at the time and in the manner prescribed, shall be deemed to be in arrears, and thereupon such sum, not exceeding twelve per cent per annum which the Government may by general or special order fix, shall be payable on such sum. Any sum together with any interest thereon, shall be recoverable either through a civil court or as an arrear of land revenue. If the sum was payable under section 3, from the licensee; and if the sum was payable under sub-section (1) of section 5, either from the consumer or from the licensee, at the option of the Government.
Provides penalties for licensees who fail to keep books of account or submit returns, or who intentionally obstruct an Inspecting Officer. Penalties can include fines and imprisonment.

Addresses offences committed by companies, including penalties for directors, managers, secretaries, or other officers responsible for the company's business. Defence is available if the company proves the offence was committed without its knowledge or that it exercised all due diligence.

Grants the Government the power to exempt any licensee from the payment of the whole or part of the electricity duty for such period and subject to such terms and conditions as may be specified in a notification.

States that the Act shall not be taken to impose or authorise the imposition of a duty on the consumption or sale of electricity (whether produced by Government or other persons) which is: (a) consumed by the Government of India or sold to the Government of India for consumption by that Government, or (b) consumed in the construction, maintenance or operation of any railway by the Government of India or sold to that Government for consumption in the construction, maintenance or operation of any railway.

Empowers the Government to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act. These rules can cover the manner of payment of electricity duty, the form of accounts, and the duties and powers of Inspecting Officers.

If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of the Act in consequence of the transition from the provisions of the earlier enactments, the Government may, by notification, make such provisions as appear to it to be necessary or expedient for removing the difficulty.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against any person for anything which is in good faith done or intended to be done under this Act.
Repeals The Madras Electricity Duty Act, 1939 (Act V of 1939) and the Travancore-Cochin Electricity Duty Act, 1950 (Act IV of 1950).

important_rules: Every licensee shall, every month, pay to the Government a duty at the rate of 6 naye Paise per unit of energy sold at a price of more than 12 naye Paise per unit.
Every consumer shall pay every month to the Government, in the prescribed manner, a duty calculated at the rate specified against their class in the schedule.
Licensees shall collect and pay the electricity duty levied on consumers to the Government.
Any sum due on account of electricity duty, if not paid at the time and in the manner prescribed, shall be deemed to be in arrears and shall bear interest not exceeding twelve per cent per annum.
The Government may exempt any licensee from the payment of duty under such terms and conditions as it may impose.

penalties: Failure to keep books of account or submit returns: fine which may extend to one thousand rupees.
Intentionally obstructing an Inspecting Officer: fine which may extend to one thousand rupees.
Offences by companies: liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Inspecting Officers appointed by the Government, and the Government itself.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspection of books of account, collection and recovery of duty, imposition of penalties for non-compliance and obstruction, and legal proceedings for offences.

rights: Consumers have the right to be charged electricity duty as per the prescribed rates and schedules.
Licensees have the right to collect electricity duty from consumers.
Licensees have the right to recover unpaid duty as arrears of land revenue.
Individuals acting in good faith under the Act are protected from legal proceedings.
duties: Licensees have the duty to collect and pay electricity duty to the Government.
Licensees have the duty to maintain books of account as prescribed.
Consumers have the duty to pay the electricity duty levied on them.
Companies and their officers have a duty to ensure compliance with the Act.
obligations: Licensees are obligated to adhere to the rates of duty specified.
Licensees are obligated to comply with the procedures for collection and payment of duty.
Consumers are obligated to pay the prescribed duty on energy consumed.

key_procedures: Monthly collection and payment of electricity duty by licensees to the Government.
Procedure for recovery of unpaid duty as arrears of land revenue with interest.
Inspection of licensee's books of account by Inspecting Officers.
Process for seeking exemption from duty by the Government.
administration: The Government of Kerala (implied, as it is the Kerala Electricity Duty Act).
important_notes: The Act repeals The Madras Electricity Duty Act, 1939, and The Travancore-Cochin Electricity Duty Act, 1950.
The Government has the power to exempt certain consumers or licensees from paying the duty.
The Act provides for penalties for offences committed by licensees and companies.
The Government has the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.
No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against any person for anything done in good faith under this Act.

title: The Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature (Amendment) Act, 1989
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature Act, 1976.
scope: Applies to Members of the Kerala Legislature.

main_sections.description: (1) This Act may be called the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature (Amendment) Act, 1989. (2) Clause (1) of section 2 shall come into force at once and clause (11) thereof shall be deemed to have come into force on the 15th day of January, 1987.

In section 2 of the Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature Act, 1976 (Act 46 of 1976),— (i) after sub-section (1C) the following sub-section shall be inserted, namely:— "(1D) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, a person entitled to pension under sub-section (1) shall also be entitled to receive the full amount of pension payable to him or her as spouse under sub-section (1A) or sub-section (1B) or sub-section (1C)."; (ii) in the Explanation to the proviso to sub-section (2), for the words, brackets and letters "clauses (a) and (aa)", the word, brackets and letter "clause (a)" shall be substituted.

important_rules: A person entitled to pension under sub-section (1) shall also be entitled to receive the full amount of pension payable to him or her as spouse under sub-section (1A) or sub-section (1B) or sub-section (1C).
In the Explanation to the proviso to sub-section (2), the word, brackets and letter "clause (a)" shall be substituted for "clauses (a) and (aa)".

rights: Right to receive full amount of pension as spouse under specific sub-sections.

important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 22nd day of August, 1989 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 786 dated the 24th August, 1989.

title: The Kerala Payment of Pension to Members of Legislature Act, 1976
purpose: An Act to provide for the payment of pension to persons who have been Members of the Legislature.
scope: Applies to persons who have been Members of the Legislature of Kerala.

key_definitions.legislature: Refers to the Legislative Assembly of Kerala or its predecessors.
key_definitions.pension: Payment made to former members of the legislature under specific conditions.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and when it comes into force.

Defines the conditions and amounts of pension payable to former members of the Legislature. It specifies eligibility criteria based on periods of service and other offices held, and outlines provisions for additional pension and explanations of terms like 'salary'.

Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of the Act, including the form of application, required certificates, and any other necessary matters. It also specifies the procedure for laying rules before the Legislative Assembly.

important_rules: Members who have served for a period of five years after August 15, 1947, are eligible for pension.
Eligibility criteria include membership in the Kerala Legislative Assembly, former State Legislatures of Travancore-Cochin and Madras, and the Legislative Council of the former State of Madras.
Partly as a member referred to in any preceding clauses and partly as a member referred to in any one or more of the other preceding clauses also qualifies for pension.
An additional pension of fifty rupees per mensem for every year in excess of five, but not exceeding four hundred and fifty rupees per mensem, is payable.
A person is deemed to have served as a member of a Legislative Assembly during the period when that Legislative Assembly remains suspended under Article 356 of the Constitution of India.

Persons entitled to pension under sub-section (2) of Section 2, such as those elected to the office of the President or Vice-President of India or appointed to the Office of the Governor, or becoming a member of the Council of States or the House of the People, or the Legislative Assembly of any State or Union Territory, or constituted under Section 3 of the Delhi Administration Act, 1966, or employed on a salary under the Government of India or any State Government or any corporation owned or controlled by them, are not entitled to any pension under sub-section (1) for the period during which they continue to hold such office or are employed.
If the salary payable to such person is less than the pension payable, they are entitled to receive only the difference.

Persons entitled to pension under sub-section (1) are also entitled to pension from the Government of India or any State Government or any corporation owned or controlled by the Government of India or any State Government, or any local authority, under any law or otherwise, provided the amount of pension to which he is entitled under such law or otherwise, is equal to or in excess of that to which he is entitled under sub-section (1). If the amount of pension is less, they shall be entitled to pension under that sub-section only of an amount which falls short of the amount of pension to which he is otherwise entitled under that sub-section.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through rules made under the Act and laid before the Legislative Assembly.

rights: Right to receive pension as per the provisions of the Act.
Right to receive additional pension for years of service exceeding five.
duties: Members who hold other offices or are employed on salary are subject to specific conditions regarding pension entitlement.

key_procedures: Application for pension: The form and authority to which application for pension should be made are to be prescribed by rules.
Submission of certificates: Certificates required for pension application will be prescribed by rules.
Rule making and laying: The Government makes rules, which are then laid before the Legislative Assembly for approval or modification.
administration: The Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 28th day of November 1976 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 883, dated 1st December 1976.
The Legislative Assembly has the power to modify or annul any rule made under the Act, but such modification or annulment will not affect the validity of anything previously done under that rule.

title: THE KERALA APPROPRIATION (No. 2) ACT, 1976
purpose: To provide for the authorisation of appropriation of moneys out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala to meet certain expenditure for the financial year ended on the 31st day of March, 1967, in excess of the amount granted for that service and for that year.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala, authorizing appropriation from its Consolidated Fund.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Kerala Appropriation (No. 2) Act, 1976.

main_sections.section_title: Issue of Rs 214 out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala to meet certain excess expenditure for the year ended on the 31st March, 1967.
main_sections.description: Authorizes the issue of Rs 214 from the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala for specified services during the financial year ended on March 31, 1967, in excess of the amount already granted. Details are provided in a schedule.

States that the sum deemed to have been authorized to be paid and applied from and out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala under this Act shall be deemed to have been appropriated for the service and purpose expressed in the Schedule in relation to the financial year ended on March 31, 1967.

important_rules: Appropriation of Rs 214 from the Consolidated Fund for specific services in excess of the granted amount for the financial year ending March 31, 1967.
The sums appropriated are for the services and purposes expressed in the Schedule.
key_procedures: Authorization for the issue of funds from the Consolidated Fund.
Appropriation of these funds for specific services as detailed in the Schedule.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be managed by the State of Kerala's financial administration.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 22nd day of May, 1976 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 313, dated 24th May 1976.

title: The Kerala Appropriation (Vote on Account) Act, 1989
purpose: To authorize the withdrawal of certain sums from and out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala for the services and purposes specified in the Schedule during the financial year 1989-90, pending sanction of the expenditure for the year by law.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and its Consolidated Fund.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and its commencement. It is referred to as the Kerala Appropriation (Vote on Account) Act, 1989.

main_sections.section_title: Issue of Rs. 10,37,64,25,900 out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala
main_sections.description: Authorizes the withdrawal of a specific sum of money from the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala for the services and purposes specified in the Schedule for the financial year 1989-90.

main_sections.section_title: Appropriation of moneys out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala
main_sections.description: Provides for the appropriation of the sums voted by the Legislative Assembly of the State of Kerala for the services and purposes specified in the Schedule.

important_rules: Sums withdrawn must be accounted for according to the provisions of the Constitution and the relevant laws.
The withdrawal is for the financial year 1989-90 and is pending the passing of the Finance Act for that year.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The provisions of the Act are enforced through the financial and legislative processes of the Kerala State Government and Legislature.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through parliamentary approval and budgetary allocation.

duties: Duty of the State Government to manage the Consolidated Fund as per law.
obligations: Obligation to appropriate funds as per the votes of the Legislative Assembly.

key_procedures: Vote on Account: The Legislative Assembly votes on account for a portion of the estimated expenditure for the upcoming financial year.
Appropriation: The sums voted on account are then appropriated from the Consolidated Fund.
Sanction of Expenditure: This vote on account is a provisional measure until the full appropriation bill is passed.
administration: Finance Department, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act is a 'Vote on Account' which means it allows for provisional expenditure before the final budget is approved.
The amounts specified are subject to the final approval of the budget for the financial year 1989-90.
The schedule details the specific amounts for various departments and services.

title: THE KERALA FISHERMEN WELFARE SOCIETIES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1986
purpose: An Act further to amend the Kerala Fishermen Welfare Societies Act, 1980. It is expedient to further amend the Kerala Fishermen Welfare Societies Act, 1980, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala Fishermen Welfare Societies Act, 1980 and amendments made by this Act.

main_sections.description: The Act may be called the Kerala Fishermen Societies (Amendment) Act, 1986 and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 29th day of November, 1984.

In clause (d) of section 2 of the Kerala Fishermen Welfare Societies Act, 1980 (7 of 1981), for the word "Government", the words "Kerala State Co-operative Federation for Fisheries Development" shall be substituted.
In sub-section (4) of section 15 of the principal Act, for the word "Government", the words "Kerala State Co-operative Federation for Fisheries Development" shall be substituted.
In section 32 of the principal Act, after the word "society", the words "or an officer appointed under the provisions of this Act" shall be inserted.

The Kerala Fishermen Welfare Societies (Amendment) Ordinance, 1986 (53 of 1986), is hereby repealed. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 30th day of November, 1986 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 1074 dated 30th November, 1986.

title: THE KERALA MUNICIPAL CORPORATIONS (THIRD AMENDMENT) ACT, 1976
purpose: To provide for the extension of the term of office of the Mayor, Deputy Mayor, Councillors, and members and chairmen of standing committees of the Corporation of the City of Cochin, and to modify temporarily certain provisions of the said Act.
scope: Applies to the Corporation of the City of Cochin.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Municipal Corporations (Third Amendment) Act, 1976. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of June, 1976.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of the term of office of Mayor, Deputy Mayor, Councillors, etc., of the Corporation of the City of Cochin
main_sections.description: Notwithstanding anything contained in the Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, 1961 (30 of 1961) (hereinafter referred to as the said Act), the term of office of the Mayor, the Deputy Mayor and other councillors and the members and chairmen of standing committees of the Corporation of the City of Cochin constituted under the said Act, which expires on the 2nd day of June, 1976, shall extend up to noon on the 2nd day of December, 1976.

main_sections.section_title: Act 30 of 1961 to be modified temporarily

main_sections.description:
(1) The Kerala Municipal Corporations (Third Amendment) Ordinance, 1976 (4 of 1976), is hereby repealed.
(2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the said Ordinance or under the said Act as modified by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act or, as the case may be, under the said Act as modified by this Act.

important_rules: The term of office of the Mayor, Deputy Mayor, Councillors, and members and chairmen of standing committees of the Corporation of the City of Cochin is extended until December 2, 1976.
Elections for the council must be held so that newly elected councillors can take office on December 2, 1976.
The term of office for newly elected councillors will expire on December 2, 1981.
Elections for Mayor and Deputy Mayor will be held at the first council meeting after December 2, 1976.
Elections for chairmen of standing committees will be held at the first meeting of each committee after the Mayor's election.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government (implied for conducting elections and ensuring adherence to the Act)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, 1961, as amended by this Act.

rights: The right of newly elected councillors to enter office on December 2, 1976.
The right to elect a Mayor and Deputy Mayor after December 2, 1976.
duties: The duty of the Government to cause elections to be held.
The duty of the Mayor and Deputy Mayor to be elected at the first meeting of the council after December 2, 1976.

key_procedures: Conducting elections for the council to take effect on December 2, 1976.
Holding the first meeting of the council after December 2, 1976, for the election of the Mayor and Deputy Mayor.
Holding the first meeting of each standing committee after the Mayor's election for the election of the committee chairman.
administration: The Government of Kerala (implied)
important_notes: The Act retroactively came into force on June 1, 1976.
This Act repeals the Kerala Municipal Corporations (Third Amendment) Ordinance, 1976, but validates actions taken under it.
The extension of the term of office is until noon on December 2, 1976.

title: THE KERALA KHADI AND VILLAGE INDUSTRIES BOARD ACT, 1957
purpose: To provide for the organisation, development and regulation of khadi and village industries in the State of Kerala and to constitute a Board to carry out the said objects.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Board: means the Kerala Khadi and Village Industries Board established under section 4
key_definitions.Khadi: means any cloth woven on handlooms in India from cotton, silk or woollen yarn, handspun in India or from a mixture of any two or all of such yarns
key_definitions.prescribed: means prescribed by rules made under this Act
key_definitions.regulations: means regulations made by the Board under this Act
key_definitions.village industries: means all or any of the industries specified in the Schedule to the Khadi and Village Industries Commission Act, 1956 (61 of 1956), and includes any other industry declared by the Government under section 3 to be a village industry.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its extent (State of Kerala), and that it comes into force on a date notified by the Government.
Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'Khadi', 'prescribed', 'regulations', and 'village industries'.
Empowers the Government to declare any industry as a village industry by notification in the Gazette. It also requires a copy of every such notification to be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

Provides for the establishment of the Kerala Khadi and Village Industries Board by notification. Outlines its body corporate status, perpetual succession, common seal, power to acquire and dispose of property, and ability to contract. It also details the composition of the Board (not less than five and not more than seven members) appointed by the Government, and the payment of allowances to the Chairman and other members from the Board's funds.

Allows any member of the Board to resign by giving written notice to the Government. Resignations are effective upon notification in the Gazette, and members are deemed to have vacated their office. It also notes that the Government may remove a member.

main_sections.section_title: Disqualification for appointment on the Board
main_sections.description: Lists grounds for disqualification for appointment or continuation as a member of the Board, including holding profit-making office, unsound mind, insolvency, direct or indirect interest in contracts with the Board, directorship or secretarial roles in incorporated companies or co-operative societies with certain interests, and publishing advertisements relating to the Board.

main_sections.section_title: Removal or suspension of a member
main_sections.description: States that the Government may remove a member for reasons specified, such as refusal to act, becoming incapable, being habitually abusive, absence from meetings for a specified period, ceasing to reside in Kerala, or otherwise unsuitable. It also clarifies that removal under this sub-section does not prevent re-appointment.

main_sections.section_title: Vacancy to be filled in as early as possible
main_sections.description: Mandates that vacancies on the Board should be filled as early as possible, and any disqualification of a member or vacancy is not invalidating to the Board's proceedings.

Declares that no act or proceeding of the Board is invalid due to a defect in its constitution or the disqualification of a chairman or member, provided the member did not participate after their disqualification was known.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of members of staff of Board and conditions of their service
main_sections.description: Grants the Board the power to appoint its staff, with remuneration and conditions of service to be determined by the Government.

Allows the Board to appoint committees from time to time for the purpose of efficiently discharging its functions, specifying the purpose of securing efficient discharge of its functions and particulars regarding the constitution of the Board and the circumstances and requirements of khadi and village industries.

Specifies that the Board shall meet at such times and places as provided by rules, subject to provisions of sub-sections (2) and (3). The Board must meet at least once every three months. Decisions are made by a majority of votes, with the chairman having a casting vote. The Chairman or, in their absence, a member chosen by those present presides over meetings.

Grants the Board the power to enter into and perform all necessary contracts for its purposes. Contracts are made on behalf of the Board by the chairman and other members, and must be executed in the prescribed manner. Unexecuted contracts according to the manner provided are not binding.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office of members of the Board
main_sections.description: States that the term of office of the chairman and other members shall be as prescribed.

Outlines the primary duty of the Board to organize, develop and regulate khadi and village industries, and perform other functions as prescribed by the Government. Specific functions include: starting, encouraging, assisting and running khadi and village industries; helping people by providing them with work; giving monetary accommodation; organizing co-operative societies; conducting training centres; arranging supply of raw materials, tools and implements; arranging for publicity and popularising products; endeavouring to educate public opinion and patronise products; seeking and obtaining advice and guidance; undertaking and researching work; and carrying out other incidental and connected activities.

Confers general powers on the Board for carrying out its functions under the Act, including acquiring and holding movable and immovable property, and leasing or selling such property. It also stipulates that immovable property can only be exercised with previous Government sanction.

main_sections.section_title: Preparation and submission of annual Programme
main_sections.description: Requires the Board to prepare and forward its annual programme to the Government by a specified date each year. The programme should include particulars of the scheme, proposals for the next year's work, and any other prescribed details.
States that the Government may approve and sanction the programme, with or without modifications.
Allows the Board to prepare and forward a supplementary programme for Government sanction, subject to the provisions of section 18.
Allows the Board to transfer buildings, land, or other property to the Government, and to manage them under conditions and restrictions as the Government deems fit.
Empowers the Government to give directions to the Board.

main_sections.section_title: Members of Board and members of staff of Board to be public servants
main_sections.description: Declares members of the Board and its staff to be public servants within the meaning of the Indian Penal Code.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken under Act
main_sections.description: Protects the Government, the Board, its Chairman, members, officers, and servants from legal action for anything done or intended to be done in good faith under the Act.
Grants the Government the power to make rules consistent with the Act.
Grants the Board the power to make regulations consistent with the Act and rules made thereunder.

States that anything done or any action taken under any law in force before the commencement of this Act which is consistent with the provisions of this Act shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

duties: Duty of the Board to organise, develop and regulate khadi and village industries and perform such functions as the Government may prescribe.

key_procedures: Preparation and submission of annual programmes by the Board to the Government.
Sanction of programmes by the Government.
Preparation and submission of supplementary programmes for sanction.
administration: The Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act was enacted by the President in the Eighth Year of the Republic of India.
Published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary dated 27th March 1957.

title: The Koodalmanickam Devaswam (Amendment) Act, 1976
purpose: This act amends the Koodalmanickam Devaswam Act, 1971, to incorporate specific changes related to the administration and management of the Koodalmanickam Devaswam.
scope: This Act applies to the Koodalmanickam Devaswam, its properties, and its administration within the state of Kerala. It specifically amends the provisions of the Koodalmanickam Devaswam Act, 1971.

key_definitions.Board: Refers to the Koodalmanickam Devaswam Board constituted under the principal Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and specifies when it comes into force.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 2 of Act 12 of 1971
main_sections.description: Amends section 2 of the Koodalmanickam Devaswam Act, 1971, likely to modify or add definitions.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 6 of Act 12 of 1971
main_sections.description: Amends section 6 of the principal Act, which likely deals with the composition or powers of the Devaswam Board.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 14 of Act 12 of 1971
main_sections.description: Amends section 14 of the principal Act, which may relate to the functions, powers, or duties of the Devaswam Board.
Inserts a new section, 24A, into the principal Act. This new section will introduce new provisions not previously present.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 28 of Act 12 of 1971
main_sections.description: Amends section 28 of the principal Act, potentially concerning the financial administration, audit, or reporting of the Devaswam.
Provides for the validation of certain actions or decisions taken under the principal Act or previous laws, which might have been irregular.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Act amends specific sections of the Koodalmanickam Devaswam Act, 1971 (Act 12 of 1971), to introduce changes in the governance and administration of the Devaswam.
Rule 2: A new section 24A is inserted into the principal Act, implying the addition of new powers, responsibilities, or procedures for the Devaswam.
Rule 3: The Act includes a validation clause, which regularizes past actions or decisions that might have been made without proper legal authority.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Koodalmanickam Devaswam Board and relevant state authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the amended Koodalmanickam Devaswam Act, 1971, and other applicable laws governing religious endowments in Kerala.

rights: Right to administer the Koodalmanickam Devaswam according to the amended Act.
duties: Duty to manage the affairs of the Devaswam in accordance with the provisions of the Act and its amendments.
Duty to ensure proper financial management and audit.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the amendments introduced by this Act.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Amendments to existing sections (like 2, 6, 14, 28) will alter the established procedures related to definitions, board composition, powers, and financial administration.
Procedure 2: The insertion of section 24A will introduce a new set of procedures governed by this new section.
administration: The Koodalmanickam Devaswam Board, under the oversight of the Kerala State Government.
important_notes: Note 1: The Act is an amendment and relies on the original Koodalmanickam Devaswam Act, 1971, for its full context.
Note 2: The validation section is crucial as it addresses potential legal challenges to past administrative actions.

title: The Koodalmanickam Devaswom Act 1971
purpose: To provide for the better administration, management and improvement of the Koodalmanickam Temple and its connected institutions.
scope: Applies to the Koodalmanickam Temple, its properties, and its connected institutions, and the administration thereof.

key_definitions.Committee: The Committee constituted under section 4 of the Act for the administration of the Devaswom.
key_definitions.Administrator: The Administrator appointed under section 16 of the Act.
key_definitions.Temple Fund: The fund established under section 23 of the Act.

main_sections.description: Requires the Administrator to prepare an annual budget for the Devaswom, which requires the approval of the Committee and the Government. It also outlines procedures for revised or supplementary budgets.
Details the process for submitting revised or supplementary budgets to the Government.
Mandates annual audit of the Devaswom accounts by an auditor appointed by the Government, and specifies the auditor's remuneration.
Establishes the 'Sree Koodalmanickam Temple Fund' and specifies its sources of income and its utilisation for prescribed purposes.
Empowers the Government to call for and examine records of the Devaswom and the Committee, and to pass orders regarding any decision or order found to be irregular.
Grants the Government the power to make rules, by notification in the Gazette, to carry out the purposes of the Act. It lists specific areas for which rules may be made.
Allows the Committee, subject to the approval of the Government, to make regulations consistent with the Act and the rules. It outlines specific areas for which regulations may be provided.
Deals with the Committee's entitlement to take and be in possession of all movable and immovable properties belonging to the Devaswom and outlines procedures for requisitioning property.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection from suits or other legal proceedings against the Government, Committee, or Administrator for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Public officers to furnish copies of or extracts from certain documents
main_sections.description: Obligates public officers in custody of Devaswom records to furnish copies or extracts as required by the Administrator.

main_sections.section_title: Acts of Administrator not to be invalidated
main_sections.description: States that acts of the Administrator are not invalidated due to reasons of appointment or ground not being entitled to hold or continue office.

main_sections.section_title: Certain rights and privileges of Kaimal not to be affected
main_sections.description: Clarifies that certain rights and privileges of the Kaimal are not affected by this Act.

States that nothing in the Act shall affect express provisions of this Act or rules made thereunder, or any honour, emolument or perquisite to any person or established usage in regard to other matters.
Grants the Government the power to make provisions by order for the purpose of removing any difficulty arising in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Repeals the Koodalmanickam Devaswom Proclamation (Cochin) issued on 30th November, 1917, and the scheme of management published thereunder, and saves actions taken under the repealed proclamation.
