important_rules: The Administrator must prepare an annual budget of receipts and expenditure for the Devaswom.
The budget, after approval by the Committee, must be submitted to the Government before a prescribed date.
Before sanctioning a budget, the Government must satisfy itself that adequate provision has been made for the maintenance of the Devaswom and for meeting its liabilities.
The Government may modify any part of the budget to ensure such provisions are made.

The decision of the Government sanctioning the budget, subject to modifications, must be communicated to the Committee at least fifteen days before the commencement of the year to which the budget relates.
No alteration shall be made in the working balance without the consent of the Government.
The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make rules to carry out the purposes of this Act, providing for matters like management of the Devaswom, allowances, custody of records, etc.

The Committee may, subject to Government approval, make regulations not inconsistent with the Act and rules, covering areas like conditions of service, observance of rites, and other matters for the purposes of the Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government, the Committee, and the Administrator, as per their respective powers and duties under the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the preparation and sanction of budgets, audit of accounts, making of rules and regulations, revision of decisions, and protection of actions taken in good faith. The Act also provides for the requisitioning of property and the protection of actions taken in good faith.

rights: The Committee has the right to take and be in possession of all movable and immovable properties belonging to the Devaswom.
The Committee has the right to requisition property.
The Administrator has the right to call for and examine records of the Devaswom and the Committee.
Public officers have a duty to furnish copies or extracts of Devaswom records when required by the Administrator.
duties: The Administrator has a duty to prepare an annual budget.
The Administrator has a duty to audit the accounts of the Devaswom.
The Committee has a duty to manage the affairs of the Devaswom in accordance with the Act and rules.
obligations: The Devaswom must ensure adequate provision is made in the budget for its maintenance and liabilities.

key_procedures: Budget preparation, submission, and sanction process involving the Administrator, Committee, and Government.
Audit of Devaswom accounts by a Government-appointed auditor.
Rule-making by the Government and regulation-making by the Committee.
Procedure for requisitioning property by the Collector on behalf of the Committee or Administrator.
Process for the repeal of previous proclamations and saving of actions taken thereunder.
administration: The administration of the Koodalmanickam Devaswom is overseen by the Committee and the Administrator, under the overall authority of the Government.
important_notes: The Act repeals the Koodalmanickam Devaswom Proclamation (Cochin) issued on 30th November, 1917.
Actions taken under the repealed proclamation are deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.
Certain rights and privileges of the Kaimal are preserved.
The Government has the power to make provisions to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
Protection is provided for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

title: THE KOODALMANICKOM DEVASWOM PROCLAMATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1957
purpose: To amend The Koodalmanickom Devaswom Proclamation (Cochin) dated the 30th November, 1917, and the scheme of management suspended thereunder.
scope: The Koodalmanickom Devaswom Proclamation and its scheme of management.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Koodalmanickom Devaswom Proclamation (Amendment) Act, 1957 and it shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

Amends clause (b) of section 3 of the Koodalmanickom Devaswom Proclamation (Cochin) dated the 30th November, 1917. It substitutes a new clause (b) defining 'controlling authority' as meaning such authority, officer or person as may be appointed, from time to time, by the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the scheme of management.
main_sections.description: Amends the scheme of management appended to the Proclamation by omitting specific words and figures from Articles 4 and 5, and also omitting Article 9 entirely.

important_rules: The Act commences on a date appointed by the Government via notification in the Gazette.
The definition of 'controlling authority' is amended to include persons appointed by the Government.
Specific provisions related to the scheme of management are amended by omission.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By notification in the Gazette.

key_procedures: Appointment of a controlling authority by the Government.
Government notification in the Gazette for commencement of the Act.
Amendments to the scheme of management are implemented by omission of specified text.
administration: Government (implied through appointment of controlling authority and notification)
important_notes: The Koodalmanickom Devaswom Proclamation (Cochin) was dated 30th November, 1917.
The scheme of management was suspended thereunder.
The Preamble mentions the British Resident in the former States of Travancore and Cochin as the controlling authority prior to this amendment.

title: THE KOODALMANICKAM DEVASWOM ACT, 2005
purpose: To provide for the proper administration of the Koodalmanickam Devaswom at Irinjalakuda.
scope: Applies to the Koodalmanickam Temple at Irinjalakuda and its properties and endowments. It aims to ensure the proper administration and management of the Devaswom.

key_definitions.Commissioner: An officer not below the rank of the Secretary to Government, who professes the Hindu Religion and believes in Temple worship, appointed by the Government, by notification in the Gazette, to be the Commissioner for the purposes of this Act.
key_definitions.Committee: The Koodalmanickam Devaswom Managing Committee constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.Court: The District Court having jurisdiction over the area in which the Temple is situated.
key_definitions.Devaswom: The Temple, and includes its properties and endowments and the subordinate temples attached thereto.
key_definitions.Hindu: A person who is a believer in God and temple worship or any person Hindu by religion or in any sect.
key_definitions.Person having interest in the Temple: Means a person who is entitled to perform worship or to do service in the temple or who is in the habit of performance of worship or service in the temple or entitled to partake, or is in the habit of partaking, in the benefit of the distribution of Temple favours thereof.
key_definitions.Prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Koodalmanickam Devaswom Act, 2005 and it shall come into force at once.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including Administrator, Commissioner, Committee, Court, Devaswom, Hindu, Person having interest in the Temple, Prescribed, Temple, Scheduled Caste, and Scheduled Tribe.
States that the administration, control and management of the Devaswom shall be vested in a Committee constituted in the manner hereinafter provided.

Details the composition of the Committee, including nomination of members by the Government, representation from Thantri, employees, and nomination by the Hindu in the Council of Ministers. It also outlines disqualifications for membership.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office of Non-official members, resignation and removal of such members and casual vacancies arising in their places
main_sections.description: Specifies the term of office for non-official members, procedures for resignation and removal, and how casual vacancies are filled.
Outlines the conditions under which the Government can supersede the Committee and the subsequent procedures.
Details the requirements for meetings of the Committee, including location, quorum, and decision-making processes.

main_sections.section_title: Acts or proceedings of the Committee not to be invalidated
main_sections.description: States that the acts or proceedings of the Committee shall not be invalidated due to any vacancy, defect, or irregularity.

main_sections.section_title: Remuneration of the Chairman and Members
main_sections.description: Addresses the remuneration of the Chairman and members of the Committee.

Encompasses the duties of the Committee, including the arrangement for proper performance of rites and ceremonies, providing facilities for worshippers, ensuring the safe custody of funds and properties, and maintaining hygienic conditions.
Likely covers the procedures for the alienation of Devaswom properties.

main_sections.section_title: Limitation of power for borrowing and lending
main_sections.description: Likely addresses the powers of the Devaswom regarding borrowing and lending.
Likely requires the preparation and submission of an administration report.
Covers the appointment of an Administrator.
Details the conditions of service for the Administrator.

main_sections.section_title: Holding Additional charge of the Office of the Administrator
main_sections.description: Addresses situations where an Administrator might hold additional charge.
Outlines the powers and duties of the Administrator.
Likely related to the staff and establishment of the Devaswom.
Covers the appointment of officers and employees of the Devaswom.

main_sections.section_title: Fixing of Standard scales of Expenditure
main_sections.description: Likely relates to setting standard scales for expenditure.
Covers the preparation and approval of the budget.
Addresses the process for revised or supplementary budgets.
Covers the maintenance of accounts and the audit process.

main_sections.section_title: Authority to whom audit report is to be submitted
main_sections.description: Specifies the authority to whom the audit report should be submitted.
Details the information to be included in the audit report.

main_sections.section_title: Rectification of defects disclosed in audit and order of surcharge against committee, etc.
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for rectifying defects found in audit and imposing surcharges.

main_sections.section_title: Authority of Committee to incur expenditure for certain purposes
main_sections.description: Grants authority to the Committee to incur expenditure for specified purposes.

main_sections.section_title: Committee to be in possession of Devaswom Properties
main_sections.description: Ensures the Committee's possession of Devaswom properties.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of Action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Public offices to furnish copies, etc. or certain documents
main_sections.description: Likely mandates public offices to provide copies of documents.
Covers the costs associated with proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Notifications, Orders etc., not to be questioned in court of law
main_sections.description: States that notifications and orders issued under the Act are generally not challengeable in courts.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to call for records and pass orders
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to call for records and pass orders.
Contains provisions for saving certain existing rights or actions.

main_sections.section_title: Thantri to be final authority in religious matters
main_sections.description: Designates the Thantri as the final authority in religious matters.
Empowers the Government to make rules under the Act.
Empowers the Committee or other authorities to make regulations.
Provides a mechanism for removing difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of previous enactments and savings.

important_rules: Rule 1: Members of the Committee shall, before entering their office, make an oath in writing with signature before the Commissioner in the form: 'I, ............ do swear in the name of God that I profess the Hindu Religion and believe in Temple worship and I do not believe in the practice of untouchability'.
Rule 2: The Committee shall establish its office at such place or places at Irinjalakuda as the Committee may determine, for the transaction of its business.
Rule 3: No business shall be transacted in any meeting of the Committee unless at least three members thereof are present.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Likely the Administrator, Commissioner, and the Committee, with oversight from the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, including the appointment of an Administrator, constitution of a Committee, audit, and potential legal proceedings for non-compliance.

rights: Right to worship and perform service in the temple for eligible individuals.
Right to receive benefits from the distribution of temple favours.
duties: Duty of the Committee to arrange for the proper performance of rites and ceremonies.
Duty of the Committee to provide facilities for worshippers.
Duty of the Committee to ensure the safe custody of funds, valuable securities and jewellery and the preservation and management of the properties vested in the Temple.
Duty of the Committee to ensure maintenance of order and discipline and proper hygienic conditions in the temple and the subordinate temples.
Duty of the Committee to maintain the proper standard of cleanliness and purity in the offerings performed within the temple.
Duty of the Committee to ensure that the funds of the endowments of the Temple are spent according to the known wishes of the donors.
Duty of the Committee to make provisions for the payment of suitable emoluments to the salaried staff of the Devaswom.
Duty of the Committee to do all such things as may be incidental and conducive to the efficient management of the affairs of the Devaswom and for the facilities of the worshippers.
obligations: Obligation for members of the Committee to take an oath professing Hindu Religion and believing in Temple worship.
Obligation for public offices to furnish copies of certain documents.
Obligation for the Committee to be in possession of Devaswom Properties.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Appointment of Administrator, detailing their conditions of service, powers, and duties.
Procedure 2: Constitution and functioning of the Koodalmanickam Devaswom Managing Committee, including composition, term of office, meetings, and duties.
Procedure 3: Budget preparation, accounting, and audit processes, including rectification of defects and surcharges.
Procedure 4: Supersession of the Committee by the Government under specified circumstances.
Procedure 5: The process for making rules and regulations under the Act.
administration: The Koodalmanickam Devaswom Managing Committee, with an Administrator appointed under its supervision, and oversight from the Government.
important_notes: The Act was enacted to provide for the proper administration of the Koodalmanickam Devaswom at Irinjalakuda.
The preamble highlights the historical significance of the Koodalmanickam Temple and the need for its proper management.
Certain provisions of the Act have retrospective effect.
The Thantri is considered the final authority in religious matters.
The Koodalmanickam Devaswom Act, 1971, was enacted to provide better management of the Devaswom in supersession of all previous laws and arrangements.
The Act acknowledges the Supreme Court's judgment regarding the Koodalmanickam Devaswom Act, 1971, and the High Court of Kerala's judgment.
The received assent of the President on the 10th August, 2007 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No 1556 dated 23rd August, 2007.

title: The Kottayam Electric Supply Agency (Undertaking) Acquisition Act, 1980
purpose: To provide for the acquisition of the undertaking of the Kottayam Electric Supply Agency.
scope: The Act applies to the undertaking of the Kottayam Electric Supply Agency, which is engaged in the supply of electrical energy in the areas falling under the jurisdiction of the Kottayam Municipal Council.

key_definitions.Board: means the Kerala State Electricity Board constituted under section 5 of the Electricity Supply Act
key_definitions.document: means account books, records, registers, maps, plans, drawings, records of survey and all other documents of whatever nature relating to the undertaking
key_definitions.Electricity Act: means the Indian Electricity Act, 1910 (Central Act 9 of 1910)
key_definitions.Electricity Supply Act: means the Electricity Supply Act, 1948 (Central Act 54 of 1948)
key_definitions.fixed assets: includes works, spare parts, stores, stocks, instruments, tools, motor and other vehicles, office equipments and furniture
key_definitions.licence: means the Kottayam Electric Licence, 1105, granted under the Travancore Electricity Act of 1907 M. E
key_definitions.licensee: means the holder of the licence
key_definitions.prescribed: means prescribed by rules made under this Act
key_definitions.undertaking: means the undertaking of the Kottayam Electric Supply Agency
key_definitions.works: means electric supply lines and any lands, buildings, workshops, projects, machinery, plants or apparatus required to supply electricity and to carry into effect the objects of the licence

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kottayam Electric Supply Agency (Undertaking) Acquisition Act, 1980. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 13th day of February, 1980.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including Board, document, Electricity Act, Electricity Supply Act, fixed assets, licence, licensee, prescribed, undertaking, and works.

Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force or in any contract or other document, with effect from the appointed day, the undertaking shall, by virtue of this Act, stand transferred to and vest in the Government.
The undertaking vested in the Government under section 3 shall be deemed to include the properties, rights, liabilities and obligations specified below.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of undertaking to the Board
main_sections.description: The Government may, by order in writing, transfer the undertaking vested in the Government under section 3 to the Board on such terms and conditions as may be specified in the order, and on such transfer, the undertaking, together will all assets, liabilities, rights, and obligations by virtue of this Act have vested in or devolved on the Government shall vest in or devolve on the Board.
For the transfer, and vesting in, the Government, the Government shall pay to the licensee an amount as determined.

main_sections.section_title: Gross amount payable to the licensee
main_sections.description: The market value of the undertaking on the appointed day and any difference of dispute regarding market value shall be determined by an appointed arbitrator.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of transactions not bona fide
main_sections.description: Where the Government is of the opinion that the licensee has not acted bona fide, the Government may deduct from the amount payable to the licensee any amount which it considers to be a loss sustained by the Government.

The Government shall be entitled to deduct from the gross amount payable to the licensee, amounts like advance payments, interest, advances from consumers, amounts due from consumers, loans to financial institutions, and remaining amounts in Tariffs and Dividends Funds.

main_sections.section_title: Manner of payment of net amount
main_sections.description: The Government shall appoint a Special Officer to assess the net amount payable under this Act and to assist in assessing the net amount payable.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of services of existing employees
main_sections.description: Every whole time officer or other employee who was immediately before the appointed day employed in connection with the undertaking shall, on and from the appointed day, become an employee of the Government or the Board, and their service conditions shall remain the same unless altered by the Government or the Board.
Any employee of the Government or the Board authorized by general or special order may, at any time, enter any land, premises, or other place for inspection or investigation.

main_sections.section_title: Duty to deliver possession of properties etc.
main_sections.description: Every person in possession, custody or control of any property appertaining to the undertaking, which has been transferred, shall, on demand by the Government or the Board, deliver the property to the Government or the Board.

Penalties for wrongfully withholding property, failing to deliver property, or removing or destroying property belonging to the undertaking. Imprisonment for up to two years or fine up to ten thousand rupees or both.
If an offence is committed by a company, every person in charge of the conduct of the business of the company, as well as the company, shall be deemed guilty and liable to be proceeded against.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against the Government or any officer or employee for anything done or intended to be done in good faith in pursuance of this Act or any rule or order made thereunder.
The provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent contained in the Electricity Act, the Electricity Supply Act, or any other Act.
The Government may, by notification, provide anything necessary to remove difficulties arising in giving effect to the provisions of this Act.

No court shall take cognizance of any offence under this Act except on a complaint made by the Government or an authorized officer.  Magistrates of the First Class specially empowered may impose a fine not exceeding five thousand rupees when awarding punishment under section 14.
The Government may make rules to carry out the purposes of this Act.
The Government shall have the power to make rules for the purpose of carrying out the provisions of this Act.

Any law corresponding to the provisions of this Act in force immediately before the commencement of this Act shall stand repealed and the provisions of section 6 of the General Clauses Act, 1897, shall apply to such repeal.

important_rules: Employees of the undertaking are transferred to the Government or the Board with their existing terms and conditions of service.
Employees transferred shall not be entitled to any compensation for the transfer of their services.
The Government or the Board can authorize employees to enter any premises related to the undertaking for inspection or investigation.
All properties, assets, and records of the undertaking must be delivered to the Government or the Board upon demand.

penalties: Wrongfully withholding property, failing to deliver property, or removing/destroying property: imprisonment up to two years or a fine up to ten thousand rupees or both.
Offences by companies: liable to punishment as if committed by individuals.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government and its authorized officers/employees.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings, imposition of penalties, and the exercise of powers of entry and demand for delivery of property.

rights: Right to acquire the undertaking.
Right to determine the amount payable to the licensee.
Right to deduct amounts for specific reasons (e.g., bad faith transactions).
Right to appoint a Special Officer for assessment.
Right of entry for inspection.
Right to demand delivery of properties.
duties: Duty to provide for the acquisition of the undertaking.
Duty to pay the determined amount to the licensee.
Duty to transfer employees.
Duty to deliver possession of properties and records.
obligations: The Government has obligations to the employees transferred from the undertaking.
The Government or Board has obligations regarding the management and operation of the acquired undertaking.

key_procedures: Vesting of the undertaking in the Government on the appointed day.
Transfer of the undertaking from the Government to the Board, if ordered.
Determination of the gross amount payable to the licensee.
Deduction of specific amounts from the gross amount.
Appointment of a Special Officer to assess the net amount payable.
Payment of the net amount to the licensee.
Transfer of employees.
Delivery of possession of properties and records to the Government or Board.
Initiation of legal proceedings for penalties.
Cognizance of offences by courts upon complaint by the Government or authorized officer.
administration: The Government of Kerala and the Kerala State Electricity Board.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the President on 27th day of March 1980 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 224 dated 27th March 1980.
The Act has effect notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the Indian Electricity Act, 1910, or the Electricity Supply Act, 1948, or any other law.
The Government has the power to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
Offences under section 14 can be tried by Magistrates of the First Class specially empowered.

title: The Kovalam Palace (Taking Over By Resumption) Act, 2005
purpose: To provide for taking over by resumption of the historic site of Kovalam Palace and the surrounding buildings and lands by the Government of Kerala, ensuring their preservation as a tourist attraction and for public tourism.
scope: The Act applies to the historic site of Kovalam Palace and the surrounding buildings and lands, and to the Government of Kerala, its officials, and persons involved in the management or possession of the property.

key_definitions.Commissioner: Means the Commissioner of Payment of compensation appointed under section 6.
key_definitions.Kovalam Palace: Means the Palace known as Halcyon Castle constructed by the Regent, Maharani Sethulekshmi Bai of Travancore in the land in Survey No 7/1 of Vizhinjam Village of Neyyattinkara Taluk in Thiruvananthapuram District and the surrounding buildings and lands measuring 4.13 30 hectares.
key_definitions.Prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as The Kovalam Palace (Taking over by Resumption) Act, 2005, and states it came into force on the 25th day of September, 2004.
Provides definitions for 'Commissioner', 'Government', 'Kovalam Palace', and 'Prescribed'.

main_sections.section_title: Taking over by resumption of Kovalam Palace
main_sections.description: States that notwithstanding anything in any other law, the Kovalam Palace, its historic site, buildings and lands shall stand transferred to and vest in the Government, free from encumbrances and the right title and interest of all other persons, from the date of commencement of the Act. It also clarifies that any person in possession of the property shall be deemed to have taken under the provisions of this Act and on the 27th day of September, 2004.

Confirms that notwithstanding anything in any other law, all contracts or arrangements relating to the historic site of Kovalam Palace are deemed to have been terminated upon commencement. Persons in charge of the historic site are deemed to have vacated their charge.

Deals with the payment of compensation for improvements made to the historic site of Kovalam Palace and the value of any interest which may have accrued in favour of any person from the date of handing over of possession to the Government in 1970. Compensation is to be given by the Government following prescribed principles.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of Commissioner of Payment of Compensation
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to appoint a Commissioner for the purpose of payment of compensation and to appoint other officers to assist the Commissioner. The salaries and allowances of the Commissioner and other persons appointed are to be defrayed from the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala.

main_sections.section_title: Claims to be made to the Commissioner
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for any person having a right to compensation to prefer a claim to the Commissioner. The Commissioner is to examine claims, give an opportunity of being heard, and apply principles for determining compensation. The Commissioner is also empowered to regulate his own procedure and to make inquiries out of the exercise of his powers.
Allows claimants to appeal the decision of the Commissioner within thirty days from the date of knowledge of the decision to the Principal District Court of Thiruvananthapuram.

States that the provisions of this Act or any rule thereunder shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any other law or any instrument having effect by virtue of any law other than this Act or in any decree or order of any Court or other authority.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides that no suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against the Government or any of its officers or employees for any act or omission done or intended to be done under the Act.

Except as otherwise provided, no Civil Court shall have jurisdiction to decide or deal with any question or to determine any matter which is, by or under this Act, required to be decided or dealt with or to be determined by the Commissioner or any other officer.
Empowers the Government to make rules by notification in the Official Gazette to carry out the purposes of the Act. Such rules, when made, shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

Grants the Government the power to make orders to remove any difficulties arising in giving effect to the provisions of the Act, provided such orders are not inconsistent with the provisions of the Act.

Validates certain actions taken in Government Order G.O.(P) No. 302/2004/RD dated 25th September, 2004, concerning the taking possession of Kovalam Palace and its surrounding buildings and lands, and any subsequent ordinances or proceedings.
Repeals The Kovalam Palace (Taking over by Resumption) Ordinance, 2005 (6 of 2005) and saves any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the said Ordinance.

important_rules: The Kovalam Palace (Taking over by Resumption) Act, 2005 came into force on September 25, 2004.
All persons in charge of the historic site of Kovalam Palace are deemed to have vacated their charge on the commencement of the Act.
Rules made under the Act must be laid before the Legislative Assembly.
Any difficulties in implementing the Act can be resolved by Government orders, provided they do not contradict the Act.
The Kovalam Palace (Taking over by Resumption) Ordinance, 2005 is repealed.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala and the Commissioner of Payment of Compensation.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the vesting of the property in the Government, appointment of a Commissioner to handle compensation claims, and by overriding other laws.

rights: Any person having a right to compensation has the right to prefer a claim to the Commissioner.
Claimants have the right to an opportunity of being heard by the Commissioner.
Claimants have the right to appeal the Commissioner's decision to the Principal District Court.
duties: Persons in possession of the historic site of Kovalam Palace have a duty to vacate their charge.
The Government has a duty to pay compensation for improvements made to the historic site.
obligations: The Government is obligated to ensure the historic site is served for the public purpose and in particular by retaining the Kovalam Palace and the surrounding lands as objects of historic interest and heritage site.

key_procedures: Filing a claim for compensation with the Commissioner.
Examination of claims by the Commissioner, including hearing the affected person.
Determination of payable compensation by the Commissioner.
Appealing the Commissioner's decision to the Principal District Court.
administration: The Government of Kerala, through departments responsible for tourism and land management, and the Commissioner of Payment of Compensation.
important_notes: The Act has overriding effect over other laws.
No legal proceedings can be taken against the Government or its officers for actions taken in good faith under the Act.
Civil Courts are barred from jurisdiction on matters to be decided by the Commissioner or other designated officers.

title: THE LAND ACQUISITION (KERALA AMENDMENT) ACT, 1985
purpose: To amend the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, in its application to the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Land Acquisition (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1985, extends to the whole of the State of Kerala, and came into force on the 17th day of April, 1985.
Amends section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (Central Act I of 1894) by inserting specific words related to "appropriate Government", "Board of Revenue", "Collector", and "locality".
Substitutes a new sub-section (2) for section 5A of the principal Act, detailing the process for the Collector to make a report on objections received regarding land acquisition.
Amends section 6 of the principal Act by inserting specific words related to "appropriate Government" and "Board of Revenue" or "Secretary of the Board of Revenue".
Amends section 7 of the principal Act by inserting specific words related to "appropriate Government" or "Board of Revenue".

Amends section 17 of the principal Act by inserting specific words related to "appropriate Government", "District Collector", "Board of Revenue", and the substitution of phrases like "the appropriate Government may direct" and "the case may be, may direct".

Repeals The Land Acquisition (Kerala Amendment) Ordinance, 1985. It also states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

key_procedures: Objection handling: If objections are received concerning land acquisition, the Collector must submit a report to the Government after giving a hearing to the objector and considering their arguments. (Section 5A)
Notification process: When an acquisition is notified under section 4, the Government or the Board of Revenue may issue further instructions regarding proceedings. (Section 4)
Decision making: The Government or the Board of Revenue is responsible for making decisions on objections and related proceedings in land acquisition cases. (Section 4)
important_notes: The Act came into force on the 17th day of April, 1985. (Section 1)
The amendments made by this Act are to the principal Act, which is The Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (Central Act I of 1894). (Preamble, Section 2)
The repeal of the Ordinance does not affect actions taken under it prior to the commencement of this Act. (Section 7)

title: THE LEGISLATIVE ASSEMBLY (REMOVAL OF DISQUALIFICATIONS) AMENDMENT ACT, 1968
purpose: To further amend the Legislative Assembly (Removal of Disqualifications) Act, 1951, for purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Legislative Assembly of Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Legislative Assembly (Removal of Disqualifications) Amendment Act, 1968, and it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of January, 1968.

Amends section 2 of the Legislative Assembly (Removal of Disqualifications) Act, 1951. It inserts the word "or" at the end of clause (vi) and adds new clauses (vii) and (viii). Clause (vii) specifies holding the office of Chairman or member of the Kerala State Law Commission as not causing disqualification. Clause (viii) specifies being the Chairman or Vice-Chairman or a member of the State Planning Board or the Backward Classes Reservation Commission constituted by the Government as not causing disqualification.

important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary, No. 94 dated 20th April, 1968.

title: The Legislative Assembly (Removal of Disqualifications) (Amendment) Act, 1983
purpose: To amend The Legislative Assembly (Removal of Disqualifications) Act, 1951 for the purpose hereinafter appearing.
scope: The Act applies to the Legislative Assembly of Kerala, its members, and the provisions of The Legislative Assembly (Removal of Disqualifications) Act, 1951.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Legislative Assembly (Removal of Disqualifications) Amendment Act, 1983. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of November, 1982.

Amends section 2 of the Legislative Assembly (Removal of Disqualifications) Act, 1951. Specifically, in clause (ii) of sub-section (2) after the words "the Chairman", the words "or Vice-Chairman" shall be inserted.

Repeals The Legislative Assembly (Removal of Disqualifications) Amendment Ordinance, 1983 (22 of 1983). Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 4th day of January, 1984, and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 23 dated the 6th January 1984.

title: THE LEGISLATIVE ASSEMBLY (REMOVAL OF DISQUALIFICATIONS) AMENDMENT ACT, 1979
purpose: To further amend the Legislative Assembly (Removal of Disqualifications) Act, 1951.
scope: Applies to the Legislative Assembly of Kerala.

key_definitions.Government Company: Means a company in which not less than fifty-one per cent of the paid up share capital is held by the Government of Kerala or jointly by the Central Government and the Government of Kerala, and includes a company which is a subsidiary of any such company; or a Corporation established or constituted by or under any Central or State Act and owned or controlled by the Government of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Legislative Assembly (Removal of Disqualifications) Amendment Act, 1979.

Amends Section 2 of the Legislative Assembly (Removal of Disqualifications) Act, 1951. It renumbers sub-section (1) and inserts a new sub-section (2) which states that no person shall be disqualified or deemed ever to have been disqualified for being chosen as, and for being, a member of the Legislative Assembly of the State of Kerala by reason only of the fact that they hold or have held the office of the Chairman of a Government Company.

Repeals the Legislative Assembly (Removal of Disqualifications) Amendment Ordinance, 1978, but states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act if this Act had come into force on the 29th day of December, 1978.

important_rules: A person holding the office of Chairman of a Government Company is not disqualified from being a member of the Legislative Assembly of Kerala.
Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are validated if they align with this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Implicitly, the Legislative Assembly and relevant governmental bodies for matters of disqualification.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application of the Act's provisions regarding disqualifications of members.

rights: Right of individuals to be members of the Legislative Assembly without being disqualified solely for holding the office of Chairman of a Government Company.

key_procedures: Amendment of existing law through legislative process.
Validation of past actions taken under a previous Ordinance.
administration: Implied to be under the purview of the Legislature of Kerala and related government departments.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 26th March, 1979.
Published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 221, dated 27th March, 1979.
The Act, when enacted, was deemed to have come into force on December 29, 1978.

title: The Legislative Assembly (Removal of Disqualifications) Amendment Act, 1957
purpose: To amend The Legislative Assembly (Removal of Disqualifications) Act, 1951, to remove certain disqualifications for membership of the Legislative Assembly of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the Legislative Assembly of Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Legislative Assembly (Removal of Disqualifications) Amendment Act, 1957.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 2, Act XV of 1951
main_sections.description: Amends section 2 of the Legislative Assembly (Removal of Disqualifications) Act, 1951, by adding a new clause (vi) to the existing clause (v). This new clause (vi) specifies that a person is not disqualified if he is a member of the Air Defence Reserve or the Auxiliary Air Force raised under the Reserve and Auxiliary Air Forces Act, 1952.

important_rules: Rule: A person is not disqualified from being a member of the Legislative Assembly if they are a member of the Air Defence Reserve or the Auxiliary Air Force raised under the Reserve and Auxiliary Air Forces Act, 1952.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not specified in the provided text.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not specified in the provided text.

rights: Right to be a member of the Legislative Assembly without disqualification if meeting the conditions of this amendment.

administration: Not specified in the provided text.
important_notes: The Act was enacted by the President in the Seventh Year of the Republic of India.
The amendment is made in exercise of the powers conferred by section 3 of the Kerala State Legislature (Delegation of Powers) Act, 1956.
Published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 12-11-1957.

title: The Legislative Assembly of Travancore-Cochin (Removal of Disqualifications) Amendment Act, 1954
act_number: Act XV of 1951 (amended by Act X of 1954)
purpose: To amend The Legislative Assembly of Travancore-Cochin (Removal of Disqualifications) Act, 1951, for the purpose hereinafter appearing.
scope: This act applies to the Legislative Assembly of Travancore-Cochin.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Legislative Assembly of Travancore-Cochin (Removal of Disqualifications) Amendment Act, 1954. It shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 2, Act XV of 1951.
main_sections.description: Amends Section 2 of the Legislative Assembly of Travancore-Cochin (Removal of Disqualifications) Act, 1951 (Act XV of 1951). Specifically, it adds the word 'or' after clause (iv) and inserts a new clause (v) stating that holding an office in the National Cadet Corps or the Territorial Army, when raised and maintained under specified Acts, will not be a disqualification.

important_rules: Holding an office in the National Cadet Corps or the Territorial Army, when raised and maintained under the National Cadet Corps Act, 1948 (Central Act XXXI of 1948), or in the Territorial Army, when raised and maintained under the Territorial Army Act, 1948 (Central Act LVI of 1948), shall not be a disqualification for being a member of the Legislative Assembly of Travancore-Cochin.
important_notes: The amendment is made in the Fifth Year of the Republic of India.
The amendment refers to Central Acts XXXI of 1948 and LVI of 1948.

title: The Legislative Assembly (Removal of Disqualifications) Amendment Act, 2012
purpose: To further amend The Legislative Assembly (Removal of Disqualifications) Act, 1951.
scope: Applies to members of the Legislative Assembly of Kerala, including Ministers, the Speaker, the Deputy Speaker, the Leader of the Opposition, and the Chief Whip. The amendments are deemed to have come into force with respect to certain dates in 1977 and 1982.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as The Legislative Assembly (Removal of Disqualifications) Amendment Act, 2012 and states it shall come into force on the 11th day of October, 1951.

Amends Section 2 of The Legislative Assembly (Removal of Disqualifications) Act, 1951 by inserting an Explanation and a Note. The Explanation clarifies that 'members of the Legislative Assembly' include Ministers, the Speaker, the Deputy Speaker, the Leader of the Opposition, and the Chief Whip. The Note specifies that this explanation is deemed to have come into force in respect of the Leader of the Opposition on September 1st, 1977, and the Chief Whip on October 1st, 1982.

Repeals The Legislative Assembly (Removal of Disqualifications) Amendment Ordinance, 2012 (23 of 2012). It also includes a saving clause stating that anything done or any action taken under the repealed Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

key_procedures: Insertion of an Explanation and a Note into Section 2 of the principal Act, with specific retrospective commencement dates for the Explanation.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 26th day of June 2012 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 1367 dated 27th June, 2012.
The amendments related to the Leader of the Opposition are retrospective to September 1st, 1977.
The amendments related to the Chief Whip are retrospective to October 1st, 1982.
The Act repeals the Legislative Assembly (Removal of Disqualifications) Amendment Ordinance, 2012, ensuring continuity of actions taken under the Ordinance.

title: THE LEGISLATIVE ASSEMBLY (REMOVAL OF DISQUALIFICATIONS) AMENDMENT ACT, 2016
purpose: To further amend the Legislative Assembly (Removal of Disqualifications) Act, 1951.
scope: Applies to members of the Legislative Assembly of Kerala.

key_definitions.Administrative Reforms Commission: A body of experts constituted by the State Government from time to time, to study different aspects of administration and recommend measures for its improvement.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Legislative Assembly (Removal of Disqualifications) Amendment Act, 2016 and states that it shall come into force on the 11th day of October, 1951.

Inserts a new sub-section (3) into section 2 of the Legislative Assembly (Removal of Disqualifications) Act, 1951. This new sub-section specifies that no person shall be disqualified or deemed ever to have been disqualified for being chosen as, and for being, a member of the Legislative Assembly of the State of Kerala by reason only that he holds or has held the office of the Chairman of the Administrative Reforms Commission.

important_rules: No person shall be disqualified or deemed ever to have been disqualified for being chosen as, and for being, a member of the Legislative Assembly of the State of Kerala by reason only that he holds or has held the office of the Chairman of the Administrative Reforms Commission.
administration: Law (Legislation-B) Department, Government of Kerala

title: The Local Authorities Laws (Amendment) Act, 1987
purpose: To further amend the Town Planning Act (IV of 1108), the Madras Town Planning Act, 1920 (Madras Act VII of 1920), the Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1961 (20 of 1961), the Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, 1961 (30 of 1961) and the Kerala State Rural Development Board Act, 1971 (15 of 1971).
scope: Applies to the local authorities in Kerala as defined by the various Acts being amended.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Local Authorities Laws (Amendment) Act, 1987. It also specifies that Section 4, sub-clause (b) of clause (1) and clause (2) of Section 5 of this Act shall come into force at once and the remaining provisions shall be deemed to have come into force on the 12th day of May, 1987.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Act IV of 1108.—In the Town Planning Act (IV of 1108),—
main_sections.description: Amends Section 53BA and 53BB of the Town Planning Act (IV of 1108) regarding the appointment and term of office of the Chairman of the Development Authority. It also amends Section 53BC regarding the Executive Committee.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Madras Act VII of 1920.—In the Town Planning Act, 1920 (Madras Act VII of 1920),—
main_sections.description: Amends Section 54BA and 54BB of the Town Planning Act, 1920, concerning the appointment and term of office of the Chairman of the Development Authority and the nomination of members by the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Act 20 of 1961.—In the Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1961 (20 of 1961),—
main_sections.description: Amends Section 9 and Section 10 of the Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1961, by substituting phrases related to the authority of officers.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Act 30 of 1961.—In the Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, 1961 (30 of 1961),—
main_sections.description: Amends Section 5 and Section 44 of the Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, 1961, concerning the Council's composition, the number of councillors, and provisions for women in the Council, including reserved seats for Scheduled Castes and women.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Act 15 of 1971.—In section 4 of the Kerala State Rural Development Board Act, 1971 (15 of 1971),—
main_sections.description: Amends Section 4 of the Kerala State Rural Development Board Act, 1971, regarding the appointment of the Chairman and the composition of the Board, allowing for non-official members.

main_sections.section_title: Repeal and saving.—(1) The Local Authorities Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1987 (3 of 1987) is hereby repealed.
main_sections.description: Repeals the Local Authorities Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1987. It also states that anything done or any action taken under the various amended Acts prior to this repeal is deemed to have been done or taken under the corresponding provisions of this Act.

important_rules: The term of office for a Chairman of a Development Authority shall not in any case exceed three years.
Provisions regarding the nomination of members to the Development Authority and their term of office.
Specific amendments related to the number of councillors and reserved seats for women and Scheduled Castes in the Municipal Council.
The Board composition can include non-official members who have been chosen as members of the Panchayats in the State at the last election.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be the respective local authorities and government departments.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the amended Acts and the oversight of the government.

rights: Right of the Government to nominate persons to represent constituencies.
Right of the Government to determine the term of office of Chairmen and members.
Right to reserve seats in the Council for women and Scheduled Castes.
duties: Duty to comply with the provisions of the amended Acts.
Duty to ensure that the composition of local authorities reflects the provisions of the Act.
obligations: Obligation to implement the amendments brought forth by this Act.
Obligation to ensure that provisions for reservations in councils are met.

key_procedures: Process of amending existing local authority laws.
Procedures for appointment and term of office of Chairmen and members of Development Authorities.
Procedures for council composition, including reservations.
Repeal of previous ordinances and saving of actions taken thereunder.
administration: Government of Kerala, Law (Legislation-C) Department
important_notes: Certain sections (Section 4, sub-clause (b) of clause (1) and clause (2) of Section 5) of this Act came into force on the date of publication, while others were deemed to have come into force on 12th May, 1987.
The Act repeals the Local Authorities Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1987, but validates actions taken under it.
The amendments aim to regularize and update the functioning of various local authorities in Kerala.

title: THE LOCAL AUTHORITIES LAWS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1978
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960, the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960 and the Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, 1961.
scope: Applies to electoral rolls for Panchayats, Municipalities, and Municipal Corporations in Kerala.

key_definitions.qualifying date: For the purposes of the sections related to the preparation or revision of an electoral roll, it means the first day of January of the year in which it is so prepared or revised.
key_definitions.ordinarily resident: A person shall not be deemed to be ordinarily resident in a municipality or panchayat on the ground only that he owns, or is in possession of, a dwelling house therein. A person absenting himself temporarily from his place of ordinary residence shall not by reason thereof cease to be ordinarily resident therein. A person who is a patient in any establishment maintained wholly or mainly for the reception and treatment of persons suffering from mental illness or mental defectiveness or who is detained in prison or other legal custody at any place shall not by reason thereof be deemed to be ordinarily resident therein. In any case if a question arises as to whether a person is ordinarily resident in a municipality or panchayat area at any relevant time, the question shall be determined with reference to all facts of the case and to such rules as may be made in this behalf by the Government.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Local Authorities Laws (Amendment) Act, 1978. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 20.h day of April, 1978.
Amends the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960, specifically sections 14 and 15, by substituting certain provisions relating to electoral rolls for every panchayat area.

Amends the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1961, particularly sections 57, 57A, 57B, 57C, 57D, 58, 58D, and 58E, relating to electoral rolls, disqualifications for registration, conditions of registration, meaning of ordinarily resident, preparation and revision of electoral rolls, jurisdiction of civil courts, and making false declaration.
Amends the Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, 1961, by inserting a clause defining 'election authority' and substituting sections 46 and 48 related to electoral rolls.
Repeals the Kerala Local Authorities Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1978, and includes a saving provision.

important_rules: A person shall be disqualified for registration in an electoral roll if he is not a citizen of India; or is of unsound mind and stands so declared by a competent court; or is for the time being disqualified from voting under the provisions of any law relating to corrupt practices and other offences in connection with elections.
The name of any person who becomes so disqualified after registration shall forthwith be struck off the electoral rolls.
No person shall be registered in the electoral roll for more than one local authority.
No person shall be registered more than once in any panchayat area.
A person shall not be deemed to be ordinarily resident in a panchayat area on the ground only that he owns, or is in possession of, a dwelling house therein.

Every person whose name appears in the electoral roll for a panchayat shall, so long as such roll remains in force, be entitled, subject to the provisions of this Act, to vote at an election for the ward concerned, and no person whose name does not appear in such roll shall vote at an election.
No civil court shall have jurisdiction to entertain or adjudicate upon any question whether any person is or is not entitled to be registered in an electoral roll.

If any person makes in connection with the preparation, revision or correction of an electoral roll, or the inclusion or exclusion of any entry in or from an electoral roll, a statement or declaration in writing which is false and which he either knows or believes to be false or does not believe to be true, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.

penalties: Punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both (for making false declarations).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Electoral authorities, Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Removal of names from electoral rolls, disqualification from registration, prosecution for false declarations.

rights: Right to vote at an election if name appears in the electoral roll.
Right to be registered in the electoral roll if conditions are met.
duties: Duty to ensure accurate preparation and revision of electoral rolls.
Duty to comply with provisions regarding registration and disqualification.
obligations: Obligation to not make false statements or declarations in relation to electoral rolls.

key_procedures: Preparation and revision of electoral rolls: The electoral roll for each panchayat/municipality shall be prepared by the election authority in the prescribed manner by reference to the qualifying date and shall come into force immediately upon its final publication in accordance with the rules made under this Act.
Division of electoral rolls: The electoral roll for a panchayat/municipality shall be divided into separate parts for each ward.

Inclusion of names: Every person whose name appears in the electoral roll for a municipality/panchayat shall be entitled to vote at an election, provided certain conditions are met (e.g., not disqualified).
Removal of names: Names of persons disqualified after registration shall be struck off the electoral rolls.
administration: Government, Election Authority.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on April 20, 1978.
Explanations are provided for terms like 'municipality', 'panchayat', and 'ordinarily resident' to clarify their application within the context of the amended acts.
The Act repeals the Kerala Local Authorities Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1978.

title: The Local Authorities Laws (Amendment) Act, 1988
purpose: To amend the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960, the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960, and the Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, 1961.
scope: Applies to the amendments made to the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960, the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960, and the Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, 1961.

key_definitions.local authority: Means a Municipal Corporation or a Municipal Council or a Panchayat or a Township Committee and 'other authority' means any authority by whatever name called, constituted by the Government under any law or established by or under any State Enactment for the time being in force.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Local Authorities Laws (Amendment) Act, 1988. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 10th day of January, 1988.

Amends Chapter VI, after section 107, the following sections are inserted: 107A. List of Officers and Staff of the Government Departments, Local Authorities or other authorities to be furnished. 107B. Breaches of official duty in connection with elections. 107C. Requisitioning of premises etc., for election purposes.

After section 75, the following sections are inserted: 75A. List of officers and staff of the Government Departments, Local Authorities or other authorities to be furnished. 75B. Breaches of official duty in connection with elections. 75C. Requisitioning of premises etc., for election purposes.

After section 65, the following sections are inserted: 65A. List of officers and staff of the Government Departments, Local Authorities or other authorities to be furnished. 65B. Breaches of official duty in connection with elections. 65C. Requisitioning of premises etc., for election purposes.

The Local Authorities Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1988 (1 of 1988) is hereby repealed. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960 (32 of 1960) or the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1961 (14 of 1961) or the Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, 1961 (30 of 1961) as amended by the said Ordinance, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960 (32 of 1960) or the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1961 (14 of 1961) or the Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, 1961 (30 of 1961), as the case may be, as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Officers and staff of Government Departments, Local Authorities, or other authorities are required to furnish a list of officers and staff to the election authority upon requisition, for performing election duties.
Any person who commits a breach of official duty in connection with an election may be punishable with fine.
Premises, vehicles, or vessels can be requisitioned by the election authority for election purposes, such as polling stations or storage of ballot boxes.
No vehicle or vessel being lawfully used by a candidate or their agent for election purposes shall be requisitioned.
The requisitioned property must be returned to the owner or person in possession, not extending beyond the period for which it is required.
Contravention of orders made under the requisitioning provisions can lead to imprisonment and fine.

penalties: Fine, which may extend to five hundred rupees for failure to furnish list of officers and staff.
Fine, which may extend to five hundred rupees for breaches of official duty.
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months or fine with both for contravening requisition orders.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Election authority, Government Departments, Local Authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through imposition of fines, imprisonment, and requisitioning powers.

rights: Right to requisition premises, vehicles, or vessels for election purposes.
Right to receive compensation or due process when property is requisitioned.
duties: Duty to furnish list of officers and staff to the election authority upon requisition.
Duty to perform official duties in connection with elections without neglect or failure.
Duty to comply with requisition orders for premises, vehicles, or vessels.
obligations: Obligation to ensure that lawful use of candidate's or agent's vehicles/vessels for election purposes are not disrupted by requisition.

key_procedures: Procedure for requisitioning premises, vehicles, or vessels for election purposes by the election authority, including written orders.
Procedure for the return of requisitioned property after the election period.
Procedure for contravening requisition orders and the subsequent penalties.
administration: Government of Kerala, Law (Legislation—C) Department
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on January 10, 1988.
Definitions of 'premises', 'vehicle', and 'vessel' are provided in the context of requisitioning.

title: THE LUXURY TAX ON TOBACCO (VALIDATION) ACT, 1964
purpose: To provide for the levy of a luxury tax on tobacco for the period beginning with the 17th day of August, 1950 and ending on the 31st day of December, 1957, and the validation of the levy and collection of fees for licences for the vend and stocking of tobacco for the aforesaid period.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala, excluding the Malabar district referred to in sub-section (2) of section 3 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956. It applies to every person vending or stocking tobacco within any area to which the Act extends.

key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made by the Government under this Act.
key_definitions.tobacco: Includes leaf of tobacco, plant, snuff, cigars, cigarettes, beedies, beedi tobacco, tobacco powder and other preparations or admixtures of tobacco.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Luxury Tax on Tobacco (Validation) Act, 1964, and specifies its extent of application.
Defines 'prescribed' and 'tobacco'.

Specifies the period for which the tax is leviable and how it is to be levied on vendors or stockers of tobacco, and that it shall be deemed to have been in force in any area to which the Act extends.

Grants the Government the power to make rules, including provisions for the prohibition of the vending of tobacco, the issue of licences for vending and stocking, the classification of licences and the rate of tax, and appeals from orders under the rules. It also validates rules and notifications specified in sub-section (3) of section 4 of the Travancore Tobacco Rules, 1950, and the Cochin Tobacco Act, VII of 1904, as they relate to or purpose to relate to the levy and collection of fees for licences, and the vend and stocking of tobacco.

Validates the levy or order of any court, all fees for licences for the vend or stocking of tobacco levied or collected or purported to have been levied or collected under any of the rules or notifications specified in sub-section (3) of section 4 for the period beginning with the 17th day of August, 1950 and ending on the 31st day of December, 1957, and further validates the levy or collection of fees for licences for the vend and stocking of tobacco for the period in force on and from the 17th day of August, 1950, and the fees for licences were in force on and from the 17th day of August, 1950 and the fees for licences were a luxury tax on tobacco levied under the provisions of this Act, and accordingly-(a) no suit or other proceeding shall be maintained or continued in any court for the refund of any fees paid or purported to have been paid under any of the said rules or notifications; and (b) no court shall enforce a decree or order directing the refund of any fees paid or purported to have been paid under any of the said rules or notifications.

Deals with the recovery of licence fees refunded under section 4, stating that any amount paid or purported to have been paid as a fee for licence under any of the rules or notifications specified in sub-section (3) of section 4 has been refunded after the 24th day of January, 1962, and such amount would not have been liable to be refunded if this Act had been in force on the date of the refund, thereupon to whom the refund was made shall repay the amount so refunded to the credit of the Government in any Government, then on or before the 16th day of April, 1964, and, where such amount is not so paid, the amount may be recovered from him as an arrear of land revenue under the Revenue Recovery Act for the time being in force.
Repeals the Luxury Tax on Tobacco (Validation) Ordinance, 1963 (Ordinance No. 1 of 1963), and hereby repealed.
Details the rates of luxury tax on different categories of tobacco products.

important_rules: Rules may be made by the Government for the prohibition of the vending of tobacco.
Rules may prescribe the issue of licences for the vend and stocking of tobacco.
Rules may classify licences and specify the rate of tax for each class of licences.
Rules may provide for appeals from orders made under the rules.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through rules made by the Government and by legal proceedings for recovery of refunded fees.

duties: Persons vending or stocking tobacco must comply with licence requirements and pay luxury tax.
Individuals who received refunds of licence fees under certain conditions must repay them.

key_procedures: Obtaining licences for the vend and stocking of tobacco.
Payment of luxury tax on tobacco.
Procedure for recovery of refunded licence fees.
Appeals from orders made under the rules.
administration: The Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act is published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 4th March, 1964.
Received the assent of the President on the 3rd day of March, 1964.
For Statement of Objects and Reasons - See Gazette Extraordinary dated 12th February, 1964.
The Act's provisions regarding validation apply to rules and notifications issued under the Travancore Tobacco Rules, 1950, and the Cochin Tobacco Act, VII of 1904.
No suit or other proceeding shall be maintained or continued in any court for the refund of any fees paid or purported to have been paid under any of the said rules or notifications.

title: THE MADRAS BUILDINGS (LEASE AND RENT CONTROL) AMENDMENT ACT, 1957
purpose: To amend the Madras Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1949.
scope: This act applies to the Madras Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1949 (Madras Act XXV of 1949).

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Madras Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Amendment Act, 1957, and shall come into force at once.

Amends sub-section (3) of section 1 of the Madras Building (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1949. It specifies that in the Malabar District referred to in sub-section (2) of section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (Central Act 37 of 1956), for the expression "30th September 1957", the expression "31st March 1958" shall be substituted.
Repeals The Madras Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Amendment Ordinance, 1957 (Ordinance No. 9 of 1957).

important_notes: The amendment regarding the substitution of dates is specific to the Malabar District and the application of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.

title: THE MADRAS BUILDINGS (LEASE AND RENT CONTROL) AMENDMENT ACT, 1958
purpose: To amend The Madras Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1949.
scope: The act applies to the Madras Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1949, as amended by the Malabar district referred to in sub-section (2) of section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Madras Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Amendment Act, 1958, and that it shall come into force at once.

This section amends sub-section (3) of section 1 of The Madras Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1949. It substitutes the words, figures and letters "the 30th September 1958" with "the 31st March 1958".

administration: The Act is administered by the State Government.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the President on the 29th of March, 1958.

title: The Madras Commercial Crops Markets (Amendment and Validation) Act, 1964
purpose: To amend the Madras Commercial Crops Markets Act, 1933, in its application to the Malabar district, to insert a sub-section (2) to section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, and to validate the levy and collection of cess under that Act.
scope: Applies to the Malabar district in the Madras Commercial Crops Markets Act, 1933. The validation aspect applies to the levy and collection of cess under section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Madras Commercial Crops Markets (Amendment and Validation) Act, 1964 and that Section 2 shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of November, 1956 and the remaining provisions of this Act shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 11
main_sections.description: Substitutes a new section 11 for section 11 of the Madras Commercial Crops Markets Act, 1933, regarding the principal Act. The substituted section deals with the levy of fees by Market Committees.
States that section 15 of the Principal Act, in sub-section (1), the words "or cess" shall be omitted.

States that section 17 of the principal Act shall be re-numbered as sub-section (1) of that section and after sub-section (1) as so renumbered, the following sub-section shall be inserted, namely:-"(2) Any person removing or attempting to remove any commercial crop from any notified area before the fee payable under sub-section (1) of section 11 has been paid thereon and a receipt obtained in respect of such payment, or practising any device in order to evade or to facilitate the evasion of the payment of the said fee, or evading payment of the said fee shall be punishable with fine which may extend to two hundred rupees".

States that notwithstanding any judgment, decree or order of any court, all cess on any commercial crop levied or collected or purported to have been levied or collected under section 11 of the principal Act, by the Market Committee constituted under the principal Act, for the period beginning from the 1st day of November, 1956 and ending on the 28th day of November, 1963, shall be deemed to have been levied or collected as fees under the principal Act, as amended by this Act, and accordingly, (a) no suit or other proceeding shall be maintained or continued in any court for the refund of any such cess paid or purported to have been paid under section 11 of the principal Act, and (b) no court shall enforce a decree or order directing the refund of any such cess paid or purported to have been paid under section 11 of the principal Act.
In section 19-A of the principal Act, the word "ees" wherever it occurs, shall be omitted.

If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, the Government may, as occasion may arise, by order, do anything not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act, which appears to them necessary for the purpose of removing the difficulty.

Repeals The Madras Commercial Crops Markets (Amendment and Validation) Ordinance, 1963 (Ordinance No. 3 of 1963) and states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act, as if this Act had commenced on the 31st day of December, 1963.

important_rules: Rule: Levy of fees by Market Committees on notified commercial crops.
Rule: The fees referred to in sub-section (1) shall be paid by the purchaser of the commercial crop.

Rule: Out of the fees levied under sub-section (1) on the commercial crop or crops bought and sold in any part of the notified area which constitutes a village as defined in the law for the time being in force for the constitution of Panchayats, such proportion as may be prescribed, shall be paid by the Market Committee to the Panchayat concerned.

penalties: Fine which may extend to two hundred rupees for removing or attempting to remove any commercial crop from any notified area before the fee payable under sub-section (1) of section 11 has been paid thereon and a receipt obtained in respect of such payment, or practising any device in order to evade or to facilitate the evasion of the payment of the said fee, or evading payment of the said fee.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government, Market Committees, Courts
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Levy and collection of fees, imposition of fines, maintenance or continuation of suits or proceedings, enforcement of decrees or orders.

rights: Right to receive receipt for fee payment.
duties: Duty to pay fees on commercial crops bought and sold in a notified area.
Duty not to remove commercial crop from notified area before fee payment.
Duty not to practice devices to evade fee payment.

key_procedures: Procedure: Payment of fees by the purchaser of the commercial crop.
Procedure: Obtaining a receipt upon payment of the fee.
Procedure: Removal of difficulty by Government order if necessary.
administration: Government, Market Committees
important_notes: Fees for commercial crops are specified in a table with rates for Arecanut (0.33 Rs. per quintal) and Coconut and its products (0.16 Rs. per every 1000 coconuts or part thereof).
The validation covers the period from November 1, 1956, to November 28, 1963.
The Madras Commercial Crops Markets (Amendment and Validation) Ordinance, 1963, has been repealed and replaced by this Act, with a saving clause.

title: The Madras Commercial Crops Markets (Amendment) Act, 1980
purpose: To further amend the Madras Commercial Crops Markets Act, 1933, for the purpose hereinafter appearing.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Madras Commercial Crops Markets (Amendment) Act, 1980 and it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 15th day of November, 1980.
Amends section 11 of the Madras Commercial Crops Markets Act, 1933 by substituting a new Table of rates for various commercial crops, specifically for 'Arecanut' and 'Coconut and its products'.
Repeals the Madras Commercial Crops Markets (Amendment) Ordinance, 1980 (7 of 1980) and saves any action taken or anything done under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance.

important_rules: The rates for 'Arecanut' are specified as one rupee and fifty paise per every quintal of cured arecanuts or part thereof, and ten paise for every 1000 ripe or soaked arecanuts or part thereof.
The rates for 'Coconut and its products' are specified as one rupee and fifty paise for every quintal of by-products (copra or desiccated coconuts) or part thereof.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not specified in the provided excerpt.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not specified in the provided excerpt.

key_procedures: The act involves amendment of existing legislation regarding commercial crops markets.
The amendment introduces a new table of rates for specific commercial crops.
administration: Not specified in the provided excerpt.
important_notes: The Act was received the assent of the Governor on the 14th day of January, 1981 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 43 dated the 16th January, 1981.

title: THE MALABAR DISTRICT BOARD (TEMPORARY PROVISIONS) ACT, 1957
purpose: To provide for the appointment of a Special Officer to perform the functions of the Malabar District Board.
scope: Applies to the Malabar District Board and its functions. It also refers to the Madras District Boards Act, 1920 and the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.

main_sections.description: Names the act as the Malabar District Board (Temporary Provisions) Act, 1957. It extends to the whole of the Malabar District referred to in sub-section (2) of section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, and comes into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of a Special Officer to perform the functions of the Malabar District Board
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to appoint a Special Officer to exercise the powers, discharge the duties, and perform the functions of the Malabar District Board. The Special Officer is constituted under the principal Act and the District Board or its president, as the case may be, acts as the Executive Authority. The Special Officer acts as the Executive Authority or its president.  The salary etc. of the Special Officer are to be defrayed from the fund constituted under section 114 of the principal Act.

States that the salary and allowances of the Special Officer appointed under sub-section (1) of section 2 shall be prescribed by rules made by the Government and may be paid from the district fund constituted under section 114 of the principal Act.
