Grants the Government the power to make any order, do anything which appears to them necessary for the purpose of removing any difficulty that may arise in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, or of the principal Act.

Repeals the Malabar District Board (Temporary Provisions) Ordinance, 1957 (Ordinance No. 5 of 1957). Notwithstanding the repeal, any action taken or any order made or any thing done or any action taken in the exercise of the powers conferred by or under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken in the exercise of the powers conferred by or under this Act, as if this Act were in force on the day on which such thing was done or action was taken.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By appointing a Special Officer to exercise powers and discharge duties, and by the Government's power to remove difficulties.

duties: The Special Officer is to perform the functions of the Malabar District Board.

key_procedures: Appointment of a Special Officer by the Government to perform the functions of the Malabar District Board.
Prescribing rules for the salary and allowances of the Special Officer by the Government.
Removal of difficulties by the Government through orders or actions.
administration: The Government of Kerala (implied).
important_notes: The Act is temporary in nature.
It repeals the Malabar District Board (Temporary Provisions) Ordinance, 1957, but saves actions taken under the ordinance.
The Act is enacted in the Eighth Year of the Republic of India.

title: THE MADRAS DISTRICT BOARDS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1957
purpose: To amend the Madras District Boards Act, 1920, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Madras District Boards.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Madras District Boards (Amendment) Act, 1957 and it shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 74-B, Madras Act XIV of 1920
main_sections.description: Amends Section 74-A of the Madras District Boards Act, 1920, specifically in sub-section (2) of section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956. It omits the words "being a tax on the annual rent value of lands" and "the principal Act" in relation to the Malabar district. It also omits 'every five cents of land or part thereof' regarding the tax on land.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 78, Madras Act XIV of 1920
main_sections.description: Substitutes the existing section 78 of the principal Act with a new section. The new section 78 states that 'the land-cess shall be levied on all lands in the district, other than any land or class of land which the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, exempt and shall consist of a tax of one naya paisa per annum for every five cents of land or part thereof.'

main_sections.section_title: Omission of sections 79 to 86, Madras Act XIV of 1920
main_sections.description: Omites sections 79 to 86 of the principal Act.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 87, Madras Act XIV of 1920
main_sections.description: Amends section 87 of the principal Act by omitting the words 'In the case of lands held on ryotwari tenure'.

main_sections.section_title: Omission of section 90, Madras Act XIV of 1920
main_sections.description: Omits section 90 of the principal Act.

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act is subject to Government notification in the Gazette.
important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 8th January 1958.

title: The Madras District Municipalities (Amendment) Act, 1958
purpose: To further amend the Madras District Municipalities Act, 1920, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Madras District Municipalities and their councillors.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Madras District Municipalities (Amendment) Act, 1958. It shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of term of office of councillors of municipalities expiring on 1st November, 1958.
main_sections.description: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in section 8 of the Madras District Municipalities Act, 1920 (Madras Act V of 1920), as in force in the Malabar district referred to in sub-section (2) of section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (Central Act 37 of 1956), the term of office of the councillors of every municipality constituted under the said Act shall extend upto noon on the first day of September, 1959.

main_sections.section_title: Date of elections and term of office of councillors.
main_sections.description: The provisions of the said Act shall have effect, subject to the following modifications, namely: (a) The Government shall cause elections to be held to every municipality concerned, so that the newly elected members may come into office on the first day of September, 1959. (b) The term of office of the newly elected councillors shall expire at noon on the first day of September, 1962.

main_sections.section_title: Supersession of council on expressing opinion against extension of term.
main_sections.description: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in section 2, where a municipal council, the term of office of the councillors of which has been extended under that section, has before the commencement of this Act, passed a resolution with the support of not less than three-fourths of the number of councillors present and voting expressing opinion against such extension, or passes such a resolution with such support as is specified above, after the commencement of this Act, it shall be lawful for the Government, by notification in the Gazette, to supersede the council till the first day of September, 1959. (2) The supersession shall take effect from such date as may be specified in the notification, or, if no date is therein specified, from the noon on the date of publication of the notification and thereupon the following consequences shall ensue: (a) All the members of the council as well as its chairman and vice-chairman shall forthwith be deemed to have vacated their offices. (b) All or any of the functions of the council and of its chairman, including where the chairman is also the executive authority, his functions as such may, during the period of supersession, be exercised and performed, as far as may be, and to such extent as the Government may determine, by a Special Officer appointed by the Government in that behalf and such Special Officer may, if the Government so direct, receive payment for his services from the municipal fund. (3) When a council is superseded under this section, the Government until the date of the reconstitution thereof and the reconstituted council thereafter shall be entitled to all the assets and be subject to all the liabilities of the council as on the date of the supersession and on the date of the reconstitution respectively.

If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, or of the said Act as amended by this Act, the Government may, as occasion may require, by order, do anything which appears to them necessary for the purpose of removing the difficulty.

(1) The Madras District Municipalities (Amendment) Ordinance, 1958 (9 of 1958), is hereby repealed. (2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken in the exercise of any powers conferred by or under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken in the exercise of the powers conferred by or under this Act, as if this Act were in force on the date on which such thing was done or action was taken.

important_rules: Councillors' term of office expiring on 1st November, 1958, is extended to noon on the first day of September, 1959.
Elections for new councillors must be held so that they take office on September 1, 1959.
Newly elected councillors' term of office will expire on noon on September 1, 1962.
A council can be superseded until September 1, 1959, if a resolution against the extension of its term is passed.
During supersession, council functions may be exercised by a Special Officer appointed by the Government.
Assets and liabilities of the superseded council are transferred to the reconstituted council.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By notification in the Gazette and by appointment of Special Officers.

rights: Right to elect councillors.
Right of Special Officer to exercise council functions during supersession.
duties: Duty of the Government to cause elections to be held.
obligations: Reconstituted council is subject to assets and liabilities of the superseded council.

key_procedures: Supersession of a council: (1) A resolution must be passed by not less than three-fourths of councillors present and voting, either before or after the commencement of this Act, expressing opinion against the extended term. (2) The Government then may, by notification in the Gazette, supersede the council. (3) The supersession takes effect from the date specified in the notification or upon its publication.
Removal of difficulties: If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, the Government may issue orders to remove such difficulty.
administration: The Government
important_notes: This Act is an amendment to the Madras District Municipalities Act, 1920.
The Act takes effect immediately upon its enactment.
The Madras District Municipalities (Amendment) Ordinance, 1958, is repealed, but actions taken under it are saved.
The reorganisation of states is referenced in relation to the applicability of the Madras District Municipalities Act.

title: THE MADRAS ESSENTIAL ARTICLES CONTROL AND REQUISITIONING (TEMPORARY POWERS) AMENDMENT ACT, 1958
purpose: To amend The Madras Essential Articles Control and Requisitioning (Temporary Powers) Act, 1949.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and references amendments to various Acts including the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 and the Travancore-Cochin Public Safety Measures Act, 1950.

main_sections.description: This section states the short title of the Act and that it shall come into force at once.

Amends section 1 of the Madras Essential Articles Control and Requisitioning (Temporary Powers) Act, 1949. It specifies the wording to be substituted in sub-sections (1) and (2) of section 1 of the principal Act, including replacing "Malabar district" with "the State of Kerala" and providing for the application of the Interpretation and General Clauses Act, 1894.
Amends section 5 of the principal Act by substituting specific words and figures in sub-section (1) and by omitting sub-section (2).
Amends section 9 of the principal Act by substituting "Malabar district" with "the State of Kerala".

main_sections.section_title: Amendments to the Travancore-Cochin Public Safety Measures Act, 1950.
main_sections.description: Amends the Travancore-Cochin Public Safety Measures Act, 1950. It specifies omissions for sections 3 to 7 (both inclusive) and amendments to sub-section (1) of section 14, and also omits sub-section (2).
Repeals The Madras Essential Articles Control and Requisitioning (Temporary Powers) Amendment Ordinance, 1958 (Ordinance No. 2 of 1958).

important_notes: The Act received the assent of the President on 3rd April 1958 and was published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 4th April 1958.

title: The Madras General Sales Tax (Turnover and Assessment) Rules Validation Act, 1963
purpose: To validate the Madras General Sales Tax (Turnover and Assessment) Rules, 1939, and to provide for the validation of certain acts and things done or omitted to be done thereunder.
scope: Applies to the validation of the Madras General Sales Tax (Turnover and Assessment) Rules, 1939, and to all acts, proceedings, or things done or taken by the Government or any officer thereof, or any court, in connection with the levy or collection of taxes under these rules, or with the refund of such taxes.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Madras General Sales Tax (Turnover and Assessment) Rules Validation Act, 1963.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of the Madras General Sales Tax (Turnover and Assessment) Rules, 1939
main_sections.description: This section validates the Madras General Sales Tax (Turnover and Assessment) Rules, 1939, notwithstanding anything contained in any judgment, decree, or order of any court. It also validates all acts, proceedings, or things done or taken by the Government or any officer thereof, or any court, in connection with the levy or collection of taxes under these rules, or with the refund of such taxes. The section further states that no act or omission on the part of any person shall be punishable as an offence which would not have been so punishable if this Act had not been passed. It also clarifies that nothing contained in subsection (1) shall be deemed to revive the Madras General Sales Tax (Turnover and Assessment) Rules, 1939, which had been superseded by the extension of the Travancore-Cochin General Sales Tax Rules, 1950.

penalties: No act or omission on the part of any person shall be punishable as an offence which would not have been so punishable if this Act had not been passed.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government or any officer thereof, any court.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By validating actions taken under the Madras General Sales Tax (Turnover and Assessment) Rules, 1939.

rights: Right to levy and collect taxes under the validated rules.
Right to receive refund of taxes paid.
duties: Duty to comply with the Madras General Sales Tax (Turnover and Assessment) Rules, 1939.
obligations: Obligation to have acts, proceedings, or things done or taken in connection with the levy or collection of taxes, or refund of taxes, validated.

key_procedures: Validation of the Madras General Sales Tax (Turnover and Assessment) Rules, 1939.
Validation of acts, proceedings, or things done or taken in connection with the levy, collection, or refund of taxes under the said rules.
administration: Government of Madras (as the Act pertains to the Madras General Sales Tax)
important_notes: The validation extends to any judgment, decree or order of any court.
The validation covers acts done under the rules in force in the Fourteenth Year of the Republic of India.
The Act is retrospective in nature, validating actions from before its enactment.
Received the assent of the Governor on 4th March 1963 and published in the Gazette Extraordinary, dated 4th March 1963.

title: The Madras General Sales-tax (Revival and Special Provisions) Act, 1971
purpose: To revive the Madras General Sales-tax Act, 1939 (Madras Act IX of 1939) and to make certain special provisions for the levy of tax on the sales of tea and rubber made in the Malabar district, referred to in sub-section (2) of section 5 of the State Re-organisation Act, 1956, during the period commencing on and from the 1st day of April, 1951 and ending with the 30th day of September, 1957, and to make certain special provisions in respect of such levy, assessment, re-assessment and collection.
scope: Applies to the Malabar district, specifically to sales of tea and rubber.

key_definitions.General Sales-tax Act, 1939: The Madras General Sales-tax Act, 1939 (Madras Act IX of 1939)
key_definitions.Malabar district: The Malabar district referred to in sub-section (2) of section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (Central Act 37 of 1956).

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Madras General Sales-tax (Revival and Special Provisions) Act, 1971. It extends to the whole of the Malabar district and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of October, 1957, and remaining provisions on the 1st day of April, 1951.
All expressions used but not defined in this Act and defined in the Madras General Sales-tax Act, 1939 (Madras Act IX of 1939), shall have the meanings respectively assigned to them in that Act.

main_sections.section_title: Revival of Madras Act IX of 1939 and rules made thereunder for certain purposes
main_sections.description: The Madras General Sales-tax Act, 1939, and rules made thereunder are revived and shall be deemed to have always been in force to the extent and subject to special provisions hereinafter contained for the purposes of levy, assessment, re-assessment and collection (including appeals, reviews and revisions) of tax on sales of tea and rubber during the period from April 1, 1951, to September 30, 1957.

main_sections.section_title: Special provisions in respect of tax on sales of tea and rubber
main_sections.description: This section details the application of provisions regarding tax on sales of tea and rubber. It outlines that dealers not exempt from tax under section 3 of the Madras Act shall pay tax at specified rates. It also provides for the recovery of tax not previously paid, the procedure for dealers to apply for assessment or re-assessment, and the enforcement of these provisions.

The amount of tax on the sale of tea or rubber collected during the period from April 1, 1951, to September 30, 1957, shall be adjusted towards the tax due. If the tax collected is in excess of the amount due, it shall be refunded to the dealer.

Nothing in this Act renders any person liable to be convicted of an offence or liable to any penalty in respect of anything done or omitted to be done before the publication of this Act in the Gazette, if such act or omission was not an offence or penalty under the Madras Act.

important_rules: Dealers not exempt under section 3 of the Madras Act are liable to pay tax on sales of tea and rubber.
Tax on sales of tea and rubber is levied at a rate of 1.5625 percent (one and nine-sixteenth per cent) of the amount of sale.
Tax due under the Madras Act or the rules made thereunder shall be assessed or re-assessed.
Any tax due and not previously paid shall be recovered.
The amount of tax already collected on tea and rubber sales between April 1, 1951, and September 30, 1957, will be adjusted against the tax due under this Act.
If the tax collected is in excess, it will be refunded.
No conviction or penalty will be applied for acts or omissions prior to the Act's publication if they were not offences/penalties under the previous Madras Act.

penalties: Conviction for offence
Liability for penalty
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Assessing authority or any other officer authorized by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment, re-assessment, and collection of tax. Dealers may be required to provide returns for assessment or re-assessment. Penalties and convictions are subject to the provisions of the Madras Act.

rights: Right to adjustment of already collected tax.
Right to refund if tax collected is in excess of the amount due.
Right to an opportunity of being heard, to present one's case before the assessing authority.
duties: Duty to pay tax on sales of tea and rubber at the specified rate.
Duty to comply with assessment and re-assessment provisions.
Duty to provide turnover return to the assessing authority.
obligations: Obligation to allow the assessing authority to examine the turnover of sales of tea or rubber.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 102.

Amends section 7 of the principal Act by substituting sub-section (3) and (4) regarding the composition of the Board. The Board shall consist of nine Hindu members, one of whom shall be a woman, one shall be a person belonging to Scheduled Castes and one shall be a person belonging to Scheduled Tribes. For sub-section (4), nine members specified in sub-section (3) including the woman member, the member belonging to the Scheduled Castes and the member belonging to the Scheduled Tribes shall be nominated by the Hindu among the Council of Ministers and the other two members shall be elected by the Hindus among the Members of the Legislative Assembly of the State of Kerala as provided in section 7L.

title: The Madras Marumakkattayam (Amendment) Act, 1958
purpose: To further amend the Madras Marumakkattayam Act, 1932.
scope: The Act applies to the Madras Marumakkattayam District and concerns matters related to Marumakkattayam law, inheritance, property, and family relations within that jurisdiction. Specifically, it addresses maintenance, alimony, partition, and the burden of proof for certain transactions.

key_definitions.tarwad: A joint family governed by Marumakkattayam law.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Madras Marumakkattayam (Amendment) Act, 1958, and it shall come into force at once.
Amends section 3 of the Madras Marumakkattayam Act, 1932 (Madras Act XXII of 1933), by omitting a specific clause.

Inserts new sections concerning Maintenance Pendente Lite and Expenses of Proceedings (10-A), Permanent alimony and maintenance (10-B), and Enforcement of and appeal from orders (10-C) into the principal Act.
Amends section 14 of the principal Act, stating that a second proviso shall be omitted.

Re-numbers section 32 of the principal Act as sub-section (1) of that section and inserts a new sub-section (2) which deals with the inspection of accounts by the Karnavan or other competent authority.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 33.
main_sections.description: Substitutes a new section 33, which prohibits the sale or mortgage of any immovable property of a tarwad or tavazhi without the consent of the major members.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 34.
main_sections.description: Substitutes a new section 34, titled 'Debt contracted and transaction entered into by karnavan when binding on tarwad.' It clarifies that no debt contracted or transaction entered into by a karnavan shall bind the tarwad unless the debt or transaction is entered into for consideration and for tarwad necessity or benefit.

Inserts a new section 34-A, titled 'Burden of proving tarwad necessity.' It states that the burden of proving tarwad necessity or benefit shall lie on the purchaser, mortgagee, pledgee, or other alienee, or creditor, as the case may be, but the Court may presume such necessity where the majority of the major members of the tarwad are parties to the transaction.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 38.
main_sections.description: Substitutes a new section 38, titled 'Right of member of tarwad or tavazhi to claim partition.' It states that any member of a tarwad or tavazhi may claim to take his or her share of all the properties of the tarwad or tavazhi over which the tarwad or tavazhi has power of disposal, and separate from the tarwad or tavazhi. Explanations clarify what constitutes a bar to partition and who are considered members entitled to claim shares.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 39.
main_sections.description: Substitutes a new section 39, titled 'Partition on change of religion.' It states that any member of a tarwad or tavazhi who has changed his or her religion may be compelled by any other member of the tarwad or tavazhi to take his or her share of all the tarwad or tavazhi properties over which the tarwad or tavazhi has power of disposal and separate from the tarwad or tavazhi.
Sections 40 and 41 of the principal Act shall be omitted.

main_sections.section_title: Omission of Chapter VII and the Schedule.
main_sections.description: The headings 'Chapter VII' and 'Impartible Tarwads' occurring before section 42, and sections 42 to 47 of, and the Schedule to the principal Act shall be omitted.
In sub-section (2) of section 49 of the principal Act, clause (b), the brackets and letter '(a)' at the beginning and the word 'and' at the end of clause (a) shall be omitted.

important_rules: Rule 1: No sale or mortgage of any immovable property of a tarwad and no lease of any such property shall be valid unless it is executed by the Karnavan for consideration and with the written consent of the majority of the major members of the tarwad.
Rule 2: The burden of proving tarwad necessity or benefit shall be on the purchaser, mortgagee, pledgee, or other alienee, or creditor.

Rule 3: Any member of a tarwad or tavazhi may claim to take his or her share of all the properties of the tarwad or tavazhi over which the tarwad or tavazhi has power of disposal, and separate from the tarwad or tavazhi.
Rule 4: Any member of a tarwad or tavazhi who has changed his or her religion may be compelled by any other member to take his or her share of all the tarwad or tavazhi properties and separate.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through court proceedings, including enforcement of orders, appeals, and presumptions of necessity in certain cases. Maintenance and alimony orders are enforceable by the Court.

rights: Right of a member of a tarwad or tavazhi to claim partition and separate their share of properties.
Right to claim maintenance and alimony.
Right to appeal court orders regarding maintenance and alimony.
duties: Duty of the Karnavan to act for the benefit of the tarwad or tavazhi.
Duty to obtain consent of major members for sale, mortgage, or lease of tarwad property.
Duty to prove tarwad necessity or benefit for certain transactions.
obligations: Obligation to pay maintenance pendente lite and expenses of proceedings.
Obligation to pay permanent alimony and maintenance.
Obligation to separate one's share upon change of religion, if compelled by other members.

key_procedures: Procedure for claiming maintenance pendente lite and expenses of proceedings. The court may order the husband to pay expenses, and if dissatisfied with any order, may modify or rescind it.
Procedure for claiming permanent alimony and maintenance. The court may order the respondent to pay alimony and maintenance, and can charge immovable property for such payments.

Procedure for enforcement of and appeal from orders under sections 10-A and 10-B. All orders made by the Court in any proceeding under these sections are enforceable as a decree of the original civil jurisdiction and may be appealed from under any law for the time being in force.
Procedure for partition. Any member can claim their share and separation.
Procedure for proving tarwad necessity or benefit for transactions.
administration: The Courts administer the provisions of this Act.
important_notes: The amendment is effective from the Ninth Year of the Republic of India.
Orders made by the Court under sections 10-A and 10-B are enforceable as decrees and are appealable.
The burden of proof for tarwad necessity or benefit lies with the purchaser/creditor, but the Court may presume it if major members are parties to the transaction.
Provisions relating to partition and claims to share are subject to explanations that clarify the scope and applicability.

title: THE MADRAS PLANTATIONS AGRICULTURAL INCOME TAX (REVIVAL) ACT, 1959
purpose: To revive the Madras Plantations Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1955 (Madras Act V of 1955) for the purposes and to the extent hereinafter specified. This revival is to address the decision of the Honourable High Court of Kerala to revive the said Act for the purposes of levy, assessment, re-assessment and collection of agricultural income-tax.
scope: Applies to agricultural income derived from plantations in the Malabar district, specifically concerning the assessment years 1957-58 and periods prior to the 1st day of November, 1958.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Madras Plantations Agricultural Income-tax (Revival) Act, 1959. It came into force on the 1st day of April, 1957.

main_sections.section_title: Revival of Madras Act V of 1955 for certain purposes
main_sections.description: The Madras Plantations Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1955 (Madras Act V of 1955) is hereby revived and shall be in force and shall be deemed to have been in force to the extent and for the purposes necessary for the levy, assessment, re-assessment and collection of the agricultural income-tax under the Madras Act on the agricultural income of every person for the period or periods prior to the 1st day of November, 1958. For the purposes of levy, assessment, re-assessment and collection of agricultural income-tax under the Madras Act for the assessment year 1957-58, notwithstanding anything contained in sub-clause (i) of clause (t) section 2 of the Madras Act, "previous year" shall be the period commencing from the day next after the last day of the previous year in respect of the assessment year 1956-57 and ending on the 31st day of October, 1956. Provided that, notwithstanding anything contained in section 3 of the Madras Act, the tax chargeable on the total agricultural income for the assessment year 1957-58 shall be at the rate applicable to the "average annual income" according to the Schedule to the Madras Act, such "average annual income" shall be an amount bearing to the aforesaid total agricultural income the same proportion as the period of twelve months bears to the period for which the agricultural income is reckoned. Provided further that the limit for exemption from chargeability to tax for the assessment year 1957-58 shall be determined with reference to the "average annual income".

The Madras Plantations Agricultural Income-tax (Revival) Ordinance, 1959 (1 of 1959), is hereby repealed. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken in the exercise of any powers conferred by or under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken in the exercise of the powers conferred by or under this Act.

important_rules: The Madras Plantations Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1955 is revived for the purpose of levying, assessing, re-assessing, and collecting agricultural income-tax for periods prior to November 1, 1958.
For the assessment year 1957-58, the "previous year" is defined as the period from November 1, 1956, to October 31, 1957.
Tax for assessment year 1957-58 will be calculated based on the total agricultural income, proportionally adjusted for the reckoning period, using the rates from the Schedule to the Madras Act.
Exemption limits for the assessment year 1957-58 will be determined with reference to the "average annual income."

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be the tax authorities responsible for agricultural income-tax.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the procedures of levy, assessment, re-assessment, and collection of agricultural income-tax as per the revived Act.

rights: Right to claim exemption from tax based on the "average annual income" for assessment year 1957-58.
duties: Duty to pay agricultural income-tax as per the provisions of the revived Act.

obligations: Obligation to report agricultural income derived from plantations for taxation purposes.

Determination of the "previous year" for the assessment year 1957-58.
Calculation of tax liability based on the "average annual income" and its proportionality to the income reckoning period.
Application of exemption limits determined by the "average annual income."
administration: The administration of this Act would fall under the purview of the relevant tax department responsible for agricultural income-tax in the Madras region, as guided by the Madras Act of 1955.
important_notes: This Act specifically revives the Madras Plantations Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1955.
The revival is deemed effective from April 1, 1957.

important_rules: Rule 1: Every member of the Board shall be entitled to hold office for a period of two years from the date of his nomination or election, as the case may be.
Rule 2: A person who ceases to be a member of the Board by reason of expiration of his term of office shall, if he is otherwise qualified, be eligible for re-nomination or re-election.

Rule 3: A member of the Board may be removed from his office by the Government on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity, based on a complaint received from a Hindu, after conducting a detailed inquiry in the prescribed manner.
Rule 4: Meetings of the Board shall be presided over by the President and in his absence by a member chosen by the members present from among themselves.
Rule 5: The quorum for a meeting shall be five.

Rule 6: In case of difference of opinion among the members, decisions shall be taken by a majority of votes, and where the votes are equally divided the President or the person presiding shall have and exercise a casting vote.

Rule 7: The Secretary shall keep the minutes of the proceedings of each meeting in a book to be kept for the purpose which shall be signed by the President or the person presiding and the members present at such meeting.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Board, the Commissioner, and other authorities as designated by the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through provisions outlined in the Act for the administration and regulation of religious and charitable endowments.

rights: Right to hold office for a period of two years.
Right to be eligible for re-nomination or re-election if otherwise qualified.
duties: Members shall take an oath before the Commissioner stating they are persons professing Hindu religious rites and are believers of God and temple worship.
Members must not be disqualified for nomination or election.
Members shall not be removed from office except under specific provisions and after inquiry.
Members must provide reasonable opportunity of showing cause against removal from office.
Members shall be entitled to honorarium and travelling allowances.
The Board shall ensure proper functioning and shall have Standing Committees.
Standing Committees shall meet at least once in a month.
obligations: Members of the Board shall, before entering office, take an oath.
Members of the Board shall be subject to disqualifications.
The Board shall constitute Standing Committees for specific functions.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Election of members to the Board shall be conducted by the Government, by notification in the Gazette, appointing a Secretary to Government, who is a Hindu, as the Chief Commissioner to exercise all powers and perform all duties of the Board under this Act.
Procedure 2: Meetings of the Board shall be convened by the Secretary and held on the direction of the President, or by a requisition by not less than three members.
Procedure 3: The Board shall nominate one member of each Standing Committee as its Chairman.
Procedure 4: Recommendations of the Standing Committees shall be unanimous, and in case of difference of opinion among the members, it shall be placed before the Board for decision.
administration: The Board and its officers, including the Commissioner, Assistant Commissioners, and Deputy Commissioners, as well as the Government.
important_notes: Explanation for the purpose of section 7: "Scheduled Castes" and "Scheduled Tribes" shall have the same meaning as is assigned to them in clauses (24) and (25) respectively, of article 366 of the Constitution of India.
Provided that a member shall not be removed under sub-section, unless he is given a reasonable opportunity of showing cause against his removal.
Provided that nothing contained in this section shall prevent the Board from providing a conveyance facility to the President.
The Act provides for the constitution of Standing Committees for Finance and Resource Mobilization, Works, Development and Environment, and Establishment, Temple Arts and Devotional service.

important_rules: Members of the Board shall hold office for a term of two years from the date of his nomination or election, and shall be eligible for re-nomination or re-election.

A person shall be qualified for nomination or election as a member of the Board only if he is a permanent resident of the Malabar area, professes the Hindu religion, is a believer of temple worship, and has completed the age of fifty years.

A member of the Board shall, before entering office, take an oath before the Commissioner of the Board stating that he is a person professing Hindu religious rites and is a believer of God and temple worship.

No person shall be eligible for nomination or election as a member of the Board if he is of unsound mind, is an undischarged insolvent, is an office-holder or a servant of the Government, a Local Authority, or a Devaswom Board, or is interested in an existing contract for the supply of any material to the Board or for executing any work on behalf of the Board, or has been convicted by a criminal court for any offence involving moral turpitude, or is a Member of the Parliament or of the Legislature of any State or of a Local Self Government Institution, or has been removed from holding any office in pursuance of a court order.
The Board shall consist of members from different classes of citizens, shall have a common seal, and shall be a body corporate.
The Board shall have a President and members, and shall meet at least once in a month.
The quorum for a meeting shall be five.
Decisions shall be taken by a majority of votes.
The Secretary shall keep the minutes of the proceedings of each meeting in a book to be kept for the purpose which shall be signed by the President and the members present at such meeting.

The Board shall constitute its proper functioning, the following Standing Committees: Standing Committee on Finance and Resource Mobilization, Standing Committee on Works, Development and Environment, and Standing Committee on Establishment, Temple Arts and Devotional service.
The Board shall nominate one member of each Standing Committee as its Chairman.

rights: Right to re-nomination or re-election for members (subject to eligibility).
Members are entitled to honorarium and travelling allowances.
duties: Members shall take an oath before assuming office.
Members shall attend meetings and contribute to the Board's functions.
The Board and its members are responsible for the proper administration of religious and charitable endowments.
obligations: Members must be of sound mind and not be undischarged insolvents.
Members must not have conflicts of interest with contracts of the Board.
Members must not have been convicted of moral turpitude.
Members must not hold certain other political or government offices.
Members must not have been removed from office by a court order.
Members must not be involved in the business of production or sale of liquor.
Members shall not be removed from office except under specific circumstances, and after a reasonable opportunity to show cause.

key_procedures: Nomination and election of Board members based on specified qualifications and procedures.
Taking of oath by members before assuming office.
Conduct of Board meetings with a quorum of five and decisions by majority vote.
Establishment and functioning of Standing Committees for specific areas.
Procedure for election of members of the Board by any person authorized by the Governor of Kerala.
The election of the members shall be held in accordance with the rules specified in the Schedule II, by the person commissioned by the Governor to preside over the meeting.
administration: The Act refers to the 'Commissioner' and the 'Board' in the context of administration. The Devaswom Board is likely the primary administrative body.

The Act commenced on the 9th day of January, 2008.
Explanation provided for the purpose of Section 7 regarding 'Scheduled Castes' and 'Scheduled Tribes'.

title: THE MALABAR TENANCY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1960
purpose: To amend the Malabar Tenancy Act, 1929.
scope: Applies to the Malabar region, specifically concerning tenancy matters governed by the Malabar Tenancy Act, 1929.

main_sections.description: This section likely provides the short title of the Act and specifies when it comes into force.
This section details amendments to section 50 of the Malabar Tenancy Act, 1929, which pertains to the revision of average market price of crops.

important_rules: Rule 1: The Collector may revise the average market price of any crop published under sub-section (1) if satisfied that such revision is necessary on the ground of new evidence or objection not made available for consideration by him at the time of the publication of the average market price, or on account of some mistake or error apparent on the face of the record or for any other sufficient reason. The average market price so revised shall be published in the District Gazette.

Rule 2: The Collector shall cause notice to be given to the public, in such manner as he thinks fit, of the revision proposed to be made and consider objections, if any, received within the time fixed therefor in the notice.

Rule 3: Where the average market price fixed under sub-section (1) has subsequently been revised under sub-section (1A) and any decree or order has been passed by a court for payment of rent or underpayments on the basis of the market price published under sub-section (1), such decree or order shall, on application by any person affected by such decree or order, be re-opened and modified on the basis of the revised rates. Any application for such re-opening and modification may be made, within two months from the date of such revision, to the court which passed such decree or order, or to the court to which execution of such decree or order is pending, and the court shall pass appropriate orders on such application.
key_procedures: Procedure 1: Revision of average market price by the Collector: If the Collector believes revision is necessary due to new evidence or an overlooked objection, or a mistake in the record, they can revise the average market price of any crop. This revised price must be published in the District Gazette.
Procedure 2: Public notice and objections: Before revising the market price, the Collector must notify the public in the prescribed manner and allow for objections within a specified time.

Procedure 3: Re-opening and modification of court orders: If a court order (for rent or underpayments) was based on a previous market price that is later revised, any affected person can apply to the court that issued the order (or the court handling its execution) to re-open and modify the order based on the new rates. This application must be made within two months of the revision.
administration: Likely the relevant revenue or land reforms department of the Kerala government.
important_notes: The Act was received the assent of the President on 23rd December, 1960 and published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 30th December, 1960.
The Act amends Section 50 of the Malabar Tenancy Act, 1929, specifically addressing the process of revising and applying market prices for rent calculations.

title: The Mappila Marumakkathayam (Amendment) Act, 1963
purpose: To amend the Mappila Marumakkathayam Act, 1939 (Madras Act 17 of 1939) for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to all Muslims following the Marumakkathayam law, who are either domiciled in the State of Kerala, or have property situate within the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Mappila Marumakkathayam (Amendment) Act, 1963. It shall come into force at once.
In the Preamble to the Mappila Marumakkathayam Act, 1939 (Madras Act XVII of 1939), herein-after referred to as the principal Act, for the word "Mappilas", the word "Muslims" shall be substituted.
In sub-section (a), for the word "Mappila", the word "Muslim" shall be substituted.

After section 13 of the principal Act, the following section shall be inserted, namely :-"13-A. Devolution of interest in the property of Tarwad. - When any member of a Muslim Tarwad dies after the date of publication of the Mappila Marumakkathayam (Amendment) Bill, 1963, in the Gazette, namely 3rd September 1963, having at the time of his or her death an interest in the property of the Tarwad, his or her interest in the property shall devolve according to the Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) and not according to the Marumakkathayam Law. Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, any person on whom such right devolves may claim to take his or her share of the properties of the Tarwad.
Explanation. - For the purposes of this section, the interest of a member of a Muslim Tarwad in the property of the Tarwad shall be deemed to be the share in the property of the Tarwad that would have fallen to him or her if a partition of that property per capita had been made immediately before his or her death among the members of the Tarwad then existing, and such share shall be deemed to have been allotted to him or her absolutely."

important_rules: Rule: All Muslims following Marumakkathayam law domiciled in Kerala or owning property in Kerala are subject to this Act.
Rule: Upon the death of a member of a Muslim Tarwad, their interest in the Tarwad property devolves according to Muslim Personal Law (Shariat), not Marumakkathayam Law.
Rule: Individuals who inherit an interest in Tarwad property under Muslim Personal Law can claim their share.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text.

rights: Right to inherit Tarwad property according to Muslim Personal Law upon death of a member.
Right to claim a share of Tarwad properties for those inheriting under Muslim Personal Law.

key_procedures: Procedure: Amendment of the Preamble of the Mappila Marumakkathayam Act, 1939, to replace 'Mappilas' with 'Muslims'.
Procedure: Amendment of Section 1(a) of the principal Act to replace 'Mappila' with 'Muslim'.
Procedure: Insertion of a new section (13-A) detailing the devolution of interest in Tarwad property for Muslim members upon their death.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided text.
important_notes: Received the assent of the President on the 30th day of October, 1963 and published in the Gazette Extraordinary, dated 4th November, 1963.

The amendment regarding the devolution of property interest applies when a Muslim Tarwad member dies after the publication of the Mappila Marumakkathayam (Amendment) Bill, 1963, in the Gazette (September 3, 1963).

title: THE MINIMUM WAGES (KERALA AMENDMENT) ACT, 1960
purpose: An Act to amend the Minimum Wages Act, 1948, in its application to the State of Kerala.
scope: The whole of the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Minimum Wages (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1960. It also specifies its extent, applying to the whole of the State of Kerala, and that it shall come into force at once.

This section amends section 3 of the Minimum Wages Act, 1948 (Central Act 11 of 1948). It deals with the fixation of minimum rates of wages in respect of employment specified in Part I and Part II of the Schedule to the Act. The amendment clarifies that the appropriate Government, in relation to the State Government, shall have effect in the State of Kerala subject to the amendments specified in sub-section (2). It further modifies sub-section (1) of section 3 by replacing the words "the appropriate Government" with "The State Government" and by substituting clause (a) with specific provisions regarding the date for fixing figures, letters, and words. It also inserts a further proviso for fixing minimum rates of wages by notification in the Gazette. An explanation is provided for the purposes of this proviso, concerning employees employed in a particular locality or in any process or branch of work not existing at the time.

important_rules: The State Government may, from time to time, fix by notification in the Gazette, the minimum rates of wages payable to employees.
The proviso to sub-section (1) of section 3 of the Principal Act is to be amended, allowing for the insertion of further provisions related to fixing minimum rates of wages.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The State Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications in the Gazette.

key_procedures: The State Government may fix minimum rates of wages by notification in the Gazette.
The amendment involves substituting specific words and clauses within section 3 of the Principal Act to update provisions related to the fixation of minimum wages.
administration: State Government (implied)
important_notes: The amendment received the assent of the President on 10th September, 1960 and was published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 22nd September, 1960.
The amendment is effective from the Eleventh Year of the Republic of India.
Explanation regarding employees employed in a particular locality or in any process or branch of work not existing at the time minimum rates of wages were fixed.

title: The Motor Vehicles (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1969
purpose: To further amend the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, in its application to the State of Kerala.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala and amends the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Motor Vehicles (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1969. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 47, Central Act IV of 1939
main_sections.description: Amends clause (c) of sub-section (1) of section 47 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, by inserting a new clause regarding the publication of a scheme under section 68C in respect of service of stage carriages.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 58, Central Act IV of 1939
main_sections.description: Amends sub-section (2) of section 58 of the Principal Act, by inserting a new provision stating that notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in this Chapter, the Regional Transport Authority shall, in considering an application for the renewal of a stage carriage permit, have regard also to the publication of a scheme under section 68C in respect of service of stage carriages.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new section 68CC in Central Act IV of 1939
main_sections.description: Inserts a new section 68CC into the Principal Act. This new section deals with the issue of temporary permits to the State Transport Undertaking. It states that notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in Chapter IV or in this Chapter, after the date of publication of a scheme under section 68C in respect of service of stage carriages, whether such publication was before or after the date of commencement of the Motor Vehicles (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1969, the State Transport Undertaking may apply for a temporary permit in respect of the area or route or portion thereof, specified in the said scheme, and on such application the Regional Transport Authority shall issue such temporary permit to the State Transport Undertaking. It also specifies that a temporary permit issued under this sub-section shall be effective till the grant of permit to the State Transport Undertaking under sub-section (1) of section 68F. Provided that if the scheme is not approved under sub-section (2) of section 68D, the temporary permit shall be effective till the expiration of a period of one week from the date of refusal to approve the scheme under sub-section (2) of section 68D.

States that all applications for, and proceedings relating to, the grant of a stage carriage permit or the renewal of a stage carriage permit, pending before any Court, authority or officer on the date of commencement of this Act shall be disposed of under the principal Act, as amended by this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Regional Transport Authority

key_procedures: Application for renewal of a stage carriage permit must have regard to the publication of a scheme under section 68C.
State Transport Undertaking may apply for a temporary permit for a specified area or route if a scheme under section 68C is published.
Temporary permits issued to State Transport Undertaking are effective until a regular permit is granted or until one week after the refusal to approve a scheme.
Pending applications and proceedings related to stage carriage permits or renewals will be disposed of under the amended Act.
important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 129, dated 23rd May, 1969.

title: The Motor Vehicles (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1971
purpose: An Act further to amend the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939 (Central Act 4 of 1939).
scope: The Act shall extend to the whole of the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Motor Vehicles (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1971. It shall extend to the whole of the State of Kerala.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Sixth Schedule, Central Act 4 of 1939.
main_sections.description: In the Sixth Schedule to the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939 (Central Act 4 of 1939), for the letters "KL" occurring in the second column, the letters "KL, KR" shall be substituted.

important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 482, dated 4th November, 1971.

title: The Motor Vehicles (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1976
purpose: To further amend the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, in its application to the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Motor Vehicles (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1976. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.

Amends section 59 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939 (Central Act 4 of 1939). The amendment inserts a new subsection (1A) which deals with granting permission for transfer of permits under certain conditions, particularly concerning the provisions of the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Payment of Fair Wages Act, 1971, and other relevant enactments.

important_rules: Rule 1: Before granting permission for transfer of permits, the transport authority shall make such enquiry as it may deem necessary to satisfy itself that the transfer asked for is bona fide and not likely to defeat the provisions of the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Payment of Fair Wages Act, 1971, or any other law in force.
Rule 2: If after enquiry, the transport authority finds the transfer is not bona fide or is likely to defeat the provisions of the relevant Acts, it shall not grant permission for the transfer.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Transport authority
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the process of granting or denying permission for transfer of permits.

rights: Right to apply for bona fide transfer of permits.
duties: Duty of the transport authority to enquire into the bona fides of the transfer request.
Duty to consider the provisions of the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Payment of Fair Wages Act, 1971, and other relevant laws.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Application for transfer of permit.
Procedure 2: Enquiry by the transport authority to ascertain if the transfer is bona fide and does not defeat the provisions of relevant Acts.
Procedure 3: Decision by the transport authority to grant or refuse permission for the transfer based on the enquiry.
administration: Transport Department/Authority of the State of Kerala
important_notes: The amendment was necessitated to address concerns related to the bona fide nature of permit transfers and to ensure compliance with the Kerala Motor Transport Workers' Payment of Fair Wages Act, 1971.
The Act was received the assent of the President on the 16th day of February, 1977, and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 135 dated 26th February, 1977.

title: The Motor Vehicles (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1993
purpose: To amend the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, in its application to the State of Kerala.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala and amends the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Motor Vehicles (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1993. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 26th day of February, 1993.

In section 71 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (Central Act 59 of 1988), in sub-section (4), for the words "five" and "ten", the words "ten" and "fifty" shall be substituted, respectively. For the words "any company", the words "any co-operative society or to any company" shall be substituted.

The Motor Vehicles (Kerala Amendment) Ordinance, 1993 (3 of 1993) is hereby repealed. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act, as amended by the said Ordinance, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act, as amended by this Act.

important_notes: Received the assent of the President on the 19th day of April 1993 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 465 dated the 22nd April 1993.

title: The Motor Vehicles (Kerala Second Amendment) Act, 1971
purpose: To further amend the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, in its application to the State of Kerala.
scope: The Act applies to the whole of the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Motor Vehicles (Kerala Second Amendment) Act, 1971, and it extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.

This section omits section 43A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939 (Central Act 4 of 1939), which was inserted by section 3 of the Motor Vehicles (Madras Amendment) Act, 1948, and amended by section 2 of the Motor Vehicles (Madras Amendment) Act, 1954.

This section inserts a new section 43A after section 43 of the principal Act. The new section deals with the power of the State Government to issue orders and directions to Transport Authorities regarding matters like road transport. It also specifies the State Government's power to direct the State Transport Authority or any Regional Transport Authority to open new routes or extend existing ones, or to reduce the number of stage carriages on specified routes.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government, State Transport Authority, Regional Transport Authority
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By issuing orders and directions of a general character relating to road transport.

key_procedures: The State Government may issue orders and directions concerning road transport.
The State Government may direct the opening of new routes, extension of existing routes, or reduction of stage carriages on specified routes.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be managed by transport authorities under the State Government.
important_notes: The Act is published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 436, dated 5th October 1971.
Section 43A is amended to allow the State Government to issue orders and directions.
Section 43A also allows the State Government to direct the opening of new routes or extension of existing ones.

title: The Motor Vehicles (Kerala Third Amendment) Act, 1971
purpose: To amend the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, in its application to the State of Kerala, specifically concerning the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and is applicable to motor vehicles, stage carriages, contract carriages, and public carriers within the State.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Motor Vehicles (Kerala Third Amendment) Act, 1971. It also states that it extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall be deemed to have come into force on the first day of June, 1971.

This section details the amendment to section 43 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939. It includes provisions regarding the inclusion of tax payable by passengers or consignors of goods in fares and freights for stage carriages, contract carriages, and public carriers. It also addresses revised rates of fares for stage carriages and the collection and refund of taxes.

This section provides for the validation of directions relating to fares for stage carriages issued by the Government on or after the first day of March 1963, and the revision of fares for stage carriages. It also states that no suit or other proceedings shall be maintained or continued against the Government or any other authority for any refund of any tax collected, and no court shall enforce any decree or order directing the refund of any tax collected.

This section deals with savings. It states that notwithstanding the cessation of operation of the Motor Vehicles (Kerala Amendment) Ordinance, 1971, anything done or action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act. It also covers investigations, legal proceedings, or remedies instituted, continued, or enforced under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance. Furthermore, it clarifies that no person shall be convicted of any offence committed after the cessation of operation of the said Ordinance and before the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette.

important_rules: Fares and freights for stage carriages, contract carriages, and public carriers shall be inclusive of the tax payable by passengers or consignors of goods.
Revised rates of fares for stage carriages fixed by the State Transport Authority are deemed to be inclusive of the tax payable.
All taxes collected or purported to have been collected from operators of stage carriages shall be deemed to be, and to have always been validly collected in accordance with law.
No suit or other proceedings shall be maintained or continued against the Government or any other authority or person whatsoever for the refund of any tax so collected.
No court shall enforce any decree or order directing the refund of any tax so collected.
No person shall be convicted of any offence committed after the cessation of operation of the said Ordinance and before the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette.

penalties: No penalty or punishment shall be imposed under the provisions of the Principal Act as amended by this Act for any offence committed after the cessation of operation of the said Ordinance and before the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government, State Transport Authority, and Courts (for legal proceedings).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through Government directions, revised fare structures, collection of taxes, and legal proceedings.

rights: Right to have fares and freights inclusive of tax.
Right to have revised rates of fares deemed inclusive of tax.
Protection from refund of taxes collected.
duties: Duty to operate stage carriages, contract carriages, and public carriers in accordance with the amended provisions.
Duty to collect taxes as per the law.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the amended Motor Vehicles Act, 1939.

key_procedures: Issuance of directions by the Government regarding fares for stage carriages.
Revision of fares for stage carriages by the State Transport Authority.
Collection and remission of taxes by operators of stage carriages.
Maintenance and continuation of legal proceedings related to the Act.
Publication of the Act in the Gazette for commencement.
administration: State Transport Authority and Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act is a third amendment to the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, specifically for the State of Kerala.
The provisions relating to tax collection and refund are validated for the period specified.
The savings clause ensures continuity of actions taken under the previous Ordinance and protects against retrospective penalties for offences committed during a specific transitional period.

title: The Motor Vehicles (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1968
purpose: To amend the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, in its application to the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Kerala, amending provisions related to motor vehicles permits.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Motor Vehicles (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1968, and specifies that it extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.

Amends sub-section (1) of section 47 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939 (Central Act 4 of 1939). It substitutes the proviso to give preference to applications for stage carriage permits from the Kerala State Road Transport Corporation, and then to co-operative societies, over applications from individual owners, provided other conditions are equal.

important_rules: Rule 1: Applications for stage carriage permits from the Kerala State Road Transport Corporation shall be given preference over other applications, assuming other conditions are equal.

Rule 2: Subject to the preference given to the Kerala State Road Transport Corporation, applications for stage carriage permits from co-operative societies registered under relevant enactments shall be given preference over applications from individual owners, assuming other conditions are equal.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated within the provided text, but implied to be the authorities responsible for implementing the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the application and enforcement of the amended provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, in Kerala.

rights: The Kerala State Road Transport Corporation has a right to preference for stage carriage permits under specified conditions.
Co-operative societies have a right to preference for stage carriage permits over individual owners under specified conditions.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Application for a stage carriage permit is made.
Procedure 2: The application is evaluated based on the conditions stipulated in section 47, including the preference given to the Kerala State Road Transport Corporation and co-operative societies.
Procedure 3: A decision on the permit is made, adhering to the preferential treatment outlined in the amendment.
administration: Not explicitly stated within the provided text, but likely falls under the Transport Department or related agencies of the Kerala State Government.
important_notes: The amendment focuses on preferential treatment for permit applications.
The preference is conditional on 'other conditions being equal'.

title: The Municipal Amendment Act, 1956
purpose: To further amend the Travancore District Municipalities Act, 1920, the Cochin Municipal Act, 1911, and the Madras District Municipalities Act, 1920, and to make provisions for the application of certain amendments.
scope: Applies to the areas governed by the Travancore District Municipalities Act, 1920, the Cochin Municipal Act, 1911, and the Madras District Municipalities Act, 1920.

key_definitions.person: Includes also the manager of a joint Hindu or Marumakkathayam family.
key_definitions.aggregate income: Shall not include dearness or local allowances or allowances for house rent, carriage hire or travelling expenses.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Municipal (Amendment) Act, 1956. It shall come into force at once, except clause (i) of section 2, clause (ii) of section 3 and clause (iii) of section 4 shall have to come into force on the 1st day of April, 1955, and the rest of this Act shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

Amends the Travancore District Municipalities Act, 1116, by inserting new sub-sections in section 34 and section 91, and by substituting words in various sections, including those related to 'dearness or local allowances' and 'aggregate income'.

Amends the Cochin Municipal Act, 1116, by substituting words and phrases in various sections, including those pertaining to 'our Government', 'the Collector', 'house rent', 'carriage hire', and 'travelling expenses'. It also includes provisions for the Collector's power to enforce execution of resolutions and immediate action for necessary grounds referred to in a clause.

Amends the Cochin Municipal Act, 1113, by substituting words like 'dearness or local allowances', 'house rent', 'carriage hire', and 'travelling expenses'. It also includes provisions for the substitution of 'Government' and 'Collector' in various contexts, and for cases where a company or person proves that it or he has paid a profession tax under another Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Amendments made by this Act shall come into force on dates specified in section 1.
Rule 2: For the purposes of section 3, 'aggregate income' shall not include dearness or local allowances or allowances for house rent, carriage hire or travelling expenses.
Rule 3: Provisions regarding the profession tax payable by companies or persons under other Acts are detailed.

penalties: Not explicitly detailed in the provided pages, but implied through amendments relating to profession tax and enforcement of resolutions.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government and the Collector.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers granted to the Government and the Collector to issue notifications, appoint dates, and enforce resolutions.

rights: Right of the Government to appoint dates for the commencement of certain provisions.
Right of the Collector to make remarks on the report submitted by the municipal council.
Right of the Government to apportion tax between local authorities.
duties: Duty of the Government to submit a report to the Collector for information.
Duty of the municipal council to submit reports to the Government.
obligations: Obligation for persons or companies to pay profession tax as specified.
Obligation to adhere to amendments made by the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Notification by the Government to bring certain sections into force.
Procedure 2: Submission of reports by the municipal council to the Government and by the Government to the Collector.
Procedure 3: Process for the Collector to enter on and inspect, or cause to be entered and inspected, any immovable property or any work in progress under the control of any municipal authority.
Procedure 4: Action by the Collector in case of necessary grounds referred to in a clause, including seeking resolution or order from the Government.
administration: The Government of Kerala, and Municipal Authorities.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to existing Municipal Acts in Kerala.
Certain provisions have retrospective effect from April 1, 1955.
Specific definitions for 'person' and 'aggregate income' are provided for the purposes of this Act.

title: THE MUNICIPAL LAWS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1958
purpose: An Act further to amend the Trivandrum City Municipal Act, the Travancore District Municipalities Act, 1116 and the Cochin Municipal Act, XVIII of 1113.
scope: Applies to the Trivandrum City Municipal Act, the Travancore District Municipalities Act, 1116 and the Cochin Municipal Act, XVIII of 1113.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Municipal Laws (Amendment) Act, 1958. It shall come into force at noon on the first day of January, 1959 and shall cease to be in force at noon on the first day of September, 1962, except as respects things done or omitted to be done before noon on that date, and section 4 of the Interpretation and General Clauses Act, 1125 (VII of 1125), shall apply upon the expiry of this Act as if it had then been repealed by an Act of the Kerala State Legislature.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of term of office of Mayor, chairmen and councillors.
main_sections.description: Nothing contrary to the provisions of section 29 and 57 of the Trivandrum City Municipal Act (IV of 1116) or section 8 of the Travancore District Municipalities Act, 1116 (XXIII of 1116) or section 8 of the Cochin Municipal Act, XVIII of 1113, shall apply to the Mayor, the chairmen of standing committees and the councillors of the Corporation of the City of Trivandrum constituted under the Trivandrum City Municipal Act and of the councillors of every municipality constituted under the Travancore District Municipalities Act, 1116 or the Cochin Municipal Act, XVIII of 1113, holding office at the commencement of this Act. This extension shall last up to noon on the first day of September, 1959.

main_sections.section_title: Section 29 of the Trivandrum City Municipal Act to have effect subject to certain modifications.
main_sections.description: The provisions of section 29 of the Trivandrum City Municipal Act (IV of 1116) shall, in their application to the election of the Mayor and the chairman of each standing committee in the year 1959, have effect as if for the words "first day of January", the words and figures "first day of September, 1959" were substituted and the words "in each year" in both the places where they occur were omitted.

main_sections.section_title: Date of elections and term of office of councillors.
main_sections.description: The provisions of the Trivandrum City Municipal Act (IV of 1116), the Travancore District Municipalities Act, 1116, and the Cochin Municipal Act, XVIII of 1113, shall have effect, subject to the following modifications, namely: (a) The Government shall— (i) cause elections to be held, and make appointments of councillors, to the Corporation of the City of Trivandrum so that the newly elected and appointed councillors may come into office on the first day of September, 1959, and (ii) cause elections to be held to every municipality constituted under the Travancore Municipal Act, 1116 or the Cochin Municipal Act, XVIII of 1113, so that the newly elected councillors may come into office on the first day of September, 1959. (b) The term of office of the newly elected or appointed councillors shall expire at noon on the first day of September, 1962.

main_sections.section_title: Supersession of council on expressing opinion against extension of term.
main_sections.description: (1) Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in section 2, where the council of the Corporation of the City of Trivandrum or the council of a municipality constituted under the Travancore District Municipalities Act, 1116 or the Cochin Municipal Act, XVIII of 1113, has, before the commencement of this Act, passed a resolution with the support of not less than three-fourths of the number of councillors present and voting, expressing opinion against such extension, or passes such a resolution with such support after the commencement of this Act, it shall be lawful for the Government, by notification in the Gazette, to supersede the council till the first day of September, 1959. (2) The supersession shall take effect from such date as may be specified in the notification or, if no date is therein specified, from the noon on the date of publication of the notification and thereupon the following consequences shall ensue: (a) All the members of the council including the Mayor and chairman of standing committees or the chairman or vice-chairman, as the case may be, shall forthwith be deemed to have vacated their offices. (b) All or any of the functions of the council and of the Mayor and chairmen of standing committees or the chairman and vice-chairman, as the case may be, including where the chairman is also the executive authority, his functions as such may, during the period of supersession, be exercised and performed, as far as may be, and to such extent as the Government may determine, by a special officer appointed by the Government in that behalf and such special officer may, if the Government so direct, receive payment for his services from the municipal fund. (3) When a council is superseded under this section, the Government, until the date of the reconstitution thereof and the reconstituted council thereafter, shall be entitled to all the assets and be subject to all the liabilities of the council on the date of the supersession and on the date of the reconstitution respectively.

If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act or of the Trivandrum City Municipal Act (IV of 1116) or the Travancore District Municipalities Act, 1116 or the Cochin Municipal Act, XVIII of 1113, as amended by this Act, the Government may, as occasion may require, by order, do anything which appears to them necessary for the purpose of removing the difficulty.

important_rules: All members of the council, including the Mayor and chairman of standing committees or the chairman or vice-chairman, shall be deemed to have vacated their offices upon supersession of the council.

The Mayor, chairmen of standing committees, and councillors of the Corporation of the City of Trivandrum, and councillors of municipalities under the Travancore District Municipalities Act, 1116 or the Cochin Municipal Act, XVIII of 1113, shall continue in office until noon on the first day of September, 1959.
Newly elected councillors shall take office on the first day of September, 1959.
The term of office for newly elected councillors shall expire on the first day of September, 1962.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications, orders, and appointment of special officers.

duties: The Government has the duty to cause elections to be held and make appointments of councillors.
The Government is entitled to all assets and subject to all liabilities of a superseded council.
obligations: The superseded council's assets and liabilities devolve upon the Government until reconstitution.

key_procedures: Superseding a council: Requires a resolution with support from at least three-fourths of present and voting councillors, expressing opinion against the extension of term. The Government may then supersede the council by notification.
Exercise of functions during supersession: A special officer appointed by the Government can exercise the functions of the council, Mayor, and chairmen.
Removal of difficulties: The Government can issue orders to resolve any difficulties arising from the Act or amended acts.
administration: The Government
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to existing municipal laws.
The provisions of section 4 of the Interpretation and General Clauses Act, 1125 (VII of 1125), apply upon the expiry of this Act as if it had been repealed.
The term of office extension is temporary, with specific end dates.
The Government has broad powers to remove difficulties.

title: The Municipal (Temporary Provisions) Act, 1953
purpose: To amend certain Municipal Acts and to make temporary provisions for the functioning of Municipal Councils.
scope: Applies to the Travancore City Municipal Act, IV of 1948, the Travancore District Municipalities Act, 1116 (XXIII of 1116) and the Cochin Municipal Act, XVIII of 1113.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Municipal (Temporary Provisions) Act, 1953, and it shall come into force at once. It shall cease to be in force at noon on the first day of January 1956 except as respects things done or omitted to be done before noon on that date. Section 7 of the Travancore-Cochin Interpretation and General Clauses Act, 1125 (VII of 1125) shall apply as if this Act had then been repealed by an Act of the Travancore-Cochin State Legislature.

main_sections.section_title: The Municipal Acts to have effect subject to certain modifications.
main_sections.description:
During the continuance in force of this Act, the provisions of the Travancore City Municipal Act, IV of 1116, the Travancore District Municipalities Act, 1116 (XXIII of 1116), and the Cochin Municipal Act, XVIII of 1113 shall have effect subject to the following modifications:
