(1) In the Travancore City Municipal Act, IV of 1116, to sub-section (1) of Section 57, the following proviso shall be added, namely:-
"Provided that, in the case of the Council constituted immediately before the commencement of the Municipal (Temporary Provisions) Act, 1953, the term of office of the Councillors shall be for the period beginning at noon on the fifteenth day of February 1953 and expiring at noon on the first day of January 1956".
(2) In the Travancore District Municipalities Act, 1116 (XXIII of 1116) —
(a) for the proviso to sub-section (1) of Section 8, the following proviso shall be substituted, namely :-
"Provided that, in the case of the Councils constituted immediately before the commencement of the Municipal (Temporary Provisions) Act, 1953, the term of office of the Councillors shall be for the period beginning at noon on the fifteenth day of February 1953 and expiring at noon on the first day of January 1956".
(b) after Section 392, the following section shall be inserted, namely:-
"392A. Special provisions in the case of newly constituted Councils.—(1) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, when a Municipality is constituted for the first time, the Government may appoint a Special Officer to exercise the powers, discharge the duties and perform the functions of a Municipal Council and its Chairman and Executive Authority.
(2) The Special Officer shall cause arrangements for election to be made so that the newly elected Councillors may come into office on a day to be fixed by the Government.
(3) The Special Officer shall exercise the powers, discharge the duties and perform the functions of the Municipal Council until a Chairman has been elected, or the Executive Authority until a Chairman has been elected or a Commissioner has been appointed, as the case may be.
(4) As soon as may be after the constitution of the Council, a meeting of the Council shall be held on a day and at a time fixed by the Special Officer for the election of a Chairman. If at such meeting no Chairman is elected, a fresh election shall be held on such day and at such time as may be fixed by the Special Officer.
(5) The term of office of the Councillors or of the Councillors elected in their places at casual vacancies shall expire at the end of three years if the day referred to in sub-section (2) is the first day of January and in other cases at the end of three years from the first day of January immediately preceding such day.
(3) In the Cochin Municipal Act, XVIII of 1113 —
(a) to sub-section (1) of Section 8, the following proviso shall be added, namely: —
"Provided that, in the case of the Councils constituted immediately before the commencement of the Municipal (Temporary Provisions) Act, 1953, the term of office of the Councillors shall be for the period beginning at noon on the fifteenth day of February 1953 and expiring at noon on the first day of January 1956".
(b) in sub-section (5) of Section 374, for the word "November" in both places where it occurs, the word "January" shall be substituted.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 365, Act IV of 1116.—
main_sections.description:
Until such time as a fresh division of the City into territorial divisions becomes necessary, Section 365 of the Travancore City Municipal Act, IV of 1116, shall have effect as if —
(i) the opening paragraph, for the words "and the power to issue notifications under Section 46 are", the words "shall be" were substituted; and
(ii) in clause (a), the words "or notification" were omitted.

main_sections.section_title: Budget provisions of Municipal Acts to have effect subject to certain modifications.

main_sections.description:
(1) The Municipal (Temporary Provisions) Ordinance, 1952 (IV of 1952) is hereby repealed.
(2) The repeal by this Act of the said Ordinance shall not affect the previous operation thereof, and any order made, action taken, thing done or notification issued in the exercise of any powers conferred by the said Ordinance shall, for all purposes, be deemed to have been made, taken, done or issued in the exercise of powers conferred by this Act, and if this Act were in force at the time such order was made, action was taken, thing done or notification was issued.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government, Special Officer
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Appointments of Special Officers, conduct of elections, exercise of powers and discharge of duties by Special Officers.

key_procedures: Election of Chairman: A meeting of the Council shall be held to elect a Chairman. If no Chairman is elected, a fresh election shall be held.
Arrangement for Election: The Special Officer shall arrange for elections so that newly elected Councillors can take office on a date fixed by the Government.
administration: Government of Travancore-Cochin
important_notes: The Act is temporary and will cease to be in force on January 1, 1956.
Special provisions are made for the term of office of councillors in newly constituted municipalities.
A Special Officer can be appointed to manage municipalities until a Chairman is elected or a Commissioner is appointed.
The Municipal (Temporary Provisions) Ordinance, 1952, is repealed, but actions taken under it are deemed valid under this Act.

title: The Municipal and Panchayats (Amendment) Act, 1955
purpose: To further amend the Cochin Municipal Act, XVIII of 1113 and the Travancore-Cochin Panchayats Act, 1950.
scope: Applies to Municipalities and Panchayats within the purview of the Cochin Municipal Act and the Travancore-Cochin Panchayats Act.

key_definitions.director: Means the Director of Local Bodies appointed by the Government and includes an acting or officiating Director and also any officer appointed by the Government to exercise or to be in charge of the functions of the Director.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Municipal and Panchayats (Amendment) Act, 1955, and it shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new Section 367A in the Cochin Municipal Act, XVIII of 1113.
main_sections.description: Inserts Section 367A into the Cochin Municipal Act, XVIII of 1113. This new section deals with the delegation of powers by the Government to any person through notification in the Gazette, with exceptions for powers mentioned in specific chapters. It also outlines powers to fix contribution amounts, make rules, alter, add to, or cancel Schedules, and sanction prosecutions.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 2 of the Travancore-Cochin Panchayats Act, 1950.
main_sections.description: Amends clause (4) of Section 2 of the Travancore-Cochin Panchayats Act, 1950. The substituted clause provides the definition of 'Director'.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government (for delegation of powers and sanctioning prosecutions)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notification in the Gazette for delegation of powers.

key_procedures: Delegation of powers by the Government through notification in the Gazette.
Amendment of existing Acts requires substitution of clauses or insertion of new sections.
administration: Department of Local Bodies (implied by the definition of 'Director')
important_notes: The Act was enacted in the Sixth Year of the Republic of India.
The Act came into force at once upon enactment.

title: The Municipal (Temporary Provisions) Amendment Act, 1956
purpose: To amend the Municipal (Temporary Provisions) Amendment Act, 1953, by extending the term of office for certain municipal authorities and providing for other related matters.
scope: Applies to municipalities in Kerala and specifically mentions the Trivandrum City Municipal Act, 1948, and other relevant municipal acts and ordinances in effect.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Municipal (Temporary Provisions) Amendment Act, 1956, and that it shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 1, Act III of 1953
main_sections.description: Amends Section 1 of the Municipal (Temporary Provisions) Act, 1953, by substituting 'first day of January, 1959' for 'first day of January, 1956'.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new sections 1A and 1B in Act III of 1953
main_sections.description: Inserts new sections 1A and 1B into the Principal Act. Section 1A extends the term of office of Mayor, Chairman and Councillors. Section 1B makes provisions for the effect of certain modifications on elections.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 2, Act III of 1953
main_sections.description: Amends Section 2 of the Principal Act by substituting provisions regarding the term of office of Councillors.

Repeals the Municipal (Temporary Provisions) Amendment Ordinance, 1955, and specifies that the repeal shall not affect the operation of any order, action taken, or notification issued under the said Ordinance.

important_rules: The term of office of the Mayor, Chairman and Councillors shall be for the period beginning on noon on the fifteenth day of March, 1956, and expiring on noon on the first day of January, 1959.

The provisions of Section 29 of the Trivandrum City Municipal Act, 1948, and Section 8 and 392A of the Travancore District Municipalities Act, 1948 (XXIII of 1948) shall have effect as if for the words 'first day of January, 1956' and 'fifteenth day of March, 1956', the words and figures 'fifteenth day of March, 1956' and 'fifteenth day of March, 1959' in both the places where they occur were omitted.
key_procedures: The Act is effective immediately upon its enactment.
Specific amendments are made to existing sections of the Principal Act (Act III of 1953) by substitution of dates and insertion of new sections.
important_notes: The Preamble highlights that it is expedient to amend the Municipal (Temporary Provisions) Act, 1953 (III of 1953).
This Act was enacted in the Seventh Year of the Republic of India.
Published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 12th March 1956.

title: The Munnar Special Tribunal Act, 2010
purpose: The purpose of the Act is to provide for the establishment of a Special Tribunal for the purpose of hearing and disposing of cases relating to matters arising in Munnar. The Act aims to expedite the resolution of such cases, considering the specific nature and urgency of issues pertaining to the Munnar region.
scope: The Act applies to all matters arising in Munnar that fall within the jurisdiction of the Special Tribunal as defined by the Act. It seems to be applicable to legal proceedings and disputes related to the Munnar area.

key_definitions.tribunal: Refers to the Munnar Special Tribunal established under this Act.
key_definitions.tribunal area: Means the area specified by the Government in this behalf.
key_definitions.matters: Includes all cases, suits, applications or other proceedings of a civil or criminal nature, which are pending before any court or authority or which may be filed or instituted in respect of matters arising in the Tribunal Area.
key_definitions.member: Means a Member of the Tribunal and includes the Presiding Officer.

main_sections.description: Provides for the short title of the Act and its commencement. Mentions that the Act may be called the Munnar Special Tribunal Act, 2010, and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'Tribunal', 'Tribunal Area', 'matters', 'Presiding Officer', 'Member', 'Government', 'notification', etc.

Provides for the establishment of a Special Tribunal by the Government. It specifies the composition of the Tribunal, including the Presiding Officer and other members. The section also details the qualifications and appointment process for the Presiding Officer and members.
Defines the powers and jurisdiction of the Tribunal. It outlines the types of cases and matters that the Tribunal is empowered to hear and decide. This includes matters arising in the Tribunal Area.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and procedure of the Tribunal
main_sections.description: Specifies the powers that the Tribunal can exercise, such as the power to take evidence, summon witnesses, and pass orders. It also lays down the procedure that the Tribunal shall follow while conducting its proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of cases to the Tribunal
main_sections.description: Deals with the transfer of cases from other courts or authorities to the Special Tribunal. It provides for the mechanism and conditions under which such transfers can be made.
Lays down the provisions related to appeals against the orders or decisions of the Tribunal. It specifies the appellate authority and the period within which an appeal can be filed.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act. This includes rules regarding the procedure, powers, and other ancillary matters related to the Tribunal.
States that the provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent contained in any other law for the time being in force.
Empowers the Government to remove any difficulties that may arise in giving effect to the provisions of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of any existing law or provision that is inconsistent with this Act and provides for savings.

important_rules: The Tribunal shall have the same powers as are vested in a Civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, when trying a suit in respect of matters like summoning witnesses, examining them on oath, etc. (Section 5(1)).
The Tribunal shall have the power to pass interim orders in any proceeding before it. (Section 5(2)).

The Tribunal shall not be bound by the procedure laid down by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, or the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, but shall be guided by the principles of natural justice, fairness and equity. (Section 5(3)).

penalties: The Act itself does not explicitly mention specific penalties for non-compliance with its provisions. Penalties would likely be determined by the nature of the offense and any existing laws that the Tribunal is enforcing.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Munnar Special Tribunal is the primary enforcement authority for matters falling under its jurisdiction.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The Tribunal enforces its decisions and orders through the powers vested in it, which are akin to those of a Civil Court. This can include issuing summons, taking evidence, making judgments, and potentially utilizing other legal mechanisms for execution of its orders.

rights: Parties to a case have the right to present their case before the Tribunal.
The right to appeal against the orders of the Tribunal, as provided under Section 7.
duties: Parties are duty-bound to appear before the Tribunal when summoned and to provide truthful evidence.
Individuals and entities are expected to comply with the orders and directions issued by the Tribunal.
obligations: The Act imposes an obligation on the Government to establish and constitute the Special Tribunal.

key_procedures: Filing of cases or applications before the Tribunal.
Summoning of parties and witnesses.
Examination of evidence (oral and documentary).
Hearing of arguments.
Passing of orders or judgments by the Tribunal.
Filing of appeals against the Tribunal's orders, if applicable.
administration: The Act is administered by the Government of Kerala. The specific department responsible for its day-to-day administration is not explicitly stated but would likely fall under the purview of the Law Department or the Revenue Department, depending on the nature of the cases handled by the Tribunal.
important_notes: The Act has an overriding effect, meaning its provisions will prevail over any other conflicting laws. (Section 9).
The Act is intended to expedite the disposal of cases relating to Munnar, indicating a focus on efficiency and timely resolution.
The Government has the power to make rules to facilitate the implementation of the Act. (Section 8).

title: THE MUSLIM PERSONAL LAW (SHARIAT) APPLICATION (KERALA AMENDMENT) ACT, 1963
purpose: To amend the Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act, 1937 (Central Act 26 of 1937), in its application to the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and concerns the application of Muslim Personal Law (Shariat).

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1963 and shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Central Act 26 of 1937 in its application to the State of Kerala to be amended.
main_sections.description: Amends the Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act, 1937 (Central Act 26 of 1937) in its application to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of a new section for section 2, Central Act 26 of 1937.
main_sections.description: Substitutes a new section for section 2 of the Central Act 26 of 1937. The new section 2 deals with the application of personal law to Muslims, covering intestate succession, special property of females, marriage, divorce, and other matters of personal law for Muslims.

Repeals the Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application (Madras Amendment) Act, 1949 (Madras Act XVIII of 1949) as in force in the Malabar district, and sub-section (2) of section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.

important_rules: Application of personal law to Muslims: Notwithstanding any custom or usage to the contrary, in all questions regarding intestate succession, special property of females including personal property inherited or obtained under contract or gift or any other provision of personal law, marriage, dissolution of marriage, including talaq, ila, zihar, lian, khula and mubaraat, maintenance, dower, guardianship, gifts, trusts and trust properties and wakfs (other than charities and charitable institutions and charitable and religious endowments), the rule of decision in cases where the parties are Muslims, shall be the Muslim Personal Law (Shariat).
administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but likely administered by the relevant legal and judicial authorities in Kerala.
important_notes: Received the assent of the President on the 4th day of December, 1963 and published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 12th December, 1963.

title: The National University Of Advanced Legal Studies Act, 2005
purpose: To establish and incorporate a University by the name of the National University of Advanced Legal Studies for the advancement of the study of law and legal processes, legal research, legal aid, law reform and such other purposes as are ancillary and further the cause of legal education in the State of Kerala and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the establishment and incorporation of the National University of Advanced Legal Studies in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.University: The National University of Advanced Legal Studies established by this Act.

main_sections.description: Establishes the National University of Advanced Legal Studies and makes it a body corporate.

main_sections.section_title: Objects and Powers of the University
main_sections.description: Outlines the objectives and powers of the University, including promoting advanced study and research in law, providing legal education, and conducting research in legal and allied subjects.
Defines the territorial jurisdiction of the University.
States that the University shall be recognized by the University Grants Commission.
Details the various powers vested in the Syndicate of the University, including making statutes, ordinances, and regulations, managing the funds, and appointing staff.
Specifies the powers and functions of the Vice-Chancellor of the University.
Outlines the powers and functions of the Executive Committee of the University.
Details the powers and functions of the Academic Council of the University, concerning academic matters.
Defines the powers and functions of the Senate of the University.
Specifies the officers of the University.
Deals with the making and amendment of statutes of the University.
Relates to the making and amendment of ordinances of the University.
Covers the making and amendment of regulations by the University.
Provides for the first statutes of the University.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly detailed for general violations within the provided text, but the University itself, and by extension, the State Government, would be the ultimate authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the statutes, ordinances, and regulations of the University, and potentially legal recourse.

rights: Right to establish and incorporate the University.
Right to promote advanced study and research in law.
duties: Duty to provide for advanced study and research in law and legal processes, legal research, legal aid, law reform and such other purposes as are ancillary and further the cause of legal education in the State of Kerala.

key_procedures: Procedure for making Statutes: Statutes shall be made by the Senate, subject to the provisions of this Act and the Statutes.
Procedure for making Ordinances: Ordinances shall be made by the Syndicate, subject to the provisions of this Act and the Statutes.
Procedure for making Regulations: Regulations shall be made by the Academic Council, subject to the provisions of this Act, the Statutes and the Ordinances.
administration: The University is administered by its various authorities like the Senate, Syndicate, Academic Council, and Executive Committee, under the overall governance framework established by the Act. The State Government is involved in its establishment and may have oversight functions.
important_notes: The Act establishes the National University of Advanced Legal Studies.
The University is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal.
The University aims at the advancement of the study of law and allied subjects.

title: The National University of Advanced Legal Studies (Amendment) Act, 2008
purpose: To amend The National University of Advanced Legal Studies Act, 2005 for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to The National University of Advanced Legal Studies.

main_sections.description: States that the Act is called The National University of Advanced Legal Studies (Amendment) Act, 2008 and it shall come into force on the 9th day of June, 2008.
Amends the preamble of the National University of Advanced Legal Studies Act, 2005 by omitting the words "on self financing basis".
Amends sub-section (1) of section 3 of the principal Act.

Amends section 12 of the principal Act by inserting specific items after item (x) and item (xi), namely: "(xib) The Principal Secretary, Finance Department, Government of Kerala," and "(xib) A member nominated by the Executive Council of the Higher Education Council from among its members,", and also inserts item (xiv) "Two legal experts nominated by the Government, of which one shall be a woman".

Amends sub-section (2) of section 17 of the principal Act by adding words after existing words, and amends item (vii) by adding words after existing words, and amends item (xiii) by adding specific text.
Substitutes the following clause for clause (a) in sub-section (1) of section 27 of the principal Act: "(a) One nominee of the Bar Council of Kerala."

Inserts section 46A which grants the Government power to give direction to the University to consider the instructions of the Government made from time to time in respect of the determination of the fee and admission of students to the University. Provided that on such direction the decision of the Executive Council shall be final.

Repeals The National University of Advanced Legal Studies (Amendment) Ordinance, 2008 (21 of 2008) and states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By issuing directions to the University regarding fee determination and student admissions.

administration: The National University of Advanced Legal Studies, overseen by the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 3rd day of January, 2009 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No 34, dated 5th January, 2009.

title: The Non Resident Keralites Welfare Act, 2008
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a Welfare Fund to grant relief to, to ensure the welfare of and to pay pension and other benefits to the Non-Resident Keralites and to promote companies or co-operative societies or other institutions of Non-Resident Keralites for their welfare.
scope: The Act applies to Non-Resident Keralites. 'Keralite' means a person born or domiciled in the State of Kerala and includes wife/husband of such person and their minor children. 'Non-Resident Keralite' means a Keralite holding a valid Indian passport and is employed or residing in abroad with the VISA of the foreign country or a Keralite who was holding an Indian passport having validity and was employed or resided for livelihood abroad for at least two years with the VISA of a foreign country. It also applies to members of the Fund and beneficiaries of the welfare schemes.

key_definitions.Board: Kerala Non-Resident Keralites' Welfare Board constituted under Section 9 of the Act.
key_definitions.Chief Executive Officer: The Chief Executive Officer appointed under sub-section (1) of section 12 of the Act.
key_definitions.Company: A company registered under the Companies Act, 1956 (Central Act 1 of 1956).
key_definitions.Contribution: The sum of money payable to the Fund under section 4 of the Act.
key_definitions.Co-operative Society: A Co-operative Society registered under the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969 (Act 21 of 1969).
key_definitions.Deemed Member: A Non-Resident Keralite (India) whose membership has been ceased owing to his return to Kerala but who is paying the contribution continuously to the Fund under sub-section (4) of section 7 of the Act.
key_definitions.Dependent: The family member of the Fund and in the absence of a family, the major brothers and widowed sisters of the member.
key_definitions.Family: Wife/husband, minor son and unmarried or widowed daughter including adopted children; Father, mother, unmarried sisters and minor brothers who are solely dependent on the member and in the absence of such dependents, the major son and married daughter.
key_definitions.Fund: The Non-Resident Keralites' Welfare Fund constituted under section 3 of the Act.
key_definitions.Keralite: A person born or domiciled in the State of Kerala and includes wife/husband of such person and their minor children.
key_definitions.Non-Resident Keralite: A Keralite holding a valid Indian passport and is employed or residing in abroad with the VISA of the foreign country or a Keralite who was holding an Indian passport having validity and was employed or resided for livelihood abroad for at least two years with the VISA of a foreign country.
key_definitions.NORKA-ROOTS: The company NORKA-ROOTS constituted under the Companies Act, 1956 (Central Act 1 of 1956).
key_definitions.Notification: A notification published in the Gazette.
key_definitions.Overseas Development and Employment Prom: The public sector undertaking under the Overseas Development and Employment Promotion Consultants Limited constituted under the Companies Act, 1956 (Central Act 1 of 1956).
key_definitions.Prescribed: Prescribed by rules issued under this Act.
key_definitions.Re-patriated person: A member who returns to Kerala and resides permanently in Kerala after working as a Non-Resident Keralite for a period of not less than two years.
key_definitions.Scheme: The Non-Resident Keralites' Welfare Scheme framed under this Act.
key_definitions.Special Aid Fund: The Special Aid Fund constituted under section 8 of the Act.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Non-Resident Keralites' Welfare Act, 2008 and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

Defines various terms used in the Act, including Board, Chief Executive Officer, Company, Contribution, Co-operative Society, Deemed Member, Dependent, Family, Fund, Government, Keralite, Member, Non-Resident Keralite, NORKA-ROOTS, Notification, Overseas Development and Employment Promotion Consultants Limited, Prescribed, Re-patriated person, Scheme, Special Aid Fund, State, and Year.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, frame a Scheme to be called the Non-Resident Keralites' Welfare Scheme for the constitution of a Fund for the welfare of the Non-Resident Keralites under this Act and there shall be constituted, as soon as may be, after the framing of the Scheme, a Fund in accordance with the provisions of this Act and the Scheme. The following shall be credited to the Fund: contributions, grants, loans or advances, donations, application/registration fees, amount borrowed by the Board, profit or interest or dividend, unclaimed consolidated amount, and any amount raised by the Board or any other source. The Fund shall vest in and be administered by the Board and may be utilized for pension, payment on death of a member, financial assistance for medical treatment, marriage of women members and daughters, giving financial assistance or loans for construction of dwelling house or purchase of land or house, for education facilities, for self-employment assistance or loans, for payment of financial assistance to a member who suffers from permanent physical disability, for investment in any company or firm or co-operative society or any other society or institution, and for any other purpose specified in the Scheme. The Scheme framed under sub-section (1) may provide for the matters specified in sub-section (4) and in the Schedule to this Act.

Every Non-Resident Keralite (abroad) member continuing in employment abroad shall pay an amount of rupees three hundred per month and every Non-Resident Keralite (abroad) member came back from abroad and settled permanently in Kerala shall pay an amount of rupees two hundred per month as contribution to the Fund.

important_rules: Every Non-Resident Keralite (abroad) member continuing in employment abroad shall pay a contribution of Rs. 300 per month.
Every Non-Resident Keralite (abroad) member who has returned from abroad and settled permanently in Kerala shall pay a contribution of Rs. 200 per month to the Fund.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Board and the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The Scheme will be framed by the Government, and the Board administers the Fund and its utilization. The Scheme may provide for matters related to enforcement and penalties.

rights: Right to pension and other benefits.
Right to relief and welfare measures.
Right to utilize services of companies or co-operative societies or other institutions of Non-Resident Keralites.
Right to access financial assistance for housing, education, and self-employment.
Right to financial assistance for medical treatment, marriage, and in case of death of a member.
Right to claim refund of contribution in certain circumstances.
duties: Duty to pay contributions to the Fund as prescribed.
Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act and the Scheme.
Duty to provide correct information to the Board.

key_procedures: Framing of the Non-Resident Keralites' Welfare Scheme by the Government.
Constitution of the Non-Resident Keralites' Welfare Fund.
Administration and utilization of the Fund by the Board for various welfare purposes.
Crediting of contributions, grants, loans, donations, fees, and other amounts to the Fund.
Payment of pension, financial assistance, and other benefits from the Fund.
Procedures for refund of contributions in specific cases.
administration: The Kerala Non-Resident Keralites' Welfare Board.
important_notes: The Act was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 75 dated 12th January, 2009.
The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 12th day of January, 2009.
For computing the period of five years for the purpose of refund of contribution, the contributions given by him as a member and as a deemed member shall be counted.

The Scheme shall be laid as soon as may be, after it is framed, before the Legislative Assembly while it is in session for a total period of fourteen days which may be comprised in one session or in two successive sessions, and if, before the expiry of the session in which it is so laid or the session immediately following, the Legislative Assembly makes any modification in the Scheme, the Scheme shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form, so however that any such modification shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under the Scheme.

title: The Non-Resident Indians' (Keralites) Commission Act, 2015
purpose: To constitute a Commission for Non-Resident Indians hailing from Kerala with a view to protect and safeguard their interest in the State of Kerala and to recommend remedial measures for their welfare and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Non-Resident Indians hailing from Kerala and their welfare and interests in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Chairperson: Means the Chairperson of the Commission.
key_definitions.Commission: Means the Non-Resident Indians' (Keralites) Commission constituted under section 3 and that may be known as NRI (Kerala) Commission.
key_definitions.complaint: Means all petitions or communications received in the Commission from a Non-resident Indian or from any other person on his behalf, in person or by post, fax, e-mail or by any other means alleging disputes or such violation or denial of justice by a public servant or a private person or from Institutions including Government/Quasi Government/Public Sector Institutions/Bank or such providing material on the basis of which the Commission takes suo-moto cognizance;
key_definitions.Member: Means a member of the Commission and includes the Chairperson and Secretary;
key_definitions.Non-resident Indians: Means a person of Indian citizen domiciled in Kerala who is either permanently or temporarily settled outside India for— (i) taking up employment outside India; or (ii) carrying on a business or vocation or for studying outside India; or (iii) any other purpose, in such circumstances, as would indicate his intention to stay outside India for an uncertain period.
key_definitions.family: Means— (i) Wife/husband, minor son including adopted children and unmarried divorced or widowed daughter; (ii) Father, mother, unmarried sisters and minor brothers who are solely dependent on the Non-resident Indians (Keralites) and in the absence of such dependents, the major son and married daughter;
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act;
key_definitions.regulations: Means the regulations made by the Commission as per sub-section (8) of section 7 of this Act.

main_sections.description: (1) This Act may be called the Non-Resident Indians' (Keralites) Commission Act, 2015. (2) It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'Chairperson', 'Commission', 'complaint', 'Member', 'Non-resident Indians', 'family', 'prescribed', and 'regulations'.

(1) The Government shall as soon as, may be after the commencement of this Act, constitute a body to be known as the Non-resident Indians' (Keralites) Commission to exercise the powers conferred upon and to perform the functions assigned to it, under this Act. (2) The Commission shall consists of the following members nominated by the Government, namely:— (i) A person who is or has been a Judge of the High Court of Kerala, who shall be the Chairperson of the Commission; (ii) Two members from Non-resident Indians (Keralites) who are abroad for not less than five years; (iii) Two members from Non-resident Indians' (Keralites) who returned after being abroad for 5 or more years. (iv) An officer not below the rank of a Joint Secretary to Government or a retired officer from All India Service not below the rank equivalent to that shall be the Secretary of the Commission and he shall exercise such powers and perform such functions as may be delegated to him by the Commission; (v) A person who has completed the age of 65, shall not be continued as Chairperson or member.

main_sections.section_title: Term of office and conditions of service of members
main_sections.description: (1) Except Secretary appointed from service, every member shall hold office for a period of three years from the date on which he assumes office and shall be eligible for re-appointment for not more than one term. (2) A casual vacancy caused by reason of death, removal or resignation of any member shall be filled by fresh nomination: Provided that a person so nominated shall hold office only for the remaining period of the term of the person in whose place such person is nominated. (3) The members other than the Secretary shall be paid with such allowances or sitting fees for attending the meeting of the Commission, as may be prescribed.

(1) The Government shall provide the Commission with such Officers and other employees as may be required for the proper functioning of the Commission; (2) The salaries and allowances payable to and other terms and conditions of service of the Officers and other employees shall be such as may be prescribed.
The headquarters of the Commission shall be at Thiruvananthapuram.

(1) The Commission shall hold its sittings ordinarily at Thiruvananthapuram at such time as the Chairperson may think fit. It may also hold its sittings at any other place within the State, if necessary. (2) The meeting of the Commission shall be presided over by the Chairperson. In the absence of the Chairperson, a member to be elected among the members present at the meeting, shall preside over the meeting. (3) The quorum for a meeting of the Commission shall be three. (4) The Commission shall meet at least once in two months. (5) All questions at a meeting of the Commission shall be decided upon by the majority of the votes of the members present and voting and in the case of equality of votes, the Chairperson or the member presiding over the meeting, shall have a right for a casting vote. (6) The Commission, for the purpose of transacting any business before it or for considering any special issue, may invite persons having specialized knowledge in the matter but such person shall have no right to vote. (7) All orders and decisions of the Commission shall be authenticated by the signature of the Chairperson or any other member who presides over the meeting. Other instruments executed by the Commission shall be authenticated by the signature of the Secretary. (8) The Commission shall with the previous approval of Government make regulations for regulating its procedure and the disposal of its business and such regulations shall, after they are made, be published in the Gazette.

The Government may, by order, remove the Chairperson or any member if he— (a) is adjudged as undisdischarged insolvent; or (b) has been convicted of an offence which in the opinion of the Government involves moral turpitude; or (c) is of unsound mind and stands so declared by a competent Court; or (d) without obtaining permission from the Commission, has been absent from three consecutive meetings of the Commission; or (e) in the opinion of the Government, has abused his official position so as to render his continuance in office detrimental to public interest: Provided that no person shall be removed under this clause until he has been given a reasonable opportunity of being heard in the matter.

(1) Subject to the provisions of this Act, it shall be the duty of the Commission to assist, promote and develop the welfare of the Non-Resident Indians' (Keralites) and to perform such other functions as the Government may assign to it, from time to time. (2) The Commission may in furtherance of its object, perform the following functions, namely:— (a) help the Non-Resident Indians' (Keralites) and their family in protecting their rights, particularly in the issues of life and property in the State of Kerala; (b) pursue the interests of the Non-Resident Indians' (Keralites) with the State and Central Government; (c) Help to Safeguard the investment in all forms of Non-Resident Indians' (Keralites) in Kerala; (d) Facilitate Social Service Organisations for the Non-Resident Indians' (Keralites) and their spouses and parents living in Kerala for community life and health care; (e) Inquire into unfair practice, against Non-Resident Indians' (Keralites) and make recommendations to concerned Government Departments or Agencies on the action to be taken in the matter; (f) Report to Government the inadequacies or shortcomings in the existing laws in force which affect the Indian Constitutional right to equality and fair treatment of Non-Resident Indians' (Keralites) and also on the remedial Legislative measures to be taken to meet the situation; (g) To enquire into the unfair practices of recruitment agencies and to ensure that the interests of the Non-Resident Indians' (Keralites) are protected; (h) Act for the protection of the interests, assets and deposits of the overseas citizen of Indian card holders who had been permanent resident in Kerala and has been registered as per the provisions of section 7A of the Citizenship Act, 1955 (Central Act 57 of 1955) and family members and to facilitate the social service organizations for the health care of their family members in Kerala; (i) to suggest suitable measures to be adopted in the issues of Non-Resident Indians' (Keralites).

(1) The Commission shall, while performing its functions under section 9, have all the powers as are vested in a Civil court while trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Central Act 5 of 1908), in respect of the following matters, namely:— (a) summoning and enforcing the attendance of any witness and examining him on oath; (b) requiring the discovery and production of any document; (c) receiving evidence on affidavits; (d) requisitioning any public records or copy thereof from any public office;

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Commission, with the previous approval of Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The Commission shall with the previous approval of Government make regulations for regulating its procedure and the disposal of its business.

rights: Protection of interests, assets and deposits of overseas citizen of Indian card holders who had been permanent resident in Kerala.
Protection of rights, particularly in the issues of life and property in the State of Kerala for Non-Resident Indians' (Keralites).
duties: To assist, promote and develop the welfare of the Non-Resident Indians' (Keralites).

key_procedures: Receiving petitions or communications regarding disputes or violations related to Non-resident Indians.
Inquiring into unfair practices against Non-Resident Indians.
Reporting inadequacies in laws affecting Non-Resident Indians.
Facilitating social service organizations for Non-Resident Indians.

The Commission shall hold its sittings ordinarily at Thiruvananthapuram. Meetings shall be presided over by the Chairperson, or an elected member in their absence. Quorum is three members. Meetings to be held at least once in two months. Decisions by majority vote, with casting vote for the presiding member in case of tie. Special issues can involve invited persons with specialized knowledge but no voting rights. Orders and decisions authenticated by the Chairperson or presiding member; other instruments by the Secretary. Regulations for procedure and business require Government approval and Gazette publication.
administration: Government of Kerala, Law (Legislation-H) Department
important_notes: The act is an English translation published by authority of the Governor.

The Government may remove a member for reasons including insolvency, conviction of an offence, unsound mind, absence from meetings, or abuse of official position, after providing an opportunity to be heard.
The Commission has powers similar to a Civil court in matters of summoning witnesses, production of documents, and receiving evidence on affidavits.

title: The Non-Resident Keralites' Welfare (Amendment) Act, 2015
purpose: To amend the Non-Resident Keralites' Welfare Act, 2008.
scope: Applies to Non-Resident Keralites' Welfare Fund and its members.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act as The Non-Resident Keralites' Welfare (Amendment) Act, 2015, and states that it shall come into force on the 24th day of February, 2009.

Amends section 3 of the principal Act by inserting a new clause (aa) regarding the payment of pension to members and deemed members who have become members of the fund after completing fifty-five years of age but before attaining sixty years of age and have remitted contribution for a period of not less than five years.

Amends section 6 of the principal Act. It substitutes the words 'fifty-five years of age' with 'sixty years of age' in sub-section (1) and adds a new sub-section (8) specifying that the membership period of a member shall be from the date on which he enrolled as member in the Welfare Scheme to sixty years or the date on which he becomes eligible for pension, whichever is later.
Amends section 8 of the principal Act by substituting the words 'fifty-five years of age' with 'sixty years of age'.

States that notwithstanding anything contained in the principal Act and Rules and Scheme made thereunder, within the period from 24th February, 2009 to the date on which the Act has been published in the Gazette, all proceedings with respect to the granting of membership and issue of benefits thereunder to any person who has completed 55 years of age but submitted application for membership in the Fund before completing 60 years of age and the membership and benefits given as such shall be deemed to have been validly taken and issued under the principal Act as amended by this Act and any action taken with regard to this shall not be challenged before any courts or other authorities.

rights: Right to receive pension under certain conditions (Section 2).
obligations: Members must remit contribution for not less than five years to be eligible for pension under specific conditions (Section 2).

key_procedures: Application for membership and pension eligibility is subject to specific age and contribution criteria (Section 2, Section 3(8)).
Validation of past actions related to membership and benefits (Section 5).
administration: Law (Legislation-H) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Non-Resident Keralites' Welfare Act, 2008.
Amendments related to age for pension eligibility and membership period are key changes.
Section 5 provides for the validation of actions taken under the principal Act and Rules and Scheme before the commencement of this amendment Act.

title: THE NURSES AND MIDWIVES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1964
purpose: To further amend the Nurses and Midwives Act, 1953.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala, concerning the registration and practice of nurses, midwives, and auxiliary nurse-midwives.

key_definitions.register: Means the register of nurses or the register of midwives or the register of auxiliary nurse-midwives or the register of health visitors, or the register of "dh ais" maintained under this Act, and "registered" means registered or deemed to be registered under this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Nurses and Midwives (Amendment) Act, 1964, and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Amends the preamble of the principal Act by substituting certain words.
Amends section 2 of the principal Act by substituting clause (f).
Amends section 3 of the principal Act by substituting sub-section (a) and clause (d).

Amends section 30 of the principal Act, substituting specific words.
Amends section 32 of the principal Act, substituting specific words.

Amends section 34 of the principal Act, substituting specific words.

important_rules: Rule 1: No person shall confer or issue or hold himself out as entitled to confer, grant or issue any degree, diploma, licence, certificate or other document stating or implying that the holder, grantee or recipient is qualified to practise the profession of a registered nurse, midwife, auxiliary nurse-midwife, health visitor or dhai, unless such person is so entitled under this Act or rules or bye-laws made thereunder.

Rule 2: Whoever contravenes the provisions of sub-section (1) shall be punishable with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, and if the person so contravening is an association, every member of such association who knowingly and willfully authorises or permits the contravention shall be punishable with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees.

penalties: Fine up to one thousand rupees for contravening section 34A (1).
Fine up to five hundred rupees for members of an association authorizing or permitting contravention of section 34A (1).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be government authorities responsible for the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through prosecution and imposition of fines for contravention of the Act's provisions, particularly section 34A.

rights: Right to be registered as a nurse, midwife, auxiliary nurse-midwife, health visitor, or dhai if qualified and meeting the criteria.
Right to practice the profession if registered.
duties: Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act and the rules made thereunder.
Duty of registered persons to maintain professional standards.
obligations: Obligation for individuals to be registered to practice as nurses, midwives, etc.
Obligation to refrain from conferring or issuing unauthorized qualifications.

key_procedures: Procedure for registration of nurses, midwives, auxiliary nurse-midwives, health visitors, and dhais.
Process for amendment of sections of the principal Act by the State Government through notification.
administration: Implied to be the Health Department of the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act came into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
The amendments are aimed at updating the definitions and provisions related to various categories of nursing and midwifery professionals.
Specific provisions address the nomination of members to committees in case of election default.

title: THE OPIUM (KERALA AMENDMENT) ACT, 1963
purpose: To amend the Opium Act, 1878, in its application to the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: (1) This Act may be called the Opium (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1963. (2) It shall come into force at once.

Amends the Opium Act, 1878 (Central Act 1 of 1878) by modifying sub-section (2) of section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (Central Act 37 of 1956). Specifically, it addresses amendments to section 20 of the Opium Act, 1878, by omitting section 20 A and inserting a new section 20A concerning the powers of Excise or Prohibition Officers.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Official Gazette, State Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Notification in the Official Gazette

key_procedures: The amendment to section 20 of the Opium Act, 1878, involves changes related to the officer in charge of the nearest police-station and the officer of the Excise or Prohibition Department in charge of the range.
A new section 20A is inserted, granting powers to Excise or Prohibition Officers with the powers of an officer in charge of a police-station.
administration: Prohibition Department, Excise Department
important_notes: Received the assent of the President on 2nd March, 1963.
Published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 7th March 1963.

title: THE PAMPA RIVER BASIN AUTHORITY ACT, 2009
purpose: To provide for the constitution of an Authority in the State for the conservation of water resources in the Pampa River and its basins as an integral unit and matters connected therewith or incidental thereto, to ensure the quality of water in the river and to take measures to prevent pollution and to undertake integrated planning, monitoring, management and development of water resources in the river with the river basins as an integral unit.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala, specifically concerning the Pampa River and its basins. It covers water resources, prevention of pollution, and integrated planning, monitoring, management, and development of these resources.

key_definitions.Authority: means the Pampa River Basin Authority constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.Chairperson: means the Chairperson of the Authority.
key_definitions.Executive Committee: means the committee constituted under section 11.
key_definitions.Fund: means the Pampa River Basin Authority Fund constituted under section 12.
key_definitions.member: means a member of the Authority.
key_definitions.Member-Secretary: means the Member-Secretary of the Authority.
key_definitions.notification: means a notification published in the Official Gazette.
key_definitions.Pampa Action Plan: means the plan of the Government of Kerala for the conservation of Pampa River and its reservoirs by averting pollution, through the projects undertaking integrated planning, monitoring, management and development of water sources.
key_definitions.Pampa River Basin: means the reservoir areas of the Pampa River, its two banks and its tributaries.
key_definitions.Project Director: means the Project Director of the Authority.
key_definitions.prescribed: means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.regulations: means the regulations made under section 21.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Pampa River Basin Authority Act, 2009, and it shall come into force on the 2nd day of August, 2008.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including Authority, Chairperson, Executive Committee, Fund, Government, member, Member-Secretary, notification, Pampa Action Plan, Pampa River Basin, Project Director, prescribed, regulations, and State.

Establishes the Pampa River Basin Authority, a body corporate constituted by notification by the Government, to be known by that name, having perpetual succession and a common seal, with power to acquire, hold and dispose of property, and to contract and sue and be sued.

Details the members of the Authority, including the Chairman (Chief Minister), Vice-Chairman (Minister for Water Resources), Member-Secretary (Secretary, Water Resources), and other nominated members representing various Government Departments, local bodies, and individuals with expertise.

title: The Pattazhi Devaswom Lands (Vesting and Enfranchisement) Act, 1961
purpose: To provide for the enfranchisement of certain lands belonging to the Pattazhi Devaswom Temple and its Keezhedu and for the vesting in the Government of Kerala of certain other lands belonging to the said Temple and Keezhedu.
scope: Applies to certain lands belonging to the Pattazhi Devaswom Temple and its Keezhedu, and other lands belonging to the said Temple and Keezhedu in the Government of Kerala. It covers tenants, proprietors, and tharissu lands.

key_definitions.Act: The Pattazhi Devaswom Lands (Vesting and Enfranchisement) Act, 1961.
key_definitions.basic tax: The basic tax imposed by the Government under the provisions of the Kerala Land Tax Act, 1961.
key_definitions.holding: Means any land owned by the Temple and held by a tenant.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Temple: Means the Pattazhi Devaswom Temple situated in the Pattazhi Village in the Tittuvapuram Taluk and includes the following Keezhedus of the said Temple, namely: (i) the Kundayam temple situated in the Pattazhi Village in the Pathanapuram Taluk; and (ii) the Mannadi temple situated in the Kadampanadu Village in the Konnthur Taluk.
key_definitions.tenant: Means a person holding at the commencement of this Act lands owned by the Temple on enipattam, kanam or any other kind of tenure directly under the temple.
key_definitions.tharissu: Means land owned by the Temple and entered as 'tharissu' in the revenue records.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Pattazhi Devaswom Lands (Vesting and Enfranchisement) Act, 1961, and specifies that it shall come into force at once.
Nothing in this Act shall apply to the lands specified in the Schedule.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'Act', 'basic tax', 'Government', 'holding', 'prescribed', 'Temple', 'tenant', and 'tharissu'.

main_sections.section_title: Cessation of the rights of the Temple
main_sections.description: Specifies that after the commencement of this Act, notwithstanding anything contained in any law or contract, the Temple shall cease to have any right, claim or interest in the specified lands, and that tharissu shall vest in Government.

main_sections.section_title: Tenants to be proprietors and tharissu to vest in Government
main_sections.description: States that every tenant shall, subject to the provisions of section 7, have full proprietary rights in the land comprised in his holding, and tenants shall not be liable to pay rent to the Temple; and all tharissu shall vest in the Government.
The Government shall pay to the Temple a sum of four lakhs and seventy-five thousand rupees as compensation for the extinguishment of rights, claims and interests.

main_sections.section_title: Tenants to pay compensation for rights vested in them
main_sections.description: Tenants in a vested section 5 holding shall be liable to pay compensation to the Government. The compensation is calculated based on the annual rent or land revenue, with specific rates for paddy lands and other lands.

main_sections.section_title: Liability to pay basic tax and cess on land
main_sections.description: Details the liability of tenants and the Temple to pay basic tax and cess on lands, particularly in relation to the financial year 1958-59 and lands under the jurisdiction of Panchayats.

main_sections.section_title: Issue of pattas, etc., to tenants
main_sections.description: The Government may appoint officers to issue pattas or other documents evidencing the right of the tenants in their holdings.

main_sections.section_title: Amounts due to Government to be recoverable under the Revenue Recovery Act
main_sections.description: Any amount due to the Government from tenants or due from the Temple under the provisions of the Travancore-Cochin Revenue Recovery Act, 1951, shall be recoverable as arrears of public revenue due to the Government.
Provides indemnity for actions taken in good faith under this Act and prohibits suits, prosecution or other legal proceedings against any officer duly appointed or authorized under the Act.

Grants the Government the power to make rules for the purpose of carrying into effect the provisions of this Act, including rules regarding settlement of tax, determination of dates, procedure for issuing documents, and other related matters. These rules, if made, shall be subject to the condition of previous publication.
Empowers the Government to make any order necessary for giving effect to the provisions of the Act, if any difficulty arises.

Rules made under Section 12 must be subject to the condition of previous publication and shall, as soon as possible after they are made, be laid before the Legislative Assembly of the State of Kerala for a period of not less than fourteen days. title: The Pattazhi Devaswom Lands (Vesting and Enfranchisement) Amendment Act, 1972
purpose: To amend the Pattazhi Devaswom Lands (Vesting and Enfranchisement) Act, 1961.
scope: Applies to the Pattazhi Devaswom Lands (Vesting and Enfranchisement) Act, 1961.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Pattazhi Devaswom Lands (Vesting and Enfranchisement) Amendment Act, 1972.
Amends section 7 of the Pattazhi Devaswom Lands (Vesting and Enfranchisement) Act, 1961 (21 of 1961) regarding the amount payable and its payment.
Inserts new sections 9A (Appeal) and 9B (Revision) into the principal Act.
Amends section 12 of the principal Act, specifically clauses (e) and (f) concerning the form and manner of appeals under section 9A.

important_rules: The amount payable under sub-clause (a) of clause (i) of sub-section (3) shall bear interest at the rate of 4 per cent per annum from the date of receipt by the tenant of the order of the officer appointed or authorised under sub-section (2) of section 9, settling such amount.
The amount payable shall be paid in twelve equal half-yearly instalments together with interest accrued due on the amount outstanding on the date of payment of each instalment.

Provided that nothing contained in this sub-section shall be deemed to preclude the tenant from paying such amount in lesser number of instalments than twelve or from paying the whole amount due in one instalment.

Provided further that no interest shall be payable on such amount if it is paid in a lump sum within thirty days next following the date of receipt by the tenant of the order referred to in clause (a).

Any person aggrieved by an order passed by any officer appointed or authorised under sub-section (2) of section 9 may, within a period of sixty days from the date on which that order was communicated to him, prefer an appeal to the Revenue Divisional Officer of the division in which the land in respect of which such order has been passed is situate.

The Revenue Divisional Officer may admit an appeal after the expiration of the said period of sixty days, if he is satisfied that the appellant had sufficient cause for not preferring the appeal within that period.
An appeal under sub-section (1) shall be in the prescribed manner and shall be verified by a fee of two rupees.

The Revenue Divisional Officer shall, after giving the appellant and any other person affected by the order appealed against an opportunity of being heard, and after making such further inquiries as he may consider necessary, pass such order on the appeal as he thinks fit.

The District Collector may, either of his own motion or on the application of any person aggrieved, call for and examine the record of any proceeding under this Act in which an order has been passed by the Revenue Divisional Officer or by any officer appointed or authorised under sub-section (2) of section 9, for the purpose of satisfying himself as to the correctness, legality, propriety or regularity of such order, and may pass such order thereon as he thinks fit.

Provided that the District Collector shall not call for and examine the record of any proceeding in which an order has been passed by any officer appointed or authorised under sub-section (2) of section 9, if the appeal against that order is pending or if the time for preferring an appeal against such order has not expired.
The District Collector shall not revise any order under sub-section (1) if that order has been made more than one year previously.
An application made under sub-section (1) by an aggrieved person shall be made within a period of one year from the date on which the order in question was communicated to him:

Provided that the District Collector may admit an application made after the expiry of the said period of one year, if he is satisfied that the applicant had sufficient cause for not making the application within that period.
Every application for revision under sub-section (1) shall be accompanied by a fee of two rupees.
An order prejudicial to a person shall not be passed under sub-section (1) unless that person has been given a reasonable opportunity of showing cause against such order.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Revenue Divisional Officer, District Collector
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through appeals and revisions of orders.

rights: Right to appeal against orders passed by designated officers.
Right to prefer an appeal even after the expiry of the period if sufficient cause is shown.
Right to be heard before an order is passed that affects one.
Right to apply for revision of an order.
Right to be given a reasonable opportunity of showing cause against a prejudicial order.
duties: Duty to pay amounts due as per the Act.
Duty to prefer appeals within the specified time.
Duty to accompany revision applications with a fee.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the payment schedule of instalments with interest.

key_procedures: Appeal Process: An aggrieved person can appeal to the Revenue Divisional Officer within 60 days of communication of the order. The RDO can admit appeals after the period if sufficient cause is shown. The appeal must be in the prescribed manner, verified, and accompanied by a fee of two rupees. The RDO will hear both parties and make a decision.

Revision Process: The District Collector can suo motu or upon application examine records of proceedings to ensure correctness, legality, propriety, or regularity of orders passed by the Revenue Divisional Officer or other designated officers. The Collector cannot review pending appeals or orders where the time for appeal has expired, or orders older than one year. An application for revision must be made within one year, with possible admission after the period if sufficient cause is shown. It requires a fee of two rupees. Prejudicial orders cannot be passed without giving the affected person an opportunity to show cause.
administration: The Act is administered by authorities like the Revenue Divisional Officer and the District Collector.
important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 708, dated 28th November, 1972.
The term 'sub-section' refers to the provisions within sections of the Act.
Interest at 4% per annum is applicable on outstanding amounts.
Payment in lump sum within 30 days avoids interest.
Appeal fee is two rupees.
Revision application fee is two rupees.
An order declining to interfere shall be deemed to be an order prejudicial to a person.

title: The Payment Of Salaries And Allowances (Amendment) Act, 2003
purpose: To further amend the Payment of Salaries and Allowances Act, 1951, for the purposes herein appearing.
scope: Applies to members of the Legislative Assembly, other than the Speaker, the Deputy Speaker, the Leader of Opposition, the Chief Whip and the Ministers, regarding free transit coupons and fuel coupons.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Payment of Salaries and Allowances (Amendment) Act, 2003. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of July, 2003.

In the Payment of Salaries and Allowances Act, 1951 (XIV of 1951), in section 3, the following shall be added at the end, namely:-- "and a constituency allowance of two thousand and five hundred rupees per mensem."
In the principal Act, in section 4, the following shall be added at the end, namely:-- "and a constituency allowance of two thousand and five hundred rupees per mensem."
In the principal Act, for the words "one thousand eight hundred and fifty rupees", the words "five thousand rupees" shall be substituted.

In section 8 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1),— (i) in clause (aa), for the words "rupees two thousand and five hundred", the words "rupees three thousand and five hundred" shall be substituted; (ii) in the proviso to clause (b), for the words "four thousand and five hundred rupees", the words "seven thousand and five hundred rupees" shall be substituted.
In section 8A of the principal Act, in sub-section (5), for the words "three thousand rupees", the words "four thousand rupees" shall be substituted.

In section 9A of the principal Act,— (i) for the marginal heading and sub-section (1), the following shall be substituted, namely:— "9A Free transit coupons for members of the Legislative Assembly.—(1) Subject to such rules as may be made in this behalf, every member of the Legislative Assembly, other than the Speaker, the Deputy Speaker, the Leader of Opposition, the Chief Whip and the Ministers, shall, at the option of such member, be provided with all or any of the following free transit coupons of an aggregate value of fifty four thousand rupees for a period of twelve calendar months, namely:— (i) rail travel coupons for travel by such member by rail, and (ii) fuel coupons for the purchase of fuel for the travel of such member in a private vehicle Provided that it shall be lawful for the Government to enhance, by order, from time to time, the aforesaid amount of free transit coupons proportionate to the periodical increase in rail charges made by the Central Government.”. (iii) sub-section (3) shall be omitted."

title: THE PAYMENT OF RAJABHOGAM TO THEKKEMADOM SWAMIYAR MATHAPRAM (ABOLITION) ACT, 1980
purpose: To provide for the extinguishment of the right of the Thekkemadom Swamiyar Mathapram to receive, and the liability of the landholders to pay, Rajabhogam, and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to the right of the Thekkemadom Swamiyar Mathapram to receive Rajabhogam and the liability of landholders to pay it.

key_definitions.appointed day: The day on which this Act comes into force.

key_definitions.Mathapram: The Thekkemadom Swamiyar Mathapram at Trichur.
key_definitions.Rajabhogam: The assessment on the Sanketham lands, payable to the Thekkemadom Swamiyar Mathapram, whether called Muppara or Ettilonnu.
key_definitions.Sanketham lands: The lands in the Manicka-mangalam village in the Alwaye Taluk of Ernakulam District, in respect of which Rajabhogam is payable to the Mathapram.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Payment of Rajabhogam to Thekkemadom Swamiyar Mathapram (Abolition) Act, 1980 and specifies its commencement date. The Act came into force on the date of notification in the Gazette, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'landholder', 'Mathapram', 'Rajabhogam', and 'Sanketham lands'.

Declares that notwithstanding anything contained in any law, or in any judgment, decree or order of any court, or in any contract or other document, the right of the Mathapram to receive Rajabhogams shall stand extinguished, and the landholder shall have no liability to pay Rajabhogam to the Mathapram.

States that notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force, or in any contract or other document, no compensation shall be payable to the Mathapram for the extinguishment under section 3 of the right of the Mathapram to receive Rajabhogam from the landholders.

Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in this Act, all arrears of Rajabhogam which accrued due before the appointed day and remain unpaid to the Mathapram on that day shall be recoverable by or on behalf of the Mathapram in the same manner as they were recoverable immediately before the appointed day.

Grants the Government the power to make rules, by notification in the Gazette, to carry out the purposes of this Act. Such rules, if made before the Legislative Assembly, must be in session for a total period of fourteen days, and if they comprise in one session or in two successive sessions, and if, before the expiry of the session in which it is so laid or the session immediately following, the Legislative Assembly makes any modification in the rule or decides that the rule should not be made, the rule shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect, as the case may be; so however that any such modification or annulment shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that rule.

important_rules: The right of the Mathapram to receive Rajabhogams is extinguished.
Landholders are no longer liable to pay Rajabhogam to the Mathapram.
No compensation is payable to the Mathapram for the extinguishment of this right.
Arrears of Rajabhogam accrued before the appointed day are still recoverable.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government can make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through rules notified in the Gazette by the Government.

rights: The Mathapram has the right to recover arrears of Rajabhogam accrued before the appointed day.
obligations: Landholders are relieved of the obligation to pay Rajabhogam to the Mathapram after the appointed day.

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act: Upon notification in the Gazette.
Rule making procedure: Rules are made by the Government by notification in the Gazette and are subject to the approval and modification of the Legislative Assembly.
administration: The Government (likely through a relevant department or authority responsible for revenue or land matters in Kerala).
