Every member of the Legislative Assembly (other than the Speaker, the Deputy Speaker and the Ministers) shall be provided with one free non-transferable first class pass which shall entitle him to travel by any railway in India for a distance of six thousand kilometres in the aggregate during a period of twelve calendar months. Subject to the provisions of sub-section (1), a free railway pass issued to a member under that sub-section shall be valid for the term of his office, and on the expiration of such term, the pass shall be surrendered to the Secretary to the Legislative Assembly. A member who performs any journey by using the pass shall not be entitled to any travelling or daily allowance for such journey.
Amends the Schedule of the principal Act. It adjusts currency values and specifies traveling and daily allowances for members of the Legislative Assembly.

important_rules: Rule for maintenance and repair of conveyance for the Deputy Speaker.
Rules regarding concessions for rest houses and tourist bungalows.
Rules for telephone facilities for members of the Legislative Assembly (excluding Speaker and Ministers).

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By notification in the Gazette.

rights: Members of the Legislative Assembly (excluding Speaker and Ministers) are entitled to concessions in rest houses and tourist bungalows.
Members of the Legislative Assembly (excluding Speaker and Ministers) are entitled to telephone facilities.
Members of the Legislative Assembly (excluding Speaker, Deputy Speaker and Ministers) are entitled to a free non-transferable first class railway pass for a certain distance per year.
duties: Members using the free railway pass are not entitled to travelling or daily allowance for that journey.
The free railway pass must be surrendered to the Secretary to the Legislative Assembly upon expiration of the term of office.

key_procedures: Government to notify commencement date in Gazette.
Surrender of railway pass upon expiration of term of office.
administration: Government of Kerala
important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 759, dated 16th December, 1972.

title: THE PAYMENT of SALARIES and ALLOWANCES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1973
purpose: An Act further to amend the Payment of Salaries and Allowances Act, 1951.
scope: Applies to the Payment of Salaries and Allowances Act, 1951. Specific provisions relate to members of the Legislative Assembly, Speaker, and Ministers.

main_sections.description: (1) This Act may be called the Payment of Salaries and Allowances (Amendment) Act, 1973. (2) It shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 9A.
main_sections.description: Substitutes a new section 9A into the Payment of Salaries and Allowances Act, 1951. The new section 9A deals with 'Free transit by railway'. It states that every member of the Legislative Assembly, Speaker, and Ministers shall be provided with railway coupons for travel within India. The section also outlines rules for spouse travel and limits on distance and duration.

(1) The Payment of Salaries and Allowances (Amendment) Ordinance, 1973 (5 of 1973), is hereby repealed. (2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act, if this Act had come into force on the 21st day of April, 1973.

important_rules: Every member of the Legislative Assembly, the Speaker, and the Ministers shall be provided with railway coupons.
These coupons shall be subject to such rules as may be made by the Government.
Coupons can be used for travel by the member or their spouse.
The aggregate distance for travel using these coupons is ten thousand kilometres in the aggregate during a period of twelve calendar months.
The aggregate distance for the purposes of the sub-section is deemed to have travelled double that distance where a member and their spouse travel together.
A member performing a journey using railway coupons provided under sub-section (1) is not entitled to any travelling or daily allowance for such journey.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government (through rules made by them)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through rules and regulations governing the use of railway coupons.

rights: Members of the Legislative Assembly, Speaker, and Ministers have the right to free transit by railway within India for a specified distance and duration.
duties: Members are subject to rules made by the Government regarding the use of railway coupons.
Members are not entitled to travelling or daily allowance if they use railway coupons for travel.

key_procedures: Issuance of railway coupons to eligible individuals.
Usage of railway coupons for travel by eligible individuals and their spouses.
Rule-making by the Government regarding the use of coupons.
administration: The Government of Kerala (implied by context of Kerala Acts)
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Payment of Salaries and Allowances Act, 1951.
The Act came into force on the 21st day of April, 1973, retroactively.
The Payment of Salaries and Allowances (Amendment) Ordinance, 1973, has been repealed and saved.

title: THE PAYMENT OF SALARIES AND ALLOWANCES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1974 (ACT 13 OF 1974)
purpose: To amend the Payment of Salaries and Allowances Act, 1951, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the payment of salaries and allowances, likely for Government officials or members of the legislature in Kerala, as inferred from the context and mentions of the Kerala Service Rules and Legislative Assembly.

key_definitions.first grade officer: Means an officer classified as a first grade officer under rule 1 of Part II of the Kerala Service Rules, 1959.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Payment of Salaries and Allowances (Amendment) Act, 1974. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

In section 2 of the principal Act (Payment of Salaries and Allowances Act, 1951), after clause (b), the following clause shall be inserted: - '(c) "first grade officer", means an officer classified as a first grade officer under rule 1 of Part II of the Kerala Service Rules, 1959 "'.
In section 3 of the principal Act, in the places where they occur, the words "eight hundred rupees" and "one thousand rupees" shall be substituted.

In section 4 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), the words "eight hundred rupees" and "one thousand rupees" shall be substituted. Also in sub-section (2), the words "five hundred rupees" and "fifty rupees" shall be substituted.
In section 5A of the principal Act, the brackets and figure '(1)' shall be omitted, and paragraph (ii) shall be omitted.

In section 9 of the principal Act, after sub-section (2), the following sub-section shall be inserted: - "(3) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), but subject to such rules as may be made by the Government in this behalf, any member of the Legislative Assembly entitled to a pass under the said sub-section may opt to travel by special conveyance, and a member making such option shall not be entitled to such pass".

In section 9A of the principal Act, to sub-section (3), the following proviso shall be added: - "Provided that a member who performs such journey inside the State for attending a meeting of the Legislative Assembly or any committee thereof shall be entitled to incidental expenses at the rates applicable to first grade officers of Government.".

In the Schedule to the principal Act, amendments are made to clauses regarding allowances for travel. Specifically, in paragraph 4, "thirty-two paise" and "forty paise" are substituted with "thirty-two paise" and "forty paise" respectively. In paragraph (ii), "thirty-two paise" and "forty-five paise" are substituted with "twenty paise" and "thirty paise".

important_rules: Members of the Legislative Assembly may opt to travel by special conveyance and are not entitled to a pass if they do so (subject to rules made by the Government).
Members attending Legislative Assembly meetings or committee meetings within the State are entitled to incidental expenses at the rates applicable to first grade officers of Government.
Specific monetary amounts for allowances (e.g., "eight hundred rupees", "one thousand rupees", "five hundred rupees", "fifty rupees") are amended.
The definition of 'first grade officer' is introduced.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government (as indicated by 'by notification in the Gazette' and 'made by the Government')
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through Government notifications in the Gazette and rules made by the Government.

rights: Right to receive salaries and allowances as per the Act.
Right to travel by special conveyance and receive incidental expenses (for certain members and journeys).
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act and any rules made by the Government.
Obligation for the Government to notify commencement dates.

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Government through a Gazette notification.
Opting for special conveyance: Members of the Legislative Assembly can opt for special conveyance under specific conditions and rules.
Claiming incidental expenses: Members are entitled to incidental expenses for journeys within the State for attending meetings.
Amendment of Schedule: Specific monetary figures in the Schedule are substituted to reflect updated allowances.
administration: The Government of Kerala (implied by 'Kerala Service Rules', 'Legislative Assembly', and 'Gazette of India/Kerala')
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on 25th day of April 1974 and published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 392 dated 25th April, 1974.
The amendments update monetary figures related to salaries and allowances.
The definition of 'first grade officer' is a key addition.
The Act itself refers to and amends 'The Payment of Salaries and Allowances Act, 1951'.

title: THE PAYMENT OF SALARIES AND ALLOWANCES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1977
purpose: An Act further to amend the Payment of Salaries and Allowances Act, 1951, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to members of the Legislative Assembly, Ministers, Speaker, Deputy Speaker and Leader of the Opposition in Kerala.

key_definitions.members of family: Means the wife or husband, children including adopted children and step children, and parents wholly dependent upon the member of the Legislative Assembly.
key_definitions.Speaker: Refers to the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly.
key_definitions.Deputy Speaker: Refers to the Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly.
key_definitions.Leader of the Opposition: Refers to the leader of the largest party in opposition in the Legislative Assembly and recognised as such by the Speaker.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Payment of Salaries and Allowances (Amendment) Act, 1977.
Amends the long title of the Payment of Salaries and Allowances Act, 1951, by substituting specific terms related to official positions.
Amends the preamble of the principal Act by substituting specific terms.
Amends section 2 of the principal Act. Introduces definitions for 'Deputy Speaker', 'Leader of the Opposition', and 'Speaker'.
Amends section 3 of the principal Act. Substitutes words in relation to 'Ministers', 'Speaker', and 'Leader of the Opposition'.

Amends section 4 of the principal Act. Stipulates that a salary of seven hundred and fifty rupees per mensem and dearness allowance at specified rates are to be paid to the Deputy Speaker, and a salary of seven hundred and fifty rupees to officers of Government drawing a salary of seven hundred and fifty rupees, from the time to time.
Amends section 5 of the principal Act. Substitutes words for 'Speaker' and 'Leader of the Opposition' and 'Speaker and the Leader of the Legislative Assembly'.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new sections for sections 5A, 5B, 6 and 6A.
main_sections.description: Substitutes new sections for existing sections 5A, 5B, 6 and 6A. These new sections cover medical facilities for Ministers, Speaker, Deputy Speaker and Leader of the Opposition, including their families; accident insurance; conveyance for members; and free use of boats.
Amends section 7 of the principal Act. Substitutes specific wording in provisos related to travelling allowance for journeys performed in any Government conveyance.
Amends section 7A of the principal Act. Amends words, figures, and brackets in sections 4, 5, 6 and 7 of the principal Act.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 7B.
main_sections.description: Substitutes a new section for section 7B. This new section provides medical facilities to members of the Legislative Assembly, including their families, for medical treatment and attendance. It also clarifies that 'members of family' includes spouse, children, and dependent parents.
Amends section 8 of the principal Act by inserting specific terms.
Amends section 8A of the principal Act by substituting specific terms.
Amends sections 9 and 9A of the principal Act by substituting specific terms.

Inserts a new section 9B which deals with Deduction of Government dues from allowances payable to members of the Legislative Assembly. It specifies that any amount payable to the Government by a member, if not paid within a specified time, shall be deducted from their allowances.
Amends the Schedule to the principal Act. Makes specific substitutions in the marginal note and in sub-clause (d) of clause (1) of the letters and figures.

important_rules: Ministers, Speaker, Deputy Speaker and Leader of the Opposition are entitled to free medical treatment in any Government institution and to free medical attendance by any medical practitioner or other person in the service of the Government, for themselves and their family members.
Ministers, Speaker, Deputy Speaker and Leader of the Opposition are entitled to accident insurance paid for by the Government, for expenses incurred during journeys by air on public business.
Ministers, Speaker, Deputy Speaker and Leader of the Opposition are entitled to conveyance allowances for journeys performed in Government conveyances, subject to certain conditions and limits.
Ministers, Speaker, Deputy Speaker and Leader of the Opposition are entitled to the exclusive use of boats belonging to the Government without payment of charges when touring on public business.
Travelling allowance for journeys performed in Government conveyances by the Leader of the Opposition is subject to rules specified by the Government.

Travelling allowance and daily allowances for journeys performed in any Government conveyance by Ministers, Speaker, Deputy Speaker and Leader of the Opposition are subject to rules specified by the Government.
Any amount due to the Government from a member of the Legislative Assembly shall be deducted from their allowances if not paid within the specified time or on the date fixed for its payment.

penalties: Deduction of Government dues from allowances payable to members of the Legislative Assembly if not paid within the specified time or on the date fixed for its payment. The deduction is up to the amount payable by the Government in excess of the sum not paid.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be the administrative machinery responsible for disbursing salaries and allowances and managing Government dues.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through deduction of dues from the salaries and allowances of the concerned individuals.

rights: Right to receive salary and dearness allowance.
Right to free medical facilities for self and family.
Right to accident insurance for air journeys on public business.
Right to conveyance allowances for official journeys.
Right to use Government boats for public business tours.
duties: Duty to pay any Government dues within the specified time.
Duty to comply with rules regarding travelling allowance and daily allowances.
obligations: Obligation to have Government dues deducted from allowances if not paid promptly.

key_procedures: Amendments to the Payment of Salaries and Allowances Act, 1951, are made through this Act.
Specific sections of the principal Act are amended by substituting certain words, figures, and clauses.
New sections are inserted to address medical facilities, accident insurance, conveyance, and deduction of Government dues.
The schedule to the principal Act is amended.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but likely falls under the purview of the Finance Department or General Administration Department of the Kerala Government.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 1st day of September, 1977, and published in the Kerala Gazette No. 510 dated 1st September, 1977.
The Act provides for retrospective application of certain amendments.
'Members of family' definition includes spouse, children, and dependent parents.
Specific monetary amounts and rates for salaries, dearness allowances, and reimbursements are mentioned.
Rules regarding conveyance for journeys and use of boats are detailed.

rights: Right to medical facilities for members and their families.

title: THE PAYMENT OF SALARIES AND ALLOWANCES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1982

scope: Applies to the payment of salaries and allowances as per the principal Act of 1951.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Payment of Salaries and Allowances (Amendment) Act, 1982. It shall come into force at once.
Amends the long title of the Payment of Salaries and Allowances Act, 1951, to replace "the Leader of the Opposition and members" with "the Leader of the Opposition, the Chief Whip and members".
Amends the preamble of the principal Act, by replacing "the Leader of the Opposition" with "the Leader of the Opposition, the Chief Whip".

Amends section 3 of the principal Act, to substitute "Leader of the Opposition" with "Leader of the Opposition and Chief Whip".

Amends section 5B of the principal Act, by substituting "Leader of the Opposition and Chief Whip" for "Leader of the Opposition and the Chief Whip".

Amends section 6A of the principal Act, by substituting "Leader of the Opposition and Chief Whip" for "Leader of the Opposition".

Amends section 9 of the principal Act, substituting "Leader of the Opposition and Chief Whip" for "the Leader of the Opposition".

title: The Payment of Salaries and Allowances (Amendment) Act, 1985

title: THE PAYMENT OF SALARIES AND ALLOWANCES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1979
purpose: To further amend the Payment of Salaries and Allowances Act, 1951.
scope: Applies to members of the Legislative Assembly in Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Payment of Salaries and Allowances (Amendment) Act, 1979.

Amends section 6 of the Payment of Salaries and Allowances Act, 1951 (Act XIV of 1951) by substituting "two hundred rupees", "two hundred and fifty rupees" for "one hundred and fifty rupees" and omitting "and" before "at the end shall be omitted" in sub-section (1)(a) and (b) respectively. Also inserts a clause for travelling allowance for members whose usual place of residence is within a radius of eight kilometers from the Assembly Chamber.

Amends section 8 of the principal Act.  In sub-section (1)(a), substitutes "two hundred and fifty rupees" for "one hundred and fifty rupees". In sub-section (2), substitutes "two hundred and fifty rupees" for "one hundred and fifty rupees".

Amends section 8A of the principal Act. Inserts a new sub-section (3) stating that every member of the Legislative Assembly, other than the Speaker, the Deputy Speaker, the Leader of the Opposition and the Ministers, shall be provided with one telephone at his usual place of residence, which may be specified by the member for the term of his office and for a period of fifteen days immediately thereafter.  Sub-section (4) states that subject to such rules as may be made in this behalf, charges in respect of the installation and rental of the telephone provided in pursuance of sub-section (3) shall be paid by the Government. Sub-section (5) states that every member referred to in sub-section (3) shall be entitled to a telephone allowance of two hundred rupees per mensem for meeting the charges in respect of such telephone other than the charges referred to in sub-section (4).
Amends section 9 of the principal Act. Sub-section (3) shall be omitted.
Amends section 9A of the principal Act by substituting "fifteen thousand kilometres" for "ten thousand kilometres".

Amends the Schedule to the principal Act. In paragraph 1, in sub-clause (a) of clause (1), substitutes "forty-five paise" and "sixty-five paise" for "forty-five paise" and "sixty-five paise" respectively. In sub-clause (a) of clause (2), substitutes "forty-five paise" and "sixty-five paise" for "fifty-five paise" and "sixty-five paise" respectively.  For paragraph III, the following paragraph shall be substituted: 'III. Members of the Legislative Assembly.-The members of the Legislative Assembly shall be given travelling and daily allowances at the following rates: (1) Inside the State of Kerala— travelling allowance—fifty-five paise per kilometre: Provided that the minimum travelling allowance for a to and fro journey shall be one hundred rupees; daily allowance—twenty-five rupees; (2) outside the State of Kerala— for journeys by rail—cost of one first class railway fare plus twelve paise per kilometre; for journeys by road—fifty-five paise per kilometre; daily allowance—thirty-five paise per kilometre.'

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, likely administrative bodies related to the Legislative Assembly and government finances.

rights: Right to receive salaries and allowances as per the Act.
Right to a telephone at the usual place of residence for members of the Legislative Assembly.
Right to travelling and daily allowances for members of the Legislative Assembly.
obligations: Members of the Legislative Assembly are obligated to have their place of residence within a radius of eight kilometers from the Assembly Chamber for specific travelling allowance rules.

key_procedures: Amendments to existing sections of the Payment of Salaries and Allowances Act, 1951 are made by this Act.
Specific monetary values for allowances and distances are amended or introduced.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be managed by the Government of Kerala and the administration of the Legislative Assembly.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 27th April 1979 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 328, dated 2nd May 1979.

title: The Payment of Wages(Kerala Amendment) Act, 2015
purpose: The purpose of this Act is to amend the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, in its application to the State of Kerala. It aims to ensure timely payment of wages to employees and to address related matters. Specifically, the amendment seeks to bring the provisions of the Act in line with contemporary industrial practices and legal requirements, possibly by increasing the wage threshold for applicability and modifying the penalty structure.
scope: This Act applies to the State of Kerala and specifically to the payment of wages to persons employed in any factory, industrial or other establishment to which the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, for the time being applies. The amendments likely adjust the wage ceiling for applicability of the Act.

key_definitions.wage: Refers to all remuneration, capable of being expressed in terms of money, which would, if the terms of the employment so permitted, be payable during the period of employment in respect of the time actually worked, but does not include any bonus other than a performance bonus, or other special payment by the employer to the person employed in respect of any period of whose work is not done, any house-accommodation, electricity, water, any other supply or service or any privilege or benefit, and any holiday or leave or any locality allowance.
key_definitions.employer: Means the owner of any railway, canal or building or operations, any, or any contractor, in cases where the employment of labour in any such work is carried on by or through a contractor. This definition is likely expanded or clarified by the amendment.

main_sections.description: This section likely states the short title of the Act as 'The Payment of Wages (Kerala Amendment) Act, 2015' and specifies the date from which it comes into force. It may also indicate that it forms part of the principal Act.

This section pertains to the amendment of Section 1 of the Principal Act (The Payment of Wages Act, 1936). It likely modifies the applicability of the Act, potentially by increasing the wage ceiling up to which the Act applies to employed persons.

This section deals with amendments to Section 15 of the Principal Act, which generally relates to claims arising out of deductions from wages or delay in payment of wages. The amendment might alter the procedures for filing claims, the powers of the authorities, or the time limits for such claims.

This section introduces a new Section 20A into the Principal Act. This new section likely deals with specific penalties or provisions related to violations of the Act's provisions concerning payment of wages, possibly for offenses not covered by existing penalty clauses. The text mentions a penalty for contravention of Section 13A, which could be related to timely disbursement of wages. There is also a reference to a penalty for delay or non-payment. The amendment might also cover a penalty for false statements.

important_rules: Wages must be paid before the expiry of the seventh day if there are less than one thousand employees, and before the expiry of the tenth day if there are one thousand or more employees.
Wages shall be paid in current coin or currency notes or in both.
No employer shall deduct wages except those specified under the Act.
Deductions for the payment of wages shall not exceed the prescribed limits.
Wages shall be paid in the current currency of India.

penalties: Fine for contravention of section 13A: Rs. 10,000 to Rs. 50,000.
Penalty for delay or non-payment of wages: Rs. 1,000 to Rs. 5,000.
Penalty for false statement: Rs. 1,000 to Rs. 5,000.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Act is enforced by various authorities, including Inspectors, the Authority appointed under Section 15 of the Act (for claims), and the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enforcement is through inspection of establishments, adjudication of claims by the appointed authority, and imposition of penalties for non-compliance. The Inspectorate of Labour under the Labour Department is the primary enforcement agency.

rights: Employees have the right to receive their wages on time.
Employees have the right to claim deductions made incorrectly from their wages.
Employees have the right to redressal for delayed payment of wages.
duties: Employers have the duty to pay wages to their employees on or before the prescribed dates.
Employers have the duty to maintain records of wages paid and deductions made.
Employers have the duty to comply with all provisions of the Act, including display of notices.
obligations: The employer is obligated to ensure that wages are paid in the prescribed manner and within the stipulated timeframes.

key_procedures: Claim Filing: An employee or their representative can file a claim for delayed wages or unauthorized deductions with the prescribed authority within a specified time limit.
Verification and Adjudication: The authority will verify the claim and hear both parties before passing an order.
Recovery of Wages: If the authority finds the claim valid, it will order the employer to pay the due wages and compensation.
Maintenance of Registers: Employers are required to maintain registers showing the amount paid to each person employed, deductions made, and receipts signed by persons employed.
administration: The Labour Department of the Kerala State Government is responsible for the administration and implementation of this Act.
important_notes: The amendment increases the wage ceiling for the applicability of the Act to Rs. 24,000 per month.
The Act specifies the time limits for wage payment based on the number of employees.
Penalties have been introduced for contraventions of specific sections, including section 13A, and for false statements.

title: THE PAYMENT OF WAGES(KERALA AMENDMENT) ACT, 2015

title: The Plantations Labour (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1969
purpose: To further amend The Plantations Labour Act, 1951, in its application to the State of Kerala.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Kerala and amends The Plantations Labour Act, 1951. It specifically addresses plantations and the employment of labour within them.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called The Plantations Labour (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1969. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint. It also inserts a new sub-section (1A) regarding welfare officers in any plantation.

Amends section 18 of The Plantations Labour Act, 1951 (Central Act 69 of 1951) by inserting a new sub-section (1A) which states that in section 18 of the Principal Act, after sub-section (1), the following sub-section shall be inserted, namely— ' (1A) If in any plantation, welfare officers are not employed as required by the rules made under sub-section (1), the chief inspector may appoint the required number of welfare officers and thereupon such officers shall be deemed to have been employed by the employer under sub-section (1)'. It also includes a proviso that before appointing welfare officers, the employer shall be given an opportunity of being heard.

Inserts a new section 18A titled "Chief Inspector to provide facilities on default by employer". This section empowers the Chief Inspector to provide or maintain facilities if the employer defaults in doing so as required by section 8 or section 9 or section 12 or section 15 or the rules made under section 11 or section 14 or section 17. The Chief Inspector may cause such facilities to be provided or maintained and recover the cost from the defaulting employer. It also includes a proviso that the employer shall be given an opportunity of being heard before providing or maintaining such facilities. Furthermore, for the recovery of the cost, the Chief Inspector may certify the amount to the Collector, who may recover such amount as an arrear of land revenue.

important_rules: Welfare officers must be employed in plantations as required by the rules. If not, the Chief Inspector can appoint them.
Before appointing welfare officers, employers must be given an opportunity to be heard.

duties: Employers have a duty to employ welfare officers as required by the rules.

obligations: Obligation to comply with the rules regarding the employment of welfare officers.

obligations: Companies or persons may be assigned a class in the profession tax scale based on their half-yearly income.

key_procedures: The levy and collection of profession tax are validated.
Reassessment of profession tax can be undertaken in certain cases, with the Executive Authority having the power to reopen assessments and make them de novo.
administration: Implied to be the municipal authorities responsible for administering the Travancore District Municipalities Act, 1116.
important_notes: The Act has retrospective effect from April 1, 1950, for the purpose of validation.
Amendments made to the Taxation and Finance Rules are validated.
The reassessment provisions in Section 3 apply to specific circumstances involving the classification of companies or persons based on their income.

title: THE PROHIBITION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1973
purpose: An Act further to amend the Prohibition Act, 1950, for the purposes hereinafter appearing
scope: Applies to the Prohibition Act, 1950, as amended.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Prohibition (Amendment) Act, 1973.

In section 1 of the Prohibition Act, 1950 (XIII of 1950) (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), in sub-section (3), in clause (a), for the words and figures "sections 7 and 11", the word and figure "section 7" shall be substituted.

In section 2 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), for the brackets, words and figures "(except sections 1, 7 and 11)", the brackets, words and figures "(except sections 1 and 7)" shall be substituted.
In section 6 of the principal Act, in sub-section (2), for the words and figures "sections 1, 7 and 11", in the places where they occur, the words and figures "sections 1 and 7" shall be substituted.
Section 11 of the principal Act shall be omitted.

important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 608 dated 10th July, 1973.

title: The Prohibition (Amendment) Act, 1978
purpose: To further amend the Prohibition Act, 1950.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala, India.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Prohibition (Amendment) Act, 1978 and it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 2nd day of October, 1977.

Amends section 3 of the Prohibition Act, 1950 (XIII of 1950). It specifies that the brackets, words and figures (except sections 1 and 7) and the brackets, words and figures (except sections 1, 7 and 11) shall be substituted.

Amends section 6 of the principal Act, in subsection (2), for the words and figures "sections 1 and 7", in both the places where they occur, the words and figures "sections 1, 7 and 11" shall be substituted.

Inserts a new section 11 after section 10 of the principal Act. The new section is titled 'Prohibition of advertisements' and deals with who is prohibited from printing or publishing advertisements related to any liquor or intoxicating drug, and penalties for contravention. It also specifies exceptions for advertisements in medical journals or for medicinal value approved by the Indian Medical Council, and for circulation within the State of newspapers, periodicals and books printed and published in accordance with law outside the State.

Repeals The Prohibition (Amendment) Ordinance, 1977 (18 of 1977). It also states that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Prohibition of advertisements: No person shall print or publish any advertisement, book, leaflet, booklet or any other single or periodical publication or otherwise displays or distributes any advertisement or other matter commending, soliciting the use of, or offering any liquor or intoxicating drug (other than liquor or drugs exempted under section 21), shall be punishable with imprisonment which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

Exceptions to advertisement prohibition: This prohibition shall not apply to price lists which may be generally or specially approved by the Commissioner, or to advertisements in medical journals or to notices and literature circulated exclusively to members of the medical profession, if such advertisements, notices or literature relate to any liquor or intoxicating drug which has been specially approved as of medicinal value by any Medical Council established by or under any law for the time being being in force in the territory of India or any part thereof, or to the normal circulation within the State of newspapers, periodicals and books printed and published in accordance with law outside the State.

penalties: Imprisonment which may extend to six months
Fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Implied to be the authorities responsible for enforcing the Prohibition Act, potentially the Commissioner or other designated officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings and imposition of penalties as outlined in the Act.

duties: Duty to comply with the prohibition of advertisements related to liquor or intoxicating drugs.
Duty to ensure advertisements, if permitted under exceptions, are circulated only to the intended audience or within approved parameters.

key_procedures: Insertion of new section 11: The process involves amending the principal Act by adding a new section to regulate advertisements.
Repeal and saving: The Ordinance is repealed, and actions taken under it are validated as if taken under the amended Act.
administration: Implied to be the Government of Kerala, specifically departments related to prohibition enforcement.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on October 2, 1977.
Received the assent of the Governor on the 10th day of March 1978 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extra ordinary No. 173 dated 14th March 1978.

title: THE KERALA PUBLIC BUILDINGS (EVICTION OF UNAUTHORISED OCCUPANTS) ACT, 1968
purpose: An Act to provide for the eviction of unauthorized occupants from public buildings and for matters connected therewith.
scope: The Act applies to public buildings in the State of Kerala and concerns the eviction of unauthorized occupants. It also covers matters related to the recovery of rent and damages and the disposal of property left in public buildings by unauthorized occupants.

key_definitions.estate officer: An officer appointed as such by the Government under section 3.
key_definitions.local authority: A municipal corporation, a municipal council, a township committee, a panchayat or any other authority by whatever name called, constituted under any law for the time being in force for the purpose of local self-government and includes the Trivandrum City Improvement Trust Act, 1960 (I of 1961) or any other authority constituted under any law for the time being in force for the development of any local area.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.public building: Means any building or part of a building belonging to, or taken on lease or requisitioned by, or on behalf of, the Government or a local authority and includes— (i) the garden, grounds and outhouses, if any, appertaining to such building or part of a building; and (ii) any fittings affixed to such building or part of a building for the more beneficial enjoyment thereof.
key_definitions.rent: In relation to any public building, means the consideration payable periodically for the authorised occupation of the building, and includes— (i) any charge for electricity, water or any other services in connection with the occupation of the building, (ii) any tax (by whatever name called) payable in respect of the building, where such charge or tax is payable by the Government or the local authority, as the case may be;
key_definitions.unauthorised occupation: In relation to any public building, means the occupation by any person of the building without authority for such occupation and includes the continuance in occupation by any person of the public building after the authority (whether by way of lease or any other mode of transfer) under which he was allowed to occupy the building has expired or has been determined for any reason whatsoever.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Public Buildings (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1968. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'estate officer', 'local authority', 'prescribed', 'public building', 'rent', and 'unauthorised occupation'.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint persons, being Gazetted Officers of Government below the rank of District Collector, as estate officers for the purposes of this Act. In the case of local bodies, executive authorities of the concerned local authorities shall be appointed as estate officers and they shall define the local limits within which they shall exercise the powers conferred.

main_sections.section_title: Issue of notice to show cause against order of eviction
main_sections.description: If the estate officer is of opinion that any persons are in unauthorised occupation of any public building and that they should be evicted, the estate officer shall issue in the manner hereinafter provided a notice in writing calling upon all persons concerned to show cause why an order of eviction should not be made. The notice shall specify the grounds on which the order of eviction is proposed to be made and shall require all persons who are, or may be, in occupation of, or claim interests in, the public building, to show cause why an order of eviction should not be made, giving a date not earlier than ten days from the date of issue thereof. The notice shall be served by affixing the notice on the outer door or some other conspicuous part of the public building.

If, after considering the cause, if any, shown by any person in pursuance of a notice under section 4 and any evidence produced in support of the same and after giving him a reasonable opportunity of being heard, the estate officer is satisfied that the public building is in unauthorised occupation, the estate officer may, on a date to be fixed for the purpose, make an order of eviction for reasons to be recorded therein, directing that the public building shall be vacated by all persons who may be in occupation thereof or any part thereof, and cause a copy of the order to be published by affixing it on the outer door or some other conspicuous part of the public building. If any person refuses or fails to comply with the order of eviction within thirty days of the date of its publication, the estate officer may evict that person from and take possession of the public building and may, for that purpose, use such force as may be necessary.

main_sections.section_title: Disposal of property left in public building by unauthorised occupants
main_sections.description: Where any persons have been evicted from any public building under section 5, the estate officer may, after giving fourteen days' notice to the persons from whom possession of the public building has been taken and after publishing the notice in at least one newspaper having circulation in the locality, remove or sell or dispose of by public auction any property left by such persons in such building. The sale proceeds shall, after deducting the expenses of the sale and the amount, if any, due to the Government or the local authority, be paid to such person or persons as may appear to the estate officer to be entitled to the same. Provided that where the estate officer is unable to decide as to the person or persons to whom the balance of the amount is payable or as to the apportionment of the same, he may refer such dispute to the civil court of competent jurisdiction and the decision of the civil court shall be final.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of unauthorised occupant to pay damages
main_sections.description: Any person who has been in unauthorised occupation of any public building shall be liable to pay for the whole period of such occupation, such damages on account of the use and occupation of such building as may be assessed by the estate officer having regard to such principles of assessment of damages as may be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Power to recover rent and damages in respect of public buildings
main_sections.description: The estate officer may, by order, require that person to pay the same within such time and in such instalments as may be specified in the order.

An estate officer shall, for the purpose of holding any inquiry under this Act, have the same powers as are vested in a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (5 of 1908), when trying a suit, in respect of the following matters, namely: (a) summoning and enforcing the attendance of any person and examining him on oath; (b) requiring the discovery and production of documents; (c) any other matter which may be prescribed.

An appeal shall lie from any order of the estate officer made in respect of any public building under section 5 or section 8 to the Collector of the District in which the public building is situate. An appeal under sub-section (1) shall be preferred, (a) in the case of an appeal from an order under section 5, within fifteen days from the date of publication of the order under sub-section (1) of that section; and (b) in the case of an appeal from an order under section 8, within fifteen days from the date on which the order is communicated to the appellant. Where an appeal is preferred from an order of the estate officer, the District Collector may stay the enforcement of that order for such period and on such conditions as he deems fit. Every appeal under this section shall be disposed of by the District Collector as expeditiously as possible.

If the estate officer has reason to believe that any persons are in unauthorised occupation of the building, the estate officer or any other officer duly authorised by him in this behalf may require those persons, or any other person who he has reason to believe is in possession of information relating to the names and other particulars of the persons in occupation of the public building, to furnish such information within such time as may be specified in the requisition, and every person so required shall be bound to furnish the information in his possession accordingly.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of heirs and legal representatives
main_sections.description: Where any person against whom any proceeding for (a) the determination of arrears of rent; or (b) the assessment of damages, is to be, or has been taken under this Act, dies, before the proceeding is taken or during the pendency thereof, the proceeding may be taken or, as the case may be, be continued against the heirs or legal representatives of that person.

main_sections.section_title: Recovery of rent, etc., as arrears of public revenue due on land
main_sections.description: If any person refuses to pay the arrears of rent payable under sub-section (1) of section 8 or costs awarded under sub-section (2) of that section or section 8 or costs awarded under sub-section (5) of section 10, or any portion of such rent, damages or costs within the time, if any, specified therefor in the order relating thereto, the estate officer may issue a certificate to the Collector to the effect that the person has failed to pay the arrears and that he shall, thereupon, proceed to recover the same as arrears of public revenue due on land.

If the person refusing or failing to pay any of the amounts referred to in section 13 is in receipt of salary, the estate officer may, notwithstanding the issue of a certificate to the Collector under the said section, require any person paying the salary to deduct from any payment of salary subsequent to the date of such requisition any amount or portion thereof as may be specified in the requisition and such person shall comply with any such requisition and shall pay the sum so deducted to the credit of the Government or the local authority, as the case may be.

Save as otherwise expressly provided in this Act, every order made by an estate officer or appellate officer under this Act shall be final and shall not be called in question in any suit, application or execution proceeding, and no injunction shall be granted by any court or other authority in respect of any action taken or to be taken in pursuance of any power conferred by or under this Act.

(1) If any person who has been evicted from any public building under this Act also occupies the building without authority, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both. (2) Any Magistrate convicting a person under sub-section (1) may make an order for evicting that person summarily and he shall be liable to such eviction without prejudice to any other action that may be taken under this Act. (3) If a person fails without reasonable cause or excuse to deduct and pay any amount as required under section 14, he shall be punishable with fine which may extend to ten rupees for every day during which the default continues.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: No suit, prosecution or other legal proceedings shall lie against the Government or a local authority or the estate officer or any other officer in respect of anything which is in good faith done or intended to be done in pursuance of this Act or of any rule or order made thereunder.

(1) The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act. (2) In particular and without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing power, such rules may provide for all or any of the following matters, namely: (a) the form of any notice required or authorised to be given under this Act and the manner in which it may be served; (b) the holding of inquiries under this Act; (c) the distribution and allocation of work to estate officers and the transfer of any proceedings pending before an estate officer to another estate officer; (d) the procedure to be followed in taking possession of public buildings; (e) the manner in which damages for unauthorised occupation may be assessed and the principles which may be taken into account in assessing such damages; (f) the manner in which appeals may be preferred and the procedure to be followed in appeals; (g) any other matter which has to be, or may be, prescribed. (3) Every rule made under this section shall be laid as soon as may be after it is made, before the Legislative Assembly while it is in session for a total period of fourteen days which may be comprised in one session or in two successive sessions, and, if, before the expiry of the session immediately following the session in which it is so laid, or the session immediately following the session in which it is so laid, the Legislative Assembly makes any modification in the rule or decides that the rule should not be made, the rule shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect, as the case may be; so however that any such modification or annulment shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that rule.

important_rules: Unauthorized occupants of public buildings are liable to eviction.
Estate officers are appointed to carry out the provisions of the Act.
A notice to show cause must be issued before an eviction order is made.
Property left in public buildings by evicted occupants may be removed or sold.
Evicted occupants are liable to pay damages for unauthorized occupation.
Rent and damages can be recovered as arrears of public revenue.
Appeals against orders of estate officers can be made to the District Collector.
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected.

penalties: Imprisonment up to one year, or fine up to one thousand rupees, or both, for re-occupying a building after eviction.
Fine up to ten rupees for every day of default in deducting and paying amounts as required under section 14.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Estate Officers, District Collectors, and Magistrates.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Eviction orders, recovery of rent and damages as arrears of public revenue, imposition of penalties for offences.

rights: Right to show cause against an eviction order.
Right to appeal against an order of the estate officer.
Right to receive balance of sale proceeds of property left in public buildings after deduction of expenses and dues.
duties: Duty to vacate public buildings upon an eviction order.
Duty to pay damages for unauthorized occupation.
Duty to comply with requisitions for information.
Duty to deduct and pay amounts as required under section 14.

key_procedures: Issuance of notice to show cause against eviction.
Holding of inquiries by estate officers with powers similar to civil courts.
Appeals to the District Collector.
Recovery of rent and damages as arrears of public revenue.
Making and serving of rules by the Government.
administration: The Government of Kerala is responsible for making rules and appointing estate officers. The District Collector handles appeals.
important_notes: The Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 234, dated 24th September, 1968.
The estate officers have powers vested in a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected from legal proceedings.

title: The Public Wakfs (Extension of Limitation) Kerala Amendment Act, 1974
purpose: To further amend the Public Wakfs (Extension of Limitation) Act, 1959, in its application to the State of Kerala.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This section provides the short title of the Act, states that it extends to the whole of the State of Kerala, and specifies that it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of January, 1973.

This section amends section 3 of the Public Wakfs (Extension of Limitation) Act, 1959 (Central Act 29 of 1959). It substitutes the words "the 31st day of December, 1972" with "the 31st day of December, 1975" in force in the State of Kerala.

important_notes: Received the assent of the President on the 10th day of January, 1975 and published in the Gazette Extraordinary No 31 dated 16th January, 1975.

title: THE PUBLIC WAKFS (EXTENSION OF LIMITATION) KERALA AMENDMENT ACT, 1971
purpose: To amend the Public Wakfs (Extension of Limitation) Act, 1959, in its application to the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Public Wakfs (Extension of Limitation) Kerala Amendment Act, 1971' and that it extends to the whole of Kerala and comes into force on the 1st day of January, 1971.

Amends section 3 of the Public Wakfs (Extension of Limitation) Act, 1959 (Central Act 29 of 1959) by substituting the words, figures and letters "the 31st day of December, 1970" for "the 31st day of December, 1972".

Repeals the Public Wakfs (Extension of Limitation) Kerala Amendment Ordinance, 1971 (10 of 1971). It also includes a saving clause stating that anything done or any action taken under the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary, No. 222, dated 22nd April, 1971.

title: The Registration (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1998
purpose: To amend the Registration Act, 1908 in its application to the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: Provides for the short title of the Act as the Registration (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1998 and its commencement.

Amends Section 17 of the Indian Registration Act, 1908, by adding a proviso to clause (vi) of sub-section (1) of Section 17 of the principal Act. This amendment concerns registration of certain documents related to movable property.
Amends Section 78 of the principal Act. This amendment likely relates to fees or other administrative aspects of registration.

administration: Likely the Inspector General of Registration or the relevant department under the Government of Kerala, based on the subject matter of registration.
important_notes: The amendment specifically adds a proviso to Section 17(1)(vi) of the Registration Act, 1908.
The proviso exempts certain documents concerning movable property from compulsory registration under specific conditions related to value.

title: The Registration (Kerala Amendment) Act, 2012
purpose: To further amend the Registration Act, 1908, in its application to the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: Specifies the short title of the Act and states that it may be called the Registration (Kerala Amendment) Act, 2012. It also states that it extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force at once.

Amends section 17 of the Registration Act, 1908. It introduces new clauses (f) and (g) regarding instruments purporting to operate as a contract for the sale of immovable property of the value of one hundred rupees and upwards, and power of attorney creating any power or right of management, administration, development, transfer or any other transaction relating to immovable property of the value of one hundred rupees and upwards. It also omits the Explanation in sub-section (2).

Inserts a new sub-section (3) into section 71 of the principal Act. This new sub-section states that no registering officer shall accept for registration any document involving transfer of property including contract for sale of immovable property belonging to or vested in the Government of Kerala or public sector undertakings operating in the State or local self-government institutions unless it is accompanied by a no objection certificate issued by an officer authorised by the State Government in this behalf.

Inserts new sections 83A and 83B after section 83 of the principal Act. Section 83A deals with the cancellation of registered documents in certain cases, where the Deputy Inspector General of Registration may cancel a document if it is found that someone has falsely personated another, or if the execution and registration of the document is detrimental to another person, and the cancellation is made upon enquiry. Section 83B provides for the appeal to the Government from orders of the Inspector General of Registration. Any person aggrieved by an order of the Inspector General of Registration under section 83A may prefer an appeal to the Government within thirty days from the date of receipt of such order, and the Government shall pass an order confirming, modifying or cancelling the order of the Inspector General of Registration as they deem fit.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Inspector General of Registration, Deputy Inspector General of Registration, District Collector, Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through enquiries, cancellation of registered documents, and appeals to the Government.

rights: Right to appeal to the Government against orders of the Inspector General of Registration.
Right to have a registered document cancelled under specific circumstances.
duties: Duty of registering officers to accept documents only with a No Objection Certificate from authorized officers for specific property transfers.

key_procedures: Procedure for cancellation of registered documents upon enquiry by the Inspector General of Registration.
Procedure for appealing to the Government against orders of the Inspector General of Registration.
administration: Law (Legislation-A) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: Instruments purporting to operate as a contract for the sale of immovable property of the value of one hundred rupees and upwards are covered.

Power of attorney creating any power or right of management, administration, development, transfer or any other transaction relating to immovable property of the value of one hundred rupees and upwards is covered.

No objection certificate from an authorized officer is required for registration of documents involving transfer of property to the Government, public sector undertakings, or local self-government institutions.

title: The Requisitioning and Acquisition of Property (Amendment) Act, 1968
purpose: To further amend the Requisitioning and Acquisition of Property Act, 1955.
scope: Applies to the Requisitioning and Acquisition of Property Act, 1955.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Requisitioning and Acquisition of Property (Amendment) Act, 1968.
In sub-section (3) of section 1 of the Requisitioning and Acquisition of Property Act, 1955 (1 of 1956), for the words "twelve years", the words "eighteen years" shall be substituted.

(1) The Requisitioning and Acquisition of Property (Amendment) Ordinance, 1968 (1 of 1968), is hereby repealed.
(2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the Requisitioning and Acquisition of Property Act, 1955 (1 of 1956), as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the said Act as amended by this Act as if this Act had come into force on the 11th day of January, 1968.

important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 49, dated 22nd February, 1968

title: THE S.K.V.A CO-OPERATIVE PHARMACY AND STORES (ACQUISITION AND TRANSFER OF UNDERTAKING) ACT, 1976
purpose: To provide for the acquisition of the undertaking of the S.K.V.A Co-operative Pharmacy and Stores and the transfer of the undertaking to the Pharmaceutical Corporation (Indian Medicines) Kerala Ltd.
scope: Applies to the acquisition and transfer of the undertaking of the S.K.V.A Co-operative Pharmacy and Stores to the Pharmaceutical Corporation (Indian Medicines) Kerala Ltd. It covers the assets, rights, powers, authorities and privileges of the Society, its contracts, dealings, and the transfer of its employees.

key_definitions.Administrator: Means the Administrator of the Society.
key_definitions.appointed day: Means the date on which this Act comes into force.
key_definitions.Company: Means the Pharmaceutical Corporation (Indian Medicines) Kerala Ltd., being a Government company as defined in section 617 of the Companies Act, 1956 (Central Act 1 of 1956) and having its registered office at Trichur in the State of Kerala.
key_definitions.Society: Means the S.K.V.A Co-operative Pharmacy and Stores, a co-operative society deemed to be registered under the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969 (21 of 1969) and having its registered office at Trichur.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.share: Means a share in the capital of the Society.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the S.K.V.A Co-operative Pharmacy and Stores (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertaking) Act, 1976 and states that it shall come into force at once.
Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'Administrator', 'appointed day', 'Company', 'Society', 'prescribed', and 'share'.

main_sections.section_title: Undertaking of Society to vest in Government
main_sections.description: States that on the appointed day, the undertaking of the Society shall, by virtue of this Act, stand transferred to and vested in the Government and the Society shall be deemed to have been dissolved.

Details the general consequences of the vesting of the undertaking in the Government, including the transfer of all assets, rights, powers, authorities and privileges, and the cessation of enforceability of contracts or arrangements relating to the undertaking.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to direct vesting of undertaking in Company
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to direct, by order in writing, that the undertaking of the Society shall vest in the Company, with all its properties, assets, liabilities and obligations, on the date of publication of the order or on such earlier or later date as specified.

main_sections.section_title: Duty to deliver possession of property acquired and documents relating thereto
main_sections.description: Mandates that any property vested in the Government or the Company under the Act shall be delivered into the possession or custody of the Government or the Company, as the case may be. It also requires any person with possession of books, documents, or other papers to deliver them up.

Requires the Administrator or other officer of the Society to furnish to the Government or the Company, within one month from the appointed day, a complete inventory of all the properties and assets of the Society, along with liabilities and obligations, and any other particulars as may be required.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of service of existing employees
main_sections.description: States that every officer or other employee employed immediately before the appointed day in connection with the undertaking shall, from that day, become an officer or employee of the Government or the Company, with similar remuneration, terms, conditions, rights and privileges. It also includes provisions for compensation in certain circumstances and continuity of service.

main_sections.section_title: Provident, superannuation, welfare and other funds
main_sections.description: Deals with the transfer of provident, superannuation, welfare, and other funds established by the Society to the Government or the Company. It specifies how moneys from these funds are to be dealt with.

Specifies that for the transfer of the undertaking under section 3, the amount payable to the Government by the Company shall be equal to the value of the shares held by the shareholders in the Society immediately before the appointed day. It also details payment timelines and interest on delayed payments.

Requires the District Collector, Trichur, to pay to every shareholder of the Society any amount due to them as dividend immediately before the appointed day. It also outlines payment timelines and interest on delayed payments.

Outlines penalties for various offenses, including unlawful possession or control of property, wrongful withholding of property, and wilful withholding or furnishing false information. Penalties can include imprisonment and fines.

Specifies how offenses committed by companies under this Act are to be dealt with, deeming individuals in charge of the company's affairs at the time of the offense to be guilty. It includes a proviso that such persons will not be liable if they prove their diligence to prevent the commission of the offense.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides that no suit, prosecution, or other legal proceeding shall lie against the Government or the Company or any of their officers or employees for anything done or intended to be done in good faith under the Act.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: All assets, rights, powers, authorities and privileges of the Society, as well as all its immoveable and moveable property, including lands, buildings, workshops, stores, instruments, machinery and equipment, cash balances, cash on hand, reserve fund, investments and book debts, shall stand transferred to and vested in the Government. (Section 4(1))

All contracts and working arrangements subsisting immediately before the appointed day and affecting the Society shall cease to have effect or be enforceable against the Society or any person who was surety, or had guaranteed the performance thereof. (Section 4(2))

Every officer or other employee employed immediately before the appointed day shall, from that day, become an officer or employee of the Government or the Company, with the same remuneration, terms and conditions, and with the same rights and privileges as to pension, gratuity and other matters. (Section 8(1))
Moneys which stand transferred under section 9(1) to the Government or the Company shall be dealt with by them in such manner as may be prescribed. (Section 9(2))

The amount payable by the Company to the Government for the transfer of the undertaking shall be equal to the value of the shares held by the shareholders in the Society immediately before the appointed day. (Section 10(1))

penalties: Punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years or with fine, or with both for offenses under Section 12.
Offences committed by companies are punishable, with individuals in charge deemed guilty.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government and the Company, and by implication, the court system for enforcing penalties.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legal proceedings initiated by the Government or the Company, and through the imposition of penalties as stipulated in the Act. The Act also vests powers in the Government to direct vesting and make rules.

rights: Right of the Government to acquire the undertaking of the Society.
Right of the Government to direct the vesting of the undertaking in the Company.
Rights of employees to continue employment with equivalent terms and conditions.
Right of shareholders to receive the value of their shares.
duties: Duty of the Society to vest its undertaking in the Government.
Duty to deliver possession of property acquired and documents.
Duty to furnish particulars regarding the Society's assets and liabilities.
Duty of the Government or Company to continue employees under specified terms.
Duty of the District Collector to pay shareholders their dividends.
obligations: Obligations of the Company to take over the undertaking and make payments as stipulated.
Obligations of individuals to comply with the provisions of the Act and furnish information.
Obligations regarding the management of transferred funds.

key_procedures: The Government acquiring the undertaking of the Society.
The Government directing the transfer of the acquired undertaking to the Pharmaceutical Corporation (Indian Medicines) Kerala Ltd.
Delivery of possession of all vested properties and documents to the Government or the Company.
Furnishing of inventory and particulars of the Society's assets and liabilities.
Transfer of employees with continuity of service and terms.
Transfer and management of provident, superannuation, and other funds.
Payment of amounts to shareholders and undisbursed dividends.
Actions taken by the Government to direct vesting and make rules.
administration: The Government of Kerala and the Pharmaceutical Corporation (Indian Medicines) Kerala Ltd. are involved in the administration of this Act.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have received the assent of the President on the 5th day of July, 1976, and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 410, dated 10th July, 1976.
The Act overrides other laws to the extent of inconsistency regarding the transfer of undertakings and employees.
No suit, prosecution, or other legal proceeding shall lie against the Government or the Company or its officers/employees for anything done in good faith under this Act.
The Act has provisions for penalties and offenses, including those committed by companies.

title: THE SILENT VALLEY PROTECTED AREA (PROTECTION OF ECOLOGICAL BALANCE) ACT, 1979
purpose: To provide for certain measures and safeguards for the protection of the ecological balance in the protected area of the Silent Valley Hydro-Electric Project in the Mannarghat taluk of the Palghat district of the State of Kerala.
scope: The Act applies to the protected area of the Silent Valley Hydro-Electric Project in the Mannarghat taluk of the Palghat district of Kerala, and its provisions are to be enforced by the Government of Kerala, Project Authority, and other specified authorities.

key_definitions.Committee: The Silent Valley Environmental Monitoring Committee constituted under section 3.
key_definitions.full capacity contour: The contour of full reservoir level of the project.
key_definitions.monitoring operations: The operations for collecting, observing and interpreting the data relating to the environment of the protected area and the changes thereto.
key_definitions.monitoring station: A monitoring station established under section 4.
key_definitions.monitoring team: The monitoring team appointed by the Government under section 4.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.project: The Silent Valley Hydro-Electric Project in the Mannarghat taluk of the Palghat district of the State.
key_definitions.project area: The submersible area below the full capacity contour, the project dam site, the power intake and their permanent appurtenant works and such other areas within the protected area as may be specified by the Government by notification in the Gazette, in consultation with the Committee and the Project Authority, being required for the execution and operation of the project.
key_definitions.Project Authority: The Kerala State Electricity Board or such other authority as may be specified by the Government in this behalf by notification in the Gazette.
key_definitions.protected area: The area comprised in the Silent Valley Reserved Forest notified under the Kerala Forest Act, 1961 (4 of 1962).

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Silent Valley Protected Area (Protection of Ecological Balance) Act, 1979.

Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'Committee', 'full capacity contour', 'monitoring operations', 'monitoring station', 'monitoring team', 'prescribed', 'project', 'project area', 'Project Authority', and 'protected area'.

The Government shall, in consultation with the National Committee on Environmental Planning and Co-ordination by notification in the Gazette, constitute a committee by the name "the Silent Valley Environmental Monitoring Committee" for the purpose of exercising the powers and performing the functions of the Committee under this Act. The functions of the Committee shall be to advise on the monitoring of the environmental impacts of the project and the ecological aspects of the protected area; and to ensure the implementation of the environmental safeguards provided in this Act.

The Government shall, on the recommendation of the Committee, establish one or more monitoring stations in the protected area for the purpose of on-the-spot monitoring operations. The monitoring operations shall be carried out by a monitoring team appointed by the Government on the recommendation of the Committee. The monitoring team shall consist of such number of persons possessing the prescribed qualifications as may be decided by the Government and shall include representatives of the National Committee on Environmental Planning and Co-ordination.
The expenses on account of the Committee, the monitoring team, the monitoring stations and the monitoring operations shall be met by the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Restriction on construction of roads and colonies in the protected area.
main_sections.description: Roads shall not be constructed in the protected area except along or within the full capacity contour. The Project Authority shall be responsible for the construction of roads and the transportation of the staff, labourers and other persons engaged in the construction of the works in connection with the project, in the protected area. Construction of colonies, staff quarters, offices, workshops and other works for essential services, within the protected area, required for the execution of the project, shall be subject to the following restriction, namely:- site selected for the purpose shall be such that deforestation shall be the minimum; and only the minimum area necessary for the purpose, as may be decided by the Committee, shall be utilised. No such colonies shall be established outside the full capacity contour or the project area except in consultation with the Committee.
No forests shall be felled in the protected area except those within the full capacity contour or the project area.

No person engaged in the construction of the project shall keep cattle or goats or let out any animal into the protected area for grazing. No person referred to in sub-section (1) shall, without the previous sanction of the Project Authority, bring any land in the protected area under cultivation or put up any structure, temporary or permanent, in the protected area.

No person shall carry on quarrying in, or remove earth or soil from, the protected area, except in or from the area within the full capacity contour or the project area. The Project Authority shall take all necessary soil conservation measures in the quarries and burrow pits and work and building sites inside the protected area.

main_sections.section_title: Minimum maintenance staff to be allowed to stay in protected area.
main_sections.description: After the completion of the construction of the project, only the minimum number of staff required for the maintenance of the project, as determined by the Project Authority, shall be allowed to stay in the protected area.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of certain persons to assist in fire protection measures.
main_sections.description: All persons engaged in the construction of the project in the protected area and all persons allowed to stay in the protected area shall assist in measures to protect the forest in the protected area from fire, when required to do so by any forest officer.

main_sections.section_title: Restriction on survey and other operations by Project Authority.
main_sections.description: The Project Authority shall not carry out any survey or other similar operations which are required to be carried out in the protected area outside the full capacity contour, without the prior concurrence of the monitoring team.

No person shall enter into the protected area without an identity card or pass issued by the Project Authority or any forest officer or other officer authorised in that behalf by the Committee. Issue of identity cards and passes under sub-section (1) shall be subject to such conditions and restrictions as may be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Compensatory measures for loss of forest trees.
main_sections.description: The Project Authority shall provide and place at the disposal of the Kerala Forest Department, funds for compensatory afforestation of an area equivalent to the area comprised in the forests felled for the purpose of the project, and such funds shall be provided before the trees in that area are allowed to be felled.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of officers and other employees.
main_sections.description: The Government may appoint such number of officers and other employees in such manner as may be prescribed to assist the Committee in the exercise of its powers and the performance of its functions under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power to prevent commission of offences.
main_sections.description: Every Forest Officer and every officer authorised under the Government shall have the powers of Police Officers for the purpose of investigation or prevention of offences under this Act and the collection of evidence.

If any person contravenes any provision of this Act, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.

No court shall take cognizance of any offence punishable under this Act except on a report in writing of the facts constituting such offence made by a forest officer or any other officer authorised by the Government in this behalf.

main_sections.section_title: Members of Committee, etc., to be public servants.
