main_sections.description: The members of the Committee, the officers and servants of the Committee and the members of the monitoring team shall be deemed to be public servants within the meaning of section 21 of the Indian Penal Code (Central Act 45 of 1860).

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
main_sections.description: No suit, prosecution or other legal proceedings shall lie against any person for anything which is in good faith done or intended to be done in pursuance of this Act or any rule made thereunder.

The Government may, in consultation with the Committee and by notification in the Gazette, make rules for the purpose of carrying into effect the provisions of this Act. Every rule made before the Legislative Assembly while it is in session for a total period of fourteen days which may be comprised in one session or in two successive sessions and, if before the expiry of the session in which it is laid, or the session immediately following, the Legislative Assembly makes any modification in the rule or decides that the rule should not be made, the rule shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect, as the case may be, so however that any such modification or annulment shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that rule.

The Silent Valley Protected Area (Protection of Ecological Balance) Ordinance, 1978 (31 of 1978), is hereby repealed. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under this Act as if this Act had come into force on the 30th day of December, 1978.

important_rules: No roads shall be constructed in the protected area except along or within the full capacity contour.
No forests shall be felled in the protected area except those within the full capacity contour or the project area.
No person engaged in the construction of the project shall keep cattle or goats or let out any animal into the protected area for grazing.
No person shall carry on quarrying in, or remove earth or soil from, the protected area, except in or from the area within the full capacity contour or the project area.

All persons engaged in the construction of the project in the protected area and all persons allowed to stay in the protected area shall assist in measures to protect the forest in the protected area from fire when required.
No person shall enter into the protected area without an identity card or pass issued by the Project Authority or any forest officer or other officer authorised by the Committee.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Forest officers, other authorized officers, Project Authority, Government of Kerala, Silent Valley Environmental Monitoring Committee.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Investigation and prevention of offences by authorized officers, court proceedings for cognizance of offences based on reports from authorized officers.

rights: Right to carry out necessary construction of roads, staff quarters, offices, workshops, and other works for essential services within the protected area under specific conditions.
Right to appoint officers and employees to assist the Committee.
duties: Duty of Project Authority to provide and place at the disposal of the Kerala Forest Department funds for compensatory afforestation.
Duty of all persons engaged in construction or staying in the protected area to assist in fire protection measures.
obligations: Obligation to obtain identity cards or passes before entering the protected area.
Obligation to adhere to restrictions on construction, felling of forests, grazing, cultivation, and quarrying within the protected area.

key_procedures: Constitution of the Silent Valley Environmental Monitoring Committee by the Government in consultation with the National Committee on Environmental Planning and Co-ordination.
Establishment of monitoring stations in the protected area by the Government on the recommendation of the Committee.
Carrying out monitoring operations by a monitoring team appointed by the Government on the recommendation of the Committee.
Issuance of identity cards and passes by the Project Authority or authorized officers for entry into the protected area.
Submission of reports by forest officers or other authorized officers to courts for the cognizance of offences.
administration: Government of Kerala, in consultation with the National Committee on Environmental Planning and Co-ordination, and the Project Authority (Kerala State Electricity Board or other specified authority).
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 28th March, 1979 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 235, dated 29th March, 1979.
The Silent Valley Protected Area (Protection of Ecological Balance) Ordinance, 1978 (31 of 1978), is repealed.
Anything done or any action taken under the Ordinance as if this Act had come into force on the 30th day of December, 1978, is deemed to have been done or taken.

title: The Sivagiri Mutt (Emergency Provisions) Act, 1997
purpose: To provide for the management of the Sivagiri Mutt, its properties, and assets in an emergency situation.
scope: Applies to the Sivagiri Mutt and its properties and assets.

key_definitions.emergency_period: The period during which the emergency provisions are in effect, as declared by the Government.
key_definitions.trustees: Refers to the existing or appointed trustees of the Mutt.
key_definitions.competent_authority: Any officer or authority appointed by the Government to exercise powers and perform functions under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and its territorial extent of application.
Defines key terms used in the Act.
Empowers the Government to declare an emergency in relation to the Mutt if it is satisfied that the management of the Mutt is in a state of emergency.
Authorizes the Government to appoint an administrator to manage the affairs of the Mutt during the emergency period.
Outlines the powers and responsibilities of the appointed administrator, including the management of properties, assets, and affairs of the Mutt.

main_sections.section_title: Dissolution of existing board of trustees, etc.
main_sections.description: Provides for the dissolution of the existing board of trustees or managing committee of the Mutt upon the declaration of emergency.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Grants protection to any action taken by the Government or the administrator in good faith in pursuance of the provisions of this Act.
Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of this Act.
Provides for the repeal of any existing law or provision inconsistent with this Act and saves anything done or action taken under the repealed provisions.

important_rules: The Government can declare an emergency if it is satisfied that the management of the Sivagiri Mutt is in a state of emergency.
During the emergency period, the administrator appointed by the Government shall manage the Mutt's affairs.
Existing boards of trustees or managing committees will be dissolved.
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government and the appointed administrator.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers vested in the Government and the administrator as defined in the Act, including the management of properties and affairs of the Mutt.

rights: Right to protection for actions taken in good faith.
duties: Duty of the administrator to manage the Mutt's affairs efficiently.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act and any rules made thereunder.

key_procedures: Declaration of emergency by the Government.
Appointment of an administrator by the Government.
Management of the Mutt's affairs by the administrator.
Dissolution of existing management bodies.
administration: The Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act is intended to provide for the management of the Sivagiri Mutt during emergency situations.
The provisions of this Act override any inconsistent provisions in other laws.
The Act may be repealed or amended by subsequent legislation.

title: The Sree Pandaravaka Lands (Vesting And Enfranchisement Amendment Act, 1975
purpose: To amend The Sree Pandaravaka Lands (Vesting and Enfranchisement) Act, 1971.
scope: Applies to the amendment of the principal Act concerning Sree Pandaravaka Lands.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called The Sree Pandaravaka Lands (Vesting and Enfranchisement) Amendment Act, 1975, and specifies its commencement date as the first day of August, 1973.
Amends section 13 of the principal Act by substituting the words "two years" with "four years".

Repeals The Sree Pandaravaka Lands (Vesting and Enfranchisement) Amendment Ordinance, 1975 (1 of 1975). It also includes a saving clause stating that anything done or any action taken under the repealed Ordinance as amended by the principal Act shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

administration: Not specified in the provided text.
important_notes: Received the assent of the President on the 3rd day of April, 1975 and published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 177 dated 4th April, 1975.

title: THE SREE PANDARAVAKA LANDS (VESTING AND ENFRANCHISEMENT) ACT, 1971
purpose: To provide for the enfranchisement of Sree Pandaravaka lands held by landholders and for the vesting in the Government of certain Sree Pandaravaka Thanathu lands.
scope: Applies to Sree Pandaravaka lands held by landholders in the Government of certain Sree Pandaravaka Thanathu lands. Also covers landholders, the Temple, and government officials involved in administration and enforcement.

key_definitions.appointed day: The day on which the Act comes into force.
key_definitions.basic tax: The tax imposed under the provisions of the Kerala Land Tax Act, 1961 (13 of 1961).
key_definitions.financial year: The year commencing on the 1st day of April.
key_definitions.holding: Any parcel or parcels of Sree Pandaravaka land held by a landholder.
key_definitions.kuthakapatom: A lease of Sree Pandaravaka Thanathu lands or of trees on such lands granted for a consideration payable in money or in kind or in both, whether annually or otherwise.
key_definitions.landholder: A person who holds Sree Pandaravaka land directly under the Temple on Pattam, Otti, Jenmom, Kudienmom or Danam or under any other tenure by whatever name called, and includes his heirs, legal representatives and assigns, but does not include a person who holds Sree Pandaravaka Thanathu lands on kuthakapattom.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.rent: Whatever is lawfully payable in money or in kind or in both, to the Temple by a landholder for the use and occupation of any Sree Pandaravaka land.
key_definitions.Sree Pandaravaka land: Any land owned by the Sree Pandaravaka Temple and registered in the revenue records as "Sree Pandaravaka".
key_definitions.Sree Pandaravaka Thanathu land: Land registered as 'Sree Pandaravaka Thanathu' in the revenue records and includes such lands held on kuthakapatom.
key_definitions.Temple: The Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple at Trivandrum.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called The Sree Pandaravaka Lands (Vesting and Enfranchisement) Act, 1971, and it shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'basic tax', 'financial year', 'holding', 'kuthakapatom', 'landholder', 'prescribed', 'rent', 'Sree Pandaravaka land', 'Sree Pandaravaka Thanathu land', and 'Temple'.

main_sections.section_title: Extinguishment and vesting of certain rights of the Temple.
main_sections.description: Deals with the extinguishment of rights of the Temple and the vesting of rights and interest of the Temple in Sree Pandaravaka Thanathu lands in the Government. It also covers the vesting of land belonging to the Temple before the appointed day and its use as an office for the administration of Melkanganam.

main_sections.section_title: Landholders to be vested with proprietary right.
main_sections.description: Vests proprietary right in landholders, subject to the provisions of Section 8, making such right heritable and alienable, but landholder shall be liable to pay rent to the Temple.

Specifies that where in respect of Sree Pandaravaka Thanathu lands vested in the Government under clause (b) of sub-section (1) of section 3, there is a lease or kuthakappattam, such lease shall be deemed to continue under the Government on the same terms and conditions as under the Temple. It also allows the Government to assign on registry any such land for Government or public purposes.

Details the compensation payable by the Government to the Temple for the extinguishment of its rights and interests in Sree Pandaravaka Thanathu lands and buildings. The compensation includes an amount of fifty-eight thousand and five hundred rupees as an annuity.

main_sections.section_title: Certain landholders to pay compensation for rights vested in them.
main_sections.description: Stipulates the annual rent payable by every landholder who has a proprietary right vested in him. It also outlines the method of calculation and payment of this annual rent, and the commutation rate for rents in respect of lands in Chirayinkil taluk.

States that with effect from the appointed day, all Sree Pandaravaka lands held by landholders shall be deemed to be Pandaravaka lands for all purposes and shall be subject to the provisions of the Kerala Land Tax Act, 1961, and landholders shall be liable to be charged with basic tax.

main_sections.section_title: Issue of pattas and other documents to landholders.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to issue pattas or other documents evidencing the full proprietary rights of the landholders.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of officers to settle compensation payable by landholders and for issue of pattas.
main_sections.description: Allows the Government to appoint or authorise officers to make inquiry and determine compensation payable by landholders, and for the issue of pattas or other documents.

Provides for an appeal by any person aggrieved by an order of any appointed officer or authorised under section 10, to the District Collector, Trivandrum, or any other officer empowered in this behalf by the Government.

Grants the Board of Revenue the power to either suo motu or on application by any person aggrieved by an order passed by any officer under the Act, call for and examine the record of any proceeding. It also clarifies when the Board of Revenue shall not call for and examine records.

Empowers the Temple to collect arrears of rent from any landholder. It also specifies how arrears of rent shall be collected, including interest, and that such arrears shall be deemed to be fully discharged if the landholder pays a certain amount.

main_sections.section_title: Certain amounts to be first charge.
main_sections.description: Declares that compensation payable by a landholder under section 7 and any amount which the Tahsildar is entitled to collect under sub-section (1) of section 13 shall be a first charge upon the land in respect of which such compensation or amount is payable.

Provides for the application of certain provisions to the persons employed in the Melkanganam branch of the Sree Pandaravaka Department. It specifies that the Government shall have power to terminate the services of such persons and that persons whose services are retained shall be governed by such rules as the Government may make.

important_rules: Landholders vested with proprietary rights are heritable and alienable, but they are liable to pay rent to the Temple.
Sree Pandaravaka Thanathu lands leased or under kuthakappattam shall continue under the Government on the same terms.
Basic tax shall be charged on all Sree Pandaravaka lands held by landholders.
The Temple has the power to collect arrears of rent from landholders, including interest.
Compensation payable by landholders and certain amounts to be collected by the Tahsildar are a first charge on the land.

rights: Landholders have a vested proprietary right in their holdings.
Landholders have the right to appeal against orders of officers appointed under the Act.
The Board of Revenue has the right to revise orders passed by officers.
duties: Landholders have a duty to pay rent to the Temple.
Landholders have a duty to pay basic tax.
Landholders have a duty to pay compensation as determined under the Act.
Government officials have a duty to administer the Act and its provisions.
obligations: Landholders are obligated to pay rent and basic tax.
The Government is obligated to compensate the Temple for vested rights.
The Government is obligated to provide for the maintenance, upkeep, and use of Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple and any attached thereto.

key_procedures: Issuance of pattas and other documents to landholders to confirm proprietary rights.
Appointment of officers to inquire into and settle compensation payable by landholders and to issue pattas.
Appeals against orders of appointed officers to the District Collector or other empowered officer.
Revision of proceedings by the Board of Revenue.
Collection of arrears of rent by the Temple from landholders.
administration: Board of Revenue, District Collector and other officers to have certain powers of civil court; Government may appoint or authorise officers.
important_notes: The Act came into effect on a date appointed by the Government.
The Act defines various terms crucial to its interpretation.
The Government can issue rules for the application of the Act.
The Act is amended by Section 2, Act 13 of 1961.

title: THE SREE SANKARACHARYA UNIVERSITY OF SANSKRIT (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2003
purpose: To amend The Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit Act, 1994.
scope: Applies to The Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit, Kerala.

key_definitions.recognised institution: Means the Kerala Kalamandalam at Cheruthuruthy in Thrissur District, a society registered under the Travancore-Cochin Literary, Scientific and Charitable Societies Registration Act, 1955 (12 of 1955).

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (Amendment) Act, 2003 and it came into force on the 28th day of November, 2002.
Amends section 2 of the Principal Act by inserting a definition for 'recognised institution'.

Amends section 7 of the Principal Act by inserting clauses (iv a) and (vi a) under item (iv) and item (vi) respectively. These clauses relate to prescribing degree courses in fine arts and conferring degrees for courses of study in recognised institutions.

Amends sub-section (2) of section 14 of the Principal Act by inserting clauses (xxa) and (xxb). These clauses relate to coordinating, supervising, regulating and controlling teaching in recognised institutions and prescribing qualifications for teachers.

Repeals the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (Amendment) Ordinance, 2002 (10 of 2002) and states that any action taken under the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: Degree courses in fine arts such as music, drama and painting according to Indian traditions are to be conducted in recognised institutions.
Persons who have undergone such courses of study are eligible for examinations.
Degrees are to be conferred on persons who have pursued a course of study in a recognised institution and passed the examination.
The university must co-ordinate, supervise, regulate and control the conduct of teaching in prescribed courses in recognised institutions.
Qualifications for teachers for the prescribed courses in recognised institutions must be prescribed.

rights: Right to confer degrees on persons who have pursued a course of study in a recognised institution and passed the examination.
duties: Duty to conduct degree courses in fine arts in recognised institutions.
Duty to prescribe qualifications for teachers in recognised institutions.
obligations: The university has an obligation to co-ordinate, supervise, regulate and control the conduct of teaching in the prescribed courses in the recognised institution.

key_procedures: Inserting new clauses into existing sections of the Principal Act to define 'recognised institution' and specify the university's role in conducting courses, conferring degrees, and regulating teaching.
Repealing a previous ordinance and ensuring continuity of actions taken under it.
administration: The Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on 7th March, 2003 and was published in Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 393 dated 7th March, 2003.
The commencement date is retrospective (November 28, 2002).

title: THE SREE SANKARACHARYA UNIVERSITY OF SANSKRIT (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2008
purpose: An Act, further to amend the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit Act, 1994, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit.

key_definitions.Pro-Vice-Chancellor: "Pro-Vice-Chancellor" means the Pro-Vice-Chancellor of the University.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (Amendment) Act, 2008, and it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 9th day of June, 2008.
Amends Section 2 of the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit Act, 1994, by inserting a clause defining "Pro-Vice-Chancellor".
Amends Section 3 of the principal Act by replacing the words "the Vice-Chancellor" with "the Pro-Vice-Chancellor".

Amends Section 12 of the principal Act regarding 'Ex-officio Members'. It renumbers existing items and inserts new items, including the Pro-Vice-Chancellor and the Secretary to Government, Finance Department. It also clarifies that certain individuals nominated to the Syndicate will not stand vacant on election to the Chairperson of the University Union and such Chairperson will stand nominated to the Syndicate on the date of his election.
Amends sub-section (3) of Section 15 of the principal Act by replacing "the Pro-Vice-Chancellor" and "in his absence" with "the Pro-Vice-Chancellor, and in the absence of both".
Amends sub-section (3) of Section 16 of the principal Act, under the heading 'Ex-Officio Members', by inserting new clauses.

Amends sub-section (3) of Section 18 of the principal Act regarding the Pro-Vice-Chancellor. It specifies that the Pro-Vice-Chancellor, or in his absence, the Vice-Chancellor, if present, may preside over a meeting of the Academic Council.
Amends sub-section (1) of Section 21 of the principal Act by inserting the title "The Pro-Vice-Chancellor".
Amends Section 23 of the principal Act by inserting the title "The Pro-Vice-Chancellor".

Amends sub-section (6) of Section 24 of the principal Act. In the event of a temporary vacancy in the office of the Vice-Chancellor or where the Vice-Chancellor is temporarily absent, the Pro-Vice-Chancellor shall exercise the powers and perform the duties of the Vice-Chancellor or perform the routine duties of the Vice-Chancellor, as the case may be.
After sub-section (11) of section 26 of the principal Act, the following sub-section is inserted: "(12) The Vice-Chancellor may delegate any of his powers to the Pro-Vice-Chancellor."

Inserts a new Section 27 detailing the appointment, tenure, salary, and conditions of service of the Pro-Vice-Chancellor. The Pro-Vice-Chancellor shall be appointed by the Chancellor from a panel submitted by the Pro-Vice-Chancellor, shall not have completed sixty-five years of age, shall be a whole time salaried officer, shall hold office for a term of four years from the date of appointment and be eligible for re-appointment, and their salary and other conditions of service shall be prescribed by the Statutes. Their powers and functions are subject to the provisions of the Act, Statutes, Ordinances and Regulations and shall be exercised in consultation with the Vice-Chancellor.

Repeals the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (Amendment) Ordinance, 2008. It also provides that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor (as per the provisions of the Act and related statutes/ordinances)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers and functions vested in the university authorities as outlined in the Act and its amendments.

rights: Right of the Pro-Vice-Chancellor to perform duties of the Vice-Chancellor in case of vacancy or absence (Section 10).
Right of the Vice-Chancellor to delegate powers to the Pro-Vice-Chancellor (Section 11).
duties: Duty of the Pro-Vice-Chancellor to exercise powers and perform duties of the Vice-Chancellor during temporary absence or vacancy (Section 10).
Duty of the Pro-Vice-Chancellor to perform duties in consultation with the Vice-Chancellor (Section 12, sub-section 6).
obligations: Obligation of the Pro-Vice-Chancellor to be appointed from a panel submitted by the Chancellor (Section 12).
Obligation to adhere to age limit and tenure for the Pro-Vice-Chancellor (Section 12).

key_procedures: Appointment of Pro-Vice-Chancellor: Appointed by the Chancellor from a panel submitted by the Pro-Vice-Chancellor (Section 12).
Delegation of powers: The Vice-Chancellor may delegate any of his powers to the Pro-Vice-Chancellor (Section 11).
Exercise of powers during vacancy/absence: In case of temporary vacancy or absence of the Vice-Chancellor, the Pro-Vice-Chancellor shall exercise powers and perform duties (Section 10).
Presiding over Academic Council meetings: Pro-Vice-Chancellor or Vice-Chancellor may preside over Academic Council meetings if present (Section 7).
administration: Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit Act, 1994.
The amendments came into force from June 9, 2008.
The Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (Amendment) Ordinance, 2008 (22 of 2008) is repealed and saved.
The Act specifies detailed provisions for the Pro-Vice-Chancellor's role, appointment, and service conditions.

title: The Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (Amendment) Act, 2018
purpose: To amend the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit Act, 1994, for purposes of re-enactment and for matters connected therewith.
scope: This Act applies to the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit and its functioning within Kerala. It specifically deals with the retirement age of teachers and other personnel within the university.

main_sections.description: (1) This Act may be called the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (Amendment) Act, 2018. (2) It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of November, 2017.

This section provides for the substitution of a new sub-section (3) in section 31 of the Principal Act (Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit Act, 1994). The new sub-section deals with the retirement age of teachers and other university employees. It specifies that teachers in the University's colleges will retire at the age of 60, and their retirement will be effective at the end of the academic year. For other university employees and teaching staff not covered by the initial clause, the Government may, by notification, fix the retirement age based on the working of teaching staff. However, the new sub-section clarifies that the age of retirement for any person in relation to a 'self-financing institution' shall not be less than 60 years and shall be regulated in the manner prescribed by the statutes of the said institution.

(1) The Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (Amendment) Ordinance, 2018 (2018 of 24) is hereby repealed. (2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken or any proceedings commenced or any appointment made or any penalty incurred or any punishment awarded or any penalty or punishment imposed or any offence committed or any fine imposed or any tax levied or any notice issued or any license granted or any mortgage created or any debt incurred or any security furnished or any agreement entered into or any other instrument executed under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken or commenced or made or incurred or awarded or imposed or committed or levied or issued or granted or created or incurred or furnished or entered into or executed under the corresponding provisions of this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Teachers in the University's colleges will retire at the age of 60, and their retirement will be effective at the end of the academic year.
Rule 2: For other university employees and teaching staff not covered by the initial clause, the Government may, by notification, fix the retirement age based on the working of teaching staff.

Rule 3: The age of retirement for any person in relation to a 'self-financing institution' shall not be less than 60 years and shall be regulated in the manner prescribed by the statutes of the said institution.
Rule 4: Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are considered valid under the corresponding provisions of this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government of Kerala and relevant university authorities.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act and its related statutes and regulations, including the functioning of the university and its self-financing institutions.

key_procedures: Amendment of Section 31 of the Principal Act: This involves substituting a new sub-section (3) that defines the retirement age for university personnel, particularly differentiating between regular colleges and self-financing institutions.
Repeal and Saving: The process of repealing the Ordinance and ensuring that actions taken under it are saved and deemed valid under the new Act.
administration: The Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit and the Department of Higher Education, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The amendment is deemed to have come into force on 1st November 2017.
A distinction is made in retirement age regulation between regular university teaching staff and staff in 'self-financing institutions'.

title: The Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (Amendment) Act, 2005
purpose: To amend The Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit Act, 1994.
scope: Applies to The Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title as 'The Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (Amendment) Act, 2005' and states that it shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Amends Section 2 of the Principal Act (1994-C. 15) by inserting a new clause (ii-a) to define 'academic year'.
Amends Section 3 of the Principal Act (1994-C. 15) by substituting the existing sub-section (1) and (2) with new sub-sections regarding the duration of terms of office for certain appointments.

Amends Section 4 of the Principal Act (1994-C. 15) by adding new clauses (ii-a) and (ii-b) to sub-section (1) regarding the powers of the Syndicate. It also inserts new sub-sections (ii) and (iii) to provide for the remuneration and allowances of the Vice-Chancellor and Pro-Vice-Chancellor.
Amends Sections 15 and 16 of the Principal Act (1994-C. 15) by inserting new clauses regarding the powers of the Syndicate in relation to admissions and examinations.

Amends Section 16 of the Principal Act (1994-C. 15) by substituting the existing sub-section (3) with a new sub-section regarding the selection of persons for appointment as teachers and other academic staff.
Amends Section 18 of the Principal Act (1994-C. 15) by substituting the existing sub-section (3) with a new sub-section regarding the procedures for the establishment of new departments and courses.
Amends Section 20 of the Principal Act (1994-C. 15) by substituting the existing sub-section (3) with a new sub-section regarding the functions of the Academic Council.
Amends Section 21 of the Principal Act (1994-C. 15) by substituting the existing sub-section (1) and (2) with new sub-sections regarding the composition and functions of the Senate.
Amends Section 23 of the Principal Act (1994-C. 15) by substituting the existing sub-section (1) with a new sub-section regarding the meetings of the Senate.
Amends Section 24 of the Principal Act (1994-C. 15) by substituting the existing sub-section (6) with a new sub-section regarding the powers of the Syndicate.
Amends Section 27 of the Principal Act (1994-C. 15) by substituting the existing sub-section (1) and (2) with new sub-sections regarding the procedure for amending Statutes and Ordinances.
Amends Section 29 of the Principal Act (1994-C. 15) by substituting the existing sub-section (1) with a new sub-section regarding the powers of the Vice-Chancellor.
Amends Section 31 of the Principal Act (1994-C. 15) by substituting the existing sub-section (3) with a new sub-section regarding the powers of the Pro-Vice-Chancellor.
Amends Section 38 of the Principal Act (1994-C. 15) by substituting the existing sub-section (10) with a new sub-section regarding the powers of the Syndicate to make Statutes.
Amends Section 44 of the Principal Act (1994-C. 15) by substituting the existing sub-section (1) and (2) with new sub-sections regarding the powers of the Syndicate to make Ordinances.

Repeals the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (Amendment) Ordinance, 2005 (Ordinance No. 3 of 2005) and provides for savings.

administration: The Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit
important_notes: The amendment aims to modify various sections of the original Act to update its provisions.

Specific changes are made to sections related to definitions, terms of office, powers of various university bodies (Syndicate, Senate, Academic Council, Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor), and procedures for making Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations.
The amendment repeals a previous ordinance and ensures continuity of actions taken under it.

title: THE SREEPADAM LANDS ENFRANCHISEMENT ACT, 1969
purpose: To provide for the enfranchisement of Sreepadam lands on payment of compensation and for matters connected therewith.
scope: Applies to Sreepadam lands and landholders of Sreepadam lands. The act's provisions are effective from the appointed day, which is the date of publication in the Gazette.

key_definitions.appointed_day: The day on which the act comes into force, notified in the Gazette.
key_definitions.basic_tax: The tax imposed under the provisions of the Kerala Land Tax Act, 1961.
key_definitions.financial_year: The year commencing on the 1st day of April.
key_definitions.holding: Any parcel or parcels of Sreepadam lands held by a landholder.
key_definitions.kuthakapatom: A lease of Sreepadam lands or of trees on such lands or of both, granted for consideration payable in money or in kind or in both, whether annually or otherwise.
key_definitions.landholder: A person holding at the commencement of this Act Sreepadam lands on Sreepadam pattam or other favourable tenures, but does not include a person holding Sreepadam lands on Kuthakapatom.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.rent: Whatever is lawfully payable in money or in kind or in both, to the Sreepadam Palace by a landholder for the use and occupation of any Sreepadam land.
key_definitions.Sreepadam lands: Lands comprised in the free-hold villages of Idakkode, Illamba, Muddakkal, Alamkodu, Avanavancherry, Attingal and Kilattingal in the Chirayinkil Taluk, the revenue from which is wholly assigned in favour of the Sreepadam Palace.
key_definitions.tharisu: Lands entered as tharisu in the revenue records (other than lands held under Kuthakapatom) and owned by the Sreepadam Palace, but does not include any such land held by a landholder.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act and that it shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'basic tax', 'financial year', 'holding', 'kuthakapatom', 'landholder', 'prescribed', 'rent', 'Sreepadam lands', and 'tharisu'.

main_sections.section_title: Extinguishment of the rights of Sreepadam Palace
main_sections.description: Declares that notwithstanding any contravention in law or contract, all rights, title and interest of the Sreepadam Palace in all Sreepadam lands held by landholders shall stand extinguished, and all Sreepadam lands held on Kuthakapatom shall vest in the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Landholders to be registered holders under Government
main_sections.description: States that notwithstanding any contravention in law or contract, all landholders shall, subject to the provisions of section 9, have full proprietorship in the land comprised in his holding, and such right shall be heritable and alienable, except as provided in section 10, no landholder shall be liable to pay rent to the Sreepadam Palace.

Details the compensation payable to the Sreepadam Palace. For Sreepadam lands held on Kuthakapatom, the compensation is an amount of 31,075 rupees as annuity. For tharisu lands, the compensation is calculated at the rate of four hundred and ninety-four rupees per hectare of tharisu. These payments are to be made in lump sums annually or in such manner as may be prescribed, and bear interest at 5 per cent per annum if paid late.

main_sections.section_title: Treatment of lands held on Kuthakapatom
main_sections.description: Specifies that where Sreepadam lands are held on Kuthakapatom, such lease shall be deemed to continue under the Government on the same terms and conditions as under the Sreepadam Palace. Subject to the provisions of sub-section (1), the Government may, at any time after the appointed day, after reserving the lands necessary for Government or public purposes, assign on registry in such manner and on payment of such consideration as may be prescribed, the remaining lands vested in the Government under clause (b) of section 3.

States that all tharisu vested in the Government under clause (c) of section 3 shall be surveyed and demarcated in such manner as may be prescribed. After survey and demarcation, the Government shall, after reserving the necessary tharisu for Government or public purposes, assign on registry in such manner and on payment of such consideration as may be prescribed. Preference shall be given to the persons in actual occupation of the tharisu immediately before the appointed day.

main_sections.section_title: Recovery of amounts due to Government
main_sections.description: Specifies that all amounts due as arrears of Kuthakapatom or towards consideration for assignment of lands on registry shall be a first charge on the land held under Kuthakapatom or assigned on registry and shall be recoverable as arrears of land revenue under the Revenue Recovery Act for the time being in force.

States that from the appointed day, all Sreepadam lands held by landholders immediately before that day shall be deemed to be pandaravaka lands for all purposes and shall be liable to be charged with basic tax. Landholders shall be liable to pay basic tax and the provisions of the Kerala Land Tax Act, 1961, shall apply to the levy and collection of such tax.

States that the Sreepadam Palace shall not be entitled to collect any rent accrued due to it from any landholder in respect of his holding before and outstanding on that day. However, the Tahsildar of the taluk in which the holding is situated shall cease to collect all arrears of rent and any interest payable thereon if they were arrears of public revenue due on land. Provided that if a landholder pays within two years from the appointed day, in such manner as may be prescribed, an amount equal to the arrears of rent for three financial years, the actual arrears outstanding on the appointed day, whichever is less, together with interest thereon, all arrears of rent shall be deemed to be fully discharged and no suit or other proceedings shall be or continue for the recovery thereof. Amounts paid or collected under sub-section (1) shall be paid to the Sreepadam Palace after deducting five per cent thereof on account of collection charges, or the amount if any, due from the Sreepadam Palace to the Government, or the rent, if any, collected before the appointed day by the Sreepadam Palace from any landholder in respect of any Sreepadam lands, or any subsequent financial year. All amounts which the Tahsildar is entitled to collect under sub-section (1) shall be a first charge upon the land in respect of which such amounts are payable, subject only to the charge for basic tax.

main_sections.section_title: Issue of pattas, etc., to landholders
main_sections.description: States that as soon as may be after the appointed day, the Government shall issue pattas or other documents evidencing the right of the landholder in the lands comprised in their holdings. The pattas or other documents issued under section (1) shall contain such particulars as may be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Appointment of officers to settle tax, etc.
main_sections.description: Specifies that the Government may appoint or authorise such officer or officers as they deem necessary for the purpose of settling the tax or other dues payable by landholders to the Government or to any other authority and for the issue of the pattas or other documents referred to in sub-section (1) of section 11. The appointed or authorised officer or officers may also be prescribed.

Any person aggrieved by any order of any officer appointed or authorised under sub-section (1) of section 12 may appeal to the Revenue Divisional Officer having jurisdiction over the area in which the holding is situate, within sixty days from the date of the order. A copy of every order against which an appeal lies under sub-section (1) shall be communicated in such manner as may be prescribed.

The District Collector may, either suo motu or on an application by a landholder, call for the record of any proceeding in which an order has been passed by the Revenue Divisional Officer under section 13, and may make such inquiry or cause such inquiry to be made and pass such order thereon as he thinks fit. Provided that the District Collector shall not revise any order under this section in any case where the application is made by the landholder for such revision, unless the application is made within one year from the date of the order sought to be revised; and where the order is sought to be revised by the District Collector of his own motion, if such order is made more than one year previously.

Any order passed by any officer or authority under this Act in respect of matters to be determined for the purposes of this Act shall, subject only to any appeal or revision provided under this Act, be final. No such order shall be liable to be questioned in any court of law.

No suit or other legal proceeding shall lie against the Government for any act which is in good faith done or intended to be done under this Act. No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall be instituted against any officer or other person for anything in good faith done or intended to be done under this Act or any rule made there under.

main_sections.section_title: Provisions in regard to liabilities of Sreepadam Palace
main_sections.description: All claims and liabilities enforceable immediately before the appointed day against the Sreepadam Palace in respect of any Sreepadam lands shall, on or after that day, be enforceable only against the annuity or compensation, as the case may be, payable to the Sreepadam Palace under this Act, and to the same extent to which such claim and liabilities were enforceable against the Sreepadam Palace in the said lands immediately before the appointed day. No court shall, on or after the appointed day, order or continue execution in respect of any decree or order passed against the Sreepadam Palace or against the interest it had in any Sreepadam lands, and execution shall be ordered or continued in such cases in conformity with the provisions of sub-section (1) only as against the annuity or compensation payable to the Sreepadam Palace. All rights and privileges which may have accrued in any Sreepadam lands to any person before the appointed day against the Sreepadam Palace shall cease and determine and shall not be enforceable against the Sreepadam Palace or against the Government, and every such person shall be entitled only to such rights and privileges as are recognised or conferred on him by or under this Act.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make rules for the purpose of carrying into effect the provisions of this Act. Such rules may provide for the procedure for the issue of pattas or other documents, prescribing forms where forms are necessary, the fees for appeals and applications for revision, regulating the powers of the Revenue Divisional Officer in appeals under this Act and the procedure to be followed in such appeals, and any other matter which has to be, or may be, prescribed. Every rule made under this section shall be laid as soon as may be after it is made before the Legislative Assembly while it is in session for a total period of fourteen days which may be comprised in one session or in two successive sessions, and if before the expiry of the session in which it is so laid or the session immediately following, the Legislative Assembly makes any modification in the rule or decides that the rule should not be made, the rule shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect, as the case may be; but so, however, that any such modification or annulment shall be without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that rule.
Amends section 2 of the Kerala Land Tax Act, 1961 (13 of 1961), in sub-section (1), clause (iii) by omitting the validity.

important_rules: Landholders shall have full proprietorship of their holdings and such rights are heritable and alienable.
No landholder is liable to pay rent to the Sreepadam Palace.
Arrears of Kuthakapatom or consideration for assignment of lands are a first charge on the land and recoverable as arrears of land revenue.
Sreepadam lands held by landholders are liable to be charged with basic tax.
The Sreepadam Palace cannot collect rent accrued due before the appointed day.
Government shall issue pattas or other documents evidencing landholder rights.
Appeals against orders must be filed within sixty days.
District Collector can revise orders under section 13.
No suit or legal proceeding shall lie against the Government or officers for good faith acts.
Claims and liabilities against Sreepadam Palace are enforceable only against the annuity or compensation.
Rules made under the Act must be laid before the Legislative Assembly.
Certain amendments are made to the Kerala Land Tax Act, 1961.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government, Revenue Divisional Officer, District Collector
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By making rules, issuing notifications, conducting inquiries, hearing appeals and revisions, and through the application of the Revenue Recovery Act for arrears.

rights: Landholders have full proprietorship of their holdings.
Land rights are heritable and alienable.
Landholders have the right to receive pattas or other documents evidencing their rights.
Persons in actual occupation of tharisu before the appointed day have preference for assignment.
Right to appeal orders to the Revenue Divisional Officer.
Right to seek revision of orders from the District Collector.
Rights and privileges recognised or conferred by this Act.
duties: Landholders are liable to pay basic tax on Sreepadam lands.
Landholders are liable to pay compensation to the Sreepadam Palace (as annuity or otherwise).
Persons seeking revision by the District Collector must apply within one year.

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act upon notification by the Government.
Definition of key terms used in the Act.
Extinguishment of Sreepadam Palace rights and vesting of lands in the Government.
Registration of landholders as holders under the Government.
Payment of compensation to the Sreepadam Palace.
Survey and demarcation of tharisu lands.
Assignment of tharisu lands on registry.
Recovery of amounts due to the Government as land revenue.
Payment of basic tax by landholders.
Collection of rent arrears (with specific provisions for discharge).
Issuance of pattas or other documents to landholders.
Appointment of officers for tax settlement and issue of documents.
Appeals process against officer's orders.
Revision process by the District Collector.
Rule-making power of the Government.
Amendment of the Kerala Land Tax Act, 1961.
administration: The Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act came into effect on a date notified in the Gazette.
Compensation for Sreepadam lands is paid as an annuity of 31,075 rupees.
Compensation for tharisu lands is 494 rupees per hectare.
Late payments of compensation and arrears attract interest at 5% per annum.
Any contravention in law or contract does not affect the extinguishment of Sreepadam Palace rights or the landholder's proprietorship.
The Act provides for the establishment of a procedure for the enfranchisement of Sreepadam lands.
Rules made under section 18 will have effect in modified form or be of no effect if modifications or annulments are made by the Legislative Assembly.

title: THE STATE TRANSPORT AUTHORITY AND THE REGIONAL TRANSPORT AUTHORITIES (CONTINUANCE OF THE TERM OF OFFICE) VALIDATION ACT, 1960
purpose: To validate the continuance of the term of office of the State Transport Authority and certain Regional Transport Authorities.
scope: Applies to the State Transport Authority and Regional Transport Authorities in Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the State Transport Authority and the Regional Transport Authorities (Continuance of the Term of Office) Validation Act, 1960.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of the sanction for the continuance of the term of office of the State Transport Authority and certain Regional Transport Authorities.
main_sections.description: This section validates the continuance of the term of office of the State Transport Authority and Regional Transport Authorities sanctioned by the Government. It also validates all orders and actions taken by these authorities. It clarifies that no suit or other proceeding challenging these actions shall be maintained if it is on the ground that the sanction or the Government's continuation of the term was not authorised by law.

important_rules: All powers exercised, orders performed, passed, done and taken by or under any provision of the said Motor Vehicles Act or the rules made thereunder by the said Authorities during the respective periods of Vrsal, shall be deemed to have been validly exercised, performed, passed, done and taken.

No suit or other proceeding challenging the validity of any such power exercised, duty performed, order passed, thing done or action taken or of any relief on the ground that such power, duty, order, thing or action was not validly exercised, performed, passed, done or taken, shall be maintained or continued in any court.

penalties: Provides that no action or omission on the part of any person shall be punishable as an offence which would not have been so punishable if this Act had not been passed.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Impliedly the State Transport Authority and Regional Transport Authorities, with oversight by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the validation of past actions and by preventing legal challenges to them.

rights: The right to have previous actions of the transport authorities validated.
The right to be free from prosecution for actions that would have been lawful had this Act been in force.

administration: The State Transport Authority and the Regional Transport Authorities, under the overall governance of the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Government notification No. 74520/58/FW/TB.1 dated the 23rd December, 1958, regarding the continuance of the term of office of the State Transport Authority and certain Regional Transport Authorities after the expiry of their term of office.
The High Court of Kerala's pronouncement that the said notification dated the 23rd December, 1958, cannot have retroactive operation.
This Act is published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 1st November, 1960.

title: THE STAY OF RECOVERY OF ARREARS OF JENMIKARAM ACT, 1975
purpose: To provide for the temporary protection of Kanam tenants and persons deriving title from them against proceedings for recovery of arrears of Jenmikaram and for matters incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to Kanam tenants and persons deriving title from them in Kerala, specifically concerning proceedings for the recovery of arrears of Jenmikaram.

key_definitions.jenmikaram: A term likely related to land revenue or rent payable by a Jenmi (landlord) or tenant in Kerala. The exact definition would be in a referenced act like the Kanam Tenancy Act, 1955.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and states that it may be called the Stay of Recovery of Arrears of Jenmikaram Act, 1975. It also specifies the commencement date (22nd day of January, 1975) and the date it ceases to have effect (31st day of December, 1975). Provisions of the Interpretation and General Clauses Act are made applicable.
States that words and expressions used in this Act have the meanings respectively assigned to them in the Kanam Tenancy Act, 1955 (XXIV of 1955).

main_sections.section_title: Stay of suits, applications, etc., for arrears of jenmikaram.
main_sections.description: This is the core section. It mandates that notwithstanding anything to the contrary in any other law or in any contract, no suit or application, nor any decree or order of any court, related to the recovery of arrears of jenmikaram accrued before the commencement of this Act shall have any effect. Furthermore, no application or proceedings in execution of a decree or order for the recovery of such arrears, or any suits, applications, decrees, or orders incidental or ancillary thereto, shall lie in any court or before any authority or officer at or after the commencement of this Act. All appeals against decrees or orders relating to such arrears, and all revisions against such decrees or orders, pending at the commencement of this Act, shall stand stayed, and no court or other authority or officer shall proceed with any such appeal or revision.

Specifies that when computing the period of limitation for the institution of suits or other proceedings, or for the making of applications or the filing of appeals and revisions, any duration during which such suits or other proceedings or applications or appeals or revisions were prohibited under this Act shall be excluded.

Repeals the Stay of Recovery of Arrears of Jenmikaram Ordinance, 1975 (2 of 1975). Notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the said Ordinance is deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: No suit or application, nor any decree or order of any court, for the recovery of arrears of jenmikaram accrued before the commencement of this Act shall have any effect.

No proceedings in execution of a decree or order for the recovery of arrears of jenmikaram, or any ancillary suits or applications, shall be entertained by any court or authority after the commencement of this Act.
All pending appeals and revisions related to arrears of jenmikaram shall be stayed.
Time during which recovery proceedings were prohibited by this Act must be excluded when calculating limitation periods.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts and other relevant authorities
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By staying proceedings, refusing to entertain new suits or applications, and halting execution of decrees/orders related to jenmikaram arrears.

rights: Right to a stay on proceedings for recovery of pre-commencement arrears of Jenmikaram.
Right to have limitation periods adjusted to exclude the period of prohibition.
obligations: Courts and authorities have a duty to stay all relevant proceedings and not entertain new ones.

key_procedures: The Act automatically stays proceedings upon its commencement. No specific application by tenants is detailed for this stay, implying it's a statutory effect.
Parties involved in appeals or revisions must be aware that these will be stayed. They cannot proceed further without explicit direction after the Act's influence ceases.
administration: While not explicitly stated, the administration would likely fall under departments dealing with land revenue, tenancy, and judicial matters in the State of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act had a limited duration, ceasing to have effect on December 31, 1975.
The Act received the assent of the President on the 3rd day of April, 1975, and was published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 176 dated 4th April, 1975.
The Act is a temporary measure to provide protection.
The Kanam Tenancy Act, 1955, is referenced for definitions of terms.

title: THE STAY OF RECOVERY OF ARREARS OF JENMIKARAM ACT, 1974
purpose: To provide for the temporary protection of kanam tenants and persons deriving title from them against proceedings for recovery of arrears of jenmikaram and for matters incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to suits, applications, etc., for arrears of jenmikaram. It also specifies limitations on proceedings and appeals related to jenmikaram arrears.

key_definitions.jenmikaram: Not explicitly defined in the provided text, but inferred to be a form of rent or arrears associated with land tenure in Kerala.
key_definitions.kanam tenant: Not explicitly defined, but refers to tenants who derive title from a jenmi.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called The Stay of Recovery of Arrears of Jenmikaram Act, 1974. It shall come into force at once and shall cease to have effect on the 30th day of June, 1974. It also mentions that upon the expiry of this Act, the provisions of section 4 of the Interpretation and General Clauses Act, 1125 (VII of 1125) shall apply as if this Act had then been repealed by an Act of the Kerala State Legislature.
Defines words and expressions used in the Act, stating they shall have the meanings respectively assigned to them in the Kanam Tenancy Act, 1955 (XXIV of 1955).

main_sections.section_title: Stay of suits, applications, etc., for arrears of Jenmikaram
main_sections.description: States that notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in the Kanam Tenancy Act, 1955 (XXIV of 1955) or in any other law or in any contract, or in any judgment, decree or order of any court, with effect from and on the commencement of this Act: (a) no suit or application or other proceedings for the recovery of arrears of jenmikaram accrued due before the commencement of this Act; or (b) no application for, or proceedings in, execution of a decree or order for the recovery of such arrears of jenmikaram or other application or proceedings incidental or ancillary thereto, shall lie in any court or before any other authority or officer, and all suits, applications and other proceedings for recovery of such arrears of jenmikaram and all applications for, and proceedings in, execution of decrees or orders for recovery of such arrears of jenmikaram and other applications and proceedings incidental or ancillary thereto, pending in any court or before any other authority or officer at the commencement of this Act, shall stand stayed. Additionally, all appeals against decrees or orders relating to arrears of jenmikaram accrued due before the commencement of this Act and all revisions against decrees or orders relating to such arrears of jenmikaram, pending in any court or before any other authority or officer at the commencement of this Act, shall stand stayed, and no court or other authority or officer shall proceed with any such appeal or revision filed after such commencement.

Specifies that in computing the period of limitation for the institution of suits or other proceedings or the making of applications or the filing of appeals and revisions prohibited under this Act, the time during which such suits or other proceedings or applications or appeals or revisions were prohibited under this Act shall be excluded.

important_rules: No suit or application for recovery of jenmikaram arrears accrued before the commencement of the Act shall lie.
No proceedings in execution of a decree or order for recovery of jenmikaram arrears shall be initiated or continued.
All pending suits, applications, and proceedings for recovery of jenmikaram arrears shall be stayed.
All appeals and revisions against decrees or orders related to jenmikaram arrears shall be stayed.
The time during which proceedings are stayed under this Act shall be excluded for computing limitation periods.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts and other authorities as per existing laws, but their proceedings are stayed by this Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: The Act enforces the stay of proceedings. Enforcement of the stay itself would be through judicial and administrative directives.

rights: Right of kanam tenants and persons deriving title to temporary protection from recovery proceedings for jenmikaram arrears.
duties: Duty of courts and authorities to stay proceedings as mandated by the Act.

key_procedures: Automatic stay of all suits, applications, and execution proceedings for jenmikaram arrears from the commencement of the Act.
Stay applies to pending and new actions, including appeals and revisions.
Application of Interpretation and General Clauses Act upon expiry of the Act for future legal interpretations.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be managed through the judicial and revenue administration of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act is temporary and has a specific expiry date (30th June, 1974).
The Act overrides any contrary provisions in other laws, contracts, judgments, decrees, or orders.
Interpretation of terms is governed by the Kanam Tenancy Act, 1955.

title: The Super Clays and Minerals Mining Company (Private) Limited (Acquisition of Undertakings) Act, 1983
purpose: To provide for the acquisition and transfer of the undertakings of The Super Clays and Minerals Mining Company (Private) Limited with a view to securing the proper management of such undertakings so as to subserve the interests of the general public by ensuring the continued production and distribution of china clay which is essential to the needs of the economy of the State and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to the acquisition and transfer of the undertakings of The Super Clays and Minerals Mining Company (Private) Limited. It aims to ensure the continued production and distribution of china clay, essential to the economy of Kerala.

key_definitions.appointed day: The date of commencement of this Act.
key_definitions.Commissioner: The Commissioner of Payments appointed under section 14.
key_definitions.Company: The Super Clays and Minerals Mining Company (Private) Limited, being a company within the meaning of the Companies Act, 1956 (Central Act 1 of 1956) and having its registered office at Cannanore.
key_definitions.Custodian: The person or body of persons appointed as Custodian under sub-section (2) of section 8.
key_definitions.Government Company: Means the Government Company in which the undertakings of the Company are directed to vest under section 6.
key_definitions.Hindustan China Clay Works: Means the concern known under the name and style 'Hindustan China Clay Works, Pappinissery' and includes the proprietors or owners thereof.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by the Government by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.specified date: Means such date as the Government may, for the purpose of any provisions of this Act, by notification in the Gazette, specify, and different dates may be specified for different provisions of this Act.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Super Clays and Minerals Mining Company (Private) Limited (Acquisition of Undertakings) Act, 1983. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 5th day of November, 1983.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'appointed day', 'Commissioner', 'Company', 'Custodian', 'Government Company', 'Hindustan China Clay Works', 'prescribed', and 'specified date'.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer and vesting in the Government of the undertakings of the Company.
main_sections.description: On the appointed day, the undertakings of the Company, the right, title and interest of the Company in relation to its undertakings and, save as otherwise expressly provided in this Act, the liabilities of the Company in relation to its undertakings, shall, by virtue of this Act, stand transferred to, and shall vest in, the Government.

The undertakings of the company shall be deemed to include all assets, rights, lease-holds, powers, authorities and privileges, and all property, movable and immovable, including lands, buildings, work-shops, stores, instruments, machinery and equipments, cash balances, cash on hand, cheques, demand drafts, reserve funds, investments, book debts and all other rights and interests in, or arising out of such property, as were immediately before the appointed day in the ownership, possession, power or control of the Company.

main_sections.section_title: Government not to be liable for certain prior liabilities
main_sections.description: No liability incurred by the Company before the appointed day, for the contravention of any provision of law for the time being in force, shall be enforceable against the Government, or where the undertakings of the Company are directed to vest in a Government Company, against that Government Company.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to direct vesting of the undertakings of the Company in a Government Company
main_sections.description: The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, direct that the right, title, interest and liabilities of the Company in relation to its undertakings which have vested in the Government under section 3 shall, instead of vesting in the Government, vest in a Government Company.
Details the payment of the amount for the transfer and vesting of the undertakings of the Company, including the manner of payment and interest.

main_sections.section_title: Management etc. of the undertakings of the Company.
main_sections.description: Governs the general superintendence, direction, control and management of the affairs and business of the undertakings of the Company, and the appointment of a Custodian.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of persons in charge of management of the undertakings of the Company to deliver assets, etc.
main_sections.description: Requires persons in charge of the management of the undertakings to deliver all assets, books of account, registers and other documents to the Government Company or the Custodian.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of persons to account for assets, etc., in their possession.
main_sections.description: Requires any person who, on the appointed day, had in his possession or under his control any assets, books, documents or other papers relating to any undertaking owned by the Company, and which has vested in the Government or a Government Company, to account for them.
Deals with the preparation and audit of accounts of the undertakings.
Ensures continuity of employment for employees of the company.
Deals with the transfer and continuance of provident fund and other funds.
Provides for the appointment of a Commissioner of Payments.

main_sections.section_title: Payment by Government to the Commissioner.
main_sections.description: Specifies the payment to be made by the Government to the Commissioner.

main_sections.section_title: Certain powers of the Government or the Government Company.
main_sections.description: Grants certain powers to the Government or the Government Company.

main_sections.section_title: Claims to be made to the Commissioner
main_sections.description: Directs claims to be made to the Commissioner.

main_sections.section_title: Examination and admission or rejection of claims
main_sections.description: Covers the process of examination, admission, or rejection of claims.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Commissioner to regulate his procedure, etc.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Commissioner to regulate his own procedure.
Allows for appeals by claimants.

main_sections.section_title: Disbursement of money by the Commissioner to claimants.
main_sections.description: Details the disbursement of money by the Commissioner to claimants.
Deals with the disposal of any remaining amount after payments.

main_sections.section_title: Right of Government to retain machinery, equipment, etc., not belonging to the Company.
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the right to retain machinery and equipment not belonging to the Company.

main_sections.section_title: Undisbursed or unclaimed amount to be deposited to the general revenue account.
main_sections.description: Mandates that any undisbursed or unclaimed amount be deposited into the general revenue account.
States that this Act has an overriding effect.
Outlines the penalties for offenses under the Act.
Addresses offenses committed by companies.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith.
Allows for the delegation of powers.
Grants the Government the power to make rules.
Grants the Government the power to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of any prior enactments and provides for savings.

important_rules: The undertakings of The Super Clays and Minerals Mining Company (Private) Limited, along with their liabilities, shall be transferred to and vest in the Government on the appointed day (November 5, 1983).
The Government can direct that these undertakings vest in a Government Company instead of directly in the Government.
All assets, rights, and property of the Company vest in the Government/Government Company.
The Government is not liable for prior contraventions of law by the Company.
A Commissioner of Payments will be appointed to manage the disbursement of amounts related to the acquisition.
Persons in charge of the Company's management must deliver all assets and documents to the Government Company or Custodian.
Employees of the Company are to have continuity of employment.

penalties: Penalties as prescribed under section 26 for offenses.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government, Government Company, and the appointed Commissioner of Payments.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act, including the appointment of a Commissioner, examination of claims, and penalties for offenses.

rights: Right of the Government to acquire the undertakings.
Right of the Government to direct vesting in a Government Company.
Right of the Government to retain machinery and equipment not belonging to the Company.
Right to appeal for claimants.
duties: Duty of persons in charge of management to deliver assets.
Duty of persons to account for assets in their possession.
Duty to comply with rules and directions issued under the Act.
obligations: Obligation of the Government to pay the determined amount for the acquisition.
Obligation of the Commissioner to disburse money to claimants.

key_procedures: Vesting of undertakings and liabilities in the Government or a Government Company.
Appointment of a Commissioner of Payments to manage financial aspects of the acquisition.
Process for claimants to make and prove their claims.
Disbursement of funds to claimants.
Overriding effect of the Act on other laws.
administration: The Government of Kerala is the primary administrative body, with powers delegated to the Government Company and the Commissioner of Payments.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force retrospectively from November 5, 1983.
The Act has an overriding effect, meaning it supersedes other laws that may be inconsistent with its provisions.
Protection is provided for actions taken in good faith under the Act.
The Government has the power to make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act.

title: The Supply of Paddy And Rice to Travancore Palace (Extinguishment of Right and Liabilities) Act, 1976
purpose: To provide for the extinguishment of the rights and liabilities in respect of four thousand paras of paddy, one hundred and ten paras of Njavara rice and one and a half paras of Oora rice to the Travancore Palace.
scope: Applies to the supply of paddy and rice to the Travancore Palace.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Supply of Paddy and Rice to Travancore Palace (Extinguishment of Rights and Liabilities) Act, 1976, and it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 20th day of April, 1972.

main_sections.section_title: Extinguishment of right of supply of paddy and rice.
main_sections.description: Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law, contract, or document, all rights, liabilities, and obligations in respect of four thousand paras of paddy, one hundred and ten paras of Njavara rice, and one and a half paras of Oora rice supplied annually by the Government to the Travancore Palace for use by the former Maharaja of Travancore and the Palace, in pursuance of the Order of the former Government of Travancore-Cochin No. G5-18313/49/CS, dated 12th December, 1949, shall stand extinguished, and no paddy or rice in pursuance of the said Order shall be supplied to the Travancore Palace.

Notwithstanding anything contained in any law, contract, or other document, no compensation shall be payable to the former Maharaja of Travancore or the Travancore Palace for the extinguishment of rights in respect of the paddy and rice mentioned in section 2.

important_rules: All rights, liabilities, and obligations concerning the specified supply of paddy and rice to the Travancore Palace are extinguished.
No further supply of paddy or rice under the Order of 1949 shall be made to the Travancore Palace.

rights: The right to the supply of paddy and rice to the Travancore Palace as per the 1949 Order is extinguished.

important_notes: The Act received the assent of the President on the 13th day of September, 1976, and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 526, dated 23rd September 1976.
The Act is deemed to have come into force on the 20th day of April 1972.

title: THE TERM OF OFFICE OF MUNICIPAL COUNCILLORS AND CHAIRMAN (EXTENSION) ACT
purpose: To extend the term of office of Municipal Councillors and Chairman.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin, including the Corporation of Trivandrum and all Municipalities constituted under the Travancore District Municipalities Act, 1116 or the Cochin Municipal Act, XVIII of 1113.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Term of Office of Municipal Councillors and Chairman (Extension) Act, 1950. It extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin and shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of term of office of Municipal Councillors and Chairman.
main_sections.description: This section deals with the extension of the term of office. It refers to Section 57 of the Travancore City Municipal Act, 1115 (IV of 1116), Section 8 of the Travancore District Municipalities Act, 1116 (XXIII of 1116), and Section 8 of the Cochin Municipal Act, XVIII of 1113, as continued in force by the United State of Travancore and Cochin Administration and Application of Laws Act, 1125 (VI of 1125), or Section 2 of the Travancore District Municipalities (Term of Office of Councillors Extension) Act, 1126. It grants the Government power to direct by notification in the Gazette that the term of office of councillors and chairman of the Corporation of Trivandrum constituted under the Travancore City Municipal Act, 1116, or of councillors and chairman of all or any Municipality constituted under the Travancore District Municipalities Act, 1116, or the Cochin Municipal Act, XVIII of 1113, shall extend up to such date as may be fixed by them. The Government can advance or postpone any date fixed under this sub-section, provided it is not later than the first day of November 1950.

important_rules: The Government has the power to extend the term of office of Municipal Councillors and Chairman.
The extension can be directed by notification in the Gazette.
The extension applies to the Corporation of Trivandrum and all Municipalities under specific Acts.
The Government can advance or postpone the fixed date of extension, but not beyond November 1, 1950.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notification in the Gazette.

rights: The right of the Government to direct the extension of term of office.

key_procedures: The Government issues a notification in the Gazette to extend the term of office of Municipal Councillors and Chairman.
The Government can advance or postpone the date fixed for the extension, provided it is not later than November 1, 1950.
administration: The Government of Travancore-Cochin
important_notes: The Act refers to several previous Acts, indicating a consolidation or amendment of existing provisions.
The extension is specific to the term of office and does not imply other changes to the councillors' or chairman's roles.

title: The Thiruppuvaram Payment (Abolition) Act, 1969
purpose: To provide for the extinguishment of the right to receive and the liability to pay Thiruppuvaram.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala, formerly comprised in the State of Travancore.

key_definitions.appointed day: The day on which the Act comes into force.
key_definitions.landholder: Any person liable to pay Thiruppuvaram in respect of any land.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Thiruppuholder: A person entitled to receive Thiruppuvaram immediately before the appointed day.
key_definitions.Thiruppuvaram:
