Means an assignment of the whole or a specific portion of the revenue payable to the Government by the holder of a specified land in favour of a person called the Thiruppuholder, in lieu of any payment which the Government were under an obligation to make to such person and entered as Thiruppuvaram in the revenue accounts and includes sums payable to the Thiruppuholder directly by the Government consequent on-
(i) the omission to enter in the Land Revenue Settlement Register of 1986 M.E. the assignment in favour of a Thiruppuholder of the whole or a portion of the land revenue payable by a landholder to the Government, or
(ii) the land revenue fixed as payable by a landholder at the Land Revenue Settlement of 1086 M.E. being less than the Thiruppuvaram assigned thereto that settlement in favour of a Thiruppuholder out of the land revenue payable by that landholder.
key_definitions.revenue accounts: Means the approved Janıabandi accounts and includes the settlement register.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its extent to the State of Kerala, and that it shall come into force on a date notified by the Government.
Defines terms used in the Act, including appointed day, compensation officer, landholder, prescribed, Thiruppuholder, Thiruppuvaram, and revenue accounts.

Abolishes the right to receive Thiruppuvaram and the liability to pay Thiruppuvaram on and after the appointed day. The Thiruppuholder shall not have the right to receive Thiruppuvaram, and the landholder shall have no liability to pay any Thiruppuvaram to the Thiruppuholder.

main_sections.section_title: Compensation to certain religious or charitable institutions of public nature
main_sections.description: Deals with compensation for Thiruppuvaram that has been extinguished for religious or charitable institutions of a public nature. Compensation is to be paid annually, deducting five percent thereof by way of collection charges. Explains when no such deduction is made and the procedure for appeals. Also covers service Thiruppuholders.

Addresses the provisions relating to service Thiruppuholders, including the payment of annuity to the institution in respect of service Thiruppuvaram. It also details the process for complaints and appeals related to service Thiruppuholders.

main_sections.section_title: Scale of compensation to Thiruppuholder not governed by section 4
main_sections.description: Specifies the scale of compensation payable to a Thiruppuholder not governed by section 4. It states that the Government shall pay to every Thiruppuholder compensation at twelve times the amount of Thiruppuvaram payable annually to the Thiruppuholder. It also outlines how to calculate the compensation in certain cases and mentions that the Thiruppuvaram payable on the Government's account shall be deducted.
Provides for the appointment of compensation officers by the Government to carry out functions and duties under the Act.
Details the process for compensation officers to inquire into Thiruppuvaram claims, including the submission of claims, decision-making, and the conditions under which grants are made.

main_sections.section_title: Lapse of Thiruppuvaram in certain cases
main_sections.description: States that Thiruppuvaram shall lapse in certain cases, such as when the grantee fails to comply with conditions or has ceased to perform the service.
Specifies the time limit for preferring claims for compensation by Thiruppuholders entitled to compensation.
Outlines the procedure for the compensation officer to determine the annuity payable and the compensation payable under section 4 or section 6.

main_sections.section_title: Determination of annuity and compensation in cases of delay
main_sections.description: Deals with the determination of annuity and compensation in cases of delay. It specifies how compensation is to be paid in case of delay.

main_sections.section_title: Compensation rate of paddy and other commodities
main_sections.description: Mentions that the compensation rate of paddy and other commodities shall be determined.
Concerns the payment of compensation.
Provides for appeals from orders made under section 14.

main_sections.section_title: Unclaimed or undisbursed amounts how to be dealt with
main_sections.description: Specifies how unclaimed or undisbursed amounts are to be dealt with.

main_sections.section_title: Wrong or excess payments to be recoverable as arrears of public revenue
main_sections.description: States that wrong or excess payments are to be recoverable as arrears of public revenue.

main_sections.section_title: Intrunt compensation to be paid in case of delay of compensation
main_sections.description: Addresses intrunt compensation to be paid in case of delay of compensation.
States that the landholder is liable to pay compensation.
Specifies that compensation is recoverable in twelve instalments.
Details how compensation is to be paid.

main_sections.section_title: Board of Revenue may condone default
main_sections.description: Allows the Board of Revenue to condone default.

main_sections.section_title: Compensation recoverable under Revenue Recovery Act
main_sections.description: States that compensation is recoverable under the Revenue Recovery Act.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of Central Board of Revenue
main_sections.description: Describes the powers of the Central Board of Revenue.
Deals with arrears of Thiruppuvaram.

main_sections.section_title: Communication of decisions or orders against which appeal or revision lies
main_sections.description: Concerns the communication of decisions or orders against which an appeal or revision lies.
Relates to the limitation period for actions or claims.
Specifies the finality of orders passed under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Jurisdiction of courts barred in certain cases
main_sections.description: Bars the jurisdiction of civil courts in certain cases.

main_sections.section_title: Compensation officer to be public servant
main_sections.description: Declares compensation officers to be public servants.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of Board of Revenue, etc., to summon and examine witnesses
main_sections.description: Grants powers to the Board of Revenue and other authorities to summon and examine witnesses.

main_sections.section_title: Payment of compensation to discharge of liability to pay Thiruppuvaram
main_sections.description: Concerns the payment of compensation to discharge the liability to pay Thiruppuvaram.
Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
Amends the Land Tax Act, 1961.

important_rules: On and after the appointed day, no Thiruppuholder shall have the right to receive Thiruppuvaram, and no landholder shall have any liability to pay any Thiruppuvaram to the Thiruppuholder. (Section 3)
Compensation for extinguished Thiruppuvaram of religious or charitable institutions of public nature is to be paid annually, with a deduction of five percent for collection charges. (Section 4(1))
The Government shall pay compensation to Thiruppuholders at twelve times the amount of Thiruppuvaram payable annually, for those not governed by section 4. (Section 6(1))
Compensation officers shall inquire into Thiruppuvaram claims and make decisions. (Section 8)
Thiruppuvaram shall lapse in certain cases, such as failure to perform service. (Section 9)
Claims for compensation must be preferred within the stipulated time. (Section 10)
Wrong or excess payments of compensation are recoverable as arrears of public revenue. (Section 17)
Compensation is recoverable in twelve equal instalments. (Section 20)
Compensation officers are public servants. (Section 30)

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Compensation Officers, Board of Revenue, District Collector.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inquiries, decisions, appeals, and recovery as arrears of public revenue. Orders passed by compensation officers can be appealed to the District Collector and then to the Government. Government orders can be subject to revision by the Board of Revenue. Section 23 states compensation is recoverable under the Revenue Recovery Act.

rights: Right to receive compensation for extinguished Thiruppuvaram.
Right to appeal decisions of compensation officers.
duties: Landholders have a duty to pay compensation.
Thiruppuholders have a duty to provide service in lieu of Thiruppuvaram (in certain cases before abolition).
Compensation officers have a duty to inquire into claims and make decisions.
obligations: The Government has an obligation to pay compensation to Thiruppuholders.

key_procedures: Determination of compensation by compensation officers.
Process for preferring claims for compensation.
Appeals from orders of compensation officers to the District Collector and then to the Government.
Revision of Government orders by the Board of Revenue.
Recovery of compensation as arrears of public revenue.
Procedure for inquiring into Thiruppuvaram claims.
Procedure for the payment of compensation.
administration: The Government (through appointed compensation officers, District Collectors, and the Board of Revenue).
important_notes: The Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 98, dated 9th April, 1969.
Jurisdiction of civil courts is barred in certain cases (Section 29).
The Act extinguishes the right to receive and the liability to pay Thiruppuvaram.

title: The Thunchath Ezhuthachan Malayalam University Act, 2013
purpose: The purpose of the act is to establish and incorporate a University by the name of Thunchath Ezhuthachan Malayalam University for the development and promotion of Malayalam language and literature and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: The Act applies to the establishment, incorporation, powers, functions and administration of the Thunchath Ezhuthachan Malayalam University.

key_definitions.University: Thunchath Ezhuthachan Malayalam University.
key_definitions.Vice-Chancellor: the Vice-Chancellor of the University appointed under section 11.
key_definitions.Statutes: Statutes of the University made under section 26.
key_definitions.Ordinances: Ordinances of the University made under section 27.
key_definitions.Regulations: Regulations of the University made under section 28.
key_definitions.Prescribed: prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Teacher: means a Professor, Associate Professor, Assistant Professor or such other      person      as      may      be      appointed      for      teaching      by      the      University      and      includes      such      visiting      Professors      and      such      other      persons      as      may      be      appointed      for      teaching      in      the      Colleges      or      Institutions      maintained      by      the      University      or      admitted      to      the      rights      and      privileges      of      teachers      in      the      Colleges      or      Institutions      of      the      University.
key_definitions.Member of the University: means the members of the Syndicate, the Academic Council, the Finance Committee, the Senate, the College Councils, the Faculty Councils, the Staff Councils, the Alumni Associations, the students of the University and such other persons as may be or may become members of the University under the provisions of this Act or the Statutes.
key_definitions.Governing Body: means the Governing Body of a college or an institution maintained by the University.
key_definitions.Head of the Department: means the Head of the Department of the University.
key_definitions.Pro-Vice-Chancellor: means the Pro-Vice-Chancellor of the University.
key_definitions.Registered Graduate: means a graduate whose name is entered in the Register of Graduates.
key_definitions.Syndicate: means the Syndicate of the University.
key_definitions.Academic Council: means the Academic Council of the University.
key_definitions.Finance Committee: means the Finance Committee of the University.
key_definitions.Senate: means the Senate of the University.
key_definitions.College Councils: means the College Councils of the University.
key_definitions.Faculty Councils: means the Faculty Councils of the University.
key_definitions.Staff Councils: means the Staff Councils of the University.
key_definitions.Alumni Associations: means the Alumni Associations of the University.
key_definitions.Court: means the Court of the University.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Thunchath Ezhuthachan Malayalam University Act, 2013 and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.
Provides definitions for various terms used in the Act, such as University, Vice-Chancellor, Statutes, Ordinances, Regulations, etc.

Declares the incorporation of the University by the name of Thunchath Ezhuthachan Malayalam University, which shall be a body corporate, having perpetual succession and a common seal, with power to acquire, hold and dispose of property and to enter into contracts.

Outlines the objectives of the University, including promotion and development of Malayalam language, literature and culture, conducting research, establishing departments, offering courses, conducting examinations and awarding degrees, diplomas and certificates.

Details the powers of the University, such as establishing colleges and institutions, co-operating with other universities, appointing staff, and performing all such acts as are necessary to further its objectives.
Specifies the territorial jurisdiction of the University.

main_sections.section_title: University to be open to all castes, creeds, etc.
main_sections.description: States that the University shall be open to all persons irrespective of caste, creed, sex, race or religion.
Ensures that admission to the University shall be open to all eligible persons who conform to the academic and other requirements prescribed by the University.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of the Pro-Vice-Chancellor
main_sections.description: Outlines the powers and functions of the Pro-Vice-Chancellor, including assisting the Vice-Chancellor, exercising powers delegated by the Vice-Chancellor, and performing other duties assigned by the Vice-Chancellor.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of the Registrar
main_sections.description: Details the powers and functions of the Registrar, such as being the administrative head of the University, maintaining records, and ensuring implementation of decisions of the University authorities.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of the Finance Officer
main_sections.description: Describes the powers and functions of the Finance Officer, including managing the finances of the University, preparing budgets, and advising the University on financial matters.

main_sections.section_title: Powers and functions of the Controller of Examinations
main_sections.description: Explains the powers and functions of the Controller of Examinations, such as conducting examinations, preparing results, and issuing certificates.
Provides for the making of Statutes by the University, which shall govern the powers and functions of the University and its authorities. The Statutes require the assent of the Government.

Details the making of Ordinances by the University, which shall provide for matters relating to the conduct of the University's academic and administrative affairs. Ordinances are made by the Syndicate subject to the Statutes.

Outlines the making of Regulations by the University, which shall provide for specific details not covered by Statutes or Ordinances, and are made by the Academic Council subject to the Statutes and Ordinances.
Provides for the procedure to fill up vacancies in the various authorities and bodies of the University.

main_sections.section_title: Proceedings of authorities not invalidated by vacancy, etc.
main_sections.description: States that the proceedings of any authority or body of the University shall not be invalidated by reason of any vacancy in its membership or by any defect in the election or appointment of any member thereof.
Grants the Government the power to make orders, not inconsistent with the provisions of the Act, for the purpose of removing any difficulty in relation to the commencement or operation of the Act.
Empowers the Government to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, and such rules shall be published in the Official Gazette and shall have effect as if enacted by the Act.

important_rules: University shall have a Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, Finance Officer, Controller of Examinations, and other officers as may be appointed.
The University shall have authorities namely the Senate, the Syndicate, the Academic Council, the Finance Committee and such other authorities as may be constituted.
The University shall consist of the colleges maintained by the University and such other colleges and institutions as may be admitted to its privileges.
The University shall have the power to confer degrees, diplomas and other academic distinctions.
The University shall be open to all persons irrespective of caste, creed, sex, race or religion.

rights: Right to establish and maintain colleges and institutions.
Right to affiliate colleges and institutions.
Right to conduct examinations and award degrees.
Right to enter into agreements with other universities and institutions.
Right to acquire, hold and dispose of property.
duties: Duty to promote and develop Malayalam language, literature and culture.
Duty to conduct research and disseminate knowledge.
Duty to provide for the advancement of higher education and research.
Duty to ensure the quality of education and research.
Duty to maintain academic and administrative efficiency.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the provisions of the Act and the Statutes.
Obligation to maintain financial discipline.
Obligation to ensure transparency in its functioning.
Obligation to serve the needs of the society.

key_procedures: Procedure for establishment and incorporation of the University.
Procedure for appointment of the Vice-Chancellor and other officers.
Procedure for the constitution and functioning of the University authorities.
Procedure for making Statutes, Ordinances and Regulations.
Procedure for admission of students and award of degrees.
Procedure for affiliation of colleges and institutions.
administration: The University shall be administered by the Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, Registrar and other officers, and the various authorities like the Senate, Syndicate and Academic Council.
important_notes: The Government has the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
The Government has the power to remove difficulties in the implementation of the Act.
The University's operations are subject to the oversight of the Government.

title: THE TIRUR MUNICIPAL COUNCIL (EXTENSION OF TERM OF OFFICE OF COUNCILLORS) ACT, 1979
purpose: To provide for the further extension of the term of office of the councillors of the Tirur Municipality.
scope: Applies to the Tirur Municipality and its councillors.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Tirur Municipal Council (Extension of Term of Office of Councillors) Act, 1979. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 30th day of November, 1978.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of term of office of municipal councillors.
main_sections.description: Notwithstanding anything contained in the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960 (14 of 1961), the term of office of the councillors of the Tirur Municipality constituted under the said Act, which expires on the 1st day of December, 1978, shall extend upto the 1st day of October, 1979.

The Tirur Municipal Council (Extension of Term of Office of Councillors) Ordinance, 1978 (29 of 1978), is hereby repealed. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: The term of office of the councillors of the Tirur Municipality, which was to expire on December 1, 1978, is extended to October 1, 1979.
Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are deemed to be taken under this Act.
important_notes: The Act was received the assent of the Governor on the 29th March, 1979 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 233, dated 29th March, 1979.
The Act is deemed to have come into force on November 30, 1978.

title: The Toddy Workers Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 1978
purpose: To amend the Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 1969, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to toddy workers in Kerala.

key_definitions.fund: Means the Kerala Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund established under the principal Act.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 1978 and it shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Act.
Amends section 1 of the principal Act by substituting 'Kerala Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund Act' for 'Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund Act'.
Amends section 2 of the principal Act, involving substitutions for 'a scheme' and 'fund'.
Amends section 3 of the principal Act, substituting 'Kerala Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund Scheme' for 'Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund Scheme'.
Amends section 5 of the principal Act, stating that the words 'either prospectively or retrospectively' shall be inserted at the end.
Amends section 6 of the principal Act, substituting 'Kerala Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund Board' for 'Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund Board'.

Inserts a new section 8A regarding Provisional assessment of contribution. It details how every employer shall, pending determination, pay an amount equivalent to one-twelfth of the amount annually payable in respect of his shop, according to the last determination under the said section. It also covers advance contributions and the recovery of arrears.

Amends section 9 of the principal Act, substituting 'together with interest thereon at the rate of nine per cent per annum' for 'together with interest thereon at the rate of nine per cent per annum'.

Amends section 14 of the principal Act, regarding punishments. It specifies that no court inferior to that of a Judicial Magistrate of the first class shall try any offence punishable under this Act. It also adds new clauses concerning cognizance of offences.

Inserts new sections 14A (Enhanced punishment for default in payment of employees' contributions) and 14B (Enhanced punishment for second or subsequent offence). Section 14A covers enhanced punishment for default in contribution payments, while 14B deals with repeat offences.

Inserts new sections 15A (Directions by Government), 15B (Power to order inquiry), and 15C (Power to supersede the Board). These sections grant the Government powers related to directions, inquiries, and supersession of the Board.
Omits section 16 of the Principal Act.

Inserts new section 17A concerning jurisdiction of civil courts. It states that no civil court shall have jurisdiction to settle, decide or deal with any question or to determine any matter which is by or under this Act required to be settled, decided or dealt with by the Government or the Board or the Chief Welfare Fund Inspector or any Welfare Fund Inspector.

Inserts new section 19, granting the Government power to make rules by notification in the Gazette for carrying into effect the provisions of this Act. It also specifies how rules made under this Act shall be laid before the Legislative Assembly.

Amends the Schedule to the Principal Act. It inserts new items relating to the payment by the employer of such sum of money as may be necessary to meet the cost of administering the fund and the rate at which and the manner in which such payment shall be made. It also introduces provisions for the rate of gratuity payable to members and conditions under which any amount due to the Board may be written off.

important_rules: Employers must pay contributions to the Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund.
The Government has the power to make rules for the Act and these rules must be laid before the Legislative Assembly.
The Board's decisions can be reviewed by the Government, and the Board can be superseded under certain conditions.

penalties: Offences punishable under section 14: The court trying any offence punishable under this Act, shall, if it finds the offender guilty, sentence him to a fine which may extend to two thousand rupees.
Enhanced punishment for default in payment of employees' contributions (section 14A): Fine may extend to four thousand rupees.
Enhanced punishment for second or subsequent offence (section 14B): Fine may extend to four thousand rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Judicial Magistrate of the first class (for trying offences), Government, Board, Chief Welfare Fund Inspector, Welfare Fund Inspector.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Prosecution for offences, levying of contributions, supersession of the Board, inquiries.

rights: Right to receive benefits from the Welfare Fund (implied).
Members of the fund are eligible for gratuity as per the amended schedule.
duties: Employers have a duty to pay contributions towards the Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund.
Employers must pay the amount annually payable in respect of their shops as per provisional assessment.
Contributions must be paid within a specified period.
obligations: Employers are obligated to pay their share of contributions and ensure their employees' contributions are paid.

key_procedures: Provisional assessment of contributions by employers.
Payment of contributions by employers within the specified time.
Submission of reports or information as required by the Board or Inspectors.
Procedures for superseding the Board, including issuing notification and reconstituting the Board.
Making and laying of rules before the Legislative Assembly.
administration: The Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund Board, overseen by the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Toddy Workers' Welfare Fund Act, 1969.
Certain amendments are retrospective.
No civil court shall have jurisdiction to decide matters that are required to be settled by the Government, Board, or Inspectors.
Rules made under the Act are subject to modification by the Legislative Assembly without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done.

title: The Town Planning Laws (Amendment) Act, 1986
purpose: To further amend the Town Planning Act (IV of 1108) and the Madras Town Planning Act, 1920 (Madras Act VII of 1920).
scope: Applies to amendments made to the Town Planning Act (IV of 1108) and the Madras Town Planning Act, 1920. The amendments themselves are likely to apply to areas covered by these original acts within Kerala.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as "The Town Planning Laws (Amendment) Act, 1986" and specifies that it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 7th day of October, 1985.

Substitutes sections for section 53B in the Town Planning Act (IV of 1108). This section details the composition of a Development Authority, including the Chairman, General Council, and Executive Committee, and their appointment and tenure.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Madras Act VII of 1920
main_sections.description: Substitutes sections for section 54B in the Madras Town Planning Act, 1920. Similar to section 2, this amendment also deals with the composition of a Development Authority, its General Council, and Executive Committee, including appointment and tenure.

Repeals The Town Planning Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1986. It also states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the Town Planning Act (IV of 1108) or the Madras Town Planning Act, 1920 (Madras Act VII of 1920), as amended by the said Ordinance, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the Town Planning Act (IV of 1108) or, as the case may be, the Madras Town Planning Act, 1920 (Madras Act VII of 1920), as amended by this Act.

important_rules: The Act is deemed to have come into force on October 7, 1985.
The composition of the Development Authority includes a Chairman, General Council, and Executive Committee.
The Government appoints the Chairman of the Development Authority.
The General Council may include representatives of transport undertakings or corporations, and members nominated by the Government from among local authorities.
The Government fixes the strength of the General Council and the Executive Committee, with specific minimum and maximum numbers of members and exclusions.
The term of office for nominated members of the Executive Committee and the Development Authority is not exceeding three years, unless fixed by the Government.
Members of the Executive Committee and General Council can cease to be members under certain conditions.
The Government has the power to prescribe functions and powers of the General Council and Executive Committee.
Certain words in section 53E, 53F, and 54H of the respective Acts are substituted.
The Town Planning Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1986, is repealed.
key_procedures: Amendment of section 53B of Act IV of 1108 regarding the composition of the Development Authority.
Amendment of section 54B of Madras Act VII of 1920 regarding the composition of the Development Authority.
Substitution of specific words in sections 53E, 53F, and 54H of the respective Acts.
Repeal of the Town Planning Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1986.
administration: Law (Legislation-C) Department, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The amendments to Act IV of 1108 and Madras Act VII of 1920 are made for the purposes stated in the Preamble.
The Act is published by order of the Governor.
The repeal of the Ordinance does not affect actions taken under it, which are now considered to have been taken under the amended Acts.

title: The Town Planning Laws (Amendment) Act, 1968
purpose: To further amend the Town Planning Act, 1108 and to amend the Madras Town Planning Act, 1920.
scope: Applies to town planning matters within Kerala, specifically amending existing Acts related to town planning.

key_definitions.Council or municipal council: Means the council of a municipal corporation or of a municipality.
key_definitions.Municipality: Means any city as defined in the Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, 1961 (30 of 1961) and any local area in which the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960 (14 of 1961) is in force.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Town Planning Laws (Amendment) Act, 1968, and it shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 2 of the Town Planning Act (Act IV of 1108)
main_sections.description: Amends section 2 of the Town Planning Act, 1108 by substituting specific clauses for 'Council' or 'municipal council' and 'municipality'.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 45 of the Town Planning Act
main_sections.description: Substitutes a new section 45 concerning the Constitution of Trusts, outlining the appointment of a chairman, elected members, persons appointed by the Government, and executive trustees. It also specifies the number of trustees, their election and nomination, and the term of office. Provisions for Government notification to terminate or reduce office tenure are included.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new section 45-A in the Town Planning Act
main_sections.description: Inserts a new section 45-A regarding the Appointment of Executive Trustee, stating that the Government shall appoint any person to be the full-time executive trustee of the trust, who shall exercise specified powers and perform duties.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 46 of the Town Planning Act
main_sections.description: Amends section 46 of the Town Planning Act by substituting the words 'chairman' and 'executive trustee'.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 2 of the Madras Town Planning Act VII of 1920
main_sections.description: Amends section 2 of the Madras Town Planning Act, 1920, by substituting clauses for 'Council' or 'municipal council' and 'Municipality'.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 46 of the Madras Town Planning Act
main_sections.description: Substitutes a new section 46 for section 45 of the Madras Town Planning Act, also concerning the Constitution of Trusts, with similar provisions to section 3 of the Town Planning Act.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new section 46-A in the Madras Town Planning Act
main_sections.description: Inserts a new section 46-A in the Madras Town Planning Act, concerning the Appointment of Executive Trustee, similar to section 45-A.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 47 of the Madras Town Planning Act
main_sections.description: Amends section 47 of the Madras Town Planning Act by substituting the words 'chairman' and 'executive trustee'.

Repeals the Town Planning Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1968. It also states that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act as if it had come into force on the 8th day of August, 1968.

important_rules: A trust referred to in section 44 shall consist of a chairman appointed by the Government, elected members, persons appointed by the Government, and an executive trustee.
The Government shall fix the strength of the trust, which shall not be less than seven and not more than fifteen.
Trustees shall be elected, nominated, or appointed by the Government.
The Government may appoint the special officer exercising the powers of the municipal council to be a trustee.
Each trustee shall hold office for a period of five years.
The executive trustee shall exercise such powers and perform such duties as may be prescribed.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be the authorities responsible for town planning and municipal administration.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the implementation of the amended provisions of the Town Planning Act and the Madras Town Planning Act.

rights: Right to be appointed as trustee (subject to qualifications and appointment process).
Right to hold office for a period of five years (for trustees).
duties: Executive trustee to exercise powers and perform duties as prescribed.
Trustees to act in accordance with the provisions of the Act.

key_procedures: Appointment of trustees (chairman, elected, nominated, executive trustee).
Election and nomination of trustees.
Government notification for termination or reduction of tenure of trustees.
Replacement of repealed Ordinance with the Act.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but likely falls under the purview of the State Government's departments responsible for town planning and local administration.
important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 228, dated 18th September, 1968.
The amendments are effective from the 8th day of August, 1968, due to the saving clause for the repealed Ordinance.

title: The Town Planning Laws (Amendment) Act, 1976
purpose: To further amend the Town Planning Act (IV of 1108) and the Madras Town Planning Act, 1920 (Madras Act VII of 1920).
scope: Applies to town planning matters and involves the creation and functioning of development authorities. Specifically amends existing acts related to town planning in Kerala.

key_definitions.development authority: A special authority constituted by the Government by notification, in any area, for the purpose of carrying out the provisions of this Act.
key_definitions.chairman: Refers to the Chairman of the development authority.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Town Planning Laws (Amendment) Act, 1976.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new Chapter IX-A in Act IV of 1108.
main_sections.description: Provides for the insertion of a new Chapter IX-A into the Town Planning Act (IV of 1108), which will cover Development Authorities.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new Chapter IX-A in Madras Act VII of 1920
main_sections.description: Provides for the insertion of a new Chapter IX-A into the Madras Town Planning Act, 1920, as in force in the Malabar district, which will cover Development Authorities.
Concerns the repeal and saving provisions related to the amendments.

Outlines the process by which the Government can constitute a special authority, known as a Development Authority, for specific areas to manage town planning interests. It also details the legal status of the authority as a body corporate.

Specifies the composition of a development authority, including the appointment of a Chairman and other members nominated by the Government, elected by local authorities, or from specific organizations.
Details the appointment of a Secretary for the development authority, who must be an officer of a certain rank and will exercise prescribed powers and perform delegated duties.
Grants development authorities the power to borrow money through loans and debentures, subject to government approval. It also mandates the maintenance of a sinking fund for loan repayment.

main_sections.section_title: Application of Act to development authorities.
main_sections.description: Clarifies that when a development authority has been constituted, certain provisions of the Act will apply, and specific terms like 'municipal council' and 'chairman of the council' will be substituted with 'development authority' and 'chairman of the development authority' respectively.

main_sections.section_title: Application of certain provisions to development authority.
main_sections.description: Indicates that specific sections of the Act will apply to development authorities, with necessary substitutions for terms like 'development authority', 'chairman of the development authority', 'secretary of the development authority', 'trust', 'chairman of the trust', and 'member of the development authority'.
Empowers development authorities to purchase land for town planning schemes, with the value of the land not exceeding the value fixed by the District Collector.
Allows the development authority to delegate its powers to the Chairman or other officers of the authority, with the previous sanction of the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Transfer of staff, assets and liabilities to development authority.
main_sections.description: Deals with the transfer of officers, staff, assets, and liabilities from trusts or other entities to development authorities, ensuring continuity of employment and rights.
Similar to section 53A, this section outlines the creation of development authorities by the Government for specific areas to implement town planning provisions.
Similar to section 53B, this section defines the composition of a development authority, including a Chairman appointed by the Government and other members elected or nominated.
Similar to section 53C, this section covers the appointment of the Secretary of the development authority and the conditions of service.
Similar to section 53D, this section grants development authorities the power to borrow money and requires the maintenance of a sinking fund.

main_sections.section_title: Application of Act to development authorities.
main_sections.description: Similar to section 53E, this section details the application of the Act to development authorities, including substitutions of terms.

main_sections.section_title: Application of certain provisions to development authority.
main_sections.description: Similar to section 53F, this section specifies the application of certain provisions to development authorities with necessary substitutions.
Similar to section 53G, this section grants development authorities the power to purchase land for town planning schemes.

important_rules: The Government can constitute a special authority by notification to be called a Development Authority for managing town planning interests in an area.
A development authority is a body corporate with perpetual succession and a common seal, capable of acquiring, holding, and disposing of property, and suing and being sued.
The number of members of a development authority shall not be less than eleven or more than twenty-eight.

A member of a development authority holds office for a term of five years from the date of appointment, election, or nomination, unless they cease to be a member of the local authority or body they represented.
Development authorities can borrow money through loans and debentures, subject to Government approval.
Development authorities must maintain a sinking fund for loan repayment.
Development authorities have the power to purchase land for town planning schemes.
Development authorities can delegate powers to the Chairman or other officers with Government sanction.
Officers, staff, assets, and liabilities can be transferred to development authorities from existing trusts or bodies.

rights: Right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property (for Development Authority).
Right to borrow money (for Development Authority).
Right to purchase land (for Development Authority).
duties: Duty to carry out provisions of the Act (for Development Authority).
Duty to maintain a sinking fund (for Development Authority).
Duty to ensure continuity of employment and rights for transferred staff (implied).
obligations: Obligation to obtain Government sanction for delegation of powers (Development Authority).

key_procedures: Constitution of a development authority by Government notification.
Appointment of Chairman and members of the development authority.
Appointment of the Secretary of the development authority.
Borrowing money by the development authority.
Purchase of land by the development authority.
Delegation of powers by the development authority.
administration: The Government and specifically established Development Authorities.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the President on the 25th day of March, 1976 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 195, dated 25th March 1976.
Certain sections are applied with substitutions of terms to reflect the establishment of development authorities.

title: THE TRAVANCORE-COCHIN NURSES AND MIDWIVES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1960
purpose: To amend the Travancore-Cochin Nurses and Midwives Act, 1953, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Travancore-Cochin region and concerns the regulation of nurses and midwives.

key_definitions.register: Means the register of nurses or the register of midwives or the register of dhais maintained under this Act, and "registered" means registered or deemed to be registered under this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Nurses and Midwives (Amendment) Act, 1960, and it came into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Amends the preamble of the Travancore-Cochin Nurses and Midwives Act, 1953, by excluding the Malabar district and its relevant provisions.
Amends section 1 of the principal Act. In sub-section (1), 'Nurses and Midwives Act' shall be substituted. In sub-section (2), it extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.

Amends section 2 of the principal Act. In clause (f), 'Kerala Nurses and Midwives Council' shall be substituted. In clause (f), 'register' means the register of nurses or the register of midwives or the register of dhais maintained under this Act, and 'registered' means registered or deemed to be registered under this Act. In clause (g), for the words 'registered in the register of practitioners or the word "registered" or deemed to be registered in the register of practitioners', shall be substituted.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 3.
main_sections.description: Substitutes section 3 of the principal Act. The section states that the Government shall, by notification in the Gazette, establish a Council to be called the Kerala Nurses and Midwives Council. The Council shall consist of the following members: (a) the Director of Health Services, the Professor of Gynaecology, Medical College, Trivandrum, the Professor of Gynaecology, Medical College, Kozhikode, the Superintendent, Women and Children's Hospital, Trivandrum and the Superintendent, Women and Children's Hospital Kozhikode, to be ex officio members; (b) one member elected by the members of the Medical Council from among themselves; (c) three registered nurses nominated by the Government, two of whom shall be Superintendents of nursing schools and the third shall be the Matron-Superintendent of a Major Hospital; (d) five members elected by the registered nurses from among the midwives registered in Part A of the register of nurses; (e) three members elected by the registered midwives from among the midwives registered in Part A of the register of midwives.

In section 5 of the principal Act, for the words "in the case of the first Council established under this Act", the words, brackets and figures "in the case of the first Council established after the commencement of the Travancore-Cochin Nurses and Midwives (Amendment) Act, 1960," shall be substituted.

In section 6 of the principal Act, after clause (a), the following clause shall be inserted namely:-"(aa) if he is not a resident of the State of Kerala;". This amendment is applicable if the person is not a resident of Kerala.

In sub-section (1) of section 7 of the principal Act, in clause (a), for the words "the first Council", the words, brackets and figures "the first Council established after the commencement of the Travancore-Cochin Nurses and Midwives (Amendment) Act, 1960," shall be substituted.

In section 8 of the principal Act, for the first sentence, the following sentence shall be substituted, namely:- "Vacancies in the office of the elected or nominated members of the Council shall be filled by election or nomination, as the case may be."
In section 9 (5) of the principal Act, for the words "Surgeon General", the words "Director of Health Services" shall be substituted.

In section 11 of the principal Act, for clause (a), the following clause shall be substituted, namely:-"(a) subject to the provisions of sub-section (2) of section 7, on the expiry of the term of office."

In section 18 of the principal Act, after sub-section (2), the following sub-section shall be inserted namely:-" (2-A) The Government shall, cause to be prepared a separate register of dhies registered under the Madras Nurses and Midwives Act, 1926, and holding appointments or practising in the Malabar district, referred to in sub-section (2) of section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (Central Act 37 of 1956), in such form and containing such particulars as may be prescribed."

In section 25 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), for the words "nurses and midwives", the words "nurses, midwives and dhai" shall be substituted. In sub-section (2), for the words "nurses and midwives", the words "nurses, midwives and dhai" shall be substituted. In sub-section (3), after the words "registered midwife" in both places where they occur, the words "or registered dhai" shall be inserted.
In sub-section (1) of section 28 of the principal Act, for the words "nurses and midwives", the words "nurses, midwives and dhai" shall be substituted.

In section 29 of the principal Act, after sub-section (2), the following sub-section shall be added, namely:-"(3) Every nurse or midwife deemed to be registered under sub-section (1) of section 40-A and every dhai entitled to practise under the provisions of this Act shall give notice of any change of address to the local supervising authority within whose jurisdiction he is practising."
In section 30 of the principal Act, for the words "nurse or midwife" in both places where they occur, the words "nurse, midwife or dhai" shall be substituted.
In sub-section (1) of section 32 of the principal Act, for the words "nurse or midwife" in both places where they occur, the words "nurse, midwife or dhai" shall be substituted.
In sub-section (1) of section 33 of the principal Act, for the words "nurse or midwife" wherever they occur, the words "registered nurse, midwife or dhai" shall be substituted.
In section 34 of the principal Act, for the words "nurse or midwife" the words "nurse, midwife or dhai" shall be substituted.
In section 35 of the principal Act, in clause (k) of sub-section (2), for the words "nurses and midwives", the words "nurses, midwives and dhai" shall be substituted.

Section 40-A of the principal Act, shall be renumbered as sub-section (1) of that section and after sub-section (1) as renumbered the following sub-section shall be added namely:-"(2) The Registrar shall, on application and on production of evidence, enter the names of nurses and midwives, who are deemed to be registered under sub-section (1), in the appropriate register. No fee shall be charged on such application."

Section 41 of the principal Act shall be renumbered as sub-section (1) of that section and after sub-section (1) as so renumbered the following sub-section shall be added, namely:-" (2) The Madras Nurses and Midwives Act, 1926 (Madras Act III of 1926), as in force in the Malabar district referred to in sub-section (2) of section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, is hereby repealed."

rights: Right to be registered as a nurse or midwife.
duties: Duty to give notice of change of address to the local supervising authority.
obligations: Obligation to practice within the scope of registration.

key_procedures: Establishment of the Kerala Nurses and Midwives Council by the Government through a notification in the Gazette.
Filling of vacancies in the Council through election or nomination.
Preparation and maintenance of a separate register of dhies registered under the Madras Nurses and Midwives Act, 1926.
Application for registration of nurses and midwives with the Registrar, requiring evidence and entry into the appropriate register.
Giving notice of change of address by registered nurses, midwives, and dhai to the local supervising authority.
administration: The Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act commenced on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
The amendment excludes the Malabar district from certain provisions of the original Act.
The Act repeals the Madras Nurses and Midwives Act, 1926, as in force in the Malabar district.
No fee is charged for the application to enter names in the appropriate register.

title: The Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions (Third Amendment) Act, 1990
purpose: To further amend the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: The Act applies to the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions.

key_definitions.Hindu: means a person who is a Hindu by birth or by conversion into Hinduism or who professes the Hindu Religion-whether or not such person believes in God and temple worship.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions (Third Amendment) Act, 1990. The provisions of sections 2 and 3 shall be deemed to have come into force on the 4th day of March, 1989 and the remaining provisions shall come into force at once and any reference in any such provision to the commencement of this Act shall be construed as a reference to the coming into force of that provision.

In section 2 of the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950 (XV of 1950) (hereinafter referred to as the principal Act), after clause (a), the following clause shall be inserted, namely- '(aa) "Hindu" means a person who is a Hindu by birth or by conversion into Hinduism or who professes the Hindu Religion-whether or not such person believes in God and temple worship. Provided that a Hindu member to be nominated or elected to the Board under section 4 shall be a person who believes in God and temple worship and who shall make an oath before the Secretary of the Board to that effect in the form prescribed by the Government for the purpose before he enters upon his office'.
In section 6 of the principal Act, for the words "professes the Hindu religion" the words "is a Hindu" shall be substituted.
In sub-section (1) of section 8 of the principal Act, for the words "ceases to profess the Hindu Religion" the word "ceases to be a Hindu" shall be substituted.
Sub-section (3) of section 10 shall be omitted.

After section 13 of the principal Act the following section shall be inserted, namely - "13A. Appointment of Chief Commissioner. In the event of all the members of the Board's ceasing to hold office as such, the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint an officer not below the rank of a member of the Board of Revenue, and who is a Hindu as the Chief Commissioner to exercise such powers and perform such duties of the Board as may be specified in the notification till the new members assume office."
In sub-section (2) of section 29 of the principal Act, for the words "person professing the Hindu religion" the word "Hindu" shall be substituted.

Notwithstanding anything contained in any judgement, decree or order of any Court anything done or any action taken in connection with the nomination or election as a member of the Travancore Devaswom Board before the commencement of this Act shall not be invalid or shall be deemed ever to have been invalid for any person whatsoever and such nomination made or election conducted to the Travancore Devaswom Board before the commencement of this Act shall be valid and shall be deemed always to have been valid for all purposes as if the nomination was made and the election was conducted in accordance with the provisions of the principal Act as amended by this Act and no suit or other legal proceedings shall be maintained or continued in any Court challenging the validity of such nomination or election.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Appointment of Chief Commissioner in certain circumstances.

key_procedures: Nomination or election of a Hindu member to the Board requires the member to believe in God and temple worship and to take an oath.
If all members of the Board cease to hold office, the Government may appoint a Chief Commissioner to exercise the Board's powers and duties until new members are appointed.
administration: Travancore Devaswom Board (implied)
important_notes: The commencement of sections 2 and 3 is retrospective to March 4, 1989.
Section 5 omits sub-section (3) of section 10.
Section 8 declares that any nomination or election to the Travancore Devaswom Board prior to the Act's commencement is valid, irrespective of any court judgment or legal proceedings.

title: The Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions (Amendment) Act, 1990
purpose: To further amend the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950, for the purposes appearing therein.
scope: Applies to the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions (Amendment) Act, 1990. It shall come into force at once.

After section 62 of the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950 (XV of 1950), the following sections shall be inserted, namely:

"62A Devaswom Properties-All immovable properties vested in the Cochin Devaswom Board under sub-section (1) of section 62 shall be dealt with as Devaswom properties. The provisions of the Kerala Land Conservancy Act, 1957 (8 of 1958) shall be applicable to Devaswom lands as in the case of Government lands.

62B Applicability of Kerala Land Conservancy Act to unassigned lands of Devaswoms under the Board-All unassigned lands belonging to the Devaswom under the sole management of the Board shall be deemed to be the property of the Government for the purpose of the Kerala Land Conservancy Act, 1957 (8 of 1958) and all the provisions of that Act shall, so far as they are applicable, apply to such lands."

rights: Properties vested in the Cochin Devaswom Board are to be dealt with as Devaswom properties.
Unassigned lands belonging to the Devaswom under the Board's sole management are deemed Government property for the purpose of the Kerala Land Conservancy Act.

important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 21st day of April 1990 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 421 dated the 23rd April 1990.

title: THE TRAVANCORE-COCHIN HINDU RELIGIOUS INSTITUTIONS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1994
purpose: To amend the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950.
scope: Applies to Hindu religious institutions within the former Travancore-Cochin region and the State of Kerala, particularly concerning the definition of 'Hindu' and nomination procedures.

key_definitions.Hindu: A person who is a Hindu by birth or by conversion into Hindu religion and professes Hindu religion and believes in God and temple worship.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions (Amendment) Act, 1994, and it came into force on the 4th day of October, 1993.
Amends section 2 of the principal Act by inserting a definition for 'Hindu'.
Amends section 4 of the principal Act by inserting a new sub-section (1A) regarding the nomination of a Hindu.
Amends section 5 of the principal Act by adding a provision related to Hindu members of the Legislative Assembly.
Amends section 61 of the principal Act by substituting the opening paragraph of clause (4A) with a new definition of 'Hindu'.
Amends section 63 of the principal Act by adding a proviso regarding the nomination and declaration by members of the Council of Ministers.
Amends section 64 of the principal Act by adding a clause concerning Hindu members of the Legislative Assembly.
Amends Schedule II of the principal Act by substituting words in rule 3 regarding the definition of a Hindu.

Repeals the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions (Amendment) Ordinance, 1993 (3 of 1993) and states that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Every Hindu member of the Legislative Assembly of the State of Kerala intending to participate in an election shall, before participating, deliver to the person who presides over the meeting, a declaration signed by him to the effect that he professes the Hindu religion and believes in God and temple worship.

Each of the Hindus among the Council of Ministers, before making a nomination, shall deliver to the authority specified by the Government a declaration signed by him to the effect that he professes the Hindu religion and believes in God and temple worship.

rights: Right of Hindu members of the Legislative Assembly to participate in elections after fulfilling declaration requirements.
Right of Hindus among the Council of Ministers to make nominations after fulfilling declaration requirements.
duties: Duty to declare oneself as professing the Hindu religion and believing in God and temple worship for participating in elections.
Duty to declare oneself as professing the Hindu religion and believing in God and temple worship for making nominations by Council of Ministers.

key_procedures: Procedure for Hindu members of the Legislative Assembly to participate in elections: deliver a declaration signed by them to the presiding person.
Procedure for nominations by Hindus among the Council of Ministers: deliver a declaration signed by them to the specified authority.
administration: The administration would likely fall under the purview of the department responsible for religious endowments or endowments within the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 2nd day of March, 1994 and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 172, dated the 2nd March 1994.
The Act is deemed to have come into force on the 4th day of October, 1993.
The repeal of the Ordinance does not affect actions taken under it, which are considered valid under the amended Act.

title: The Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions (Amendment) Act, 1999
purpose: To amend the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950, for the purposes specified therein.
scope: Applies to Hindu religious institutions in the Travancore-Cochin region.

key_definitions.Hindu: Means a person who is a Hindu by birth or by conversion and professes the Hindu religion.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called The Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions (Amendment) Act, 1999 and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 15th day of December, 1998.
Amends Section 2 of the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950, by substituting the definition of 'Hindu'.
Amends Section 4 by amending sub-section (1A) of the principal Act.

Amends Section 5 by omitting certain words from the principal Act. It specifically redefines the eligibility criteria for members of the Legislative Assembly to participate in the election of those who preside over religious meetings, requiring them to profess the Hindu religion and believe in God and temple worship.
Amends Section 61 by substituting the opening paragraph with a new definition of 'Hindu'.
Amends Section 63 by omitting the proviso to section 63 of the principal Act.

Amends Section 64 by omitting certain words from the principal Act. It redefines the eligibility criteria for members of the Legislative Assembly to participate in the election of those who preside over religious meetings, requiring them to profess the Hindu religion and believe in God and temple worship.

Repeals The Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions (Amendment) Ordinance, 1998 (18 of 1998) and states that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Members of the Legislative Assembly who intend to participate in the election of persons presiding over religious meetings must profess the Hindu religion and believe in God and temple worship.
Rule 2: The definition of 'Hindu' includes those who are Hindu by birth or by conversion and profess the Hindu religion.

rights: Right of eligible Hindu individuals to participate in the election of those who preside over religious meetings, under specific conditions.
obligations: Obligation for elected officials presiding over religious meetings to profess the Hindu religion and believe in God and temple worship.

key_procedures: Procedure: Amendment of specific sections of the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950, including definitions, election of presiding officials, and repealing previous ordinances.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but likely falls under the purview of the department responsible for religious endowments in Kerala.
important_notes: The Act has retrospective effect from December 15, 1998.
The Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions (Amendment) Ordinance, 1998, is repealed.
Actions taken under the repealed ordinance remain valid if they align with the amended Act.

title: The Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions (Second Amendment) Act, 1990
purpose: To further amend the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950.
scope: Applies to the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions (Second Amendment) Act, 1990 and that it shall come into force at once.

Amends section 12 of the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950 by substituting the figures "Rs. 450" and "Rs. 400" with "Rs. 1500" and "Rs. 1250" respectively for letters and figures.
Amends section 71 of the principal Act, in sub-section (2), by substituting the figures "Rs. 300" and "Rs. 250" with "Rs. 1500" and "Rs. 1250" respectively for letters and figures.

important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 21st day of April, 1990 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 422 dated the 23rd April, 1990.

title: THE TRAVANCORE - COCHIN HINDU RELIGIOUS INSTITUTIONS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2007 (ACT 5 OF 2007)
purpose: To further amend the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950.
scope: Applies to the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions.

key_definitions.Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe: Shall have the same meaning as is assigned to it in clause (24) and (25) respectively of Article 366 of the Constitution of India.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions (Amendment) Act, 2007. All sections of this Act, except section 13 and section 31, shall be deemed to have come into force on the 5th day of February, 2007. Section 13 and section 31 shall come into force on such date as the Government may appoint, by notification in the Gazette.

Amends Section 2 of the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950, substituting a proviso to the existing proviso regarding nomination of a Hindu member elected or nominated to the Board and the oath of office.

Amends Section 6 of the principal Act by substituting the words 'has attained thirty five years of age' with 'has attained the age of fifty years in the case of a male member' and 'has attained the age of sixty years' in the case of a female member.

Inserts new Sections 15A and 15B. Section 15A defines the duties of the Board, including ensuring regular rituals, monitoring officials, and maintaining proper facilities. Section 15B deals with the constitution and functions of Standing Committees of the Board.

Inserts new Section 29A which states that appointments to certain positions shall be made through the Kerala Public Service Commission, following recruitment and conditions of service rules for officers and employees of the Devaswom Administrative Service.

Inserts new Section 31A titled 'Formation of Temple Advisory Committees', stating that a committee may be constituted in each temple to ensure participation of Hindu devotees, and such committees may be approved by the Board.
Amends Section 63 of the principal Act, concerning the Constitution of the Cochin Devaswom Board, by substituting provisions related to the members of the Board.
Amends Section 65 of the principal Act, similar to the amendment in Section 6, by modifying the age requirements for members.
Amends Section 67 of the principal Act, with provisions for insertion and substitution of clauses related to cessation of membership and restoration of membership.
Amends Section 71 of the principal Act, regarding letters and figures for amounts, substituting 'Rs 1500' and 'Rs 1250' with 'Rupees five thousand only' and 'Rupees three thousand five hundred only'.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new section after section 73
main_sections.description: Inserts a new section after Section 73, stating that the Secretary shall be the Convener of the Board and Standing Committees and also responsible for proper functioning of day-to-day affairs.

main_sections.section_title: Special provisions relating to the existing members of the Travancore Devaswom Board and Cochin Devaswom Board.
main_sections.description: This section pertains to special provisions for existing members of the Travancore Devaswom Board and Cochin Devaswom Board.
Deals with the repeal of certain provisions and saving clauses.

important_rules: Members of the Board must take an oath before the Principal Secretary to the Government of Kerala, Department of Devaswom, professing Hindu religious rites and being a believer of God and temple worship.
Appointments to certain positions shall be made through the Kerala Public Service Commission.
Temple Advisory Committees are to be constituted to ensure participation of Hindu devotees.
The Board shall constitute Standing Committees for Finance and Resource Mobilisation, Works, Development and Environment, and Establishment, Temple Arts and Devotional Services.
The Standing Committees shall meet at least once in a month.

penalties: Fines not less than Rupees Two thousand five hundred for matters involving economic offences.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be the Board, Devaswom Commissioner, and potentially the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the Act and the powers vested in the Board and its committees.

rights: Right of existing members of the Travancore and Cochin Devaswom Boards to special provisions.
Right to form Temple Advisory Committees.
duties: Duty of the Board to ensure regular rituals and ceremonies.
Duty to monitor administrative officials and employees.
Duty to ensure proper maintenance and upliftment of Hindu religious institutions.
Duty of the Secretary to convene meetings and manage day-to-day affairs.
Duty of the Board to manage Devaswom properties.
Duty of Standing Committees to perform their assigned functions.
obligations: Members must take an oath of office.
Appointments are subject to Kerala Public Service Commission regulations.

key_procedures: Constitution of the Board with a Hindu member nominated or elected and taking an oath.
Formation of Temple Advisory Committees by the Board.
Constitution of Standing Committees by the Board and their meetings.
Reporting by the Devaswom Commissioner to the Government.
Appointments made through Kerala Public Service Commission.
Audit report submission within two months from the end of the financial year.
Appointment of a Commission by the Government to inquire into irregularities, corruption, maladministration or misappropriation of funds.
administration: Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions and Devaswom Department/Board.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on 11th April, 2007, and was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 694 dated 12th April, 2007.
Certain sections came into force on 5th February, 2007, while others would come into force on a date appointed by the Government.
The provisions related to the 'Scheduled Caste' and 'Scheduled Tribe' have the same meaning as assigned in the Constitution of India.
Restoration of membership to the Board, if satisfied that there was reasonable and sufficient grounds for not attending meetings, shall not be allowed more than once.

title: THE TRAVANCORE-COCHIN HINDU RELIGIOUS INSTITUTIONS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1995
purpose: An Act to further amend the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950. WHEREAS it is expedient further to amend the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950 for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions (Amendment) Act, 1995, and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 2nd day of March, 1995.

Amends sub-section (2) of section 122 of the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950 (Act XV of 1950) by adding clause (f) regarding the grant of travelling and halting allowances to the members of the Board and the officers of the Board.

Repeals the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions (Amendment) Ordinance, 1995 (7 of 1995). It also states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be the authorities under the principal Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the provisions of the amended Act.

administration: Not explicitly mentioned.
important_notes: The Act was received the assent of the Governor on the 5th day of August 1995, and published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 791, dated 5th August 1995.

title: The Travancore Chitties (Amendment) Act, 1964
purpose: To amend the Travancore Chitties Act, 1120, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: This act applies to Chitties governed by The Travancore Chitties Act, 1120, and specifically amends Section 13 of the said Act.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore Chitties (Amendment) Act, 1964.

For sub-section (1) of section 13 of the Travancore Chitties Act, 1120 (Act XXVI of 1120), the following sub-section shall be substituted, namely: "(1) Subject to the provisions of this Act and to the conditions contained in the variola, the subscribers of a chitty may, by special resolution,- (a) alter or add to the articles in the variola in respect of all or any of the following matters, namely:— (i) the time at which or the place where the chitty is to be conducted, (ii) the reduction of the chitty amount; (iii) the continuance of the chitty in accordance with the provisions of section 38; (iv) the suspension or prolongation of the chitty; (v) the termination of the chitty; (b) omit the name of any approved bank specified in the variola or add the name of any approved bank in the variola; (c) alter or substitute any of the articles of the variola that may be found to be not in consonance with any of the provisions of this Act or the rules made thereunder. Any such alteration, addition, or substitution shall be as valid if originally contained in the variola and shall be subject, in like manner, to alteration, addition or substitution by a special resolution".

important_rules: Subscribers of a chitty may, by special resolution, alter or add to the articles in the variola regarding the time/place of conduct, reduction of chitty amount, continuance, suspension/prolongation, or termination of the chitty.
Subscribers may, by special resolution, omit or add an approved bank specified in the variola.
Subscribers may, by special resolution, alter or substitute articles in the variola that are not in consonance with the Act or rules.
Any alteration, addition, or substitution made by special resolution is valid and subject to further alteration, addition, or substitution by a special resolution.

rights: Right of subscribers to alter or add to variola articles by special resolution.
Right to omit or add an approved bank by special resolution.
Right to alter or substitute variola articles by special resolution.

key_procedures: Alteration, addition, or substitution of variola articles requires a special resolution by the subscribers of a chitty.
Such changes must be in accordance with the provisions of the Act and rules.
important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 23rd March, 1964.
Received the assent of the President on the 19th day of March, 1964.
For Statement of Objects and Reasons—See Gazette Extraordinary dated 20th August, 1963.

title: The Travancore-Cochin Prevention of Eviction of Kudikidappukars Act
purpose: To make provision for the prevention of eviction of Kudikidappukars except under certain special circumstances.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin. It applies to Kudikidappukaran who is in occupation of a Kudiyiruppu. The Act is not applicable to certain lands etc. and certain suits related to Kudiyiruppu.

key_definitions.eviction: Means the recovery of possession of a Kudiyiruppu from a Kudikidappukaran.
key_definitions.holding: Means a block of land held by a person whether as owner, mortgagee, lessee or otherwise on any portion of which there is a Kudiyiruppu.
key_definitions.Kudikidappukaran: Means a person who has no homestead or land of his own to erect a homestead and has been permitted by an owner of land to have the use and occupation of a portion of the land for the purpose of creating a homestead with or without an obligation to pay rent for the use and occupation of the site so given; and 'Kudiyiruppu' means the site so given together with the house, hut or shed thereon which is used as a place of residence by the Kudikidappukaran with the permission of the owner.
key_definitions.landholder: Means a person who is entitled to be and is in possession and enjoyment of a parcel of land or holding and is in possession and enjoyment of a parcel of land or holding whether as owner, mortgagee, lessee, or otherwise.
key_definitions.owner: Means a person who is entitled to the absolute proprietorship of land and includes in the case of land in which superintendence has been assumed by the Court or the Cochin Court of Wards Act, XIII of 1097, the Collector or Tahsildar, as the case may be.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by Rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Prevention of Eviction of Kudikidappukars Act, 1955. It extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'eviction', 'holding', 'Kudikidappukaran', 'landholder', 'owner', and 'prescribed'.

main_sections.section_title: Act not applicable to certain lands etc.
main_sections.description: Specifies that this Act shall not apply to lands in the possession of the Government or lands administered by the Administrator General, Official Receiver or any officer appointed by a court under the provisions of any law, or lands for any housing or land improvement purposes, or lands or buildings rented out including houses, shops, ware-houses, etc., or lands or buildings rented out for industrial or commercial purposes.

main_sections.section_title: Kudikidappukaran to have permanent right of occupancy in Kudiyiruppu.
main_sections.description: States that every Kudikidappukaran who is at the date of commencement of this Act in occupation of a Kudiyiruppu to which this Act applies, or who may thereafter be permitted by an owner or any other land-holder with the owner's consent to be in occupation of a Kudiyiruppu to which this Act applies, shall have a permanent right of occupancy in such Kudiyiruppu.

main_sections.section_title: No merger of the right of Kudiyiruppu.
main_sections.description: A person who has under the Act a right of occupancy in a Kudiyiruppu shall continue to retain that right even after he becomes entitled to the possession of the whole property of which the Kudiyiruppu forms a portion either as mortgagee or lessee.

main_sections.section_title: Kudikidappukaran's interest heritable, but not alienable.
main_sections.description: The interest of a Kudikidappukaran in his Kudiyiruppu shall be heritable but not alienable.
