main_sections.section_title: Kudikidappukaran not liable to be evicted except on certain grounds.
main_sections.description: No Kudikidappukaran shall be evicted from his Kudiyiruppu except in execution of a decree for eviction which may be passed him on any of the following grounds: (1) that the owner requires the land for bona fide building purposes for himself or for any member of his family or tarwad or thavazhi and the site is necessary for the convenient occupation of the building to be constructed. Explanation: The wife or husband and the children and grand-children of the owner shall be deemed to be members of the owner's family. (2) that he has alienated his right to the Kudiyiruppu to another person; (c) that he has rented or leased out his Kudiyiruppu to another person; (d) that he or his family has ceased to reside in his Kudiyiruppu for a continuous period of one year. (e) that he has another Kudikidappu or has obtained ownership and possession of land on which a homestead could be erected.
No suit shall be maintainable for the eviction of a Kudikidappukaran from a Kudiyiruppu to which this Act applies except in accordance with the provisions of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Claims in respect of Kudiyiruppu may be jointly tried with claims for recovery of possession of property.
main_sections.description: Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law, the contrary all claims in respect of any Kudiyiruppu arising in any suit for the recovery of possession of immovable property shall be tried and settled in such suit, and the decree shall contain a description of the Kudiyiruppu on any such property sufficient for the purpose of fixing the location thereof.

main_sections.section_title: Court's power to order re-location of Kudiyiruppu.
main_sections.description: In a suit by the owner, mortgagee, lessor or any other person for the recovery of possession of immovable property wherein there is a Kudiyiruppu to which this Act applies the court shall, on the application of any of the parties to the suit or may of its own motion, direct the dwelling house to be removed and re-erected on another site at the cost of the applicant or of the party directed by the court and its extent fixed in such manner as not to cause inconvenience to the parties and as appears to the court just and equitable.

Notwithstanding anything contained in any other provision of this Act, the owner of a holding may require the Kudikidappukaran to shift to a new Kudiyiruppu to be erected at the owner's cost either on the same or another land of the owner and if the Kudikidappukaran does not comply with the demand may institute a suit against him for the purpose and if the court is of consideration that all the circumstances from just and equitable to do so may direct the re-location of the Kudiyiruppu at the cost of the owner. Provided that no such suit shall be instituted without giving the Kudikidappukaran one month's notice by registered post.

main_sections.section_title: Register of Kudikidappukars to be kept in every village.
main_sections.description: (1) Government shall, as soon as may be, cause a register of Kudikidappukars to be maintained in each village showing the survey number of the land or holdings, the location of the Kudiyiruppu, the name of the owner and of the person in possession of such holding and the name of the Kudikidappukaran with such other particulars as may be prescribed. (2) Every Kudikidappukaran who is in occupation of a Kudiyiruppu at the commencement of this Act, shall apply to the Village Officer of the village where he resides to be registered as such within one year from the date of the commencement of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to make Rules.
main_sections.description: The Government shall have power to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions contained in this Act.

(1) The Travancore Prevention of Eviction Act, 1124 (Act XVIII of 1122) and the Cochin Proclamation, XVIII of 1122 are hereby repealed. (2) Every Kudikidappukaran registered under the Travancore Prevention of Eviction Act, 1124 (Act XXII of 1124) shall be deemed to be a Kudikidappukaran registered under this Act. (3) The suits seeking eviction of Kudikidappukars and appeals, reviews, revisions, decrees and applications in execution in respect of such suits stayed by the Cochin Proclamation XVIII of 1122 shall be disposed of in accordance with the provisions of this Act.

important_rules: Kudikidappukars have a permanent right of occupancy in their Kudiyiruppu.
The interest of a Kudikidappukaran is heritable but not alienable.
A Kudikidappukaran cannot be evicted except on specific grounds related to the owner's bona fide building needs, alienation of rights, or abandonment of residence.
No suit for eviction is maintainable except in accordance with the provisions of this Act.
The government shall maintain a register of Kudikidappukars in each village.
Kudikidappukars must apply to be registered within one year of the Act's commencement.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts, Government (for making rules and maintaining registers)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through suits for eviction or re-location, and by maintaining registers of Kudikidappukars.

rights: Right of permanent occupancy in Kudiyiruppu.
Right for the interest to be heritable.
duties: Kudikidappukaran must apply for registration within one year of the Act's commencement.

key_procedures: Procedure for eviction of a Kudikidappukaran, which must follow the Act's provisions.
Procedure for re-location of a Kudiyiruppu by the owner, requiring court intervention if necessary.
Procedure for registration of Kudikidappukars by the Government and application by Kudikidappukars.
administration: The Government is responsible for making rules and causing registers to be maintained. The administration of specific cases would involve courts and village officers.
important_notes: The Act does not apply to government lands, lands administered by the Administrator General or Official Receiver, lands for housing or land improvement, or certain types of rented properties like shops and warehouses.
The wife, husband, children, and grand-children of an owner are considered part of the owner's family for the purpose of bona fide building needs.
The Act repeals the Travancore Prevention of Eviction Act, 1124, and the Cochin Proclamation, XVIII of 1122, with provisions for continuing proceedings under the new Act.

title: THE TRAVANCORE-COCHIN ADAPTATION OF LAWS ACT (XXIX OF 1950)
purpose: To provide for the adaptation of laws applicable to the State of Travancore and the State of Cochin and to make the said laws applicable to the United State of Travancore and Cochin.
scope: The Act applies to the United State of Travancore and Cochin and extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin.

key_definitions.State of Travancore and Cochin: Refers to the United State of Travancore and Cochin.
key_definitions.Division Peishkar: Shall be construed as references to District Collector or Collector.
key_definitions.Assistant Peishkar: Shall be construed as references to Deputy Collector.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Adaptation of Laws Act, 1950, extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin, and shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Construction of references to State and Government and Division Peishkar, etc.
main_sections.description: Provides for the construction of references in any enactment, rule, bye-law, regulation, notification, order or instrument to the State of Travancore, the State of Cochin, the Government of Travancore, the Government of Cochin, the Division Peishkar, or the Assistant Peishkar, to be construed as references to the United State of Travancore and Cochin, the Government of the United State of Travancore and Cochin, the District Collector or Collector, and the Deputy Collector, respectively.

main_sections.section_title: Construction of references to rupees etc.
main_sections.description: Deals with the construction of references to rupees, British rupees, Indian rupees, annas, pies, and Sirkar rupees in any enactment, rule, bye-law, regulation, notification, order or instrument. It specifies how these references shall be construed in the context of the new currency system and monetary equivalents, particularly in relation to British and Indian rupees, and provides rules for calculation where the equivalent is less than one pie.

important_rules: References to the State of Travancore and the State of Cochin shall be construed as references to the United State of Travancore and Cochin.
References to the Government of Travancore and the Government of Cochin shall be construed as references to the Government of the United State of Travancore and Cochin.
References to Division Peishkar shall be construed as references to District Collector or Collector.
References to Assistant Peishkar shall be construed as references to Deputy Collector.
References to British rupees or British half rupees shall be construed as references to Indian rupees or Indian half rupees.

References to rupees, Sirkar rupees, fanams, chuckrams or cash shall be construed as references to their respective equivalents calculated in Indian currency (twenty-eight chukrams and eight cash being equivalent to one Indian rupee, 68 Indian rupees being considered as equivalent to 57 Sirkar rupees).
Where the equivalent is less than one pie, fractions of less than half of one pie shall be disregarded, and fractions of half or more than half of one pie shall be taken as one pie.
key_procedures: Adaptation of existing laws to the newly formed United State of Travancore and Cochin by reinterpreting references to the former states and their authorities.
Conversion of monetary references from older currency systems to the new Indian currency system as specified in the Act.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be the Government of the United State of Travancore and Cochin.
important_notes: The Act is an adaptation of laws.
The Act aims to harmonize laws across the merged states of Travancore and Cochin.

title: THE TRAVANCORE-COCHIN AGRICULTURAL INCOME-TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1957
purpose: To amend the Travancore-Cochin Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Travancore-Cochin Agricultural Income-ta: Referred to as the principal Act

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Agricultural Income-tax (Amendment) Act, 1957, and it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April 1957.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Long Title and Preamble
main_sections.description: Amends the Long Title and Preamble of the Travancore-Cochin Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950 (Act XXII of 1950), by substituting "State of Travancore-Cochin" with "State of Kerala" and "agricultural income-tax" with "agricultural income-tax".

In sub-section (1) of section 1 of the principal Act, for the words "Travancore-Cochin Agricultural Income-tax Act", the words "Agricultural Income-tax Act" shall be substituted. In sub-section (2), the following sub-section shall be substituted, namely:- "(2) It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala."

In section 2 of the principal Act, amendments are made to clause (h) and the following clause is substituted: "(h) 'Company' means a company as defined in section 3 of the Companies Act, 1956 (Central Act 1 of 1956)"; and the following new clause shall be inserted, namely: "(kk) 'Hindu undivided family' includes a family governed by the Madras Nambudri Act, 1932 (Madras Act XXI of 1933)"; and amendments are made to clauses (m) and (r).
In sub-section (3) of section 3 of the principal Act, for the words "Marumakkathayam tarwad", the words "Aliyasanta family or branch or Marumakkathayam tarwad" shall be substituted.
In clauses (a) and (e) of section 10 of the principal Act, for the words "Marumakkathayam tarwad", the words "Aliyasanta family or branch or Marumakkathayam tarwad" shall be substituted.
In sub-section (1) of section 21 of the principal Act, for the words "Marumakkathayam tarwad", the words "Aliyasanta family or branch, Marumakkathayam tarwad" shall be substituted.
In sub-sections (1) and (3) of section 29 of the principal Act, for the words "Marumakkathayam tarwad", the words "Aliyasanta family or branch or Marumakkathayam tarwad" shall be substituted.
In section 42 of the principal Act, for the words "Marumakkathayam tarwad", the words "Aliyasanta family or branch or Marumakkathayam tarwad" shall be substituted.
In section 56 of the principal Act, for the words "Marumakkathayam tarwad", the words "Aliyasanta family or branch or Marumakkathayam tarwad" shall be substituted.
In section 57 of the principal Act, for the words "Marumakkathayam tarwad", the words "Aliyasanta family or branch or Marumakkathayam tarwad" shall be substituted.
In sub-section (2) of section 64 of the principal Act, for the words "Marumakkathayam tarwad", the words "Aliyasanta family or branch or Maru-makkathayam tarwad" shall be substituted.
The existing Schedule to the principal Act shall be substituted namely:- [See Schedule]

If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, the Government may by order make such provisions or give such directions as appear to them to be necessary for the removal of the difficulty.

The Madras Agricultural Plantations Income-tax Act, 1955 (Act V of 1955), as in force in the Malabar District, referred to in sub-section (2) of section 3 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, is hereby repealed.

important_rules: Agricultural income-tax shall not be payable on a total agricultural income of less than three thousand rupees.
The agricultural income-tax payable in no case exceed one-half of the amount by which the total agricultural income exceeds three thousand rupees or six thousand rupees, as the case may be.
In the case of every company, agricultural income-tax shall be charged at the maximum rate on the whole of the total agricultural income.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Orders and directions may be issued by the Government to remove difficulties.

rights: Right to claim that no agricultural income-tax is payable if total agricultural income is less than three thousand rupees.
obligations: Obligation to pay agricultural income-tax as per the rates specified in the schedule.
Obligation for companies to pay agricultural income-tax at the maximum rate on the whole of the total agricultural income.

key_procedures: Substitution of definitions and references within the principal Act.
Amendment of schedules containing tax rates.
Government's power to issue orders for removal of difficulties in implementing the Act.
administration: The Act is administered by the Government, likely through its tax departments.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April 1957.

The limit referred to in the above proviso shall be Rs. 6,000 in the case of every Hindu undivided family or an Aliyasantana family or branch or a Marumakkathayam tarwad, including a Nambudiri family or a family like that of the Moochathu or any other class governed by the law applicable to Nambudiris, which satisfies as at the end of the previous year the condition that it consists of at least five members.

title: THE TRAVANCORE-COCHIN AGRICULTURAL INCOME-TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT
purpose: To amend the Travancore-Cochin Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to agricultural income and references to officers, authorities, tribunals, or courts related to agricultural income under the said Acts.

main_sections.section_title: (1) This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Agricultural Income-tax (Amendment) Act, 1951. (2) It shall come into force at once.
main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act and its commencement date.

main_sections.section_title: For Section 71 of the Travancore-Cochin Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950 (Act XXII of 1950), the following Section shall be substituted, namely:—
main_sections.description: This section outlines the substitution of Section 71 of the original Act. The substituted Section 71 deals with the repeal and saving of certain Acts and the interpretation of references to officers, authorities, tribunals, or courts.

important_rules: Repeal of Travancore Income-tax Act, 1121 and Cochin Income-tax Act, VI of 1117, in so far as they relate to tax on agricultural income.

Provided that any reference in the said Acts to an officer, authority, tribunal, or court shall be construed as a reference to the corresponding officer, authority, tribunal, or court appointed or constituted under this Act.
If any question arises as to who such corresponding officer, authority, tribunal or court is, the decision of the Government thereon shall be final.
Nothing contained in sub-section (1) shall affect the liability of any person to pay any sum due from him or any existing right of refund under the said Acts.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government (for deciding on corresponding officers/authorities)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the decision of the Government on matters of corresponding officers, authorities, tribunals, or courts.

rights: Right of refund under the said Acts is preserved.
obligations: Liability to pay any sum due under the said Acts.

administration: The administration is implied to be handled by the relevant tax authorities and the Government of Travancore-Cochin.
important_notes: The Act is published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 21st March 1951.

title: The Travancore Cochin Agricultural Income Tax Act
purpose: To provide for the levy and collection of a tax on agricultural income in the State of Travancore-Cochin.
scope: Applies to all agricultural income received by individuals, Hindu undivided families, firms, companies, and other entities in the State of Travancore-Cochin. It also covers situations of transfer of ownership, death of a person, dissolution of a firm, and changes in constitution of a firm or association.

main_sections.section_title: Assessment in case of departure from the State.
main_sections.description: Deals with the assessment of agricultural income of a person who departs from the State, including the powers of the Agricultural Income-tax Officer to assess total agricultural income and estimate it based on past years.

main_sections.section_title: Assessment in case of transfer of right to land.
main_sections.description: Covers the assessment of agricultural income when the right to land is transferred. It specifies how the transferor and transferee are assessed and how the tax can be recovered.

main_sections.section_title: Tax of deceased person payable by representative.
main_sections.description: Defines the liability of the legal representative of a deceased person for the agricultural income-tax due from the deceased.

main_sections.section_title: Assessment in case of discontinuance of business.
main_sections.description: Addresses the assessment of agricultural income when a company, firm, or association discontinues its business, including provisions for recovery of tax.

main_sections.section_title: Liability in case of discontinued business of firm or association.
main_sections.description: Deals with the liability for agricultural income-tax when a firm or association is dissolved or its business is discontinued, and how such tax is recoverable from partners or members.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure in registration of firm or association.
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for making an application to the Agricultural Income-tax Officer for the registration of a firm or for specifying the registrar of partners.

main_sections.section_title: Change in constitution of a firm and succession to business.
main_sections.description: Covers situations where there is a change in the constitution of a firm or succession to its business, and how the assessment is made and tax is recovered.

main_sections.section_title: Assessment after partition of a Hindu undivided family or Marumakkathayam tarwad.
main_sections.description: Details the assessment of agricultural income when a Hindu undivided family or a Marumakkathayam tarwad is partitioned, including the liability of members or groups of members.
Specifies the procedure for issuing a notice of demand for any tax or penalty due under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Appeal against assessment or any order.
main_sections.description: Deals with the right of appeal against an assessment or any order passed under various sections of the Act, including the procedure for hearing and deciding appeals.

main_sections.section_title: Appeals against orders passed by Assistant Commissioner.
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for appealing against orders passed by the Assistant Commissioner to the Appellate Tribunal.

main_sections.section_title: Appeal against an order of refusal to refund.
main_sections.description: Covers appeals against any order of refusal to refund under this Act or the rules made thereunder.

Grants the Commissioner the power to call for the record of any proceeding and to make inquiries or issue orders for the purpose of satisfying himself about the legality or propriety of any order passed.
Provides for the assessment or reassessment of agricultural income that has escaped assessment in any financial year.
Empowers the authority that passed an order to rectify any mistake in that order, provided certain conditions are met.

important_rules: Rule: If the proportionate share of any member of a company in the undistributed income of the company has been included in his total agricultural income, the tax payable in respect thereof shall be recoverable from the company if it cannot be recovered from such member.

Rule: Where agricultural income is recovered from a company or association, a notice of demand shall be served upon it, and if the sum is not paid, it shall be recoverable as if it were an income-tax due from the company.

Rule: Where agricultural income-tax has been paid in respect of any undistributed agricultural income of a company, and subsequently distributed in any year, the proportionate share therein of any member of the company shall be excluded from his total agricultural income of that year.

Rule: When a shareholder receives a dividend and the amount of dividend is to be treated as part of his total agricultural income, the same shall be done for the purpose of application of that sub-section to distributions of agricultural income by that company.

Rule: Agricultural Income-tax Officer may serve a notice upon a person requiring him to furnish within such time (not being less than four days) information for the purpose of making an assessment under sub-section (2) of section 17.

Rule: If the notice issued under sub-section (2) of section 17 is not complied with, the Agricultural Income-tax Officer may serve a notice upon the person requiring him to furnish within such time, information for the purpose of making an assessment.

Rule: Where a person dies, his executor, administrator or other legal representative shall be liable to pay out of the estate of the deceased person, to the extent to which the estate is capable of meeting the charge, the agricultural income-tax payable by such person or any agricultural income-tax which would have been payable by him under this Act if he had not died.

Rule: Where a person dies before the 1st June in any year or before he is served with a notice under sub-section (2) of section 17 or under section 35, as the case may be, his executor, administrator or other legal representative shall, on the serving of the notice under sub-section (2) of section 17 or under section 35, as the case may be, comply therewith.

Rule: If any agricultural income is received by a company, firm or association and the business through which such income is received is discontinued in any year, an assessment may be made and it shall be dealt with by the Agricultural Income-tax Officer in such manner as may be prescribed.

Rule: Any person discontinuing any such business shall give to the Agricultural Income-tax Officer notice of such discontinuance within thirty days thereof. If any person fails to give the notice required by this sub-section, such officer may direct that a sum shall be recovered from him by way of a penalty not exceeding the amount of agricultural income-tax subsequently assessed on him in respect of any agricultural income of a company, firm or association of persons up to the date of the discontinuance of the business.

penalties: Penalty for failure to give notice of discontinuance of business: not exceeding the amount of agricultural income-tax subsequently assessed.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Agricultural Income-tax Officer, Assistant Commissioner, Commissioner
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment, demand notices, recovery proceedings, and appeals.

rights: Right to appeal against assessment or orders.
Right to present grounds of appeal and be heard.
Right to rectification of mistakes.
Right to apply for revision of orders.
duties: Duty to furnish information when required.
Duty to pay tax and penalties.
Duty to give notice of discontinuance of business.
Duty to comply with notices and orders.
obligations: Obligation to pay tax on agricultural income.
Obligation for legal representatives to pay tax due from deceased.

key_procedures: Assessment Procedure: The Agricultural Income-tax Officer shall serve a notice upon a person requiring him to furnish information for the purpose of making an assessment.
Appeal Procedure: Any assessee objecting to an order passed by an Assistant Commissioner may appeal to the Appellate Tribunal within sixty days of the date on which such order is communicated to him.
Rectification Procedure: The authority that passed an order may, at any time within three years from the date of such order, rectify any mistake which is apparent from the record.

Notice of Demand: When any tax or penalty is due in consequence of any order passed under this Act, the Agricultural Income-tax Officer shall serve on the assessee a notice of demand specifying the sum so payable.
administration: Agricultural Income-tax Department
important_notes: The Act applies to agricultural income which has escaped assessment or has been assessed at a low rate.
The Act provides for penalties for non-compliance with its provisions.
The Act allows for appeals and revisions against orders passed by authorities.
The provisions of Sections 31 and 32 are applicable to any order of refusal to refund under this Act.

title: THE TRAVANCORE COCHIN AGRICULTURAL INCOME-TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1955.
purpose: To further amend the Travancore-Cochin Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950.
scope: Applies to the Travancore-Cochin region.

key_definitions.dividend: Defined in relation to agricultural income.
key_definitions.total agricultural income: Includes income from shares of an association, subject to recovery.

main_sections.description: Names the Act as the Travancore-Cochin Agricultural Income-tax (Amendment) Act, 1955, and states it comes into force on the 1st day of April 1951.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 2, Act XXII of 1950
main_sections.description: Amends Section 2 of the principal Act by substituting "total agricultural income" for "dividend" in clause (i) and by defining "total agricultural income" in clause (ii) based on Section 10, with specific references to brackets, letters, and figures.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 10, Act XXII of 1950
main_sections.description: Omitted Section 14 of the said Act.

main_sections.section_title: Omission of Section 14, Act XXII of 1950
main_sections.description: This section appears to be a duplicate or typo in the numbering as it refers to omitting Section 14 again.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new Section for Section 21, Act XXII of 1950
main_sections.description: Substitutes a new section for Section 21. The new section deals with power to assess individual members of certain associations, defines 'agricultural income-tax officer', and outlines conditions for exemption from tax for individuals and associations. It also addresses the Commissioner's approval for assessment and recovery from the association. A significant part explains the scope of agricultural income-tax for companies and the recovery of sums from them.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 44, Act XXII of 1950
main_sections.description: Amends Section 44 by omitting the words "or on his behalf" and "treated as paid on his behalf".

main_sections.section_title: Omission of Sections 46 and 47, Act XXII of 1950
main_sections.description: Omitted Sections 46 and 47 of the said Act.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 52, Act XXII of 1950
main_sections.description: Amends Section 52. It details omissions for Section 14 in clause (a) and clause (b).

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new Section for Section 58, Act XXII of 1950
main_sections.description: Substitutes a new Section 58 concerning the "Application of Act to super-tax". It states that all provisions of the Act relating to charge, assessment, collection, and recovery of agricultural income-tax apply to super-tax, except those in sub-section (1) of Section 3 and clauses (c), (d), and (e) of Section 10.

important_rules: Any association of individuals where the sum payable and such company or association shall be deemed to have been assessed in respect of such sum, for the purposes of Chapter VI.

The Commissioner of Agricultural Income-tax shall not give his approval to any order proposed to be passed by the Agricultural Income-tax Officer under this section until he has given the firm, association or company concerned an opportunity of being heard.

Where any member of an association of individuals makes default in the payment of tax on his share of income which has been included in his total agricultural income under the provision of sub-section (1), such tax may be recovered from the association.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Agricultural Income-tax Officer, Commissioner of Agricultural Income-tax
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Assessment, collection, and recovery of agricultural income-tax and super-tax.

rights: Right to be heard by the Commissioner before approval of an order proposed by the Agricultural Income-tax Officer.
Right to recovery of tax from the association if an individual member defaults.
obligations: Individuals and associations are liable for agricultural income-tax.
Associations are responsible for the payment of tax on behalf of their members in certain circumstances.

key_procedures: Procedure for assessment of individual members of associations and recovery of tax.
Procedure for the Commissioner of Agricultural Income-tax to grant approval for assessment orders.
Procedure for recovery of tax from associations when individual members default.
administration: Agricultural Income-tax Department/Officer.
important_notes: The Act comes into force from the 1st day of April 1951.
The Act makes amendments to The Travancore-Cochin Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950 (Act XXII of 1950).
Certain sections of the principal Act are omitted or substituted.

The provisions of this Act relating to charge, assessment, collection and recovery of agricultural income-tax apply to super-tax, with specific exceptions for sub-section (1) of Section 3 and clauses (c), (d), and (e) of Section 10.

title: The Travancore Cochin Agricultural Pests and Diseases (Amendment) Act, 1956
purpose: To amend the Travancore-Cochin Agricultural Pests and Diseases Act, 1955, for certain purposes.
scope: Applies to the State of Travancore-Cochin.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Agricultural Pests and Diseases (Amendment) Act, 1956.

In Section 2 of the Travancore-Cochin State Legislature (Delegation of Powers) Act, 1955 (XX of 1955), for the expression "Section 3" or "Section 8", the expression "Section 3" or Section 8A" shall be substituted.

After Section 8 of the principal Act, the following section shall be inserted, namely:-
"8A. Preventive or remedial measures in emergent cases:-
(1) Notwithstanding anything contained in Sections 3 to 8, if the Government are satisfied that any pest or disease is such as to require immediate action to prevent or check its spread in any local area, or from any place to another, they may, by notification in the Gazette.-
(a) declare that such pest or disease is an insect pest or plant disease;
(b) prescribe such preventive or remedial measures as may be necessary in respect of such pest or disease;
(c) prohibit or restrict the removal of any plant from one place to another;
(d) define the local area within which, and the period during which, such notification shall be in force; and
(e) declare that it shall be competent to the Government to cause the prescribed preventive or remedial measures to be carried out in the notified area.
(2) Upon the issue of a notification under sub-section (1), it shall be competent to the inspecting officer appointed under section 20 to enter on any land or water within the notified area and carry out the prescribed preventive or remedial measures or cause such measures to be carried out under his supervision.
(3) Where any preventive or remedial measures are carried out under sub-section (2), the occupier shall be liable to pay to Government towards the cost of the measures an amount not exceeding the percentage of such cost prescribed by Government by notification in the Gazette. The inspecting officer shall by order in writing determine the amount payable by the occupier and demand payment of the amount within such time as may be specified therein. If the occupier defaults payment as aforesaid, the amount shall be recoverable from him as if it were an arrear of land revenue.
(4) for calculating the cost of the preventive or remedial measures for the purposes of sub-section (3), the following shall be taken into account, namely:-
(a) charges for labour, material or use of implements; and
(b) proportionate charges for any special establishment entertained for the purpose.
(5) Any occupier considering himself aggrieved by an order passed by the inspecting officer under sub-section (3), may apply by such officer as may be authorised by the Government in this behalf to revise the order of the inspecting officer: Provided that no such application shall lie unless.-
(i) it is made within thirty days from the date of receipt by the occupier of such order; and
(ii) the amount demanded has been paid in accordance with such order.
(6) The officer to whom an application is made under sub-section (5) may, after making such enquiry as he thinks fit, either affirm or vary the order of the inspecting officer and his decision shall be final.
(7) Where the amount payable by the occupier is in excess of the amount payable under the order as revised, such excess shall be refunded to him."
In sub-section (1) of Section 10 of the principal Act, for the expression "Section 8" or Section 8A" shall be substituted.

important_rules: Rule 1: If the Government is satisfied that any pest or disease requires immediate action, they may declare it as an insect pest or plant disease, prescribe preventive or remedial measures, and prohibit or restrict the movement of plants.
Rule 2: Inspecting officers can enter land to carry out preventive or remedial measures under government supervision.
Rule 3: Occupiers are liable to pay a portion of the cost of preventive or remedial measures, as determined by the inspecting officer.
Rule 4: Costs for calculating preventive or remedial measures include labour, materials, implements, and special establishment charges.
Rule 5: Occupiers aggrieved by an order can apply for revision within thirty days of receiving the order, after paying the demanded amount.

penalties: Amount not exceeding a prescribed percentage of the cost of measures, recoverable as arrears of land revenue.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Inspecting officers appointed under section 20, and the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By issuing notifications, entering land, carrying out measures, determining and demanding payment of costs, and through revision of orders.

rights: Right to apply for revision of an order regarding cost of measures.
duties: Duty to comply with prescribed preventive or remedial measures.
Duty to pay for a portion of the cost of preventive or remedial measures.
Duty to pay demanded amount within the specified time.
obligations: Obligation to pay for preventive or remedial measures as determined by the inspecting officer.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Government declares pest/disease and prescribes measures via notification.
Procedure 2: Inspecting officer enters land and carries out measures.
Procedure 3: Inspecting officer determines and demands payment of costs from occupier.
Procedure 4: Occupier can apply for revision of the order within 30 days of receipt and after paying the amount.
Procedure 5: Revising officer makes a final decision on the order.
administration: The Government (presumably the relevant department dealing with agriculture and pests).
important_notes: Section 8A is for emergent cases of pests and diseases.
The cost recoverable from the occupier cannot exceed a percentage prescribed by the Government.
Revisional applications are only considered if the demanded amount has been paid.

title: THE TRAVANCORE-COCHIN AGRICULTURAL PESTS AND DISEASES ACT, 1955
purpose: An Act to make provision for preventing the spread of insect pests, plant diseases and noxious weeds within the State of Travancore-Cochin.
scope: Applies within the State of Travancore-Cochin.

key_definitions.insect pest: Any insect or other invertebrate animal which has been declared by notification under Section 3 of this Act to be an insect pest.
key_definitions.plant disease: Any fungoid, bacterial, parasiticaI or other disease which has been declared by notification under Section 3 of this Act to be a plant disease.
key_definitions.noxious weed: Any weed which has been declared by notification under Section 3 of this Act to be a noxious weed.
key_definitions.plant: Includes the fruit, leaves, bark, cuttings or any living portion of a plant but does not include the seed unless the seed has been especially included in the definition of plant by the Government by notification.
key_definitions.occupier: Means the person having for the time being the right of occupation of any land, premises or water or his authorised agent or any person in actual occupation of the land, premises or water; and includes a local authority and a company having such right of occupation or in such actual occupation.
key_definitions.notified area: Means the area covered by a notification published under Section 3.
key_definitions.Director of Agriculture: Means every appoint ed by the Government to be the Director of Agriculture and includes every person who for the time being performs the duties of the office.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by notification or rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Agricultural Pests and Diseases Act, 1955, extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin, and shall come into force at once.
Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'insect pest', 'plant disease', 'noxious weed', 'plant', 'occupier', 'notified area', 'Director of Agriculture', and 'prescribed'.

main_sections.section_title: Notification of areas affected by insect pests, plant diseases or noxious weeds.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to notify areas affected by pests, diseases, or weeds, and to prohibit or restrict the removal of such plants or prescribe remedial measures. It also defines the scope and duration of such notifications.
States that occupiers within a notified area are bound to carry out prescribed remedial and preventive measures.
Grants appointed officers the right to enter any land or water within the notified area to take action.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure where measures prescribed to eradicate insect pests include removal or destruction of plants.
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for plant removal or destruction by inspecting officers, including issuing notices and the right of appeal for occupiers.

main_sections.section_title: Inspecting officer may serve a notice on occupier to take remedial or preventive action.
main_sections.description: Allows inspecting officers to issue notices to occupiers to take remedial or preventive action. It also details the process for appealing such notices.

main_sections.section_title: Occupier failing to comply with the notice served on him commits an offence.
main_sections.description: Declares that failure to comply with a notice constitutes an offence.

main_sections.section_title: Recovery of the amount of compensation.
main_sections.description: Specifies that the cost of preventive or remedial measures carried out by the inspecting officer can be recovered from the occupier. It also details the recovery process and appeal procedures.

main_sections.section_title: Destruction of trees or plants in execution of remedial or preventive measures and compensation therefor.
main_sections.description: Covers the destruction of trees or plants as part of remedial or preventive measures, specifying which types of plants can be destroyed and detailing the compensation payable for such destruction.

main_sections.section_title: Claims for compensation how and when to be made.
main_sections.description: Defines the procedure and timeframe for making compensation claims.
Outlines the process for awarding compensation, including inquiry and transmission of awards.
Provides for the right to appeal against compensation awards.

main_sections.section_title: Obligation of village officers to report on insect pests, plant diseases or noxious weeds.
main_sections.description: Places an obligation on village officers to report occurrences of pests, diseases, or weeds.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for offence under Section 6 or 8.
main_sections.description: Specifies the punishment for offences related to non-compliance with notices or orders.

main_sections.section_title: Contravening notification under Section 3 (1) (b) to be an offence and punishment therefor.
main_sections.description: Defines contravention of certain notifications as an offence and prescribes punishment.

main_sections.section_title: Compensation for trees and plants destroyed by occupier.
main_sections.description: Specifies compensation for trees and plants destroyed by an occupier.

main_sections.section_title: Compensation not payable for noxious weeds destroyed.
main_sections.description: States that compensation is not payable for noxious weeds destroyed.

main_sections.section_title: Institution of prosecutions or other legal proceedings under the Act.
main_sections.description: Regulates the institution of prosecutions and legal proceedings, requiring prior sanction.
Empowers the Government to appoint inspecting officers.
Allows the Government to delegate powers under the Act.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for various aspects of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Rules to be laid before the Legislative Assembly.
main_sections.description: Specifies that rules made under the Act must be laid before the Legislative Assembly.
Repeals the Travancore Plant Pests and Plant Diseases Act, XII of 1094 and the Cochin Plant Pests and Plant Diseases Act, XIV of 1098.

important_rules: Occupiers in a notified area are bound to carry out prescribed remedial and preventive measures.
Inspecting officers can serve notices on occupiers to take remedial or preventive action.
Destruction of trees or plants may occur as part of remedial or preventive measures, with provisions for compensation.
Village officers must report occurrences of insect pests, plant diseases, or noxious weeds.
The Government can make rules consistent with the Act regarding various aspects like notification, qualifications of officers, and compensation.

penalties: Punishment for offence under Section 6 or 8: Not exceeding fifty rupees or simple imprisonment for a period not exceeding ten days.
Punishment for contravening notification under Section 3(1)(b): Fine not exceeding fifty rupees or simple imprisonment for a period not exceeding ten days.
Punishment for confiscation and destruction of plants without the Act's authority: Fine not exceeding fifty rupees or simple imprisonment for a period not exceeding ten days.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Inspecting officers, Director of Agriculture, Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notification of affected areas, issuance of notices for remedial/preventive measures, right of entry for officers, recovery of costs for measures taken, and institution of prosecutions for non-compliance.

rights: Right of entry for appointed officers into notified areas.
Right to appeal against notices served by inspecting officers.
Right to compensation for trees and plants destroyed under specific circumstances.
Right to appeal against compensation awards.
duties: Duty of occupiers to carry out prescribed remedial and preventive measures.
Duty of village officers to report on insect pests, plant diseases or noxious weeds.
obligations: Occupiers are obligated to comply with notices served by inspecting officers.

key_procedures: Notification of affected areas by the Government.
Issuance of notices by inspecting officers to occupiers for remedial or preventive action.
Procedure for removal or destruction of plants, including appeals.
Claiming and awarding compensation for destroyed plants.
Reporting of pests, diseases, and weeds by village officers.
Institution of prosecutions with prior sanction.
administration: The Government, through the Director of Agriculture and appointed inspecting officers.
important_notes: Compensation is not payable for noxious weeds destroyed.
No prosecution can be instituted without the previous sanction of the District Collector.
No prosecution can be commenced after six months from the date of the alleged offence.
The Act repeals the Travancore Plant Pests and Plant Diseases Act, XII of 1094 and the Cochin Plant Pests and Plant Diseases Act, XIV of 1098.

title: THE TRANANCORE-COCHIN ANIMALS AND BIRDS SACRIFICES PROHIBITION ACT, 1953
purpose: To prohibit the sacrifice of animals and birds in or in the precincts of Hindu temples in the State of Travancore-Cochin.
scope: Applies to the State of Travancore-Cochin. Prohibits sacrifice of animals and birds in Hindu temples and their precincts.

key_definitions.precincts: In relation to a temple, includes all lands and buildings near a temple, whether belonging to the temple or not, which are ordinarily used for purposes connected with the worship conducted inside the temple or outside and in particular the mandapams, prakarams, back-yards, front-yards and foot-yards of temple, by whatever name called, and also the ground on which the temple car ordinarily stands.
key_definitions.sacrifice: means the killing or maiming of any animal or bird for the purpose or with the intention of propitiating any deity.
key_definitions.temple: means a temple as defined in Section 2, clause (1) of the Travancore-Cochin Temple Entry (Removal of Disabilities) Act, 1950 (Act XXVIII of 1950).

main_sections.description: States the short title as The Travancore-Cochin Animals and Birds Sacrifices Prohibition Act, 1953. Specifies its extent to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin and that it comes into force on a date appointed by the Government.
Provides definitions for 'precincts', 'sacrifice', and 'temple' as used in the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Sacrifice of animals and birds in temple or its precincts prohibited.
main_sections.description: Prohibits any person from inside any temple or its precincts to sacrifice any animal or bird.

Prohibits any person from officiating or offering to officiate at, performing or offering to perform, or serving, assisting, participating, or offering to serve, assist, or participate in, any sacrifice in a temple or its precincts. Also prohibits using any temple or its precincts for sacrifice, or being in possession of an animal or bird for sacrifice in such a location.

main_sections.section_title: Temple or its precincts not to be allowed to be used for sacrifice.
main_sections.description: No person shall knowingly allow any sacrifice to be performed at any place which is situated within any temple or its precincts, and is in his possession or under his control.
Outlines penalties for contravening the provisions of Sections 3, 4, and 5.
Specifies that the enquiry into and trial of offences under this Act shall be conducted by a Court of a Magistrate of the first or second class.

important_rules: Sacrifice of animals and birds in Hindu temples or their precincts is prohibited.
Officiating at, performing, or assisting in any sacrifice in a temple or its precincts is prohibited.
Knowingly allowing a temple or its precincts to be used for sacrifice is prohibited.
Possessing an animal or bird for the purpose of sacrifice within a temple or its precincts is prohibited.

penalties: Contravention of Section 3: Punishable with fine which may extend to three hundred rupees.
Contravention of Section 4: Punishable with fine which may extend to three hundred rupees.
Contravention of Section 5: Punishable with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months or with fine which may extend to three hundred rupees or with both.

If the offender is an officer, servant, authority, trustee or priest of the temple or the holder of any office in receipt of emoluments or requisites for the performance of any service in the temple, he shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months or with fine which may extend to three hundred rupees or with both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Magistrate of the first or second class
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Enquiry and trial by Magistrate of the first or second class.

duties: Duty to not sacrifice animals or birds in temples or precincts.
Duty to not officiate, perform, or assist in sacrifices in temples or precincts.
Duty to not allow temples or precincts to be used for sacrifice.
Duty to not possess animals or birds for sacrifice in temples or precincts.

key_procedures: Enquiry into offences by a Magistrate of the first or second class.
Trial of offences by a Magistrate of the first or second class.
administration: The administration and enforcement of the Act are handled through the judicial process overseen by Magistrates.
important_notes: The Act was reserved for the assent of the President and received his assent.
Published in the Gazette dated 7th July 1953, Part I, Section iii.

title: THE TRAVANCORE-COCHIN CINEMAS (REGULATION) ACT, 1955.
purpose: An Act to make provision for regulating exhibitions by means of cinematographs.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin.

key_definitions.cinematograph: Includes any apparatus for the representation of moving pictures or series of pictures; 'place' includes a house, building, tent or any description of transport, whether by water, land or air; and 'prescribed' means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.licensing authority: The authority having power to grant licenses under this Act, hereinafter referred to as the 'licensing authority', shall be the Government (in the City of Trivandrum), the Municipal Council (in any Municipal area), or the Panchayat (in any Panchayat area), or any such authority as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, specify.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Cinemas (Regulation) Act, 1955. It extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Defines 'cinematograph', 'place', and 'prescribed'.
No cinematograph exhibition shall be given except in a place licensed under this Act or otherwise than in compliance with conditions and restrictions imposed by such license.
Specifies the authorities empowered to grant licenses, including the Government, Municipal Councils, and Panchayats, or other authorities notified by the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Restrictions on powers of licensing authority.
main_sections.description: The licensing authority shall not grant a license unless rules under the Act have been complied with and adequate precautions have been taken to provide for the safety of persons attending exhibitions. The Government or such officer as the Government may specify may grant licenses under this Act, subject to such terms and conditions as they think fit. Any person aggrieved by the decision of a licensing authority refusing a license may appeal to the Government or such officer as the Government may specify.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government or District Magistrate to suspend exhibition of films in certain cases.
main_sections.description: The Government or the District Magistrate, in respect of the whole or part of the State within their jurisdiction, may suspend the exhibition of any film if they are of opinion that the film is being publicly exhibited, is likely to cause a breach of the peace, by order. Such suspension can be for a period not exceeding 30 days. The Government may also issue an order to suspend exhibitions of films in certain cases for a period of two months from the date the order is made.

main_sections.section_title: Penalties for contravention of the Act and rules made thereunder.
main_sections.description: Penalties for contravention of the Act and rules include fines of up to one thousand rupees, with a further fine for continuing offences. Penalties also apply to persons exhibiting films without a license or in contravention of suspension orders.

Where the holder of a license has been convicted of an offence under Section 7 of the Cinematograph Act, 1952 (Central Act XXXVII of 1952) or under Section 7 of this Act, the license may be revoked by the licensing authority.

main_sections.section_title: Power to revise proceedings under the Act.
main_sections.description: The Government may call for and examine the record of any proceeding taken under this Act and make any further enquiry and may pass such order in reference thereto as they think fit.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make rules for the purpose of carrying into effect the provisions of this Act. These rules can cover terms and restrictions for licensing, fees for licensing, inspection of places, sanitary arrangements, and other conditions related to exhibitions.

The Government may, by order in writing, exempt subject to such conditions and restrictions as they may impose, any cinematograph exhibition or class of cinematograph exhibitions from all or any of the provisions of this Act or of any rules made thereunder.

The Travancore Cinematograph Act, 1902 (Act I of 1902) and the Cochin Cinematograph Act, Act IV of 1102 are hereby repealed in so far as they relate to regulation of cinemas including their licensing.

important_rules: Cinematograph exhibitions must be licensed.
Licenses shall not be granted unless rules under the Act are complied with and safety precautions are taken.
The Government or District Magistrate can suspend film exhibitions if likely to cause a breach of peace.
Rules may be made regarding terms and restrictions for licensing, fees, inspection, and sanitary arrangements.
The Government can exempt certain exhibitions from the Act's provisions.

penalties: Contravention of the Act or rules can result in a fine up to one thousand rupees, and a further fine of one hundred rupees for each day during which the offence continues.
Exhibiting films after suspension without authority can lead to a fine of one thousand rupees and a further fine of one hundred rupees for each day of continued offence.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Licensing authorities, Government, and District Magistrates.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the granting and revocation of licenses, suspension of exhibitions, imposition of fines, and potentially by invoking powers of the Government and District Magistrate to maintain public order.

rights: Right to appeal to the Government against the decision of a licensing authority refusing a license.
duties: Exhibitors have a duty to comply with the Act and its rules.
Exhibitors must ensure safety of persons attending exhibitions.
Operators of cinematographs must ensure their apparatus is used in compliance with the Act.
obligations: Obtain a license to exhibit cinematograph films.

key_procedures: Application for a license from the relevant licensing authority (Government, Municipal Council, or Panchayat).
Compliance with rules regarding terms, conditions, fees, safety, and sanitary arrangements.
Appeal to the Government if a license is refused.
Potential suspension of exhibition by Government or District Magistrate in specific circumstances.
Revocation of license upon conviction for certain offences.
administration: The Government, and specifically the relevant licensing authorities (which can include the Government itself, Municipal Councils, and Panchayats, or authorities notified by the Government).
important_notes: The Act repeals the Travancore Cinematograph Act, 1902 and the Cochin Cinematograph Act, Act IV of 1102, in so far as they relate to the regulation and licensing of cinemas.

Any appointment, notification, order, license, rule or form made or issued under the repealed enactments shall continue in force and be deemed to have been made or issued under the provisions of this Act, unless and until it is superseded by any appointment, notification, order, license, rule or form made or issued under this Act.

title: THE TRAVANCORE-COCHIN CIVIL COURTS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1952
purpose: To amend the Travancore-Cochin Civil Courts Act, 1951, for the purposes herein after appearing.
scope: Applies to civil suits and appeals within the jurisdiction of the Travancore-Cochin Civil Courts.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Civil Courts (Amendment) Act, 1952. It shall come into force on such date (hereinafter referred to as the "appointed day") as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 12, Act XXII of 1951.
main_sections.description: In sub-section (4) of Section 12 of the Travancore-Cochin Civil Courts Act, 1951 (Act XXII of 1951), for the abbreviation and figures "Rs. 200/0" (Rupees two hundred only), the abbreviation and figures "Rs. 3000" (Rupees three thousand only) shall be substituted.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 13, Act XXII of 1951.
main_sections.description: In Section 13 of the said Act, for the abbreviation and figures "Rs. 100" (Rupees one hundred only), the abbreviation and figures "Rs. 100" (Rupees one hundred only) shall be substituted.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 22, Act XXII of 1951.
main_sections.description: In sub-section (1) of Section 22 of the said Act, for the words "except when the amount or value of the subject matter exceeds two thousand rupees" the words "except when the amount or value of the subject-matter of suit exceeds three thousand rupees" shall be substituted.

main_sections.section_title: Institution of certain suits and appeals and disposal of certain appeals.
main_sections.description: (1) All suits and proceedings of a civil nature of which the amount or value of the subject-matter exceeds Rs. 2,000 but does not exceed Rs. 3,000 already instituted in a District Court or the Court of a Subordinate Judge before the appointed day shall be tried by such Court. (2) Appeals from the decrees and orders of the District Munsiffs and Subordinate Judges in original suits and proceedings of a civil nature of which the amount or value of the subject-matter exceeds Rs. 2,000 but does not exceed Rs. 3,000 which have not been preferred to the High Court before the appointed day shall, when such appeals are allowed by law, lie to the District Court: Provided that such appeals already preferred to the High Court before the appointed day shall be decided and heard by the High Court; Provided further that if on the appointed day, the period within which such appeals could have been preferred to the High Court has not elapsed, the appeals may be preferred to the District Court within such period.

important_rules: The Act comes into force on an appointed day to be notified by the Government.
Amendments to monetary limits for suits and appeals are made.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government (for notification of appointed day and gazetting)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the functioning of the Civil Courts under the amended Act.

rights: Right to appeal to the District Court for suits with subject matter value between Rs. 2,000 and Rs. 3,000, if not already preferred to High Court before the appointed day.
Right to have appeals already preferred to the High Court decided by the High Court.
duties: The Government has the duty to appoint a day for the commencement of the Act and notify it.
Courts have the duty to try suits and hear appeals according to the amended provisions.

key_procedures: The Act is brought into force by a Government notification.
Suits with subject matter value between Rs. 2,000 and Rs. 3,000 are to be tried by the District Court or Subordinate Judge's Court if instituted before the appointed day.
Appeals for such suits, if not preferred to the High Court before the appointed day, will lie to the District Court.
Appeals already preferred to the High Court will continue to be heard by the High Court.
administration: Travancore-Cochin Civil Courts system.
important_notes: The amended Act is a procedural amendment to the existing Travancore-Cochin Civil Courts Act, 1951.
The monetary limits for suits and appeals have been significantly increased.
Specific provisions are made for handling appeals that were in process or within the appeal period at the time of commencement.

title: THE TRAVANCORE COCHIN CIVIL COURTS ACT
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to the Civil Courts subordinate to the High Court of the State of Travancore-Cochin.
scope: Applies to the State of Travancore-Cochin and governs the jurisdiction and functioning of Civil Courts subordinate to the High Court.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Civil Courts Act, 1951. It extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin and shall come into force at once. It also states that the High Court's jurisdiction definition means the High Court of Judicature of this State, and references to the Travancore Civil Courts Act III of 1076 and Cochin Civil Courts Act III of 1084 shall stand repealed. Any references to enactments hereby repealed shall be construed as if made to this Act or the corresponding provisions thereof. It also mentions publication in Part I, Section II of the Gazette dated 25-12-1951.

There shall be four classes of Civil Courts subordinate to the High Court, namely: (i) the District Court; (ii) the Court of the Subordinate Judge; (iii) the Court of Small Causes; and (iv) the Court of the District Munsiff.

main_sections.section_title: Number of District Courts to be established or continued
main_sections.description: The number of District Courts shall be fixed and may, from time to time, be altered by Government. When, in the opinion of Government, the state of business pending before the Judge of any District Court (hereinafter called the District Judge) so requires, the District Judge may, in consultation with the High Court, appoint one or more Additional District Judges to that Court either permanently or for such period as Government may deem necessary. The Additional District Judges so appointed shall discharge all or any of the functions of the District Judge under this Act or any other law for the time being in force. The District Judge may assign to them and in the discharge of those functions, they shall exercise the same powers as the District Judge.

main_sections.section_title: Number of Subordinate Judges and Judges of Small Cause Courts and District Munsiffs
main_sections.description: The number of Subordinate Judges and Judges of Small Cause Courts and District Munsiffs to be appointed under this Act shall be fixed and may, from time to time, be altered by Government.

When more than one District Munsiff is appointed to a District Principal and Additional District Munsiff's Court, one of the District Munsiffs shall be appointed the Principal District Munsiff and the others Additional District Munsiffs. Any Additional District Munsiff may exercise all or any of the powers conferred on the Court of a District Munsiff by this Act or any other law for the time being in force and shall discharge such of the functions, which the District Munsiff may assign to them and in the discharge of these functions, they shall exercise the same powers as the District Munsiff.

main_sections.section_title: Place at which Court to be held
main_sections.description: The place at which any Court under this Act shall be held may be fixed and from time to time be altered by Government.

main_sections.section_title: Appointments to be notified in Gazette
main_sections.description: All appointments of Judges and Munsiffs shall be notified in the Government Gazette.
Every Court under this Act shall use a seal of such form and dimensions as are for the time being prescribed by Government.

main_sections.section_title: Local limits of jurisdiction of Civil Courts to be fixed by Government
main_sections.description: Local limits of the jurisdiction of Civil Courts to be fixed by Government.

main_sections.section_title: Jurisdiction of District Judge or a Subordinate Judge
main_sections.description: Jurisdiction of District Judge or a Subordinate Judge extends, subject to the rules contained in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, to all original suits and proceedings of a civil nature. The District Court shall be deemed to be the principal civil court of original jurisdiction in the District within the meaning of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. Jurisdiction of Judges of Small Cause Courts extends, subject to the rules contained in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, to all suits and proceedings of a civil nature of which the amount or value of the subject matter does not exceed five hundred rupees, except suits specified in the Schedule hereto annexed. Jurisdiction of District Munsiffs extends, subject to the rules contained in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, to all suits and proceedings of a civil nature of which the amount or value of the subject matter does not exceed Rs. 5,000, except suits specified in the Schedule hereto annexed. Provided that the Government, on the recommendation of the High Court, may by notification in the Gazette, invest any Munsiff, within such local limits as they shall from time to time appoint, with jurisdiction extending to all original suits and proceedings of which the amount or value of the subject matter does not exceed Rs. 5,000 and may by notification withdraw such jurisdiction.

main_sections.section_title: Every Government Munsiff shall hear and determine all small cause suits
main_sections.description: Every Government Munsiff shall hear and determine all small cause suits of a civil nature, except suits specified in the Schedule hereto annexed, the amount or value of which does not exceed Rs. 100. District or Subordinate Judges may be invested with small cause powers.

main_sections.section_title: Government may invest Munsiffs with small cause powers
main_sections.description: District or Subordinate Judges may be invested with small cause powers.

main_sections.section_title: Application of Act and Code to Court invested with two courts
main_sections.description: A Court invested with the jurisdiction of a Court of Small Causes which deems itself unable to hear and determine with respect to the exercise of its jurisdiction in suits of a civil nature, shall for the purposes of this Act and the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, be deemed to be different Courts.

main_sections.section_title: Return of plaints in suits involving question of titles
main_sections.description: (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in Sections 12, 13 and 14, when the right of a plaintiff and the relief claimed by him in a Court of Small Causes or in a Court otherwise competent with the jurisdiction of a Court of Small Causes depend upon the proof or disproof of title to immovable property or other title which such Court cannot finally determine, such Court may, at any stage of the proceedings, return the plaint to be presented to a Court having jurisdiction to determine the title. (2) When a Court returns a plaint under sub-section (1), it shall comply with the provisions prescribed by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, for the return of plaints and shall make such order with respect to costs as it deems just and the Court shall, for the purposes of the law of limitation, for the time being in force be deemed to have been unable to entertain the suit by reason of a cause of a nature like to that of a defect of jurisdiction. (3) A Court invested with the jurisdiction of a Court of Small Causes with jurisdiction in suits of a civil nature which are not cognizable by a Court of Small Causes may, instead of returning the plaint under sub-section (1) transfer it to the court of original jurisdiction in suits of a civil nature which are not cognizable by a Court of Small Causes.

main_sections.section_title: Modification of Civil Courts as so applied
main_sections.description: (2) When in the exercise of its jurisdiction in suits of a civil nature which are not cognizable by a Court of Small Causes, a Court invested with the jurisdiction of a Court of Small Causes, the Court of Small Causes shall have jurisdiction in suits of civil nature which are not cognizable by a Court of Small Causes. The documents mentioned in Order XXI, Rule 6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, shall not be sent with the decree unless in any case the Court, by order in writing requires them to be sent.

main_sections.section_title: Continuation of proceedings of abolished Courts
main_sections.description: (1) Where a Court of Small Causes or a Court invested with the jurisdiction of a Court of Small Causes, has from any cause ceased to have jurisdiction with respect to any case, any proceeding in relation to the suit, whether before or after decree, which the Court had not ceased to have jurisdiction, might have been had therein if the Court in which the suit out of which the proceeding has arisen were about to be instituted, would have had jurisdiction to try the suit. (2) Nothing in this section applies to cases for which special provision is made in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 for extended to Courts of Small Causes, or in any other enactment for the time being in force.

main_sections.section_title: Application of the Code of Civil Procedure
main_sections.description: The procedure in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, except the provisions specified in Section 7 and Application of the Order L thereof as inapplicable to suits tried as small cause suits shall be the procedure followed in a Court of Small Causes, and in a Court exercising the jurisdiction of a Court of Small Causes in all suits cognizable by it, and in all proceedings arising out of such suits.

main_sections.section_title: Finality of decisions in small causes
main_sections.description: Provided that the defendant shall state his defence orally or in writing if he so chooses and the Court shall in the former case record the substance of the statement, in its own hand-writing and no written statement other than the plaint and defence, shall be received from any party to the suit, unless required by a written order of the Court, setting forth the reasons.

main_sections.section_title: Suits by or against Government etc., to be instituted in District Court.
main_sections.description: The decisions of Judges of Small Cause Courts and of Munsiffs, Subordinate Judges and District Judges in the exercise of the small cause powers shall be final, except orders specified in clause (h) of sub-section (1) of section 104 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, from which an appeal shall lie subject to the provisions of the said Code relating to reference and revision.

Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, suits or other proceedings by or against the Government, or the Government of India, the Executive Officer of the Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple, the Travancore Board or the Cochin Board shall be instituted in the District Court having local jurisdiction.

main_sections.section_title: Power to require witness or party to make oath or affirmation
main_sections.description: (1) Appeals from original or appellate decrees or orders of a District Court shall, when such appeals are allowed by law, lie to the High Court. (2) Appeals from original or appellate decrees or orders of a District Court shall, when such appeals are allowed by law, lie to the High Court, except when the amount or value of the subject matter does not exceed two thousand rupees, in which case the appeal shall lie to the High Court.
Every Court under this Act may require a witness or party to make such oath or affirmation as is in accordance with any law or usage having the force of law for the time being in force.

main_sections.section_title: Judge or Munsiff not to try suits in which he is interested
main_sections.description: Law administered by Courts. In any suit or proceeding, it is necessary for any Court under this Act to decide any question regarding succession, inheritance, marriage or caste, or any religious usage or institution. (a) the Mohammedan Law in cases where the parties are Mohammedans and the Hindu Law in cases where the parties are Hindus, or (b) any custom (if such there be) having the force of law and governing the particular property concerned, shall form the rule of decision, unless such Law or custom has by legislative enactment been altered or abolished, or (c) in cases where no specific rule exists, the Court shall act according to justice, equity and good conscience.

main_sections.section_title: Declaration to be made by Judge or Munsiff
main_sections.description: No District Judge, Subordinate Judge, Judge of Small Cause Court or District Munsiff shall try any suit to or in which he is interested, or shall adjudicate upon any proceeding connected with, or arising out of, such suit. No District Judge shall try any appeal against a decree or order passed by himself in another capacity. When any such suit, proceeding or appeal comes before any officer in another capacity, the officer shall report the circumstances to the Court of such Munsiff, and shall be immediately subordinate. The Superior Court shall thereupon dispose of the case in the manner prescribed by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

main_sections.section_title: Vacancies of Judges and Munsiffs to be reported
main_sections.description: Every Judge or Munsiff appointed whether permanently or temporarily shall, previous to entering upon the duties of his office make and subscribe the following declaration before any of the Judges of the High Court: "I, A.B., appointed District Judge, Additional District Judge, Judge of the Small Cause Court, District Munsiff or Additional District Munsiff of......................do solemnly declare that I will faithfully perform the duties of my office to the best of my ability, knowledge and judgment."

main_sections.section_title: District Judge to control all Civil Courts in the District
main_sections.description: The District Judge, on the occurrence within his District of any vacancy in the office of Subordinate Judge, Judge of Small Cause Court, District Munsiff or Additional Munsiff, shall at once report such vacancy to Government.
The High Court shall likewise report to Government the occurrence of any vacancy in its office of District Judge.

Subject to the other provisions of this Act and prescribed by the High Court in this behalf, the general control over all the Civil Courts in the District shall vest in the District Judge. The District Judge may, with the sanction of the Government, permit not exceeding sixty days for summer, and not exceeding seventy days for Onam and Tamil festivals respectively in each year.

important_rules: The High Court's jurisdiction definition means the High Court of Judicature of this State.
References to the Travancore Civil Courts Act III of 1076 and Cochin Civil Courts Act III of 1084 are repealed.
All references to any enactment hereby repealed shall be construed as if made to this Act or the corresponding provisions thereof.
The number of District Courts, Subordinate Judges, Judges of Small Cause Courts and District Munsiffs shall be fixed and may be altered by Government.
Additional District Judges may be appointed to discharge functions of a District Judge.
The place where a Court is held may be fixed and altered by Government.
All appointments of Judges and Munsiffs must be notified in the Government Gazette.
Each Court must use a prescribed seal.
Local limits of jurisdiction of Civil Courts are fixed by Government.
District Judges and Subordinate Judges have jurisdiction over all original suits and proceedings of a civil nature.
District Courts are principal civil courts of original jurisdiction.
Judges of Small Cause Courts have jurisdiction up to Rs. 500, with exceptions.
District Munsiffs have jurisdiction up to Rs. 5,000, with exceptions.
Government may invest Munsiffs with jurisdiction up to Rs. 5,000 and withdraw such jurisdiction.
Government Munsiffs must hear and determine small cause suits up to Rs. 100, with exceptions.
District or Subordinate Judges may be invested with small cause powers.
Courts unable to determine title issues in Small Cause Courts may return plaints.
Written statements are generally not received unless ordered by the Court.
Decisions in small cause suits are final, except for specific orders allowing appeal.
Suits by or against the Government must be instituted in the District Court.
Every Court may require oaths or affirmations.
No Judge or Munsiff shall try suits in which they are interested.
Law administered by Courts includes Mohammedan Law, Hindu Law, or custom, and in the absence of these, according to justice, equity, and good conscience.
Judges and Munsiffs must make a declaration of faithful performance of duties.
District Judges have general control over Civil Courts in their district.
