Civil Courts may be adjourned for a period not exceeding sixty days for summer and seventy days for festivals annually.
Appeals against decrees or orders of a District Court lie to the High Court, unless the amount or value does not exceed two thousand rupees.
Appeals from decrees or orders of District Munsiffs lie to the District Court.
The High Court shall report vacancies in the office of District Judge to Government.
The District Judge shall report vacancies in the office of Subordinate Judge, Judge of Small Cause Court, or District Munsiff to Government.

rights: Right to appeal against certain decisions.
Right to have cases heard according to justice, equity, and good conscience when specific laws or customs do not apply.
duties: Judges and Munsiffs must faithfully perform their duties.
Judges and Munsiffs must not try cases in which they are interested.
Courts must apply relevant laws (Mohammedan Law, Hindu Law, custom) or principles of justice, equity, and good conscience.
Courts must follow procedures outlined in the Code of Civil Procedure.
Appointed Judges and Munsiffs must make a declaration of their commitment to their duties.
District Judges have the duty of general control over Civil Courts in their district.
obligations: To adhere to the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
To conduct proceedings according to established laws and principles.

key_procedures: Plaints involving questions of title may be returned by Small Cause Courts to a court with jurisdiction to determine title.
Appeals from District Courts lie to the High Court, with exceptions based on the value of the subject matter.
Appeals from District Munsiffs lie to the District Court.
Proceedings of abolished courts continue.
Procedures in Small Cause Courts follow the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, with specific exceptions.
Reporting of vacancies in judicial offices to the Government.
administration: Government, High Court, and District Judges.
important_notes: The Act consolidates and amends existing law.
The Act came into force immediately upon enactment.
The Act applies to the entire State of Travancore-Cochin.
The Act specifies the hierarchy and jurisdiction of Civil Courts subordinate to the High Court.
Specific monetary limits are defined for the jurisdiction of different courts (e.g., Small Cause Courts, District Munsiffs).
The Act allows for the appointment of Additional District Judges.
The High Court has oversight over the functioning of Civil Courts.
The Government plays a role in fixing court numbers, local limits, and appointing judges.

title: The Travancore-Cochin Compensation for Tenants Improvements Act, 1956
purpose: To make provision for payment of compensation for improvements made by tenants in the State of Travancore-Cochin.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin. It pertains to tenants and improvements made by them on land.

key_definitions.improvement: Means any work or product of a work which adds to the value of the holding, is suitable to it and consistent with the purpose for which the holding is let, mortgaged or occupied, but does not include such clearance, embankments, dwellings, enclosures, temporary wells and water channels as are made by the tenant in the ordinary course of cultivation and without any special expenditure or any other benefit accruing to land from the ordinary operations of husbandry.
key_definitions.tenant: Means the "State of Travancore-Cochin" and contains expressions including a person who has taken, sub-lessee, mortgagee or sub-mortgagee or in good faith believes himself to be lessee, sub-lessee, mortgagee or sub-mortgagee of land, is in possession thereof, or who with the bona fide intention of returning and paying a reasonable rent to the person entitled to cultivate or let waste-land but without the permission of such person, brings such land under cultivation and is in occupation thereof as cultivator.
key_definitions.eviction: Means the recovery of possession of land from a tenant.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Compensation for Tenants -Improvements Act, 1956, it extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin, and it shall come into force at once.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including "improvement", "tenant", and "eviction".

main_sections.section_title: What are presumed to be improvements
main_sections.description: Specifies a list of works that are presumed to be improvements for the purposes of this Act, such as the erection of dwelling houses, construction of tanks, etc.

main_sections.section_title: Tenant entitled to compensation for improvements
main_sections.description: States that every tenant shall, on eviction, be entitled to compensation for improvements which were made by him, his predecessor-in-interest or any person not in occupation at the time of eviction who derived title from either of them and for which compensation had not already been paid, and every tenant to whom compensation is so due shall, notwithstanding the determination of the tenancy or the payment or tender of the mortgage money or premium, if any, be entitled to remain in possession until rejection in execution of a decree or order or count.

main_sections.section_title: Decree in eviction to be conditional on payment of compensation
main_sections.description: Details the procedure for determining and paying compensation when a tenant is evicted. The court ascertains the amount, and if it is found due under sections 7 to 16, the amount of compensation is paid to the plaintiff before the eviction decree is passed.

main_sections.section_title: Tenant's right to remove buildings, works or trees deemed not improvements
main_sections.description: Grants tenants the right to remove buildings, works or trees that are not considered improvements, provided they can be removed without substantial injury to the holding. The removal must be done within a time fixed by the court.

main_sections.section_title: Improvement producing an increase in the value of the annual net produce
main_sections.description: Deals with improvements that increase the annual net produce of the holding. The compensation is based on the average net money value of such increase, which is calculated as twenty times the net money value of the increased annual net produce.

States that the improvement consisting of trees or plants spontaneously grown during the period of the tenancy or lease is not an improvement, unless it consists of timber trees or other useful trees or plants, the compensation for which is three-fourths of the sum that the trees or plants might reasonably be expected to realize if sold by public auction.
Covers other types of improvements not specifically mentioned, where compensation is awarded to the cost of labour, supervision, etc., and materials.

main_sections.section_title: Value of improvement to be ascertained in the way most favourable to the tenant
main_sections.description: Mandates that the value of an improvement should be ascertained in the manner most favorable to the tenant.

main_sections.section_title: Improvement consisting in protection and maintenance of trees and plants
main_sections.description: Addresses compensation for the protection and maintenance of trees and plants. In such cases, the compensation shall be the proper cost of such protection and maintenance.

main_sections.section_title: Power to frame tables of maximum and minimum rates of compensation
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to prepare tables showing maximum and minimum rates of compensation for improvements, which shall not ordinarily exceed such rates.

main_sections.section_title: Power to prepare tables of prices of produce, etc.
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to prepare tables for the purpose of determining compensation, specifically for the price of produce. These tables, once published, are binding.

main_sections.section_title: Values how ascertained when no table has been prepared or presumption is rebutted
main_sections.description: Outlines how values are to be ascertained when no table is available or when a presumption is rebutted. The compensation is awarded at the average price, and the presumption can be rebutted.
States that tables prepared under this Act shall be published in the Gazette and kept publicly posted in Civil Courts.
Provides for compensation in cases of overplanting, with specific rates per acre for different types of trees.

main_sections.section_title: Contracts affecting compensation for improvements to be invalid
main_sections.description: Declares that any contract made by a tenant to make improvements and to relinquish his right to compensation for them shall be invalid. However, it also states that this does not affect any agreement in writing registered and made after the effectuating of the improvements setting the amount of compensation.
Repeals the Cochin Tenancy Act, XV of 1113.

important_rules: Improvements are presumed to be made for the purpose of cultivation or agricultural purposes.
Tenants are entitled to compensation for improvements made by them or their predecessors.
Compensation for improvements is conditional on payment.
Tenants have the right to remove buildings, works, or trees not deemed improvements, provided it doesn't cause injury to the holding.
The value of an improvement should be assessed in the manner most favorable to the tenant.
Contracts that waive a tenant's right to compensation for improvements are invalid, with exceptions for registered agreements.
Any contract made by a tenant to make improvements and relinquish his right to compensation is void.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through court decrees and orders concerning eviction and compensation payments.

rights: Right of the tenant to compensation for improvements.
Right of the tenant to remove certain structures/trees.
Right to remain in possession until compensation is paid.
Right to have the value of improvement ascertained in the most favorable way.
duties: Duty to make improvements suitable for the purpose of the holding.
Duty to not cause substantial injury to the holding when removing improvements.
obligations: Obligation of the landlord/person entitled to possession to pay compensation for improvements.
Obligation to follow court orders regarding compensation and eviction.

key_procedures: Eviction of a tenant is conditional on the payment of compensation for improvements.
The court ascertains the amount of compensation due.
If compensation is due, it is paid to the plaintiff before the eviction decree is executed.
When no table of prices is prepared or a presumption is rebutted, the value is ascertained based on average prices, and the presumption can be rebutted.
Tables of maximum and minimum rates of compensation and prices of produce are prepared and published by the Government.
administration: The Government of Travancore-Cochin (presumably through relevant departments like Revenue or Land Administration).
important_notes: The Act was promulgated by the President of India.
Republished in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 31st October, 1956.
The Cochin Tenancy Act, XV of 1113, is repealed by this Act.

title: The Travancore Cochin Cooperative Societies Act 1951
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to cooperative societies in Travancore-Cochin.
scope: Applies to cooperative societies registered or deemed to be registered under this Act.

key_definitions.society: Includes a registered society, a federal cooperative society, or a society deemed to be registered.
key_definitions.Registrar: Means the person appointed by the Government as the Registrar of Co-operative Societies, and includes any person on whom the powers of the Registrar have been conferred.
key_definitions.liquidator: Includes any person appointed to liquidate the affairs of a society.

main_sections.description: Details the powers of a liquidator appointed under Section 51 or Section 52, including the power to sue and be sued, to pay debts, to compromise claims, to call for monies due, and to carry on the business of the society.

main_sections.section_title: Saving so far as is expressly provided in this Act
main_sections.description: States that no civil court shall have cognizance of any matter connected with the winding up or dissolution of a society under this Act, except as provided.
Explains how surplus assets of a society after winding up are to be disposed of, potentially to another new society or for charitable purposes.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Registrar to assess damages against promoters, etc.
main_sections.description: Gives the Registrar the power to assess damages against promoters, officers, or members who have misapplied or become liable for any money or property of the society.
Details the circumstances under which the Registrar can attach the property of a liquidator or any other person and the conditions for such attachment.
Provides for the reference of disputes touching the business of a registered society to arbitration.
Deals with the finality of orders passed by the Registrar or arbitrator under various sections, and the conditions under which they can be challenged in a civil court.
Grants the Registrar or persons authorized by him the power to enforce attendance of witnesses and compel the production of documents in inquiries and proceedings.
Specifies the methods by which money ordered to be paid by a liquidator or arbitrator can be recovered, including as a decree of a civil court.

important_rules: Managing committee reconstruction is subject to Registrar's approval.
Action against a society requires Registrar's permission.
Liquidation orders can be passed by the Registrar if a society is unable to pay its debts.
Disputes involving a registered society can be referred to arbitration.

penalties: Criminal liability for certain offences.
Recovery of money as a decree of a civil court.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Registrar of Co-operative Societies
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inquiries, orders, assessment of damages, attachment of property, and recovery as civil court decrees.

rights: Right to appeal against certain orders of the Registrar.
Right to question the Registrar's decision regarding attachment of property.
duties: Duty of managing committee to reconstruct.
Duty of liquidator to manage affairs and realize assets.
Duty to deposit records with the Registrar upon winding up.
obligations: Obligation to comply with orders of the Registrar and arbitrator.

key_procedures: Procedure for reconstruction of managing committee.
Procedure for winding up of a society.
Procedure for arbitration of disputes.
Procedure for recovery of money.
Procedure for attachment of property.
administration: Co-operative Department (inferred)
important_notes: Appeals against orders of the Registrar must be filed within two months of the communication of the order.
The Act consolidates and amends the law relating to cooperative societies.
The provisions regarding the winding up and dissolution of societies are detailed.

title: The Travancore Cochin Court Fees (Amendment) Act, 1956
purpose: To amend the Travancore-Cochin Court Fees Act, 1125.
scope: Applies to court fees in Travancore-Cochin.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Court Fees (Amendment) Act, 1956, and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Schedule II to Act II of 1125.
main_sections.description: Amends Article 1 of Schedule II to the Travancore-Cochin Court Fees Act, 1125. It inserts words in clause (a) and substitutes a clause (d) in its entirety. The substituted clause (d) specifies court fees for different types of directions, orders, or writs, including those under Article 226 and Article 227 of the Constitution, and for any other case.

important_rules: Court fees for directions, orders, or writs under Article 226 of the Constitution, other than the writ of habeascorpus: Twenty-five rupees.
Court fees for directions, orders, or writs under Article 227 of the Constitution: Twenty-five rupees.
Court fees for any other case: Two rupees.
key_procedures: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Government through a Gazette notification.
Specific court fees are to be paid for various legal documents and actions as outlined in the amended Schedule II.
important_notes: The amendment is made to the Travancore-Cochin Court Fees Act, 1125 (Act II of 1125).
The amendment was enacted in the Seventh Year of the Republic of India.
Published to the Gazette Extraordinary dated 17th March 1956.

title: The Travancore-Cochin Criminal Procedure (Temporary Provisions) Act
purpose: To amend the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (Central Act V of 1898) in its application to the State of Travancore-Cochin.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin. Provisions continue to apply to any proceeding pending before a Court of Sessions immediately before the expiry of the Act, and all such proceedings shall be heard and determined as if the Act were still in force.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, commencement and duration.
main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Criminal Procedure (Temporary Provisions) Act, 1951. It extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin. It shall come into force at once and shall remain in force for a period of six months.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure regarding trials before Court of Session.
main_sections.description: For so long as this Act is in force, nothing in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 shall be deemed to require trials before a Court of Session to be by Jury or with the aid of assessors, and notwithstanding any of the provisions of that Code, such trials shall be held in the same manner and in accordance with the same procedure as obtained under the law in force immediately before the 1st day of April 1951.

The Travancore-Cochin Criminal Procedure (Temporary Provisions) Ordinance, 1951 (III of 1951) is hereby repealed. The repeal by this Act of the said Ordinance shall not affect the previous operation thereof, and any order, made, action taken, or thing done in the exercise of any powers conferred by or under the said Ordinance shall for all purposes be deemed to have been made, taken or done in exercise of powers conferred by this Act as if this Act had commenced on the 1st day of April 1951.

important_rules: Trials before a Court of Session shall not be by Jury or with the aid of assessors for the duration of this Act.
Trials shall be held in the same manner and in accordance with the same procedure as obtained under the law in force immediately before April 1, 1951.
key_procedures: Trials before a Court of Session are to be conducted without a Jury or assessors, adhering to the procedure in place before April 1, 1951.
important_notes: The Act is temporary and in force for six months.
Proceedings pending before a Court of Sessions before the expiry of the Act will continue to be dealt with as if the Act were still in force.
The repeal of the Ordinance III of 1951 does not invalidate past actions taken under it.

title: The Travancore Cochin Easements Act
purpose: To define and regulate the law relating to easements and licenses.
scope: Applies to the territories of Travancore and Cochin concerning easements and licenses.

main_sections.description: The dominant owner must exercise the right in the mode which is least onerous to the servient owner, and when the exercise of an easement can without detriment to the dominant owner be confined to a determinate part of the servient heritage, such exercise shall at the request of the servient owner be so confined.

main_sections.section_title: Subject to the provisions of Section 22, the dominant owner may, from time to time, alter the mode and place of enjoyment of right of way.
main_sections.description: The dominant owner may alter the mode and place of enjoyment of a right of way, provided that this does not impose any additional burden on the servient heritage. The dominant owner of a right of way cannot vary its line of passage at pleasure, even though he does not thereby impose any additional burden on the servient heritage.

main_sections.section_title: Dominant owner entitled to full enjoyment of easement.
main_sections.description: The dominant owner is entitled to the full enjoyment of the easement, but such acts must be done at such time and in such manner as without detriment to the dominant owner's right to cause inconvenience if possible. The dominant owner must repair, as far as practicable, the damage caused by the act to the servient heritage.

main_sections.section_title: Expenses incurred in constructing or making necessary for preservation of easement.
main_sections.description: Expenses incurred in constructing or making necessary for the preservation of an easement shall be defrayed by the dominant owner.

main_sections.section_title: Liability for damage from want of repair.
main_sections.description: When an easement is enjoyed by means of an artificial work, the dominant owner is liable to compensation for any damage to the servient heritage arising from the want of repair of such work.

main_sections.section_title: Servient owner not bound to do anything for enjoyment of easement.
main_sections.description: The servient owner is not bound to do anything for the enjoyment of the dominant heritage, and he is entitled, as against the dominant owner, to use the servient heritage in any way consistent with the enjoyment of the easement; but he must not do any act tending to restrict or render its exercise less convenient.

main_sections.section_title: Extent of easements and the mode of their enjoyment.
main_sections.description: The provisions of the following sections shall take effect as to the extent of easements and the mode of their enjoyment.

main_sections.section_title: Dominant owner cannot alter or substantially increase appropriation of easement.
main_sections.description: The dominant owner cannot, by merely altering or adding to the dominant heritage, substantially increase the appropriation of an easement. Where an easement has been granted or bequeathed so that its extent shall be proportionate to the extent of the dominant heritage, if the dominant heritage is increased by alluvion, the easement is proportionately increased, and if the dominant heritage is diminished by alluvion, the easement is proportionately diminished. Save as aforesaid, no easement is affected by any change in the extent of the dominant or the servient heritage.

Where dominant heritage is divided between two or more persons, the easement annexed to such heritage is divided to each of the shares, but not so as to impose substantially the burden on the servient heritage: provided that such annexation is consistent with the terms of the instrument, decree or reversing proceeding (if any) under which the division was made, and in the case of prescriptive rights, with the user during the prescriptive period.

main_sections.section_title: Obstructing in cases of excuse to user.
main_sections.description: In the case of excessive user of an easement the servient owner may, without prejudice to any other remedy, without prejudice to any other remedy, obstruct the user, but only on the servient heritage; provided that such user cannot be obstructed when the one-terfere with the lawful enjoyment of the easement.
The owner or occupier of the dominant heritage is entitled to enjoy the easement without disturbance by any other person.

The owner of any interest in the dominant heritage, or the occupier of such heritage, may institute a suit for compensation for the disturbance of the easement or of any right appurtenant thereto: provided that the disturbance has actually caused substantial damage to the plaintiff.

main_sections.section_title: When cause of action arises for removal of support.
main_sections.description: The removal of means of support to which a dominant owner is entitled does not give rise to a right to recover compensation, unless and until substantial damage is actually sustained.

main_sections.section_title: Injunction to restrain disturbance of easement.
main_sections.description: Subject to the provisions of the Specific Relief Act for the time being in force relating to preventive relief, an injunction may be granted to restrain the disturbance of an easement. If the easement is actually disturbed – when compensation for such disturbance might be recovered under this Act – when the act threatened or intended necessarily, if performed, disturbs the easement.

main_sections.section_title: Abatement of wrongful obstruction of easement.
main_sections.description: Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 24, the dominant owner cannot himself abate a wrongful obstruction of an easement.

main_sections.section_title: Extinction by disclaimer of servient owner.
main_sections.description: When from a cause which preceded the imposition of an easement, the person by whom it was imposed ceases to have any right to the servient heritage, the easement is extinguished. Nothing in this Section applies to an easement lawfully imposed by a mortgagee in accordance with Section 10.

An easement is extinguished when the dominant owner releases it, expressly or impliedly, to the servient owner. Such release can be made only in the circumstances and to the extent to which the dominant owner can alienate the dominant heritage. An easement may be released as to part only of the servient heritage.
An easement is extinguished when the servient owner, in exercise of a power reserved in this behalf, revokes the easement.

main_sections.section_title: Extinction by limited period or condition.
main_sections.description: An easement is extinguished where it has been imposed for a limited period, or acquired on condition that it shall become void on the performance or non-performance of a specified act and the period expires or the condition is fulfilled.
An easement of necessity is extinguished when the necessity comes to an end.

important_rules: A dominant owner must exercise an easement in a mode that is least onerous to the servient owner.
If an easement can be confined to a specific part of the servient heritage without detriment, it should be done at the request of the servient owner.
A dominant owner can alter the mode and place of enjoyment of a right of way, provided it doesn't increase the burden on the servient heritage.
A riparian owner, as against lower riparian owners, must not pollute a stream by throwing saw dust into it.

A servient owner is not obligated to do anything for the enjoyment of an easement and can use their heritage in any way consistent with the easement's enjoyment, provided it doesn't restrict the easement's exercise.
An easement is extinguished if the dominant owner releases it, expressly or impliedly.
An easement can be extinguished if the servient owner revokes it, given a reserved power.
An easement imposed for a limited period or on a condition is extinguished when that period expires or the condition is fulfilled.
An easement of necessity is extinguished when the necessity ceases to exist.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts (through injunctions and damages)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through suits for injunctions to restrain disturbance and for compensation for damages.

rights: Right to the full enjoyment of an easement without disturbance.
Right to alter the mode and place of enjoyment of a right of way, provided no additional burden is imposed on the servient heritage.
Right to necessary acts for the preservation of an easement.
Right to sue for compensation for disturbance of an easement.
Right to an injunction to restrain the disturbance of an easement.
Right to sue for removal of substantial damage caused by disturbance of easement.
Right to extinguish an easement by release or if the necessity ceases.
Right to enjoy the benefit of an easement of necessity.
duties: Duty to exercise an easement in the least onerous mode for the servient owner.
Duty to repair damage caused to the servient heritage as a result of exercising an easement.
Duty not to impose additional burden on the servient heritage when altering the mode of enjoyment of a right of way.
Duty not to abate a wrongful obstruction of an easement.
Duty to ensure that any act tending to restrict or render the exercise of an easement less convenient is not done.
obligations: Obligation to compensate for damage to the servient heritage arising from the want of repair of an artificial work used for an easement.
Obligation to ensure that the exercise of an easement does not interfere with the lawful enjoyment of the servient heritage.

key_procedures: To obtain an injunction against disturbance of an easement, a suit must be filed, demonstrating actual or threatened disturbance that would necessarily result in disturbance.
To recover compensation for disturbance of an easement, a suit must be filed, proving that substantial damage has actually been sustained.
When an easement is enjoyed by means of an artificial work, the dominant owner is liable to compensate the servient owner for damages resulting from the want of repair of that work.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but likely falls under the general judicial administration for civil matters.
important_notes: Illustrations are provided for various sections to clarify their application.
Prescriptive rights are considered when assessing the mode and extent of easement enjoyment.
The provisions of the Specific Relief Act are applicable regarding preventive relief for easements.
Easements of necessity are extinguished when the necessity ceases to exist.
The extent of a prescriptive right to pollute water or air is determined by the pollution that occurred during the period of its acquisition.
An easement is extinguished if the servient heritage is lawfully imposed upon by a mortgagee under Section 10, unless otherwise specified.

title: The Travancore Cochin Electricity Supply Surcharge (Repeal) Act, 1971
purpose: To repeal The Travancore-Cochin Electricity Supply Surcharge Act, 1955.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and concerns electricity supply surcharges collected by the Kerala State Electricity Board.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Electricity Supply Surcharge (Repeal) Act, 1971. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1968.
The Travancore-Cochin Electricity Supply Surcharge Act, 1955 (14 of 1955) is hereby repealed.

main_sections.section_title: Assignment of arrears to the Board
main_sections.description: Any amount of surcharge collected by the Kerala State Electricity Board and payable to the Government and any arrears of surcharge recoverable under or by virtue of the provisions of the Act, shall be credited, or shall be recovered and credited, as the case may be, in the revenue accounts of the said Board as if they were the revenue accruing to that Board, notwithstanding anything contained in the Act so repealed.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Kerala State Electricity Board and the Government of Kerala.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Surcharge amounts collected and arrears are to be credited or recovered into the revenue accounts of the Board.

key_procedures: The repeal of the 1955 Act comes into effect retroactively from April 1, 1968.
All surcharge amounts collected and any arrears are to be treated as revenue for the Kerala State Electricity Board.
administration: Kerala State Electricity Board and the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 488, dated 9th November, 1971.

title: THE TRAVANCORE COCHIN ELECTRICITY SUPPLY SURCHARGE ACT, 1955
purpose: An Act to authorise the levy and collection of a surcharge on the price of all supplies of energy made by the Government or by a licensee.
scope: The Act applies to the State of Travancore-Cochin and covers the levy and collection of a surcharge on the price of all supplies of energy made by the Government or by a licensee. It also applies to persons including a company or a local authority licensed under Part II of the Indian Electricity Act, 1910, and to any person carrying on a company or a local authority who has obtained the sanction of the Government to supply or distribute electrical energy under Part III of the aforesaid Act.

key_definitions.licensee: means any person including a company or a local authority licensed under Part II of the Indian Electricity Act, 1910 (Central Act IX of 1910), to supply electrical energy or any person carrying on a company or a local authority who has obtained the sanction of the Government to supply or distribute electrical energy under Part III of the aforesaid Act.
key_definitions.supply of energy for domestic and genera: means supply of energy for the following purposes — (i) lighting and combined installation of lights and fans (radio and photography included); (ii) public lamps.
key_definitions.supply of energy for industrial purposes: means supply of energy for the following purposes — (i) cinematograph installations (light, fans and power); (ii) temporary illuminations and display lighting; and (iii) industrial and agricultural use.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Electricity Supply Surcharge Act, 1955. It extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin. It shall come into force at once.
Defines terms used in the Act, including 'energy', 'licensee', 'supply of energy for domestic and general purposes', and 'supply of energy for industrial purposes'.

Specifies the rates at which surcharge is levied on the price of energy supplied for domestic and general purposes (12.5 per cent) and for industrial purposes (20 per cent). It also outlines special rates for certain industrial purposes under specific conditions.

Details how the surcharge is collected by the Electricity Department of the Government or by a licensee, and specifies that all licensees shall pay to the Government every month all amounts collected by them, retaining a small percentage for themselves.
States that all amounts due to the Government under the Act are recoverable as arrears of land revenue.

main_sections.section_title: Licensee not to supply energy without realising surcharge
main_sections.description: Prohibits licensees from supplying energy for domestic, general, industrial, or agricultural purposes without realizing the surcharge.
Prescribes a penalty for contravention of Section 6, which may extend to five hundred rupees.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of Act on contracts for supply of energy
main_sections.description: Clarifies that the provisions of the Act do not affect any contract for the supply or distribution of energy in any law for the time being in force.

Repeals the Travancore-Cochin Electric Supply Surcharge Order, 1950, and the Travancore-Cochin Electric Supply Surcharge Order, 1950, issued under the Cochin Essential Articles Control and Requisitioning Powers Act, VIII of 1922. It also states that amounts due and unrecovered under the repealed provisions shall be recovered under the current Act.

important_rules: Licensees must realize and collect surcharge on the price of energy supplied.
Licensees are prohibited from supplying energy for domestic, general, industrial, or agricultural purposes without realizing the surcharge.
All collected surcharge amounts must be paid to the Government every month, with licensees retaining 1 per cent for their efforts.
Amounts due under the Act are recoverable as arrears of land revenue.

penalties: Penalty for contravention of Section 6: fine which may extend to five hundred rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Electricity Department of the Government and licensees (for collection and remittance).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through realization and remittance of surcharge by licensees, and through penalties for non-compliance with the prohibition on supplying energy without surcharge.

rights: The Government has the right to levy and collect a surcharge on the price of energy.
duties: Licensees have the duty to realize and collect the surcharge.
Licensees have the duty to remit collected surcharge amounts to the Government monthly.
Licensees have the duty to not supply energy without realizing the surcharge.

key_procedures: Levy surcharge at specified rates for different purposes of energy supply.
Licensees collect the surcharge from consumers at the point of sale of energy.
Licensees remit the collected surcharge to the Government monthly, retaining a small percentage for their service.
The Government recovers any due amounts as arrears of land revenue.
administration: The Electricity Department of the Government.
important_notes: The surcharge rates differ for domestic/general purposes and industrial purposes.

Special surcharge rates apply for industrial purposes concerning lighting and combined installation of lights and fans, if such excess were supplies of energy for lighting and combined installation for lights and fans.
The Act repeals previous orders related to electricity supply surcharge and savings provisions ensure continuity of recovery for dues under the repealed orders.

title: The Travancore-Cochin Entertainments Tax (Validation of Levy and Collection) Act, 1955
purpose: To validate the levy and collection of entertainments tax made by local authorities in the State of Travancore-Cochin on and from the 1st day of December, 1951.
scope: Applies to the State of Travancore-Cochin, validating actions taken by local authorities regarding the levy and collection of entertainments tax.

key_definitions.entertainment: Means the same as assigned in the Travancore-Cochin Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1951.
key_definitions.local authority: Means the same as assigned in the Travancore-Cochin Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1951.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Entertainments Tax (Validation of Levy and Collection) Act, 1955, and shall come into force at once.
Defines 'entertainment' and 'local authority' by referencing the Travancore-Cochin Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1951.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of levy and collection of entertainments tax made by local authorities
main_sections.description: Validates all levies and collections of entertainments tax by local authorities under Section 12 of the Travancore-Cochin Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1951, regardless of whether bye-laws have been made, or if the levy and collection are based on bye-laws. It also states that such levies and collections shall not be deemed invalid or ineffective due to any such reason.

important_rules: All orders and action taken by local authorities in connection with the levy or collection of entertainments tax, or in the exercise of jurisdiction or powers conferred by or under any law, are hereby declared to have been validly made, passed or taken.

Any judgment, order or decree pronounced or passed by any Court on the ground that a local authority has not made bye-laws under Section 12 of the Travancore-Cochin Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1951, shall be void and of no effect.

penalties: Provided that no act or omission on the part of any person shall be punishable as an offence which would not have been so punishable if this Act had not been passed.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Local authorities
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the levy and collection of entertainments tax, and exercise of jurisdiction or powers conferred by law.

key_procedures: Levy and collection of entertainments tax by local authorities.
Validation of past actions related to levy and collection.
administration: Local authorities in the State of Travancore-Cochin.
important_notes: The Act is enacted in the Sixth Year of the Republic of India.
The Act commenced and came into force immediately upon its enactment.
The Act specifically addresses and validates actions taken prior to its enactment, ensuring continuity and legality.
The Act aims to cure any potential defect in the levy and collection of entertainments tax arising from the absence or inadequacy of bye-laws.

title: The Travancore-Cochin Fisheries Act
purpose: To make provisions relating to fisheries in the State of Travancore-Cochin.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin and shall come into force at once.

key_definitions.fixed engine: means any net, cage, trap or other contrivance for taking fish, fixed in the soil or made stationary in any other way.
key_definitions.private water: means water which is the exclusive property of any person in which any person has for the time being an exclusive right of fishery, whether as owner, lessee or in any other capacity.
key_definitions.explanation_water: Water shall not cease to be 'private water' within the meaning of this definition, by reason only that other persons may have by custom a right of fishery therein.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Travancore-Cochin Fisheries Act, 1950, its extent to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin, and that it comes into force at once.
Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'Fish', 'Fixed engine', and 'Private water'.
Empowers the Government to notify a close time by notification in the Gazette, during which it shall be unlawful to capture fish in any specified water area.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of fish in selected waters by rules passed by Government
main_sections.description: Grants the Government power to make rules for the protection of fish in selected waters, including restrictions on fishing, sale, or barter of fish killed in contravention of such rules. It also covers rules regarding fixed engines, the size of fish, and destruction of fisheries.

main_sections.section_title: Offering or exposing for sale or barter any fish killed in contravention of rules under Section 4
main_sections.description: Prohibits the offering or exposing for sale or barter of any fish killed in contravention of rules made under Section 4. Penalties are prescribed for such contraventions.
Specifies penalties for contravention of rules made under Section 4 and Section 3. It also deals with the forfeiture of any fishing gear used in contravention.

main_sections.section_title: Destruction of fish by explosives in inland waters and on coasts
main_sections.description: Prohibits the use of dynamite or other explosive substance for the destruction of fish in any water, inland or on the coast. Penalties are specified for contravention.

main_sections.section_title: Destruction of fish by poisoning waters
main_sections.description: Prohibits the use of poison or noxious material to destroy fish in any water. Penalties are prescribed for contravention.
Empowers the Government to grant licenses, subject to terms and conditions, for various purposes, including fishing in private waters and the sale or barter of fish.
Outlines the grounds for cancellation of a license, including contravention of terms and conditions, or the holder being convicted of an offence against the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Period of and fees for license
main_sections.description: Specifies that licenses are transferable and renewable for a period not exceeding one year, subject to payment of fees and conditions. It also allows for free licenses in certain circumstances.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of license holders to produce license
main_sections.description: Mandates that every holder of a license shall be bound to produce their license for inspection by any Police Officer or other authorized person.

main_sections.section_title: Whoever, having been already convicted of an offence under this Act
main_sections.description: Provides for enhanced penalties for subsequent convictions of offences under the Act.

States that if any person is convicted of an offence under this Act, any fish in respect of which the offence has been committed, and any instruments used in the commission of the offence, shall be confiscated.

main_sections.section_title: Presumption of commission of certain offences
main_sections.description: Establishes a presumption that if fish is found with instruments for capturing it, the holder is presumed to have committed an offence.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of Court as regards cancellation of license
main_sections.description: Requires that when a person is convicted of an offence, the Court shall send a copy of its judgment to the licensing authority to cancel the license.

main_sections.section_title: Power of seizure as to offence committed in presence of certain officers and persons
main_sections.description: Grants powers to Police Officers and other authorized persons to arrest and seize any person committing an offence in their presence, or whom they reasonably suspect of having committed an offence.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, which may include provisions for the granting of licenses, fees, and other matters.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to concede right of taking certain imported fish to club or associations
main_sections.description: Allows the Government to make arrangements for preserving and protecting fish by granting rights to clubs or associations for capturing or preserving fish in any water, subject to their approval and regulation.

main_sections.section_title: Fishing without license in conceded waters
main_sections.description: Prohibits fishing without a license in waters where the Government has conceded fishing rights to clubs or associations, or in waters under special rules.
Grants power to Police Officers to arrest any person without a warrant if they commit an offence under the Act, or if they are reasonably suspected of having committed an offence.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition against attracting prawns into private waters except under a license
main_sections.description: Prohibits the attraction of prawns into private waters except under a license, and specifies penalties for contravention. It also allows the Government to make rules regarding the fees and conditions for such licenses.

main_sections.section_title: Power to apply provisions of Act to shells of fish
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to apply the provisions of the Act to the collection of shells of fish.
Repeals the Travancore Fisheries Act, XI of 1907 and the Cochin Fisheries Act, III of 1902, with a saving clause for acts done or granted under the repealed Acts.

important_rules: No person shall destroy fish by dynamite or other explosive substance in any water.
No person shall destroy fish by poisoning waters.
No person shall offer or expose for sale or barter any fish killed in contravention of rules made under Section 4.
Fishing without a license is prohibited in waters where the Government has conceded fishing rights to clubs or associations, or under special rules.
Attracting prawns into private waters is prohibited except under a license.

penalties: For contravention of rules under Section 4 or Section 3, a penalty up to one hundred rupees.
For destruction of fish by explosives or poison, a term which may extend to two months or with fine which may extend to two hundred rupees, or both.
For offering or exposing for sale or barter fish killed in contravention of rules under Section 4, a penalty up to fifty rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Police Officers and other persons authorized by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through arrest, seizure of fish and instruments, imposition of fines, and cancellation of licenses.

rights: License holders have the right to fish under the terms of their license.
The Government has the right to grant licenses and make rules for fisheries.
duties: License holders have the duty to produce their license for inspection.
Persons are under a duty to comply with the rules and provisions of the Act.
obligations: Obligation to not destroy fish by explosives or poison.
Obligation to not sell or barter fish obtained in contravention of rules.

key_procedures: Application for and grant of licenses for fishing or other related activities.
Notification of close times for fishing.
Seizure of offending persons and articles.
Cancellation of licenses for offences.
Application of Act provisions to shell fish.
administration: The Government of Travancore-Cochin (as inferred from the context of the Act being passed by the Legislative Assembly and assented to by His Highness the Raj Pramukh).
important_notes: The Act repeals the Travancore Fisheries Act, XI of 1907, and the Cochin Fisheries Act, III of 1902.
The Government can exempt any person from taking out a license in the interests of scientific research or for other causes.
Rules made under the Act can be applied to shells of fish.
The Act includes provisions for the confiscation of fish and instruments used in the commission of an offence.

title: THE TRAVANCORE-COCHIN FOREST (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1957
purpose: To amend the Travancore-Cochin Forest Act, 1951.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala, excluding the Malabar district referred to in sub-section (2) of section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.

key_definitions.forest produce: Includes trees and leaves, flowers and fruits and all other parts or produce of trees; plants not being trees (including grass, creepers, reeds and moss) and all other parts or produce of such plants; wild animals and skins, tusks, horns, bones, silk cocoons, honey and wax and all other parts or produce of animals; peat, surface oil, rock and minerals (including limestone and laterite), mineral oils and all produce of mines and minerals.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Forest (Amendment) Act, 1957. It shall come into force at once.
Amends Section 1 of the Travancore-Cochin Forest Act, 1951 (Act III of 1951) to extend its application to the whole of Kerala, excluding the Malabar district.
Substitutes a new clause (e) in Section 2 of the principal Act, defining "Forest Produce" to include specific items like trees, plants, wild animals, peat, surface oil, rock and minerals, etc.
Omits Chapter VIII of the principal Act.
Amends Section 93 of the principal Act by adding a sub-section (2).

In Section 99 of the principal Act, the words "timber and found" shall be omitted. Also, in clause (d), the words "belonging to or" occurring between the words "but grown on lands" and "in the occupation of private persons" shall be omitted. A new clause (dd) is inserted to regulate or prohibit the felling, lopping, cutting, maiming or otherwise maltreating of trees standing on land temporarily or permanently assigned, the right of the Government over which has been expressly reserved in the deed of grant or assignment of such land.

main_sections.section_title: Saving of operation of sections 55 to 65
main_sections.description: The repeal of sections 55 to 65 of the principal Act shall not affect the operation of the said sections or respects: (i) the rights of the Government over trees which are royalties and which have been felled before the commencement of this Act; (ii) the preferring of claims to kudivila in pursuance of a notice under section 65 issued before the commencement of this Act; (iii) the inquiry into claims for kudivila preferred either before or after the commencement of this Act; and (iv) the powers of the Forest Officer, the District Court or the High Court, to pass awards or to modify or reverse such awards on reference or on appeal, and any such rights, claims, inquiries, and powers may be enforced, preferred, conducted or exercised as if the said sections have not been repealed.

rights: Government's rights over trees which are royalties and felled before the commencement of this Act.
Right to prefer claims to kudivila in pursuance of a notice under section 65.
Right to inquiry into claims for kudivila.
Powers of Forest Officer, District Court or High Court to pass awards or modify/reverse awards on reference or appeal.

key_procedures: Submitting claims to kudivila in pursuance of a notice under section 65.
Inquiring into claims for kudivila.
Awards passed by Forest Officer, District Court or High Court may be enforced as if sections 55 to 65 had not been repealed.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Travancore-Cochin Forest Act, 1951.
The amendment extends the application of the Act to the entire State of Kerala except the Malabar district.
The definition of 'Forest Produce' is expanded.
Chapter VIII of the principal Act is omitted.
Saving provisions exist for actions taken under repealed sections 55 to 65 prior to this amendment.

title: The Travancore Cochin Forest Act, 1951
purpose: To provide for the control and management of forests, timber, and other forest produce within the territories of Travancore-Cochin.
scope: Applies to all forest land and forest produce within the State of Travancore-Cochin. It also covers the movement of timber and other forest products and the collection of drift and stranded timber.

key_definitions.forest: Includes forest land, trees, timber, and any other produce obtained from forests.
key_definitions.timber: Includes wood of any kind and includes trees, logs, beams, planks, firewood, charcoal, and other forest produce.

main_sections.section_title: Compulsory acquisition of forest land by Government
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to acquire forest land for public purposes, making compensation in accordance with the Land Acquisition Act.
Deals with the protection of forests by the owner or the Government, including the right to form conservation trusts for forests and the management of such forests.

main_sections.section_title: Management of forests and waste lands
main_sections.description: Allows the Government to take over the management of any forest or waste land, either for its own purposes or jointly with the owner, and to issue rules for its management.
Empowers the Government to appoint Forest Officers to carry out the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Control of timber and other forest products in transit
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to make rules to regulate the transit of all timber or of certain classes of timber within local limits, including routes of import and export, and prohibition of timber without a pass.
Deals with timber in transit and the requirement of inspection by a Magistrate or Forest Officer.

main_sections.section_title: Collection of drift and stranded timber
main_sections.description: Provides for the collection and disposal of drift and stranded timber, including rules for its registration and claiming by owners.
Prohibits killing, wounding, or capturing of wild elephants in any place within the State without the sanction of the Government.
States that tusks and teeth of elephants killed or captured shall be delivered to the nearest Forest or Police Officer.
Allows the Government to grant permits for the shooting or capturing of wild elephants.

main_sections.section_title: Rules regarding killing or wounding of wild elephants
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to make rules regulating the killing or wounding of any wild elephant in defence of person or property.
Deals with royalties on trees and forest produce, stating that certain trees and forest produce are the property of the Government unless granted otherwise.

main_sections.section_title: Notice of agency to cut and remove royalty trees
main_sections.description: Requires notice to be given to the registered holder of land before cutting or removing royalty trees from private lands.

main_sections.section_title: Joint mahazar for removal of trees
main_sections.description: Prescribes the procedure for a joint mahazar to be prepared by a Forest Officer in conjunction with the local Provertihear and the owner or authorized agent for the removal of trees.
Requires notice to be published calling for claims for kudivilla (a type of forest produce).

main_sections.section_title: Inquiry by Forest Officer into claims for Kudivilla
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for the Forest Officer to inquire into claims for kudivilla.

important_rules: Rule: Any owner of forest land who declines to comply with regulations may have such lands acquired by the Government upon payment of compensation.
Rule: The Government may make rules to regulate the transit of timber, including routes of import and export, prohibition of timber without a pass, and methods of examination and marking.
Rule: Wild elephants cannot be killed, wounded, or captured without the sanction of the Government.
Rule: Tusks and teeth of wild elephants killed or captured must be delivered to the Forest or Police Officer.
Rule: Royalties are payable to the Government on certain specified trees and forest produce.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or both (for contravention of rules under Section 38).
Imprisonment which may extend to one month or fine which may extend to one hundred rupees, or both (for contravention of Section 40).
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or both (for contravention of rules under Section 46).
Imprisonment which may extend to six months or fine or both for each animal (for killing or wounding wild elephants outside defence of person or property).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Forest Officers, Magistrates, Police Officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, seizures, imposition of fines, and imprisonment. Government can also acquire forest land. Rules are enforced through notification and compliance with prescribed procedures.

rights: Right of landowners to compensation for acquired forest land.
Right to obtain permits for shooting wild elephants.
Right to claim ownership of drift and stranded timber upon proof.
Right to remove royalty trees after proper notice and procedure.
duties: Duty of owners to comply with forest regulations.
Duty to deliver tusks and teeth of wild elephants to authorities.
Duty to obtain permits for shooting or capturing wild elephants.
Duty to follow prescribed procedures for removal of trees and claims.
obligations: Obligation to pay royalties on specified forest produce.

key_procedures: Procedure for Government to acquire forest land: notification, payment of compensation.
Procedure for regulating timber transit: obtaining passes, following prescribed routes, examination.
Procedure for claiming drift and stranded timber: notice to claimants, inquiry, delivery upon proof.
Procedure for removing royalty trees: joint mahazar, notice to registered holder.
Procedure for inquiry into claims for kudivilla: by Forest Officer as per Civil Procedure Code.
administration: Forest Department of the Government of Travancore-Cochin.
important_notes: Section 48 of the Act is referred to for exceptions regarding the operation of wild elephant shooting permits.
The Act supersedes previous proclamations and declarations regarding forests and forest produce.
Rules made under the Act must be published in the Gazette.
Compensation for damage caused by river obstruction or removal is provided for under Section 38(i).
Timber marked in a particular manner is considered property of the Government unless proven otherwise.

title: The Travancore Cochin General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 1956
purpose: To further amend The Travancore-Cochin General Sales-tax Act, 1125 (Act XI of 1925).
scope: Applies to the territory of Travancore-Cochin.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called The Travancore-Cochin General Sales-tax (Amendment) Act, 1956, and it shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 3, Act XI of 1125
main_sections.description: Amends Section 3 of the principal Act. It inserts a new sub-section after sub-section (1) of Section 3. This new sub-section specifies that a dealer shall pay the sum demanded within such time as may be fixed by the authority. It also substitutes the expression "sub-sections (1), (1A) and (2)" for "sub-sections (1) and (2)" in sub-section (5).
States that the principal Act shall be read and construed as if the amendments made by Section 2 had formed part of the principal Act from its commencement.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be the authority mentioned in Section 2.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Implied through the demand and payment of sums by dealers.

duties: Dealers have the duty to pay the sum demanded within the time fixed by the authority.

key_procedures: The amendment to Section 3 requires dealers to pay demanded sums within a stipulated time.
The substitution of expression in sub-section (5) of Section 3 of the principal Act.
administration: Implied to be the sales tax administration of the Travancore-Cochin state.
important_notes: The amendment has retrospective effect from the commencement of the principal Act.
The Act amends The Travancore-Cochin General Sales-tax Act, 1125.

title: THE TRAVANCORE COCHIN GENERAL SALES TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1957
purpose: To further amend the Travancore-Cochin General Sales Tax Act, 1951, for the purpose of expunging the provisions thereof to the whole State of Kerala and for certain other purposes.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 1957. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Preamble, Act XI of 1925
main_sections.description: Amends the Preamble to the Travancore-Cochin General Sales Tax Act, 1125 (Act XI of 1125) by substituting the words 'State of Travancore-Cochin' with 'State of Kerala'.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 1, Act XI of 1125
main_sections.description: Amends section 1 of the principal Act by substituting the words 'Travancore-Cochin General Sales Tax Act' with 'General Sales Tax Act'.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 2, Act XI of 1125
main_sections.description: Amends section 2 of the principal Act. It specifies amendments to various sub-sections and clauses, including the omission of 'cinchona' and substitution of 'State of Travancore-Cochin' with 'State' where they occur.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 2B, Act XI of 1125
main_sections.description: Introduces a new section 2B concerning the appointment of Deputy Commissioners of Sales Tax. The Government may appoint one or more Deputy Commissioners for the purpose of performing functions conferred on the Deputy Commissioner, or under this Act. The Deputy Commissioner or Deputy Commissioners so appointed shall perform such functions within such local limits as the Government may assign to them.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 3, Act XI of 1125
main_sections.description: Amends section 3 of the principal Act. It provides for the calculation of tax on the basis of rates specified in Schedule I for every rupee in the turnover, relating to goods taxed at a rate of two and a half paisa for every rupee in the turnover relating to all other goods.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 4, Act XI of 1125
main_sections.description: Amends section 4 of the principal Act, adding a reference to 'the Opium Act, 1878 (Central Act 1 of 1878)'.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 5, Act XI of 1125
main_sections.description: Amends section 5 of the principal Act by omitting certain clauses and substituting others. It also mentions the substitution of the word 'State' in certain contexts.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 6, Act XI of 1125
main_sections.description: Amends section 6 of the principal Act by substituting the word 'State of Travancore-Cochin' with the word 'State'.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 8, Act XI of 1125
main_sections.description: Amends section 8 of the principal Act by substituting the word 'State' for 'State of Travancore-Cochin'.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 18, Act XI of 1125
main_sections.description: Amends section 18 of the principal Act by substituting the word 'State' for 'State of Travancore-Cochin'.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 24, Act XI of 1125
main_sections.description: Amends section 24 of the principal Act by substituting the word 'State' for 'State of Travancore-Cochin'.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 26, Act XI of 1125
main_sections.description: Amends section 26 of the principal Act. It includes substitutions for clauses and sub-sections, particularly relating to the 'State of Travancore-Cochin'.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new section 26A, Act XI of 1125
main_sections.description: Inserts a new section 26A titled 'Transitory Provisions'. This section deals with the application of the Act to Malabar district and its financial year ending with March 1958. It also allows the Government to notify additions, alterations, or cancellations to Schedule II.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 27, Act XI of 1925
main_sections.description: Amends section 27 of the principal Act, renumbering sub-section (1) and referring to the Madras General Sales Tax Act, 1939, the Madras Tobacco (Taxation of Sales and Registration) Act, 1953, and the Madras Sales of Motor Spirit Taxation Act, 1930.
Indicates that schedules are to be inserted.

important_rules: Tax is calculated at the rates specified in Schedule I for every rupee in the turnover.
For goods taxed at a rate of two and a half paisa for every rupee in the turnover, this applies to all other goods.
The Act may be amended by Government notification.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By notification in the Gazette.

key_procedures: Appointment of Deputy Commissioners of Sales Tax by the Government.
The Deputy Commissioner or Deputy Commissioners shall perform functions within assigned local limits.
Government may, by notification, add, alter, or cancel Schedule II.
administration: The Government of Travancore-Cochin
important_notes: The Act's commencement date is to be notified by the Government.
The Preamble refers to the 'State of Kerala'.
Specific amendments to various sections of the principal Act.
Transitory provisions for the Malabar district are included.

References are made to other Acts including the Madras General Sales Tax Act, 1939, the Madras Tobacco (Taxation of Sales and Registration) Act, 1953, and the Madras Sales of Motor Spirit Taxation Act, 1930.

title: The Travancore-Cochin General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 1952
purpose: To amend the Travancore-Cochin General Sales Tax Act, 1125 (XI of 1125) for purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Travancore-Cochin state.

key_definitions.foodgrains: Means paddy, rice, wheat, maize, jowar, bajra, barley and ragi and includes such other articles as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, specify as such.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called The Travancore-Cochin General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 1952, and that it shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 2, Act XI of 1125.
main_sections.description: Introduces a new clause (dd) after clause (d) of Section 2 of the Travancore-Cochin General Sales Tax Act, 1125 (XI of 1125), defining 'foodgrains'.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 3, Act XI of 1125.
main_sections.description: Amends sub-section (2) of Section 3 of the said Act by substituting the entry 'Nine pies' in column 2 against item (viii), with the entry 'Or anna and nine pies'.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government (by notification in the Gazette)
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notification in the Gazette for specifying articles as foodgrains.

key_procedures: Government may specify additional articles as 'foodgrains' by notification in the Gazette.
Substitution of existing entry 'Nine pies' with 'Or anna and nine pies' in a specific section of the Principal Act.
administration: Implied to be administered by the Government of Travancore-Cochin.
important_notes: Published in Gazette Extraordinary dated 1st August 1952. Sec. III.

title: THE TRAVANCORE-COCHIN GENERAL SALES-TAX (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 1955
purpose: To further amend the Travancore-Cochin General Sales-tax Act, 1125.
scope: Applies to the State of Travancore-Cochin.

key_definitions.motor spirit: Means any substance which by itself or in admixture with other substances is ordinarily used directly or indirectly to provide reasonably efficient fuel for automotive or stationary internal combustion engines, and includes petrol, diesel oil and other internal combustion oils, but does not include kerosene, furnace oil, coal or charcoal.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin General Sales-tax (Second Amendment) Act, 1955, and it shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 2, Act XI of 1125
main_sections.description: Inserts a definition for 'motor spirit' in clause (f) of Section 2 of the Travancore-Cochin General Sales-tax Act, 1125.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 3, Act XI of 1125
main_sections.description: Amends Section 3 of the principal Act, concerning the rate of tax on petrol and other motor spirit.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 5, Act XI of 1125
main_sections.description: Amends Section 5 of the principal Act by inserting the words 'motor spirit' in clause (vii) of sub-section (2), and omits certain entries.

important_rules: The tax on petrol shall be at the rate of two annas and three pies for every Rupee in the turnover relating to petrol.
The tax on every Rupee in the turnover relating to motor spirit other than petrol shall be at the rate of nine pies.
important_notes: This Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 1st December, 1955.

title: THE TRAVANCORE-COCHIN GENERAL SALES TAX AMENDMENT ACT, 1955
purpose: To amend the Travancore-Cochin General Sales Tax Act, 1125, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to sales tax in the Travancore-Cochin state, with specific provisions regarding the applicability of tax to certain goods and the collection of tax by municipalities. It also defines the scope of appellate and revisional powers.

key_definitions.Deputy Commissioner: Any person appointed by a Deputy Commissioner of Sales Tax under Section 2B.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 1955, and it shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 2, Act XI of 1125.
main_sections.description: Inserts new Sections 2A and 2B, detailing the appointment and functions of the Appellate Tribunal and the appointment of the Deputy Commissioner of Sales Tax.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new Sections 2A and 2B in Act XI of 1125.
main_sections.description: This section appears to be incorrectly listed in the table of contents. Section 2 is the amendment of Section 2. Section 3 is the insertion of new sections. Based on the text, Section 3 inserts new sections 2A and 2B into Act XI of 1125. Section 2A pertains to the Appellate Tribunal, its constitution, powers, and procedures. Section 2B pertains to the appointment of a Deputy Commissioner of Sales Tax.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 3, Act XI of 1125.
main_sections.description: Amends Section 3 to modify the rate of tax for certain goods, including items like "pepper, ginger, turmeric, nuxvomica, kacholam, cinnamon", "Mill cloth", "Cotton cloth", and "Refrigerators, air conditioning plants, component parts of refrigerators or air conditioning plants". It also substitutes the words 'Radio gramophones' with 'component parts of radio-gramophones'.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 4, Act XI of 1125.
main_sections.description: Omits the words and figure of Section 3 from Section 4.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 5, Act XI of 1125.
main_sections.description: Amends Section 5 regarding the tax on "sale of any cloth woven on handlooms wholly or partly with mill yarn" and "newspapers". It also specifies tax on "sale of pepper, ginger, turmeric, nuxvomica, kacholam, cinnamon" at a single point in the series of sales.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 9, Act XI of 1125.
main_sections.description: Amends Section 9, concerning the words 'actually incurred by him' and 'which are specified in the accounts and which the assessing authority considers legitimate'.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new Section 11A, in Act XI of 1125.
main_sections.description: Inserts Section 11A, titled 'Government etc., entitled to collect tax as registered dealers'. This section clarifies that notwithstanding anything in the Act, the Government, the Council of the Corporation of the City of Trivandrum, and every Municipal Council collecting tax by way of tax under sub-section (1) shall pay over to the Government the amount collected, and any such amount is not the Collector's responsibility or requisition. The assessing authority can make an order directing the person having custody of the municipal fund to pay it in priority to any other charge against such fund, except for the service of authorised loans.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 14, Act XI of 1125.
main_sections.description: Amends Section 14 regarding 'assessment made on him', 'provided', and 'further'.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new sections for Section 15, Act XI of 1125.
main_sections.description: Substitutes new sections for Section 15. These new sections deal with 'Authorities competent to pass orders in revision' and 'Appellate Tribunal'. It outlines the powers of the Deputy Commissioner and the Board of Revenue to revise orders, and the jurisdiction and procedures of the Appellate Tribunal. It also details the process for appeals to the Appellate Tribunal and the High Court.

main_sections.section_title: Disposal of certain applications pending with the Board of Revenue or the Deputy Commissioner on the appointed day.
main_sections.description: Specifies how applications pending with the Board of Revenue or the Deputy Commissioner on the appointed day should be disposed of.

main_sections.section_title: Institution of certain appeals and applications and the disposal thereof.
main_sections.description: Deals with the institution and disposal of appeals and applications.

important_rules: Rule 1: The tax shall be calculated at the rate of six pies for every Rupee in the turnover relating to certain specified goods.
Rule 2: Certain cloth woven on handlooms or with mill yarn shall be exempt from taxation under Section 3, sub-section (1).
Rule 3: Newspapers shall be exempt from taxation under Section 3, sub-section (1).

Rule 4: The Appellate Tribunal shall, with the previous sanction of the Government, make regulations consistent with the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder, for regulating its procedure and the disposal of its business.
Rule 5: Regulations made under sub-section (4) shall be published in the Gazette.
Rule 6: The Deputy Commissioner may revise any order or proceeding under sub-section (1) or any other provision of this Act, on application.
Rule 7: The Board of Revenue may revise any order passed or proceeding recorded by the Deputy Commissioner under sub-section (1) or any other provision of this Act, on application.

penalties: The Act does not explicitly detail specific monetary penalties or durations for offences within the provided excerpt. However, it outlines procedures for assessment and appeal, implying enforcement mechanisms.
The Act allows for the High Court to confirm, vary, or set aside any order of assessment made by the Deputy Commissioner or the Appellate Tribunal.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Assessing authorities, Deputy Commissioner, Appellate Tribunal, Board of Revenue, High Court.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment of tax, appeals, revisions, and judicial review by the High Court. Municipalities collect tax and pay it to the Government. Directing payment from municipal funds for tax in priority to other charges.

rights: Right to appeal to the Appellate Tribunal against orders of assessment.
Right to apply for revision of orders passed by the Deputy Commissioner.
Right to petition the High Court against orders of the Appellate Tribunal or Deputy Commissioner on grounds of law.
Right of parties to appeal to the Appellate Tribunal or High Court for reasonable opportunity of being heard.
Right to prefer a revision against an order of assessment within four years.
Right to prefer a review against an assessment within one year.
Right to petition the High Court for revision of orders of the Appellate Tribunal or Deputy Commissioner.
duties: Duty to pay tax as calculated under the Act.
Duty to comply with orders of assessment and revision.
Duty to submit to the jurisdiction of the Appellate Tribunal and High Court.
Duty of the municipality to pay over collected tax to the Government.
obligations: Obligation for the Government, Corporation of the City of Trivandrum, and Municipal Councils to collect tax and pay it to the Government.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Application to the Appellate Tribunal for revision of orders of assessment. Within sixty days from the date of the order, if the assessee is aggrieved.
Procedure 2: Appeal to the High Court from any order of the Appellate Tribunal or Deputy Commissioner on a question of law. Within sixty days from the date of the order.
Procedure 3: Revision of orders by the Deputy Commissioner or Board of Revenue. Applications for revision shall be in the prescribed form, accompanied by a fee of one hundred rupees.
Procedure 4: The Appellate Tribunal may admit an appeal or revision preferred after the period of sixty days if sufficient cause is shown.

Procedure 5: The Appellate Tribunal may, in its discretion, permit the assessee to pay the tax in such number of instalments, or give such other direction in regard to the payment of the tax, as it thinks fit.
Procedure 6: The High Court may admit a petition preferred after the period of sixty days if the petitioner had sufficient cause for not preferring the petition within that period.
