Procedure 7: The petition to the High Court shall be in the prescribed form, be verified in the prescribed manner, and shall be accompanied by a fee of one hundred rupees.
administration: The administration appears to be shared. The Government notifies the commencement date. The Deputy Commissioner of Sales Tax is appointed. The Board of Revenue and the Appellate Tribunal are also involved in administrative and judicial functions.
important_notes: The Act specifies that the tax on sale of pepper, ginger, turmeric, nuxvomica, kacholam, and cinnamon shall be at a single point in the series of sales by successive dealers.

The Act clarifies that the Government, the Council of the Corporation of the City of Trivandrum, and every Municipal Council collecting tax are entitled to collect tax as registered dealers, with specific provisions for payment to the Government.
The Appellate Tribunal may admit an appeal or revision preferred after the prescribed period if sufficient cause is shown.
The High Court may admit a petition preferred after the prescribed period if sufficient cause is shown.

title: THE TRAVANCORE COCHIN HACKNEY CARRIAGE (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1955
purpose: To amend The Travancore-Cochin Hackney Carriage Act, 1950 (Act XXXV of 1950) for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Travancore-Cochin region and concerns Hackney Carriages. The amendments are made to the Travancore-Cochin Hackney Carriage Act, 1950.

key_definitions.hackney_carriage: "Hackney Carriage" means any wheeled vehicle (including a cycle-rickshaw) which: (i) is drawn, pushed, or propelled by man, or is drawn by horse, bullock or other animal; (ii) is used for the conveyance of any person; and (iii) stands or plies for hire by the hour or day or according to distance.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Hackney Carriage (Amendment) Act, 1955. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 2, Act XXXV of 1950.
main_sections.description: Amends Section 2 of the principal Act of 1950. In clause (4), for the words "dragging or pushing", the words "drawing, pushing or propelling" and for the words "drags or pushes", the words "draws, pushes or propels" shall be substituted.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 7, Act XXXV of 1950.
main_sections.description: Amends Section 7 of the principal Act of 1950. In clause Fourth, for the words "drawn or pushed", the words "drawn, pushed or propelled" shall be substituted.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 8, Act XXXV of 1950.
main_sections.description: Amends Section 8 of the principal Act of 1950. In clause (f), after the word "rickshaw", the word "cycle-rickshaw" shall be inserted and for the words "or rushed", the words "pushed or propelled" shall be substituted.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 39, Act XXXV of 1950.
main_sections.description: Amends Section 39 of the principal Act of 1950. After the word "rickshaws", the words "or cycle-rickshaws" shall be inserted.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 50, Act XXXV of 1950.
main_sections.description: Amends Section 50 of the principal Act of 1950. After clause (c), the following shall be inserted as clause (cc): "(cc) the inspection of hackney carriages with a view to see if such carriages are in a fit condition for public use;".

important_rules: Rule 1: If a hackney carriage is drawn, pushed, or propelled by man, or drawn by horse, bullock, or other animal, it must be used for the conveyance of any person and stand or ply for hire by the hour, day, or distance.
Rule 2: Substitute "drawing, pushing or propelling" for "dragging or pushing" and "draws, pushes or propels" for "drags or pushes" in clause (4) of Section 2 of the principal Act.
Rule 3: Substitute "drawn, pushed or propelled" for "drawn or pushed" in clause Fourth of Section 7 of the principal Act.
Rule 4: Insert "cycle-rickshaw" after "rickshaw" in clause (f) of Section 8 of the principal Act, and substitute "pushed or propelled" for "rushed".
Rule 5: Insert "or cycle-rickshaws" after "rickshaws" in Section 39 of the principal Act.
Rule 6: Insert a new clause (cc) in Section 50 of the principal Act to allow for the inspection of hackney carriages for their fitness for public use.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government, through notification in the Gazette.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspection as per Section 50 (cc) and enforcement of the amended provisions of the principal Act.

rights: Right to have hackney carriages inspected for fitness for public use.
duties: To ensure hackney carriages are drawn, pushed, or propelled in accordance with the amended definitions.
To ensure hackney carriages are used for conveyance and ply for hire as specified.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Amendment of the principal Act (Act XXXV of 1950) through specified changes in its sections.
Procedure 2: The Act comes into force on a date appointed by the Government through a Gazette notification.
administration: The Government of Travancore-Cochin (presumably through relevant transport or police departments).
important_notes: The amendments are retrospective to some extent, as indicated by the reference to "Sixth Year of the Republic of India" for the original Act.
The amendments clarify the terminology related to propulsion of hackney carriages.

title: THE TRAVANCORE-COCHIN HACKNEY CARRIAGE ACT (XXXV OF 1950)
purpose: To regulate the registration, numbering, licensing, and operation of Hackney Carriages within the territories of Travancore-Cochin.
scope: Applies to all local areas in the State of Travancore-Cochin, as notified by the Government.

key_definitions.Registrar/Registering Officer: The Inspector-General of Police, or any other person appointed by the Government, by name or by official designation to perform the functions of a Registering Officer under this Act.
key_definitions.Magistrate: Means any Magistrate having local jurisdiction in any area to which this Act extends.
key_definitions.Hackney Carriage: Means any wheeled vehicle drawn or pushed by any person (like hand-trolley, cycle-rickshaw, bullock-cart, etc.) or animal (like horse, bullock) used for the conveyance of any person for hire.
key_definitions.Driver: Includes a person who drives, draws, or pushes any hackney carriage.
key_definitions.Year of registration: Means the year ending with the last day of March.
key_definitions.Minor: Means any person who has not completed the age of eighteen years.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (all local areas in Travancore-Cochin), and when it comes into force (by notification).
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'Registrar', 'Magistrate', 'Hackney Carriage', 'Driver', 'Horse', 'Year of registration', and 'Minor'.
Mandates that every hackney carriage must be annually registered by the Registering Officer.
Outlines the process for applying for the registration of a hackney carriage, including submission of the vehicle and required documents.

States that every applicant under Section 4 is entitled to registration unless the Registering Officer is of the opinion that the vehicle is not fit for public use or that the number of vehicles of that description is already excessive.
Details the process of granting a carriage license upon successful registration, including the issuance of a license signed by the Registering Officer.
Specifies the particulars that must be entered in the license, including the owner's name and residence, a description of the carriage, and the date of license expiry.
Prescribes the fees to be paid for each license, with different rates for four-wheeled and two-wheeled carriages drawn by horses, or by rickshaws, perambulators, etc.
Details the process for the Registering Officer to grant a driver's license, including the information the license should contain (name, abode, age, description of animals).

main_sections.section_title: Particulars of license to be registered
main_sections.description: Requires particulars of every driver's license to be entered in the register and on payment of a fee.

main_sections.section_title: Maximum fares for use of hackney carriages
main_sections.description: Sets maximum fares for the use of hackney carriages and prohibits backfares.
Deals with the deposit of property left in hackney carriages and the procedure for its return to owners or sale if unclaimed.
Relates to the disposal of criminal charges concerning hackney carriages.
Empowers the Government or other specified authorities to make bye-laws for the regulation of hackney carriages.

important_rules: Hackney carriages must be annually registered.
Carriage licenses are valid for the year of registration.
Driver's licenses are required for operating hackney carriages.
Maximum fares are stipulated and backfares are prohibited.
Lost property found in hackney carriages must be deposited with the police.
Property not claimed within a specified period can be sold.
Defacing or destroying plates is prohibited.

penalties: Penalty for keeping hackney carriage without license: fine not exceeding twenty-five rupees.
Penalty for plying for hire without plate: fine not exceeding twenty rupees.
Penalty for using counterfeit plate: fine not exceeding fifty rupees.
Penalty for refusal to let a hackney carriage for hire: fine not exceeding ten rupees.
Penalty for wilful injury to hackney carriage: fine not exceeding fifty rupees.
Penalty for using or driving without a license: fine not exceeding fifty rupees.
Penalty for plying for hire without fare plate: fine not exceeding twenty rupees.
Penalty for not producing license before Magistrate: fine not exceeding fifty rupees.
Penalty for carrying more passengers than permitted: fine not exceeding ten rupees.
Penalty for any offence under the Act for which no specific penalty is provided: fine not exceeding one hundred rupees, or imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or both.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Registering Officer, Police Officers, and Magistrates.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspection, imposition of fines, suspension or cancellation of licenses, seizure of counterfeit plates, and prosecution in Magistrate courts.

rights: Right to obtain a carriage license upon successful registration and payment of fees.
Right to be issued a driver's license if deemed fit by the Registering Officer.
Right to carry passengers up to the licensed capacity of the carriage.
Right to claim lost property found in a hackney carriage.
duties: Duty to register hackney carriages annually.
Duty to obtain a carriage license.
Duty to obtain a driver's license.
Duty to display the license and particulars of the carriage.
Duty to charge fares within the prescribed maximums.
Duty to deposit lost property found in the carriage.
Duty to produce license when demanded by an authorized officer.
Duty to keep the carriage and animals in good condition.
obligations: Obligation to comply with all provisions of the Act and any rules or bye-laws made thereunder.
Obligation to notify the Registering Officer of any change of residence or place where the carriage is kept.

key_procedures: Application for registration of a hackney carriage.
Grant of carriage license upon registration.
Application for and grant of a driver's license.
Procedure for reporting and returning lost property.
Procedure for dealing with disputes between hirers and drivers.
Procedure for suspension or cancellation of licenses.
Procedure for seizure of counterfeit plates.
administration: The Registering Officer, likely a functionary within the Police Department, and Magistrates for enforcement and prosecution.
important_notes: The Act may be extended to any local area by notification.
The Registering Officer has the power to refuse registration if the number of vehicles of a certain description is already excessive or if the vehicle is unfit.
The Registering Officer may suspend or cancel a license if the carriage or its harness is unfit for public use.
Certain provisions regarding the carriage of passengers and luggage apply.
Special provisions exist for lost property and compensation for frivolous prosecution.

title: THE TRAVANCORE-COCHIN HIGH COURT (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1951
purpose: To amend the Travancore-Cochin High Court Act, 1951 for purposes hereinafter appearing, specifically regarding the preamble, jurisdiction, powers of Judges, Division Benches, and other matters connected with the functions of the High Court.
scope: Applies to the Travancore-Cochin High Court and its functions, jurisdiction, and powers.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin High Court (Amendment) Act, 1951, and it shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of preamble, Act V of 1925
main_sections.description: Amends the preamble of the Travancore-Cochin High Court Act, 1125 (Act V of 1925) to make provision regulating the business of the High Court, fixing jurisdiction and powers of Judges, Division Benches, and for other matters connected with the functions of the High Court.

main_sections.section_title: The heading "Part I. Preliminary" occurring before Section 1 of the Act shall be deleted.
main_sections.description: Deletes the heading "Part I. Preliminary" from the Act.

main_sections.section_title: For Section 1 of the Act, the following shall be substituted:-
main_sections.description: Substitutes Section 1 of the Act with "1. This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin High Court Act, 1125."

main_sections.section_title: Section 4 of the Act shall be deleted.
main_sections.description: Deletes Section 4 of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: The heading "Part II. Constitution of the High Court" occurring before Section 5 of the Act shall be deleted.
main_sections.description: Deletes the heading "Part II. Constitution of the High Court" from the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Section 5 of the Act shall be deleted.
main_sections.description: Deletes Section 5 of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: In Section 6 of the Act, the words "shall be a Court of record and" shall be deleted.
main_sections.description: Amends Section 6 of the Act by deleting specific words.

main_sections.section_title: For Section 7 of the Act, the following shall be substituted:-
main_sections.description: Substitutes Section 7 of the Act with provisions regarding the jurisdiction exercisable notwithstanding any vacancy in the office of a Judge, and how any Judge, a Division Bench of two Judges, or a Full Bench may exercise jurisdiction and powers.

main_sections.section_title: Sections 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, and 14 of the Act shall be deleted.
main_sections.description: Deletes Sections 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, and 14 of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Section 17 of the Act shall be deleted.
main_sections.description: Deletes Section 17 of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: The heading "Part III. Jurisdiction of High Court" occurring before Section 18 of the Act shall be deleted.
main_sections.description: Deletes the heading "Part III. Jurisdiction of High Court" from the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Sub-sections (2), (3) and (4) of Section 18 of the Act shall be deleted.
main_sections.description: Deletes sub-sections (2), (3), and (4) of Section 18 of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: In Section 19 of the Act for the words "constituted under this Act" occurring at the end, the words "of the State of Travancore Cochin" shall be substituted.
main_sections.description: Amends Section 19 of the Act by substituting specific words.

main_sections.section_title: In clause (4) of Section 20 of the Act, (1) in sub clause (A), for item (iv) the following shall be substituted:-
main_sections.description: Amends sub-clause (A) of clause (4) of Section 20 of the Act by substituting item (iv). It also makes a substitution for item (vii) in sub-clause (A) for item (x) and for sub-clause (C) of clause (x) for item (4).

Makes several substitutions in Section 21 of the Act, relating to hearing and deciding appeals, and amendments to sub-clause (ii) of sub-clause (A) of clause (2) of Section 25. It also includes substitutions for sub-clause (ii) of clause (B) of sub-clause (4) and sub-clause (ii) of clause (B) of sub-clause (4).

main_sections.section_title: The proviso to Section 24 of the Act shall be deleted.
main_sections.description: Deletes the proviso to Section 24 of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Sections 25 and 26 of the Act shall be deleted.
main_sections.description: Deletes Sections 25 and 26 of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: The heading "Part IV. Administrative functions of the High Court" occurring before Section 27 of the Act shall be deleted.
main_sections.description: Deletes the heading "Part IV. Administrative functions of the High Court" from the Act.

main_sections.section_title: For Section 27 of the Act, the following shall be substituted:-
main_sections.description: Substitutes Section 27 of the Act, empowering the High Court to depute a Judge to visit subordinate courts, correct their procedure and practice, and generally to examine and report on their working.

main_sections.section_title: Section 28 of the Act shall be deleted.
main_sections.description: Deletes Section 28 of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: The heading "Part V. Miscellaneous" occurring before Section 29 of the Act shall be deleted.
main_sections.description: Deletes the heading "Part V. Miscellaneous" from the Act.

main_sections.section_title: For Section 30 of the Act, the following shall be substituted:-
main_sections.description: Substitutes Section 30 of the Act, stating that the conduct of business in the High Court shall be regulated by the Chief Justice in the High Court.

main_sections.section_title: In Section 32 of the Act, the words "and in the 'courts subordinate to the High Court'" shall be deleted.
main_sections.description: Amends Section 32 of the Act by deleting specific words.

key_procedures: Procedure for substitution of preamble, including provisions for regulating business, fixing jurisdiction, powers of Judges, Division Benches, and other High Court functions.
Procedure for substituting Section 1, naming the Act.
Procedure for substituting Section 7 to address jurisdiction and exercise of powers by Judges and Benches, notwithstanding vacancies.
Procedure for amending Section 19 by substituting specific phrases.
Procedure for amending Section 20, clause (4), sub-clause (A), item (iv), and other related items and sub-clauses.
Procedure for substituting Section 21 with new provisions concerning appeals and the powers of a single Judge or Division Bench.
Procedure for substituting Section 27 to empower the High Court to depute Judges to visit subordinate courts and report on their working.
Procedure for substituting Section 30 to regulate the conduct of business in the High Court by the Chief Justice.
Procedure for amending Section 32 by deleting specific phrases.
Procedure for hearing and deciding appeals under the amended provisions.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Travancore-Cochin High Court Act, 1951 (Act V of 1125).
The Act makes extensive deletions and substitutions across various sections and headings of the principal Act.
Specific mention of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, and the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, in relation to amendments.
The amendment allows a Judge to refer any application or appeal for the decision of a Division Bench of two Judges or a Full Bench.
Provisions are made for circumstances where the jurisdiction can be exercised by a Judge, a Division Bench of two Judges, or a Full Bench even in the event of a vacancy.

title: The Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions (Amendment) Act, 1974
purpose: To further amend the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950, for the purposes appearing therein.
scope: Applies to Hindu religious institutions in Travancore-Cochin.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions (Amendment) Act, 1974.

Amends sub-section (1) of section 4 of the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950. It specifies the composition of the Board, stating that two of the Hindu members shall be nominated by the Hindus among the Council of Ministers and one elected by the Hindus among the members of the Legislative Assembly of the State of Kerala.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 11
main_sections.description: Substitutes the existing section 11 of the principal Act. The new section states that the President of the Board shall be one of the members of the Board nominated by the Hindus among the Council of Ministers.
In section 33 of the principal Act, substitutes the words "the Ruler of Travancore" and "the Ruler" with "the Government" in both places where they occur.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 63
main_sections.description: Substitutes section 63 of the principal Act. The new section likely deals with the Constitution of the Cochin Devaswom Board, specifying that the Board shall consist of three Hindu members, two of whom shall be nominated by the Hindus among the Council of Ministers and one elected by the Hindus among the members of the Legislative Assembly of the State of Kerala.

For sub-section (1) of section 71 of the principal Act, the following sub-section shall be substituted: "(1) The Hindus among the Council of Ministers shall nominate one of the members of the Board as its President."

In section 107 of the principal Act, in sub-sections (1) and (2), for the words "the Ruler of Cochin" and "the Ruler", in both the places where they occur, the words "the Government" shall be substituted.

Repeals the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions (Amendment) Ordinance, 1974 (12 of 1974). It also states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act. The saving clause also mentions that this Act came into force on the 26th day of August, 1974.

important_rules: The Board shall consist of three Hindu members.
Two Hindu members shall be nominated by the Hindus among the Council of Ministers.
One Hindu member shall be elected by the Hindus among the members of the Legislative Assembly of the State of Kerala.
The President of the Board shall be one of the members of the Board nominated by the Hindus among the Council of Ministers.
The words "the Ruler of Travancore" and "the Ruler" in section 33 of the principal Act are substituted with "the Government".
The words "the Ruler of Cochin" and "the Ruler" in sub-sections (1) and (2) of section 107 of the principal Act are substituted with "the Government".
key_procedures: Nomination of two Hindu members to the Board by the Hindus among the Council of Ministers.
Election of one Hindu member to the Board by the Hindus among the members of the Legislative Assembly of the State of Kerala.
Nomination of the President of the Board by the Hindus among the Council of Ministers.
important_notes: The Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions (Amendment) Ordinance, 1974 (12 of 1974) is repealed.
Anything done or action taken under the Ordinance is deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.
This Act came into force on the 26th day of August, 1974.

title: THE TRAVANCORE COCHIN HINDU RELIGIOUS INSTITUTIONS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1955
purpose: To further amend the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950.
scope: Applies to the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions (Amendment) Act, 1955 and it shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new Section 4A in Act XV of 1950.
main_sections.description: Inserts a new Section 4A titled 'Validity of proceedings' in Act XV of 1950. This section states that no act or proceeding of the Board shall be deemed to be invalid by reason only of a defect in its constitution or on the ground that the President or any member thereof was disqualified for, or had ceased to hold, his office, or by reason of such act or proceeding having been done or taken during the period of any vacancy in the office of the President or any member of such Board.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new Section 72A in Act XV of 1950.
main_sections.description: Inserts a new Section 72A titled 'Validity of proceedings.' in Act XV of 1950. This section is identical in wording to the newly inserted Section 4A, addressing the validity of proceedings of the Board despite defects in constitution or disqualification/vacancy of members.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of certain acts, etc., of the Cochin Devaswom Board.
main_sections.description: All acts done and all proceedings taken by the Cochin Devaswom Board in the exercise or purported exercise of jurisdiction or powers conferred by the said Act while any member of the said Board was disqualified or during the period of any vacancy in the said Board are declared to have been validly done or taken, as the case may be.
The Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions (Amendment) Ordinance, 1954 (I of 1954) is repealed.

important_notes: The Act aims to cure defects in the constitution of the Board and to validate actions taken during periods of disqualification or vacancy.

title: THE TRAVANCORE-COCHIN HINDU RELIGIOUS INSTITUTIONS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1958
purpose: To further amend the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950.
scope: The act applies to Hindu Religious Institutions in Travancore-Cochin.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions (Amendment) Act, 1958.

Amends sub-section (1) of section 4 of the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950. The amended sub-section concerns the composition of a Board, which shall consist of three Hindu members nominated by the Ruler of Travancore, one member nominated by the Council of Ministers, and one elected by the Hindus among the members of the Legislative Assembly of the State of Kerala.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 5.
main_sections.description: Replaces section 5 with new provisions regarding the procedure for the election of members to the Board. It outlines the process for summoning a meeting of the Hindus, election of a member by the Governor of Kerala, and the requirement for the election to be held in accordance with rules specified in Schedule II.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 63.
main_sections.description: Substitutes section 63 with new provisions concerning the Constitution of the Cochin Devaswom Board. The Board, as per the substituted sub-section (1) of section 62, shall consist of three Hindu members nominated by the Ruler of Cochin, one by the Hindu members of the Council of Ministers, and one elected by the Hindus among the members of the Legislative Assembly of the State of Kerala.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 64.
main_sections.description: Replaces section 64 with new provisions regarding the procedure for the election of members to the Board. Similar to the amendment for section 5, this section details the process for summoning meetings of the Hindus, election of a member by the Governor of Kerala, and adherence to rules in Schedule II for elections.

Amends Schedule II to the principal Act. Specifically, rule 3 is amended to allow any Hindu member of the Legislative Assembly of the State of Kerala to nominate a duly qualified Hindu person who is not subject to disqualification for election as a member of the Board. The process for disqualification involves the Board by delivering to the Chairman, within the specified hours, a nomination paper signed by the proposer and another Hindu member of the Legislative Assembly. The person nominated shall affix their signature to the nomination paper before it is delivered to the Chairman, stating their willingness to serve if elected.

important_rules: Rule 1: Election of members to the Board must follow specified procedures and adhere to rules in Schedule II.
Rule 2: Nomination papers for Board membership must be signed by a proposer and another Hindu member of the Legislative Assembly.
Rule 3: Nominated individuals must affix their signature to the nomination paper, confirming their willingness to serve if elected.
key_procedures: Procedure for election of members to the Board: This involves summoning a meeting of the Hindus, election of a member by the Governor of Kerala, and conducting the election in accordance with rules specified in Schedule II.

Procedure for nomination and disqualification of Board members: Candidates can be nominated by a proposer and another Hindu member of the Legislative Assembly. Disqualification processes are to be handled by the Board by delivering relevant documents to the Chairman within specified hours.
administration: Likely administered by the relevant department overseeing religious institutions or governance in the State of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the President on 23rd July 1958 and was published in the Gazette dated 24th July 1958.
Amendments are made to the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950.

title: THE TRAVANCORE-COCHIN IDENTIFICATION OF PRISONERS ACT
purpose: To authorise the taking of measurements and photographs of convicts and others.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin. It applies to the taking of measurements and photographs of convicts and others. Section 3 specifically mentions persons convicted with rigorous imprisonment for a term of one year or upwards, or of any offence which would render him liable to enhanced punishment on a subsequent conviction. Section 4 applies to persons who have been arrested in connection with an offence punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term of one year or upwards. Section 5 applies to persons for the purposes of investigation, or in relation to whom an offence has been committed, or who are to be produced before a Magistrate.

key_definitions.measurements: includes finger impressions and foot-print impressions.
key_definitions.police officer: means an officer in charge of a police station, a police officer making an investigation under Chapter XIV of the Travancore or Cochin Code of Criminal Procedure, or any other police officer not below the rank of Inspector; and "prescribed" means prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the short title as 'The Travancore-Cochin Identification of Prisoners Act, 1950'. It states that the Act extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin and shall come into force at once.

Defines 'measurements' to include finger impressions and foot-print impressions, and 'police officer' to mean an officer in charge of a police station, an investigating officer under Chapter XIV of the Travancore or Cochin Code of Criminal Procedure, or any other police officer not below the rank of Inspector. It also states that 'prescribed' means prescribed by rules made under this Act. It clarifies that these definitions are subject to anything repugnant in the subject or context.

Covers persons convicted of an offence punishable with rigorous imprisonment for one year or upwards, or liable to enhanced punishment on a subsequent conviction. It also covers persons ordered to give security for good behaviour under Section 114 of the Travancore Code of Criminal Procedure, or Section 102 of the Cochin Code of Criminal Procedure. These individuals must, if so required, allow their measurements and photographs to be taken by a police officer.

main_sections.section_title: Taking of measurements etc., of non-convicted persons.
main_sections.description: States that any person arrested in connection with an offence punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term of one year or upwards shall, if so required by police officers, allow their measurements to be taken in the prescribed manner.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Magistrate to order a person to be measured or photographed.
main_sections.description: Empowers a Magistrate to order any person to be measured or photographed for the purposes of investigation, or when an offence has been committed, or when the person is to be produced before a Magistrate. The Magistrate can direct any person to allow these actions. Provided that no order shall be made directing any person to be photographed except by a Magistrate of the first class. Further, no order shall be made under this section unless the person has at some time been arrested in connection with such investigation or proceeding.

main_sections.section_title: Resistance to the taking of measurements, etc.
main_sections.description: States that if any person who, under this Act, is required to allow his measurements or photographs to be taken, resists or refuses to allow the taking of the same, it shall be lawful to use all means necessary to secure the taking thereof. Resistance or refusal to allow the taking of measurements or photographs under this Act is deemed an offence under Section 170 of the Travancore Penal Code and Section 172 of the Cochin Penal Code.

main_sections.section_title: Destruction of photographs and records of measurements, etc., on acquittal.
main_sections.description: Specifies that where any person, who has been previously convicted of an offence punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term of one year or upwards, or has had his measurements taken or has been photographed in accordance with the provisions of this Act, is released without trial or discharged or acquitted, all measurements and photographs (both negatives and copies) shall, unless the Court or a case where such person is released without trial the District Magistrate, for reasons to be recorded in writing otherwise directs, be destroyed or made over to him.

Grants the Government the power to make rules for the purpose of carrying into effect the provisions of this Act. Without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing provision, such rules may provide for: (a) the restrictions on the taking of photographs of persons under Section 5; (b) the places at which measurements and photographs may be taken; (c) the nature of the measurements that may be taken; (d) the method in which any class or classes of measurements shall be taken; (e) the dress to be worn by a person when being photographed under Section 3; and (f) the preservation, safe custody, destruction and disposal of records of measurements and photographs.
States that no suit or other proceeding shall lie against any person for anything done, or intended to be done, in good faith under this Act or under any rule made thereunder.
Repeals The Travancore Identification of Prisoners Act, XI of 1112 and the Cochin Identification of Prisoners Act, XV of 1112.

important_rules: Measurements include finger impressions and foot-print impressions.
Police officers are defined to include officers in charge of police stations and investigating officers, among others.
Rules can be made by the Government to prescribe the nature and method of measurements, dress for photography, and preservation/destruction of records.
No suit or proceeding shall lie against any person for anything done in good faith under this Act or its rules.

penalties: Resistance or refusal to allow taking of measurements or photographs is an offence under Section 170 of the Travancore Penal Code and Section 172 of the Cochin Penal Code.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Police officers and Magistrates
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through orders from Magistrates for taking measurements and photographs, and through the use of necessary means to overcome resistance. Penalties are governed by the respective Penal Codes of Travancore and Cochin.

rights: Right to have measurements and photographs destroyed or made over upon acquittal or discharge, unless a court or District Magistrate directs otherwise.
duties: Duty to allow measurements and photographs to be taken if required under the Act.
Duty to not resist or refuse the taking of measurements or photographs.
obligations: Persons convicted of offences punishable with rigorous imprisonment for one year or upwards, or liable to enhanced punishment, have an obligation to provide measurements and photographs.
Persons ordered to give security for good behaviour have an obligation to provide measurements and photographs.
Persons arrested in connection with certain offences have an obligation to provide measurements.

key_procedures: Taking of measurements and photographs: Persons falling under Sections 3 and 4 must allow their measurements and photographs to be taken by a police officer if required. For persons under Section 5, a Magistrate can order measurements and photographs to be taken.
Overcoming resistance: If resistance is met, lawful means may be used to take the measurements or photographs.
Destruction of records: Upon acquittal or discharge, measurements and photographs are to be destroyed or made over, unless otherwise directed by the court or District Magistrate.
administration: The Government of Travancore-Cochin (through unspecified departments) is responsible for making rules under Section 8.
important_notes: The Act repeals the Travancore Identification of Prisoners Act, XI of 1112 and the Cochin Identification of Prisoners Act, XV of 1112.
Photography orders under Section 5 are only to be made by a Magistrate of the first class, and only if the person has been previously arrested in connection with an investigation or proceeding.
The Act aims to ensure that measurements and photographs are taken in a prescribed manner and provides for their subsequent destruction or preservation.

title: The Travancore Cochin Indebted Agriculturists Relief Act, 1956
purpose: To provide for the relief of indebted agriculturists in the State of Travancore-Cochin.
scope: Applies to the State of Travancore-Cochin and to agriculturists within that state.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Indebted Agriculturists Relief Act, 1956, extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin, and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'Agriculturist' and 'Debt'.

No suit for recovery of debt shall be instituted, and no application for execution of a decree in respect of a debt shall be made against an agriculturist in any civil or revenue court before the expiry of six months from the commencement of this Act.
Deals with the payment of debts in instalments, including provisions for when the debtor fails to make payments and the implications for creditors.
Specifies how interest on debts should be calculated and applied, including limitations on such interest.
Allows agriculturists to deposit the amount of their debt into court, and outlines the procedure for such deposits and their effect on the debt.
Provides for appeals against orders passed by the court under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Presumption as to transfer of immovable property of the debtor
main_sections.description: Establishes a presumption regarding the transfer of immovable property by a debtor before and after the commencement of the Act, in relation to the benefit of creditors.
Specifies that certain periods shall be excluded when calculating the time for limitation for suits or applications related to the recovery of a debt.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of payment or deposit under Section 4 or Section 6
main_sections.description: Clarifies the effect of payments or deposits made under Sections 4 and 6 on the recovery of a debt.
Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

important_rules: No suit for recovery of debt or application for execution of a decree in respect of a debt shall be made against an agriculturist for six months from the commencement of the Act.
Debts can be paid in instalments, and interest calculation is regulated.
Agriculturists can deposit their debt amount into court.
Transfers of immovable property by debtors may be subject to presumption regarding creditor's benefit.
Certain periods are excluded for calculating the limitation for debt recovery actions.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Civil Courts and Revenue Courts within the State of Travancore-Cochin.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the institution of suits, applications for execution of decrees, and appeals as provided in the Act, with specific rules regarding payment of debts and interest.

rights: Agriculturists have the right to relief from excessive debt.
Agriculturists have the right to pay debts in instalments.
Agriculturists have the right to deposit debt amounts into court.
Creditors have the right to recover debts, subject to the provisions of the Act.
duties: Debtors have a duty to pay their debts.
Debtors have a duty to comply with court orders regarding debt repayment.
obligations: Agriculturists have an obligation to adhere to the instalment payment plans or court-ordered repayment schedules.
Creditors have an obligation to accept payments as stipulated by the Act and court orders.

key_procedures: Procedure for instituting suits and applications for debt recovery against agriculturists (subject to limitations).
Procedure for payment of debts in instalments.
Procedure for depositing debt amounts into court.
Procedure for appeals against court orders.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but likely administered by the judiciary and relevant revenue departments of the State of Travancore-Cochin.
important_notes: The Act specifically defines 'Agriculturist' to exclude certain individuals with significant income from non-agricultural sources or property.
The definition of 'debt' excludes certain sums payable to the State, Central Government, local authorities, and specified co-operative societies.
Explanations are provided for certain definitions to clarify their scope and application.
The Act provides for the presumption of fraudulent transfer of property by a debtor.
Specific rules govern the calculation of interest and the effect of payments and deposits.

title: The Travancore-Cochin Insolvency (Amendment) Act, 1957
purpose: To amend The Travancore-Cochin Insolvency Act, 1955.
scope: Applies to The Travancore-Cochin Insolvency Act, 1955.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Insolvency (Amendment) Act, 1957, and it shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

Amends Section 1 of the Travancore-Cochin Insolvency Act, 1955 (Act II of 1956). It modifies the text in sub-section (1) to refer to "Travancore-Cochin" and substitutes the words "six annas" with "thirty-seven naye paise" in sub-section (2). It also amends sub-section (1) of section of the principal Act, clause (g), to read "State" means the State of Kerala.
Amends Section 2 of the principal Act. In clause (g) of sub-section (1) of section 2, the words "State" means the State of Kerala.
Amends Section 39 of the principal Act. It replaces the words "six annas" with "thirty-seven naye paise" and the words "thirty-seven naye paise" with "fifty naye paise".
Amends Section 43 of the principal Act. In clause (a) of section 43, the words "eight annas" are replaced by "fifty naye paise" in the two places where they occur.

For section 86 of the principal Act, the following section shall be substituted: "86. Repeal.-The Travancore Insolvency Act, 1908 (Act VIII of 1908), the Cochin Insolvency Act, VII of 1908 and the Provincial Insolvency Act, 1920 (Central Act V of 1920), as in force in the Malabar district referred to in sub-section (2) of section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (Central Act 37 of 1956), are hereby repealed."

key_procedures: Commencement of the Act: Upon notification in the Gazette by the Government.
Amendment process: Specific changes to existing sections of The Travancore-Cochin Insolvency Act, 1955 are detailed in sections 2 through 5.

Repeal of certain Acts: Section 6 details the repeal of the Travancore Insolvency Act, 1908, the Cochin Insolvency Act, VII of 1908, and the Provincial Insolvency Act, 1920, as applicable to the Malabar district.
administration: The Government (through appropriate notifications).
important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 8th October 1957.
The amendments refer to specific monetary values (e.g., "six annas", "thirty-seven naye paise", "fifty naye paise") and territorial references (e.g., "State of Kerala", "Malabar district").
The repeal in Section 6 is contingent on the provisions of sub-section (2) of section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.

title: The Travancore Cochin Insolvency Act, 1955
purpose: To consolidate and amend the law relating to insolvency and to make provisions for the administration of the property of insolvents.
scope: Applies to cases of insolvency within the territories of the former Travancore and Cochin States.

key_definitions.insolvent: A person who has committed an act of insolvency or against whom an insolvency petition has been presented.
key_definitions.secured creditor: A creditor holding a mortgage or charge on the property of the debtor, or entitled to any lien or charge thereon.
key_definitions.debtor: A person who is indebted and against whom an insolvency petition may be filed.
key_definitions.property: Includes movable and immovable property of the insolvent.
key_definitions.court: The court by which the insolvency petition is presented or by which the same is for the time being being is being entertained.

main_sections.section_title: Cases in which Court must refuse an absolute discharge
main_sections.description: Details the circumstances under which the Court is compelled to refuse an absolute discharge to an insolvent, such as cases where the insolvent has not surrendered all assets, has not kept proper books, or has continued to trade after contracting debts provable without reasonable expectation of being able to pay them, or has brought on insolvency by rash or hazardous speculations.
Covers situations where the Court may annul an adjudication or make it otherwise think fit, and when a debtor can be released from custody, with provisions for recommitting the debtor to custody.

Specifies the effects of an order of discharge, stating that it shall release the insolvent from all debts due to the Government, any debt or liability incurred by means of any fraud or fraudulent breach of trust, and any debt or liability in respect of which he has obtained forbearance.

main_sections.section_title: Debt payable at a future time
main_sections.description: Addresses how debts payable at a future time are handled, allowing a creditor to prove for the debt and receive dividends, with provisions for rebate of interest.

Outlines the rights of secured creditors, including the ability to realize their security and prove for the balance due, and the Court's power to intervene if the creditor realizes the security without sufficient reason.
Describes the method of proof for debts, which includes an affidavit or a statement in writing by the creditor or their authorised agent.

main_sections.section_title: Restriction of rights of creditor under execution
main_sections.description: Limits the rights of a creditor who has obtained a decree and has attached or taken in execution the property of the debtor. Such rights are only enforceable to the extent that they were obtained before the date of the admission of the insolvency petition.

main_sections.section_title: Duties of Court executing decree as to property taken in execution
main_sections.description: Details the duties of a Court that has executed a decree where the debtor's property has been taken in execution, specifying how such property should be dealt with upon the admission of an insolvency petition.

States that no transfer of property, made by a person before the date of the adjudication, and which is voluntary or made in favour of a purchaser or incumbrancer in good faith and for valuable consideration, shall be voidable by the assignee.

Establishes the order of priority for the distribution of an insolvent's property, giving preference to debts due to the Government or any local authority, and then to salary or wages of clerks, servants, or labourers in respect of services rendered during the four months prior to the date of the presentation of the petition.

important_rules: An insolvent cannot obtain an absolute discharge if they have failed to surrender all their assets.
An insolvent must keep proper books of account showing their financial position.
Transactions made in fraud or with intent to defeat creditors are voidable.
Secured creditors have the right to realize their security.
Debts payable at a future time are provable and eligible for dividends with rebate.
Voluntary transfers of property made before adjudication are generally voidable.
Certain debts, like wages of labourers, have priority in distribution.
Official Receivers have broad powers to manage and dispose of the insolvent's property.
The Court can summon persons for examination regarding the insolvent's affairs.
Transactions made with intent to defraud creditors or give preference can be annulled.

penalties: Concealment or fraudulent disposition of property may lead to penalties or imprisonment.
Failure to appear or provide information when summoned by the Court can result in apprehension and examination.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Court and the Official Receiver.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through court orders, summons, apprehension of individuals, seizure of property, annulment of transactions, and imposition of penalties.

rights: Insolvent has the right to apply for discharge.
Creditors have the right to prove their debts and receive dividends.
Secured creditors have the right to realize their security.
The Court has the power to investigate the insolvent's affairs.
Debtors have a right to a discharge under certain conditions.
duties: Insolvent has the duty to surrender all property to the receiver.
Insolvent has the duty to attend court and assist the receiver.
Insolvent has the duty to disclose all assets and liabilities.
Creditors have a duty to prove their debts.
Persons summoned by the court have a duty to appear and provide information.
obligations: Insolvent is obligated to keep accurate books of account.
Insolvent is obligated to not contract further debts without reasonable expectation of payment.
The receiver is obligated to manage and distribute the insolvent's property according to the Act.

key_procedures: Filing of an insolvency petition by a debtor or a creditor.
Adjudication of the debtor as insolvent by the Court.
Appointment of an Official Receiver to manage the insolvent's property.
Proof of debts by creditors.
Realization and distribution of the insolvent's property.
Application for discharge by the insolvent and Court's decision on it.
Examination of the insolvent and other persons by the Court.
administration: The Courts and the Official Receiver.
important_notes: The Act deals with both voluntary and compulsory insolvency.
Certain transactions, like voluntary transfers, can be set aside.
The Act distinguishes between secured and unsecured creditors.
Special provisions exist for the distribution of property, prioritizing certain debts.
The Court has significant powers to ensure fair dealing and prevent fraud.

title: The Travancore-Cochin Interpretation and General Clauses (Amendment) Act, 1957
purpose: To further amend the Travancore-Cochin Interpretation and General Clauses Act, 1125.
scope: Applies to the State of Travancore-Cochin. The amendments affect the interpretation of existing acts within this jurisdiction.

key_definitions.Act: shall mean a Proclamation or Act of Travancore or Cochin, an Act or Ordinance of Travancore-Cochin, an Act passed by the Legislature of the State of Kerala, an Ordinance promulgated by the Governor under Article 213 of the Constitution or, where with respect to the State of Travancore-Cochin or Kerala the power to make laws is vested in the President or other authority under sub-clause (a) of clause (1) of Article 357 of the Constitution, any law made in exercise of such power.
key_definitions.Gazette or Kerala Government Gazette: shall mean the Gazette published by or under the authority of the Government.
key_definitions.registered: used with reference to a document, shall mean registered in India under the law for the time being in force for the registration of documents.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Interpretation and General Clauses (Amendment) Act, 1957.
Amends sub-section (1) of section 1 of the Travancore-Cochin Interpretation and General Clauses Act, 1125 (VII of 1125) by omitting the word "Travancore-Cochin".
Amends section 2 by substituting new definitions for 'Act' and 'Gazette or Kerala Government Gazette', and by adding a new definition for 'Government' and 'registered'.

Amends section 3 of the principal Act. The sub-section substituted states that where any Act is not expressed to come into operation on a particular day, then it shall come into operation on the day on which the Act or Ordinances are published in the Gazette. It also details how this applies to the Rajpramukh, Governor, or President, and to laws made by the President or other authority.

important_rules: Any Act not expressed to come into operation on a particular day shall come into operation on the day of its publication in the Gazette.
This commencement rule applies to Acts and Ordinances promulgated by the Governor or the President, and to laws made by the President or other authority.
key_procedures: Amendment of Section 1: Omitting the words "Travancore-Cochin" from the short title of the principal Act.
Amendment of Section 2: Revising definitions of 'Act', 'Gazette', 'Government', and 'registered'.
Amendment of Section 3: Specifying the commencement date for Acts and Ordinances when not explicitly stated, based on Gazette publication.
administration: The President and the Governor of the State of Kerala are involved in the promulgation of ordinances and the exercise of powers, indicating administrative oversight.
important_notes: The amendment to Section 2(a) clarifies the definition of 'Act' to include laws made under specific constitutional provisions concerning the President's legislative powers.

The amendment to Section 2(b) and (c) clarifies the application of the definition of 'Government' to acts done before and after the commencement of the Constitution of India (7th Amendment) Act, 1956.
The amendment to Section 4 provides a mechanism for determining the commencement date of legislation when it is not explicitly defined.

title: The Travancore-Cochin Interpretation and General Clauses (Amendment) Act, 1956
purpose: To amend The Travancore-Cochin Interpretation and General Clauses Act, 1125.
scope: Applies to the Travancore-Cochin region, amending an existing act. The specific scope of the original act being amended is not detailed in this document snippet.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Interpretation and General Clauses (Amendment) Act, 1956.
Amends clause (3) of section 2 of the Travancore-Cochin Interpretation and General Clauses Act, 1125. It replaces the words "and a Proclamation" with "a Proclamation and a President's Act".

Substitutes sub-section (1) of section 3 of the principal Act with new text. The new text states that when an Act is not expressed to come into operation on a particular day, it shall come into operation on the day it is first published in the Gazette after receiving the assent of the Rajpramukh or the President, as the case may be.

important_rules: If an Act does not specify an operation date, it comes into effect upon its first publication in the Gazette after receiving the assent of the Rajpramukh or the President.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not specified in this excerpt.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not specified in this excerpt.

key_procedures: Procedure for commencement of Acts: If an Act's commencement date is not explicitly stated, it shall commence on the date of its publication in the Gazette following the relevant assent (Rajpramukh or President).
administration: Not specified in this excerpt.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Travancore-Cochin Interpretation and General Clauses Act, 1125.
The amendment to section 2 introduces the phrase 'President's Act' alongside 'Proclamation'.
The amendment to section 3 clarifies the default commencement date for Acts when not otherwise specified.
The Act was enacted by the President in the seventh year of the Republic of India.
The Act was republished in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 31st October 1956.

title: The Travancore Cochin Irrigation (Amendment) Act, 1957
purpose: To amend the Travancore-Cochin Irrigation Act, 1956, for the purpose hereinafter appearing.
scope: The Act applies to the Travancore-Cochin region.

key_definitions.authorized officer: Means an officer authorized under section 3.
key_definitions.hospital: Means any hospital established or maintained by the Government, or by any municipal council, or other local authority and includes any other hospital which may be declared by the Government, by notification in the Gazette, to be a hospital for the purposes of this Act.
key_definitions.near relative: Means any of the following relatives of the deceased, namely, wife, husband, parent, son, daughter, brother or sister and includes any other person who is related to the deceased (i) in lineal consanguinity within six degrees, or (ii) by collateral consanguinity within six degrees, or (iii) by marriage with any of the relatives aforesaid.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made by the Government under this Act.
key_definitions.teaching medical institution: Means any of the institutions specified in the Schedule to this Act, and includes any other institution which may be declared by the Government, by notification in the Gazette, to be a teaching medical institution for the purposes of this Act.
key_definitions.unclaimed body: Means the body of a person who dies in a hospital, prison or public place, which has not been claimed by any of his near relatives or by any recognised religious or public institution belonging to the religion of the deceased, within such time as may be prescribed.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called The Travancore-Cochin Irrigation (Amendment) Act, 1957, and it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 20th day of November, 1956.

Inserts a new section 40A into the Travancore-Cochin Irrigation Act, 1956 (President's Act VII of 1956) concerning procedure on failure to contribute cost or labour for work to be done by joint labour.
Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including authorized officer, hospital, near relative, prescribed, and teaching medical institution.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to authorize officers to act under section 3
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to authorize officers to act under section 3 for the area to which the Act applies or for any part thereof.

main_sections.section_title: Unclaimed bodies in hospitals, prisons and public places how to deal with
main_sections.description: Lays down the procedure for dealing with unclaimed bodies found in hospitals, prisons, and public places, including the role of the authorized officer and the Magistrate.

important_rules: If a proprietor fails or neglects to do his share of work or contribute his share of the cost or labour, it shall be lawful for the Collector, the Puzha Special Officer, or any officer specially authorized by the Government to do the work or pass orders.

The authorized officer shall take possession of the unclaimed body and hand it over to the authority in charge of a teaching medical institution for the purpose of anatomical examination or dissection.
No person shall be punished for any thing done or intended to be done in pursuance of this Act in good faith.

penalties: Whoever disposes of, or abets the disposal of, any unclaimed body save as provided by this Act, or obstructs any authority in charge of a teaching medical institution or an authorized officer from handing over, taking possession of, removing or using such dead body for the purpose specified in section 4, shall be punishable with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Collector, the Puzha Special Officer, or any officer specially authorized by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through orders issued by authorized officers and potential fines for non-compliance.

rights: Right to have the work done or cost recovered if a proprietor fails to contribute their share.
duties: Duty of Police and other officers to assist in obtaining possession of unclaimed bodies.
Duty of authorized officers to take all reasonable measures to assist authorized officers in the discharge of their duties under this Act.
obligations: Obligation to contribute to the cost or labour for work to be done by joint labour.

key_procedures: Procedure on failure to contribute cost or labour for work to be done by joint labour: The Collector or authorized officer can carry out the work, recover costs, or pass necessary orders.
Procedure for dealing with unclaimed bodies: The authorized officer takes possession, hands over to a teaching medical institution, and can be subject to specific conditions.
Procedure for dealing with doubts or disputes: Doubts or disputes as to near relative status are referred to the Magistrate of the First Class for final decision.
administration: The Government of Travancore-Cochin and its authorized officers.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on the 20th day of November, 1956.
The Act provides for the disposal of unclaimed bodies for the purpose of anatomical examination or dissection.
Protection of persons acting under this Act is provided, provided the action is taken in good faith and intended to be done in pursuance of the Act.

title: The Travancore-Cochin Irrigation Act, 1956
purpose: To provide for the construction, repair and maintenance of irrigation works, the conservation and distribution of water for purposes of irrigation and the levy of betterment contribution and the levy of water cess.
scope: Applies to the State of Travancore-Cochin. Governs the construction, repair, and maintenance of irrigation works, including petty and major irrigation works. Also covers the distribution of water, betterment contributions, and penalties related to irrigation. The act can be extended by Government notification to specific areas.

key_definitions.Collector: means the Collector of a district
key_definitions.irrigation: means with its grammatical variations includes "drainage" with its corresponding variations
key_definitions.irrigation Officer: means an officer appointed by the Government to perform all or any of the functions of an Irrigation Officer under this Act
key_definitions.irrigation work: includes all irrigation works, irrigation stations, etc.
key_definitions.majority of proprietors: means the proprietors of more than one-half of the acreage benefited by an irrigation work
key_definitions.minor irrigation work: includes all irrigation works other than major and petty irrigation works
key_definitions.notification: means a notification published in the Gazette
key_definitions.petty irrigation work: includes all irrigation works irrigating or useful for the drainage or protection of an extent of over five acres
key_definitions.prescribed: means prescribed by rules made under this Act
key_definitions.proprietor: means the owner of the land and includes the cultivator or person in actual possession of such land

main_sections.description: Names the act as The Travancore-Cochin Irrigation Act, 1956, specifies its extent to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin, and states that it shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification, appoint.

Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'Collector', 'contribution', 'irrigation', 'irrigation Officer', 'irrigation work', 'major irrigation work', 'minor irrigation work', 'notification', 'petty irrigation work', 'prescribed', and 'proprietor'.

States that the Government may, from time to time, by notification, invest any Collector or any Board constituted under the Act with all or any of the powers conferred or imposed by or under the Act on the Government and shall declare the local limits within which such powers or duties shall be exercised or performed.

main_sections.section_title: Construction, repair and maintenance of petty irrigation works.
main_sections.description: Deals with the construction, repair, and maintenance of petty irrigation works by the Government, with provisions for who bears the cost, including levy of annual cess or betterment contribution.

main_sections.section_title: Construction, repair and maintenance of minor irrigation works.
main_sections.description: Covers the construction, repair, and maintenance of minor irrigation works by the Government, including the levy of annual cess and betterment contribution.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure of the Collector on an application for execution of new minor irrigation works.
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for the Collector when an application is made for the execution of new minor irrigation works, including the interest of proprietors, estimation of cost, and notification.
Describes the process of issuing notice to proprietors regarding proposed irrigation works and allowing them to raise objections.

main_sections.section_title: When Government may carry out the work.
main_sections.description: Specifies conditions under which the Government can carry out irrigation works, even if proprietors do not agree, after considering objections.

main_sections.section_title: Accident to any petty or minor irrigation work.
main_sections.description: Addresses the situation of accidents to petty or minor irrigation works and the recovery of costs for repairs.

main_sections.section_title: Execution of work for the proper maintenance of petty and minor irrigation work.
main_sections.description: Details the procedure for the proper maintenance of petty and minor irrigation works, including the role of the Panchayat and the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Construction, repair and maintenance of major irrigation works.
main_sections.description: Covers the construction, repair, and maintenance of major irrigation works, which shall devolve on the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure of construction of major irrigation work.
main_sections.description: Details the procedure for the construction of major irrigation works, including the proposal, objections, and Government sanction.
Describes how objections to proposed major irrigation works are investigated.

main_sections.section_title: When the Government may carry out the work.
main_sections.description: Outlines when the Government can proceed with major irrigation works after considering objections.
Grants the Government the power to levy an annual cess on any land benefited by a major irrigation work, with an explanation for how it is calculated and applied.

main_sections.section_title: Irrigation Officer to report periodically on condition of major irrigation works.
main_sections.description: Mandates that the Irrigation Officer report periodically on the condition of major irrigation works.

main_sections.section_title: Impressionment of materials for urgent works of repair etc.
main_sections.description: Allows for the impressment of materials for urgent repair works.
Specifies how payment for materials taken for urgent works is to be made.

main_sections.section_title: Compensation for damage in taking materials.
main_sections.description: Provides for compensation for damage incurred while taking materials.

main_sections.section_title: Distribution of water from irrigation works.
main_sections.description: Deals with the distribution of water from irrigation works.
Specifies offences that are punishable under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Cost of carrying out work to be recovered from convicted person.
main_sections.description: Allows for the recovery of the cost of work from a person convicted under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Suit of application for the issue of an injunction.
main_sections.description: Enables suits or applications for injunctions to be filed.
Grants power to arrest without a warrant in certain circumstances.
Defines the period of limitation for actions under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken under Act.
main_sections.description: Provides protection for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Bar of action against Government or Panchayat.
main_sections.description: Restricts legal action against the Government or Panchayat for certain acts done in good faith.

main_sections.section_title: Rate of cess fixed under this Act to be final and not to be questioned by any Civil Court.
main_sections.description: Declares that the rate of cess fixed under the Act is final and cannot be questioned in any Civil Court.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of Irrigation Boards, their functions.
main_sections.description: Allows for the constitution of Irrigation Boards and defines their functions.
Empowers the Government to delegate its powers under the Act.
Defines the liability of individuals to pay cess.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act.
Deals with the repeal of any existing laws and savings provisions.

important_rules: The Government may, by notification, extend the provisions of this Act to any specified area.
The Government may levy an annual cess on any land benefited by a major irrigation work, with the cess not exceeding three per cent on the capital outlay.
The Government can carry out irrigation works if proprietors do not agree after objections are heard and considered.
Materials can be impressed for urgent repair works, with provision for payment and compensation for damage.
The rate of cess fixed under the Act is final and cannot be questioned by any Civil Court.

penalties: Offences punishable under the Act.
Cost of carrying out work to be recovered from convicted person.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government, Collector, Irrigation Officer, Panchayat
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through imposition of penalties, recovery of costs, suits or applications for injunction, and arrest without warrant.

rights: Right to raise objections against proposed irrigation works.
Right to receive payment for materials taken.
Right to receive compensation for damage.
duties: Duty to pay betterment contribution.
Duty to pay annual cess.
Duty to allow Government to carry out works.
obligations: Obligation to maintain petty and minor irrigation works.
Obligation to comply with notifications and orders under the Act.

key_procedures: Application for execution of new minor irrigation works: Collector's procedure involving notice to proprietors, consideration of objections, and execution of work.
Construction of major irrigation works: Involves proposal, objections, investigation, Government decision, and execution.
Levy of cess: Government can levy annual cess on benefited land, with specific rates for different types of lands.
Objections to works: Proprietors can raise objections, which are to be investigated by the Collector.
administration: The Government of Travancore-Cochin and its appointed authorities (Collectors, Irrigation Officers, Panchayats).
important_notes: The Act was enacted by the President in the seventh year of the Republic of India.
The President of India empowered to enact this Act.
The Government may by notification extend the provisions of this Act to any specified area.
The rate of cess fixed under this Act shall be final and shall not be questioned by any Civil Court.

title: THE TRAVANCORE-COCHIN IRRIGATION TANKS (PRESERVATION AND IMPROVEMENT) ACT, 1952 (ACT XXIII OF 1952)
purpose: To preserve and improve existing irrigation tanks in the State of Travancore-Cochin.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin and shall come into force in such areas and on such dates as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, specify. Applies to irrigation tanks, wells, canals, eries or other reservoirs used for the storage of water for purposes of cultivation, paddy and other food crops, and for irrigation.

key_definitions.irrigation tank: means a tank, well, canal, erie or other reservoir used for the storage of water for purposes of cultivation of paddy and other food crops, and notified by the Government as an irrigation tank for the purposes of this Act.
key_definitions.Collector: means the Collector of the District.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Irrigation Tanks (Preservation and Improvement) Act, 1952. It extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin and shall come into force in such areas and on such dates as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, specify.
Defines 'Collector' and 'Irrigation tank'.

The Government may, for the purpose of notifying irrigation tanks under this Act, require by notification in the Gazette, the persons in possession and control of tanks, wells, canals, eries or other reservoirs used for the storage of water for purposes of cultivation, to furnish to the Collector within specified periods particulars of the said tanks, wells, canals, eries or other reservoirs used for the storage of water for purposes of cultivation, in such form as may be prescribed. The Government may also determine whether a tank, well, canal, erie or other reservoir used for the storage of water for purposes of cultivation shall be deemed fit to be notified as an irrigation tank for the purposes of this Act, cause such enquiries to be made as they may consider necessary.

Prohibits conversion of irrigation tanks into wet land etc. unless notified. Whoever fails to make the return mentioned in sub-section (1) or makes a return which is false in any material particular, shall be liable to a penalty not exceeding one hundred rupees as may be fixed by the Collector. No person shall convert an irrigation tank into wet land or dry land without the previous sanction in writing of the Collector.

Whoever converts an irrigation tank into wet land or dry land in contravention of the provisions of Section 4 shall be liable to a penalty not exceeding two hundred rupees as may be fixed by the Collector.

main_sections.section_title: Restoration and repair of irrigation tanks
main_sections.description: If any person in possession and control of an irrigation tank converts it into wet land or dry land in contravention of the provisions of Section 4, the Collector, by notice in writing, may require such person within such time as may be fixed by the Collector to restore the irrigation tank to its original state. If the person so required fails to restore the irrigation tank to its original state, the Collector may, without prejudice to any other action that may be taken under this Act, cause such work to be executed as he may take such measures or do that which in his opinion is necessary for restoring the same to its original state. The Collector may either authorize the entry into the irrigation tank and the lands adjacent to it of such persons as may be necessary for the execution of such work. The expenses incurred by the Collector in the execution of such work shall be recoverable from the person who was required to execute the work, or arrears of land revenue under the provisions of the Travancore-Cochin Revenue Recovery Act, 1951. Where an irrigation tank is not maintained in good repair, the Collector may, by notice in writing, require the person in possession and control thereof or other persons who are in possession and control of adjoining lands and who are likely to be benefited by maintaining the tank in good repair, to maintain in good repair the said tank within such time as may be specified in the notice. If the aforesaid persons do not repair and maintain the tank as required by the Collector within the time specified, the Collector may cause such repairs or be executed or may take such measures or do that which in his opinion is necessary for maintaining the tank in good repair. The Collector shall, subject to the striking between several persons whose lands are benefited, apportion the expenses of repair between the several persons whose lands are benefited by the repair in proportion to the benefit derived or derivable by such persons or account of such repairs. Any expenses incurred by the Collector for the purpose of repairing and maintaining an irrigation tank and any amount apportioned by the Collector due from a party under this sub-section may be recovered from the party concerned as an arrear of land revenue under the Travancore-Cochin Revenue Recovery Act, 1951. The Collector may, by notification or authorise the entry into the irrigation tank and the land adjoining to it of such persons as may be necessary for the execution of such repairs and other maintenance works.

An appeal shall lie to the Board of Revenue from any order passed by the Collector under Section 3 or Section 5 or Section 6. Appeals shall be presented within thirty days from the date of receipt of the order complained against. Provided that, in cases of disputes relating to liability on apportionment under Section 6 (2), any aggrieved party may sue any other or others and the court may by its decree reopen the liability. The Government may at any time call for and examine the record of any case pending before, or disposed of, by the Board of Revenue and may pass such order in reference thereto as the Government may think fit. Provided that no order shall be passed under this sub-section without notice to the party who may be affected by the order.
The penalties imposed under Section 3 or Section 5 or Section 6 shall be recoverable as an arrear of land revenue under the provisions of the Travancore-Cochin Revenue Recovery Act, 1951.
The Cochin Preservation of Eries Act, XXIII of 1120, is hereby repealed.

important_rules: No person shall convert an irrigation tank into wet land or dry land without the previous sanction in writing of the Collector.
