If an irrigation tank is not maintained in good repair, the Collector may require the person in possession or control, or adjoining landowners likely to benefit, to maintain it in good repair.
Expenses incurred by the Collector for repair and maintenance of irrigation tanks are recoverable as arrears of land revenue.

penalties: Penalty not exceeding one hundred rupees for false or omitted returns (Section 3).
Penalty not exceeding two hundred rupees for converting an irrigation tank into wet land or dry land (Section 5).
Penalties imposed under Section 3, 5, or 6 are recoverable as arrears of land revenue (Section 8).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Collector, Government, Board of Revenue
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Notices in writing requiring restoration or repair, execution of work by the Collector, recovery of expenses/penalties as arrears of land revenue, appeals to the Board of Revenue, review by the Government.

rights: Right to appeal against orders of the Collector to the Board of Revenue.
Right to sue in cases of disputes relating to apportionment of liability under Section 6(2).
Right to receive notice before an order is passed affecting them under Section 7(2).
duties: Duty to furnish returns regarding irrigation tanks as required by the Government (Section 3).
Duty not to convert irrigation tanks into wet land or dry land without sanction (Section 4).
Duty to restore an irrigation tank to its original state if converted without sanction (Section 6).
Duty to maintain irrigation tanks in good repair when required (Section 6).
obligations: Obligation to pay penalties for contraventions of the Act.
Obligation to bear apportioned expenses for repair and maintenance of irrigation tanks.
Obligation to comply with notices issued by the Collector for restoration or repair.

key_procedures: Notification of irrigation tanks by the Government and requirement of returns from persons in possession.
Determination by the Government whether a water storage structure qualifies as an irrigation tank.
Issuance of notice by the Collector for restoration or repair of an irrigation tank.
Execution of repair or maintenance work by the Collector if required persons fail to act.
Apportionment of repair expenses among beneficiaries.
Appeals process to the Board of Revenue and review by the Government.
administration: The Collector is the primary enforcement authority. The Board of Revenue and the Government have appellate and supervisory roles.
important_notes: The Act repealed the Cochin Preservation of Eries Act, XXIII of 1120.
Penalties are recoverable as arrears of land revenue.
Appeals can be made against orders of the Collector.
The Government has the power to review decisions of the Board of Revenue.

title: THE TRAVANCORE-COCHIN GOVERNMENT LAND ASSIGNMENT ACT
purpose: To provide for the assignment of Government lands and to remove any doubt as to the validity of previous assignments and to remove any doubt as to the validity of previous assignments and restrictions imposed upon land assigned by Government or under their authority.
scope: Applies to Government lands and their assignment within the State of Travancore-Cochin. The Act covers all public roads, streets, lands and paths, the bridges, ditches, dykes and fences on or beside the same.

key_definitions.land: Includes the bed of the sea and of harbours and creeks below high water-mark; the beds and banks of rivers, streams, irrigation and drainage channels; canals, tanks, lakes, back-waters and water-courses; and all 'llanda' wherever situated; save in so far as the same are the property of- (a) proprietors of Edavagas or Jenmis or holders of Inams; or (b) all holders of land in any way subject to the payment of land revenue to the Government; or (c) any other registered holder of land in proprietory right; (d) any person holding land under grant from the Government otherwise than by way of lease or licence; or (e) any person claiming through or holding under any of the persons referred to in clauses (a), (b), (c) or (d); and are hereby declared to be, Government lands, except as may be otherwise provided by any law for the time being in force, subject to all rights of way and other public rights and to the natural and easement rights of other land owners and to all customary rights legally subsisting.
key_definitions.assigned land: Means a transfer of land by way of lease. 'Assignment' includes a transfer of land by way of lease. 'Assigned' includes 'is' here. 'Prescribed' means prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Government Land Assignment Act, 1950. It extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin and shall come into force at once.
Defines 'land' and 'assigned land' for the purposes of the Act.
Government land may be assigned by the Government or by any prescribed authority either absolutely or subject to such restrictions, conditions and limitations as may be prescribed.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure to be followed before Government lands are assigned
main_sections.description: When any Government land is proposed to be assigned, the Tahsildar of the Taluk in which the land is situated or any officer empowered by the Government shall notify in the prescribed manner that such land will, by public auction or otherwise, be assigned, and call upon those who have any claim to such land to prefer to him their objections, if any, in writing, within a time to be fixed by such notification. If any objection is preferred within the time fixed in the notification, the Tahsildar or such other officer shall enquire into such claims and pass an order in writing either accepting or rejecting the claim and intimate in writing the fact of such disposal to the claimant.
Deals with the process of assignment, including when the time fixed in the notification has elapsed and no claim has been preferred, and the process for appealing against an order of assignment.

No suit shall be entertained in any Civil Court in respect of any order passed under this Act except upon the ground that the order is in breach of any completed agreement to assign, or the land in respect of which such order has been passed is not a Government land.
Empowers the Government to make rules prescribing the manner in which assignment of land may be made, whether by public auction or otherwise, and other related procedures.

main_sections.section_title: Assignment to take effect with restrictions, conditions, etc. according to their tenor
main_sections.description: All provisions, restrictions, conditions and limitations over, contained in a patta, or other document evidencing assignment of Government land and any in-terest therein shall be valid and take effect according to their tenor, or any rule of law, statute, enactment or usage to the contrary notwithstanding.
Repeals The Travancore Land Assignment Act, III of 1097 (Travancore) and the Government Land Grant Act of 1118 (Cochin).

important_rules: Rules may be made prescribing the manner in which assignment of land may be made, whether by public auction or otherwise.
Rules may also prescribe the authority by which such assignment may be made.
Rules may prescribe the procedure to be followed in assigning the land.
Rules may provide for the publication of notices and service of notices.
Rules may prescribe the procedure to be followed in enquiry regarding claims preferred.
Rules may prescribe the rates at which tree-growths may be valued.
Rules may provide for the protection of royalties on the land assigned.
Rules may prescribe the restrictions, limitations and conditions subject to which an assignment could be made in any case or class of cases.
Rules may provide for appeals from the orders of any authority competent to assign any land.
Rules may prescribe the time within which appeals ought to be preferred.
Rules may regulate the issue of Pattah or other title deed evidencing the assignment.
Rules may prescribe for whom Forms are necessary; and generally for carrying out the purposes of this Act.
All rules made under this Act shall be published in the Gazette and thereupon they shall have the force of law.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Prescribed authority
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notification, enquiry, orders, and potentially by prescribed authorities based on rules.

rights: Right of way and other public rights
Natural and easement rights of other land owners
Customary rights legally subsisting

key_procedures: When Government land is proposed for assignment, the Tahsildar notifies and calls for objections.
Enquiry into claims and passing of orders by the Tahsildar or empowered officer.
Appeals against assignment orders can be preferred.
Rules can prescribe detailed procedures for assignment, publication of notices, enquiry, valuation of tree-growths, and appeals.
administration: The Government (implied, as they can assign land and prescribe rules)
important_notes: All public roads, streets, lands and paths, bridges, ditches, dykes and fences on or beside the same are considered Government lands.
The Act aims to remove doubts about previous assignments and imposed restrictions.
Assignment of land can be absolute or subject to restrictions, conditions, and limitations.
Any order passed under this Act is generally not subject to Civil Court jurisdiction, except for specific grounds like breach of agreement or the land not being Government land.
The Act repeals specific earlier Acts from Travancore and Cochin.

title: The Travancore Cochin Land Conservancy (Amendment) Act, 1956
purpose: To amend the Travancore-Cochin Land Conservancy Act, 1951.
scope: Applies to the Travancore-Cochin area, specifically concerning the property of the Government and the rights of agriculturists and co-operative societies. It amends the principal Act of 1951.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Land Conservancy (Amendment) Act, 1956.

Inserts a new Section 5A into the Travancore-Cochin Land Conservancy Act, 1951. This new section deals with the unauthorized destruction, removal, or appropriation of earth, metal, laterite, lime-shell, or other notified articles of value from any land which is the property of the Government. It outlines prohibitions, penalties, and compensation provisions.

Amends Section 13 of the principal Act by replacing the word "appropriated" with "appropriated" and the words "and all costs of eviction", the following shall be inserted, namely: – "compensation or damages payable under Section 5A".

important_rules: It is unlawful for any person to destroy, remove, or appropriate for himself earth, metal, laterite, lime-shell, or other notified articles of value from any land which is the property of the Government.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, prescribe the rate at which compensation shall be payable for earth, metal, laterite, lime-shell or other notified articles of value destroyed, removed or appropriated from land which is the property of the Government.

Whoever unauthorisedly destroys, removes or appropriates property belonging to the Government shall be liable to pay a fine not exceeding fifty rupees as may be imposed by the Collector, and also be liable to pay, by way of damages or an equivalent compensation, the compensation which could have been payable if sub-section (2) were applicable thereto.

penalties: Fine not exceeding fifty rupees, imposed by the Collector.
Liable to pay damages or compensation equivalent to what would have been payable under sub-section (2).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Collector
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Imposition of fines and recovery of compensation by the Collector.

rights: Right to receive compensation for earth, metal, laterite, lime-shell or other notified articles of value destroyed, removed or appropriated, in favour of any agriculturist or for a co-operative society.
obligations: Obligation not to destroy, remove or appropriate Government property (earth, metal, laterite, lime-shell, etc.) without permission.

key_procedures: Notification by the Government in the Gazette to prescribe compensation rates for destroyed or appropriated government property.
Assessment and imposition of fines and compensation by the Collector for unauthorized appropriation.
Amendment of Section 13 to include 'compensation or damages payable under Section 5A'.
administration: Likely the Revenue Department or Land Conservancy department of the Government of Travancore-Cochin.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Travancore-Cochin Land Conservancy Act, 1951.
Compensation payable under sub-section (2) of the new Section 5A is applicable.
The Government may remit in whole or in part the compensation or damages payable under the section.
Compensation is payable in favour of an agriculturist or for a co-operative society.
The Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary, dated 10th September 1956.

title: THE TRAVANCORE-COCHIN LAND CONSERVANCY ACT
purpose: To enact a uniform law for checking the unauthorised occupation of Government lands.
scope: Applies to all Government lands within the State of Travancore-Cochin. The Act also deals with public roads, streets, lanes, paths, bridges, ditches, tanks, lakes, backwaters, watercourses, and land within the ambit of the Survey Act.

key_definitions.Poramboke: Includes all public roads, streets, lanes, pathways, the bridges, dykes and fences on or beside the same; the beds and banks of rivers, irrigation and drainage channels, canals, tanks, lakes, backwaters and watercourses; markets, burial grounds, landing ghats; and all other property which the Government may, for the purpose of this Act, from time to time, declare to be Poramboke.
key_definitions.Occupant: Shall mean a person actually in possession of a land which is the property of Government.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Land Conservancy Act, 1951. It extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin and shall come into force at once.

The Travancore Land Conservancy Act of 1091 (TV of 1091) and the Cochin Land Conservancy Act, IV of 1096 are hereby repealed. But such repeal shall not affect any right or privilege acquired or liability incurred under the said Acts.

Defines 'Poramboke' and 'Occupant'. 'Poramboke' includes public roads, streets, lanes, pathways, bridges, dykes, fences, river beds, irrigation channels, canals, tanks, lakes, backwaters, watercourses, markets, burial grounds, landing ghats and any other property declared by the Government as Poramboke. 'Occupant' means a person in possession of Government land.

main_sections.section_title: Land which is the property of Government not to be occupied without permission.
main_sections.description: Prohibits occupation of Government land without permission. Land which is the property of Government, whether Poramboke or not, shall not be occupied without permission from the Government or such officer as may be empowered.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for unauthorisedly occupying a land which is the property of Government.
main_sections.description: Any person unauthorisedly occupying Government land is liable to pay a fine not exceeding two hundred rupees as imposed by the Collector.

main_sections.section_title: Levy of assessment on lands which are the property of Government unauthorisedly occupied.
main_sections.description: Any person unauthorisedly occupying a Poramboke or other Government land is liable to pay a fine or a moiety of assessment by way of assessment for the whole period of occupation, to be fixed by the Collector based on the rate prescribed by the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Levy of prohibitory assessment on Poramboke unauthosarily occupied.
main_sections.description: Any person unauthorisedly occupying a Poramboke land is liable to pay a fine or prohibitory assessment as imposed by the Collector.
Unauthorised occupation of a Poramboke or other Government land is liable to a fine or assessment as provided in Section 7, which shall be realised by the Collector.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for destruction or appropriation of trees.
main_sections.description: Any person who destroys or appropriates any useful tree belonging to the Government is liable to a fine or imprisonment for a period not exceeding one month with fine not exceeding one hundred rupees, or both.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of unauthorised occupant to summary eviction, forfeiture of crops, etc.
main_sections.description: Unauthorised occupants may be summarily evicted, their crops forfeited, and any building or structure erected or anything removed shall also be forfeited. The Collector may deem any such removed property as Government property.

Before eviction, notice must be given to the occupant. The Collector can order enquiry and may suspend or postpone eviction. The Collector may also require any subordinate officer to conduct an enquiry.
The Government may make rules or orders, either generally or in any particular instance, for regulating assessment rates, prohibiting occupation, and carrying out the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Recovery of fines, assessment, etc., as arrears of land revenue.
main_sections.description: All fines, assessments, and prohibitory assessments, and costs of eviction or removal of encroachments shall be recoverable as arrears of land revenue.

main_sections.section_title: Officers to exercise powers of Collector.
main_sections.description: The Government may, by notification, authorise any officer to exercise powers of a Collector under this Act.

Deals with the process of appeal and revision against orders made under the Act, specifying the authorities and time limits for such actions. No order shall be passed in appeal without previous notice to the party. No appeal shall lie against a decision unless it has been passed by the Board of Revenue. Pending disposal of any appeal or revision, the appellate or revisional authority may suspend the order appealed against.

No appeal shall be brought after the expiration of 60 days from the date of the decision or order complained of, provided that if the applicant satisfies the authority that there was sufficient cause for not preferring the appeal within the period prescribed, the appeal may be admitted after the period.

main_sections.section_title: Petition of appeal to be accompanied by the order appealed against.
main_sections.description: Every petition of appeal shall be accompanied by an authenticated copy of the order appealed against.

main_sections.section_title: Saving of operation of other laws in force.
main_sections.description: Nothing in this Act shall be construed as exempting any person from liability under any other law in force. However, if any penalty has been levied under Section 6 or 7, no similar penalty can be levied under any other law for such occupation.

main_sections.section_title: Saving of suits by persons aggrieved by proceedings under this Act.
main_sections.description: No suit against the Government shall be entertained in any Civil Court in respect of any order passed under this Act, except upon the ground that the land in respect of which such order has been passed is not a land which is the property of Government. Civil Courts shall not take cognizance of any such suit unless it is instituted within one year from the date on which the cause of action arose.

important_rules: Land which is the property of Government cannot be occupied without permission.
Unauthorized occupation of Government land is punishable with fine.
Assessment may be levied on unauthorizedly occupied Government lands.
Trees belonging to the Government cannot be destroyed or appropriated without permission.
Unauthorized occupants are liable to summary eviction, forfeiture of crops and any structures.
Prior notice must be given to an occupant before eviction.
Appeals and revisions against orders have specific time limits and procedures.

No suit against the Government regarding orders under this Act is maintainable in Civil Courts, except on the grounds that the land is not Government property, and must be filed within one year of the cause of action.

penalties: Fine not exceeding two hundred rupees for unauthorised occupation.
Fine or moiety of assessment for unauthorised occupation of Government land.
Fine or imprisonment for one month with fine not exceeding one hundred rupees, or both, for destroying or appropriating Government trees.
Summary eviction, forfeiture of crops, and forfeiture of buildings/structures for unauthorised occupants.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Collector
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Eviction, imposition of fines and assessments, forfeiture of crops and structures, and recovery of dues as arrears of land revenue.

rights: Right to occupy Government land with permission.
Right to appeal and seek revision against orders.
Right to not be subjected to penalty under other laws if already penalized under this Act.
Right to sue the Government if the land is not Government property, within one year of cause of action.
duties: Duty to obtain permission before occupying Government land.
Duty to pay fines or assessment for unauthorised occupation.
Duty not to destroy or appropriate Government trees.
Duty to comply with eviction orders.
Duty to prefer appeals within the prescribed time limits.
obligations: Obligation to pay dues as arrears of land revenue.
Obligation to provide authenticated copies of orders for appeals.

key_procedures: Obtaining permission for occupation of Government land.
Eviction process for unauthorised occupants, including notice and enquiry.
Levy and recovery of fines and assessments.
Appeal and revision process for challenging orders.
Procedure for recovery of fines, assessments, and costs as arrears of land revenue.
administration: The Collector and other officers authorized by the Government.
important_notes: The definition of 'Poramboke' is extensive and includes various types of public land and infrastructure.
The 'high-water mark' is defined as the highest point reached by the ordinary spring tide at any season of the year.
Unsurveyed lands within Edavagais and private estates used for public purposes are treated as property of Government for the purpose of this Act.
The Act does not affect any right or privilege acquired or liability incurred under previous similar Acts.
Provided that no person shall be prosecuted or imprisoned under Sections 183, 186, and 138 of the Indian Penal Code in respect of the same facts.
The Collector may suspend or postpone eviction and may direct a subordinate officer to hold an enquiry.

title: THE TRAVANCORE COCHIN LAND DEVELOPMENT ACT
purpose: To provide for the preparation and execution of schemes for the control and prevention of soil erosion by constructing terraces and other anti-erosion works, and to provide generally for the preparation and execution of other schemes for the improvement of cultivation of lands, reclamation of waste lands, preservation of forests and such other matters.
scope: Extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin. Applies to the subject matter as defined in the Act.

key_definitions.Board: means the Land Development Board constituted under Section 3.
key_definitions.Collector: means the Collector of the District.
key_definitions.Land Development Officer: means an Officer appointed as such by Government.
key_definitions.Owner: includes the person for the time being receiving or entitled to receive, whether on his own account or as agent, trustee, guardian, manager or receiver for another person, the rent or profit derivable from land, a tenant, an occupier or a mortgagee in possession of land.
key_definitions.Prescribed: means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Work: means any work carried out or to be carried out under any scheme under this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Land Development Act, 1950, that it extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin, and that it shall come into force at once.
Defines various terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'Collector', 'Land Development Officer', 'Owner', 'Prescribed', and 'Work'.
Provides for the constitution of a Land Development Board consisting of a Chairman and four members, two of whom at least shall be non-officials.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of the Board to direct preparation of land development schemes and matters for which the scheme may be prepared.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Board to direct the preparation of land development schemes. Specifies the purposes for which such schemes may be prepared, including preservation and improvement of soil, prevention of soil erosion, improvement of water supply, reclamation of waste lands, and planting of trees and grasses.

main_sections.section_title: Publication of scheme and inviting objections.
main_sections.description: Details the procedure for publishing a draft scheme and inviting objections from the public. This includes publication in the Gazette and local newspapers, and inviting objections from affected persons.
Requires the Inquiring Officer to inquire into objections received and submit a report to the Board with recommendations for modification of the scheme.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of the Board to sanction scheme with or without modification.
main_sections.description: Grants the Board the power to sanction a draft scheme, either with or without modifications, after considering the objections and the report of the Inquiring Officer.
States that when a scheme comes into force, it has effect as if enacted in the Act, and the Land Development Officer shall execute the scheme.
Grants the Land Development Officer the power to enforce the scheme, including carrying out work, and recovering expenses from owners if they fail to comply.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of persons whose lands are not included in the scheme to contribute.
main_sections.description: Deals with the liability of persons whose lands are not included in the scheme to contribute towards the cost of works carried out under the scheme, if they benefit from it.
Provides for reference to the Court for determination of disputes regarding liability to contribute to the scheme expenses.

main_sections.section_title: Grant of loan for carrying out work under any scheme.
main_sections.description: Allows for the grant of loans by the Land Development Officer for carrying out work under any scheme, subject to terms and conditions.
Grants the right of entry to the owner, engineer, surveyor and other officers for the purpose of preparing, examining or executing any scheme.

main_sections.section_title: Maintenance, repair and use of works carried out under the scheme.
main_sections.description: Lays down the procedure for maintenance, repair, and use of works carried out under the scheme, including responsibility of owners and the Collector.

main_sections.section_title: Obligations of persons to maintain and repair works.
main_sections.description: Specifies the obligations of persons to maintain and repair works under the scheme and the consequences of failure to do so.

main_sections.section_title: Amounts to be recoverable as arrears of land revenue.
main_sections.description: States that all amounts payable to the Government under the Act shall be recoverable as arrears of land revenue.

main_sections.section_title: Permission to owners to increase rent on account of improvement effected.
main_sections.description: Deals with the permission to owners to increase rent on account of improvements effected by the scheme.
Empowers the Government to delegate powers conferred by the Act to subordinate officers.

main_sections.section_title: Certain officers to be public servants.
main_sections.description: Declares certain officers appointed under the Act to be public servants.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of persons acting in good faith; limitation of suits and prosecutions.
main_sections.description: Provides protection to persons acting in good faith under the Act and sets limitations for suits and prosecutions.
Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of the Act.
Indicates the start of Section III of the Act, likely covering further provisions not detailed in the initial sections.

important_rules: Schemes prepared under the Act can include provisions for soil erosion control, improvement of cultivation, reclamation of waste lands, and preservation of forests.
Affected persons have the right to object to draft schemes.
Owners of lands that benefit from a scheme, even if not included in it, may be liable to contribute to its cost.
The Land Development Officer has the power to enforce schemes and recover costs.
Amounts payable to the Government under the Act are recoverable as arrears of land revenue.
The Government has the power to make rules to implement the Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Land Development Officer, Collector, Board, Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the execution of schemes, recovery of costs as arrears of land revenue, and by making rules.

rights: Right of entry for preparation, examination, or execution of schemes.
Right to object to draft schemes.
Right to potentially increase rent on account of improvements.
duties: Duty to comply with schemes.
Duty to maintain and repair works under the scheme.
Duty to contribute to the cost of schemes if benefiting.
obligations: Obligation to contribute to the cost of schemes if benefiting, even if land is not included.
Obligation to maintain and repair works as specified.

key_procedures: Preparation and publication of land development schemes, inviting objections.
Inquiry into objections and submission of a report by the Inquiring Officer.
Sanctioning of schemes by the Board with or without modifications.
Execution of schemes by the Land Development Officer.
Recovery of costs and expenses incurred by the Land Development Officer.
Granting of loans for carrying out scheme work.
Procedure for maintenance and repair of works.
administration: The Travancore-Cochin Land Development Act is administered by the Land Development Board, the Collector, and the Land Development Officer, with the Government having overall rule-making power.
important_notes: The Act aims to improve land use and prevent soil erosion.
The definition of 'Owner' is broad and includes various beneficial interests in land.
Failure to comply with scheme requirements can lead to recovery of costs as arrears of land revenue.
The Act allows for the grant of loans to facilitate scheme implementation.
Protection is provided for persons acting in good faith under the Act.

title: The Travancore Cochin Land Tax Act, 1955
purpose: To provide for the levy of a low and uniform rate of basic tax on all lands in the State of Travancore-Cochin.
scope: Applies to all lands in the State of Travancore-Cochin. It is enacted in the Sixth Year of the Republic of India.

key_definitions.basic tax: The tax imposed under the provisions of this Act.
key_definitions.Jenmikaram: Means jenmikaram as defined in the Travancore Jenmi and Kudiyan Act of 1971.
key_definitions.Thiruppuvaram or Melvaram: Means Thiruppuvaram or Melvaram entered as such in the revenue accounts.
key_definitions.Oodukoor holdings: Means holdings which are by customary law recognised as such.
key_definitions.Irriagation assessment: Means assessment so entered in the revenue accounts.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Land Tax Act, 1955. It extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Defines 'basic tax', 'Jenmikaram', 'Thiruppuvaram or Melvaram', 'Oodukoor holdings', and 'Irrigation assessment'.

main_sections.section_title: The arrangement under the Act to be a general revenue settlement.
main_sections.description: States that the arrangement made for the levy of the basic tax shall be deemed in toto to be a general revenue settlement of the State. It outlines provisions regarding the pattern fixed by the Government for the revenue settlement, and arrangements for jenmikaram, Thiruppuvaram or Melvaram, and irrigation assessment.

Subject to the provisions of the Act, there shall be charged and levied in respect of all lands in the State, whatever description and held under whatever tenure, a uniform rate of tax to be called the basic tax.

The basic tax charged and levied under the foregoing section shall be at the rate of three pies per Cent of land per annum. The basic tax charged and levied at this rate shall be the taxable payable to the Government in lieu of any existing tax in respect of the land.

main_sections.section_title: Construction of stipulation in contract, etc.
main_sections.description: Where in any contract or agreement or lease or other transaction, there is a stipulation to pay the land revenue assessment of any land or any amount in lieu thereof, such stipulation shall be construed as a stipulation to pay the amount of basic tax on the said land charged and levied under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Act not to apply to certain classes of lands.
main_sections.description: This Act is not applicable to lands held or leased by the Government or any kind or class of lands which the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, either wholly or partially exempt from the provisions of this Act.

Jenmikaram charged on and payable in respect of any land under the Travancore Jenmi and Kudiyan Act of 1971 shall continue to be paid to those entitled to it as heretofore in addition to the basic tax thereon payable to the Government.
Thiruppuvaram or Melvaram charged on and payable in respect of any land shall continue to be paid to those entitled to it as heretofore in addition to the basic tax thereon payable to the Government.
The irrigation assessment charged on tank beds and other poomnbokes brought under registry in the Travancore area, since the completion of the Kodayar Project is hereby abolished.
Nothing in this Act shall affect the power of the Government to levy any rate, or alter any existing rate, of irrigation or water cess on any land as they deem fit.
Except irrigation water cess referred to in Section 11, all cesses, whether charged on land or not, and customarily levied as public revenue due to the Government are hereby abolished.
The Government may appoint such officers as they deem necessary for the purpose of this Act. The appointment of such officers shall be notified in the Gazette.
No suit against the Government shall be entertained in any Civil Court in respect of anything done or any order passed under this Act.

Nothing in this Act shall affect the conditions of any agreement, grant or deed relating to any land except to the extent hereinbefore provided; affect any rights which have accrued to the Government before the date on which this Act comes into force.

The Government may make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of this Act. These rules may pertain to various aspects including the generality of the foregoing power, apportionment of basic tax on Oodukoor holdings, and defining powers and duties of officers.
The Travancore Land Tax Proclamation, 1121, and the Cochin Settlement Proclamation dated 10th March 1905, in so far as it provides for the assessment of land revenue, are hereby repealed.

important_rules: The basic tax shall be levied at a uniform rate of three pies per Cent of land per annum.
Jenmikaram and Thiruppuvaram or Melvaram payments shall continue to be paid in addition to the basic tax.
Irrigation assessment on tank beds and other poomnbokes in the Travancore area is abolished.
All extra cesses, except irrigation water cess, are abolished.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government-appointed officers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the levy of basic tax and general administration of the Act.

rights: Right to receive Jenmikaram and Thiruppuvaram or Melvaram.
Rights accrued to the Government before the Act's commencement are not affected.
duties: Duty to pay the basic tax as levied under the Act.
obligations: Where a stipulation exists in a contract to pay land revenue, it is construed as an obligation to pay the basic tax.

key_procedures: Appointment of officers by the Government to administer the Act.
Notification of these appointments in the Gazette.
Rules may be made for the levy of installments and their due dates.
administration: The Government, through appointed officers, administers the Act.
important_notes: The Act is not applicable to lands held or leased by the Government, or lands that the Government may exempt.
The arrangement made for the levy of basic tax is considered a general revenue settlement of the State.
Existing taxes in lieu of which basic tax is levied are to be replaced by the basic tax.
Suits against the Government regarding actions taken under this Act are barred in Civil Courts.

title: THE TRAVANCORE-COCHIN LIME-SHELLS (CONTROL) ACT, 1956
purpose: To provide for the control of the acquisition, sale, supply and distribution of lime-shells in the State of Travancore-Cochin.
scope: Applies to the State of Travancore-Cochin. It extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin.

key_definitions.dealer: A person carrying on, either personally or through any other person the business of selling lime-shells, whether wholesale or retail.
key_definitions.purasing Authority: An officer appointed by the Government to perform the functions of a Licensing Authority under this Act.
key_definitions.Lime-shells: The shells of all varieties of shell fish by whatever name called.
key_definitions.offer for sale: Includes an intimation by a dealer or producer of the price proposed by him for a sale of lime-shells made by the publication of a price list, by exposing his lime-shells for sale in association with a mark indicating price, by the furnishing of a quotation or otherwise however, this Act;
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act;
key_definitions.producer: A person carrying on the business of collecting lime-shells and stocking the same for sale. A dealer or producer shall be deemed to be in possession of lime-shells (a) when they are held on his behalf by another person; (b) notwithstanding that they are mortgaged to another person.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its territorial extent, and when it commences.
Defines various terms used in the Act, such as "dealer", "purchasing Authority", "lime-shells", "offer for sale", "prescribed", and "producer".
Deals with the licensing of dealers and producers of lime-shells. It outlines the process for applying for a license, conditions for refusal, and the procedure for appeal.

main_sections.section_title: Fixing of maximum prices and maximum quantities which may be held or sold.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to fix maximum prices and quantities of lime-shells that may be sold or held. These can be varied for different localities or dealers/producers.

main_sections.section_title: Restrictions on sale, etc., where maximum is fixed under section 4.
main_sections.description: Prohibits the sale or offer for sale of lime-shells exceeding the maximum quantity fixed under section 4, or selling to any person any quantity exceeding that limit.

main_sections.section_title: Duty to declare possession of excess stocks.
main_sections.description: Requires dealers or producers to report excess stocks of lime-shells to the Licensing Authority, who may direct their storage or disposal.
States that no dealer or producer licensed under the Act shall refuse to sell without sufficient cause, except when limited by quantity.
Mandates that every dealer or producer must give a cash memorandum when selling lime-shells, with specific details and value.
Prohibits the disposal of lime-shells except in specified circumstances and under conditions laid out by the Government.
Outlines the penalties for contravening the provisions of the Act or rules made thereunder. Penalties include imprisonment and fines.
Deals with offences committed by companies, making persons in charge of the company's business liable. It also clarifies when directors may be deemed guilty.
States that no person other than a police officer or Inspector of Police shall investigate any offence under this Act.
Grants competent persons the power to search any place and seize any lime-shells believed to be related to an offence under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
main_sections.description: Provides protection against legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith under the Act.
Allows the Government to exempt any person or class of persons from any provisions of the Act, subject to conditions and notifications.

Grants the Government the power to make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act, including regulations on licensing, fees, maintenance of records, and other related matters. All rules must be published in the Gazette.

important_rules: Dealers and producers must obtain a license.
Dealers or producers cannot refuse to sell lime-shells without sufficient cause.
A cash memorandum must be provided with every sale of lime-shells.
The Government can fix maximum prices and quantities for lime-shells.
Excess stocks of lime-shells must be declared to the Licensing Authority.
Rules made by the Government under this Act must be published in the Gazette.

penalties: Whoever contravenes the provisions of this Act or any terms and conditions of a license issued thereunder shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
The court may order the confiscation of any stock of lime-shells involved in an offence.
Offences by companies can lead to penalties for individuals in charge of the company's business.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Licensing Authority, Government officials (Inspectors of Police, police officers).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Investigation of offences, search and seizure of lime-shells, prosecution, imposition of penalties (imprisonment and fines), confiscation of property.

rights: Producers have the right to obtain a license.
Dealers have the right to obtain a license.
Individuals have the right to appeal decisions of the Licensing Authority regarding licenses.
duties: Dealers and producers have a duty to obtain a license.
Dealers and producers have a duty to declare possession of excess stocks.
Dealers and producers have a duty to provide a cash memorandum with each sale.
Individuals must comply with the provisions of the Act and any rules made thereunder.
Companies must ensure their officers comply with the Act.
obligations: Obligation to sell lime-shells only under a license.
Obligation to adhere to maximum prices and quantities if fixed by the Government.
Obligation to provide accurate information to the Licensing Authority.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining a license: Application to the Licensing Authority, conditions for grant or refusal, appeal process.
Procedure for fixing maximum prices and quantities: Notification by the Government in the Gazette.
Procedure for declaring excess stocks: Reporting to the Licensing Authority and following directions for storage or disposal.
Procedure for search and seizure: Conducted by authorized personnel based on reasonable belief of an offence.
Procedure for making rules: Government notification in the Gazette.
administration: Government of Travancore-Cochin (likely through departments related to trade, fisheries, or natural resources).
important_notes: The Act was repealed by Act 18 of 1958.
The Act extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin.
The Act came into force on a date specified by notification in the Gazette.
Exemptions from the Act can be granted by the Government.
Protection is provided for actions taken in good faith under the Act.

title: The Travancore-Cochin Live-stock Improvement Act, 1954
purpose: An Act to provide for the improvement of live-stock in the State of Travancore-Cochin.
scope: Applies to the State of Travancore-Cochin.

key_definitions.cow: means a buffalo-cow and a heifer
key_definitions.Director: means the officer appointed by the Government as the Director of Animal Husbandry and includes any other person on whom the powers or duties of the Director under this Act have been conferred or imposed under Section 3
key_definitions.licensing Officer: means the Director or any other officer or person authorised to grant licences under Section 4
key_definitions.prescribed: means prescribed by rules made under this Act
key_definitions.person: is said to 'keep a bull' if he owns the bull or has the bull in his possession or custody

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Live-stock Improvement Act, 1954. It extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin. This section shall come into force at once, and the Government may, from time to time by notification in the Gazette, apply all or any of the remaining provisions of this Act to the whole or any portion of the State of Travancore-Cochin from such date and for such period, if any, as may be specified in the notification, and may cancel or modify any such notification.
Defines terms used in the Act, including 'bull', 'cow', 'Director', 'licensing Officer', 'prescribed', and 'person'.
The Government may by special order confer or impose on any person all or any of the powers or duties conferred or imposed by the Director under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Bulls which have attained a certain age to be licensed.
main_sections.description: No person shall keep a bull which has attained the prescribed age except under and in accordance with the terms, conditions and restrictions of a licence granted under this Section, unless it is effectively castrated. Every licence under this section shall be granted by the Director or any officer or person authorised by him by general or special order. It shall be in such form, for such period, and subject to such terms, conditions and restrictions as may be prescribed. No fee shall be charged for the grant of the licence.

The licensing officer may refuse to grant or may revoke a licence in respect of any bull if in his opinion the bull appears to be: (a) defective or inferior in conformation and consequently likely to beget defective or inferior progeny, or (b) suffering from an incurable, contagious or infectious disease or from any other disease rendering the bull unsuitable for breeding purposes, or (c) of a breed which it is undesirable to propagate in the area in which it is kept. The licensing officer may also revoke a licence granted in respect of any bull kept within his jurisdiction (whether such licence was granted by himself or by any other officer) if in his opinion: (a) the licence was granted under circumstances of which the licensing officer was not aware at the time of granting the licence, or (b) there has been a breach of any of the terms, conditions or restrictions of the licence. If a licence is revoked under this section, the officer revoking the licence shall give notice thereof to the person keeping the bull or to the person stated in the licence to be the owner of the bull. The notice shall set out the grounds of the revocation.

A licence granted in respect of a bull shall be surrendered without delay to the licensing officer, if: (a) the period specified in the licence expires, or (b) the licence is revoked under this Act, or (c) the bull dies, or is certified by the prescribed officer to have been effectively castrated by a method and in a manner approved by the Director.

The licensing officer may by order require any person keeping a bull to submit it for inspection by himself or by any officer or person deputed by him for the purpose, at any reasonable time, either at the place where the bull is kept for the time being or at any other reasonable place specified in the order, and thereupon it shall be the duty of the person keeping the bull to submit it for inspection accordingly, and render all reasonable assistance in connection with such inspection to the officer concerned.

main_sections.section_title: Power to order castration of bulls.
main_sections.description: The licensing officer may by order require any person keeping a bull which in his opinion has attained the prescribed age and in respect of which no licence is for the time being in force under this Act to have it castrated, within one month from the date of the service of the order, by a method and in a manner approved by the Director and specified in the order. Such castration shall be performed, or caused to be performed by the licensing officer free of charge unless the owner or other person keeping the bull desires to make his own arrangements for complying with the order.

main_sections.section_title: Duty to inform owner of contents of notice or order of castration.
main_sections.description: If any notice or order is served under Section 7 or Section 8 on any person who is not the owner of the bull it shall be the duty of that person forthwith to take all reasonable steps to inform the owner of the contents of such notice or order, and if he fails to do so, he shall be liable to indemnify the owner against any loss the owner may sustain by reason of such failure.

It shall be the duty of any person who for the time being keeps a bull in respect of which a licence has been obtained and is in force, to produce such licence: (a) within a reasonable time, at any place where the bull is for the time being, on demand made by a licensing officer or an officer of the Animal Husbandry Department not below the rank of Veterinary Surgeon, or an Officer of the Revenue Department not below the rank of Deputy Tahsildar or such other officer as may be authorised in this behalf by the Government by general or special order; or (b) before a cow is served by the bull, on demand made by the person in charge of the cow.

Whoever: (a) keeps a bull in contravention of this Act or of any rule or order made thereunder, or of any terms, conditions or restrictions of a licence, or (b) neglects or fails to submit a bull for inspection when required to do so under Section 7, or (c) neglects or fails to comply with an order served under Section 8, or (d) neglects or fails to produce a licence when required to do so under Section 10, shall be punishable with fine which may extend to fifty rupees and in the case of a second or any subsequent offence with fine which may extend to one hundred rupees.

main_sections.section_title: Power of licensing officer to castrate bulls.
main_sections.description: If a person who keeps a bull neglects or fails to submit it for inspection or to have it castrated when required to do so under Section 7, or Section 8, the licensing officer may direct that the bull shall be castrated by a method and in a manner approved by the Director and marked with a prescribed mark in the prescribed manner, free of charge. If it is not known in whose possession, possession or custody a bull is for the time being and the fact cannot be ascertained after an inquiry in the prescribed manner, the licensing officer may seize the bull or cause it to be seized, and if he is of opinion that the bull has attained the prescribed age and is unsuitable for breeding purposes on any of the grounds specified in sub-section (1) of Section 5, he may direct that the bull shall be castrated by a method and in a manner approved by the Director and marked with a prescribed mark in the prescribed manner, free of charge. Every bull seized under clause (a) shall, after it has been castrated and marked as aforesaid where necessary, be sold by public auction or its proceeds of sale shall have paid to the owner after deducting therefrom the costs, charges and expenses incurred for the maintenance and sale of the bull; and in any other case, the bull shall be delivered to the owner on payment of the costs, charges and expenses incurred for its maintenance.

main_sections.section_title: Power of licensing officer, etc., to inspect or mark bulls and enter premises.
main_sections.description: For the purposes of this Act, a licensing officer or any officer or person authorised by him in this behalf shall have power at all reasonable times— (a) to inspect any bull; (b) to mark any bull with a prescribed mark in the prescribed manner; and (c) subject to such conditions and restrictions, if any, as may be prescribed, to enter any premises or other place where he has reason to believe that a bull is kept.

main_sections.section_title: Duty of officers to report offences, etc.
main_sections.description: It shall be the duty of all officers and servants of the Animal Husbandry and Revenue Departments: (a) to give immediate information to the nearest licensing officer of the commission of any offence, or of the intention or preparation to commit any offence, punishable under this Act, which may come to their knowledge; and (b) to assist any licensing officer in carrying out the provisions of this Act.
No Magistrate shall take cognizance of any offence under this Act except upon a complaint made by a licensing officer or any person authorised by such officer in this behalf.

The Director, every licensing officer, all officers and persons authorised by the Director or a licensing officer under this Act, and all officers and servants of the Animal Husbandry and Revenue Departments shall be deemed to be public servants within the meaning of Section 21 of the Indian Penal Code.

(1) No suit, prosecution or other proceeding shall lie against any officer or servant of the Government for any act done or purporting to be done under this Act without the previous sanction of the Government. (2) No officer or servant of the Government shall be liable in respect of any such act in any civil or criminal proceeding if the act was done in good faith in the course of the execution of duties or the discharge of functions imposed by or under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Limitation for certain suits and prosecutions.
main_sections.description: No suit shall be instituted against the Government and no suit, prosecution or other proceeding shall be instituted against any officer or servant of the Government in respect of any act done or purporting to be done under this Act, unless the suit, prosecution or other proceeding is instituted within six months from the date of the act complained of.

The Government may at any time either suo motu or on application call for and examine the record of any order passed by, or any proceedings recorded by, any officer or person under this Act, for the purpose of satisfying themselves as to the legality or propriety of such order or as to the regularity of such proceedings, and may pass such order in reference thereto as they think fit. Nothing contained in this section shall apply to the orders or proceedings of any Court or Magistrate.

(1) The Government may make rules to carry out the purposes of this Act. (2) In particular and without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing power, such rules may provide for (a) all matters expressly required or allowed by this Act to be prescribed; (b) the circumstances in which duplicates of licences may be granted, the fees which may be charged for the grant of such duplicates and the conditions, restrictions and limitations subject to which they may be granted; (c) the powers to be exercised and the duties to be performed by officers appointed under this Act, and the procedure of such officers; and (d) the service of notices and orders issued under this Act. (3) In making a rule under sub-section (1) or sub-section (2) the Government may provide that a person guilty of a breach thereof shall be punishable with fine which may extend to fifty rupees. (4) The power to make rules conferred by this section shall be subject to the condition of the rules being made after previous publication. (5) All rules made under this section shall be published in the Gazette and upon such publication shall have effect as if enacted in this Act. (6) All rules made under this section shall be laid for not less than seven days before the Legislative Assembly as soon as possible after they are made, and shall be subject to such modifications as the Legislative Assembly may make during the session in which they are so laid.

Nothing contained in this Act shall apply to a bull dedicated in good faith to a religious purpose in accordance with any religious usage or custom, provided that notice of the dedication is given in the prescribed manner to the licensing officer.
The Cochin Live-stock Improvement Act, III of 1120 is hereby repealed.

important_rules: No person shall keep a bull which has attained the prescribed age unless it is licensed and effectively castrated (Section 4).
Licensing officers can refuse or revoke licences for bulls that are defective, infertile, diseased, or of an undesirable breed (Section 5).
Owners must surrender licences if the bull dies, is castrated, or the licence expires or is revoked (Section 6).
Licensing officers can order castration of bulls if they are not licensed or meet certain criteria (Section 8).
Penalties include fines for contravening the Act, neglecting inspection, failing to comply with orders, or failing to produce a licence (Section 11).
Licensing officers have the power to seize and castrate bulls if the owner is unknown or fails to comply with orders (Section 12).
Licensing officers and authorized personnel can inspect bulls and enter premises where bulls are kept (Section 13).
Government may make rules concerning various aspects of the Act, including licensing, fees, and procedures (Section 20).

penalties: Fine not exceeding fifty rupees for the first offence and not exceeding one hundred rupees for a subsequent offence for contravention of the Act, neglecting inspection, failing to comply with castration orders, or failing to produce a licence.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Licensing Officer, Director, and other authorized officers of the Animal Husbandry and Revenue Departments.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Inspection of bulls, ordering castration, seizing and selling bulls, prosecution of offenders, and making rules and regulations.

rights: Right to receive a licence for a bull that meets the prescribed age and conditions, unless it's effectively castrated.
Right to have a licence surrendered without delay under specified conditions.
Right to be informed of the seizure and sale of a bull if the owner is unknown.
Right to receive proceeds from the sale of a seized bull after deducting costs.
Right to seek revision of orders passed by officers by the Government.
duties: Duty to obtain a licence for a bull that has attained the prescribed age (Section 4).
Duty to surrender a licence if the bull dies, is castrated, or the licence expires/is revoked (Section 6).
Duty to submit a bull for inspection upon order (Section 7).
Duty to comply with castration orders (Section 8).
Duty to inform the owner if a notice or order is served on someone who is not the owner (Section 9).
Duty to produce the licence of a bull when requested (Section 10).
Duty of officers and servants of Animal Husbandry and Revenue Departments to report offences and assist licensing officers (Section 14).
obligations: Obligation to comply with the terms, conditions, and restrictions of a licence.
Obligation to allow castration of a bull as ordered by the licensing officer.
Obligation to ensure that a bull is not served if it is under a castration order.
Obligation to pay costs, charges, and expenses incurred for the maintenance and sale of a seized bull if the owner is known.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining a licence for a bull of a prescribed age.
Procedure for refusal and revocation of licences by the licensing officer.
Procedure for surrender of a licence.
Procedure for inspection of bulls by the licensing officer or authorized personnel.
Procedure for ordering castration of bulls and compliance by the owner.
Procedure for seizure and sale of bulls if the owner is unknown or fails to comply.
Procedure for reporting offences and assisting in enforcement.
administration: The Animal Husbandry Department and the Revenue Department of the Government of Travancore-Cochin.
important_notes: No fee is charged for the grant of a licence for a bull (Section 4).
The Act does not apply to bulls dedicated in good faith to a religious purpose, provided notice is given to the licensing officer (Section 21).
The Cochin Live-stock Improvement Act, III of 1120 is repealed (Section 22).

title: The Travancore Cochin Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act
purpose: To provide for the imposition and collection of a tax on entertainments in local authority areas.
scope: The Act applies to the City of Trivandrum, the Corporation of Trivandrum, Municipal areas, and areas within the jurisdiction of a Panchayat or Village Union, and to any other local area as may be declared by the Government.

key_definitions.entertainment: Includes any exhibition, performance, amusement, game, sport, or race to which persons are admitted for payment.
key_definitions.local authority: Means the area within the jurisdiction of a local authority, including the City of Trivandrum, Municipal areas, and areas within the jurisdiction of a Panchayat or Village Union.
key_definitions.payment for admission: Includes any amount made by a person who having been admitted to one part of a place of entertainment is subsequently admitted to another part thereof, or admission for a season ticket or for other accommodation.
key_definitions.proprietor: In relation to any entertainment includes any person responsible for the management thereof.

main_sections.description: The Act is called The Travancore-Cochin Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1951. It extends to the City of Trivandrum and all areas in the State of Travancore-Cochin. It shall come into force on such date as the Government may by notification in the Gazette appoint.
Defines key terms used in the Act, including 'admission', 'entertainment', 'agriculture', 'institution', 'local authority', 'payment for admission', 'prescribed', and 'proprietor'.

main_sections.section_title: General provisions regarding the levy of the tax and the rate of the tax
main_sections.description: Any local authority in whose local area this Act is in force may levy a tax (hereinafter referred to as the entertainments tax) at a rate not less than ten per cent nor exceeding twenty per cent, on all payments for admission to any entertainment.

main_sections.section_title: Composition and consolidated payment of tax
main_sections.description: Provides for the proprietor of any entertainment in respect of which the entertainments tax is payable under such section as the local authority may, subject to general rules, make in this behalf, to compound the tax payable in respect of such entertainment for a consolidated payment.

main_sections.section_title: Admission of persons to entertainments subject to tax
main_sections.description: No person shall be admitted for payment to any entertainment where the payment is subject to the entertainments tax, except with a ticket stamped with an impressed, embossed, engraved or adhesive label issued by the local authority indicating the proper tax for such ticket, or in special cases with the approval of the local authority through a barrier which, or by means of a mechanical contrivance which automatically registers the number of persons admitted.

The entertainments tax shall be levied in respect of each person admitted for payment and in the case of admission by ticket, shall be paid by means of a ticket, or in the case of admission otherwise than by ticket, shall be calculated and paid on the number of admissions.

main_sections.section_title: Entertainment exempt from payment of tax
main_sections.description: Lists categories of entertainments that are not liable for tax, including wholly educational, cultural or scientific institutions, and institutions not conducted for profit and established solely for the purpose of promoting public health or the interest of agriculture or a manufacturing industry, and religious or charitable purposes.
Specifies how the entertainments tax and any fines imposed under the Act shall be recovered by the local authority in the same manner as any tax payable to the local authority.
Any officer authorized by the local authority may enter any place of entertainment to check compliance with the Act and rules. Penalties are prescribed for obstruction or failure to pay tax.

If any person is admitted for payment to any place of entertainment and the provisions of Section 5 are not complied with, the proprietor of the entertainment to which such person is admitted shall, on conviction by a Magistrate, be liable in respect of each such offence to a fine not exceeding two hundred rupees, and in addition to pay any tax which should have been paid.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the Government to make rules
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to make rules to carry out all or any of the purposes of the Act, including rules for the composition and consolidated payment of tax, and for the presentation and disposal of applications for exemption from payment of the entertainments tax.

main_sections.section_title: Power of the local authority to make bye-laws
main_sections.description: Empowers any local authority to make bye-laws, not inconsistent with the Act or rules made thereunder, for the supply and use of tickets, the admission of more than one person on a ticket, the regulation of the time and mode of collecting the tax, and for controlling barriers or mechanical contrivances, checking of accounts, furnishing of returns, renewal of damaged or spoiled labels, keeping of accounts, and regulation of time and mode of collecting the tax.
Repeals certain sections of the Cochin Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1914, and specific sections of the Travancore Municipalities Act, 1110 and the Trivandrum City Municipal Act, 1116.

important_rules: Entertainment tax shall be levied on all payments for admission to any entertainment, at a rate not less than ten per cent nor exceeding twenty per cent.
No person shall be admitted to an entertainment subject to tax without a proper tax-stamped ticket or approval from the local authority.
Local authorities may levy a tax on entertainments at a specified rate.
The Government may exempt certain entertainments from tax.
Bye-laws can be made by local authorities for the effective implementation of the Act, including rules for tickets, admission, and tax collection.

penalties: Fine not exceeding two hundred rupees for obstruction or non-payment of tax.

Breach of bye-laws may be punishable with a fine which may extend to fifty rupees, and in case of a continuing breach, with a further fine which may extend to fifteen rupees for every day during which the breach continues after conviction for the first breach.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Local authorities and officers authorized by them.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Inspection of entertainment venues, checking of tickets and admissions, recovery of tax and fines, and prosecution for offenses.

rights: Right of the local authority to levy entertainments tax.
Right of the Government to make rules and grant exemptions.
Right of the local authority to make bye-laws.
duties: Duty of proprietors to collect and pay entertainments tax.
Duty of proprietors to issue proper tax-stamped tickets.
Duty of proprietors to provide returns and accounts to the local authority.
Duty of every person to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules and bye-laws.
obligations: Obligation to pay entertainments tax on admission to taxable entertainments.
Obligation to obtain authorization for special cases of admission or ticket dispensing.

key_procedures: Application for exemption from entertainment tax (if applicable).
Issuance and use of tax-stamped tickets for admission.
Payment of tax by proprietors, either by tickets or through composition.
Inspection and verification by local authority officers.
Recovery of tax and penalties.
Making and enforcing bye-laws by local authorities.
Making rules by the Government.
administration: Local Authorities (e.g., Municipalities, Panchayats, Village Unions) and the State Government.
important_notes: Certain entertainments are exempt from tax (e.g., educational, cultural, scientific, charitable).
The Government has the power to make rules and issue notifications to implement the Act.
Local authorities have the power to make bye-laws for specific local needs.
The Act repeals certain previous legislative provisions related to entertainments tax.

title: The Travancore Cochin Local Authorities Loans Act, 1951
purpose: To provide for the borrowing of money by local authorities in the Travancore-Cochin area.
scope: Applies to local authorities within the State of Travancore-Cochin.

key_definitions.local authority: Any person legally entitled to the control or management of any local, village or municipal fund, or legally entitled to impose any cess, rate, duty or tax within any local area.
key_definitions.funds: Used with reference to any local authority includes any local, village or municipal fund to the control or management of which such authority is legally entitled and any cess, rate, duty or tax which such authority is legally entitled to impose and any property vested in such authority.
key_definitions.prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.work: Includes a survey, whether incidental to any other work or not.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Local Authorities Loans Act, 1951. It extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin and shall come into force at once.
Defines 'local authority' and 'funds' as described in key_definitions.
Details the conditions under which local authorities can borrow money, including the need for Government sanction and the purposes for which loans can be raised.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to make rules.
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to make rules consistent with this Act regarding the nature of funds, the manner of borrowing, applications for permission, inquiries, forms, and other incidental matters related to loans.

main_sections.section_title: Remedy by attachment of loan not repaid.
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for attaching the property of a local authority if a loan is not repaid, including the appointment of an officer by the Government to manage the attached property and the application of proceeds to repay the loan.

main_sections.section_title: Recovery of money lent before commencement of Act.
main_sections.description: States that no local authority shall, except as provided by or under this Act, borrow money upon the security of its funds for any purpose for which it could not do so before the Act's passing.

Repeals and amends certain provisions of the Travancore Local Authorities Loans Act, 1120 and the Cochin Municipal Act, XVIII of 1113, and the Travancore-Cochin Panchayat Act (II of 1950), stating that such repeal or amendment will not affect the previous operation of the enactments or the validity of anything done or any action taken under them.

important_rules: Local authorities must obtain prior sanction from the Government to borrow money.

Loans can be raised for specific purposes, including carrying out works, relief and establishment, prevention of disease, and any measures connected with or ancillary to purposes of clauses (ii) and (iii).
No portion of money borrowed shall be applied for purposes other than that for which it was borrowed.
The time for repayment of any loan borrowed before the commencement of this Act shall not exceed sixty years.

The time for repayment of any money borrowed for the purpose of discharging any previous loan shall not, except with the express sanction of the Government, extend beyond the unexpired period of the period for which such previous loan was raised.

Nothing in this section shall be deemed to authorize any local authority to borrow or spend money for any purpose for which, under the law for the time being in force, it is not authorized to apply its funds.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through rules made by the Government, and through the attachment and sale of the local authority's property in case of loan non-repayment.

rights: Local authorities have the right to borrow money under specific conditions and with Government sanction.
duties: Local authorities have a duty to repay borrowed loans.
Local authorities must ensure that borrowed funds are used only for the purpose for which they were borrowed.
obligations: Local authorities are obligated to follow the rules and procedures laid down by the Government for borrowing and repayment of loans.

key_procedures: Procedure for borrowing: Obtain Government sanction, specify the purpose, and adhere to repayment timelines.
Procedure for loan repayment: Repay loans within the stipulated time.
Procedure for non-repayment: If a loan is not repaid, the Government can attach the property of the local authority and apply the proceeds to repay the loan and associated costs.
administration: The Government of Travancore-Cochin
important_notes: The Act provides for the repeal and amendment of certain earlier legislative provisions related to local authority loans.
The Government has the power to make rules concerning the application and management of loans.

title: The Travancore Cochin Maternity Benefit Act
purpose: To prevent the employment of women in factories and plantations for some time before and some time after confinement and to provide for payment of maternity benefit to them.
scope: The Act applies to women employed in factories and plantations within the State of Travancore-Cochin.

key_definitions.employer: Includes the occupier and the manager of a plantation or a factory.
key_definitions.factory: Means a factory as defined in the Factories Act, 1948.
key_definitions.inspector: Means an Inspector appointed under Section 9.
key_definitions.worker: In relation to a factory has the same meaning as assigned to it by the Factories Act, 1948 and in relation to a plantation, means a person employed in a plantation directly or through an agency, whether for hire or not, to do any work, skilled or unskilled, manual or clerical but does not include a person whose total emoluments exceed two hundred rupees per mensem or any member of the managerial staff, that is to say, the Manager, Assistant Manager, Supervisor or other Agent of the employer.
key_definitions.plantation: Means any estate which is maintained for the purpose of growing cinchona, rubber, coffee, tea or cardamom, and (i) which is fifty acres or more in extent, or (ii) in which fifty or more persons are employed or were employed on any day of the preceding twelve months for that purpose.
key_definitions.maternity benefit: Means the amount of money payable under the provisions of this Act to a woman employed in a plantation or a factory.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Maternity Benefit Act, 1952, extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin, and shall come into force on such date as the Government may appoint by notification in the Gazette.
Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including employer, factory, inspector, worker, plantation, maternity benefit, prescribed, and woman.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of employment of women in factories and plantations immediately after confinement.
main_sections.description: Prohibits the employment of women in factories and plantations during the four weeks immediately following the day of her confinement.

main_sections.section_title: Right to maternity benefit of women in factories and plantations.
main_sections.description: Entitles every woman in a factory or plantation to be paid maternity benefit at the rate of five rupees and four annas a week for the actual days of her absence, provided she has been in employment for at least eighty weeks immediately preceding the date of her confinement, for the period immediately preceding her confinement and eight weeks following it.

main_sections.section_title: Notice of claim of maternity benefit and payment thereof.
main_sections.description: Outlines the process for claiming maternity benefit, including providing notice to the employer and the employer's obligation to pay the benefit. It also specifies conditions under which a woman is not entitled to maternity benefit.

main_sections.section_title: Payment of maternity benefit in case of claimant's death.
main_sections.description: Details how maternity benefit is to be paid if the claimant dies. The payment will be made to the person who undertakes the care of the child, if the child is living, and if not, to the nominee mentioned in the notice given under Section 5.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of notice of dismissal to woman in certain cases.
main_sections.description: Prohibits an employer from dismissing a woman within six months of her confinement or giving notice of dismissal within that period, except for gross misconduct. Dismissal for any other reason is unlawful and the woman is still entitled to maternity benefit.

States that if a woman works in any factory or plantation after she has been permitted by her employer to absent herself under the provisions of Section 5, she shall forfeit her claim to payment of maternity benefit to which she is entitled.
Empowers the Government to appoint officers by notification in the Gazette to inspect factories and plantations and assign them such local limits as they think fit.
Specifies the powers and duties of Inspectors, including inspecting any place within their local limits, questioning employers and employees, and examining registers and records.
Declares Inspectors to be public servants within the meaning of Section 21 of the Indian Penal Code.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for contravention of Act by employer.
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for employers who contravene the provisions of the Act or any rule made thereunder, including a fine extendable to two hundred and fifty rupees.

States that no prosecution under the Act shall be instituted except by or with the previous sanction of the Inspector. No Court inferior to that of a Magistrate of the First Class shall try any offence under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Period of limitation for prosecution under Act.
