main_sections.description: Specifies that no Court shall take cognizance of or try a person for any offence under the Act or any rule thereunder unless complaint thereof has been made within six months of the date on which the offence was committed. The period of six months includes the time, if any, taken for the purpose of obtaining the previous sanction of the Inspector.

Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of the Act, including rules for preparation and maintenance of a muster roll, inspection of factories and plantations, exercise of powers by Inspectors, and payment of maternity benefit.

main_sections.section_title: A copy of Act and rules to be exhibited in factories and plantations employing women.
main_sections.description: Mandates that a copy of the Act and the rules be exhibited in a conspicuous place in every factory and plantation employing women, in the local language.
Repeals the Travancore Maternity Benefit Act, XIX of 1116 and the Cochin Maternity Benefit Act, XXVII of 1118.

important_rules: Women employed in factories and plantations cannot be employed for four weeks immediately following the day of their confinement.

Maternity benefit is to be paid at the rate of five rupees and four annas a week for the actual days of absence, provided the woman has been employed for at least eighty weeks preceding the date of her confinement.

A woman is not entitled to maternity benefit unless she has been employed in the factory or plantation from whom she claims maternity benefit for at least one hundred and fifty days during the period of twelve months immediately preceding the date on which she gives notice.
If a woman works in any factory or plantation after being permitted to absent herself for confinement, she forfeits her maternity benefit.
Employers are prohibited from dismissing a woman within six months of her confinement, except for gross misconduct.
A copy of the Act and rules must be displayed in local language in factories and plantations employing women.

penalties: Contravention of the Act or any rule by an employer is punishable with a fine which may extend to two hundred and fifty rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Inspectors appointed by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspection of factories and plantations, questioning employers and employees, examination of registers and records, and prosecution for contravention of the Act.

rights: Right to maternity benefit for women employed in factories and plantations.
Right to receive maternity benefit even if dismissed under certain circumstances.
Right to nominate another person to receive maternity benefit.
Right to receive benefit if the claimant dies, to the person caring for the child or nominee.
duties: Duty of employer to provide maternity benefit.
Duty of employer not to dismiss a woman within six months of her confinement, except for gross misconduct.
Duty to display a copy of the Act and rules in factories and plantations employing women.
obligations: Obligation for women to provide notice of claim for maternity benefit.
Obligation for women to not work in a factory or plantation during the period for which maternity benefit is paid.

key_procedures: Claiming Maternity Benefit: A woman must give notice to her employer of her claim for maternity benefit. She may nominate another person to receive the benefit on her behalf. The employer is obligated to pay the benefit.

Inspection and Enforcement: Inspectors appointed by the Government have the power to inspect factories and plantations, examine records, and take action against employers for contravention of the Act. Prosecutions require the sanction of the Inspector.
Exhibition of Act and Rules: A copy of the Act and rules must be prominently displayed in the local language in all factories and plantations employing women.
administration: The Government of Travancore-Cochin (implied by the name of the Act and the power to make rules and appoint inspectors).
important_notes: The Act repeals the Travancore Maternity Benefit Act, XIX of 1116 and the Cochin Maternity Benefit Act, XXVII of 1118.
The Act extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin.
The Act came into force on a date appointed by the Government in the Gazette.
Women employed in plantations with less than 50 acres or employing less than 50 persons are not covered under the definition of 'plantation' for the purpose of this Act.

title: The Travancore Cochin Medical Practitioners Act, 1953
purpose: To regulate the qualifications and registration of medical practitioners in the State of Travancore-Cochin, to define what shall be deemed to be qualified medical practitioners, and to prescribe penalties for illegal practice.
scope: Applies to the State of Travancore-Cochin. It concerns individuals practicing medicine, including modern medicine, homoeopathic medicine, ayurvedic medicine, siddha medicine, and unani tibbi medicine.

key_definitions.legally_qualified_medical_practitioner: Means a practitioner whose name has been registered in Part A of the Register, or who possesses a recognized qualification specified in the Schedule.
key_definitions.registered_practitioner: Means a practitioner whose name has been entered in the Register.
key_definitions.medical_practitioner: Includes a practitioner of modern medicine, homoeopathic medicine, ayurvedic medicine, siddha medicine, or unani tibbi medicine.

main_sections.description: Details the process and requirements for registration of medical practitioners, including application procedures, fees, and the authority for registration.

Specifies the fee for application for registration under this Act, which is Rs. 20. Also details fees for registered practitioners to appear in respect of any additional recognized qualification (Rs. 5).

main_sections.section_title: List of practitioners as on 1st April 1953
main_sections.description: The Registrar shall prepare and keep a list called 'List of persons in practice on the first day of April 1953'. Every person not being a registered practitioner who has been in practice for one year or more, may be entitled to have their name entered in the list, with a fee of Rs. 10.

main_sections.section_title: Practitioners registered under the Travancore Medical Practitioners Act, 1119
main_sections.description: Every practitioner registered under the Travancore Medical Practitioners Act, 1119 shall be deemed to be a practitioner registered under this Act if their name is entered in the register maintained under the Travancore Medical Practitioners Act, 1119 and they are registered in India.

A person whose name is in the register may be removed for disqualifications mentioned in clause (b) to (d) of Section 7, or for professional misconduct. A registered practitioner shall not be relieved of obligations or compliance with rules of conduct which may be imposed upon registered practitioners.
The Registrar shall, every year or before the date to be fixed by the appropriate council, publish a full list of names and qualifications of all practitioners registered under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Persons not registered under this Act, etc., not to practise
main_sections.description: Prohibits unregistered persons from practicing medicine. Defines who is considered a registered practitioner. Also states that the section shall not apply to any person or class of persons or to any specified area in the State where none of the three classes of practitioners mentioned above carries on medical practice. It also does not apply to a practitioner eligible for registration under Section 23 after filing the application for registration, or until the period prescribed for applications under Section 23 expires.
Any person who acts in contravention of Section 38 shall, on conviction, be punishable with fine which may extend to Rs. 100 for the first offence, and to Rs. 500 for every subsequent offence.

The right of conferring, granting or issuing in the State of Travancore-Cochin degrees, diplomas, licenses, certificates or other documents stating or implying that the holder, grantee or recipient thereof is qualified to practise modern medicine, homoeopathic medicine, ayurvedic medicine, siddha medicine or unani tibbi medicine shall be exercisable only by an authority, body or institution mentioned in the Schedule.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of conferment etc. of degree etc.
main_sections.description: No person shall confer, grant or issue, or hold himself out as entitled to confer, grant or issue any degree, diploma, license, certificate or other document relating to the practice of medicine. Whoever contravenes this shall be punishable with fine.

important_rules: No practitioner shall be eligible for registration under sub-section (1), sub-section (3) or sub-section (4) if he is subject to any of the disqualifications mentioned in clauses (a) to (c) of Section 7.
Every registered practitioner who applies to the Registrar for registration in respect of any additional recognized qualification shall pay a fee of Rs. 5.

Nothing in sub-section (1) or sub-section (2) shall be deemed to apply to any person whose name has been registered for the primary or additional recognized qualification, as the case may be, under any enactment for the time being in force in India for the registration of practitioners in modern medicine, homoeopathic medicine or indigenous medicine.
All rules made under this section shall be published in the Gazette.

penalties: Fine up to Rs. 100 for the first offence of illegal practice (contravention of Section 38).
Fine up to Rs. 500 for every subsequent offence of illegal practice (contravention of Section 38).
Fine for contravening provisions of sub-section (1) of Section 41.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Registrar, the appropriate council, and the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through registration processes, preparation and publication of lists of practitioners, removal of names from registers for misconduct or disqualification, and penalties for illegal practice.

rights: Right to apply for registration if eligible.
Right to have one's name entered in the list of practitioners if in practice for a specified period.
Right to appeal to the council against the action of the Registrar.
Right to appeal to the Government from the decision of the council.
duties: Duty to practice only if registered.
Duty to comply with rules of conduct.
Duty to obtain recognized qualifications.
obligations: Obligation to have one's name entered in the register to practice legally.
Obligation to pay prescribed fees for registration and other services.

key_procedures: Application for registration: Applications for registration under Section 23 shall be sent direct to the Registrar. The Registrar shall place all applications under this section before the committee of the appropriate council appointed for the purpose for its report.

Removal from registers: A name can be removed if the person becomes subject to disqualifications or for professional misconduct. The appropriate council, on sufficient cause shown, may direct that the name of the practitioner so removed shall be re-entered in the register.
Appeal to the council: Any person aggrieved by the action of the Registrar regarding registration may appeal to the appropriate council.

Appeal to the Government: An appeal shall lie to the Government from every decision of a council under Sections 24, 27, 28 and 33. Such appeal shall be preferred within three months from the date on which notice of the order of the council was issued.
administration: The Registrar and the appropriate council, with oversight by the Government.
important_notes: Provided that no practitioner shall be registered under this Act or the rules made thereunder after the expiration of one year, or such other longer period as may be fixed by the Government, from the date on which this Act comes into force.

Nothing in sub-section (1) or sub-section (2) shall be deemed to apply to any person whose name has been registered for the primary or additional recognized qualification, as the case may be, under any enactment for the time being in force in India for the registration of practitioners in modern medicine, homoeopathic medicine or indigenous medicine.

Provided that no practitioner shall be eligible for registration under sub-section (1), sub-section (3) or sub-section (4) if he is subject to any of the disqualifications mentioned in clauses (a) to (c) of Section 7.

The right of conferring, granting or issuing in the State of Travancore-Cochin degrees, diplomas, licenses, certificates or other documents stating or implying that the holder, grantee or recipient thereof is qualified to practise modern medicine, homoeopathic medicine, ayurvedic medicine, siddha medicine or unani tibbi medicine shall be exercisable only by an authority, body or institution mentioned in the Schedule.
The Government may, after previous publication, make rules to carry out all or any of the purposes of this Act not inconsistent therewith.

title: The Travancore-Cochin Nurses and Midwives Act, 1953
purpose: To provide for the registration and training of nurses and midwives in the State of Travancore-Cochin.
scope: The Act applies to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin and comes into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.

key_definitions.Council: The Travancore-Cochin Nurses and Midwives Council established under Section 3.
key_definitions.Institution: Any association which maintains or controls an establishment for training nurses or midwives or both and which is recognised by the Council.
key_definitions.Medical Council: The Council of Medical Education, established under the Travancore-Cochin Medical Practitioners Act, 1953.
key_definitions.President: Means the President of the Council.
key_definitions.Register: Means a register of nurses or midwives maintained under this Act, and 'registered' means registered under this Act.
key_definitions.Registered Practitioner: Means a practitioner who is registered in the register of practitioners for modern medicine maintained under the Travancore-Cochin Medical Practitioners Act, 1953.
key_definitions.Registrar: Means the Registrar appointed under Section 17.
key_definitions.Regulations: Means regulations made by the Council under this Act.
key_definitions.Rules: Means rules made by the Government under this Act.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its extent (the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin), and that it shall come into force on such date as the Government may appoint.
Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including Council, Institution, Medical Council, Nurse, President, Register, Registered Practitioner, Registrar, Regulations, and Rules.

main_sections.section_title: Establishment, incorporation and constitution of the Council.
main_sections.description: Details the establishment and powers of the Travancore-Cochin Nurses and Midwives Council.

main_sections.section_title: Nomination of members in default of election.
main_sections.description: Concerns the nomination of members to the Council if elections are not held.

main_sections.section_title: Nomination of members to the first Council.
main_sections.description: Specifies how members are nominated for the initial Council.
Outlines the conditions under which a person is disqualified from being a member of the Council.
Defines the duration of membership for Council members.
Addresses how vacancies on the Council are to be filled.
Covers the election and functions of the President and Vice-President of the Council, including provisions for their absence or resignation.

main_sections.section_title: Appointments to be notified in the Gazette.
main_sections.description: Requires that all appointments and nominations to the Council and the Registrar must be published in the Gazette.
Specifies the circumstances under which a member's membership ceases, including absence, disqualifications, or resignation.
Details the process for members to resign from the Council.
Ensures that the Council's proceedings are valid even if there are defects in the election or nomination of members, or if a member has taken part in proceedings without being qualified.
Governs the meeting schedule and procedures of the Council, including quorum requirements and the summoning of meetings.

main_sections.section_title: Presidency at meetings of Council and procedure thereof.
main_sections.description: Outlines who presides over Council meetings and the general procedure to be followed.
Details the payment of fees and allowances to the President, Vice-President, and other members of the Council and its Committees.
Covers the appointment, salary, allowances, and removal of the Registrar by the Government. It also outlines the Council's power to appoint other officers and servants.
Specifies the responsibilities of the Registrar, including maintaining separate registers for nurses and midwives, keeping them correct, and ensuring they are in accordance with the Act and rules.
Grants the Government power to take action if the Council fails to perform its duties or exceeds its powers, including dissolving the Council and reconstituting it.

Lays down the conditions for eligibility for registration as a nurse or midwife, including undergoing a prescribed course of training and passing an examination, or having practiced for a specified period.
Outlines the procedure for applying for registration and the required documentation, such as a certificate from a registered practitioner or the Tahsildar of the taluk.

main_sections.section_title: Refusal of Registration and removal and re-entry.
main_sections.description: Details the grounds for refusing registration and the process for removing names from the register, with provisions for re-entry.
Provides a mechanism for appealing orders made under Section 23 (refusal of registration and removal).

main_sections.section_title: Annual list of nurses and midwives.
main_sections.description: Requires the publication of an annual list of registered nurses and midwives.

main_sections.section_title: Institutions for training nurses and midwives.
main_sections.description: Deals with institutions that train nurses and midwives.

main_sections.section_title: Appeal against refusal to recognise institutions under Section 26.
main_sections.description: Provides for appeals against decisions regarding the recognition of training institutions.
Designates the authority responsible for supervision.

main_sections.section_title: Notice of commencement and continuance of practice.
main_sections.description: Requires notice of the commencement and continuance of practice by nurses and midwives.
Specifies the disabilities faced by individuals who are not registered under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for dishonest use of certificates.
main_sections.description: Prescribes penalties for the dishonest use of certificates.

main_sections.section_title: Nurses or midwives not registered under this Act not to practise.
main_sections.description: Prohibits unregistered nurses or midwives from practicing.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for unlawful assumption of title of registered nurse or midwife.
main_sections.description: Imposes penalties for unlawfully assuming the title of a registered nurse or midwife.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for instrumental manipulations by nurse or midwife.
main_sections.description: Penalizes nurses or midwives for engaging in instrumental manipulations.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to make rules.
main_sections.description: Grants the Government the power to make rules under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Council to make regulations.
main_sections.description: Grants the Council the power to make regulations under the Act.
Details the procedure for prosecuting offenses under the Act.
Specifies the jurisdiction of Magistrates in matters related to this Act.
Bars the jurisdiction of Civil Courts in certain matters under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Nurses and Midwives registered under Act XVIII of 1121 entitled to be registered under this Act.
main_sections.description: Allows nurses and midwives registered under a previous Act (Act XVIII of 1121) to be registered under this Act.
Announces the repeal of any previous enactments that are inconsistent with this Act.

penalties: Penalty for dishonest use of certificates.
Penalty for unlawful assumption of title of registered nurse or midwife.
Penalty for instrumental manipulations by nurse or midwife.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Council and the Registrar, with Government oversight and powers.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through prosecution for offenses, including the practice by unregistered persons, misuse of certificates, and unlawful assumption of titles. The Government can also dissolve the Council in case of default.

rights: Right to be registered if eligibility criteria are met.
Right to appeal against orders of refusal of registration or removal from the register.
Right to practice if registered under the Act.
duties: Duty to undergo prescribed training and pass examinations for registration.
Duty to maintain registers correctly.
Duty to notify commencement and continuance of practice.
obligations: Obligation to not practice if unregistered.
Obligation to not unlawfully assume the title of a registered nurse or midwife.

key_procedures: Registration of nurses and midwives: Application, examination, and approval by the Council.
Appeals: Process for appealing decisions related to registration and recognition of institutions.
Meeting procedures: Rules for conducting Council meetings, including quorum and voting.
Appointment and notification of Council members and Registrar.
administration: The Travancore-Cochin Nurses and Midwives Council, with the Government having overarching powers to make rules and intervene in case of default.
important_notes: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin.
Unregistered persons are subject to disabilities.
The Government has the power to make rules, and the Council has the power to make regulations.
Jurisdiction of Civil Courts is barred in certain matters.
Nurses and Midwives registered under Act XVIII of 1121 are entitled to be registered under this Act.

title: The Travancore-Cochin Panchayats (Amendment) Act, 1954
purpose: To further amend the Travancore-Cochin Panchayats Act, 1950.
scope: Applies to the Travancore-Cochin region.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Panchayats (Amendment) Act, 1954 and shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 55, Act II of 1950
main_sections.description: Amends Section 55 of the Travancore-Cochin Panchayats Act, 1950. It substitutes "Sub-section (1)" with "this section" and adds a new sub-section (3) to Section 55. This new sub-section (3) states that notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), it shall be lawful for the Government to contribute to the Panchayat Fund such amount as may, in their opinion, be necessary for meeting the expenditure in connection with the management of any institution or the execution or maintenance of any work or the performance of any duty within the Panchayat area which the Government may, from time to time, make over to the Panchayat under Section 46.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through contributions to Panchayat Fund as deemed necessary by the Government for specific purposes outlined in the amended Section 55.

rights: The Government has the right to contribute to the Panchayat Fund for specified expenditures.
duties: Government may make over management of institutions, execution of works, or performance of duties to the Panchayat.

key_procedures: The amendment comes into force immediately upon enactment.
The Government's decision to contribute to the Panchayat Fund is based on their opinion of necessity for specific expenditures related to institutions, works, or duties transferred to the Panchayat.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but likely related to the department that oversees Panchayats.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Travancore-Cochin Panchayats Act, 1950.
The amendment specifically addresses Section 55 of the principal Act.
The Government's contribution is discretionary and based on necessity for tasks managed by the Panchayat.

title: THE TRAVANCORE-COCHIN PANCHAYATS (VALIDATION OF IMPOSITION AND COLLECTION OF RATES, TAXES, CESSES AND FEES) ACT, 1958.
purpose: To validate the imposition and collection of certain rates, taxes, cesses and fees by Panchayats.
scope: Applies to the imposition and collection of rates, taxes, cesses and fees by Panchayats under the Travancore-Cochin Panchayats Act, 1950. The act specifically mentions that it aims to validate actions taken under section 56 of the Travancore-Cochin Panchayats Act, 1950, or sub-rule (3) of rule 118 of the Travancore-Cochin Panchayat Rules, 1951.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Panchayats (Validation of Imposition and Collection of Rates, Taxes, Cesses and Fees) Act, 1958, and that it shall come into force at once.

Provides that notwithstanding anything contained in clause (c) of section 56 of the Travancore-Cochin Panchayats Act, 1950, or sub-rule (3) of rule 118 of the Travancore-Cochin Panchayat Rules, 1951, and notwithstanding anything contained in any judgement, decree or order, if any, the imposition and collection of all cesses, rates, taxes and fees by the Panchayats under section 56 of the said Panchayats Act on and from the 15th day of August 1951 and all actions made and all action taken by them in the exercise or purported exercise of the powers conferred by the said Panchayats Act and the rules issued thereunder in connection with the imposition or collection of such cess, rate, tax or fee are hereby declared to have been validly made, passed or taken, as the case may be. It also states that such imposition, collection, order or action shall not be called in question on the ground only that the previous sanction of the Government was not obtained or that the maxima of the rates of such cess, rate, tax or fee were not prescribed as required under clause (c) of section 56 or sub-rule (3) of rule 118 aforesaid. Additionally, it clarifies that no action or omission on the part of any person shall be punishable as an offence which would not have been so punishable if this Act had not been passed.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be the Panchayats and relevant authorities under the Travancore-Cochin Panchayats Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the imposition and collection of rates, taxes, cesses, and fees by Panchayats.

duties: Panchayats have the duty to impose and collect rates, taxes, cesses, and fees.

key_procedures: The act implicitly validates procedures for the imposition and collection of rates, taxes, cesses, and fees by Panchayats as per the Travancore-Cochin Panchayats Act, 1950 and its associated rules.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be the administrative departments overseeing Panchayats in Travancore-Cochin.
important_notes: The Act was published in the Gazette Extra ordinary dated 14th March 1958.

title: THE TRAVANCORE-COCHIN PAYMENT OF SALARIES AND ALLOWANCES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1952
purpose: To amend the Travancore-Cochin Payment of Salaries and Allowances Act, 1951.
scope: Applies to the Travancore-Cochin Legislative Assembly and its members.

key_definitions.Legislative Assembly: Refers to the Travancore-Cochin Legislative Assembly.
key_definitions.fixed allowance: A fixed allowance of one hundred and twenty rupees per month.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Payment of Salaries and Allowances (Amendment) Act, 1952. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 27th day of June, 1952.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 6, Act XIV of 1951.
main_sections.description: In Section 6 of the Travancore-Cochin Payment of Salaries and Allowances Act, 1951, the words 'one hundred and twenty-five rupees' shall be substituted by 'one hundred and twenty rupees'.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for Sections 8 and 9, Act XIV of 1951.
main_sections.description: For Sections 8 and 9 of the said Act, the following section shall be substituted, namely: '8. (1) Every member of the Legislative Assembly who does not hold any of the offices referred to in Sections 3 and 4 shall be entitled to receive— (a) a fixed allowance of one hundred and twenty rupees per month, and (b) travelling and daily allowances at the rates specified in the Schedule and upon such conditions as may be specified by rules made by the Government, for attending meeting of the Legislative Assembly or of any Committee thereof or of any Committee or Board constituted by the Government. (2) The fixed allowance referred to in clause (a) of sub-section (1) shall accrue to a member from the date on which he is declared duly elected, or in the case of a member nominated by the Rajpramukh to fill a seat in the Legislative Assembly, from the date on which he is nominated, or if such declaration or nomination is made before the vacancy occurs, from the date of occurrence of the vacancy: Provided that the fixed allowance shall not be paid until the member has made and subscribed the oath or affirmation prescribed by Article 138 read with Article 238 of the Constitution of India.'

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Schedule, Act X:V of 1951.
main_sections.description: In items III and IV and the entries against them in the Schedule to the said Act the following item and entry shall be substituted, namely: — 'III. Members of the Legislative Assembly. The members of the Legislative Assembly shall be given travelling and daily allowances at the following rates — For journeys by rail Double first class railway fare. For journeys by road Eight annas per mile. Daily allowance Ten rupees'.

important_rules: Members of the Legislative Assembly are entitled to a fixed allowance of one hundred and twenty rupees per month.
Members are entitled to travelling and daily allowances for attending meetings, subject to government rules.
Fixed allowance accrues from the date of declaration of election or nomination.
Travelling and daily allowances for railway journeys are double the first-class fare.
Travelling and daily allowances for road journeys are eight annas per mile.
Daily allowance for members is ten rupees.

rights: Right to receive a fixed allowance of one hundred and twenty rupees per month (for members not holding specific offices).
Right to receive travelling and daily allowances for attending meetings of the Legislative Assembly or its committees.
Right to receive travelling and daily allowances for journeys by rail and road.
duties: Duty to make and subscribe the oath or affirmation before receiving the fixed allowance.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to conditions specified by government rules for travelling and daily allowances.

key_procedures: To receive the fixed allowance, a member must have been declared duly elected or nominated, and must have made and subscribed the oath or affirmation.
Travelling and daily allowances are to be claimed based on the rates specified in the Schedule and subject to government rules.
administration: Travancore-Cochin Government (implied through rule-making power)
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on June 27, 1952.
The amendment substitutes previous rates for allowances.
The fixed allowance is paid only after the oath or affirmation is made and subscribed.

title: THE TRAVANCORE COCHIN PAYMENT OF SALARIES AND ALLOWANCES ACT
purpose: To provide for the salaries and allowances of Ministers, the Speaker and Deputy Speaker and members of the Legislative Assembly.
scope: Applies to Ministers, the Speaker and Deputy Speaker, and members of the Legislative Assembly of Travancore-Cochin.

key_definitions.residence: Includes the staff-quarters and other buildings appurtenant thereto, and the gardens thereof.
key_definitions.maintenance: In relation to a residence includes the payment of local rates and taxes and the provision of electricity and water.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Payment of Salaries and Allowances Act, 1951. It shall come into force at once.
Defines 'residence' and 'maintenance' in relation to a residence.

Provides for the salary of each Minister to be seven hundred rupees per mensem and dearness allowance at such rates as officers of Government drawing a salary of seven hundred rupees per mensem be entitled to from time to time.

Provides for the salary of the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly to be seven hundred rupees per mensem and dearness allowance at such rates as officers of Government drawing a salary of seven hundred rupees per mensem be entitled to from time to time. Also provides for the Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly a salary of three hundred and fifty rupees per mensem and dearness allowances at such rates as officers of Government drawing a salary of three hundred and fifty rupees per mensem be entitled to from time to time.

Provides for the residence of each Minister and the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly to be of fully furnished residence in the City of Trivandrum and the drum throughout their terms of office and for a period of fifteen days immediately thereafter and no charge shall fall upon the Minister or Speaker personally in respect of the maintenance of the residence, nor in lieu of the use of such furnished residence and its maintainance, to a house-rent allowance of one hundred and fifty rupees per mensem.

The Government shall, from time to time, provide suitable conveyances for the use of the Ministers and the Speaker subject to such rules as regards their maintenance and repair, as may be made by the Government. The Ministers and the Speaker shall be paid a consolidated sum of one hundred and seventy-five rupees per mensem in lieu of the cost of petrol and oil for the conveyances.

Details traveling allowance for each Minister, Speaker, and Deputy Speaker while traveling on public business, touring, and daily allowances at rates specified in the Schedule and upon such conditions as may be specified by rules made by the Government.

Every member of the Legislative Assembly who does not hold any of the offices referred to in Sections 3 and 4 shall be entitled to receive at his option: (a) a consolidated allowance of one hundred and twenty rupees per mensem; or (b) in lieu of such consolidated allowance, travelling and daily allowances for attending the meetings of the Legislative Assembly or of any Committee thereof, subject to rules made by the Government. Also, a member shall be entitled to allowances referred to in sub-section (1) from the date on which he is declared duly elected or if such declaration is made before the vacancy occurs, from the date of occurrence of the vacancy. Provided that such allowances shall not be paid until the member has made and subscribed the oath or affirmation prescribed by Article 188 read with Article 238 of the Constitution of India.

Members of the Legislative Assembly shall be entitled to travelling and daily allowances at the rates specified in the Schedule and upon such conditions as may be specified by rules made by the Government. Provided that nothing in this Section shall authorise a member who received a consolidated allowance under Section 8 to draw travelling and daily allowances for attending meetings of the Legislative Assembly or of any Committee thereof.

All rules made under this Act shall be published in the Gazette. All rules made under this Act shall be laid for not less than seven days before the Legislative Assembly as soon as possible after they are made and shall be subject to such modifications as the Legislative Assembly may make during the session in which they are so laid.

important_rules: Ministers and the Speaker shall be given daily and travelling allowances at the rates for journeys performed by them.

Travelling allowances for journeys by air, cost of one and a half first class railway fare, when travelling by road, a mileage of one rupee, when travelling by air, actual plane fare plus half first class railway fare and a daily allowance of thirty rupees except for Delhi, Calcutta and Bombay, where the rate of daily allowance will be forty-five rupees.

The Deputy Speaker shall, for journeys performed by him, be paid travelling allowance at the same rates as in the case of first class officers of Government, the rate of daily allowance being hereafter fifteen rupees.
Members of the Legislative Assembly who have opted to receive daily allowance and travelling allowance in lieu of a consolidated allowance for attending the meetings of the Legislative Assembly.
Members of the Legislative Assembly travelling on public business shall be given daily and travelling allowance at the rates specified in Paragraph III above.

rights: Right to salaries and allowances as provided by the Act.
Right to residence and house-rent allowance (for Ministers and Speaker).
Right to conveyances (for Ministers and Speaker).
Right to travelling and daily allowances for attending Legislative Assembly or Committee meetings.
duties: Members must make and subscribe the oath or affirmation before receiving allowances.
obligations: To provide suitable conveyances for Ministers and Speaker.
Publication of rules in the Gazette.
Laying of rules before the Legislative Assembly.

key_procedures: Rules made under the Act must be published in the Gazette.
Rules made under the Act must be laid before the Legislative Assembly for a period of not less than seven days.
Modifications to rules can be made by the Legislative Assembly during the session they are laid.
administration: The Government (presumably the State Government of Travancore-Cochin)
important_notes: Published in Gazette Extraordinary dated 11th October 1951.

title: THE TRAVANCORE COCHIN PAYMENT OF SALARIES AND ALLOWANCES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1956
purpose: To further amend the Travancore-Cochin Payment of Salaries and Allowances Act, 1951.
scope: Applies to the state of Travancore-Cochin. It pertains to the salaries and allowances of Ministers and Members of the Legislative Assembly.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Payment of Salaries and Allowances (Amendment) Act, 1956. It also specifies that Section 2 of this Act shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April 1955 and the rest of this Act shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 6, Act XIV of 1951.
main_sections.description: Amends Section 6 of the Travancore-Cochin Payment of Salaries and Allowances Act, 1951. It specifies that in the said Act, the words "throughout their terms of office and for a period of fifteen days immediately thereafter" shall be inserted after "the Speaker" and "subject to" respectively. It also adds a proviso to sub-section (1) regarding the publication in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 17th March 1956.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 7, Act XIV of 1951.
main_sections.description: Amends Section 7 of the Travancore-Cochin Payment of Salaries and Allowances Act, 1951. It introduces a proviso to sub-section (1) of Section 7, which states that if a Minister, while on tour, is allowed free board and lodging at the expense of the Government of India or the Government of any State, he shall be entitled to only one-half of the daily allowance admissible to him at the station concerned.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Schedule to Act XIV of 1951.
main_sections.description: Amends the Schedule to Act XIV of 1951. In item (1) of clause (2) of the entry relating to the words "cost of one first-class railway fare plus two annas per mile", it is substituted with "cost of one first-class railway fare plus two annas per mile". In item (1) of clause (2) of the entry relating to the words "actual plane fare plus first class railway fare", it is substituted with "actual plane fare plus first class railway fare". It also amends item (1) in item III, for the words "Cost of one first class railway fare plus two annas per mile" to "Cost of one first class railway fare plus two annas per mile".

main_sections.section_title: Validation of payment of certain allowances.
main_sections.description: Validates the receipt of travelling allowance by a Member of the Legislative Assembly who performed a journey by railway before the 1st day of April 1954. It specifies that any abolition of first-class accommodation on such railway and the entitlement to receive travelling allowance in respect of such journey, if not abolished in fact, shall be deemed to have been validly made. It further clarifies that the first-class accommodation was not abolished on such railway and that the journey was not in fact travelled by first class.

important_rules: Rule: If a Minister on tour is allowed free board and lodging at the expense of the Government of India or any State, they are entitled to only one-half of the daily allowance admissible at the station concerned.
Rule: The wording "throughout their terms of office and for a period of fifteen days immediately thereafter" is to be inserted in Section 6 of Act XIV of 1951.

Rule: Payments of certain allowances made to a Member of the Legislative Assembly for railway journeys before April 1, 1954, are validated under specific conditions regarding the abolition of first-class accommodation and entitlement to travelling allowance.

rights: Ministers are entitled to daily allowances when on tour, subject to conditions.
Members of the Legislative Assembly are entitled to travelling allowance for journeys by railway.

key_procedures: Procedure: To amend Section 6 of Act XIV of 1951, specific wording is to be inserted, and a proviso related to Gazette publication is added.
Procedure: To amend Section 7 of Act XIV of 1951, a proviso regarding the daily allowance for Ministers on tour who receive free board and lodging is added.
Procedure: To amend the Schedule to Act XIV of 1951, specific substitutions for the wording related to railway fares and plane fares are made.
Procedure: To validate past allowance payments, the act deems them valid if certain conditions concerning the abolition of first-class accommodation and entitlement to travelling allowance were met.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Travancore-Cochin Payment of Salaries and Allowances Act, 1951.
Section 2 of this amending Act is deemed to have come into force on 1st April 1955.
The rest of the Act comes into force immediately upon enactment.
A proviso in Section 7 clarifies the entitlement to daily allowance when free board and lodging are provided.
Section 5 validates certain past travelling allowance payments, particularly related to first-class rail travel.

title: THE TRAVANCORE-COCHIN PLACES OF PUBLIC RESORT ACT, 1951
purpose: To provide for the inspection of places of public resort and entertainment, and for the licensing of the same by competent authority.
scope: The Act extends to the City of Trivandrum and to all areas in the State of Travancore-Cochin which have been or may hereafter be declared as Municipalities under the law for the time being in force governing the constitution of Municipalities in the State. It also applies to any area declared as a Panchayat area under the Travancore-Cochin Panchayats Act, 1950, with specific references to Section 81 of that Act. However, it explicitly states that the Act shall not apply to any temple, church, mosque or other place of public worship or to any building belonging to or under the control of the Government.

key_definitions.building: Includes any house, hut, shed or roofed enclosure.
key_definitions.place of public entertainment: Shall mean any place, enclosure, building or tent, booth or other erection, whether permanent or temporary, where music, singing, dancing or any diversion or game of the means of carrying on the same is provided and to which the public are admitted either on payment of money, or with the intention that money may be collected from those admitted, otherwise than for a home side charitable purpose, and shall include a race-course, circus, theatre, music-hall, billiard room, bagatelle room, gymnasium and fencing school.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as the Travancore-Cochin Places of Public Resort Act, 1951. It also specifies its commencement date and territorial application. The Act shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint. It extends to the City of Trivandrum and all areas declared as Municipalities. For Panchayat areas, specific provisions of the Travancore-Cochin Panchayats Act, 1950 apply. It excludes temples, churches, mosques, etc.
Provides definitions for 'building' and 'place of public entertainment'.

main_sections.section_title: No enclosed place or building with area of five hundred square feet to be used for public resort without a licence.
main_sections.description: Prohibits the use of any enclosed place or building with an area of five hundred square feet or upwards for public resort or entertainment without a license previously obtained.

main_sections.section_title: Application for licence. What it must contain.
main_sections.description: Outlines the requirements for applying for a license, specifying what information must be included in the application.

main_sections.section_title: Authority to whom application should be made.
main_sections.description: Specifies the authority to whom the application for a license should be submitted. For the City of Trivandrum, it's the Commissioner of the Corporation. For Municipalities and Panchayats, it's the respective Executive Authority, with powers to make exceptions via notification.

main_sections.section_title: The authority shall inspect and may require addition or alteration to place or building.
main_sections.description: Grants the authority the power to inspect any place or building for which a license is sought. They can also demand additions or alterations to the place or building to ensure safety and compliance before granting a license.

Details the conditions under which the authority can grant a license. It also covers the authority's right to refuse a license, including reasons for refusal and the possibility of requiring written explanations for proposed uses.

main_sections.section_title: Licence to state period for which it is to be in force.
main_sections.description: Mandates that every license granted under the Act must specify the period for which it is valid, and it will cease to be in force upon the expiration of that period.

Empowers any authority granting a license to revoke or suspend it for reasons such as contravention of the Act or its conditions, or if the licensed place or building can no longer be safely used for its intended purpose. It also covers situations where the license has been fraudulently obtained.

main_sections.section_title: Appeal against order under Sections 6, 7, or 9.
main_sections.description: Provides for an appeal process against orders issued under Sections 6, 7, or 9. The appeal is to be preferred within thirty days of the order date. For orders passed by the Executive Authority of a Municipality, the appeal lies to the Municipal Council. For other areas, the appeal lies to the Standing Committee of the Corporation, or the Government as specified.

main_sections.section_title: Power to enter place of public resort to inspect licence or to prevent further use.
main_sections.description: Grants the licensing authority or any authorized person the power to enter any enclosure or building at any time to inspect a license or to prevent its use if required, especially if the license is absent or if the use is deemed unauthorized.

main_sections.section_title: District Magistrate may revise any proceedings under this Act.
main_sections.description: Empowers the District Magistrate to call for and examine the records of any proceeding taken under this Act. The Magistrate can inquire into and make any further orders as deemed necessary.
Specifies penalties for persons who, without a license, use any place for public resort or entertainment. The penalty is a fine which may extend to five hundred rupees.

Grants the Government the power to make rules consistent with the Act for carrying out its purposes, including amendment or cancellation of rules. These rules must be published in the Gazette and come into force on the date of publication or as specified.

Repeals the Cochin Places of Public Resort Act, X of 1097, Section 290 of the Travancore District Municipalities Act (116 G.E./41 A.D.), and Section 294 of the Travancore City Municipal Act 1116 (IV of 1116).

important_rules: No enclosed place or building with an area of five hundred square feet or more is to be used for public resort or entertainment without a valid license.
Applications for licenses must contain specific details and be submitted to the designated authority.
Licenses can be revoked or suspended if the Act or its conditions are contravened, or if the place is no longer safe for use.
Rules made by the Government will be published in the Gazette and will come into effect on the date of publication.

penalties: Fine not exceeding five hundred rupees for using any place of public resort or entertainment without a license.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The licensing authority, the District Magistrate, and the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspection, requiring alterations, granting/refusing/revoking licenses, hearing appeals, and imposing penalties for violations.

rights: The right to apply for a license to use a place for public resort or entertainment.
The right to appeal against orders issued by the licensing authority under Sections 6, 7, or 9.
duties: Licensees have a duty to comply with the terms and conditions of their license.
The public has a duty to ensure that places of public resort and entertainment are properly licensed.
The authority has a duty to inspect and ensure compliance with the Act.
obligations: Obligation to obtain a license before using an enclosed place or building of 500 sq. ft. or more for public resort or entertainment.

key_procedures: Application for a license involves submitting specific details to the appropriate authority.
Inspection and potential modification of the place or building may be required before license issuance.
Appeals against licensing decisions or orders must be filed within a specified timeframe (thirty days) to the designated appellate authority.
Rules made by the Government are published in the Gazette and become effective upon publication.
administration: The Government of Travancore-Cochin, through various authorities such as Municipal Corporations, Municipal Councils, Panchayat Executive Authorities, and the District Magistrate.
important_notes: The Act does not apply to temples, churches, mosques, or buildings controlled by the Government.
Licenses specify the period of validity and cease to be effective upon expiration.
The District Magistrate has the power to revise proceedings under the Act.

title: The Travancore Cochin Police Act, 1951
purpose: This act seems to be an act to consolidate and amend the law relating to the Police in the United State of Travancore and Cochin. It defines the powers and duties of police officers, regulates public order, and outlines penalties for various offences.
scope: Applies to the United State of Travancore and Cochin.

main_sections.section_title: Power to reserve any street or public place.
main_sections.description: The Inspector-General may subject to the orders of the Government by public notice temporarily reserve for any public purpose any street or public place and prohibit persons from entering the area so reserved save under such conditions as may be prescribed by the Inspector-General.

main_sections.section_title: Enforcement of orders issued under Sections 24 to 27.
main_sections.description: Details the enforcement of orders issued under Sections 24 to 27, including powers of Magistrates and Police Officers to require persons to desist from action or to arrest them.

main_sections.section_title: Power to give directions to prevent disorder at places of public amusement, etc.
main_sections.description: The Inspector-General and officers of higher rank can give directions to prevent disorder at places of public amusement or meeting to maintain public peace.

main_sections.section_title: Issue of orders by District Magistrate for prevention of riot, etc.
main_sections.description: District Magistrates can issue orders to prevent riot or grave disturbance of the peace, temporarily take possession of buildings, and exclude persons from certain areas.

main_sections.section_title: Issue of orders for maintenance of order at religious ceremonies etc.
main_sections.description: District Magistrates can issue orders for the maintenance of order at religious ceremonies, corporate displays, or public assemblies to prevent dispute or contention which may lead to grave disturbance of the peace. These orders are subject to review by the Government.

The District Magistrate may, by public notice, proclaim that any stray dogs found during such period may be destroyed if found wandering in streets or public places. Dogs found wearing collars may be similarly destroyed or their owners penalized.

main_sections.section_title: EXECUTIVE POWERS AND DUTIES OF THE POLICE.
main_sections.description: Outlines the duties of every Police Officer, including promptly serving summons, executing lawful orders, collecting and communicating intelligence, arresting offenders, preserving peace, preventing offences, aiding persons in need, and preventing injury to public property.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of Police Constable on the occasion of a fire.
main_sections.description: Defines the powers of a Police Constable during a fire, including removing persons, preventing interference, extinguishing fire, and calling for assistance.

main_sections.section_title: Power to deal with property suspected to be stolen.
main_sections.description: Allows a Police Officer to deal with property suspected to be stolen, requiring the possessor to account for it and potentially reporting to a Magistrate.

main_sections.section_title: Pawnbroker, etc. to report stolen property or tendering for pawn or sale.
main_sections.description: Requires pawnbrokers and dealers in second-hand property to report stolen property or any property tendered for pawn or sale to the police. Failure to comply can result in penalties.

main_sections.section_title: Power to deal with unclaimed property.
main_sections.description: It is the duty of every Police Officer to take charge of all unclaimed property found by him or made over to him, and to furnish without any unreasonable delay an inventory thereof to a Magistrate.

main_sections.section_title: Applicability of the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
main_sections.description: States that the provisions of Sections 523, 524 and 525 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, shall apply as nearly as may be practicable to all property detained or taken charge of by the police under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: A superior Police Officer may perform duty assigned by law or by a lawful order.
main_sections.description: A superior Police Officer may perform any duty assigned by law or by a lawful order, and may also supplement the orders or actions of an inferior officer.
It is lawful for any Police Officer to lay information for the summons, warrant, search-warrant, or other legal process as may by law issue against any person committing an offence.

main_sections.section_title: Persons bound to conform to directions of Police.
main_sections.description: All persons shall be bound to conform to any reasonable direction of a Police Officer given for the fulfilment of any of the duties vested in them under this Act. Police Officers may also restrain or remove persons refusing or omitting to conform to such directions.
Covers offences related to resisting or disobeying police orders, including failure to deliver up certificates, arms, etc., and subsequent actions by the Inspector-General.

main_sections.section_title: Unlawful assumption of Police function or power.
main_sections.description: Prohibits persons from unlawfully assuming police functions or power, wearing distinctive dress or accoutrements, or acting as a police officer. Penalties are prescribed for such offences.
Details offences by Police Officers, including contravening provisions of Section 18, resigning office or withdrawing himself from duty, and wilful breach or neglect of duty or any provision of law.

important_rules: Persons must conform to reasonable directions of a Police Officer for the fulfilment of their duties.
Police Officers have the power to restrain or remove persons who refuse or omit to conform to such directions.
Stray dogs found wandering in streets or public places may be destroyed.
Pawnbrokers and second-hand dealers must report stolen property or property tendered for pawn or sale to the police.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or to both, for unlawfully assuming police function or power.
Liable to fine not exceeding two hundred rupees, or to imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or to both, for certain offences related to execution of warrants.
Liable to a penalty not exceeding two hundred rupees, or to imprisonment of either description for a period which may extend to six months, or to both, for any punishment whatsoever.
Penalties for Police Officers contravening provisions of Section 18.
Penalties for Police Officers resigning office or withdrawing himself from duties.
Penalties for Police Officers guilty of wilful breach or neglect of duty or any provision of law.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Police Officers, Magistrates, Inspector-General of Police, Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Arrest, detention, prosecution, imposition of fines and imprisonment, seizure of property, issuing orders and directions.

rights: Right to reserve public places for public purpose.
Right to give directions to prevent disorder at public amusements.
Right to take possession of buildings to prevent riot.
Right to exclude persons from certain areas.
Right to issue orders for maintenance of order at religious ceremonies.
Right to destroy stray dogs.
Right to search for and examine property.
Right to take charge of unclaimed property.
Right to lay information for legal process.
Right to restrain or remove persons refusing to conform to directions.
duties: Duty to promptly serve summons and execute lawful orders.
Duty to collect and communicate intelligence.
Duty to arrest offenders.
Duty to preserve peace.
Duty to prevent offences.
Duty to aid persons in need.
Duty to prevent injury to public property.
Duty to arrange for the proper sustenance and shelter of every person who is under arrest or in custody.
Duty to conduct searches to refrain from needless disturbance.
Duty to deal with women and children with strict regard to decency and reasonable gentleness.
Duty to prevent any loss or damage by fire.
Duty to avert any accident or danger to the public.
Duty to regulate and control traffic in streets.
Duty to prevent obstruction therein.
Duty to keep order in the streets and at and within public bathing, washing and landing places, public worship.
Duty to prevent overcrowding, threat and in public ferry boats.
Duty of every Police Officer to take charge of all unclaimed property.
Duty of every Police Officer to promptly perform duties assigned by law or lawful order.
Duty of every Police Officer to conform to reasonable directions of Police.
obligations: Persons are obligated to conform to reasonable directions of a Police Officer.
Police Officers are obligated to perform their duties with diligence and impartiality.

key_procedures: Procedure for reservation of public places: Public notice by the Inspector-General with conditions prescribed by him.
Procedure for enforcement of orders: Powers of arrest and requirement to desist from action by Magistrates and Police Officers.
Procedure for preventing disorder at public amusements: Directions by Inspector-General or higher-rank officers.
Procedure for prevention of riot: Orders by District Magistrate, temporary possession of buildings, exclusion of persons.
Procedure for maintenance of order at religious ceremonies: Orders by District Magistrate, subject to Government review.
Procedure for destruction of stray dogs: Public notice by District Magistrate, destruction of found dogs.
Procedure for dealing with property suspected to be stolen: Police Officer requires account, reports to Magistrate.
Procedure for reporting stolen property: Pawnbrokers and dealers report to police, penalties for failure.
Procedure for unclaimed property: Police Officer takes charge, provides inventory to Magistrate.
Procedure for arrest and custody: Police Officer must arrange for sustenance and shelter of persons under arrest.
Procedure for conducting searches: Police Officer must refrain from needless disturbance, act with decency towards women and children.
Procedure for managing traffic and public order: Regulation and control of traffic, prevention of obstruction, maintaining order in streets and public places.
Procedure for fire incidents: Police Constable's powers to remove persons, extinguish fire, and secure the area.
Procedure for dealing with property during fire incidents: Costs of establishments and appliances for extinguishing fire may be defrayed by the municipality.
Procedure for unlawfully assuming police function: Arrest and prosecution of offenders.
administration: Home Department (implied, as police matters are typically under Home)
important_notes: The Inspector-General may reserve any street or public place for any public purpose.
Magistrates and Police Officers have broad powers to enforce orders issued under Sections 24-27.
Police officers have wide-ranging duties to maintain public peace and order.
The Act references and incorporates provisions from the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.
Penalties for offences can include fines and imprisonment.

Any damage done on the occasion of fires by members of any fire-brigade or any Police Officers or their assistants in the due execution of their duties shall be deemed to be damaged by fire within the meaning of any policy of insurance against fire, but nothing in this section shall exempt any Officer of Police or any member of any fire-brigade from liability to damages on account of any acts done by him without reasonable cause.

title: The Travancore Cochin Police (Amendment) Act, 1956
purpose: To amend The Travancore Cochin Police Act, 1951.
scope: Applies to the Travancore-Cochin Police.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Travancore Cochin Police (Amendment) Act, 1956.

Amends Section 2 of the principal Act, substituting 'Assistant Superintendent of Police' for 'Assistant Superintendent of Police' and 'Deputy Superintendents of Police' for 'Deputy Superintendents of Police'.

Amends Section 3 of the principal Act. It inserts provisions regarding the dismissal, suspension, or reduction in rank of subordinate police officers, subject to the provisions of Article 311 of the Constitution and rules made under the Act. The Inspector-General, Deputy Inspector-General, Assistant Inspector-General, and District Superintendents of Police may, at any time, dismiss, remove, suspend or reduce to a lower post or time scale or to a lower stage in time scale, any officer of the subordinate police whom they shall think fit, or who shall be found guilty of any charge of disobedience, absence without leave, inefficiency or neglect of duty or misconduct, or in any other way prove himself unworthy of the trust reposed in him, or who shall have been guilty of any offence or misconduct which shall have brought or may bring disrepute to the Force, or who shall have been found by reason of his character or antecedents to be unsuitable for service in the Force or who shall have been guilty of insubordination, inefficiency, neglect of duty, misconduct or any other offence or breach of discipline in relation to the Force.

Amends Section 4 of the principal Act. It inserts provisions regarding the dismissal, suspension or reduction in rank of officers of the subordinate police, subject to the provisions of Article 311 of the Constitution and such rules as the Government may from time to time make under this Act, the Inspector-General, Deputy Inspector-General, Assistant Inspector-General and District Superintendents of Police may, at any time, dismiss, suspend or reduce to a lower post or time scale or to a lower stage in time scale, any officer of the subordinate police whom they shall think fit, or who shall be found guilty of any charge of disobedience, absence without leave, inefficiency or neglect of duty or misconduct, or in any other way prove himself unworthy of the trust reposed in him, or who shall have been guilty of any offence or misconduct which shall have brought or may bring disrepute to the Force, or who shall have been found by reason of his character or antecedents to be unsuitable for service in the Force or who shall have been guilty of insubordination, inefficiency, neglect of duty, misconduct or any other offence or breach of discipline in relation to the Force.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 6.
main_sections.description: Substitutes a new section for Section 6 of the principal Act. The new section deals with the dismissal, suspension, or reduction in rank of officers of the subordinate police, similar to the provisions in the amended Section 3 and 4.
Amends Section 7 of the principal Act. It substitutes 'Every police officer' for 'Every police officer appointed as an officer of the subordinate police'.

important_notes: Republished in the Gazette Extraordinary, dated 10th September 1956.

title: THE TRAVANCORE-COCHIN PREVENTION OF CORRUPTION ACT
purpose: To make more effective provision for the prevention of bribery and corruption.
scope: Applies to the whole of Travancore and Cochin and to all public servants in its jurisdiction or outside the State.

key_definitions.public servant: Every officer appointed by Government or by any local authority or any other person empowered by law to perform public duties, including arbitrators and persons involved in elections. It also covers those whose appointment has been referred by Government or a local authority to the Court.
key_definitions.election: Refers to the election for any municipal or other public authority, or the selection of persons to an office or employment by way of prescription.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Prevention of Corruption Act, 1950. It extends to the whole of Travancore and Cochin and applies also to all public servants in the jurisdiction or outside the State. It shall come into force at once.
Defines 'Public Servant' and 'election' for the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: (1) Offences under Sections 153 and 157 of the Travancore Penal Code or Sections 147 and 151 of the Cochin Penal Code to be cognizable offences. (2) Extension of the definition of 'public servant'.
main_sections.description: Specifies that certain offenses under the Travancore and Cochin Penal Codes are cognizable. It also extends the definition of 'public servant'.

main_sections.section_title: Presumption where public servant accepts gratification other than legal remuneration.
main_sections.description: Establishes a presumption of guilt if a public servant accepts gratification other than legal remuneration.

main_sections.section_title: Criminal misconduct in the discharge of official duty.
main_sections.description: Defines and provides penalties for criminal misconduct by a public servant in the discharge of their official duty.
Outlines special provisions related to punishments for offenses under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Public servants to furnish particulars of property on demand.
main_sections.description: Mandates public servants to furnish particulars of their property upon demand by the Government or Commissioner.

main_sections.section_title: Institutions and persons to furnish particulars of property or transactions of public servants with them.
main_sections.description: Requires institutions and persons dealing with public servants to provide information about property or transactions.

main_sections.section_title: Powers of Commissioner or officer of anti-corruption measures.
main_sections.description: Grants powers to the Commissioner or anti-corruption officers.
Specifies how courts will take cognizance of offenses under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Accused person to be competent witness.
main_sections.description: States that an accused person is a competent witness.

main_sections.section_title: Bar against prosecution of officers acting under this Act.
main_sections.description: Prevents prosecution of officers acting in good faith under this Act, with exceptions.
Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of this Act.

important_rules: Public servants must not accept gratification other than legal remuneration.
Public servants engaging in criminal misconduct in the discharge of their official duty are liable for punishment.
Public servants must furnish particulars of their property on demand.
Certain institutions and persons must provide information about property or transactions involving public servants.

penalties: Imprisonment and fine for offenses related to accepting gratification.
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both, for criminal misconduct.
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both, for failing to produce documents.
Punishment for offenses under Sections 153 and 157 of the Travancore Penal Code or Sections 147 and 151 of the Cochin Penal Code.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Commissioner or officer of anti-corruption measures, Courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through investigation by police, cognizance by courts, and application of relevant penal codes. Presumptions of guilt are established in certain circumstances.

rights: An accused person is a competent witness.
Officers acting under this Act in good faith are protected from prosecution (with exceptions).
duties: Public servants have a duty not to accept illegal gratification.
Public servants have a duty to furnish property particulars when demanded.
Public servants have a duty to conduct themselves without criminal misconduct.
obligations: Institutions and persons must furnish information about property or transactions of public servants.

key_procedures: When a public servant accepts gratification other than legal remuneration, a presumption of guilt arises.
Public servants are required to furnish property particulars upon demand by the Government or Commissioner.
Courts take cognizance of offenses under this Act.
Accused persons are competent witnesses in their trials.
The Government can make rules to implement the Act.
administration: Commissioner or officer of anti-corruption measures, Government.
important_notes: The Act extends to the whole of Travancore and Cochin and applies to all public servants.
Presumption of guilt applies when a public servant accepts illegal gratification.
Certain offenses under the Travancore and Cochin Penal Codes are made cognizable.
The Act provides for special punishments for certain offenses.
Officers acting in good faith under the Act are generally protected from prosecution.

title: The Travancore Cochin Prisoners Act
purpose: To enact a law relating to prisoners confined by order of a Court.
scope: The Act applies to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin.

key_definitions.court: Includes any officer lawfully exercising Civil, Criminal or Revenue jurisdiction.
key_definitions.Inspector General: Means the Inspector General of a prison.
key_definitions.prison: Includes any place which has been declared by the Government by general or special order, to be a subsidiary jail.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Prisoners Act, 1950. It extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin. It shall come into force at once.
Defines 'court', 'Inspector General', 'prison', and 'State'.

main_sections.section_title: Officers in charge of prisons to receive and detain all persons duly committed to their custody.
main_sections.description: Officers in charge of prisons shall receive and detain all persons duly committed to their custody under this Act or otherwise, according to the exigency of any writ, warrant or order by which such person has been committed or until such person is discharged or removed in due course of law.

main_sections.section_title: Officer in charge of a prison shall forthwith, after the execution of every such writ, order or warrant as aforesaid, send to the Government a copy of the same.
main_sections.description: Officer in charge of a prison shall forthwith send to the Government a copy of every writ, order or warrant, together with a certificate endorsed and signed by him showing how the same has been executed or by whom the person committed thereby has been discharged from custody before the execution thereof.

main_sections.section_title: Power for officers in charge of prisons to give effect to any sentence or order for warrant.
main_sections.description: Officers in charge of prisons in the State may give effect to any sentence or order or warrant for the detention of any person passed or issued by the High Court or by any other Court or tribunal acting within the State under the general or special authority of the Government, or by any other Court or tribunal in India if the reception detention or imprisonment of persons sentenced by any such Court or tribunal has been authorised by general or special order of the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Warrant of officer of such Court to be sufficient authority.
main_sections.description: A warrant under the official signature of an officer of such Court or tribunal as is referred to in Section 5 shall be sufficient authority for holding any person in confinement in charge of the prison.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure where officer in charge of prison doubts the legality of warrant or order sent to him for execution.
main_sections.description: If the officer in charge of a prison doubts the legality of a warrant or order, he shall send it to the Government. The Government will then decide whether to execute it or not.
The Government may by general or special order provide for the removal of prisoners from one prison to another within the State.

main_sections.section_title: Application of Section 8 to Lunatic Asylums.
main_sections.description: Details how Section 8 applies to the removal of prisoners to Lunatic Asylums.

Any Civil Court may, if it thinks that the evidence of any person confined in any prison within the State is material in any matter pending before it, make an order in the form set forth in the first schedule, directed to the officer in charge of the prison.

main_sections.section_title: Attendance of prisoners pending a Civil matter.
main_sections.description: Details the process when a Civil Court orders the attendance of a prisoner.

main_sections.section_title: Attendance of prisoners in Criminal Court.
main_sections.description: Any Criminal Court may, if it thinks that the evidence of any person confined in any prison within the State is material in any matter pending before it, make an order in the form set forth in the first schedule, directed to the officer in charge of the prison.

main_sections.section_title: Attendance of persons confined in district jails.
main_sections.description: Outlines the procedure for the attendance of persons confined in district jails.

No order in any Civil matter shall be made by a Court under any of the provisions of this Part until the amount of the costs and charges of the execution of such order (to be determined by the Court) is deposited in such Court.

The Government may make rules regarding the escort of prisoners to and their custody during the period of such attendance, and for regulating the amount to be allowed for the costs and charges of such escort and for the guidance of officers in all other matters connected with the enforcement of this Part.

main_sections.section_title: Rules made under Sub-section (1) shall be published in the Gazette and shall, from the date of such publication, have the same force as is enacted by this Act.
main_sections.description: Rules made by the Government under Section 22 shall be published in the Gazette and will have the force of law from the date of publication.
The Cochin Prisoners' Act, XLVI of 1112, is hereby repealed.

important_rules: Officers in charge of prisons must receive and detain all persons duly committed to their custody.
Officers in charge of prisons must send a copy of every writ, order or warrant, with execution details, to the Government.
Courts can order the attendance of prisoners for evidence, with prescribed procedures and costs.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government, High Court, and other Courts or tribunals.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through warrants, orders, and the issuance of rules by the Government.

rights: Prisoners have the right to be detained or removed according to law.
Prisoners have the right to be released if the warrant or order is found to be illegal.
Prisoners to be removed to a Lunatic Asylum have rights as per the Government's order and law.
duties: Officers in charge of prisons have a duty to receive, detain, and discharge prisoners as per legal orders.
Officers in charge of prisons have a duty to ensure the safe custody and production of prisoners when required by a Court.
The Government has a duty to issue orders for the removal of prisoners and to make rules for the enforcement of the Act.

key_procedures: Procedure for issuing warrants for the detention or removal of prisoners.
Procedure for the attendance of prisoners in Courts for giving evidence.
Procedure for the removal of prisoners from one prison to another.
Procedure for the transfer of prisoners to Lunatic Asylums if they are found to be of unsound mind.
Procedure for the Government to make rules for the escort and custody of prisoners attending court.
Procedure for the publication of Government rules in the Gazette.
administration: Government of Travancore-Cochin
