important_notes: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin.
The Act comes into force at once.
Warrants from certain Courts are sufficient authority for holding persons in prison.
If an officer doubts the legality of a warrant, they must refer it to the Government.
Costs and charges for executing orders related to prisoner attendance must be deposited.
The Cochin Prisoners' Act, XLVI of 1112, is repealed.

title: THE TRAVANCORE-COCHIN PUBLIC ACCOUNTANTS ACT
purpose: To prevent loss to the Government by the default or misconduct of Public Accountants.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin.

key_definitions.Public Accountant: Every person who is a Public Accountant within the meaning of this Act, who, by reason of being employed in the service of the Government, is entrusted with the receipt, custody or control of any moneys or securities for money, documents or other property belonging to Government, or who, in his capacity as a Government servant, is entrusted with the receipt, custody or control of any moneys or securities for money, documents or other property belonging to any person or persons or to any institution.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Public Accountants Act, 1951. It extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin. It shall come into force at once.
Defines who constitutes a Public Accountant based on their employment with the Government and their role in handling money, securities, documents, or property.

main_sections.section_title: Statement of particulars of claim to be drawn up by Collector or other Head of Department.
main_sections.description: Details the process for a Collector or other Head of Department to draw up a statement of particulars of claim against a Public Accountant.

main_sections.section_title: Demand of Collector to be in writing.
main_sections.description: If a Collector has not satisfied a claim against a Public Accountant, they can seek the assistance of a Magistrate to realize moneys or property.

main_sections.section_title: Seizure and attachment of property of Public Accountant.
main_sections.description: Outlines the circumstances under which the property of a Public Accountant can be seized and attached by a Magistrate, especially if there's an attempt to conceal, destroy, or otherwise dispose of securities or documents.

Specifies that proceedings under the Act may be taken or continued by legal representatives if the Public Accountant dies or is unable to act, provided such legal representatives are also legally capable.
States that nothing in the Act prevents any parties aggrieved by any order from instituting civil suits, with some exceptions regarding the time limit for such suits.
Repeals the Travancore Public Accountants Act, Act III of 1030, and the Cochin Public Accountants Act, Act II of 1114, stating they are hereby repealed.

important_rules: Rule: Public Accountants are entrusted with the receipt, custody, or control of moneys, securities, or documents belonging to Government or others.
Rule: Collectors or Heads of Departments must draw up a statement of particulars of claim against a Public Accountant.
Rule: If a claim is not satisfied, the Collector can seek to recover the amount by attachment and sale of the Public Accountant's property or by other legal means.
Rule: Property of a Public Accountant can be seized if there is an attempt to conceal, destroy, or dispose of securities or documents related to the claim.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Collector or other Head of Department, Magistrate, and potentially Civil Courts.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through demand for written statements of claims, attachment and sale of property, seizure of documents and securities, and realization of moneys.

rights: Right for aggrieved parties to sue for their rights, subject to specific limitations.
Right for Collectors/Heads of Departments to initiate proceedings against defaulting Public Accountants.
duties: Duty for Public Accountants to manage entrusted moneys, securities, and documents responsibly.
Duty for Collectors/Heads of Departments to draw up statements of claims and pursue recovery.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the provisions of the Act for the realization of government dues from Public Accountants.

key_procedures: Procedure: Drawing up a statement of particulars of claim by a Collector or Head of Department.
Procedure: Demand of moneys or securities in writing from the Public Accountant.
Procedure: Seizure and attachment of property of the Public Accountant if there is a risk of concealment or destruction of assets.
Procedure: Realization of moneys and recovery of securities by the Magistrate.
Procedure: Continuation of proceedings by legal representatives in case of death or incapacity of the Public Accountant.
administration: Collectors and Heads of Departments are responsible for initiating and managing claims against Public Accountants. Magistrates are involved in the enforcement aspects.
important_notes: The Act clarifies the definition of a 'Public Accountant'.
Legal representatives can continue proceedings if the Public Accountant dies or becomes incapable.
The Act provides for the repeal of previous relevant Acts from Travancore and Cochin.

title: THE TRAVANCORE-COCHIN PUBLIC DEBT ACT, 1954 (Act V of 1954)
purpose: To make provision relating to Government Securities issued by the Government and for the management by the Reserve Bank of India of the Public Debt of the Government.
scope: Extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Public Debt Act, 1954, and that it extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin and shall come into force at once.

States that the Act applies to Government Securities issued by the Government and rules made thereunder by the Central Government, as well as to Government Securities of the State issued after the 13th day of July, 1954, and to Government Securities of the State specified in Part A of the First Schedule to the Constitution of India. References in the said Act and Rules to 'State' and 'State Government' shall be construed as references to 'Travancore-Cochin' and 'Government of Travancore-Cochin' respectively.

If any doubt or difficulty arises in giving effect to the purposes and provisions of this Act, the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make such provisions or give such directions as appear to them to be necessary for the removal of such doubt or difficulty.

Nothing in this Act shall affect anything contained in any law governing public debt in force in the State of Travancore-Cochin immediately before the 13th day of July, 1953. Provided that nothing in any such law shall apply to any Government Securities to which this Act applies.
The Travancore-Cochin Public Debt Ordinance, 1953 (Ordinance V of 1953) is hereby repealed.

administration: Reserve Bank of India (for management of Public Debt)
important_notes: The Act was received the assent of the President and published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 1st May 1954.

title: THE TRAVANCORE-COCHIN REGISTRATION OF BIRTHS AND DEATHS ACT, 1953
purpose: To make provision for the registration of births and deaths in rural tracts.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin. Also applies to Municipalities constituted under the law for the time being in force for the constitution of Municipalities and the City of Trivandrum as defined in the Trivandrum City Municipal Act, 1116.

key_definitions.revenue_village: Any local area which for purposes of revenue administration is now recognised as a Pakuthi or a village or which may hereafter be declared by the Government to be a village.
key_definitions.Registrar: A person appointed Registrar of Births and Deaths for a village or ward under Section 3 of this Act.
key_definitions.Taluk: Means any local area which for purposes of revenue administration is now recognised as a Taluk or which may hereafter be declared by the Government to be a Taluk.
key_definitions.Taluk Registrar: Means a person appointed Taluk Registrar of Births and Deaths for a Taluk under Section 3 of this Act.
key_definitions.District: Means any local area which for purposes of revenue administration is now recognised as a District or which may hereafter be declared by the Government to be a District.
key_definitions.District Registrar: Means a person appointed District Registrar of Births and Deaths for a District under Section 3 of this Act.
key_definitions.Registrar-General: Means a person appointed Registrar-General of Births and Deaths for the State under Section 3 of this Act.
key_definitions.Prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1953. It shall come into force at once and shall apply to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin except (i) the Municipalities constituted under the law for the time being in force for the constitution of Municipalities and (ii) the City of Trivandrum as defined in the Trivandrum City Municipal Act, 1116.
Defines terms such as 'revenue village', 'Registrar', 'Taluk', 'Taluk Registrar', 'District', 'District Registrar', 'Registrar-General', and 'Prescribed'.

The Government may appoint any person either by name or by virtue of any office to be a Registrar-General of Births and Deaths, a District Registrar of Births and Deaths, or a Taluk Registrar of Births and Deaths. The Government may also divide any village into wards and appoint a person, either by name or by virtue of any office, to be Registrar of Births and Deaths for each ward. Every Registrar shall, unless otherwise expressly authorised by the Registrar-General in writing, reside within the village or ward of which he is the Registrar and shall cause his name, with the addition of Registrar of Births and Deaths for the village or ward for which he is so appointed, written in Malayalam or Tamil, to be placed in some conspicuous place on or near the outer door of his office.

main_sections.section_title: Registrars to live in their villages and wards
main_sections.description: Registrars are required to reside within the village or ward for which they are appointed and to have their names displayed at their office.

main_sections.section_title: Registrar-General to have registers printed and supplied
main_sections.description: The Registrar-General shall cause to be printed and supplied a sufficient number of register books for making entries of births and deaths according to such forms and instructions as may, from time to time, be prescribed by the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Information of births to be given within two weeks
main_sections.description: The father or karanavan of every child, or in the case of death, the midwife who was present at the birth, and in her default, every adult male member of the family resident in the house in which the child was born and any person having charge of the child, or in default of the above, the mother, shall within two weeks next after the day of such birth, give or cause to be given, either orally or in writing, information to the Registrar according to the best of his knowledge and belief, or the several particulars required to be entered in the forms prescribed under Section 5.

main_sections.section_title: Information to be given respecting new born child found exposed
main_sections.description: In case any new born child is found exposed, it shall be the duty of any person finding such child and of any person in whose charge such child may be placed, to give to the best of his knowledge and belief, to the Registrar within seven days after the finding of such child, such information of the particulars required to be registered concerning the birth of such child as the informant possesses.

main_sections.section_title: Information of death to be given within seven days
main_sections.description: The nearest male adult relative present at the death, or in attendance during the last illness, any person dying in a village, or, in case of the default of such relative, every adult male person present at the death or, in case of their default, the occupier of the house, or in his default, every adult male person living in the house in which such death has happened, or in case of the default of such inmate, the person undertaking the disposal of the corpse, shall within seven days from the date of death, give or cause to be given, either orally or in writing, information to the Registrar according to the best of his knowledge and belief, of the several particulars required to be entered in the forms prescribed under Section 5.

main_sections.section_title: Village Officer bound to give information regarding other death
main_sections.description: In case any person is found dead in a village under circumstances not covered by section 8, it shall be the duty of the Village Officer to give forthwith, to the best of his knowledge and belief to the Registrar such information of the particulars required to be registered concerning such death as he possesses.

main_sections.section_title: In case of births and deaths in hospitals and nursing homes
main_sections.description: (1) In case of births and deaths in hospitals and nursing homes, Medical Officers or other person in charge to send notice to the Registrar. (2) In case of births and deaths in choultries, etc., keeper or person in charge to give the information required.

main_sections.section_title: A person giving oral information to write his name in the register
main_sections.description: Every person who has orally given information required under this Act shall write his name, description and place of abode, and if he cannot write, shall put his mark in the register, to his name, description and place of abode, these particulars being entered in such case entered by the Registrar.

main_sections.section_title: When Registrar to give extract free of charge
main_sections.description: The Registrar shall, as soon as the registration of the birth of a child has been completed, give on application, free of all charge, to the person who gives information of the birth an extract under his hand from the register relating to such birth.

main_sections.section_title: Registrar to register information without fee and inform himself of every birth and death
main_sections.description: Every Registrar shall without the payment of any fee, register all information furnished to him under Sections 6 to 11, and it shall also be his duty to inform himself carefully of every birth and of every death which takes place in his village or ward, and he shall ascertain and register, as soon as convenience may be after the event, the particulars required to be registered according to the forms prescribed under Section 5, touching every such birth or death or the case may be, which has not already been registered.

Where the birth of any child has been registered without a name, the parent or guardian of such child shall within thirteen months of the date of its birth, give information to the Registrar regarding the name of the child to the Registrar, either orally or in writing, and thereupon the Registrar shall enter such name in the register and initial and date the entry.

main_sections.section_title: Search of birth and death registers
main_sections.description: Subject to any rules which the Government may make under Section 18, any person may, at all reasonable times, on payment of a fee of four annas for each visit, search any register of births and deaths and may on payment of a further fee of four annas obtain an extract from such register, relating to any birth or death registered therein.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for omission to give information, etc.
main_sections.description: (1) Any person who (a) fails without reasonable cause to give any information which it is his duty to give under Sections 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 14 of this Act; or (b) gives, or causes to be given, for the purpose of being inserted in any register of births or deaths, any information which is false and which he knows or believes to be false, touching any of the particulars required to be known and registered; or (c) refuses to write his name, description and place of abode or to put his mark in the register as required by Section 11; shall, on conviction before a Magistrate, be liable to a fine not exceeding ten rupees. (2) The Government may impose a penalty not exceeding twenty-five rupees on any person who, having been appointed as Registrar under Section 3, fails without sufficient cause to perform his duties as such.

main_sections.section_title: Prosecutions not to be instituted except under the order of District Registrar or Registrar-General
main_sections.description: No prosecution in respect of any offence punishable under this Act shall be instituted except under the order of the District Registrar having jurisdiction over the village in which the offence was committed or of any officer to whom the District Registrar is subordinate. The Registrar-General or any officer generally or specially empowered by him in this behalf may stay such prosecution.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to frame Forms and make rules
main_sections.description: The Government may, after previous publication, make rules with reference to all matters expressly required or allowed by this Act to be prescribed; defining the powers, duties and functions of the Registrar-General, District Registrars, Taluk Registrars and Registrars; for the conduct of the duties of the Registrar during his absence on other duty or on account of illness or other cause; for the custody, production and transfer of the registers and other records kept by Registrars; for the correction of clerical errors which may be discovered in the registers of births or deaths and (6) generally to carry out the provisions of this Act.
The Travancore Registration of Births and Deaths Act, VII of 1096 and the Cochin Registration of Births and Deaths Act, II of 1081 are hereby repealed.

important_rules: Information of births must be given within two weeks.
Information of deaths must be given within seven days.
Village Officers must provide information on deaths that occur under circumstances not covered by Section 8.
In case of births and deaths in hospitals, nursing homes, or choultries, the Medical Officer or person in charge must send a notice to the Registrar.
Every person giving oral information must write their name in the register or put their mark.
Registrars must register information without fee and keep registers updated.

penalties: Fine not exceeding ten rupees for failure to give information, providing false information, or refusing to sign the register.
Penalty not exceeding twenty-five rupees on a Registrar for failing to perform duties without sufficient cause.
Power for the Registrar-General to compound offences.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: District Registrar or Registrar-General (for prosecutions).
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through prosecutions instituted under the order of the District Registrar or Registrar-General, or by imposing penalties on Registrars.

rights: Right to receive an extract of a birth registration free of charge.
Right to search birth and death registers upon payment of a fee.
Right to obtain an extract from the register upon payment of a fee.
duties: Duty to provide information about births within two weeks.
Duty to provide information about deaths within seven days.
Duty of Village Officers to report deaths in certain circumstances.
Duty of persons in charge of hospitals, nursing homes, and choultries to notify the Registrar of births and deaths.
Duty of a person giving oral information to sign the register.
Duty of Registrars to register information and keep registers updated.
Duty to register the name of a child within thirteen months of birth if not registered initially.

key_procedures: Procedure for registering births: Information to be given within two weeks by the father, karanavan, midwife, or other responsible person. Details to be entered in prescribed forms.

Procedure for registering deaths: Information to be given within seven days by the nearest male adult relative, person present at death, or occupier of the house. Details to be entered in prescribed forms.
Procedure for registering the name of a child: Parent or guardian to inform the Registrar within thirteen months of birth if the name was not registered initially.
Procedure for searching registers: Any person may search registers upon payment of a fee.
Procedure for obtaining extracts from registers: Obtainable upon payment of a fee.
administration: The Government is empowered to frame rules and make appointments for the administration of the Act.
important_notes: Provided that a person not required to give information in the first instance but only in default of some other person shall not be bound to give information under this Act, if he had reasonable cause to suppose that the information had been or would be duly given by such other person.

Provided also that, in the case of an illegitimate child, it shall in the first instance be the duty of the mother of such child to give information under this Act and not person shall, as father of such child, be required to give information under this Act concerning the birth of such child and the Registrar shall not enter in the register, the name of any person as father of such child, unless at the joint request of the mother and of the person acknowledging himself to be the father of such child, and unless such person shall sign the register together with the mother.

All extracts given under this section shall be certified as provided in Section 76 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, (Central Act I of 1872) and may be produced in proof of the entries of which they purport to be copies.
The Registrar-General may, subject to the approval of Government, delegate his powers under sub-section (3) to any District Registrar or Taluk Registrar.

title: The Travancore Cochin Removal of Civil Disabilities Act
purpose: To prevent forfeiture of right of inheritance or of rights to property of a person who renounces or is excluded from the communion of any religion or is deprived of his caste.
scope: The entire State of Travancore-Cochin.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore Cochin Removal of Civil Disabilities Act, 1950. It extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin and shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Change of religion not to entail forfeiture of rights to property or inheritance.
main_sections.description: No person shall incur forfeiture of his right of inheritance or of rights to property by reason of his renouncing or being excluded from the communion of any religion or being deprived of caste, notwithstanding any law, custom or usage to the contrary. Provided that wherever a member of a joint Hindu or Marumakkathayam family renounces or is excluded from the communion of his religion or is deprived of caste, he shall be deemed to have severed his joint status from such family with full rights to partition of his share of the family properties and he shall not be entitled to the right of residence in the family B trust or to exercise the rights of a manager or katanavan of such family.

important_rules: No person shall forfeit inheritance or property rights due to renouncing religion, exclusion from religious communion, or being deprived of caste.

Members of joint Hindu or Marumakkathayam families renouncing or being excluded from religion or deprived of caste are deemed to have severed their joint status and lose rights to family property partition, residence in the family trust, or management.

rights: Right to inheritance
Rights to property
Right to partition of family properties
Right to residence in the family trust
Rights of a manager or katanavan of such family

important_notes: The Act overrides any existing law, custom, or usage to the contrary.
The provision concerning joint families applies to members who renounce or are excluded from religion or are deprived of caste.

title: THE TRAVANCORE-COCHIN REQUISITIONING AND ACQUISITION OF PROPERTY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1958
purpose: An Act to amend the Travancore-Cochin Requisitioning and Acquisition of Property Act, 1955.
scope: Applies to the Travancore-Cochin Requisitioning and Acquisition of Property Act, 1955, and potentially the entire State of Kerala as it amends the definition of 'State'.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Requisitioning and Acquisition of Property (Amendment) Act, 1958, and it shall come into force at once.

Amends section 1 of the Travancore-Cochin Requisitioning and Acquisition of Property Act, 1955, by substituting the words "Requisitioning and Acquisition of Property Act" with "Requisitioning and Acquisition of Property Act" and further elaborating its extension to the whole of the State of Kerala.
Amends section 2 of the principal Act, specifically clause (g), by substituting the definition of 'State' to mean 'the State of Kerala'.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not specified in the provided sections.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not specified in the provided sections.

administration: Not specified in the provided sections.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the President on 6th February, 1959, and was published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 14th February 1959.

title: The Travancore Cochin Requisitioning and Acquisition of Property Act, 1955
purpose: To provide for the requisitioning and acquisition of property for public purposes, not being purposes of the Union.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin.

key_definitions.award: Means any award of an arbitrator made under Section 8.
key_definitions.landlord: Means any person who, for the time being, is receiving or is entitled to receive, the rent of any premises, whether on his own account, or on account or on behalf or for the benefit, of any other person, or who, as trustee, guardian, or receiver for any other person, or who would, would receive the rent or be entitled to receive the rent if the premises were let to a tenant.
key_definitions.person interested: In relation to any property, includes all persons claiming, or entitled to claim, an interest in the compensation payable on account of the requisitioning or acquisition of that property under this Act.
key_definitions.premises: Means any building or part of a building and includes: (i) the garden, grounds and out-houses, if any, appertaining to such building or part of a building; (ii) any fittings affixed to such building or part of a building for the more beneficial enjoyment thereof;
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.property: Means movable or immovable property of every kind and includes any rights in or over such property.

main_sections.section_title: Short title, extent, commencement and duration.
main_sections.description: Names the Act as The Travancore-Cochin Requisitioning and Acquisition of Property Act, 1955. Extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin. Comes into force at once and remains in force for a period of six years from the date of commencement.
Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'award', 'landlord', 'person interested', 'premises', 'prescribed', and 'property'.

Grants the Government the power to requisition property for public purposes. Outlines the procedure for issuing a notice of requisition and its effects. Specifies exceptions for certain types of property such as religious institutions and places of worship.

main_sections.section_title: Power to take possession of requisitioned property.
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to take possession of requisitioned property. Details the process of issuing a notice and the consequences of non-compliance. Also covers cases where the property is destroyed or damaged.
States that all property requisitioned under Section 3 shall be used for such purposes as mentioned in the notice of requisition.
Provides for the release of requisitioned property if it is no longer needed, or if the conditions causing its requisition are no longer in force.

Grants the Government the power to acquire requisitioned property if it is of the opinion that it is necessary for a public purpose. Outlines the procedure for issuing a notice of acquisition and the acquisition becoming absolute.

main_sections.section_title: Principles and method of determining compensation in cases where immovable property is requisitioned or acquired.
main_sections.description: Lays down the principles for determining compensation. Compensation can be fixed by agreement or determined by an arbitrator appointed by the Government. The arbitrator's decision is final, subject to appeals.

main_sections.section_title: Payment of compensation relating to immovable property.
main_sections.description: Specifies how compensation for immovable property is to be paid, subject to rules made under the Act and as determined by the Government or by an arbitrator.

main_sections.section_title: Appeals from awards in respect of compensation.
main_sections.description: Provides for appeals against awards of arbitrators in respect of compensation to the High Court.

main_sections.section_title: Government and Officers and authorities empowered by Government and arbitrator to have certain powers of civil courts.
main_sections.description: Confers powers of civil courts on Government officers and arbitrators for the purposes of this Act, including summoning, enforcing attendance, and compelling production of documents and evidence.

main_sections.section_title: Principles and method of determining compensation in cases where movable property is requisitioned or acquired.
main_sections.description: Similar to Section 8, this section deals with the principles and methods for determining compensation for movable property.
Grants the Government the power to obtain information regarding any property that is intended to be requisitioned or acquired.
Empowers Government officers to enter and inspect any property for the purpose of determining whether it should be requisitioned or acquired.
Specifies how notices and orders issued under this Act are to be served.
Ensures that easements are not disturbed by the requisitioning or acquisition of property.
Allows the Government to delegate its powers under this Act to subordinate officers.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
main_sections.description: Provides protection to persons acting in good faith under the provisions of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Bar of jurisdiction of Civil Courts.
main_sections.description: Limits the jurisdiction of civil courts in matters concerning requisitioning and acquisition of property under this Act, except for appeals provided.
Defines penalties for contravention of the provisions of this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Certain persons to be public servants.
main_sections.description: Declares certain persons discharging duties under this Act as public servants.
Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of certain requisitions and acquisitions.
main_sections.description: Provides for the validation of certain past requisitions and acquisitions.
Repeals any existing laws inconsistent with this Act and provides for savings.

important_rules: Property requisitioned can only be used for the purpose stated in the notice of requisition.
Compensation for requisitioned or acquired immovable property is to be determined based on principles outlined in Section 8.
Compensation for movable property is to be determined based on principles outlined in Section 12.
Notices and orders under the Act must be served in the prescribed manner.

penalties: Penalty for offences is defined in Section 20.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government and officers empowered by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the powers conferred on Government officers and arbitrators, which include powers of civil courts for summoning, enforcing attendance, and compelling production of documents and evidence. Also through penalties defined for offences.

rights: Right to compensation for requisitioned or acquired property.
Right to appeal against arbitration awards to the High Court.
Right for certain persons to be declared public servants.
duties: Duty to comply with notices and orders issued under the Act.
Duty for persons in possession of requisitioned property to surrender it.
Duty to provide information when requested by the Government.
obligations: Obligation to release requisitioned property when no longer required.
Obligation to pay compensation for requisitioned or acquired property.

key_procedures: Procedure for Requisitioning: Government issues a notice specifying the public purpose. Property is requisitioned, and possession may be taken.
Procedure for Acquisition: If necessary, the Government can acquire requisitioned property after issuing a notice. Acquisition becomes absolute on publication.
Procedure for Compensation Determination: Compensation can be fixed by agreement or determined by an arbitrator. The arbitrator's award can be appealed to the High Court.
Procedure for Appeal: Appeals from arbitration awards on compensation lie with the High Court.
administration: The Government of Travancore-Cochin, and officers and authorities empowered by the Government.
important_notes: The Act has a limited duration of six years from its commencement.
Certain properties, like those exclusively used for religious worship, are exempt from requisitioning.
The Act aims to serve public purposes and is not for purposes of the Union.
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected.

title: THE TRAVANCORE COCHIN REVENUE ENQUIRIES AND SUMMONS ACT
purpose: To empower Revenue Officers to summon persons and produce documents for the purpose of disposal of matters connected with revenue administration, and to conduct enquiries.
scope: The Act applies to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin.

key_definitions.Revenue Officers: Includes Collectors, Deputy Collectors, Tahsildars and Deputy Tahsildars who have the power to summon any person.
key_definitions.Summons: A written order authenticated by the signature and seal of the officer by whom it is issued, requiring the person summoned to appear at a stated time and place and specify whether his attendance is required for the purpose of giving evidence or to produce documents, or both.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Revenue Enquiries and Summons Act, 1950, extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin, and shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Revenue Officers empowered to summon persons etc.
main_sections.description: Confers power upon Board of Revenue, Collectors, Deputy Collectors, Tahsildars, and Deputy Tahsildars to summon any person whose evidence may appear to them to be necessary for the investigation of any matter in which they are authorized to hold an enquiry, and also to require the production of any document relevant to the matter under enquiry.
Details the requirements for a summons to be valid, including authentication, appearance at a stated time and place, and the purpose of the summons (giving evidence, producing documents, etc.).

Prescribes the method of serving summons, which includes delivering a copy to the summoned person or their authorized agent, or affixing a copy to the outer door of the house if the person cannot be found and no adult male member of the family can be conveniently served. It also outlines the process for returning the original summons with an endorsement of service.

Allows for persons summoned to produce documents and allows for the production of documents by third party. If the summoned person fails to produce the document without reasonable cause, the summons shall be deemed to have been complied with if the document is produced at the time of attendance.

main_sections.section_title: When personal attendance of witnesses may be dispensed with
main_sections.description: Allows for the personal attendance of a witness to be dispensed with if they are unable to appear due to sickness, infirmity or other sufficient cause, or if they are exempted from appearance in Civil Courts, or if they are a woman according to the custom of her community. The enquiry officer may, in such cases, direct that the evidence be taken by a subordinate deputed by him, or at the place where the witness resides.

main_sections.section_title: Travelling and other expenses of persons summoned
main_sections.description: States that any person summoned under this Act shall be entitled to his travelling and other expenses.
Requires any officer making an enquiry to orally examine any person summoned to give evidence, or to acquire any fact relevant to the matter. The statements recorded may be reduced into writing.

main_sections.section_title: Investment of powers on other officers
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to invest, by notification in the Gazette, any officer with any of the powers conferred by this Act.
Repeals the Revenue Summons Act, V of 1063 (Travancore) and the Cochin Revenue Enquiries Act, I of 1084.

important_rules: Summons must be in writing and authenticated by the signature and seal of the issuing officer.
A summoned person must appear at the stated time and place for the purpose specified in the summons.
If a person summoned to produce documents fails to do so without reasonable cause, the summons is considered complied with if the document is produced at the time of attendance.
Personal attendance of witnesses can be dispensed with under certain circumstances, with evidence taken by a subordinate or at the witness's residence.
Statements made by witnesses during examination shall be bound to answer truly all questions relating to the matter.

penalties: Failure to appear or produce documents may be treated as an offence leading to a penalty or forfeiture.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Revenue Officers as empowered by the Act, and any officer to whom powers are delegated by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the issuance of summons, examination of witnesses, and requiring production of documents. Non-compliance can lead to penalties.

rights: Right to receive travelling and other expenses for summoned persons.
Right to have personal attendance dispensed with under specific conditions.
duties: Duty to appear when summoned.
Duty to produce documents when summoned.
Duty to answer questions truly during examination.
obligations: Obligation to comply with the terms of the summons.

key_procedures: Issuance of a summons by an empowered Revenue Officer.
Service of the summons on the individual concerned.
Appearance of the summoned person at the specified time and place.
Examination of the summoned person or review of produced documents.
Dispensing with personal attendance under specific circumstances.
Enforcement of compliance through penalties.
administration: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to be under the purview of the Revenue administration of the State of Travancore-Cochin.
important_notes: The Act repeals the Travancore Revenue Summons Act, V of 1063 and the Cochin Revenue Enquiries Act, I of 1084.
The Act is applicable to the entire State of Travancore-Cochin.
The Government has the power to invest officers with the powers granted by this Act.

title: The Travancore Cochin Revenue Recovery Act, 1951
purpose: To provide a uniform law for the recovery of public revenue in the State of Travancore-Cochin.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin. It covers the recovery of public revenue from defaulters.

key_definitions.public_revenue_due_on_land: Includes the 'assessment, rent or money charged on lands and payable to the Government of Sri Pandara Vargal and all fees and cesses, whether in kind or money, which, whether charged on land or not, are recovered as assessment on land and all cesses or other dues payable to the Government on account of water used for purposes of irrigation.
key_definitions.arrears_of_public_revenue: Means the whole or any portion of any kist or instalment of public revenue not paid on the day on which it falls due, according to the kistbandy or any engagement or usage.
key_definitions.land_holder: Means the registered holder for the time being of any land, and includes his legal representatives and assigns, and includes any person who holds the land for the time being in force is liable for the payment of public revenue in respect of land held by him.
key_definitions.defaulter: Means a person from whom an arrear of public revenue is due, and includes a person who is responsible as surety for the payment of any such arrear of revenue.
key_definitions.collector: Means the chief officer in charge of the revenue administration of the District and includes an acting or officiating Collector, and also any officer appointed by the Government to exercise the functions of the Collector.

main_sections.description: This section likely states the short title of the Act, its territorial extent (the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin), and the date of commencement.
This section defines various terms used in the Act, such as 'public revenue due on land', 'arrears of public revenue', 'land-holder', 'defaulter', and 'Collector'.
This section likely details what constitutes security for public revenue, possibly including the land itself and any other property of the defaulter.

main_sections.section_title: Revenue to be paid to the officer authorised in time.
main_sections.description: This section probably specifies the designated officer to whom revenue payments should be made and the timeframe for such payments.
This section is likely to detail the provisions for charging interest on overdue revenue payments.

main_sections.section_title: Process of recovering arrears of revenue.
main_sections.description: This section probably outlines the general procedures and steps to be followed for the recovery of revenue arrears.

main_sections.section_title: Rules for seizure and sale of movable property.
main_sections.description: This section outlines the rules and procedures for seizing and selling the movable property of a defaulter to recover revenue arrears.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure when the distrainer is other than the Tahsildar.
main_sections.description: This section likely details the process to be followed when the person responsible for distress is someone other than the Tahsildar.
This section likely covers the process and conditions for the sale of property that has been distrained.
This section likely specifies which officer is responsible for conducting the sale of distrained property.
This section details the procedure and manner in which the sale of distrained property should be conducted.

main_sections.section_title: Payment of the purchase-money - Re sale.
main_sections.description: This section likely covers the payment of the purchase money by the buyer and the procedures for a resale if the initial payment is not made.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure where defaulter tenders payment of the arrear after distraint but before sale of his property.
main_sections.description: This section outlines the procedure to be followed if the defaulter pays the arrears after the property has been distrained but before it is sold.

main_sections.section_title: Claims to property distrained and sold.
main_sections.description: This section likely addresses claims made by third parties regarding property that has been distrained and sold.

main_sections.section_title: What places distrainer may enter or force open and enter
main_sections.description: This section specifies the places that a distrainer can enter or force open to execute the distress.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure where property is lodged within apartments appropriated to women.
main_sections.description: This section details the specific procedure to be followed when property to be distrained is located within parts of a dwelling designated for women.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for entry into such apartments.
main_sections.description: This section likely describes the penalties for unlawfully entering apartments designated for women during distress.

main_sections.section_title: Notice to state value of revenue in kind.
main_sections.description: This section probably mandates notice regarding the value of revenue payable in kind.

main_sections.section_title: Demand to be served prior to attachment of immovable property.
main_sections.description: This section likely requires a formal demand notice to be served before attaching immovable property.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure when defaulter neglects to pay.
main_sections.description: This section probably outlines the steps to be taken when a defaulter fails to pay after being served with a notice.
This section details the process of attaching the immovable property of a defaulter.
This section likely covers how attached immovable property is to be managed to preserve its value.
This section probably deals with the appointment of an agent to manage the attached property.
This section likely details the requirement of giving notice before resuming management of attached property.

main_sections.section_title: Agent to collect rents and profits.
main_sections.description: This section probably states that the appointed agent is responsible for collecting rents and profits from the attached property.
This section likely mandates that the agent must render accounts of the collected rents and profits.

main_sections.section_title: Surplus to go to the defaulter.
main_sections.description: This section probably states that any surplus proceeds from the sale of attached property, after satisfying the revenue due, should be returned to the defaulter.

main_sections.section_title: Effect of existing agreements between land-holder and tenant.
main_sections.description: This section likely addresses how the Act affects existing agreements between landowners and tenants.
This section probably relates to how tenants are expected to make payments in the context of revenue recovery.

main_sections.section_title: Release of attachment when objected to by auy other than the defaulter.
main_sections.description: This section details the procedure for releasing an attachment if an objection is raised by someone other than the defaulter.

main_sections.section_title: Persons interested in the land may obtain release from attachment.
main_sections.description: This section allows persons with an interest in the land to obtain its release from attachment under certain conditions.
This section focuses on the procedures for the sale of attached immovable property.

main_sections.section_title: Application to set aside sale of immovable property on deposit.
main_sections.description: This section likely allows for setting aside a sale of immovable property if a deposit is made within a specified period.

main_sections.section_title: Sale to be free of all encumbrances.
main_sections.description: This section states that the sale of property under this Act is free from all encumbrances.

main_sections.section_title: Defaulter entitled to recover arrears of rent due on day of sale.
main_sections.description: This section likely grants the defaulter the right to recover rent due up to the day of the sale.

main_sections.section_title: Lands sold to be proportionate to arrears due.
main_sections.description: This section probably ensures that only the necessary portion of land is sold to recover the due arrears.

main_sections.section_title: Apportionment of assessment when part only of a single property is sold.
main_sections.description: This section details how the assessment is to be apportioned when only a portion of a property is sold.

main_sections.section_title: Security by behalf ofponent of sale.
main_sections.description: This section might refer to security provided by a bidder or purchaser at the sale.
This section likely outlines the conditions under which a sale can be postponed.

main_sections.section_title: Sureties liable for the arrears as well as the principals.
main_sections.description: This section clarifies the liability of sureties for the arrears, along with the principal defaulters.
This section likely deals with the payment of 'batta' (allowance) to persons serving processes related to the recovery.

main_sections.section_title: Who to bear expense of countermanded sale.
main_sections.description: This section determines who is responsible for the expenses if a sale is countermanded.

main_sections.section_title: Procedure when a defaulter or his surety resides or holds property in another Taluk.
main_sections.description: This section details the procedure when the defaulter or their surety is located in a different Taluk.

main_sections.section_title: Attachment of securities and debts of defaulters.
main_sections.description: This section covers the attachment of securities and debts owed to defaulters.
This section likely grants a higher authority the power to revise decisions made under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Saving of rights to sue - Limitation.
main_sections.description: This section likely saves the right of a party to file a civil suit and may also address limitations on such suits.

main_sections.section_title: Questions as to sale or amount of assessment not to be considered by a Civil Court.
main_sections.description: This section likely restricts the jurisdiction of Civil Courts in questioning sales conducted under the Act or the amount of assessment.

main_sections.section_title: Judgement-creditor of the defaulter may pay arrears.
main_sections.description: This section allows a judgment-creditor of the defaulter to pay the arrears to protect their interest.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of agent to suit or prosecution.
main_sections.description: This section likely specifies the liability of an agent appointed under the Act to suits or prosecution for misconduct.
This section might refer to the delegation or invention of powers conferred by the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Power of Government to declare the Act applicable to any institution.
main_sections.description: This section grants the Government the power to extend the provisions of the Act to specific institutions.

main_sections.section_title: The provisions of the Act applicable to the recovery of certain arrears of revenue other than land revenue.
main_sections.description: This section extends the applicability of the Act to the recovery of specific types of revenue, other than land revenue.

main_sections.section_title: Who shall not bid at revenue sales.
main_sections.description: This section specifies individuals who are prohibited from bidding at revenue sales.
This section likely deals with the repeal of any previous laws or enactments that are inconsistent with this Act.

important_rules: Movable property of a defaulter may be distrained for arrears of revenue.
Distrained movable property can be sold after following specific procedures, including public auction.
If a defaulter tenders the entire arrear amount along with costs of distress and sale before the sale, the property shall be released.
Sales of immovable property are generally to be conducted by the Collector or Tahsildar.
A sale of immovable property may be set aside if the defaulter deposits the arrears along with costs within a specified period after the sale.
Sales conducted under this Act are free from all encumbrances.
Land sold shall be proportionate to the arrears due.
A judgment-creditor of a defaulter may pay the arrears to protect their interests.
Certain persons are prohibited from bidding at revenue sales.

penalties: Penalties for unlawful entry into apartments appropriated to women during distress (Section 22).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Collector, Tahsildar, and other officers authorized by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through seizure and sale of movable and immovable property of defaulters, imposition of interest on arrears, and other legally prescribed procedures.

rights: Right of a defaulter to recover arrears of rent due up to the day of sale (Section 40).
Right of persons interested in the land to obtain release from attachment (Section 36).
Right of a defaulter to receive surplus proceeds from the sale of property after arrears are cleared (Section 32).
Right to apply to set aside a sale of immovable property on deposit (Section 38).
duties: Duty to pay public revenue to the authorized officer in time.
Duty of the agent to collect rents and profits and render accounts.
Duty to comply with the procedures for seizure and sale of property.
obligations: Obligation of the defaulter to pay arrears of revenue.
Obligation of sureties to pay arrears along with the principal.

key_procedures: Procedure for seizure and sale of movable property: This involves distraining the property, preparing a list, notifying the defaulter, and conducting a public sale. (Section 7 onwards).

Procedure for attachment and sale of immovable property: This involves serving a demand notice, attaching the property, potentially managing it through an agent, and then conducting a sale. (Section 24 onwards).
Procedure for setting aside a sale: A defaulter can get a sale set aside by paying the arrears and costs within a stipulated time after the sale.
Procedure for persons other than the defaulter to claim release of attached property.
administration: The revenue administration of the District, headed by the Collector, is responsible for the implementation of this Act. The Tahsildar is also a key official in the process.
important_notes: The Act was enacted by the Legislative Assembly and assented to by H. H. the Raj Pramukh.
Published in Part I Section III of the Gazette dated 22nd May 1951.
The Act provides for the recovery of public revenue, which includes assessment, rent, fees, and cesses payable to the Government.
Certain provisions apply to the recovery of revenue other than land revenue.
Civil Courts are restricted from questioning sales conducted under the Act or the amount of assessment.

title: The Travancore Cochin Sale of Khaddar Act
purpose: To regulate the sale of Khaddar or Khadi in the State of Travancore-Cochin.
scope: Applies to the whole of Travancore-Cochin State.

key_definitions.Khaddar: Means any cloth woven on handlooms in India, from cotton, silk or woollen yarn hand-spun in India, or from a mixture of any two or all of such yarns.
key_definitions.Dealer: Means a person carrying on the business of selling 'Khaddar' or 'Khadi' whether whole-sale or retail, and whether in conjunction with any other business or not.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Sale of Khaddar Act, 1951. It extends to the whole of the Travancore-Cochin State and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint.
Defines 'Dealer' and 'Khaddar' or 'Khadi'.

main_sections.section_title: Sale of Khaddar or Khadi by licensed dealers only.
main_sections.description: No dealer shall sell 'Khaddar' or 'Khadi' except under and in accordance with a licence granted by a licensing authority under this Act.
The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint one or more persons as they may think fit, to be the licensing authority for any local area or for the whole State.

Subject to any rules made under this Act, a licensing authority may, on the application of a person and after making such inquiry as it thinks fit, grant a licence to him to sell 'Khaddar' or 'Khadi'.

Any dealer who contravenes the provisions of Section 3 or commits a breach of any of the conditions of a licence granted under this Act shall be punishable with imprisonment which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees.

If the person committing an offence under this Act is a company, every director, manager, secretary or other officer or agent thereof shall, unless he proves that the offence took place without his knowledge or that he exercised all due diligence to prevent the commission of such offence, be deemed to be guilty of such offence.
No Court shall take cognizance of any offence punishable under this Act except upon a complaint in writing made by the licensing authority for the area in which the offence is committed.

Nothing in this Act shall apply to any dealer who holds a certificate in the form prescribed by rules made under this Act from the Secretary of the All-India Spinner's Association or from such other person as may be authorised in writing in this behalf by the said Secretary.

The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act. Such rules may provide for the form in which an application for a licence is to be made, the form in which the conditions subject to which a licence may be granted, the fees to be levied for the grant of licences, and the form in which certificates under Section 9 may be granted.

important_rules: Rule 1: No dealer shall sell 'Khaddar' or 'Khadi' except under and in accordance with a licence granted by a licensing authority under this Act.
Rule 2: Rules may be made for the form of application for licence, conditions of licence, fees for licence, and form of certificates under Section 9.

penalties: Imprisonment which may extend to six months or fine which may extend to one thousand rupees for contravening Section 3 or breaching licence conditions.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Licensing authority.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through complaints filed by the licensing authority to the Court.

rights: Right to apply for a licence to sell Khaddar or Khadi.
Exemption from the Act if holding a certificate from the All-India Spinner's Association or authorized person.
duties: Dealers have a duty to obtain a licence before selling Khaddar or Khadi.
Dealers must adhere to the conditions of their licence.
obligations: Corporations committing offences are liable, with individual officers/agents also liable if they cannot prove lack of knowledge or due diligence.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Application for a licence to sell Khaddar or Khadi by a dealer to the licensing authority.
Procedure 2: Inquiry by the licensing authority before granting a licence.
Procedure 3: Filing a complaint by the licensing authority to initiate court proceedings for offences.
administration: Licensing authorities appointed by the Government.
important_notes: The Act is applicable to the entire Travancore-Cochin State.
The Act came into force on a date to be notified in the Gazette.
Certain persons holding certificates from the All-India Spinner's Association are exempted from the provisions of the Act.

title: The Travancore-Cochin Stamp (Amendment) Act, 1955
purpose: An Act to amend the Travancore-Cochin Stamp Act, 1125.
scope: Applies to the Travancore-Cochin region, specifically amending existing stamp act legislation.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Stamp (Amendment) Act, 1955, and it shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 12, Act I of 1125
main_sections.description: Amends Section 12 of the Travancore-Cochin Stamp Act, 1125. It specifies that in the said Act, for clause (c), the following clause shall be substituted: "(c) entry as an Advocate on the roll of the High Court."

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Article 30 of the Schedule to Act I of 1125
main_sections.description: States that in Article 30 of the Schedule to the said Act, clause (b) shall be omitted.

important_notes: The Preamble indicates that it is expedient to amend the Travancore-Cochin Stamp Act, 1125.
The Act was enacted in the Sixth Year of the Republic of India.

title: The Travancore Cochin State Aid to Industries (Amendment) Act, 1956
purpose: To amend The Travancore-Cochin State Aid to Industries Act, 1952, for the purposes described therein.
scope: This act applies to the Travancore-Cochin State and concerns the State Aid to Industries Act, 1952.

main_sections.description: States that the short title of the Act is the Travancore-Cochin State Aid to Industries (Amendment) Act, 1956, and it shall come into force on the 10th day of April, 1956.

Amends Section 11 of the Travancore-Cochin State Aid to Industries Act, 1952 (XIX of 1952). It specifies provisions related to loans, including the maximum loan amount in proportion to the value of the industry's assets and the procedure for discharging encumbrances on property when the loan is made or offered as collateral security.

main_sections.section_title: Validation of things done and action taken.
main_sections.description: Validates any act or action taken in the exercise of powers conferred by the Travancore-Cochin State Aid to Industries Ordinance, 1956 (1 of 1956), as if such act or action were in force at the time the Ordinance was enacted.

important_rules: Loans granted under the Act shall not exceed a prescribed percentage of the value of the assets of the industry to which it is granted.
When a loan is offered as collateral security, the property offered must be free from any existing encumbrances.
When the loan is made, the value ascertained by the Director must be stated.
Any loan offered as collateral security must be secured first on the assets and other property of the borrower.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Director
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Ascertainment of value of assets and property by the Director.

rights: Right to receive aid/loans for industries under the Act.
duties: Duty to ensure loans do not exceed prescribed percentage of asset value.
Duty to ensure collateral is free from encumbrances.
obligations: Obligation to have the value of assets and property ascertained by the Director when a loan is made.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining loans: Loans are subject to a prescribed percentage of asset value and require collateral to be free from encumbrances, with the value ascertained by the Director.

Procedure for discharging encumbrances: When a loan is granted, or offered as collateral security, the property must be free of existing encumbrances, and the loan is secured first on the assets and other property of the borrower.
administration: The administration is implied to be handled by the authorities responsible for implementing the State Aid to Industries Act, 1952.
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Travancore-Cochin State Aid to Industries Act, 1952.
The amendment comes into force on April 10, 1956.
Certain provisions of Section 11 of the principal Act are substituted.
Actions taken under the Travancore-Cochin State Aid to Industries Ordinance, 1956, are validated.

title: THE TRAVANCORE-COCHIN STATE AID TO INDUSTRIES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1955
purpose: To amend the Travancore-Cochin State Aid to Industries Act, 1952.
scope: Applies to the Travancore-Cochin State.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin State Aid to Industries (Amendment) Act, 1955. It shall come into force at once.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 11, Act XIX of 1952.
main_sections.description: Amends Section 11 of the Travancore-Cochin State Aid to Industries Act, 1952 (Act XIX of 1952) by substituting a new proviso. The new proviso states that no loan shall exceed the prescribed percentage of the net value of the assets of the industry to which it is granted and of other property, if any, offered as collateral security, after deducting all encumbrances thereon existing at the time when the application for the loan is made. It also adds a clause stating that nothing in the first proviso can be construed as taking away or limiting the rights of the Government to inquire into the assets of the industry or any property offered as collateral security existing at the time the loan application is made.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Section 13, Act XIX of 1952.
main_sections.description: Amends Section 13 of the Travancore-Cochin State Aid to Industries Act, 1952 by substituting a new sub-section. This new sub-section states that the Director may sanction a loan not exceeding the prescribed limit in any case of any one industry if the Board has recommended the grant of such loan. If the Board has not recommended it, the Director shall forthwith make a report to the Government of such case. In all other cases, the Director shall submit to the Government the application and the opinion of the Board and all connected papers together with such remarks, if any, as he has himself to make.
Repeals the Travancore-Cochin State Aid to Industries (Amendment) Ordinance, 1955 (III of 1955).

important_rules: Loans granted under the Act shall not exceed a prescribed percentage of the net value of the industry's assets or offered collateral security.
Government has the right to inquire into existing assets and collateral security when processing loan applications.
The Director has the authority to sanction loans recommended by the Board, or to report to the Government if the Board does not recommend a loan.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Director

rights: Right of the Government to inquire into assets and collateral security.
obligations: The Director must report to the Government if the Board has not recommended a loan.

key_procedures: Loan application process involving the Director and the Board, with provision for Government review.
Submission of loan applications, Board's opinion, and related documents to the Government for review when the Board has not recommended the loan.
important_notes: The Act came into force immediately upon its enactment.
The Travancore-Cochin State Aid to Industries (Amendment) Ordinance, 1955, has been repealed.

title: THE TRAVANCORE-COCHIN STATE AID TO INDUSTRIES ACT, 1952
purpose: To provide for the giving of State aid to industries in the Travancore-Cochin State.
scope: The Act applies to all industries in the Travancore-Cochin State.

key_definitions.Board: The State Aid to Industries Board constituted under Section 3.
key_definitions.Director: The Director of Industries and includes any person appointed by the Government either by name or by virtue of his office, to perform any of the functions of the Director under this Act.
key_definitions.industry: Any industrial business or enterprise conducted in the State by any individual, company, association or body of individuals whether incorporated or not.
key_definitions.machinery: Includes plant apparatus, tools and other appliances required for the purpose of carrying on any industrial operation or process.
key_definitions.owner: Means the person who owns any industrial undertaking and includes the successors in interest of such person in respect of such undertaking.
key_definitions.prescribed: Means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.State Aid: Means aid given by or on behalf of the Government under the provisions of this Act and the rules, if any, thereunder.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin State Aid to Industries Act, 1952. It extends to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin and shall come into force on such date as the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, appoint in that behalf.
This section provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'Director', 'industry', 'machinery', 'owner', 'prescribed', and 'State Aid'.

main_sections.section_title: Constitution of a State Aid to Industries Board
main_sections.description: This section details the establishment, composition, and functioning of the State Aid to Industries Board. It specifies the number of members, their appointment, term of office, resignation, removal, and the role of the Chairman and Vice-Chairman.

This section outlines the term of office for the Chairman and members of the Board, which is three years, and provisions for reappointment or continuation in office until their successor is appointed.
This section explains the process for the Chairman or any member of the Board to resign their position.
This section describes the grounds on which the Government may remove the Chairman or any member of the Board from office.

main_sections.section_title: Vacancy of Chair man or member
main_sections.description: This section deals with how vacancies in the position of Chairman or member of the Board are filled.
This section clarifies who presides over the meetings of the Board.

main_sections.section_title: Interested members not to vote or take part in discussion
main_sections.description: This section specifies that members with a personal interest in a matter before the Board cannot vote or participate in discussions on that matter.
This section allows the Government to abolish the Board by notification in the Gazette under certain circumstances.
This section details the various forms of State aid that can be granted to industries, including loans, guarantees, subsidies, and machinery on hire-purchase.

This section outlines the types of industries eligible for State aid, including new or nascent industries, industries to be newly established in underdeveloped areas, profitable industrial ventures, cottage industries, and others the Government deems deserving.
This section describes the procedure for applying for State aid, including the required information and process for submission and inquiry.

main_sections.section_title: Percentage of value to be deposited by hirer.
main_sections.description: This section relates to the hire-purchase system for machinery and specifies the percentage of the value to be deposited by the hirer.

main_sections.section_title: Particulars to be specified in the order when application is allowed.
main_sections.description: This section outlines the details that must be included in an order when an application for State aid is allowed, particularly concerning the hire-purchase of machinery.

main_sections.section_title: Conditions of supply of machinery on hire purchase system.
main_sections.description: This section details the conditions under which machinery can be supplied on a hire-purchase system.
This section describes the consequences when a hirer defaults on their obligations under the hire-purchase system.

main_sections.section_title: Option of hirer to purchase machinery seized for default.
main_sections.description: This section provides the hirer with an option to purchase machinery that has been seized due to default.
This section outlines the conditions under which a hirer can terminate the hiring agreement.

main_sections.section_title: Liability of hirer on termination of hiring under Sections 23 and 25.
main_sections.description: This section details the liability of the hirer upon termination of the hiring agreement, referencing Sections 23 and 25.

main_sections.section_title: Termination of hiring on payment of cost of machinery.
main_sections.description: This section covers the termination of hiring upon payment of the full cost of the machinery.

main_sections.section_title: Penalty for omission to remove metal plate when machinery becomes property of hirer.
main_sections.description: This section imposes a penalty for failing to remove a metal plate when machinery becomes the property of the hirer.
This section likely pertains to the process of revising decisions or orders made under the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Methods of recovery of money due.
main_sections.description: This section describes the methods by which money due to the Government under the Act can be recovered.

main_sections.section_title: Finality of decision of Government and protection of persons acting under this Act.
main_sections.description: This section deals with the finality of decisions made by the Government and provides protection for individuals acting in good faith under the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.section_title: Persons acting under the Act to be deemed public servants.
main_sections.description: This section declares that persons acting under the Act shall be considered public servants.
This section likely outlines general penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions.
This section grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.
This section repeals any previous legislation that is inconsistent with this Act.

important_rules: The Board shall consist of not less than seven and not more than twelve members, and the Director of Industries shall be an ex-officio member.

Members of the Board, not being less than three as may be fixed by the Government, shall be elected by the members of the State Legislative Assembly in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.
The remaining members shall be nominated by the Government.
Not less than three-fifths of the elected members shall be non-officials.
The Chairman of the Board shall be appointed by the Government from among the members of the Board.
The nomination, election, resignation and removal of the Chairman and members of the Board shall be notified in the Gazette.
The Chairman and members of the Board shall hold office for a term of three years but shall continue to hold office until their successor is appointed.

The Chairman and members may be removed by the Government for physical or mental disability, conviction of an offence, absence without excuse for three consecutive meetings, or contravention of Section 9.
No business shall be transacted at any meeting of the Board unless one-half of the sanctioned number of members are present.
No member of the Board shall vote or take part in discussion if he has a direct or indirect pecuniary interest in the matter.
State aid may be given in the form of loans, guarantees, subsidies, and machinery on hire-purchase.
Loans shall be secured and repaid in the prescribed manner and upon such terms as may be fixed by the order granting the loan.
The loan amount shall not exceed the prescribed percentage of the net value of the assets of the industry.
Loans shall be repayable within a period not exceeding twenty years.
The securing of a loan shall include insurance of the property and the assignment of security in favour of the Government.
Applications for State aid shall be made to the Director in the prescribed manner and shall contain particulars as may be prescribed.
The Director shall make such inquiries as he thinks necessary on every application.
Every application shall, thereafter, be placed with the remarks of the Director together with all connected papers before the Board at a meeting for its opinion.
The Government may grant State aid to any industry, subject to the provisions of the Act and rules.
State aid shall not be given to any joint stock company unless it is registered in India with a rupee capital and agrees to maintain the prescribed proportion of its Directors on its Board.
Every recipient of State aid shall make provision for the training of apprentices as may be prescribed.
The Government has the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

penalties: Penalty for omission to remove metal plate when machinery becomes property of hirer.
General penalties for contravention of the Act's provisions (Section 33).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government and the Director of Industries.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through application review, granting of aid, imposition of conditions, recovery of dues, and penalties for non-compliance. Decisions of the Government are generally final. Persons acting under the Act are deemed public servants.

rights: Industries have the right to apply for State aid.
Hirers of machinery have the option to purchase seized machinery.
Protection for persons acting under the Act.
duties: Recipients of State aid must secure and repay loans in the prescribed manner.
Recipients of State aid must make provision for the training of apprentices.
Hirers must adhere to the terms of the hire-purchase agreement.
Companies receiving aid must maintain a certain proportion of Directors on their Board.
obligations: To comply with the terms and conditions of the State aid granted.
To adhere to the rules and regulations prescribed under the Act.

key_procedures: Application for State aid: An application must be made to the Director in the prescribed manner. The Director will conduct inquiries and then place the application with remarks before the Board for its opinion.
Granting of State aid: The Government may grant State aid based on the Board's opinion and the provisions of the Act.
Recovery of money due: Methods for recovering money due to the Government are outlined.
Termination of hiring (hire-purchase): Procedures for termination by the hirer and the consequences thereof.
Removal of Board members: Government can remove members on specific grounds.
Abolition of the Board: Government can abolish the Board by notification.
administration: The Director of Industries and the State Aid to Industries Board, under the overall authority of the Government.
important_notes: The Act extends to the entire State of Travancore-Cochin.
The Act came into force on a date appointed by the Government through a Gazette notification.
The Government has the power to make rules for the implementation of the Act.
Decisions of the Government are generally final.
Persons acting under the Act are deemed public servants.

title: The Travancore-Cochin Suppression of Immoral Traffic Act, 1951
purpose: To make better provision for the suppression of brothels and of traffic in women in the State of Travancore-Cochin.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Travancore-Cochin.

key_definitions.brothel: Any house, room, or place which the occupier or person in charge thereof habitually allows to be used by any other person for the purpose of prostitution.
key_definitions.magistrate: A salaried Magistrate of the First Class.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Travancore-Cochin Suppression of Immoral Traffic Act, 1951.

The Government may, from time to time by notification in the Gazette, apply all or any of the provisions of this Act to the whole or any portion of the State of Travancore-Cochin from such date as may be specified in the notification, and may cancel or modify any such notification.
Defines 'Brothel', 'Magistrate', and 'Prostitution'.

main_sections.section_title: Punishment for keeping a brothel or allowing premises to be used as a brothel.
main_sections.description: Punishes persons who keep or manage brothels or assist in the management, with imprisonment and fine.
