Inserts a new section 51A, which is not detailed in the provided excerpt.
Amends section 52 of the principal Act, which is not detailed in the provided excerpt.
Amends the First Schedule of the principal Act.
Amends the Second Schedule of the principal Act.

important_rules: No person shall sell or purchase liquor except under a license.
Liquor may be sold only in a licensed shop during the hours specified in the license.
Consumption of liquor in public places is prohibited.
Transport of liquor is restricted and requires a permit.
Possession of liquor above a certain limit without a license is an offense.
Denatured spirits unfit for human consumption are prohibited from being rendered fit.
Anyone found in a state of intoxication may be arrested and required to produce a medical certificate.
The Government may grant exemptions to certain individuals or groups from the provisions of this Act.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months and fine which may extend to one thousand rupees for a first offense.
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year and fine which may extend to two thousand rupees for a second and subsequent offenses.
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months and fine which may extend to five hundred rupees for a first offense.
Imprisonment which may extend to two thousand rupees, but in the absence of special and adequate reasons to the contrary to be mentioned in the judgment of the court.
Imprisonment which may extend to two years and fine which may extend to five thousand rupees.
Imprisonment which may extend to six months and fine which may extend to one thousand rupees.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Collector, Police Officers, Magistrates, Special Magistrates.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By virtue of powers of entry, search, arrest, and seizure as outlined in the Act.

rights: Right to obtain a license for the sale, purchase, or possession of liquor under prescribed conditions.
Right to be given an opportunity to show cause before a license or permit is cancelled or suspended.
duties: Duty to comply with the provisions of the Act and rules made thereunder.
Duty to produce a medical certificate if found in a state of intoxication.
obligations: Obligation to not render denatured spirits fit for human consumption.
Obligation to not possess liquor above the prescribed limit without a license.

key_procedures: Procedure for obtaining licenses for liquor sale, purchase, or possession.
Procedure for arresting individuals found in a state of intoxication and obtaining medical certificates.
Procedure for the cancellation or suspension of licenses and permits, including providing an opportunity for the holder to show cause.
Procedure for search, seizure, and inspection by authorized officers.
Procedure for the Government to notify and appoint officers and to grant exemptions.
administration: The Act is administered by the State Government, with powers delegated to Collectors, Magistrates, and other authorized officers.
important_notes: The expression "State" as adopted by the Kerala Adaptation of Laws Order, 1956, shall, in section 1 of the principal Act and wherever it occurs in that Act, have effect as if the words "State of Kerala" were substituted therefor.

Nothing contained in this sub-section shall apply to (i) any act done under, and in accordance with, the provisions of this Act or the terms of any rule, notification, order, licence or permit issued thereunder, or (ii) to the possession, sale, purchase, use or consumption of duty-paid medicinal or toilet preparations for bona fide medicinal or toilet purposes.

For the purposes of this sub-section "foreign tourist" means any person who not a citizen of India and who stays in India for more than twenty-four hours and less than six months for any non-immigrant purpose.

title: THE TRIVANDRUM CITY MUNICIPAL (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1964
purpose: To provide for the extension of the term of office of the Mayor and other Councillors and Chairman of Standing Committees of the Corporation of Trivandrum.
scope: Applies to the Corporation of Trivandrum.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Trivandrum City Municipal (Amendment) Act, 1964.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of the term of office of the Mayor, Councillors, etc., of the Corporation of Trivandrum.
main_sections.description: Provides for the extension of the term of office of the Mayor and other Councillors and Chairman of Standing Committees of the Corporation of Trivandrum. Notwithstanding anything contained in the Trivandrum City Municipal Act (Travancore Act IV of 1911), hereinafter referred to as the principal Act, the term of office of the Mayor and other councillors and the chairmen of standing committees of the Corporation of Trivandrum constituted under the principal Act, shall extend upto noon on the 1st day of July, 1964.

main_sections.section_title: Trivandrum City Municipal Act to be modified temporarily.
main_sections.description: The provisions of the principal Act shall have effect subject to the following modifications, namely:

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of section 5, Act IV of 1116.
main_sections.description: In section 5 of the principal Act, for the proviso to clause (a) of sub-section (1), the following proviso shall be substituted, namely: "Provided that such number shall not be less than forty or more than fifty ".

main_sections.section_title: Division of the city of Trivandrum into new territorial divisions.
main_sections.description: As soon as may be after the commencement of this Act, the city of Trivandrum shall be divided into new territorial divisions for the purposes of the election of councillors. The division shall be made in accordance with the provisions of the principal Act and such division shall take effect from the date of the ordinary elections held next after the commencement of this Act.

(1) The Trivandrum City Municipal (Amendment) Ordinance, 1963 (Ordinance No. 2 of 1963), is hereby repealed.
(2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act, as if this Act had commenced on the 30th day of December, 1963.

main_sections.description: Provides for the extension of the term of existing councillors.

important_rules: The council shall consist of such number of councillors as may be notified by the Government, not less than twenty-four or more than forty.
The councillors shall be elected by the municipal electors.

Seats shall be reserved for Scheduled Castes in the council, the number of which shall be determined by the Government based on the total number of seats in the council and the population of Scheduled Castes in the city.
No person shall be qualified for election as a councillor if they are of unsound mind, a deaf-mute, or a leper.

No person shall be disqualified for election as a councillor if they have been convicted by a Criminal Court for an offence and sentenced to transportation or imprisonment for not less than two years, unless five years have elapsed since their release.
No person shall be disqualified for election as a councillor if they are an undischarged insolvent.
No person shall be disqualified for election as a councillor if they are a contractor with the Corporation or involved in certain business dealings with it.
The electoral roll for the city shall be divided into separate lists for each division.
The election of councillors shall be by ballot.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government, Municipal Commissioner, and the Corporation.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through election processes, disqualifications, and potential imprisonment as per criminal court convictions.

rights: Right to vote in elections for councillors.
Right of Scheduled Castes to have reserved seats in the council.
duties: Duty of the Government to notify the number of councillors and fix boundaries of electoral divisions.
Duty of the Corporation to contribute to leave allowances, provident fund, and gratuity of the Commissioner.
obligations: Obligation for councillors to be elected by municipal electors.
Obligation for the election of councillors to be conducted by secret ballot.

key_procedures: Electoral divisions will be created, and the Government will fix their boundaries.
Seats will be reserved for Scheduled Castes, with their proportion determined by the Government.
Elections will be held by secret ballot.
The Commissioner's tenure and removal from office are subject to specific provisions.
The process for appointing and removing the Commissioner is detailed.
administration: The Trivandrum City Municipal Corporation, overseen by the Government.
important_notes: The provisions of this Act relating to reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes shall have effect up to the expiration of a period of nine years from the date on which the councillors elected at the first ordinary elections after the commencement of this Act take office.
Nothing contained in clause (2) shall be deemed to prevent members of Scheduled Castes from acceding to non-reserved seats in the council.

For the purposes of this Act, "Scheduled Castes" shall mean the castes which the Government may by notification declare to be Scheduled Castes, and "population" shall mean the population as ascertained at the last preceding census, of which the relevant figures have been published.

Explanation I: In the case of any Assembly Constituency, there is no distinct part of the electoral roll relating to the city, all persons whose names are entered in such roll under the representation of the city and whose addresses are entered in such roll are situate in the city shall be entitled to have their names entered in the electoral roll for the city prepared for the purposes of this Act.
Explanation II: No person's name shall be included in the electoral roll for more than one division or in the electoral roll for any division in more than one place.

title: The Trivandrum Municipal Corporation (Dissolution) Act, 1976
purpose: To provide for the dissolution of the Corporation of the City of Trivandrum.
scope: Applies to the Corporation of the City of Trivandrum.

key_definitions.corporation: Means the Corporation of the City of Trivandrum
key_definitions.council: Means the Corporation of the City of Trivandrum
key_definitions.mayor: Means the Mayor of the Corporation
key_definitions.deputy_mayor: Means the Deputy Mayor of the Corporation

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called The Trivandrum Municipal Corporation (Dissolution) Act, 1976, and it shall come into force on the 8th day of December, 1975.
Defines "Corporation", "council", "Mayor", and "Deputy Mayor".
Declares that the council shall be deemed to have stood dissolved on and from the 8th day of December, 1975.
States that on the dissolution of the council, all councillors, the Mayor, and the Deputy Mayor shall be deemed to have vacated their offices.

main_sections.section_title: Functions of council, etc., to be exercised by person or persons appointed by Government
main_sections.description: Empowers the Government to appoint a person or persons to exercise the functions of the council, Mayor, and Deputy Mayor during the interval between dissolution and reconstitution. Such appointed persons may receive payment from the Corporation fund. The Government can also determine the relationship of the appointed person(s) with the Government.

States that the council shall be reconstituted in accordance with the provisions of the Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, 1961, on the 1st day of November, 1976. The term of office of the reconstituted council's councillors shall expire at noon on the 1st day of November, 1981.

The Government, until the date of reconstitution of the council, shall be entitled to all assets and be subject to all liabilities of the council as on the date of dissolution. This also applies to assets and liabilities until the date of reconstitution.
Repeals the Trivandrum Municipal Corporation (Dissolution) Ordinance, 1975. Nothing done or any action taken under the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

important_rules: The council of the Corporation of the City of Trivandrum stood dissolved from December 8, 1975.
The Mayor and Deputy Mayor also vacated their offices upon dissolution.
The Government has the power to appoint individuals to perform the functions of the dissolved council and its office bearers.
The reconstituted council's term will end on November 1, 1981.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the appointment of persons to exercise functions, and by managing assets and liabilities.

rights: The Government has the right to appoint persons to exercise the functions of the council, Mayor, and Deputy Mayor.
The Government has the right to determine the relationship of appointed persons with the Government.
The Government is entitled to all assets of the council.
The Government is subject to all liabilities of the council.
obligations: The Government has the obligation to reconstitute the council.
The appointed persons may receive payment from the Corporation fund for their services.

key_procedures: The Government appoints persons to exercise council functions after dissolution.
The Government manages assets and liabilities until council reconstitution.
The council is reconstituted according to the Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, 1961.
The Ordinance of 1975 is repealed, and actions taken under it are not considered to be under this Act.
administration: The Government of Kerala is responsible for the administration of this Act, particularly concerning appointments and reconstitution of the council.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on March 22, 1976.
The Act was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No 175, dated March 22, 1976.
The dissolution was effective from December 8, 1975.
The reconstitution of the council was planned for November 1, 1976, with the term ending November 1, 1981.

title: The Trivandrum Municipal Corporation (Dissolution) (Amendment) Act, 1978
purpose: To further amend the Trivandrum Municipal Corporation (Dissolution) Act, 1976.
scope: Applies to the Trivandrum Municipal Corporation.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Trivandrum Municipal Corporation (Dissolution) Amendment Act, 1978, and that it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 31st day of January, 1978.
Amends section 6 of the Trivandrum Municipal Corporation (Dissolution) Act, 1976, by substituting certain figures, letters, and words related to dates.

Repeals the Trivandrum Municipal Corporation (Dissolution) Ordinance, 1978, and states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 18th day of March, 1978 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 188 dated 18th March, 1978.

title: The Trivandrum Municipal Corporation (Dissolution) Amendment Act, 1976
purpose: To amend The Trivandrum Municipal Corporation (Dissolution) Act, 1976 for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to The Trivandrum Municipal Corporation and actions taken under the principal Act.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called The Trivandrum Municipal Corporation (Dissolution) Amendment Act, 1976 and it shall come into force on the 1st day of November, 1976.
Amends section 6 of The Trivandrum Municipal Corporation (Dissolution) Act, 1976 by substituting figures, letters and words related to dates.

Repeals The Trivandrum Municipal Corporation (Dissolution) Amendment Ordinance, 1976 (11 of 1976) and states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 15th day of January, 1977 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 32 dated 18th January, 1977.

title: THE TRIVANDRUM MUNICIPAL CORPORATION (DISSOLUTION) SECOND AMENDMENT ACT, 1978
purpose: To further amend the Trivandrum Municipal Corporation (Dissolution) Act, 1976, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Trivandrum Municipal Corporation.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Trivandrum Municipal Corporation (Dissolution) Second Amendment Act, 1978, and that it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 31st day of May, 1978.
Amends section 6 of the Trivandrum Municipal Corporation (Dissolution) Act, 1976, by substituting the figures, letters and words '1st day of June, 1978' with '1st day of November, 1978'.
Repeals the Trivandrum Municipal Corporation (Dissolution) Second Amendment Ordinance, 1978, but saves any action taken or to be taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance.

important_rules: The Act is deemed to have come into force on May 31, 1978.
Specific date substitutions related to June 1, 1978, are replaced with November 1, 1978.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not specified.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Not specified.

administration: Not specified.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 4th day of August, 1978 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 515 dated 5th August, 1978.

title: THE UNIVERSITY LAWS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1990
purpose: To further amend the Kerala University Act, 1974 and the Calicut University Act, 1975.
scope: Applies to the Kerala University Act, 1974 and the Calicut University Act, 1975.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the University Laws (Amendment) Act, 1990. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 26th day of April, 1990.

Amends section 21, in item (a) under the heading "Other Members", of the Kerala University Act, 1974. It substitutes "Twelve members" with "Thirteen members" and "six members" with "seven members" where the words referred to persons who are not teachers, or persons belonging to a Scheduled Caste or a Scheduled Tribe.

Amends section 21, in item (a) under the heading "Other Members", of the Calicut University Act, 1975. It substitutes "Twelve members" with "Thirteen members" and "six members" with "seven members" where the words referred to persons who are not teachers, or persons belonging to a Scheduled Caste or a Scheduled Tribe.

Sections 3 and 4 of the University Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1990 (2 of 1990) are hereby repealed. Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the Kerala University Act, 1974 (17 of 1974) or the Calicut University Act, 1975 (5 of 1975) as amended by the said sections shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the Kerala University Act, 1974 or the Calicut University Act, 1975, as the case may be, as amended by this Act.

important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 22nd day of June, 1990 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 627 dated the 23rd June, 1990.

title: The University Laws (Amendment) (No. 2) Act, 2019
purpose: To further amend the Cochin University of Science and Technology Act, 1986, the Thunchath Ezhuthachan Malayala University Act, 2013, and the A. P. J. Abdul Kalam Technological University Act, 2015. The amendments primarily concern the appointment and tenure of Registrars, Controllers of Examinations, and Finance Officers in these universities.
scope: This Act applies to the Cochin University of Science and Technology, Thunchath Ezhuthachan Malayala University, and A. P. J. Abdul Kalam Technological University, all established in Kerala. It amends existing university acts, thus affecting their administrative and academic functions.

key_definitions.Registrar: An officer of the University appointed by the Syndicate, selected by the Government from a panel furnished by the Syndicate. The tenure is typically four years or until the age of fifty-six years, whichever is earlier, with eligibility for re-appointment.
key_definitions.Controller of Examinations: An officer of the University appointed by the Syndicate, selected by the Government from a panel. The tenure is typically four years or until the age of fifty-six years, whichever is earlier, with eligibility for re-appointment.
key_definitions.Finance Officer: An officer of the University who is a full-time employee. The appointment and tenure are subject to conditions prescribed by Statutes, typically for four years or until the age of fifty-six years, whichever is earlier, with eligibility for re-appointment.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the University Laws (Amendment) (No. 2) Act, 2019, and it is deemed to have come into force on March 6, 2019.

Introduces amendments to the Cochin University of Science and Technology Act, 1986. It inserts the 'Controller of Examinations' as a position, modifies the appointment and tenure of the Registrar, and inserts a new section for the Controller of Examinations, and modifies the appointment of the Finance Officer.
Introduces amendments to the Thunchath Ezhuthachan Malayala University Act, 2013. It modifies the appointment and tenure of the Registrar, the Controller of Examinations, and the Finance Officer.
Introduces amendments to the A. P. J. Abdul Kalam Technological University Act, 2015. It modifies the appointment and tenure of the Registrar, the Finance Officer, and the Controller of Examinations.

main_sections.section_title: Special provision relating to existing Registrars, Controllers of Examinations and Finance Officers
main_sections.description: Deals with the tenure of existing officers. If an officer has completed four years of service or reached the age of fifty-six, their tenure is considered to have ended upon the commencement of this Act. Those who have not completed either will continue until they do. It also addresses the service conditions of officers appointed from other departments.

Repeals the University Laws (Amendment) (No. 2) Ordinance, 2019 (35 of 2019). It also provides that anything done or purported to have been done under the repealed Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done under the amended Acts.

important_rules: The appointment of Registrar, Controller of Examinations, and Finance Officer in the specified universities is subject to selection by the Government from a panel provided by the Syndicate (for Registrar and Controller of Examinations).
The tenure for these positions is a maximum of four years from the date of joining or until the officer completes the age of fifty-six years, whichever comes first.
Officers are eligible for re-appointment for one additional period, subject to the provisions of their respective appointment clauses.
The existing officers who have completed their tenure (four years or fifty-six years of age) upon the commencement of the Act are deemed to have vacated their posts.
Existing officers who have not completed their tenure will continue until they reach the completion of four years or fifty-six years of age.

rights: The right of the Syndicate to furnish panels for the selection of Registrar and Controller of Examinations.
The right of the Government to select from the furnished panels for appointment of Registrar and Controller of Examinations.
The eligibility of appointed officers for re-appointment for one additional term.
The right of existing officers not yet completing their tenure to continue in service.
duties: The duty of the Syndicate to appoint officers as prescribed by the Act and Statutes.
The duty of the Government to select from the panel for appointments.
The duty of the appointed officers to serve on prescribed terms and conditions.
The duty to vacate office if tenure is completed as per the Act.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the tenure limits and age restrictions for appointments.
Obligation to follow the procedures for selection and appointment of key university officers.
Obligation for existing officers to vacate office if their tenure is completed upon commencement of the Act.

key_procedures: For Registrar and Controller of Examinations: Syndicate provides a panel of two names to the Government. Government selects one person from this panel for appointment. The appointed person serves for a period of four years or until the age of fifty-six, whichever is earlier. They are eligible for re-appointment for one additional period.

For Finance Officer: Appointment is made by the Syndicate under terms and conditions prescribed by Statutes. The tenure is four years or until the age of fifty-six, whichever is earlier, with eligibility for re-appointment for one additional period.
For existing officers: If they have completed four years or reached fifty-six years of age, their tenure is deemed to have ended. If not, they continue until such completion.
administration: The administration of the act, particularly concerning amendments to the university acts, would fall under the purview of the Law Department and the Higher Education Department of the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act is retrospective, deemed to have come into force on March 6, 2019.
The appointment of Registrars, Controllers of Examinations, and Finance Officers is a key focus, aiming to standardize tenure and selection processes across these universities.
The Act clarifies the status of existing officers, ensuring a smooth transition and preventing disruption in university administration.

title: The University Laws (Amendment) Act, 1977
purpose: To further amend the Cochin University Act, 1971, the Kerala University Act, 1974, and the Calicut University Act, 1975.
scope: Applies to the Cochin University Act, 1971, the Kerala University Act, 1971, the Kerala University Act, 1974, and the Calicut University Act, 1975.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the University Laws (Amendment) Act, 1977. The provisions of this Act (except section 5 which shall come into force at once) shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of February, 1976.

In section 16 of the Cochin University Act, 1971 (30 of 1971), after subsection (3), the following subsection shall be inserted, namely:— "(3A) Notwithstanding anything contained in the first proviso to subsection (2), a principal elected under item (1), or a member of the teaching staff of a constituent college or a recognised institution elected under item (6), or a member of the non-teaching staff of a constituent college elected under item (12), under the heading "ELECTED MEMBERS" in section 15 shall not cease to be a member of the Senate merely on the ground— (a) that he has been transferred to an educational institution within the State, situated beyond the territorial limits of the University; or (b) that the college of which he is the principal or in which he is a teacher or a member of the non-teaching staff has been transferred to another University; or (c) in the case of a teacher, that he has been promoted as principal."

In the Kerala University Act, 1974 (17 of 1974),— (a) in section 18, after sub-section (3), the following sub-section shall be inserted, namely:— "(3A) Notwithstanding anything contained in the first proviso to sub-section (3), a principal elected under item (1), or a teacher of a Government college elected under item (5), or a teacher of a private college elected under item (6), or a member of the non-teaching staff of an affiliated college elected under item (10), under the heading "ELECTED MEMBERS" in section 17 shall not cease to be a member of the Senate merely on the ground that— (a) he has been transferred to an educational institution within the State, situated beyond the territorial limits of the University; or (b) the college of which he is the principal or in which he is a teacher or a member of the non-teaching staff has been transferred to another University; or (c) in the case of a teacher, he has been promoted as principal."; (b) section 22 shall be renumbered as sub-section (1) of that section and, after sub-section (1) as so renumbered, the following sub-section shall be inserted, namely:— "(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in the first proviso to sub-section (1), a member of the Syndicate referred to in sub-item (ii) of item (a) under the heading "Other Members" in section 21, or referred to in sub-item (iii) of that item who is a teacher of a private college or a Government college, shall not cease to be such member merely on the ground that— (a) he has been transferred to an educational institution within the State, situated beyond the territorial limits of the University; or (b) the college of which he is the principal or in which he is a teacher or a member of the non-teaching staff has been transferred to another University; or (c) in the case of a teacher, he has been promoted as principal."

In the Calicut University Act, 1975 (5 of 1975),— (a) in section 18, after sub-section (3), the following sub-section shall be inserted, namely:— "(3A) Notwithstanding anything contained in the first proviso to sub-section (3), a principal elected under item (1), or a teacher of a Government college elected under item (3), or a teacher of a private college elected under item (6), or a member of the non-teaching staff of an affiliated college elected under item (10), under the heading "ELECTED MEMBERS" in section 17 shall not cease to be a member of the Senate merely on the ground that— (a) he has been transferred to an educational institution within the State, situated beyond the territorial limits of the University; or (b) the college of which he is the principal or in which he is a teacher or a member of the non-teaching staff has been transferred to another University; or (c) in the case of a teacher, he has been promoted as principal."; (b) section 22 shall be renumbered as sub-section (1) of that section and, after sub-section (1) as so renumbered, the following sub-section shall be inserted, namely:— "(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in the first proviso to sub-section (1), a member of the Syndicate of the University of Cochin who has ceased to be such member before the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette on the ground that he has ceased to be a member of the Senate on any of the grounds specified in clause (a), shall be restored to the membership of such Syndicate; and (c) a member of the Syndicate of the University of Kerala or the University of Calicut who has ceased to be such member before the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette, referred to in sub-item (ii) of item (a) under the heading "Other Members" in section 21, or in sub-item (iii) of that item (being a teacher of a private college or a Government college) who has ceased to be such member on any of the grounds specified in clause (a), shall be restored to such membership."

Notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force,— (a) a member of the Senate of the University of Cochin or the University of Kerala or Calicut who has been elected under item (1) or item (6) or item (12) under the heading "Elected Members" in section 17 of the Cochin University Act, 1971, or item (1) or item (5) or item (6) or item (10) under the heading "Elected Members" in section 17 of the Kerala University Act, 1974, or under item (1) or item (5) or item (6) or item (10) under the heading "Elected Members" in section 17 of the Calicut University Act, 1975, as the case may be, and who has ceased to be such member before the date of publication of this Act, in the Gazette, merely on the ground— (i) that he has been transferred to an educational institution within the State, situated beyond the territorial limits of the University; or (ii) that the educational institution of which he is the principal or a member of the non-teaching staff has been transferred to another University; or (iii) in the case of a teacher other than a principal, that he has been promoted as principal; shall be restored to such membership; (b) a member of the Syndicate of the University of Cochin who has ceased to be such member before the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette on the ground that he has ceased to be a member of the Senate on any of the grounds specified in clause (a), shall be restored to the membership of such Syndicate; and (c) a member of the Syndicate of the University of Kerala or the University of Calicut who has ceased to be such member before the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette, referred to in sub-item (ii) of item (a) under the heading "Other Members" in section 21, or in sub-item (iii) of that item (being a teacher of a private college or a Government college) who has ceased to be such member on any of the grounds specified in clause (a), shall be restored to such membership.

rights: Restoration of membership for certain individuals whose membership in the Senate or Syndicate was affected by transfer of institutions or promotion.

important_notes: The commencement date for most provisions of the Act is February 1, 1976, with the exception of section 5.
Specific amendments are made to the Cochin University Act, 1971, the Kerala University Act, 1974, and the Calicut University Act, 1975.

The amendments address situations where individuals, such as principals, teachers, or non-teaching staff, might have lost their Senate or Syndicate membership due to institutional transfers or promotions.

title: THE UNIVERSITY LAWS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1985 (Act 29 of 1985)
purpose: To further amend the Kerala University Act, 1974 and the Calicut University Act, 1975.
scope: Applies to the Kerala University Act, 1974 and the Calicut University Act, 1975.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the University Laws (Amendment) Act, 1985 and it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 18th day of November, 1982.

Amends Section 56 of the Kerala University Act, 1974. It modifies the clauses related to affiliation of colleges and the procedure for affiliation by the Syndicate, with provisions for extension of the period for specified circumstances.

Amends Section 56 of the Calicut University Act, 1975. Similar to the amendment in Section 2, it modifies clauses related to affiliation of colleges and the Syndicate's procedure, including provisions for notification and period extensions.

Repeals The University Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1985 (60 of 1985). It also states that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the Kerala University Act, 1974 (17 of 1974), or the Calicut University Act, 1975 (5 of 1975), as amended by the said Ordinance, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the Kerala University Act, 1974, or as the case may be, the Calicut University Act, 1975, as amended by this Act.

key_procedures: Affiliation of colleges and the procedure for affiliation by the Syndicate, including requirements for application, consideration by the Syndicate, and potential notification by the Chancellor for extending periods.
Notification in the Gazette by the Chancellor for extending the period for considering applications for affiliation under specific circumstances.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 14th day of October, 1985 and was published in the Kerala Gazette, Extraordinary No. 837 dated the 15th October, 1985.
The commencement of the Act is deemed to be the 18th day of November, 1982.

title: The University Laws (Amendment) Act, 2019
purpose: This Act amends several existing University Laws in Kerala to make changes and modifications, likely to streamline or update provisions related to university administration and functioning.
scope:
The act applies to various university laws in Kerala. It specifically amends the following acts:
- The Kerala University Act, 1974
- The Calicut University Act, 1975
- The Mahatma Gandhi University Act, 1985
- The Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit Act, 1994
- The University of Calicut Act, 1996
- The Central University Act, 2005
- The Kannur University Act, 1996

main_sections.description: Specifies that the Act is called the University Laws (Amendment) Act, 2019 and that it came into force on 6th November 2019.
Amends Section 12, 13, and 14 of The Kerala University Act, 1974, by replacing existing subsections to define the tenure of Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, and Registrar.
Amends Section 12, 13, and 14 of The Calicut University Act, 1975, by replacing existing subsections to define the tenure of Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, and Registrar.
Amends Section 12, 13, and 14 of The Mahatma Gandhi University Act, 1985, by replacing existing subsections to define the tenure of Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, and Registrar.

Amends Section 23 and 28 of The Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit Act, 1994, by inserting new clauses and replacing existing subsections to include Pro-Vice-Chancellor and Registrar and define their tenures.
Amends Section 14, 15, and 16 of The Kannur University Act, 1996, by replacing existing subsections to define the tenure of Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, and Registrar.
Amends Section 28, 29, and 30 of The Central University Act, 2005, by replacing existing subsections to define the tenure of Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, and Pro-Vice-Chancellor.

main_sections.section_title: Special provisions regarding Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor and Registrar
main_sections.description: This section clarifies that the tenures of Vice-Chancellor, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, and Registrar appointed under the amended acts shall be considered as tenure under this Act, and their terms will be counted from the date of commencement of this Act.

important_rules: Tenure of Vice-Chancellor: The tenure of the Vice-Chancellor is defined as a period of five years from the date of appointment, or until they attain the age of sixty-five years, whichever is earlier.

Tenure of Pro-Vice-Chancellor: The tenure of the Pro-Vice-Chancellor is defined as a period of five years from the date of appointment, or until they attain the age of sixty-five years, whichever is earlier.
Tenure of Registrar: The tenure of the Registrar is defined as a period of five years from the date of appointment, or until they attain the age of sixty-five years, whichever is earlier.
Extended tenure: In certain circumstances, the tenure can be extended by another five years from the date of expiry of the initial term.

Clarification of tenure for existing appointments: Vice-Chancellors, Pro-Vice-Chancellors, and Registrars appointed before the commencement of this Act will have their tenure counted from the date of commencement of this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be the respective university authorities and potentially the State Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amendments to existing university laws and the enforcement of new tenure provisions.

key_procedures: Appointment of Vice-Chancellor: The Act implies that the appointment process for the Vice-Chancellor remains as per the respective university acts, with the tenure now defined.
Appointment of Pro-Vice-Chancellor: Similar to the Vice-Chancellor, the appointment procedure is governed by the respective university acts.
Appointment of Registrar: The appointment of the Registrar follows the procedures laid out in the individual university acts.
administration: The administration of this act would fall under the purview of the respective universities in Kerala and the Department of Higher Education, Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The primary purpose of this amendment is to standardize and define the tenure of key administrative positions in various universities across Kerala.
The commencement date of the Act is November 6, 2019.
The Act retroactively applies to existing appointments in some cases, defining their tenure from the commencement date of this Act.

title: The University Laws (Amendment) Act, 1978
purpose: To further amend the Kerala University Act, 1974 and the Calicut University Act, 1975.
scope: Applies to the Kerala University Act, 1974 and the Calicut University Act, 1975.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the University Laws (Amendment) Act, 1978, and it came into force on the 21st day of April, 1978.

Amends the Kerala University Act, 1974 (17 of 1974). It inserts new subsections (15A) and (15B) into section 10, and also inserts a new section '80A' into section 80 concerning the duty of teachers, etc., in connection with University examinations, and the consequences of non-compliance.

Amends the Calicut University Act, 1975 (5 of 1975). It inserts new subsections (15A) and (15B) into section 10, and also inserts a new section '79A' into section 79 concerning the duty of teachers, etc., in connection with University examinations, and the consequences of non-compliance.

Repeals the University Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1978 (12 of 1978). It also states that anything done or any action taken under the Kerala University Act, 1974, or the Calicut University Act, 1975, as amended by the said Ordinance, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the Kerala University Act, 1974, or the Calicut University Act, 1975, as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Rule: Teachers and other employees of the University (or affiliated colleges) must not do any work in connection with an examination conducted by the University without the permission of the competent officer or authority.
Rule: If any teacher or member of the non-teaching staff refuses without sufficient cause to satisfy the requirements of the Act, they shall be deemed to be in contravention of the Act.

Rule: Any person aggrieved by an order referred to in subsection (4) may, within sixty days from the date on which such order is served, appeal to the Appellate Tribunal, and the Appellate Tribunal may, after giving the parties an opportunity of being heard and after such further inquiry as may be necessary, pass such order thereon as it deems fit.

penalties: Forfeiture of pay and allowances for a period of two months commencing on the date of commencement of the examination for contravening the provisions regarding examination work.

Forfeiture of pay and allowances for a period of two months commencing on the date of commencement of the examination for contravening the provisions regarding examination work (Calicut University Act).
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Vice-Chancellor (for appointment of examiners and related matters), Competent officer or authority of the University (for general enforcement).

obligations: Obligation to obtain permission before engaging in work related to University examinations.

Procedure for appealing decisions of the Vice-Chancellor or competent authorities to the Appellate Tribunal.
administration: University administration, likely involving the Vice-Chancellor and competent authorities.

title: The University Laws (Amendment) Act, 1989
purpose: To further amend the Kerala University Act, 1974, the Calicut University Act, 1975 and the Mahatma Gandhi University Act, 1985, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Kerala University Act, 1974, the Calicut University Act, 1975 and the Mahatma Gandhi University Act, 1985.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the University Laws (Amendment) Act, 1989. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 6th day of May 1989.

Amends section 57 of the Kerala University Act, 1974. It addresses the appointment of teachers in private colleges and the management of educational agencies within the University area. It also provides for disputes arising between management of private colleges and teachers.
Amends section 57 of the Calicut University Act, 1975, with similar provisions to Section 2 regarding appointment of teachers in private colleges and management of educational agencies.

Amends section 27 and section 58 of the Mahatma Gandhi University Act, 1985. It includes provisions for the formation of faculties and further amends section 58 to address appointment of teachers in private colleges and management of educational agencies.

Repeals the University Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1989 (1 of 1989). It also states that any action taken under the repealed Ordinances is deemed to have been done or taken under the corresponding provisions of this Act.

important_rules: Notwithstanding anything contained in the Act, the Statutes, Ordinances and Regulations made thereunder, a person appointed as teacher in a private college on or after the 14th day of March, 1974 and continuing as such, shall be appointed as teacher in any permanent vacancy or any temporary vacancy of longer duration that may arise, after such appointment in the temporary vacancy, in the private college or, as the case may be, any of the private colleges under the management of the educational agency within the University area.

A teacher relieved from a private college on or after the 14th day of March, 1974 due to the abolition of a course of study in that private college or the cessation of the period for which he was appointed or for any other reason except disciplinary action against him, shall be given preference in the matter of future appointments in the private college or, as the case may be, any of the private colleges under the management of the educational agency within the University area.

Any dispute arising or pending between the management of a private college and the teacher of that college, in respect of any matter coming under clause (a) or (b), shall be decided in accordance with the provisions of this Act and the Statutes made thereunder.

rights: Teachers relieved from private colleges shall be given preference in future appointments in the same or other private colleges under the same management.
Teachers have the right to have disputes with management decided according to the Act and Statutes.
obligations: University Acts, Statutes, Ordinances, and Regulations are subject to the amendments made by this Act.

key_procedures: Decisions on disputes between private college management and teachers are to be made in accordance with the Act and Statutes.
administration: The respective University administrations governed by the Acts being amended.
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 29th day of June 1989 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 608 dt. the 29th June 1989.

The provisions regarding appointment of teachers in private colleges and management of educational agencies apply regardless of clauses concerning the number of claimants or the preference for appointment.

title: The University Laws (Amendment) Amending Act, 2005 (Mal) (Act 29 of 2005)
purpose: This act amends the University Laws (Amendment) Act, 2005, to address specific provisions related to the functioning and administration of universities in Kerala. It appears to be an amendment to an existing amendment act.
scope: Applies to universities in Kerala.

main_sections.description: This section amends the Principal Act (Act 29 of 2005). It specifically states that for the words '2005-ലെ സർവ്വകലാശാല നിയമ (ഭേദഗതി) നിയമം' (University Laws (Amendment) Act, 2005) in the Principal Act, the words '2005-ലെ സർവ്വകലാശാല നിയമ (ഭേദഗതി) ഭേദഗതി നിയമം' (University Laws (Amendment) Amending Act, 2005) shall be substituted. It also amends sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Principal Act with respect to the definition of 'Act' and the year of enactment. It further amends section 18 of the Principal Act concerning the commencement of the Act.

This section deals with the validation of certain actions taken under the Principal Act. It clarifies that the appointment of the Vice-Chancellor and Pro-Vice-Chancellor of universities, as made in accordance with the provisions of the Principal Act, and any actions taken by them, are deemed to have been done in accordance with the law, despite any defects or irregularities. This section specifically refers to the appointment made in 2005-06 and the relevant sections of the Principal Act (sections 2 and 4 of Act 29 of 2005, and sections 1(1)-30 of the Kerala University Act, 1974, etc.). It aims to prevent legal challenges to appointments and subsequent actions.

This section addresses the repeal of the Ordinance (Ordinance No. 11 of 2005) and makes provisions for savings. It states that the repeal of the Ordinance shall not affect any action taken or things done under the Ordinance. Specifically, it clarifies that anything done or omitted to be done under the Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or omitted under the corresponding provisions of the Principal Act. This is a standard provision to ensure continuity and prevent disruption when an ordinance is replaced by an act.

key_procedures: Substitution of specific phrases in the Principal Act to reflect the amending nature of the current act.
Validation of appointments made under the Principal Act, ensuring continuity and legal standing of actions taken by appointed officials.
Repeal of a related Ordinance and ensuring that actions taken under the Ordinance are recognized and continue to be valid under the new Act.
important_notes: The act is an amendment to an existing amendment act (Act 29 of 2005).
Section 2 specifically aims to validate appointments of Vice-Chancellors and Pro-Vice-Chancellors, suggesting there might have been procedural issues or challenges to these appointments.
Section 3 ensures that the transition from an Ordinance to an Act is smooth and legal actions taken under the Ordinance are preserved.

In section 18 of the Calicut University Act, 1975 (5 of 1975), after sub-section (3A), the following sub-section shall be inserted, namely:-- "(3B) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or in the Statutes no person elected under item (2) under the heading "Elected Members" in section 17 shall cease to be a member of the Senate merely on the ground that he has ceased to be employed or normally resident within the territorial limits of the University."

title: The University Laws (Second Amendment) Act, 2014
purpose: To further amend the Kerala University Act, 1974, the Calicut University Act, 1975, the Mahatma Gandhi University Act, 1985, the Sree Sankaraacharya University of Sanskrit Act, 1994 and the National University of Advanced Legal Studies Act, 2005.
scope: Applies to the Kerala University Act, 1974, Calicut University Act, 1975, Mahatma Gandhi University Act, 1985, Sree Sankaraacharya University of Sanskrit Act, 1994, and National University of Advanced Legal Studies Act, 2005.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the University Laws (Second Amendment) Act, 2014. Clause (a) of section 4 shall be deemed to have come into force on the 9th day of September, 2013. Section 2, clause (b) of section 4 and sections 5 to 7 shall be deemed to have come into force on the 17th day of September, 2013 and the remaining sections shall come into force at once.

In the Kerala University Act, 1974 (17 of 1974), in section 6, for sub-section (2), the following sub-section shall be substituted, namely: "(2) In making appointments to the teaching and non-teaching posts, the University shall, mutatis mutandis, observe the provisions of clauses (a), (b) and (c) of rule 14 and the provisions of rules 15, 16, 17 and 17A of the Kerala State and Subordinate Services Rules, 1958, as amended from time to time, and communal rotation shall be followed category-wise treating all the departments as one unit."

In the Calicut University Act, 1975 (5 of 1975), in section 6, for sub-section (2), the following sub-section shall be substituted, namely: "(2) In making appointments to the teaching and non-teaching posts, the University shall, mutatis mutandis, observe the provisions of clauses (a), (b) and (c) of rule 14 and the provisions of rules 15, 16, 17 and 17A of the Kerala State and Subordinate Services Rules, 1958, as amended from time to time, and communal rotation shall be followed category-wise treating all the departments as one unit."

In the National University of Advanced Legal Studies Act, 2005 (27 of 2005), in section 4, for sub-section (3), the following sub-section shall be substituted, namely: "(3) In making appointments to the teaching and non-teaching posts, the University shall, mutatis mutandis, observe the provisions of clauses (a), (b) and (c) of rule 14 and the provisions of rules 15, 16, 17 and 17A of the Kerala State and Subordinate Services Rules, 1958, as amended from time to time, and communal rotation shall be followed category-wise treating all the departments as one unit."

In the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit Act 1994 (5 of 1994), section 32, the following sub-section shall be substituted, namely: "32. Reservation of appointments. In making appointments to the teaching and non-teaching posts, the University shall, mutatis mutandis, observe the provisions of clauses (a), (b) and (c) of rule 14 and the provisions of rules 15, 16, 17 and 17A of the State and Subordinate Services Rules, 1958, as amended from time to time, and communal rotation shall be followed category-wise treating all the departments as one unit."

In the National University of Advanced Legal Studies Act, 2005 (27 of 2005), in section 4, for sub-section (3), the following sub-section shall be substituted, namely: "(3) In making appointments to the teaching and non-teaching posts, the University shall, mutatis mutandis, observe the provisions of clauses (a), (b) and (c) of rule 14 and the provisions of rules 15, 16, 17 and 17A of the Kerala State and Subordinate Services Rules, 1958, as amended from time to time, and communal rotation shall be followed category-wise treating all the departments as one unit."

Notwithstanding anything contained in the Calicut University Act, 1975, on the date of commencement of the Calicut University (Amendment) Ordinance, 2013 (48 of 2013), the existing members in office nominated under item (5) under the heading "Other Members" in section 6 of the Calicut University Act, 1975, shall be deemed to have vacated their office by virtue of the provision of the said Ordinance.

(1) The University Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 2014 (2 of 2014) is hereby repealed. (2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken or deemed to have been taken under the Mahatma Gandhi University Act, 1985 or the Calicut University Act, 1975 and anything done or taken under the Kerala University Act, 1974 and the National University of Advanced Legal Studies Act, 2005 as amended by the said ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the said Acts respectively as amended by this Act.

This must be done mutatis mutandis and category-wise.
Existing members nominated under item (5) in section 6 of the Calicut University Act, 1975, in the Calicut University (Amendment) Ordinance, 2013, are deemed to have vacated their office.
Repeal of the University Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 2014 (2 of 2014) with saving provisions for actions taken under previous acts and ordinances.
administration: Law (Legislation-G) Department, Government of Kerala

The Act aims to harmonize appointment procedures across various universities in Kerala.
Specific dates are mentioned for the commencement of different sections of the Act.
The Act repeals the University Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 2014.

title: THE UNIVERSITY LAWS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1979
purpose: To further amend the Cochin University Act, 1971, the Kerala University Act, 1974 and the Calicut University Act, 1975.
scope: Applies to the Cochin University Act, 1971, the Kerala University Act, 1974, and the Calicut University Act, 1975.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the University Laws (Amendment) Act, 1979. It shall come into force at once.

Amends section 10, sub-section (6) of the Cochin University Act, 1971, regarding remuneration payable to and other conditions of service of the Vice-Chancellor, which shall be determined by the Chancellor.

Also, amends items (8) and (9) under the heading "Exofficio Members" in section 17, to be substituted by the Secretary to Government or Additional Secretary to Government, General Education Department, nominated by the Government (for item (8)) and Secretary to Government or Additional Secretary to Government, Higher Education Department, nominated by the Government (for item (9)).

important_rules: The remuneration payable to, and the other conditions of service of, the Vice-Chancellor shall be determined by the Chancellor (amended in Acts of 1971, 1974, and 1975).

The Secretary to Government or the Additional Secretary to Government, General Education Department, to be nominated by the Government, shall be an 'Exofficio Member' (amended in Acts of 1974 and 1975).

The Secretary to Government or the Additional Secretary to Government, Higher Education Department, to be nominated by the Government, shall be an 'Exofficio Member' (amended in Acts of 1974 and 1975).
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 11th May, 1979 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 352, dated 19th May, 1979.

title: The University Laws (Amendment) Act, 1976
purpose: To further amend the Kerala University Act, 1974 and the Calicut University Act, 1975.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the University Laws (Amendment) Act, 1976.

In section 27 of the Calicut University Act, 1975 (5 of 1975),— (a) for sub-section (1), the following sub-section shall be substituted, namely:— "(1) There shall be a Dean of each faculty, who shall be nominated by the Chancellor in consultation with the Vice-Chancellor ", (b) in sub-section (3), for the word "re-election", the word "re-nomination" shall be substituted.

important_rules: Substitute 're-nomination' for 're-election' in relevant sub-sections of both the Kerala University Act and the Calicut University Act.
Deans of faculties shall be nominated by the Chancellor in consultation with the Vice-Chancellor.
Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are deemed to be taken under this Act if commenced on February 3, 1976.

title: The University Laws (Amendment) Act, 2014
