scope: Applies to the Kerala University Act, 1974, the Calicut University Act, 1975, the Mahatma Gandhi University Act, 1985, the Kannur University Act, 1976, and the Kannur University (Amendment) Act, 2001.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the University Laws (Amendment) Act, 2005. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 6th day of January, 2005.

Amends the Kerala University Act, 1974. It includes provisions for omitting certain clauses, inserting new items related to affiliated colleges, university departments, qualification of teachers, and substituting certain words and figures. It also allows for the omission of specific sections and re-numbering of sub-sections.

Amends the Calicut University Act, 1975. Similar to Section 2, it involves omitting clauses, inserting new items for affiliated colleges and university departments, fixing minimum infrastructural facilities, and fixing the qualification of teachers and non-teaching staff. It also allows for omitting specific items and re-numbering of sub-sections.

Amends the Mahatma Gandhi University Act, 1985. It includes provisions for omitting clauses, inserting new items for affiliated colleges and university departments, fixing minimum infrastructural facilities, and fixing the qualification of teachers and non-teaching staff. It also allows for omitting specific items and re-numbering of sub-sections.

Amends the Kannur University Act, 1996. Similar to other amendment sections, it includes provisions for omitting clauses, inserting new items for affiliated colleges and university departments, fixing minimum infrastructural facilities, and fixing the qualification of teachers and non-teaching staff. It also allows for omitting specific items and re-numbering of sub-sections.

Amends the Kannur University (Amendment) Act, 2001. It provides for the omission of sub-sections related to the Senate and Syndicate being dissolved and reconstituted. It also clarifies that the Senate shall exercise all powers and perform all functions of the Syndicate until the reconstitution of the Senate.

main_sections.section_title: Special provision for alternate arrangements temporarily of the Senate and Syndicates of the Kerala and Calicut Universities.
main_sections.description: This section provides for temporary arrangements for the Senate and Syndicates of the Kerala and Calicut Universities in case of dissolution or reconstitution. It allows for the Government to nominate an interim body to exercise powers and perform functions. It also lists the composition of this interim body, including ex-officio members and nominated members, with specific criteria for representation.

Repeals the University Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 2005 (2 of 2005). It states that notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Acts as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By notification in the Gazette.

key_procedures: Insertion of new items into existing Acts, specifying criteria for affiliated colleges, university departments, and qualifications of staff.
Re-numbering of sub-sections within existing Acts.
Omission of specific clauses and sections as per the amendments.
administration: The specific department or agency is not explicitly mentioned, but likely falls under the purview of the Department of Higher Education or Education Department of the Kerala Government.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on January 6, 2005.
The amendments apply to multiple University Acts in Kerala.
A special provision exists for temporary arrangements regarding the Senate and Syndicates of Kerala and Calicut Universities.
The repeal of the Ordinance does not invalidate actions taken under it.
Appointments to certain posts are to be made only against posts sanctioned by the Government and authorized by such officers as may be authorized by the Government.

title: The Unregistered Cashewnut Factories Prohibition (Amendment) Act, 2008
purpose: To amend The Unregistered Cashewnut Factories Prohibition Act, 1967.
scope: Applies to the Unregistered Cashewnut Factories Prohibition Act, 1967. It addresses the sale of seized cashewnuts and penalties for contravention of the Act.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called The Unregistered Cashewnut Factories Prohibition (Amendment) Act, 2008 and shall be deemed to have come into force on the 13th day of December, 2007.

Amends section 5 of the Unregistered Cashewnut Factories Prohibition Act, 1967 (11 of 1967) by inserting words and the machines, equipments and other instruments used or about to be used for such processing, in such premises.

Inserts a new section 5A titled 'Sale of cashewnuts seized'. This section details the process for the Revenue Divisional Officer to order the sale of seized cashewnuts under certain conditions and outlines procedures for inventory, seizure, and sale of cashewnuts.

For the purposes of the principal Act, the following section shall be substituted: "6 Penalties—If any person contravenes or attempts to contravene or abets the contravention of the provisions of section 4, or of any rule made under this Act, he shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years but which shall not be less than six months and with a fine which may extend to one lakh rupees but which shall not be less than twenty-five thousand rupees and in the case of repeated contravention with an additional fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees for every such contravention."
Amends section 8 of the principal Act by inserting words and the machines, equipments and other instruments used for such contravention.

Repeals The Unregistered Cashewnut Factories Prohibition (Amendment) Ordinance, 2008 (25 of 2008) and states that anything done or deemed to have been done or any action taken under the principal Act, as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act, as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Rule for sale of seized cashewnuts: The Revenue Divisional Officer may order the sale of seized cashewnuts if they are likely to deteriorate or are subject to speedy and natural decay.

Prohibition on sale of cashewnuts without order: No order for sale of cashewnuts shall be passed under section 5A unless the person from whom the same is seized is given an opportunity of being heard.
Penalties for contravention: Imprisonment up to two years (minimum six months) and fine up to one lakh rupees (minimum twenty-five thousand rupees). Repeat offenders face additional fines.
Saving clause for actions under Ordinance: Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are deemed valid under the amended Act.

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years but which shall not be less than six months
Fine which may extend to one lakh rupees but which shall not be less than twenty-five thousand rupees
In the case of repeated contravention, an additional fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees for every such contravention
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Revenue Divisional Officer, Magistrate, Inspector
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Seizure of cashewnuts, ordering sale of seized cashewnuts, prosecution for contravention, imposition of penalties.

rights: Right to be heard before sale of seized cashewnuts.
duties: Duty to comply with the provisions of The Unregistered Cashewnut Factories Prohibition Act, 1967.
Duty of Revenue Divisional Officer to prepare inventory of seized cashewnuts and ensure their safety.
obligations: Obligation to ensure proper processing of cashewnuts in registered factories.

key_procedures: Procedure for sale of seized cashewnuts: The Revenue Divisional Officer, upon receiving a report of seizure, may order the sale if he thinks it expedient to do so, directly to the raw cashewnuts so seized, to be produced before him for inspection. He may order the sale to be either to the Kerala State Cashew Development Corporation or to the Kerala State Cashew Workers' Apex Industrial Co-operative Society Ltd. at the prevailing market rate or in public auction.

Procedure for inventory and evidence: Where an application is made under sub-section (3), the Magistrate shall, as soon as may be, allow the application (a) certifying the correctness of the inventory so prepared, or, (b) taking, in the presence of such Magistrate, photographs of such raw cashewnuts and certifying such photographs as true.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but enforcement involves Revenue Divisional Officers, Magistrates, and Inspectors.
important_notes: The Act is deemed to have come into force on December 13, 2007.
Received the assent of the Governor on 3rd January, 2009 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No 36 dated 5th January 2009.
The amendments incorporate details regarding the sale of seized cashewnuts and penalties for contraventions.

title: The Unregistered Cashewnut Factories Prohibition Act, 1967
purpose: To prohibit the working of unregistered cashewnut factories in the State of Kerala.
scope: The Act extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and applies to the processing of cashewnuts in unregistered factories.

key_definitions.Inspector: An Inspector appointed or deemed to be appointed under section 3.
key_definitions.Prescribed: Prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.Processing: With reference to cashewnuts, includes extraction of cashewnut oil and, roasting, shelling, peeling, grinding and treating of cashewnuts.
key_definitions.unregistered cashewnut factory: A factory wherein processing of cashewnuts is being carried on, which has not been registered and licensed in pursuance of the rules made under the Factories Act.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act as 'The Unregistered Cashewnut Factories Prohibition Act, 1967' and specifies its territorial extent to the whole of the State of Kerala.

Provides definitions for terms used in the Act, including 'Factories Act', 'Inspector', 'Prescribed', 'Processing', and 'unregistered cashewnut factory'. It also clarifies that words and expressions not defined in this Act but defined in the Factories Act shall have their meanings from that Act.

Empowers the Government to appoint Inspectors for the purposes of the Act and assign them local limits. It also states that Inspectors appointed under the Factories Act are deemed to be Inspectors for the purposes of this Act within their assigned local limits.

main_sections.section_title: Prohibition of processing of cashewnuts in unregistered factories
main_sections.description: Prohibits any person from processing cashewnuts in an unregistered cashewnut factory.

Details the powers of Inspectors, including the power to enter premises (if necessary by force) to search, seize cashewnuts being processed in contravention of Section 4 along with their packaging, and seize related books of account, returns, or documents. It also states that the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, relating to search and seizure apply.

Specifies penalties for contravening or attempting to contravene Section 4 or any rule made under the Act. Penalties include imprisonment up to six months, a fine up to one thousand rupees, or both. For continuing contravention, an additional fine of up to one hundred rupees per day after the first conviction may be imposed.

Defines how offences committed by a company are handled. It holds individuals in charge of the company's business responsible, along with the company itself, unless they prove the offence was without their knowledge or they exercised due diligence. It also holds directors, managers, or other officers liable if the offence was committed with their consent, connivance, or due to their neglect. 'Company' includes firms and associations of individuals.
States that cashewnuts, along with their packaging, in respect of which a contravention has been committed, shall be forfeited to the Government upon conviction, by order of the court.

Mandates that no court shall take cognizance of an offence under this Act except upon a complaint made by an Inspector. It also specifies that only Magistrates of the First Class or higher courts can try offences punishable under this Act.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
main_sections.description: Provides protection from suits, prosecutions, or other legal proceedings against any person for anything done or intended to be done in good faith in pursuance of the Act or its rules. It also protects the Government from legal proceedings for damages caused or likely to be caused by actions taken in good faith under the Act.
Declares that every Inspector shall be deemed to be a public servant within the meaning of Section 21 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

Grants the Government the power to make rules for carrying into effect the provisions of the Act. It also outlines the procedure for laying such rules before the Legislative Assembly for modification or annulment.

Repeals the 'Unregistered Cashewnut Factories Prohibition Ordinance, 1967 (5 of 1967)'. It also includes a saving clause, stating that anything done or any action taken under the repealed Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act, effective from June 15, 1967.

important_rules: No person shall process cashewnuts in an unregistered cashewnut factory (Section 4).
Any contravention of Section 4 or rules made under the Act is punishable with imprisonment, fine, or both (Section 6).
Cashewnuts processed in contravention of the Act may be forfeited to the Government (Section 8).

penalties: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months.
Fine which may extend to one thousand rupees.
Both imprisonment and fine.
Additional fine of up to one hundred rupees for every day during which a continuing contravention continues after the first conviction.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Inspectors appointed under the Act and deemed to be appointed under the Factories Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through search and seizure powers of Inspectors, prosecution upon complaint by an Inspector, and cognizance by courts of the First Class and above. Enforcement also involves the forfeiture of cashewnuts and compliance with rules made by the Government.

rights: Right to protection from legal proceedings for actions taken in good faith under the Act (Section 10).
duties: Duty not to process cashewnuts in unregistered factories.
Duty to comply with rules made under the Act.
obligations: Obligation for companies to ensure no offences are committed by them or their personnel.
Obligation for directors, managers, and officers of companies to act with due diligence to prevent offences.

key_procedures: Appointment of Inspectors by the Government and assignment of local limits.
Search and seizure of premises, cashewnuts, and documents by Inspectors under specific conditions and in accordance with the Code of Criminal Procedure.
Initiation of legal proceedings through a complaint made by an Inspector.
Trial of offences by Magistrates of the First Class or higher.
Rule-making procedure by the Government, involving laying rules before the Legislative Assembly.
administration: The Government of Kerala is responsible for appointing Inspectors, making rules, and generally administering the Act. The Legislative Assembly has a role in the rule-making process.
important_notes: The Act repeals the Unregistered Cashewnut Factories Prohibition Ordinance, 1967.
Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are deemed to have been taken under this Act from June 15, 1967.
Inspectors are deemed public servants under the Indian Penal Code.

title: The Valiamma Thampuran Kovilakam Estate and The Palace Fund (Partition) Act, 1961
purpose: An Act to make provision for the partition of the Valiamma Thampuran Kovilakam Estate and the Palace Fund.
scope: Applies to the Valiamma Thampuran Kovilakam Estate and the Palace Fund belonging to the family of the Maharaja of Cochin.

key_definitions.Board: Means the Board of Trustees appointed under Section 3 of the Proclamation.
key_definitions.Estate: Means the Valiamma Thampuran Kovilakam Estate and all properties belonging to the said Estate.
key_definitions.Maharaja of Cochin: Means the Ruler of the former State of Cochin within the meaning of clause (22) of Article 366 of the Constitution of India.
key_definitions.Member: Means a member of the family of the Maharaja of Cochin.
key_definitions.Palace Fund: Shall have the same meaning as in clause (c) of section 2 of the Proclamation.
key_definitions.Proclamation: Means the Proclamation (IX of 1124) dated 29th June, 1949 promulgated by the Maharaja of Cochin.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Valiamma Thampuran Kovilakam Estate and the Palace Fund (Partition) Act, 1961. It shall come into force at once.
Defines terms used in the Act, including 'Board', 'Estate', 'Maharaja of Cochin', 'Member', 'Palace Fund', and 'Proclamation'.

main_sections.section_title: Maharaja of Cochin to order partition.
main_sections.description: Allows the Maharaja of Cochin to order the partition of the Estate and Palace Fund if satisfied that the interests of the family would be best served by it. The Maharaja may declare his decision to effect a partition under his supervision and control, and direct the Board to proceed with the partition.

Each member shall be entitled to an equal share of the Estate and the Palace Fund. The share obtained by a member on partition shall be the separate property of the member. A child who is in the womb on the date of the publication of the decision under section 3, and who is subsequently born alive, shall have the same right for a share in the Estate and the Palace Fund as any other member as if he or she had been born on or before the date of such publication.

main_sections.section_title: Power to exclude properties from partition.
main_sections.description: Notwithstanding anything contained in section 3, the Maharaja of Cochin may, if he is satisfied that any specified property or properties of the Estate and the Palace Fund shall not be partitioned, but shall mean as common property for the benefit of the family, exclude such property or properties from being partitioned. Any property excluded under sub-section (1) shall be subject to the management of the Board and the provisions of the Proclamation shall apply to such property.

main_sections.section_title: Execution and registration of partition deed.
main_sections.description: The deed of partition shall be executed on behalf of all the members by the Maharaja of Cochin and the members of the Board and shall be binding on all the members of the family and shall be registered under the provisions of the Indian Registration Act, 1908.
No suit for partition in this Act shall be deemed to confer on any member the right to institute a suit for partition of the Estate and the Palace Fund.

main_sections.section_title: Personal privileges of the Maharaja not to be affected.
main_sections.description: The partition of the Estate and the Palace Fund under the provisions of this Act shall not be deemed to affect the personal rights, privileges, dignities and titles guaranteed to the Maharaja of Cochin and to the members of his family by the Covenant entered into by the Rulers of Travancore and Cochin for the formation of the State of Travancore-Cochin.

main_sections.section_title: Pay, pension etc., of employees to be a charge.
main_sections.description: The partition of the Estate and the Palace Fund under the provisions of this Act shall not affect the claims of any employee for the pay, gratuity or provident fund due to them immediately before partition and suitable provision shall be made for payment of such amounts out of the Estate and the Palace Fund. The amounts due to the employees by way of pay, gratuity or provident fund shall be a charge on the Estate and the Palace Fund.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956.
main_sections.description: Clause (iii) of section 6 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 shall be omitted with effect on and from the date of the execution of the partition deed under section 6.

In the Proclamation (IX of 1124) dated 29th June, 1949, promulgated by the Maharaja of Cochin: (i) in section 1, for the words 'so as to secure representation for each of the four main thavazhies', the words 'so as to secure representation, as far as possible, for each of the four main thavazhies' shall be substituted. (ii) sub-section (2) of section 21 shall be omitted.

important_rules: The partition deed shall be executed on behalf of all members by the Maharaja of Cochin and the members of the Board.
The partition deed shall be binding on all members of the family.
The partition deed shall be registered under the provisions of the Indian Registration Act, 1908.
No suit for partition of the Estate and the Palace Fund is permitted.
Personal privileges of the Maharaja and his family are not affected by the partition.
Employee claims for pay, gratuity, and provident fund are a charge on the Estate and Palace Fund.
Specific amendments are made to the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 and the Proclamation.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Maharaja of Cochin and the Board of Trustees.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the execution and registration of a partition deed, and by ensuring employee dues are a charge on the Estate and Palace Fund. Amendments to existing laws are also part of enforcement.

rights: Each member is entitled to an equal share of the Estate and Palace Fund.
A child in the womb at the time of the decision has a right to a share.
Employees have rights to their pay, gratuity, and provident fund.
duties: The Maharaja of Cochin has the duty to order and supervise the partition.
The Board of Trustees has duties related to the management of excluded properties and the partition process.
Members have a duty to abide by the partition deed.
obligations: Suitable provision must be made for employee payments.

key_procedures: The Maharaja of Cochin issues an order for partition, declaring his decision and directing the Board to proceed.
The Board of Trustees manages the partition process.
A partition deed is executed by the Maharaja and Board members on behalf of all family members.
The partition deed is registered under the Indian Registration Act, 1908.
administration: The Board of Trustees, appointed under Section 3 of the Proclamation, appears to be the primary administrative body, under the supervision of the Maharaja of Cochin.
important_notes: The Act commenced on the 6th May 1961.
Received the assent of the President on 6th May 1961 and published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 18th May 1961.
Properties can be excluded from partition and remain as common property for the benefit of the family.
Personal privileges of the Maharaja and his family are unaffected.

title: THE VALIAMMA THAMPURAN KOVILAKAM ESTATE AND THE PALACE FUND (PARTITION) AND THE KERALA JOINT HINDU FAMILY SYSTEM (ABOLITION) AMENDMENT ACT, 1978
purpose: To amend The Valiamma Thampuran Kovilakam Estate and the Palace Fund (Partition) Act, 1961 and the Kerala Joint Hindu Family System (Abolition) Act, 1975.
scope: Applies to the Valiamma Thampuran Kovilakam Estate and the Palace Fund and the Kerala Joint Hindu Family System in Kerala.

key_definitions.family: Means the Marumakkathayam joint family consisting of the four main thavazhies of the Ruler of the former State of Cochin within the meaning of clause (22) of article 366 of the Constitution of India.
key_definitions.Maharaja of Cochin: Includes the Ruler of former Cochin.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Valiamma Thampuran Kovilakam Estate and the Palace Fund (Partition) Amendment Act, 1978.
Amends section 2 of the Valiamma Thampuran Kovilakam Estate and the Palace Fund (Partition) Act, 1961, by inserting provisions regarding the board and the action to be taken by the board.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 3.
main_sections.description: Substitutes section 3, dealing with the seniormost male member of the family, within sixty days from the date of commencement of the Valiamma Thampuran Kovilakam Estate and the Palace Fund (Partition) and the Kerala Joint Hindu Family System (Abolition) Amendment Ordinance, 1978.
Omit sections 4 and 5 of the principal Act and deem them to have been omitted with effect from and from the 28th day of December, 1976.
Amends section 6 by substituting words in the marginal note and in the main body.
Amends section 8 of the principal Act by substituting words.

main_sections.section_title: Substitution of new section for section 11.
main_sections.description: Substitutes section 11 of the principal Act, inserting provisions related to Proclamation IX of 1124 and its effect, and amendments to the definition of 'family'.
Amends the Kerala Joint Hindu Family System (Abolition) Act, 1975, by inserting a new section related to Proclamation IX of 1124 and its continuance in force, and the powers of the Board of Trustees.

Repeals the Valiamma Thampuran Kovilakam Estate and the Palace Fund (Partition) and the Kerala Joint Hindu Family System (Abolition) Amendment Ordinance, 1978 (1 of 1978), with a saving clause for actions taken under the Ordinance.

important_rules: The seniormost male member of the family shall, within sixty days from the date of commencement of the Valiamma Thampuran Kovilakam Estate and the Palace Fund (Partition) and the Kerala Joint Hindu Family System (Abolition) Amendment Ordinance, 1978, direct the Board to effect partition of the Estate and the Palace Fund among all the members entitled to a share of the Estate and the Palace Fund under section 4 of the Kerala Joint Hindu Family System (Abolition) Act, 1975.

Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or in any other law for the time being in force, Proclamation (IX of 1124) dated the 29th June, 1949, promulgated by the Maharaja of Cochin, as amended by the Valiamma Thampuran Kovilakam Estate and the Palace Fund (Partition) Amendment Act, 1978, and the Kerala Joint Hindu Family System (Abolition) Amendment Act, 1978, and the Kerala Joint Hindu Family System (Abolition) Amendment Ordinance, 1978, shall continue to be in force and shall apply to the Valiamma Thampuran Kovilakam Estate and the Palace Fund administered by the Board of Trustees appointed under section 3 of the said Proclamation.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Board of Trustees appointed under section 3 of Proclamation IX of 1124.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Actions taken under the Ordinance are deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act or the said Proclamation or Act.

rights: Right to partition of the Estate and the Palace Fund among entitled members.
duties: The seniormost male member of the family has the duty to direct the Board to effect partition.

key_procedures: The seniormost male member of the family must direct the Board to effect partition within sixty days of the commencement of the Amendment Ordinance.
Actions taken under the repealed Ordinance are deemed valid and taken under the principal Act or Proclamation.
administration: Board of Trustees appointed under section 3 of Proclamation IX of 1124.
important_notes: Received the assent of the President on the 18th day of March 1978 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 194 dated 19th March, 1978.
The Valiamma Thampuran Kovilakam Estate and the Palace Fund (Partition) and the Kerala Joint Hindu Family System (Abolition) Amendment Ordinance, 1978 (1 of 1978), is hereby repealed.

Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act or the Proclamation (IX of 1124) dated the 29th June, 1949, promulgated by the Maharaja of Cochin or the Kerala Joint Hindu Family System (Abolition) Act, 1975 (30 of 1976), as amended by the said Ordinance, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act or as if this Act had come into force on the 6th day of January, 1978.

title: The Wakf (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1972
purpose: To amend the Wakf Act, 1954, in its application to the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: States that this Act may be called the Wakf (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1972, extends to the whole of the State of Kerala, and shall come into force at once.

Amends section 3 of the Wakf Act, 1954 (Central Act 29 of 1954) by modifying clause (g) to include specific details regarding income from 'pidiyari, kettuthengu and similar other voluntary contributions in kind or in cash' and grants received from the State Government for institutions like mosques, orphanages, madrassas, schools, and colleges, as well as donations for maintenance of orphanages or inmates of orphanages and madrasas and arabic colleges.

Repeals the Wakf (Kerala Amendment) Ordinance, 1972 (6 of 1972). It also states that notwithstanding the repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act, provided that if such Act had come into force on the 22nd day of June, 1972.

important_notes: The Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 627, dated 2nd November, 1972.

title: THE CALICUT MUNICIPAL CORPORATION (EXTENSION OF TIME FOR RECONSTITUTION) AMENDMENT ACT, 1979
purpose: To further amend the Calicut Municipal Corporation (Extension of Time for Reconstitution) Act, 1976, for the purposes hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Calicut Municipal Corporation and related to its reconstitution. It amends the principal Act of 1976.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Calicut Municipal Corporation (Extension of Time for Reconstitution) Amendment Act, 1979. It shall come into force on the 31st day of October, 1978.

In section 3 of the Calicut Municipal Corporation (Extension of Time for Reconstitution) Act, 1976, for the figures, letters and words "1st day of November, 1978" and "1st day of October, 1979", the figures, letters and words "1st day of November, 1983" and "1st day of October, 1984" shall be substituted, respectively.

The Calicut Municipal Corporation (Extension of Time for Reconstitution) Third Amendment Ordinance, 1978 (23 of 1978) is repealed. Notwithstanding this repeal, any action taken or done or any step taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 29th March, 1979 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No. 290, dated 29th March, 1979.

title: The Calicut University (Amendment) Act, 1976
purpose: To amend the Calicut University Act, 1975, for the purpose hereinafter appearing.
scope: Applies to the Calicut University.

main_sections.description: (1) This Act may be called the Calicut University (Amendment) Act, 1976. (2) It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 20th day of September, 1975.

In section 17 of the Calicut University Act, 1975 (5 of 1975), in item (2) under the heading "Elected Members": for the words "not being teachers" the words, brackets and figures "not being persons eligible to be elected under item (1), (4), (5), (6), (9), (10), (11) or (12) or under item (1), (4), (5), (6), (9), (10), (11) or (12) under the heading "Elected Members" in section 17 of the Kerala University Act, 1974" shall be substituted.

(1) The Calicut University (Amendment) Ordinance, 1975 (8 of 1975), is hereby repealed. (2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the principal Act as amended by the said Ordinance shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

administration: The Calicut University
important_notes: Received the assent of the Governor on the 13th day of March 1976 and published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary No 159, dated 13th March 1976.

title: The Kerala Appropriation (No. 2) Act, 1988
purpose: To provide for the withdrawal of certain sums from and out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala for the services of the financial year commencing on the first day of April, 1988.
scope: Applies to the financial year commencing on the first day of April, 1988, and covers various services and purposes as detailed in the schedule.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Appropriation (No. 2) Act, 1988.

Withdrawal of Rs. 25, 97, 24, 09, 300 from and out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala for the financial year commencing on the first day of April, 1988. From and out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala there may be paid and applied sums not exceeding those specified in column (3) of the Schedule amounting in the aggregate to the sum of two thousand five hundred and ninety-seven crores, twenty-four lakhs, nine thousand and three hundred rupees (which shall be inclusive of the sum of eight hundred and sixty-five crores, seventy-four lakhs, sixty-nine thousand and seven hundred rupees specified in section 2 of the Kerala Appropriation (Vote on Account) Act, 1988 (3 of 1988) towards defraying the several charges which will come in course of payment during the financial year commencing on the first day of April, 1988, in respect of the services and purposes specified in column (2) of the Schedule.

The sums authorised to be paid and applied from and out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala by this Act shall be appropriated for the services and purposes specified in the Schedule in relation to the said year.

important_rules: Sums specified in column (3) of the Schedule are authorized for withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund of Kerala for the financial year 1988-89.
These sums are to be applied towards defraying charges for services and purposes specified in column (2) of the Schedule.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be the State Government of Kerala.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the appropriation of funds as per the Act and the Schedule.

duties: The Government is pleased to authorise the publication of the foregoing translation in the English language of the Kerala Appropriation (No. 2) Act, 1988.

key_procedures: Withdrawal of specified sums from the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala.
Application of these sums for services and purposes outlined in the schedule.
Appropriation of the authorized sums for the specified services and purposes.
administration: Law (Legislation-A) Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act is enacted in pursuance of clause (3) of article 348 of the Constitution of India.
The schedule provides a detailed breakdown of amounts allocated for various services and purposes, including Revenue and Revenue Capital.

title: THE KERALA APPROPRIATION (No. 3) ACT, 1961
purpose: To provide for the appropriation of certain further moneys out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala for the service of the financial year commencing on the 1st April, 1961.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and its financial year commencing on the 1st April, 1961.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Appropriation (No. 3) Act, 1961.

main_sections.section_title: Further appropriation out of the Consolidated Fund for the financial year commencing on the 1st April, 1961.
main_sections.description: Authorizes the appropriation of a further sum not exceeding forty-five lakhs, thirty-three thousand and five hundred rupees for the financial year commencing on the 1st April, 1961. It also specifies that supplementary grants made by the Kerala Legislative Assembly for that year, as set forth in column (3) of the Schedule; and the supplementary expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala for that year, as set forth in column (4) of the Schedule, are also appropriated.

Contains the details of the sums voted by the Legislative Assembly and charged on the Consolidated Fund for various services and purposes, categorized under Revenue Account and Capital Expenditure Outside the Revenue Account, and also for Disbursement of Loans and Advances and Repayment of Public Debt.

important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 10th July, 1961.

title: The Kerala Appropriation (No. 4) Act, 1961
purpose: To provide for the appropriation of moneys out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala to meet the amounts spent on certain services during the financial year ended on the 31st day of March, 1957 (last five months), in excess of the amounts granted for those services and for that year.
scope: The Act applies to the financial year ended on the 31st day of March, 1957, specifically for services rendered in the last five months of that year.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called The Kerala Appropriation (No. 4) Act, 1961.

main_sections.section_title: Issue of Rs. 4,52,23,494 out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala to meet certain excess expenditure for the year ended on the 31st March, 1957 (last five months).
main_sections.description: This section authorizes the issue of a specific sum (Rs. 4,52,23,494) from the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala to cover excess expenditure incurred during the last five months of the financial year ending on March 31, 1957.

This section appropriates the sums specified in the schedule to the purposes mentioned therein, to be paid from and out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala, under the relevant expenditure heads for the financial year ended on the 31st day of March, 1957 (last five months).

important_rules: The Act provides for the appropriation of funds already spent in excess of the granted amounts for specific services during the last five months of the financial year 1956-57.

The sums to be appropriated are detailed in the Schedule annexed to the Act, which specifies the Vote, Services and purposes, amounts Voted by the Assembly, amounts Charged on the Consolidated Fund, and the Total amounts.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly mentioned, but likely the State Government of Kerala and its financial departments.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through legislative approval and subsequent financial transactions as authorized by the Act.

rights: The right to appropriate funds to cover legitimate excess expenditures.
duties: The duty of the State Government to account for and seek legislative approval for expenditures.
obligations: The obligation to adhere to the appropriations authorized by the Act.

key_procedures: The Act itself serves as the authorization procedure for appropriating funds.
The Schedule details the specific services and amounts that are being retroactively appropriated.
administration: The Finance Department of the Government of Kerala would typically administer the appropriation of funds.
important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 10th July, 1961.
The Act retroactively approves expenditures made in excess of the original grants.

The Schedule lists specific categories of expenditure such as Land Revenue, Excise, District Administration, Administration of Justice, Scientific Departments, Public Works, Electricity, Pensions, Transport, Revenue Account, and schemes related to Government Trading and Debt Repayment.

title: THE KERALA APPROPRIATION (No. 5) ACT, 1961
purpose: To provide for the authorisation of appropriation of moneys out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala to meet the amounts spent on certain services during the financial year ended on the 31st day of March, 1958 in excess of the amounts granted for those services and for that year.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Appropriation (No. 5) Act, 1961.

main_sections.section_title: Issue of Rs. 4,95,16,439 out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala to meet certain excess expenditure for the year ended on the 31st March, 1958.
main_sections.description: Authorises the issue of Rs. 4,95,16,439 out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala to meet certain excess expenditure for the financial year ended on the 31st day of March, 1958. This amount is specified in column (2) of the Schedule, which is in excess of the amounts granted for those services and for that year. This appropriation is to be charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala.

The sums deemed to have been authorised to be paid and applied from and out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of Kerala under this Act shall be deemed to have been appropriated for the services and purposes expressed in the Schedule in relation to the financial year ended on the 31st day of March, 1958.

administration: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be related to the financial administration of the State of Kerala.
important_notes: Published in the Gazette extraordinary dated 10th July, 1961.

title: The Kerala Finance Act, 1988
purpose: To give effect to certain financial proposals of the Government of Kerala for the financial year 1988-89.
scope: Applies to financial proposals of the Government of Kerala for the financial year 1988-89. It amends existing acts like the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, and the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976. The act introduces amendments related to sales tax on various goods and services, and also relates to motor vehicle taxes based on vehicle class and quarterly tax rates.

key_definitions.foreign liquor: Means any liquor manufactured in any country other than India and brought to India.
key_definitions.liquor: Means toddy, wine, brandy, champagne, sherry, rum, gin, whisky, beer, cider, cocoa, brandy, arrack and all other distilled or spirituous or fermented beverages brought into or produced or manufactured in the State.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Finance Act, 1988, and it shall be deemed to have come into force on the 1st day of April, 1988.

This section details the amendments to the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963. It involves inserting new sub-sections, amending existing ones, and making changes to schedules related to taxable goods and services, including rates of tax for various items like palmolein, rationed articles, foreign liquor, and cooked food. It also specifies turnover thresholds and associated tax amounts.
This section makes an amendment to the Kerala Additional Sales Tax Act, 1978, by substituting the words "twenty-five per cent" with "twenty per cent" in sub-section (1) of section 2.

This section details amendments to the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976. It involves substituting figures in Serial Number 3 and Serial Number 6A of the Schedule, relating to the 'rate of quarterly tax' for various classes of vehicles. This includes specific monetary amounts for different vehicle categories and weight classes.

important_rules: Certain goods like palmolein, rationed articles, rice, wheat, sugar, and kerosene when sold exclusively by an authorised retail or wholesale distributor are not liable to get himself registered under this Act.
Application for registration for certain businesses must be made to such authority, in such manner, and within such period as may be prescribed and shall be accompanied by a fee as specified.

Specific monetary thresholds for total turnover determine the applicable fees for registration. For instance, a turnover of less than three lakhs rupees requires a fee of Fifty rupees, up to ten lakhs rupees requires One hundred rupees, and ten lakhs rupees and above requires Two hundred and fifty rupees.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be tax authorities under the Kerala General Sales Tax Act and the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through amendments to existing tax laws and their respective enforcement mechanisms.

rights: Right to apply for registration if the business falls within prescribed criteria.
duties: Duty to comply with the provisions of the amended Acts.
Duty to register if required.
Duty to pay taxes as per the revised rates and provisions.
obligations: Obligation to adhere to the financial proposals implemented through this Act.

key_procedures: Procedure for registration under the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, including fee payment.
Procedure for amendment of tax rates for specific goods and services.
Procedure for revised taxation of motor vehicles based on class and quarterly tax rates.
administration: Government of Kerala, Law (Legislation-A) Department.
important_notes: Amendments to the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963 include changes to sales tax on 'Cooked food including beverages not falling under entry 76A' for hotels/restaurants and attached hotels and/or restaurants, and also for foreign liquor and toddy.

The Act specifies that if the sale of foreign liquor is liable to tax under section 5, except where the sale is to the Kerala State Beverages (Manufacturing and Marketing) Corporation, Limited, the tax shall be levied at the point of first sale by a dealer who is liable to tax under section 5 as on 31st day of March, 1988, which had suffered tax on or before that date at the first point of levy as per the Fifth Schedule.

The amendments to the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976, provide detailed substitutions for quarterly tax rates for various vehicle classes, including tourist motor cabs and specific types of vehicles described by their weight and usage.

title: THE KERALA LAND DEVELOPMENT (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1969
purpose: To amend the Kerala Land Development Act, 1964.
scope: The Act applies to the state of Kerala. It amends the Kerala Land Development Act, 1964.

key_definitions.Padasekharam: A collection of fields contiguously situated with a common outer bund and with all or any of the agricultural operations like pumping operation done jointly by all the owners.

main_sections.description: This section states that the Act may be called the Kerala Land Development (Amendment) Act, 1969, and it shall come into force at once.
This section amends section 2 of the Kerala Land Development Act, 1964 (17 of 1964), by inserting definitions for 'Padasekharam' and 'Padasekharam Committee'.

This section amends section 3 of the principal Act, for item (a), by substituting the Minister for Agriculture for the Chairman and the Commissioner for Agricultural Production for the Vice-Chairman of the Padasekharam Committee.

This section amends section 5 of the principal Act by renumbering sub-section (1) and inserting provisions regarding grant or loan made or advanced to the District Committee or Padasekharam Committee for purposes under section 18, and the procedure for obtaining such grant or loan.

This section amends section 6 of the principal Act by inserting provisions regarding non-official members absenting themselves from three consecutive meetings of the District Committee, and the nomination to vacancies under sub-section (6) being made by the Government.

main_sections.section_title: Insertion of new sections after section 7.
main_sections.description: This section inserts new sections 7A and 7B. Section 7A deals with the constitution and powers of the Padasekharam Committee, including election of members, their term of office, eligibility for re-election, resignation, and filling of vacancies. Section 7B outlines the functions of the Padasekharam Committee, including executing schemes on appointment by the District Committee and following procedures prescribed by rules.

This section amends section 8 of the principal Act by substituting words in item (a) and renumbering item (m) and (n) to include provisions for erecting pumpsets and providing channels for watering and dewatering purposes.

This section amends section 9 of the principal Act by providing for the receipt of an order from the Government under section 4, for the Board to be satisfied with the recommendation of the District Committee or Padasekharam Committee, and for the District Committee to prepare a draft scheme in consultation with the Padasekharam Committee.

This section amends section 13 of the principal Act by substituting 'District Agricultural Officer' with 'District Agricultural Officer' and 'Padasekharam Committee' with 'agents of the District Committee'.

This section amends section 15 of the principal Act by allowing the Government to fix the cost to be recovered from owners and also providing that the Government may appoint the Padasekharam Committee as agents to execute any work.

This section substitutes section 18 of the principal Act, which deals with the power to make, grant or advance loan. The Government may make a grant or advance a loan to a District Committee or a Padasekharam Committee or any person or stand guarantee for the payment of any loan advanced by any bank or other financial institution.

This section amends section 19 of the Principal Act by substituting 'District Committee' with 'Committee' or 'President of the Padasekharam Committee' and 'District Committee or' with 'Padasekharam Committee or'.
This section amends section 20 of the Principal Act by substituting 'The Executing Officer' with 'the Executing Officer or the Padasekharam Committee, as the case may be' and 'acre' with 'hectare'.
This section amends section 27 of the principal Act by substituting 'Committee' with 'District Committee or the Padasekharam Committee'.
This section amends section 31 of the Principal Act by substituting 'Committee' with 'District Committee or the Padasekharam Committee'.

important_rules: A non-official member absenting himself from three consecutive meetings of the District Committee shall cease to be a member.
Nomination to vacancies under sub-section (6) shall be made by the Government.
Members of the Padasekharam Committee shall elect a president who shall preside over the meetings. The president shall have and exercise a second or casting vote in the case of an equality of votes.

Subject to the provisions of this section, every member of the Padasekharam Committee shall hold office for a period of three years from the date of declaration of his election to the Padasekharam Committee but shall be eligible for re-election.

Any member of the Padasekharam Committee may resign by tendering his resignation in writing to the Chairman of the Committee and on such resignation being accepted by the Committee, the member shall be deemed to have vacated his office.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: District Committee or Padasekharam Committee, as agents of the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: By execution of schemes and recovery of costs from owners.

rights: Right to receive grant or loan from the Government for land development.
duties: Duty to manage and operate schemes for land development.
Duty to carry out operations like pumping.
obligations: Obligation to contribute to the cost of land development schemes.

key_procedures: Procedure for election of members and president of the Padasekharam Committee.
Procedure for resignation and filling of vacancies in the Padasekharam Committee.
Procedure for the Padasekharam Committee to carry out schemes as agents of the District Committee.
Procedure for recovery of costs of schemes from owners.
administration: Department of Agriculture, Government of Kerala (inferred from 'Minister for Agriculture').
important_notes: The Act is an amendment to the Kerala Land Development Act, 1964.
Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 36, dated 11th February, 1969.

title: THE KERALA MUNICIPAL LAWS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1960
purpose: To provide for the further extension of the term of office of the Mayor and other councillors and chairmen of standing committees of the Corporation of Trivandrum, and of the councillors of municipalities.
scope: Applies to the Corporation of Trivandrum and municipalities within Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Kerala Municipal Laws (Amendment) Act, 1960.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of the term of office of the Mayor, councillors, etc., of the Corporation of Trivandrum, City Municipal Act (Travancore Act IV of 1116) shall have effect subject to the following modifications, namely:—
main_sections.description: Extends the term of office of the Mayor, councillors, etc., of the Corporation of Trivandrum. It specifies modifications regarding elections and expiry of terms for newly elected councillors.

main_sections.section_title: Trivandrum City Municipal Act to be modified temporarily.
main_sections.description: Modifies the Trivandrum City Municipal Act (Travancore Act IV of 1116) temporarily, subject to specific modifications.

main_sections.section_title: Extension of the term of office of the municipal councillors of the Corporation of Trivandrum, and of the councillors of municipalities.
main_sections.description: Extends the term of office for municipal councillors of the Corporation of Trivandrum and other municipalities. It also specifies that the Government may, by notification in the Gazette, extend the term of office of the councillors of any municipality constituted under any of the aforesaid Acts up to such date not later than the 1st day of April, 1961, as may be specified in the notification.

main_sections.section_title: Election and term of office of new councillors.
main_sections.description: Deals with the election and term of office of new councillors, stating that the Government shall cause elections to every municipality concerned to be so held that the newly elected councillors enter upon office on the date specified.

Empowers the Government to do anything necessary to remove difficulties in giving effect to the provisions of this Act or of the Trivandrum City Municipal Act, the Travancore District Municipalities Act, the Cochin Municipal Act, the Madras District Municipalities Act, or the Kerala Local Authorities Laws (Amendment) Act, 1959.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the Kerala Local Authorities Laws (Amendment) Act, 1959.
main_sections.description: Amends specific sections (2, 3, 4, 5 and 7) of the Kerala Local Authorities Laws (Amendment) Act, 1959.
Repeals The Kerala Municipal Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1960 (Ordinance No. 5 of 1960).

important_rules: Rule regarding elections to municipalities to ensure newly elected councillors enter office on the specified date.
Rule regarding the expiry of the term of office for newly elected councillors.
Rule that the Government may, by notification, extend the term of office of councillors of any municipality.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The Government
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notifications and orders to remove difficulties.

key_procedures: Government shall cause elections to be held for municipalities.
Newly elected councillors shall enter office on the specified date.
Government may issue notifications to extend terms of office.
Government may issue orders to remove difficulties in implementing the Act.
administration: The Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act was published in the Gazette Extraordinary dated 24th October, 1960.
The extensions provided by this Act are temporary.

title: THE KERALA ADDITIONAL TAX ON LANDS ACT, 1961
purpose: An Act to provide for the levy of an additional tax on certain lands.
scope: Applies to the whole of the State of Kerala. Effective from the 1st day of April, 1961. Applies to lands belonging to the Government, Sree Padmanabha swami Temple, and Sreepadham Palace. Also applies to lands held by a person to whom additional tax or other sum of money is payable under this Act. "Lands" are defined to include lands belonging to the Government. The expression "tenant" shall have the meaning assigned to it in the Kerala Agrarian Relations Act, 1960. "Prescribed" means prescribed by rules made under this Act. "Prescribed authority" means the authority appointed by the Government under clause (7) of section 3 of the Kerala Land Tax Act, 1961.

key_definitions.additional tax: the additional tax on lands imposed under the provisions of this Act.
key_definitions.appellate authority: means the appellate authority appointed by the Government.
key_definitions.assessee: means a person by whom additional tax or any other sum of money is payable under this Act, and includes every person in respect of whom any proceeding under this Act has been taken for the assessment of additional tax payable by him.
key_definitions.prescribed: means prescribed by rules made under this Act.
key_definitions.prescribed authority: means the authority appointed by the Government under clause (7) of section 3 of the Kerala Land Tax Act, 1961.
key_definitions.to hold: with reference to a land means to be in possession of the land as owner or as tenant or as mortgagee.

main_sections.description: States the short title of the Act, its extent to the whole of Kerala, and its commencement from the 1st day of April, 1961.

Specifies exemptions from the Act, including lands belonging to the Government, Sree Padmanabha swami Temple, and Sreepadham Palace. The Government may, by notification in the Gazette, exempt any land belonging to any public body or institution from the provisions of this Act if satisfied that such exemption is necessary in the public interest.
Defines key terms used in the Act, such as 'additional tax', 'appellate authority', 'assessee', 'prescribed', 'prescribed authority', and 'to hold'.

Levies an additional tax on certain lands from the 1st day of April, 1961. The tax is at the rate of two rupees per acre per annum, on all lands of whatever description held by a person, the gross income from which is not less than twenty rupees per acre per annum. No additional tax is levied on lands held by a person if the total extent of the lands held by him does not exceed two acres.

main_sections.section_title: Return relating to lands liable to additional tax.
main_sections.description: Requires every person who, on the 1st day of April, 1961, held any land liable to the additional tax, to furnish, by the 30th day of September of that year, a return to the prescribed authority in the prescribed form and verified in the prescribed manner.  Returns must be submitted within ninety days of the date on which they come to hold such land.  The prescribed authority may permit late filing of returns.

main_sections.section_title: Return after due date and amendment of return.
main_sections.description: Deals with the submission of returns after the due date and the amendment of returns. If a person has not furnished a return within the time allowed, or has furnished a return under section 5, or has furnished a wrong return, the prescribed authority may serve a notice and the person must furnish a return or amend the existing one.

Outlines the process of assessment. If the prescribed authority is satisfied without requiring the presence of the assessee or production of evidence, they will determine the extent of lands held and the amount payable. If not satisfied, they will serve a notice on the assessee to attend in person or produce evidence. The prescribed authority may require production of documents and evidence. If any person fails to make a return or comply with a notice, the prescribed authority can determine the extent of land and the amount payable based on available information.

Allows for provisional assessment in certain circumstances, particularly where lands have not been surveyed. The prescribed authority may make a provisional assessment of the additional tax payable by a person holding such lands.

Provides for the reassessment of additional tax. The additional tax shall be payable by the assessee for every financial year until reassessment is made. The prescribed authority may determine the extent of lands liable to the additional tax and reassess the amount payable.
Details the procedure for issuing a notice of demand for any additional tax due under the Act. The notice will specify the sum payable.

Establishes an appeal process for any assessee objecting to the determination of the extent of lands held by him, or to the assessment of additional tax. Appeals are to be filed with the appellate authority within thirty days of the date of the order. A fee of five rupees must accompany the appeal. If the appellate authority finds the appeal has merit, they may admit it. The appellate authority may, after giving the assessee an opportunity of being heard, pass orders.

Allows for a reference to the District Court on questions of law arising out of any order passed by the appellate authority. The District Court's decision on such a reference is final.  The District Court is defined for this section as meaning the District Court having jurisdiction over the area in which the land on which additional tax is levied is situated.
Empowers the Board of Revenue to revise any order passed by the appellate authority.  Applications for revision must be made within thirty days of the date of the order.
Specifies that any amount of additional tax payable under this Act is to be paid in such manner and within such time as may be prescribed.  Interest is charged on arrears.

States that arrears of additional tax, together with interest, shall be a first charge on the interest of the holder of the land. These arrears are recoverable under the law for the time being in force relating to the recovery of land revenue, and any such sale is free from encumbrances.
Makes it an offense to make a false statement in a declaration or return. The offense is punishable under the Indian Penal Code.

main_sections.section_title: Failure to furnish return or document.
main_sections.description: Penalizes persons who fail to furnish a return or document as required by the Act. Punishable with fine which may extend to five rupees for every day during which the default continues.

main_sections.section_title: Power to take evidence on oath, etc.
main_sections.description: Grants the prescribed authority, the appellate authority, and the revisional authority powers to take evidence on oath, affirmations, and to compel the attendance of persons and production of documents, similar to powers vested in a court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

Lays down the procedure for prosecutions under the Act. No person shall be proceeded against for an offense except with the sanction of such officer as may be authorized by the Government. Proceedings should not be instituted without prior inquiry.

Specifies that the extent of lands held by a person will be determined by the prescribed authority of the area in which the lands are situated, or where the lands are situated within the jurisdiction of two or more prescribed authorities, by such of those authorities in such manner as may be prescribed.
Allows the prescribed authority or the appellate authority to rectify any mistakes in any order passed by them within three years from the date of the order.

main_sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith.
main_sections.description: Provides protection to persons acting in good faith in pursuance of the provisions of the Act or rules made thereunder.
Empowers the Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, including prescribing forms, manner of assessment, and fees.
Allows for remission of additional tax under certain circumstances.

important_rules: Every person liable to additional tax must furnish a return by September 30th of the relevant year.
Returns must be verified in the prescribed manner.
Appeals must be filed within thirty days of the date of the order being appealed against.
A fee of five rupees must accompany an appeal.
Arrears of additional tax are a first charge on the interest of the land holder.

penalties: Failure to furnish return or document: Fine up to five rupees per day.
False statements in declaration: Punishable under the Indian Penal Code.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The prescribed authority, appointed by the Government.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment, notice of demand, recovery of arrears as land revenue, and prosecution for offenses like making false statements or failing to furnish returns.

rights: Right to appeal against assessment orders.
Right to a reference to the District Court on points of law.
Right to seek revision of orders by the Board of Revenue.
Opportunity to be heard before adverse orders are passed.
Opportunity to show cause against proposed assessments.
Refund of overpaid or wrongly paid amounts.
duties: Duty to furnish returns by the prescribed date.
Duty to disclose correct information regarding land holdings.
Duty to pay additional tax and arrears on demand.
obligations: Obligation to comply with notices issued by the prescribed authority.
Obligation to appear in person or produce documents when required.

key_procedures: Furnishing a return of lands liable to additional tax.
Assessment of additional tax by the prescribed authority.
Issuance of notice of demand for payment of tax.
Filing an appeal against assessment orders to the appellate authority.
Seeking a reference to the District Court on questions of law.
Applying for revision of orders to the Board of Revenue.
Rectification of mistakes in orders by the prescribed or appellate authority.
administration: The Government of Kerala, through prescribed authorities and appellate/revisional authorities.
important_notes: The Act does not apply to lands held by a person if the total extent of the lands held by him does not exceed two acres.
The expression "tenant" has the meaning assigned to it in the Kerala Agrarian Relations Act, 1960.
The Act seeks to supplement the Kerala Agrarian Relations Act, 1960.
Actions taken in good faith under the Act are protected.
The District Court's decision on a reference is final.

title: THE KERALA GENERAL SALES TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1989
purpose: To amend the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, specifically to introduce provisions for the transit of goods and to address related matters.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala, concerning the movement of goods within the State and the taxation of such goods.

key_definitions.transit of goods: The movement of goods from any place outside the State and bound for any place outside the State through the State.
key_definitions.registered dealer: A person who is registered under the Act for the purpose of transacting in goods.

main_sections.description: States that the Act is called the Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 1989, and it came into force on the 25th day of November, 1988.

Inserts a new section 30B into the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963, concerning the transit of goods. This new section details the requirements for obtaining a transit pass for goods passing through the State, the procedure for checking such goods, and the presumption of tax liability if certain conditions are not met.

Repeals the Kerala General Sales Tax (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1988, and provides for savings, ensuring that any action taken under the repealed Ordinance is deemed to have been taken under the principal Act as amended by this Act.

important_rules: Rule 1: Transit passes are required for goods moving through the State. These passes must be obtained from the officer-in-charge of the first check post.
Rule 2: If a vehicle or driver fails to deliver the transit pass as required, it will be presumed that such goods are liable to tax under the Act.
Rule 3: For the purpose of this section, the owner or driver of a vehicle carrying goods is deemed to be a registered dealer under the Act, unless they are registered under the Act.

Rule 4: Goods consigned or transported from another State into the State, if declared false or fraudulent in the prescribed manner, are presumed to be subject to tax unless proof to the contrary is provided.

penalties: If goods are found to be in contravention of the transit provisions, they may be assessed for tax with penalties, even if the turnover is not fully ascertained.
Penalties may be imposed if the owner or driver fails to provide proof of goods not being liable to tax under certain circumstances.
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: The assessing authority under the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963.
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through the assessment and collection of sales tax, imposition of penalties, and checking of goods at designated check posts.

rights: Right to obtain a transit pass for goods passing through the State.
Right to prove that goods are not liable to tax under specific circumstances.
duties: Duty to obtain and deliver a transit pass for goods moving through the State.
Duty to satisfy the assessing authority that goods are not liable to tax.
obligations: Obligation for owners or drivers of vehicles carrying goods through the State to comply with transit regulations.
Obligation for dealers to ensure goods are properly declared and accounted for.

key_procedures: Procedure 1: Obtain a transit pass from the officer-in-charge of the first check post for goods entering the State. Deliver the pass to the officer-in-charge of the last check post before exiting the State.
Procedure 2: If goods are presumed liable to tax due to failure to comply with transit pass requirements, the owner or driver must provide proof to the assessing authority to rebut this presumption.
administration: The Sales Tax Department of the Government of Kerala.
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on the 31st day of January, 1989.
The Act was published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary on January 31st, 1989.
The provisions of the Act are presumed to apply with retrospective effect from November 25th, 1988.
The Kerala General Sales Tax (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1988, has been repealed.

title: The Payment Of Wages (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1969
purpose: To amend the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, in its application to the State of Kerala.
scope: The Act applies to the whole of the State of Kerala.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Payment of Wages (Kerala Amendment) Act, 1969. It extends to the whole of the State of Kerala and shall come into force at once.

Amends Section 7 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 (Central Act 4 of 1936) by inserting a new clause '(p)' for deductions for repayment to the State Government of the amount of financial aid granted under the Kerala Financial Aid (to the Discharged or Dismissed Labour) Rules, 1958.

important_notes: Published in the Gazette Extraordinary No 249 dated 8th October, 1969.

title: THE PRISONS LAWS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1976
purpose: To amend the Prisons Act, 1894, in its application to the State of Kerala, and the Travancore-Cochin Prisons Act, 1950.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala and the Travancore-Cochin Prisons Act, 1950.

main_sections.description: This Act may be called the Prisons Laws (Amendment) Act, 1976. It shall be deemed to have come into force on the 10th day of October, 1972.

In section 59 of the Prisons Act, 1894 (Central Act 9 of 1894), as in force in the Malabar district referred to in sub-section (2) of section 5 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (Central Act 37 of 1956), the words "The State Government may make rules consistent with this Act", the words "either prospectively or retrospectively" shall be inserted.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Travancore-Cochin Act, XVIII of 1950
main_sections.description: In section 59 of the Travancore-Cochin Prisons Act, 1950 (XVIII of 1950), after the words "The State Government may make rules consistent with this Act", the words "either prospectively or retrospectively" shall be inserted.

Notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force, or in any judgment, decree or order of any court, the amendment purporting to have been made in rule 67 of the Kerala Prisons Rules, 1958, with retrospective effect from the 11th day of December, 1959, by notification G.O. (MS) No 153/72/Home dated the 10th October, 1972, published as S R O No. 536/72 in the Kerala Gazette No. 42, dated the 24th October, 1972, shall be deemed to have been made under section 59 of the Prisons Act, 1894 (Central Act 9 of 1894) and section 59 of the Travancore-Cochin Prisons Act, 1950 (XVIII of 1950), as amended by this Act, and accordingly, no appointment or promotion in the grade of Jailor, Deputy Jailor or Assistant Jailor in the Jails Department of the Government, of any person who had not passed the Jail Officers' Test before such appointment or promotion, made or purporting to have been made on or after the 11th day of December, 1959 and before the date of publication of this Act in the Gazette, shall be deemed to be invalid or ever to have been invalid merely on the ground that such person had not passed the said test before such appointment or promotion as required by rule 67 of the Kerala Prisons Rules as originally made, and no such appointment or promotion shall be called in question in any court on the said ground.

(1) The Kerala Prisons Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1975 (14 of 1975), is hereby repealed. (2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the Prisons Act, 1894 and the Travancore-Cochin Prisons Act, 1950, as amended by the said Ordinance, shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the said Acts as amended by this Act.

important_notes: The Act deems amendments to have come into force on October 10, 1972.
Validation of amendments made to rule 67 of the Kerala Prisons Rules, 1958, concerning appointments and promotions of Jailors.
Repeal of the Kerala Prisons Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1975, with saving provisions for actions taken under the Ordinance.

title: THE KERALA STATE LEGISLATURE (DELEGATION OF POWERS) ACT, 1959
purpose: To confer on the President the power of the Legislature of the State of Kerala to make laws.
scope: Applies to the State of Kerala. The Act grants powers to the President to make laws for Kerala when the State Legislature is not in session, with provisions for parliamentary oversight.

key_definitions.proclamation: Means the Proclamation issued on the 31st day of July, 1959, by the President under article 356 of the Constitution.

main_sections.description: States that the Act may be called the Kerala State Legislature (Delegation of Powers) Act, 1959.
Defines 'Proclamation' as per article 356 of the Constitution.

main_sections.section_title: Conferment on the President of the power of the State Legislature to make laws
main_sections.description: Grants the power to the President to make laws for the State of Kerala, exercisable by the President or under parliamentary authority. This power is available when the State Legislature is not in session. The President must consult a committee before enacting laws, consisting of thirty members of the House of the People nominated by the Speaker and fifteen members of the Council of State nominated by the Chairman. Any Act enacted by the President under this section must be laid before each House of Parliament. Parliament may, by resolution passed within seven days of the Act being laid before it, direct any modifications to be made, and such modifications shall be given effect to by the President by enacting an amending Act. The validity of the Act or any action taken thereunder is not affected by this sub-section.

important_rules: Rule 1: The President can make laws for the State of Kerala when the State Legislature is not in session.
Rule 2: Any Act enacted by the President under this power must be laid before both Houses of Parliament.
Rule 3: Parliament can modify the President's Act by a resolution within seven days of it being laid before Parliament.

rights: Right of Parliament to modify laws enacted by the President under this Act.
duties: Duty of the President to consult a committee before enacting laws.
Duty to lay enacted Acts before Parliament.
obligations: Obligation of the President to make modifications if directed by Parliament.

key_procedures: Procedure for enacting laws by the President: 1. President enacts an Act. 2. Act is laid before Parliament. 3. Parliament may pass a resolution within seven days to modify the Act. 4. President gives effect to modifications by enacting an amending Act.
administration: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be under the President's office and parliamentary oversight.
important_notes: The Proclamation referred to was issued on July 31, 1959, under Article 356 of the Constitution.
The Act received the assent of the President on 17th December, 1959.
Central Act published in the Gazette of India extraordinary dated 17th December 1959 and republished in the Gazette of Kerala dated 26th January 1960.

key_definitions.Affiliated College: A college affiliated to the University to conduct courses of study.

Establishes the University as a body corporate with perpetual succession and common seal.
Specifies the objectives including promotion of technical education, research, innovation, and industry collaboration.

Approval of statutes and ordinances by competent authorities.

important_notes: The University is named after Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.
Published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary, 2015.

title: The Kerala Clinical Establishments (Registration and Regulation) Act, 2018

Minimum standards of facilities and services must be maintained.

Penalty for violation of prescribed standards

penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, suspension or cancellation of registration, and imposition of penalties.

Periodic inspection and renewal of registration.
Appeal mechanism against adverse orders.

important_notes: The Act applies to both public and private healthcare institutions.

title: The Calicut City Municipal Act, 1961

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963

Interest on arrears of tax

penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment, inspection, recovery proceedings and penalties.

Recovery of arrears as arrears of land revenue
Appeal before Appellate Tribunal

scope: Applies to headload workers and establishments engaging them throughout the State of Kerala.

Repeals the Kerala Loading and Unloading (Regulation of Wages and Restriction of Unlawful Practices) Act, 2002, with savings clause.

Expanded definition covers workers engaged through various intermediaries.
