Excess land above ceiling limits is liable to be surrendered.
Fair rent shall be determined by statutory authorities.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Land Tribunal and Land Board
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through adjudication, surrender proceedings and statutory orders.

rights: Right of tenants to fixity of tenure
Right to purchase landlord’s rights
duties: Payment of fair rent
Compliance with land ceiling provisions
obligations: Surrender of excess land
Compliance with orders of Land Tribunal

key_procedures: Determination of fair rent
Purchase of landlord’s rights
Surrender and redistribution of excess land
administration: Revenue Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act is a cornerstone of agrarian reform in Kerala.
Provides strong statutory protection to cultivating tenants.

key_definitions.Autonomous College: A college granted autonomy by the University Grants Commission with concurrence of the State Government and University.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of the Kerala University Act, 1974

Specifies the authorities such as Academic Council, Board of Studies and Governing Council of Autonomous Colleges.

Inspection by expert committee
Approval by Autonomy Approval Committee

Right to appeal against assessment orders

Payment of tax within prescribed time

Compliance with VAT provisions

Filing of appeals and revisions
Recovery of arrears

important_notes: The Act forms part of Kerala’s transition to the VAT regime.
Multiple sections have retrospective effect.

title: The Local Authorities Laws (Amendment) Act, 1989
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Panchayats Act, 1960, the Kerala Municipalities Act, 1960, the Kerala Local Authorities Entertainments Tax Act, 1961 and the Kerala Municipal Corporations Act, 1961.
scope: Applies to Panchayats, Municipalities and Municipal Corporations in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Local authority: A Panchayat, Municipality or Municipal Corporation governed by the respective Acts.

main_sections.description: Provides that the Act may be called the Local Authorities Laws (Amendment) Act, 1989 and shall be deemed to have come into force on 11th November 1988.
Introduces provisions relating to collection of profession tax from salaried employees and registration of marriages.
Enhances financial powers of municipalities including taxation limits and recovery mechanisms.
Provides power of exemption and modifies entertainment tax provisions.
Increases monetary limits relating to sanctions, taxes and penalties.
Repeals the Local Authorities Laws (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1988 with saving clause.

important_rules: Local authorities may recover profession tax through employers.
Taxation powers are subject to prescribed limits.

penalties: Penalty for default in payment of local taxes
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Local Authorities
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through notices, recovery proceedings and attachment.

obligations: Compliance with statutory tax limits

Grant of tax exemptions
Registration of marriages

important_notes: The Act strengthens fiscal autonomy of local bodies.
Includes retrospective commencement.

title: The Munnar Special Tribunal Act, 2010
purpose: To provide for the constitution of a Special Tribunal for the adjudication of disputes in respect of land in the Munnar area and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to land disputes in the Munnar area comprising specified villages in Idukki District, Kerala.

key_definitions.Tribunal: The Munnar Special Tribunal constituted under this Act.
key_definitions.Munnar area: Lands comprised in the villages of Chinnakanal, Kannan Devan Hills, Santhanpara, Vellathooval, Aanavillassom, Pallivasal, Aanaviratty and Bison Valley.

main_sections.description: Provides that the Act may be called the Munnar Special Tribunal Act, 2010 and shall be deemed to have come into force on 14th June 2010.
Provides for constitution of a three-member Tribunal headed by a District Judge.
Transfers all land-related disputes in the Munnar area pending before courts and authorities to the Tribunal.
Confers powers of a Civil Court including summoning, evidence, inspection and issuing commissions.
Provides for appeal to the High Court on substantial questions of law.

important_rules: Civil courts shall have no jurisdiction over matters assigned to the Tribunal.
Tribunal decisions are final subject to limited appeal.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Munnar Special Tribunal
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through judicial adjudication and execution of Tribunal orders.

rights: Right to adjudication by Special Tribunal
Right to appeal on substantial questions of law
duties: Compliance with Tribunal orders
obligations: Transfer of pending cases to the Tribunal

key_procedures: Transfer of cases from courts
Adjudication by Tribunal
Appeal to High Court
administration: Revenue Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act was enacted to resolve large-scale land disputes in Munnar.
Tribunal functioning ceases after disposal of all disputes.

title: The Kerala Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1991
purpose: To provide for the levy, assessment and collection of tax on agricultural income in the State of Kerala and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
scope: Applies to agricultural income derived from land situated within the State of Kerala and to persons liable to pay agricultural income tax.

key_definitions.Agricultural income: Rent or revenue derived from land used for agricultural purposes and income derived from agricultural operations as defined under the Act.
key_definitions.Assessee: Any person by whom agricultural income tax or any other sum is payable under this Act.
key_definitions.Assessment year: The twelve-month period commencing on the first day of July.

main_sections.description: Provides that the Act may be called the Kerala Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1991 and extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.
Levies agricultural income tax for each assessment year on the total agricultural income of the previous year.
Specifies allowable deductions, expenses, depreciation and investment allowance for computing agricultural income.
Provides for payment of agricultural income tax at compounded rates in specified cases.
Mandates filing of returns of agricultural income by assessees.
Provides for payment of tax, penalty for default and recovery procedures.
Provides for appeals against orders passed by Agricultural Income Tax Officers.
Prescribes penalties for failure to furnish returns, concealment of income and other defaults.

important_rules: Agricultural income tax shall be charged annually based on previous year income.
Only specified deductions are allowable for computation.
Returns must be filed within prescribed time.

penalties: Penalty for failure to file return
Penalty for concealment of agricultural income
Interest on tax in default
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Agricultural Income Tax Authorities
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through assessment, demand notices, recovery proceedings and penalties.

rights: Right to appeal against assessment orders
Right to claim lawful deductions and refunds
duties: Filing of returns
Payment of tax within due dates
obligations: Maintenance of accounts
Disclosure of true agricultural income

key_procedures: Assessment and reassessment
Recovery of tax arrears
Appeals and revisions
administration: Revenue Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act repealed earlier agricultural income tax laws.
Contains detailed schedules prescribing compounded tax rates for plantations.

title: The Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969
purpose: To consolidate, amend and unify the laws relating to co-operative societies in the State of Kerala and to facilitate their orderly development.
scope: Applies to the registration, management, supervision and dissolution of co-operative societies throughout the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Co-operative society: A society registered or deemed to be registered under this Act.
key_definitions.Registrar: The Registrar of Co-operative Societies appointed under the Act.
key_definitions.Member: A person admitted to membership of a co-operative society in accordance with the Act and bye-laws.

main_sections.description: Provides that the Act may be called the Kerala Co-operative Societies Act, 1969 and extends to the whole of the State of Kerala.
Empowers the Registrar to register co-operative societies and issue registration certificates.
Specifies eligibility, disqualifications and conditions for membership.
Vests the final authority of a society in the general body of members.
Provides for audit of accounts of co-operative societies.
Mandates reference of disputes touching the business of a society to the Registrar.
Provides grounds and procedure for winding up of co-operative societies.
Defines offences and prescribes penalties under the Act.

important_rules: Co-operative societies shall function on democratic principles.
Accounts must be audited annually.
Disputes shall be resolved through statutory mechanisms.

penalties: Penalties for offences by officers or members
Surcharge for misappropriation or negligence
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Registrar of Co-operative Societies
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through audit, inquiry, surcharge proceedings and prosecution.

Right to inspect records subject to rules
duties: Compliance with bye-laws
Proper use of society funds
obligations: Submission to audit and inquiry
Obedience to lawful directions of Registrar

key_procedures: Registration and amendment of bye-laws
Audit and inspection
Settlement of disputes
Winding up and liquidation
administration: Co-operation Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act has undergone multiple amendments to strengthen regulation.
Provides a complete statutory framework for the co-operative sector in Kerala.

title: The Kerala Court-Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1960
purpose: To amend and consolidate the law relating to court-fees and valuation of suits in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to all courts, suits, appeals, applications and proceedings where court-fees are payable in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Market value: The value of the subject-matter as determined in accordance with the provisions of the Act.

main_sections.description: Provides the name of the Act, extends it to the whole of Kerala and enables the Government to notify its commencement.

main_sections.section_title: Levy of fee in courts and public offices
main_sections.description: Mandates payment of prescribed court-fees for documents filed or recorded in courts or public offices.

main_sections.section_title: Documents falling under two or more descriptions
main_sections.description: Provides that the highest applicable fee shall be levied where a document falls under multiple descriptions.

main_sections.section_title: Statement of particulars of subject-matter of suit
main_sections.description: Requires plaintiffs to file a valuation statement of the subject-matter of the suit.
Lays down the principles for computation of court-fees.
Provides for constitution of the Legal Benefit Fund.
Repeals earlier corresponding laws relating to court-fees and valuation.

important_rules: Court-fee shall be paid before a document is acted upon.
Valuation of suits shall follow statutory rules.
Deficit court-fee may be directed to be paid by the court.

penalties: Rejection or stay of proceedings for non-payment of proper court-fee
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Courts and Board of Revenue
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through scrutiny of pleadings, inquiries and judicial orders.

rights: Right to refund of excess court-fee in prescribed cases
duties: Proper valuation of suits
Payment of prescribed court-fees
obligations: Compliance with court directions regarding valuation and fee

key_procedures: Inquiry into valuation
Refund and remission of fees
Appeals on court-fee determinations
administration: Law Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act contains detailed schedules governing fee computation.
Applies uniformly to civil courts across Kerala.

title: The Kerala District Administration Act, 1979
purpose: To provide for a decentralized system of administration at the district level by constituting district councils and delegating certain powers and functions of the State Government to such councils.
scope: Applies to district administration and governance through district councils throughout the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.District council: A district council constituted under this Act.
key_definitions.President: The elected President of the district council.

main_sections.description: Provides the name of the Act, its application to the whole of Kerala and commencement by notification.
Empowers the Government to constitute district councils for each district.
Provides for reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and women.
Fixes the term of office of members of district councils.
Provides for election, powers and functions of the President and Vice-President.
Provides for constitution of a Finance Commission for district councils.
Empowers the Government to dissolve or supersede district councils under specified circumstances.

important_rules: District councils function subject to Government supervision.
Elections shall be conducted in accordance with prescribed rules.

penalties: Penalties for election offences
Penalties for obstruction of council functioning
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Government and Election Authorities
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through statutory inquiries, prosecutions and administrative action.

rights: Right of elected members to participate in district governance
duties: Faithful discharge of council functions
Compliance with statutory and Government directions
obligations: Observance of financial and administrative discipline

key_procedures: Election of members
Constitution of committees
Budget preparation and approval
administration: Local Self Government Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act introduced district-level decentralization prior to Panchayati Raj reforms.

title: The Kerala Drugs and Other Stores (Unlawful Possession) Act, 1971
purpose: To provide for the punishment of the offence of unlawful possession of drugs and other stores belonging to specified departments of the Government of Kerala.
scope: Applies to unlawful possession of drugs and other stores belonging to the Health Department, Animal Husbandry Department and the Department of Indigenous Medicine in Kerala.

key_definitions.Drug: Includes medicines and substances intended for diagnosis, treatment or prevention of disease in humans or animals.
key_definitions.Inspector: An Inspector appointed under the Act.
key_definitions.Other stores: Articles and appliances belonging to specified Government departments.

main_sections.description: Provides that the Act extends to the whole of Kerala and shall be deemed to have come into force on 2nd December 1970.

main_sections.section_title: Unlawful possession of drugs or other stores
main_sections.description: Defines the offence and prescribes punishment for unlawful possession.
Provides for appointment of Inspectors for enforcement of the Act.
Confers powers of search, seizure and examination.
Prescribes procedure for seizure and production before Magistrate.
Restricts cognizance of offences to complaints made by Inspectors.
Provides saving of actions taken under the earlier Ordinance.

important_rules: Possession of Government-marked drugs without authority is an offence.
Search and seizure shall follow Criminal Procedure Code provisions.

penalties: Imprisonment up to two years
Fine not less than one thousand rupees

Production before Magistrate
Trial before competent court

title: The Kerala Finance Act, 2025
purpose: To give effect to certain financial proposals of the Government of Kerala for the Financial Year 2025–2026.
scope: Applies to fiscal measures, taxation, fees, levies and amendments to various tax-related laws in the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Commissioner of State Tax: The authority empowered to administer and implement tax provisions under the amended Acts.

main_sections.description: Provides that the Act may be called the Kerala Finance Act, 2025 and specifies different commencement dates for different provisions.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Kerala Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1960
main_sections.description: Enhances court fees, revises valuation provisions, and introduces new fee structures for various proceedings.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Kerala Land Tax Act, 1961
main_sections.description: Revises land tax rates based on area classifications such as Panchayat, Municipality and Corporation areas.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963
main_sections.description: Introduces arrear settlement schemes, modifies definitions of goods and strengthens inspection and confiscation provisions.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976
main_sections.description: Revises motor vehicle tax rates including special provisions for electric vehicles.

main_sections.section_title: Amendment of Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
main_sections.description: Introduces amendments relating to definitions, local funds and compliance mechanisms.

important_rules: Different provisions come into force on different notified dates.

Special arrear settlement schemes are time-bound.

Confiscation of goods and conveyances in specified cases
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Commissioner of State Tax and other designated authorities
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, assessments, recovery proceedings and adjudication.

duties: Payment of revised taxes and fees
Compliance with amended procedures
obligations: Maintenance of records
Adherence to statutory timelines

key_procedures: Settlement of arrears through notified schemes
Assessment and reassessment under amended laws
Recovery and enforcement actions

title: The Kerala General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 2005
purpose: To further amend the Kerala General Sales Tax Act, 1963 in order to revise definitions, tax rates and assessment procedures.

key_definitions.Dealer: A person liable to pay tax under the principal Act.

Revises provisions relating to levy of tax on petroleum products.

penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through audits, inspections and assessment proceedings.

Audit visit
Best judgment assessment

Introduces compounded tax scheme for certain categories.

title: The Kerala Hindu Places of Public Worship (Authorisation of Entry) Act, 1965
purpose: To make better provisions for the entry of all classes and sections of Hindus into places of public worship.
scope: Applies to all Hindu places of public worship within the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Section or class: Any division, sub-division, caste or denomination of Hindus.

main_sections.description: Bars civil court jurisdiction in matters governed by the Act.

Regulations shall not discriminate against any section or class.

Provides for constitution and administration of the Board’s fund.
Prescribes penalties for contravention of provisions of the Act.

important_rules: Housing schemes shall be framed and sanctioned as prescribed.
The Board may acquire land and recover betterment fees.

Penalty for obstruction of Board functions

The Board functions under Government supervision.

Collection of contributions
Disbursement of welfare benefits

key_definitions.Lottery seller: A person engaged in the sale of lottery tickets issued by the Government of Kerala.

Provides for the constitution of a Board to administer and manage the Welfare Fund.
Provides for payment of pension, financial assistance, medical aid and other welfare benefits to members.

important_rules: Membership in the Welfare Fund is mandatory for eligible agents and sellers.
Contributions shall be paid at prescribed rates.

Collection of contributions

key_definitions.Practitioner: A registered medical practitioner authorised to practise medicine under this Act.
key_definitions.Register: The register of medical practitioners maintained under the Act.

title: The Kerala State Youth Commission Act, 2014

scope: Applies to youth welfare, empowerment, protection of youth rights and advisory functions within the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Commission: The Kerala State Youth Commission constituted under this Act.
key_definitions.Youth: A person who has completed eighteen years of age but has not completed forty years.

main_sections.description: Provides that the Act may be called the Kerala State Youth Commission Act, 2014 and shall be deemed to have come into force on 1 November 2012.
Provides for constitution of the Youth Commission consisting of a Chairperson and members appointed by the Government.

Submission of recommendations
Preparation of annual reports

title: The Kerala Toddy Workers’ Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 1996
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Toddy Workers’ Welfare Fund Act, 1969 with a view to strengthening welfare measures, pension provisions and administrative powers of the Welfare Fund Board.

Provides for Government contribution to the Welfare Fund every year at a minimum of 7.5 per cent of the employers’ contribution by way of grant.

Provides for borrowing powers of the Board, audit of accounts and laying of annual reports and audited accounts before the Legislative Assembly.

important_rules: Government shall contribute annually to the Welfare Fund.
Employers shall make advance monthly contributions.
Pension eligibility and payment are incorporated into the Schedule.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Kerala Toddy Workers’ Welfare Fund Board

title: The Kerala Town and Country Planning (Amendment) Act, 2021
purpose: To amend the Kerala Town and Country Planning Act, 2016 to restructure planning authorities, revise definitions and strengthen spatial planning and development processes.
scope: Applies to town and country planning, spatial development, perspective plans and planning authorities throughout the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Perspective Plan: A long-term spatial development plan with a planning horizon of about twenty years.
key_definitions.Special Area: An area identified for urgent planning intervention due to disaster, environmental sensitivity or infrastructure needs.

main_sections.description: Provides that the Act may be called the Kerala Town and Country Planning (Amendment) Act, 2021 and shall be deemed to have come into force on 25 February 2021.
Substitutes and inserts several definitions relating to development, disaster, land, plans and planning authorities.
Provides for constitution of the State Town and Country Planning Committee in place of the earlier Board.
Specifies matters to be included in the State Spatial Perspective Plan including infrastructure, environment and disaster-prone areas.
Revises procedures for preparation, approval and publication of the State Perspective Plan.

important_rules: Spatial planning shall follow an integrated and sustainable approach.
Public participation through publication and objections is mandatory.
Approved plans shall guide State and local development programmes.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: State Town and Country Planning Committee and Local Planning Authorities
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through statutory planning approvals, directions and regulatory controls.

rights: Right of the public to submit objections and suggestions on published plans

key_definitions.Fisheries education: Education and research in production, conservation, processing and sustainable management of fishery resources.

key_definitions.Fish farm: An enclosed area used for aquaculture activities.

Enumerates powers including providing instruction, conducting examinations, granting degrees, diplomas and certificates, affiliating colleges and promoting research.
Declares the Governor of Kerala as the Chancellor and prescribes his powers and functions.
Provides for appointment, term of office, powers and duties of the Vice-Chancellor.
Specifies the authorities of the University such as the Senate, Syndicate, Academic Council, Faculties, Boards of Studies and Students’ Council.
Provides for framing of Statutes governing the University administration.
Provides for making Ordinances regulating academic and administrative matters.
Provides for repeal of corresponding provisions and saving of actions taken.

important_rules: The University shall be open to all classes and creeds.
Academic and administrative authorities shall function as per Statutes and Ordinances.
Affiliated colleges must comply with University regulations.

penalties: Withdrawal of affiliation for non-compliance
Disciplinary action against teachers and staff as prescribed
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: University Authorities and Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, disciplinary proceedings and statutory controls.

rights: Right of students to education and examinations
Right of colleges to seek affiliation
duties: Duty to maintain academic standards
Duty to comply with University laws
obligations: Submission of accounts and reports
Compliance with Government and University directions

key_procedures: Affiliation of colleges
Conduct of examinations
Appointment of University authorities
administration: Higher Education Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act gives retrospective effect to the commencement date.
The University headquarters is at Kottayam.

title: The Kerala Co-operative Land Mortgage Banks (Amendment) Act, 1983
purpose: To further amend the Kerala Co-operative Land Mortgage Banks Act, 1960 to enable issue of debentures by the Board to approved bodies with Government guarantee.
scope: Applies to Kerala Co-operative Land Mortgage Banks constituted under the Kerala Co-operative Land Mortgage Banks Act, 1960.

main_sections.description: Provides that the Act may be called the Kerala Co-operative Land Mortgage Banks (Amendment) Act, 1983 and shall come into force at once.
Inserts section 4B empowering the Board, with previous sanction of the Government, to issue debentures to approved persons or bodies, with repayment and interest guaranteed by the Government.
Amends section 7 of the principal Act by inserting reference to section 4B.

important_rules: Debentures shall not be issued without Government guarantee.
Conditions imposed by Government shall apply to such debentures.

penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Registrar of Co-operative Societies and Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through statutory supervision and compliance under the principal Act.

key_procedures: Issue of debentures with Government sanction
administration: Co-operation Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act received the assent of the Governor on 22 April 1983.
Published in the Kerala Gazette Extraordinary dated 25 April 1983.

title: The Kerala Lifts and Escalators Act, 2013
purpose: To provide for the regulation of the erection, maintenance and safe working of lifts and escalators and all machinery and apparatus pertaining thereto in the State of Kerala.
scope: Applies to installation, operation, maintenance, inspection and safety of lifts and escalators in buildings throughout the State of Kerala.

key_definitions.Lift: A hoisting mechanism designed to carry passengers or goods in a substantially vertical direction.
key_definitions.Escalator: A power-driven continuous moving stairway used for transporting passengers.
key_definitions.Inspector: The Electrical Inspector appointed under the Electricity Act having jurisdiction.

main_sections.description: Provides that the Act may be called the Kerala Lifts and Escalators Act, 2013 and shall be deemed to have come into force on 1 March 2012.
Defines key terms such as lift, escalator, owner, inspector and rules.

main_sections.section_title: Permission to erect lifts and escalators
main_sections.description: Prohibits erection of any lift or escalator without prior permission of the Inspector.
Mandates licence for working any lift or escalator after inspection.

main_sections.section_title: Power to cancel or suspend licence
main_sections.description: Empowers the Inspector to cancel or suspend licences for safety violations or misrepresentation.
Prescribes penalties including fine and imprisonment for contravention of the Act or rules.
Fixes liability on companies and persons in charge for offences.

important_rules: Permission and licence are mandatory for erection and operation.
Regular inspection and maintenance are compulsory.
Unsafe lifts or escalators may be ordered to stop operation.

penalties: Fine up to five thousand rupees
Imprisonment up to three months for continuing offences
penalties_and_enforcement.enforcement_authority: Electrical Inspectorate and Government of Kerala
penalties_and_enforcement.how_enforced: Through inspections, suspension of licences, prosecution and penalties.

rights: Right to apply for permission and licence
duties: Duty to maintain lifts and escalators in safe condition
obligations: Compliance with safety directions and inspection requirements

key_procedures: Application for permission to erect
Grant and renewal of licence
Inspection and accident reporting
administration: Electrical Inspectorate / Energy Department, Government of Kerala
important_notes: The Act consolidates safety regulation for lifts and escalators.
Applies to both existing and new installations subject to conditions.
